title: Rashi on the Prophets and Writings - English Translation (AI-drafted, v1.0 CC0, 2026).

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: all the mighty men of valour
Joshua.english_translation: Those among you shall cross over as the vanguard (armed men going ahead).
He will provoke (anger over) your words.

I am compelled to say that he sent them during the days of mourning for Moses, for at the end of three days, when the days of mourning for Moses were over, they crossed the Jordan. From there we learn that Moses died on the seventh of Adar, when you count thirty-three days backward from the day they came up out of the Jordan, on the tenth of the first month. And you must also say that after the spies were sent, [Israel] did not cross the Jordan until the fifth day, for it is said: “and they abode there three days, until the pursuers were returned.” That night, “they passed over and came to Joshua the son of Nun”; “and Joshua rose early in the morning, and they removed from Shittim” — that is the fourth day — “and they lodged there before they passed over.” So it turns out that they did not cross until the fifth day.

In secret (Aramaic: *beraz*); so Jonathan translated. [Rashi's explanation:] he said to them, “Make yourselves like deaf men (*cheresh*), so that they will not hide their words from you.” Another explanation: *cheresh* [also means] clay; “Load yourselves with pots, so that you look like potters.”

But Jericho was included [in “the land”]; why was it singled out? Because it was as weighty as all the others (lit., “hard against all of them”), since it lay on the frontier. A similar case (2 Samuel 2:30): “and there were missing of David's servants nineteen men and Asahel”; but was not Asahel included? Why was he singled out? Because he was as weighty as all the others. Similarly (1 Kings 11:1): “Now King Solomon loved many strange women, together with the daughter of Pharaoh”; but was not Pharaoh's daughter included? Why was she singled out? Because he was fonder of her than of all the others, and because of the sin she caused him to commit, more than all of them. So it is taught in the Sifrei (Ekev 52).
Jonathan translated: *pundekita* (an innkeeper), one who sells various kinds of food.
To spy, as in (Job 39:29): “From thence she spieth out the prey.”

Some verses speak of several people in the singular, because she hurried to hide them, and in a narrow place, as if he were a single person. And in one version of Midrash Aggadat Tanchuma (Shelach 1) it says: it was Phinehas and Caleb, and Phinehas stood before them and they did not see him, because he was like an angel. Another explanation: “and she hid him” — each one by himself. We find a parallel (Proverbs 27:9): “Oil and perfume rejoice the heart,” and it does not say “rejoice” in the plural.
Flax in its stalks.
The place where the water is crossed, for they thought that [the spies] had gone back toward the plains of Moab, with the Jordan lying between.
[They shut it—] the gatekeepers.
That you will do [this] when you come and conquer the city, that you will recognize the sign and let me live.
She saw by the Holy Spirit that they would return at the end of three days (Sifrei, Devarim 22).
Behold, we place the matter on you, to make this sign.
An expression for a cord and a rope.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: his blood shall be upon his head
Joshua.english_translation: The guilt for his death will be on his own head, because he will cause his own death.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: his blood shall be on our head
Joshua.english_translation: The guilt for his death will be upon us.
The Jordan.

Because they all descended from Levi, the father of Amram's father, they were called Levites, as our Rabbis explained in Bereshit Rabbah: in forty-eight places (in Yevamot 86b and Tamid 27a and others the reading is: in twenty-four places) the priests are called Levites, and this is the reason (heard from my teacher).
Joshua.translator_note: In the printed Hebrew the first “father” in “Levi (father of) the father of Amram” is in parentheses, which marks it as doubtful or to be deleted. The last words, “heard from my teacher” (מפי רבי), could also be read differently; the meaning is uncertain.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: and ye shall go after it
Joshua.english_translation: This journey differed from the other journeys, for as long as Moses was alive the pillar of cloud traveled first and showed them the way, and the Ark traveled after two divisions; now the Ark travels first (Sotah 32b).

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: Yet there shall be a space
Joshua.english_translation: It is the honor of the Omnipresent.

[The form *uveineiu*] is like *uveino* (“and between it”); and similar to it (Psalms 149:2): “Let Israel rejoice in his Makers” (in the plural form). Another explanation: there were two arks, that of the Divine Presence and that of Joseph, going together.
So that you will be able to go and pray before it on the Sabbath; so it is explained in Midrash Tanchuma, because He knew that [Israel] would be besieging Jericho on the Sabbath.
This refers back to “and you shall go after it.”

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: for you have not passed this way
Joshua.english_translation: You have not gone in this manner until now.
On the third day; the thirtieth day of mourning was the first of the three days.
Make yourselves ready.
When you cross the Jordan.
Jonathan translated: *perishan*.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: And Joshua spoke unto the priests
Joshua.english_translation: On the following day.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: Take up the ark of the covenant
Joshua.english_translation: Until now the Levites carried it; today, the priests.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: When you are come to the brink of the waters of the Jordan
Joshua.english_translation: When you enter inside its edge.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: you shall stand still in the Jordan
Joshua.english_translation: Until all the people have crossed to the other side.
He squeezed them all in between the two poles of the Ark; this is one of the places where the few held the many.
By what you see, that all of you are squeezed together here.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth
Joshua.english_translation: The covenant of the Holy One, blessed be He, who is Lord of all the earth. And do not wonder at the “the” (*ha-*) of *ha-brit* (“the covenant”), for many verses speak this way, such as (2 Kings 16:17): “the borders of the bases” (*ha-misgarot ha-mekhonot*); (Jeremiah 31:40): “the valley of the dead bodies” (*ha-emek ha-pegarim*).
Joshua.translator_note: The printed Hebrew gives the reference as Jeremiah 31:39, but the phrase “the valley of the dead bodies” stands in Jeremiah 31:40 of the Hebrew Bible.

Joshua.english_translation: He goes ahead before you, to enter into the Jordan.
Prepare them to be ready for what I will command them when you cross the Jordan.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: the waters that come down from above
Joshua.english_translation: [Down] below, as is the way of all flowing rivers.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: and they shall stand in one heap
Joshua.english_translation: When the waters came down to the place where they were cut off, they do not descend from there downward, but gather together and swell and rise upward, in mounds upon mounds.
Like (Psalms 33:7): “He gathereth the waters of the sea together as a heap”; (Isaiah 17:11): “a heap of harvest”; an expression of height, and so Menahem connected them.
An expression for a high bank.
For the days of Nisan are days of harvest.
From the place where they stood, they were cut off.
So it was named.
Those that were flowing down from there downward at first.
They went on in their course like all the streams that go to the sea, until they ended.
By the bank of the Jordan.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: in the midst of the Jordan
Joshua.english_translation: And as long as they stood, the upper waters did not come down below, and meanwhile all the people were crossing on dry ground.
Directed and standing straight, one opposite the other.
These are the ones mentioned above, to be ready.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: pass over before the ark, etc.
Joshua.english_translation: Enter now into the Jordan and cross over, up to [the place] before the priests.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: Joshua also set up twelve stones
Joshua.english_translation: Other [stones]: Joshua set them up in the midst of the Jordan.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: And it came to pass, when all the people were wholly passed over, that the ark etc.
Joshua.english_translation: Not in the way that the others crossed, but as is explained below, in the passage: “the soles of the priests' feet were plucked up unto the dry land” — onto the bank into which they had entered and beside which they were standing — and the waters returned backward to flow as before. So it turns out that the Ark and its bearers were on this side, and all Israel on that side, and the Ark carried its bearers and crossed.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: in the presence of the people
Joshua.english_translation: In the sight of the people.
Here Scripture explains what was said above, how the Ark of the Lord and the priests crossed before the people, etc.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: come up out of the Jordan
Joshua.english_translation: “And they crossed” is not written here, but “and they came up”; we learn that they came up onto the bank beside which they were standing. It is impossible to say that they were standing by the western bank of the Jordan, for it is said above (3:15): “the feet of the priests that bore the ark were dipped in the brink of the water,” and there it says: “And the priests stood … while all Israel passed over.”

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: the soles of the priests' feet were plucked up
Joshua.english_translation: From the water onto the dry ground beside them, and the waters returned to their place. So the Ark was on this side and Israel on that side; the Ark carried its bearers and crossed. And for this matter Uzzah was punished (2 Samuel 6:7) when he took hold of the Ark: if it carried its bearers, would it not all the more carry itself?

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: did Joshua set up in Gilgal
Joshua.english_translation: This is the lodging-place where we lodged for the night.
From the side to which the Israelites had crossed, it is the western side; until now they had been on the eastern bank.
It was named for the event, for [the foreskins] became like a hill.
As I explained: [the reason is] that the north wind had not blown; and it was they who were circumcised now.
*Be-atrehon* (Aramaic: in their place); and they did not lay siege to the city.
From the wound [of the circumcision].
I have removed; like (Psalms 119:22): “Remove from me reproach and contempt”; (Genesis 29:10): “and he rolled the stone.”
From here [we learn] that the outskirts of a city count as part of the city, since it is impossible to say “inside Jericho.”
Aramaic: *ha-le-masa'adna atita* — “Have you come to help us?”
As its Targum [renders]: “held fast by *dashin* of iron and made strong by *'avrin* of bronze.”
Joshua.translator_note: The two Aramaic words in the Targum's phrase (*dashin* and *'avrin*), meaning something like bolts and bars, are not clear to me. The Targum text itself reads as Rashi quotes it. Audit 4: the Aramaic quotation was checked against Targum Jonathan/the Ketuvim Targum (Mikraot Gedolot, Sefaria) at JOS 6:1 and reads as quoted; the meaning of the unclear word, if noted above, is still unresolved.

Joshua.english_translation: Rams.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: when they make a long blast
Joshua.english_translation: At the last blast, when the blower prolongs the sound.
[In] its own place.

The sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad passed before them, because the sons of Gad were mighty and struck with a strong arm, as it is said (Deuteronomy 33:20): “and he teareth the arm, yea, the crown of the head.”
The tribe of Dan, which traveled last and gathered in all who lagged behind at the end.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: And the city shall be devoted
Joshua.english_translation: Holy, for the day is the holy Sabbath, and the spoil taken on it is fit to be holy.
An expression of troubled (muddy) waters.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: And the young men the spies went in
Joshua.english_translation: Here they needed alacrity, and they became like alert young men; and on the first night they were like angels, for they kept themselves from sin with Rahab the harlot. Therefore they were called “angels” there; therefore they were called “men,” “angels,” “young men.”

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: with the loss of his first-born shall he lay the foundation thereof, and with the loss of his youngest
Joshua.english_translation: At the beginning of the foundation, when he builds on it, his firstborn son will die, and he will bury him and go on [building], until the youngest dies, when the work is completed, which is the setting up of the doors.
Next to Beth-aven.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: on the east side of Beth-el
Joshua.english_translation: East of Beth-el.
Until they broke them (Aramaic: *ad detavronon*).

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: would that we had been content
Joshua.english_translation: Would that we had decided to dwell on the eastern bank of the Jordan, in the land of Sihon and Og, which had already been conquered.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: and what wilt Thou do for Thy great name
Joshua.english_translation: [What will You do for] the Name that is joined with ours? This is its midrashic [reading]. Its plain sense: And what will You do for the name of Your might, which has already gone out? And now they will say, “His strength has grown weak.”

“*Kam lekha*” (it stood for you) is written: what you prayed before Me and mentioned has stood [before Me]. Another explanation: you stood by yourself in the camp and did not go out with them; yet I said (Numbers 27:17): “who may go out before them and who may come in before them”; for you will bring the children of Israel [into the land] and I will be with you (cf. Deuteronomy 31:23); (Deuteronomy 3:28): “for he shall go over before this people, and he shall cause them to inherit.” If you go before them they will succeed, and if not they will not succeed. Another explanation: “Arise,” because of you this has happened to them; I did not tell you to devote the spoil of the city.
One family contains many fathers' houses.
By individual heads; all the men of the house shall come to the lot.
The tent and the movable property.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: he and all that he hath
Joshua.english_translation: According to the law explained below (verse 25): him and the animals by stoning. The *zakef* (cantillation mark) on “with fire” proves that it is separate from “him”; for we find verses which the cantillation divides, such as (Deuteronomy 11:30): “behind the way of the going down of the sun,” where “behind” is set apart from “the way” by the accent. And so is its interpretation: he who is taken with the devoted thing shall be burnt with fire — that which is fit to be burnt, as it explains below.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: he and all that he hath
Joshua.english_translation: According to the law stated below. This is a brief verse, and similar to it (2 Samuel 5:8): “whosoever smiteth the Jebusites, let him get up to the gutter” — it did not explain what he will have; and in Chronicles (1 Chronicles 11:6) it explained: “shall be chief.” So here too it did not explain what is to be done to “him and all that he hath,” and below it explained.
Before the breastplate, where the tribes are inscribed; and the Holy One, blessed be He, gave him a sign: the tribe that sinned, its stone would grow dim; and the stone of Judah grew dim.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: And he brought near the family of Judah
Joshua.english_translation: By one lot the heads of the families came near, one man from each family, and they cast the lot on whom it would fall; and afterward on all the fathers' houses of that family, and one man from each fathers' house came to the lot; and afterward all the men of that house came.

He began to cast aspersions on the lot. [Achan] said to him: “You come at me by lot? You and Eleazar the priest are the greatest of the generation; cast the lot on the two of you, and it will fall on one of you.” [Joshua] said to him: “Give glory, I beg of you; do not cast aspersions on the lots by which the land will in the future be divided.”
He saw the men of Judah assembling for war; he said, “Better that I die alone, and that thousands of Israel not be killed.”

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: and thus and thus have I done
Joshua.english_translation: Also with other devoted things in the days of Moses, as it is said (Numbers 21:2): “then I will utterly destroy their cities.”

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: When I saw among the spoil
Joshua.english_translation: I considered what is written in the Torah (Deuteronomy 20:14): “and you shall eat [the spoil of your enemies], etc.”

Its Targum: *istala* (garment) of Babylon. For every king who did not acquire a palace in the land of Israel was not at ease in his kingdom, as it is said (Jeremiah 3:19): “and I gave you a desirable land, the inheritance of the beauty of the hosts of nations”; and the king of Babylon had a palace in Jericho, and when he came here he would put on [such garments].

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: and they ran unto the tent
Joshua.english_translation: So that the tribe of Judah would not get there first and take it from there, to deny the lot.

*Ve-atikhunun* (Aramaic: and he poured them out). And our Rabbis said (Sanhedrin 44a): He came and struck them before the Omnipresent, and said before Him: “Master of the Universe, shall the majority of the Sanhedrin fall on account of these?”

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: and his sons … and all Israel
Joshua.english_translation: To see his punishment, so that they would be warned from doing as he did.
Joshua.translator_note: The Hebrew word בִּרְדוּיוֹ (here rendered “his punishment”) is unclear to me; the sense is inferred from the context.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: and his ox, and his ass
Joshua.english_translation: To destroy them, as it is said (above, verse 15): “and it shall be that he that is taken with the devoted thing shall be burnt with fire, he and all that he hath.”

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: And all Israel stoned him with stones
Joshua.english_translation: Because he desecrated the Sabbath.
The tent and the movable property.
The ox and the animals.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: its spoil … shall ye take for a prey unto yourselves
Joshua.english_translation: And do not devote the spoil any more.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: till we have drawn them away
Joshua.english_translation: An expression of *tik* (sheath): that we draw them out of the sheath (*tik*) of the city; in Old French, *esfodrer* (“to draw from the sheath”). It may also be interpreted as an expression of drawing off (*netikah*), like (Jeremiah 12:3): “pull them out like sheep for the slaughter.”
Joshua.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is דישפורי״ר; Darmesteter (1909, p. 43) reads it as *esfodrer*, “to draw from the sheath.”

Joshua.english_translation: *Ve-titrekhun* (Aramaic: and you shall drive out).
For Ai is east of Beth-el, and Beth-el is west of Ai.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: but Joshua lodged that night among the people
Joshua.english_translation: To be ready to rise early in the morning.
As the Omnipresent said to him: if he crosses before them, they cross; and if not, they do not cross.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: And he took about five thousand men
Joshua.english_translation: One ambush after another; one nearer the city than the other.
This “setting” is an expression of readiness, near the wall for battle, as it is said of Ben-hadad (1 Kings 20:12): “Set [yourselves] against the city”; “and they set.”
“And its ambush” (*arbo*), like (Genesis 27:36): “and he has supplanted me (*va-ya'kveni*).”

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: and Joshua went that night into the midst of the valley
Joshua.english_translation: Our Rabbis said (Sanhedrin 44b): he spent the night in the depth of the Halakhah (legal study).
For the time of day on which they had conferred together the day before: “at that hour we shall go out,” for they were diviners and soothsayers.
An expression of being struck (as its Targum: *ve-itberu*, “and they were broken”); they made themselves appear as if they were beaten before them.
It was the sign for the ambush to come out from its hiding place, when they saw the javelin stretched out toward the city. *Kidon* (javelin): in Old French, *espiet* (“spear”).
Joshua.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is שפיד״ו; the manuscripts Darmesteter (1909, p. 43) collated read *espiét/espède*, which he glosses “the sword.” Whether Rashi meant a spear or a sword here is therefore uncertain.

Joshua.english_translation: Strength.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: and the people that fled to the wilderness
Joshua.english_translation: Israel, who had fled toward the wilderness as said above, turned to fight against the pursuer.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: and the others issued out of the city
Joshua.english_translation: The ambush that had set the city on fire.
This passage is written out of chronological order, for he did this from the day they crossed the Jordan.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: And he wrote there upon the stones
Joshua.english_translation: These are the very stones mentioned above; after this event they peeled off the plaster from them and brought them to Gilgal.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: to bless the people of Israel first
Joshua.english_translation: To put blessings before curses: “Blessed is the man who does not make a graven or molten image.”
As the sons of Jacob acted with guile (Genesis 34) toward Hamor, the father of Shechem, who was a Hivite; and the inhabitants of Gibeon were of the Hivites, as is said in the passage.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: and made as if they had been ambassadors
Joshua.english_translation: They made themselves like those who go on a mission, an expression of (Jeremiah 49:14): “and an ambassador is sent among the nations.” And in every word whose root begins with *tsade*, when it is in the *hitpael* or *nitpael* form, a *tet* comes in its midst and separates the letters of the root of the word; for example (Genesis 44:16): “*mah nitztadak*” (how shall we clear ourselves), from the root *tzedek*, where it says *nitztadak*; and so (Daniel 4:30): “*yitztaba*” (shall be wet), from the root *tzeva*.
Joshua.translator_note: The printed Hebrew gives the Daniel reference as 5:30; the word *yitztaba* occurs in Daniel 4:30 (and 5:21) in the Hebrew Bible.

Joshua.english_translation: So that they would look like men who had come from a distant land.
An expression of “split”; in the Aramaic language: *tziriya dechitei*, which bind wineskins (*zikei*).
In Old French, *arsiz* (“burnt”); an expression of “hearth” (*moked*); and so Jonathan translated: *kesanin*.
Joshua.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is ארשי״ץ; Darmesteter (1909, p. 43) reads *arsiç*, “burnt,” and notes that one manuscript adds the gloss *tostes* (“toasted”). The Aramaic word *kesanin* is left untranslated here.

Joshua.english_translation: Perhaps you are among the inhabitants of the land.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: we took it for our provision
Joshua.english_translation: An expression of provisions (*tzedah*), when we took it out as provisions for the road.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: And the men took of their victuals
Joshua.english_translation: They accepted their words, for they had trapped them with their mouths; an expression of (Exodus 21:13): “and [he] who did not lie in wait.”

He sang a song beneath the sun, because he said to the sun, “Be silent (*dom*)” — be silent from saying song — and as long as it is silent, it stands and does not move, for during all the time of its going it says song. And the plain sense of the verse: *dom* is an expression of waiting, like (1 Samuel 14:9): “If they say thus unto us: Wait (*dumu*),” and likewise (Psalms 37:7): “Be still before the Lord.”

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: And thou, Moon, in the valley of Aijalon
Joshua.english_translation: At that time the moon stood opposite the valley of Aijalon, and it is far from Gibeon, for Gibeon is on the border of Benjamin and Aijalon on the border of Dan.

This matter is written in the Torah, for Jacob said to Joseph (Genesis 48:19): “his seed shall be fullness [of the nations], etc.” When? On the day the sun stood still for Joshua, [when] the whole world was filled with the fame of Joshua; “and the sun stood still in the midst of heaven, and hasted not to go down about a whole day.”
Roll stones to the mouth of the cave.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: none moved his tongue against any of the children of Israel
Joshua.english_translation: This is an abbreviated verse: “the one who whets did not whet his tongue against any of the children of Israel.”

An expression of speaking [with] the tongue; and so (Exodus 11:7): “no dog shall whet [move] his tongue,” and so (2 Samuel 5:24): “then you shall bestir yourself,” said of David: you shall call, cry out with the sound of the shouts of battle.
A place where the waters of the hills pour down.

The southern side of the land of Israel, from east to west; and he did not manage to conquer the whole border, and [the stretch] from Gaza to the sea remained; this is what it says below: “and all the land that remaineth: the Gazite and the Ashdodite, etc.”
South of Gennesaret (the Sea of Galilee).
The districts of Dor; in Old French, *contrédes* (“regions”).
Joshua.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is קונטדו״ש; Darmesteter (1909, p. 43) reads *kontrédes*, “regions.”

Joshua.english_translation: Westward.
Jonathan translated: *charitzei yama* (“trenches of the sea”), for they make trenches and the waters of the sea flow into them, and they are burned by the heat of the sun and become salt.
Whose wall was not destroyed, as Jericho, whose wall fell; and so Ai, of which it says (above 8:28): “and he made it a heap for ever, a desolation.”
In the tradition: he burned it (Bereshit Rabbah, Vayishlach); Moses had commanded him and told him so.

*Turah she'iya* (Aramaic: a smooth mountain), slippery: “the bare mountain, unto Baal-gad” on the eastern border; and during his lifetime he did not manage to conquer the whole border up to the north — Tosefta.
*Mishar Gad* (“the plain of Gad”).

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: Joshua made war a long time
Joshua.english_translation: Scripture tells this to his discredit, for he intended to postpone the conquest of the land in order to prolong his days, because it is said (above 1:10): “and you shall cause them to inherit it.” In Midrash Tanchuma.
Joshua.translator_note: The quoted wording does not appear in Joshua 1:10 as printed; compare Joshua 1:6, “for thou shalt cause this people to inherit the land.” The reference is given as it is in the Hebrew edition.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: whom the children of Israel smote
Joshua.english_translation: In the days of Moses.
For there was the boundary of the land of the children of Ammon, the end of the border of the land of the children of Ammon; and from there onward the Ammonites ruled.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: and half Gilead, even unto the border of Sihon
Joshua.english_translation: There the border of the dominion of Sihon was, as we said above that half of Gilead was his; and this is the other half, of Og.
In the districts of Dor.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: and there remaineth yet very much land
Joshua.english_translation: Of what I told Abraham, there remained [land] to be inherited which had not been conquered.
Districts; in Old French, *marches* (“borderlands”).
Joshua.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is מרקא״ש; Darmesteter (1909, p. 44) reads *marches*.

Joshua.english_translation: That is the Nile; that is the Brook of Egypt, which is near the boundary of the south-western corner of the land of Israel, as it says in Eleh Masei (Numbers 34:5). And we learn here that Joshua did not conquer in his lifetime the whole southern border, only [that] from the wilderness of Zin — which is the smooth mountain that rises toward Seir — to the Nile, which is the boundary of Gaza mentioned above: from Kadesh-barnea to Gaza.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: unto the border of Ekron northward
Joshua.english_translation: The Ekronite lives by the sea, and extends toward the north more than the others.
It is from the land of the Canaanite that I gave to Abraham.
This is the end, the completion of the border, up to the Great Sea in the west.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: the Gazite, and the Ashdodite, the Ashkelonite
Joshua.english_translation: He counts six lords, but at the beginning calls them five. Rabbi Yonatan said (Hullin 60b): their *idonriki* were five; the important ones were five, for he does not count the Avvim among the important lords. One can also explain: “the five lords of the Philistines” — the Gazite, the Ashdodite, the Ashkelonite, the Gittite and the Ekronite — these are five, and there remained also to be conquered the land of the Avvim, who are not of the Philistines.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: the south; all the land of the Canaanites
Joshua.english_translation: The first verse counted from the southern side, from east to west; and this one counts the breadth of that remaining portion still to be conquered, how far it is from south to north.
This “from the south” is Mearah of the Sidonians, to Aphek, to the border of the Amorites.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: and the land of the Gebalites, and all Lebanon, toward the sunrising
Joshua.english_translation: And on the eastern border there remained to be conquered, in the northern corner, all of Lebanon, from Baal-gad to the end of the border; and in breadth, from east to west, up to the entrance of Hamath. This is the whole northern border, “to the entrance of Hamath,” in the north-western corner, in Eleh Masei (Numbers 34:8).
After your death.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: only divide thou it by lot unto Israel for an inheritance
Joshua.english_translation: And each and every tribe will conquer in time what fell in its lot.
With the first half of Manasseh, the Reubenites and the Gadites took their inheritance.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: from Aroer, that is on the edge of
Joshua.english_translation: He counts, one after another, the whole land beyond the Jordan, and afterward explains the border of each and every tribe: “And Moses gave to the tribe of so-and-so and so-and-so.”

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: of the remnant of the Rephaim
Joshua.english_translation: Whom Chedorlaomer and the kings with him struck down, as it is said (Genesis 14:5): “and smote the Rephaim in Ashteroth-karnaim.”

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: in the mount of the valley
Joshua.english_translation: *Be-turah de-mishra* (Aramaic: in the mountain of the plain).

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: and half the land of the children of Ammon
Joshua.english_translation: Half of what they conquered of the land of the children of Ammon and from Sihon.
The Jordan and its borders: the cities on its bank.
The walled cities.
The cities of the open country, without a wall.
Which they were caused to inherit.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: For the children of Joseph were two tribes
Joshua.english_translation: In place of the tribe of Levi.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: as it was in my heart
Joshua.english_translation: And not as it was in my mouth: the spies were of one counsel, and Caleb was afraid to tell them that he would not say what they said; but when he came [to Moses] he contradicted them. And this is what it says there (Numbers 14:24): “But my servant Caleb, because he had another spirit with him” — for he used to say one thing with the mouth and another in the heart.

We learn that they spent seven years conquering the land: for in the second year Moses sent the spies, thirty-eight remained [years] that they walked in the wilderness, and seven that they conquered; that is forty-five.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: was the greatest man among the Anakim
Joshua.english_translation: The father of Ahiman, Sheshai and Talmai; Arba was his name. Another explanation: [Arba means “four”,] from the name of the father and three sons, for thus it calls them (Numbers 13:22): “the children of Anak.”

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: And the land had rest from war
Joshua.english_translation: This refers back to the first matter: after seven [years], when they had conquered their surroundings, the Amorites submitted and no longer assembled for war against them; therefore they began to engage in the division of the land. And a midrash aggadah: “the greatest man among the Anakim” is Abraham our father; it was he who caused the land to be quiet from war for the forty years that they were delayed in the wilderness, as the reward for their honoring the elder in Kiriath-arba, when they said to him (Genesis 23:6): “Thou art a prince of God among us.”
Close to the border of Edom.
In the area of the southern border of the land of Israel.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: at the uttermost part of the south
Joshua.english_translation: At the end of the entire border.
The southern border of Judah.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: from the end of the Salt Sea
Joshua.english_translation: It is the south-eastern corner of the land of Israel, in Eleh Masei (Numbers 34:3).
Of the sea.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: and it went out to the south of the ascent of Akrabbim
Joshua.english_translation: It does not say “and it went out and turned and drew,” [but uses “went out” for] a place where the line of the border juts outward or bends inward toward the interior, so that it does not run straight; and here it juts outward and comes from the south toward the ascent of Akrabbim, to the south of the ascent of Akrabbim, so the ascent of Akrabbim lies inside the line; and it passed on and came to the west.
[It means] to Zin (*le-Tzin*); and in every word that requires a *lamed* at its beginning, a *heh* is added at its end.

Everything that goes up from the east goes up toward Jerusalem, and from Jerusalem onward it goes down; from here we learned that Jerusalem is higher than all the rest of the land of Israel. And Jerusalem is not mentioned in this border, for it was on the northern border of Judah, as is stated in the passage.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: and went up on the south to Kadesh-barnea
Joshua.english_translation: The line goes to the south of Kadesh-barnea, so Kadesh lies inside the line.
He goes on counting toward the west, until “and the goings out thereof were at the sea.”

The end of the border at the Great Sea, which is the western border of the whole land of Israel. So the border of Judah takes in the whole length of the land of Israel from east to west, and lies in the south of the land of Israel.
A line stretched along the eastern border of Judah.
Which is the south-eastern corner of the land, in Eleh Masei (ibid.).

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: and the border of the north quarter
Joshua.english_translation: The breadth of Judah's border extends only opposite the Dead Sea, up to the place where the Jordan falls into the Dead Sea; for the Jordan also lies on the eastern border of the land of Canaan, as it says in Eleh Masei on the eastern border (Numbers 34:12): “and the border shall go down to the Jordan, and the goings out of it shall be at the Salt Sea,” which is in the corner.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: and the border of the north quarter
Joshua.english_translation: A line of the border stretched along the northern border from east to west, from the tongue of the Dead Sea, from the place where the Jordan falls into it, where we said that the breadth of the eastern border ends; and it went up toward the west to Beth-hoglah, and the line passed north of Beth-arabah, so that Beth-arabah is within the border of Judah, inside the line.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: and the border went up, etc., the stone of Bohan
Joshua.english_translation: Everything that goes toward Jerusalem is “going up.”

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: and the border went up toward Debir from the valley of Achor
Joshua.english_translation: For the valley of Achor was between the stone of Bohan and Debir.

And when it reaches opposite Gilgal, the border widens and the line of the border goes out toward the north to Gilgal, which faces the ascent of Adummim, which is on the south of the brook; so the brook is outside the line, not in Judah's border.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: on the south side of the brook
Joshua.english_translation: It was a valley and a slope without water.

The spring of the launderers. Jonathan translated: *Ein Kitzra* (“the spring of the fuller”); and he calls the launderer *rogel* because he kicks the woolen garments with his feet; in Old French, *folon* (“fuller”).
Joshua.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is פולוש; Darmesteter (1909, p. 44) reads *folon*, “fuller.”

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: And the border went up … the Valley of the son of Hinnom
Joshua.english_translation: It still rises a little, up to Ein Etam, and from there onward it goes down; and this is what our Rabbis of blessed memory said in [the chapter] “Shechitat Kodashim” (Zevachim 54b): they thought to build them at Ein Etam, which is a little higher than Jerusalem.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: to the shoulder of the Jebusite on the south
Joshua.english_translation: So Jerusalem is outside the line, and is not in the border of Judah, but in the border of Benjamin, which is north of Judah.
An expression of “and it turned around in a circle,” like (Isaiah 44:13): “and he marketh it out with the compasses”; and Jonathan translated all of them [as] “*vi-sachar*” (and it turned around).

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: and went out to the cities of mount Ephron
Joshua.english_translation: The line goes out toward the north, and the border widened to the cities of Mount Ephron.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: and the border was drawn to Baalah
Joshua.english_translation: This is not toward the west, but the projection toward the north.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: And the border turned about from Baalah westward
Joshua.english_translation: Now it returns to its first counting, from east to west.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: unto the side of mount Jearim on the north
Joshua.english_translation: For the line was north of Mount Jearim, so Mount Jearim is within the border of Judah, inside the line.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: and the goings out of the border
Joshua.english_translation: The end of the border.
To the Great Sea, which is on the western side.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: according to the commandment of the LORD to Joshua
Joshua.english_translation: As the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Joshua.
After the death of Joshua; for in the days of Joshua Hebron had not yet been taken, as it is said in the Book of Judges (1:20); and it is written here only because of the division [of the land].
Our Rabbis said (Temurah 16a): these are the laws that were forgotten in the days of mourning for Moses, which Othniel the son of Kenaz restored by his dialectic reasoning.
From his mother.
*Ve-itrekhinat* (Aramaic): she bent herself to fall at his feet.
Sustenance.

Dry, like (Genesis 8:13): “the face of the ground was dry,” which [the Targum] translates: *negivu* (dried); in Old French, *sheyka*; “a house emptied of all good” — a person who has nothing but Torah.
Joshua.translator_note: The Old French word is printed שייקא; it is not in Darmesteter's collection. It is probably “dry,” but this is a guess.

Joshua.english_translation: “You have given me”; as (Genesis 37:4): “they could not speak (*daberu*) peaceably” — [meaning] speak to him; (Jeremiah 10:20): “my children have gone forth (*yetza'uni*)” — gone out from me; (1 Kings 19:21): “and boiled their flesh (*uvishel*)” — boiled for them.
Springs.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: And the cities … of the tribe of the children of Judah
Joshua.english_translation: In the border of the tribe of Judah; this is what our Rabbis said (Gittin 7a): Joshua counted only the towns that stood on the borders.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: all the cities are twenty and nine
Joshua.english_translation: But when you count them in detail you find thirty-eight; rather, these extras were taken by the sons of Simeon from the portion of the sons of Judah, and they are mentioned in the inheritance of Simeon: Beer-sheba, Moladah, Hazar-shual, Ezem, Eltolad, Hormah, Ziklag, Ain and Rimmon — these are the nine extras counted here.

But in detail [there are] fifteen. I say that Tappuah and Enam are one, and this is its meaning: “Tappuah and its spring (*ein*),” which is the En-tappuah mentioned in the inheritance of Manasseh: “to the inhabitants of En-tappuah.”

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: and the Great Sea and its border
Joshua.english_translation: Islands (*nisin*) in the sea, which are called *isles* in Old French.
Joshua.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is אלשי״ש; Darmesteter (1909, p. 44) reads *isles*, “islands.”

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: the children of Judah could not drive them out
Joshua.english_translation: We learned in the Sifrei: Rabbi Joshua ben Korhah says they were able, but they were not permitted because of the oath that Abraham swore to Abimelech. And this “Jebusite” was not [named] for the nation, but for the Tower of David that was in Jerusalem, whose name was Jebus; and the inhabitants of that district were of the Philistines; and when the sons of Judah conquered Jerusalem they did not dispossess the inhabitants of that district.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: and the lot of the children of Joseph came forth
Joshua.english_translation: On the northern border of the completion of Joshua's conquest the lot fell to them, as it is written below: “and the children of Joseph shall abide in their border on the north”; and much of the land was between the children of Judah and the children of Joseph, which the other tribes took after them (meaning: between them), as we find with the tribe of Benjamin (below 18:11): “and the border of their lot came forth between the children of Judah and the children of Joseph.”

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: from the Jordan by Jericho, unto the waters of Jericho on the east
Joshua.english_translation: The border began at the east.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: the wilderness, going up from Jericho
Joshua.english_translation: The border goes up from Jericho into the wilderness, and goes to the west, to Beth-el.
In the east it begins from Ataroth-addar, and from there its breadth of territory [runs] to Beth-horon; that is its breadth.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: And the border went out westward
Joshua.english_translation: Its length was toward the west, to Michmethath; the line runs north of Michmethath.
The breadth of the territory spreads toward the north, and the line goes out, in its projection, east of Taanath-shiloh.

And the border passed Taanath-shiloh, and the line passed east of Janoah — all this is the projection of the breadth — until “and it goeth out at the Jordan”; and there is a city named Tappuah; and from there the line turns to the measure of the length of the border, westward to the brook of Kanah.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: and the cities that were separated
Joshua.english_translation: And this too is still of the inheritance of Ephraim: they had cities separated from their territory and enclosed within the inheritance of the sons of Manasseh.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: to Machir the firstborn of Manasseh
Joshua.english_translation: Therefore he took first, in the days of Moses, on the other side of the Jordan; and Gilead and Bashan were his.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: and there fell ten portions to Manasseh
Joshua.english_translation: Six, for the six fathers' houses counted above, and four for the daughters of Zelophehad — not that each was a fathers' house by herself, but they took four portions: the portion of their father, who was among those who left Egypt (for the land was divided according to the number of those who left Egypt); and he shared with his brothers in the estate of Hepher his father, who was also among those who left Egypt; and since he was the firstborn he took two portions; and they also had the portion of their father's brother, who died in the wilderness without sons, and they took an inheritance in his portion. So our Rabbis said in Bava Batra (118a). And Scripture was not required to tell us the number of the daughters' portions except to teach that they took a firstborn's portion, and to let us know that the land of Israel was an inheritance held by them from their fathers; for otherwise the firstborn does not take a double share in what is yet to come into possession as he does in what is already held.
Which is across the Jordan; it belonged to the remaining sons of Manasseh.
The villages and hamlets; and Tappuah itself, the city, belonged to the sons of Ephraim.
On the border of Manasseh, at the end of its border.
From Tappuah to the brook of Kanah, they belonged to Ephraim, within the cities of Manasseh.
Ephraim took its portion on the south, toward the land that is between the children of Judah and the other tribes.
Manasseh took toward the north.

*Talata pelakhin* (Aramaic: three districts); and the “three heights” mentioned here belonged to Dor and to En-dor, as is said above in this book (12:23): “the king of Dor in the heights of Dor,” and in another verse it says (above 11:2): “in the heights of Dor on the west”; and here it says thus: “and the inhabitants of Dor and her towns” — the three heights that belonged to it.
“And he was willing”: he consented.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: And the children of Joseph spoke
Joshua.english_translation: The tribe of Manasseh.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: forasmuch as the Lord hath blessed me hitherto
Joshua.english_translation: Until you see that our number increased from the first census to the second by twenty thousand five hundred, the number of “*koh*” by gematria [*kaf* = twenty thousand, *heh* = five hundred]. In the first census you find for Manasseh, in the Book of Numbers (1:34): thirty-two thousand two hundred; and in [the portion] Pinehas (Numbers 26:34): fifty-two thousand seven hundred. Another explanation: “until hitherto” (*ad koh*) — a blessing was said to Abraham (Genesis 15:5): “So (*koh*) shall thy seed be” — it has been fulfilled in me. And by its plain sense: *ad asher ad koh* means “until such a degree, as you see.”

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: If thou be a great people
Joshua.english_translation: You have the strength to cut down forests and clear [the land], in the manner called *essarter* in Old French, and there you will build cities.
Joshua.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is אישרטי״ר; Darmesteter (1909, p. 44) reads *aisartér*, “to clear land.”

Joshua.english_translation: An expression of cutting, like (Ezekiel 23:47): “and they shall hew them down with their swords”; in Old French, *essarter*.
Joshua.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is אישרטרא״ש; see Darmesteter (1909, p. 44).

Joshua.english_translation: Pressed, cramped.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: The hill will not be enough for us
Joshua.english_translation: For it is too narrow for us, as you said.
Will not suffice.

And as for what you say, to go up to the forest and conquer in the land of the Perizzite and the Rephaim — that Canaanite is a strong people, and has chariots of iron. Do not wonder if they call the Perizzite and Rephaim “Canaanite,” for they were all sons of Canaan.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: but the hill-country shall be thine
Joshua.english_translation: That of which I said to you, “Go up for yourself to the forest.”

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: it is a forest, thou shalt cut it down
Joshua.english_translation: For it is a forest and is fit only for a numerous people; they will clear it and open it up.
You, who are a numerous people.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: and the goings out thereof shall be thine; for thou shalt drive out the Canaanite
Joshua.english_translation: Because you are a numerous people.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: though they have chariots of iron
Joshua.english_translation: And none of the other tribes is fit to fight against him.

And you have the ability, and you will drive him out. And our Rabbis explained (Bava Batra 118a): “Go up to the forest” — hide yourselves in the forests, so that the evil eye will not have power over you.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: and set up the tent of meeting there
Joshua.english_translation: That which they made in the wilderness; and it had no roof there, but a house of stones below and curtains above; so we learned in [the chapter] “Shechitat Kodashim” (Zevachim 54b).

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: and the land was subdued before them
Joshua.english_translation: Once the Tabernacle was set up, the land was easy to conquer before them.

For Reuben, Gad and half the tribe of Manasseh had already received their inheritance in the days of Moses across the Jordan, and in the land of Canaan the lot had already fallen to Judah, Ephraim and half the tribe of Manasseh — that makes five tribes.
Slackening (Aramaic: *mitrashlin*).
For each tribe of the seven.

Into seven portions, not equally but according to the tribes that were fit for their portion: to the many according to their number, and to the few according to their fewness, as it is said (Numbers 26:54): “To the many thou shalt give the more inheritance, and to the few thou shalt give the less inheritance,” etc.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: and they shall divide it into seven parts
Joshua.english_translation: That which was already conquered and that which is yet to be conquered.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: Judah shall abide in his border on the south
Joshua.english_translation: In the land of Israel, where the whole southern border fell to him by lot.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: and the house of Joseph … on the north
Joshua.english_translation: North of what has already been conquered; and there is still much to conquer along the border from Baal-gad to the entrance of Hamath, which is near Mount Hor on the northern border. The seven tribes shall divide that which lies between Judah and Joseph, and that which is yet to be conquered.
And I will throw, like (Exodus 15:4): “he hath cast (*yarah*) into the sea.”

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: And their border on the north side
Joshua.english_translation: And the northern boundary of theirs began from the Jordan, for the border begins in the east; and it went up to the shoulder of Jericho on the north, and went up from there toward the west, to the side of Jericho, and the line is drawn on the north of Jericho. So Jericho is inside the line, in the portion of Benjamin.
To the wilderness belonging to Beth-aven.
Toward the west.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: to Luz, to the shoulder of Luz southward, which is Beth-el
Joshua.english_translation: Which Jacob named (Genesis 28:19). This is not the Beth-el near Ai, for it says in the border of Joseph (above 16:2): “and it went out from Beth-el to Luz,” so we learn that there were two [places]. Luz was not in the portion of Benjamin, for the line of the border lies inside [i.e., south of] Luz, as it says (v. 13): “to the shoulder of Luz southward” — the line runs on the south of Luz, so Luz is outside the line, in the inheritance of the children of Joseph; and Beth-el was in the portion of Benjamin, as it is written below (v. 22) in the account.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: And the border was drawn and turned about on the west side southward
Joshua.english_translation: At Ataroth-addar the northern length ends, from east to west. From there the line turns to the western border of Benjamin, going southward from north to south: the western line from the mountain that lies before Beth-horon southward, from the mountain on the south of Beth-horon. From there the western-northern corner of Benjamin began, and the line comes from north to south.

Its south-western corner [reaches] to Kiriath-jearim of Judah. So the breadth of the border of Benjamin takes up the whole breadth of the land between Judah and Ephraim: its southern border [touches] the northern border of Judah, and there was Jerusalem, as is said below in the account; therefore the two tribes had a share in it. The northern border of Benjamin and the southern border of Ephraim touch each other, and there was Shiloh, in the portion of Ephraim, as it is said (Psalms 78:60, 67): “So that He forsook the tabernacle of Shiloh,” etc., “and He refused the tent of Joseph, and chose not the tribe of Ephraim”; and Benjamin too had a share in it. And so we learned in [the chapter] “Shechitat Kodashim” (Zevachim 54b): in three places the Divine Presence rested for Israel — Shiloh, Nob and the Eternal House — and in all of them it rested only in the portion of Benjamin.
The western side, from Ataroth-addar to Kiriath-jearim.

The border (another reading: the side) south of Benjamin, which is the north of Judah. All the boundaries counted here are counted on the north of Judah, and wherever it is written here “and went down,” in Judah it is written “and went up,” because here he counts from west to east, and there he counts from east to west.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: and the border went out westward
Joshua.english_translation: To a sea; and I do not know which sea it is.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: to the bay of the Salt Sea northward
Joshua.english_translation: On the north of the bay; so the whole bay is in the portion of Judah.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: at the south end of the Jordan
Joshua.english_translation: The place where the Jordan falls into the Salt Sea; it was counted as the north-eastern corner of Judah, and here it is counted as the south-eastern corner of Benjamin.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: and the Jordan bounded it on the east side
Joshua.english_translation: The Jordan was the eastern boundary of Benjamin, for the Jordan runs along the breadth of all its border on the east.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: and Zela-ha-eleph, and the Jebusite, which is Jerusalem
Joshua.english_translation: Each one a city by itself; and likewise Gibeath and Kiriath — five cities in this verse.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: and the second lot came forth
Joshua.english_translation: Second to Benjamin, for the lot of Benjamin was the first for the seven tribes, of whom Joshua said to his emissaries, “and ye shall divide it into seven parts,” since Judah and Joseph had already taken, as is said there (above 18:5): “Judah shall abide in his border on the south,” etc. From here on he counts seven lots in succession.
[More] than was fitting for them.

I say that it is an expression for *kislayim* (loins, flanks), *flancs* in Old French: not in its height nor in its lower part, but on its slope and near its middle, close to the back side and away from its front side, in the manner that the flanks stand on an animal. And where it says (below v. 34): “Aznoth-tabor,” it is near its top, in the place of the ears.
Joshua.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is פלנק״ש; Darmesteter (1909, p. 44) reads *flancs*, “the flanks.”

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: eastward toward the sunrising to Gath-hepher
Joshua.english_translation: East of Gath-hepher, the city of Jonah the son of Amittai (2 Kings 14:25).
Now the name of the city is Eth-kazin.
It is attached to Neah, that is, from there the border was drawn to Neah. And so Jonathan translated: “and goes out to Rimmon, and from there turns round to Neah.”
Cities called *kerikhen* are called *tokfa* (Aramaic: strength, stronghold).
Joshua.translator_note: The printed word כריכן is unclear to me; the translation is literal and uncertain.

Joshua.english_translation: An expression for “rock” (*tzur*).
From the boundary of Achzib, from the lot of Chezib.
To Naphtali belonged Ziddim, Zer.
It was Judah's (above 15:33), and the lot of the sons of Dan fell next to them.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: and the border of the children of Dan went out beyond them
Joshua.english_translation: Here they took a part, and a lot fell to them also in another place, far from their border, with other tribes lying in between.
Afterward, in the days of Othniel the son of Kenaz, and in the days of the idol of Micah, as is said in the Book of Judges (18:2).
This is Laish, mentioned in the Book of Judges (18:14).
Gave as an inheritance.

If he is released from exile, he shall be released; and if he is condemned to exile, he shall return to his city of refuge (Numbers 35:25), “and he shall dwell therein until the death of the high priest.”

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: And beyond the Jordan at Jericho eastward, they assigned
Joshua.english_translation: In the days of Moses, as it is said (Deuteronomy 4:43): “Bezer in the wilderness,” etc.
The designation: those designated for this purpose.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: And the rest of the children of Kohath
Joshua.english_translation: These are the sons of Moses, and the sons of Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: out of the families of the tribe of Ephraim
Joshua.english_translation: These cities fell to them from the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Ephraim, for from each and every tribe they took, as it is said (Numbers 35:8): “from the many ye shall take many, and from the few ye shall take few; every one according to his inheritance which he inheriteth shall give of his cities unto the Levites.”
Because above he did not mention the names of the cities that were given to them, and below he spells out their names; therefore he said: “which are mentioned by name.”
And in Chronicles (1 Chronicles 6:45) [it is written]: “and Alemeth,” which is Bahurim, for Jonathan (2 Samuel 3:16) translates it “Alemoth.”
Two thousand cubits in every direction.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: Moreover when Joshua sent them away
Joshua.english_translation: To the half-tribe of Manasseh, as when he sent the children of Reuben and Gad.

The children of Reuben and Gad. Some interpret: “with your brethren” who remained to guard the cities with the women and little ones, and did not cross the Jordan with the vanguard — they too took a share of the spoil.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: to go up against them to war
Joshua.english_translation: Because the high places had been forbidden once the Tabernacle was fixed at Shiloh.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: if the land of your possession be unclean
Joshua.english_translation: In that the Holy One, blessed be He, did not choose to cause His Presence to rest in it.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: neither rebel against us (ve-otanu al tamrodu)
Joshua.english_translation: Like “and against us (*uvanu*) do not rebel.”
He will exact punishment from him.

From the anxiety of fear of a matter [of reproach] we did [this], as it explains: “lest your children say to our children tomorrow” — to reproach our children when they go to offer in the tabernacle of Shiloh — they might say: What have you to do with the Lord? For has He not set the Jordan as a border between us and you? This was our anxiety and we did [it]. Every *dagah* in Scripture is an expression of fear, like (Jeremiah 38:19): “I am afraid (*do'eg*) of the Jews” — said by Zedekiah.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: but it shall be a witness
Joshua.english_translation: That we have not removed ourselves from the law of the altar.
And the children of Israel gave thanks before the Lord (the Aramaic rendering of Jonathan: *ve-odiyu kadam Adonai bnei Yisrael*).

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: And the children of Reuben and the children of Gad called the altar—: ‘for it is a witness
Joshua.english_translation: This is one of the abbreviated verses, and one word must be added: “and the children of Reuben and the children of Gad called the altar ‘Witness.’”

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: Behold, I have allotted unto you
Joshua.english_translation: By lot, as an inheritance.
To be conquered.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: and scourges in your sides (ule-shotet be-tzidchem)
Joshua.english_translation: They will roam for plunder and spoil round about you.

An expression for camps [or encircling], and so (Ezekiel 23:24): “and they shall come against thee with *hatzen*,” like the *tzinnah* (shield) that surrounds a man on three sides, as it is said (Psalms 5:13): “as with a shield wilt Thou encompass him with favor” — surround him — like (1 Samuel 23:26): “and Saul and his men were compassing David and his men”; *otrim* means surrounding.
Joshua.translator_note: The printed phrase “an expression for camps” (לשון מחנות) is translated literally; the sense is uncertain.

Joshua.english_translation: Lacking a *heh*: how many quarrels and trials I made with him, before I gave him seed.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: and brought the sea upon them
Joshua.english_translation: Upon each and every one of them: if an individual fled so as not to enter the sea, a wave of the sea pursued him and caught him.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: and the men of Jericho fought against you, the Amorite, and the Perizzite
Joshua.english_translation: All seven idolatrous nations are mentioned here, because Jericho stood on the frontier and was the bolt and lock of the land of Israel; the mighty men of valor of all seven nations gathered into it.

In most places every expression of lordship is in the plural, as (Genesis 42:30): “the lord (*adonei*, plural form) of the land”; (Genesis 39:20): “Joseph's master (*adonei*)”; (Exodus 22:14): “if its owner (*ba'alav*) be with it”; (2 Samuel 7:23): “whom God (*Elohim*) went to redeem,” because this name is a name of authority.

Joshua saw that in the days of Ezekiel they would again protest and say (Ezekiel 20:32): “We will be as the nations”; therefore he made it heavy on them now, and for that reason they were answered in the days of Ezekiel (vv. 32–33): “And that which cometh into your mind shall not be at all,” etc., “As I live, surely with a mighty hand,” etc. [He meant: ] You already accepted it upon yourselves in the days of Joshua, and do not say that what we accepted in the days of Moses we did in order to enter the land; behold, in the days of Joshua you had already entered, and you accepted it.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: and set him a statute and an ordinance in Shechem
Joshua.english_translation: He arranged for them there the statutes of the Torah, and they accepted them upon themselves.

Jonathan translated: “And Joshua wrote these words and hid them in the book of the Torah of the Lord.” In tractate Makkot (11a) the Amoraim disagree: one says these are the eight verses (Deuteronomy 34:5–12) from “So Moses died” to “in the sight of all Israel,” for the scroll of the Torah was lacking, and he completed it; and the other says that he wrote this section of the cities of refuge in his book as they were written in the Torah scroll.

*Tachot alta* (Aramaic): it is the doorpost of the entrance, as it is said (1 Kings 6:31): “the lintel and the doorposts were a fifth part,” and one measure for the porch. And some say it is the oak that was near Shechem, as it is written of Jacob (Genesis 35:4): “and Jacob hid them under the oak.”

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: that was by the sanctuary of the LORD
Joshua.english_translation: Because they had brought the Ark there, as is said above (v. 1): “and they presented themselves before God.”

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: this stone shall be a witness against us
Joshua.english_translation: [Jonathan translated:] “Behold, this stone shall be to us like the two tablets of stone that endure, for we made it for a witness; for the words that are written on it are corresponding to all the words of the Lord that He spoke with us.” And it can also be interpreted according to its plain sense: for it heard the words that I spoke to you, in the mission of the Omnipresent.

That is its name; and in another place (Judges 2:9) He calls it Timnath-heres, because they set up the image of the sun on his (Joshua's) grave, to say: this is the one who made the sun stand still, and everyone who passes by it says: Alas for this one who did such a great thing and died. Some say its name is Timnath-heres, and why was it called Timnath-serah? Because its fruits stink (*mas'richin*) from the abundance of their fat.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: on the north of the mountain of Gaash
Joshua.english_translation: It teaches that the mountain shook upon them to kill them, because they did not eulogize him properly.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: that prolonged their days after Joshua
Joshua.english_translation: Days they prolonged; years they did not prolong, for they were punished.
From Shechem they stole him; to Shechem they returned him.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: in the Hill of Phinehas his son
Joshua.english_translation: From where did Phinehas have a share in the land? He inherited it from his wife.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: Now it came to pass after the death of Moses
Joshua.english_translation: Connected to the order of the Torah, which ends with the passing of Moses, and this is connected to it.

And if he were alive, I would desire him. And our Rabbis expounded it (Temurah 16a) concerning three thousand laws that were forgotten in the days of mourning for Moses: Joshua came and asked; the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: “Moses My servant is dead,” and the Torah is called by his name; to tell you: it is not possible; go and trouble them with war.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: Every place that the sole of your foot shall tread upon
Joshua.english_translation: Likewise was it said to Moses, and we learned in the Sifrei (Ekev): If [the verse comes] to teach about the borders of the land of Israel, it already says “from the wilderness and this Lebanon”; if so, why is it said “whereon the sole of your foot shall tread”? [To include] even outside the Land: when you conquer the Land, whatever you conquer outside the Land will be holy and will be yours.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: From the wilderness, and this Lebanon
Joshua.english_translation: It is the wilderness of Kadesh, the wilderness of Zin that is by Edom, which was at the south-eastern corner, and by way of there they entered the Land, as it is said (Numbers 20:16): “and, behold, we are in Kadesh,” etc.; and how [do we know] that it is at the south-eastern [corner]? As it is said (ibid. 34:3): “and your south side shall be from the wilderness of Zin along by the side of Edom.”

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: even unto the great river, the river Euphrates
Joshua.english_translation: This is its breadth, from south to north.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: all the land of the Hittites
Joshua.english_translation: Included in this.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: and unto the Great Sea toward the going down of the sun
Joshua.english_translation: Its length, from east to west.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: Be strong and of good courage
Joshua.english_translation: In the way of the land [i.e., in worldly matters], as it says: “for thou shalt cause this people to inherit.”

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: Only be thou strong and very courageous
Joshua.english_translation: In the Torah, as it says: “that thou mayest observe to do according to all the law.”
Succeed.
The book of Deuteronomy was before him.
Joshua.translator_note: Hebrew: *sefer Mishneh Torah* (the book of Deuteronomy).

Joshua.english_translation: And thou shalt consider it: and you shall reflect upon it; every *higayon* in the Torah is in the heart, as you say (Psalms 19:15): “and the meditation (*higayon*) of my heart before Thee”; (Isaiah 33:18): “thy heart shall meditate (*yehgeh*) terror.”

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: Have not I commanded thee? Be strong and of good courage
Joshua.english_translation: In war, as it is said: “be not affrighted, neither be thou dismayed”; and where did He command him? In the days of Moses, as it is said (Deuteronomy 31:23): “And He gave Joshua the son of Nun a charge,” etc.
On the day that the days of weeping and mourning for Moses ended.

Everything needed for the road, and their weapons for war — he told them to prepare; for if you say [it means] food and drink, behold they were sustained by the manna in their vessels until the sixteenth of Nisan, and so it says (below 5:12): “And the manna ceased on the morrow” (from my teacher).
Joshua.translator_note: The closing words מפי רבי are rendered literally (“from my teacher”); I do not identify who is meant.

Joshua.english_translation: At the end of three days: while you are here three days, and afterward you shall cross.
The eastern side of the Jordan.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: neither did there remain any more spirit in any man
Joshua.english_translation: Even to lie with a woman. They said: There was no prince or ruler who had not come to Rahab the harlot; and she was ten years old when Israel went out of Egypt, and she was a harlot all forty years (Zevachim 116b).

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: Then she let them down by a cord through the window
Joshua.english_translation: By that same cord and window the adulterers used to go up to her. She said: Master of the world, with these I sinned, with these forgive me (Zevachim, ibid.).

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: and carry them over with you
Joshua.english_translation: As Moses commanded (Deuteronomy 27) to build for themselves an altar on Mount Ebal and to write upon them the words of the Torah; and on that very day they came to Mount Ebal and built the altar with them and offered burnt-offerings and peace-offerings, and ate and drank, and they gathered them up and came and lodged in Gilgal.
Joshua.translator_note: The Hebrew verb וקפלו is rendered “gathered them up”; its exact sense here (literally “folded”) is not certain.

Joshua.english_translation: In Gilgal, for this memorial.

As we learned in tractate Sotah (34a): while they were still in the Jordan, Joshua said to them: Know why you are crossing the Jordan: in order that you shall dispossess all the inhabitants of the land, etc.

As its Targum: “sharp scalpels”; and so (Psalms 89:44): “Yea, Thou turnest back the edge of his sword” (*tzur charbo*) — when the sharp edge turns to the sides and does not cut well; and so (Isaiah 54:17): “No weapon that is formed (*kli yotzer*) against thee.”

They had already circumcised on the night of their departure from Egypt, a great congregation together, and this is the second time; for all the forty years that they were in the wilderness the north wind did not blow for them, and they had no day suitable for circumcising, as we learned in Yevamot (71b). And our Rabbis said (ibid.): “the second time” — this is *periah* (uncovering), which was not given to Abraham our father.

By a divine word he circumcised them. He said to them: Do you think to inherit the land uncircumcised? Was it not said so to Abraham (Genesis 17:9): “and thou shalt keep My covenant,” etc., (ibid. v. 8): “and I will give unto thee, and to thy seed after thee, the land of thy sojournings”?

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: all the people that came forth
Joshua.english_translation: Not one of them was here, for they all had died, and they [those who came out] were circumcised, as it is said: “for all the people that came out were circumcised.”

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: And their children, whom He raised up in their stead
Joshua.english_translation: And their children, whom He raised up in their stead, are those born in the wilderness; those Joshua circumcised.

I have removed the reproach of Egypt, for they used to say: “See that evil is before your faces” — there is a star whose name is “Ra'ah” [evil], and it is a sign of blood; we see it over you in the wilderness. And that is what Moses said in the wilderness (Exodus 32:12): “Wherefore should the Egyptians speak, saying: For evil (*be-ra'ah*) did He bring them out” — and they do not know that it is the blood of circumcision. And when they circumcised in the days of Joshua and that blood came, that reproach was removed — for as yet the mixed multitude that went up with them were counting it against them. So expounded Rabbi Moses the Preacher.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: on the morrow after the passover
Joshua.english_translation: The day of the waving of the Omer, when they first offered an omer; and from the seventh of Adar, when Moses died, the manna ceased, and they were sustained until now from the manna in their vessels that they had gathered on the seventh of Adar, as it is said (Exodus 16:35): “they did eat the manna forty years” — but is it not forty years less thirty days, for the beginning of the descent of the manna was on the fifteenth of Iyar? Say, then, that in the cake that Israel brought out of Egypt they tasted the taste of manna.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: neither had the children of Israel manna any more
Joshua.english_translation: Therefore: “and they did eat of the produce of the land”; if they had had manna, they would not have eaten of the grain, for the manna was pleasant for them. A parable: one says to a child: Why are you eating barley bread? Because I have no wheat bread. Therefore it is said: “and there was no more manna,” etc.

To your aid, for no man can fight against it and take it, to bring the wall down; but in the days of Moses your master I came and he did not desire Me, as it is said (Exodus 33:15): “If Thy presence go not,” etc.
Israel, who is a host (*tzava*) to the Lord; and it was Michael, as it is said (Daniel 10:21): “Michael your prince.”
It was the Sabbath.

Joshua.english_lemma_JPS: The Mighty One, God, the Lord
Joshua.english_translation: The God of all the gods is the Lord, who knows that it was not in rebellion, etc.; and when he doubled, saying “Elohim” twice, [it means] in this world and in the world to come.
They said it toward the Divine Presence.

Judges.english_translation: Jonathan translated: “After they had sinned, they were not able to drive out the inhabitants of the plain.”

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: and the Jebusite … dwelt in Jerusalem
Judges.english_translation: There was a district (*machoz*) in Jerusalem whose name was Jebusi (Pirkei deRabbi Eliezer 36), and they were of the sons of Abimelech, and he did not dispossess them because of the oath (Genesis 21:23–24) until David came (2 Samuel 5:6–7), because his grandson was still alive; for he had sworn to him, and to his son, and to his grandson.

Which fell in their lot (Joshua 16:1). And although the idol of Micah was with them — for Micah was of the tribe of Ephraim (Judges 17:1) — it is said here “and the Lord was with them.” This is what Daniel said (Daniel 9:7): “To Thee, O Lord, belongeth righteousness, but unto us confusion of face.”

[Done] through others. (Targum:) “and they sent men who go in.” “And they shall spy out the land” (Numbers 13:2) is said of the spies themselves; but of those who sent spies it is said “and they spied out” (*vayatiru*).
For they used to enter it by way of the cave, and a *luz* (nut) tree stood at the mouth of the cave, and they entered by way of the *luz* into the cave.
Judges.translator_note: Darmesteter (1909, p. 44) records at Judges 1:24 an Old French gloss *coldre* (“coudrier,” hazel tree) for the *luz*; the Sefaria text of this comment does not show that word.

Judges.english_translation: With his finger.
Because fine nuts grew in it: *coldre* in Old French.
Judges.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is קולדר״א; Darmesteter (1909, p. 44, Judges 1:24, note: “Lire: coldre”) reads *coldre*, which he renders *coudrier* (hazel tree).

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: which is the name thereof unto this day
Judges.english_translation: Sennacherib did not disturb it, and Nebuchadnezzar did not destroy it.
Scripture tells of his disgrace: that they began to trespass against the Holy One, blessed be He, who commanded them (Numbers 33:52): “and ye shall drive out all the inhabitants of the land,” etc.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: and when (vechi) the Lord raised up
Judges.english_translation: A present-tense form: and whenever He raised up judges for them, the Lord was with the judge, etc.
That He relented toward them concerning the evil; so Jonathan translated.
On account of their groaning, which went up before Him on account of their enemies.
They did not let anything be admonished [or: convinced] for all that came upon them.
The *heh* is vocalized with a *chataf patach*, because it is an expression of question and test.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: only that the generations … might know
Judges.english_translation: Only for this one thing He left them: that the generations of the children of Israel to come may know and consider what sin causes; for now they need to be taught war.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: at the least such as before knew nothing thereof
Judges.english_translation: Those who used to stand to serve the Lord.
These wars and their stratagems, and they had no need of them.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: the five lords of the Philistines
Judges.english_translation: These are the nations which He left in order to test.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: And the spirit of the LORD came upon him
Judges.english_translation: Rabbi Tanchuma expounded (Midrash Tanchuma, Shemot 20): He looked at them [or: into them]; for the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moses in Egypt (Exodus 3:7): “I have surely seen the affliction of My people.” What are these two “seeings”? He said to him: I see that they will err with the calf, and nevertheless “I have seen the affliction of My people.” This Othniel expounded: he said: whether they are righteous or guilty, it is upon Him to save them.
Jericho.

Jonathan translated: *gever gamid yad yeminei*. Every *gamid* is an Aramaic expression: something contracted from illness, *retrait* in Old French; he had no control over his right hand. And in the Hebrew language, *itter* is “stopped up,” as (Psalms 69:16): “neither let the pit shut (*ta'ater*) her mouth upon me” — stopped up in his right hand, so that he had no control over it.
Judges.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is ריטרי״ט; Darmesteter (1909, p. 44) reads *rétréit* (re + *tractum*), “contracted.”

Judges.english_translation: A shortened cubit; and in the language of Ashkenaz (German): *doimen lang*; and in Old French: *gaskorte*.
Judges.translator_note: The printed Hebrew spellings are דוימ״ן לאנ״ג and גשקור״ט. Darmesteter (1909, p. 45) lists for the German gloss “petite coudée” (a small cubit) with the form דומילנא (*Domilane*) in manuscript A, and for the French gloss reads *waskorte*, “from *was* (very) and *korte*, that is, very short.” The printed form of the German gloss differs from the form Darmesteter records.

Judges.english_translation: Since he is a master of his left hand, he would grasp it with his left.
(Targum:) *patim* (fat).
He turned back and accompanied the company of Israel who had come with him to bear the present, and accompanied them to Gilgal.
Alone.
The place where they hew out stones from the mountain; and so Jonathan translated: *min machtzevaya* (from the quarries). And he came to Eglon and said to him…
Eglon said: Quiet everyone away from me. And Jonathan translated *has* as *salik* (remove), remove every man; and nevertheless *has* is an expression of “be silent.”
(Targum:) in the upper chamber of the summer house, which was open to the air and cool.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: I have a message from God unto thee
Judges.english_translation: And you must stand.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: And he arose out of his seat
Judges.english_translation: For this he merited that Ruth came forth from him.
It is the iron into which the blade is fixed, which is called *halt* in Old French; it is what keeps the sword fixed at the mouth of its sheath.
