Judges.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is הול״ט; Darmesteter (1909, p. 45) reads *halt* and renders it “la garde” (the hilt-guard), from the German *halten* (compare English *hilt*).

Judges.english_translation: It is the sharp part (*shanun*), which is called *brant* in Old French, and in Old French also *lame*.
Judges.translator_note: Old French glosses: the printed Hebrew spellings are ברונ״ט and למ״א; Darmesteter (1909, p. 45) lists *brant*, *bront* and *lame*, “la lame” (the blade), and says these words all have the same meaning.

Judges.english_translation: Its fat: for he was very fat, and it covered the whole length of the sword.

Jonathan translated: *venafak okhlei shefikh*. He made them two words, and the *shin* serves both: *vayetze ha-peres* (“and the dung came out”), *shedonah* (“poured out”), by pouring. *Shafakh* (“he poured”) is *shada*, like his Targum.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: and Ehud went forth through the porch (ha-misderonah)
Judges.english_translation: From the upper chamber to the porch; Jonathan translated: *le-achsadra*.
With a key.
Ehud went out, and Eglon's servants came.
(Targum:) *avid tzorkhei* (he is doing his needs): these are the large orifices.
Judges.translator_note: The last phrase (הם נקבים הגדולים) is translated literally.

Judges.english_translation: Till delay, that is, a long time.
Fled, *eschamuçer* in Old French.
Judges.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is אישקימוצייר; Darmesteter (1909, p. 45) reads *eschamuçer*, “il s'enfuit” (he fled).

Judges.english_translation: Like (Song of Songs 1:12) “while the king was at his table”; (ibid. 2:7) “that ye awaken not, nor stir up love, until it please” — while both of us desire it.

A forest, thin and thick, called *brosse* in Old French; and it is good for hiding. And there is much in the Order Zeraim where the thin branches of trees are called *se'ar*: (Kilayim 4:9) “he turns over the *se'ar*”; (Peah 2:3) “and if the *se'ar* was crushing.”
Judges.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is ברוצ״ש; Darmesteter (1909, p. 45) reads *brosse* and renders it “forêt de broussailles petites et épaisses” (forest of small and thick brushwood).

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: And it came to pass, when he was come
Judges.english_translation: That he crossed the Jordan and came to his place in the land of Canaan.

Which was in the land of Canaan on the western side of the Jordan; and the land of Moab was across the Jordan, on its east. Since they ruled over Israel and crossed the Jordan, they took possession of Jericho, as is written above (v. 13): “and they set their lords and rulers over Israel.”
Judges.translator_note: The quotation “and they set their lords and rulers over Israel” does not appear in Judges 3:13 of the Hebrew text (verse 13 ends “and they possessed the city of palm-trees”). It is translated as printed.

Judges.english_translation: To kill all of Moab that is across our Jordan.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: and took the fords of the Jordan
Judges.english_translation: So that Moab could not cross over to flee and return to their land.
(Targum:) *kol gever eimtan* (every man of awe).
It is the *dorban*, the *mardea*, *aguillon* in Old French.
Judges.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is אגויילו״ן; Darmesteter (1909, p. 45) reads *aguillon*, modern *aiguillon* (goad).

Judges.english_translation: By the hand of Moses (Deuteronomy 20:17): “but thou shalt utterly destroy them”; so it is taught in the Mekhilta (Bo 12).

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: and he went up at his feet (be-raglav)
Judges.english_translation: With him.

(Targum:) *mishar agnaya*: a level place of marshes (*bitzim*), *maresk* in Old French; and it is *agnei gevim*, a kind of hollows where the waters gather: (Kiddushin 61a) “the *agnei* of the earth are called…”
Judges.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is מריש״ק; Darmesteter (1909, p. 45) reads *marésk*, the old form of *marais* (marsh). The Talmud quotation אגני דארעא מקרון is translated literally and its meaning is uncertain.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: from Harosheth-ha-goiim unto the brook Kishon
Judges.english_translation: He summoned them to go to the brook Kishon from Harosheth-ha-goiim, where he dwelt.
Jonathan translated: *begunka*; and Rav Hai explained (Shabbat 51a): *gunka* — *glufkarin*, *cote* in Old French.
Judges.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is קוט״א; Darmesteter (1909, p. 46) reads *cot* (modern *cotte*) and renders it “manteau” (cloak). The word גלופקרין is transliterated as printed.

Judges.english_translation: For milk makes the body heavy, so as to fall asleep.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: Stand in the door of the tent
Judges.english_translation: Bestir yourself in the matter. And some interpret: *amod* is like *la'amod* (to stand).
*Chevil* in Old French, which is driven into the ground with the lower edges of the tent to stretch it.
Judges.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is קבילי״ל; Darmesteter (1909, p. 46) reads *cheville* (peg), “as in modern French.”

Judges.english_translation: (Targum:) *arzefta*, *martel* in Old French.
Judges.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is מרטי״ל; Darmesteter (1909, p. 46) reads *martel*, “le marteau” (the hammer).

Judges.english_translation: (Targum:) *baraz* (secretly), *charash* (silently).

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: and it pierced through into the ground
Judges.english_translation: (Targum:) “and it was fixed in the earth.”
(Targum:) *be-tzidigeih* (in his temple), *nile timpie* in Old French; “and she drove it through his temple into the ground.”
Judges.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is ניל״ה טימפי״ה. Darmesteter (1909, p. 46) lists *tenple*, to be read *tempora*, the old form of *tempe* (temple of the head). The first word, ניל״ה, I cannot explain.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: for the leaders taking the lead in Israel, for the people offering themselves willingly
Judges.english_translation: When breaches came upon Israel, in which their enemies broke through them because they forsook the Lord, and the people offered themselves to return in repentance: from now on, bless the Lord for the deliverances that He wrought.

Doubled. I heard an aggadic Midrash (Yalkut Shimoni II, 47): The Holy One, blessed be He, did not withhold the reward of Tabor and Carmel, who came at the giving of the Torah so that the Torah might be given upon them, and returned in shame. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to them: In the end I will repay you double. At Sinai it is said (Exodus 20:2): “I am the Lord thy God”; at Tabor it shall say: “I, I.” At Sinai it is said (ibid.): “I am the Lord thy God”; at Carmel it shall say, doubled (1 Kings 18:39): “the Lord, He is God; the Lord, He is God,” in the days of Elijah.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: Lord, when Thou wentest forth out of Seir
Judges.english_translation: This is the giving of the Torah, as it is said (Deuteronomy 33:2): “and He shone forth from Seir unto them.” And what is its connection to here? Thus said Deborah: The Torah is hard to depart from, and good to cleave to, for it was given with awe and with might; and therefore Israel were delivered into the hands of their enemies for departing from it, and when they offered themselves to engage in it they were saved. All this is to be learned from the Targum of Jonathan.
They caused the dew of life to flow.
They melted like flowing water.
It has already been explained what was seen on it (Exodus 19:20): smoke all of it, and sound, and torches and fire.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: at the presence of the LORD
Judges.english_translation: This is an abbreviated verse: “this Sinai” — what happened on it? Before the Lord, because the Lord descended upon it.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: In the days of Shamgar the son of Anath, In the days of Jael
Judges.english_translation: It teaches that Jael also judged Israel in her days.
Israel were afraid to go out on their roads because of the enemies, and used to walk by a winding path in hiding.
The cities of the open country (*perazi*), which have no wall, ceased to be inhabited because of their enemies, and the people gathered into the fortified cities.
Like *she-kamti* (“that I arose”); and so (Judges 6:17): “that thou talkest with me” (*she'atah medabber*).

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: They chose new gods; Then was war in the gates
Judges.english_translation: When Israel chose for themselves new gods, then they were compelled to fight at their gates. See now, when they offered themselves willingly, whether a shield and spear were seen in Israel, so that [they] needed to fight against the forty thousand heads of troops that the nation brought upon them; and the Omnipresent confounded all of them in the war of the stars (v. 20), and the brook Kishon swept them away.
Like (Deuteronomy 17:2): “if there be found in the midst of thee, in one of thy gates” — towns.
I, Deborah, [turn] to the lawgivers of Israel, to love the sages of Israel who offered themselves among the people, saying: Bless the Lord and return to Him.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: You that ride on white asses
Judges.english_translation: The merchants and the officers, who from now on will ride on white asses, the esteemed ones, without fear and anxiety about their enemies. And those who sit on *middin* — an expression for judges — who were afraid to carry out judgment in public, and so Jonathan translated: “who were gathering to sit in judgment.” And those who walk on foot along the road: tell and relate this deliverance, [from the time] when, from the sound of the archers (*mechatzetzim*) among you — ambushers, bandits and tax-collectors who sat in troops in lines to lie in wait at the crossings of the water — there now the riders of asses and those who walk on the road shall give the righteous acts of the Lord. And what are the righteous acts (v. 11)? “the righteous acts toward His villages in Israel,” that He caused Israel to be at rest, to dwell in open country and to go out scattered, alone, not in a gathering of people.

Menahem interpreted: those who arrange war and set the battle in order; and he connected it with (Proverbs 30:27): “The locusts have no king, yet go they forth all of them by bands (*chatzotz*)” — an expression for troops. Another explanation:

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: from the noise of archers, in the places of drawing water (mikol mechatzetzim bein mashavim)
Judges.english_translation: When you used to go among the drawing-places to draw water, you were afraid of the sound of stones, the pebbles of the brook, *kiesels* in Old French, so that [the sound of] whoever passed over them could be heard, and you feared that your enemies would notice you. From now on there is no need to fear this, and therefore it is a commandment upon you to give thanks to His name.
Judges.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is קיזל״ש. Darmesteter's collection (1909, pp. 43–49) has no entry for this passage, so the word could not be checked.

Judges.english_translation: An expression for the stones, the pebbles of the brook, as (Lamentations 3:16): “and He crushed with gravel (*bechatzatz*).”

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: Then the people of the LORD went down to the gates
Judges.english_translation: They returned to the cities of their dwellings, from which they had fled to be gathered into the fortified cities.

An expression of praise according to its plain sense: “be strong in your song.” And our Rabbis said (Pesachim 66b): because she praised herself and said (v. 7), “until that I arose, Deborah,” the Holy Spirit departed from her.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: then came down a remnant of the nobles (az yered saríd la-adirim)
Judges.english_translation: *Yered* — *yardah* (“she ruled”), like (Isaiah 45:1): “to subdue (*lered*) nations before him”: the remnants of Israel ruled over the mighty of the nations.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: the Lord came down for me among the mighty
Judges.english_translation: He ruled for me over the mighty of the nations.

From Ephraim came the root of Joshua the son of Nun, to rule over Amalek, to weaken him by the edge of the sword. And this verse is connected to the one above, to explain: “the Lord came down for me among the mighty” — He raised up Joshua to rule over Amalek.

Saul the son of Kish will arise from the tribe of Benjamin, and will crush him and make him dim like dim coals. And one can interpret “*be-ammamekha*” as the army of two hundred thousand foot soldiers with which Saul came upon them.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: Out of Machir came down governors
Judges.english_translation: Great officers who conquered the Amorite, who conquered (Deuteronomy 3:4) “sixty cities, all the region of Argob,” which Jair conquered.

The princes in Issachar: these are Sanhedrins engaged in Torah — (1 Chronicles 12:33) “men that had understanding of the times” — who were always with Deborah to teach in Israel statute and ordinance.
Judges.translator_note: The printed reference is 1 Chronicles 11:32; the quoted words stand at 1 Chronicles 12:33 of the Hebrew text.

Judges.english_translation: This *yod* is superfluous and serves no purpose; it is like the *yod* in (Psalms 8:8) “beasts of the field” (*behemot sadai*) and (Jeremiah 22:14) “and cutteth him out windows” (*vekara lo challonai*).
And the rest of the people of Issachar, so they are with Barak, for all that he shall command.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: Into the valley they rushed forth at his feet
Judges.english_translation: He sent them on all his errands: to gather the people and for all the needs of the war.

But in the divisions of Reuben's heart there were great searchings of heart. (Targum:) *nikhlei libba* (devices of the heart) — craftiness; and what was his craftiness? He sat down between the sheepfolds (*mispetei*) of the battle to hear who would win, and he would be with him.
To hear the sound of the flocks of war: whose is the sound of the shout of might, and whose is the sound of the shout of weakness.
And did not come to the war; and so Dan put his property into ships, to stay and to flee.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: and abode by his creeks (ve-al mifratzav)
Judges.english_translation: To guard the breaches of his land.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: Zebulun is a people that jeoparded their lives
Judges.english_translation: He despised his life and abandoned himself to die in the war with Barak; and so Naphtali, upon the high places of the field, on Mount Tabor.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: In Taanach by the waters of Megiddo
Judges.english_translation: Jonathan translated: “In Taanach they were encamping and reached to the waters of Megiddo”: the head of the camp in Taanach, and reaching to the waters of Megiddo.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: They took no gain of money
Judges.english_translation: They came to the aid of Sisera for nothing; they did not ask a reward from him.
And the Holy One, blessed be He, also sent His hosts against them, who want no reward at all.

The head of the star is in heaven and its end is on the earth. From here they said (Tanchuma, Bereshit 5) that the thickness of the firmament is like the air between heaven and earth, for the star is fixed in the firmament like a bolt in a door, and the measure of its length is like the thickness of the firmament; and from the verse that testifies “from their highways they fought,” we hear that the thickness of the firmament is like the height of heaven from the earth.
He swept them out of the world, like this rake that sweeps the ashes from the hearth.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: that ancient river, the river Kishon (nachal kedumim)
Judges.english_translation: Which became a surety to the sea for this, from the days of Egypt, as it is said in Pesachim (118b).

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: O my soul, march on with strength (tidreki nafshi oz)
Judges.english_translation: With the feet [trample] the strength of the mighty ones of Canaan.

The hoofs of their horses were stripped off (*nishtalfu*), because the heat of the star made the mud boil and the hoof was dislodged, as when one scalds the feet with boiling water and the hooves come off; since they were stripped, the feet were battered (*nehelmu*).

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: by the prancings of their strong ones
Judges.english_translation: They made their horses dance in the war, like (Nahum 3:2): “and the horse prancing” (*sus daher*); it is an expression for making a horse dance.
Some say it was a star, and others say it was an important man (Moed Katan 16a); and he was near the place of the war and did not come.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: said the angel of the LORD
Judges.english_translation: Barak said, on the mission of the Holy One, blessed be He.
Those who dwell within his four cubits (ibid.); with four hundred shofars Barak excommunicated Meroz.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: to the help of the LORD
Judges.english_translation: As it were, for whoever helps Israel is like one who helps the Divine Presence.

Sarah, of whom it is said (Genesis 18:9): “Behold, in the tent.” Rebekah, of whom it is said (Genesis 24:67): “And Isaac brought her into the tent.” Rachel and Leah, of whom it is said (Genesis 31:33): “and he went out of Leah's tent,” etc.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: Above women in the tent shall she be blessed
Judges.english_translation: Why Jael? They bore and raised [children], and had it not been for Jael, this wicked one would have come and destroyed them; so it is in Bereshit Rabbah (48:15). Another explanation: Jael too was a tent-dweller, therefore he mentioned her in the blessing of the tent-dwellers.
To know whether his mind was on him, so as to distinguish between the taste of water and the taste of milk; so Jonathan translated.
In a bowl in which water is drunk; for water is called “mighty,” as it is said (Exodus 15:10): “in the mighty waters.”
Sisera, who was weary and toilsome.
An expression of *chikui*.
Judges.translator_note: The word *chikui* (חיקוי) is left untranslated because its sense here is uncertain (it usually means “imitation”).

Judges.english_translation: An expression for smiting (*machatz*).
It goes out on the other side.

An expression for speech, like (Isaiah 57:19): “the fruit of the lips (*niv sefatayim*)”; and our Rabbis explained it (Rosh Hashanah 33b) as an expression for groaning, like the *teruah* [blast], which we translate *yevava* (Leviticus 23:24). And I say: an expression for seeing, like (Zechariah 2:12) “the apple (*bavat*) of his eye,” and so Menahem connected it.
Judges.translator_note: The printed references are Isaiah 17:19 and Zechariah 2:2; the quoted phrases stand at Isaiah 57:19 and Zechariah 2:12 of the Hebrew text.

Judges.english_translation: A window.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: her wise ladies (chakhmot sarotheha) answered her
Judges.english_translation: The wise ones among her princesses; therefore the *chet* is vocalized with a *patach*. *Chokhmot* as a noun is vocalized with a *chataf kamatz*, as (Proverbs 14:1) “Wisdom (*chokhmot*) is too high for a fool,” and this one is vocalized *chakhmot*, and so (ibid. 14:1) “every wise woman (*chakhmot nashim*) buildeth her house” — the wise ones among women.
Judges.translator_note: The printed reference for the first quotation is Proverbs 14:1; the quoted words (ראמות לאויל חכמות) stand at Proverbs 24:7 of the Hebrew text.

Judges.english_translation: The *dagesh* of the *nun* serves in place of a third *nun*, and its meaning is *ta'aneynah otah* (“they answered her”); the *dagesh* of the *nun* serves in place of “otah” (her), like (Leviticus 6:14) “baked (*murbekhet*) shalt thou bring it (*tevi'enah*).”

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: Yea, she returneth answer to herself
Judges.english_translation: Comfort for herself: why do I wonder with astonishment at the delay of my son?

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: have they not found, are they not dividing the spoil?
Judges.english_translation: And it is that which delays them.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: A damsel, two damsels to every man
Judges.english_translation: They afflict the beautiful women in Israel, and each one of them has in his bed two and three women.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: so let all Thine enemies perish
Judges.english_translation: Deborah said: These are vain comforts for her; “so let all Thine enemies perish, O Lord, as he perished.”

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: but let them that love Him be as the sun when he goeth forth in his might
Judges.english_translation: In the time to come, (Isaiah 30:26) “sevenfold, as the light of the seven days,” which is one to three hundred and forty-three, equal to the number of forty-nine sevenths.
This is not from the words of Deborah but from the words of the writer of the book.

Until here it is said “and they continued” (*vayosifu*), because sin was accumulating upon sin; but in this song all that they had done was forgiven them, and now they begin to sin [again]. So it is expounded in Aggadat Tehillim (Midrash Tehillim 18:6).
(Targum:) *matmorita*; and in Old French: *vodvés*. And because they make in them a small light, in a place that is not noticeable, he calls them *minharot*; *loisettes* in Old French.
Judges.translator_note: Old French glosses: the printed Hebrew spellings are וודו״ש and לויישיט״ש. Darmesteter (1909, p. 46) reads *vodvés*, “les voûtes” (the vaults), and *loisètes*, “caverns with a small window in their darkest part, hence their name,” formed on *lucere* (to shine).

Judges.english_translation: *Grotes* in Old French.
Judges.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is גרוטי״ה; Darmesteter (1909, p. 46) reads *grotes*, “les cavernes” (modern *grottes*).

Judges.english_translation: *Plesediç* in Old French, because they are made in forests by felling the trees all around.
Judges.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is פליישדי״ץ; Darmesteter (1909, p. 46) reads *plesediç* (preserved in the place-name Pleissis) and renders it “les clairières” (the clearings).

Judges.english_translation: To graze the crops.
This prophet is Phinehas, in Seder Olam (chapter 2).
Of the sons of Abiezer the son of Gilead the son of Manasseh.
His father was threshing it, and he was sifting it. He said to him: Father, you are old, and if the Midianites come you will not be able to flee; you go, and I will thresh.
In the beams of the olive-press.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: The LORD is with thee, thou mighty man of valour
Judges.english_translation: For He gave thee such strength.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: if the LORD be with us
Judges.english_translation: And if the Lord be with us, why has all this befallen us? etc.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: which our fathers told us of
Judges.english_translation: It was Passover. He said to him: Last night my father taught me the Hallel, and I heard him say (Psalms 114:1): “When Israel went out of Egypt,” [and] “but now He hath cast us off.” If our fathers were righteous, let Him do for us for their sake; and if they were wicked, just as He did His wonders for them for nothing, so let Him do for us. And where are all His wonders?

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: and the Lord looked upon him
Judges.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He, Himself.
In the strength of this merit, that you pleaded a defense for my children; so Rabbi Tanchuma expounded (Midrash Tanchuma, Shofetim 4).
The thousand in which I am counted, to be under the chief of the thousand, is the poorest thousand among all the thousands of Manasseh.
Like *she-atah*.
Judges.translator_note: The printed text reads only “like *she-atah*,” which seems incomplete or garbled; I cannot tell what it was meant to equate.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: unleavened cakes of an ephah of flour
Judges.english_translation: We learned that it was Passover, the day of the waving of the Omer; therefore it is said (below 7:13): “and, behold, a cake of barley bread tumbled,” etc.
And the gravy.
An expression of anxiety, as if to say: What will become of me?
Because I have seen an angel of the Lord, therefore I am anxious and cry “Alas.”
Gideon [called] the altar.
The Lord is our peace.
The choice bullock; for an ox one day old is called *shor*.
(Targum:) *vetora tinyana* (“and the second bullock”).

(Targum:) “which was fattened seven years for idolatry.” Eight things were permitted on that night: that which was set aside [for idolatry], the *asherah*, and the night, and the high place, etc., as is stated in Temurah (28b).

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: on the top of this stronghold
Judges.english_translation: On the top of the rock.
On behalf of the Baal.
Will you avenge his vengeance? And so (1 Samuel 25:32): “and mine own hand hath saved me (*vehoshi'ah yadi li*)” — said by David concerning Nabal.
Judges.translator_note: The printed reference is 1 Samuel 25:32 and the printed wording is והושיעה ידי לי; the Hebrew text of 1 Samuel 25:33 reads והשע ידי לי.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: he that will plead for him
Judges.english_translation: On his behalf.
Wait until the morning.
He will plead his own plea and his own vengeance; and in order to put them off until Gideon should flee, he said so.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: let him plead against him (yarev bo)
Judges.english_translation: Concerning Gideon: after *riv* (“to plead”) there follows *im*, or *et*, or *bo*, as (Genesis 31:36): “and chode with Laban” (*vayarev be-Lavan*); but *lo* does not fit the idiom, and every *lo* written here means “on account of.”
A spirit of might.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: and Abiezer was gathered after him
Judges.english_translation: The whole family.

That there was dew on the fleece alone, more than in other places, as he says (v. 37): “a bowlful of water”; but “upon all the ground it was dry” was not fulfilled, for a covenant was made with the dew that it shall not be withheld (Taanit 3a).
An expression of pressing, and so (Isaiah 1:6): “they have not been pressed (*zoru*) nor bound up (*chovashu*)” — not bound up, to bring out the moisture.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: by the hill of Moreh, in the valley
Judges.english_translation: (Targum:) “that looks toward the plain.” *Moreh* is an expression of teaching and seeing, like (Proverbs 6:13) “he teacheth with his fingers” (*moreh be-etzbe'otav*), for from there they watch and signal in the valley.
*Tzalul* is written, for the generation was clear [or: pure] from the righteous.
Judges.translator_note: The meaning of “clear from the righteous” (צלול מן הצדיקים) is uncertain.

Judges.english_translation: (Targum:) *charar delechem se'orin*: a *chararah* that they bake on the coals.
It is the merit of the Omer offering brought on Passover.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: and smote it that it fell
Judges.english_translation: The tent. “And overturned it”: the tent from below to above, and the tent fell.
The narration of the dream. (Targum:) *yat shavita chelma ve-yat pishrei* (“the telling of the dream and its interpretation”).
“And its sale” (*mimkaro*) — that is: and its interpretation.

To recall the merit of the giving of the Torah. And its plain sense: it was night, as is written (v. 9): “and it was dark”; therefore they carried torches there to give them light, and put them in pitchers so that they [the enemy] would not notice the torches.
Judges.translator_note: The words “and it was dark” are not found in Judges 7:9 of the Hebrew text (which begins “And it came to pass the same night”).

Judges.english_translation: What I do, see and do likewise.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: I and all that are with me
Judges.english_translation: One of the heads; and a hundred men were with him (v. 19).

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: For the LORD and for Gideon
Judges.english_translation: (Targum:) “a sword that kills from before the Lord, and we have prevailed by the hand of Gideon.”

Already the soldiers [had set] the watchers whose watch was the middle watch; for it is the way of troops to station watchers: these keep the first third of the night, and these the second third, and these the last third.
Judges.translator_note: The printed sentence lacks a verb (it reads “already the soldiers the watchers”); the bracketed word is supplied.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: and they brake the pitchers (venafotz ha-kadim)
Judges.english_translation: And to break the pitchers that were in their hands.
A blast for marching and fleeing.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: and take before them the waters
Judges.english_translation: Those that divide between Aram and the land of Canaan.
For it too was a divider.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: they brought to Gideon beyond the Jordan
Judges.english_translation: In the morning, when Gideon crossed the Jordan to pursue Zebah and Zalmunna.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: What have I now done in comparison with you
Judges.english_translation: How important is what I did at the beginning, compared with what you did at the end.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: is not the gleaning of the grapes of Ephraim better (tov olelot)
Judges.english_translation: That came into your hands at the end, from the beginning of the vintage that I and my family gathered; for the Lord gave the kings into your hands.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: and what was I able to do
Judges.english_translation: To do so that it would be as important as your deed.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: passed over, he, and the three hundred men
Judges.english_translation: They were crossing the Jordan after Zebah and Zalmunna, who had crossed the Jordan first and were laying waste, beyond the Jordan, the land of Reuben, Gad and Manasseh; and he crossed there in order to take vengeance on them too.
They were Israelites.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: are the palms of Zebah and Zalmunna already in thy hand?
Judges.english_translation: For you boast that you saved us from the hand of Midian.
*Ronces* in Old French.
Judges.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is רונצי״ש; Darmesteter (1909, p. 47) reads *ronces* (brambles).

Judges.english_translation: The name of a place.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: by the way of them that dwell in tents
Judges.english_translation: By the way of the land of Kedar and Arabia, who dwell in the wilderness in their tents, always spread out with their cattle, and do not dwell in houses.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: on the east of Nobah and Jogbehah
Judges.english_translation: For they are cities of Israel, and he did not want to go there except by a winding path, so that they would not notice him, and he could throw them into confusion suddenly.
Before the sun set, while the sun was still seen high.
(Targum:) *vetavar behon* (“and he broke [them] with them”).

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: each one resembled the children of a king
Judges.english_translation: Jonathan translated: “There was one among them whose form was like the form of the king's sons.” And one can interpret: “as thou art, so were they” — one form for you [all], for they were like the form of the sons of kings.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: But the youth drew not his sword
Judges.english_translation: To kill them, for he was afraid of them.
*Lunes* in Old French, of gold.
Judges.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is לוינ״ש; Darmesteter (1909, p. 47) reads *lunes*, “les croissants d'or” (the golden crescents).

Judges.english_translation: (Targum:) *anakaya ve-kelila*.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: and Gideon made it into an ephod
Judges.english_translation: To be a memorial of a great deliverance, so that one might see how heavy their army was, since all this gold was from the earrings of their important men.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: and all Israel went astray after it
Judges.english_translation: After the death of Gideon.
That is its name.
For they killed his sons, as is written in the account (below 9:5).
Hasty in their deeds, acting without discernment.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: by the oak of the pillar (im elon mutzav)
Judges.english_translation: (Targum:) *mishar kamta*: a plain in which there were pillars.
It is a parable.
Othniel the son of Kenaz (Judges 1:13), who came from the tribe of Judah, which is called an olive tree, as it is said (Jeremiah 11:16): “a leafy olive tree, fair, with goodly fruit,” etc.
An expression for fat.
Deborah.
The honey of bees.
Gideon, who is of the seed of Joseph (Judges 6:11), of whom it is said (Genesis 49:22): “a fruitful bough” (*ben porat*), (and Onkelos translated there:) “like a vine that is planted,” etc.
For the Levites do not say the song of the offering except over the libations.
*Espine* in Old French.
Judges.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is ספינ״ה. Darmesteter (1909, p. 47) records for “l'épine” (the thorn) mainly *aiglantier*, and in manuscript V *espines*.

Judges.english_translation: That I am fit for kingship.
Against their will he ruled as lord, and in arrogance.
Hatred, *shlanesh* *maltalent* in Old French.
Judges.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is שלנ״ש מלטלינ״ט. Darmesteter (1909, p. 47) reads *maltalent* and says that it corresponds in Old French to the sense of the Hebrew. The first word, שלנ״ש, I cannot explain.

Judges.english_translation: He was of another nation.
(Targum:) “and they made festivals” (*changinin*).

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: Who is Abimelech, and who is Shechem
Judges.english_translation: Who is Abimelech, to be a prince over Shechem, and who is Shechem, to be slaves to Abimelech? Was not Abimelech the son of Jerubbaal, of Ophrah of the Abiezrite (above 6:11)?
And this officer of the city, whose name is Zebul, is Abimelech's officer; and his master has no right of kingship in the city, and his officer too is nothing.
If you have come to buy lords for yourselves, come and serve the men of Hamor, who was the prince of the land from of old (Genesis 34:2).
[That is,] Abimelech.
And Gaal said it in the presence of Zebul; [Zebul] informed Abimelech.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: Increase thine army, and come out
Judges.english_translation: From the place where you are, and we shall see your greatness.
Like *be-mirmah* (in deceit): in secrecy and in hiding.
Four troops.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: by the middle of the land
Judges.english_translation: (Targum:) “from the strength of the land,” [meaning] from the highest of all the mountains.
(Targum:) “the plain of Meonenim.”

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: that the people went out into the field
Judges.english_translation: The men of Shechem.
Those who told Abimelech that the people of the city went out to the field to do their business.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: the entrance of the gate of the city
Judges.english_translation: So that they could not enter.
A forest in which trees and branches were bent round about, called *pleisher* in Old French.
Judges.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is פלייש״ר. Darmesteter (1909, p. 47) renders the gloss “la clairière, endroit dont les arbres sont enlevés” (a clearing, a place from which the trees have been removed). The Hebrew verb printed here (כפו) I have translated “bent”; the sense is uncertain.

Judges.english_translation: That stronghold belonged to Baal-berith, the name of their idol; and Zalmon (v. 48) — there was a forest there; and some interpret: *tzerich* is *vodvé* in Old French, which they make in the ground.
Judges.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is וודוו״י. Darmesteter (1909, p. 47) lists for this word, “according to others, vault, underground chamber,” the form *vodve*.

Judges.english_translation: A branch of trees.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: a piece of a millstone (pelach rekhev)
Judges.english_translation: A piece of the upper millstone, which is called *rekhev*.
And she crushed.
Lest they say about me.
That is his name.
(Targum:) *ulin* — young horses.
Thirty towns without a wall belonged to them; therefore they were called *irim*, an expression for *iyyarot* (towns).
Seven idolatries are counted here.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: forsook the LORD, and served Him not
Judges.english_translation: Even in partnership with these.
When Jair died.
The land of Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh, who were their neighbors.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: did not [I deliver you] from Egypt?
Judges.english_translation: There are seven deliverances here, corresponding to the seven idolatries that they were worshipping.
The name of a nation.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: and His soul was grieved for the misery of Israel
Judges.english_translation: As it were, there was no room in the place for Him to endure and to contain the trouble that He had over the misery of Israel.
They were gathered by means of a herald.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: the children of Ammon made war
Judges.english_translation: This is the one spoken of above (10:9).
The condition between them.
To the place where all were gathered, for the Divine Presence rests upon the majority of the congregation.
In the south of the land of Edom; and the land of Edom is in the south of the land of Canaan.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: let me pass, I pray thee, through thy land
Judges.english_translation: From south to north, to enter the land of Canaan.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: and also to the king of Moab
Judges.english_translation: For his land was at the end of the land of Edom, on the east of Edom and on the south of the land of Israel.

Moses alluded to it in the Torah (Deuteronomy 2:29): “as the children of Esau that dwell in Seir, and the Moabites that dwell in Ar, did unto me” — just as Edom did not let them pass, so Moab did not let them pass.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: but they went through the wilderness
Judges.english_translation: From west to east, along the southern border of Edom and Moab.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: and compassed the land of Edom
Judges.english_translation: All its south side.
All its south side; and when he reached the south-eastern corner, he turned to the north to go around the eastern border.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: and came by the east side of the land of Moab, and they pitched on the other side of the Arnon
Judges.english_translation: To the end of the east of the land of Moab; and there the land of Sihon and Og began, and they conquered Transjordan on the east of the land of Canaan, and crossed the Jordan, and entered the land of Canaan by way of the east.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: And they possessed … from the Arnon even unto the Jabbok
Judges.english_translation: For what you say is yours (v. 13), they took from Sihon.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: and from the wilderness even unto the Jordan
Judges.english_translation: There were wildernesses there before the Jordan.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: by the side of the Arnon
Judges.english_translation: Beside the Arnon; for they were of Moab, and they knew that it was not for them [Israel] to pass over upon them, for they conquered them from Sihon (Numbers 21:24), who had taken them from the king of Moab (ibid. 21:26).

From when they conquered the land in the days of Joshua until Jephthah. From here one must learn the years of the judges mentioned until now — whether the years of servitude of each nation are counted within the days of the judge or not. We learned in Seder Olam (chapter 12): Joshua led Israel twenty-eight years, and there is no verse from which to learn [it]. Othniel (above 3:11), forty years, and the years of servitude of Cushan-rishathaim (ibid. v. 8) are included in them. After him Ehud (ibid. v. 30), eighty years, and the eighteen years of the servitude of Eglon (ibid. v. 14) are within them: that is one hundred forty-eight years. Deborah (ibid. 5:31), forty years, and the years of servitude of Jabin (ibid. 4:3) are within them: that is one hundred eighty-eight. Afterward, seven years of the servitude of Midian (ibid. 6:1), and forty of Gideon (ibid. 8:28), and three of Abimelech (ibid. 9:22): that is two hundred thirty-eight years. After him, twenty-three of Tola (ibid. 10:2) and twenty-two of Jair (ibid. 10:3) — except that one year went up [was counted] for both — and eighteen of the children of Ammon (ibid. v. 8) before Jephthah came: that is three hundred.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: he passed over unto the children of Ammon
Judges.english_translation: To the children of Ammon.
(Targum:) “the plain of vineyards.”

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: thou hast brought me very low
Judges.english_translation: A feminine form, and similar to it (Song of Songs 4:9): “Thou hast ravished my heart (*libavtini*), my sister, my bride.”

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: thou art become one of them that trouble me (be-okhrai)
Judges.english_translation: All my blood is troubled; you have cut off my foot.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: and go down upon the mountains
Judges.english_translation: An expression of wailing, and an example of it (Isaiah 15:3): “on its housetops and in its broad places everyone shall wail, descending with weeping” — one who grieves in weeping until his body is broken. And in the aggadic Midrash Rabbi Tanchuma expounds (Behukotai 5): “upon the mountains” — before the Sanhedrin: perhaps they will find an opening for your vow.
Since it is not written “her virginal years” (*betulotehah*), it implies actual virginity (*betulim*).

They decreed that no one should do so again; for if he had gone to Phinehas, or [Phinehas] had come to him, he would have released him from his vow. They stood upon their dignity, and between the two of them she was lost, and they were punished: from Phinehas the Divine Presence departed, as it is said in Chronicles (1 Chronicles 9:20): “and the Lord was with him in former times” — we learn that in the end He was not with him; and Jephthah was struck with a skin disease and his limbs fell off, as it is said (below 12:7): “and was buried in the cities of Gilead.” And one can interpret further: “and it was a custom in Israel” — connected to the following verse.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: from year to year went the daughters of Israel, etc.
Judges.english_translation: This thing they fixed upon themselves as a custom.
To mourn.
And he crossed the Jordan, and they went to the north of Transjordan, to Gilead.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: because they said: Ye are fugitives of Ephraim, O Gilead
Judges.english_translation: The lowly among Ephraim used to despise Gilead, and said to them: What are you, Gilead, [that you are] important among Ephraim and among Manasseh? So Jonathan translated.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: And the Gileadites took the fords
Judges.english_translation: They were guarding at the place of the fords.
“The *shibbolet* of this river I will cross.”

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: he could not frame to pronounce it right
Judges.english_translation: For they stammered with their tongue.
This is Boaz.
(Targum:) “new and old wine” (*chamar chadat ve-atik*).
A razor (*ta'ar*), because it shaves (*moreh*) and casts off the hair.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: and eat not any unclean thing
Judges.english_translation: Things forbidden to a Nazirite.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: unto the child that shall be born
Judges.english_translation: The one who is about to be born.
After her counsel.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: how shall the child be ordered, and how shall we do unto him?
Judges.english_translation: (Targum:) “What is fitting to be done for the boy, and what shall we do for him?”
Let us gather thee into the house.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: when thy words come to pass
Judges.english_translation: If a message comes to us from you, once we know and recognize your name.
And we will do what you send us.
Hidden: it is always changing, and it is not known why it changes today (Sifrei, Naso 42).
This [time].

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: nor would He have told us such things as these
Judges.english_translation: He would not have announced this good tiding to us if we were deserving of death.
To enter within him at times.
A pretext to provoke them.
Concerning the woman: he spoke to her relatives; so Jonathan translated.
(Targum:) *kina de-dabreyata*: a gathering of bees.

An expression for detaching the adhesion of anything that sticks; and so with bread that sticks in the oven, its detaching is called *rediyah* (Shabbat 117b): “one who removes (*harodeh*) bread from the oven”; (Bava Metzia 64a): “one who removes his beehive.” For the honey is made in combs that are made sticking to the walls of the vessel on all sides, from wall to wall, according to the circle of the vessel; and so Jonathan translated: *vayirdehu* — *venasseyah*.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: And his father went down unto the woman
Judges.english_translation: (Targum:) “on account of the woman.”
Friends for the office of groomsmen.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: And it came to pass on the seventh day
Judges.english_translation: Of the days of the week, and not the seventh of the feast; it was the fourth of the days of the feast.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: have ye called us to impoverish us? is it not so? (halirshenu keratem lanu halo)
Judges.english_translation: Jonathan translated: “Have you invited us to make us poor? Is it not so?”
The remaining ones of the seven days, from the fourth onward.
Before sunset, for they still had time until the evening.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: If you had not plowed with my heifer
Judges.english_translation: It is a parable. (Targum:) “had you not examined through my wife.”
(Targum:) “a spirit of might from before the Lord.”
Garments that he stripped off from them.
She was given to one of his groomsmen.
Justly will I do them harm.

“tail to tail he turned” — it implies that he himself turned (as in Exodus 32:15, *vayifen vayered*); [here] *vayifen* implies that he turned others; and so is the usage of every word whose verb has a *heh*: (Exodus 1:20) “and the people multiplied” (*vayerev*); (Lamentations 2:5) “and hath multiplied in the daughter of Judah mourning” (*vayerev*); (2 Kings 25:21) “So Judah was carried away out of his land” (*vayigel*), [meaning] he exiled; (ibid. 18:11) “And the king of Assyria carried Israel away unto Assyria” (*vayigel*), [meaning] and he exiled.
The son-in-law of the Philistine who was in Timnah (above 14:1).

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: If you do after this manner
Judges.english_translation: And perhaps you are accustomed to this: to give one man's wife to another.
(Targum:) *parshin im ragla'in* (“horsemen with footmen”). A horse-rider does not lean on his thigh but on his shin, one foot being placed in the iron that hangs from the saddle.
In the hollow of the rock of Etam; and he connected it with (Isaiah 57:5) “the clefts of the rocks” (*se'ifei ha-selaim*), (ibid. 10:33) “lops the boughs” (*mesa'ef pa'orah*).
And they dispersed.
The name of a place.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: Why are you come up against us
Judges.english_translation: Are we not slaves to you?
That you bind him and deliver him to us.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: No; but we will bind thee fast
Judges.english_translation: We will not kill you, but we will only bind you fast.
(Targum:) “a spirit of might from before the Lord.”
His ties.
Moist; and I saw in a book of remedies that it calls the moisture that comes out of a wound *teriyah*.
With the jawbone of the ass, to pile up many piles. (Targum:) *bela'a de-chamra ramitinun de-gurin* (“with the jawbone of the ass I cast them down in heaps”).
The cavity in which the tooth sits, made in the manner of a mortar (*machtetet*).
A spring that came because of the cry of him who called to the Lord.
It was said to the men of Gaza.
They conducted themselves in silence.
And he uprooted them from their place.
Thin ropes.
He did not need to exert himself in breaking them.
Thick ropes.
Tresses, *plonish* in Old French.
Judges.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is פלוני״ש. Darmesteter (1909, p. 47) renders this entry “tresses” and gives his own reading *floçés* (following manuscript W).

Judges.english_translation: The beam over which the weaver stretches the warp; and the name of the beam is *ensuble* for *massekhet*, *ortoire* in Old French.
Judges.translator_note: Old French glosses: the printed Hebrew spellings are אנשובל״א and אורטר״א. Darmesteter (1909, p. 47) reads *ésuble* (modern *ensouple*, a loom beam, “bois sur lequel on tisse la chaîne”), and, for the second word, *ortoire* (“now one says *ourdissoire*”).

Judges.english_translation: She pressed him, and it has no parallel.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: And when Delilah saw that he had told her
Judges.english_translation: The words of truth are recognizable.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: and she called for a man
Judges.english_translation: For the messenger of the lords.
The place of the beginning of his corruption.
At the mill: heavy labor; and our Rabbis (Sotah 10a) explained what they explained.
Upon which the house was established.
*Palper* in Old French, like (Genesis 27:12): “perhaps my father will feel me.”
Judges.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is פאלפא״ר (*palper*). Darmesteter (1909, p. 48) records for this verse (“fais-moi tâter,” let me feel) the form *taster* in the manuscripts.

Judges.english_translation: Remember the twenty years that I judged Israel, and I did not say to any of them: Move this staff for me from place to place.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: that I may be at once avenged of the Philistines for my two eyes (nekam achat mishte einai)
Judges.english_translation: And leave the reward for the second eye for me for the world to come, and here pay me the reward of one of them.
And he seized, *embracer* in Old French, as (Ruth 3:8): “and the man was startled, and he *vayilafet*” — seized in the arms of the woman.
Judges.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is אינברצ״א; Darmesteter (1909, p. 48) reads *embraça* (manuscripts differ: *embraçier*, *abraçier*, *abraser*).

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: there was a man of the hill-country of Ephraim
Judges.english_translation: Although these two sections — that of Micah and that of the concubine in Gibeah — were written at the end of the book, they happened at the beginning of [the period of] the Judges, in the days of Othniel the son of Kenaz, as it is said (below 18:31): “And they set them up Micah's graven image … all the time that the house of God was in Shiloh”; we learn that all the days of Shiloh the likeness of Micah was there. And in [the story of] the concubine in Gibeah it is said of Jebus, which is in Jerusalem (ibid. 19:12): “We will not turn aside into the city of a stranger”; we learn that they had not yet conquered Jerusalem.
That were stolen from you; and there is a parallel to it (1 Samuel 21:6): “for women have been kept (*atzurah*) from us” (*lanu*) — kept from us (*mimenu*).
The curse upon all who had stolen it; and you also spoke the curse in my ears.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: behold, the silver is with me
Judges.english_translation: I acknowledge to you about it, that it is in my hand, that I took it.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: And he restored the eleven hundred pieces of silver to his mother
Judges.english_translation: He said [that he wished] to return it to her; and [now that] it is there, it is in your possession.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: I had wholly dedicated the silver unto the Lord from my hand for my son
Judges.english_translation: I took upon myself to hand it over from my hand to your hand for the sake of a graven image and a molten image: give it to me now, and from my hand I will return it to you. Some say that this woman is Delilah, because it is written (above 16:5) “eleven hundred pieces of silver”; but they are mistaken, for Micah preceded Samson by many years; rather, the sections were placed next to each other because of the evil silver that is the same here and there, and both were silver of calamity.
A house of idolatry; and so every “*Elohim*” mentioned in this section is secular, except for this one (below 18:31): “all the time that the house of God was in Shiloh” (Shevuot 35b).

He initiated him for the service of the image, to be a priest before it. Every initiation into a thing by which a person enters upon an office is called “filling of hands,” *revestir* in Old French; and when offices are given to a person, they call the giving *revestir* in Old French.
Judges.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spellings are רישוושטי״ר and רישוישטי״ר. Darmesteter (1909, p. 48) lists *mainvestir* for “he invests” (the act by which one invests is called “emplissage des mains”) and *revestir* for “to enter upon office.”

Judges.english_translation: And he was a Levite on his mother's side. And our Rabbis said (Bava Batra 109b): because he did the deed of Manasseh, who came from Judah, he called him “of the family of Judah”; and he was Levi, the son of Gershom the son of Moses our Teacher, as is explained in the account (below 18:30): “and Jonathan the son of Gershom,” etc.
The way of his journey.
My livelihood, to earn a living.
At the end of a year.
A pair of changes of garments, which are the arrangement and order for all people, as is fitting for them, for the year.
*Aparaillement* in Old French.
Judges.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is אפרליימנ״ט; Darmesteter (1909, p. 48) reads *aparaillement* (from *appariculamentum*), “a pair of garments.”

Judges.english_translation: And thy sustenance.
After his counsel.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: for unto that day their inheritance had not fallen
Judges.english_translation: An inheritance as befitted them, in a conquered land, as it is said in Joshua (19:47): “and the border of the children of Dan went out beyond them”; and even from here one may learn that this event took place at the beginning of [the period of] the Judges, immediately.

There are many astonishing questions here (Bava Batra 110b): Are you not of the seed of Moses our Teacher, of whom it is said (Exodus 3:5): “draw not nigh hither,” (ibid. 4:11): “who hath made man's mouth?” (ibid. 4:2): “What is that in thine hand?”

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: Ask counsel, we pray thee, of God
Judges.english_translation: Of the teraphim, which speak through sorceresses.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: before the LORD is your way
Judges.english_translation: Before the Holy One, blessed be He, it is revealed; for this one [the idol] has no substance.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: and there was none that put them to shame in anything
Judges.english_translation: None of them needs his fellow, so as to send him away empty and shame him, as it is said at the end of the account (v. 10): “a place where there is no want of any thing”; so I heard.
Few heirs, so that if one kills these, there are no more claimants left to fight with those who hold the inheritance.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: and they were far from the Zidonians
Judges.english_translation: From the help of the Zidonians.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: and had no business with any man
Judges.english_translation: No covenant had been made that they would come to their aid in time of need.
That is: what answer do you bring? What did you find in the place where our lot fell? What is the people — is it strong or weak?
Slothful.
Burdens: anything that is heavy in going, that cannot run if the people of the place pursue them.
*Pesantoume* in Old French.
Judges.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is פיזנטו״מא; Darmesteter (1909, p. 48) reads *pesanteume* (formed on *pesant* with the suffix *-ume*) and renders it “le poids (les fardeaux)” (the weight, the burdens).

Judges.english_translation: The children of Dan [turned] to those who called to them.
And what is left to me still?
Short-tempered people who are in our company.

The name of the city; and in the Book of Joshua (19:47) He calls its name “Leshem,” because they found there a precious stone named *leshem*, which was on the breastplate for the tribe of Dan, its name written upon the *leshem*; and they knew that it truly is their inheritance.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: until the day of the captivity of the land
Judges.english_translation: In the days of Sennacherib, in the first exile.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: And his concubine played the harlot against him
Judges.english_translation: She went astray from his house to the outside; every expression of *zenut* is only an expression for “going out” (Onkelos, Genesis 34:31): *nafkat bara* (“she went out”) — going out from her husband to love others.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: Be content, I pray thee, and tarry all night
Judges.english_translation: [Tarry] the night.
The sun has weakened from its strength and inclines to set.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: behold, the day groweth to an end
Judges.english_translation: The time when all travelers incline to encamp in a house.
Gibeah of Benjamin.
Like *ve-lanenu*; the *dagesh* of the *nun* [stands] in place of the second *nun*.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: and I am now going to the house of the LORD
Judges.english_translation: I am going to Shiloh.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: and gave provender (vayabol) unto the asses
Judges.english_translation: And he gave *yevul* (produce, fodder) to the asses; *vayabol*: *aprovender* in Old French.
Judges.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is אפרוונד״ר. Darmesteter (1909, p. 48) reads *afodrer* (“to give fodder,” formed on the Gothic *fodr*) from most manuscripts; manuscript T has *aprovender*, “which has an analogous sense,” as printed here.

Judges.english_translation: Homosexual intercourse.
For she was dead.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: the chiefs of all the people
Judges.english_translation: (Targum:) *reishei kol ama* (“the heads of all the people”).

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: and they thought to kill me (damu)
Judges.english_translation: They intended to kill, *aneshmenteu* in Old French.
Judges.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is אנישמינט״ו. Darmesteter (1909, pp. 48–49) lists for “they meditated” forms such as *adesmerent* (from *ad* + *aestimare*); the printed form differs from those I could read, and I could not match it.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: that they may do, when they come
Judges.english_translation: On their coming to Gibeah of Benjamin: “according to all the folly,” etc.
Equal in one counsel.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: through all the tribe of Benjamin
Judges.english_translation: Ten tribes: his ten families were counted as ten tribes, so that there should be twelve tribes from Rachel.
Contracted in their right hand; they had no control over it, as if it were stopped, like (Psalms 69:16): “neither let the pit shut her mouth upon me.”
These seven hundred men.
At a hair's thread.
Would not err.

But they did not try [to inquire] whether to win or to be defeated; and at the end, when they tried, He said (v. 28): “Go up, for tomorrow I will deliver him into thy hand”; they rose early and completed their words.
They were punished for not having been equally zealous about the matter of the idol of Micah, which already existed.
In the plain of Jericho.
Drawn out, like (Job 40:23): “he can draw the Jordan to his mouth” (*yagi'ach*); (Psalms 22:10): “Thou art He that took me (*gochi*) from the womb.”

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: out of the meadow of Gibeah (mi-ma'arei-Geva)
Judges.english_translation: From a narrow place, the nakedness (*ervah*) and exposure of Gibeah of Benjamin, its weak spot, from which it is easy to conquer it, as (Genesis 42:9): “to see the nakedness of the land are ye come.”

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: And the men of Israel gave place
Judges.english_translation: Who were in the field, a place for Benjamin to flee to the Gibeah, for Israel relied on the ambush, that they would come out to meet them.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: and the liers in wait drew themselves along
Judges.english_translation: He drew out with the shofar. Another explanation: he drew with the shofar the people who were with him, toward the city.
From the beginning there was a sign between Israel and the ambush: that the ambush would raise much smoke from the city, and Israel would understand that the ambush had captured Gibeah.
The height of the smoke.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: And the men of Israel turned
Judges.english_translation: Now he returns to the beginning of the matter and repeats and explains the twenty-five thousand that we wrote above (v. 35): how they fell and where they fell.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: and them which came out of the cities
Judges.english_translation: The ambush that entered the city: they destroy it in the midst of the tribe, in the midst of the city.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: They inclosed the Benjamites round about
Judges.english_translation: They surrounded Benjamin like a crown (*keter*) that surrounds the head; and so (Psalms 22:13): “the strong bulls of Bashan have beset me” (*kitteruni*); and so (Habakkuk 1:4): “for the wicked doth compass about (*makhtir*) the righteous”; and so also in the language of *atarah*, surrounding is called (1 Samuel 23:26): “and Saul and his men were compassing David and his men to take them.”
Judges.translator_note: The printed reference for the Psalms quotation is 22:3; the quoted words stand at Psalms 22:13 of the Hebrew text.

Judges.english_translation: They call a pursuit after him; they shout to one another to pursue.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: trod them down at their resting place (menuchah hidrichuhu)
Judges.english_translation: Near the cities in which they rest, there they overtook him.
They overtook him; and there is a parallel in the language of the Gemara (Ketubot 60b): “he ran after him a parsa in sand (*bechala*) and did not overtake him (*adrakhei*).”
Judges.translator_note: The printed Talmud wording רהט בתריה פרסא בחלא ולא אדרכיה is translated literally; the meaning of בחלא (“in sand”) is my reading and is uncertain.

Judges.english_translation: From the east of Gibeah.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: And there fell of Benjamin eighteen thousand men
Judges.english_translation: In the field, in the midst of the battle.
Killing after killing, like the gleanings after the vintage.
That makes twenty-three thousand.
The name of a place.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: and smote of them two thousand men
Judges.english_translation: That makes the twenty-five thousand mentioned above (v. 35); and as for the hundred written above (ibid.), it did not explain where they fell.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: turned again upon the children of Benjamin
Judges.english_translation: In all the cities.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: both the entire city, men (me-ir metom)
Judges.english_translation: All the inhabitants of the cities were destroyed (*tamu*).

And people were included in “*metom*,” for “*metom*” is an expression of destruction. And one may wonder about a thousand: where are they? For twenty-six thousand were counted from the cities, and from Gibeah six hundred, and here he counted among the fallen twenty-five thousand and one hundred men, and six hundred escaped to the rock of Rimmon, and the thousand fled to the cities and fell the next day when the children of Israel returned to the cities of Benjamin to put under the ban the women and little ones.
Judges.translator_note: The printed text says “six hundred” for Gibeah; Judges 20:15 says seven hundred, and only seven hundred makes the missing thousand that this comment is accounting for (26,000 + 700 − 25,100 − 600 = 1,000).

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: that there should be one tribe lacking (lehipaked)
Judges.english_translation: To be diminished.
They turned to think of them as a remnant to be saved.
Young virgin girls: they seated them at the mouth of barrels of wine; one who has known a man — her scent spreads; a virgin — her scent does not spread.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: and yet so they sufficed them not
Judges.english_translation: They did not have enough for them.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: an inheritance for the escaped (yerushat peleitah)
Judges.english_translation: The inheritance of the tribe remained empty; give counsel, so that they may beget sons and take hold of their inheritance, the remnant that remains, and a tribe shall not be blotted out from Israel.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: on the east side of the highway
Judges.english_translation: On the east of the highway; Shiloh is north of Beth-el and south of Lebonah, and on the east of the highway that goes up from Beth-el to Shechem.
To come to us in war.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: and we said unto them: Be favorable unto them
Judges.english_translation: Have mercy on them, for they do not know what to do; “because we took not for each man his wife in the war” of Jabesh-gilead, except for four hundred men of them; and if you are particular about the oath, there is no sin for you in the matter, “for ye did not give unto them” your daughters, so that there should be guilt for you in the matter; and peace to you, fear not.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: Who shall go up for us against the Canaanites
Judges.english_translation: Concerning places that we had caused to fall by lot [to the tribes] and had not yet been conquered.
The tribe of Judah shall go up first to conquer its lot.
To the tribe of Simeon.

And help me conquer that which fell to my lot. And some interpret: “Judah shall go up” — it is Othniel, it is Jabez, as we say in tractate Temurah (16a): What is his name? Judah the brother of Simeon is his name; and to Simeon his brother he said that he should go with him.
The name of a place.

From here you learn the greatness and wealth of the kings of Canaan, for Adoni-bezek was not worthy to be counted (Joshua 12) with the kings of Canaan by the name of “king,” and it is written of him thus.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: And they brought him to Jerusalem
Judges.english_translation: For they went from there to fight against Jerusalem.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: and set the city on fire
Judges.english_translation: They sent fire into it.
On his mother's side.
(Targum:) “and she took counsel with him” — an expression of taking counsel: that one advises a person and persuades his heart toward another matter; so it appears to me.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: she alighted from off her ass
Judges.english_translation: (Targum:) “and she bowed down,” to fall at her father's feet.
A person whose house is dried up of all good, who has nothing but Torah.
A field of the house of the owner; (Targum:) “a place of a house of irrigation of waters.”

This is Jericho, for the rich soil of Jericho was given to them to eat until the Temple would be built, and whoever's portion the House of Choice would be built in would take it, so that all Israel would have a share in the House of Choice; and they gave it to the sons of Jethro for four hundred and forty years; and the disciples among them left it and went to Othniel the son of Kenaz, who is Jabez, in the wilderness of Judah, which is in the south of Arad, to learn Torah.
Judges.translator_note: Hebrew דושנה (“its richness”) is rendered “rich soil.”

Judges.english_translation: With the disciples who sat before him he asked the Holy One, blessed be He, that He would prepare worthy disciples for him, as it is said (1 Chronicles 4:10): “And Jabez called on God,” etc.; and He prepared for him these pious ones.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: And the angel of the LORD came up
Judges.english_translation: We learned in Seder Olam (chapter 19): this was Phinehas.
The name of the place.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: I made you to go up
Judges.english_translation: Such was My intention at first, to bring you up from Egypt, and so I did, in order to dispossess My enemies.
Now I said in My anger.
To those who are at your sides, in troops and armies, to plunder and spoil.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: Now when Joshua had sent the people away
Judges.english_translation: This event was earlier; but because he was going to say (v. 11) “and the children of Israel did evil,” he began by saying thus: “Joshua”: when he died, and they had accepted before him to serve the Lord, he sent each man to his inheritance, and they served the Lord all his days and all the days of the elders; and afterward: “and the children of Israel did evil.”

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: that prolonged their days after Joshua
Judges.english_translation: Days they prolonged, years they did not prolong, because they were lax in eulogizing him; that is what is said (v. 9): “Mount Gaash,” for the mountain shook upon them to kill them.
Because they set up an image of the sun on his grave, as if to say: Alas for the man who made the sun stand still and lies in a grave.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: Whithersoever they went out, the hand of the LORD was against them for evil
Judges.english_translation: It is said in Seder Olam (chapter 12) concerning Abimelech, Mahlon and Chilion.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: And the LORD raised up judges
Judges.english_translation: Constantly, from generation to generation, as it counts on in this book, judge after judge.
The other generation, who did not know the miracles of the wars of Canaan and did not see the great deed, and rebelled and trespassed against the Omnipresent.
The name of a city, because it was strong and ruling.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: he mightily oppressed the children of Israel
Judges.english_translation: Rabbi Tanchuma expounded (Tzav 2): with blasphemies; and so it says (Malachi 3:13): “Your words have been stout against Me.”
For she used to make wicks for the Sanctuary.
She had date palms in Jericho.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: between Ramah and Beth-el in the hill-country of Ephraim
Judges.english_translation: According to the Targum of Jonathan one must learn that this verse is not according to its plain meaning, and these are not signs of the place where she dwelt; rather, we learned that she was a wealthy woman, and from these places was her livelihood, and she sat in her city, whose name was Atarot.

She had date palms in Jericho, and vineyards in Ramah, and olives in the valley of Beth-el, which is a place of oil, and white earth in the hill-country of Ephraim, (Targum:) “in the king's mountain” — I say that they sell it to potters. And some interpret “white earth” as a sown field, as (Shevi'it 2:1) “a white field.”
Judges.translator_note: The Targum phrase is rendered literally (“in the king’s mountain”).

Judges.english_translation: *Vanter* in Old French.
Judges.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is וונטי״ר; Darmesteter (1909, p. 46) reads *vanter* and renders the verse word “pourrait s’enorgueillir” (might vaunt itself).

Judges.english_translation: In the morning, an Aramaic expression: *tzafra*.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: Every one that lappeth … every one that boweth down upon his knees to drink
Judges.english_translation: Set him by himself, apart from your company, for they will not go with you, for thus they are accustomed to bow before the worship of idols.

Judges.english_lemma_JPS: that lapped, putting their hand to their mouth
Judges.english_translation: This is not the manner of bowing, like one who laps with his tongue.
Dwelling in the valley.
Out of respect for Moses a *nun* is written, to change the name, and it is written suspended, to say that he was not Manasseh but Moses.

1 Samuel.english_translation: A present-tense form: he used to go up from season to season to Shiloh. And [in] an aggadic Midrash (Yalkut Shimoni there): by the road by which he went up in this year, he did not go up in another year, so as to make Israel hear and do likewise.
Targum: “and it was the day of the festival.”

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: but unto Hannah he gave a double portion
1 Samuel.english_translation: (Targum:) “one choice portion,” fit to be received with a pleasant countenance.
The other wife of her husband, Peninnah.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and her rival provoked her sore (gam ka'as)
1 Samuel.english_translation: Anger after anger, constantly; therefore it says “also anger” (*gam ka'as*). She would say to her: Have you bought today a cloak for your big son, or a robe for your small son?
That she should complain. And our Rabbis said (Bava Batra 16a): “to make her fret” — that she should pray; and she intended it for the sake of Heaven.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: the LORD had shut up her womb
1 Samuel.english_translation: Against her womb; and so every expression of *be'ad*.
Elkanah.
He would give her a choice portion, to show her that he loved her; and her rival, according to the love that her husband showed her, would increase her provoking of her.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: after they had eaten in Shiloh
1 Samuel.english_translation: Without a *mappik* in the *heh*, and the *alef* has a *chataf kamatz*; and it is like “after eating in Shiloh and after drinking.” And the form applies equally to masculine and feminine: *acharei okhlah* is an expression of the passive, like *le-okhlah* (“for eating”), an expression of “to do.”

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: now Eli the priest sat upon his seat
1 Samuel.english_translation: On that day he sat upon a great seat, for he had been appointed judge (and in the Yalkut Shimoni: high priest) over Israel.
Like *etzel mezuzat* (“beside the post of”).

Why is this name singled out here? She said before Him: Master of the world, two hosts You created in Your world: the upper ones — they do not bear, nor multiply, nor die; and the lower ones — they bear, multiply, and die. If I am of the lower ones, let me be fruitful and multiply and die; and if I am of the upper ones, I shall not die. This I found in the aggadah of Rabbi Yose the Galilean (Pesikta Rabbati). And our Rabbis expounded in tractate Berakhot (31b) what they expounded: Until now no person had called the Holy One, blessed be He, “Tzevaot”; but thus she said before Him: Master of the world, of all the hosts that You created in Your world, is it hard in Your eyes to give me one son?
Our Rabbis expounded it in tractate Berakhot (ibid.) as they expounded.
Mentioned three times in Scripture, corresponding to three things that the woman is commanded.
Righteous ones, as you say (1 Kings 2:32): “two men more righteous.”
Important ones, as you say (Deuteronomy 1:13): “wise men and understanding.”

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: I will give him unto the LORD
1 Samuel.english_translation: That he should be fit to be given to the Lord.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and there shall no razor come
1 Samuel.english_translation: Jonathan translated: “and no human authority shall be over him.”
He was waiting to see when she would stop; so Jonathan translated: “and Eli waited for her until she ceased.”
An expression of waiting, like (Genesis 37:11): “but his father kept the saying”; (Job 14:16): “Thou dost not watch over my sin.”

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: therefore, Eli thought she had been drunken
1 Samuel.english_translation: Because they were not accustomed to pray silently.
Because she had said a harsh thing to him, she turned back and appeased him, that he should not hand her over to be abandoned and put to shame before her rival, a daughter of Belial.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: for out of the abundance of my complaint and my vexation
1 Samuel.english_translation: I have spoken before you harshness.

In some places it is an expression of anguish of heart. Another explanation: “out of the abundance of my complaint” — as its Targum [renders]: “for because of the abundance of my zeal and my vexation I have prolonged [my words] in His shadow until now.”
That my rival vexes me.
An expression of handing over, as (Psalms 27:12): “Deliver me not (*al titteneni*) unto the soul of mine adversaries.”
Missing an *alef*, so as to expound in it an expression of children, like (Deuteronomy 28:57): “and her afterbirth (*uvshilyatah*) that cometh out,” etc.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and the God of Israel grant thy petition
1 Samuel.english_translation: He announced to her that her prayer had been accepted.
To ask mercy for her.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and her countenance was no more
1 Samuel.english_translation: A face of wrath.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and they came to their house, and Elkanah knew
1 Samuel.english_translation: From here [we learn] that a guest is forbidden marital relations.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: when the time was come about
1 Samuel.english_translation: The minimum of *tekufot* is two, the minimum of days is two: [that is] six months and two days. From here [we learn that] a woman who gives birth at seven [months] gives birth *lemekutta'im* (“in broken [periods]”).
He is called after *El* [God] and after the event, for “from Him I asked him.”
(Targum:) *yat dvach mo'adaya* (“the sacrifice of the festivals”).
Vows that he vowed between one festival and the next, he would offer at the festival.
At the end of twenty-two (other books: twenty-four) months, for that is the time of a child's nursing.

The “forever” of the Levites is fifty years, as it is said (Numbers 8:25): “and from the age of fifty years they shall return from the service of the host”; and so were the days of Samuel, fifty-two. For Eli judged Israel forty years, and on the day of Hannah's prayer he was appointed judge; subtract that year for the conception of Samuel, leaving thirty-nine; and Samuel led Israel from the death of Eli thirteen years. For on the day Eli died the Ark was exiled, and it sat in the field of the Philistines seven months (1 Samuel 6:1); from there it came to Kiriath-jearim, [where it was] until David brought it up — [that is,] from when he reigned seven years in Hebron over Judah and all Israel made him king over them; and it is written (ibid. 7:2): “And it came to pass, from the day that the ark abode in Kiriath-jearim, that the time was long; for it was twenty years.” Subtract from them the seven years that David reigned in Hebron; so from when the Ark was exiled until Saul died [it was] thirteen years and seven months, and Samuel died four months before Saul.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: only the LORD establish His word
1 Samuel.english_translation: That which you asked of Him — a man-child (*zera anashim*); and Eli announced to you by the Holy Spirit: “the God of Israel grant thy petition”; “the Lord establish His word.” And this is according to its plain sense. And an aggadic Midrash: Rabbi Nehemiah, in the name of Rabbi Samuel bar Rav Isaac, said: Every single day a heavenly voice goes forth and resounds in the world and says: A righteous one is destined to arise, and his name is Samuel. And every woman who gave birth to a son would call his name Samuel; when they saw his deeds, they would say: This is not Samuel. And when this one was born and they saw his deeds, they said: It seems that this is he; and this is what is said: “the Lord establish His word” — that this one be Samuel the righteous.

I heard in the name of Rabbeinu Yitzchak ha-Levi: one ephah of flour is three *seah*, to produce from it three *issaron* of fine flour, as is fitting for the one bullock, as we learned (Menachot 76b): the showbread is twenty-four tenths from twenty-four *seah*, an *issaron* of fine flour from a *seah* of wheat.
For the libation.
(Targum:) *ve-ravya hava yanik* (“and the boy was a suckling”).

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and they brought the child to Eli
1 Samuel.english_translation: To see that his prophecy had been fulfilled. And our Rabbis expounded what they expounded: that he [Samuel] ruled on a law — that a priest is not needed for the slaughter of sacrifices — as is stated in Berakhot (31b).
To set your eyes upon him, that he be your disciple. And according to the Midrash of our Rabbis: that he not punish him with death.
Do not say: this one will die and another will be given to you.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: therefore I also have lent him to the LORD
