1 Samuel.english_translation: Like a man who lends a vessel to his master, or lends his son to serve him.
*Enprunteiz* in Old French; that is: you are not permitted to punish him; the Holy One, blessed be He, has become a borrower of him, for I lent him to Him, and it is upon Him to return him to me.
1 Samuel.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is אנפרוצטי״ץ; Darmesteter (1909, p. 49) reads *enprunteç* (modern *emprunté*), “borrowed.”

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: And he worshipped the LORD there
1 Samuel.english_translation: Samuel; and some say Elkanah.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Neither is there any rock like our God
1 Samuel.english_translation: There is no artist (*tzayyar*) like our God — He who forms a form within a form.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: talk no more so exceedingly proudly
1 Samuel.english_translation: All the proud, whose hour is successful; and because of Peninnah, who was boasting over her, she speaks. According to its plain sense, and according to its homiletical interpretation, [it is] as its Targum that Jonathan translated.

A strong thing. Another explanation: an expression of departure (*sarah*), like (Genesis 12:8): “and he removed (*vayatek*) from thence unto the mountain” — let no word of deviation (*sarah*) come out of your mouth.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: For the LORD is a God of knowledge
1 Samuel.english_translation: He knows what is in your hearts.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: And by Him actions are weighed
1 Samuel.english_translation: All the deeds of man are counted before Him.
An expression of counting, like (Exodus 5:18): “and the tale of bricks (*tokhen levenim*) shall ye deliver.”

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: The bows of the mighty men are broken
1 Samuel.english_translation: Such is the craft of the Holy One, blessed be He: He weakens the mighty and strengthens the weak, satisfies the hungry and makes the satisfied hungry.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: They that were full have hired out themselves for bread
1 Samuel.english_translation: And they did not need to be hired for any work; He makes them hungry, and they are hired for bread, their sustenance.
Who were toiling and laboring for food.
From their toil.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: so that the barren hath born seven, and she that hath many children languisheth, etc.
1 Samuel.english_translation: And while the barren bears seven sons, she who has many children pines away and buries her children. Hannah bore seven, as it is said (below v. 21): “for the Lord visited Hannah, and she conceived, and bore three sons and two daughters”; and when Hannah bears one, Peninnah buries two. And she had ten children, as it is said (above 1:8): “Am not I better to thee than ten sons?” — [that is,] of Peninnah. When Hannah bore four, Peninnah buried eight; and when she became pregnant and bore a fifth child, Peninnah prostrated herself at her feet and begged for mercy, and they lived and were called by her name. These are the words of Rabbi Nehemiah. Rabbi Judah says: grandchildren are as children. And some say: seven — in gematria equal to the number of Samuel.
1 Samuel.translator_note: The numbers are translated as printed; the verse cited (2:21) lists three sons and two daughters.

1 Samuel.english_translation: *Chasido* is written, *chasidav* is read: whether singular or plural; and so “they that strive with the Lord shall be broken” (v. 10): *meribav* [or] *meribo*, whether singular or plural.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: against him will He thunder in heaven (alav ba-shamayim yar'em)
1 Samuel.english_translation: *Alo* is written: even if they went up into heaven, He thunders against them and brings them down.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: the Lord shall judge the ends of the earth (yadin afsei aretz)
1 Samuel.english_translation: He judges them and chastises them: *justiçér* in Old French.
1 Samuel.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is יושטיציי״א; Darmesteter (1909, p. 49) reads *justiçér* (modern *juger*), “(God) judges.”

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: did minister unto the LORD before Eli the priest
1 Samuel.english_translation: From here [we learn] that one who serves the face of Torah scholars is like one who serves the Divine Presence.
They fixed for themselves this rule, and they had no inheritance except the breast and the thigh of the peace-offerings.
A pot.
A cauldron.
A frying pan.
An expression of contempt.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: a child, girded with a linen ephod
1 Samuel.english_translation: (Targum:) *kardut de-butz*; and it is an expression for a robe (*me'il*), for Jonathan translated (2 Samuel 13:18) “*me'ilim*” (“robes”) — [from the verse] “for with such robes were the king's daughters that were virgins apparelled” — as *kardutin*.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: his mother made him a little robe
1 Samuel.english_translation: From year to year.
A present-tense form: he used to bless him every year.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: for the loan which was lent
1 Samuel.english_translation: [She asked] for him a son, and he said to him: “The Lord give thee seed,” etc.; may it be [His] will that all the children that shall be yours be from this righteous woman; and this is an inverted verse.

According to its plain sense. And our Rabbis said (Yoma 9a): because they delayed their [the women's] offerings of birds, and the women were waiting until they saw their offerings brought near, Scripture counts it against them as if they had lain with them.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: I hear the Lord's people to transgress (asher anokhi shome'a ma'avirim am Adonai)
1 Samuel.english_translation: A report that the Lord's people spread about you, an expression like (Exodus 36:6) “and they caused a voice to pass through the camp”: they put out a voice about you, an evil report.
An expression of judgment, like (Exodus 21:22): “and he shall pay as the judges determine (*bifelilim*).”
A judge.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: because the LORD would slay them
1 Samuel.english_translation: For the decree of judgment had already been sealed; but before the decree of judgment was sealed, it is said (Ezekiel 18:32): “For I have no pleasure in the death of him that dieth.”

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: And there came a man of God
1 Samuel.english_translation: This is Elkanah.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: did I plainly reveal myself unto the house of thy father
1 Samuel.english_translation: From here [we learn] that Aaron prophesied in Egypt; and what was the prophecy? It is what is said (Ezekiel 20:7): “and I said unto them: Cast you away every man the detestable things of his eyes, and defile not yourselves with the idols of Egypt.”
1 Samuel.translator_note: Audit 4: the English now follows JPS exactly (“Cast you away”); Rashi’s Hebrew matches Ezekiel 20:7.

1 Samuel.english_translation: Did you know that this good and this greatness I gave to Aaron?

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: I have commanded in My habitation
1 Samuel.english_translation: Which I commanded in My dwelling.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: to make yourselves fat with the chiefest
1 Samuel.english_translation: This is an inverted verse: “and honorest thy sons above Me, for My people” — before the eyes of My people you honored your sons above Me; and what is the honor? “to make yourselves fat with the chiefest of all the offerings of Israel”: your meal preceded My meal, as it is said (above v. 15): “Also before they burned the fat,” etc.
An expression of a meal, like (2 Samuel 13:5): “let my sister Tamar come, and give me bread to eat (*vetivreni lechem*).”
It refers back to “and honorest thy sons above Me”: you showed My people that you are honored above Me; and by what did you show it? “to make yourselves fat with the chiefest of My offering.”

Twice I fixed greatness for the sons of Ithamar: of the sons of Gershon and of the sons of Merari it is said (Numbers 4:28, 33): “under the hand of Ithamar the son of Aaron the priest”; and Eli was of the sons of Ithamar. This I saw in the Midrash of Samuel; and I heard a more fitting expression than this: “I said indeed that thy house and the house of thy father,” etc. At first I gave the high priesthood to Eleazar the priest, as it is said (Numbers 20:26): “and strip Aaron of his garments,” etc.; and in the days of the concubine [at Gibeah], when Israel were lax in most of the commandments — and who caused them [to be]? Phinehas and the like, for it was for them to go about from city to city and rebuke them — I took the high priesthood away from them and gave it to you, for you are of the sons of Ithamar; and I said: “they shall walk before Me for ever,” for when greatness is fixed for a man, it is fixed for him and for his generations forever.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: for them that honour Me I will honour
1 Samuel.english_translation: The sons of Phinehas, who honored Me in Shittim (Numbers 25:11); and so it was in the days of Solomon, when the Temple was built: (1 Kings 2:27) “So Solomon thrust out Abiathar from being priest unto the Lord, that he might fulfil the word of the Lord, which He spoke concerning the house of Eli”; and Zadok became high priest in his place, for he was of the sons of Phinehas, as they trace their descent in Chronicles (1 Chronicles 6:38).

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and they that despise Me shall be lightly esteemed
1 Samuel.english_translation: Of themselves, after I depart from them.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: I will cut off thine arm
1 Samuel.english_translation: The strength that you have in My house, that you say: “and if not, I will take it by force.”

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: And thou shalt behold a rival in My habitation
1 Samuel.english_translation: And you shall see your rival at your side within My dwelling, like a woman who sees her rival with her in the house.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: in all the wealth which God shall give Israel (be-khol asher yetiv et Yisrael)
1 Samuel.english_translation: When the Eternal House shall be built, in the days of Solomon, and the good of Israel will be complete, as it is said there (1 Kings 8:56): “there hath not failed one word of all His good promise”; (ibid. 5:1) “Judah and Israel were many, as the sand which is by the sea shore,” etc.; (ibid. 5:5) “And Judah and Israel dwelt safely, every man under his vine and under his fig-tree, all the days of Solomon.”
1 Samuel.translator_note: The printed reference for the quotation about the sand is 1 Kings 5:1; the words (“Judah and Israel were many as the sand…”) stand at 1 Kings 4:20 of the Hebrew text, and the Hebrew text there reads “which is by the sea,” not “by the sea shore.”

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and there shall not be an old man in thy house
1 Samuel.english_translation: Measure for measure: you ate sacred things before their time, before they burned the fat; so you too shall die before your time.
Like *ule-da'ev*.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: shall die in the flower of their age (yamutu anashim)
1 Samuel.english_translation: Young men: the mourning for a young man is not like the mourning for an infant.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: And this shall be the sign unto thee
1 Samuel.english_translation: That the matter will come to pass: on one day your two sons will die, and it shall be a sign for you that all the calamity that was said to you will be fulfilled: “and thou shalt behold a rival in My habitation,” and “all the increase of thy house shall die as men.”
This is Zadok.
In order to earn a *ma'ah* of silver.
From the weights: it is twenty *gerah* (Exodus 30:13).
Gather me (*aspheni*).
Was withheld; and so (Proverbs 17:27): “a man of understanding is of a precious (*yekar*) spirit” — withheld in words, a man who understands.
(Targum:) “there was no revealed prophecy.” *Nifratz* is an expression like (Genesis 28:14): “and thou shalt spread abroad (*ufaratzta*) to the west and to the east.”
In his place, in the court of the Levites who guard the Temple; and so Jonathan translated: “and Samuel lay in the court of the Levites.”

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: in the temple of the LORD
1 Samuel.english_translation: Where the Ark of God was.

And a voice came out of the sanctuary of the Lord, from the house of the Holy of Holies, which called Samuel; the end of the upper verse is connected to the beginning of the lower verse. This is what Scripture says (Job 37:5): “God thundereth marvellously with His voice.” Eli was a priest and was keeping watch inside, and Samuel was a Levite and was lying down outside, and the voice leaped by way of Eli to Samuel; in tractate Tamid.
1 Samuel.translator_note: Audit 4: spelling set to JPS (“marvellously”).

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: before he knew the Lord (terem yeda et Adonai)
1 Samuel.english_translation: He was not yet acquainted with the matter of the voice of prophecy. Every *terem* in Scripture is an expression of “not yet,” as its Targum [renders it] “*ad la*,” and it is not an expression of “before”; and this will prove it, and further, (Exodus 9:30): “for ye will not yet fear” (*terem tire'un*) — explained by it; and so (Genesis 2:5): “and every plant of the field before it was in the earth” (*terem yihyeh*).
And he did not mention the Name of the Omnipresent, as Eli had commanded him; he said: Perhaps it is another voice.
It is the taking of the Ark by the Philistines.
An expression for cymbals (*tziltzalim*), *tentiner* in Old French.
1 Samuel.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is טנטיני״ר; Darmesteter (1909, p. 49) reads *tentiner* (“they will ring”).

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: when I begin, I will also make an end (hachel vechaleh)
1 Samuel.english_translation: On that day My decree upon the house of Eli will begin, that Hophni and Phinehas will die; and from here on I will finish My decree and complete it upon them from generation to generation, causing them to die as men of eighteen years.
*Acomencement*, *aesplaiement* in Old French.
1 Samuel.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is אקומיינצ״ט אאישפליימנ״ט; Darmesteter (1909, p. 49) reads *coménçant é esplayant* (“beginning and ending”).

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: because his sons made themselves vile (mekallelim lahem)
1 Samuel.english_translation: “Me” (*li*) he should have said, but Scripture used a euphemism.
Treating lightly (*mekilim*); and so every *kelalah* is an expression of lightness and contempt.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and he restrained them not (velo kihah)
1 Samuel.english_translation: He did not dim (*hikhah*) their faces, to remove them from their greatness.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: so do God to thee (koh ya'aseh lekha)
1 Samuel.english_translation: Like that same curse: that you shall not have worthy sons; and so it was fulfilled in him; and even though he told him and did not hide [it], from here they said (Makkot 11a): the curse of a sage, even if conditional, comes true.
He is the Master, and everything is His.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: for the LORD revealed Himself to Samuel
1 Samuel.english_translation: Since it said above “and the word of the Lord was precious in those days,” it says here: for from now on, for Samuel's sake, He revealed Himself, and repeated, and became accustomed to be revealed.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: And the word of Samuel came to all Israel
1 Samuel.english_translation: The word that was said to Samuel came to pass and came upon all Israel, and how the calamity was: and Israel went out to meet the Philistines to battle.
It was not yet named so, for in the days of Samuel it was so called (below 7:12), and here He called it after its end.
The battle spread out, like (below 30:16): “and, behold, they were spread abroad (*netushim*) upon all the face of the earth”; and so (Judges 15:9): “and spread themselves (*vayinatshu*) in Lehi.”

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: with all manner of plagues and in the wilderness
1 Samuel.english_translation: At the Red Sea; and Jonathan translated: “and for His people He did *perishan* in the wilderness.” And in the Sifrei we learned: this section is a mixture of words; whoever said this did not say that. The upright among them said: “Who shall deliver us out of the hand of these mighty gods?” And the wicked said: “These are the gods that smote Egypt with all the plagues” — all the plagues that He had, He brought upon the Egyptians; He has no more plague now.
This was Saul, who snatched the Tablets from the hand of Goliath and fled.
Beside the wayside he was watching.
*Afrakuteh* (Aramaic): the bone of the neck.

By necessity its meaning is *laledet* (“to bear”), and it has no parallel; and Menahem connected it with the root of *yelalah* (“wailing”), because her birth pangs came upon her with wailing; and the root of *yelalah* has no letter in its root but *lamed* alone.
Changed from their usual way; therefore she died.
The hinges of the doors of her belly, *chardonnail* in Old French.
1 Samuel.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is קרדוני״ל; Darmesteter (1909, p. 49) reads *chardonail* (formed from *cardin[em]* + *aculum*) and renders it “les gonds” (the hinges).

1 Samuel.english_translation: No glory (*ein kavod*); and so (Job 22:30): “He will deliver the one who is not innocent (*i naki*)” — one who is not innocent.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: because the ark of God was taken
1 Samuel.english_translation: Like *al ha-lakach*; and there is no need to move it from the sense of *el*, for one who knows how to understand its speech.
*Étavirs l'estre pris* in Old French.
1 Samuel.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is איטיויר״ש לאישטריפו״ש; Darmesteter (1909, p. 49) reads *étvairs le estre pris* (*étvairs* = Old French *estovoir*, “to be due”), and renders it “because of the taking (literally: due to be taken) of the ark.”

1 Samuel.english_translation: And [because of] this misfortune, that her father-in-law and her husband had died.
An image made in the likeness of a fish (*dag*).
The doorstep (*askuppah*).
An expression of desolation.
*Chalcholet*, *karkesha*: a plague of the orifice; mice enter into their orifices and pull out their intestines, and come out.
1 Samuel.translator_note: The word karkesha (כרכשא) is left untransliterated in meaning; the description is translated literally.

1 Samuel.english_translation: Like *vayisteru* (with a *samekh*), for it is in the Masorah: [letters] written with *shin* and explained with an expression of *samekh*; the plague of the house of the secret places.

All confusions (*mehumot*) come by means of thunder, and this is their father: (below 7:10) “But the Lord thundered with a great thunder (on that day) upon the Philistines, and discomfited them” (*vayehummem*). So it is explained in the aggadah of the “Thirty-two Rules” of Rabbi Eliezer the son of Rabbi Yose the Galilean.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: wherewith shall we send it (bameh neshallchenu)
1 Samuel.english_translation: In what manner shall we send it, so that His anger may not burn and His wrath may turn away from us.
A sign of a matter in which you admit that you trespassed.
You shall be healed, and it shall be known to you that it was He who did it; for why else should His hand not turn away from you then?
They are five, as it is said (in Joshua 13:3): “the Gazite, and the Ashdodite, the Ashkelonite, the Gittite, and the Ekronite.”
Nursing ones.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: on which there hath come no yoke
1 Samuel.english_translation: All this is a test: these are not fit to draw; and further, they low after their calves; and if the Ark has the power that they bring it of themselves, we shall know that it was He who did this to us.
*Escrinio* in Old French.
1 Samuel.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is שקריניי״ו; Darmesteter (1909, p. 50) reads *eskrin* and renders it “écrin” (a casket).

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and shut up at home (kalu va-bayit)
1 Samuel.english_translation: An expression of confinement.

This word is androgynous [both masculine and feminine in form]; it teaches that even the calves were reciting song: “*Roni, roni ha-shittah hitnofefi*,” etc., as is stated in tractate Avodah Zarah (24b). And according to its plain sense, *vayyashrnah* is an expression of “a straight way”: they went straight.
1 Samuel.translator_note: The quotation רוני רוני השיטה התנופפי is transliterated as printed; I have not translated it because its meaning is uncertain.

1 Samuel.english_translation: An expression of the lowing of cattle, *ge'iyah*.
Israelites were there.
A village that has no wall.

It is the great stone mentioned above, [the word being written with] a *lamed* in place of a *nun*, and so *nishkah* in place of *lishkah*, in the Book of Nehemiah (13:7); and because mourning (*evel*) befell them in the matter, he called it *Abel*.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: seventy men, and fifty thousand men
1 Samuel.english_translation: Jonathan translated: “and he slew among the elders of the people seventy men, and in the congregation fifty thousand men.” And our Rabbis said (Sotah 35b): “seventy men” — each one was equal to fifty thousand; or “fifty thousand men” — each equal to seventy Sanhedrins.
Designated.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: from the day that the ark abode in Kiriath-jearim
1 Samuel.english_translation: And they saw the calamity that came upon them for the sin of the house of Eli, and the might that the Holy One, blessed be He, wrought against the Philistines.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and all the house of Israel lamented after the Lord (vayinahu … acharei Adonai)
1 Samuel.english_translation: Through Samuel, who went around from city to city, judging them and rebuking them.

An expression of drawing, and it is Aramaic: *titnahu lefulchani* (“you will draw him to worship”); and so (Ezekiel 7:11): “nor any of their wealth, nor *noah* among them” (*velo noah bahem*) — there is no benefit in them to draw them to the good. And Menahem connected *vayinahu* as an expression of wailing, as (Micah 2:4): “lament with a doleful lamentation” (*nehi nihyah*), and so (Ezekiel, ibid.) “*velo noah bahem*”; and the explanation of *vayinahu acharei Adonai* is that they mourned over their evil deeds and returned after the Lord. Another explanation: *vayinahu* is like (Jeremiah 3:17): “and all the nations shall be gathered unto it” (*venikvu elehah*), which we translate: “and all the nations shall be led to worship in it”; and from this matter also (Ezekiel, ibid.): “*velo noah bahem*,” like what it says there: “not of them, nor of their multitude,” and not *manah* among them, that is, not of their gathering (other books: it is not so).
1 Samuel.translator_note: This comment is complex and partly garbled in the printed text; it is translated literally. The Targum quotation titnahu lefulchani is as printed.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and drew water, and poured it out
1 Samuel.english_translation: Jonathan translated: “and they poured out their hearts in repentance like water before the Lord.” And according to its plain meaning, it is only a sign of submission: Behold, we are before You like this water that is poured out.
Between a man and his fellow, over their monetary dealings, or over matters of transgression that they had committed.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and offered it for a burnt-offering (vaya'aleh olah)
1 Samuel.english_translation: *Vaya'aleh* is written: it was a female; from here our Rabbis learned: a female burnt-offering is valid on a private high place, in tractate Avodah Zarah (24b).
Lower than Beth-sharon.
The tooth (*shen*) of the rock.
They themselves.

Another explanation: that is, the justice. And our Rabbis said (Shabbat 56a): the sons of Samuel did not sin; rather, they did not walk in their father's ways, for he used to go around to all the places of Israel and judge them in their cities, and they did not do so, in order to increase the reward of their attendants and their scribes.
Because they said: “to judge us like all the nations.”

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: solemnly protest unto them (ha-ed ta'id bahem)
1 Samuel.english_translation: Warn them, so that the fear of their king may be upon them.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and to make his instruments of war
1 Samuel.english_translation: To make them craftsmen, smiths and carpenters.
Preparers of unguents and perfumes, for the cosmetics of his wives.
In the land in which there is a prophet.
Like *tzofeh* (“seer”).

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: lest my father leave off caring for the asses
1 Samuel.english_translation: So that our worry over him will grow, until he forgets the asses.
*Itobitarah* in Old French.
1 Samuel.translator_note: The printed Old French word is איטוביטאר״ה. Darmesteter's collection has no entry at this verse; at 10:2 he lists, for the same Hebrew word, a form read *démentér*. I cannot identify the printed word, and I give no translation of it.

1 Samuel.english_translation: The matter of the asses, what became of them, for on their account we went all this way.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: what shall we bring the man
1 Samuel.english_translation: Jonathan translated: “if he takes money, what is [the pledge] for the man.” Saul did not know the deeds of Samuel, and thought that he would ask for payment.

Jonathan translated: *umidam dekhasher* (“and something fitting”), an expression of straightness (*yosher*). And Menahem interpreted: *teshurah* is an expression of offering, [for] seeing the face of a king or an important person — an expression like “I shall behold him (*ashurennu*)” (Numbers 24:17); and his words seem right.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: the fourth part of a shekel
1 Samuel.english_translation: One silver *zuz*.
The writer wrote this; and it is not from the words of Saul's lad.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: for he that is now called a prophet
1 Samuel.english_translation: He who is called a prophet today was called a “seer” beforetime.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: As soon as you are come into the city, you shall straightway find him
1 Samuel.english_translation: They [the maidens] lingered in their words, in order to look at the beauty of Saul.
Jonathan translated: “to the house of *asachruta*.” Once Shiloh was destroyed, the high places were permitted, and they used to offer peace-offerings on a high place and eat together.

Jonathan translated: “for he breaks bread (*hu faris mezona*)”: he breaks over the food. Over peace-offerings they bless upon eating them: “Blessed art Thou, Lord our God, King of the universe, who hast sanctified us by His commandments and commanded us to eat the sacrifice.”
As the day stands.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: shall reign over my people (ya'tzor be-ammi)
1 Samuel.english_translation: He shall rule (other books: not so), like (Deuteronomy 32:36): “shut up and left” (*atzur ve-azuv*). Such is the way of a ruler: to restrain the people in war, so that they do not scatter and do not spread apart from one another, and to restrain each one from doing evil. In our language we call it *ma'atzor* (restraint); *kierestenir* in Old French.
1 Samuel.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is קירשטני״ר. Darmesteter (1909, p. 50) lists several manuscript forms for “he will keep my people in good order”; he reads *déstenir* (modern *maintenir*).

1 Samuel.english_translation: Jonathan translated: *ve-ara* (“and approached”).

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: And on whom is all the desire of Israel?
1 Samuel.english_translation: Here he came to hint to him the matter of kingship.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: in the chiefest place among them that were bidden
1 Samuel.english_translation: In the place of the banquet of the great ones, for by the arrangement of their reclining it was recognizable in which place the great one reclines.
Because Samuel knew that Saul would come, he commanded that a fine portion be given to him for his need.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: the shoulder and that which was upon it (et ha-shok ve-he-alayah)
1 Samuel.english_translation: The shank and the thigh that is above it.
From the portions of those invited, and it was set apart for your need.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: set it before thee and eat
1 Samuel.english_translation: In the last chapter of Zevachim (120a): we hold that the breast and thigh [are given] on a great high place, and there is no breast and thigh on a small high place; therefore it was permitted for Saul to eat.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: because unto the appointed time hath it been kept for thee
1 Samuel.english_translation: For the time of eating this thigh had been kept for your need.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: saying: I have invited the people
1 Samuel.english_translation: My saying was to the cook of the people: I invited for the meal, and I know their number, and be careful with their portions; and I gave him the portions according to their number, and this one is kept for your need.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and he communed with Saul upon the roof
1 Samuel.english_translation: He rebukes him and teaches him to fear the Holy One, blessed be He.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and he passed on before us
1 Samuel.english_translation: And he went far from him, and did not hear our words.
The lad [passed on] before them; and to Saul he said: And you, stand with me.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: by Rachel's sepulchre in the border of Benjamin
1 Samuel.english_translation: But is not Rachel's sepulchre in the border of Judah, in Bethlehem? Rather, now they are at Rachel's sepulchre, and when you meet them you will find them in the border of Benjamin, in Zelzah; so it is taught in the Tosefta of Sotah (chapter 11).
The shade (*tzel*) for the brightness (*latzach*) of the Holy One, blessed be He, who is white and ruddy; and it is Jerusalem.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and take thought for you (vedaag lakhem)
1 Samuel.english_translation: He will fear for you; every expression of *dagah* is an expression of fear: *dushtir* in Old French.
1 Samuel.translator_note: The printed Old French word is דושטי״ר. Darmesteter (1909, p. 50) lists for this verse (“il s'inquiétera,” he will be anxious) forms read *démentér*; the printed form differs from those I could read, and I could not match it.

1 Samuel.english_translation: The plain of Tabor.
The hill of Kiriath-jearim, where the Ark of God is now.
Soldiers whom they appointed over Israel, who were ruling in it, and they station garrisons (*netzivim*) in the cities of Israel.
Jonathan translated: “a company of scribes.” *Chevel* means a company, and so (2 Samuel 22:6): “the cords of Sheol compassed me about” — “the host of the wicked surrounded me.”
Jonathan translated: “from the house of *asachruta*.”

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and let these signs come unto thee
1 Samuel.english_translation: And you will know that my words are true; and just as these signs came to you, so the matter of the kingship will be fulfilled.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: do as thy hand shall find
1 Samuel.english_translation: Prepare for yourself royal garments, and make ready for yourself the arrangements of kingship, as you are able.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: And thou shalt go down before me to Gilgal
1 Samuel.english_translation: And after you reign, you shall go down to Gilgal before me, before I go down.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and, behold, I will come down unto thee
1 Samuel.english_translation: At the end of seven days, after you go down.
Wait.
A spirit of royal might.
What is your wonder at the matter “who is the father of prophets”? Is prophecy an inheritance?

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: but of the matter of the kingdom he told him not
1 Samuel.english_translation: There was modesty in him.
Even though he was not there, the lot fell upon him, for their names were written on letters and put in a box, and the prophet put in his hand and took out one letter.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: he hath hid himself among the baggage
1 Samuel.english_translation: In the house where those who arrived had put down their vessels, for he was fleeing from greatness. And an aggadic Midrash of Rabbi Tanchuma: “and unto the *keilim*” — by the Urim and Thummim; he said: perhaps I am not fit for greatness until they ask by the Urim and Thummim; and they asked, and it came up in his hand.
“Men who fear sin, in whose hearts the fear from before the Lord had been placed.”

According to its plain sense. And an aggadic Midrash (Yalkut Shimoni, section 111): “Bring me the book of your Torah that was given from the right [hand], and I shall burn it, because it is written in it (Deuteronomy 23:4): ‘An Ammonite or a Moabite shall not enter,’ etc.”
Blasphemy.
After the appointed time of the coming of the herd from the field.
Of his cattle.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: And he numbered them in Bezek
1 Samuel.english_translation: Our Rabbis said (Yoma 22b): with potsherds (some versions: not so). Another explanation: *Bezek* — with stones, in that he took a stone from each one and counted them; like (below 15:4) “and numbered them in Telaim,” where he took a lamb from each one and counted them with them, just as they used to count them by half-shekels. And [Jonathan] translated (Proverbs 26:8): “as a bag of stone in a sling” as *heikh bizka de-kheifa be-kala'a*. And in the Yelammedenu: “and numbered them in Telaim” — when they are poor, with these *bizkayya* [pebbles]; when they are rich, with these lambs (*imraya*). Another explanation: *Bezek* is the name of a place mentioned in the Book of Judges (1:5): “and they found Adoni-bezek in Bezek.”
In language of contempt: “Shall Saul reign over us?” — give those men and we will put them to death.
In astonishment.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and Samuel said … and renew the kingdom there
1 Samuel.english_translation: Because at first they were contesting the matter, and now all were pleased.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and I am old and grayheaded
1 Samuel.english_translation: Our Rabbis said: old age leaped upon him, as stated in tractate Taanit (5b).
For my work.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: or whose ass have I taken?
1 Samuel.english_translation: When I used to go from city to city to judge them concerning their needs, I used to go on my own ass, and I could have taken from theirs.
Every expression of *ratzah* that is adjacent to *oshek* is an expression of oppressed and crushed (*ratzutz*): robbing the poor and crushing.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: or of whose hand have I received any bribe to blind mine eyes therewith? (ve-a'lim einai bo)
1 Samuel.english_translation: In order to hide my eyes from judgment for the sake of money.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and I will restore it you
1 Samuel.english_translation: Whatever you say.
A heavenly voice goes forth and says: “Witness.” And this is one of three places where the Holy Spirit appeared in the court below, as stated in tractate Makkot (23b).

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: that appointed Moses and Aaron (asher asah et Moshe ve-et Aharon)
1 Samuel.english_translation: To be ready for His mission, to bring your fathers out of Egypt.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: that I may plead with you
1 Samuel.english_translation: I will contend with you.
This is Samson, who came from the tribe of Dan.

Behold, [there are] three light ones of the world with three weighty ones of the world — Moses, Aaron and Samuel — to tell you that the light one in his generation is like the weighty one in his generation: every court that is appointed over the generation, one must go after it as if it were the mightiest of the mighty.
And you shall endure for length of days, both you and the king.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: then shall the hand of the Lord be against you, as it was against your fathers
1 Samuel.english_translation: That is: it will be against you after it was against your fathers. And our Rabbis said (Yevamot 63b): “against you and against your fathers” — *chatuti shechvei*: it is a plague of contempt upon the dead.
1 Samuel.translator_note: The phrase חטוטי שכבי is transliterated as printed; I read it as “the digging up of those who lie [buried],” but I am not certain.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: now therefore stand and see, etc.
1 Samuel.english_translation: And just as by my prayer I can change the seasons, so if war had befallen you there was power in my prayer to stand against the enemy; and you did not need to ask for a king in my lifetime, even though I am old.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Is it not wheat harvest to-day
1 Samuel.english_translation: And rains are a sign of a curse, and it is hard in the eyes of the Holy One, blessed be He, to bring calamity for nothing; nevertheless there is power in me, and I will call unto the Lord, and He shall send thunder and rain.
That you had no need to ask for a king, in order to belittle me.
That His name is called upon you, that He is your Savior, and so that the name of His greatness may not be diminished.
He swore, like (below 14:24): “and Saul adjured (*vayo'el*) the people.”
1 Samuel.translator_note: The printed reference is 14:25; the quoted words stand at 1 Samuel 14:24 of the Hebrew text.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: moreover as for me, God forbid that I …
1 Samuel.english_translation: Since you will do your part, to return to the Lord, so too, God forbid that I should cease praying on your behalf.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Saul was [a son of] one year when he began to reign
1 Samuel.english_translation: Our Rabbis of blessed memory said (Yoma 22b): like a son of one year, who had not tasted the taste of sin. And one can interpret: “Saul was a son of one year in his reign” — in the first year in which he was made king; and he reigned two years over Israel; and in the first year, immediately: “And Saul chose him three thousand men.”
A soldier whom they had over Israel, and they stationed him in Gibeah of Benjamin.
That we have rebelled against the Philistines, so that they [the Philistines] should be on guard against them.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and Israel also was had in abomination (nivash)
1 Samuel.english_translation: Their savor stank among the Philistines — an expression of hatred.
This is what Samuel said to him (above 10:8): “and thou shalt go down before me to Gilgal.”
On the east of Beth-aven.
A place where thorns are gathered: *espinei* in Old French.
1 Samuel.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is שפנ״י; Darmesteter (1909, p. 50) reads *espinéyd*, from *spinetum*, and renders it “dans les ronces” (in the brambles).

1 Samuel.english_translation: *Pleisheiz* in Old French.
1 Samuel.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is פליישי״ץ; Darmesteter (1909, p. 50) reads *pleisediç* and renders it “dans les clairières” (in the clearings).

1 Samuel.english_translation: Hollows.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: went over the Jordan to the land of Gad
1 Samuel.english_translation: To flee from the Philistines, for the Philistines were in the land of Canaan, on the west side of the Jordan.
They hurried to go after him.
He waited.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: according to the set time that Samuel had appointed
1 Samuel.english_translation: This verse is missing one word: “for the set time that Samuel appointed” (*asher sam Shmuel*) or “for the set time of Samuel” (*asher le-Shmuel*); and a parallel to it (2 Samuel 4:2): “and two men were captains of bands [for] the son of Saul” — he should have written “for the son of Saul”; so too here “*asher le-Shmuel*,” for he said to him (above 10:8): “seven days shalt thou tarry, till I come to thee.”

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: bring hither the burnt-offering to me
1 Samuel.english_translation: A non-priest is permitted to offer on a high place.
Did I not say to you, “Behold, I come down unto thee to offer the burnt-offering” — I will offer it, and not you.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: at the set time of the days (le-mo'ed ha-yamim)
1 Samuel.english_translation: At the beginning of the day.
I strengthened myself against my will; for my heart said to wait for you, [and] against my will I set my heart and I offered the burnt-offering.
Before you did this.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: would the LORD have established thy kingdom upon Israel for ever
1 Samuel.english_translation: For when greatness is fixed for a man, it is fixed for him and for his generations (Megillah 13b).

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: But now thy kingdom shall not continue
1 Samuel.english_translation: For so Moses said in the Torah (Deuteronomy 17:20): “that he turn not aside from the commandment, to the right hand or to the left; to the end that he may prolong his days,” etc. Hence, if he turns aside, he will not prolong his days. And if you say that this was not said concerning the command of a prophet, but concerning a command of the Torah — behold, it was already said (ibid. v. 19): “to keep all the words of this law,” and afterward: “that his heart be not lifted up … and that he turn not aside from the commandment” — even from the command of a prophet.
For the people had scattered from him, and these remained.

In which the *tzevo'im* are found; this is what we learned: Rabbi Meir says: also the *tzavua*. And Jonathan translated: *af'aya*. And so our Rabbis of blessed memory explained (Bava Kamma 16a): the *tzavua* is the *af'eh* (viper), a kind of evil and harmful reptile.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Now there was no smith found
1 Samuel.english_translation: He was not found at the beginning of the reign of Saul; for the Philistines, who ruled over Israel, had removed all the iron-smiths from Israel, lest they make weapons to fight with.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: but all Israel went down to the Philistines
1 Samuel.english_translation: And when Israel needed iron-smiths to sharpen the mattocks, axes and plowshares, they were obliged to go down to the land of the Philistines.
*Soc* in Old French.
1 Samuel.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is שו״ק; Darmesteter (1909, p. 50) reads *soc* (a plowshare).

1 Samuel.english_translation: *Coltre* in Old French.
1 Samuel.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is קולטר״א; Darmesteter (1909, p. 50) reads *coltre* (“son coutre,” his coulter).

1 Samuel.english_translation: *Besagur* in Old French.
1 Samuel.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is בשגו״ר; Darmesteter (1909, p. 50) reads *besagude* (*bis* + *acuta*), a battle-axe (compare modern *besaiguë*).

1 Samuel.english_translation: *Fosoir* in Old French.
1 Samuel.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is פישוייר״א; Darmesteter (1909, p. 50) reads *fosuir*, from *fossorium*, and renders it “sa bêche” (his spade).

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and the file was for the mattocks (vehayetah ha-petzirah fim lamacharashot)
1 Samuel.english_translation: And those who had the trouble of going down to the Philistines to sharpen had the *petzirah pim*: a file, *lime* in Old French, which has *hefetz pi'ot*, that is, many mouths and edges; they had it to sharpen the plowshare and the plow-points.
1 Samuel.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is לימ״א; Darmesteter (1909, p. 50) reads *lime* (“la lime,” the file).

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and for the three-pronged fork (ulshalosh kilshon)
1 Samuel.english_translation: A fork made like an *eter*, which is called *forche* in Old French, and it has three teeth.
1 Samuel.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is פורקד״א; Darmesteter (1909, p. 50) reads *forche* (“fourche,” fork), noting that manuscript W has *forje* and *aguylon*. The word עתר is left untranslated.

1 Samuel.english_translation: To sharpen it at its head, to fix it and set it in the *mardea* (goad-handle).

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and there was found for Saul
1 Samuel.english_translation: By means of a miracle.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: And the garrison of the Philistines
1 Samuel.english_translation: It is the way of soldiers to make from them a garrison and a destroying band; they are the ones who spread out and run after the spoil to the city, which is called *cenbel* in Old French.
1 Samuel.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is צנבי״ל; Darmesteter (1909, p. 51) reads *cênbel* and renders it “troupe qui s'égaille pour piller” (a troop that scatters to plunder).

1 Samuel.english_translation: They are posts (*netzivim*) to guard, so that the destroyers should not go out from the city against them.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: went out to the pass of Michmash
1 Samuel.english_translation: The Philistines were encamped in Michmash, and Michmash is on a mountain, and Israel was in a city called Geba, and Geba was at the top of the mountain, and there were two mountains facing each other, with the ravine between them, as is said in the account. And the garrison of the Philistines approached the pass of Michmash on the side of Geba, to the ravine between them.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Now there was a certain man
1 Samuel.english_translation: All is in order: Moses delivered the Torah to Joshua, and Joshua to the elders, and one judge to another judge, until it reached Eli, and from him to Samuel, as we learned (Avot 1:1): “and the elders to the prophets.”
There were two heights that look out and see one another. And Jonathan translated: *tzofim* — “from the disciples of the prophets.”
He was a Levite, of the sons of Abiasaph son of Korah; so he traces his lineage in Chronicles (1 Chronicles 5:8).

Jonathan translated: “from the mountain of Beth-Ephraim (in the hill-country of Ephraim).” And an aggadic Midrash (Yalkut Shimoni, Samuel, remez 77): “Ephrathite” — son of a palace Abginos, an important man, like (Bava Metzia 119a): “a palanquin was brought to Rabbi Simeon” — an expression of grace.
1 Samuel.translator_note: *Abginos* (אבגינוס) is transliterated as printed.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: am not I better to thee
1 Samuel.english_translation: One who loves thee.
Whom Peninnah bore me.
You are not a master in this matter; you showed yourself that the Holy Spirit does not rest upon you, so that you would know that I am not drunk with wine.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: My mouth is enlarged over mine enemies
1 Samuel.english_translation: Over Peninnah.
They were looking at how it came alone, and in their joy they treated it lightly, for they were not looking at it with awe and in a respectful way.
This is Gideon.

Every “*halaz*” and “*lazeh*” in Scripture is not an expression of “this,” but an expression of something opposite him, and he points it out with a finger; and in Old French it is not an expression of *cest* in Old French, but *cil* in Old French.
1 Samuel.translator_note: Old French glosses: the printed Hebrew spellings are ציש״ט and ציי״ל. Darmesteter (1909, p. 51) reads *cil* (“celui-là,” which points to what is opposite; he says it is not the sense of the French) and, separately, *cest*.

1 Samuel.english_translation: The ravine of the two mountains.
1 Samuel.translator_note: The Hebrew reads גי, which I take to be a short form of גיא (“ravine”).

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: in the uttermost part of Gibeah
1 Samuel.english_translation: At the end of the hill.
The Urim and Thummim.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: And between the passes, by which Jonathan sought to go over
1 Samuel.english_translation: It was made thus: the tooth of the rock was on the one side, opposite the passes on this side, and the tooth of the rock opposite the passes on that side; the ravine is called “between the passes”; and it had a rock here and a rock there, this on its side and that on its side, and the ravine between the two sides — that ravine Jonathan sought to cross.
1 Samuel.translator_note: The description of the two crags and the ravine is compressed in the Hebrew; translated literally.

1 Samuel.english_translation: The name of the one tooth was Bozez, and the name of the second Seneh.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: rose up on the north in front of Michmas
1 Samuel.english_translation: Sloping and rising from the north side toward Michmas.
From which Jonathan went out.

Wait, as (Joshua 10:12): “Sun, stand thou still (*dom*) upon Gibeon”; and so (Psalms 37:7): “Resign thyself (*dom*) unto the Lord.” If they say thus: “Wait (*domu*) until we come up to you” — their hour is succeeding and their heart is lifted up over them.
1 Samuel.translator_note: The last clause is terse in the Hebrew (“their hour is succeeding, and their heart is high upon them”); translated literally.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: But if they say thus: Come up unto us
1 Samuel.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He, put fear in their heart, and they are afraid to move from their place.
An expression of raising the voice.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: upon his hands and upon his feet
1 Samuel.english_translation: That is, with all strength and running.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: within as it were half a furrow’s length in an acre of land
1 Samuel.english_translation: Within the measure of an area of ground, the full half of a furrow of the plough of a yoke of oxen that ploughs in a field.
It is the furrow of the plough, which they call *reie* in Old French; and it is a great feat of strength, that they were close to one another and ready to help one another.
1 Samuel.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is ריי״א; Darmesteter (1909, p. 51) reads *réie* (“sillon,” furrow; modern *raie*).

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: the watchmen of Saul in Gibeath-benjamin
1 Samuel.english_translation: The watchmen who were Saul’s in Gibeah of Benjamin, *tzofim*; *ishqagatsh* in Old French.
1 Samuel.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is אישקאגט״ש. Darmesteter (1909, p. 51) lists, for this verse word, forms read *badètes* or *bedètes* (“les guetteurs”); the printed form differs and I could not match it, so I give no reading of it.

1 Samuel.english_translation: Of the Philistines: it melted from its place and went, and drew near hither toward Israel.
As (Genesis 4:12): “a fugitive and a wanderer.”
An expression of mustering, as (Job 7:18): “and that Thou shouldest remember him every morning” (*u-tifkedenu li-vkarim*, lit. “and Thou musterest him every morning”).

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Bring hither the ark of God
1 Samuel.english_translation: The Urim and Thummim.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: For the ark of God was there at that time
1 Samuel.english_translation: The verse lacks one word: “for the ark of God was *there* on that day.”

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: the Hebrews that were with the Philistines
1 Samuel.english_translation: In their help, out of fear, from yesterday and the day before; and today they too turned, together with their fellows, to be in the help of their brothers.
They were hurrying and urgent to fight against the Philistines.
An expression of oath (*alah*).
Every kind of food is included, as (Jeremiah 11:19): “Let us destroy the tree with the fruit thereof” (*be-lachmo*, literally “with its bread”).

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: there was honey upon the ground
1 Samuel.english_translation: Honey of reeds grows in the Land of Israel.
That was dripping from the reeds.

In the reed of the honey, as (Exodus 2:3): “and laid it in the flags” (*ba-suf*), which we translate (Targum): *ve-shavyateh be-ye'ara*. And *suf* are the reeds of a marsh, and so (Song of Songs 5:1): “I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey” (*ya'ri*, “my honeycomb”). And in the language of Ishmael they call that honey *sukra* in Old French, from the mouth of Rabbi Nathan the Ishmaelite.
1 Samuel.translator_note: The Old French word is printed סוקר״א; it is not in Darmesteter’s collection, so I give only the printed form.

1 Samuel.english_translation: He confused their mind and their deliverance, like turbid waters.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: had there not been then a much greater slaughter
1 Samuel.english_translation: In astonishment.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: the people flew upon the spoil
1 Samuel.english_translation: Like *va-ya'at ha-am*, an expression of *ayit* (a bird of prey; Genesis 15:11).

I say: this is [the prohibition] “you shall not kill it and its young” (Leviticus 22:28), and therefore it called them sinners. And our Rabbis said, regarding the slaughter of sacred offerings, that they used to consecrate them as peace-offerings and eat them before the sprinkling of the blood; that is what is said: “and the people did eat with the blood” — they were eating sacred offerings while the blood was still in the basin.
1 Samuel.translator_note: The Hebrew says only that our Rabbis spoke “regarding the slaughter of sacred offerings” (בשחיטת קדשים) without naming a place; translated as written.

1 Samuel.english_translation: An expression of *gilgelu* (“roll”).

While it was still day; and below (v. 34) it says: “and they brought every man his ox with him that night.” Our Rabbis disagreed on the matter at the end of tractate Zevachim: some of them explained: in one place [it speaks] of non-sacred animals, in the other of sacred offerings. And some of them explained: in one place it speaks of sacred offerings that were consecrated to be offered on the great high place of Nob, in the other of sacred offerings consecrated to be offered on a small high place; it teaches regarding an individual’s burnt-offering that it is valid to be slaughtered at night.
He made it a high place, to throw the blood upon it and to burn the fats.
Proclaim in many places, and the proclaimers will be scattered among the people.
Here, in a place of slaughter. Another explanation: he examined a knife for them.
Animals of non-sacred [meat] were slaughtered at night; so it is explained in Zevachim (ibid.).

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: the same was the first altar
1 Samuel.english_translation: That altar was the first of the altars that Saul built.
The princes of the people; the cornerstone (*even ha-pinnah*) is the important one.
To cast a lot between all of you and us.
Give a true lot.
Free from the lot.
They released Saul from his oath.
1 Samuel.translator_note: Literally the Hebrew reads “they permitted to him, to Saul, his oath.”

1 Samuel.english_translation: And he gathered an army (*va-ye'esof chayil*).

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Abner, the son of Ner, Saul’s uncle
1 Samuel.english_translation: And Ner was Saul’s uncle, the brother of Kish, and both were sons of Abiel; and Abiel too is called Ner, in Chronicles (I 8:33), for he used to light lamps for the public in dark entrances (Leviticus Rabbah 9:2).

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and when Saul saw any mighty man
1 Samuel.english_translation: An expression of the present: whenever Saul saw a mighty man of valour, he would gather him to himself.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: now therefore hearken thou unto the voice of the words of the LORD
1 Samuel.english_translation: Once you acted foolishly; now take heed for yourself.
For they were sorcerers, and would change themselves and look like an animal.
An expression of proclamation, as (above 14:20): “And Saul and all the people that were with him assembled themselves.”

He told each one to take a lamb from the flock of the king, and afterwards he counted the lambs, because it is forbidden to count Israel, as it is said of them (Genesis 32:12): “which cannot be numbered for multitude.”
1 Samuel.translator_note: Printed as Genesis 32:12 (English numbering); the quoted words are at Genesis 32:13 in the Hebrew verse numbering used in this reader.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and lay in wait in the valley
1 Samuel.english_translation: And he fought in the valley (*nachal*). And our Rabbis said (Yoma 22b): over the matter of the valley he argued and judged himself: if for one soul the Torah said, “break the heifer’s neck in the valley,” for all these souls, all the more so! If a man sinned, what did the beast sin?

The sons of Jethro, who were dwelling in the wilderness of Judah in the south of Arad, who went to Jabez to learn Torah; and Arad is Amalek: the Canaanite king of Arad was Amalek, as it is said (Numbers 21:1): “who dwelt in the South,” and “Amalek dwelleth in the land of the South” (ibid. 13:29).

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: to all the children of Israel
1 Samuel.english_translation: That Moses and Aaron and all the elders of Israel enjoyed his meal, and so it counts it to him as if he had done kindness with all the children of Israel.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: the young of the second birth
1 Samuel.english_translation: It has no parallel; and they are the sturdy ones. And I say: it is an expression of *mishnim*, as (Genesis 43:12): “double money” (*kesef mishneh*), because it is doubled in flesh and in fat; and so (Judges 6:25): “and the second bullock of seven years old.”
Like *nivzeh*, and the *mem* is an appendage in it.
A thought came up in My heart concerning the kingship of Saul whom I made king.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: he is setting him up a monument
1 Samuel.english_translation: He is building himself an altar — it is the altar of which it is said of Elijah (1 Kings 18:30): “And he repaired the altar of the LORD that was thrown down.” And Jonathan translated: *ve-ha metaken leih tamman atar le-fallega beih bizzeta* (“and behold he is preparing for himself there a place to divide the spoil in it”).
As its Targum: *orikh* — its meaning is “wait.”

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: art thou not head of the tribes of Israel
1 Samuel.english_translation: Jonathan translated: “The tribe of Benjamin crossed the sea at the head of all the people, as it is said (Psalms 68:28): ‘there is little Benjamin their ruler.’”
The people who are with you will consume them.
Like *va-ta'af* (“and thou didst fly”), an expression of *ayit* (Genesis 15:11).

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: the chief of the devoted things
1 Samuel.english_translation: The choicest of the devoted things; and so (Deuteronomy 18:4): “the first-fruits of thy corn,” as it is said (Numbers 18:30): “when you set apart the best thereof from it.” And Jonathan translated: “before they devote [them].”

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: to obey is better than sacrifice
1 Samuel.english_translation: [To hearken] to His voice is better than a sacrifice.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: to hearken than the fat of rams
1 Samuel.english_translation: This is connected to “behold, to hearken is better than a sacrifice,” and to give heed [is better] than the fat of rams.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, And stubbornness is as idolatry and teraphim
1 Samuel.english_translation: And as the punishment of *aven* and teraphim, so is the punishment of stubbornness. And Jonathan translated: “for like the sin of the men, etc., and like the sins of the people who erred after idolatry, so is the sin of every man who persists and adds, etc.”
1 Samuel.translator_note: The Targum is quoted abridged (“etc.”) in the printed text.

1 Samuel.english_translation: An expression of addition, and so (Genesis 33:11): “and he urged him” — he multiplied words to him.
Doeg the Edomite, who was important, [as much as] all of them.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: he laid hold upon the skirt of his robe
1 Samuel.english_translation: By its plain meaning it means that when Samuel turned to go from after Saul, Saul seized the skirt of Samuel’s [robe], because Saul was asking him to return, until he would bow down in Gilgal, where the Tent of Meeting was. And an aggadic Midrash (Shocher Tov): Amoraim disagree; some say: Saul tore Samuel’s robe; and some say: Samuel tore Saul’s robe, and gave him this sign: whoever cuts off the skirt of his robe, he shall reign in his place; and that is what Saul said to David on the day he cut off the robe (below 24:20): “and now, behold, I know that thou shalt surely be king.”

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: the Glory of Israel will not lie
1 Samuel.english_translation: And if you say, “I will return from my iniquity before Him” — it will no longer avail to take the kingship from him to whom it was given; for the Holy One, blessed be He, who is the Victory of Israel, will not lie about giving the good to him of whom He said to give it.
1 Samuel.translator_note: The first clause is elliptical in the Hebrew; translated literally.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: And Agag came unto him in chains
1 Samuel.english_translation: Jonathan translated: *Agag mefanka* (“Agag, the pampered one”).

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Surely the bitterness of death is at hand
1 Samuel.english_translation: In truth I know that the bitterness of death has come and drawn near to me.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: As thy sword hath made women childless
1 Samuel.english_translation: To make them sit as widows [bereft] of their husbands, for you were cutting off the tails of the young men of Israel.
He cut him into four; and this word has no parallel. And the Targum of *vayeshasef* is *u-fasach*. And in our Gemara there is: *hava mefashach ve-yahiv lan alita* — that is, splitting.
1 Samuel.translator_note: The Aramaic phrase from the Gemara is transliterated as printed; only Rashi’s own gloss “splitting” is translated.

1 Samuel.english_translation: In Beth-lehem; and so is the way of everything whose name is in two words, like Beth-lehem, Beth-shemesh, Beth-el, Kiriath-arba: if one wishes to put the letter *he* in it, he puts it between the two words, for example: Kiriath ha-Arba, Beth ha-Eli, Beth ha-Lachmi.
They hurried to go out toward him.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Surely the LORD’S anointed is before Him
1 Samuel.english_translation: And he said in his heart: Surely, this is true.
On the beauty of his form.
Because he is quick to anger, as it is said (below 17:28): “And Eliab’s anger was kindled against David.”

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: for it is not as man seeth
1 Samuel.english_translation: Even though you called yourself a seer, for you said to Saul (above 9:19): “I am the seer,” here I inform you that you do not see.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Then Jesse made Shammah to pass by
1 Samuel.english_translation: He is Shimea.
The youngest is left over.
We will not sit down to eat; every sitting of a meal is called *haseva*.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: the spirit of the LORD came mightily
1 Samuel.english_translation: A spirit of might.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: thy servants, that are before thee
1 Samuel.english_translation: Behold, your servants are before you, who will do your commands.
The distinguished one among them, Doeg the Edomite.
His whole intention was to bring Saul’s evil eye upon David, so that he would be jealous of him.
Thus is the name of the place.
A mighty man, to go out from his line of battle, to stand between the two lines.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: clad with a coat of mail
1 Samuel.english_translation: Like the scales of fish made of iron, falling over the back of the coat of mail [another version: the openings of the coat of mail], a scale for each opening.
Like an iron hand that comes out of the helmet opposite the threads, which they call *nasl* in Old French, and it reached down to his feet.
1 Samuel.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is נש״ל; Darmesteter (1909, p. 51) reads *nasal* and renders it “le nasal (poignée d’airain qui sort du casque vis-à-vis du nez)”.

1 Samuel.english_translation: Jonathan translated: *u-mesachpa de-nechasha nafik min kolsa u-metal bein katfohi*. Explanation: like a bronze spear protruding from the helmet and extending between his shoulders, to guard his neck from the sword.
1 Samuel.translator_note: The Aramaic word *mesachpa* is left untranslated; Rashi’s explanation is translated. Audit 4: the Aramaic quotation was checked against Targum Jonathan/the Ketuvim Targum (Mikraot Gedolot, Sefaria) at 1SA 17:6 and reads as quoted; the meaning of the unclear word, if noted above, is still unresolved.

1 Samuel.english_translation: Jonathan translated: *ke-aksan de-gardain* (“like the weavers’ beam”), *ensouble* in Old French.
1 Samuel.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is אינשובל״א; Darmesteter (1909, p. 51) reads *ensouble*, “comme l’ensouple des tisserands” (the weavers’ beam). The Aramaic word *aksan* is left untranslated. Audit 4: “weavers’ beam” rests on Darmesteter’s gloss of *ensouble* (“l’ensouple des tisserands”), which Rashi gives as the equivalent of the Aramaic; the Aramaic wording itself reads as quoted in Targum Jonathan at 1 Samuel 17:7.

1 Samuel.english_translation: All the shekels mentioned in the Prophets are *manim* (minas).
1 Samuel.translator_note: The Hebrew states this without explanation; translated literally.

1 Samuel.english_translation: All of you, to set the battle in array? Let one fight against me on behalf of all of you, and on the condition that is explained: “if he be able to fight with me,” etc.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: am not I a Philistine, and you servants to Saul
1 Samuel.english_translation: I am neither a captain of a hundred nor a captain of a thousand, but a Philistine like one of the others; and even though I fought many wars for them, I killed Hophni and Phinehas and captured the Ark, and you have become servants to Saul, and he has not saved you in all his days by his might.
Choose for yourselves.
Saul; and let him come down to me.
Beth-lehem is situated in the land of Ephrath.

And as for what is written (1 Chronicles 2:15): “Ozem the sixth, David the seventh,” and it does not write further — one may say that one died without sons, and therefore they did not write him there.
He was counted in the assemblies of the distinguished.
For he had been in Saul’s house before that, to play before him.
He used to go and return constantly from Saul’s side to his father’s house.
Our Rabbis said (Sotah 42b): in order to make them neglect the recital of the Shema.
(Targum:) “cheeses of milk.”

I say: to the captain of that thousand to which his brothers belong (another reading: to which I belong), for all the tribes had captains of thousands according to their thousands; and I heard: “the captain of the thousand” is this Jonathan, of whom it says (above 13:2): “and a thousand were with Jonathan in Gibeah of Benjamin.”
And take the assurance of their deliverance and their welfare in your ears and in your heart, and tell me; and so Jonathan translated: “and bring their welfare.”

An expression of deliverance, as (Psalms 119:122): “Be surety for Thy servant for good”; *garantis* in Old French. And our Rabbis said (Shabbat 56a): “a bill of divorcement he shall take from them and bring to their wives,” to separate the bond (*iruv*) between him and her.
1 Samuel.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is גרנטי״ש; Darmesteter (1909, p. 51) reads *garantis* (“tu prendras leur garantie”).

1 Samuel.english_translation: Around the camp they make a circle, and whoever goes out beyond it, forward or backward, is liable: forward, lest the men of the enemy lines run upon him; backward, [because] he is seeking to flee.
The battle line of Israel.
Of the men of the army.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: out of the ranks of the Philistines
1 Samuel.english_translation: It is written [*mima'arot*]; our Rabbis expounded (Sotah 42b): a hundred men uncovered (*he'eru*) the back of the neck of his mother when she parted from after Ruth and Naomi her mother-in-law.
1 Samuel.translator_note: A wordplay on מערות and הערו; translated as written.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: make his father’s house free in Israel
1 Samuel.english_translation: From matters stated in the laws of kingship.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: there came a lion, or a bear
1 Samuel.english_translation: (Targum:) “and a lion came, and also a bear.”

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: both the lion and the bear
1 Samuel.english_translation: These are amplifications (*ribbuyin*): a lion and its two cubs, and a bear and its two young.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: The LORD that delivered me out of the paw of the lion
1 Samuel.english_translation: I know that this matter did not befall me for nothing, but that in the future I will come to a like case for the deliverance of Israel, and I will rely on it and go out. And this is one of two righteous men to whom a hint was given, and they were quick to understand the matter, David and Mordecai, as it is said (Esther 2:11): “And every day Mordecai walked before the court,” etc. He said: This righteous woman did not rise for nothing, she who was seized into the bed of this uncircumcised one, but she is destined to stand up for Israel on a day of distress.

They changed to become the size of David after he was anointed with the anointing oil, even though they were Saul’s, who was taller than all the people from his shoulders and upward (above 9:2); and when Saul saw this, he cast the evil eye upon him, and David sensed the matter.

Jonathan translated: “and he was not willing to go.” There are words that serve for a thing and its opposite, like (Isaiah 10:33): “shall lop the boughs with terror” (*mesa'ef pa'orah*); (Psalms 52:7): “and root thee out of the land of the living” (*ve-shorashkha me-eretz chayyim*).

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: for he had not tried it
1 Samuel.english_translation: (Targum:) “for he was not accustomed.”

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: for I have not tried them
1 Samuel.english_translation: (Targum:) “for there is no miracle in them” — the praise of a miracle is not in this. Another explanation: “and he essayed to go” — he wanted to go and to try, and when he saw that they were heavy upon him, he took them off.
Thin and smooth stones.
*U-ve-tarmilei* (“and in his bag”) (Targum).

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and to the beasts of the field
1 Samuel.english_translation: It is not the way of beasts to eat a man. David said: This one’s mind is already deranged — it is mine. So David came and said to him: “and I will give the carcasses of the host of the Philistines,” etc., “and to the wild beasts of the earth.”
1 Samuel.translator_note: The words “it is mine” (שלי הוא) are terse in the Hebrew; translated literally.

1 Samuel.english_translation: He should have fallen only backward, for he was struck on his forehead; but [he fell forward] so that David would not have to trouble himself to go and cut off his head, for David gained now twelve cubits and two spans: his height was six cubits and a span; he gained a full height backward and a full height forward (Midrash Tehillim).
From pursuing, as (Genesis 31:36): “thou hast hotly pursued after me.”

Did he not know him? Is it not written (above 16:21): “and he loved him greatly; and he became his armour-bearer”? Rather he saw him conducting himself in the manners of royalty. Saul said: If he comes from the family of Perez, he will be a king, for a king breaks (*poretz*) a fence to make a road for himself, and none protest against him; and if he comes from the family of Zerah, he will be an important man. Doeg said to him: Before you ask whether he comes from a family that is fit for kingship or not, ask whether he is fit to enter the congregation or not, for behold Ruth the Moabitess came [from whom he descends]. Abner said to him: We learned: an Ammonite, but not an Ammonitess. Doeg said to him: If so, a *mamzer* but not a *mamzeret*. He said to him: Here it is said (Deuteronomy 23:5): “because they met you not with bread and with water,” and it is not the way of a woman to do so. He said to him: They should have met men with men, and women with women. Abner was silenced. Saul said to him: You ask whose son this lad (*elem*) is. Above it is written *na'ar*, and here it is written *elem*. He said to him: This law was hidden (*nit'alma*) from you; go and ask in the study house, as is found in Yevamot (76b).
Jonathan translated: *u-ve-tzeltzelin*. A kind of musical instrument.
And what does he still lack, that one need add to him?
He needs nothing more except the kingship.
(Targum:) “an evil eye.”
*Ve-ishtatei* (Targum: “and he raved”). A prophet and a madman speak words of hints that are not recognizable.
1 Samuel.translator_note: The Aramaic word is printed as given; the second sentence is translated literally.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: I will smite David even to the wall
1 Samuel.english_translation: One blow I will strike, so that the spear will enter David and the wall.
Successful.
In his heart.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Let not my hand be upon him
1 Samuel.english_translation: Lest I be punished.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: but let the hand of the Philistines be upon him
1 Samuel.english_translation: Therefore he said to him: “and fight the LORD’S battles.”

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: But it came to pass at the time when Merab Saul’s daughter should have been given to David
1 Samuel.english_translation: When the time arrived that was fixed to give her to him, and while they were still occupied with giving her to him, the matter turned about and she was given to Adriel.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: through the one of the twain
1 Samuel.english_translation: I have two daughters; with one of them you shall become my son-in-law. And so Jonathan translated: “with one of two.” Similar to it (2 Samuel 24:12): “I lay upon thee three things” — one of three, as is explained there: “choose thee one of them.”

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: And the days were not expired
1 Samuel.english_translation: He did not wait until the end of the days that [Saul] had fixed for him to bring the hundred foreskins.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and they gave them in full number to the king
1 Samuel.english_translation: *Prisentir* in Old French.
1 Samuel.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is פרישנטי״ר; Darmesteter (1909, p. 51) reads *présanter* and renders it “ils les donnèrent au complet.”

1 Samuel.english_translation: To fear.
To come in troops to take spoil in Israel.
Near my father; *ainsheish* in Old French.
1 Samuel.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is איינשיי״ש. Darmesteter (1909, p. 51) lists several manuscript forms for this verse word (“à côté de mon père”) and reads them *ès ses ayses*; the printed form is similar but not identical, so I give his reading and no reading of my own.

1 Samuel.english_translation: So that they would not understand that he had fled and pursue him.
They are made in the likeness of a human body.
A whole skin stripped off, like a skin-bottle; *plotsil* in Old French.
1 Samuel.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is פלוצי״ל; Darmesteter (1909, p. 52) reads *floçel* for this verse word (“la peau de chèvre”).

1 Samuel.english_translation: Because teraphim have no hair, and this resembles human hair.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: He said unto me: Let me go
1 Samuel.english_translation: You delivered me into the hand of a certain robber; he drew his sword against me until I let him go.
(Targum:) “in the house of study.”
(Targum:) “a company.”

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: And he also stripped off his clothes
1 Samuel.english_translation: The royal garments, to put on the garments of the disciples.
*Va-nafal barshan*; Jonathan translated: “and he fell *artilai*.” And in the name of Rabbi Menahem, who heard it from the mouth of an Arab: *barshan* in the Arabic language means “mad.”
As by a single step I was released from his presence; and he struck the spear into the wall — by that step I was saved from death.
The renewal of the moon; and none of those who eat at the king’s table refrains from coming to the meal on the festival.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: when I should sit with the king to eat
1 Samuel.english_translation: It is an expression of the present: and I am accustomed to sit with the king always, to eat beside him.
From now on; and I will hide until the evening of the third day, and I shall not be with those who eat, and my seat will be missed, and the king will wonder at me, either tomorrow or the day after.
He asked permission of me.
From year to year at this season.
That he will not be angry.
He has no intention in his heart to kill me.
That is, that I would be available to him to kill me.
In the end, he has an evil thought against me.
To send me away.
Such [a thing] — to suspect me — that I should know of him that the evil has been determined by him, and not tell you.
In the place where I shall hide.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: The LORD, the God of Israel
1 Samuel.english_translation: An expression of an oath.
In the days of tomorrow — this is the third day, at the present hour; for tomorrow is the new moon, and perhaps my father will not wonder tomorrow, but he will wonder on the third day.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: The LORD do so to Jonathan, and more also
1 Samuel.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He [do so to me], for I will search out my father and find that he is good toward you — if I do not send by a messenger and uncover your ear; for the good I can disclose; but if it is good to my father to do you evil, that I will not disclose, lest my father come to know the place where you are, and I myself will uncover your ear.
1 Samuel.translator_note: The Hebrew is compressed here; translated literally, with the supplied words in brackets.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: And thou shalt not only while yet I live
1 Samuel.english_translation: It is an expression of request, like (2 Kings 5:17): “If not, yet, I pray thee, let there be given to thy servant.” And it does not depart from its meaning: and you shall not do me a kindness while I am yet alive, that you do with me the kindness of the LORD before I die; and what is the kindness? That you shall not cut off your kindness from my house; in this you shall make a covenant with me in my lifetime.
1 Samuel.translator_note: The printed quotation reads לעבדיך; the verse reads לעבדך. The explanation is terse in the Hebrew and is translated literally.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: no, not when the LORD hath cut off
1 Samuel.english_translation: And also you shall not remove your kindness from the LORD, for even when calamity comes upon my father’s house — for I know that the Omnipresent will cut off your enemies.
1 Samuel.translator_note: The printed text reads מה׳ (“from the LORD”); it is translated as printed, and its sense is not clear to me.

1 Samuel.english_translation: This covenant.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: at the hand of David’s enemies
1 Samuel.english_translation: Scripture used a euphemism, and its explanation is: the Holy One, blessed be He, will require the iniquity from the hand of David, when he transgressed the covenant and said to Mephibosheth (2 Samuel 19:30): “Thou and Ziba divide the land,” a heavenly voice went forth and said: Rehoboam and Jeroboam shall divide the kingdom (Shabbat 56b). And so Jonathan translated: “and may the LORD exact [vengeance] for him from the hand of David’s enemies.”
And it is the way of all who eat at the king’s table to come to the table on a festival day.

My father will miss you and ask where you are: “for thy seat will be empty” — your seat in which you sit will be lacking; and so Jonathan translated: “and you will be sought, for *meruach beit asschartakh* will be.”
1 Samuel.translator_note: Two Aramaic words in Jonathan’s rendering are left untranslated, because I could not confirm their meaning. Audit 4: the Aramaic quotation was checked against Targum Jonathan/the Ketuvim Targum (Mikraot Gedolot, Sefaria) at 1SA 20:18 and reads as quoted; the meaning of the unclear word, if noted above, is still unresolved.

1 Samuel.english_translation: An expression of remembrance.
An expression of lack.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: And in the third day thou shalt hide thyself well
