1 Samuel.english_translation: Three days, and then you shall go down greatly; that is, when the third day arrives, you shall go down to a hidden place and hide yourself much, for then they will seek you; and you shall come to this hiding place in which you are hidden today, which is a day of doing work. And so Jonathan translated: *be-yoma de-chola* (“on a weekday”), for that day he hid, as it is said (v. 24): “So David hid himself in the field” — immediately — “and it came to pass, the new moon” — tomorrow.
A stone that was a sign for travelers on the road.
Those who go on the way; and so Jonathan translated: *even ata*, the stone of the sign.

With no *mappik* in the *he*; and the explanation of *tzidah* is like *le-tzad* (“to the side”): every word that needs a *lamed* at its beginning has a *he* put at its end. By the side of that stone I shall shoot arrows at a mark, so that the lad does not understand, and this shall be a sign for you to infer whether you need to flee.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: And, behold, I will send the lad
1 Samuel.english_translation: And it is the way of one searching for an arrow that was shot: he goes to the place where he saw the arrow go, and he cannot aim well; sometimes he searches for it and the arrow is farther from him, and sometimes he goes farther than the arrow and searches for it; and this omen shall be for you.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Behold, the arrows are on this side of thee; take them, and come
1 Samuel.english_translation: Go out yourself from the place of your hiding, and take it and come to me, for you have nothing to fear, for there is peace to you; the Holy One, blessed be He, desires that you be here, and you shall not fear, even if I have heard evil from my father.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: go thy way; for the LORD hath sent thee away
1 Samuel.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He, is telling you to flee and escape.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: the matter which I and thou have spoken of
1 Samuel.english_translation: The covenant that we made together.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: the LORD is between me and thee
1 Samuel.english_translation: A witness to that matter.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: even upon the seat by the wall
1 Samuel.english_translation: At the head of the couch, beside the wall.

He stood up from his place, because it is not the way of a son to recline beside his father, for their way was to eat reclining on couches, and David used to recline between Jonathan and Saul; now that David did not come, Jonathan did not recline until Abner sat at Saul’s side, and afterward Jonathan sat at Abner’s side. And if you say he did not sit at all — behold it says (v. 34): “So Jonathan arose from the table,” which implies that he had sat.
A seminal emission (*keri*): he had one.
And he has not yet immersed from his emission; for if he had immersed from his emission, he would not need the setting of the sun for non-sacred food.
This is giving a reason for the matter: because he is not clean, therefore he did not come, so as not to defile the meal.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: on the morrow after the new moon
1 Samuel.english_translation: From the morrow of the renewal of the moon.
On the second day of the month.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: my brother, he hath commanded me
1 Samuel.english_translation: The head of the household commanded me to be there, and he is my brother Eliab.
*Eshkemotsid* in Old French; “I shall go one day and come back.”
1 Samuel.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is אשקמוצי״ד; Darmesteter (1909, p. 52) lists forms for this verse word (“je m’enfuirai”) that he reads *eschemoçeré*, with W.

1 Samuel.english_translation: An expression of *na* (“wandering”): a woman wandering and straying, a wanton (*yotz'anit*); as you say *ze'avah* from *za*, so you say *na'avah* from *na*, and the *tav* is from the joining, for it is joined to *mardut*.

That she is fit to be subdued (*lirdot*) and chastised. Another explanation: when the Benjamites seized [wives] from the daughters of Shiloh who went out to dance in the vineyards, Saul was shy and did not want to seize, until she herself came and brazened her face and pursued him.

On account of the vineyards, and it is a winepress (*gat*), as (Avodah Zarah 74b): *na'avah artachu*; *yetufun na'avahi be-chamar* (Targum on the portion Vayechi, on the verse “his eyes shall be red with wine,” Genesis 49:12) — and not from the noun.
1 Samuel.translator_note: Rashi’s wording is terse and the Aramaic quotations are transliterated, not translated.

1 Samuel.english_translation: On account of David.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: because his father had put him to shame
1 Samuel.english_translation: On account of David.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: at the time appointed with David
1 Samuel.english_translation: At the appointed time that David had fixed for him.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: he shot an arrow beyond him
1 Samuel.english_translation: The arrow passed beyond the lad.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: out of a place toward the South
1 Samuel.english_translation: (Targum:) “from the side of the stone of the sign, which is opposite the south.”
He wept much.
And the oath that we swore — the LORD will be a witness over it forever.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and the young men have I appointed to such and such a place
1 Samuel.english_translation: An expression of toil: the young men who went out with me, I made them toil to run before me to a certain place, so-and-so.
Like (Judges 8:16): “and with them he taught the men of Succoth.”
*Almoni* is from *ein shem* (“no name”), [a place] whose name I do not wish to mention, for it is a secret matter.
Like (Deuteronomy 17:8): “*ki yippale*” (“too hard”) — it will be hidden.
If there are not five, give me what is found in your hand.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: if only the young men have kept themselves from women
1 Samuel.english_translation: With difficulty I feed them to non-priests (*zarim*); but this I cannot feed to the unclean.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: women have been kept from us
1 Samuel.english_translation: Withheld from us.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: the vessels of the young men were holy
1 Samuel.english_translation: Pure.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: though it was but a common journey
1 Samuel.english_translation: And the bread, once it is taken off the table and the pans [of frankincense] have been burned, is close to being non-sacred, for it has gone out from the law of misappropriation (*me'ilah*) once it has had an hour of permission for the priests.

And even if today were the beginning of its holiness on the table, I would be obliged to take it from there and feed him, for ravenous hunger (*bulmus*) has seized him and he is in danger; so it is explained in Menachot.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: to put hot bread in the day when it was taken away
1 Samuel.english_translation: Another [explanation]: “in the day when it was taken away” — this. And our Rabbis said (Yoma 21a): “hot on the day of its taking”; also on the day of its removal, hot as on the day of its arrangement.
He restrained himself before the Tent of Meeting, to occupy himself with Torah.
Head of the court (*av beit din*).
And if there is here.
In haste.
Wrapped, and so (1 Kings 19:13): “he wrapped his face in his mantle.”
After he had inquired by the Urim and Thummim, he said to him so; and so Jonathan translated: “after he inquired of him by the ephod.”

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Is not this David the king of the land?
1 Samuel.english_translation: They said to Achish: There was a condition between us (above 17:9): “If he be able to fight with me, and kill me, then will we be your servants” — you have no choice but to come down from your throne, and he will be king of this land.
His words.
He acted insane.
And he wrote.
His saliva; a thing that drips is called *rir*, and so (Job 6:6): “*be-rir challamut*”; and so (Leviticus 15:3): “whether his flesh run with his issue.”

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: shall this fellow come into my house?
1 Samuel.english_translation: An expression of astonishment, and therefore it is vocalized with a *chataf-patach*, and is soft (*rafe*).

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and they dwelt with him all the while that David was in the stronghold
1 Samuel.english_translation: Near Moab; and when David went out from there to the forest of Hereth, the king of Moab killed his father and his mother and his brothers, except one of them whom Nahash the Ammonite kept alive, and this is the kindness of which David said (2 Samuel 12): “as his father showed kindness unto me,” as is found in Midrash Rabbi Tanchuma.
1 Samuel.translator_note: The reference “2 Samuel 12” is as printed; the quoted words are at 2 Samuel 10:2.

1 Samuel.english_translation: For he took heed to guard against him.

One that was on the border of Benjamin; and our Rabbis said (Taanit 5b): it was Samuel’s Ramah, and they are two places; and so is its midrash: “And Saul was sitting in Gibeah” — in the merit of the great tamarisk (*eshel*) that is in Ramah, for he used to pray for him.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and hast inquired of God for him
1 Samuel.english_translation: You made him king, for one does not inquire by the Urim and Thummim for a commoner.
Like (Genesis 19:3): “and they turned in unto him” — and draws near to your service and to hear your words; and was it for me to understand that he does not go on your mission?

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Have I to-day begun to inquire of God for him?
1 Samuel.english_translation: In astonishment: for many days the need of the public has been with him, for you appointed him to go out and come in before Israel, and since then I inquire of God for him.
From doing this thing for rebellion and treachery.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: the guard that stood about him
1 Samuel.english_translation: They were Abner and Amasa.

They expounded the limiting particles *akh* and *rak* (Joshua 1:18): “Whosoever he be that shall rebel against thy commandment,” etc. — one might think even [if the command is] for a matter of transgression; therefore the text says “only” (*rak*).
His name was changed; he said to him: You were caught like a fish (*dag*); you informed against them; you kill them.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: I have brought about the death of all the persons of thy father’s house
1 Samuel.english_translation: I turned the matter about until it came to this.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: for he that seeketh my life seeketh thy life
1 Samuel.english_translation: One man pursues the two of us; in the place where I escape, you shall escape, for you will always be under my guard; so Jonathan translated: “for whoever wishes to kill me wishes to kill you.” And there is more to explain: for he who loves me will love you, and he who guards my soul will guard your soul; and there is a parallel in Scripture (Proverbs 29:10): “The men of blood hate him that is sincere; and as for the upright, they seek his life” (*nafsho*, lit. “his soul”) — behold, here “seeking a soul” is for good.
1 Samuel.translator_note: JPS “life” is *nefesh*, which Rashi reads as “soul”; the quoted Proverbs words are JPS’s.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: God hath delivered him into my hand
1 Samuel.english_translation: He shut him in, and so (Obadiah 1:12): “thou shouldest not have gazed on the day of thy brother in the day of his disaster” (*be-yom nokhro*). And it is of the pattern of the strong ones, like (Lamentations 2:9): “He hath destroyed and broken her bars.” And if it had wished to speak in the pattern of the weak ones, it would have been vocalized *nakar*.
1 Samuel.translator_note:
The grammatical terms (“strong” and “weak” patterns) are translated literally.
Rashi reads *nokhro* as “delivered up, shut in” (*hisgir*); JPS renders it “disaster.”

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: he is shut in, by entering into a town that hath gates and bars
1 Samuel.english_translation: And he will rely on this, and will not take care to flee from him.
(Targum:) *kamin yat bishta*.
1 Samuel.translator_note: The Aramaic phrase is left untranslated; its general sense is lying in wait with evil.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Will the men of Keilah deliver me up into his hand?
1 Samuel.english_translation: We learned from here that one who asks two things, they answer him only one, and they answer him only the first; and here David asked out of order, for he should first have asked, Will Saul come down? and [then], Will they deliver me up into his hand? — and they answered him in order.
(Targum:) “in a place that is fit to go,” in the place of their rescue.
He renewed the covenant between them.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and our part shall be to deliver him up
1 Samuel.english_translation: And it is upon us to deliver him up.
Whoever said it.
He conducts himself with cunning: today here, and tomorrow in another place, so that his place will not be known.
Upon a matter established and true.
For Saul was going to go after them, and they went before him to search with certainty.
Encircling and surrounding from side to side, like a crown (*atarah*) that encircles the head.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: But there came a messenger unto Saul
1 Samuel.english_translation: A real angel, in order to save David.
Because Saul’s heart was divided into two opinions, whether to return to save his land from the hand of the Philistines, or to pursue and seize David; so Jonathan translated.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: the rocks of the wild goats
1 Samuel.english_translation: The rocks of the wild goats.
To turn aside to the large orifices [of the body], a euphemism for relieving himself.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: And it came to pass afterward, that David’s heart smote him
1 Samuel.english_translation: (The Hebrew gives only the opening words of the verse and no comment text.)

These two verses are written out of their order; rather, since he began to speak of the cutting of the robe, he finished all his words, and said that even in the cutting of the robe he regretted; and afterward he returns to his first speech and says [in answer to] what his men said to him, “Behold the day,” etc., he answered them: “The LORD forbid it me,” etc.
He separated and pushed them off with words.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Wherefore hearkenest thou to men’s words
1 Samuel.english_translation: Why do you accept against me the evil speech of Doeg?

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and some bade me kill thee; but mine eye spared thee
1 Samuel.english_translation: Behold, two words are missing here: “and the one who said that I should kill thee said so, and my soul spared thee,” like (2 Samuel 13:39): “and king David longed to go forth unto Absalom” — “and the soul of David longed.”
1 Samuel.translator_note: JPS renders the quoted words of 2 Samuel 13:39 “And the soul of king David failed with longing.”

1 Samuel.english_translation: That is, give heed to the matter, and also see the testimony: that the skirt of your robe is in my hand, and I could have killed you.
The proverb of the Ancient One of the world — the Torah, which is the proverb of the Holy One, blessed be He.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Out of the wicked cometh forth wickedness
1 Samuel.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He, prepares for a wicked man that he fall into the hand of a wicked man like himself; and where did the Torah say it? (Exodus 21:13): “but God cause it to come to hand,” as is found in tractate Makkot (10b).

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: I know that thou shalt surely be king
1 Samuel.english_translation: For I see that the Holy One, blessed be He, saves you from my hands. And an aggadic Midrash (Yalkut Shimoni §134): Samuel gave him this sign, that whoever tears his robe will reign in his place.
The name of the city.
His livestock and his acquisitions.
Rich.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and he was shearing his sheep in Carmel
1 Samuel.english_translation: And it came to pass one day, when the time of shearing his flock in Carmel arrived — and it was his custom to make a feast and festival for the shearers of the flock.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and he was of the house of Caleb
1 Samuel.english_translation: From the house of Caleb.

“Thus to the living one”: So may it be next year, shearing. (“Thus to the living one”: So may it be next year, the fortune of one who lives and endures.) (Another version: “Thus to the living one”: They said upon his slaughtered animal and his libation that you will see, thus it is fitting for a living man, for an alert and important man, like (2 Samuel 23:20): “the son of a valiant man … who had done mighty deeds” (*rav pe'alim*, lit. “great in deeds”) — alive and alert, a man of deeds; end.)
1 Samuel.translator_note: The parenthetical sentences are in the printed Hebrew; they are translated as given.

1 Samuel.english_translation: Good and enduring.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and peace be both unto thee
1 Samuel.english_translation: So may it be for length of days.
If they needed us for anything, we did not send them back empty.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: neither was there aught missing unto them
1 Samuel.english_translation: We found them, for we were guards to them.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: wherefore let the young men find favour in thine eyes
1 Samuel.english_translation: [The young men] who are mine — [that they] find favour in your eyes, for the good that your servants will tell you about them.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: for we come on a good day
1 Samuel.english_translation: Relying on the feast and festival that you have, we have come now to ask for something: it was the eve of Rosh Hashanah, and we need a festival meal.

They were weary from the toil of the road, and they hurried to fulfil David’s command, and did not rest until they spoke to him, and afterward “and ceased”; and Jonathan translated: “and they stopped” — that is, they stopped speaking further, until they should hear his answer.
What is he, that he is important, that I should give him what is mine? Did not Ruth the Moabitess come [from him]?
1 Samuel.translator_note: The final clause is elliptical in the Hebrew; “[from him]” is supplied for the sense.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: David also girded on his sword
1 Samuel.english_translation: From here [we learn] that in capital cases one begins the judgment with the youngest first (Sanhedrin 36a).
To guard their tents and their vessels.
Hers.
(Targum:) *afrachinon be-millin* (Yalkut Shimoni §134, and its explanation: he forced them with his evil words), an expression of *ayit* (Genesis 15:11).
We were not shamed.
From David against him.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: he is such a base fellow, that one cannot speak to him
1 Samuel.english_translation: And our master is a base man, so that one cannot speak to him what I am saying to you, for he will be angry with us.

Jonathan translated: *tachavra*, “stuffed with fine meat and eggs”; *pashtitz* in Old French, as we learned in Pesachim (74a — see there well in Rashi, s.v. “Rabbi Ishmael calls it,” etc., and it is a duty to settle it): “and he puts the legs and its entrails into it.” Rabbi Tarfon calls it *tachavra*, what is inside it by itself, like Rabbi Akiva, who said they hang it outside it; so it is taught in the Tosefta; Rabbi Kalonymos of blessed memory from Rome explained it to us so.
1 Samuel.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is פשטי״ץ. Darmesteter (1909, p. 52) renders this verse word “des pâtés” and reads the manuscript forms as *farside* (from *farcita*, modern *farcie*); the printed form is not among the manuscript forms he reads. The bracketed reference to Rashi on Pesachim is part of the printed text.

1 Samuel.english_translation: Dried grapes.
Round cakes of fig-cake: figs pressed and packed in a vessel.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: David and his men came down towards her
1 Samuel.english_translation: There was a ravine between the two mountains; she was coming down from this mountain, and they were coming down from the opposite mountain.
In his heart, when his young men told him Nabal’s insults: “Surely in vain have I kept,” etc.
Jonathan translated: *yada meda*, *mashit kirot libo*. Another explanation: even a dog, whose way is to urinate against a wall.
1 Samuel.translator_note: The Aramaic phrase is left untranslated.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Upon me, my lord, upon me be the iniquity
1 Samuel.english_translation: At first she said so, so that he would incline his ear to her words, and at the end she told him the truth: “I thy handmaid saw not the young men of my lord.”
That He sent me to meet you, to withhold you from bloodshed.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and from finding redress for thyself with thine own hand
1 Samuel.english_translation: From avenging yourself with your own hand, and being punished.
She prophesied by the Holy Spirit that he would not live long.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: let it be given unto the young men that follow my lord
1 Samuel.english_translation: “And let it be given to the young men who go about,” etc. *Natnah* is an expression of the past, and *nittenah* is an expression of the future.
1 Samuel.translator_note: The two forms are identical in the unvocalized printed text; they are distinguished here by their sense.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: the LORD will certainly make my lord a sure house
1 Samuel.english_translation: To be king over Israel; therefore, “and evil is not found in thee”; therefore it is not fitting for you to act unlawfully, to bring an evil report upon your kingship.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: as from the hollow of a sling
1 Samuel.english_translation: A wide piece of leather made like a spoon in the middle of the sling, in which he puts the stone.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: And it shall come to pass, when the LORD shall have done to my lord
1 Samuel.english_translation: “And it shall come to pass, when the LORD shall have done,” etc. — and you shall reign.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: that this shall be no stumblingblock unto thee
1 Samuel.english_translation: For stumbling, like (Nahum 2:11): “and the knees smite together”; for if you had done this, you would have no opening of the mouth to rule over men for future generations because of the shedding of blood.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: or that my lord hath found redress for himself
1 Samuel.english_translation: That you avenge your vengeance.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: that hast kept me this day
1 Samuel.english_translation: You have restrained me, like (Psalms 40:12): “Withhold not Thou Thy tender mercies”; “none of us shall withhold from thee” (Genesis 23:6).

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and from finding redress for myself with mine own hand
1 Samuel.english_translation: It refers back to “from coming into bloodguiltiness”: the *mem* of *mi-bo* is attached to *ve-hoshea*, as if [it said] “from coming into blood and from finding redress for myself with my hand.”

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: when the wine was gone out of Nabal
1 Samuel.english_translation: (Targum:) “when the wine had gone out of Nabal.”

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and his heart died within him
1 Samuel.english_translation: That he was distressed over the gift that had been brought to David.

The seven days of mourning for Samuel the Holy One, blessed be He, held him back, so that the mourning of a wicked man would not be mixed with Samuel’s mourning; and afterward he was ill three days and died, as it is said: “and the LORD smote Nabal”; and Mar said (Semachot 3:9): “he was ill three days and died” — this is death by plague. And our Rabbis said (Rosh Hashanah 18a): these are the ten days of repentance, for the Holy One, blessed be He, waited for him that he should return in repentance. And some say: corresponding to the ten morsels that Nabal gave to David’s servants, for David sent him ten young men and he fed them.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: that hath pleaded the cause of my reproach
1 Samuel.english_translation: The insults with which he reproached me (above v. 10): “there are many servants now-a-days that break away.”

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and hath kept back His servant from evil
1 Samuel.english_translation: That I did not kill him.
Fixed.
Some say he swore to his inclination, and some say he swore to Abishai: if you kill the righteous man, I will mix your blood with his blood.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: but the LORD shall smite him
1 Samuel.english_translation: He will bring his death near.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: or his day shall come to die
1 Samuel.english_translation: The day in which the time of his death is.
A small flask.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: hath stirred thee up against me
1 Samuel.english_translation: To my hatred; every *hasatah* is an expression of *sumah* (“placing”); *amitmint* in Old French.
1 Samuel.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is אמיטמינ״ט; Darmesteter (1909, p. 52) reads *amètement* (a noun from *ametre*) and renders the verse word “Dieu t’excite.”

1 Samuel.english_translation: He will accept my prayer with mercy, to turn your wrath away from me.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: for they have driven me out this day
1 Samuel.english_translation: From the Land of Israel.
One who goes out from the Land of Israel to outside the Land at the time of the Temple is as if he worships idols. And Jonathan translated: “Let David go among the peoples who serve idols.”

A bird whose name is *kore*, and in Old French *perdiz*, and so (Jeremiah 17:11): “As the partridge that sitteth on eggs, and hatcheth them not”; and it pursues the nests of other birds and sits upon their eggs.
1 Samuel.translator_note: The Old French word is printed פרדי״ץ; it is not in Darmesteter’s collection, so I give only the printed form.

1 Samuel.english_translation: To every righteous one.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: I shall now be swept away one day
1 Samuel.english_translation: Lest he lie in wait and come upon me suddenly.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: for why should thy servant dwell in the royal city with thee?
1 Samuel.english_translation: And I would be a burden to you.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: a full year and four months
1 Samuel.english_translation: “Days” at the least is two; and it is impossible to interpret “days” here as a year, for David did not go to Achish until Samuel died, and Saul did not reign after the death of Samuel except four months, as we learned in Seder Olam. And also from the count of the years of Eli, and the twenty years that the Ark was in Kiriath-jearim — behold, sixty years; take out of them the fifty-two [years] of Samuel, and one year for its intercalation, with these four months, and the seven years that David reigned in Hebron before he brought the Ark from Kiriath-jearim — it is found that Saul did not reign after the death of Samuel more than four months.
1 Samuel.translator_note: The arithmetic is translated as written; it is terse and I have not tried to reconstruct it. Audit 4 arithmetic check: 52 + 1 + 7 = 60, which equals the sixty years, so only the four months remain. The premises (Eli’s years and Samuel’s fifty-two) are Rashi’s and were not rechecked.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: And David and his men went up
1 Samuel.english_translation: An expression of the present: he was constantly accustomed to this.
(Targum:) “from the entrance of Chagra.”
1 Samuel.translator_note: The Aramaic words are translated as printed; I could not confirm their meaning. Audit 4: the Aramaic quotation was checked against Targum Jonathan/the Ketuvim Targum (Mikraot Gedolot, Sefaria) at 1SA 27:8 and reads as quoted; the meaning of the unclear word, if noted above, is still unresolved.

1 Samuel.english_translation: The *lamed* is exchanged for a *nun*, as in “and he made for him a *nishkah*” in the book of Ezra (Nehemiah 13:7), like *lishkah* (“chamber”).

Behold, it was already said, “And Samuel died”; rather, because he came to speak of Saul, who needed to inquire of a woman with a familiar spirit, he began and said “and Samuel was dead,” for had he been alive, Saul would have inquired of him; and Saul had removed the familiar spirits, and he needed to seek a woman who was a mistress of a familiar spirit.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and buried him in Ramah, even in his own city
1 Samuel.english_translation: (Targum:) “and all Israel lamented over him and buried him in Ramah, and each man lamented over him in his city”; “and in his city” is connected to “and they lamented him”: they lamented him in Ramah when they buried him, and each man lamented him in his city.
Because he killed Nob the city of the priests, he was not answered.

He changed his garments, and so (1 Kings 22:30): “I will disguise myself, and go into the battle”; and so (Job 30:18): “By the great force [of my disease] is my garment disfigured” (*yitchapes*, which Rashi takes as “disguised”); and so Jonathan translated: “and Saul changed himself.”

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and they came to the woman by night
1 Samuel.english_translation: It was day, but because of their distress it seemed to them like night; so expounded Rabbi Tanchuma (Parashat Emor 2).
Seeking a stumbling.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: she cried with a loud voice
1 Samuel.english_translation: For she saw him coming up not in the way of those who come up, for when one raises [the dead] by mentioning him, their feet come up first, and this one came up with his head upward, for the honor of Saul (Tanchuma, ibid.).
1 Samuel.translator_note: The phrase שהמעלה בזכורו is translated literally; its exact sense is not certain.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: I see a godlike being coming up out of the earth
1 Samuel.english_translation: Two angels, Moses and Samuel, for Samuel was afraid lest I be summoned to judgment, and he brought up Moses with him (as is found in Chagigah 4b).

Three things were said about a familiar spirit: the one who raises it sees it and does not hear its voice, and the one who inquires of it hears it and does not see it, and therefore he asked, “What form is he of?”; and another [person] neither sees it nor hears it (Tanchuma, ibid.).

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and he is covered with a robe
1 Samuel.english_translation: For he was accustomed to wear a robe, as it is said (above 2:19): “Moreover his mother used to make him a little robe,” and in his robe he was buried, and so he came up, and so in the future to come they will stand in their garments (Tanchuma, ibid.).
You have alarmed me.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: neither by prophets, nor by dreams
1 Samuel.english_translation: But he did not tell him about the Urim and Thummim, even though he had inquired by them, as stated above, because he was ashamed before him for having killed Nob, the city of the priests.

An expression of “and I cried out after you,” like (2 Samuel 1:6): *nikro nikrati* on mount Gilboa; and like (ibid. 20:1): “and there *nikra* a base fellow”: I needed to be called to you, that you might make known to me what I shall do.
1 Samuel.translator_note: The printed quotations differ from the verse readings (2 Samuel 1:6 reads נקרא נקריתי), and I could not make out how the citations bear on the sense, so the sentence is translated as printed. Checked against the Hebrew Tanakh: the second quotation (II Samuel 20:1, ושם נקרא איש בליעל) matches the verse exactly; the first, printed נקראתי, differs from II Samuel 1:6 (נקרא נקריתי).

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Wherefore then dost thou ask of me
1 Samuel.english_translation: Behold, you have inquired of the living prophets.
(Targum:) “and He is in the help of the man whose enemy you are.”
1 Samuel.translator_note: The Aramaic is translated literally; I could not confirm its exact sense. Audit 4: the Aramaic quotation was checked against Targum Jonathan/the Ketuvim Targum (Mikraot Gedolot, Sefaria) at 1SA 28:16 and reads as quoted; the meaning of the unclear word, if noted above, is still unresolved.

1 Samuel.english_translation: An expression of enemy, and there are several in Scripture: (Isaiah 14:21) “and fill the face of the world with *arim*”; (Micah 5:13) “and I will destroy thy *arekha*”; (Daniel 4:16) “the dream be to them that hate thee, and the interpretation thereof to thine *arekh*”; (Daniel 4:16).
1 Samuel.translator_note: The printed text cites Daniel 4:16 twice; the Aramaic wording of the second quotation is in that verse. Rashi reads *arim* and *arekha* in the first two quotations as “enemies”.

1 Samuel.english_translation: And in his lifetime he did not mention his name to him, but “and hath given it to thy neighbour, that is better than thou” (above 15:28), because he was afraid of him lest he kill him, since he had anointed him to kingship (Tanchuma, ibid.).

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: shalt thou and thy sons be with me
1 Samuel.english_translation: In my section.
(Targum:) a fattened calf.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: since he fell away unto me
1 Samuel.english_translation: From the day of his encamping with me.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and came to the brook Besor
1 Samuel.english_translation: Six hundred men.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: where those that were left behind stayed
1 Samuel.english_translation: When they reached the brook Besor, some of them were weary, and some of them were left there.
Who held back; and I say it is an Aramaic expression, the Targum of *ve-neherasu* (“and they shall be broken down”).

The south of the Philistines; we find in another place that the Philistines are called “the nation of the Cherethites” (Zephaniah 2:5): “the inhabitants of the sea-coast, the nation of the Cherethites.”
The Amalekites were accustomed to be smitten on the day “tomorrow,” as it is said (Exodus 17:9): “tomorrow I will stand,” etc.; therefore it says *le-mochoratam* (“on their morrow”).

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: all the flocks and the herds
1 Samuel.english_translation: Which the troop had taken from the south of Judah and from the south of Caleb.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: which they drove before those other cattle
1 Samuel.english_translation: Men leading and going before that livestock, to be honoured and to boast: “This is David’s spoil.”

It does not say “and onward” but “and upward”: Abraham had already instituted this law (Genesis 14:24): “save only that which the young men have eaten,” etc. — these are those who sit by the vessels — “and the portion of the men” — those who go to war, in Genesis Rabbah (43:9).
To his friends.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: where David himself and his men were wont to haunt
1 Samuel.english_translation: Those who hid him from Saul.

1 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Now the Philistines fought against Israel
1 Samuel.english_translation: Like a person who says, “Let us return to the first subject.”
Like “about him” — about Saul.
Targum: “and they burned [spices] over them, as they burn over kings there,” as we learned (Avodah Zarah 11a): “They burn [spices] for kings, and it is not of the ways of the Amorites.”

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: a man came out of the camp
2 Samuel.english_translation: There is in the Pesikta that this was Doeg, and it does not sit well in my heart.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: the agony hath taken hold of me
2 Samuel.english_translation: (Targum:) *achadani retita* (“trembling has seized me”). And an aggadic Midrash (see Yalkut Shimoni §141): because of the sin of the priests whom he killed, and it is written of them (Exodus 28:4): “a tunic of chequer work” (*ketonet tashbetz*).

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: because my life is just yet in me
2 Samuel.english_translation: Hurry and put me to death; it is better for me that you put me to death than that these should kill me and abuse me.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and the bracelet that was on his arm
2 Samuel.english_translation: (Targum:) “and the *totafta* that was on his arm.”

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Thy blood be upon thy head
2 Samuel.english_translation: (Targum:) “The guilt of your killing be upon your head”; there is no punishment for your death except for yourself.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: To teach the sons of Judah the bow
2 Samuel.english_translation: And David said: From now that the mighty men of Israel have fallen, the sons of Judah need to be taught war and to draw the bow.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Behold, it is written in the book of Jashar
2 Samuel.english_translation: Is it not written in the book of Genesis, which is the book of the upright ones — Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; and where is it alluded to? (Genesis 49:8): “thy hand shall be on the neck of thine enemies” — what warfare is it in which one aims his hand toward his forehead, which is opposite his neck? Say, this is the bow.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Thy beauty, O Israel, upon thy high places is slain
2 Samuel.english_translation: The standing-place of Israel: upon the strength of your stronghold you have fallen slain; so Jonathan translated.
2 Samuel.translator_note: The Hebrew word מצבן is translated literally; its sense here is not clear to me.

2 Samuel.english_translation: The mountains that are in Gilboa.
(Targum:) “There shall not be in you produce, like the portion from which they would make challah.”
2 Samuel.translator_note: The Aramaic word *kemisat* is uncertain to me; the phrase is translated as nearly as I can. Audit 4: the Aramaic quotation was checked against Targum Jonathan/the Ketuvim Targum (Mikraot Gedolot, Sefaria) at 2SA 1:21 and reads as quoted; the meaning of the unclear word, if noted above, is still unresolved.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: For there the shield of the mighty was vilely cast away
2 Samuel.english_translation: They had shields of leather, and when they went out to battle they would anoint them with oil, so that the weapon that strikes upon it would slide off, as you say (Isaiah 21:5): “Rise up, you princes, anoint the shield.” And here he was lamenting thus: “there the shield of the mighty was vilely cast away” — it cast out its fat and nothing stuck to it, and it became as though it had not been anointed with oil. Every *hag'alah* is an expression of a thing that casts out what is put into it, like (Job 21:10): “Their bull gendereth, and faileth not” (*yag'il*).
2 Samuel.translator_note: Rashi reads *yag'il* in Job 21:10 as “cast out.”

2 Samuel.english_translation: He was not accustomed to turn backward.
To do the will of their Creator.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Who clothed you in scarlet, with other delights
2 Samuel.english_translation: (Targum:) “who clothed you in garments of colours and brought you delicacies” (the language of Targum Jonathan).

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: upon thy high places is slain
2 Samuel.english_translation: (Targum:) “in the house of thy strength thou wast slain.”
Saul and Jonathan, who were the weapons of Israel.

A verse was expounding that two kings were destined to arise from Benjamin, for the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Jacob (Genesis 35:11): “and kings shall come out of thy loins,” and all his sons had already been born except Benjamin.
2 Samuel.translator_note: The printed reference reads Genesis 35:12, but the quoted words are in 35:11. The opening sentence is terse and is translated literally.

2 Samuel.english_translation: (Targum:) “the portion of the slain,” on account of the swords, as you say (Psalms 89:44): “Yea, Thou turnest back the edge of his sword.”
Like the fifth rib, the place where the gall and the liver are attached (Sanhedrin 49a); and Jonathan translated: “to the *chomesh*,” in the side of his thigh.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and died in the same place
2 Samuel.english_translation: (Targum:) “and he died in his place.”

If you had spoken so; *lulei* is like *lu* (“if”). And one can also interpret it according to its plain meaning: had you not spoken what you said (above v. 14): “Let the young men, I pray thee, arise and play before us.”
The name of a district.

But is not Asahel included among David’s servants? Why is he set apart? Because he was equal to all of them. And so (Joshua 2:1): “Go, view the land, and Jericho”; and so (1 Kings 11:1): “Now king Solomon loved many strange women, together with the daughter of Pharaoh.”

And in another place he is called “and the second, Daniel.” And why was his name called Chileab? Rabbi Isaac said: Because the scoffers of the generation were saying, Abigail was pregnant by Nabal; his features were changed and he came to resemble his father. And our Rabbis said (Berakhot 4a): Because he used to put to shame (*mekhalim*) the face of Mephibosheth in halakhah.
2 Samuel.translator_note: The “other place” is 1 Chronicles 3:1. The sentence about the features is terse and is translated literally.

2 Samuel.english_translation: This is Michal, who was beloved to him, and so he says (Judges 14:18): “If you had not plowed with my heifer.” But is it not written (below 6:23): “And Michal the daughter of Saul had no child unto the day of her death”? “Unto the day of her death” — she had none from that incident onward; before that incident she had.
With all his strength on behalf of the house of Saul, to establish his kingship.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Am I a dog’s head that belongeth to Judah?
2 Samuel.english_translation: Am I considered even like the head of the keeper of David’s dogs? But according to the cantillation, in which the accent is on *ha-rosh* and *kelev anokhi* is joined by a *maqqef*, its interpretation is this: “The head?” — would I desire to be head in your house? It is better for me to be a dog and a commoner in the house of David; and so Jonathan translated.
2 Samuel.translator_note: The printed Hebrew reads אשר לדוד (“of David”); the verse reads ליהודה (“of Judah”).

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: This day do I show kindness
2 Samuel.english_translation: From now on it is fitting for me to do kindness with the house of Saul and with all his friends, as I have done until now, and I have not delivered you into David’s hand.
2 Samuel.translator_note: The printed form is המציתיך; the verse reads המצאתיך.

2 Samuel.english_translation: (Targum:) “from his place, saying: I swear by Him who made the earth.”
2 Samuel.translator_note: The Aramaic is translated as nearly as I can; I could not confirm *mekayemna*. Audit 4: the Aramaic quotation was checked against Targum Jonathan/the Ketuvim Targum (Mikraot Gedolot, Sefaria) at 2SA 3:12 and reads as quoted; the meaning of the unclear word, if noted above, is still unresolved.

2 Samuel.english_translation: An expression of an oath: by Him to whom the land belongs. Another explanation: *tachtav* — he mentioned his own name first in the letter, and afterward mentioned David’s name, and therefore he was punished; he wrote: “From me, Abner, captain of the host of Israel, to David, king of Israel, peace.”
To him to whom the kingship is fitting I send, saying: “Make thy league,” etc.
Before you see my face — your bringing Michal.
Jonathan translated: “from beside her husband.”
Over the commandment that was going from him, for all those years he had stuck a sword in the bed between himself and her, and he did not stumble with her.
2 Samuel.translator_note: The word מצוה is translated literally as “commandment”; the sense of the phrase is not clear to me.

2 Samuel.english_translation: Before this.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: the LORD hath spoken of David
2 Samuel.english_translation: About David, and it does not depart from the meaning of *el*.
They spread out in a raiding troop, to take spoil from the enemy.

The name of a place; and our Rabbis said (Sanhedrin 49a): *Bor* (a pit) and *sirah* (a thorn) caused Abner to be killed, because he did not uphold David’s words concerning the flask of water that David took from Saul’s headrest, and also concerning the skirt of Saul’s robe he said, Perhaps one of the thorns (*sirim*) caught on it and tore it.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: into the midst of the gate
2 Samuel.english_translation: Before the Sanhedrin, to be judged for the blood of Asahel his brother.
In error, since Abner did not understand that [Joab] had it in his heart to kill him; and he transposed the verse: “and Joab took him aside *be-shali* into the midst of the gate to speak with him.”
2 Samuel.translator_note: “Transposed the verse” is a literal rendering of וסרס המקרא; the exact sense is uncertain.

2 Samuel.english_translation: *Yachulu* — “let them rest”; “let the blood of Abner” refers back to the verse before it, in which he said, “I and my kingdom are guiltless … of the blood of Abner”; let his blood fall upon the head of Joab — the blood mentioned in the verse before it.
2 Samuel.translator_note: Rashi’s sentence is terse; translated as literally as the sense allows.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: or that leaneth on a staff
2 Samuel.english_translation: Leaning on his stick because of an ailment of the feet.

Like “*et* Abner,” and similar to it (Isaiah 38:14): “*ashkah li arvaveni*” — “it oppressed me”; and so (Numbers 12:13): “*refa na lah*” — “heal her”; and like it (2 Chronicles 17:7): “he sent to his princes, to Ben-hail, and to Obadiah,” etc., “to teach in the cities of Judah” — and its meaning is: he sent his princes, [namely] Ben-hail.
2 Samuel.translator_note: Rashi’s point is that the particle *lamed* stands as the direct-object marker; the three parallels are translated as given.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Should Abner die as a churl dieth
2 Samuel.english_translation: Like the death of a wicked man, by the sword?
They were [so] — and how did a mighty man like you fall before the sons of iniquity?
2 Samuel.translator_note: The word היו (“they were”) is elliptical in the Hebrew; translated literally.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: to cause David to eat bread
2 Samuel.english_translation: An expression of a meal.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: And I am this day weak
2 Samuel.english_translation: (Targum:) “And I am today an ordinary man (*hedyot*), and one anointed to be king.”
They were to the son of Saul (*hayu le-ven Shaul*), like (1 Samuel 13:8): “*le-mo'ed asher Shemuel*” — [meaning] *asher li-Shemuel* (“that was Samuel’s”).
When Saul died, because the children of Israel abandoned the cities around the Philistines, as stated above, then the Beerothites fled.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Now Jonathan, Saul’s son, had a son
2 Samuel.english_translation: He goes on enumerating how the kingship ceased from the house of Saul: he and his sons were killed, and this one who remained — they killed him upon his bed, and the son of Jonathan fell and became lame.
Broken of feet.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: And they came thither into the midst of the house
2 Samuel.english_translation: With merchants, buyers of wheat.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: instead of giving a reward for his tidings
2 Samuel.english_translation: Who thought to gladden me, so that I would give him the reward for his tidings.

The fortress of Zion was called Jebus, and they were of the seed of Abimelech, and they had two images, one blind and one lame, which were made after Isaac and Jacob, and in their mouth was the oath that Abraham swore to Abimelech; and therefore, when [Israel] captured Jerusalem, they did not drive them out — they did not capture the fortress, as it is said (Joshua 15:63): “And as for the Jebusites, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the children of Judah could not drive them out”; and it was taught: Rabbi Joshua ben Levi said: They were able, but they were not permitted (Sifre Re’eh 12:17).
The one who said [it].
They are their idols.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Whosoever smiteth the Jebusites, and getteth up to the gutter
2 Samuel.english_translation: (Targum:) “Whoever slays the Jebusite and begins to conquer the city.”
And he shall also smite the lame and the blind, who are hated of David’s soul.
Because they say, “Blind and lame” — [meaning,] as long as the blind and the lame shall be here.
2 Samuel.translator_note: Rashi’s sentence is clipped; translated literally.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: he cannot come into the house
2 Samuel.english_translation: “David shall come hither.” Behold, this is an elliptical verse, for it said, “Whosoever smiteth the Jebusites, and getteth up to the gutter,” and did not explain what shall be done for him; and in Chronicles (1 Chronicles 11:6) it explained: “Whosoever smiteth the Jebusites first shall be chief and captain”; and like this (Genesis 4:15): “Therefore whosoever slayeth Cain,” and it did not explain what shall be done to him, but of itself it is understood as an expression of rebuke and reproof.
2 Samuel.translator_note: The opening words (יבא דוד הנה) are as printed; how they relate to the lemma is not clear to me.

2 Samuel.english_translation: An expression of the height of the tower, for there their images were placed; and in the days of David the generations mentioned in the oath had already passed.

A circuit of a low wall, and they fill it with earth, and the height of the mound is in the middle and slopes down toward every side — it is called Millo; and upon it David built houses; and that Millo was around the fortress.
When he saw all his deeds prospering, and the kings of the nations sending him a gift.
And they spread out.
The plain of Perazim.
Like waters that burst the banks of the brink.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and David and his men took them away
2 Samuel.english_translation: (Targum:) “and David and his men burned them.”
It is near Jerusalem, in the book of Joshua (15:8).
(Targum:) “opposite the trees.”

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: the sound of marching in the tops of the mulberry-trees
2 Samuel.english_translation: They are angels marching on the tops of the trees, whom I send to your aid.
You shall raise the sound of battle and the clash of the sword — *glapid* in Old French; and so (Exodus 11:7): “shall not a dog whet his tongue.”
2 Samuel.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is גלפי״ד; Darmesteter (1909) reads *glapir* for this verse word.

2 Samuel.english_translation: To gather.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: all the chosen men of Israel, thirty thousand
2 Samuel.english_translation: Because they had gathered to him when they made him king in Hebron, and this was a second gathering, therefore “again” is said.

It is Kiriath-jearim, as it is said in Joshua (15:9): “and the border was drawn to Baalah, the same is Kiriath-jearim”; and so in Chronicles (1 Chronicles 13:6): “And David went up, and all Israel, to Baalah, that is, to Kiriath-jearim.” And *ba'al* is an expression of “plain.”

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: And David arose, and went … from Baale-judah
2 Samuel.english_translation: Who were gathered there to bring up the Ark from there, etc.
That a name was called upon the Ark; and what is the name? That the name of the LORD of hosts was upon it.

He erred in a thing that even children of the schoolhouse know, that “the service of the sanctuary belonged unto them; they bore it upon the shoulder” (Numbers 7:9); and because he said (Psalms 119:54): “Thy statutes have been my songs in the house of my pilgrimage,” he was punished by coming to this, and Uzzah died through him; therefore when he brought it up from the house of Obed-edom, he brought it on the shoulder, as it is said (1 Chronicles 15:12–13): “and said unto them: You are the heads of the fathers’ houses of the Levites; sanctify yourselves … that you may bring up the ark …; for because you [bore it] not at the first, the LORD our God made a breach upon us, for that we sought Him not according to the ordinance.”
Behold, this is an elliptical verse: and they came with the Ark of God.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: with all manner of instruments made of cypress-wood
2 Samuel.english_translation: From which they make musical instruments.

For the oxen made it slip and shook it; and so Jonathan translated: *ari margohi toraya*; as he translates (Deuteronomy 19:5) “and his hand fetcheth a stroke with the axe” — *ve-titmarig yadeih be-farzela*.
2 Samuel.translator_note: The Aramaic words are transliterated, not translated.

2 Samuel.english_translation: For the error, for he should have reasoned from a fortiori: it carried its bearers in the Jordan — would it not, all the more so, [carry] itself?
2 Samuel.translator_note: The a fortiori argument is stated tersely and is translated literally.

2 Samuel.english_translation: He was a Levite, as it is written in Chronicles (1 Chronicles 15:18), and was of the gatekeepers (ibid.).
His wife and her eight daughters-in-law gave birth to six sons in one womb, as it is said (1 Chronicles 26:6, 8): “Peullethai the eighth”; sixty-two for Obed-edom.
2 Samuel.translator_note: The Hebrew says “six sons in one womb” and does not say “each”; it is translated literally. The printed reference is 26:6, 8.

2 Samuel.english_translation: Dancing.
A linen coat, *porçeint* in Old French; and Jonathan translated: *kardot*; and so Jonathan translated the “robes” of Tamar, Absalom’s sister (below 13:18): *kardotin*.
2 Samuel.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is פורציינ״ט; Darmesteter (1909) lists the form “Porçejjnt” and renders it “un manteau de lin” (a linen cloak), with a cross-reference to p. 24.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: a cake made in a pan
2 Samuel.english_translation: One of six [portions] in a bull (Pesachim 36b).
2 Samuel.translator_note: Rashi’s Hebrew is terse and is translated literally.

2 Samuel.english_translation: A jar of wine (ibid.).
(Targum:) “one of the empty ones” (the language of Targum Jonathan).

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and will be base in mine own sight
2 Samuel.english_translation: Before Him, more than this that I have lowered myself now.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: with them will I get me honour
2 Samuel.english_translation: They do not despise me; rather, I am held important in their eyes because of this.
From that day onward.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and the LORD had given him rest
2 Samuel.english_translation: He said: Behold, (Deuteronomy 12:10) “and He giveth you rest from all your enemies,” etc., has been fulfilled; what is written after it? “Then it shall come to pass that the place which the LORD your God shall choose,” etc. — from now it is upon us to build the House of the Choice.

Rabbi Hanina bar Papa said: The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Nathan: This man to whom I am sending you is quick; perhaps he will hire workers, and I will be found to have caused him loss; hurry and say to him, “Thou shalt not build the house.” Rabbi Simon says: This man to whom I am sending you is a maker of vows, as it is said (Psalms 132:2–3): “How he swore unto the LORD, and vowed unto the Mighty One of Jacob: Surely I will not come into the tent of my house”; perhaps he will say, I will not eat and I will not drink until I do thus, and I will be found to have caused him loss (Yalkut Shimoni §143).

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: in a tent and in a tabernacle
2 Samuel.english_translation: The Tabernacle of Shiloh had no roof, but [was] a house of stones below, and curtains above.
It is an expression of astonishment; therefore the *he* is vocalized with a *chataf-patach*, and the *dalet* is soft (*rafe*).
The pen of the shepherds, like (Zephaniah 2:6): “*neot kerot ro'im*” (JPS: “meadows for shepherds”).

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: like unto the name of the great ones
2 Samuel.english_translation: This is what we say: “Shield of David.”

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and have cut off all thine enemies
2 Samuel.english_translation: And therefore it came into your heart to build the House, as it is written in the Torah.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: And I will appoint a place
2 Samuel.english_translation: Moreover I desire to give rest, that my people be quiet and at ease in the days of your son.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: even from the day that I commanded
2 Samuel.english_translation: It is connected to the preceding: and they shall not again afflict them as at first, before the judges, and as they did from the days of the judges until now.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and I will cause thee to rest
2 Samuel.english_translation: More and more, until you rest from all your enemies.
Today, through me, that a house will be made for you, to seat your son on your throne, and the house of kingship will be established for you, and he shall build the House.
This is Hadad and Rezon son of Eliada.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and with the stripes of the children of men
2 Samuel.english_translation: This is Ashmedai, who drove him out of his kingdom; and the demons are the sons of the first man, for all the hundred and thirty years that Adam separated from his wife after the death of Abel, the spirits were conceiving and bearing from him (Yalkut Shimoni §146).
Before the Ark.
That You made me king.
To make my son king after me.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and this too after the manner of great men
2 Samuel.english_translation: In astonishment: is it fitting that flesh and blood be given such tidings? Another explanation: You have done for me as You did for the first man, to whom You showed the generations destined to come forth from him.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: And what can David say more unto Thee?
2 Samuel.english_translation: What more shall I ask?
You have given me all my needs, like (Proverbs 12:10): “A righteous man regardeth the life of his beast.”
To fulfil what You said to Samuel, to make me king.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and according to Thine own heart
2 Samuel.english_translation: It is Your will, and not that I am worthy.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: to make Thy servant know it
2 Samuel.english_translation: The tidings with which You gladdened me.
Moses and Aaron, as it is said (Exodus 7:1): “I have set thee in God’s stead to Pharaoh”; and so Jonathan translated: “who went as messengers from before the LORD.”

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: to redeem unto Himself for a people
2 Samuel.english_translation: So the messengers said to Israel: The Holy One, blessed be He, sent us to redeem a people for Himself, and to make Him a name, and to do for you the great thing.

You did for Your land after they went out from there; and what are the awesome things? “From before Thy people” — to drive out peoples and their gods; and this verse lacks “to drive out,” and in Chronicles (1 Chronicles 17:21) it is explained: “to drive out from before Thy people, whom Thou didst redeem out of Egypt, nations and its gods”; and it is not a lack, for from the implication of what is said, “from before Thy people, nations,” we understand an expression of driving away and expulsion.
2 Samuel.translator_note: The printed quotation of 1 Chronicles 17:21 is a condensed form; it is translated as printed and still to be compared with that verse.

2 Samuel.english_translation: Ruler, and You have the power to fulfil.
Be pleased.

And in Chronicles (1 Chronicles 18:1) it is written: “And David took Gath out of the hand of the Philistines,” and it is called *metheg ha-ammah* because it is a rod ruling over all the Philistines, the metropolis (*metropolin*) of kings, for we do not find, among all the lords of the Philistines in Gaza, in Ashdod, in Ekron and in Ashkelon, a name of kingship, but in Gath we find it (1 Samuel 21:11): “Achish the king of Gath.”
2 Samuel.translator_note: The printed quotation of 1 Chronicles 18:1 is not word for word the verse (which also says “and her towns”); it is translated as printed.

2 Samuel.english_translation: *Agoillon* in Old French.
2 Samuel.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is אגויילו״ן; Darmesteter (1909) lists the form “Agojjlon” and renders it “l’aiguillon” (the goad).

2 Samuel.english_translation: It is the wooden ox-goad.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: two lines to put to death
2 Samuel.english_translation: Because they had killed his father and his mother and his brothers, as it is said (1 Samuel 22:4): “And he brought them before the king of Moab,” and we do not find that they went out from there.
When Hadadezer went.
As its Targum: *le-ashna'ah techumeih* (“to alter his boundaries”), for he conquered part of the land outside the border of his own land, and enlarged his border.
2 Samuel.translator_note: The Aramaic word *le-ashna'ah* is translated as “to alter”; I could not confirm it. Audit 4: the Aramaic quotation was checked against Targum Jonathan/the Ketuvim Targum (Mikraot Gedolot, Sefaria) at 2SA 8:3 and reads as quoted; the meaning of the unclear word, if noted above, is still unresolved.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: David houghed all the chariot horses
2 Samuel.english_translation: Because of (Deuteronomy 17:16): “Only he shall not multiply horses to himself.”

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: but reserved of them for a hundred chariots
2 Samuel.english_translation: Because they were needed for his chariotry; and a chariot [has] four horses, as it is said (2 Chronicles 1:17): “a chariot for six hundred shekels of silver, and a horse for a hundred and fifty”; here we have learned that a chariot [has] four horses.

They are quivers in which arrows are put, as you say (Jeremiah 51:11): “Make bright the arrows, fill the quivers.” All these sections he placed next to the section of the Temple, because from all these wars he gathered consecrated things for the needs of the House.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: And David got him a name
2 Samuel.english_translation: That he buried the slain whom he had killed in Edom, and it is a good name for Israel that they bury their enemies; and so it says of the war of Gog and Magog (Ezekiel 39:13): “Yea, all the people of the land shall bury, and it shall be to them a renown.” And whence [do we know] that David buried them? As it is said in the book of Kings (1 Kings 11:15): “For it came to pass, when David was in Edom, and Joab the captain of the host was gone up to bury the slain.”
And in the book of Psalms (60:2) it says twelve thousand; say, then, there were two wars.
Officers to collect tribute.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: And David reigned over all Israel
2 Samuel.english_translation: David caused Joab to be successful over the host, because he executed justice and righteousness; and Joab caused David to execute justice and righteousness, because [David] judges while Joab is an officer and subduer at his hand; and furthermore, because Joab occupied himself with the wars, David was not troubled by them, and his heart was free to judge righteously.
He reminds [the king] which case came before him first, to decide it first.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: over the Cherethites and the Pelethites
2 Samuel.english_translation: Jonathan translated: “and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, appointed over the archers and over the slingers.” And our Rabbis said (Berakhot 4a): the Cherethites and Pelethites are the Urim and Thummim.
Jonathan translated: “they were great ones.”

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: have I given unto thy master’s son
2 Samuel.english_translation: The king is permitted to transfer an inheritance, as it is said in the law of the king (1 Samuel 8:14): “And he will take your fields, and your vineyards … and give them to his servants.”

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: so shall thy servant do; but Mephibosheth eateth at my table
2 Samuel.english_translation: Ziba said: “So shall thy servant do,” and David replied: “and Mephibosheth eateth at my table.”
2 Samuel.translator_note: Rashi gives the last clause to David; the JPS rendering gives it to Ziba.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: all that dwelt in the house of Ziba
2 Samuel.english_translation: His sons and his servants.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: as his father showed kindness unto me
2 Samuel.english_translation: And what is the kindness? When David was fleeing from Saul, his father and his mother and his brothers came to him (1 Samuel 22:4): “And he brought them before the king of Moab,” and said to him: “Let my father and mother, I pray thee, abide with you,” and he killed them, except for one of them who fled and escaped to the land of the children of Ammon, to Nahash (in Midrash Rabbi Tanchuma, in [the portion] *Vayera elav*).
2 Samuel.translator_note: The printed words of David’s request differ from the wording of 1 Samuel 22:3; they are translated as printed.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Thinkest thou that David doth honour thy father
2 Samuel.english_translation: Does it appear in your eyes that David honours your father? They (Israel) are warned, “thou shalt not seek their peace,” and he seeks your peace?
2 Samuel.translator_note: The warning is from Deuteronomy 23:7.

2 Samuel.english_translation: Their tunics.
The buttocks.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: with Shobach the captain of the host of Hadadezer
2 Samuel.english_translation: Because he was very mighty and fierce, they mentioned him by name.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: at the time when kings go out
2 Samuel.english_translation: There is a time in the year when it is the way of armies to go out, when the land is full of standing grain and the horses find grain in the field to eat.
From her menstrual impurity.
For he intended that he lie with his wife, and that he would think she was pregnant by him.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: a mess of food from the king
2 Samuel.english_translation: (Targum:) “the king’s meal.”

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: that he may be smitten, and die
2 Samuel.english_translation: So that she would be divorced retroactively, and it would turn out that he had not come upon a married woman, for everyone who goes out to war writes a bill of divorce for his wife on condition, if he dies in the war (Shabbat 56a).
He is Gideon, who contended with the *bosheth* — that is, the Baal.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: make thy battle more strong against the city, and overthrow it
2 Samuel.english_translation: Up to here are the words of the message.
David said to the messenger: And strengthen him, Joab, with words of consolation, that his heart not grow faint.
He likened the evil inclination first to a “traveller,” who is passing on his way, and afterward to a “guest,” who becomes a lodger, and afterward to a “man,” who is the master of the house.
One who robs the poor, it is as if he takes his soul, as it is said (Proverbs 1:19): “it taketh away the life of the owners thereof.”
So it befell him, for he was struck in four of his children: the child, and Amnon, Tamar, and Absalom.
2 Samuel.translator_note: The Hebrew says “four sons” (בנים), but the list includes Tamar.

2 Samuel.english_translation: Michal the daughter of Saul.
And I would have added to you.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: thou hast greatly blasphemed the enemies of the LORD
2 Samuel.english_translation: This is a euphemism, a respectful manner concerning [Him who is] above; and Jonathan translated: “because by opening you have opened the mouth of the enemies of the people of the LORD.”
An expression of illness.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: he lay all night upon the earth
2 Samuel.english_translation: And he would come into the house and spend the night lying on the ground.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: neither did he eat bread with them
2 Samuel.english_translation: An expression of eating, like (below 13:6): “that I may eat at her hand” (*ve-evreh mi-yadah*).
Who loved him.
It had two fortifications of wall, an outer and an inner; the outer city was the royal city, and the inner was for a fortress and for strength.
The abomination of the children of Ammon; *Malkam* is its name, an expression of Molech.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and it was set on David’s head
2 Samuel.english_translation: Ittai the Gittite nullified it (Avodah Zarah 44a).

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: under saws, and under harrows of iron, and under axes of iron
2 Samuel.english_translation: Like a kind of file (*pitzira*) — *pim* — which they call *lime*; kinds of torments.
2 Samuel.translator_note:
The word פים is as printed; its sense here is not clear to me.
Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is לימ״א. Darmesteter (1909, on 2 Samuel 12:31) reads *lime* (a file).

2 Samuel.english_translation: A knife nicked with many nicks, close one to another.
It is a notched threshing-sledge (*morag*), full of notches, like a kind of file (*pitzira*) — *pim* — which they call *lime*.
2 Samuel.translator_note:
The word פים is as printed; its sense here is not clear to me.
Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is לימ״א. Darmesteter (1909, on 2 Samuel 12:31) reads *lime* (a file).

2 Samuel.english_translation: In the mud of the streets; and so Jonathan translated: “and he dragged them in the streets.”
Who was his mother’s daughter.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: so distressed that he fell sick
2 Samuel.english_translation: Until he became ill.

Modest in the house and not going out; therefore “and it seemed hard to Amnon,” etc. — it was concealed and hidden from him what pretext he could seek to lie with her, like (Deuteronomy 17:8): “*ki yippale mimkha*” — Targum: *ari yitkasei mimakh* (“if it be hidden from you”).
For wickedness.
Lean, like (Genesis 41:19): “*dalot ve-ra'ot to'ar*” (“poor and very ill-favoured”).
The meal.
*Ve-tachlot* (“and she scalded”): fine flour mixed in boiling water first, and afterward in oil.
The Targum of *machavat* (“pan”) is *masrita*.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: for he will not withhold me from thee
2 Samuel.english_translation: That I am permitted to you, because my mother conceived me while she was a gentile, a woman of beautiful form whom David took in war; and one who has a son or daughter from a maidservant, that is not his child for any purpose.
Our Rabbis said (Sanhedrin 21a): A hair became wound around him, and it made him *kerut shofkhah* (one whose organ was cut off).
2 Samuel.translator_note: The Talmudic expression *kerut shofkhah* is left in transliteration with a literal gloss.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Not so, because this great wrong
2 Samuel.english_translation: Do not [do it], on account of this evil of sending away, which is greater than the other that you did with me and afflicted me; and you would add yet an evil beyond it, to send me away.
And their way was to make a feast at the shearing of their flocks.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: If not, I pray thee, let my brother Amnon go with us
2 Samuel.english_translation: And if you cannot go, let Amnon go with us.
By Absalom’s command this appointment was appointed upon his servants, to kill Amnon.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: And the soul of king David failed with longing
2 Samuel.english_translation: Behold, this is an elliptical verse: “and the soul of David longed”; and so Jonathan translated: “and the longing of David’s soul,” like (Psalms 84:3): “My soul yearneth, yea, even pineth” — an expression of desire.
2 Samuel.translator_note: JPS renders the words “And the soul of king David failed with longing.”

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: for he was comforted concerning Amnon
2 Samuel.english_translation: He accepted consolation.
Our Rabbis said (Menachot 85b): Because olive oil is found there, therefore wisdom is found there.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Of a truth I am a widow
2 Samuel.english_translation: *Aval*: in truth (*be-kushta*).

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: the iniquity be on me, my lord, O king
2 Samuel.english_translation: This is a euphemism out of respect for him, that is, you are putting me off, saying: I will give an order concerning you, and I will go my way, and you will not give an order concerning me — and my son will be killed: on whom is this iniquity?
2 Samuel.translator_note: Rashi’s sentence is terse; translated literally.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: let the king remember the LORD thy God
2 Samuel.english_translation: That He was strict regarding the length of the road in order to save lives, as it is said (Deuteronomy 19:6): “and overtake him, because the way is long”; and this is [the meaning of] “that the avenger of blood destroy not any more” — and you are putting me off.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Wherefore then hast thou devised such a thing
2 Samuel.english_translation: That you have suspected Israel, that they would come to kill the second [son] without witnesses and warning.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: for in speaking this word the king is as one that is guilty
2 Samuel.english_translation: And this thing that you decreed for others, for you said to me, “not one hair of thy son shall fall to the earth” — now that I reveal to you that this matter concerns only your two sons, do not regret, saying, “I spoke this as one guilty,” and “Behold, I retract,” so as not to bring back the king’s son Absalom, who was banished from him and fled.
*Okenon parlteis* in Old French.
2 Samuel.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is אוקינו״ן פרלטי״ש; Darmesteter (1909) reads *é ke non parolt* for this verse word. The printed form is not identical to his reading, so I give the printed form and his reading and offer no reading of my own.

2 Samuel.english_translation: And let us be content with that punishment.
2 Samuel.translator_note: The Hebrew is terse (ודיינו באותו עונש); translated literally.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: neither doth God respect any person
2 Samuel.english_translation: [He does not spare] any man from death; therefore “let the king devise devices, that none banished be banished from him.”

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Now therefore seeing that I am come to speak this word unto my lord the king
2 Samuel.english_translation: By way of euphemism: concerning me and concerning my son.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: because the people have made me afraid
2 Samuel.english_translation: They frightened me from entreating my lord concerning his son, lest he be angry with me.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and thy handmaid said: I will now speak
2 Samuel.english_translation: Along these lines: “It may be that the king will perform,” etc.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: For the king will hear, to deliver his servant out of the hand of the man
2 Samuel.english_translation: Who comes to kill my son, and to destroy us together from the inheritance of God.

Since the king will command concerning me, let his word be for rest for my son, for he will not retract from his good word, for as the angel of the LORD is my lord the king, and anger and hatred will not turn him back from his good word.
2 Samuel.translator_note: The printed text reads “angel of the LORD”; the verse reads “angel of God.”

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: none can turn to the right hand or to the left
2 Samuel.english_translation: *Im esh* is like *im yesh*, like *ha-yesh*, and so (Micah 6:10): “*od ha-esh beit rasha*,” like *ha-yesh*.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: to change the face of the matter
2 Samuel.english_translation: To bring about a turn, until the matter of the king’s son should come out into the light.
And you understood that it came from Joab.
Close to my property, in a place where I can do damage.
*Inmeis oust* in Old French.
2 Samuel.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is אינמי״ש אוש״ט; Darmesteter (1909) reads *an més ayses* (“à mon côté”). The printed form is similar but not identical, so I give the printed form and his reading only.

2 Samuel.english_translation: And let the king kill me.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and fifty men to run before him
2 Samuel.english_translation: All of them with the spleen removed, and the soles of their feet engraved.
2 Samuel.translator_note: The Hebrew is translated literally.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: And Absalom used to rise up early
2 Samuel.english_translation: Every morning.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Thy servant is of one of the tribes of Israel
2 Samuel.english_translation: Of such-and-such a tribe.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and I would do him justice
2 Samuel.english_translation: (Targum:) “and I would judge him in truth.”

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: at the end of forty years
2 Samuel.english_translation: From when Israel asked Samuel for a king, the matter of rebellion and debasement in the kingship came about.
To Hebron.
Our Rabbis said (Sotah 34b): To bring sheep from Hebron, for fat sheep were there.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: that were invited, and went in their simplicity
2 Samuel.english_translation: It is explained in the tractate Sotah of the Jerusalem Talmud (1:8) that he asked his father to write for him that any two men whom he would ask to go with him should go; and he showed it to two here, and afterward to two others, and so on at length.
(Targum:) “in the place that is far.”
Next to him; he stands and they pass by.
With Absalom.
And we are fleeing without provisions and food, and because you are a foreigner you will not find those who have compassion.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and also an exile from thine own place
2 Samuel.english_translation: And even if you are an exile from the king’s people, because you do not wish to be with him, return to your place; for your going with me is not good, for you came only yesterday.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: should I this day make thee go up and down with us
2 Samuel.english_translation: And I have no place where I can seat you and escape, for I am going wherever the chance happens to take me; every day when I hear that the pursuers are here, I flee from here; and so Jonathan translated “and also an exile, thou, to thy place”: *ve-af im gali at azil lakh le-atrakh* (“and even if you are an exile, go to your place”).
I am grateful to you for the kindness and truth that you did with me.
With the rest of the people, since you do not wish to part from me.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: as all the people passed over
2 Samuel.english_translation: From the king onward; since he is standing, he calls them “passing.”
Like *va-yatzigu* (“and they placed”); (Targum:) *ve-akimu yat aruna* — they stood it to one side, and the people passed by, for David wanted to carry it with him.
Behold, this is a verse with transposed order: “and they set down the ark of God until all the people had done passing.”

On that day he was removed from the priesthood, because he inquired by the Urim and Thummim and was not answered, and Zadok entered in his place; and so we learned in Seder Olam and in tractate Yoma (73b).
If you see that it is sound counsel, return to the city, etc.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and your two sons with you
2 Samuel.english_translation: Through them you will be able to inform me of what you hear from the king’s house; according to what you inform me, I will escape.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: by the ascent of the mount of Olives
2 Samuel.english_translation: On the Mount of Olives.
Wrapped, in the manner of mourners.
(Targum:) *kerikhu* (“wrapped”).
And the teller told David.
Spoil, like (Ecclesiastes 10:14): “A fool also multiplieth words.”

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: to the top of the ascent
2 Samuel.english_translation: (Targum:) “to the top of the mountain.”

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: where God was wont to be worshipped
2 Samuel.english_translation: Where he was accustomed to bow down when he came to Jerusalem; he would see from there the tent in which the Ark was, and would bow down.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: as I have been thy father’s servant in time past
2 Samuel.english_translation: Like “and I was your father’s servant of old”; and it is a verse with transposed order.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: was at the point of coming into Jerusalem
2 Samuel.english_translation: He set his heart that he would come to Jerusalem.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and a hundred of summer fruits
2 Samuel.english_translation: (Targum:) “and a hundred *menan* of fig-cake.”
2 Samuel.translator_note: The Aramaic word *menan* is left untranslated. Audit 4: the Aramaic quotation was checked against Targum Jonathan/the Ketuvim Targum (Mikraot Gedolot, Sefaria) at 2SA 16:1 and reads as quoted; the meaning of the unclear word, if noted above, is still unresolved.
