2 Samuel.english_translation: So shall he curse.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: because the LORD hath said unto him
2 Samuel.english_translation: Is it possible that a man like him, who is head of the Sanhedrin, would curse the king unless it had been told him by the Holy One, blessed be He?

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: the LORD will look on mine eye
2 Samuel.english_translation: The tear of my eye.
With the young men.
2 Samuel.translator_note: The Hebrew gives only the word בבחורים; translated literally.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: then will the hands of all that are with thee be strong
2 Samuel.english_translation: For now their hands are slack to help you, for they say in their hearts, “The son will repent before his father, and we will be hated by the king.”
To you.
Your request will be done with him, and he will be killed, and afterward all the people will be at peace; and this is an elliptical verse.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and all the elders of Israel
2 Samuel.english_translation: The elders of *Ashmai*.
2 Samuel.translator_note: The word אשמאי is as printed; I could not confirm its meaning.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and thy father is a man of war
2 Samuel.english_translation: And he knows the matters of war and its stratagems and the quality of an ambush, and he is certain that you will pursue him by night to come upon him; therefore he will not lodge with the rest of the people.
And when you come against the camp of the people who are with him, he will not be there, that you could kill him.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: when they fall upon them at the first
2 Samuel.english_translation: I told you that his men are mighty and embittered, and if they kill among your people, there will be a defeat among them in this war, which is the first; and the hearer from all Israel who come to join you will hear, and will say, There was a plague among the people of Absalom.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: then even he that is valiant
2 Samuel.english_translation: And that hearer, even if he is a valiant man and his heart is as the heart of a lion, will utterly melt in fear and trembling, and will not attach himself further to you, for he will say, He has already begun to fall and is punished on account of his father, and will not succeed.
For this is my counsel.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and that thou go to battle in thine own person
2 Samuel.english_translation: At the head; (Targum:) “and you shall go at the head of all of us.”

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and we will light upon him
2 Samuel.english_translation: And we shall rest upon him, an expression of encamping, like (Exodus 10:14): “and rested in all the borders of Egypt”; (Isaiah 7:2): “Aram is encamped upon Ephraim.”
(Targum:) “camps” (*mashrayin*), like (1 Samuel 10:5): *chevel nevi'im* (“a band of prophets”); (Psalms 119:61): *chevlei resha'im* (“the bands of the wicked”).
We shall drag the wall of the city into the ravine.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: but in any wise pass over
2 Samuel.english_translation: The Jordan.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: lest the king be swallowed up
2 Samuel.english_translation: For I did not advise him for good, and he may do according to the words of Ahithophel.
2 Samuel.translator_note: The subject of the second clause is not clear in the Hebrew.

2 Samuel.english_translation: He will tell it to him in secret and in a swallowed (muffled) manner.
(Targum:) “at the spring of the fuller” (*ein katzra*) — launderers of woolen garments, who beat them there, who kick them with the foot.
A curtain.
Crushed wheat, like (Proverbs 27:22): *be-toch ha-rifot* (“in the midst of the groats”).
I do not know an interpretation of it in any lexicon (*machberet*), and its interpretation follows its context, like *shibbolet ha-nahar*.
2 Samuel.translator_note: The phrase במחברת כל is translated as “in any lexicon.”

2 Samuel.english_translation: He is Jesse, the father of David; our Rabbis said (Bava Batra 17a) that he died without sin, through the serpent’s doing (*be-itvo shel nachash*).
He is Hanun the son of Nahash.
Bedding.
They are utensils, like (2 Kings 12:14): *sippot kesef* (“silver cups”).

Kinds of parched grain; our Rabbis said (Avodah Zarah 38b): Barzillai brought David two kinds of *shetita*, one of wheat and one of lentils, in keeping with what is stated here; “meal and parched corn” is of grain; “and beans and lentils and parched pulse” — of kinds of legumes which they dry in the oven when they are moist, and they are always sweet, and they grind them and make from them a food that they call *shetita*.
(Targum:) “and cheeses of milk.”

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: they will not care for us
2 Samuel.english_translation: It will not be an important matter in their eyes to gain strength and boast, since you are not in the battle.
For now, while you are in your honour, you are as important as we.
As ten thousand men like us.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: that thou be ready to succour us out of the city
2 Samuel.english_translation: (Targum:) “And now it is better that you pray for us from the city, to aid.”

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Deal gently for my sake with the young man
2 Samuel.english_translation: If he meets you in the battle, have mercy on him.

And from where was there a forest for Ephraim across the Jordan to the east, where no portion was given except to the children of Gad and the children of Reuben and to Manasseh? But because Joshua stipulated that they might pasture in forests, and that forest was adjacent to Ephraim, except that the Jordan divides, and they pastured their animals there, it was called the forest of Ephraim.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and the forest devoured more people
2 Samuel.english_translation: Wild beasts that were in the forest; so Jonathan translated.
An expression of chance and happening.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and he was taken up between the heaven and the earth
2 Samuel.english_translation: Our Rabbis said (Sotah 10b): He drew his sword to cut his hair, and saw Gehinnom open beneath him.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Beware that none touch the young man
2 Samuel.english_translation: Whoever comes into his hand shall guard him.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: I may not tarry thus with thee
2 Samuel.english_translation: I will not make any further request of you, for I will go.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: for he said: ‘I have no son
2 Samuel.english_translation: Who would fill my place and be important like me.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: to keep my name in remembrance
2 Samuel.english_translation: I will set up for myself a stone pillar; and it was an important building.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: but thou shalt bear tidings another day
2 Samuel.english_translation: Another tiding, of salvation.
Because the king’s son has died, therefore this tiding is not good for you.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: seeing that thou wilt have no reward for the tidings
2 Samuel.english_translation: No gift of reward for tidings is to be found today.
That is, so what if I have no reward?
(Targum:) “and he preceded the Cushite.”
Murmuring and moving in the battle.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: When Joab sent the king’s servant, and me thy servant
2 Samuel.english_translation: Behold, this is a verse with transposed order: “when Joab sent the king’s servant and thy servant” — after Joab sent this king’s servant, [Ahimaaz] ran after him.
2 Samuel.translator_note: The final clause is terse; translated literally, with the speaker supplied from the verse.

2 Samuel.english_translation: He speaks of himself: “and I knew not what it was” afterward.
Turn to another side and stand here, and we shall hear what this one says.
Eight times; our Rabbis said (Sotah 10b): seven, for he brought him up from the seven chambers of Gehinnom, and one, for he brought him to the World to Come.
(Targum:) “he wrapped his *tzizfohi*,” in the manner of mourners.
2 Samuel.translator_note: The Aramaic word צזפוהי is as printed; I could not confirm it. Audit 4: the Aramaic quotation was checked against Targum Jonathan/the Ketuvim Targum (Mikraot Gedolot, Sefaria) at 2SA 19:5 and reads as quoted; the meaning of the unclear word, if noted above, is still unresolved.

2 Samuel.english_translation: Like (1 Kings 19:13): “and wrapped his face in his mantle”; (1 Samuel 21:10): “behold, it is here wrapped in a cloth.”
If you do not go out.
Those who had been with Absalom.
Disputing with one another.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: For the speech of all Israel was come to the king
2 Samuel.english_translation: All this is from the words of his message.
Who is [to be] captain of the host, you shall say: “Are you not my sister’s son?”
2 Samuel.translator_note: Rashi paraphrases the verse’s “my bone and my flesh.”

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: And they rushed into the Jordan
2 Samuel.english_translation: (Targum:) “they cleft it with their shields.”

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: And the ferryboat passed to and fro
2 Samuel.english_translation: The ferryboat in which they cross the breadth of the river.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: the first of all the house of Joseph
2 Samuel.english_translation: All Israel sinned against you, and I more than all of them, and behold, I have come to ask forgiveness; if you accept me, all Israel will be confident that you will accept them, and if not, they will be afraid to return to you again.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: shall there any man be put to death this day in Israel?
2 Samuel.english_translation: In astonishment: for today I am king! Until now I thought that such a great man would not have belittled me unless my kingship had been cut off by the Omnipresent, and He had said to him, Curse David; but now that he repents, I know that I am king.
It is an expression of grooming: the removal of the hair between the legs.
*Grenon* in Old French.
2 Samuel.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is גרנו״ן; Darmesteter (1909) reads *grenon*.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Wherefore wentest not thou with me
2 Samuel.english_translation: To go out from Jerusalem when I went out.
And I cannot go on my feet.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: to bring him on the way over the Jordan
2 Samuel.english_translation: To escort him.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: for he was a very great man
2 Samuel.english_translation: In wealth.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: How many are the days of the years of my life
2 Samuel.english_translation: That I have left to live.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: that I should go up with the king unto Jerusalem
2 Samuel.english_translation: Are they not few? And what benefit would I have in your sustaining me?

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: can I discern between good and bad?
2 Samuel.english_translation: Between good food and bad food; and our Rabbis of blessed memory said (Shabbat 152a): He was steeped in licentiousness; therefore old age leapt upon him.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Thy servant would but just go over the Jordan with the king
2 Samuel.english_translation: A small escort your servant will cross to escort you, after you cross the Jordan.
Which is not good for me.
He was his son.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Because the king is near of kin to us
2 Samuel.english_translation: He is of my tribe.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: or hath any gift been given us?
2 Samuel.english_translation: Like (Genesis 43:34) *masot* (“portions”) — a portion from the king’s house.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: We have ten parts in the king
2 Samuel.english_translation: For we are ten tribes.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and we have also more right in David than you
2 Samuel.english_translation: Even though he is closer to you, I am more drawn to him than you, for I am ten parts.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: why then did you despise us
2 Samuel.english_translation: That you should be first; was not my word the first to bring back my king? And before this our word came to him to bring him back, as it is written above (v. 12): “And the speech of all Israel was come to the king.”

An expression of (Zephaniah 2:1) *hitkoshshu* (“gather yourselves together”): the word of the man of Judah was seen and made equal, for he showed them the letter that David had sent them, “Why are you the last to bring the king back,” etc.; so it is explained in the aggadah. And one can explain *vayekesh* as an expression of hardness and strength, and so Jonathan translated: *u-takif* (“and it was strong”).
2 Samuel.translator_note: The words נראה והושוה (“was seen and made equal”) are translated literally.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Now there happened to be there
2 Samuel.english_translation: He happened to be present (*nizdamen*), an expression of (Zephaniah 1:7): “He hath consecrated His guests” (*keru'av*); (above 13:23): “And Absalom invited all the king’s sons” (*vayikra*), an expression of summoning.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Call me the men of Judah together
2 Samuel.english_translation: That they be here within three days.
At the end of the three days be careful to be standing here before me, for he wanted to pursue Sheba the son of Bichri.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: but he tarried longer than the set time
2 Samuel.english_translation: He found the Sages who had begun a tractate (*ashkechinhu le-rabbanan de-fatchu be-massekhta*), as it is stated in Sanhedrin (49a).
After Amasa, the captain of the host, delayed and did not bring the army of Judah, take you of those found around me, and pursue him.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and escape out of our sight
2 Samuel.english_translation: And deliver himself from our sight, and this is an elliptical verse.
Attached very close to his body across the breadth of his loins, not in the manner of those who gird a sword, so that it would be apt to fall, and he would not need to draw it from its sheath.
Toward Amasa.

The sword from its sheath, because it was smooth and polished, and was not hanging at the side of his thigh but across the breadth of his loins, and almost as he bent himself toward the ground, it fell out of its sheath, and he took hold of it in his right hand, and Amasa did not notice the matter.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: when he saw that every one that came by him stood still
2 Samuel.english_translation: When the man saw that everyone who came upon him stood still.
When he was drawn away, like (Proverbs 25:4): “Take away the dross from the silver”; and like (ibid. v. 5): “Take away the wicked from before the king.”

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: And he went through all the tribes of Israel
2 Samuel.english_translation: Sheba the son of Bichri, to persuade them to make him king over them.
I do not know what it is.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and it stood in the moat
2 Samuel.english_translation: (Targum:) “and they surrounded the camps.” And some explain *ve-ta'amod ba-chel* as an expression of (Lamentations 2:8) “*chel ve-chomah*” (“rampart and wall”): they felled the outer wall, and it was strengthened to stand by means of the inner.
2 Samuel.translator_note: The subject of “it was strengthened” is not clear in the Hebrew.

2 Samuel.english_translation: As it is said of you (below 23:8): *yoshev ba-shevet tachkemoni*.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: They were wont to speak in old time, saying
2 Samuel.english_translation: You should have spoken peace first; if they answer you with peace and open to you, you would have had no need to fight against them.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: They shall surely ask counsel at Abel
2 Samuel.english_translation: If your army’s men had asked after the peace of this city, whose name is Abel.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and so they ended the matter
2 Samuel.english_translation: Immediately the people of the city would have made peace with you.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: We are of them that are peaceable and faithful in Israel
2 Samuel.english_translation: I am of the people of the city, who are whole and faithful to Israel and to the king. And an aggadic midrash (Genesis Rabbah 94:9, and Yalkut Shimoni §21): She was Serach the daughter of Asher; I made whole one faithful to another faithful: through me the coffin of Joseph was revealed to Moses; I told Jacob that Joseph is alive.
2 Samuel.translator_note: The sentence “I made whole one faithful to another faithful” is translated literally; its sense is not certain.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Far be it, far be it from me
2 Samuel.english_translation: Far be it from me, far be it from the king.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: hath lifted up his hand against the king, even against David
2 Samuel.english_translation: Against a king, even if he is not David, he is liable to death; and against David, even if he is not king, he is liable to death; and all the more so against a king, David; so it is expounded in Midrash Ecclesiastes (9:18).

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Then the woman went unto all the people in her wisdom
2 Samuel.english_translation: We learned in the Tosefta (Terumot, end of chapter 7): She said to them: Since he is killed and they are killed, give him to them; if he could be saved — for example, that he is inside and you are outside, and you are in danger and he can escape — one does not push aside one life on account of another, to kill him for the sake of saving you; but now that he too will be killed along with you, since the walls have been breached and there is no strength to escape, better that he die alone and that you not die with him. Rabbi Simeon says: This is what she said to them: One who rebels against the kingship of the house of David is liable to death.
2 Samuel.translator_note: The Tosefta passage is terse and is translated as literally as the sense allows.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Now Joab was over all the host of Israel
2 Samuel.english_translation: Even though David said concerning Amasa (above 19:14): “for I will make you captain of the host in place of Joab,” now that Amasa had died, Joab did not move from his place, and through Joab it became necessary to appoint his colleagues.
2 Samuel.translator_note: The printed words of David differ from the wording of 2 Samuel 19:14; the last clause is translated literally.

2 Samuel.english_translation: Jonathan translated: “Ira the Jairite (*Ya'ira'ah*), who is of Tekoa.” And so he is called in this book (below 23:26): “Ira the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite.” And he is called *Yairi* because we learned in Menachot (85b): “Tekoa is first for oil,” for olive oil is found there, from which they light the lamps.
To him he would give all his priestly gifts; so our Rabbis said (Eruvin 63a); and the plain sense of the verse is that he made him a chief and a judge.
For the sin of Saul, who was buried suddenly in secret, for the men of Jabesh-gilead stole him and buried him, and he was not eulogized according to his honour.
Because he killed Nob, the city of the priests.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: because he put to death the Gibeonites
2 Samuel.english_translation: When he killed Nob, the city of the priests, he killed seven of them (the Gibeonites): two wood-choppers, two water-drawers, a sexton, a cantor and a scribe; so it is explained in the Jerusalem Gemara in Sanhedrin (17). And our Rabbis said: Because he killed the priests, who used to supply them with food, Scripture accounts it to him as though he had killed them. And do not be astonished, for the Holy One, blessed be He, demands His honour and demands for the offence, for so it is written (Zephaniah 2:3): “who have wrought His ordinance” — “in that His ordinance, there they wrought”; so we learned in Yevamot (78b).
2 Samuel.translator_note: The final quotation is translated as printed, and its relation to Zephaniah 2:3 is not clear to me.

2 Samuel.english_translation: Words of appeasement, that they would forgo their due (lit. “pass over their measures”) and forgive Saul and his house.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: now the Gibeonites were not of the children of Israel
2 Samuel.english_translation: That is, they themselves showed a trait of cruelty, [proving] that they are not from the seed of Abraham our father and are not fit to cleave to Israel; and therefore David decreed against them that they not enter the congregation; he said: There are three signs in this nation: merciful, bashful, and doers of kindness; one who has these three signs is fit to be cleaved to.
In the days of Joshua, when they appointed them wood-choppers and water-drawers for the altar (Joshua 9:15).

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: in his zeal for the children of Israel
2 Samuel.english_translation: When he set his heart to cleanse and to purify Israel and to do their needs, he sought to kill them, and this zeal is for good, like (Numbers 11:29): “Art thou jealous for my sake?”; and so (2 Kings 10:16) [of Jehu]: “in my zeal for the LORD”; this is its plain sense. But according to its midrash, he did not say [to kill] anyone but the priests, and this zeal stated here is not for good but for evil, for he knew that his kingship would not continue from the day that he did not keep the commandment of the Holy One, blessed be He, regarding Amalek, and from then he became jealous of them.
2 Samuel.translator_note: The sentence “he did not say [to kill] anyone but the priests” is translated literally.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: that you may bless the inheritance of the LORD
2 Samuel.english_translation: Pray for them.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: It is no matter of silver or gold between us and Saul
2 Samuel.english_translation: But only souls. He sought to appease them with money, and they did not want it; he said, Perhaps they are ashamed before one another; he went and appeased each one separately, and they were not appeased; therefore it is written, “There is no silver or gold to me,” etc., in the singular; this I saw in the Jerusalem Talmud (Sanhedrin 6:7).
2 Samuel.translator_note: The printed quotation reads אין לי (singular); the verse reads אין לנו (plural). It is translated as printed.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: neither is it for us to put any man to death in Israel
2 Samuel.english_translation: Among all the rest of the children of Israel, who did not sin against us.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and that devised against us, so that we have been destroyed
2 Samuel.english_translation: Who said in his heart that we should be destroyed by him from standing, etc., for he thought to destroy us.
He planned against us to destroy us.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and we will hang them up
2 Samuel.english_translation: Hanging.
To the Name of the Omnipresent, to make known His judgment.
A heavenly voice went forth and said: “chosen of the LORD” (Berakhot 12b).
He asked for mercy that the Ark not take him in, for he passed them before the Ark; whoever the Ark takes in is for death (Yevamot 79a).

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: the five sons of Michal the daughter of Saul, whom she bore to Adriel
2 Samuel.english_translation: Did Michal give birth? Was it not Merab who bore them to him? Rather, Merab bore them and Michal raised them; therefore they were called by her name, and one who raises an orphan boy or girl in his house, it is as if he had borne him, and he is called by his name (Sanhedrin 19b).

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: at the beginning of barley harvest
2 Samuel.english_translation: In the days of Nisan.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: until water was poured upon them from heaven
2 Samuel.english_translation: In the rainy season, in Tishrei, for they were not given for burial; but is it not written (Deuteronomy 21:23): “his body shall not remain all night upon the tree”? But they said: Better that one letter be uprooted from the Torah, and the Name of Heaven be sanctified in public; for those passing by and returning would say: What is the nature of these? They would be told: They are of the sons of kings, and what did they do? They stretched out their hand against proselytes, drawn-in ones (*gerim gerurim*). They would say: There is no nation fit to be cleaved to like this nation (Yevamot 79a).

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: And David went and took the bones of Saul
2 Samuel.english_translation: For it was said to him concerning them, “It is for Saul,” because he had not been eulogized properly.
The seven who were hanged.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and they performed all that the king commanded
2 Samuel.english_translation: To eulogize over them in all the cities of Israel.

It is like the case at the head of the handle of the lance, which is called *aristoil* in Old French, and it is made like a cap; and there is a parallel to it in Zevachim (88b; see Shitah Mekubbetzet there): “The pomegranates of the robe, to what are they similar? To *kulsot* on the heads of children” — *kulsot* is *heilmes* in Old French.
2 Samuel.translator_note: Old French glosses: the printed Hebrew spellings are ארישטויי״ל and היילמ״ש. Darmesteter (1909) reads *arestoil* (“poignée de lance,” the handle of a lance) and *hélmes*. The phrase “(see Shitah Mekubbetzet there)” is in the printed text.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: he being girded with new armour
2 Samuel.english_translation: A new girdle. And I have heard that on that day he was initiated into wearing weapons of war; and it is the way of those who are initiated to achieve victory and valour on the day of their initiation, to acquire a name; therefore “and he said to smite David.”

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: But Abishai the son of Zeruiah succoured him
2 Samuel.english_translation: That he helped him with prayer, as is stated in Chelek (Sanhedrin 95a).
This (war) had already preceded all of them, and it is not numbered here except to join together the death of the four sons of Orpah.
2 Samuel.translator_note: The sentence is terse and is translated literally.

2 Samuel.english_translation: David.
Because his family were weavers of the curtain for the Sanctuary, which is called “forest.”
(Targum:) *ke-aksan de-gardain* (“like the weavers’ beam”), which is called *ensouble* in Old French; let weaving come and stand opposite weaving.
2 Samuel.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is אינשובל״א; Darmesteter (1909, p. 51) reads *ensouble* (see 1 Samuel 17:7). The Aramaic word *aksan* is left untranslated. Audit 4: “weavers’ beam” rests on Darmesteter’s gloss of *ensouble*, which Rashi gives as the equivalent of the Aramaic; the Aramaic wording reads as quoted in Targum Jonathan at 2 Samuel 21:19.

2 Samuel.english_translation: As its Targum: *gavar de-meshachin*. For the root of the word is only *mem* and *dalet*, like (Psalms 65:8) *mi-sha'on* — *shin* and *alef* — (Genesis 17:4) and *mi-hamon* — *he* and *mem*. And in Chronicles (1 Chronicles 11:23) it is written: “a man of great stature” (*ish middah*), that is, very tall, for one measures how much is his measure.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: six fingers, and on every foot six toes
2 Samuel.english_translation: Our Rabbis explained in Bekhorot (45b) that it was necessary to say “twenty and four,” lest you say that the fingers of his two hands are only six and the toes of his feet only six; therefore it says “twenty and four”; and if it had written “twenty and four” and not said “six and six,” I would say seven on one and five on the other; and what [does] “in number” [teach]? That all of them were counted in the order of the fingers on the back of the hand.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: in the day that the LORD delivered him
2 Samuel.english_translation: At the time of his old age, after all his troubles had passed over him and he had been saved from them all.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and out of the hand of Saul
2 Samuel.english_translation: But was not Saul included? Rather, he was his enemy and his pursuer more than all of them. Similar to it (above 2:30): “nineteen men and Asahel”; similar to it (Joshua 2:1): “Go, view the land, and Jericho”; and similar to it (1 Kings 11:1): “And king Solomon loved many strange women, together with the daughter of Pharaoh.”

They are an expression of strength: “rock” according to its plain meaning; “fortress” is a forest stronghold (*metzudat ye'arim*), which is called *pleisein* in Old French; and on account of the miracle done for him at the Rock of Divisions (1 Samuel 23:8), and strongholds in the forest.
2 Samuel.translator_note: Printed as 1 Samuel 23:8; the “Rock of Divisions” is at 1 Samuel 23:28. Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is פליישאי״ן. Darmesteter (1909) glosses it “Mon asile” and records manuscript variants (פלישיץ, פליישיר, פלייטיד); the reading of the French word is not settled.

2 Samuel.english_translation: My refuge with the army of Israel in the battle, and at times He is a refuge for me when I am alone, such as from Ishbi in Nob (above 21:17).
An expression of “rock,” for a rock is a shelter for wayfarers from the rain and the winds; *abriemes* in Old French.
2 Samuel.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is אבריאמ״ש; Darmesteter (1909) reads *abriement*. The printed form is similar but not identical, so I give the printed form and his reading only.

2 Samuel.english_translation: An expression of covering, for I used to take cover in Him for help.
My supporter.
For I used to flee to Him for help.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Praised, I cry, is the LORD
2 Samuel.english_translation: As its Targum: “When I call to Him I will praise Him,” because I trust that I shall be saved from my enemies; and it is possible to interpret “I call and am saved” as an expression of the present.
They encircled me.
As its Targum: “like a woman who sits on the birthstool” — so it is the place of the stones where the woman gives birth.
Troops flooding like a stream.
As its Targum: *mashrit* (“camp”), like (1 Samuel 10:5): *chevel nevi'im* (“a band of prophets”).
They came before me.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: In my distress I called upon the LORD
2 Samuel.english_translation: So is the way of the language of the present: it speaks in the language of the past and the language of the future at one time.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Then the earth did shake and quake
2 Samuel.english_translation: It was not said about miracles that befell him, but about the miracles done for Israel; and the beginning of the verse is connected to its end.

*Ki* is used here in the sense of “when,” and so is its meaning: and when He was wroth because of those who provoke Him, the earth shook and quaked, and the foundations of the heavens trembled and shook.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Smoke arose up in His nostrils
2 Samuel.english_translation: So it is with an angry man: smoke goes out of his nostrils, and so (Psalms 18:9): “There went up a smoke out of His nostrils.” And this is the whole expression of burning anger, for the nose snorts and sends up vapour.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: And fire out of His mouth did devour
2 Samuel.english_translation: From the decree of the word of His mouth, fire consumes among the wicked.
To take vengeance on His enemies, from Egypt and from Pharaoh.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: And He made darkness pavilions round about Him
2 Samuel.english_translation: For a booth, as it is said (Exodus 14:20): “and there was the cloud and the darkness,” separating between Egypt and Israel.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Gathering of waters, thick clouds of the skies
2 Samuel.english_translation: From where was the darkness? There were thick clouds of the skies, which sift water upon the earth.

It is an expression of a sieve, for it falls upon the earth finely, finely (Taanit 9b); and so it says in many aggadot: they sift it through a sieve. And one can explain *chashrat* as an expression of “binding” (*kesher*), for the heavens are bound with clouds by means of the water, like *chashureihem* mentioned in the wheels of the stand (1 Kings 7:33), which are the arms of wood that tighten and bind its circles together.
Lest you say that He dwells in darkness; rather, the brightness is inside the partition, and from that brightness before Him, coals of fire burned, by which arrows were sent upon Egypt.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: The foundations of the world were laid bare
2 Samuel.english_translation: That the deep was split open; when the Red Sea was split, all the waters in the world were split (Yalkut Shimoni §161).

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: At the blast of the breath
2 Samuel.english_translation: From the force of the blowing of the wind of His nostrils.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: for they were too mighty for me
2 Samuel.english_translation: When they were too mighty.
When they went out after him into the wilderness and relied on his promise.
2 Samuel.translator_note: The pronoun “him” is not identified in the Hebrew.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: With the merciful Thou dost show Thyself merciful, With the upright man
2 Samuel.english_translation: Corresponding to the three Patriarchs, whose righteousness the Holy One, blessed be He, repaid to their children.
Pharaoh.

An expression of “twisted and crooked,” and in the book of Psalms (18:27) it is written: *titpatal*. Another explanation: “He sent from on high, He took me” — he said it of himself, when he was hurrying to go away from Saul at the Rock of Divisions and was near to being caught, and an angel came to Saul, saying: “Make haste and come, for the Philistines have raided”; “And He returned,” etc., “according to my righteousness” — that I did not kill him when I cut off the skirt of his robe.
2 Samuel.translator_note: This “another explanation” appears to comment on verses earlier than the lemma (22:17 and 22:21); it is translated as printed.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: The word of the LORD is tried
2 Samuel.english_translation: Clear; He promises and does.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: And who letteth my way go forth straight
2 Samuel.english_translation: From every stumbling block, and from every sin, and from every danger, until it was complete and well trodden.
2 Samuel.translator_note: The word כבוש is translated as “well trodden”; the sense is not certain.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: So that mine arms do bend a bow of brass
2 Samuel.english_translation: And a bow of brass was bent on my arm, for I have strength to bend it. Bows were hung up for David in his house, and the kings of the nations used to come and see them, and say to one another: Do you think he is able to bend them? This is only to frighten us; and David, hearing, would take them and break them before them. And the bending of a bow is an expression of *chit*, and so in Psalms: *chitzekha nichatu vi*.
2 Samuel.translator_note: The Aramaic word *chit* is left untranslated.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: And Thy condescension hath made me great
2 Samuel.english_translation: You made great for me the quality of Your humility.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Thou hast enlarged my steps under me
2 Samuel.english_translation: When a person joins his feet one to the other, he is apt to fall; and so it says (Proverbs 4:12): “When thou goest, thy step shall not be straitened.”
My heels.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: They looked, but there was none to save
2 Samuel.english_translation: Behold, this is a verse with transposed order: “They looked unto the LORD, but He answered them not,” and “there was none to save”; like (Isaiah 17:7): “shall a man regard his Maker,” like “shall turn.” And Menachem connected it with (Genesis 4:4): “And the LORD had respect unto Abel,” and interpreted it as an expression of entreaty, and the language applies both to the one who entreats and to the one entreated, like (ibid. 25:21): “And Isaac entreated the LORD … and the LORD was entreated of him”; so here too “they looked, but there was none to save” applies to the one who prays, and “and the LORD had respect” applies to the language, to the one before whom they pray.
2 Samuel.translator_note: Rashi’s last sentences are terse and are translated literally.

2 Samuel.english_translation: I will trample them, and there are many in the book of Ezekiel: (6:11) *u-reka be-raglekha*; (25:6) *u-rak'akha ba-regel*.
2 Samuel.translator_note: The printed second quotation is not word for word the verse in Ezekiel 25:6; I give the Hebrew in transliteration.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: from the contentions of my people
2 Samuel.english_translation: From Doeg, from Ahithophel, and Saul, and the Ziphites.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Thou hast kept me to be the head of the nations
2 Samuel.english_translation: You have kept me for this. And an aggadic midrash: David said: Master of the world, save me from the judgment of Israel, for if I pervert it, or subjugate Israel in his service, I will be punished; rather, set me over the Philistines, and they will serve me, and on account of them I will not be punished.
2 Samuel.translator_note: The Hebrew (אם אטהו או ארדה את ישראל בעבודתו) is terse and is translated literally.

2 Samuel.english_translation: From fear, they will tell me lies.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: As soon as they hear of me, they obey me
2 Samuel.english_translation: Even in my absence they fear me, at the hearing of their ears, to submit to my authority.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: The sons of the stranger fade away
2 Samuel.english_translation: They will grow weary, an expression of (Jeremiah 8:13) “and the leaf is faded” (*ve-aleh navel*) — *flesteront* in Old French.
2 Samuel.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is פלישטירונ״ט; Darmesteter (1909) reads *flestre*. The printed form is not identical to his reading, so I give the printed form and his reading only.

2 Samuel.english_translation: An expression of lame ones.
From the hardness of the sufferings of the prison with which I make them suffer.
He who does these for me.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Now these are the last words of David
2 Samuel.english_translation: The prophecy of David, the last [words]; and who are the first? The words of the song stated above; but in all the songs and praises that he said, they are not called “words.”
Raised up above.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: And the sweet singer of Israel
2 Samuel.english_translation: Israel sing in the Temple only his songs and his psalms.

He caused His holy spirit to rest upon me, and spoke in me; and every expression of prophecy takes the expression “speaking,” like (Numbers 12:2): “Hath the LORD indeed spoken only with Moses? hath He not spoken also with us?”; (ibid. v. 6): “I do speak with him”; and the reason for the matter is that the spirit enters into the prophet and speaks in him.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: The Rock of Israel spoke to me
2 Samuel.english_translation: To me spoke and commanded the Rock of Israel that I be a ruler over man, over Israel, who are called “man,” as it is said (Ezekiel 34:31): “ye are men” (Yevamot 61a); and that I be a righteous ruler, fearing God. And our Rabbis (Moed Katan 16b) explained it in another way: David said: The God of Israel spoke to me, the Rock of Israel spoke to me: I rule over man; and who rules over me? A righteous one, for I decree a decree and he annuls it. But according to the settling of the verses, the first is the plain sense of the verse.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: And as the light of the morning, when the sun riseth
2 Samuel.english_translation: And He assured me that my greatness would go on increasing, like the light of brightness that goes and grows brighter.
A light that is not dark.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: When through clear shining after rain, The tender grass springeth out of the earth
2 Samuel.english_translation: My morning shines more than the brightness that comes from rain, like “clear heat upon light” (Isaiah 18:4), when rain falls on the earth full of grass, and the sun shines upon it and makes it gleam; and so its meaning: more than the brightness that comes from rain, of grass from the earth.
2 Samuel.translator_note:
The last clause is terse and is translated literally.
Isaiah 18:4: JPS renders “like clear heat in sunshine”; Rashi’s quoted words are translated literally.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: For is not my house established with God?
2 Samuel.english_translation: That my morning would be dense (clouded).
2 Samuel.translator_note: Rashi’s comment is clipped; translated literally.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: For an everlasting covenant He hath made with me
2 Samuel.english_translation: The Torah that He set for me, arranged in all my house and preserved.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: For all my salvation, and all my desire
2 Samuel.english_translation: My needs are prepared before Him, and this is an elliptical verse.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Will he not make it to grow?
2 Samuel.english_translation: Still, to a king after my kingship. Another explanation: For He set an everlasting covenant for my house, that my kingship be established, and the covenant is arranged in all, in the mouth of all the prophets.
2 Samuel.translator_note: The first sentence is clipped; translated literally.

2 Samuel.english_translation: *Chardon* in Old French, which in its smallness is soft, moving and shaking, and in the end becomes hard, until it cannot be taken by hand.
2 Samuel.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is קרדו״ן; Darmesteter (1909) reads *chardon*.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: But the man that toucheth them Must be armed with iron
2 Samuel.english_translation: He must clothe his flesh with iron, and fill his hand with weapons in order to cut them down.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: And they shall be utterly burned with fire in their place
2 Samuel.english_translation: And there is no remedy there except burning, and sitting and warming oneself opposite them; so the wicked have no remedy except burning in Gehinnom.
The Holy One, blessed be He, sitting on the throne of judgment.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: whom David had: Josheb-basshebeth a Tahchemonite
2 Samuel.english_translation: “Sitting in the seat” — sitting in the seat of the Sanhedrin; and he is the *Tachkemoni* (“the wise one”); and he is “head of the three” — a father built up in wisdom and in valour; in these three things he is chief, as it is said (1 Samuel 16:18): “prudent in affairs, and a comely person, and a mighty man of valour.”
2 Samuel.translator_note: The three adjectives are quoted in the order Rashi prints them; JPS has them in the verse’s order, “a mighty man of valour, and a man of war, and prudent in affairs, and a comely person.”

2 Samuel.english_translation: When he engages in Torah, he curls and ties himself up like a worm, like (Job 38:31) *ma'adannot Kimah* (“the chains of the Pleiades”); and when he went out to war he was hard as a tree, and killed eight hundred slain in one battle (Moed Katan 16b).
Thus is his name.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: one of the three mighty men
2 Samuel.english_translation: The most excellent of the mighty men.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: when they jeoparded their lives against the Philistines
2 Samuel.english_translation: They struck hands [in pledge] to fight them and to conquer them.
Jonathan translated: *le-chaletza ketilaya*; there was no one to help him kill, but all of them were stripping the slain after him.
From the mountain.
As a troop, like the beasts of the field.
Jonathan translated: *mi-gavri reishei mashrita* (“of the men, chiefs of the camp”).

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and the garrison of the Philistines was then in Beth-lehem
2 Samuel.english_translation: The army was encamped in the valley of Rephaim, and they sent their garrison to Beth-lehem.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: Oh that one would give me water to drink
2 Samuel.english_translation: Our Rabbis said (Bava Kamma 60b): He needed to ask a question of the Sanhedrin sitting at the gate of Beth-lehem.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: but poured it out unto the LORD
2 Samuel.english_translation: Thus he said: I have a tradition from the court of Samuel of Ramah: Whoever surrenders himself to death for the words of Torah, one does not say a teaching from his mouth; and what is “and poured it out unto the LORD”? That he said them in the name of the Gemara (ibid. 61a).
2 Samuel.translator_note: Rashi’s explanation is terse and is translated literally.

2 Samuel.english_translation: An expression of astonishment.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: howbeit he attained not unto the first three
2 Samuel.english_translation: (Targum:) “and to the three men he did not reach.”

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: he smote the two altar-hearths of Moab
2 Samuel.english_translation: (Targum:) “the two chiefs of Moab.” And our Rabbis said (Berakhot 18b): that he left none like him, neither in the first Temple nor in the second Temple.
Because Solomon built it, who came from Ruth the Moabitess.
Every “thirty” in this section, Jonathan translated: *gavraya* (“the men”).

And they are not enumerated here; and I say: Joab did not need to be mentioned, for he is captain of the host; and as for the rest who are lacking, perhaps the sons of (Jesse) [read: Jashen] were three or four.
2 Samuel.translator_note: The bracketed correction “read: Jashen” (צ״ל ישן) is in the printed text.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: And again the anger of the LORD was kindled against Israel
2 Samuel.english_translation: I do not know on account of what.
He incited.

*Kahem* is double, and *kahem* is two doubles — behold, four doubles; and so he repeats and doubles the doubling, up to a hundred times; so Joab’s blessing turns out to exceed that of Moses, who said (Deuteronomy 1:11): “make you a thousand times so many more as you are”; and further, Moses’s blessing was for a long time, and Joab’s was immediate, for it says there: “and may the eyes of my lord the king see it.”
2 Samuel.translator_note: The arithmetic of the doublings is translated as written.

2 Samuel.english_translation: He began with the children of Gad, because they are mighty and hard; he said: Would that they fight against me, and obstruct it through me.
2 Samuel.translator_note: The last clause (ויעכבו על ידי) is translated literally.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: and to the land of Tahtim-hodshi
2 Samuel.english_translation: A place of new settlement, whose population is small; perhaps in the meantime David will regret, and send him a messenger to retract.
Among the children of Dan.
The name of the place.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: the sum of the numbering of the people
2 Samuel.english_translation: If “number,” why “muster” (*mifkad*)? He made two *anpiyarot*, a large and a small; he said: I will show him the small, and if he is angry, I will show him the large; therefore it says *mifkad*, an expression of lack; so it is expounded in the Pesikta.
2 Samuel.translator_note: The word *anpiyarot* is left untranslated.

2 Samuel.english_translation: Their strength grew weak, like a female.

And in Chronicles (1 Chronicles 21:5) it says: “a thousand thousand and a hundred thousand.” In the aggadah of the Amoraim (Yalkut Shimoni on the Prophets and Writings, §165:16) we find: Rabbi Joshua ben Levi said: The Writings add here what is lacking here; these are the two tribes that were not counted, for so it is written in Chronicles (ibid. v. 6): “But Levi and Benjamin counted he not among them; for the king’s word was abominable to Joab.” Joab said: In these I can slip away and say, The tribe of Levi is not counted in the number of the other tribes but from a month old and upward, and as for Benjamin, it is enough that it was diminished and destroyed through the concubine at Gibeah. And in the thirty-two measures of Rabbi Eliezer the son of Rabbi Jose the Galilean we learned: One verse says: “And all Israel were a thousand thousand and a hundred thousand, and Judah four hundred and seventy thousand,” and another verse says: “and Israel were eight hundred thousand, and the men of Judah five hundred thousand”; there are found between them three hundred thousand; these three hundred thousand, what are they? The third verse came and decided (ibid. 27:1): “Now the children of Israel after their number, the heads of fathers’ houses and the captains of thousands and of hundreds, and their officers that served the king in any matter of the courses, that came in and went out month by month throughout all the months of the year, of every course were twenty and four thousand” — this teaches that these three hundred thousand were written in the king’s register, and did not need to be counted. How? Twenty-four thousand for twelve — behold here two hundred and eighty-eight thousand; there remain twelve thousand — these are the princes of Israel.
2 Samuel.translator_note: The Yalkut reference in parentheses, with the section number, is in the printed text.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: I lay upon thee three things
2 Samuel.english_translation: One of three, and so (1 Samuel 18:21): “Thou shalt this day be my son-in-law through the one of the twain” — through one of two. “Three things I lay upon thee,” corresponding to the three that you laid upon Saul (ibid. 26:10): “surely the LORD will smite him; or his day shall come to die; or he shall go down into battle and perish.”

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: I am in a great strait
2 Samuel.english_translation: The smallest of them is very hard.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: let us fall now into the hand of the LORD
2 Samuel.english_translation: The pestilence, and not the sword and famine, for even this (famine) is given into the hands of the rich, the hoarders of produce. Rabbi Alexandri said: David said, If I choose the sword for myself now, Israel will say: He relies on his mighty men, that he will not die and the others will die; and if I choose famine, they will say: He relies on his wealth; I will choose for myself a thing in which all are equal (see Yalkut Shimoni §165).

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: from the morning even to the time appointed
2 Samuel.english_translation: (Targum:) “from the time when the daily offering is slaughtered until it is offered up.”
He was the chief of the fortress of Zion, whose name was Jebusi.
He was hiding from the angel; so it is written in Chronicles (1 Chronicles 21:20).
A wooden implement full of notches, and it is heavy, and they pass it over straw constantly, and it cuts it up to be chaff for the food of animals.

2 Samuel.english_lemma_JPS: All this did Araunah the king
2 Samuel.english_translation: He was a prince of the Jebusites.

And in Chronicles (ibid. v. 25) it says: “six hundred shekels of gold by weight.” How is that? He collected fifty shekels of silver from each and every tribe — behold, six hundred — and gave him silver at the value of the gold; and so we learned at the end of the slaughter of consecrated things (Zevachim 116b): he collected silver at six hundred, silver in gold shekels. And so we learned in the Sifre. Here ends the book of Samuel.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: but he could get no heat
1 Kings.english_translation: Our Rabbis said (Berakhot 62b): “Whoever treats garments with contempt does not in the end benefit from them,” because he tore the skirt of Saul’s robe. And an aggadic midrash: Rabbi Samuel the son of Nachmani said: When David saw the angel standing in Jerusalem with his sword in his hand, his blood grew cold from fear of him (see Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer, chapter 43).
Her virginity warms her flesh.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and be a companion unto him
1 Kings.english_translation: Warming, and so (Ecclesiastes 10:9): *u-vokea etzim yiskan bam*.
1 Kings.translator_note: Rashi reads *yiskan* here as “be warmed”; the JPS renders Ecclesiastes 10:9 differently. I give the Hebrew in transliteration.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: but the king knew her not
1 Kings.english_translation: For a virgin is better for warming than one who has been known. And our Rabbis said (Sanhedrin 22a): because of “neither shall he multiply wives to himself” (Deuteronomy 17:17), and he already had eighteen (Rashi there).
Glorifying himself.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and fifty men to run before him
1 Kings.english_translation: With spleens removed and soles of their feet engraved (ibid. 21b).
He did not anger him; it teaches you that one who withholds reproof from his son brings him to death.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and he was also a very goodly man
1 Kings.english_translation: Like Absalom, as it is said (2 Samuel 14:25): “and like Absalom there was no handsome man”; it was this that caused them to become arrogant.
1 Kings.translator_note: The printed wording paraphrases 2 Samuel 14:25.

1 Kings.english_translation: His mother.
That is, he was raised in the manner of the upbringing with which Absalom’s mother raised [Absalom].

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And he conferred with Joab the son of Zeruiah
1 Kings.english_translation: Because he knew that David had it in his heart against him for killing Abner and Amasa and Absalom, and that in the end he would command his son who would reign in his place concerning him; therefore he wanted this one to reign through him, and that he would love him.

Who was removed from the priesthood from when David fled from Jerusalem because of Absalom, because he inquired by the Urim and Thummim and it did not come up for him, as it is said (2 Samuel 15:24): “and Abiathar went up”; and he was of the descendants of Eli, and he knew that he would not serve in the days of Solomon, for it was said to Eli (1 Samuel 2:35): “And I will raise Me up a faithful priest … and he shall walk before Mine anointed”; and he wanted this one to stand through him.
Who prophesied to David that Solomon would reign, as it is said in Chronicles (1 Chronicles 22:9): “and his name shall be Solomon.”
A fattened ox.

A large stone, on which the young men would test their strength, to move it and drag it; an expression of flowing waters; (Deuteronomy 32:24) “crawling things of the dust.” And Jonathan translated: *even sakhuta* (“the stone of the lookout”), on which they stand and look far.
Jonathan translated: *ein katzra* (“the spring of the fuller”); he is a launderer, who prepares woolen garments with his feet, by kicking.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: Solomon his brother, he called not
1 Kings.english_translation: For he knew that the prophet had prophesied concerning him that he would reign.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: that thou mayest save thine own life
1 Kings.english_translation: From the dispute after the king’s death, when your son will want to reign, as the Holy One, blessed be He, promised him.
Lacking and prevented from greatness, like (Judges 20:16): “every one could sling stones at a hair-breadth, and not miss.”
In astonishment.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: For he is gone down this day
1 Kings.english_translation: For the city was high, and the Stone of Zoheleth was below in the ravine.
It is a sign to him that he will reign, and the beginning of greatness, for no commoner rides the king’s horse.
1 Kings.translator_note: Rashi’s printed wording says “horse”; the verse says “mule.”

1 Kings.english_translation: It is the spring of Siloam; from here [we learn] that kings are anointed only at a spring, a sign that his kingship will continue.
He places oil on him between the lashes of his eyes, in the form of a crown, like this.
1 Kings.translator_note: The printed text refers to a drawing (“like this”) that is not reproduced.

1 Kings.english_translation: May Solomon live.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and make his throne greater than the throne of my lord king David
1 Kings.english_translation: From here [we learn] that a person is not jealous of his son.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and the Cherethites and the Pelethites
1 Kings.english_translation: Jonathan translated: “and the archers and the slingers.” And our Rabbis said (Berakhot 4a): the Urim and Thummim.
From the anointing oil that Moses made.
For the Ark was placed in the City of David, and a flask of anointing oil before the Ark (as we learn in tractate Yoma 52b).
*Plaouti* in Old French.
1 Kings.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is פלאוט״י; Darmesteter (1909) lists *chalemèls* for this verse word, and the printed form is not matched to it, so I give the printed form only.

1 Kings.english_translation: The prophets spoke in the language of exaggeration (*havai*), like the language of men.
That is, now my tidings are not good for you.
Which was in Gibeon; he said: Those executed by the court are buried in the graves of the court; let me die here, and be buried in the graves of my fathers (so Rabbi Tanchuma expounded, Massei 12).

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: what Joab the son of Zeruiah did unto me
1 Kings.english_translation: That he showed the letter that David sent by the hand of Uriah (in Midrash Rabbi Tanchuma, ibid.).

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and shed the blood of war in peace
1 Kings.english_translation: For they had peace with him, and were not on guard against him.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and put the blood of war upon his girdle that was about his loins
1 Kings.english_translation: That he girded his sword attached to his loins, not in the manner of those who gird, when going out to meet Amasa, and its mouth downward so that it would fall, as it is said (2 Samuel 20:8): “and as he went forth it fell out”; and when it fell and he took it up, Amasa supposed that he took it only to lift it from the ground, and did not guard himself from the sword that was in Joab’s hand.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and in his shoes that were on his feet
1 Kings.english_translation: Abner he killed by cunning, for he asked him how a one-handed woman performs *chalitzah*, as it is said (ibid. 3:27): “And Joab took him aside into the midst of the gate to speak with him *be-shali*,” an expression of *shal na'alkha* (“take off thy shoe”).

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and let not his hoar head go down to the grave in peace
1 Kings.english_translation: Do not allow him to die his own death and fall into Gehinnom.
Explicit, like (Job 16:3) “what provoketh thee” (*mah yamritzekha*), (ibid. 6:25) “and how *nimretzu*” — like “how *nimletzu*.”
1 Kings.translator_note: The meaning given for מפורשת is “explicit.”

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: for thou art a wise man
1 Kings.english_translation: Set your heart to find a capital offence in him on account of another matter, and this is “and thou wilt know what thou oughtest to do unto him.”

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and his kingdom was established firmly
1 Kings.english_translation: Even over those above.
To speak on his behalf, on behalf of Adonijah.
Our Rabbis said (Bava Batra 91b): To the mother of the monarchy — she is Ruth.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: ask for him the kingdom also
1 Kings.english_translation: When he makes use of the king’s sceptre, that is the beginning of authority.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and who hath made me a house
1 Kings.english_translation: A house of kingship, as He spoke by the hand of Nathan.
He was from there.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: for thou art deserving of death
1 Kings.english_translation: For you rebelled against my father’s kingship when you were with Adonijah, to make him king without his knowledge.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: because thou didst bear the ark
1 Kings.english_translation: When my father fled from Absalom.
With him in that distress, as it is said (2 Samuel 17:29): “The people is hungry, and faint, and thirsty, in the wilderness.”

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: which He spoke concerning the house of Eli
1 Kings.english_translation: (1 Samuel 2:35) “And I will raise Me up a faithful priest,” etc.; (ibid. v. 32): *ve-hibbatta tzar ma'on*, etc.; and when Shiloh was destroyed, there was no important house for the service of the Holy One, blessed be He, and now when the House of Choice was to be built, the Holy One, blessed be He, fulfilled His word to expel the sons of Eli.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And the tidings came to Joab
1 Kings.english_translation: The tidings of David’s command that he be killed, and he knew that Solomon hated him.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: for Joab had turned after Adonijah, though he turned not after Absalom
1 Kings.english_translation: In the end — but he wished to turn [toward Absalom], but was afraid, because David’s vitality (lit. “moisture”) still persisted.

Two [things] I will not accept upon myself: the curses that David your father cursed me with at the death of Abner (2 Samuel 3:29): “let it fall upon the head of Joab” — let Solomon take them upon himself, and afterward I will go out.
1 Kings.translator_note: The first sentence is terse and is translated literally.

1 Kings.english_translation: I accept them upon myself; therefore all these clung to the seed of David: Uzziah was a leper, Asa held to a spindle, Jehoiakim fell by the sword, and Zedekiah lacked bread.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: in his own house in the wilderness
1 Kings.english_translation: For his house was ownerless like the wilderness, open to the poor.
So that he would be available to him, and to find a capital sin for him.
An expression of warning.
With which I made you swear by the LORD.
That is, [Solomon] was not punished for all these.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And Solomon became allied to Pharaoh king of Egypt by marriage
1 Kings.english_translation: And all the time that Shimei his teacher was alive, he did not become allied by marriage with him; from here they said (Berakhot 8a): A person should always dwell in the place of his teacher.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: until he had made an end of building
1 Kings.english_translation: And afterward he built her a house.
For the sake of Heaven; anyone who wished would build an altar on the top of his roof, or in his courtyard.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: walking in the statutes of David his father
1 Kings.english_translation: Four years, until he began to build the House; but when he began to build, “And Solomon became allied to Pharaoh by marriage” — you find yourself saying (Jeremiah 32:31): “For this city hath been to Me a provocation of Mine anger and of My fury from the day that they built it even unto this day”; so we learned in Seder Olam; we learn that the sections are not written in order.
Scripture spoke to his disparagement, that he delayed the building of the House for four years.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: that was the great high place
1 Kings.english_translation: It is the copper altar that Moses made in the wilderness, and it was established in Shiloh; Shiloh was destroyed in the days of Eli and it came to Nob; Nob was destroyed in the days of Saul, and they came to Gibeon.
Like *ma'aleh* (“offers up”) Solomon.
In one day.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and Thou hast kept for him
1 Kings.english_translation: An expression of confirming his words, like (Deuteronomy 7:12): “and the LORD thy God shall keep with thee,” etc.; so here too “and Thou hast kept for him” the kindness — You confirmed Your word to fulfil for him the kindness that You promised by the hand of Nathan the prophet.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: I am but a little child
1 Kings.english_translation: He was twelve years old, and this is the reckoning: “and he called his name Jedidiah” (2 Samuel 12:25); in this same period Amnon afflicted Tamar, as it is said (ibid. 13:2): “And it came to pass after this that Absalom had a fair sister”; “after two full years … sheep-shearers for Absalom” (ibid. v. 23), and he killed Amnon, and Absalom fled and went to Geshur, “and was there three years” (ibid. v. 38) — behold, five years; and Absalom returned to Jerusalem, “and dwelt in Jerusalem two years” (ibid. 14:28) — behold, seven for Solomon; and he rebelled against his father and was killed; after this (ibid. 21:1): “And there was a famine in the days of David three years” — behold, ten; in the eleventh he numbered Israel, “and when they had gone to and fro through all the land … nine months” (ibid. 24:8); in the year of his death he established the courses, as it is said (1 Chronicles 26:31): “In the fortieth year of the reign of David they were sought for” — behold, twelve for King Solomon.
1 Kings.translator_note: The printed reference for “And it came to pass after this that Absalom had a fair sister” is 2 Samuel 13:2; the words are in 13:1.

1 Kings.english_translation: Because they are many, they have many affairs and come to judgment, and I have no leisure to examine their cases. Another explanation: “for who is able to judge this Thy great (lit. heavy) people” — their judgment is very heavy: if a case of two gentiles comes before me and I take from this one and give to that one not according to law, I am not punished; but for Israel I am punished with a capital punishment on account of it, as it is said (Proverbs 22:23): “and despoil of life those that despoil them.”

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And if thou wilt walk in My ways … then I will lengthen thy days
1 Kings.english_translation: The wealth and honour that I did not stipulate in My Torah to give to a king, I will give you, whether righteous or guilty; but length of days and the kingship of the generations I already stipulated in My Torah (Deuteronomy 17:20): “that he turn not aside from the commandment … to the end that he may prolong his days in his kingdom,” etc.; and that condition I will not change; and “if thou wilt walk in My ways … then I will lengthen,” etc.; and likewise for the kingship of his descendants after him, He said to him (below 9:4–5): “And as for thee, if thou wilt walk before Me,” etc., “there shall not fail thee a man,” etc.; so it is taught in the Sifre. And Rabbi Hanina ben Gamliel says: Behold, it says: “both riches and honour,” etc.
1 Kings.translator_note: The last sentence (Rabbi Hanina ben Gamliel) is terse and is translated literally.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And Solomon awoke, and, behold, it was a dream
1 Kings.english_translation: And behold, he understood that his dream was true: he hears a bird chirping and understands its language, a dog barking and understands its language (Song of Songs Rabbah 1:1).
A feast of rejoicing of heart, for he understood that his dream was true.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: but when I had looked well at it
1 Kings.english_translation: I set my mind to look at him.
A heavenly voice appeared and said: “She is his mother” (Makkot 23b).

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And king Solomon was king over all Israel
1 Kings.english_translation: Once they saw his wisdom, all rejoiced in his kingship.
To write the chronicles.
Which case came before him first, that he decide it first; so I have heard.
There were twelve prefects, to sustain the king and his household.
Which he levied upon Israel, as it is said (below 5:27): “And king Solomon raised a levy.”

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: who provided victuals for the king
1 Kings.english_translation: All his meal, and the food of the horses, and all the needs of expense.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: in all the region of Dor
1 Kings.english_translation: (Targum:) “the districts of Dor.”
He was appointed over them to collect the king’s tax, for it is the king’s due to collect his expenses from the people, as it is said in the law of the king in the book of Samuel (1 Samuel 10:25).

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and one officer that was [over all the officers] in the land
1 Kings.english_translation: Rav and Shmuel disagree: one says: One was appointed over all of them, he is Azariah the son of Nathan mentioned above; and one says: corresponding to the intercalated month (Sanhedrin 12a).
Fattened in the stall.
From the meadow.
Some of our Rabbis say: fattened chickens (Bava Metzia 86b).

And in Chronicles (2 Chronicles 9:25) it says: “four thousand”; our Rabbis explained (Sanhedrin 21b): There were forty thousand stalls, and in each one four thousand *itztevlaot*; or four thousand stalls, and in each one forty thousand *itztevlaot*.
1 Kings.translator_note: The Hebrew word אצטבלאות is left in transliteration; the figures are as printed.

1 Kings.english_translation: Even [food] of the summer months in the rainy season.
These prefects used to bring them to the place where the king would be.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: excelled the wisdom of all the children of the east
1 Kings.english_translation: What is the wisdom of the children of the east? They know the constellations (*mazalot*), etc., as it is stated in the Pesikta of the Red Heifer, and this whole section is expounded there according to its sense.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: For he was wiser than all men
1 Kings.english_translation: According to its plain meaning.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Heman, and Calcol, and Darda
1 Kings.english_translation: They were brothers, sons of Zerah the son of Judah, as it is said (1 Chronicles 2:6): “And the sons of Zerah: Zimri, and Ethan” (they were Levite singers).

They knew how to compose psalms stated with the dances (*mecholot*) of song, for the Levites used to say on their platform psalms that were composed in the book of Psalms (psalms 88–89): “Maskil of Ethan the Ezrahite”; and “Maskil of Heman the Ezrahite.” An aggadic midrash in the Pesikta: “than all men” — this is Adam the first; “Ethan the Ezrahite” — this is Abraham; “Heman” — this is Moses; “Calcol” — this is Joseph; “Darda” — this is the generation of the wilderness; “Mahol” — because it was forgiven (*nimchal*) them for the deed of the calf.
1 Kings.translator_note: In the Psalms, Psalm 88 is for Heman and Psalm 89 for Ethan; the printed text lists them in the reverse order.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And he spoke three thousand proverbs
1 Kings.english_translation: Three “learnings” of proverbs: “The proverbs of Solomon” is written three times in the book of Proverbs.
These three [of Proverbs], and the Song of Songs, and Ecclesiastes.
In each one there is enough to learn. And an aggadic midrash (Eruvin 21b): that he used to say, on each verse, three thousand proverbs, and on each proverb, a thousand and five reasons.

What is the remedy of each one, and that such-and-such a tree is good for such-and-such a building, and for planting in such-and-such a soil; and likewise concerning animals, what is its remedy, and the main point of its growth and its food. And an aggadic midrash (Yalkut Shimoni §178): What did he see for the leper to be purified with the highest of the high and the lowest of the low? And concerning animal and bird, what did he see that this one is fit with one sign in slaughter and that one with two signs; and fish and locusts without anything.

He was not permitted, because of the war, and Scripture says (Deuteronomy 12:10): “and He giveth you rest from all your enemies round about,” and afterward (v. 11): “Then it shall come to pass that the place,” etc.; “unto His habitation shall ye seek” (v. 5).
They were neighbours of the forest on one side, and in Hiram’s dominion.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: I will make them into rafts
1 Kings.english_translation: He calls them *raftsodot* in Chronicles (2 Chronicles 2:15), and in the German language *plitsin*, and in Old French *rits*; they bind the trees one with another, and float them on the surface of the water, and lead them as ships are led.
1 Kings.translator_note: Old French and German glosses: the printed Hebrew spellings are פליצי״ן (German) and רי״ץ (Old French). Darmesteter (1909) reads the German as *vlos* and the French as *réç*.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: unto the place that thou shalt appoint me
1 Kings.english_translation: That you will inform me, to bring them there.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and will cause them to be broken up there
1 Kings.english_translation: When he unties their bundle and brings them out to the dry land, each tree by itself, it is called *nippuz* (every whole thing which they divide into parts is called *nippuz*); *depecer* in Old French.
1 Kings.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is דיפצי״ר; Darmesteter (1909) reads *dépecer*.

1 Kings.english_translation: An expression of food.
Clean oil, for the olives are not ground in mills, but he crushes them in a mortar, and it does not bring up as much sediment as the ground.
Amounting to the pay of thirty thousand men.

As he concludes and says: “a month they were in Lebanon”: when ten thousand men were in Lebanon in Tishrei, and the twenty thousand men at home, in Marcheshvan the second ten thousand exchange and go out to Lebanon, and these return to their homes; and in Kislev the third ten thousand go out to Lebanon, and these return to their homes; and in Tevet the first go out and return to Lebanon, and so it goes round again; so it turns out that each ten thousand of them: a month in Lebanon, and two months at home.
To collect it.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: threescore and ten thousand that bore burdens
1 Kings.english_translation: To bring the stones from the mountain to the city, and eighty thousand who hewed them in the mountain, behold, a hundred and fifty thousand, and all of them were proselytes, drawn in (*gerim gerurim*), who converted on account of the greatness of Solomon and his table; and so it is written in Chronicles II (2:16): “And Solomon numbered all the strangers, and found them a hundred and fifty thousand, and he made of them seventy thousand,” etc.
1 Kings.translator_note: Rashi’s quotation of 2 Chronicles is abridged.

1 Kings.english_translation: Taskmasters and prefects over those who did the work.

And in Chronicles II (2:17) it says: “and six hundred.” I say: three thousand three hundred were appointed over a hundred and fifty thousand, so that each one is appointed over forty-five and more, and the three hundred added in Chronicles were appointed over all of them, so that each one is appointed over five hundred and more. And know that there are two more verses on this matter, and they contradict each other, for it is said of it in this book (below 9:23): “These were the chief officers that were over Solomon’s work, five hundred and fifty”; and in Chronicles (2 Chronicles 8:10) it says: “two hundred and fifty” — behold four verses that contradict each other. But we have to explain that in the latter verses [they were] appointed over all of them; and Solomon had these proselytes to be bearers of burdens and to hew stones in the mountain, and he had other workers for the store-cities, who were citizens, for those verses are said there; and in the book of Kings he counted the proselyte prefects in two counts: the commanders of forty-five alone, and the three hundred important ones he combined with two hundred and fifty who were appointed over the workers of the store-cities, and counted five hundred and fifty officers; and in Chronicles he counted all the prefects of the proselytes by themselves, the great with the small, three thousand six hundred, all of them proselytes. And the prefects of the store-cities, who were Israelites, two hundred and fifty, he counted by themselves.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: who bore rule over the people that wrought in the work
1 Kings.english_translation: The taskmasters of the people who did the work.
From the mountain, an expression of uprooting.
Heavy.

Dressed and hewn. And if you say, But is it not already said (below 6:7): “and there was neither hammer nor axe … heard in the house while it was in building” — the explanation is that no iron was heard in the house while it was being built, but he used to hew outside, and bring in and build inside (so it is expounded in Sotah 48b).
In the mountains.
A nation whose name is Gebal, and they are skilled at hewing stones and building, as it is said (Ezekiel 27:9) of Tyre: “The elders of Gebal and the wise men thereof were in thee thy calkers.”
An expression of preparation.
It is Iyar, for in it there is brightness (*ziva*) for the tree, and so Jonathan translated: *ziv nitzniya*.
By the count of the months, for Nisan is the new year for months.
It refers to the fourth year, the fourth of the reign of Solomon, and so it says in Chronicles (2 Chronicles 3:2): “And he began to build in the second month, in the fourth year of his reign.”
1 Kings.translator_note: The printed quotation of 2 Chronicles 3:2 is abbreviated; the verse reads “on the second day of the second month, in the fourth year of his reign.”

1 Kings.english_translation: The Hekhal and the Devir together.
In front of the Hekhal, at its entrance.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: twenty cubits was the length thereof, according to the breadth of the house
1 Kings.english_translation: The length of the Ulam across the breadth of the Hekhal, from north to south; every greater measure is called “length,” and the lesser is called “breadth,” because in the Hekhal the measure from east to west is greater, it is called length, and in the Ulam in which the measure from north to south is greater, it is called length from north to south, and from east to west it is called in it “breadth.”
In front of the house, on the east side, toward the outside.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: windows broad within, and narrow without
1 Kings.english_translation: Our Rabbis explained (Menachot 86b): *shekufim* is an expression of seeing and opening and looking out: open on the outside and closed on the inside, narrow on the inside, not in the manner of other windows which are made for light, to show that He has no need of its light.
1 Kings.translator_note: The JPS renders this verse “broad within, and narrow without,” the opposite of the arrangement Rashi describes here.

1 Kings.english_translation: *Apentiz* in Old French, and it has three names: *yatzia*, *ta*, *tzela* (so it is explained in Bava Batra 61a).
1 Kings.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is אפנטי״ץ; Darmesteter (1909) reads *apéndiç*.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: against the walls of the house round about
1 Kings.english_translation: That is, opposite the Hekhal and the Holy of Holies, which is the Devir, he made ribs on the outside, on the south and west and north; and the end of the verse is an explanation of its beginning: “And he built against the wall of the house” — adjacent to the wall of the house — “a side-structure round about.” How? He made the walls of the house for the Hekhal and for the Devir, he made side-chambers.
Like *asah*, and so (Exodus 15:2): “and He is become my salvation” (*va-yehi li li-yeshuah*), like *hayah li li-yeshuah*.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: the nethermost story of the side-structure
1 Kings.english_translation: On each and every side the chambers were three, one on top of the other, and the measure of their length is not stated here; and in tractate Middot (chapter 4, mishnah 3) we learned: There were thirty-eight chambers, fifteen in the north, five on top of five, and five on top of them, and likewise in the south, and eight in the west, three on top of three, and two on top of them. The lowest was five, and the middle six, and the upper seven. Why? For “*migra'ot* (rebatements) he made for the house round about outside”; the height of the chamber was five cubits, and when the wall of the Hekhal rises five cubits, it reduces its thickness, and goes in one cubit inward, and places upon that setback the ends of the beams of the roof of the upper chamber of the chamber, which is the floor for the middle one; and when it rises ten, it goes in a cubit, to place the ends of the beams of the middle upper-story, which is the floor of the upper; so the middle is a cubit wider than the lowest, and the upper is a cubit wider than the middle.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: that the beams should not have hold in the walls of the house
1 Kings.english_translation: That the ends of the beams not be fixed through holes in the walls of the house, for that is a damaging of the wall, and not a way of beauty.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: was built of stone made ready at the quarry
