1 Kings.english_translation: As they moved it from the mountain by means of the *shamir*, as it came from there, they set it in the wall of the building, and did not hew it with iron implements; and the “hewn stones” mentioned above are a matter of dispute in Sotah (48b).
*Daluta* in the language of Russia (*Rusya*).
1 Kings.translator_note: The gloss is in a Slavic language, not Old French; I give the printed form.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: The door for the lowest row of chambers was in the right side of the house
1 Kings.english_translation: Jonathan translated this “middle” like “lowest,” not a “middle” between upper and lower, for in the five chambers that are in the south it had an opening to the outside in the lowest row, and this is [the Targum]: “and by winding stairs they went up to the middle.”
1 Kings.translator_note: The printed Hebrew of this comment and the next one (which has an empty lemma) overlap and look garbled; both are translated literally.

1 Kings.english_translation: “The middle” — Jonathan translated: *metzi'ata* (“middle”), for these chambers were not open to the outside. There were three openings for each one, so it is taught in tractate Middot (ibid.): one to the chamber on the right, one to the chamber on the left, and one to the chamber above it. And it teaches here that one of the lowest [chambers] in the south wall had an opening to the outside, and through that opening they enter all of them; and “the middle side-chamber” of the verse is not a middle between upper and lower, but the middle of the five chambers, which in the south had an opening to the outside in the lowest row; and this is the Targum “and by winding stairs they went up to the middle,” which is above it, implying that the middle side-chamber was below.
1 Kings.translator_note: The printed Hebrew of this comment and the previous one overlap and look garbled; both are translated literally. The Hebrew lemma is empty in the printed text. Audit 5 source check: a passage with the same wording (12 consecutive words) is found in Mishnah Middot 4.3 (Sefaria Hebrew text, labelled Public Domain). This is a wording match only; the translation was not changed.

1 Kings.english_translation: Jonathan translated: *mesibta*, which in our language is called *veyn* in Old French, and in German *windel-shtein* and the common name *shwindel-shtig*; and it is a structure of a pillar of stones made with steps upon steps, and one who goes up on them is like one circling around a pillar, and one ascends in it many and many cubits high, and has no need for a slope like other ladders, for its circling is its slope.
1 Kings.translator_note: Old French and German glosses: the printed Hebrew spellings are וויי״ן, ווינד״ל שטיי״ן and שווינד״ל שטי״ג. Darmesteter (1909) reads the French as *wiç* (modern *vis*) and the German as *vindalstein*.

1 Kings.english_translation: Like *el ha-shelishiyim*.
An expression of covering a ceiling.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: with planks of cedar over beams
1 Kings.english_translation: Two ceilings, one made for ornament from below, and one of cedar boards from above; the lower is of *gevim*; and Jonathan translated: *be-hantukhin*, and I do not know what they are; and I heard in the name of Rabbi Menachem of blessed memory that they are woven planks, beautiful, in the form of a pattern, which in our language is called *çilid*, and in German *gehimelt*, and it is an expression of “heavens,” “the heavens of the beam.” And I say that they are hollow bricks, and they are like a half of a round reed, which they make for covering houses (in the German language *deck-tsigel*).
1 Kings.translator_note: Old French and German glosses: the printed Hebrew spellings are צילי״ד and גהימל״ט. Darmesteter (1909) reads the French as *çéled* and the German as *himle*.

1 Kings.english_translation: An Aramaic expression: *guvta de-kanya*; and these were (above), and the *sedarot* (below).
1 Kings.translator_note: The printed positions “above” and “below” in this comment seem to contradict the previous comment; they are translated as printed. The Aramaic phrase is left in transliteration.

1 Kings.english_translation: Cedar boards arranged above the *gevim*, for treading of the foot when they go up to see to the repair of the House; and so Jonathan translated: “and rows in cedars, and above them (that is, the *gevim*) *sidra de-rakhfat reishei sheritta arza'ya*,” and *rakhfat* is an expression of joining, and its companion (2 Samuel 22:12) “thick clouds of the skies,” Targum Jonathan: *meri'khefet ananin kelilin* (and *sedarot*, that is, boards arranged one beside another, Radak).
1 Kings.translator_note: The parentheses, including the one naming Radak, are in the printed text and look like editorial additions rather than Rashi’s own words. The Aramaic is left in transliteration.

1 Kings.english_translation: Of each and every one — behold, their height is fifteen cubits, besides the thickness of the ceiling.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and they rested on the house
1 Kings.english_translation: It is the covering of the upper roof; and the *safun* mentioned above is the ceiling of the upper story.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And he built the walls of the house within with boards of cedar
1 Kings.english_translation: Walls of cedar next to the wall of stone, in order to coat gold upon it, as he says below (v. 21): “So Solomon overlaid the house within with pure gold”; and it is impossible to coat gold upon stones, except by means of wood and nails.
The walls of the upper story.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and he covered the floor of the house
1 Kings.english_translation: The whole floor.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: twenty cubits on the hinder part of the house
1 Kings.english_translation: Twenty, which are from the end of the Hekhal onward; and the twenty at the end of the house are of the Bet ha-Kapporet (that is, the Holy of Holies).
To the ceiling; he made a wall of cedar to cover the wall of stone, to coat gold upon it.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: he even built them for himself
1 Kings.english_translation: Those twenty cubits.
Within the partition of one cubit, the *traksin* (curtain), which separates between the forty and the twenty; and that partition is called Devir.
He set them apart for those twenty cubits.
In front of the Devir, toward the outside.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And the cedar on the house within was carved with knops
1 Kings.english_translation: That is, those cedar walls that he made within the house, to cover the wall of stone, were carved with designs of carvings and shapes of *peka'im*, like buttons: *peka'im*. *Lemoisheils* in Old French.
1 Kings.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is למויישייל״ש; Darmesteter (1909) reads *lemoiséls* (and compares the Glosses of Gershom, *lemsel*).

1 Kings.english_translation: Jonathan translated: *ve-atunin shoshanin* — the shape of chains.
1 Kings.translator_note: The Aramaic word *atunin* is left untranslated. Audit 4: the Aramaic quotation was checked against Targum Jonathan/the Ketuvim Targum (Mikraot Gedolot, Sefaria) at 1KI 6:18 and reads as quoted; the meaning of the unclear word, if noted above, is still unresolved.

1 Kings.english_translation: An expression of ropes, in the language of the Gemara, like (Moed Katan 29a; Berakhot 8a): *ke-fiturei be-fi veshet* (“like the *piturei* of the mouth of the gullet”).
1 Kings.translator_note: The Gemara quotation is left in transliteration; its sense is not clear to me.

1 Kings.english_translation: An expression of flowers, like (Numbers 17:23): *va-yatzetz tzitz* (“and it put forth blossoms”): ropes and flowers. And Menachem connected *pitturei* to it, an expression of (Exodus 13:12) *peter rechem* (“that which openeth the womb”), and like (Psalm 22:8) *yaftiru be-safah* (“they open the lip”).

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: all was cedar; there was no stone seen
1 Kings.english_translation: (Targum:) The whole house was covered with boards of cedar; no stone was seen.
Jonathan translated: *gelaf chizu bei'in* (explanation: engraved in the likeness of round eggs).
1 Kings.translator_note: The Aramaic is left in transliteration. The parenthetical explanation is in the printed text.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: the Sanctuary in the midst of the house within
1 Kings.english_translation: A partition of a cubit, the *traksin* (curtain).
Like *latet*.
Inside that partition, a space twenty in length, and twenty in breadth.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: twenty cubits in the height thereof
1 Kings.english_translation: That is, the upper story of the Holy of Holies is lower than that of the Hekhal.
The Devir, which is the partition.

Our Rabbis explained it (Yoma 45a): when it was opened for sale, all other shops were closed. And Jonathan translated: *dahav tav* (“good gold”), meaning: whoever has any of it shuts it up for himself.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: an altar, which he covered with cedar
1 Kings.english_translation: It is the altar of incense; and I wonder: and that of Moses, why was it hidden away?
1 Kings.translator_note: The sense of the last clause is unclear; translated literally.

1 Kings.english_translation: The house of the Holy of Holies.
An expression of bars.
Chains (*shalsheilot*).
The whole Hekhal altogether.
(Targum:) of olive trees.

And their feet stood on the ground, one on the north of the ark and one on the south, spreading over the ark and over its staves; the length of the wings covers part of (the breadth of the staves), for the ark was placed with its length across the breadth of the house, and its staves projected at the opening of the Devir, against the curtain opposite the opening, and its staves were placed at the ends of their length, so that two Levites could enter between them when they carried it in the wilderness.
1 Kings.translator_note: The sentence is elliptical in the Hebrew; the pronouns in “at the ends of their length” are translated as printed. The parenthesis is in the printed text.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: from the uttermost part of the one wing unto the uttermost part of the other were ten cubits
1 Kings.english_translation: When they were spread out, the wings of both, which touched one another, filled the whole space of twenty cubits, and the body of the cherubim is not part of the measure, and stands by a miracle (Bava Batra 99a).

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: the wing of the one touched the one wall
1 Kings.english_translation: The north.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: the wing of the other cherub touched the other wall
1 Kings.english_translation: The south, spreading over the ark and over its staves.
And the ends of the wings which are in the middle of the house.
For the whole space of the house is twenty.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And he carved all the walls of the house
1 Kings.english_translation: The walls of wood.
Surrounded with figures.
Engraved with the form of cherubim and palm-trees and ropes and flowers.
For the inner Bet ha-Kapporet, and for the outer Hekhal.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And the floor of the house
1 Kings.english_translation: The whole pavement.
For the Bet ha-Kapporet and the Hekhal.
Wood of the olive.

The *eilei* of the opening, which are the doorposts on this side and that, made round, in the form of *ayalim*: *eilav ve-eilamav* (other books: *eilah ve-alon*); and so in the whole building of Ezekiel the thresholds of the openings are called *eilim*.
1 Kings.translator_note: The word *ayalim* (“rams”) is left untranslated because the comparison is not clear to me. The variant reading in parentheses is in the printed text.

1 Kings.english_translation: The one threshold, and the doorposts on this side and that two, behold three, and the lintel above it made like two, like this, and this is the drawing: so I heard. But I say: *mezuzot chamishit* — the doorposts had five sides, and were not square; and he is not speaking of the threshold or of the lintel, for we do not find threshold and lintel called *eilim*.
1 Kings.translator_note: The drawing mentioned in the text is not reproduced in the printed edition.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and he spread the gold upon the cherubim
1 Kings.english_translation: He beat out the gold into thin plates over the carved shapes, so that it would sink into the place of the engraving and project over the projection, so that the gold would not nullify the forms, and the forms of the wood would be recognizable in the gold.
The doorposts of the Hekhal were square; and so Jonathan translated: *min arba'ah sitreihon meruba'in* (“from their four sides squared”).
Each one the size of half the breadth of the opening.
Jonathan translated: *tarein tzirin* (“two hinges”), the upper hinge and the lower hinge.
(Targum:) *sagalgalin* (“rounded”).
This too is translated “hinges”; an expression of *kela'im* (“slings”), I say it is an Aramaic expression, an expression of entering, for it enters the hole of the threshold.
1 Kings.translator_note: The word play on *kela'im* is translated as printed.

1 Kings.english_translation: Upon the doors.
The gold was fitted to the engraving of the forms, sinking in its sunken place and projecting in its projecting place, so that the forms are recognizable in it.

It is the Court of the Priests and the Court of Israel, and it was before the Ulam, and he calls it “inner” because it was inside the Women’s Court (and in Scripture we do not find “*ezrat*” written, except in the Mishnah).
1 Kings.translator_note: The parenthesis is in the printed text and may be an editor’s addition.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and a row of cedar beams
1 Kings.english_translation: A course of walls (hewn) he made in the wall.
1 Kings.translator_note: The parenthetical word in the printed text is translated as printed.

1 Kings.english_translation: Of King Solomon.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: was the foundation of the house of the LORD laid
1 Kings.english_translation: Its foundation was begun.
It is Marcheshvan, for the grass has withered (*balah*) in the field, and they mix (*bolelin*) fodder for the animals from the house, from the expression (Judges 19:21): *va-yavol la-chamorim*.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And Solomon was building his own house thirteen years
1 Kings.english_translation: In the work of the Most High he was quick, and in his own he was slow; and Scripture tells of it in his praise.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: the house of the forest of Lebanon
1 Kings.english_translation: Jonathan translated: *beit mekirat malkaya* (“the house of the king’s dwelling”). (The cedar pillars standing along the length of the hundred cubits, each and every row along the hundred; and from the first row to the fourth row, fifty cubits, and that is the breadth of the house. A gloss from the author of *Tzurat ha-Bayit*.)
1 Kings.translator_note: The parenthesis is in the printed text and is attributed there to a later author (*Tzurat ha-Bayit*), not Rashi.

1 Kings.english_translation: Beams of cedar, along the length of the house. There was a row of pillars on the ground, and the beams from pillar to pillar. (And the second row opposite the first row across the breadth of the house, and so the four rows; and the covering of the boards for the floor of the house from row to row upon the beams; and these pillars were made with openings, openings, in the manner of a portico; and the beams were like the lintel that is over the doorposts; and these beams too were to support upon them the partitions, which are the side-chambers mentioned in the verse. And that it says “the side-chambers which were upon the pillars,” and does not say “upon the beams,” is because the pillars are the main thing, for the house stands upon them, and the beams are only to hold and join pillar to pillar so that the tent be one; and they lay on their side and were not upright. And in saying “upon the pillars,” it means upon the beams that are upon the pillars, and they are not called by a name of their own in relation to them. And it is also possible that the beams do not rise above the pillars, for they do not lie above, but are placed at the tops of the pillars and level with them above, and not like a lintel that overlooks the doorposts, but like a long peg that joins two pillars; and what is written “and beams upon the pillars,” its meaning is: at the upper side of the pillars. It turns out that what is upon the beams is upon the pillars. Up to here is the explanation of the author of *Tzurat ha-Bayit*.)
1 Kings.translator_note: This long parenthesis is an explanation by a later author (*Tzurat ha-Bayit*), included in the printed text. It is technical and elliptical in several places and is translated literally.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And it was covered with cedar
1 Kings.english_translation: A roofing over it from above.

The upper partitions that are upon the beams: four partitions, one next to the other across the breadth, drawn along the length of the house, all of them openings and windows, for it is a summer house, made for the air; and upon those partitions was the roofing of the covering. The covering was forty-five boards: three rows of boards (for the three spaces) between the four rows of pillars, fifteen boards to the row (that is, fifteen of them were placed in each space); their length across the width between row and row, and their breadth along the length of the house, one beside the other.
1 Kings.translator_note: The parentheses are in the printed text. The architecture described is intricate and is translated literally.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And there were beams in three rows
1 Kings.english_translation: And he made another roofing alongside the three rows of boards, and the three rows of the *shekufim*; for the breadth of fifteen boards did not roof the house along its whole length, which is a hundred cubits, and he made beside it, for the roofing of the house, a roofing of small boards, placed upon the small beams that remain (it should say: that are placed) from row to row of cedar beams, three beams one beside (it should say: at the end of) the other, and *shekufin* on their two sides, like the lintel in which the door overlooks, and upon those *shekufin* the ends of the small boards are placed; the length of the small boards corresponds to the breadth of the large boards that he placed first.
1 Kings.translator_note: The parenthetical corrections (“it should say…”) are in the printed text. The structure described is technical and is translated literally.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and light was over against light
1 Kings.english_translation: The ends of the boards of this *shakuf* are opposite (the ends of) the boards of that (*shakuf*).

An expression of an edge; and Menachem so explained it, and connected it with (Psalm 107:30): *el mechoz cheftzam* (“unto their desired haven”). And every *chazit* in the language of the Mishnah is so: in the order of the Tamid service (Tamid 29a); and so he does *chazit* on the outside, in the chapter “The Partners” in Bava Batra (2a). And Jonathan too translated it: *zavi le-kavel zavi* (“corner against corner”). But “*shekufim atumim*” (above 6:4); and so (here, verse 5): “square in the frame” — all of these he translated *kelunsa*.
1 Kings.translator_note: The Mishnaic references and the word *chazit* are translated as printed; the Aramaic is left in transliteration.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And all the doors with their posts
1 Kings.english_translation: For the unspecified “dwelling of kings” is made with openings, openings, because of the air, and therefore it was called “house of the forest,” for it resembles a forest.

Jonathan translated: *meruba'in ve-chafan kelunsa*. And the openings were covered with thin boards; they were square like the other openings of houses, and not made arched like the openings of the porch.
1 Kings.translator_note: The Aramaic words are left in transliteration.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and light was over against light
1 Kings.english_translation: And over against that *machaza*, it turns toward the other *machaza*, the end of the board facing the end of the board, three times in each and every ceiling; and I do not know how.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And he made the porch of pillars
1 Kings.english_translation: He made a porch before these pillars, an entrance to the house, fifty cubits its length, along the breadth of the house, which was fifty cubits, and thirty its breadth before the length of the extent of the house; but the greater measure is always called “length,” and the shorter is called “breadth.”
He made a high porch over the whole house.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and pillars and thick beams before them
1 Kings.english_translation: And upon the cedar beams that were upon the lower pillars, he set up on (it should say: more) other pillars, and beams from pillar to pillar, the pillars to weave in them side-chambers from this to that, and the *avim* for the roofing of the upper story. An *av* is a beam, as we learned: “and the *avim*, these are the beams.”
1 Kings.translator_note: The parenthetical correction is in the printed text. The Mishnah reference is not named there.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And he made the porch of the throne
1 Kings.english_translation: (Targum:) “and the porch to set up there the seats of the court that judges there; he made a vestibule (*prosda*) for the court” — *prosda* is an expression of *prozdor* (“corridor”).

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and it was covered with cedar
1 Kings.english_translation: The ground of the floor was covered with cedars.
Jonathan translated: *min ushya ad ushya* (“from foundation to foundation”): from the foundation of this wall to the foundation of that wall.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And his house where he might dwell
1 Kings.english_translation: A complete dwelling, to eat there and to lie down there.
Inside the porch of the House of the Forest of Lebanon.
It came into his heart to make a house for the daughter of Pharaoh.
Like the work of this porch.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: All these were of costly stones
1 Kings.english_translation: All these stones were made heavy.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: according to the measures of hewn stones
1 Kings.english_translation: According to the measure of hewn stones; there was one measure for hewn stones in the country.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: even from the foundation unto the coping
1 Kings.english_translation: This building was made of these hewn stones in height, from the foundation to the top of the beam.
An expression of foundation.
The top of a beam, as (Isaiah 48:13): *vi-ymini tippechah shamayim* (“and My right hand hath spread out the heavens”).
On the outer side the whole extent of the walls was of these stones, up to the great court.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And the foundation was of costly stones, even great stones
1 Kings.english_translation: And the foundation that was within the ground was of stones larger than the measure of hewn stones.
And above the foundations were costly stones up to the coping, as stated above.
(Targum:) “and covered with boards of cedar,” as stated (verse 7): “and it was covered with cedar.”
The wall was made of three courses of stones, and a course of wood upon them.
A craftsman.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and he was filled with wisdom and understanding and skill
1 Kings.english_translation: Three instruments of craftsmanship with which the world was created, as it is said (Proverbs 3:19–20): “The LORD by wisdom founded the earth; by understanding He established the heavens. By His knowledge the depths were broken up.” With the three of them the House was built.
1 Kings.translator_note: The Proverbs quotation is abridged in Rashi’s Hebrew; JPS wording is not used here.

1 Kings.english_translation: Which he set up in the porch: Jachin and Boaz.

And in Chronicles (2 Chronicles 3:15) it says: “thirty and five cubits high,” for he cast both of them as one, and the missing cubit, I say, was a half-cubit at the top of each, which is not like the work of the rest of the pillar, as stated below (verse 22) in the matter: “and upon the top of the pillars was lily-work.”

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and a line of twelve cubits did compass it about; [and so] the other pillar
1 Kings.english_translation: It teaches that it was four cubits by four cubits round, for anything that has three handbreadths in its circumference has a handbreadth in its width; and its thickness was four fingers, and it was hollow; so it is explained at the end of the book of Jeremiah (52:21). And this is an abbreviated verse: it explained the length of one, and the second is learned from it, and it explained the circumference of the second, and the first is learned from it. And so Jonathan translated: “and a line measuring twelve cubits compassed it, and so the second pillar.”
*Pomels* in Old French.
1 Kings.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is פומייל״ש; Darmesteter (1909) reads *pomels* (modern *pommeaux*, “knobs”).

1 Kings.english_translation: *Tresjeter* in Old French.
1 Kings.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is טרישגיטי״ר; Darmesteter (1909) records the forms *tresjited*, *tresjitir*, etc., and glosses “Fondu” (from *trans* + *jectatum*).

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: the height of the one capital was five cubits
1 Kings.english_translation: And at the end of the book (2 Kings 25:17) it says: “three cubits.” We learned in the Mishnah of the Forty-nine Measures: the two lower cubits of the capitals were level with the pillar, for there was no form on them, and the three upper ones projected outward, encompassed with form, as it is said (in verse 17): “nets of checker-work,” like a kind of palm-branches they were encompassed. And I say that he did not count those two lower cubits at the end of the book because they were level with the pillar, and the pillar was thrust into the capital two cubits.
The nets that they had, resembling a kind of dome, which are called *coifa*.
1 Kings.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is קויפ״א; Darmesteter (1909) reads *coife* (modern *coiffe*).

1 Kings.english_translation: There were encompassing forms of palm-branches, like (Job 18:8): *ve-al sevakhah yithallekh* (“and he walketh upon the toils”); and they had twisted cords (*gedilim*), like the work of chains.
1 Kings.translator_note: The Job quotation is left in transliteration because Rashi’s use of it for “checker-work” is elliptical.

1 Kings.english_translation: Seven palm-branches to the circuit of one network.

Of pomegranates, and of brass; the pomegranates thrust into the chains that encompassed the capital; so it is explained in Chronicles (2 Chronicles 3:16) and in the Mishnah of the Forty-nine Measures.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: to cover the capitals that were upon the top of the pomegranates
1 Kings.english_translation: Behold, this is a verse in transposed order: to cover the pomegranates over the capitals that are upon the top; and so the capitals were made according to the order of the meaning of the verses: like a kind of two basins was each one; the lower basin, its receptacle upward, and it is called *gulah* (“bowl”), as stated in the matter (below, verse 41): “and the bowls of the capitals”; and Jonathan translated it: *agnei karuntan*. The upper is turned over upon the lower, its receptacle downward, and it is called *sevakhah* (“network”), as it is said in this matter (ibid.): “and the two networks to cover the two bowls of the capitals.” So its width is at the place of the joining, and it slopes upward and slopes downward, and it is called *beten* (“belly”), and so Jonathan translated *mi-le'umat ha-beten* (verse 20): *mi-lekabel devaka*. And the height of these two basins is four cubits, and this is what it said (verse 19): “and lily-work in the porch, four cubits”; they were figured upon them like lily-blossoms, in the manner of the figures on the wall of the porches, four cubits high; and the fifth cubit is a small capital above the large one, which is what is said (verse 20): “and capitals upon the two pillars.”
1 Kings.translator_note: The Aramaic words *agnei karuntan* and *mi-lekabel devaka* are left in transliteration.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: close by the belly which was beside the network
1 Kings.english_translation: Which is toward the network, at the end of the network at its edge; it is in the middle, at the place of the joining (that is upon the network) (it should say: that the network) is joined to the bowl that is beneath it.
1 Kings.translator_note: The parenthetical correction is in the printed text.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and the pomegranates were two hundred
1 Kings.english_translation: Pomegranates made in two rows round about, strung on a chain, and encompassing the network.
This too is an abbreviated verse: upon the one, and likewise upon the second.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And upon the top of the pillars was lily-work
1 Kings.english_translation: A half-cubit at the top of each one, its wall was thin as a lily, and the rest of the pillar was four fingers thick, hollow; therefore that cubit is not counted in the casting of the pillars in Chronicles, because it was not like the work of the pillar.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: of ten cubits from brim to brim
1 Kings.english_translation: In its middle, for the whole width of a round vessel is in its middle.
Its depth; and in Chronicles (2 Chronicles 4:6) it says that he made it for the washing of the priests, to immerse in it.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and a line of thirty cubits did compass it round about
1 Kings.english_translation: This is what they said: anything that has three handbreadths in its circumference has a handbreadth in its width: its circumference thirty, and its width ten; and he measures from within it (Eruvin 14a).
And a form in the shape of an egg; Jonathan translated it.
1 Kings.translator_note: The sentence ends abruptly in the printed text (“Jonathan translated”) without giving the Targum word.

1 Kings.english_translation: In the three lower cubits, which were square, for so we learned in the Gemara of Eruvin (ibid., page b): the three lower were square, and the two upper round; and it would be impossible for it to hold two thousand baths, which are a hundred and fifty *mikva'ot* of purification, forty... [but] only in this way, as our Rabbis explained in Eruvin: the upper square and the lower round — it cannot be said, for it is written that its brim is round about. Therefore it says: with these knops, ten to the cubit, they encompass the sea round about; for in the place of its squareness its circumference is forty cubits, ten cubits to each side; but in the place of its roundness it is impossible to say ten to the cubit all round.
1 Kings.translator_note: The printed text of this comment is garbled in places (the numbers and the order of “upper/lower”) and appears to contradict itself; it is translated literally and the Eruvin 14b parallel should be consulted.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: the knops were in two rows, cast when it was cast
1 Kings.english_translation: All of it cast together, not that he joined the knops to it after their casting by means of nails or by means of glue, which in Old French is called *soldera*.
1 Kings.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is שולדר״א; Darmesteter (1909) reads *soldedure* (modern *soudure*, “soldering”).

1 Kings.english_translation: Of these oxen.
Their hinder parts faced toward the place under the sea; [three] (two) of those in the north facing those in the south, and those in the east opposite those in the west.
1 Kings.translator_note: The printed text has a bracket and a parenthesis here that give different numbers (“three” and “two”); both are shown.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And it was a hand-breadth thick
1 Kings.english_translation: Its base and its sides; except that near its mouth it was thin, and beaten, and rolled thin, like the work of the rim of a cup from which one drinks, and figured with a flower and a lily.

Six thousand *se'ah*, for a *bat* is three *se'ah*, as it is said (Ezekiel 45:11): “the ephah and the bath shall be of one measure.” It turns out a hundred and fifty *mikva'ot* of purification: the forty hundreds [are] a hundred *mikva'ot*, and the twenty hundreds, fifty *mikva'ot* (Eruvin, there). And even when you divide the whole according to the measure that the Sages estimated, a cubit by a cubit with a height of three cubits for a *mikveh*, you will find it so: three square cubits, a hundred *mikva'ot*, and the two round, fifty *mikva'ot*, for the square exceeds the round by a quarter. And in Chronicles (2 Chronicles 4:5) it is written: “it held three thousand baths,” and our Rabbis explained (there) that it was in the measure of dry things, where the heaped part was a third of the receptacle.
1 Kings.translator_note: The numerical calculation is translated as printed and has not been independently re-worked.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and three cubits the height of it
1 Kings.english_translation: Of the base alone, the height of the wheel (explanation: apart from the stand itself; the hand of the wheel is the wheel) that sits on it, a cubit and a half, and the height of the base a cubit and a half (four cubits the length, etc.). The cubit of height was square, but the half-cubit was round, as it is said (verse 35): “and in the top of the base a half-cubit in height, round about.”
1 Kings.translator_note: The parentheses are in the printed text. The measurements are intricate and are translated literally.

1 Kings.english_translation: I saw in the Mishnah of the Forty-nine Measures: the borders were like tablets.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and there were borders between the stays
1 Kings.english_translation: The borders are from one wheel-hand to another wheel-hand; and the wheel-hand is a piece of wood thrust into the wheel through a hole, and it is called *aissel* in Old French. And the four wheels in the base: borders on this side and borders on this side, on four sides, and between this one and that one four cubits in breadth, and above, *saranim*, like *nesarim* (“boards”), opposite the borders, and the *shelavim* from the lower to the upper. “And other borders” — between the *shelavim*. Like the work of the legs of the bed of villagers, which are not round but project, to form in them lions and cherubim. And I say that these *shelavim* are like the rungs of a ladder, like brass sticks standing upright upon the lower border, like two and three between stick and stick, borders fixed from rung to rung. And Jonathan translated: *shelaviya*.
1 Kings.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is איישי״ל; Darmesteter (1909) reads *aissel* (modern *essieu*, “axle”). The explanation is difficult and partly garbled in the printed text, so I flag the reading as uncertain.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and on the borders that were between the stays
1 Kings.english_translation: Forms of lions, forms of oxen and cherubim were pictured.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and upon the stays it was in like manner above
1 Kings.english_translation: A base, to seat the laver upon it, above the border that is upon their top.
1 Kings.translator_note: The sense of “base” (*bassis*) here is as printed and is not clear to me.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and beneath the lions and oxen
1 Kings.english_translation: Those embroidered on the borders between the stays.
*Layot*: like a male and female joined together.

Beaten thin, like a thin beaten plate, and not projecting in thickness, and not engraved in sunken work. And Jonathan translated: *layot ma'aseh moredh*: *medabbek ovad kavush*, *solders* in Old French.
1 Kings.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is שולדור״ש; Darmesteter (1909) reads this word (on the related passages) as *soldedure* / *soldore* (modern *soudure*, “soldering”).

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And every base had four brazen wheels
1 Kings.english_translation: Two in front of it and two behind, in the manner of great wagons.
Jonathan translated: *ve-nesarin de-nechash*. They are the upper boards opposite the borders.
Like *nesarim* (“boards”).
Of the stand that was upon them.

Projecting above the boards at the corners of the stand; and the shoulders were cast beneath the laver that sat on the stand. (Other books: to teach that the shoulders came out of the stand in one casting, and the shoulders held the laver so that it should not fall down into the hollow of the stand.)
1 Kings.translator_note: The parenthesis is in the printed text.

1 Kings.english_translation: At the side of each one of the shoulders there were wreaths of male and female figured “at the side of a man,” like “a man to his brother” mentioned of the cherubim (Exodus 25:20).

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And the mouth of it within the crown and above was a cubit high
1 Kings.english_translation: The mouth of the stand comes out from the mouth of the capital and rises a cubit above, and the capital is the roof of the base, made like a hat sloping on all its sides, and in the middle a round hole was fixed, a cubit and a half in breadth in the round, and around that hole a kind of surrounding partition, half a cubit high round about; and so it is explained below (verse 35) in the matter, as it is said: “and in the top of the base was there a round compass of half a cubit high.” And it is called “the mouth of the capital,” and the stand rests upon that surround, and the bottom edges of the stand are thrust into the mouth of the surround, and above it, it projects a cubit; and this is what it says here: “and the mouth of it within the crown and above was a cubit high.”

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and the mouth thereof was round after the work of a pedestal
1 Kings.english_translation: And the mouth of the capital is round, like the model of the round stand.
Its width in the round.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and also upon the mouth of it were gravings
1 Kings.english_translation: A form of flowers.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And the four wheels were underneath the borders
1 Kings.english_translation: For the borders are from one wheel-hand to another wheel-hand, as I explained.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and the axletrees of the wheels
1 Kings.english_translation: It is a piece of wood thrust into the wheels, and they call it *aissel*.
1 Kings.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is איישי״ל; Darmesteter (1909) reads *aissel* (modern *essieu*, “axle”).

1 Kings.english_translation: Attached, cast in the base in one casting.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: was like the work of a chariot wheel
1 Kings.english_translation: Jonathan translated: “like the work of the wheels of a chariot”: a wheel within the wheel, crosswise, as it says in Ezekiel (1:16) of the lofty chariot.
*Aissel*.
1 Kings.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is איישי״ל; Darmesteter (1909) reads *aissel* (modern *essieu*).

1 Kings.english_translation: *Bojols* in Old French; they are the holes.
1 Kings.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is בוייל״ש; Darmesteter (1909) reads *bojols* (“Leurs trous,” “their holes”).

1 Kings.english_translation: They are the circles round about, which is their binding.
The arms of the wheels, thrust from their *gabbeihem* into their rims, which are called *rais* in Old French.
1 Kings.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is ריי״ש; Darmesteter (1909) reads *rajjs* / *rais* (“Leurs bras,” “their arms”; modern *rais*, “spokes”).

1 Kings.english_translation: As I explained above, “and the four feet thereof had undersetters”; and he repeated it here only to say “and from the base itself its undersetters.”

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: a round compass of half a cubit high
1 Kings.english_translation: It is the partition, as I explained above, which is around the hole, and the cubit is square.
They are the brass *saranim* mentioned above.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and the borders thereof were of one piece therewith
1 Kings.english_translation: The lower borders were cast with it, and not that he joined them afterward.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And on the plates of the stays thereof, and on the borders thereof, he graved
1 Kings.english_translation: The lower ones on both: he engraved and carved cherubim and lions (“and palm-trees” — other books do not have it).

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: according to the space of each, with wreaths round about
1 Kings.english_translation: He engraved round about a male and female embracing in their arms; so our Rabbis explained it (Yoma 54a).

An expression of grasping and clinging, like a male joined to a female, and its meaning is: a man and his *layot*. And according to its sense *layot* is an expression of joining, *soldure* in Old French: as if they were joined there, made like the *ma'arat* (“joining”) of a man; and the *ma'arah* is as we explained.
1 Kings.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is שולדור״א; Darmesteter (1909) reads *soldora* / *soldore*, taken from Latin *solidatura* (modern *soudure*).

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: all of them had one casting
1 Kings.english_translation: As he cast the first, so he cast them all.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: After this manner he made the ten bases
1 Kings.english_translation: An explanation from the author of *Tzurat ha-Bayit*: And this is the work of the base. He made four wheels of brass, as it is said (verse 30): “And every base had four brazen wheels,” like the form of a great wagon, and the height of one wheel a cubit and a half. And the work of the wheels was like the work of a chariot wheel, a wheel within a wheel, so that he could lead them wherever the spirit and the will was to lead them, there he would lead them, without needing to turn them this way and that; and the distance from wheel to wheel from east to west was four cubits, and likewise from north to south, for it is square, not long like our wagons; and this is what it said (verse 27): “four cubits was the length of one base, and four cubits the breadth thereof.” And a thick and long stick was thrust into the two wheels that are from east to west on the north side, and likewise into the two on the south; and likewise, as in those wheels that were inside these, a stick was placed and thrust into two of them from north to south on the east side, and likewise into the two western ones; and these sticks Scripture called *yadot* (“axletrees”): this is what it said, “their axletrees.” And the meaning of “their naves” is the centres of the wheels inside which these sticks revolve, and they are called *gav* because it is the height in the wheel, when it lies on the ground; and likewise the whole centre of the circle is the height from which all the sides extend. And the meaning of “their felloes” is the outer circles that bind their spokes, which are the thin pieces of wood, like arms, thrust and placed from the nave to the felloe; and it is from the expression “*va-chashukkeihem* silver” (Exodus 27:10); and it is the wheel that rolls on the ground, and they are accustomed to make a round iron around it, and it is called in the language of the Mishnah in chapter 11 of Kelim (mishnah 3): the *sovev* of a wheel. And here there was no need for a *sovev*, for it is all of brass. “And borders” — the meaning: they were made for them like tablets upon the axletrees on four sides in a square; and this is what it said (verse 31): “and their borders were foursquare, not round.” And they enclose the wagon on its four sides, therefore they were called *misgerot* (“borders”). And upon these borders are boards of brass; Scripture called them “axles of brass” (*sarnei nechoshet*), and it is a transposed word; “and upon them,” that is: outside and not on top of them, made like rungs of a ladder, and between rung and rung borders, “and upon them the form of oxen,” etc. And the boards rose above the borders up to the height of the wheels, and sloped and went on like a hat and like a kind of covering on turtle-wagons, until they came opposite the height of the wheel, and there they extend one to another until they cover it, except that in the middle above they do not cover, but there is a round hole in them, its circle a cubit and a half wide; and this covering is called *kothereth* (“capital”), and the hole in it “the mouth of the capital”; and this is what it said (ibid.): “and the mouth thereof was round after the work of a pedestal, a cubit and a half”; and around this hole there rises a partition to the height of half a cubit; this is what it said (verse 35): “and in the top of the base was there a round compass of half a cubit high.” And into this partition the stand enters and is thrust, which is a vessel of receiving that receives the laver, when the laver is thrust into the stand, and the stand is within this partition that is on the wagon, and the stand at the bottom is round to half a cubit, according to the height of the partition above the round hole in the base, and the stand rises above this partition a cubit; and this is what it said (verse 31): “and the mouth of it within the crown and above was a cubit high.” And now we have three cubits as the height of the base: for the wheel is a cubit and a half, and the round partition half a cubit, and a cubit of the stand’s height goes out above it; and this cubit is square, and has four undersetters at its four corners; and this is what it said (verse 34): “and there were four undersetters … of the base itself were its undersetters.” For the laver is below in its bottom, sloping so as to enter the stand, and so that it not fall into it more than the measure desired, therefore these undersetters were made, to carry and bear it. Up to here is the language of *Tzurat ha-Bayit*.
1 Kings.translator_note: This whole comment is the later author’s explanation (*Tzurat ha-Bayit*), included in the printed text with no lemma. The technical description is intricate and is translated literally; I flag it as uncertain.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And he made ten lavers of brass
1 Kings.english_translation: It is written (2 Chronicles 4:6): “the work of the burnt-offering they rinsed in them.”

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: on the right side of the house
1 Kings.english_translation: Opposite the right side of the house.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: on the right side of the house eastward, toward the south
1 Kings.english_translation: Extended from the south side to the north side, and this is “eastward, toward the south”: the north-eastern corner, opposite the open space between the north wall of the house and the side of the wall of the Court; and the north side is called “toward the south” as drawn out and distant from the south; and *mul* and *mi-mul* are not equal in meaning.
1 Kings.translator_note: The compass directions in this comment are puzzling in the printed text (north called “toward the south”); translated literally.

1 Kings.english_translation: And Rabbi said: the *kiyyorot* are the *sirot* (“pots”), as you say (Zechariah 12:6): “like a *kiyyor* of fire among wood”; and so (1 Samuel 2:14): “and he struck it into the *kiyyor*.”
1 Kings.translator_note: The Hebrew lemma printed is “*va-ya'as Chirom*, etc.”; the comment itself concerns *ha-kiyyorot* (“the pots”).

1 Kings.english_translation: Of brass, to clear the ashes of the altar.
Rakes of brass, which are called *vidul* in Germany, to rake with them the ashes into the pots.
1 Kings.translator_note: German gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is ווידו״ל. Darmesteter (1909) transcribes a similar form (OCR-uncertain here) and glosses “Les pelles” (“the shovels”).

1 Kings.english_translation: A hundred pomegranates to a row, strung on chains.
He melted them and cast them in their pattern.
(Targum:) “in the thickness of the clay.”
From weighing the weight of these vessels, because of their exceeding abundance; and he ceased to count their weight.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: five on the right side, and five on the left
1 Kings.english_translation: It is impossible to say five on the right of the entrance and five on the left of the entrance, for then we would find a candlestick in the north, and the Torah said (Numbers 3:29): “on the side of the Tabernacle southward.” But that of Moses was in the middle, five on its right and five on its left.
Of the candlestick.
The small cups in which they put the oil and the wick.
With which they lift the wick out of the oil.
A vessel of the kinds of song, and so *mazmerot* (“pruning-hooks”).
1 Kings.translator_note: The identification of this vessel and the link with *mazmerot* are as printed; the sense is not clear to me.

1 Kings.english_translation: To receive blood.
For the bowls of frankincense.
To take with them the terumah of the ashes and the coals, to carry from the outer altar to the inner altar to burn incense.
Keys (*maftechot*); I heard that they open the lock with them.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: for the doors of the house
1 Kings.english_translation: Which is the Holy of Holies.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and for the doors of the house
1 Kings.english_translation: Which is for the Hekhal: all their hinges were of gold.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: the things which David his father had dedicated
1 Kings.english_translation: What remained of the silver and gold that his father had dedicated. And an aggadic Midrash (Yalkut Shimoni §186): Solomon did not wish to give from that dedicated property toward the building of the House. And I heard from wise men of Israel who used to say: because he knew that its end was to be destroyed, so that the idolaters should not say, “Their fear is hard, for they took their vengeance from the House, which was built from the robberies and violence that David took from them.” And some say: Solomon said this: There was a famine in the days of his father, three years, year after year, and he should have spent these dedicated things to keep alive the poor of Israel.
1 Kings.translator_note: The attribution “some say: Solomon said this” follows the printed text.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: the princes of the fathers’ houses of the children of Israel
1 Kings.english_translation: Of the children of Israel.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: out of the city of David
1 Kings.english_translation: Where David had placed it when they brought it from the house of Obed-edom.

Jonathan translated: “in the month of the ancient ones, which they call the first month at the festival, and now it is the seventh month.” From the time the Torah was given and it is written of Nisan that it is “the first of months,” Tishrei is called the seventh.
1 Kings.translator_note: The Aramaic is translated as printed; the phrase “which they call the first month” is as printed.

1 Kings.english_translation: That Moses made, and Solomon hid it away after the First House was built, as we learned in the Tosefta of Sotah (13:1).
Which David pitched for the ark.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: under the wings of the cherubim
1 Kings.english_translation: Those that Solomon made, standing on their feet on the ground, and these are not the cherubim of the cover that is upon the ark.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: over the place of the ark
1 Kings.english_translation: From wall to wall, as stated above in the matter.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And the staves were so long that the ends of the staves were seen
1 Kings.english_translation: On the curtain opposite the opening, in the cubit of the *traksin*. One might think they would pierce through it and come out; therefore the verse says “but they could not be seen without.” How so? They pressed and projected like two breasts of a woman, as it is said (Song of Songs 1:13): “that lieth betwixt my breasts” (Yoma 54a).

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: when the priests were come out of the holy place
1 Kings.english_translation: The priests who bore the ark into the Devir; when they went out the Shekhinah rested in the Hekhal.

When he saw the cloud, he said: Now I see that the Shekhinah rests in the House I built, for so He promised to come and dwell in it in a cloud and thick darkness. And where did He say it? (Leviticus 16:2): “for I appear in the cloud upon the ark-cover”; so it is taught in the Sifre.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: A place for Thee to dwell in for ever
1 Kings.english_translation: For from when it was chosen, the high places were no longer permitted, and the Shekhinah did not rest in any other place.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: who spoke with His mouth unto David my father
1 Kings.english_translation: That He would give him a son who would build a house.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and hath with His hand fulfilled it
1 Kings.english_translation: He fulfilled His word with His good hand.
This He spoke to David my father.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And Solomon stood before the altar of the LORD
1 Kings.english_translation: It is written (2 Chronicles 6:13): “For Solomon had made a brazen scaffold, and had set it in the midst of the court,” etc., “and he stood upon it, and kneeled down upon his knees.”
1 Kings.translator_note: The Chronicles quotation is abridged in Rashi’s Hebrew.

1 Kings.english_translation: Waiting and treasuring up, to keep the covenant and the mercy, to fulfil His promise.
An expression of the trustworthiness of a promise.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: But will God in very truth
1 Kings.english_translation: An expression of wonder.
Cannot hold Thee.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: If a man sin against his neighbour
1 Kings.english_translation: Who has relations with another man’s wife.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and an oath be exacted of him to cause him to swear
1 Kings.english_translation: As the water tests her, so the water tests him (Sotah 27b).
An expression of a creditor’s exacting (*noshe*).

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and he come and swear before Thine altar
1 Kings.english_translation: “And the priest shall set the woman before the LORD” (Numbers 5:18).

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: to bring his way upon his own head
1 Kings.english_translation: “And her belly shall swell,” etc. (ibid., verse 27).
“Then she shall be cleared, and shall conceive seed” (ibid., verse 28); so it is expounded in the Tosefta of Sotah (1:3).
For a man is obliged to bless over the evil (Berakhot 54a).
In order that Thou mayest afflict them; *ki* serves in the sense of *asher*.
That the grain does not go up in the stalk to make an ear.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: according to all that the stranger calleth to Thee for
1 Kings.english_translation: And of Israel he says (above, verse 39): “and render unto every man according to all his ways”; because Israel recognizes the Holy One, blessed be He, and knows that the power is in His hand, and if his prayer is not heard, he attributes the matter to himself and his sin; but an idolater raises a complaint, and says: A house whose name goes to the end of the world — I wearied myself in many ways and came and prayed in it, and found nothing real in it, as there is nothing real in the worship of idols; therefore “according to all that the stranger calleth to Thee for.” But with Israel, if you see that he is ruining his fellow through money, do not give to him.
1 Kings.translator_note: The final sentence (“if you see that he is ruining his fellow through money, do not give to him”) is elliptical and is translated literally.

1 Kings.english_translation: They turn toward Jerusalem.
Their vengeance upon their enemies.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: from the midst of the furnace of iron
1 Kings.english_translation: Potsherds in which gold is refined are called *kur*.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: according to all that He promised
1 Kings.english_translation: And where did He promise? “and He giveth you rest from all your enemies” (Deuteronomy 12:10).

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: that He maintain the cause of His servant, and the cause of His people Israel
1 Kings.english_translation: To demand payment for their insult from the hand of the enemy.
Words as they are written; the words of Rabbi Judah: he sanctified the pavement of the Court with the sanctity of the altar, to burn on the pavement (Zevachim 59a).
The altar of stones which he made in place of the altar of brass.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: was too little to receive the burnt-offering, and the meal-offering
1 Kings.english_translation: Because they brought many. Rabbi Yose said to him: But has it not already been said (above 3:4): “A thousand burnt-offerings did Solomon offer upon that altar,” which Moses made? And when you come to the calculation of cubits and the number of burnt-offerings, this of stone is larger than that of Moses, for the place of the arrangement of wood of the altar of Moses was a cubit by a cubit, and this one’s place of arrangement was twenty-four by twenty-four, so that Solomon’s was five hundred seventy-six times that of Moses (Zevachim 59b). If so, what is “the king hallowed the middle of the court”? That he fixed in it an altar of stones joined to the pavement (ibid., 61).
1 Kings.translator_note: The reasoning is compressed (the Talmudic dispute in Zevachim 59b) and is translated literally; the arithmetic is as printed. Audit 4 arithmetic check: 24 × 24 = 576, as printed.

1 Kings.english_translation: He says this of that of Moses, as a man says to his fellow: “So-and-so is a dwarf and unfit for service” (ibid. 59b).
1 Kings.translator_note: The comparison is as printed; its sense in the Talmudic source is not clear to me.

1 Kings.english_translation: Which is in the north of the Land of Israel.
Which is opposite it in its south, in Parashat *Eleh Mas'ei* (Numbers 34:5, 8).
Of the dedication.
The Feast of Tabernacles; it turns out that they ate and drank on the Day of Atonement (Moed Katan 9a).

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: that the LORD had shown unto David His servant
1 Kings.english_translation: To make known that He forgave him his sins, as is found in Moed Katan (ibid.): when Solomon sought to bring the ark into the Holy of Holies, the gates clung one to the other.
That He forgave them the sin of the Day of Atonement; and a heavenly voice went forth and said: All of you are destined for the life of the World to Come (ibid.).

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and Mine eyes and My heart shall be there
1 Kings.english_translation: The Targum of Jonathan: *ve-tehei shechinati sharya bei im re'uti mit'avda*: “My eyes shall be there, if My heart and My desire are there.”
1 Kings.translator_note: The Aramaic is left in transliteration; the conditional sense (“if”) follows the printed Hebrew.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and this house, which I have hallowed for My name
1 Kings.english_translation: It is a condition between Me and you; and if you do not hearken, what is said there (Leviticus 26:31)? “And I will make your sanctuaries desolate.”

As its Targum: *u-le-shu'i*: they will tell of the evils that come upon it and mock it, like (Genesis 37:9) *va-yesapper* — *ve-ishtai*. And the expression *shininah* is also an expression of speaking, as it is written (Deuteronomy 6:7): *ve-shinnantam le-vanekha* (“and thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children”).
1 Kings.translator_note: The Aramaic and the linking of *va-yesapper* with *ishtai* are translated as printed.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and this house which is so high
1 Kings.english_translation: As long as you have not sinned; and when you sin, every one that passes by it shall be astonished and hiss; and so it is written in Chronicles (2 Chronicles 7:21): “And this house, which was so high, every one that passeth by it,” etc. And so its meaning: “and this house which was high and awesome, even to idolaters, as it said above (8:41): ‘Moreover concerning the stranger, that is not of Thy people,’ etc., and now, in its destruction, every one that passes by it, even an idolater, shall be astonished and hiss, and shall say that Israel’s sin caused it.”
He will wonder, like (Leviticus 26:32) “and your enemies … shall be astonished at it,” (Job 18:20) “they that come after shall be astonished at his day.”
*Sifler* in Old French; and so is the way of everyone who sees a sudden destruction, to hiss.
1 Kings.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is שופילי״ר; Darmesteter (1909) records the form *sibler* (modern *siffler*, “to whistle, hiss”) for the related verse.

1 Kings.english_translation: Seven years for the House of the LORD, and his own house thirteen years, as stated above.
An expression of bearing (*amas*): he sustained his burden in this matter.
The land of fetters (*kevalim*), a land of mud, for the foot sinks in and is fettered in it.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And this is the account of the levy
1 Kings.english_translation: What is explained at the end of the matter (verse 20): “all the people that were left,” etc., “and upon them did Solomon levy a bond-service”; that levy was to build with it all these.
A place in Jerusalem in the City of David, called Millo because it was surrounded by a low wall, and they filled (*mil'u*) it inside with earth.
A dowry.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: in the wilderness, in the land
1 Kings.english_translation: “And Tadmor in the wilderness, in the land” — near the settled region.
1 Kings.translator_note: The Hebrew lemma is empty in the printed text; the words are those of the verse.

1 Kings.english_translation: It is called a treasure-house.
Appointed over the appointed.

Three hundred of them were proselytes appointed over the seventy thousand that bore burdens and the eighty thousand that hewed in the mountain, and three thousand three hundred who ruled over the people, as he said above (5:30): “beside Solomon’s chief officers,” etc., “three thousand and three hundred.” And in Chronicles (2 Chronicles 2:16) it says: “six hundred”: these three hundred that are lacking there he counted here, for they were appointed over all of them; and the two hundred and fifty that remain were Israelites, appointed over the rest of those doing the work. And in Chronicles (2 Chronicles 8:10) he counted them by themselves: “And these were the chief officers of king Solomon, even two hundred and fifty, that bore rule over the people,” those doing the work.
1 Kings.translator_note: The numbers (and how they are reconciled) are translated as printed; compare the earlier comment on 1KI 5:30.

1 Kings.english_translation: Who at first was in the City of David, as it is said at the beginning of the book (3:1): “and brought her into the city of David.”

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: came up out of the city of David
1 Kings.english_translation: And in Chronicles (2 Chronicles 8:11) it explains: “for he said: My wife shall not dwell in the house of David king of Israel, because the places are holy, whereunto the ark of the LORD hath come.”
1 Kings.translator_note: The Chronicles quotation is abridged and adapted in Rashi’s Hebrew.

1 Kings.english_translation: Solomon.

To build inside it houses for her servants and maidservants; and this is what Jeroboam rebuked him with (below 11:27): “Thy father left it broken down for the pilgrims, and thou hast built it to make a corvée for Pharaoh’s daughter” (Sanhedrin 101b); and this is the “but” (*akh*) mentioned here: but in this Solomon was punished, that he built Millo for her; so I heard. And I say: *akh bat Pharaoh*, etc. — that is, the cities mentioned above he needed to build for store-houses, for chariot and for horsemen and for greatness, but Millo he would not have built for any greatness, for his father had left it for the pilgrims to pitch tents in; but because Pharaoh’s daughter went up to her house, and Millo was next to that house, “then he built Millo.”
1 Kings.translator_note: The first explanation is introduced as “I heard” (a received tradition); the second is Rashi’s own.

1 Kings.english_translation: Of the House of Eternity.
And that altar of incense which was before the LORD, for the burning of the sweet spices.
*Oni* (“a ship”).

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and his burnt-offering which he offered in the house of the LORD
1 Kings.english_translation: The way of entrance that he prepared from his house to the Temple, by which he went up to the House of the LORD.
*Corail* in Old French.
1 Kings.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is קוריי״ל; Darmesteter (1909) reads *korjl* / *coral* (modern *corail*, “coral”).

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: pillars for the house of the LORD
1 Kings.english_translation: And in Chronicles (2 Chronicles 9:11) it is written: “highways to the house of the LORD”; therefore I say this *mis'ad* is an expression of a floor.
For the sons of Levi.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: gave to the queen of Sheba
1 Kings.english_translation: This giving was only the teaching of wisdom.

(He came to her and Nebuchadnezzar was born of her, and he destroyed the House that stood four hundred and ten years in the portion of all twelve tribes. From the Ari, of blessed memory.) Apart from what he gave her of gifts and delicacies that are mentioned here and are not found in her own land.
1 Kings.translator_note: The parenthesis is in the printed text and is attributed there to “the Ari” (Rabbi Isaac Luria, 16th century); it is a later addition, not Rashi’s.

1 Kings.english_translation: Hiram gave him a hundred and twenty, and the queen of Sheba a hundred and twenty, and the ship of Tarshish brought from Ophir four hundred and twenty: behold, six hundred and sixty; and the six I do not know from where. And in Chronicles (2 Chronicles 8:18) it is written: that they brought from Ophir four hundred and fifty, and he does not count the hundred and twenty of Hiram there; and the verse must be emended, for the extra thirty were from the hundred and twenty of Hiram, for Hiram’s servants were there with his servants.
1 Kings.translator_note: The arithmetic is translated as printed; Rashi himself says he does not know the source of the remaining six. “The verse must be emended” (lit. “there is to emend the verse”) is as printed. Audit 4 arithmetic check: 120 + 120 + 420 = 660, leaving the unexplained six of 666; 450 − 420 = 30, as Rashi says.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: beside that which came of the merchants
1 Kings.english_translation: Those who were bringing to him, the merchants who go about the land for trade.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: of the traffic of the traders
1 Kings.english_translation: Sellers of spices, who carry them from city to city.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and of all the kings of the mingled people
1 Kings.english_translation: Jonathan translated: *u-chol malkei somkhuta*, an expression of pledge (*eruvah*): the kings who were in their pledge and who rely on him; *garantie* in Old French.
1 Kings.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is גאראנטיא״ה; Darmesteter (1909) reads *garantie* (“Une garantie”).

1 Kings.english_translation: It surrounds a man on three sides, and this is what is said in the book of Psalms (5:13): “as with a shield wilt Thou compass him with favour.”
That is six *manim*, for the gold is the dinar.
1 Kings.translator_note: The equation “gold = dinar” and the *manim* are as printed; the sum is not worked out in the comment. Audit 4 arithmetic check: 600 dinars is six *manim* if a *maneh* is 100 dinars, the usual reckoning.

1 Kings.english_translation: It is soft and easy to hammer.
Shining like a pearl.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: There were six steps to the throne
1 Kings.english_translation: Steps for going up on it, and the top of the throne was round, the place where the king sat.
The fixing of the throne was broad, and the steps were on the side of its front, and on the side of its breadth, at its back, the seat was higher than the throne, a round place.
1 Kings.translator_note: The description of the throne’s shape is terse and is translated literally.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and there were arms on either side
1 Kings.english_translation: To rest his arms upon them: like sticks of gold from side to side, stretched to the right and to the left.
Of gold; and the whole form of the throne is explained in the Aggadah of the Scroll of Esther (Esther Rabbah 15:12; Yalkut Shimoni §1054).

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: none were of silver; it was nothing accounted
1 Kings.english_translation: There was no silver in any of them, for it was not accounted.
(Targum:) “a ship of Africa.”
(Targum:) “elephant’s tooth, and monkeys, and peacocks.”
1 Kings.translator_note: The Targum’s last word is printed *tosin*; I render it as in JPS’s “peacocks”, and the sense of the Aramaic is not certain to me.

1 Kings.english_translation: Instruments of arms.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: a thousand and four hundred chariots
1 Kings.english_translation: And in Chronicles (2 Chronicles 1:14) it is written: “a thousand and seven hundred.” And I say: a thousand and four hundred were in the chariot cities, and the three hundred with the king in Jerusalem, and this is its explanation in Chronicles: “and he bestowed them in the chariot cities,” and with the king there was yet another chariot force in Jerusalem. And here its explanation is: “and he bestowed them in the chariot cities, and with the king” some of them were in Jerusalem.
1 Kings.translator_note: Rashi’s harmonization of the two numbers is translated as printed; the Chronicles text is not quoted by number in the Hebrew.

1 Kings.english_translation: And led them.
And above (verse 21) it says “nothing accounted.” Our Rabbis explained (Sanhedrin 21b): here, before Solomon married the daughter of Pharaoh; there, after Solomon married the daughter of Pharaoh.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And the horses which Solomon had were brought out
1 Kings.english_translation: Was from Egypt.

The gathering of the horse-dealers in Egypt; the merchants of King Solomon used to buy them at a price from Egypt from the king, so that no man could take a horse out from there except through them; so I heard. And therefore the *u-mikveh* is pointed with the accent *zakef gadol*, to teach that the word stands by itself and is not joined to what follows.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and a horse for a hundred and fifty
1 Kings.english_translation: We learned that the chariot is with four horses; and so at these prices for all the kings of the Hittites and for the kings of Aram.
Of the merchants of Solomon, going out of Egypt.

She too was one of the foreign women, but she was dearer to him than all of them, so he counted her by herself; and so (2 Samuel 23:30; actually 2 Samuel 2:30 in the printed text) “And there were missing of David’s servants nineteen men and Asahel.”
1 Kings.translator_note: The printed reference is “Samuel II 2:30”, and the quoted words are from 2 Samuel 2:30. The comparison is that Asahel was counted separately although he was one of the dead.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: Then did Solomon build a high place
1 Kings.english_translation: Our Rabbis said (Shabbat 56b): because he did not protest to his wives, it is called by his name.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: in the mount that is before Jerusalem
1 Kings.english_translation: The Mount of Olives.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: Forasmuch as this hath been in thy mind
1 Kings.english_translation: That thou knewest that thou wast transgressing My commandments.
Then Hadad fled from David and Joab.

That they buried the slain of Edom; this is what is said there in the book of Samuel (2 Samuel 8:13): “And David made him a name when he returned from smiting Edom,” for all were praising him: a pious man who buries his slain; and so it says in the wars of Gog and Magog (Ezekiel 39:13): “Yea, all the people of the land shall bury, and it shall be to them a renown.” And Jonathan translated “to bury the slain”: *le-chalatza et kattilaya*, to take their spoils (*chalitzatam*).
1 Kings.translator_note:
The Aramaic *le-chalatza et kattilaya* and the sense “to take their spoils” are as printed.
The quotation of 2 Samuel 8:13 reads “Edom”, as printed; the standard Hebrew text of that verse reads “Aram” (JPS: “the Arameans in the Valley of Salt”).

1 Kings.english_translation: He said to his servants: Give him such and such an amount of bread per day.
The queen.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: that David slept with his fathers
1 Kings.english_translation: Of David, who died his own death, “sleeping” is said; of Joab, who was killed, “death” is said. Another explanation: of David, who left a worthy son to fill his place, “sleeping” is said; of Joab, who did not leave a worthy son to fill his place, “sleeping” is not said, but “death” (Bava Batra 116a).

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And God raised up another adversary unto him
1 Kings.english_translation: To Solomon; and this is what Nathan the prophet said to David (2 Samuel 7:14): “whom, if he commit iniquity, I will chasten with the rod of men.”

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: beside the mischief that Hadad did
1 Kings.english_translation: Together with the evil that came through Hadad, there was also this of Rezon.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: he also lifted up his hand against the king
1 Kings.english_translation: He rebuked him in public.
For which he rebuked him.

And in this building he closed the breach of the City of David, for the breach was behind Millo. He said to him: Your father made breaches in the wall for the pilgrims to enter by, and you have closed it, to make a corvée for the daughter of Pharaoh, to seat there her servants and attendants (Sanhedrin 101b).

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and Solomon saw the young man
1 Kings.english_translation: Before this.
Quick in his work and diligent.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: over all the labour of the house of Joseph
1 Kings.english_translation: (Targum:) “over all the bearers of the tribute of the house of Joseph,” Manasseh and Ephraim, because he was of the tribe of Ephraim.
Dominion; and *nir* is an expression of “yoke.”

For in the days of the Messiah the kingdom will return to him. And in *Seder Olam* I found: “And I will for this afflict the seed of David” — corresponding to the thirty-six years since Solomon intermarried with the daughter of Pharaoh, whom he married in the fourth year of his reign; and corresponding to it a decree was decreed that the kingdom of the house of David be divided; and the kingdom was fit to return in the days of Asa in the sixteenth year of his reign, but he spoiled it by sending a bribe to the king of Aram and not relying on the Holy One, blessed be He; and this is what is said in Chronicles (2 Chronicles 16:1): “In the thirty and sixth year of the reign of Asa, Baasha built Ramah.” And it is not possible, for Asa buried Baasha in the twenty-sixth year of his reign; but the sixteen years of his, he calls thirty-six, which are the end of thirty-six from the division of the kingdom; and Scripture declares that in that year Asa spoiled it. “But not for ever” — but thirty-six years.
1 Kings.translator_note: The chronology (Seder Olam) is translated as printed; the numbers have not been independently re-worked.

1 Kings.english_translation: My little finger.
*Esguilanter* in Old French, which sting like a scorpion.
1 Kings.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is אשגלנטי״ר; Darmesteter (1909) records forms like *aiguilantier* and reads *églantier* (“Des églantiers”, briars / dog-roses).

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: now see to thine own house, David
1 Kings.english_translation: The Temple that you built, let it be yours alone.
He is Adoniram.
Those who stood at the border, for the border of Judah and Benjamin was next to each other.

There is no sitting in the Court except for the kings of the house of David alone; and he will be sitting and I standing; and at the close of the Sabbatical year, at the time of the Assembly, he will read the portion of the king, who is head in his country, and I, like the rest of the people — I shall be found despised (Sanhedrin 101b).
At the end of the border of the land.
He expounded to them that it is the month of the ingathering, and in it the festival ought to be.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: which he had devised of his own heart
1 Kings.english_translation: An expression of falsehood: *controver* in Old French.
1 Kings.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is קונטרובי״ר; Darmesteter (1909) reads *controvér* (modern *controuver*, “to invent falsely”).

1 Kings.english_translation: This was Iddo.
The one in Beth-el and the one in Dan (Midrash Tanchuma, *Toledot* 12).
Of this Jeroboam; but he showed him honor (ibid.).

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And he gave a sign the same day
1 Kings.english_translation: The prophet gave a sign for his words on the day that he prophesied: This is the sign for you — the altar will be split by itself today, and the ashes will be poured out on the ground.

The Holy One, blessed be He, takes vengeance for the honour of a righteous man more than for His own honour: when he stood and burned incense to an idol his hand did not dry up, but because of the slander against the righteous man his hand dried up (ibid.).
And not my God; he was still standing in his rebellion.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and became as it was before
1 Kings.english_translation: Standing and burning incense to an idol.
Eat.
A false prophet.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: there dwelt an old prophet in Beth-el
1 Kings.english_translation: And he was not from there, but came from Samaria; and so it says in the matter of Josiah (2 Kings 23:18): “So they let his bones alone, with the bones of the prophet that came out of Samaria.”
The false prophet.
The man of God; from here they said (Sanhedrin 104a): Great is the meal, for it causes the Shekhinah to rest on the prophets of Baal.
1 Kings.translator_note: The Talmudic saying is translated as printed (*gedolah leguma*); the term is not clear to me.

1 Kings.english_translation: The old prophet, to the man of God.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: for the prophet whom he had brought back
1 Kings.english_translation: Put there for the man of God to ride upon.
In the burial-place that this false prophet had in the city.
Perhaps his bones will escape together with my bones.

That he saw this sign and heard the words of the prophet, and nevertheless did not repent. And our Rabbis expounded it (Sanhedrin 102a): after the Holy One, blessed be He, took hold of him by his garment and said to him: Repent, and I and you and the son of Jesse will walk in the Garden of Eden.
A kind of parched grain, which they dry in the oven and make into flour to make food from it, which in the language of the Gemara is called *shetita*.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: that she will feign herself to be another woman
1 Kings.english_translation: As though she were not this one.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: for I am sent to thee
1 Kings.english_translation: From the Holy One, blessed be He, with a hard mission.
Jonathan translated: “one who knows knowledge, who strikes his heart on the walls.”
1 Kings.translator_note: Rashi’s lemma here is the idiom “one that urinates against a wall”; the Targum is translated as printed and its sense is not clear to me.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: him that is shut up and him that is left at large
1 Kings.english_translation: “Shut up” is one who has someone to hold his hand, like (1 Samuel 9:17) “this same shall rule over (*ya'atzor*) My people”; and “left at large” is one who has no one holding by the hand.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: as a man sweepeth away dung
1 Kings.english_translation: One who burns up the food in his mouth to make dung: so will I sweep away after him until it is all gone.
1 Kings.translator_note: The image is as printed; its construction is terse.
