1 Kings.english_translation: That he abolished his watch: his father had set him as a guard so that no one should go up on pilgrimage, and he abolished his watch and went up.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: who shall cut off the house of Jeroboam that day. But what is it even then?
1 Kings.english_translation: Those born to him today, and those who are destined to be born to him from now on; so Jonathan translated.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: the city which the LORD had chosen
1 Kings.english_translation: And nevertheless.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And Judah did that which was evil
1 Kings.english_translation: And they did not lay this to heart.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and they moved Him to jealousy
1 Kings.english_translation: An expression of provocation.
Like the rest of the tribes.
Adultery.

We find in the Midrash on the Song of Songs (Esther Rabbah 1:12) that he is Pharaoh Necho, and was called Shishak because he was longing (*shokek*) and craving all his days for the ivory throne that Solomon his son-in-law had; and now he went up and took it.
The throne, the dearest of all.
Before him in honour, and afterward they bring them back to the chamber where the guards stand continually.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: in the eighteenth year of king Jeroboam
1 Kings.english_translation: One year after the death of Rehoboam; and in the twentieth year of Jeroboam Asa reigned; the third year of Nadab (Abijam) is counted as one year for King Asa, and for him too it is counted.
1 Kings.translator_note: The parenthetical “(Abijam)” is in the printed text; the chronology is difficult and is translated literally.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And he put away the sodomites
1 Kings.english_translation: Jonathan translated: *u-faley nafkat bara* (“and he removed the harlots outside”).
1 Kings.translator_note: The Aramaic is left in transliteration.

1 Kings.english_translation: From being a *gevirah*.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: she had made an abominable image
1 Kings.english_translation: Our Rabbis said (Avodah Zarah 44a): it is a wonder of mockery; she made for herself a kind of male organ, and she had relations with it every day.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: But the high places were not taken away
1 Kings.english_translation: Private high places, on which they were accustomed to offer to Heaven from the destruction of Shiloh until the House was built, when high places were permitted — these were not removed now, even though they were forbidden once the House was built, and the penalty for them was *karet*.
Even a bridegroom from his chamber, of whom it is said (Deuteronomy 24:5): “he shall be free for his house one year.”
The second and the third of Asa.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: In the third year of Asa king of Judah began Baasa
1 Kings.english_translation: The third year of Asa is counted for Nadab and for Baasa.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And moreover by the hand of the prophet Jehu the son of Hanani came the word of the LORD against Baasa
1 Kings.english_translation: That is: behold, Elah the son of Baasa reigned, and moreover this too, the word of the LORD came by the hand of Jehu, that his kingdom would not endure.

Since he too walked in his sins, it turns out he had no right to kill him; therefore he was punished for killing him; and so we find (Hosea 1:4): “and I will visit the blood of Jezreel upon the house of Jehu,” since they did not turn aside from the ways of Ahab, they were punished for their killing.
He and another were captains over the chariots.
(Targum:) “his relatives and his friends.”
When Asa gave Omri’s daughter in marriage to Jehoshaphat his son, they killed Tibni, when they saw Omri’s importance, in *Seder Olam*.
1 Kings.translator_note: The statement that Asa gave “Omri’s daughter” to Jehoshaphat is as printed (the usual tradition is that Jehoshaphat’s son married Athaliah); it is translated literally.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: In the thirty and first year of Asa king of Judah began Omri to reign
1 Kings.english_translation: A complete reign; and the dispute of Tibni was five years, from the twenty-seventh of Asa to the thirty-first.
The total: five in dispute and seven of complete reign; and it is impossible to say twelve years of complete reign, for Ahab his son reigned in the thirty-eighth year of Asa.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: six years reigned he in Tirzah
1 Kings.english_translation: Before he built Samaria.
Adding to the calves of Jeroboam.
A tree that is worshipped.

Hiel who was from Beth-el, like (1 Samuel 16:1) “Jesse the Beth-lehemite”; and it is not said *ha-Bet Lachmi*; and so “Joshua the Beth-shemite” in the book of Samuel (1 Samuel 6:14), and not *ha-Bet Shimshi*; and so “in Ophrah of the Abiezrite” (Judges 6:11), and it is not said *ha-Avi Ezri*. And some explain: *Beit ha-Eli* because he took upon himself the curses of Joshua (Joshua 6:26): “Cursed be the man … that riseth up and buildeth,” etc. Our Rabbis said (Jerusalem Talmud, Sanhedrin 10:2): Hiel was of the portion of (Benjamin), and Jericho of the portion of Jehoshaphat (Benjamin); and why did they hang it on Ahab? Because they hang the curse on the one who is spoiled [other books: cursed].
1 Kings.translator_note: The parenthetical “(Benjamin)” in the Talmudic passage is in the printed text and looks garbled; the Hebrew pun on *Beit ha-Eli* is left as printed.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: with Abiram his first-born he laid the foundation thereof
1 Kings.english_translation: When he laid its foundation his first-born son died, and he buried him and went on, and buried all his sons until the last died when the doors were set up; and so are the curses of Joshua (ibid.): “with the loss of his first-born shall he lay the foundation thereof, and with the loss of his youngest son shall he set up the gates of it.”
From a land (other books: the name of the city) whose name was Tishbi.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: As the LORD, the God of Israel, liveth
1 Kings.english_translation: Why is this joined here? Elijah and Ahab went to comfort Hiel in his mourning; Ahab said to Elijah: Is it possible that the curse of the disciple was fulfilled and the curse of Moses our teacher was not fulfilled, as it is said (Deuteronomy 11:16–17): “and ye turn aside, and serve other gods, and worship them; and the anger of the LORD be kindled against you, and He shut up the heaven,” and all Israel are serving idols, and the rains are not held back? Immediately “and Elijah said,” etc. (Jerusalem Talmud, Sanhedrin 10:2).
From Ahab and Jezebel.
So that he would know the need for rain and take the trouble to reveal [the rain]; for it was hard in the eyes of the Holy One, blessed be He, that Israel lay dead of hunger.
1 Kings.translator_note: The phrase “take the trouble to reveal” is terse in the printed text; translated literally.

1 Kings.english_translation: The name of the city.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: I have commanded a widow there
1 Kings.english_translation: In My household, that a widow woman sustain thee there.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: Fetch me, I pray thee, a little water
1 Kings.english_translation: He did not recognize the widow of whom the Holy One had told him, and learned from Eliezer, Abraham’s servant, and said: The one who gives me water to drink, she is the widow.
Like *ugah*.
Jonathan translated: *meli pisat yada*.
*Bouteille* in Old French, as is said of Saul (1 Samuel 26:12): “the cruse of water at his head.”
1 Kings.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is ביטויל״א; Darmesteter (1909) reads *botojjle* / *bouteille* (“Dans une bouteille”).

1 Kings.english_translation: From there onward we shall die of hunger.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: make me thereof a little cake first
1 Kings.english_translation: There is an aggadic Midrash in Genesis Rabbah (why “first”) — “and Leah said: *Bagad*.”
1 Kings.translator_note: The Midrashic reference is garbled in the printed text; translated literally.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: the son of the woman, the mistress of the house, fell sick
1 Kings.english_translation: So that he would need the key of the resurrection of the dead, as is found at the end of the aggadah of Chelek (Sanhedrin 113a).

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: to bring my sin to remembrance
1 Kings.english_translation: Until you came to me, they weighed my deeds and the deeds of my city, and I was worthy of a miracle; since you came here, I am not accounted anything, and my righteousness is not apparent (other books: remembered); and so of Lot it says (Genesis 19:19): “and I cannot escape to the mountain,” beside Abraham, so that my merit not be remembered beside him (Genesis Rabbah 50:11).
From the expression of measure (*middah*); he prostrated himself upon him.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: for it was so, when Jezebel cut off
1 Kings.english_translation: It comes to tell how Obadiah feared the LORD.
And fifty men in another cave.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: that we lose not all the beasts
1 Kings.english_translation: That all our beasts not be cut off from us.
As he explains and says: “and the spirit of the LORD shall carry thee whither I know not.”
That the people cannot find you.
The two thoughts: that you do not understand how to decide who is God.
God, go after him.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And the people answered him not a word
1 Kings.english_translation: For they did not know how to distinguish.

For it was slipping away from them, so that it should not draw near to idolatry, and it fled under the wings of Elijah. He said to it: Go; through both of you the place will be sanctified (Numbers Rabbah 23:9; Yalkut Shimoni §214).

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And they danced in halting wise about the altar which was made
1 Kings.english_translation: Jonathan translated: *ve-ishtatu* — they were dancing in their manner at their altars.
Like *va-yifse'u* (“and they stepped”).
(Targum:) “for you say he is a fear (*dachala*).”
1 Kings.translator_note: The Aramaic *dachala* is left untranslated; the sense in this Targum is not clear to me. Audit 4: the Aramaic quotation was checked against Targum Jonathan/the Ketuvim Targum (Mikraot Gedolot, Sefaria) at 1KI 18:27 and reads as quoted; the meaning of the unclear word, if noted above, is still unresolved.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: either he is musing, or he is gone aside
1 Kings.english_translation: Perhaps he has a matter with his counsellors now, or he is pursuing and overtaking in war now.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: or he is in a journey
1 Kings.english_translation: To the toilet.
An expression of scratching with an instrument, and so was their custom.
(Targum:) “and they raved.”

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And he repaired the altar of the LORD that was thrown down
1 Kings.english_translation: He built an altar, and reminded Israel to have the altar of the LORD come up in their hearts and be fluent in their mouths, for it had been torn down and fallen and its name and mention had ceased from the mouths of all the ten tribes; so I heard its plain sense. And its Midrash I heard: that Saul built an altar on Mount Carmel, and this is what it says (1 Samuel 15:12): “Saul came to Carmel, and, behold, he is setting him up a monument,” and elsewhere (Genesis 33:20) it says: “And he erected there an altar”; and the kings of Israel tore down all the altars and high places in their land that had been made for the sake of Heaven; and Elijah built this altar of Saul’s, which had been torn down.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: the word of the LORD came, saying: ‘Israel shall be thy name.’
1 Kings.english_translation: Why is this said here? Because on the day that the Shekhinah was revealed to Jacob in Beth-el and called him Israel, on that very day He said to him: “a nation and a company of nations shall be of thee” — your sons are destined to be gathered like the other peoples, and to build an altar to burn offerings upon it in the time when the high places are forbidden, and I will accept it; in Genesis Rabbah (82:5).
1 Kings.translator_note: The Midrashic source is cited by chapter and verse in the printed text; the paraphrase is translated literally.

1 Kings.english_translation: *Fossé* in Old French.
1 Kings.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is פושאד״ו; Darmesteter (1909) glosses it “Un fossé” (a ditch); the OCR of the variants is garbled in my copy.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: as great as would contain two measures of seed
1 Kings.english_translation: Its width a place for two *se'ah*, a hundred by fifty, like the court of the Tabernacle.
1 Kings.translator_note: Rashi’s equation of the area with the Tabernacle court (100 × 50 cubits) is as printed.

1 Kings.english_translation: To enlarge the miracle.

Elisha poured on his hands, and his fingers became like springs, and the trench was filled; this is what is said (2 Kings 3:11): “Elisha the son of Shaphat, who poured water on the hands of Elijah”; and a miracle with water was done by his hands, and it is fitting that the miracle with water be done by his hands (Eliyahu Rabbah, chapter 17).
1 Kings.translator_note: The Midrashic source “Eliyahu Rabbah” is given as printed; the idea that the miracle was by Elisha’s hands is as printed.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and that I have done all these things at Thy word
1 Kings.english_translation: That I offered on a high place in the time when the high places were forbidden.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: Hear me, O LORD, hear me
1 Kings.english_translation: Answer me with fire, (and with water) answer me with rain; so Jonathan translated. And our Rabbis said (Berakhot 9b): Answer me with fire; answer me that they should not say it is an act of sorcery.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: that this people may know that Thou, LORD, art God
1 Kings.english_translation: And when You send me to inform them in the future, they will believe me, if today You answer me.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: for Thou didst turn their heart backward
1 Kings.english_translation: Thou gavest them a place to turn aside from after Thee, and it was in Thy hand to make their heart steadfast toward Thee (ibid., 31b). And an aggadic Midrash (Numbers Rabbah 18:12): If You do not answer me, I too shall be a denier and say, You turned their heart backward; and so Moses said (Numbers 16:29): “If these men die the common death of all men,” I too shall deny and say, The LORD hath not sent me to speak the Torah and the commandments; and so Micaiah said (below 22:28): “If thou return at all in peace, the LORD hath not spoken by me.”
1 Kings.translator_note: The Hebrew text of the first part is terse (*natata lahem makom*); it is translated literally. The second part is the printed Midrash.

1 Kings.english_translation: And not Baal is God.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and he bowed himself down upon the earth
1 Kings.english_translation: (Targum:) “and bent down to the earth,” to pray for the rains.
If thou seest a cloud rising from the sea.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: Make ready thy chariot, and get thee down
1 Kings.english_translation: Harness your chariots and go down from Mount Carmel to return to your house, lest the rain hinder you on the way.
While the messenger went, and while he harnessed the chariot, the heavens grew black.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And the hand of the LORD
1 Kings.english_translation: (Targum:) “a spirit of might from before the LORD clothed itself in strength” to run before the chariot on his feet, so that Ahab should not go alone, for he gave honour to the kingdom (Mekhilta; Yalkut Shimoni §217).
1 Kings.translator_note: The Targum, quoted in Aramaic in the printed text, is paraphrased here as printed.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and he girded up his loins
1 Kings.english_translation: Like *va-ye'zor*; and it has no parallel, and it too comes only to teach an expression of haste: he hurried like a mighty man.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: So let the gods do [to me]
1 Kings.english_translation: As thou didst to the prophets of Baal.
*Genévrier* in Old French.
1 Kings.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is ייניבר״א; Darmesteter (1909) reads *genévrier* (“Un genévrier,” a juniper).

1 Kings.english_translation: (Targum:) “Long enough for me; how long shall I be harried so?”
Coals; and so (Isaiah 6:6): “and in his hand a *ritzpah*”.
1 Kings.translator_note: JPS renders the word in Isaiah 6:6 as “a glowing stone”.

1 Kings.english_translation: It is the cleft of the rock (Exodus 33:22) in which Moses stood (see Megillah 19b).
Private high places made for the sake of Heaven, for the altar of the House of Election was in Jerusalem.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and a great and strong wind
1 Kings.english_translation: (Targum:) “a camp of angels of wind.”
(Targum:) “a camp of angels of quaking.”
(Targum:) “a camp of angels of fire.”

(Targum:) “a voice of those who praise in a whisper”; but of the prophets of the nations of the world He says (Job 4:16): “There was silence, and I heard a voice”; for them the silence was for praise. And I heard a voice coming from within the silence: *retentissement* in Old French; and one does not hear the voice itself.
1 Kings.translator_note:
The last clause (“one does not hear the voice itself”) is terse in the printed text and is translated literally.
Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is דטינטישמנ״ט; Darmesteter (1909) reads *retentissement* (“Une voix retentissante”).

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: he wrapped his face in his mantle
1 Kings.english_translation: (Targum:) “and covered his face,” and so it says (1 Samuel 21:10): “wrapped in a cloth.”

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: shalt thou anoint to be prophet in thy room
1 Kings.english_translation: I do not want your prophecy, since you teach accusation against my children.
We do not find that he killed anyone except forty-two children by means of the bears at Jericho (2 Kings 2:24).
1 Kings.translator_note: The printed text says “at Jericho”; in the verses cited (2 Kings 2:23–24) the episode takes place on the way up to Beth-el.

1 Kings.english_translation: From after me.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: for what have I done to thee
1 Kings.english_translation: That thou shouldest come after me.

He cooked the flesh for them. So Donash and Menachem explained, and so Jonathan translated it as two words (*bashil lehon*). And I say: there is no need to divide it into two words; and what is “*bashlam* the flesh”? He cooked for the two oxen their flesh, for a yoke is not less than two.
1 Kings.translator_note: The reference to “Donash” is Dunash ben Labrat; the argument about dividing the word is translated literally.

1 Kings.english_translation: Out of great joy he made a feast.
“For I sent unto thee,” etc., “thou shalt deliver me.” I knew that you would give them to me, but I decree something else upon you.
1 Kings.translator_note: The Hebrew lemma is empty in the printed text; the comment begins with the words of the verse.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: whatsoever is pleasant in thine eyes, they shall put it in their hand, and take it away
1 Kings.english_translation: But are not all the first things desirable things? What then is “the desire of thine eyes”? A desirable thing out of desirable things: this is the Torah scroll, of which it is said (Psalm 19:11): “More to be desired are they than gold, yea, than much fine gold.” Ahab said in his heart: This is a great thing that he seeks; it is not mine alone, it is the elders of Israel’s; therefore “then the king of Israel called all the elders of the land” (Midrash Tanchuma, *Shemot* 29; Sanhedrin 102b). Even though they were serving idols, they honoured the Torah.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: if the dust of Samaria shall suffice for handfuls for all the people that follow me
1 Kings.english_translation: (Targum:) “to take in the soles of the feet of the people who are with me” — dust that clings to the soles of the feet.

An expression of the treading of the sole of the foot, and so (Numbers 22:24) “in a path (*mish'ol*) between the vineyards”; and so (Isaiah 40:12) “Who hath measured the waters in the hollow (*she'alo*) of his hand,” for He trod in the Red Sea, as it is said (Habakkuk 3:15): “Thou hast trodden the sea with Thy horses.”
1 Kings.translator_note: Rashi’s connection of *she'alim* with treading, and the link to Habakkuk 3:15, are translated as printed.

1 Kings.english_translation: If there be enough.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: Let not him that girdeth on his armour boast himself as he that putteth it off
1 Kings.english_translation: The Targum: “Say to him: Let him not boast who hurries and goes down to battle like a man who has won and come up from it.” “Let not him that girdeth on” his sword to go down to war boast, for he does not know whether he will conquer or not.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: as he that putteth it off
1 Kings.english_translation: He who has ungirded his sword, who has already come up from the battle and conquered; so your lord should not boast of what is in the future.
The siege-implements against the city.
He is Micaiah the son of Imlah (*Seder Olam*).

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: By the young men of the princes of the provinces
1 Kings.english_translation: They are the sons of the hostages, for all the princes of the other nations gave their sons into his hand as sureties that they would not rebel against him.
Who will set in order to command it.
Go out thou first, and so thou wilt put him to death (“and now sound the alarm” — other books do not have it).
I say: they are those of whom it was said above (19:18): “all the knees which have not bowed unto Baal,” seven thousand.
That they made for themselves against the sun.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: at the return of the year
1 Kings.english_translation: (Targum:) “at the end of the year.”

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and put governors in their room
1 Kings.english_translation: Since they will not be from an exalted family, they will take care to strengthen themselves in order to find favour.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and surely we shall be stronger than they
1 Kings.english_translation: That is: and thou wilt see if we are not stronger than they.
They provisioned themselves for war with supplies of food: instruments of arms and all the needs of war.
They were provided for.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: like two little flocks of kids
1 Kings.english_translation: Gatherings of goats; and it has no parallel; and Menachem connected it with an expression of uncovering, like (Genesis 30:37) “the white of the peeled (*machsof*) ”; (Isaiah 47:2) “uncover the train (*chasfi shovel*)”; and an expression of uncovering applies to flocks of goats, like (Song of Songs 4:1) “that trail down from mount Gilead” (*she-galshu*), when they come down from the mountain, the mountain is uncovered.
1 Kings.translator_note: The wording of the citations is as printed; the explanation of the image is translated literally.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: spoke unto the king of Israel, and said
1 Kings.english_translation: Rabbi Johanan said: In every place where it says “and he said … and he said,” it needs expounding. The first saying: He said to him, “I will deliver all this great multitude into thy hand”; the second saying: If Ben-hadad falls into thy hand, do not have pity on him; therefore when he pitied him he said to him (below, verse 42): “Because thou hast let go out of thy hand the man whom I had devoted to destruction,” etc. (Jerusalem Talmud, Sanhedrin 11:5).
1 Kings.translator_note: The Hebrew lemma gives “and he said to the king of Israel and he said, etc.”; the quotation of verse 42 is abridged as printed.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: Now the men took it for a sign, and hastened to catch it from him
1 Kings.english_translation: *Yenachashu* is an expression of one who divines (*menachesh*): they said, since words of peace fell from his mouth even unintentionally, it is a good omen; and they hastened to take hold of the matter.

An expression of finality: they cut the matter off from his mouth, so he could not retract; and the *he* of *ha-mimmennu* leans in the Masorah to the two words, as if it were written *va-yachlitu-ha mimmennu*, if the word came out of him with intent of heart.
1 Kings.translator_note: The remark about the Masorah and the letter *he* is technical and translated as printed.

1 Kings.english_translation: Ben-hadad: The cities which my father took from thy father Omri I will restore to thee.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and thou shalt make streets for thee in Damascus
1 Kings.english_translation: And thou shalt be ruler in it, and it is the head of my kingdom.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: as my father made in Samaria
1 Kings.english_translation: Your city, against your will; and he was saying all this out of fear. Ahab said to him: And I, with this covenant, shall send thee away.

This sign is bad for Ahab, for the prophet told him by the word of the Almighty to smite Ben-hadad and he did not smite him; and this one too, to whom the prophet said by the word of the LORD “smite me,” and he did not smite him: as He took vengeance on this one, so He will take vengeance on Ahab.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: by the word of the LORD
1 Kings.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He, said that you should smite me.
A blow of bruising (*chaburah*).

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and disguised himself with his headband over his eyes
1 Kings.english_translation: He changed his headband so that they would not recognize him; every change of garments is an expression of *chippus* (“disguise”).
Jonathan translated: *be-ma'afra*, which is a kerchief.
From the way to me.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and brought a man unto me
1 Kings.english_translation: A captive from the war.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: if by any means he be missing
1 Kings.english_translation: If he escapes; an expression of (Numbers 31:49) “and there lacketh not one man of us” (*lo nifkad*), an expression of lack.
He fled away.
Either a life, or a talent of silver.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: the man whom I had devoted to destruction
1 Kings.english_translation: A man of My war; an expression of *cherem*, and the expression *cherem* applies in war, and so (Isaiah 34:5) “and upon the people of My ban shall it come down.” And an aggadic Midrash: How many snares and nets (*cheramim*) I spread for you until he fell into your hand.
(Targum:) “vexed and sad”: his spirit departed from him.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And it came to pass after these things
1 Kings.english_translation: Yet another to hasten his death.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: the worth of it in money
1 Kings.english_translation: This vineyard.
1 Kings.translator_note: The lemma in the printed text is “*mechir zeh*” (“this price”), but the comment explains “this vineyard.”

1 Kings.english_translation: The elders of Ashmai, the old men of Bahata.
1 Kings.translator_note: The place names are transliterated as printed (the Aramaic *sabei de-vehata*); they are not identified.

1 Kings.english_translation: And on a day of fast they are accustomed to examine the transgressions in their hands.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: Naboth did curse God and the king
1 Kings.english_translation: A euphemism for “curse”; and the Targum: *gadif Navot kadam Adonai u-malka lat* (“Naboth blasphemed before the LORD and cursed the king”).

Some of the Sages say: the property of those executed by the kingdom goes to the king; and some say: he was the son of his father’s brother, and he and his sons were killed, and it was proper for him to inherit him (Sanhedrin 48b).
Thou hast sold thyself to provoke thy Creator; *hitmakhrekha* is like (Deuteronomy 28:68) “and there you shall sell yourselves unto your enemies” (*ve-hitmakkartem*).
In the valley of Jezreel; *chel* is the Targum of “valley.”

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: But there was none like unto Ahab
1 Kings.english_translation: Scripture testifies of him that there was none like him among the kings, for Jeroboam and all who came after him served the calves out of fear that if the people went up to Jerusalem the kingdom would return to the house of David; and this one added Baal and the Asherah to provoke.
He was sold to idolatry. I saw in the Jerusalem Talmud (Sanhedrin 10:2): Hiel the Beth-elite was his best man, and every day he took his money and gave it to idol-worship.
1 Kings.translator_note: The Jerusalem Talmud reference is as printed; the sense of the second sentence is terse.

1 Kings.english_translation: Barefoot.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: I will not bring the evil
1 Kings.english_translation: The evil of his house I will not bring in his days; but the decree “the dogs shall lick his blood” cannot come in the days of his son, but upon him.
1 Kings.translator_note: The Hebrew lemma is empty in the printed text; the comment begins with the words of the verse.

1 Kings.english_translation: Since he sent Ben-hadad away.
Slack: *siamo pigri* in Old French.
1 Kings.translator_note: Old French(?) gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is סיאמ״ו פיגר״י. Darmesteter (1909) lists this passage (“Paresseur”) but the variants in my copy are garbled and I could not confirm the reading; I give the printed letters transliterated.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: Is there not here besides a prophet of the LORD
1 Kings.english_translation: I have a tradition: no two prophets prophesy in the same language, and these all say the same language (Sanhedrin 89a).
1 Kings.translator_note: The Hebrew lemma is empty in the printed text; the comment begins with the words of the verse.

1 Kings.english_translation: Because he said, “Because thou hast let go out of thy hand the man whom I had devoted to destruction,” etc.
He did not say it to him in the name of the LORD.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and the LORD will deliver it
1 Kings.english_translation: Would that He would deliver it into the hand of the king.

Thou alone wilt die in the battle, as it is said (below, verse 31): “Fight neither with small nor great, save only with the king of Israel.” And although it is said (above 20:42), “and thy people for his people,” the drop that came from that righteous man Micaiah, whom his fellow struck, smiting and wounding, was an atonement for all Israel. So it is explained in the Aggadah (Jerusalem Talmud, Sanhedrin 10:5).
1 Kings.translator_note: The link to the earlier verse 20:42 and the “drop” of blood are as printed; the logic is terse.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: on His right hand and on his left
1 Kings.english_translation: Is there a left above? Has it not been said (Psalm 118:16) “The right hand of the LORD is exalted; the right hand of the LORD doeth valiantly”; (Exodus 15:6) “Thy right hand, O LORD, glorious in power; Thy right hand, O LORD, dasheth in pieces the enemy”? But these are on the right and these on the left: those on the right argue merit, those on the left argue guilt (Midrash Tanchuma, *Shemot* 18).

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And there came forth the spirit
1 Kings.english_translation: The spirit of Naboth (Sanhedrin 89a).

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: Which way went the spirit of the LORD from me
1 Kings.english_translation: Which is the way it went; and this is an abbreviated verse; in Chronicles (2 Chronicles 18:23) it is written: “Which way went the spirit of the LORD from me,” etc.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: I will disguise myself, and go into the battle
1 Kings.english_translation: To disguise myself and go: I will disguise myself, I will change my royal garments so that they will not recognize me, for if they recognize me they will turn to me to fight.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: but put thou on thy robes
1 Kings.english_translation: That are upon you, for you are not the king of Israel but the king of Judah, and your people have no quarrel.
To the Holy One, blessed be He.
This was Naaman.
He did not know that he was the king of Israel.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: between the lower armour and the breastplate
1 Kings.english_translation: Between the *dvakim* and the *shirayon* — there are coats of mail made in scales, as it is said (1 Samuel 17:5) “and he was clothed with a coat of mail of scales”; and the scales fall upon the holes of the coat of mail and stop them up, and they are called *devakim*.
1 Kings.translator_note: The Hebrew lemma is empty in the printed text; the comment begins with the words of the verse.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: was stayed up in his chariot
1 Kings.english_translation: Strengthening himself and standing, so that Israel should not recognize his wound and flee; and the beginning of a fall is a test.
1 Kings.translator_note: The last clause (“the beginning of a fall is a test”) is terse in the printed text and is translated literally.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and the dogs licked up his blood
1 Kings.english_translation: And I say that Naboth was killed there, for the prophet said, “In the place where dogs licked the blood of Naboth,” etc.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: the harlots also washed themselves there
1 Kings.english_translation: And they washed the instruments of war there from the blood; so Jonathan translated. And our Rabbis said (Sanhedrin 39b): Ahab was cold, and Jezebel made for him a likeness of two harlots in his chariot.
Elephant’s tooth.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And Jehoshaphat made peace with the king of Israel
1 Kings.english_translation: Because there had been war between Asa his father and Baasa king of Israel, he was compelled to say so.
They practise adultery in public.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And there was no king in Edom: a deputy was king
1 Kings.english_translation: In the days of David the deputy was the king; and it is written here because in the days of Jehoram his son, who spoiled it, in his days Edom rebelled and made a king for themselves; but in the days of Jehoshaphat they were still subject to him.

Because he joined with Ahaziah in this, therefore they were broken; and so the prophet said to him in Chronicles (2 Chronicles 20:37): “Because thou hast joined thyself with Ahaziah, the LORD hath made a breach in thy works.”
1 Kings.translator_note: The Hebrew lemma is empty in the printed text; the comment begins with the words of the verse.

1 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat
1 Kings.english_translation: Some wonder at this verse, because it is said of Ahab that he reigned twenty-two years, and of Jehoshaphat that he began to reign in the fourth year of Ahab, so it turns out that the days of Ahab ended in the nineteenth year of Jehoshaphat, and here it says Ahaziah reigned in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat. But I examined and found, in the Chronicles of the kings of Israel, that he is not exact in counting their years: if he came to the throne at the end of a year, he counts it for him at the beginning, and does not count it for him elsewhere. Therefore I say that in the fourth year of Ahab, which was said of Jehoshaphat’s beginning, the first year of Ahab was not counted with him; and so you find in most of them; and also the year in which Jehoshaphat began was not counted in these seventeen.
1 Kings.translator_note: The chronology is translated as printed and has not been independently re-worked.

2 Kings.english_translation: *Grade* in Old French. I say they are accustomed to weave it crosswise from long and short boards, called *cantinel* in Old French, and make holes, holes, like a lattice, and it is called *prodne* in Old French. And I heard that *sevakhah* is *vis* in Old French, and in the German language *swindel-steig*, as I explained (1 Kings 6:8): “and they went up by winding stairs.”
2 Kings.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spellings are גראד״ה, קנטינל״י, פרדונ״י and ווי״ץ. Darmesteter (1909) glosses “Croisées à jour en forme de grille appelée” *prodne* (his variants *prodine*, *perozne*; he notes the reading is uncertain, perhaps modern *prône*), and “selon d’autres, c’est un escalier tournant, en français” *vis*. I could not match *grade* and *cantinel* in his collection.

2 Kings.english_translation: *Va-yichal*: an expression of sickness.
2 Kings.translator_note: The Hebrew lemma is empty in the printed text; the comment begins with the word of the verse.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And Jehoram began to reign in his stead
2 Kings.english_translation: He was his brother.
2 Kings.translator_note: The Hebrew lemma is empty in the printed text; the comment begins with the words of the verse.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: in the second year of Jehoram the son of Jehoshaphat
2 Kings.english_translation: Is it possible to say so? Did he not reign in the nineteenth year of Jehoshaphat, since Ahaziah reigned in the seventeenth and reigned two years; and just after it is written, “in the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat Jehoram began to reign,” and Jehoshaphat reigned twenty-five years before Jehoram his son reigned? But Jehoshaphat deserved to be killed at Ramoth-gilead, and as the reward of his crying out, seven years were hung up for him, and from that time he counts it for his son (Tosefta, Sotah 12:2).
2 Kings.translator_note: The chronology is intricate and is translated as printed (the printed text itself reads “twenty-five years before Jehoram his son reigned”).

2 Kings.english_translation: In a whirlwind spirit.
He wished to put him off out of humility, so that he should not see him being taken.
And not “our master”: it teaches that they were equal to Elijah (ibid., verse 5).
2 Kings.translator_note: The reference “ibid.” is as printed and the Talmudic source is not given.

2 Kings.english_translation: He wound it up, so that it would be convenient to strike with.
And not a real winding, but *koleit* (other books: *loket*), which they call *plier* in Old French.
2 Kings.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is פייגד״ו; Darmesteter (1909) lists this verse (“Il plia son manteau”) with variants like *coillier*, *cuillir*; I could not match the printed form.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: Thou hast asked a hard thing
2 Kings.english_translation: It is not possible to give you more than I have in my hand.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: if thou see me when I am taken from thee
2 Kings.english_translation: Then I shall be able to do more and more for you.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: it shall be so unto thee; but if not, it shall not be so
2 Kings.english_translation: For the power is not in my hand.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: My father, my father, the chariots of Israel and the horsemen thereof
2 Kings.english_translation: My master, my master, who by his prayer was better to Israel than chariots and horsemen (Targum).

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: Where is the LORD, the God of Elijah?
2 Kings.english_translation: For I was promised that a double portion of his spirit would rest on me.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and when he also had smitten the waters
2 Kings.english_translation: *Af hu*: in the Chapters of Rabbi Eliezer son of Rabbi Jose the Galilean: Great is the crossing of Elisha, double that of Elijah, for at first it was the merit of both of them, and now it is his merit alone.
2 Kings.translator_note: The source is cited in the printed text as “the Chapters of Rabbi Eliezer son of Rabbi Jose the Galilean”; the sense of “double” is as printed.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: lest peradventure the spirit of the LORD hath taken him up
2 Kings.english_translation: Is it possible? Yesterday they said to him, “Knowest thou that the LORD will take away thy master from thy head to-day?”, and now they do not know where he is! It teaches that from the day Elijah was hidden away, the law departed and the holy spirit was removed from the prophets, and the holy spirit was no longer abundant in Israel (ibid.).

He was ashamed before them, so that they should not say he does not want to receive his master’s face, because he took his greatness and does not want him to return. All this I saw in the Tosefta of Sotah (ibid.).

And because of the water the land bereaves its inhabitants, to bury them; if so, what is “the situation of the city is pleasant”? From here they said: the grace of a place is upon its inhabitants (Sotah 47a).
2 Kings.translator_note: “Bereaves its inhabitants, to bury them” is translated literally from the Hebrew and is terse.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: unto the spring of the waters
2 Kings.english_translation: From which they were flowing.
But is not salt a thing that spoils water? Rather, a miracle within a miracle.
Who were shaken free (*menu'arin*) of the commandments.

Go up from here, for the bald one has bald-ed (*hikreach*) the place for us; for until now we used to be paid to bring sweet water from afar, and make a living by it, and since he made it sweet their livelihood is lost. So it is explained in Sotah (46b).

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And he looked behind him and saw them
2 Kings.english_translation: He saw that there was not in them, nor in their seed, any moisture of goodness (ibid.).

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: Now Jehoram the son of Ahab
2 Kings.english_translation: This section too was written here in order to tell of the miracle of Mesha king of Moab, which was done through Elisha; for eight miracles are counted for Elijah and sixteen for Elisha, to fulfil “a double portion of thy spirit be upon me,” and he wrote them all side by side. So I saw in the Thirty-two Rules of Rabbi Eliezer the son of Rabbi Jose the Galilean; and the crossing of the Jordan by Elisha is double that of Elijah.
2 Kings.translator_note: The source is cited in the printed text as “the Thirty-two Rules of Rabbi Eliezer, son of Rabbi Jose the Galilean.”

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: but not like his father, and like his mother
2 Kings.english_translation: For they added Baal, to provoke.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: Nevertheless he cleaved unto the sins of Jeroboam
2 Kings.english_translation: And so all the kings of Israel, out of worry that the kingdom would return to the house of David if they went up on pilgrimage; therefore they served the calves.
A master of flocks.
2 Kings.translator_note: The comment translates *noked* by an Aramaic phrase meaning “owner of sheep-folds.”

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and of a hundred thousand rams
2 Kings.english_translation: The rams of the flock, with their wool.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: The way of the wilderness of Edom
2 Kings.english_translation: For the king of Edom also will go with us.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: to deliver them into the hand of Moab
2 Kings.english_translation: That they should die of thirst.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: who poured water on the hands of Elijah
2 Kings.english_translation: On Mount Carmel; and by his pouring his fingers became like springs of water, until the trench was filled; and it is fitting that a miracle with water be done for us by his hand (Yalkut Shimoni §214).

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: Nay; for the LORD hath called these three kings together
2 Kings.english_translation: (Targum:) “Pray, do not remember that wicked one’s iniquities; pray for mercy for us, for the LORD is ready,” etc.
Because of the anger the Shekhinah departed from him.
Pits full of water.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And this is but a light thing
2 Kings.english_translation: And this miracle too is light and small in the eyes of the LORD, and He added to do you another wonder: and He will deliver Moab into your hand.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and shall fell every good tree
2 Kings.english_translation: Although it is said (Deuteronomy 20:19) “thou shalt not destroy the trees thereof,” here He permitted it to you, for it is a despised and contemptible nation before Him; and so it says (Deuteronomy 23:7) “Thou shalt not seek their peace nor their prosperity” — these are their good trees.
A sown field: *komici* in Old French.
2 Kings.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is קומצ״י; Darmesteter (1909) lists this verse (“Tout champ fertile”, “every fertile field”), but the variants in my copy are garbled and I could not confirm the reading.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: about the time of making the offering
2 Kings.english_translation: The waters began to descend from heaven in the morning in the land of Edom, and at the time of the offering they come flowing and come to that brook, because it was said, “Ye shall not see wind, neither shall ye see rain”; in the Midrash of Rabbi Tanchuma.
On the frontier, which is called *marche*.
2 Kings.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is מרק״א; Darmesteter (1909) reads *marche* (“Sur la frontière”, on the border).

2 Kings.english_translation: So is the nature of water: when the sun shines on it in the morning it turns red.
From afar; and they had never seen water in that wadi, therefore they thought it was blood.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And they beat down the cities
2 Kings.english_translation: They were tearing down.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: they cast every man his stone
2 Kings.english_translation: They would take the stones from the walls, until he left all the stones of the walls in the wall, to stand on their potsherd, which is the clay; that is, there was no longer a stone in the wall; and after this “the slingers encompassed it and smote it” — what was left in the portion, so that the wall was not broken, and they brought it down.
2 Kings.translator_note: The Hebrew is terse and elliptical at the end; translated literally.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: Then he took his eldest son
2 Kings.english_translation: In the Pesikta of the section of *Shekalim* it is expounded: that he asked his servants what is the nature of this nation for whom such miracles are done; they said to him: Their father Abraham had an only son, and the Holy One said to him, “Offer him before Me,” and he wished to offer him to the Holy One. He said to them: I too have a first-born son; I will go and offer him to idolatry.
Lacking a *vav*, for he was a worshipper of the sun (*chammah*).
2 Kings.translator_note: The comment plays on the written form (*ha-chomah* / *ha-chammah*); the text of the verse has “upon the wall” and the pun is translated as printed.

2 Kings.english_translation: For their sins were remembered, for they too were worshipping idols, and were not worthy of a miracle.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: of the wives of the sons of the prophets
2 Kings.english_translation: She was the wife of Obadiah. Everywhere in Scripture “sons of the prophets” — its Targum is “disciples of the prophets.”

He is Jehoram the son of Ahab, who lent to him at interest what he had spent to feed the prophets in the days of his father, in the Midrash of Rabbi Tanchuma; therefore it is said (below 9:24): “and smote Joram between his arms,” for he had stretched out his arms to take interest.
2 Kings.translator_note: The connection with 2 Kings 9:24 follows the printed text.

2 Kings.english_translation: The measure of an anointing of oil; and the *alef* in the word belongs to the root, like the *alef* of (Job 13:17) *ve-achvati be-oznekhem* and the *alef* of (Ezekiel 21:20) *avchat cherev*.
2 Kings.translator_note: Rashi’s examples from Job and Ezekiel are left in transliteration because JPS does not render the word he is comparing.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And thou shalt go in, and shut the door
2 Kings.english_translation: The honour of the miracle is to come in secret.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and thou shalt set aside that which is full
2 Kings.english_translation: From before thee, and thou shalt place another vessel in its place to fill it, and the flask of oil thou shalt not move from its place, for the Holy One makes it like a spring, and the way of a spring is not to move from its place; I heard an aggadic Midrash.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: they brought the vessels to her
2 Kings.english_translation: The vessels.
From coming further; and an aggadic Midrash (in Genesis Rabbah 35:3): the price of oil became dear.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: Then she came and told the man of God
2 Kings.english_translation: She came to take advice whether to sell or to wait until it became dearer. He said to her: Go, sell, for there is enough for all your creditors, and to live, thou and thy sons, on the rest, until the dead live.
Important; and I saw in the Chapters of Rabbi Eliezer (chapter 33): she was the sister of Abishag the Shunammite.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And so it was, that as oft as he passed by
2 Kings.english_translation: In that city, he would turn aside to her house to eat bread.
An expression of the present: he used to turn aside there.
For she never saw a fly on his table, and *keri* on his sheet (Berakhot 10b).
2 Kings.translator_note: The printed text reads *keri* as a euphemism for emission; translated as transliterated.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And it fell on a day
2 Kings.english_translation: And it was one day.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: thou hast been careful for us
2 Kings.english_translation: For our sake.
To set this business to your heart, like (Isaiah 66:2) “and trembleth at My word,” careful that the thing be done, and takes it to heart.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: what is to be done for thee?
2 Kings.english_translation: What do you need us to do for you, since for our sake you took all this trouble?
Among my relatives; no one harms me; I need neither the king nor the captain of the host.
Elisha to Gehazi.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: What then is to be done for her?
2 Kings.english_translation: In return for this kindness.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: At this season, when the time cometh round
2 Kings.english_translation: As you are alive today and in peace, so you will be alive at this season, and embracing a son.
Do not say “embracing a son”; what is his embrace to me if in the end I shall bury him? And this is what she said to him when he died: “Did I not say, Do not deceive me?”

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: do not lie unto thy handmaid
2 Kings.english_translation: Do not show me a thing that will cease; it is in your power to ask for mercy and a son will be given to me; but I ask of you, give me only a son who will live.
Like (Isaiah 58:11) “whose waters fail not.”
2 Kings.translator_note: The printed reference is “(ibid. 50:11)”, which appears to be a slip for Isaiah 58:11.

2 Kings.english_translation: At that time, when she was alive and in peace; and therefore it is pointed *ka-et*.
I am sick in my head.
His father to one of the servants: Carry him to his mother.
Hurry.
Do not delay the riding for me.
This is an abbreviated verse, for it should have written, “and he asked her, and she said: It is well.”
To you: Do not deceive your handmaid.
Do not lead me astray with a thing of error.

Do not greet him; and all this so that he not multiply words and he be asked, Where are you going, and he would say, To revive the dead; and it is not honour for the miracle that the one who came through it should boast; but he did not do so, but to everyone who asked he said, My master sent me to revive the dead (Tanchuma, *Beshalach* 26; Jerusalem Talmud, Sanhedrin 10:2).
2 Kings.translator_note: The Midrashic references are given as printed; the logic of the first part is terse.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and he stretched himself upon him
2 Kings.english_translation: Jonathan translated: *ve-alahi alohi*, which is an expression of weariness; there is a parallel in the baraita of *Ha'azinu* and in the Sifre; and Menachem explained: *va-yigehar*, the meaning of the word is according to its sense: he prostrated himself on him.
2 Kings.translator_note: The Aramaic is left in transliteration; Rashi’s account of Jonathan’s word is as printed.

2 Kings.english_translation: He sneezed.
Put it on the stove.
A cooked dish.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: for the sons of the prophets
2 Kings.english_translation: For the disciples of the prophets.
A seed which they call *orga* (rocket), which lights up the eyes; and some interpret *orot* as vegetables, like (Isaiah 18:4) “like clear heat upon light” (*alei or*).
2 Kings.translator_note: Old French/Aramaic gloss: Darmesteter (1909) lists the word *oroga* for this verse (“De la roquette”, modern *roquette*, rocket).

2 Kings.english_translation: (Targum:) *gufna be-chakla*.

There grew from it wild gourds (*peku'ot sadeh*), called *bulaiç* in Old French, a deadly poison. And in the name of Rabbi Menachem I heard: “and he gathered” from it, apart from it (*bilado*), wild gourds.
2 Kings.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is בוליי״ן; Darmesteter (1909) reads *bulaiç* (“Plante vénéneuse”, a poisonous plant).

2 Kings.english_translation: He split them open.
The name of a district; and Jonathan translated: “from the land of the south.” *Ba'al* is an expression of “plain,” and it is frequent in Scripture.
At Passover, when the grain ripens early.
In his garment.
To the disciples whom he supported.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: How should I set this before
2 Kings.english_translation: Each and every loaf.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: Now Naaman, captain of the host
2 Kings.english_translation: The miracles done by Elisha, in order.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: the LORD had given victory unto Aram
2 Kings.english_translation: He drew a bow at a venture and killed Ahab (Yalkut Shimoni §222).
When a hundred or two hundred go out by themselves to plunder what they find, it is called a *gedud*.
A little girl, from the city of Naaron (Chullin 5a).
*Ve-havat meshamsha kadam atat Na'aman* (Targum).

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: Would that my lord were with the prophet
2 Kings.english_translation: An expression of (Exodus 32:11) “and Moses besought”: all who pray for him would be with him; that the miracle should come before the prophet.
2 Kings.translator_note: The sense of the verb in this explanation is terse in the printed text.

2 Kings.english_translation: *Sohaydemant* in Old French, that is, this is a request that he needs.
2 Kings.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is שוהיידמנ״ס; Darmesteter (1909) reads *sohaydemant* (“Plût au ciel”, a formula of wish; modern *souhait*).

2 Kings.english_translation: Naaman.
The king of Aram.
A gift for the prophet.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and six thousand pieces of gold
2 Kings.english_translation: Gold coins.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: saying: ‘And now when this letter is come unto thee
2 Kings.english_translation: The letter said to him: “And now when this letter is come,” etc.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: that thou mayest recover him of his leprosy
2 Kings.english_translation: “Gathering” of a leper is an expression of his healing, for when he is healed he is gathered among people, and in his sickness all separate from him.
The *he* is pointed with a *patach*, to teach that it is an expression of astonishment.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: he seeketh an occasion against me
2 Kings.english_translation: Seeks a pretext to provoke me.
An expression of pretexts for charges (Deuteronomy 22:14).
I thought: The prophet will come out to me and speak with me and see the sickness.
The leprosy.
Like “my lord.”

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: wouldest thou not have done it?
2 Kings.english_translation: Would you not do it, even if he said a troublesome thing to you?
It is an argument from the lesser to the greater: he told you an easy thing: Wash, and be clean.
A gift of greeting upon receiving, which a disciple or servant asks in greeting the master: *salud* in Old French.
2 Kings.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is שולד״ו; Darmesteter (1909) reads *salud* (“Un salut”, a greeting).

2 Kings.english_translation: Because the price of idolatry is mixed in it.
An expression of request, an expression of “would that.”
Of this earth, from the Land of Israel, which is holy, two mules’ burden, and I shall carry it to my city and make it into an altar.
The name of an idol.
Against my will, when my master bows and he is leaning on my hand.
A name of a measure of land, like (Isaiah 5:10) “ten acres of vineyard” (*tzimdei kerem*): *arpent* in Old French.
2 Kings.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is ארפינ״ט; Darmesteter (1909) reads *arpent* (“Un arpent de terre”).

2 Kings.english_translation: Lacking an *alef*, because this taking was a blemish (*mum*).
2 Kings.translator_note: The written form of the word in the verse does not match the claim in an obvious way; the comment is translated as printed.

2 Kings.english_translation: *Ve-itrakhin* (Targum).
Be satisfied with him who sent thee.

Kinds of garments and kerchiefs, like (Isaiah 3:22) “the kerchiefs and the *charitim*”; so Menachem connected it. But Jonathan translated this *paldesin*, and the one in the book of Isaiah he translated *machkaya*; and the interpreters say: “in two bags” — in two long purses, *brides* in Old French.
2 Kings.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is פירדיי״ש; Darmesteter (1909) lists this verse (“Bourses longues”, long purses) and reads *brides* (the printed spelling is close to his variants).

2 Kings.english_translation: Of Naaman.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and they bore them before him
2 Kings.english_translation: Before Gehazi.
Jonathan translated: *le-atar kasi*.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: he took them from their hand
2 Kings.english_translation: From the hand of the two servants of Naaman.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and he let the men go
2 Kings.english_translation: So that Elisha should not see them.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: Is it a time to receive money
2 Kings.english_translation: To become rich, and to receive from him garments and olives, etc.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And the sons of the prophets said unto Elisha
2 Kings.english_translation: The miracles done for him, in order. Our Rabbis said (Sotah 47a): from here that Gehazi used to push the disciples away from before him; and when he was driven out, many disciples came, and the place was crowded by them.
Be willing.
The iron head.
I borrowed it, and I have nothing with which to pay.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and made the iron to swim
2 Kings.english_translation: It floated on the water.
Hidden and concealed; *peloni* is an expression of (Deuteronomy 17:8): “If there be too hard (*yippale*) for thee.”
*Ki yippale* — be hidden; *almoni*: without a name, for he did not wish it to be revealed.
2 Kings.translator_note: The Hebrew lemma is empty in the printed text.

2 Kings.english_translation: A place of ambush, and I will lie in wait for the king of Israel or his bands passing to plunder in my land by way of that place.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: that thou pass not such a place
2 Kings.english_translation: From going there.
Encamping.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And the king of Israel sent
2 Kings.english_translation: He used to send and see whether it was true.
That the man of God had warned him of passing there.
He did so for him, but many times.
Who reveals his secret?
Where is he?
Those that help us.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: Elisha prayed unto the LORD, and said
2 Kings.english_translation: For the curse he did not mention the Name, but for the opening of the eyes he mentioned the Name, for both, for the servant’s and for the band’s.
A sickness of amazement: he sees and does not know what he sees.
In which the prophet is; and he told them the truth, for he had already left it.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: hast thou taken captive with thy sword and with thy bow those whom thou wouldest smite?
2 Kings.english_translation: Is it your way to kill those whom you bring as captives (and take captive)?
An expression of preparing a meal.
The dung that flows from doves.
He thought she was asking for food.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and she hath hid her son
2 Kings.english_translation: He died, and she wants to eat him by herself (Yalkut Shimoni §231).
Through the rent, at the sackcloth under his garments.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: if the head of Elisha the son of Shaphat shall stand on him
2 Kings.english_translation: Because he has the power to ask for mercy.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and the king sent a man from before him
2 Kings.english_translation: The king sent to kill him, and before that messenger came to Elisha, he was revealed to him by the holy spirit, and he said to the elders: Behold, the messenger is coming down to him and the king behind him.
The king.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: Behold, this evil is of the LORD
2 Kings.english_translation: This is one of the curses that was cursed through Moses (Deuteronomy 28:53): “and thou shalt eat the fruit of thy body, in the siege and in the straitness,” etc.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: why should I wait for the LORD any longer?
2 Kings.english_translation: To save; will it not avail?

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: Now there were four leprous men
2 Kings.english_translation: “And four men”: Gehazi and his sons (Sotah 47a).
2 Kings.translator_note: The Hebrew lemma is empty in the printed text; the comment begins with the words of the verse.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: at the entrance of the gate
2 Kings.english_translation: As it is said (Leviticus 13:46): “he shall dwell alone; without the camp shall his dwelling be.”

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: had made the host of the Arameans to hear
2 Kings.english_translation: It seemed to them as though they heard.
We shall become liable to the kingdom.
As they had been, full from the beginning; they had not taken out what was inside them.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: They know that we are hungry
2 Kings.english_translation: And eager to go out to the plunder and to food.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: that remain, which are left in the city
2 Kings.english_translation: In the city, who did not die of hunger.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: behold, they are as all the multitude of Israel that are left in it
2 Kings.english_translation: If they say they are in danger, so that no one should kill them, behold, they are in this city in the danger of hunger like all the multitude of Israel that are left in it; and if they die, behold, they are like all the multitude of Israel who are consumed by hunger.
In their hurry to flee.
Yesterday, when he came to Elisha’s house.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: Now Elisha had spoken unto the woman
2 Kings.english_translation: This was seven years before.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: for the LORD hath called for a famine
2 Kings.english_translation: It is the famine that was in the days of Joel the son of Pethuel.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: for her house and for her land
2 Kings.english_translation: Which robbers had seized.
To bring Gehazi back in repentance (Sotah 47a).
He said this concerning Hazael, that he would live in place of Ben-hadad, to the kingship.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And he settled his countenance stedfastly upon him
2 Kings.english_translation: His sorrowful face, which wanted to weep, he kept firm, so as not to weep before Hazael, and set his heart to stand firm and restrain himself.
Like *boshesh* (“delayed”); and he could not restrain himself and wept.
An expression of bursting open the bowels, and the father of all of them (Isaiah 13:18): “and their bows shall dash the young men in pieces.”

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and rip up their women with child
2 Kings.english_translation: Their pregnant ones.
The Targum of Jonathan: *gunba*, and so (Judges 4:18) “and she covered him with a rug”: the Targum is *be-gunba*, and it is a garment.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and spread it on his face
2 Kings.english_translation: To cool himself.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And in the fifth year of Joram
2 Kings.english_translation: Jehoshaphat made Joram king during his own lifetime two years, when they returned from the war they had fought against the king of Moab; so it is taught in *Seder Olam*: in the fifth year of Jehoram, and Jehoshaphat in the fiftieth year, for a decree had been decreed upon Jehoshaphat to be killed at Ramoth-gilead, but on account of his crying out seven years were hung up for him.
2 Kings.translator_note: The chronology is translated as printed; the number “fiftieth year” is as printed.

2 Kings.english_translation: Dominion.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and made a king over themselves
2 Kings.english_translation: And from the days of David they had no king, as it is said (1 Kings 22:48): “And there was no king in Edom: a deputy was king”; (2 Samuel 8:14): “And he put garrisons in Edom.” Eight kings reigned in Edom before a king reigned over Israel, numbered in the book of Genesis (36:31–43); corresponding to them eight kings reigned in Israel: Ish-bosheth, and David, and Solomon, and Rehoboam, and Abijam, and Asa, and Jehoshaphat, and Jehoram, and there was no king of Edom. And what is written above, that the king of Edom went with Jehoram the son of Ahab and with Jehoshaphat to the war against the king of Moab, was not a complete king but a deputy, who too was called king, and as it is said (1 Kings 22:48): “And there was no king in Edom; a deputy was king,” the deputy was for them in place of a king.
2 Kings.translator_note: The count of eight kings in Israel (and of Edom’s kings) is as printed and has not been independently verified.

2 Kings.english_translation: Those near the border.

The inhabitants of Libnah rebelled and rebelled against the king, and I do not know from which nation they were, for Libnah is of the Land of Israel; and I say they were of the tribe of Judah, and rebelled against the king.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and was buried with his fathers in the city of David
2 Kings.english_translation: And in Chronicles (2 Chronicles 21:20) it says: “in the city of David, but not in the sepulchres of the kings.”
At that time when Jehoram was sick in Jezreel.
2 Kings.translator_note: The Hebrew lemma is “And Elisha the prophet called,” etc.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: one of the sons of the prophets
2 Kings.english_translation: It was Jonah the son of Amittai.
Every girding of the loins is an expression of urging on in valour, because he is sent for a matter of danger (that needs urging).

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: the young man, even the young man the prophet
2 Kings.english_translation: The servant of Elisha the prophet; so Jonathan translated: “and the boy, the disciple of the prophet, went.”

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: You know the man and what his talk was
2 Kings.english_translation: You know the man, that he is mad.
You are saying; you are hiding what he said to you.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: on the top of the stairs
2 Kings.english_translation: (Targum:) *al darag sha'aya*: a kind of steps made opposite the hours of the day, to know each and every hour when the shadow descends one hour. *Gerem* is *orlé* in Old French, an expression of a notch; and the *gerema* in the laws of slaughtering is from this expression: that it scratches and descends, and appears like a kind of bump above.
2 Kings.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is אורלי״ו. Darmesteter (1909) lists this verse (“Degrés du cadran”) with the reading *cran* (“notch”), which matches the sense given by Rashi; the printed spelling differs, so I give it in transliteration.

2 Kings.english_translation: That I should reign.
From Ramoth-gilead.
Like *le-hagid*.
A band.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: when I and thou rode together
2 Kings.english_translation: That I and you were riding together (other books: in pairs) after Ahab, on the day he killed Naboth.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: the LORD pronounced this burden against him
2 Kings.english_translation: By the hand of Elijah the prophet this burden, and we heard.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: Smite him also in the chariot
2 Kings.english_translation: And in Chronicles (2 Chronicles 22:9) it says: “And he sought Ahaziah, and they caught him — now he was hiding in Samaria — and they brought him to Jehu.” The verses must be reconciled: “And he fled by the way of the garden-house,” from Jezreel to Samaria, and Jehu pursued after him. But there is a difficulty in the matter, for Jehu’s rule was not in Samaria until the next day, as is explained in the matter (below 10:1): “And Jehu wrote letters and sent to Samaria,” etc. Our Rabbis explained in the Aggadah of Chelek (Sanhedrin 102b) “and he was hiding in Samaria”: that he used to cut out the Divine Names and write idolatry in their place. And according to their words one may say that this hiding was not on account of Jehu, but its meaning is: “and he sought Ahaziah, and they caught him” when he was fleeing by the way of the garden; and he was one who acted wickedly from the beginning, for he would come to Samaria and hide from the princes of Judah in order to do this abomination, because the inhabitants of Samaria were worshippers of idols and constellations; “and they brought him to Jehu”: the men of Jehu who pursued him, “and he said, Smite him in the chariot.”
2 Kings.translator_note: Rashi’s reconciliation of the verses is long and technical; it is translated literally.

2 Kings.english_translation: For there they brought him to him.
Struck by treachery.
2 Kings.translator_note: The phrase “struck by treachery” (*nikhlut*) is as printed.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And in the eleventh year of Joram the son of Ahab began Ahaziah to reign
2 Kings.english_translation: Above it says “in the twelfth year,” and of necessity his father Jehoram did not die until the twelfth year of Joram, for he began to reign in the fifth year of Joram and reigned eight years. And what is it that it says here, in the eleventh year? I say that he reigned during his father’s lifetime for a year, for he was smitten with evil diseases, as it is said in Chronicles (2 Chronicles 21:18): “And after all this the LORD smote him in his bowels with an incurable disease. And it came to pass, in process of time, after the end of two years, that his bowels fell out by reason of his sickness,” etc.; “and the inhabitants of Jerusalem made Ahaziah king.” Here it says “twenty and two years old was Ahaziah when he began to reign”, and in Chronicles (2 Chronicles 22:2) “forty and two years old was Ahaziah when he began to reign”; and all the days of Jehoram his father were forty years and no more, as it is said of him thirty-two years when he began to reign, and he reigned eight years; and how can a son be older than his father by two years? But twenty years before he was born, which is two years before his father was born, this decree was decreed: from the day Asa took the daughter of Omri for Jehoshaphat his son, a decree was decreed upon the house of David that it should come to an end together with the house of Ahab; and so it says (ibid., verse 7): “And the destruction of Ahaziah was of God, in that he went to Joram,” etc. So it is taught in *Seder Olam* and in the Tosefta of Sotah (12:3). But in all Scripture we do not find that Jehoshaphat married the daughter of Omri; but I found in Chronicles (2 Chronicles 18:1): “and he allied himself with Ahab by marriage,” and perhaps this is his sister whom he married; and he married her in the thirty-first year of Asa, as it is said (1 Kings 16:23): “In the thirty and first year of Asa king of Judah began Omri to reign.” And we learned in *Seder Olam* that he reigned a complete reign, for six years before he had reigned over half the people; and when Asa took his daughter for Jehoshaphat, Omri was elevated and they killed Tibni. Go and compute from the thirty-first year of Asa until the death of Ahaziah, and you will find them forty-two.
2 Kings.translator_note: This is a long chronological reconciliation; the numbers are translated as printed and have not been independently re-worked. The text itself speaks of Asa taking “the daughter of Omri” for Jehoshaphat, which is as printed.

2 Kings.english_translation: (Targum:) “and adorned her head,” so as to be comely in Jehu’s eyes, and he would marry her.
She wished to be at peace with him.
If you killed your master, this is nothing new, for Zimri too killed Elah the son of Baasa.
Who among you is to help me?
From the window to the ground.
Our Rabbis said (Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer 17): that she used to dance before bridegrooms with her hands and her feet and shaking her head.
Its Targum: “as manure.”

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: them that brought up [the sons of]Ahab
2 Kings.english_translation: Those who raised his sons.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and there are with you chariots and horses
2 Kings.english_translation: And there is strength in you to fight.
Joram and Ahaziah.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: Now the king’s sons, being seventy persons, were with the great men of the city
2 Kings.english_translation: He wrote all this in the letter, and I know their number: seventy persons, and they were with the great men of the city who were bringing them up.
2 Kings.translator_note: The Hebrew begins “All this he wrote in a book”; the sense that this is Jehu’s knowledge is as printed.

2 Kings.english_translation: Pots.
Piles, heaps: *monts* in Old French.
2 Kings.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is מונטי״ס; Darmesteter (1909) reads *moncéls* (“Tas”, heaps).

2 Kings.english_translation: All of you, in your own eyes, are righteous, and hold me to be wicked, for I killed the king; and now see: behold, I conspired against my master and killed him; who smote all these? I did not kill them; but from these you shall know then that the decree of the King is upon them, and he who kills them is righteous and fulfils the commandment of the Omnipresent.
(Targum:) The house of the shepherds’ assembly.
An expression of binding; a place of the gathering of shepherds.
Jezebel.
Jehu.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: Is thy heart right, as my heart is with thy heart?
2 Kings.english_translation: And whole in what I am doing, as my heart is whole with your heart.
And I shall hold on to it, and lift me up to you into the chariot.
With deceit, an expression of (Genesis 27:36): “and he hath supplanted me.”

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: Sanctify a solemn assembly for Baal
2 Kings.english_translation: Proclaim an assembly, that they be gathered into the house of Baal.
Jonathan translated: *le-dammena al kometria*. Chests and boxes, in which they wrap and store the ornaments of the worshippers of Baal.
2 Kings.translator_note: The Aramaic words are left in transliteration.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: his life shall be for the life of him
2 Kings.english_translation: The life of the guard in place of the life of the one who escaped.
(Targum:) *Ve-ramu rahatya u-gavraya ketilin*: they cast the slain, the worshippers of Baal.
2 Kings.translator_note: The Aramaic is transliterated; the rendering is literal.

2 Kings.english_translation: An expression of a privy, and so (Isaiah 36:12): “to eat their own dung” (*lechol et chorehem*).

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: Howbeit from the sins of Jeroboam
2 Kings.english_translation: Out of worry that the kingdom would return to the house of David, as Jeroboam feared.
By the hand of Jonah.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: thy sons of the fourth generation
2 Kings.english_translation: Four generations, in place of your having destroyed the house of Ahab, who reigned four generations: Omri, and Ahab, and Ahaziah, and Jehoram.
2 Kings.translator_note: The list is as printed in the Hebrew.

2 Kings.english_translation: Like (Genesis 27:46): “I am weary of my life.”

In the upper chamber of the house of the Holy of Holies, as it says (below verse 3): “And he was with her in the house of the LORD hid,” etc. Of him David said (Psalms 27:5): “For He concealeth me in His pavilion … He hideth me in the covert of His tent.” And Scripture calls it the “chamber of the beds” on account of (Song of Songs 1:13): “that lieth betwixt my breasts.” And this is what Rabbi Eliezer composed: “Shatter the chamber of the beds; the destruction of Your house shall atone for them.”
2 Kings.translator_note: The last line is a liturgical poem attributed to “Rabbi Eliezer” in the printed text; translated literally.

2 Kings.english_translation: Captains of hundreds of the mighty ones, and captains of hundreds of the runners; and the form is *Kari*, not *Kerim*, the name of a collective body of the mighty ones: *barnier* in Old French.
2 Kings.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is ברני״ר. Darmesteter (1909) lists this verse (“La noblesse”) with variants ברניד / ברנייר and derives it from Latin *baronatum*.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: he made a covenant with them
2 Kings.english_translation: That they would be at his help, to make the king’s son king.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: a third part of you, that come in on the sabbath
2 Kings.english_translation: The watches were renewed and came on the sabbath, the priestly and Levitical watches, one entering and one leaving; and he commanded the entering watch to divide into three parts: a third in the king’s house, to guard that no man stand against the king to kill him; and a third at the gate Sur. That is the eastern gate in the court, the gate of the *Sirah*.
2 Kings.translator_note: The name of the gate is transliterated as printed.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: at the gate behind the guard
2 Kings.english_translation: This too is one of the gates of the court, and Jonathan translated: *be-tar'a de-vatrohi tar'a rahatya*. And the gate of the runners is where they come from the king’s house to the Temple, as is said at the end of the passage; and that gate of the court after which is the gate of the runners, it is called in Chronicles (2 Chronicles 23:4) “the gate of the thresholds.”
2 Kings.translator_note: The printed reference is 2 Chronicles 23:4, where the text speaks of “the thresholds” (*ha-sippim*); the Aramaic is transliterated.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: shall keep the watch of the house
2 Kings.english_translation: This guard, *tzom*, concerns the first part, of which he said: “and they shall keep the watch of the king’s house.”
2 Kings.translator_note: The printed word צום is unclear (possibly a slip for צוה, “he commanded”); translated as printed.

2 Kings.english_translation: Guard it greatly, that you not turn aside your attention, an expression of despair (1 Samuel 27:1), that there be no despair in the matter; and the *mem* of *massach* is of the root.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: the other two parts of you
2 Kings.english_translation: Of which I said that they should be at the gate Sur and at the gate of the runners, and with them all those going out on the sabbath: all the men of the watch that goes out.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: shall keep the watch of the house of the LORD about the king
2 Kings.english_translation: That no harm come to him from within the house of the LORD; and all this was needed only the first sabbath, until Athaliah was put to death and her helpers fled from the city.

A foreign man who comes into the precinct called *sederot*, which is the place of the king’s entry from his house to the house of the LORD; and I do not know what the language of *sederot* is. And Jonathan translated: *sudarya*.

The Torah scroll, as it is written (Deuteronomy 17:19): “And it shall be with him, and he shall read therein all the days of his life.” And our Rabbis said (Avodah Zarah 44a): the crown is the testimony, for whoever is fit for kingship, it fits him, and whoever is not fit for kingship, it does not fit him.
It is the king’s standing place in the house of the LORD.
Rebellion, rebellion is here.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: Have her forth between the ranks
2 Kings.english_translation: From the Temple to the ranks; and bring her by the way of the house of the ranks to the king’s house, and do not let her go out by the exit of the court to the city, lest she find helpers and allies.
In her help.
To put to death with the sword.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: So they made way for her
2 Kings.english_translation: A place, *estance* in Old French.
