2 Kings.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is אשטנצ״א. Darmesteter (1909) glosses it “(On lui donna) de la place”; I give *estance* as the likely reading, not confirmed.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: between the LORD and the king and the people
2 Kings.english_translation: That the king and the people be after the LORD; and afterwards between the king and the people, that they be servants to the king.
Appointees to guard in the place of their watch properly, for Athaliah had annulled the order of the watches of the house.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: by the way of the gate of the guard
2 Kings.english_translation: To the king’s house.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: all his days wherein Jehoiada the priest instructed him
2 Kings.english_translation: But after Jehoiada died, then the princes of Judah came to prostrate before the king and made him a god. They said to him: One who enters the Holy of Holies for an hour is in danger of death, and you hid in it six years; you are worthy to be a god. Then the king listened to them (2 Chronicles 24:17; Exodus Rabbah 8:2).
2 Kings.translator_note: The Exodus Rabbah reference is as printed.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: in current money, the money of the persons for whom each man is rated
2 Kings.english_translation: There are two monies here: “current money,” which is the money of the shekels every year, of which it is said (Exodus 30:13): “every one that passeth among them that are numbered”; and a man who vows the valuation of persons: one who says, “My valuation is upon me.”

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: all the money that cometh into any man’s heart
2 Kings.english_translation: For example, one who says: Behold, upon me a maneh for the repair of the house.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: let the priests take it to them
2 Kings.english_translation: It shall be theirs, and they shall take upon themselves to strengthen the repair of the house from their own.
2 Kings.translator_note: The lemma is printed “להס”, a misprint for “להם”.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: from him that bestoweth it upon him
2 Kings.english_translation: From his acquaintance, who is familiar with him.
A breach and a crack in the wall.
Further; and do not strengthen the house from your own.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: deliver it for the breaches of the house
2 Kings.english_translation: If it be less, it will be less; and if it leave over, it will leave over.
In the court.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: on the right side as one cometh into the house of the LORD
2 Kings.english_translation: On the right of the coming of the men.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: the priests that kept the threshold
2 Kings.english_translation: The thresholds of the court, those appointed over the keys of the court, for Jonathan translated: *amarkelaya*. And the *amarkalim* were seven, for the seven gates of the court, in the Tosefta of Shekalim (2:15).
From day to day (continually): “when they saw that there was much money in the chest, that the king’s scribe came up,” etc.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: the money that was weighed out
2 Kings.english_translation: They would give that counted money, after it had been taken out of the chest and they had weighed it and counted it; they would give it through the treasurers who were appointed over the workers.
An expression of counting, like (Exodus 5:18): “shall you deliver the tale of bricks.”
The appointed.
An expression of expenditure, to hire carpenters.
They are the master-builders (*ardekhilin*), the stone craftsmen, whose fellows work according to their word, the chiefs of the craft.
2 Kings.translator_note: The word *ardekhilin* (“master-builders”) is rendered following the sense of the comment.

2 Kings.english_translation: Builders of the wall, disciples of the master-builders.
From the mountain.
And they are instruments of song.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: they reckoned not with the men
2 Kings.english_translation: The *amarkalim* did not come to a reckoning with the men, the treasurers, through whom the *amarkalim* gave the money continually, to give it to the workers, because they were not suspect in their eyes, for they acted in good faith.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: The forfeit money, and the sin money
2 Kings.english_translation: One who sets aside money for his sin-offering and for his guilt-offering, and bought the animal, and some of the money remained.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: was not brought into the house of the LORD
2 Kings.english_translation: For the repair of the house.

And they take from them summer burnt-offerings (*olot kayitz*) for the altar, the flesh for the burnt-offering and the hides theirs. So we learned in Temurah (23b): This is a Midrash that Jehoiada the priest expounded: all that comes from the surplus of a sin-offering and from the surplus of a guilt-offering, burnt-offerings are bought with it.
2 Kings.translator_note: The phrase *olot kayitz* is rendered literally as “summer burnt-offerings”; its precise sense (altar “summer-fruit” offerings) is not explained in the printed text.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: Then Hazael king of Aram went up
2 Kings.english_translation: After the death of Jehoiada, and Joash made himself a god.
In that place.
The name of a place.
The name of a place.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: Jozacar the son of Shimeath, and Jehozabad the son of Shomer
2 Kings.english_translation: It is written in Chronicles (2 Chronicles 24:26): “Shimeath the Ammonitess and Jehozabad the son of Shimrith the Moabitess.” Why did Scripture specify? To teach that the Holy One, blessed be He, punished him through men like himself: let Ammonites and Moabites, ungrateful, come — who denied the kindness of Abraham our father, who did for Lot when he fought with the kings to save him, and they hired Balaam to curse his sons — and He would punish Joash, who denied the kindness of Jehoiada and killed Zechariah his son, as is explained in Chronicles (ibid., verse 21). And this Midrash is in the Sifre.
2 Kings.translator_note: Rashi’s quotation of 2 Chronicles 24:26 is abbreviated (it omits “Zabad”).

2 Kings.english_translation: Joash the son of Jehoahaz, of whom it is said (below verse 19): “three times shalt thou smite Aram.”
2 Kings.translator_note: The printed quotation paraphrases verse 19 (JPS: “thou shalt smite Aram but thrice”).

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: In the thirty and seventh year of Joash king of Judah
2 Kings.english_translation: This verse is contradicted from two sides, and I have found no one to repair it: it should have said thirty-nine, for his father stood in the twenty-third year of Joash and reigned seventeen years, so he died in the thirty-ninth year of Joash. And furthermore, it is said below in the passage (14:1), “In the second year of Joash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel, Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah began to reign”; so Joash son of Jehoahaz stood in the fortieth year of Joash, which was his last year, and in the second year of Joash son of Jehoahaz Amaziah reigned. And even if you say that Amaziah reigned in the year of his father’s death, and Scripture called it the second year of Joash, you learn that Joash king of Israel did not reign until the thirty-ninth year of Joash king of Judah.
2 Kings.translator_note: The chronological arithmetic is translated exactly as printed; the passage is internally difficult and has not been independently checked. Audit 4 arithmetic check: a reign beginning in Joash’s twenty-third year and lasting seventeen years ends in the thirty-ninth year on inclusive counting, as Rashi says; this agrees with 2 Kings 13:1. Audit 5 source check: a passage with the same wording (5 consecutive words) is found in Seder Olam Rabbah 19.1 (Sefaria Hebrew text, labelled Public Domain). This is a wording match only; the translation was not changed.

2 Kings.english_translation: He was his son. And it is astonishing why these two verses were written here, since further on he goes on telling of the deeds of Joash, and returns and writes “And the rest of the acts of Joash,” etc., “and Joash slept with his fathers,” etc. And I say that they were written only to interrupt, so that the death of Elisha not be placed next to a verse of idolatry, to say “and he did that which was evil,” etc., “and Elisha was fallen sick,” etc.
Opposite the land of Aram, which is in the east, as it is said (Isaiah 9:11): “The Arameans on the east.”
*Shedei* and *shada* (Aramaic).
2 Kings.translator_note: The Aramaic equivalents of “shoot” and “he shot”, given without further comment.

2 Kings.english_translation: Elisha said: This arrow shall be a sign of victory for Israel.
The name of the city.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: Thou shouldest have smitten five or six times
2 Kings.english_translation: It was incumbent on you.
If you had done so, you would have smitten Aram five or six times, for it was as a sign of victory that I placed your hands upon the bow.
They were accustomed to come and plunder in the land.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: at the coming in of the year
2 Kings.english_translation: *Be-me'al shata* (Aramaic): at the return of the year, while the land is still full of grass and there is food for their cattle, which is the time when armies go out.
2 Kings.translator_note: The Aramaic phrase is transliterated; the sense follows the explanation in the comment.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: called the name of it Joktheel
2 Kings.english_translation: That it was for *kihuy shinayim*; as it is written in Chronicles (2 Chronicles 25:14): “Now it came to pass, after that Amaziah was come from the slaughter of the Edomites, that he brought the gods of the children of Seir, and set them up to be his gods, and prostrated himself before them,” etc. And the prophet rebuked him and said to him (ibid. verse 16): “I know that God hath determined to destroy thee.” And what is the counsel? That he advised him to provoke the king of Israel.
2 Kings.translator_note: The printed words לקיהוי שינים are unclear; I give them in transliteration and do not translate them (possibly a form related to “dulling of teeth”, *kehut shinayim*, but this is only a guess). The end of the quotation from Chronicles is abbreviated.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: Come, let us look one another in the face
2 Kings.english_translation: In war.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: The thistle that was in Lebanon
2 Kings.english_translation: Shechem the son of Hamor.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: sent to the cedar that was in Lebanon
2 Kings.english_translation: Jacob.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: there passed by the wild beasts
2 Kings.english_translation: The sons of Jacob came upon the slain; here too you come to speak a parable to me, and it is a parable of contempt, for he likened him to a thistle and himself to a cedar.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: wild beasts that were in Lebanon, and trod down the thistle
2 Kings.english_translation: Since you have become haughty, the bands of my armies shall trample you too.
Sons of the princes who were given in the king’s house as a pledge (*eravon*), that their fathers not rebel against him; and so Jonathan translated: *benei rabrevaya* (“sons of the nobles”).

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: lived after the death of Jehoash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel fifteen years
2 Kings.english_translation: All fifteen years Uzziah his son reigned in his lifetime, for so it is written in Chronicles (ibid. verse 27): “Now from the time that Amaziah did turn away from following the LORD.”

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: made a conspiracy against him in Jerusalem
2 Kings.english_translation: From when they heard what the prophet said: “for the LORD hath determined to destroy thee.”
There he was all fifteen years.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: after that the king slept with his fathers
2 Kings.english_translation: After the death of Amaziah his father. From here you learn that Uzziah reigned in the days of his father; and nevertheless Elath was not given into his hand until after his father’s death; for if he had not reigned in his father’s lifetime, why would it need to say “after that the king slept with his fathers”? And when you count the days of the Temple according to the years of the kings, if you do not subtract these fifteen years that were counted for Amaziah and for Uzziah, you will find that it stood four hundred and twenty-five.
2 Kings.translator_note: The figure of 425 years is as printed.

2 Kings.english_translation: From the hand of the kings of Aram.

He is the one who anointed Jehu, who said to him: “Thy sons of the fourth generation shall sit for thee.” But our Rabbis (Yevamot 91a) were exacting: (Jonah 3:1) “And the word of the LORD came unto Jonah the second time,” and not a third time, because he sought the honour of the son and did not seek the honour of the Father. And this verse was difficult for them, and they resolved it: “according to the word of the LORD which He spoke by the hand of Jonah” to Nineveh, and an evil decree was turned to good; so it was turned for Israel in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash, from the evil that was in it, “for the king of Aram had destroyed them, and made them like the dust in threshing,” and now it turned for them to good.
2 Kings.translator_note: The printed reference is “Yevamot 91a” (translated as printed, not checked). The quotation resembles 2 Kings 13:7 but is not cited there in the printed text.

2 Kings.english_translation: Very distressed, *contrarios* in Old French, like (Joshua 1:18): “that shall rebel against thy commandment”; (Deuteronomy 9:24): “You have been rebellious”; (Genesis 26:35): “And they were a bitterness of spirit.” And some interpret: *morah me'od*, very low (*yarod me'od*), an expression of (Exodus 15:1): “hath He cast into the sea.”
2 Kings.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is קונטריאי״ש; Darmesteter (1909) lists this verse (“Opprimé”) and reads *contrarios* (from Latin *contrariosum*). Reference notes: the printed references are Genesis 26:34 and Exodus 15:1; the wording “ותהיין מרת רוח” is Genesis 26:35 and “ירה בים” is Exodus 15:4.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: In the twenty and seventh year of Jeroboam king of Israel
2 Kings.english_translation: Is it possible to say so? Did not Uzziah and Jeroboam reign as one, as he explained nearby? Rather, what does the text mean to say “in the twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam Azariah reigned,” who reigned an afflicted reign? We learn that he was smitten with leprosy in the twenty-seventh year of his reign.
2 Kings.translator_note: The reasoning is terse; translated literally.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And the LORD smote the king
2 Kings.english_translation: It is explained in Chronicles (2 Chronicles 26:16–21) that he entered the Sanctuary to burn incense on the altar.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: dwelt in a house set apart
2 Kings.english_translation: He made himself a house in the cemetery, as you say (Psalms 88:6): “Set apart among the dead.” In the Jerusalem Talmud.
2 Kings.translator_note: The Hebrew “bi-Yerushalmi” is as printed.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: In the thirty and eighth year of Azariah king of Judah
2 Kings.english_translation: From here too one can learn that Azariah reigned, after Joash king of Israel died, fifteen years in the lifetime of Amaziah his father; for if he had not stood until his father died, it turns out that he did not stand until the fifteenth year of Jeroboam son of Joash; and Jeroboam reigned forty-one, so it turns out that Jeroboam died in the twenty-seventh year of Uzziah, and how can it say “in the thirty-eighth year”? Rather, of necessity, Uzziah and Jeroboam reigned together, only Jeroboam reigned in the lifetime of his father Jehoash three years; therefore it says “and Jeroboam sat upon his throne,” that he had already sat; and Uzziah stood after Joash died, and Jeroboam reigned a complete reign. And in *Seder Olam* I saw that Jeroboam reigned in his father’s lifetime one year, and I do not know whether it is a scribal corruption, for one cannot settle “in the thirty-eighth year of Azariah Zechariah reigned” except in this way.
2 Kings.translator_note: The chronological arithmetic is translated exactly as printed and has not been independently checked. Audit 5 source check: a passage with the same wording (6 consecutive words) is found in Seder Olam Rabbah 19.1 (Sefaria Hebrew text, labelled Public Domain). This is a wording match only; the translation was not changed.

2 Kings.english_translation: *U-mechehi kadam amma* (Aramaic), that is, before the eyes of the people.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And so it came to pass
2 Kings.english_translation: Not that his kingdom was worthy of continuing so long, but to fulfil the word of a king, as it is said (Isaiah 55:11): “So shall My word be that goeth forth out of My mouth,” etc.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: because they opened not to him
2 Kings.english_translation: The governor of the city did not open the city to him, to accept him as king over them.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: all the women therein that were with child
2 Kings.english_translation: The pregnant women who were in it, he split open.
A mighty man of his.
Every *Argov* is an expression for distinguished palaces, and so every *tarkhonin* in the Aramaic language: palaces distinguished for the kingship, in the great citadel that is next to the Argov.
2 Kings.translator_note: Rashi’s Aramaic term *tarkhonin* is left in transliteration; the sentence is terse in the printed text.

2 Kings.english_translation: One can say that a golden lion stood in that citadel.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: in the twentieth year of Jotham the son of Uzziah
2 Kings.english_translation: It should have said “in the fourth year of Ahaz,” for all the days of Jotham’s reign were sixteen years; but since Ahaz was wicked, Scripture wished to count them for Jotham in the grave and not for Ahaz in life. So it is in *Seder Olam*.
At the end of the days of Jotham.
To incite.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: carried the people of it captive to Kir
2 Kings.english_translation: The people that were in it he exiled to a province whose name is Kir.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: against the coming of king Ahaz
2 Kings.english_translation: Before the king came from Damascus.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And the brazen altar, which was before the LORD
2 Kings.english_translation: It is impossible to say the brazen altar that Moses made, for it was hidden away; and it is impossible to say the stone altar that Solomon made and which Scripture called (2 Chronicles 7:7) “the brazen altar,” for it is impossible to bring it near from corner to corner unless he demolished it; and we learned that the fire that came down in the days of Solomon did not depart from the altar until Manasseh came and removed it, for he demolished the altar, as we find in the Aggadah of Chelek (Zevachim 61b). I have nothing to explain this altar except as the basins and the stands of brass that were needed for the altar and were beside the holy altar; and when Ahaz made the altar for idolatry, he removed the laver and brought it near to another side, from the face of the house, so as not to interpose between the altar he had made and the house of the LORD, and he put it beside the holy altar to the north. And we find that our Rabbis explained something like it (Shabbat 55a): “And they went in, and stood beside the brazen altar” (Ezekiel 9:2) — was there a brazen altar? He said to them: Begin from the place where they say song before Me. Here they called an instrument of song made of brass an “altar.”
2 Kings.translator_note: References are as printed (“Aggadah of Chelek … Zevachim 61b”; Shabbat 55a). The Aramaic question “was there a brazen altar?” is translated literally.

2 Kings.english_translation: At intervals, when it arises in my heart to inspect it.
*Itztablaot* on which the stands are made, as is said (1 Kings 7:28): “And the work of the bases was on this manner: they had borders.”
2 Kings.translator_note: The word *itztablaot* is left in transliteration.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: the covered place for the sabbath
2 Kings.english_translation: A roof of a tent, made for shade, to sit under it in the court on the sabbath day.

That by which he used to come from his house to the house of the LORD by the outside route, he turned to a hidden place, on account of the king of Assyria, lest he covet those vessels; and the entry too he turned, lest he need to hide and flee in secret.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: In the twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah
2 Kings.english_translation: It is impossible to say that Hoshea reigned in the twelfth year of Ahaz, for in the fourth year of Ahaz he killed Pekah and reigned in his place, and when you examine the years of Pekah you will find so. And it is also impossible to say that he reigned only nine years, for he reigned from the fourth year of Ahaz until the sixth year of Hezekiah, in which Samaria was captured, which is more than sixteen years; and why does it say nine years? From when he rebelled against the king of Assyria; so it is taught in *Seder Olam*. And it is impossible to say that in the twelfth year of Ahaz he began to rebel, for then you would find the two years of his rebellion five years in the days of Ahaz and six years in the days of Hezekiah, which is eleven, and here it says nine. The twelfth year of Ahaz is mentioned only for the matter of the verse after it, “Against him came up Shalmaneser,” etc., for in the twelfth year of Ahaz Sennacherib came up against Hoshea, and exiled those across the Jordan; and so we learned in *Seder Olam*; and a verse is written in Chronicles (1 Chronicles 5:26): “And the God of Israel stirred up the spirit of Pul king of Assyria, and he carried them away, the Reubenites and the Gadites,” and it did not specify at what time, and here it specified that it was in the twelfth year of Ahaz. The ten tribes were exiled in three exiles: in the twentieth year of Pekah, as it is written above (15:29): “there came Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria and took Ijon and Dan,” etc., “all the land of Naphtali, and he carried them captive to Assyria”, and this was the fourth year of Ahaz; he waited eight years and came upon them, in the twelfth year of Ahaz, and exiled the Reubenites and the Gadites; and when Hoshea the son of Elah saw, he rebelled against him and sent messengers to So king of Egypt (below 17:4); he waited eight years, and came and besieged Samaria, and it was captured at the end of three years, and all of them were exiled. And this is what is said (Isaiah 8:23): “In the former time He lightened the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali” — He lightened even in the second, for he exiled only two tribes, but the last He made heavy, He swept away everything, like one who sweeps the house. And in any case, according to the reckoning that he wrote here, the number of the two years of his rebellion is nine years; he did not rebel against him until the fourteenth year of Ahaz, for Ahaz reigned sixteen; three years of Ahaz were the rebellion, and six years in the days of Hezekiah.
2 Kings.translator_note: This long chronological passage is translated exactly as printed and has not been independently re-worked. Notes: the printed text names “Sennacherib” where the verse speaks of Shalmaneser; the quotation of 2 Kings 15:29 reads “Ijon and Dan” (the verse itself reads “Ijon, and Abel-beth-maacah”); the quotation from 1 Chronicles 5:26 is abbreviated.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: yet not as the kings of Israel that were before him
2 Kings.english_translation: For he abolished the *pardisaot* that had been posted from the days of Jeroboam on the roads, to guard that Israel not go up on the pilgrimage; and he abolished them because the golden calves had already been exiled in the two exiles: in the first exile, “and he took Ijon and Dan,” he exiled the calf that was in Dan, and in the second, when Reuben and Gad were exiled, he took the calf that was in Beth-el, to fulfil what is said (Hosea 10:6): “It also shall be carried unto Assyria.” And because the *pardisaot* were abolished and they refrained from going up on the pilgrimage, therefore the decree of their judgment was sealed to be exiled in his days; for until now they had hung the failing on their kings, and now there was no one on whom to hang it; and this is what Hosea the son of Beeri said (ibid. 5:3): “for now, O Ephraim, thou hast committed harlotry, Israel is defiled” — now your evil has been revealed.
2 Kings.translator_note: The word *pardisaot* (guard posts) is left in transliteration; the quotation “Ijon and Dan” is as printed (see 17:1).

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: In the ninth year of Hoshea
2 Kings.english_translation: Of the rebellion of Hoshea.

“And he exiled Israel” (*va-yagleh*): and this is the rule for every word whose verb ends in *he*, such as *panah* (turned), *banah* (built), *galah* (was exiled), *zanah* (went astray), *ravah* (multiplied): when one comes to place at the head of the word a *vav* and *yod*, if the word is turned upon the verb itself, the *yod* is pointed with *chirik*, such as (Genesis 12:7): “and he builded there an altar”; (Exodus 32:15): “and Moses turned and went down”; (below, verse 23): “So Judah was carried away out of his land”; (Jeremiah 3:8): “and she went and played the harlot also”; (Exodus 1:20): “and the people multiplied, and waxed very mighty.” And if it speaks in the causative language, the *yod* is pointed with *segol*, such as (Judges 15:4): “and turned tail to tail”; (below 18:11): “and he carried Israel away unto Assyria”; (2 Chronicles 21:11): “and made the inhabitants of Jerusalem to go astray”; (Lamentations 2:5): “and hath multiplied in the daughter of Judah mourning and moaning.”
2 Kings.translator_note: The printed quotation for “verse 23” reads “Judah” (verse 23 of this chapter reads “Israel”); the grammatical terms and verb forms are transliterated.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: did impute things that were not right
2 Kings.english_translation: They fabricated; its interpretation is according to its context.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: from the tower of the watchmen
2 Kings.english_translation: Which is made only to station a lookout to watch; in every high house they set up the worship of idols.
Like “from small to great.”
He warned them.
“Prophets of every vision”: there is a *chozeh* that is a noun, like (Isaiah 28:15): “and with Sheol we have made a *chozeh*.”
2 Kings.translator_note: JPS renders the word in Isaiah 28:15 as “agreement”.

2 Kings.english_translation: In Beth-el and in Dan.
An idol whose name is Baal.
They sold themselves for that.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: removed them out of His sight
2 Kings.english_translation: For they went into exile with Hoshea the son of Elah.
This is pointed with a *chirik*, which is an expression of “was exiled,” and not an expression of “caused to be exiled.”

Although the nations are worshippers of idols, they fear Him, and they call Him *Elaha de-elahaya* (“God of gods”), as is said (Malachi 1:14): “and My name is feared among the nations”; and these did not fear Me, for they said: Had there been fear in Him, He would not have given His people to exile.
2 Kings.translator_note: The word “ואלו” is translated “and these”, following the sense of the passage.

2 Kings.english_translation: Israel, while they were still there.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: every nation made gods of their own
2 Kings.english_translation: For each and every nation, the idol worship that they used to serve in their land; here too all the nations of the city whom Sennacherib had settled there, in the cities of Israel, did so.
The likeness of a hen with her chicks.
The likeness of a rooster.
The likeness of a he-goat; and so they are called in the language of each and every nation, and so our Rabbis explained in Sanhedrin (63b).
The likeness of a dog.
The likeness of a donkey.
The likeness of a mule.
The likeness of a horse (ibid.).

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: after the manner of the nations from among whom they had been carried away
2 Kings.english_translation: Those idolatries and constellations that the nations worship, whom Sennacherib and his multitude exiled from there, these worshipped here.

A complete fear, like the practice of Israel; and although they converted from fear of the lions, their fear of the LORD is not a complete fear, as it goes on to explain, for they do not occupy themselves with the Torah and the commandments that the LORD commanded the children of Jacob, and they do not do according to their statutes and their ordinances, which they should have done once they converted, but as the priest taught them, who was of the Samaritans, who worshipped idols.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: with whom the LORD had made a covenant
2 Kings.english_translation: When He gave them the Torah at Mount Sinai.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: in the third year of Hoshea
2 Kings.english_translation: Of the rebellion of Hoshea.
An expression of contempt, as if to say: What need is there of this? It is nothing but a serpent of brass (*nachash nechoshet*).
He succeeds.
The doors, which were of gold.
Jonathan translated: *ve-et sekufaya*, thresholds (*iskufot*).

We learned in *Seder Olam* that the three did not come together, but only Rab-shakeh alone, as is written in the book of Isaiah (36:2); and Tartan and Rab-saris came on a second mission, when a rumour reached him about Tirhakah king of Ethiopia: “and he heard,” and “he sent messengers to Hezekiah,” etc. (ibid. 37:9).
*Poskiere* in Old French: a pool that is made for fish-ponds.
2 Kings.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is פוסקיר״ה. Darmesteter (1909) lists this verse (“Dans le fossé”) but his manuscripts read *fossé* (a ditch); I give the printed form in transliteration.

2 Kings.english_translation: A field in which the fullers spread out garments; and so Jonathan translated: *chakal meshatach katzraya*.
Whatever case comes first before the king, that he may decide it first.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: Sayest thou that a mere word of the lips is counsel and strength for the war?
2 Kings.english_translation: You said until now: I shall serve the king of Assyria; but it was only a word of the lips; as long as he had not left his place to come against you, you had no need of counsel and strength; but now that he has gone out and come, you need counsel and strength for this war. Now say, in whom have you trusted?
When a man leans on the support of a bruised reed that breaks in his hand, the ends of the splinters (*kromiyot*) come and pierce his palm.
2 Kings.translator_note: The word *kromiyot* is rendered “splinters” following the sense of the comment.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: is not that He, whose high places and whose altars Hezekiah hath taken away
2 Kings.english_translation: One can learn from here that Rab-shakeh was an apostate Israelite (see Sanhedrin 61), for he acknowledged that the Holy One, blessed be He, is God, but he wished to worship idols.
2 Kings.translator_note: The parenthetical “(see Sanhedrin 61)” is an editorial addition in the printed Hebrew, not Rashi’s own words.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: make a wager with my master the king of Assyria
2 Kings.english_translation: Boast against him; come into a pledge, on condition that, if you can, you give yourself riders for the two thousand horses.
2 Kings.translator_note: The Hebrew is terse and elliptical; translated literally.

2 Kings.english_translation: *Gajer* in Old French.
2 Kings.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is גיי״ר; Darmesteter (1909) reads *gajer*, from Latin *vadiare* (“Engage-toi”).

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: turn away the face of one captain, even of the least of my masters servants
2 Kings.english_translation: For even the least of them is a commander over a thousand men, and you cannot reach a thousand men. We learn from here about the chiefs of the troops, one hundred and eighty-five thousand who fell with Sennacherib: the least of them was a commander of a thousand men who were with him.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: Am I now come up without the LORD against this place
2 Kings.english_translation: Did I come without permission? Isaiah already prophesied (7:17) in the days of Ahaz your father: “The LORD shall bring upon thee, and upon thy people,” etc., “even the king of Assyria.”
This one he added of his own.
We are palace people, and we know the Aramaic language and other languages; and do not speak to us in the Jews’ language, which all the people know, and we do not want them to hear.
In the famine of the siege.
The excrement that comes out through the hole of the anus; and our Rabbis explained (Megillah 25b): to refer to it by a more pleasant expression, *tzo'atam*.
Liquid excrement, *shinei dekharkhasha dekayma atlat shinei*, or an expression of *gelal*, which comes by the chewing of the teeth.
2 Kings.translator_note: The Aramaic phrase is difficult in the printed text and is left in transliteration without translation.

2 Kings.english_translation: A greeting of peace, like (Genesis 47:7): “And Jacob blessed Pharaoh.”

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: a land like your own land
2 Kings.english_translation: This is my way, to transfer the nations from province to province. He should have said “to a good land, better than yours,” for he came to entice them; but he knew that they would recognize that his words were false.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: a land of corn and wine
2 Kings.english_translation: This is Africa (Jerusalem Talmud, Shevi'it 6:1).
Those the king of Assyria destroyed and exiled.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: have they delivered Samaria out of my hand
2 Kings.english_translation: And the Samaritans worshipped the gods of Aram, who were their neighbours.
Because they heard the blasphemies against the Name.
For the wicked contend and put on a bold face for their words, saying: Ours is the strength and the might.
Israel.
Until a trouble resembling a woman sitting on the birthstool who has no strength to give birth; *mashber* is the name of the sitting-place of a woman crouching to give birth.
*Esprouver* in Old French: He showed a bold face for his words, for he prospered in everything wherever he went.
2 Kings.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is אישפרובי״ר; Darmesteter (1909) lists this verse (“Il vous a prouvé”) with the variant אפרוביר (*éprouver*).

2 Kings.english_translation: “And he will go up from upon you and return to his land,” not on account of the rumour, but after a time he will return to his land in shame, and “I will cause him to fall there by the sword.” And what is the rumour? “And he heard of Tirhakah” (verse 9): he heard that Tirhakah had gone out to fight with him, and he went up from Jerusalem and went to Cush, and fought with Tirhakah and Put and Egypt who were with him, and defeated them, and took the desirable things of their treasures, and came to Jerusalem and fell there; this is what is said (Isaiah 45:14): “The labour of Egypt, and the merchandise of Ethiopia,” etc., “shall come over unto thee,” etc.
2 Kings.translator_note: The Hebrew opens with the continuation of the verse’s own sense; translated as printed.

2 Kings.english_translation: To inform him that he was not returning to his land, but to fight with Cush, and to come back here.
The name of a province.
Those — the king of Assyria.
2 Kings.translator_note: The printed sentence has no verb (compare the comment on 18:34, “destroyed and exiled”); translated as printed.

2 Kings.english_translation: It is true that the kings of Assyria laid waste the nations and put their gods in the fire.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: to the height of the mountains
2 Kings.english_translation: The Temple Mount.
The Temple, which makes white (*malbin*) iniquities.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: I have cut down the tall cedars thereof
2 Kings.english_translation: I shall not return until I destroy it.
Its end.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: The forest of his fruitful field
2 Kings.english_translation: The fullness of its land and the beauty of its glory.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: I have digged and drunk Strange waters
2 Kings.english_translation: That is, I began every undertaking and completed it, like one who digs a pit and finds strange waters and drinks flowing water; he calls them “strange” because until now they were not known.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: with the sole of my feet have I dried up
2 Kings.english_translation: If I besieged a city that trusted in its rivers, I brought upon it many troops who dried up its rivers by their drinking and the drinking of their cattle and the trampling of their feet.
The present tense: so is my way always.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: Hast thou not heard? Long ago I made it
2 Kings.english_translation: Why do you boast and exalt yourself in this? It is not yours, for you heard from afar, through the prophets, that I decreed upon the nations to bring you upon them, as in the matter that is said (Isaiah 10:5): “O Asshur, the rod of Mine anger.”

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: In ancient times I fashioned it
2 Kings.english_translation: From when the world was created it arose in thought, as is said (ibid. 30:33): “For *tofteh* is ordered of old; yea, for the king it is prepared” — this is Sennacherib, who was burned by the fire of Gehinnom, as is said (ibid. 31:9): “saith the LORD, whose fire is in Zion.”
2 Kings.translator_note: The Hebrew word *tofteh* (Isaiah 30:33) is left in transliteration; JPS renders it “a hearth”.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: Now have I brought it to pass
2 Kings.english_translation: And this is the strength that is in your hand.
The coming of my decree: to lay waste fortified cities, to become ruinous heaps, heaps of earth in which vegetables grow, which you destroy by my decree.
2 Kings.translator_note: The Hebrew is terse; translated literally.

2 Kings.english_translation: An expression of *she'iyah* (desolation), solitary (*galmudah*).

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: Therefore their inhabitants were of small power
2 Kings.english_translation: They — it was I who weakened their strength before you; and the might is not yours, you are not mighty, but they are weak.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: As the grass on the housetops
2 Kings.english_translation: That which hastens to dry up.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: corn blasted before it is grown up
2 Kings.english_translation: Like blasted ears before they harden and reach the stage of standing grain.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: thy sitting down, and thy going out, and thy coming in
2 Kings.english_translation: Jonathan translated: *u-mitvakh be-itza u-mipkakh le-agacha kerava u-meitakh le-ar'a de-Yisrael galei kodami* (“your sitting in counsel, and your going out to wage battle, and your coming to the land of Israel are revealed before Me”); from Me it came to be.
2 Kings.translator_note: The Aramaic is transliterated, with a literal gloss in brackets.

2 Kings.english_translation: And that which is your end — to be arrogant and to rise against Me with rage and noise: *estremie* in Old French.
2 Kings.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is אשטרימי״ה; Darmesteter (1909) lists this verse (“De ce que tu t’es irrité”) with the reading *estomir* (“irriter”); I give the printed form in transliteration.

2 Kings.english_translation: Like *sha'onekha*.
It is a kind of *shir*, by which they draw an animal whose ways are evil, as we learned (Shabbat 51b): “All who have a *shir* go out with the *shir*.”
2 Kings.translator_note: The word *shir* (a chain or ring for an animal) is left in transliteration.

2 Kings.english_translation: Jonathan translated: *zamam*, and it is of iron, and they thrust it into the nostrils of the she-camel (*na'akah*) and she is drawn by it, because her ways are evil; and this is what we learned (ibid.): “and a she-camel with a nose-ring.”

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: this shall be the sign unto thee
2 Kings.english_translation: The prophet said to Hezekiah: This that I told you, that Sennacherib will fall here, shall be a sign for you also for the coming days, in which you fear to die of hunger, since Sennacherib laid waste the land and cut down the trees.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: you shall eat this year that which groweth of itself
2 Kings.english_translation: In this year plants will sprout for you and you will be sustained from them.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: in the second year that which springeth of the same
2 Kings.english_translation: Cut-down trees that will sprout; and when you see my word fulfilled in the downfall of the host, it will be a sign for you that this promise too will be fulfilled.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: the zeal of the LORD of hosts shall perform this
2 Kings.english_translation: That He will be zealous for His honour and His Name, and not that there is merit in your hands, for your father Ahaz did much wickedness.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: neither shall he come before it with shield
2 Kings.english_translation: No shield will be arrayed before it.

A heap of earth, to raise a mound to stand upon in order to fight against the city; and because he subdues it and beats it with sticks and mallets so that it be trodden and firmly pressed down, he calls it *solelah*, an expression of (Isaiah 62:10): “Cast up, cast up the highway.”
When Sennacherib returned from Cush and came as far as Nob, which was near Jerusalem.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: a hundred fourscore and five thousand
2 Kings.english_translation: All of them chiefs of the troops.
It is the head of the land of Assyria.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: the house of Nisroch his god
2 Kings.english_translation: A plank (*nesser*) from Noah’s ark.
They heard him say to its slaughterers before it, if it would save him, that the princes of the kingdom, whose sons had died by his hand, should not kill him (Sanhedrin 96a).
2 Kings.translator_note: The sentence is elliptical in the printed text and is translated literally; the Sanhedrin reference is as printed.

2 Kings.english_translation: Three days before the fall of Sennacherib.
And on the third day, when he went up to the House of the LORD, the day of the fall of Sennacherib — and it was the festival day of Passover (*Seder Olam*, chapter 23).
In this world.
In the World to Come, because you did not take a wife, as is in Berakhot (11).
2 Kings.translator_note: The reference is as printed (“Berakhot 11”).

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: before Isaiah was gone out of the inner court of the city
2 Kings.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He, hastened to announce his healing, before a sound of report went out in the city that death had been decreed upon him, as is in the Jerusalem (Talmud, Sanhedrin 10:2).

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: I will deliver thee and this city out of the hand of the king of Assyria
2 Kings.english_translation: We learned that he fell sick before the fall of Sennacherib.
When they are moist they are called figs (*te'enim*), and when they are pressed in a round mould they are called *develah*.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: and laid it on the boil, and he recovered
2 Kings.english_translation: A miracle within a miracle, for even living flesh, when you put a *develah* on it, it putrefies; and the Holy One puts a thing that spoils into a thing that is spoiled, and it is healed (Mekhilta, Exodus 15).

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: shall the shadow go forward ten degrees, or go back ten degrees?
2 Kings.english_translation: This is an abbreviated verse. The shadow had already descended the steps made for the hours of the day, like *orloyen* in Old French, which people make to test the hours of the day: do you want it to wait in the place where it is for the space of ten hours, or to return up ten steps and appear as if it were morning?
2 Kings.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is אורלויי״ן. I did not find an entry for this verse in Darmesteter’s list, so I give only the printed form in transliteration.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: It is a light thing for the shadow to decline ten degrees
2 Kings.english_translation: It is an easy thing to decline in its place, and its declining and standing ten steps is not a thing so noticeable; not so, but let the shadow return, and let the matter be a wonder, for they saw that the day had turned to evening, and it returns to be morning.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: by which it had gone down on the dial of Ahaz
2 Kings.english_translation: On the day Ahaz died, the day was shortened and the shadow hurried to descend ten steps, so that he not be eulogized; and those ten hours were now returned to Hezekiah (Sanhedrin 96a).

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: for he had heard that Hezekiah had been sick
2 Kings.english_translation: And until that day no man was sick and lived; and how did he hear? He was accustomed to eat at the third hour of the day and to sleep until the ninth; when the sphere of the sun returned for Hezekiah, he awoke at the ninth hour and found that it was morning. He wished to kill his servants; he said: You let me sleep a day and a night! They said: The sphere of the sun has returned. He said to them: Who returned it? They said to him: The God of Hezekiah, as is in the Pesikta.
2 Kings.translator_note: The printed text does not name the subject of “he” (apparently Berodach-baladan).

2 Kings.english_translation: The house of the treasures of his spices, like (Genesis 37:25): “spicery and balm and ladanum.”

Some interpret it as the anointing oil, and some interpret it as oil of balsam (*apharsemon*, balsamon), which is found in the Land of Israel, as it is said (Ezekiel 27:17): “Judah and the land of Israel, they were thy traders in wheat of Minnith and pannag.” And I saw in the Book of Yosippon: *pannag* is balsam, and it grows in Jericho, and on account of the fragrance it is called Jericho.
2 Kings.translator_note: The Ezekiel quotation is abbreviated and reordered compared with the verse.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: there was nothing in his house
2 Kings.english_translation: The ark, and the tablets, and the Torah scroll (Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer chapter 52; see Song of Songs Rabbah 3:4).
2 Kings.translator_note: The words “see Song of Songs Rabbah 3:4” are an editorial addition in the printed Hebrew.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: They are come from a far country, even from Babylon
2 Kings.english_translation: This is one of three whom the Holy One, blessed be He, examined and found a vessel (*aviyt*) of turbid water: Cain, Hezekiah, and Balaam. Cain — (Genesis 4:9) “I know not; am I my brother’s keeper?” — he should have said: Master of the Universe, are not all hidden things revealed to You? as is in Tanchuma (see Numbers Rabbah 20:6). Balaam — to whom the Omnipresent said (Numbers 22:9): “What men are these with thee?” — he should have said, “O Lord GOD, Thou knowest,” as is said in Ezekiel (37:3); and he answered with arrogance: “Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab, hath sent unto me” — I have many who seek me. Hezekiah — he should have answered Isaiah: You are the prophet of the Omnipresent, and you ask me? Hezekiah began to boast and said: “From a far country they have come unto me”; therefore he was punished, and also because he rejoiced over them and fed them at his table (Sanhedrin 104a).
2 Kings.translator_note: The word *aviyt* (a vessel) is left in transliteration; “see Numbers Rabbah 20:6” is an editorial addition in the printed Hebrew.

2 Kings.english_translation: Measure for measure: “there was nothing” (verse 13).

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And of thy sons that shall issue from thee
2 Kings.english_translation: Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: Good is the word of the LORD
2 Kings.english_translation: Since there will be peace in my days.
In Chronicles.
Nahum and Habakkuk; and since Manasseh was wicked, they were not called by his name, to specify that they were in his days.
2 Kings.translator_note: The last clause is terse in the printed text; translated literally.

2 Kings.english_translation: An expression of cymbals (*metzaltayim*): *tentener* in Old French.
2 Kings.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is טינטני״ר; Darmesteter (1909) lists this verse and reads *téntener* (variants *tinter*, *tentiçier*).

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: the plummet of the house of Ahab
2 Kings.english_translation: It is a cord to which the builders of a wall tie lead, to straighten the wall with it.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: as a man wipeth a dish
2 Kings.english_translation: He will wipe the bowl.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: I have found the book of the Law
2 Kings.english_translation: Hidden beneath the course of stones, where they hid it when Ahaz burned the Torah.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: Go you, inquire of the LORD for me
2 Kings.english_translation: See, it is written (Deuteronomy 28:36): “The LORD will bring thee, and thy king.”
2 Kings.translator_note: The printed text gives no reference; the words are Deuteronomy 28:36.

2 Kings.english_translation: Our Rabbis said (Megillah 14b): Because a woman is more merciful than a man, therefore he did not send to Jeremiah. And some say: Jeremiah was not there, for he had gone to bring back the ten tribes.

In the house of study. There is a gate in the court whose name is the Huldah Gate, in tractate Middot (34a). And some interpret “in the *mishneh*” as outside the wall, between the two walls, which is a second (*mishneh*) to the city. [“In the *mishneh*”: she used to teach the Oral Torah to the elders of the generation, and that is the Mishnah — gloss of R״A.] [“In the *mishneh*”: from “These are the words” until “before all Israel”; and so all the things that are doubled in the Torah, she expounded in public, and revealed the punishments and exiles that are doubled for those who transgress its secret and the hints of the Torah. The Secret of Mesharim.]
2 Kings.translator_note: The two bracketed passages are later additions in the printed Hebrew, not Rashi’s own words (the first is signed “הג״ה דר״ע”); they are translated literally.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: thou shalt be gathered to thy grave in peace
2 Kings.english_translation: And what is the peace? “Neither shall thine eyes see” the destruction of the Temple.
The standing place of the king in the Temple.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: the priests of the second order
2 Kings.english_translation: Deputies of the priesthood, who are second to the high priests.
*Amarkalim* appointed over all the needs of the House, and the keys of the court are in their hands.
In the plain of Kidron.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: carried the ashes of them unto Beth-el
2 Kings.english_translation: To an unclean place, where he defiled the altar that Jeroboam made, and burned upon it the priests of the high places.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: to offer in the high places
2 Kings.english_translation: And those who offered incense on the high places in the cities of Judah.
Houses of lewdness (*zimmah*).
Curtains (*yeri'ot*).
The priests who burned incense for idolatry shall not go up again to serve at the altar of the LORD.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: but they did eat unleavened bread among their brethren
2 Kings.english_translation: That is, in this matter only they did not depart from their priesthood, that they are permitted to eat of the holy things; they are like those with blemishes, who share and eat but do not offer.
Meal-offerings, and the same for all holy things.
It is Molech; and because the priests beat on drums (*tofim*), so that the father not hear the groaning of the son when he is burned by the image of the idol Molech, they called it Topheth.
Those who bow to the sun had horses prepared to go out toward the sun in the morning.
So was his name.
I do not know what they are.
And he cleared them out from there.
The Mount of Olives, which is the Mount of Anointing; and since he mentioned its name in connection with idolatry, he changed its name to a disgrace.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: What monument is that which I see
2 Kings.english_translation: He saw a tomb; on one side of it grew brambles and nettles, and on one side myrtles and spices; and he wondered about it and said, What is this? and they answered him.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: It is the sepulchre of the man of God
2 Kings.english_translation: And the false prophet who commanded his sons to bury him beside him (1 Kings chapter 13).
For Josiah was king over all Israel, those who had returned of the ten tribes through Jeremiah.
The majority of the people never gathered at any Passover as they gathered at this one.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: from the days of the judges
2 Kings.english_translation: From the days of Samuel; it is written in Chronicles (2 Chronicles 35:18), because Samuel too returned Israel to the good, and gathered them at Mizpah. Another interpretation: “there was not kept such a passover to the LORD in Jerusalem”; (but) from when the kings of Israel and the kings of Judah reigned, all Israel did not keep Passover in Jerusalem, because the kingdom was divided into two from Jeroboam, and they used to go to the calf at Beth-el and Dan, until now that the ten tribes were exiled and Jeremiah returned them and Josiah reigned over them, and they all came to Jerusalem.
Figures through which they speak by sorcery, and he who makes them must concentrate for one hour in the year, and one year is suitable for this.
2 Kings.translator_note: The last clause is terse in the printed text; translated literally.

2 Kings.english_translation: He did not need anointing, but because Jehoiakim his brother was two years older than he, as it is written in the passage (verse 36).

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: of every one according to his taxation
2 Kings.english_translation: According to his wealth.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: Surely at the commandment of the LORD came this upon Judah
2 Kings.english_translation: All the evil that came upon Judah through these bands.

Not on his bed, for Nebuchadnezzar bound him in fetters to take him to Babylon, and they dragged him, and he died in their hands, as it is said (Jeremiah 22:19): “He shall be buried with the burial of an ass, drawn and cast forth.” And in Chronicles (2 Chronicles 36:6) it wrote that Nebuchadnezzar bound him to take him to Babylon.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: came not again any more out of his land
2 Kings.english_translation: To help Jehoiakim.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: for the king of Babylon had taken
2 Kings.english_translation: For they were defeated in battle in the fourth year of Jehoiakim, at Carchemish on the River Euphrates, as is written in the book of Jeremiah (46:2).

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: went out to the king of Babylon
2 Kings.english_translation: To do his will, and not for war.

Jonathan translated: *umaniya ve-tar'aya* (“craftsmen and gatekeepers”). And our Rabbis said (Gittin 88a): sages great in the Torah, that when one opens, all are silent, as it is written (Isaiah 41:1): “Keep silence before Me, O islands”; *masger* — all sit before him and learn from him, as it is said (ibid. 22:22): “so he shall open, and none shall shut; and he shall shut, and none shall open.”
2 Kings.translator_note: The Aramaic words are transliterated, with a literal gloss in brackets.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: the chief men of the land
2 Kings.english_translation: These are the nobles of Judah and Benjamin, and they were righteous; of them Scripture says (Jeremiah 24:5): “Like these good figs, so will I regard the captivity of Judah.”

And above it says ten thousand; a third verse comes and decides, in the book of Jeremiah (52:28): “This is the people whom Nebuchadrezzar carried away captive: in the seventh year three thousand Jews.” Say therefore that three thousand were from the tribe of Judah, and seven thousand from Benjamin and the other tribes; and so we learned also in *Seder Olam*.
“May God (Yah) justify the judgment upon thee, if thou rebel against me” (Horayot 11b).

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: For through the anger of the LORD did it come to pass in Jerusalem and Judah
2 Kings.english_translation: Therefore “and Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon”: the Holy One, blessed be He, put it into his heart to rebel against him, so that he would be exiled.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: in the ninth year of his reign
2 Kings.english_translation: Of Zedekiah.
Jonathan translated: *karkum*.
2 Kings.translator_note: The Aramaic word is transliterated as printed.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: by the way of the gate between the two walls
2 Kings.english_translation: A cave that runs from his house to the plains of Jericho, and he fled by way of the cave; and the Holy One, blessed be He, prepared a deer that walked on the roof of the cave outside the city, and the Chaldeans pursued after the deer, and when they reached the mouth of the cave in the plains of Jericho, they saw him and caught him; this is what is said (Ezekiel 12:13): “My net also will I spread upon him, and he shall be taken in My snare.”
He argued with him about the oath.
Synagogues in which Torah and prayer are magnified, and the houses of the princes (see Megillah 27a).
2 Kings.translator_note: The words “see Megillah 27a” are an editorial addition in the printed Hebrew.

2 Kings.english_translation: Who listened to the voice of Nebuchadnezzar and went out to him from the city, like (1 Chronicles 12:20): “As he went to Ziklag, there fell to him of Manasseh,” etc.
2 Kings.translator_note: The printed reference has an extra letter after the verse number.

2 Kings.english_translation: Diggers of the ground, an expression of *yekavim* (wine-vats), which are excavations in the ground.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: the height of the capital was three cubits
2 Kings.english_translation: And at the beginning of the book (1 Kings 7:16) it says five cubits. And there I reconciled the verses.
*Coife* in Old French, a kind of cap.
2 Kings.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is קופיי״א; Darmesteter (1909) reads *coife* (“Un réseau, sorte de coiffe”).

2 Kings.english_translation: Pomegranates.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: the scribe of the captain of the host
2 Kings.english_translation: Who knew the number of each and every city, how many men it sends out to the army.
Who went out from the city to hide in strongholds and in *tinerim* and in rocks and in forests.
2 Kings.translator_note: The word *tinerim* is left in transliteration as printed.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: did lift up the head of Jehoiachin
2 Kings.english_translation: That Nebuchadnezzar died, and Evil-merodach reigned in his place.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: on the seven and twentieth day of the month
2 Kings.english_translation: And in Jeremiah (52:31) it says: on the twenty-fifth; but on the twenty-fifth Nebuchadnezzar died, and he was buried on the twenty-sixth; on the twenty-seventh Evil-merodach took him out of his grave and dragged him, in order to nullify his decrees, as is said in Isaiah (14:19): “But thou art cast forth away from thy grave like an abhorred offshoot,” etc.

2 Kings.english_lemma_JPS: And he spoke kindly to him
2 Kings.english_translation: Words of comfort.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The Vision of Isaiah the son of Amoz
Isaiah.english_translation: Rabbi Levi said: This is a tradition in our hands from our fathers: Amoz and Amaziah king of Judah were brothers.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem
Isaiah.english_translation: But did he not prophesy concerning many nations — the burden of Babylon, the burden of Moab? Hence you learn that this is not the beginning of the book, and the book is not called after the name of this vision. And so we learned in the Baraita of the Mekhilta: “In the year that king Uzziah died” is the beginning of the book; but there is no earlier and later in the order, and the matters prove it, for on the day of the earthquake, the day Uzziah was struck with leprosy, it is said, “And I heard the voice of the Lord, saying: Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” (below, chapter 6), and he said, “Here am I; send me” — we learned that it is the beginning of his mission, and this prophecy was said afterward. And of this one alone it is said “which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem,” just as it says of the burden of each and every nation, “the burden of such-and-such a nation”; so here he wrote: this vision he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem. And because they are rebukes of harshness, he called them “vision” (*chazon*), which is harder than the ten expressions by which prophecy is called, as is said in Genesis Rabbah; and a proof of the matter: “A grievous vision is declared unto me” (below, chapter 21).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah
Isaiah.english_translation: These four kings of Judah. *Kippeach* in his days: on the day Uzziah was struck with leprosy, the Shekhinah rested upon him, and he prophesied all the days of these kings until Manasseh arose and killed him. (And this prophecy was said in the days of Hezekiah, after the ten tribes were exiled. From a manuscript.)
Isaiah.translator_note: The printed word קפח is unclear and is left in transliteration. The parenthetical sentence at the end is a later addition in the printed Hebrew (marked “from a manuscript”), not Rashi’s own words.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Hear, O heavens, and give ear, O earth
Isaiah.english_translation: Moses said (Deuteronomy 32:1): “Give ear, O heavens, and let the earth hear.” Why did Isaiah change the language? Our Rabbis taught in this matter, and many Midrashim are in the section *Ha'azinu* in the Sifre; and the Sages disagreed about them and said: It is not so, but when witnesses come and testify and their words are found to agree, their testimony stands, and if not, their testimony does not stand. Had Isaiah not come and given “hearing” to the heavens and “giving ear” to the earth, the heavens would testify and say, when we were called to this testimony in the days of Moses, who said, “I call heaven and earth to witness against you this day,” in the language of giving ear we heard; and the earth would testify: I was called in the language of hearing; and their testimony would not agree. Isaiah came and exchanged the matter, and both are found testifying in the language of giving ear and in the language of hearing.

(That you be witnesses to the matter when I warned them in the days of Moses; therefore come and hear that I am contending with them, for they transgressed the warning. I did not sin against them, but raised them and exalted them, and they rebelled against Me. Another version:) That you be witnesses to the matter. And where did He speak? “Give ear, O heavens, and I will speak” (ibid.), in the Mekhilta.
Isaiah.translator_note: The opening parenthesis (ending “Another version:”) is how the text stands in the printed Hebrew, with the abbreviation ס״א (“another version”).

Isaiah.english_translation: He prepares him by plowing during the day, and since he is accustomed to it he knows him; but a stopped-up ass does not understand its owner until he feeds it; and Israel was not opened to know like an ox, when I called him “Israel shall be thy name” and let him know a few of My statutes; and they forsook Me, as is explained (Ezekiel 20:39), and says: “every man [after] my idols,” etc.; and even after I took them out of Egypt and fed them the manna and called them “My people, the children of Israel,” they did not discern, like an ass. (סא״א.) Another interpretation: “The ox knoweth his owner”: the ox recognizes his owner, that his fear is upon him; he does not change what I decreed upon him, to say: I will not plow today; and the ass does not say to its owner: I will not carry today. And these, which were created to serve you, and have neither receiving of reward if they merit nor repayment of punishment if they sin, did not change their measure that I decreed upon them; and Israel, who if they merit receive reward and if they sin receive punishment —
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotation from Ezekiel 20:39 does not match the verse’s wording exactly (as printed). The last sentence breaks off in the printed text and is translated as it stands.

Isaiah.english_translation: They were unwilling to know; and they knew and trampled with the heel; “and My people did not give heart to discern.”
Isaiah.translator_note: The Hebrew is terse; translated literally.

Isaiah.english_translation: Every *hoy* in Scripture is an expression of complaint and lament, like a man who groans from his heart and cries “Alas!”; but a few of them are an expression of a cry, calling aloud, such as (Zechariah 2:10): “Ho, ho, flee from the land of the north,” and its Targum is *akhlu* [as printed], an expression of proclamation. Here one must cry out over a holy nation that turned to become a sinful nation, and a people of whom it is said, “for thou art a holy people,” turned to become a people heavy with iniquity.
Isaiah.translator_note: The Targum word (printed אכלו) is unclear; left in transliteration. The words “for thou art a holy people” are given without a reference in the printed text.

Isaiah.english_translation: Heaviness of iniquity. *Kaved*, a man who is heavy, *pesant* in Old French; *kaved*, the name of a thing of heaviness, *pesantume* in Old French; and it is joined to the word *avon*.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spellings are פישנ״ט and פישנטומ״א; Darmesteter (1909) lists this verse (“Charge d’iniquités”) and reads *pesant* and *pesantume*.

Isaiah.english_translation: And they were “the seed blessed of the LORD”; they were sons to the Holy One, blessed be He; they turned into corrupters.
They made Him angry.

*Nezirah* is nowhere anything but an expression of separation, and so it says (Leviticus 22:2): “that they separate themselves from the holy things of the children of Israel”; “him that was separate from his brethren” (Genesis 49:26). Here too: *nazoru* — they withdrew backward from beside the Omnipresent.
Isaiah.translator_note: In Genesis 49:26 JPS renders the Hebrew phrase as “the prince among his brethren”.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: On what part will you yet be stricken
Isaiah.english_translation: A man who was struck and returns to his sin, his fellow rebukes him and says to him: For this you were struck, and you do not take heart to say, For this sin I was struck, I will not return to do it again. Here too: “On what part will you be stricken,” since you still add rebellion, to turn aside from after the Omnipresent? “Is not every head already sick?” and why do you not understand?
From *tom*: an expression of wholeness, complete, without pain.
A blow of a sword.
An expression of injury (*chavalah*).
Jonathan translated *merassa*: crushed and shattered.

*Demiceide* in Old French; and in the language of the Gemara there is *trayah le-reisheih*. Menachem interpreted an expression of moisture, that is, moist and wet, always flowing, *moiste* in Old French.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spellings are דמיצייד״א and מוישט״א; Darmesteter (1909) lists this verse (“Plaie suppurante”) and reads *démincéde*.

Isaiah.english_translation: These sores have not been scattered upon by physicians with powder of drugs of a bandage — an expression of “brimstone shall be scattered (*yezoreh*) upon his habitation” (Job 18:15); and Menachem interpreted an expression of healing, like “None deemeth of thy wound that it may be bound up (*lamazor*)” (Jeremiah 30:13); “and not bound up”: an expression of healing.

Their wound was not softened with oil, as is the way with other wounds; and it does not fit here to say “they were not softened with oil,” for one softens only at the place of the wound; but the *mazor* and the binding, their language applies to the whole body; therefore the plural applies to them: the sores were not scattered upon and not bound up. And Jonathan interpreted the whole verse in the manner of a parable, because they are soiled and afflicted with iniquity, and translated: “From the sole of the foot to the head” — from the small to the great; “there is no soundness in it” — there is no good in it; “wounds and bruises” — transgression and iniquities and sins; “they have not been pressed,” etc. — that is, they were not healed so as to return in complete repentance; “neither mollified with oil” — not even a side of a thought of repentance is in their heart.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Your land, strangers devour it in your presence
Isaiah.english_translation: Before your eyes your enemies will eat it.
A desolation from you, like an inheritance that is turned over to strangers, and it is desolate of its owners; so Jonathan translated.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And the daughter of Zion is left
Isaiah.english_translation: Empty of her inhabitants, for they will go into exile from within her, as the booth of the vineyard that a watchman made is left; and at the time the vineyard is harvested he leaves his booth and goes: *batar dekatfuhi* (Aramaic) — after they have harvested it.
Isaiah.translator_note: The Aramaic phrase is transliterated, with a literal gloss.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: As a lodge in a garden of cucumbers
Isaiah.english_translation: As the lodge is abandoned that the watchman made at the head of the cucumber field to guard its cucumbers, and when it is gathered, he leaves it and goes. This one in the vineyard is called a *sukkah* because he lives there day and night: by day he guards it from the birds and by night from thieves; but cucumbers are hard and there is no need to fear birds, and no need to guard it by day; therefore it is called a *melunah*, because it is a lodging (*linat*) for the nights, like a hammock, *ke-arsal mi-batuta*, like the bed of the lodge in the cucumber field; *bi-mekshiya batar de-av'iyohi* (Aramaic) — after they have gathered it; an expression of the Mishnah: “three *av'iyot* in the day.”
Isaiah.translator_note: The Aramaic words are transliterated; the phrase *ke-arsal mi-batuta* is left untranslated because its sense is unclear in the printed text.

Isaiah.english_translation: As a city that they besieged, and they make booths around it for the troops to hide there; and when they depart from it they leave them and go. All this is Targum Jonathan.
He left us a remnant of Himself and in His mercy, and not through our righteousness.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: We should have been as Sodom
Isaiah.english_translation: All of us consumed.
Rulers whose deeds are like Sodom. From here they said: A man should not open his mouth to Satan.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I am full of the burnt-offerings of rams
Isaiah.english_translation: Like (Proverbs 25:17): “Lest he be sated with thee, and hate thee.”
Fattened animals of the flock.
Since you transgress My Torah, “the sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Who hath required this at your hand
Isaiah.english_translation: To trample My courts, since your heart is not whole with Me.
I warn you: do not bring Me your vain offering, from which the smoke rises — a vapour of abomination it is to Me, and not a pleasing savour.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I cannot endure iniquity along with the solemn assembly
Isaiah.english_translation: And to call a convocation, new moon and sabbath, that you gather to call an assembly and a gathering on them — I cannot bear the iniquity in your heart, which leans toward idolatry, and the assembly with it; for these two things are not fit together, to call an assembly to be gathered before Me, and the iniquity in your heart for idolatry, and you do not remove it from your heart.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And when you spread forth your hands, I will hide Mine eyes from you
Isaiah.english_translation: Because your hands are full of blood.
Murder.
(It has a *patach*:) an expression of command, because it is from the form *rachatz*; but *rachatzu* with a *kamatz* is an expression of the past, because it is from the form *rachatz*.
Isaiah.translator_note: The grammatical statement repeats the same form twice in the printed text and looks corrupt; translated as it stands.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Wash you, make you clean, Put away the evil of your doings
Isaiah.english_translation: Ten warnings of the language of repentance are here, corresponding to the Ten Days of Repentance, and corresponding to the ten (verses of) Kingship, Remembrance and Shofar-blasts.
Cease from evil deeds.

Like *le-hara*; there is no need to write *mi-lehara*, for so the language of Scripture falls on an expression of “ceased” and “ceasing to do”: “and forbeareth to keep the passover” (Numbers 9:13); “until they left off numbering” (Genesis 41:49) — that is, the numbering ceased, the doing ceased; here too: you shall cease the evil.

*Limdu* (soft pointing) is from the form *lamud* — they were learners to do good. The one who learns for himself is of the light form; therefore its plural imperative is pointed with a *chirik*, like *imru*, *shim'u*; but one who teaches others is of the heavy form, with a *dagesh*, and if he comes to command the many it is pointed *lammedu*; and so they expounded from the form *derosh*. But *ashru*, where the *shin* is dagesh'd, is of the heavy form and from the form *asher*; therefore the plural imperative is pointed with a *patach* (like *ashru, dabberu, sapperu, bassru*).
Isaiah.translator_note: The grammar is terse in the printed text; translated literally. The list in parentheses at the end appears to be an editorial addition.

Isaiah.english_translation: Strengthen the robbed; and it is a Mishnaic expression, *ashranuhu*; *i ishar chayli* — *yasher kochakha*. Another version: Lead him in the path of truth to win what is his; an expression of “My foot hath held fast to His steps” (Job 23:11), and “and guide thy heart in the way” (Proverbs 23:19).
Isaiah.translator_note: The Mishnaic phrases are left in transliteration.

Isaiah.english_translation: Such a one is innocent; such a one is guilty.
Exert yourselves in her case, to contend on her behalf, so that she not go out to chase after her litigants. (סא״א.)
Robbed, and similar to it: “Out of the grasp of the unrighteous and ruthless man” (*me'avel ve-chomeitz*) (Psalms 71:4).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Come now, and let us reason together
Isaiah.english_translation: Together, I and you, and we shall know who sinned against whom; and if you sinned against Me, I still give you hope to return.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Though your sins be as scarlet
Isaiah.english_translation: *Ketumim* before Me, like redness; scarlet (*shanim*) — I shall whiten them like snow.
Isaiah.translator_note: The word *ketumim* is left in transliteration; its sense is unclear in the printed text.

Isaiah.english_translation: He says to you always thus, as in “according to the commandment of the LORD they remained encamped” (Numbers 9:20). Another interpretation: “Come now, and let us reason together” — what is written above it? “Cease to do evil, learn to do well”; and after you return to Me, “Come now, and let us reason together,” to let Me know: we did what is upon us, do what is upon You. And I say, “Though your sins be as scarlet,” “as white as snow,” etc.
A dye with which they dye red; they are seeds, and there are worms in each and every one.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For the mouth of the LORD hath spoken
Isaiah.english_translation: And where did He speak? “And I will bring a sword upon you” (Leviticus 26:25).
Straying from her God.
That was faithful and full of justice; righteousness lodged in her, and now murderers.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: She that was full of justice
Isaiah.english_translation: Like “that was full of people” (*rabati am*) (Lamentations 1).

The morning *tamid* offering atoned for the transgressions of the night, and the afternoon one atoned for those of the day. Another interpretation: they used to lodge capital cases in her; if they did not find a merit for him on the first day, they did not complete his judgment until the next day, perhaps they might find a merit for him; and now they have become murderers. And we find in the Pesikta: Rabbi Menachem son of Oshaya said: There were four hundred and eighty-one synagogues in Jerusalem, corresponding to the numerical value of *melei'ati* (“full”).
They killed Uriah; they killed Zechariah.
For they used to make copper coins and plate them with silver in order to deceive with them.

Your drinks are mixed with water, as is in the Pesikta. *Mahul* is mixed, and has no parallel in Scripture; and another interprets it by “I said of laughter: ‘It is mad’” (*mehollal*) (Ecclesiastes 2:2): mixed up.
Isaiah.translator_note: The abbreviation מ״א (“another”) is left as printed; the commentator is not named.

Isaiah.english_translation: Turning aside from the straight way.

*Tashlumin*. Targum Jonathan: They say, a man to his fellow: Do for me good in my case, and I shall pay you in your case. A judge who was a robber, and the one robbed cries out against him before another judge; this one says to him: Acquit me today, and I shall pay you your reward when they cry out against you before them. Hence “one who chases after payments of recompense.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Neither doth the cause of the widow come unto them
Isaiah.english_translation: The widow comes to cry out, and the orphan goes out, and she meets him and asks him: What did you gain by your outcry before the judge? And he says: All this day I toiled for him with work, and in the end I gained nothing. And she turns back and says: And this one, who is a man, did not benefit — I, all the more so! Hence “they judge not the fatherless, neither doth the cause of the widow come unto them” at all.
For everything is His, and it is in His hand to uproot you from your land and to plant others in it.
The strength of Israel.

An expression of summoning and proclaiming, and similar to it is “Ho, ho, flee from the land of the north” (Zechariah 2:10); “and all shall know that I will ease Me of Mine adversaries,” who angered me with their deeds.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And I will turn My hand upon thee
Isaiah.english_translation: Blow after blow until the transgressors are consumed.

An expression of *borit*: *savon* in Old French; and its language is an expression of cleanliness, like “and a pure heart” (*u-var levav*) (Psalms 24:4), named so because it cleans the garment of its stains.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is סבו״ן; Darmesteter (1909) lists this verse (“Savon”) and reads *savon*.

Isaiah.english_translation: That which was said above: “Thy silver is become dross”; a mixture of copper in silver is called *sig*; here too, the mixture of the wicked with the fit; I shall consume the transgressors, who are the dross.
Tin mixed in silver; that is, the wicked among you are tin: *esteyn* in Old French.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is אשטיי״ס; Darmesteter (1909) lists this verse (“Ton étain”) and reads *esteyn* (modern *étain*).

Isaiah.english_translation: I will establish for you fit judges.
As at first, righteousness lodged in her.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Zion shall be redeemed with justice
Isaiah.english_translation: Through there being in her one who does justice.
From her iniquities.
Those who do repentance within her (with righteousness: those who justify themselves, in judgment and in righteousness that is within her).
Isaiah.translator_note: The parenthetical at the end looks like a later addition in the printed Hebrew; translated literally.

Isaiah.english_translation: For He rebuked all of them above: “and they have rebelled against Me,” “sinful nation,” “they have forsaken the LORD.”
