Isaiah.english_translation: All this is from the prophecy that was said above — “for thus the LORD said to me,” and further this He said to me: *tzor te'udah*, an expression of “I have testified against you this day”; an expression of warning: bind My warning, and seal the Torah upon the heart of the learning of your disciples, the God-fearing, who are called “learned of the LORD.” And if you say that an expression of binding does not apply to the study of Torah — it does apply to it, as it is said: “Bind them continually upon thy heart” (Proverbs 6).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And I will wait for the LORD
Isaiah.english_translation: Isaiah said: I who wait for the LORD who hides His face from the ten tribes — I hoped for Him, to confirm these words and to deliver the house of David.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: shall be for signs and for wonders in Israel
Isaiah.english_translation: For signs: two signs: of punishment (Pekah), as the child was called Maher-shalal-hash-baz; and of the salvation of the house of David, as the child was called Immanuel. This is the settling of the matter according to its plain meaning. And Midrash Aggadah, in Bereshit Rabbah: on Ahaz, who seized the synagogues and the houses of study so that the children of the schoolhouse would not learn Torah; he said: If there are no kids, there are no he-goats; if there is no flock, there is no shepherd; I will cause Him to remove His Shekhinah. The prophet said to him: All that you bind the testimony and seal the Torah, to shut it so that it not be found in Israel, will not help you.

There is no prophecy as severe as that hour, when Moses said (Deuteronomy 31:18): “And I will surely hide My face in that day”; and even on that very day He assured them: “and this song shall testify before him as a witness; for it shall not be forgotten out of the mouth of his seed” (there).
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s wording of Deuteronomy 31:21 (“before him … his seed”) differs from the JPS verse (“before them … their seed”); translated as printed.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the children whom the LORD hath given me
Isaiah.english_translation: They are the disciples, who are dear to Me as sons; they will be for signs and for wonders, that the Torah will be upheld in Israel through them.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And when they shall say unto you
Isaiah.english_translation: Rabbi Simon said: Be'erah, the father of Hoshea son of Be'eri, prophesied these two verses, and there was not enough in them for a book, and they were attached to Isaiah, and he prophesied them for the exile of the ten tribes, when Sennacherib exiled the Reubenite and the Gadite (and they exiled him with them), as it is said (I Chronicles 5): “Beerah his son, prince of the Reubenites, whom Tilgath-pilneser exiled.”
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s wording of 1 Chronicles 5:6 differs slightly from the JPS verse; translated as printed.

Isaiah.english_translation: The nations.

An expression of disparagement, for even their speech is only like these birds, which chatter with their voice; an expression of chirping and muttering (*hegeh*) is used for birds: “Like a swallow or a crane, so do I chatter, I do moan as a dove” (below 38); and so we find an expression of chirping in a low voice, as it is said (below 29): “and thy voice shall be as of a ghost out of the ground, and thy speech shall chirp out of the dust.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: should not a people seek unto their God
Isaiah.english_translation: This shall be your answer: “Is not a people like us, which has a God like our God, to its God shall it seek?” Perhaps you will say to us to be like you, to seek the needs of the living from the dead?

Connected with what is above it: Perhaps we should seek unto the dead for instruction and for testimony on behalf of the living, to teach us what to do. All this according to the Midrash. And according to its plain meaning one can explain: “And when they shall say unto you,” etc. is the conclusion of his prophecy, which says “and admonished me that I should not walk in the way of this people”; and the Holy One, blessed be He, rebuked the prophet and the company of Hezekiah: when Shebna and his company say to you — who saw Hezekiah rejecting idolatry — “Seek unto the ghosts and the familiar spirits,” and inquire in idolatry as the earlier fathers did, and return the kingship to Sennacherib: “Should not (every) people seek unto its God?” — they serve idolatry and seek on behalf of the living of the dead; you too should do the same.
Isaiah.translator_note: The word “(every)” is in parentheses in the printed text.

Isaiah.english_translation: This shall be your answer: that you keep the Torah, as is said above, “Bind up the testimony, seal the Torah,” and do not believe their words.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Surely they will speak according to this word, wherein there is no light
Isaiah.english_translation: Since you answer him with this answer, you will see and hear whether the upright among them do not concede your words, and say “according to this word” — that it is true — “which has no dawn”: no ghost or familiar spirit has any dawn; it is not fitting to seek (*leshachar*) its face. So Jonathan translated. And Midrash Aggadah: on itself it does not bring up the dawn, for it has eyes and does not see, and how can it bring up the dawn for others? Another interpretation: “if they do not speak according to this word” — now you will see whether they do not say to you according to this word, “Seek unto the ghosts,” although it has no dawn and nothing real in this thing — they will not be ashamed to say it to you.
Isaiah.translator_note: The first explanation is terse and partly obscure in the printed text; translated literally.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And they shall pass this way
Isaiah.english_translation: It refers back to what is said at the beginning of the matter: “and admonished me that I should not walk in the way of this people,” and he explained what the way is: “Say you not: A conspiracy” — to the conspiracy of the ten tribes, who conspired with the kings of Egypt; and he explained their punishment: “And He shall be for a sanctuary,” and “and many among them shall stumble,” and the whole matter.
He who passes along that way — those who leave the Holy One, blessed be He, and rely on the kings of Egypt.
A hard occurrence.
Wearied with hard troubles and with famine; for hardness and siege and oppression and famine will come upon them in the days of siege — three years — in which Sennacherib besieged Samaria.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: curse by their king and by their God
Isaiah.english_translation: And he cursed by the calves and by the *ba'alim* whom they used to serve.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: whether they turn their faces upward
Isaiah.english_translation: To seek from the Holy One, blessed be He, and he will not be heard, for the decree has been sealed; and so Targum Jonathan.
Perhaps he will find a help — for Hoshea son of Elah sent messengers to So king of Egypt (II Kings 10 [as printed]).
Isaiah.translator_note: The printed reference “II Kings 10” does not match; the sending of messengers to So king of Egypt is II Kings 17:4.

Isaiah.english_translation: For they will not help him, and also Shebna went out to Sennacherib, for evil to himself.
Weariness of distress.

Through darkness he is driven away, for an expression of *niduach* is used for darkness, like (Jeremiah 23:12): “Wherefore their way shall be unto them as slippery places in the darkness; they shall be thrust, and fall therein” — and to darkness they are driven.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For is there no gloom to her that was stedfast?
Isaiah.english_translation: For the king of Assyria, who was given to press and to distress her — your land — is not weary and not slothful to come upon them up to three times. One, in the days of Pekah (II Kings 15:29): “who took Ijon, and Abel-beth-maacah, and Kedesh, and the Galilee, all the land of Naphtali”; and that exile was in the fourth year of Ahaz. And [another] in the twelfth year: “And the God of Israel stirred up the spirit of Pul king of Assyria, and he carried them away” — the Reubenites, and the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh — this verse (I Chronicles 5); and this exile was in the twelfth year of Ahaz, the beginning of the rebellion of Hoshea son of Elah, as in the matter that is said (II Kings 17:4): “And the king of Assyria found conspiracy in Hoshea,” etc., after he had been subjected to him for eight years. And the reckoning is not explained openly in Scripture, but one can learn it from the Baraita of Seder Olam. And the third, in the sixth year of Hezekiah, the ninth year of the rebellion of Hoshea, when Samaria was captured — it is the royal city — and all of them were exiled. And this is what is said here: “for there is no weariness for the enemy who presses her” — the land of Israel, mentioned in the matter, “and he looks unto the earth.”
Isaiah.translator_note:
Rashi’s quotations from II Kings 15:29 and I Chronicles 5:26 are abridged.
u|The exact sense of the clause “after he had been subjected to him for eight years” is taken from the printed text as given.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Now the former hath lightly afflicted the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali
Isaiah.english_translation: This middle exile will be light, like that of the first time, which lightly afflicted [the exile of] the land of Zebulun and Naphtali, for even in the second He exiled only the two tribes and the half-tribe that are beyond the Jordan; but the latter, the third journey, is [the heavy one].

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: hath dealt a more grievous blow
Isaiah.english_translation: He swept everything away like one sweeping (*mechabbed*) a house; and one can also explain it as an expression of weight (*koved*), according to the matter of the verse, which began first with the expression “lightly afflicted the land of Zebulun” and “the latter dealt a more grievous blow.” And when Isaiah said this prophecy, the first had already been exiled.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: by the way of the sea
Isaiah.english_translation: Those who dwell on the Sea of Tiberias — it is the land of Naphtali, as it is said (Deuteronomy 33:23): “Possess thou the sea and the south.”
That is the second exile, of Reuben and Gad.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: in the district of the nations
Isaiah.english_translation: It is the entire Land of Israel, which rolled (*golelet*) all the nations toward it, for all desire it and come to it for trade, as in the matter that is said (Jeremiah 3:19): “the heritage of the beauty of the hosts of the nations.” And Jonathan translated another expression.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The people that walked in darkness
Isaiah.english_translation: They are the inhabitants of Jerusalem, who were in darkness from fear of Sennacherib, as in the matter that Hezekiah said (below 37): “This day is a day of trouble, and of rebuke, and of contumely.”
At the fall of Sennacherib.
They became great to all who heard of them, when the nations heard the miracles that were done for them.

[For him,] and not for his enemies; and it is written *lo* with *lamed* and *alef*, because Hezekiah’s joy was not complete, for in that period it was said to him: “Behold, the days come, that all that is in thy house shall be carried [to Babylon]” (below 38 [as printed]).
Isaiah.translator_note: The quoted words are Isaiah 39:6; the printed reference “below 38” does not match.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: according to the joy in harvest
Isaiah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: *ke-chedvat nitzchei krav* (“like the joy of the victors of battle”), which is like the harvest: killers of men, cutters of necks. And Scripture changed its language in order to teach that this miracle was on the night of the harvest of the omer.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: As men rejoice when they divide the spoil
Isaiah.english_translation: Egypt in the days of Moses; for here too they divided the spoil of Cush and Egypt and the desirable things of all the nations, as is written (below 37), that when he returned from [the war with] Tirhakah king of Cush, he came to Jerusalem with all the treasures of Cush and Egypt, as in the matter that is said (below 45): “The labour of Egypt, and the merchandise of Ethiopia, and of the Sabeans … shall come over unto thee,” etc.; and Hezekiah and his people plundered it all.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For the yoke of his burden
Isaiah.english_translation: The yoke that was a burden to Hezekiah, and that bent his shoulder to a heavy load, to bring up heavy tribute; and the rod of Judah with which he was oppressed — in Hezekiah.
That fled together in one night.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: as in the day of Midian
Isaiah.english_translation: In the days of Gideon, for they too fell together in one night, and on the night of the harvest of the omer, as it is said: “and, behold, a cake (*tzelil*) of barley tumbling into the camp of Midian.”
Isaiah.translator_note: JPS (Judges 7:13) reads “a cake of barley bread tumbled into the camp of Midian”; translated as printed.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For every boot stamped with fierceness
Isaiah.english_translation: Some interpret it as an expression of *se'ah* and measure, as our Rabbis expounded it; but according to the plain sense of the language of Scripture it is not possible to explain it from its root, since the *vav* and the *nun* are not part of the root of the word, but are like *sha'on* from *sho'ah*, and *hamon* from *homeh*, and *charon* from *charah*; it is not made reflexive with *hamon* to say *so'an*, but *so'ah*, like *homeh* from *hamon* and *sho'ah* from *sha'on*; and one does not say *sho'an*, *homan*, *choran*. And I say that its interpretation is according to the matter, and it has no parallel in Scripture, and its interpretation is an expression of the shouting of victory in war, for “every *se'on* that stamps with noise” is a voice of victory — any victor in war — with the noise of the tramp of horses and the clatter of shields.
Isaiah.translator_note: The grammatical argument is terse and partly obscure in the printed text; translated literally.

Isaiah.english_translation: Those slain in war are rolled in blood; but this victory has no noise and no blood. “And it shall be for burning, fuel of fire” — *yekod*: a burning of consuming.
Isaiah.translator_note: The last phrase (יקוד מאכולת) is translated literally.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For a child is born unto us
Isaiah.english_translation: Although Ahaz is wicked, his son who was born to him some years ago will be a righteous king for us in his place; and he will be a servant of the Holy One, blessed be He, with His yoke on his shoulder — that he will engage in Torah and observe commandments, and will bend his shoulder to the burden of the Holy One, blessed be He.
The Holy One, blessed be He, who is “Wonderful in counsel,” “mighty God,” “Father forever,” called the name of Hezekiah “Prince of Peace,” for peace and truth will be in his days.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: That the government may be increased
Isaiah.english_translation: For whom is the name called? For the king, who increases the government of the Holy One, blessed be He, upon himself, to fear before Him.

An expression of authority (*sarar*) — this is for the answer to others. But one can say that also “Prince of Peace” is among the names of the Holy One, blessed be He, and the calling of this name is not for an actual name but for a name of greatness and authority, like “and call a name in Beth-lehem” and like “and I will make thee a name”; so too here, “and his name is called” — He gave him a name and dominion.
Isaiah.translator_note: Compare Ruth 4:11 and II Samuel 7:9 for the phrases quoted.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: of peace there be no end
Isaiah.english_translation: That is given to him, there is no end: that he had peace from all his sides; and this “no end” is not an expression of cessation forever, but no end to his surroundings. “Upon the throne of the kingdom of David” there will be this peace, “through justice and righteousness” that Hezekiah did.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And of peace there be no end
Isaiah.english_translation: This *vav* is the correction of the word: he increased dominion on his shoulder; and what reward will be paid to him? Behold, for his peace there is no end and no limit.
Isaiah.translator_note: The explanation of the *vav* is terse; translated literally.

Isaiah.english_translation: The “forever” of Hezekiah is all his days; and so we find that Hannah said of Samuel, “and abide there for ever” (I Samuel 1:22). And for the answer to others who say that it is he who is there, one can answer them: What is “from henceforth”? Did he not come until the end of three hundred years?

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The zeal of the LORD of hosts
Isaiah.english_translation: That He was zealous for Zion because Aram and Pekah took counsel against it.

And Ahaz is not worthy of this, and even the merit of the fathers has ended. Addition: And our Rabbis said: The Holy One, blessed be He, wished to make Hezekiah the Messiah, and Sennacherib Gog and Magog. The ministering angels said before the Holy One, blessed be He: He who cut off the doors of the Temple and sent them to the king of Assyria — shall he be made Messiah? Immediately Scripture closed it.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The Lord sent a word into Jacob
Isaiah.english_translation: The prophecy that he prophesied about the punishment of Pekah son of Remaliah.
From now on it will be fulfilled in them.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: in pride and in arrogancy of heart
Isaiah.english_translation: What they were saying in pride and in arrogance of heart.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The bricks are fallen, but we will build with hewn stones
Isaiah.english_translation: The kings who were ours before Pekah reigned, such as Jehoahaz the son of Jehu, in whose days they were diminished, as it is said (II Kings 13:7): “for the king of Aram destroyed them” — they were low, and they went away like a shaky building of bricks that falls; but this one, who is now strong, is like a building of hewn stones; and so cedars are better than sycamores for building.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the adversaries of Rezin against him
Isaiah.english_translation: They trust in the fact that they leaned on Rezin king of Aram, and the Holy One, blessed be He, will exalt the king of Assyria against him and will entangle him, to incite him to come upon him — so I heard. And I say: “his enemies” — he says this with regard to the Shekhinah: the Holy One, blessed be He, will entangle His enemies one with another, nation against nation, Aram and the Philistines against Israel, and Israel against one another, as is said below in the matter of Manasseh: “Manasseh against Ephraim,” etc.
Aram did them harm from the east in the days of Jehoahaz and Joash; and the Philistines did them harm from behind, for the Philistines are to the west of them.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For all this His anger is not turned away
Isaiah.english_translation: And still His hand is stretched out until He brings upon them Sennacherib. Another interpretation: “Aram on the east and the Philistines behind” were destroying Judah in the days of Ahaz, as is explained (II Chronicles 25 [as printed]); and Isaiah was lamenting these troubles for Israel and for Judah.
Isaiah.translator_note: The printed reference “II Chronicles 25” does not match; the invasions in the days of Ahaz are described in II Chronicles 28.

Isaiah.english_translation: To the Holy One, blessed be He, who brings upon him these blows.
An expression of kings and rulers.
*Arcvolt* in Old French; that is, those who hover over them like this arch (*kipah*).
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is ארקוול״ר; Darmesteter (1909) lists this verse (“Voûte”) with several forms and derives the word from *arcum* + *vollum*; the exact reading is as printed.

Isaiah.english_translation: And this too is a small arch, and because it is bent like a reed (*agmon*) he calls it *agmon*. And in the Baraita of Samuel we find that there are constellations in the firmament that are appointed, and these are their names; and here the prophet said that all their sages who prophesy to them and gaze at the stars concerning what will come upon them, the LORD will cut off from them.
Isaiah.translator_note: The names of the constellations are not listed in the printed text.

Isaiah.english_translation: *Me'asheri* — my guides, like “My foot hath held fast to His steps” (Job 23:11); and *me'usharav* — those who learned paths from the paths of the one who goes astray (*sa''a*).
Isaiah.translator_note: The printed word in the Job quotation is *be-ashuri* (“in my steps”); the verse reads *be-ashuro*.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: they that are led of them are destroyed
Isaiah.english_translation: Those who tread in the way of those who lead astray, who guide them in these ways: ways that are hidden and confused, with no opening to go out of them. And an expression of swallowing (*bilu'a*) applies to the way, as in the matter that is said in another place: “O My people, they that lead thee cause thee to err, and the way of thy paths they swallowed” (above 3).
Isaiah.translator_note: JPS renders the last words of Isaiah 3:12 as “And destroy the way of thy paths”; Rashi takes the verb as “swallow.”

Isaiah.english_translation: Wicked, like “a seed of evil-doers” (above 1).
Their wickedness will burn in them and consume them like fire.
Theirs: it will consume the rebels and the transgressors among them.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: it kindleth in the thickets of the forest
Isaiah.english_translation: In the lowly of the people; *sevakhei* — thickets of branches.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: they roll upward in thick clouds of smoke
Isaiah.english_translation: They will be confused and shut in by the strength of the smoke of the burning; and *yit'abku* — every expression of *nevach* — the root of the word is only *bach*, like “*mi-bichei* of rivers” (Job 28:11), “the valley of Baca” (Psalms 84); and the *nun* comes to it at times, and here an *alef* has come into it in place of a *nun*, like the *alef* of “*avachat* of the sword” (Ezekiel 21:20) and the *alef* of “*achavati* in your ears” (Job 13).

Jonathan translated: *charuka ar'a* (“the land is scorched”). And it is difficult in my eyes to explain it so, for he should have said *ne'tema ha-aretz*. And since it has no parallel in Scripture — neither the language of the Targum nor another language — I explain it according to its matter: in the wrath of the Holy One, blessed be He, this smoke … to the land; and it is an expression decreed upon the land, or an expression of melting (*netach*), and reached the land.
Isaiah.translator_note: The sentence “in the wrath … this smoke *ne'tam* to the land” is translated literally; the verb *ne'tam* is left unexplained, and the last sentence is terse.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: one snatcheth on the right hand
Isaiah.english_translation: They will plunder and spoil one another, on the right or on the left, and nothing will be found for them.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: They eat every man the flesh of his own arm
Isaiah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: *gevar nichsoi kerivoi yivzun* (“a man will plunder the possessions of his relatives”).
Manasseh will join with Ephraim.
With Manasseh; and together they will join against Judah.
Writs of iniquity — forged documents.
It is an Arabic expression, like *mikhtavin* (the *mem* with a *chirik*, the *kaf* with a *sheva*, and the *tav* with a *kamatz*) in the Hebrew language.
Isaiah.translator_note: The printed text says “Arabic” (ערבי); translated as printed.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: To turn aside the needy from judgment
Isaiah.english_translation: By means of false documents, the poor from the judgment of merit that is proper for them.
That the Holy One, blessed be He, will visit your iniquities upon you.
An expression of destruction.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: To whom will you flee for help
Isaiah.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He, is not at your help.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: where will you leave your glory
Isaiah.english_translation: All the glory that you gather from robbery, when you go into exile.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: They can do nought except crouch under the captives
Isaiah.english_translation: “In the place where there is no kneeling”: and no one of you shall understand that there was not there the kneeling of the lying-down in that place; in that place you will be bound — that is, outside your land you will be bound; and so Jonathan translated: *bar min arekhon asirin titasarun* (“outside your land, bound you will be bound”).
Isaiah.translator_note: The first clause is terse in the printed text; translated literally.

Isaiah.english_translation: Place, like “abide you every man in his place” (Exodus 16:29).
And in that place slain men will fall.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: O Asshur, the rod of Mine anger
Isaiah.english_translation: For I made Assyria the rod of My anger, to chastise My people with it.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: In whose hand as a staff is Mine indignation
Isaiah.english_translation: My indignation is in the hand of the sons of Assyria.
Israel.
Sennacherib.
That the decree is from Me and I send him; “he thinks” — *cuider* in Old French.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is קוויידייר; Darmesteter (1909) lists this verse (“Il ne pensera pas ainsi”) and reads *cuydiér*.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Neither doth his heart think so
Isaiah.english_translation: That I sent him on a matter of money, to plunder and to take spoil; for in his heart is to destroy everything in his pride.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Are not my princes all of them kings
Isaiah.english_translation: Therefore his heart is lofty.

Just as the sons of Carchemish are princes and rulers, so are the sons of Calno. Therefore, “if not like Arpad,” which is of the dominions of Hamath, which I took from the hand of Aram; and “if not like Damascus,” which I took from the hand of Aram, so I did to Samaria. “If not like Arpad” — *Chamat* is in the construct state, “like Arpad of Hamath”; therefore it is pointed with a *patach*.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Whose graven images did exceed them of Jerusalem and of Samaria
Isaiah.english_translation: They were from Jerusalem and from Samaria; hence the wicked of Israel supplied the likenesses of their idols to all the nations around them. And since the worshippers of the idols of Samaria and Jerusalem fell into my hand and their idols did not save them, so Samaria and Jerusalem will not be saved.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: as I have done unto Samaria and her idols
Isaiah.english_translation: This he will say after he conquers Samaria.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: when the Lord hath performed His whole work upon mount Zion and on Jerusalem
Isaiah.english_translation: But it was not as he imagined; rather, after the Holy One, blessed be He, finishes all His work and His vengeance on Israel and on the outskirts of the cities of Judah, and from that fear the children of Zion and Jerusalem will be humbled to return to Me, I will make known to the king of Assyria that not by his strength did he prevail.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I will punish the fruit of the arrogant heart of the king of Assyria
Isaiah.english_translation: For the fruit that he increased and multiplied of the greatness of the heart of the king of Assyria, to boast in his strength falsely — fruit of the greatness (*craysement de grandéze* in Old French) of the heart of Sennacherib.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is קריישמנ״ס דגרנדיי״א; Darmesteter (1909) lists this verse (“L'accroissement d'orgueil”) and reads *craysement de grandéze*.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the glory of his haughty looks
Isaiah.english_translation: Because he glorified himself in his pride; *tiferet* — *vantement* in Old French.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is ונטמנ״ט; Darmesteter (1909) lists this verse (“Fierté”) with several forms and reads *vantance* (the act of boasting); the printed form is closer to *vantement*.

Isaiah.english_translation: Coarseness of spirit, as in the matter that is said: “haughty of eye and proud of heart” (Psalms 101:5).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: By the strength of my hand I have done it
Isaiah.english_translation: All my might is not from the Holy One, blessed be He.
My wisdom.
Their standing and their position.
I brought them down from their greatness.
Many inhabitants; *kabir* — *pluysors* in Old French.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is פולשור״ש; Darmesteter (1909) lists this verse (“Nombre de”) and reads *pluysors* (modern *plusieurs*).

Isaiah.english_translation: Like nests of birds that are ownerless.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: as one gathereth eggs that are forsaken
Isaiah.english_translation: And as a man gathers forsaken eggs that their mother forsook, and none protests, to cover over them.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: none that moved the wing, Or that opened mouth, or chirped
Isaiah.english_translation: All this language applies to birds, because he likened the exiles to a nest of birds and to forsaken eggs; he said this expression: the father and mother did not chirp over them.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Should the axe boast itself against him that heweth therewith
Isaiah.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He, says: You should not have boasted in this, for you are only like My axe, and I am the one who hews with you, taking vengeance through you on My enemies. You are the saw, and I am the one who wields it; and is it the way of a saw to boast over the one who wields it? *Saw* — *meyra* in Old French.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is מייר״א; I did not match it in Darmesteter (his entry for this verse, “La cognée”, concerns the word for axe: *doledoire*). My transliteration is of the printed form only.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: As if a rod should move them that lift it up
Isaiah.english_translation: As if the rod were wielding itself and the hand of the one who lifts it; but does not a man wield a rod?

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: lift up him that is not wood
Isaiah.english_translation: It is not the wood that lifts, but the man who lifts.
Under their garments they will be burned; garments are what honour (*mechabdim*) a person.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: A burning like the burning of fire
Isaiah.english_translation: A burning will burn, like the burning of fire. And Midrash Aggadah: here He repaid the descendants of Shem the honour that Shem did for his father, when he covered the nakedness of Noah his father, as it is said (Genesis 16 [as printed]): “And Shem and Japheth took,” etc.
Isaiah.translator_note: The printed reference “Genesis 16” does not match; the quotation is Genesis 9:23.

Isaiah.english_translation: The Torah in which Hezekiah engages will be a fire for Sennacherib.
The Holy One, blessed be He. Another interpretation: “his Holy One” — the righteous of the generation.
His officers and his mighty men.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the glory of his forest and of his fruitful field
Isaiah.english_translation: They are the multitude of his armies.
A high forest.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: as when a sick man wasteth away
Isaiah.english_translation: Because he likened them to trees of the forest, he likened their punishment to a worm that saws with its mouth and grinds the wood, and calls it *sas*, like “and the worm shall eat them like wool” (below 51).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: as when a sick man wasteth away
Isaiah.english_translation: Like the sawing of the one who saws.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: as when a sick man wasteth away
Isaiah.english_translation: Like the *masos* of a sawyer, which is ground fine, fine, since the worm grinds; so the ash and the burning of their bodies would be fine. *Masos* is what is ground and falls through a worm; *nosés* is the worm.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the remnant of the trees of his forest
Isaiah.english_translation: Those who remain of his armies.
Easy to count, for they are few, and a youth can write them. And our Rabbis said: ten remained of them, for there is no child who cannot write a small *yod*.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: stay upon him that smote them
Isaiah.english_translation: To lean on the kings of Egypt, who were the first of those who oppressed them.
The remnant among them will return to the Holy One, blessed be He.
Who showed them might in the matter of Sennacherib.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For though thy people, O Israel, be as the sand of the sea
Isaiah.english_translation: To Hezekiah the prophet said: If your people be as the sand of the sea, the remnant that will return in it to the good will sweep away the destruction determined to come upon them, and will hold it back from coming, through the righteousness with which it conducts itself.
You will see that the Holy One, blessed be He, executes (judgment) upon the wicked, and you will be humbled and return to Him.
Because I know that you will return to Him — Hezekiah and his company. (Another interpretation: “Therefore” — an expression of oath: “Therefore, in truth.”)

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: though he smite thee with the rod
Isaiah.english_translation: With the rod of his mouth he will curse and revile you through Rabshakeh.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: lift up his staff against thee
Isaiah.english_translation: To terrify, as he did to Egypt. And one can further explain “with the rod he will smite you” — that until now he has smitten you with a rod, and is accustomed to lift his staff and his terror over you, in the manner of the Egyptians. In the name of Rabbi Menachem; Rabbi Joseph told me.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For yet a very little while, and the indignation shall be accomplished
Isaiah.english_translation: A very few days, and it will be finished — My indignation that was given to a rod in the hand of Assyria, as it says above: “and the staff in their hand is My indignation.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Mine anger shall be to their destruction
Isaiah.english_translation: That was for a rod will return upon their destruction (*tavlitam*) — an expression of “it is perversion (*tevel*)” (Leviticus 20:12) — for the reviling and blasphemy with which the servants of the king of Assyria blasphemed Me.
Isaiah.translator_note: JPS renders Leviticus 20:12 “they have wrought corruption.”

Isaiah.english_translation: And to rouse against him.
A blow of chastisements.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: as in the slaughter of Midian at the Rock of Oreb
Isaiah.english_translation: Who were killed in one night, and the kings who fled from them and escaped — Oreb was killed at the rock of Oreb, as is explained in the Book of Judges; so too this one, after he returns to his land, will die there by the sword.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: as His rod was over the sea
Isaiah.english_translation: And further He will rouse against him His rod that was over the sea, against Pharaoh and his host.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: so shall He lift it up after the manner of Egypt
Isaiah.english_translation: And carried him off from the world, in the way that He carried off Egypt.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the yoke shall be destroyed by reason of fatness
Isaiah.english_translation: Sennacherib, on account of Hezekiah, who was pleasant to his generation like oil (*shemen*); and our Rabbis explained: on account of the oil of Hezekiah, which burned in the synagogues and in the houses of study, for he led them to engage in Torah, as in the matter that is said: “which the men of Hezekiah copied out,” etc. (Proverbs 25).

He enumerates the journeys that Sennacherib made, when he came upon the cities of Judah to come to Jerusalem on the day of his fall: Aiath, Migron, and Michmas; Ramah, Gibeah of Saul, Bath-gallim, Laishah, Anathoth, Madmenah, Gebim. All of them are places.
An expression of lodging.
Fled; all of them fled from before his armies.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Cry thou with a shrill voice
Isaiah.english_translation: To warn the people.
To the sound of the shofar, and flee away; and so “poor Anathoth.”

They gathered to flee. And our Rabbis expounded “Cry thou with a shrill voice,” and the whole verse, in a different Midrash, in Aggadat Chelek, and they fixed the journeys at ten; but Jonathan translated all of them as names of places.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: This very day shall he halt at Nob
Isaiah.english_translation: All this way he pressed on in order to stand at Nob while it was still day, because his astrologers said to him: If you attack it today, you will conquer it. And when he stood at Nob and saw Jerusalem small, he did not heed the words of his astrologers, and began to wave his hand in pride: “And over a city like this I have alarmed all these armies? Lodge here tonight, and tomorrow each man will throw his stone at it.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: at the mount of the daughter of Zion
Isaiah.english_translation: *Har* — the daughter of Zion, to the mount of the daughter of Zion.
Isaiah.translator_note: This short gloss is translated literally; its sense is not certain.

Isaiah.english_translation: In that night.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Shall lop the boughs with terror
Isaiah.english_translation: He will chop off its boughs, the main limbs of its trees.

With a saw that cuts off the branches. This *pa'orah* is not an expression of a winepress (*gat*), for it is not written with a *vav*, like “I have trodden the winepress (*purah*) alone” (below 63) and like “to draw out fifty from the press (*purah*)” (Haggai 2:16), but with an *alef*, like “and its boughs (*pa'orotav*) became long” (Ezekiel 31:5); and *mesa'ef* is an expression of cutting off branches — *esbrancher* in Old French — like “and consume its branches (*se'ifeha*)” (below 27), and so “in the branches (*bis'ifeiha*) of the fruitful tree” (below 17).
Isaiah.translator_note:
Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is אישברנקיי״ר; Darmesteter (1909) lists this verse under 10:33 (“Il va ébrancher”) and reads *esbranchiér*.
The printed lemma of this comment is *be-ma'aratzah* (“with terror”), but the comment begins by explaining the saw and then the word *pa'orah*; translated as printed.

Isaiah.english_translation: With an instrument of destruction, which terrifies (*ho'ertz*) and shatters them.
The kings and the princes.
An expression of *gidu'a* applies only to trees and to a hard thing.
This too is an expression of cutting, like “as the shaking (*ke-nokef*) of an olive-tree”; and *venikaf* is a passive expression.
The important and mighty branches.
“And the Lebanon”: the thickness of his forest and of his fruitful field — they are the multitude of his armies.
Isaiah.translator_note: The words “And Lebanon shall fall by a mighty one” stand at the start of 11:1 in the site’s JPS verse division, so the highlighted words here are only the nearest ones in 10:34.

Isaiah.english_translation: “By a mighty one shall they fall” — they will fall by means of an angel. Another interpretation: “by a mighty one” — in the merit of Hezekiah, who is their mighty one and the ruler of Israel, as it is said: “and his mighty one shall be of him” (Jeremiah 30:21).
Isaiah.translator_note: JPS renders Jeremiah 30:21 “And their prince shall be of themselves.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: there shall come forth a shoot out of the stock of Jesse
Isaiah.english_translation: And if you say: behold, this is consolation for Hezekiah and his people, that they will not fall into his hand — but what will be with the exile that he exiled to Halah and Habor? Perhaps their hope is lost? It is not lost; in the end our King Messiah will come and redeem them.
A rod of kingship.
An expression of a suckling shoot of a tree.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: a twig shall grow forth out of his roots
Isaiah.english_translation: And in the whole matter and at its end: “And it shall come to pass in that day, that the Lord will set His hand again the second time”; so this prophecy was said for the comfort of the exiles from Assyria. (The copyist said: In the days of my youth I raised a difficulty to ask several Geonim about what my grandfather the Rema, of blessed memory, wrote in his gloss on the laws of Rosh Hashanah, that *egoz* (nut) is, in gematria, *chet* (sin) — but is it not also, in gematria, *tov* (good)? And I resolved it on the basis of the Zohar, regarding what R. Eleazar asked his father R. Shimon bar Yochai about what the Sages, of blessed memory, said: “and there arose not a prophet in Israel, but among the nations of the world there did arise,” and they counted Balaam, etc.; and he answered him from the verse “God hath made even the one as well as the other” (*gam zeh le'umat zeh*), etc., until even though there is holiness in impurity, it is forbidden to learn it, as it is said, “but of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil thou shalt not eat”; and it will be understood that, although *egoz* is, in gematria, *tov*, since it has a shell (*klipah*) whose gematria is *chet*, it is not eaten on Rosh Hashanah; and those Geonim nodded their heads to me. End of his words.)
Isaiah.translator_note: The parenthesis is not Rashi’s: it is a note added by a later copyist or editor, printed inside the commentary. I have translated it literally; the abbreviation א״מ before “my grandfather” is left untranslated.

Isaiah.english_translation: He will be filled with the spirit of the fear of the LORD; and in Old French *iraunmirloy*.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is איראונמירלו״י; Darmesteter (1909) lists this verse (“Et il n'animera”) with several manuscript forms, one in the margin by a later hand close to the printed form, and reads *éd énosmera illuy* (“and he will make him smell”). My transliteration is of the printed form.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: he shall not judge after the sight of his eyes
Isaiah.english_translation: For with the wisdom of the Holy One, blessed be He, within him he will know and understand who is innocent and who is guilty.
An expression of gentle and soft.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: he shall smite the land with the rod of his mouth
Isaiah.english_translation: As its Targum: *u-yimcheh chayyavei ar'a* (“and he will smite the guilty of the land”).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: with the breath of his lips
Isaiah.english_translation: *U-vi-mmalel sefavvateih* (“and by the speech of his lips”).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: righteousness shall be the girdle of his loins
Isaiah.english_translation: Targum: *ve-yehon tzaddikaya sechor sechor leih* (“and the righteous will be round about him”), clinging to him like a girdle.
A fattened ox.
And sported.

A hole in the earth in which the snake nests; *crote* in Old French. *Pethen* — a snake that, when it grows old, becomes deaf, and is called *pethen*, for it no longer has a charm, as it is said (Psalms 58): “which hearkeneth not to the voice of charmers.”
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is קרו״ט; Darmesteter (1909) lists this verse (“La grotte”) and reads *crote*.

Isaiah.english_translation: Jonathan translated: *chizu gilgalei einei chivvei chorman*; and Menachem interpreted it as an expression of a hole and holes of earth, and so “*Ur* of the Chaldees” (Genesis 11), and so “in the *urim* glorify the LORD” (below 24).
Isaiah.translator_note: The Targum phrase is left in transliteration. JPS renders Isaiah 24:15 “in the regions of light.”

Isaiah.english_translation: A child weaned from his mother’s breasts.

Targum Jonathan: *yadohi yoshit* (“he will stretch out his hand”); like “the *hed* of the mountains” (Ezekiel 7:7) and like “*heidad*” (below 15 [as printed]), which is an expression of raising a voice — this too is an expression of raising; and the final *heh* comes in it, the root falling out, like *asah*, *banah*, *kanah*.
Isaiah.translator_note: The printed reference “below 15” does not match; the word *heidad* is at Isaiah 16:9.

Isaiah.english_translation: To know the LORD.
For peoples to lift up an ensign, to be gathered to him.
Like He acquired them from Egypt, for their redemption was clear, without subjugation; but the redemption of the Second Temple is not counted, for they were subject to Cyrus.
They are the islands of Kittim — Greece.
*Perche* in Old French; and it will be a sign for gathering to him, and to bring the exiles of Israel as a gift to him.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is פירקא; Darmesteter (1909) lists this verse (“L'étendard (perche)”) and reads *perche*.

Isaiah.english_translation: The Messiah son of Joseph and the Messiah son of David will not envy one another.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: they shall fly down upon the shoulder of the Philistines on the west
Isaiah.english_translation: Israel will fly and run with one shoulder against the Philistines, who are to the west of the Land of Israel, and will conquer their land, like “they murder with one shoulder (*shichma*)” (Hosea 6:9), “with one shoulder” (Zephaniah 3); and so Targum Jonathan: *ve-yitchabrun kitfa chad le-mimcha Pelishtai di be-ma'arva* (“and they will join shoulder to shoulder to smite the Philistines who are in the west”).
Isaiah.translator_note: In Hosea 6:9 JPS renders *shichma* as “toward Shechem”; in Zephaniah 3:9, “with one consent.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the children of Ammon shall obey them
Isaiah.english_translation: As its Targum: *yishtam'un lehon* (“they shall obey them”) — they accept their commandments upon themselves.
To dry it up so that the exiles of Israel will pass through it from Egypt.
The River Euphrates, so that the exiles from Assyria may pass through it.
It has no parallel in Scripture, and according to the matter it is to be interpreted as the strength of his wind.
Into seven parts, so that the seven exiles mentioned above may pass through it — from Assyria and from Egypt, etc.; and “from the islands of the sea” is not from the same side.
In its midst the exiles.
On dry land.
In the midst of the water, for the remnant of His people.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I will give thanks unto Thee
Isaiah.english_translation: When you see this.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: though Thou was angry with me
Isaiah.english_translation: For You were angry with me and exiled me, and my exile atoned for me; and now my iniquity is accepted, and Your anger has turned back, and You comfort me. And Jonathan translated: “I will thank You, O LORD, for I sinned against You, and therefore You were angry with me; and were it not for Your mercies I would not have been worthy that Your anger turn back and that You comfort me; and behold, Your anger has turned back from me.”

The strength and the praise of the Holy One, blessed be He, He has been for me for salvation; and one should not explain *uzzi* as “my strength,” for we have not found in Scripture *uzzi* pointed with a *chataf kamatz*, but with a *shuruk*, *uzzi*, except in three places where it is in construct next to *ve-zimrat*; and *ve-zimrat* is not like *zimrati*, but perforce *ve-zimrat* is attached to the word after it. Therefore I say that the *yod* of *uzzi* is only like the *yod* of “dwellers of the bush” (*shochni sneh*) (Deuteronomy 33).
Isaiah.translator_note: The grammatical argument is terse and partly obscure in the printed text; translated literally.

Isaiah.english_translation: Until now His name was divided, and at the fall of Amalek it became whole; and so it says: “for a hand upon the throne of Yah” (Exodus 17:16) — the throne is not whole, and the Name is not whole, until there is war for the LORD against Amalek.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And He is become my salvation
Isaiah.english_translation: Like *hayah li li-yeshuah*; and it is the way of Scripture to speak so, like “and he that regarded not the word of the LORD left his servants and his cattle” (Exodus 9), and further in Chronicles (II 10): “But as for the children of Israel that dwelt in the cities of Judah, Rehoboam reigned over them” (*va-yimlokh*) — he should have said *malakh aleihem Rechav'am*.
*Ve-tekablun ulfan chadat* (Targum: “and you will receive new teaching”).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Out of the wells of salvation
Isaiah.english_translation: For their heart will expand through the salvation that will come to them, and the secrets of the Torah that were forgotten in Babylon because of the troubles will be revealed to them.
His deeds.
To praise, for He is exalted.
A burden of punishment that is upon Babylon.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Set you up an ensign upon the high mountain
Isaiah.english_translation: To gather on a mountain that is quiet and secure in tranquillity; lift up an ensign for the nations, and raise a voice to those who gather, that they come upon it.
To them, to those who are far away, who cannot hear, and they will see the sign of the waving of the hand and come into the gates of the nobles of the princes of Babylon.

Like “*be-fitchei*” — “and she dwelt in her father’s house” (Genesis 31 [as printed]) — hidden in her father’s house; and Menachem ben Saruk interpreted: swords, like “yet were they *petichot*” (Psalms 55).
Isaiah.translator_note:
The printed reference “Genesis 31” does not obviously match; the words “and she dwelt in her father’s house” occur at Genesis 38:11, and the connection to this word is not clear in the printed text.
JPS renders Psalms 55:22 “drawn swords.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I have commanded My consecrated ones
Isaiah.english_translation: That they should come and begin to provoke them — and they are Persia and Media, the men of Cyrus and Darius, whom I summoned for this.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Yea, I have called My mighty ones for mine anger
Isaiah.english_translation: To work My burning anger in them, for they are the exultants of My pride, in whom I take glory.
They are the mighty men of Media and Persia.
Of Babylon.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: As destruction from the Almighty shall it come
Isaiah.english_translation: Like a day of plunder, from the Holy One, blessed be He, it will come.
Of Babylon.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Pangs and throes shall take hold of them
Isaiah.english_translation: They are an expression of the pains of a woman who crouches to give birth, for the hinges (*tzirei*) of the doors of her womb are loosened to open.
*Chil* and *chalchalah* are an expression of trembling.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: They shall look aghast one at another
Isaiah.english_translation: The children of Babylon, at those who besiege them, for they are strange.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Their faces shall be faces of flame
Isaiah.english_translation: I say that their faces are yellow and greatly terrified; or one can say that they are with the thinkers of thoughts, and the children of Babylon (he likened them to them on account of astonishment).
Isaiah.translator_note: The second explanation is terse and partly obscure in the printed text; the parenthesis looks like a later addition.

Isaiah.english_translation: Its sinners.
Their constellations (*mazzalot*).
They will shine, and so “when His lamp shined (*bi-hilo*)” (Job 29:3), and so “the light when it shined (*yahel*)” (Job 31).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The sun shall be darkened in his going forth
Isaiah.english_translation: From their distress it will seem to them as if the sun were darkened.
Upon their land.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I will make man more rare than fine gold
Isaiah.english_translation: On that very night I will honour Daniel more than fine gold, when they brought him to read the writing, “*Mene mene tekel u-farsin*” (Daniel 5:25): “Then Belshazzar said, and they clothed Daniel with purple,” etc.
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi quotes Daniel 5:29 in Aramaic; JPS renders “Then commanded Belshazzar.”

Isaiah.english_translation: A gathering of the gold of Ophir.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I will make the heavens to tremble
Isaiah.english_translation: All its host will tremble; and it says (below 14): “How art thou fallen from heaven, O day-star,” and afterwards “How art thou cut down to the ground, that didst weaken the nations”; so too here, first “I will make the heavens to tremble,” and afterwards “and the earth shall be shaken” — its inhabitants will shake at the sound of its fall, for they will be astonished at the matter.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And it shall come to pass
Isaiah.english_translation: The inhabitant of Babylon.
From its place.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Every one that is found shall be thrust through
Isaiah.english_translation: Outside, he will be pierced.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: every one that is caught shall fall by the sword
Isaiah.english_translation: Upon the inhabitants of the city, who are gathered in with them in the siege — he will fall by the sword when the city is captured. *Nispeh* is an expression of “to add (*sefot*) the watered to the thirsty” (Deuteronomy 29), “add (*sefu*) year to year” (below 29), “add (*sefu*) your burnt-offerings to your sacrifices” (Jeremiah 7); *acoillier* in Old French.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is אקוייליי״ר; Darmesteter (1909) lists this verse (“Refugié”) and reads *akoylid* (modern *accueilli*).

Isaiah.english_translation: They will be split open; and so “young men shall they dash in pieces (*tiratashna*).”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I will stir up the Medes against them
Isaiah.english_translation: Darius the Mede killed Belshazzar, and so it says of him: “In that night Belshazzar was slain” (Daniel 5:30), and “Darius the Mede received the kingdom” (there, 6).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: they shall not delight in it
Isaiah.english_translation: They care only to kill and to take vengeance for all the evil that the kings of Babylon did to all the peoples.
Of the Medes.
Of Babylon.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: shall dash the young men in pieces
Isaiah.english_translation: They will split them open with their arrows, which they shoot with their bows.
Tender babes.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And Babylon, the glory of kingdoms
Isaiah.english_translation: Two punishments came upon it in two years: Darius killed Belshazzar and reigned a year, and in the second year it was overturned like the overturning of Sodom, from heaven. And so we learned in Seder Olam (Jeremiah 51:46): “And there shall come in the year the rumour” — of Darius; and after it, “in the year the rumour.” “And Babylon shall be the glory of kingdoms,” etc., for it was the seat and head of the kingdoms, and for it was the splendour of the pride of the Chaldeans; now “it shall be like the overturning of Sodom.”
Isaiah.translator_note: The second half of the Seder Olam citation is terse in the printed text; translated literally.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Neither shall the Arabian pitch tent there
Isaiah.english_translation: Like *lo ye'ahel*: he will not spread a tent there, even an Arab, whose way is to dwell in tents and to move their cattle from place to place; it will not find favour in their eyes to fix their tents there, for it will not even be fit for the pasturing of flocks. And do not wonder at *lo yahel*, which is explained as if it had an *alef*, for there are many places where the sound of a letter stands in place of the letter; and so (Job 35:11) “*malefenu mi-behemot aretz*” — like *me-alefenu*; and so (Proverbs 17:4) “a liar *mezin*” — in the language of *havayah*, like “a liar *ma'zin*.”
Isaiah.translator_note: JPS renders Job 35:11 “Who teacheth us more than the beasts of the earth” and Proverbs 17:4 “a liar giveth ear.”

Isaiah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: *tamun*; they are weasels (*nemiyot*); *martrines* in Old French.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is מרטרינ״ש; Darmesteter (1909) lists this verse (the printed French gloss of his entry is unclear in my copy) and reads *martrines* (martens).

Isaiah.english_translation: I do not know what kind of animal they are. (*Ochim* — an expression of thorns and briers and thistles.)
Isaiah.translator_note: The parenthesis looks like a later addition to the commentary.

Isaiah.english_translation: Demons.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And jackals shall howl in their castles
Isaiah.english_translation: And cats will dwell in his palaces.
Like “and she shall respond there” (*ve-anatah*, Hosea 2) and “his dens (*u-me'onotav*) with ravin” (Nahum 2). And one can further explain: *ve-anah* is an expression of answering with a voice.
They will respond in the halls of their delight.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: her days shall not be prolonged
Isaiah.english_translation: The days of her prosperity will not be prolonged, for Israel had already been promised (Jeremiah 29): “After seventy years are accomplished for Babylon I will remember you”; and that remembrance will be through Cyrus king of Persia, who will take the kingship from Babylon after Darius the Mede; for both of them, Media and Persia, joined against them, and stipulated between them: *i minan malkhei minaikhu aparkhei*.
Isaiah.translator_note: The Aramaic stipulation at the end is left in transliteration; I read it as “[if] from us, kings; from you, governors,” but this is not certain.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For the LORD will have compassion on Jacob
Isaiah.english_translation: To keep for them the promise of their redemption from the hand of Babylon.
In the future He will redeem them with a complete redemption.
And they will be added; and so “attach me, I pray thee” (I Samuel 2:36), and so “from cleaving unto the inheritance of the LORD” (there, 27 [as printed]).
Isaiah.translator_note: The printed reference “there, 27” does not match; the quoted words are I Samuel 26:19. JPS renders I Samuel 2:36 “Put me, I pray thee.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: shall possess them in the land of the LORD
Isaiah.english_translation: They will be inherited from them; and so “and you may make them an inheritance” (Leviticus 25).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: they shall rule over their oppressors
Isaiah.english_translation: An expression of dominion and oppression, like “thou shalt not rule over him” (there).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the LORD shall give thee rest
Isaiah.english_translation: Scripture is speaking of Israel.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: from thy travail, and from thy trouble
Isaiah.english_translation: That the king of Babylon grieved and angered you; and when you see his fall, He will give you rest, for you will go out free.
An expression of increase of pride and heavy burden; and our Rabbis expounded: those who say *medod ve-hav* (“measure and bring”).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: hath broken the staff of the wicked
Isaiah.english_translation: Who smote peoples in wrath.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: With a persecution that none restrained
Isaiah.english_translation: Persecuted (*murdaf*): every nation and nation was persecuted by him, without his restraining himself from pursuing and from chasing after each nation and nation.
This joyful song they burst forth: the whole earth is at rest and quiet.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Yea, the cypresses rejoice at thee
Isaiah.english_translation: Even the rulers rejoiced (*af shiltonin chadiu*) — they rejoiced at your fall.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: To meet thee at thy coming
Isaiah.english_translation: When you go down to Gehinnom; and what is the stirring? To rouse to meet them.
Giants who lie there.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: all the chief ones of the earth
Isaiah.english_translation: All the kings of the idolaters, the princes and rulers; Scripture likens them to bulls and cows and he-goats, like “Many bulls have encompassed me” (Psalms 22:13) and like “kine of Bashan that are in Samaria” (Amos 4:1); and here it likens them to he-goats.
He cast down.
In Gehinnom — all the kings of the nations.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Art thou also become weak as we?
Isaiah.english_translation: We are astonished: how has evil come upon you, that you too have become sick, to be like us, to die?

Psalteries and harps that were played before you. And one can interpret *hemiyat nevalecha* as the commotion (*hemiyat*) of the sons of *naval* — the doers of obscenity (*nevalah*) among your armies. And it seems to me that in the Great Masorah it joined this with “and the melody of psalteries” (there, 5) in an alphabet of two languages.
Isaiah.translator_note: The reference “there, 5” is not resolved in the printed text, and the Masoretic remark is terse; translated literally.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: O day-star, son of the morning
Isaiah.english_translation: The star Nogah, which gives light like the morning star. This is the lament upon the prince of Babylon, said of one who will fall from heaven.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: How art thou cut down to the ground
Isaiah.english_translation: You, Nebuchadnezzar, who used to weaken the nations by casting lots over them — over the kings: which of them would serve you on such-and-such a day, and which on such-and-such a day; and our Rabbis expounded that he used to cast lots over the kings, etc.
Israel.
A mountain where all are gathered (*mit'adim*) there — it is Mount Zion.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: In the uttermost parts of the north
Isaiah.english_translation: In the Courtyard, a place in which the northern thigh (*yerech*) was chosen, as in the matter that is said (Leviticus 1): “on the side (*yerech*) of the altar northward.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I will ascend above the heights of the clouds
Isaiah.english_translation: I am not worthy to dwell with human beings; I will make myself a small cloud in the air and sit in it. Jonathan translated: *asek aloi kol ama* (“I will go up above all the people”).
They will look through openings and lattices; *abauter* in Old French.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is אבוט״ר; Darmesteter (1909) lists this verse (“S'examineront”) and compares Godefroy’s *abaater*.

Isaiah.english_translation: *Porpenser* in Old French.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is פורופנשי״ר; Darmesteter (1909) lists this verse (“Ils penseront en eux-mêmes”) and reads *porpausér*.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: That opened not the house of his prisoners
Isaiah.english_translation: He did not open for them the house of their prisoners, to let them out, all the days of their life, for release, to go to their homes. Every word that requires a *lamed* at its beginning has a *heh* put at its end.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Every one in his own house
Isaiah.english_translation: In his grave; and so Targum Jonathan: *be-veit almeih* (“in his eternal house”).

Like the sucker of a tree that is abominable in its owner’s eyes, who digs and uproots and removes it; so you were cast out of your grave. The Sages said: When he became a beast and a wild animal for seven years, the people of the land made Evil-merodach king; and when he [Nebuchadnezzar] returned to his kingship, he took him [Evil-merodach] and imprisoned him in the prison until the day of his [Nebuchadnezzar’s] death. When he died, they took Evil-merodach out of the prison to make him king, and he did not accept it; he said: If he returns to his kingship, he will kill me. They said to him: He died and was buried; and he did not believe until they took him out of his grave.
Isaiah.translator_note: The names in square brackets are my clarification of the pronouns in the printed text.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: In the raiment of the slain
Isaiah.english_translation: In soiled clothing, like the clothing of the slain.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: that are thrust through with the sword
Isaiah.english_translation: Pierced by spears; *medukar* in the Arabic language is *mut'an*.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: go down to the pavement of the pit
Isaiah.english_translation: To the depths of a pit, a place where stones sink; there you went down.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: As a carcass trodden under foot
Isaiah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: *medashdesh*, like “*nabus* our adversaries” (Psalms 44) and “and upon My mountains *avusenu*” (here, 25), “wallowing (*mitbosesset*) in thy blood” (Ezekiel 15 [as printed]); trodden like the mire of the streets.
Isaiah.translator_note: The printed reference “Ezekiel 15” does not match; the words are Ezekiel 16:6.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Thou shalt not be joined with them in burial
Isaiah.english_translation: You will not be equal to the other kings, to rest in your grave.

With much labour, and you killed your people for nothing, as is explained in Daniel: “and he said to destroy all the wise men of Babylon”; therefore they hated you, and treated you with contempt, to cast you out of your grave.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The seed of evil-doers shall not
Isaiah.english_translation: And even your sons will be punished for your iniquity and will not endure many days after you, for your enemies will join against them and destroy them, and will say to one another:

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Prepare you slaughter for his children
Isaiah.english_translation: So that they not rise and inherit the land, and the earth be filled with enemies and oppressors; and so Jonathan translated: *ba'alei dvavin* (“adversaries”), like “and is become thine adversary” (I Samuel 28:16). And one can further explain “and fill the face of the world with cities”: since we said above that the world was as a wilderness and its cities he destroyed, it returned and said “and cut off his seed,” and the inhabitants of the cities will return to their places, and “fill the face of the world” with towns.
Isaiah.translator_note: The last explanation is terse in the printed text; translated literally.

Isaiah.english_translation: Remnant.
A son who rules in his father’s kingship.
A son’s son. *Nin* — this is Belshazzar; and *nekhed* — this is Vashti.
*Heriçon* in Old French.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is הריצו״ן; Darmesteter (1909) lists this verse (“Le hérisson”) and reads the form *hérisson*.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I will sweep it with the besom of destruction
Isaiah.english_translation: An expression of sweeping; *escobier* in Old French; as our Rabbis said: The Rabbis did not know what is “*ve-tatiteiha*” until they heard it, etc.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French gloss: the printed Hebrew spelling is אשקובי״ר; Darmesteter (1909) lists this verse (“Je le balayerai”) and reads *escobier*.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Surely as I have thought, so shall it come to pass
Isaiah.english_translation: With Assyria so it was; you, Nebuchadnezzar, saw that the words of the prophets of Israel were fulfilled in Sennacherib.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: That I will break Asshur in My land
Isaiah.english_translation: And by this you will know that what I have counselled you will also stand.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: upon My mountains tread him under foot
Isaiah.english_translation: It refers back to “as I have thought, so it was.”
That I said to trample him and tread upon him.
Upon Assyria in its time and upon Babylon in its time.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: In the year that king Ahaz died
Isaiah.english_translation: And Hezekiah his son reigned; this burden was upon the Philistines.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Rejoice not, O Philistia, all of thee
Isaiah.english_translation: That you lifted your head in the days of Ahaz, who was wicked, whose wickedness caused him to be delivered into your hands, as it is said (II Chronicles 28:18): “and the Philistines invaded the cities of the Lowland,” etc.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Because the rod that smote thee is broken
Isaiah.english_translation: Because the kingdom of the house of David, which was accustomed to smite you, has become weak and abased — as we find with David, and likewise with Uzziah king of Judah, who smote you, as it is said (II Chronicles 26): “And he went forth and warred against the Philistines, and broke down the wall of Gath.”

From the root of that serpent a *tzefa* (basilisk) will come forth, which is harsher than a serpent; and who was this? Hezekiah, of whom it is said (II Kings 18:8): “He smote the Philistines unto Gaza and the borders thereof, from the tower of the watchmen to the fortified city.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: his fruit shall be a flying serpent
Isaiah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: *ve-yehon ovadohi bekhon ke-ḥivya* (“and his deeds against you shall be like a serpent”).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the first-born of the poor shall feed
Isaiah.english_translation: They shall feed in the days of the princes of Israel, who are now poor because of you. *Bekhorei* is an expression meaning “princes,” as (Psalm 89:28): “I also will appoint him first-born.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: there cometh a smoke out of the north
Isaiah.english_translation: A harsh calamity will come upon them from the north like smoke. Gaza and its borders, which Hezekiah smote, were in the south of the Land of Israel, in the south-western corner; so the Land of Israel is found to lie to the north of it. And so we find in the Sifre on *Ha’azinu*: they sought to flee toward the south, and they would hand them over, as it is said (Amos 1:6): “For three transgressions of Gaza” — we learn that Gaza is in the south.
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s printed reference reads “Amos 2:1”; the verse he quotes, with “Gaza” and “deliver them up,” is Amos 1:6.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: there is no straggler in his ranks
Isaiah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: *u-leit de-me’aḥer bi-zemanohi* (“and there is none who delays at his appointed times”) — in the troops which He appointed to come upon you. That is: none will delay his steps so as to be a straggler (*boded*) and come alone by himself, but all of them will come as one, with force.
Isaiah.translator_note: The punctuation between the Targum quotation and Rashi’s own gloss (“in the troops which He appointed…”) is uncertain. Audit 4: the Aramaic quotation was checked against Targum Jonathan/the Ketuvim Targum (Mikraot Gedolot, Sefaria) at ISA 14:31 and reads as quoted; the meaning of the unclear word, if noted above, is still unresolved.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: What then shall one answer the messengers of the nation
Isaiah.english_translation: And what will the messengers of Israel, who go to announce tidings, say in the days of Hezekiah? Thus they will say: The LORD has founded Zion, He has set up in it a worthy and strong king; the LORD is with him.
Isaiah.translator_note: The final words (“*ve-ḥazak ha-Shem immo*”) can mean “the LORD is with him” or “with His people”; “with him” is given here.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: in her shall the afflicted of His people take refuge
Isaiah.english_translation: Even from the ten tribes they come there, as is explained (in II Chronicles 30), that Hezekiah sent messengers throughout all the border of Israel to return to the Holy One, blessed be He.
Isaiah prophesied that Sennacherib would come upon Moab and exile them, as it is said (below, 16): “In three years, as the years of a hireling, and the glory of Moab shall wax contemptible.”
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotation is Isaiah 16:14.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For in the night that Ar of Moab is laid waste
Isaiah.english_translation: Moab was made silent (*nidmah*), as though asleep (*domeh*), unable to fight; and in another night in which Kir of Moab was plundered it was made silent. Targum Jonathan: *ve-inun redimin* (“and they are asleep”). Ar and Kir are two provinces of Moab.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: He is gone up to Baith, and to Dibon
Isaiah.english_translation: Moab went up to the house (*ha-bayit*), and the people of Dibon to the high places.
These weep in the house, and those weep on the heights of their high places.
Groaning and roaring with weeping, as (Judges 11:37): “and go down upon the mountains,” and as (Lamentations 3:19): “Remember mine affliction and mine anguish.”
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi cites Hebrew *ve-yaradti* (Judges 11:37) and *u-merudi* (Lamentations 3:19); the JPS wording of those verses differs.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Therefore the armed men of Moab cry aloud
Isaiah.english_translation: Because the armed men of Moab cry out toward the battle; and the soul of Moab will be evil to it (*yera lo*), crying out like one mourning over himself.
Isaiah.translator_note: The phrase *yera lo mit-ro’e’a’at* is obscure; translated literally.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: My heart crieth out for Moab
Isaiah.english_translation: The prophets of Israel are not like the prophets of the nations of the world. Balaam sought to uproot Israel for no cause, while the prophets of Israel lament over the calamity that is coming upon the nations.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Her fugitives reach unto Zoar, A heifer of three years old
Isaiah.english_translation: Over every stronghold of Moab my heart cries out, as far as Zoar, which is the “third heifer” — the main strength of theirs is like a heifer that is third to the womb. Another explanation: *shlishiyah* means “mighty” (*gavratanit*). And Jonathan translated *bariḥeha* like *boreḥeha*: the fugitives will flee from them to escape as far as Zoar, as Lot their father did, who fled to Zoar.
The place of the ascents of a mountain named *Ma’aleh ha-Luḥit*; and so too the descent of Horonaim (Jeremiah 48:5): the fugitives will weep by way of there. And all these places belong to Moab.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: They raise up a cry of destruction
Isaiah.english_translation: They will cry out; and it is an Aramaic expression, for Targum Jonathan renders “the treader shall not tread with *hedad*” as *lo ye’o’erun be-kalhon* (“they shall not cry out with their voice”).
Isaiah.translator_note: The verse underlying the Targum quotation is not identified in the printed text.

Isaiah.english_translation: A river of that place.
From the blood of the slain, which mixes and falls into them.

That is, their mighty men and their kings and their rulers. And since the praise of the land of Moab is its good pasture, as we learned (in the Mishnah), “rams from Moab,” therefore he likened the calamity to the destruction of its pasture.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Therefore the abundance they have gotten
Isaiah.english_translation: Because it did excessively (*yitrah asah*), this calamity will come upon it — for they were ungrateful; for in many places Abraham stood by Lot: when he left Haran, and when he went to Egypt, and in his merit he was sent out from the midst of the overturning, and he fought for him against Amraphel and his companions. They should have repaid kindness to his seed. But they reckoned them (*monim otam*) when Sennacherib exiled the Reubenites and the Gadites, while Israel were weeping and lamenting, and they would say to them: Why do you lament? Are you not going to your father’s house? Your father Abraham — did he not come from beyond the River? And this is what is said (Zephaniah 2): “I have heard the taunt of Moab, and the revilings of the children of Ammon.” And further, they aided Sennacherib the three years that he besieged Samaria; that is what is said (below, 16): “In three years, as the years of a hireling, and all the glory of Moab shall be contemned.”
Isaiah.translator_note: The sense of *ve-hayu monim otam* (“they reckoned them”) is uncertain; the context suggests that Moab taunted the exiles. The Isaiah quotation is 16:14, and Zephaniah 2:8.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: that which they have laid up
Isaiah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: *u-teḥumehon de-al yama ma’arva yitnesev* (“and their borders that are on the western sea shall be taken”). And it is an expression of appointment, as (Numbers 4): “And the charge (*u-fekudat*) of Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest” — that is, their land, over which you were appointed (*pekadetem*), shall be taken from them.
Isaiah.translator_note: The Numbers quotation is 4:16.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: to the brook of the willows
Isaiah.english_translation: The enemies will take them — the borders. And there is a further explanation: *u-fekadtem alehem* — this shall be *naḥal ha-aravim*; *yis’um* — the enemies will exile them to the land of Babylon, which is the “brook of the willows,” as it is said (Psalm 137): “Upon the willows in the midst thereof we hanged up our harps.”
Isaiah.translator_note: The grammar of this second explanation is compressed in the printed text; translated literally.

Isaiah.english_translation: And *Be’er-elim* are places on the border of Moab.
Of Moab.
Like *u-le-Be’er Elim* (“and to Beer-elim”).
The name of the river.
In keeping with the name of the river.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I will bring yet more upon Dimon
Isaiah.english_translation: Its name is *dam* (blood), and the blood of the slain I will add to it, to fill it; and it is an expression of *sefu* (“add”): “add ye year to year” (below, 29), “to add the sweeping away of the moist” (Deuteronomy 29:18). And Targum renders *nosafot* as *kenishat meshiryen* — camps that are gathered together.
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotations are Isaiah 29:1 and Deuteronomy 29:18.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: A lion upon him that escapeth of Moab
Isaiah.english_translation: The remnant that Sennacherib leaves, Nebuchadnezzar will come in his time and destroy; and he is called a lion, as it is said (Jeremiah 4:7): “A lion is gone up from his thicket.”
Of Israel.
Your land.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Send you the lambs for the ruler of the land
Isaiah.english_translation: Do not exalt yourselves in your pride; do you not know that the ruler of your land, Mesha king of Moab (in II Kings 3), was a sheep-master, and he rendered to the king of Israel a hundred thousand lambs? Send that lamb of your ruler from Sela of the wilderness to the mount of the daughter of Zion.
Isaiah.translator_note: The construction of “send him the lamb of the ruler, yours” is compressed in the printed text; translated literally.

Isaiah.english_translation: From its nest.
Like fledglings cast out from their nest, who go about tossed to and fro — so shall the daughters of Moab be at the fords of Arnon.
It is an expression of debate over judgment, to choose for yourself the good, as (Job 34:4): “Let us choose for us that which is right.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Make thy shadow as the night
Isaiah.english_translation: Set your shadow at noon, so that your shade will grow dark as night, to hide in it from your enemies.
If the outcasts of my people flee yet again by way of you in the days of Nebuchadnezzar, do not hand them over, but hide them.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Let mine outcasts dwell with thee
Isaiah.english_translation: The children of Israel who flee.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: be thou a covert to him
Isaiah.english_translation: For know also the soul of the wanderers — what their distress is.
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s “*da’i*” is read as an imperative addressed to Moab; the connection to the lemma is compressed.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For the extortion is at an end
Isaiah.english_translation: Your *ha-mets*: your wealth and your honour that you had through your sheep and your cattle, from which you suck milk and butter.
An expression of *shadayim* (breasts) that give sufficient milk, as (below, 60): “and the breast of kings (*shod melakhim*) thou shalt suck.”
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotation is Isaiah 60:16.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: They that trampled down are consumed
Isaiah.english_translation: Your beasts that trample on the earth.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And a throne is established through mercy
