Isaiah.english_translation: When this breaking comes upon you, then the throne of David will be established and become great; for at that time Sennacherib will fall by the hand of Hezekiah, and his throne will be established through the kindness that he will do, as we find that he was one who did kindness, as it is said in Chronicles (II 30): “For Hezekiah king of Judah did give (*herim*) to the congregation a thousand bullocks and seven thousand sheep.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And there sitteth thereon in truth
Isaiah.english_translation: One who judges, and seeks justice, and is swift in righteousness. Targum Jonathan: *ve-avid kushta* (“and does truth”).
He exalted himself greatly.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Even of his haughtiness, and his pride, and his arrogancy
Isaiah.english_translation: Unlawfully so; for the main increase of his sons is through bastardy and through the illicit relations of the daughters with their father.
His pregnancy (*ibburo*) and his conception. Another explanation: *evrato* means his wrath, which he kept for Israel.
*Lo khen* — his mighty men acted, for they were ungrateful.
Isaiah.translator_note: The connection between the lemma and the gloss is compressed in the printed text; translated literally.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Therefore shall Moab wail for Moab
Isaiah.english_translation: Over Moab.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: for the sweet cakes of Kir-hareseth
Isaiah.english_translation: To the walls of Kir-ḥareset; *ashishei* as in (Jeremiah 50): “her *ashyoteha* are fallen.”
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s printed reference reads “Jeremiah 40”; the quotation is Jeremiah 50:15 (JPS: “Her buttresses are fallen”).

Isaiah.english_translation: Breakings.
You shall lament.
Fields of grain.

One may learn that Heshbon was a place of fields and Sibmah a place of vineyards. And if you say, all these are cities of the other side of the Jordan, and Israel took them from the hand of Sihon — when did they return to the hand of Moab? When Sennacherib exiled the Reubenites and the Gadites, the Moabites who were adjacent to them came and settled in them.
Dried up; laid waste (*ḥarev*).
The plantings of its *sorek* (choice vine).
The fields of the vine and the *sorek* mentioned here are only a parable, and they are camps and bands in the days of these peoples; and so Targum Jonathan:
Isaiah.translator_note: The sentence breaks off in the printed text; the Targum rendering is not given.

Isaiah.english_translation: They went into exile.
Isaiah.translator_note: The printed word is abbreviated (*ba-gol’*); read as “in exile.”

Isaiah.english_translation: To the wilderness.
Its twigs (*zemoroteha*); and they are a parable for its exiles.

They were dispersed, like (Ezekiel 29:5) “and I will cast thee (*ve-netashtikha*) into the wilderness,” and (I Samuel 30:16) “and behold, they were spread abroad (*netushim*),” and “and they spread themselves (*va-yinateshu*) in the valley of Rephaim” (there, 25 [as printed]).
Isaiah.translator_note: The last quotation is II Samuel 5:18; the printed reference “there, 25” does not match.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Therefore I will weep with the weeping of Jazer
Isaiah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: *ke-ma de-ayitit meshrayin al Ya’zer ken ayti ketolin al Sivmah* (“as I brought camps upon Jazer, so I will bring slayers upon Sibmah”). And the language of the verse: the prophet speaks in the manner of the laments of Jazer — I have cause to lament over you, O vine of Sibmah.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I will water thee with my tears
Isaiah.english_translation: *Arayikh* — I will pour my tear upon you. There is a word that serves as two words, as in (Jeremiah 10:20) “my children are gone forth of me (*banai yetza’uni*),” (Joshua 15) “thou hast set me in the Southland (*eretz ha-negev nettatani*),” (Genesis 37) “and could not speak peaceably unto him (*dabero le-shalom*).”
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotations are Jeremiah 10:20, Joshua 15:19 and Genesis 37:4; Rashi’s printed references read “Joshua 16” and “Genesis 37.”

Isaiah.english_translation: Figs that are dried in the summer (*kayits*).
*Hedad*: the voice of robbers and plunderers.
*Ha-Karmel*: a place of forest and grain fields.
*Lo yeru’a’* — an expression of a joyful shout.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I have made the vintage shout to cease
Isaiah.english_translation: *Hedad hishbati*: the voice of those who gather to lay the beam to press the grapes.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: my heart moaneth like a harp
Isaiah.english_translation: *Yehemu* — in a dirge.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Moab hath wearied himself upon the high place
Isaiah.english_translation: To fight upon the high places of the towers.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: he shall come to his sanctuary to pray
Isaiah.english_translation: To the place where they sanctify themselves and gather there to pray.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: This is the word that the LORD spoke concerning Moab
Isaiah.english_translation: The final destruction of Moab at the hand of Nebuchadnezzar.
From many days before the calamity came upon him, Isaiah prophesied this to him. Another explanation: *me’az* — from the time that Balak hired Balaam.
To bring the calamity near to them.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Within three years, as the years of a hireling
Isaiah.english_translation: On account of the three years in which they assisted Sennacherib when he besieged Samaria, and helped him without gain, as though they were hired labourers for him; therefore “the glory of Moab shall be contemned” among all the rest of the multitude of Sennacherib, whom he swept away into captivity from among that host, and he went his way. And so it is explained in *Seder Olam*: he swept away the Ammonites and the Moabites, who had been assisting them when he besieged Samaria three years, in fulfilment of what is said, “Three years, as the years of a hireling,” etc. And further it may be explained: “three years as the years of a hireling” — three years have been decreed upon you for a long time, but they will be exact, and the calamity will not be delayed any longer, just as the hireling is exact regarding the years of his hire, to be precise.
Isaiah.translator_note: The phrase “decreed upon you for a long time” (*le-orekh zeman*) is obscure; translated literally.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the glory of Moab shall wax contemptible
Isaiah.english_translation: In the eyes of all the great multitude of Sennacherib.
The remnant that remains to Moab.
It shall be.
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s single word supplies the verb for the phrase *me’at mez’ar*.

Isaiah.english_translation: *Lo khabbir*: an expression of abundance (*rov*).
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi reads *kabbir* as “many”; JPS renders “without strength.”

Isaiah.english_translation: *Musar me-ir*: an expression of removal.
From being a city.
*Me’i*: an expression of lowliness and depth, as in *me’ot yamim*.
Isaiah.translator_note: The source of the phrase *me’ot yamim* is not identified in the printed text.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The cities of Aroer are forsaken
Isaiah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: an expression of destruction, as in *aroer tit’ro’er*; and its explanation is: over the cities of Aram. And an aggadic midrash asks in wonder: since Aroer belonged to the Land of Israel, as it is said (Numbers 32), “and Aroer” — does he stand in Damascus and proclaim concerning Aroer? But there were in Damascus markets equal to the number of the days of the solar year, and each one had an idol, and they worshipped it one day in the year; and Israel made all of them one assembly, and they worshipped all of them every day; therefore he mentioned the fall of Aroer next to Damascus. And I explain it according to the plain sense of the verse: Rezin and Pekah son of Remaliah had allied together, and the prophet was prophesying about the fall of Damascus, and he said: “Behold, Damascus is taken away from being a city”; the cities of Aroer, which were Pekah’s, were already forsaken, for the Reubenites and the Gadites had already gone into exile; and behold, they are given continually to flocks of sheep, and the sheep of Moab lie down there, and none makes them afraid. The kingdom of Pekah will go on diminishing and being consumed, and Samaria too will be taken in the days of Hoshea; and then “the fortress shall cease from Ephraim, and the kingdom from Damascus” — that Rezin will be slain.
Isaiah.translator_note: The Numbers reference is 32:34 (“the children of Gad built… Aroer”).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: as the glory of the children of Israel
Isaiah.english_translation: The ten tribes will be so: these too went into exile to Halah and Habor, and those will go into exile to Kir, as it is said (II Kings 16:9): “and carried the people of it captive to Kir, and slew Rezin.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the fatness of his flesh shall wax lean
Isaiah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: *ve-otar yekareh yigle* (“and the wealth of his glory shall be…”).
Isaiah.translator_note: *Yigle* can mean “be exiled” or “be uncovered”; Rashi quotes the Targum without comment.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: when the harvestman gathereth the standing corn
Isaiah.english_translation: As at the time of reaping the standing grain, the reaper gathers the bundle (*tzvat*) of standing grain in one hand, and with his other arm he reaps ears with a sickle; so Sennacherib will uproot and exile everything. And even the gleaning that falls at the time of harvest he will glean and carry off — that is, even the fugitives will not escape his hand, and he will glean them (as one gleans ears; *s.a.* [“another version”] in the printed text).
Isaiah.translator_note: The parenthetical “as one gleans ears,” marked *s.a.* (“another version”), is a textual variant in the printed text.

Isaiah.english_translation: It is the valley that lies before Jerusalem; in the Book of Joshua you will find that the Valley of Rephaim is adjacent to Jerusalem.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: there shall be left therein gleanings
Isaiah.english_translation: Hezekiah and his supporters, who are inside Jerusalem — few men, like the gleanings of a vineyard, and like the beating of an olive tree, which leaves two or three berries.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: As at the beating of an olive-tree
Isaiah.english_translation: One who cuts off olives in order to gather them from the tree; and so “and He shall cut down (*ve-nikaf*) the thickets of the forest” (above, 10). And our Rabbis expounded: “and there shall be left therein” — in the multitude of Sennacherib, few men, like the beating of an olive tree, as it appears in the aggadah of *Ḥelek* (the chapter in Sanhedrin).
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotation is Isaiah 10:34.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: In the top of the uppermost bough
Isaiah.english_translation: On the head of the branch.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: in the branches of the fruitful tree
Isaiah.english_translation: In its branches (*be-se’ifeha*); and so “and consume the branches thereof (*se’ifeha*)” (below, 27) and so “lop the boughs (*mesa’ef pa’orah*)” (above, 10).
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotations are Isaiah 27:10 and 10:33.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: shall a man regard his Maker
Isaiah.english_translation: *Yish’eh*: he will turn to his Maker, as in “and the LORD had respect (*va-yisha*) unto Abel” (Genesis 4).
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotation is Genesis 4:4.

Isaiah.english_translation: The righteous who remain among them.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And he shall not regard the altars
Isaiah.english_translation: *Lo yir’eh*: they will not be reckoned in his eyes.
Of Israel.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: after the manner of woods and lofty forests
Isaiah.english_translation: Forsaken like this forest — ruined, without man.
*Ḥoresh*: it is a forest, as Targum renders “in the forest” (*ba-ya’ar*) as *be-ḥorsha*.

*Ve-ha-amir*: also a forest, a place of trees. Like the forsaking of the cities of the Amorite, which they left ruined in the days of Joshua like the *ḥoresh* and the *amir*; and they fled from the children of Israel, and the Land of Israel was desolate.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Therefore thou didst plant plants of pleasantness
Isaiah.english_translation: Therefore: as I planted you at the beginning, I planted a plant of delights — the twelve sons of Jacob — and when your plantings rose into shoots, they put in seed that was not fitting, like strange shoots (*zemorot zarot*), which are not of the vine kind but resemble the vine.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And didst set it with slips of a stranger
Isaiah.english_translation: *Tizra’enu*: you put your seed into that plant. And further one may say: “*u-zemorat zar tizra’enu*” — you intermarried with the Cuthites, and they became mixed with you.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: In the day of thy planting thou didst make it to grow
Isaiah.english_translation: *Tesagsegi*: an expression of entanglement (*sikhsukh*): your shoots became entangled with kinds of herbage and mixtures that spoil the branches of the vine; that is, in the place where I planted you for Myself as a vineyard, there you spoiled with your deeds. This is what He said to them (Ezekiel 20:5): “In the day when I chose Israel, and lifted up My hand unto the seed of the house of Jacob, and made Myself known unto them in the land of Egypt”; and it is said (there): “But they rebelled against Me, and would not hearken unto Me,” etc. And here too, *tesagsegi* — you were mixed with the abominations of the Egyptians.
Isaiah.translator_note: The second quotation is Ezekiel 20:8.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: in the morning thou didst make thy seed to blossom
Isaiah.english_translation: And on the next day, when I took you out from there, I brought you into the land; there too you made your evil seed blossom.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: A heap of boughs in the day of grief
Isaiah.english_translation: *Nad ketzir be-yom naḥalah*: a stack of evil harvest, which proved itself on the day of *naḥalah*; that harvest reached the day of distress.
Isaiah.translator_note: The clause “which proved itself” (*asher hokhiaḥ*) is obscure; translated literally.

Isaiah.english_translation: *Nad* is an expression of height, and so “they stood upright as a heap (*ke-ned*)” (Exodus 15), and “He gathereth… as a heap (*ka-ned*)” (Psalm 33). And *ned* and *nod* are not the same.
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotations are Exodus 15:8 and Psalm 33:7.

Isaiah.english_translation: That your reward was completed.
Isaiah.translator_note: The printed form is feminine (*she-nishlemet*); read as “that your reward was completed.”

Isaiah.english_translation: *Anush*: troubled with an evil sickness; and so “and it was sick (*va-ye’enash*)” (II Samuel 11), and so “for her wound is incurable (*anushah*)” (Micah 1:9). Another explanation: “and in the morning thou didst make thy seed to blossom” — before the *sharav* (hot wind) came you made them blossom; and the way of the vineyard is to blossom when the *sharav* comes, and one who makes it blossom in the morning is not fit. This is in the Midrash of Rabbi Tanḥuma.
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s printed reference reads “II Samuel 11”; the word *va-ye’enash* occurs in II Samuel 12:15.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Ah, the uproar of many peoples
Isaiah.english_translation: A measure that operates throughout all generations: the rod with which Israel is beaten is itself ultimately to be beaten. Therefore the prophets who prophesy the calamities of Israel by means of the nations place after it the calamity of the nation through which Israel was smitten.
The hosts of Sennacherib.
*Yish’on*: an expression of tumult and humming.
The Holy One, blessed be He, against that tumult.
He likened the wicked to the worst of kinds, and to the worst of that kind: dry chaff of the mountains, as opposed to that of the valleys.
Isaiah.translator_note: The phrase *mi-shel amakim* is read here as “as opposed to that of the valleys.”

Isaiah.english_translation: It is a blowing-away of thorns that are called *chardons* (Old French, “thistles”), resembling that with which they card woollen garments, but not hard; and when it comes near the end of summer they burst apart by themselves and the wind scatters them. And that scattered thing is made like a round wheel, with a kind of wood (another version: “eye”) in the middle, and its five arms around it.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *chardons*, read per Darmesteter (“Lire: chardons”).

Isaiah.english_translation: Demons come upon the enemy and terrify him.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: before the morning they are not
Isaiah.english_translation: And the enemy is no longer in the world.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: This is the portion of them that spoil us
Isaiah.english_translation: The portion of Sennacherib and the portion of Gog and Magog when they come to plunder us.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Ah, land of the buzzing of wings
Isaiah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: *de-atan leh be-sefinin me-ar’a reḥikta ve-kal’ehon perisan ke-nishra de-ṭayis bi-khenafohi* (“who come to it in ships from a far land, and their sails are spread like an eagle that flies with its wings”). I say: because they dwell in the east and the land is hot, the birds gather there, and it buzzes with the wings of birds. And this prophecy concerns the hosts of Gog and Magog, as in the matter that is said (Ezekiel 38:5): “Persia, Cush, and Put with them.”
Isaiah.translator_note: The Aramaic word *kal’ehon* (rendered “their sails”) is the least certain part of the Targum quotation.

Isaiah.english_translation: To see whether it is true that Israel has returned to their place, which is… “a nation tall and of glossy skin,” to a people that was terrible in its strength.
Isaiah.translator_note: The printed phrase *asher hu ha-Shem* is unclear; rendered as “which is…” and left incomplete.

Isaiah.english_translation: *Min hu ve-hal’ah*: from the day on which it was chosen as a people, and onward.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: A nation that is sturdy and treadeth down
Isaiah.english_translation: That was punished for its iniquity measure for measure, and was given to trampling. Another explanation: *kav kav* is an expression of vomit, filth and loathing (Lamentations 3).
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotation “filth and loathing” is Lamentations 3:45 (JPS: “offscouring and refuse”).

Isaiah.english_translation: The rulers of Cush and Noph.
Isaiah.translator_note: The gloss is bare in the printed text, with no explanation of how it relates to “rivers.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: All you inhabitants of the world
Isaiah.english_translation: You need not send emissaries concerning this, for “when an ensign is lifted up on the mountains you shall see,” at the ingathering of the exiles, and “when the horn is blown you shall hear.”
From the completion of the recompense of Gog I will turn away from all My affairs, and I will look in My dwelling-place, to do good to him.
Isaiah.translator_note: The opening “from the completion…” and the pronoun “him” in the closing phrase are ambiguous in the printed text.

Isaiah.english_translation: It will shine and sparkle for him like the heat of the sun, bright upon the greenery, as in “to gather herbs (*le-leqet orot*)” (II Kings 4).
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotation is II Kings 4:39.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Like a cloud of dew in the heat of harvest
Isaiah.english_translation: For which the reapers long, to refresh the soul in the heat of harvest.
The ripening of the harvest of Amalek and of Gog, before his desire is fulfilled — and they supposed that he is plotting to destroy his brother.
Isaiah.translator_note: The identity of “his brother” and the subject of “supposed” are not explained in the printed text.

Isaiah.english_translation: His; and the grain draws near to ripening in its ears (*meliloteha*), and the unripe fruit (*pagei*) of the blossom (*netzah*) of its vine becomes a sour grape (*boser*), and the young fruit (*gomel*) is weaned to become thick like the white broad-bean; that is *boser*, that is *gerua* (“reduced”).
Isaiah.translator_note: The sense of the closing words (*gomel nigmal*, *gerua*) is uncertain; translated literally.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: He will cut off the sprigs
Isaiah.english_translation: The one who cuts off the *zalzalim* of the vine, which are the shoots and tendrils.
Old French *serpes*.
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi gives the word in French letters; read per Darmesteter.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the shoots will He take away
Isaiah.english_translation: Those are the stocks (*ikarei*) of the vines, which are called in French *ceps*.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *ceps* (“vine stocks”), read per Darmesteter.

Isaiah.english_translation: He cut off and chopped off — that is, He will kill the princes and rulers of Gog, and his armies and his helpers.
Their corpses.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: unto the ravenous birds of the mountains
Isaiah.english_translation: To the bird of the mountains.
All the days of summer.
*Teḥerof*: all the days of winter. From here they said: the judgment of Gog in the time to come is twelve months.
Swift to send; swift is the decree of His word to exact retribution from Egypt.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the idols of Egypt shall be moved at His presence
Isaiah.english_translation: They will have no power to save their people from the hand of the emissaries of Assyria. And the reason the prophet said the calamity of Egypt in this language, which he did not say in this language to the other nations, is that they are accustomed to being struck in this manner: “and I will pass through the land of Egypt” (Exodus 12), “and against all the gods of Egypt” (there); and the way of the world is to frighten a man with the blow that has already struck him.
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotation is Exodus 12:12.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And I will spur Egypt against Egypt
Isaiah.english_translation: Its end explains its beginning: “and they shall fight every one against his brother.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: shall be made empty within it
Isaiah.english_translation: *Ve-nevekah ruaḥ*: its wisdom will be emptied, as in (below, 24) “maketh the earth empty (*boker ha-aretz*).”
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotation is Isaiah 24:1.

Isaiah.english_translation: One of the names of idol-worship.
Isaiah.translator_note: The printed abbreviation (*avodat gilulim* / *oveid gilulim*) is read here as “idol-worship.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And I will give over the Egyptians
Isaiah.english_translation: *Ve-sakharti*: like *ve-sagarti* (“and I will shut up”). And there is a further explanation: an expression of “and the fountains of the deep were stopped (*va-yisakheru*)” (Genesis 8) — I will stop it up and bind it.
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotation is Genesis 8:2.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the hand of a cruel lord
Isaiah.english_translation: Every expression of lordship (*adnut*) is called in the plural, even for one person, as in (there, 39) “Joseph’s master (*adonei*),” “until his lord (*adonav*) came” (there).
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotations are Genesis 39:20 and 39:16.

Isaiah.english_translation: The king of Assyria.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the waters shall fail from the sea
Isaiah.english_translation: And the waters shall be dried up from the sea.

An expression of desolation and breaking (Lamentations 3). For all the praise of the land of Egypt is through the Nile, since rain does not fall there, but the Nile rises and waters it by way of canals (*ye’orim*) made by human hands; therefore he likens its calamity to the drying up of the canals.
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotation (“desolation and destruction”) is Lamentations 3:47.

Isaiah.english_translation: And the sea will not return the Nile to its rear, and the Nile will descend into it and will not rise and water Egypt.
Isaiah.translator_note: The sense of “return the Nile to its rear” is compressed in the printed text; translated literally.

Isaiah.english_translation: This is the Nile.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And the rivers shall become foul
Isaiah.english_translation: When the waters diminish, the mud is noticeable in them, and they become mire and are cast off (*nizanaḥim*).
In the *Maḥberet* (of Menaḥem): “if it be poor (*dal hu*)” (Leviticus 14).
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotation is Leviticus 14:21; the *Maḥberet* is the Hebrew lexicon of Menaḥem ben Saruq.

Isaiah.english_translation: Deep canals in the trenches (*ḥaritzei*) of the fortresses of the towns.
Which grew there from the abundance of their waters.

When the canals dried up, the reeds stopped growing any longer; they dry out and fall. Targum Jonathan: *kamelu* — *lo yis’qun* (“they shall not rise”); and in another place he translated “*he-ḥfir Levanon kimmel*” as *nattar*. And I say that it is an expression of cutting (*qetzitah*), for they are cut off of themselves because of their dryness and fall.
Isaiah.translator_note: The “other place” is Isaiah 33:9 (JPS: “Lebanon is ashamed, it withereth”); the printed text does not name it.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The mosses by the Nile, by the brink of the Nile
Isaiah.english_translation: *Arot*: an expression of something rooted (*me’ora*) and well rooted; and similar to it (Psalms 36) “the wicked in great power, and spreading himself (*u-mit’areh*) like a leafy tree in its native soil.” And so Menaḥem composed it in his *Maḥberet*: plants rooted on the Nile, and even on its bank; and all that is sown on it — everything will be dry and blown away.
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s printed reference reads “Psalms 36”; the quotation is Psalm 37:35.

Isaiah.english_translation: An expression of mourning (*oni*) and grief.
They are the Egyptians who catch fish from the Nile, which spreads and rises into many canals made on its bank over the whole land of Egypt — which is not so with all rivers.
*Aym* in the vernacular.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *aym* (“fishhook”), from Latin *hamus*, per Darmesteter.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: they that work in combed flax
Isaiah.english_translation: Sowers of flax on the river.
Flax that they comb, and they weave from it fishing nets, which are made with holes upon holes.
*Ḥori*: like “beasts of the field (*behemot sadai*)” (there, 8), and “and cutteth him out windows (*ḥalonai*)” (Jeremiah 22:14).
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotation “there, 8” is Psalm 8:8. Compare Rashi on Isaiah 20:4: the final *yod* is superfluous, as in *ḥaloni*, *ḥori* and *sadai*.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And her foundations shall be crushed
Isaiah.english_translation: *Sekher* is *eskluse* in the vernacular, like (Genesis 8) “and the fountains of the deep were stopped (*va-yisakheru*),” for they dam up the waters that come out beyond the bank of the river and spread out and become a pool of water, gathered and standing in its place, and many fish are there. And the prophet said that the foundations of their excavations will be crushed, and the pools of the dam which they made will fall.
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotation is Genesis 8:2. Old French *eskluse* (“sluice”), per Darmesteter.

Isaiah.english_translation: *Agmei nefesh*: pools of rest — an expression of “and rested (*va-yinafash*)” (Exodus 31) — for the waters of the pools are at rest and stand in one place. And Targum Jonathan: *de-havu avdin sukhra ve-khanshin maya gavar le-nafsheih* (“who were making a dam and gathering water, each man for himself”).
Isaiah.translator_note: The Exodus quotation is 31:17 (Rashi’s printed reference reads “32”).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: How can you say unto Pharaoh
Isaiah.english_translation: Henceforth, to Pharaoh — each man of you for himself — “I am a son of the wise”; and since he will stumble through your counsel, how can you boast before him, saying, “We are sons of the wise; you are a son of ancient kings”?
Isaiah.translator_note: The opening words (*me-atah le-Faroh kol ish mikhem al atzmo*) are compressed; translated literally.

Isaiah.english_translation: An expression of fools (*evilim*).
As in “the serpent beguiled me (*hishi’ani*)” (Genesis 3).
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotation is Genesis 3:13.

Isaiah.english_translation: He poured a mixed drink for them within her, which perverted their spirit — an expression of “she hath mingled her wine (*masekhah yeinah*)” (Proverbs 9). A mixture of drink in a cask, until it settles in its taste, is called *masakh*.
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotation is Proverbs 9:2.

Isaiah.english_translation: The name of an illness of derangement of the mind.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: head or tail, palm-branch or rush
Isaiah.english_translation: These are the soothsayers (*ḥartumim*) and the astrologers who gaze at the stars: in the firmament there are constellations and stars called by these names, made in the likeness of a head and a tail, and they are set in *Teli* (another version: “in *Ṭaleh*”). And one may explain as Targum renders: head and governor (*hegemon*), ruler and *aṭron*.
Isaiah.translator_note:
*Teli* and *Ṭaleh* are traditionally identified as the constellations Draco and Aries.
u|The two Targum terms (*hegemon*, *aṭron*) are given as printed; their exact meaning is uncertain. Audit 4: the Aramaic quotation was checked against Targum Jonathan/the Ketuvim Targum (Mikraot Gedolot, Sefaria) at ISA 19:15 and reads as quoted; the meaning of the unclear word, if noted above, is still unresolved.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And the land of Judah shall become a terror unto Egypt
Isaiah.english_translation: When the survivors in Egypt from the captivity of Sennacherib hear of his downfall — that he fell in the land of Judah without any war of the arm of flesh — they will know that the Divine Presence is in Israel and that their Saviour is strong, and they will fear and tremble before the land of Judah.

An expression of breaking and dread and fear; an expression of “they reel to and fro (*yaḥogu*), and stagger like a drunken man” (Psalms 107), and so “in the clefts (*ḥagvei*) of the rock” (Song of Songs 2).
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotations are Psalm 107:27 and Song of Songs 2:14.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: because of the purpose of the LORD of hosts
Isaiah.english_translation: To cause it to fall into the hand of Sennacherib, while Judah will escape from his hand.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: there shall be five cities in the land of Egypt
Isaiah.english_translation: We learned in *Seder Olam*: after the downfall of Sennacherib, Hezekiah arose and dismissed the host that Sennacherib had brought with him from Egypt and from Cush in collars before Jerusalem; and they accepted upon themselves the kingship of Heaven and returned to their place, as it is said, “In that day there shall be five cities,” etc. And they went and built an altar to the LORD in the land of Egypt and offered sacrifice upon it to Heaven, in fulfilment of what is said, “In that day there shall be an altar to the LORD in the land of Egypt.” And some of our Rabbis expounded it, in tractate *Menaḥot*, as referring to the altar of the house of Ḥonyo, son of Simeon the Righteous, who fled to Egypt and made an altar there.
Like Israel, who are in the land of Canaan.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: one shall be called The city of destruction
Isaiah.english_translation: (Targum Jonathan: *karta de-Beit Shemesh de-atida le-meḥrav yitamar hi ḥada minhon* — “the city of Beth-shemesh, which is destined to be destroyed, shall be called one of them.”) Targum explains *heres* in two ways: the expression of “who commandeth the sun (*ha-ḥeres*) and it riseth not” (Job 9), and the expression of demolition (*harisah*) and destruction. And from where did Jonathan learn it? From the prophecy of Jeremiah, who prophesied in Tahpanhes: “and he shall break the pillars of Beth-shemesh that is in the land of Egypt” (Jeremiah 43) — we learn that Beth-shemesh in the land of Egypt, and the pillar, is destined to be destroyed; and the pillars mentioned there are the pillar beside its border to the LORD mentioned here. And one may say that Beth-shemesh sat on the border of Egypt, on the boundary; therefore “its border” is said beside it.
Isaiah.translator_note:
The quotations are Job 9:7 and Jeremiah 43:13.
u|The sentence “we learn that Beth-shemesh… and the pillar” is compressed in the printed text; translated literally.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And it shall be for a sign
Isaiah.english_translation: The altar shall be for a sign and a witness between them and the Omnipresent.
A saviour and a prince.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And the LORD shall make Himself known to Egypt
Isaiah.english_translation: The power of His might will be recognized by them.
It is an expression of a blow.
And after the blow He will bring them healing.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: He will be entreated of them
Isaiah.english_translation: He will be pleased with them.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: a highway out of Egypt to Assyria
Isaiah.english_translation: There will be a trodden road on which they will walk constantly from Egypt to Assyria.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the Assyrian shall come into Egypt
Isaiah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: *ve-yagiḥun Aturai le-Mitzrai* (“and the Assyrians shall advance to the Egyptians”).
Isaiah.translator_note: The Aramaic verb *yagiḥun* is rendered “advance”; its exact sense here is uncertain. Audit 4: the Aramaic quotation was checked against Targum Jonathan/the Ketuvim Targum (Mikraot Gedolot, Sefaria) at ISA 19:23 and reads as quoted; the meaning of the unclear word, if noted above, is still unresolved.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: shall Israel be the third with Egypt and with Assyria
Isaiah.english_translation: For peace and for blessing; for at that time there was no nation as esteemed in the world as Egypt and Assyria, while Israel was lowly in the days of Ahaz and in the days of Hoshea son of Elah. And the prophet said that through the miracle that would be done for Hezekiah the name of Israel would be raised on high, and they would be esteemed like one of these kingdoms, for blessing and for greatness.
Israel.
Israel, whom I chose for Myself as a people when they were in Egypt.

I showed them through the mighty deeds with which I wrought wonders upon Assyria; and through those miracles they will return to Me and will be as though I had now made them anew; and they will be My inheritance — Israel. And Targum Jonathan is like this.
Isaiah.translator_note: The final sentence (“and Targum Jonathan is like this”) is elliptical in the printed text.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: loose the sackcloth from off thy loins
Isaiah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: *ve-tisar saka be-ḥartzekh* (“and remove sackcloth from your loins”). But the context proves otherwise, for until now He had not commanded him to gird sackcloth that He should tell him to loosen it; and further, He says “and put thy shoe from off thy foot,” which is a sign of mourning. And the explanation of *u-fitaḥta* is as in (Exodus 39) “*mefutaḥot* — engravings of a signet”: to gird sackcloth tightly upon his flesh, so that it appears engraved in his flesh.
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotation is Exodus 39:6.

Isaiah.english_translation: Above your loins.
Targum Jonathan: *paḥiaḥ* — in torn and worn-out clothes, and not truly naked.
Isaiah.translator_note: The Aramaic word as printed is *פחיח*; the transliteration is uncertain.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: for three years a sign and a wonder
Isaiah.english_translation: He will walk thus as a sign and a wonder to Egypt and to Cush, for at the end of three years the king of Assyria will lead the captives of Egypt, etc. We learn that Tartan conquered Ashdod three years before the downfall of Sennacherib, for his downfall was when he brought the captives of Egypt, and Tirhakah king of Cush, before Jerusalem in collars, when he came to besiege Hezekiah.
Like *ḥasuf shet*; and the *yod* is extra, like the *yod* in *ḥaloni*, *ḥori* and *sadai*.

The place where dung issues; and so (II Samuel 10:4) “and cut off their garments… even to their buttocks (*shetotehem*).” And this recompense was theirs in return for Ham their father, who saw the nakedness of his father and did not cover it — measure for measure.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And they shall be dismayed and ashamed
Isaiah.english_translation: All who look and hope for the help of Cush, and who boast in the support of Egypt.
*Vantance* in the vernacular.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *vantance* (“boasting”), read per Darmesteter.

Isaiah.english_translation: The Land of Israel, who were leaning on Pharaoh for help.
An expression of the islands of the sea.

This prophecy is about Babylon, as is explained in it. And if you say: has he not already prophesied about it (above, 13), “Upon the bare mountain set ye up an ensign,” and that whole section? Sometimes the prophecy comes in his mouth one day in one style, and after a time in another style.
Isaiah.translator_note: In JPS the words “The burden of the wilderness of the sea” close the preceding verse. Rashi’s quotation is Isaiah 13:2.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: As whirlwinds in the South sweeping on
Isaiah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: *mi-ṭal meshrayin de-ayyatyan mi-madbera ke-mei yamma* (“because of camps that come from the wilderness like the waters of the sea”).
Like a stormwind that turns about in a dry land, raising much dust.
*Laḥalof*: in this way many camps will pass on, coming against Babylon.
They will come to her.

Targum Jonathan: *me-ar’a de-it’avidat bah ḥasinin* (“from a land in which mighty ones were made”). And one may explain that it is a place of serpent and scorpion, as it is said (Deuteronomy 1:19): “that great and dreadful wilderness.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: A grievous vision is declared unto me
Isaiah.english_translation: The prophet says: this prophecy, harsh upon Babylon, was told to me.

Targum Jonathan: *anisaya mit’anasin u-vozaya mitbazezin* (“the oppressors are oppressed and the plunderers are plundered”). And the Hebrew expression, according to the Targum, has this meaning: the traitor — another comes after and betrays him (another version: “you”); and the robber — another comes after and robs him (another version: “you”). These are Persia and Media, who plunder and despoil Babylon, which despoiled and plundered all the provinces until now.
And come upon her.
Upon Babylon, in siege. Compare “my God, my rock (*tzuri*)” (II Samuel 22): the accent there is below, on the *resh*, while this one has its accent above, on the *tzadi*, like *shuvi*.
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotation is II Samuel 22:3.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: All the sighing thereof have I made to cease
Isaiah.english_translation: The *he* has no *mappiq*, because it is like “all the sighings of the world”; and it is an expression of the sighing of many people — *sospiredic* in the vernacular. “All the sighing have I made to cease”: that the world was sighing because of the yoke of the kingdom of Babylon; now I have made it cease.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *sospiredic* (“sighing, groaning”), per Darmesteter.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Therefore are my loins filled with convulsion
Isaiah.english_translation: The prophet is compassionate and sighs over the calamity of the nations; this is an aggadic midrash. And by its plain sense, the prophet recites the lament and the mourning as though it were Babylon lamenting.
An expression of pain and birth-pangs. Our Rabbis said: a woman has doors and hinges (*tzirim*), just as the doors of a house have hinges.
A sickness, which is called *avit* in the language of the Sages.
Panic.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The twilight that I longed for
Isaiah.english_translation: The night that I desired for joy and for feasting. In the Book of Yosippon we find that he rejoiced that night because his troops had defeated the Persian army; He set it for me for trembling, as it is said (Daniel 5): “Belshazzar the king made a great feast,” etc.; “they drank wine,” etc.; “in that night Belshazzar was slain,” etc.; “and Darius the Mede received the kingdom” (there, 6).
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s quotations are in Aramaic: Daniel 5:1 and 5:30, and 6:1 (JPS).

Isaiah.english_translation: Set up the lampstand. In *Bereshit Rabbah* (?) they call a lampstand *tzefita*.
Isaiah.translator_note: The abbreviation *be-V”R* is read here as *Bereshit Rabbah*; the expansion is uncertain.

Isaiah.english_translation: And in the midst of the eating and drinking they cried out: “Rise up, you princes!”

They are strips of boiled leather, and they anoint them with oil so that the weapon slides off. And thus it is said of Saul: “for there the shield of the mighty was vilely cast away” — it threw off its anointing and did not receive it, and the shield of Saul became as though it had not been anointed with oil.
Isaiah.translator_note:
The quotation is II Samuel 1:21.
u|The word *megiri* (“strips”) is uncertain.

Isaiah.english_translation: One of your disciples is destined to lodge a complaint against My ways, concerning the long tranquillity of Babylon — and he is Habakkuk, who drew a circle and stood within it and said (Habakkuk 2), “I will stand upon my watch,” and “will look out to see what He will speak by me.” The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Isaiah: Station that watchman, and promise him from Me that he will stand at his post, and that whatever he sees of the fall of Babylon he shall declare.
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotation is Habakkuk 2:1.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And when he seeth a troop, horsemen by pairs
Isaiah.english_translation: And I will show him there a kind of chariot, a pair of horsemen — one riding a donkey and one riding a camel — and it is a sign for Persia and Media.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: He shall hearken diligently with much heed
Isaiah.english_translation: And there he will hear, in his prophecy, a kind of great murmuring, the shouts of armies.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And he cried as a lion
Isaiah.english_translation: He is Habakkuk; *aryeh* (“lion”) in gematria equals the number of *Ḥavakkuk*. Isaiah prophesied that Habakkuk would pray about this and say thus.
O LORD, my God, upon the watch-tower I stand continually by day, to let me know about this.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: there came a troop of men
Isaiah.english_translation: When he prays about this, he will see a kind of troop of men, etc.

Targum Jonathan: *nafelat ve-af atidah le-mipal* (“she has fallen, and moreover she is destined to fall”): two fallings, year after year — first through Media and Persia, and in the second year through Heaven; “and Babylon shall be the glory of kingdoms, as the overthrow of Sodom.” And so we find in *Seder Olam*: and this report came in the year of Darius, and after him in the year of the report: “and Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, shall be as the overthrow,” etc. (above, 13).
Isaiah.translator_note: The sentence beginning “and so we find in *Seder Olam*” is compressed in the printed text; translated literally. The quotation is Isaiah 13:19. Audit 5 source check: a passage with the same wording (9 consecutive words) is found in Seder Olam Rabbah 28.1 (Sefaria Hebrew text, labelled Public Domain). This is a wording match only; the translation was not changed.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: O thou my threshing, and the winnowing of my floor
Isaiah.english_translation: My holy produce, my pile of wheat, that I was commanded by the mouth of the Holy Spirit to set you right on the straight path, like a man who threshes and winnows his grain on the threshing-floor.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: That which I have heard from the LORD of hosts
Isaiah.english_translation: From Him I declared it to you.
It is Edom; and so it says, “Who was there like Tyre (*ke-dumah*) in the midst of the sea?” (Ezekiel 27).
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi cites Ezekiel 27:32 (*mi ke-Tzor ke-dumah*) as evidence that Dumah is Edom; JPS renders the verse “Who was there like Tyre, fortified in the midst of the sea?”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: One calleth unto me out of Seir
Isaiah.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He, said: Unto Me the prophet or the angel calls, from under the yoke of the kingdom of Seir.
Guardian of Israel, what will become of this night and this darkness?
The Holy One, blessed be He.
It is before Me to cause the light to shine, to make a morning for you.
It is prepared for Esau at the time of the End.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: If you will inquire, inquire you
Isaiah.english_translation: If you seek your request, to hasten the End.
In repentance.
Concerning the Arabs.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: In the thickets in Arabia shall you lodge
Isaiah.english_translation: I saw what you did when Assyria exiled My people: they were asking their captors to lead them by way of you, because you are the sons of their cousins — perhaps you would have mercy on them; and you would go out and lodge in the forest, by way of the passing of caravans.
Isaiah.translator_note: The last clause (*derekh ha’avarat shayarot*) is ambiguous; translated literally.

Isaiah.english_translation: The sons of your cousins.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Unto him that is thirsty bring you water
Isaiah.english_translation: It is the way to bring water; but you, inhabitants of the land of Tema, did not do so. Rather, “with his bread they met the fugitive” — they brought them kinds of salted foods and inflated skins full of wind; and he would eat and seek to drink, and he would put the mouth of the skin into his mouth, and the wind would enter his innards, and he would die. Another explanation: “to meet the thirsty, bring water” — I did not do so to your father: when he was thirsty, I revealed to him a well of water.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For they fled away from the swords
Isaiah.english_translation: My people.

Stretched out upon the face of the earth, as (I Samuel 30:16) “and behold they were spread abroad (*netushim*) over all the ground,” (there, 25) “and they spread themselves (*va-yinateshu*) in the valley of Rephaim.” Another explanation: *netushah* is like *letushah* (“sharpened”); all letters whose points of articulation are close, so as to be from one place, interchange with one another: *nun* with *lamed*, as it is said (Nehemiah 13:7), “to make him a chamber (*nishkah*),” like *lishkah*.
Isaiah.translator_note: The “there, 25” quotation is II Samuel 5:18; the printed reference does not match.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: according to the years of a hireling
Isaiah.english_translation: I will be exacting with her to make the time precise, like a hired labourer who is hired by the year, who is exacting about the time of payment for his year.
Remnant.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the mighty men of the children of Kedar
Isaiah.english_translation: Masters of an abundance of the bow, who are like their father, of whom it is said (Genesis 11), “and he became an archer (*rovah keshet*).”
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotation is Genesis 21:20 (Rashi’s printed reference reads “11”).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The burden concerning the Valley of Vision
Isaiah.english_translation: It is Jerusalem, a valley concerning which most prophecies were prophesied.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: that thou art wholly gone up to the housetops
Isaiah.english_translation: When an army came upon them, they go up on their roofs to see the army and to fight. And our Rabbis explained it as referring to priests who went up on the roof of the Sanctuary with the keys of the Court in their hands, as appears in tractate *Ta’anit*. And an aggadic midrash says that they were haughty, in *Eikhah Rabbati*.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Thou that art full of uproar
Isaiah.english_translation: A city that was full of tumult — the voice of a multitude of people, noisy and joyous; now what ails you that you mourn?

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Thy slain are not slain with the sword
Isaiah.english_translation: It would have been good if they had been slain by the sword, rather than now, when they are slain by famine.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: All thy rulers are fled together
Isaiah.english_translation: Zedekiah and his officers, who went out to flee by night.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Without the bow they are bound
Isaiah.english_translation: Who, from fear of those shooting arrows with the bow, were bound to be shut up inside the city; and all who were found in it were bound together in fetters, but most of them had fled from afar before that.
Cease from me. Thus the Holy One, blessed be He, says to the ministering angels.
*U-mevusah*: trampling, as (Jeremiah 12) “they have trodden (*bosesu*) My portion,” and as (Zechariah 10) “as mighty men, treading down (*bosim*) in the mire of the streets.”
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotations are Jeremiah 12:10 and Zechariah 10:5.

Isaiah.english_translation: The day of the pulling down (*kirkur*) of the wall of the rampart.
And the sound of crying, to flee to the mountains in order to escape.
Quivers of arrows — *cuivres* in the vernacular.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *cuivre* (“quiver”), read per Darmesteter.

Isaiah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: *ve-al shur dabeku tarisin* (“and upon the wall they fastened shields”); and it is like *arot al ye’or* (above, 19) and *u-mit’areh ke-ezraḥ ra’anan* (Psalms 37:35). And one may explain: *ve-Kir arah magen* — Kir is the name of the city, as (II Kings 15) “and carried it captive to Kir”; the people of that province uncovered their shields against Jerusalem.
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s printed reference reads “II Kings 15”; the quotation is II Kings 16:9.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the horsemen set themselves in array at the gate
Isaiah.english_translation: They set a siege on the gates; and its likeness is in Kings, in the war with Ben-hadad: “set (*simu*) against the city” (I Kings 20).
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotation is I Kings 20:12.

Isaiah.english_translation: An expression of uncovering.
It is the Temple, which shielded and covered and screened over them.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: that thou didst look in that day
Isaiah.english_translation: Stratagems to fight against them.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the armour in the house of the forest
Isaiah.english_translation: They are the shields — three hundred, and two hundred (targets) — that Solomon made, and the king put them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon (there, I 7).
Isaiah.translator_note: The three hundred shields and two hundred targets are I Kings 10:16–17; the House of the Forest of Lebanon is I Kings 7:2.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the breaches of the city of David
Isaiah.english_translation: You saw the breaches of the wall, that they were many.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: you gathered together the waters of the lower pool
Isaiah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: *ve-khenishton yat ama le-mei brikhta ar’ita* (“and you gathered the people to the waters of the lower pool”), which is beside the breaches of the city of David, to fight there, since you saw that there was a weak point (*torfah*) for Jerusalem, and that it is easy to conquer from there.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And you numbered the houses of Jerusalem
Isaiah.english_translation: How many houses each one has, that they should give from them according to the count, in order to take the stones and the timber to fortify the wall.
To strengthen; an expression of “fortified cities” (Numbers 12).
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotation is Numbers 13:28 (Rashi’s printed reference reads “12”).

Isaiah.english_translation: A pool of water, to be a strengthening for the city.
The walls were doubled — a rampart and a wall — and between [them were] the waters of the old pool.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: But you looked not unto Him that had done this
Isaiah.english_translation: And if you say: Hezekiah also did so, as it is said (II Chronicles 35), “And he took courage, and built up all the wall that was broken down, and raised it up to the towers, and another wall without, and strengthened Millo in the city of David” — “He trusted in the LORD, the God of Israel,” etc. (II Kings 18) — but you, in the days of Jehoiakim and Zedekiah, did not look unto Him who made it.
Isaiah.translator_note: The Chronicles quotation is II Chronicles 32:5 (Rashi’s printed reference reads “35”); the Kings quotation is II Kings 18:5.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Him that fashioned it long ago
Isaiah.english_translation: Since He created the world, Jerusalem and the Temple arose in His thought.
You did not think.
The Holy One, blessed be He — as it were — is in mourning before Him, and you are eating and rejoicing.
Isaiah.translator_note: The phrase “before Him” (*lefanav*) is as printed and reads oddly.

Isaiah.english_translation: [As for] the World to Come: the prophets tell us from the Holy One, blessed be He, that we shall have no portion in the World to Come; let us make enjoyment for ourselves in our lifetime.
Targum Jonathan: *mota tinyana le-alma de-ati* (“the second death, for the World to Come”).

He was a possessor of benefits (*ba’al ha-na’ot*), and so (there, I 1) “and she was a *sokhenet* to him.” And an aggadic midrash says that he was from Sakhni and came to Jerusalem, in *Vayikra Rabbah*.
Isaiah.translator_note:
The verse is I Kings 1:2 (JPS renders the word “be a companion”).
u|The abbreviation *u-m”a* is read here as “and an aggadic midrash”; the expansion is uncertain.

Isaiah.english_translation: He was appointed over the Temple. Some say he was High Priest, and some say *amarkal*.

The verse rebukes him because he wanted to hand Hezekiah over to the king of Assyria, as we say in Sanhedrin: he wrote a note and shot it by an arrow; Shebna and his faction made peace, Hezekiah and his faction did not make peace.
Who of your family is buried here?

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Thou that hewest thee out a sepulchre on high
Isaiah.english_translation: For he hewed himself a grave among the graves of the house of David, to be buried among the kings; therefore He says to him: What inheritance have you in these graves?
*Ḥikki* (“engrave”). The *yod* is extra, as in (Deuteronomy 33) “dwellers (*shokhni*) in the bush,” (Psalms 113) “who raiseth up (*mekimi*) the poor out of the dust.”
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotations are Deuteronomy 33:16 and Psalm 113:7.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: will hurl thee up and down with a man’s throw
Isaiah.english_translation: Like this rooster that is tossed from place to place (Aramaic: *ke-hadin tarnegola de-metaltel me-atar le-atar*). And our Rabbis said: the tossing of a man is harder than that of a woman (Aramaic: *ṭalṭula de-gavra kasheh mi-de-itta*).
Isaiah.translator_note: The Aramaic sentences are given as printed; the printed text does not say whether the first is from the Targum.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Yea, He will wind thee round and round
Isaiah.english_translation: Like (I Samuel 25:14) “and he flew upon them (*va-ya’at bahem*)” — an expression of *ayit* (bird of prey): He will make you fly like a bird into exile. And our Rabbis said: leprosy took flight upon him, as it is said (Leviticus 13:45), “and he shall cover his upper lip (*ya’teh*).”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: He will violently roll and toss thee
Isaiah.english_translation: Like a turban (*mitznefet*) that encircles the head, enemies and oppressors will encircle you.
Like an encircling *shur*. And our Rabbis explained: an expression of *kadur* (“ball”), which is called *pelote* in the vernacular, which they throw and receive from hand to hand.
Isaiah.translator_note:
Old French *pelote* (“ball”), per Darmesteter.
u|The words *ke-shur mekaf* are obscure; left as printed.

Isaiah.english_translation: In Casiphia, the name of the place.
And you will not be buried in the graves of the house of David; and there the chariots of your glory will be turned into the shame of the house of your lord, whom you sought.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: from thy station shalt thou be pulled down
Isaiah.english_translation: And from your service in the Temple He will tear you down.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: my servant Eliakim the son of Hilkiah
Isaiah.english_translation: He was over the house when Sennacherib fell, as we find: when they went out to Rabshakeh, Shebna and his faction revealed [it] to him, and they dragged him by the tails of their horses, as appears in Sanhedrin; when Sennacherib went to Tirhakah king of Cush, he swept away Shebna and his faction, and went on his way. Thus we learned in *Seder Olam*.
Isaiah.translator_note: The verb *galah* (“revealed” / “went into exile”) and the pronouns in this sentence are ambiguous in the printed text.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And the key of the house of David
Isaiah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: *meftaḥ beit mikdasha ve-shulṭan beit David* (“the key of the Sanctuary and the authority of the house of David”).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And I will fasten him as a peg in a sure place
Isaiah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: *ve-amnaneih amarkal mehemen mashmesh be-atar kayyam* (“and I will appoint him a trusted officer, serving in an enduring place”). *Ne’eman* is an expression of permanence — a place that is secure for those who lean on it, for it will not give way. Transpose the verse: *ve-teka’tihu yated ne’eman ba-makom* (“and I will fasten him a sure peg in the place”).

Targum Jonathan: *benaya u-vnei benaya* (“sons and sons’ sons”). And Menaḥem joined it with “the dung of the herd (*tzefi’ei ha-bakar*)” (Ezekiel 4); he taught that it is an expression of tiny infants coming out of their mother’s womb, and *tzefi’ei* would be an expression of going out — something that goes out.
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotation is Ezekiel 4:15 (JPS: “cow’s dung”).

Isaiah.english_translation: The small ones among their families will glory in him and lean on him.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: from the vessels of cups even to all the vessels of flagons
Isaiah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: *mi-khahanaya levishei efoda ve-ad benei Levi aḥadei nevalaya* (“from the priests who wear the ephod, even to the Levites who take up harps”). And *aganot* will be an expression of the ministering vessels with which the priests serve in the Temple.
In which the Levites say the song.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: shall the peg that was fastened in a sure place give way
Isaiah.english_translation: The greatness of Shebna.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the burden that was upon it shall be cut off
Isaiah.english_translation: His family and his faction, who lean on him and hang upon him the vessels of their glory; and since he likened him to a peg, he likened those who glory in him and lean upon him to a load (*masa*) that is loaded upon the peg. And some interpret it as: and the prophecy that was prophesied concerning him will be fulfilled.
Who were growing rich through the merchants of Tyre, who used to bring ships of Tarshish with merchandise to Tyre. Tarshish is the name of the sea.
Isaiah.translator_note: In JPS the words “Howl, you ships of Tarshish” (Rashi’s lemma) close the preceding verse.

Isaiah.english_translation: For it is plundered from within: a place where you were accustomed to the inn (*pundak*), from entering any more into it; and there will be no more a place for you in Tyre to lodge there.
Isaiah.translator_note: The first clause (*makom she-hayitem ragilin la-pundak mi-lavo od le-tokho*) is compressed; translated literally.

Isaiah.english_translation: They are the Romans.

The plunderer, to the men of Tyre. Another explanation: from the land of Kittim was revealed to the men of Tarshish the plunder of Tyre, for the sons of Tyre fled to Kittim, and from there the report was heard.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Be still, you inhabitants of the coast-land
Isaiah.english_translation: Mourn, and sit silent, inhabitants of the island of the sea. Why? Because the merchants of Zidon, who pass over the seas, were regulars in filling you with every merchandise. Now when Tyre falls, Zidon will fall with her, for they were close to one another, within a day’s journey.
The seed would come from Egypt, which sits on the river Shihor, to Tyre.
Egypt was the grain-supplier of Tyre.
It is the Nile, as it is said (Joshua 13:3), “from the Shihor, which is before Egypt”; and they would bring the grain to Tyre in Egyptian ships.
Tyre.
From the great multitude that was in her; all the nations would bring her merchandise.
Who was subordinate to Tyre.

For Tyre, which dwells in the stronghold of the sea, which is the chief head of the kingdom, said: Behold, I am as though I had not travailed and had not borne young men, for all of them were killed; and behold, I am as though I had not raised up virgins. And so Targum. And our Rabbis said in aggadah: “Be ashamed, O Zidon; for the sea hath spoken” — What am I, who have no sons and daughters to worry about, lest they be caught in iniquity? I do not change the commandment of my Maker, to cross the boundary of sand that He set for me. All the more so, be ashamed, O Zidon, who have reason to worry about all these!

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: When the report cometh to Egypt
Isaiah.english_translation: When they heard concerning Egypt that I brought upon them ten plagues, and in the end they sank in the sea.
They will be alarmed.

Those who hear, when the report of Tyre goes out; for the plagues of Tyre too will be like those plagues: “blood and fire” (Joel 3:3) is like the plague of blood; “a voice of uproar from the city” (below, 66) is the croaking of the frogs; and “its streams shall be turned into pitch,” etc.
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotations are Joel 3:3, Isaiah 66:6 and Isaiah 34:9.

Isaiah.english_translation: [Pass over,] men of Tyre, to flee to Tarshish.

Behold, she has fallen before you, and He says to you: Is this the city that was joyous in your eyes, which from ancient days was joyous? Now her feet will carry her from afar to seek rest for herself.
Her merchants (*tagareha*), as in (Hosea 12:8) “the trafficker (*Kena’an*), the balances of deceit are in his hand,” and “there shall be no more a trafficker (*Kena’ani*)” (Zechariah 14:21).
A strong standing.
To exile.
Like this Nile, which rises and spreads.
Tyre, which dwells in the sea of Tarshish.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: there is no girdle any more
Isaiah.english_translation: You have no more strength or girdle with which to gird your loins. *Mezaḥ* is an expression of a girdle, as in (Psalms 109) “and for the girdle (*u-le-mezaḥ*) wherewith he is girded continually”; and every girdle is an expression of strength.
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotation is Psalm 109:19.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: He hath stretched out His hand over the sea
Isaiah.english_translation: *Ha-noteh* — the One who stretches out.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The LORD hath given commandment concerning Canaan
Isaiah.english_translation: He commanded those whom He calls concerning Canaan.
Isaiah.translator_note: The word *kor’av* (“those whom He calls” / “His summoned ones”) is uncertain.

Isaiah.english_translation: *Le-shamid* is like *le-hashmid* (“to destroy”); and so “to go to tell (*le-gid*) in Jezreel” (Kings 29 [as printed]), like *le-hagid*; and so “to make the voice of thanksgiving heard (*le-shamia*)” (Psalms 26), like *le-hashmia*.
Isaiah.translator_note: The “Kings” quotation is II Kings 9:15; the printed reference “29” does not match. The Psalms quotation is 26:7.

Isaiah.english_translation: Tyre and Zidon belonged to Canaan, as it is said, “Zidon his first-born.”
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotation is Genesis 10:15.

Isaiah.english_translation: To the land of Kittim — arise, pass over; even there you will have no rest. Why do I say “arise, pass over”?
Isaiah.translator_note: The sentence breaks off after the question; the answer is not printed.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: this is the people that was not
Isaiah.english_translation: Which is not worthy to be a people, for they are called “that bitter and impetuous nation” (Habakkuk 1); it is a foolish people among the creatures, concerning whom the Holy One, blessed be He, regrets that He created them, as we learned: “Three the Holy One, blessed be He, regrets,” in tractate *Sukkah*.
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotation is Habakkuk 1:6.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: when Asshur founded it for shipmen
Isaiah.english_translation: To station in it his fleets, his ships — large *birniyot* — like “a gallant ship (*tzi addir*)” (below, 33).
Isaiah.translator_note:
The quotation is Isaiah 33:21.
u|The word *birniyot* is uncertain.

Isaiah.english_translation: They will set up their siege-engines against Tyre. *Baḥuniv* is an expression of *ofel u-voḥan* (below, 32): *berfreid* in the vernacular, which they make for sieges against the cities.
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotation is Isaiah 32:14. Old French *berfreid* (modern *beffroi*, “siege tower”), per Darmesteter.

Isaiah.english_translation: They will destroy; an expression of “rase it, rase it” (Psalms 137), an expression of demolition to the foundation.
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotation is Psalm 137:7.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Tyre shall be forgotten seventy years
Isaiah.english_translation: Since he mentions her in language of disgrace, the language of a harlot, he said “and thou shalt be forgotten,” like a harlot whom her lovers have forgotten: she too will be forgotten, with no merchants and traders turning to her, because she will be ruined.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: according to the days of one king
Isaiah.english_translation: The days of David were seventy years, and I do not know what this sign is that is given here.
A small remembrance, in that she will shake off her lowliness and return to those who were accustomed to come to her, to return to her former state.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: as in the song of the harlot
Isaiah.english_translation: For she sees that none turns to her, and she lifts up a sweet and pleasant voice in song, perhaps she will please her lovers.
That is: multiply also supplications and humble your pride.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: she shall return to her hire
Isaiah.english_translation: To her former state and to her wealth through her merchandise; and He designates her in a language of disgrace.
And she will supply merchandise — but He designated her in a language of disgrace.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: shall be holiness to the LORD
Isaiah.english_translation: The righteous are destined to plunder her when King Messiah comes.
To be a treasure.
He will not bequeath it to their children.
For garments of beauty; *atik* means excellent, as in “they speak arrogancy (*atak*)” (Psalms 94).
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotation is Psalm 94:4.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Behold, the LORD maketh the earth empty
Isaiah.english_translation: Behold, this prophecy is a calamity for Israel: since he prophesied to them this consolation, and they are destined to see great distress before it, therefore He said to them: I am not telling you this so that you will inherit it, for behold, the Holy One, blessed be He, empties and lays waste you; but the remnant of you, to the day of redemption — “they shall lift up their voice, they shall sing” — this is the end of the matter, and to them I prophesied the good prophecy.
Isaiah.translator_note: The clause “so that you will inherit it” (*she-tirashuha*) is as printed; the object “it” is not specified.

Isaiah.english_translation: *Bokek*: emptying.
*U-volkah*: laying it waste.
And He terrified its notables. *Avah* is an expression like *ne’evetī* (“I am bent”) from “hearing” (above, 21).
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotation is Isaiah 21:3.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And it shall be, as with the people, so with the priest
Isaiah.english_translation: (Addition.) Not as with other travellers, where the master leads his servant and the mistress leads her maidservant — the master is honoured and the servant is lowly, the mistress is honoured and the maid is lowly — but when the captor leads captives, all are equal before him.
Isaiah.translator_note: The printed word *tosefet* (“addition”) introduces this comment; its function is unclear.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: As with the buyer, so with the seller
Isaiah.english_translation: At a time when the people dwell securely on their inheritance, the buyer rejoices and the seller is sad, for he will not return to his sale; but when the captor leads them away, let the buyer not rejoice and let the seller not mourn. And so “as with the lender, so with the borrower”: the two are equal, for the borrower has nothing to pay, and the lender — had he not lent to this one, the captor would have taken it. Likewise “as with the creditor (*noshe*), so with the debtor”: as in “he of whom it is owed (*noshe bo*),” *loveh* applies to money, and *noshe* applies to all other things, such as wine and oil and grain and honey, as it is written (Deuteronomy 24:10): “When thou dost lend thy neighbour any manner of loan (*mashat me’umah*).” End.
Isaiah.translator_note: The idiom “applies to” (literally “falls in,” *nofel be-*) is rendered by sense.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The earth shall be utterly emptied
Isaiah.english_translation: *Ha-bok tavok*: it will be emptied.
*Ha-boz tavoz*: an expression of plunder and spoil.
Like (Jeremiah 8:13) “and the leaf is faded (*navel*)”: an expression of withering and loss of strength.
*Umlelah*: an expression of lowliness, as in “the feeble Jews” (Nehemiah 5 [as printed]).
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotation is Nehemiah 3:34 (Rashi’s printed reference reads “5”).

Isaiah.english_translation: *Tevel* is the Land of Israel, which is spiced (*mitubelet*) with many commandments.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The lofty people of the earth
Isaiah.english_translation: The pride of the people of the earth.
Like a kind of flattery (*ḥanufah*): it produces grass but does not produce standing grain; it shows the appearance of standing grain, but there is no wheat in its stalk.
Because of its inhabitants.
It is the Torah that they accepted by covenant.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Therefore hath a curse devoured the earth
Isaiah.english_translation: For the sin of a vain oath.
An expression of dryness and thirst in the heat of *ḥorev*, as in (Jeremiah 6) “the bellows blow fiercely (*naḥar*).”
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotation is Jeremiah 6:29.

Isaiah.english_translation: That you were saying, “Behold joy and gladness” (above, 22).
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotation is Isaiah 22:13.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Broken down is the city of wasteness
Isaiah.english_translation: When it is broken, it is called “the city of *tohu*.”
From anyone’s entering into it.
It was darkened.
It is Jerusalem.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the gate is smitten unto ruin
Isaiah.english_translation: Through the desolation of loneliness — because the houses will be desolate for lack of an inhabitant — the gates will be smitten by demons.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For thus shall it be in the midst of the earth
Isaiah.english_translation: Israel will remain among the nations, one from a city and two from a family.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: As at the beating of an olive-tree
Isaiah.english_translation: He who leaves berries on the top of the bough.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Those yonder lift up their voice
Isaiah.english_translation: To that small remnant that remains will come the good that I prophesied above.
More than they shouted at the sea at the redemption from Egypt.

Targum Jonathan: *bi-mei nehora le-tzaddikaya* (“in the … of light for the righteous”), concerning two (another version: “lights”) — of the redemption from Babylon and from Edom. And Menaḥem said: *urim* is an expression of clefts and crevices where they fled; and so “Ur of the Chaldees” (Genesis 11) is “the valley of the Chaldees,” and so “the hole (*me’urat*) of the asp” (above, 11): the cleft of the hole of its dwelling.
Isaiah.translator_note:
The quotations are Genesis 11:28 and Isaiah 11:8.
u|The Aramaic word *mitei* is uncertain. Audit 4: the Aramaic quotation was checked against Targum Jonathan/the Ketuvim Targum (Mikraot Gedolot, Sefaria) at ISA 24:15 and reads as quoted; the meaning of the unclear word, if noted above, is still unresolved.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: From the uttermost part of the earth
Isaiah.english_translation: Jonathan translated: “from the Temple,” which is at the end of the Land of Israel, in its east, as we learned: “Lod from the west and the Jordan from the east” — so it comes out that from Jerusalem to the Jordan is a day’s journey. And I say, by its plain sense: “we heard from behind the curtain that they are destined to raise songs from the edge of the earth.” And what are the songs? “Glory (*tzvi*) to the righteous” — a station and a standing is destined to be for the righteous.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: But I say: I waste away, I waste away, woe is me
Isaiah.english_translation: Woe is me, for two secrets were revealed to me — a secret of calamity and a secret of salvation — and behold, the salvation will be far off until enemies come, plunderers after plunderers and robbers after robbers; five treacheries are mentioned here.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Terror, and the pit, and the trap, are upon thee
Isaiah.english_translation: Upon the nations, inhabitants of the earth.
A hollow to fall into, as it explains and says.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: he who fleeth from the noise of the terror
Isaiah.english_translation: “(From the presence of) [from the voice of] the terror he shall fall into the pit,” etc. He who escapes from the sword of Messiah son of Joseph will fall into the sword of Messiah son of David, and he who escapes from there will be caught in the snare, in the war of Gog.
Isaiah.translator_note: The words in round and square brackets are the printed text’s own textual correction.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The earth is broken, broken down
Isaiah.english_translation: An expression of breaking, as in (Psalms 2) “Thou shalt break them (*te-ro’em*) with a rod of iron.”
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotation is Psalm 2:9.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The earth is crumbled in pieces
Isaiah.english_translation: *Por hitporerah*: an expression of crumbs.
A watchmen’s hut at the top of the tree.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the host of the high heaven on high
Isaiah.english_translation: He will bring down the princes of the nations first.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And they shall be gathered together, as prisoners are gathered in the dungeon
Isaiah.english_translation: *Ve-ussefu*: the idolaters — a gathering, which is for their harm, like putting a prisoner into a pit prepared for him: those liable to Gehinnom, to Gehinnom.
Isaiah.translator_note: The opening words (*ha-akum asefah*) are compressed in the printed text.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: shall be shut up in the prison
Isaiah.english_translation: *Ve-sugru al masger*: these are the seven compartments of Gehinnom.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: after many days shall they be punished
Isaiah.english_translation: The iniquities of many days will be reckoned upon them. And this is what Ha-Kalir composed (in the *silluk* of the *yotzer* for Parashat Zakhor): “for many days, to be counted, to reckon accounts for them.”
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotation from Kalir’s poem is given as printed and was not checked against the poem.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Then the moon shall be confounded, and the sun ashamed
Isaiah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: *ve-yevhatun de-falḥin le-sihara ve-yitkan’un de-sagdin le-shimsha* (“and those who worship the moon shall be ashamed, and those who bow to the sun shall be humbled”).
Counsels that You counselled from afar to Abraham, at the Covenant between the Pieces.
*Emunah* is “faithful”; *omen* is like *ohel* (“tent”) and *okhel* (“food”), and is not an expression of an agent but of the act — *averement* in the vernacular.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *averement* (“truth, verification”), per Darmesteter; his manuscript variants are garbled.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For Thou hast made of a city a heap
Isaiah.english_translation: Mount Seir, from a city to a heap.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: A castle of strangers to be no city
Isaiah.english_translation: A dwelling that they made in your city, which destroyed it: You will make its palaces a ruin, which will never be built.

A tent-covering to save from the rain-storm, and a shade to protect from the heat. And what is this storm (*zerem*)? It is the wind of the terrible ones; for he likened their wind to the stream that strikes a wall and topples it.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: As the heat in a dry place
Isaiah.english_translation: In a time of dryness that dries up the seeds, to wither them, so You will subdue the noise of strangers.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: As the heat by the shadow of a cloud
Isaiah.english_translation: When the waters are bound in a thick cloud in the days of the *sharav* (hot wind), in which everyone rejoices, so the song of the righteous will respond to the song of the terrible ones and their fall.
Isaiah.translator_note: The phrase “will respond to the song of the terrible ones” (*ya’aneh shir ha-tzaddikim al zemir aritzim*) is compressed.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the song of the terrible ones
Isaiah.english_translation: *Zamir*: an expression of “thou shalt not prune (*lo tizmor*)” (Leviticus 25).
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotation is Leviticus 25:4.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And in this mountain will the LORD of hosts make unto all peoples
Isaiah.english_translation: When they come to wage war (*tzava*) against Jerusalem.
For they think that it will go smoothly for them, like oil; it will turn into a feast of lees.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Of fat things full of marrow
Isaiah.english_translation: Smooth and fat, like the marrow of bones, there will be lees refined from every drink — oil and wine — so that there will be nothing there but lees alone. And all this is in the wars of Gog and Magog.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The face of the covering that is cast over all peoples
Isaiah.english_translation: The covering cast over [all] peoples, that covers all peoples. *Ha-lot* is like “and wrapped (*va-yalet*) his face” (I Kings 19), “behold, it is wrapped (*lutah*) in a cloth” (I Samuel 21).
Isaiah.translator_note: The word “[all]” in square brackets is the printed text’s own textual correction. The quotations are I Kings 19:13 and I Samuel 21:10.

Isaiah.english_translation: An expression of princedom and rulership.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: He will swallow up death for ever
Isaiah.english_translation: He will cover it and make it vanish for ever from Israel.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And it shall be said in that day
Isaiah.english_translation: His people in that day: “Lo,” etc.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For whom we waited, that He might save us
Isaiah.english_translation: We were hoping to Him that He would save us.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For in this mountain will the hand of the LORD rest
Isaiah.english_translation: The might of the Omnipresent.
[Moab] will be trodden down.
In his place; and *ve-nadosh* is like *ve-naratz ha-galgal* (Ecclesiastes 12).
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotation is Ecclesiastes 12:6 (JPS: “and the wheel falleth shattered”).

Isaiah.english_translation: Straw.
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi glosses *mi-teven* simply as “straw.”

Isaiah.english_translation: Mud; and so “for dung (*le-domen*) upon the face of the ground” (Jeremiah 15).
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s printed reference reads “Jeremiah 15”; the phrase occurs in Jeremiah 16:4 (also 8:2).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And when he shall spread forth his hands in the midst thereof
Isaiah.english_translation: And he will shatter his hands and his arms, clapping palms in weeping.
Isaiah.translator_note: The printed word *yadon* is read as *yadav* (“his hands”).

Isaiah.english_translation: The one who floats in the water.
