To float; and so “waters of swimming (*mei sheḥu*)” (Ezekiel 47).
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotation is Ezekiel 47:5.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: His pride shall be brought down
Isaiah.english_translation: [The One] who humbles his pride.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: together with the cunning of his hands
Isaiah.english_translation: An expression of “and lie in wait (*ve-arav*) for him” (Deuteronomy 19). Jonathan translated *ashvvot yadohi*: the place where he sets his hands to lie in ambush, and they are high towers; *ashvvot* are walls and towers, like (Jeremiah 3 [as printed]) “her buttresses are fallen.”
Isaiah.translator_note: The Deuteronomy quotation is 19:11; “Jeremiah 3” is Jeremiah 50:15 (JPS: “Her buttresses are fallen”).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And the high fortress of thy walls
Isaiah.english_translation: He says this to Moab.
The city of Jerusalem, which was always for us a stronghold; “salvation shall He appoint” — the Saviour [appoints] her walls and her rampart.
A low wall in front of the high wall.
Hers; “and let a righteous nation enter into her.”

That kept and looked forward, in its exile, for many days, to the faithfulness of the Holy One, blessed be He, that He would fulfil His promise, which He promised through His prophets, to redeem them.
*Shomer*: awaiting, and so (Genesis 37) “and his father kept the saying,” and (Deuteronomy 6 [as printed]) “and the LORD thy God shall keep (*ve-shamar*) with thee.”
Isaiah.translator_note: The Genesis quotation is 37:11; the Deuteronomy quotation is 7:12 (Rashi’s printed reference reads “6”).

Isaiah.english_translation: Who was resting on the Holy One, blessed be He, and leaning on Him firmly, not moving from his faith because of any fear or suffering.
That there be peace, for in You he trusted; therefore it is fitting for You to guard him.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For the LORD is GOD, an everlasting Rock
Isaiah.english_translation: For one should lean on Him, for He is *deḥila* (“awesome”): the LORD is a rock and a crag, a refuge for ever.
Isaiah.translator_note: The Aramaic word *deḥila* is read as “awesome / revered.”

Isaiah.english_translation: Tyre and the other lands.
King Messiah, of whom it is said, “poor, and riding upon an ass” (Zechariah 9:9).
Israel, who were poor until now.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The way of the just is straight
Isaiah.english_translation: A path that will be level for the receiving of the reward of the righteous. “Thou, O LORD” — for You are an upright God — “makest plain the path of the just,” to lead him on that path so that he receives his reward. And the righteous one is Jacob and his seed; and this is its interpretation: a path for the righteous to take the reward of the uprightness with which he conducts himself.
Isaiah.translator_note: The final clause (*she-noheg bahen*) does not say whether God or the righteous “conducts.”

Isaiah.english_translation: You, the Holy One, blessed be He: “the path of the feet of the righteous You make plain” for him, for that path. This *pillus* (levelling) is an expression of *contrepeis* in the vernacular — like a king who sits and reckons and weighs in his heart which would be fit, this one or that one; so the Upright One, in His heart, to lead him on the way of receiving reward for all that he conducted his deeds before You with fitness.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *contrepeis* (“counterbalance”), per Darmesteter (“Tu égalises”).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Yea, in the way of Thy judgments, O LORD, have we waited for Thee
Isaiah.english_translation: Just as we looked to receive the good from You, so too we hoped that You would show us the way of Your judgments of vengeance upon the wicked.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: To Thy name and to Thy memorial is the desire of our soul
Isaiah.english_translation: Our soul longs to see the name that has gone out for You from of old, to take vengeance upon Your adversary.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: With my soul have I desired Thee in the night
Isaiah.english_translation: In my exile, which is like night, to do these things.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Yea, with my spirit within me have I sought Thee earnestly
Isaiah.english_translation: I will plead to You for all this. Why? Because when Your judgments come upon the earth — when You execute judgment upon the wicked —

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The inhabitants of the world learn righteousness
Isaiah.english_translation: They learn to justify Your judgments and to acknowledge Your measures, for they see the sinner smitten and the righteous receiving good reward.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Let favour be shown to the wicked
Isaiah.english_translation: Is it for You to show favour to Esau the wicked, who dwelt between two righteous ones and did not learn righteousness?

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: In the land of uprightness will he deal wrongfully
Isaiah.english_translation: Jerusalem and the Temple: he will deal wrongfully — to plunder and to despoil and to destroy.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And will not behold the majesty of the LORD
Isaiah.english_translation: He did not regard Your greatness and Your majesty in his eyes. And *u-bal yir’eh* is an expression of habit and continuity: “did not see” means “did not consider,” like “thus did Job (*kakha ya’aseh*)” (Job 1).
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotation is Job 1:5.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Thy hand was lifted up, yet they see not
Isaiah.english_translation: I have seen many aggadic midrashim on the verses of this passage, above and below, and they do not settle either the grammar of the language or the order of the verses, and I needed to explain it according to its sequence. And a midrash aggadah says that there is one who asks — the prophet, etc. — and He said to him: Better that they see and be ashamed. But this does not follow the language, for it is not written here “Thy hand has been lifted (*harimu*)”; and further, the word differs from a similar word: every *yad ramah* in Scripture has its accent below (on the last syllable), but this one has its accent above (on the first), like (Genesis 37) “behold, my sheaf arose (*kamah*)” and like (Ruth 1) “behold, thy sister-in-law is gone back (*shavah*),” all of which are in the past tense. So too here: O LORD, the hand of Your might has withdrawn from Your adversaries, so that they do not see Your might, for they have seen their way prosper; at Your request they will see and be ashamed.
Isaiah.translator_note:
The quotations are Genesis 37:7 and Ruth 1:15.
u|The opening of the comment (“and a midrash aggadah says that there is one who asks…”) is abbreviated in the printed text.

Isaiah.english_translation: In the good that You do for Your people, they will also see in themselves the judgment of Your vengeance, that fire shall consume them.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Thou wilt establish peace for us
Isaiah.english_translation: You will establish; and so (II Kings 4) “set on (*shefot*) the pot,” and (Psalms 22) “and to the dust of death You lay me (*tishpetni*)”; and one may interpret all of them as an expression of placing: You will set peace for us.
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotations are II Kings 4:38 and Psalm 22:16.

Isaiah.english_translation: The evil ones.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: wrought all our works for us
Isaiah.english_translation: Corresponding to them, we received from Your hand for all our sins.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: other lords beside Thee have had dominion over us
Isaiah.english_translation: They became lords over us and oppressed us.

In a matter that is not Your will — seeking other gods, to transgress Your Torah — and we alone made mention of You, and we shall not mention the name of His divinity in another god, but in Him alone.
The name of Your divinity we shall mention, saying: Our God alone is God.
May it be Your will that these wicked ones do not live in the World to Come; and these shades, who slackened their hands from Your commandments — let there be no resurrection for them.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: To that end hast Thou punished and destroyed them
Isaiah.english_translation: Have You not already visited upon them and destroyed them by the words of Your mouth, as it is said, “for I will utterly blot out the remembrance of Amalek” (Exodus 17:14)?

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Thou hast gotten Thee honour with the nations
Isaiah.english_translation: To Israel You added Torah and greatness and honour, and as much as You added to them, You were honoured, for they acknowledge and praise You for all the good. Behold, in their prosperity Israel do this — offer praise and honour before You — and in their distress…
Isaiah.translator_note: The comment breaks off at “and in their distress,” leading into the next verse.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: LORD, in trouble have they sought Thee
Isaiah.english_translation: They do not think ill of Your measures.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Silently they poured out a prayer
Isaiah.english_translation: He poured out speech and prayer.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: when Thy chastening was upon them
Isaiah.english_translation: When the chastisement of Your sufferings was coming upon them; and such was their prayer.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Like as a woman with child, that draweth near the time of her delivery
Isaiah.english_translation: So were we before You: we see troubles renewed and suppose that they are signs of salvation and redemption, because we are promised to be redeemed out of distress and tribulation, like this woman in labour, for [they] are signs of salvation and redemption.
Because of Your decrees.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: We have been with child, we have been in pain
Isaiah.english_translation: We writhed like a woman in labour, as if we gave birth, as if we were near to being redeemed — and it is wind, and there is no salvation.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: We have not wrought any deliverance in the land
Isaiah.english_translation: In all our burdens and our trouble we do not prepare salvation for ourselves.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Neither are the inhabitants of the world come to life
Isaiah.english_translation: And the nations do not fall — they who are inhabitants of the world, who conquered and filled the earth. And Jonathan translated *bal yippolu* as an expression of “and we shall be distinguished (*ve-niflinu*), I and Thy people” (Exodus 33:16): the inhabitants of the world cannot do a wonder (*pele*).
Isaiah.translator_note: JPS renders *yippolu* “come to life”; Rashi reads it as “fall” and, with the Targum, as “do a wonder.”

Isaiah.english_translation: Here he prayed that the righteous live: at Your request let those who were put to death for You live; let a royal word go forth from before You, saying: “My corpse(s) shall arise — the corpses of My people, who made themselves corpses for Me — to them let this resurrection be,” in exchange for what is written above, “shades shall not arise,” but these shall arise.
Isaiah.translator_note: The phrase *she-nivlu atzman alai* is translated literally.

Isaiah.english_translation: All this the Holy One, blessed be He, will say to them: *Hakitzu ve-ranenu* — this is an imperative.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For Thy dew is as the dew of light
Isaiah.english_translation: For it is fitting for You to do so, that the dew of Your Torah and Your commandments be for them a dew of light.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And the earth shall bring to life the shades
Isaiah.english_translation: And to the earth and to the dust You will cast down the land of the shades, who slackened their hands from Your Torah.
Because it said, “and let the inhabitants of the world not fall (*yippolu*),” it repeats and says, “You make them fall,” for our righteousness is not enough to make them fall.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Come, my people, enter thou into thy chambers
Isaiah.english_translation: He answered the prophet with this answer: “Come, my people, enter into your chambers” — into the synagogues and the study houses. Another explanation: Contemplate your deeds in the chambers of your heart. Thus expounded Rabbi Tanḥuma.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And shut thy doors about thee
Isaiah.english_translation: Shut your door behind you. Targum Jonathan: *avid lakh uvadin tavin de-yeginnun alakh* (“do good deeds that will protect you”). And Rabbi Tanḥuma expounded: Shut the doors of your mouth, that you not think ill of the attribute of Justice.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Hide thyself for a little moment
Isaiah.english_translation: Hide yourself a little until the indignation passes, for in truth I will visit upon your enemies.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the LORD cometh forth out of His place
Isaiah.english_translation: From the attribute of Mercy to the attribute of Justice.
It is Mount Seir.
Whom they killed of Israel.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: will punish leviathan the slant serpent
Isaiah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “upon the king who exalted himself, like Pharaoh the first king, and upon the king who magnified himself, like Sennacherib the second king.” *Bariaḥ* is plain language, like this bar, because he is first.
Isaiah.translator_note: JPS renders *nachash bariach* “the slant serpent.”

Isaiah.english_translation: A doubled expression, because he is second. And I say: because these are three important nations — Egypt, Assyria and Edom — therefore He said this concerning these, as He said at the end of the matter, “and they shall come that were lost in the land of Assyria, and those dispersed in the land of Egypt” (below, 27).
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotation is Isaiah 27:13.

Isaiah.english_translation: It is Egypt.
It is Assyria.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: and He will slay the dragon that is in the sea
Isaiah.english_translation: She dwells in the heart of the seas, and so Kittim are called “the isles of the sea.”
Isaiah.translator_note: The feminine “she” is as printed; the referent is not named.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: In that day sing you of her
Isaiah.english_translation: At the time of redemption they will sing of Israel: This is “a vineyard of *ḥemer*” — it brought forth its good wine. *Ḥemer* — *vinos* in the vernacular.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *vinos* (“winy”), per Darmesteter (“vineuse”).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I the LORD do guard it
Isaiah.english_translation: At the time of exile.

Little by little I give her to drink the cup of calamity that comes upon her, lest I visit upon her all at once and consume her; therefore night and day I watch over her. And Jonathan translated: “Were it not that I visit upon them the iniquities which they habitually bring before Me, night and day I would shield them.”
Isaiah.translator_note: The Targum paraphrase is compressed.

Isaiah.english_translation: I have no opening to strengthen My wrath against the idolaters, since Israel too sin, and the attribute of Justice prosecutes.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Would that I were as the briers and thorns in flame
Isaiah.english_translation: “Among the sons of My war” — and that is Ishmael. Who will grant me that I may visit upon them, and the attribute of Justice will not be able to object that Israel might return in repentance, and it gives me “briers and thorns” among the sons of war: I will step a step upon the attribute of Justice, and I will visit upon them even an excess and additions over their iniquity, and I will set them alight together. So Targum Jonathan, concerning the nations; and our Rabbis of blessed memory interpreted it concerning Israel, and it is turned back to what is written: “Fury is not in Me” — in all the angers with which this vineyard angered Me, I cannot pour out My wrath to burn it, because of the oath I swore to their fathers. Who will grant me, as in days past — were it not for the oath, I would be briers and thorns and tread upon the vineyard, and set it alight together.
Isaiah.translator_note: The sense of *poshe’a ba-kerem* (“tread upon the vineyard”) is uncertain.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Or else let him take hold of My strength
Isaiah.english_translation: *Or* is an expression of *im* (“if”), as in “*or* it be known that the ox was wont to gore” (Exodus 21:36): If he holds fast to My strength, so that he seeks no strength but Mine, then he will make peace for Me, to set My mind at ease — and even what rattles within Me because I am not taking vengeance on My adversary — and I will take vengeance on them.
Isaiah.translator_note:
The quotation is Exodus 21:36.
u|The clause “and even what rattles within Me” is compressed in the printed text.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: yea, let him make peace with Me
Isaiah.english_translation: From the attribute of Justice, that it cannot accuse and say: How are these different from those?

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: In days to come shall Jacob take root
Isaiah.english_translation: Do you not know what I did at first, to those who came to Egypt, whom Jacob rooted: they sprouted and blossomed there until the face of the world was filled with fruitage.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Hath He smitten him as He smote those that smote him
Isaiah.english_translation: Did you see, in My might, that I smote them according to the smiting with which they smote Jacob? They drowned them in the water, and I drowned them in the water. There are questions of astonishment that stand as assertions, like this one and like (I Samuel 2) “Did I reveal Myself (*ha-nigloh niglêti*)?” (Ezekiel 8) “Seest thou (*ha-ro’eh atah*) what they do?”
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotations are I Samuel 2:27 and Ezekiel 8:6.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Or is he slain according to the slaughter of them that were slain by Him
Isaiah.english_translation: Israel, who were slain by Pharaoh — He slays Pharaoh and his people.
In that same measure.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: when Thou sendest her away, Thou dost contend with her
Isaiah.english_translation: When Egypt sent Israel away, the measure will contend with her in her own *se’ah*.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: He hath removed her with His rough blast
Isaiah.english_translation: *Hagah* — He spoke a word in His harsh speech.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: in the day of the east wind
Isaiah.english_translation: On the day of “and the LORD caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind” (Exodus 14:21).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Therefore by this shall the iniquity of Jacob be expiated
Isaiah.english_translation: Even now, by this the iniquity of Jacob will be atoned, so as to merit being redeemed as in the past.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And this is all the fruit of taking away his sin
Isaiah.english_translation: The good for him — to remove his sin — if he makes all the stones of the altars of his high places like chalkstones that are beaten in pieces, dashed, pierced; and so (Psalms 137) “and dasheth (*ve-nippetz*) thy little ones,” and (Jeremiah 13) “and I will dash them (*ve-nippatztim*) one against another.” *Gir* (chalk) is a kind of dye.
Isaiah.translator_note:
The quotations are Psalm 137:9 and Jeremiah 13:14.
u|The word *medukkarot* (“pierced”) is translated literally.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: So that the Asherim and the sun-images shall rise no more
Isaiah.english_translation: In order that they not set up idols for themselves.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For the fortified city is solitary
Isaiah.english_translation: For when they do this, the fortified city of Ishmael will be solitary, and the habitation will be sent away and abandoned like the wilderness.
Ephraim will inherit it, who is called “calf,” as it is said (Jeremiah 31:18), “as a calf untrained.”
Its branches.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: When the boughs thereof are withered
Isaiah.english_translation: The branches of its roots, like “she sent out her boughs (*ketzirah*)” (Psalms 80) and “and put forth boughs (*katzir*)” (Job 14): that is, when the merit of the little by which he honoured his father comes to an end, then its branches shall be broken.
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotations are Psalm 80:12 and Job 14:9.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The women shall come, and set them on fire
Isaiah.english_translation: A people weak as women will kindle them; so Targum. *Me’irot* is like (Malachi 1) “neither do you kindle (*ta’iru*) My altar for nought”; and so Dunash interpreted: because the wood will be dry, it will be easy to kindle. But Menaḥem interpreted it as “gathering,” like “I have gathered (*ariti*) my myrrh” (Song of Songs 5) and “and all that pass by the way pluck her (*aruha*)” (Psalms 80). Dunash answered him: But is it not written “when the boughs are withered,” and from dry branches one does not gather fruit? And so our Rabbis, who forbade accepting charity from them, for this reason, as they said in Bava Batra, chapter 1 (page 10): *leit leih*: “when its boughs are withered, they shall be broken.”
Isaiah.translator_note:
The quotations are Malachi 1:10, Song of Songs 5:1 and Psalm 80:13.
u|The closing Talmudic sentence (*leit leih bi-yevesh ketzirah tishbarnah*) is abbreviated in the printed text.

Isaiah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: *yitramon ketilin* (“the slain shall be cast down”). And I say: these two expressions, beating and gleaning, apply to one another — like one who beats his olives and then returns and gathers them, while others gather them from the ground; so the Holy One, blessed be He, will begin the gathering, as it is said (below), “shall blow a great horn.”
Isaiah.translator_note: The quotation is Isaiah 27:13.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: From the flood of the River
Isaiah.english_translation: They are those lost in the land of Assyria.
They are the dispersed in the land of Egypt.
Euphrates — they are the sons of Assyria who dwell on the Euphrates.
These are the inhabitants of Egypt; He will beat them off like one who beats olives.
From the exiles.
Whoever finds one of you will bring him as an offering.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: that were lost in the land of Assyria
Isaiah.english_translation: Because they were scattered to a distant land, farther in than the river Sambatyon, he called them “the lost.”
Isaiah.translator_note: “Farther in than” renders *lifnim min*; whether it means “beyond” or “inside” the river is not stated.

Isaiah.english_translation: For they used to get drunk on the good wine of the province of Perugita, as it is said: “the waters of Dormaskit and the wine of Perugita did away with the Ten Tribes.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the fading flower of his glorious beauty
Isaiah.english_translation: And from the place where his glorious plantation stands, its blossoming flower will be fading. These are the spoiled figs, as we learned in Berakhot about the *novelot*, and our Rabbis explained them as *bushlei kamra* (“ripened in a *kamra*”; see Rashi at 34:4). And *tzitz* is *netz*, as we translate “and the blossom (*tzitz*) blossomed” (*ve-anetz netz*).
Isaiah.translator_note: *Kamra* is Aramaic and is left untranslated; Rashi explains the expression at 34:4.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Which is on the head of the fat valley
Isaiah.english_translation: This is Kinneret, whose fruits are sweet, and there they strike themselves with wine.

Crushed by wine (*hamar*). There is another way to explain “the fading flower of his glorious beauty, which is on …”: the beauty of the glory that is on the head of the Ten Tribes, who are anointed with the pride of the heads of oils, as it is said (Amos 6:6): “anoint themselves with the chief ointments.” *Gay* means pride, as (above, 16:6; the printed text says 15) Moab is “very proud” (*gē me’od*). (And that flower will be like the flower of a fading one.) “Smitten with wine” — thus he calls them because of their drunkenness, as it is said of them (Amos 6:6): “drink wine in bowls.”
Isaiah.translator_note:
Rashi’s printed reference “chapter 15” for *gē me’od* is 16:6.
u|The parenthesis “(and that flower …)” is Rashi’s own aside, with unclear connection.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Behold, the Lord hath a mighty and strong one
Isaiah.english_translation: The LORD has a strong and mighty wind, which is like a storm of hail and a tempest of bitter destruction.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: That casteth down to the earth with violence
Isaiah.english_translation: He will set it down upon their land with His strong hand, and it will fell the fading ones from the figs.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: as the first-ripe fig before the summer
Isaiah.english_translation: Like the ripening of the fig of the fading flower.

The time of the ripening of the other figs. For since it is an early fig, one leaps upon it and swallows it while it is still in his hand. So He will be intent on the evil and bring it upon us (Daniel 9:14).
When the transgressors have come to an end.
For the righteous who remain in it.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And for a spirit of judgment
Isaiah.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He, will be a spirit of judgment — to teach judgment.
He will be strength for those who turn back the battle — the battle of Torah.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: But these also reel through wine
Isaiah.english_translation: Those who sit in judgment and those who turn back the battle in this generation, that is, the good and respected among them, have erred through wine, for now there is nothing good in them.
They mocked the words of the prophets. And the Targum translates “in a meal of delicacies,” since they saw it as a pleasure for themselves.
Isaiah.translator_note: The Targum is quoted as Rashi gives it; I have not independently checked it.

Isaiah.english_translation: They made justice stumble.
An expression of *piq birkayim* (“the knees smite together,” Nahum 2:11) and of *puqah* (“stumblingblock,” I Samuel 25:31; Rashi cites only “25”).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For all tables are full of filthy vomit
Isaiah.english_translation: Their tables, those of sacrifices to the dead, for they are like vomit of filth.
The mind cannot bear them.
Perhaps it is to infants who do not know how to understand? For the grown ones have turned to an evil way.
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s explanation is compressed; the translation keeps his two clauses as they stand.

Isaiah.english_translation: Separated from milk.

An expression of “and he removed from thence” (Genesis 12:8). Another explanation: separated from the Torah, which is called milk; and “drawn from the breasts” — taken away from before the Torah scholars.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: precept by precept, precept by precept
Isaiah.english_translation: A prophet commands them from the Holy One, blessed be He, and they have a *tzav* of idolatry against this *tzav*. The prophet again reproves them, and they always say: We have precept against precept; ours is more important than yours.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Line by line, line by line
Isaiah.english_translation: They have a line — a plumb-line of wicked judgments — against the line of righteousness.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Here a little, there a little
Isaiah.english_translation: The prophet says to them, “In a little while evil will come upon you,” and they say: a little there — let Him hasten, let Him speed His work, in a few days!
And so every term for *la’agim*, and so (below, 32:4) *illegim*; both are an expression of reversed speech that is not straight to hear.
Isaiah.translator_note: The sense of *la’ag* here (mockery or stammering) is not fully spelled out; the translation leaves the Hebrew terms.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Shall it be spoken to this people
Isaiah.english_translation: Whoever speaks to them a word of prophecy and reproof, it seems to them like a stammering tongue that they cannot understand.
The prophet said to them: “This is the rest” — that you may be at ease: leave the weary alone, that you not rob him; this shall be your refreshing.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And so the word of the LORD is unto them
Isaiah.english_translation: Measure for measure He will measure out to them. He decrees that the precept (*tzav*) of the nations that enslave them will be spoken over them: precept — levy (*pequdah*) upon levy, service upon service. A line of punishment against the line of the transgressions in their hands. *Qav leqav* means *tiqvah*, hope in exchange for hope: they hoped for light, and behold, darkness.
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s equation of *qav* with *tiqvah* is stated tersely; rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Here a little, there a little
Isaiah.english_translation: In a few days it will come upon them, and they will be diminished there in the land of their enemies.
Those who speak mockery in the language of a parable, such as:

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: We have made a covenant with death
Isaiah.english_translation: That it not come upon us.

A boundary that it will not cross. And so “their desired haven” (Psalm 107:30), and so “light over against light” (I Kings 7:5) — all are an expression of a boundary. And the outer edge of a matter is *ashumayir* in the foreign tongue (Old French).
Isaiah.translator_note: The Old French is spelled in Hebrew letters (*ashumayir*). Darmesteter lists it, under the (misnumbered) heading 28:13, with the sense “to trace a limit.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: When the scouring scourge shall pass through
Isaiah.english_translation: A plague that walks about in the land.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: It shall not come unto us
Isaiah.english_translation: It shall not come upon us.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For we have made lies our refuge
Isaiah.english_translation: We have set — idolatry.
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi abbreviates (*ע״א*); read as “idolatry.” The verb object is left implicit in his comment.

Isaiah.english_translation: Our shelter.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And in falsehood have we hid ourselves
Isaiah.english_translation: In idolatry we trusted to hide us.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone
Isaiah.english_translation: It is past tense, like (Esther 1:8) “for so the king had appointed” (*yissad ha-melekh*; Rashi cites it as “Megillah 1”); and so it must be explained: Behold, I am the one who has already founded. (In Zion, a stone —) the decree has already been decreed before Me, and I have set up King Messiah, who will be in Zion; for a *bohan* stone — an expression of fortress and strength, like “the mound and the tower” (*ofel ve-vohan*, below, 32:14) and like “they set up their towers” (above, 23:13).
Isaiah.translator_note: The parenthetical “(בציון אבן כבר)” stands in the printed text before “the decree has already been decreed”; its exact role is unclear.

Isaiah.english_translation: The first has a *patah* because it is in the construct state: “a foundation of a foundation” — that is, a complete foundation.
Isaiah.translator_note: The printed text repeats the word *mosad* in a way that is hard to parse; translated as it stands.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: He that believeth shall not make haste
Isaiah.english_translation: He who believes this matter will not hurry it — he will not say, “If it is true, let it hurry and come.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And I will make justice the line
Isaiah.english_translation: Before that king comes, I will bring decrees upon you to finish off the transgressors among you. “And I will make justice” — the judgment of his sufferings — “the line”; that is, I will set a measuring-line of the measure of suffering to bring upon you. “And righteousness the plummet” — I will make righteousness a plumb-line that straightens the building of those who build walls; that is, righteousness will go before them and straighten their ways, so that the transgressors will perish and the righteous will remain.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And the hail shall sweep away the refuge of lies
Isaiah.english_translation: That cover of which you said, “we have made lies our refuge” — hail will come and sweep it away. *Ya’eh* is an expression of sweeping, like “the shovels” (*ha-ya’im*, I Kings 7:40; Rashi’s printed reference is “Kings 6”), with which they scoop out the ashes of the stoves.
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s printed reference “I Kings 6” for *ha-ya’im* is 7:40.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And the waters shall overflow the hiding-place
Isaiah.english_translation: Of which you said, “and in falsehood have we hid ourselves” — the waters will wash it away. That is, I will bring a multitude (of nations) that will smash its pillars and its idols. And the word *mishpat* said here is *justice* (*yushtitsa*) in the foreign tongue (Old French).
Isaiah.translator_note:
“(אומו׳)” is an abbreviation, read here as “nations.”
Old French *justise* is confirmed in Darmesteter.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: your covenant with death shall be disannulled
Isaiah.english_translation: The covenant of which you said, “we have made a covenant with death,” will be annulled. Every *kapparah* is an expression of wiping away, removal of a thing; and so (Genesis 32:21) “I will appease him” (literally, “I will wipe his face”).
Of which you said: “with the nether-world we have made an agreement.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: When the scouring scourge shall pass through
Isaiah.english_translation: Of which you said, “It shall not come upon us” — and you will be a trampling-ground for it.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For morning by morning shall it pass through
Isaiah.english_translation: That is, constantly, constantly I will bring decrees upon you.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And it shall be sheer terror to understand the message
Isaiah.english_translation: Terror to all who hear, to understand the tidings of the hard calamities that I will bring upon you — all who hear will tremble.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For the bed is too short for a man to stretch himself
Isaiah.english_translation: For I will bring upon you an enemy who will press you, so that you will not be able to complete service to him; when he spreads his bed upon you, it will be too short for the one lying on it to stretch out.
To lie flat, to extend his limbs — *estandiliér* in the foreign tongue (Old French).
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *estandiliér* (“to stretch oneself”) is confirmed in Darmesteter.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And the covering too narrow when he gathereth himself up
Isaiah.english_translation: The prince (*nasikh*) who will rule over you — your place will be too cramped for him when he gathers into it. Our Rabbis expounded it of the idol which Manasseh brought into the Temple: “this bed is too short to stretch out upon,” to rule over it — two … at once. But I have explained it according to its plain sense, and in this way the Targum Jonathan. Even the midrash of our Rabbis can be reconciled with the manner of the passage, that is: Why do I bring this calamity upon you? Because the bed is too short for Me alone to stretch out on it, as it is said (I Kings 8): “Behold, the heavens do not contain You” — how much more when you bring an idol in alongside Me; so to speak, the place is cramped for us.
Isaiah.translator_note:
“שני רעים” (“two …”) is ambiguous and I have left it as an ellipsis.
Rashi’s citation of I Kings 8 paraphrases verse 27 (“heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain Thee”).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For the LORD will rise up as in mount Perazim
Isaiah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “For as the mountains trembled when the glory of the LORD was revealed in the days of Uzziah the king, and the miracles He wrought for Joshua in the plain of Gibeon, etc. — so will He be revealed to exact retribution from those who do, etc.”
Isaiah.translator_note: The Aramaic is abbreviated with “etc.” in the printed text.

Isaiah.english_translation: It will seem strange to you, because a hard calamity will come upon you.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: That He may do His work
Isaiah.english_translation: To do His work, like “working the ground” — *laborer* in the foreign tongue (Old French).
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *laborer* (“to work”) is confirmed in Darmesteter.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Now therefore be you not scoffers
Isaiah.english_translation: After “we have made a covenant with death.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Lest your bands be made strong
Isaiah.english_translation: Sufferings.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Is the plowman never done with plowing to sow
Isaiah.english_translation: It is an expression of astonishment; therefore it is vowelled with a *hataf patah*.

One who plows in order to sow — does the plower plow in order to sow forever? If so, what use is it? Likewise the prophets reprove you to bring you back to the good; will they reprove forever and not avail?

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: With the opening and harrowing of his ground
Isaiah.english_translation: Will he never sow, but always break open the ground with hoes and the tools of the plow? *Yeshadded* is an expression of field-work. “He opens and harrows” — at first he makes wide furrows, and at the end he makes small furrows — in the Midrash of R. Tanhuma.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: When he hath made plain the face thereof
Isaiah.english_translation: So is the way of the plower: once he has plowed, he levels the face of the ground, and afterwards he sows.
If it is *qetzach* that he comes to sow, he sows it by scattering; if cummin, he sows it by throwing. *Qetzach* is a kind of food.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: put in the wheat in rows
Isaiah.english_translation: And if it is grain that he comes to sow, this is his practice: he sows the wheat in the middle of the plowing, and the barley he sows around them, and the spelt he sows on the borders of the field and its edges. *Sorah* is an expression of a row: he sows in the middle, and it is found as a row upon the barley and the spelt.
Isaiah.translator_note: “A row upon the barley and the spelt” is rendered literally; Rashi’s picture is the wheat in the center with the other grains around it.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For He doth instruct him aright
Isaiah.english_translation: Even one whom his God instructs — not forever will He send prophets to reprove him; since he does not listen to rebuke, He will chastise him with judgments of suffering, so that the labor of his reproof which he reproved will avail; like this one who levels the face of the earth to sow, so that the labor of his plowing which he plowed will succeed.
It is a wooden implement made with grooves, and its name is *morag*; with it they cut up the stalks to become chaff.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For the black cummin is not threshed
Isaiah.english_translation: Because its seed comes out easily from its stalks. And so for cummin: they do not turn a wagon wheel to thresh it, since *qetzach* is light; it is beaten with a *matteh* (staff) and the cummin with a *shevet* (rod).
And whom do they crush with hard things — the bread-grain, since it is not easily beaten?
Isaiah.translator_note: The printed text of this comment is difficult; this is the most literal reading.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Nay, he will not ever be threshing it
Isaiah.english_translation: Behold, this *ki* is used in the sense of “but”: not forever do they thresh upon it; because the kernels of the seed are never pounded so as to be threshed, to be crushed by the sledge and the wagon wheel.

And when wagon wheels are turned upon it to crush it and to thresh it, even the wheel is crushed and broken, and likewise the other parts of the wagon with it — the ones that separate the grain from its stalks — they do not crush it; and the wheat is not crushed so as to be ground. *Adosh yedushennu* is like *asoh ya’aseh* (Ezekiel 31:11, “he shall surely deal with him”), *tzanof yitznof* (above, 22:18), and this *alef* comes in place of a *he*, like “and after this did Jehoshaphat join himself” (*etḥabbar*, II Chronicles 20:35; Rashi cites “II Chronicles 20”), which is like *hitḥabbar*; so here too, *hadosh yedushennu*; and so Menahem [ben Saruk] explained it.
Isaiah.translator_note:
“Chaps. 22” and “Chronicles 20” are Rashi’s chapter-only references; the verses are named in brackets from the text.
“Menahem … *ḥibbro*” (lit. “joined it”) is rendered as “explained it,” which is the likely sense.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: This also cometh forth from the LORD of hosts
Isaiah.english_translation: This too, like the way of those who thresh grain and those who beat black cummin and cummin, comes from the Holy One, blessed be He.

To show you hints in the manner of a novel, wonderful and veiled parable: for as the cummin and the black cummin do not burden themselves with much threshing, since they are beaten lightly, so, if you were quick to accept chastisement, He would not make decrees heavy upon you; but you are hard to accept rebukes, like grain that is hard to thresh; therefore He will burden you much, but He will not contend forever to destruction and crushing, just as “not forever does one thresh,” and the arrows of His blows will come to an end, and you will not come to an end — like the breaking of the wheel and the wagon, and the wheat not being crushed. And if you were inclined to be consumed, He would not test you with hard sufferings, like this flax-beater, who, when he knows that his flax is good, taps it lightly.
Isaiah.translator_note: The last sentence (*menaqesh*, “taps”) is terse; rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “the altar of the LORD,” and Ezekiel too called it so, as it is said (Ezekiel 43:16) “and the *ariel* is twelve [cubits],” named for the fire from above that crouched like a lion (*ari*) upon the altar, as we learned in the order of Yoma. But our Rabbis explained it of the Temple hall (*heikhal*), which was narrow at the back and wide at the front.
Isaiah.translator_note: JPS renders the Ezekiel word *ariel* as “hearth.”

Isaiah.english_translation: Targum: “that was built in the city where David dwelt.”
And continually your iniquities go on and grow stronger, until your festivals will be struck off and cut off. It is an expression of “beating an olive-tree” (above, 17:6).
She will be surrounded by those slain by the sword, like the altar surrounded by animal offerings.
Like a row of encircling troops.
An expression like *rikkum* set upon the towns.
Isaiah.translator_note: The word “*kerikkum*” in the printed text is unclear to me; translated literally, sense uncertain.

Isaiah.english_translation: An expression of siege (*matzor*).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: thou shalt speak out of the ground
Isaiah.english_translation: It will seem as if the speech that issues from your mouth issues from beneath the ground.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: thy speech shall chirp out of the dust
Isaiah.english_translation: To entreat Me; and from your entreaty My compassion will be stirred.
It is an expression of a whispering sound, like the voice of small birds.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the multitude of thy foes shall be like small dust
Isaiah.english_translation: The hosts of Sennacherib, who will be food for fire and become dust.
This matter.
A sudden event.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: There shall be a visitation from the LORD of hosts
Isaiah.english_translation: And after you have been humbled and your speech chirps, Ariel will be visited by Me to be saved, with thunder and earthquake, etc.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Shall be as a dream, a vision of the night
Isaiah.english_translation: For it is like one who seems to see and has not seen; so the multitude of all the nations will imagine they will conquer, but it will not come to pass in their hands.

Those who set up a post (*matzav*) against her, and destroyers (*mashchit*) — called *cenbel* in the foreign tongue (Old French) — as it is said of Saul (I Samuel 14:15): “the garrison, and the spoilers, they also trembled.”
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *cenbel* is confirmed in Darmesteter, who glosses it “pillards” (plunderers).

Isaiah.english_translation: Craving; and so “and thy desire shall be to thy husband” (Genesis 3:16; Rashi cites “Genesis 13”).
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s printed reference “Genesis 13” is Genesis 3:16.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: So shall the multitude of all the nations be
Isaiah.english_translation: They will not attain their desire, which they plan to do.
Be deliberate, to examine, to reflect upon your deeds.
And be astonished at your corruption.
An expression of “And shut their eyes” (above, 6:10): be blind from seeing.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: You that are drunken, but not with wine
Isaiah.english_translation: Yourselves, and not from wine. Why?
Isaiah.translator_note: The comment is elliptical (*shikru* … *atzmekhem ve-lo miyayin lamah*); rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For the LORD hath poured out upon you the spirit of deep sleep
Isaiah.english_translation: Etc. An expression of mixing, as in “she hath mingled her wine” (Proverbs 9:2); or an expression of *nesikhut*: He set a spirit of deep sleep to rule over you. He was prophesying about the transgressors of Israel who were gazing at the stars.

All that you used to see in the constellations will be hidden from you, like the words of a letter sealed with wax which they give for reading to one who knows how to read a letter, and he says: I cannot — for I do not see inside it, since it is sealed.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the writing is delivered to him that is not learned
Isaiah.english_translation: And when they take it from him and open its seal and give it to one who does not recognize the language of a letter, and say to him, “Read this, I pray thee,” and he says, “I am not learned” — so when you adjure the prince of fire, he will say, “I cannot, for the matter is sealed from me”; and when you adjure his fellow, he will say, “I do not recognize this Name by which you adjure me, for this is not my name.” And this is what Jeremiah said: “I will turn back the weapons of war that are in your hands” (Jeremiah 21:4) — this is the Explicit Name, in the Midrash of Psalms.
Isaiah.translator_note: The link between Jeremiah 21:4 and the Explicit Name is as Rashi states it in the Midrash of Psalms; the passage is terse and I have not tried to expand it.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Forasmuch as this people draw near
Isaiah.english_translation: Jonathan translated “because this people has exalted itself”; that is, they drew near to raise themselves up to heaven, they show themselves as honoring Me with mouth and lip, but they have kept their heart far from Me.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: a commandment of men learned by rote
Isaiah.english_translation: Not with a whole heart, but by the commandment of the men who teach them; they made themselves appear submissive before Him in order to seduce Him with your mouth.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I will again do a marvellous work among this people
Isaiah.english_translation: It is He who will continue to do a wonder, and in addition to a wonder — covering upon covering, stopping-up upon stopping-up. And what is the wonder-and-wonder? “And the wisdom of their wise men shall perish” — the removal of the wise men of Israel is doubly hard, like the destruction of the Temple. And all the curses in Deuteronomy are only one wonder, as “then the LORD will make thy plagues wonderful” (Deuteronomy 28:59); and here there are two wonders.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: seek deep to hide their counsel
Isaiah.english_translation: Like *lehastir* (to hide) counsel.
This perversity of yours: you know that it is like the potter’s clay, for the clay cannot say to its maker, “He did not make me”; so you cannot say that I do not understand your deeds.
Isaiah.translator_note: “You know that it is like the clay of the potter” is compressed in the Hebrew; rendered with the sense of the next clause.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Shall the potter be esteemed as clay
Isaiah.english_translation: It is an expression of astonishment (a question), and there are astonishments that are affirmed.
Isaiah.translator_note: “Astonishments that are affirmed” is taken to mean rhetorical questions that stand as statements.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: say of him that made it
Isaiah.english_translation: Like “of the maker”; and its parallel is “And Pharaoh will say of the children of Israel” (Exodus 14:3) and *lest they say of me, A woman slew him* (Judges 9:54).
He said of his Former, “He does not understand” — what is in his formation (*yitzro*)? Did He not Himself build the hidden places and the chambers and the thoughts?
Isaiah.translator_note: *Mah be-yitzro* (“what is in his formation / inclination”) is ambiguous.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Is it not yet a very little while
Isaiah.english_translation: In a few days; it will be easy in My eyes if you return to Me.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And Lebanon shall be turned into a fruitful field
Isaiah.english_translation: Which is a forest of trees, to become a Carmel; and it will revert to fields and vineyards.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: shall be esteemed as a forest
Isaiah.english_translation: Jonathan translated: “many towns shall be inhabited.” And an aggadah in Genesis Rabbah: *ḥorshin* — a man will settle cities, and they will be dense and full of people like this forest, which is full of trees.
Isaiah.translator_note: The Genesis Rabbah citation is cut short in the printed text; rendered as it stands.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: shall the deaf hear the words of a book
Isaiah.english_translation: And the curse stated above will be canceled — “For the LORD hath poured out upon you,” “And the vision of all this is become unto you,” and “And the wisdom of their wise men shall perish.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The humble also shall increase their joy
Isaiah.english_translation: Patient bearers, who bore the yoke of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His decrees.
Those who watch and consider how they may work iniquity.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: make a man an offender by words
Isaiah.english_translation: These are the false prophets.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: lay a snare for him that reproveth in the gate
Isaiah.english_translation: Targum: “and for him who reproves them they seek a stumbling-block”; an expression of *moqesh* (snare).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: turn aside the just with a thing of nought
Isaiah.english_translation: Targum: “and they perverted with falsehood the judgment of the innocent.”
From Ur of the Chaldeans.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Jacob shall not now be ashamed
Isaiah.english_translation: Because of his father.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Neither shall his face now wax pale
Isaiah.english_translation: Because of his father’s father, for no flaw is found in his bed, and his bed is whole.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: When he seeth his children, the work of My hands, in the midst of him
Isaiah.english_translation: Who will be the work of My hands — that is, righteous ones — in his midst; for when he sees in his midst that his hands are the work of My hands, they will sanctify My name, such as Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah; therefore his face will not wax pale.
Isaiah.translator_note: The printed text reads “his hands” where the verse reads “his children” (*yeladav*); translated as printed.

Isaiah.english_translation: An expression of “and you murmured in your tents” (Deuteronomy 1:27): those who were complaining and murmuring against the words of the prophets will learn instruction.
Isaiah.translator_note: “(מתלוננים)” is in parentheses in the printed text, marking a doubtful word.

Isaiah.english_translation: Turning aside from the way.
To set a ruler over themselves, with My spirit and My knowledge not in the matter. And what is the pouring (*nesokh*)? It is Pharaoh.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: That walk to go down into Egypt
Isaiah.english_translation: About Hoshea son of Elah, who “had sent messengers to So king of Egypt” (II Kings 17:4).
The Land of Israel is higher than all the lands. Another explanation: for them it is a descent.
To cover oneself — *abrier* in the foreign tongue (Old French).
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *abrier* (“s’abriter,” to take shelter) is confirmed in Darmesteter.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For his princes are at Zoan
Isaiah.english_translation: Those of the king of Israel, on a mission to the king of Egypt.
It is Tahpanhes.
All of them shamed themselves to acquire lords for themselves for nothing; and the people of the land will not profit them.
Isaiah.translator_note: *Ve-am ha-aretz* (“and the people of the land”) is rendered literally; Rashi’s exact sense is not clear.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: a people that cannot profit them
Isaiah.english_translation: On account of a people who will not profit them.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: a shame, and also a reproach
Isaiah.english_translation: Reviling — *destraber* in the foreign tongue (Old French).
Isaiah.translator_note: Darmesteter lists the Old French (with many variant spellings, among them *destraber / destorbier*) with the gloss “outrage.” The spelling in the printed text is uncertain.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The burden of the beasts of the South
Isaiah.english_translation: Targum: “burdens on their beasts, by the way of the south.” Since the land of Egypt is south of the Land of Israel; and this is the reviling and the reproach with which they are mocked — those who load the burdens of their money upon their beasts to carry a bribe to Egypt for nothing, and endanger themselves in the wildernesses, a land of trouble and anguish, etc.
Isaiah.translator_note: “(ורואין)” is in parentheses in the printed text, marking a doubtful word.

Isaiah.english_translation: The viper is an evil kind of snake, and there are only two in the world, a male and a female, and they give birth every seventy years. And “flying serpent” is also a kind of snake — not that it has wings to fly, but it leaps and jumps very far and throws a flame from its mouth.
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s natural-history statements are reported as he gives them.

Isaiah.english_translation: Their money.

The hump — *haldroba* in the foreign tongue (Old French) — that a camel has in the place of the load; and because it constantly festers, and they smear honey there for healing, it is called *dabbeshet*, as we say in B.M.: “honey and *dabish* is fit for camels’ bruises.”
Isaiah.translator_note:
“B.M.” is read as Bava Metzia; I have not checked the quotation there.
Darmesteter reads the Old French as “la bosse des chameaux” (the camels’ hump).

Isaiah.english_translation: Egypt.
The haughty.
A people idle and boasting for nothing. Another explanation: *shevet* — their arrogance and their haughtiness ought to cease.
Engrave it — this prophecy.
Israel.
Flatteries.
Prophesy.
Turn *us*.
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi supplies the missing object (“us”).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Get you out of the way
Isaiah.english_translation: We desire false prophecy.
True prophecy.
Shameful and scoffing.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: As a breach ready to fall
Isaiah.english_translation: Of a wall that has fallen.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: swelling out in a high wall
Isaiah.english_translation: Uncovered, so that one may enter it — “in the walls of your stronghold.” *Nivʿah* is an expression of being revealed, as in Obadiah (1:6) *nivʿu mitzfunav*, which the Targum renders “his hidden things were revealed.” And Dunash interpreted *nivʿah* as a bulge, that the wall becomes like blisters from the rains and the spoiling of crumbling mortar.
A jug (*nod*) of clay.
Among its shattered pieces, a large sherd that would be fit to rake fire from the hearth and to draw fire from the fire-bed; every drawing of fire takes on the expression of *ḥittiyah*.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: to take water out of the cistern
Isaiah.english_translation: To draw; and so “to draw out fifty press-measures” (Haggai 2:16), and so *ḥisfi shovel* (below, 47:2), “draw water from your path” — *espuiser* in the foreign tongue (Old French).
Isaiah.translator_note: The Old French is spelled אשפוייש״נט in the printed text; Darmesteter lists the word with the gloss “pour puiser” (to draw), in several variant spellings, and reads it *espuiser*.

Isaiah.english_translation: A pit full of water.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For thus said the Lord GOD
Isaiah.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He, to you: For some time now you have not needed to seek for yourselves the stronghold of Egypt and to waste your money; for in sitting still and rest you will have salvation without any toil, if you listen to Me.
Isaiah.translator_note: *Zeh yamim* is rendered “for some time now”; the Hebrew is terse.

Isaiah.english_translation: An expression of dwelling and repose; and so “Return, O LORD, unto the ten thousands of the families of Israel” (Numbers 10:36).
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi cites Numbers 10:36 as a parallel for *shuvah* in the sense of dwelling/rest; he does not spell out the connection.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: in confidence shall be your strength
Isaiah.english_translation: Coming to you from Me; and in confidence will be your might.
We will ally ourselves with the kings of Egypt and bring from there swift horses to flee.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: One thousand shall flee at the rebuke of one
Isaiah.english_translation: A thousand of you, before the rebuke of one of the enemies; or, all of you shall flee before the rebuke of five.
Like *asher notartem* (“that you are left”).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: a beacon upon the top of a mountain
Isaiah.english_translation: A tall tree fixed in the ground, like the mast of a ship, which is called *mast* in the foreign tongue (Old French).
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *mast* (“mât”) is confirmed in Darmesteter.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: as an ensign on a hill
Isaiah.english_translation: It too is a tall pole that they place on top of the hill; and when the watchman sees troops coming, he puts a cloth on it, and the wind carries it, and it is a sign that they should flee or gather.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And therefore will the LORD wait
Isaiah.english_translation: Because you were not willing to listen.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: that He may be gracious unto you
Isaiah.english_translation: He does not skip over for you the evil decree that was decreed upon you in order to hasten and bring the good; rather, He will wait and tarry until its end comes.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And therefore will He be exalted
Isaiah.english_translation: He will keep far away, for your compassion.
Isaiah.translator_note: *Yitrahheq le-rahamkhem* is terse; rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For the LORD is a God of justice
Isaiah.english_translation: And He will exact payment … from those who rebel against Him.
Isaiah.translator_note: Two words in the printed text (תחי ווה) are unclear to me and are left out of the translation.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Happy are all they that wait for Him
Isaiah.english_translation: For the consolations that He promised, for no word will fall.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For, O people that dwellest in Zion at Jerusalem
Isaiah.english_translation: Yet more days are coming: whoever remains to be dwelling in Zion and in Jerusalem will be righteous.
You will not need to seek requests from the Holy One, blessed be He, with weeping, for at the voice of your cry He answers you.
You will not be chasing after pleasures as you are now, as it is said, “drink wine in bowls” (Amos 6:6), “And behold joy and gladness” (above, 22:13).
He will not be covered from you by the corner of His garment; that is, He will not hide His face from you.
The Holy One, blessed be He, who teaches you for your benefit.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: thine ears shall hear a word behind thee
Isaiah.english_translation: Not as you are doing now, rejecting His word and saying, “Prophesy not unto us right things” (above, 30:10); but your ears will be inclined even after you to hear a word from Me — perhaps a prophet will come and teach you the way to go, between right and left.
Ornament.
They will be loathsome in your eyes, like a menstruant.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And He will give the rain for thy seed
Isaiah.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He, will give the rain of your seed.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: and it shall be fat and plenteous
Isaiah.english_translation: An expression of “a fat thing,” and not of oil (*shemen*); therefore its accent is below, and it is pointed with *kamatz*.
Isaiah.translator_note: “Its accent is below” is rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_translation: So that the pastures will be fat and broad.

A lamb; another explanation: a broad plain, like “the plain of the Jordan” (Genesis 13:10; Rashi’s printed reference is “Genesis 12”) and like *karmel* (Leviticus 23:14, “fresh ears”), which is a *kar* that is full of grain.
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s printed reference “Genesis 12” for *kikkar ha-Yarden* is Genesis 13:10.

Isaiah.english_translation: Oxen.
Like “over his fodder” (Job 6:5; Rashi’s printed reference is “Job 7”): straw and chaff, soured and strengthened with the grain that is among them, they will eat.
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s printed reference “Job 7” for *al be-lilo* is Job 6:5.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: with the shovel and with the fan
Isaiah.english_translation: The grain is winnowed twice, once with the *raḥat* and once with the *mizreh*, in order to clean the grain; therefore the chaff will be mixed with the grain that was winnowed with the *mizreh*, next to the stalks.
*Pele* in the foreign tongue (Old French), a shovel.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *pale / pele* (“la pelle”) is confirmed in Darmesteter.

Isaiah.english_translation: *Van* in the foreign tongue (Old French); and an aggadic midrash: *belil* is an expression of *balul* (mixed), so that the food will be mixed with straw.
Isaiah.translator_note: The printed text reads יו״ן; Darmesteter gives the Old French as *van* (winnowing fan).

Isaiah.english_translation: Rivers of water, as “spreadeth out its roots by the river” (Jeremiah 17:8).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: In the day of the great slaughter
Isaiah.english_translation: That there will be a great slaughter (in the land of Assyria). And Jonathan translated: “on the day of a great killing, at the fall of the great ones.”
Isaiah.translator_note: “(בארץ אשור)” is in parentheses in the printed text, marking a doubtful phrase.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: sevenfold, as the light of the seven days
Isaiah.english_translation: *Shiv‘atayim* — seven sevens, like the light of the seven days; behold, forty-nine sevens, which come to three hundred and forty-three.
His might, which will be a name for Him through what Sennacherib will do.
Isaiah.translator_note: Whether *mah she-ya‘aseh Sancheriv* means what he will do or what will be done to him is not clear; rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_translation: To confirm what He promised many days ago.
Isaiah.translator_note: *Lehe’emin* is rendered “to confirm.”

Isaiah.english_translation: The *he* is superfluous, and it is only like *massa* (“lifting”); therefore it is pointed with a *rafeh*.
So that whoever passes through it is divided by it up to his neck, since there is no power in him to stand before the rush of the waters.
To wave / to shake — *vanner* in the foreign tongue (Old French).
Isaiah.translator_note: The printed text reads אווני״ר; Darmesteter gives *vaner / vanner* with the gloss “pour agiter” (to shake).

Isaiah.english_translation: Not to profit them, while they think they are profiting.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: a bridle that causeth to err
Isaiah.english_translation: In the foreign tongue (Old French): פרומבי״א (*frombia*?) and פרינ״ק (*frenk*?).
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s two Old French words are transliterated from the Hebrew letters as printed; I could not find them in Darmesteter, so the reading is uncertain.

Isaiah.english_translation: On the night of Passover this joy will come to you.

As you said the song of the Passover offerings in Egypt; and this verse seems as if it came to teach about Sennacherib, but it taught about Pharaoh, that they said Hallel on the night of eating the Passover offerings — Midrash Tehillim.
Isaiah.translator_note: The sentence “seems … but it taught about Pharaoh” is rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: as when one goeth with the pipe
Isaiah.english_translation: And you will rejoice at the fall of Sennacherib, like the joy of those who bring first-fruits, before whom the flute was played to come to the mountain of the LORD, as we learned in tractate Bikkurim.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the lighting down of His arm
Isaiah.english_translation: This is not an expression of *nach* (rest) but an expression of *nuḥot* — *posement* in the foreign tongue (Old French) — as in “and rested in all the borders of Egypt” (Exodus 10:14; Rashi’s printed reference is “Exodus 17”). The lighting down of His might He will show in a flame of fire, for the hosts of Sennacherib were burned.
Isaiah.translator_note:
Rashi’s printed reference “Exodus 17” is Exodus 10:14.
u|Old French *posement* (printed פושלמנ״ט) is confirmed in Darmesteter, who glosses it “l’appui (de son bras).”

Isaiah.english_translation: An expression of breaking, to a greater degree.
Isaiah.translator_note: *Yoter* (“more”) is rendered “to a greater degree.”

Isaiah.english_translation: A flow of sweeping rain.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For through the voice of the LORD shall Asshur be dismayed
Isaiah.english_translation: He opened ears for them, and they heard song from the mouth of the *ḥayyot*, and died — in the aggadah of *Helek*.
Isaiah.translator_note: “The aggadah of *Helek*” is read as the aggadic section of the chapter *Helek* (Sanhedrin); I have not looked up the passage.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The rod with which He smote
Isaiah.english_translation: Asshur, who was accustomed to smite you with his rod.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And in every place where the appointed staff shall pass
Isaiah.english_translation: All the passages of the strength of the foundations of his hosts — all the places where they passed and destroyed them; and on the day of their fall the LORD will lay (the staff) upon them, at the report of their fall, and they will be with tabrets and harps. And this is the explanation of the verse by transposition: “And it shall be with tabrets and harps” — every passage of the staff of his foundation which the LORD shall lay upon him; “and in battles of wielding” — up and down — the Holy One, blessed be He, fights with them. And a midrash aggadah: the waving of the harvest *omer* stood by Israel in that battle, for it was the night of the sixteenth of Nisan.
Isaiah.translator_note:
The phrase “*tenufat shav*” in the printed text differs from the verse’s *tenufah*; translated as “wielding.”
The terse first clause (“the strength of the foundations of his hosts”) is rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For a hearth is ordered of old
Isaiah.english_translation: The second day of the creation of the world — a day that has a “yesterday” (the first day) and no “day before yesterday.”
Gehinnom, for everyone who is enticed (*mitpateh*) by his inclination falls there.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: for the king it is prepared
Isaiah.english_translation: For the need of Sennacherib and his army.
An expression of rising fire; an arrangement of wood on the fire is called a *medurah*.
The blowing of His spirit.
Burning.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Woe to them that go down to Egypt for help
Isaiah.english_translation: About Hoshea and the Ten Tribes who go down to Egypt for help, who sent messengers to So, king of Egypt (II Kings 17:4).
Those that come from there, because they are swift to run.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: look not unto the Holy One of Israel
Isaiah.english_translation: (Like “and they looked not to the Holy One of Israel”) — as Hezekiah did, as it is said (II Kings 18:5, 7): “He trusted in the LORD, the God of Israel” and “he rebelled against the king of Assyria.”
Isaiah.translator_note: The parenthesis in the printed text pairs *yish‘enu* with *sha‘u*; rendered as printed.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: doth not call back His words
Isaiah.english_translation: As He said, “And the LORD shall bring thee back into Egypt in ships” (Deuteronomy 28:68) — measure for measure; for I said to you there, “Thou shalt see it no more again”; and you went of your own will; your end is to go into exile against your will.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: against the house of the evil-doers
Isaiah.english_translation: Against the Ten Tribes, who are a house of evil-doers, and against Egypt, who are a help to them.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: when the LORD shall stretch out His hand
Isaiah.english_translation: For the Holy One, blessed be He, supports everything in His hand, and when He tilts it they fall, like one who holds something in his palm and when he tilts his palm it falls; so here. And a midrash aggadah; and the Targum Jonathan: “He will lift the hand of the *maḥat* of His might.”
Isaiah.translator_note: The Aramaic word *maḥat* is unclear to me and is left untranslated.

Isaiah.english_translation: The sound of a voice, as “And mourn sore like doves” (below, 59:11).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Though a multitude of shepherds be called forth against him
Isaiah.english_translation: They will gather against him with the calling of a voice, a multitude.
A gathering of shepherds; and so “Even they have cried aloud after thee” (*male*, Jeremiah 12:6) and so “They gather themselves together against me” (Job 16:10) — all are expressions of gathering.

He will not be humbled; he will not make himself poor (*ani*); and so “to humble thyself before Me” (Exodus 10:3; Rashi’s printed reference is “Exodus 11”) and so *ve-anah ge’on Yisra’el* (Hosea 5:5).
Isaiah.translator_note:
Rashi’s printed reference “Exodus 11” is Exodus 10:3.
u|JPS renders Hosea 5:5 “the pride of Israel shall testify”; Rashi’s point is that *anah* here means “humble.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: So will the LORD of hosts come down
Isaiah.english_translation: And He will not be afraid of the multitude of the nations.
A skipping over; and there is another way to explain it: an expression of sparing.
He will bring Israel out of trouble — an expression of *himlatah* (escape) — *escamucier* in the foreign tongue (Old French).
Isaiah.translator_note: Darmesteter lists the word, in variant spellings (*esmucier / eschamucier*), with the gloss “il fera échapper” (he will cause to escape).

Isaiah.english_translation: To Him against whom you have deepened your thoughts how to depart from Him, and you have departed from upon Him — now return to Him.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: his rock shall pass away by reason of terror
Isaiah.english_translation: And his strength will grow weak from much fear.
Because of the miracles that they will see the Holy One, blessed be He, doing for Israel.
There the fire will be prepared to burn them.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: a king shall reign in righteousness
Isaiah.english_translation: It is not the manner of a king to reign except to do righteous judgment.
And over whom is he to reign? Over princes who will rule for judgment. And the prophet said this concerning Ahaz, who was wicked, but Hezekiah his son will reign, and he is worthy.
A man mighty in the fear of the Holy One, blessed be He — this is Hezekiah — will be for Israel.
Like the shelter of a rock in which one hides from the wind and is concealed there from the heat; so will those who remain of the Ten Tribes trust in him.
An expression of dryness, *tziyah*.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: As in the shadow of a great rock in a weary land
Isaiah.english_translation: In a sunny place, for the land there is weary and dry and craves shade.
Not as they are now: “And make their ears heavy, And shut their eyes” (above, 6:10) — an expression of plastering over.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The heart also of the rash shall understand knowledge
Isaiah.english_translation: Not as now: “Make the heart of this people fat” (there, 6:10).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the tongue of the stammerers shall be ready to speak plainly
Isaiah.english_translation: And not as now: “For with stammering lips” (above, 28:11).
Anyone who does not know how to direct his speech so that it be clear is called *illeg* and *nil‘ag*.
A cheat, a swindler, a plower of evil.
An expression of “lord,” for all turn and look to him.
*Yedabber* (“speaks”) — it is in the present tense.
He will gather thoughts of iniquity, as “hath gotten me this wealth” (Deuteronomy 8:17; *asah li*).
He thinks thoughts how he can practice *ḥanufah*. *Ḥonef* is a noun; therefore its accent is above, and it is pointed with *patah*.
Isaiah.translator_note: *Ḥanufah* (flattery / hypocrisy / ungodliness) is left untranslated.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: to cause the drink of the thirsty to fail
Isaiah.english_translation: According to its plain sense: that they rob the poor. And its Targum: “the words of the Torah, which are like water to the thirsty, they … to nullify.”
Isaiah.translator_note: The Aramaic verb *medamen* is unclear to me and is left out of the translation.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And the needy when he speaketh right
Isaiah.english_translation: To corrupt the needy in his judgment. This *mishpat* is an expression of the beginning of the words in a judgment: when the needy states his claims, this counselor devises a scheme to cause him to stumble with his cunning. *Mishpat* serves three senses: the beginning of the claim — *desrainement* in the foreign tongue (Old French); the end of the case — *jugement* in the foreign tongue; and the *mishtar* with which they enforce it upon him with sufferings — *justice* in the foreign tongue.
Isaiah.translator_note:
*Mishtar* (“the officer / enforcement”) is rendered by its Old French sense, “execution of the sentence.”
Darmesteter lists all three Old French words for these three senses: *derainement* (“exposé de la plainte”), *jugement* (“la sentence”) and *justice* (“exécution de la sentence”).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: by liberal things shall he stand
Isaiah.english_translation: On account of his generosity he will have a standing.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: you women that are at ease
Isaiah.english_translation: Targum: “provinces that dwell at ease.”
Targum: “walled cities that dwell in security.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: After a year and days shall you be troubled
Isaiah.english_translation: Like (above, 29:1) “Add you year to year”: constantly your iniquities grow stronger, and in the end “you shall be troubled” — these who are now secure — for the vintage of the grapes will fail from them and the ingathering of grain will not come to the house.
A noun; therefore its accent is above, and it is pointed with *patah*.
Like *lirgoz*.
Like *lifshot*.
Like *la‘arot* — an expression of nakedness (Micah 1:11, “in nakedness and shame”).

Like *laḥgor*; therefore its accent is above. And so Jonathan translated: “strip off, strip yourselves bare, and bind upon your loins” — since they will strip and be bare of their clothes, they will not gird over their clothes, but upon their loins.
Isaiah.translator_note: The Aramaic first word (*shalḥu*) is read as “strip off.”

Isaiah.english_translation: They will beat upon their hearts.

(“For the breasts of delight, for the fields”) — their delights. And a midrash aggadah: they will lament over the sages of the Sanhedrins, who are like nursing breasts; and over their desirable city, which will be plowed like a field; and “for the fruitful vine” — these are Israel, who are called a vine, as it is said, “Thou didst pluck up a vine out of Egypt” (Psalm 80:9).
Isaiah.translator_note: “מ״א” in the printed text is read as *midrash aggadah*; the first words are in parentheses in the printed text.

Isaiah.english_translation: *Hovai* and *bor*; for all this destruction will be upon all the houses of joy and upon the joyous city — Jerusalem, which is “The joy of the whole earth” (Lamentations 2:15).
Isaiah.translator_note: *Hovai* and *bor* are left untranslated; I could not confirm their sense.

Isaiah.english_translation: The Temple (palace) of the king, the king of Judah, will be abandoned.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The city with its stir shall be deserted
Isaiah.english_translation: Exiled.
My Temple, which was a fortress for them.
It will be within ruins. *Me‘arot* is an expression of “Rase it, rase it” (Psalm 137:7), and *ba‘ad* is like “Can He judge through the dark cloud?” (Job 22:13).
Until the time of the end. *Ofel* and *bohan*: both are an expression of fortress.
Isaiah.translator_note: The sentence is cut short in the printed text; the second clause may belong with the previous comment.

Isaiah.english_translation: For the desire of Ishmael (and for the pasture of Edom) and for his armies.
Isaiah.translator_note: The words “(and for the pasture of Edom)” are in parentheses in the printed text, marking a doubtful phrase.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Until the spirit be poured upon us from on high
Isaiah.english_translation: He will pour out upon us, as in “emptied her pitcher” (Genesis 24:20); the expression of pouring applies also to the spirit, as “And I will pour upon the house of David” (Zechariah 12:10), and so “I will pour out My spirit upon all flesh” (Joel 3:1).
Isaiah.translator_note: In the printed text the references are transposed: Joel 3:1 stands beside the Zechariah quotation and Zechariah 12:10 beside the Joel one. The verses are given here with their correct references.

Isaiah.english_translation: Many towns, like this forest which is full of trees.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Then justice shall dwell in the wilderness
Isaiah.english_translation: In Jerusalem, which is like a wilderness.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: righteousness shall abide in the fruitful field
Isaiah.english_translation: That is the Land of Israel, which will be in those days like Carmel.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: in the downfall of the forest
Isaiah.english_translation: Necessarily this *barad* is not a noun, for its pointing is half *kamatz*, half *patah*, in the form of a verb; and so its explanation is an expression of action, like *ve-raḥatz*, *ve-yashav*, *ve-amad*: *u-barad* — *va-yavrod* the *beridat* of the forest. And the *bet* of *beridet* is part of the root, like *ateret*, *akeret*; that is, the Holy One, blessed be He, will cause to rain the rain of the pits of the wicked, who are now built up and full of cities like a forest.
Isaiah.translator_note: The grammatical argument is compressed; rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_translation: That Israel has been lowered until now.
A metropolis of Persia; and so Jonathan translated: “And hail will descend and will kill from the camp of the nations.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Happy are you that sow beside all waters
Isaiah.english_translation: Israel — for the sowing of your righteousness has succeeded, like those who sow upon waters; henceforth you shall reap and gather the grain of your good reward; “you shall send forth the foot of the ox” to thresh the grain and the donkey to bring it to the house. So the Targum Jonathan; that is, you will receive the reward of your good deeds.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Woe to thee that spoilest, and thou wast not spoiled
Isaiah.english_translation: The enemy: that you plunder constantly and you were not plundered; and you deal treacherously constantly and no one deals treacherously with you or despoils you.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: When thou hast ceased to spoil
Isaiah.english_translation: To be a plunderer; when you complete your plundering upon those against whom a decree was decreed to be plundered by you, you will be plundered.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: when thou art weary with dealing treacherously
Isaiah.english_translation: Menahem joined *kinlotekha* with *lo yeteh la’aretz minlam* in one section; and in *minlam* the first *mem* is a root letter that drops out, like the *mem* of *ma’amar* and of *mada*; and it may be an expression of consumption, according to the context.
