Isaiah.translator_note: The grammatical argument is compressed; rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_translation: An expression of *ke-khalotkha* (“when you finish”); and *lo yeteh la’aretz minlam* — the consumption decreed upon them will not bend to the earth, to become void and fade, but goes and grows strong.
Of the plundered, in the hand of the plunderer.
Isaiah.translator_note: Elliptical; rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_translation: Every day, every day, when he distresses them; also may our salvation be in time of trouble.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: At the noise of the tumult the peoples are fled
Isaiah.english_translation: That which comes from before You — peoples have wandered until now, when You wrought wonders for us, Your miracle.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And your spoil is gathered as the caterpillar gathereth
Isaiah.english_translation: This refers back to “and when thou art weary with dealing treacherously, they shall deal treacherously with thee”; and “the gathering of your spoil” — you who betray My people — when your visitation comes, the remnant of My people will plunder you and will gather your spoil, like the gathering of the *ḥasil*, which gathers grain for itself in the summer, each one for himself; so here too, each man will plunder for himself.

Like the sound of the roar of water that gathers and falls into pits with a roar, so will those who come to plunder and to spoil roar. *Mashaq* is an expression of roaring, as in “As a roaring lion, and a ravenous bear” (Proverbs 28:15), and so *mimshaq ḥarul* (Zephaniah 2:9): when the wind blows through the thistles and they strike one another, they give forth a sound; and so *ba-ir yashoqqu* (Joel 2).
Like “to take water out of the cistern” (above, 30:14); and our Rabbis expounded it in the aggadah of *Helek* about the plunder of the hosts of Sennacherib.
Isaiah.translator_note: “The aggadah of *Helek*” is read as the aggadic section of the chapter *Helek* (Sanhedrin); I have not looked up the passage.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The LORD is exalted, for He dwelleth on high
Isaiah.english_translation: He showed His might, for He is high above all, and His hand is uppermost.

“And the stability of thy times shall be,” etc.: “A hoard of salvation, wisdom and knowledge” — that which you believe in your Creator: the times that He fixed for you — for terumot and tithes, at the time of their separation; for gleanings, forgotten sheaf and corner of the field, at their time; to keep sabbatical years and jubilees at their time. Another explanation: “the faithfulness of your time” — that you had faith in the Holy One, blessed be He, in the times that passed over you and you hoped for salvation — will be a hoard of strength for you.
That you fear before Him is a good treasure, so that through it a treasury will be opened to you from Him.

The prophet was prophesying consolations and says that the calamity has already devoured him, “and from now I will arise and be exalted to redeem them”: “Behold, over their *ar’ellim*” — their altar — they have already cried out and lamented in their streets and their squares with weeping and wailing.
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s reading of *ar’ellam* as “their altar” follows his comment on Ariel (29:1).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The ambassadors of peace weep bitterly
Isaiah.english_translation: Their messengers, who used to announce peace, will weep bitterly and say, “The highways lie waste; the wayfaring man ceaseth.”
The enemy [broke] the covenant that he made with Israel.
Plunder in his eyes; every enemy does not regard man.
An expression of mourning.
Dried up and cut off.
It is in the past tense.
The name of a district for pasturing cattle, as we learned: “rams from Moab, calves from Sharon.”
A ruin.
An expression of *tishnuq*, as in “the LORD overthrew the Egyptians” (Exodus 14:27).
Isaiah.translator_note: The word *tishnuq* is left untranslated; I could not confirm its meaning.

Isaiah.english_translation: Because of the many evils that the enemy did to My people, I will no longer restrain Myself; now I will arise and be exalted and lifted up.
A kind of chaff — a thing that is easily kindled.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Your breath is a fire that shall devour you
Isaiah.english_translation: From your own body a fire-wind will go out and consume the chaff and the straw.
Cut off; *kesuḥim* is like “nor prune thy vineyard” (Leviticus 25:4) — Targum Onkelos: *lo takhsaḥ*.
Those who believe in Me and do My will from their youth.
Penitents, who have drawn near to Me anew.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The sinners in Zion are afraid
Isaiah.english_translation: How will they find an opening for repentance?

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Who among us shall dwell with the devouring fire?
Isaiah.english_translation: That is, who will stand in our stead to quench the burning wrath? Another explanation: “who shall dwell for us” — that is, who is there for us that shall dwell in Zion with the Rock, who is a devouring fire — and He answers: “One who loves righteous deeds,” etc.
Isaiah.translator_note: The reply quoted (*ohev tzedaqot*) differs from the verse’s next words (*holekh tzedaqot*, 33:15); translated as printed.

Isaiah.english_translation: Who is he that will be found walking in righteous deeds?

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: That shaketh his hands from holding of bribes
Isaiah.english_translation: *Escot* in the foreign tongue (Old French).
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *escot* (printed אשקו״ט) is confirmed in Darmesteter, who glosses it “agitant ses mains” (shaking his hands).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: That stoppeth his ears from hearing of blood
Isaiah.english_translation: Stops up; and so *shequfim atumim* (I Kings 6:4; Rashi cites “Kings 1:6”).
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s quotation (*shequfim atumim*, “closed frames”) is left untranslated, since JPS renders I Kings 6:4 differently.

Isaiah.english_translation: Closes; and so (above, 29:10) “hath closed your eyes.”
He will not need to seek bread, for from heaven they will supply him with food.
The source of his waters will not fail — that is, his seed will grow great and all his needs will be supplied.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Thine eyes shall see the king in his beauty
Isaiah.english_translation: The explanation: you will merit to see from a land of far places your King in the splendor of His majesty. Or the explanation: (the Holy One, blessed be He, who is King — you will see Him from a distant land where you stand; you will see the miracles and the greatness that I will do for you, “and the people of obscure speech” will not see the Presence of the King in His beauty. End.) All of this is not in other books.
Isaiah.translator_note: The second explanation is in parentheses in the printed text, followed by the note that it is not found in other books.

Isaiah.english_translation: I say to you, the righteous one, that you will merit to see the radiance of the Presence of the Omnipresent.
Jonathan translated: “you shall look and see those who go down into the earth of Gehinnom.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Thy heart shall muse on the terror
Isaiah.english_translation: When you see the princes and the wise men of the nations who were rulers in their lifetime, and behold, they are being judged in Gehinnom, your heart will muse on terror and you will say: Where is the wisdom and the greatness of these? Where is he who counted in his lifetime and weighed every matter of wisdom, from whom they asked all the counsel of the kingdom?

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Where is he that counted the towers
Isaiah.english_translation: The explanation: he who counted the towers in each city, for those tall houses were considered more important and paid more in tax; and all that thought and fear will be yours no more.
Like *lo‘ez*: these are Assyria and Babylon, whose language is not the holy tongue.
You will not think in your heart that all of them will be dark and low.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: A people of a deep speech
Isaiah.english_translation: Like “And the whole earth was of one language” (Genesis 11:1) — *safah* means language.
*Agalim*, and “deep of speech” (above, “23” as printed) — all this is a foreign tongue, which they do not recognize in the holy tongue.
Isaiah.translator_note: The printed word *agalim* and the reference “above, 23” are given as printed; I could not confirm either.

Isaiah.english_translation: And whom will you see in your heart to be counted as kingship and rule? Zion, which is for us the city of the house of assembly.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: A tent that shall not be removed
Isaiah.english_translation: *Bal yitza‘an* — shall not be moved; and similar is *Elon be-tza‘ananim* (Judges 4:11, Rashi: “Judges 4”). The Targum translates it “plain of the basins,” and these are the hollows in the fields which are called *puits* in the foreign tongue (Old French) — like “the basins of the earth” it is called, for the waters gather there from the mountains and the hillocks. And the *bet* of *be-tza‘ananim*, I say, is not rooted in the word, but is a prefix.
Isaiah.translator_note:
Rashi’s Targum quotation (*mishor aganya*) and its Aramaic gloss (*aganei de-ar‘a*) are paraphrased as printed.
Old French *puits* (“well, hollow”) is not found in Darmesteter under this verse; the reading is from the Hebrew letters.

Isaiah.english_translation: The pegs to which they tie the cords of the tent: He shall not pluck them from the ground, from the place where they were fixed, like “and they quarried great stones” (I Kings 5:31) and so “and plucked them up, bar and all” (Judges 16:3) — an expression of tearing out.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: But there the LORD will be with us in majesty
Isaiah.english_translation: *Ki im* refers back to “shall never be plucked up” and “neither shall any of the cords thereof be broken”: the evil will not be, but only the good. The LORD will be there mighty for us, and the city will be a place of rivers and streams, in the manner stated in Ezekiel (Rashi: “Ezekiel 4”; he means 47:5): “and he measured a thousand, and made me cross a stream which I could not cross.” And so Joel prophesied: “And a fountain shall come forth of the house of the LORD” (Joel 4:18) — it is the stream that goes on growing stronger.
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s printed reference “Ezekiel 4” is Ezekiel 47.

Isaiah.english_translation: A ship that sails on water.
And a great *burni*.
Isaiah.translator_note: *Burni* (Aramaic, a kind of ship) is left untranslated.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For the LORD is our Judge
Isaiah.english_translation: Our ruler and judge.
Those who draw the ship — guilty Rome.
Isaiah.translator_note: *Rome ha-ḥayyevet* is rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_translation: *Ken*: establish well.
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s two words (*ha-ken heitev*) are terse; rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_translation: The mast of the ship.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: They do not spread the sail
Isaiah.english_translation: They will not be able to spread the sail that steers the ship.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Then is the prey of a great spoil divided
Isaiah.english_translation: *Adda‘ah*.
Isaiah.translator_note: *Adda‘ah* (Aramaic) is left untranslated; it appears to be a word for “booty.”

Isaiah.english_translation: They will divide much of the spoil of Sennacherib.
(Israel,) who until now were weak.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And the inhabitant shall not say
Isaiah.english_translation: Of Israel.
Because of this nation, the evil came upon me; for the people — Israel, who are called the people dwelling in Jerusalem — will be forgiven iniquity.
Isaiah.translator_note: The first clause is difficult in the printed text and is rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And all the host of heaven shall moulder away
Isaiah.english_translation: They will be afraid when I cast down the princes of Assyria and Babylon.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And the heavens shall be rolled together as a scroll
Isaiah.english_translation: An expression of rolling: *venigllu* “as a scroll the heavens.” Targum Jonathan: “and they shall be blotted out from under the heavens, as was said of them in the book.” But I explain it according to the context: because now the good and the light are for the wicked, when they are blotted out and destroyed, the world will be silent, dark upon them, as if the sun and the light were rolled up like the rolling of a scroll.
Wither.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: as a falling fig from the fig-tree
Isaiah.english_translation: A shriveled fruit on the tree is called *novelet*; and this is what our Rabbis explained (Berakhot 40): “What are *novelot*? *Bushlei kumra*” — figs that ripened in a *kumra*: after their picking, one piles them up and they warm and ripen.
Isaiah.translator_note: The Rabbinic quotation is given as Rashi cites it; I have not looked it up in Berakhot.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For My sword hath drunk its fill in heaven
Isaiah.english_translation: To kill the princes above; and afterward it will descend upon Amalek below, for no nation is smitten until its prince in heaven is smitten.
The people of My war — an expression of the Mishnah (Ketubot 17): “At a time of *ḥerem* they taught,” and so (I Kings 20:42) *ish ḥermi*, of Ahab.
Isaiah.translator_note: The tail of the comment (*ish ḥermi de-Ach’av*) is given as printed; JPS renders I Kings 20:42 “the man whom I had devoted to destruction.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the fat of the kidneys of rams
Isaiah.english_translation: Princes and rulers.

It belongs to the land of Moab; but because it set up a king over Edom, as it is said, *And Husham died and Jobab son of Zerah of Bozrah reigned in his stead* (Genesis 36), therefore it will be smitten with them — in the Pesikta.
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s wording of Genesis 36 combines verse 33 (“Bela died, and Jobab the son of Zerah of Bozrah reigned”) and verse 34 (“Husham”); translated as he gives it.

Isaiah.english_translation: With the he-goats written above.
Fat and great bulls, as you say: “Strong bulls of Bashan have beset me round” (Psalm 22:13).
That He will pay recompense for the matters of the quarrel of Zion, who cries out before Him to judge her from those who do her evil.
Of the Babylonians.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: From generation to generation it shall lie waste
Isaiah.english_translation: From that generation until the last generation. Another explanation: it is the curse of Moses (Exodus 17:16): “the LORD will have war with Amalek from generation to generation” — from the generation of Moses to the generation of Saul, and from there to the generation of Mordecai, and from there to the generation of our King Messiah.
A bird that flies at night, *coeta* in the foreign tongue (Old French).
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *coete* (“chouette,” owl) is confirmed in Darmesteter.

Isaiah.english_translation: Judgment of desolation.
Weights of a judgment of destruction, as (Deuteronomy 25:15) “A perfect and just weight.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: none shall be there to be called to the kingdom
Isaiah.english_translation: Her princes stand, and not one of them calls himself by the name of rulership and kingship.
Destruction.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: thorns shall come up in her palaces
Isaiah.english_translation: So is the way of ruins to sprout thorns and *sena’im*, and it is *qimmosh* and it is *ḥoaḥ* — all are kinds of thorns, such as *urtias* (Old French) and the like.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *ortias / ourties* (nettles) is confirmed in Darmesteter, who prints the gloss “ronces” beside it.

Isaiah.english_translation: A wilderness in which it is the way for *tannim* to be — a kind of evil beast.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the wild-cats shall meet with the jackals
Isaiah.english_translation: “And the *tamon* shall meet with the cats” — so Jonathan translated; *tamon* are *nemiyyot*, *martrines* in the foreign tongue (Old French).
Isaiah.translator_note:
*Nemiyyot* is left untranslated.
Darmesteter lists Old French *martrines* (“Lire : martrines”) under this verse with the gloss “panthères.”

Isaiah.english_translation: A demon.
An expression of rest.
The name of a she-demon.
An expression of a bird’s nest (Deuteronomy 22:6, “a bird’s nest”).
It is *qippod*.
And she will bear an egg.
This is the coming out of the chicks from the egg; and so it says (below, 59:5): “They hatch basilisks’ eggs.”
It is the calling of the bird, for the bird calls with its throat to draw chicks after it — *glocier* in the foreign tongue (Old French) — and so (Jeremiah 17) *qore dagar*.
Isaiah.translator_note:
Old French *glocier* (“gloussera,” to cluck) is confirmed in Darmesteter.
u|JPS renders Jeremiah 17:11 “the partridge that broodeth”; Rashi takes *dagar* as “calls.”

Isaiah.english_translation: *Voltures* in the foreign tongue (Old French).
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *voltiers / voltures* (“vautours,” vultures) is confirmed in Darmesteter.

Isaiah.english_translation: Like *el re‘utah*.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Seek you out of the book of the LORD, and read
Isaiah.english_translation: Read from the Book of Genesis: when He brought the Flood, He decreed that all creatures gather to be shut into the ark, male and female. Not one of them was absent from coming; how much more so when He decrees this upon them — to be gathered to drink blood, to eat flesh and fat.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: No one of these shall be missing
Isaiah.english_translation: They shall not lack, like “and there lacketh not one man of us” (Numbers 31:49).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For My mouth it hath commanded
Isaiah.english_translation: That they shall come.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the breath thereof it hath gathered them
Isaiah.english_translation: That of My mouth — it gathered them. *Ruḥo* refers to *pi*, like “And all the host of them by the breath of His mouth” (Psalm 33:6); here too, the breath of the mouth gathered them.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And He hath cast the lot for them
Isaiah.english_translation: Now the prophet speaks of the Holy One: And He cast for them — for those beasts and birds — a lot, that these will come up to their portion.

They will rejoice over them — like “they will rejoice from them” — as in “My children are gone forth of me” (*yetz’uni*, Jeremiah 10:20), which means “gone out from me”; and so “and boiled their flesh” (*bashel ha-basar*, I Kings 19:21) — he cooked the flesh for them.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The wilderness and the parched land shall be glad
Isaiah.english_translation: Jerusalem, which is called parched land, and Zion, which is called wilderness — they will rejoice over the fall of the mighty of Seir (and Bozrah).
Isaiah.translator_note: “(and Bozrah)” is in parentheses in the printed text, marking a doubtful phrase.

Isaiah.english_translation: Of Jerusalem.
Like *ve-lerannen*.
The Temple.
His glory is to Zion.

All the prophets, announcers of salvation, comfort Israel and strengthen their weak hands. “חזקו” is in the weighty pattern, and its explanation is: strengthen others. And if it had meant to say “strengthen yourselves, whose hands are weak,” it would have been pointed “חזקו ואמצו” (II Chronicles 32:7, “Be strong and of good courage”). Now that he tells them to strengthen and encourage others, it is pointed “חזקו אמצו, חזקו אל תיראו.” This one is pointed “חזקו” in the light form: strengthen yourselves of your own accord, as one would say to an individual, “Be strong and of good courage” (Joshua 1:6), and not say “strengthen.”
Isaiah.translator_note: The printed text lacks vowel marks, so the vowel distinctions Rashi draws between the forms of “חזקו” cannot be seen here; the Hebrew forms are given as printed.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Say to them that are of a fearful heart
Isaiah.english_translation: Those who hasten the redemption and are distressed over its delay.
Like *be-naqam yavo*.
He will come upon the wicked, and you He will save.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the eyes of the blind shall be opened
Isaiah.english_translation: Those who until now were blind to recognizing this fear of Me upon them.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped
Isaiah.english_translation: Who did not hear the voice of the prophets until now, “shall be opened and unstopped,” for I will give them a spirit directed to fearing Me. And of Israel he says this, for he called them blind and deaf, as it is said: “Hear, you deaf,” etc. (Isaiah 42:18).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the lame man leap as a hart
Isaiah.english_translation: Israel, who are now lame and weak; we find that He calls them lame and weak, as it is said, “The lame take the prey” (above, 33:23).
In My salvation.
The tongue of Israel who were among the Chaldeans, mute, hearing reproaches and not answering.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For in the wilderness shall waters break out
Isaiah.english_translation: For His salvation will gladden them, and they will flourish like a parched wilderness thirsty for water with springs bursting forth within it; that is, salvation will sprout for the crushed.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And the parched land shall become a pool
Isaiah.english_translation: To them, for a pool. One who craves salvation will be saved; and the prophet spoke in the language of a parable.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: In the habitation of jackals herds shall lie down
Isaiah.english_translation: In the habitation — a place that was a parched wilderness, a resting-place of the jackal, will be moist, a place of grass that turns to reed and rush; and reed and rush grow only in a place of water, as it is said (Job 8:11): “Can the rush shoot up without mire?”
*Ravtzah* is a noun like *marbetz* (“resting-place”), for it has no *mappiq* in the *he*.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And a highway shall be there, and a way
Isaiah.english_translation: For those who go and return.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The unclean shall not pass over it
Isaiah.english_translation: That road — any unclean person; that is, it will no longer be for the nations.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: but it shall be for those
Isaiah.english_translation: It is the road of those blind, deaf, lame and mute ones mentioned above, and the going on that road; and even if they are fools they will not err, for I will make it straight before them.

The boar from the forest (Psalm 80:14, “The boar out of the wood”) — there is no “breaker” among the beasts like the wild boar; and also the lion from his thicket (Jeremiah 4:7) — he is Nebuchadnezzar — will not be found there.

To that road. *Derekh* is used for both masculine and feminine, as it is written, “the way wherein they must walk” (Exodus 18:20) — behold, feminine; “[they shall come out against thee] one way” (Deuteronomy 28:7; Rashi cites “Deuteronomy 18”) — behold, masculine.
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s printed reference “Deuteronomy 18” for *be-derekh eḥad* is Deuteronomy 28:7.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: They shall not be found there
Isaiah.english_translation: [No] evil beast [will be found] there.
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s two words (*ḥayah ra‘ah sham*) are completed in brackets.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And everlasting joy shall be upon their heads
Isaiah.english_translation: The joy that they had long ago, already on the way of their leaving Egypt: “And the LORD went before them by day” (Exodus 13:21).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And sorrow and sighing shall flee away
Isaiah.english_translation: Sorrow and sighing from them.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the conduit of the upper pool
Isaiah.english_translation: *Fosier* (?) in the foreign tongue (Old French).
Isaiah.translator_note: The printed word is פושי״ר; Darmesteter lists it in several variant spellings with the gloss “dans le fossé” (in the ditch), so I have not committed to one reading.

Isaiah.english_translation: A place for the gathering of water, dug in the ground by human hands to put fish in, long and wide.
A beaten road — *chemin* in the foreign tongue (Old French).
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *chemin* (“dans le sentier”) is confirmed in Darmesteter.

Isaiah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “a field, the spreading-place of the fullers,” where the fullers spread out the garments.
One who writes the memorials in the books of the chronicles. (Another explanation: the reminder — what case comes before him first, that he decides it first.)

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I said: It is but vain words
Isaiah.english_translation: Until now it is only words of the lips in his mouth, saying, “I will not serve the king of Assyria”; and when he sees that I go up against him with an army, he will retract. Now behold, I have gone up; from now he will either serve me, or he must seek counsel and strength for war.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Now on whom dost thou trust
Isaiah.english_translation: Now that the time has come, tell me, on whom do you trust that you rebel against me?
On the broken, shattered reed, and the slivers enter his palm and pierce it; so Pharaoh to those who trust in him — in the end his help is to their harm.
Isaiah.translator_note: *Ha-qerumiyyot* is rendered “the slivers”; the exact sense is not given.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: whose high places and whose altars Hezekiah hath taken away
Isaiah.english_translation: He burned out all the houses of idolatry and the altars and the high places, and obligated all of Judah to bow before one altar.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: make a wager with my master
Isaiah.english_translation: Concerning this matter, if you are able to fulfill them: an expression of pledge (*eravon*), which is called *gagier* in the foreign tongue (Old French).
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *gagier* (“engage-toi”) is confirmed in Darmesteter.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: turn away the face of one captain
Isaiah.english_translation: Even the face of one commander, who is among my master’s small servants — for the least among the heads of his troops is appointed over a thousand men.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the least of my master’s servants
Isaiah.english_translation: “One of the servants,” like “under one of the shrubs” (Genesis 21:15), “one of the vain fellows” (II Samuel 6:20).
Not without His permission.

The prophets had already prophesied, “the riches of Damascus and the spoil of Samaria shall be carried away before the king of Assyria” (above, 8:4); and he erred in saying: As I did to Samaria, so will I do to Jerusalem.
We recognize it; *shome‘im* is an expression of *entendant* in the foreign tongue (Old French).
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *entendant* (“comprenant”) is confirmed in Darmesteter.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: speak not to us in the Jews’ language
Isaiah.english_translation: For all the people recognize the Jewish language, and they are afraid of your words. (Because he said to them, “Say now to Hezekiah,” (they thought) that he had not come to frighten the people; and Rab-shakeh was an apostate Israelite; they thought that although his master’s commandment was upon Rab-shakeh, his heart was drawn to his family, and his consolations would be moved.)
Isaiah.translator_note: The parenthesis is in the printed text and is hard to follow; the translation is literal.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Hath my master sent me to thy master, and to thee
Isaiah.english_translation: It is a question; therefore it is pointed with a *hataf patah*. Was it to your master and you alone that my master sent me? Did he not send me to all of them? And therefore I came, that all the people may hear and see, and that Hezekiah not incite them to rebel.
Even they, in the hunger of the siege.

Their excrement that comes out through their opening; and for a refined expression the scribes (Sofrim) instituted reading it “their going-out” (*tze’atam*). So our Rabbis taught: verses written in a disgraceful way are read in a praiseworthy way, such as (Deuteronomy 28) *ba-ophalim* [read] *ba-techorim*; (there) *yishgalennah* [read] *yishkavennah*; *ḥoreihem* [read] *tze’atam*.
Their urine; *shineihem* is moist excrement. *Shinei de-karkashta* is the rectum, which is called *tabbaḥiya* in the foreign tongue, and it stands by three teeth.
Isaiah.translator_note: The Old French word (טבחיא) and the last phrase are given as printed; I did not find them in Darmesteter.

Isaiah.english_translation: Will mislead.
Come out to me in peace and bless me, and bring me a gift of peace.
*Berakhah* is *salud* in the foreign tongue (Old French), as “And Jacob blessed Pharaoh” (Genesis 47:10).
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *salud* (“une salutation”) is confirmed in Darmesteter.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: eat you every one of his vine
Isaiah.english_translation: “And I will go away from you, and dwell in peace until I find a good land like your land and exile you there” — for such is his way, to move nations from land to land, as it is said (above, 10:13): “I have removed the bounds of the peoples.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: a land like your own land
Isaiah.english_translation: R. Shimon ben Yohai said: this one was a fool — a parable of a king, etc., in the Sifrei, parashat *Ve-haya ekev*. He should have said “to a land better than your land,” but he could not speak disparagingly of it.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: have they delivered Samaria out of my hand
Isaiah.english_translation: And the people of Samaria used to worship the gods of Aram, their neighbors; and Hamath is of Aram.
Because they heard blasphemy of the Name; it is like *birkat ha-Shem*.
*Esprovement* in the foreign tongue (Old French): the enemies reprove by their success, saying, “our hand is exalted, and there is no god like our God.”
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *esprovement* (“épreuve”) is confirmed in Darmesteter.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: for the children are come to the birth
Isaiah.english_translation: The children of Israel, children of the Holy One, blessed be He.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: there is not strength to bring forth
Isaiah.english_translation: A time of trouble like a woman sitting on the birth-stool with no strength for the child to come out.
He told his strength and showed his success and rebuked — *esprover* in the foreign tongue (Old French).
Isaiah.translator_note:
Rashi does not name the subject of “told … showed … rebuked”; the translation is literal.
Old French *esprover* (“il a prouvé”) is confirmed in Darmesteter.

Isaiah.english_translation: Immediately — this is the rumor of Tirhakah, king of Cush — and because of it he will go away from you this time to fight Tirhakah, and this is not a return to his land; and afterward he will come back here; and I am destined to return him to his land and to cause him to fall there by the sword.
The king of Assyria.
Saying: Tirhakah has come out to fight against you.

The second “and he heard” is not like the first “and he heard”: the first is an expression of hearing, and the second an expression of accepting — he accepted the words of the messengers and they pleased him, to set his heart to withdraw from Jerusalem to fight first with Cush.
To inform him that he was not withdrawing entirely, but only in order to return.
The name of a kingdom, as you say (Ezekiel 27:23): “Haran and Canneh and Eden.”
“Has the king of Assyria shaken him and overturned him?” — he destroyed them and carried them away from their place.
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi reads *Hena* and *Ivvah* as verbs (“shook him and overturned him”).

Isaiah.english_translation: It is true that the kings of Assyria destroyed.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: all the countries, and their land
Isaiah.english_translation: “The countries” — (the chief) provinces — “and their land” — (their land) adjoining them: the cities of the kingdom that are heads of provinces he calls “countries,” and the other districts around them he calls “their land.” And in the book (II Kings 19:17) it is written, “the nations and their lands,” and it is the same expression.
Isaiah.translator_note: The words in parentheses are in parentheses in the printed text, marking doubtful readings.

Isaiah.english_translation: Like *ve-natun otto ‘al kol eretz Mitzrayim* — an expression of a passive form, like *shamur*, *zakhur*: *donant* in the foreign tongue (Old French).
Isaiah.translator_note:
Rashi gives no reference for his example; I read it as Genesis 41:43 (“and he set him over all the land of Egypt”).
Old French *donant* (“et donnant”) is confirmed in Darmesteter.

Isaiah.english_translation: They [are]; therefore there was no power in them, and the king of Assyria destroyed them.
The Temple Mount.
The Temple.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I have cut down the tall cedars thereof
Isaiah.english_translation: I will not go to his land until I have destroyed it.
Its end.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The forest of his fruitful field
Isaiah.english_translation: The goodness of its praise and the weight of its strength.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I have digged and drunk water
Isaiah.english_translation: That is, I began all my works, and finished, and succeeded, like one who digs a pit and finds water and succeeds. *Qarti* is an expression of a spring (*maqor*).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: with the sole of my feet have I dried up
Isaiah.english_translation: (If) I came to besiege a city that trusted in the strength of its rivers, I brought many troops against it, and the waters of their rivers were exhausted by their animals’ drinking and by the tread of their feet.
Present tense — that is, such is my way constantly.
The rivers of a city that comes under siege by means of rivers.

And why do you boast? This is not yours, for it is a decree from before Me many years ago that you be the one who exacts punishment from the nations, as it is said (above, 10:5): “the rod of Mine anger.”

More than seventy years ago Amos prophesied (Amos 7:11), two years before the earthquake: “And Israel shall surely be led away captive out of his land.” From then you should have heard that I had made and prepared this punishment.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: In ancient times I fashioned it
Isaiah.english_translation: From the six days of Creation that decree that was decreed upon you came up in My mind, as it is said (above, 30:33): “For a hearth is ordered of old; Yea, for the king it is prepared.” Now, when I made you mighty over the nations, I brought you to that decree, so that you would reduce fortified cities to heaps — that you kill their inhabitants and they become desolate of people, and be ready to be heaps sprouting greenery.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Therefore their inhabitants were of small power
Isaiah.english_translation: I weakened their strength before you.
*Shedemah* is what is called *estoble* in the foreign tongue (Old French): the roots of the harvest that remain in the ground.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *estoble* (“herbe desséchée, racine de l’épi qui reste dans le sol”) is confirmed in Darmesteter.

Isaiah.english_translation: When it has not yet reached ripening and hardening to come to the state of standing grain, and it is weak and tender.
Before it becomes standing grain.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: thy sitting down, and thy going out, and thy coming in
Isaiah.english_translation: Targum: “and your sitting in counsel, and your going out to the field to wage battle, and your coming to the Land of Israel are revealed before Me”; when the thought came up in your heart and you took counsel to destroy My house, I knew.
Your shaking and your exalting yourself against Me.
Like *ve-sha’onekha*.
A kind of ring, and they thrust it into the lip of an animal whose ways are evil, to draw it by it.

Targum: *zamam*; it is of iron and they thrust it into the nostrils of the she-camel, and this is what we learned, “and the she-camel with a nose-ring,” in tractate Shabbat. (Requires investigation, for from the verse it appears explicitly to be the opposite, for *ḥaḥ* is in the nose and *metheg* in the lip.)
Isaiah.translator_note: The bracketed remark “(requires investigation …)” is in the printed text and appears to be a later editor’s note, not Rashi’s own.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And this shall be the sign unto thee
Isaiah.english_translation: This speech is not to Sennacherib; rather the prophet spoke to Hezekiah: and this answer will be for you a sign of another assurance. Behold, the legions have destroyed all the crops and cut down all the trees, and the Holy One, blessed be He, assures you that this year you will be sustained by the aftergrowth of the crops that will sprout of themselves.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: you shall eat this year that which groweth of itself
Isaiah.english_translation: To eat this year aftergrowth (*safiah*).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: in the second year that which springeth of the same
Isaiah.english_translation: They are aftergrowths of the cut-down trees; so it is in Seder Olam. But Jonathan translated *katkatin*, “aftergrowths of aftergrowths.” And “this is the sign”: when you see that My word is fulfilled — that Sennacherib returns to his land and falls — believe that the second assurance will be fulfilled as well.
Isaiah.translator_note: The Aramaic *katkatin* is left untranslated.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the zeal of the LORD of hosts shall perform this
Isaiah.english_translation: That He will be zealous for His Name, and not because of a merit in your hands; we have learned that the merit of the fathers has ended.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: neither shall he come before it with shield
Isaiah.english_translation: He will not array a shield before you, as the Targum translates *lifnei* (“before”) by *qedam*.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: nor cast a mound against it
Isaiah.english_translation: He will not heap up against it a *melita*. I say it is that they pour earth and heap it up before the wall and the towers in order to build upon it a *karkom*.
Isaiah.translator_note: *Karkom* is left untranslated; its sense is not clear to me.

Isaiah.english_translation: *Sollelah* is named for the fact that they pave and pack it with mallets so that it hardens; and its Targum is *melita*, because they first make for it two partitions of reed fencing and pour the earth between them and pack it there after they have filled the partitions. And I have heard that they break it down by throwing large stones, which are called *perrière* in the foreign tongue (Old French); but there is nothing in stones of the sense of pouring or of paving, and the language of the Targum does not fit this explanation.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *perrière* (“jet de grosses pierres”) is confirmed in Darmesteter.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And the angel of the LORD went forth
Isaiah.english_translation: After he went and fought with Cush, he returned and came to Jerusalem, and at that hour “the angel of the LORD went forth.” And thus it is taught in Seder Olam: “Behold, I will put a spirit in him, and he shall hear a rumour” — as it is said, “And he heard say concerning Tirhakah, etc.” (above, 37:9). [Sennacherib] swept away Shebna the steward and his company, led them in chains, went to Cush, took the choicest of all the treasures, and came to Jerusalem, to fulfill what is said (below, 45:14): *the labor of Egypt and the merchandise of Cush shall pass over you* — this is Jerusalem; *they shall go after you* — this is Hezekiah. At that time “and he sent Tartan and Rab-saris” — they are mentioned in the Book (II Kings 18:17); and they are the “messengers” of whom it is said that he sent after the rumor, as it is said (above, 37:9) “he sent messengers to Hezekiah”; and they did not come with Rab-shakeh on the first mission. And to those letters Isaiah replied (there, 37:22) “She hath despised thee and laughed thee to scorn.” At that hour “the angel of the LORD went forth and smote,” etc. All of them were kings with crowns tied on their heads, and the smallest among them was commander over two thousand, as it is said (above, 36:8–9): “I will give thee two thousand horses” and “How then canst thou turn away the face of one captain,” etc. — we learned that even the smallest of the governors is commander over thousands of men; and they fell, they and their armies.
Isaiah.translator_note:
The identity of the subject of the verbs “swept away … led … took” is not stated in the printed text; I supplied “Sennacherib” in brackets from the context.
The quotation from Isaiah 45:14 is Rashi’s abridgment and the identifications (“this is Jerusalem … this is Hezekiah”) are given as he states them.

Isaiah.english_translation: It is the head of the kingdom, as it is said (Genesis 10:11): “From that land Asshur went forth and built Nineveh.”
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi reads Genesis 10:11 as “Asshur went forth”; JPS renders “he went forth into Asshur.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the house of Nisroch his god
Isaiah.english_translation: *Nesar* — a plank from the ark of Noah, as explained in the aggadah of *Helek*.
Isaiah.translator_note: “The aggadah of *Helek*” is read as the aggadic section of the chapter *Helek* (Sanhedrin); I have not looked up the passage.

Isaiah.english_translation: For he said, “If You save me, so that my royal subjects do not kill me — for I brought their sons here and they died — I will offer my two sons before You”; they stood up and killed him.

Three days before the fall of Sennacherib Hezekiah fell sick; and on the third day, when he went up to the House of the LORD, which is the day of the fall of Sennacherib, it was the first festival day of Passover.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: for thou shalt die, and not live
Isaiah.english_translation: You will die in this world and not live in the world to come, because you did not take a wife, etc., as is stated in Berakhot.
Where is Your compassion?

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I will add unto thy days fifteen years
Isaiah.english_translation: I am the one who will add to your days.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I will deliver thee and this city out of the hand of the king of Assyria
Isaiah.english_translation: We learn that he fell sick before the fall of Sennacherib.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And this shall be the sign unto thee
Isaiah.english_translation: That you will be healed and your days added, as explained below; and in Kings (II 20) he asked him, “What is the sign that I shall go up?”
Backward ten degrees — the shadow that had gone down.
A kind of steps made opposite the sun to test the hours of the day with them, like the *orlogin* (horologe) that craftsmen make.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: which is gone down on the sun-dial of Ahaz
Isaiah.english_translation: It hurried to go down, and the day was shortened by ten hours on the day Ahaz died, so that they would not eulogize him; and they now went back up on the day Hezekiah was healed, and ten hours were added to the day.
Targum Jonathan: “Hezekiah wrote a thanksgiving over the miracle that was done for Hezekiah.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: In the noontide of my days I shall go
Isaiah.english_translation: When I saw my days in *demi* — in desolation and stillness — like “all the people of Canaan are undone” (*nidmah*, Zephaniah 1; JPS: “all the merchant people are undone”): that is, when I fell sick I said, “I shall go to the gates of Sheol; now I will die,” for until that day no sick person had been healed.
Isaiah.translator_note: *Ḥarishah* (“stillness” / “plowing”) is ambiguous; rendered “stillness.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I am deprived of the residue of my years
Isaiah.english_translation: Like “there lacketh not one man of us” (Numbers 31:49) — I am lacking the rest of my years. And Jonathan translated: “for my remembrance for good, years have been added to me” — I was remembered for good and my years were increased.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I said: I shall not see the LORD
Isaiah.english_translation: (Additions: “I said, I shall not see Yah”: I shall no longer use the Name Yah.
Isaiah.translator_note: This and the next comment are printed in parentheses as an addition (*tosafot*) to Rashi’s text.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Even the LORD in the land of the living
Isaiah.english_translation: The living use it, but the dead are not permitted, as it is said, “*lo ha-metim yehalelu-Yah*” (Psalm 115:17; JPS “The dead praise not the LORD”) — it is a statute for the dead that they never mention a two-letter name. End.)
(Abbreviation בב״ה, not expanded in the printed text.)
Isaiah.translator_note: The abbreviation בב״ה is not expanded in the printed text; it may stand for “in the House of the LORD.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I shall behold man no more
Isaiah.english_translation: Still living.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: with the inhabitants of the world
Isaiah.english_translation: That I shall be with the dead, who dwell in the land of cessation and are prevented from the living.
The people of my generation have departed from me. *Nasa* is like *nasaḥ* (torn out), like “shall never be plucked up” (above, 33:20).
Like the tent of a herdsman of animals, who moves it from here and fixes it in another place when this pasture is finished.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I have rolled up like a weaver my life
Isaiah.english_translation: I cut my life short quickly, like the weaver who hastens to weave; all this I thought. And Jonathan translated “like a stream of banks (*gedudin*)” — like a stream drawn between high banks, which does not spread out, and therefore its waters are swift to run; and I say it is a rapid stream whose name is *oreg*, which is what is said (Job 7:6): “My days are swifter than a weaver’s shuttle” (*oreg*), “They are passed away as the swift ships” (there, 9:26).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: He will cut me off from the thrum
Isaiah.english_translation: Targum: “from the honor of my kingship I am exiled”; I thought that now He would cut me off from all my honor. *Dalah* is an expression of *gavvah*, and so *ve-dallat roshekh* (Song 7:6; JPS “the hair of thy head”).
Isaiah.translator_note: Targum *miyyaqar malkuti ana galei* is rendered as printed; *gavvah* is left untranslated. Audit 4: the Aramaic quotation was checked against Targum Jonathan/the Ketuvim Targum (Mikraot Gedolot, Sefaria) at ISA 38:12 and reads as quoted; the meaning of the unclear word, if noted above, is still unresolved.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: From day even to night wilt Thou make an end of me
Isaiah.english_translation: Like “from male to female”; that is, from days and nights You will finish me. And so Jonathan translated: “my days and my nights are complete.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I make myself like unto a lion until morning
Isaiah.english_translation: I set myself all night to bear the pains of the illness, and strengthened myself like a lion to bear it.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The more it breaketh all my bones
Isaiah.english_translation: Like “so they multiplied and spread abroad” (Exodus 1:12): as much as I strengthen myself, so the illness grows stronger upon me to break all my bones.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Like a swallow or a crane
Isaiah.english_translation: Like *sus*, which is the name of a bird.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Like a swallow or a crane
Isaiah.english_translation: Like *sus* and *agur*. (Another explanation:) like that bird that is seized by its throat and chirps; and so Targum Jonathan: “like a *susia* that is seized and chirps.”
Isaiah.translator_note: The Targum’s last word (*mantzif*) is rendered “chirps,” as in Rashi’s own explanation.

Isaiah.english_translation: Like *oshuq otti*: take me from the hand of the angel of death and be surety for me to be saved — an expression of suretyship, *garantie* in the foreign tongue (Old French) — like “Be surety for Thy servant for good” (Psalm 119:122).
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *garantie* (“sois garant pour moi”) is confirmed in Darmesteter.

Isaiah.english_translation: *Oshuq otti* — from his hand — as you say, “Heal her now” (Numbers 12:13): “heal her.”
Praise and laud before Him — and behold, He told me consolations and He did them.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I shall go softly all my years
Isaiah.english_translation: Like “and my sleep fled” (Genesis 31:40): I shall be moved away from all my sleep to laud before Him. Jonathan translated *shenot* as an expression of years.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: for the bitterness of my soul
Isaiah.english_translation: That was bitter, and He consoled me.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: O Lord, by these things men live
Isaiah.english_translation: Targum: “LORD, over all the dead You said to revive.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And altogether therein is the life of my spirit
Isaiah.english_translation: “And before all of them You revived the life of my spirit.” And I say, according to its plain sense: “LORD, upon them” — upon my years mentioned above.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: O Lord, by these things men live
Isaiah.english_translation: The LORD, who caused His Presence and His kindness to dwell upon them, and said to me by the mouth of His prophet, “they shall live.”
Isaiah.translator_note: The heading printed with this comment (“I shall go softly all my years”) belongs to 38:15; the comment itself fits 38:16.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And altogether therein is the life of my spirit
Isaiah.english_translation: And for everything on which the life of my spirit depends, the LORD said of them, “and they shall live.”
From now I know that You will restore me and give me life. *Taḥlimeni*: You will heal me and strengthen me, as (Job 39:4) “Their young ones wax strong.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Behold, for my peace I had great bitterness
Isaiah.english_translation: When I was told of peace, that too was bitter to me, for they hung my healing on the merit of others: “Thus saith the LORD, the God of David thy father” (above, 38:5), “for Mine own sake, and for My servant David’s sake” (37:35); here You made known to me that I am a sinner. So the Sages explained. But according to the settling of the verse it implies: “Behold, for peace I had great bitterness” — when I was told by You that You would save me from the hand of Sennacherib, I had great bitterness over my illness, for I was inclined to die and I did not rejoice at the tidings; and You, in Your goodness, desired my soul, so that it not descend to the pit.
Isaiah.translator_note: In the printed text “(above, 37)” follows the first quotation; the two quotations are from 38:5 and 37:35.

Isaiah.english_translation: If I had died, I would not have given thanks to You for the miracle of the fall of Sennacherib, and I would not have looked toward the truth of Your promise that You promised me about it.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The living, the living, he shall praise Thee
Isaiah.english_translation: An expression of living human beings: that is, when there are living people in this world, this one living and that one living, the thanksgiving goes forth from between them. (Another version: “Living, living — You are living, and it is fitting to give thanks to the Living One.”)
*Enseigner* in the foreign tongue (Old French).
Isaiah.translator_note: The printed spelling is אשישפ״ר; Darmesteter lists the Old French, in several variant spellings, as *enseigner* (“il enseignera,” he will teach).

Isaiah.english_translation: The father informs and directs the mind of his son toward Your truth, to believe in You.
A cake made of figs: when they are moist they are called figs, and when they are pressed into a round they are called *develah*.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: lay it for a plaster upon the boil
Isaiah.english_translation: And they smeared it, to make it stick to the boil. And it was a miracle within a miracle, for even living flesh on which a *develah* is placed becomes putrid; but the Holy One, blessed be He, puts a damaging thing into a thing that is damaged, and heals.
How good and how pleasant is this sign given to me, by which I shall go up to the house of the LORD.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: for he heard that he had been sick, and was recovered
Isaiah.english_translation: He [the king of Babylon] was accustomed to eat at the third hour and sleep until the ninth; when the orb of the sun turned back for Hezekiah, he rose from his sleep at the ninth hour and found that it was morning. He wanted to kill all his servants; he said, “You let me sleep day and night until morning!” They said to him, “It is the orb of the sun that turned back.” He said to them, “And who turned it back?” They said to him, “The God of Hezekiah,” etc., as is stated in Tanhuma and in the Pesikta.
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi does not name the king; “[the king of Babylon]” is supplied from the verse.

Isaiah.english_translation: His storehouse of spices, like “spicery and balm and ladanum” (Genesis 37:25).

Some interpret it as the anointing oil, and some say it is balsam oil, which was found in the Land of Israel, and it is the *pannag* mentioned in Ezekiel (27:17): “Judah and Israel, they were your traders; with wheat of Minnith and *pannag*”; and I saw in the Book of Yosippon that it is balsam, and it grows in Jericho; therefore it is called Jericho (*Yeriho*), from the fragrance (*reiaḥ*).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: there was nothing in his house
Isaiah.english_translation: Even a Torah scroll.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: They are come from a far country unto me
Isaiah.english_translation: This is one of three persons whom the Omnipresent tested: Cain, Hezekiah and Balaam. Hezekiah should have answered, “You are the prophet of the Omnipresent, and you ask me?” He began to boast and said, “From a far country they came to me”; therefore he was punished — and for rejoicing over them and feeding them at his table. And so Balaam, to whom He said, “Who are these men with thee?”, and he answered and said, “Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab, hath sent unto me” (Numbers 22:10). And so Cain, to whom He said, “Where is Abel thy brother?” (Genesis 4:9; Rashi’s printed reference is “Genesis 14”); he should have said, “Master of the Universe, are not all hidden things revealed to You?”, etc., as stated in Tanhuma.
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s printed reference “Genesis 14” for “Where is Abel thy brother?” is Genesis 4:9.

Isaiah.english_translation: Measure for measure, corresponding to “there was nothing (*lo hayah davar*).”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And of thy sons that shall issue from thee
Isaiah.english_translation: They are Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Good is the word of the LORD
Isaiah.english_translation: Since in my days there will be peace.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Comfort you, comfort you My people
Isaiah.english_translation: He returns to his future prophecies; for from here to the end of the book are words of consolation; this section he set as a break between them and the calamities: Comfort, you prophets, comfort My people.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: That her time of service is accomplished
Isaiah.english_translation: Targum: “She is destined to be filled with the people of her exiles,” like *ki mal’ah mi-tzeva’ah*; and some interpret *tzeva’ah* as in “Is there not a time of service to man upon earth?” (Job 7:1).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: That her guilt is paid off
Isaiah.english_translation: Appeased.

Targum: “For she has received the cup of consolations from before the LORD, as if she had been smitten two for one for all her sins.” And according to the plain sense it is possible to explain: “for she received double punishment.” And if you say, how is it the way of the Holy One, blessed be He, to repay a person double for his sin — we find an explicit verse (Jeremiah 16:18): “And first I will recompense their iniquity and their sin double.”
Isaiah.translator_note: The printed text reads *ve-shalluti* in the Jeremiah quotation; the verse reads *ve-shillamti*.

Isaiah.english_translation: The Holy Spirit calls in the wilderness.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Clear you in the wilderness the way of the LORD
Isaiah.english_translation: The road of Jerusalem, for her exiles to return into her.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Every valley shall be lifted up
Isaiah.english_translation: “And the mountain shall be lowered” — behold, a smooth, level and easy road.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And the rugged shall be made level
Isaiah.english_translation: Mountains adjacent to one another, and because of their adjacency the descent between them is upright and not crooked, so that it is easy to descend and ascend. (*Ha-rekhasim* is translated “its banks” [*gedudaw*], an expression of height, like “the banks of the river.”)
Isaiah.translator_note: The parenthesis is in the printed text and is hard to follow; the Aramaic *gedudaw* is rendered “its banks.”

Isaiah.english_translation: Like “and they shall bind the breastplate” (*ve-yirkesu*, Exodus 28:28).
*Campagne* in the foreign tongue (Old French): a smooth and level land.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *campagne* (“plaine”) is confirmed in Darmesteter.

Isaiah.english_translation: From the Holy One, blessed be He, who says to me: Proclaim!

My spirit [says] to him, “What shall I proclaim?”, and the voice answers him: Proclaim this: “All flesh is grass” — all who exalt themselves, their greatness will be overturned and will be like grass. (Another explanation: “All flesh is grass”) — the end of man is to die; therefore if he says he will do kindness, it is like the flower of the field that is crushed and dries up, and one cannot rely on him, for it is not in his power to fulfil — perhaps he will die; for when the grass dries, the flower fades, so when a man dies his promise is annulled. “But the word of our God shall stand,” for He lives and endures, and it is in His power to fulfil; therefore, upon a high mountain get up, O herald of Zion, for from the mouth of the One who lives forever is the promise of the tidings.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the goodliness thereof is as the flower of the field
Isaiah.english_translation: “For ḥesed …” “… sin” (Proverbs 14).
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s quotation is abbreviated (*ki ḥesed etc. ḥatat*) and does not match Proverbs 14:34 word for word; JPS renders it “But sin is a reproach to any people.”

Isaiah.english_translation: Withered.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: O thou that tellest good tidings to Zion
Isaiah.english_translation: Targum: “the prophets who announce to Zion”; and in another place He says “the feet of the messenger” (below, 52:7; Rashi’s printed reference is “22”). If they merit, light like the male; if they do not merit, weak like the female, and he delays his steps until the end.
Isaiah.translator_note:
Rashi’s printed reference “below 22” for “the feet of the messenger” is 52:7.
u|The final clause is Rashi’s comment on the feminine form *mevasseret*; rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: will come as a Mighty One
Isaiah.english_translation: Upon the nations, to exact retribution.
Prepared with Him for the righteous.
The reward of work which is upon Him to give them.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Even as a shepherd that feedeth his flock
Isaiah.english_translation: He whose flock grazes in his arm; he gathers lambs, and in his bosom he carries them.
Targum: “the nursing ones He leads gently” — the sheep that nurse.
Like *menahel*.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Who hath measured the waters in the hollow of his hand
Isaiah.english_translation: All this He had power to do, and surely He has power to keep these promises.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: in the hollow of his hand
Isaiah.english_translation: In His walking, as it is said, “Thou hast trodden the sea with Thy horses” (Habakkuk 3:15). *Bish‘olo* is like “in a hollow way between the vineyards” (Numbers 22:24) — a path. Another explanation: that it is named for a vessel, and so “for handfuls of barley” (Ezekiel 13:19).
*Amolier* in the foreign tongue (Old French): an expression of measure and number, as “and the tale of bricks shall you deliver” (Exodus 5:18).
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *amolier* (from *ad + modulare*, “to measure”) is confirmed in Darmesteter.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the dust of the earth in a measure
Isaiah.english_translation: And He measured in thirds: a third wilderness, a third inhabited land, a third seas and rivers. Another explanation: with a *shalish* — from the thumb to a cubit, thirds of the fingers. And Menahem explained that it is the name of a vessel, and so “And given them tears to drink in large measure” (Psalm 80:6; Rashi’s printed reference is “Psalms 60”).
Isaiah.translator_note:
Rashi’s printed reference “Psalms 60” for *shalish* is Psalm 80:6.
u|The second explanation (“from the thumb to a cubit, thirds of the fingers”) is rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_translation: All according to the earth: a heavy mountain is fixed in hard earth, and the lighter ones in soft earth.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: meted out the spirit of the LORD
Isaiah.english_translation: The Holy Spirit in the mouth of the prophets — the LORD measured it, and it is worthy to be believed.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Or who was His counsellor that he might instruct Him?
Isaiah.english_translation: His spirit — so Targum Jonathan; and according to its sense, “the man of His counsel” refers back to the beginning of the verse: who has measured His spirit, and who is the man of His counsel who informs the Holy One of counsel?
Isaiah.translator_note: “His spirit — so Targum Jonathan” is terse; rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_translation: Which of the nations did He consult, as He consulted with the prophets, as it is said of Abraham, “Shall I hide from Abraham that which I am doing” (Genesis 18:17), etc.?
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s printed reference here is “Genesis 26”; the quotation is Genesis 18:17 (Genesis 26:5 is the verse quoted in the next comment).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And taught Him in the path of right
Isaiah.english_translation: Which of the nations did this — that taught him wisdom — as He did for Abraham, to whom He gave a heart to recognize Him on his own and to understand the Torah, as it is said, “and he kept My charge” (Genesis 26:5), and it says, “to the end that He may command” (there, 18:19), etc.; and his kidneys were pouring forth wisdom, as it is said, “Yea, in the night seasons my reins instruct me” (Psalm 16:7). (“With whom took He counsel and instructed him?” The man [counsels] the Holy One? “Behold, all the nations before Him are as a drop of a bucket” — how could they teach Him?)
Isaiah.translator_note: The closing parenthesis (“The man …?”) is hard to follow in the printed text; rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Behold, the nations are as a drop of a bucket
Isaiah.english_translation: The idolaters, who refuse to recognize their Creator, and they are not esteemed by Him so that prophets be set up from among them to reveal His secret.
Like a bitter drop that drips from the edges of the bucket, and from the sediment of the foulness of the water and the rot of the wood: *limonide* in the foreign tongue (Old French).
Isaiah.translator_note: Darmesteter lists the Old French (*limonide* / *limonie*) with the gloss “comme une goutte tombant d’un seau.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the small dust of the balance
Isaiah.english_translation: For the copper produces mould and becomes powdery.
Fine dust.
Like dust that is carried and rises by the wind: “as fine dust that is taken up.”
For His altar.
Its beasts, of Lebanon: not enough for a burnt-offering. Another explanation: “and Lebanon is not sufficient for fuel,” etc. — to atone for the iniquity of the nations.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: All the nations are as nothing before Him
Isaiah.english_translation: They are as nothing in His eyes and are not esteemed before Him.
He pours for himself an image.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the goldsmith spread over with gold
Isaiah.english_translation: A craftsman of iron casts it from iron or copper, and afterward the goldsmith hammers it out in plates of gold and overlays it from above.
Chains.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: He chooseth a tree that will not rot
Isaiah.english_translation: Or if he comes to make it of wood, the learned one who knows how to distinguish between wood that lasts and other woods will choose wood that will not rot quickly.
The learned one, as “was I ever wont (*ha-haskein hiskanti*) to do so unto thee?” (Numbers 22:30).
Separation: the selecting of the woods.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Have you not understood the foundations of the earth?
Isaiah.english_translation: The foundations of the earth — who founded it? Him you ought to have served.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: above the circle of the earth
Isaiah.english_translation: An expression of compass (below, 44:13, “with the compasses”): a circle; *compas* in the foreign tongue (Old French).
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *compas* (“compas”) is confirmed in Darmesteter.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And the inhabitants thereof are as grasshoppers
Isaiah.english_translation: Before Him, like grasshoppers.
Like a hanging, *toile* in the foreign tongue (Old French).
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *toile* (printed טייל״א; Darmesteter: “toile”) is confirmed.

Isaiah.english_translation: Even they are like those who were not planted.
And moreover, they will be rooted up as if they had not been sown; sowing is less than planting.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Scarce hath their stock taken root in the earth
Isaiah.english_translation: When they are uprooted, the stock will not take root in the ground. So that it differs from every *shoresh* in Scripture, whose accent is on the first letter and whose *resh* is pointed with *patah*; this one has its accent below and is pointed with *kamatz*, because it is a verbal form — *enraciner* in the foreign tongue (Old French).
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *enraciner* (“s’enracinant”) is confirmed in Darmesteter.

Isaiah.english_translation: All the host that you see on high.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: By the greatness of His might, and for that He is strong in power
Isaiah.english_translation: That He has, and that He is mighty in power — not one of the host is missing so as not to be called by name.
My people, Jacob, and you speak in exile.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: My way is hid from the LORD
Isaiah.english_translation: He hid from before His eyes all that we served Him, and set over us those who did not know Him.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: my right is passed over from my God
Isaiah.english_translation: He removed from before Him the judgment of good recompense that it was His to pay to our fathers and to us.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The Creator of the ends of the earth
Isaiah.english_translation: And He who has such power and such wisdom knows the thoughts — why does He delay your good? Only in order to end transgression and complete sin through sufferings.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: He giveth power to the faint
Isaiah.english_translation: And in the end He will exchange strength for your weariness.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Even the youths shall faint and be weary
Isaiah.english_translation: The might of the Chaldeans, who are shaken free of the commandments, will grow faint.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the young men shall utterly fall
Isaiah.english_translation: Those who are now mighty and strong will stumble, and you who hope in the LORD will exchange for new and strong strength.
Wing.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And let the peoples renew their strength
Isaiah.english_translation: “Keep silence before Me” — in order to hear a word.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And let the peoples renew their strength
Isaiah.english_translation: “O islands” — the nations of idolaters.
Let them adorn themselves and strengthen themselves with all their might; perhaps they will stand in judgment by force.
Here; and then, when they draw near, let them speak.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Let us come near together to judgment
Isaiah.english_translation: To reprove them to their faces.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Who hath raised up one from the east
Isaiah.english_translation: The one whom righteousness calls to his foot: who roused Abraham, to bring him from Aram, which is in the east; and the righteousness that he did was before his feet wherever he went.
He who roused him from his place to journey, He gave before him four kings and their armies.
*Yardeh*.
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s single word (ירדה) is given as printed.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: His sword maketh them as the dust
Isaiah.english_translation: Targum: “He casts the slain like dust before his sword.” He gave his sword and makes many slain like dust, and his bow He gave — makes many dead and fallen like driven stubble.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: He pursueth them, and passeth on safely
Isaiah.english_translation: He went along his paths in peace; he did not stumble when he pursued them.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The way with his feet he treadeth not
Isaiah.english_translation: A way which he had not previously come with his feet; “he does not come” — he was not accustomed to come.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Who hath wrought and done it?
Isaiah.english_translation: Who has done this for him? He who calls the generations from the beginning, from the first Adam — He did this also for Abraham.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I, the LORD, who am the first
Isaiah.english_translation: To do a wonder and to help.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And with the last am the same
Isaiah.english_translation: Also with you, the last children, I will be, and I will help you.
The worshippers of idols [see] the mighty acts that I will do, and they will fear.
Together, they gather to fight when they see the redemption.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: They helped every one his neighbour
Isaiah.english_translation: He will say, “Be strong for the war” — perhaps their gods will stand for them.
The caster of the image.
The one who hammers it out with gold.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: he that smootheth with the hammer
Isaiah.english_translation: At the end, when he strikes gently to smooth the work.
He is the one who begins it, when it is a lump, and strikes with all his strength.
Isaiah.translator_note: *Ḥeshet* (“lump / ingot”) is rendered by its likely sense.

Isaiah.english_translation: Concerning those who would go after good ground to cleave to it iron *‘ashashiyyot*.
Isaiah.translator_note: *‘Ashashiyyot barzel* is rendered literally (“iron *‘ashashiyyot*”); the word is left untranslated.

Isaiah.english_translation: *Soldure* in the foreign tongue (Old French): a soldering.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *soudure* (printed שולדור״א; Darmesteter: “La soudure”) is confirmed.

Isaiah.english_translation: To the image.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: that it should not be moved
Isaiah.english_translation: All of them will strengthen one another.

And upon Me it rests to help you — the end of the verse: “Fear not, for I am with thee.” So it appears to me the connection of the matter according to its plain sense. But an aggadic midrash in Genesis Rabbah expounds the whole matter as referring to Melchizedek and Abraham.

“The isles saw, and feared” (41:5): that war — Shem was afraid of Abraham, lest he say to him, “You have established these wicked ones in the world”; and Abraham was afraid of Shem, because he had slain the sons of Elam, who are descended from Shem.
Isaiah.translator_note:
The printed lemma here (“(ה) ראו איים”) is the verse-number marker followed by the words of 41:5.
u|The lemma phrase belongs to 41:5, which the site divides differently; an in-verse phrase is used as the lemma.

Isaiah.english_translation: “Isles”: just as the isles of the sea are set apart in the world, so Abraham and Shem were set apart in the world.
Isaiah.translator_note: The lemma phrase “isles” belongs to 41:5–6; see the note on the preceding comment.

Isaiah.english_translation: “Each one helped his neighbour” (41:6): this one helps that one with blessings — “Blessed be Abram” (Genesis 14:19; printed “14:20”) — and that one helps this one with gifts — “And he gave him a tenth of all” (there, 14:20).
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s printed reference “Genesis 14:20” for the blessing is 14:19; the gift of the tenth is 14:20.

Isaiah.english_translation: “And the craftsman strengthened” (41:7): this is Shem, who was a smith, making nails and bolts for the ark.
“the goldsmith” (41:7): this is Abraham, who refines the creatures to bring them near to the Divine Presence.
“him that smiteth the anvil” (41:7): this is Abraham, who smote all these kings at one time.
“Saying of the soldering: ‘It is good’” (41:7): it is good to cleave to the God of this one.
“And he fastened it” (41:7): Shem [strengthened] Abraham, so that he might cleave to the Holy One, blessed be He, and not be moved.
Abraham, who was not of the seed of the righteous — I did all this for him. “And thou, Israel, My servant” — acquired by Me from two fathers.
Isaiah.translator_note: “Acquired by Me from two fathers” is rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The seed of Abraham My friend
Isaiah.english_translation: Who did not come to know Me through rebuke and the teaching of his fathers, but out of love.
Isaiah.translator_note: The Hebrew says he did not know Me “from rebuke and teaching of his fathers”; rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Thou whom I have taken hold of
Isaiah.english_translation: I took thee for My portion, as “and he put forth his hand, and laid hold of it” (Exodus 4:4).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: from the ends of the earth
Isaiah.english_translation: From the rest of the idolaters.
From the great ones among them.
By name, for My portion: My son, My firstborn, Israel.
Unlike that one of whom it is said (Malachi 1) “I hated.”
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s printed reference “Malachi 1” is Malachi 1:3 (“But Esau I hated”).

Isaiah.english_translation: Let thy heart not melt, to become like this wax. And this is the rule: every word whose root begins with *shin*, when it comes to speak in the reflexive form (*hitpa‘el*), the *tav* is split off and enters between the two letters of the word’s root, as in *va-yishtomem* (Isaiah 29 [printed]), *va-yishtamer ḥukkot ‘Omri* (Micah 7 [printed]), *tishtakkerin* (1 Samuel 1), *tishtapekh nafshi* (Job 30).
Isaiah.translator_note:
Rashi’s printed references slip: “Micah 7” is 6:16 (“For the statutes of Omri are kept”); “1 Samuel 1” is 1:14 (“How long wilt thou be drunken?”); “Job 30” is 30:16 (“my soul is poured out within me”). *Va-yishtomem* appears at Isaiah 59:16; the printed “Isaiah 29” is not matched.
u|The reference for *va-yishtomem* is identified by the word, not by Rashi’s printed chapter.

Isaiah.english_translation: The family of Jacob, weak as a worm, which has no strength except in its mouth. *Worm* (*vermener*, printed וירמונ״א) in the foreign tongue (Old French).
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *vermener* / *vermine* (Darmesteter: “Vermisseau”) is confirmed.

Isaiah.english_translation: The number of Israel.

A wooden implement, heavy, made with notches upon notches like the iron smiths’ tool called *lime* in the foreign tongue (Old French); it is dragged over the stalks of the ears and cuts them until they become fine straw.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *lime* (“file”) is confirmed in Darmesteter.

Isaiah.english_translation: While it is new, before the mouths of its notches have been smoothed, it cuts much; but once it has aged, the mouths of its notches have been smoothed.
These are the sharp edges of the notches.
Kings and princes.
Thou shalt scatter them as with a winnowing-fan to the wind.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the wind shall carry them away
Isaiah.english_translation: Of themselves, to Gehinnom.

The prophet prophesied about the end of days: “Not a famine for bread, nor a thirst for water, but to hear the word of the LORD” (Amos 8:11); they shall wander to seek the word of the LORD and shall not find it. And when His anger turns back, He will prepare bread and water for them, and cause His Divine Presence and spirit to dwell in the mouths of their prophets.
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s wording of Amos 8:11–12 is a paraphrase, not the verse word for word; JPS reads “not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but of hearing the words of the LORD.”

Isaiah.english_translation: *Nishtat* is an expression of “and the waters shall fail (*nishtu*) from the sea” (above, 19 [19:5]); an expression of “desolation and destruction” (*ha-sha’et ve-ha-sheber*, Lamentations 3:47); and all are expressions of ruin and dryness. Therefore the *tav* has a dagesh, for it stands in place of two [letters]; for there is no *sha’et* without a *tav*. And it should have said, for the feminine, *nishtatah*; for in the masculine singular one says *nashetah* (?) and in the plural *nashetu*.
Isaiah.translator_note: The grammatical remark at the end is compressed in the printed text (and the form *nashetah* as printed is uncertain); rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_translation: A heart that understands Torah and prophecy.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the wilderness a pool of water
Isaiah.english_translation: A place where there was no wisdom of Torah.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: in the wilderness the cedar, the acacia-tree
Isaiah.english_translation: All kinds of settlement; so too I will give in them all kinds of wisdom and goodness and peace.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the cypress, the plane-tree, and the larch
Isaiah.english_translation: Names of barren trees, made for building.
All the idolaters: come, and contend and dispute with My children.
Your strong and firm claims; and this is an expression of contention in the language of the Mishnah: two who were contending (*mit‘atzmin*) in judgment, in tractate Sanhedrin.
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi gives no exact Mishnah reference; the printed text only says “in tractate Sanhedrin.”

Isaiah.english_translation: The idolaters, their prophets and their diviners.
That which will befall in the future.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The former things, what are they?
Isaiah.english_translation: Which were before the creation of the world, and for what was it created? What are they? (Another version: events that have already begun — what will be their end.)

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Or announce to us things to come
Isaiah.english_translation: Let him tell us what is to come, and we shall see whether there is substance in them, that their words will be fulfilled.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Declare the things that are to come hereafter
Isaiah.english_translation: “Declare the letters backward” — the wonders that come at the end.
Isaiah.translator_note: The printed lemma reads *ha-otiyyot* (“the letters”), which looks like a scribal slip for the word of the verse; rendered as printed.

Isaiah.english_translation: “*Ve-nishta‘eh*” — and we shall tell their words; “*vayesaper*” we translate (in the Targum) *ve-ishta‘i*.
And your words — how will they be fulfilled?

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: your work a thing of nought
Isaiah.english_translation: You are nothing but criers (*po‘im*), raising a voice to mislead with words of falsehood.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: An abomination is he that chooseth you
Isaiah.english_translation: The abominable ones choose you — and not the Holy One, blessed be He, nor His servants nor His ministers.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I have roused up one from the north, and he is come
Isaiah.english_translation: I who declare the things to come: behold I rouse Cyrus from the north to rebuild the ruins of Jerusalem, “and he is come” to Babylon to destroy it.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: From the rising of the sun one that calleth upon My name
Isaiah.english_translation: “All the kingdoms of the earth hath the LORD, the God of heaven, given me” (Ezra 1:2). And it appears that the land of Persia is north-east of the Land of Israel.
