Another explanation: “I have roused from the north” Nebuchadnezzar, to destroy My city, “and he is come”; and Cyrus I roused from the east, that he should call upon My name to build My city, for the kingdom of Persia is east of the Land of Israel, as it is said, “I saw the ram” etc. (Daniel 8:4). And Targum Jonathan: “I have brought openly a king who is strong, from the north wind, and he shall come like the rising of the sun in his might; from the province I have strengthened him in My name.”
Isaiah.translator_note: The Targum quotation is compressed and partly obscure (*bega‘lai*, *agbarinei*); rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And he shall come upon rulers as upon mortar
Isaiah.english_translation: And he shall come against the king of Babylon and his officers as one comes to tread upon mortar, and like a potter who treads clay for earthen vessels, so shall he tread rulers.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Who hath declared from the beginning, that we may know?
Isaiah.english_translation: Which of the prophets of the Baal declared, as I did, a thing of the future to come? And who of old declared it, so that when it comes we may say that he is righteous, whose prophecy is right?
But there is none among you who declares future things and it is fulfilled.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: there is none that heareth your utterances
Isaiah.english_translation: Who testifies, when the future event comes: “So-and-so the prophet of the Baal prophesied it beforehand.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: A harbinger unto Zion will I give
Isaiah.english_translation: A first king who will give heart to Zion: “Behold, this is what I said.” And although the redemption will not be completed through him, he will be the one to begin — “Whosoever there is among you of all His people” (Ezra 1:3).
The elders of Israel will be ready at his word to go up from the exile and to begin.
In those days, Haggai and Zechariah, who will stir them to build, in the days of Darius the third of Persia.
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s “Darius the third of Persia” is rendered as printed.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And I look, but there is no man
Isaiah.english_translation: Continually I look at the prophets of the Baal, and there is no man who declares a future thing.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Even among them, but there is no counsellor
Isaiah.english_translation: Of all these things that are to come, there is none among them who is a counsellor who stood in the council of the LORD and knew them.
Isaiah.translator_note: The printed text reads *be-sof* (“in the end of”) the LORD; *be-sod* (“in the council of”) seems intended, and the translation follows that sense.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: when I ask of them, can give an answer
Isaiah.english_translation: Who will return a word if I ask them.
You have to know that all the prophets who deny the Torah are vanity and nought: all their works, their libations.
Isaiah.translator_note: The Hebrew (*mekhaḥashei Torah*) is rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Their molten images are wind and confusion
Isaiah.english_translation: “Their molten images” — like “the image, the craftsman hath cast it” (above, 40:19). And Targum Jonathan renders in another sense: “A harbinger unto Zion” etc. — “The words of consolation which the prophets prophesied of old concerning Zion — behold, they have come.” And according to the Targum the whole matter speaks of the King Messiah and the final redemption. But I see a prophecy that Isaiah prophesied about Cyrus, all of it in the language of the style of this section: “I the LORD have roused him up in victory” (45:13); “calling a ravenous bird from the east” (46:11); “the things to come (printed *ha-otiyyot*) — ask Me” (45:11); “declaring the end from the beginning” (46:10) — the whole inclines toward the subject of this section.
Isaiah.translator_note:
Rashi’s four quotations are, in order, Isaiah 45:13, 46:11, 45:11 and 46:10; he gives no references.
u|The word printed *ha-otiyyot* (“the letters”) appears to stand for *ha-ottiyyot* / *ha-’ototot* (“the things to come,” Isaiah 45:11); rendered by the sense of that verse.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Behold My servant, whom I uphold
Isaiah.english_translation: “Behold My servant” — Jacob, who is not like you; for I uphold him.
Israel is called “Mine elect”: “For the LORD hath chosen Jacob unto Himself” (Psalm 135:4); and it says (below, 45) “For the sake of Jacob My servant, and Israel Mine elect” (45:4).

Upon him I have put My spirit, to make known to his prophets His secret and the end. “He shall make the right to go forth to the nations,” as it is said (above, 2), “And many peoples shall go” etc., “and He will teach us of His ways” etc. (2:3).

He shall not lift up his voice. He will not need to rebuke and to prophesy to the nations, for of themselves they will come to learn from them, as it is said (Zechariah 8:23), “We will go with you, for we have heard that God is with you.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: A bruised reed shall he not break
Isaiah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “The afflicted, who are like a bruised reed, shall not be broken; and the darkened, who are like a dim wick (i.e., a lamp gone out), shall not be quenched.”
Isaiah.translator_note: The Aramaic *ʿami* and *yetafun* are rendered by their likely sense; Rashi’s own gloss is “a lamp gone out.”

Isaiah.english_translation: A moist flax wick, close to going out: their king shall not rob the poor, nor crush the needy and the weak.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: He shall not fail nor be crushed
Isaiah.english_translation: Like *lo yeratsets* (“shall not be crushed”), for the earth shall be full of knowledge (above, 11 [11:9]), and they will listen to them, as it is said (Zephaniah 3:9), “For then will I turn to the peoples” etc. And that is “and the isles shall wait for his teaching” — all will hear His Torah.
Master of judgment and master of mercies.
At first like a skein of the warp, and afterward He stretched them out, as it is set forth in tractate Hagigah.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: that which cometh out of it
Isaiah.english_translation: He creates that which comes out of it.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: He that giveth breath unto the people
Isaiah.english_translation: The breath of life.
To all of them equally.
Holiness.
Those who walk before Him.
He says it to Isaiah.
When I formed thee, this was My thought: that thou shouldst set My people for My covenant, and give them light.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For a light of the nations
Isaiah.english_translation: Every tribe is called a nation by itself, as it is said, “A nation and a company of nations” (Genesis 35:11).
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi gives no reference; the quotation is Genesis 35:11.

Isaiah.english_translation: Who do not see His might, so as to set their heart to return to Me.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: To bring out the prisoners from the dungeon
Isaiah.english_translation: And through their eyes being opened, prisoners will go out of the dungeon. Another explanation: to announce to them the exile of Babylon that is destined to come upon them, that their end is to go out from it.
“He” is expressed in the language of lordship and power; and it rests upon Me to show that I am Lord; therefore, “My glory will I not give to another.”
Which I promised Abraham concerning the exile in Egypt (Genesis 15): “and also that nation,” etc.
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s printed reference “Genesis 15” is 15:14.

Isaiah.english_translation: I kept My promise; and now I declare new things to My people, to assure them concerning the second exile.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: His praise from the end of the earth
Isaiah.english_translation: Against their will: when they see My might toward Israel, all the idolaters will acknowledge that I am God.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: You that go down to the sea
Isaiah.english_translation: Those who spread sail in ships.

Those who are settled in the sea, and not on islands but in the midst of the water: they pour earth, each one the size of a house, and go from house to house by ship — as the city of Venice (*Venise*).
Isaiah.translator_note: The city is named in the printed text as Venice (*Venise*); rendered as printed.

Isaiah.english_translation: A voice in song.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The villages that Kedar doth inhabit
Isaiah.english_translation: (It refers back to “lift up.”) The wilderness of Kedar, who now dwell in tents, shall lift up a voice and sing (like “and the villages that Kedar doth inhabit”); in the wilderness of Kedar, who now dwell in their tents, there will be settled cities and villages.
Isaiah.translator_note: The parenthesis and the second half are compressed in the printed text; rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Let the inhabitants of Sela exult
Isaiah.english_translation: The dead who will live again — so Targum Jonathan.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: from the top of the mountains
Isaiah.english_translation: Targum: “From the top of the mountains they shall raise their voices.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I have long time held My peace
Isaiah.english_translation: For many days I have held My peace over the destruction of My House, and continually I shall be silent.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I have been still, and refrained Myself
Isaiah.english_translation: An expression of the present: until now My spirit has distressed Me, but from now on I will cry out like a woman in travail.
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s *le-shon hoveh* is rendered “an expression of the present”; the rest is rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_translation: I will be alarmed.
And I will long to destroy all together all My enemies.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I will make waste mountains and hills
Isaiah.english_translation: I will slay kings and rulers of the idolaters.
All who are joined to them.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And dry up all their herbs
Isaiah.english_translation: An expression of dryness, said of a moist thing, such as herbage and rivers.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I will bring the blind by a way that they knew not
Isaiah.english_translation: Israel, who until now were blind to looking to Me, in the good way which they did not know to walk in.
“I will do so” — an expression of prophecy, speaking of the future as though it were done.
And “the blind” — He speaks of Israel.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Who is blind, but My servant?
Isaiah.english_translation: Among you there is no one [blind] except My servant — he is the blindest of all of you; and the deaf one among you, behold, he is like My messenger whom I send to prophesy prophecies.
Isaiah.translator_note: The sense is compressed; rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: blind as he that is wholehearted
Isaiah.english_translation: Who among you was blind has already received his sufferings, and behold he is like one who has been paid all his recompense, and he goes out clean.
Many sights are before you, and you do not take heed to look at My works and return to Me.
I am busy opening your ears through My prophets, and no man among you hears My words; and it is an expression of the present.
To show you and to open your ears, for the sake of righteousness; and therefore He magnifies and glorifies the Torah for you.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: But this is a people robbed and spoiled
Isaiah.english_translation: This people is despised and plundered; and the end of the matter: “and none layeth it to heart” — they do not set all this to heart, to say, “Why hast Thou called us this?” “Who gave Jacob for a spoil?”
Isaiah.translator_note: “And the end of the matter” is printed so; the quotation is compressed.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: They are all of them snared in holes
Isaiah.english_translation: “In their holes are snares of the soul, all of them” (Targum). Another explanation: “The snare in holes, all of them” — they will put themselves in the traps of the earth and in holes; and “in prison-houses they are hid” proves that it is so.
Isaiah.translator_note: The abbreviation תו׳ is not expanded in the printed text; it most likely means the Targum. Rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_translation: Like *hashev* [imperative], therefore it is soft (*rafeh*); but *hashev* in “returned in our sacks” (Genesis 43:18) has a dagesh.
Isaiah.translator_note: The grammatical remark is compressed; the reference “returned in our sacks” is Genesis 43:18 (“the money that was returned in our sacks”).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Who among you will give ear to this?
Isaiah.english_translation: To set heart to this: “Who gave Jacob for a spoil?”
He will listen and hear a matter that will stand him in good stead at the end; and so Targum Jonathan: “for the end”; and so every *le-ahor* in Scripture means it is to be in the future.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: He against whom we have sinned
Isaiah.english_translation: This is what brought about the spoil and the plunder — Him against whom we have sinned.
Our fathers, to walk in His ways.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: it set him on fire round about
Isaiah.english_translation: So that they would see and take reproof, as it is said (Zephaniah 3:6), “I have cut off nations, their corners are desolate … I said: Surely thou wilt fear Me,” etc.
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s printed reference “3 6” is Zephaniah 3:6–7.

Isaiah.english_translation: He knows, but he treads upon the heel — he is not careful to understand this and to return from his wickedness.
Isaiah.translator_note: *Dash ba-‘akev* (“treads upon the heel”) is rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_translation: After the punishment of the idolaters round about, it burned in himself.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: But now thus saith the LORD
Isaiah.english_translation: Even all this: “thus saith the LORD, Fear not.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: When thou passest through the waters
Isaiah.english_translation: When thou didst pass through the Red Sea, I was with thee.
Thou didst sojourn among the Egyptians and the nations, who were as many as the waters of a river, and they were not able to destroy thee.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: When thou walkest through the fire
Isaiah.english_translation: In the time to come: “For, behold, the day cometh, it burneth as a furnace” (Malachi 3:19), when I make My wrath hot upon the wicked; “and the day that cometh shall set them ablaze” (there); “there too thou shalt not be burned.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Neither shall the flame kindle upon thee
Isaiah.english_translation: That will burn the nations, as it is said, “And the peoples shall be as the burnings of lime” (Isaiah 33:12); that too shall not burn thee.
Isaiah.translator_note:
Rashi’s printed text has *mis’refot sir* (“burnings of a pot”); the verse (Isaiah 33:12) reads *mis’refot sid* (“burnings of lime”).
u|Rendered by the sense of the verse.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I have given Egypt as thy ransom
Isaiah.english_translation: And they were thy ransom, for their firstborn died while thou, My firstborn son, wast saved; and ye were liable to destruction, as it is said (Ezekiel 20:8), “Then I said I would pour out My fury upon them … in the midst of the land of Egypt.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: will I give men for thee
Isaiah.english_translation: Constantly I am accustomed to this.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I will say to the north
Isaiah.english_translation: To the north wind: give up the exiles who are in the north.

Which is a strong wind: do not hold back from blowing strongly to bring My exiles; and so (Song of Songs 4:16), “Awake, O north wind, and come, thou south.” Since the north wind is weak, it needs strengthening; therefore it is written “awake,” “give up.” But the south wind, which does not need strengthening, [only] “come” is written, as it is; and so “keep not back.”
Isaiah.translator_note: That the north wind is “weak” and the south “strong” is Rashi’s statement as printed.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Every one that is called by My name
Isaiah.english_translation: All the righteous who are called by My name, and everything made for My glory — I have formed him; yea, I have made him: I have prepared him with everything he needs, and I prepared everything. That is: although they have passed through exile and distress, I have already prepared for them all the needs of their redemption.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The blind people that have eyes shall be brought forth
Isaiah.english_translation: “Bring forth” — to bring out of exile those who were exiled because they became as blind, although they had eyes, and did not see.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: All the nations are gathered together
Isaiah.english_translation: If all the nations of the idolaters have gathered together, who among them and among their prophets can declare future things and the like, out of their error; or “the former things” that have already passed, let them make us hear, saying: “We declared them before they came.”

Who heard that these [things] were prophesied about them before, and so they may be justified. But I have witnesses: you are My witnesses, that I declared the exiles to Abraham your father, and they came.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And My servant whom I have chosen
Isaiah.english_translation: Jacob.
He will testify that I promised him when he went to Aram-naharaim, and I kept My promise.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: That you may know and believe Me
Isaiah.english_translation: All this I did so that you would set your heart to know Me.
The exiles — to Abraham.
To fulfil My word at the time of *ratz*.
Isaiah.translator_note: The printed text reads *be-‘et ratz* (“at the time of running”); possibly *ratzon* (“favour”) is meant. Rendered as printed.

Isaiah.english_translation: To you, the former things.
In those days when I did all these things, no strange god was seen among you all, among the idolaters, to show his greatness and his divinity before Me.
That I opened for you the seven heavens, and you saw no image.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: since the day was I am He
Isaiah.english_translation: Not only that day was I alone, for also since the day was I am He, alone.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I will work, and who can reverse it?
Isaiah.english_translation: If I come to work, there is none who can turn it back.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For your sake I have sent to Babylon
Isaiah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “For the sake of your sins I have exiled you to Babylon.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I will bring down all of them as fugitives
Isaiah.english_translation: “And I brought them down in oars (*meshotin*), all of them”; *meshotin* is the wood that steers the ship and keeps it straight.

They led you in the ships of their shouting. And one may also explain it as the tidings of redemption: “For your sake I have sent” — I will send the kings of Media to Babylon, and bring down the Chaldeans in ships and oars into exile to the land of Media; and the Chaldeans I will bring down in the ships in which was their shouting.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: who maketh a way in the sea
Isaiah.english_translation: At the Red Sea, and there I brought out Egypt to pursue after you — chariot and horse, army and power — and all of them together lie dead on the shore of the sea, not to rise.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: they are quenched as a wick
Isaiah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan translated: “Like a dim wick they are extinguished.”
Isaiah.translator_note: The Aramaic (*ke-butza ‘ami tafu*) is rendered by its likely sense.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Remember you not the former things
Isaiah.english_translation: These miracles that I mention to you, which I did in Egypt — do not remember them from now on, for in this redemption you shall be occupied with giving thanks and praise.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Neither consider the things of old
Isaiah.english_translation: Do not look at them; do not set your heart to them.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The beasts of the field shall honour Me
Isaiah.english_translation: A place that is ruined and a lair for the beasts of the field, for jackals and for the daughters of the ostrich.
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s gloss on “shall honour Me” is rendered literally; it describes the place rather than the verb.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Because I give waters in the wilderness
Isaiah.english_translation: That is: in a ruined land I will give habitation.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: That they might tell of My praise
Isaiah.english_translation: For My praise they shall recount.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Yet thou hast not called upon Me
Isaiah.english_translation: And thou — not Me didst thou call, when thou turnedst after idolaters.
You quickly grew weary in My service.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Thou hast not brought Me the small cattle of thy burnt-offerings
Isaiah.english_translation: But [only] to idolatry.
Isaiah.translator_note: The abbreviation כ״א is read here as *ki im* (“but”); the printed text does not expand it, and *la-ʿakum* is rendered “to idolatry.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I have not burdened thee with a meal-offering
Isaiah.english_translation: Is it great service? In the meal-offering, a handful, a little, goes up to the Most High; and even that I did not tell thee to offer as an obligation but as a freewill offering.
Isaiah.translator_note: The opening is compressed in the printed text; it is read as a rhetorical question.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Thou hast bought Me no sweet cane with money
Isaiah.english_translation: For the incense thou didst not need to buy it with money, since it was found plentifully in your land. Rabbi Abba said: cinnamon grew in the Land of Israel, and goats and gazelles used to eat it — in the Midrash on Lamentations.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: thou hast burdened Me with thy sins
Isaiah.english_translation: You caused Me to be a servant to worshippers of idols, as Ezekiel saw: “And behold, a stormy wind came out of the north” (Ezekiel 1:4) — that was the Chariot of the Divine Presence returning from Babylon, which had gone to conquer the whole world under the hand of Nebuchadnezzar, so that they should not say that He delivered His children into the hand of a lowly nation, as it is set forth in tractate Hagigah.
Isaiah.translator_note: The sentence about the Chariot is compressed in the printed text; rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I, even I, am He that blotteth out thy transgressions
Isaiah.english_translation: I am He who blotted them out from of old, and I blot them out even now.
Not for thy merit and not for the righteousness of thy fathers.
Any recompense that thou and thy fathers have against Me.
Let us come to judgment.
Isaiah.translator_note: The printed text reads *nava* (without the *vav*); read as “let us come.”

Isaiah.english_translation: In his saying, “Whereby shall I know?” (Genesis 15).
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s printed reference “Genesis 15” is 15:8.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: thine intercessors have transgressed against Me
Isaiah.english_translation: Among all the intercessors on whose merit thou dost rely there is none in whom I did not find transgression: Isaac loved My hater.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Therefore I have profaned the princes of the sanctuary
Isaiah.english_translation: Because of your iniquities.
To return to My Torah, Jacob My servant.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For I will pour water upon the thirsty land
Isaiah.english_translation: As I pour water upon the thirsty, so will I pour My spirit upon thy seed.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And they shall spring up among the grass
Isaiah.english_translation: Among Amalek, through the proselytes who will be added to them. “Among the grass” — it is Amalek, of whom it is said, “And it shall be a habitation of wild-dogs, an enclosure (*ḥatzir*) for ostriches” (above, 34).
Isaiah.translator_note:
Rashi’s printed reference “above, 4” is Isaiah 34:13.
u|The printed text reads “Amalek” here; it is rendered as printed.

Isaiah.english_translation: These are the completely righteous.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: shall call himself by the name of Jacob
Isaiah.english_translation: These are the minors, the children of the wicked.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: shall subscribe with his hand unto the LORD
Isaiah.english_translation: These are the penitents.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: surname himself by the name of Israel
Isaiah.english_translation: These are the proselytes from among the idolaters. So it is taught in Avot de-Rabbi Natan.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And who, as I, can proclaim
Isaiah.english_translation: And who can proclaim that he is like Me, and declare and set in order for Me all that has been since I appointed the people of old until now?
All creatures.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And the things that are coming
Isaiah.english_translation: Words of wonder (*mofet*).
Isaiah.translator_note: The printed text reads *ve-otiyyot* (“and letters”), for the verse’s *ve-ottiyyot*; rendered by the sense.

Isaiah.english_translation: And let them declare the things destined to come, as I do now, when the House has not yet been destroyed, nor have you gone into exile, nor has Cyrus been born, and I announce him to you.
It has no parallel, and its interpretation according to the context is like *al tehatu*: do not be afraid to make My name known among the idolaters.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Have I not announced unto thee of old, and declared it?
Isaiah.english_translation: From Mount Sinai, and I declared to you there that there is no god beside Me.
That I opened for you the seven heavens and showed you that there is no other; and you are witnesses in this matter, that there is no God beside Me.
Targum Jonathan: “And there is none strong, except one to whom strength is given from before Me.”
An expression like “and I know thee by name” (Exodus 33:17); “He hath known thy walking” (Deuteronomy 2:7); “I did know thee in the wilderness” (Hosea 13:5).
The idols are witnesses to the shame of those who worship them; for we see that they neither see nor know, and yet they worship them.
Those who worship them.
An expression of pouring and casting; and the *nun* in the word is a root letter that falls away from it, such as the *nun* of *nashakh* and of *nagaf*.
Isaiah.translator_note: The grammatical remark is compressed; rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Behold, all the fellows thereof shall be ashamed
Isaiah.english_translation: Of that moulder and caster of idols: those who are joined with him to serve his creation and his casting will be ashamed.
Those moulders and casters are of men — all the more so is their creation, which is vanity.
A smith of iron.
It is one of the smiths’ tools.
The carver works with charcoal. *Charbon* in the foreign tongue (Old French).
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *charbon* is confirmed in Darmesteter (“Charbon”).

Isaiah.english_translation: *Martel* in the foreign tongue (Old French).
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *martel* (“marteau”) is confirmed in Darmesteter.

Isaiah.english_translation: An expression of shaping.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: worketh it with his strong arm
Isaiah.english_translation: Even he, the maker, lacks strength and is weak; for if he grows hungry he has no strength, or if he has not drunk water he immediately faints. All the more so, his work has no use to help.
And if he comes to make it of wood, “a carpenter” — this is his way.

As is the way of the carpenters; and by the line he shapes it with a *sered*, straightens it with a *masor*, which is called *doloire* in the foreign tongue (Old French). *Yetaarehu*: he makes it beautiful.
Isaiah.translator_note:
Old French *doloire* (an adze or broad axe) is confirmed in Darmesteter.
u|*Sered* and *masor* are left untranslated; *masor* is not rendered “saw” because the Old French gloss names a different tool.

Isaiah.english_translation: And he smooths it with a *rehitni* and a chisel; *mikzo‘ot* — Targum: *izmeliya* (chisels).
Isaiah.translator_note: *Rehitni* is left untranslated.

Isaiah.english_translation: An expression of “and the border was drawn” (Joshua 15:9). If he comes to make round figures in it, he goes round it with the compasses, *compas* in the foreign tongue (Old French).
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *compas* is confirmed in Darmesteter (printed קונפ״ש).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: According to the beauty of a man
Isaiah.english_translation: That is the woman, who is the beauty of her husband.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: taketh the ilex and the oak
Isaiah.english_translation: Kinds of barren trees.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: strengtheneth for himself one among the trees of the forest
Isaiah.english_translation: He makes supports for himself, whether for support or for ornament, from kinds of trees that differ from one another in appearance.
When he finds a shoot and a planting suited to it, he plants it for that, and the rain makes it grow.
An expression of a sucker-plant, *plançon* in the foreign tongue (Old French).
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *plançon* is confirmed in Darmesteter (who glosses it “Une racine”).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Then a man useth it for fuel
Isaiah.english_translation: And part of that tree is for the needs of man, for burning.
From the trees; and he warms his body before them.
From them, an oven; and he bakes bread.
Isaiah.translator_note: The printed text is fragmentary; rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Yea, he maketh a god, and worshippeth it
Isaiah.english_translation: From the remainder.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And none considereth in his heart
Isaiah.english_translation: [He does not say:] “Half of it I burned in the fire.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Neither is there knowledge nor understanding
Isaiah.english_translation: In him, to say this.
The rot of wood.

His heart, which was deceived, turned him aside to make for himself a shepherd of ash: the image, half of which was burned and became ash. This fool used to say that it was for him a shepherd and provider. Another explanation: *ro‘eh efer* is an expression of companionship (*re‘ut*): he worships the worship of others, and joins to himself the worship of others, which is ash.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: That he cannot deliver his soul
Isaiah.english_translation: He who leads his soul astray, to say, “Is there not a lie in my right hand?”, and be separated from it.
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s sentence is compressed; rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_translation: Thou shalt not be forgetful of My fear.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I have blotted out, as a thick cloud, thy transgressions
Isaiah.english_translation: In Egypt and in the wilderness; and even now, return to Me.
An expression of opening of the mouth.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: He that formed thee from the womb
Isaiah.english_translation: From the time that “the children struggled together within her” (Genesis 25:22), I was a help to thee, and I chose thee.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: That stretched forth the heavens alone
Isaiah.english_translation: The heavens, alone.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: That frustrateth the tokens of the imposters
Isaiah.english_translation: Since I stretched out the heavens, therefore I am able to frustrate them.

Those who gaze at the stars by the signs of the heavens; and because many times they lie, they are called *baddim* (“liars”), for I change the princes above and those who are consulted by them err. And since the astrologers of Babylon used to gaze at the stars, as it says (below, 47 [47:13]), “Let them stand now and save thee, the dividers of the heavens,” therefore He says that He frustrates the signs of their *baddim*; for I am He who frustrated the signs of the *baddim* of Egypt.
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s wording of Isaiah 47:13 is shortened; JPS reads “Let now the astrologers, the stargazers … stand up, and save thee.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: That confirmeth the word of His servant
Isaiah.english_translation: Moses.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And performeth the counsel of His messengers
Isaiah.english_translation: An angel said to Jacob, “Israel shall be thy name” (Genesis 32); and I fulfilled his words; so too here I will fulfil the counsel of My prophets, who said of Jerusalem, “She shall be inhabited.”
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s printed reference “Genesis 32” points to 32:29 (the angel’s words, “Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel”); the wording “Israel shall be thy name” is in Genesis 35:10.

Isaiah.english_translation: He who says to Babylon: Be dry.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I will dry up thy rivers
Isaiah.english_translation: Because she sits upon rivers, he likens the slaying of her multitude to the drying up of rivers.
My king.

Every name of greatness is called anointing, as “unto thee have I given them for a consecrated portion” (*le-mashḥah*) (Numbers 18:8); and our Rabbis said: to the King Messiah the Holy One, blessed be He, says, “I have a complaint to make to thee about Cyrus,” as it is set forth in tractate Megillah.
To flatten and to beat down nations before him; *lārēd* means to spread out.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And to loose the loins of kings
Isaiah.english_translation: This is an expression of weakness and the breaking of strength; for the girding of the loins is the rousing of strength, as “Gird up thy loins now like a man” (Job 40:7), “Thou therefore gird up thy loins” (Jeremiah 1:17), and “looseth the belt of the strong” (Job 12:21) — an expression of the breaking of strength.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: To open the doors before him
Isaiah.english_translation: The doors of the gates of Babylon. *She‘arim* is the hollow of the opening of the gate; *delatayim* are the leaves with which they open and close the gate.

Targum: “and the walls I will subdue,” like *hadar hadrana* (?), because the wall surrounds the city. And it is possible to explain *ha-hadurim* as crooked roads: I will make them straight before him.
Isaiah.translator_note: The comparison “like *hadar hadrana*” is printed so and is not clear; rendered literally. The Targum’s Aramaic *shuraya* means “walls.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Who call thee by thy name
Isaiah.english_translation: Thou wast not yet born, and I call thee by the name Cyrus.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For the sake of Jacob My servant
Isaiah.english_translation: That thou shouldst bring him out of the exile of Babylon.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: though thou hast not known Me
Isaiah.english_translation: Thou didst not do My will; for I said, “He shall build My city”; and he, when he arose, said, “Whosoever there is among you of all His people” (Ezra 1:3) — he gave them permission to go, and he shook all the toil off his neck.
For the righteous.
For Babylon; and so “I make peace and create evil.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Drop down, you heavens, from above
Isaiah.english_translation: The “righteousness” mentioned in the verse refers both to the pouring and to the dropping: “Drop down, you heavens, righteousness” and “let the skies pour down righteousness” — that is, from Me righteousness will come, to do them good from heaven.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I the LORD have created it
Isaiah.english_translation: I created this thing.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Woe unto him that striveth with his Maker
Isaiah.english_translation: Isaiah prophesied about Habakkuk, who was destined to arise and make a complaint about the long prosperity of Nebuchadnezzar: “O LORD, how long shall I cry” etc. (Habakkuk 1:2) “and makest men as the fishes of the sea” (1:14). And the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Isaiah: Why does this one come to quarrel with Me? He thinks that I do not set My heart to save My people, until the time is fulfilled the time when the land has paid her sabbaths (Leviticus 26:34).
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s printed reference (Habakkuk 1:2) covers the first quotation; “and makest men as the fishes of the sea” is Habakkuk 1:14.

Isaiah.english_translation: He has no place.
Isaiah.translator_note: *Ein makom lo* is rendered literally; the sense (“he has no room to answer”) is not stated by Rashi.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Woe unto him that saith unto his father
Isaiah.english_translation: He thinks that he is more merciful to the son than his father. Another explanation: Woe to the son who says to his father, “Why didst thou beget?” — he is like this one who strives with his Maker.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Ask Me of the things that are to come
Isaiah.english_translation: The *he* is pointed with a *kamatz*; thou learnest that it is not a question of astonishment; and so they explained: If you have come to ask Me — you prophets — ask Me about the signs of heaven and the wonders which you see born in the earth: about them you used to ask Me what they are. But about My sons and about the work of My hands, the upright, for whose sake I created everything, you come to command Me and to raise a complaint before Me?
Isaiah.translator_note: The printed lemma reads *ha-otiyyot* (“the letters”) for the verse’s *ha-ottiyyot* (“the things to come”); the grammatical remark is rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_translation: It is astonishing: is it for you to command about My sons? I have already created for them the deliverance in the thought that arose before Me. How? “I have roused him up in victory” (45:13) — He speaks of Cyrus.
And I gave it to whom it seemed right in My eyes.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The labour of Egypt, and the merchandise of Ethiopia
Isaiah.english_translation: Behold, I have made known to you by what means I will save My sons from the hand of Babylon, for it is for this that I roused Cyrus in My righteousness. And further I make known to you the deliverance from Sennacherib in the days of Hezekiah: when he returned (above, 37) from Tirhakah king of Cush and came to Jerusalem — and the coveted treasures of all Cush and Egypt, who went to help Cush, in his hand — and he would come with that spoil and fall at Jerusalem, and Hezekiah and his people would plunder everything. So it is explained in Seder Olam, that it was said of Sennacherib.
Isaiah.translator_note:
Rashi’s printed reference “above, 37” points to Isaiah 37:9 (Tirhakah king of Ethiopia).
u|The sentence about the treasures of Cush and Egypt is compressed in the printed text; rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_translation: Men tall of stature.
[Unto thee] — Jerusalem.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: in chains they shall come over
Isaiah.english_translation: For Sennacherib had brought them there, led away in neck-irons; and after his fall Hezekiah arose and released all the captives, and they became proselytes and acknowledged the kingdom of Heaven.
Isaiah.translator_note: *Shelulim ba-kolarim* is rendered “led away in neck-irons.”

Isaiah.english_translation: They will acknowledge that there is no God but the LORD alone.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Verily Thou art a God that hidest Thyself
Isaiah.english_translation: And so they will say to the Holy One, blessed be He: Verily we have understood that, in order to collect the debts of Thy people, Thou dost hide Thyself from showing Thy victory — as it were, there is no power in Thee; and when Thy mercies are roused, Thou art the God of Israel, the Saviour. So it is explained in the Mekhilta.
Craftsmen of the figures of the idols of the idolaters and of the constellations.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: He created it not a waste
Isaiah.english_translation: For to be inhabited He formed it.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I have not spoken in secret
Isaiah.english_translation: When I gave the Torah; and I did not say to the seed of Jacob, “Seek Me” for nothing, in vain, but in order to receive a great reward.

Since I opened with them with a word of My righteousness, to make known to them the giving of their reward, afterwards I declared to them upright things — My statutes and My Torah; for before the giving of the Torah it was said to them (Exodus 11 [printed]), “And now, if you will hearken” etc., “and you shall be unto Me a kingdom of priests” etc.
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s printed reference “Exodus 11” is Exodus 19:5–6.

Isaiah.english_translation: An expression of drawing near (*hagashah*), and the *nun* is an accessory letter in it, as when one says *hitnagfu*.
Isaiah.translator_note: The grammatical remark is rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: You that are escaped of the nations
Isaiah.english_translation: Who remained from the sword of Nebuchadnezzar.
To understand knowledge.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Who hath announced this from ancient time
Isaiah.english_translation: Which among your idols announced from of old that your god would bring deliverance, each to his own worshippers?
That I make known what I am going to do for My people, and I fulfil My word.
And leave your idols, all ends of the earth, and by this you shall be saved.

“And it went forth from My mouth in righteousness (*tzedakah*)” — to receive all who return to Me. “The word is gone forth … and shall not come back” — what is the righteousness that has gone forth from My mouth? That “unto Me every knee shall bow” — and I will receive them, as it is said, “For then will I turn to the peoples” etc. (Zephaniah 3:9).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Only in the LORD, shall one say of Me
Isaiah.english_translation: This verse is inverted, and thus is its interpretation: “Only to me, in the LORD, he said: righteousness and strength.” Although all the nations will bow down before Him, only to me, the Community of Israel, alone — in the LORD, righteousness and strength were promised to me; and those who deny the Torah will not come to profane My honour.
Isaiah.translator_note: The last clause is compressed in the printed text; rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Even to Him shall men come in confusion
Isaiah.english_translation: All who rage against the Holy One, blessed be He, will come to Him to repent of what they did in their lives, and will be ashamed.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: All they that were incensed against Him
Isaiah.english_translation: Those who provoke.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: In the LORD shall all the seed of Israel
Isaiah.english_translation: In the assurance of the support of His love they will find righteousness and will take pride in His strength.
*Porvanter* in the foreign tongue (Old French).
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *porvanter* (printed פרוונטי״ר; Darmesteter: “Ils seront fiers,” from *pro* + *vanilare*) is confirmed.

Isaiah.english_translation: The deities of Babylon bowed, stooped. It is an expression of ridicule of idolatry: like one who has a disease of the bowels and cannot manage to sit on the seat of the privy until he squats.
Isaiah.translator_note: The abbreviation בה״כ is read as *bet ha-kisse* (“privy”), and the verb *nitraz* as “squats”; Darmesteter’s gloss for this passage is “Ironie contre Bel et Nebo … comme si, pris de maux d’entrailles, ils s’accroupissaient jusqu’à l’épuisement de leurs corps.”

Isaiah.english_translation: *Acroupir* is Bel; *conchier* is Nebo (in the foreign tongue, Old French). So I heard in the name of our Rabbi Gershom, Light of the Exile.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *acroupir* (“to squat”) and *conchier* (“to befoul oneself”) are confirmed in Darmesteter, who translates “Bel s’est accroupi, Nebo s’est conchié.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Their idols are upon the beasts
Isaiah.english_translation: The images of the figures of Bel and Nebo were for the beast and the cattle — they were made like beast and cattle, who soil and befoul themselves with their dung.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: A burden to the weary beast
Isaiah.english_translation: The dung in their bowels is heavy to carry, like a burden for a weary man; therefore they stooped and bowed together — the stooping with the bowing.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: They could not deliver the burden
Isaiah.english_translation: To expel the excrement in their bowels as others do who excrete properly.

An expression of bringing out from a swallowing place; and so (above, 34 [34:15]) “There shall the arrow-snake make her nest, and lay” — she brought out her egg; and so (below, 66 [66:7]) “she was delivered of a man-child.” And Jonathan did not translate these verses so.

From when you were born in the house of Laban the Aramean I have carried you upon My arms; for since then idolaters have stood against you in every generation; and not like the idolaters who were loading and carrying their gods, as was said above; but you are loaded and borne on My arms.

Until you are old and your strength has failed, when you have no merit, I am He, in My mercy and in My attribute of goodness, to save you, and to bear and to carry and to deliver; for it was said of their fear [of idols] that it is borne, and moreover its burden it cannot deliver; He said: I, who bear others and their burden, will deliver.
Isaiah.translator_note: “Their fear” (*yirathem*) is printed; the sense is the idols’ worshippers’ dread of their gods. Rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_translation: Like “and I am become like (*va-etmashel*) dust and ashes” (Job 30:19) — an expression of likeness.
That I and he may be like one another.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: You that lavish gold out of the bag
Isaiah.english_translation: An expression of “the waters flow” (Psalm 147:18).
It is the beam of the scales, called *flael* in the foreign tongue (Old French).
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *flael* (“fléau,” from *flagellum*) is confirmed in Darmesteter.

Isaiah.english_translation: That which I desire to say.
And strengthen yourselves — like *le-ashishei Kir ḥareshet* (above, 16).
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi takes *ashishei* in Isaiah 16:7 as an expression of strength; JPS renders that verse “the sweet cakes of Kir-hareseth.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Bring it to mind, O you transgressors
Isaiah.english_translation: And what do I say to you? To remember and to bring it to mind.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Remember the former things of old
Isaiah.english_translation: Which you have seen — that I am God and there is none else; I am God, and there is none like Me.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Declaring the end from the beginning
Isaiah.english_translation: I made known the exile of Egypt and its redemption at the Covenant between the Pieces, before it came to be.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Calling a bird of prey from the east
Isaiah.english_translation: From the land of Aram, which is in the east, I called Abraham for Myself, to be consulted in My counsel. *Ayit* is like *hativ ‘ata* (Daniel 2:14), and the sense is that of *it‘ayatu kol sarkhei malkhuta* (“All the presidents of the kingdom have consulted together,” Daniel 6:8). And one may also explain it in the language of a bird: I called quickly after him, like a bird that flies and wanders from its place.
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s printed references “Daniel 2” and “there, 6” are Daniel 2:14 and 6:8.

Isaiah.english_translation: I called the man of My counsel, and with him I took counsel at the Covenant between the Pieces about four exiles, as is explained in Genesis Rabbah: “and, lo, a dread, even a great darkness, fell upon him” (Genesis 15:12), etc.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I have spoken, I will also bring it to pass
Isaiah.english_translation: With him, the exiles and their redemption; “I will also bring it.”
You who have strengthened your heart and cleaved to Me.
For whom the days have grown long, and I have not shown you My righteousness to redeem.
From now, and it shall not be far off.
No kingdom.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: thou shalt no more be called
Isaiah.english_translation: That they shall call thee again tender and delicate.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Take the millstones, and grind meal
Isaiah.english_translation: It is hard labour; that is: be enslaved henceforth to the kings of Media and Persia. Another explanation: “and grind flour” for provision for the road of thy exile.
Thine arms and thy shins — things that are bound up (*mezummat*), tied, and covered.
Uncover the paths from the water that is upon them, for by the way there thou shalt go out into exile; or: uncover thy leg and pass over the rivers.
I will not seek the face of any man in order to take My vengeance.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Our Redeemer, the LORD of hosts is His name
Isaiah.english_translation: The prophet says: all this the Holy One, blessed be He, does in order to redeem us from there.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Upon the aged hast thou very heavily
Isaiah.english_translation: Upon the old, who were not able to bear the toil, thou didst make thy yoke heavy.

In thy heart: “For ever shall I be mistress, and no punishment will come upon me”; and this thing led thee astray, so that thou didst not lay to thy heart these blows that will come upon thee, and didst not remember the end of the evil that thou hast done.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: thou that art given to pleasures
Isaiah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: *pankata*.
Isaiah.translator_note: The Aramaic word is left as printed.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: there is none else beside me
Isaiah.english_translation: “*Ve-afsi ‘od*” — *efes* beside me, like “there is none but me.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: But these two things shall come to thee in a moment
Isaiah.english_translation: That which thou saidst — that thou wouldst not sit as a widow nor know bereavement — shall come to thee suddenly.
From thy inhabitants.
From thy king. All burying of children and the exile of the people of the land is called *shekhol* (bereavement).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: In their full measure shall they come upon thee
Isaiah.english_translation: All of them complete in their decree of bereavement and widowhood.
An expression of sorcery, like “and a charmer of charms” (Deuteronomy 18).
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s printed reference “Deuteronomy 18” is 18:11 (“or a charmer”).

Isaiah.english_translation: Thy wisdom and the evil of thy heart — it has turned thee away; it turned thy heart to be *shovevah* (turned aside), *envoisiée* in the foreign tongue (Old French), [and drew] thee away from the way of the rest of the creatures.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *envoisiée* (printed אינווייז״א; Darmesteter: “T’ont séduite,” from *in* + *vitiata*) is confirmed.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Thou shalt not know how to harm it away
Isaiah.english_translation: Thou shalt not know how to seek [mercy] concerning it: before whom wilt thou plead to deliver thee from it?
Isaiah.translator_note: The first words are Aramaic in the printed text and the whole clause is compressed; rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Thou shalt not be able to put it away
Isaiah.english_translation: To wipe it away and remove it; and this is every use of *kapparah*: it is an expression of wiping and removal.
Strengthen thyself now.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: If so be thou mayest prevail
Isaiah.english_translation: Perhaps thou wilt be able to be strong.
Isaiah.translator_note: The printed gloss is Aramaic (Targum): rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Let now the astrologers, the stargazers
Isaiah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “like gazers of heaven, who look to the constellations of heaven …”; [and the word is] like “clear (*barah*) as the sun” (Song of Songs 6:10) and “sincerely (*barur*) they shall speak” (Job 33:3). And so Menahem joined them: those who make clear the course of the constellations. And this is its explanation: because the diviners cannot stand upon the knowledge of the moments of the day and the night until the heavens are clear and pure. And Micah also said in prophecy (Micah 3:6), “And it shall be dark unto you, that you shall not divine” — teaching that on a dark day the stars are sealed and they cannot divine.
Isaiah.translator_note:
Rashi’s Job 33:3 quotation (*u-lebarur millelu*) is JPS “that which my lips know they shall speak sincerely.”
u|The Aramaic words after “gazers of heaven” are garbled in the printed text and are rendered only by their likely sense.

Isaiah.english_translation: For at the renewal of the moon they see, at the hour of its birth, a part of what is destined to come, and they do not know the whole with certainty; therefore *me-asher* (“from that which”) is said. And so He says in another place (above, 8 [8:19]), “that chirp and that mutter” — like those birds that chirp and mutter and do not know about what.
Thy seers are like straw.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: It shall not be a coal to warm at
Isaiah.english_translation: There is no remnant for them, like this straw, in whose burning there are no coals to warm by their light.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Thus shall they be unto thee
Isaiah.english_translation: “They shall wander, every one to his own quarter” — each to his way, “toward the side of his face.”
Isaiah.translator_note: The verse as divided on the site ends before this phrase, so an in-verse phrase is used as the lemma; Rashi’s lemma *ish le-ever-o ta‘u* belongs to the continuation of 47:15.

Isaiah.english_translation: Two tribes that are destined to go into exile to Babylon.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Who are called by the name of Israel
Isaiah.english_translation: This is the tribe of Benjamin, who are not called after the tribe of Judah but by the plain name “the tribes of Israel.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: come forth out of the fountain of Judah
Isaiah.english_translation: And the tribe of Judah, who came forth and flowed from the waters of the buckets of Judah, as you say, “Water shall flow from his buckets” (Numbers 24:7).
Isaiah.translator_note: JPS renders *dalyav* in Numbers 24:7 “his branches”; Rashi reads it as “his buckets.”

Isaiah.english_translation: As it says (Jeremiah 5:2), “And though they say: ‘As the LORD liveth’, surely they swear falsely” — that is: you were not [worthy] to be redeemed, but because they were called from the holy city; and it caused them that they were not exiled, like the ten tribes in the days of Sennacherib, to Halah and Habor, who have no redemption.
Isaiah.translator_note: The last clause (“who have no redemption”) is ambiguous in the Hebrew; it is rendered literally. Halah and Habor: 2 Kings 17:6.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: stay themselves upon the God of Israel
Isaiah.english_translation: In the days of Hezekiah, of whom it is said, “He trusted in the LORD, the God of Israel” (2 Kings 18:5); it caused them that they were not exiled except in the days of Nebuchadnezzar, who exiled them to Babylon, and they had redemption through Cyrus.
Those that passed: the redemption from Egypt and the deliverance of Hezekiah from the hand of Sennacherib.
Before they came to be; “and suddenly I did them.”
As I declared at first by the mouth of My prophets.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Because I knew that thou art obstinate
Isaiah.english_translation: Because I knew that thou art obstinate — and if the miracle were to come and I had not declared it beforehand, thou wouldst say, “My idol made them,” and not that they are from the Holy One, blessed be He; therefore I declare it to thee from of old, before it comes, etc. “*Mi-da‘ati*”: this *mem* serves to give a reason, like “because I knew”; and its like is “but because the LORD loved you, and because He would keep the oath” (Deuteronomy 7:8).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Thou hast heard, see, all this
Isaiah.english_translation: Thou hast heard the former things that I declared; see that all of them came.
And you will bear witness to Me that not a thing has fallen [short].

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I have announced unto thee new things from this time
Isaiah.english_translation: Now I again make you hear new things, which are new to you, but before Me they have been revealed from of old.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Even hidden things, which thou hast not known
Isaiah.english_translation: And guarded in My treasuries, and you did not know them.
They were created, and are not from of old.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And before this day thou heardest them not
Isaiah.english_translation: Before the day of their being, I make you hear them.
Until the day; and “before this day” refers back to “I have announced unto thee” said above.

Targum Jonathan: “Even you did not hear the words of the prophet; even you did not receive the teaching of the Torah; even the words of the blessings and the curses, the covenant that I established with you in Horeb, you did not incline your ears to.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For I knew that thou wouldest deal very treacherously
Isaiah.english_translation: When I descended to rescue thee from the hand of Egypt, it was revealed before Me that thy end would be to deal treacherously, and yet I kept the oaths of the fathers; and this is what is said, “I have surely seen the affliction of My people” (Exodus 3:7) — two “seeings”: I see that their end is to deal treacherously, and in any case “I have seen the affliction of My people.” So Rabbi Tanhuma expounded.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: called a transgressor from the womb
Isaiah.english_translation: From when thou wast in Egypt, as is explained in Ezekiel (20:5), “and made Myself known unto them in the land of Egypt” etc., and “And I said unto them” etc. (20:7).
An expression of the present.

“And this is My praise, that I restrain (*eḥtam*) for thee” — an expression of the nose (*ḥotem*): “[I will stop] My nose, [lest] smoke of the nostrils” — from being angry with thee; for the one who is angry sends out smoke from his nostrils, as you say, “Smoke arose up in His nostrils” (Psalm 18:9). And so every *ḥaron af* is an expression of the heating of the nose: *ḥarah api*; and so “and my bones are burned with heat” (Job 30:30) — “my nose is heated from the excess of heat.”
Isaiah.translator_note: The middle of the explanation (“My nose … smoke of the nostrils”) is compressed in the printed text; rendered literally with the bracketed words supplied.

Isaiah.english_translation: Not by the fire of Gehinnom, like the refiner of silver with fire.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I have tried thee in the furnace of affliction
Isaiah.english_translation: I have chosen for thee a furnace of affliction instead of fire. A furnace (*kur*) is a vessel in which silver and gold are melted.
And for the sake of My holy name.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For how should it be profaned?
Isaiah.english_translation: How would My name be profaned by My cutting you off?

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And My glory will I not give to another
Isaiah.english_translation: For My enemies would say, “The hand of their idols is exalted.”
The name by which your father called you.
From Me you were called Israel; and Targum Jonathan: “and Israel My summoned one.”
For him who will do the desire of the Holy One, blessed be He, against Babylon.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And show His arm on the Chaldeans
Isaiah.english_translation: He will show it in the land of the Chaldeans; and of Cyrus he said so.
I redeemed Israel from Egypt, and I will redeem all Israel from the last exile and from the four corners of the earth.

Cyrus. And Targum Jonathan: “the LORD loved Israel; yea, I called him — Abraham.” And this “calling” is an expression of greatness, to be among the called, as “these were the called ones of the congregation” (Numbers 1:16).
Isaiah.translator_note:
JPS renders the phrase in Numbers 1:16 “the elect of the congregation.”
u|The Targum quotation is compressed; rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: From the time that it was, there am I
Isaiah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “From the time that the nations were separated from fear of Me, there I brought Abraham your father near to My service.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And now the Lord GOD hath sent me, and His spirit
Isaiah.english_translation: The prophet said, “And now the LORD God hath sent me, and His Word (*Memra*).” This is a mixing of statements: the one who said this did not say that. And Rabbi Tanhuma explained it as an aggadic midrash: “Hear you this” — the Torah of Moses, of which it is said, “This is the Torah”; “from the beginning I have not spoken in secret” — at Sinai; and the prophet says, “from the time that it was” (the thing about which he says), “there am I” — and we learn from this that all the prophets stood at Sinai, “and now He hath sent me” to prophesy to them. And even in this explanation there is a mixing of statements: “from the beginning I have not spoken in secret” the Divine Presence said; “from the time that it was, there am I” the prophet says. And one may explain it so that there be no mixing of statements: “Come near unto Me, hear this” — that I prophesy to you about the fall of Babylon and your redemption; “from the beginning I have not spoken in secret” — I spoke it from the time that the Holy One, blessed be He, decreed to bring them; “there was I” learning (another version: thou didst learn) that from the moment of the decree the Holy One, blessed be He, appoints the prophet who is destined to prophesy about the matter at the end of the heavenly company, even though he has not yet been created.
Isaiah.translator_note: The last sentence (“there was I learning / thou didst learn”) is hard in the printed text; rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_translation: [Like the grains] of the sea — like the fish of the sea, in multitude.
Concerning Nebuchadnezzar and his seed.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The LORD hath called me from the womb
Isaiah.english_translation: From when I was in the womb, it arose before Him in thought that my name should be Isaiah, to prophesy deliverances and consolations.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And He hath made my mouth like a sharp sword
Isaiah.english_translation: To rebuke the wicked and to prophesy punishment upon them.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: In the shadow of His hand hath He hid me
Isaiah.english_translation: So that they could not harm me.
Polished — *clair* (printed קלי״ר) in the foreign tongue (Old French).
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *clair* (“une flèche polie”) is confirmed in Darmesteter, who corrects the printed form to this reading.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: In His quiver hath He concealed me
Isaiah.english_translation: A vessel, the sheath of arrows, which is called *cuivre* (printed קוייכר״א) in the foreign tongue (Old French).
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *cuivre* (“carquois,” quiver) is confirmed in Darmesteter, who corrects the printed form to this reading.

Isaiah.english_translation: When I saw that I rebuke them and they do not listen.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Yet surely my right is with the LORD
Isaiah.english_translation: He knows that it is not from me but from them.
He will return to Him in repentance.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: It is too light a thing
Isaiah.english_translation: It is a small gift in My eyes that this alone should be to thee — that thou be to Me a servant to raise up Jacob and to restore to Me the preserved ones of Israel — and behold, I add to thee still more: “and I will give thee for a light of the nations,” and to prophesy about the fall of Babylon, which is a joy to the whole world.

Like “and wily of heart (*u-netzurat lev*)” (Proverbs 7:10) — whose heart is hemmed in by the evil inclination, thoughts of transgression, like a besieged city, from the siege of those who besiege it.
A despised soul.
To one whom the nation abhors.
Him, and they shall rise.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Because of the LORD that is faithful
Isaiah.english_translation: To keep His promise which He promised Abraham about the kingdoms, as it is said, “behold a smoking furnace” etc. (Genesis 15:17).
[That is,] He, “who hath chosen thee.”
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s two words are rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_translation: At a time of prayer, when thou art favoured and appeased before Me.
When thou shalt need deliverance.
And I will guard thee.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For a covenant of the people
Isaiah.english_translation: To be a covenant people to Me.
The Land of Israel, chosen for Me from among all lands.
At the time when I say to the prisoners of the exile, “Go forth.”
Targum Jonathan renders *negadin* (“streams”): brooks of water.
Isaiah.translator_note: JPS renders *shefayim* “high hills”; Rashi, following the Targum, takes it as watercourses.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Neither shall the heat nor sun smite them
Isaiah.english_translation: *Sharav* — heat.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And I will make all My mountains a way
Isaiah.english_translation: Since it was said (above, 33 [33:8]), “The wayfaring man ceaseth,” through its destruction, now passers-by and returners will again walk in it.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: My highways shall be raised on high
Isaiah.english_translation: Since it was said there, “The highways lie waste” — they were ruined, with no one to repair them — now “and My highways shall be raised on high”: they will repair the damage of the roads, and He will raise them up according to the custom, with smooth stones and earth.
From the land of the south.
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s identification (Targum-style “land of the south”) is rendered as printed.

Isaiah.english_translation: His people.
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s gloss is a single phrase completing the lemma; rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_translation: She thought that I had forgotten her.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Can a woman forget her sucking child
Isaiah.english_translation: Her suckling.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: That she should not have compassion on the son of her womb?
Isaiah.english_translation: From having compassion on the son of her womb.
Even if these may forget, I will not forget thee.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: upon the palms of My hands
Isaiah.english_translation: Upon My palms I see as if thou wert engraved upon My palms, to see thee and to remember thee always. Another explanation: *‘al kappayim* — above the clouds of glory, like *‘al kappayim kissah or* (Job 32 [printed]).
Isaiah.translator_note:
Rashi’s printed reference “Job 32” is Job 36:32 (JPS: “He covereth His hands with the lightning”); Rashi reads *kappayim* there as “palms” / “heights.”
u|Rashi’s second explanation is rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_translation: To return.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: shalt thou be too strait for the inhabitants
Isaiah.english_translation: Thou shalt be narrow because of the multitude of inhabitants who will come into thee; the place will be too narrow for them, to build houses for themselves.
Children of whom thou wast bereaved.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Give place to me that I may dwell
Isaiah.english_translation: Draw near to another side for my sake, and I will dwell.
*Soléde* (printed שולדא) in the foreign tongue (Old French).
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *soléde* (from *solata*; Darmesteter: “Abandonnée”) is confirmed; he corrects the printed form to this reading.

Isaiah.english_translation: Removed from every person; all say of me, “Depart from her.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I will lift up My hand
Isaiah.english_translation: [My hand] — My ensign: a sign to bring the exiles.
*Perche* (printed פירקא) in the foreign tongue (Old French), like “and as an ensign on a hill” (above, 30 [30:17]); and it is a sign of gathering, and they put a cloth on its top.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *perche* (“pole”) is confirmed in Darmesteter, who corrects the printed form to this reading.

Isaiah.english_translation: *Aisselle* (printed איישיל״א) in the foreign tongue (Old French); and similar to it in Ezra: “Also I shook out my lap (*ḥotsni*)” (Nehemiah 5:13).
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *aisselle* (“armpit”) is confirmed in Darmesteter. Rashi writes “in Ezra” because Nehemiah belongs to the book of Ezra in the Talmudic reckoning.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Shall the prey be taken from the mighty
Isaiah.english_translation: Do you suppose that it is impossible to take from Esau the spoil — the captives of Jacob the righteous?

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And I will contend with him that contendeth with thee
Isaiah.english_translation: And with thy contenders I will contend.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And I will feed them that oppress thee
Isaiah.english_translation: I will feed the Babylonians to the beast of the field — their flesh. *Monayikh* is an expression of “you shall not wrong one another” (Leviticus 25:14, 17) — wronging by words: those who provoke thee with their blasphemies.
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s printed reference is “Leviticus 25”; the expression occurs at 25:14 and 25:17.

Isaiah.english_translation: The sweetness of wine.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: they shall be drunken with their own blood
Isaiah.english_translation: So shall those who are accustomed to drink blood be drunk from their blood. And who are they? The fowl of heaven — so Targum Jonathan.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Wherefore, when I came, was there no man?
Isaiah.english_translation: [I came] to draw near to you, and there was no man among you who turned to Me.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I clothe the heavens with blackness
Isaiah.english_translation: The host of heaven — the princes of the idolaters — when I come to exact retribution from the nation.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The tongue of them that are taught
Isaiah.english_translation: Isaiah was saying: The LORD sent me and gave me a tongue fit to teach, in order to know how to sustain the weary — and the thirsty — to hear the words of the Holy One, blessed be He: a word.
Isaiah.translator_note: The last phrase (“a word”) is printed so and is rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_translation: Menahem joined it with “It is time for the LORD to work” (Psalm 119:126) — to fix times for them.
He rouses my ear with His holy spirit.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: To hear as they that are taught
Isaiah.english_translation: In the manner of the taught: the truth and the right.
And He made me hear: “Whom shall I send?” (above, 6 [6:8]); “I sent Amos, and they called him *Pesilos*; I sent Micah” etc., as it is set forth in the Pesikta “Nahamu, nahamu.”
From going on His mission, nor did I turn backward, but said, “Here am I; send me” (there).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I gave my back to the smiters
Isaiah.english_translation: He says to me: Isaiah, my son, they are stubborn, they are troublesome; [go] on condition that you not be angry with them. I said to Him: On that condition.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For the Lord GOD will help me
Isaiah.english_translation: If they rise up against me.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: He is near that justifieth me
Isaiah.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He, is near me, to vindicate me in judgment.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The moth shall eat them up
Isaiah.english_translation: The worms of garments.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: That obeyeth the voice of His servant
Isaiah.english_translation: The voice of the prophets.
Even if trouble comes upon him, let him trust in the name of the LORD, for He will save him.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Behold, all you that kindle a fire
Isaiah.english_translation: Who do not hear the voice of His prophets.
His wrath upon you.

“Holders of sparks” — these are sparks and coals of fire hurled from a sling; and there is a parallel to it in the Aramaic language: *zikkukin di-nur* (“sparks of fire”); and thus: *kakh ve-khakh zikta pasik lan*.
Isaiah.translator_note: The closing Aramaic words are printed so and are left untranslated.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Begone in the flame of your fire
Isaiah.english_translation: According to your way you shall be punished.
Isaiah.translator_note: *Tillaku* is rendered “you shall be punished” (literally “lashed”).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: This shall you have of My hand
Isaiah.english_translation: This shall be your recompense.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Look unto the rock whence you were hewn
Isaiah.english_translation: From it.
[The quarry] in which they bore and hew the pits — in which you were bored.

An expression of “in the cleft of the rock” (Exodus 33:22); “the ravens of the valley shall pick it out” (Proverbs 30:17). And who is the rock? It is Abraham your father; and who is the quarry? It is Sarah, “that bore you” (*teḥolelekhem*) — an expression of “for as soon as Zion travailed (*ḥalah*), she brought forth” (below, 66 [66:8]).
Who bore you.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For when he was but one I called him
Isaiah.english_translation: For he was one, alone, in the land of Canaan, to which I exiled him from his land and his birthplace; I called him — I multiplied him and made him great — an expression of “the called ones of the congregation” (Numbers 1:16); and as he was alone and I made him great, so will I make you great, who are alone to Me.
Isaiah.translator_note: JPS renders the phrase in Numbers 1:16 “the elect of the congregation.”

Isaiah.english_translation: This too is an expression of wilderness, like “in a land of deserts and of pits” (Jeremiah 2:6); except that the *‘aravah* had settlement before and was laid waste.
A voice of thanksgiving.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For instruction shall go forth from Me
Isaiah.english_translation: The words of the prophets are Torah, and the judgments in the end will be a repose and rest for the nations, to whom I will turn a pure language to serve Me (Zephaniah 3:9).
I will cause to rest.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Mine arms shall judge the peoples
Isaiah.english_translation: They will chastise: *justicier* (printed יושטיצ״א) in the foreign tongue (Old French).
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *justicier* (Darmesteter: “Jugeront, c.-à-d. châtieront”) is confirmed.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the heavens shall vanish away like smoke
Isaiah.english_translation: The princes of the hosts of the nations, in heaven.

Worn out, like “old rags and worn clouts” (Jeremiah 38:11) — a spoiled garment. Another version: *nimlaḥu* — confused, an expression of the sailors (*malaḥim*) of the sea who stir the water with oars, the steersmen of the ship; and so “*memulaḥ*, pure, holy” (Exodus 30:35 [printed “35”]).
Isaiah.translator_note:
Rashi’s printed reference “Exodus 35” is Exodus 30:35; JPS renders *memulaḥ* there “seasoned with salt.” Rashi takes *nimlaḥu* as “mixed, confused.”
u|The Jeremiah quotation is Rashi’s wording (*beluei ha-seḥavot ve-ha-malaḥim*); JPS reads “worn clouts and worn rags.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And the earth shall wax old like a garment
Isaiah.english_translation: The rulers of the earth.
The rest of the people.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: But My salvation shall be for ever
Isaiah.english_translation: To My people it will be for ever. Another explanation: the heavens and the earth literally; and thus is its interpretation: Lift up your eyes and look to the heavens and to the earth and see how strong and sturdy they are, and yet they will wear out, and My righteousness and My salvation will be for ever — so My righteousness is sturdier and stronger than they.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the moth shall eat them up
Isaiah.english_translation: [The moth] and the worm are kinds of worms.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Awake, awake, put on strength, O arm of the LORD
Isaiah.english_translation: It is the prophet’s prayer.
Egypt, of which *Rahav* is written: “*Rahav hem shavet*” (above, 30 [30:7]).
Isaiah.translator_note: JPS renders Isaiah 30:7 “Therefore have I called her arrogancy that sitteth still”; Rashi takes *Rahav* as a name of Egypt.

Isaiah.english_translation: An expression of slaying: *ḥalal* (slain).
Pharaoh.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And the ransomed of the LORD shall return
Isaiah.english_translation: An expression of prayer, and it refers back to “Awake, awake.”
A daughter of the righteous like thyself, full of merits — why shouldst thou fear mortal man, whose end is to die?

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And hast forgotten the LORD thy Maker
Isaiah.english_translation: And hast not leaned upon Him.
The rulers of the nations of the world who enslave you.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: As he maketh ready to destroy
Isaiah.english_translation: Ready (present).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And where is the fury of the oppressor?
Isaiah.english_translation: Tomorrow it comes and is not.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: He that is bent down shall speedily be loosed
Isaiah.english_translation: Even if the passages are hard on him and he needs to be opened by the movement of the bowels so that he not die for the pit; and since he hastens to be opened, he needs much food, for if his bread fails, he too will die.
Isaiah.translator_note: This is the aggadic reading (see the end of ISA.51.14.4); the sentence is compressed and rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_translation: An expression of a thing destined to be poured out, as is said of Moab, whom the prophet likened to wine (Jeremiah 48:11), “He hath settled on his lees, and hath not been emptied from vessel to vessel”; and it says there (48:12), “And I will send unto him them that tilt up (*tso‘im*), and they shall tilt him up; and they shall empty his vessels.” Another explanation: “speedily is the *tso‘eh*” — that oppressing enemy who is now girded at the loins and equipped with strength will hasten to be opened and be weak.
Isaiah.translator_note: “Girded at the loins and equipped with strength” (*ḥagur motnayim ḥaluts koaḥ*) is rendered by its likely sense.

Isaiah.english_translation: Girded — like “*tso‘eh* in the greatness of his strength” (below, 63 [63:1]).
Isaiah.translator_note: JPS renders that phrase “stately in the greatness of his strength.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: shall not go down dying into the pit
Isaiah.english_translation: Who is delivered into his hand, to the pit. But the first explanation is from an aggadic midrash, in the Pesikta Rabbati.
An expression of “My skin closeth up” (Job 7:5): *froncer* (printed פרונצ״א) in the foreign tongue (Old French).
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *froncer* is confirmed in Darmesteter, who reads it with manuscript A (“Lire : froncér”).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: That I may plant the heavens
Isaiah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “To establish the people of whom it was said that they would be numerous as the stars of heaven.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And lay the foundations of the earth
Isaiah.english_translation: “And to perfect the congregation of whom it was said that they would be numerous as the dust of the earth.”

Targum Jonathan: *pili* — and it is the name of a cup. To me it appears that *kubba‘at* means these lees that are fixed (*kevu‘im*) at the bottom of the vessel, and *matsit* is said of it, as it is said, “its dregs they shall drain (*yimtsu*)” (Psalm 75:9).

A drink that stupefies and weakens a man’s strength, as if bound, tied and wrapped — like “the cypresses are shaken (*hor‘alu*)” (Nahum 2:4) and “the veils” (*ha-re‘alot*, Isaiah 3:19), which is an expression of wrapping; and in tractate Shabbat: “Median *re‘ulot*” — a fine kind of cloak to wrap oneself in.
Isaiah.translator_note:
JPS renders Nahum 2:4 “the cypress spears are brandished”; Rashi takes the verb as “wrapped, bound.”
u|The quotation from Nahum and the Shabbat reference are rendered as printed.

Isaiah.english_translation: *Entomisement* (printed אינטומישמנ״ט) in the foreign tongue (Old French).
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *entomisement* is confirmed in Darmesteter (“étourdissement”).

Isaiah.english_translation: *Agoter* (printed אגושטי״ר) in the foreign tongue (Old French).
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *agoter* (“to taste”; from *ad* + *gustare*) is confirmed in Darmesteter, who gives the printed spelling as a variant.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: These two things are befallen thee
Isaiah.english_translation: Doubled troubles, two by two.
Whom shall I bring to you to comfort you, and to say, “Another nation too was struck like you”?
An expression of weariness, like “the fair virgins … shall faint (*titalafnah*) for thirst” (Amos 8:13): *pasmer* (printed פשמי״ר) in the foreign tongue (Old French).
