Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *pasmer* (“to swoon”) is confirmed in Darmesteter.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: As an antelope in a net
Isaiah.english_translation: Ownerless (*hefker*), like this antelope that fell into a net; *to* is like *u-te’o* (Deuteronomy 14 [14:5]).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And drunken, but not with wine
Isaiah.english_translation: Drunk from another thing, not from wine.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: that pleadeth the cause of His people
Isaiah.english_translation: Who will judge a case with His people.
Those who move thee and shake thee about, like “and, behold, the multitude melted away (*namog*)” (1 Samuel 14:16): *croler* (printed קרושלי״ר) in the foreign tongue (Old French).
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *crolér* (“to shake”) is confirmed in Darmesteter (“Ceux qui te détruisent”).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Bow down, that we may go over
Isaiah.english_translation: [That we may go over] — upon thy back.
*Escorre* (printed אישקור״א) in the foreign tongue (Old French), like one who shakes out a cloak.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *escodre* (from *excutere*; Darmesteter: “Secoue ta poussière”) is confirmed; the printed form is one of the variants he lists.

Isaiah.english_translation: From the ground — from the phrase “she shall sit upon the ground” (above, 3 [3:26]).
On the throne.
Be loosened.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Loose thyself from the bands of thy neck
Isaiah.english_translation: *Cojongles* (printed קריגל״ש) in the foreign tongue (Old French): bands, straps.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *cojongles* (Darmesteter: “Les liens de ton cou”; from *cingula*, modern *sangles*) is confirmed; the printed form is a variant.

Isaiah.english_translation: Like *shevuyah* (captive).
For a matter of nothing — this is the evil inclination, which is not for your reward.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: you shall be redeemed without money
Isaiah.english_translation: But by repentance.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: My people went down aforetime into Egypt to sojourn there
Isaiah.english_translation: The Egyptians had some claim against them, for they had become their hosts and had sustained them; but Assyria oppressed them for nothing and without cause.
Why do I tarry, and cause My children to tarry, here?
They glory, saying, “Our hand is exalted.”
*Mit’natsetz* (“blasphemes itself”) — and this is a parallel to “and he heard the Voice speaking (*mi-dabber*) unto him” (Numbers 7:89; printed “8”).
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s printed reference “Numbers 8” is Numbers 7:89.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Therefore My people shall know My name
Isaiah.english_translation: When I redeem them they will recognize that My name is Lord, Ruler and Governor, according to its meaning.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Therefore they shall know in that day
Isaiah.english_translation: At their redemption they will understand that I am He who spoke, and “behold, here I am” — I have fulfilled it.
Watchmen stationed on the walls and towers, to announce and to see who comes to the city.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: hath made bare His holy arm
Isaiah.english_translation: Revealed.
Do not touch; they shall be an abomination to you, from touching them.
Isaiah.translator_note: The last word is abbreviated in the printed text (מליג׳) and is read as “from touching.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Go you out of the midst of her
Isaiah.english_translation: From the midst of the exile. All these last consolations are only about the last exile.
Purify yourselves.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: You that bear the vessels of the LORD
Isaiah.english_translation: The priests and Levites, who were bearers of His vessels (of the Holy One) in the wilderness. (From here [is a proof for] the resurrection of the dead.)
Isaiah.translator_note: The closing parenthesis is a later addition in the printed text; rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For the LORD will go before you
Isaiah.english_translation: The two things at the end of this verse settle the two things at its beginning. “For you shall not go out in haste” — what is the reason? “For the LORD will go before you,” to guide you on the way; and whoever has his messenger go before him to guide him on the way, his departure is not in haste. “Neither shall you go by flight” — because “the God of Israel will be your rearward” (*me’asifkhem*): He goes behind you to guard you from every pursuer, like “And the standard of the camp of the children of Dan, which was the rearward (*me’assef*) of all the camps, set forward” (Numbers 10:25). The one who goes after the camp is called *me’assef* because he waits for the weak and the stumbling; and so it says in Joshua, “and the rearward went after the ark” (6:9).
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi gives no references for the two quotations: Numbers 10:25 and Joshua 6:9.

Isaiah.english_translation: Behold, at the end of days My servant Jacob shall prosper — the righteous among them.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: According as many were appalled at thee
Isaiah.english_translation: As many peoples were astonished at them when they saw their lowliness, and said to one another: How marred is the appearance of the man (of Israel)! See how their form is darker than that of other men — so, as we see with our own eyes.
Isaiah.translator_note: The closing words (“so, as we see with our own eyes”) connect to the next verse; rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: So shall he startle many nations
Isaiah.english_translation: So now too his hand will prevail, and he will cast down the horns of the idolaters who goaded him.
Isaiah.translator_note: *Zeiruhu* is rendered “goaded”; its sense is uncertain.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Kings shall shut their mouths because of him
Isaiah.english_translation: They will close their mouths out of great astonishment, for they saw in him a glory that had not been told them of any person.
They have looked.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Who would have believed our report?
Isaiah.english_translation: So will the idolaters say to one another: Had we heard from others what we see, it would not be believable.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And to whom hath the arm of the LORD been revealed?
Isaiah.english_translation: [An arm] like this, in greatness and splendour — upon whom has it been revealed until now?

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For he shot up right forth as a sapling
Isaiah.english_translation: This people, before this greatness came to it, was a very lowly people, and rose of itself like a shoot among the suckers of trees.
Isaiah.translator_note: The first words are elliptical in the printed text (*lefanav*); rendered by the sense.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And as a root out of a dry ground
Isaiah.english_translation: It rose from a parched land.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: He had no form nor comeliness
Isaiah.english_translation: He had at first no form and no splendour.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: that we should look upon him
Isaiah.english_translation: And when we first saw him with no appearance, how could we desire him (*ve-nehmedehu*)? And *ve-nehmedehu* is astonishing.
Isaiah.translator_note: The last clause is rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: He was despised, and forsaken of men
Isaiah.english_translation: [He] was. So is the way of this prophet: he mentions all Israel as one man — “Fear not, My servant Jacob” (Jeremiah 30:10) — and also here, “Behold, My servant shall prosper” (52:13), in the house of Jacob. He said *yaskil* — an expression of success, like “And David had great success (*maskil*) in all his ways” (1 Samuel 18:14).
Isaiah.translator_note:
Rashi gives no reference for “Fear not, My servant Jacob”; the wording is Jeremiah 30:10 (also 46:27).
u|“In the house of Jacob” is printed so and is rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And as one from whom men hide their face
Isaiah.english_translation: From the greatness of their shame and lowliness, they were like one hiding his face from him — their faces covered in concealment, so that we should not see them — like a man stricken with a plague who hides his face and fears to look.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Surely our diseases he did bear
Isaiah.english_translation: *Akhen* is an expression of “but” everywhere: but now we see that it did not come upon him because of his lowliness, but he was chastised with sufferings.
We were thinking that he was hated by the Omnipresent, and it was not so, but he was pierced from our transgressions and crushed from our iniquities.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The chastisement of our welfare was upon him
Isaiah.english_translation: The sufferings that belonged to the peace we had came upon him, for he was chastised so that there might be peace for the whole world.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: All we like sheep did go astray
Isaiah.english_translation: Now it is revealed.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the LORD hath made to light on him
Isaiah.english_translation: He was entreated through him and was appeased concerning the iniquity of all of us, that He did not destroy His world. *Hifgia*: *esprier* (printed אשפריאיר) in the foreign tongue (Old French) — an expression of supplication.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *esprier* (from *er* + *precavit*) is confirmed in Darmesteter (“Il a intercédé”).

Isaiah.english_translation: Pressed by oppressors and pushers.
By wronging with words: *sorparler* (printed שורפרלרי״ן) in the foreign tongue (Old French).
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *sorparler* (Darmesteter: “Il a été maltraité”; see Godefroy, *sourparler*) is confirmed.

Isaiah.english_translation: He bore it and was silent, like the lamb that is led to the slaughter, and like a ewe that is dumb before her shearers.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Yea, he opened not his mouth
Isaiah.english_translation: It refers back to “a lamb that is led to the slaughter.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: By oppression and judgment he was taken away
Isaiah.english_translation: The prophet announces good tidings and says that the idolaters will say this at the end of days, when they see — when he was taken from the restraint in which he was restrained in their hands, and from the judgment of the sufferings that he bore until now.
The years that have passed over him.

Who will speak of the hardships that befell him, for it was decreed from the beginning? And he was banished from the land of the living, which is the Land of Israel; for the transgression of my people this stroke came upon the righteous among them.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And they made his grave with the wicked
Isaiah.english_translation: He gave himself to be buried according to all that the wicked of the nations decreed upon him, who imposed upon them killing and burial of asses in the bowels of dogs.
Isaiah.translator_note: The last clause is rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_translation: With the consent of the wicked he agreed to be buried, and not to deny the living God.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And with the rich his tomb
Isaiah.english_translation: And with the consent of the ruler he gave himself over to every kind of death that he decreed upon him, because he would not accept denial [of God], to do evil and to commit violence like all the nations among whom he was a sojourner.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Neither was any deceit in his mouth
Isaiah.english_translation: [He did not consent] to accept idolatry upon himself.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Yet it pleased the LORD to crush him by disease
Isaiah.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He, desired to crush him and to restore him to the good; therefore He made him ill.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: To see if his soul would offer itself in restitution
Isaiah.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He, said: I shall see whether his soul will be given and surrendered in My holiness, to return it to Me as a guilt-offering for all that he trespassed — I shall repay him his recompense, “and he shall see his seed” etc. *Asham* here is an expression of ransom that a man gives to him whom he has wronged — *amende* (printed אמינדא) in the foreign tongue (Old French) — as is said of the Philistines, “send it not empty; but in any wise return Him a guilt-offering” (1 Samuel 6:3).
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *amende* (“rançon”) is confirmed in Darmesteter (“Rangon : amendle”).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Of the travail of his soul he shall see to the full
Isaiah.english_translation: He would eat and be satisfied; he did not rob or take by violence.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Who by his knowledge did justify the Righteous One
Isaiah.english_translation: My servant used to judge true judgment for all who came to judgment before him.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And their iniquities he did bear
Isaiah.english_translation: He used to bear them, as is the way of all the righteous, as it is said, “Thou and thy sons … shall bear the iniquity of the sanctuary” (Numbers 18:1).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Therefore will I divide him a portion among the great
Isaiah.english_translation: For doing this I shall apportion to him an inheritance and a lot among the many, together with the first fathers.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Because he bared his soul unto death
Isaiah.english_translation: An expression of “and she emptied (*va-te‘ar*) her pitcher” (Genesis 24:20).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And was numbered with the transgressors
Isaiah.english_translation: He bore sufferings as though he had sinned and transgressed, while he, for the sake of others, bore the sin of many.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And made intercession for the transgressors
Isaiah.english_translation: Through the sufferings that came by his hand, good came to the world.
Jerusalem, which was as one who had not borne.
An expression of birth, for the one who gives birth bears through pangs and labour.
The daughter of Edom.
Afar.
These are thin ropes hanging from the edges of tents and tied to pegs, which are called *chevilles* (printed קביל״ס) in the foreign tongue (Old French); and they drive them into the ground.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *cheville* (“peg”) is confirmed in Darmesteter (LIV, 2, “Et tes chevilles”).

Isaiah.english_translation: Thou shalt prevail.
Thy youth.
When she is rejected, sometimes it is that he is angry with her a little.
Menahem explained it as “burning of anger”; and Dunash said, “in a little wrath,” like “for a small moment have I forsaken thee” (below, 54:7); and so Targum Jonathan.
That it will endure for ever.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For this is as the waters of Noah unto Me
Isaiah.english_translation: An oath is with Me; and he goes on to explain His word: “as I have sworn that the waters of Noah should no more go over” etc.
Even if the merit of the fathers and the mothers should come to an end, My kindness shall not depart from thee.
Whose heart is tossed by the multitude of troubles.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I will set thy stones in fair colours
Isaiah.english_translation: I will pave thy pavement with stones of *nofekh*.
Isaiah.translator_note: *Nofekh* (a precious stone) is left untranslated.

Isaiah.english_translation: A kind of precious stone.

Targum Jonathan: *amakh*; and Menahem joined it with *yeshamshuniyah*. And some explain it as an expression of windows of the sun, in which the sun shines, and they make a partition opposite it of various kinds of coloured glass for ornament. And Midrash Tehillim explains “thy pinnacles” as “a sun and a shield” (Psalm 84:12) — the teeth of the wall.
Isaiah.translator_note: The Targum word and Menahem’s comparison are printed so; they are not rendered further.

Isaiah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “stones of *gomar*” (*gomerin*, the Targum’s rendering of “coals”). He explained *ekdaḥ* as an expression of *kodeḥei esh* (“kindlers of fire”) — and they are a kind of precious stones burning like torches, and it is *carboncle* (printed קרבונקל״א) in the foreign tongue, from the word for “coal.” And some explain it as an expression of *makdeaḥ*: large stones, so that the whole hollow of the doorway is bored out of it, and the doorposts, the threshold and the sill are all made from the stone.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *carboncle* (modern *escarboucle*) is noted in Darmesteter’s footnote.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: all thy border of precious stones
Isaiah.english_translation: For stones of need.
Isaiah.translator_note: *Avnei tsaruk* is rendered literally; the sense is uncertain.

Isaiah.english_translation: Like “Shake thyself from the dust” (above, 52 [52:2]): thou shalt be far from those who oppress thee.

(“Be thou far from oppression” — thou shalt keep far from oppressing human beings, in the way that the wicked do who gather money by robbery; but you will not need to rob, for you will not fear want and poverty, nor ruin, for it will not come and will not befall you. Abarbanel.)
Isaiah.translator_note: This comment is printed in parentheses and ends with the name Abarbanel (1437–1508), who lived centuries after Rashi; it is a later addition and is translated as printed.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: In righteousness shalt thou be established
Isaiah.english_translation: (In the righteousness that thou wilt do, thou shalt be established with an everlasting redemption, and thou shalt be far from the oppression of men, for thou shalt not even see fear, and no fear of them shall be to thee; and thou shalt be far from ruin, that it not draw near to thee. *Ayyelah Sheluḥah*.)
Isaiah.translator_note: This comment is printed in parentheses and ends with a name (*Ayyelah Sheluḥah*) that is not expanded; it is a later addition and is translated as printed.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Behold, they may gather together, but not by Me
Isaiah.english_translation: Behold, he will fear and dread (*yagur* is from the stem of fear); the evils of that one with whom I am not — he is *sa‘ir*.
Isaiah.translator_note: The end of the comment is compressed in the printed text; rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_translation: Whoever is gathered against thee for war; or “who is a *ger*” — whoever became embroiled with thee. And our Rabbis explained it of proselytes, to say that they do not accept proselytes in the days of our Messiah. But even in its plain sense it is possible: those who became proselytes with thee in thy poverty shall fall upon thee in thy riches, like “he fell over against all his brethren” (Genesis 25:18).
Isaiah.translator_note: JPS renders *nafal* in Genesis 25:18 “he did settle”; Rashi reads it as “fell” (settled upon).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Behold, I have created the smith
Isaiah.english_translation: I who created the smith who prepares a vessel, and I who created the destroyer who ruins it — that is: I am He who stirred up the enemy against thee; I am He who prepared punishment for him.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: bringeth forth a weapon for his work
Isaiah.english_translation: For the purpose of finishing all his need.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: No weapon that is formed against thee shall prosper
Isaiah.english_translation: Every weapon that they will whet and sharpen for thee, to fight against thee.
An expression of “knives of flint” (Joshua 5:2) and “the edge of his sword” (Psalm 89:44).
“Ho” is an expression of calling and summoning and gathering, and there are many in Scripture: “Ho, ho, flee then from the land of the north” (Zechariah 2:10).
To the Torah.
An expression of “to buy corn” (Genesis 42:3): buy.
A purchase better than wine and milk.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Wherefore do you spend money for that which is not bread?
Isaiah.english_translation: Why do you bring upon yourselves to weigh out money to your enemies, without bread?
That I will repay to David his kindnesses.
A prince and one great over them, and a reprover, and a witness against their ways to their faces.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Behold, thou shalt call a nation that thou knowest not
Isaiah.english_translation: For thy service; if you will hearken to Me, for the sake of the name of the LORD which is called upon thee.
Isaiah.translator_note: The person of the verb changes in the printed text (“you will hearken … upon thee”); rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_translation: Before the decree of judgment is sealed, while He is saying to you, “Seek Me.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For My thoughts are not your thoughts
Isaiah.english_translation: Mine and yours are not equal; therefore I say to you, “Let the wicked forsake his way,” and take hold of My way.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Neither are your ways My ways
Isaiah.english_translation: “And the man of iniquity his thoughts” (55:7) — and let him take hold of My thoughts, to do what is good in My eyes. And an aggadic midrash: “For My thoughts are not your thoughts” etc. — My law is not like the law of flesh and blood: with you, he who confesses in judgment is held liable; but I — “whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall obtain mercy” (Proverbs 28:13).
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s lemma (“and the man of iniquity his thoughts”) belongs to Isaiah 55:7; it is quoted in the text because the site’s verse division places it before this verse. His printed reference “Proverbs 25” is Proverbs 28:13.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For as the heavens are higher than the earth
Isaiah.english_translation: That is: there is a difference and a gradation of levels and praise in My ways beyond your ways, and in My thoughts beyond your thoughts, like the height of the heaven above the earth: you set your heart to rebel against Me, and I set My heart to bring you back.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For as the rain cometh down and the snow from heaven
Isaiah.english_translation: And it will not return empty, but will benefit the world.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: So shall My word be that goeth forth out of My mouth
Isaiah.english_translation: To make known to you through the prophets: it shall not return empty, but will benefit you if you hearken to them.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For you shall go out with joy
Isaiah.english_translation: From the exile.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The mountains and the hills shall break forth before you into singing
Isaiah.english_translation: That they will give you their fruits and their produce, and their inhabitants will enjoy [them] (will sing).
Isaiah.translator_note: The parenthetical word is a variant reading in the printed text.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Instead of the thorn shall come up the cypress
Isaiah.english_translation: Our Rabbis expounded: instead of the wicked, the righteous will come up.
[*Na‘atsuts*] and *sirpad* are kinds of thorns — that is: the wicked will perish, and the righteous will take their dominion.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Happy is the man that doeth this
Isaiah.english_translation: [The one who] keeps the Sabbath, etc.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The LORD will surely separate me from His people
Isaiah.english_translation: “Why should I convert? Surely the Holy One, blessed be He, will separate me from His people when He pays their reward.”
“Why should I mend my ways and my deeds? Behold, I am a dry tree, with no remembrance.”
Holding.
And not for Israel alone, for even to proselytes.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Yet I will gather others to him
Isaiah.english_translation: Of the nations who will convert and attach themselves to them.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: beside those of him that are gathered
Isaiah.english_translation: Added to the gathered ones of Israel.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: All you beasts of the field, come to devour
Isaiah.english_translation: All proselytes of the nations: come and draw near to Me; and devour all the beasts in the forest — the mighty ones of the nations who steeled their hearts against converting.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Yea, all you beasts in the forest
Isaiah.english_translation: The beast of the field is not as strong as the beast of the forest; the beast of the field is weaker and feebler in strength than the beast of the forest. And because it said “Yet I will gather others to him,” Scripture said this.

Because it said, “Seek the LORD,” and the whole matter, and they do not listen, it goes on to say: Behold, the prophets cry out to them and proclaim repentance, and it will be good for them; yet their leaders are all blind and do not see what is destined to be — like the watchman appointed to see the sword coming, to warn the people, who is blind to seeing the sword come and dumb to warning the people; like a dog that was appointed to guard the house and is dumb from barking. So the leaders of Israel do not warn them to return to the good.
Dunash explained: “dozing, lying down”; and Jonathan translated: “sleepers, lying down”; and it has no parallel.
They want to fill their belly: *engres* (printed אינגר״ש) in the foreign tongue (Old French).
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *engres* (Darmesteter, “Au cœur impudent,” from *acre talentum*) is confirmed as the gloss on *‘azei nefesh*; the printed word is a variant.

Isaiah.english_translation: As the dogs do not know satiety, so the shepherds do not know how to understand what will be in the end of days.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: They all turn to their own way
Isaiah.english_translation: They have turned toward the way of their own benefit, each to his gain, to rob the rest of the people who are appointed under them.
Like “all the people from every quarter” (Genesis 19:4) — from the end of their number to its end, all conduct themselves so.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Come you, I will fetch wine
Isaiah.english_translation: Thus they used to say to one another.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: to-morrow shall be as this day
Isaiah.english_translation: In food and drink.
Such as Josiah.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And no man layeth it to heart
Isaiah.english_translation: Why he was removed.
There is none among those who remain who understands what the Holy One, blessed be He, saw in removing him.
The evil destined to come upon the generation — the righteous one is gathered.
For thus the Holy One, blessed be He, said: Let this righteous man come to his fathers in peace and not see evil.
In the time of the evil — this one who walked straight in his uprightness, like “to do right (*nekhokhah*)” (Amos 3:10).
The survivors after the righteous have been removed — and receive your punishments.
Children of sorceries.
The male is an adulterer.
The female.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Against whom do you sport yourselves?
Isaiah.english_translation: Since you have turned away from after Me, on whom will you lean to delight in good? Had you merited, then you would delight in the LORD; but now — in whom will you delight?

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Against whom make you a wide mouth
Isaiah.english_translation: When you mock and scoff at His prophets.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: You that inflame yourselves among the terebinths
Isaiah.english_translation: Who warm themselves in lust under the terebinth and the oak.
Isaiah.translator_note: The abbreviation ש״ז is not expanded in the printed text; “lust” is the likely sense.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: That slay the children in the valleys
Isaiah.english_translation: For idolatrous sacrifice.
The cleft of the rocks, and so “to the cleft of the rock” (Judges 15:11).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Among the smooth stones of the valley
Isaiah.english_translation: Stones that are in the brook.
With them they will stone thee.
To be grieved by them — why? For to them too hast thou poured a drink-offering.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Should I pacify Myself for these things?
Isaiah.english_translation: From doing thee evil.
The bed of thy adultery with idolatry, on the high mountains.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And behind the doors and the posts
Isaiah.english_translation: [It is said] of one who likens her to an adulterous woman, whose adulterers look and wait before the opening of her house, while her heart and her memory are on the door and the doorpost — how it will open and she will go out to them.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For thou hast uncovered, and art gone up from Me
Isaiah.english_translation: Thou wert lying beside Me, and thou didst uncover the covering with which they were covered together, and thou didst go up from beside Me.
To receive many adulterers in it.
A covenant with them.
When thou sawest for thyself a hand and a place, to show them thy love.
*Aise* (printed אייש״י) in the foreign tongue (Old French) — and so “See, Joab’s field is near mine (*el yadi*)” (2 Samuel 14:30).
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *aise* (Darmesteter: “Quand tu as vu un endroit convenable”) is confirmed.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And thou wentest to the king with ointment
Isaiah.english_translation: And I at the beginning raised thee up, and thou didst receive the face of thy king with all kinds of delicacies. *Tashuri* is an expression of seeing the face, like “I behold him (*ashurennu*), but not nigh” (Numbers 24:17); and so “there is not a present (*teshurah*) to bring” (1 Samuel 9:7) — there is nothing to bring as a gift for receiving the face.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And didst send thine ambassadors far off
Isaiah.english_translation: Thy messengers to afar, to collect tribute from the kings of the nations.
[And thou didst bring low] the mighty of the nations down to Sheol — so Jonathan translated.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Thou wast wearied with the length of thy way
Isaiah.english_translation: Thou didst busy thyself with thy needs, to fulfil thy desire, to increase thy wealth.
Thou didst not say: I will despair of these and not hasten again to occupy myself with them, for I will give heart to Torah and to the commandments.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: thou didst find a renewal of thy strength
Isaiah.english_translation: The need of thy hand thou didst find; thou didst succeed in thy works.
Thy heart did not grow sick to be concerned about My service, to occupy thyself with Torah. *Ḥayyat* is an Arabic expression meaning “need.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: of whom hast thou been afraid
Isaiah.english_translation: Of whom wast thou made afraid?

Because thou didst cut thyself off from My service and didst fail Me, as “whose waters fail not” (below, 58:11); “All men are liars” (Psalm 116:11). *Faliance* in Old French. And so every expression of *kazav* [failing, lying] is said of one in whom people trust, and he fails and betrays.
Isaiah.translator_note:
Old French *faliance*: the printed form is פליינצ"א; Darmesteter corrects it to read *faliance*.
Rashi’s Hebrew quotation of Psalm 116:11 matches JPS “All men are liars.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Have not I held My peace
Isaiah.english_translation: For I held My peace over how many transgressions that thou didst transgress against Me.
I constantly declare to thee things that, if thou wilt do them, thou wilt be righteous.
Which thou doest not by My will shall not profit thee in the time of thy evil.
Isaiah.translator_note: The Hebrew has “which thou doest” in the masculine form; rendered as printed.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: let them that thou hast gathered deliver thee
Isaiah.english_translation: Let now the gatherings of idols and images and deniers of the Torah, which thou hast gathered, arise, and deliver thee when thou criest out from thy distress. Surely the wind shall carry all of them away, and they will not be able to deliver.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Cast you up, cast you up
Isaiah.english_translation: Thus the prophet says in My name to My people: Build up a paved highway; remove the evil inclination from your ways.
Remove the stones over which your feet stumble; they are the thoughts of wickedness.
I dwell, and from there I am with the contrite and lowly of spirit, for I incline My Presence (*Shekhinah*) upon him.
The crushed, who bear poverty and sicknesses.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I will not contend for ever
Isaiah.english_translation: If I bring sufferings upon man, My contention with him is not for long days, nor My wrath for ever.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the spirit that enwrappeth itself is from Me
Isaiah.english_translation: When the spirit of man, which is from before Me, which was given into him by Me, enwraps itself, he will confess and submit over his trespass, like “That faint for hunger” (Lamentations 2:19), and “swoon” (*be‘atef*, ibid. 2:11). “And the souls which I have made.”
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s *ha-‘atufim ba-ra‘av* matches JPS “That faint for hunger” (Lamentations 2:19). The second quotation, *be‘atef ‘olel*, is from Lamentations 2:11 (printed only “ibid.”); JPS renders it “swoon.”

Isaiah.english_translation: This *ki* serves in the sense of “when,” like *ki tir’eh* and *ki tavo* [“when thou seest,” “when thou comest”]; that is, when his spirit is enwrapped and he is humbled, I annul My contention and My wrath from him.
His robbery.

*Katsafti* — at first, “and I smote him”; “I hid My face” continually from his distress, “and I was wroth,” and because he goes backsliding in the way of his heart. And the verse is transposed, and so is its explanation: For the iniquity of his covetousness, and he went on frowardly in the ways of his heart, I was wroth and smote him.
Isaiah.translator_note:
The printed text of the first half is compressed and its clauses are hard to separate; rendered literally.
Rashi’s paraphrase has *darkhei libo* (“ways of his heart”); the verse has *derekh libo* (“the way of his heart”).

Isaiah.english_translation: When he submits before Me, because distress has come upon him.
I will lead him in the way of healing; or *ve-anḥehu* is an expression of setting down (*hanaḥah*) and repose.
Those who are grieved over him.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: createth the fruit of the lips
Isaiah.english_translation: I create for him a new fruit of the lips, because until now distress had come upon him and everyone cried out against him; now they will call to him, “Peace, peace.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: him that is far off and to him that is near
Isaiah.english_translation: Both are equal: he who has long been established and accustomed to My Torah and service from his youth, and he who has now drawn near, to return from his evil way. HaShem said, “And I will heal him” — of his sickness and of his sins.
Who do not set their heart to return.

This sea: its waves exalt themselves upward and to go out beyond the border of the sand that I set as a boundary for the sea, and when it reaches there, it is broken against its will; and all this, one wave sees its fellow and does not turn back. So the wicked man sees his fellow smitten for his wickedness and does not turn back. And just as the sea’s mire and its foulness are at its edge, so the wicked: their foulness is in their mouth. For example, Pharaoh said, “Who is the LORD” (Exodus 5:2); Sennacherib said, “Who among all the gods of the lands” (Isaiah 36:20); Nebuchadnezzar said (ibid. 14), “I will be like the Most High.”
Isaiah.translator_note:
Printed references: “Exodus 5,” “Isaiah 36:20” and “ibid. 14.” The last is Isaiah 14:14 (JPS: “I will be like the Most High”).
Rashi’s “Who among all the gods of the lands” is shorter than JPS Isaiah 36:20, “Who are they among all the gods of these countries.”

Isaiah.english_translation: Like a sea that is driven out (*nigrash*), which is driven out all the day, mire and clay.
Isaiah.translator_note: The comment is elliptical; the verse continues “and its waters cast up mire and dirt.”

Isaiah.english_translation: Since He said to the righteous and to the penitents, “Peace, peace to him that is far off,” etc., He turned back and said, “There is no peace for the wicked.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: declare unto My people their transgression
Isaiah.english_translation: These are the Torah scholars, whose every inadvertence is a transgression (*pesha‘*), for an error in study comes to count as wilful sin.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the house of Jacob their sins
Isaiah.english_translation: These are the unlearned (*‘ammei ha-aretz*), whose very wilful sins are as inadvertences.
As it is said, “But they beguiled Him with their mouth” (Psalm 78:36).
Isaiah.translator_note: The printed reference is “Psalms 78”; the verse is 78:36.

Isaiah.english_translation: They desire to ask rulings of the sages, as though they wished to fulfil them.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: As a nation that did righteousness
Isaiah.english_translation: So they ask Me constantly for righteous judgment, but their mind is not to fulfil it. And when they fast and are not answered, they say, “Wherefore have we fasted, and Thou seest not?” And I say, “Behold, in the day of your fast you pursue your business”: all the business of your needs you labour to find, even through robbery and violence.
Your debtors, who are grieved on your account — you exact payment from them on the day of your fast.
In keeping with the rule of the day: to break your hearts, so that your voice be heard on high.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: bow down his head as a bulrush
Isaiah.english_translation: This *he* is [a letter] of astonishment; that is, “Is it to bow down his head like an *agmon* that I need?” The *agmon* is a kind of bent needle with which fish are caught, and it is called *aim* in Old French.
Isaiah.translator_note:
Old French *aim* (fish-hook, from Latin *hamus*): printed איי"ם; Darmesteter reads *aim* and glosses it “l’hameçon.”
JPS renders *agmon* as “bulrush”; Rashi takes it as a hook, so the translation keeps *agmon*.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Wilt thou call this a fast
Isaiah.english_translation: An expression of astonishment; therefore the *he* is vowelled with *ḥataf patah*.
An expression of tying and binding.
The turning aside of judgment.
Targum Yonatan: “And every perverted judgment ye shall remove.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the poor that are cast out
Isaiah.english_translation: Groaning and moaning over their distress, like “mine affliction and mine anguish” (Lamentations 3:19), “I am distraught in my complaint” (Psalm 55:3).
Isaiah.translator_note: Printed references: “Lamentations 3:19” and “Psalms 55”; the Psalm verse is 55:3.

Isaiah.english_translation: And from thy relative.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: thy light break forth as the morning
Isaiah.english_translation: Like the pillar of the dawn that breaks through the clouds.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: thy healing shall spring forth speedily
Isaiah.english_translation: And thy healing quickly, as “I will bring up healing (*arukhah*) for thee” (Jeremiah 30:17).
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s Hebrew *a‘aleh arukhah lakh* is not JPS’s wording; JPS renders Jeremiah 30:17 “For I will restore health unto thee.” The link is the word *arukhah*.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: draw out thy soul to the hungry
Isaiah.english_translation: With consolations of good words.
In a time of thirst and drought; so Targum Yonatan [renders].
He will arm, as in “armed for war” (*ḥaluṣei ṣava*, Numbers 31:5).
Isaiah.translator_note: The printed reference is “Numbers 31”; the phrase is in 31:5.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The restorer of paths to dwell in
Isaiah.english_translation: Yonatan translated: “One who returns the wicked to the Torah.”
Like *meshiv* [one who returns].
For the settlement (*yishuv*) of the world.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the heritage of Jacob thy father
Isaiah.english_translation: An inheritance without boundaries, as it is said, “and thou shalt spread abroad to the west, and to the east,” etc. (Genesis 28:14) — not like Abraham, of whom it is said, “the land which thou seest” (ibid. 13:15); and Jacob kept the Sabbath, as it is said, “and encamped before the city” (ibid. 33:18), for he fixed boundaries at twilight (*dimdumei ḥamah*). So explained R. Shimshon.
Isaiah.translator_note:
Printed references: “Genesis 28:14,” “ibid. 13” and “ibid. 33”; the verses are Genesis 13:15 and 33:18.
R. Shimshon is not further identified in the printed text.

Isaiah.english_translation: That you were not saved is not from the shortness of His hand.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: your sins have hid His face from you
Isaiah.english_translation: They caused Him to hide His face from you.
An expression of filth, and so “polluted bread” (Malachi 1:7).
Isaiah.translator_note: The printed reference is “Malachi 1”; the verse is 1:7.

Isaiah.english_translation: A kind of evil snake.
*Esclostrent* in Old French [“they hatch”]; that is, ugly deeds that are not for their good they did.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *esclostrent*: the printed form is אישקלורש"ט; Darmesteter reads *esclostrent* (“Ils font éclore”).

Isaiah.english_translation: *Irayne* in Old French [spider]; and *kurei* [is rendered] אורטור״ש in Old French. *Kurei* are the weaver’s implements in which the warp is woven, and Menaḥem joined it to the section of *korot* [beams], because the spider weaves its webs in beams.
Isaiah.translator_note:
Old French *irayne* (araignée): the printed form is אריניי"ש; Darmesteter reads *irayne*.
The second Old French word is printed אורטור"ש. Darmesteter’s gloss refers to a web whose warp is set (“ourdit la chaîne”) and records variant readings, so the exact form is uncertain. The word is left as printed.

Isaiah.english_translation: Targum Yonatan [renders] *meshaḥnan*, an expression of warming, which is called in Old French *couver* [to brood]; the one that warms them comes out of them when it breaks the shell. And the root sense of *ve-hazureh* is an expression of pressing, to bring out what is absorbed within it, like “and wrung” (*va-yazar*, Judges 6:38); and the pressing of this is its warming.
Isaiah.translator_note:
Old French *couver*: printed קובי"ר; Darmesteter reads *couver*.
The phrase “the one that warms them comes out of them” is ambiguous (the subject may be the one warmed or the one warming); rendered literally.
Judges 6:38 in JPS: “and wrung dew out of the fleece.”

Isaiah.english_translation: A kind of snake that is evil; so they will not be repaid for their deeds except with evil.
That is, in the circuit of their ways there is nothing judged truly according to its law.
They themselves perverted their way for themselves.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Therefore is justice far from us
Isaiah.english_translation: Because we were crying out “violence” against our enemies, and the Holy One, blessed be He, does not judge to take vengeance.
The good consolations that He promised us do not overtake us, to come.
We hope [for brightness], and in darkness we walk.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: in dark places like the dead
Isaiah.english_translation: Menaḥem explained it as an expression of dark places, and most of the interpreters agree with him. But Dunash explained it as an expression of fatness (*shoman*), and the *alef* is added in it, like the *alef* in *aḥvati* (Job 13:17) and in *akhzav* (Jeremiah 15:18) and in *derekh ha-atarim* (Numbers 21:1). So here too: among the fat ones, among the living who are fat, we are like the dead. And Targum Yonatan [renders] an expression of confinement: *itaḥad be-apna*, as graves are shut upon the faces of the dead.
Isaiah.translator_note:
The Aramaic (*itaḥad be-apna*) is garbled in the printed text; rendered as printed, with the explanatory clause after it translated literally.
Printed references: “Job 13,” “Jeremiah 15” and “Numbers 21”; the words are in Job 13:17 (JPS “my declaration”), Jeremiah 15:18 (“a deceitful brook”) and Numbers 21:1 (“by the way of Atharim”).

Isaiah.english_translation: An expression of wailing.
Like “to speak oppression.”

To shoot and to bring out. *Horo* is an expression of “He hath cast into the sea” (Exodus 15:4). Another explanation: *horo ve-hogu* — the master and the disciple, the name of the infinitive (*sa"a*); and *hogu* as “When he was removed out of the highway” (2 Samuel 20:13), “Take away the dross from the silver” (Proverbs 25:4).
Isaiah.translator_note:
The words “(*sa"a*)” are printed as an abbreviation that is not expanded; left as printed. The sentence beginning “Another explanation” is compressed; rendered literally.
Printed references: “Exodus 15:4,” “2 Samuel 20:13,” “Proverbs 25:4”; the JPS wording is used for all three.

Isaiah.english_translation: Our vengeance on our enemies, which is hanging on the Holy One, blessed be He; “and righteousness standeth afar off” — why? Because truth has stumbled in our broad places. And since truth has stumbled from the earth, even from heaven righteousness and judgment do not come.
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s wording has plural *birḥovoteinu* (“in our broad places”); the verse has singular “in the broad place.”

Isaiah.english_translation: He is held to be a fool among people, like “I will go stripped” (Micah 1:8); and it is from the stem of *shogeg* [error], which we render *shelu*; and so “for his error” (*al ha-shal*, 2 Samuel 6:7).
Isaiah.translator_note:
Rashi connects *meshotelel* and *shalal* (Micah 1:8) with the stem of *shegagah* (error); JPS Micah 1:8 reads “I will go stripped and naked.”
The printed reference is “2 Samuel 10”; the phrase *al ha-shal* is in 2 Samuel 6:7 (JPS “for his error”), so the printed letter appears to be a slip.

Isaiah.english_translation: Therefore He brought the punishment upon them.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: And He saw that there was no man
Isaiah.english_translation: And now, as He relents concerning the evil to His people, He sees that there is no righteous man to stand in the breach.

He is struck dumb, to see whether there is an intercessor for them, and there is no intercessor. *Va-yishtomem* is an expression for a man who stands, wonders and is silent in his amazement. And the *tav* of *va-yishtomem* is like the *tav* of *meshotelel*; both here serve the reflexive (*hitpa‘el*) form. And so is the way of a word whose first root letter is *shin* or *samekh*: when it turns to the reflexive form, *nitpa‘el* and *yitpa‘el*, the *tav* comes in the middle of the root letters of the word. It turns out that *va-yishtomem* is an expression of “Be astonished (*shamu*), O ye heavens” (Jeremiah 2:12), “appalled (*mashmim*) among them” (Ezekiel 3:15), “shall be astonished (*nashamu*) … they that come after” (Job 18:20) — an expression of amazement.
Isaiah.translator_note: Printed references: “Jeremiah 2:12,” “Ezekiel 3:15,” “Job 18:20.” JPS has Jeremiah 2:12 “Be astonished, O ye heavens,” Ezekiel 3:15 “appalled” and Job 18:20 “they that come after shall be astonished at his day.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: His own arm brought salvation unto Him
Isaiah.english_translation: And He will take vengeance on His enemies.
It supported Him, to lift Him and strengthen His hands in His vengeance, even though we are not worthy to save.
Isaiah.translator_note: The Hebrew ends *she-ein anaḥnu hegunim lehoshia‘* (“not worthy to save,” causative form); the sense may be “to be saved.” Rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_translation: *Enprenement* in Old French, to be zealous for His great Name.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French: the printed form is אינפרימנ"ט; Darmesteter glosses it “zèle” (zeal). The exact Old French form is uncertain (*emprennant* or *enprenement*); the sense is not in doubt.

Isaiah.english_translation: As is due, to repay for the recompenses of the enemies.
As is due, to repay upon them: He will repay.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: distress will come in like a flood
Isaiah.english_translation: Distress upon His enemies.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Which the breath of the LORD driveth
Isaiah.english_translation: Wonders in it — an expression of *nes* [miracle, banner]. Another explanation: *nosesah bo* — it eats in it like a worm in wood, as (above, 10) “And it shall be as when a sick man wasteth away.”
Isaiah.translator_note: Printed reference: “above 10”; the verse is Isaiah 10:18 (JPS “as when a sick man wasteth away”). Rashi reads *nosess* there as “consuming, as a worm.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: a redeemer will come to Zion
Isaiah.english_translation: As long as Zion is in ruins, the redeemer has not yet come. *Sa"a*.
Isaiah.translator_note: The printed text ends with the abbreviation *sa"a*, which is not expanded; left as printed.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: this is My covenant with them
Isaiah.english_translation: In this matter I made My covenant with them, and I will fulfil it: that even in their exile My Torah will not be forgotten from them.
On *gasasin*; on the loins of kings shall they be carried.
Isaiah.translator_note: The word *gasasin* is printed as is and its meaning is not clear; the rest is rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: thou shalt see and be radiant
Isaiah.english_translation: Then thou shalt see and thou shalt shine.
Isaiah.translator_note: This comment and the next three are in Aramaic and are printed without attribution.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: thy heart shall throb and be enlarged
Isaiah.english_translation: And it shall marvel, and thy heart shall be enlarged.
Isaiah.translator_note: The first verb has no expressed subject in the printed text; rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the abundance of the sea shall be turned unto thee
Isaiah.english_translation: For the wealth of the west shall pass over to thee.
Isaiah.translator_note: *Ma‘arva* (“west”) renders *yam* (“sea”), as the sea is the west of the Land. JPS: “shall be turned unto thee.”

Isaiah.english_translation: The possessions of the worshippers of the stars.
Abundance.
The *hugnei* of Midian are young camels (*gemalim beḥurim*), and so “a swift young camel” (*bikrah*, Jeremiah 2).
Isaiah.translator_note: *Hugnei* is left as printed. The printed reference is “Jeremiah 2”; the verse is 2:23 (JPS “a swift young camel”).

Isaiah.english_translation: They too are of the sons of Midian: “Ephah, and Epher” (Genesis 25:4).
Isaiah.translator_note: Printed reference: “Genesis 25:4.”

Isaiah.english_translation: Rams (*dikhrei*) of Nebaioth.

Like “as at first,” in the days of Solomon, as it is said (1 Kings 10:22), “For the king had at sea a navy of Tarshish … once every three years came the navy of Tarshish.” Tarshish is the name of the sea.
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s Hebrew has *oni Tarshish* (“a ship of Tarshish”); JPS renders “navy of Tarshish.” The quotation is abridged by Rashi (“etc.”).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the name of the LORD thy God
Isaiah.english_translation: Because it is called upon thee — for they will hear His fame, and the name of His might, and will come.
He has given thee glory (*pe’er*).
And in My being reconciled to thee, *en mon apaisement* in Old French.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *apaisement* (appeasement): the printed form is אימונ"א פייזמנ"ט; Darmesteter glosses it “Et dans mon apaisement.” The exact spelling of the Old French form in his note is hard to read.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Thy gates also shall be open
Isaiah.english_translation: An expression of “open,” on the pattern (*mishkolet*) of the heavy [intensive] form, because their opening is an everlasting opening, a perpetual opening, like *shever* from the expression of breaking (*shevirah*); so from the expression of opening, *tres overts* in Old French.
Isaiah.translator_note:
The grammatical explanation is compressed; rendered literally.
Old French *tresoverts* (“wide open”): the printed form is טי"ש אובירט"ש; Darmesteter reads *tresoverts*, noting that *tres-* strengthens the verb.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The cypress, the plane-tree and the larch
Isaiah.english_translation: Kinds of trees of the forest of Lebanon.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The Zion of the Holy One of Israel
Isaiah.english_translation: Zion in which the Holy One of Israel took delight; Zion of the Holy One of Israel.
Isaiah.translator_note: The first clause is in Aramaic.

Isaiah.english_translation: An expression of breasts, and “thou shalt suck” (*tinaki*) points to it.
That they took from thee.
And I will set thy leaders in peace, and thy rulers in merit.
Isaiah.translator_note: This comment is in Aramaic.

Isaiah.english_translation: Thy officers; and our Rabbis said: the visitations that came upon thee in thy exile, and the taskmasters who oppressed thee, shall be to thee for peace and for righteousness.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: no more thy light by day
Isaiah.english_translation: Thou wilt not need the light of the sun.
An expression of “withdraw their shining” (Joel 2:10) — they took in their light.
Isaiah.translator_note: Printed reference: “Joel 2”; the verse is 2:10.

Isaiah.english_translation: That I shall glory in them: *porvanter* in Old French.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *porvanter*: the printed form is פורוונטי"ר; Darmesteter reads *porvanter* and glosses it “Pour me glorifier.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: will hasten it in its time
Isaiah.english_translation: If they merit, I will hasten it; if they do not merit, [it will come] in its time.
Isaiah.translator_note: The bracketed words complete the sense; Rashi’s Hebrew has only “if they do not merit, in its time.”

Isaiah.english_translation: This anointing is nothing but an expression of rulership and greatness.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: To proclaim liberty to the captives
Isaiah.english_translation: That is, to announce to them the tidings of redemption.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the opening of the eyes to them that are bound
Isaiah.english_translation: Open their prey and the captives, and release them.
Isaiah.translator_note: The Hebrew (*pekaḥ et malkoḥam ve-shavim ve-hatiram*) is compressed and the first words are difficult; rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_translation: A year of appeasement and favour.
An expression of trees, as (above, 2) “of the terebinths which you have desired” (Isaiah 1:29); and “the planting of the LORD” points to it.
Isaiah.translator_note: The printed reference is “above 2”; the verse is Isaiah 1:29.

Isaiah.english_translation: Drivers of the plow.
Princes of the Holy One, blessed be He.
The possessions of the worshippers of the stars.
Isaiah.translator_note: This comment is in Aramaic, as at Isaiah 60:5.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: in their splendour shall you revel
Isaiah.english_translation: You shall enter in their place into the honour that they have taken until now.

Instead of your shame, which was double. “They too shall cry out ‘Confusion’” always, as their portion. That is: instead of what until now My people were always crying out, “Confusion is their portion.” There is a *rinnah* [cry] that is mourning, as in “Arise, cry out in the night” (Lamentations 2:19), and as in “And there went a cry” (1 Kings 22:36) — the cry of Ahab.
Isaiah.translator_note:
The opening is compressed and the relation of its clauses is not spelled out; rendered literally.
Printed reference: “1 Kings 22”; the verse is 22:36 (JPS “And there went a cry throughout the host”).

Isaiah.english_translation: For this reason He does not accept the burnt-offerings of the idolaters, for all of them are robbery.
Of Israel, that it be in truth; or “And I will give their recompense” — the reward for what they worked, because they bore the revilings of the idolaters for My honour — in truth.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: a bridegroom putteth on a priestly diadem
Isaiah.english_translation: Who puts on garments of glory like a high priest.
Her ornaments.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the earth bringeth forth her growth
Isaiah.english_translation: That brings forth her growth, etc.
Isaiah.translator_note: The lemma is cut off in the printed text; the comment is the continuation of the verse.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: will I not hold My peace
Isaiah.english_translation: I will act, and will not keep silent concerning what they did to her.
There shall be no peace before Me until her righteousness goes forth as brightness.
He will specify it.
Inhabited.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: a young man espouseth a virgin
Isaiah.english_translation: For as a lad dwells with a virgin, so shall thy sons dwell in thy midst.
Isaiah.translator_note: This comment is in Aramaic.

Isaiah.english_translation: Our Rabbis expounded it according to its plain meaning: angels who remind HaShem of its destruction, to rebuild it. What do they say? “Thou wilt arise, and have compassion upon Zion” (Psalm 102:14); “For the LORD hath chosen Zion” (ibid. 132:13), as it is stated in tractate Menaḥot. And Targum Yonatan [renders] “thy walls”: the early fathers who shield us like a wall.
Isaiah.translator_note: Printed references: “Psalms 102” and “ibid. 132”; the verses are 102:14 and 132:13.

Isaiah.english_translation: To write a book of remembrances, so that their merit not be forgotten before Me.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: They shall never hold their peace
Isaiah.english_translation: From mentioning their merit before Me.
The merit of the fathers.
Do not be silent.
It refers back to “thy corn.”
It refers back to “thy *tirosh*” [new wine].
Isaiah.translator_note: JPS (Isaiah 62:8) renders the word “thy wine.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Go through, go through the gates
Isaiah.english_translation: The prophet said: Pass over and return at the gates; turn the heart of the people to the right path.
Isaiah.translator_note: This comment is in Aramaic.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Cast up, cast up the highway
Isaiah.english_translation: Pave the way: *batez le chemin* in Old French. *Solu* is of the expression *mesillah* [highway].
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *batez le chemin*: the printed form is בטי"ץ לוקמי"ן; Darmesteter reads it as “Battez le chemin.”

Isaiah.english_translation: Clear the highway and cast the stumbling stones to the sides. *Sakelu* [“clear of stones”] is *espierrez* in Old French.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French: the printed form is אישפירייא"ן, which the manuscripts recorded by Darmesteter give in several variants; his gloss is “Otez-en les pierres” (remove the stones from it). The spelling *espierrez* is a modern normalisation; the sense is certain.

Isaiah.english_translation: So that there be no stone there. And against the evil inclination He says this; and it is also possible to explain it as the repair of the roads for the gathering of the exiles.
Isaiah.translator_note: The Hebrew *me-hayot sham even* is literally “from being a stone there.”

Isaiah.english_translation: A pole (*kelones*), *perche* in Old French. It is a sign that they shall gather to Me and bring to Me the exiles who are among them.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *perche* (pole): the printed form is פורקא; Darmesteter corrects it to *perche* (“Lire : pérche”) and glosses it “Étendard” (standard).

Isaiah.english_translation: That which is prepared to give to His servants is prepared with Him.
The reward for the work that they worked with Him is prepared before Him to give.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Who is this that cometh from Edom
Isaiah.english_translation: The prophet prophesied about what the Holy One, blessed be He, said, that He is destined to take vengeance on Edom, and that He Himself, in His glory, will slay their prince first, as the matter is stated above (34): “For My sword hath drunk its fill in heaven,” and afterwards “it shall come down upon Edom.” And “recognized in the fury of his face” — for He slew them with great slaughter. And the prophet speaks in the language of wars of human beings clothed in garments, and when they slay a slaughter the blood spatters on their garments, for so is the way of Scripture when speaking of the Presence (*Shekhinah*): in the manner of human beings, to “break the ear” [adapt to the ear] with what it is able to hear. And so “and His voice was like the sound of many waters”: the prophet likened His strong voice to the sound of many waters, to “break the ear” in the way it is possible for it to hear, since there is no understanding and no hearing the might of our God, to cause it to be heard as it is.
Isaiah.translator_note:
The last clause is compressed; rendered literally.
Printed reference: “above 34”; the verse is Isaiah 34:5 (JPS “For My sword hath drunk its fill in heaven; Behold, it shall come down upon Edom”).
The quotation “and His voice was like the sound of many waters” is not referenced in the printed text; the wording matches Ezekiel 43:2.
“To break the ear” is Rashi’s idiom for adapting speech to what the ear can bear.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Who is this that cometh from Edom
Isaiah.english_translation: Israel says, “Who is this,” etc. “Coming … crimsoned garments dyed with blood.” And anything that is revolting (*mitna’ets*) in its smell and in its appearance, the expression of *ḥimuts* is applied to it.
Isaiah.translator_note:
The word *mitna’ets* is difficult (it may be connected with *na’ats*, “to spurn”); the clause is rendered literally.
JPS renders *ḥamuts* “crimsoned.”

Isaiah.english_translation: Our Rabbis said: the prince of Seir is destined to err twice. He thinks that Bozrah is Bezer in the wilderness, which was a city of refuge, and he errs, because it receives only the one who killed inadvertently, whereas he killed Israel wilfully. And there is further an aggadic midrash: because Bozrah supplied a king for Seir at the death of its first king, as it is said, “And Jobab the son of Zerah of Bozrah reigned in his stead” (Genesis 36:33); and Bozrah is of Moab, as it is said, “upon Kerioth, and upon Bozrah” (Jeremiah 48:24).
Isaiah.translator_note: The verses are not referenced in the printed text; their wording matches Genesis 36:33 and Jeremiah 48:24, and Rashi refers to the city of refuge at Bezer (Deuteronomy 4:43).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: This that is glorious in his apparel
Isaiah.english_translation: (Who was) splendid in his clothing, and stooping, and girded in the greatness of his strength. And the Holy One, blessed be He, answers him: I am the one who rose before Me to speak in the righteousness of the fathers and in the righteousness of the generation of the distress; and My righteousness is also with them, and I was revealed to be great to save. And they say, Why red in Thy clothing? Why are Thy garments red?
Isaiah.translator_note:
This comment is obscure. “Who rose before Me” and “the generation of the distress” are rendered literally; the parenthesis (“Who was”) is as printed.
The closing words (*madua adom le-levushekha, madua bigdekha adumim*) paraphrase Isaiah 63:2 (JPS “Wherefore is Thine apparel red”).

Isaiah.english_translation: Standing before Me to fight.
Their blood, which is the strength and victory of a man.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I have stained all My raiment
Isaiah.english_translation: Like “polluted with blood” (Lamentations 4:14).
Isaiah.translator_note: Printed reference: “Lamentations 4.” Rashi’s *nig’alu ba-dam* matches JPS “They are polluted with blood.”

Isaiah.english_translation: For Israel.
An expression of silence; and I have already explained above, “And was astonished that there was no intercessor.”
Isaiah.translator_note: Isaiah 59:16.

Isaiah.english_translation: My wrath that I have against the nations — I was angry a little at My people, and they helped for evil — it upheld Me: it strengthened My hand and aroused My heart to exact punishment from them, although Israel are not worthy and fit for redemption.
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s wording matches Zechariah 1:15 (JPS “for I was but a little displeased, and they helped for evil”); the verse is not named in the printed text.

Isaiah.english_translation: An expression of wallowing in blood and treading with the feet, as in “wallowing in thy blood” (Ezekiel 16:6) and as in “They have trodden My portion under foot” (Jeremiah 12:10).
Isaiah.translator_note: Printed references: “Ezekiel 16:6” and “Jeremiah 12:10.”

Isaiah.english_translation: The might of their victory.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I will make mention of the mercies of the LORD
Isaiah.english_translation: The prophet said: I will remind Israel of the mercies of HaShem.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the great goodness toward the house of Israel
Isaiah.english_translation: I will mention what He bestowed on the house of Israel in His compassion.
Although it is revealed before Me that they will betray Me, nevertheless they are My people, and behold, they are before Me as sons who will not deal falsely.
That He brought upon them.

He did not afflict them according to their deeds, for which they deserved to be smitten, because the angel of His presence — he is Michael, the prince of the presence, who ministers before Him — saved them continually, by the mission of HaMakom [the Omnipresent].
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s lemma is the written form *lo tsar* (with *alef*, “not afflicted”), which he explains as “He did not afflict.” JPS follows the reading *lo* (“to Him”), “He was afflicted.”

Isaiah.english_translation: They provoked; like “you have been rebellious” (*mamrim heyitem*).
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s quotation matches Deuteronomy 9:7 and 9:24 (JPS “you have been rebellious against the LORD”); the printed text gives no reference.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: His people remembered the days of old, the days of Moses
Isaiah.english_translation: The prophet laments and says, in the language of supplication: today, in exile, His people remember the days of old, the days of Moses, and in their distress they say, “Where is Moses, our shepherd, who brought us up from the Red Sea?”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: With the shepherds of His flock
Isaiah.english_translation: The likeness of a shepherd who brings up his flock. “Where is He that put in the midst of Israel” the holy spirit of the Holy One, blessed be He, and taught us statutes and ordinances?

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: His glorious arm to go at the right hand of Moses
Isaiah.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He, used to lead the arm of His might at the right hand of Moses; at every time that he needed the help of the Holy One, blessed be He, His arm was ready at his right hand.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: As a horse in the wilderness
Isaiah.english_translation: That does not stumble because it is smooth ground; so they did not stumble in the deep.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the cattle that go down into the valley
Isaiah.english_translation: That goes down in a valley; and a valley (*bik‘ah*) is smooth ground with no obstacle: *canpanye* in Old French.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *canpanye* (plain): the printed form is קנפניי"א; Darmesteter reads *canpanye* and glosses it “Dans la plaine.”

Isaiah.english_translation: It will spread out, like (above, 45) “to subdue nations before him”; so the spirit of HaShem will set it down in the deep, and made a trodden path in it.
Isaiah.translator_note: Printed reference: “above 45”; the verse is Isaiah 45:1 (JPS “To subdue nations before him”). The Hebrew has “and made” as printed.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: So didst Thou lead Thy people
Isaiah.english_translation: So it was in everything, as we said: “Thou didst lead Thy people.”
The earlier [zeal].

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: The yearning of Thy heart and Thy compassions
Isaiah.english_translation: That used to yearn (*lehemot*) over us as of old, as it is said, “Therefore My heart yearneth for him” (Jeremiah 31:20); “and the multitude of Thy first compassions” toward us are now restrained, held back from yearning over us as of old.
Isaiah.translator_note: Printed reference: “Jeremiah 31:20.”

Isaiah.english_translation: Like “and he refrained himself, and said: Set on bread” (Genesis 43:31) — he restrained himself and did not recognise that his compassions were kindled toward his brother.
Isaiah.translator_note: The clause “and did not recognise” is printed as is; its object is not expressed. Rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_translation: And upon Thee it is to look and to see our troubles.
In the distress of Egypt.
In the wilderness, for they had already departed from the world.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Thou, O LORD, art our Father
Isaiah.english_translation: In all of them Thou didst become a father to us; and our Rabbis expounded it as they expounded in tractate Shabbat.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: why dost Thou make us to err from Thy ways
Isaiah.english_translation: For it is in Thy hand to remove the evil inclination, as it is said, “as the clay in the potter’s hand,” etc. (Jeremiah 18:6), and it says, “and I will take away the stony heart,” etc. (Ezekiel 36:26).
Isaiah.translator_note: The printed reference is “Jeremiah 18:4”; the quoted phrase is in 18:6. Ezekiel 36:26 is as printed.

Isaiah.english_translation: An expression of strengthening of the heart.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Thy holy people they have well nigh driven out
Isaiah.english_translation: Their greatness and their inheritance was theirs for a short time.
They trampled.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: We are become as they over whom Thou never borest rule
Isaiah.english_translation: Now we are like a people whom Thou didst not choose to rule over ever, and as if Thy name was not called upon them.
And come down to deliver us now, as Thou didst come down to deliver from the hand of Egypt; then “the mountains flowed down at Thy presence,” with trembling and quaking.
Isaiah.translator_note: JPS renders the clause as “the mountains might quake at Thy presence.” “With trembling and quaking” is Rashi’s addition.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the fire causeth the waters to boil
Isaiah.english_translation: As the burning of fire (*kedoaḥ esh*) — the thing that melts before it; and as the fire makes the water bubble (*tove‘ah*): when one puts a coal or a metal into water, the water raises bubbles. All this Thou didst in Egypt: “So there was hail, and fire flashing up in its midst” (Exodus 9:24). But Targum Yonatan [applies] “as fire kindleth the brush-wood” to Elijah at Mount Carmel, as it is said of him, “and licked up the water that was in the trench” (1 Kings 18:38).
Isaiah.translator_note:
The phrase Rashi comments on (*kiqdoaḥ esh ha-masim*) stands at the end of the preceding verse in JPS (Isaiah 63:19, “As when fire kindleth the brush-wood”); the verse division differs.
Printed reference: “1 Kings 15”; the quoted words are in 1 Kings 18:38 (JPS “and licked up the water that was in the trench”). Exodus 9:24: JPS “fire flashing up amidst the hail.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: To make Thy name known to Thine adversaries
Isaiah.english_translation: As is said in that same plague, “But in very deed for this cause have I made thee to stand,” etc. (ibid.): If Thou hadst done so now, then “the nations would tremble at Thy presence.”
Isaiah.translator_note: The reference “ibid.” is Exodus 9:16 (JPS “But in very deed for this cause have I made thee to stand, to show thee My power”).

Isaiah.english_translation: In Egypt and among all the enemies: awesome things that we did not hope Thou wouldest do for us, all those awesome things, for we were not worthy of it.
To Mount Sinai: then “the mountains flowed down at Thy presence.” So explained Dunash ben Labrat.
Isaiah.translator_note: JPS renders the clause “that the mountains might quake at Thy presence.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: from of old men have not heard
Isaiah.english_translation: Such awesome acts as were done for any of all the idolaters beforehand; “neither hath the eye seen a god beside Thee, who worketh for him that waiteth for Him” — what a god does for one who waits for him, [that] Thou didst for one who waits for Thee. So I heard from R. Yose *ve-ha-na’ani*. But our Rabbis, who said: All the prophets, all of them, prophesied only for the days of the Messiah, but for the World to Come, “the eye hath not seen,” etc. — its meaning is: the eye of no prophet has seen what the Holy One, blessed be He, will do for one who waits for Him, save Thine eyes, O God.
Isaiah.translator_note: The name “R. Yose *ve-ha-na’ani*” is printed as is and is not resolved here.

Isaiah.english_translation: Like “and he fell upon him, so that he died” (1 Kings 2): Thou didst remove from us and slay the righteous, who rejoiced to do righteousness; for the ways of Thy compassion they used to mention Thee in their prayer.
Isaiah.translator_note: Printed reference: “1 Kings 2”; the wording matches 2:25 (JPS “and he fell upon him, so that he died”).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Thou wast wroth, and we sinned
Isaiah.english_translation: When Thou wast wroth with us for all in which we had been sinning, from of old we were saved by their prayer; we were saved from of old.
An expression of the present.
After the righteous have departed from us.
And as a garment kept at a distance, as a loathsome garment of which all say, “Remove it”; *‘idim* is a Targum rendering of removal.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: we all do fade as a leaf
Isaiah.english_translation: And we shall wither like a leaf: *flaisdir* in Old French.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *flaisdir* (to wither; modern *flétrir*): the printed form is פליישט"ר; Darmesteter corrects it (“Lire : flaisdir”) and glosses it “Nous nous flétrirons.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: our iniquities, like the wind, take us away
Isaiah.english_translation: And through our sins, like the wind, we have been carried off.
Isaiah.translator_note: This comment is in Aramaic. The last word is printed abbreviated (איתנטילנ'); the rendering supplies the expected full form.

Isaiah.english_translation: Like one who overcomes his inclination.
And Thou hast caused us to move.
Isaiah.translator_note: The Hebrew is *vetaniy‘enu*.

Isaiah.english_translation: Wilt Thou be silent over what has been done to us? Up to here is the prayer of the prophet, and its beginning is “I will make mention of the mercies of the LORD” (63:7).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: to them that asked not for Me
Isaiah.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He, answers him: It is impossible not to take vengeance on them, for I was approachable to them, to rebuke them through My prophets, and they did not ask.
Isaiah.translator_note: The abbreviation (*a"a*) is read here as “it is impossible” (*i efshar*); this is the usual expansion but is not stated in the text.

Isaiah.english_translation: Return to Me, and behold, I am ready to receive.
Who did not desire to be called by My name.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I have spread out My hands
Isaiah.english_translation: In order to receive them in repentance.
Who turned aside from the way.
They set up idols in their gardens, and there they burn spices on the bricks.
So that an unclean spirit of demons (*shedim*) rest upon them.
They are the corpses of the dead, who are as though placed under siege and cannot go out.
An abominable gravy, like “and pour out the broth” (Judges 6:20).
Isaiah.translator_note: Printed reference: “Judges 6:20.”

Isaiah.english_translation: To the righteous: Draw near to thyself, stand by thyself, and do not approach me.
For I am more holy and pure than thou; so Targum Yonatan.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: These are a smoke in My nose
Isaiah.english_translation: The abomination that they did — behold, it is for a smoke of fury in My nose.
Their sin is before Me; their sentence has already been decreed and sealed.
Yours and your fathers’ together I will repay to you.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: when wine is found in the cluster
Isaiah.english_translation: Targum Yonatan [renders]: As Noah the righteous was found in the generation of the Flood.
This is Noah, who was sweet.
In the bereaved generation (*dor ha-meshukhal*); and one can explain it according to its plain meaning.
For the sake of every single righteous one who is found among them.
The name of a district that was in the Land of Israel.
According to its plain meaning.
The wicked of Israel who held fast to idolatry and died in their wickedness.
The name of an idol made after the name of the *mazal* [constellation, fortune]; and in the language of the Mishnah there are *gad*, *gadi* and *sinok* — no.
Isaiah.translator_note: The comment ends with a word that may be an abbreviation or a rejected reading (לא); the sentence is rendered literally.

Isaiah.english_translation: For the counting (*minyan*) of the reckoning, the priests (*komarim*) used to fill bowls of mixed wine.

Wine mixed with water according to its rule, as in “to try mixed wine” (Proverbs 23:30), “she hath mingled her wine” (ibid. 9:2). And some explain *lemani* as: to the idol that you have counted upon you; but *u-manitti etkhem*, which is not pointed (*she-lo nakud*) — *u-manitti* with a *dagesh* indicates that it is an expression of counting.
Isaiah.translator_note:
The last clause is compressed and its word *she-lo nakud* is unclear; rendered literally. The next verse (65:12) has *u-manitti etkhem* (JPS “will I destine you”).
Printed references: “Proverbs 23” and “ibid. 9”; the verses are 23:30 and 9:2.

Isaiah.english_translation: The righteous (of Israel).
Those who transgress against Me.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: leave your name for a curse
Isaiah.english_translation: He takes from your name a curse and an oath for the generations: “if it not befall us as it befell so-and-so.”
Eternal death.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: call His servants by another name
Isaiah.english_translation: A good name and a remembrance for blessing.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: he who blesseth himself in the earth
Isaiah.english_translation: For My awe will be upon all of them, and the earth shall be full of knowledge. And he who glories and praises himself in the earth shall bless himself by the God of truth — he shall glory that he is a servant of the God of truth, the God of truth, who confirmed and kept this promise.
Therefore they will call Me the God of truth.

The ministering princes above shall be renewed, and the princes of Israel shall be supernal princes and the princes of the nations lower; and so on the earth. And some say, new heavens literally, and so is the main view, for Scripture proves it: “For as the new heavens,” etc. (below, 66).
Isaiah.translator_note: Printed reference: “below 66”; the verse is Isaiah 66:22 (JPS “For as the new heavens and the new earth, which I will make”).

Isaiah.english_translation: A lad, like *‘olel* (Lamentations 2); *‘ul yamim*: small in years.
Isaiah.translator_note: Printed reference: “Lamentations 2” with no verse.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: shall die a hundred years old
Isaiah.english_translation: He shall be one liable to punishments (*ben ‘onshin*), to be liable to death for a transgression that carries death; so it is explained in *Bereshit Rabbah*.
For a transgression that requires excommunication (*niddui*).
Targum Yonatan [renders]: the Tree of Life.
And he will not need to destroy among the animals.

Behold, dust is his bread, readily available to him continually. And an aggadic midrash: “And the lion shall eat straw like the ox” — since we find that Esau falls into the hand of the sons of Joseph, as it is said, “And the house of Joseph a flame … and the house of Esau for stubble,” etc. (Obadiah 1:18), but into the hand of the sons of the other tribes, who were likened to beasts, we do not find this. Therefore it says, “and the lion shall eat straw like the ox”: those tribes that were likened to a lion, such as Judah and Dan, together with Joseph, who was likened to an ox, shall eat him who was likened to straw.
Isaiah.translator_note:
Rashi’s Hebrew order is “the house of Esau for stubble and the house of Joseph a flame” (*beit Esav le-kash u-veit Yosef lehavah*); JPS’s order is different, but the words are the same.
The likening of Joseph to an ox and of Judah and Dan to lions is not referenced in the printed text.

Isaiah.english_translation: I have no need of your Temple (*Beit ha-Mikdash*).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Where is the house that you may build unto Me
Isaiah.english_translation: That would be worthy of My Presence (*Shekhinah*).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: all these things hath My hand made
Isaiah.english_translation: The heavens and the earth My hand made this, and yet I contracted My Presence in your midst when you were obedient to Me, for thus is My way: to look to the poor and contrite of spirit, who trembles at My word.
