But now I have no desire in you, for behold, the slaughterer of the ox has struck its owner and robbed him of it; therefore he who sacrifices the lamb is, before Me, like one who breaks a dog’s neck; and he who offers the meal-offering, behold, he is before Me as swine’s blood; and he who “maketh a memorial-offering of frankincense” burns frankincense, as in “*azkarathah*” (Leviticus 5) and “that it may be to the bread for a memorial-part” (ibid. 24).
Isaiah.translator_note: Printed references: “Leviticus 5” and “ibid. 24”; the verses are Leviticus 5:12 (JPS “as the memorial-part thereof”) and 24:7 (JPS “that it may be to the bread for a memorial-part”).

Isaiah.english_translation: He blesses Me with a gift of coercion (*tashurat ones*): *mevarekh aven* [“one who blesses iniquity”] — from *mitashir ones* [“a gift of coercion”]; this is its interpretation. And the expression of blessing is used of a gift, which is for the receiving of favour, as “Take, I pray thee, my gift” (Genesis 33:11) and “Make a blessing with me, and come out to me.”
Isaiah.translator_note: Rashi’s Hebrew in Genesis 33:11 is *kaḥ na et birkhati* (“my blessing”); JPS renders “my gift.” The last quotation matches Isaiah 36:16 (JPS “Make your peace with me, and come out to me”); the printed text gives no reference.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: they have chosen their own ways
Isaiah.english_translation: They desire these evil ways, and I too will choose and desire their mockings. And if thou sayest, what is “also” here? It is the way of the Hebrew language to say two “also”s one next to the other, as in “both young man and virgin” (Deuteronomy 32:25), “both for me and for thee” (1 Kings 2), “both love and hatred” (Ecclesiastes 9:1), and the expression “and they shall not die, both they and ye” (Numbers 18:3). So here too: they too chose, and I too will choose.
Isaiah.translator_note:
The printed reference is “1 Kings 2”; the words *gam li gam lekha* are in 1 Kings 3:26 (JPS “It shall be neither mine nor thine”).
JPS Numbers 18:3 reads “that they die not, neither they, nor you.”

Isaiah.english_translation: To deal wantonly with them (*lihyot ‘olel bahem*) — an expression of “because thou hast mocked me” (ibid. 20).
Isaiah.translator_note: The printed reference is “ibid. 20”; the quoted words *ki hit‘allalta bi* are in Numbers 22:29 (JPS “Because thou hast mocked me”).

Isaiah.english_translation: That which they fear.
Hear, hearken, and return to Me.
Saying, “I have heard.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: You that tremble at His word
Isaiah.english_translation: The righteous, who hasten in trembling to draw near to His words.
The transgressors of Israel mentioned above. Another explanation: *amru aḥeikhem* — the ones who excommunicate you (*menaddeikhem*), who said to you, “Depart, unclean” (Lamentations 4:15).
Isaiah.translator_note: Printed reference: “Lamentations 4”; the quotation is in 4:15 (JPS “Depart you! unclean!”).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: cast you out for My name
Isaiah.english_translation: Those who say, “Draw near to thyself, do not approach me” (above, 65): “for My name’s sake — let the LORD be glorified.” In our greatness the Holy One, blessed be He, is glorified, since we are nearer to Him than you.
Isaiah.translator_note: Printed reference: “above 65”; the words are Isaiah 65:5 (JPS “Stand by thyself, Come not near to me”).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: That we may gaze upon your joy
Isaiah.english_translation: The prophet says: But it is not so, as their words; for “in your joy we shall see,” and they shall be ashamed. Why? Because the voice of their tumult comes before the Holy One, blessed be He, on account of what they did in His city, and a voice goes out from His Temple and accuses those who destroyed it; and afterwards, “the voice of the LORD that rendereth recompense to His enemies.”
Isaiah.translator_note: The speaker of “we shall see” is not stated in the printed text; rendered literally. The closing quotation is from Isaiah 66:6.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Before she travailed, she brought forth
Isaiah.english_translation: Zion, the pang of the woman in labour, gave birth to her sons; that is, her sons shall be gathered into her, who had been desolate of them and bereaved, and it is as though she had borne them now without the pangs of a woman giving birth, for all the idolaters will bring them into her.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: She was delivered of a man-child
Isaiah.english_translation: Every emergence of a thing that was enclosed is called *hamlatah*; and *hemlitah* is *esmucier* in Old French.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *esmucier* (to let escape): the printed form is אישקמוציי"ר; Darmesteter reads it as *esmucier* and glosses “Elle laisse échapper.” The same word is found in his notes on Numbers and Deuteronomy.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Is a land born in one day
Isaiah.english_translation: Does the pang come to a woman in labour, to bear a land full of sons in one day?

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: Shall I bring to the birth, and not cause to bring forth
Isaiah.english_translation: Shall I bring the woman to the birthstool (*mashber*) and not open her womb to bring out her fetus? That is: shall I begin a thing and not be able to finish it? Surely I am the one who delivers all who give birth, and now have I held back? — in astonishment.
An expression of breasts.
*Sucer* in Old French [to suck].
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *sucer*: the printed form is שוציי"ר; Darmesteter reads *suçer* and glosses “Pour que vous suciez.”

Isaiah.english_translation: From great glory that is moving and stirring to come to her.
*Esmovement* in Old French [movement].
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *esmovement*: the printed form is אישמובימנ"ט; Darmesteter corrects it (“Lire : ésmovement”) and glosses “Du mouvement de sa gloire.”

Isaiah.english_translation: I extend to her the glory of the nations.
On the sides of your nurses — on *gisisin*.
Isaiah.translator_note: The word *gisisin* is printed as is (see also Isaiah 60:4) and its exact meaning is not clear.

Isaiah.english_translation: You shall be fondled, as one fondles the infant: *esbanier* in Old French.
Isaiah.translator_note: Old French *esbanier* (to amuse, to fondle): the printed form is אישבניי"ר; Darmesteter reads *esbanéiér* and glosses “Vous serez choyés.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the hand of the LORD shall be known toward His servants
Isaiah.english_translation: When He carries out His vengeances and His awesome acts, His servants will know the strength of the might of His hand.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: the LORD will come in fire
Isaiah.english_translation: He will come in fiery wrath upon the wicked.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: To render His anger with fury
Isaiah.english_translation: To repay to His adversaries, in fury, His anger.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: For by fire will the LORD contend
Isaiah.english_translation: “By fire” of Gehinnom HaShem enters into judgment (*nishpat*) with His adversaries; and since He is both litigant and judge, the expression *nishpat* is used of Him, for He also argues His claims to find their iniquity and transgression, and so “and I will plead against him” (Ezekiel 38:22), “Behold, I will enter into judgment with thee” (Jeremiah 20:4). It is an expression of disputation: *deraisnier* in Old French. And its plain sense: “for by the fire of HaShem and by His sword all flesh is judged”; and so many [verses] are transposed in Scripture.
Isaiah.translator_note:
The printed reference is “Jeremiah 20:4”; the words are in Jeremiah 2:35 (JPS “Behold, I will enter into judgment with thee”).
Old French *deraisnier* (to plead, to dispute): the printed form is דרישניי"ר; Darmesteter reads *déraisniér* and glosses “Dieu entre en contestation, sens de plaider.”

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: They that sanctify themselves and purify themselves
Isaiah.english_translation: Those who agree among themselves: “I and you will go on such-and-such day to worship such-and-such idol.”
For they sowed vegetables there, and there they set up idols.
As Yonatan translated: “a company after a company, sanctifying and purifying themselves to serve a company after the one whose fellow had finished its service.”
In the middle of the garden; so was their way to set it up.

And I — what is it for Me to do? Their works and their thoughts have come before Me, and it will oblige Me to gather all the nations and to make known that their works are vanity, and that their thoughts, which they think, “for (My) name’s sake let the LORD be glorified,” they will understand to be false. And where is that gathering? It is the ingathering that Zechariah prophesied: “I will gather all the nations to Jerusalem” (Zechariah 14:2).
Isaiah.translator_note: The word “(My)” is in parentheses in the printed text. JPS Zechariah 14:2 reads “For I will gather all nations against Jerusalem to battle.”

Isaiah.english_translation: When I fight against them with the plague of the rotting of their flesh, their eyes and their tongue (ibid.).
Isaiah.translator_note: The reference “ibid.” is Zechariah 14:12 (JPS “Their flesh shall consume away while they stand upon their feet, And their eyes shall consume away in their sockets, And their tongue shall consume away in their mouth”).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: I will work a sign among them
Isaiah.english_translation: Survivors will escape the war, and I will leave them in order that they go and announce to the distant isles My glory that they saw in the war; and even among those survivors I will place one of the signs by which their fellows were judged, in order to make known to the distant ones, “By this plague those who gathered against Jerusalem were smitten.”
They are wagons arranged with partitions and a tent; and similar to it: “six covered wagons” (Numbers 7:3).
Isaiah.translator_note: Printed reference: “Numbers 7:3.”

Isaiah.english_translation: With song they play and dance, as in “and David danced” (2 Samuel 6:14): *treper* in Old French. And Menaḥem explained it as an expression of a lamb (*kebes*), as in “Send you the lambs for the ruler of the land” (above, 16).
Isaiah.translator_note:
Old French *treper*: the printed form is טריפי"ר; Darmesteter reads *treper*.
Printed references: “2 Samuel 6:14” and “above 16” (Isaiah 16:1).

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: bring their offering in a clean vessel
Isaiah.english_translation: A meal-offering in a clean vessel, for acceptance; so shall they bring your brethren as an offering of acceptance.

Isaiah.english_lemma_JPS: of them also will I take for the priests
Isaiah.english_translation: From the nations that bring them, and from those who are brought, I will take priests and Levites; and before Me the priests and Levites among them are revealed, and I will choose them from among them, and they shall minister before Me.
And where did He say it? “The secret things belong unto the LORD our God” (Deuteronomy 29:28). So it is explained in Aggadat Tehillim.
Isaiah.translator_note: The connection between the comment and the lemma is not spelled out; rendered literally. The work named is *Aggadat Tehillim* (the midrash on Psalms).

Isaiah.english_translation: The maggot that eats their flesh.
In Gehinnom.
An expression of contempt; and Targum Yonatan [renders] like two words, *di re’iyah*, until the righteous say about them, “*Misat*, we have seen.”
Isaiah.translator_note: The Aramaic *di* means “enough” and *re’iyah* means “seeing”; the word *misat* is as printed.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: The words of Jeremiah the son of Hilkiah
Jeremiah.english_translation: Let a son of a corrupt [woman], whose deeds are upright — Jeremiah, who came from Rahab the harlot — come and rebuke the sons of the upright, whose deeds are corrupt: these are Israel, who corrupted their deeds although they came from fitting seed.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The first sentence is in Aramaic.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: to whom the word of the LORD came
Jeremiah.english_translation: In which the Presence (*Shekhinah*) began to rest upon him at that time.

And he was a prophet all the remaining days of Josiah, and the days of Jehoiakim his son, and the days of Zedekiah his son, until the end of the eleventh year, which is the year until the exile of Jerusalem in the fifth month.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Rashi’s “his son” is repeated as printed; the verse names Jehoiakim and Zedekiah as sons of Josiah.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Before I formed thee in the belly
Jeremiah.english_translation: From the days of Adam the first, the Holy One, blessed be He, showed Adam each generation and its prophets.
An expression of form.
*Conoistre* in Old French [to know], as in “I made Me not known to them” (Exodus 6:3).
Jeremiah.translator_note:
Old French: the printed form is קנייושט"וי. It is not in Darmesteter’s glossary, so the exact form is uncertain; the reading *conoistre* follows the sense given by the verse Rashi cites.
Rashi’s Hebrew *lo nodati lahem* matches JPS “I made Me not known to them.”

Jeremiah.english_translation: I designated thee for this.

To Israel, who were conducting themselves like idolaters. So it is expounded in the Sifrei: “A prophet from the midst of thee,” etc. (Deuteronomy 18:15) — “He will raise up for thee,” and not for those who deny the Torah. How then do I fulfil “a prophet to the nations”? “I have given thee among the children of Israel, who were behaving like idolaters.” Another explanation: “Before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee” — about thee I said to Moses, “I will raise them up a prophet … like unto thee” (Deuteronomy 18:18): this one rebuked them and that one rebuked them; this one prophesied forty years and that one prophesied forty years.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Rashi’s quotations are abridged: Deuteronomy 18:15 in JPS reads “A prophet will the LORD thy God raise up unto thee, from the midst of thee, of thy brethren, like unto me.” His “I will raise up a prophet for them like unto thee” abridges 18:18.

Jeremiah.english_translation: An expression of wailing: *conpleint* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French *conpleint* (complaint): the printed form is קונפליינ"ט; Darmesteter reads *conpléint* (from *cum* + *planctus*).

Jeremiah.english_translation: I am not fit to rebuke them. Moses rebuked them near his death, when he had already been esteemed in their eyes through the many miracles he did for them: he took them out of Egypt, split the sea for them, brought down the manna, caused the quail to come, gave them the Torah, brought up the well. I, at the beginning of my mission, come to rebuke them.
To the idolaters.
To Israel thou shalt speak.
Any sending that is by the hand is an expression of extending. Another explanation, as the Targum: “And the LORD sent forth the words of his prophecy.”
Jeremiah.translator_note: The abbreviation *l"a* is read here as “another explanation.”

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: I have this day set thee
Jeremiah.english_translation: I appointed thee over the idolaters.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: To root out and to pull down
Jeremiah.english_translation: *Despecier* in Old French [to break to pieces].
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French *despecier*: the printed form is דיספציר; it is not in Darmesteter’s glossary, but the form is clear.

Jeremiah.english_translation: *Amendlier* in Old French [almond tree]; and Yonatan translated “a rod of an almond-tree”: a king who smites for evil.
Jeremiah.translator_note:
Old French *amendlier* (almond tree): the printed form is מנדולי"ר; Darmesteter reads *améndlier*.
The Aramaic of Yonatan (*melekh de-moḥei le-avasha*) is rendered literally; the first word is as printed.
The site’s JPS text of this verse reads “aalmond-tree”; this is noted in the review.

Jeremiah.english_translation: This almond tree is quick to put forth blossom before all the trees; so too I am quick to carry out My word. And an aggadic midrash: this almond, from the time of its setting until the completion of its ripening, is twenty-one days, like the number of days between the seventeenth of Tammuz, on which the city was breached, and the ninth of Av, on which the Temple was burned.
Boiling: *bouillant* in Old French.
Its boilings: אשישאונדי"ש in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Old French word is printed אשישאונדי"ש; it is not in Darmesteter’s glossary and its exact form is uncertain, so it is left as printed.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Out of the north the evil shall break forth
Jeremiah.english_translation: Babylon is to the north of the Land of Israel.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: I will utter My judgments against them
Jeremiah.english_translation: I will contend with them, with Judah and Jerusalem.
An expression of urging, like a man of valour.
Against the kings of Judah.
And they will be contending and stirring against thee, to conceal the words of thy prophecy.
Jeremiah.translator_note: This comment is in Aramaic (a Targum-style rendering), printed without attribution.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: I remember for thee the affection of thy youth
Jeremiah.english_translation: If you were returning to Me, I would long to have compassion on you, because thou didst remember the lovingkindness of thy youth, and the love of thine espousals, for I brought thee into the bridal canopy; and it is an expression of bringing in. *Kelulotayikh* [thine espousals]: *noces* in Old French. And what is “the lovingkindness of thy youth”? Thy going after the emissaries of Moses and Aaron: from an inhabited land you went out to the wilderness with no provisions for the way, because you believed in Me.
Jeremiah.translator_note:
The printed *zakharta* (“thou didst remember”) differs from the verse’s *zakharti* (“I remember”); it is rendered as printed.
Old French *noces* (wedding): the printed form is נוצי"ש; Darmesteter reads *noces* and glosses “Tes noces.”

Jeremiah.english_translation: Like a heave-offering (*terumah*).
Like the first of the harvest before the Omer, which is forbidden to be eaten, and whoever eats it is liable; so all who eat of it shall be held guilty; so Targum Yonatan.
For we shall go after other gods.
*Planure* in Old French [plain].
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Old French form, printed פלנור"א, is transparent; it is not in Darmesteter’s glossary.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Inclined: אינפוושיא"ה in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Old French word is printed אינפוושיא"ה; it is not in Darmesteter’s glossary and its exact form is uncertain, so it is left as printed.

Jeremiah.english_translation: דישגאט"ה in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Old French word is printed דישגאט"ה; it is not in Darmesteter’s glossary and its exact form is uncertain, so it is left as printed.

Jeremiah.english_translation: An expression of darkness.
“Unto the land of Carmel”: to the Land of Israel, which was planted like a Carmel [orchard]. He explained: planted like a forest.
Jeremiah.translator_note:
The lemma is blank in the printed text; the lemma phrase, *el eretz ha-Karmel*, stands at the head of the comment.
The first sentence is in Aramaic, in the manner of the Targum.

Jeremiah.english_translation: The Sanhedrin.
The kings.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Hebrew word is *ha-ro‘im* (“the shepherds”).

Jeremiah.english_translation: In the name of Baal.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: I will yet plead with you
Jeremiah.english_translation: Before I bring evil upon you, I will contend with you again through My prophet, even though I have already contended with you for many days.
To the isles of the Kittim.
*Isles* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French *isles* (islands): the printed form is אישל"ש; Darmesteter reads *isles*.

Jeremiah.english_translation: And to Kedar send, to see their custom.
And pay attention to look at the matter well.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: if there hath been such a thing
Jeremiah.english_translation: Like “if”: if a nation has exchanged its god, though they are not gods, and My people have exchanged their glory, in which they were honoured. And the Kittim and the Kedarites are tent-dwellers and shepherds of livestock, travelling and going and moving about from pasture to pasture and from wilderness to wilderness, and they carry their gods with them to the place where they encamp; yet I carried you until I settled you, and you left Me. So Targum Yonatan. And our Rabbis said: the Kittim worship water and the Kedarites worship fire, and although they know that water extinguishes fire, they did not abandon their gods.
In an idol in which there is no benefit.
An expression of amazement, like “be appalled” (*hishtomemu*); and it is an imperative expression, like “If they say thus unto us: Tarry” (1 Samuel 14:9).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed reference: “1 Samuel 14:9.”

Jeremiah.english_translation: An expression of *sa‘ar* [storm].
As if you were being laid waste over the Temple, which is destined to be destroyed.

If they had exchanged their fear for the like of it, there would be one evil here; but now that they have forsaken Me, who am a source of living waters, to go after the idolaters, who are like cisterns of collected waters that break and crack and whose waters are swallowed up in their cracks — behold, two evils.
To dig.
*Tendront* in Old French [“shall hold”] their waters, for the waters wear away their rim and their walls, and they fall.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French *tendront*: the printed form is טינדרונ"ט; Darmesteter gives *tendront* and glosses “Ne tiendront plus.”

Jeremiah.english_translation: The son of the maidservant.
*Sho’agim* [roaring] — an expression of the present.
Kings.
They were set on fire.
They are the Egyptians, on whom you rely for help.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Feed upon the crown of thy head
Jeremiah.english_translation: An expression of crushing, as we translate *ve-ratsots* [“and crushed”]: *ve-ra‘u*.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Aramaic rendering is quoted without a verse reference.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Is it not this that doth cause it unto thee
Jeremiah.english_translation: Surely this evil and this punishment — the guilt and the iniquity of thy having forsaken the LORD thy God — cause it to thee.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: When He led thee by the way
Jeremiah.english_translation: For He was teaching thee the good and upright way.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: what hast thou to do in the way to Egypt
Jeremiah.english_translation: Why wouldst thou forsake Me and trust in Egypt?
For your males drowned in the Nile. Shihor is the Nile, as it is said, “from the Shihor which is before Egypt” in the Book of Joshua (13:3).
To rebel against Me, that thou mayest be exiled to the way of Assyria, to the crossing of the river Euphrates.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Thine own wickedness shall correct thee
Jeremiah.english_translation: In the end, thy wickedness will bring sufferings upon thee.
An expression of “backsliding children” (below, 3).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed reference: “below 3”; the words are Jeremiah 3:14 (JPS “Return, O backsliding children”).

Jeremiah.english_translation: An expression of chastisement (*musar*).

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Neither is My fear in thee
Jeremiah.english_translation: My fear was not in thy heart, to fear Me.
The yoke, which is of wood, takes an expression of breaking; and the bands, which are of leather, take an expression of tearing.
They are the straps with which the yoke is tied.
Upon thy words.
But thou didst not keep thy promise, and upon every hill thou art stretched out (*tso‘ah*) — an expression of lying down and a couch; for *ki* serves in the sense of *ela* [“but”].

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: I had planted thee a noble vine
Jeremiah.english_translation: *Sorek* is the branches of a good vine; that is, the sons of upright and righteous fathers. And its midrash: “I planted thee *sorek*” — I added to thee, beyond the seven commandments of the sons of Noah, six hundred and six, the numerical value of *sorek*.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The numerical value of *sorek* (300 + 6 + 200 + 100) is 606; with the seven commandments of the sons of Noah, 613.

Jeremiah.english_translation: *Destoltures* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French *destoltures*: the printed form is דישטורלטור"ש; Darmesteter reads *destolture* (from *destolir*, “to remove”) and glosses the phrase “Branches bâtardes de vigne sauvage.”

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Of a strange vine unto Me
Jeremiah.english_translation: That which grows in forests.
A kind of earth with which they wash and scour garments.
Cleanness, as in “and a pure heart” (Psalm 24:4); and some of the vernacular speakers [say] that *borit* is *savon* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed reference: “Psalms 24:4.”

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: thine iniquity is marked before Me
Jeremiah.english_translation: Behold, as the mark of a stain that is not clean, so are thy sins many before Me.
Jeremiah.translator_note: This comment is in Aramaic.

Jeremiah.english_translation: A stain: *taye* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French *taye* (stain; modern *taie*): the printed form is טאק"א; Darmesteter corrects it (“Lire : taye”) and glosses “Une tache.”

Jeremiah.english_translation: It is said of the iniquity of the calf that it endures for ever, as it is said, “And in the day when I visit, I will visit their sin upon them” (Exodus 32:34); every visitation that comes upon Israel will have in it a part of the iniquity of the calf.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed reference: “Exodus 32:34.”

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: See thy way in the Valley
Jeremiah.english_translation: What thou didst opposite Beth-peor; and even now thou holdest to that way, like a swift young camel that intertwines her ways.

A female camel, a young one, who loves to move about. “The young camels of Midian” (Isaiah 60:6) is translated *hugnei* of Midian, and they are young camels, as we find in Sanhedrin: “Many are the old camels laden with the skins of *hugni*.”
Jeremiah.translator_note:
The Sanhedrin passage is quoted in Aramaic; the tractate is named without a page.
See Isaiah 60:6 above.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Holding fast to the ways of her youth. An expression of *masrikh sarikh*. And one may connect it with “shoe-latchet” (Genesis 14:23): she binds the ways of her youth in her heart.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed reference: “Genesis 14:23.”

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: A wild ass used to the wilderness
Jeremiah.english_translation: שלוואטיק"ו in Old French; and some of the vernacular speakers [say] קוליי"ן in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Both Old French words are printed as given (שלוואטיק"ו and קוליי"ן); neither is in Darmesteter’s glossary and the exact forms are uncertain, so they are left as printed.

Jeremiah.english_translation: One accustomed to being in wildernesses; so she loves to move about.
She opens her mouth and pants for wind, and it always returns to its place.

That same trait of the *tanin* which is in her, for the *tanin* also pants for wind, as it is said, “they gasp for air like jackals” (Jeremiah 14:6); “who can hinder it” from that trait? So you — who can turn you back from your evil way?
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed reference: “Jeremiah 14.” JPS renders the animal in 14:6 as “jackals”; Rashi’s word is *tanin*.

Jeremiah.english_translation: For in vain they will weary themselves, since they cannot overtake her; and what is her end? “In her month they shall find her”: there is one month in the year in which she sleeps all the month, and then she is caught. So too you: one month (it is Av) has been prepared for you since the days of the spies, when your fathers fixed a weeping in vain; in it you shall be caught. *Ta’anatah*: *son dagronement* in Old French; and so Targum Yonatan: *kirud’a*. Another explanation: an expression of wailing, like “mourning and moaning” (*ta’aniyah va-aniyah*, Lamentations 2). Another version: שאקונטריא"ה in Old French, like “Taanath-shiloh” (Joshua 16).
Jeremiah.translator_note:
Old French *dagronement* (rut): the printed form is שו"ן דגרונמינ"ט; Darmesteter reads *son dagronement* (from *dagron*, “dragon,” by metathesis) and glosses “Son rut.” The second Old French word, שאקונטריא"ה, is not in Darmesteter’s glossary and is left as printed. The Aramaic *kirud’a* is as printed.
The words “(it is Av)” are in parentheses in the printed text.
Printed references: “Lamentations 2” (verse 5, JPS “Mourning and moaning”) and “Joshua 16” (verse 6).

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Withhold thy foot from being unshod
Jeremiah.english_translation: This is thy trait, like a wild ass that loves to move about. My prophets say to thee: Withhold thyself from idolatry, that thou not walk barefoot in exile, and withhold thy throat from dying of thirst; and thou sayest, in answer to the words of the prophets, “*no’ash*, there is no concern”: I have despaired of your words. *No’ash* — *nonchaloir* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French *nonchaloir* (not to care): the printed form is נוקליי"ר; Darmesteter reads it as *nonchaloir* and glosses “Point ne me chaut.”

Jeremiah.english_translation: At first, when he is found to be a thief and he had been held trustworthy; so Targum Yonatan.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: in the time of their trouble
Jeremiah.english_translation: To Me: “Arise, and save us.” And so Targum Yonatan: “And at the time that evil comes upon them they deny their idols and confess before Me, and say: Have compassion upon us and redeem us.”

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: according to the number of thy cities
Jeremiah.english_translation: In every single city, a different god.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Wherefore will you contend with Me
Jeremiah.english_translation: How will you come to dispute in contention and say, “We have not sinned”?

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: You all have transgressed against Me
Jeremiah.english_translation: Even the righteous are implied; this is what people say: “Along with the thorn, the cabbage is smitten.”
Jeremiah.translator_note: The proverb is in Aramaic (*be-hadei hotsa laki karva*). “Thorn” and “cabbage” translate its two nouns; the printed text gives no explanation.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: In vain have I smitten your children
Jeremiah.english_translation: For nothing, for it did not help that they would take chastisement.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Your sword hath devoured your prophets
Jeremiah.english_translation: Your prophets; you killed Zechariah and Isaiah.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: see you the word of the LORD
Jeremiah.english_translation: He brought out for them the jar of manna; He said to them, “See here what the word of HaShem avails.” “Have I been a wilderness unto Israel?” It is an expression of astonishment; therefore the *mem* is pointed *rafeh* and the *he* with *ḥataf patah*. Did it seem to your fathers that it was a wilderness, when they walked in it, when I brought down for them bread, this “day's portion every day”?
Jeremiah.translator_note: Rashi’s quotation “*davar yom be-yomo*” matches Exodus 16:4 (JPS “a day’s portion every day”).

Jeremiah.english_translation: An expression of darkness.

We have separated from Thee, like one who takes bread out of the oven. So is the midrash of Rabbi Tanḥuma; and Menaḥem explained *radnu* as an expression of descent, and there are other aspects as well.
Thou adornest thyself to meet thy adulterers, like “and attired her head” (2 Kings 9) of Jezebel in the section of Jehu.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed reference: “2 Kings 9”; the verse is 9:30.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Thou wentest around every evil way to learn the most corrupt of them all.
An expression of “even.” *Lakhen*: an expression of an oath of truth — “Truly, the evil way among all the ways thou hast taught thyself.”
Thou hast conducted.
Thou didst not find them in a tunnel when thou killedst them.
So it is said to a female: an expression of *pa‘alt* [“thou didst”]; and there are many in the Book (Ezekiel 16:58): “thou hast borne them” (*at nesa’tim*).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed reference: “Ezekiel 16:58”; JPS: “Thou hast borne thy lewdness and thine abominations.”

Jeremiah.english_translation: For they were rebuking thee with these words.
In thy heart.
That I am innocent, my soul.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Hebrew (*asher zakkah ani nafshi*) is as printed; rendered literally.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: I will enter into judgment with thee
Jeremiah.english_translation: I will come with thee into judgment.
An expression of contempt (*zilzul*).
To leave Me and rely on Egypt for help, in the days of Jehoiakim and Zedekiah (below, 36).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed reference: “below 36,” left as printed.

Jeremiah.english_translation: An expression of change.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: As thou wast ashamed of Asshur
Jeremiah.english_translation: For Ahaz relied on him, and he distressed him and did not strengthen him, as it is said (2 Chronicles 28).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed reference: “2 Chronicles 28”; the verse is 28:20 (JPS “and distressed him, but strengthened him not”).

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: If a man put away his wife
Jeremiah.english_translation: I have the right to say that thou art no longer fit for Me; for such is the way of one who sends away his wife, and she goes from him, etc.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: But thou hast played the harlot with many lovers
Jeremiah.english_translation: With many lovers; and nevertheless, return to Me.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: wouldest thou yet return to Me
Jeremiah.english_translation: Like “to do” and “to return to Me”: I am occupied with thee.
Jeremiah.translator_note: This short comment is compressed and its grammatical point is not spelled out; rendered literally.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Streams of water.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Hebrew is *yivlei mayim*. JPS renders *shefayim* “high hills.”

Jeremiah.english_translation: An expression of concubine (*pilegesh*).
To be ready to meet them.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: As an Arabian in the wilderness
Jeremiah.english_translation: A tent-dweller, who is always found outside, in wildernesses; and for this reason he is called an *Aravi*, for he dwells in the *aravah*.
Like the rain that falls in Nisan on the ears of grain and on the stalks; and *malkosh* is *tardive* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Old French form, printed טרדיו"א, is transparent; it is not in Darmesteter’s glossary.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Would that thou wouldst turn from thy evil and call Me “My father”; and if thou doest so, will thy Master bear a grudge for ever against thee for that which thou hast sinned against Him? “Will He keep it for ever?” He will not keep it.
With thy mouth: “We will not come any more to Thee,” and that same evil thou doest, and thou dost not set thy heart to return.
And thou hast prevailed to rebel.

Thou hast prevailed and art proven, in the days of Josiah the king, when He commanded me to return the ten tribes: “Hast thou seen what backsliding Israel did?” The backsliding one (*ha-shovavah*): *enveyséde* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note:
The first phrase (*nitzaḥat u-mukhaḥat*) is difficult in the printed text; rendered literally.
Old French *enveyséde* (“the seduced one”): the printed form is אנבוזייא"ה; Darmesteter reads *enveyséde* (from *invitiata*) and glosses “La séduite.”

Jeremiah.english_translation: The ten tribes.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: she went up upon every high mountain
Jeremiah.english_translation: While she was still on her land, before she was exiled, in the days of Hezekiah, with Hoshea son of Elah.
She was going upon every high hill.
To idolatry. And *va-tizni* is like *va-tizen*; the *yod* is extra.
Through My prophets Amos and Hosea the son of Beeri and the other prophets: “She will return to Me.”

All of this: *bogedah* [treacherous] is harsher than *meshuvah* [backsliding]. Israel, who were first to corruption and did not see a punishment from which to learn and to return, are called *meshuvah*; Judah, who saw that these were exiled and did not take chastisement, are called *bogedah*.

The accents of this verse teach its explanation: “Israel” is pointed with a disjunctive *zakef*; *shilḥatiha* is pointed with a *zakef gadol* by itself. And this is its explanation: “And I saw” — I looked at her to exact punishment from her. And why? “For on all the accounts that backsliding Israel committed adultery.” And what was My vengeance? “I put her away from My presence.” “And treacherous Judah feared not,” who had seen the punishment of Samaria, to set her heart to return.
And she erred with the worshippers of stones and trees. And Targum Yonatan [renders] *mikkol zenutah* as an expression of lightness, since her errors were light in her eyes.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Aramaic *ta‘avatha* can mean “her errors” or “her idols.”

Jeremiah.english_translation: For they saw the punishment in the corruption of their fellows.

The generation of Josiah showed themselves to be righteous, and they were wicked: they engraved forms of idols on their doors from the inside, half on this one and half on that one, and when the idol-eradicators searched, the door was open and they did not recognise it.
She cleared herself and exempted herself from the judgment, for she had no one from whom to learn.

*Haloch* — as its Targum has it, *azil* — is an expression of command. Here He commanded him to go and return the ten tribes in the days of Josiah, as He said above, that in the days of Josiah this prophecy was spoken to him; and some of them returned in the eighteenth year of Josiah.
To the places where they were exiled, in Assyria.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: I will not frown upon you
Jeremiah.english_translation: My anger; so Targum Yonatan.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Hebrew is *panai* (“My face”).

Jeremiah.english_translation: Thou hast rebelled.
An expression of harlotry — spreading of the legs for a woman’s couches.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The last phrase is rendered literally.

Jeremiah.english_translation: *Enveysir* in Old French, for you turned your way astray from the abundance of all that you were in, in ease and pleasure, as He says, “That thrum on the psaltery” (Amos 6:5), “That drink wine in bowls” (ibid.).
Jeremiah.translator_note:
Old French: the printed form is אנווישיי"ר; Darmesteter reads *énveyséç* (from *invitiatus*) and glosses it “Égarés” (led astray).
Printed reference: “Amos 7”; the verses are Amos 6:5 and 6:6. Rashi’s *ha-portim* is rendered with JPS “That thrum.”

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: for I am a lord unto you
Jeremiah.english_translation: And you will be called by My name, for I am master of you, and it is not My honour to leave you in the hand of My enemies.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: The ark of the covenant of the LORD
Jeremiah.english_translation: For your whole entering shall be holy, and I will dwell in it as though it were an ark.
Like *yizkeru* [“they shall remember”].

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: neither shall it be made any more
Jeremiah.english_translation: What was already done with it in Shiloh, when they brought it into the war with the Philistines in the days of Eli (1 Samuel 4).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed reference: “1 Samuel 4.”

Jeremiah.english_translation: And they shall be gathered together; an expression of *mikveh* of water.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: the stubbornness of their evil heart
Jeremiah.english_translation: An expression of seeing, like “I behold him” (Numbers 24:17).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed reference: “Numbers 24.”

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: shall walk with the house of Israel
Jeremiah.english_translation: They will join with them and be added to them, to be one kingdom.
In My heart; and therefore I made them inherit to your fathers.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: How would I put thee among the sons
Jeremiah.english_translation: My congregation and My nation among the other sons; therefore I chose a fine portion, and I gave thee a pleasant land.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: The goodliest heritage of the nations
Jeremiah.english_translation: The splendour of all the hosts of the nations.
But you did not do My intention, except like a woman who betrays her companion because he cannot supply her sustenance; so you have betrayed Me, who supply you every good. So the aggadic midrash.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Rashi’s *meri‘ah* (“from her companion”) corresponds to JPS “from her husband.”

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: upon the high hills is heard
Jeremiah.english_translation: It is near to being heard.

The prophet teaches them to confess and to say thus: “Here we are come to Thee,” “Truly, falsehood,” etc., and “the shame hath devoured,” etc., “let us lie down in our shame” — all this is an expression of prayer that the prophet teaches them to say.
We have come.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Truly vain have proved the hills
Jeremiah.english_translation: We guarded against the hills and the multitude of the mountains, for we served idols there.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The verb *shamarnu* (“we guarded”) is as printed and the sense is not clear; rendered literally.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Truly in the LORD our God
Jeremiah.english_translation: In truth.
The idolatry in which we were engaged, as it is said, “and they separated themselves unto the shameful thing” (Hosea 9:10).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Hosea 9:10 in JPS: “They separated themselves unto the shameful thing.”

Jeremiah.english_translation: Through the sin of its worship our labour went to plunder.
By this repentance, return to Me — to thy honour and thy former greatness.
Then thou shalt not wander to go out in exile.
When thou swearest by My name, swear in truth — not as now, of which it is written about you (below, 5): “And though they say, As the LORD liveth, surely they swear falsely.”
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed reference: “below 5”; the verse is Jeremiah 5:2.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: the nations bless themselves by Him
Jeremiah.english_translation: If you do so, then the nations will be blessed through Israel: every nation will say to its son, “May you be like so-and-so of Israel.”
They will tell your praises. Another explanation: *yithallelu* — whoever is able to cleave to Israel will glory in the matter: *porvanter* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French *porvanter*: the printed form is פורוונטי"ר; Darmesteter reads *porvanter* (“Seront glorifiés”).

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Break up for you a fallow ground
Jeremiah.english_translation: “Plough for yourselves a fallow field”: be learning from tillers of the soil, who plough it in the summer days to kill the roots of the weeds so that it will not bring up thorns at the sowing time in winter; so you, improve your deeds before the evil comes upon you, so that your prayer not be rejected when you cry out.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Rashi’s *nir lakhem nir* is “break up for you a fallow ground.”

Jeremiah.english_translation: And let your cry before Me not be out of wickedness, but out of repentance, so that you not be like one who sows without ploughing, and it turns into thorns: *cardons* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French *cardons* (thistles): the printed form is קרדונ"ש; Darmesteter reads *kardons* and glosses it “En chardons.”

Jeremiah.english_translation: Before My fury goes out like fire; this is like ploughing before the sowing.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Blow you the horn in the land
Jeremiah.english_translation: Warn the inhabitants of the land that they blow the shofar, to flee.

An expression of gathering, and there are many in Scripture: “though a multitude of shepherds be called forth against him” (Isaiah 31:4), “they have cried aloud after thee” (below, 12), “they gather themselves together against me” (Job 16:10).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed references: “Isaiah 31:4,” “below 12” (Jeremiah 12:6) and “Job 16:10.”

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Set up a standard toward Zion
Jeremiah.english_translation: To flee to Zion.
Gather yourselves, like “send, hasten in” (Exodus 9).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed reference: “Exodus 9”; the verse is 9:19 (JPS “send, hasten in thy cattle”).

Jeremiah.english_translation: Nebuchadnezzar.
The way of a lion is to sit in ambush in the thickets of the forest: *espaises* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French *espaises* (thickets): the printed form is אשפיישי"ש; Darmesteter corrects it (“Lire : espaises, fourrés”).

Jeremiah.english_translation: An expression of *tsiyah* [dryness].

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: For this gird you with sackcloth
Jeremiah.english_translation: What is “this”? “For the fierce anger of the LORD is not turned back,” etc. And although above he spoke of Nebuchadnezzar and the destruction, here he turns to speak of the death of Josiah.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Is not turned back from us
Jeremiah.english_translation: And although Josiah returned with a whole heart, it is said of him (2 Kings 22:1), “the LORD turned not from His anger, because of all the provocations wherewith Manasseh had provoked Him.”
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed reference: “2 Kings 22:1”; the words quoted are in 2 Kings 23:26 (JPS “Notwithstanding the LORD turned not from the fierceness of His great wrath … because of all the provocations wherewith Manasseh had provoked Him”). Rashi abridges.

Jeremiah.english_translation: In the day of Josiah they will be astonished: why did all this come upon him? — and they do not know that his generation did not repent well. When he came to eradicate idolatry, what did the scoffers of the generation do? They carved the form of an idol on their doors, half in this door and half in that door; when he opened it, it was not recognised, and when he went away from there he closed it, and it joined together.
אטינטא"ר in Old French; an expression of “The serpent beguiled me” (Genesis 3:13) — for the false prophets prophesy to you: Peace shall be to you.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Old French word is printed אטינטא"ר; it is not in Darmesteter’s glossary and its exact form is uncertain, so it is left as printed.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Of this people, when all of them go into exile.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: A hot wind of the high hills
Jeremiah.english_translation: It sweeps and brushes even the fields of the water-channels to make them a wilderness. Another explanation: *tsaḥ* is an expression of thirst, which we translate *tsaḥuta*.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Toward the daughter of My people
Jeremiah.english_translation: That wind comes — and not to winnow chaff from the threshing-floor: אהבוניי"ר in Old French, like “and winnowed them with a fan” (below, 21).
Jeremiah.translator_note:
The Old French word is printed אהבוניי"ר; it is not in Darmesteter’s glossary and is left as printed.
Printed reference: “below 21”; the word *mizreh* (JPS “And I fan them with a fan”) is in Jeremiah 15:7.

Jeremiah.english_translation: It comes to cleanse grain — that is, not for good but for evil, to exile men (and women), infants and cattle.
Jeremiah.translator_note: “(and women)” is in parentheses in the printed text.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: A wind too strong for this
Jeremiah.english_translation: From these punishments a wind shall come for Me — a full wind, a complete wind, that I will not retract and will not repent. A wind: *talant* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French *talant*: the printed form is טלנ"ט; Darmesteter’s note on the word reads *talant*.

Jeremiah.english_translation: An expression of dispute.
*[Printed Old French: איקומאטרובילו]* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Thy violence (*ḥamasekh*).
Jeremiah.translator_note: JPS renders the word differently (“baleful thoughts”); this is Rashi’s gloss.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Targum: “For the voice of prophets prophesying concerning them that they shall go into exile, because they served the calf that is in Dan, and announcing evil tidings that shall come upon them, because they were enslaved to the image that Micah set up in the mountain of the house of Ephraim.” And although the calves had gone into exile long ago, from the days of Sennacherib, their iniquity still stands. Great is the sin that breaks what is before it and what is after it: before it, from the days of Abraham, as it is said, “and pursued as far as Dan” (Genesis 14:14); when he reached Dan his strength failed, for his descendants were destined to worship idols there; and after it, in the destruction of the Temple, as it is said, “For hark! one declareth from Dan.”
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Aramaic wording of the Targum is translated as printed.

Jeremiah.english_translation: *On* means breaking.
Those who set a siege against them.
Like *sadeh* (field).
She provoked Me, as in “you have been rebellious” (Deuteronomy 9:7) — they enraged.
To do these things to thee.
An expression of trembling and shaking.
*[Printed Old French: אנטינא"ש]* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Because thou hast heard, O my soul
Jeremiah.english_translation: From behind the curtain (*pargod*) tidings came to me of the sound of the battle-cry.
The destruction of Jerusalem, upon the exile of Jeconiah.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Compressed; rendered literally.

Jeremiah.english_translation: In a moment my curtains were despoiled.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: How long shall I see the standard
Jeremiah.english_translation: These gatherings — those who raise a standard to assemble, to come and fight.
They were torn loose and thrown from their places; and Menahem connected it with “he shaketh the arrows to and fro” (Ezekiel 21:26).

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: the fruitful field was a wilderness
Jeremiah.english_translation: The land planted with every good thing, like Carmel, has become a wilderness. Aggadic midrash: “I beheld the mountains” — these are the Patriarchs; “and all the hills” — these are the Matriarchs; that is, their merit is exhausted. “There was no man” — the merit of Moses, of whom it is said, “meek above all men” (Numbers 12); “and, lo, the Carmel” — Elijah.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Elliptical midrash, rendered literally. “There was no man” is from Jeremiah 4:25 and “the mountains … the hills” from 4:24. The printed reference “Numbers 12” is 12:3; Rashi’s wording “meek above all men” is translated rather than JPS’s “above all the men that were upon the face of the earth.”

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Yet will I not make a full end
Jeremiah.english_translation: In its inhabitants; for I will leave survivors who will go into exile.
It shall be destroyed.
An expression of thought.
This punishment; and I will fulfil it.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: neither will I turn back from it
Jeremiah.english_translation: And I will not repent of thinking good thoughts concerning them.
Like *ramah* in the sea (Exodus 9).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed reference “Exodus 9”; the phrase is at Exodus 15:1 (“hath He thrown into the sea”).

Jeremiah.english_translation: In thick forests: a place of tangled thorns in which to hide.
*Sela* is rendered by the Targum *bekifaya*.
To adorn herself and to find mercy before the plunderer.
An expression of tearing, for the paint makes the eye appear to widen the tear. So I heard; and Menahem too did not differ in the section of *kera*.
An expression of *kaḥol* (eye-paint).
Those who play with women in the manner of kinds of adultery, as in “and she doted upon their concubines” (Ezekiel 23).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed reference “Ezekiel 23”; the verse is 23:20. Rashi’s wording “upon their concubines” differs from JPS (“upon concubinage with them”) and is translated as Rashi has it.

Jeremiah.english_translation: They seek to kill thee.
Like a woman bringing forth her first child, at the beginning of her giving birth.
She wails and cries out, groanings — *conpleint* in Old French — like “and such as breathe out violence” (Psalms 27:12), an expression of speech.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed קונפליינ"ט; Darmesteter reads *conpleint*.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Thus she says.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The words “Woe is me” (*oy na li*) lie at the end of the verse; the site’s JPS has no separate rendering of them, so the lemma is the nearest phrase of the verse.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: are not Thine eyes upon truth
Jeremiah.english_translation: Are they not people of faithfulness, to whom to do good? Why, then, have these dealt treacherously with Thee, and none seek faithfulness?
Jeremiah.translator_note: Compressed; rendered literally.

Jeremiah.english_translation: And they did not become sick over the blow, to take it to heart and to return from their evil.
Like *lakaḥat*.
The prophet says thus: But they are poor in wisdom, these with whom I speak.
An expression of *avil* (fool), as its Targum has it: *itpatshu*.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: I will get me unto the great men
Jeremiah.english_translation: They will listen; but I did not profit, for they too together have broken the yoke of the Holy One, blessed be He, from upon them.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: a lion out of the forest
Jeremiah.english_translation: The kingdom of Babylon.
The kingdom of Media.
The kingdom of Assyria.
In Edom.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The meaning is not spelled out in Rashi’s brief comment; rendered literally.

Jeremiah.english_translation: An expression of *aravah* and of a pit; the wolf of the wilderness.
Hastening. And Menahem connected it with an expression of guarding, as in “Watching daily at my gates” (Proverbs 8:34). Targum Jonathan: an expression of lying in ambush.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Rashi’s words are *lishkod al daltotai*; the JPS wording is quoted.

Jeremiah.english_translation: “Shall I pardon thee?” — in astonishment: perhaps for this I should pardon thee. And Menahem explained *ei* as *ein* — because thy sons have forsaken Me, and I satisfied them with all good.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The comment is compressed; rendered literally.

Jeremiah.english_translation: They gather in troops.
Every morning they rose early at the light of morning, in early rising.
This expression applies to horses, as in “At the sound of the neighing of his strong ones” (below, 8) — an expression of neighing; *[printed Old French: אנוויישמינ"ט]* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed reference “below 8” is 8:16. The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Go you up into her rows
Jeremiah.english_translation: An expression of a plain (*mishor*). And Menahem connected it with an expression of a wall, with “by my God do I scale a wall” (Psalms 18:30); but her shoots (*netishoteha*) — *[printed Old French: צי"ש]* in Old French, which are the roots of a vine — would not be fitting to be counted with the walls and not with the plain. And I say that *sharotheha* is an expression of the rows of the vine. And the Targum renders *besharoteha* “in her walls” and *netishoteha* “her branches.”
Jeremiah.translator_note: Psalms 18:30 is quoted in the JPS wording. The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter. The Aramaic words are left in transliteration.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Targum: “Not from before Him does good come upon us.”
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Aramaic word printed here is *tavta* (“good”); translated as printed.

Jeremiah.english_translation: As the Targum has it: “and the false prophets shall be for *lelama*” — that is, the prophecy that false prophets prophesy to us in the name of the Holy One, blessed be He, their words will turn to vanity, and the holy speech that they tell us in the name of the Holy One, blessed be He, is not in them.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Aramaic word *lelama* is left as printed.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Thus be it done unto them
Jeremiah.english_translation: The prophet says to those who say this: “Thus be it done unto them,” as HaShem said to me. And what did HaShem say to me? “Because you speak this word,” etc.
And it shall devour them.
Mighty.
From the days of old it began to rebel against Me, in the generation of the Dispersion, in the land of Shinar.
The place of the sheath (*nartik*) of the arrows.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: They shall batter thy fortified cities
Jeremiah.english_translation: This is a transposed verse: “He shall batter with the sword the cities of thy fortifications, wherein thou trustest.”
He will impoverish.
By means of armies; and so He says, “neither shall the sword go through your land” (Leviticus 26).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed reference “Leviticus 26”; the verse is 26:6.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Is not the sea, which has no worry about punishments and does not look for the receiving of reward, afraid of Me, and does not cross the boundary that I have set around it?
An expression of fear.
Its waves, raised up to cross the boundary — and they shall not be able to cross.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Compressed; rendered literally.

Jeremiah.english_translation: A great noise of voice.
The waves shall not cross the boundary.
As the Targum has it: *bekhir* and *lekish*.
Seven weeks in which He ordained for us two statutes of the harvest: the statute of the Omer and the statute of the Two Loaves.
That the harvest may be at its time.
They turned these statutes away from you, so that they do not keep for you, and you are consumed by famine.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Compressed; rendered literally.

Jeremiah.english_translation: He will lie in ambush; and so, “because of them that lie in wait for me” (Psalms 5:9), an expression of “I behold him, but not nigh” (Numbers 24:17).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Rashi’s words in Psalms 5:9 are *lema‘an shoreray*; the JPS wording is quoted.

Jeremiah.english_translation: As the snare (*yakush*) bites — the device they make to catch deer in the forest: when its foot comes into it, it bites it and holds it by its foot, and it is caught; and they call it *piédje* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed פיי"ד; Darmesteter’s notes in this section read *piédje*.

Jeremiah.english_translation: *cenbel* [printed צינבי"ל] in Old French (an ambush) — so ambushers act against a city or on a road.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French *cenbel* (“an ambush”). The reading is from Darmesteter’s index (*cénbél*) and his entry at Jeremiah 5:26 (“Embuscade”), which lists the printed form (צינבייל) among its manuscript variants. Godefroy has *cembel / cenbel* in the sense “small band of men.”

Jeremiah.english_translation: Like “the garrison (*matsav*) of the Philistines” (סא"א).
Jeremiah.translator_note: The parenthetical abbreviation is left as printed; the phrase is at 1 Samuel 13:23.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: As a cage is full of birds
Jeremiah.english_translation: A place where they fatten fowl; and so Jonathan rendered, “like a house of fattening (*bet pitma*),” and in Old French *franc*.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed פרנ"ק; Darmesteter’s index has *franc* (81).

Jeremiah.english_translation: An expression of “ivory (*eshet shen*)” (Song of Songs 5): a thick body; and in Old French *[printed אישפישור"ט]*.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed reference “Song 5” is 5:14. The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: they overpass in deeds of wickedness
Jeremiah.english_translation: If evil or transgression came into their hands, they did not turn aside from it, but passed into it and committed it.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: That they might make it to prosper
Jeremiah.english_translation: In order that they may prosper.
Astonishment.

A thing abominable to all. And what is the astonishing thing? The prophets prophesy falsely and say, “Be robbers and oppressors”; and the priests, who are the judges of the people and its taskmasters, rule the people by the hands of the prophets, that is, after them, as in “and the king passes, and all the people pass by his hand (pursuing) (another reading: of David) after him” (2 Samuel 16) — so here also “by their hands” means after them, to act according to the words of the prophets.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The phrase “rule … by the hands of the prophets” is from the next verse (5:31). The printed reference “2 Samuel 16” is 16:6, but the words as printed differ from that verse (compare 15:18, “passed on beside him”); the two bracketed readings are as printed.

Jeremiah.english_translation: To go to your cities to guard your fortresses.
It is the name of a place.
A standard, to assemble and to fight for your lives.
I have laid waste. Jonathan rendered it as an expression of “and the peaceable folds are brought to silence” (below, 25), “Ashkelon is brought to nought” (below, 47).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed references “below 25” and “below 47” are Jeremiah 25:37 and 47:5; JPS wording is quoted.

Jeremiah.english_translation: It is a parable: kings and their armies.
They ate.
His place round about.
Its time.
At the time the day turns.
When it turned toward evening, they set the fire in the Temple.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed abbreviation בבה"מ, read as “in the Temple”; the comment is brief and not further explained.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Without a *mappiq* in the *heh*, and it is an expression of *ets* (tree), for an expression of cutting does not apply to counsel (*etsah*); and the *etsah* mentioned here is an expression of many trees, as *dagah* is an expression of many fish.
Whose visitation has come.
An expression of a spring (*makor*).
A well.
So their wickedness wells up always, adding and renewing.
[ע"כ] “I brought upon her evil and a blow.”
Jeremiah.translator_note: Aramaic words as printed; the opening abbreviation ע"כ is left as printed and not expanded.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Accept correction (*musar*).
Lest thou be torn away. *Hoka* is an expression of joining, as in “and hang them up” (Numbers 25:4); and there is an expression of removal of joining, and many words are used in this way.
*[Printed Old French: גרפאי"ן]* in Old French: after they have harvested the vineyard and gleanings remain, and the poor come and glean them — so they shall plunder, and return and plunder again.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Jeremiah.english_translation: You, the enemy: turn back thy hand to plunder a second time, like the grape-gatherer who returns his hand upon the *salsilot*, who feels about and searches for the gleanings. And so it was: after he exiled Jehoiakim and slew him and made Jeconiah king, he returned at the end of three months and exiled him; he returned at the end of eleven years and exiled Zedekiah.

*[Printed Old French: רבירקר"ש]* in Old French, like “Extol her (*salselah*), and she will exalt thee” (Proverbs 4); so Dunash explained. And Menahem explained it as an expression of *sal* (basket): *[printed Old French: פניר"ש]* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Both Old French forms are printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter. Printed reference “Proverbs 4” is 4:8; JPS wording is quoted.

Jeremiah.english_translation: An expression of warning (*hatra’ah*).
Stopped up; and so every expression of *orlah*.
They revile it.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: I am full of the fury of the LORD
Jeremiah.english_translation: My heart is full of prophecy that the wrath of HaShem is to come upon them.
Like “to contain” — *[printed Old French: אשופרי"ר]* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Pour it out upon the babes
Jeremiah.english_translation: To pour out upon the sucklings.
In the market.
Near to death, and he is more than old.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Their fields and their wives together
Jeremiah.english_translation: They shall be turned over to others.
Forcible taking of money.
It is easy for the false prophets to bring out of their mouths and say, “Peace shall be to you”; and by this thing they heal with their words the breach that is destined to come upon them.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: They shall be put to shame
Jeremiah.english_translation: Targum: *aleihon lemivhat* (“upon them to be ashamed”).

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Neither know they how to blush
Jeremiah.english_translation: Like *lehakhlim*.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: they are not at all ashamed
Jeremiah.english_translation: They are not ashamed of their evil deeds.
Rest.

It is that men are stationed on the towers in a time of emergency — a man who watches and sees; if an army comes to the city he sounds the shofar and warns the people to be equipped and to come upon the wall. So too I stationed prophets, who let you hear the coming punishment, so that you hasten and amend your ways and be saved; and this is like the shofar blasts of the watchman: “Attend to the sound of the horn,” and arm yourselves.
The meaning is: I have already set them; and so Targum Jonathan: *ve-akimit*. “Watchmen”: *[printed Old French: גיט"ש]* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The printed Old French form is transparent (*guets*, “watchmen”) but could not be located in Darmesteter.

Jeremiah.english_translation: The evil that is in their hands.
The reward of their thoughts.

This is like “The LORD is my strength and song, and He is become my salvation” (Exodus 15:2), where he should have said “He was to me for salvation”; here too he should have said “and My teaching they rejected”; and it is the way of the verses to speak thus.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The printed reference is Exodus 15:2. Rashi quotes a part of the verse in a form that does not match JPS word for word; the JPS wording is given for the quotation.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: the frankincense that cometh from Sheba
Jeremiah.english_translation: That you offer before Me, which comes from Sheba.
They were not pleasant.
They take, as in “and laid hold of it” (Exodus 4); and so “anguish hath taken hold of us” (above, 24) — it has seized me.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Rashi’s quotation is in the first person (“has seized me”), while the site’s JPS of 6:24 reads “us”; translated as Rashi has it.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Fear. Another version: an expression of gathering, as in *megurei el ḥerev* (Ezekiel 21:17), and so Jonathan translated.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Rashi’s quoted words are left in Hebrew; JPS renders that verse “they are thrust down to the sword.”

Jeremiah.english_translation: Roll about.
The mourning for an only son — one who has only one son, and he died.
Because it is in the construct, *mispad* is vowelled with a *patah*, and not vowelled *mispad* with a *tsere*.
As it were, upon Me and upon you.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: I have made thee a tower
Jeremiah.english_translation: To Jeremiah it was said: “Strong have I made thee in their midst, and thou shalt know and try their way” — that thou shalt rebuke them, and they will not hearken. *Bahon* is an expression of strength, as in “the mound and the tower” (Isaiah 32:14), “they set up their towers” (ibid. 23).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Rashi’s paraphrase of the verse is translated as he has it. Printed “ibid. 23” is Isaiah 23:13.

Jeremiah.english_translation: They turn aside from the way.

“Between the brass and the iron” — casters of enmity between two officers who have strength to contend together: so I heard. And I say: they are talebearers, and strong as brass and iron to maintain their lies. And Targum Jonathan renders *rakhil* as an expression of *nokhel*: “they walk in their craftiness,” like one who mixes brass with iron; and *nokhel* is an expression of thought, as in “they conspired against him to slay him” (Genesis 37).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed reference “Genesis 37” is 37:18.

Jeremiah.english_translation: A parable: when they refine silver they blow with a bellows and always put lead into the crucible, and it helps in the refining; but with you, I came to refine you — the bellows was scorched and burned by the force of the fire, and all the lead was consumed. *Naḥar* is an expression of *ḥarah*, as in “against Job was his wrath kindled” (Job 32:2), “and my bones are burned with heat” (ibid. 30); *[printed Old French: אישר"ש]* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. Printed “ibid. 30” is Job 30:30.

Jeremiah.english_translation: For nothing did the refiner refine, for it did not help.
From their evil way — that is, the prophets toiled to rebuke, and did not profit.
*[Printed Old French: פורצטראקי"ץ]* in Old French. (Another reading: “*ve-ra‘im* is like *resha‘im*” סא"א).
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Jeremiah.english_translation: That is not refined by any toil.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: The temple of the LORD, the temple of the LORD
Jeremiah.english_translation: Targum: “Three times in the year you appear before Him.”
In astonishment: Will you do all these things, and the Temple avail you?
Has this house been in your eyes — said in astonishment.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Behold, I, even I, have seen it
Jeremiah.english_translation: For so it is in your eyes.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: as I have done to Shiloh
Jeremiah.english_translation: In the days of Eli.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: as I have cast out all your brethren
Jeremiah.english_translation: The Ten Tribes.
The form (*dfus*) of the star.
They called the great star the queen of heaven — an expression of royalty; and so Targum Jonathan: “to the star of heaven.”
It descends and reaches, as in “and the rain was not poured upon the earth” (Exodus 9:33) — it did not reach.

That you offer as whole-offerings — it is good for you to add them to your peace-offerings and offer them as peace-offerings and eat the flesh; for they are not accepted before Me, and why should you lose them?

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: in the day that I brought them out of the land of Egypt
Jeremiah.english_translation: The beginning of the condition was only: “if you will hearken unto My voice indeed, and keep My covenant, then you shall be Mine own treasure” (Exodus 19).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed reference “Exodus 19” is 19:5.

Jeremiah.english_translation: In the sight of their heart; an expression of “I behold him” (Numbers 24).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed reference “Numbers 24” is 24:17.

Jeremiah.english_translation: From day to day, rising early and sending.

Pluck out thy hair, as in “*vayagoz* quails” (Numbers 11), “and shaved his head” (Job 1:20). Another version: *nizrekh* is thy crown, an expression of greatness; and so Jonathan translated *ravrevekh* (“thy great ones”), and so Menahem connected it.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed reference for the first quotation is “ibid. 9”; the phrase is at Numbers 11:31.

Jeremiah.english_translation: And He forsook.

That is Molech, which was of brass; they would heat it from beneath, with its hands stretched out and heated, and they would place the child on its hands, and he would be burned and roar; and the priests would beat drums so that the father would not hear the voice of his son and his compassion be aroused. *Tofet* is from the word *tof* (drum).
On account of the roaring (*nehimat*) of the son.

By a commandment that they offer their sons as a sacrifice; and I did not speak to any of the prophets; and when I spoke to Abraham to slaughter his son, it did not come to My mind that he should slaughter, but only to make known his righteousness.
The birds from upon the carcasses.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: they shall spread them before the sun
Jeremiah.english_translation: And the Chaldeans will lodge, to besiege the city, in the graves of the princes, which were beautiful as a palace.
For manure.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: death shall be chosen rather than life
Jeremiah.english_translation: Even though they see the dead given over to contempt, the distress of the living is greater than it, and they will choose death.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Do men fall, and not rise up again
Jeremiah.english_translation: Is it good for them to throw themselves into a fall from which there is no rising?

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Doth one turn away, and not return
Jeremiah.english_translation: When they wish to return from their evil, the Holy One, blessed be He, will not turn back from His decree. Another explanation: even if they repent, it will not be established in their hands, for they will hasten to return to their wickedness; and so Targum Jonathan: “If to return — it is revealed before Me that they will not return.”
Eternal backsliding, like *netsaḥ* (eternity).
They seized.
With deceit (*mirmah*).
Not justly, as in “The daughters of Zelophehad speak right” (Numbers 27:7).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Rashi quotes only the words *ken benot Tselofḥad*; the JPS wording is given for the verse.

Jeremiah.english_translation: In the former way they sin and return and sin; “in their course” — *[printed Old French: קורש"י]* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed קורש"י; Darmesteter glosses the word “in their course” (*course*) and lists the manuscript readings.

Jeremiah.english_translation: *[Printed Old French: אישפרידי"ן]* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Darmesteter glosses the word “carried away” (*emporté*) and reads *esfredéç* (modern *effrayé*), the manuscripts varying; the printed form is left as printed.

Jeremiah.english_translation: *[Printed Old French: ציגוניא"ה]* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The printed form is transparent (“stork”); it was not located under this verse in Darmesteter.

Jeremiah.english_translation: The time of their passing to the isles of the sea because of the cold, and the time of their return.
They waited.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: the turtle and the swallow and the crane
Jeremiah.english_translation: And *shafnina*, and *kurkaya*, and *sununita*. *Kurkaya* is *gruah* in Old French; *sununit* is *arondele* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French *gruah* (“crane”) and *arondele* (“swallow”) are given by Darmesteter for this verse. The Aramaic words are those of the Targum, left in transliteration.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Behold, your wisdom is for falsehood among you, to heal you lightly.
Your prophet.
Such as you; and what is the shame? Behold, they have rejected the words of HaShem; and what wisdom is in them?
Jeremiah.translator_note: Rashi’s wording has “the words of HaShem” (plural); JPS reads “the word of the LORD.”

Jeremiah.english_translation: Like *vayirpa’u*.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: They shall be put to shame
Jeremiah.english_translation: Shame and disgrace shall come upon them.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: they are not at all ashamed
Jeremiah.english_translation: They are not ashamed of their evil deeds, to set their heart to return.
An expression of destruction, as in “I will utterly consume all things” (Zephaniah 1:2).
Nothing will be left over.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Hebrew is very brief and can also be read “no more.” Rendered as above.

Jeremiah.english_translation: An expression of withering, *flestris* in Old French, as in “and as a falling fig from the fig-tree” (Isaiah 34:4), “as a terebinth whose leaf fadeth” (ibid. 1).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed פליישטי"ש; Darmesteter reads *flestris*. Printed “ibid. 1” is Isaiah 1:30.

Jeremiah.english_translation: All this shall be theirs because I gave them statutes and they transgressed them.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: let us be cut off there
Jeremiah.english_translation: “And let us be silent there” — we will sit there silent and in mourning.
*[Aramaic as printed: “kas dalvot bish”; “krishei ḥiyvan”]* The head of asps is the venom that is in their teeth.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The two Aramaic phrases are obscure in the printed text and are left in transliteration; the final clause is translated.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Because they worshipped the calf that is in Dan.
The sneezings of his nostrils.

The playful neighings of his horses. And we find elsewhere that horses are called *abirim*: “By reason of the prancings, the prancings of their mighty ones” (Judges 5:22) — an expression for a galloping horse (Nahum 3); and Targum Jonathan: “from the sound of the steps of his mighty ones.”
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “Nahum 3” is 3:2 (“prancing horses”).

Jeremiah.english_translation: At the end of seventy years it becomes a *tsefa*, and it stops its ear so as not to hear the voice of the charmer who whispers to it, as it is said, “They are like the deaf asp that stoppeth her ear” (Psalms 58:5), which is what is said, “Which will not be charmed.”
Jeremiah.translator_note: The subject of “it becomes a *tsefa*” is not stated in the printed text. Printed reference “Psalms 58” is 58:5; JPS wording is quoted.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Like *hivligti* (“I have taken comfort”), and it is a noun — *[printed Old French: מישאיטינמנ"ץ]* in Old French — that is, if I said, “I shall console myself and restrain myself over my sorrow.”
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed מישאיטינמנ"ץ; Darmesteter glosses “my consolation” and reads *mes esteneméinç*.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: My heart is faint within me
Jeremiah.english_translation: From the sound of the prophecies revealed to me concerning the punishments to come.
I hear that in the end they will cry out in a land of far-off places. And why all this? Is not HaShem in Zion? And if they return to Him, He will be found for them.

We looked for the help of Egypt, and it did not come; we said, “Let the harvest pass, and they will be free and will come”; and behold, the time of the harvest in Iyar has passed, and the time of the summer in Tammuz, and they have not come.
An expression of blackness and darkness.
Astonishment.
It has seized me.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Is there no balm in Gilead
Jeremiah.english_translation: For the balm came from there, as it is said, “Go up into Gilead, and take balm” (below, 45) — that is, did they not have righteous men from whom to learn, so that they would improve their ways?
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed reference “below 45” is Jeremiah 46:11; JPS wording is quoted.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Healing — *[printed Old French: אינפלשטר"א]* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The printed Old French form is transparent (“plaster”) but could not be located in Darmesteter.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Gatherings of traitors.

This expression applies to the readying of the bow to shoot an arrow. And a bow is *arbaleste* in Old French, and they tread it with the feet; therefore it calls it *dereikhah* (treading). And the prophet likened their tongue to a bow of falsehood — that they bent their tongue, a bow, in falsehood.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed ארבלישט"א; Darmesteter reads *arbalestre* for this verse (“Ils tendent leur langue comme leur arbalète”).

Jeremiah.english_translation: From transgression to transgression.
He will surely lie in ambush.
They toiled and labored to pervert their way.
Like *hakhbed et libo* (Exodus 8:11) — to pervert.
