Jeremiah.translator_note: Rashi cites the infinitive form of the verb; JPS renders that verse “he hardened his heart.”

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Thy habitation is in the midst of deceit
Jeremiah.english_translation: When they sit, they plan thoughts of deceit, and through deceit they exchanged My fear and refused to know Me.
Because of the deceit.
By afflictions.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Because of the daughter of My people
Jeremiah.english_translation: Targum: “From before the sins of the assembly of Israel.”

Drawn out, as in “beaten gold” (1 Kings 10:16), and so “gone deep in making slaughter” (Hosea 5:2); *[printed Old French: טריי"ט]* in Old French. Another version: an expression of actual slaughter, *[printed Old French: טראנקא"ט]* in Old French; and so Menahem connected it; and so Targum Jonathan: “like an arrow that is sharpened.”
Jeremiah.translator_note: Both Old French forms are printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter. Rashi’s phrase from Hosea 5:2 is translated in the JPS wording.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: *uvme‘ohi* (“and in his inward parts”).
Over the destruction of the mountains.
The abode of shepherds that is in the wildernesses; *ne’ot* is an expression of abode, and so “the habitations of God” (Psalms 83:13), and so “Holiness becometh Thy house” (ibid. 93).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “ibid. 93” is Psalms 93:5.

Jeremiah.english_translation: An expression of aridity (*tsiyyah*), and so *nitsetah*.

In the end they would go. For fifty-two years no man passed through Judah, from the exile of Zedekiah until the decree of Cyrus king of Persia; there were fifty-two years. And a hint to the matter: “and the beast” — its sum is, by gematria, 52; and the calculation is set out precisely in tractate Megillah.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The word *behemah* by itself totals 52 (bet 2 + heh 5 + mem 40 + heh 5); the printed words are “*ve-ad behemah*”. No page of Megillah is named in the printed text.

Jeremiah.english_translation: *Degorin* (Aramaic).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Very brief; the Aramaic word is left in transliteration.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Who will understand this? And who is the prophet to whom the mouth of HaShem has spoken?
And who will tell on what account the land perished, and all this punishment came?
A bitter herb.
The venom of a serpent.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: our dwellings have cast us out
Jeremiah.english_translation: Their inhabitants. And it can also be said: the enemies have cast our dwellings to the ground.
From the market, as in “and thou shalt make streets for thee in Damascus” (1 Kings 20).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed reference “1 Kings 20” is 20:34.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Let not the wise man glory
Jeremiah.english_translation: Do not glory, saying, “We are wise.” Behold, you rejected My words, and what wisdom have you? If you have understood and known Me, then you may glory in your wisdom.
Like *hakhbed* (Exodus 8:11) (*entéliant* in Old French).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed אגטליינ"ט; Darmesteter glosses “en me comprenant” and reads *entéliant*.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Upon every circumcised one who has a foreskin, even the foreskin of the heart.
They were neighbours of the Land of Israel, and were smitten after it, close to it, as it is written (Ezekiel 29), and it is explained in *Seder Olam*.
An expression of an extremity: those set far off in the corner of the wilderness.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Very brief; rendered literally.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Learn not the way of the nations
Jeremiah.english_translation: And “be not dismayed at the signs of heaven” — when the sun is smitten and the luminaries are smitten.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The printed text begins “And then”; translated as printed.

Jeremiah.english_translation: A craftsman.
*Doloire* in Old French (adze).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed דולדוייר"א; Darmesteter reads *doloire* (“avec la doloire”).

Jeremiah.english_translation: *[Printed Old French: קלוי"ש]* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The printed form is transparent (“nails”) but is not in Darmesteter’s glossary for this verse.

Jeremiah.english_translation: A sledge-hammer (*kornes*): *martel* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed מרטי"ל; Darmesteter reads *martel* (“et avec le marteau”).

Jeremiah.english_translation: He will bend his knees, an expression of *pukah* (“stumblingblock,” 1 Samuel 25), and “the knees smite together” (Nahum 2).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed references “1 Samuel 25” and “Nahum 2” are 25:31 and 2:11. JPS wording is quoted.

Jeremiah.english_translation: He strikes them with a hammer until he makes them stand tall, like a palm-tree.
If you separate from them, for they will not harm you.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Neither is it in them to do good
Jeremiah.english_translation: If you serve them. *Heitiv* is like *lehativ*.
To Thee it is fitting.
Idolaters. And what is the “one”? The instruction of the vanities — their wooden [idols] — and they are instructed by it. *Yiv‘aru* is an expression of folly, and so *ve-yikhselu*.
Beaten thin.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: But the LORD God is the true God
Jeremiah.english_translation: Why? Because He is the living God and King of the world; therefore He is able to make His words true. But flesh and blood says that he will do, and he dies, or his strength fails, or he comes down from his possessions, and it is not in his hand to fulfil.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Thus shall you say unto them
Jeremiah.english_translation: This is a letter that Jeremiah sent to Jeconiah and his exiles in the exile, to answer the Chaldeans in Aramaic, a reply if they tell them to serve idolatry.
*[Printed Old French: טינדי"ש]* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: At the sound of His giving
Jeremiah.english_translation: When a sound comes which gives a multitude of waters in the heavens.
Clouds.
*flandor* [printed פלנדורי"ש] in Old French (lightning).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French *flandor* (“lightnings,” Darmesteter: “les éclairs”). Darmesteter notes that the good reading, preserved in one manuscript only, is *splandor*, while the others read *flandor* or *flandre*; the printed form is of the *flandor* group.

Jeremiah.english_translation: An expression of “a brutish man” (Psalms 92:7), and so “the shepherds are become brutish” (here).
An expression of *massekhah* (casting).

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: In the time of their visitation
Jeremiah.english_translation: When I visit upon them.

Hide it; and so Targum Jonathan: “Gather up thy merchandise from the land,” as in “As for the trafficker (*kena‘an*), the balances of deceit are in his hand” (Hosea 12). And Menahem explained *kin‘atekh* as an expression of humbling and lowliness, and *asfi* as an expression of bowing: bow and lower thyself more than the lowliness of the earth, thy humbling — Jerusalem, which sits now in siege.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Compressed; rendered literally. Printed “Hosea 11” is Hosea 12:8.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Like one who throws a stone with a sling.
That they may find the reward of their deeds.
An expression of sickness.
Targum Jonathan: *ve-asovrineih*; *[printed Old French: אשופריר"לוי]* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: My children are gone forth of me
Jeremiah.english_translation: They went out from me; Jerusalem says thus.
The kings.
They did not succeed in their kingship, as in “Whithersoever he turneth, he prospereth” (Proverbs 17:8).
The flock of their pasture.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: man’s way is not his own
Jeremiah.english_translation: For the evil inclination that Thou hast created in him turns him from the way. Another explanation: “I know, HaShem, that man’s way is not his own” — it is not in the hand of any man to make his way succeed; and if it were not by Thy word, no power is in the hand of an enemy to destroy Thy house.
By chastenings.
*Justice* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed יושטיצ"א; Darmesteter reads *justice* (“avec justice”). JPS renders the Hebrew word “in measure.”

Jeremiah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “But with judgment, withhold.”
Lest there be destruction.
*[Printed Old French: דוורירו"נט]* in Old French, and likewise “*ve-akhaluhu*.”
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Jeremiah.english_translation: That he be cursed.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Very brief; rendered literally.

Jeremiah.english_translation: An expression of warning.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: I brought upon them all the words of this covenant
Jeremiah.english_translation: The curses stated in the covenant, concerning the things which I commanded to do, and they did not do.
From the cities of Judah.
In their supplication and in their prayer.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: What hath My beloved to do in My house
Jeremiah.english_translation: What has the people of My treasure to do, any more, in My house?
To do — that is her scheme, the counsel of her sins.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Compressed; rendered literally.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Among them.
Even circumcision they annulled from their flesh, through which they were sanctified to Me.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: When thou doest evil, then thou rejoicest
Jeremiah.english_translation: When you commit a transgression, you rejoice.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: the noise of a great tumult
Jeremiah.english_translation: An expression of the noise of a great people that will come upon them.
And they shattered its branches.
Thus the prophet says: the Holy One, blessed be He, made known to me their punishment.
That is led to the slaughter.
Because I make known to them the evil, they say that they will kill me.

Dunash and Judah ben Koreish interpreted it as “like a lamb and an ox that is led to the slaughter,” and *alluf* is like *alafekha* in “the increase of thy kine” (Deuteronomy 28:4). And although it did not say *alluf* [in that sense], we have its like: “The sun and moon stand still in their habitation” (Habakkuk 3:11), “Like a swallow or a crane, so do I chatter” (Isaiah 38:14). And Menahem interpreted “like a lamb *alluf*” as a large lamb (see Psalms 58, in Rashi). And Jonathan supports him, who translated “like a chosen lamb.”
Jeremiah.translator_note: The bracketed cross-reference “(see Psalms 58, in Rashi)” is as printed. Rashi’s quotations are given in the JPS wording; his point about them (an omitted letter or word) is not spelled out in the printed text.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Let us destroy the tree with the fruit thereof
Jeremiah.english_translation: Targum: “Let us cast the poison of death into his food.”

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Let me see Thy vengeance on them
Jeremiah.english_translation: He was cursing the men of Anathoth.
Like “upon the men of Anathoth.”

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Right wouldest Thou be, O LORD
Jeremiah.english_translation: When I argue with Thee, I know that Thou art right in Thy words; yet I desire to speak of judgments with Thee, that Thou make known to me Thy way.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Wherefore doth the way of the wicked prosper
Jeremiah.english_translation: That Thou gavest greatness to Nebuchadnezzar the wicked, and madest him prosper to destroy Thy house. Another explanation: he was crying out concerning the men of Anathoth and lodging a complaint.
An expression of tranquillity.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: But Thou, O LORD, knowest me
Jeremiah.english_translation: Also against the men of Anathoth who stand against me, help me; for Thou knowest me.
Remove them from life to death — *[printed Old French: דישטאקאלו"ש]* in Old French — as in “till we have drawn them away from the city” (Joshua 8:6).
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Make them ready.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: How long shall the land mourn
Jeremiah.english_translation: Up to here are the words of the prophet, and the Holy Spirit answers him: from the wickedness of those who dwell in it, the beasts and birds are consumed.
Be laid waste.
*[Printed Old French: פוניד"א]* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Jeremiah.english_translation: The inhabitants of this land.
It is not revealed before Him what will be at our end.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: If thou hast run with the footmen
Jeremiah.english_translation: Thy relatives the priests are like thee, and the men of thy city come to kill thee; “with footmen” — *[printed Old French: פיאוניד"ש]* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The printed Old French form is transparent (“foot-soldiers”) but could not be located in Darmesteter.

Jeremiah.english_translation: To run with the horses; that is, if thy relatives the priests come to kill thee, how much more will the princes of Judah rise up to kill thee; and this is My anger against them, and this is the prospering of the enemy. And so Targum Jonathan: “This is the reply,” etc. And a midrash of our Sages: If for the reward of the three steps that Nebuchadnezzar ran for My honour, in the days of Merodach-baladan, thou art amazed that I increased his greatness so much, what wilt thou be amazed at further when thou seest the repayment of reward that I shall pay to the righteous who ran before Me like horses?
Jeremiah.translator_note: No source is named for the midrash in the printed text.

Jeremiah.english_translation: *[Printed Old French: אאטיר"ש]* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Darmesteter has an entry for this word glossed “comment rivaliseras-tu?” (“how wilt thou rival?”); the manuscript readings listed there are אאטיר. The printed form is left as printed.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: in a land of peace thou art secure
Jeremiah.english_translation: Where thou trustest, they have wearied thee.

The princes of Judah; and “the pride of the Jordan” is a parable, because it is a place of lions and leopards; and so we have learned from Jonathan in many places. And here he translated: “And thus art thou likened to receive the beasts of the field that are in the height of the Jordan.” “Behold, he shall come up like a lion from the thickets of the Jordan” (below, 9) — Targum Jonathan, in two places: “like a lion that comes up from the height of the Jordan.”
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed reference “below 9” is Jeremiah 49:19 (the same phrase recurs at 50:44). Rashi’s Hebrew “pride of the Jordan” is rendered by JPS “thickets of the Jordan.”

Jeremiah.english_translation: A gathering of people.
The people of My treasure.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: She hath uttered her voice against Me
Jeremiah.english_translation: The outcry of her violence went up before Me.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Is My heritage unto Me as a speckled bird of prey
Jeremiah.english_translation: The *heh* is a question of astonishment; therefore it is vowelled with a *patah*: Are they a speckled bird, stained with blood, so that the other birds gather upon it? Another explanation: *ayit tsavua* is one bird which is speckled, and all the birds gather upon it to eat it, because they hate it.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Are the birds of prey against her round about
Jeremiah.english_translation: Perhaps these are birds of the heaven — the troops, the swift bands that are round about her.
Come.
Heads of the troops of Nebuchadnezzar’s army, as it is said above, “Shepherds with their flocks come unto her” (above, 6).
An expression of trampling, and so “Treading down in the mire of the streets in the battle” (Zechariah 10:5).
*[Printed Old French: קנפני"א]* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The printed form is transparent (*campagne*, open country); it was not located in Darmesteter for this verse.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Before Me.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: They have sown wheat, and have reaped thorns
Jeremiah.english_translation: They prayed, and their prayer was not accepted. Why? Because they had not ploughed for themselves the ploughing of repentance and good deeds; therefore they sowed among thorns. A book in which *zar‘u* is vowelled with a *ḥirik* under the *zayin* is a corruption.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The phrasing echoes Jeremiah 4:3 (“Break up for you a fallow ground, and sow not among thorns”); Rashi does not cite it.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: They have put themselves to pain
Jeremiah.english_translation: An expression of sickness: they have been sick in their pain, and their cry is before Me, and they will not avail.
From your deeds.
Egypt, Ammon and Moab, and Tyre and Sidon, who were neighbours of the Land of Israel and harmed them.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: I will again have compassion on them
Jeremiah.english_translation: All of them were smitten near the destruction of the Temple, and of all of them it is said “and I will turn the captivity” in this book.
If they believe in HaShem.
An expression of building.
*porceint* [printed פורצינ"ט] in Old French (a belt).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French *porceint*, read from the letters; it is not in Darmesteter. Godefroy attests *porceint* in the sense “ceinture” (belt, girdle), which fits Rashi’s lemma “girdle.”

Jeremiah.english_translation: To launder it when it is full of sweat, so that it will rot quickly.
It is not fit for anything.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: that it be as this girdle
Jeremiah.english_translation: Their pride shall be like this rotted girdle.
It is an earthenware vessel, made to put wine into.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: I will dash them one against another
Jeremiah.english_translation: I will strike one upon another until they break into small pieces; like “Thou shalt dash them in pieces like a potter’s vessel” (Psalms 2), and “and dasheth thy little ones” (ibid. 137), and so every “dashing” (*nipuz*) in Scripture.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “ibid. 137” is Psalms 137:9; “Psalms 2” is 2:9.

Jeremiah.english_translation: I will dash one beside another.
They will stumble: *[printed Old French: אצופי"ר]* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed אצופי"ר; Darmesteter glosses “trébuchent” and reads *acoper* (modern *achopper*).

Jeremiah.english_translation: Mountains of darkness, as they go in exile.
Like “and to make the light into gross darkness.”
Because of your greatness, which will be annulled. Another explanation: because of the pride of the Kingdom of Heaven, which will be given to the idols of the Chaldeans.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: the king and to the queen-mother
Jeremiah.english_translation: Jehoiachin and his mother.

*[Printed Old French: וושטרי קאי"ץ]* in Old French — your uppermost place, as it is said (2 Kings 28), “And Jehoiachin the king of Judah went out to the king of Babylon, he, and his mother, and his servants,” and all of them he led into exile.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed וושטרי קאי"ץ; Darmesteter reads *vostre chevéç* (the glossary entry: “celui qui est à votre tête”). The Hebrew word Rashi uses is *aliyyatkhem*, rendered above as “your uppermost place.” Printed “2 Kings 28” is 2 Kings 24:12.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: The cities of the South are shut up
Jeremiah.english_translation: Before those who come upon them from the north — the cities of the Land of Israel were shut for fear of Nebuchadnezzar.

Jehoiachin will not fight, for he went out in peace and he exiled him. Another version: *shelomim* — *[printed Old French: גרדונאמינ"ץ]* in Old French — that is, the repayment of their iniquity; and so Targum Jonathan: “the full payment of their sins has been received.”
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Those who come upon you from the north.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Where is the flock that was given thee
Jeremiah.english_translation: After they are exiled, He will say thus to Jerusalem.
The Holy One, blessed be He, upon thee.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Whom thou thyself hast trained against thee
Jeremiah.english_translation: Thou didst send them messengers, to the Chaldeans, to bring their idols from there, to serve them, as it is said (Ezekiel 23:16), “And as soon as she saw them she doted upon them, and sent messengers unto them into Chaldea.” Another explanation: “thou hast taught them to be chieftains over thee” — Hezekiah, who showed the messengers of Merodach-baladan all his treasure-house (Isaiah 39).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed reference “Isaiah 39” is 39:2.

Jeremiah.english_translation: The hems of the garments — *[printed Old French: טי"ש אורלא"ש]* in Old French; when they strip a woman in disgrace, they turn her garment over from below upward.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Thy ways were cut off. *Nehmasu* is like “And He hath stripped His tabernacle, as if it were a garden” (Lamentations 2:6).
*Traces* in Old French [printed טרצי"ש] — those who pass on the way have stopped.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Darmesteter glosses the word “tes traces” (*traces*).

Jeremiah.english_translation: The name of a black man, and they call him *Maure* [printed מא"ר] in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The printed Old French form is transparent (“Moor”) but was not located in Darmesteter.

Jeremiah.english_translation: *Léopard* [printed ליאפר"ט] in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The printed Old French form is transparent but was not located in Darmesteter.

Jeremiah.english_translation: The leopard is spotted, and these are the spots — *taches* [printed טק"ש] in Old French — and it is impossible that they be changed.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Darmesteter reads *tache* (“ses taches”).

Jeremiah.english_translation: Like *lehara*.
The portion of thy measures: measure for measure.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: uncover thy skirts upon thy face
Jeremiah.english_translation: I have uncovered the hems of thy garments, to turn them over upon thy face.
Like the neighing of adulterous horses.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: thou wilt not be made clean
Jeremiah.english_translation: After how long — thou wilt yet be clean.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The site’s JPS begins the next verse (14:1) with “When shall it ever be?”, which is how JPS renders the words *aharei matai* that Rashi comments on; the lemma is therefore the nearest phrase of this verse.

Jeremiah.english_translation: That He will bring famine upon them. And Menahem connected it with an expression of *mivtsar* (fortress), as in “And the high fortress of thy walls” (Isaiah 25:12).
Its cities.
The cry of Jerusalem, as in “Let them shout from the top of the mountains” (ibid. 42).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “ibid. 42” is Isaiah 42:11.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Pits in which the water gathers.
Because no rain had fallen.
An expression of covering.
*[Printed Old French: בובייר"ש]* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The printed Old French form is transparent (*boviers*, “oxherds”) but was not located in Darmesteter.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Her offspring, to seek pasture for herself.
Streams of water — *rivéyres* in Old French [printed ריבייר"ש].
Jeremiah.translator_note: Darmesteter reads *rivéyres* (“courants d’eau”).

Jeremiah.english_translation: They testified against us.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: work Thou for Thy name’s sake
Jeremiah.english_translation: Do what Thou wilt do with us for the sake of the great Name that has gone out for Thee, that Thou rulest over all, and we are Thy people and the flock of Thy pasture; and it is not fitting that Thou give the Name of Thy victory to the idols. And there is an aggadic midrash on “for Thy name’s sake,” etc.
Hope.
*[Printed Old French: רקרו"ץ]* in Old French — one who withdraws his hand from the battle; and some say *[printed Old French: רקריאנ"ץ]* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Darmesteter’s glossary has the entry “stupefait; selon d’autres …”, lists the manuscript variants, and in his note reads *recredanç* (cf. *recroire*, *recreu*). The printed forms are left as printed.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Thy name is called upon us
Jeremiah.english_translation: Therefore Thy honour is not in that.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Very brief; rendered literally.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Its meaning is: like *ta‘azvenu*.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Even so have they loved to wander
Jeremiah.english_translation: Thus: as I decreed exile upon them in Egypt and in Babylon, they loved to be exiles there, to serve their idols; they distanced themselves.
An expression of *al*: a thing that is not.
An expression of sickness.
They went about to seek deliverance.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The printed word is abbreviated (הצל׳); read as *hatsalah* (“deliverance”).

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: to a land, and knew it not
Jeremiah.english_translation: To another land, and they did not know it until now.
On the condition that He not return upon it; for if Thy mind is to return, why hast Thou smitten us with no healing?
Jeremiah.translator_note: Compressed; rendered literally.

Jeremiah.english_translation: That Thou art called merciful.
The Temple. And aggadic midrash: Israel, who are engraved on the throne of Thy glory.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The printed abbreviation בה"מ is read as “the Temple.”

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Or can the heavens give showers
Jeremiah.english_translation: Of themselves, if not by Thy word? — in astonishment. Every doubled expression of astonishment has the first with a *heh* and the second with *im*, as “whether in camps, or in strongholds” (Numbers 13:19), “whether it is good or bad” (ibid.), “Hast Thou utterly rejected Judah? Hath Thy soul loathed Zion?” (here). So here also: “Are there any among the vanities of the nations … or can the heavens …”

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Though Moses and Samuel stood before Me
Jeremiah.english_translation: Both of them engaged in seeking mercy for Israel, and at first they brought them back to the good, and afterwards prayed for them; and it did not come into their heart to turn back My anger until they had brought them back to the good. Moses: “Put you every man his sword upon his thigh,” etc. (Exodus 32:27), and “and strewed it upon the water,” etc. (ibid.), and afterwards “I will go up unto the LORD, peradventure I shall make atonement” (ibid.). Samuel: at Mizpah, “the children of Israel did put away the Baalim” (1 Samuel 7:4), and afterwards “Gather all Israel to Mizpah, and I will pray for you” (ibid.). Thou canst not bring them back to Me; therefore pray not for them.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed references: Exodus 32:30 for the first quotation (the verse is 32:27; “strewed it upon the water” is 32:20 and “I will go up” is 32:30); 1 Samuel 7:5 for the first Samuel quotation (the verse is 7:4; the second quotation is at 7:5).

Jeremiah.english_translation: My will.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Such as are for death, to death
Jeremiah.english_translation: Every later one in the verse is harder than its fellow: the sword is harder than death — death by the sword is disgraceful, and death on one’s bed is not disgraceful, and so He says (Psalms 116:15), “Precious in the sight of the LORD is the death of His saints”; famine is harder than the sword, for this one suffers and that one does not suffer, and so He says, “They that are slain with the sword are better than they that are slain with hunger” (Lamentations 4:9); captivity — all of them are within it.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The last clause is in Aramaic in the printed text.

Jeremiah.english_translation: An expression of appointment and charge.
To drag; and so “Surely the least of the flock shall drag them away” (below, 49).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “below 49” is Jeremiah 49:20.

Jeremiah.english_translation: From the root of “that he stood not up, nor moved” (Esther 5:9); and like it *ga’avah*, from the root of “He is very proud” (Isaiah 15).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 15” is Isaiah 16:6.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: among all the kingdoms of the earth
Jeremiah.english_translation: Whoever hears the evil that has come upon them will tremble.
Will lament.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: turn aside to ask of thy welfare
Jeremiah.english_translation: To thee, to turn aside from his way to thee, to ask thee of thy welfare.
How many times I thought to destroy, and I repented of the evil; now I am weary of repenting. *Hinnaḥem*: *de porpenser* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed דפורפנשי"ר; Darmesteter reads *de porpenser* (glossary: “je suis fatigué de pardonner, ou de me raviser”).

Jeremiah.english_translation: A winnowing fan (*nafah*), which they call *van* in Old French; like one who winnows barley, that they should not all go into exile to one place.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed וו"ן; Darmesteter reads *van* (“avec le van”).

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Their widows are increased to Me
Jeremiah.english_translation: His widows increased before Me.
Upon Jerusalem, which was a city and a mother in Israel.
Everything will be open before him, all their hidden treasures.

I made to dwell upon them suddenly the troops of a city, and many terrors. Some interpret *ir* as an expression of an enemy, as in “and is become thine adversary” (1 Samuel 28:16), and its interpretation is “to thine adversaries” (Daniel 3).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “Daniel 3” is Daniel 4:16 (“the dream be to them that hate thee, and the interpretation thereof to thine adversaries”); the printed abbreviation is left as printed.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: She that hath borne seven languisheth
Jeremiah.english_translation: Samaria and the assembly of the Ten Tribes, from whom seven families arose — it has already languished and gone into exile.

These are Judah and part of Benjamin, who remained in Israel — “to the sword will I give.” These are the seven families: Jeroboam son of Nebat and his house, Baasha and his house, Omri and his house, Jehu and his house, Menahem and his house, Pekah and his house, Hoshea and his house.
An expression of “her soul pined”; we translate “and languishing of soul” (Deuteronomy 28:65) as *u-mafḥan nefesh*.

Before their time they hastened to fall; so it is expounded in tractate Gittin; and in Midrash Rabbi Tanhuma they expounded it of Jerusalem and count seven wicked: Jehoram, Joash, Ahaz, Manasseh, Amon, Jehoiakim, Zedekiah; but one should count also Rehoboam, Abijah, Amaziah, Ahaziah.
An expression of shame.
Jeremiah was lamenting over himself, that the men of his city hated him on account of his words of rebuke.
A man of strife, like “My spirit shall not contend” (Genesis 6:3).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Rashi takes *yadon* as “contend”; JPS renders it “abide.”

Jeremiah.english_translation: Like “thou shalt not be to him as a creditor” (Exodus 22:24).

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Yet every one of them doth curse me
Jeremiah.english_translation: I do not quarrel with them over matters of money, in which I have a claim against them, or they against me; and behold, all the people curse me.

*Sheritikha*: I have left thee over, an expression of remnant (*she’erit*); and so Menahem interpreted. But Dunash interpreted it as an expression of loosing, and *sheritikha* is like “loosing of knots” (*meshare ketarin*, Daniel 5). And the interpretation of *sheritikha* is thus: as it is said, “And now, behold, I loose thee this day from the chains which are upon thy hand” (below, 40) — that is, on the day on which HaShem fulfilled His word, it was said to him, “And now, behold, I loose thee this day from the chains which are upon thy hand. If it seem good unto thee to come with me into Babylon.” And Israel also asked of him that he pray for them, as it is said to him (below, 42), “pray for us unto the LORD thy God … for we are left but a few of many.”
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “below 40” and “below 42” are Jeremiah 40:4 and 42:2. “Daniel 5” is 5:12.

Jeremiah.english_translation: An expression of oath.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The printed text has the abbreviation שבוע׳, read as “oath” (*shevu‘ah*).

Jeremiah.english_translation: The enemy, when the evil comes upon them, will entreat thee that thou seek mercy for them — such as Zedekiah, who said to him, “Inquire, I pray thee, of the LORD for us,” etc. Another explanation: Nebuzaradan will ask of thee, “If it seem good unto thee to come with me into Babylon” (below, 40).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “below 40” is Jeremiah 40:4.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Can iron break iron from the north and brass
Jeremiah.english_translation: I say: iron that comes from the north is harder than other iron. And so is its meaning: they are likened to iron — “Going about with slanders; they are brass and iron” (above, 6) — and to Jeremiah it was said, “I have made thee … an iron pillar and brazen walls” (above, 1); and his is stronger than theirs, for Nebuchadnezzar will come from the north according to his words against them.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “above 6” and “above 1” are Jeremiah 6:28 and 1:18.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Will their iron break thine? Another explanation: will Pharaoh, who comes to your aid and is as hard as iron, break Nebuchadnezzar, who is iron that comes from the north, and brass? And Targum Jonathan inclines to this side.
An expression of money.
He says it to Israel.
And on account of all thy sins shall this be to thee.
In which thou didst set up idols in all of them.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Take me not away because of Thy long-suffering
Jeremiah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “Give not respite to those who afflict me.” Do not take my dispute so as to leave it for Thy long-suffering, but hasten and avenge me.
Like “I have borne.”
For Thy sake.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Thy words were found, and I did eat them
Jeremiah.english_translation: At first for desire; and they became for joy, because I imagined that they would now listen to me.
Because of the prophecy that came to me from Thee.
Alone and astonished, in mourning, for a prophecy of wrath filled me, of the destruction of Thy house.
Sick, as in “and it was very sick” of the son of Bathsheba (2 Samuel 12:15).

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Wilt Thou indeed be unto me as a deceitful brook
Jeremiah.english_translation: Thou art to me like a deceitful brook — like a man whose trust is cut off from him; for Thou leavest me to suffer at their hands. *Akhzav* is a spring that fails — *faillants* [printed פייליינ"ץ] in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed פייליינ"ץ; Darmesteter glosses the word “faisant défaut” (failing) and lists the manuscript forms.

Jeremiah.english_translation: To rely upon them.
Because I bear these troubles.
To me.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: If thou return, and I bring thee back
Jeremiah.english_translation: Thou, Israel, through me, and I will bring thee back to Him; He said to me, “Before Me shalt thou stand.”
Jeremiah.translator_note: Compressed; the printed abbreviation ע"י is read as “through me.” Rendered literally.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: if thou bring forth the precious out of the vile
Jeremiah.english_translation: If thou bring forth a worthy man from a wicked man, so that thou bring him back to the good.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Thou shalt be as My mouth
Jeremiah.english_translation: For I decree a decree, and thou annullest it.
Aramaic (Targum): “They shall return to thy word, and thou shalt not turn to err after them.”
A feast. In the Sifre, in the section of Beth-peor, I saw: “they returned to make for themselves *marzeiḥin*”; but our Rabbis explained *marzeaḥ* as mourning.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The site’s JPS follows the second explanation (“house of mourning”).

Jeremiah.english_translation: Will lament.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: I have taken away My peace
Jeremiah.english_translation: When Abraham, their father, did righteousness and justice, I gave to his seed lovingkindness and mercy: “the LORD thy God shall keep with thee the covenant and the mercy” (Deuteronomy 7:12), and “and show thee mercy” (ibid. 13). They turned justice to wormwood, and righteousness they cast to the ground (Amos 5:7); so I too have returned and gathered to Myself My lovingkindness and My mercy.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “ibid. 13” is Deuteronomy 13:18. Rashi’s wording of Amos 5:7 differs from JPS (“You who turn judgment to wormwood, And cast righteousness to the ground”) and is translated as he has it.

Jeremiah.english_translation: *[Printed Old French: אטואי"ש]* in Old French, like “God hath taken away my reproach” (Genesis 30:23).
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Both the great and the small shall die
Jeremiah.english_translation: And since all die, what business hast thou to lament?

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: nor cut themselves, nor make themselves bald for them
Jeremiah.english_translation: It is the way of mourners to gash themselves and to scratch their flesh and to make a baldness on their heads; and in any case it is forbidden to Israel, and He mentions it here only as an example of mourning.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: neither shall men break bread for them in mourning
Jeremiah.english_translation: An expression of breaking, as in “MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN” (Daniel 5:25); for they serve the mourners the meal of consolation in the open square and spread for them the blessing *ha-motsi*; “because he doth bless the sacrifice” (1 Samuel 9:13), which Jonathan translated, “for he spreads over the food.”
Jeremiah.translator_note: The word *mevarin* is the term for the mourners’ meal of consolation.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: neither shall men give them the cup of consolation to drink
Jeremiah.english_translation: Behold, the reason for what I said: do not go to lament.
Of which I said to thee above, “thou shalt not come” — this is the reason: “Behold, I will cause to cease from this place,” etc.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: there shall you serve other gods
Jeremiah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “And ye shall serve there the nations who worship idols.”
An expression of oath: even though you have betrayed Me, it is an oath in My hand that I shall redeem you.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: it shall no more be said
Jeremiah.english_translation: Our Rabbis expounded (Berakhot 12): not that the exodus from Egypt will be uprooted from its place, but that the final redemption will be the main thing, and the exodus from Egypt secondary to it.

As the fisherman draws them from the place of their growth, so will these be caught in the midst of the city; and as to the work of a fish, once it is caught it dies, so I shall bring killers upon them, and afterwards I shall send hunters for the remainder and for those who flee from the sword to the mountains and hills, and they shall hunt them to exile them in captivity.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: their iniquity and their sin double
Jeremiah.english_translation: That they have repeated their iniquity, to do the iniquities of their fathers; and Jonathan translated thus: “I will repay the second as the first — two for one.”

*[Printed Old French: אנטיפויימאנ"ט]* in Old French; and Menahem connected it with an expression of wonder, as in “Thou hast given a banner to them that fear Thee, that it may be displayed” (Psalms 60:6), and so “HaShem is my banner” (Exodus 17:15); and Dunash interpreted it as an expression of refuge itself.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. Printed “Exodus 7” is Exodus 17:15; JPS transliterates the name as Adonai-nissi.

Jeremiah.english_translation: In the end the nations will return to Thee and serve Thee with one consent; and Thy people — how did they make themselves gods who are no gods?
Like *miketseh*.
An expression of inheritance.
An expression of profit.
As it sounds: ruler and sovereign, to fulfil My decree.

It is a parable — that is, engraved by sinking in, and not easy to erase. And aggadic midrash: “with a pen of iron” — with the nail of the *shamir*; through Jeremiah, who was called an iron pillar, and through Ezekiel, to whom it is said, “As an adamant harder than flint have I made thy forehead” (Ezekiel 3:9).
Engraved, like one who ploughs deep.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: upon the tablet of their heart
Jeremiah.english_translation: For they do not forget their idols.
As their remembrance of their sons, so was their remembrance of their altars — like a man who yearns for his son.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: their Asherim are by the leafy trees
Jeremiah.english_translation: Which are upon a leafy tree — “upon” is like “beside”; and Targum Jonathan: “under every leafy tree.”

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: upon the mountain in the field
Jeremiah.english_translation: Jerusalem, which sits on a mountain of plain — all around the city is the plain of the field. And *harari* is an expression like *aravi* (“Arabian,” Isaiah 13), after the one who dwells in the *aravah*; *[printed Old French: מונטיינד"ש]* in Old French — “dwellers of the mountain” (another version: “she who dwells on the mountain”).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed מונטיינד"ש; Darmesteter’s glossary has “montagnard” with the forms *montaniers* etc.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Like “thy money.”

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: thy high places, because of sin
Jeremiah.english_translation: Thy high places, made in sin for the name of idolatry, in all thy borders.
Against thy will thou shalt release thy land, because it did not keep the sabbath in your sabbatical years, of which I told you, “then shall the land keep a sabbath” (Leviticus 25:2).

I will take vengeance because of thine inheritance, which I gave thee, that thou didst not do My will to let it lie fallow. Another explanation: “and in thee” — from thine inheritance; and in thee I will take vengeance — from thine inheritance, that I shall exile thee from it.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: kindled a fire in My nostril
Jeremiah.english_translation: You have kindled in My nostrils.
In his ploughing and his reaping, saying, “I shall sow in the seventh year and eat.”
Like “his help”; and so Targum Jonathan: “his confidence.”

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: whose heart departeth from the LORD
Jeremiah.english_translation: For He promised him, “then I will command My blessing upon you” (ibid.); so I heard.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “ibid.” is Leviticus 25:21.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Like a lone tree, an expression of *ariri* (“childless,” Genesis 15); and some say *[printed Old French: דגאשטי"ה]* in Old French. And Menahem explained it as the name of one of the trees of the forest, whose name is *arar*; and so he explained “like a tamarisk in the wilderness” — one of the trees of the forest.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. Printed “Genesis 15” is 15:2.

Jeremiah.english_translation: An expression of plain.
Dryness, as in “and my bones are burned with heat” (Job 30:30).
A land that is salty and shall not be inhabited.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: shall not see when heat cometh
Jeremiah.english_translation: The tree, when heat comes.
An expression of famine — *[printed Old French: פאמצ"א]* in Old French. Another version: *batsoret* is an expression of fortress (*mivtsar*), and so Menahem connected it.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The printed Old French form is transparent (“famine”) but could not be located in Darmesteter.

Jeremiah.english_translation: He will not fear.
Full of pretext, and tortuous above every evil.
An expression of sickness; this is its sickness.
He thinks, “Who can know it?” — I, HaShem, search it.
*Coucou* *glouçant* [printed קוק"ו גלונצנ"ט] in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Darmesteter’s glossary has the entry “le coucou glousse” (the cuckoo clucks) for this word, with the manuscript forms.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: over young which she hath not brought forth
Jeremiah.english_translation: This partridge draws after it chicks that it did not bear but hatched. The chirping which the bird makes with its voice is to draw chicks after it; but these that the partridge hatched will not follow it when they have grown, for they are not of its kind; so does he who makes riches, and not by right.
He will be called wicked.

Because he is coming to say, “All that forsake Thee shall be ashamed,” he begins with the praise of HaMakom [the Omnipresent] and speaks before Him: Thou, whose throne of glory and height are from the beginning of the creation of the world, and are directly opposite our Sanctuary.
HaShem sits upon it; therefore all that forsake Thee shall be ashamed.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: shall be written in the earth
Jeremiah.english_translation: Those who turn aside from my words, who do not hearken to my mission, shall be written in the graves, the lower parts of the earth.
In Thee I boast and glory, saying that Thou art my savior.
*[Printed Old French: וונטנצ"א]* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed וונטנצ"א; Darmesteter’s glossary glosses the word “mon orgueil” (my pride), and in his notes reads *vontançe* / *vantément* for it.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Where is the word of the LORD
Jeremiah.english_translation: The punishment of which thou prophesiest.
I did not hasten to urge Thee to bring them, from being a good shepherd who goes after Thee to seek mercy for them.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: have I desired the woeful day
Jeremiah.english_translation: I did not desire the sickness of punishment. And Targum Jonathan: “And I did not delay beyond Thy word to prophesy to them, to bring them back to Thy fear.” And according to the Targum, *atsti* would be an expression of delay — that is, I did not delay from telling them Thy mission and from bringing them back to Thee, if they would listen to me.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: That which came out of my lips was manifest before Thee
Jeremiah.english_translation: To turn Thy wrath away from them.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Be not a ruin unto me
Jeremiah.english_translation: Let Thy mission not be a ruin.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Let them be ashamed that persecute me
Jeremiah.english_translation: The men of Anathoth alone.
Your fathers, as to what I commanded them.
Like *u-lavo*.
On the anvil — *[printed Old French: פורמא"ש]* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The printed Old French form is transparent (*formes*) but its meaning here could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: that he made of the clay
Jeremiah.english_translation: That he makes from the clay was marred in the hand of the potter while it was still moist; and the verse is transposed.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: because of which I have spoken against it
Jeremiah.english_translation: From the transgressions in its hand, on account of which I spoke against it, to uproot and to pull down — *[printed Old French: אשרפורק"י]* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Jeremiah.english_translation: And I thought another thought.
And I knew that they would say to thee, concerning thy words, that they pay no heed to them.
A shameful thing.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Doth the snow of Lebanon fail
Jeremiah.english_translation: Will a man who needs to drink forsake the flowing waters from the rock in the fields, which come from the snow of Lebanon, which is clean?

Or will they forsake living, flowing waters, which are strangers (*zarim*) until now to every man, and they are cold (*karim*), strangers they flow? And this proves it: “I dug and drank strange waters” (Isaiah 37:25). And Menahem connected *zarim* with “they have not been pressed (*zoru*), neither bound up” (ibid. 1), an expression of waters of healing; and he gave a reason for his words and said: if he had wished to speak in the language of *zerem* (flood), he would have doubled the *mem* and added *yod mem*, and would have said *zerumim*, to increase the waters and to make them streams.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The grammatical argument ascribed to Menahem is compressed; rendered literally. Rashi’s quotation “I dug and drank strange waters” has the word “strange” as in 2 Kings 19:24; Isaiah 37:25 (JPS) reads “I have digged and drunk water.”

Jeremiah.english_translation: Like *sadeh*.
*[Printed Old French: פריוודא"ש]* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The printed Old French form is transparent (“cold”) but could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Jeremiah.english_translation: *[Printed Old French: קוראנ"ץ]* in Old French. And there is also another way to interpret it: “Or are they plucked up” — that the waters, which are cold and flowing, would become strange, loathsome waters.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The printed Old French form is transparent (*corants*, “flowing”) but could not be confirmed in Darmesteter.

Jeremiah.english_translation: (*Zarim*, in the first interpretation, is an expression of *zerem* [stream]; in the second interpretation it is an expression of strangeness — that is, loathsome waters.)
Jeremiah.translator_note: The printed text has this comment in parentheses without a lemma.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Thus did My people, who forgot Me, and burn incense to vanity.
Paths that were made right — they said that they are a stumbling-block, in order to walk a way not cast up, not trodden.
One who passes over ruins that he had already seen as good buildings is accustomed to whistle.
He will be amazed.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: upon their back, and not their face
Jeremiah.english_translation: When they flee from the enemy.
And I will not save them.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Come, and let us devise devices against Jeremiah
Jeremiah.english_translation: Jeremiah was complaining about the men of Anathoth, and says that they say thus.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: instruction shall not perish from the priest
Jeremiah.english_translation: For it is for the priests to teach Torah, as it is said, “They shall teach Jacob Thine ordinances” (Deuteronomy 33).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed reference “Deuteronomy 33” is 33:10.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: nor the word from the prophet
Jeremiah.english_translation: The words of prophecy.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The printed word is abbreviated (נבוא׳); read as “prophecy.”

Jeremiah.english_translation: Aramaic: “And let us testify against him false testimony.”
(Bring them down by the sword) — an expression of “Mine eye is poured out” (Lamentations 3), “as waters that are poured down a steep place” (Micah 1).
Jeremiah.translator_note: The first words are in parentheses in the printed text. Printed “Lamentations 3” is 3:49; “Micah 1” is 1:4.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: to the power of the sword
Jeremiah.english_translation: By means of troops.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: And let their men be slain of death
Jeremiah.english_translation: Of the widows — they shall be those slain by the Angel of Death.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: they have digged a pit to take me
Jeremiah.english_translation: For they suspected him of a married woman, as it is said, “For a harlot is a deep ditch” (Proverbs 23).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed reference “Proverbs 23” is 23:27.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Let it not be blotted out; and because it is a feminine form, a *yod* is put into it, and this too is superfluous, like the *yod* of *vatizni vam* (“and didst play the harlot with them,” Ezekiel 15).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed reference “Ezekiel 15”; the phrase *vatizni vam* is at Ezekiel 16:17.

Jeremiah.english_translation: A flask.
That is, of a potter, that is, of earthenware.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: and take of the elders of the people
Jeremiah.english_translation: “Go with thee; and of the elders of the people” is attached to “go”: and go with thee, with some of the elders of the people.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Compressed; rendered literally.

Jeremiah.english_translation: The gate of the refuse-heaps, where they throw the potsherds that are broken; and so Targum Jonathan: “the gate of the dump.”
*[Printed Old French: טינטני"ר]* in Old French — an expression of cymbals (1 Chronicles 15): “Praise Him with the loud-sounding cymbals” (Psalms 150).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed טינטני"ר; Darmesteter’s glossary has “tinteront” (they will ring) for this word. Printed “1 Chronicles 15” is 15:19; “Psalms 150” is 150:5.

Jeremiah.english_translation: They made it foreign before Me.
And I will empty out — an expression of *bukah*, “She is empty, and void, and waste” (Nahum 2:11); and on account of the *bakbuk* of which he speaks, he took his language thus.
An expression of trouble, like *tsukah*.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: that cannot be made whole again
Jeremiah.english_translation: (It refers to the people; but the city I shall make like Topheth, and I shall purify it in the future.)
Jeremiah.translator_note: The printed text is bracketed and begins with the word אהעם, read as “on the people”; rendered literally.

Jeremiah.english_translation: All of it full of slain, like Topheth where they kill the children for Molech.
The name of the place of the prisoners; and Targum Jonathan: “to the vault (*kifta*)” — *[printed Old French: ארוולו"ר]* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed ארוולו"ר; Darmesteter glosses “la voûte” and reads *arvolud* (from *arcum volutum*).

Jeremiah.english_translation: Fear.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: The LORD hath not called thy name Pashhur
Jeremiah.english_translation: Thy name was not called Pashhur but for this reason — namely, *pasaḥ shaḥor*, like a tree that has split (*nifshaḥ*), and so “and pulled me in pieces” (Lamentations 3). And so He said to him, “not Pashhur did HaShem call thy name,” for the word *Pashḥur* implies a great man and a freeman, *pash ḥor*; but rather for this reason thy name is called Pashḥur: *pasaḥ shaḥor*. Another explanation: *pesh saḥor* — many are around thee to kill thee; and according to this explanation *magor* is an expression of gathering, as in *megurei el ḥerev* (Ezekiel 21:17).
Jeremiah.translator_note: The wordplay on *Pashḥur* is rendered as printed. Rashi’s quotation “pulled me in pieces” is Lamentations 3:11 (JPS wording). In Ezekiel 21:17 JPS renders the phrase “they are thrust down to the sword.”

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: all the store of this city
Jeremiah.english_translation: Money.
To go on Thy mission.
Thou hast made Thy strong hand heavy upon me, to go against my will.
And Thou hast conquered.
All the people mock me.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: For as often as I speak
Jeremiah.english_translation: Whenever I speak to them I must cry out and raise my voice, and I do not call to them good, but prophecies of violence and spoil.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: the word of the LORD is made
Jeremiah.english_translation: Therefore His word became to me a reproach, for they revile me.
And for speech, like *vekilsah*.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Very brief; the comparison is not spelled out and the source of *vekilsah* is not named. Rendered literally.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: I will not make mention of Him
Jeremiah.english_translation: And if my heart says to me not to go on His mission any more.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: there is in my heart as it were a burning fire
Jeremiah.english_translation: The prophecy is like a burning fire, and against my will I must go.
And the fire is gathered in my bones.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: I weary myself to hold it in
Jeremiah.english_translation: To bear the fire.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: For I have heard the whispering of many
Jeremiah.english_translation: I said that I would not mention Him because I heard the slander of the many — those who whisper about me.
An expression of gathering, and so Targum Jonathan.
False testimony against him.

“And we will testify against him.” And Menahem explained *haggidu venaggidenu* like “you shall not cut yourselves” (Deuteronomy 14), and so he connected “He that denounceth (*yagid*) his friends” (Job 17:5), an expression of destruction, like “Hew down (*gudu*) the tree” (Daniel 4). But Dunash interpreted it as an expression of actual telling, and so is its interpretation: Tell false words against him, and we will tell the king. And we have many words in Scripture of this kind (like *naggidenu*), whose interpretation cannot be established unless they are divided into two words or three, as in “and could not speak peaceably unto him” (Genesis 37), “my children are gone forth of me” (above, 10).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Compressed; rendered literally. Printed references: “Deuteronomy 14” is 14:1, “Daniel 3” is 4:11, “Genesis 37” is 37:4, “above 10” is 10:20. The JPS wording of Job 17:5 is “He that denounceth his friends for the sake of flattery.”

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Them that watch for my halting
Jeremiah.english_translation: Watching for my downfall.
That he will listen to us and err after us.
They did not succeed in their counsel.

*[Printed Old French: פוא"י אינייניר"ט]* in Old French — it is the hour of conception. And through compulsion his father Hilkiah had relations with his wife, on the day he was fleeing from Manasseh, who was killing the prophets; and he cohabited with his wife and fled.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Jeremiah.english_translation: The *mem* has a *dagesh*, because it is an expression of gladdening others — that he gladdened his father with his tidings.
Sodom and Gomorrah.
Once He had decreed destruction upon them, He did not think another thought to annul His decree.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Because He slew me not from the womb
Jeremiah.english_translation: The Angel of Death, from the womb; and this is among the verses that are brief in speech.
A pregnancy for ever.
The destruction of the Temple.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: I will turn back the weapons of war
Jeremiah.english_translation: There are among you those who know how to adjure the princes above who are appointed over punishments, to save each man from the evil over which he is appointed, and in this you trust. Behold, I turn the authority of this one to that one, and you will not know whom to adjure.

The weapons of war, into the midst of this city, so that I destroy you with pestilence through the Angel of Death, who is among the upper princes; and so it is explained in the passage: “they shall die of a great pestilence.”

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: his life shall be unto him for a prey
Jeremiah.english_translation: As a person takes spoil and seizes it and goes his way, so shall his life be spoil for me — rescued from death, from the killers.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The printed text reads “for me” (*li*), where the verse has “unto him” (*lo*); translated as printed.

Jeremiah.english_translation: As its Targum has it: My anger.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: out of the hand of the oppressor
Jeremiah.english_translation: Its reason is below: that it is not a noun, but the name of the robber who oppresses others.
That no survivor may escape for you.
Jerusalem is in the midst of a valley. Another explanation: that the Holy One, blessed be He, has deepened counsel against thee to destroy thee.
Round about it is a plain.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Who shall come down against us
Jeremiah.english_translation: Who will encamp against us, as in “for thither the Arameans are coming down” (2 Kings 6:9).
This is wronging with words.
Targum: “If thou wert dear before Me like the Temple, which is high at the head of the mountain, [yet] I would surely make thee a wilderness.”
The Temple, from which come balm and healing for all the world.
And I have prepared.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: they shall cut down thy choice cedars
Jeremiah.english_translation: Because they likened it to Lebanon, this expression (of cutting) is used here.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Weep you not for the dead
Jeremiah.english_translation: For Jehoiakim, who will die before the gate when they drag him to exile him.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: weep sore for him that goeth away
Jeremiah.english_translation: For Jehoiachin and for Zedekiah. Say, then: the death of Jehoiakim, of whom it is said, “his dead body shall be cast out in the day to the heat, and in the night to the frost” (below, 36), is dearer than the life of Jehoiachin, of whom it is said, “a continual allowance … was given him” (below, 52).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “below 36” and “below 52” are Jeremiah 36:30 and 52:34.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: touching Shallum the son of Josiah
Jeremiah.english_translation: He is Zedekiah, and so he is called (1 Chronicles 3): “the fourth Shallum.” And he calls him the fourth in the kingship among the sons of Josiah, for first Jehoahaz reigned, and after him Jehoiakim, and after him Jehoiachin, and after him Zedekiah.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed reference “1 Chronicles 3” is 3:15.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: who went forth out of this place
Jeremiah.english_translation: And even though he had not yet gone out, he prophesies about him as if he had gone out.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Woe unto him that buildeth his house by unrighteousness
Jeremiah.english_translation: He says this concerning Jehoiakim, who was wicked, and the end of the passage proves it: “Therefore thus saith the LORD concerning Jehoiakim,” etc.
A large house, like “men of great stature” (*anshei middot*, Numbers 13:32), in which there is something to measure.

And he enlarged for him. Others emended it to *vekara lo* — and opened for him; and so “thou enlargest thine eyes with paint” (above, 14), “Oh, that Thou wouldest rend the heavens” (Isaiah 63:19) — all are an expression of opening.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “above 14” is Jeremiah 4:30.

Jeremiah.english_translation: He covers the roof with cedars.

And paints with pigments. Targum Jonathan: *shashar* is a colour, of the kind of paintings. Another version: *mashuaḥ* like the line of measure (*ḥut ha-mishḥah*) — *[printed Old French: אליינאנ"ט אנשינופל"א]* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Compressed; rendered literally. The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Wilt thou lengthen days because thou vyest to make thy rule heavy, to make known that thou art king?

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Did not thy father eat and drink
Jeremiah.english_translation: Josiah, who conducted himself with humility. Did he not eat and drink and see good all the days of his life?
To steal money.

Crushing the poor; and “oppression” will testify of it, for *ashuk* and *ratsuts* are always adjacent in the language of Scripture, and so “whom have I defrauded? or whom have I oppressed?” (1 Samuel 12:3).
Woe over his splendour.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: He shall be buried with the burial of an ass
Jeremiah.english_translation: Aramaic (Targum Jonathan): “As they throw out the carcass of an ass, so shall they throw out his carcass.” *Yishgerun* — they will drag.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Go up to Lebanon, and cry
Jeremiah.english_translation: Aramaic (Targum): “Go up to the Temple, and cry out.”

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: lift up thy voice in Bashan
Jeremiah.english_translation: Over the Bashan, that it will be destroyed. And the Targum: “and at the gates of the Temple mount.” And I do not know how to explain how the word *Bashan* fits the gates of the Temple Mount — unless it be because of the doors that they make from the oaks of Bashan, which is the name of a place; or the word *Bashan* is an expression of a place of wide breach, such being the circuit of the Temple Mount, an open space for the Temple.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The printed abbreviation בה"מ is read as “the Temple.” Rashi himself says he does not know how to explain the Targum’s rendering.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Targum: “and cry out over *Magizta*” — and they are an expression of a place.
When thou wast at ease.
All thy kings.
An east wind shall break them.
That thou hast set thy nest in the towers, houses of cedar, to build great houses.

How wilt thou find favour in the eyes of thy plunderers, on account of the height of thy towers, when the pangs of childbirth come upon thee? And Menahem explained *nehanat* as an expression of encamping (*ḥaniyyah*), but Dunash interpreted it as an expression of grace (*ḥen*).

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: the signet upon My right hand
Jeremiah.english_translation: Engraved and sealed in the flesh of My arm.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: yet would I pluck thee thence
Jeremiah.english_translation: *Etkenkha*: I will tear thee away (*antikekha*), an expression of “Pull them out like sheep for the slaughter” (above, 12), “till we have drawn them away” (Joshua 8:6); and the *nun* is extra in it. And aggadic midrash: in the place where he was torn away, he was repaired (*nitkan*), for he repented in Babylon; and the Holy One, blessed be He, was asked concerning that which He had sworn, “Write you this man childless” (here). And Zerubbabel was born to him in Babylon, and it was said to him through the prophet, “In that day … will I take thee, O Zerubbabel, My servant, the son of Shealtiel … and will make thee as a signet” (below, end of 43), because He had said to his father, “were he the signet upon My right hand, I would pluck him thence.”
Jeremiah.translator_note: The printed reference “below, end of 43” does not correspond to the quotation, which is Haggai 2:23. The explanation of “because He had said to his father” is compressed; rendered literally. Printed “above 12” is Jeremiah 12:3.

Jeremiah.english_translation: An expression of casting.
An expression of consolations, for their souls lift themselves up to be consoled and to say: “We shall yet return to our land.”
It is in astonishment: Is this man, who was cast out from before Me, perhaps a broken and despised image, like one in whom there is no desire?

Shattered, as in “Thou shalt dash them in pieces like a potter’s vessel” (Psalms 2:9). And others emended *ha-etsev* to be like “they swaddle (*me‘atsevin*) the infant” in tractate Shabbat — that is, art thou despised and shattered in thine eyes like a little infant that they swaddle — *[printed Old French: מילויילי"ר]* in Old French? This is not fitting.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The final remark is brief and rendered literally. Old French printed מילויילי"ר; Darmesteter has the entry “un enfant qu’on emmaillote” and notes that the old form is *emmailloter*.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Cast away — an expression of casting which has no rising, as in “Though he fall, he shall not be utterly cast down” (Psalms 37).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “Psalms 37” is 37:24.

Jeremiah.english_translation: From his land he went into exile to another land; and thou, Land of Israel, hear the word of HaShem. Another explanation: “Land, land, land” — the land that is the land of the lands, which was the most important of all. Another explanation: the Land of Israel; there were three lands in it: Judah, the Transjordan, and the Galilee.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: A man that shall not prosper in his days
Jeremiah.english_translation: Write him down as a man who will not prosper in his days.
The kings of Judah.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: have not taken care of them
Jeremiah.english_translation: You were not careful to guard them.
And they shall not be missed — an expression of “and there lacketh not one man of us” (Numbers 31).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “Numbers 31” is 31:49 (JPS wording quoted).

Jeremiah.english_translation: And will succeed.
HaShem will make us righteous in the days of this one.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: My heart within me is broken
Jeremiah.english_translation: For the words of the prophets who say, “You shall have peace,” my heart is broken. *Raḥafu*: they go and tremble like the wings of a bird that hovers over its nest — *[printed Old French: טרנבליר"ט]* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed טרנבליר"ט; Darmesteter has the entry glossed “frissonnent” (they shiver), with the form *trenblent*. The printed form reads as the verb *trembler*.

Jeremiah.english_translation: For I hear from Him this evil decree.
A false oath.
Laid waste.
*[Printed Old French: קורש"א]* in Old French; and Targum Jonathan: an expression of will.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Not rightly.
Even these, from whom all learn.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: in My house have I found their wickedness
Jeremiah.english_translation: For they set up an image in the Temple hall.
A smooth land, in which the foot slips and the man falls.
Stumbling upon stumbling. In slippery places in the light there is stumbling; in darkness without slippery places there is stumbling.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: unseemliness in the prophets of Samaria
Jeremiah.english_translation: Before they were exiled.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: in the prophets of Jerusalem I have seen a horrible thing
Jeremiah.english_translation: I now see an abomination, a shameful thing.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: they strengthen the hands of evil-doers
Jeremiah.english_translation: They say to the wicked, “You shall have peace.”

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: none doth return from his wickedness
Jeremiah.english_translation: That the evildoers not return, each from his evil.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: walketh in the stubbornness of his own heart
Jeremiah.english_translation: “And to every one that walketh in the stubbornness of his own heart,” etc.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: who hath stood in the council of the LORD
Jeremiah.english_translation: “And hear” what is decreed from before Him — he who attended to the word of His Torah and hearkened to His commandments, and not these wicked ones. The first “hearing” in this verse is actual hearing; the last “hearing” is acceptance.
It settles, returns to settle; “and upon the head of the wicked it shall settle.”
Jeremiah.translator_note: The printed quotation reads *yishkon* (“shall settle”) where the verse reads *yaḥul* (“shall whirl”); translated as printed.

Jeremiah.english_translation: An expression of thought.
They should have made My words and My Torah heard to My people, and not mislead them with it away from Me.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Am I a God near at hand
Jeremiah.english_translation: That I see only what is near Me, and I have no power to judge the lower beings, who are far from Me, and I do not know their deeds.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Can any hide himself in secret places
Jeremiah.english_translation: This is a double astonishment — “Am I a God near at hand?” — in the manner of all doubled expressions of astonishment.
“They prophesy lies.” And is it in the heart of these prophets who prophesy falsehood, to fulfil their thoughts which they think, to make My people forget My name, etc.?
Jeremiah.translator_note: Rashi’s sentence is elliptical; rendered literally.

Jeremiah.english_translation: An expression of deceit.
Let him tell it as an idle matter, like other dreams, and not strengthen it with words of prophecy.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: What hath the straw to do with the wheat
Jeremiah.english_translation: What has falsehood to do with truth?
With the grain.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Is not My word like as fire
Jeremiah.english_translation: They should not have erred and likened dreams, saying that they are prophecy; for a word of prophecy, when it comes into the mouth of the prophet, comes into him with might, like a burning fire, as it is said, “there is in my heart as it were a burning fire” (above, 20), and it says, “and the hand of the LORD was strong upon me” (Ezekiel 3:14).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “above 20” is Jeremiah 20:9 (JPS wording quoted).

Jeremiah.english_translation: *Pic* in Old French; and some say *martel* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed פי"ק; Darmesteter has the entry *pic*. The second form, מרטיי"ל, is transparently *martel* (“hammer”) but was not located in Darmesteter.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: that steal My words every one from his neighbour
Jeremiah.english_translation: “Every one from his neighbour”: they have spies among the true prophets, and hear the manner of speech in which they prophesy, and speak false prophecy in that same language, as Hananiah son of Azzur did. He heard Jeremiah prophesying in the upper market, “Behold, I will break the bow of Elam,” and he prophesied in the lower market, “I have broken the yoke of the king of Babylon” (below, 28), as our Rabbis said in Sanhedrin.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “below 28” is Jeremiah 28:2; Jeremiah’s words are at 49:35 (JPS wording quoted).

Jeremiah.english_translation: Who teach their tongue to say their lies in the expression “saith HaShem,” like the true prophets, so that they will be believed.
An expression of astonishment; *estordison* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed אישטורדיזו"ן; Darmesteter has the entry *estordisoun*.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: What is the burden of the LORD
Jeremiah.english_translation: An expression of mockery, since his prophecy to them is a burden.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: What burden! I will cast you off
Jeremiah.english_translation: They say to you, “What is the burden?” You are a burden to the Holy One, blessed be He, and He said that He will cast you off and throw you from His arms, from heaven to earth; so I heard.
And I will forsake.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: own word shall be his burden
Jeremiah.english_translation: Although you pervert “the burden” into a disgrace — “the burden of the word of HaShem” is for a man’s word and for a man’s counsel, which He reveals — and you pervert it into the sense of a load: this I did not hear so, though it is the principal one. But so I heard: that the load will be a load of punishment for the one who says it, the one who asks, “What is the burden?” Another explanation: “the burden of HaShem” is an expression of prophecy. And the false prophet would ask the true prophet to tell him the word of the Holy One, blessed be He, in the manner of expression in which it came to him; and the manner of expression did not explain the utterance so much, and the false prophet would pervert the interpretation to another side and would speak in the likeness of the true prophet, so that they would believe him; and so did Hananiah son of Azzur. Therefore He says: Do not ask “the burden of HaShem” — that manner of expression — but rather “What hath He answered” and “What hath He spoken” — the interpretation of the matter. Ask the true prophet to tell them what the Holy One, blessed be He, says and to where His words incline.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Long and compressed; “signon” rendered as “manner of expression.” The sentence beginning “this I did not hear so, though it is the principal one” is rendered literally and its reference is not fully clear.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: own word shall be his burden
Jeremiah.english_translation: A manner of expression: plainly, “the Holy One, blessed be He, said it”; plainly, “to a man his counsel,” who is not suspected of perverting it. But you ask Him in order to pervert it, and you have perverted the words of the Holy One, blessed be He. And this is what He said above, “that steal My words every one from his neighbour” (here); this, too, is a superfluous expression.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Rendered literally; the closing remark is brief and its precise reference is not stated.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Thus shalt thou say to the prophet
Jeremiah.english_translation: When you come to ask the words from the prophet.
An expression of “the sinew of the thigh-vein” (Genesis 32:33), and an expression of “their might hath failed” (below, 51): leaping and being shaken from place to place.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “below 51” is Jeremiah 51:30 (JPS wording quoted).

Jeremiah.english_translation: Pots.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: set before the temple of the LORD
Jeremiah.english_translation: Prepared.

And the smith — Torah scholars who were exiled with Jeconiah; and I already explained it in the book (2 Kings 24): *haḥarash vehamasger* — *[printed Old French: לימייטראה ליפורטי"ר]* in Old French. Another explanation: *haḥarash* is an expression of “deaf,” and *hamasger* is an expression of “shut”: that is, great sages in the Torah, so that when one of them spoke, all were silent; “shut,” because they would shut and none would open.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed לימייטראה ליפורטי"ר; not found in Darmesteter; left as printed. Printed “2 Kings 24” is 24:14 or 24:16.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Which ripened fully at the beginning of the first-fruits of the figs, which are dear to those who find them at their beginning.
This is a transposed verse: so will I regard for good the captivity of Judah, whom I already exiled — Jeconiah and his exile.
An expression of uprooting.
That they will hear the evil coming upon them and tremble.
That all will repeat and speak of their punishment.

The year in which their decree was sealed — that they would be exiled, and that they would drink the cup of wrath, as it is stated in the passage, “Take this cup,” etc. And before the decree was sealed He told the prophet to rebuke them, perhaps they would repent and their decree not be sealed.
Josiah reigned thirty-one years; take away from them twelve years; there remain nineteen; and four of his son — behold, twenty-three.
An expression of the present: I was rising early and speaking continually.
It is a sign of the circumcision feast, because they grind and crush spices for it for healing.
A sign of a feast; so we learned in Sanhedrin.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: all that is written in this book
Jeremiah.english_translation: Against Babylon.
At its end.
Like “for they shall make bondmen of them” — of the Babylonians.
Media and Persia.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: cup of the wine of fury
Jeremiah.english_translation: The prophecy of punishment.
Prophesy to them that it will not be turned back again by any repentance.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Hebrew *shelo tashuv od bishum teshuvah* could also be read “that thou shalt not return again with any reply”; rendered literally.

Jeremiah.english_translation: And they will go mad.
An expression of folly; they will be demented.
As they are today, after the destruction; Jeremiah wrote his book.
All the support (*somkhuta*) that Pharaoh pledged, and his staff upon them for help. *Ha‘erev* — *[printed Old French: גרנטיא"ה]* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed גרנטיא"ה; Darmesteter has *garantie* (guarantee).

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: the isle which is beyond the sea
