Jeremiah.english_translation: All these eight listed until here are neighbours of the Land of Israel.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: the corners of their hair polled
Jeremiah.english_translation: Those cut off at the edge of that direction.
Arabia.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: all the kings of the mingled people
Jeremiah.english_translation: The support of the Arabs.
It is Babylon, by *at-bash*: *bet-shin*.
Like a man who drinks too much and vomits.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: the sword which I will send among you
Jeremiah.english_translation: The strife of war.
Beginning.
He mourns over the destruction of his house.
An expression of *hoy*: for those who do heavy work call out in a loud voice to urge one another to strengthen themselves, and treaders of winepresses are accustomed to it.
Every expression of *aniyyah* is a calling out in a loud voice.
He contends in judgment.
That I set them at odds with one another.
As its Targum: from the ends.
An expression of wailing.
Roll about in the dust — *[printed Old French: ווטרליי"ר]* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed ווטרליי"ר; Darmesteter has *voltrer* (modern French *se vautrer*).

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: I will break you in pieces
Jeremiah.english_translation: This is an abbreviated verse; that is, “and your dispersions are drawing near to come.”
That is: if you say, “We are very important,” there are precious vessels of glass that fall and are shattered and lost.
An expression of desolation, an expression of *hidamnu*; and “let us be cut off there” (above, 8).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “above 8” is Jeremiah 8:14 (JPS wording quoted).

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: forsaken His covert, as the lion
Jeremiah.english_translation: The king went into exile from his cities, like a young lion that leaves its lair.
Drunk with wine; so Targum Jonathan. Another explanation: an expression of oppression (*ona’ah*).

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: In the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim
Jeremiah.english_translation: This latter section preceded the former by four years.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: When the princes of Judah heard these things
Jeremiah.english_translation: For the false prophets and the priests had seized Jeremiah.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: the entry of the new gate
Jeremiah.english_translation: Others emended: When Jehoiachin was exiled, and some of all the house of our God with him, the army of Nebuchadnezzar broke the eastern gate, and Zedekiah returned and repaired it and renewed it; therefore it is called “new.”
Jeremiah.translator_note: “And some of all the house of our God with him” is rendered literally; its precise sense is not stated.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Of Moresheth (Aramaic *demin Marisha*).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Rashi’s form is *Marisha* (Mareshah), where the verse has *Morashti*; translated as printed.

Jeremiah.english_translation: *Galim* [mounds].

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: entreat the favour of the LORD
Jeremiah.english_translation: An expression of prayer.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Thus might we procure great evil
Jeremiah.english_translation: If we kill him.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: there was also a man that prophesied
Jeremiah.english_translation: The one who said this did not say that. Up to here are the words of the righteous; and the wicked who were there arose and said, “also a man prophesying,” etc.: As Uriah was killed, let Jeremiah be killed. So it is explained in the Sifrei.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Rendered literally; the printed source name is “Sifrei.”

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: In the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim
Jeremiah.english_translation: Three years before Nebuchadnezzar reigned, he prophesied about him that he would reign.
They are the straps of the yoke, which are called *[printed Old French: קוריגל"ש]*.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed קוריגל"ש; Darmesteter glosses “des courroies” (straps) and corrects the reading to *cojongles* (from *cingula*; modern French *sangles*).

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: send them to the king of Edom
Jeremiah.english_translation: In the days of Zedekiah, in the fourth year of his reign, when Nebuchadnezzar made him ruler over five kings.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: king of Moab, and to the king of the children of Ammon
Jeremiah.english_translation: These are five kings whom Nebuchadnezzar placed under the hand of Zedekiah. For fifteen years they were on his neck, from one year of Jehoiakim until the fourth year of Zedekiah, when Hananiah son of Azzur broke them from him.
Jeremiah.translator_note: “They were on his neck” is rendered literally; the reckoning of the fifteen years is not spelled out in the text.

Jeremiah.english_translation: That he will do My will, to exact retribution from My enemies.
Evil-merodach.
Belshazzar.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: until the time of his own land come
Jeremiah.english_translation: That Darius the Mede and Cyrus will come and kill Belshazzar.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: I spoke to Zedekiah king of Judah
Jeremiah.english_translation: All this Jeremiah said to the messengers of the kings.
Which were exiled with Jeconiah.
Targum Jonathan: *basisaya*, like “the laver and its base” (Exodus 35:16).
Like *behagloto* [in his being exiled].

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: all the nobles of Judah and Jerusalem
Jeremiah.english_translation: Like *sarei* [princes].

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: until the day that I remember them
Jeremiah.english_translation: In the days of Cyrus, as is explained in the Book of Ezra.

When that time arrived, in which Nebuchadnezzar had made Zedekiah ruler over five kings, Jeremiah was delivering his mission and sending the bands and the yokes to the kings by the hand of their messengers.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: in the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah
Jeremiah.english_translation: At the beginning, when he made him ruler over the five kings. And it is impossible to say “at the beginning of his reign,” for it says “in the fourth year”: that year he went down to appear before Nebuchadnezzar in Babylon, and Seraiah, the quartermaster, with him, as is said at the end of the book (51:59); and he made him ruler over the kings.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: spoke unto me in the house of the LORD
Jeremiah.english_translation: Our Rabbis said: Who misled Hananiah? He heard that Jeremiah was prophesying in the upper market, “Behold, I will break the bow of Elam” (below, 49), and this prophecy was spoken at the end of the book, at the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah, as is explained there. And because Elam is near Babylon, he arose in the lower market and expounded and reasoned *kal vaḥomer*: If Elam, which came only to help the Chaldeans, etc. — as it is in Sanhedrin.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “below 49” is Jeremiah 49:35 (JPS wording quoted).

Jeremiah.english_translation: *[Printed Old French: פאצ"א]* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed פאצ"א; it appears to be the subjunctive of *faire* (“may He do”), but it was not found in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Jeremiah.english_translation: An expression of prayer. *[Parenthetical in the printed text, unreadable: של"ש שטי"ן אלו ע"ד והביא"ו לבית הכל"א לא סדר"ן הר"ב המחב"ר]* (“Amen, so may HaShem do,” etc. The masters of Aggadah say that thus he said to him: ‘Would that your words be fulfilled! I profit and you lose. I am a priest and eat the holy things of heaven if the House stands in its building; and you are a Gibeonite, as it is written here) “who is of Gibeon,” and “thou shalt be to me a servant, hewer of wood and drawer of water” (and *Moreh Tsedek*, who did not explain, holds the reason of our Rabbis, who learned from here: whoever flatters a wicked person falls in the end into his hand, or into the hand of his son, or into the hand of his son’s son; for Irijah son of Shelemiah son of Hananiah seized him [Jeremiah] at the end and brought him to the prison).
Jeremiah.translator_note: The first parenthetical consists of abbreviations that could not be deciphered and is left as printed. The sentence about *Moreh Tsedek* is rendered literally; its meaning is unclear. The words “thou shalt be to me a servant, hewer of wood and drawer of water” are not in this verse. For Irijah son of Shelemiah son of Hananiah see Jeremiah 37:13.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Until “the prophet who prophesieth of peace”: he said, “I prophesy punishments; if it does not come, I am not a liar — the Holy One, blessed be He, repented of the evil. But the prophet who prophesieth of peace,” etc.: when the word of the prophet comes, he is known, etc.; but if his word does not come, he is a liar, as it is said, “God is not a man, that He should lie” (Numbers 23:19). So Rabbi Tanhuma expounded.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: the beasts of the field also
Jeremiah.english_translation: That he rode upon a lion and tied a serpent to its head.
And in the coming year thou shalt be buried.

But the seventh month is not [counted] of that year; rather he died on the eve of Rosh Hashanah and commanded his sons to bury him after Rosh Hashanah and not before, and they concealed his death that day, in order to make the prophecy of Jeremiah false.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The abbreviation ער"ה is read as “the eve of Rosh Hashanah” (*erev Rosh Hashanah*); the sentence is rendered literally.

Jeremiah.english_translation: The king’s mother.
An expression of incitement, like “The serpent beguiled me” (Genesis 3).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 3” is 3:13.

Jeremiah.english_translation: In My ways; and this is an abbreviated verse.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: the king that sitteth upon the throne of David
Jeremiah.english_translation: Zedekiah, who was not exiled.
An expression of horror (Hosea 6).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “Hosea 6” is 6:10: “a horrible thing” (JPS).

Jeremiah.english_translation: That they will reproach them — *[printed Old French: דשטרווי"ר]* in Old French; and so every “reproach” in Scripture.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed דשטרווי"ר; Darmesteter has *destraber*, glossed “à l’outrage.”

Jeremiah.english_translation: An expression of roasting in fire (Leviticus 2).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “Leviticus 2” is 2:14: “parched with fire” (JPS).

Jeremiah.english_translation: As is explained in Sanhedrin: Thus said the Holy One, blessed be He: “Lie with my fellow.”
An expression of testimony.
The name of a place.
He wrote thus to Zephaniah.
Appointed ones.
A dome (*kippah*).
A block [*sadan*] — *[printed Old French: ציפ"ש]* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed ציפ"ש; Darmesteter glosses “les ceps” (the stocks).

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: forasmuch as he hath sent unto us
Jeremiah.english_translation: For thou shouldest have rebuked him for having sent to us in Babylon, saying: “Your exile there is long.”
Like *al asher* [because].
And thou shalt not say, “Why should I write it? For they will all perish and none will read in it and none will remember it any more.” “For, lo, the days come,” etc.
Some interpret it of the report from Babylon, from which those who were exiled there trembled; and aggadic midrash — of the war of Gog and Magog.
Is it the way of males to give birth, that pangs seize them like a woman in travail?
Like *motnav* [his loins].
The day of the killing of Belshazzar and the fall of Babylon. Another explanation: the day of the fall of Gog.
The yoke of the nations will be removed from upon Israel.
Of all the evils that thou shalt see coming upon Babylon, in which thou art.
Like *veshaket* [and quiet].
With restrained judgment.
An expression of sweeping away, destruction.
*Shivrekha* [thy fracture]: *[printed Old French: אנפר"ש]* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed אנפר"ש; Darmesteter reads the form as *énfers* (from *infirmus*, “weak, infirm”).

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: that it may be bound up
Jeremiah.english_translation: A remedy: no man thinks that there will be salvation for thee.
A remedy, an expression of benefit.
Afflictions of cruelty; the chastisement is cruel.
An oath.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: they that spoil thee shall be a spoil
Jeremiah.english_translation: An expression of plunder; and Targum Jonathan: *vihon ‘adayikh le‘adei*.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Aramaic is transliterated as printed.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Healing.
The Temple.
That they will be a numerous (*kaved*) people.
Like *yime‘atu* [they shall be diminished].
Their prince.
An expression of pledge (*eravon*) — *[printed Old French: פרוויל"א הטינ"א]* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed פרוויל"א הטינ"א; Darmesteter reads the two nouns *fermaille* (from *firmacula*) and *haatine* (his “aatine”), which correspond to the sense of pledging.

Jeremiah.english_translation: To war, to restrain My hand.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Literally “to protest against My hand” (*lemaḥot beyadi*).

Jeremiah.english_translation: Encamping and dwelling, an expression of “the land of my sojournings”; and its counterpart, “a whirling storm” (above, 23), stated in the other verse, is this one, for both are an expression of encamping.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “above 22” is Jeremiah 23:19 (JPS wording quoted). Rashi’s phrase “the land of my sojournings” is not found verbatim in Scripture; rendered as printed.

Jeremiah.english_translation: On the head of the idolaters.
In the eyes of the generation of the wilderness.
Egypt, and Amalek, and the Canaanite.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: when I go to cause him to rest
Jeremiah.english_translation: When they go to inherit the land of their rest.
By the merit of the fathers.
To me, the prophet; and He said to me to say to the Congregation of Israel, “With an everlasting love have I loved thee.”

Two buildings were yours, made by the hand of man; therefore they were destroyed. “Again will I build thee”: I Myself, a third building, and thou shalt be built for ever. *Ta‘di*: thou shalt be adorned.
In the fourth year they shall “profane” the fruit [of the vineyard], to redeem it with money.

Scouts on the tops of high towers, to proclaim a voice that is heard from afar. Another explanation: *notserim* is like “keeping mercy unto the thousandth generation” (Exodus 34:7), an expression of guarding: that is, there is a day when they will call to those who kept the Torah, and will say, “Arise.” And Targum Jonathan: “For there is length of days and abundant good that is destined to come to the righteous who kept My Torah from of old.”

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: shout at the head of the nations
Jeremiah.english_translation: On high towers, so that they will be heard from afar.
Even those among them who stumble, I will not reject.
Through prayer and repentance.
*[Printed Old French: ספריינ"ש]* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Jeremiah.english_translation: They will gather like a river.
Oil.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: A voice is heard in Ramah
Jeremiah.english_translation: “A voice on high of the world was heard, the voice of the House of Israel weeping for Jeremiah the prophet, when Nebuzaradan sent him from Ramah to return after the exiles to Gedaliah son of Ahikam,” as is said in this book (below, 39).
Jeremiah.translator_note: The passage is Aramaic in the printed text. Printed “below 39” refers to Jeremiah 39:14 and 40:1.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Aggadic midrash: it said that the patriarchs and matriarchs went to appease the Holy One, blessed be He, because Manasseh had set up an image in the Temple hall, and He was not appeased. Rachel entered and said before Him: “Master of the Universe, whose compassion is greater — Thy compassion, or the compassion of flesh and blood? Say: Thy compassion is greater. Did not I bring my rival into my house? For all the service that Jacob served my father he served only for my sake; when I came to enter the bridal canopy, they brought in my sister; and it was not enough that I kept silent, but I gave her my signs. So Thou too, if Thy sons have brought Thy rival into Thy house, be silent for them.” He said to her: “Well hast thou argued the defence; there is reward for thy deed and for thy righteousness, that thou gavest thy signs to thy sister.”
*Conpleint* [printed קומפליינ"ט] in Old French, an expression of “Who shall bemoan thee” (above, 19).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed קומפליינ"ט; Darmesteter has *conpleint*. Printed “above 19” is Jeremiah 15:5 (JPS wording quoted).

Jeremiah.english_translation: Through afflictions, Thou, the Holy One, blessed be He.
*[Printed Old French: פושאגויילונ"י]* in Old French, an expression of “the ox-goad” (Judges 4). At first I was so; therefore I sinned against Thee.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. Printed “Judges 4” is Judges 3:31 (“ox-goad,” JPS).

Jeremiah.english_translation: I regret my abominations.
That I reflected upon myself, that I had trespassed — *aperçuy* [printed אפרינו"יי] in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed אפרינו"יי; Darmesteter reads *aperçuy je* (“I perceived”), glossing the verse “après avoir pris connaissance.”

Jeremiah.english_translation: That my enemies can revile me for the sin of my youth.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Is Ephraim a darling son unto Me
Jeremiah.english_translation: These are the words of the Shekhinah; that is: He is wavering, and my heart is turned over within me to have compassion — perhaps he is my darling son; like one who has only one son, for whom he does all his will — delights (*sha‘ashu‘im*): *esbaniement* [printed אישבניימני"ץ] in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed אישבניימני"ץ; Darmesteter has *esbaniement* (cf. Godefroy, *esbanoi*).

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: as often as I speak of him
Jeremiah.english_translation: At every time that I speak of him; and the midrash of Leviticus Rabbah: “*Dei* — of the utterances that I put in him, that I taught him My Torah — to have compassion on him.”
Jeremiah.translator_note: The citation of Leviticus Rabbah is rendered literally; its precise sense is not spelled out.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Signs on the roads of thy good fathers.

Small palm trees planted as a sign on the road. And the plain sense of the verse: Make signs, to know the road by which thou wentest from the Land of Israel to Babylon, so that thou mayest return by that same road — that is, surely thou wilt return from there.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: the way by which thou wentest
Jeremiah.english_translation: *Halakhta* is written *halakhti* [“I went”]: and everywhere thou didst go, I went with thee. And Jonathan translated: “Set up for thyself bitter ones: pray with the bitterness of thy soul.” (And Menahem explained *tamrurim* as an expression of *mo‘al*, and so he explained “and pillars of smoke” [Joel 3:3]. *Sa”a*.)
Jeremiah.translator_note: The parenthetical about Menahem is rendered literally; the sense of *mo‘al* and the closing abbreviation סא"א are not clear. “Pillars of smoke” is Joel 3:3 (JPS).

Jeremiah.english_translation: Thou wilt hide from Me, ashamed to return to Me because of thy way. Behold, a new thing is created in the earth: that the female will go after the male to seek him, that he may take her — an expression of “go about the city … I will seek him” (Song of Songs 3:2); and in the name of Rabbi Judah the Preacher I heard: “A female shall go around to become a man.” I set thee as a daughter who takes a tenth of the estate — seven nations out of seventy; in the end thou shalt take all, like a male son who inherits all.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The final teaching of Rabbi Judah the Preacher is rendered literally; Rashi’s compressed wording is not expanded.

Jeremiah.english_translation: So said Jeremiah: All that time that I was sleeping and slumbering in prophecy of punishment, in this prophecy I awoke from my slumber.
Pleasant.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: seed of man, and with the seed of beast
Jeremiah.english_translation: The good and the foolish among them — I will sow all of them, to be My seed. “The seed of man and the seed of beast”: Jonathan translated: “I will establish them as sons of man, and I will make them prosper as the beast whose iniquities are not visited upon it.”
A fruit that is not ripened, and it dulls the teeth.
The sons are punished for the iniquity of the fathers.
*[Printed Old French: איאקלארזי"ר]* in Old French, and so Targum Jonathan: *lanhara*.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed איאקלארזי"ר; it appears to be a form of *esclairier* (“to illuminate”) but was not found in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Moves it and makes it boil, and it becomes folds upon folds, like “my skin closeth up” (Job 7).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “Job 7” is 7:5 (JPS wording quoted).

Jeremiah.english_translation: Like *lo yamish* [“shall not depart”].
How high they are.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: cast off all the seed of Israel
Jeremiah.english_translation: Concerning Israel — that is: just as they will not be measured and not searched out, so Israel will not be cast off for all that they have sinned.
A valley where the corpses of the camp of Sennacherib fell.
The place where the ashes were poured out, which was outside Jerusalem. They will add it to the city and bring all this within its walls; and this prophecy is destined to come.
*[Printed Old French: קנפני"א]* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed קנפני"א; Darmesteter reads *canpanye* (“les plaines”).

Jeremiah.english_translation: An expression of siege.
An expression of a house of guarding.
The “remembrance” of every man is death.
He did not say so to Zedekiah; rather the verse explains why he shut him up, and returns to its first utterance to explain what the matter was that came to Jeremiah.
By the word [of HaShem].
The bill of sale.
With its seal, when it is sealed according to law and statute.

That which was established in a court on the strength of its witnesses, and the judges wrote it and signed it — *asharta dedayyanei*, which is the confirmation of deeds, to make the matter open and publicized, lest the witnesses die. And our Rabbis explained it with regard to a plain *get* and a tied one, in Bava Batra.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: in the presence of Hanamel mine uncle
Jeremiah.english_translation: And until now they called him “my uncle’s son”; perhaps there were two, and if not, I do not know what this is. Some tend to say that Hanamel was both uncle and cousin of Jeremiah — for example, Reuben married the daughter of Simeon his brother, and she bore him Nemuel, and Simeon had already begotten Jamin; behold, Jamin is the uncle of Nemuel, for he is the son of the brother of his mother, and also his cousin, for he is the son of Simeon, the brother of the father of Nemuel. But that is not the usage, for we do not find anywhere in Scripture the brother of the mother called *dod*.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The site’s English text reads “mine uncle[’s son],” the bracket being the translators’ note on the Hebrew.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Do not say, “I am hiding them for nothing, for all are going into exile.”
In the end they will buy houses.
It will not be hidden. And Thou knowest that in the end we shall go into exile; and why didst Thou tell me to buy a field?

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: into the bosom of their children after them
Jeremiah.english_translation: This generation, who walk after their fathers in the evil way.
And he did not say “and the revered.” He said: Idolaters leap about in His Temple; where are His awesome deeds? In tractate Yoma.

Among other people. Another explanation: signs that were balanced for Israel and for Egypt. How? “And there was the cloud and the darkness here, yet gave it light by night there” (Exodus 14:20) — the very same sign that served as darkness for Egypt served as light for Israel. Aggadic midrash.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Thou hast caused all this evil to befall them
Jeremiah.english_translation: Thou hast caused to befall them — an expression of happenstance.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: what Thou hast spoken is come to pass
Jeremiah.english_translation: Evil that was and is coming upon it.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: the city is given into the hand of the Chaldeans
Jeremiah.english_translation: And why do I need a field?
Are future things hidden from Me?

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: from the day that they built it
Jeremiah.english_translation: On the day that the Temple was founded, Solomon married the daughter of Pharaoh.
An expression of action — *aprenant* [printed אפרננ"ט] in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed אפרננ"ט; Darmesteter glosses this verse “et leur apprenant.”

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: I will gather them out of all the countries
Jeremiah.english_translation: In mercy, from everything to which I drove them there in My anger.
In the prison.
He who does this.
To make known to thee the things to come.
Preserved in My heart, to do them.
To make of them mounds — heaps piled up on high, which the people of the city build in order to go up on the mounds to fight from above against the Chaldeans.
Aramaic: “To strengthen the wall before those who slay with the sword.”

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: to fill them with the dead bodies of men
Jeremiah.english_translation: And the houses that they tore down they make into graves for the corpses of those who are slain within the city.
“Thus saith HaShem: Behold, I will bring it healing,” etc.
A blessing of peace — *saloud* [printed שלוד] in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed שלוד; Darmesteter has *saloud* (“salut”).

Jeremiah.english_translation: A dwelling of shepherds.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: pass under the hands of him that counteth them
Jeremiah.english_translation: Israel will go out and come in through a leader who goes at their head.
A cutting-off for ever — unless it ceases; its end is to return.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The sentence is brief and elliptical; rendered literally.

Jeremiah.english_translation: A seed fit to offer a burnt-offering and to burn a meal-offering shall not be cut off from them.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: break My covenant with the day
Jeremiah.english_translation: If you can break My covenant that I made with the day and with the night, that they be in their time, which I made with Noah and his sons: “and day and night shall not cease” (Genesis 8:22).
The kingship and the priesthood.
And by these words they cause My people to despise being a nation unto Me.
In the face of these their words, with which they teach them to say: The Holy One, blessed be He, will not turn back from His anger any more, and repentance will not avail you.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: if I have not appointed the ordinances of heaven and earth
Jeremiah.english_translation: It is impossible that the covenant that I made with the day and the night, that they be in their time, should not stand, and it is impossible that the ordinances of heaven and earth be annulled, as if I had not appointed them. “Then will I also cast away the seed of Jacob,” etc. And our Rabbis expounded it with regard to the covenant of the Torah, to learn from here that for the sake of the Torah heaven and earth were created; but the midrash is not settled according to the order of the verses.

Our Rabbis said that Nebuchadnezzar died in his [Zedekiah’s] days; for all the days of Nebuchadnezzar his prisoners did not go out of their prisons; and when Nebuchadnezzar died, Zedekiah went out of the prison house, and the next day he died and they buried him with honour.
Thus was their way: to burn upon the kings their beds and the vessels of their use.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: after that the king Zedekiah had made a covenant
Jeremiah.english_translation: In the seventh year of his reign. So we learned in Seder Olam: “And it came to pass in the seventh year that certain men of the elders of Judah came to inquire of HaShem; they said to Ezekiel: A priest’s slave whom his master sold — may he eat of the terumah?” That is, because they wished to say that he was not punished on account of the commandments, since they had taken back the slaves.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The last sentence is rendered literally; its subject (“he was not punished”) is not specified. The verse quoted from Seder Olam is Ezekiel 20:1, whose JPS text reads “elders of Israel.”

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: I proclaim for you a liberty
Jeremiah.english_translation: From Me, who am not a master for you to save; and you will be ownerless, to the sword and to the famine.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: when they cut the calf in twain
Jeremiah.english_translation: When they returned and subdued them [the slaves], all of them made a covenant to rebel against HaMakom, and they cut the calf in two and passed between its parts, to rebel against Him; and it was a strong and complete covenant, saying: “Thus shall he be cut and divided who passes over it.”

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: that are gone up from you
Jeremiah.english_translation: Because of the army of Pharaoh that went out from Egypt, as is explained in this book (37).
And Pharaoh’s army will return to its land, and the Chaldeans will return upon you.
The sons of Jonadab son of Rechab; and they were of the descendants of Jethro.
A prophet of HaShem.
The steward (*amarkal*) — *[printed Old French: טרשורי"ר]* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed טרשורי"ר; it appears to be *tresorier* (“treasurer”) but was not found in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Jeremiah.english_translation: In the wildernesses where you sojourn (*garim*) there; they had no portion in the Land, because they were sons of sojourners (*gerim*).

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: when Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon came up against the land
Jeremiah.english_translation: We came to the city against our will; therefore now we sit in houses.
In the prison.
It is the eastern gate; so Jonathan translated.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: We will surely tell the king
Jeremiah.english_translation: Perhaps he will hear.
*Ḥatserah* — to the court. Every word that requires a *lamed* at its beginning [“to”], he put a *hei* at its end.

Our Rabbis interpreted: wood, named for burning in unity (*aḥvah*) — that is, that they kindle from one another like brothers who benefit one another, *sa”a*. And according to its plain sense, it means a vessel upon which they kindle a fire before the princes.

Our Rabbis said: It was the Scroll of Lamentations. They read before him “How doth the city sit solitary” (Lamentations 1:1), “She weepeth sore in the night” (1:2), “Judah is gone into exile” (1:3), “The ways of Zion do mourn” (1:4) — in all this he took no heed. He said: “I am king over the remnant.” When he read “Her adversaries are become the head” (1:5), he said: “From now on I am not king!” Immediately “he cut it with the penknife.”
Like *kera‘ah* [he tore it].
They supplicated.

At first there were three alphabetical acrostics: “How doth the city sit solitary” (Lamentations 1:1), “How hath the Lord covered with a cloud” (2:1), “How is the gold become dim” (4:1); and he added to it “I am the man” (3:1), for every letter in it is tripled.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Zedekiah the son of Josiah reigned as king
Jeremiah.english_translation: Because from now on he comes to relate and to say that the punishments which he prophesied until here were fulfilled, he began to say so: And when the time of reckoning came, when the days drew near for the words to be fulfilled, “and another king reigned over Judah in place of Coniah the son of Jehoiakim,” etc.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: came in and went out among the people
Jeremiah.english_translation: When Zedekiah reigned, he commanded and they took him out of the prison house in which Jehoiakim had imprisoned him; for Zedekiah was righteous and his generation wicked, and Jehoiakim was wicked and his generation righteous.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: army was come forth out of Egypt
Jeremiah.english_translation: To help Judah.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: shall return to Egypt into their own land
Jeremiah.english_translation: They were coming in ships, and the Holy One, blessed be He, signalled to the sea and it caused [the drowned] to float upon it like bottles and wineskins (that is, swollen), resembling the skins of human beings. They said to one another: What is this? They said: These are our fathers, whom the fathers of those to whose help we are going drowned in the sea. Immediately they returned to their land.
Jeremiah.translator_note: “Caused to float upon it” (*vehetsif alav*) is rendered literally; the bodies are implied.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Aramaic: “to divide his inheritance in the midst of the people.” And while the Chaldeans were besieging it, he did not go out from it, because he was praying for the city that it not be captured.
Appointed to guard, that no man go out of the city to make peace with the Chaldeans.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: the son of Shelemiah, the son of Hananiah
Jeremiah.english_translation: He is Hananiah son of Azzur — this one was his grandson, and therefore Scripture gave his lineage, to teach that whoever flatters a wicked man falls in the end into his hand, or into the hand of his son, or into the hand of his son’s son; and Jeremiah flattered him, for he said to him, “Amen! the LORD perform thy words” (above, 28). And aggadic midrash: that Hananiah commanded his son: See that I am dying by the hand of Jeremiah, and he made me appear a liar in my prophecy; if thou canst cause him to stumble, cause him to stumble. And his son commanded his sons likewise, and when the time came, he caused him to stumble.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “above 28” is Jeremiah 28:6 (JPS wording quoted).

Jeremiah.english_translation: Jonathan translated: *legaw min ḥanvata*. There were shops before that prison house.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Aramaic is rendered as “within, from the shops”; the construction is not explained.

Jeremiah.english_translation: From the market of the bakers, like “thou shalt make streets for thee in Damascus” (1 Kings 20).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “1 Kings 20” is 20:34.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: his life shall be unto him for a prey
Jeremiah.english_translation: And his life shall be a rescue for him, as if he had taken the spoil of his soul, like a man who takes spoil and profits; so shall this one profit his soul.
*[Printed Old French: אלאקנ"ץ]* in Old French, an expression of slackening.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Like *yakhol* [“can”], because he weakeneth, etc.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Rendered literally; the comparison is not spelled out.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Belonging to Malchiah.
Baruch son of Neriah.
Zedekiah: as the Ethiopian is distinguished in his skin, so Zedekiah was distinguished in his righteousness above all his generation. And there is a midrash that expounds “the Ethiopian” of Baruch.
A great man (*gever rav*).
Had they left him in his place he would have died of himself of hunger, and they did evil to hasten his death.
Because their strength was weakened with hunger, all of them were needed.
Worn-out garments that are dragged.
An expression of rot, like “they shall vanish away like smoke” (Isaiah 51).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 51” is 51:6 (JPS wording quoted).

Jeremiah.english_translation: So that the ropes will not hurt thee.
*[Printed Old French: איישילא"ש]* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed איישילא"ש (*aisseles*, “armpits”); Darmesteter has the same word for Ezekiel 13:18 (“aux aisselles”).

Jeremiah.english_translation: I do not know where it is; perhaps it is in the Israelites’ court, since the rampart and the Women’s court are before it.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Rashi himself says he does not know the location.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Afraid.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: lest they deliver me into their hand
Jeremiah.english_translation: The Chaldeans into the hands of the Jews, to say: Let your king be your servant, because you were first to make peace with us.
The Jews — *[printed Old French: איגברונ"ט]* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Jeremiah.english_translation: The false prophets, who said to thee: Thou wilt not be captured.
Mud; an expression of “Can the rush shoot up without mire?”
Jeremiah.translator_note: The quotation is Job 8:11 (JPS wording quoted); Rashi does not name the book.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Behold, thou art as one who burns it with his own hands, for thou art the cause of it.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: all the princes of the king of Babylon came in
Jeremiah.english_translation: This teaches that the prophecy above was fulfilled here: “and they shall set every one his throne at the entrance of the gates of Jerusalem” (above, 1).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “above 1” is Jeremiah 1:15 (JPS wording quoted).

Jeremiah.english_translation: Aramaic *bitra‘a metsi‘ata* — the gate of the Temple court, the Nicanor gate, the eastern one, which is between the gate of the Women’s court and the gate of the Sanctuary. And our Rabbis said: the “middle gate” is the gate in which they decide the halakhot. Of them it says, “in the place of justice, that wickedness was there” (Ecclesiastes 3:16).

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: by the way of the king
Jeremiah.english_translation: He had a cave from his house to the plains of Jericho, and he went out to go by way of the cave. What did the Holy One, blessed be He, do to fulfil “My net also will I spread upon him” (Ezekiel 12)? He arranged a deer before the Chaldeans, walking on the roof of the cave outside the city, and they ran after it to seize it, and it ran to the mouth of the cave, and they saw Zedekiah coming out of the cave.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “Ezekiel 12” is 12:13 (JPS wording quoted). “Cave” is printed in abbreviated form (מער').

Jeremiah.english_translation: Why didst thou transgress the oath?
These are the Sanhedrin, because they released him from his oath: it was a sin in the eyes of God that they released the oath.
Synagogues.
Fields, to work them. Every *yegevah* is an expression of digging — *[printed Old French: אפושי"ץ]* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Like *sarei* [princes of].
Who had fallen to the Chaldeans by the word of Jeremiah; and when the city was captured, he appointed him ruler over those who remained there.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: they shall be accomplished before thee
Jeremiah.english_translation: And the words will be before thee, so that thou shalt see them fulfilled.
Into the hand of the Chaldeans.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: The word which came to Jeremiah
Jeremiah.english_translation: What is stated at the end of the matter (Jeremiah 42): “And it came to pass after ten days, that the word of HaShem came,” etc.; except that he wrote first about what was said to him. And aggadic midrash in Eichah Rabbati: What was the word? “And go back to Gedaliah.” He said to him: “Either thou go down with them and I remain here, or thou remain here and I go down with them.” He said: “If I go down with them, what use am I to them? Rather let *beriyehon* go down with them, for he is of great use to them.”
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “Jeremiah 42” is 42:7 (JPS wording quoted). u|The Aramaic words *beriyehon* are left untranslated: the form could mean “their Creator” or “their creatures,” and the speakers are not named in the passage as printed.

Jeremiah.english_translation: That he went into exile of his own accord with them; he would see a company of *shelulim* in neck-irons, and he would put his neck among them, etc., as it is in the Pesikta of the haftarah “The Words of Jeremiah.” For it is impossible to say that Nebuzaradan put him in fetters, since Nebuchadnezzar commanded him, “do him no harm” (above, 39).
Jeremiah.translator_note: *Shelulim* is left transliterated (“stripped” or “plundered” captives). Printed “above 39” is Jeremiah 39:12 (JPS wording quoted).

Jeremiah.english_translation: *[Printed Old French: בזיאו"ש]* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Why dost thou grieve over them? Did not thou prophesy to them, and they did not hearken? As it is in the Pesikta.
An expression of “and he ungirded the camels” (Genesis 24:32); and Targum Jonathan: “And now, behold, I have loosed thee”; and Menahem explained all of them as an expression of actual opening.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Yet he would not go back
Jeremiah.english_translation: In spite of all this he was not willing to return. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: “And go back to Gedaliah,” who was appointed over the poor who remained; they too need thee, like the other exiles.
Gifts and presents (Aramaic: *matnan unvizban*).
Fig-cake (*develah*).

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: one of the chief officers of the king
Jeremiah.english_translation: And the officers of the king were jealous of him, because he had taken greatness.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: to bring them to the house of the LORD
Jeremiah.english_translation: When they set out from their homes they did not know of the destruction of the Temple; on the way they heard, and tore their clothes and shaved their beards.
An expression of scratching.
Because he should have been wary of the counsel of Johanan son of Kareah, and was not, [Scripture] counts it against him as though they had been killed by his hand.
Aramaic: “At a pool of many waters.”

In the lodging that David gave to Chimham son of Barzillai the Gileadite when he returned from the war of Absalom, as it is said in the Book of Samuel (2 Samuel 19): “Chimham shall go over with me,” etc.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed 2 Samuel 19:39. Rashi’s wording of the verse differs slightly from the Hebrew; the JPS wording is quoted.

Jeremiah.english_translation: That the watchmen blow, to warn the people.

This *mem* is a letter that “falls” from the root of the word, like *makom*, *ma‘amad*, *ma‘aseh*, and its root is *lat*, like “he wrapped his face” (1 Kings 19): “Wrap it in the mud in the framework.” *Bamelet* — *envolopement* [printed אנוולופמנטו] in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: “A letter that falls from the root” (*yesod nofel*) is rendered literally; the sense is that the *mem* is a formative prefix and the root is *lat*. Old French printed אנוולופמנטו; Darmesteter has *encolopemant* (also *envelopement* in the Glossary h.f.). Printed “1 Kings 19” is 19:13 (JPS wording quoted).

Jeremiah.english_translation: His tent; and its counterpart, “By His breath the heavens are serene” (Job 26:13).
Jeremiah.translator_note: The word is *shaprir* (pavilion), compared with *shifrah* (“serene”).

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: he shall fold up the land of Egypt
Jeremiah.english_translation: He will wrap up all her spoil and go out, as a shepherd wraps and rolls up his garment and throws it from off his shoulders when he leads his flock before him.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The phrase “from off his shoulders” (*me‘al ketifav*) is rendered literally; whether the garment is taken off or thrown over the shoulders is not clear.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Altars that were made there by those who converted in the days of Hezekiah — the captives of Sennacherib, whom he led from Cush and from Egypt before Jerusalem on the day of his downfall — as it says (Isaiah 19): “In that day there shall be five cities in the land of Egypt that speak the language of Canaan, and swear to the LORD of hosts; one shall be called The city of destruction”; and Jonathan translated “city of destruction” (*ir haheres*): “The city of Beth-shemesh, which is destined to be destroyed, shall be said to be one of them.”
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 19” is 19:18.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Their heart from their evil.
Jeremiah and Baruch returned there, whom Nebuchadnezzar exiled when the land of Egypt was given into his hand, in the twenty-seventh year of his reign (Ezekiel 29). So it is taught in Seder Olam.
Without their knowledge.
Moulds in the likeness of idols (*atsavim*; “*atsavim*” being a likeness of a maiden, as above, 22).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “the likeness of a maiden” (*demut almah*) is rendered literally; the reading is uncertain. Printed “above 22” is Jeremiah 22:28.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Like *velo yukhal* [“and was not able”].
“Pharaoh the broken one” (Aramaic *teviraya*); and this *ḥet* is used in place of a *hei*.

The Shekhinah did not rest upon me to prophesy, like “and the spirit rested upon them” (Numbers 11:26). How have I changed from the disciples of the prophets? Joshua served Moses — the Holy Spirit rested upon him; Elisha served Elijah — the Holy Spirit rested upon him; how have I changed?

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: And this in the whole land
Jeremiah.english_translation: It is the land that is judged with this uprooting and demolition.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: seekest thou great things for thyself
Jeremiah.english_translation: Prophecies, like “Tell me, I pray thee, all the great things” (2 Kings 8:4); “and will tell thee great things” (above, 33). The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: If there is no vineyard, there is no fence; if there is no flock, there is no shepherd; I do not reveal Myself to the prophets except for the sake of Israel. So it is taught in the Mekhilta, at its beginning.
It is of leather, and it is boiled, and when it goes out to war they anoint it with oil.
Of wood, resembling our *tiryasin*.
Like “it shall be scoured and rinsed” (Leviticus 7) — *forbir* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French *forbir* is confirmed by Darmesteter (“Fourbissez”). Printed “Leviticus 7” is 6:21 (“it shall be scoured, and rinsed in water,” JPS).

Jeremiah.english_translation: Egypt.
They had no leisure any more to stand in battle.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: like the Nile that riseth up
Jeremiah.english_translation: That he was accustomed to bring up armies around him, like a river for a flood around him.
Aramaic: “whose waters are agitated.”

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: like the Nile that riseth up
Jeremiah.english_translation: He was accustomed to rise.
Like *a’abed* [“I will destroy”].
An expression of folly.
An expression of satiety. Another explanation: an expression of drunkenness, like *shakhar*, which we translate *meravvei*.
For Pharaoh went against Nebuchadnezzar at Carchemish, and he also fell and his mighty men were killed, and he fled from the battle.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: the mighty man hath stumbled against the mighty
Jeremiah.english_translation: When they fled, they stumbled and tripped over one another.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: should come and smite the land of Egypt
Jeremiah.english_translation: This is the second blow, for Nebuchadnezzar destroyed Egypt in the twenty-seventh year of his reign (Ezekiel 29:14), as we learned in Seder Olam.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Ezekiel 29:14 is printed; the twenty-seventh year is stated at 29:17.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Facing the war; *vehakhen* — “prepare”: Aramaic *ve’atkin*.

They were swept away and slipped, thy mighty ones, like “a sweeping rain” (Proverbs 28:3), “his field was swept away” in the language of the Mishnah. And Menahem connected it with an expression of destruction, and so he connected “a sweeping rain”; and Dunash interpreted “a sweeping rain” like “a lopping rain,” as in “Shall lop the boughs” (Isaiah 10:33).
The Holy One, blessed be He, who thrust him, and multiplied stumbling for him.
They gathered one to another, saying: Let us arise and return to our people, to the place from which we went forth to fight.
Aramaic: “The sword of the enemy, which is like wine that inebriates.” *Hayonah* is an expression of wine. Another explanation: an expression of oppression.
In the war they proclaimed a proverb of reproach.
That he would raise the voice of his noise, shouts, to boast in his armies.
That he appointed a fixed day of war to go out and fight, and did not go out, and the day of the appointed time passed.
For as it is a true thing that Tabor is fixed among the mountains, and Mount Carmel by the sea, so in truth will this thing come upon Egypt.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Furnish thyself to go into captivity
Jeremiah.english_translation: A man who goes out on a journey prepares for himself a skin-bottle and an earthenware cup to drink from.
An expression of parching.
Aramaic: “A beautiful kingdom.”
Aramaic: “Killing nations.” *Kerets* is an expression of cutting, and so “I also am formed out of the clay” (Job 33).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “Job 33” is 33:6 (JPS wording quoted).

Jeremiah.english_translation: From Babylon.
Her princes, like “with a razor that is hired” (Isaiah 7).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 7” is 7:20 (JPS wording quoted).

Jeremiah.english_translation: *[Printed Old French: קופל"א]* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed קופל"א; Darmesteter reads *cople* (modern *couple*) and notes that the Glossary h.f. gives *crèche*.

Jeremiah.english_translation: They turned the back, seeking to flee.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: The sound thereof shall go like the serpent
Jeremiah.english_translation: Behold, the serpent comes to teach about Egypt, and is found to be taught; we learn from here that when the Holy One, blessed be He, said to the serpent, “upon thy belly shalt thou go” (Genesis 3), He cut off its legs, and its sound went to the end of the world. So it is taught in the Thirty-Two Rules of Rabbi Eliezer son of Rabbi Jose the Galilean.
Jeremiah.translator_note: “Is found to be taught” (*nimtsa lamed*) is rendered literally. Printed “Genesis 3” is 3:14.

Jeremiah.english_translation: To her.
There is strength in them to cut down her entire forest.
The number of their hosts.
Upon Amon; upon the prince Amon; some say it is an expression of greatness, like “Art thou better than No-amon” (Nahum 3:8).
Alexandria the Great — *[printed Old French: לאשיניוריא"ה דלישנדר"א]* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Jeremiah.english_translation: After forty years, as Ezekiel said (29:13).

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: But fear not thou, O Jacob My servant
Jeremiah.english_translation: The righteous who are in Egypt, who were exiled there against their will.
In restrained judgment, little by little.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: But I will not make a full end of thee
Jeremiah.english_translation: An expression of sweeping away and destruction; and so Jonathan translated it: an expression of finishing.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The words “But will not utterly destroy thee” fall at the start of the next verse in the site’s verse division; the lemma is taken from this verse.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Concerning the Philistines.

When Nebuchadnezzar was besieging Jerusalem, in the tenth year of Zedekiah, the army of Pharaoh went out from Egypt, and the Chaldeans went up from Jerusalem; Pharaoh heard, and overran Gaza, and returned to his land. In Seder Olam.
It has no likeness; and Jonathan translated it: “from his striding.”
From the noise that is of his chariot.
The wheels of his chariots.
To save them.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: To cut off from Tyre and Zidon
Jeremiah.english_translation: The Philistines used to help them against their enemies.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: The remnant of the isle of Caphtor
Jeremiah.english_translation: *[Printed Old French: איזל"ש]* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed איזל"ש (*isles*); Darmesteter has the entry “Isles.”

Jeremiah.english_translation: Laid waste.
Thou wilt gash thyself in mourning and weeping.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: O thou sword of the LORD
Jeremiah.english_translation: That the Holy One, blessed be He, brings upon the world.
An expression of rest (*margo‘a*).
The name of a place.
“Madmen” is the name of a place; and according to their names He mentions their punishment.
Jeremiah.translator_note: *Velefi shemotam* could also be read “because of their death”; rendered “according to their names,” the sense being that the name Madmen echoes *tidmi* (“shalt be brought to silence”).

Jeremiah.english_translation: Thou shalt be laid waste.
Aramaic: “Her rulers, the younger among the kings.”
The name of a place; it is the ascent of a mountain.

A tower of *aro‘er* made in the wilderness, with no settlement around it except dwellers in tents; and a tower standing where there is no settlement looks like a ruin. So Jonathan translated. And Menahem explained *ke‘aro‘er* as the name of a tree among the trees of the forest.

“Give a wing to Moab.” Anything hanging that protrudes from a man or from an animal is called *tsits*, like “it shall be unto you for a fringe” (Numbers 15:39), and “I was taken by a lock of my head” (Ezekiel 38).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “Ezekiel 38” is 8:3 (JPS wording quoted).

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: she must fly and get away
Jeremiah.english_translation: For in flight and in haste ye shall go out into exile; and *netsa* will be from the root *natsah*; so Menahem connected it, and so “Yea, they fled away and wandered” (Lamentations 4:15). And Jonathan translated: “Remove the crown from Moab”; give to others the *tsits*, the diadem, that belongs to Moab.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: doeth the work of the LORD
Jeremiah.english_translation: The work of destroying Moab, which is the mission of HaMakom.
Is not altered.
Emptiers; and so “He that is bent down shall speedily be loosed” (Isaiah 51:14) — it is the going of the bowels with diarrhoea.
The casks of the Moabites.
They will break them, like “How are they esteemed as earthen pitchers” (Lamentations 4:2); “Every bottle is filled with wine” (above, 13).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “above 13” is Jeremiah 13:12 (JPS wording quoted).

Jeremiah.english_translation: In whom he trusted.
The golden calf.
An expression of lament, like *al tanud lo*.
Ask of the fugitives and the escapees from Moab, “What has happened?” — whether anything escaped the destroyer.
And punishment has come.
Make him drink the cup of poison until he becomes drunk.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: he also shall be in derision
Jeremiah.english_translation: Just as [Israel] was a laughing-stock to him.

Thou wast shaking thy head and mocking at our destruction. Another explanation: “for as often as thou speakest of him” — thou wast rejoicing over our destruction; thou shalt be driven to go out into exile. And Targum Jonathan: “Because ye multiplied words against them, therefore ye shall be tossed about.”

A place where the water digs beneath the high banks of the edge of the stream; and when the stream diminishes, the hollow is found empty, and the dove nests in one of the sides of the hollow; and when the stream grows strong it sweeps away the nest, and she wanders from there. So I heard. But Jonathan did not translate so, but: “And be like a dove that leaves the mouth of her dovecote and descends and dwells in the bottom of a pit.”
His hatred of Israel is not in truth and not in justice.
His mighty ones.
They did not repay as was due to the seed of Abraham, who fought with the kings and saved Lot, their father.
A city in the land of Moab.
Moaning like doves that coo.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: With more than the weeping of Jazer will I weep for thee
Jeremiah.english_translation: When this prophecy was spoken, Jazer was already destroyed, and it is adjacent to Moab.
I will weep on thy account, like that weeping, for thou also wilt be destroyed like it.
It was a land of vineyards.
Since he likened it to a vine, he likened its mighty ones to the branches of the vine.
They went into exile.
An expression of the summer fruit (*kayits*) of figs; and *ketsekha*, which is an expression of “end” (*ketz*), has no *yod*, and the *tsadi* has a *dagesh*.
And it will come to an end, so that it will not be seen.
Grapes, with the sound of shouting of *hedad* in gladness, as they used to do.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: The shouting shall be no shouting
Jeremiah.english_translation: For they will cry *hedad*; it will not be the first *hedad*, but a *hedad* of flight from the sword.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: A heifer of three years old
Jeremiah.english_translation: A mighty province.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: the abundance that he hath gotten is perished
Jeremiah.english_translation: Because he made arrogance; therefore they perished.
Gashings.
Wail over her and say: “How is it broken down!”
The enemy against Moab.
Fly.
The name of the city.
These are two hard things next to each other: for the terror causes him to flee, and the pit is prepared for him to fall into.
*[Printed Old French: פוש"א]* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed פוש"א; Darmesteter has *fose* (“la fosse”).

Jeremiah.english_translation: Because it is high and has a shadow.
The fugitives, to rest in the shadow, who no longer had strength to flee.
From the city of Sihon, like “the son of Reuben” (in Joshua 9).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “Joshua 9” does not match; the phrase “the Stone of Bohan the son of Reuben” is at Joshua 15:6 and 18:17.

Jeremiah.english_translation: *[Printed Old French: אטריפירצד"א]* in Old French; and Menahem connected it to an expression of *makor* [source]; and Targum Jonathan: *viḳirei*, an expression of preciousness.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Those who raised a voice of glory.
The *bet* is soft and the *hei* has a *ḥataf patah*, for it is an expression of astonishment.
The idol of the children of Ammon; Malcam is its name, as it is said (2 Kings 23): “and for Milcom the abomination of the children of Ammon.”
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “2 Kings 23” is 23:13 (JPS wording quoted).

Jeremiah.english_translation: The one adjacent to it, and it is of the land of Ammon.
Rabbah of the children of Ammon.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: run to and fro among the folds
Jeremiah.english_translation: Jonathan translated: *ve’ithammemon bisi‘an*; “gather yourselves in troops.” He interpreted *vehitshotatna* as an expression of roaming troops, and *gederot* as an expression of sheepfolds filled with flocks. But it may also be interpreted: *vehitshotatna* and *vehit‘olalna* “in the dung of the sheepfolds” — an expression of contempt, like “So Esau despised” (Genesis 25) and *shat* Esau.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The final words (“and *shat* Esau”) are rendered as printed; the reading is unclear. The Aramaic is transliterated as printed.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Thou boastest — *vanter* [printed וונטי"ר] in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed וונטי"ר; Darmesteter glosses the verse “Pourquoi es-tu fière?” (the form is read *vanter*).

Jeremiah.english_translation: For thy land is a land of valleys, and the withholding of rain is not severe for it, for the sun does not rule over it.
A blow of much rain came, until the waters flowed in the valley and swept away the roots of the crop; so Menahem explained.
Whoever can hurry and flee.
An expression of “a fugitive and a wanderer” (there, 4).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “there 4” is Genesis 4:12 (JPS wording quoted).

Jeremiah.english_translation: Edom is in the south of the Land of Israel, as it is said, “your south side shall be from the wilderness of Zin close by the side of Edom” (Numbers 34:3).
From this generation.
It has become spoiled.
Remove yourselves from this place, an expression of “and they shall empty (*ufinu*) the house” (Leviticus 14).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “Leviticus 14” is 14:36 (JPS: “that they empty the house”).

Jeremiah.english_translation: To hide in the depths of hiding places. *Nusu*, *hafnu*, *he‘miku* — all of them are imperatives.

“I have uncovered,” etc.; “I have heard a message,” etc. Everything of this kind Obadiah prophesied about Edom; and since one manner of expression applies to several prophets, yet no two prophets prophesy in one manner, in some of the words they vary.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The last clause is rendered literally. Rashi’s “*shemu‘ah shamati*” is Jeremiah 49:14 (JPS wording quoted); the parallel passage is Obadiah 1.

Jeremiah.english_translation: In astonishment: But the plunderers who came upon thee left thee nothing.

I have revealed, like “making the white appear” (Genesis 30:37) — and “thou deliveredst up my survivors,” so that none of them should remain, as it is said, “Neither shouldest thou have delivered up those of his that did remain” (Obadiah 1:14).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Rashi’s “thou deliveredst up my survivors” is rendered literally; the printed words differ from the verse in Obadiah.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: he shall not be able to hide himself
Jeremiah.english_translation: And he will seek to hide, and will not be able.
Those whom thou didst make fatherless in Israel.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The verb *sheyitamt* is rendered as “thou didst make fatherless”; its subject is not stated.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: it pertained not to drink of the cup
Jeremiah.english_translation: Who were not brothers to them; and if they did evil to them, there is not for them a sentence of death like thine.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Rendered literally; the persons referred to are not named.

Jeremiah.english_translation: “And for a curse,” Bozrah shall be. Bozrah is of the cities of Moab, but because of the matter, as is said, “Jobab the son of Zerah of Bozrah” (Genesis 37), it is smitten with him.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 37” is 36:33 (JPS wording quoted).

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: I make thee small among the nations
Jeremiah.english_translation: For among them there is no king the son of a king; it was not their way in Rome to appoint a king the son of a king.

An expression of terror: that thou wast hasty and alarmed, to arouse thy enmity against thy brother. And some render it in the vernacular as an expression of *pelatsut*, and some in the vernacular as an expression of *mifletset*.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The vernacular renderings are named only by their Hebrew forms and are not Old French in the printed text; rendered literally.

Jeremiah.english_translation: To harm them.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: that dwellest in the clefts of the rock
Jeremiah.english_translation: Dweller.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: That holdest the height of the hill
Jeremiah.english_translation: Like *toféish* [one who holds]; the *yod* is superfluous in it.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: From the thickets of the Jordan
Jeremiah.english_translation: For it is a place of lions, as the Targum of Jonathan; so will the enemy come up to the strong habitation.
I will bring near the moment (*rega*).

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: make him run away from it
Jeremiah.english_translation: Suddenly and with success he will lay it waste and return to his place in a small moment. And I say: “I will make him run from upon it” — from above it, so that he will be strong over it and above it; and so “above the firmament,” and so “Above Him” (Isaiah 6), “upon his apparel” (1 Samuel 12).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “1 Samuel 12”: the phrase *me‘al lemaddav* occurs at 1 Samuel 17:39. Isaiah 6 is 6:2; “above the firmament” is Genesis 1:7 (JPS wording).

Jeremiah.english_translation: The one whom I have chosen to take My vengeance upon her — I will appoint.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: who will appoint Me a time
Jeremiah.english_translation: To war, to fight with Me.
King.
An expression of “truly.”
They will drag them.
The despised ones of the nations; and our Rabbis expounded: Persia, which is the youngest of the sons of Japheth.
An expression of desolation.
The cities of Aram, for they heard bad tidings about Damascus, which is the head of Aram, as it is said, “For the head of Aram is Damascus” (Isaiah 7:8); therefore they melted.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: There is trouble in the sea
Jeremiah.english_translation: Its anxiety is like the anxiety of the sea: it cannot be quiet. Every *de’agah* is an expression of fear.
Her hands grew weak from fighting.
Trembling.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: How is the city of praise left unrepaired
Jeremiah.english_translation: She was not filled with earth around her wall, to strengthen the wall, like “and they left Jerusalem unto the broad wall” (Nehemiah 3:8). And one may also interpret: why was she not spared (*ne‘ezvah*) from this evil, that the evil should not come upon her?
Jeremiah.translator_note: JPS renders Nehemiah 3:8 “and they restored Jerusalem even unto the broad wall”; Rashi reads *vaya‘azvu* as “they left,” and his wording is translated.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Thus will her king mourn over her.
An expression of oath.
They will be destroyed; and it does not depart from the expression of *dumah* [silence], for in every ruined city no voice is heard.
They are dwellers in the wildernesses, in tents; they have no wall and no city.
*[Printed Old French: אמאשמנ"ט]* in Old French. Another explanation: an expression of fear.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Jeremiah.english_translation: And what is the counsel? “Arise, go up against a nation that is at ease.”
Dwelling in security by themselves; they do not need to gather and dwell in a multitude, for they do not fear that an enemy will come upon them.
Set apart from the edge to the edge of the directions.
The hope of Elam (another version: the strength of Elam).
The best of their might.
My siege.
Jeremiah.translator_note: *Metsur sheli* is rendered literally; it could also be read “My stronghold.”

Jeremiah.english_translation: *[Printed Old French: פורק"א]* in Old French — it is a sign of gathering.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed פורק"א; Darmesteter glosses this verse “étendard” and reads *perche*.

Jeremiah.english_translation: “And Merodach” are names of idols of Babylon.
Media and Persia.
In the direction of this place, Jerusalem, they will turn their faces when Babylon is destroyed and they go out from it with the permission of Cyrus king of Persia.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Their shepherds have caused them to go astray
Jeremiah.english_translation: Their great ones led them astray from Me.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: turned them away on the mountains
Jeremiah.english_translation: “To the mountains” — to the idolatry on the mountains. *Shovevum* — *[printed Old French: אנווייזאנ"ץ]* in Old French; *shovevum* — their kings. And Targum Jonathan: “the mountains *shovevum*” — *shiltaniya bizunon*.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. The Aramaic is transliterated as printed (*shiltaniya* “rulers”; *bizunon* “despised them”).

Jeremiah.english_translation: Aramaic: “and the hope of their fathers.”

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Flee out of the midst of Babylon
Jeremiah.english_translation: From now, go out from there.
It is the way of the he-goats to go before the flock, at the head of the goats.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: set themselves in array against her
Jeremiah.english_translation: And they will set the battle in order against her.
Plunderers of My heritage.
An expression of fatness.
That threshes in the grain and eats continually.
Your assembly (*knisatkhem*).
Jeremiah.translator_note: *Knisatkhem* could also be read “your entrance”; rendered “your assembly.”

Jeremiah.english_translation: You Chaldeans: if your beginning is great, your end shall be a wilderness.
Cast stones at her, like “and have cast stones upon me” (Lamentations 3:53).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed Lamentations 3:53 (JPS wording quoted).

Jeremiah.english_translation: Like a man who has no strength and extends his hand to everyone he sees, to ask mercy and help; and so “We have given the hand to Egypt” (there, 5): we extended a hand to Egypt, to ask help from them.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “there 5” is Lamentations 5:6 (JPS wording quoted).

Jeremiah.english_translation: The strength of her foundations; and so “and the foundations they are digging out” (Ezra 4:12) — *ve’ashaya yaḥiṭu*; and in the language of the Mishnah, “such as these who sew for the *ushin*”; and so *vehit’osheshu* — and they strengthened themselves.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Mishnaic phrase “who sew for the *ushin*” and the final comparison are rendered literally; their sense is not explained in the text.

Jeremiah.english_translation: To the city of HaShem [Jerusalem].

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Cut off the sower from Babylon
Jeremiah.english_translation: Aramaic: “Destroy the king from Babylon, and those who hold the sword at the time of slaughter.”

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: First the king of Assyria hath devoured him
Jeremiah.english_translation: For he exiled the ten tribes.
*Garmo* — he gnawed (*girem*) his bones, for he finished off the remnants, Judah and Benjamin; *itsamo* — *[printed Old French: דישושא"ר]* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed דישושא"ר; Darmesteter glosses this verse “a brisé des os” and reads *desosad* (modern *désossa*).

Jeremiah.english_translation: An expression of pasture.
Because thou hast rebelled against Me and angered Me.
The name of a province, and so “Pekod and Shoa and Koa” (Ezekiel 23:23); Jonathan: names of provinces.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: do according to all that I have commanded thee
Jeremiah.english_translation: Thou, Cyrus, by the hand of Isaiah the prophet (45).

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: the hammer of the whole earth
Jeremiah.english_translation: Because it shattered and smashed everything.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: I have laid a snare for thee
Jeremiah.english_translation: An expression of a snare (*mokesh*).

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Come against her from every quarter
Jeremiah.english_translation: From the end of the city they began upon it, so that she not know, and be seized suddenly.
Targum Jonathan: *avulaha* — her gates; it has no likeness; and Menahem connected it with an expression of *evus* [manger].
Thresh her.
Threshing-floors.
Her princes; such is the way of the prophets, to liken princes to mighty bullocks and to he-goats.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Call together the archers against Babylon
Jeremiah.english_translation: An expression of “and Saul summoned the people” (1 Samuel 16): Summon them to gather against Babylon — shooters with arrows, like “His archers compass me round about” (Job 16:13).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “1 Samuel 16” is 15:4 (JPS wording quoted).

Jeremiah.english_translation: An expression of oath.
When Babylon falls there will be rest and ease for all.
Upon her soothsayers.
In their divinations; and similar is “That frustrateth the tokens of the imposters” (Isaiah 44); and so Targum Jonathan: because they invent and speak lying words.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed Isaiah 44:25 (JPS wording quoted).

Jeremiah.english_translation: Support — *garantie* [printed גרנטיא"ה] in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed גרנטיא"ה; Darmesteter reads *garantie* (“l’alliance”).

Jeremiah.english_translation: They will go mad. Another explanation: *[printed Old French: פורוונטרונט]* in Old French; and Targum Jonathan: “they boast in the gods of the Anakim that they had.”
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed פורוונטרונט; it appears to be a form of *vanter* (“to boast”), in keeping with the Targum, but was not found in Darmesteter for this verse; left as printed.

Jeremiah.english_translation: *Ye‘aron timon bechatolin* — kinds of animals that are found in a ruin.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Aramaic phrase is transliterated as printed.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: he shall come up like a lion
Jeremiah.english_translation: As he comes up from the thickets of the Jordan, so will the plunderer come to the strong habitation. So Jonathan translated: “Behold, a king with his army shall go up against them like a lion that goes up from the height of the Jordan.” We learn that the thicket of the Jordan is a place of lions; and so Jonathan translated also “yet how wilt thou do in the thicket of the Jordan” (Jeremiah 12:5): “to face the beasts of the field in the height of the Jordan.”
Jeremiah.translator_note: Rashi does not name Jeremiah 12:5; the verse is identified from the wording.

Jeremiah.english_translation: When I bring the moment.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: make them run away from it
Jeremiah.english_translation: From above it.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: who will appoint Me a time
Jeremiah.english_translation: For the war.
Persia, which is the youngest of the sons of Japheth.
“Chaldeans,” by the numerical value *at-bash*. “A destroying wind” — the spirit of the king of Persia and Media, who is destroying: wind — *talant* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed טלנ"ט; Darmesteter has the entry “Un souffle (destructeur)” with the form *talant*.

Jeremiah.english_translation: And they shall scatter her.
And they shall empty.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Let the archer bend his bow against her
Jeremiah.english_translation: This is an abbreviated verse: [toward] that against which I say, there let the archer bend his bow.
Let him not be healed.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Rashi’s reading differs from JPS (“lift himself up”); translated as printed.

Jeremiah.english_translation: They have not forgotten to take His vengeance.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: their land is full of guilt
Jeremiah.english_translation: Of the Chaldeans.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Flee out of the midst of Babylon
Jeremiah.english_translation: Israel, from the midst of Babylon.
Babylon was until now in the hand of HaShem, to make the whole earth drunken with the wine of wrath.
They became drunk and mad.
Its punishment rose up to heaven.
We were remembered before Him for merit, and the righteousness of our fathers came before Him.
An expression of cleanness.
Quivers in which the arrows are placed.
Many days ago.
His plan: it is the way of Scripture to say two *gam*’s one after the other, and through the last the first comes.
Thine end.
The measure of thy violence. Another explanation: “the measure of thy end,” like *ki yivtsa‘*.
*[Printed Old French: אינשימישימו"ש]* in Old French.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Jeremiah.english_translation: An expression of “truly.”

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: I will fill thee with men, as with the canker-worm
Jeremiah.english_translation: Aramaic: “I will fill thee with the host of many nations, like the canker-worm (*zaḥla*).”

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: lift up a shout against thee
Jeremiah.english_translation: Aramaic: “And they shall raise [a shout] over thee with their voice.”

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: Every man is proved to be brutish
Jeremiah.english_translation: He who makes an image for a god.
An expression of a molten image.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: In the time of their visitation
Jeremiah.english_translation: When the Holy One, blessed be He, takes account of them and of their worshippers.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: is the tribe of His inheritance
Jeremiah.english_translation: Jacob, mentioned above at the beginning of the verse.
Until now I have set thee up for Me as a destroyer and to shatter the nations against which I decreed exile.
After all this, when I complete My vengeance by his hand upon the idolaters.
Appoint them.
An expression of army (or an expression of lord).
To bristle — *herisier* [printed הריצי"יר] in Old French, like “That made the hair of my flesh to stand up” (Job 4:15).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed הריצי"יר; Darmesteter has the entry “Hérissé” for this verse.

Jeremiah.english_translation: An expression of trembling.
It leaped, like “the sinew of the thigh-vein” (Genesis 33), which leaped from its place.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 33” is 32:33 (JPS wording quoted).

Jeremiah.english_translation: Behold, she is now full like a threshing-floor at the time when they have threshed her grain, when it is full of wheat.
And she will be emptied, and will resemble a threshing-floor at the beginning of the harvest, when it is empty.
The cry of my violence, and my sustenance, which my kin have eaten.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: They shall roar together like young lions
Jeremiah.english_translation: An expression of a braying donkey.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: With their poison I will prepare their feast
Jeremiah.english_translation: I will intend that their feasts be at the time of heat, so that they become drunken.
And they shall sleep.

An eternal sleep. And so it came to pass there: from the midst of feasting and drunkenness they were destroyed and killed, and the city was captured, as it is said in Daniel: “Belshazzar, while he tasted the wine” (Daniel 5), “They drank wine” (there), “In that night Belshazzar the Chaldean king was slain” (there), “And Darius the Mede received the kingdom” (there).
Jeremiah.translator_note: The last quotation is Daniel 5:31 in the Hebrew/Aramaic text and 6:1 in JPS. The Aramaic quotations are given in JPS wording.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Lambs; and Targum Jonathan: “like bulls.”
Babylon, by the numerical value *at-bash*.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: The sea is come up upon Babylon
Jeremiah.english_translation: A great army, like the sea.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: I will punish Bel in Babylon
Jeremiah.english_translation: Upon the idolatry of Babylon.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: that which he hath swallowed up
Jeremiah.english_translation: That all the inhabitants of the earth were brought low beneath him.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: shall not flow any more unto him
Jeremiah.english_translation: And they shall not gather; and so “And all nations shall flow unto it” (Isaiah 2:2) — like the waters of the rivers, all of which go to the sea.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: the rumour that shall be heard in the land
Jeremiah.english_translation: This report about Belshazzar who was killed.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: a rumour shall come one year
Jeremiah.english_translation: In that very year the report will come that Babylon was destroyed of itself from heaven, as it is said (there, 13): “And Babylon, the glory of kingdoms, the beauty of the Chaldeans’ pride, shall be as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah.”
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “there 13” is Isaiah 13:19.

Jeremiah.english_translation: The second.
The good [report] for you: “Thus saith Cyrus king of Persia” (Ezra 1), “Whosoever there is among you of all His people.”
Jeremiah.translator_note: “Thus saith Cyrus king of Persia” is Ezra 1:2; “Whosoever there is among you of all His people” is 1:3 (JPS wording).

Jeremiah.english_translation: Darius the Mede reigned one year, and in the second year Cyrus the Persian.
