Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: As Babylon hath caused the slain of Israel to fall
Jeremiah.english_translation: Babylon, too, was such that the slain of Israel fell in her.
The slain of all her land shall fall.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: You that have escaped the sword
Jeremiah.english_translation: Israel who were exiled into it, who escaped from the sword of Nebuzaradan.
For the Chaldeans were saying and reviling us, saying: “The hand of our god is exalted, for we destroyed His house.”
A slain man cries out when they kill a person with an arrow or with a spear, and he groans when the spear is drawn out: that is the groaning (*anaka*).

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: fortify the height of her strength
Jeremiah.english_translation: An expression of a fortress of strength.
From Me — from the heavens, which are higher than she — the spoilers will come to her.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: The noise of their voice is uttered
Jeremiah.english_translation: The sound of their outcry is heard.
An expression of digging, an expression of “Rase it, rase it, even to the foundation thereof” (Psalms 137:7).
With much emptiness that will come upon them.
Chief of the presentation (*rav takrovta*): through him those who bring a gift to the king would see the king’s face.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: through the anger of the LORD
Jeremiah.english_translation: It [the anger] caused him the rebellion of Zedekiah against the king of Babylon, which is the beginning of the destruction.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The subject (“it”) is supplied in brackets; the sentence is elliptical.

Jeremiah.english_translation: *Karkom*.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The word *karkom* is left transliterated as printed; its meaning in this context is not stated.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: all the men of war fled
Jeremiah.english_translation: Like *barḥu* [“they fled”].

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: the way of the gate between the two walls
Jeremiah.english_translation: He had a cave from his house to the plains of Jericho, and I have already explained it in this book (31).
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “(31)”; the explanation is at Jeremiah 39:4.

Jeremiah.english_translation: It is Antioch.
Because he transgressed the oath.
The Sanhedrin, to whom he said: You released his oath for him; and it was a sin in the eyes of God to release the oath.
Jeremiah.translator_note: The speaker is not named in the passage.

Jeremiah.english_translation: In the house of the prisoners.
Synagogues, in which prayer is magnified; and some say houses of study, in which the Torah is magnified. It is a dispute of the Amoraim.
Like *hehamon*.
Diggers in the ground. Our Rabbis said: catchers of the *ḥilazon*.
Of the lavers.
They are musical instruments.

Targum Jonathan: *kuliya*; and I do not know whether it is of the kinds of musical instruments; and I say that they are basins to receive blood, like “in the blood that is in the basin” (Exodus 12:22). And some explain *hasipim* as an expression of jugs, according to the Targum of Jonathan, who translated *kuliya*, for so Targum Onkelos: “and her pitcher upon her shoulder” (Genesis 24:15) — *vekultah al ketifha*. And this expression seems to indicate that the *sipim* are not of the kinds of musical instruments, but are jugs.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 27” is 24:15 (JPS wording quoted).

Jeremiah.english_translation: With which they scoop coals from the altar.
The golden supports on which they used to stand the showbread, as we learned in Menahot.
I do not know how, for they were under the sea; and it seems to me that this is only “beside the bases.”
Jeremiah.translator_note: Rashi himself says he does not know how this is.

Jeremiah.english_translation: Would encircle it; its circumference is round.
Four fingers around its hollow.
Hollow.

Made like two basins, one in its manner turned upside down over the mouth of the lower one, and the upper is called *sevakhah* [network] — *coife* [printed קויפ"א] in Old French. And the pomegranates were threaded on chains, and the two ends of the chain were tied together and placed upon the network from above, at the place where the network is narrow above, and it descends to the place of the joining of the network and the capital, which is the wide belly in the capital, and there it stands; and the pomegranates cover the place of the joining, the two mouths of the basins that are joined together.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Old French printed קויפ"א; Darmesteter has the entry “Une coiffe” and reads *coife*.

Jeremiah.english_translation: And at the end of the verse it says, “all the pomegranates were a hundred upon the network”; and in the book (1 Kings 7) it says, “and the pomegranates were two hundred, in rows,” four hundred for the two networks. Say, then: four hundred were for the two networks on the two pillars, two rows for each network, and a row was a hundred. This is what is said here: “all the pomegranates were a hundred upon the network” — for the one row; and two hundred for the two rows, this is what it says there: “the pomegranates two hundred in rows round about” — two hundred for two rows round about the one pillar, and so for the second; behold, four hundred. And the pillars Solomon set up in the porch, near the wall of the Sanctuary, and the wall covers four pomegranates of each row, which are not seen from outside. This is what is said here: “And the pomegranates were ninety and six on a side.”
Jeremiah.translator_note: The words “the pomegranates were two hundred, in rows” are from 1 Kings 7:20; the four hundred are at 7:42 (printed “1 Kings 7:42”).

Jeremiah.english_translation: Like *laruaḥ* [to a side]: every word that requires a *lamed* at its beginning, he put a *hei* at its end; and therefore the accent is above, under the *resh*. That is: ninety-six of them are seen toward the sides of the pillar. I learned this in the chapter of the Thirty-Two Rules, which Rabbi Eliezer son of Rabbi Jose the Galilean said.
Jeremiah.translator_note: “The accent is above, under the *resh*” is rendered literally; Rashi’s sense about the position of the accent is not spelled out.

Jeremiah.english_translation: The deputy of the priests, appointed under the High Priest to serve in his place should a disqualification befall him.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: the three keepers of the door
Jeremiah.english_translation: Stewards (*amarkalin*) to whom the keys of the Temple court are entrusted.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: seven men of them that saw the king’s face
Jeremiah.english_translation: And in the book (2 Kings 25) it says “five men.” The two were important, but not so important.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “2 Kings 25” is 25:19.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: who mustered the people of the land
Jeremiah.english_translation: He knew the number of every single city, how many men it provides for the army.

This is the exile of Jehoiachin; and in the Book of Kings it says “in the eighth year.” How so? The eighth year that Nebuchadnezzar reigned is the seventh year since he subdued Jehoiakim as a servant; for the Master said: In the first year he conquered Nineveh; in the second he went up and subdued Jehoiakim.
Jeremiah.translator_note: “In the eighth year” is 2 Kings 24:12.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: three thousand Jews and three and twenty
Jeremiah.english_translation: And from the other tribes seven thousand — behold ten thousand. This verse, which explains “Jews three thousand,” decides between the two verses at the end of the Book of Kings: one verse says ten thousand (2 Kings 24), and one says seven thousand (there, 25). This one came and explained “Jews three thousand,” and from the other tribes seven thousand — behold ten thousand.
Jeremiah.translator_note: Printed “there 25” does not match; “seven thousand” is at 2 Kings 24:16 and “ten thousand” at 24:14.

Jeremiah.english_translation: This is the exile of Zedekiah; and above it says (here) “the nineteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar”: nineteen of his reign, eighteen since he subdued Jehoiakim.
Tyre was given into his hand, and he overran the Jews who were around Ammon and Moab, seven hundred forty-five. So it is explained in Seder Olam.

Jeremiah.english_lemma_JPS: in the five and twentieth day of the month
Jeremiah.english_translation: And in another place it says, “on the twenty-seventh day of the month” (2 Kings 25:27). On the twenty-fifth of the month his adversary Nebuchadnezzar died, and on the twenty-sixth he was buried, and Evil-merodach took him out of his grave; and on the twenty-seventh he reigned and lifted up the head of Jehoiachin.
He raised him and made him great. Another version: he counted him with the rest of the kings, like “When thou takest the sum [lit. ‘lift the head’] of the children of Israel” (Exodus 30:12).
He receives a portion from the king’s house for all his needs.

Ezekiel.english_translation: The prophet left his words unspecified, and did not explain who he is, nor explain from what he counted. Therefore the Holy Spirit interrupted his words with the two verses adjacent to this one, to teach who the prophet is, and to teach from what he counted, as it is said, “in the fifth day of the month — which was the fifth year,” etc. These are not the words of the prophet, for he had already said that on the fifth of the month he was standing; and, furthermore, at first he told his prophecy in his own language — “as I was among the captives,” “and I saw visions of God” — and so at the end, “And I looked, and, behold, a stormy wind,” etc. And these two verses interrupt his words as though another were speaking about him: “the word of the LORD came expressly unto Ezekiel,” “and the hand of the LORD was there upon him.”
That is, outside the Land of Israel.
The name of the river.

Because he did not see through a luminous speculum, he calls it “visions of God,” like a dream and not actual; and all the prophets, too, saw through a non-luminous speculum, except Moses our teacher, as it is said, “and by the ministry of the prophets have I used similitudes” (Hosea 12:11).

We learn that he counted thirty years from the beginning of the Jubilee, for the last Jubilee began at the beginning of the eighteenth year of Josiah, which is the year in which Hilkiah found the book (2 Kings 22). And so we learned in Seder Olam that it was the beginning of the Jubilee. Josiah reigned thirty-one years; take away from them seventeen, which had already passed — fourteen years remained. Jehoiakim reigned eleven years — behold, twenty-five. And Jeconiah his son reigned only three months and went into exile, and the year in which Ezekiel prophesied was the fifth of his exile — behold, the thirtieth year of the Jubilee. And so we find at the end of his prophecy that he gave a sign for the counting of the Jubilee, as it is said, “In the five and twentieth year of our captivity, in the beginning of the year, in the tenth day of the month” (below, 2); and our Rabbis said: Which is the year whose New Year is on the tenth of the month? Say: this is the Jubilee year.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “below, 2” is Ezekiel 40:1 (JPS wording quoted). 2 Kings 22:8: “I have found the book of the Law.”

Ezekiel.english_translation: Our Rabbis said: It had come already, since the Shekhinah does not rest upon a prophet outside the Land except by having rested upon him first in the Land. And we learned in the baraita of the Mekhilta: “Son of man, stand upon thy feet” (below, 12) was the beginning of the book, but there is no earlier or later [in order of Scripture]. And some say that “Son of man, put forth a riddle” (below, 17) is the beginning of the book. And I say that that prophecy was said to him before they were exiled, for it is fit to be said to him in the Land, since no exile is mentioned in it; and it is recognized as the beginning of his mission to them. And Jonathan also translated so: “There was a word of prophecy from before HaShem with Ezekiel son of Buzi the priest in the land of Israel; he returned a second time, he spoke with him in the province of the land of the Chaldeans.” And Ezekiel was exiled with the craftsmen and the smiths who were exiled with Jehoiachin.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Rashi’s quotation “Son of man, stand upon thy feet” is Ezekiel 2:1 (printed “below 12”); “Son of man, put forth a riddle” is 17:2. The Aramaic Targum passage is translated as printed.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the hand of the LORD was there upon him
Ezekiel.english_translation: Every expression of “hand” that is said in this book, and in every expression of prophecy, is only an expression of strength: that the prophecy overpowers him against his will, like a man who goes mad — *destrece* [printed דיישטרי"צא] in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Old French printed דיישטרי"צא; Darmesteter has *destrette* (from *districtia*) for this verse, glossed “La main de Dieu, c.-à-d. l’esprit prophétique qui s’empare du prophète malgré lui et fait de lui une sorte de fou.”

Ezekiel.english_translation: It is the chariot, the throne of glory of the Shekhinah, as is stated in the passage; and because it came in wrath to destroy Israel, it is therefore likened to a stormy wind and a cloud.

It was returning from the land of the Chaldeans, which is in the north, as it is said, “Out of the north the evil shall break forth” (Jeremiah 1); and why did it go there? To subdue the whole world under Nebuchadnezzar, so that the Babylonians should not say, “He delivered His children into the hand of a lowly nation”; for the Chaldeans were a lowly nation, as it is said, “this is the people that was not” (Isaiah 23). So our Rabbis expounded in tractate Hagigah.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed Jeremiah 1:14 and Isaiah 23:13 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: a brightness was round about it
Ezekiel.english_translation: To the cloud around it on the outside — a hint that Israel is destined to be redeemed from there.

*Ḥashmal* is an angel whose name is so, and like the hue of him he saw out of the fire. And so our Rabbis said: There was an incident of a child who was expounding the Account of the Chariot and understood *ḥashmal*, and fire went out from *ḥashmal* and consumed him. And they said also that the word is composite, as they said: What is *ḥashmal*? Rabbi Judah said: Living creatures of fire speaking (*ḥayyot esh memallelot*). In a baraita it was taught: Sometimes silent (*ḥashot*) and sometimes speaking (*memallelot*): at the hour when the utterance goes forth from the mouth of the Holy One, blessed be He, they are silent; at the hour when no utterance goes forth from the mouth of the Holy One, blessed be He, they speak — that is, praising and glorifying HaShem. And it is possible that *ḥashmal* is the name of the “eye” [colour] that is close to the eye of fire; for he said “*ḥashmal* out of the midst of the fire,” and he said “as the colour of *ḥashmal*,” “as the appearance of fire round about enclosing it, from the appearance of his loins and upward”; and he said in the second vision, “and from his loins and upward, as the appearance of brightness, as the colour of *ḥashmal*.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: JPS renders *ḥashmal* as “electrum.” The two visions quoted are Ezekiel 1:27 and 8:2 (JPS wording).

Ezekiel.english_translation: Of that fire I saw as the colour of *ḥashmal*, appearing out of the fire, and it was not known what it was; and the midrash that our Rabbis expounded on it — “living creatures of fire speaking” — is not settled with the matter.

It is surprising, for they also had the likeness of an ox, a lion and an eagle; and it appears to me that because this one is the father of all, the prophet praised the chariot with it, and it is the likeness of the face of our father Jacob.

“To each” — to the human face alone there were four faces; and so to the lion, and to the eagle, and to the ox: behold, sixteen to a creature; and so to each and every creature; and four wings to each of the faces — behold, sixty-four wings to a creature; and this is what Jonathan translated: two hundred and fifty-six wings.

Legs, *keyonan* [aligned], one opposite the other. Another explanation: “straight” — that they have no joints (*arkhubot*) with which to bend their shins, since they have neither sitting nor lying down, and they have no need of joints, such as an animal has — an upper joint and a lower joint — with which it bends its shins to lie down.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The first word, *keyonan*, is left as printed; its source is not named.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: like the sole of a calf
Ezekiel.english_translation: A round foot; and so Jonathan translated: *raglin sagalgalin* [round feet].
From their brightness it seems as though sparks go out from them, as we say in tractate Yoma: “She also made a lamp of gold,” etc.; “at the hour when the sun shines, sparks go out from it,” etc.
Like *kemareh*.
Refined and shining; and Menahem connected it with “parched with fire” (Leviticus 3).
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “Leviticus 3” is 2:14 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the hands of a man under their wings
Ezekiel.english_translation: As its Targum: *lemeḥtei bhon gumrin de’asha*, etc. [“to take coals of fire with them”]. And so we find in this book: “And the cherub stretched forth his hand from between the cherubim unto the fire that was between the cherubim, and took thereof, and put it into the hands of him that was clothed in linen,” and also after it, “And there appeared in the cherubim the form of a man’s hand” (below, 10): human hands take the fire and give it to the cherub, and the cherub to the messenger, so that the coals cool from hand to hand, to lighten the punishment from upon Israel.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “below 10”: Ezekiel 10:7–8 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_translation: Toward the four directions of the world, for they have faces and wings for every direction.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the faces and wings of them four
Ezekiel.english_translation: As its Targum: equal on all four of them.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: their wings were joined one to another
Ezekiel.english_translation: The wing of this one is spread toward the wing of that one, to this side, and likewise to that side, until they are joined and reach one another; and in this way they cover their faces, for the wings are spread above the faces.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: they turned not when they went
Ezekiel.english_translation: If they wish to go to whichever direction they wish, they do not need to turn their faces, for they have faces on every side; therefore “they went every one straight forward” — toward the side of the face, toward the direction in which they wish to go, they go.

Had I not seen the great *zakef* accent marked on “*ufenehem*,” I would not have known how to explain it; but the cantillation taught me to separate them from one another and to set the word “*ufenehem*” by itself. And so is its explanation: “And their faces” were theirs; “and their wings were stretched upward,” above their faces, and covered them. How? For a man two joined — a man for every face and face two; their wings are joined: to each one, the wing of this creature is spread toward the wing of that creature, and that one’s toward this one’s, and the faces between them are covered by them. And there is a parallel to the language of this verse elsewhere in this passage: “*ugabbehem*, *vegovah lahem*, *veyir’ah lahem*” — the word *ugabbehem* stands by itself.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The sentence beginning “How? For a man two joined” is compressed and is rendered literally.

Ezekiel.english_translation: And the two remaining wings cover their bodies.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: whither the spirit was to go
Ezekiel.english_translation: The desire to go.
This appearance walks about among all the creatures.
More than our fire.
*Plandor* [printed פלנדור"ש] in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Old French printed פלנדור"ש; Darmesteter has the entry “Éclair: *plandour*.”

Ezekiel.english_translation: Our Rabbis explained: “running and returning” like the flame of the furnace, which goes out constantly from the mouth of the furnace and hastens to return and enter; so when they put forth their head from beneath the firmament that is stretched out above them, as is explained in the passage, they recoil from before the Shekhinah that is above the firmament, and hasten to bring back their head.

*[Printed Old French: דלאטנצי"לא]* in Old French; and the colour of fire for them is like the colour of fire that comes out from between the potsherds in which gold is refined in a furnace, and the fire that goes out from there is coloured with hues. (*Tosafot*: And some explain *bazak* as an expression of scattering, as our Rabbis explained it: “as the appearance of *bazak*” — Rabbi Judah said in the name of Rabbi Simon in the name of Rabbi Levi ben Perata: like one who scatters (*bozek*) olive pomace in a hearth, that is, scatters the refuse of olives in a hearth, which kindles quickly and gives off flame, and the flame goes up and down, and this is the explanation of “running and returning.” And there is further in their words *bazak* as an expression of scattering — “*bezak bahu afra*, and they became ruins,” that is, scattered; and so in the Mishnah, “they scatter salt on the ramp so that they not slip”; and some understand *bazak* as *barak*, an expression of searching.) End of Tosafot. *Sa”a*.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. The parenthetical is marked in the printed text itself as a quotation from Tosafot; the Aramaic phrase is transliterated as printed. Audit 5 source check: a passage with the same wording (6 consecutive words) is found in Shemot Rabbah 43.8 (Sefaria Hebrew text, labelled Public Domain). This is a wording match only; the translation was not changed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: On the floor of the firmament.

Of each creature; or, the wheel has four faces. Our Rabbis said: This is Sandalphon, who stands on the earth, and his head reaches among the living creatures; but according to the passage we learn that the wheels are four.
Like a precious stone whose name is *tarshish* — *cristal* [printed קרישטא"ל] in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is transparently *cristal* (“crystal”); it was not looked up in Darmesteter.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Fixed within the wheel crosswise; since they go to every side, their faces being to the four directions, the wheel must be able to turn to the four directions.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: they went toward their four sides
Ezekiel.english_translation: Because of the work of the wheels it was necessary to repeat it, to say that the wheels do not hinder them, for they too are made for this.
And they have a back.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: they were high and they were dreadful
Ezekiel.english_translation: They are fearsome to one who sees them; and some interpret “*veyir’ah lahem*” as “they stand in awe.”

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: had their rings full of eyes
Ezekiel.english_translation: *[Printed Old French: אילוירשורצילי]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: To see in every direction, for they did not turn when they went.
From above the floor of the firmament; and Targum Jonathan: “from below to the height of heaven” — that is, as they were lifted from below upward.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Whithersoever the spirit was to go
Ezekiel.english_translation: The will of the Holy One, blessed be He.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: as the spirit was to go thither
Ezekiel.english_translation: It was not necessary to say to them, “Go to this side,” for the spirit of the Holy One, blessed be He, was in the living creatures, and the spirit of the living creature was in the wheels.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The abbreviation אצ"ל is read as “it was not necessary”; the sentence is rendered with that sense.

Ezekiel.english_translation: The living creatures.
The wheels.
Targum Jonathan: *gelid ḥasin* [strong ice]; *glace forte* [printed גליא"ה פור"ט] in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French is transparently *glace forte* (“strong ice”); it was not looked up in Darmesteter.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: conformable the one to the other
Ezekiel.english_translation: Aligned.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: like the noise of great waters
Ezekiel.english_translation: One might think a low voice; therefore Scripture says “like the voice of the Almighty” — like the voice that is specified in the Writings: “The voice of the LORD is powerful” (Psalms 29:4); “The voice of the LORD breaketh the cedars.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: The second quotation is Psalms 29:5.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: a noise of tumult like the noise of a host
Ezekiel.english_translation: Aramaic: “The voice of their praises, when they give thanks and bless before their Master, is like the voice of the host of the angels on high.”

From making a sound. And Targum Jonathan: “In their places their wings are silenced before the Word (*dibbura*)” — the utterance of HaMakom that goes forth from above their heads, to let the prophets hear His mission, as the passage continues: “there was a voice,” etc. And aggadic midrash: “when they stood” — ceasing from praise for the sake of the righteous, that they may praise first.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: there was a voice above the firmament
Ezekiel.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “When it was pleasing before Him to let His servants the prophets hear a word, there was a voice heard from above the firmament, from between the cherubim, from beneath the firmament that was over their heads.”
From fear of the utterance.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I saw as the colour of electrum
Ezekiel.english_translation: He did not give permission to contemplate this verse.
*Beit lah* — within it, as the appearance of fire.
And I prostrated myself.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I heard a voice of one that spoke
Ezekiel.english_translation: And what did it say?

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Son of man, stand upon thy feet
Ezekiel.english_translation: “Son of man” — He calls Ezekiel so because he had seen the chariot, going about among its upper parts and making use of it like the angels, [and it was to say:] there is none here born of woman but this one. (And all this the accents explain: *ish aḥad* … *vehana’ahu*.) But it seems to me that He called him “son of man” only so that his mind should not grow proud, since his heart had become familiar with the vision of the chariot and the work of the upper beings. *Sa”a*.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The parenthetical (וכ"ז הטעים אי"ש אח"ד לר' והנ"אהו) is unreadable and is left as printed in transliteration. “Going about among its upper parts” is rendered literally.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I heard Him that spoke unto me
Ezekiel.english_translation: “The one who speaks with me.” And it is an honour to write *medabber* of Above: for the one who says *medabber* with a *sheva* is heard as a man speaking to his fellow, turning to him face to face; and the one who says *medabber* (with a *ḥiriq*) means that the Shekhinah speaks by itself in its glory, and His messengers hear — *[printed Old French: בורפאלי"ן]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. The contrast of vocalizations is rendered literally.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Two tribes are called two nations (*goyim*).
Because it said, “their fathers have transgressed against Me,” these, their children, are hard of face.
Perhaps they will hear; perhaps they will cease from hearing.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: for they are a rebellious house
Ezekiel.english_translation: They are men of provocation (*kentorin*); but I wish that they know, at the time of their punishment, that a prophet was among them who rebuked them, and they did not hearken.
An expression of rebellion — that is, rebels; and Dunash interpreted it as an expression of thorns, and thorns have twenty names.
An expression of thorns, and so “a pricking brier … nor a piercing thorn” (below, 28).
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “below 28” is Ezekiel 28:24 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_translation: The people whom thou rebukest will weary thee and provoke thee, as though thou wert sitting upon scorpions that sting thee from every side.
*[Printed Old French: אגלינטייר"ש]* in Old French. Another explanation: actual scorpions; and so Jonathan translated: “and in the midst of a people whose deeds are like scorpions thou dwellest.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: Old French printed אגלינטייר"ש; it appears to be *aglentiers* (“briars”), but was not found in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: From going on My mission.
Open; and so “have opened their mouth” (Lamentations 3:46).
It is a parable: incline thine ear and hear, and it will be sweet to thee as though thou wert eating food in hunger.
What is the giving? It is the scroll of the book.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: behold, a hand was put forth
Ezekiel.english_translation: There are words that serve both the masculine and the feminine, like “The sun was risen upon the earth” (Genesis 19:23); “unto you that fear My name shall the sun of righteousness arise” (Malachi 3:20); “If Esau come to the one camp, and smite it” (Genesis 32).
Ezekiel.translator_note: Rashi’s point is grammatical gender. Printed “Genesis 32” is 32:9.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Aramaic: “What was from the beginning, and what is destined to be at the end.”
The punishment of the righteous in this world.
The giving of their reward, over which they will sing in the time to come.
The wailing of the wicked in the World to Come.
Aramaic: “And I received them, and their words were in my mouth like sweet honey.”
That they have a deep language which thou dost not recognize.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: but to the house of Israel
Ezekiel.english_translation: For to the house of Israel I send thee, whose language is like thy language.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Surely, if I sent thee to them
Ezekiel.english_translation: It is an expression of oath: if I sent thee to them — as I live — if they would not hearken to thee [that is, surely they would hearken]; and the verse is transposed.

A kind of worm, which they show upon the stone and it splits before it. (Gloss: Another version: *shamir* is an expression of hard rock; and in the Jerusalem Targum it is the translation of *tsur*, and so the Targum of “out of the rock of flint” (Deuteronomy 8): *shamir tanra*. And some understand *shamir* as strong iron, for as the hard rock is called *shamir*, so iron is called *shamir* because of its strength. *Sa”a*.)
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “Deuteronomy 8” is 8:15.

Ezekiel.english_translation: This prophecy is to say it to you.
Ezekiel.translator_note: “To you” (*aleikhem*) is translated as printed; the verse speaks of “them.”

Ezekiel.english_translation: Either they will hear or they will cease — say it to them.
After he finished his words, He commanded the spirit to carry him to the place where the sons of the exile were.
Kissing: striking one against another; and a song is heard in their striking, as he says above, “I heard the noise of their wings.”
For it was hard in my eyes to provoke the sons of my people.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the hand of the LORD was strong upon me
Ezekiel.english_translation: His pressure and His might, to lead me against my will.
To Tel-abib, the name of a place.
Stunned — a man struck dumb from speaking.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I have appointed thee a watchman
Ezekiel.english_translation: Why art thou silent? Is it not like the watchman whom they place upon the towers to see whether troops come to the city, so he blows the horn to warn the people that they gather and strengthen themselves? So have I set thee, to warn them to beware of the punishment, that I not bring it upon them.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I will lay a stumblingblock before him
Ezekiel.english_translation: When he does his deeds in secret and shows himself as a righteous man, I place a public transgression before him, in order to reveal his deeds; and when I bring evil upon him, they will not question Me.
His righteous deeds. Our Rabbis explained it of one who is dismayed over the former ones — that is, who regrets the former righteous deeds that he did.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the glory of the LORD stood there
Ezekiel.english_translation: He went before him to go there — an extra measure of humility, which it is not the way of flesh and blood to do; the disciple waits for the master, and here the Master waits for the disciple.
To show them that they are not worthy of rebuke.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: bands shall be put upon thee
Ezekiel.english_translation: Be bound in thy house as though thou wert bound with ropes; and so Jonathan: “Behold, the decree of My words is upon thee like one bound with cords,” etc.
When I wish to speak with thee, I will send thee to them.
All the words of My mission.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: he that heareth, let him hear
Ezekiel.english_translation: This is not part of the mission, but the Holy Spirit said to the prophet: Say to them My mission; and as for them, let the hearer hear and the one who ceases cease; for I know that not all of them will hear, for they are a rebellious house.
*[Printed Old French: טויל"ה]* in Old French; and some of them are large.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Old French printed טויל"ה (*tuile*); Darmesteter has the entry “Tuile” (*tella*) for this verse.

Ezekiel.english_translation: *Mangonel* [printed מגוניי"ל] in Old French, in which they throw stones at the city.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Old French printed מגוניי"ל; Darmesteter glosses it “Machine avec laquelle on lance des pierres contre la ville” (*mangonel*).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: cast up a mound against it
Ezekiel.english_translation: He pours out earth and heaps it up and packs it with sticks, and makes a high mound to stand upon and see inside the city and shoot arrows.
*[Printed Old French: בסטי"ון]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: *ifrurin*; and they are villages that his armies make, and they dwell in tents at the sides of the city, so that no one goes out or comes in. And the explanation of *karim* is princes appointed over the army: this one guards one side and that one another.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Aramaic *ifrurin* is transliterated as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: A model of the city wall that separates between the army and the city.
That so Jerusalem will come into siege.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: lie thou upon thy left side
Ezekiel.english_translation: To bear pain and afflictions, a count of days like the count of years “which my spirit has distressed me,” as it were, because they angered Me; and “it was doubled over their iniquity” after, since the punishment that I say I will bring upon them is hard in thine eyes.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The wording of this comment is corrupt or elliptical in the printed text (*asher hetsikatni ruḥi*; *vetakhpal al avonam aḥarei*); it is rendered literally and its sense cannot be confirmed.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: For I have appointed the years of their iniquity
Ezekiel.english_translation: I have lightened it for thee to receive the pain that I suffered for the number of years in which they sinned before Me: I have turned them for thee into a number of days. (Another version: *shenei* is like *shanim*; and so Jonathan translated: “And I have given thee, for one, two, for their sins.” *Sa”a*.)

We learned in Seder Olam: This teaches that Israel sinned three hundred and ninety years from when they entered the Land until the ten tribes were exiled from it. And you find of them specified two hundred and forty-three, from when Jeroboam reigned until Hoshea son of Elah was exiled, and in the days when the judges judged, one hundred and eleven years; and the rest are unspecified. These are the three hundred and ninety years that I found in the responsa of Rabbi Joseph, head of the academy: that the ten tribes sinned from the days of Joshua until Sennacherib exiled them from Samaria. Count in the days of the Judges: eight under Cushan, eighteen under Eglon, twenty under Sisera, seven under Midian, eighteen under the children of Ammon, forty under the Philistines — behold, one hundred and eleven; from Micah until the Ark was captured in the days of Eli, forty — behold, one hundred and fifty-one. Count for Jeroboam son of Nebat twenty-two; Nadab his son, two; Baasha, twenty-four; Elah his son, two; Omri, twelve; Ahab, twenty-two; Ahaziah his son, two; and Jehoram his brother, twelve; and Jehu, twenty-eight; Jehoahaz, sixteen; Joash his son, sixteen; and Jeroboam his son, forty-one — behold, three hundred and fifty years. And Menahem son of Gadi, ten; Pekahiah his son, two; and Pekah son of Remaliah, twenty; and Hoshea son of Elah, nine years — behold, three hundred and ninety-one. And the last year of Hoshea is not part of the count, because in the ninth year of Hoshea Samaria was captured, and the count of the kingship of Hoshea was only eight years — behold, three hundred and ninety years. And the forty years in which the kings of Judah sinned after the exile of Sennacherib, until this section was said to Ezekiel, are explained below, and I did not need to explain them. *Sa”a*.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Arithmetic as printed: the reigns listed from Jeroboam to Hoshea add up to 240 (199 + 41), where the printed text says 243. Translated as printed.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: bear the iniquity of the house of Judah
Ezekiel.english_translation: This teaches that the house of Judah sinned, from when the ten tribes were exiled until Jerusalem was destroyed, forty years: twenty-two of Manasseh, of whom it is written “as did Ahab” (2 Kings 21), and Ahab reigned twenty-two years; and two of Amon; and some say of Jehoiakim; and this prophecy was said to Ezekiel in the fifth year of Zedekiah — behold, forty. The total of all of them is four hundred and thirty; and after this prophecy six years remained — behold, eight Jubilees and thirty-six years. In eight Jubilees there are eight weeks of Sabbatical years, behold fifty-six Sabbatical years, and eight Jubilee years — behold, sixty-four; and in thirty-six years there are five Sabbatical years — behold, sixty-nine Sabbatical years; and the year of the last Jubilee was counted against them as a sin, for it was through their sin that they went into exile from it — behold, seventy years of Sabbatical sanctity that Israel did not release. Therefore they were exiled seventy years, to fulfil “Then shall the land be paid her sabbaths” (Leviticus 26:34); and that is what is written at the end of Chronicles: “to fulfil the word of the LORD by the mouth of Jeremiah, until the land had been paid her sabbaths; for as long as she lay desolate she kept sabbath, to fulfil threescore and ten years.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “2 Kings 21” is 21:3. The Chronicles passage is 2 Chronicles 36:21 (JPS wording).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: thou shalt lie on thy right side
Ezekiel.english_translation: [Thy left side] — for Samaria; thy right side — for Judah, because Judah is in the south of the Land of Israel, as it is said, “And thine elder sister is Samaria, that dwelleth at thy left hand” (below, 15–16); and also in the Book of Joshua he delimited the boundary of the tribe of Judah — the whole southern boundary.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “below 15–16” is Ezekiel 16:46 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_translation: Which thou hast engraved upon the brick, thou shalt set thy face: when thou liest on thy left side, the brick shall be opposite thee, and so when thou liest on the right.
It shall be bared before thee like a man who fights; it is a sign of Nebuchadnezzar fighting against it.
Like *geluyah* [revealed].
The decree of My commandment shall be heavy upon thee, as though thou wert bound with ropes, so that thou turn not from thy side to thy side.
The number of these days that I have decreed upon thee.

And millet and spelt — *panis*, *espeautre* [printed פאני"ץ איאפיילטר"א] in Old French — a sign of the famine that will be upon them in the days of the siege, and they will eat mixed bread, and in loathsomeness.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Old French printed פאני"ץ איאפיילטר"א; the forms appear to be *panis* (millet) and *espeautre* (spelt), in keeping with the Hebrew, but were not found in Darmesteter.

Ezekiel.english_translation: A sign for the people of the siege, who fear the famine and eat by weight and drink by measure.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: from time to time shalt thou drink
Ezekiel.english_translation: From day to day thou shalt drink this measure, a sixth of a hin.
Its preparation is repulsive, like the preparation of barley, and not fine like the preparation of a wheat cake.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: dung that cometh out of man
Ezekiel.english_translation: Thou shalt bake them in their coals, which dries them and burns them.
An expression of loathsomeness.
An expression of sighing.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: my soul hath not been polluted
Ezekiel.english_translation: I did not think by day and come to uncleanness at night.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: that which dieth of itself, or is torn of beasts
Ezekiel.english_translation: Flesh of an animal in danger of death, which resembles a *nevelah* and a *terefah*.
An animal about which a sage gave a ruling; for it is not possible to say actual *nevelah* and *terefah*, for if so, what would be the point?
Ezekiel.translator_note: The ruling is not stated in the printed text; translated literally.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Dung (*gelalim*).
The support of bread — *[printed Old French: פיצ"א דיפא"ן]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: They worry lest the bread run out for them.
*[Printed Old French: איינש"א]* in Old French; and in our language, *[printed Old French: טרוא"ר]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists the first form (איינשא) and glosses it “Avec crainte” (“with fear”). For the second, his manuscripts read דובטור (*dobtor*, from Latin *dubitorem*), whereas this printing has טרוא"ר, which could not be confirmed; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: that they may want bread and water
Ezekiel.english_translation: Their worry and their desolation is because they will lack bread and water in the days of the siege, and will worry lest it run out.
A sign of the sword of Nebuchadnezzar.

*Ta’ar hagalavim* — of the cobblers (*hara’tsanim*); and it is a Greek expression. And some say *[printed Old French: פרקמציר]* in Old French. And Menahem connected *ta’ar hagalavim* with “razor of the shavers,” and it has no likeness in Scripture.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. The final abbreviation (בתור') is read as “in Scripture.”

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: in the midst of the city
Ezekiel.english_translation: “Which thou hast engraved upon the brick”: when the days of thy siege are fulfilled, it is a sign that a third will be consumed within it by the burning pangs of famine, which are like fire, as it is said, “Our skin is hot like an oven because of the burning heat of famine” (Lamentations 5).
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “Lamentations 5” is 5:10 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_translation: Smite it with the sword.
Around that brick — a sign for those who flee from the city, whom the Chaldeans will overtake and slay around Jerusalem.

A sign for the exiles who will go to Egypt — Johanan son of Kareah and his company — “and I will draw out a sword after them” there; for Nebuchadnezzar went and destroyed Egypt, and they were slain there.
These are the few who will go into exile to Babylon and live.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: And of them again shalt thou take
Ezekiel.english_translation: Of those few.
A sign for Ahab son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah son of Maaseiah, whom the king of Babylon roasted.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: therefrom shall a fire come forth
Ezekiel.english_translation: From these hints that I hint to thee, the punishment shall go forth upon all the house of Israel.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: in the midst of the nations
Ezekiel.english_translation: In the middle of the world.
“And she changed My ordinances.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: Rashi reads *vatemer* as “changed”; JPS renders “rebelled.”

Ezekiel.english_translation: For so it is written in the Mishneh: “And Manasseh made Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem to err, so that they did evil more than did the nations, whom the LORD destroyed before the children of Israel” (2 Chronicles 33). And there are interpreters who say that the nations did not accept His Torah, whereas these accepted it and transgressed it.
Ezekiel.translator_note: “In the Mishneh” is printed as במשנה and is taken here as a reference to Chronicles (2 Chronicles 33:9); this identification is not certain. JPS wording quoted.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Because you have outdone the nations
Ezekiel.english_translation: Because you prepared yourselves for lawlessness (*hefker*) beyond the nations.
Ezekiel.translator_note: “Hefker” (literally “ownerless”) is left transliterated.

Ezekiel.english_translation: An expression of “and the king appointed (*vayeman*) for them” (Daniel 1); and Menahem explained it as an expression of tumult (*homah*), like “Nations were in tumult (*hamu*)” (Psalms 47).
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “Psalms 47” is 46:7. JPS wording quoted for both verses (Daniel 1:5, “the king appointed for them”).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: neither have done after the ordinances of the nations
Ezekiel.english_translation: For they did not exchange their gods, though they are no gods; and you exchanged My glory for that which does not profit. And our Rabbis explained: like the better ones among them you did not do; like the corrupt ones among them you did.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Rashi’s “exchanged My glory for that which does not profit” is his own wording of Jeremiah 2:11, not JPS’s.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Thou hast betrayed Me, and I too am against thee.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I will satisfy My fury upon them
Ezekiel.english_translation: When I take vengeance upon them, My fury will rest, and My spirit will not trouble Me.
And I shall be comforted for the grief that they grieved Me.
*[Printed Old French: דישטרוי"ר]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Old French printed דישטרוי"ר; Darmesteter prints the same form (in his manuscripts דישטרויר) and glosses it “Outrage.” Left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Contempt.
Chastisements (*yissurin*).
Bewilderment (*timahon*).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I will increase the famine upon you
Ezekiel.english_translation: It is the famine of the *perutah*, spent from the purse; so I heard.
The support of bread.
An expression of height (*ramah*).
An expression of *gai* (valley).
A kind of form of idolatrous images made on the roofs for the sun.
They will be recognizable in their guilt.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The rendering “recognizable” follows the printed word נכרים.

Ezekiel.english_translation: My kindness and My mercies, with which I had compassion on them when they acted perversely before Me in their land.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: how that I have been anguished with their straying heart
Ezekiel.english_translation: I humbled Myself before them: although their heart went astray and turned from Me, I sought of them through My prophets to return to Me, and I would do them good, and they were not willing.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: loathe themselves in their own sight
Ezekiel.english_translation: Menahem connected it with “I beheld them that were faithless, and strove with them” (there, 119): they will quarrel with themselves because they did not hearken to Me. And Targum Jonathan: *vidankon ve-inun yehon ḥazan*; and so he translated “the sighing” as *demaddenekim*, and “weeping and sighing” as *demaddenkan*; *[printed Old French: דמוניי"ר]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists the Old French form as printed (דמוניר, *demonir*) and glosses it “Ils réfléchiront tristement” (“they will reflect sadly”). The Aramaic words are transliterated as printed and not otherwise verified. “There, 119” is Psalms 119:158 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_translation: Its subject points to it: he strikes his foot on the ground and flattens the mud; and it is a manner of mourning.
A cry of grief and woe.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: he that remaineth and is besieged
Ezekiel.english_translation: He who is gathered into the city and they besiege him.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: thus will I spend My fury upon them
Ezekiel.english_translation: I shall complete all My wrath and My desire for their evil.
*[Printed Old French: פלנצו"ן]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: An expression of “a thick tree” (below, 20), whose branches are many.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “below 20” is Ezekiel 20:28.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Without an inhabitant.
Astonishment (*timahon*), at which those who see it will be astonished.

For I said, “you shall have been long in the land, and shall deal corruptly” … “I testify against you this day that you shall utterly perish” (Deuteronomy 4). And *venoshantem* has the numerical value of 852, and they stayed in it 850: four hundred and forty from when they entered it until the Temple was built, and four hundred and ten years the Temple stood.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Rashi abbreviates Deuteronomy 4:25–26; JPS has “I call heaven and earth to witness against you this day, that you shall soon utterly perish.”

Ezekiel.english_translation: A complete evil, singular above all the evils; and it is the destruction of the Temple.
Its accent is on the *alef*; it is an expression of the active (*po’elet*) form.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The grammatical term *po’elet* is left transliterated.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Its accent above is on the *bet*, and it is an expression of completed action: the turn has already come; like “came and set … the light of dawn,” and “the glory has come.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: Rashi’s two comparison phrases are printed in a compressed form and are rendered literally; their sources are not identified.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Aramaic: “and not to be saved in the fortresses of the mountains.” And *had* is an expression of a proclaiming cry to arise and flee to the tops of the mountains, like “I have made the vintage shout to cease” (Isaiah 17), and “and they shall answer him with a shout” (Jeremiah 21) — the sounding of the voice of one who carries a load of grapes to the winepress, and those who carry the beam.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 17” is 16:10 (JPS wording quoted); printed “Jeremiah 21” is 25:30, where Rashi’s Hebrew wording differs from the verse as the site prints it.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Quickly.
Behold, the day has come.
The evil.
The dawn of the day of the evil has risen.
To smite you.
Nebuchadnezzar the wicked has been revealed.
The violence that is in your hands has risen against you as a rod of wickedness to destroy you.
Thus said the Holy One, blessed be He, to the Destroyer: Thou art not obliged to leave a soul of the wicked of Israel, for no good comes out of them, nor of their sons, nor of their multitude.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: neither is there eminency among them
Ezekiel.english_translation: There is none among them who yearns after Me, longing and giving heart to Me, like “and all the house of Israel yearned after the LORD” (1 Samuel 6); and it is an Aramaic expression, *ve-itnehiu lefulḥana*, an expression of desire and longing. And Menahem connected it with an expression of wailing, and so “and all the house of Israel yearned” he explained as an expression of wailing; and there is nothing in the word but the *he*, which is the root.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “1 Samuel 6” is 7:2 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_translation: Although it is the way of one who sells his field to be sad, let him not be sad, for your end is to go into exile.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: For the seller shall not return to that which is sold
Ezekiel.english_translation: When he goes into exile he will not return and see again the field that he sold; and why should he mourn?
All the days of their lives they shall not return to their place.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: for the vision is touching the whole multitude thereof
Ezekiel.english_translation: Aramaic: “For the prophet prophesies concerning all their *atargushtehon*, to return in repentance, and they do not return.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Aramaic word אתרגושתהון is left transliterated; its meaning could not be confirmed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Each one of them: his life, and his soul is clinging to his iniquity.
They will not strengthen their hearts against their evil inclination to return to their Torah.
When the adversary comes upon them they prepare themselves for war, but none goes out to fight.
It is the way of doves to gather in the valleys and moan there; and they shall be moaning on the mountains where they flee, each in his iniquity, like the doves of the valleys, all of whom moan.
From the sweat of dread.
It will be an abomination (*shikkuts*) to them.

Of the Holy One, blessed be He, which He set for pride for them: this is the Temple, which is called “the pride of their strength,” as it is said (below, 24), “I will profane My sanctuary, the pride of your power”; they made idols of abominations in it; therefore, etc.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “below 24” is Ezekiel 24:21 (JPS wording quoted). “Therefore” is the printed abbreviation ע"כ.

Ezekiel.english_translation: The place where I was hidden among them.
A chain: it is a sign that they will go into exile bound in fetters.
Those liable to execution (*ḥayyavei ketol*).
The wicked and cruel among the idolaters.
And they will pass as an inheritance to others.
The houses of the temple of the high places where they used to meet; an expression of the house of their appointed gathering (*zimmun*).
Like “I have rolled up like a weaver my life” (Isaiah 38:12) — an expression of cutting off.
Ezekiel.translator_note: JPS wording quoted for Isaiah 38:12.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Event upon event, happening after happening; and Menahem connected it with an expression of breaking.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: instruction shall perish from the priest
Ezekiel.english_translation: Those accustomed to teaching, as it is said, “And they should seek the law at his mouth” (Malachi 2:7).
Ezekiel.translator_note: JPS wording quoted.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Of the exile of Jeconiah.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: from the appearance of his loins
Ezekiel.english_translation: It is forbidden to contemplate this verse.
By the hair of my head; *[printed Old French: פלוציי"ל]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: He showed me as though He were carrying me and bringing me to Jerusalem.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the gate of the inner court that looketh toward the north
Ezekiel.english_translation: The gate of the Azarah, which is inner to the Temple Mount; and it had gates on all its sides.

The form of jealousy, a provoker of jealousy and a vexer of the Holy One, blessed be He, for they placed it there to provoke the Holy One, blessed be He, to anger; and so Targum Jonathan: *tselem dekin’ata demargezin*.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Aramaic is transliterated as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: To the Temple Mount outside the Azarah; for he was standing at the opening of the northern gate of the Azarah on the outside, and “the way toward the north” is to the gate outside the Azarah.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: northward of the gate of the altar
Ezekiel.english_translation: On the Temple Mount, north of that northern gate of the Azarah; and I say that this gate was aligned opposite the altar.
When a person comes to enter the Azarah he finds it there, at the entry — *[printed Old French: אלאנטריא"ה]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Old French printed אלאנטריא"ה; it appears to be *l’entrée* (“the entrance”), but was not found in Darmesteter.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: that I should go far off from My sanctuary
Ezekiel.english_translation: So that I distance Myself from My sanctuary.
He brought me near to the opening of that very gate.
The wall of the Azarah.
And widen the hole.
Through the hole I saw the opening of a chamber.
Made for idolatrous abomination.
Engraved upon the wall.
He was esteemed, and his generation learned from him; therefore He was exacting with him.

*Temor ketor*, the cloud of incense; and *’atar* is an expression of abundance, and so “and have multiplied your words against Me” (below, 35), and so “the kisses of an enemy are importunate” (Proverbs 24); and so Menahem connected all three in one division, and the explanation of the matter is “they are abundant”; but each is an expression of human speech.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The opening words (תמור קטור) and the closing clause (אך כל אחד לשון בני אדם) are unclear in the printed text and are rendered literally. Printed “below 35” is Ezekiel 35:13 and “Proverbs 24” is 27:6 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_translation: *Meshukhah* in a pavement of marble stones; an expression of “and will cover thee with My hand” (Exodus 32).
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “Exodus 32” is 33:22 (JPS wording quoted, “cover”). *Meshukhah* is left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the door of the gate of the LORD’S house
Ezekiel.english_translation: Within the space of the Azarah, to the opening of the Sanctuary (*heikhal*) which is in the north; for the Master said: There were two wickets in the Chamber of the Hearths (*Beit HaḤalifot*), one in the north and one in the south.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The name of the chamber is left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: A certain image, which they heat from within; and its eyes were of lead, and they melt from the heat of the fire, so that it appears as though it were weeping; and she says: it is an offering that it asks.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The last clause (ואומרת תקרובת הוא שואל) is unclear and is rendered literally.

Ezekiel.english_translation: An expression of heating, like “than it was wont to be heated” (Daniel 3:19), and *ve-atuna azeh yatira* (there).
Ezekiel.translator_note: JPS wording quoted for the first phrase; the Aramaic phrase is in Daniel 3:22 (JPS: “and the furnace exceeding hot”).

Ezekiel.english_translation: *[Printed Old French: פיישנ"ט פלורי"ר לא"ל קאלפי"ץ]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the inner court of the LORD’S house
Ezekiel.english_translation: It is the Azarah, for the Temple Mount is called the outer court; and until now he was standing inside it, except that he had entered by the northern gate, and he showed him in the Chamber of the Hearths the image of Tammuz, and he returned and led him to the east, before the Sanctuary and the altar.

From the words “and their faces toward the east” I know that their backs were toward the Sanctuary; but it tells that their backs were uncovered, for they would open themselves wide and *mat’rizin* toward below.
Ezekiel.translator_note: *Mat’rizin* (מתריזין) is left transliterated; its meaning could not be confirmed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: It serves for two words: an expression of destruction and an expression of bowing. So it is in the Jerusalem Talmud: “they were destroying the Temple and bowing to the sun”; and so Targum Jonathan: *ve-inun mitḥablin vesagdin*. And Menahem connected it with an expression of bowing down, like “Bow down, that we may go over” (Isaiah 51).
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 51” is 51:23 (JPS wording quoted). “It serves for two words” is rendered literally from בשתי תיבות הוא משמש.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Is it a light thing to the house of Judah
Ezekiel.english_translation: Is it little to them, and light in their eyes, the other transgressions that are in their hands?

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: that they commit the abominations which they commit here
Ezekiel.english_translation: If they had ceased from doing all the abominations that they did in My house here.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: in that they fill the land with violence
Ezekiel.english_translation: And that iniquity is light in their eyes, and they return to provoke Me in the midst of My house with these abominations.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: they put the branch to their nose
Ezekiel.english_translation: And behold, they send to their nostrils the foul smell of this branch which they prune, by the wind that issues from the mouth of the ring — that is to say, their shame shall return upon their faces. And Menahem explained: “And lo, they put the branch to their nose” is a matter of blemish and disgrace; according to his explanation, equate the smell of their incense and the anger of their offering and the sweet savours with the work of blemish of the orifices; and “their backs toward the temple of the LORD” points to the matter.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The final sentence (Menahem’s explanation) is compressed in the printed text and is rendered literally; its sense is uncertain.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: them that have charge over the city
Ezekiel.english_translation: Bring near the appointed ones whom I have appointed to destroy the city.
Our Rabbis explained them in tractate Shabbat: Wrath (*ketsef*), Anger (*af*), Fury (*ḥemah*), Destroyer (*mashḥit*), Breaker (*mashber*), Consumer (*mekhalleh*).
That breaks everything, as in “dasheth thy little ones against the rock” (Psalms 137).
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “Psalms 137” is 137:9 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_translation: A notebook (*pinkas*): tablets covered with wax, and they engrave on them with a pen.
It is the altar of stones that Solomon made in place of the copper altar that Moses made in the wilderness.

From the *kapporet*, where the Shekhinah had rested until now; and it began to withdraw and go out little by little, ten journeys, and this is the first journey: from the cherub to the threshold of the Holy of Holies. (See Amos 9, verse 1, in Rashi, and it requires further study. *Yosh”h*.)
Ezekiel.translator_note: The parenthesis is not Rashi’s own wording but a later editor’s note; its last word (יוש"ה) is left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: And thou shalt make a mark.
The righteous, to be a sign that the destroyers shall not strike them.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: to the others He said in my hearing
Ezekiel.english_translation: To the six destroyers.

From those who stand before My sanctuary; and our Rabbis said: Read not *mimmikdashi* but *mimmekudashai* — from those sanctified to Me. They are the ones marked with the *tav*, whom He had warned against harming; He again commanded to destroy them, because the attribute of Justice said before Him: What is different about these from those? Behold, they did not protest against them — as is stated in tractate Shabbat.
And I remained.
Perverted judgment.

Over the heads of the four living creatures of the chariot; and in this section He again calls them cherubim, because the face of the ox was turned into the face of a cherub, as is written in this section. And our Rabbis said: Ezekiel sought mercy, and they turned it into a cherub. He said before Him: Master of the World, a prosecutor does not become a defender.

Between the wheels. Wherever it is said “and He said, and He said,” it is only for exposition: the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Gabriel, and he asked the cherub to give them to him, so that the coals might cool and the decree be lightened; and so it is explained in the matter: “and took thereof, and put it into the hands of him that was clothed in linen.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: Rashi’s citation “and took, and put into the hands of him that was clothed in linen” is Ezekiel 10:7; his wording is slightly different from the verse as the site prints it.

Ezekiel.english_translation: He did not throw them at once; and although the one clothed in linen received them, he did not throw them until after six years from his receiving them, for the coals were dimmed in his hand all six years; and know it, for this prophecy was said in the sixth year, and the city was destroyed in the eleventh year.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the right side of the house
Ezekiel.english_translation: In the south.
It is the Azarah.
It is the very departure mentioned above.

The Temple Mount. One might think [that it was heard no further] because the voice was low; therefore Scripture says “as the voice of God Almighty when He speaketh.” Rather, when it reaches the outer court it is cut off.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The bracketed words are supplied to complete the sense.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Because one of the faces was changed, it was needed to repeat and recount here the whole work of the living creatures as at first, lest you say it is another chariot.
Of the wheels: they are the hole in which the chariot rolls, which they call *boiel* [printed בויי"ל] in Old French; and Targum Jonathan: *ve-ashdatehon ushefukhehon*.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists the form as printed (בויל, *boïl*) with its manuscript variants; he adds no gloss beyond the Hebrew “and their hands.” The Aramaic is transliterated as printed.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the wheels that they four had
Ezekiel.english_translation: Of the four wheels of the living creatures.
I heard that the angel was calling the *ofan* “galgal.”

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: they were called in my hearing
Ezekiel.english_translation: To them the name “galgal” was called.
These were the faces of the ox that were turned into a cherub.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the door of the east gate of the LORD’S house
Ezekiel.english_translation: The opening of the Sanctuary (*heikhal*).
That in the east; and this was the second journey of departure: from the threshold of the Holy of Holies to the Azarah.
Since I saw in this chariot all the work of the first chariot, I say: this is what I saw at the river Chebar.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I knew that they were cherubim
Ezekiel.english_translation: That the face of the ox was turned into a cherub; and there were in it two faces of a man: a small face of a child and a large face of a man.
These are the very ones of whom it said above “their backs toward the temple of the LORD,” except that it did not specify there who they were, and here it specifies the names of two of them.
The words of the prophets will come upon us [not soon].
Ezekiel.translator_note: The bracketed words are supplied to complete the sense.

Ezekiel.english_translation: There is no need to be concerned about them; rather, build houses and dwell in them, for we shall not be exiled from this city until our death.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: this city is the caldron, and we are the flesh
Ezekiel.english_translation: Just as the flesh does not leave the pot until its cooking is complete, so we shall not leave it until we die.

I know that you said this, that Jerusalem is the pot and you are the flesh. But I say to you that for the slain whom you have placed in it, it is a pot, for they were completed in it; but for you it shall not be a pot to enclose you until the day of death, for I will bring you out of it.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the things that come into your mind
Ezekiel.english_translation: What comes up in your mind — *[printed Old French: בוטר"א טלנ"ט]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Old French printed בוטר"א טלנ"ט; it appears to be *votre talent* (“your desire, your mind”), but was not found in Darmesteter at this verse; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Like *lehotsi*; and in vain have you built the houses, for into exile shall the fathers and the sons go, and none will inherit the houses.
When you turned for help to the king of Egypt, as it is said of Zedekiah, “But he rebelled against him in sending his ambassadors into Egypt” (below, 16).
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “below 16” (יו) is Ezekiel 17:15 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_translation: At the end of the border, and it is Riblah in the land of Hamath, which is Antioch; there Zedekiah was judged by Nebuchadnezzar, as it is said in the Book of Kings (2 Kings 25): there he slew his sons, there he put out his eyes. And it is the end of the border, as it is said of the spies, and in several places, “at the entrance to Hamath” (Numbers 13).
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “Numbers 13” is 13:21 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_translation: The *mishmeret* — I have set it [for them] until the completion of their cooking.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The first word and the sentence are unclear in the printed text and are rendered literally.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: you shall be the flesh in the midst thereof
Ezekiel.english_translation: That you shall be cut up in it and broken in it, like flesh in a pot and in a cauldron.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The first verb (שחותכו) is unclear in the printed text; rendered by sense.

Ezekiel.english_translation: And not in it shall you die.
The exile of Samaria and the exile of Jeconiah.
Who went into exile.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: concerning whom the inhabitants of Jerusalem have said
Ezekiel.english_translation: Concerning whom the inhabitants of Jerusalem said — those who were not exiled with Jeconiah, because Nebuchadnezzar made Zedekiah king over them; and now they too make sport of their brethren who were exiled, and say of them, “Get you far from the LORD.”
Aramaic: “to the synagogues in which they dwell, second to the Temple.”
A heart soft and easily humbled.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: whose heart walketh after the heart of their detestable things
Ezekiel.english_translation: And those whose heart goes after the heart of an abomination and abominations, who remained in Jerusalem and were not exiled, and err after idolatry and its abominations.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I will bring their way upon their own heads
Ezekiel.english_translation: That I will bring upon them sword and captivity, and they will go into exile.
After He finished His words to me, it departed.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the mountain which is on the east side of the city
Ezekiel.english_translation: It is the Mount of Olives, which is on the east of the city; and this was the third journey.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: in the vision by the spirit of God
Ezekiel.english_translation: It seemed to me as though now He were returning me from Jerusalem to Babylon.

A vessel for drinking and a small *mekidah* for kneading a cake in it — a sign to the house of Israel that is in Jerusalem that they would do so, and would not need to knead dough in a hollow on the ground with the gravel stones entering into it; and they did not hearken to him and were compelled to it. And that is the verse in the book of Lamentations: “He hath also broken my teeth with gravel stones” (Lamentations 3), in the Midrash on Lamentations.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “Lamentations 3” is 3:16 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: remove as though for exile by day
Ezekiel.english_translation: From day to day, two or three days, conduct thyself like a man who prepares his steps for exile, that the sons of the exile may see and ask, What is thy doing? and thou shalt tell them that it is a sign for Zedekiah and his people; and these will send their messengers to them, and inform their brethren and relatives who are there of all that they hear from thy mouth. And so every *yomam* in Scripture is an expression of “day by day,” a matter practised for many days. So I heard in the name of Rabbi Menahem, and his words are true.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: it may be they will perceive
Ezekiel.english_translation: Perhaps they will understand — *[printed Old French: אפרצברונ"ט]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Old French printed אפרצברונ"ט; it appears to be *aperceveront* (“they will perceive”), but was not found in Darmesteter.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: for they are a rebellious house
Ezekiel.english_translation: Therefore it is still “perhaps.”

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: as when men go forth into exile
Ezekiel.english_translation: *[Printed Old French: קומ"א אישוא"ש]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: A sign for Zedekiah, that he would go out by way of a tunnel, a cave, for he feared to go out openly because of the Chaldeans.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: carry it forth in the darkness
Ezekiel.english_translation: When it grows dark thou shalt carry out thy vessels.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I brought forth my stuff by day, as stuff for exile
Ezekiel.english_translation: Day by day I showed them that I was preparing for myself vessels of exile.
Concerning King Zedekiah I show this burden — an expression of prophecy.
Out of shame, because he flees the city by night.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: My net also will I spread upon him
Ezekiel.english_translation: He had a cave from his house to the plains of Jericho, and he went out by way of the cave. What did the Holy One, blessed be He, do? He brought a deer before the Chaldean army, and it went before them upon the roof of the cave, and they pursued it; and when Zedekiah came out of the cave on the plains of Jericho, they saw him coming out and seized him.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: yet shall he not see it
Ezekiel.english_translation: For at Riblah, in the land of Hamath, He spoke judgments with him, and blinded his eyes, and afterward brought him to Babylon, as it is said in the Book of Kings (2 Kings 25, and in Jeremiah 39).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: all that are round about him to help him
Ezekiel.english_translation: His princes; and Menahem interpreted it as an expression of wings.

*[Printed Old French: אפנדר"י]* in Old French. They are Johanan son of Kareah and the officers of the armies who went into exile to Egypt, and there the sword of Nebuchadnezzar overtook them when he destroyed Egypt.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Old French printed אפנדר"י; it appears to be *espandre* (“to scatter”), but was not found in Darmesteter.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: that they may declare all their abominations
Ezekiel.english_translation: And they will say: Through our iniquities we suffered, for thus and thus we did; and I will make known that it was not for nothing that I consumed them.
From its wealth.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: because of the violence of all them that dwell therein
Ezekiel.english_translation: For the sin of the violence of its inhabitants.
*[Printed Old French: לי"ש אשייא"ש]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Why do you always speak so in your mouths, to use this saying?
And the punishment does not come, and in the meantime the evil vision that the prophets prophesy to us will perish, and be forgotten, and fade away.
An expression of *mashal*.
The false prophets will no longer be able to promise you peace falsely, for I will quickly bring forward the words of the true prophets to come.
*[Printed Old French: דבנייל"א]* in Old French — a divination of smooth things (flatteries).
Ezekiel.translator_note: Old French printed דבנייל"א; it appears to be *devinaille* (“divination”), but was not found in Darmesteter.

Ezekiel.english_translation: *[Printed Old French: שר"א אלונגי"א]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Old French printed שר"א אלונגי"א; it appears to be *sera alongié* (“will be prolonged”), but was not found in Darmesteter.

Ezekiel.english_translation: The prophecy will not be fulfilled except at a distant time.
The fools.
Like “their own will.”
When a man comes at the breach of the ruin, the fox flees by way of another breach, and does not stand in the breach to fight.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: You have not gone up into the breaches
Ezekiel.english_translation: You have not done good deeds by which you could hold back the evil from coming.
An expression of prophecy.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: yet they hope that the word would be confirmed
Ezekiel.english_translation: And how do they expect to fulfil their words? An expression of hope; and some say *[printed Old French: איקוויירירא"ט]* in Old French — another expression: an expression of waiting.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: it buildeth up a slight wall
Ezekiel.english_translation: And behold, My people are like builders of a partition wall, and the prophets daub it with *tafel* — a ground-material resembling lime — and it does not stand before the rains.
Ezekiel.translator_note: *Tafel* is left transliterated.

Ezekiel.english_translation: *[Printed Old French: אוטומנ"ץ]* in Old French; and some say *[printed Old French: בלאשטניי"א]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: *Ve-attenah* is like *ve-atten* [“and you,” feminine].

Large hailstones. And I say that because they are bright like all crystal stones, he likens them to *gavish*, which is a precious stone, as it is said, “coral or of crystal” (Job 28). And our Rabbis said: *El-gavish* — those that stood in the air on the back of a man (*al gav ish*); and this is Moses our teacher, as it is said, “and the rain was not poured upon the earth” (Exodus 9) — those that had begun to descend did not reach the earth.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “Job 28” is 28:18 and “Exodus 9” is 9:33 (JPS wording quoted). The word “(hail)” in the printed text is an editor’s gloss.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Upon the wall.
So when the evil comes, it will be said to you: Where is the peace that you promised?
It is Jerusalem.

*[Printed Old French: קוטרא"ש]* in Old French: a kind of small cushions they would sew and hang upon the joints of the arms of those who inquired of them, and they divined for them with those cushions false divination; and for whom they wished, they said a good divination, and for whom they wished, they said an evil divination.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: *[Printed Old French: איישיל"ש]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this form (איישילש) with the gloss “aux aisselles” (“to the armpits”).
