Ezekiel.english_translation: Like *atsilei yadayim*, and like *talmei sadai* (Hosea 11).
Ezekiel.translator_note: The phrase *talmei sadai* occurs in Hosea 10:4 and 12:12 (JPS: “in the furrows of the field”); the printed reference “Hosea 11” does not match either, and which verse Rashi means is not confirmed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Upon the heads of the men; these too to divine with them. And I do not know what they are; since it is said, “and I will tear them” (v. 20), I say that they are of cloth. And Jonathan translated them *pat komarim*; and so he translated *bamot teluot*: *meḥayfin pat komarim*.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Targum words are transliterated as printed and not otherwise verified.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Like “Put me, I pray thee, into one of the priests’ offices” (*sappaḥeni na*) (1 Samuel 2); *[printed Old French: לישאגמנ"ץ]* in Old French. And some have *[printed Old French: פלטראיי"ש]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. JPS wording quoted (1 Samuel 2:36).

Ezekiel.english_translation: With them they hunt the souls to Gehinnom, for they strengthen the hands of the wicked by divining peace for them, and weaken the hands of the righteous by divining evil for them.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Will you hunt the souls of My people
Ezekiel.english_translation: It is an expression of astonishment.
*Lakhenah* is like *lakhem* [for you]; for you receive payment for this and are sustained by it.
Like “Who hath measured the waters in the hollow of his hand” (Isaiah 40); *[printed Old French: אונגיאלוניא"ש]* in Old French; another explanation: an expression of measure.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. JPS wording quoted (Isaiah 40:12).

Ezekiel.english_translation: *[Printed Old French: איאנפיצא"ש]* in Old French — for you receive it as your payment.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: to slay the souls that should not die
Ezekiel.english_translation: That is, to say of souls that should not die that these shall die, and to say of those that should not live that they shall live; for your divinations are false, and My people accept your lying divinations.
To be flying away upon your arms to Gehinnom.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I will let the souls go
Ezekiel.english_translation: As its Targum: “And I will deliver the souls that you are plotting, their souls, to destruction.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Aramaic is rendered literally.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the souls that you hunt as birds
Ezekiel.english_translation: *Et nefashim* — the men, so that the souls fly away.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Because with lies you have cowed the heart of the righteous
Ezekiel.english_translation: When you divine evil for him, he is pained and his heart is crushed.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Then came certain of the elders of Israel unto me
Ezekiel.english_translation: All of them with one heart for evil; therefore it says “and he came.” But an aggadic midrash says: because the Holy One, blessed be He, uncovered the prophet’s ear beforehand: Behold, so-and-so and so-and-so will come to thee.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: set up their idols in their mind
Ezekiel.english_translation: Their heart is toward their idols, to worship them.
So that the idol is always before them, for fear and as a god.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: should I be inquired of at all by them
Ezekiel.english_translation: A warning: for I will inquire for them, and will answer their words; many astonishments are fulfilled.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The sentence is compressed in the printed text and is rendered literally.

Ezekiel.english_translation: *[Printed Old French: שויי"ש רפונדו"ץ]* in Old French — although he comes before Me with the multitude of his idols; so Targum Jonathan.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Old French printed שויי"ש רפונדו"ץ; it appears to be *suis respondus* (“I am answered”), but was not found in Darmesteter.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: take the house of Israel in their own heart
Ezekiel.english_translation: Aramaic: “In order to draw near the house of Israel to give repentance in their heart.”
Like “the prince among his brethren” (*nezir eḥav*) (Genesis 49); *[printed Old French: פורינ"ט אשיברי"ץ]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The first printed form begins פורינ"ט, which appears to be *furent* (“they were”); the whole could not be confirmed in Darmesteter and is left as printed. The printed reference “Genesis 49” is 49:26 (JPS “prince among his brethren”); Rashi cites it for the root, meaning separation.

Ezekiel.english_translation: From your ways.
Your hearts.
Which you have set up upon your hearts.
Those before whom you have set the stumblingblock of your iniquities.
Aramaic: “As he inquires of him, by My Word I shall be sought by him.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Aramaic is rendered literally; the sense of *edrash lo* here is not certain.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I will set My face against that man
Ezekiel.english_translation: Afterward, if he does not hearken to the words of the prophet.
*[Printed Old French: מישאירא"ש]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: *ve-ashtsiniyeh*.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Aramaic is transliterated as printed.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: And when the prophet is enticed and speaketh a word
Ezekiel.english_translation: That is not true.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I the LORD have enticed that prophet
Ezekiel.english_translation: I opened for him an opening to whatever he wishes; and from here it is said: one who comes to defile himself, they open for him.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the iniquity of the prophet shall be even as the iniquity of him that inquireth
Ezekiel.english_translation: Aramaic: “Like the guilt of one who comes to learn and does not learn, so shall be the guilt of the false prophet.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Aramaic is rendered literally.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: break the staff of the bread thereof
Ezekiel.english_translation: The support of bread.

Because these three saw three worlds: Noah saw the world built, and destroyed, and built; and Daniel — the Temple, or himself — first a prince over all the princes, at the end thrown into the lions’ den, and he returned to his greatness; and so Job saw himself settled, and ruined, and settled. Therefore He brought them as an example for the generation of Jeconiah, who saw the House in its building, and its destruction, and the second building. And so the Holy One, blessed be He, said to them: An extra affection I show you, you of Jeconiah and his exile: if one of the lands of the idolaters should sin against Me, and I decree upon them one of these four judgments — either famine, or evil beast, or sword, or pestilence — as they are arranged in this section one after another, and these three righteous men were in it, they would not save either son or daughter; and I will bring all four of them upon Jerusalem, and I will leave for you some of your sons who are there, though you are not among them — not that they are worthy of being saved, but to comfort you when they go into exile to you, and you see their evil deeds and are comforted over the evil that I brought upon them, for you will see that they were not fit to be borne any longer. (Behold, this is the course of the order of this entire section; this language cannot be settled, and it appears that it is not the language of the Master; and further it appears that in this book one of the four judgments is missing, from “*me-az*” until “*az*”; another version: from “*me-o*” until “*o*”.) Another explanation: “When a land sinneth against Me,” etc. “though these three men, Noah, Daniel, and Job, were in it” — because the Holy One, blessed be He, saved these three from these three (four) judgments, Scripture mentioned these. Noah escaped from three of them. From the evil beast, whence do you say? At the time he entered the ark, all the animals sought to enter, and the Holy One, blessed be He, did not let them, as it is written, “and the LORD shut him in” (there, 7); “shut” is nothing but from animals, as it says, “and hath shut the lions’ mouths, and they have not hurt me” (Daniel 7). A lion came to enter, and its teeth were dulled; a bear came to enter, and its legs were entangled, etc., in Genesis Rabbah. From the famine, whence? As it is said, “from the ground which the LORD hath cursed” (Genesis 5): go and learn in Genesis Rabbah, in the place where it counts the ten famines that came into the world, and you will find that in the days of Noah there was one of them; and it brings proof from “the ground which He hath cursed.” From the sword — this is the Flood; and also, his generation sought to attack him and said, We will not let him enter; but the Holy One, blessed be He, saved him. The Holy One, blessed be He, said: I will not let him enter except at midday, and whoever senses it, let him speak. Hence it is written, “In the selfsame day entered Noah” (there, 7) — in the very midst of the day. Daniel: at the time Nebuchadnezzar entered the Temple in the days of Jehoiakim and killed Jehoiakim, and left Daniel and exiled Daniel with an exile of *shelomit*, because he found him full of the spirit of wisdom. From the famine: for before Jerusalem was conquered in the days of Jehoiakim, Nebuchadnezzar besieged it three years, as it is said, “And there was a great famine in the city” (2 Kings 5), and also (Jeremiah 52:6) “the famine was sore.” From the beasts, whence? “And hath shut the lions’ mouths” (Daniel 7), “and they have not hurt me.” And so you find Job escaped from the three. From the famine, whence? According to the one who says that Job lived in the days of Jacob, we find that there was famine in his days. From the beast, whence? As it is written, “and his possessions are increased in the land” — he broke the fence of the world. From the sword, whence? “He cleaveth my reins asunder, and doth not spare” (Job 16).
Ezekiel.translator_note: Several points are marked as uncertain: (1) “Daniel — the Temple, or himself —” is translated as printed. (2) The parenthesis beginning “Behold, this is the course…” is an editor’s remark, not Rashi’s own wording. (3) “*shelomit*” (שלומי') is left transliterated. (4) The printed “and whoever senses it, let him speak” (ודרגיש לי' ימלל) is rendered literally. (5) Printed reference “2 Kings 5” does not match the verse; the nearest verses are 2 Kings 6:25 (famine in Samaria) and 25:3. JPS wording quoted where the Hebrew matches: Genesis 7:16 (“and the LORD shut him in”), Daniel 6:23 (printed “Daniel 7”: “and hath shut the lions’ mouths, and they have not hurt me”), Genesis 5:29 (“which the LORD hath cursed”), Genesis 7:13 (“In the selfsame day entered Noah”), Job 1:10 (“his possessions are increased in the land”), Job 16:13 (“He cleaveth my reins asunder, and doth not spare”).

Ezekiel.english_translation: Why were sons and daughters not mentioned in the death by famine, that it is not said of them “if sons or if daughters they shall save,” as they were mentioned in the last two judgments? [It is] an example regarding Daniel, who is one of them, and he was from the generation of Jeconiah, and neither sons nor daughters escaped with him; and concerning him Isaiah prophesied (56): “For thus saith the LORD concerning the eunuchs that keep My sabbaths.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “(56)” is Isaiah 56:4 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: If I cause evil beasts to pass through the land
Ezekiel.english_translation: If a beast.
Armies for war.

An expression of *kal va-ḥomer*, “how much the more”; and so throughout Scripture, for instance “Behold, we are afraid here in Judah; how much more then if we go to Keilah” (1 Samuel 23); and so in this section (Ezekiel 15:5), “Behold, when it was whole, it was meet for no work; how much less, when the fire hath devoured it,” etc.
Ezekiel.translator_note: JPS wording quoted for both verses; 1 Samuel 23:3.

Ezekiel.english_translation: *[Printed Old French: מישגושטיש"ש]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: *[Printed Old French: איירטרמאי"ש]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: In captivity, and they will bring them here.
Their deeds.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: what is the vine-tree more than any tree
Ezekiel.english_translation: What is its end compared with all other trees?

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the vine branch which grew up among the trees of the forest
Ezekiel.english_translation: Not of the vine of the vineyards, which makes fruit, do I speak to thee, but of vine shoots that grew in the forests.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Shall wood be taken thereof to make any work
Ezekiel.english_translation: It is not fit for that.
Any vessel at all.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: it is cast into the fire for fuel
Ezekiel.english_translation: *[Printed Old French: ארבירי"ר]* in Old French. Behold, I asked thee about the whole one, and it is not fit for anything; now I add further to the question: behold, if they put a branch of it into the fire, and the fire consumed it at both its ends around, until its inside was singed.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: What remained from the fire — *broier* [printed ברואי"ר] in Old French. *Nehar* is an expression of “and my bones are burned with heat” (Job 30); and some foreign-language speakers say *[printed Old French: אשאר"ט]* in Old French; and so “He hath also kindled His wrath against me” (there, 19) — Menahem connected it with “and my bones are burned.” Is it yet fit for work?
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists the form ברואיר (*broier*, with variants) and glosses it “Roussi” (“singed, scorched”). The second Old French form (אשאר"ט) could not be confirmed; left as printed. JPS wording quoted: Job 30:30; Job 19:11 (printed “there, 19”).

Ezekiel.english_translation: An expression of *kal va-ḥomer*, “how much the more”; and so throughout Scripture, for instance “Behold, we are afraid here in Judah; how much more then if we go to Keilah” (1 Samuel 23).
Ezekiel.translator_note: JPS wording quoted (1 Samuel 23:3).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: so do I give the inhabitants of Jerusalem
Ezekiel.english_translation: Jerusalem, both of whose ends the fire consumed — two exiles. When Jehoiakim was exiled, there went into exile with him some of the royal seed and of the nobles, as it is said in Daniel; after him Jeconiah his son was exiled, and the craftsmen and the smith; “and the midst of it is singed” — Zedekiah, who remained in it: already His decree was upon him, “fill both thy hands with coals of fire … and dash them against the city” (above, 10).
Ezekiel.translator_note: JPS wording quoted: Daniel 1:3 (“the seed royal, and … the nobles”), Jeremiah 29:2 (“the craftsmen, and the smiths”), Ezekiel 10:2.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: out of the fire are they come forth
Ezekiel.english_translation: Aramaic: “Concerning the words of the Torah which were given from the midst of fire, they transgressed; and the nations that are strong as fire shall destroy them.”

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: cause Jerusalem to know her abominations
Ezekiel.english_translation: *[Printed Old French: פיישבויי"ר]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Old French printed פיישבויי"ר; it appears to be *faire savoir* (“to make known”), but was not found in Darmesteter.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Like *megurotayikh* [“thy sojournings”]; and Menahem connected it with an expression of offspring, and so he explained “Weapons of violence their kinship” (Genesis 49), “every man from him that bestoweth it upon him” (2 Kings 12), “beside that which is his due” (Deuteronomy 18) — all of them expressions of generations.
Ezekiel.translator_note: JPS wording quoted; JPS renders the last two verses differently from Rashi’s sense. Genesis 49:5; 2 Kings 12:6; Deuteronomy 18:8.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the Amorite was thy father, and thy mother was a Hittite
Ezekiel.english_translation: Abraham and Sarah: from there they took their greatness; and the sons of Heth gave her a burial place.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: in the day thou wast born
Ezekiel.english_translation: *[Printed Old French: פושניא"ה]* in Old French. When I chose thee in Egypt, thou wast without any tending; and because he likened the matter to a birth, he mentioned here the tendings of the newborn.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Like *shorrekh*.

For the polishing (*tsaḥtsuaḥ*) of the bare rock (*tsaḥiaḥ hasela*); its Targum is *she‘iyut kefa*; *[printed Old French: אפלצמנ"ט]* in Old French. And Menahem connected *lemish‘i* with an expression of delights (*sha‘ashu‘im*).
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. The Aramaic is transliterated as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: From here we learn that they salt the newborn, in order that its flesh may become firm.
An expression of wrapping in cloths, and so “and thick darkness a swaddlingband for it” (Job 38) — which means that they wrap the newborn.
Ezekiel.translator_note: JPS wording quoted (Job 38:9).

Ezekiel.english_translation: To spare.
*[Printed Old French: אנבורישמנ"ט]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Trampled down, like “we tread down our adversaries.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: The printed Hebrew (יבוס קמינו) differs from Psalms 44:6 (JPS: “Through Thy name do we tread them under that rise up against us”); translated as Rashi has it.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Even in thy foulness: in this thou shalt not die. And that He repeated it, to say it twice, is because by the blood of the Passover and the blood of circumcision they were redeemed. Another explanation: *mitboseset* — *[printed Old French: שוייליא"ה]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. “Even in thy foulness: in this thou shalt not die” is rendered literally from the printed text.

Ezekiel.english_translation: As it is said, “And the children of Israel were fruitful, and increased abundantly, and multiplied” (Exodus 1:7).

An expression of completeness (*makhlol*); and Menahem explained *ba‘adi* as *adi adayim*, an expression of *ad*, like “Trust you in the LORD for ever” (Isaiah 26) — *[printed Old French: אנגוק"א אשיגל"א]* in Old French. But Dunash explained it as an expression of *adi* [ornament], and the form of *adi* — *adayim* — is from ten nouns: *ari* — *arayim*, *tsvi* — *tsviyim*, *gedi* — *gediyim*.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Old French printed אנגוק"א אשיגל"א; it appears to be *enjusqu’à siècle* (“until the age, for ever”), but was not found in Darmesteter. JPS wording quoted (Isaiah 26:4).

Ezekiel.english_translation: *[Printed Old French: פורינ"ט אפייטיאש]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The first word of the printed Old French (פורינ"ט) appears to be *furent* (“they were”); the whole could not be confirmed in Darmesteter and is left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Signs of maidenhood.
*[Printed Old French: אמיטיא"ש]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Old French printed אמיטיא"ש; it appears to be *amitiés* (“affections”), but was not found in Darmesteter.

Ezekiel.english_translation: An expression of anointing. And the whole subject is only a parable; and Jonathan explained all of it, and there is nothing to add to the Targum, and so he explained it.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Then washed I thee with water
Ezekiel.english_translation: [On “thine origin and thy nativity,” etc.] Aramaic: “Your sojournings and your births from the land of the Canaanites: there I was revealed to Abraham your father between the pieces, and I made known to him that you would go down to Egypt; and with an exalted arm I will redeem you, and by the merit of your fathers I will drive out the Amorites and destroy the Hittites.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Aramaic passage is printed in the source under this verse, though it renders Ezekiel 16:3–13; the lemma shown is taken from this verse. Rashi has just said that Jonathan explained all of it.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Then washed I thee with water
Ezekiel.english_translation: [On “thy nativity, in the day thou wast born,” etc.] Aramaic: “And also when your fathers went down to Egypt, dwelling in a land not theirs, enslaved and afflicted, the congregation of Israel was like a child cast out upon the face of the field, whose navel was not cut, and who was not washed in water to be cleansed, and was not salted with salt, and was not tended with bandages.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Aramaic passage is printed in the source under this verse, though it renders Ezekiel 16:3–13; the lemma shown is taken from this verse. Rashi has just said that Jonathan explained all of it.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Then washed I thee with water
Ezekiel.english_translation: [On “No eye pitied thee,” etc.] Aramaic: “The eye of wicked Pharaoh did not pity you, to do you one good thing, to give you rest from your servitude, to have compassion upon you; and he decreed upon you a final decree, to cast your males into the river, to destroy you at the time that you were in Egypt.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Aramaic passage is printed in the source under this verse, though it renders Ezekiel 16:3–13; the lemma shown is taken from this verse. Rashi has just said that Jonathan explained all of it.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Then washed I thee with water
Ezekiel.english_translation: [On “And when I passed by thee,” etc.] Aramaic: “And for the remembrance of the covenant of your fathers before Me I was revealed to redeem you, for it was known before Me that you were afflicted in your servitudes; and I said to you: By the blood of circumcision I will have pity on you; and I said to you: By the blood of the Passover I will redeem you.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Aramaic passage is printed in the source under this verse, though it renders Ezekiel 16:3–13; the lemma shown is taken from this verse. Rashi has just said that Jonathan explained all of it.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Then washed I thee with water
Ezekiel.english_translation: [On “I cause thee to increase, even as the growth of the field.”] Aramaic: “I multiplied you like the plants of the field, I gave you; and you increased and grew strong and became seeds and tribes; and through the deeds of your fathers the time of the redemption of your congregation was fixed, for you were enslaved and afflicted.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Aramaic passage is printed in the source under this verse, though it renders Ezekiel 16:3–13; the lemma shown is taken from this verse. Rashi has just said that Jonathan explained all of it. The Aramaic is translated literally as printed. The word תקניא is rendered by sense.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Then washed I thee with water
Ezekiel.english_translation: [On “I cause thee to increase.”] As it is said, “And the children of Israel were fruitful, and increased abundantly, and multiplied” (Exodus 1:7).
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Aramaic passage is printed in the source under this verse, though it renders Ezekiel 16:3–13; the lemma shown is taken from this verse. Rashi has just said that Jonathan explained all of it.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Then washed I thee with water
Ezekiel.english_translation: [On “naked and bare.”] Of the commandments.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Aramaic passage is printed in the source under this verse, though it renders Ezekiel 16:3–13; the lemma shown is taken from this verse. Rashi has just said that Jonathan explained all of it.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Then washed I thee with water
Ezekiel.english_translation: [On “Now when I passed by thee, and looked upon thee.”] Aramaic: “And I was revealed to Moses in the bush, and it was known before Me that the time of your redemption had arrived; and I sheltered you by My Word, and removed your sins, and swore by My Word to redeem you, as I swore to your fathers. Said the LORD God: That you may be a people ministering before Me.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Aramaic passage is printed in the source under this verse, though it renders Ezekiel 16:3–13; the lemma shown is taken from this verse. Rashi has just said that Jonathan explained all of it.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Then washed I thee with water
Ezekiel.english_translation: [On “I spread my skirt.”] The wing of a garment.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Aramaic passage is printed in the source under this verse, though it renders Ezekiel 16:3–13; the lemma shown is taken from this verse. Rashi has just said that Jonathan explained all of it.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Then washed I thee with water
Ezekiel.english_translation: [On “yea, I swore unto thee.”] “Wherefore say unto the children of Israel: I am the LORD, and I will bring you out” (Exodus 6), and *lakhen* is nothing but an oath, as it is said, “And therefore I have sworn unto the house of Eli” (1 Samuel 3).
Ezekiel.translator_note: The printed references “(there, 6)” and “1 Samuel 6” are Exodus 6:6 and 1 Samuel 3:14 (JPS wording quoted). The Aramaic passage is printed in the source under this verse, though it renders Ezekiel 16:3–13; the lemma shown is taken from this verse. Rashi has just said that Jonathan explained all of it.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Then washed I thee with water
Ezekiel.english_translation: [On “and entered into a covenant with thee.”] “Behold the blood of the covenant, which the LORD hath made with you” (Exodus 24).
Ezekiel.translator_note: JPS wording quoted (Exodus 24:8). The Aramaic passage is printed in the source under this verse, though it renders Ezekiel 16:3–13; the lemma shown is taken from this verse. Rashi has just said that Jonathan explained all of it.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Then washed I thee with water
Ezekiel.english_translation: [On “Then washed I thee with water.”] Aramaic: “And I redeemed you from Egyptian servitude, and removed the might of the *marvata* from you, and led you into freedom.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Aramaic passage is printed in the source under this verse, though it renders Ezekiel 16:3–13; the lemma shown is taken from this verse. Rashi has just said that Jonathan explained all of it. The Aramaic is translated literally as printed. The word מרוותא is left transliterated.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Aramaic: “And I clothed you in embroidered garments from the choice things of your enemies.”
*[Printed Old French: איקאלצייטוי"י טיישו"ן]* in Old French; and Aramaic: “and I put precious shoes on your feet.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: Old French printed איקאלצייטוי"י טיישו"ן; it appears to be *je te chaussai* (“I shod thee”) and *taisson* (“badger”), but was not found in Darmesteter.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: wound fine linen about thy head
Ezekiel.english_translation: *[Printed Old French: איפוציינישטוי]* in Old French; and Aramaic: “and I sanctified priests from among you to minister before Me, in turbans of fine linen.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: *[Printed Old French: שווייא"ה]* in Old French; and Aramaic: “and the High Priest in garments of colours.” And aggadic midrash: “and covered thee with silk” — these are the seven clouds of glory, as it is written, “the pillar of cloud by day … departed not from before the people” (Exodus 13).
Ezekiel.translator_note: Old French printed שווייא"ה; it appears to be *soie* (“silk”), but was not found in Darmesteter. JPS wording quoted (Exodus 13:22).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I decked thee also with ornaments
Ezekiel.english_translation: *[Printed Old French: איפאריטו"י]* in Old French; and Aramaic: “and I adorned you with the adornment of the words of the Torah, written on two tablets of stone.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: Old French printed איפאריטו"י; it appears to be *je te parai* (“I adorned thee”), but was not found in Darmesteter.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I put bracelets upon thy hands
Ezekiel.english_translation: By the hand of Moses.
Its companions: each utterance opposite its fellow, five opposite five.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The first word (חברתי') is read as “its companions.”

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I put a ring upon thy nose
Ezekiel.english_translation: Aramaic: “And I gave the Ark of My covenant among you.”
An expression of *nezem*; and Aramaic: “and a cloud of glory overshadowed you” — because they were surrounded in a circle.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: a beautiful crown upon thy head
Ezekiel.english_translation: Aramaic: “and an angel, a messenger from before Me, speaks at your head,” as it is said, “And their king is passed on before them, and the LORD at the head of them” (Micah 2:13).
Ezekiel.translator_note: JPS wording quoted.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Aramaic: “And I gave My Tabernacle among you, fashioned with gold and silver, and a curtain of fine linen and colours and embroideries; and manna that is good, like fine flour and like honey and like oil, I fed you; and you grew rich, and became exceedingly strong, and prospered, and ruled over all kingdoms.”

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: thou didst eat fine flour, and honey, and oil
Ezekiel.english_translation: The manna, which was changing to all tastes: to “thou didst eat fine flour, and honey, and oil.” And aggadic midrash: there are thirteen things here, and corresponding to them the Holy One, blessed be He, told them to bring the thirteen things counted in the offering for the Tabernacle; and nevertheless He repays them corresponding to these in the time to come with thirteen things: “And the LORD will create over the whole habitation of mount Zion …” “And there shall be a pavilion for a shadow in the day-time from the heat …” (Isaiah 4).
Ezekiel.translator_note: JPS wording quoted (Isaiah 4:5–6); Rashi’s Hebrew is abbreviated.

Ezekiel.english_translation: An expression of beauty.

An expression of completeness (*makhlol*). Another explanation: *ki kalil hu* — for it was whole. Another explanation: *kalil* — *[printed Old French: קרונ"א]* in Old French, like *nezer*, which we translate *kelila*.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Old French printed קרונ"א; it appears to be *corone* (“crown”), but was not found in Darmesteter.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: play the harlot because of thy renown
Ezekiel.english_translation: Thou didst trust in the name of the beauty that went forth for thee.
Thou didst show thy beauty to every passer-by, until the desire of thy harlotry was poured out upon them, to entice thee to commit harlotry with them.

And when they desired thee, thou didst abandon thyself to them; and to everyone who asked, thy harlotry was his. And Targum Jonathan: “and it was not fitting for you to do so,” as if it were written *lo yihyeh* [“it shall not be”]. And all this parable is about the calf in the wilderness and the other idolatries that the tribe of Dan served in the wilderness, as it is written, “all that were enfeebled in thy rear” (Deuteronomy 25); and we find in the Pesikta: this is the tribe of Dan, whom the cloud spewed out, for all of them were idolaters.
Ezekiel.translator_note: JPS wording quoted (Deuteronomy 25:18).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: high places decked with divers colours
Ezekiel.english_translation: Covered with garments embroidered with kinds of dyed colours — *[printed Old French: פלטריא"ש]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the like things shall not come
Ezekiel.english_translation: This was not fit to come — *[printed Old French: נו"ן אבני"ר אינו"ן אייטר"א]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The first two printed words (נו"ן אבני"ר) appear to be *non avenir* (“not to come”); the whole could not be confirmed in Darmesteter and is left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Because he likened her to a harlot woman, he likened the idols to the male who commits adultery with her.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: set it before them for a sweet savour
Ezekiel.english_translation: On the day they made the calf, the manna came down for them, and they gave some of it before the calf; and nevertheless “and thus it was” — to the next day, and it did not cease. And so it is also explained in the book of Ezra (Nehemiah 9): “Yea, when they had made them a molten calf …; yet Thou in Thy manifold mercies forsookest them not …, and withheldest not Thy manna from their mouth” — it was proper to withhold it from them, and Thou didst not withhold it. So also here, “and thus it was, saith the Lord GOD”: the bread was, and did not cease descending until the next day. So Rabbi Tanhuma expounded.
Ezekiel.translator_note: JPS wording quoted (Nehemiah 9:18–20); Rashi’s Hebrew is abbreviated. Printed “the book of Ezra” is the book of Nehemiah.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: whom thou hast borne unto Me
Ezekiel.english_translation: He had five sons: four of them to worship idols, and one set aside for the school; and when he came to offer one of his sons to Molech, he offered this one who had been set aside to study Torah — in the Midrash of Rabbi Tanhuma. And I say: “whom thou hast borne unto Me” — these are the firstborn; and so it says in this book (below, 20), “and I polluted them in their own gifts, in that they set apart all that openeth the womb.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: JPS wording quoted (Ezekiel 20:26).

Ezekiel.english_translation: My kindnesses that I did with thee in Egypt.
Aramaic: “Woe to you for that you have sinned, and woe to you for that you have not repented.”
A height in the manner of a platform (*bimos*) and an altar; and *tivni* is an expression of building.
Because he likened her to a harlot, he spoke in the language of intercourse, in which there is a spreading of the legs — *[printed Old French: איאקיישמ"ש]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Possessors of the organ of intercourse.
Thy sustenance in the days when the judges judged.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the will of them that hate thee
Ezekiel.english_translation: In the days of Samson.
Jonathan translated: “for if thou hadst sent prophets to them, they would have submitted” — and they would not go in the way of thy lewdness.
Since thou wast not satisfied with the abominations of Egypt.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: thou hast played the harlot with them
Ezekiel.english_translation: An expression of harlotry — *[printed Old French: אהאנשאר"ה אאל"ש]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: land of traffic, even with Chaldea
Ezekiel.english_translation: The Chaldeans are not of the land of Canaan, and this is its explanation: thou didst add the idols of the Chaldeans to those of the Canaanites that were near thee, and thou hadst already played the harlot with them. And Jonathan translated: “and thou didst multiply thy harlotries with the Chaldeans,” and they were likened to the Canaanites, steeped in idolatry; “and thou didst increase thy idols, to join the people of Canaan, to walk in the statutes of the Chaldeans.” But to me it appears that *Canaan* is like “merchant,” as in “Canaan, in his hand are balances of deceit” (Hosea 12), for he calls the land of the Chaldeans a land of merchants, as it is said (below, 17), “and carried it into a land of traffic; He set it in a city of merchants.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: The printed references are Hosea 12:8 (JPS renders it “As for the trafficker, the balances of deceit are in his hand”) and Ezekiel 17:4 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_translation: Corrupted; and so “the feeble Jews” (Nehemiah 3), and so “for I languish away” (Psalms 6).
Ezekiel.translator_note: JPS wording quoted (Nehemiah 3:34; Psalms 6:3).

Ezekiel.english_translation: Like *libbekh*.
Whose inclination rules over her.
Like *bivnotekh* — an expression of building.
To speak and to boast of the fair hire that is given her; and so every expression of *kelas* is an expression of speech — *parler* [printed פארלי"ץ] in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Old French printed פארלי"ץ; it appears to be *parler* (“to speak”), but was not found in Darmesteter.

Ezekiel.english_translation: It is an expression of wages — *[printed Old French: לויאי"ץ]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Old French printed לויאי"ץ; it appears to be *loiers* (“wages”), but was not found in Darmesteter.

Ezekiel.english_translation: The woman who commits adultery.
While she is under her husband, she sets her eyes on others.
Dowry (*mohar*).
From the abundance of harlotry that was in thee, thou didst so.
No harlot has been made a harlot like thy harlotry.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The printed sentence (לא נזנה לכל זונה כזנותך) is compressed and is rendered literally.

Ezekiel.english_translation: It is an expression of bottoms (*shulayim*), which they call *fonz* [printed פונ"ץ] in Old French; and so too in many places in the Order Tohorot: “the bottom (*neḥushto*) of the oven.” “Thy filthiness was poured out” — from the abundance of lust for harlotry thy source was flowing.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this form (פונץ) and glosses it “le fond d’un vase, d’un four” (“the bottom of a vessel, of an oven”).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: all the idols of thy abominations
Ezekiel.english_translation: And because of all the idols of thy abominations.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: for the blood of thy children
Ezekiel.english_translation: And for the sin of the blood of thy children I will do thee this evil, explained in the passage: “Behold, I will gather,” etc.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: unto whom thou hast been pleasant
Ezekiel.english_translation: *[Printed Old French: מאלא"ש]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the blood of fury and jealousy
Ezekiel.english_translation: And I will deliver thee to the slayers in fury and jealousy and anger.
The buildings of the heights of thy ordinances (*nimusekha*).
An expression of high places (*bamot*).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: thrust thee through with their swords
Ezekiel.english_translation: It has no likeness. And Targum Jonathan: “and they shall cleave thee” — *[printed Old French: איטרופ"ר נרונטו"י]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: From being any longer a harlot.
Like *hinneh*.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: hast thou not committed this lewdness
Ezekiel.english_translation: Although I have put thy way upon thy head, thou didst not devise a plan to set thy heart upon thy abominations, to return from them. Every *zimmah* in Scripture is an expression of counsel; sometimes for good and sometimes for evil.
An expression of proverb and riddle.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: As the mother, so her daughter
Ezekiel.english_translation: The *he* of *ke-immah* does not give *mappik*, because it serves nothing: it is only “as the mother, so the daughter.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: The grammatical remark is compressed and is rendered literally.

Ezekiel.english_translation: The nation of Canaan, whose land you inherited.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: that loatheth her husband and her children
Ezekiel.english_translation: Who multiplied their abominations until the land loathed and spewed out its inhabitants, fathers and sons together.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: thou art the sister of thy sisters
Ezekiel.english_translation: Sodom, which is adjacent to the Land of Israel.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: your mother was a Hittite, and your father an Amorite
Ezekiel.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “Was not your mother Sarah among the Hittites, and she did not act as their deeds? And your father Abraham among the Amorites, and he did not walk in their counsel?”

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: that dwelleth at thy left hand
Ezekiel.english_translation: Because the inheritance of Judah was in the southern border of the Land of Israel, all the other tribes were found on their left.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Yet hast thou not walked in their ways
Ezekiel.english_translation: Would that thou hadst walked in their ways, and not been more abominable than they! And so “If not, yet I pray thee let there be given to thy servant” (2 Kings 5), and so “And thou shalt not only while yet I live” of Jonathan (1 Samuel 11) — *[printed Old French: אפליי"אוט]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. JPS wording quoted (2 Kings 5:17; 1 Samuel 20:14, printed “1 Samuel 11”); JPS translates these verses differently from the sense Rashi gives them here.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Thy abominations would have been a trifle before Me, if thou hadst not been more abominable than they; but thou didst act more corruptly than they; and so Targum Jonathan. And there are interpreters who read “Yet hast thou not walked in their ways” as it sounds: a trifle were their abominations in thine eyes, and thou didst act more corruptly than they. *Kat* — *[printed Old French: פיקו"ט]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: She and her daughters, as is explained in Job: “As for the earth, out of it cometh bread,” and the whole passage, until they said: “Let the law of the foot be forgotten from our land,” for they come only to diminish.
Ezekiel.translator_note: JPS wording quoted for Job 28:5. The words “the law of the foot be forgotten from our land” (נשכח תורת רגל מארצינו) do not appear in Job as written; compare Job 28:4 (JPS: “They are forgotten of the foot that passeth by”). The source of Rashi’s wording was not confirmed.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I removed them when I saw it
Ezekiel.english_translation: Their way, as it is said regarding Sodom, “I will go down now, and see” (Genesis 18:21).

Before thou didst become more abominable than they, they were judged guilty; and since thou didst act more wickedly than they, thou didst make them appear righteous, and gavest them an opening of the mouth to say: There are some who have angered Thee more than I.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: in that thou hast given judgment for thy sisters
Ezekiel.english_translation: That thou didst judge them before thou becamest more wicked than they; thou didst say of them: They are worthy of punishment.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the captivity of Sodom and her daughters
Ezekiel.english_translation: I shall heal the land of brimstone and salt, and I shall settle inhabitants in it.
Like *betokhan*.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: in that thou art a comfort unto them
Ezekiel.english_translation: When thou didst become more wicked than they and gavest them an opening of the mouth. Another explanation: “in that thou comfortest them” — when the evil comes upon thee, they will be comforted, saying: Not we alone were punished.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: thy sister Sodom was not mentioned
Ezekiel.english_translation: As a question of astonishment.
To rebuke the many and say: Beware lest ye be overturned like Sodom — as though thou hadst a new report.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The last clause is rendered literally.

Ezekiel.english_translation: When thou wast in thy greatness.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: as at the time of the taunt of the daughters of Aram
Ezekiel.english_translation: As thou wast uncovered at the time I delivered thee into the hand of the kings of Aram, who came against Ahaz: “In those days the LORD began to send against Judah Rezin the king of Aram” (2 Kings 15), and in Chronicles (II 28): “Wherefore the LORD his God delivered him into the hand of the king of Aram,” and “The Philistines also had invaded the cities of the Lowland, and of the South of Judah.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: JPS wording quoted (2 Kings 15:37; 2 Chronicles 28:5, 18). Printed “II 11” is 2 Chronicles 28; Rashi’s Hebrew has “kings of Aram” where JPS has “king of Aram.”

Ezekiel.english_translation: An expression of contempt, and the *alef* is not read; and for “and he despised” they translate *ve-shat*.
Thou hast borne them; and it is a feminine form in several places in this book.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I will even deal with thee as thou hast done
Ezekiel.english_translation: I have done to thee evil according to thy deeds that thou hast done.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: who hast despised the oath in breaking the covenant
Ezekiel.english_translation: That which thou didst accept upon thyself at Horeb: “that thou shouldest enter into the covenant of the LORD thy God—and into His oath” (Deuteronomy 29); but I will not annul the covenant, so as to remember it, for I am not like thee.
Ezekiel.translator_note: JPS wording quoted (Deuteronomy 29:11).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: My covenant with thee in the days of thy youth
Ezekiel.english_translation: That was with thee in the days of thy youth.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Then shalt thou remember thy ways
Ezekiel.english_translation: When I do thee good, thy evil ways; and thou shalt be ashamed before Me that thou didst repay Me evil, and I repay thee good.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: when thou shalt receive thy sisters
Ezekiel.english_translation: When thou shalt conquer, to inherit the places round about thee, the small and the great.
As suburbs for thee, subjugated to thee, like Sodom and her daughters and *Kefarnaha*.
Ezekiel.translator_note: *Kefarnaha* (וכפרנהא) is left transliterated; the place is not identified.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: but not because of thy covenant
Ezekiel.english_translation: And not through thy keeping the covenant that I made with thee, but in My kindness and My mercy do I keep My covenant. And an aggadic midrash of Rabbi Tanhuma: “but not because of thy covenant” — not from thy *patrimonia* did I give it to Abraham thy father between the pieces; and this expression is close to the vernacular, for so they now call kinship *patrimonia* in Old French; and so they call everything that a man has from the inheritance of his fathers.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French word is printed פטרא"מוניא and appears to be *patrimoine*; it was not found in Darmesteter. The reference of “it” is not stated in the printed text, and the sentence is rendered literally.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Thy way, when I do thee good.
To lift up thy face to Me.
When I pardon thee: for what thou hast done thou shalt be ashamed, and thou shalt know that it is not out of thy good recompense that I have done thee good.
The prophecy in this passage is in the form of a riddle, for he likens Nebuchadnezzar to an eagle and the kings of Judah to the treetop of cedars.
Like *kanaf* — *ale* [printed אל"א] in Old French. Another explanation: as it sounds, an expression of actual limbs (*evarim*).
Ezekiel.translator_note: Old French printed אל"א; it appears to be *ale* (“wing”), but was not found in Darmesteter.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Its plumage is beautiful and variegated.
All the foliage of the tree — *cime* [printed צימא] in Old French. It is a parable: he exiled Jehoiakim and his mighty men.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this form (צימא) and glosses it “cime” (“top”). Printed “Jehoiakim” is translated as printed; the exile in the verse is that of Jehoiachin (2 Kings 24:12).

Ezekiel.english_translation: He humbled his greatness and his kingship; *yenikotav* is like his branches.
To a land of merchants — it is Babylon.
Zedekiah, his son.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Translated as printed; 2 Kings 24:17 says Zedekiah was Jehoiachin’s father’s brother.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: planted it in a fruitful soil
Ezekiel.english_translation: In Jerusalem, a royal city.
Rooted by many waters — that is, he gave him greatness and dominion over those round about him.
A kind of willow tree whose branches are many — *[printed Old French: שאלק"א]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Like “the overhanging part” (Exodus 26:12) — large.
Ezekiel.translator_note: JPS wording quoted.

Ezekiel.english_translation: To serve the king of Babylon.
Its branches (*zemorotav*).
To the king of Babylon.
Under the king of Babylon.
Poles (*motot*).
And it grew.
Many branches.
The king of Egypt.

An expression of hunger, as in “At destruction and famine thou shalt laugh” (Job 5): the roots of this vine hungered and longed for that eagle. Addition: And some understand *kafnah* as *asfah* [“gathered”], and it is reversed; and in the words of our Rabbis there is something similar to it, for they call the gathering of the people *kenufya*; and *kafna* is like *kanfa*; *amasser* [printed אמאש"א] in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The word “Addition” (תוספות) marks a later gloss in the printed text. Old French printed אמאש"א; it appears to be *amasser* (“to gather”), but was not found in Darmesteter. JPS wording quoted (Job 5:22).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: shot forth its branches toward him
Ezekiel.english_translation: And it sent its messengers to him, to come to it and water it.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: from the beds of its plantation
Ezekiel.english_translation: From the *ha’ugiyot* of water that the first eagle had made for it.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The word מהעוגיות is left transliterated; its sense could not be confirmed.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: It was planted in a good soil
Ezekiel.english_translation: That is, it did this for nothing, for it was planted in a good field.
A strong vine.
The whole alphabet is in this verse; and I wonder, for *arno* is counted in the Masorah.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The final clause is compressed and is rendered literally.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Shall he not pull up the roots thereof
Ezekiel.english_translation: The first eagle.
Like *yekutsats* [“cut off”]; these are the sons of Zedekiah, whom he slaughtered before his eyes.
Leaves — *foillie* [printed פוייליי"א] in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Old French printed פוייליי"א; it appears to be *foillie* (“foliage”), but was not found in Darmesteter.

Ezekiel.english_translation: The second eagle shall come to its help.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: plucked up by the roots thereof
Ezekiel.english_translation: Opposite those who uproot it and remove it from its roots.
Now planted according to its will.
Is it possible that this one will prosper, which betrayed the one who first planted it?
What is this riddle? and explain it to them.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: took the king thereof, and the princes thereof
Ezekiel.english_translation: They are the top of the cedar: Jehoiakim and his princes.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “Jehoiakim” is translated as printed; the exile in the verse is that of Jehoiachin (2 Kings 24:12).

Ezekiel.english_translation: It is the city of the merchants.
Zedekiah.
The princes of the land.
In order that it might endure.
When Nebuchadnezzar comes and casts up a mound against Jerusalem.
To slay the people of the city.
He promised in good faith, and lifted his hand in the covenant.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: bring it upon his own head
Ezekiel.english_translation: It is the putting out of his eyes.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I will spread My net upon him
Ezekiel.english_translation: As I explained above, at the beginning of the book (above, 12), that He summoned a deer to run along the roof of the cave.
And I will argue with him.
As its Targum: *vet kol gibborohi* [“and all his mighty men”]; and Menahem connected it with “Make haste, my beloved” (end of Song of Songs); and this is its meaning: and all the fugitives.
Ezekiel.translator_note: JPS wording quoted (Song of Songs 8:14).

Ezekiel.english_translation: In all their wings — that is, in all their strength, by the sword shall they fall.
*[Printed Old French: שרונאפנדו"ן]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Old French printed שרונאפנדו"ן; it appears to be *seront espandus* (“will be scattered”), but was not found in Darmesteter.

Ezekiel.english_translation: As its Targum: *ve-akeymineh* [“and I will establish it”]. “Moreover I will take, even I” — the King Messiah.
It is the way to graft only from the tender shoot that grew last year, which they call *graife* [printed גרייפי"א] in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this form (גרפייא, with variants) and glosses it “greffe” (“graft”).

Ezekiel.english_translation: An expression of *tel* [mound], for it is the way of a mound to be high and steep — *amoncelée* [printed אומנצלי"ה] in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this form (אמונצליץ, with variants) and glosses it “amoncelée” (“heaped up”).

Ezekiel.english_translation: The dagesh of the *nun* serves in place of a second *nun*, as if it were written *tishkonenah*.
The Chaldeans, who ruled over Israel.
Zedekiah and his seed.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: made the dry tree to flourish
Ezekiel.english_translation: Jehoiachin, who was exiled without sons, will beget in Babylon Zerubbabel, and he will be governor of Judah.
Ezekiel.translator_note: JPS “governor of Judah” (Haggai 1:1).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: What mean you, that you use this proverb
Ezekiel.english_translation: *[Printed Old French: אשנפלאנ"ץ]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Old French printed אשנפלאנ"ץ; it appears to be *essamples* (“examples”), but was not found in Darmesteter.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Fruit before it has ripened — *verjus* [printed ביירגו"ץ] in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Old French printed ביירגו"ץ; it appears to be *verjus* (“sour juice of unripe grapes”), but was not found in Darmesteter.

Ezekiel.english_translation: *[Printed Old French: אגאצירונ"ט]* in Old French. Thus is the way of the Holy One, blessed be He: the fathers sin and the sons are punished — for how many years did the kings of Israel sin before they were exiled; and we too need not worry about being punished for our iniquities.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form appears to be *agacieront* (“will be set on edge”) but was not found in Darmesteter. The last clause is rendered literally.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Like *limshol*.
And why should the son who has not sinned against Me be punished? Is he not Mine?
Aramaic: “On the mountains he did not serve the idol, to eat the sacrifices of the dead.”

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the idols of the house of Israel
Ezekiel.english_translation: Other idolatry, such as the Baal in Samaria and the calves in Bethel and in Dan.
(*Yonah*: an expression of wronging; that is, he wronged no man.)
Ezekiel.translator_note: The parentheses are in the printed text.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: restored his pledge for a debt
Ezekiel.english_translation: If he took in pledge his fellow’s garment for his debt, he returns it to him at sunset.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: to a brother any of these things
Ezekiel.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “and does to his brother one of these.”

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: whereas he himself had not done any of these things
Ezekiel.english_translation: All these good things that his father did.
Lying with a male.
He saw in his heart that it is not good to do so — *aperçoit* [printed איאפרצוי"ט] in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Old French printed איאפרצוי"ט; it appears to be *aperçoit* (“perceives”), but was not found in Darmesteter.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: withdrawn his hand from the poor
Ezekiel.english_translation: From doing him evil.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: None of his righteous deeds that he hath done shall be remembered
Ezekiel.english_translation: Our Rabbis explained [it] of one who regrets them.
Like *lo yitaken* [“shall not be set right”] — *[printed Old French: אפייאט"ש]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Return yourselves, and turn others back — *retourner* [printed רטורני"ר] in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Old French printed רטורני"ר; it appears to be *retourner* (“to return, to turn back”), but was not found in Darmesteter.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: How was thy mother a lioness
Ezekiel.english_translation: How esteemed was thy mother — thou, Zedekiah — who was likened to a lioness!
Ezekiel.translator_note: The grammar of the printed sentence is compressed; rendered literally. The next comment says the lament concerns the sons of Josiah.

Ezekiel.english_translation: The princes of Judah.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: she brought up one of her whelps
Ezekiel.english_translation: This lament was said about the sons of Josiah, of whom the first is Jehoahaz.

He plunders Israel, for Israel are called *adam*, as it is said (below, 34), “And you My sheep, the sheep of My pasture, are men”; and according to the parable, any beast that has tasted the taste of human flesh constantly attacks people.
Ezekiel.translator_note: JPS wording quoted (Ezekiel 34:31).

Ezekiel.english_translation: Pharaoh, king of Egypt.
*Shaḥatam* means pits; they dig them and cover their mouths with straw, and the beast falls into it.
Something like iron rings: they pierce his nose and pull him by them.
Her mother — the Community of Israel.
An expression of sickness.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: she took another of her whelps
Ezekiel.english_translation: Jehoiakim.
He made him king. Every *kefir* in Scripture is a choice and mighty lion.

He afflicts the women and kills their husbands. Some explain *almanotav* as *armenotav* (“his palaces”), and *vayeda* as an expression of crushing and destroying, as in “And the haughty He knoweth from afar” (Psalms 138:6).
He imposed a tax on the land, to give to Pharaoh every year, as it is said (2 Kings 23:35).
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “2 Kings 23:35” is given as in the source.

Ezekiel.english_translation: And HaShem sent against him the bands of Aram, the bands of the Chaldeans, the bands of Moab, and the bands of the children of Ammon (2 Kings 24:2).
Ezekiel.translator_note: Rashi’s wording and order differ from the verse in 2 Kings 24:2; translated as printed.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the nations cried out against him
Ezekiel.english_translation: And they gathered.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Rashi gives only this Aramaic word; it is translated here.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: *bekolarin*.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Rashi gives only the Aramaic word of the Targum; it is transliterated, not translated.

Ezekiel.english_translation: That he be shut up there.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Thy mother was like a vine
Ezekiel.english_translation: Further, this is from the lamentation.
*Bedamkha* is an expression of likeness and parable; that is, you are like one whose mother was a vine planted by water.
Like *poreh rosh*; an expression of bearing fruit.
By means of many waters.
Mighty rulers and strong kings.
Trees whose branches are many.
Every plucking up and planting is a thing cast scattered over the face of the whole earth.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Translated literally; the sense of the sentence is not clear.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Nebuchadnezzar.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed as the abbreviation נ"נ, read as Nebuchadnezzar.

Ezekiel.english_translation: He slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: fire is gone out of the rod of her branches
Ezekiel.english_translation: Because of the iniquity of her kings and her princes the evil came upon her.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: To be a sceptre to rule
Ezekiel.english_translation: *Eliya* is this prophecy, and it shall be for *eliya*. [“It is a lamentation, and it was for a lamentation.”]
Ezekiel.translator_note: Rashi’s lemma, “It is a lamentation, and it was for a lamentation,” is the last clause of the Hebrew of 19:14, which JPS prints at the start of 20:1; the lemma shown is the nearest wording in this verse. The Aramaic word *eliya* is transliterated as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Concerning their needs: and if He does not hear us, we too will not be punished for the sins in our hands, for we have already been sold, and He has nothing against us. A slave whom his master sold, and a woman whom her husband divorced — does the one have anything at all against the other? And from the end of the matter you learn, from the answer with which He answered them: “And that which cometh into your mind shall not be at all” etc. (below, 32).
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “below, 32” is Ezekiel 20:32 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I will not be inquired of by you
Ezekiel.english_translation: At your request. And at the end of this book He said, “I will be inquired of by the house of Israel.” This is one of the places that teach us that the Holy One, blessed be He, relents from the evil; and concerning the like of this, that one said, “Will He not do it?” (Numbers 23:19). Midrash Tanchuma.
Ezekiel.translator_note: “At the end of this book” is Ezekiel 36:37, which Rashi does not name. “That one” is translated as printed; the verse in Numbers 23:19 reads: “When He hath said, will He not do it?”

Ezekiel.english_translation: An expression of contention.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: In the day when I chose Israel
Ezekiel.english_translation: Behold, this hatred was kept suppressed before HaMakom for nearly nine hundred years, from when they were in Egypt until Ezekiel, and His love was covering over them; and because they now increased transgression, it was aroused. Concerning this it is said, “Hatred stirreth up strifes” etc. (Proverbs 10:12).

Aaron prophesied this prophecy to them before the Holy One, blessed be He, revealed Himself to Moses at the bush; and this is what is said (1 Samuel 2:27) to Eli: “Did I reveal Myself unto the house of thy father, when they were in Egypt” etc.

These are the wicked, the majority of Israel, who died in the three days of darkness, as it is said, “and *ḥamushim* went up, the children of Israel” etc. (Exodus 14) — one in fifty; and some say one in five hundred.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Rashi’s word order differs from the verse (“and the children of Israel went up armed,” Exodus 13:18); printed “Exodus 14” is Exodus 13:18. Rashi connects *ḥamushim* with the number five (*ḥamishah*).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: that it should not be profaned
Ezekiel.english_translation: That My name should not be profaned, since I had made Myself known to them and had promised to bring them out, and the Egyptians recognized that they are My people. Had I been destroying them, their enemies would say: Because there was no ability in His hand to bring them out.
It is a great sign for them that I gave them My day of rest for a rest; behold, it is a great mark that I sanctified them to Me.
They tested Me with the calf and at Rephidim, from accepting the Torah, and they left over of the manna.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Translated literally; “from accepting the Torah” is as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: They went out from among the people to gather manna.
The tribe of Dan; and likewise “those that have joined themselves unto the Baal of Peor” (Numbers 25:5), after the generation of the wilderness had died.
From then I promised to scatter them: “When thou shalt beget children, and children’s children” etc. (Deuteronomy 4:25).

He delivered them into the hand of their inclination, to stumble in their sin. And so Targum Jonathan: “And I delivered them into the hand of their foolish inclination, and they went and made decrees that were not proper, and laws by which they would not endure.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Aramaic of Targum Jonathan is translated as printed.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: polluted them in their own gifts
Ezekiel.english_translation: Those gifts that I decreed for them, to sanctify to Me every firstborn — I delivered them into the hand of their inclination, to pass those firstborn to Molech. Behold, statutes that are not good.
Ezekiel.translator_note: “Decreed” renders *shehakakti* (literally, “engraved”).

Ezekiel.english_translation: *Ashimem* — I will lay them waste and destroy them. *Ashmem* is an expression of desolation (*shemamah*); and the one who explains it as an expression of guilt (*ashmah*) is mistaken, for the *alef* is not among the root letters of the word.
When I bring the evil upon them.
They added to do so when I brought them into the land.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: So the name thereof is called Bamah
Ezekiel.english_translation: An expression of disparagement; that is to say, “Of what account (*bamah*) is it considered?”

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: after the manner of your fathers
Ezekiel.english_translation: An expression of astonishment: Is it fitting that you defile yourselves in the way of your fathers, and that I be inquired of by you, to answer your question?
And in the taking of your gifts, which you should have given to Me, and you take them from Me, to pass your firstborn to idolatry.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: that which cometh into your mind
Ezekiel.english_translation: That which comes up in your mind.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: We will be as the nations
Ezekiel.english_translation: We will cast off His yoke from upon our necks, since He has sent [us] away from Himself.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The word “us” is supplied in brackets.

Ezekiel.english_translation: For you already took it upon yourselves of your own will in the days of Joshua, as it is said (Joshua 24:1), “And Joshua gathered all the tribes of Israel” and the whole matter.
It is the wilderness in which they went forty years; and so he prophesied (Hosea 2), “and bring her into the wilderness.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “Hosea 2” is Hosea 2:16 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_translation: That you will be subject to Me and to My discipline.
In the covenant that I delivered to you.
An expression of selecting (*berirah*).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: out of the land where they sojourn
Ezekiel.english_translation: From the land of their exile I will bring them out, and I will cause them to die in the wilderness.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Go you, serve every one his idols
Ezekiel.english_translation: And do not show the nations that you are called by My name, when you come to the prophet to ask Torah of him; and since he tells you My words and you do not hearken to Me — as in the matter that is said (below, 33), “And, lo, thou art unto them as a love song” etc. — they hear your words and do not do them.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “below, 33” is Ezekiel 33:32. Rashi’s closing words (“they hear your words and do not do them”) differ slightly from the JPS wording of 33:32.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: with your gifts, and with your idols
Ezekiel.english_translation: For you set aside the firstborn under the name of firstborn, as I commanded you, and once My name is called upon the thing, you offer them to idolatry.
Like *she’erotekhem*, an expression of food, as in “her food, her raiment, and her conjugal rights, shall he not diminish” (Exodus 21); and so Menahem classed it.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “Exodus 21” is Exodus 21:10 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_translation: *Ve-nekotutem* — an expression of strife (*ketatah*). Another explanation: as its Targum, *vetidnekon*; and so Jonathan translated “the sighing”: *demonir* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this Old French form (*demonir*, printed דמוני"ר) and glosses it as an expression of sad reflection (see Ezekiel 6:9). The Aramaic word is transliterated as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: The land of Israel, which is to the south of Babylon.
Toward My Temple, which is destined to be like a forest and a field, to be plowed, with foxes walking in it.
An expression of the burning (*tzarevet*) of a boil (Leviticus 13); “and upon his lips as a burning fire” (Proverbs 16) — an expression of burning.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “Leviticus 13” is 13:23 and “Proverbs 16” is 16:27. In Proverbs 16:27 JPS reads: “in his lips there is as a burning fire.”

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: from the south to the north
Ezekiel.english_translation: All the men who are in the south of Babylon, which is in the north. An expression of *tzarav* — *retraire* in Old French [printed רטרי"יר].
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this verse (Ezekiel 21:3) with a similar form (variant spellings, e.g. רטריירא) and glosses it “racorniront” (“they will shrivel”). The printed spelling differs from his.

Ezekiel.english_translation: When I prophesy to them in the language of a parable and riddle, such as the forest and a fire that devours the moist and the dry.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the word of the LORD came unto me
Ezekiel.english_translation: Prophesy to them an explicit prophecy: what I said to you, “set thy face toward the South,” I explain to you: “set thy face toward Jerusalem.”
And prophesy; and so, “Preach you not” (Micah 2), and “and preach not against the house of Isaac” (Amos 7).
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “Micah 2” is Micah 2:6 and “Amos 7” is Amos 7:16 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_translation: It is the “forest of the field.”
Two destructions.
It is the green and the dry.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Seeing then that I will cut off from thee the righteous and the wicked
Ezekiel.english_translation: And I knew that the idolaters would rejoice at your misfortune; I will be angry with them and stir up Nebuchadnezzar against all of them; and that is what I wrote: “and all the southern faces shall be seared in it.”

Two swords: first the sword of the king of Babylon, and afterward the sword of the children of Ammon by the hand of Ishmael son of Nethaniah, who would kill Gedaliah and those gathered to him from the remnant of the sword, as is explained in Jeremiah (41:11–12).
Ezekiel.translator_note: The printed reference is Jeremiah 41:11–12; the killing of Gedaliah by Ishmael son of Nethaniah is narrated in Jeremiah 41:1–3.

Ezekiel.english_translation: *Forbie* in Old French [printed פורביא"ה]. Menahem classed it as an expression of drawing out; and so, “And he gave it to be furbished,” and so all of them.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this form (פורבידא and variants) and glosses it “fourbie” (“furbished”).

Ezekiel.english_translation: So that it may have a flash (*zehorit*) — *flandours* in Old French [printed פלנדור"ש].
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this form (פלנדורש, *flandours*) at this verse and glosses it “l’éclair” (“lightning, flash”).

Ezekiel.english_translation: An expression of astonishment: Is it perhaps that we still have cause to rejoice?

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the rod of My son, contemning every tree
Ezekiel.english_translation: The rod with which I strike My son to chasten him is harder than all rods, and it despises the blow of every staff and every tree, for they are as nothing beside it.
The rod.
To polish it, so that it may be easy and fitting for the one who grasps it by the hand.
It is the rod — a sharpened sword; and it is furbished, to give it into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar to kill with it.
An expression of wailing.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: for it is upon My people
Ezekiel.english_translation: The sword will be upon My people and upon all their princes and their officers.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: they are thrust down to the sword
Ezekiel.english_translation: Gatherings of peoples, coming to the sword, were round about My people. So Targum Jonathan. *Megurei* is an expression of storing — “A wise son gathereth in summer” (Proverbs 10:5); “gathereth her food in the harvest” (Proverbs 6:8); “The barns are broken down” (Joel 1:17); “is the seed yet in the barn?” (Haggai 2:19). And Menahem connected it with fear, as in “And Moab was sore afraid” (Numbers 22).
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “Numbers 22” is Numbers 22:3 (JPS wording quoted). Joel 1:17 is quoted in JPS wording.

Ezekiel.english_translation: For mourning and lamentation.
“A trial” in many troubles: many other calamities were tried upon them — judgment, pestilence, famine and wild beast.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: what if it contemn even the rod
Ezekiel.english_translation: And what will become of My son, if even this rod that despises comes upon him together with the other trials?

My son will be no more in the world; and so Targum Jonathan: “they shall not endure.” But he did not translate the rest of the verse this way, and so it appears in my eyes. And I have heard many interpretations of it, and I have seen it in books of interpretations, and they did not settle in my mind. And the liturgical poet who composed [a poem] for Hanukkah (on the first Sabbath, in the *yotzer*) — *hamo’eset kol etz hadakir hamazneh* — supports me, for he called the sword “despising every tree.” And Jonathan so translated “Or shall we make mirth?” etc.: “Because the tribes of the house of Judah and Benjamin rejoiced over the tribes of Israel when they went into exile, because they served error, and they themselves turned to err after images of wood.” He too explains *o nasish* as an expression of astonishment.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The words *hadakir hamazneh* from the liturgical poem are transliterated; their sense is not clear to the translator. The Aramaic of Targum Jonathan is translated as printed. Audit 4: the Aramaic quotation was checked against Targum Jonathan/the Ketuvim Targum (Mikraot Gedolot, Sefaria) at EZK 21:15 and reads as quoted; the meaning of the unclear word, if noted above, is still unresolved.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: For there is a trial; and what if it contemn even the rod?
Ezekiel.english_translation: For prophets prophesied to them, and they did not return; that is to say, the matter is already outside [i.e., settled] that they will not return — and what will be at their end?
Ezekiel.translator_note: “The matter is already outside” is an idiom translated literally; its sense is not certain. The Aramaic is translated as printed.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: what if it contemn even the rod
Ezekiel.english_translation: He said: Even the tribes of the house of Judah and Benjamin shall surely go into exile, and in their evil deeds they will not endure. The kingdom of the tribe [Judah] that despised its fellow, and mocked them and the evil that came upon them — it too will not be and will not stand. Further, I will explain it in another way — “Or shall we make mirth?” etc.: perhaps I should rejoice when you say to Me, “the rod of My son, contemning every tree”; the kings of Judah are despisers of idolatry, as we find with Abijah, who said, “and there are with you the golden calves” (2 Chronicles 13:8), and Asa and Jehoshaphat and Hezekiah and Josiah, who removed all the idolatry in the world that was under their hand; and these too will return in repentance.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed reference is 2 Chronicles 13:8 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_translation: And do not rejoice over this, for it will be upon My people. And why? “For there is a trial” — the matter was already tested before Me, that they will not repent properly. “And what if it contemn even the rod? It shall be no more.” And what shall I wait for further? Even if they came to return and to despise idolatry, the matter would not endure in their hands, for they would hasten to return to their wickedness; and that is what He said to Jeremiah, “If he returns, he shall not return.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: Rashi’s lemma, “Cry and wail” (21:17), heads this comment; the lemma shown is from this verse. Rashi does not name the verse in Jeremiah; the quotation is translated as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: In the manner of mourners. And what is the prophecy?

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: let the sword be doubled the third time
Ezekiel.english_translation: I said, “A sword, a sword” — the sword of Nebuchadnezzar to destroy Jerusalem, and the sword of the children of Ammon against Gedaliah. There is yet a third sword, doubled, for both of these will be a sword of the slain; and it is the sword of the great slain one, which causes many slain to fall.

Wherever you go out, it will pursue you into the innermost chambers. Behold, Johanan son of Kareah and the captains of the forces will go to Egypt; there the sword will overtake them. And so in all the places to which they flee, into fortified cities, as is said in the matter, “I have set the point of the sword against all their gates.”
An expression of movement; another interpretation: an expression of something melting.
And the stumblings multiplied. And so every *harbeh* in Scripture is an expression of *harbot* [multiplying], in the passive form (*pa’ul*).

Some explain *avḥat* as *tivḥat* [slaughter], a *ṭet* in place of the *alef*, by [the substitution of] *alef–ṭet, bet–ḥet*; and some explain it like *av’at* [from] *be’atah* [terror], but this cannot be, for the *tav* in *avḥat* is not a root letter and comes only for the construct state, whereas the *tav* in *be’atah* is part of the root. And I say: *avḥat ḥerev* is the sounding of the voice of those slain by the sword, an expression of barking (*nevichah*) — *glapisement* in Old French [printed גלאפ"י שמינ"ט] — for the *nun* of *nevichah* is a root letter that falls away, like the *nun* in *neshichah*, and an *alef* comes in its place, as in “and my declaration (*ve-aḥavati*) in your ears” (Job 13:17), “save a pot of oil (*asuch*)” (2 Kings 14). And Menahem explained it like *eimat ḥerev* [terror of the sword]; there is no comparison for it, but his explanation fits the context.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this verse (Ezekiel 21:20) and glosses the Old French as “cri des blessés” (“cry of the wounded”), form *glapisemant*. Printed “2 Kings 14” is 2 Kings 4:2 (JPS wording: “save a pot of oil”). Job 13:17 is quoted in JPS wording. The Hebrew grammatical forms are transliterated as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Woe and alas, for it is made for flashing — furbished and polished.

And wrapped in a garment, until it is grasped in the hand for slaughter on the day of battle.
