And some explain *me’uteh* as an expression of diminishing (*mi’ut*), because it diminishes when it is sharpened — and they err, for the lack of the *vav* and the *dagesh* of the *ṭet* shows that the *mem* is not a root letter in the word, like the *mem* of *me’onah*, *meshunah* and *me’utah*, and “overlaid with sapphires” (Song of Songs 5). And Menahem connected *me’uteh* with an expression of thought, as in “returned answer with counsel and discretion” (Daniel 2:14). But Dunash explained it like *oteh or* — “Who coverest Thyself with light as with a garment” (Psalms 104:2).
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “Song of Songs 5” is 5:14. The Hebrew grammatical forms are transliterated as printed.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Go thee one way to the right
Ezekiel.english_translation: To one place — either to the right or to the left.
Rashi’s lemma is *mo’adot*: Prepared.
Ezekiel.translator_note: JPS renders the Hebrew phrase containing *mo’adot* as “whither is thy face set.”

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I will also smite My hands together
Ezekiel.english_translation: I say to you, “Smite hand upon hand,” and I too, like you, lament over them, and I will smite My hands together; but My wrath burns in Me, and I will lay it to rest.
As the verse concludes.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: mark it clear at the head of the way to the city
Ezekiel.english_translation: Clear for yourself a place at the head of the road on which you are; make for yourself a kind of forked road, at a parting of the ways: one turns to the right and one turns to the left.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: they twain shall come forth out of one land
Ezekiel.english_translation: The two roads.

A place cleared of thorns and brambles — *essarter* in Old French [printed אישרטי"ר] — and its like in the Book of Joshua (17): “get thee up to the forest, and cut down (*uvarata*) for thyself there”; and further, “for though it is a forest, thou shalt cut it down” (*uvarata*) (ibid.). And Menahem connected all of them with an expression of selection (*berirah*), as in “choose (*bru*) you a man for you” (1 Samuel 17:8) — *[printed Old French: לישנ"ט]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists the first Old French form (אישרטיר, *essarter*) at this verse and glosses it “débarrasse-le des broussailles qui l’encombrent” (“clear it of the brambles that encumber it”). The Old French form at the end could not be confirmed in Darmesteter. Printed “Joshua 17” is 17:15 and “ibid.” is 17:18 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_translation: A sign: these two roads are for the king of Babylon, who goes out from his land in order to go either to Jerusalem or to Rabbah of the children of Ammon — to whichever of the two the lot falls for him by his divinations — as explained [in] “For the king of Babylon stood” etc.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: at the parting of the way
Ezekiel.english_translation: *Carrefour* in Old French [printed קארפו"ר].
Ezekiel.translator_note: Old French printed קארפו"ר; it appears to be *carrefour* (“crossroads”), but was not found in Darmesteter.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: he shaketh the arrows to and fro
Ezekiel.english_translation: He made the arrows blaze with the heat of arrows: he threw an arrow upward, and it turns of itself to the right or to the left, and to the place where it turns — that is the lot.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The first phrase is translated literally; its sense is not certain.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: he shaketh the arrows to and fro
Ezekiel.english_translation: Menahem connected it with “burnished brass” (above, 1) and with “and one do not whet the edge” (Ecclesiastes 10); and there is one who understands *kilkel* as an expression of spoiling, as in “and all the hills (*hitkalkelu*)” (Jeremiah 4). And some of those who speak the vernacular render *kilkel* [printed Old French: טראאי"ט] in Old French. And so Targum Jonathan: “he shook the bow with arrows, *bagirraya*.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. The Aramaic word is transliterated as printed. Printed “above, 1” is Ezekiel 1:7; “Ecclesiastes 10” is 10:10 (JPS wording quoted); “Jeremiah 4” is 4:24, where JPS renders the verb “moved to and fro,” whereas Rashi takes it as spoiling.

Ezekiel.english_translation: An image that speaks through sorceries; and there is an hour that is fixed, such that if one makes it at that hour, it has speech forever.
There are experts who divine by the liver.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: In his right hand is the lot Jerusalem
Ezekiel.english_translation: All his lots divined for him to come to Jerusalem.
Appointed rulers, heads of troops.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Rashi reads *karim* as appointed commanders, not as “battering rams” (JPS).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: to set battering rams against the gates
Ezekiel.english_translation: You and your troop, sit at such-and-such a gate.
They pour out earth and build a ramp, piling up a high mound and pressing it down, as they press down the mounds of the towers, to stand upon it and fight against the people of the city.
For Israel — what Nebuchadnezzar did.
And they will not believe that he will succeed. But in truth, “weeks upon weeks” are theirs: forty-nine times Nebuchadnezzar divined for them, and all the divinations were directed alike.

Nebuchadnezzar, in his divining of his divinations, would mention the iniquities that were in Israel’s hands, which Ammon and Moab, their neighbors, who heard the rebukes of the prophets, would make known to him.
That Israel should be seized in his hand.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Because you have made your iniquity to be remembered
Ezekiel.english_translation: For you renew transgressions from day to day, and your earlier iniquities are recalled through them.
The new ones.
The old ones.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: because that you are come to remembrance
Ezekiel.english_translation: Before Me, for evil; therefore —

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: you shall be taken with the hand
Ezekiel.english_translation: You shall be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: O wicked one, that art to be slain
Ezekiel.english_translation: Condemned to be slain in your wickedness.
Zedekiah.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: in the time of the iniquity of the end
Ezekiel.english_translation: At the time when the measure was filled and the last iniquity that fills the measure had arrived.
As its Targum: “Remove the turban from Seraiah the high priest, and annul the crown from Zedekiah the king; He said: this and that shall not endure in its place.”

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: that which is low shall be exalted
Ezekiel.english_translation: Gedaliah son of Ahikam — [the kingship] which was not his, they will take it; and Zedekiah’s, which was his, will be removed from him.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Aramaic is brief; the bracketed words are supplied, and the sense is not certain.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: A ruin, a ruin, a ruin
Ezekiel.english_translation: An expression of “heaps of the field”; an expression of ruin after ruin — twice and three times will I make it. It was already taken from Jeconiah and given to Zedekiah, and from Zedekiah it will be given to Gedaliah. Behold, two. And Menahem connected *avvah* with *avvatah*, as in “Vashti the queen hath not done wrong” (Esther 1) and “we have done iniquitously” (Psalms 106).
Ezekiel.translator_note: The abbreviated word (שתי') is read as “two.” Printed “Esther 1” is 1:16; “Psalms 106” is 106:6 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: this also shall be no more
Ezekiel.english_translation: Even for Gedaliah it will not endure, until Ishmael son of Nethaniah comes.
Upon whom I have set the exacting of My vengeance and My judgment.
Into his hand.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: concerning the children of Ammon, and concerning their taunt
Ezekiel.english_translation: Who rejoiced when the lot of Nebuchadnezzar fell, in his divinations, to come against Jerusalem, and reproached Me and My people, saying: “The hand of their idolatry is exalted.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: The final phrase (*yad akum shelahem ramah*) is translated literally; its sense is not certain.

Ezekiel.english_translation: To contain many slain, for the sake of its flash — so that the sight of its blaze not be darkened by the slain.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: While they see falsehood unto thee
Ezekiel.english_translation: The diviners of Ammon saw falsehood for them, saying: It will not come upon us again.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: To lay thee upon the necks of the wicked that are to be slain
Ezekiel.english_translation: To lead you astray, and to place your neck like the necks of the slain wicked of Israel.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Rashi’s wording (“like the necks”) differs slightly from the verse.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Their day.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Cause it to return into its sheath
Ezekiel.english_translation: Like *hashev*, for the *shin* is soft (*rafeh*): Wait for me until the sword that is upon Israel returns — do not [put it] into its sheath; and afterward, when it finishes its vengeance upon Israel, it will return upon you: “In the place where thou wast created” etc.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The grammatical reasoning is translated literally; the sense of *hashev* here is as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: An expression of the blowing of fire with a bellows.
They conduct themselves in madness, to ruin and to destroy.

Craftsmen of killing [Aramaic]. (For many days I have interpreted this passage as written above; now I see, from the variation of its expressions, that the prophet is speaking only of the sword.) “To lay thee upon the necks of the wicked that are to be slain” etc., “Cause it to return into its sheath” etc., “I will blow upon thee” etc. — this expression applies only to metal, and so “skilful to destroy.” And it seems in my eyes that this prophecy was spoken about Nebuchadnezzar, and so it implies: “Prophesy, and say: Thus saith the Lord GOD concerning the children of Ammon, and concerning their taunt” — that is, (that I reproached / that they were reproaching) concerning Nebuchadnezzar (for the sake of Nebuchadnezzar), that the children of Ammon taunt Israel because Nebuchadnezzar destroyed them.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The printed text contains two parenthetical variant readings (“that I reproached / that they were reproaching” and “for the sake of Nebuchadnezzar”); they are translated as printed in parentheses. The Aramaic word is translated as printed.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I will pour out My indignation upon thee
Ezekiel.english_translation: Rashi’s lemma is “a sword, a sword, drawn” (Ezekiel 21:33): The doubled sword of Nebuchadnezzar, to go out by the two roads against Jerusalem and against the children of Ammon, as in the earlier passage; behold, a punishment for the children of Ammon.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The source places a comment on Hebrew 21:33 at this verse; the lemma shown is the nearest wording in the id’s own verse.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I will deliver thee into the hand of brutish men
Ezekiel.english_translation: “While they see falsehood unto thee, While they divine lies unto thee”: You think that by means of your divinations of vanity and falsehood and lie you succeed, [and] that your sword is given upon the necks of the slain wicked, whose day has come by a decree from before Me, at the time of the completion of their end.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The source places a comment on Hebrew 21:34 at this verse; the lemma shown is from the id’s own verse.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: with the fire of My wrath
Ezekiel.english_translation: “Cause it to return into its sheath”: That is, the time will come when you will return to your sheath and the sword will receive its retribution from the hand of the kings of Media; and then I will blow upon you with the fire of My wrath, and it will be given into the hand of foolish smiths, who are the “skilful to destroy,” who will come to sharpen you and to polish you, as from of old; and they destroyed you.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The source places a comment on Hebrew 21:35 at this verse; the lemma shown is from the id’s own verse. The tense of the last verb is as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Jerusalem.
With a *mappik* in the *hei*: *vehoda’atah* means *vehoda’ata otah* (“and you shall make her know”).
This is a transposed verse, and this is its explanation: “O city that sheddest blood in the midst of thee,” saith the Lord GOD, “that thy time may come.”
Like “and who made idols” etc.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: art come even unto thy years
Ezekiel.english_translation: The decree of *venoshantem* (Deuteronomy 4), by the numerical value (*gematria*) that Moses stated.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The abbreviation בגי' is read as *gematria*.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Rumor — for everyone speaks of you; in Old French [printed פרלרי"ץ].
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists the same printed form (פרלריץ) at Ezekiel 23:11, glossed “un objet de conversation” (“a subject of conversation”); this verse itself was not found there.

Ezekiel.english_translation: And what is the mockery? “Defiled of name” — this is that you defiled your name: they were called a holy people, sons of their Maker, and they caused themselves to be called “a people of unclean lips” (Isaiah 6:5).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: every one according to his might
Ezekiel.english_translation: Whoever is strong prevails.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Aramaic saying, translated as printed.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: made light of father and mother
Ezekiel.english_translation: All the abominations in the portion “You shall be holy,” concerning which they were warned, are enumerated here.
Ezekiel.translator_note: “You shall be holy” (*Kedoshim*) is the Torah portion Leviticus 19–20.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Thou hast despised My holy things
Ezekiel.english_translation: And not as I said, “you shall sacrifice it to be accepted” (Leviticus 19).
Ezekiel.translator_note: Rashi writes *lirtzonkhem tizbachu*; in Leviticus 19:5 JPS reads “you shall offer it that you may be accepted.”

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: they have eaten upon the mountains
Ezekiel.english_translation: And on the mountains they served idolatry in you.
Counsels of wickedness.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: thou hast greedily gained of thy neighbours by oppression
Ezekiel.english_translation: You enriched your lovers with the oppression with which you oppressed the poor. Another explanation: *vativtze’i* is an expression of robbery, as in “And the covetous vaunteth himself, though he contemn the LORD” (Psalms 10:3); and thus is its interpretation: “and you robbed your neighbors by oppression.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “Psalms 6” is Psalms 10:3 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_translation: I cried “Woe!” and a lamentation.
Here we learned that robbery is the worst of all, for on account of it the decree of judgment was sealed.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: that I shall deal with thee
Ezekiel.english_translation: I work upon you according to your work.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I will consume thy filthiness out of thee
Ezekiel.english_translation: *Vehatimoti* — and I will finish.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: thou shalt be profaned in thyself
Ezekiel.english_translation: You will tremble within yourself over what you did.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Rashi takes *venichalt* as an expression of trembling; JPS renders it “profaned.”

Ezekiel.english_translation: A mixture of waste matter mixed into silver and gold, which must be melted in fire to refine it.
In which gold is refined.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: As they gather silver and brass
Ezekiel.english_translation: As the smelter gathers all the dross into the furnace.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: to blow the fire upon it
Ezekiel.english_translation: To blow.
The Targum translates *vayatzakta* [“and you shall pour”] as *vatatich* [“you shall melt”].
Ezekiel.translator_note: Rashi names no verse for *vayatzakta*.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: nor rained upon in the day of indignation
Ezekiel.english_translation: She was not given the rain proper to her, to cleanse her in the day of wrath. And the interpretation of the matter is as its Targum: “No good deeds were done in her that would shield her in the day of cursing.”

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: There is a conspiracy of her prophets
Ezekiel.english_translation: They are bound together in an evil counsel.
For they would take bribes and strengthen the hands of evildoers to kill and to plunder and to despoil, and would prophesy peace to them.
Money.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: have done violence to My law
Ezekiel.english_translation: It was incumbent on them to rebuke, and to teach, and to make known statute and judgment, and they did not; behold, this is violence, that they robbed it from those who need to learn.
And I was profaned.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: so as to get dishonest gain
Ezekiel.english_translation: To snatch money.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: have daubed for them with whited plaster
Ezekiel.english_translation: They are like those who plaster a building with mortar that has not been worked as much as needed, which has no straw in it and which dissolves of itself when rains come upon it; and the expression *tafel* is for anything lacking repair.
Two provinces, which are like two women.
Both of them were from one assembly, divided into two in the days of Rehoboam.
The sons of Egypt [pressed] their breasts — an expression of “bruised” (Leviticus 22).
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “Leviticus 22” is 22:24 (JPS wording: “bruised”).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: there their virgin breasts were bruised
Ezekiel.english_translation: The Egyptians [pressed] the breasts of their virginity — that is, they taught them the ways of their abominations; *they made* — *[printed Old French: איטיינירי"ש]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: By epithet: Oholah and Oholibah.

The first ones: Samaria — she whom I call Oholah, for at the outset she became a tent (*ohel*) for the calves of Jeroboam and the house of Baal of Ahab. And although Samaria was built only in the days of Omri, He calls the kings of Israel by its name, because once it was built it became the head.
Because My tent was in her, and My Sanctuary.
And she desired — *[printed Old French: אישויי"ר]* in Old French; another version: *[printed Old French: דיששירי"ר]*.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this verse (Ezekiel 23:5) with the printed form אישוייר and glosses it “elle a follement aimé” (“she loved madly”). The other printed form appears to be *désirer* (“to desire”), but was not found in Darmesteter.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Who were neighbors to her, and they sent to them to be a help to them. This was Menahem son of Gadi (2 Kings 15:19), who gave tribute to Pul king of Assyria, “that his hand might be with him to confirm the kingdom in his hand.” And the prophet likens the matter to an adulterous woman: for had they served the Holy One, blessed be He, they would not have needed the kings of Assyria.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Rashi paraphrases 2 Kings 15:19 (“gave tribute”); the quoted words are JPS.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: she bestowed her harlotries upon them
Ezekiel.english_translation: She gave upon them a heart of adulteries and a spirit of harlotries, for she longed for them.
With all the idolaters with whom she associated, she learned their ways and was defiled with their idols.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Neither hath she left her harlotries brought from Egypt
Ezekiel.english_translation: They also relied on the kings of Egypt, for we find (there, 17) with Hoshea son of Elah, “for he had sent messengers to So king of Egypt.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “there, 17” is 2 Kings 17:4 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: for in her youth they lay with her
Ezekiel.english_translation: And from then, “and they poured out their lust upon her” — the desire of harlotries entered her from the days of her youth.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I delivered her into the hand of her lovers
Ezekiel.english_translation: For Sennacherib came and exiled them.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Translated as printed; 2 Kings 17:3 names Shalmaneser, king of Assyria, as the one who came up against Hoshea.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: she became a byword among women
Ezekiel.english_translation: A curse is taken from them for all adulteresses, so that they be warned by it: See what befell so-and-so for her lewdness.
Like *shefatim* [judgments] — *[printed Old French: יושטישא"ט]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Old French printed יושטישא"ט; it appears to be a form of *justicier* (“to judge”), which Darmesteter lists at other verses, but this verse was not found there.

Ezekiel.english_translation: All the evil that came upon her sister for her harlotries — and she did not see.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Translated literally as printed; the final phrase is unclear.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Her desire — *[printed Old French: זויט"ר]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this verse (Ezekiel 23:11) with variants (e.g. וויטיר) and glosses it “sa passion effrénée” (“her unbridled passion”); he reads *waytéd* and notes a possible relation to *gaité*. The printed spelling differs slightly from his.

Ezekiel.english_translation: This is Ahaz, who sent to the king of Assyria for help (there).
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “there” is 2 Kings 16:7 (Ahaz sent messengers to Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria).

Ezekiel.english_translation: To long for images that she had not seen, only their likeness.
With vermilion (*shashar*) — her sister did not do the like of this.
The likeness of the men of the Chaldeans, who differ in their garments.
Kinds of drawing.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: girded with girdles upon their loins
Ezekiel.english_translation: Such is the way of the garments of the Chaldeans.

Extra-large hats. And Menahem explained it like “and they dipped (*vayitbelu*) the coat in the blood” (Genesis 37:31); but the interpretation of *seruchei tevulim* is thus: like “the overhanging part (*serach ha’odef*)” (Exodus 26) of the dyed turban; *tevulim* has no parallel, and its interpretation is according to the context. And so Targum Jonathan: *machatin kolsin*.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Aramaic words of Targum Jonathan are transliterated; their meaning is not given by Rashi. Printed “Exodus 26” is 26:12 (JPS wording: “the overhanging part”).

Ezekiel.english_translation: Mighty ones.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: as soon as she saw them
Ezekiel.english_translation: Because she saw the likeness of their form.

They cut a covenant together. And I say that this was said of Hezekiah, who rejoiced over the messengers of Merodach-baladan (Isaiah 39:1), and fed them at his table, and showed them his entire treasure-house. And the prophet’s example, “men portrayed upon the wall,” is because they came from a far land, and the Chaldeans were not familiar to them, as it is said there (Isaiah 39:3), “They are come from a far country unto me”; and because of seeing their faces once, they became dear to him, and the Holy One, blessed be He, was displeased at the matter, as it is said, “Behold, the days come, that all that is in thy house” etc. (there) (and in Chronicles II 32:25): “But Hezekiah rendered not according to the benefit done unto him; for his heart was lifted up; therefore there was great wrath upon him,” etc.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Rashi’s quotation from Chronicles reads “great wrath” (*ketzef gadol*); JPS 2 Chronicles 32:25 reads “wrath.” Rashi’s words (“from a far country they came to me”) are given in the JPS wording of Isaiah 39:3.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: her soul was alienated from them
Ezekiel.english_translation: Because Jehoiakim and Zedekiah rebelled against them; *vatika* — *[printed Old French: אשלוקי"ר]* in Old French. *Vatika* is like “and the hollow of Jacob’s thigh was strained (*vateka*)” (Genesis 32:26) — *hoka’ah* [dislocation]. An expression of joining, and of the fixing of a tree in the ground; and likewise, when it is pulled from the ground, an expression of *ke’iyah* falls upon it, as you say “and it took deep root (*vatashresh sharasheha*)” (Psalms 80), an expression of taking root, and “in all my produce (*tashresh*)” — an expression of uprooting; and so “in the branches (*besa’ifeha*) of the fruitful” (Isaiah 17:6), an expression of branches, and “*mesa’ef pa’arah*” (there, 10), an expression of cutting the branches of the tree and its boughs.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The grammatical argument is translated literally; the word *ke’iyah* is left transliterated. Darmesteter lists this verse (Ezekiel 23:17) with variants (e.g. אשלוקר) and glosses the Old French as “s’est éloignée” (“she withdrew”). The printed spelling differs slightly from his. Printed references: “Genesis 32:26”; “Psalms 80” is 80:10; “there, 10” is Isaiah 10:33; the quotation “in all my produce” is not named by Rashi (it appears in Job 31:12).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: remembering the days of her youth
Ezekiel.english_translation: The desire for the sons of Egypt came up into her heart, for Zedekiah sent to her, as it is said (above, 17), “But he rebelled against him in sending his ambassadors into Egypt.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: “To her” is translated as printed; the referent is not clear. Printed “above, 17” is Ezekiel 17:15 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: she doted upon concubinage with them
Ezekiel.english_translation: Upon their concubinage — to be a concubine to them.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: whose flesh is as the flesh of asses
Ezekiel.english_translation: The organ of intercourse.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: whose issue is like the issue of horses
Ezekiel.english_translation: An expression of abundant intercourse, for they have intercourse more than all other males among the beasts.
The flow of seed, as in “The tempest of waters floweth over” (Habakkuk 3:10).
And you remembered.
An expression of pressing.
The Chaldeans, who were pleasing to Hezekiah.
Ezekiel.translator_note: “Pleasing to” renders *arvu al*; the sense is not certain.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: from whom thy soul is alienated
Ezekiel.english_translation: Whom Zedekiah turned away from and hated, and rebelled against them.

Targum Jonathan: names of provinces; and the verse supports him (in the book of Jeremiah): “Go up against the land of Merathaim, even against it, and against the inhabitants of Pekod.” And the interpreters say it is an expression of officers, princes and rulers.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed reference is Jeremiah 50:21 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_translation: *Semons* in Old French [printed שמונ"ץ].
Ezekiel.translator_note: Old French printed שמונ"ץ; it appears to be *semons* (“summoned”), but was not found at this verse in Darmesteter.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Dunash explained: one of the instruments of war. And I say: an expression of encircling of camps, like “and for pricks in your sides” (Numbers 33:55) and [in Aramaic] *ulmashirin makifnakhon*. (Menahem explained it like *tzinah* [shield], as in “His truth is a shield and a buckler” (Psalms 91:4); and Dunash does not agree with him; and the Targum, which translates “and they shall come upon thee with instruments of war,” supports Dunash.) *Hatzen* is like *behotzen*; and there is one who understands *hotzen* as *chotzen*, from “and they shall bring thy sons in their bosom” (*bechotzen*) (Isaiah 49:22), the meaning of which is “arm”; and so “and they shall come against thee with *hotzen*” (here); and its meaning is force, as in “and the arms of the south” (Daniel 11:15), the meaning of which is “the forces of the south.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Aramaic phrase *ulmashirin makifnakhon* is transliterated; its source is not named by Rashi and its sense is not certain. The parentheses are as printed. JPS renders *chotzen* in Isaiah 49:22 as “bosom”; Rashi takes it as “arm.” Printed references: Numbers 33:55, Psalms 91:4, Isaiah 49:22 and Daniel 11:15, each quoted in JPS wording.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I will commit the judgment unto them
Ezekiel.english_translation: What is upon Me to judge, I will make them My messengers to carry out the judgment.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: they shall judge thee according to their judgments
Ezekiel.english_translation: A judgment that I did not write in My Torah, which is from the judgments of their laws. And which is it? This is the blinding of the eyes, for they blinded the eyes of Zedekiah.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: they shall take away thy nose and thine ears
Ezekiel.english_translation: They are the beauty of the face; and to them He likened the priesthood and the kingship.
The rest of the people.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: thy residue shall be devoured by the fire
Ezekiel.english_translation: And the best of your lands, for they are a security on which to lean for livelihood.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Aramaic phrase is translated as printed; its sense is not certain.

Ezekiel.english_translation: The priestly garments.
The Chaldeans, against whom you rebelled.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: These things shall be done unto thee
Ezekiel.english_translation: An expression of the passive form (*pa’ul*) — *faisant* in Old French [printed פיישנ"ט].
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this verse (Ezekiel 23:30) with the form *faysant* (printed פיישנט) and glosses it “faisant” (“doing, making”).

Ezekiel.english_translation: Too much to contain, like “too much to bear.”
Astonishment.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Thou shalt even drink it and drain it
Ezekiel.english_translation: An expression of sucking out until the dregs — *[printed Old French: אישוצרא"ש]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: thou shalt craunch the sherds thereof
Ezekiel.english_translation: He likened the cup of drink of punishment for Israel to an earthen vessel, which, when it is broken, has no repair; so when their salvation comes and the cup is broken, it will not return to give them to drink any more. And when He speaks of giving the idolaters to drink, He calls it gold, as it is said, “Babylon hath been a golden cup … That made all the earth drunken” (Jeremiah 51:7).
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed reference is Jeremiah 51:7 (JPS wording quoted in part).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: thou shalt craunch the sherds thereof
Ezekiel.english_translation: Like “and shall break their bones in pieces” (Numbers 24:8); “They leave not a bone for the morrow” (Zephaniah 3:3). *Rongier* in Old French [printed רונגייר]: gnawing with the teeth round the bone or the sherd, to scrape off the flesh stuck to it. And Menahem connected it with an expression of breaking, and so he explained “and shall break their bones in pieces,” and so “they leave not a bone for the morrow.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this verse (Ezekiel 23:34) with the form רונגייר among the variants and glosses it “tu rongeras” (“you will gnaw”).

Ezekiel.english_translation: Receive the debts [guilt] of the counsel of your sins.
An expression of contention.
In their adulteries they shed blood.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: with their idols have they committed adultery
Ezekiel.english_translation: Their adultery was with their idols.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: their sons, whom they bore unto Me
Ezekiel.english_translation: And this is the shedding of blood that is in their hands (that is, that they emitted seed in vain with their hands and did not repent).
Ezekiel.translator_note: The parentheses are as printed.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: they have defiled My sanctuary in the same day
Ezekiel.english_translation: On the day that they slaughtered their children to idolatry, they came before Me into My Sanctuary to commit an abomination in it, to provoke Me.
For they used to slaughter their sons on the Sabbath.
And all the more — the worst of all — “you send” to bring to them some of the princes of the idolaters, their enemies, and they see the desecration with which they desecrate My Sanctuary.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: unto whom a messenger was sent
Ezekiel.english_translation: From Oholah and Oholibah, to come to them.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: for whom thou didst wash thyself
Ezekiel.english_translation: *Le’asher* — Jonathan translated it *le’atar* [“to a place”]; *[printed Old French: אללו"א]* in Old French: To the place that you appointed for them, saying: In such-and-such a place we will go out to meet you, adorned, in the bath and with kohl.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: A kind of dye, and its name is *kachol*, and they dye their eyes with it — *[printed Old French: אוקליר"א]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Adorned with beautiful bedding — *paréda* [printed פריד"י] in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this verse (Ezekiel 23:41) with the form פרידא (*paredle*) and glosses it “parée” (“adorned”).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the voice of a multitude being at ease
Ezekiel.english_translation: Many idolaters were in her; and not a multitude of war, but the sound of a carefree multitude.
On account of men; and that multitude was of men and not of animals.
For there were in her those brought to commit adultery from the wilderness.
For they dwelt around her — her neighbors Ammon and Moab; and so the Targum of *sabaim* is *mesachor sachor* [“round about”].
Ezekiel.translator_note: JPS renders *sov’im* as “drunken”; Rashi takes it as “those round about.”

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: they put bracelets upon their hands
Ezekiel.english_translation: Oholah and Oholibah put bracelets upon their hands, to adorn themselves to commit adultery. That is: Ammon and Moab, because they are many, she adorns and glorifies herself to them; and because they are her neighbors, she glorifies herself before their eyes with her ornaments. Therefore “and they put bracelets upon their hands” — so as to be pleasing in the eyes of the adulterers. And the *vav* of *vayitnu* is superfluous, like that [*vav*] of “And He is become my salvation” (Exodus 15) and like that [*vav*] of “and he that regarded not the word of the LORD left” (ibid. 9).
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “Exodus 14” is Exodus 15:2; “ibid. 9” is Exodus 9:21 (JPS wording quoted). Rashi’s word “*otah*/*otekh*” is read as “that [*vav*].”

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Then said I of her that was worn out by adulteries
Ezekiel.english_translation: “Now they will commit harlotries” etc. — My heart said to me concerning this one who wore out and grew old in adulteries: from now that she has grown old, her harlotries will go from her, and the desire of her harlotry will depart from her heart, and she will turn back; and behold, she is still in her harlotries as at the beginning.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Still they commit harlotries with her
Ezekiel.english_translation: “They go out” — every harlot; the Targum is *nafkat bara* [“she goes out abroad”]. So I heard; and so Targum Jonathan.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Aramaic is transliterated and translated as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Like *labalah ba-ni’ufim* [“worn out by adulteries”]; as you say, “And Tamar went and dwelt in her father’s house” (Genesis 38), as if “in her father’s house”; “they shall wash with water” (Exodus 30), as if “with water”; “then shall she go out for nothing” (ibid. 21), as if “in vain”; “And if a woman vowed in her husband’s house” (Numbers 30) — as if “in her husband’s house.” And so Dunash explained; and Menahem connected it with “*tevel asu*” (Leviticus 20), but his words are not tenable.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 35” is Genesis 38:11; “Exodus 30” is 30:20; “ibid. 21” is Exodus 21:11; “Numbers 30” is 30:11; “Leviticus 20” is 20:12, where JPS reads “they have wrought corruption” (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_translation: Everyone whose heart filled him.
Women of lewdness.

Men who are judges: the princes of the king of Babylon and of the king of Assyria. And Targum Jonathan: “meritorious in their acceptance.” According to the deeds of these harlots, the idolaters are righteous; it benefits [them].
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Aramaic of Targum Jonathan and the closing words are translated as printed; the sense is not fully clear.

Ezekiel.english_translation: As is explained after it.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: An assembly shall be brought up against them
Ezekiel.english_translation: *Ha’aleh*, and *natun*, and *bara* — all of them are an expression of doing and of the passive form (*pa’ul*).
The killing of their sons and daughters and the burning of their houses is the judgment of adulteresses.
That is the judgment of those who shed blood; and *bara* is an expression of cutting, and so, “and thou shalt cut it down, for forest shall be thine,” in the book of Joshua (17:17).
Ezekiel.translator_note: Rashi’s wording differs in order from Joshua 17:18 (“for though it is a forest, thou shalt cut it down”); the printed reference “17:17” is not where the words occur (see 17:18 and 17:15).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: your lewdness shall be recompensed upon you
Ezekiel.english_translation: Your judges will put the judgment of your lewdness upon your heads.
Of Zedekiah.
On this day he laid siege against it.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Set on the pot, set it on
Ezekiel.english_translation: *Shefot* — on the stove, at its place of sitting, is called *shefitah* in the language of the Mishnah, as our Rabbis said, “the place of the setting of two pots”; and further we learned, “one sets the pot, and one puts water into it, and one puts spice into it.” We learned that *shefitah* is the placing of it on the stove before they put anything into it. And this illustration is for Jerusalem, concerning which you said (above), “She is the pot”; now the time has come for her to be a pot, and you in her for flesh; Nebuchadnezzar will come and set her on the fire. And Menahem explained it as an expression of placing.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Rashi quotes the Mishnah without naming the tractate. Printed “above” gives no chapter; the saying is in Ezekiel 11:3 (JPS: “this city is the caldron, and we are the flesh”).

Ezekiel.english_translation: They are the needs of the siege; *yatzuk* is like *shafoch* [“pour”].

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Gather into it the pieces belonging to it
Ezekiel.english_translation: Out of fear of the siege, they gathered into her all her chiefs and her princes.
Every mighty man, fearsome in their dread, and a man who makes war — so Targum Jonathan.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Take the choice of the flock
Ezekiel.english_translation: Take, you, Nebuchadnezzar, the choice of your forces round about her — so Targum Jonathan; but it does not settle with the matter of the pot, and so one must interpret it: the choicest of Israel will come and enter into her.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: pile also the bones under it
Ezekiel.english_translation: Arrange and set the bones beneath the other limbs; that is, the mighty will fight for the sake of the weak, and these will lean upon them. *Dur* is an expression of arrangement, and so “He will violently roll and toss thee like a ball” (Isaiah 22:18) — rows, encirclement of troops; and so *shurah* in the Targum is *dara*. Menahem explained it like “I also will make the pile great.”
And after they are all in it, they will bring the instruments of siege and war near to the city.
Its scum, which is removed from its mouth through its boiling, which is called *escume* in Old French [printed אשקומ"א]; that is, the wicked who are in her will not go out of it.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this verse (Ezekiel 24:6) with the form אישקומא (*escoume*) and glosses it “son écume” (“its scum”).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: bring it out piece by piece
Ezekiel.english_translation: Exile after exile; whoever went out and fell to the Chaldeans, each man alone.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: no lot is fallen upon it
Ezekiel.english_translation: Not like other pots, from which they take out their pieces together, to give before each and every one his portion and lot. And Jonathan translated: “Since repentance was not done in her, the lot of HaMakom did not fall upon her.”
Smoothness.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: she poured it not upon the ground
Ezekiel.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “Willfully and with a raised arm she shed it; she did not shed it in tranquility, to do repentance upon it.” And our Rabbis explained it as the blood of Zechariah son of Jehoiada: they did not treat it like the blood of a gazelle nor like the blood of a deer.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: that it might cause fury to come up
Ezekiel.english_translation: I commanded that blood beforehand not to be absorbed in the ground, so that it would be remembered to take its vengeance.
Ezekiel.translator_note: “Beforehand” renders *lefanai* (literally, “before Me”); the sense is not certain.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I also will make the pile great
Ezekiel.english_translation: A large kindling — *[printed Old French: פואיא"ה]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Old French printed פואיא"ה; it appears to be *fouaille*, but was not found at this verse in Darmesteter.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: heaping on the wood, kindling the fire
Ezekiel.english_translation: To multiply the wood and to kindle the fire.

When the flesh is hot above the bones, and it shrinks and is mixed into the broth and stirred with a spoon, it is like a compounding of spices that is mixed very well; and from the shrinking of the flesh, its smoke is turned back into it, which is called *aorsir* [printed אאורש"יר] in Old French. And this is what He said: “and the bones shall be burned (*yecharu*), shall dry up and smoke” — an expression of burning, as in “my bones are burned with heat” (Job 29); and so, “that it may be hot, and the bottom thereof may burn” — as in a pot whose waters have been consumed in its boiling: it becomes hot, its sherds are burned, and the food is spoiled.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this form (אאורשיר, *adormser*) at Ezekiel 24:10 and glosses it “laisser brûler” (“to let burn”). Printed “Job 29” is Job 30:30 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the filth of it may be consumed
Ezekiel.english_translation: Its scum will end, and be absorbed in its brass; it is a pot of brass.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: It hath wearied itself with toil
Ezekiel.english_translation: With pretexts and deceit you wearied the poor; therefore the wicked who are within her will not go out of it, but by the fire of its punishment they will be consumed.
In the uncleanness of lewdness you will be finished.
To rebuke through the prophets, “and thou wast not purged,” etc.
I will not annul My decree.
To turn back from My evil thought that I spoke to do to you.
Your wife, as the matter proves at its end.
Waste away in silence — *[printed Old French: שוא"ש]* — *demonir* [printed דמוני"ץ] in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. The form resembles *demonir*, which Darmesteter lists for Ezekiel 36:31 (“et vous vous épuiserez”: “and you will wear yourselves out”), but this verse was not found there.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Tefillin. All these are commandments of mourners, and you [do] the reverse: a mourner is forbidden tefillin and sandal, and is obligated in covering the head, and they feed him his first meal from the food of others.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Rashi’s lemma is *pe’arkha*, which JPS renders “headtire.”

Ezekiel.english_translation: Not to observe mourning.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: what these things are to us
Ezekiel.english_translation: What are these hints concerning us.
In Jerusalem, when you went out into exile.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: you shall do as I have done
Ezekiel.english_translation: You will not observe mourning, for there will be none to console you, for there is not one among you who will not be a mourner, and there is no mourning except where there are comforters. Another explanation: that you will be afraid to weep before the Chaldeans among whom you are.
*Grenon* in Old French [printed גרינו"ן].
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists the same form (גרינון, *grenon*) for the same Hebrew word (*safam*) elsewhere, glossed “sa moustache” (“his moustache”); this verse was not found there.

Ezekiel.english_translation: *[printed Old French: אישרויי"ץ]* — *[printed Old French: דמוני"ץ]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. The form resembles *demonir*, which Darmesteter lists for Ezekiel 36:31 (“et vous vous épuiserez”: “and you will wear yourselves out”), but this verse was not found there.

Ezekiel.english_translation: When this evil comes.
For their soul is lifted up in them.

It is impossible for the fugitive to come on the day of the destruction; and so is its interpretation: “in that day” — that the fugitive will come to you, to make your ear hear; “in that day your mouth shall be opened.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: Translated literally; the sense of the first sentence is not fully clear.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: to cause thee to hear it with thine ears
Ezekiel.english_translation: To announce the tidings that the city has been struck.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: together with him that is escaped
Ezekiel.english_translation: With the fugitive.
Because I said to you, “and thou shalt be dumb, and shalt not be to them” etc. — from now they will see that your words are true, and you will no longer be dumb from prophesying to them.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Rashi does not name the verse; the quoted words are Ezekiel 3:26 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_translation: An expression of joy.
Because it was inherited, and became an inheritance for others.
Ezekiel.translator_note: JPS renders *nachal* as “profaned”; Rashi takes it as “inherited.”

Ezekiel.english_translation: The Chaldeans and Aram are to the east.

For the sake of joy. And although at the beginning of the book (above, 6) He said so concerning mourning — “Smite with your hand and stamp with your foot and say, Aha!” — there are things that are done both for mourning and for joy, but their purposes are not alike; and so, “flutes for the bride and for the dead.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: Rashi’s wording of Ezekiel 6:11 differs slightly from JPS (“Smite with thy hand, and stamp with thy foot, and say: Alas!”).

Ezekiel.english_translation: An expression of *marpes* [stamping].
Ezekiel.translator_note: The bracketed gloss is the translator’s.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: all the disdain of thy soul
Ezekiel.english_translation: An expression of contempt; they interpret it like “Esau despised” (Genesis 25:34), which Onkelos translates *ve-sat Esav*. And I say *sha’at* is an expression of flood — *golosement* in Old French [printed גולוזמנ"ט].
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this verse (Ezekiel 25:6) with the form גולוזמונט (*golosement*) and glosses it “de toute ton avidité” (“with all your greed”).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Behold, the house of Judah is like unto all the nations
Ezekiel.english_translation: The love of the Holy One, blessed be He, ceased from them, and they were rejected, to be given into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar like the other idolaters. And an aggadic midrash: that they [the nations] entered the Sanctuary and folded up the forms of the cherubim that Solomon had engraved on the wall of the Sanctuary, “according to the space of each, with wreaths” (1 Kings 7:36), and took them outside; they said: See these who showed themselves as modest — what were they engaged in?

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I will open the flank of Moab
Ezekiel.english_translation: The fortresses of the land of Moab that are on the border, at the end of their boundary; it is the shoulder (*katef*), the end of the boundary of their land, as in “And for the other side” (Exodus 27:15), which the Targum translates *le’ivra* [“to the side”].
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Aramaic is transliterated and translated as printed. Rashi’s Hebrew is *ulakatef hashenit*; JPS reads “And for the other side.”

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: unto the children of the east
Ezekiel.english_translation: I will entice them to come upon the children of Ammon by way of the land of Moab.
And the inhabitants of Dedan.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: by the hand of My people Israel
Ezekiel.english_translation: They will be My messengers to take My vengeance.
In hatred and with cruelty, like a man who takes his vengeance on his enemy.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I will cut off the Cherethites
Ezekiel.english_translation: Aramaic: “A people condemned to destruction.” And I say: since I saw in another place that He calls the Philistines Cherethites — “the inhabitants of the sea-coast, the nation of the Cherethites” (Zephaniah 2:5) — and He does not call another nation so, it appears in my eyes that there is a region among the Philistines whose name was Cherethite; and so I find in the book (Samuel I 30), in the troop that burned Ziklag: “We made a raid upon the South of the Cherethites.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “Samuel I 30” is 1 Samuel 30:14 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_translation: *Marche* in Old French [printed מארק"א]: they are the Philistines, who dwell in the southwestern corner of the border of the Land of Israel, on the last sea.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Old French printed מארק"א; it appears to be *marche* (“border region”), but was not found at this verse in Darmesteter. “The last sea” is literal.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Of Zedekiah.
That was under siege.
An expression of the sound of joy.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: she is broken that was the gate of the peoples
Ezekiel.english_translation: A city into which all the idolaters entered for trade; from now she will be broken, for the siege will not go away from her until she is captured.
From now the trade of the peoples has been turned to me.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I shall be filled with her that is laid waste
Ezekiel.english_translation: I shall be filled from the city of Jerusalem, which is laid waste.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I will also scrape her dust from her
Ezekiel.english_translation: And I will uproot — as in “The LORD will pluck up the house of the proud” (Proverbs 15:25) and “and you shall be plucked from off” (Deuteronomy 28).
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “Deuteronomy 28” is 28:63 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_translation: Because it was built on a rock in the midst of the sea, when it is shattered and its dust swept into the sea, the rock remains smooth. And so Targum Jonathan: *leshe’ayut kif gale* [“to smoothness, a rock of waves”].

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: a place for the spreading of nets
Ezekiel.english_translation: On the rock the fishermen will spread the nets of their fishing-nets, to dry them.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: her daughters that are in the field
Ezekiel.english_translation: The villages subject to her round about her.
“And he will set up against you those armed with shields.”

It is one of the stratagems of the siege: to throw large stones, and it strikes against it — *[printed Old French: אילקולי"אה דשאפורי"ירא]* in Old French; and some of those who speak the vernacular [render] *kabbelo* — *[printed Old French: דשארבלי"טא]* in Old French; and some, *[printed Old French: פוריירא]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. The sentence structure is translated as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: With the craft of destruction that he brings with him.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Rashi derives *bechorvotav* from *churban* (“destruction”); JPS renders “axes.”

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: By reason of the abundance of his horses
Ezekiel.english_translation: When there are many horses, they raise dust with their feet, and it rises and becomes like a cloud and darkens the earth; it is called *shif’at*, and so “and abundance of waters cover thee” (Job 22) — *[printed Old French: דלאפוי"שון]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. Printed “Job 22” is Job 22:11 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: As men enter into a city
Ezekiel.english_translation: As they enter a city that has been breached — [from] the wall, whose wall was broken through.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Aramaic is translated as printed; the sense is not fully clear.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Your trade goods.
At the breakings, lest there come upon them too something like your breaking.

An expression of breaking, as in “*ori rega*” (Job 26) and “*al rig’ei aretz*” (Psalms 35), meaning “against the crushed of the earth.” And Menahem explained it as an expression of “moment,” as in “For His anger is but for a moment” (ibid. 30).
Ezekiel.translator_note: The printed words before “Job 26” (*ori rega*) appear corrupt; Job 26:12 reads “He stirreth up the sea” (*raga hayam*), and Isaiah 51:15 “Who stirreth up the sea” is the likely parallel. In Psalms 35:20 JPS renders *rig’ei aretz* as “them that are quiet in the land”; Rashi takes it as “the crushed.” Printed “ibid. 30” is Psalms 30:6.

Ezekiel.english_translation: An expression of astonishment.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: that wast peopled from the seas
Ezekiel.english_translation: Some vocalize it soft (*rafeh*) and interpret it as “inhabited from ancient seas [times]”; and some vocalize it with a *dagesh* and interpret it as “inhabited strongly by means of the seas that surround it.” And so Jonathan translated; and so it is.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Hebrew grammatical terms are translated as printed.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: That caused your terror to be
Ezekiel.english_translation: Round about, for all the inhabitants.
*[printed Old French: לורדפריימ"נט]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Like *ha’iyim* [“the isles”].
From your going out into exile.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: when I shall bring up the deep upon thee
Ezekiel.english_translation: “When I bring up against you hosts of many nations, like the deep (*tehoma*)”; “and many nations will cover you” — so Targum Jonathan. And as it implies: at first she was given into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar, and at the end the sea rose and drowned her.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: them that descend into the pit
Ezekiel.english_translation: With those who descend to Gehinnom.
With the other idolaters who have been there from of old.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: like the places that are desolate of old
Ezekiel.english_translation: Like the cities that were destroyed from then, like Sodom and its companion cities.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I will set glory in the land of the living
Ezekiel.english_translation: And I will give the glory in Jerusalem.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I will make thee a terror
Ezekiel.english_translation: Jonathan interpreted *ballahot* as “*kedla havet*” [“as if you had not been”]; and the interpreters say: an expression of a place of dancing for satyrs and demons.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: that dwelleth at the entry of the sea
Ezekiel.english_translation: On the harbor, where the ships come up to the wall and the gates; and many cities sit on the sea but it is not a place of harbor, and the ships cannot come near them.
*Port* in Old French [printed פור"ט].
Ezekiel.translator_note: Old French printed פור"ט; it appears to be *port* (“harbor”), but was not found in Darmesteter.

Ezekiel.english_translation: So was their custom: merchants who came to her, this one from the north and that one from the south, were not permitted to do business with each other, but the inhabitants of the city would buy from this one and sell to that one.

Until now everyone has said of Jerusalem “the perfection of beauty” (Lamentations 2:15–16), “the joy of the whole earth” (Psalms 48:3); now you pride yourself, saying, “I am the perfection of beauty”; the end of the completion of beauty is contained in me.
Your architects (*ardekhlayikh*) — an expression of building.
Because she was built in the sea, and in the sea she perished, the prophet likened her to a splendid ship whose load was made heavy within it, and it sank in the east wind.
*Tur talga* [“the mountain of snow”].
The planks of which the ship is made.
The name of a forest in which cedars are found.

It is the upright, tall timber fixed in the ship, on which they hang the sail, which is called *veile* [printed בוייל"א] in Old French; and it has holes at its top, through which the rope with which they draw the ship goes in and out — *mast* [printed מש"ט] in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this verse (Ezekiel 27:5) with the forms ווילא (*veile*) and משט (*mast*) and glosses them “arbre planté au milieu du navire où est attachée la voile” (“a tree planted in the middle of the ship to which the sail is attached”) and “qui s’appelle mât” (“which is called mast”).

Ezekiel.english_translation: From a barren tree, called *chesne* [printed קיישנ"א] in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this verse (Ezekiel 27:6) with the form קיישנא (*chesne*) and glosses it “chênes” (“oaks”).

Ezekiel.english_translation: They are the broad-ended ones with which they steer the ship — *rimes* [printed ריימ"ש] in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this verse (Ezekiel 27:6) with the form ריימש and glosses it “tes rames” (“your oars”).

Ezekiel.english_translation: It is the broad board at the end of the second [end] of a ship, opposite the mast at its head, by which they turn the ship to all its sides and direct it on the way, and the captain (*rav hovel*) holds it; in the language of the Mishnah, *kavarnit*; and in the vernacular, *gouvernail* [printed גובריינא"ל].
Ezekiel.translator_note: JPS renders *kerashekha* as “thy deck.” The Old French printed גובריינא"ל appears to be *gouvernail* (“rudder”), but was not found in Darmesteter.

Ezekiel.english_translation: It cannot be but of wood; and this is *bat ashurim*, as if it were one word, an expression of “and the larch” (Isaiah 41:19). Both [terms] in Targum Jonathan are *ashkeru’in*. And the steersman’s [board] of Tyre he likened to a board of *ashkeru’a* overlaid with ivory by nails, for beauty and strength; for so Jonathan translated: “boards of *ashkeru’in* fastened in ivory; *dafil beit chofa’ah*, do not guard its covering; it will not fall.” But Jonathan interpreted this *kavarnit* according to the matter of the city, [as] the boards of its gates.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Aramaic of Targum Jonathan is transliterated in part; its last clause is not clear to the translator. In Isaiah 41:19 JPS renders *te’ashur* as “the larch.” Audit 4: the Aramaic quotation was checked against Targum Jonathan/the Ketuvim Targum (Mikraot Gedolot, Sefaria) at EZK 27:6 and reads as quoted; the meaning of the unclear word, if noted above, is still unresolved.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Of fine linen with richly woven work from Egypt
Ezekiel.english_translation: Corresponding to linen, made with embroidered figures.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Translated literally; the sense of the opening word is not fully clear.

Ezekiel.english_translation: It is what is called in German *sigel*, and in our language *veile* [printed בווייל"א] in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this verse (Ezekiel 27:7) and glosses it “ta voile : en allemand *sigla* ; en français *veile*.”

Ezekiel.english_translation: To spread it on the cedar pole and to raise it on the mast; *nes* in the language of the Mishnah is *kilonos* [“pole”], and in Old French *perche* [printed פורקא].
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this verse (Ezekiel 27:7) with the form פירקא (*perche*) and glosses it “étendard, perche” (“standard, pole”).

Ezekiel.english_translation: For a tent and a roof over the whole ship.
Those who hold your oars to steer you.
Those who hold the steering board, to direct and straighten the ship.
Craftsmen of building, as it is said, “and Hiram’s builders and the Gebalites” (1 Kings 5:32).
Those who repair your leaks so that water not enter them — *[printed Old French: אפייטונ"ט טאקראוצ"א]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Their sailors.
They were around you, to sail to the faraway provinces to bring merchandise into you.
An expression of surety (*arevut*): it is all the needs of a person by which he lives; and a man’s money is his surety and his rescue for his life — *garantie* [printed גרנטיא"ה] in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this verse (Ezekiel 27:9) with the form גרנטיאה (*garantiah*) and glosses it “pour échanger ta marchandise ; la racine signifie garantie.”

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: The men of Arvad and Helech
Ezekiel.english_translation: And the rest of the force of men who dwell within you.

Targum Jonathan: “and also Cappadocians.” I heard in the name of Rabbi Menahem that because they descend in the sea to the deep, from the gates [measures] of *gomdei amot* of its depth, they are called *gamadim* — *[printed Old French: אנדוי"ש]* in Old French. And some interpret that they are dwarves, who enter into the measure of a cubit.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. The Aramaic is translated as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: They are quivers in which arrows are put, as in “Fill the quivers” (Jeremiah 21) — *[printed Old French: קויכרינ"ה]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. Printed “Jeremiah 21” is Jeremiah 51:11 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_translation: Many hangings upon hangings.
A sea whose name is Tarshish.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: by reason of the multitude of all kinds of riches
Ezekiel.english_translation: That was within you, and the merchants were confident that they would find in you merchandise suited to them.
*Estain* in Old French [printed אשטיי"ן].
Ezekiel.translator_note: Old French printed אשטיי"ן; it appears to be *estain* (“tin”), but was not found in Darmesteter.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Your strengtheners and your helpers, as in “and they restored Jerusalem even unto the broad wall” (Nehemiah 3:8); and a man’s money is his strength, that makes him stand on his feet.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Rashi reads *izevonayikh* as “your supporters”; JPS renders it “thy wares.”

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: they traded the persons of men
Ezekiel.english_translation: Male and female slaves, to sell.
Your place.
Horns of wild goats and bones of elephant; and *tavasim* [peacocks] — birds whose name is *paon* [printed פאו"ן] in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this verse (Ezekiel 27:15) with the form פאון (*paon*) and glosses it “oiseaux dont le nom est…” (“birds whose name is…”). Rashi takes *hovnim* as “peacocks”; JPS renders it “ebony.”

Ezekiel.english_translation: They brought you a gift.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: they traded for thy wares with carbuncles
Ezekiel.english_translation: With the precious stones mentioned in Scripture, and purple, and embroidery, and fine linen.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: by reason of the multitude of thy wealth
Ezekiel.english_translation: Because they knew that your leaders and your princes show them works of beauty and splendor for adornment.
*Escarboucle* [printed איקרבונקל"א] in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Old French printed איקרבונקל"א; it appears to be *escarboucle* (“carbuncle”), but was not found in Darmesteter.

Ezekiel.english_translation: The name of a place whose wheat is fine, as in “until thou come to Minnith” (Judges 18); and an aggadic midrash: fine and large wheat sold by count (*minyan*). And Jonathan translated “in wheat of *rechosh*” — an expression of a gathering of many counted things — *[printed Old French: טרוקא"ס]* in Old French. And his companion in the Pesikta: “Just as the blood is *rachush* in the leaves, so Leah was *rechusha* with sons”; and I did not know what it is. From the mouth of Rabbi Simeon I found that he found in Scripture the Jerusalemite Targum: “in wheat of Minnith,” *u-fanag dechushla ve-kalma*; “barley of *chushla*” — in the Gemara we learn “peeled barley.” And I say: *Minnith* is an expression of portions (*manot*), prepared food. And also according to the vocalization with a *dagesh*, it is Jonathan’s way to translate a word sometimes by its meaning and sometimes by its midrash; so he translated, and also the name of the city *HaMonah* — we vocalize there *vehamonah*, without a *mappik* in the *hei* — and he translated: “also there shall be cast down the slain of the city of many, *itragushteha*.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. The Aramaic phrases and the quotation from the Pesikta are translated or transliterated as printed; the sense of parts is not clear to the translator. Printed “Judges 18” is Judges 11:33 (JPS: “until thou come to Minnith”). The reference to *HaMonah* is Ezekiel 39:16.

Ezekiel.english_translation: I saw in the book of Joseph the Priest: the balsam tree is *panag*; and they were found in Jericho, and from the good fragrance Jericho was named — *balsame* [printed באלסמ"א] in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Old French printed באלסמ"א; it appears to be *balsame* (“balsam”), but was not found in Darmesteter.

Ezekiel.english_translation: White boiled wine; and Menahem connected it with “the fat of wheat” (Psalms 146) — an expression of goodness.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “Psalms 146” is Psalms 147:14 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_translation: And *omer* — the word *kevina*: on the day the lamb is born, and its mother cleans it with her licking, they make a covering and fasten it around him with hooks, so that his wool will be clean.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Aramaic words are transliterated as printed; the sense of the opening is not clear.

Ezekiel.english_translation: White, like “white asses” (Judges 5).
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “Judges 5” is Judges 5:10 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_translation: They are provinces.
Spun thread of *shirayin*.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The meaning of *shirayin* is not given by Rashi and the word is transliterated.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Made like lumps (*ashashiyot*) — *mass* [printed מש"ש] in Old French; and it is Indian iron.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this verse (Ezekiel 27:19) with forms such as משיץ (*masiç*) and glosses it “en lingots, en masses” (“in ingots, in masses”). The printed spelling differs from his.

Ezekiel.english_translation: In costly clothing, for chariots.
Lambs; and Jonathan translated “in bulls”; and so he translated “a hundred thousand rams (*karim*) of Mesha king of Moab” (2 Kings 3:4).
Ezekiel.translator_note: In 2 Kings 3:4 JPS renders *karim* “lambs”: “the wool of a hundred thousand lambs.”

Ezekiel.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “provinces of Assyria and Media.”
In things that are for adornment (*michlol*) — *parement* [printed פרמונ"ט] in Old French. And what are the *michlulim*? Cloaks of blue and embroidery — shawls of blue, embroidered.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this verse (Ezekiel 27:24) with the form פרמינט (*partment*) and glosses it “avec des ornements de toilette” (“with toilet ornaments”). The printed spelling differs slightly from his.

Ezekiel.english_translation: In splendid ornaments, which they store in coffers called *escrin* [printed אשקרי"ן] in Old French; and they are covered with leather and decorated for beauty with kinds of nails in rows and designs; and they are called in Aramaic *kamtrin* and in Hebrew *berumim*; and they are bound and tied with ropes of linen (*butz*) for beauty.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this verse (Ezekiel 27:24) with the form אשקרין (*escrin*) and glosses it “des boîtes qu’on nomme” (“boxes called…”).

Ezekiel.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “wood of myrtles.” Those coffers were placed in towers of myrtle wood, and they bring them into the towers, and the chests that are within them, and the ornaments that are within the chests, all together for merchandise; and thus is the interpretation of the language in brief: “and in chests (*gnazei berumim*) bound with cords” and “cedar-lined” within cedar wood, for the *berumim* are the *kamtrot*, and they were tied with cords and placed in towers of myrtle, which is one of the kinds of cedar. And the *michlulim* that are within the *berumim* Jonathan called *ve-kushfin d’arza be-imlin di zehorita* — ornaments needing proper guarding, *dimachtin bekomatrin* — placed in the chests. And the “towers” in the Targum, as we learn, “chest and tower” — *[printed Old French: שיפרייט"ש]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. The Aramaic phrases of Targum Jonathan are transliterated in part; the sense of parts is not clear to the translator. Audit 4: the Aramaic quotation was checked against Targum Jonathan/the Ketuvim Targum (Mikraot Gedolot, Sefaria) at EZK 27:24 and reads as quoted; the meaning of the unclear word, if noted above, is still unresolved.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Your *sharotayikh* were to you for a plain and a level ground; as the level ground is a trodden road to bring merchandise by it to a city that sits on dry land, so the ships of Tarshish were to you, in their place, a highway to bring your merchandise into you.
An expression of Sharon and level ground, and its like, “Go you up into her rows” (Jeremiah 5).
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “Jeremiah 5” is Jeremiah 5:10 (JPS wording quoted). Rashi takes *sharotayikh* as “level plains”; JPS renders “tribute.”

Ezekiel.english_translation: They brought into you a great load, and made your load heavier than was needed.

As is the way of the large ships, which they sail out into the open sea; and because you were filled and heavy, the east wind came and broke you in the heart of the seas. And as to the likeness of the city: because you were filled with wealth, your heart was lifted up, and punishment came upon you.
*Migrashot* — like the *migrashim* (open land) of the city.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Rashi takes *migrashot* as the open land around the city; JPS renders “the waves.”

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: They shall stand upon the land
Ezekiel.english_translation: What have we any more in the ships? Where shall we carry merchandise any more?

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: They shall roll themselves in the ashes
Ezekiel.english_translation: They will roll about.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: they shall take up a lamentation for thee
Ezekiel.english_translation: In their dirge.
So was the name of the chiefs of Edom, as in “The burden of Dumah” (Isaiah 21:11); and Targum Jonathan: “there is none like her.”
Like her likeness.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: When thy wares came forth out of the seas
Ezekiel.english_translation: All this they will lament over you in their dirge.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: They are troubled in their countenance
Ezekiel.english_translation: Their faces are indignant; and so, “to make her fret” (1 Samuel 1:6); and so every complaint is *tore’ameta*.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Aramaic word is transliterated as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: *Sibler* [printed שובלי"ר] in Old French; so they hiss at something that has passed and gone.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this verse (Ezekiel 27:36) with the form שיבליר (*sibler*) and glosses it “ils siffleront” (“they will hiss”).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I sit in the seat of God
Ezekiel.english_translation: He made for himself in the air over the sea, with devices, a kind of seven heavens, and sat upon the highest.

Nebuchadnezzar came to make Daniel a god: “and he worshipped Daniel, and an offering and sweet odours he commanded to pour out to him,” and he did not accept it upon himself; and you make yourself a god!
Ezekiel.translator_note: Rashi’s Aramaic follows Daniel 2:46 (JPS: “and worshipped Daniel, and commanded that they should offer an offering and sweet odours unto him”) and is translated as printed.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: no secret that they can hide from thee
Ezekiel.english_translation: “Nothing hidden from you” — they are *kantorin*, who *mekantrin*; that is, perhaps you are wise like Daniel, of whom it is said, “and no secret causeth thee trouble” (Daniel 6).
Ezekiel.translator_note: The words *kantorin* and *mekantrin* are transliterated; their sense is not clear. Printed “Daniel 6” is Daniel 4:6 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_translation: You acquired possessions for yourself.
And you gathered [Aramaic].

As it sounds. And an aggadic midrash: pederasty, for he was used as women. Three made themselves a god and were used as women: Joash son of Ahaziah, as it is said (2 Chronicles 24), “So they executed judgment upon Joash,” and Hiram, and Nebuchadnezzar.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Rashi’s wording reads the verse as “they made Joash into those judged [abused]”; JPS reads “they executed judgment upon Joash.” The reference is 2 Chronicles 24:24.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Your *hofa’atekha* — an expression of beauty of countenance; and the Midrash expounds it as “the beauty of your time (*yofi itekha*).”
Like “your slayer.”
You are he who is full of wisdom to seal and to stamp every pattern and form.
*Peinture* [printed פיינטור"א] in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Old French printed פיינטור"א; it appears to be *peinture* (“painting”), but was not found in Darmesteter.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: thou wast in Eden the garden of God
Ezekiel.english_translation: With much goodness and delights you are delighted, as if in Eden, the garden of HaShem, you dwell; all wealth, treasures and honor are given to you; all good stones are arranged on your garment.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Aramaic of the Targum is translated as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Your canopy (*chuppatekha*); another version: the garment, your covering.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the workmanship of thy settings and of thy sockets was in thee
Ezekiel.english_translation: Although I gave you this honor, I knew that you would be proud, and I made in you the work of drums and holes, which send out breath with a sound of song, like a drum; and by these you should have understood.

You are the bird of measure — that is, the great bird that covers with its wings a great covering, that is, rules a great dominion. *Mimshach* is an expression of greatness, as in “men of measure” (Numbers 14), which we translate (Aramaic) “*gavrei demeshachan*.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “Numbers 14” is Numbers 13:32, where JPS reads “men of great stature.”

Ezekiel.english_translation: And I gave you a place to acquire there for yourself, in the building of My holy mountain, for you assisted Solomon with cedar wood.
You acquired for yourself a remembrance among the kings of Israel, who are like the ministering angels.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: till unrighteousness was found in thee
Ezekiel.english_translation: In your saying, “I am a god.”
Like *male’u*.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: have I cast thee as profane out of the mountain of God
Ezekiel.english_translation: You caused that I should wipe you out, so that you would no more be accounted righteous in the building of My House.
Like *va’a’abedkha*.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: from the midst of the stones of fire
Ezekiel.english_translation: That you not take a share with the righteous. And our Rabbis, in an aggadic midrash, expounded this matter concerning the first man, and thus the prophet said to Hiram: Why were you proud of your firmament? Were you perhaps in the Garden of Eden, as the first man was? “Every precious stone,” etc. — for all these canopies I made for the first man, and the lowest of them all is gold, which is counted last. “The workmanship of thy settings,” etc.: In this I compared you to him, and not in another; and in you I looked, and I created drums and holes in the first man. “Thou wast the far-covering cherub”: Perhaps you are like that cherub who was great in the span of the covering, all of it from one end of the heavens to the other end of the heavens? And perhaps I placed you on holy mountains, as I placed him?

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: thou hast corrupted thy wisdom by reason of thy brightness
Ezekiel.english_translation: That you were proud of your brightness.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: that they may gaze upon thee
Ezekiel.english_translation: To look upon your shame; *lir’avah* is like *lir’iyah*.
Your holiness.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: a fire from the midst of thee
Ezekiel.english_translation: Words of pride that came out of your mouth, saying, “I am a god.” Another version: as its Targum: “And I will bring mighty nations like fire because of the sins of your insolence.”
They were astonished.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the wounded shall fall in the midst of her
Ezekiel.english_translation: Because they will see the sword round about outside, the inhabitants of the city will fall and will be certain to be slain within her.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: fall in the midst of her
Ezekiel.english_translation: Like “I had not thought” (Genesis 48) — “I had not reckoned”; and like “Even our enemies themselves being judges” (Deuteronomy 32:31) — they will judge themselves to be slain within her.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 48” is Genesis 48:11 (JPS: “I had not thought to see thy face”).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: no more a pricking brier unto the house of Israel
Ezekiel.english_translation: Because He prophesied about Ammon and Moab and Philistia and Edom and Tyre and Sidon, who are the neighbors of the Land of Israel, that they would be destroyed; and since all of them will perish, there will be no brier or thorn for Israel in all their surroundings to hurt them and to harm them.
A kind of nettles and thorns.
A matter of causing pain, as in “a malignant leprosy” (Leviticus 13:51) — *poignant* [printed פוניינ"ט] in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this verse (Ezekiel 28:24) with the form פוייניינט (*poynyant*) and glosses it “piquante” (“pricking”).

Ezekiel.english_translation: Those who despise them.
As He gave it to Jacob as an inheritance without boundaries: “and thou shalt spread abroad to the west, and to the east, and to the north, and to the south” (Genesis 28:14).
