Because all the greatness of Egypt and all the plenty in it is by means of the rivers of the Nile, therefore the prophet likens its king to a *tannin* and its people to the fish of the river.
I do not need the upper [waters], for I have my river, sufficient for all my needs.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I have made it for myself
Ezekiel.english_translation: By my might and my wisdom I increased my greatness and my dominion.
Like iron rings — *[printed Old French: איינ"ש]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: *[printed Old French: אינטישאיקראטי"ש]* in Old French; that is: I will put into the heart of all your mighty men to go out with you to war, and they will all fall.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I will cast thee into the wilderness
Ezekiel.english_translation: This is the destruction of fish: once they are cast upon the dry land, they die — *[printed Old French: א"י אטינדר"י טו"י]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: How many times they relied on them, in the days of Sennacherib and in the days of Nebuchadnezzar, and it did not help them — with this reed, which is soft and does not support the one who leans on it.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: When they take hold of thee with the hand
Ezekiel.english_translation: “*Bakaf*” (with the hand) is the form as read (*qere*) — like a man who walks and leans on his staff.
You will be crushed.
Their shoulders — like a man who leans on a reed, and it breaks, and the man falls upon it, and the splinters enter his shoulders.
Ezekiel.translator_note: “Splinters” renders *kromiyot*; the sense is not certain.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: makest all their loins to be at a stand
Ezekiel.english_translation: Since you will break, they will need to strengthen their loins and to stand upon them; and behold, you are like a man whose companion leans on him, and he is weak, and says to him: Strengthen yourself on your loins, for you shall no more lean on me. And so Targum Jonathan: “and there shall not be for them a [house of] support.” And some interchange “*ve-he’emadta lahem*” for “*vehama’adta*” [“and thou makest slip”], and I do not see their words; and Menahem connected it with “*ma’amad raglayim kamoni*” [“a standing of feet like me”].
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Aramaic and the closing quotation are translated as printed; the sense of the Aramaic is not fully clear.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: neither shall it be inhabited forty years
Ezekiel.english_translation: Forty-two years of famine were decreed in Pharaoh’s dream, corresponding to the three times that the dream is written: “seven kine and seven ears, lean” (Genesis 41:20); he saw it and told it to Joseph — behold, twice; and Joseph said to him, “the seven kine, the empty and the lean, and the seven ears, the empty” (ibid.) — behold, forty-two for the famine; and they had only two, as it is said, “For these two years hath the famine been in the land” (ibid. 45); and from when Jacob went down to Egypt the famine ceased, for in the third year they sowed, as it is said, “and give us seed, that we may live” etc. (ibid. 47); and the forty were exacted from them now.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Rashi’s wording of the dream paraphrases Genesis 41 (see 41:3–4, 41:19–20, 41:27); “ibid.” is 41:27; “ibid. 45” is Genesis 45:6; “ibid. 47” is Genesis 47:19 (JPS wording quoted where it matches).

Ezekiel.english_translation: *Sera* [printed שר"א] *[printed Old French: אשיגיא"ה]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: *Megoratam* [their dwelling]; another version: like *toledotam* [their origin]; and so Menahem connected it.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: no more rule over the nations
Ezekiel.english_translation: An expression of dominion, as in “and have dominion over the fish of the sea” (there, 1).
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed reference is Genesis 1:28 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: no more the confidence of the house of Israel
Ezekiel.english_translation: Egypt will no longer be a confidence for the house of Israel, reminding them of iniquity, for the Holy One, blessed be He, said to them, “you shall see them again no more” (Exodus 14:13).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: in the seven and twentieth year
Ezekiel.english_translation: Of the reign of Nebuchadnezzar; in that year Egypt was given into his hand. So we learned in *Seder Olam*. And in this book there are many prophecies written out of order, earlier and later.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: caused his army to serve a great service
Ezekiel.english_translation: A great service against Tyre.
The men of his troops.

As is the way of those who besiege a city for many days, laboring and wearied by carrying loads of wood and stones; and he captured Tyre in the twenty-third year of his reign, as we find in *Seder Olam*. *Mukrach* — *[printed Old French: קאלב"ו]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: *Pelée* [printed פלי"אה] in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Old French printed פלי"אה; it appears to be *pelée* (“peeled”), but was not found in Darmesteter.

Ezekiel.english_translation: After they had plundered its spoil, the sea rose and swept it away from them, because it had been decreed that it and its spoil would perish in the sea.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: as his hire for which he served
Ezekiel.english_translation: As wages for the work that he performed at My command at Tyre, I will give him the land of Egypt.
Egypt, evil in their staff, for they promised My people their help — vanity.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: cause a horn to shoot up
Ezekiel.english_translation: I did not hear, and I did not find, the interpretation of this verse: what is the sprouting of the horn of Israel in the downfall of Egypt, since Israel went into exile eight years before the downfall of Egypt? And I say that “in that day” refers to the passage above, “At the end of forty years will I gather the Egyptians,” and that reckoning ended in the year that Belshazzar reigned. And we find in Daniel that in that year the kings of Persia began to grow strong and a downfall was decreed upon Babylon, as it is said (Daniel 7:1), “In the first year of Belshazzar … Daniel had a dream and visions” etc.; “The first was like a lion” (ibid.) is Babylon; and it is written (ibid.), “I beheld till the wings thereof were plucked off” etc.; and “behold another beast, a second, like to a bear” is Persia; and it is written, “and thus they said to it, Arise, devour much flesh” — that is, seize the kingship. And the kingdom of Persia is the sprouting of a horn for Israel, as it is said of Cyrus, “He shall build My city, and he shall let Mine exiles go free” (Isaiah 45:13). And how do we know that the forty years of Egypt ended at that time? Egypt was given into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar in the twenty-seventh year of Nebuchadnezzar, in the year in which this prophecy was spoken to Ezekiel; add forty years: behold, sixty-seven. Account for them: forty-five for Nebuchadnezzar and twenty-three for Evil-merodach, as we say in tractate Megillah; and one year of them was counted for this one and that one, as we say there: they were broken [partial] years.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Aramaic quotations from Daniel 7 are translated as printed and set beside the JPS wording of Daniel 7:1, 7:4 and 7:5. “Account for them” renders *tze mehem* (literally, “go out from them”).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I will give thee the opening of the mouth in the midst of them
Ezekiel.english_translation: To you, Ezekiel, there will be an opening of the mouth when they see your prophecy fulfilled.
Like *ahah*: Alas for the day that is destined to come upon those idolaters.
Aramaic: “The time of the breaking of the nations.”
An expression of trembling: when they hear of the downfall of Egypt, they will tremble for their lives, lest the king of Babylon come up against them.
Targum Jonathan: “and all the supporters”; all the guarantors, the surety of Egypt — *garantie* [printed גרנסי"אה] in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this verse (Ezekiel 30:5) with the form גרנטיאה (*garantiah*) and glosses it “tous les alliés, ceux qui s’engagent (avec l’Égypte)” (“all the allies, those who pledge themselves with Egypt”). The printed spelling differs slightly from his.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the children of the land that is in league
Ezekiel.english_translation: Those who made a covenant with Egypt to help her.
My wrath is like fire.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: shall messengers go forth from before Me
Ezekiel.english_translation: Troops of armies going on My mission in many convoys, to terrify Ethiopia, which dwells in security.
Like “but ships shall come from the coast of Kittim” (Numbers 24:24); and so Jonathan translated it: *belegyonin* [“with legions”].

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I will make the rivers dry
Ezekiel.english_translation: The land of the rivers is Egypt.
As its Targum: *ve-imsar* [“and I will deliver”].
Alexandria.
Its wall will be breached.
Adversaries will come upon it day after day.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: these cities shall go into captivity
Ezekiel.english_translation: Both provinces — Aven and Pi-beseth.
The light will be withheld.
Trouble will come upon her and cover her, and she will be darkened like a day covered by a cloud.
*Ve-chafranha* [“and her villages”].
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Aramaic is transliterated and translated as printed.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I have broken the arm of Pharaoh king of Egypt
Ezekiel.english_translation: Already another time I gave his army into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim, as is said in the book (Jeremiah 46:2): “Of Egypt: concerning the army of Pharaoh-neco king of Egypt, which was by the river Euphrates in Carchemish, which Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon smote,” etc.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: it hath not been bound up to be healed
Ezekiel.english_translation: From that day onward, as is said in the book of Kings (2 Kings 24:7) at its end: “And the king of Egypt came not again any more out of his land; for the king of Babylon had taken, from the Brook of Egypt unto the river Euphrates.” And in this style Jeremiah too prophesied about that same blow, in the language of “no healing,” as it is said (Jeremiah 46:11): “Go up into Gilead, and take balm, O virgin daughter of Egypt; In vain dost thou use many medicines; There is no cure for thee.”
An expression of binding, as one binds a broken bone.
The work of garments and a bandage, as in (above, 16) “nor swaddled at all.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “above, 16” is Ezekiel 16:4 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_translation: That he might still have strength to fight.
I will break the second, and both of them will be broken; that is, the king of Babylon has already taken from one side; further, I will deliver to him all the rest of the kingdom.
An expression of strength.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I will hold up the arms
Ezekiel.english_translation: An expression of grasping, that one holds in his hand for support so that it not fall; and its end will prove it: “and the arms of Pharaoh shall fall down,” for He does not hold them.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Whom art thou like in thy greatness
Ezekiel.english_translation: In your becoming great before Me, to whom did you think to liken yourself?
Whom I already felled.
Was.
A forest providing great shade.
Trees of freshness.
*Cime* [printed צימ"א] in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this form (צימא) for Ezekiel 31:3 and glosses it “sa cime” (“its top”).

Ezekiel.english_translation: *Fossés* [printed פושיץ] in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this verse (Ezekiel 31:4) with the form פושיץ (*foséç*) and glosses it “ses fosses” (“its channels”).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Unto all the trees of the field
Ezekiel.english_translation: To water them; and the illustration is as the Targum of Jonathan: “Behold, Assyria is like a cedar in Lebanon,” etc., like a pillar.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Aramaic quotation and its final word are translated as printed; the sense of the last word is not certain.

Ezekiel.english_translation: “With many peoples, with supporters, he strengthened the kings whom he made subject under his kingdom, and his governors he appointed over all the provinces of the earth.” And an aggadic midrash: “And among the thick boughs was its top” — from where did it merit greatness? Because it held back from the counsel of the Generation of the Dispersion, as it is said (Genesis 7), “Out of that land went forth Asshur”; when all who came into the world were made one braid, to come with counsel to rebel against Him, then its top was seen by itself and was not drawn along with them. “The waters nourished it; the deep made it to grow”: and because it hearkened to the voice of Jonah son of Amittai, who descended to the deep, and the men of Nineveh turned “from the violence that is in their hands.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 7” is Genesis 10:11 (JPS wording quoted). The final quotation is from Jonah 3:8 (JPS wording).

Ezekiel.english_translation: His branches.
His tendrils.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Because of the multitude of waters, when it shot them forth
Ezekiel.english_translation: “His branches” through many waters, in its shooting forth its branches — that is, in the growing of its branches; and an expression of sending falls upon them, as in “and shot forth sprigs” (above, 16).
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “above, 16” is Ezekiel 17:6 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_translation: In its branches.
An expression of a nest.
An expression of beauty.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: In the length of its branches
Ezekiel.english_translation: These too are an expression of branches stretched out lengthwise to every side, like the tendrils of the vineyard — *[printed Old French: שישטרוי"ילאש]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: They did not dim its appearance; that is, there was not among them one more beautiful than it.
That is, in the whole world.
*Chastaigniers* [printed קאשטיני"ש] in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this verse (Ezekiel 31:8) with the form קאשטיניש (*kastinijjers*) and glosses it “et les châtaigniers” (“and the chestnut trees”). Rashi takes *armonim* as chestnuts; JPS renders “plane-trees.”

Ezekiel.english_translation: That is, all the splendid kings.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Because thou art exalted in stature
Ezekiel.english_translation: Thus I said to Assyria.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: into the hand of the mighty one of the nations
Ezekiel.english_translation: Into the hard hand among the nations; into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar I gave him; for the Master said: In the first year he captured Nineveh.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: he shall surely deal with him
Ezekiel.english_translation: Nebuchadnezzar, according to all My will.
And they will fell him to the ground, as in “and let them fall by the camp” (Numbers 11:31).
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed reference is Numbers 11:31 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_translation: As its Targum: “upon the fall of his slain.”

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: none of all the trees by the waters
Ezekiel.english_translation: That they are soft and weak, only that their branches are soft and long because of the moisture of the water; they should not liken themselves to the cedars of Eden — that is, he [Assyria] should not have been proud over Israel, and they [the nations] shall not stand over them.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The sentence is translated literally; the bracketed identifications are the translator’s reading of the context.

Ezekiel.english_translation: They shall not be proud so as to equate their might — a drinker of water — with the trees of thick boughs.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: In the day when he went down to the nether-world
Ezekiel.english_translation: When I abased the king of Assyria into the hand of his enemy.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I caused the deep to mourn
Ezekiel.english_translation: Many mourners who were dependent on him.

I covered for his sake the deep, which was accustomed to water him and to make him great, as He said above, “the deep made it to grow”; on that day I covered it so that it not rise and extinguish his burning; that is, I weakened his helpers.
Which were flowing round about his planting.
Which made [its] branches long, as He said above, “and its branches became long because of many waters.”

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I caused Lebanon to mourn for him
Ezekiel.english_translation: For his sake — Lebanon.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I caused Lebanon to mourn for him
Ezekiel.english_translation: An expression of blackness.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: all the trees of the field fainted
Ezekiel.english_translation: For his channels were sent to them, as He said above.
For his sake their moisture ceased, like a person who faints and his spirit flies away — *pasmer* [printed פשמי"ר] in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this word (Ezekiel 31, *alfah*) with the form פשמיר (*pasmer*) and glosses it “se pâmeront” (“they will swoon”). His reference in the scan appears as verse 13.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: were comforted in the nether parts of the earth
Ezekiel.english_translation: The other descendants into Gehinnom received consolation; they said: This one too is like us.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: they that were in his arm
Ezekiel.english_translation: And his helpers, who dwelt in his shadow.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: To whom art thou thus like
Ezekiel.english_translation: You, Pharaoh — to which of the trees of Eden did you liken yourself, that you be as great as Assyria in honor and size? And behold, you saw that I brought him down to Sheol; you too will be brought down with the trees of Eden, with the other mighty kings.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: unto the nether parts of the earth
Ezekiel.english_translation: Gehinnom.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: a young lion of the nations
Ezekiel.english_translation: You should have rested inside your river, as is the way of fish, and not gone out onto the dry land; and you grew proud in your heart, and imagined yourself a young lion that rules on the dry land and goes out to seize prey.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: thou didst gush forth with thy rivers
Ezekiel.english_translation: You went out abroad with your rivers; an expression of “Thou art He that took me out (*gochi*) of the womb” (Psalms 26), “though the Jordan rush forth (*yagiach*)” (Job 41), and “the liers-in-wait of Israel broke forth (*megiach*) out of their place” (Judges 20:33) — an expression of something that touches and goes out from a hidden house.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “Psalms 26” is Psalms 22:10 and “Job 41” is Job 40:23 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_translation: An expression of muddying.

You had no feet, and you made yourself feet like the beasts of the land, to cross the waters of lands and to trample their rivers. And the illustration is in Targum Jonathan: “and you waged war with your host, and made nations quake with your supporters, and destroyed their province.”
An expression of a net; and there are many in Scripture: “they catch them in their net” (Habakkuk 1:15); “snares and nets” (Ecclesiastes 7).
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “Ecclesiastes 7” is 7:26 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: fill the valleys with thy foulness
Ezekiel.english_translation: I cast you down like “hath He thrown (*ramah*) into the sea” (Exodus 15:1); and some say *ramotekha* is an expression of a worm (*rimmah*), as in “and it bred worms, and rotted” (ibid. 16).
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “ibid. 16” is Exodus 16:20 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_translation: The land in which you float on the surface of the waters of your river, as in “Waters flowed over my head” (Lamentations 3:54) and “and made the iron to swim” (2 Kings 7): that land I will water with your blood.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “2 Kings 7” is 2 Kings 6:6 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_translation: *[printed Old French: טונפרוט"מנט]* in Old French; “to the mountains” — to the high mountains in it.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: *Rivières* [printed ראויר"ש] in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this verse (Ezekiel 32:6) with the form ריוורש (*riwjjers*) and glosses it “et les rivières” (“and the rivers”). The printed spelling differs slightly from his.

Ezekiel.english_translation: When your burning is extinguished, the smoke will rise and cover the heavens and darken the lights; that is, all who hear your report will mourn and be astonished, for every man will worry for his life, saying: Upon us too the destroyer will stand.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: All the bright lights of heaven
Ezekiel.english_translation: The heavenly princes, your advocates.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I will also vex the hearts of many peoples
Ezekiel.english_translation: That is, their heart will be agitated and tremble.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: when I shall bring thy destruction among the nations
Ezekiel.english_translation: “When I bring the broken ones of your battle among the nations.”

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: make many peoples appalled at thee
Ezekiel.english_translation: An expression of astonishment.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: when I shall brandish My sword before them
Ezekiel.english_translation: An expression of a flying bird: when I send against you forces, My messengers, through their land.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: they shall tremble at every moment
Ezekiel.english_translation: At the breakings, lest the breaking come upon them too. Another version: an actual expression of “moment”; so Menahem connected it.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: every man for his own life
Ezekiel.english_translation: Each one for himself — *[printed Old French: שויימ"אימאש]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Of the other provinces, whose waters you used to muddy.
So that the foot of cattle will not muddy them, and the mud will settle, and the waters will be clear and clean like refined oil.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: destitute of that whereof it was full
Ezekiel.english_translation: A land that is now full of all good.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: wail for the multitude of Egypt
Ezekiel.english_translation: Weep and lament.
Prophesy about it and about all the deniers of prophecy who descended to the pit of destruction; here the Holy One, blessed be He, showed Ezekiel that all the deniers of prophecy descend to Gehinnom.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Whom dost thou pass in beauty
Ezekiel.english_translation: Are you more pleasant than the other idolaters? You too, go down to the pit, and lie with them.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: she is delivered to the sword
Ezekiel.english_translation: Egypt has been given to the sword.
They will speak about him and about his helpers.

He transposed the verse and expounded it: “They shall speak of him, with his helpers”; that is, also about his helpers together with him will the mighty ones in Sheol speak, and so they will say about them, “they are gone down, they lie still, the uncircumcised,” etc. Every *lo*, *li*, *lahem*, *lekha* that is adjacent to speaking is only an expression of “about.”
In Gehinnom.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: their graves are round about them
Ezekiel.english_translation: In the midst of Sheol his graves are prepared, for from there he will not go out to rest in his grave.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the uttermost parts of the pit
Ezekiel.english_translation: In the depths of the pit, in the midst of its depth.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: her company is round about her grave
Ezekiel.english_translation: In the midst of Sheol, around her burial.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: who caused terror in the land of the living
Ezekiel.english_translation: Who inflicted breaking in the Land of Israel.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Rashi’s gloss reads *shever* (“breaking”) for *chittit* (“terror”).

Ezekiel.english_translation: To Elam.
Like “the slain of.”

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: shall not lie with the mighty
Ezekiel.english_translation: These who are mentioned [shall not lie] with the mighty who died a natural death, for the fallen are inferior to the idolaters who died a natural death and went down to Sheol with their weapons of war.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: whose swords are laid under their heads
Ezekiel.english_translation: Their buriers placed their swords under their heads as a sign, to make known that no sword ruled over them.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: whose iniquities are upon their bones
Ezekiel.english_translation: Nothing was lacking of their iniquity, for the sword of slaying did not atone for them, since they were not slain; and what is the iniquity? That the terror of those mighty ones was in the land of the living.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: But thou, in the midst of the uncircumcised shalt thou be broken
Ezekiel.english_translation: He is speaking to Pharaoh.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: with them that are slain by the sword
Ezekiel.english_translation: And not with those who died a natural death.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: ashamed for all the terror which they caused by their might
Ezekiel.english_translation: “In their breaking, from their might they are ashamed.”

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: For I have put My terror in the land of the living
Ezekiel.english_translation: “My terror in the land of the living” — for I will place My fear in the Land of Israel, and the terror of man will no more be placed in it.
*Badeta* [printed באדי"טא] in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this word (the scan reads “XXXIII, 22”; our verse is 33:2) with the form בדיטא (*badete*) and glosses it “en sentinelle” (“as sentinel”). The printed spelling differs slightly from his.

Ezekiel.english_translation: They are the troops.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: his blood shall be upon his own head
Ezekiel.english_translation: The guilt of his death will be required from his own hand, for he sinned against himself.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: he would have delivered his soul
Ezekiel.english_translation: If he had taken warning, he would have escaped.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I have set thee a watchman
Ezekiel.english_translation: As that watchman who is placed to warn so that a soul not be lost, so I have set you to warn Israel.
Therefore you do not wish to repent; you think that repentance will not avail you.
By his righteousness.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: none of his righteous deeds shall be remembered
Ezekiel.english_translation: To save him from being punished for this transgression.
A pledge that I commanded to return at sunset.
For their sake he will be punished.

As He said at the beginning of the book (above, 3), “and thou shalt be dumb, and shalt not be to them a reprover,” and afterward He said to him (above, 24): “In that day when I take from them their stronghold … he that escapeth shall come unto thee … In that day shall thy mouth be opened together with him that is escaped, and thou shalt speak, and be no more dumb.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “above, 3” is Ezekiel 3:26 and “above, 24” is Ezekiel 24:25–27; Rashi’s wording is a paraphrase, with the JPS wording used for the quoted fragments.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: against his coming to me in the morning
Ezekiel.english_translation: That is, “ere his coming to me in the morning,” as “before his coming to me in the morning.”

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Abraham was one, and he inherited the land
Ezekiel.english_translation: This is one of four things that Rabbi Akiva used to expound and that Rabbi Simeon ben Yochai, his disciple, does not expound like him; and thus Rabbi Simeon used to expound it: Abraham, who was commanded concerning only one commandment, inherited the land; we, who were commanded concerning many commandments, all the more so is the land given to us for an inheritance — that is what the prophet answers them.

“And shall you possess the land?” — in astonishment. If you were commanded, you do not keep it. “You eat with the blood”: you eat delicacies [obtained] through murder, for they kill owners of property and take their money.
That is, all your confidence — you strengthened yourselves upon your sword.
Pederasty.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: they that are in the waste places
Ezekiel.english_translation: In the fortified cities that are destined to become ruins.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: in the strongholds and in the caves
Ezekiel.english_translation: In a hiding place, to hide from the sword — I will send pestilence among them.
They mock you.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: sit before thee as My people
Ezekiel.english_translation: As if they were My people.
Laughter, like *ugav* [“pipe”].
Their robbery.
“And behold, you are to them like the song of pipes.”
The evil upon them.
For truth is ready to come; then they will know that your words were not a jest, for a true prophet was among them.
Concerning the leaders of Israel.
They were delighting themselves with the money of their fellows who were under them.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: should not the shepherds feed the sheep
Ezekiel.english_translation: Is it not the rule for shepherds to feed the flock, and not to feed themselves?
The thin, who lack strength — *doloroses* [printed דולרושי"אש] in Old French — who need strengthening, to be supported by hand.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Old French *doloroses* (“the weak,” Darmesteter: “les faibles”): Darmesteter lists Ezekiel 34:4 with the form דולורושש and his index gives *dolorosés*; the printed spelling differs slightly from his.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: bound up that which was broken
Ezekiel.english_translation: To bind the fractures of the bone to one another, according to the practice of physicians.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: brought back that which was driven away
Ezekiel.english_translation: That was driven out of the flock to the outside.
You chastised.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: My sheep wandered through all the mountains
Ezekiel.english_translation: They go astray over all the mountains; that is, they became ownerless, each to do as he wishes, and you did not rebuke them, and you did not judge between a man and his fellow.
“And the shepherds fed them” — themselves.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Rashi’s citation reads the verse’s object as “them”; he explains that it means themselves.

Ezekiel.english_translation: “Neither shall the shepherds feed them any more” — themselves.
*U-vikkarti-m* (“and I will seek them out”) — an expression of visiting the sick.
When they are scattered, and he goes among them and gathers them together.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the day of clouds and thick darkness
Ezekiel.english_translation: For so is the way of sheep, to scatter on a cloudy day.
The one that pushes and shoves its companions.
Between those who have fists [the strong] and the weak.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Seemeth it a small thing unto you
Ezekiel.english_translation: That the strong among you graze the good pasture — would that you did not trample the remainder with your feet, and the rest of My sheep would eat them; but you trample even the remainder of your pasture with your feet; and it is not enough for you that you drink water of a drinking-place, but you foul the remaining ones with your feet.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Hebrew is translated as printed; the clause “and the rest of My sheep would eat them” is awkward in the printed text.

Ezekiel.english_translation: The clear waters whose mud has settled and which have not been muddied by feet. And the illustration is as its Targum: “Is it too little for you that you are sustained with good sustenance, and the remainder of your sustenance you tread with your feet, and you drink clear drink, and the remainder you tread with your feet?”

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: they eat that which you have trodden
Ezekiel.english_translation: “And My people eat the remainder of food that [printed *shemashikhon*], and the remainder of drink that [printed *shemashikhon*] they drink.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Aramaic word printed *shemashikhon* is not clear to me and is left untranslated; the sense is evidently what is left over by the shepherds.

Ezekiel.english_translation: “*Beriyah*” — strong.
*Maigre* [printed מייגר"א] in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: It appears to be *maigre* (“lean”), but the form was not found in Darmesteter.

Ezekiel.english_translation: A king from his seed.
Targum Jonathan: “and they shall journey in the forest”; and one may interpret it as an expression of sleep.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: make them and the places round about My hill
Ezekiel.english_translation: Its giving shall be in blessing; *ve-natati* is like *ve-hishkanti* (“and I will cause to dwell”).
A permanence, that it be for an eternal name.
Hidden away by hunger, because of the shame of hunger and poverty.
You are not like the beasts in My eyes.

And you will be brought low, like “And I will pour down the stones thereof into the valley” (Micah 1:6); for they used to hand them over to their enemies when they fled by way of their land. And this is what is said (Obadiah 1:14): “Neither shouldest thou have stood in the crossway.”
At the time when I delivered them into the hand of the enemy.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the time of the iniquity of the end
Ezekiel.english_translation: When the end of their iniquity was completed and their measure was filled.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I will prepare thee unto blood
Ezekiel.english_translation: Falling by the sword.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: thou hast hated thine own blood
Ezekiel.english_translation: You despised the birthright, whose service was entrusted to them, and you hated to defile yourself with the blood of the offerings of My service; and the defilement of the blood of the slain will pursue you. Some say: you fear murderers like all other men, and murderers will pursue you. And some say: “Thou hast hated the blood of thy brother,” which is your flesh and your blood.

Not as I said to Egypt (above, 29), “and I will turn the captivity of Egypt,” and “I will bring back the captivity of the children of Ammon” (Jeremiah 49:6). And this is what is said (Malachi 1:3): “and made his mountains a desolation” — for they are destined to be desolate forever.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “above, 29” is Ezekiel 29:14 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_translation: Israel and Judah. And an aggadic midrash — Rabbi Tanhuma expounds it: because Esau went to Ishmael to ally himself with him by marriage, to rouse him against Isaac regarding Abraham’s inheritance, so that Ishmael would kill Isaac, “and I shall be the avenger of blood and kill Ishmael.” And this is [the meaning of] “Let the days of mourning for my father be at hand” (Genesis 27:41) — “and I will inherit Isaac and Ishmael.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: The words “and I shall be the avenger of blood and kill Ishmael” and “and I will inherit Isaac and Ishmael” are the midrash’s expansion and are not in JPS Genesis 27:41.

Ezekiel.english_translation: He knows your thoughts.
According to that anger which you showed toward Israel I will do to you.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I will make Myself known among them
Ezekiel.english_translation: When I judge you, then they will recognize My might.
*Ve-ha‘tartem* — you multiplied; and so “and a thick cloud of incense went up” (above, 8) is an expression of multiplication.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “above, 8” is Ezekiel 8:11 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_translation: When I take My kingship, for then the earth will rejoice, as it is said, “The LORD reigneth; let the earth rejoice” (Psalms 96). Then I will make you desolate.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “Psalms 96” is Psalms 97:1 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_translation: Joy.
The Land of Israel, which is the height and the beauty of the world.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: swallowed you up on every side
Ezekiel.english_translation: Your neighbors were astonished and amazed, keeping silent and watching for the end of your destruction, and panting, and longing, and hoping that you would become an inheritance for the rest of the nations.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: taken up in the lips of talkers
Ezekiel.english_translation: And now, at your destruction, everyone speaks and murmurs about you, saying: “Aha, behold, they are desolate.”

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the evil report of the people
Ezekiel.english_translation: *Parlement* [printed פארלמנ"ט] in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists the form פרלמנט (*parlement*) in this section of Ezekiel; the gloss is not legible in the scan used. The printed spelling differs slightly from his.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: to cast it out for a prey
Ezekiel.english_translation: Because they saw it cast out for plunder, that it was thrown to spoil.
To drive out your inhabitants from within you is called bereavement.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Thou land art a devourer of men
Ezekiel.english_translation: This land is accustomed to destroy its inhabitants: the Amorites perished in it, and the Jews perished in it.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: as the uncleanness of a woman in her impurity
Ezekiel.english_translation: Scripture likened it to a menstruant woman, whose husband waits for the time she will be purified and longs to return to her.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: when they came unto the nations
Ezekiel.english_translation: Since it said “house of Israel” at the beginning of the section, it reads the whole section in the singular. And an aggadic midrash: the Holy One, blessed be He, came with them into exile and inclined His ear to what they were saying: “Do these come as captives? Behold, these are the people of HaShem!” — and He had no power to save them. (In Midrash Lamentations Rabbah.)
Ezekiel.translator_note: Rashi’s lemma reads the verb as singular (*va-yavo*), as explained in his comment. The midrash’s Hebrew phrase translated as “Do these come as captives?” is not fully clear and the rendering is uncertain.

Ezekiel.english_translation: They lowered My honor. And what is the profanation? That their enemies said of them, “These are the people of HaShem, and from His land they went forth” — and He had no power in His hand to save His people and His land.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I do not this for your sake
Ezekiel.english_translation: The salvation with which I shall save you.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I will sanctify My great name
Ezekiel.english_translation: And what is the sanctification? “And I will take you from among the nations.”
I will atone for you and remove your uncleannesses by sprinkling the waters of the sin-offering, which remove the uncleanness of the dead.
An inclination that has been renewed for good.
*Demonier* [printed דמוניי"ר] in Old French: you will waste away within yourselves in your shame, over the evil recompense you rendered before Me, while I render good to you.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this verse (Ezekiel 36:31) with the form דמוניר (*demonir*) and glosses it “et vous vous épuiserez” (“and you will exhaust yourselves”). The printed spelling differs slightly from his.

Ezekiel.english_translation: The land that was desolate until now will be worked and sown.
Now it has been turned into a garden of Eden.
For many days now they have dwelt fortified.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I will yet for this be inquired of
Ezekiel.english_translation: I will be entreated by them through their prayer, when they seek Me concerning this.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I will increase them with men like a flock
Ezekiel.english_translation: Men like a flock in abundance.

Which comes to Jerusalem at the festivals — the Passovers. Another explanation, as its Targum: “I will increase them with men, and I will make them prosper with cattle” — that is, that their iniquities will not be remembered against them.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: The hand of the LORD was upon me
Ezekiel.english_translation: Every “hand of HaShem” in prophecy is an expression of compulsion: the spirit compelled him to go, like one driven mad, to the place where the spirit desired.

Our Rabbis said that they were of the tribe of Ephraim, who went out of Egypt before the end [appointed time], and the men of Gath, who were born in the land, killed them, as stated in the Book of Chronicles.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: caused me to pass by them round about
Ezekiel.english_translation: Around the valley, but they did not bring him into it because he was a priest.
Does it seem in your eyes that they are able to live?

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I will lay sinews upon you
Ezekiel.english_translation: But in the Book of Job he says, “Thou hast clothed me with skin and flesh,” and afterward, “and knit me together with bones and sinews” (Job 10:11). Why, then, were these like a man who undresses and dresses again, putting on first what he took off last? Whereas at the beginning of the formation of the fetus it is skin and flesh first, and afterward bones and sinews.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The question is stated as printed; Rashi’s answer in the printed text is brief and the sense is rendered literally.

Ezekiel.english_translation: An expression of a crust [*kerum*] — *[printed Old French: איקרוטיי"רייא]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: And behold, a rattling of the bones, which were striking one against another.
The bones, each one wherever it had been scattered, leaped and drew near, each one to the place of its joint.
Wherever their souls went to roam, to the four directions of the world, from there they shall be gathered and come.
*U-fechi* — like “that bloweth the fire of coals” (Isaiah 54:16).
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 54:16” is correct (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: these bones are the whole house of Israel
Ezekiel.english_translation: A hint and an illustration for the whole house of Israel in their troubles, for they say in their troubles, “Our bones are dried up, our hope is lost” — and what shall we hope for, for salvation, any more? Another explanation: all these were of Israel; and because You are reviving them now, they say, “Our hope is lost, and we shall not live a second time” when the dead are revived.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The “another explanation” is rendered literally from the printed Hebrew and its sense is not fully clear.

Ezekiel.english_translation: For I am destined to revive them a second time.
“And write upon it: For Judah, and for the children of Israel his companions” — these four words, write upon it, saying: This stick is for Judah and for the tribe of Benjamin that joined him.
“This is for Joseph, the stick of Ephraim,” and the other nine tribes that came after Jeroboam, who was of the tribe of Ephraim.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Translated as printed; the verse is quoted loosely in Rashi’s Hebrew.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: that they may become one in thy hand
Ezekiel.english_translation: I shall join them, the two sticks, so that it is one stick in your hand.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I will take the stick of Joseph
Ezekiel.english_translation: So that they will no longer be two kingdoms.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: that I have given unto Jacob My servant
Ezekiel.english_translation: In the manner that I gave it to Jacob, without borders.
This is the name of the king.
The name of the nation, as it is said, “Gomer, and Magog” (Genesis 10).
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 10” is Genesis 10:2 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_translation: I will make you wayward — *enveisier* [printed אנבו"יישיר] in Old French. Everyone who goes by the stubbornness of his heart is called wayward, as in “and he went on frowardly in the way of his heart” (Isaiah 57:17).
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this verse (Ezekiel 38:4) with the forms אינוויישייר / אינווייזייר (*enveisier*) and glosses it “et je te séduirai” (“and I shall seduce you”). The printed spelling differs slightly from his.

Ezekiel.english_translation: It is the way to bring out a wild beast by hooks in its jaws, since it does not wish to go out. So too I shall put in your heart thoughts and an inclination that draws you from your land to come against the Land of Israel.
All around it.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Be thou prepared, and prepare for thyself
Ezekiel.english_translation: Prepare yourself, and prepare for yourself other forces.
Make yourself ready.
It is the way of kings to give attention to their armies, how they go out, and to post guards, lest a destroyer come upon his army at night.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Rashi reads the clause as “and thou shalt be a guard to them”; JPS renders it differently.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: After many days thou shalt be mustered for service
Ezekiel.english_translation: From many days in which you sinned against Me, you shall now be mustered before Me, to recall your iniquities and to return your recompense; and I shall lead you in the latter years to come to the Land of Israel, which is restored from the sword, whose inhabitants have returned from the exile into which they went by the sword of the enemy.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: which have been a continual waste
Ezekiel.english_translation: For many years; and shortly before your coming against it they returned.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: but it is brought forth out of the peoples
Ezekiel.english_translation: And you should have set it on your heart that it was brought out from the peoples, and He who brought it out from the peoples will not abandon it into your hand.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: thou shalt come like a storm
Ezekiel.english_translation: Like darkness that covers the land; *shoah* — *bruine* [printed ברואינ"ה] in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this verse (Ezekiel 38:9) with the form ברואינא (*broine*) and glosses it “comme l’obscurité” (“like the darkness”). The printed spelling differs slightly from his.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: things shall come into thy mind
Ezekiel.english_translation: Thoughts will arise.
To make war against Me.
Dwellers in villages without a wall, who trust in their strength and are not afraid to gather into fortified cities.
Like “from the cities of the Perizzi” — without a wall.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Rashi’s Hebrew cites the phrase without a reference; it is translated as printed.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I will come upon them that are at quiet
Ezekiel.english_translation: Upon the quiet ones, and I shall see what their security is.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: to turn thy hand against the waste places that are now inhabited
Ezekiel.english_translation: To destroy a second time the cities that were ruins until now and have now become settled.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the people that are gathered out of the nations
Ezekiel.english_translation: From peoples who are now making cattle and possessions.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: dwell in the middle of the earth
Ezekiel.english_translation: Upon the height and the strength of the land, like this navel, which is the middle of a man and slopes from all its sides.
The keen merchants in it, who are accustomed to go out and roam like young lions through all the provinces, and who know where the wealth is.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Comest thou to take the spoil
Ezekiel.english_translation: That is: who told you the place of the wealth? Do you know that you are going to a land full of spoil and plunder, and there you will truly find abundant wealth?
Targum Jonathan: “Thou shalt know the retribution of My might” — that is, you will know and recognize who is their stronghold and their security.

In those days the Holy One, blessed be He, will say: Art thou he of whom I spoke in former days by the hand of My servants the prophets of Israel, such as Ezekiel and Zechariah, who also prophesied about the wars of Gog and Magog — “For I will gather all nations” (Zechariah 14:2)? And our Rabbis said that Eldad and Medad prophesied about him, and this is the “years” mentioned here: do not read *shanim* (“years”) but *shenayim* (“two,” with a patach) — two prophets prophesied one prophecy in one chapter (but not in one style).
Through voices and thunders, as it says.

I heard that they are sheer rocks, standing upright and hanging, that appear as if falling; but I say they are the mounds of towers, which they dig around and throw the earth into the middle to raise the mound, and it is made in steps — *escalons* [printed אשקלונ"ש] in Old French — so that the earth will stand; and after it has been well packed down, they take away the bricks that hold up the step.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this verse (Ezekiel 38:20) with the form אשקלונש (*escalons*) and glosses it “et les degrés” (“and the steps”).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I will call for a sword against him
Ezekiel.english_translation: That a sword may come among them against him; “I will call” — I will summon. And what is the sword that I will call against him? Their own sword: “every man’s sword shall be against his brother.”

Hailstones that shine like precious stones whose name is *gavish*, as it is said (Job 28), *ramot* and *gavish* (“coral … crystal”). And our Rabbis said: *El gav ish* (“upon the back of the man”) — hailstones that began to fall on Egypt and stood in the air upon the back of the man, Moses, who prayed that they not descend, as it is said (Exodus 5), “was not poured upon the earth” — it did not reach the earth.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “Job 28” is Job 28:18 (JPS: “coral or of crystal”) and printed “Exodus 5” is Exodus 9:33 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_translation: Like *ve-hissi’tikha* upon My people, like Psalms 89: “The enemy shall not exact from him” (*lo yashi oyev bo*).
Ezekiel.translator_note: The first citation is not identified; the second is Psalms 89:23 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: neither will I suffer My holy name to be profaned any more
Ezekiel.english_translation: The lowliness of Israel is the profanation of His name, in that it is said of them (above, 30), “These are the people of HaShem” — and He was not able to save them.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “above, 30” is Ezekiel 36:20 (JPS: “These are the people of the LORD”).

Ezekiel.english_translation: Like an oven that was heated, in the language of the Mishnah.
*[printed Old French: אנא"ר מורא"ש]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: A place where there will be a grave for them, because he is of the seed of Japheth, who covered his father’s nakedness; therefore he merited burial.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the valley of them that pass through
Ezekiel.english_translation: The valley where they cross the Sea of Chinnereth, to bring from there the fruits of Gennesaret continually.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: on the east of the sea
Ezekiel.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “on the east of the Sea of Gennesaret.”

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: it shall stop them that pass through
Ezekiel.english_translation: And it shuts off those who pass through, like “Thou shalt not muzzle” (Deuteronomy 25), for most of the corpses that fall there will stop the passers-by from passing; therefore they will pass over them and bury them. And Menahem interpreted it in his book: “they shall stop their nose from smelling the odor of the corpses.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “Deuteronomy 25” is Deuteronomy 25:4 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: all the people of the land shall bury them
Ezekiel.english_translation: Those who died there.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: it shall be to them a renown
Ezekiel.english_translation: All the nations will relate their name for praise and kindness: there is no nation like this one — merciful ones! Is there a man who buries his enemy who stood to kill him?
Men who are appointed for this, Israel will set apart, to pass through the land to gather the scattered ones.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: to bury with them that pass through
Ezekiel.english_translation: They bury, together with the passers-by, the corpses that block and hinder the passage, for those who cross the sea bury them for their own benefit — “the passers-by with the passers-by.” So I heard, and so is Targum Jonathan.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: those that remain upon the face of the land
Ezekiel.english_translation: Far from the crossing, which those who cross the sea do not occupy themselves to bury — these appointed and set-apart men will bury them.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: after the end of seven months
Ezekiel.english_translation: The majority of the corpses visible to their eyes will have been buried, and from then on they will search the land, in the places of hiding, in the thorns and among the thistles, and bury what they find.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: when they that pass through shall pass through the land
Ezekiel.english_translation: Travelers on the roads who see a man’s bone.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: he set up a sign by it
Ezekiel.english_translation: A sign that there is a bone of a dead person here, so that travelers and those who prepare pure things will keep away from it until the men of continual employment, who are set apart, come to search, and bury them.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Hamonah shall also be the name of a city
Ezekiel.english_translation: And also the city whose name is *Homiyah* from the multitude of people — it is the great city; also the host of its inhabitants — there they will bury.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The last clause is rendered literally from the printed Hebrew and its sense is not fully clear.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Thus shall they cleanse the land
Ezekiel.english_translation: Israel in the land: their pure things and their heave-offerings.
It has no mappiq in the *heh*, because the final *heh* serves as the noun-ending of *hamonah*, like *homiyah*.
Kings and dukes, rulers and princes.
A fattened ox is called *almari* in the Arabic language.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Arabic form is translated as printed; it was not checked against a lexicon.

Ezekiel.english_translation: My retribution — *justicia* [printed יושטיצ"א] in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this form (as יושטיצא, *justiça*) and glosses it “ma justice” (“my justice”); he cites the verse as 39:22.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: went into captivity for their iniquity
Ezekiel.english_translation: When they see My might, they will recognize that it was not from shortness of My hand that I did not save them, but because of their iniquity I hid My face from them, and they went into exile.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: be jealous for My holy name
Ezekiel.english_translation: And I shall clothe Myself with jealousy of salvation and vengeance for the sake of My holy name, that it be profaned no more.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: be jealous for My holy name
Ezekiel.english_translation: On account of My holy name, as in “Art thou jealous for my sake?” (Numbers 11).
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “Numbers 11” is Numbers 11:29 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_translation: When I do good to them and do not recompense them according to their evil, then they will bear their shame and be too ashamed to lift up their face. And Menahem explained *ve-nasu* like “Happy is he whose transgression is forgiven” (Psalms 32:1) — an expression of atonement.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: I will leave none of them any more there
Ezekiel.english_translation: Not one of them in the exile.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: in the beginning of the year, in the tenth day of the month
Ezekiel.english_translation: Which year is it whose Rosh Hashanah is on the tenth of the month? Say: this is the Jubilee. For the Temple was destroyed in the thirty-sixth year of the Jubilee cycle, which began in the eighteenth year of [printed: Isaiah] — and at the end of fourteen the Jubilee should have been; and it is the twenty-fifth year of the exile of Jeconiah, who was exiled in the twenty-sixth year, in the fourteenth Jubilee: of Josiah from eighteen to thirty-one, and Jehoiakim eleven.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The chronology is translated literally from the printed Hebrew and its figures are not fully clear. The printed text reads “Isaiah” (*Yeshayahu*) where the context (the eighteenth year of Josiah, named in the same sentence) suggests Josiah.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the hand of the LORD was upon me
Ezekiel.english_translation: The strength of His force, to take me against my will.
To the smitten city, that is Jerusalem; in that year He showed him the building of the Temple of the future to come.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: In the visions of God brought He me
Ezekiel.english_translation: He did not take me there, but showed me as though I were there.
For so it is destined to be high, as it is said (Isaiah 2), “and shall be exalted above the hills.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 2” is Isaiah 2:2 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_translation: Like the building of a city.
On the south of the mountain.
Like the radiance of the Chayyot, and sparkling like the look of burnished brass.
Ezekiel.translator_note: JPS Ezekiel 1:7 reads “like the colour of burnished brass.”

Ezekiel.english_translation: For measuring ground there is nothing better than a cord of flax.
To measure with it the thickness of the wall and the length and width of the gates.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: all that I shall show thee
Ezekiel.english_translation: The matter of the building.
From Babylon.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: a wall on the outside of the house round about
Ezekiel.english_translation: He showed me one building of a house on the north of the mountain, and the wall outside, all around; so it is explained at the end of the book, that the city is on the south and the house on the north.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: six cubits long, of a cubit and a hand-breadth
Ezekiel.english_translation: Targum Jonathan so: “six cubits by the cubit that is a cubit and a handbreadth.” This is the middle cubit of six [handbreadths], which is a cubit and a handbreadth in the cubit of five.
The thickness of the wall.

And this is the outer height that is around the Temple Mount, and it was low, as we learned: All the walls there were high, except the eastern wall, for the priest who burns the heifer stands on the Mount of Anointing, etc.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the gate which looketh toward the east
Ezekiel.english_translation: He entered within the enclosure and came to the eastern gate of the Women’s Court; it is called “the outer court” throughout this passage because it is before the Court of Israel.
For the slope of the mountain goes up from the lower rampart to the Women’s Court, twelve steps, like that which we learned: within it was the rampart, ten cubits, and twelve steps were there.
It is the doorpost of the gate.
Six cubits, and it covers the entire thickness of the wall, which was one reed, as he said above.
The second doorpost: one on the north and one on the south.

The *te’a* is a ledge, called *apendiz* [printed אפנדי"ן] in Old French; and there were three on the right of the gate and three on the left, as stated in the passage. And the cells were adjacent to the eastern wall of the Women’s Court on the outside, toward the Temple Mount. And from where do I learn that they are on the outside? From what is written after the whole passage, “Then brought he me into the outer court”: from here I learn that all that is stated above was outside it, for he had not yet entered into it.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this verse (Ezekiel 40:7) with the form אפנדיץ (*apendiz*) and glosses it “et la chambre” (“and the chamber”). The printed spelling differs slightly from his. The quoted words are Ezekiel 40:17.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: one reed long, and one reed broad
Ezekiel.english_translation: The inner space of each one was six cubits square.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the space between the cells was five cubits
Ezekiel.english_translation: The walls that divide between the cells, their thickness five cubits; and so Targum Jonathan translated: “and between the cells, a wall of five cubits”; and so we learned in Tractate Middot: the wall of the cell, five.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the jambs of the gate by the porch of the gate within were one reed
Ezekiel.english_translation: Inside the gate there was made a porch joined to the gate, as is explained in the passage, projecting into the Women’s Court ten cubits, and at its head doors and doorposts; and this is what it says: “the threshold of the gate,” which is beside the porch of the gate.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Rashi’s printed lemma reads “the threshold of the gate”; JPS renders the Hebrew as “the jambs of the gate.”

Ezekiel.english_translation: That is, toward the inside.

Its breadth, to cover the thickness of the walls of the porch, one on the right and one on the left, for the thickness of the wall of the porch on the right and on the left is one reed, as he goes on to explain.
Inside the gate.
The thickness of the walls on the right and on the left, on which the porch rests.
The length of its projection into the Women’s Court.

*[printed Old French: אשישלטינ"ץ]* in Old French. All the “posts” (*eilim*) mentioned in the passage are like round pillars made of hewn stones, standing at an opening, one on the right and one on the left, in place of thresholds, in place of doorposts; and so Targum Jonathan on “And the posts of the door were moved” (Isaiah 6:4): *ilanot sappaya* (“trees of the thresholds”). They are called *eilim* after round things like *elah* and *elon* (terebinth, oak).
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: The thickness of their roundness; and they stand at the end of the space of the porch, attached, this one to the right wall and that one to the left wall. Thus the projection of the porch and its posts is ten cubits into the court, inside the gate.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the porch of the gate was inward
Ezekiel.english_translation: Because the porches of the gate of the Court of Israel protruded and were drawn toward the outside, as is explained in the passage, explaining that the porches of the gates of the Women’s Court were drawn toward the inside; and the gates of the Women’s Court are aligned opposite the gates of the Court of Israel, so that a porch is opposite a porch, and this is a matter of beauty.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the cells of the gate eastward
Ezekiel.english_translation: This gate which is toward the east, in the eastern wall of the Women’s Court: three were on this side and three on that side, three to the south and three to the north, adjacent to the wall of the Women’s Court, and their faces toward the Temple Mount; and the measure of the space inside and of the wall dividing between each one is explained above.
Those made for the thresholds of the porch, from the inside.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: on this side and on that side
Ezekiel.english_translation: And on this side, on the right and on the left; their measure was two cubits.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the breadth of the entry of the gate
Ezekiel.english_translation: The breadth of the space of the entry; and so we learned: all the entries were ten cubits wide.
It is the space of the porch of the gate, from the north to the south.

Ten corresponding to the space of the entry, and a cubit and a half here and a cubit and a half there. And do not wonder that beside the entry he calls it “breadth,” and beside the space of the porch he calls it “length”: for the entry — its height is its length, and the breadth is from threshold to threshold; and the porch — because the extent of the projection of its space from east to west is less than the measure of its space from north to south, for this is eight cubits and that thirteen — he calls the greater measure “length.” And behold, there is evidence for the matter in *mishkana* (1 Kings): “and the porch before the temple of the house, twenty cubits was the length thereof, according to the breadth of the house.” Thus from north to south it is called, for the Hekhal, “breadth,” and for the porch, “length,” because the measure of the Hekhal from east to west exceeds that from north to south, whereas in the porch the measure is the reverse, for the greater measure is called “length.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Hebrew word *mishkana* followed by “(1 Kings)” is translated as printed; the verse quoted is 1 Kings 6:3 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_translation: The cells on this side and on that side of the gate were drawn back from opposite the space of the inner porch, a cubit to the north and a cubit to the south — for it was already explained that it is from the house [printed], drawn back from opposite the space of the gate a cubit and a half to the north and likewise to the south — and now he explains that the outer cells are drawn back to the north one cubit more than the porch, and likewise to the south one cubit; thus they are drawn back from the space of the breadth of the entry two and a half cubits on this side and two and a half cubits on that side. And this is what is said: “and a border” — *[printed Old French: אשומיי"ל]* in Old French — an empty place. And the wall of the cell is five thick. So the thickness of the northern wall (printed correction: it should read “southern”) of the northern cell and the thickness of the northern wall of the porch end, one opposite the other, for the wall of the porch is six thick and the wall of the cell five, and it extends one cubit inward opposite the thickness of the wall of the porch; and likewise to the south.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. The last sentences are rendered literally from the printed Hebrew; the printed text has an editorial correction in brackets (“northern” corrected to “southern”), and the sense of the clause “end, one opposite the other” is not fully clear.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: from the roof of the one cell to the roof of the other
Ezekiel.english_translation: From the roof of the cell on the north of the gate to the roof of the cell on the south of the gate.

The thickness of the wall of the cell, five, and likewise the thickness of the wall of the cell on the other side — behold, ten; and two and a half cubits that it is drawn back from the space of the entry, here and likewise there — behold, fifteen; and the space of the entry, ten cubits — behold, twenty-five. And all are the measure of the breadth of the gate, corresponding to the thirteen cubits of the space of the porch on the inside and two walls, a reed here and a reed there — behold, twenty-five.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The printed text has a small editorial bracket after “that it be”; it is omitted here. The arithmetic is as printed (5 + 5 + 2½ + 2½ + 10 = 25; 13 + 6 + 6 = 25). Audit 4 arithmetic check: the sums were recomputed and agree.

Ezekiel.english_translation: The opening of the cell beside the gate on the south is aligned opposite the opening of the cell beside the gate on the north; for none of these six cells had an opening in the wall on the outside, but the two cells adjacent to the gate had openings facing the air of the gate between them. And so it says below, “and to their posts within the gate” — we learn that their openings face the gate.
The height of the posts of the thresholds of the porch was sixty cubits.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the posts of the court in the gates round about
Ezekiel.english_translation: And so for all the posts of the court, in all the porches of the gates all around; for on the north and on the south too it had gates made in the pattern of this gate, as is explained in the passage.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the forefront of the gate of the entrance
Ezekiel.english_translation: The height of this gate; and it is called “the gate of the entrance” (*ha-itton*) because it serves as entrance and exit for all who come into the court.
*Itton* — an Aramaic [rendering] of “coming.”

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the forefront of the inner porch of the gate
Ezekiel.english_translation: With the height of the porch of the gate, which is inside the gate, fifty cubits; and from the height of the other gates in the passage, which are fifty cubits, I learn that “*al penei*” as stated here is height (that is, from the outer gate its height is fifty cubits across the whole porch, which is the inner gate of the porch, for at the end of the porch too there is a gate, as is already explained in verse 7). (printed abbreviation: סא"א)
Ezekiel.translator_note: it is left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: These cells had no openings to the outside, but this one opened into that one. And so we find in Tractate Middot, regarding the cells around the Hekhal: three openings to each — one to the cell on the right, one to the cell on the left, and one to the cell above it. And the cells in the court, which were only three cells one beside another and had no cells above them: the middle one had two openings, one to the cell on the right and one to the cell on the left; and the outer one at the side of the gate had two openings, one opening into the middle one and one toward the side of the gate; and so for the outer cell of the second shoulder, on either side of the gate, as is written above, “door against door.” And they had windows *shekufim atumim*, open to the outside and closed toward the inside — that is, narrow toward the inside and wide toward the outside, toward the east. And Menahem interpreted *shekufim* as an expression of looking out, as in “Who is she that looketh forth” (Song of Songs 6:10), “For He hath looked down from the height of His sanctuary” (Psalms 102:20); and so “to the lintel” (Exodus 12) he likewise interpreted as an expression of looking out.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “Exodus 12” is Exodus 12:22 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: and to their posts within the gate
Ezekiel.english_translation: And to the shoulders of the openings of the two cells adjacent to the gate on either side, whose openings were into the air of the gate — the opening of the northern cell from the north of the gate and the opening of the southern cell from the south of the gate — and the shoulders of the openings on either side of the opening of the cell are the posts; and they had windows open to the air of the break in the breadth of the gate that divided between the cells. And that air he calls “within the gate,” for whoever enters between the air of the projection of the cells on this side and that appears to be entering the gate.
And so there were windows to the arches of every gate.
In the wall toward the court, on the inside.

Targum Jonathan: *kotarta* — capitals: at the top of the post there was made a kind of capitals resembling a palm tree, for in the *mishkana* of Solomon they are translated “form of palms.” *Pomels* [printed פומיל"ש] in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: It appears to be *pomels* (“pommels”). Darmesteter lists this form elsewhere (glossed “leurs pommeaux”) but not at this verse.

Ezekiel.english_translation: *[printed Old French: פלנקי"ץ]* in Old French. As for *ritzpah* (“pavement”), I say that it is an upper story round about, like that which we learned: “It was smooth at first, and they surrounded it with a balcony.” And on that upper story were the chambers — *[printed Old French: קנברא"ש]* in Old French. And from what is said in the passage, “and the pavement by the side of the gates, and below them corresponding to the height of the gates,” we learn that this pavement is an upper story.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The first Old French form is opaque and was not found in Darmesteter; the second appears to be *chambres* (“chambers”) but was likewise not found.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: by the side of the gates
Ezekiel.english_translation: The height of the court gate interrupted the upper story, so that it did not encircle the whole court; and it was at the shoulders of the gate on this side and that, corresponding to the height of the gates.

This word differs from every “lower” (*tachtonah*) in Scripture, for everywhere the accent is on the *nun*, and this one is on the *tav*; we learned that this “lower” is not a pavement beneath another, but it is one pavement, and the bottom of the pavement was opposite the height of the gate. And the *heh* of *tachtonah* is like the *heh* of *beitah*, of *ezrathah* and of *chelathah*, which are superfluous.
The space of the Women’s Court.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: from the forefront of the lower gate
Ezekiel.english_translation: This is the gate explained above.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: unto the forefront of the inner court without
Ezekiel.english_translation: Up to the Court of Israel.
On its two sides, its space was a hundred cubits.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: he measured the length thereof and the breadth thereof
Ezekiel.english_translation: As the measure of the east gate; so it is explained in the passage.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the length thereof was fifty cubits
Ezekiel.english_translation: Its height.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the breadth five and twenty cubits
Ezekiel.english_translation: From the roof of the cell to its roof.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the arches thereof were before them
Ezekiel.english_translation: And the porch of the gate was before the steps; before one entered the porch he went up by steps.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: a gate to the inner court
Ezekiel.english_translation: To the Court of Israel.
The outer ones — aligned.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: he measured from gate to gate
Ezekiel.english_translation: The lower to the upper, a hundred cubits; that is the width of the space of the Women’s Court.
To the outer court.

Rabbi Tanhuma expounded: this *heh* is superfluous; an expression of *kehah* — “dim” windows, wide on the outside and narrow on the inside, to say: I do not need its light; for all windows made to admit light are narrow on the outside and widen toward the inside.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: steps to go up to it
Ezekiel.english_translation: *Olotav* — like *ma‘alotav* (“its steps”).
On top of the post was a palm tree depicted.
Of the inner court.
*[printed Old French: ארבו"ץ]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: The wall was made of porches, porches entering into its thickness; and these arches were on the inside (another version: above the cells; for the cells were on the inside in the inner court, since the porch of the gate protruded toward the outer court, as stated in the passage; and it is impossible that the cells and the porch faced the same place, so that the openings of the cells would open into the porch, for the passage equates all the measures of the outer gates and the inner ones and does not distinguish between them except for the projection of the porches) (for the cells were on the outside, and six cells and their walls and the fifteen cubits of the breadth of the gate amount to eighty-one cubits [printed correction: ninety-one], and the entire inner court is only a hundred by a hundred, as is explained in the passage). (printed abbreviation: סא"א)
Ezekiel.translator_note: it is left as printed. The figures in the final parenthesis carry an editorial correction in the printed text and are translated as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: The porch of the inner gate was not toward the inside as the porches of the outer gate were, but protruded on the outside.
Its height was fifty cubits.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the posts thereof were toward the outer court
Ezekiel.english_translation: *[printed Old French: אשישפיאר"קאש]* in Old French; and the porch of the gate is called “posts” here.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. Darmesteter lists the word *eilim* in this passage (cited as Ezekiel 40:37, “ואיליו,” glossed “et ses portiques,” “and its porticoes”) with forms such as מישלינט; the printed spelling here differs, and I did not rely on it.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: a chamber with the entry thereof
Ezekiel.english_translation: It was beside the northern gate in the Court of Israel.
Of the chamber, to the posts of the gate, toward the gate.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: by the posts at the gates
Ezekiel.english_translation: There are verses in the passage that call the shoulders of the gate *eilim* — *[printed Old French: מיינשליש]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. Darmesteter lists the word *eilim* in this passage (cited as Ezekiel 40:37, “ואיליו,” glossed “et ses portiques,” “and its porticoes”) with forms such as מישלינט; the printed spelling here differs, and I did not rely on it.

Ezekiel.english_translation: The burnt-offering that is slaughtered in the north.
They would wash the entrails.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: in the porch of the gate
Ezekiel.english_translation: The northern one.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: were two tables on this side
Ezekiel.english_translation: In its east, and two in its west; and though they were drawn into the outer court, their holiness is as that of the inside.
And to the side of the opening of the porch, outside the space of the porch, into the space of the opening of (another version: of the side of) the Court of Israel.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: as one goeth up to the entry of the gate toward the north
Ezekiel.english_translation: When he enters into the gate and goes up the steps of the entrance of the court.
Tables at the shoulder of the entrance on the east (and so) on the west.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: on the other side of the porch of the gate
Ezekiel.english_translation: Which is at the opening of the porch: two tables.
On them they place the knives and the basins in which they receive the blood, so that they are ready for those who slaughter there the most holy offerings in the north.

Iron hooks fixed in the dwarf pillars in the slaughterhouse in the north, to hang the offerings on them and to flay them.
