That is what we learned in Pesachim: “Iron hooks were fixed in the pillars and in the walls, on which they hang and flay.” And so Targum Jonathan: “and hooks projecting one handbreadth.”
Fixed in the space of the court, in the house, within it.
And outside the space of the porch of the gate, into the air of the inner court, as is explained at the end of the verse.
Chambers of the Levite singers.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: their prospect was toward the south
Ezekiel.english_translation: Their opening toward the south.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: one at the side of the east gate
Ezekiel.english_translation: One chamber at the shoulder of the east gate.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: having the prospect toward the north
Ezekiel.english_translation: And its opening toward the north.
“The ministers of the house,” it seems, are the Levite singers.
The space of the Court of Israel before the porch and the Hekhal.
The porch of the Hekhal.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: measured each post of the porch
Ezekiel.english_translation: *Va-yamod el ulam* — like *eil ulam*: the thickness of the shoulders of the opening he measured from east to west (and I, the writer, found it in other commentaries, as I have copied). (printed abbreviation: סא"א)
Ezekiel.translator_note: The final parenthetical is the copyist’s remark and is translated as printed. it is left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the breadth of the gate was three cubits on this side
Ezekiel.english_translation: (“And the breadth of the gate was three cubits on this side,” etc. — this is the thickness of the northern post into the space of the opening toward the west, and likewise the thickness of the southern post into the space of the porch toward the west. And though we learned thus: “the wall of the porch five, and the porch eleven,” in the future it is only three; but in the porch of the Second Temple, etc.) (printed abbreviation: סא"א)
Ezekiel.translator_note: The source gives no lemma here; a nearby phrase from the verse is used. it is left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: And so it was also in the Second [Temple], for we learned: the wall of the porch five, and the porch eleven; except that in the porch of the Second Temple there were no shoulders to the entrance to the north and south, for the breadth of the entrance was twenty cubits, like the breadth of the porch. But here it is written, “and the breadth of the gate was three cubits on this side, and three cubits on that side,” and I do not know [how to] explain it, except that, for the breadth of the shoulders of the entrance, three cubits close off the space of the entrance on this side and three cubits on that side.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Translated literally from the printed Hebrew; the sense is not fully clear.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: The length of the porch was twenty cubits
Ezekiel.english_translation: Corresponding to the breadth of the Hekhal.
From east to west.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: it was by steps that it was ascended
Ezekiel.english_translation: And the way by which they go up to it was by steps, as we learned: between the porch and the altar twenty-two cubits, and twelve steps were there, the height of a step half a cubit.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: there were pillars by the posts
Ezekiel.english_translation: In place of Jachin and Boaz that were in the First Temple.
It is the thickness of the wall of the Hekhal between the Hekhal and the porch (from east to west).
The breadth of the porch, which is the breadth of the porch and the length of the Hekhal; in other commentaries: “the breadth of the tent” — the tent of the entrance.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the sides of the entrance were five cubits
Ezekiel.english_translation: For the Hekhal was twenty cubits wide and the breadth of the entrance was ten; thus its shoulders on this side and on that are five and five.
To the partition that divides between the Hekhal and the Holy of Holies.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: measured each post of the entrance
Ezekiel.english_translation: Its thickness was two cubits; this is not equal to the cubit of the *traksin*.
I cannot explain it except as its height.
Across the breadth of the Hekhal.
The western wall.

*Apendiz* [printed אפנדי"ץ] in Old French: the cell behind it, its space four cubits; and that of the Second Temple was six. And perforce this Temple is of the future, for in the Second Temple there was no wall dividing to the Holy of Holies.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists the form אפנדיץ (*apendiz*) at Ezekiel 40:7 (“et la chambre”). The last sentence is rendered literally from the printed Hebrew.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the side-chambers were one over another
Ezekiel.english_translation: Cell to cell, and cell upon cell.

And in the Second Temple there were thirty-eight: fifteen in the north and fifteen in the south — five upon five and five on top of them — and eight in the west. It is a *tzela*, it is a *yatsia*, it is a *ta*. And I say that the cells in the north and south were arranged thus: the length of each one was twelve cubits — behold sixty cubits for five cells — and five walls of five cubits each — behold eighty-five — and the breadth of five cubits of the *munach* [the left-over space] completes ninety cubits of the length of the wall; and likewise to the south. And those in the west: one upon another, and a third upon them, and their length upon them twenty cubits, corresponding to the breadth of the Holy of Holies — behold eleven in every row; and Targum Jonathan: “eleven in a row.” (Another version: “thirty-three times” — three times eleven: eleven upon one, eleven upon them; and so Targum Jonathan: “eleven in order.” And in the Second Temple, etc., until “it is a cell,” and no more.)
Ezekiel.translator_note: Translated literally from the printed Hebrew; the sense is not fully clear. The Aramaic phrase is translated as printed.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: in the wall which belonged to the house for the side-chambers
Ezekiel.english_translation: The beams of the upper stories of the ledges — their ends on the side of the outer partition of the cells would come and pierce the wall on its inner side; and this is “which belonged to the house for the side-chambers,” on its side that is within the cells; and this is “that they might have hold therein” — fixed firmly. *[printed Old French: פופרי"ש]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. The rest is translated literally from the printed Hebrew; the sense is not fully clear.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: and not have hold in the wall of the house
Ezekiel.english_translation: The ends on the side of the wall of the Hekhal would come and pierce at recesses, for the wall of the Hekhal protruded into the cells, as stated in the building of Solomon (1 Kings 2): “for on the outside he made rebatements in the wall of the house round about.” The lowest ledge: five by the cubit the breadth of its space, and its upper story six, for the wall of the Hekhal was drawn in from above by a cubit; therefore the space of the middle one was six cubits broad, and the third seven by the cubit broad; and that was the upper story of the middle one, for the wall of the Hekhal was drawn in toward it by a cubit from above, and these too were like them. And this is what it said: “and not have hold in the wall of the house” — they did not pierce the wall of the Hekhal as the other ends of the beams of low [buildings] fixed in a high wall, which pierce the wall and drive the ends of the beams into the holes.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “1 Kings 2” is 1 Kings 6:6 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_translation: And the side-chambers went on widening upward, as I explained: the middle one broader than the lowest by a cubit, and likewise the top one than the middle by a cubit.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: as they wound about higher and higher
Ezekiel.english_translation: And *musabbah* (“winding”): a staircase called *vis* [printed וי"ץ] in Old French, of stone building, a kind of pillar with steps going up in it, and one who goes up on them is like one who goes round the circumference of a stone pillar; and in the language of Ashkenaz it is called *shvindl shtayn* [printed שווינד"ל שטיין]. This is what is said in the building of Solomon, “and they went up by winding stairs into the middle row”; it is also translated “and by a winding stair” (*u-vemesibta*), like “as they wound about higher and higher”; and so a winding stair goes up to the roof of the upper cell, as he goes on to explain, that the winding stair goes up from the lowest to the middle and from the middle to the upper.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this word (the scan reads “XLI, 1”; the verse is 41:7) with the form ויץ (*vis*) and glosses it “un escalier tournant” (“a spiral staircase”), adding the German *Windelstein*. The quoted words from Solomon’s building are 1 Kings 6:8 (JPS wording).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the winding about of the house
Ezekiel.english_translation: To the side-chambers.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: therefore the breadth of the house continued upward
Ezekiel.english_translation: Therefore we said, “and wider upward”: the breadth of the house within the side-chambers; the topmost is the widest of all.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: so one went up from the lowest row to the highest by the middle
Ezekiel.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “And by a winding stair they go up from the lowest to the upper by way of the middle”; and so they go up by means of a winding stair from the lowest to the upper by way of the middle.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Aramaic word printed *be-orekh* is rendered as the usual “by way of.”

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: had a raised basement round about
Ezekiel.english_translation: He did not state its measure, but in Tractate Middot we learned of a height of a hundred cubits.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the foundations of the side-chambers were a full reed
Ezekiel.english_translation: The foundation of the side-chambers was a full reed.

Targum Jonathan: *rivach* (“breadth”). The foundation of the partition of the side-chamber within the ground was six cubits wide, but above the ground its breadth was five cubits, as is explained in the passage in the verse after it.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the outer wall which belonged to the side-chambers
Ezekiel.english_translation: The partition of the cells adjacent to the court; that is the western partition.
And so we learned in Tractate Middot, that this wall is five.

And there was an empty place left at the northern and southern corners near the east, for the cells did not encircle the whole house; and to that empty place were the openings of the cells in the eastern corners, as stated in the passage, “and the doors of the side-chambers were toward the place that was left”; for they had no openings to the cells, neither toward the court nor toward the Hekhal, except for those in the north-east corner and the south-east corner, where the opening was in the wall of its breadth, open to that place that was left; and through that opening they enter it, and from it to the second cell, and from the second to the third, and so all around; for so we learned in Tractate Middot: three openings to each one — one to the cell on the right, one to the cell on the left, and one to the cell above it. And so also Targum Jonathan: *ve-atar shevik* (“and a place left”). Another version: “and so that which was left” — that is, and likewise those [on the inner side] of the side-chambers on the side of the house: a vacant place was left between the cells and the house, and in that place were the openings of the cells, as explained in the passage, “and the doors of the side-chambers were toward the place that was left”; and its breadth was five cubits, as it says, “and the breadth of the place that was left was five cubits,” as I explained above, that the cells would not be adjacent to the house at all, but air would be between them; and the house five cubits; and so Targum Jonathan: *ve-atar shevik*.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Translated literally from the printed Hebrew; the sense is not fully clear. The Aramaic is translated as printed.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: side-chambers that belonged to the house
Ezekiel.english_translation: Opposite the air of the breadth of the side-chambers at the corner angle. The “round about” that is written regarding the place left does not mean four sides as its plain sense, but rather: from here and from here, south and north — the south-east corner and the north-east corner.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: between the chambers was a breadth of twenty cubits
Ezekiel.english_translation: Chambers were in the outer court, in the north of the inner court, beside its height; and a break of twenty cubits between the breadth of the partitions of the chambers and the partitions of the cells that were round about. And the house was not so in the building of the Second Temple, but in the building of the future.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: toward the place that was left
Ezekiel.english_translation: And the openings of the outer cells open to the place left empty at a corner, as I explained.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the building that was before the separate place
Ezekiel.english_translation: The breadth of the whole building toward the western direction: the breadth of the house, and the thickness of the northern and southern walls with the northern and southern cells and the thickness of their walls to the north and to the south, is seventy cubits broad; and so it was in the Second Temple, and so we learned in Tractate Middot: in the western wall, from north to south, seventy cubits; and it gives the reckoning.
Targum Jonathan: *be-tzurta*. And I say that the high house is called so, and the low cells which surround it he calls “building.” And Menahem interpreted *gizrah* as an expression of “chamber.”

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: at the side toward the west
Ezekiel.english_translation: The western direction.

The breadth of the building from north to south, seventy cubits; and here is the reckoning: the northern cell four, and its walls ten — behold, fourteen — and five of the vacant place between the cell and the house — behold, nineteen. The breadth of the foundation of the walls was absorbed in the space of the cell and in the vacant place. And the wall of the Hekhal six — behold, twenty-five — and its space twenty broad — behold, forty-five — and the southern wall of the Hekhal six — behold, fifty-one — and nineteen of the southern cells: the total is seventy.
The walls of the cells.

The length of the building of the cells and the left space, ninety cubits, north and south, apart from the Bet ha-Chalifot, which is not counted with it, because it protruded to the outside, north and south, and was not level with the rest of the building; for the house was thirty cubits wider in front than behind it, as we learned: the porch exceeds the Hekhal by fifteen cubits in the north and fifteen cubits in the south; and it was called Bet ha-Chalifot because there they store the knives; and the length of that building from east to west was ten cubits. There remained ninety cubits of length against the breadth of seventy, for the whole house was a hundred in length on this side and that, as is explained in the passage and in Tractate Middot.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: measured the house, a hundred cubits long
Ezekiel.english_translation: The total, with the extent of the Bet ha-Chalifot. And so we learned in Tractate Middot: the Hekhal a hundred by a hundred, in height a hundred; from east to west a hundred: the wall of the porch five, and its breadth eleven; the wall of the Hekhal six, and its length forty; and the cubit of the *traksin*, and twenty cubits the Holy of Holies, and a wall six, and the cell six, and the wall of the cell five. And above, in the passage, so too the measure of all of them is explained, except for the cubit of the *traksin*, which is written in this passage as two cubits; and corresponding to them he reduces the breadth of the cell by a cubit — for the cell in the Mishnah is six broad and its wall five, and here its breadth is four and its wall six, for it is said here, “the foundations of the side-chambers were a full reed,” and above he narrows and draws in a cubit, as it is said, “and the wall of the side-chamber was five cubits.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: The printed text reads “the wall of the side-chamber was five cubits” (compare Ezekiel 41:9, “five cubits”).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the separate place, and the building, with the walls thereof
Ezekiel.english_translation: The end of the verse explains its beginning, to say: the total is a hundred cubits.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the breadth of the face of the house and of the separate place toward the east
Ezekiel.english_translation: The separate place and the cell behind it, which is built like a building, and the thickness of the walls, all together a hundred cubits. That is what I explained above, that the house extends in front by thirty cubits in breadth, for the porch is wider than the Hekhal and the cells by fifteen cubits to the north and fifteen cubits to the south — not that the space of the porch is wider than the space of the Hekhal, but because the Bet ha-Chalifot is joined to the porch on this side and on that.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the length of the building before the separate place
Ezekiel.english_translation: Now he returns and measures the length of the house to the south, as he measured to the north (I found); and this is “at the back thereof” — that is, backward, for he returned and measured on his heel toward the west.
Targum Jonathan: *zaviyyot* (“corners”) — that is, with the extent of the Bet ha-Chalifot that is in the corners of the house.

The end of this verse does not refer back to its beginning but is joined to the verse after it, and so is its explanation: “and the inner temple,” which is the Holy of Holies, and likewise “the porches of the court,” explained above, and porches round about; to all these, the thresholds and the closed windows and the *atikim* round about, to the three of them — whether to the separate place, which is the Hekhal, or to the porches, or to the Holy of Holies — for all three of them the thresholds were doorposts for their openings, and for all three of them there were closed windows, and for all three of them there were *atikim*; and I do not know what they are, and I say that they are a kind of square pillars protruding in the wall for strengthening, and they call them *pilers* [printed פיליר"ש] in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this word (cited as Ezekiel 41:16, “והאתיקים”) with the form פיליירש (*pilers*) and glosses it “les piliers” (“the pillars”). The printed spelling differs slightly from his.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: a plank of cedar.
Opposite the doorposts of the opening, within the space of the thickness of the opening, he veneered with wood (printed abbreviation: סא"א) I found.
Ezekiel.translator_note: it is left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: That is, on this side and on that, on the two sides of the space of the opening.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: from the ground up to the windows
Ezekiel.english_translation: From the bottom of the wall a wall of cedar planks is made opposite it, and goes up to the windows, and the windows too are covered by it. I found that the windows too were closed from the inside, as it is said here, “and closed windows to the house” (printed abbreviation: סא"א); and all this is on the inside, because they plastered it with a gold overlay, for the whole house was plastered with gold, and one cannot plaster gold over stones.
Ezekiel.translator_note: it is left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: to the space above the door
Ezekiel.english_translation: In height.
All the Holy of Holies, to its entirety.
Toward the Hekhal.
On all its walls.
In the Holy of Holies and in the Hekhal.
Covered with large planks made to measure.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: it was made with cherubim and palm-trees
Ezekiel.english_translation: And that cedar was depicted with cherubim and palms.

One the face of a young lion and one the face of a man, this one turned this way and that one turned that way; when the palm stood between cherub and cherub, the face of the young lion was toward it on one side and the face of a man on the other, as stated in the passage.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: through all the house round about
Ezekiel.english_translation: For the Holy of Holies.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: so on the wall of the temple
Ezekiel.english_translation: And likewise for the wall of the Hekhal.
I heard regarding the building of Solomon, “*mezuzat revu‘ah*,” that it had doorposts on two sides, and a threshold below and a lintel above; but I say that the doorposts were squared.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: an appearance such as is the appearance
Ezekiel.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “Its appearance like the radiance of its glory” — like the appearance of the throne of glory that I saw in the Chariot at the river Chebar, and a light of brightness I saw in the Holy of Holies.
Targum Jonathan: “opposite the altar, a table.” That is, he calls the table “altar,” because in the present time it atones like an altar; so I heard.
(its legs, its top and its length; Scripture writes “its top,” and it and its legs, and the “length” written in Scripture is “its top” — [printed correction: it should read …]) the body of the table.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The parenthetical is garbled in the printed text and carries an editorial correction; it is translated as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Its frames.
For each opening, two closers [leaves], one opposite the other: one in the northern doorpost and one in the southern doorpost.

For the opening of the Hekhal there were two pairs of doors, as we learned in Tractate Middot: it had four doors, two on the inside and two on the outside. The outer ones open into the entrance, to cover the thickness of the wall, which was six cubits; and the door’s breadth was five, by the measure of half the breadth of the entrance, and a cubit was recessed inward from the doorpost; thus the thickness of the wall, five cubits, was exposed, and when the outer door was inward in the entrance it would cover it. And the inner ones open into the house, to cover behind the doors, for the whole house was plastered with gold except behind the doors. Rabbi Judah says: the inner ones too stood within the entrance, and like an *istermita* they were folded behind them: these two and a half cubits, and those two and a half cubits, and half a cubit doorpost on this side and half a cubit doorpost on that side, for it is said, “And the doors had two leaves [apiece], two turning leaves,” etc. And this is its explanation: both the inner and the outer stand within the thickness of the wall, and both are recessed half a cubit inward from the doorpost; the inner ones open toward the outer, and the outer toward the inner. And how? Two doors of five cubits each open one opposite the other, within the [printed: ה"א] breadth of the thickness of the wall — they were of segments — and at their middle they were folded behind them when opened, like wooden writing-tablets on which one writes with an iron pen, which fold one behind the other; thus when they are folded they stand at two and a half cubits, and when they are opened one opposite the other they cover the five cubits of the thickness of the wall.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The passage is closely based on Mishnah Middot; the clause “within the [printed: ה"א] breadth … they were of segments” is rendered literally and its sense is not fully clear.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: thick beams of wood upon the face of the porch without
Ezekiel.english_translation: (*Ev* — *tref* [printed טרי"ף] in Old French, an expression of the beams of our houses; printed abbreviation: סא"א.) Poles of cedar were fixed from the wall of the Hekhal to the wall of the porch, so that it not bulge; so we learned in Tractate Middot; and this is “thick beams,” going out from the wall of the house and coming upon the face of the porch outside.
Ezekiel.translator_note: It appears to be *tref* (“beam”), but the form was not found in Darmesteter. it is left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: on the sides of the porch
Ezekiel.english_translation: On the two sides of the entrance.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the brackets of the house, and the thick beams
Ezekiel.english_translation: “And he showed me the brackets and the thick beams.” And our Rabbis of blessed memory said: “the brackets of the house” — these are the *meltasin*; “and the thick beams” — these are the *merishot*. And what are they? *Merishot* are beams; *meltasin* are cedars which they place at the tops of the walls, to lay upon them the ends of the beams.
From the inner court.
By the northern gate mentioned above, and a gate to the inner court opposite the gate toward the north, and it was set in the middle of the length of the Court of Israel, which is a hundred cubits.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the chamber that was over against
Ezekiel.english_translation: (To one of the first chambers; another version: [printed abbreviation: סא"א]) To the place of the chambers — *chambres* [printed קנברי"ץ] in Old French — they are the chambers standing in the north of the house, separated twenty cubits from the cells, as stated above, “And between the chambers was a breadth of twenty cubits round about the house.” And no one can enter those chambers, nor the air of the breadth of twenty between them and the cells, except by way of the (inner) [printed correction: outer] court, as is explained below in the passage; for it said that the inner court is a hundred by a hundred square before the house toward the east, and said of the breadth of the house toward the east, a hundred cubits; thus the breadth of the house blocks the breadth of the outer [printed correction: inner] court, and he cannot enter within from the sides of the chambers, neither to the north nor to the south; therefore it was necessary to come to those chambers by way of the northern outer court.
Ezekiel.translator_note: it is left as printed. The text carries two editorial corrections (“inner”/“outer”) which are translated as printed. Darmesteter lists this word (Ezekiel 42:1, “הלשכה”) and glosses it “les chambres” (“the chambers”); the forms are not legible in the scan used.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: that was over against the separate place
Ezekiel.english_translation: Those chambers were opposite the whole hundred cubits of the length of the house from east to west, as stated in the passage regarding those chambers: “and, lo, before the temple were a hundred cubits.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: Rashi’s Hebrew words are “upon the face of the Hekhal”; JPS Ezekiel 42:8 is quoted.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the front of the length of a hundred cubits
Ezekiel.english_translation: The north door [leads] to the door of the chamber, which faces north toward the outer court, and sees opposite it fifty cubits of breadth to the northern wall of the outer court; and the length is a hundred cubits, for the chambers extend from east to west a hundred cubits, and its breadth from north to south is fifty cubits, as it says below in the passage, and the space of the outer court is a hundred cubits in breadth, as stated above, “and he measured from gate to gate a hundred cubits.” Thus before the chambers is an empty space a hundred cubits long and fifty broad.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the twenty cubits which belonged to the inner court
Ezekiel.english_translation: All this is a sign of the place of the chambers: beside the twenty, the breadth of the air that belongs to the inner court round about the house, as stated above, and the building of the chambers twenty cubits broad.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the pavement which belonged to the outer court
Ezekiel.english_translation: For we said above that upon it the court was encircled (round about) around it.
I do not know what it is.

(Tosafot) “*Atik* before *atik*”: *atik* is a pillar, as Rashi also explained (above, 16): “and the *atikim* round about the three of them,” which are pillars; and “the upper chambers” are those same chambers that are spoken of, and he calls them “upper” because they are on the height of the mountain, as Rashi explained regarding “and from under these chambers”; and so it is explained in order.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The source gives no lemma here; a phrase from the verse is used. This is a printed supplementary note (marked “Tosafot”), not Rashi’s own comment. Printed “above, 16” is Ezekiel 41:16.

Ezekiel.english_translation: That are on the height of the mountain: two of them were short, that is, not spacious, because the *atikim* reduced them; for the way of builders to strengthen the work of their building is to make pillars up to two-thirds of the wall, and from there onward they finish and slope off; therefore the third is not short — and this is what it says, “for they were in three stories,” and they have no pillars, since no strengthening is needed as below. “And they had not pillars as the pillars of the courts” — that is, the pillars of these chambers are not like other pillars; for other pillars sit beside the wall for strengthening, but these are in the thickness of the wall, protruding outward and inward, and therefore they eat from the building.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The printed lemma belongs to Ezekiel 42:6; a nearby phrase from 42:3 (the id’s own verse) is used. The passage is a supplementary explanation, translated as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: As its Targum: “pressed,” because they are in the thickness of the wall, protruding outward and inward, and strengthen the chambers.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The printed lemma belongs to Ezekiel 42:6; a nearby phrase from 42:3 (the id’s own verse) is used. The Aramaic is translated as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: To the side of the ground. So I found in the name of the *Eshel Gadol* (printed abbreviation: סא"א).
Ezekiel.translator_note: The printed lemma belongs to Ezekiel 42:6; a nearby phrase from 42:3 (the id’s own verse) is used. it is left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: *mitlatin* — it implies that those chambers were three-fold, one above another, and the verses prove this also, for it says, “and the upper chambers are shorter than the lower and the middle.” And I was not able to understand at all in these three verses what it is: “for the *atikim* could” — what are those *atikim*, and how do they eat from the upper ones and not eat from the lower and the middle ones; and the reason that it gives for the matter, “For they were in three stories, and they had not pillars,” I did not know how to understand. (And I had neither teacher nor helper in this whole building, except as they showed me from Heaven.)
Ezekiel.translator_note: The printed lemma belongs to Ezekiel 42:6; a nearby phrase from 42:3 (the id’s own verse) is used. The Aramaic is translated as printed.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: a walk of ten cubits breadth inward
Ezekiel.english_translation: It seems to me that, since the space of the outer [court] is a hundred broad from north to south, and of this the chambers are fifty broad, and before them fifty of air toward the north — behold, here is the whole breadth of the court; thus the whole breadth of the court is blocked, for there is no air at all between the chambers and the corner of the Bet ha-Chalifot, and there is no entry by which to enter the air of the twenty between the chambers and the cells. For the air of twenty cubits that divides between the cells and the chambers is the fifteen cubits behind the Bet ha-Chalifot, with five cubits added to them. And if you say that an air of five [printed: ה"א] is found between the corners of the Chalifot and the corners of the chambers — behold, the thickness of the wall that divides between the inner court and the outer court, coming from east to west, blocks it, for its thickness is six [printed: ו"א], and its end finishes at that corner, within the hundred of the length of the inner court, at the corner of the Bet ha-Chalifot. Therefore there is no entry to that air of twenty, neither in the inner nor in the outer, unless it sloped and narrowed when the end of the wall between the two courts finished — in the thickness of the wall a cubit, for the entering of a man — and he enters into the air of five between the wall of the Chalifot and the wall of the chamber, and goes in that air toward the west ten cubits, and there the extent of the Bet ha-Chalifot ends, and he enters into the air of the breadth of twenty. And this is what it said, “a walk of ten cubits breadth, to come inward,” and “a way of one cubit,” for he enters it by way of an opening of one cubit, which sloped and narrowed at the end of the wall. And why does he call it a “walk of breadth,” and should not have said “a walk of ten cubits length”? Because with regard to the building of the Chalifot it is breadth, since the building of the Chalifot is fifteen from north to south and from east to west only eleven.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Translated literally from the printed Hebrew; the sense is not fully clear. The printed abbreviations ה"א and ו"א (possibly “five” and “six”) are left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: their doors were toward the north
Ezekiel.english_translation: The doors of these chambers are to the north — I found; and this is the explanation of “the north door” written above, where the speech was abbreviated, and here he explains it. (This belongs to Rashi at 42, verse 2, at the end of the comment above, and this is the explanation of Rabbi Shemaiah, and he wrote it from his own understanding — Tosafot.)
Ezekiel.translator_note: The final parenthetical is a printed editorial note, translated as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: I did not understand them at all.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the galleries took away from these
Ezekiel.english_translation: “For the *atikim* could” — like “they will eat”: eaters, and they diminish the air of the chambers.
That divides between the chambers and the outer court, on the east side.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the length thereof was fifty cubits
Ezekiel.english_translation: From north to south.
From north to south, fifty cubits.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: before the temple were a hundred cubits
Ezekiel.english_translation: From east to west, opposite the porch, the Hekhal, the house of the Kapporet, and the cells: a hundred cubits.

I do not know whether it comes to teach that they had passages beneath them, or comes to teach that there were chambers in the east of the court; and because the mountain slopes toward the east, he calls it “and from under these chambers,” for these are on its height and those on its low part. And so it says, “and in the low part of the court, to the entrance which is from the east, as one comes to them from the outer court.”

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: In the breadth of the wall of the court toward the east
Ezekiel.english_translation: One who comes from the east of the outer court and turns to the north by way of the north-east corner of the walls of the inner court, on the outside, to come to those chambers in the north, finds, “on the face of the wall of the court” — the east wall of the inner court, which is west of the outer — opposite the separate place and the building in the inner [court], chambers adjacent to that wall and standing in the outer [court]. I found.
Before these chambers there is a way, a breadth of air in the (outer) court, fifty cubits, “like the appearance of the way of the chambers which were toward the north,” written above.
Of the northern chambers — their length is the length of these, and likewise their breadth.
Like the exit of the northern chambers.
Of the northern chambers.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: so were also the doors of the chambers that were toward the south
Ezekiel.english_translation: The doors of the eastern chambers; for also in the south there were chambers separated from the southern cells by twenty cubits, as stated above, “And between the chambers was a breadth of twenty cubits,” from house to house round about.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: there was a door in the head of the way
Ezekiel.english_translation: The eastern chambers had a door at the head of a way, and the way was before the *gederet ha-ginah* — Targum Jonathan: *duchan* of the Levites; and the term *gederet ha-ginah* is a building of a stone fence made in steps, on which they played and sang.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: toward the way from the east
Ezekiel.english_translation: For the platform was in the east, as it is written in Chronicles, in the portion “And all the work was finished”: “also the Levites who were the singers, all of them, even Asaph, Heman, Jeduthun, etc., … stood at the east end of the altar.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: The printed portion name is *va-tishlam* (2 Chronicles 5); the quoted words are 2 Chronicles 5:12 (JPS wording).

Ezekiel.english_translation: When they enter those chambers to eat.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: shall they not go out of the holy place
Ezekiel.english_translation: From them, for they are holy.
In the holy garments that are upon them.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: there they shall lay their garments
Ezekiel.english_translation: “And shall approach to that which pertaineth to the people” — they may touch the garments of the people if they wish; but with the priestly garments they shall not touch the people, for these have degrees of purity, and ordinary garments are a *midras* to them.
The whole circumference of the Temple Mount, from the outside.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: He measured it by the four sides
Ezekiel.english_translation: Three thousand by three thousand cubits, since the reed is six [cubits]. And this is what the Kalir established (in the *kedushta* of the second day of Sukkot): “David will stretch the line — three thousand cubits measured by three thousand cubits, and it is thirty-six, like the first measure”; for the Temple Mount was five hundred cubits by five hundred cubits. Divide three thousand by three thousand into strips of five hundred cubits, warp and weft, and you will find there thirty-six squares of five hundred by five hundred; and therefore the poet said (there, in the *kedushta*), “thirty-six, as it was multiplied.” I found.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The quotations from the liturgical poem are translated as printed; I did not check them against the poem itself.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: it had a wall round about
Ezekiel.english_translation: For the Temple Mount.
Five hundred, warp and weft; this is the wall of the rampart that encircles the whole mountain.
To separate the people between the holy that is within and the profane that is outside. I found the completion of the whole measure (printed abbreviation: סא"א).
Ezekiel.translator_note: it is left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: he brought me to the gate
Ezekiel.english_translation: He returned and brought me into the east gate, and I saw the glory descending to the court.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the appearance of the vision which I saw
Ezekiel.english_translation: Nine visions are written in this verse, and from within them the prophets used to see, except for Moses our teacher, who saw from within one vision; therefore his lens shines and sees truly. And this is what the poet established (there, in the *silluk*): “the visions that are polished, in nine visions.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: The quotation is from a liturgical poem; I did not check it against the poem.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: when I came to destroy the city
Ezekiel.english_translation: In the portion “and set a mark” (above, 9), where it is said there, “Cause you them that have charge over the city to draw near,” and there he explained the likeness of the Chariot.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “above, 9” is Ezekiel 9:1 and 9:4 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_translation: He speaks with me. It is an honor to say that He speaks upward; like *mitdabber* (“conversing”): that is, He speaks between Himself and His glory, and the voice comes to me.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Rendered literally; the sense of “it is an honor to say upward” is not fully clear.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Because their houses were adjacent (to the cemetery), as we find with kings — with Solomon and with Athaliah — and sometimes they used to bury them within their house, as is explained: and he said, “in their setting of their threshold by My threshold.” I found.
*Va-ochal* — like *va-ochalah* and *kiliti* (“and I consumed … I finished”).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Now let them put away their harlotry
Ezekiel.english_translation: Even against their will they will keep their harlotry far, for I have set apart for Myself a wide surrounding boundary all around.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: that they may be ashamed of their iniquities
Ezekiel.english_translation: When I show them My kindness, that I do not reject them for their iniquity. I found.
And let them measure through you, for you instruct them in the reckoning of the building’s proportions.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: if they be ashamed of all that they have done
Ezekiel.english_translation: That they be ashamed and subdue their faces from all that they have done — then make known to them what I am destined to do for them.
And the boundary of the building, how it is from its front to its back, arranged to its four sides.
The reckoning of its cells and its chambers.
Cherubim, palm-figures, posts and porches. I found.
Not explained.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: that they may keep the whole form thereof
Ezekiel.english_translation: They shall learn the matters of the measures from your mouth, so that they will know to do them at the time of the end. I found. The second coming of Ezra was worthy to be like the first coming of Joshua, to come with a strong arm and with a miracle, as we expound “until [it] pass over”; and this building was due to them from then, when they went up from the exile, for an everlasting redemption; but sin caused that their repentance was not proper, so as not to sin, and they went out with the permission of Cyrus and built for themselves. And some say that in Babylon they stumbled with foreign [wives].
Ezekiel.translator_note: The words “until … pass over” are Rashi’s abbreviated quotation; the verse is not named.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: these are the measures of the altar
Ezekiel.english_translation: Which he explains below: fourteen long by fourteen wide.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the cubit is a cubit and a handbreadth
Ezekiel.english_translation: By a cubit of six [handbreadths], which is a cubit and a handbreadth in a cubit of five.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the bottom shall be a cubit
Ezekiel.english_translation: But the base, which was not measured by the ordinary cubit, which is of five — *cheik* is an expression of “its engraving,” fixedness; and it is the base: the cubit is the ordinary cubit, and not “a cubit and a handbreadth,” which is a cubit of six. And so we learned in Menachot, that the base and the surround and the horns are measured by a cubit of five.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The printed text says the base was “not” measured by the ordinary cubit, which seems to contradict the rest of the comment; translated as printed.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the bottom shall be a cubit
Ezekiel.english_translation: This is the base.
This is the surround.
These are the horns: one span from its middle he measured, a span in each direction — behold, a cubit by a cubit.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: this shall be the base of the altar
Ezekiel.english_translation: And by this cubit the top of the golden altar was measured, a cubit its length and a cubit its breadth, square; so it is explained in Eruvin, and in Menachot (page 97b) it is explained more fully by the reckoning: “the *cheik* of the cubit” in its height went up a cubit, and a cubit’s width it narrowed — the narrowing of the surround — by a cubit of five. But its rising which we learned, “it went up five and narrowed a cubit,” is not by a cubit of five.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Translated literally; the reckoning is compressed and its sense is not fully clear.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the border thereof by the edge thereof
Ezekiel.english_translation: The horns, both for their breadth and for their height, by a cubit of five.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: from the bottom upon the ground
Ezekiel.english_translation: From the base, from the ground of the earth.
Up to the top of the first frame.

And it was not so in the Eternal House [the Temple described in the Mishnah], for there we learned, “he brings a frame of thirty-two by thirty-two, and its height a cubit,” and here its height is two.

When he placed the second frame upon it, the second frame was thirty by thirty; thus there is an indentation to it all around, a cubit wide, and that is the base. Behold, it rose two and narrowed a cubit, and that is the base. Targum Jonathan: *azarah* — *mesamta*, an expression of a pavement, for he would fill the frame with chunks of stones, pitch, lime, *konya*, and melt and pour and smooth it on top, and behold, it is like a pavement.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The word *konya* is left untranslated. The Aramaic is translated as printed.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: from the lesser settle to the greater settle shall be four cubits
Ezekiel.english_translation: From the roof of the lower frame to the roof of the frame above it, four cubits in height.
It is the narrowing of the surround: it rose four and narrowed a cubit; this is the surround. And the lower he calls “small” because its height is only two, and the upper one’s height is four.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the hearth shall be four cubits
Ezekiel.english_translation: It is the height of the top of the altar from the surround upward; and in the Eternal House it was only three; and Targum Jonathan too: “and of the altar, four cubits.”

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: twelve cubits long by twelve broad
Ezekiel.english_translation: The place of the arrangement was twenty-four by twenty-four, and this is twelve by twelve.

For from its middle he measures twelve in each direction — behold, twenty-four by twenty-four. So it is explained in Zevachim, and so we learned in Tractate Middot: the altar was thirty-two by thirty-two; it went up a cubit and narrowed a cubit — this is the base — so it is thirty by thirty; it went up five and narrowed a cubit — this is the surround — so it is twenty-eight by twenty-eight; the place of the horns, a cubit on this side and a cubit on that side, so it is twenty-six by twenty-six; the place of the priests’ walking, a cubit on this side and a cubit on that side, so it is twenty-four by twenty-four, the place of the arrangement.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the settle shall be fourteen cubits long by fourteen broad
Ezekiel.english_translation: The top of the altar, with the place of the horns and the place of the priests’ feet, is twenty-eight by twenty-eight; and the fourteen mentioned here he measures from its middle, as is explained, “on its four sides.”
Targum Jonathan: *ve-gadnafa* (“and the edge”); and our Rabbis explained it as the horns.
He measures from its middle; thus a cubit by a cubit.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the bottom thereof shall be a cubit about
Ezekiel.english_translation: This is the narrowing of the base.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the steps thereof shall look toward the east
Ezekiel.english_translation: And the ramp by which one goes up it was on the south, so that the one going up on it faces east; for all the turns were to the right, and when you place the ramp on the south, the one going up on it and turning to the right faces east.
Who are of the tribe of Levi.
Since he was the High Priest who served first in the Temple in the days of Solomon, they were called by his name.
Of the altar.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the four corners of the settle
Ezekiel.english_translation: The top of the altar.
You shall wipe off from it its ordinary character, to bring it into holiness, that it be fit to atone upon it from now on.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the appointed place of the house
Ezekiel.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “in the place suited to the house,” that is, in a holy place. And the expression *be-mifkad ha-bayit* is a place where the house ends, like “there lacketh not (*lo nifkad*) one man of us” (Numbers 35). It is the bullock of the consecrations, in the way they did in the Tabernacle, and that bullock was burnt and not eaten. And so our Rabbis expounded in Menachot: they offered consecrations in the days of Ezra as they offered in the days of Moses.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “Numbers 35” is Numbers 31:49 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: thou shalt offer a he-goat without blemish for a sin-offering
Ezekiel.english_translation: This was not in the Tabernacle; and for the consecrations of the future, so they are, by the command.
From purifying.
For a burnt-offering.
An expression of favor.

Our Rabbis applied this verse to the southern wicket that the gate of the Hekhal had — a *pishpesh* is a small opening. So we learned in Tractate Middot: two wickets the great gate had, one in the south and one in the north; the one in the south no man ever entered by; concerning it Ezekiel spoke explicitly: “This gate shall be shut.”
In the future.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: As for the prince, being a prince
Ezekiel.english_translation: As for the prince, I give permission: he is a prince and an important person, and it is not his way to sit and eat with the other priests in the chambers.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: he shall sit therein to eat bread before the LORD
Ezekiel.english_translation: To eat bread within its space.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: he shall enter by the way of the porch of the gate
Ezekiel.english_translation: When he enters the inner court in order to enter this small gate to eat in it, by way of the porch of the gate of the court in the east he shall enter the court, and by the same way he shall return; when he returns he goes out by the way he came in. And because he says below (46), in the passage, “But when the people of the land shall come before the LORD in the appointed seasons, he that entereth by the way of …” etc., that He commanded to make the court a thoroughfare (*kapandarya*) — because that coming is to appear before [Him] and it must look beautiful — it was necessary to say here regarding the comings of all the days of the year that he not make it a thoroughfare, because this coming is not for appearing before [Him] like that of the festivals; and so he testified further below in the passage many times.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “below (46)” is Ezekiel 46:9 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: As for the prince, being a prince
Ezekiel.english_translation: I found. “As for the prince”: the High Priest. He is a prince, and because of his importance he is permitted to eat flesh and bread of holy things in that gate, which they open for him at the time of his eating.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The source gives no lemma here; the phrase from the verse is used.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: he shall enter by the way of the porch of the gate
Ezekiel.english_translation: By way of the porch of the eastern gate he shall enter the court and come to that wicket to eat his bread in it.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: shall go out by the way of the same
Ezekiel.english_translation: For this is not fit to be a thoroughfare like the other gates, and all the day, when it is not at the time of the prince’s eating, it shall be shut. (printed abbreviation: סא"א)
Ezekiel.translator_note: it is left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Whose deeds have made themselves strangers to their Father in heaven; and they are uncircumcised in heart.
A priest whose brothers died because of circumcision.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: you have set keepers of My charge in My sanctuary to please yourselves
Ezekiel.english_translation: You set for yourselves, by your own opinion, in My sanctuary, murderous men who are not fit to be keepers of My charge.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: But the Levites, that went far from Me
Ezekiel.english_translation: But rather, thus you shall do to them: the Levites who went far from Me (and became idolatrous priests) and have now repented.
From approaching My altar any more. “*Pekudot* of the gates of the house”: *pekudot* — *comandises* [printed קומנדישא"ש] in Old French — they shall be guards and officers.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Godefroy (a secondary reference; not Darmesteter) lists *commandise* and glosses it “commandement, ordre, domination”; the printed form appears to be that word, but it was not found in Darmesteter.

Ezekiel.english_translation: A service that is valid when done by strangers, by slaves and by women.
Idolatrous priests for the idolaters, to draw them to it.
Of the tribe of Levi.
Since he was the High Priest who served first in the Temple in the days of Solomon, they were called by his name.
*[printed Old French: קנאינשר"ר]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the gates of the inner court
Ezekiel.english_translation: In the innermost, on Yom Kippur.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The printed abbreviation בי"ה is read as Yom Kippur from the context (the High Priest’s inner service).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: no wool shall come upon them
Ezekiel.english_translation: The blue wool that was in the robe and in the sash he shall not wear on Yom Kippur in the inner service.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The printed abbreviation בי"ה is read as Yom Kippur from the context.

Ezekiel.english_translation: And inward.
*Capeles* [printed קאפייל"ש] in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: It appears to be *chapels* (“hats”), but the form was not found in Darmesteter.

Ezekiel.english_translation: We learned in a baraita: they do not gird at a place where they sweat, neither above their armpits nor below their hips, which is a place of sweat — *enlaçure* [printed אנלאשויי"רא] in Old French. Another version: the Torah forbade the priests woolen garments, for wool causes the body to sweat and causes the flesh to sweat. (printed abbreviation: סא"א)
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. Godefroy (a secondary reference) lists *enlaceure / enlaçure* and glosses it “enlacement” (“binding”), which fits girding. it is left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Since he was speaking about the Hekhal, “inner,” and he called them “the inner court,” and beside them he should call the Court of Israel “the outer court,” it was therefore necessary to repeat it twice, to say that he speaks of the Women’s Court, the place where all Israel enter.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: lay them in the holy chambers
Ezekiel.english_translation: As Moses our teacher said (Leviticus 16:23): “and shall put off the linen garments, which he put on … and shall leave them there.”

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: that they sanctify not the people with their garments
Ezekiel.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “and they shall not mingle with the people in their garments” — that is, they shall not touch the people with their holy garments, for ordinary garments are not pure relative to holy garments.
To remove all the hair.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: nor suffer their locks to grow long
Ezekiel.english_translation: They shall not let hair grow long.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: they shall only poll their heads
Ezekiel.english_translation: Like this spelt (*kusemet*), whose [grains] are arranged on the ear, the head of one toward the root of the other: so I heard in the name of Rabbi Menahem, of blessed memory. And it is possible to explain it as an expression of measure: of a thing that is level — neither a shearing of the head nor a growing of hair, but in an equal measure; *amoler* [printed אמולי"ר] in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this verse (Ezekiel 44:20) with forms such as אמולל and אמוניר and glosses it “taillant les cheveux en les égalisant” (“cutting the hair, making it even”). The printed spelling differs slightly from his.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: when they enter into the inner court
Ezekiel.english_translation: Into the Hekhal.

The High Priests shall take [virgins]; but there are priests who take the widow, such as ordinary ones, and this is “of a priest they shall take”: there are among the priests those who are permitted a widow. I found.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: a widow that is the widow of a priest
Ezekiel.english_translation: A true widow, excluding a divorcée and a *chalutzah*; though she is unmarried she is forbidden even to an ordinary [priest].
After his withdrawal from the dead; so it is taught in [printed: מ"ק].
Ezekiel.translator_note: The printed abbreviation מ"ק is not resolved here; it is left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: When first he enters the holy place to be initiated for the service, he shall offer his sin-offering — this is his tenth of an ephah. So it is taught in [printed: מ"ק], that an ordinary priest is obligated to bring a tenth of an ephah on the day of his initiation, as it is said (there, 6), “This is the offering of Aaron and of his sons,” etc., and as is explained in Tractate Menachot.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The printed abbreviation מ"ק is not resolved here; it is left as printed. Printed “there, 6” is Leviticus 6:13 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: it shall be unto them for an inheritance
Ezekiel.english_translation: The priesthood, as an inheritance.
An expression of “holy”; and so every expression of *cherem* that is applied to a holy thing.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: to cause a blessing to rest on thy house
Ezekiel.english_translation: *Apoiser* [printed אפושי"ר] in Old French, like “and rested in all the borders of Egypt” (Exodus 8:12).
Ezekiel.translator_note: It appears to be a form of *apaiser* (“to calm, to settle”), but was not found in Darmesteter. Printed “Exodus 8:12” is Exodus 10:14 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: any thing that dieth of itself, or is torn
Ezekiel.english_translation: Since the pinching of a bird’s sin-offering, which is a *nevelah* and *terefah*, was permitted to them, it was necessary to warn them regarding other *nevelot* and *terefot*; so our Rabbis explained.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: when you shall divide by lot the land for inheritance
Ezekiel.english_translation: For they are destined to divide the Land of Israel into twelve strips — not like the first division, which was for the large according to its number and for the small according to its census, and two or three tribes were in one strip; now the portions are equal, and like the rows of a vineyard, from the west sea to the east side, as is explained at the end of the book.
To build the Temple in it.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Of this there shall be for the holy place
Ezekiel.english_translation: Of this offering there shall be, for the need of the Holy Place of the Temple Mount, five hundred reeds, and the remainder for the houses of the priests, as is explained at the end of the book.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: of this measure shalt thou measure
Ezekiel.english_translation: By the measuring reed by which the square of the Temple Mount, five hundred by five hundred, was measured, as is said in the passage above (42): “He measured it by the four sides; it had a wall round about, the length five hundred,” etc.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “(42)” is Ezekiel 42:20 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: a length of five and twenty thousand
Ezekiel.english_translation: Twenty-five thousand reeds, and a breadth of ten thousand reeds. And because it did not explain in the first verse what the twenty-five thousand are — whether reeds or cubits — it was necessary to say that those thousands are measured for the offering by the same measuring reed by which the five hundred by five hundred of the Temple Mount were measured.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: It is a holy portion of the land
Ezekiel.english_translation: He transposed the verse: the surplus of the holy place which is of the land shall be for the priests, the ministers of the sanctuary, who offer, etc.; “a holy portion of the land” is this offering.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: it shall be for the priests, the ministers of the sanctuary
Ezekiel.english_translation: The surplus beyond the five hundred of the Temple Mount: twelve thousand two hundred and fifty to the east and the same to the west, with the Temple in the middle, and four thousand seven hundred and fifty to the north and the same to the south.
This surplus that is around the Temple.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: a place consecrated for the sanctuary
Ezekiel.english_translation: And the five hundred by five hundred in the middle shall be sanctified for the need of the Temple — *[printed Old French: אישיינטיג"יאה אלשיינטואיירא]* in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: five and twenty thousand in length
Ezekiel.english_translation: Reeds in length and ten thousand in breadth. You shall set apart another strip beside this one, to the south of it, for the need of the Levites; so it is explained at the end of the book, that it is in the south. I found. Twenty chambers shall the Levites have around the Temple, to guard the House and for beauty, and the remainder of the strips they shall make for their needs. (Tosafot)
Ezekiel.translator_note: The final “(Tosafot)” marks a printed supplementary note.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Around the city: a holding of ordinary dwelling for it, in which Israel may build houses.
South of the second, and the length as the measure of the two strips; thus the whole offering is square, twenty-five thousand by twenty-five thousand.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: side by side with the offering of the holy portion
Ezekiel.english_translation: That is, in the length-measure of the strips of the holy offering.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: it shall be for the whole house of Israel
Ezekiel.english_translation: That third strip shall be a dwelling for outsiders.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: And for the prince, on the one side and on the other side
Ezekiel.english_translation: At the end of the section he divides the Land of Israel, from its east to its west, into thirteen strips — twelve for the number of the tribes, each twenty-five thousand reeds in breadth, and their length as the length of the whole Land of Israel — and one strip for the offering, its length from the east border to the west border, and its breadth twenty-five thousand reeds, like each other portion. And from that strip he sets apart, in its middle, these three strips mentioned above, which are twenty-five thousand by twenty-five thousand; and the surplus beyond them to the east, to the end of the border of the land, and likewise to the west, shall be for the prince on this side and that, to the east and to the west.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: in front of the holy offering and in front of the possession of the city
Ezekiel.english_translation: Corresponding to the whole breadth of the three strips set apart: for the holy offering, the strip of the priests and Levites, and the possession of the city.
From the west of the holy offering and the city to the west of the border.

And from the east of the offering to the boundary on the east, corresponding to one of the portions of the tribes that are explained at the end of the book, which run from the sea border of the Land of Israel to the eastern border.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: of the land; it shall be to him for a possession in Israel
Ezekiel.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “this land shall be great for an inheritance.”

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: shall no more wrong My people
Ezekiel.english_translation: An expression of monetary wronging (*ona’ah*), in that they rob them of their inheritance.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: take away your exactions from My people
Ezekiel.english_translation: Remove that by which you drive My people out of their inheritance.
For the dry measure.
For the liquid measure.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: The ephah and the bath shall be of one measure
Ezekiel.english_translation: An expression of measure; the homer and the kor — *muid* [printed מוי"י] in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: It appears to be *muid*, a measure of capacity; Godefroy (a secondary reference) lists *muid* as a measure of capacity. The form was not found in Darmesteter.

Ezekiel.english_translation: An expression of counting, like “yet shall you deliver the tale of bricks” (Exodus 5:18): one measure — this is a tenth of a homer of the dry [measure], which is thirty *se’ah*, and this is a tenth of a homer of the liquid.
Like “to take”; and so Targum Jonathan: *le-musav* (“to take”) — “from the tenth of the homer shall the bath be,” and likewise a tenth of the dry homer.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the measure thereof shall be after the homer
Ezekiel.english_translation: The total reckoning of the bath and the ephah shall be according to the size of the homer. I found. If they add to the homer, they add to the bath; if they diminish it from this, they diminish it from this, so that its tenth matches it.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the shekel shall be twenty gerahs
Ezekiel.english_translation: Twenty *ma‘ah*.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: twenty shekels, five and twenty shekels, ten, and five shekels
Ezekiel.english_translation: Behold, sixty shekels.

*[printed Old French: לוצונ"ט]* in Old French; and Menahem connected it with an expression of counting. And behold, there are here two hundred and forty *zuz*; from this, that the holy maneh was double, and in the days of Ezekiel a sixth was added to it — behold, two hundred and forty. And when Scripture divided it into three, and did not simply write “sixty shekels shall be your maneh,” He commanded to make from it the weight of its third and the weight of its fourth and the weight of the ordinary maneh which it was at first. And so Targum Jonathan: “thirds of a maneh, twenty selas; a maneh of silver, twenty-five selas; fourths of a maneh, fifteen selas — all of them sixty; and the great maneh, the holy one, shall be for you.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. The Aramaic is translated as printed.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the sixth part of an ephah out of a homer of wheat
Ezekiel.english_translation: Behold, one-sixtieth: one who diminishes shall not diminish below this; and this is what they said: a stingy eye, one in sixty.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the sixth part of an ephah out of a homer of barley
Ezekiel.english_translation: And you shall divide one-sixth of an ephah for the offering of a homer of barley.
For the tithe.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the tithe of the bath out of the cor
Ezekiel.english_translation: The bath, which is the measure of oil — this is the tithe of the bath shall be out of the kor, I found; the tithing: that the bath tithes the kor shall be. How? (The tithe of the bath out of the kor: a tenth of a bath of the kor — *dix mesures* [printed די"ץ מזור"ש] in Old French. This word serves for itself and for others, like “the service of the holy” and “the service of the sons of Merari.” Printed abbreviation: סא"א.)
Ezekiel.translator_note: Translated literally; the sense is not fully clear. it is left as printed. Darmesteter lists this verse (Ezekiel 45:14, “עשרת הבתים”) with a form read as *dix mesures* (a single manuscript) and glosses it “dix mesures” (“ten measures”).

Ezekiel.english_translation: The homer shall be for you, and then it is possible to take from it one bath as a tithe.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: for ten baths are a homer
Ezekiel.english_translation: Since the homer will be ten baths for you; and so Jonathan translated: “one of ten is a bath of a kor, for ten baths are a kor.”
The choicest of his flock; and so Moses said, “all your choice vows” (Deuteronomy 12:11) — *le meilleur* [printed לומיי"לור] in Old French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: It appears to be *le meilleur* (“the best”), but the form was not found in Darmesteter. The verse is not named in the printed text; it is Deuteronomy 12:11 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_translation: Our Rabbis expounded this with regard to the libations: from the surplus of two hundred that remained in a pit into which fell wine of *orlah* or of *kilayim* of the vineyard; from here, that *orlah* and *kilayim* of the vineyard are nullified in two hundred.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: from the well-watered pastures of Israel
Ezekiel.english_translation: From what is permitted to Israel: all their offerings shall be a drink that is fit for Israel; the whole essence of the meal is called by the name of the drink — that is, the eating with the drinking shall be from what is permitted to Israel.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: All the people of the land shall give this offering
Ezekiel.english_translation: The [offering] mentioned above shall be with the knowledge of all the people of the land.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: it shall be the prince’s part
Ezekiel.english_translation: I say that this prince speaks of the High Priest, and so every “prince” in the passage; and I heard in the name of Rabbi Menahem that it speaks of the king.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: thou shalt take a young bullock without blemish
Ezekiel.english_translation: It is the bullock of the consecrations mentioned at the beginning of the section, and he teaches here that the consecrations shall be on the first of Nisan.
And you shall purify.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: thou shalt do on the seventh day of the month
Ezekiel.english_translation: One may say: “and so you shall do” every seven [days]; and so it says above, “seven days they shall make atonement for the altar”; and our Rabbis so explained it in Menachot: and so you shall do — a bullock that is not eaten — for the seven tribes who innovated a matter and their court ruled that fat is permitted, and the seven tribes, who are the majority of the congregation, acted according to their ruling: they bring a bullock for the unwitting error of a matter.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Translated literally; the sense is not fully clear.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: for every one that erreth, and for him that is simple
Ezekiel.english_translation: Behold, this verse is transposed: “and you shall make atonement for the house — for every one that erreth and for him that is simple.” After the seven days of consecration, when the altar is initiated, they shall bring their sin-offerings and guilt-offerings and be atoned; for when Israel is atoned the House is atoned.
Because from it they begin to count seven weeks. I found.
Matzot shall be eaten on it, on the festival.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: upon that day shall the prince prepare
Ezekiel.english_translation: Our Rabbis said that they wished to hide the Book of Ezekiel, because its words contradict the words of the Torah; but remembered for good be Hananiah son of Hezekiah son of Garon, who sat in an upper room and expounded it. But because of our iniquities what he expounded regarding the offerings is hidden from us: “a bullock on the fourteenth of Nisan — why?” And I say: perhaps on the fourteenth of Nisan of the first Passover on which the House was initiated, and this bullock comes in place of the calf, a young bull, that Aaron offered on the eighth day of the consecrations; and it tells that if they did not offer it on the eighth day of the consecrations, let them offer it on the fourteenth of Nisan, in order that he be initiated for service before the festival, because upon him are the offerings and the burnt-offering of the festival to do, as it says above, “and it shall be the prince’s part to give the burnt-offerings, and the meal-offerings, and the drink-offerings, in the feasts,” etc.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: seven bullocks and seven rams without blemish daily the seven days
Ezekiel.english_translation: And the Torah said, “young bullocks, two, and one ram”; I cannot establish this verse except as seven bullocks and seven rams for the seven days, a bullock a day and a ram a day, and it comes to teach that the bullocks do not hinder one another, nor do the rams hinder one another; and so we learned in Menachot. But they did not bring proof from this verse, but from the verse said below (46), “and in the day of the new moon a young bullock without blemish, and six lambs, and a ram”; and perhaps this one too comes to teach so. And so its explanation: seven bullocks and seven rams a day — adding together “day by day,” seven bullocks go up for the seven days.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The words “young bullocks, two, and one ram” are Rashi’s abbreviated quotation from the Torah; the passage below is Ezekiel 46:6.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: a he-goat daily for a sin-offering
Ezekiel.english_translation: The he-goats of the festivals.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: a meal-offering, an ephah for a bullock
Ezekiel.english_translation: The meal-offering of the libations: “an ephah for a bullock” — I do not know what it is, for the Torah said three tenths; and one may say, an ephah of flour, from which to take out a tenth of fine flour from the *se’ah*, for an ephah is three *se’ah*. “And an ephah for a bullock” teaches you that if he does not find fine flour sifted so much, he brings from [flour of] a tenth per *se’ah*.
This too is flour, from which to take out two tenths of fine flour, sifted as fully as needed, as we learned: the two loaves, two tenths from three *se’ah*.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: a hin of oil to an ephah
Ezekiel.english_translation: I did not know why; and one may say that he did not offer the whole hin, but there were marks in the hin, and he would offer oil according to the fine flour, as the law of the sacrifice: for the bullock according to its law, and for the ram according to its law, according to the marks of the hin.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: The gate of the inner court that looketh toward the east
Ezekiel.english_translation: Our Rabbis taught in Tractate Middot: two wickets the gate of the Hekhal had, one in the south and one in the north; the one in the south, of it it is explained in the Tradition (above, 44), “neither shall any man enter in by it,” and it was shut.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “above, 44” is Ezekiel 44:2 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: by the way of the porch of the gate without
Ezekiel.english_translation: As is said above, “and the arches thereof were toward the outer court” — by the porch of the gate of the court; that is, he shall enter by the way of the eastern gate, which serves as entrance and exit, and come to that wicket.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The quoted words are Ezekiel 40:31 (JPS wording).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: stand by the post of the gate
Ezekiel.english_translation: That small gate is the wicket.
A burnt-offering of appearance and peace-offerings of the festival offering; and this verse refers to a festival day. So I found in exact commentaries.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: stand by the post of the gate
Ezekiel.english_translation: The gate of the inner [court] is the one that he explained — it is the wicket — as the master said: Is it possible that a man’s offering is offered and he does not stand over it?

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the gate shall not be shut until the evening
Ezekiel.english_translation: Why shall it not be shut?

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the people of the land shall worship
Ezekiel.english_translation: All the day, and also all who come; and toward evening they shall shut it.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: in the sabbath day six lambs without blemish and a ram without blemish
Ezekiel.english_translation: I did not know why, for the Torah said “two he-lambs” (Numbers 28); and “on the sabbath day” implies the Sabbath of Creation, and it implies a festival. And I say that this Sabbath is not the Sabbath of Creation but a festival, which requires seven lambs and two rams; and it comes to teach you that they do not hinder one another: if he does not find seven he brings six, and if he does not find two rams he brings one, as the Sages expounded regarding the new moon.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “Numbers 28” is Numbers 28:9 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: as he is able to give
Ezekiel.english_translation: He taught that the meal-offerings do not hinder one another.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: in the day of the new moon it shall be a young bullock without blemish
Ezekiel.english_translation: Our Rabbis expounded this verse in Menachot: “bullock” — what does it teach? Since it is said in the Torah, “and in your new moons … two young bullocks,” from where [do we learn] that if he does not find two he brings one? Therefore it says “bullock.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: The quoted words are Numbers 28:11 (JPS wording).

Ezekiel.english_translation: What does it teach? Since it is said in the Torah “seven,” from where [do we learn] that if he does not find seven he brings six? Therefore it says “and six lambs.” And from where [that he may bring] even one? The Talmud says: “and for the lambs according as his means suffice.” I found.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The quoted words are Ezekiel 46:7 (JPS wording).

Ezekiel.english_translation: On the new moon and on the Sabbath of Creation, when Israel are not commanded regarding appearing, and he comes to worship.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: by the way of the porch of the gate
Ezekiel.english_translation: He goes out by that same gate. He is not commanded to make the Temple Court a shortcut; but on the festivals, regarding which it is said (Deuteronomy 16) “shall all thy males appear,” he too is obliged to make it a shortcut like the rest of the people. This is what is written, “in the midst of them: when they go in he shall go in, and when they go forth they shall go forth.”

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: But when the people of the land shall come before the LORD
Ezekiel.english_translation: It is a commandment upon them to be seen within the Temple Court well (literally “well, well”).

He too, when he enters the Temple Court to come in by the southern wicket of the Temple in order to prostrate himself, is commanded to make the Temple Court a shortcut. He comes in by the north gate and goes out by the south gate with the rest of the people of the land, and he enters and goes out straight ahead by the other gate. This is “in the midst of them: when they go in he shall go in, and when they go forth they shall go forth” — all of them, the prince with the rest of the people. He does not come by the east gate, as he does on the day of the New Moon and on the Sabbath of Creation, because there is no gate opposite the east gate in the west.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The phrase printed here, “Sabbath of Creation” (shabbat bereshit), appears to mean an ordinary weekly Sabbath.
