Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: And when the prince shall prepare a freewill-offering
Ezekiel.english_translation: On the six working days.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: one shall open for him the gate
Ezekiel.english_translation: He does not enter the Temple by it but stands there, and the priests prepare his burnt-offering and his peace-offerings, and he prostrates himself and goes out. For it is said, “as he doth on the sabbath day.” And what does it say about the sabbath day? (Here) “and shall stand by the post of the gate, and the priests shall prepare his burnt-offering…”

It does not say here “but the gate shall not be shut until the evening,” as it says about the sabbath day. For about the sabbath day it says “the people of the land shall worship at the door of that gate”; therefore it is left open. But on a weekday it is not their way to come to prostrate themselves, since each one is busy with his work; therefore “after his going forth one shall shut the gate.”

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: a lamb of the first year
Ezekiel.english_translation: The daily burnt-offering (olat hatamid).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the sixth part of an ephah
Ezekiel.english_translation: A Jerusalem (ephah), which is a fifth of a wilderness (ephah). And they are two tenth-parts (issarons): one for the daily meal-offering and one for the griddle-cakes. Even though the griddle-cakes are offered in halves, he brings a whole tenth-part in the morning and divides it, as we learned in (tractate) Menachot.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Translated literally as printed (“a fifth of a wilderness one”); I did not interpret the comparison further.

Ezekiel.english_translation: “To rus the fine flour”: ilperisir in French. Another explanation: imlelir in French. “To rus the fine flour” means to crush it and to mix the flour with it. It is an expression of resisim (fragments), as in (Amos 6:11) “and the great house shall be smitten into splinters,” and an expression of the Mishnah: “if it was thick or crushed (merussas).”
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. Amos 6:11 is quoted in JPS wording (JPS “splinters” for Rashi’s resisim).

Ezekiel.english_translation: The Jubilee year.
Like ve-shavah (“and it shall return”).

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: but as for his inheritance, it shall be for his sons
Ezekiel.english_translation: Like “but his inheritance shall be for his sons,” and it shall not be given permanently to another.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Then he brought me through the entry
Ezekiel.english_translation: By way of the passage (ha-amah) in the corner of the Beit HaChalifot, by which one enters the twenty-cubit open space between the chambers in the north and the side-chambers of the Temple.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed ha-amah (“the cubit”); it could mean a cubit-wide passage or a channel, and Beit HaChalifot is left untranslated. I did not resolve either.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: which was at the side of the gate
Ezekiel.english_translation: The north gate. “The side of the gate” is that which is from the gate to the west.
For they have doors toward the outer court on the north, and they had doors toward the twenty-cubit open space.
At the end of the chambers, to the west.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: that they bring them not forth
Ezekiel.english_translation: Like “to bring them forth,” for the most holy things are disqualified by going out (of the court).
Targum Jonathan: “to mingle with the people.”

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: in every corner of the court
Ezekiel.english_translation: Anglesh in French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: It appears to be Old French *angle* (“corner”), but the form was not found in Darmesteter.

Ezekiel.english_translation: We learned in tractate Middot: “ketorot” means nothing other than that they are not roofed, and there it explains what they were used for.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: In the four corners of the court
Ezekiel.english_translation: At the angle of the corners of the court.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: And there was a row of masonry round about in them
Ezekiel.english_translation: A row of a course: a wall of stones projecting from the wall near the ground, with holes in it, the place for setting pots. Beneath the row is a hollow in which to kindle a fire beneath, with the pots above.
It is the hollow beneath the setting of the pots.
The breast and thigh of the peace-offerings, which are not disqualified by going out beyond the Israelites’ Court, as the sin-offering and the guilt-offering are.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The printed wording is “like the sin-offering and the guilt-offering”; read in context, it means that those are disqualified and the peace-offerings are not.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Into the inner court.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: unto the door of the house
Ezekiel.english_translation: And the waters descend from beneath the right shoulder of the house, welling up from beneath the threshold, which is in the middle of the east, and they turn aside diagonally to the right and go out from the Temple Court on the south of the altar, and go out beyond the city. In tractate Yoma we learned: Rabbi Pinchas said in the name of Rav Huna Tzippora’ah: The spring that issues from the Holy of Holies is at first like the horns of sela’im; when it reached the opening of the Hekhal it became like a thread of the warp; when it reached the opening of the Ulam it became like a thread of the woof; when it reached the opening of the Temple Court it became like the mouth of a small flask.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Two words are left as printed: sela’im (printed סלעים) and Tzippora’ah (printed צפוראה, possibly “of Tzippori”). I did not choose a meaning for either.

Ezekiel.english_translation: From the inner court to the outer court, by the north gate.
Around the wall of the inner (court), within the outer.
The outer one, which faces east.
Bouyant in French: wide, like the width of the mouth of the flask. So our Rabbis explained, as above.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this word (Ezekiel 47:2) with the gloss “Eaux courantes” (flowing waters); his forms are spelled slightly differently from the printed one.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: waters that were to the ankles
Ezekiel.english_translation: Outside the wall. And throughout all those thousand cubits the stream did not grow deeper than afsayim, which are the ankles, called kavilish in French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this word (Ezekiel 47:3) with the gloss “Des chevilles” (ankles); his forms are spelled slightly differently from the printed one.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Others; and they deepened to the knees, and another thousand and they deepened to the loins. From here on, “a river that could not be passed through.” From this (we learn) that it is forbidden to enter water from the loins upward, lest the water sweep him away. When he came to the waters of the loins he went out onto the bank of the river and measured another thousand ahead of him, “a river that could not be passed through,” while his feet stood on dry land. This is what is written, “and caused me to return to the bank of the river,” that is, beside the bank of the river, where he was standing.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The printed Hebrew form differs slightly from the wording of 47:6; JPS wording is quoted.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Like “they grew large.”

Nuerinant in French: waters in which one must swim, and not cross on foot, lest they sweep him away. Shachu means swimming, as in (Isaiah 25:11) “as he that swimmeth spreadeth forth his hands to swim.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this word (Ezekiel 47:5) with the gloss “Eaux de nage (guéables)” and forms such as נואיר; the printed form is longer.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Hast thou seen this, O son of man?
Ezekiel.english_translation: How much this stream is growing stronger.
While he led me and brought me back, there sprouted on the bank of the river very many trees on this side and on that: a tree, aabirets in French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. It may correspond to *arbres* (“trees”), but I did not find it in Darmesteter.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Lamarka in French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this word (Ezekiel 47:8) with the gloss “La frontière” (the frontier), in forms such as מרישק; the printed form is spelled differently.

Ezekiel.english_translation: The eastern one. Our Rabbis taught in the Tosefta of Sukkah: Where do they (the waters) go? To the Sea of Tiberias, and to the Sea of Sodom, and to the Great Sea, to heal their salty waters and to sweeten them.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed לרפות (lerapot, literally “to weaken/ease”); rendered “to heal” to match the verse’s “shall be healed.”

Ezekiel.english_translation: This is the Sea of Tiberias.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: when they shall enter into the sea
Ezekiel.english_translation: This is the Sea of Sodom.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: into the sea of the putrid waters
Ezekiel.english_translation: This is the sea of the Ocean, which goes out (motsi) from the inhabited world to encircle the world.
The waters, of their saltiness. And an aggadic midrash: Why does it call them “motsa’im”? Because of the two times that they went out.
This river, which divides into several rivers, sweetens the waters that mingle with it, and their fish that swarm in them are alive and sweet.
For a net (mikhmoret).
The heh has no mappiq, and its meaning is: their fish shall be of many kinds.
An expression of many kinds, like (Exodus 7:18) “And the fish that are in the river,” (Isaiah 51) “All the sighing thereof have I made to cease.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 51”; the quoted words are Isaiah 21:2 (JPS wording quoted).

Ezekiel.english_translation: Of the sea, like (Job 8:11) “Can the rush shoot up without mire?” Marash in French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Like (2 Kings 3:16) “Make this valley full of trenches.” The bitsim are the bitsa’im (swamps) around it, and the gevim are the clefts in which the water gathers.
The opposite of sweetening. Why? Because they are given for salt.
This vav is subsidiary and superfluous.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: it shall bring forth new fruit every month
Ezekiel.english_translation: Month by month it will ripen its fruits.

Our Rabbis of blessed memory explained: to loosen the mouth of the dumb and the mouth of the barren. Its meaning is an expression of healing, like (Jeremiah 10) “They have healed also the hurt of My people lightly,” and so Menachem joined it.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “Jeremiah 10”; the quoted words are Jeremiah 6:14 (also 8:11). JPS wording of 6:14 quoted.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “this is the boundary,” like “this border.” And likewise (above, 25) *ve-netattikha le-vag la-goyim*, as though *le-vaz la-goyim* (“for a spoil to the nations”). Another possibility is to interpret *geh* as an expression of *gay* (“valley”).
Ezekiel.translator_note: The printed reference “25” is Ezekiel 25:7.

Ezekiel.english_translation: Joseph shall take two portions: one for Manasseh and one for Ephraim.

Not as at the first (division), each according to his numbered ones, but now all the tribes are equal; and like a row of a vineyard, each portion extends from the eastern border to the Ocean Sea in the west, as is explained in the passage, and no two tribes are in one strip.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: And this shall be the border of the land
Ezekiel.english_translation: The limits and boundaries of the Land of Israel.
The northern direction.
Which is the border on the west.
It comes to the east side, to Hethlon, and to Zedad, and to Hamath, and Berothah, and Sibraim; all these towns are on the northern boundary.
Targum Jonathan: “the pool of Agbai.”

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: which is by the border of Hauran
Ezekiel.english_translation: The border of Damascus in the east, near the corner.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: And the border from the sea shall be Hazar-enon
Ezekiel.english_translation: And the border of the northern side shall be from the sea to Hazar-enon.

That is, it is on the border of Damascus, for Hazar-enan is in the north-eastern corner, as is explained in the borders that Moses our teacher wrote (Numbers 34:10): “and the goings out thereof shall be at Hazar-enan,” etc.; “And you shall mark out your line for the east border from Hazar-enan,” etc. The border of Damascus is in the north-eastern corner beside Hazar-enan, as is said above, “Hazar-enon and the border of Damascus.” And the border of Hamath is in the north-western corner, as it is said (ibid.): “And this shall be your north border: from the Great Sea you shall mark out your line unto mount Hor; from mount Hor you shall mark out a line unto the entrance to Hamath”; and from there, Zedad.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Printed “Numbers 34:10”; the words “and the goings out thereof shall be at Hazar-enan” are Numbers 34:9, and “you shall mark out your line for the east border from Hazar-enan” is 34:10. JPS wording quoted.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: northward is the border of Hamath
Ezekiel.english_translation: That is, all the northern boundary specified in the Torah, and the border of Hamath, which is also on the northern boundary, as it is said (ibid.): “from the Great Sea you shall mark out your line unto mount Hor; from mount Hor you shall mark out a line unto the entrance to Hamath; and the goings out of the border shall be at Zedad.” This is the Zedad mentioned here: “by the way of Hethlon, unto the entrance of Zedad.”
And behold, you have the north side.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: between Hauran and Damascus and Gilead, and the land of Israel
Ezekiel.english_translation: The eastern boundary of the Land of Canaan. Transjordan is not within these boundaries, but only the Land of Canaan alone; so too in the boundaries delimited in the Torah, Transjordan is not within them. So too is the interpretation of this verse: “and the eastern boundary of the Land of Canaan, which is between Hauran and Damascus, which stand beside it in the north-eastern corner, as is said above in the passage, and between Gilead and the Land of Israel, which is across the Jordan, eastward.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: Translated as printed; I could not tell what “which is across the Jordan, eastward” refers back to.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: from the border unto the east sea shall you measure
Ezekiel.english_translation: The Jordan is its eastern boundary, from the border of the northern corner, which is the Hazar-enan explained above, to the eastern sea, which is the Salt Sea, in the south-eastern corner. “You shall measure” the length of the eastern boundary. In the Torah too it is explained so regarding the eastern border: “and the goings out thereof shall be at the Salt Sea,” in the southern corner.
That is, behold, you have the east side.
From Jericho, which is the city of palm trees (temarim), and so Targum Jonathan.
It is the wilderness of Zin.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: to the Brook, unto the Great Sea
Ezekiel.english_translation: And from there the border goes to the Brook of Egypt, which falls into the Great Sea in the south-western corner. And Moses also gave the southern (negev) border thus: from the wilderness of Zin by way of Edom, and he enumerates on to Azmon, the Brook of Egypt, “and the goings out thereof shall be at the Sea.” The word nachalah mentioned here is like lenachalah, and I found it translated achsana (“inheritance”); and were it not that the accent is below, and I saw nachalah Mitzrayim, where the accent is above, and the Masorah on it says “none in the accent,” I would say it is a corruption, and Jonathan did not translate so, but readers err.
Ezekiel.translator_note: This last passage is difficult; it is translated as literally as possible and I could not confirm its sense. The Aramaic (achsana, “none in the accent”) is translated as printed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: And the western boundary.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the Great Sea, from the border as far as over against the entrance of Hamath
Ezekiel.english_translation: From the southern corner mentioned above, which is the Brook of Egypt.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: as far as over against the entrance of Hamath
Ezekiel.english_translation: To the north-western corner, which is mount Hor, which is opposite the entrance of Hamath, for Hamath is in the north-western corner beside mount Hor, as it is written: “from the Great Sea you shall mark out your line unto mount Hor; from mount Hor you shall mark out a line unto the entrance to Hamath.” I found.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The printed text ends with the word matsati (“I found”); left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: in what tribe the stranger sojourneth
Ezekiel.english_translation: Who converted in the Exile, within that tribe.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: Now these are the names of the tribes
Ezekiel.english_translation: The order of the portions in which they shall divide it among themselves: the place of each and every one.
Dan shall take the northern border from Hazar-enan, which is in the eastern corner, which extends to the border of Damascus (which is in the corner of the west-north, סא"א).
Ezekiel.translator_note: it is left as printed.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: and they shall have their sides east and west
Ezekiel.english_translation: That is, from the east side to the sea, Dan one. Behold, it has specified the length and has not specified the breadth. And in the baraita of the Sifre, in the portion Haazinu: Why does Scripture say, “Judah one, Dan one, Asher one”? It teaches that Israel are destined to take (a strip) in length from the east to the west, with a breadth of 25,000 reeds, which are seventy-five mil. And from where did they learn this measure? From the offering, which is like one of these portions, as is explained in the passage. I found that so it is written: “and in length as one of the portions,” and it is 25,000 reeds broad, and the length from the west side to the east side is 25,000 reeds, 150,000 cubits, for a reed is six cubits and every two thousand cubits is a mil, as we learn in tractate Yoma concerning the ten booths, that from Jerusalem to Tzok it is 150,000 cubits, which amounts to seventy-five mil. And this is what Rabbi Eleazar composed in the piyyut (in the silluk of the second day of Sukkot): “When I take the appointed time, at the time of the division of My lands, like a row of the vineyard, to its outskirts, in length from the east side to its ends, to the Ocean Sea, to its limits, in breadth seventy-five mil, its channels.” (Another version [וי"ג]: seventy-five mil for thirteen strips, between the strips of the tribes and the strips of the holy portion, amount to nine hundred and seventy-five mil; and by the count of 400 parasangs by 400 parasangs of the Land of Israel, the mil come to sixteen hundred, according to the sum of the Kalir, who said four mil is a parasang. And perhaps the mil of the reckoning of the strips are large, so that four of them do not enter into a parasang; but indeed he intends to count two mil to a half (and half) parasang; they would come to four hundred parasangs for a thousand mil, while the reckoning of the mil of the strip comes to only nine hundred and seventy-five mil; the count is still lacking twenty-five mil. The count of the mil of the strips of 89 did not agree with the count of four hundred parasangs. And from where did Rabbi Eliezer learn the length of the rows to the Ocean Sea, which is at the end of the world, whereas Scripture testifies to the western boundary as far as the Great Sea, which is much inside the Ocean Sea?)
Ezekiel.translator_note: This long parenthetical passage is difficult; it is translated as literally as possible. The abbreviations וי"ג (read here as “another version”) and פ"ט (“89”) are not confirmed, and several words of the piyyut (outskirts, limits, channels) are uncertain.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: And by the border of Dan
Ezekiel.english_translation: And beside the border of Dan, on its south.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: shall be the offering which you shall set aside
Ezekiel.english_translation: And if you say: How can it be that Jerusalem is in its place? Was not Jerusalem on the northern boundary of Judah, who took the south of the Land of Canaan, whereas here it is in the middle of the tribes? This division is not like the division of Joshua, for this one is like a row of a vineyard and all the portions are equal; whereas in the division of Joshua the tribe of Judah had a large portion, and even more so, (his portion was) larger than it, until Simeon took in his lot, as it is said (Joshua 19:9): “Out of the allotment of the children of Judah was the inheritance of the children of Simeon.” Therefore there is now enough in the breadth of the portion that Judah took in the days of Joshua for the five remaining tribes to take a portion in it now, because the length is very great, from the east side to the Ocean, and Jerusalem is in its place.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The clause “and even more so, (his portion was) larger than it” is difficult (the printed text has a parenthetical “his portion was”); it is translated literally.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: and the sanctuary shall be in the midst of it
Ezekiel.english_translation: As it explains as it goes on.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: The offering that you shall set apart unto the LORD
Ezekiel.english_translation: From this portion that was set apart beside Judah on its south, in length from the east to the sea and in breadth 25,000 reeds, from it shall be an offering to HaShem, for the Temple and a place for houses for the priests: 25,000 reeds long, from east to west, and 10,000 broad, from north to south.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: And for these, even for the priests
Ezekiel.english_translation: And these, 10,000 in breadth and 25,000 in length, shall be for the priests in the north, within the strips of the great offering, beside the south of Judah.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: toward the north five and twenty thousand
Ezekiel.english_translation: That is the length, from east to west.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: and toward the west ten thousand in breadth
Ezekiel.english_translation: On the west side, ten thousand in breadth, from north to south.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: and toward the east ten thousand in breadth
Ezekiel.english_translation: And the east side, ten thousand, from north to south.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: and toward the south five and twenty thousand in length
Ezekiel.english_translation: From east to west.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: and the sanctuary of the LORD shall be in the midst thereof
Ezekiel.english_translation: This is the Temple Mount: five hundred reeds by five hundred reeds shall be in the middle of this strip, and all around it, for the priests, twelve thousand two hundred and fifty to the east side and likewise to the west side, and in breadth four thousand seven hundred and fifty to the north and likewise to the south, as is said above in the passage: “shall be a measure to the holy place, five hundred by five hundred, square.”
Ezekiel.translator_note: Rashi’s wording of Ezekiel 45:2 (“a measure,” madah) differs from the verse (“of this,” mizeh); his wording is translated.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: The sanctified portion shall be for the priests
Ezekiel.english_translation: This sanctified portion shall be for the priests.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: a portion set apart from the offering of the land
Ezekiel.english_translation: “Set apart” (meforeshet): terumah is a name for setting apart; “terumiyah” means set apart. And this strip was theirs, set apart from the offering of the land, from the great offering that was offered up from the land, in length from the Ocean to the eastern border, in breadth 25,000, as is said above; from it they shall separate this strip, in the middle of its length, for the priests and for the Temple.

For all the great offering is holy for the priests and the Levites and the prince and the possession of the city and the servants of the city, as is explained as it goes on; and this, 25,000 long and 10,000 broad, in its north, which is set apart from it for the priests and for the Temple, shall be most holy.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: by the border of the Levites
Ezekiel.english_translation: Beside the strips of the Levites.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: And answerable unto the border of the priests
Ezekiel.english_translation: Beside the strips of the priests, according to the measure of the priests, opposite its whole length.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: all the length shall be five and twenty thousand
Ezekiel.english_translation: All the strips are 25,000 in length.
And he shall not exchange them for other land.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: And the five thousand that are left in the breadth
Ezekiel.english_translation: The strips of the great offering, which was 25,000 in breadth and in length as one of the portions, from the east side to the west side; and from it he again set apart two strips in its middle, 25,000 in length and their breadth 20,000. Still there remained in its breadth five thousand. Those five thousand in breadth shall be for the dwelling of the city, their length along the 25,000 length of the offering of the Levites.

And they are not holy, like the offering of that strip of the priests and the Levites; it is common (chol) in relation to them, and they shall be for the city, for the dwelling of Israel, and for open land around the city.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: and the city shall be in the midst thereof
Ezekiel.english_translation: In the middle of that strip.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: And these shall be the measures thereof
Ezekiel.english_translation: Of the city.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the north side four thousand and five hundred
Ezekiel.english_translation: Square: 4,500 reeds by 4,500 reeds. There remained in the breadth five hundred; these shall be for it as open land: 250 on the north and 250 reeds on the south, as is said in the verse below, and likewise to the east and west. Behold, 5,000 by 5,000 in the middle of the strip; behold, its whole breadth is filled. And in the length of this third strip there remained 10,000 to the east and 10,000 to the west; about these it explains and says: “And the residue in the length, answerable unto the holy offering, shall be ten thousand eastward, and ten thousand westward.”

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: And the city shall have open land
Ezekiel.english_translation: All the open lands of a city in Scripture are an empty place: neither houses nor field.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: and the increase thereof shall be for food
Ezekiel.english_translation: For bread for the servants of the city. They are the Gibeonites, who were appointed as hewers of wood and drawers of water. So I heard in the name of Rabbi Menachem, of blessed memory.
Eisarbant in French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. It may correspond to *essartant* (from *essarter*, “to clear land,” which a secondary reference, Godefroy, glosses “défricher”), but this is not confirmed.

Ezekiel.english_translation: For they gave them this portion in the land.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: All the offering shall be five and twenty thousand by five and twenty thousand
Ezekiel.english_translation: The sanctified (offering) that is set apart from within the great offering: 25,000 reeds by 25,000 reeds.
Square, together with the holy offering for the priests and the Levites.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: with the possession of the city
Ezekiel.english_translation: “Possession”: porpris in French.
Ezekiel.translator_note: It appears to be Old French *porpris*, but the form was not found in Darmesteter.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: And the residue shall be for the prince
Ezekiel.english_translation: And the residue in the length of the great offering.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: on the one side and on the other
Ezekiel.english_translation: To the east and to the west of the holy offering and of the possession of the city.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: in front of the five and twenty thousand of the offering
Ezekiel.english_translation: Along the breadth of 25,000 of the offering, to the eastern border of the Land of Israel, etc.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: and westward in front of the five and twenty thousand
Ezekiel.english_translation: And so too to the west, in front of the three strips of the priests and the Levites and the possession of the city, in a breadth of 25,000.
Like “as far as the western border,” as far as the Ocean.
Corresponding to the length of the portions of the tribes.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: it shall be for the prince
Ezekiel.english_translation: “Shall be.”
It is the strips of the priests.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: and the sanctuary of the house shall be in the midst thereof
Ezekiel.english_translation: All of it is in the middle of the inheritance of the prince.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the possession of the Levites, and the possession of the city
Ezekiel.english_translation: It too shall be within that which belongs to the prince.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: between the border of Judah and the border of Benjamin
Ezekiel.english_translation: The whole breadth of the strip that is between these two tribes, Judah on the north and Benjamin on the south, shall be for the prince; and it is the strip that was set apart first, 25,000 in breadth, in length following the portions of the tribes.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: And as for the rest of the tribes
Ezekiel.english_translation: They shall take, on the south of that strip: Benjamin beside it, and beside him Simeon, and beside him Issachar, and beside him Zebulun, and beside him Gad. It turns out that Gad is on the southern boundary of the Land of Israel.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: And by the border of Gad
Ezekiel.english_translation: Its southern boundary.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: from Tamar unto the waters of Meribath-kadesh
Ezekiel.english_translation: From Jericho, the city of palm trees, in the eastern corner; and it comes to the west to the waters of Meriboth-kadesh, and comes and goes as far as the Brook of Egypt, which pours into the Great Sea in the south-western corner.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: the goings out of the city
Ezekiel.english_translation: Its gates, on its four sides.
It is the measuring reed: four thousand and five hundred reeds.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: It shall be eighteen thousand reeds round about
Ezekiel.english_translation: The circumference of the city is 18,000 reeds; so the reckoning of its square comes out.

Ezekiel.english_lemma_JPS: And the name of the city from that day shall be
Ezekiel.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “and the name of the city, that is explained from the day when HaShem will cause His Shekhinah to dwell there.” That is, no other name will be called for it but the first name that it had from the day that Abraham bound Isaac his son, the name that he called it, “Yireh” (HaShem will see), and its name was Shalem — behold, Jerusalem. And there is another way to interpret: “and the name of the city” in the future, from the day of its building and onward, they will call it “HaShem is there.” The book of Ezekiel is complete.
Ezekiel.translator_note: Part of the Aramaic is translated as printed; the closing words (“The book of Ezekiel is complete”) are Aramaic.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah
Hosea.english_translation: He outlived these four kings in his days, for he lengthened years in the lives of all of them; from here they said: Woe to the matron who buries her husbands.
Hosea.translator_note: Printed קפח (here rendered “outlived”) is a guess from context.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash
Hosea.english_translation: Of the sons of Jehu. He too reigned with Uzziah and Jotham, but a merit caused him to be counted with these righteous ones, because he did not accept evil speech (lashon hara) about Amos, as is explained in Pesachim, in the chapter HaIshah (page 16), for it is said (Amos 7:10): “Amaziah the priest of Beth-el sent … ‘Amos hath conspired against thee,’” etc.
Hosea.translator_note: The page number is printed “16” (Pesachim); I did not verify it.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: When the LORD spoke at first with Hosea
Hosea.english_translation: Our Rabbis said: first of the four prophets who prophesied (in those days): Hosea, Isaiah, Amos, and Micah. Isaiah prophesied, as it is said (Isaiah 6): “And the posts of the door were moved,” etc., and that was the day that Uzziah was struck with leprosy when he entered the Temple, for the upper (beings) shook to burn him and the lower to swallow him, like the punishment of the company of Korah, among whom were those swallowed and those burned. Of Amos it is said “two years before the earthquake.” And Hosea preceded them all, and Micah was last of them all, as it is said of him (Micah 1): “in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah,” and Uzziah is not mentioned in it. But the plain sense of the verse is: the beginning of the speech with which the Holy One, blessed be He, spoke with Hosea, He said this to him.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Go, take unto thee a wife of harlotry
Hosea.english_translation: Our Rabbis said: as it sounds (literally), because He said of Israel, “Exchange them for another nation,” as is explained in Pesachim at the beginning of (the chapter) HaIshah.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: and children of harlotry
Hosea.english_translation: That she shall bear you children who will be of doubtful bastardy. And Jonathan translated: “prophesy a prophecy against the inhabitants of the city of idolatry.” And the word “take” said here is an expression of teaching: teach them to return in repentance.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: for the land doth commit great harlotry
Hosea.english_translation: It is an expression of the present (continuing) tense.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Gomer the daughter of Diblaim
Hosea.english_translation: Our Rabbis said: Thus was her name on account of her harlotry, for all complete (gomerin) with her and thresh with her like a fig-cake (dvelah). And Targum Jonathan (explains) Gomer: if they return from their way, their punishment is finished (gamrah); and if not, they will be like a fig falling from the fig-tree.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: and she conceived, and bore him a son
Hosea.english_translation: And they continued to do evil deeds.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Call his name Jezreel
Hosea.english_translation: “Call their name ‘scattered ones’”: prophesy against them that they will go into exile and be sown in the lands.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: the blood of Jezreel
Hosea.english_translation: As its Targum renders: the blood of the house of Ahab, whom Jehu slew in Jezreel because they served the Baal; and he and his sons afterwards went and served idolatry. Therefore I reckon against them the blood of the house of Ahab as innocent blood.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: upon the house of Jehu
Hosea.english_translation: Jeroboam the son of Joash was of the sons of Jehu (2 Kings 15), and Zechariah his son was killed.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: I will no more have compassion
Hosea.english_translation: To have compassion.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: that I should in any wise pardon them
Hosea.english_translation: I will distribute to them the portion of their cup and their deed, like “and he took portions” (Genesis 43).
Hosea.translator_note: Rashi cites the word as it is written (va-yissa mas’ot); JPS renders the verse “And portions were taken unto them.”

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: But I will have compassion upon the house of Judah
Hosea.english_translation: After I put an end to the kingdom of Israel, after the Ten Tribes had been exiled, the house of Judah was included in compassion, from Hezekiah until Zedekiah.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Now when she had weaned Lo-ruhamah
Hosea.english_translation: According to its Targum: and that generation came to an end among the nations to which they were exiled.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: she conceived, and bore a son
Hosea.english_translation: And they continued and did evil deeds. And according to its plain sense, as it sounds.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea
Hosea.english_translation: What is the connection of punishment and consolation adjacent in one speech? And our Rabbis explained in Pesachim: Hosea felt within himself that he had sinned in saying, “Exchange them”; he arose and sought mercy on their behalf. And in the Sifre of the school of Rav, the portion “And Israel abode in Shittim,” we learned: Rabbi says: There are passages adjacent to one another and distant from one another, as the east is distant from the west: “for you are not My people” and “the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea.” What is the connection of this beside that? A parable: a king who was angry with his wife sent for the scribe to come and write her a bill of divorce. Before the scribe came, the king was appeased toward his wife. The king said: Is it possible that this scribe should leave here chaluk? — that is, his heart is divided and he wonders, saying: Why did he send for me? He said to him: Come and write for her, for I am doubling her ketubah. And according to the plain sense, this is its adjacency: “for you are not My people, and I will not be yours” — I will show Myself as though I am not yours, and you will be exiled among the nations; and even there you will multiply and flourish, and there you will bethink yourselves, to return to Me, as it was said through Moses (Deuteronomy 30): “and thou shalt bethink thyself among all the nations, whither the LORD thy God hath driven thee,” etc., “that then the LORD thy God will turn thy captivity,” etc. So too here: “And the children of Judah and the children of Israel shall be gathered together,” etc.
Hosea.translator_note: The word chaluk in the parable is left untranslated and glossed as Rashi glosses it (“his heart is divided”).

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: one head
Hosea.english_translation: David their king.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: for great shall be the day of Jezreel
Hosea.english_translation: The ingathering of their seed.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Say you unto your brethren: ‘Ammi’
Hosea.english_translation: As its Targum renders: “Return to My Torah, and upon your assembly I will have compassion.”

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Plead with your mother
Hosea.english_translation: With your present congregation (knesset), which is the mother of the generations to come.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: from between her breasts
Hosea.english_translation: The way of adulteresses, who press (something) between their breasts. And Jonathan translated: “and the worship of her idols from between her walls.”

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And set her as in the day that she was born
Hosea.english_translation: As on the day that I found her in Egypt, as is explained in Ezekiel (16:4–5): “And as for thy nativity, in the day thou wast born thy navel was not cut,” etc., and “thou wast cast out in the open field in the loathsomeness of thy person”; “No eye pitied thee.”
Hosea.translator_note: Rashi cites the clauses of Ezekiel 16:4–5 in a different order from the verses; JPS wording is quoted for each.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And make her as a wilderness
Hosea.english_translation: The decrees that I decreed upon them in the wilderness: “in this wilderness they shall be consumed, and there they shall die” (Numbers 14:35).

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And slay her with thirst
Hosea.english_translation: “And I will slay her.”

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: their mother
Hosea.english_translation: Their congregation (knesset).

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: hath done shamefully
Hosea.english_translation: Their teachers were ashamed (Aramaic): the sages who instruct them with rulings are ashamed before the people of the land; they say to them, “Do not steal,” and they steal; “Do not lend at interest,” and they lend.
Hosea.translator_note: The Aramaic words (bihatu milfayhon) are translated as printed; the printed text does not say who the subject of “they steal” and “they lend” is.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: I will go after my lovers
Hosea.english_translation: In the ways of the idolaters.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: I will hedge up thy way with thorns
Hosea.english_translation: An expression of closing, like (Isaiah 5:5) “I will take away the hedge thereof,” like (Proverbs 15) “as though hedged by thorns.”
Hosea.translator_note: Rashi’s spelling of the word for “hedge” in Proverbs 15:19 differs slightly from the verse; JPS wording is quoted.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: thy way
Hosea.english_translation: Roads and paths on which you walk.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And she shall run after her lovers
Hosea.english_translation: This is of the forms of the heavy (intensive) conjugation, like (ibid. 12) “he that followeth after vain things”: porcaçier in French; that is, she will return after them and will not overtake them.
Hosea.translator_note: Printed “ibid. 12” refers to Proverbs 12:11 (JPS wording quoted). Darmesteter lists this word (Hosea 2:9) with the gloss “Elle poursuivra” (she will pursue), in the form פורקציר (porcaçier); the printed form is the same word.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: her lovers
Hosea.english_translation: Egypt and Assyria; and you will not be able to seek help from them.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: she shall seek them
Hosea.english_translation: “And she shall seek them.”

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: For she did not know
Hosea.english_translation: She did not set it to heart, and she made herself out as one who does not know.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And multiplied unto her silver and gold
Hosea.english_translation: And they made it for the Baal.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: in the time thereof
Hosea.english_translation: At the time of the completion of the ripening of the fruits.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And will snatch away
Hosea.english_translation: From her.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: My wool and My flax
Hosea.english_translation: Which was to cover her nakedness. Every “hatsalah” in Scripture is an expression of taking off and setting apart, and proof for it: “Thus God hath taken away the cattle of your father” (Genesis 31:9); “For all the riches which God hath taken away from our father” (ibid.).
Hosea.translator_note: The second quotation is Genesis 31:16 (printed “ibid.”).

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And none shall deliver her out of My hand
Hosea.english_translation: Even the merit of their fathers has come to an end.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And I will lay waste
Hosea.english_translation: An expression of desolation.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: These are my hire
Hosea.english_translation: Like etnan.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And I will make them a forest
Hosea.english_translation: For the beasts walk there and eat the fruits.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And I will visit upon her
Hosea.english_translation: The recompense of punishment.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: the days of the Baalim
Hosea.english_translation: Continually to them; and it is an expression of the present.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And decked herself with her ear-rings and her jewels
Hosea.english_translation: An expression of “adi” (ornament), like a harlot adorning herself toward adulterers.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: her jewels
Hosea.english_translation: In the Arabic language it is an ornament.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: I will allure her
Hosea.english_translation: I will persuade her to be drawn after Me: lozanyer in French. And what is the allurement? “And I will bring her into the wilderness” — in the Exile, which is for her like a wilderness and desert; and there she will bethink herself that it was good for her when she did My will, more than when she rebelled against Me.
Hosea.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this word (Hosea 2:16) with the gloss “Je l’attirerai” (I will attract her), in forms such as אטרייר (atrayer). The printed form לוזאניי"ר is different and was not found in Darmesteter.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: her vineyards
Hosea.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: an expression of leaders and guides; and so “He turneth not by the way of the vineyards” (Job 24:18); and so “But mine own vineyard have I not kept” (Song of Songs 1:6). Another explanation: “And I will bring her into the wilderness” — into the wilderness of Sihon and Og; and in this style Ezekiel prophesied (Ezekiel 20:35), for it is said: “and I will bring you into the wilderness of the peoples, and there will I plead with you” — “so will I plead with you” — “and I will bring you into the bond of the covenant, and I will purge out from among you the rebels,” etc.; and the proper ones I will establish. And this is “her vineyards.”
Hosea.translator_note: Rashi cites Ezekiel 20:35–38 as one continuous quotation; JPS wording is quoted clause by clause (the middle clause is from 20:36).

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And the valley of Achor
Hosea.english_translation: The depth of the troubles, which are turbid (akhurim). There I will give her a door of hope, for out of those troubles she will set her heart to return to Me.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And she shall respond there
Hosea.english_translation: An expression of a dwelling, like (Nahum 2) “the den of the lions.”

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: as in the days of her youth
Hosea.english_translation: For she dwelt in Egypt many days.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: as in the day when she came up out of the land of Egypt
Hosea.english_translation: For she cried to Me from Egypt out of the bondage, and I redeemed her; so too now.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: That thou shalt call Me Ishi
Hosea.english_translation: You shall serve Me out of love and not out of fear. “Ishi” is an expression of marriage and of the affection of youth.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And shalt call Me no more Baali
Hosea.english_translation: An expression of lordship and fear. And our Rabbis explained: like a bride in her father-in-law’s house, and not like a bride in her father’s house.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And they shall no more be mentioned by their name
Hosea.english_translation: Israel by the name of the Baalim; or: the Baalim shall not be mentioned by the name of Israel, to say that they are gods to them; or: the name of the Baalim shall no longer be mentioned, as it is said (Isaiah 2:18): “And the idols shall utterly pass away.”

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: With the beasts of the field
Hosea.english_translation: For I will cause harmful creatures to cease from the world; and so it says (ibid. 11): “They shall not hurt nor destroy,” etc.
Hosea.translator_note: Printed “ibid. 11” is Isaiah 11:9.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: in righteousness, and in justice
Hosea.english_translation: In which you shall conduct yourselves.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And in lovingkindness, and in compassion
Hosea.english_translation: That will come to you from Me by means of them. About Abraham our father it is written (Genesis 18:19): “For I have known him, to the end that he may command … to do righteousness and justice”; and corresponding to them the Holy One, blessed be He, gave his children lovingkindness and compassion, as it is said (Deuteronomy 13:18): “and show thee mercy,” and (ibid. 17): “the LORD thy God shall keep with thee the covenant and the mercy.” When they ceased from righteousness and justice, as it is said (Amos 5:7): “You who turn judgment to wormwood, and cast righteousness to the ground,” the Holy One, blessed be He, also withdrew from them lovingkindness and compassion, as it is said (Jeremiah 15:1): “for I have taken away My peace from this people … even mercy and compassion.” And when they return to doing righteousness and justice, as it is said (Isaiah 1:27): “Zion shall be redeemed with justice,” etc., the Holy One, blessed be He, adds to them compassion and lovingkindness, and makes them a crown for the four of them and seats them at their head.
Hosea.translator_note: Printed “ibid. 17” is Deuteronomy 7:12; printed “Jeremiah 15:1” is Jeremiah 16:5 (JPS wording quoted; JPS renders the same two words as “mercy and compassion”).

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And I will betroth thee unto Me in faithfulness
Hosea.english_translation: In reward for the faithfulness with which you believed, in the Exile, the promises made through My prophets.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: I will respond to the heavens
Hosea.english_translation: To pour out upon the skies the streams of good that depend on the word; and they shall respond, to pour water upon the earth.
Hosea.translator_note: Printed מפלג הטוב is rendered “the streams of good”; I did not confirm the exact sense.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And they shall respond to Jezreel
Hosea.english_translation: The exiles who were sown and gathered.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And I will sow her unto Me in the land
Hosea.english_translation: Like one who sows a se’ah in order to bring in many kor, so will many proselytes be added to them in the Land of Israel.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: a woman beloved of her friend and an adulteress
Hosea.english_translation: Dear to her husband and beloved by him, and she commits adultery under him, like the love of the Holy One, blessed be He, for Israel, and they go astray under Him after other gods.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: cakes of raisins
Hosea.english_translation: Menachem explained: goblets of wine; they love to get drunk on their wine and do not occupy themselves with Torah. And so we find that he rebukes them about this elsewhere: “That drink wine in bowls” (Amos 6:6).

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: So I bought her to me
Hosea.english_translation: An expression of trade: bargaine in French; like (Genesis 50:5) “which I have digged for me” (asher karithi li). And in the coastal cities they call a sale “kirah.”
Hosea.translator_note: Rashi compares the word to karithi in Genesis 50:5, which JPS renders “digged.” Darmesteter lists this word (Hosea 3:2) with the gloss “Je t’achèterai (sens de commerce)” in the form ברגיינא (bargaine); the printed form is the same word.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: for fifteen pieces of silver and a homer of barley, and a half-homer of barley
Hosea.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “And I redeemed them by My word on the fifteenth day of the month of Nisan, and he gave the silver of shekels as atonement for their souls, and I said that they would offer before Me an omer of the wave-offering, ma’alelat of barley”; that is, I did not weary them with hard words.
Hosea.translator_note: The Aramaic is translated as printed. The word מעללת (ma’alelat) is left transliterated.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: fifteen pieces of silver
Hosea.english_translation: In gematria: Nisan. And in the Pesikta it is expounded: “fifteen of silver” — on the fifteenth of Nisan. And a homer and a letech: behold, forty-five, for the homer is thirty se’ah and the letech is half a homer.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Thou shalt sit solitary for me many days
Hosea.english_translation: “Days” — two; “many” — three; behold, five. These are the fifty days between Passover and Shavuot. On that very day I gave them the Torah, and in it I warned her.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: thou shalt not play the harlot, and thou shalt not be any man’s wife
Hosea.english_translation: “Thou shalt have no other gods” (Exodus 20:3).

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: nor will I be thine
Hosea.english_translation: “I am the LORD thy God” (ibid.). And as for His making two reckonings from the fifty days — one for the end of the homer and one for the end of the letech — corresponding to the manna that descended for them at the end of thirty days, on the fifteenth of Iyar, and from there fifteen days, the count of the se’ahs of the letech; on this day they came to the wilderness of Sinai, on the New Moon of Sivan. And in the name of Rav Hai I found a fitting thing: “So I bought her to me,” etc.: I fixed the money of her ransom opposite Me in small sums. One who says, “The valuation of my person is incumbent on me”: if from sixty years old and upward, “thy valuation shall be fifteen shekels”; and a homer of barley. The valuation of a male from twenty years old and upward until sixty is fifty shekels, and this is the redemption-price of a homer of barley, for that too is fifty shekels of silver. And a letech of barley is the redemption-price of land: a letech of barley (sowing) to the Sanctuary — twenty-five shekels. The fixed valuation from a month old to five years is five shekels, and from five years old to twenty years old thy valuation is twenty shekels: behold, twenty-five. After all this affection I said to her: Many days thou shalt sit solitary for Me; thou shalt not play the harlot with other gods, for if thou playest the harlot, many days shall thy sons sit without king and without prince and without sacrifice in the Temple in Judah, and without the pillar of the Baal in Samaria for the kings of Israel, and without the ephod of Urim and Thummim that tells them hidden things, and without teraphim — they are an image made at a single determined hour, made for that purpose, and they speak of themselves and tell hidden things. And so Targum Jonathan: “and there is no ephod and one who reveals.”
Hosea.translator_note: This long, compressed passage is translated as literally as possible; I could not confirm every detail of the reckoning. The Aramaic at the end is translated as printed. The Leviticus 27 valuations match Leviticus 27:3, 5, 6, 7 and 16.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: afterward
Hosea.english_translation: The days of the Exile.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: shall the children of Israel return, and seek the LORD their God
Hosea.english_translation: It was taught in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai: In three things the children of Israel rebelled in the days of Rehoboam: against the kingdom of Heaven, and the kingdom of the House of David, and the Temple. This is what is written (1 Kings 12:16): “What portion have we in David?” — as it sounds; “to your tents, O Israel” (ibid.) — do not read “to your tents” but “to your God”; “now see to thine own house, David” (ibid.) — this is the Temple. Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya said: A good sign is not shown to Israel until they return and seek all three. “Afterward shall the children of Israel return and seek the LORD their God” — this is the kingdom of Heaven; “and David their king” — as it sounds; “and shall come trembling unto the LORD and to His goodness” — this is the Temple, as it is said, “this good mountain.”
Hosea.translator_note: The phrase “this good mountain” appears to be from Deuteronomy 3:25 (JPS: “that goodly hill-country”); no reference is printed.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Swearing and lying
Hosea.english_translation: They swear falsely.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: They break all bounds
Hosea.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “and they beget children from the wives of their fellows.”

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: and blood toucheth blood
Hosea.english_translation: They add liabilities upon liabilities; and according to its plain meaning, they breached the fence and multiplied bloodshed until the blood of one slain touched the blood of his fellow.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Therefore doth the land mourn
Hosea.english_translation: It will be laid waste, and the mourning in it will grow great.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: are taken away
Hosea.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “they will become few because of their sins”; an expression of ending, like (Jeremiah 8) “I will utterly consume them.”

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Yet let no man strive
Hosea.english_translation: You warn the true prophets that they should not contend with you and not rebuke you, as was said in Amos, where Amaziah the priest of Beth-el said to him: “Do not prophesy against the house of Israel, and do not preach against the house of Isaac”; and that was in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash, in whose days Hosea prophesied.
Hosea.translator_note: Printed “Amos 7:10”; the words quoted are Amos 7:16 (JPS: “Prophesy not against Israel, And preach not against the house of Isaac”). Rashi’s wording (“the house of Israel”) differs slightly from the verse; his wording is translated.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: For thy people are as they that strive with the priest
Hosea.english_translation: They contend with their teachers (Aramaic), for the priests were the people of instruction, as it is said (Deuteronomy 33:10): “They shall teach Jacob Thine ordinances.”

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Therefore shalt thou stumble in the day
Hosea.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “And you will stumble by day, and the false prophets of your people will stumble as by night, and I will put to shame your assembly”; that is, I will put to shame your congregation.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: the prophet also shall stumble with thee
Hosea.english_translation: The prophets who are with you.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And I will destroy thy mother
Hosea.english_translation: Like “nidmu ami” (Hosea 4:6): like a man who sits and is bewildered and has no answer in his mouth.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: I also will forget thy children
Hosea.english_translation: For those who stood at Mount Sinai gave their children as guarantors in place of their fathers, to keep the Torah.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: The more they were increased, the more they sinned against Me
Hosea.english_translation: When they multiplied and grew, so they added to sinning. “So they sinned” — “ken” is an expression in Hebrew in several places: “But the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied” (Exodus 1:12); “The more they called them, the more they went from them” (Hosea 11:2). As much as the prophets called to them to rebuke them, so they fled from them.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: I will change their glory into shame
Hosea.english_translation: Therefore I will change their glory into shame.
Hosea.translator_note: The printed lemma repeats “The more they were increased, the more they sinned”; the comment explains the end of the verse.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: They feed on the sin of My people
Hosea.english_translation: Every “chatat” in the Book of the Twelve Prophets is pointed with a patach (chatat), because all of them are joined to the next word, except one (Micah 1:13): “She was the beginning of sin to the daughter of Zion.” The sins of My people shall they eat — the false prophets of whom He said above, “and the prophet also shall stumble with thee.” They became priests of the high places for them, and they eat what the priests were fit to eat.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And set their heart on their iniquity
Hosea.english_translation: The prophet will lift up his soul toward the iniquity of Israel, and the prophet himself waits for them to bring him money and offerings for atonement.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: like people, like priest
Hosea.english_translation: I will make the people equal to the disgrace of the priests who profaned them by serving as priests for them; and therefore I too will profane the people with idolatry. So too Targum Jonathan.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: and shall not increase
Hosea.english_translation: Sons will not grow up.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Harlotry, wine, and new wine
Hosea.english_translation: For they are busy with them; they have taken their heart from after Me.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: My people ask counsel at their stock
Hosea.english_translation: In an image made of wood.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And their staff declareth unto them
Hosea.english_translation: To his words he listens, which the prophets of the Baal say to him in the name of idolatry.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Under oaks
Hosea.english_translation: Kayania in French, in which grows a fruit called glanz in French.
Hosea.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this verse (Hosea 4:13) with the gloss “Chêne” (oak), in forms such as קישנא, and for the fruit “glant,” in forms such as גלנאץ (close to the printed גלננ"ץ). The printed first form קייאני"א differs slightly.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: poplars
Hosea.english_translation: A tree whose bark is white.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: terebinths
Hosea.english_translation: Olma in French, whose branches are many, and they plant it for shade.
Hosea.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this word (Hosea 4:13) with the gloss “Ormeau” (elm), in forms such as אולמא; the printed form is the same word.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Therefore your daughters commit harlotry
Hosea.english_translation: Because you associate with the idolaters according to the practices of the ancient nations, and they associate with you; and you used to intermarry with them, and your daughters born to you from their daughters follow the custom of their mother and commit harlotry. So too Targum Jonathan.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: I will not punish your daughters when they commit harlotry
Hosea.english_translation: Any more to test them with the bitter waters when they commit harlotry — why? For their husbands themselves consort with harlots, and when the man is not clean of iniquity, the waters do not test his wife.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: For they themselves consort with lewd women
Hosea.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “mistayyein” — an expression of company; that is, they associate with them to drink wine. And Menachem joined it with “perudot” in “avshu perudot,” which are wine casks.
Hosea.translator_note: The words avshu perudot are from Joel 1:17 (no reference is printed).

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And the people that is without understanding is distraught
Hosea.english_translation: Since you do not set your heart to understand, therefore you shall stumble, to be smitten with punishment. “Libbut” is an expression of the toil of the road and the weariness of carrying a burden: delasser in French.
Hosea.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this word (Hosea 4:14) with the gloss “Trébuche : ce verbe indique la lassitude” (stumbles; this verb indicates weariness), in forms such as דלשיר; the printed form is the same word.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Though thou, Israel, play the harlot
Hosea.english_translation: The sons of Judah shall not learn their ways. Another explanation: “Though thou, Israel, play the harlot, yet let not Judah become guilty” — if Israel plays the harlot, the sons of Judah are not liable for it, and I do not hold them liable, as is said above (Hosea 1:7): “But I will have compassion upon the house of Judah.”

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And come not you unto Gilgal
Hosea.english_translation: The sons of Judah (are warned) not to come to Gilgal, provided only that the sons of Judah do not come to Gilgal, for there the Ten Tribes serve idolatry, as it is said, “All their wickedness is in Gilgal” (below, 9), and “To Gilgal, and multiply transgression” (Amos 4:4).
Hosea.translator_note: Printed “below, 9” is Hosea 9:15 (JPS wording quoted). The Amos 4:4 quotation is in JPS wording.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Neither go you up to Beth-aven
Hosea.english_translation: It is Beth-el, where Jeroboam set up the calves.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Nor swear: ‘As the LORD liveth.’
Hosea.english_translation: With them: “As the LORD liveth,” for “And though they say: ‘As the LORD liveth,’ surely they swear falsely” (Jeremiah 5:2). When they swore falsely they would mention the name of Heaven, and when they swore truly they swore by the name of the Baalim.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: For Israel is stubborn like a stubborn heifer
Hosea.english_translation: Like an ox that is fattened and kicks (Aramaic): so Israel was stubborn from much eating and drinking.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Now shall the LORD feed them as a lamb in a large place?
Hosea.english_translation: A narrow pasture, like a lamb that grazes in an open place, and not like a fattened ox, which they stall-feed with barley and vetches.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Ephraim is joined to idols
Hosea.english_translation: He is attached to idolatry and it is impossible for him to separate; therefore leave him alone, you, the prophet, and do not prophesy to rebuke him, for it will not help.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: When their carouse is over
Hosea.english_translation: Their feast has become foreign to Me. “Sar” is an expression of “foreign,” like (Jeremiah 2:21) “the degenerate plant of a strange vine”; that is, it departed from its place and was changed into another.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: When their carouse is over
Hosea.english_translation: Their wine-feast, which was with the harlots.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Her rulers deeply love dishonour
Hosea.english_translation: They prepared dishonour for themselves. “Havu” is an expression of preparation, like (Genesis 11:7) “Come, let us go down,” “Come, let us build us a city” (ibid.), “come, let us deal wisely with them” (Exodus 1).

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Her rulers
Hosea.english_translation: Her princes and her kings.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: The wind hath bound her up in her skirts
Hosea.english_translation: The wind clings to her wings, like that bird which the wind does not let settle until it carries it far away; so the enemies will come upon them and exile them into captivity.
Hosea.translator_note: JPS renders kenafeha “in her skirts”; Rashi’s comment reads it as “wings.”

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: The wind hath bound her up in her skirts
Hosea.english_translation: “From the altars of their abominations,” to which they do not turn. As one says “chata chat’ah,” so one says “zevach zivchah”: from the places where they used to sacrifice. And so Targum Jonathan: “from the igurei of their abomination.” In Midrash Tanchuma I found an aggadic expression: like a man who threatens one who provokes him, “By your life, I am binding for you in your wings”; so this verse threatens Israel: “My zeal is bound, and My wrath is to take vengeance in the end,” and they will be ashamed of their deeds.
Hosea.translator_note: In JPS the clause “And they shall be ashamed because of their sacrifices” falls at the start of 5:1, so the lemma is anchored to a nearby phrase of 4:19. The Aramaic is translated as printed; the word igurei is left transliterated.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: For unto you pertaineth the judgment
Hosea.english_translation: The judgment of afflictions is upon you, house of the king of Israel; “for you have been a snare on Mizpah, and a net spread upon Tabor.” On these two mountains they set up guard-posts (pardesiyot) to guard that Israel should not go up on pilgrimage to the Temple.
Hosea.translator_note: Pardesiyot is rendered “guard-posts” from the context; I did not confirm the word.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And they that fall away are gone deep in making slaughter
Hosea.english_translation: They deepened the extent of their folly. I said: Whoever does not go up on pilgrimage transgresses a positive commandment; and they decreed: Whoever goes up on pilgrimage shall be killed. Behold, they went deeper than I. And “shachatah” is an expression like (1 Kings 10:16) “beaten gold” (zahav shachut): drawn out and stretched. And Targum Jonathan: an expression of slaughtering sacrifices to idols.
Hosea.translator_note: Printed “העול'” is read as “the one who goes up” (ha-oleh).

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And I am rejected of them all
Hosea.english_translation: And I too will chastise them with chastisements; I will prepare chastisement for all of them.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: For now, O Ephraim, thou hast committed harlotry
Hosea.english_translation: Until Hoshea the son of Elah, they used to blame the corruption on their kings, who were preventing them from going up on pilgrimage. This one arose and abolished the guard-posts, and they still did not go up; therefore they were exiled. “For now, O Ephraim, thou hast committed harlotry” — and they have no one on whom to blame it, such as a king. So I learned in Seder Olam.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Their doings will not suffer them
Hosea.english_translation: They will not leave their evil way, like (Song of Songs 2) “give forth their fragrance”; (Genesis 31) “but God suffered him not to hurt me”; “And Sihon would not suffer Israel” (Numbers 21:23).

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: But the pride of Israel shall testify to his face
Hosea.english_translation: And the glory of Israel shall be brought low (Aramaic), like (Exodus 10) “to humble thyself before Me”: an expression of affliction and humbling.
Hosea.translator_note: The Aramaic is translated as printed. “Brought low” for וימאך is inferred from Rashi’s own explanation (“humbling”).

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: to his face
Hosea.english_translation: “And they see” (Aramaic); and Dunash ben Labrat explained it as an expression of testimony: when punishments come upon them, it will testify against them, and in their faces, the pride and haughtiness with which they acted proudly and transgressed My will.
Hosea.translator_note: The printed words ואינון חזן are read as Aramaic (“and they see”), as in the Targum quoted at Hosea 7:10; the sentence is translated as printed.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: With their flocks and with their herds
Hosea.english_translation: With their offerings.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: He hath withdrawn Himself from them
Hosea.english_translation: Withdrawn, like (2 Samuel 2:21) “and take thee his armour”: garments that you strip from upon them.
Hosea.translator_note: Rashi’s wording of the verse has “their” where the verse has “his”; JPS wording is quoted.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: For they have begotten strange children
Hosea.english_translation: For they intermarried with the idolaters.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Now shall the new moon devour them
Hosea.english_translation: The month of Av.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Blow you the horn in Gibeah
Hosea.english_translation: That they should beware and guard against the sword of the troops that will come upon them.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Sound an alarm at Beth-aven
Hosea.english_translation: “Behind thee, O Benjamin!” — the troop goes behind you. Sound this alarm at Beth-aven. And Targum Jonathan: “Blow the shofar, tidings of a sword coming, because they made Saul king over them, who was at Gibeah, and did not listen to the voice of Samuel, who was from Ramah; and their kings caused them to turn away from after Me, such as Jeroboam and his companions. Sound an alarm over them: iniquity and great destruction.”
Hosea.translator_note: The Aramaic is translated as printed. The printed text does not mark where the Targum quotation ends.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Behind thee, O Benjamin
Hosea.english_translation: Because you delayed and turned backward from going up on pilgrimage to the Temple, which is in the portion of Benjamin.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Behind thee, O Benjamin
Hosea.english_translation: On account of your delaying of Benjamin.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Ephraim shall be desolate in the day of rebuke
Hosea.english_translation: And when I come to contend with them, they will be desolate and astonished, and there will be no answer in their mouths. Why? Because among the tribes of Israel I made known the faithful Torah, and they transgressed it.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Among the tribes of Israel do I make known that which shall surely be
Hosea.english_translation: “Among the tribes of Israel I made known (the) faithful (thing)”: Rabbi Abbahu in the name of Rabbi Acha the son of Rabbi Chanina said: On the day when the Holy One, blessed be He, contends with them in judgment, they will have no opening of the mouth, for I made known among the tribes that the judgment is a true judgment. You find that when the Ten Tribes were exiled, Judah and Benjamin were not exiled, and the Ten Tribes said: Because they are of His palace, He did not exile them; there is partiality in the matter, God forbid! There is no partiality, but their measure had not yet been filled. When they sinned, they were exiled. Then the Ten Tribes heard, with no answer in their mouths, and said (Aramaic): “This God is strong, this is truth, for even to the members of His house He does not show favor,” to fulfill what is said, “Among the tribes of Israel I made known the faithful (thing).”

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: like them that remove the landmark
Hosea.english_translation: Like a man who attaches (to his own) his fellow’s boundary; so they hurried to seize the ways of Israel, their fellow kings. Therefore “upon them I will pour out,” etc. And as it sounds, they were robbing fields. But this is difficult in my eyes, for he should have written “mesigei gevul” and not “kemasigei.”

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Oppressed is Ephraim
Hosea.english_translation: By the hand of the idolaters.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: crushed in his right
Hosea.english_translation: Afflicted with afflictions. And why does he have all this? Because he wished it and went after the new commands of the prophets of the Baal.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: as rottenness
Hosea.english_translation: A worm that eats wood and grinds it.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: his wound
Hosea.english_translation: An expression of sickness.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Ephraim went to Assyria
Hosea.english_translation: This is Hoshea the son of Elah, who was a servant to him (Assyria), and returned and rebelled (2 Kings 17:1).
Hosea.translator_note: The printed reference is 17:1; the servitude and the rebellion are narrated in 2 Kings 17:3–4.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And sent
Hosea.english_translation: Judah.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: King Contentious
Hosea.english_translation: This is Ahaz, who gave a bribe to Tiglath-pileser to help him against Rezin king of Aram and Pekah the son of Remaliah (2 Kings 16).

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: But he is not able to heal you
Hosea.english_translation: From the many troops of Philistines and Arabs who came upon Ahaz, as explained in Chronicles (II 24): “For Ahaz stripped the house of the LORD … and gave thereof unto the king of Assyria; but it helped him not.”
Hosea.translator_note: Printed “II 24”; the words quoted are 2 Chronicles 28:21 (JPS wording quoted).

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Neither shall he cure you of your wound
Hosea.english_translation: No pain will depart from you. And I say that it is among the reversed words, an expression of removal, as (2 Samuel 20:13) “When he was removed out of the highway”; (Isaiah 59:13) “Conceiving and uttering from the heart”; (Proverbs 25:4) “Take away the dross from the silver.”
Hosea.translator_note: Rashi’s wording of Isaiah 59:13 (horu ve-hogu) differs slightly from the verse; JPS wording is quoted.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: I will take away
Hosea.english_translation: I will carry off the prey.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: I will go and return to My place
Hosea.english_translation: I will withdraw from them and return to the heavens.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Till they acknowledge their guilt
Hosea.english_translation: They will hold themselves guilty, to confess their guilt.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: they will seek Me earnestly
Hosea.english_translation: They will seek Me.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: For He hath torn, and He will heal us
Hosea.english_translation: They will say, “Come, and let us return,” etc.
Hosea.translator_note: In JPS the words “Come, and let us return unto the LORD” are at the end of 5:15.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: He hath smitten, and He will bind us up
Hosea.english_translation: “Yakh” is an expression of the present: He strikes us, and He will bind us up.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: After two days will He revive us
Hosea.english_translation: He will strengthen us after the two calamities that passed over us, from the two Temples that were destroyed.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: On the third day He will raise us up
Hosea.english_translation: In the building of the third House He will raise us up.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: After two days
Hosea.english_translation: Of two times that passed over us.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: On the third day
Hosea.english_translation: In the third time.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: eagerly strive to know the LORD
Hosea.english_translation: In truth and in wholeness; firm as the dawn, this one whose going forth is firm.
Hosea.translator_note: The sentence is elliptical; it is translated literally.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And He shall come unto us as the rain
Hosea.english_translation: Like the rain that comes to be life for the world; for then He will come to teach life that will come to us.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: that watereth the earth
Hosea.english_translation: “Yoreh” — He will water (yarveh) the earth.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: what shall I do unto thee
Hosea.english_translation: Because of the attribute of justice, how shall I bring your judgments to light?

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: your goodness is as a morning cloud
Hosea.english_translation: All your goodness and your righteousness is nothing.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Therefore have I hewed them by the prophets
Hosea.english_translation: Because I hewed My words upon them through the prophets and they were not careful with them, therefore I slew them with the words of My mouth — because of the words of My mouth; so Jonathan translated.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Therefore
Hosea.english_translation: Like “because,” and so (Genesis 33:10) “forasmuch as I have seen thy face,” and (ibid. 38) “forasmuch as I gave her not to Shelah my son.”

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And thy judgment goeth forth as the light
Hosea.english_translation: In astonishment (as a question): And how can I show you favor, on account of the attribute of justice? And it refers back to “what shall I do unto thee.”

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And the knowledge of God rather than burnt-offerings
Hosea.english_translation: I desired it more than burnt-offerings.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: like men
Hosea.english_translation: Like the first man.
Hosea.translator_note: JPS renders ke-adam “like men”; Rashi reads it “like Adam (the first man).”

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: There have they dealt treacherously against Me
Hosea.english_translation: In the good land in which I settled them, there they dealt treacherously with Me, like Adam, whom I brought into the Garden of Eden, and he transgressed My commandment.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: It is covered with footprints of blood
Hosea.english_translation: Full of those who lie in ambush to murder, like (Joshua 8) “their rear lying in wait” (ve-et ekvo), and (Genesis 27) “he hath supplanted me” (vaya’kveni).

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And as troops of robbers wait for a man
Hosea.english_translation: And like the gathering of a man, a fisher of fish, who gathers them together with a hook: so the “chakkei” of their troops, the companies of their priests who join together to go on the road — they murder there, all of them, with one shoulder (shekhem ekhad).

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Yea, they commit enormity
Hosea.english_translation: For it is counsel that they took before their gathering: to which place they will go to murder and to take spoil. And “kechakkei” is imdors in French. And even in the language of the Mishnah “chakkei” is an expression of joining (Bava Kamma 119; see there): “and he shall not insert in it more than three chakkin,” which are stitches by which the carder joins two ends of the garment together when he beats it with sticks. And this expression is mine, and it is fitting in my eyes; and so is its interpretation: and when there is among them a joining of people gathered together, it is a company of priests for murder.
