And the first is from the words of R"M, the sheliach tzibbur, of blessed memory.
Hosea.translator_note: The abbreviation ר"מ is left as printed. Darmesteter lists this word (Hosea 6:9) with the gloss “Et comme les pêcheurs” (and like fishers), in forms such as איימדורש; the printed form is the same word, which he derives from a reconstructed *hamalores* (Latin *hamus*, “hook”).

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: toward Shechem
Hosea.english_translation: An expression of one company.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: a horrible thing
Hosea.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: an expression of change, that they changed their way; and so (Jeremiah 5) “An appalling and horrible thing.”

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Also, O Judah
Hosea.english_translation: He too, since he acted corruptly.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: appointed
Hosea.english_translation: He set a time of punishment for her.
Hosea.translator_note: The printed word is המשית; it is read as השית (“set”).

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: a harvest
Hosea.english_translation: The time of her departure and her exile, like “Yet a little while, and the time of harvest shall come for her” (ibid. 51) — regarding the punishment of Babylon in the Book of Jeremiah.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: When I would turn the captivity of My people
Hosea.english_translation: When I rebuke them, to turn them back from their backslidings.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: the captivity of My people
Hosea.english_translation: An expression of backsliding of young women and of women who bear: einvaisura in French; and so “backsliding children” (ibid. 3), “O thou backsliding daughter” (ibid. 31).
Hosea.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this word (Hosea 6:11) in forms such as אנביישדורא, with a gloss that is partly illegible in my copy (it appears to be “égarement,” straying); the printed form is a close variant. The words “and of women who bear” fit poorly and are translated as printed.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: When I would heal Israel
Hosea.english_translation: When I desire to save them and to heal their iniquities, they were revealed before Me, for they constantly practiced falsehood, and thieves among them constantly come and steal the money of their fellows, and their troops even spread out in brigandage to rob people.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And let them not say to their heart
Hosea.english_translation: They do not set it to their heart that all their wickedness is written as a remembrance before Me.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: They make the king glad with their wickedness
Hosea.english_translation: Their king desires the evil that they do.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: As an oven heated by the baker
Hosea.english_translation: That was heated by the hand of the baker; so their inclination burns within them.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Who ceaseth to stir
Hosea.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: what it translated; and I cannot reconcile the language of Scripture with it. And according to its sense: their evil inclination, which was stirring them up, will cease.
Hosea.translator_note: The printed text does not give the Targum’s wording.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: From the kneading of the dough until it be leavened
Hosea.english_translation: After he has thought the evil in his heart, how he will do it, he rests and sleeps until the morning, when he is able to do it, like the baker who rests from kneading the dough until it has leavened and he is able to bake. And so he says (Micah 2:1): “Woe to them that devise iniquity and work evil upon their beds! When the morning is light, they execute it.”
Hosea.translator_note: Rashi’s wording of Micah 2:1 (“all their beds”) differs slightly from the verse; JPS wording is quoted.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: On the day of our king
Hosea.english_translation: On the day when they used to make their kings reign.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: The princes make him sick
Hosea.english_translation: Our princes were made sick.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: with the heat of wine
Hosea.english_translation: From the heat of the wine burning within them; and the king draws his hand away from the good and proper ones to associate with scoffers.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: For they have made ready their heart like an oven
Hosea.english_translation: They prepared and made ready their heart in their act of lying in wait, like this oven, which they prepare and heat for baking.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Their baker sleepeth all the night
Hosea.english_translation: Their baker, who heats the oven after they have prepared their heart and reckoned the completion of the evil, how they will do it.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Their baker sleepeth
Hosea.english_translation: That is, until the morning they sleep, and in the morning they burn like fire until they have completed their evil.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And devour their judges
Hosea.english_translation: They killed their Sanhedrin because they protested against them. And what came of it for them? “All their kings are fallen,” because there is none among them who calls to Me. And in the Yerushalmi, tractate Avodah Zarah, they expounded: “On the day of our king the princes make him sick with the heat of wine” — on the day that they made Jeroboam king, as is explained: They came to him and said to him: “Arise, make us an idol.” He said to them: “Now it is evening time, and all the people are drinking” — that is, it is a time of drunkenness; perhaps now you are drunk and tomorrow you will change your minds. “Go, and come in the morning.” They went and came in the morning. This is “For they have made ready their heart like an oven,” etc. He said to them: “I fear your Sanhedrin.” They said to him: “We shall kill them.” This is “and devour their judges.”
Hosea.translator_note: Part of the Yerushalmi passage is in Aramaic; it is translated as printed.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: All their kings are fallen
Hosea.english_translation: When he saw a righteous person, he would seat two scoffers beside him, and they would say to him: “Which generation is the dearest of all generations?” And he would say to them: “The generation of the wilderness.” And they would say to him: “But did they not practice idolatry?” And he would say to them: “Since they were dear, they were not punished.” And they would say to him: “Hush! the king wants to do thus” — be silent, for the king wants to do thus.
Hosea.translator_note: Rashi’s lemma (“He stretcheth out his hand with scorners,” 7:5) belongs to 7:5; the comment is placed here in the source. The lemma here is anchored to a nearby phrase of 7:7.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: he mixeth himself with the peoples
Hosea.english_translation: He will be mixed up in the Exile among the nations.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: a cake not turned
Hosea.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “like a loaf which, before it was turned, was eaten.” “Ugah” is a loaf that is baked on the coals.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And he knoweth it not
Hosea.english_translation: He did not set it to his heart that the kings of Aram devoured him in the days of Jehoahaz, as it is said (2 Kings 13:7): “For there was not left to Jehoahaz” etc., “and made them like the dust in threshing”; and nevertheless Jeroboam his son did not turn from the knowledge (another version: from the evil) of his father.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: gray hairs are here and there upon him
Hosea.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “Even weakness has reached them, and they do not take note.”

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And the pride of Israel testifieth to his face
Hosea.english_translation: “And the glory of Israel will be brought low, and they see” (Aramaic) — an expression of affliction. And this “ve-anah” is not an expression of the future but an expression of the past, like “And one called unto another” (Isaiah 6) — I heard that “one called to another” — and like “and he made him a coat of many colours” (Genesis 37); and this too is an expression of the past: they have already become few and lowly, and in spite of all this they have not returned to the LORD.
Hosea.translator_note: The Aramaic is translated as printed. “Brought low” for וימאך is inferred from Rashi’s own explanation (“affliction”).

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: without understanding
Hosea.english_translation: To discern what is good for them and what is bad for them.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: They call unto Egypt
Hosea.english_translation: Those who always did them evil, they call for help.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: they go to Assyria
Hosea.english_translation: To the king of Assyria they went, that he might help them.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Even as they go
Hosea.english_translation: To Egypt.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: I will spread My net upon them
Hosea.english_translation: For the eagle and the hawk rise above it and bring it down to the ground; so will I bring them down in Egypt by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: as their congregation hath been made to hear
Hosea.english_translation: I will bring chastisements upon them according to all that I make their congregation hear through Jeremiah the prophet, for they are destined to say to him, “Pray now for us” etc. (Jeremiah 42), “that the LORD thy God may tell us,” etc., “whether it be good or evil,” etc.; and he said to them: If you place yourselves to return to Egypt, “then it shall come to pass, that the sword, which you fear, shall overtake you there,” and the whole passage.
Hosea.translator_note: Rashi’s “Pray now for us” and “If you place yourselves to return to Egypt” are paraphrases of Jeremiah 42:2 and 42:15; JPS wording is quoted where Rashi’s words match the verse.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: I will chastise them
Hosea.english_translation: An expression of chastisements. And Menachem explained it as an expression of binding: “and will burst thy bands” (Jeremiah 30:8). But Dunash interpreted it as an expression of chastisements, as (Leviticus 26) “I will chastise you,” and the second yod is added in “esirem,” as it was added in “yishiru” in “and let thine eyelids look straight before thee” (Proverbs 4:25). Another explanation: like a bird of the heavens that is caught in a net hung on poles, and after they are in the net, they lower the net.
Hosea.translator_note: Rashi’s “to chastise you” is Leviticus 26:18 (spelled slightly differently there); JPS wording is quoted.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Shall I then redeem them
Hosea.english_translation: I was desiring to redeem them from the evil in which they are.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Seeing they have spoken lies against Me
Hosea.english_translation: They said to Jeremiah, “Thou speakest falsely” (ibid. 43), “the LORD our God hath not sent thee to say: You shall not go into Egypt.”

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Though they wail upon their beds
Hosea.english_translation: For therefore wailing will come upon them; so Targum Jonathan.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: They assemble themselves for corn and wine
Hosea.english_translation: They have granaries of grain; therefore they turn aside and rebel against Me.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Though I have trained and strengthened their arms
Hosea.english_translation: In My fear, through My prophets, to listen to them in that wherewith they chastise them, and their arms would be strengthened.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: They return, but not upwards
Hosea.english_translation: They returned to Egypt, and not to benefit themselves; therefore the “al” is pointed with a kamatz, like (2 Samuel 23:1) “the man raised on high,” because it is an expression of elevation and is not joined to the word after it.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: They are become like a deceitful bow
Hosea.english_translation: When he wishes to shoot an arrow with it to the north, it shoots to the south.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Their princes shall fall by the sword
Hosea.english_translation: Johanan the son of Kareah (Jeremiah 43:4) and all the soldiers who returned to Egypt.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: for the rage of their tongue
Hosea.english_translation: A harsh tongue, in that they answered Jeremiah.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: This shall be their derision in the land of Egypt
Hosea.english_translation: That they will mock them in the land of Egypt: “Why did you dwell with us, to bring punishments upon us? Is it not written for you, ‘you shall see them again no more for ever’ (Exodus 14:13)?”

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Set the horn to thy mouth
Hosea.english_translation: The Shekhinah says to the prophet: Hear the sound of your palate and call out like a shofar. And He says: Fly and hasten, enemies, as the vulture swoops and comes to the house of the LORD. “To thy palate a shofar” — as if the shofar were set to your palate.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Will they cry unto Me
Hosea.english_translation: When the evil comes upon them.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: My God, we Israel know Thee
Hosea.english_translation: “Are we not Your people?” And they transposed it and expounded it: “Israel will cry out to Me: My God, we know You,” and I shall not listen to them, for
Hosea.translator_note: The printed text ends with “for” and appears to be cut off.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Israel hath cast off that which is good
Hosea.english_translation: Therefore the enemy shall pursue him.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: They have made princes
Hosea.english_translation: They made princes. Another explanation: they removed this one from the kingship and made that one king. And the book of the Masorah proves it, for they compiled in the Masorah that they write a shin and read a samekh, and its interpretation is with a samekh.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: That they may be cut off
Hosea.english_translation: Because they had gold in abundance, and they caused wealth to be cut off from them.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Thy calf, O Samaria, is cast off
Hosea.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He, has cast you off, sons of Samaria, for the sin of the calves in Beth-el, which the kings of Samaria serve there.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: How long will it be ere they attain to innocency?
Hosea.english_translation: To turn their hearts to be cleansed of that filth.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: For from Israel is even this
Hosea.english_translation: It is collected from the silver and gold of each and every one, and the craftsman made it; and the vav of “vehu” falls away. And there are many vavs like it: (Ezekiel 46) “But the miry places thereof, and the marshes thereof, shall not be healed.” So too here: “for from Israel” you designated it and prepared it, and it was made. And one can settle this vav thus: “for from Israel, and it” — even this calf came from them, like the death of the first calf.
Hosea.translator_note: Printed “Ezekiel 46”; the verse is Ezekiel 47:11 (JPS wording quoted). The last phrase (“like the death of the first calf”) is translated as printed and is not clear to me.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: shall be broken in shivers
Hosea.english_translation: Splinters of boards (nisrei luchin). And it is an Aramaic word, as in “shiva mikhshora” (Sanhedrin 7).
Hosea.translator_note: The Aramaic expression is left transliterated.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: It hath no stalk
Hosea.english_translation: For their seed; that is, they will not succeed in their deeds.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: If so be it yield
Hosea.english_translation: Even if it yields flour.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: strangers shall swallow it up
Hosea.english_translation: Even if they succeed in their possessions, its end is to fall into the hands of strangers.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Like a wild ass alone by himself
Hosea.english_translation: They became like a wild ass that goes alone by itself, panting for wind from place to place to wander.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Ephraim hath hired lovers
Hosea.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: an expression of jackals (tannim), like this wild ass that goes in the wildernesses, panting for wind like jackals, to acquire for themselves lovers, adulterers, strangers; they “hired”: idgroniyot in French. And one may interpret it as an expression of etnan (hire).
Hosea.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this verse (Hosea 8:9) with the gloss “Aspiraient (à des amours adultères), comme frémissent les narines du dragon” (they panted for adulterous loves, as the nostrils of the dragon quiver), in forms such as אינדרגונירנט; the printed form is a close variant of the same verb.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Yea, though they hire among the nations
Hosea.english_translation: Even though they did this, that they hired lovers among the idolaters.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Now will I gather them up
Hosea.english_translation: When the time of their redemption comes, I will not delay it.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And they begin to be minished
Hosea.english_translation: They will be humbled a little in their exile in Babylon, from fear of the burden of king and princes, from the yoke of the nations who were among them.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: For Ephraim hath multiplied altars to sin
Hosea.english_translation: Therefore I will make him ill from the burden of king and princes.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Though I write for him never so many things of My Law
Hosea.english_translation: I constantly rebuke him through My prophets and write for him the multitude of My Torah, and they are considered as a stranger’s.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: As for the sacrifices that are made by fire unto Me
Hosea.english_translation: The sacrifices of My burnt-offering, which flame before Me with the fire on My altar.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Let them sacrifice flesh and eat it
Hosea.english_translation: What are they to Me, that they bring them? Let them sacrifice, so that they have flesh for their eating, and let them eat it, for I do not want them.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Rejoice not, O Israel, unto exultation, like the peoples
Hosea.english_translation: Like the other ancient idolaters, who did not receive Torah and did not come to My portion; and you have gone astray from Me and lost many good things.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Thou hast loved a harlot’s hire
Hosea.english_translation: To be like a harlot, to receive hire.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: upon every corn-floor
Hosea.english_translation: As is the way of a harlot, to whom they give grain on the threshing-floor as her hire.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: They shall not dwell in the LORD’S land
Hosea.english_translation: They shall not tarry in their land.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: They shall not pour out wine-offerings
Hosea.english_translation: An expression of nesekh (libation).

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Neither shall they be pleasing unto Him
Hosea.english_translation: Their meal-offering shall not be pleasing to Him.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: as the bread of mourners
Hosea.english_translation: Like bread of robbery, which comes through force and might (onim).

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: For their bread shall be for their appetite
Hosea.english_translation: This is fit for them as food, and not to come to the house of the LORD. Another explanation: “as the bread of mourners” — like the bread of mourners, which is unclean; and its end proves it: “All that eat thereof shall be polluted.”

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: the day of the appointed season
Hosea.english_translation: On the day of a fixed time, for the enemy is appointed to come upon you.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: the feast of the LORD
Hosea.english_translation: The sacrifice of slaughter that He has among you.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: For, lo, they are gone away from destruction
Hosea.english_translation: From their place, because of the multitude of plunderers who will come upon them with Nebuchadnezzar.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Memphis
Hosea.english_translation: It is of the land of Egypt.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Their precious treasures of silver
Hosea.english_translation: Houses of the desirable treasures of their silver.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: nettles
Hosea.english_translation: A thorn; kinds of beasts Jonathan translated.
Hosea.translator_note: The printed sentence is brief and I could not confirm its sense; it is translated literally.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: The days of visitation are come
Hosea.english_translation: That your iniquities will be visited.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: The days of recompense are come
Hosea.english_translation: “Completion of debts” (Aramaic).

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: The prophet is a fool
Hosea.english_translation: Even among their true prophets there will be fools, such as Hananiah the son of Azzur, whose beginning was that of a true prophet.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: the enmity is great
Hosea.english_translation: For the Holy One, blessed be He, hates your deeds.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Ephraim is a watchman with my God
Hosea.english_translation: They appoint for themselves their prophets, who draw them toward their idolatry.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: As for the prophet, a fowler’s snare is in all his ways
Hosea.english_translation: And for the true prophets they lay snares to trap them.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And enmity in the house of his God
Hosea.english_translation: In the Temple they killed Zechariah, and they sought to kill Jeremiah, as it is said (Jeremiah 26:11): “This man is worthy of death,” etc.
Hosea.translator_note: Rashi’s Hebrew (mishpat mavet la-ish ha-zeh, “a sentence of death for this man”) is not word for word the verse; JPS wording is quoted.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: As in the days of Gibeah
Hosea.english_translation: Some say this is Gibeah of Benjamin, in the matter of the concubine (Judges 19); and some say this is Gibeah of Saul (1 Samuel 11), because they asked for themselves a king and rebelled against the words of the prophet.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: I found Israel like grapes in the wilderness
Hosea.english_translation: Like grapes, which are dear in the wilderness, so I loved Israel.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: as the first-ripe in the fig-tree
Hosea.english_translation: Like a fig ripened on the fig-tree.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: at her first season
Hosea.english_translation: At the beginning of the ripening of the figs.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: I saw your fathers
Hosea.english_translation: So your fathers appeared in My eyes, to love them.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: They separated themselves
Hosea.english_translation: “Nezirah” everywhere is only an expression of separation.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: the shameful thing
Hosea.english_translation: To the idol, which is their shame.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And became detestable
Hosea.english_translation: Before Me.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: like that which they loved
Hosea.english_translation: The daughters of Moab.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: their glory shall fly away like a bird
Hosea.english_translation: The prophet said: Would that they were like this bird that wanders from its nest and ceases from fruitfulness and multiplying; so shall they lose their seed, either at the time of birth, or it will be absorbed in the womb and they will miscarry, or at the time of conception they will not conceive. For what profit is there in their raising their sons, since they will raise them and I will bereave them of man.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Yea, though they bring up
Hosea.english_translation: To the fathers.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: when I depart from them
Hosea.english_translation: Like “besuri mehem,” and it is from the Masorot: they write a shin and read a samekh. Another explanation: “like a bird their glory shall fly away,” etc.: like this bird that flies and is not, so all their glory will fly away and flee — all that they toiled over their children in birth and in pregnancy: “from birth” — this is the pain of birth; “and from the womb” — these are the days of gestation; “and from conception” — at the time of intercourse. All their toil will come to an end. How? For when they raise their children, I will bereave them.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: like as I have seen Tyre
Hosea.english_translation: In her tranquility she is crowned and rich above all the provinces; so I saw Ephraim, planted in a dwelling-place. And Ephraim — what recompense did he pay Me? He busied himself to bring out his sons to the slayer, to sacrifice them to the idol of Molech. So Targum Jonathan translated.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Give them, O LORD, whatsoever Thou wilt give
Hosea.english_translation: The prophet prays that they die small, for the mourning for a small one is not like the mourning for a grown one. Therefore, if it is not possible (to avert) birth and womb and conception, for it was already decreed from the creation of the world (Genesis 3:16), “and thy desire shall be to thy husband,” give them speedily, in their smallness, what You said You would give them later, as You said: “Yea, though they bring up their children, Yet will I bereave them.”

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Give them a miscarrying womb and dry breasts
Hosea.english_translation: At the time when they go out to the air of the world, they will die, or the breasts of their mother will shrivel, so that she has no milk to nurse.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: All their wickedness is in Gilgal
Hosea.english_translation: There they multiplied serving idols in the high places, because the Tabernacle was there at first; the prophets of the Baal used to say to them that it is a chosen place; and it belonged to the kings of Israel.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: I will love them no more
Hosea.english_translation: To love them.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: They shall bear no fruit
Hosea.english_translation: It is not good for them to be fruitful and to multiply, for “Yea, though they bring forth, Yet will I slay the beloved fruit of their womb.”

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: My God will cast them away
Hosea.english_translation: It is not a curse but a tiding: He is destined to cast them away.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Israel was a luxuriant vine
Hosea.english_translation: Israel is like a vine that sheds all its good fruit; so they forsook Me, for I am the good fruit, and that which is fitting for him.
Hosea.translator_note: The last clause (“and that which is fitting for him”) is translated literally; I could not confirm its sense.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Which put forth fruit freely
Hosea.english_translation: The fruit that is fitting for him, and that will be good for him.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: As his fruit increased, He increased his altars
Hosea.english_translation: When I bestowed upon them the good, they multiplied making calves for altars. Another explanation: “Israel is a luxuriant vine”; the fruit of his deeds caused him that “fruit shall be fitting for him” — it will benefit him to be luxuriant; for they made altars, and they benefited their assemblies for evil. And this is the language of the Targum.
Hosea.translator_note: The second explanation is compressed; it is translated as literally as possible.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: The more goodly were his pillars
Hosea.english_translation: They multiplied pillars.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Their heart is divided
Hosea.english_translation: From Me.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Now shall they bear their guilt
Hosea.english_translation: This is the matter: “He will break down their altars” — He will destroy; an expression of “and shall break the heifer’s neck there” (Deuteronomy 21), “then thou shalt break its neck” (Exodus 13): He will break their necks. Another explanation, according to an aggadic midrash: Great is peace, for even if Israel served idols, if there is peace among them, Satan does not accuse among them, as it is said: “Ephraim is joined to idols; Let him alone” (above, 4); but when the dispute is changed, as it is said, “Their heart is divided; Now shall they bear their guilt,” Satan has an opening of the mouth to accuse.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Surely now shall they say
Hosea.english_translation: When the evil comes upon them, they will say, “We have no king”: our king in whom we trusted, saying that he would go out first and fight our wars, is of no benefit to us — that is,
Hosea.translator_note: The printed text ends with “that is” (kelomar) and appears to be cut off.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: They speak words, They swear falsely, they make covenants
Hosea.english_translation: “Swearing falsely” (alot): to swear falsely, like “kerot” (making) — an expression of the present. Making a covenant with the idol of Molech; therefore judgment of chastisements and punishment will spring up upon them like rosh, which is a bitter herb that springs up in the furrows of the field. And Targum Jonathan: “on the furrows of the field” — on account of the sin that they move the boundaries of fields.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: In the furrows of the field
Hosea.english_translation: The furrow (ma’anit) of the plow is called a telem. Another explanation: “on the furrows of the field” — for they make their altars there, as it is said (below, 12): “Yea, their altars shall be as heaps In the furrows of the field”; there judgment for their iniquity will spring up. Another explanation: “Swearing falsely” — every covenant that they make with one another they transgress, and “judgment springs up like rosh on the furrows of the field”: like rosh that springs up on the furrows of the field, which is a bitter herb, so their judgments spring up and grow bitter for the poor and the needy. And Amos also said so: “That you have turned justice into gall” (Amos 6:12).

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: For the calves of Beth-aven
Hosea.english_translation: For the punishment destined to come upon the calves in Beth-el, which is called Beth-aven in the Book of Joshua.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: shall be in dread
Hosea.english_translation: Its neighbors in Samaria will fear it. Why? Because its people mourn over it, and its priests, who always rejoiced over it, will now mourn over its glory, for it has gone into exile.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: It also shall be carried unto Assyria
Hosea.english_translation: This was in the twelfth year of Ahaz: “And HaShem stirred up the spirit of Pul king of Assyria, and he exiled them, the Reubenites and the Gadites” (Chronicles I 5), etc.; and he took the golden calves that were in Beth-el and went away, to fulfill what is said: “It also shall be carried unto Assyria.”
Hosea.translator_note: Rashi’s wording of 1 Chronicles 5:26 differs slightly from the verse (JPS: “the God of Israel stirred up the spirit of Pul king of Assyria … and he carried them away, even the Reubenites, and the Gadites”); his wording is translated.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: King Contentious
Hosea.english_translation: This is Sennacherib.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Ephraim shall receive shame
Hosea.english_translation: Jeroboam, who is of the tribe of Ephraim, who set up this calf for himself as a god, shall take shame for himself.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And Israel shall be ashamed of his own counsel
Hosea.english_translation: Of that counsel that they took to make them, as it is said (1 Kings 12:28): “Whereupon the king took counsel, and made two calves of gold.”

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: her king is cut off
Hosea.english_translation: The king of Samaria has been silenced, and behold, he is like the foam on the face of the water, which is oscuma in French.
Hosea.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this word (Hosea 10:7) with the gloss “Comme l’écume” (like foam), in forms such as אישקומא; the printed form is a close variant.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: The high places also of Aven shall be destroyed
Hosea.english_translation: The high places of Beth-el.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: The thorn and the thistle shall come up on their altars
Hosea.english_translation: For those who served them were exiled, and no one turns to them any more.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And they shall say to the mountains
Hosea.english_translation: Israel.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: to the mountains: ‘Cover us’
Hosea.english_translation: That our enemies may not see us in our shame.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: From the days of Gibeah thou hast sinned, O Israel
Hosea.english_translation: This “chatat” is pointed without a dagesh (rafeh), for it is a feminine form and in the past tense, like “asat,” “ba’at,” “azlat yad.” From the days of Gibeah of Benjamin thou hast sinned, Israel, because the incident of the concubine in Gibeah was in the days of Othniel the son of Kenaz, who was the first of the judges, in the days of Cushan-rishathaim; and in his days was the idol of Micah; and all this we find in Seder Olam.
Hosea.translator_note: The three Hebrew examples are left transliterated as printed.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: There they stood
Hosea.english_translation: In that same measure they have clung to themselves since then.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: No battle was to overtake them in Gibeah
Hosea.english_translation: And since the sin of idolatry was in their hands and they did not take care about it, therefore their hand did not succeed in the war of Gibeah against the sons of Benjamin; and He called them “children of arrogancy” (bnei alvah), children of pride, who made themselves lofty and did not listen to the voice of their brothers to hand over the people of Gibeah. And Jonathan translated it as referring to the fact that they asked for themselves a king and made Saul king; and it does not settle for me according to the Hebrew language, and also the rest of the connection of the passage falls on the first expression.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: When it is My desire, I will chastise them
Hosea.english_translation: According to My will I constantly chastised them, from judge to judge, and delivered them into the hand of their plunderers.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And the peoples shall be gathered against them
Hosea.english_translation: Since he likened them to a heifer, as it says after it, “Ephraim is a heifer well broken,” therefore he likened their chastisements to a cow that they weary with plowing and bind in the yoke of the plow; and the simlonei of the yoke pierce and go down, one from here and one from there, beside the two eyes of the ox. And so Targum Jonathan: “like one who binds a padna upon its two eyes”; padna is a yoke of oxen.
Hosea.translator_note: The word וסימלוני (simlonei) is left transliterated, and the Aramaic is translated as printed.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And Ephraim is a heifer well broken
Hosea.english_translation: Porpointe in French: made with bruises, bruises, by the goad of oxen, which they call desgoliyon in French; that is, I brought many chastisements upon her, and behold, she was not humbled, and she always loves to thresh grain, a place of food and fatness, and was not humbled to plow; that is, they were not humbled to the Torah, but followed the stubbornness of their hearts.
Hosea.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this word (Hosea 10:11) with the gloss “Aiguillonnée” (goaded) in forms such as פורפויינטא (porpointe; a past participle of *porpoindre*), and, at the same verse, “Piquée par l’aiguillon” (pricked by the goad) in forms such as אגויילון. The printed forms are variants of these.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: That loveth to thresh
Hosea.english_translation: An extra yod, like (Genesis 31) “stolen by day” (ganuvti yom).

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And I have passed over upon her fair neck
Hosea.english_translation: Therefore I bring upon them kings who will weaken their strength.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: I will make Ephraim to ride, Judah shall plow
Hosea.english_translation: If you wish that I make Ephraim ride over idolaters, Judah shall plow, and (Jacob) shall break up for himself a plowing of good deeds, as He explains as it goes on and says: “Break up your fallow ground,” etc.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Sow to yourselves according to righteousness
Hosea.english_translation: But you have plowed wickedness, etc.; therefore “a tumult shall arise among thy people.”
Hosea.translator_note: Rashi’s “among thy people” differs slightly from the verse (10:14, JPS “among thy hosts”); “You have plowed wickedness” is 10:13.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Break up your fallow ground
Hosea.english_translation: Occupy yourselves in Torah, and from there you will learn to go in a good way, to overcome the evil inclination, like one who breaks up the field to turn over the roots of the weeds that weaken the grain, in the days of the summer heat, some days before the sowing; and a time you shall fix to seek HaShem — for the study of Torah.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Till He come and cause righteousness to rain upon you
Hosea.english_translation: When you toil in it, He will make you understand, to make known to you its hidden things in righteousness. Another explanation: “Break up for yourselves fallow ground” — do good deeds before distress comes upon you, and this will cause your prayer to be accepted at the time of need, and then it will be a fitting time for you to seek the Holy One, blessed be He, regarding all your needs, for then He will hear your cry, and “He will teach righteousness to you” and will rain righteousness upon you, as in “hath He cast into the sea” (Exodus 15).

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: You have eaten the fruit of lies
Hosea.english_translation: “You have received the completion of your deeds” (Aramaic).

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: shall a tumult arise
Hosea.english_translation: The sound of cries: “Flee! Flee!”

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: As Shalman spoiled Beth-arbel in the day of battle
Hosea.english_translation: Like plunderers who come suddenly upon a people dwelling in peace, by way of an ambush, who were not careful regarding them to flee from them, and who plunder everything.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Beth-arbel
Hosea.english_translation: Jonathan translated it “beit ma’arav” (house of ambush), and the aleph and lamed are superfluous in it, like Jezreel, which is not a name of a city, as (above, 2) “they shall respond to Jezreel”; and they called it in the language of a city-name. Here too he called it a kind of city-name; and so Menachem connected it, but Dunash interprets it as the name of a place.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: The mother was dashed in pieces with her children
Hosea.english_translation: It was split open; and so “And their bows shall dash the young men in pieces” (Isaiah 13:18) and “Their babes also shall be dashed in pieces” (ibid.). Another version: “rotshah” — forsaken, like “notshah.”
Hosea.translator_note: The second quotation is Isaiah 13:16 (printed “ibid.”).

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: So hath Beth-el done unto you
Hosea.english_translation: All this punishment was caused to you by the calf in Beth-el.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Because of your great wickedness
Hosea.english_translation: The evil of your wickedness: your deliberate transgressions.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: At daybreak is the king of Israel utterly cut off
Hosea.english_translation: Lulled to sleep, as if in the night; that is, there is no strength in him. And why all this? Because when Israel was a child and I loved him, (he was) shaken out of all good.
Hosea.translator_note: The last clause is compressed; it is translated literally.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: out of Egypt I called My son
Hosea.english_translation: Through My prophets, to cleave to My Torah; and what did they do?

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: The more they called them, the more they went from them
Hosea.english_translation: All that the prophets called to them, to teach them the good way, so they turned the back of the neck to flee from them.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: They sacrificed unto the Baalim
Hosea.english_translation: The way of Scripture is to speak thus, like “The more they were increased, the more they sinned against Me” (above, 4) and “But the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied” (Exodus 1:12).

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: I taught Ephraim to walk
Hosea.english_translation: I sent before them a leader who trained them gently.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Taking them by their arms
Hosea.english_translation: This is Moses, of whom it is said (Numbers 11:12): “as a nursing-father carrieth the sucking child.”

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: I taught Ephraim to walk
Hosea.english_translation: Like “hirgalti”; and there is no parallel to it.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: But they knew not that I healed them
Hosea.english_translation: They did know, but they trampled with the heel; they made themselves as not knowing. And an aggadah in Midrash Rabbi Tanchuma expounded this regarding the sons of Joseph: when he brought them before Jacob to bless them, Jacob saw that wicked men were destined to come out of Ephraim — Jeroboam and Ahab — and the Holy Spirit departed from him, and he said, “Who are these?” (Genesis 48). Joseph sought mercy, and the Holy Spirit rested on Jacob and he blessed them. This is “And I taught to walk”: My spirit upon Jacob, for the sake of Ephraim, “taking them by his arms.”
Hosea.translator_note: The last sentence is compressed; it is translated literally.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: I drew them with cords of a man
Hosea.english_translation: I was constantly drawing them with the soft cords with which a man draws his son; that is, with the drawing of compassion; and so Targum Jonathan.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And I was to them as they that take off the yoke on their jaws
Hosea.english_translation: Like the good farmers who lift the yoke with their hands by means of boards, to lighten it from the plowing cow; so I was with them in every trouble, to lighten it from upon them. (Another version: סא"א.) “Like those who lift the yoke on their jaws” — like farmers who lift a yoke from the neck of the ox by lengthening the pole on whose end the yoke is placed, to lighten it from the plowing cow; so I was with them in every trouble, to lighten it from upon them. So Jonathan translated: “like a good farmer, and he lengthens at their cheeks.”
Hosea.translator_note: it is left as printed. The Aramaic is translated as printed. The Aramaic verb (מוריך), here rendered “lengthens,” follows Rashi’s own explanation.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: on their jaws
Hosea.english_translation: An expression of the lechi (side-post) of an alley (mavoi).

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And I fed them gently
Hosea.english_translation: I inclined strength to him to bear the yoke of chastisements; and Jonathan translated it on account of the fact that He provided them with food in the wilderness.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: He shall not return into the land of Egypt
Hosea.english_translation: I promised him, “you shall see them again no more for ever” (Exodus 14:13), and what good did it do? Behold, against his will Assyria is his king. Behold, they sinned and caused themselves to be servants to Assyria, “because they refused to return.”

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And the sword shall fall upon his cities
Hosea.english_translation: And a sword shall rest in his cities.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And shall consume his bars, and devour them
Hosea.english_translation: And it shall consume his warriors and devour them.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Because of their own counsels
Hosea.english_translation: Two accents are marked in it, the tipcha and the silluk, since it is a word on its own; and so lehechalo, with “lo yitama ba’al be’amav” (Leviticus 21), and so ledorotekhem, with “shemen mishchat kodesh” (Exodus 30).
Hosea.translator_note: This note concerns cantillation accents and is compressed; it is translated as printed. The Leviticus verse is 21:4 and the Exodus verse is 30:31.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And My people are in suspense about returning to Me
Hosea.english_translation: When the prophets teach them to return to Me, they are in suspense whether to return or not to return; with difficulty will they return to Me.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And though they call them upwards
Hosea.english_translation: “And to the matter upon which the prophets call him together, My people will not exalt it,” and it is not fitting to do it. And there is one who interprets “and to al they call him” — hard blows will befall them; and “el” is like “yesh le’el yadi” (Genesis 31); but this is not so, for it is pointed with a patach, and if “v’el” were a noun it would be pointed with a tzere. And Jonathan translated: “with a hard evil they will be yit’aru’un”; he made “el” (סא"א על) an expression of hardness. And to me it seems that I have interpreted it properly.
Hosea.translator_note: it is left as printed. The Aramaic verb yit’aru’un is left transliterated.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: None at all will lift himself up
Hosea.english_translation: Targum: “Together they will not walk in upright stature.”

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: How shall I give thee up
Hosea.english_translation: I will deliver you into the hand of your enemies, as in “who hath delivered thine enemies into thy hand” (Genesis 14:20).
Hosea.translator_note: Printed “ibid. 14”; the phrase quoted (מגן צריך) is Genesis 14:20.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: kindled together
Hosea.english_translation: They became hot; an Aramaic expression. And so “Our skin is hot like an oven” (Lamentations 5:10): “nikhmaru.”

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: I will not return to destroy Ephraim
Hosea.english_translation: From the good words that I said (Leviticus 26): “I will not reject them, neither will I abhor them” — to be destroying Ephraim.
Hosea.translator_note: Printed “Leviticus 26”; the verse is Leviticus 26:44.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: For I am God, and not man
Hosea.english_translation: The One who fulfills the word of My goodness; and it is not My attribute to repent of the good.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: The Holy One in the midst of thee; And I will not come in fury
Hosea.english_translation: Another explanation: I have already promised to cause My Shekhinah to dwell in your midst in Jerusalem, and I will not cause it to dwell again upon another city. And some explain “be-ir” as an expression of enmity, like “and is become thine adversary” (1 Samuel 28:16).
Hosea.translator_note: Printed “1 Samuel 25”; the phrase quoted (ויהי ערך) is 1 Samuel 28:16.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Who shall roar like a lion
Hosea.english_translation: He will yet roar to them like a lion, so that they come out of the exiles and go after Him.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: the children shall come trembling from the west
Hosea.english_translation: And the exiles shall be gathered from the west.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: compasseth Me about
Hosea.english_translation: “Already, with lies and deceit” are “Ephraim and the house of Israel” — the kings of the ten tribes and all the people; but Judah still “rules with God,” still in the fear of God. “Rad” is like “And out of Jacob shall one have dominion” (Numbers 24:19); still their kings are with the Holy One, blessed be He.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Ephraim striveth after wind
Hosea.english_translation: An expression of “friend”: he joins himself to words of wind, to the idolaters; and their oil they carry to Egypt, to give a bribe to Egypt to help them.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: The LORD hath also a controversy with Judah
Hosea.english_translation: To them He relates the words of His controversy, which their brothers, the house of Israel, did to Him; and let them not be astonished when He punishes Jacob according to his ways.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: In the womb he took his brother by the heel
Hosea.english_translation: All this I did for him. His holding on to his heel is a sign that he would be a master to him.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: He wept
Hosea.english_translation: The angel.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: made supplication unto him
Hosea.english_translation: When he said to him, “I will not let thee go, except thou bless me” (Genesis 32:27), the angel was asking of him: Let me be now. In the end the Holy One, blessed be He, will be revealed to you at Beth-el, “and there he would find him, and there he would speak with us,” and He and I will agree with you about the blessings with which Isaac blessed you. And that angel was the prince of Esau, and he was contesting the blessings.
Hosea.translator_note: The printed “ידב'” is read as “ידבר” (will speak).

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: the LORD, the God of hosts, The LORD is His name
Hosea.english_translation: As I was from of old, so am I now; and if you walked with Me in wholeheartedness like Jacob your father, I would deal with you as I dealt with him.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: turn thou to thy God
Hosea.english_translation: On His promise and on His support — on what He promises you — you can lean, and you will return to Him. Only “Keep mercy and justice,” and you are assured of hoping for His salvation always.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: the balances of deceit are in his hand
Hosea.english_translation: You rely on your gain, because you are traders and deceivers, and on your riches you say, “Surely I am become rich,” and I will not serve the Holy One, blessed be He.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: I have found me wealth
Hosea.english_translation: “Aven” is strength. And Rabbi Shimon, of blessed memory, used to expound an aggadic midrash: “I have found aven li” — I have found for myself a bond of debt, that I have kingship over Israel: “And his brethren also went and fell down… Behold, we are thy bondmen” (ibid. 50). “Aven li” — the laws of a document, as they write upon it “its ono,” and as in “ba-oni ehad u-vetimi ahat in Bereshit Rabbah.” And this is its explanation: “And Ephraim said: Surely I am become rich, I have found me aven.” Jeroboam son of Nebat, who was of the tribe of Ephraim, boasts of himself and says: Surely I am become rich, I have found me aven — a single document, that all Israel are slaves to me, because my father acquired them, as it is written, “And his brethren also went and fell down before his face; and they said: Behold, we are thy bondmen,” and what a slave acquires, his master acquires, and all their money is mine; therefore there is no sin in me if I take all that they have, for they are my slaves. What is written after it? “I am the LORD thy God from the land of Egypt” (Exodus 20:2): the greatness that came to your father in Egypt was from Me. The Holy One, blessed be He, said: “Behold, we are thy bondmen” you did not forget; but “I am the LORD thy God,” as it is said in the Ten Commandments, you forgot, for you set up two calves, one in Beth-el and one in Dan. And as for the plain sense of the verse, you say, “I have found aven for me” through oppression and balances of deceit; “and I am the LORD thy God from the land of Egypt” — there I distinguished between the drop of a firstborn and the drop of one who is not a firstborn; I too know, and I exact payment from balances of deceit that are made without understanding, and from him who hides his weights in salt in order to deceive.
Hosea.translator_note: The passage beginning “‘Aven li’ — the laws of a document…”, including “they write upon it its ono” and the abbreviation “באוני אחד ובטימי אחת בב"ר”, is obscure in the printed text and is translated literally; “בב"ר” is read as Bereshit Rabbah. The last sentence (“balances of deceit that are made without understanding”) is also terse. Printed “ibid. 50” is Genesis 50:18. The words “I am the LORD thy God from the land of Egypt” are those of Hosea 12:10, though the printed reference is to Exodus 20:2.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: In all my labours
Hosea.english_translation: It is good for you if you say in your heart: All my wealth will not suffice to atone for the iniquity that I have sinned. So Jonathan translated: The prophet said to them, “All your riches will not endure for you on the day your sins are completed.”

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: they shall find in me
Hosea.english_translation: They will not suffice, like “will they suffice them?” (Numbers 11:22). And it is not possible to explain “kol yegi’ai” as “all the toils to seek iniquity, and no iniquity will be found in me,” for if so it would have been proper to write “kol yagia’” without a yod and to vocalize it with a tzere; but now it is not an expression of “yaga” (toil) but an expression of “yegia’” (produce, labor).

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: I will yet again make thee to dwell in tents
Hosea.english_translation: I will cut off from your midst traders of deceit, and I will make you dwell in tents: I will raise up from your midst disciples who engage in Torah.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: As in the days of the appointed season
Hosea.english_translation: Like the days of the first appointed season, when Jacob was “a quiet man, dwelling in tents.”
Hosea.translator_note: The quoted words are Genesis 25:27; no reference is printed.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: I have also spoken unto the prophets
Hosea.english_translation: To rebuke you and to bring you back to the good.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: have I used similitudes
Hosea.english_translation: I appeared to them in many likenesses. Another explanation: “Adameh” — I liken to them My words by means of parables, in order to settle them upon those who hear them.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: If Gilead be given to iniquity
Hosea.english_translation: If breaking and distress came upon them, they caused it to themselves, for they were only vanity; and in Gilgal they sacrificed bullocks to idolatry.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: their altars shall be as heaps
Hosea.english_translation: Many, like the heaps that are upon the furrows of the field. “The furrows of the field” is the ma’anit of the plowing, which is called a “telem” (furrow).

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And Jacob fled into the field of Aram
Hosea.english_translation: Like a person who says: Let us return to the first things that we spoke of above — “and he strove with the angel” — and in addition I did this for him: he was compelled to flee to the field of Aram; you know how I kept him.
Hosea.translator_note: Rashi’s wording has “the angel”; JPS Hosea 12:5 reads “an angel”.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: for a wife he kept sheep
Hosea.english_translation: The flock.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And by a prophet the LORD brought Israel up out of Egypt
Hosea.english_translation: And because you despise the prophets and mock their words — was it not “by a prophet the LORD brought Israel up out of Egypt,” etc.?

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Ephraim hath provoked most bitterly
Hosea.english_translation: His Creator — by despising His prophets and by betraying Him.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: most bitterly
Hosea.english_translation: They are for him, because of his bloodshed which he shed by causing Israel to sin, to cleave to idolatry; and one who causes another to sin is worse for him than one who kills him, as we learn from Ammon and Moab, who caused Israel to err to cleave to Baal-peor, and the Writ punished them more than the Egyptian and the Edomite, who drowned them in the river and went out with the sword to meet them.
Hosea.translator_note: Rashi’s lemma is the plural noun “bitternesses” (תמרורים); JPS renders the word as an adverb (“most bitterly”). The printed “לאד'” is read as “לאדם”.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: shall his blood be cast upon him
Hosea.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He, will cast them upon him.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: his reproach
Hosea.english_translation: That he reproached Solomon, as in the matter that is said (1 Kings 11), “he lifted up his hand against the king” — that he rebuked him in public because Solomon built the Millo, as is explained in “Chelek.”
Hosea.translator_note: Printed “1 Kings 11”; the verse is 1 Kings 11:27. “Chelek” is printed without further identification.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: his Lord return unto him
Hosea.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He, for it is He who is able to do evil more than he.
Hosea.translator_note: The last clause (שהרי הוא הרע לעשות יותר ממנו) is terse; translated literally.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: When Ephraim spoke, there was trembling
Hosea.english_translation: When Jeroboam became zealous for the Omnipresent and spoke against Solomon harsh words, and with trembling, for Solomon was a great king.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: He exalted himself in Israel
Hosea.english_translation: From there he merited to be raised up, to be king over Israel.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: he became guilty through Baal
Hosea.english_translation: Once he rose to greatness, he became guilty through idolatry.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: he died
Hosea.english_translation: The house of Jeroboam was cut off, and so the house of Ahab. And Jonathan translated: When one of the house of Ephraim spoke, trembling seized the nations; they were arrogant in Israel, and when they sinned with idolatrous worship they are slain.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And now they sin more and more
Hosea.english_translation: The house of Jehu, who saw all this, will continue to sin.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: According to their own understanding
Hosea.english_translation: According to their pattern.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: They that sacrifice men kiss calves
Hosea.english_translation: The priests of Molech say to Israel: One who sacrifices his son to idolatry is worthy to kiss the calf, for he has offered it a beloved gift. So our Rabbis explained in Sanhedrin; and it is more settled upon the language of Scripture than the Targum of Jonathan.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And as the dew that early passeth away
Hosea.english_translation: And dew, de-mohi, ceases.
Hosea.translator_note: The Aramaic word דמוהי is unclear in the printed text and is left transliterated; the rest means “and dew … ceases.” The Aramaic is translated as printed.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: As the chaff that is driven with the wind out of the threshing-floor
Hosea.english_translation: Like chaff that the wind blew from the threshing-floor.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: driven with the wind
Hosea.english_translation: “Which a storm carries it away.”

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Yet I am the LORD thy God
Hosea.english_translation: And you should not have rebelled against Me.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: I did know thee in the wilderness
Hosea.english_translation: I set My heart to know your need, and I supplied you.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: great drought
Hosea.english_translation: It has no parallel, and its interpretation according to its context: a tel (mound) in which they draw all good and do not find.
Hosea.translator_note: Rashi explains the word as a compound of “tel” and “she’uvin”.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: When they were fed
Hosea.english_translation: When they came to the land of their pasture and were sated, then…

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: their heart was exalted
Hosea.english_translation: Like “and he lifted up (va-yarem) the rod” (Exodus 7:20) — an expression of lifting. Another explanation: “va-yarem” here — and he himself became high.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: As a leopard will I watch by the way
Hosea.english_translation: Every “Ashur” in Scripture has a dagesh, and this one is soft, because it is not a place name; rather, “I will lie in wait and I will watch,” like “I behold him, but not nigh” (Numbers 24:17).
Hosea.translator_note: Printed “Numbers 24”; the verse is Numbers 24:17.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: bear that is bereaved of her whelps
Hosea.english_translation: Like “shokhel”; as you say “gracious and compassionate,” so “shakhul” — that is, it is entirely clothed in bereavement and ready to bereave men.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And will rend the enclosure of their heart
Hosea.english_translation: In the manner of the bear, which sets its claws in the chest and tears up to the heart. Another explanation: “the enclosure of their heart” — their heart, which is closed from understanding to return to Me.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: It is thy destruction, O Israel
Hosea.english_translation: You have ruined yourself, Israel, for against Me you have transgressed; you rebelled against your Helper. And this is an elliptical verse, and one who understands the language of Scripture finds it settled at heart.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: against Me, against thy help
Hosea.english_translation: For the rebellion that you rebelled was against Me; and if you say, “What is it to you?” — against your Helper you rebelled when you rebelled against Me.
Hosea.translator_note: The sentence is terse; translated literally.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Ho, now, thy king
Hosea.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “Where is your king?” And I say: there is no need to uproot it from its meaning — “ehi”: I stand opposite to see where is your king; I will make myself see what is your end, where is your savior.
Hosea.translator_note: JPS renders “ehi” as “Ho”; Rashi takes it as “I shall be (standing)”.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: The iniquity of Ephraim is bound up
Hosea.english_translation: I have not relinquished it; it is stored with Me.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: For it is time
Hosea.english_translation: Distress comes upon him, such that he will not be able to stand and to endure.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: the breaking forth of children
Hosea.english_translation: That on which the woman giving birth sits to give birth; and in French they call the mishbar “shila.”
Hosea.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters (שיל"א). Darmesteter lists it at Hosea 13:13 with the gloss “on the chair (of childbirth)” and gives the forms שילא; the printed spelling matches.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: the breaking forth of children
Hosea.english_translation: Like a mishbar (birthing-stool) that is made for the birth of children.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Shall I ransom them from the power of the nether-world
Hosea.english_translation: I am He who used to redeem them from the hand of Sheol and deliver them from death; but now “ehi devarekha mot” — I will set myself to speak against you the words of death.
Hosea.translator_note: Rashi’s reading of “ehi devarekha mot” (JPS: “Ho, thy plagues, O death”) is translated as printed.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Ho, thy plagues, O death
Hosea.english_translation: “Koteb” — upon you is the decree of Sheol.
Hosea.translator_note: Rashi’s comment glosses the following “ehi” clause of the verse (“Ho, thy destruction, O netherworld”); the printed lemma is only “ehi.”

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Repentance be hid from Mine eyes
Hosea.english_translation: I will not repent of this evil. “Nocham” is an expression of comfort (nihum), and the mem belongs to the root of the word, like the mem of “noam,” for the accent is above and the het is vocalized with a patah. And if it were an expression of “nach” and the mem served in it as a plural, its accent would be under the het and it would be vocalized with a kamatz: נוחם, רוחם.
Hosea.translator_note: The argument depends on vowel points and accents that are not printed in the text; translated literally, and the last two words are left as printed.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: be fruitful among the reed-plants
Hosea.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: For they are called sons, and their deeds are corrupt; they multiplied. “Achim” is an expression of an evil thing, like “ah! it is made glittering” (Ezekiel 21:20), and it says, “Alas! because of all the evil abominations” (ibid. 7).
Hosea.translator_note: Printed “את עשויה לברק” reads את; the verse has אח. Printed “ibid. 7”; the phrase “Alas! because of all the evil abominations” is in Ezekiel 6:11.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: be fruitful
Hosea.english_translation: An expression of “a root that beareth gall and wormwood” (Deuteronomy 29:17). But I say: “achim” is an expression of “and they fed in the reed-grass” (Genesis 41:2): “among reeds he shall be fruitful” — blossoming and sprouting in the reed-grass, among that which grows by streams of water, which always bears fruit; and because He likened him to reed-grass, He says: Let an east wind come, and his spring will dry up. Another explanation: “For he among brothers will be fruitful” — Jeroboam is the son who hifri’a the brotherhood of Israel; through him they were divided into two kingdoms; “yafri” is an expression of “pere adam” (a wild man).
Hosea.translator_note: The phrase “הוא בן שהפריא אחוותן של ישראל” plays on the verb in the verse and is translated with the verb left transliterated (hifri’a).

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: An east wind shall come
Hosea.english_translation: A king as strong as the east wind: by the word of HaShem, from the way of the wilderness he shall ascend.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: He shall spoil the treasure of all precious vessels
Hosea.english_translation: That king will plunder the treasures of all his precious vessels.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: They shall fall by the sword
Hosea.english_translation: From now her guilt will be revealed.
Hosea.translator_note: Rashi’s lemma, “Samaria shall bear her guilt,” stands in JPS at the end of Hosea 13:15 on this site, so a nearby phrase from this verse is used as the lemma.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: their women with child shall be ripped up
Hosea.english_translation: The pregnant women who are within her.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Return, O Israel, unto the LORD thy God
Hosea.english_translation: Who are in the land of Judah, lest it befall you as it befell Samaria; therefore the matters were placed adjacent. A parable: to a king against whom a province rebelled; the king sent a polemarch and told him to destroy it. That polemarch was knowledgeable and composed. He said to them: Take for yourselves days, and if not, I will do to you as I did to such-and-such province and its neighbors, and to such-and-such eparchy and its neighbors. Therefore it is said, “Samaria shall bear her guilt,” and it says, “Return, O Israel, unto the LORD thy God,” as is found in the Sifrei in the portion “And Israel abode in Shittim.”
Hosea.translator_note: “Polemarch” and “eparchy” are transliterations of the Greek terms printed in Hebrew letters.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: unto the LORD thy God
Hosea.english_translation: It was taught in the name of Rabbi Meir: “Return, O Israel,” while He is “HaShem,” the attribute of mercy; and if not, “thy God,” the attribute of justice — before the defender (sanegoria) becomes the prosecutor (kategoria).

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: thou hast stumbled in thine iniquity
Hosea.english_translation: Stumbling-blocks have come to you because of your iniquities.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Forgive all iniquity
Hosea.english_translation: Forgive all our iniquities.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: accept that which is good
Hosea.english_translation: “And take good” — and teach us the good way. Another explanation: the few good deeds in our hands, take into Your hand and judge us after them. And so David says: “Let my judgment come forth from Thy presence; Let Thine eyes behold equity” (Psalms 17:2). Another explanation: “And take good” — and receive thanksgiving from us, as it is said, “It is a good thing to give thanks unto the LORD” (ibid. 92).
Hosea.translator_note: Printed “ibid. 92” is Psalms 92:2.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: So will we render for bullocks the offering of our lips
Hosea.english_translation: What we should have offered before You, we will make good with the appeasement of the words of our lips.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: Asshur shall not save us
Hosea.english_translation: Again they said this before Him: We will no longer seek the help of man, not from Assyria and not from Egypt.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: We will not ride upon horses
Hosea.english_translation: This is the help of Egypt, who used to send them horses, as they said to Isaiah (Isaiah 50 [sic]): “No, for we will flee upon horses… We will ride upon the swift.” And we will not say any more.
Hosea.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 50” (נ); the verse is Isaiah 30:16 (ל).

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: the work of our hands our gods
Hosea.english_translation: That they are our gods.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: For in Thee the fatherless findeth mercy
Hosea.english_translation: In You alone will be our hope — You who have compassion on orphans.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: I will heal their backsliding
Hosea.english_translation: The prophet said: Thus the Holy Spirit said to me: Since they will say before Him thus, “I will heal their backsliding, and love them freely” — through the freewill-offering of My spirit; although they are not worthy of love, I will volunteer to love them, “for Mine anger is turned away from him.”
Hosea.translator_note: The clause “מאחר שיאמרו לפני כן ארפא משובתם” is terse and its punctuation is uncertain; translated literally.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: And cast forth his roots as Lebanon
Hosea.english_translation: He will cast his roots and make them succeed like Lebanon, like the roots of the trees of Lebanon, which are great.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: His branches shall spread
Hosea.english_translation: Sons and sons will multiply, and their splendor will be like the splendor of the lamp of the Sanctuary, and their fragrance like the fragrance of the incense of spices.
Hosea.translator_note: The phrase “בנין ובנן” is rendered literally. The Aramaic is translated as printed.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: his fragrance as Lebanon
Hosea.english_translation: Like the house of the Sanctuary.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: They that dwell under his shadow shall again
Hosea.english_translation: Those who were already dwelling in the shade of Lebanon, to which He likened Israel and the Temple, and have now been exiled from his people, will return to it.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: The scent thereof shall be as the wine of Lebanon
Hosea.english_translation: Like the remembrance of the blasts of the trumpet over old wine that is poured out in the Sanctuary — for they would blow trumpets over the libations when the Levites recited the song.
Hosea.translator_note: The first part is Aramaic.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: What have I to do any more with idols
Hosea.english_translation: He shall say: What have I any more to go after the idols? And they shall return from idolatry. I will answer him from his distress.
Hosea.translator_note: The printed אתרי is read as אחרי (after).

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: look on him
Hosea.english_translation: I will look upon his affliction.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: I am like a leafy cypress-tree
Hosea.english_translation: I will bend down to him, so that he may hold his hand on Me, like a leafy cypress that bends toward the ground so that a person takes hold of its branches; that is, I will be available to him.

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: From Me is thy fruit found
Hosea.english_translation: Is it not I from whom all your good comes?

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: let him understand these things
Hosea.english_translation: Among you; “and let him understand these things.” Who among you is wise and will contemplate, to set his heart to all these, and return to Me?

Hosea.english_lemma_JPS: transgressors do stumble therein
Hosea.english_translation: On their account, because they did not walk in them. So Jonathan translated.

Joel.english_translation: The son of Samuel the prophet, who persuaded God (pitah le-El) by his prayer. Some say that this prophecy was spoken during those seven years of which Elisha said (2 Kings 8), “for the LORD hath called for a famine,” etc.; and they were in the days of Joram son of Ahab. And in Halakhot Gedolot it is found that Joel and Nahum and Habakkuk were in the days of Manasseh.
Joel.translator_note: Printed “2 Kings 8”; the verse is 2 Kings 8:1.

Joel.english_lemma_JPS: Hath this been in your days
Joel.english_translation: That which is said below.

Joel.english_lemma_JPS: That which the palmer-worm hath left hath the locust eaten
Joel.english_translation: Gazam, arbeh, yelek, chasil are kinds of locusts; and he prophesied about them that they would come, and they came in those days, and they consumed all the fruit of the tree and the herb of the field.
The good wine.

Joel.english_lemma_JPS: a people is come up upon my land
Joel.english_translation: He figuratively called these locusts like the army of a nation.
They are the large teeth with which it chews.
To despair of life (mappach nefesh).
Joel.translator_note: The gloss “למפח נפש” is terse; translated literally.

Joel.english_lemma_JPS: He hath made it clean bare, and cast it down
Joel.english_translation: Peeled the bark of the tree and cast it down, until the branches of the vine turned white.
A lament; we translate it “allya.”
Like “nikhrat”: the heh, vocalized with a hataf-kamatz, stands in the place of a nun, like “and the beasts of the field shall be at peace (hushlemah) with thee” (Job 5:23).
Joel.translator_note: Printed “Job 5”; the verse is Job 5:23. The word compared is printed השלמ' and read as השלמה.

Joel.english_translation: Be put to shame.
Those who guide the plow.

Joel.english_lemma_JPS: For the wheat and for the barley
Joel.english_translation: This refers back to the husbandmen; and concerning the vinedressers he said…
Joel.translator_note: The printed sentence ends with “he said.”

Joel.english_translation: It was cut off; its fruit ceased.
Like “yavesh” (dried).
Prepare a fast.
A gathering.
An expression of a groan of wailing.
And like the plunder of robbers.
From the Omnipresent.
We are seeing.
They brought up rust and mustiness; in French, “moyishir.”
Joel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters (מוי"ישיר). Darmesteter lists it at Joel 1:17 for עבשו with the gloss “have become moldy” (moisi) and the forms מוישיר / מויישיר; the printed spelling matches.

Joel.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “jars of wine.”
Targum Jonathan: “their stoppers” — the stopper, the covering of the casks.
Of wine and of oil.
Granaries of wheat.
They were confused and shut in and wandered in the forests and in the wildernesses.
They were ruined in their guilt.
An expression of dwelling.
It cries out, as Dunash interpreted: “arag” for stags, “naham” for lions, “ga’ah” for calves, “tzahal” for horses, chirping for birds, and “navach” for dogs.

Joel.english_lemma_JPS: Blow you the horn in Zion
Joel.english_translation: In order to make them hear, that they return in repentance before this evil comes upon them.
What we said above.

Joel.english_lemma_JPS: As blackness spread upon the mountains
Joel.english_translation: The locust and the gazam spread out over the mountains like the dawn that spreads over the whole world.

Joel.english_lemma_JPS: There hath not been ever the like
Joel.english_translation: For all these kinds to come one after the other; but the locust kind alone has not been like that one of Egypt, as it is said, “neither after them shall be such” (Exodus 10:14).
Joel.translator_note: The first clause is a fragment in the printed text; translated literally.

Joel.english_translation: They destroy everything, as if a fire were consuming before them and a flame blazing behind them.

Joel.english_lemma_JPS: as the garden of Eden before them
Joel.english_translation: The land was so before his coming, and after he goes he leaves the land as a desolate wilderness.

Joel.english_lemma_JPS: The appearance of them is as the appearance of horses
Joel.english_translation: In his running.

Joel.english_lemma_JPS: a flame of fire That devoureth the stubble
Joel.english_translation: That which devours stubble causes a sound to be heard.

Joel.english_lemma_JPS: As a mighty people set in battle array
Joel.english_translation: Because it is attached, it is vocalized with a hataf-segol.
Joel.translator_note: The comment concerns the vocalization of the word; translated as printed.

Joel.english_translation: Blackness like a pot, as you say, “and seethed it in pots” (Numbers 11); and the alef that is written is superfluous and is not read.
Joel.translator_note: Printed “Numbers 11”; the verse is Numbers 11:8. Rashi’s word is the singular “pot” (פרור); JPS has “pots.”

Joel.english_lemma_JPS: And they entangle not their paths
Joel.english_translation: It has no parallel, and its interpretation according to its context: they will not turn crooked.

Joel.english_lemma_JPS: And they break through the weapons
Joel.english_translation: Like “through the windows”: over the face of weapons they will fall and encamp.

And they will not receive money. And Jonathan interpreted it in it as an expression of “mission”: for the sake of the mission of the Holy One, blessed be He, they cast themselves down, “they took no gain of money.”
Joel.translator_note: No reference is printed for the closing phrase; it is Judges 5:19.

Joel.english_translation: An expression of making a sound, like “As locusts leap” (Isaiah 33:4), “a ravenous bear” (Proverbs 28), “the breeding-place of nettles” (Zephaniah 2:9). And Targum Jonathan: an expression of nesheq (weapon) — arming themselves.
Joel.translator_note: Printed “Proverbs 28” is Proverbs 28:15. JPS renders these verses differently from the sense of “sound” that Rashi draws from the words.

Joel.english_translation: On account of the punishment coming upon Israel they are agitated and tremble.
They drew in their light.
He gave His voice upon them by the utterance of His prophets, before He sent against them this army of His.

Joel.english_lemma_JPS: For His camp is very great
Joel.english_translation: That He will send against you if you do not do well.
For I do not care about the tearing of your garments. Another explanation: Rend your hearts, and you will not need to rend your garments because of mourning.

Joel.english_lemma_JPS: And repenteth Him of the evil
Joel.english_translation: He turns to another thought.
That there is iniquity in him; He will turn and relent.
Joel.translator_note: The syntax is terse; translated literally.

Joel.english_lemma_JPS: And leave a blessing behind Him
Joel.english_translation: The chasil and the gazam; after him a blessing: through repentance a blessing will come in the fruits.
Joel.translator_note: The comment is terse and its punctuation is supplied.

Joel.english_translation: From the forms of “shelach,” “qibbutz,” “eli” — an expression soft and light.
Joel.translator_note: The comment (ממשקלות שלח קבוץ אלי ל' רפי וקל) is obscure; the words are rendered as printed.

Joel.english_translation: To revilings.
An expression of a proverb and a sharp saying.

Joel.english_lemma_JPS: was the LORD jealous for His land
Joel.english_translation: An expression of “Art thou jealous for my sake?” (Numbers 11): her trouble entered His heart, and He fought her battle and busied Himself with her needs. And our Rabbis explained it as an expression of warning: He warned the locusts concerning the affairs of His land.
Joel.translator_note: Printed “Numbers 11”; the verse is Numbers 11:29. The printed ונלח' and במלחמת' are read as ונלחם and במלחמתה.

Joel.english_translation: A reviling, that they call you “lacking bread.”

It is possible to interpret it of the army of the locust, and upon it falls the expression “and will drive him into a land barren and desolate.” Another explanation: the people that comes from the north, the kings of Assyria; and our Rabbis say: this is the evil inclination, which is hidden (tzafun) in the heart of man.

Joel.english_lemma_JPS: With his face toward the eastern sea
Joel.english_translation: The eastern; and our Rabbis who explained it of the evil inclination expounded these two seas as the First Temple and the Second Temple; and so they explained it: because he set his face against the First and Second Temple and destroyed them. And according to the Targum, which explained it of the army of the king of Assyria, it must be read “his face (toward) the eastern sea” — part of his army I will send to the east and part of it to the west.
Joel.translator_note: The printed (אל) is in parentheses in the source.

Joel.english_translation: “Be’asho” (his ill savour) indicates it, that it is an expression of filth and soiling.
Joel.translator_note: The phrase באשו יורה עליו is terse; it is read here as pointing to the next word of the verse.

Joel.english_lemma_JPS: Because he hath done great things
Joel.english_translation: He saw that he stretched out his hand against the great.
Joel.translator_note: The subject of “saw” is not stated in the printed text; translated literally.
