Joel.english_translation: The Land of Israel — if you return in repentance.

Joel.english_lemma_JPS: the former rain in just measure
Joel.english_translation: Your prophets, who teach you to return to Me, in order to justify you.

Joel.english_lemma_JPS: The former rain and the latter rain
Joel.english_translation: Like “the former rain and the latter rain” (Deuteronomy 11:14).

In Nisan. And although the yoreh is the first rainfall that comes down upon the seed, and it is in Marcheshvan, that year they sowed in Nisan, as is explained in tractate Ta’anit, that the grain grew in eleven days.
An expression of making a sound, when the stream flows down from the winepress into the vat; and it is the pit that is before the winepress.

Joel.english_lemma_JPS: And it shall come to pass afterward
Joel.english_translation: In the time to come.
Upon one whose heart has become soft like flesh, like “and I will give you a heart of flesh” (Ezekiel 36:26).
Erect columns of smoke rising on high.

Joel.english_lemma_JPS: The sun shall be turned into darkness
Joel.english_translation: To shame those who bow down to the sun.
And where did He say it? “And all the peoples of the earth shall see that the name of the LORD is called upon thee” (Deuteronomy 28:10).
Among the remnant that He will leave.

Joel.english_lemma_JPS: those whom the LORD shall call
Joel.english_translation: An expression of those invited to a feast or to the service of the king; an expression of summoning.
I will go down with them into the depth of the judgment; “Jehoshaphat” — the judgments of Yah.

Joel.english_lemma_JPS: they have cast lots for My people
Joel.english_translation: Like “And have cast stones upon me” (Lamentations 3:53).

Joel.english_lemma_JPS: will you render retribution on My behalf
Joel.english_translation: This is the recompense that Solomon gave to Hiram king of Tyre — twenty cities (1 Kings 9).
Joel.translator_note: Printed “1 Kings 9”; see 1 Kings 9:11.

Joel.english_translation: An expression of alacrity.
To the children of Sheba.
And where did He speak? “a servant of servants shall he be unto his brethren” (Genesis 9:25). So it is explained in our Mekhilta.
Joel.translator_note: The printed name במכילתין is read as “our Mekhilta.”

Joel.english_translation: If you are able to fight against Me.
In French, “qalter’sh.”
Joel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters (קלטר"ש). Darmesteter lists it at Joel 4:10 for אתיכם with the gloss “your coulters” (vos coutres) and the forms קולטרש / קולטרא; the printed spelling lacks the vav.

Joel.english_translation: In French, “sharpesh’a.”
Joel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters (שרפש"א). Darmesteter lists it at Joel 4:10 for מזמרותיכם with the gloss “your pruning-knives” (vos serpes) and the forms שרפש / שרפשא; the printed spelling matches.

Joel.english_translation: Like “chushu” (hasten); so Menachem connected it. And Jonathan translated, “let them be gathered.” And I say that it is an expression of “eshet barzel,” iron that is gathered together — “masse” in French; and there is no tav in it as a root letter.
Joel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters (מש"א). Darmesteter lists it at Joel 4:11 with the gloss “press together, come in a mass” and reads it as “masse”; the printed spelling matches.

Joel.english_lemma_JPS: cause Thy mighty ones to come down
Joel.english_translation: There, in the gathering of the valley of Jehoshaphat, He will break your might; so Jonathan translated. And I do not know whether it is an Aramaic expression of lowering, or an expression of dread (chittat); and the nun in it drops out, like “han’el” in Daniel 2 (“Then Arioch brought in Daniel before the king”), which has no root letter other than “ʻal.”
Joel.translator_note: Printed “Daniel 2”; the verse is Daniel 2:25.

Joel.english_translation: Send swords — those who go on My mission to destroy the enemies of HaShem.
That is, their time has arrived; and the matter is likened to a harvest that is reaped with sickles when its ripening is complete.

Of grapes; come and tread them — that is, the measure of their iniquity has been filled. “Redu” is an expression of subduing (kevishah), and “redui” is like “and have dominion over the fish of the sea” (Genesis 1:28).
Joel.translator_note: The printed ורדוי is left as printed (probably a variant of ורדו).

Joel.english_translation: The sound of the stream of the vats, descending into the pit that is before the winepresses, is heard.
For there it is decided (charuts), since the judgment is true. And so Jonathan translated: “the plain of the division of judgment.”
They drew in their light.

Joel.english_lemma_JPS: the LORD shall roar from Zion
Joel.english_translation: Because of what they did to Zion.

Joel.english_lemma_JPS: the heavens and the earth shall shake
Joel.english_translation: He will exact punishment from the princes above (the princes of the Chaldeans), and afterward from (the Chaldeans).
Joel.translator_note: The parentheses are in the printed text.

Joel.english_translation: An expression of covering, and in French, “abriayil.”
Joel.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters (אבריאיי"ל). Darmesteter lists it at Joel 4:16 for מחסה with the gloss “shelter” (abri) and the form אבריאיר, ending in resh; the printed form ends in lamed.

Joel.english_translation: The place from which water emerges.

Joel.english_lemma_JPS: And shall water the valley of Shittim
Joel.english_translation: According to its plain sense; and Jonathan: “and shall water the plain of Shittim.” And its midrash: it will atone for the sin of Peor (see Zechariah 14).
Joel.translator_note: The reference “(see Zechariah 14)” is in parentheses in the printed text.

Joel.english_translation: He joined them to each other for punishment. You find that without Egypt there would have been no Edom, as it is said (1 Kings 1): “for six months Joab remained there until he had cut off every male in Edom,” and it is written (ibid. 1): “Hadad fled, he and Edomite men,” “and Hadad found favor in the eyes of Pharaoh,” etc., “and Hadad heard that David slept with his fathers,” etc., and in the end, “he was an adversary to Solomon.” The Holy One, blessed be He, said: I will consume this one and that one.
Joel.translator_note: Printed “1 Kings 1” and “ibid. 1”; the verses are 1 Kings 11:16–25. Rashi’s quotations are abbreviated and differ slightly from the verses, and his wording is translated. The printed “כל זר באדום” reads “every stranger”; the verse has “every male” (זכר), and the translation follows the verse.

Joel.english_lemma_JPS: For the violence against the children of Judah
Joel.english_translation: Because of the violence that the idolaters did to the children of Judah, whose blood they shed.

Joel.english_lemma_JPS: I will hold as innocent their blood that I have not held as innocent
Joel.english_translation: And even if I acquit them of the other sins that are in their hands and of the evils they did to Me, I will not acquit them of the blood of the children of Judah. When will this be? At the time when the Holy One, blessed be He, dwells in Zion.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: who was among the herdmen of Tekoa
Amos.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “who was a master of flocks,” like “Now Mesha king of Moab was a sheep-master” (2 Kings 3:4).
Amos.translator_note: The Aramaic word גיתין is rendered as “flocks.” The Aramaic is translated as printed.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: two years before the earthquake
Amos.english_translation: Two years before Uzziah was smitten, the day that Isaiah prophesied, as it is said, “And the posts of the door were moved” (Isaiah 6:4), and it says, “like as you fled from before the earthquake…” (Zechariah 14:5).

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: The LORD roareth from Zion
Amos.english_translation: From the Holy of Holies the speech goes forth.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: and the pastures of the shepherds shall mourn
Amos.english_translation: And the dwellings of the kings will be laid waste, and the stronghold of their cities will be destroyed.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: For three transgressions of Damascus
Amos.english_translation: As it is written, “Lo, all these things doth God work, twice, yea thrice, with a man” (Job 33:29), and if more, more; and here it is so: I have already dealt with them according to My attribute, to forgo for them three times; and if there are more, all the more so, for the few is included in the many.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: I will not reverse it
Amos.english_translation: For the fourth transgression, I no longer have to turn him back empty, from repaying him recompense, and all the more so since he has many transgressions now. This one I will visit upon them: that they threshed the inhabitants of Gilead, who are adjacent to them.
Amos.translator_note: The phrase להשיבו ריקם מלהשיב לו גמול is terse; translated literally.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: sledges of iron
Amos.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “with a moriga of iron.” And it is like a “shofina” that they call “lima,” which is made with notches, notches; and with them they subdue people with torments, and with them they cut the hard stalks of grain to make straw.
Amos.translator_note: The Old French is printed in Hebrew letters. Darmesteter lists לימ"א at Amos 1:3 (gloss “with saws”; he reads it as lime). The word שופינ"א could not be found in Darmesteter and is left as printed. The Aramaic is translated as printed.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Hazael
Amos.english_translation: And Ben-hadad — kings of Aram; and the head of Aram is Damascus.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Bikath-Aven
Amos.english_translation: It is a place in Aram.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: him that holdeth the sceptre
Amos.english_translation: “And making a ruler,” like “The sceptre shall not depart” (Genesis 49:10), because the ruler drives the people with staves.
Amos.translator_note: The verb “rodeh” can mean “rules” or “drives/strikes”; it is rendered “drives” here. The Aramaic is translated as printed.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Beth-eden
Amos.english_translation: A place.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: unto Kir
Amos.english_translation: A place, and there Sennacherib exiled them in the days of Ahaz, as it is said, “went up against Damascus and took it, and exiled Aram to Kir” (2 Kings 16:9). All the punishments that the prophets of Israel prophesied would come by the sword upon the idolaters: the prophets who were before Sennacherib, such as Isaiah and Amos, prophesied about the sword of Sennacherib, and Jeremiah and Ezekiel prophesied about the sword of Nebuchadnezzar.
Amos.translator_note: Rashi’s wording of 2 Kings 16:9 differs from the verse (“carried the people of it captive to Kir”); his wording is translated.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Gaza
Amos.english_translation: It was of the Philistines.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: a whole captivity
Amos.english_translation: The captivity of Israel, so that the captivity would be complete, that no one would escape, for they stood on the roads and seized the fugitives and delivered them up; and the men of Tyre did likewise; and likewise to the four directions at the destruction of the Second Temple, as is explained in Aggadat Ha’azinu: Gaza from the south, Tyre from the north, Damascus from the east, the Arabians from the west, as it is said (Isaiah 21:13), “The burden upon Arabia. In the thickets in Arabia shall you lodge.”

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Ashdod
Amos.english_translation: Ashkelon, Ekron — they are the lords of the Philistines.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: I will turn My hand
Amos.english_translation: I will smite, and I will repeat.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: remembered not the brotherly covenant
Amos.english_translation: That was between Hiram and Solomon, as it is said, “and they two made a league together” (1 Kings 5); and they used to call one another “brother,” as it is said (ibid. 9), “What cities are these which thou hast given me, my brother?”
Amos.translator_note: Printed “1 Kings 5” and “ibid. 9”; the verses are 1 Kings 5:26 and 9:13.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: because he did pursue his brother with the sword
Amos.english_translation: As it is said (Numbers 20), “lest I come out with the sword against thee.” And still now he tears with his anger and keeps his wrath, and has not retracted.
Amos.translator_note: Printed “Numbers 20”; the verse is Numbers 20:18.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: his anger did tear perpetually
Amos.english_translation: He held on to it and did not leave it.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: the palaces of Bozrah
Amos.english_translation: It is between Moab and Edom; it is from the land of Moab and was drawn after Edom; and it set up a king for him after the death of the first king, as it is said, “Jobab the son of Zerah of Bozrah” (Genesis 37 [sic]).
Amos.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 37”; the verse is Genesis 36:33.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: because they have ripped up the women with child of Gilead
Amos.english_translation: They destroyed it and also ripped up their pregnant women, so that no heir would remain to contest the inheritance. And so it says (Jeremiah 49:1), “Of the children of Ammon. Thus saith the LORD: Hath Israel no sons? Hath he no heir? Why then doth Malcam take possession…”

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: burned the bones of the king of Edom into lime
Amos.english_translation: Once the king of Edom fell into the hand of the king of Moab, and he burned his bones and plastered them on the walls of the house; and the Holy One, blessed be He, demanded redress for the wrong done to the king, in that they treated him with contempt.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: the palaces of Kerioth
Amos.english_translation: The name of a place, as it is said (ibid. 48), “and upon Kerioth, and upon Bozrah.”
Amos.translator_note: Printed “ibid. 48”; the verse is Jeremiah 48:24.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: with tumult
Amos.english_translation: The sound of the multitude of war.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: sell the righteous for silver
Amos.english_translation: The judges would sell one who was innocent in judgment for the bribe money that they received from the hand of his opponent.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: And the needy for a pair of shoes
Amos.english_translation: Jonathan translated in two places (below 8:6), “in order that they may possess.” And I say that this is its meaning: they pervert the justice of the needy so that he must sell his field that lay among the fields of the judges, and this one surrounds him and takes it for a small price, in order to fence in and enclose all his fields together, so that there is no break between them.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: That pant after the dust of the earth on the head of the poor
Amos.english_translation: Upon the dust of the earth on which they walk is all their longing and all their thought; it is at the head of the poor — how they may rob them and take what is theirs. “She’ifah” (longing) is “goloshir” in French.
Amos.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters (גולושי"ר). Darmesteter lists it at Amos 2:7 for השואפים with the gloss “aspire (to bring down into the dust)”, derived from Latin gulosus, with the forms גולושיר; the printed spelling matches.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: And turn aside the way of the humble
Amos.english_translation: The weak turn aside from their way and go by a roundabout road because of their fear, as you say (Job 24:4), “They turn the needy out of the way.”

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: the same maid
Amos.english_translation: The betrothed.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Upon clothes taken in pledge
Amos.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: על מטות שוויין דמשכון מסתחרין. They enter a debt against the poor and take their pledges, and make their garments into spreads and recline upon them in leaning at the time of their meal, in the house of their god — in an idolater’s house that they have beside an altar.
Amos.translator_note: The Aramaic of the Targum could not be rendered with confidence and is left as printed.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: lay themselves down
Amos.english_translation: An expression of a banquet (mesibah), for every banquet meal is in leaning, for he leans on his left.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: The wine of them that have been fined
Amos.english_translation: That they fine them money, and drink wine with it.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: strong as the oaks
Amos.english_translation: In French, “qeyshnesh.”
Amos.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters (קיישנ"ש). Darmesteter lists it at Amos 2:9 with the gloss “like oaks” (chênes) and the forms קישנש / קיישנש; the printed spelling matches.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: I destroyed his fruit from above
Amos.english_translation: The upper princes.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: And his roots from beneath
Amos.english_translation: The lower princes. Another explanation: the hornet used to blind their eyes from above and to castrate them from below.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: for Nazirites
Amos.english_translation: Jonathan translated, “for teachers,” for they were separated from the ways of the people of the land and engaged in Torah. “Nezirah” everywhere is only an expression of separation.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Is it not even thus, O you children of Israel
Amos.english_translation: As a question of astonishment; that is, can you deny this?

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: But you gave the Nazirites wine to drink
Amos.english_translation: So that they would not instruct you, for a drunkard is forbidden to instruct. “But you gave the Nazirites wine to drink” — Jonathan translated: “and you led your teachers astray with wine.”

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Prophesy not
Amos.english_translation: Amaziah, priest of Beth-el, so commanded Amos: “O thou seer, go, flee thee away into the land of Judah” (below, 7).
Amos.translator_note: Printed “below 7”; the verse is Amos 7:12.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: I will make it creak
Amos.english_translation: The Aramaic translation of “metzik.”

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: under you
Amos.english_translation: Your encampment.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: As a cart creaketh that is full of sheaves
Amos.english_translation: Because of the heaviness of the load that is upon it.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: he that is swift of foot shall not deliver himself
Amos.english_translation: His soul.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Shall flee away naked in that day
Amos.english_translation: “Artilai” — without weapons.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: You only have I known of all the families of the earth
Amos.english_translation: I loved, and you transgressed against Me; therefore, etc. And our Rabbis expounded it in another direction in tractate Avodah Zarah.
Amos.translator_note: The printed tractate name is עכו"ם.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Will two walk together
Amos.english_translation: For you say to the prophets, “Prophesy not.” Do the prophets prophesy from their own heart, unless they were commanded? Are things done except according to their way?
Amos.translator_note: The last clause (כלום דברים נעשים אלא על פי דרכם) is terse; translated literally.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Except they have agreed
Amos.english_translation: Unless they fixed a time to walk together to such-and-such a place.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Will a lion roar in the forest
Amos.english_translation: When a lion holds prey, it is its way to roar, and it does not roar unless it has caught; and so it says (Isaiah 5), “They shall roar like young lions, yea, they shall roar, And lay hold of the prey,” and likewise (ibid. 31), “Like as the lion, or the young lion, growling over his prey.”
Amos.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 5” and “ibid. 31”; the verses are Isaiah 5:29 and 31:4.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Will a bird fall in a snare upon the earth
Amos.english_translation: Into the snare on which it fell, and it has no lure?
Amos.translator_note: The comment is terse; translated literally.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Will a snare spring up from the ground
Amos.english_translation: From the place where it was laid there — unless a bird is caught in it; when it wants to flee, it uproots the snare and lifts it a little from its place, and at that moment it has already been caught.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Shall the horn be blown in a city
Amos.english_translation: For the lookout sees troops coming into the city and blows the horn to warn the people; these are only words of a parable and an analogy.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Shall evil befall a city
Amos.english_translation: It is Nebuchadnezzar. Another explanation: The prophets liken the Holy Spirit that comes upon them to the roar of a lion, as they say below, “The lion hath roared, Who will not fear?” And here this is the explanation of the analogy: Does the Holy Spirit come into the mouths of the prophets to speak a word of evil from the Holy One, blessed be He, unless the punishment has been decreed before Him? That is the prey. Would the Holy One, blessed be He, give His voice to speak harshly unless He had caught you in the snare of iniquity? “Will a bird fall in a snare” — and the snare does not make it stumble; that is, is it possible that you commit transgressions and they will not be a snare to you? “Will a snare spring up…” — thus will your iniquities rise upward and not catch you? “Shall the horn be blown in a city” — thus you should have trembled at the words of the prophets, who are looking out for you to rescue you from the evil, that it not come; and when the evil comes upon you, will you not know that the Holy One, blessed be He, is doing it to you because you were not careful with His prophets?
Amos.translator_note: Rashi’s lemma, “Will a lion roar,” belongs to verse 4; this long comment gathers verses 4–6 and quotes its own lemmas within the text, so a nearby phrase of this verse is used as the lemma. The sentences “and the snare does not make it stumble” and “It is Nebuchadnezzar” are terse and translated literally.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: He revealeth His counsel unto His servants the prophets
Amos.english_translation: [He has revealed] that secret to His servants the prophets.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: The lion hath roared, Who will not fear
Amos.english_translation: So the Holy One, blessed be He, spoke to the prophets to prophesy; who will not prophesy?

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Proclaim it
Amos.english_translation: You sons of the Philistines and sons of Egypt: and proclaim this, and say in your palaces that they assemble upon the mountains of Samaria, to see from above the mountains, in the midst of the city, their evil way.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: to do right
Amos.english_translation: Straight.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: violence and robbery
Amos.english_translation: Money of robbery.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: An adversary, even round about the land
Amos.english_translation: The adversary is ready to come, and he will come round about this land.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: As the shepherd rescueth
Amos.english_translation: A small thing.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: a piece of an ear
Amos.english_translation: “Chaschos” of the ear.
Amos.translator_note: The Aramaic word חסחוס is left transliterated. The Aramaic is translated as printed.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: So shall the children of Israel
Amos.english_translation: A few people.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: the corner of a couch
Amos.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “in the strength of the ruler, and in reliance upon Damascus.” And I say that the explanation of the Targum is because in the days of Jehoahaz son of Jehu it is written (2 Kings 13:7), “for the king of Aram destroyed them,” and Jeroboam, his grandson, saved them in part, as it is said (ibid. 14), “And the LORD said not that He would blot out the name of Israel from under heaven; but He saved them by the hand of Jeroboam…” (ibid.), “He restored the border of Israel.” And this is “with the corner of a couch”: the corner of the house is the strength of the house; therefore it translated, “in the strength of the ruler,” of Jeroboam. And Amos prophesied in the days of Jeroboam, and he prophesied further that in the end they would lean upon the kings of Aram; and so they did in the days of Pekah son of Remaliah, who allied himself with Rezin. And this is “and in Damascus a bed”: the main place of their rest and their trust will be upon Damascus. And our Rabbis said in Seder Olam: Rabbi Nehorai says in the name of Rabbi Joshua: These are the ten tribes who leaned upon Hezekiah king of Judah and upon Judah, and escaped with them.
Amos.translator_note: Printed “2 Kings 13:7” is correct; “ibid. 14” and “ibid.” are 2 Kings 14:27 and 14:25. Rashi reads “ובדמשק ערש” as “and in Damascus a bed”; JPS renders the phrase “and the leg of a bed.”

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: and the leg of a bed
Amos.english_translation: This teaches that only one of eight of them remained, and the rest of the bed — where is it? In Damascus, to fulfil what is said (below 5), “Therefore will I cause you to go into captivity beyond Damascus.” And I heard in the name of Rabbi Menachem, of blessed memory, that he explained this as one of eight, for it does not say “pe’ah” but “bi-fe’at mittah” — in a part of it, in one of the two directions of the pe’ah; and it is an eighth of the bed, for there are four corners, and two directions to a corner. Another explanation: I found in the words of Rabbi Meir, of blessed memory: “bi-fe’at mittah” — for the sin of Ahaziah son of Ahab, who sent to inquire of Baal-zebub the god of Ekron, “whether I shall recover of this sickness” (2 Kings 1:2); “and in Damascus a bed” — Ben-hadad king of Aram, who sent to inquire of the God of Israel (ibid. 8).
Amos.translator_note: Printed “below 5” is Amos 5:27; “ibid. 8” is 2 Kings 8:8. Rashi reads “ובדמשק ערש” as “and in Damascus a bed”; JPS renders the phrase “and the leg of a bed.”

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: the winter-house with the summer-house
Amos.english_translation: Since they were living in luxury, the wealthy built for themselves two houses, one for the winter and one for the summer.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: houses of ivory
Amos.english_translation: [Houses] that are overlaid with the ivory of the elephant.
Amos.translator_note: The Aramaic מכבשין (literally “pressed”) is rendered “overlaid.” The Aramaic is translated as printed.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: kine of Bashan
Amos.english_translation: The wives of the princes and the governors; and Targum Jonathan: “the rich in possessions.”

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: That you shall be taken away with hooks
Amos.english_translation: And the nations will carry you upon their shields.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: And your residue with fish-hooks
Amos.english_translation: Targum: “and your daughters in a fisherman’s boat.” It is a small ship of fish-hunters, and because it is small he calls it “sir” (pot), and he calls it in the language of the Mishnah “dugit” in Bava Batra. “Your residue” (acharitkhen): Dunash ben Labrat explained: we find a man’s seed called his “acharit,” like “And when he shall stand up, his kingdom shall be broken, and shall be divided toward the four winds of heaven; but not to his posterity” (Daniel 11:4) — that is, he will not leave his kingdom to his son.
Amos.translator_note: The printed בב"ב is read as Bava Batra.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: And you shall go out at the breaches
Amos.english_translation: And through the breaches of the wall you shall go out there to flee.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: every one straight before her
Amos.english_translation: Through the breach that she finds before her, like “and the people went up into the city, every man straight before him” (Joshua 6); there will be many breaches in the wall, and they will not need to seek gates.
Amos.translator_note: Printed “Joshua 6”; the verse is Joshua 6:20.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: And you shall be cast into Harmon
Amos.english_translation: And you shall cast away from yourselves the pride and the dominion that you took. And it is an Aramaic expression: in the Gemara (Bava Metzia, chapter 3) “harmana de-malka” is the king’s command. And Targum Jonathan: “and they shall exile you beyond the mountains of Harmini,” and they are the mountains of darkness, an expression of sword and desolation.
Amos.translator_note: The words “mountains of darkness, an expression of sword and desolation” (הרי חשך ל' חרב וחרבה) are unclear as printed and are translated literally. The tractate reference is as printed. The Aramaic is translated as printed.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Come to Beth-el, and transgress
Amos.english_translation: Like a person who says to a scoundrel: Do, do, until your measure is filled.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: And bring your sacrifices in the morning
Amos.english_translation: (4–5) “And bring your sacrifices in the morning.” This the priests of Baal say to them: Idolatry is lenient and is not strict with you. The Torah said (Exodus 23) “shall not remain overnight until the morning,” but idolatry: “and bring in the morning.” The Torah said of lesser holy things “It shall be eaten the same day you offer it, and on the morrow” (Leviticus 19:6), but idolatry: “after three days your animal tithes.” The Torah said, “you shall not burn leaven” (ibid. 2), but idolatry: “and offer a sacrifice of thanksgiving of that which is leavened.” The Torah said, “thou shalt not be slack to pay it” (Deuteronomy 23:22), but idolatry: “and proclaim freewill-offerings” — “publish,” mention, whoever vowed and forgot shall set it to heart and remember. And Targum Jonathan: “and offer … of leaven” — from compulsion, like “relieve the oppressed” (Isaiah 1) and “Out of the grasp of the unrighteous and ruthless man” (Psalms 71:4).
Amos.translator_note: The source gives no lemma, and the lemma used is the first phrase quoted in the comment. Printed “Exodus 23” is Exodus 23:18; Rashi’s wording is abbreviated. The printed “ibid. 2” is Leviticus 2:11 (JPS: “you shall make no leaven, nor any honey, smoke as an offering”); Rashi’s wording is translated. The Targum phrase is translated as printed.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: And proclaim freewill-offerings and publish them
Amos.english_translation: With a voice of song, and they say that this sacrifice is desired and accepted as a freewill-offering; so Targum Jonathan.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Cleanness of teeth
Amos.english_translation: Bluntness of teeth. Another explanation: “cleanness of teeth” is the lack of eating meat, which gets in between the teeth, as it is said, “While the flesh was yet between their teeth” (Numbers 11).
Amos.translator_note: Printed “Numbers 11”; the verse is Numbers 11:33.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: When there were yet three months to the harvest
Amos.english_translation: “Until the harvest” — that is, three months before the harvest.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: One piece was rained upon
Amos.english_translation: A plain of a field: *campagne* in French.
Amos.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this word (Amos 4:7) with the gloss “a plain” and reads it as *campayne*; the printed form (קמפנייא) is a close variant.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: was rained upon
Amos.english_translation: It will be a place of rain (Ta’anit 20). The master said: Both are for a curse — this one rots and this one dries up.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: And the piece whereupon it rained not withered
Amos.english_translation: It will not see itself rained upon.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: The multitude of your gardens
Amos.english_translation: That you are engaged in multiplying your gardens.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Hath the palmer-worm devoured
Amos.english_translation: The gazam ate.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: in the way of Egypt
Amos.english_translation: As I sent upon you in the wilderness when you came out of Egypt.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: And have carried away your horses
Amos.english_translation: That the horses too would be slain.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: the stench of your camp to come up
Amos.english_translation: The smell of your corpses, which sickens your nose, I brought up.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: a brand plucked out of the burning
Amos.english_translation: *Tison* in French — that is, black and dark and gloomy.
Amos.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this word (Amos 4:11) with the gloss “like a brand” (tison) and the forms טישון / טיזון; the printed form (טיסו"ן) is spelled with a samekh.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Therefore thus will I do unto thee
Amos.english_translation: Because you did not return to Me.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: thus will I do unto thee
Amos.english_translation: Like all these evils.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Because I will do this unto thee
Amos.english_translation: For you hear from the mouth of My prophet that I will do this to you.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Prepare to meet thy God
Amos.english_translation: To return from your wickedness.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: And declareth unto man what is his thought
Amos.english_translation: All his deeds are itemized before him at the time of his death.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: That maketh the morning darkness
Amos.english_translation: For the righteous, like shining light.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: morning darkness
Amos.english_translation: “Ephah” — He turns the brightness of the wicked into dark gloom, like “behold distress and darkness, the gloom of anguish” (Isaiah 8:22), and likewise “A land of thick darkness” (Job 10:22); “Though there be darkness, it shall be as the morning” (ibid. 11) — your darkness shall be like a shining morning.
Amos.translator_note: Printed “ibid. 11” is Job 11:17.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: And treadeth upon the high places of the earth
Amos.english_translation: He humbles the lofty and the proud.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: The virgin of Israel is fallen
Amos.english_translation: Once they are exiled, in the days of Hoshea son of Elah (2 Kings 16), no king of the ten tribes will arise any more.
Amos.translator_note: Printed “2 Kings 16”; Hoshea son of Elah appears at 2 Kings 15:30 and 17:1.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: She is cast down upon her land
Amos.english_translation: Anything that is thrown and left lying and scattered on the field he calls “netishah.”

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: The city that went forth a thousand
Amos.english_translation: The one that sends out a thousand men.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Seek you Me, and live
Amos.english_translation: Go up on the pilgrimage to pay your vows in Jerusalem.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: And pass not to Beer-sheba
Amos.english_translation: It does not say here “do not come” and “do not seek,” but “do not pass over”; we learn that there was no idolatry there. Rather, as long as one of the ten tribes went out to seek and had not passed Beer-sheba, he could still turn to the Temple in Jerusalem, but once he passed Beer-sheba, that was the way to the calf at Beth-el or the calf at Dan; and so it is in another place (below, 8): “As thy God, O Dan, liveth,” etc. And know that the Writ decreed a decree of punishment upon Gilgal and Beth-el, but did not decree upon Beer-sheba.
Amos.translator_note: Printed “below 8” is Amos 8:14.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: For Gilgal shall surely go into captivity
Amos.english_translation: According to its name is its curse (Gilgal galoh yigleh). And so Beth-el: there is a city adjacent to it whose name is Beth-aven, in the book of Judges 7.
Amos.translator_note: Printed “Judges 7”; Beth-aven beside Beth-el is mentioned in Joshua 7:2, not in Judges 7.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: And Beth-el shall come to nought
Amos.english_translation: “They shall be for nothing” — which is the Aramaic translation of “hevel” (vanity); and this is like “If Gilead be given to iniquity Becoming altogether vanity” (Hosea 12).

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Lest He break out like fire
Amos.english_translation: Lest His anger burn like fire.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: in the house of Joseph
Amos.english_translation: Like “against the house of Joseph.” “Lest He break out like fire” — lest His wrath go up like fire against the house of Joseph.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: You who turn judgment to wormwood
Amos.english_translation: And they do not remember My overturnings, that I overturn, etc.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: And bringeth on the shadow of death in the morning
Amos.english_translation: There are those who are now sunk in darkness, and I give them light.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: And darkeneth the day into night
Amos.english_translation: And there are those whose hour stands for them like the light of day, and I darken it into night.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: That calleth for the waters of the sea
Amos.english_translation: Jonathan translated: “who says to gather many hosts like the waters of the sea and scatters them over the face of the earth.” Our Rabbis explained it of the generation of Enosh, that He flooded them with the waters of the ocean.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: The LORD is His name
Amos.english_translation: You should have served Him, and He would have made you prevail over your haters.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: That causeth destruction to flash upon the strong
Amos.english_translation: He who makes strong, like “that I may take comfort a little” (Job 10:20), “Though I would take comfort against sorrow” (Jeremiah 8:18).
Amos.translator_note: Rashi takes the root as “making strong”; JPS renders these two verses “take comfort.”

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: So that destruction cometh upon the fortress
Amos.english_translation: A man who is plundered and weak; (Targum:) who makes the weak prevail over the strong, and makes plunderers rule over strong cities.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: They hate him that reproveth in the gate
Amos.english_translation: You did not fear Him or His prophets, and you hated those who reprove you in the gates of the courts.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: you trample upon the poor
Amos.english_translation: Like “bosesakhem”: that you trample and tread upon his head, as “They have trodden My portion under foot” (ibid. 12).
Amos.translator_note: Printed “ibid. 12” is Jeremiah 12:10 (the previous reference in the source is Jeremiah 8:18).

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: exactions of wheat
Amos.english_translation: Charging of a loan: that you raised the prices against them to sell them grain at interest, in order to take their inheritance from them; therefore the houses and vineyards that you built and planted on those inheritances will not stand in your hands. And “mas’at” is an expression of a burden, that they weigh upon them.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: pleasant vineyards
Amos.english_translation: Vineyards of desirability.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: You that afflict the just
Amos.english_translation: They oppress the righteous.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: And that turn aside the needy in the gate
Amos.english_translation: In the gates of your courts you perverted the justice of the needy.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Therefore the prudent doth keep silence in such a time
Amos.english_translation: One who is wise will be silent when the evil comes and will not question the attribute of justice, for all these they did.
Amos.translator_note: The printed מה"ד is read as מדת הדין (the attribute of justice).

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: it is an evil time
Amos.english_translation: A time set aside to receive their evil.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: will be with you, as you say
Amos.english_translation: If you do this, then the Omnipresent will be with you, as you said in your hearts, that your greatness will endure for you.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: the remnant of Joseph
Amos.english_translation: All Israel are called by his name because he sustained them.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Alas! alas!
Amos.english_translation: An expression of crying out.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: And they shall call the husbandman to mourning
Amos.english_translation: The caravans of husbandmen who plow in the fields will meet the sound of the lamentation of the mourners who cry out in the streets.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: lamentation to such as are skilful of wailing
Amos.english_translation: Targum: “and the one who makes lamentation ye’are among those who make wailing (aliya).” It is only a doubled expression, like “my right and my cause” (Psalms 9).
Amos.translator_note: The Aramaic word יערע is unclear and is left transliterated. The Aramaic is translated as printed.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Woe unto you that desire the day of the LORD
Amos.english_translation: Those who say, “Let Him make speed, let Him hasten His work” (Isaiah 5:19).

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Wherefore would you have the day of the LORD
Amos.english_translation: A parable of a rooster and a bat that were waiting for the light, as is found in “Chelek.”
Amos.translator_note: “Chelek” is printed without further identification.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: And I will take no delight in your solemn assemblies
Amos.english_translation: The offering of your assembly, when you call an “atzeret.”

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: the peace-offerings of your fat beasts
Amos.english_translation: And the peace-offerings of your fatlings — fattened animals.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Take thou away from Me the noise of thy songs
Amos.english_translation: That the Levites sing upon the platform, seeing that you are violent men and perverters of justice.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: But let justice well up as waters
Amos.english_translation: And do this, and I will accept you: let the justice that you suppressed and hid be revealed and flow among you like gushing waters.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: And righteousness as a mighty stream
Amos.english_translation: It will be revealed like a mighty stream.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Did you bring unto Me sacrifices and offerings
Amos.english_translation: Is it sacrifices and meal-offerings that I desire? Did I not in the wilderness speak with your fathers to offer Me sacrifices? I said, “When any man of you bringeth an offering” (Leviticus 1:2) — when he wishes to offer; and it says, “Let the children of Israel keep the passover in its appointed season” (Numbers 9) — this tells that Israel did not do so in the wilderness except for that one Passover alone.
Amos.translator_note: Printed “Numbers 9”; the verse is Numbers 9:2.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Siccuth your king
Amos.english_translation: He returns to the matter of the punishment above: “darkness for them is the day of HaShem, and not light”; and you will carry into exile with you your idols, and the enemies will mount them on your necks to carry with you into exile.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Siccuth your king and Chiun your images, the star of your god
Amos.english_translation: They are names of idols.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Therefore will I cause you to go into captivity beyond Damascus
Amos.english_translation: That is, you will not be exiled to your neighbors, as until now when you were delivered into the hand of the kings of Aram, who did not carry you off to a distant place but only to Damascus; but from now I will deliver you into the hand of Sennacherib, and he will exile you far away.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: The notable men of the first of the nations
Amos.english_translation: They used to call you the choicest nation among the idolaters.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: To whom the house of Israel come
Amos.english_translation: They chose their laws and came into their company.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Pass you unto Calneh, and see
Amos.english_translation: Why have you despised My Torah, to cling to the statutes of the idolaters? Pass over and see among the prominent idolaters whether they are better than these kingdoms that are in Samaria and in Jerusalem.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Calneh
Amos.english_translation: Babylon.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Hamath the great
Amos.english_translation: Antioch.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Gath of the Philistines
Amos.english_translation: The most important of their five lords, for it is called “Metheg-ammah” (2 Samuel 8:1) because it rules over them all, and it is the mother of the kingdom.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Or is their border greater than your border
Amos.english_translation: And what injustice did you find in Me?

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: put far away the evil day
Amos.english_translation: You put yourselves far away for the evil day.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: cause the seat of violence to come near
Amos.english_translation: You bring yourselves near to dwelling in exile, which will deal violently with you, as it is said of it, “For the violence done to thy brother Jacob” (Obadiah 1). This is the midrash of Rabbi Shimshon of blessed memory. Another explanation: “that put far away the evil day” — who scorn the prophecy of evil days that the prophets prophesy to them. “And cause the seat of violence to come near” — this is like what Isaiah said: “Woe unto them that join house to house” (Isaiah 5:8); you bring near a seat among them, one beside the other, through violence.
Amos.translator_note: Printed “Obadiah 1”; the verse is Obadiah 1:10.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: stretch themselves upon their couches
Amos.english_translation: They lie flat and stretch themselves out upon their couches. But our Rabbis explained: they exchange their wives with one another and make their couches stink with semen that is not theirs.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: lambs
Amos.english_translation: Lambs.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: the midst of the stall
Amos.english_translation: A place where the calves are gathered; and in French, *קופל"א*.
Amos.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Amos 6:4, glossed as an enclosure (“parc”) where the bulls are gathered, with the form קופלא; the printed spelling (קופל"א) matches it.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: That thrum on the psaltery
Amos.english_translation: Menachem connected it with “the fallen fruit (peret) of thy vineyard” (Leviticus 19:10), and I see that his words are right, for the singer, to the sound of the musical instrument, cuts up the speech into small bits (perutrot), all according to the pleasantness of the sound of the instrument, to raise and to lower.
Amos.translator_note: Printed “Leviticus 9”; the verse is Leviticus 19:10.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: devise for themselves instruments of music, like David
Amos.english_translation: They considered their instruments of song like the instruments of song of David — that his are for Heaven, and these are for pleasure.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: That drink wine in bowls
Amos.english_translation: There are some of our Rabbis who say, in tractate Shabbat, that they would throw their cups to one another. And some explain it on account of a vessel that had two mouths and was long, and this one drinks from here and that one from there; it is thrown from his mouth to his mouth.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: the chief ointments
Amos.english_translation: The choicest of oils, and it is afarsemon (balsam).

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: they are not grieved
Amos.english_translation: An expression of sickness.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: the hurt of Joseph
Amos.english_translation: For they heard from the mouth of the prophets that it was destined to come upon them.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: the revelry of them that stretched themselves shall pass away
Amos.english_translation: And the banquets of the proud and the haughty of spirit will be abolished. *Marzeach* is an expression of banquets. In the Sifrei, in the portion “And Israel abode in Shittim” (Numbers 25:1), I found: and they went back and made banquets (*marzechim*) for themselves, and they would call to them and eat.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: hath sworn by Himself
Amos.english_translation: With knowledge and intention.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: I abhor the pride of Jacob
Amos.english_translation: Like מתעב (“abominate”); and so Targum Jonathan translated: “I am disgracing the Temple, the greatness of Jacob,” for the Temple is called “the pride of their strength,” as it is said, “Behold, I will profane My sanctuary, the pride of your power” (Ezekiel 24).
Amos.translator_note: Printed “Ezekiel 24”; the verse is Ezekiel 24:21.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: the city with all that is therein
Amos.english_translation: Jerusalem and its inhabitants.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: if there remain ten men in one house
Amos.english_translation: If they are left over from the pestilence and the sword in one house, they shall die. For the enemies will burn the house upon them when they capture the city.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: a man’s uncle shall take him up, even he that burneth him
Amos.english_translation: His relative and his friend, who saves his bones from the burning. So Targum Jonathan: “and his relative will lift him from the burning.”

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: shall say unto him that is in the innermost parts of the house
Amos.english_translation: The one who brings out from the burning says to “him that is in the innermost parts of the house” — to his fellow who went to search inside the house.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Is there yet any with thee?
Amos.english_translation: A living person besides you who escaped from the hiding places.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: he shall say: ‘No’
Amos.english_translation: There is no one alive, only the dead. And this one said to him, “Hes” the corpses — “hes” means throw and clear away everything — for this has come upon them because they did not wish to mention the name of HaShem. So Targum Jonathan.
Amos.translator_note: Rashi explains “hes” as “throw away” rather than “be silent,” so the JPS wording “Hold thy peace” is not used.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: into splinters
Amos.english_translation: That it will be shattered into fine fissures.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: into chips
Amos.english_translation: Larger than splinters; according to its importance, so will its blow be. So Targum Jonathan: “and He will strike the great kingdom with a strong blow, and the small kingdom with a weak blow.”

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Do horses run upon the rocks?
Amos.english_translation: Will they endure in their running if they change the order of the world?

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Doth one plow there with oxen?
Amos.english_translation: A man with oxen on the rock? — for you think to change the good way and still endure and prosper.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: a thing of nought
Amos.english_translation: Over their greatness and their wealth, which is nothing, which will not endure.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: horns
Amos.english_translation: Strength and might to gore the poor and the needy with horns.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: from the entrance of Hamath
Amos.english_translation: Which is in the northwest corner of the Land of Israel.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: unto the Brook of the Arabah
Amos.english_translation: The Brook of Egypt, which is in the southwest corner.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Thus the Lord GOD showed me
Amos.english_translation: The punishment that He wished to bring: locusts.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: in the beginning of the shooting up of the latter growth
Amos.english_translation: An expression of *malkosh* (the late rain): when the grain rises up on its stalk.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: the latter growth after the king’s mowings
Amos.english_translation: It was sprouting after the king’s shearings: after they had cut the king’s grain, before it had risen up on its stalk they would cut it as fodder, to feed to the animals. And so Targum Jonathan: “for the king’s fodder was shorn.” And in the language of the Mishnah it means to reap for fodder and to feed the animal.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: when they had made an end of eating
Amos.english_translation: When it had finished eating.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: the grass of the land
Amos.english_translation: In that field.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: O Lord GOD, forgive, I beseech Thee
Amos.english_translation: And do not destroy the land.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: How shall Jacob stand?
Amos.english_translation: Who will arise and entreat concerning their sins?

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: for he is small
Amos.english_translation: Targum: “for they are being moved about.”
Amos.translator_note: The Aramaic is translated as printed; the exact sense of מטלטלין here (“moved about” or “driven away”) is not certain.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: The LORD repented concerning this
Amos.english_translation: He was appeased by his prayer and yielded to me.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Thus the Lord GOD showed me
Amos.english_translation: Another punishment to bring upon you.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: the Lord GOD called to contend by fire
Amos.english_translation: His retinue (*pamalya*) to contend with you with the punishment of a burning fire.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: eaten up the land
Amos.english_translation: The plot (*chelkat*) of the field.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: a wall made by a plumbline
Amos.english_translation: On the wall of judgment (*shura de-dina*), and so Dunash explained. *Anach* is an Arabic expression: the thread, the line of the lead weight by which the builder of the wall looks in order to straighten the *dimos*. Here too it is an expression of the line of the weight of judgment.
Amos.translator_note: The word דימוס is left untranslated; I could not confirm its meaning here.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: I will set a plumbline
Amos.english_translation: Behold, I judge them by the line of strict justice.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: pardon them any more
Amos.english_translation: To wait for them on account of their transgressions.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: the sanctuaries of Israel
Amos.english_translation: That is Beth-el, as it is said, “for it is the king’s sanctuary.”
Amos.translator_note: The quotation is Amos 7:13.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: the house of Jeroboam
Amos.english_translation: The son of Joash.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Amaziah the priest of Beth-el
Amos.english_translation: A priest of his idolatry.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Jeroboam shall die by the sword
Amos.english_translation: But he did not say so; rather, “And I will rise against the house of Jeroboam” (Amos 7:9) — that is, his son Zechariah, whom Shallum the son of Jabesh killed (2 Kings 15).
Amos.translator_note: Printed “2 Kings 15”; the killing is told in 2 Kings 15:10.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: O thou seer
Amos.english_translation: You who prophesy things to come.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: go, flee thee away into the land of Judah
Amos.english_translation: For there is the Sanctuary of the Holy One, blessed be He, in whose name you prophesy.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: and there eat bread
Amos.english_translation: An expression of contempt. He said to him: There they will give you crumbs of bread as the wage for your prophesying to them.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: prophesy not again any more at Beth-el
Amos.english_translation: For only the name of idolatry is mentioned here.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: I was no prophet
Amos.english_translation: I am not one of your false prophets, who take their wages for prophesying. I have no need for all this, and I have not behaved so, for I am rich, an owner of livestock and property — as Targum Jonathan says: “for I am an owner of livestock, and I have sycamores in the lowland.”

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: a herdman
Amos.english_translation: A herder of cattle.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: a dresser of sycamore-trees
Amos.english_translation: One who searches among the sycamores to see which one is due to be cut, in order to add branches, and which one is fit for beams, for so is the way that they cut the “virgins” of the sycamore (*betulot ha-shikmah*). And *bolés* is like *bolésh*; but Amos stammers with his tongue, for so they said: Why was he called Amos? Because he was burdened (*amus*) in his tongue. And Israel call him *Psilos*, as it is stated in the Pesikta.
Amos.translator_note: Rashi uses the term בתולות השקמה (“virgins of the sycamore”); the printed text does not define it.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: preach not against the house of Isaac
Amos.english_translation: It is an expression of prophecy, and there are many such in Scripture: “preach toward the South” (Ezekiel 21).
Amos.translator_note: Printed “Ezekiel 21”; the verse is Ezekiel 21:2.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: a basket of summer fruit
Amos.english_translation: A basket full of the last figs (*sofei te’enim*), which are not good.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: the songs of the palace
Amos.english_translation: Who sing within their palaces, at their banquets.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: The dead bodies shall be many
Amos.english_translation: Many are the corpses of the slain.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: In every place silence shall be cast
Amos.english_translation: In every place he will say: Throw and carry away — “Throw out from here” (in another version: “Remove from here”) these corpses.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: that would swallow the needy
Amos.english_translation: Who swallow up the needy.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: destroy the poor of the land
Amos.english_translation: Like “and to destroy”; and an example is “lashmid ma’uzneha” (“to destroy the strongholds thereof,” Isaiah 23:11), “lelechet lagid be-Yizre’el” (“to go to tell it in Jezreel,” 2 Kings 9:15).

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: When will the new moon be gone
Amos.english_translation: This is the eager longing (*sha’ifah*): they wait for the time when the grain will become dear, and they will sell to the poor on interest and take their fields. “Let the month pass” — Targum Jonathan: “When will the year be intercalated and the month of intercalation come?” And it is an expression of passing over, as in “He hath let the appointed time pass by” (Jeremiah 46:17). For since they postpone the offering of the Omer, and the year is prolonged, the old grain becomes dear.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: And the sabbath, that we may set forth corn
Amos.english_translation: When will the Sabbatical year come, and the grain become dear, and we shall open our storehouses of grain?

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Making the ephah small
Amos.english_translation: To sell by a small measure, and to receive our silver by a large shekel.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: for a pair of shoes
Amos.english_translation: Targum: “in order that they may possess.”

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: sell the refuse of the corn
Amos.english_translation: Targum: “and from the מהממת of grain we shall sell” — the refuse that fell from the wheat through the sieve we shall sell dear to the poor.
Amos.translator_note: The Aramaic word מהממת could not be confirmed; it is left as printed.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Shall not the land tremble for this
Amos.english_translation: Is this iniquity not enough that the land should be laid waste because of it?

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: it shall rise up wholly like the River
Amos.english_translation: And in another place it says, “and it riseth up wholly like the River” (below, 9). And Targum Jonathan renders both alike: “and a king will go up against it with his camps, which are as many as a river, and they will cover all of it.” And it is hard in my eyes to explain *ke-or* as *ke-ye’or* (like the River); but it can be explained like “He spreadeth abroad the cloud of His lightning” (Job 37:11), “He covereth His hands with the lightning” (Job 36:32) — “and it shall rise like a cloud of rain,” all of it darkness and gloom.
Amos.translator_note: Printed “below, 9” is Amos 9:5; printed “ibid. 36” is Job 36:32. Rashi joins phrases from Job 37:11 and Job 36:32 in one quotation.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: troubled and sink again, like the River of Egypt
Amos.english_translation: The Nile rises once in forty years and waters the land, and when it rises it brings up mire and clay on its bank; and when it returns from its watering it returns within its banks and its waters become clear, and this is called “sinking” (*shikua*), for the mud that clouds its waters sinks. “And be troubled” (*nigrashah*) is like “and its waters cast up mire and dirt” (Isaiah 27). So too the land will vomit out the wicked who are in it, and afterward it will be at rest.
Amos.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 27”; the verse is Isaiah 57:20.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: I will cause the sun to go down at noon
Amos.english_translation: When they have great peace, a downfall will come suddenly. And our Rabbis said (Mo’ed Katan 25) that this is the day of Josiah, who died by a sword of peace, as our Rabbis said (Ta’anit 22): There is no sword of peace greater than Pharaoh Necho, who said to Josiah (2 Chronicles 35): “What have I to do with thee? It is not against thee that thou art this day; not against thee do I come this day, but only to pass through thy land to the house of my war,” etc.
Amos.translator_note: Printed “2 Chronicles 35” is 2 Chronicles 35:21. Rashi quotes loosely: he adds “not against thee do I come this day” and “to pass through thy land,” which are not in the verse (JPS: “I come not against thee this day, but against the house wherewith I have war”).

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: the sun to go down at noon
Amos.english_translation: The kingdom of the house of David is likened to the sun, as it is said, “And his throne as the sun before Me” (Psalms 89:37).

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: I will turn your feasts into mourning
Amos.english_translation: As it is said, “And all Judah and Jerusalem mourned for Josiah” (2 Chronicles 35).
Amos.translator_note: Printed “2 Chronicles 35”; the verse is 2 Chronicles 35:24.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: all your songs into lamentation
Amos.english_translation: As it is said (ibid.), “and all the singing men and singing women spoke … in their lamentations.”
Amos.translator_note: Printed “ibid.”; the verse is 2 Chronicles 35:25. Rashi’s quotation omits “of Josiah.”

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: the mourning for an only son
Amos.english_translation: Like a father who mourns for an only son.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: But of hearing the words of the LORD
Amos.english_translation: That the Holy Spirit will cease from you.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: faint for thirst
Amos.english_translation: Their spirit will fly away, like “he fainted” (Jonah 4), and so “the trees of the field fainted” (Ezekiel 31:4–5), and so in the language of the Mishnah, “she faints” (*yitalfah*) — *pasmer* [printed פשמיי"ר] in French (to faint).
Amos.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Amos 8:13 (“se pâmeront,” to faint), in the form פשמיר; the reading is *pasmer* (REJ transcription of Darmesteter’s first manuscript: *Pasmér*); the printed form (פשמיי"ר) is a variant spelling. Printed “Jonah 4” is Jonah 4:8. The source reference “Ezekiel 31:4–5” does not contain these words; they are in Ezekiel 31:15 (JPS: “all the trees of the field fainted for him”).

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: As thy God, O Dan, liveth
Amos.english_translation: One of the calves that Jeroboam set up in Dan.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: I saw the Lord standing beside the altar
Amos.english_translation: Departing from the cherub to the altar — in the manner of going out — upon the golden altar, which is in the Hekhal; and this is one of the ten journeys that the Shekhinah made.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Smite the capitals
Amos.english_translation: Which is at the top of the roof.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: that the posts may shake
Amos.english_translation: The lower thresholds of the house. So the king will be slain and the princes will tremble.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: And break them in pieces
Amos.english_translation: Like “and he will wound them.” And Targum Jonathan: “the capital of the lampstand” — *tafei menarta*: “the king Josiah will be slain, and the posts will shake, and the house will be destroyed, and the courts will become corpses.”
Amos.translator_note: The Aramaic is translated as printed; the exact sense of טפי מנרתא (left transliterated) is not certain.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: on the head of all of them
Amos.english_translation: And the vessels of the Sanctuary will go into captivity. And *u-vetsa’am* is like “their money”: it will go into exile at the head of all of them.
Amos.translator_note: The verb יגלה can mean “will go into exile” or “will be revealed”; “go into exile” fits the Targum quoted just before. The Aramaic is translated as printed.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Though they dig into the nether-world
Amos.english_translation: If they think to hide, as in the nether-world.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Thence shall My hand take them
Amos.english_translation: By My word their enemies will lead them.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: And though they climb up to heaven
Amos.english_translation: And if they go up onto high mountains as far as the צית of the heavens, from there by My word they will bring them down.
Amos.translator_note: The Aramaic word צית is left as printed; I could not confirm its meaning here. The rest of the Aramaic is translated as printed.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: in the top of Carmel
Amos.english_translation: At the top of the towers of the cities.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: I will search and take them out thence
Amos.english_translation: From there I will appoint searchers, and they will search them out.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: in the bottom of the sea
Amos.english_translation: Targum: “in the islands of the sea” — the islands of the sea.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Thence will I command the serpent
Amos.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “nations that are as strong as a serpent.”

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: toucheth the land and it melteth
Amos.english_translation: Targum: “who rebukes the earth, and it quakes”; and “and it melteth” is an expression of shaking. And HaShem is the One who touches the land, and it melts — that is to say, this decree has gone out from Me.
Amos.translator_note: Rashi paraphrases the verse rather than quoting it exactly.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: hath founded His vault upon the earth
Amos.english_translation: The gathering of His creatures. Another explanation: the gatherings of the upright — it was the foundation of the earth, for the rectification (*tikkun*) of the heavens, for it is for their sake that everything exists.
Amos.translator_note: The phrase לתקנת השמים is translated literally; its exact sense here is not certain.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: He that calleth for the waters of the sea
Amos.english_translation: Who said to gather many camps like the waters of the sea.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Are you not as the children of the Ethiopians unto Me
Amos.english_translation: Why should I refrain from taking vengeance on you, seeing that you do not return to Me? Are you not of the sons of Noah, like the other idolaters, like the Cushites, to whom you have been likened, as it is said, “Can the Ethiopian change his skin” (Jeremiah 13:23) — so you can do good.
Amos.translator_note: Translated as printed. In Jeremiah 13:23 the comparison is that one accustomed to evil can hardly do good; the printed last clause (“so you can do good”) may be defective.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Have not I brought up Israel out of the land of Egypt
Amos.english_translation: By My goodness: the beginning of My choosing you is the bringing out in which I brought you out of the land of Egypt. And what is that to Me? Even the Philistines — thus I brought them out of Caphtor, when the Caphtorim came upon the Avvim, as it is said, “And the Avvim, that dwelt in villages as far as Gaza,” etc. They also conquered the sons of Gaza, and the other lords of the Philistines in their place, and I brought them out of their hand; and nevertheless I did not make them a people for Myself.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: And Aram from Kir
Amos.english_translation: And so I am destined to bring up Aram from Kir, where Sennacherib will exile them; and at the end of days, when the kingdom of Assyria is nullified, they will go out.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: And I will destroy it from off the face of the earth
Amos.english_translation: “The kingdom” is the house of Jehu; but the house of Jacob I will not destroy.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: I will command, and I will sift the house of Israel among all the nations
Amos.english_translation: To exile them and to shake them among all the nations with a great and excessive shaking.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: Like as corn is sifted in a sieve
Amos.english_translation: That which is sifted in a sieve after the fine bran has fallen from it and the coarse remains, which cannot go out, and then the one who shakes shakes with all his strength.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: is sifted
Amos.english_translation: By means of another; and it is not possible to read it as “yanu’a,” which is something that moves of itself.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: The evil shall not overtake nor confront us
Amos.english_translation: Because of our iniquities the evil will not hurry to approach and come.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: tabernacle of David that is fallen
Amos.english_translation: After all these have come upon them, that day prepared for redemption will come, and in it “I will raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen.” Targum Jonathan: “the kingdom of the house of David.”

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: possess the remnant of Edom
Amos.english_translation: Israel [will possess] the remnant, etc., “and all the nations, for My name is called upon them.” *Asher* is like *ki* (“for”).

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: the plowman shall overtake the reaper
Amos.english_translation: “And threshing shall overtake the vintage, and the vintage shall overtake the sowing” (Leviticus 26:5): they will not manage to plow before the harvest comes, and they will not manage to gather the grapes before the time of sowing comes.
Amos.translator_note: Rashi quotes Leviticus 26:5 loosely (JPS: “your threshing shall reach unto the vintage, and the vintage shall reach unto the sowing time”).

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: all the hills shall melt
Amos.english_translation: Targum Jonathan translated *yitpalchan*: worked ground melts when the rains come.

Amos.english_lemma_JPS: sweet wine
Amos.english_translation: Good and sweet wine.

Obadiah.english_lemma_JPS: The vision of Obadiah
Obadiah.english_translation: Why is Obadiah different, in that he prophesied against Edom and prophesied no other prophecy? The Sages said: Obadiah was an Edomite convert. The Holy One, blessed be He, said: From them and by them I will bring [it] upon them. Let Obadiah come, who dwelt between two wicked ones, Ahab and Jezebel, and did not learn from their deeds, and let him exact punishment from wicked Esau, who dwelt between two righteous ones, Isaac and Rebecca, and did not learn from their deeds.

Obadiah.english_lemma_JPS: I make thee small among the nations
Obadiah.english_translation: Since his father called him “my older son” and his mother “her older son,” the Holy One, blessed be He, said: Before Me he is small. Our Rabbis expounded “small”: that they had neither script nor language.

Obadiah.english_lemma_JPS: Thou art greatly despised
Obadiah.english_translation: For they would not appoint a king the son of a king.

Obadiah.english_lemma_JPS: O thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock
Obadiah.english_translation: He relies on the support of his fathers, Abraham and Isaac, and they will not help him. *Chagvei* is like “And the land of Judah shall become a terror unto Egypt” (Isaiah 19), *ברייטיינ"א* in French. And do not wonder about the vav of *chagvei*, which is like the vav of *ketsvei* (Psalms 65) and like the vav of *kimtachavei* (Genesis 21), for the root of the word is only tet and chet.
Obadiah.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Obadiah 1:3, glossed “dans la cime,” with the form פרייטיינא (*fraiteine*, which he derives from a Latin word meaning “broken”); the printed form (ברייטיינ"א) begins with ב instead of פ. Printed “Isaiah 19,” “Psalms 65” and “Genesis 21” are Isaiah 19:17, Psalms 65:6 and Genesis 21:16. The printed root letters (tet and chet) fit כמטחוי rather than חגוי; left as printed.

Obadiah.english_lemma_JPS: thieves came to thee
Obadiah.english_translation: Upon you.

Obadiah.english_lemma_JPS: How art thou cut off!
Obadiah.english_translation: Why did you fall asleep, silent, until they stole all they desired?

Obadiah.english_lemma_JPS: Would they not leave some gleaning grapes?
Obadiah.english_translation: But these will not leave you anything, for they will search you and uncover and inquire into your hidden things.

Obadiah.english_lemma_JPS: How are his hidden places sought out!
Obadiah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: *itgaliyan* (“have been revealed”). And it is an Aramaic expression: *nev’u* means “were sought,” and so “If you will inquire, inquire you” (Isaiah 21:12).

Obadiah.english_lemma_JPS: Have conducted thee to the border
Obadiah.english_translation: Those who promised you help came with you and escorted you to the border of your land, to the frontier, where they came upon you for war; and by this they beguiled you and prevailed.

Obadiah.english_lemma_JPS: Have beguiled thee, and prevailed against thee
Obadiah.english_translation: To entice you to go out; and they turned back from behind you.

Obadiah.english_lemma_JPS: They that eat thy bread lay a snare under thee
Obadiah.english_translation: Even your food — your brother Jacob set it for you as a sickness (*mazor*), for he gave you bread and lentil stew, and through it you despised the birthright.

Obadiah.english_lemma_JPS: a snare
Obadiah.english_translation: Sickness.

Obadiah.english_lemma_JPS: thy mighty men, O Teman, shall be dismayed
Obadiah.english_translation: They will be dismayed and afraid to flee to the land of Ishmael. And Targum Jonathan: “and your mighty men will be broken, inhabitants of the southern land.”

Obadiah.english_lemma_JPS: every one may be cut off
Obadiah.english_translation: Every mighty man.

Obadiah.english_lemma_JPS: from the mount of Esau by slaughter
Obadiah.english_translation: From the abundance of slaughter that will come upon you.

Obadiah.english_lemma_JPS: For the violence done to thy brother Jacob
Obadiah.english_translation: Because of the violence you did to Jacob.

Obadiah.english_lemma_JPS: In the day that thou didst stand aloof
Obadiah.english_translation: That you did not come to help him.

Obadiah.english_lemma_JPS: Even thou wast as one of them
Obadiah.english_translation: I will come up against you as if you were among those who came against them.

Obadiah.english_lemma_JPS: But thou shouldest not have gazed on the day of thy brother
Obadiah.english_translation: You should not have (gazed) and stood aloof.

Obadiah.english_lemma_JPS: In the day of his disaster
Obadiah.english_translation: On the day he was delivered into the hand of the enemy — that is, the Babylonians. And so it says of Saul (1 Samuel 23:7), “God hath delivered (*nikar*) him into my hand” — that is, He delivered him into my hand.

Obadiah.english_lemma_JPS: Nor have laid hands on their substance
Obadiah.english_translation: Do not send your hand against his possessions. So Targum Jonathan translated; and the verse is abbreviated, and it is necessary to add “your hand” to it.

Obadiah.english_lemma_JPS: Neither shouldest thou have stood in the crossway
Obadiah.english_translation: A place where the fugitives go out by way to escape; and in French they call it *טרו"ג*. (“Do not stand at the crossway” — from here [it is learned] that it is forbidden to interrupt the Shema between one section and the next. Gloss of ר"ע.)
Obadiah.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Obadiah 1:14, glossed “the angle of the roads,” with the form טרוג; the printed form (טרו"ג) matches. The parenthetical sentence is a later gloss in the printed text; the abbreviation הג"ה דר"ע is left as printed, since I could not identify it.

Obadiah.english_lemma_JPS: For as you have drunk upon My holy mountain
Obadiah.english_translation: Just as you rejoiced over the smiting of the mountain of My holiness.

Obadiah.english_lemma_JPS: swallow down
Obadiah.english_translation: As its Targum, *vistalamun*; an expression of confusion, desolation and derangement of the mind — *estordison* [printed אישטורדישו"ן] in French (stupefaction).
Obadiah.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Obadiah 1:16 (“ils seront étourdis,” they will be stunned), in the form אישטורדישון; the reading is *estordison*, from Darmesteter’s index; the printed form (אישטורדישו"ן) matches.

Obadiah.english_lemma_JPS: possess their possessions
Obadiah.english_translation: The possessions of the nations, which they had been possessing for themselves.

Obadiah.english_lemma_JPS: For the LORD hath spoken
Obadiah.english_translation: And where did He speak? “And out of Jacob shall one have dominion, and shall destroy the remnant,” etc. (Numbers 24:19).

Obadiah.english_lemma_JPS: And they of the South shall possess the mount of Esau
Obadiah.english_translation: Israel who dwelt in the south of the Land of Israel will inherit the mount of Esau, which is on the southern border, and those of the Lowland will inherit the land of the Philistines and the mountain of Ephraim and the mountain of Samaria.
Obadiah.translator_note: Rashi writes “mountain” where the verse has “the field of Ephraim … the field of Samaria.”

Obadiah.english_lemma_JPS: And Benjamin shall possess Gilead
Obadiah.english_translation: And the sons of Manasseh, whose land was Gilead, will extend themselves further, beyond the borders of the Land of Israel in its east.
Obadiah.translator_note: As printed: Rashi’s explanation speaks of the sons of Manasseh, while the verse has Benjamin.

Obadiah.english_lemma_JPS: the captivity of this host of the children of Israel
Obadiah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “this people.” *Chel* is an expression of *chayil* (host), like “and he came to Jerusalem with a great army” (Isaiah 36:2), that of Rabshakeh, except that this one lacks a yod. And it is also possible to explain “this *chel*” as the captivity of this valley (*gai*).
Obadiah.translator_note: Rashi paraphrases Isaiah 36:2 (JPS: “And the king of Assyria sent Rab-shakeh from Lachish to Jerusalem unto king Hezekiah with a great army”).

Obadiah.english_lemma_JPS: That are among the Canaanites, even unto Zarephath
Obadiah.english_translation: The captivity that is of the children of Israel, who were exiled, of the ten tribes, to the land of the Canaanites as far as Zarephath.

Obadiah.english_lemma_JPS: And the captivity of Jerusalem, that is in Sepharad
Obadiah.english_translation: Those of the children of Judah who were exiled to Sepharad — they will inherit the cities of the South, in the south of the Land of Israel. And those who interpret say: Zarephath is the kingdom that is called *France* [printed פרנצ"א] in French. Sepharad — Targum Jonathan translated *Aspamia* (אספמיא).
Obadiah.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Obadiah 1:20 (“the interpreters say that it is the kingdom called …”), in the form פרנצא (*Frence*); the reading *France* is from Darmesteter’s index (his transcription of the first manuscript is *Frence*); the printed form (פרנצ"א) matches.

Obadiah.english_lemma_JPS: And saviours shall come up on mount Zion
Obadiah.english_translation: The princes of Israel, saviors, on Mount Zion.

Obadiah.english_lemma_JPS: To judge the mount of Esau
Obadiah.english_translation: To take vengeance on Mount Esau for what Esau did to Israel. *Lishpot* — *joustiser* [printed יושטיציי"ר] in French (to judge).
Obadiah.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Obadiah 1:21 (“pour juger,” to judge; *joustiser*); the printed form (יושטיציי"ר) matches a spelling he gives from some of his manuscripts (יושטיצייר).

Obadiah.english_lemma_JPS: the mount of Esau
Obadiah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “the great city of Esau.”

Obadiah.english_lemma_JPS: the kingdom shall be the LORD’S
Obadiah.english_translation: He taught you that His kingship is not complete until He takes vengeance on Amalek.

Jonah.english_translation: My proclamation.

Jonah.english_lemma_JPS: to flee unto Tarshish from the presence of the LORD
Jonah.english_translation: A sea whose name is Tarshish, and it is outside the Land. He said: I will flee to the sea, for the Shekhinah does not rest outside the Land.
