The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: By your life, I have messengers like you to send after you and bring you back from there. A parable: a priest’s servant fled from his master and entered a cemetery; his master said to him: I have servants like you to send after you and bring you from there. And what did Jonah see that he did not wish to go to Nineveh? He said: The idolaters are close to repentance; if I tell them and they repent, I will be found to condemn Israel, who do not listen to the words of the prophets.

Jonah.english_lemma_JPS: so he paid the fare thereof
Jonah.english_translation: He hastened to give its fare. It is not the way of seafarers to give the fare of the ship until the time of leaving it, and he gave it in advance; and not only that, but he gave the fare for all of it.

Jonah.english_lemma_JPS: so that the ship was like to be broken
Jonah.english_translation: It seemed as though it was breaking.
People who steer the ship.

Jonah.english_lemma_JPS: cried every man unto his god
Jonah.english_translation: They were there from the seventy nations of the idolaters.

Jonah.english_lemma_JPS: So the shipmaster came to him
Jonah.english_translation: The chief of the sailors, for they too are called *chovlei ha-yam*; and in French, *גובירניי"ל*.
Jonah.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Jonah 1:6 (“le chef des marins,” the chief of the sailors), reading it *governedors* (from Latin *gubernatores*), with Hebrew forms such as גובנרדורש; the printed form (גובירניי"ל) ends with ל and is a variant of the same word.

Jonah.english_lemma_JPS: What meanest thou that thou sleepest?
Jonah.english_translation: Why are you asleep? Now is not the time for sleep.
An expression of thought, and so “his thoughts” (Psalms 147) and “and the king thought” (Daniel 7).
Jonah.translator_note: Printed “Psalms 147” is Psalms 146:4 (JPS: “his thoughts perish”); printed “Daniel 7” is Daniel 6:4, in Aramaic (JPS: “and the king thought to set him over the whole realm”).

Jonah.english_lemma_JPS: Come, and let us cast lots
Jonah.english_translation: They saw other ships sailing on the sea in peace while theirs was breaking up. They said: It is on account of one of us. So it is found in Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer.

Jonah.english_lemma_JPS: for whose cause this evil is upon us
Jonah.english_translation: On account of the deeds of which of us.

Jonah.english_lemma_JPS: Tell us, we pray thee, for whose cause
Jonah.english_translation: Against whom did you sin, that because of it this evil is upon us?
Perhaps you transgressed in your trades.
Perhaps a decree was decreed upon the people of that place, even though you have no part in it.
Perhaps your people sinned.

Jonah.english_lemma_JPS: What is this that thou hast done?
Jonah.english_translation: Why did you do this, to flee from such a Ruler?
They toiled and labored like one who digs in a breach (*machteret*) in order to break in.
For the sin of sending a hand against his life.
That they would convert.

It was a male, and it was standing in comfort, and he did not set his heart to pray. The Holy One, blessed be He, signaled to the fish, and it vomited him into the mouth of a female that was full of fetuses, and he was there in distress and prayed there, as it is said, “out of the fish’s belly.” (“And HaShem prepared” (*vayman*). Those sixteen days in which Israel lacked the manna, for they did not eat it forty full years — this manna the Holy One, blessed be He, took and sustained the fish with, so that Jonah would not be digested in its bowels; and Jonah also ate of this manna inside it. Therefore it is said *vayman*, the letters yod-vav (16) and *man* (manna). And so *vayman* regarding the gourd (*kikayon*), which ate four omers; therefore *vayman* is said four times. And in the Greek language manna is called *kika*, and concerning this it is said *kik-yon*. Sod Mesharim.)
Jonah.translator_note: In the verse, the point of Rashi’s “out of the fish’s belly” is the feminine form הדגה (“the female fish”), which JPS’s “the fish’s belly” does not show. The parenthetical passage is printed in parentheses as an addition to Rashi and ends with the attribution “Sod Mesharim,” which I could not identify.

Jonah.english_translation: (“HaShem his God” — he joined [the attributes of] judgment and mercy, the merit of Abraham and Isaac. “Out of the fish’s belly” (*mi-me’ei ha-dagah*) — this is Jacob. Sod Mesharim.)
Jonah.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment; “his God” is taken from the verse. The comment is printed in parentheses as an addition to Rashi and ends with the attribution “Sod Mesharim,” which I could not identify.

Jonah.english_lemma_JPS: Out of the belly of the nether-world cried I
Jonah.english_translation: From the belly of the fish, which is for me like the nether-world.

Jonah.english_lemma_JPS: All Thy waves and Thy billows
Jonah.english_translation: Targum: “all the surges of the sea,” because the surge (*nachshol*) breaks and shatters the sea.
When they cast me into the sea, [I said:] Behold, I am dying, and I have been driven out from before Your eyes.
I saw that You had kept me alive all these days; I knew that I would again look toward Your holy Temple (*heikhal*).

Jonah.english_lemma_JPS: The weeds were wrapped about my head
Jonah.english_translation: Targum: “the Red Sea was suspended above my head,” for the Holy One, blessed be He, showed him the Red Sea and how Israel passed through it, for the two eyes of the fish were like two windows, and he would look and see everything that was in the sea.

Jonah.english_lemma_JPS: I went down to the bottoms of the mountains
Jonah.english_translation: To the end of the measure of the mountains that are fixed upon the deep I went down.

Jonah.english_lemma_JPS: The earth with her bars closed upon me
Jonah.english_translation: Opposite me, above me, closed, and I shall not go out forever. *Ba’adi* is like “and thou shalt shut the door upon thee” (*ba’adekh*, 2 Kings 4:4), and so every *ba’ad* in Scripture: “Skin for skin” (Job 1) — a limb opposite a limb.
It refers back to what he said above: “And I said: ‘I am cast out,’” and “I said, the earth, her bars are closed upon me forever.”

Jonah.english_lemma_JPS: Yet hast Thou brought up my life from the pit
Jonah.english_translation: But I have already seen Gehenna here, and from there You brought me up, and behold, I am now opposite the place beneath the Temple in Jerusalem, as it is said, “Yet I will look again toward Thy holy temple,” and “And my prayer came in unto Thee, into Thy holy temple.”

Jonah.english_lemma_JPS: When my soul fainted within me
Jonah.english_translation: In *ishtalheyut*, and so *be-hit’atef nafsham* and so *be-’atef ‘olel* (Lamentations 2).
Jonah.translator_note: The Aramaic word באשתלהיות is left transliterated; I could not confirm its meaning. The verses are Lamentations 2:12 (JPS: “When their soul is poured out”) and Lamentations 2:11 (JPS: “the young children and the sucklings swoon”); Rashi cites the Hebrew words for their sense of fainting.

Jonah.english_translation: Those who serve idolatry.

The fear of the Holy One, blessed be He, for all their kindness and their good is from Him — they forsake. But I am not so; rather, “I will sacrifice unto Thee with the voice of thanksgiving.” So Targum Jonathan translated. And Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer expounded it concerning the sailors, who forsook their kindness, for they used to do good to idolatry, and they converted.

The vows of peace-offerings and thanksgiving I shall pay to the name of the salvations that belong to HaShem. *Yeshu’atah* is like *li-yeshu’atah*, and so “*kumah ezratah lanu*” (Psalms 44:27), “Arise for our help.”

Destroyed. (And he did not say “destroyed,” because *nehpechet* serves two meanings, bad and good: if they do not repent — destroyed; and if they do repent — then *nehpechet* refers to the people of Nineveh, that they will turn from evil to good and repent. Gloss of ר"ע.)
Jonah.translator_note: This sentence is printed in parentheses as a later gloss; the abbreviation הג"ה דר"ע is left as printed, since I could not identify it.

Jonah.english_translation: A garment of honor.

Jonah.english_lemma_JPS: And he caused it to be proclaimed
Jonah.english_translation: He commanded and proclaimed.

Jonah.english_lemma_JPS: by the decree of the king and his nobles
Jonah.english_translation: On the counsel of the king and his nobles they commanded to proclaim it.

Jonah.english_lemma_JPS: let them cry mightily unto God
Jonah.english_translation: They tied up the mothers separately and the offspring separately; they said before Him: Master of the Universe, if You do not have mercy on us, we will not have mercy on these.
The transgressions that are in his hand — he will turn.
He took thought concerning the evil, to turn back from it.
He said: Now the idolaters will say that I am a false prophet.
I know that if they return in repentance, You will not destroy them, and I shall be a liar in their eyes.
An expression of preparation.

Jonah.english_lemma_JPS: to deliver him from his evil
Jonah.english_translation: From the heat of the sun.
A herb that grows upward with many branches and gives shade; and that is its name.
The worm [struck] the gourd. In a place where, for the masculine, it would say *vayach*, it says in the feminine form, *vatach*.
Our Rabbis said: when it blows, it silences all the winds before it, and it is very hot. And so Targum Jonathan: *shetika* (silence).
*pasmer* [printed פשמיי"ר] in French (to faint).
Jonah.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Jonah 4:8 (“il se pâma,” he fainted), in the form פשמיר; the reading is *pasmer*, from Darmesteter’s index; the printed form (פשמיי"ר) is a variant spelling.

Jonah.english_lemma_JPS: for which thou hast not laboured
Jonah.english_translation: In plowing and sowing and watering.

Jonah.english_lemma_JPS: which came up in a night
Jonah.english_translation: Like “a son of a night”: it grew for only one night.

Jonah.english_lemma_JPS: that cannot discern between their right hand and their left hand
Jonah.english_translation: Children.
Grown people whose understanding is like that of cattle, for they do not recognize Who created them.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: Micah the Morashtite
Micah.english_translation: “The Morashtite” — from the city of Moreshah.
Micah.translator_note: The source lemma is דבר, but the comment explains המורשתי, so the lemma is taken from the phrase it explains.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: be witness against you
Micah.english_translation: That I prophesied to you in His name and warned you.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: cometh forth out of His place
Micah.english_translation: From the throne of mercy to the throne of judgment.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: tread upon the high places of the earth
Micah.english_translation: Upon the lofty and the haughty of spirit.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: As wax
Micah.english_translation: Wax.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: As waters that are poured down a steep place
Micah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “that are poured out on a slope.” *Mugarim* is an expression of the flowing of water, and so *nigrah* (Lamentations 3:49), *nigarot* on the day of His anger (Job 20:28), *meim gar* (Job 28), *vayagar mi-zeh* (Psalms 75).
Micah.translator_note: Rashi cites these words for their root, so they are left transliterated. Printed “Job 28” is Job 28:4 and “Psalms 75” is Psalms 75:9 (JPS: “And He poureth out of the same”); Lamentations 3:49 reads in JPS “Mine eye is poured out” and Job 20:28 “His goods shall flow away.”

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: a heap in the field
Micah.english_translation: *Ligrei chaklan* (Targum): an expression of heaps (*galim*), like *Yegar-sahaduta* (Genesis 31:47).

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: pour down the stones thereof into the valley
Micah.english_translation: And I will drag [them], like those that are “poured down a steep place” (above, verse 4).

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: For of the hire of a harlot hath she gathered them
Micah.english_translation: All this wealth.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: And unto the hire of a harlot shall they return
Micah.english_translation: And to oblivion (*tamyon*), like the other hires of a harlot, all her gatherings shall return. And Jonathan translated: “and to the house of the worshipers of error all her gatherings shall be delivered.”

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: stripped
Micah.english_translation: Raving like a madman, in bewilderment of heart, as in *eshtolelu avirei lev* (Psalms 76) and *ve-sar me-ra mishtolel* (Isaiah 59). And the tav comes to serve in a word in the form *mitpa’el* and *nitpa’el*; and so is the course of a word whose root begins with shin or samekh: when a tav comes upon it in the form *mitpa’el* and *nitpa’el*, it enters inside the word, like *mishtolel*. I say that it is from the expression of error (*shogeg*), like *lo tashleh oti* (2 Kings 4), *al ha-shal* (2 Samuel 10), *di yomar shalu* (Daniel 3).
Micah.translator_note: Rashi cites these words for their root, so they are left transliterated. Printed “Psalms 76” is Psalms 76:6; “Isaiah 59” is Isaiah 59:15 (JPS: “maketh himself a prey”); “2 Kings 4” is 2 Kings 4:28 (JPS: “Do not deceive me”); “2 Samuel 10” is 2 Samuel 6:7 (JPS: “for his error”); “Daniel 3” is Daniel 3:29 (JPS: “speak any thing amiss”). In Psalms 76:6 JPS reads “The stout-hearted are bereft of sense.”

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: For her wound is incurable
Micah.english_translation: For she is sick with her wounds, like *vaye’anash* (2 Samuel 12).
Micah.translator_note: Printed “2 Samuel 12” is 2 Samuel 12:15 (JPS: “and it was very sick”).

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: Tell it not in Gath
Micah.english_translation: Lest the Philistines rejoice over us.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: At Beth-le-aphrah
Micah.english_translation: Ophrah of the Abiezrite.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: roll thyself in the dust
Micah.english_translation: A play on words (literally, “an expression that falls upon the language”), and so “O inhabitant of Saphir, in nakedness and shame,” and so “the inhabitant of Zaanan is not come forth” — all according to the name of the city, an expression of lamentation. *Hitpalshi* means roll yourself; its interpretation, according to its context, is “cover yourself with dust.”

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: Pass you away
Micah.english_translation: He began in the feminine singular, as one speaking to the assembly of the city, as it is said, “O inhabitant of Saphir,” all of them in the name of one assembly; and he said *lakhem* as one speaking to the many, for he speaks to the many.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: O inhabitant of Saphir
Micah.english_translation: The name of the city.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: in nakedness and shame
Micah.english_translation: Revealed, the place of shame (*beit ha-bushet*), as she is called Shafir, which is the name of a miscarriage that comes out of a woman’s womb.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: The inhabitant of Zaanan is not come forth
Micah.english_translation: Targum: “the inhabitants of Zaanan will not go out delivered.”

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: The wailing of Beth-ezel shall take from you the standing-place thereof
Micah.english_translation: The wailing that you caused to those who were robbed, whose inheritance you rob in order to bring house near to house, field to field, one beside the other — it will take from you its standing-place: the standing-place of the buildings that you built and set up on their inheritance. *Beit ha-ezel* — *איוטמנ"ט* in French.
Micah.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Micah 1:11, glossed “the house built in line with its neighbor,” in forms such as איוסטמנט (*ajoustement*); the printed form (איוטמנ"ט) lacks the samekh.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: waiteth anxiously for good
Micah.english_translation: For she hoped (*kiyetah*) for good — she who dwells in her tranquility and rebels against the word of the prophets.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: evil is come down from the LORD
Micah.english_translation: Behold, this *ki* is used in the sense of “but”: she hoped for good, but because of her rebelliousness evil came down upon her.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: to the swift steeds
Micah.english_translation: Harness the chariot to the *rekhesh*, which is quick to run, and you will flee. And Dunash said that it is an Arabic expression.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: Therefore shalt thou give a parting gift to Moresheth-gath
Micah.english_translation: Because you will send messengers against the kingdom of David, who made you inherit Gath, as it is said, “And David took Gath from the hand of the Philistines” (1 Chronicles 18), and you despise him, as it is said, “Forasmuch as this people hath refused the waters of Shiloah” (Isaiah 8), etc. Therefore the houses of Achzib, which were of the land of Judah and were drawn after Pekah the son of Remaliah, will in the end become *achzav* (a deceit) to the kings of Israel, for Pekah the son of Remaliah will be killed and those who rely on him will be deceived (*ve-yikhzevu*). And in the days of Ahaz this prophecy was prophesied.
Micah.translator_note: Printed “1 Chronicles 18” is 1 Chronicles 18:1; Rashi quotes it loosely (JPS: “and took Gath and its towns out of the hand of the Philistines”). Printed “Isaiah 8” is Isaiah 8:6.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: Therefore shalt thou give a parting gift
Micah.english_translation: Its explanation: *lakhen* is like *al asher* (“because”), as in “Therefore thou didst plant plants of pleasantness” (ibid. 17) — because I planted you as plants of pleasantness, and you turned into strange shoots.
Micah.translator_note: Printed “ibid. 17” is Isaiah 17:10. The words after the dash are Rashi’s explanation, not a quotation.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: The houses of Achzib shall be a deceitful thing
Micah.english_translation: A play on words. From the Aggadah of Chelek I learned the midrash of this verse thus:
Micah.translator_note: The printed text ends here, with no midrash following. “Chelek” is left as printed; the printed text gives no further identification.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: I will yet bring unto thee
Micah.english_translation: Enemies who will take possession of you — you who dwell in Mareshah; *yoresh* with *Mareshah* is a play on words (an expression that falls upon the language).

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: The glory of Israel shall come even unto Adullam
Micah.english_translation: For it is before it; from the border it will retreat backward, and the glory of Israel will come, for the idolaters will conquer from its border as far as Adullam. So Targum Jonathan: “as far as Adullam they will come into the border of the land of Israel.” And a midrash aggadah I heard in the name of Rabbi Menachem: “I will yet bring unto thee him that shall possess thee” — the sons of Elam were fit to inherit the Land of Israel, for he was the firstborn of the sons of Shem; and because of the love of your fathers I turned it to the sons of Arpachshad. Now I will bring the Chaldeans and the sons of Elam upon them.
Micah.translator_note: The first sentence is difficult as printed; it is translated literally. The Aramaic is translated as printed.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: Make thee bald
Micah.english_translation: Your head.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: poll thee
Micah.english_translation: Your hair, like “and shaved his head” (Job 1) — an expression of plucking out hair.
Micah.translator_note: Printed “Job 1” is Job 1:20.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: as the vulture
Micah.english_translation: As its Targum: “like the eagle whose wings have been shed”; the way of the eagle is to pluck out most of its wings.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: And work evil upon their beds!
Micah.english_translation: All night they resolve in their hearts how they will do the evil in the morning.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: And houses, and take them away
Micah.english_translation: It refers back to “And they covet”: they covet houses.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: take them away
Micah.english_translation: Like *ve-lakchu* (“and they take”).

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: Neither shall you walk upright
Micah.english_translation: And you will not walk with an upright stature.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: lament with a doleful lamentation
Micah.english_translation: *Venahah* is the future tense, like *ve-asah*, *u-fanah*. *Venahah*: the lamenter will lament, and he says: *nehi nihyah* — a lamentation that has come to be in the world. And what is the lamentation that has come to be? He said: *shadod nishdonu* — our enemies have plundered us. And as for the expression *nishdenu*, in which he wrote a nun at the beginning and did not write *shedonu*, since it comes to serve two senses — an expression of *nif’alnu* and an expression of *pa’alnu* — had he written *nishdenu*, the expression would refer to the plundered and not to the plunderers; and had he written *shedonu*, it would refer to the plunderers and not to the plundered; now it refers to both: we were given into the hand of those who plundered us. And in French, *שומי"ר דימשטיור"א נשו"ט*. Another explanation: *nishdonu* — we caused ourselves to be plundered.
Micah.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Micah 2:4, glossed as a complex form, both active and passive, meaning “we are handed over to men who have laid us waste,” with forms such as שומש דגשטירנט נוש; the printed form (שומי"ר דימשטיור"א נשו"ט) differs in spelling and could not be matched exactly.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: He changeth the portion of my people
Micah.english_translation: The inheritance, the portion of my people, has been exchanged to the idolaters.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: How doth he remove it from me!
Micah.english_translation: How will it turn aside to me, to restore to us our fields, which this idolater is dividing for himself? How is it possible still to restore them to me? — all these are the words of the lamenter and bearer of the parable. *Ek yamish li* — *קומ"א שדיטורנר"א אמו"י* in French — like *sorah elai* and *vayasar elav*.
Micah.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this phrase at Micah 2:4 (“comment se détournera-t-il, pour aller vers moi?”), with forms such as קום שדיסטורנרא אמויי; the printed form (קומ"א שדיטורנר"א אמו"י) matches this closely.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: cast the line by lot
Micah.english_translation: One who divides an inheritance, for it is the way to divide an inheritance with the measuring cord.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: Preach you not
Micah.english_translation: “Do not prophesy,” to rebuke them. To you, the prophets, I say, who preach continually.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: That they shall not take shame
Micah.english_translation: Lest disgrace from them overtake you, as it is said, “Reprove not a scorner” (Proverbs 9:8). Every *tipah* is an expression of prophecy, like “And preach not against the house of Isaac” (Amos 7:16), “and preach toward the South” (Ezekiel 21:2).

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: Do I change, O house of Jacob?
Micah.english_translation: Will they say this, the house of Jacob, when they hear the evil that my prophets prophesy to them?

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: Is the spirit of the LORD straitened?
Micah.english_translation: Perhaps He no longer has the ability before Him to do good, and His spirit is not as broad toward good as it was in the former days.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: Are these His doings?
Micah.english_translation: That is, to do evil.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: Do not My words do good to him that walketh uprightly?
Micah.english_translation: My spirit is not shortened, and these are not My doings, except toward the wicked; but to the one who walks uprightly I will surely do good.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: But of late My people is risen up as an enemy
Micah.english_translation: The verse is connected to the one above it: I am good, and I do good; and the matter that is opposite it, and on account of it, My people — it raises it up as an enemy to it.
Micah.translator_note: The sentence is difficult as printed; translated literally.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: With the garment you strip also the mantle
Micah.english_translation: In return for what you rob — the garment and the garment of splendor — and you strip them off all who pass by you on the way.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: as men returning from war
Micah.english_translation: Whereas they thought they were passing by in security, they have been turned into “men returning from war,” like people who return from the war, lacking garments and food, for their enemies took what was on them. *Shovei* is like *sorei ha-gefen nokhriyah* (Jeremiah 2:21), *nugei mi-mo’ed* (Zephaniah 3).
Micah.translator_note: Rashi compares the form of the word with Jeremiah 2:21 (JPS: “the degenerate plant of a strange vine”) and with Zephaniah 3:18 (printed “Zephaniah 3”; JPS: “them that are far from the appointed season”).

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: The women of My people you cast out from their pleasant houses
Micah.english_translation: Because you kill their husbands and they sit widowed; or because you take the money of their husbands, and they sit in distress and do not gladden their wives.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: you take away My glory for ever
Micah.english_translation: “Hadar” is majesty (*hod*) and wealth that I gave them.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: Arise you, and depart; for this is not your resting-place
Micah.english_translation: Arise and go into exile from the land, for not in this manner did I give it to you as a resting-place.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: Because of the uncleanness thereof, it shall destroy you
Micah.english_translation: For in order to defile it, it makes a company of “the bands of the wicked.” *Tachbol* is an expression of bands, like “a band of prophets” (1 Samuel 10:5), “the bands of the wicked” (Psalms 119:61); and so Targum Jonathan: *mist’ayin alah* — an expression of a company (*si’ah*).
Micah.translator_note: JPS renders Psalms 119:61 as “The cords of the wicked.”

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: even with a sore destruction
Micah.english_translation: And at the time of their banding together, they had already taken counsel among themselves and explained why they were joining together.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: a sore destruction
Micah.english_translation: A matter that is explained, set out well, like *mah nimratzu imrei* (Job 6:25), *mah yamritzekha* (ibid. 16), *kelalah nimretzet* (1 Kings 2).
Micah.translator_note: Rashi cites these words for their root, so they are left transliterated. Printed “ibid. 16” is Job 16:3 (JPS: “what provoketh thee”); “Job 6:25” in JPS is “How forcible are words of uprightness”; printed “1 Kings 2” is 1 Kings 2:8 (JPS: “a grievous curse”).

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: If a man walking in wind and falsehood do lie
Micah.english_translation: If they were to find a man walking in wind, a man of falsehood, prophesying to them that they should get drunk on wine and strong drink — he would be a prophet accepted by this people.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: I will surely assemble, O Jacob, all of thee
Micah.english_translation: There are yet days to come, and I will gather you.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: as sheep in a fold
Micah.english_translation: Like a numerous flock placed in the fortresses of the sheepfolds.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: As a flock in the midst of their pasture
Micah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “like a flock in the midst of a pen” — the place where it is led; and so “Then shall the lambs feed as in their pasture” (Isaiah 5:17).

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: They shall make great noise by reason of the multitude of men
Micah.english_translation: The cities will be humming from the multitude of people within them.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: The breaker is gone up before them
Micah.english_translation: Their savior, who breaks through the fence of thorns and the hedges of briars, to straighten the way before them.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: Who rob their skin from off them
Micah.english_translation: [Those who rob the skin] of the house of Israel, who are heads and chiefs over them, as he said, “heads of the house of Jacob and chiefs of the house of Israel.”
Micah.translator_note: Rashi quotes Micah 3:1 loosely (JPS: “you heads of Jacob, and rulers of the house of Israel”).

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: the flesh of my people
Micah.english_translation: The flesh of My people.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: break their bones
Micah.english_translation: They opened them to take out the marrow, like “They break forth into singing” (*pitzchu rinah*, Isaiah 14:7) — they opened the mouth with song.
Micah.translator_note: Printed “ibid. 14” is Isaiah 14:7.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: they chop them in pieces, as that which is in the pot
Micah.english_translation: And they break the limbs, as the pieces placed in the pot to be cooked are broken. *U-faresu* is an expression of breaking, like *paros la-ra’ev* (ibid. 58), *ve-lo yifrsu lahem* (Jeremiah 16), *paresah Tziyon* (Lamentations 1).
Micah.translator_note: Rashi cites these words for their root, so they are left transliterated. Printed “ibid. 58” is Isaiah 58:7 (JPS: “to deal thy bread to the hungry”); “Jeremiah 16” is Jeremiah 16:7 (JPS: “neither shall men break bread for them”); “Lamentations 1” is Lamentations 1:17 (JPS: “Zion spreadeth forth her hands”).

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: flesh within the caldron
Micah.english_translation: *caldière* [printed קלדיי"רא] in French (a cooking pot).
Micah.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Micah 3:3 (“marmite,” a cooking pot), in the form קלדירא (*caldière*); the printed form (קלדיי"רא) is a variant spelling.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: Then shall they cry unto the LORD
Micah.english_translation: Then, when that time arrives that was mentioned above — “I will surely assemble Jacob” — they will cry to HaShem to do good to them, with the favor of His people and the joy of His nation; and He will not answer them.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: when their teeth have any thing to bite
Micah.english_translation: And they eat the flesh of fattened animals, which My people, who err after them, feed them.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: That cry: ‘Peace’
Micah.english_translation: And when they feed them, they call out and prophesy peace to them.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: They even prepare war against him
Micah.english_translation: And they prepared against him for war.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: no answer of God
Micah.english_translation: *Ma’aneh* is vocalized with a kamatz (meaning, a tzere), because it is attached to the Name.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: Jerusalem shall become heaps
Micah.english_translation: *דגורין*.
Micah.translator_note: Left as printed; I could not determine the language or meaning of this word.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: And peoples shall flow unto it
Micah.english_translation: And they will be gathered there together, like the rivers that go to the sea.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: And He shall judge between many peoples
Micah.english_translation: This “judging” is an expression of rebuke — *דשרימנ"ט* in French.
Micah.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Micah 4:3 (“et il jugera,” in the sense of rebuking), in forms such as דרישנמנט (*draisnement*); the printed form (דשרימנ"ט) is closest to the form דישריינמינט that he gives from one manuscript.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: For the mouth of the LORD of hosts hath spoken
Micah.english_translation: And where did He speak? “And I will give peace in the land” (Leviticus 26:6).

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: walk each one in the name of its god
Micah.english_translation: They will go to destruction because they served idolatry. So Targum Jonathan translated.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: will I assemble her that halteth
Micah.english_translation: I will gather those driven about (*metaltelaya*); and so Targum Jonathan. But to me it appears to be an expression of healing, like *ve-asafti mi-tzara’ato* (2 Kings 5).
Micah.translator_note: Rashi’s wording is a loose quotation of 2 Kings 5:3 (JPS: “then would he recover him of his leprosy”).

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: her that I have afflicted
Micah.english_translation: And those to whom I did evil on account of their iniquity.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: And thou, Migdal-eder
Micah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “And you, Messiah of Israel, who were hidden away from before the sins of the congregation of Zion.” Its explanation: *Migdal* is an expression of stronghold, and the Targum translates *eder* as the congregation of Israel, and it translated *ophel* as an expression of *ofel* (darkness). And it is possible to explain *Migdal Eder* as the Temple, and *ophel* as an expression of a tower of strength, and so *ophel* and *bochan* (Isaiah 32).
Micah.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 32” is Isaiah 32:14 (JPS: “The mound and the tower”).

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: Unto thee shall it come
Micah.english_translation: The remnant of the lame and the driven away — all will be gathered to you.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: the former dominion shall come
Micah.english_translation: The whole dominion will come, entire, to the house of David in Jerusalem, as it was at the beginning, before it was divided. And what is the former dominion? The kingdom of the daughter of Jerusalem.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: Now why
Micah.english_translation: For you are rebelling against Me.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: why dost thou cry out aloud
Micah.english_translation: Set your heart: why do you need to seek friends and lovers, the kings of Egypt and the kings of Assyria, to help?

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: Be in pain
Micah.english_translation: An expression of trembling, like (here) “pangs have taken hold of thee”; and the language alludes to a woman in travail.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: and labour to bring forth
Micah.english_translation: Kneel and bend over your belly (*gechonekh*), and so in the language of the Mishnah, “a wall that bows toward the public domain.”

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: thou go forth out of the city
Micah.english_translation: From Jerusalem, to go into exile.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: shalt dwell in the field
Micah.english_translation: Your dwelling-place will be plowed like a field.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: Let her be defiled
Micah.english_translation: Now Zion will become guilty through her sins, and her iniquity will be visited upon her.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: let our eye gaze upon Zion
Micah.english_translation: And our eyes will see in her what we desired to see in her.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: For He hath gathered them as the sheaves to the threshing-floor
Micah.english_translation: And in the end He will gather them to the Valley of Jehoshaphat and the surroundings of Jerusalem for war, as sheaves are gathered in order to thresh them there; they too, the army of Gog and Magog, are gathered for their own harm; and the Holy One, blessed be He, will say to the congregation of Israel: “Arise and thresh, O daughter of Zion.”

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: devote
Micah.english_translation: An expression of consecration (*hekdesh*).

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: their gain
Micah.english_translation: What they gathered from robbery and violence.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: their substance
Micah.english_translation: Targum: “and their possessions.”

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: gather thyself in troops, O daughter of troops
Micah.english_translation: Now, at the time when the evil was decreed on account of the iniquity — for it has prevailed — “gather yourself in troops, O daughter of troops”: daughter of the Chaldeans, gather troops, for now is the time when you will succeed with the troop that has laid siege against us.
Micah.translator_note: The words כי גבר are difficult as printed; translated literally as “for it has prevailed.”

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: They smite the judge of Israel with a rod upon the cheek
Micah.english_translation: Who caused you to succeed? That Israel mocked their prophets and their judges and struck them on the cheek. So they used to do, and so it is found in the Pesikta; and so Isaiah says, “I gave my back to the smiters” (Isaiah 50:6).

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: Beth-lehem Ephrathah
Micah.english_translation: For David came out from there, of whom it is said, “thy servant Jesse the Beth-lehemite” (1 Samuel 17:58); and Beth-lehem is called Ephrath, as it is said, “in the way to Ephrath—the same is Beth-lehem” (Genesis 48:7).

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: Which art little to be among the thousands of Judah
Micah.english_translation: You deserved to be small among the families of Judah because of the disqualification of Ruth the Moabitess within you.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: Out of thee shall one come forth unto Me
Micah.english_translation: The Messiah son of David; and so it says, “The stone which the builders rejected” (Psalms 118:22).

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: from of old, from ancient days
Micah.english_translation: “Before the sun shall his name be continued (*yinon*)” (ibid.).
Micah.translator_note: Printed “ibid.”; the verse is Psalms 72:17. JPS renders it “May his name be continued as long as the sun,” whereas Rashi’s point is “before the sun.”

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: Therefore will He give them up
Micah.english_translation: He will give them into the hand of their enemies until the time comes when Zion, who is in travail, bears her children — Zion, who has now been seized by pangs like a woman in travail, and now she is called a woman in travail. And our Rabbis said: From here we learn that the son of David does not come until the wicked kingdom spreads over the whole world for nine months. But according to its plain sense, this is the approach that I explained.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: the residue of his brethren
Micah.english_translation: Of the king of Judah — that is, the rest of the tribe of Judah.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: shall return with the children of Israel
Micah.english_translation: They will join with the rest of the tribes, and they will be one kingdom and will no longer be divided into two kingdoms.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: feed his flock
Micah.english_translation: And he shall sustain Israel.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: they shall abide
Micah.english_translation: [They shall return] from the exiles.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: for then shall he be great
Micah.english_translation: Their king.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: unto the ends of the earth
Micah.english_translation: And they shall bring them as an offering to him, on horses and in chariots.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: this shall be peace
Micah.english_translation: Complete and fixed, with no more interruption, and it will not be like the other deliverances, after which there were troubles.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: When the Assyrian shall come into our land
Micah.english_translation: Behold, *ki* is used in the sense of “if”: if he comes into our land as he came now.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: Then shall we raise against him seven shepherds
Micah.english_translation: Seven and eight — our Rabbis explained their names in tractate Sukkah, but I do not know from where they learned it.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: And they shall waste the land of Assyria with the sword
Micah.english_translation: And they will shatter, like “Thou shalt break them with a rod of iron” (ibid. 2).
Micah.translator_note: Printed “ibid. 2” is Psalms 2:9.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: the land of Nimrod
Micah.english_translation: It is Babylon.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: when he treadeth within our border
Micah.english_translation: In the gates of its provinces.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: As dew from the LORD
Micah.english_translation: That does not come to the world through man, and no one seeks the face of man for it; so Israel will not hope for the help of any man, only for that of HaShem.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: As a lion among the beasts of the forest
Micah.english_translation: So will their king be, ruling over all.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: treadeth down and teareth in pieces
Micah.english_translation: *Remes* is the trampling of the lion when he is hungry and he eats it in its place; and *taraf* is when he carries the prey to his dens for his whelps and his lionesses.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: I will cut off thy horses out of the midst of thee
Micah.english_translation: It is the help of Egypt, upon which you lean, to provide you with horses.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: I will cut off the cities of thy land
Micah.english_translation: And you will have no need for fortified cities.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: I will destroy thine enemies
Micah.english_translation: And I will destroy those who hate you, and so *u-male’u penei tevel arim* (Isaiah 14:21), and so *vayehi areikha* (1 Samuel 28).
Micah.translator_note: The Aramaic phrase at the start is translated as printed. Rashi takes ערים as “enemies” in these verses; JPS has “cities” in Isaiah 14:21 (“fill the face of the world with cities”) and “adversary” in 1 Samuel 28:16 (“is become thine adversary”). Printed “1 Samuel 28” is 1 Samuel 28:16.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: contend thou before the mountains
Micah.english_translation: The fathers.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: the hills
Micah.english_translation: The mothers.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: what have I done unto thee
Micah.english_translation: Set your heart to recognize what good I did for you.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: wherein have I wearied thee?
Micah.english_translation: With My service.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: Testify against Me
Micah.english_translation: Bear witness against Me.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: For I brought thee up out of the land of Egypt
Micah.english_translation: Although I did for you all this good, I did not weary you with great service or with great sacrifices.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: Moses, Aaron, and Miriam
Micah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “Moses to teach the tradition of the laws, and Aaron to atone for the people, and Miriam to instruct the *nashaya*.”
Micah.translator_note: The Aramaic word נשיא could mean “women” or “the leader”; it is left transliterated. The rest of the Aramaic is translated as printed.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: And what Balaam the son of Beor answered him
Micah.english_translation: “How shall I execrate, whom the LORD hath not execrated?” (Numbers 23:8) — for I was not angry all those days.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: From Shittim unto Gilgal
Micah.english_translation: For you sinned against Me there. Know My righteous acts, that I did not withhold My goodness and My help from you until I brought you to Gilgal and conquered the land before you there.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: bow myself before God on high
Micah.english_translation: I will be bowed down.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: ten thousands of rivers of oil
Micah.english_translation: For meal-offerings.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: Shall I give my first-born for my transgression
Micah.english_translation: A sacrifice for my transgression.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: It hath been told thee, O man
Micah.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He, [has told] you, man, what is good for you to do.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: and to walk humbly
Micah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “Be modest in walking in the fear of your God.” Another explanation: “and walk humbly” — not like the attribute of the Holy One, blessed be He, is the attribute of flesh and blood. The attribute of flesh and blood: a person shames his fellow and comes to appease him, and says to him: I will not be reconciled to you until so-and-so and so-and-so come, before whom you shamed me. But the Holy One, blessed be He, desires only that one return to Him between himself and Him.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: Hark! the LORD crieth unto the city
Micah.english_translation: The voice of the prophets of HaShem to the city, proclaiming repentance to them.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: it is wisdom to have regard for Thy name
Micah.english_translation: And *tushiyah* — the prophet calls to them, to him who sees Your name, who sets his heart to contemplate and to see Your ways. And *tushiyah* refers back to the verse above it.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: Hear you the rod, and who hath appointed it
Micah.english_translation: Incline an ear and hear the rod of the punishment that will come down upon you, for the prophets warn you; and hear who it is that appoints that punishment, whether it is in his power to fulfill what he decrees. But Jonathan did not translate so.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: it is wisdom to have regard for Thy name
Micah.english_translation: (“And it is wisdom to have regard for Thy name.” From here [it is learned] that whoever recites each day a verse that begins and ends as his name begins and ends — the Torah saves him from Gehenna.)
Micah.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment; a phrase from the verse is used. It is printed in parentheses as an addition to Rashi.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: Are there yet the treasures of wickedness
Micah.english_translation: The *he* of *ha-esh* is vocalized with a patach because it expresses astonishment; and so its explanation: *od* is an expression of length of days. *Ha-esh* is like *ha-yesh*. And in Chronicles (1 Chronicles 2) we find *Ishai*, the father of David, in place of *Yishai*; here too *esh* is in place of *yesh*, and so (2 Samuel 14:19) *im esh le-hamin ule-hasmil* (“if there is to turn to the right hand or to the left”). And Targum Jonathan: “Is it so, that it will come up in your hearts that the house of the wicked will endure for length of days, and the treasures of the wicked?”
Micah.translator_note: Printed “1 Chronicles 2”; JPS has “Jesse” in that chapter (for example 1 Chronicles 2:13), and I could not confirm the spelling אישי there. For 2 Samuel 14:19 JPS reads “none can turn to the right hand or to the left.”

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: the scant measure that is abominable
Micah.english_translation: A small measure with which your wealthy men deceive the poor, and bring them to leanness (*razon*); and it is cursed (*ze’umah*) in the anger of the Holy One, blessed be He.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: I also do smite thee with a grievous wound
Micah.english_translation: I have made your blows incurable: strong, and painful, and desperate.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: I do make thee desolate because of thy sins
Micah.english_translation: To make you desolate for your sins.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: And thy sickness shall be in thine inward parts
Micah.english_translation: The food that you eat — I will bring a curse into it, in the bowels, and it will cause you sickness, so that you will be sick and go bowed down. And so he explains it in the Sifrei: Whence is it that even in the bowels? Scripture says, “and thy sickness shall be in thine inward parts” — in the portion *Ve-hayah ekev*, in the midrash on “the eyes of the LORD thy God are always upon it” (Deuteronomy 11:12). And Jonathan too translated so: “and it will be a sickness of *mata* in your bowels.”
Micah.translator_note: The Aramaic words מרע מתא could mean “sickness of the city” or “sickness of death”; they are left transliterated.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: And thou shalt conceive, but shalt not bring forth
Micah.english_translation: Your enemies who lead your sons and your daughters into captivity, and you will not rescue them; and if you rescue them, their end is the sword. And in the name of Rabbi Menachem I heard: “and you shall conceive” for the desire of intercourse, “and you shall not bring forth” — you will have no strength to emit semen; and if you emit them, its end is the sword; “I will give you.” And Targum Jonathan follows the first expression.
Micah.translator_note: The first explanation begins with only an object (“your enemies”) and no verb, and the last sentences are difficult as printed; translated literally.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: For the statutes of Omri are kept
Micah.english_translation: And I knew that you would not listen to Me, for all the statutes of Omri and Ahab will be kept by you and among you.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: And you shall bear the reproach of My people
Micah.english_translation: You will bear the iniquity of the reproach with which the idolaters reproach My people, for the Torah testified against them concerning this (Deuteronomy 25:14): “Thou shalt not have … diverse measures” — and they do not keep it.
Micah.translator_note: Rashi omits “in thy house” from his quotation of Deuteronomy 25:14.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: Woe is me!
Micah.english_translation: The prophet laments over himself: Woe is me that I was appointed a prophet at this time, when there are no righteous people in the generation.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: I am as the last of the summer fruits
Micah.english_translation: It is vocalized with a chataf-kamatz, which is not an agent form like *yoshev*, *omer*, but a *maf’al* form, like *osef ha-chasil* (Isaiah 33:4) — like the gathering of summer; and they are the last figs (*sofei te’enim*), which are bad. And so Jonathan translated: “like the last of the summer.”
Micah.translator_note: For Isaiah 33:4 JPS reads “And your spoil is gathered as the caterpillar gathereth.”

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: As the grape gleanings of the vintage
Micah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “like gleanings after the picking.”

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: There is no cluster to eat
Micah.english_translation: As its Targum: “there is no man in whom there are good deeds.”

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: Nor first-ripe fig which my soul desireth
Micah.english_translation: A good fig that ripens in its season, as its Targum: “the good ones, the desire of my soul.”

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: the upright among men is no more
Micah.english_translation: There is no upright man among people.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: They hunt every man his brother with a net
Micah.english_translation: They hunt with their net and their snare.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: Their hands are upon that which is evil to do it diligently
Micah.english_translation: For the reward of the evil of your hands you hope that He will do good to you.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: The prince asketh
Micah.english_translation: A bribe.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: and the judge is ready for a reward
Micah.english_translation: The one who judges the case — he too, for payment — says to his fellow judge, when he is a robber and liable in the case: Pay me my due in this, and I will acquit you in another case.
Micah.translator_note: The sentence is difficult as printed (“when he is a robber and liable”); translated literally.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: And the great man, he uttereth the evil desire of his soul
Micah.english_translation: The king or the prince says in judgment the desire of his soul. *Havvat nafsho* — a matter that comes to be according to his wish. And *le-nafsho* is like “My soul is not toward this people” (Jeremiah 15). And so Targum Jonathan: “the desires of his soul.”
Micah.translator_note: Printed “Jeremiah 15” is Jeremiah 15:1 (JPS: “yet My mind could not be toward this people”).

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: Thus they weave it together
Micah.english_translation: They made it a braid of sin among the three of them, like cart-ropes of sin (*avotot ha-eglah chata’ah*), for the cord (*avot*) is threefold. So I found in the Jerusalem Targum: “we made it like a braid of sins.”
Micah.translator_note: Rashi’s phrase echoes Isaiah 5:18 (JPS: “And sin as it were with a cart rope”).

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: The best of them is as a brier
Micah.english_translation: Targum: “the good one among them, it is hard to get out of his hands, as from a briar.” It is hard to escape from his hand, like the thorns that get tangled in wool.
Micah.translator_note: The Aramaic is translated as printed; the words כד מן are unclear.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: The most upright is worse than a thorn hedge
Micah.english_translation: The most upright among them is worse than a hedge of thorns; and *mesukhah* is like “I will take away the hedge thereof” (Isaiah 5).
Micah.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 5” is Isaiah 5:5.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: The day of thy watchmen, even thy visitation, is come
Micah.english_translation: The day on which you look for good — your visitation will come.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: Now shall be their perplexity
Micah.english_translation: Targum: *irbuleihon* (“their confusion”), like “They are entangled” (Exodus 14) — their tumult.
Micah.translator_note: Printed “Exodus 14” is Exodus 14:3.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: Trust you not in a friend
Micah.english_translation: As it sounds; but our Rabbis explained it as applying to Above: Do not sin and say, the Holy One, blessed be He, is our friend, and He will forgive us.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: from her that lieth in thy bosom
Micah.english_translation: Your soul — it will testify against you.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: Keep the doors of thy mouth
Micah.english_translation: The words of your mouth, the openings of your mouth.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: I will look unto the LORD
Micah.english_translation: The prophet says so.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: Rejoice not against me, O mine enemy
Micah.english_translation: Babylon, and the guilty city, Rome. (Another version: Babylon and Persia, the guilty.)

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: The day for building thy walls
Micah.english_translation: It refers back to “her that says to me” (verse 10), and she still says to me: “The day for building thy walls” — the day for which you hope, that day will be far removed; its decree, its time, will be long, and it will never come.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: There shall be a day when they shall come unto thee
Micah.english_translation: The prophet says: That day, over which you mock, saying: It is annulled and gone — that day is guarded and preserved and is not annulled. “And to thee shall it come” — Babylon will come to destroy you.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: From Assyria
Micah.english_translation: Which is the head of our *mar’enu*.
Micah.translator_note: The last word (למרענו) could mean “our pasture” or “our harm”; the sentence is obscure as printed, so the word is left transliterated.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: even to the cities of Egypt
Micah.english_translation: That is, “and as far as the cities of Mazor.” And Jonathan translated: “and from Chormini the Great.”

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: from sea to sea
Micah.english_translation: And those who dwell on the last sea, which is in the west.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: from mountain to mountain
Micah.english_translation: Like “and those who dwell in the mountain”; and Jonathan did not translate so.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: and from mountain to mountain
Micah.english_translation: The prophet announces to Israel that there is a hidden day, prepared for building the fences of their ruins; on that day will be far removed and annulled from you the statute of the decrees of the Babylonians and the Persians.
Micah.translator_note: The source gives the lemma “The day for building thy walls” (Micah 7:11) for this comment, which stands under 7:12; a phrase from 7:12 is used. The syntax of “yirchak ve-yevatel” is ambiguous as printed; I take “the statute of the decrees” as its subject.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: There shall be a day when they shall come unto thee
Micah.english_translation: At that time the exiles of Israel who are from Assyria will be gathered, etc.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: And the land shall be desolate
Micah.english_translation: The land of the Babylonians and Persians.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: That dwell solitarily
Micah.english_translation: That he may dwell in security, alone.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: as a forest in the midst of the fruitful field
Micah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “who were *tzadin* in the forest shall dwell as in Carmel.” Those who were desolate like forests shall dwell alone in the midst of Carmel, which is an inhabited place. And it is possible to explain: those who dwell alone in forests will not be seen by the beasts of the field, as in the midst of Carmel.
Micah.translator_note: The Aramaic word צדין is left as printed; I could not confirm its sense here. The rest of the Aramaic is translated as printed. Audit 4: the Aramaic quotation was checked against Targum Jonathan/the Ketuvim Targum (Mikraot Gedolot, Sefaria) at MIC 7:14 and reads as quoted; the meaning of the unclear word, if noted above, is still unresolved.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: Like crawling things of the earth
Micah.english_translation: They are serpents that crawl on their bellies in the dust of the earth.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: they shall come trembling out of their close places
Micah.english_translation: They will tremble from the great pressure of their bonds (*isureihem*) and the prison (*misger*) of their confinement.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: Thou wilt show faithfulness to Jacob
Micah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “The truth of Jacob will be given to his sons, as Thou didst covenant with him in Beth-el; the goodness of Abraham to his seed after him, as Thou didst covenant with him at the Covenant between the Pieces; Thou wilt remember for us the binding of Isaac.” Thou wilt give us in truth what Thou promised to Jacob — make true for us Thy words that Thou promised to Jacob, “for I will not leave thee” (Genesis 28).
Micah.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 28” is Genesis 28:15.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: mercy to Abraham
Micah.english_translation: The reward of the kindness that belongs to Abraham, who commanded his sons “to keep the way of the LORD, to do righteousness and justice” (Genesis 18:19). And therefore it does not say “and kindness” but “kindness”: the truth (*ha-emet*) — that Thou wilt make true for us the promise to Jacob — this will be the payment of the reward of Abraham’s kindness.
Micah.translator_note: The phrase חסד האמת is difficult as printed; translated literally.

Micah.english_lemma_JPS: As Thou hast sworn unto our fathers
Micah.english_translation: At the binding of Isaac: “By Myself have I sworn, saith the LORD, because thou hast done …” etc. (Genesis 22:16).

Nahum.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: *matal*, the cup of the curse, to make Nineveh drink.
Nahum.translator_note: The Aramaic word מטל is left transliterated, since its sense here (“burden” or “because of”) is not certain. The rest of the Aramaic is translated as printed.

Nahum.english_lemma_JPS: The book of the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite
Nahum.english_translation: *Chazon* is vocalized with a kamatz because it is not attached [to the following word], and it is not like the *chazon* of Isaiah, which is vocalized with a chataf-patach. And so is the explanation of “the book of the vision”: a [book of] vision about it was already written, and that is the prophecy of Jonah son of Amittai; and now Nahum the Elkoshite again prophesied about it this burden. Elkosh was the name of his city. And so Targum Jonathan: “Formerly Jonah son of Amittai prophesied against it, and it repented of its sins; and when it added again to sin, there prophesied against it again Nahum, who is from Beit Elkosh.”

Nahum.english_lemma_JPS: The LORD is a jealous and avenging God
Nahum.english_translation: Nahum prophesied concerning the seed of Sennacherib, in the days of Manasseh, as is found in Seder Olam.

Nahum.english_lemma_JPS: The LORD avengeth and is full of wrath
Nahum.english_translation: Since He took vengeance for Israel on their enemies, and even now He is still avenging and a master of wrath, and in the future He will take vengeance on His adversaries who destroyed His land and exiled His people; and He reserves His enmity for the Babylonians. And R. Sh. says: These three vengeances correspond to the three exiles in which Sennacherib exiled Israel, as is found in Seder Olam.
Nahum.translator_note: The abbreviation ר"ש is left as printed; it is not clear whether it stands for R. Shimon or R. Shimshon.

Nahum.english_lemma_JPS: The LORD is long-suffering, and great in power
Nahum.english_translation: He is great in power, and the ability is in His hand to take vengeance, and the fact that He did not hasten His vengeance is because He is long-suffering; but in any case “will by no means clear the guilty.”

Nahum.english_lemma_JPS: in the whirlwind and in the storm is His way
Nahum.english_translation: They are His messengers to take vengeance on His enemies, as it is said of Egypt, “a strong east wind” (Exodus 14:21); and of the generation of the Flood, “By the breath of God they perish” (Job 4:9); and of Tyre it is said (Ezekiel 26), “The east wind hath broken thee.”
Nahum.translator_note: Printed “Ezekiel 26” is Ezekiel 27:26.

Nahum.english_lemma_JPS: the clouds are the dust of His feet
Nahum.english_translation: This too is a way of His vengeance: “the LORD looked forth upon the host of the Egyptians through the pillar of fire and of cloud” (Exodus 14:24); “As for her, a cloud shall cover her” (Ezekiel 30:18).
As it sounds; and it is also an example concerning the idolaters, who are likened to waters, as it is said, “the rushing of nations, that rush like the rushing of mighty waters” (Isaiah 17:12).
Here he prophesied that the Holy One, blessed be He, would make Nebuchadnezzar king (Jeremiah 25) in the days of Jehoiakim, and he would give Assyria and all the lands to the sword.
The dwelling-places of the good.
The Sages of Israel explained it as concerning the kinds of delicacies that Solomon planted in the Holy Temple, which were of gold, and when the nations entered the Sanctuary they dried up.
The kings and the princes of the Chaldeans will fear His decree.

Nahum.english_lemma_JPS: the earth is upheaved at His presence
Nahum.english_translation: A rising of smoke.

Nahum.english_lemma_JPS: His fury is poured out like fire
Nahum.english_translation: It reached the earth, like “and the rain was not poured upon the earth” (Exodus 9:33).

Nahum.english_lemma_JPS: the rocks are broken asunder before Him
Nahum.english_translation: From fear of Him.

And even at the time when He takes vengeance on His enemies, His mercies do not cease from doing good to those who fear Him; and not like the attribute of flesh and blood, who, when he is occupied with one, is not free for the other, as it is said (ibid. 15), “The LORD is a man of war, the LORD is His name,” as it is in our Mekhilta.
Nahum.translator_note: Printed “ibid. 15” is Exodus 15:3.

Nahum.english_translation: The needs of those who take refuge in Him.
And in a flooding wrath.

Nahum.english_lemma_JPS: make a full end of the place thereof
Nahum.english_translation: Of the earth; and this refers back to “and the earth is upheaved at His presence,” as was said above.

Nahum.english_lemma_JPS: He will make a full end
Nahum.english_translation: For Nineveh; and for the kings of Assyria He will not repeat it another time.

Nahum.english_lemma_JPS: though they be like tangled thorns
Nahum.english_translation: That is, suddenly their blow will come upon them, and they will not come down from their glory little by little, for while the thorns and the brambles are tangled, they are rooted strongly.

Nahum.english_lemma_JPS: be drunken according to their drink
Nahum.english_translation: And while they are still at their banquets and their rejoicing. And some interpret “for ad sirim” as an expression of removal.
That has become full, and its ripening is complete, and it is dry.
*אשובי"ר* in French; and so *melo’atkha*, the fullness of the seed.
Nahum.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Nahum 1:10 (“herbe remplie,” grass that is full, that is, completely ripe and ready to dry), in the form אשובייר, which he reads *asovid* (a past participle of *asovir*, “to satisfy”); the printed form (אשובי"ר) matches.

Nahum.english_lemma_JPS: Out of thee came he forth
Nahum.english_translation: Nineveh.

Sennacherib, who devised evil, imagined that he would destroy the dwelling below and above. One verse says (2 Kings 19:23), “and I have entered into his farthest lodge,” and one verse says (Isaiah 37:24), “and I have entered into his farthest height”: first I will destroy the dwelling below, and finally the dwelling above, as is said in Chelek (folio 94).
Nahum.translator_note: “Chelek” is left as printed; the printed text gives no tractate.

Nahum.english_lemma_JPS: in full strength, and likewise many
Nahum.english_translation: The Targum of Jonathan settles well upon the verse: “if they are complete in counsel,” that all of them are alike in one agreement; and so “if they are very many,” the men of Nineveh, your enemies, Jerusalem; and so even if they cut the Tigris and cross the Euphrates to besiege it, they will not succeed, for I have afflicted you and will not afflict you again. And further I heard: “if whole” — the men of Nineveh in their greatness; and so if they are still many and more honored; and so *nagozu* and *avar*; and so “I will cut them (*agizam*) and make them pass (*a’avirem*)”; behold, this is like “But the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied” (Exodus 1).
Nahum.translator_note: The explanation is difficult as printed; translated literally. The Aramaic quotation is translated as printed.

Nahum.english_lemma_JPS: though I have afflicted thee, I will afflict thee no more
Nahum.english_translation: I will afflict you this time completely and decisively, and I will not trouble you any more. And our Rabbis expounded it concerning the act of charity, in tractate Gittin; but it is not in the order of the rest of the prophecy.

Nahum.english_lemma_JPS: will I break his yoke from off thee
Nahum.english_translation: The Shekhinah says so to the prophet, who is an Israelite: I will break the yoke of Assyria from upon you and from upon My people.
Now the speech turns to the king of Assyria.

Nahum.english_lemma_JPS: no more of thy name be sown
Nahum.english_translation: No king will arise from you.

Nahum.english_lemma_JPS: Out of the house of thy god will I cut off
Nahum.english_translation: And I will make the house of your god your grave; there you will flee to escape, and there you will be killed, as it is written that your father was killed — in the house of Nisroch his god.
In My eyes.
Nahum.translator_note: The source lemma is כי קלות (“for thou art become worthless”), which JPS places at the start of 2:1; a phrase from the JPS verse is used.

Nahum.english_translation: That you vowed to the Holy One, blessed be He, if He would save you from the hand of Sennacherib king of Assyria, for now you have been saved.

Nahum.english_lemma_JPS: the wicked one shall no more pass through thee
Nahum.english_translation: That worthless one (*Belial*).
He and his seed.

Nahum.english_lemma_JPS: A maul is come up before thy face
Nahum.english_translation: The scatterer who came up against you to the land of Judah in the days of Hezekiah — now he is *natzor mitzurah*: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, who is besieging him.
Look, O man of Judah, at the junction of the ways (literally, “the mother of the ways”) and see those going to besiege him, and let your loins be strengthened, and be mighty in strength.
As it was before.
They plundered them and emptied them; the expression of *bekikah* (emptying) alludes to a vine.

Nahum.english_lemma_JPS: The shield of his mighty men
Nahum.english_translation: Of Nebuchadnezzar, who are besieging Assyria.
They are reddened. And the men of their host are dyed crimson (literally, “wormed”), clothed in scarlet.

Nahum.english_lemma_JPS: The chariots are fire of steel in the day of his preparation
Nahum.english_translation: On the day that he is ready to go out with the army, he polishes his iron chariot. And I do not know what *plados* is; and I say that it is a kind of tool that polishes iron well; and some interpret *plados* as an expression of *lapid esh* (a firebrand), by way of reversal.

Nahum.english_lemma_JPS: the cypress spears are made to quiver
Nahum.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “and the great ones of their camp are clothed in colors.”
Wrapped; and similar to it is “the pendants, and the bracelets, and the veils” (Isaiah 3:19), and in the language of the Mishnah we learned: *madiyot re’ulot* (tractate Shabbat, folio 65, ע"ש).
Nahum.translator_note: The abbreviation ע"ש is left as printed.

Nahum.english_translation: They conduct themselves with madness.

Targum Jonathan: “the sound of the clashing of their weapons is heard.” And it is from the expression of *ve-hesheku ha-yekavim* (Joel 2:24), *ke-mashak gevim* (Isaiah 33:4) — an expression of making a sound.
Nahum.translator_note: Rashi cites these words for their root, so they are left transliterated. Printed “Joel 2:24” (JPS: “the vats shall overflow”) and “Isaiah 33:4” (JPS: “As locusts leap do they leap upon it”).

Nahum.english_lemma_JPS: They run to and fro like the lightnings
Nahum.english_translation: They shake those who hear, like those lightning flashes that trouble the creatures. So Targum Jonathan.

Nahum.english_lemma_JPS: He bethinketh himself of his worthies
Nahum.english_translation: The king of Assyria [remembers] his nobles and his mighty men, and imagines in his heart to go out and fight; and they stumble in their going.

Nahum.english_lemma_JPS: They make haste to the wall thereof
Nahum.english_translation: To flee, to run to the wall of the city. Every word that requires a lamed at its beginning, he put a he at its end.

Targum Jonathan: “they will build towers.” And it is possible to explain: “and the one who covers was prepared” — the king armed himself with his weapons, like *mimshach ha-sokhekh*, an expression of “ruler.”
Nahum.translator_note: Rashi’s phrase *mimshach ha-sokhekh* is from Ezekiel 28:14 (JPS: “the far-covering cherub”).

Nahum.english_lemma_JPS: The gates of the rivers are opened
Nahum.english_translation: The gates of the city that are on the side of the rivers.
It trembled and shook from the force of ballista stones (*avnei balistra*) thrown at its walls, which is called *בומ"א*.
Nahum.translator_note: The printed text does not say what language בומ"א is; I did not find it in Darmesteter, so it is left as printed.

Nahum.english_translation: She is the queen who stands at the right of the king, as it is said, “At thy right hand doth stand the queen” (Psalms 45:10).
Openly she went into captivity and was taken up out of the city.

Nahum.english_lemma_JPS: her handmaids moan as with the voice of doves
Nahum.english_translation: They conduct themselves in lamentation like the voice of doves that lament. *Menahagot* — *שרימייצנ"ט* in French.
Nahum.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Nahum 2:8 (“se lamentant,” lamenting), in forms such as שדמיינט and שידימיינט; the printed form (שרימייצנ"ט) differs in spelling, with ר and צ in place of ד.

Nahum.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: They strike their hands upon their hearts, as one strikes upon drums.
From the day it was made, it has dwelt in tranquility and none disturbs it (*menid*), like a pool of gathered waters that do not move from their place.
Now, from the great pressure, they learned to flee, and they flee.
They say to them, and no one turns his heart to listen and to stand.

Nahum.english_lemma_JPS: Take you the spoil of silver
Nahum.english_translation: You who come against Nineveh.
There is no reckoning.
For their treasuries — because the silver and gold put in a treasury are put by count (*tokhen*), as you say, “the money that was weighed out” (2 Kings 12:12).

An expression of heaviness, like “Make thyself many as the canker-worm” (below, 3), the expression of sweeping the house (*mekhabed ha-bayit*) — *אשקוונ"ט* in French; and “to sweep them from all vessels of desire”; and so Targum Jonathan: *sufu* from all kinds of desirable things. *Kavod* is like *zachor* and *shamor*.
Nahum.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Nahum 2:10 (“balayant … tous les objets précieux,” sweeping … all the precious objects), in the form אשקובנט, which he reads *escovant*; the printed form (אשקוונ"ט) has ו in place of ב. Printed “below, 3” is Nahum 3:15. The Aramaic word ספו (*sufu*) is left transliterated; I could not confirm its sense here. Audit 4: the Aramaic quotation was checked against Targum Jonathan/the Ketuvim Targum (Mikraot Gedolot, Sefaria) at NAM 2:10 and reads as quoted; the meaning of the unclear word, if noted above, is still unresolved.

Nahum.english_translation: Empty.
And emptied by those who empty (*bokekim*).
Breached in her walls — *אישברטיר"א* in French.
Nahum.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Nahum 2:11 (“ville … forcée,” a city broken into), in forms such as אישפריטירא, אישכרטידא and אישברישידא; the printed form (אישברטיר"א) is close to the form אישפריטירא that he gives from one manuscript.

Nahum.english_translation: Failure of the knees, like *le-fukah u-lemikhshol* (1 Samuel 25).
Nahum.translator_note: Printed “1 Samuel 25” is 1 Samuel 25:31 (JPS: “no stumblingblock unto thee, nor offence of heart”).

Nahum.english_translation: Blackness, like a pot.

Nahum.english_lemma_JPS: Where is the den of the lions
Nahum.english_translation: It is a lament over Nineveh, which was the dwelling of kings, mighty and strong as lions.

Nahum.english_lemma_JPS: Where the lion and the lioness walked
Nahum.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “the place where kings used to go and leave their sons there, like a lion who dwells in security.”

Nahum.english_lemma_JPS: The lion did tear in pieces enough for his whelps
Nahum.english_translation: As its Targum: its kings used to bring much spoil, until there was enough for the members of their household.
Animals for the need of his lionesses; that is, he increases his treasuries for his sons.
Targum Jonathan: “and they fill their treasuries with plunder.”

Nahum.english_lemma_JPS: I will burn her chariots in the smoke
Nahum.english_translation: The multitude of chariots in it — *קרטדי"ן* in French. The extra he is a reversal of the language, for the abundance of chariots; and so “to the pot whose filth is therein” (Ezekiel 24:6) — much filth.
Nahum.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Nahum 2:14 (“son armée de chariots,” its host of chariots, the Hebrew word being collective), in forms such as קרדיץ and קראייאיץ; the printed form (קרטדי"ן) is similar, ending in נ instead of צ.

Nahum.english_lemma_JPS: the voice of thy messengers shall no more be heard
Nahum.english_translation: The voice of your messengers, as Rabshakeh and his companions, the messengers of Assyria, did before (Isaiah 37): “and cried with a loud voice in the Jews’ language.”
Nahum.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 37” is Isaiah 36:13.

Nahum.english_translation: Robbery, which one tears away (*mefarko*) from the hand of its owner.
From within it, always.
For striking horses was always heard in it.
The wheels of the chariots.
Leaping and bounding; and so “the prancings, the prancings of their mighty ones” (Judges 5:22).
*רולימל"א* in French, for a knife and a sword are called *lahav*, like (ibid. 4) “And the haft went in after the blade.”
Nahum.translator_note: Printed “ibid. 4” is Judges 3:22, which reads in JPS “And the haft also went in after the blade”; Rashi’s wording omits “also.” Old French: Darmesteter lists this word at Nahum 3:3 (“la lame (du glaive),” the blade of the sword), in forms such as אלמילא; the printed form (רולימל"א) differs in its first letters.

Nahum.english_translation: A spear that is polished and gleams, light coming forth from it — *פלנדו"ר* in French.
Nahum.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Nahum 3:3 (“l’éclat (de la lance),” the gleam of the spear) in the form פלנדור; the printed form matches.

Nahum.english_translation: They used to multiply corpses, and there was no reckoning of the carcasses of its dead cast down in it, until those passing by were stumbling over the corpses of the slain.
Because of the flatteries of a city that knew how to entice the heart of the kings of the earth to join with them, and in the end they would subdue them beneath her.
They are the hems of a woman’s garments.
Your uncovering, like (Micah 1) “in nakedness and shame.”
Nahum.translator_note: Printed “Micah 1” is Micah 1:11. Rashi’s printed form is עריה בשת; the verse reads ערית בשת, and JPS renders it “in nakedness and shame.”

Nahum.english_translation: Filthy garments that make you loathsome, according to the context, since it likened her to a harlot; so the verse speaks.
As dung; an expression of “and he shall take away its crop with the feathers thereof” (Leviticus 1:16).
Will distance himself from you.

And in what do you trust — in your wealth and in your might? Are you indeed greater than No? It is Alexandria of Egypt. *Amon* is an expression of *pedagogue*: the great No, which was the nurse of the kings of Egypt, for they were raised in it [and] they reigned.
Nahum.translator_note: The Aramaic words דמרבי בה מלכו are difficult; they are translated tentatively. The Aramaic is otherwise translated as printed.

Nahum.english_translation: The sea was a rampart and a wall for her — *shura* and *bar shura*.

Nahum.english_lemma_JPS: Ethiopia and Egypt were thy strength
Nahum.english_translation: Cushites were a strength to her.

Nahum.english_lemma_JPS: Put and Lubim were thy helpers
Nahum.english_translation: And the Putites and the Lubim, who were your helpers — they too were in her host.
She too went into exile; nevertheless her greatness did not stand before Nebuchadnezzar.
They were bound; an expression of *retukot* of silver (Isaiah 40), “make the *ha-ratok*” (Ezekiel 7) — chains.
Nahum.translator_note: Rashi cites these words for their root, so they are left transliterated. Printed “Isaiah 40” is Isaiah 40:19 (JPS: “casting silver chains”); printed “Ezekiel 7” is Ezekiel 7:23 (JPS: “Make the chain”).

Nahum.english_translation: Chains.
Even you, according to your greatness, will be drunken like her with the cup of staggering, and you will be hidden.

Nahum.english_lemma_JPS: All thy fortresses shall be like fig-trees with the first-ripe figs
Nahum.english_translation: All your fortified cities will be easy to conquer and to plunder what is in them, like fig trees; and when they have with them first-ripe ones, the ripened ones among them, then when the tree is shaken the first-ripe fall into the mouths of the eaters.
Fig trees.
That if they are shaken forcibly by the hand of a man.

Nahum.english_lemma_JPS: Draw thee water for the siege
Nahum.english_translation: A city that people come to besiege — the people of the city gather for themselves much water into it, in barrels, to drink in the days of the siege, when there are no cisterns in it.

Nahum.english_lemma_JPS: Go into the clay, and tread the mortar
Nahum.english_translation: It, to make bricks from it in order to strengthen with it the breaches of the walls.
Take in your hand the mould that is made for the form of the bricks, to make bricks in it.

Nahum.english_lemma_JPS: Make thyself many as the canker-worm
Nahum.english_translation: With brooms it destroyed.

The one that finishes and consumes all the greenery of the field. And some interpret *hitkabed ka-yelek* as “you will be covered with a heaviness of troops like the *yelek*,” and *hitkabedi* is an expression of “a heavy people.”
Nahum.translator_note: The sentence is brief and elliptical as printed; translated literally. Rashi’s word ילק is rendered “canker-worm” in JPS of this chapter.

Nahum.english_translation: They will be swift to go out for trade, like the *yelek* that spreads out and flies.

Your princes. And the mem is a root-letter, part of the word, like the mem of *mishmarteka* and of *mishma’atkha* and of *min’alekha*; and sometimes it falls away from it, as in “*nezir echav*” (Genesis 49), and so “*nezireha*, her princes” (Lamentations 4).
