Nahum.translator_note: Rashi cites these words for their root, so they are left transliterated. Printed “Genesis 49” is Genesis 49:26 (JPS: “the prince among his brethren”); printed “Lamentations 4” is Lamentations 4:7 (JPS: “Her princes”).

Nahum.english_translation: Those appointed over you.
Like the troops of locusts (*gova’ei govai*), *קומלנגשטדי"ץ* in French.
Nahum.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Nahum 3:17 (“comme les armées de sauterelles,” like the armies of locusts), in forms such as קומלנגושטדיץ; the printed form (קומלנגשטדי"ץ) matches apart from the missing ו.

Nahum.english_lemma_JPS: Which camp in the walls in the cold day
Nahum.english_translation: So is the way of the locust and the fly, the *hasil* and the *yelek*: in the time of cold they cling to the walls, and when heat comes they wander off from there and go away; so will all your people go into exile.
Nahum.translator_note: Rashi’s word חסיל is left transliterated; the printed text does not say which insect he means.

Nahum.english_translation: And moves about.

Nahum.english_lemma_JPS: their place is not known where they are
Nahum.english_translation: Where they are, and where they have gone.
An expression of slumber.
They are unable to rise.

*Nafoshu* is like *nafotzu*; and all the letters that come from one place of articulation interchange with one another — zayin, shin, samekh, tzadi — all of them come from the end of the tongue and the edges of the teeth.

Nahum.english_lemma_JPS: There is no assuaging of thy hurt
Nahum.english_translation: There is no one distressed over your breaking, for all rejoice. *Keheh* is an expression of an obscure matter.
To rejoice.

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: The burden which Habakkuk the prophet did see
Habakkuk.english_translation: The burden of prophecy — that which he bore and received through the Holy Spirit.

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: How long, O LORD, shall I cry
Habakkuk.english_translation: He foresaw through the Holy Spirit that Nebuchadnezzar was destined to reign over the realm and to be a distress to Israel, as it is said in his prophecy (below), “For, lo, I raise up the Chaldeans,” etc.; and over this he complained and prayed.
Habakkuk.translator_note: Rashi’s idiom למלוך בכיפה is rendered tentatively as “to reign over the realm.” “Below” is Habakkuk 1:6.

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: I cry out unto Thee of violence
Habakkuk.english_translation: I will mention before You the violence done to me, and You are not saving.
Plunder and violence.
This mischief You behold and do not help.
And this is Nebuchadnezzar, who bears strife and contention, existing, enduring and prospering.
The one who bears strife and contention will endure; so Targum Jonathan.
Because of this, that Israel see his success, the Torah will lapse and pass away from them, and they will listen to him and bow to the image in the plain of Dura.
The law in its truth.
Surrounds, like “Strong bulls of Bashan have beset me round” (Psalms 22:13).
Habakkuk.translator_note: Printed reference is complete; Psalms 22:13 reads in JPS “Strong bulls of Bashan have beset me round.”

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: you will not believe though it be told you
Habakkuk.english_translation: This is for you: that I raise up the Chaldeans, the people that was not fit to be created, as it is said (Isaiah 23), “this is the people that was not” — they are one of three things that the Holy One, blessed be He, so to speak, regrets having created; and now he shall arise, bitter and impetuous, to run and go to the breadths of the lands of all the nations.
Habakkuk.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 23” is Isaiah 23:13. The closing phrase paraphrases Habakkuk 1:6 (JPS: “That bitter and impetuous nation, That march through the breadth of the earth”).

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: Their law and their majesty proceed from themselves
Habakkuk.english_translation: From them come judges, from them kings, who cast burden and fear upon all. *Mishpatim* — *justice* [printed יושטיצי"א] in French.
Habakkuk.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Habakkuk 1:7 (“sa justice,” his justice), in forms such as יושטיצא; the reading is *justice* (REJ transcription *Jousliçe*, read *joustice*); the printed form (יושטיצי"א) matches apart from an extra י.

Habakkuk.english_translation: His horsemen are many.

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: They come all of them for violence
Habakkuk.english_translation: To plunder and to spoil.

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: Their faces are set eagerly as the east wind
Habakkuk.english_translation: An expression of *hag’imini na* (Genesis 24), “He swalloweth the ground” (Job 39): running at a run for a short while a stretch of land, as though he swallowed and drank the land before him; and here too *megammat paneihem* is the swallowing, the inhaling, of their faces, resembling the east wind, the strongest of the winds. So Targum Jonathan translated it.
Habakkuk.translator_note: Rashi cites these words for their root, so they are left transliterated. Printed “Genesis 24” is Genesis 24:17 (JPS: “Give me to drink”); printed “Job 39” is Job 39:24.

Habakkuk.english_translation: He makes sport of them. And every expression of *kelasah* is an expression of speech — those who speak of it, whether for good or for bad — *parlediç* [printed פרלרי"ץ] in French.
Habakkuk.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Habakkuk 1:10 (“il sera parlé,” it will be spoken of), in forms such as פרלדיץ; the reading *parlediç* is from Darmesteter’s footnote (“Lire : parlediç”); the printed form (פרלרי"ץ) differs by ר in place of ד.

Habakkuk.english_translation: Like *sechok* (laughter), like *mishmar*, *mistor*.
Habakkuk.translator_note: Rashi gives no further explanation of the examples.

Habakkuk.english_translation: If his enemy is in a strong fortress, he laughs at it.

Upon it with the multitude of his troops, each one carries a burden of earth, and behold it is before the wall a high mound, and they fight with it against the city; and that is the pouring out of a mound, for all of them are translated: *ve-yitzbor alah malita*; and this too is an expression of the *millo* that was in the City of David, which is a high mound, and they fight with it, for on its top is a built tower, and its slope slopes to the sides, and around the bottom of it is a low wall to keep the earth from falling.
Habakkuk.translator_note: The sentence is difficult as printed; translated literally. The Aramaic is translated as printed.

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: Even they who impute their might unto their god
Habakkuk.english_translation: Then, upon seeing that his way prospers, a spirit passes and crosses over him, a spirit of guilt; and what is the spirit? This is his strength: this strength he gives to his god, and says, “My god made for me all this might.”

The prophet said: And You — why are You silent about all this? Are You not from of old, my God, my Holy One, etc.? And as for what is written “we shall not die” — it is one of the emendations of the Scribes in Scripture, for Scripture refers to the Shekhinah; and so (Malachi 1:13) “and you have snuffed at it,” and so many that are explained in Sifrei. And according to the emendation of the Scribes this is its explanation: Are You not my God from of old, my Holy One? Do not give [us] to die by his hand.
Habakkuk.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment; a phrase from the JPS verse is used. The reference “in Sifrei” (בספרי) could also mean “in my book”; it is left as Sifrei. In Malachi 1:13 JPS reads “And you have snuffed at it”; Rashi’s printed form is אותו.

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: O LORD, Thou hast ordained them for judgment
Habakkuk.english_translation: I know that You did not set him up for this except to judge those who rebel against You; but in any case why should all this endure? Is it not
Habakkuk.translator_note: The printed text breaks off here.

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: Thou that art of eyes too pure to behold evil
Habakkuk.english_translation: You are [too pure] from seeing evil.
Habakkuk.translator_note: The sentence is elliptical as printed; the bracketed words are my understanding of it.

Habakkuk.english_translation: Like “and to look on mischief.”
That he blinds the eyes of Zedekiah.

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: makest men as the fishes of the sea
Habakkuk.english_translation: Before Nebuchadnezzar, ownerless like the fish of the sea, for whoever wishes to catch, catches of them.

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: They take up all of them with the angle
Habakkuk.english_translation: All mankind — this is Nebuchadnezzar — he brought up with his hook.
An expression of “gathereth in harvest” (Proverbs 10), “the barns are broken down” (Joel 1).
Habakkuk.translator_note: Rashi cites these words for their root. Printed “Proverbs 10” is Proverbs 10:5, which reads in JPS “gathereth in summer”; Rashi’s printed wording is בקציר. Printed “Joel 1” is Joel 1:17.

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: Therefore they sacrifice unto their net
Habakkuk.english_translation: To idolatry, for he says that it subdues everything before him.

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: by them their portion is fat
Habakkuk.english_translation: Like *bahem*: on their account.
Fat.

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: Shall they therefore empty their net
Habakkuk.english_translation: There are many expressions of astonishment of this kind, like “Did I reveal Myself” of Eli (1 Samuel 2), “Seest thou?” (ibid. 2 15); here too: is it so in your eyes that for this reason he prospers, that at every moment he empties his net upon all and hunts prey? *Yarik* is like “Draw out also the spear” (Psalms 35), “he led forth his trained men” (Genesis 14) — he arms himself with his net.
Habakkuk.translator_note: The phrase יש תמיהות הרבה המתקיימת is translated freely. Printed “1 Samuel 2” is 1 Samuel 2:27; printed “ibid. 2 15” is 2 Samuel 15:27; “Psalms 35” is 35:3; “Genesis 14” is 14:14.

Habakkuk.english_translation: Habakkuk drew a circle and stood in the midst of it and said: I will not move from here until I hear what He will speak with me about this my question — why does He look on and see the success of the wicked.
Habakkuk.translator_note: The source lemma (על משמרתי אעמדה) is the end of JPS 1:17; a phrase from the JPS verse of this id is used.

Habakkuk.english_translation: To those who come to argue before me.
That they reprove me, to my face, that one should question the attribute of justice. *Tokhachat* — *mon aprovement* [printed מונאיפרובמנ"ט] in French (“my reproof”).
Habakkuk.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Habakkuk 2:1 (“le reproche qu’on m’adresse,” the reproach addressed to me), in forms such as מון אפרובמינט; the reading is *mon aprovement*, from Darmesteter’s footnote; the printed form (מונאיפרובמנ"ט) matches apart from an extra י. The words בפני שיש are difficult; translated literally.

Habakkuk.english_translation: That was revealed to you, and explain it well upon the tablets, so that one who reads it may run to read it quickly and not stumble; and this is the vision that you shall write.

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: For the vision is yet for the appointed time
Habakkuk.english_translation: There is yet destined to arise a prophet at the end of years, to whom a vision will be revealed as to when the appointed time will be of the fall of Babylon and the redemption of Israel.
And He spoke what He would say to him about the end of Babylon, when seventy years are completed for Babylon; and it will not fail.

To come, that the appointed time is prolonged for you — wait for it, for it will not be delayed at all beyond the seventy. And further it can be explained: if the prophet tarries to come — and that was Jeremiah. And Targum Jonathan: “It is written: prophecy, and explained upon the book of the Torah.” He translated “write” like “it is written”: it was already alluded to (in the Torah), “Then shall the land be paid her sabbaths” (Leviticus 26:34): Israel spoiled seventy sabbatical years and did not release the land, and corresponding to them they were exiled from it seventy years; and so it says (in Chronicles, at the end of the second), “until the land had been paid her sabbaths; for as long as she lay desolate she kept sabbath, to fulfil threescore and ten years” (2 Chronicles 36:21). And so you find (Ezekiel 4:5) “And I have given thee the years of their iniquity, three hundred and ninety days; each day for a year I have given it to thee”; and it says, “And thou, lie thou upon thy left side,” etc. You find that you say: Israel angered [Him] for three hundred and ninety years until the ten tribes were exiled, and the tribe of Judah spoiled forty; and from when the ten tribes were exiled until the destruction of Jerusalem, they are twenty-two of Manasseh — and the rest of his years were in repentance, for it is said of him (2 Kings 21), “And he did evil like all that Ahab did,” according to the number of the years of Ahab, and he reigned twenty-two years — two of Amon his son, eleven of Jehoiakim, and eleven of Zedekiah — behold forty-six. And this prophecy was said to Ezekiel in the fifth year of Zedekiah. In any case, the days of their corruption are found to be four hundred and thirty-six years, which after this prophecy added six years. Four hundred years make eight Jubilees, and each Jubilee is seven sabbatical years — behold fifty-six sabbatical years, and the eight years dedicated to the Jubilee — behold sixty-four; and in thirty-six years there are five sabbatical years — behold sixty-nine years that are sanctified; and the Jubilee year of this last one is also counted in the count, for in their iniquity it was not completed. And here thus the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Habakkuk: A vision is already written in the Torah, but it is sealed; you add and explain upon the tablets, for yet a vision will be revealed for this appointed time.
Habakkuk.translator_note: The chronological computation is difficult as printed and appears corrupt in places; it is translated literally with the numbers as printed. The Aramaic Targum quotation is translated as printed. Rashi’s quotations of Ezekiel 4:4–6 and 2 Kings 21 are loose; JPS Ezekiel 4:5 reads “the years of their iniquity to be unto thee a number of days, even three hundred and ninety days,” 4:6 reads “forty days, each day for a year, have I appointed it unto thee,” and 2 Kings 21:3 reads “as did Ahab king of Israel.” Printed “2 Kings 21” is 2 Kings 21:2–3. Printed “Chronicles … the second” is 2 Chronicles 36:21.

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: And it declareth of the end
Habakkuk.english_translation: It is an expression of speech, and there is much of it in the book of Proverbs; and because speech is nothing but breath that goes out of the mouth, He calls it *piach* and calls it *ruach*, as in “and all the host of them by the breath of His mouth” (Psalms 33:6).

His soul is always in anger and in lust, longing to swallow, and is not satisfied. *Oflah* is an expression of insolence, like (Numbers 14) “and they presumed (*va-ya’filu*),” and so “*ofel* and watch-tower” (Isaiah 32).
Habakkuk.translator_note: Printed “Numbers 14” is Numbers 14:44 (JPS: “But they presumed”). Printed “Isaiah 32” is Isaiah 32:14 (JPS: “The mound and the tower”); Rashi’s printed words are עופל ובוחן.

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: it is not upright in him
Habakkuk.english_translation: His spirit is not cooled within him to say, “Enough with what I have already acquired”; therefore the retribution will come upon him.

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: But the righteous shall live by his faith
Habakkuk.english_translation: Jeconiah the king, whom this one is destined to exile — his righteousness will stand for him; and on the day that this one is cast out of his grave, “Evil-merodach will lift up the head of Jehoiachin, and set his throne above the throne of the kings.”
Habakkuk.translator_note: Rashi’s wording combines 2 Kings 25:27–28 (JPS: “did lift up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah”; “set his throne above the throne of the kings”).

Habakkuk.english_translation: And even when Belshazzar, the son of this one’s son, comes, his wine will betray him, for “[he] drank wine before the thousand” (Daniel 5:1).
He.

His dwelling and his habitation will not endure, because he grew proud and said under the taste of wine to bring the vessels of the Temple, and drank from them; and this will cause him to be killed and his seed to be destroyed. For “a haughty man, a scorner, will not abide”: he and his habitation will not endure.
Habakkuk.translator_note: Rashi’s quotation differs from the verse, which reads (JPS) “The haughty man abideth not.” The Aramaic phrase “under the taste of wine” echoes Daniel 5:2 (JPS: “while he tasted the wine”).

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: He who enlargeth his desire as the nether-world
Habakkuk.english_translation: Nebuchadnezzar: his soul is like Sheol, to attain all his desire with breadth of heart.
Like the angel of death, who is not sated with putting to death; so this one is not sated with all his acquisitions.
That he gathered unto himself to serve him.

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: take up a parable against him
Habakkuk.english_translation: They will take up in their mouths, in the language of riddles, on his account; *lo* is like *alav*.
The one who says the taunt of the riddle.

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: Woe to him that increaseth that which is not his
Habakkuk.english_translation: This is the taunt: Alas for the one who increases wealth and kingship that are not his, for the kings of Media will come and take everything.

He goes on and on increasing, but he is only making heavy upon himself a burden of iniquity, like a thickness of clay. *Av* is an expression of a heavy beam, as we find in the Mishkan of Ezekiel: “the brackets of the house, and the thick beams” (Ezekiel 41:26), and *av etz* (ibid.).
Habakkuk.translator_note: JPS renders Habakkuk’s עבטיט as “pledges”; Rashi reads it as “thick clay.” Printed “(ibid.)” is Ezekiel 41:25 (JPS: “thick beams of wood”). The word משכנא is Aramaic; “Mishkan of Ezekiel” is left as printed and probably means Ezekiel’s Temple vision.

Habakkuk.english_translation: Like *ve-yakutzu*.
Habakkuk.translator_note: Rashi cites this word for its root; JPS renders it “awake.”

Habakkuk.english_translation: Their casting away, and their being drawn off from their places.
Habakkuk.translator_note: The forms השלכתם ונשלתם are ambiguous as printed (their casting away / you cast them away); translated literally.

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: All the remnant of the peoples shall spoil thee
Habakkuk.english_translation: The remnant of the idolaters.
For the vengeance of the blood of Israel, who are called *Adam*, as it is said (ibid. 34), “*Adam atem*.”
Habakkuk.translator_note: Printed “ibid. 34” is Ezekiel 34:31 (JPS: “are men”).

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: for the violence done to the land
Habakkuk.english_translation: The Land of Israel.
It is Jerusalem.

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: Woe to him that gaineth evil gains for his house
Habakkuk.english_translation: Seizure of money by force, which is evil for him and for his house, to build for himself a house.

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: That he may set his nest on high
Habakkuk.english_translation: As it is written in the book of Daniel (4:27): “Is not this great Babylon, which I have built for a royal dwelling-place, by the might of my power,” and so on. And at the time that this thing left his mouth he was driven away from among people, as it is said (ibid.), “While the word was in the king’s mouth,” in this matter.
Habakkuk.translator_note: “ibid.” is Daniel 4:28.

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: Thou hast devised shame to thy house
Habakkuk.english_translation: Which you devised, to cut off many peoples; and you destroyed yourself.
An expression of stripping and peeling, like “after the house hath been scraped” (Leviticus 14:43).
Like (Proverbs 20:2) “he that provoketh him to anger forfeiteth his life”; *chote* means to destroy his life — *forsfait sa arme* [printed פורפיי"ט שארמ"א] in French (“he forfeits his soul”).
Habakkuk.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this phrase at Habakkuk 2:10 (“tu pèches (tu perds, en péchant) ton âme,” you sin, you lose, by sinning, your soul), in forms such as פורשפייט שארמא and פורפייט שאמא; the reading is *forsfait sa arme*, from Darmesteter’s footnote, which adds that *arme* corresponds to Latin *anima*; the printed form matches closely. Rashi’s printed Hebrew מתעבר differs from the verse’s מתעברו.

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: For the stone shall cry out of the wall
Habakkuk.english_translation: For the stones that you robbed will cry out from the wall.

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: the beam out of the timber
Habakkuk.english_translation: To the stone, with a voice opposite it; both of them cry out.
Targum Jonathan: *ve-shifa mi-go merisha*. *Shifa* is an expression of a splinter; *shepa’in* in the language of the Sages; *doledures* [printed דלדור"ש] in French (an adze); *merish* is the beam.
Habakkuk.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Habakkuk 2:11 (“la doloire,” the adze), in forms such as דולדורש; the reading is *doledures*, from Darmesteter’s footnote; the printed form (דלדור"ש) matches apart from the missing ו.

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: Behold, is it not of the LORD of hosts
Habakkuk.english_translation: The retribution has been fully repaid to the doers of wickedness.
When His wrath comes upon them like fire until it is enough; *dei esh* — *איישי"ץ* in French.
Habakkuk.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Habakkuk 2:13 (“il y a assez de flammes,” there are enough flames), in forms such as אשיץ; the printed form (איישי"ץ) matches.

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: Woe unto him that giveth his neighbour drink
Habakkuk.english_translation: Wine; and in that giving to drink he joins and gathers his wrath upon him, and even makes him drunk with his wrath; and all this he does in order to look at their *me’oreihem*, at their exposure, and to see their nakedness. This is Nebuchadnezzar, who used to give the kings wine to drink and make them drunk and lie with them the lyings of a woman, as we say in tractate Shabbat. Another explanation: “Woe to him that giveth his neighbour drink” — in Seder Olam they expound it with regard to Belshazzar, who gave the princes to drink from the vessels of the Temple, and through them they were joined and became drunk with the wrath of the Holy One, blessed be He, and on that night he was killed.
Habakkuk.translator_note: The word נספחו is rendered literally (“were joined”).

Habakkuk.english_translation: To reveal their disgrace; and their enemies saw them in their degradation.

The heh in this word serves in the reflexive form, like (Deuteronomy 32:50) “and be gathered unto thy people”; here too *ha-arel*: be stopped up with desolation and bewilderment of heart. Every *orlah* is an expression of closing, like “their ear is dull” (Jeremiah 6:10), “uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh” (Ezekiel 44:7); and Targum Jonathan: *ve-it’artal*, an expression of “naked and bare” (ibid.).
Habakkuk.translator_note: Rashi cites the root in “their ear is *arelah*.” Printed “Deuteronomy 32:50”: JPS “and be gathered unto thy people,” of which Rashi cites the form ha-asef. The printed “(ibid.)” points to Ezekiel; the phrase “naked and bare” is found, for example, at Ezekiel 16:7.

Habakkuk.english_translation: The Temple.
The plunder of your beasts and your multitudes, who plundered My people Israel — He will break them.
From the violence against the blood of Israel.

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: for the violence done to the land
Habakkuk.english_translation: The Land of Israel.
Jerusalem.
To Babylon — the graven image.
The man who fashions, and the fashioner of this his god.
In this his handiwork he trusts that it will help him, he who came to make dumb idols.
As a question of astonishment.

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: the LORD is in His holy temple
Habakkuk.english_translation: Prepared to exact retribution.

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: Let all the earth keep silence before Him
Habakkuk.english_translation: *Has* is an expression of silencing and of the stillness of desolation.

Some interpret it as its Targum; and according to its sense, he asked for mercy for himself, for he had spoken harshly — like (above 1) “Therefore the law is slacked” and “and makest men as the fishes of the sea” — taunting the attribute of justice.
Habakkuk.translator_note: The word קנתר אחר is rendered “taunting”; the printed phrase is brief. “Above 1” points to Habakkuk 1:4 and 1:14.

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: I have heard the report of Thee
Habakkuk.english_translation: That always, from of old, You exacted retribution from those who anger You — and this wicked one You tolerate.
I said: How has the attribute of justice changed because of Israel’s iniquity?

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: revive Thy work in the midst of the years
Habakkuk.english_translation: Your first work, that You used to exact retribution for us from our enemies — in the midst of the years of the trouble in which we are placed, revive it; that is, awaken it and restore it; and in the midst of these years make it known.
That You be angry with the wicked.
*Racham* is like *le-racham*.
To have compassion on Israel.

Now he mentions before Him His first work, which he asks before Him to awaken — and the work (another version: acts) of the love of Israel and the punishments of the earlier generations: when You came to give the Torah, You went around to Esau and Ishmael, and they did not accept it.
Habakkuk.translator_note: The words ופועל (ס"א פועל) are difficult as printed; translated literally.

Habakkuk.english_translation: Esau.
Ishmael, as it says, “And he dwelt in the wilderness of Paran” (Genesis 21:21).
At Sinai, for Israel.
That day.
It was like the special light of the seven days of Creation; and so Targum Jonathan.
An expression of light: when it pierces and shines through a hole it appears as a kind of protruding horns (*keranim*); and so “the skin of his face sent forth beams” (Exodus 34:29).
From the hand of the Holy One, blessed be He, they came to them.
As its Targum: There His might was revealed, which had been hidden beforehand in the secret place of the Most High.

I found in an aggadic Midrash: At the time that the Holy One, blessed be He, gave the Torah to Israel, He drove away the Angel of Death, to divert him to other matters, so that he would not stand and taunt and say, “A nation that is destined to deny You at the end of forty days — and You are giving them the Torah?”

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: fiery bolts go forth at His feet
Habakkuk.english_translation: Angels of *reshef* came with Him to Sinai.
Habakkuk.translator_note: JPS renders reshef as “fiery bolts.”

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: He standeth, and shaketh the earth
Habakkuk.english_translation: He waited to examine closely the judgment of the generation of the Flood, to measure out to them measure for measure; and *madad* means standing, as it says, “The LORD standeth, and standeth to judge the peoples” (Isaiah 3:13) — waiting and being exacting in their judgment.
Habakkuk.translator_note: Rashi’s wording differs from the verse, which reads (JPS) “The LORD standeth up to plead, And standeth to judge the peoples.”

Habakkuk.english_translation: They corrupted [themselves] with hot things, and with hot things they were judged.
In the generation of the Dispersion, because they were of one language, all of them came into counsel, as it is written, “And the whole earth was of one language” (Genesis 11:1).
He made them leap into seventy languages, as it says, “*vayyeter* from his place” (Job 37), “*lenatter* upon them” (Leviticus 11).
Habakkuk.translator_note: Rashi cites these words for their root, so they are left transliterated. Printed “Job 36” is Job 37:1 (JPS: “is moved out of its place”); printed “Leviticus 11” is Leviticus 11:21 (JPS: “to leap upon the earth”).

Habakkuk.english_translation: The princes of the idolaters.

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: His goings are as of old
Habakkuk.english_translation: He showed them that the whole course of the world is His.
Because of the iniquity that was found in Israel.
Habakkuk.translator_note: Rashi’s gloss is a fragment (“that was found in Israel”); it is completed from the lemma תחת און (“under iniquity”).

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: The curtains of the land of Midian do tremble
Habakkuk.english_translation: Those who stand openly and ravage Israel; and “when they are humbled before You, the curtains tremble,” etc. — all of it is as its Targum.
There are expressions of astonishment that stand [as such]; You showed us that all these You did; and the explanation of the verse is as its Targum.
Habakkuk.translator_note: The word הראינו is ambiguous as printed (“we showed” / “You showed us”); translated as “You showed us.”

Habakkuk.english_translation: For us, salvation.

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: Thy bow is made quite bare
Habakkuk.english_translation: Your might was surely revealed.

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: Sworn are the rods of the word
Habakkuk.english_translation: The oaths that You swore to the tribes.
A word that is fulfilled forever. *Omer* is vowelled with a patach (that is, a segol), and its accent is above, for it is a noun.
Habakkuk.translator_note: The words “(that is, a segol)” are a later addition in the printed text.

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: Thou dost cleave the earth with rivers
Habakkuk.english_translation: As its Targum.

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: The mountains have seen Thee, and they tremble
Habakkuk.english_translation: The mountains of the streams of Arnon, which cleaved to one another.

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: The tempest of waters floweth over
Habakkuk.english_translation: When they crossed the Jordan the waters ceased, were cut off, and the flow of the flood of waters passed to the lower part of the river, and those coming from above rose up, stood still.
The inhabitants of the earth praised Him.

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: lifteth up its hands on high
Habakkuk.english_translation: The host of heaven gave thanks to Him.
*Be-meduriehon* (“in their dwellings”). Every word that requires a lamed at its beginning, he put a heh at its end; and they explained it as concerning the war of Gibeon, as its Targum.

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: At the light of Thine arrows
Habakkuk.english_translation: Israel.

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: Thou marchest through the earth in indignation
Habakkuk.english_translation: To drive out the seven idolaters.
Saul and David.
The walls of the idolaters.
It is the height of the walls and the towers.

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: Thou hast stricken through with his own rods
Habakkuk.english_translation: Sennacherib and his company, who were storming with a whirlwind to scatter me; and he was a rod with which You used to rule the idolaters; and when he came and stormed to scatter me, You pierced the heads of his armies with his rods, with which he came to subjugate.
The heads of his cities and his strongholds, like (Zechariah 2:8) “Jerusalem shall be inhabited without walls (*perazot*),” “the unwalled (*ha-perazi*) towns” (Deuteronomy 3).
Habakkuk.translator_note: Rashi cites these words for their root. Printed “Deuteronomy 3” is Deuteronomy 3:5 (JPS: “the unwalled towns”). Rashi’s printed words in Zechariah are פרזות תשב ירושלים.

Habakkuk.english_translation: They were, whenever they were able, to devour the poor in secret — Israel, who are called a poor people.

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: Thou hast trodden the sea with Thy horses
Habakkuk.english_translation: With his heavy armies, like the sand of the sea.
Targum Jonathan: *be-dagur*, an expression of *chamarim chamarim* (Exodus 8).
Habakkuk.translator_note: Printed “Exodus 8” is Exodus 8:10 (JPS: “in heaps”). Rashi cites this word for its root.

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: When I heard, mine inward parts trembled
Habakkuk.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “Babylon said: I heard, and the kings trembled before the judgment with which the Egyptians were judged.”

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: My lips quivered at the voice
Habakkuk.english_translation: At the sound of the report a trembling seized me, until my lips knock against one another and its sound is heard.
An expression of “the bells of the horse” (Zechariah 14) — *טינטי"ר* in French.
Habakkuk.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Habakkuk 3:16 among the forms טינטין and טינטיר (the French gloss is not clearly legible in my copy); the printed form (טינטי"ר) matches the form טינטיר. Rashi cites the Hebrew word for its root; printed “Zechariah 14” is Zechariah 14:20 (JPS: “upon the bells of the horses”).

Habakkuk.english_translation: In my place I am shaken.

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: That I should wait for the day of trouble
Habakkuk.english_translation: That this my rest is prepared for a day of trouble.

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: When he cometh up against the people that he invadeth
Habakkuk.english_translation: For the day of which He said, to bring up from within it the people that invades it, on account of its returning with its troops to its land.
Habakkuk.translator_note: The explanation is difficult as printed; translated literally.

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: For though the fig-tree shall not blossom
Habakkuk.english_translation: As its Targum; and it can be interpreted according to its plain sense: from now on there is no success for any deed of Babylon.
A white field.
The sheepfold.
The Assembly of Israel [says]: in HaShem I will exult.

Habakkuk.english_lemma_JPS: For the Leader. With my string-music
Habakkuk.english_translation: For the Levite who leads in song: Blessed be He, I will answer Him with my melodies, and the Levite will give a voice opposite him with the instruments of song.
As you say (Ezra 3), “And the Levites stood from twenty years old and upward, to oversee the work,” and so on.
Habakkuk.translator_note: Printed “Ezra 3” is Ezra 3:8; JPS reads “and appointed the Levites, from twenty years old and upward, to have the oversight of the work of the house of the LORD,” and Rashi’s verb differs.

Habakkuk.english_translation: It is an expression of a melodious voice, to raise and to lower — *orgenedores* [printed אורגנידור"ש] in French.
Habakkuk.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Habakkuk 3:19 (“sur mes chants … les modulations mélodieuses de la voix qui s’élève et s’abaisse,” on my songs … the melodious modulations of the voice that rises and falls), in forms such as אורגנדורש; the reading is *orgenedores*, which Darmesteter derives from Latin *organatorias*, from *organum*; the printed form (אורגנידור"ש) matches apart from an extra י.

Zephaniah.english_translation: An expression of destruction, like (Judges 18) “and thou lose thy life,” that of Micah; and an aleph is missing in the second word, since he should have written *e’esof*; but there are many like this, like “neither shall the Arabian pitch tent there” (Isaiah 13), which is like *ye’ahel*.
Zephaniah.translator_note: Rashi cites these words for their root. Printed “Judges 18” is Judges 18:25; printed “Isaiah 13” is Isaiah 13:20 (JPS: “Neither shall the Arabian pitch tent there”).

Zephaniah.english_translation: They are the idolaters.
So that there will be no remnant of his remembrance.

Zephaniah.english_lemma_JPS: the idolatrous priests with the priests
Zephaniah.english_translation: Their worshippers with their priests.
And they turn around and swear by their Malcam, by their idolatry; they make the idolatry the main thing, to say: If you do not believe the oath of HaShem, behold, I swear to you by idolatry.
He summoned His armies for the appointed day.
The ornaments of the idolaters.

Zephaniah.english_lemma_JPS: those that leap over the threshold
Zephaniah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “who walk in the customs of the Philistines, who did not tread on the threshold of Dagon,” as it is said, “Therefore neither the priests of Dagon,” and so on (1 Samuel 5).
Targum Jonathan: “from the gate of the fish”; and it was a gate in Jerusalem, and that was its name.
From the poultry gate, which is second to it.

The brook of Kidron, which is deep like a mortar (*makhtesh*) — this is Targum Jonathan. And an aggadic Midrash: “from the fish gate” — this is Acre, which is set in the lap of the sea, for many fish are caught there.
Lod, which is second to Jerusalem.
Zephaniah.translator_note: The source lemma (מן המשנה) belongs to 1:10; a word from the JPS verse of this id is used.

Zephaniah.english_translation: This is Tzippori, which sits on the tops of the mountains like a bird (*tzippor*).
Zephaniah.translator_note: The source lemma (מהגבעות) belongs to 1:10; a phrase from the JPS verse of this id is used.

Zephaniah.english_translation: This is Tiberias, which is deeper than all the Land of Israel.

Zephaniah.english_lemma_JPS: all the merchant people are undone
Zephaniah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “For the place of all the people whose deeds resemble the deeds of the people of the land of Canaan.”
Zephaniah.translator_note: The word אתר in the Aramaic is difficult as printed. The Aramaic is translated as printed.

Zephaniah.english_lemma_JPS: All they that were laden with silver
Zephaniah.english_translation: All those rich in possessions, laden with the burden of silver and gold, like (Proverbs 27:3) “A stone is heavy, and the sand weighty”; *netel* is an expression of burden.
Zephaniah.translator_note: The Aramaic words are translated as printed. Rashi cites the word for its root.

Zephaniah.english_lemma_JPS: I will search Jerusalem with lamps
Zephaniah.english_translation: I will scrutinize their iniquities.
Those who float on their lees; as “and the iron floated” (2 Kings 6:6), which we translate *u-kefa parzela*.
Zephaniah.translator_note: JPS 2 Kings 6:6 reads “and made the iron to swim.”

Zephaniah.english_lemma_JPS: The LORD will not do good
Zephaniah.english_translation: To those who do His will.
To those who transgress His will.

Zephaniah.english_lemma_JPS: Wherein the mighty man crieth bitterly
Zephaniah.english_translation: The mighty man will cry out there in a bitter voice.
An expression of desolation.
More desolation.
Upon Israel, who are called *Adam*.
Their flesh; and in the Arabic language they call flesh *al-lachm*.
Dung.
Gather and assemble together, like “to gather stubble” (*le-kosheish*) (Exodus 5).
Zephaniah.translator_note: Rashi cites this word for its root. Printed “Exodus 5” is Exodus 5:12 (JPS: “to gather stubble for straw”).

Zephaniah.english_translation: Make your deeds equal; make your deeds equal to the will of your Maker. And our Rabbis expounded: *Kashet* yourself, and afterward *kashet* others; they made both an expression of *heikesh* — a person who makes himself even and straightens his path.
Zephaniah.translator_note: Rashi’s *kashet* is left transliterated; the printed text gives no source for the saying of our Rabbis.

Zephaniah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “who did not desire to return to the Torah.”
Before the decree comes.

This is an elliptical verse: like chaff that passes before the wind, and like smoke that passes before the sun; and this is the translation of “passes a day.” So Targum Jonathan: “You shall be like chaff in which the wind blows, and like smoke that passes from before the day”; another version: “like the shadow that passes,” and so on. That is an expression of shadow.
For if you do so, I will visit upon your evil neighbors — Philistia, Ammon and Moab — as the prophet arranges them as he goes on.

Ashdod is her name; and at noon, when *ketev* ravages in it, they will drive her out and she shall be plundered. Another explanation: “at noon they will drive her out” — it was a place of pasture for sheep, and noon is hard to go out with sheep in, and so it says, “where thou makest thy flock to rest at noon” (Song of Songs 1:7).
The coast of the sea. And the expression *chevel* is a measure of ground, for they measure with a rope (*chevel*): that is, those adjacent to the sea.

Targum Jonathan: “a people who are liable to destruction.” And who are they? The inhabitants of the sea-coast: Canaan, the land of the Philistines, for the Philistines dwell on the shore of the last sea in the west of the Land of Israel, within the limits of its borders. And though Jonathan expounds it as meaning destruction (*kelayah*), *goy Keretim* is a province among the Philistines, and its name is Kereti; and so it says at Ziklag, “We made a raid upon the South of the Cherethites, and upon that which belongeth to Judah,” and Targum Jonathan [renders] “on the south of Kereti”; and below it is written, “because of all the great spoil that they had taken out of the land of the Philistines, and out of the land of Judah.”
Zephaniah.translator_note: Printed references are 1 Samuel 30:14 and 30:16.

Zephaniah.english_translation: A temporary dwelling in which the shepherds will prepare a meal in the morning. *Keroth* is an expression of “And he prepared great provision for them” (2 Kings 6:23).
Zephaniah.translator_note: The verb שיכרו is rendered “will prepare” by the sense of the proof-text; the word כירה in Rashi’s citation is spelled differently from the verse.

Zephaniah.english_lemma_JPS: And it shall be a portion for the remnant of the house of Judah
Zephaniah.english_translation: That border shall be a lot for the remnant of the children of Judah; this *chevel* is an expression of lot, and so Targum Jonathan: “and the portion shall be for the remnant of the house of Judah.”

Zephaniah.english_lemma_JPS: Wherewith they have taunted My people
Zephaniah.english_translation: When they were leading Israel into exile toward the land of the Chaldeans and passing through Ammon and Moab, and saw Israel weeping, groaning and crying out, they would taunt them, saying: What is it with you, that you are so afflicted? Why do you weep? Are you not going to your father’s house? Beyond the river your fathers dwelt from of old.
Zephaniah.translator_note: The verb מונין is rendered by its sense (“taunt”).

Zephaniah.english_translation: And they exalted themselves over their border.
You too will return to your former state — was not Lot your father from Sodom?

A making of sound, like “*meshak gevim*” (Isaiah 33), and the first mem too is a root-letter in the word, like “*mimshach* ha-sokhekh” (Ezekiel 28); *mimshak charul* — the making of the sound of the nettles that grow there, with no one passing by, and they strike against one another and make a sound.
Zephaniah.translator_note: Rashi cites these words for their root. Printed “Isaiah 33” is Isaiah 33:4 (JPS: “As locusts leap”); printed “Ezekiel 28” is Ezekiel 28:14 (JPS: “the far-covering cherub”).

Zephaniah.english_translation: A place of digging salt.
He weakened their strength.
When they see that their fear [of idols] was corrupted.
When Israel were exiled there, beyond the rivers of Cush.
Assyria is in the north, next to Babylon.
It is the head of Assyria.
All the beasts of the nations.
Birds.
*פומל"ש* that is at the top of the roof.
Zephaniah.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists the same word at Exodus 25 for כפתריה (“ses pommeaux,” its pommels), in forms such as פומלש; the printed form (פומל"ש) matches.

Zephaniah.english_lemma_JPS: Desolation shall be in the posts
Zephaniah.english_translation: The destruction will be evident in the thresholds of the house.

Zephaniah.english_lemma_JPS: Voices shall sing in the windows
Zephaniah.english_translation: The sound of birds chirping in the windows.

Zephaniah.english_lemma_JPS: For the cedar-work thereof shall be uncovered
Zephaniah.english_translation: For its cedars, uprooted and rooted out, like “Rase it, rase it” (Psalms 137); and Targum Jonathan: “and its roofing they tore down” — it is the roof of the house, paneled with cedar, for even stone houses are roofed with boards of wood.
Zephaniah.translator_note: The Aramaic words וטללה סתרו are translated tentatively. Printed “Psalms 137” is Psalms 137:7.

Zephaniah.english_lemma_JPS: and there is none else beside me
Zephaniah.english_translation: And there is none beside me.

Zephaniah.english_lemma_JPS: Woe to her that is filthy and polluted
Zephaniah.english_translation: Until now he spoke about Nineveh, and now he returns to Jerusalem: Woe, that she will be for plunder and for filth, like *ke-ro’i*, and will be polluted with the stench of her iniquity. *Mora’ah* is like *mora’to* (Leviticus 1), “and I will make thee *ke-ra’i*” (Nahum 3).
Zephaniah.translator_note: Rashi cites these words for their root. Printed “Leviticus 1” is Leviticus 1:16 (JPS: “its crop”). Printed “Nahum 3” is Nahum 3:6 (JPS: “And will make thee as dung”); Rashi’s own comment on that verse glosses כראי as “like dung.” Rashi’s printed form here is כרואי.

Zephaniah.english_translation: Like a silly dove, without heart.
Who hasten to eat their prey at night.

Zephaniah.english_lemma_JPS: They leave not a bone for the morrow
Zephaniah.english_translation: They did not leave even the bones to gnaw until morning.

Zephaniah.english_lemma_JPS: They have done violence to the law
Zephaniah.english_translation: They did not teach it to those who asked them.

Zephaniah.english_lemma_JPS: The LORD who is righteous is in the midst of her
Zephaniah.english_translation: He made His Shekhinah dwell in their midst, and therefore He cannot look upon their evil deeds, for He is righteous and there is no wrong before Him.

Zephaniah.english_lemma_JPS: doth He bring His right to light
Zephaniah.english_translation: He gives to the light; He judges a true judgment in its truth.

Zephaniah.english_lemma_JPS: But the unrighteous knoweth no shame
Zephaniah.english_translation: And with all this, the unjust judges within her did not take it to heart to be ashamed before the Righteous One who dwells among them.
I brought retribution upon the idolaters so that you would see and fear, as he concludes and goes on: “I said, Surely you will see Me.”
Zephaniah.translator_note: Rashi’s printed wording אך תראי אותי differs from the verse, which reads (JPS) “Surely thou wilt fear Me.”

Zephaniah.english_lemma_JPS: her dwelling shall not be cut off
Zephaniah.english_translation: And her dwellings shall not be destroyed.

Zephaniah.english_lemma_JPS: Despite all that I have visited upon her
Zephaniah.english_translation: And there shall not be cut off from it all the good which I commanded to bring upon her.
That I rise up to assemble against you.
Zephaniah.translator_note: JPS renders לעד as “to the prey”; Rashi’s gloss reads it as an assembling.

Zephaniah.english_lemma_JPS: From beyond the rivers of Ethiopia
Zephaniah.english_translation: They will convey an offering to Me.
Those who pray to Me.
The congregations of My dispersed ones, whom I dispersed.

Zephaniah.english_lemma_JPS: shalt thou not be ashamed for all thy doings
Zephaniah.english_translation: Because you were already smitten, and your iniquity has been paid off.
A humble people, who accept being insulted.
Your sufferings — *justices* [printed יושטיצ"א] in French.
Zephaniah.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word under Zephaniah 3 (“tes justices, c’est-à-dire tes châtiments,” your justices, that is, your punishments; the verse number is unclear in my copy), in forms such as יושטיזא and יאשטיצא; the reading *justices* is from Darmesteter’s footnote (“Lire : tés justices”); the printed form (יושטיצ"א) matches.

Zephaniah.english_lemma_JPS: A Mighty One who will save
Zephaniah.english_translation: He is a Mighty One who will save from the idolaters.

Zephaniah.english_lemma_JPS: He will be silent in His love
Zephaniah.english_translation: He will cover over your transgressions in His love; and so Targum Jonathan: “He will subdue your sin in His mercies.”

Zephaniah.english_lemma_JPS: that are far from the appointed season
Zephaniah.english_translation: I have gathered those removed from My appointed seasons, who did not keep Sabbaths and festivals.
I have made an end.
They were of your people.
For that guilt you had a burden of reproach.
An expression of removal, like “Take away the dross” (Proverbs 25), “When he was removed out of the highway” (2 Samuel 20); and there is no root in the word except the gimel alone.
Zephaniah.translator_note: Rashi cites these words for their root. Printed “Proverbs 25” is Proverbs 25:4; printed “2 Samuel 20” is 2 Samuel 20:13.

Zephaniah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “Behold, I am making a completion”; and it can be interpreted as an expression of *isuy*, like “And you shall tread down the wicked” (Malachi 3).
Zephaniah.translator_note: The word עישוי is left transliterated; the sense “treading down” is taken from the proof-text. Printed “Malachi 3” is Malachi 3:21. The Aramaic is translated as printed.

Zephaniah.english_lemma_JPS: Whose shame hath been in all the earth
Zephaniah.english_translation: In every place where they were put to shame, there I will make them a name and a praise.

Haggai.english_lemma_JPS: In the second year of Darius the king
Haggai.english_translation: He is Darius, king of Persia, who was after Ahasuerus, and we find in Midrash Vayikra Rabbah that he was the son of Esther. And in the days of Cyrus the first, Zerubbabel and Joshua the priest went up from Babylon to Jerusalem with the permission of Cyrus, as it is said (Ezra 9), “Whosoever there is among you of all His people,” etc.; and the adversaries of Judah and Benjamin stood up and sent their letters to Cyrus to command to cancel the work of the Temple that they had begun (and he commanded and they were stopped); from that day they ceased, as is explained (in Ezra 1), “Then ceased the work of the house of our God,” etc. And it ceased for three years that Cyrus reigned, and fourteen of Ahasuerus, and the first year of Darius his son; and in the second year this prophecy was said to Haggai, to urge them to return and build in the work, and not to fear, for the idolaters will not cancel them, for the Holy One, blessed be He, will make them succeed.
Haggai.translator_note: Printed “Ezra 9” is Ezra 1:3 (JPS: “Whosoever there is among you of all His people”). The “adversaries of Judah and Benjamin” are from Ezra 4:1. Printed “Ezra 1” is Ezra 4:24, in Aramaic; JPS reads “Then ceased the work of the house of God which is at Jerusalem,” and Rashi’s printed wording has “our God.” The words in parentheses “(and he commanded and they were stopped)” are a printed insertion.

Haggai.english_translation: Because their enemies stopped them at first, they think that I will not fulfil My words that I said, “when seventy years are completed for the destruction of Jerusalem,” and that the time for My house to be built will not come again. Say to them that now the time has come; but the first time was only for a visitation, to complete seventy years from the beginning of the kingdom of Babylon; and so it was: at the end of seventy years they were visited to go up by the leave of Cyrus; but the building of the House depends on the destruction of Jerusalem in the days of Zedekiah, which was eighteen years later than the kingdom of Babylon, as the Master said (Megillah 11, Arakhin 12): They were exiled in the eighteenth, they were exiled in the nineteenth; and now the eighteen are complete.
Haggai.translator_note: The Talmud references in parentheses (Megillah 11, Arakhin 12) are a printed insertion. The Aramaic phrase “as the Master said” is translated as printed.

Haggai.english_lemma_JPS: Is it a time for you
Haggai.english_translation: An expression of wonder; therefore the heh is vocalized with a patach.

Covered with boards of cedar, like “and he covered the house” (1 Kings 6), “and the house covered with cedar”; and so Targum Jonathan: “Is it fitting for you that you dwell in houses that are roofed with boards of cedar, and this Temple is desolate?”
Haggai.translator_note: Rashi’s quotation is not verbatim; JPS 1 Kings 6:9 reads “and he covered in the house with planks of cedar over beams.”

Haggai.english_translation: Upon your pursuits, for you see that there is no blessing in the work of your hands, as He says, “You have sown much, and brought in little” — all this is because of the destruction of My house.
Because of the sin of the first-fruits, which they stopped.

Haggai.english_lemma_JPS: You eat, but you have not enough
Haggai.english_translation: Because of the sin of the cessation of the meal-offerings.

Haggai.english_lemma_JPS: You drink, but you are not filled with drink
Haggai.english_translation: That the taste of the wine was taken away, because the libations ceased.

Haggai.english_lemma_JPS: You clothe you, but there is none warm
Haggai.english_translation: Because of the sin of the priestly garments that ceased.
All the profit that you make goes and is consumed, like one who puts his coins in a knot of a pierced garment.

It is written lacking a heh, corresponding to five things that were in the First Temple and were not in the Second: the Ark, the Urim and Thummim, the fire, the Shekhinah, and the Holy Spirit, as is found in tractate Yoma.
Until now you thought to bring much in from the field, and you brought in little.
I brought upon it the blow of rot and worm.
An expression of blowing on a fire of coals (Isaiah 54).
Haggai.translator_note: Rashi cites the word for its root; JPS Isaiah 54:16 reads “That bloweth the fire of coals.”

Haggai.english_lemma_JPS: over you the heaven hath kept back
Haggai.english_translation: Because of your sins.
Withheld.
On a mission of the Omnipresent.
They began cutting stones and sawing wood on the twenty-fourth of the sixth [month], and in the seventh, on the twenty-first, the word of HaShem came to Haggai.
Who was of the exiles and is still alive.

Haggai.english_lemma_JPS: that saw this house in its former glory
Haggai.english_translation: The first; this is not important in his eyes.

Haggai.english_lemma_JPS: is not such a one as nothing
Haggai.english_translation: I know that for one who saw the first, this is in his eyes only as nothing.
It and nothing — they are equal, like (Hosea 4) “And it is like people, like priest”; here too, “is like it as nothing,” it and nothing — both of them are equal.

Haggai.english_lemma_JPS: The word that I covenanted with you
Haggai.english_translation: You keep My Torah, and My spirit rests upon your prophet; do not fear.

Haggai.english_lemma_JPS: Yet once, it is a little while
Haggai.english_translation: When the kingdom of Persia, which rules over you, is finished, yet one more will arise to rule over you, to distress you, from the kingdom of Greece; and the time of its rule will be short.
With the miracles done for the sons of the Hasmoneans.

Haggai.english_lemma_JPS: the earth, and the sea, and the dry land
Haggai.english_translation: And they will understand that My Shekhinah dwells in this house, and they will bring a gift of gold and silver, as is written in the book of Joseph ben Gorion.
And it is in My hand to bring to whomever I desire.

Haggai.english_lemma_JPS: greater than that of the former
Haggai.english_translation: Rav and Shmuel: one said in the building, and one said in the years, for the years of the First Temple were four hundred and ten and of the Second Temple four hundred and twenty.

Haggai.english_lemma_JPS: Ask now the priests for instruction
Haggai.english_translation: Perhaps they forgot, in exile, the laws of holiness and of uncleanness and cleanness.
Flesh of the uncleanness of a carcass or a creeping thing.
Haggai.translator_note: The phrase is elliptical as printed; translated literally.

Haggai.english_translation: A cooked dish.

“[No].” It shall become unclean. Rav and Shmuel disagreed about it. One said: The priests were put to shame, for he asked them about the fourth in holiness, and they told him it is clean; and one said: The priests were not put to shame, for he asked them about the fifth in holiness.
Haggai.translator_note: The word יטמא (“it shall become unclean”) follows the bracketed lemma as printed and is hard to place; it is left as printed. The Aramaic is translated as printed.

Haggai.english_translation: He did not touch the creeping thing itself but a garment, which is a first.
Will it become defiled (*hista’ev*)?

Haggai.english_lemma_JPS: If one that is unclean by a dead body touch
Haggai.english_translation: The corpse itself.
For the dead body is the father of the fathers of uncleanness, and the fifth in the uncleanness of a creeping thing is the fourth in the uncleanness of a corpse.
Just as you err in this, so you err in several laws.
If they do not set their hearts to learn.
The years that have passed.

Haggai.english_lemma_JPS: before a stone was laid upon a stone
Haggai.english_translation: Before you returned to continue and to add to the foundation that you laid in the days of Cyrus, and it ceased; now set your hearts to engage in the building and in the study of the needs of the priesthood.

Haggai.english_lemma_JPS: when one came to a heap of twenty measures
Haggai.english_translation: From the time that a curse was sent upon your deeds, as until now: that they would set up a heap fit to measure twenty se’ah from it, and he found only ten.
It is the pit before the winepress, and the wine runs down into it.
To draw from it fifty measures with which they measure wine in winepresses, and their name is *purah*.
To fill, like “to take water out of the cistern” (Isaiah 30), and so “Strip off the train” (ibid. 16).
Haggai.translator_note: Rashi cites these words for their root. Printed “ibid. 16” is Isaiah 47:2; Rashi’s printed word שובל is שבל in the verse.

Haggai.english_translation: It is not that a curse was sent upon the wine more than upon the grain, but a person errs in estimating the measure of the winevat, because it is deep, whereas the heap stands before him; and in the Mishnah of Avot de-Rabbi Natan we learned a reason why He did not say a small measure for the wine, as He said for the grain, for example, “to draw out twenty-five press-measures, and there were ten”: to teach you that wine is always a greater measure, and when the wine is stricken it is a bad sign for the world; and because the wine needs to be plentiful, He counted it with a larger number.

Haggai.english_lemma_JPS: the foundation of the LORD’S temple was laid
Haggai.english_translation: For they began now, in the second [year], to add to the foundation of the first that they built in the days of Cyrus.

Haggai.english_lemma_JPS: is the seed yet in the barn?
Haggai.english_translation: You have not yet sown in this year, and the trees have not yet set their fruits; and from now on you shall sow at a time of blessing, for through the building of the House blessing will come upon the work of your hands.

Haggai.english_lemma_JPS: I will destroy the strength of the kingdoms of the nations
Haggai.english_translation: The kingdom of Persia, which now rules over the whole world, will fall into the hand of another kingdom at the end of thirty-four years from the building of the House, as we learn in tractate Avodah Zarah.
Haggai.translator_note: The printed text names the tractate עכו"ם, an older, censored title of tractate Avodah Zarah.

Haggai.english_lemma_JPS: and will make thee as a signet
Haggai.english_translation: Because it was decreed upon Jeconiah his father, “As I live, if Coniah the son of Jehoiakim will be a signet on the hand of My right hand, from there I will pluck thee” (Jeremiah 22:30), and it says there, “Write you this man childless”; we learned that his repentance helped him, and Zerubbabel was born to him and was set as a signet.
Haggai.translator_note: Printed “Jeremiah 22:30” is the citation for “Write you this man childless”; the first quotation is Jeremiah 22:24 (JPS: “though Coniah the son of Jehoiakim king of Judah were the signet upon My right hand, yet would I pluck thee thence”).

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: the word of the LORD unto Zechariah
Zechariah.english_translation: The prophecy of Zechariah is exceedingly obscure, for it contains visions resembling a dream that is given to interpretation, and we cannot stand on the truth of its interpretation until the Teacher of Righteousness comes; and to the best of my ability I will set my mind to settling the verses one by one from the interpretations that resemble them, and after the interpretations of Jonathan.
Before they began again to build in the work, for on the twenty-fourth of the month they began it.
Who were in the generation of the destruction of the Temple.
See that they were stricken with an evil blow, with famine, with sword and with captivity.

And if you say, “Even the prophets, where are they? Behold, they died!” I answer you: Was it for the prophets to live forever? But their end proves that their words were true, for all the words and decrees of calamity of Mine, which I commanded My servants the prophets concerning you — did not these overtake your fathers?
Our Rabbis explained what they explained in the aggadah of Chelek; but the order of the passage and the language is not settled by it.
Zechariah.translator_note: “Chelek” is left as printed; the printed text gives no tractate.

Zechariah.english_translation: An angel.
It is an allusion to taking vengeance on the Chaldeans through the Medes and Persians, with sword and with blood, as He says here, “and a great anger I am angry at the idolaters.”
Zechariah.translator_note: Rashi’s printed wording differs from the verse; Zechariah 1:15 reads (JPS) “and I am very sore displeased with the nations that are at ease.”

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: behind him there were horses, red, sorrel, and white
Zechariah.english_translation: Prepared for the mission of the Omnipresent; and there are in them many kinds of colors, and it is a praise to Him. *Serukim*: I do not know what color it is; and Targum Jonathan: *kavvachin*.
Zechariah.translator_note: JPS renders serukim as “sorrel.”

Zechariah.english_translation: Among the myrtle trees of Babylon.
To one angel who was showing me all this: What are these, my lord? — and that is the one riding on the red horse.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: to walk to and fro through the earth
Zechariah.english_translation: To see the tranquility of the idolaters.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: Then the angel of the LORD spoke and said
Zechariah.english_translation: He is the one who speaks with me.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: And the LORD answered the angel that spoke with me
Zechariah.english_translation: Not that the prophet heard what He answered, but from what the angel said to him, “Proclaim, saying: I am jealous,” etc., I know that He answered him good words.
I will exact vengeance for the judgment of Jerusalem from those who oppress her.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: the nations that are at ease
Zechariah.english_translation: Of whom these say that they dwell and are quiet.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: for I was but a little displeased
Zechariah.english_translation: Against My people, a little.
Upon the anger, for evil.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: a line shall be stretched forth over Jerusalem
Zechariah.english_translation: To measure her walls, her length and her breadth.
These are the idolaters who are in the four winds of heaven, who gored with their horns Judah and Jerusalem until they scattered them.
Carpenters who know how to saw off the horns; and our Rabbis explained in tractate Sukkah who they are.
These horns that I saw at first.
Zechariah.translator_note: The printed bracket closes after the word מה; the comment is understood as identifying “these” with the horns seen at first.

Zechariah.english_translation: And they brought them low, so that no man lifted up his head, and they did not allow any of the sons of My people to raise a head.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: these then are come to frighten them
Zechariah.english_translation: The craftsmen, to terrify those horns and to cast them down.
To throw down.
The measuring cord, to measure Jerusalem, how long and how wide it will be.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: the angel that spoke with me went forth
Zechariah.english_translation: He is the one in whose hand is the measuring cord.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: Run, speak to this young man
Zechariah.english_translation: Do not go out any more to measure, for the Holy One, blessed be He, consulted with His heavenly company (*pamalya*) that it shall have no measure and limit; and now run, speak to Zechariah, saying: “shall be inhabited without walls” — without a wall, so that all who come may settle in it, and it will grow from day to day.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: will be unto her a wall of fire round about
Zechariah.english_translation: As a shield, as though a wall of fire were around her; and also within her My Shekhinah will dwell, for your honor.

“Ho” is nothing but an expression of proclamation and of crying out an assembling; and so Targum Jonathan: *aklu* to the scattered — proclaim; like “The LORD thundered from heaven” (2 Samuel 22), *aklu* from heaven.
Zechariah.translator_note: The Aramaic word אכלו is left transliterated; its sense (“proclaim”) is taken from Rashi’s gloss. Rashi’s citation lacks “The LORD”; printed “2 Samuel 22” is 2 Samuel 22:14. The Aramaic is translated as printed.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: flee then from the land of the north
Zechariah.english_translation: Go out, exiles of My people, from within Babylon and Assyria.
This too is an expression of proclamation: gather together with the exile of Zion, and escape from within Babylon.
After your honor I am sent, to increase honor for you; and an aggadic Midrash: *Achar kavod* — after I repay Esau honor for having honored his father.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: and they shall be a spoil to those that served them
Zechariah.english_translation: For Israel, who are now servants to them.
And they will be joined together.
For His inheritance and His portion.
All the rest of the idolaters.
An expression of rousing and awakening.

To accuse him, because his sons were married to foreign women, as it is written in the book of Ezra: “And there were found among the sons of the priests who had settled foreign women, of the sons of Joshua the son of Jehozadak.”
Zechariah.translator_note: Rashi’s quotation is of Ezra 10:18, which reads in JPS “And among the sons of the priests there were found that had married foreign women, namely: of the sons of Jeshua, the son of Jozadak.” Rashi’s printed wording is the form given here.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: The LORD rebuke thee, O Satan
Zechariah.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He, rebukes you, Satan, and repeats and says, “and the LORD rebuke thee” — He who chooses Jerusalem — that you not enter before Him to accuse this righteous man. Is he not worthy, and he merited this, that he was saved from the fire of burning?

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: a brand plucked out of the fire
Zechariah.english_translation: It is explained in the aggadah of Chelek (folio 93) that he was thrown with Ahab the son of Kolaiah and his companion into the fire.
Zechariah.translator_note: “Chelek” is left as printed; the printed text gives no tractate. The folio number in parentheses is a printed insertion.

Zechariah.english_translation: As its Targum: “He had sons who took wives unfit for the priesthood, and he was punished because he did not protest against them.”

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: Take the filthy garments from off him
Zechariah.english_translation: His sons shall separate from their wives, and He will forgive him.
Changes of fine garments, that is, merits; but because he likened iniquity to filthy garments, he likened merits to *mechalatzot*, fine and white garments.
I, Zechariah.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: Let them set a fair mitre upon his head
Zechariah.english_translation: I sought mercy for him.
An expression of warning, like “and I will call heaven to witness against them,” etc. (Deuteronomy 31:28).
Zechariah.translator_note: JPS Deuteronomy 31:28 reads “and call heaven and earth to witness against them”; Rashi’s citation stops at “heaven,” followed by “etc.”

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: If thou wilt walk in My ways
Zechariah.english_translation: And I too will do this for you.
You shall judge, and be the officer over My Sanctuary.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: I will give thee free access
Zechariah.english_translation: As its Targum: “And in the revival of the dead I will revive you, and I will give you feet that walk among these seraphim”; and according to the plain sense, he announces concerning his sons that they will merit in the future.
Seraphim and ministering angels, who have no sitting.
They were Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah.
Men fit to have miracles done for them, for a miracle was done for them too.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: I will bring forth My servant the Shoot
Zechariah.english_translation: For now Zerubbabel, governor of Judah, a minor in the king’s court — I cause greatness to sprout for him, and there I placed him in favor in the eyes of the king, to fulfil his request in the building of the Temple and the city, as is explained in Ezra, “The words of Nehemiah the son of Hacaliah,” and he is Zerubbabel, as we say in Sanhedrin.
Zechariah.translator_note: Printed text quotes Nehemiah 1:1 under the heading of Ezra. The identification with Zerubbabel is given as printed.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: the stone that I have laid before Joshua
Zechariah.english_translation: The foundation of the House that you laid in the days of Cyrus, and it was stopped by you, and that foundation and the thickness of the wall were little in your eyes, as is explained in Ezra and in the prophecy of Haggai.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: upon one stone are seven facets
Zechariah.english_translation: In the end to widen upon one, seven; and so Targum Jonathan: “upon one stone, seven eyes see it”; and the expression *einayim* is an expression of appearances. And it appears to me: seven eyes, after the name of the eyes of the Holy One, blessed be He, whose eyes and heart are to add upon it, upon one, seven, since its likeness is in this prophecy: “and they shall see the plummet in the hand of Zerubbabel; these seven are the eyes of HaShem, which run to and fro”; but He taught that He set His eyes to increase the glory of the House in its building.
Zechariah.translator_note: JPS Zechariah 4:10 reads “even they shall see with joy the plummet in the hand of Zerubbabel, even these seven, which are the eyes of the LORD, that run to and fro through the whole earth”; Rashi’s citation is a shortened form.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: I will engrave the graving thereof
Zechariah.english_translation: Loosening its knots; frustrating the counsel of the enemies, who wrote an accusation to cancel the work.
And I will remove.

I do not know which day, (תו' on the day that they began to add to the building, the iniquity of the land will depart, and there will be blessing in its fruits, for now it is shining, as is said in the prophecy of Haggai).
Zechariah.translator_note: The Hebrew in parentheses is a later addition in the printed text. The abbreviation תו' is not resolved and is left as printed; the word מאיר' is cut off in the printed text and is read here as “shining.”

Zechariah.english_translation: Like *gulot illit* (Joshua 15) — an expression of a spring: a kind of large, round basin.
Zechariah.translator_note: Rashi cites the word for its root. Printed “Joshua 16” is Joshua 15:19 (JPS: “the Upper Springs”).

Zechariah.english_translation: A kind of small vessels (*bezikhin*) into which they put the oil and the wick.
Zechariah.translator_note: The word is left transliterated.

Zechariah.english_translation: To each and every lamp come seven small pipes, so that the oil flows from the bowl through those pipes to each and every lamp.
Beside it, two trees on which the olives grow.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: one upon the right side of the bowl
Zechariah.english_translation: And here he did not explain concerning the two golden spouts mentioned below in the passage; they are like troughs and *adashim* of an olive-press, which stand beside the olives, and the olives are beaten of themselves into the spouts and are warmed there as in a *ma’tan* and are pressed there in the olive-press, and the oil falls into the spouts, and from the spouts into the bowl, and from the bowl to the pipes, and from the pipes to the lamps; and the pipes and the lamps were forty-nine, an allusion to the light of the world to come: the light of the sun will be sevenfold, like the light of the seven days — forty-nine upon the light of the first day of Creation.
Zechariah.translator_note: Rashi’s technical terms (adashim, ma’tan) are left transliterated.

Zechariah.english_translation: What is this, that the olives are picked of themselves and the oil comes to the lamps of itself?

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: This is the word of the LORD unto Zerubbabel
Zechariah.english_translation: This is a sign for you to reassure Zerubbabel: just as the olives and this oil are completed of themselves for all their needs, so not by the army and not by the strength that is in you will you do the building of My house.

I will put My spirit upon Darius, and he will permit you (another version: command you) to build and to do all the needs of the expenses of the building from his own, and to help you with wheat and wine and oil and wood, as is explained in Ezra, so that you will not need the help of man.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: Who art thou, O great mountain before Zerubbabel?
Zechariah.english_translation: The governors beyond the river — Tattenai, governor beyond the river, and Shethar-bozenai and their companions — who stopped the work until now: from now on you will be a plain before Zerubbabel; you have no more authority and greatness over him.
Zechariah.translator_note: The Aramaic words from Ezra 5:3 are translated as printed.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: he shall bring forth the top stone
Zechariah.english_translation: The architect will take the tin stone in his hand, to be architect at the head of the builders, and they will build all according to his words, which he will command, in a beautiful and glorious building.
Zechariah.translator_note: JPS renders the stone of tin (Zechariah 4:10) as “the plummet.”

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: shoutings of Grace, grace, unto it
Zechariah.english_translation: It will be for that stone that everyone will say: How beautiful is this building that is made by means of this plummet-stone! *Teshu’ot chen* is like *teshu’ot noi*, like “*teshu’ot*, full, a tumultuous city” (Isaiah 22), “the voice of uproar” (ibid. 66) — all of them are an expression of making a sound.
Zechariah.translator_note: Rashi cites these words for their root. Printed “Isaiah 22” is Isaiah 22:2 (JPS: “full of uproar, a tumultuous city”); printed “ibid. 66” is Isaiah 66:6 (JPS: “an uproar from the city”).

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: The hands of Zerubbabel have laid the foundation of this house
Zechariah.english_translation: From the beginning to the end, in the days of Cyrus the first.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: his hands shall also finish it
Zechariah.english_translation: It, now. *Tevatzenah* is an expression of finishing, like (ibid.) “when the Lord hath performed His whole work.”
Zechariah.translator_note: Elliptical as printed; understood as “his hands will finish it now.” The printed “(ibid.)” points to Isaiah; Rashi’s words match Isaiah 10:12 (JPS: “when the Lord hath performed His whole work”).

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: who hath despised the day of small things
Zechariah.english_translation: That the House was founded, which was belittled in their eyes, as it says (in Ezra 3), “and many of the priests who had seen the first House, when this House was founded, were weeping in their eyes with a loud voice,” and in the prophecy (Haggai 2), “Is it not as nothing in their eyes?” They will rejoice now when they see the tin stone hanging on the plumb-line that is in the hand of the architect, the head of the builders, with which the cornerstone is aligned; and this will be in the hand of Zerubbabel.
Zechariah.translator_note: Rashi’s quotation of Ezra 3:12 is a loose paraphrase (JPS: “But many of the priests and Levites and heads of fathers’ houses, the old men that had seen the first house standing on its foundation, wept with a loud voice, when this house was before their eyes”). Printed “Haggai 2” is Haggai 2:3.

Zechariah.english_translation: Upon one, seven, in the first foundation that was in the days of Cyrus; and so Targum Jonathan: “seven courses like these.”

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: the eyes of the LORD, that run to and fro
Zechariah.english_translation: And it seemed right to Him to do so, and He saw that this Zerubbabel is fit for the matter.
What do they allude to, and what do the two ears of olives allude to — *טרוק"א* in French: clusters of olives on a branch, like an ear of grain.
Zechariah.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Zechariah 4:12 (“tas (d’olives),” a heap or cluster of olives), in forms such as טרוקט, טרוקש and טרוקאש; the printed form (טרוק"א) differs in its final letter.

Zechariah.english_translation: That is, beside the two spouts, like “See, Joab’s field is near mine” (2 Samuel 14).
Zechariah.translator_note: Printed “2 Samuel 14” is 2 Samuel 14:30; Rashi’s words there read, literally, “by my hand.”

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: empty the golden oil out of themselves
Zechariah.english_translation: This oil, clear and good for shining like gold, as in “Out of the north cometh golden splendour” (Job 37:22).
The horn of the priesthood and of the kingship, who are anointed with the anointing oil.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: that stand by the Lord of the whole earth
Zechariah.english_translation: To request from before Him to restore their greatness.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: These are the two anointed ones
Zechariah.english_translation: The good inclination and the evil inclination, which is turned to good by the merit of the Torah.

Our Rabbis explained: doubled, and said that the Torah was written on it, and they learned from here that the world is one in three thousand two hundred of the Torah, as is found in Eruvin (folio 21); and Targum Jonathan: “a flying scroll,” flying in the air; and according to the plain sense of the passage, it was a scroll of calamity, and it is what he saw (Ezekiel 3), “and there was written within it lamentations, and moaning, and woe.”
Zechariah.translator_note: Printed “Ezekiel 3” is Ezekiel 2:10 (JPS: “and there was written therein lamentations, and moaning, and woe”). The folio number in parentheses is a printed insertion.

Zechariah.english_translation: This one in which is written the retribution for false oaths.

Now from the Holy of Holies, from before the Shekhinah, to go about over the face of the whole land; and this is its length twenty and its breadth ten, like the measure of the opening of the Courtyard and of the Sanctuary, through which it went out.
Until now.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: swept away on the one side like it
