Zechariah.english_translation: From this retribution, as it is explained in it, “cleared” — and retribution was not repaid to individuals who transgressed the Torah, but He waited until the measure of all of them was filled, and they were all stricken as one, in the destruction and in the exile; and so everyone who swears falsely until now has been (cleared) from this retribution, as this scroll declares “cleared,” and it was not repaid; but from here on I have sent it out to wander in the land and to take vengeance on the thieves and those who swear falsely from now on: “and it shall come into the house of the thief,” etc.
Zechariah.translator_note: The explanation is difficult as printed; translated literally.

Zechariah.english_translation: Another one still goes forth, that goes out from the Holy of Holies.
The one that goes forth, which you tell me to see.
That you will see going out, a kind of ephah in which they measure.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: This is their eye in all the land
Zechariah.english_translation: And after I saw it, he said: This is the measure with which they were stricken, those whose eyes are on all the land to rob and to defraud — to make the ephah small and the shekel great — and a se’ah was measured out to them for a se’ah.
I saw that it was lifted up from the earth into the air, the weight of a talent of lead; and I saw further this one woman sitting in the midst of the ephah.

This woman whom you see inside the ephah is the measure of the way of wickedness with which the wicked conduct themselves; and behold, now they are placed in it, to be stricken within the very se’ah in which they measured, measure for measure.
Until now she was sitting, and he cast her and struck her into it — an allusion to sufferings and punishments.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: he cast the weight of lead upon the mouth thereof
Zechariah.english_translation: To sink her, so that they will no longer grow, and their voice will not be heard, to plunder the poor and needy.
From the house.
A white *dayyah*, *וולטויא"ר* in French.
Zechariah.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Zechariah 5:9 (“sorte d’oiseau,” a kind of bird), in forms such as וולטרייר and וולוטור; the printed form (וולטויא"ר) is close to these. Rashi’s word דייה is left transliterated.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: when it is prepared, she shall be set there
Zechariah.english_translation: And the house was prepared and the ephah was placed there, with the wicked in it.
In that house.

On their setting, and on its base. Here he hinted to him that through the iniquity of Israel, that they measured with the se’ah of transgressions and wickedness, they were stricken with that same measure; and two nations that reigned as one came — they are Babylon and the Chaldeans, the army of Nebuchadnezzar — and exiled them to Babylon; and there they stood fixed on the base of the setting that was fixed for them, namely, until seventy years were completed, until now that they have returned. And this explanation is after Jonathan in part; and there are several ways in which they interpret it, but they have not settled for me. And our Rabbis explained it and learned from here that the evil inclination was delivered to the Men of the Great Assembly, and they cast it into a lead pot and sealed it with lead, because its voice carries, as is found in Sanhedrin and in tractate Yoma. And as for my interpreting the kingdom of Nebuchadnezzar as the doubling of two nations, I saw in the Midrash on Psalms that these four kingdoms that enslaved Israel were doubled: Babylon and the Chaldeans, Media and Persia, Antiochus and Macedon, Edom and Ishmael; and on this basis Kalir composed, “The fourth is the eighth, over Edom.”
Zechariah.translator_note: The Aramaic words in the Talmudic quotation are translated as printed.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: the mountains were mountains of brass
Zechariah.english_translation: A sign of the strength of these kingdoms, which came to them from between two mountains, which is hard and mighty — for these four chariots are the messengers of the Holy One, blessed be He, to give dominion to the four kingdoms: Babylon, Media, Greece and Edom.
They are the ones that carried Babylon, which is red, as it is written, “Thou art the head of gold” (Daniel 2:38).
To carry Media, who blackened the faces of Israel in the days of Haman.
To carry Persia, who built the Temple.
They are spotted, to carry Greece, who afflicted Israel with various decrees, differing one from another.
To carry Ishmael (another version: Edom); and I do not know what the expression *amutzim* means; and Jonathan translated *ketamnin*.
The princes of the idolaters, the ancient kingdoms that rule in the four winds of heaven.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: after presenting themselves before the Lord of all the earth
Zechariah.english_translation: They came before Him, and He gave them permission from His own mouth to rule.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: the black horses goeth forth toward the north country
Zechariah.english_translation: To carry Media; and about the red ones he did not write “go forth,” for the dominion of Babylon had already ended.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: the white went forth after them
Zechariah.english_translation: To carry Persia; both of them in the north, and they ruled over Babylon.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: the grizzled went forth toward the south country
Zechariah.english_translation: To carry Greece, and they took the kingdom from the hand of Persia; and in its interpretation by Rav Saadiah on Daniel I saw that “the king of the Negev” is the king of Greece.
Zechariah.translator_note: JPS renders הנגב in Daniel 11:5 as “the south.”

Zechariah.english_translation: Of Him, that the length of their dominion be great, to go through all the land.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: Get you hence, walk to and fro through the earth
Zechariah.english_translation: He gave them permission to rule with great dominion, and that is the kingdom of Edom.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: they that go toward the north country
Zechariah.english_translation: To carry Media and Persia.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: have eased My spirit in the north country
Zechariah.english_translation: They quieted My wrath in Babylon, who destroyed Belshazzar and the seed of Nebuchadnezzar; it is that which was said (Isaiah 48), “He whom the LORD loveth shall perform His pleasure on Babylon,” etc.
Zechariah.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 48” is Isaiah 48:14.

Zechariah.english_translation: All these men.

He is Zerubbabel, mentioned above, “Behold, I will bring forth My servant the Shoot,” and after the name, because his greatness sprouted little by little; and some interpret it of the King Messiah, but all this matter speaks of the Second Temple.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: shall shoot up out of his place
Zechariah.english_translation: From the seed of the kingship.
The glory of princeship.
The high priest on the seat of the priesthood.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: the counsel of peace shall be between them both
Zechariah.english_translation: The prince and the priest will love one another.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: the crowns shall be to Helem
Zechariah.english_translation: It is an inverted verse: and the crowns shall be in the Temple of HaShem as a good memorial for Helem and for Tobijah, who donated the silver and the gold; and those crowns were hanging in the windows at the height of the Sanctuary, as we learned in tractate Middot.
He is Heldai.
And this thing will be for you: “if you will diligently hearken,” etc.
On her behalf, and you will not need to fast and to mourn; and so at the end of the matter, “the fast of the fifth,” and so on.
They will need a staff in their hands.
In their eyes, the great kindness that I will do for them.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: should it also be marvellous in Mine eyes?
Zechariah.english_translation: How I turned back from the great wrath; and our Rabbis expounded it concerning the slaughter of the evil inclination, in tractate Sukkah: “in My eyes it will be wondrous” how the righteous will be able to stand against it during their lifetime.
To build and to complete, and do not fear the people of the land who weaken your hands and frighten you from building, as is explained in the book of Ezra (Ezra 4:4).

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: you that hear in these days
Zechariah.english_translation: In the fourth year of Darius.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: these words from the mouth of the prophets
Zechariah.english_translation: Of consolations from the mouths of the prophets who prophesied to them then, on the day the house of HaShem was founded, in the second year of Darius — the words to begin the work. For those prophets were tested in their eyes by their words, that they are true prophets; and therefore they are worthy to be relied upon even in the words of consolation of now. And by what did they test them? For “before those days the hire of man,” etc.; and they prophesied to you that when you begin the work blessing will come upon the work of your hands, and their words were fulfilled, for now it is not as in the former days.
Concerning that which I purposed to bring upon you, to turn back [from it]; rather, I brought it so; I will not repent of the good that I purposed for you.
Zechariah.translator_note: The printed sentence lacks a negative before “to turn back”; the bracketed words are my understanding of it.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: the judgment of truth and peace
Zechariah.english_translation: It is compromise.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: let none of you devise evil in your hearts against his neighbour
Zechariah.english_translation: He warned them about baseless hatred, and that is what destroyed the Second Temple.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: The fast of the fourth month
Zechariah.english_translation: The fast of Tammuz, which is the fourth of the months.
Of Av.
The third of Tishrei, on which Gedaliah was killed.
Of Tevet.
From seventy languages — behold, seven hundred for each corner; behold, for the four corners of the garment, two thousand eight hundred.

Rabbi Judah bar Ilai expounded: This is the Messiah, who is sharp (*chad*) to the idolaters and soft (*rach*) to Israel. Rabbi Yose ben Durmaskit said to him: Judah, my son, until when will you pervert the Scriptures against us? I testify concerning myself, heaven and earth, that I am from Damascus, and there is a place whose name is Hadrach; and how do I fulfil “and Damascus shall be His resting-place”? That Jerusalem is destined to reach as far as Damascus, and His resting-place is none other than Jerusalem, as it is said, “This is My resting-place for ever” (Psalms 132). He said to him: And how do I fulfil “and the city shall be built on its mound”? He said to him: That it is not destined to move from its place. Thus a baraita is taught in Sifrei.
Zechariah.translator_note: Printed “Psalms 132” is Psalms 132:14.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: For the LORD’S is the eye of man
Zechariah.english_translation: For on that day man will turn toward his Maker, and his eyes will look toward the Holy One, blessed be He, as it said above, “We will go with you”; and they and their cities will be joined to the cities of Israel.

Are esteemed by HaShem above all the ancient nations; similarly, “And Solomon loved many foreign women, and the daughter of Pharaoh” (1 Kings 11) — was not the daughter of Pharaoh included? But the daughter of Pharaoh was dearer to him than all of them. Here too: all the nations will be HaShem’s, and Israel against all of them.
Zechariah.translator_note: Printed “1 Kings 11” is 1 Kings 11:1. JPS reads “Now king Solomon loved many foreign women, besides the daughter of Pharaoh”; Rashi’s explanation relies on reading the Hebrew word as “and.”

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: And Hamath also shall border thereon
Zechariah.english_translation: Her border will reach the border of Jerusalem.
These too are her daughters, even though she is very wise — for she made herself very wise and thinks to be mighty forever by her wisdom.
Zechariah.translator_note: Which city “her” refers to is not stated in the printed text; translated literally.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: And Tyre did build herself a stronghold
Zechariah.english_translation: And she says: Who will bring me down to the ground?

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: heaped up silver as the dust
Zechariah.english_translation: And she boasts of her wealth.
A kind of appearance of gold.
Who rules over all.
An expression of “maketh poor, and maketh rich” (1 Samuel 2).
Zechariah.translator_note: Rashi cites the word for its root. Printed “1 Samuel 2” is 1 Samuel 2:7.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: And He will smite her power into the sea
Zechariah.english_translation: And swallow her wealth into the seas; He will bring up the sea against her and drown her, as Ezekiel said.
The fall of Tyre, and fear.
She too will fear.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: for her expectation shall be ashamed
Zechariah.english_translation: For she was leaning on Tyre, which was the head of the sons of Esau, and Ekron too is Edom’s, as our Rabbis said in tractate Megillah (folio 6, ע"ש), and at first it was the Philistines’.
Zechariah.translator_note: The abbreviation ע"ש in the printed folio reference is left as printed. The folio reference in parentheses is a printed insertion.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: a bastard shall dwell in Ashdod
Zechariah.english_translation: “And a foreign people shall dwell in Ashdod” — they are Israel, who were strangers in it.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: I will take away his blood out of his mouth
Zechariah.english_translation: Of Esau: these are their *bet bimah*, where they used to throw the blood of their sacrifices; and some interpret it of the shedding of blood, in that he used to shed the blood of Israel.
Zechariah.translator_note: The term בית בימה is left transliterated.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: he also shall be a remnant for our God
Zechariah.english_translation: These are the synagogues and study halls in the Diaspora.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: he shall be as a chief in Judah
Zechariah.english_translation: These are their *tratiyot* and *kirkasiyot* (theaters and circuses), in which the princes of Judah will in the future teach Torah in public.
An expression of *aluf* and of learning (*lemud*).
Will be for Israel.
Jerusalem.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: I will encamp about My house
Zechariah.english_translation: I will encamp beside My house to protect it from those who set up a fortress and a destroyer, that they not besiege it; and its parallel, “and all her host (*tzeva’ah*) and her bulwark” (Isaiah 29); and further, it can be interpreted that *matzevah* is like *matzva* with an aleph.
Zechariah.translator_note: Rashi cites these words for their root. Printed “Isaiah 29” is Isaiah 29:7 (JPS: “all that war against her, and the bulwarks about her”).

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: For now have I seen with Mine eyes
Zechariah.english_translation: Their distress is before My eyes, even though until now I hid My face from them.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: Behold, thy king cometh unto thee
Zechariah.english_translation: It is impossible to interpret it except of the King Messiah, of whom it is said, “And his dominion shall be from sea to sea,” and we do not find a ruler of Israel like this in the days of the Second Temple.
By HaShem.
Humble.
It is the attribute of humility.
Like “and ten foals” (Genesis 32).
Zechariah.translator_note: Printed “Reshit 32” is Genesis 32:16; Rashi cites the word for its root.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: I will cut off the chariot
Zechariah.english_translation: So that they will not need it.
And a rule of his.
From the sea to the west, to the end of the world.
The Euphrates.

You too will be saved with him, as he is “triumphant and victorious”; for “because of the blood of thy covenant” — behold, I have prophesied to you for the future, and also now, from the exile of Babylon in which you are now.
Zechariah.translator_note: The sentence is difficult as printed; translated literally.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: because of the blood of thy covenant
Zechariah.english_translation: By the merit of the blood of the covenant that was sprinkled upon you at Sinai: “Behold the blood of the covenant which He made.”
Zechariah.translator_note: The quotation matches Exodus 24:8, which reads in JPS “Behold the blood of the covenant, which the LORD hath made with you.”

Zechariah.english_translation: From the exile.

To your strength and to your honor — even though you are now under the authority of the kings of Persia, you are prisoners of hope, who have hoped for Me until now for My word to be fulfilled at the end of seventy years.
Yet today I tell you a second tiding, besides this one of the building. And what is the second tiding? That I am returning to do a second time for you.
Zechariah.translator_note: The phrase שאני שב לשנות לכם is rendered by its sense (“to do a second time”).

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: For I bend Judah for Me
Zechariah.english_translation: In the end Antiochus will take the kingship from the hand of the kings of Persia and will do evil to you, and I will bend Judah to be to Me like a war bow, and they will fight with Antiochus in the days of the Hasmoneans.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: I fill the bow with Ephraim
Zechariah.english_translation: It is an elliptical verse: like “I have filled the hand of the bow with Ephraim,” like (2 Kings 9) “and Jehu filled his hand with the bow”; Ephraim will be to Me like a quiver full of arrows.
Zechariah.translator_note: Printed “Kings II 9” is 2 Kings 9:24; the Hebrew idiom there is rendered by JPS “Jehu drew his bow with his full strength.”

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: I will stir up thy sons, O Zion
Zechariah.english_translation: Against the army of Antiochus.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: the LORD shall be seen over them
Zechariah.english_translation: In the book of Yosippon we find that at that time a wonder was seen by the people of Jerusalem.
He will thunder.
To storm the men of the south (*Teman*) — they are the army of Antiochus; and some of our Rabbis interpreted it of Edom in the future to come.
The spoil of their enemies.
Beneath them, sling-stones — these are the Greeks, who are trained in the bow and in slinging with a stone.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: make a noise as through wine
Zechariah.english_translation: Murmuring in a voice of joy and gladness, as those drunk with wine murmur.
Their souls with all good.
Which is full of blood before the altar.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: like the corners of the altar
Zechariah.english_translation: On which they pour wine there, and the wine floats upon it, as we learned in tractate Sukkah; an expression of satiety, an expression of drunkenness.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: As the flock of His people
Zechariah.english_translation: Like a flock that He moved out of Egypt to be a people for Him.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: For they shall be as the stones of a crown
Zechariah.english_translation: For the priests, the sons of the Hasmoneans, who take pride in the stones of the crown — in the rows of the breastplate and of the ephod — will be displayed with miracles upon their land.
Great is His goodness — that which is hidden away for that generation.
Zechariah.translator_note: Rashi’s printed word is טובו (“His goodness”); the verse is rendered by JPS “their goodness.”

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: Corn shall make the young men flourish
Zechariah.english_translation: That gives strength to young men.
That makes maidens bloom with the sound of song and gladness; and some interpret: that sprouts and grows in virgin soil, and it is choice wine.
Zechariah.translator_note: The source lemma (ותירוש, “new wine”) falls at the start of JPS Zechariah 10:1; a phrase from the JPS verse of this id is used.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: Ask you of the LORD rain
Zechariah.english_translation: If you need.
Clouds that bring rain.
Zechariah.translator_note: JPS renders חזיזים as “lightnings”; Rashi’s gloss differs.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: To every one grass in the field
Zechariah.english_translation: On account of one man and on account of one blade of grass that needs rain.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: For the teraphim have spoken vanity
Zechariah.english_translation: “And the diviners have seen a lie, and the dreams” that misled your fathers, saying “I have dreamed,” and they strengthened their hands to rebel against the Holy One, blessed be He — “they spoke iniquity and vanity; they spoke, saying: Peace, and there is no peace.”

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: they go their way like sheep
Zechariah.english_translation: But I prophesy to them truthfully.
They will be humbled, like *la’anot mipnei*, an expression of affliction (*oni*).
Zechariah.translator_note: Rashi cites the word for its root.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: Mine anger is kindled against the shepherds
Zechariah.english_translation: Against the kings of Nebuchadnezzar and Sennacherib (another version: the kings of Greece).

Against their princes; and so Targum Jonathan: “and against the kings My wrath was, and against the rulers I rage”; and idolaters are likened to he-goats, “and the he-goat, the rough one, is the king of Antiochus” (Daniel 8); and one who wishes to explain the matter not as of the kings of the idolaters would say: “he-goats” is an expression of “princes,” as in “It stirs up for thee the shades, all the chief ones of the earth” (Isaiah 14).
Zechariah.translator_note: Rashi’s quotation of Daniel 8:21 differs from the verse (JPS: “the rough he-goat is the king of Greece”). Rashi cites the word atudim for its meaning; printed “Isaiah 14” is Isaiah 14:9 (JPS: “The shades are stirred up for thee, Even all the chief ones of the earth”).

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: as His majestic horse in the battle
Zechariah.english_translation: Like a horse whose majesty is recognized in battle.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: Out of them shall come forth the corner-stone
Zechariah.english_translation: From them their kings, from them their princes, from them the fighters of their wars.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: as mighty men, Treading down in the mire of the streets in the battle
Zechariah.english_translation: Behold, this verse is inverted: and in the battle they will be going and treading down men, like mighty men who tread down the mire of the streets. *Bosim* means treading, like “do we tread them under” (Psalms 44), “They have trodden My portion under foot” (Jeremiah 12).
Zechariah.translator_note: Rashi cites these words for their root. Printed “Psalms 44” is Psalms 44:6 (JPS: “Through Thy name do we tread them under that rise up against us”); Rashi’s printed word is יבוס, the verse’s is נבוס. Printed “Jeremiah 12” is Jeremiah 12:10.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: the riders on horses shall be confounded
Zechariah.english_translation: [They shall put to shame:] the house of Judah — the riders of horses who come to fight against them.
Zechariah.translator_note: The printed comment is a brief gloss on the verb והובישו; the bracketed words are my understanding of it.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: And I will strengthen the house of Judah
Zechariah.english_translation: In the war of the Greeks.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: I will save the house of Joseph
Zechariah.english_translation: In the place to which they were exiled — in Halah and in Habor — in the days of Sennacherib.
Like *ve-hoshavtim*, an expression of dwelling.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: they shall be as though I had not cast them off
Zechariah.english_translation: As though I had never cast them off.
In the manner of those who whistle as a sign, a signal for one who has gone astray on the road to come to them.
At the time of the end, in the future.
When I redeem them.
In exile, as they increased in Egypt.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: I will sow them among the peoples
Zechariah.english_translation: At first among the nations, like a man who sows a se’ah in order to bring in many kor.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: they shall live with their children
Zechariah.english_translation: With their children.
That is the Temple.
“And it shall not suffice them.”

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: And over the sea affliction shall pass
Zechariah.english_translation: And affliction shall pass over Tyre, which sits in the midst of the sea, and it is the head of the kingdom of Tyre.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: the waves shall be smitten in the sea
Zechariah.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He, who is the Smiter, will smite the waves in the sea, to sink Tyre.
It is Egypt.
Targum Jonathan: “Open, O nations, your gates.”

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: Wail, O cypress-tree, for the cedar is fallen
Zechariah.english_translation: For it is greater than the cypress: wail, O rulers, for the kings from the idolaters have fallen.
*chaisnes* [printed קישנ"ש] in French (oaks).
Zechariah.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Zechariah 11:2 under the entry “Cliens,” for אלוני, in forms such as קשניש, קשנש and קישכש; the reading *chaisnes* is from Darmesteter’s index; the printed form (קישנ"ש) is a variant spelling. The gloss “oaks” follows the Hebrew word glossed (*elonei*).

Zechariah.english_translation: For it was broken; and similar to it, “it shall hail, when the forest cometh down.”
Zechariah.translator_note: Rashi’s words match Isaiah 32:19 (JPS: “But it shall hail, when the forest cometh down”).

Zechariah.english_translation: The forest of the fortress; in the Aramaic: the strength of the cities.
The kings.
Their splendor.
The princes will weep.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: For the thickets of the Jordan are spoiled
Zechariah.english_translation: Which is the place of young lions and lions. And our Rabbis explained: “Open thy doors, O Lebanon” — the prophet prophesied about the destruction of the Second Temple; and forty years before the destruction the doors of the Sanctuary used to open of themselves; Rabbi Yochanan ben Zakkai rebuked them, said to them: Sanctuary, Sanctuary, until when will you frighten yourself? I know that your end is to be destroyed, and Zechariah the son of Iddo already prophesied about you: “Open thy doors, O Lebanon,” etc.
Prepare shepherds for them; that is: prophesy concerning their leaders, who are destined to shepherd them from now on.
Israel, whom their shepherds slaughter and devour.

The Babylonians, whom [שאגלם] into their midst. This one sells them, and the buyer kills and does not set it to his heart that he has guilt in the matter; and their seller boasts: Blessed be HaShem, who delivered them into my hand, and behold, I am rich.
Zechariah.translator_note: The word שאגלם is unclear as printed (perhaps “who exiled them”); it is left as printed.

Zechariah.english_translation: And behold, I am rich.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: So I fed the flock of slaughter
Zechariah.english_translation: All these are the words of the Holy One, blessed be He, to the prophet: And I shepherded them in the ancient days.
True, they were the poor of the flock when I began to shepherd them.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: I took unto me two staves
Zechariah.english_translation: In the end of days I divided them into two kingdoms because of their iniquity.
Jeroboam said: to lead them gently.
Rehoboam said to them to chastise them with scorpions; and because it is the way to lead sheep with staffs, He called their rulers “staffs.”

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: I cut off the three shepherds in one month
Zechariah.english_translation: And they corrupted their ways until I loathed them and killed them in one month, all three shepherds whom he killed — namely all the house of Ahab, and the house of Ahaziah king of Judah, and his brothers, and all the seed of the kingdom of David; and Athaliah destroyed the rest except Joash, who was hidden (2 Kings 9).
Zechariah.translator_note: The reference in parentheses is a printed insertion.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: My soul became impatient of them
Zechariah.english_translation: I loathed them; and every expression of *kotzer nefesh* is a matter of distress or a matter of loathing that the mind cannot bear, and a shortness of the heart and bowels from containing, as Elihu said, “The spirit within me constraineth me” (Job 32:18).

Their remembrance was heavy in my bowels and filled my spirit and constricted my belly. And *bachalah*: our Rabbis explained it as an expression of growth, in tractate Niddah: the Sages made a parable about a woman: *pagah*, *bochel*, *tzamel*; *pagah* — while she is still a child; *bochel* — these are the days of youth, when she has already grown; and they brought this verse as proof for their words.
I said in those days: I will cast them away from before Me, and they will be ownerless and for plunder.

I broke the might of the kings of Israel in the days of Jehoahaz the son of Jehu, until the king of Aram destroyed them and made them like the dust in threshing (2 Kings 13:7), and in the days of Hoshea the son of Elah, when I delivered them into the hand of Sennacherib and he exiled them (ibid. 17).

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: that I might break My covenant which I had made with all the peoples
Zechariah.english_translation: To show them that because they betrayed Me I broke My covenant that I made with all the peoples concerning them, that they not harm them — for on this condition I gave them the Torah: that if they keep it they will be free from the kingdoms, so that no nation and tongue will rule over them. And do not wonder if the verse speaks of their salvation from the hand of an enemy in the language of making a covenant with the enemy, for we find a parallel verse: “And in that day will I make a covenant for them with the beasts of the field,” etc.
Zechariah.translator_note: The quotation matches Hosea 2:20 (JPS: “And in that day will I make a covenant for them With the beasts of the field”).

Zechariah.english_translation: So the righteous among them, who keep My statutes, understood.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: it was the word of the LORD
Zechariah.english_translation: This decree the Holy One, blessed be He, already spoke to us through Moses: “The LORD will bring thee and thy king.”
Zechariah.translator_note: The quotation matches Deuteronomy 28:36 (JPS: “The LORD will bring thee, and thy king whom thou shalt set over thee”).

Zechariah.english_translation: To the remaining kings of Judah.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: If you think good, give me my hire
Zechariah.english_translation: Keep My commandments, and that will be My wage for all the good that I gave you, as they give a wage to the shepherd of a flock, and I will return and shepherd you.
And I too will not do good to you; and so we find that the Holy One, blessed be He, said (to Ezekiel 6), “He that heareth, let him hear, and he that forbeareth, let him forbear.”
Zechariah.translator_note: Printed “Ezekiel 6” is Ezekiel 3:27 (JPS: “he that heareth, let him hear, and he that forbeareth, let him forbear”).

Zechariah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “and they did My will, men.” Some good people — a few among them did My will, such as the craftsman and the smith: Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah, Ezekiel. And the expression “thirty pieces of silver” I do not know how to fit here, but *kesef* is an expression of longing; and our Rabbis too explained it so in Chullin, and they brought as proof “The bundle of silver he took in his hand” (Proverbs 7:20). And the “thirty” they explained: there are שמ"ה righteous in every generation, and they brought proof from *chomer se’orim* and *letech se’orim*: fifteen in Babylon and thirty in the Land of Israel, as it is said, “And I took the thirty pieces of silver and cast them into the house of the LORD,” in the Land of Israel; and the source of the number thirty — an aggadic Midrash: that Abraham our father was promised thus, that there would not be a generation with fewer than thirty righteous; from where? “So shall thy seed be” — *yihyeh* in gematria is thirty.
Zechariah.translator_note: The abbreviation שמ"ה in “there are שמ"ה righteous” is not resolved and is left as printed. Rashi’s quotation of Zechariah 11:13 is adapted. Proverbs 7:20 reads in JPS: “He hath taken the bag of money with him”; Rashi cites it for the root of “silver” as longing. The Aramaic is translated as printed.

Zechariah.english_translation: Like *el ha-otzar*, the keeper of the treasury. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to the prophet: Write and place these — they and their righteousness — to be kept until the end of the seventy years of the Babylonian exile, and the Temple [ב"ה] will be built by them; and what is the treasury? *Adar ha-yakar* — My Sanctuary, *adar tifarti*.
Zechariah.translator_note: JPS renders אדר היקר as “the goodly price.” The abbreviation ב"ה is read as “the Temple” from the context (the printed form is kept in brackets); the expansion is not confirmed by a permitted source, so the comment is flagged.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: that I was prized at of them
Zechariah.english_translation: That I removed from upon them, from being precious to them. And the expression *yakarti* is a removal of honor, and the mem of *me’aleihem* will prove it, and it is like “and root thee out of the land of the living” (Psalms 52), like “lopping the bough” (Isaiah 10); and the parallel of the interpretation I have interpreted is somewhat like the Targum of Jonathan; and I have seen many versions for the explanation of this prophecy, and I am unable to settle them.
Zechariah.translator_note: Rashi’s citations here correspond to Psalms 52:7 (JPS: “And root thee out of the land of the living”) and Isaiah 10:33 (JPS: “Shall lop the boughs”; Rashi’s printed word is פורה).

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: I cut asunder mine other staff
Zechariah.english_translation: I exiled Zedekiah.
The wicked of his generation, for he was righteous and his generation was wicked.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: the brotherhood between Judah and Israel might be broken
Zechariah.english_translation: That the sons of Judah and Benjamin became joined and clung to the abominations of the kings of Israel.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: Take unto thee yet the instruments of a foolish shepherd
Zechariah.english_translation: And this is what He said to him above, “Feed the flock of slaughter” — it is a sign that I am destined to deliver the generation of the destruction of this Second Temple into the hand of Titus.
The lost ones — the shepherd will not take note to seek them.
Targum Jonathan: “those who have wandered he will not seek.” The *na’ar*: the silly ones that do not know how to come to the fold.
That has some strength to stand on its feet, and needs help to lead it slowly; and Menachem explained: swollen, an expression of “to make thy belly to swell.”
Zechariah.translator_note: Rashi cites the word for its root; the quotation matches Numbers 5:22 (JPS: “and make thy belly to swell”).

Zechariah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan translated: “he will not support”; and the way of the shepherd is to carry in his bosom.
Zechariah.translator_note: The closing phrase echoes Isaiah 40:11.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: he will eat the flesh of the fat
Zechariah.english_translation: He will finish off the money of the wealthy.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: will break their hoofs in pieces
Zechariah.english_translation: Until finished; and similar to this Daniel said: “it devoured and broke in pieces, and stamped the residue with its feet.”
Zechariah.translator_note: The Aramaic is translated as printed; the wording matches Daniel 7:7 and 7:19.

Zechariah.english_translation: One should cry out over this one.

A shepherd of nothing; *elil* is an expression of *al* (“not”) — he is not a shepherd; and so “physicians of no value” (Job 13). *Ro’i ha-elil*: the yod is superfluous in place of the heh, like “that leaveth the flock” (here), “him that dwelt in the bush” (Deuteronomy 33), “that dwell solitarily” (Micah 6).
Zechariah.translator_note: Rashi’s gloss אליל ל' אל is understood as a negation. Printed “Deuteronomy 33” is Deuteronomy 33:16; printed “Micah 6” is Micah 7:14; Rashi’s printed word שכני לבדד is שוכני לבדד in the verse. Printed “Job 13” is Job 13:4; Rashi’s printed word רופאי is רפאי in the verse.

Zechariah.english_translation: He gives them up, ownerless, into the hand of anyone who comes to strike and to kill and to plunder.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: The sword shall be upon his arm
Zechariah.english_translation: And it is the shepherd who carries a slaughtering knife in his hand to slaughter the fat and the healthy, on whom he set his right eye, to know who are the rich, to plunder and finish their property.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: His arm shall be clean dried up
Zechariah.english_translation: In the world to come: “and I will lay My vengeance,” etc. (Ezekiel 28); and those who interpret it interpret it of Zedekiah, by the name (Jeremiah 22) “and the eyes of Zedekiah he put out” — blind; but it is impossible to fit “Behold, I raise up a shepherd in the land” to Zedekiah, for seventy years had already passed for him.
Zechariah.translator_note: The last clause is difficult as printed; translated literally. Printed “Ezekiel 28”: Rashi’s words match Ezekiel 25:14 (JPS: “And I will lay My vengeance upon Edom”), not Ezekiel 28. Printed “Jeremiah 22”: the quotation matches Jeremiah 39:7 (JPS: “Moreover he put out Zedekiah’s eyes”).

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: The burden of the word of the LORD
Zechariah.english_translation: This completes the matter that he began to speak concerning the punishment of those who devour Israel — upon Babylon and the like.

A vessel of poison, like “in the blood that is in the basin” (*ba-saf*, Exodus 12:22). *Ra’al* is an expression of desolation that stops up the heart and the limbs, so that they have no strength, like a person wrapped in a garment, like “*ha-brosh’im hor’alu*” (Nahum 2:4), “*ha-sheirot ve-ha-ra’alot*” (Isaiah 6); and in the language of the Mishnah we find “*madiyot re’ulot*” — *envolopement* [printed אונבלופמנט"א] in French (a wrapping).
Zechariah.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Zechariah 12:2 (“Vertige, engourdissement qui rend l’homme impuissant comme s’il était enveloppé dans un vêtement”), in forms such as אינוולופמנט; the reading is *envolopement*, from Darmesteter’s footnote; the printed form (אונבלופמנט"א) is a variant spelling. Printed “Isaiah 6” is Isaiah 3:19 (JPS: “the pendants, and the bracelets, and the veils”). Rashi cites Nahum 2:4 and Isaiah 3:19 for the root, so the words are left transliterated; JPS Nahum 2:4: “the cypress spears are made to quiver.” The Mishnaic phrase *madiyot re’ulot* is left transliterated.

Zechariah.english_translation: The idolaters who will be besieging Jerusalem will compel the house of David within, and idolaters will besiege them; and the children of Judah too will come against their will to besiege Jerusalem. So Targum Jonathan.
Zechariah.translator_note: The Targum reference is translated as the printed text gives it.

Zechariah.english_translation: A stone of load that is laid on people by order of the ruler, to carry it and bear it on the shoulders, and it is very heavy, so that all who bear it will be sorely wounded.
Those who besiege it, with madness; and their riders, with blindness. But for the house of Judah, who are among the besiegers against their will, I will open My eyes to protect them from this plague.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: the chiefs of Judah shall say in their heart
Zechariah.english_translation: When they see the other besiegers struck by this plague while they are saved.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: The inhabitants of Jerusalem are my strength
Zechariah.english_translation: The inhabitants of Jerusalem, who know that we come against them against our will, have strengthened themselves to help me by their prayer to HaShem their God.
They will return and fight with those who brought them there.
Like the burning of a great fire; *kiyor* is an expression of *kirah* (stove), and so Menachem connected it.
In her place.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: save the tents of Judah first
Zechariah.english_translation: Before the people of Jerusalem go out of the city, they will have deliverance to return to their tents and their houses; and afterwards deliverance will come to the people of the city. That is the deliverance of which it is said, “Then shall the LORD go forth, and fight” (below, 14).
Zechariah.translator_note: Rashi’s quotation is Zechariah 14:3 (JPS: “Then shall the LORD go forth, And fight against those nations”); the printed “14” is the chapter.

Zechariah.english_translation: To boast over them and say: You were saved only because of us.
The weakest among them.
Like great ones, like angels.
Zechariah.translator_note: Rashi gives the Aramaic *rabrevin ke-malakhin*; translated as printed.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: the angel of the LORD before them
Zechariah.english_translation: They shall prosper like an angel of HaShem before them.
Zechariah.translator_note: This is the Aramaic of Targum Jonathan (*yitzlechun ke-malakha de-HaShem kadmeihon*); translated as printed.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: I will seek to destroy all the nations
Zechariah.english_translation: I will seek in their destruction and scrutinize their iniquity. But our Rabbis explained it for merit: “I will seek” in their favor — if they have merit I will leave them, and if not I will destroy them.
Zechariah.translator_note: The printed phrase בנוגני שלהם is unclear; translated as “in their favor” from the sense of the continuation.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: spirit of grace and of supplication
Zechariah.english_translation: That it will arise in their spirit to supplicate before Me, and they will find favor in My eyes.
*talant* [printed טלנ"ט] in French.
Zechariah.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Zechariah 12:10 under “Esprit,” in forms such as טלנט; the reading is *talant*, from Darmesteter’s footnote; the printed form (טלנ"ט) matches. Darmesteter files it under “Esprit” (spirit).

Zechariah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan translated: “and they will pray before Me because they were exiled.”
Zechariah.translator_note: The Aramaic is translated as printed; the Targum’s verb *itlatlu* (“were exiled”) is taken from the printed text.

Zechariah.english_translation: To lament over those whom the nations pierced and killed among them in exile.
Over that killing.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: as one mourneth for his only son
Zechariah.english_translation: As a man laments over his only son. And our Rabbis expounded it of Messiah the son of Joseph who was killed, in tractate Sukkah.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: the mourning of Hadadrimmon in the valley of Megiddon
Zechariah.english_translation: The matter of Hadadrimmon in the valley of Megiddo is not as it seems; rather, there are two mournings: like the mourning for Ahab the son of Omri, whom Hadadrimmon the son of Tabrimmon killed at Ramoth-gilead, as it is said, “And there went a cry throughout the host” (1 Kings 22:36), and that is a lament; and like the mourning for Josiah the son of Amon, whom Pharaoh the lame killed in the valley of Megiddo, as it is said, “And Jeremiah lamented for Josiah” etc., “and all the singing men and singing women spoke of Josiah in their lamentations” etc. (2 Chronicles 35).
Zechariah.translator_note: The Aramaic phrases in the original (*ke-mispeda de-Ach’av bar Omri de-katal yatei Hadadrimmon bar Tabrimmon*, etc.) are translated as printed. The quotations match 1 Kings 22:36 and 2 Chronicles 35:25 (JPS: “And Jeremiah lamented for Josiah; and all the singing men and singing women spoke of Josiah in their lamentations”).

Zechariah.english_translation: The prophet; and some say Nathan the son of David, as it is said (1 Samuel 5), “Shammua, and Shobab, and Nathan, and Solomon.”
Zechariah.translator_note: Printed “1 Samuel 5” is 2 Samuel 5:14 (JPS: “Shammua, and Shobab, and Nathan, and Solomon”); Rashi’s printed form is שמוע ושובב ונתן.

Zechariah.english_translation: The priests and the Levites.
Shimea the son of David. At first the verse included the families of the house of David, and afterwards it specified each one.
Zechariah.translator_note: Rashi’s “Shammua” is the Shimea of 1 Chronicles 3:5 (JPS: “Shimea”).

Zechariah.english_translation: Of the house of David.

Out of modesty. And why the families of the priesthood and of the kingdom? To restore their crowns to them, as it is said at the beginning of the book, “These are the two anointed ones, that stand by the Lord of the whole earth.”
Zechariah.translator_note: The quotation is Zechariah 4:14 (JPS: “These are the two anointed ones, that stand by the Lord of the whole earth”).

Zechariah.english_translation: For the sprinkling of purification; and so Targum Jonathan: “I will forgive their sins, as one is purified with the waters of sprinkling and with the ashes of the red heifer of the sin-offering, with the ash of the sin-offering.”
False prophets.
The evil inclination.
So is the way of those who entice and lead astray: they wrap themselves in their cloaks as if they were righteous men, in order that their lies be accepted.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: I have been made a bondman from my youth
Zechariah.english_translation: Menachem interpreted it as an expression of owning cattle and sheep: for I am like all other people, not occupied with prophecy; from my youth he appointed me to keep his cattle.
Between your shoulders; there is where those who commit a transgression are flogged.
Those who loved me and rebuked me to bring me to the straight path.
Against the one whom I appointed over the flock of My exile.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: the man that is near unto Me
Zechariah.english_translation: Whom I joined to Me to guard My flock as I do.
The king of wicked Rome.
That is subdued under his hand.
And I will repeat My blows a second time.

The young rulers, below the kings. And Jonathan translated, “and the sheep shall be scattered,” as “and the rulers shall be scattered,” and he translated “the little ones” as their appointed officers, the second to them. And so Targum Jonathan on this verse concerns the nations: “The sword is revealed against the king of Babylon and against the rulers, his companions who are like him. Thus says HaShem of hosts: Kill the king of Babylon, and the rulers will be scattered.” But this language of the Targum cannot apply to Israel, for we do not find in the Targum or in Scripture “rulers” for Israel except king and princes, and their Targum is *rabrevin*.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: the third shall be left therein
Zechariah.english_translation: They will convert and live.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: I will bring the third part through the fire
Zechariah.english_translation: “And I will bring the third in the furnace of fire”: that some of the proselytes from the idolaters will suffer and bear the birth-pangs of the Messiah and the wars of Gog and Magog with Israel, and from there they will be tested whether they are true proselytes; for many of those who converted at first will return to their former ways and join Gog, as stated in the Aggadah.
Zechariah.translator_note: “As stated in the Aggadah” refers to a source not named in the text.

Zechariah.english_translation: When he prays, he will pray to HaShem and not to his former god.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: When thy spoil shall be divided
Zechariah.english_translation: “Behold, a day [of the LORD cometh]”: beloved to the Holy One, blessed be He.
Zechariah.translator_note: The words Rashi comments on, “Behold, a day of the LORD cometh,” stand at the end of Zechariah 13:9 in JPS; the comment is filed under 14:1, so this lemma is taken from 14:1.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: thy spoil shall be divided in the midst of thee
Zechariah.english_translation: The spoil that you will plunder from enemies, your inhabitants will divide in your midst; and so Targum Jonathan: “and Israel will divide the property of the nations in your midst, Jerusalem.”

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: the residue of the people shall not be cut off from the city
Zechariah.english_translation: They will not all be exiled. And why does He let half of them be exiled and the houses be plundered? So that they will have no excuse to say: We did not come to make war, but only to worship.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: As when He fighteth in the day of battle
Zechariah.english_translation: Like the day of His battle, the war at the Red Sea.
Zechariah.translator_note: Rashi’s Aramaic is *ke-yom agochayhi kerav al yama de-suf*; translated as printed.

Zechariah.english_translation: From its middle.
From the east to the west, as it concludes and goes on.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: half of the mountain shall remove toward the north
Zechariah.english_translation: Its northern half shall move from its place and extend toward the north; and so we find “its half toward the south” — toward the south; and the valley will be between them, its head toward the east and its end toward the west.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: you shall flee to the valley of the mountains
Zechariah.english_translation: Targum Jonathan: “and the valley of the mountains shall be stopped up,” since Jerusalem has mountains round about it, and there is a valley between the mountain in the north and the Mount of Olives, and likewise in the south; and when half of the Mount of Olives moves next to the mountain in its north, the valley between them will be stopped up, and likewise in the south.
Zechariah.translator_note: Rashi, following Targum Jonathan, reads the verb as “shall be stopped up” (*ve-nistam*); JPS reads “you shall flee” (*ve-nastem*).

Zechariah.english_translation: The height of the valley that was between the mountains.
To the height of the tops of the mountains on this side and that; and so Menachem connected it: “and from the nobles thereof I called thee” (Isaiah 41:9), and its meaning is an expression of height.
Zechariah.translator_note: Printed reference is (Isaiah 41:9); JPS reads “And called thee from the uttermost parts thereof.” Rashi’s printed word is ומאציליה.

Zechariah.english_translation: When you see this great miracle.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: like as you fled from before the earthquake
Zechariah.english_translation: (Ibid.) “And the posts of the doors moved” on the day that Uzziah was stricken.
Zechariah.translator_note: The word “(Ibid.)” is a printed insertion, and the quotation is Isaiah 6:4, not Zechariah. The earthquake of Uzziah’s time is mentioned in Amos 1:1.

Zechariah.english_translation: Angels.

Targum Jonathan: “There shall not be light, but fine gold and ice shall be light”; “There shall not be bright light, for *yekarot* and *kipa’on* it shall be.” *Yekarot* is an expression of *yekar* like “the glory of the pastures” (Psalms 37), a kind of light that is seen in the morning on the mountains and fades and goes away.
Zechariah.translator_note: Printed “(Psalms 37)” is Psalms 37:20 (JPS: “as the fat of lambs”), where Rashi takes the word *yekar* as an expression of glory.

Zechariah.english_translation: Thickened, dark, and dense like ice that has congealed and hardened, like “and curdled me like cheese” (Job 10).
Zechariah.translator_note: Printed “Job 10” is Job 10:10 (JPS: “And curdled me like cheese”); Rashi’s printed form is וכגבינה תקפיאני.

Zechariah.english_translation: And this thing shall be one day out of the day of the Holy One, blessed be He: it is the day known as the preparation of His salvation, of the Holy One, blessed be He.
Not a bright light, as the light of the world to come, as it is said, “And the light of the sun shall be sevenfold” etc.
Zechariah.translator_note: The quotation is Isaiah 30:26 (JPS: “And the light of the sun shall be sevenfold, as the light of the seven days”).

Zechariah.english_translation: Nor a time of trouble like the trouble of the servitude of the exiles; for before the days of our Messiah there will be none, and there will be no servitude in them.
Zechariah.translator_note: The sentence is difficult as printed and is translated literally.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: at evening time there shall be light
Zechariah.english_translation: Before a thousand years are finished, there will be bright light and all the good that is promised to Israel; and so Targum Jonathan: “not like the light of day and not like the darkness of night.”
When the Mount of Olives splits from east to west.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: living waters shall go out from Jerusalem
Zechariah.english_translation: And they will go east by that fissure to the Eastern Sea, which is at the east of the world, and half will turn west to the Western Sea. This is the spring that Joel prophesied, “And a fountain shall come forth of the house of the LORD” (there, 4); this is the stream that Ezekiel prophesied (47:4), “and he measured a thousand, and he caused me to pass through the waters” etc.
Zechariah.translator_note: Printed “(there, 4)” is Joel 4:18 (JPS: “And a fountain shall come forth of the house of the LORD”). The Ezekiel quotation follows Ezekiel 47:3–4 (JPS 47:3: “he measured a thousand cubits, and he caused me to pass through the waters”).

Zechariah.english_translation: That all the nations will abandon their idols and acknowledge Him, that He is one, and there is no strange god with Him.
That His name will be mentioned in the mouth of all.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: All the land shall be turned as the Arabah
Zechariah.english_translation: It will turn so that the whole land is like the plain; the mountains will be lowered, and the whole world will be level, and Jerusalem a mountain, so that it will be seen to be higher than everything.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: from Geba to Rimmon south of Jerusalem
Zechariah.english_translation: We learned in the Tosefta of Sotah: the south of Jerusalem is level, but Geba and Rimmon are rocky and rough ground; and so is its explanation: “from Geba to Rimmon,” which is a place of mountains — from there they will begin to turn into plain and level ground, and they will be like the south of Jerusalem, which is level.
Zechariah.translator_note: Rashi’s citation is to the Tosefta of Sotah; I did not verify it against the source.

Zechariah.english_translation: Since all around it is level, it will be seen to be high.
In its place.

It too is in its place, and from there the length of the city extends to the king’s winepresses. Targum Jonathan: “the pits of the king” — *פושיי"ן* in French — and like “pits and caves” (Bava Kamma 50b); and likewise all *yekavim* in Scripture are an expression of pits: a pit in front of the winepress into which the wine flows. And an aggadic Midrash: “the king’s winepresses” — the Ocean Sea, that Jerusalem will reach to the end of all the world: winepresses that the King of the kings of kings hewed.
Zechariah.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Zechariah 14:10 under “Fosses” (pits), in forms such as פושיץ; the printed form (פושיי"ן) is a variant spelling. The Talmudic reference (Bava Kamma 50b) is a printed insertion.

Zechariah.english_translation: The city, any more.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: Their flesh shall consume away while they stand upon their feet
Zechariah.english_translation: This is the falling off of limbs.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: a great tumult from the LORD shall be among them
Zechariah.english_translation: To confuse their wisdom and turn them to madness.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: lay hold every one on the hand of his neighbour
Zechariah.english_translation: He will seize him in order to kill him.
Whoever is stronger prevails.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: Judah also shall fight against Jerusalem
Zechariah.english_translation: Against her will she will fight against Israel.
That which is explained above: “Their flesh shall consume away.”
As our Rabbis of blessed memory explained in tractate Avodah Zarah: “I have an easy commandment, and its name is sukkah,” as is found in the first chapter (page 3).
Zechariah.translator_note: The reference “(page 3)” is a printed insertion; Rashi’s source is Avodah Zarah 3a, which I did not verify.

Zechariah.english_translation: Actual rains, to make the fruit of their land grow. And why did He see fit to decree upon them the withholding of rains? Because the commandment of the Festival concerns the rains: they are the four species of the lulav and the water libation, to entreat for the waters, since the Festival is the season of the rains of the year; and those who cast doubt on the Festival of Sukkot — the rain will not be upon them. So I learned in the Tosefta of Sukkah.
Zechariah.translator_note: The Tosefta citation was not verified against the source.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: if the family of Egypt go not up
Zechariah.english_translation: And they do not need rains, for the Nile rises and waters them.
“And not upon them” will be their rain — that is, the Nile will not water them; and so Targum Jonathan: “upon them the Nile shall not rise.”
Zechariah.translator_note: JPS renders the Hebrew “they shall have no overflow”; Rashi reads it as “and not upon them will be the rain.”

Zechariah.english_translation: Of famine.

Zechariah.english_lemma_JPS: wherewith the LORD will smite the nations
Zechariah.english_translation: This will be the punishment of Egypt and the punishment of all the idolaters, as He said, “Not upon them will be the rain.”
Zechariah.translator_note: JPS Zechariah 14:17: “upon them there shall be no rain.”

Zechariah.english_translation: The tinklers that are hung on the horse for adornment between its eyes — even those they will sanctify to make holy vessels: basins for the blood, and pots to cook the flesh of sacrifices in abundance.
Which were used for removing the ashes (the ash) — even they will be of gold and of silver, like the basins before the altar.
*טנטיני"ר* in French.
Zechariah.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Zechariah 14:20 under “Grelots” (bells), in forms such as טינטין; the printed form (טנטיני"ר) is a variant spelling.

Zechariah.english_translation: They will not need to engage in trade, like “Whose traffickers are the honourable of the earth” (Isaiah 23:8). Another explanation: there is no poor man (*ani*) here.

Malachi.english_lemma_JPS: The burden of the word of the LORD
Malachi.english_translation: *porport* [printed פורפור"ט] in French: a matter that is delivered to Malachi to bear it to the children of Israel.
Malachi.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Malachi 1:1 (“Charge (de la parole de Dieu)”), in forms such as פורפורט; the reading *porport* is from Darmesteter’s index (his gloss: “charge”); the printed form (פורפור"ט) matches.

Malachi.english_translation: It had already been entrusted to his hand for many days. From here our Rabbis derived, in the Baraita of the Mekhilta, that all the prophets stood at Mount Sinai and there the prophecies were entrusted to them; and so it says (Isaiah 48:16), “From the time that it was, there am I; and now the Lord GOD hath sent me.”
Malachi.translator_note: Rashi’s quotation ends at “hath sent me”; JPS continues “and His spirit.”

Malachi.english_translation: To give him “a pleasant land, the goodliest heritage of the nations” (Jeremiah 3:19) — a land in which all the hosts of the idolaters set their desire.
Malachi.translator_note: Rashi explains *tzvi tzeva’ot goyim* as “a land that the hosts of the nations long for” (*tzavin*); JPS renders “the goodliest heritage of the nations.”

Malachi.english_translation: To push him off to the land of Seir because of Jacob his brother. And it is the way of the world that one who has two sons chooses a fine portion for the firstborn.
They are not like the mountains of Israel.
The dwelling of jackals.

And if the destroyers of the Temple say: At the beginning we were poor, but now that we have grown rich from the plunder of Jerusalem we shall return and rebuild our ruins — “Thus saith the LORD” etc.

Malachi.english_lemma_JPS: The LORD is great beyond the border of Israel
Malachi.english_translation: His greatness will be seen beyond our border, to make known that we are His people. And Targum Jonathan: “The glory of HaShem will be great, and He will broaden the border of the land of Israel.”
A son is bound to honor a father, and so a servant his master. And you are called sons and servants. And now, if I am a father to you, where is My honor?
You priests, who despise My name.

Malachi.english_lemma_JPS: Wherein have we despised Thy name?
Malachi.english_translation: That is: I know that you will say to me: Wherein have we despised? Behold, the contempt!

Malachi.english_lemma_JPS: You offer polluted bread upon Mine altar
Malachi.english_translation: That is: and if you say, Wherein have we polluted Thee? — we have polluted for You the bread of Your altar? I answer you: In this you polluted Me, by your saying “The table of the LORD is contemptible.” They were contemptuous in dividing, each from his brother, the meal-offerings and the holy things, and they say: Since it is forbidden for us to divide a meal-offering against a meal-offering and a sacrifice against a sacrifice, and it is toil and labor to divide every single meal-offering for the sake of an olive-bulk or a double portion that falls to each one one by one …
Malachi.translator_note: The last clause is difficult as printed and is translated literally; Rashi’s explanation of how the priests “despised the table” is not fully clear to me.

Malachi.english_translation: But is this thing not evil?
And now you priests, who do this evil — how can it enter your hearts to be the emissaries of Israel to seek mercy for them? Behold, this evil was from your hand.
Your faces, to hear prayer from your mouths and to be gracious to those who sent you?
Would that a good man would arise among you who would shut the doors of My Sanctuary so as not to bring in there this abominable offering.

Malachi.english_lemma_JPS: kindle fire on Mine altar in vain
Malachi.english_translation: With fires with which I am not pleased, for I have no pleasure in you. And our Rabbis expounded in Torat Kohanim: A man says to his fellow, “Bolt this door for me” — he does not claim wages for it; “Light this lamp for me” — he does not ask payment for it. But you — who among you shut My doors for nothing, and you did not light My altar for nothing! All the more so, you did not do for nothing things that are usually done for pay. Therefore I have no pleasure in you.
Malachi.translator_note: Rashi reads *ta’iru* as “you shall light”; JPS renders “kindle fire.” The citation to Torat Kohanim was not verified against the source.

Malachi.english_lemma_JPS: My name is great among the nations
Malachi.english_translation: Our Rabbis said: “They call Him God of gods” — even he who has idolatry knows that He is over all. “And in every place offerings are presented unto My name” — even the idolaters volunteer. And our Rabbis explained: these are the disciples of the wise who engage in the laws of the Temple service in every place; and likewise all the prayers of Israel that they pray in every place are to Me as a pure oblation. And so Jonathan translated: “and every time that you do My will, I accept your prayers, and My great name is sanctified through you, and your prayer is like a pure offering before Me.” And so the verse explains: And why do you profane My name, when it is great among the nations, and I have loved and favored you, that in every place where you pray before Me, even in exile, it is burned and offered up for My name?
Malachi.translator_note: The words “that there is a God” are a later printed insertion. The Talmudic saying is cited without a source (it corresponds to Menachot 110a, which I did not verify).

Malachi.english_translation: It is Mine, for through you My name is feared among the nations, and you profane Me and My name.

Malachi.english_lemma_JPS: the fruit thereof, even the food thereof, is contemptible
Malachi.english_translation: “Its *nivo*”: the utterance of the altar that is fluent on your lips — this is always “its food is contemptible.” You say about it — that is, you have already spread this slander about it — and this utterance you have fixed upon My altar.
Malachi.translator_note: Rashi takes *nivo* (JPS: “the fruit thereof”) as “its utterance,” from *niv sefatayim*.

Malachi.english_translation: *Me-achlo* (“from its food”).
Malachi.translator_note: The printed gloss is very short; translated literally.

Malachi.english_translation: A lean animal, and we are poor and have no means to obtain choice offerings; and so Targum Jonathan: “Behold, what we have brought is our fullness.”
Malachi.translator_note: The Aramaic phrase הא דאייתינא מליאותנא is translated literally; its sense is uncertain to me.

Malachi.english_translation: This is one of the eighteen words of the emendation of the Scribes: “you have snuffed at Me” was written, but Scripture euphemized it, and they wrote “at it.” And *hifachtem* and *he’edavt…* is an expression of “the drooping of the soul” (*mappach nefesh*, Job 11).
Malachi.translator_note: The printed word והדאבת' is abbreviated and I could not resolve it; it is translated as “he’edavt…” left as printed. JPS Job 11:20: “And their hope shall be the drooping of the soul.” Printed “Job 11” is Job 11:20.

Malachi.english_translation: “Me” — and My table.
Malachi.translator_note: The printed gloss is very short; translated literally. See the previous comment on the emendation “at it.”

Malachi.english_translation: He acts deceitfully with the fraud of false words before Me, saying: I have nothing better than this.

Malachi.english_lemma_JPS: he hath in his flock a male
Malachi.english_translation: A ram fit for a burnt-offering, and he vows a sacrifice.
A blemished one, like “because their corruption is in them” (Leviticus 22).
Malachi.translator_note: The quotation is Leviticus 22:25 (JPS: “because their corruption is in them”); the Hebrew word Rashi cites is *mashchatam*.

Malachi.english_translation: To the priests I command this commandment: that you not offer these on My altar.
And I will curse your blessings — that which must be blessed for you: the grain, the new wine and the oil.
And truly, the matter should not be hung on the condition that I attached, “if you will not hearken,” for I know that you will not hearken; therefore I curse it from now on.
The dung of the animals of your festivals upon your faces — that is, you will not receive reward from Me, but only for evil, for shame; “and I will rebuke for you the seed of the field.”
Malachi.translator_note: Rashi’s last clause restates the opening of the verse in his own words (JPS: “I will rebuke the seed for your hurt”).

Malachi.english_lemma_JPS: you shall be taken away unto it
Malachi.english_translation: The dung of the animals of your offerings will carry you to it, to be gluttons and despised like it.

Malachi.english_lemma_JPS: That My covenant might be with Levi
Malachi.english_translation: That I desire that you remain (with Me) in the covenant that I made with the tribe of Levi.
As it is said to Phinehas, “Behold, I give unto him My covenant of peace” (Numbers 25), and it was promised to him and to his seed after him; so his seed will be alive.
Malachi.translator_note: Printed “Numbers 25” is Numbers 25:12 (JPS: “Behold, I give unto him My covenant of peace”).

Malachi.english_translation: That he would receive them with awe, and so he did: “and he feared Me.”
*Nichat* — an expression of *chatat* (dread): he was afraid.

Malachi.english_lemma_JPS: He walked with Me in peace and uprightness
Malachi.english_translation: Aaron, Eleazar and Phinehas; and so, in the incident of the calf, all their tribe turned back from iniquity, as it is said, “And all the sons of Levi gathered themselves together unto him” (Exodus 32:26).

It is incumbent upon them to keep knowledge — why? For they shall seek the law at his mouth, for this matter has already been entrusted to them: “They shall teach Jacob Thine ordinances” (Deuteronomy 33:10).

Malachi.english_lemma_JPS: the messenger of the LORD of hosts
Malachi.english_translation: The emissary of the Holy One, blessed be He, like the ministering angels, to serve before Him and to enter within His precincts.
The covenant that the Holy One, blessed be He, made with our fathers at Sinai.

Malachi.english_lemma_JPS: Judah hath profaned the holiness of the LORD
Malachi.english_translation: Himself, who was “the LORD’S hallowed portion, His first-fruits of the increase” (Jeremiah 2:3).
Malachi.translator_note: Rashi’s Hebrew wording is *kodesh la-Shem reishit tevu’ato*; JPS Jeremiah 2:3 renders it “Israel is the LORD’S hallowed portion, His first-fruits of the increase.”

Malachi.english_lemma_JPS: the daughter of a strange god
Malachi.english_translation: That they married foreign women in Babylon, even the priests, as is explained in the book of (Ezra 9); and our Rabbis said: Malachi is Ezra.
Malachi.translator_note: Printed “Ezra 9” is Ezra 9:2.

Malachi.english_lemma_JPS: Him that calleth and him that answereth
Malachi.english_translation: *Er* among the disciples and *oneh* among the sages; *er* is an expression of a sharp person.

Malachi.english_lemma_JPS: offereth an offering unto the LORD of hosts
Malachi.english_translation: And if he is a priest, he will not have a son who offers an offering.

The first, about which I rebuked much, is severe: that he married foreign women even though he was unmarried; and this second is more severe than it: that married Israelites took the foreign women in addition to their wives, because the Israelite women had become blackened by hunger and by exile and had become repulsive to them; and he would keep her in his house shut up like living widows, and the foreign woman was the mistress.
Malachi.translator_note: The last sentence is difficult as printed; translated literally.

Malachi.english_lemma_JPS: You cover the altar of the LORD with tears
Malachi.english_translation: They would come before the altar of HaShem and weep before it and say: What have we sinned, and what injustice have our husbands found in us? Behold, we are before the altar to be examined like suspected wives.

Malachi.english_lemma_JPS: regardeth not the offering any more
Malachi.english_translation: Until you are not worthy that I should turn to your offering and take favor from your hand.

An expression of groaning, that a person is distressed in his heart — *דמוניש"א* in French; and the father of them all is “Sigh in silence” (Ezekiel 24:17). But if *anakah* were an expression of crying out, where is the silence? And its Targum is *de-medankin*; and so he translated (ibid. 24), “*venekotem bifneikhem*,” as *ve-tidankun*, an expression of a person who groans and is distressed within himself.
Malachi.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Malachi 2:13 (“Gemissement”), in forms such as דמונישמינט; the printed form (דמוניש"א) is shortened. The Ezekiel citation is unclear: the word Rashi quotes (ונקוטתם בפניכם) appears at Ezekiel 20:43 and 36:31 (JPS: “you shall loathe yourselves in your own sight”), while the printed “24” suggests Ezekiel 24:23 (JPS: “and moan one toward another”); I translated as printed. The Aramaic is translated as printed.

Malachi.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He, for Adam and Eve at the beginning.
The spirits and the souls were Mine; from the first man they all came forth.

The one of the pair seeks to find pretexts against his wife, who is his partner, who is the seed of God: what abomination is it, that he despises her? And this is the language of Targum Jonathan, except that Targum Jonathan has: “And what does the one seek, except the seed of God.” And the interpretation is correct, were it not that the *alef* of *echad* is vocalized with the accent *zakef*, which cuts off the word *mevakesh* from joining “and what does the one” and attaches it to “the seed of God.” And there is an explanation according to the Aggadah: that those who had married idolaters gathered to the prophet. They said to him: Did not Abraham do so, who took Hagar in addition to his wife? And he said to them: “And a remnant of spirit was his” — his mind was not like your mind; he did not set his eyes on her; he had another thought. They said to him: “And what does the one seek?” — what was his thought? He said to them: To have a seed of God. And the Targum of Jonathan was acceptable in my eyes, for we do not find in Scripture or in the Mishnah that *she’ar* is used for another sense, except where one can explain it in the language of remainder, like “it devoured and broke in pieces, and stamped the residue (*ush’ara*) with its feet” (Daniel 7:7); and in the language of the Mishnah, “and the rest of those liable to death, except those that were specified.” But the language of *acher* (“another”) is used; *she’ar* is not used.
Malachi.translator_note: A long, difficult comment about the accents and the meaning of *she’ar*; translated literally. The Mishnaic quotation was not identified. The Aramaic Daniel quotation matches Daniel 7:7 (JPS: “it devoured and broke in pieces, and stamped the residue with its feet”); the Aramaic is translated as printed.

Malachi.english_translation: And against the wife of your youth let not your spirit deal treacherously.
And our Rabbis differ about it in tractate Gittin; some of them say: If you hate her, send her away with a bill of divorce, and she may marry another.

But this — is it at all fitting to do, that you spread your cloak over her to keep her as your wife, while violence is spread over that cloak, because there is hatred in your heart against her, and you constantly provoke and distress her?

Because you see the way of the wicked prosper and the righteous afflicted and stumbling, you say in your hearts one of these two things: “Every one that doeth evil is good in His sight,” or: there is no judgment and no judge to exact payment. And so the interpretation of the verse: “Every one that doeth evil is good in His sight” — therefore He makes them prosper; or if that is not so, “Where is the God of justice,” who does not exact payment from them?
Malachi.translator_note: Rashi’s lemma continues “Or where is the God of justice,” which in JPS begins Malachi 3:1; the lemma here is taken from 2:17.

Malachi.english_translation: To clear out the wicked.
One who takes vengeance for the covenant.
From the wicked.
The God of justice.
And who can contain it.
Who will be able to stand.

Like the soap of launderers, which removes every stain, so He will remove all wickedness. *Borit* is an herb that removes stain — *שנייר"א* in French. And the language of *borit* is used of one who cleanses and purifies, like “to such as are pure in heart” (Psalms 73), *le-vorei levav*.
Malachi.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Malachi 3:2 (“érbe savonére,” the soapwort herb), in forms such as אירבא שבוניירא; the printed form (שנייר"א) is a shortened variant. Printed “Psalms 73” is Psalms 73:1 (JPS: “to such as are pure in heart”).

Malachi.english_translation: He will clear himself of all his occupations to be like a refiner who refines and purifies silver.
Even though I am long-suffering, My mind concerning Myself has not changed from the beginning, to love evil and to hate good.
Although you die in your wickedness, I have not exacted payment from the wicked in their lifetime.

You are not consumed from before Me, and I have left the souls to Myself, to exact My judgments from them in Gehenna; and so Targum Jonathan: “And you of the house of Jacob — whoever dies in this world, his judgment is sealed”; that is, you think to say that My judgment is void, that there is nothing more to be exacted from him. And our Rabbis explained it: “I have not changed” — I have not struck anyone and then changed his lot; but you I left standing after much punishment, and the arrows are spent, but you are not spent.
Our Rabbis expounded it as an expression of robbery; and it is Aramaic.
That you rob from the priests and from the Levites — that is My robbery.

Malachi.english_lemma_JPS: You are cursed with the curse
Malachi.english_translation: For this sin I send a curse upon the work of your hands, and yet you rob Me.

Malachi.english_lemma_JPS: there may be food in My house
Malachi.english_translation: Let there be provision available for My ministers.
With the locust (*chasil*) and the cutter (*gazam*) that eat for you the produce of the field and the vine.
A land in which I delight.

Malachi.english_lemma_JPS: It is vain to serve God
Malachi.english_translation: We served Him for nothing, for we receive no reward.
*Kedoranit* — with lowliness of spirit.
We served Him and kept His charge, and now we see these wicked prospering, so that we call them happy for their wicked deeds.

Malachi.english_lemma_JPS: they try God, and are delivered
Malachi.english_translation: To say: Let us see what He can do to us; and they escaped from evil and did not stumble.

I answer your words: Then, when the wicked did their wickedness and the good walked mournfully, because those who feared the LORD spoke to one another not to cling to their evil deeds — and as for Me, their words were not forgotten before Me; and though I do not hasten to repay recompense, I hearkened and heard, and I commanded that a book of remembrance be written for them, and their words are upheld before Me.
Malachi.translator_note: The last clause is translated literally; the sense of *mekuyamim* as “upheld” follows the context.

Malachi.english_lemma_JPS: the day that I do make
Malachi.english_translation: That which I have stored and set aside to pay My recompense in it; there I will show you the difference between the righteous and the wicked.
A treasure — *איישטו"י* in French.
Malachi.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Malachi 3:17 (“Réserve”), in forms such as אשטוי and אישטויי; the printed form (איישטו"י) is a variant spelling.

Malachi.english_translation: This “day” is an expression for the sun; for so the Sages said: there is no Gehenna in the future, but the Holy One, blessed be He, takes the sun out of its sheath, and the wicked are judged by it and the righteous are healed by it; and that is what it says: “But unto you that fear My name shall the sun of righteousness arise.”
Malachi.translator_note: The Sages’ saying is cited without a source; I did not identify it.

Malachi.english_translation: A son and a son’s son.
Malachi.translator_note: The Aramaic words *bar u-var bar* are translated as printed.

Malachi.english_translation: An expression of fatness, like “for you grow fat as a heifer that threshes” (Jeremiah 50).
Malachi.translator_note: Printed “Jeremiah 20” is Jeremiah 50:11; JPS renders the clause “Because you gambol as a heifer at grass,” whereas Rashi reads *tafushu* as “grow fat.”

Malachi.english_translation: *Marbek* — that which enters the stall to be fattened — *קופיל"א* in French.
Malachi.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Malachi 3:20 (“veaux de parc (à l’engrais)”), in forms such as קופלא and קובלא; the printed form (קופיל"א) is a variant spelling.

Malachi.english_translation: “And you shall tread down” — and you shall subdue: an expression of crushing; and similar to it, “and there their virgin breasts were bruised” (Ezekiel 23:3).

Malachi.english_lemma_JPS: turn the heart of the fathers
Malachi.english_translation: To the Holy One, blessed be He.
