Through the sons: he will say to the sons, in a way of love and favor: Go and speak to your fathers to hold to the ways of the Omnipresent; and so “and the heart of the children to their fathers.” So I heard in the name of Rabbi Menachem, and ר"ד in tractate Eduyot: to make peace in the world.
Malachi.translator_note: The abbreviation ור"ד is not resolved and is left as printed. The reference to tractate Eduyot was not verified.

Psalms.english_translation: In ten expressions of song this book was said: *nitzuach*, *niggun*, *mizmor*, *shir*, *hallel*, *tefillah*, *berakhah*, *hoda’ah*, *ashrei*, *halleluyah* — corresponding to ten men who said it: Adam, Melchizedek, Abraham, Moses, David, Solomon, Asaph, and three sons of Korah. And they differ about Jeduthun: some say he was a man, as written in Chronicles; and some say that “Jeduthun” in this book is only after the *dattot* (decrees) and the judgments of the decrees that passed over him and over Israel.
Psalms.translator_note: The list of ten men follows the printed text, which differs from the list in the Talmud (Bava Batra 14b) that I know; it is translated as printed. The Hebrew of the last clause is cut off in the printed text.

Psalms.english_translation: (*לישפלישמנ"ץ* in French.) The happinesses of a man and the praises of a person — these are “that hath not walked”; for since he did not walk, he did not stand, and since he did not stand, he did not sit.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. The Old French is in parentheses in the printed text, as a later insertion. Darmesteter lists no gloss for Psalms 1:1.

Psalms.english_translation: (*גאבור"ש* in French. A repeated word: *גאבערס* in German: *שפעטטער*.)
Psalms.translator_note: This comment is a later insertion in parentheses; its French and German forms are left as printed (the printed word גאבערס is not clear to me). The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: his delight is in the law of the LORD
Psalms.english_translation: From this you learn that the seat of scoffers leads a person to neglect of Torah.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: in His law doth he meditate
Psalms.english_translation: At first it is called the Torah of HaShem, and once he has labored in it, it is called his own Torah.

Every expression of *hegeh* is in the heart, as it says (below, 19) “and the meditation of my heart” (Psalms 19:15), “Thy heart shall muse on the terror” (Isaiah 33:18), “For their heart studieth destruction” (Proverbs 24:2).
*פלנדי"ץ* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: *ראויארו"ש* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: Even its refuse is for a purpose: the conversation of the disciples of the wise is for a purpose and needs study.
An expression of withering — *flaistir* [printed פלישטי"ר] in French.
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 1:3 (“Ne se flétrira pas”), in forms such as פלישטייר and פלישטיר; the reading is *flaistir* (to wither), from Darmesteter’s footnote (which compares Godefroy *flachir*); the printed form (פלישטי"ר) matches.

Psalms.english_translation: An expression of straw — *קומבל"א* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Therefore the wicked shall not stand in the judgment
Psalms.english_translation: It is attached to the verse that follows it.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: the LORD regardeth the way of the righteous
Psalms.english_translation: Because He knows the way of the righteous, and it is always before Him to recognize it, while the way of the wicked is hateful in His eyes and He removes it from before Him — therefore the wicked will have no standing on the Day of Judgment, nor sinners to be written in the congregation of the righteous.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Why are the nations in an uproar
Psalms.english_translation: Our Rabbis expounded the matter of King Messiah; but according to its plain sense it is right to interpret it of David himself, in the manner that is said (2 Samuel 5:17), “And the Philistines heard that Israel had anointed David king over them, and the Philistines gathered their camps” — and they fell into his hand; and about them he said, “Why are the nations in an uproar,” and all of them were gathered.
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s wording of 2 Samuel 5:17 differs from JPS (“And when the Philistines heard that David was anointed king over Israel, all the Philistines went up to seek David”).

Psalms.english_translation: “And the peoples mutter” — in their heart, emptiness.
Menachem interpreted *le’ummim*, *ummim* and *goyim* as all close in meaning.
“And rulers” — *שיניור"ש* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: An expression of *sod* (counsel) — *פורקונשילרוו"ט* in French — and what is the counsel?
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: *דישרונפרוימ"ש לויקוראנגל"ש* in French; these are the straps with which the yoke is bound.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: *לויקורדו"ש* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: These are used in the present tense.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Then will He speak unto them
Psalms.english_translation: “*Elemo*” is like “*aleihem*” (“to them”); and what is the speech?

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I that have established My king
Psalms.english_translation: Why have you been in an uproar, when I Myself have appointed this one for Me, to anoint and to reign over Zion, My holy mountain?

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I will tell of the decree
Psalms.english_translation: David said: It is a fixed decree, and I take it upon myself to tell this and make it known.
Through Nathan, Gad and Samuel.

The head of Israel, who are called in the Torah “My son, My firstborn,” and they will be established through you, as it is said of Abner (2 Samuel 3), “Thus says HaShem: By the hand of David My servant I will save My people Israel”; and for their sake you are before Me like a son, for all of them depend on you.
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “(ibid. 2, 3)” is 2 Samuel 3:18. Rashi’s wording differs from JPS (“the LORD hath spoken of David, saying: By the hand of My servant David I will save My people Israel”).

Psalms.english_translation: That I made you king over them.

To be called My son and beloved to Me as a son, for their sake, as it is said (1 Chronicles 14:2), “And David perceived that the LORD had established him king over Israel, for his kingdom was exalted … for His people Israel’s sake”; and we find among the beloved kings of Israel that they are called sons, as it is said (2 Samuel 7) of Solomon, “I will be to him for a father, and he shall be to Me for a son”; and further we find of David in Psalm 89: “He shall call unto Me: Thou art my Father, My God, and the rock of my salvation.”
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “(2 Samuel 27)” is 2 Samuel 7:14; Rashi’s Hebrew there reads “he shall be to Me for a son, and I shall be to him for a father” (the order differs from JPS). Printed “Psalm 89” is Psalms 89:27.

Psalms.english_translation: Pray to Me at every time that you go out to fight your enemies.
You shall crush them.
That is the sword.
You shall break them; and it is the expression *nafutz* throughout Scripture: an earthen vessel broken into fine pieces.
The prophets of Israel are men of mercy and they rebuke the nations of the world to turn from their wickedness, for the Holy One, blessed be He, extends a hand to the wicked and to the righteous.
When that trembling comes of which it is written, “Trembling hath seized the ungodly” (Isaiah 33:14) — you will rejoice and be glad, if you served HaShem.

Gird yourselves with purity of heart. (Another version:) *Nashku bar* — *ארנישמנט* in French; and Menachem interpreted it as an expression of desire, like “and thy desire shall be to thy husband” (Genesis 3:16).
Psalms.translator_note: The sense “gird yourselves” for *zarzu* follows the French gloss *ארנישמנט*, which I read as “equipping”; the Old French could not be confirmed in Darmesteter.

Psalms.english_translation: Lest He be wroth.
In the way of that which is said, “But the way of the wicked shall perish” (above, 1).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: When suddenly His wrath is kindled
Psalms.english_translation: For in a little moment His anger will be kindled against you suddenly; and at that hour, “Happy are all they that take refuge in Him” — those who take refuge in Him will be recognized as happy.

The Aggadists expounded many expositions on this matter, and our Rabbis said: After the prophet said to him (2 Samuel 11), “Behold, I will raise up evil against thee out of thine own house,” his heart was stormy: perhaps a servant or a bastard will rise against me, who will have no mercy on me; once he knew that it was his son, he rejoiced. And an aggadic Midrash: because he saw that his strategy was confirmed, that his servants, the Cherethites and the Pelethites, who are the Sanhedrin, maintain his lordship over them — when he said to them (ibid. 15), “Arise, and let us flee from Absalom,” what is written there? “Whatsoever my lord the king shall choose, behold thy servants.” And when he came to Mahanaim (ibid. 17), Shobi the son of Nahash, and Machir the son of Ammiel, and Barzillai the Gileadite came out to meet him and sustained him there.
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “2 Samuel 11” is 2 Samuel 12:11 (JPS: “Behold, I will raise up evil against thee out of thine own house”). The quotation “Arise, and let us flee” is from 2 Samuel 15:14; Rashi’s words “All that my lord the king shall choose, behold thy servants” rearrange 2 Samuel 15:15 (JPS: “Behold, thy servants are ready to do whatsoever my lord the king shall choose”).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Many are they that rise up against me
Psalms.english_translation: People great in Torah, great in wisdom, great in wealth, great in stature, such as Saul and the Rapha-born, Doeg and Ahithophel.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Many there are that say of my soul
Psalms.english_translation: “Of my soul” — concerning my soul.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: There is no salvation for him in God
Psalms.english_translation: Because he came upon a married woman.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I lay me down, and I sleep
Psalms.english_translation: My heart was stopped with worry and fear.
From my worry, for I trusted that HaShem sustains me.
An expression of *she’iyah* (devastation) — *גאטירנ"ט* in French. And some say *shatu* is like *samu* (“set”), like “*lema’an shiti otothai*” (Exodus 10:1).
Psalms.translator_note: Old French unconfirmed. Rashi cites Exodus 10:1 for the root, so the words are left transliterated; JPS: “that I might show these My signs.” The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: smitten all mine enemies upon the cheek
Psalms.english_translation: It is a blow of contempt, as it says, “Let him give his cheek to him that smiteth him” (Lamentations 3:30), “They smite the judge of Israel with a rod upon the cheek” (Micah 4:14); and another explanation: a blow on the mouth, as it says, “And he set his household in order, and strangled himself” (2 Samuel 17:23).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “(2 Samuel 17:23)”: Rashi’s words “and he commanded his household, and was strangled” (*va-yetzav el beito va-yechanak*) are a close paraphrase of 2 Samuel 17:23 (JPS: “set his house in order, and strangled himself”).

Psalms.english_translation: Their strength.
It is His to deliver His servants and His people, and it is incumbent on His people to bless and give thanks to Him. Selah.

This psalm David composed, to be recited by the sons of Levi who were the overseers, with song, on the platform. The expression *nitzuach* applies to those who are strengthened in the service, as it is said (Ezra 3:8), “The Levites, from twenty years old and upward, shall stand to oversee the work of the house of the LORD.”
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s wording differs from JPS Ezra 3:8 (“and appointed the Levites, from twenty years old and upward, to have the oversight of the work of the house of the LORD”).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: set me free when I was in distress
Psalms.english_translation: In the days that passed over me; and now be gracious to me and hear my prayer.

The sons of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, who are called “man”: of Abraham it is said, “restore the man’s wife” (Genesis 20:7), of Isaac, “What man is this” (ibid. 24), of Jacob, “a quiet man” (ibid. 25).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “(ibid. 24)” is Genesis 24:65 and “(ibid. 25)” is Genesis 25:27.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: how long shall my glory be put to shame
Psalms.english_translation: Until when will you insult me? “Have you seen the son of Jesse?” (1 Samuel 22:9), “Who is David? and who is the son of Jesse?” (ibid. 25), “when my son made a league with the son of Jesse” (ibid. 22), “thou hast chosen the son of Jesse” (ibid. 20) — I have no name.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed insertion “(1 Samuel 22:9)” gives a verse that reads “I saw the son of Jesse coming to Nob” in JPS, not Rashi’s words; I translated Rashi’s words as printed. Printed “(ibid. 25)” is 1 Samuel 25:10, “(ibid. 22)” is 22:8 and “(ibid. 20)” is 20:30.

Psalms.english_translation: You pursue to find lies, such as the Ziphites who informed against me, while they showed peace to my face, and the like — informers who were in the days of Saul (ibid. 23): “Doth not David hide himself with us … in the hill of Hachilah?” and so many others.
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “(ibid. 23)” is 1 Samuel 23:19.

Psalms.english_translation: He separated.
Be terrified before the Holy One, blessed be He, and do not sin.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Commune with your own heart upon your bed
Psalms.english_translation: Reflect in your hearts that the Holy One, blessed be He, warned about this.
Make your deeds righteous, and behold, you are like those who offer sacrifices.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: put your trust in the LORD
Psalms.english_translation: That He will bestow good upon you; and do not sin against Him for the sake of money, because you expect to receive reward from Saul.
Many in Israel see wicked men in wealth and ease, and say, “Who will show us good?” — to be rich and to attain desires like these.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: lift Thou up the light of Thy countenance upon us
Psalms.english_translation: “Nesah aleinu” — raise over us as a banner the light of Your countenance, an expression of “lift up a banner” (Isaiah 62:10), “I will lift up My banner.” Another version: “Nesah aleinu” — *רפנבל"ר* in French — like “the stones of a crown, glittering” (Zechariah 9:16). But I am not jealous of them, for joy is set in my heart from the time when their corn and their wine increased. I am confident: if for those who provoke Him it is so, then for those who do His will, how much more so in the future world, which is the day of receiving their reward.
Psalms.translator_note: Old French unconfirmed in Darmesteter. JPS Isaiah 62:10: “Lift up an ensign over the peoples.” The phrase “I will lift up My banner” (*arim nisi*) has no reference in the printed text; Rashi’s last sentences refer to the next verse (4:8). The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: In peace will I both lay me down and sleep
Psalms.english_translation: If Israel were at peace together with me, I would lie down and sleep securely, and I would not fear any adversary or enemy.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: makest me dwell alone in safety
Psalms.english_translation: Like “in safety, The fountain of Jacob alone” (Deuteronomy 33:28) — an expression of trust and quiet, that he has no need to station troops with him.
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s words are *betach badad ein Ya’akov*; JPS: “And Israel dwelleth in safety, The fountain of Jacob alone.”

Psalms.english_translation: Menachem interpreted all of them — *nechilot*, *alamot*, *gittit*, *Jeduthun* — as names of musical instruments, and the melody of the psalm was according to the song fitting for that instrument. And an aggadic Midrash: some explain *nechilot* as an expression of inheritance (*nachalah*), but that is not the meaning of the word, and the subject of the psalm too does not speak of inheritance. It is possible to explain *nechilot* as troops, like a swarm (*nechil*) of bees, and like *ve-nachalei Belial* (Psalms 18:5); and Targum Jonathan: “a company of the guilty; prayer,” for the sake of troops of enemies who come upon Israel, and the psalmist says this psalm on behalf of all Israel.
Psalms.translator_note: The Targum phrase סיעת חייבין תפלה is translated literally and its sense is uncertain to me. Rashi cites *ve-nachalei Belial* for the root, so the words are left transliterated; JPS Psalms 18:5: “the floods of Belial.” The Aramaic is translated as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: When I have strength to ask my needs before You; and when I have no strength to pray before You and anxiety is held in my heart — “consider my meditation,” understand the thoughts of my heart. So it is explained in the Midrash: every *binah* in Scripture has the accent under the *nun*, except this one and its fellow (in Job 35): “If now thou hast understanding, hear this,” which is not a noun but an expression of “understand,” like (Proverbs 23) “Consider well him that is before thee”; therefore the accent is under the *bet*.
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “Job 35” is Job 34:16; printed “Proverbs 23” is Proverbs 23:1. Rashi’s Hebrew *ve-im binah shema zot* is quoted with JPS’s “If now thou hast understanding, hear this.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: in the morning shalt Thou hear my voice
Psalms.english_translation: In the morning I call to You about them, for it is the time of judgment on the wicked, as it is said, “Morning by morning will I destroy all the wicked of the land” (below, 101), “Be Thou their arm every morning” (Isaiah 33:2), “For morning by morning shall it pass through” (ibid. 28).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “below, 101” is Psalms 101:8; printed “ibid. 28” is Isaiah 28:19.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: will I order my prayer unto Thee
Psalms.english_translation: My prayer is about this; *e’erokh* is an expression of *ma’arakhah* (arrangement); so Menachem connected it.
That You will execute judgments upon them.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: a God that hath pleasure in wickedness
Psalms.english_translation: And it is fitting for You to destroy wickedness from the world.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Evil shall not sojourn with Thee
Psalms.english_translation: It will not dwell with You.
Acting foolishly; and in the language of the Mishnah, confused.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: the man of blood and of deceit
Psalms.english_translation: This is Amalek and his seed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: in the abundance of Thy lovingkindness will I come into Thy house
Psalms.english_translation: I will come to Your house to give thanks to You for Your abundant kindness, which You wonderfully showed us, to let us see vengeance upon them.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: them that lie in wait for me
Psalms.english_translation: My enemies who watch to see whether I will betray You and You will forsake me; *shurai* is like “I behold him, but not nigh” (*ashurennu*, Numbers 24:17).
They appear as friends, and they are enemies.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Their inward part is a yawning gulf
Psalms.english_translation: Their thoughts are deceit.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Their throat is an open sepulchre
Psalms.english_translation: They reach to swallow others, like a grave that swallows the body.
Their words are smooth.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Let them fall by their own counsels
Psalms.english_translation: Because they take counsel against Israel; and then “all those that take refuge in Thee shall rejoice.”
You shall protect and cover over them.
When they see that You bless Your friends and those who love You.
That surrounds three sides of a person.
*Ratzon* — contentment — *apayement* [printed אפימנ"ט] in French (goodwill).
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 5:13 (“Bont, paix du cœur”), in forms such as אפיימנט; the reading is *apayement* (from *ad* + *pacamentum*), from Darmesteter’s footnote; the printed form (אפימנ"ט) matches.

Psalms.english_translation: You shall surround him, like “for Saul and his men compassed David and his men” (1 Samuel 23:26).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “(1 Samuel 23:26)”; Rashi’s Hebrew uses a participle, JPS: “for Saul and his men compassed David and his men round about.”

Psalms.english_translation: A harp of eight strings, and *Sheminith* is its name; and so we find (1 Chronicles 15) “so-and-so and his sons upon the Sheminith, to lead.”
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “(1 Chronicles 15)” is 1 Chronicles 15:21 (JPS: “with harps on the Sheminith, to lead”); Rashi paraphrases it.

Psalms.english_translation: *Umlal* — corrupted and weak of strength (*קופנדו"ן* in French) — like “these feeble Jews” of Ezra (Nehemiah 3:34).
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 6:3 (“Abattu”), in forms such as קונפונדוץ and קונפדוץ; the printed form (קופנדו"ן) is a variant spelling. Rashi attributes the Nehemiah verse to “Ezra”; JPS Nehemiah 3:34: “What do these feeble Jews?”

Psalms.english_translation: You look on and You do not heal.
From Your wrath.
From my sickness.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Every night make I my bed to swim
Psalms.english_translation: An expression of refuse and rejection (Lamentations 3), “and their carcasses were as refuse” (Isaiah 5:25): I reject my bed with tears. And Menachem connected it with “as he that swimmeth spreadeth forth his hands to swim” (ibid. 25) and with “waters to swim in” (Ezekiel 47).
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi cites these verses for their root (*sechi*, *shoche*, *sachu*). Printed “Lamentations 3” is Lamentations 3:45 (JPS: “the offscouring and refuse”); “ibid. 25” is Isaiah 25:11; “Ezekiel 47” is 47:5.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I melt away my couch with my tears
Psalms.english_translation: I will moisten and soak it like water.

*Ashesh* — an expression of the *asheshit* of the eye, whose light is dim, and similar to it, as if he sees through a glass that is in front of his eyes; and Menachem explained it as an expression of rot, like (below, 31) “and my bones are wasted away,” and so every expression of *ash*.
Psalms.translator_note: Darmesteter lists a French gloss for this verse (“lanterne”), which is not in the printed comment. JPS Psalms 31:11: “and my bones are wasted away.”

Psalms.english_translation: *Atkah* — grown old and aged, my eye with dimness of light; and Menachem connected it with “And he removed (*vaya’tek*) from thence unto the mountain” (Genesis 12:8).
Because of the troubles that they inflict on me.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: shall be ashamed and sore affrighted
Psalms.english_translation: What is “they shall turn back, they shall be ashamed”? A second time. Rabbi Yochanan said: In the future the Holy One, blessed be He, will judge the wicked and condemn them to Gehenna, and they will protest against Him; and the Holy One, blessed be He, brings them back, and again shows their records and judges them, and they are condemned, and He returns them to Gehenna — behold, a double shame. Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani says: In the future every nation will call to its god and none will answer; and they turn and call to the Holy One, blessed be He, and He says to them: If you had called to Me first, I would have answered you; now you have made idolatry primary and Me secondary; therefore I do not answer, as it is said, “They cried, but there was none to save” — this is idolatry — and afterwards “Even unto the LORD, but He answered them not” (below, 18). Therefore it says, “they shall turn back, they shall be ashamed.”
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “(below, 18)” is Psalms 18:42. The Talmudic and Midrashic sayings are cited without a source; I did not identify them.

Psalms.english_translation: In a little time.

Menachem said that this too is one of the names of song, after the instrument, and so he explained “upon shigionot” (Habakkuk 3:1). But our Rabbis explained it as an expression of *mishgeh* (error): that he confessed and prayed about the error, in that he sang a song on the fall of Saul, as it is said, “And David spoke unto the LORD,” etc. (2 Samuel 22:1). But the subject of the psalm does not prove this; and I say that they said it concerning the matter of Ishbi in Nob (ibid. 21), that it came upon him as the punishment of Saul, as our Rabbis explained: that the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: Through you Doeg the Edomite was driven out, through you Saul and his sons were killed, etc. (as is found in Chelek, concerning the errors that David asked the Holy One, blessed be He, to be delivered into the hand of an enemy and his seed not be cut off — סא"א), and David reversed his prayer and prayed that he not fall into the hand of an enemy; and so is its interpretation: *Shiggaion* — David sang to HaShem for having erred in saying to the Holy One, blessed be He, to deliver him into the hand of an enemy, over the words of Saul, who was killed through him. Another explanation: for the error of the corner of the robe that he cut off from Saul.
Psalms.translator_note: it is left as printed. The parenthetical sentence is a later printed insertion; the printed text gives no tractate for “Chelek,” which I left as printed. Printed “(ibid. 21)” refers to 2 Samuel 21:16 (Ishbi-benob).

Psalms.english_translation: Just as a Cushite is different in his skin, so Saul was different in his deeds.
An expression of “break off (*pirku*) the golden rings” (Exodus 32:2).
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi cites the verse for the root; JPS: “Break off the golden rings.”

Psalms.english_translation: That which is explained after it.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: If I have requited him that did evil unto me
Psalms.english_translation: If I have repaid him according to his deed.

That I removed his garment by cutting off the corner of his robe — was it to destroy him and strip him and leave him empty, and I did it in hatred? I did it only to let him know that he was delivered into my hand to kill, and I did not kill him. And *ve-achaltzah* is an expression of stripping off.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed verb שיחתי is unusual; translated as “removed” from the sense.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Arise, O LORD, in Thine anger
Psalms.english_translation: Against my enemies, such as Ishbi and his brothers and the Philistines, that I not be delivered into their hand.
Be glorified, to show vengeance of wrath when You rage against them.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: awake for me at the judgment
Psalms.english_translation: That I may be able to execute upon them the judgment of vengeance that You commanded. And where did You command? “Thou shalt break them with a rod of iron” (above, 2), and “I will be an enemy unto thine enemies” (Exodus 23:22). This I found in a Midrash.
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “Exodus 23:22” (JPS: “then I will be an enemy unto thine enemies”).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: let the congregation of the peoples compass Thee about
Psalms.english_translation: If they turn after You for You to save them, do not listen to their voice; withdraw from them and return and sit in Your place on high — *רפיש"א* in French. Another explanation: “On high return,” to show them that Your hand is supreme.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: who ministerest judgment to the peoples
Psalms.english_translation: Turn the judgment away from us and place it on the wicked.
*Yadin* — an expression of sufferings.
Judge according to the good deeds that are in their hand, and not according to the transgressions.
An expression of ending; and so Menachem explained *gamar omer* (below, 16), *gamar chasid* (below, 12), and likewise all of them (סא"א).
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi cites the verses for the root, so the words are left transliterated; the verses are Psalms 77:9 (JPS: “Is His promise come to an end for evermore?”) and Psalms 12:2 (JPS: “the godly man ceaseth”). Printed “below, 16” does not match 77:9. it is left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: You know who the righteous one is whom You will establish.
So is Your name.
You are the one to judge righteously.
When He sees the deeds of the wicked.
The wicked man from his wickedness.
The Holy One, blessed be He, will whet it against him — *פורביר"א* in French — and will bend His bow.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He hath also prepared for him
Psalms.english_translation: And for the wicked man the Holy One, blessed be He, prepared instruments of death.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: His arrows which He made sharp
Psalms.english_translation: *Ledolekim* — to the pursuers, like “that thou hast hotly pursued after me” (Genesis 31:36); and so is its interpretation: His arrows, to kill the wicked who pursue the righteous, the Holy One, blessed be He, will make and prepare to slay them; every expression of *dalakah* is an expression of pursuit.
An expression of pregnancy and birth, like “There thy mother was in travail with thee” (Song of Songs 8:5).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: he conceiveth mischief, and bringeth forth falsehood
Psalms.english_translation: All that he begets and toils for, all of it is falsehood, for it will not endure in his hand. A proverb says: *kol mah de-shikra molid pachta nasva*.
Psalms.translator_note: The Aramaic proverb is left transliterated; I understand it roughly as “whatever falsehood begets, a deficiency carries off,” but this is uncertain.

Psalms.english_translation: When He justifies the complete judgment, to judge the wicked according to their wickedness.

A musical instrument that came from Gath, where craftsmen to make them are found. And our Rabbis said it refers to Edom, which is destined to be trodden like a winepress, as it is said, “I have trodden the winepress alone” (Isaiah 63); but the subject of the psalm does not prove this.
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 63” is Isaiah 63:3.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: How glorious is Thy name in all the earth
Psalms.english_translation: Beyond the strength of the measure of the lower beings; the lower beings were not worthy that Your Presence should dwell among them.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Whose majesty is rehearsed above the heavens
Psalms.english_translation: It is fitting that You set it above the heavens, and You, in Your great humility, “hast founded strength,” etc.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings hast Thou founded strength
Psalms.english_translation: You caused Your Presence to dwell in the Sanctuary and ordained that strength be offered to You in thanks from the mouths of the Levites and the priests, who are people raised in filth, like babes and sucklings. *Olelim* is an expression of “and have laid (*ve-olalti*) my horn in the dust” (Job 16:15), and after the filth all infants are called *olelim*.
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi cites Job 16:15 for the root; JPS: “And have laid my horn in the dust.”

Psalms.english_translation: To make known to them that we are Your people.
The reproach of an enemy and avenger who says: You are no better than the nations; and I, when I see Your heavens, etc., marvel in my heart: “What is man, that Thou art mindful of him?”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: but little lower than the angels
Psalms.english_translation: *Me-Elohim* means angels, for You gave power to Joshua to silence the sun and to dry up the Jordan, to Moses to split the waters of the Red Sea and to ascend on high, and to Elijah to revive the dead.

Flocks and herds, like “the increase of thy kine” (*shegar alafekha*, Deuteronomy 25); *tzonah* is an expression of action (?), as in “and folds for your sheep” (Numbers 32:24) — *oveylediç* [printed אוביילדי"ץ] in French (a pen for small livestock). There are aggadic Midrashim, but they do not square with the verses.
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 8:8 (“Enclos pour parquer le menu bétail”), in forms such as אוביינדיץ and אובלדיץ; the reading is *oveylediç* (from Latin *oviculaticium*; *yl* is a palatal *l*), from Darmesteter’s footnote and index; the printed form (אוביילדי"ץ) is a variant spelling. The clause “*tzonah* is an expression of action” is translated literally and its sense is unclear to me. Printed “Deuteronomy 25” is Deuteronomy 28:4 (JPS: “the increase of thy kine”).

Psalms.english_translation: Some interpret *al muth labben* as concerning the death of his son Absalom, but its interpretation is not possible, because it says *labben* and not *ha-ben*, and the psalm has no evidence or mention to support this interpretation. And some interpret *al muth labben* as concerning Nabal, and this too is not possible, to reverse the name, and the psalm does not mention him (סא"א). And I saw in the Great Masorah that it is one word, for it joined it (below, 48): “He will guide us eternally” (*al-mut*; ‘alamot’). Menachem and Dunash interpreted as they interpreted, and it does not seem right in my eyes. And I saw in the Pesikta that the subject speaks of Amalek, “Thou hast rebuked the nations, Thou hast destroyed the wicked,” and I say: “To the Leader, upon Muth Labben” — this song is for the future, when the childhood and dark youth of Israel are whitened, and their righteousness is revealed and their salvation draws near, that Amalek and his seed be blotted out. *Alamot* — childhood; *laben* — like *lelaben* (“to whiten”). And Menachem interpreted *alamot laben* as melodies for teaching, and so is its interpretation: “To the Leader of the melodies of teaching,” to the singer of melodies for teaching, and *laben* is like “to understand” and *levonen*; *alamot* is after a musical instrument whose name is Alamot, as he says (below, 46), “upon Alamoth, a song.” And Dunash interpreted *Laben* as the name of a man, whose name was Laben, who fought David in those days; and what it says, “Thou hast rebuked the nations, Thou hast destroyed the wicked” — this wicked one is Laben, who kills innocent people; and even though you do not see elsewhere a man whose name was Laben, only in this place, so you find with other names that are written in Scripture only once.
Psalms.translator_note: it is left as printed. The comment is long and in places difficult; translated literally. Printed “(below, 48)” is Psalms 48:15 (JPS: “He will guide us eternally”) and “(below, 46)” is Psalms 46:1 (JPS: “upon Alamoth”).

Psalms.english_translation: The final redemption, which is weighed against all the miracles, as it is said, “it shall no more be said: ‘As the LORD liveth, that brought up the children of Israel …’” (Jeremiah 16:14).

Doubled words in Scripture, with no difference between them, like “my Witness … and He that testifieth of me is on high” (Job 16:19: *edi ve-sahadi*), “His bones are as pipes of brass; His gristles are like bars of iron” (ibid. 40).
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s Hebrew in Job 16:19 reads *edi ve-sahadi ba-meromim* (the second word is Aramaic); JPS: “my Witness is in heaven, And He that testifieth of me is on high.” Printed “ibid. 40” is Job 40:18.

Psalms.english_translation: In heaven.
The throne of judgment.
Amalek, “was the first of the nations” (Numbers 24).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “Numbers 24” is Numbers 24:20 (JPS: “Amalek was the first of the nations”).

Psalms.english_translation: His forefathers.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou hast blotted out their name
Psalms.english_translation: For “I will utterly blot out” (Exodus 17:14).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: O thou enemy, the waste places are come to an end for ever
Psalms.english_translation: For the swords of hatred are upon him forever like a sharp sword. Another explanation: ruins forever to that enemy, whose swords of hatred were upon us forever, and this is Amalek, of whom it is said, “and he kept his wrath for ever” (Amos 1:11–12); *charavot* is an expression of ruin, and so is its interpretation: “O thou enemy, the ruins are come to an end for ever”; and so it is said (Ezekiel 35:9), “I will make thee perpetual desolations, and thy cities shall not return.”
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi plays on *charavot* as “swords” and “ruins”; JPS renders it “the waste places.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: the cities which thou didst uproot
Psalms.english_translation: “Whereas Edom saith: ‘We are beaten down,’” etc., “But we will return and build the waste places”; “Thus saith the LORD of hosts: They shall build, but I will throw down” (Malachi 1:4).
At that hour.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: the LORD is enthroned for ever
Psalms.english_translation: A complete name and a complete throne, as it is said “His throne”; but before it is blotted out, it is written, “The hand upon the throne of the LORD” (Exodus 17:16): *kes* is defective and the Name is divided.
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s Hebrew of Exodus 17:16 is *ki yad al kes Yah*.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He will judge the world in righteousness
Psalms.english_translation: Until the end comes, He was accustomed to judge them with mercy; according to the equitable rules with which they were commanded, He judges them at night, when they are asleep, concerning the transgressions.
Psalms.translator_note: The comment is difficult as printed and is translated literally.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: a high tower for the oppressed
Psalms.english_translation: *Dakh* is an expression of crushing — *אילאמינשי"ה* in French. In the future, when He establishes His throne for judgment, He will be a high tower for Israel, who are crushed.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: Times of distress.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Sing praises to the LORD, who dwelleth in Zion
Psalms.english_translation: When He returns His dwelling to Zion, they will sing to Him thus.
The blood that was shed in Israel.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Be gracious unto me, O LORD
Psalms.english_translation: Now, in exile.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: liftest me up from the gates of death
Psalms.english_translation: In Your redemption.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The nations are sunk down in the pit that they made
Psalms.english_translation: This is the praise that I shall tell.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The LORD hath made Himself known
Psalms.english_translation: All this is from the praise: HaShem has made Himself known to His creatures, that He is ruler and governor and takes vengeance on His enemies, for He executed judgment upon them — *יושטיצ"א* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: snared in the work of his own hands
Psalms.english_translation: The wicked stumbled.
Let this be uttered. Selah.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The wicked shall return to the nether-world
Psalms.english_translation: Rabbi Nehemiah said: Every word that needs a *lamed* at its beginning has a *heh* added at its end, such as (Genesis 12) *Mitzraymah*, *midbarah*. They objected to him: But it is written, “The wicked shall return to the nether-world (*lish’olah*)”! Rabbi Abba bar Zavda said: To the lowest level of Sheol. And what is “shall return”? After they come out of Gehenna and stand in judgment and are condemned, they return to the lowest level of Gehenna.
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi cites *Mitzraymah* for the form; JPS Genesis 12:10: “into Egypt.” The printed text gives no source for the second example (*midbarah*) or for the Talmudic dispute.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: the needy shall not alway be forgotten
Psalms.english_translation: Israel, the needy, from being remembered concerning that in which they were enslaved; and “the expectation of the poor shall not perish for ever.”
Psalms.translator_note: The first clause is elliptical in the printed text and is translated literally.

Psalms.english_translation: David was praying before the Holy One, blessed be He, that He arise and hasten to do this.
Amalek, for a long time, in his greatness.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed gloss is elliptical; translated literally.

Psalms.english_translation: Because of the anger with which they angered You in Your Sanctuary.

*Morah* — bitterness and yoke. Another explanation: *morah* is an expression of casting, an expression of “hath He cast (*yarah*) into the sea” (Exodus 15:4); and some say *morah* is an expression of a razor (סא"א).
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi cites Exodus 15:4 for the root; JPS: “Pharaoh’s chariots and his host hath He cast into the sea.” it is left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: That they are mortals and not divine, so that their might is not dominant.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: hidest Thou Thyself in times of trouble
Psalms.english_translation: You hide Your eyes at times of trouble.
*Yidlak* — he pursues, like “that thou hast hotly pursued after me” (Genesis 31:36).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: They are taken in the devices that they have imagined
Psalms.english_translation: The poor are caught in the devices that the wicked think up against them.
It refers back to “Why standest Thou afar off, O LORD”: for now Amalek the wicked boasts that he attains all the desire of his soul.
And the robber praised himself, saying: He has reviled HaShem, and I shall have peace.

Like *barakh*, an expression of a verb; and know that if it were a noun the accent would be above on the first letter and it would be vocalized with a *patach*, and this one is vocalized with a *kamatz katan* and its accent is below on the *resh*. And do not wonder at *barakh*, that it does not say *barach*, for many words ending in *resh* are used so, such as “the enemy hath reproached the LORD” (below, 74), and it does not say *cherach*.
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s example is Psalms 74:18 (JPS: “how the enemy hath reproached the LORD”). The comment is a technical remark on vocalization and accent; translated literally.

Psalms.english_translation: Like *cheref* (“reproach”), and so every expression of *ni’utz*; so Menachem interpreted.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: in the pride of his countenance
Psalms.english_translation: Because he is haughty of spirit and lifts and raises his face and his nose in his haughtiness.
All his devices say to him: The Holy One, blessed be He, will not require all that I do, for there is no judgment.
“There is no Judgment and no Judge.”
*Yachilu* — they succeed; and similar to it, “therefore his prosperity shall not endure” (Job 20:21). And some explain *yachilu* like “let it fall (*yacholu*) upon the head of Joab” (2 Samuel 3).
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi cites Job 20:21 and 2 Samuel 3:29 for the root.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thy judgments are far above out of his sight
Psalms.english_translation: Removed and far from him are Your judgments of sufferings and punishments, for they do not come upon him.
With a puff of wind he puffs at them and they fall before him.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: to all generations shall not be in adversity
Psalms.english_translation: No evil will come upon me in my generations.
*Vetokh* — an expression of evil thought that lodges within him continually.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: His eyes are on the watch for the helpless
Psalms.english_translation: The eyes of Amalek on Israel, who are your host (*cheilekha*) — they lie in wait.

*Lechelkah* — “upon You *chelkah* shall leave.” Both are in the Masorah among the words in which *kah* serves in place of *kha*, such as “and upon thee, and upon thy people” (*u-vekha u-ve-amekha*, Exodus 7:29), “Discernment shall guard thee” (*tevunah tintzerekha*, Proverbs 2:11), “all that I have commanded thee” (Exodus 29:35), “I am the woman that stood by thee” (*nitzevet immakh*, 1 Samuel 1:26). We learned from the Masorah that *chelkah* is like *cheilkha*, “your host.” And Menachem interpreted *lechelkah yitzpenu*, and likewise *ya’azov chelkah*, like “and the helpless fall” (*chelka’im*) — an expression of lowly and rebellious ones, and the *kaf* is the root of the word.
Psalms.translator_note: A technical remark on endings; Rashi cites the verses for their endings, so the Hebrew forms are left transliterated. The printed “Exodus 29:35” form (*otkhem*) differs slightly from the verse (*otekha*). The last sentence is translated literally.

Psalms.english_translation: Thus is the way of the one lying in wait: he crouches and lowers and diminishes himself, so that he not be recognized.

“The host of the broken ones.” I saw in the Great Masorah: *chelka’im* is one of fifteen words that are written as one word and read as two words, such as *ba gad* — “Fortune is come” (Genesis 30), *esh dat lamo* — “a fiery law unto them” (Deuteronomy 33), *mah lakhem* — “What mean you that you crush My people” (Isaiah 3). This too: *chelka’im* — “the host of the broken ones”; *ka’im* is an expression of “and the broken in heart he was ready to slay” (below, 109), and if you say, “the nun of the root will prove it” — “Because with lies you have cowed (*hakha’ot*) the heart of the righteous” (Ezekiel 13) — we have learned that the nun of *nakheh* is like the nun of *nivzah* (1 Samuel 15) and the nun of *nikleh*. And so is its interpretation: “and fall in his *atzumav*,” of this wicked one, with his gestures and his winks — an expression of “bring forth your reasons (*atzumotekhem*)” (Isaiah 41), “shutteth his eyes (*otzem einav*)” (ibid. 33): the host of the poor. Another explanation: “by his mighty ones (*atzumav*)” — through his strong men. Rabbi Simon said: This wicked one does not put into his *kliros* — that is, his army — any but mighty men like himself, as it is said (Daniel 3), “And he commanded certain mighty men that were in his army (*ve-legavrin gabrei chail di vechayleih*) to bind Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego.” And Menachem interpreted *chelka’im* like “poor and wretched” (*dal ve-chelekh*), and the *kaf* is a letter of the root in the word.
Psalms.translator_note: The comment is long and technical (a Masoretic list, word division, and the root of *chelka’im*) and is translated literally. Printed “(below, 109)” is Psalms 109:16; “Ezekiel 13” is 13:22; “Isaiah 41” is 41:21; “ibid. 33” is Isaiah 33:15; “Daniel 3” is Daniel 3:20 (Aramaic). JPS renders the key words as follows: Genesis 30:11, “Fortune is come”; Deuteronomy 33:2, “a fiery law unto them”; Isaiah 3:15, “What mean you that you crush My people”; Psalms 109:16, “And the broken in heart he was ready to slay.” The term *kliros* is left transliterated. The Aramaic is translated as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He, because he said in his heart, “Thou wilt not require.”
What he does, and You keep silent.
So is Your way: that You look upon trouble and anger.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: to requite them with Thy hand
Psalms.english_translation: By Your power You give a hand to the wicked to succeed in their wickedness.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Unto Thee the helpless committeth himself
Psalms.english_translation: Israel, Your people, who are Your host, they leave the burden upon You, that You execute judgment on the wicked. And Menachem interpreted *ya’azov* as an expression of help, like “thou shalt surely release it with him” (Exodus 23:5), and Menachem interpreted *chelkah* as an expression of poor and wretched, and the *kaf* is the root of the word.
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi cites Exodus 23:5 for the root; JPS: “thou shalt surely release it with him.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou hast been the helper of the fatherless
Psalms.english_translation: In the early days.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Break Thou the arm of the wicked
Psalms.english_translation: Of Amalek the wicked.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: search out his wickedness, till none be found
Psalms.english_translation: The transgressors of Israel, when they see the wicked prospering, their heart carries them to act wickedly; but when You break the arm of the wicked, if You come to seek out the wickedness of the wicked of Israel, You will not find it.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The LORD is King for ever and ever
Psalms.english_translation: After the nations perish from His land.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: To right the fatherless and the oppressed
Psalms.english_translation: To execute the judgment of Israel, the orphans and the crushed.
Esau.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: man who is of the earth
Psalms.english_translation: To crush and shatter the mortals and the sick.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: How say you to my soul
Psalms.english_translation: This is like “for they have driven me out this day that I should not cleave unto the inheritance of the LORD” (1 Samuel 26:19) — that they drove him out of the Land to outside the Land; and here he says “In the LORD have I taken refuge,” that He will return me to cleave to my inheritance. How can you say, you who harry my soul: “Flee, to your mountain, you bird that wanders”? For every person who is shaken about is compared to a bird that wanders from the nest, as it is written, “As a bird that wandereth from her nest, so is a man that wandereth from his place” (Proverbs 27:8): your nest wandered, for we drove you from the whole mountain like a bird that wanders. *Nudu* is the written form (*ketiv*), which is expounded to apply also to Israel, for the nations say this to them.
Doeg and the informers of the generation, who cast enmity between me and Saul.
The expression of treading applies to a bow, for when it is strong one must set his foot upon it when he wants to stretch it.
Their tongue — “they bend their tongue, their bow of falsehood.”
Psalms.translator_note: The quotation is Jeremiah 9:2 (JPS: “And they bend their tongue, their bow of falsehood”); the printed text gives no reference.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: ready their arrow upon the string
Psalms.english_translation: [The string] of the bow — *קורד"א דאר"ק* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: To shoot — *אהגיט"ר* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: In secret.
David and the priests of Nob.
Through you the priests of HaShem, the righteous, who are the foundations of the world, were killed.
David, who did not sin — what did he do? In spite of all this, you will bear the iniquity, not I.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The LORD is in His holy temple
Psalms.english_translation: He sees and tests their deeds; and though His throne is high in heaven, His eyes see you on earth.

And if, because I am smitten and pursued by you, you boast and say, “God hath forsaken him” (below, 71) — it is not so; rather, this is the way of the Holy One, blessed be He: to chastise and to test the righteous and not the wicked. This flax-worker: as long as he knows that his flax is good, he beats it, and when it is not good, he reduces the beating, because it snaps.
And He lays aside for him the recompense of his iniquities for the long world to come; and then He will rain upon them in Gehenna.
An expression of coals (*pechamim*).

*Zal’afot* — an expression of burning, and Menachem interpreted it as an expression of a raging tempest of destruction; and so, “because of the burning heat of famine” (Lamentations 5:10); (below, 119) “Burning indignation hath taken hold upon me,” that is, a tempest (סא"א).
Psalms.translator_note: it is left as printed. Rashi’s words after “that is” are unclear in the printed text.

Psalms.english_translation: And He will have mercy on the righteous and loves them, for “the upright shall behold His face.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The upright shall behold His face
Psalms.english_translation: It goes back to “the LORD is righteous, He loveth righteousness,” and to those “whose face shall behold the upright.” And our Rabbis interpreted “the wicked bend the bow” of Shebna and his company, and they interpreted “the upright in heart” of Hezekiah and his company.
“For the foundations are destroyed”: if the foundations were destroyed by them, what has the righteous one of the world wrought? But the order of the verses does not fit the Midrash.
Psalms.translator_note: The words Rashi comments on, “When the foundations are destroyed,” stand in Psalms 11:3; the comment is filed under 11:7, so this lemma is taken from 11:7.

Psalms.english_translation: A harp of eight strings.
*Gamar* — ended.
*Pasu* — *פיילירינ"ט* in French, like *afsu* (“have come to an end”), and so Menachem interpreted.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: the faithful fail from among the children of men
Psalms.english_translation: All lie about me and spy out the places where I hide, and tell Saul: “Doth not David hide himself with us?” (below, 54).
With two hearts: they show me peace, and there is hatred hidden in their hearts.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Our tongue will we make mighty
Psalms.english_translation: With our tongue we will prevail.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: For the oppression of the poor
Psalms.english_translation: Because of the plunder of the poor, who are plundered by you, such as I and my men and the priests of Nob; and because of the groaning of the needy, HaShem will say: Now I will arise to their help.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I will set him in safety
Psalms.english_translation: I will set them in salvation; He will speak concerning them.

An expression of much speaking, of which there is a great deal in the Book of Proverbs and in Habakkuk: “And it declareth of the end, and doth not lie” (*ve-yafe’ach la-ketz*); and Menachem interpreted it as an expression of a snare, like (below, 124) “The snare is broken.”
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi cites the verses for the root. JPS Habakkuk 2:3: “And it declareth of the end, and doth not lie”; JPS Psalms 124:7: “The snare is broken.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The words of the LORD are pure words
Psalms.english_translation: Those that He has the ability to fulfill; but the words of men are not “words,” for they die and cannot fulfill them.
Clear and enduring: all that He promises He does, and behold, He promised me salvation and kingship.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: As silver tried in a crucible on the earth
Psalms.english_translation: Behold they are like refined silver, revealed to all the earth. *Ba’alil* is an expression of revealing, in the language of the Mishnah: “whether it is seen *ba’alil* or not seen *ba’alil*,” etc.; and some explain *ba’alil* as an expression of “above,” and so is its interpretation: “silver refined *ba’alil la-aretz*” — that is, like silver refined in the best of the earth and the highest of it, for a furnace to refine, man makes from the finest earth. Another version: *ba’alil* is like *eli* (Proverbs 27): “in a mortar with the pestle” (*be-toch ha-rifot be-eli*), which is the name of a vessel in which one pounds; and so *ba’alil* is the furnace into which gold and silver are melted; and this is not likely, since it does not say the *eli* of the mortar in which they pound, but the hand of the mortar with which they pound, which in French is called *פילאו"ן*. Another version: *ba’alil* is an expression of *ba’al yad* (“possessor of hand”), that is, lord of the earth, and the praise of the word is directed to the Name; and this is the Targum of Jonathan: it is an expression of lordship, and he said that our words are refined silver from the Lord of the earth, who is the Name, who refined and purified them (סא"א).
Psalms.translator_note: it is left as printed. The Mishnaic quotation was not identified. JPS Proverbs 27:22: “Though thou shouldest bray a fool in a mortar with a pestle among groats”; Rashi’s Hebrew wording there is *be-toch ha-rifot be-eli* and is cited for the word *eli*. The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou wilt keep them, O LORD
Psalms.english_translation: Those poor and needy ones who are pursued by this generation, who are informers. “Refined sevenfold” — there is an aggadic Midrash, and it is settled in order: Rabbi Joshua of Sikhnin, in the name of Rabbi Levi: The children who were in the days of David, before they tasted the taste of sin, knew how to expound the Torah in forty-nine ways to every side; and that is “seven times”; and David prayed for them: Master of the Universe, see how clear and refined sevenfold is Your Torah and Your word in their hearts. “Thou, LORD, wilt keep them” — guard them in their hearts; “Thou wilt preserve us from this generation,” lest they learn their ways to be informers.
Psalms.translator_note: The Midrash is cited without a source; I did not identify it.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The wicked walk on every side
Psalms.english_translation: To hide snares to make me stumble.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: When vileness is exalted among the sons of men
Psalms.english_translation: From their jealousy, for their eye is evil at my greatness, that I was taken from behind the flock to be king; and this is its interpretation: “when vileness is exalted among the sons of men” — when a person who is despised in the eyes of men is exalted. And this is like what is said elsewhere, “The stone which the builders rejected” (below, 118). And an aggadic Midrash interprets it of Israel in the future, when they will be exalted. And Menachem interpreted *kerum zulut livnei adam* as “like a wild ox that devours human beings”; and *kerum* would be like *rom* and *re’em*, and *zulut* like *zolel*, and *sove* (Deuteronomy 21). And so is its interpretation: “The wicked walk on every side” around the poor man, wicked people go about to swallow him for nothing, “like a wild ox devouring human beings.”
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi cites Deuteronomy 21:20 for the root (*zolel*, JPS: “a glutton”).

Psalms.english_translation: Four times, corresponding to the four exiles, and it is said on behalf of all Israel.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: lest I sleep the sleep of death
Psalms.english_translation: For death is called sleep: “and sleep a perpetual sleep” (Jeremiah 51:39).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The fool hath said in his heart
Psalms.english_translation: David said two psalms in this book on one subject; the first on Nebuchadnezzar and the second (below, 53) on Titus the wicked. This one prophesied about Nebuchadnezzar, who was destined to enter the Sanctuary and destroy it, with no one of all his armies protesting.
“I will ascend above the heights of the clouds” (Isaiah 14:14).
*Ma’alalim* (“deeds”).
No man in his armies protests.
*Ne’elachu* — turned into corruption.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Shall not all the workers of iniquity know it
Psalms.english_translation: Will they not know in the end what befell them?
The seed of Nebuchadnezzar.
They made a feast (Daniel 5:1): “Belshazzar the king made a great feast.”
Psalms.translator_note: The Aramaic of Daniel 5:1 is translated with the JPS wording.

Psalms.english_translation: They did not think of Him and did not remember His wonders and His awesome deeds at their feasts, and they used His vessels. And our Rabbis explained: Whoever did not rob Israel did not taste a pleasant taste in his food; “those who eat My people” seemed to them like those who eat bread, who tasted the pleasant taste of food.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: There are they in great fear
Psalms.english_translation: That his recompense was paid to Belshazzar, etc.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: God is with the righteous generation
Psalms.english_translation: In the generation of Jeconiah, who were righteous.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: You would put to shame the counsel of the poor
Psalms.english_translation: You say that the counsel of Israel is shameful, because they trust in HaShem, “for the LORD is his refuge.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Oh that the salvation of Israel were come out of Zion
Psalms.english_translation: Then the day will draw near when He will give from Zion the salvation of Israel, and then “Jacob shall rejoice, Israel shall be glad.”
The good that he says in his heart is the truth, and he is not one thing in the mouth and another in the heart (סא"א).
Psalms.translator_note: it is left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: *אנקוש"א* in French, like “And he hath slandered (*va-yeragel*) thy servant” (2 Samuel 19:28). This psalm is to make known the quality of piety.
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi cites the verse for the root. The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: *רפורט"א* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: If his relative committed a transgression that carries punishment, he punishes him by law, and does not bear his reproach, so that there be an opening for the reproacher to say: So did so-and-so your relative do, and you covered up for him.
Whoever is vile in his wickedness is despised in the eyes of the righteous, such as Hezekiah, who dragged his father’s bones in disgrace.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He that sweareth to his own hurt
Psalms.english_translation: “To do evil” — to himself.
His oath; all the more so that he does not change it concerning a matter that is not to his harm.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Nor taketh a bribe against the innocent
Psalms.english_translation: Against a poor man to condemn him in judgment, to pervert his judgment. And further our Rabbis explained: he does not take a bribe against the innocent, to acquit him in his judgment — all the more so that he does not take a bribe to pervert judgment.
And he is fit to dwell in Your tents (סא"א).
Psalms.translator_note: it is left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: If he is moved, his being moved is not forever; rather, he totters and rises.

Our Rabbis said: “To David, who was lowly and perfect (*mach ve-tam*), whose blow (*makkato*) was perfect, for he was born circumcised.” But the line of Scripture does not fall on the Midrash here: there is a psalm in which it says “of David, a Michtam” — there it can be explained: this song of David, who was lowly and perfect; but here, where it says “Michtam of David,” it cannot be so explained. And I say that it is one of the names of the kinds of melodies of song, and differs in the melodies of the song. Another explanation: “Michtam of David” is an expression of a crown, like *ketem* (gold), which means that David used to say this, “Keep me, O God, for I have taken refuge in Thee,” and it was for him like a crown, as it is said (above, 5), “Thou dost encompass him with favour as with a shield” (סא"א).
Psalms.translator_note: it is left as printed. Rashi’s quotation of Psalms 5:13 is partial.

Psalms.english_translation: To the Congregation of Israel David said: You must say to HaShem, “Thou art Lord, and Thy hand is uppermost against all who come upon me.” Another explanation: “*Amarti la-Shem Adonai atah*” — he was speaking to his soul, and so we find its parallel (2 Samuel 14), “and David ceased,” whose interpretation is “and the soul of David ceased”; here too, “*amarti*” — my soul to HaShem, “Thou art my Lord”: my soul, you must say so to the Holy One, blessed be He (סא"א).
Psalms.translator_note: it is left as printed. Rashi reads *amarti* as feminine (“you said”). Printed “2 Samuel 14” is 2 Samuel 13:39 (JPS: “And the soul of king David failed with longing for Absalom”).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I have no good but in Thee
Psalms.english_translation: The good things that You do for me are not incumbent on You in order to repay me, for it is not by my righteousness that You do good to me.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: As for the holy that are in the earth
Psalms.english_translation: For the sake of the holy ones who are buried in the earth, who walked before You in truth.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: the excellent in whom is all my delight
Psalms.english_translation: They are the mighty ones in whom is all my desire, and all my needs are done for their sake.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Let the idols of them be multiplied
Psalms.english_translation: All this David says to HaShem: May the sorrows of those who deny You be multiplied — those who hurry and tremble to worship another god. Another version: *maharu* is an expression of *mohar* (bride-price) — *דואירנ"ט* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Their drink-offerings of blood will I not offer
Psalms.english_translation: I will not be like them, to throw blood to an idol, and I will not take the name of an idol upon my lips.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: the portion of mine inheritance and of my cup
Psalms.english_translation: All my good is from Him. Another version: *ve-chosi* — and my reckoning, like “you shall make your count for the lamb” (*tikhosu*, Exodus 12:4), and so Menachem connected it.

You are the one who placed my hand on the good portion, as it is said, “I have set before thee life and death … therefore choose life” (Deuteronomy 30:19) — like a man who loves one of his sons and places his hand on the good portion and says: Choose this one for yourself.

You lowered my hand upon the lot, an expression of “the rafters sink in” (*yamakh*, Ecclesiastes 10:18); so it is expounded in the Sifrei. And it may also be interpreted as an expression of support (*temikhah*), an aggadic Midrash, like “and he held up (*va-yitmokh*) his father’s hand” (Genesis 48).
Psalms.translator_note: The Sifrei citation was not verified.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The lines are fallen unto me in pleasant places
Psalms.english_translation: When the lot fell to me to be in Your portion, this is a pleasant portion; even upon me a beautiful inheritance such as this.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I will bless the LORD, who hath given me counsel
Psalms.english_translation: Until here David prophesied about the Congregation of Israel that she would say so, and now he says: And I, I too shall bless HaShem, who counseled me to choose life and to walk in His ways.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: in the night seasons my reins instruct me
Psalms.english_translation: To fear Him and to love Him. And our Rabbis explained it of Abraham our father, who learned Torah by himself before the Torah was given; but we too must settle the verses in their order.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I have set the LORD always before me
Psalms.english_translation: In all my deeds I placed His fear before my eyes. And why? Because He is always at my right hand, to help me that I not be moved. Another explanation: “I have set the LORD always before me” — a Torah scroll was with him to read in it all the days of his life; and this is what he said, “at my right hand, I shall not be moved” — after the Torah that was given with His right hand, with which I occupy myself, and therefore “I shall not be moved” (סא"א).
Psalms.translator_note: it is left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: Because I trust that You will not abandon my soul to Sheol; for with regard to the iniquity of a great transgression that was in my hand, You brought me tidings, “The LORD also hath put away thy sin” (2 Samuel 12:13) — all the more so that from now on You will not abandon me to depart from You.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou makest me to know the path of life
Psalms.english_translation: It is the future tense and not an expression of prayer.
Joy without end or limit, which is the joy of the future (סא"א).
Psalms.translator_note: it is left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: Joys that are before You, in the company that is near You.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Let my judgment come forth from Thy presence
Psalms.english_translation: The transgressions in my hand for which I deserve to be judged with sufferings — let them go out from before You and not come before You in judgment.
If there are merits in my hand, let Your eyes see with equity by them.
I know that there is a transgression in my hand, and if the judgment of my punishment comes before You, I will not be righteous in judgment, for You have already tried my heart.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou hast visited it in the night
Psalms.english_translation: At evening time, with the sin of Bathsheba, as it is said, “And it came to pass at eventide, that David arose” etc. (2 Samuel 11:2).
You tried me.
You did not find in me Your desire.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed gloss is very short; translated literally.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: a thought which should not pass my mouth
Psalms.english_translation: If it should rise again in my thought to be tested before You, let my mouth not pass over to say again, “Try me and test me,” as I already said, as it is said (below, 26), “Examine me, O LORD, and try me.” For David said before the Holy One, blessed be He: Why do they say “God of Abraham” and do not say “God of David”? He said to him: I tried him with ten trials and he was found whole. He said: “Examine me and try me,” as is found in tractate Shabbat.
Psalms.translator_note: The tractate is as printed; I did not verify the source.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: As for the doings of men, by the word of Thy lips
Psalms.english_translation: From then on, for every deed of man that I came to do, I guarded, because of the word of Your lips, the ways of the violent, to turn away from them, that I not walk in them. But “to hold up my steps” always in Your paths, “my feet have not slipped” from them. Another explanation: “As for the doings of men, by the word of Thy lips,” etc. — because a person must use his deeds according to the straightness of the word of Your lips, as You said, “Thou shalt not commit adultery,” I kept away from the ways of the violent, although I did not act as was proper, in Your goodness.
Psalms.translator_note: The last clause is difficult as printed and is translated literally.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: My steps have held fast to Thy paths
Psalms.english_translation: From then on, for every deed of man that I came to do, let Your eyes see the equities, and let the judgment go forth from before You.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed comment appears to repeat phrases from Psalms 17:2 and is difficult; translated literally.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: for Thou wilt answer me, O God
Psalms.english_translation: For I am confident that You will answer me.

*דשיבר"א* in French, like “so that we are distinguished (*ve-niflinu*), I and Thy people” (Exodus 33:16); “who savest by Thy right hand those who take refuge in Thee from those who rise up against them.” “Make Thy mercies passing great, Thou who savest those who take refuge” — behold, this is an inverted verse: “Make Thy mercies passing great, to save by Thy right hand those who take refuge,” etc.
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi cites Exodus 33:16 for the root. The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Keep me as the apple of the eye
Psalms.english_translation: *Ishon* is the black of the eye on which the light depends, and after its blackness it is called *ishon*, an expression of darkness; and the Holy One, blessed be He, prepared for it a guard, the eyelashes of the eye, which always cover it.
Because of this that they plunder me — my enemies who encompass me for my life, to take my soul.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Their gross heart they have shut tight
Psalms.english_translation: In their fat and their thickness they shut their heart and their eyes from looking at Your work, to fear You.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: At our every step they have now encompassed us
Psalms.english_translation: Our heel — now the enemies have encompassed us, and their eyes they set to bend us down to the earth, to strip us in the earth. And it seems to me that David prayed this prayer after the matter of Uriah and Joab came into his hand, when Israel was in the land of the children of Ammon, besieging Rabbah (2 Samuel 11:1); and David feared lest they stumble there because of the sin in his hand, and the Philistines and Moab and Edom and all the evil neighbors of the Land of Israel, who wait for the day of their calamity, would hear and come upon them.
*Yikhsof* — he desires, like “because thou sore longest” (*nikhsof nikhsafta*, Genesis 31).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 31” is Genesis 31:30.

Psalms.english_translation: Of the enemy.
Trip up his feet, and he will bow and fall.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Deliver my soul from the wicked, by Thy sword
Psalms.english_translation: From every wicked person, who is Your sword, whom You empower to exact payment from those who are liable to You.
From those who die by Your hand — on my bed I choose to be.
From those who die in old age, after they have gathered rust — *רדוייל"א* in French — and from the righteous, whose portion is in life.
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 17:14 (“De vieillesse, m. à m. rouille”), in forms such as רודייל and רדיילא; the printed form (רדוייל"א) is a variant spelling.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: whose belly Thou fillest with Thy treasure
Psalms.english_translation: And from those whose belly You fill with Your good, which You stored up for those who fear You.
Their possessions, which they leave at their death.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: As for me, I shall behold Thy face in righteousness
Psalms.english_translation: In the future; or: “in righteousness I shall behold Your face” — bring out my judgment from before You, and take hold of the righteous acts that are in my hand, and by them I shall behold Your face.
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s second reading puts “in righteousness” first; JPS reads “As for me, I shall behold Thy face in righteousness.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I shall be satisfied, when I awake, with Thy likeness
Psalms.english_translation: I shall be satisfied with the sight of Your likeness when the dead awake from their sleep. Another version: I shall be satisfied with the sight of Your face when the dead awake from their sleep, for they are in the form of Your likeness, as it is said, “for in the image of God made He man” (ibid. 9).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “ibid. 9” is Genesis 9:6.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: in the day that the LORD delivered him
Psalms.english_translation: When he grew old and all his troubles had already passed over him and he was saved from them.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: and from the hand of Saul
Psalms.english_translation: But was Saul not included? Rather, because he was harsh to him and pursued him more than all of them. Similar to this you say, “Go view the land, and Jericho” (Joshua 2:1).
*Erchamekha* — I will love You, as it is translated for “thou shalt love thy neighbour” (Leviticus 19:18): “and you shall have mercy (love).”
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi refers to the Aramaic rendering *ve-tirachem* of Leviticus 19:18.

Psalms.english_translation: That You helped me at the Rock of Divisions when I was hemmed in between Saul and his men, to be seized, as it is said, “for Saul and his men compassed David and his men” (1 Samuel 23:26).
An expression of stronghold.
An expression of rock.
*Echseh* — *אברי"אייר* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 18:3 (“Je me mets à l’abri”), in forms such as אבריאר; the printed form (אברי"אייר) is a variant spelling.

Psalms.english_translation: I will cover myself in His shadow, as in what is said, “And embrace the rock for want of a shelter” (Job 24:8), for the rocks are a covering and a shield to those who walk the roads from the winds and from the downpour of rains.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Praised, I cry, is the LORD
Psalms.english_translation: With praises I shall call and pray before Him constantly; that is, even before the deliverance I praise Him, because I am confident that I shall be saved from my enemies.
Many times the wicked surrounded me; *afafuni* is like *sevavuni*, and so “for innumerable evils have compassed me about” (below, 40).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “below, 40” is Psalms 40:13.

Psalms.english_translation: Camps of enemies, like “a band of prophets” in the Book of Samuel; and Targum Jonathan: “like a woman sitting on the birthstool” — an expression of birth-pangs.
Also an expression of troops that rush like a torrent.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The cords of Sheol surrounded me
Psalms.english_translation: Like “cords of Death”: camps of wicked ones; and I, what was I doing?
Psalms.translator_note: The printed word משריין is translated as “camps” from the context.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: In my distress I called upon the LORD
Psalms.english_translation: I was calling to HaShem constantly.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Then the earth did shake and quake
Psalms.english_translation: It is not connected to the verse above; rather its beginning is connected to its end: “because He was wroth, the earth did shake and quake,” for *ki* is used in the sense of “when”: when He was wroth and came to take vengeance for His people and His servants against Pharaoh and his people, the earth shook and quaked.
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi reorders the verse’s clauses; JPS reads “Then the earth did shake and quake … because He was wroth.” Rashi’s quoted clause is translated from his Hebrew.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Smoke arose up in His nostrils
Psalms.english_translation: *אנשישנאר"ילאש* in French; so it is the way of every anger to send up smoke from the nostrils.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He bowed the heavens also, and came down
Psalms.english_translation: To pass through the land of Egypt; and “came down” as it sounds. Another version: *איאנטב"יש* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: *Vayeda* — and he flew, like “as the vulture swoopeth down” (Deuteronomy 28:49).
Psalms.translator_note: The Hebrew Rashi cites reads *ka’asher yide’eh ha-nesher*; JPS: “as the vulture swoopeth down.”
