Psalms.english_translation: That in the thickness of the skies there is darkness, which is around Him. And lest you say that inside the darkness there is no light, the verse says “at the brightness before Him”; and from within His partition, through His thick clouds around Him, there burst and pass through hail and coals of fire.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: there passed through His thick clouds
Psalms.english_translation: *Avru* — *טרישפא"שנט* in French; the hail bursts and passes through upon the Egyptians at the Red Sea.
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 18:13 (“Trépassant”), in forms such as טריפטנט and טריישפשנט; the printed form (טרישפא"שנט) is a variant spelling.

Psalms.english_translation: When the sea was split.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: the foundations of the world were laid bare
Psalms.english_translation: For all the waters of the world were split.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: At the blast of the breath of Thy nostrils
Psalms.english_translation: *Mi-nishmat* — from the blowing.
His angels, to save Israel from the sea and from Egypt.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He drew me out of many waters
Psalms.english_translation: *Yamsheni* — an expression of bringing out, like “Because I drew him out of the water” (Exodus 2:10).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: They confronted me in the day of my calamity
Psalms.english_translation: My enemies would hurry and come first upon me on the day of my calamity, “but the LORD was a stay” etc.
According to the righteousness of my going after Him in the wilderness.

*Bor* — an expression of cleanness, like “and pure of heart” (*u-var levav*). Another explanation: “He sent from on high, He took me” — he said it concerning himself, in the name of the angel who came at the Rock of Divisions to remove Saul from him, as it is said, “And an angel came unto Saul,” etc.
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi cites *u-var levav* for the root; JPS renders it “a pure heart” (Psalms 24:4). The last quotation is from 1 Samuel 23:27, where JPS has “But there came a messenger unto Saul”; Rashi’s Hebrew reads *mal’akh* (“angel”) there.

Psalms.english_translation: That I did not kill him when I cut off the corner of his robe.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: all His ordinances were before me
Psalms.english_translation: I always placed them before my eyes.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: With the merciful Thou dost show Thyself merciful
Psalms.english_translation: That is: since such are His ways, to repay measure for measure — “the merciful,” “the perfect,” “the pure” — corresponding to the three Patriarchs.
*Navar* — faithful.
Corresponding to Pharaoh.
When he fought at night against the troop of Amalek that came upon Ziklag, as it is said, “And David smote them from the twilight even unto the evening of the next day” (1 Samuel 30:17).
In Your trust.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: by my God do I scale a wall
Psalms.english_translation: When he came to fight against Jebus and said, “Whosoever smiteth the Jebusites first shall be chief and captain” (1 Chronicles 11), Joab brought a green cypress and bent it, was hung upon it, and went up on the wall. David said, “Let the righteous smite me” etc. (below, 141). The Holy One, blessed be He, shortened the wall for him, and he leaped over. In Midrash Tehillim.
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “1 Chronicles 11” is 1 Chronicles 11:6; printed “below, 141” is Psalms 141:5.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The word of the LORD is tried
Psalms.english_translation: Clear; He promises and does.
He removed from my ways every stumbling and obstacle, until it became complete and trodden down (*kavush*).
The feet of the females stand more evenly than those of the males.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: arms do bend a bow of brass
Psalms.english_translation: *Venichata* — an expression of bending a bow, like “Thine arrows *nichatu* in me” (below, 38). Its verb is *nachat*, and when it is reflexive a dagesh comes and omits the nun. *Venichata* is from *ninchata*, like *nachar* my throat (below, 69) from *ninchar*; like *nachar mapuach* (Jeremiah 6:29), *nidaf* from *ninnadef*; “mine eye *niggerah*” (Lamentations 3:49), like *ninnagerah*; *nittenah*, like *ninnatenah*; *niggof*, from *ninnagef*. And it is not to be explained from the root *chatah*, for then he would have had to say *nechatatah*, as from *asah* comes *na'asetah* and from *anah* *ne'enetah*. Another explanation: “And *nichata* a bow of brass are my arms” — *chiyit*, an expression of bending a bow, like “Thine arrows *nichatu*” (below, 38). The nun is not a root letter in the word, but like *nachalu*. … “And a bow of brass was bent by my arms.” Bows of brass were hung up for David in his house, and the kings of the nations would see them and say to one another: Do you think David has the strength to bend them? This is only to frighten us. And he would hear, and would bend them in front of them.
Psalms.translator_note: Words cited for their grammatical form are left transliterated. Printed “below, 38” is Psalms 38:3 (JPS: “Thine arrows are gone deep into me”); printed “below, 69” is Psalms 69:4. In the second explanation the printed word חיית and the comparison “like נחלו” could not be resolved; they are left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thy condescension hath made me great
Psalms.english_translation: You increased the quality of Your humility, to deal with me by it.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou hast enlarged my steps under me
Psalms.english_translation: One who widens his steps is not apt to fall; and so it says, “When thou goest, thy step shall not be straitened” (Proverbs 4:12).
*Ma'adu* — *איקלורגירי"נט* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: *Karsulai* — these are the feet, from the *astorin*, which is called *chevilie* [printed קביל"ייא] in French (the ankle), and downward.
Psalms.translator_note: Old French *chevilie* (ankle): read from Darmesteter’s footnote at Psalms 18:37 (“Mes chevilles”) and his index; the printed form is a variant spelling. The printed word האסתורין is not in Darmesteter and is left as printed. The Hebrew word is rendered “my feet” by JPS.

Psalms.english_translation: They turn their necks to me and flee.
*לע"ג שלה'*
Psalms.translator_note: The printed text of this comment could not be resolved; it is left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: For there is no power in it; and they return and call to HaShem, but He answered them not.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: beat them small as the dust
Psalms.english_translation: An expression of pounding.
Like mire that is poured out, that is not thick, like “as they emptied their sacks” (Genesis 42:35); “Neither hath he been emptied from vessel to vessel” (Jeremiah 48:11).
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi cites the verbs for their root; in Jeremiah 48:11 JPS reads “And hath not been emptied from vessel to vessel.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou hast delivered me from the contentions of the people
Psalms.english_translation: That I not be punished by the law of Israel for perverting judgment, nor for enslaving anyone in Israel more than is permitted.
Psalms.translator_note: The sense of the printed text is rendered as closely as possible.

Psalms.english_translation: For there is no punishment among them.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: As soon as they hear of me
Psalms.english_translation: Even not in my presence, but only that they hear of my mission.
They will turn aside to my obedience and will be obedient to my words.
Because of fear.

They will become weary, like “thou wilt surely wear away” (*navol tavol*; Exodus 18), which is translated *mil'ah tile'i* (“you will weary”); and Menachem explained it like “After I am waxed old” (Genesis 18:12), and so he explained *navol tavol*.
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “Exodus 18” is Exodus 18:18.

Psalms.english_translation: An expression of dread, from “in the chambers terror” (Deuteronomy 32:25), which is translated *charegat mota*.

Because of the torments of prisons — a jail in which I shut them and torment them. “And they come trembling out of their close places.” Menachem interpreted it as an expression of the loosening of a girdle, and so its meaning is “and they will be loosened from their close places.” And Dunash interpreted “and they come trembling out of their close places” as “and they will limp from their fetters, which are placed upon their feet”; and the meaning of *vayacharegu* and *vayifs'chu* is as it is translated, *chagira*.
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s Hebrew “they come trembling” is rendered with JPS wording; the interpretations of Menachem and Dunash are translated from Rashi’s Hebrew.

Psalms.english_translation: He who does all this for me.
He gives me strength to take vengeance on my enemies.

*Vayadber* — and He will kill, an expression of *dever* (pestilence). Another version: like *vayanheg* (“and He leads”), which is translated *vedavar*; and so Menachem connected it, and he also connected “He subdueth (*yadber*) peoples under us” (below, 47).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “below, 47” is Psalms 47:4 (JPS: “He subdueth peoples under us”).

Psalms.english_translation: In my place and in exchange, like the matter of what is said, “And I will give man in place of thee” (Isaiah 43:3), “I have given Egypt as thy ransom” (ibid.).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 43:3” is Isaiah 43:3–4. Rashi’s first quotation is from 43:4, where JPS reads “Therefore will I give men for thee”; the second is from 43:3 (JPS: “I have given Egypt as thy ransom”).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The heavens declare the glory of God
Psalms.english_translation: The psalmist himself explained the matter: “There is no speech, there are no words” — they do not speak with people; rather, because “Their line is gone out through all the earth,” and they give light to His creatures, because of this the people tell the glory of God, and acknowledge and bless for the luminaries.

The stars and the constellations, which are the work of the hands of the Holy One, blessed be He, who are there, as it is said, “And God set them in the firmament of the heaven” (Genesis 1:17), and from there they declare His glory.

The work of creation is renewed from day to day: in the evening the sun sets, and it shines in the morning; and because of this people utter words of praise through the days and the nights, which instruct people to praise and to give thanks. Menachem explained *yabia* as an expression of a flowing spring.
An expression of declaring.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Their line is gone out through all the earth
Psalms.english_translation: The line of the heavens, which are stretched over the whole earth; and because of this “their words” are at “the end of the world,” for all speak of the wonders that they see.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: set a tent for the sun
Psalms.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: In them hath He set a tent
Psalms.english_translation: In the heavens; from here, that the sun is placed inside its case (*tiko*). Tanchuma.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed word תיקו is rendered “its case” (*tiko*) from the context.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Which is as a bridegroom coming out of his chamber
Psalms.english_translation: Every morning; and this is what it said, “The heavens declare the glory of God.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: his circuit unto the ends of it
Psalms.english_translation: The compass of its circuit, from end to end.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: nothing hid from the heat thereof
Psalms.english_translation: Had it not been placed in the lower firmament, no person would be hidden from it, because of its heat; for the sun and the moon are in the second firmament, as it is stated: There are seven firmaments — Vilon, Rakia, Shechakim, Zevul, Machon, Ma'on, Aravot — and he enumerates them in order. Vilon serves no purpose; Rakia has in it the sun and the moon, stars and constellations, etc.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The law of the LORD is perfect
Psalms.english_translation: It too shines like the sun, as it is said at the end of the passage, “enlightening the eyes,” and it says, “For the commandment is a lamp, and the teaching is light” (Proverbs 6:23). Another explanation: “And there is nothing hid from the heat thereof” — for the Day of Judgment, “and the day that cometh shall set them ablaze” (Malachi 3:19); but “The law of the LORD is perfect,” it restores the soul to the ways of life, and it protects those who study it from that blaze, as it is said, “And the sun of righteousness shall shine for them that fear My name, and healing” etc. (ibid.).
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s wording of the last quotation (Malachi 3:20) differs from JPS, which reads “But unto you that fear My name Shall the sun of righteousness arise with healing in its wings.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The testimony of the LORD is sure
Psalms.english_translation: It is trustworthy to testify concerning those who study it.

It brings it back from the ways of death to the ways of life. Torah, testimony, precepts, commandment, fear, ordinances — six, corresponding to the six orders of the Mishnah; and between each Name and Name there are five words, with the Name itself, corresponding to the five books of the Torah; and he seals at the end of them with truth: “they are righteous altogether” — all of them together are set right with kindness and truth.
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “אמת צדקו יחדיו”; JPS (Psalms 19:10): “The ordinances of the LORD are true, they are righteous altogether.”

Psalms.english_translation: It gives wisdom to the simple.
Making bright.
And the sweetness of *tzufim* — *ברויי"קאש* in French; and Menachem explained *nofet* as an expression of a drop, and so “drop honey” (Proverbs 5), “I have perfumed my bed” (Proverbs, ibid.). (סא"א)
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “Proverbs 5” is Proverbs 5:3; “ibid.” is Proverbs 7:17. The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. it is left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: In keeping of them there is great reward
Psalms.english_translation: I was careful in keeping them, for the sake of Your abundant goodness that You have stored up. And for this expression, *ekev*, like “because that Abraham hearkened to My voice” (Genesis 26). Another explanation: *ekev rav* — the end of Torah scholars is to come to greatness; *ekev* is an expression of end, and it has a counterpart in the language of the Mishnah: *ikvot meshicha*.
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 26” is Genesis 26:5. *Ikvot meshicha* is left transliterated as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: I was careful with them, but it is impossible to be careful not to err in them; and You, cleanse me of the hidden ones that were hidden from me, so that I did not know of my sin, in error.
From the deliberate sins.

I shall be perfect. The Sages said: To what is David similar? To a Cuthean who goes around to the doors, and they are cleverer in a matter than any other person: “Give me water to drink” — a thing that costs nothing. After he drank, he said: Is there a small onion here? After they gave it to him, he says: Is there an onion without salt? After they gave it to him, he said: Give me a little bread, so that the onion will not harm me. So David said in Psalms concerning errors, and afterward concerning deliberate sins, and afterward concerning rebellions; “transgressions” — these are the rebellions, where one intends to provoke; and so it says, “The king of Moab hath rebelled against me” (2 Kings 3).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “2 Kings 3” is 2 Kings 3:7.

Psalms.english_translation: For conciliation, to appease You.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The LORD answer thee in the day of trouble
Psalms.english_translation: This psalm is on account of his sending Joab and all Israel to war while he stood in Jerusalem and prayed for them, as in the matter that is said, “it is better that thou be ready to succour us out of the city” (2 Samuel 18:3–4); and our Rabbis said: Had it not been for David, Joab would not have waged war.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The name of the God of Jacob
Psalms.english_translation: For He promised him when he went to Haran, and He kept His promise; therefore it says, “God of Jacob.”
From His holy sanctuary (*heikhal*), for He dwells there.
These are the prayers that you pray in war.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: accept the fat of thy burnt-sacrifice
Psalms.english_translation: An expression of fat, like “and shall have eaten their fill, and waxen fat” (Deuteronomy 31:20); that is, He will accept them favorably, like fat burnt-offerings (*olot mechim*).
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi quotes only the words “and eaten his fill and waxen fat”; JPS reads “and they shall have eaten their fill, and waxen fat.” *Mechim* is left transliterated as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: We will shout for joy in thy victory
Psalms.english_translation: When the Holy One, blessed be He, saves you, all of us will sing to the Holy One, blessed be He.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: we will set up our standards
Psalms.english_translation: We will gather and form an army.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Now know I that the LORD saveth His anointed
Psalms.english_translation: This is the song of joy that we will now sing for this salvation that came to Joab and Israel: I know that the Omnipresent desires me and answered me from His holy heaven, for their salvation is my salvation.

There are among the nations those who trust in their iron chariots, and there are those who trust in their horses, but we will make mention of the name of HaShem, for salvation is His. *Nazkir* is an expression of burning incense and of prayer, like “He that maketh a memorial-offering of frankincense” (Isaiah 66:3); “the memorial-part thereof” (Leviticus 1); and therefore “They are bowed down and fallen.”
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “Leviticus 1” is Leviticus 2:2.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: we are risen, and stand upright
Psalms.english_translation: We prevailed over them, like “The LORD upholdeth the humble” (below, 147), an expression of strength.
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “below, 147” is Psalms 147:6.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: in Thy strength the king rejoiceth
Psalms.english_translation: Our Rabbis interpreted it of the King Messiah, and it is right to interpret it also of David himself, as a reply to others who expounded in it that after he took Bath-sheba he said this psalm.

An expression of speech, and it has no parallel; and Menachem brought for it a counterpart, *rishyon* — “according to the grant that they had of Cyrus king of Persia” (Ezra 3) — and both are expressions of the utterance of the lips.
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “Ezra 3” is Ezra 3:7.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou meetest him with choicest blessings
Psalms.english_translation: Before I asked of You, You anticipated me with Your blessing through Nathan the prophet: “And I will set up thy seed” etc. (2 Samuel 7), “and I will establish the throne of thy kingdom over Israel for ever.”
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s wording is a loose combination of 2 Samuel 7:12–13; JPS reads “I will set up thy seed after thee … and I will establish the throne of his kingdom for ever.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou settest a crown of fine gold on his head
Psalms.english_translation: “And he took the crown of their king, and it was on David’s head” (ibid. 12).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “ibid. 12” is 2 Samuel 12:30. Rashi reads *malkam* as “their king”; JPS reads “the crown of Malcam.”

Psalms.english_translation: When I was fleeing abroad because of Saul, I used to pray, “I shall walk before the LORD in the lands of the living” (below, 116).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “below, 116” is Psalms 116:9.

Psalms.english_translation: That You returned me to the Land of Israel.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: length of days for ever and ever
Psalms.english_translation: For my kingship, as You said, “And I will establish the throne of thy kingdom for ever.”
Psalms.translator_note: See the note at Psalms 21:4 on Rashi’s wording of 2 Samuel 7. Rashi’s wording differs from JPS (2 Samuel 7:13): “I will establish the throne of his kingdom for ever.”

Psalms.english_translation: Menachem explained *teshaveh* as *tasim* (“You place”); *tashit* — one expression for both.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou makest him glad with joy
Psalms.english_translation: An expression of joy.

In the Garden of Eden. And our Rabbis who expounded it of the King Messiah brought proof for the matter: “and to the Ancient of days he came, and before Him they brought him near” (Daniel 7:13); and it says, “And I will cause him to draw near, and he shall approach unto Me” (Jeremiah 30:21).
Psalms.translator_note: The Daniel quotation is Aramaic, translated as printed; JPS reads “and he came even to the Ancient of days, and he was brought near before Him.”

Psalms.english_translation: And he trusts in the mercy of the Most High that he shall not be moved.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thy hand shall be equal to all thine enemies
Psalms.english_translation: Every blow of Your hand that You have to bring — let it come upon Your enemies.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: in the time of thine anger
Psalms.english_translation: In the time of Your wrath.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The LORD shall swallow them up in His wrath
Psalms.english_translation: This is a prayer.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Their fruit shalt thou destroy from the earth
Psalms.english_translation: He prays to the Holy One, blessed be He, that the seed of wicked Amalek be destroyed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: For they intended evil against thee
Psalms.english_translation: Corresponding to wicked Titus, who said: He killed himself.
Psalms.translator_note: The sense of the printed words (שאמר הרג את עצמו) is not clear; they are translated as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: To do it.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: thou shalt make them turn their back
Psalms.english_translation: That You will make them into a portion, so that Israel will divide their money, as it is said, “And her gain and her hire” etc. (Isaiah 23:18).
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s Hebrew reads *sachrah* (“her merchandise”); JPS reads “her gain.”

Psalms.english_translation: With the strings of Your bows You will make ready Your arrows and prepare them to shoot at their faces.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Be Thou exalted, O LORD, in Thy strength
Psalms.english_translation: Over those who rise up; and we will sing and we will make music. (סא"א)
Psalms.translator_note: it is left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: The name of a musical instrument. Another explanation: concerning the Community of Israel, which is “a hind of loves,” “that looketh forth as the dawn” (Song of Songs 7:10); and our Rabbis expounded it of Esther; and Menachem explained *ayelet* as an expression of strength, like “O Thou my strength, hasten to help me” (this chapter).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “Song of Songs 7:10” is Song of Songs 6:10; the quotation “O Thou my strength, hasten to help me” is Psalms 22:20.

Psalms.english_translation: An expression of morning; and Menachem explained it as an expression of seeking, like “He that diligently seeketh good seeketh favour” (Proverbs 11:27) and like *lashachar panekha*.
Psalms.translator_note: *Lashachar panekha* is left transliterated as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: She is destined to go *begilah*, and David said this prayer concerning the future.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed word בגילה literally reads “in her joy”; it may be a misprint for בגולה (“in exile”), which would fit the context, but this is not confirmed. The word is left transliterated.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: at the words of my cry
Psalms.english_translation: And from the words of my roaring.
I call to You from day to day and You do not answer.
And He sits listening to the praises of Israel from ancient days.
He refers to all of Israel as one man.
They open, like “firstling of an ass” (*peter chamor*; Exodus 13); “as when one letteth out water” (Proverbs 17).
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi cites the word for its root; in Exodus 13:12 JPS reads “all that openeth the womb.” Printed “Proverbs 17” is Proverbs 17:14.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Let him commit himself unto the LORD
Psalms.english_translation: Like *lagolel*: a person must roll his burden and his load upon his Creator, so that He will rescue him.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: that took me out of the womb
Psalms.english_translation: My bringer-forth, my drawer, like “though the Jordan rush forth to his mouth” (Job 40).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “Job 40” is Job 40:23.

Psalms.english_translation: You prepared for man breasts to lean upon for sustenance.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Upon Thee I have been cast from my birth
Psalms.english_translation: I was cast from the womb — from when You brought me out of the womb — as in the matter that is said, “That are borne [by Me] from the birth” (Isaiah 46:3); from when the tribes were born, He bore them and led them.
Strong kingdoms.
It too is an expression of bulls in Bashan, which are fat.
They surrounded me like a crown (*keter*) that encircles the head.
Nebuchadnezzar.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: My heart is become like wax
Psalms.english_translation: Wax that melts from the heat of the fire.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: my tongue cleaveth to my throat
Psalms.english_translation: These are the gums (*chanikim*), which are called *palaiç* [printed פאליי"ש] in French (the palate). When a person is in distress there is no saliva found in his mouth. And Menachem explained *malkochai* as *אנטיילאש* in French, like “which he had taken with the tongs” (ibid. 6), and *malkoach* are the teeth, which are like the tongs of smiths. (סא"א)
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s lemma is *malkochai* (JPS: “my tongue”). Printed “ibid. 6” is Isaiah 6:6. Old French *palaiç* (the palate): read from Darmesteter (1909) at Psalms 22:16 (“Attaché à mon palais”) and his index; the printed form is close to the variant פלייש that he lists. The second Old French word, אנטיילאש, is not in Darmesteter and is left as printed. it is left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: To the crushings of death.
You will seat me, an expression of the setting of a pot, “Set on the pot” (Ezekiel 24); and Menachem explained every expression of *shefita* as an expression of placing.
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “Ezekiel 24” is Ezekiel 24:3.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Like a lion, they are at my hands and my feet
Psalms.english_translation: As if they were crushed in the mouth of a lion; and so Hezekiah said, “As a lion, so will he break all my bones” (Isaiah 38:13).
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s wording differs from JPS (Isaiah 38:13): “The more I make myself like unto a lion until morning, The more it breaketh all my bones.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I may count all my bones
Psalms.english_translation: The pain of my bones.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: They look and gloat over me
Psalms.english_translation: They rejoice at my calamity.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: for my vesture do they cast lots
Psalms.english_translation: They plunder my possessions.
My strength, like “I am become as a man that hath no help” (below, 88) and like “It is in the power of my hand” (Genesis 31:29).
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi cites *ayil* as meaning strength; JPS renders it “help” in Psalms 88:5. Printed “below, 88” is Psalms 88:5.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Save me from the lion’s mouth
Psalms.english_translation: As You answered me from the horns of the wild-oxen — this is the Amorite, “whose height was like the height of the cedars” (Amos 2:9) — thirty-one kings.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I will declare Thy name unto my brethren
Psalms.english_translation: When all my congregations are gathered; and so he says to them, “You that fear the LORD, praise Him” — these are the proselytes — “and all the seed of Jacob.”
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s quotation reads “and all the seed of Jacob”; JPS (Psalms 22:24) reads “All you the seed of Jacob, glorify Him.”

Psalms.english_translation: An expression of fear.

The cry of the poor; every *aniyah* in Scripture is an expression of crying out. And one can also interpret *anut* as an expression of submission, like “to humble thyself before Me” (Exodus 10), for he is submissive and prays before You.
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “Exodus 10” is Exodus 10:3.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Let the humble eat and be satisfied
Psalms.english_translation: At the time of the redemption, in the days of the Messiah.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: May your heart be quickened for ever
Psalms.english_translation: All this he says before them.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: shall remember and turn unto the LORD
Psalms.english_translation: The nations will remember the evil that befell us when they see the good, and will turn to HaShem.
For they will see that the kingship and the dominion return to You.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: All the fat ones of the earth shall eat and worship
Psalms.english_translation: This is a transposed verse: The humble shall eat all the fat ones of the earth, and shall bow to HaShem with praise and thanksgiving for the good. *Dishnei eretz* — the good, the fat of the land. All this the ends of the earth will see and will turn to HaShem.
Then all the dead of the wicked out of Gehinnom; and He will not have mercy on them to keep their souls alive from Gehinnom.
Psalms.translator_note: The syntax of the printed text is difficult; it is translated as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: Of each and every one.
*Lo chiyah* — will not live. Our Rabbis expounded from this verse that the dying, before their death, at the time of the taking of the soul, see the face of the Shechinah.
The seed of Israel, who serve Him always.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: told of the Lord unto the next generation
Psalms.english_translation: He transposed the verse and expounded it: It will be told to the last generation, about the name of HaShem and to praise Him, what He did for that seed.
The earlier ones, and they will declare His righteousness to the people that will be born, for He did righteousness for them.

Our Rabbis said: Wherever it is said *mizmor le-David*, he played, and afterward the Shechinah rested upon him — *mizmor* is to bring the holy spirit to David; and wherever it is said *le-David mizmor*, the Shechinah rested upon him and afterward he recited a song.
In this wilderness in which I am walking, I am confident that I shall lack nothing.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He maketh me to lie down in green pastures
Psalms.english_translation: In a dwelling of grass (*nveh deshe'in*), because he began to liken his sustenance to the pasturing of cattle, as he said, “The LORD is my shepherd”; it plays on the language of “The LORD is my shepherd” — *ne'ot deshe*. And this psalm David said in the forest of Hereth; why is it called the forest of Hereth? Because it was dried out like a potsherd (*cheres*), and the Holy One, blessed be He, moistened it from the goodness of the World to Come. (Midrash Tehillim)
Psalms.translator_note: The forest of Hereth is mentioned in 1 Samuel 22:5.

Psalms.english_translation: My spirit, which grew cold in troubles and flight, He will restore to its former state.
On level ways, that I not fall into the hand of my enemies.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: the valley of the shadow of death
Psalms.english_translation: In a land of darkness, and he said it concerning the wilderness of Ziph; every *tzalmavet* is an expression of darkness, as Dunash ben Labrat explained.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thy rod and Thy staff, they comfort me
Psalms.english_translation: The afflictions that came upon me, and the staff on which I rely upon Your kindness — both of them comfort me, for they will serve me to pardon iniquity; and I am confident that You will prepare a table before me, which is kingship.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou hast anointed my head with oil
Psalms.english_translation: I was already anointed king according to Your word.
An expression of satiety.
The Land of Israel.
The other lands.
Seven seas surround the Land of Israel, and four rivers: the Jordan, the Yarmuk, the Karmion, and the Pugah.
Psalms.translator_note: The river names are transliterated as printed (ירדן, ירמוך, קרמיון, פוגה).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Who shall ascend into the mountain of the LORD?
Psalms.english_translation: Although all the inhabitants of the world are His, not all are worthy to draw near to Him, but only “he that hath clean hands” etc.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Who hath not taken My name in vain
Psalms.english_translation: He did not swear by My name and by My soul in vain. The expression of an oath is found attached to “soul,” as it is said, “The LORD of hosts hath sworn by Himself” (Jeremiah 51:14).
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s lemma reads *nafshi* (“My soul”); JPS renders the word “My name.”

Psalms.english_translation: For such are his deeds; he is of the generation of those who seek Him.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Lift up your heads, O you gates
Psalms.english_translation: In the days of Solomon his son, when he came to bring the ark into the Holy of Holies and the gates clung one to another, he said twenty-four *rinnot* and was not answered until he said, “turn not away the face of Thine anointed; Remember the good deeds of David Thy servant” (2 Chronicles 6).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “2 Chronicles 6” is 2 Chronicles 6:42. *Rinnot* is left transliterated as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: Doors whose holiness is everlasting.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: do I lift up my soul
Psalms.english_translation: I will direct my heart.
The robbers, the violent, who leave the poor empty of their possessions, like “Or spoiled mine adversary unto emptiness” (above, 7).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “above, 7” is Psalms 7:5.

Psalms.english_translation: *אדריצימו"י* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: For Thee do I wait all the day
Psalms.english_translation: It is this world, which is day for the nations and night for Israel.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: For they have been from of old
Psalms.english_translation: From the days of the first man, to whom You said, “in the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die” (Genesis 2:17), and You gave him a day of Yours, which is a thousand years.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: According to Thy mercy remember Thou me
Psalms.english_translation: That which is fitting for Your mercy, remember for me — these are the good deeds that are in my hand.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Good and upright is the LORD
Psalms.english_translation: And He desires to justify His creatures.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: doth He instruct sinners in the way
Psalms.english_translation: Repentance. Another explanation: He instructs sinners — the murderers, as it is said, “Thou shalt prepare thee the way” etc. (Deuteronomy 19:3): “Refuge, refuge” was written at the crossroads, etc., as it is found in Makkot.
O Great One, pardon my iniquity.
For it is fitting for the Great One to pardon great iniquity.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: What man is he that feareth the LORD?
Psalms.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He, will instruct him in the way that he will choose — the way of good.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: His soul shall abide in prosperity
Psalms.english_translation: When he lodges in the grave, his soul will lodge in good.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: For I am solitary and afflicted
Psalms.english_translation: And the iniquity of the many hangs upon me, and against them I am alone; therefore turn to me and be gracious to me, for my prayer is needed for the salvation of all Israel.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: See mine affliction and my travail
Psalms.english_translation: And through them, forgive all my sins.
Unjustly.
They will guard me.

And in another place he says, “And enter not into judgment” etc. (below, 143). David said: When You judge the wicked, judge me, for compared with the wicked I am righteous; and when You judge the righteous, do not bring me into judgment.
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “below, 143” is Psalms 143:2 (JPS: “And enter not into judgment with Thy servant”).

Psalms.english_translation: Those who enter in secret to do their deeds in darkness.
I am not accustomed to come and enter into their assembly.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I will wash my hands in innocency
Psalms.english_translation: For there is no robbery in the commandments that I fulfill; a stolen *lulav* is invalid.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: That I may make the voice of thanksgiving to be heard
Psalms.english_translation: *Lishmo'a* — like *lehashmia* (“to cause to be heard”).
This is the Hallel that has in it the past, and has in it Gog, and has in it the days of the Messiah, and has in it the World to Come.
Every *zimah* in Scripture is an expression of thought; there is one for good and one for evil.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: My foot standeth in an even place
Psalms.english_translation: On a straight way.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Even then will I be confident
Psalms.english_translation: In what he said above, “The LORD is the stronghold of my life.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: to visit early in His temple
Psalms.english_translation: To appear there every single morning — so Dunash explained; and Menachem connected it with “He shall not inquire whether it be good or bad” (Leviticus 27:33), but Dunash explained it as an expression of morning.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: For He concealeth me in His pavilion
Psalms.english_translation: I am confident that He will conceal me in His Sanctuary. And it is taught in Seder Olam that this verse was said concerning Joash son of Ahaziah, whom Jehosheba his sister hid in the upper chamber of the Holy of Holies, as it is said, “And he was with her hid in the house of the LORD six years” (2 Kings 11:3).
Psalms.translator_note: The printed text says “his sister”; JPS (2 Kings 11:2) calls Jehosheba “sister of Ahaziah.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He lifteth me up upon a rock
Psalms.english_translation: He set my foot upon a rock.
Sacrifices over which a song is said.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: In Thy behalf my heart hath said
Psalms.english_translation: For Your sake, in Your mission, my heart says to me: All of you, Israel, seek My face, and I listen to it; “Thy face, LORD, will I seek.”
Psalms.translator_note: In the printed text the word לי (“to me”) is in parentheses.

Psalms.english_translation: Like “Behold, I am toward God even as thou art” (Job 33:6), meaning in his place; “Will you contend for God?” (ibid. 13), meaning in His place; so here too, “*lekha* said my heart” — in Your place my heart came to me to say so.
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi cites these verses for the sense “in place of”; JPS renders them as quoted. Printed “ibid. 13” is Job 13:8.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Put not Thy servant away in anger
Psalms.english_translation: Do not cause to incline, like “He bowed the heavens also” (above, 18).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “above, 18” is Psalms 18:10.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: For though my father and my mother have forsaken me
Psalms.english_translation: At the time of intercourse they intended their own pleasure; once their pleasure was finished, this one turns his face this way and that one turns her face that way.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The LORD will take me up
Psalms.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He, guards the drop and forms the embryo.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: unto the will of mine adversaries
Psalms.english_translation: To the desires of my enemies, that their desire be fulfilled upon me.
Speakers of evil, speech after speech, a snare. (סא"א)
Psalms.translator_note: it is left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: If I had not believed to look upon the goodness of the LORD
Psalms.english_translation: If I had not believed in the Holy One, blessed be He, those false witnesses would already have risen against me and consumed me. *Lulei* has a dot over it for a midrashic teaching, as our Rabbis expounded: I know that You give reward to the righteous in the World to Come, but I do not know whether I have a portion with them or not.
And if your prayer is not accepted, go back and hope.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Draw me not away with the wicked
Psalms.english_translation: Do not accustom me to be with the wicked — *אטרירא"ש מו"י* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: with my song will I praise Him
Psalms.english_translation: And what is the thanksgiving? “The LORD is a strength unto them,” to those who depend on Him, at the time when “He is a stronghold of salvation to His anointed.”
Psalms.translator_note: The second quotation is Psalms 28:8.

Psalms.english_translation: An expression of pasture.
Prepare for HaShem; and prepare for Him, you sons of the mighty ones of the earth; from here, that *Avot* is said; and Menachem connected *havu* with an expression of giving.
Psalms.translator_note: *Avot* (the first blessing of the Amidah) is left transliterated as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: Princes. (סא"א)
Psalms.translator_note: it is left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Ascribe unto the LORD glory and strength
Psalms.english_translation: From here, that *Gevurot* is said.
Psalms.translator_note: *Gevurot* (the second blessing of the Amidah) is left transliterated as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: the glory due unto His name
Psalms.english_translation: This is the sanctification of the Name, and there are eighteen mentions in this psalm, and corresponding to them they instituted eighteen blessings.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The voice of the LORD is upon the waters
Psalms.english_translation: Upon the Red Sea: “The LORD also thundered in the heavens” etc. (above, 18).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “above, 18” is Psalms 18:14.

Psalms.english_translation: *טורמינטאו"ש* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The voice of the LORD is powerful
Psalms.english_translation: At the giving of the Torah He restrained His voice according to the strength of Israel, as it is said, “and God answered him by a voice” (Exodus 19) — in the voice of Moses.
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “Exodus 19” is Exodus 19:19.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The voice of the LORD breaketh the cedars
Psalms.english_translation: The nations, as in the matter that is said, “But the LORD thundered with a great thunder on that day upon the Philistines” etc. (1 Samuel 7:10), “For through the voice of the LORD shall Asshur be dismayed” (Isaiah 30:31); and at the giving of the Torah, “For who is there of all flesh” etc. “and lived” (Deuteronomy 4): you heard and lived, while the nations of the world hear and die.
Psalms.translator_note: “For who is there of all flesh” is Deuteronomy 5:26; “thou hast heard, and live” echoes Deuteronomy 4:33.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He maketh them also to skip like a calf
Psalms.english_translation: The cedars and the mountains that came to hear the giving of the Torah.
Names of mountains.
*טיילנ"ט* in French; and our Rabbis explained that the utterance of the Ten Commandments came forth from His mouth in flames of fire and was engraved on the tablets in their form.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The voice of the LORD shaketh the wilderness
Psalms.english_translation: An expression of travail, “as of a woman in travail” (Jeremiah 6).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “Jeremiah 6” is Jeremiah 6:24.

Psalms.english_translation: It is the wilderness of Sinai, as our Rabbis said in tractate Shabbat: Five names were called to it: wilderness of Sinai, wilderness of Zin, wilderness of Kadesh, wilderness of Kedemot, wilderness of Paran; wilderness of Kadesh because Israel were sanctified upon it.

He will frighten, and cause to writhe in the future, the idolaters, who now stand strong like hinds, as it is said (above, 18), “Who maketh my feet like hinds’.” Rabbi Pinchas said: It does not say here “like the harts” but “like the hinds” — like females, for the feet of females stand more evenly than those of males. Another version: *yecholel* — *קריא"ה* in French, like “Before the hills was I brought forth” (Proverbs 8:25). (סא"א)
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. it is left as printed. Printed “above, 18” is Psalms 18:34.

Psalms.english_translation: Like “making the white appear” (Genesis 30:37) — He will peel the trees of the forest; that is, strip them of their glory, those who are likened to the trees of the forest, “whose height was like the height of the cedars.”
Psalms.translator_note: The last quotation is Amos 2:9. Rashi cites the word for its root; in Genesis 30:37 JPS reads “making the white appear.”

Psalms.english_translation: That will be built.
Everyone will praise Him there and will say.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The LORD sat enthroned at the flood
Psalms.english_translation: In His greatness alone, and also now, “and the LORD sits alone as King for ever,” “And the idols shall utterly pass away,” but to His people He will give strength and the blessing of peace. And our Rabbis expounded it of the giving of the Torah, when the nations were frightened and alarmed and came to Balaam and said to him: What is the sound of the tumult that we heard? Perhaps a flood is coming to the world? He said to them: He has already sworn that He will not bring a flood; rather, the sound of the tumult that you heard is the Holy One, blessed be He, giving the Torah to His people.
Psalms.translator_note: The first quotation was not identified; the second is Isaiah 2:18 (JPS: “And the idols shall utterly pass away”); “to His people He will give strength” is Rashi’s wording of Psalms 29:11 (JPS: “The LORD will give strength unto His people; The LORD will bless his people with peace”).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: a Song at the Dedication of the House
Psalms.english_translation: That the Levites would say at the dedication of the House in the days of Solomon.
You have lifted me up.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: And hast not suffered mine enemies to rejoice over me
Psalms.english_translation: Like *alai* (“over me”); for they were saying: David has no portion in the World to Come; and when they saw that for his sake the doors opened for the ark, then they knew that the Holy One, blessed be He, had pardoned him for that sin, and the faces of David’s enemies turned like the bottoms of pots.
It is the forgiveness of iniquity, like “and he will return and be healed” (Isaiah 6).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 6” is Isaiah 6:10 (JPS: “Lest they … return, and be healed”).

Psalms.english_translation: Like *mi-yeridati la-bor* — that I not go down to Gehinnom.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Sing praise unto the LORD, O you His godly ones
Psalms.english_translation: For what He did for me, for you are able to take refuge in Him, that He will do you good; and even if you are dwelling in distress, do not fear.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: For His anger is but for a moment
Psalms.english_translation: Short in His anger.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: His favour is for a life-time
Psalms.english_translation: And long life is in His being appeased and being conciliated.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Now I had said in my security
Psalms.english_translation: In my tranquility I was thinking: I shall never be moved; but the matter is not in my hands, but in the hands of the Holy One, blessed be He; by His will He established the mountains of my greatness to be strength; and as soon as He hid His face from me, I was immediately dismayed.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed words הררי את גדולתי are unusual; they are translated as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Unto Thee, O LORD, did I call
Psalms.english_translation: Continually, saying before You: “What profit is there in my blood” etc., and You heard my voice and turned my mourning into dancing for me.
*Patachta* — *אלאק"ש* in French, like “and he ungirded the camels” (Genesis 24); and ור"ד: the whole psalm concerns Mordecai and Esther and Haman, in Pesikta Zuta.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed abbreviation ור"ד is unresolved and is left as printed. The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: “Now I had said in my security” — said Haman; “Unto Thee, O LORD, did I call” — said Esther, etc., up to “be Thou my helper”; “Thou didst turn for me my mourning into dancing” — said Mordecai and all Israel.
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s lemma here is “Now I had said in my security” (Psalms 30:7); the comment is filed under Psalms 30:12, so a nearby phrase of this verse is used as the lemma.

Psalms.english_translation: *פלי"ישיץ* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: *מונאראש"מוי* in French, like “go, lead the people” (Exodus 32).
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. Printed “Exodus 32” is Exodus 32:34.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Into Thy hand I commit my spirit
Psalms.english_translation: *קומנ"דריה* in French; I commit my spirit always, because You redeemed me from trouble.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: Those who look for the salvation of ע"א.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed abbreviation ע"א is not resolved and is left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: *ליבראש"מווי* in French; and Menachem connected it with an expression of closing, and so every expression of *sagar*.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: It grew dim — an expression of *asheshit*: a person places a glass before his eyes to see something beyond the glass; that sight is not clear.
An expression of rot, as if moths had eaten them.
From all my adversaries; I was a reproach for reviling.
I am a great reproach, and a dread to my acquaintances *אמישקטיישנ"ץ* — they are frightened by my misfortunes.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I am like a useless vessel
Psalms.english_translation: One that is going to be lost. In every expression of loss, the language does not fall on the owner of the lost thing to say “he lost it”; rather, the lost thing is lost from him, as it is said, “that is lost from him” (Deuteronomy 22), “that which was lost you have not sought” (Ezekiel 34).
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s wording differs from JPS (Deuteronomy 22:3: “which he hath lost”; Ezekiel 34:4: “neither have you sought that which was lost”).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I have heard the whispering of many
Psalms.english_translation: The counsel of many; *dibbat* is an expression of *dover*, “Moving gently the lips of those that are asleep” (Song of Songs 7:10), and so every *dibbah* in Scripture; *פרלר"יץ* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 31:14 (“La parole de la foule”), in forms such as פרלדיץ and פרליץ; the printed form (פרלר"יץ) is a variant spelling.

Psalms.english_translation: Who frighten and terrify me.
When they take counsel together.
An expression of thought.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: My times are in Thy hand
Psalms.english_translation: The times that pass over me are by Your word and by Your decrees.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: O LORD, let me not be ashamed
Psalms.english_translation: After I have called upon You, it is not fitting that I be ashamed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: let them be put to silence in the nether-world
Psalms.english_translation: They will be silenced and become dumb unto death.
That say to Saul: Behold, David seeks your harm.

Deviation, a thing that is not, like “And he removed from thence” (Genesis 12); and Dunash explained it as an expression of a great and hard thing, like “*ateku* and also became mighty in power” (Job 21:7), “enduring riches” (Proverbs 8:18), and “for stately clothing” (Isaiah 23). (סא"א)
Psalms.translator_note: it is left as printed. Rashi cites *ateku* for its root; JPS renders Job 21:7 “Become old, yea, wax mighty in power.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Oh how abundant is Thy goodness
Psalms.english_translation: I know that in the World to Come there is good reward for those who fear You; but in any case, in this world, where the wicked surround them, I pray for them that You hide them in the covert of Your presence.
From companies of wicked people who bind themselves together to do evil to them.
At Keilah, when Saul said, “for he is shut in, by entering into a town that hath gates and bars” (1 Samuel 23:7).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: As for me, I said in my haste
Psalms.english_translation: When I left Keilah and came to the wilderness of Maon, and I was hurrying to go away from Saul, for he overtook me, and Saul and his men were encircling me and my men to seize them.
In my heart.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I am cut off from before Thine eyes
Psalms.english_translation: I am cut off — an expression of *garzen* (axe), which cuts the tree; because of its cutting it is called *garzen*. So Dunash explained; and Menachem connected it with *nigrashti* (“I was driven out”), and it has no parallel in the Torah. (סא"א)
Psalms.translator_note: it is left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: HaShem guards those who believe in His salvation and lean upon Him.

Measure for measure, exact, like an arrow upon the string (*yeter*) of the bow (סא"א); or one can interpret *al yeter* as rope against rope, line against line. Another version: *yeter* is an expression of pride, like “*yitrah asah*” (Isaiah 15:7). Its explanation: And He repays *al yeter* — in pride — those who act with pride. (סא"א)
Psalms.translator_note: it is left as printed. Rashi cites *yitrah asah*; JPS renders Isaiah 15:7 “the abundance they have gotten.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Be strong, and let your heart take courage
Psalms.english_translation: As you have seen what He did for me, to save me, for I hoped for Him.
The Sages said: Every psalm in which *maskil* is said, they said through an interpreter.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Happy is he whose transgression is forgiven
Psalms.english_translation: For the Holy One, blessed be He, bears transgression and covers his sins.
*אנפורדוני"ץ* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: in whose spirit there is no guile
Psalms.english_translation: Provided that there be no deceit in his spirit, having it in his mind to return to his vomit.
When I kept silent from confessing my transgressions before You.
From the abundance of my groanings and worries all day, for I worried because of the punishment.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: For day and night Thy hand was heavy upon me
Psalms.english_translation: The fear of Your hand and Your decrees was heavy upon me.

My moisture (*lichluchi*), and so “*leshad* of the oil” (Numbers 11:8) — the moisture of oil; so Dunash explained; and Menachem connected it with an expression of plundering, like “For the oppression of the poor” (above, 12), “the wicked who oppress me” (above, 17).
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s wording of Numbers 11:8 differs from JPS (“the taste of it was as the taste of a cake baked with oil”). Printed “above, 12” is Psalms 12:6; “above, 17” is Psalms 17:9.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: as in the droughts of summer
Psalms.english_translation: Until it dried up in the heat of the summer, because of the worry about the weight of Your hand, for I was worried about my sin, and therefore:

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I acknowledged my sin unto Thee
Psalms.english_translation: Continually, and it is the present tense, for I said: It is good that I confess my transgressions to HaShem; and now, when I confessed and said to Nathan the prophet, “I have sinned” (2 Samuel 12:13), You bore the iniquity of my sin, as in the matter that is said (ibid.), “The LORD also hath put away thy sin” etc.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: in a time when Thou mayest be found
Psalms.english_translation: When You are found, to accept his prayer; and what is it? “Surely, when the great waters overflow, they will not reach unto him” — that he not fall into the hand of the nations, who are like overflowing waters. And so it is found that David prayed for this and said, “let us fall now into the hand of the LORD; for His mercies are great; and let me not fall into the hand of man” (2 Samuel 24:14).
To hide in Your shadow from the fear of the enemy.
Like *tishmereni* (“You will guard me”).
A song of rescue.
It is the present tense: *sevavtani* — always; songs of deliverance, and thus You said to me
Psalms.translator_note: The printed comment ends at this point.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I will instruct thee and teach thee
Psalms.english_translation: The way to go.
I will hint to you with My eye a sign as to what to do; *e'etzah* is an expression of winking the eye, like “He shutteth his eyes (*otzem einav*) to devise froward things” (Proverbs 16:30).
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s quotation is the words “*otzem einav*” and “to devise”; JPS reads “He shutteth his eyes, it is to devise froward things.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Be you not as the horse, or as the mule
Psalms.english_translation: That does not distinguish between one who does it good and one who does it evil: when you put the bit on it, it shuts its mouth and chews its bridle; and when you groom it and scrape it, you have to restrain it and close its mouth and discipline it with bit and bridle, when you adorn it with its ornaments and make it beautiful.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed word מכסכס is rendered “chews” from the context.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: That they come not near unto thee
Psalms.english_translation: That it not come near you to harm you when you make it beautiful with bit and bridle, its ornaments, to restrain it. At the time of its adorning, when you groom it and scrape it, you have to close it with bit and bridle so that it not come near you. *Blimah* in the language of the Mishnah is an expression of closing: “its mouth is restrained, its legs are held” (tractate Bekhorot); and Menachem connected it with *livlom*, and so “over nothing (*al blimah*)” (Job 27) — an expression of *tochen*. (סא"א)
Psalms.translator_note: it is left as printed. Printed “Job 27” is Job 26:7 (JPS: “And hangeth the earth over nothing”). *Tochen* is left transliterated as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: Of ten kinds of melody.

An expression of height; and so Targum Onkelos for “stood upright as a heap” (Exodus 15:8): *kamu ke-shor* (“they stood like a wall”); and so Menachem explained; and *ned* and *no'd* are not the same.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He layeth up the deeps in storehouses
Psalms.english_translation: Beneath the earth.
He looked.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He that fashioneth the hearts of them all
Psalms.english_translation: The heart of all of them together, and He knows all the thoughts. And our Rabbis turned it back to “From the place of His habitation He looketh intently” — “He that fashioneth the hearts of them all,” and expounded from here that all of them are surveyed in one survey.

As in the matter that is said, “and scrabbled on the doors of the gate” etc. (1 Samuel 21): “And he changed his demeanour in their eyes” — that he changed his speech and his manner, and made himself a fool and let his spittle fall on his beard. (סא"א)
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s wording “in their eyes” differs from JPS (1 Samuel 21:14): “And he changed his demeanour before them.” it is left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: So all the kings of the Philistines are called, and all the kings of Egypt are Pharaoh; and although his name was Achish, he is called Abimelech. And a homiletical teaching: that he was righteous like Abimelech (who is written in the Torah with Sarah), since he did not want to kill him, and his men said to him (ibid.), “Is not this David the king of the land?” as is found in Midrash Tehillim.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: My soul shall glory in the LORD
Psalms.english_translation: I take pride and I glory that I have such a patron, to save and to protect.
*se porvantera* [printed שפורוונ"טרא] in French (he will boast).
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 34:3 (“S’enorgueillira”), in forms such as שפורוונטא; the reading is *se porvantera*, from Darmesteter’s footnote and index; the printed form (שפורוונ"טרא) is a variant spelling.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The humble shall hear thereof, and be glad
Psalms.english_translation: The wonders that He did for me; from my praising, they will understand them and rejoice.
An expression of fear, like “and Moab was sore afraid (*vayagor*)” (Numbers 22).
All those who looked to Him out of their distress.
Their faces shone.
They will be ashamed, like “Then the moon shall be confounded (*vachafrah*), and the sun ashamed” (Isaiah 24:23).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: O consider and see that the LORD is good
Psalms.english_translation: *Ta'amu* — His word.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed words טעמו דברו are translated as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: Let them be fearful — an expression of command.
An expression of poverty.
*ניסו"ן בי"ין* in French, like “any manner of work” (Exodus 12).
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. Printed “Exodus 12” is Exodus 12:16.

Psalms.english_translation: In your place.
In another place.
A face of wrath — *לישאריא"ש* in French, like “then I will set My face against that man” (Leviticus 2); so Menachem connected it.
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “Leviticus 2” is, for these words, Leviticus 20:5 (JPS: “then I will set My face against that man”). The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: The righteous, and HaShem heard.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Many are the ills of the righteous
Psalms.english_translation: Many evils and terrors come upon him, and from all of them he is delivered.
The Holy One, blessed be He, [keeps] all his bones.
It will kill the wicked — the evil that he does.
*Temotet* — will cause to die (*tamit*).
They will not regret, saying, “We are guilty,” that we took refuge in You — *ריפונטירונ"ט* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Strive, O LORD, with them that strive with me
Psalms.english_translation: Make a quarrel with those who make a quarrel with me.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Fight against them that fight against me
Psalms.english_translation: An expression of war; and so *lochamai*: wage war with those who wage war.
Arm Yourself, like “I will draw my sword” (Exodus 15:9), “and he led forth his trained men” (Genesis 14:14).
Shield between me and them like a partition.
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi explains the Hebrew *segor* as “shut/shield”; JPS renders it as part of “the battle-axe.”

Psalms.english_translation: *אימוימאימא"ש* in French, like “they have digged a pit for my soul” (Jeremiah 18:20).
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Let their way be dark and slippery
Psalms.english_translation: Both together, so that their feet slip on the slippery places, and the darkness does not let them be careful of the slippery places, as it is said (ibid. 23), “Wherefore their way shall be unto them as slippery places in the darkness, They shall be thrust, and fall therein.”
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “ibid. 23” is Jeremiah 23:12.

Psalms.english_translation: A pit to fall into.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Let destruction come upon him unawares
Psalms.english_translation: Darkness — *ברואינ"ה* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: his net that he hath hid
Psalms.english_translation: So is the way to hide the net, covering it with straw or with dust, so that the one who passes over it will not sense it until he is caught in it.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: And my soul shall be joyful in the LORD
Psalms.english_translation: When I see their downfall.
They will praise You for this, for now
Psalms.translator_note: The printed comment ends at this point.

Psalms.english_translation: Against me always, witnesses of violence, etc.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: may it return into mine own bosom
Psalms.english_translation: That is: and if they say, I did not afflict my soul except for their harm, that illnesses become heavy upon them — may my prayer that I prayed for them return upon me.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I went about as though it had been my friend or my brother
Psalms.english_translation: As if they were my brothers and my friends I walked, grieving for them over their trouble.
Whether like a son mourning for his mother or like a mother mourning for her son.
An expression of blackness.
An expression of lowliness.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: But when I halt they rejoice, and gather themselves together
Psalms.english_translation: And when I limp, for a fracture came upon me, they rejoiced and gathered.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The abjects gather themselves together against me
Psalms.english_translation: Lame people, as is translated *nakheh*: *chagira*; and Menachem connected it with *nekha'im* (Isaiah 16) — *אימנויישי"ץ* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi connects the word with *nekha'im*, which JPS renders “sorely stricken” in Isaiah 16:7. The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: They tear me, and cease not
Psalms.english_translation: If they were tearing my flesh, my blood would not trickle to the ground, since they make my face turn white.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: With the profanest mockeries of backbiting
Psalms.english_translation: For the sake of the flattery of scoffing, eating and drinking, with which they flatter Saul so that he will feed them and give them to drink, they gnash their teeth at me.
*Ma'og* — an expression of eating, like “if I have a *ma'og*” of Elijah (1 Kings 17:12); and Menachem explained it as an expression of a small cake (ibid.), and so “if I have a *ma'og*.”
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi cites the word *ma'og*; JPS renders 1 Kings 17:12 “I have not a cake.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Lord, how long wilt Thou look on?
Psalms.english_translation: How much patience You have, to see all these.
From their darkness.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Mine only one from the lions
Psalms.english_translation: It refers back to “rescue my soul”: rescue my soul, from the lions [rescue] my only one. (*Yechidati* — my soul. סא"א)
Psalms.translator_note: it is left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Let not them that are wrongfully mine enemies rejoice over me
Psalms.english_translation: Who hate me on account of a false matter, testifying against me about what never came into my mind — let them not rejoice at my downfall.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: that hate me without a cause
Psalms.english_translation: Who hate me — let them not wink at me with the eye, nor mock with their eyes at my downfall.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: let them wink with the eye
Psalms.english_translation: *צינאנ"ט* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: them that are quiet in the land
Psalms.english_translation: Over the crushed ones of the land; and so *roge'a ha-yam* (Jeremiah 31:35), *ori raga* (Job 7:5), and so Dunash explained.
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi cites these words for their root; JPS renders Jeremiah 31:35 “Who stirreth up the sea” and Job 7:5 “My skin closeth up.”

Psalms.english_translation: An expression of joy; he boasts in the desire of his heart, from the abundance of their joy at seeing their desire fulfilled.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Rouse Thee, and awake to my judgment
Psalms.english_translation: The heavenly *pamalia*, to judge my cases against my enemies.
Psalms.translator_note: *Pamalia* is left transliterated as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Transgression speaketh to the wicked, methinks
Psalms.english_translation: This is a transposed verse: There is within my heart that transgression, which is the evil inclination, says to the wicked that there should be no fear of God before his eyes.
And within my heart — like a person who says, “it seems to me.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: For it flattereth him in his eyes
Psalms.english_translation: The transgression flatters the wicked with smoothness in his eyes, so that the Holy One, blessed be He, will find his iniquity, to hate him.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He hath left off to be wise, to do good
Psalms.english_translation: He restrained himself from becoming wise, to make his deeds good.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He setteth himself in a way that is not good
Psalms.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He, put before him the way of good and the way of death, and he chooses for himself a way that is not good.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thy lovingkindness, O LORD, is in the heavens
Psalms.english_translation: Because of these wicked ones You remove kindness from the lower beings and raise Your faithfulness to the skies, to remove it from mankind.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thy righteousness is like the mighty mountains
Psalms.english_translation: It is precious (*yekarah*) among the creatures, like the mountains of God, because of the deeds of the wicked; and Your judgments come to the world as far as the great deep. Another explanation: “Your righteousness is like the mountains of God” — one with whom You wish to do righteousness, You raise up and strengthen like the mountains of God, an expression of strength, like “and the mighty of the land he took away” (Ezekiel 17:13).
Psalms.translator_note: The sense of the printed words יקרה מן הבריות is uncertain; a literal rendering is given.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thy judgments are like the great deep
Psalms.english_translation: One whom You wish to judge and from whom to take Your vengeance, You bring down to the great deep.
*יושטיצ"א* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Man and beast Thou preservest, O LORD
Psalms.english_translation: People who are shrewd in understanding, like the first man, and who make themselves like a beast in humility, You save, O LORD.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: How precious is Thy lovingkindness, O God!
Psalms.english_translation: It is not fitting that it be drawn out to these wicked ones; but the children of men who “take refuge in the shadow of Thy wings” — they shall be satisfied from the fatness of Your house, etc.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Let not the foot of pride overtake me
Psalms.english_translation: May the foot of these wicked ones not come with me at the time of receiving reward, to have their portion with the righteous. (An expression of portion — *אהלא פרט"יאה* in French. סא"א)
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. it is left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: the hand of the wicked drive me away
Psalms.english_translation: From my place, when I come to inherit a double portion, my portion and his (the wicked man’s) portion, in the good, as in the matter that is said, “Therefore in their land they shall possess double” (Isaiah 61:7); and then:
Psalms.translator_note: In the printed text the words “of the wicked” are in parentheses.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: There are the workers of iniquity fallen
Psalms.english_translation: There they will understand about their downfall, and there they were thrust down and could not rise.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Fret not thyself because of evil-doers
Psalms.english_translation: He rebukes Israel, that they not envy the success of evildoers by acting as their deeds, like “then how canst thou contend with horses” (Jeremiah 12), to run in their race; *האטיר* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 37:1 (“Ne rivalise pas”) as אאטיר; the printed form (האטיר) matches. Printed “Jeremiah 12” is Jeremiah 12:5.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Neither be thou envious against them that work unrighteousness
Psalms.english_translation: To do wrong like them.
*שרו"נט טראנקיי"ץ* in French, an expression of cutting.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: And do not say: If I do not rob and steal, or give charity to the poor, how will I be sustained?
And then you will dwell in the land for length of days.
You will eat and be sustained from the reward of the faith with which you had faith in the Holy One, blessed be He, to rely on Him and to do good.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: So shalt thou delight thyself in the LORD
Psalms.english_translation: Delight yourself with luxuries, upon the support of the Holy One, blessed be He.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Commit thy way unto the LORD
Psalms.english_translation: Roll upon Him all your needs.

Wait for His salvation, like “If they say thus unto us: Tarry (*dumu*)” of Jonathan (1 Samuel 14:9); and Menachem connected it with an expression of silence, like “And Aaron held his peace” (Leviticus 10:3), and he also explained “It is good that a man should quietly wait (*vechil udumam*)” (Lamentations 3:26); and Dunash agrees with him.
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s quotation of Lamentations 3:26 differs from JPS (“It is good that a man should quietly wait For the salvation of the LORD”).

Psalms.english_translation: An expression of hope.
To say: I will be wicked like him and I will succeed like him.
Desist from being wicked, lest anger come upon you.
A thing that brings upon you the wrath of the Holy One, blessed be He.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: For evil-doers shall be cut off
Psalms.english_translation: Those whom you see succeeding now shall be cut off.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: And yet a little while, and the wicked is no more
Psalms.english_translation: When you wait a little longer you will see that there is no wicked one.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: thou shalt look well at his place
Psalms.english_translation: And you will look at the place where he was, and he is not, for he died and perished.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: gnasheth at him with his teeth
Psalms.english_translation: Like “they gnash the teeth” (*charku shen*), *ארקי"נט* in French (Lamentations 14).
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. The printed reference “Lamentations 14” does not exist; the words *charku shen* occur in Lamentations 2:16 (JPS: “They hiss and gnash the teeth”).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The wicked have drawn out the sword
Psalms.english_translation: The wicked opened — *אנקומנצירנט* in French — the wicked begin strife and *cherem* by themselves.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. The meaning of חרום in the printed text is uncertain; it is left as *cherem*.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Better is a little that the righteous hath
Psalms.english_translation: Better are the few men who go to the aid of the righteous.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Than the abundance of many wicked
Psalms.english_translation: Amraphel and his companions, who began a war in the world in order to take Lot captive and to challenge Abraham; the few men who were with Abraham succeeded and killed all those multitudes.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The LORD knoweth the days of them that are wholehearted
Psalms.english_translation: He recognizes the deeds of their days.
And their receiving of reward from Him will be forever.
Like the light of a morning cloud that appears in the morning, whitening the expanses of a valley, which does not last; *karim* — level ground, like “large pastures” (*kar nirchav*; Isaiah 30).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 30” is Isaiah 30:23.

Psalms.english_translation: An expression of light, *or yekarot* (Zechariah 14:6); and some interpret *ki-yekar karim* as “like the glory of lambs,” which are fattened for slaughter.
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi cites the phrase *or yekarot*; JPS renders Zechariah 14:6 “there shall not be light, But heavy clouds and thick.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The wicked borroweth, and payeth not
Psalms.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He, who is the Righteous One of the world, graciously gives of His own to this one who lent, what the wicked robs from him.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: For such as are blessed of Him shall inherit the land
Psalms.english_translation: Those blessed of the Righteous One of the world shall inherit the land.
He who is mighty in the fear of the Holy One, blessed be He — *ליש פאש דופורט* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: *פורי"נט אפיטייץ* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: *לבורג"א* in French, an expression of “and she fell from the camel” (Genesis 24:64).
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s wording “and she fell” differs from JPS: “she alighted from the camel.” The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: Like *im* (“if”).
He will not be thrown down so as to be abandoned.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I have been young, and now am old
Psalms.english_translation: This verse — the Prince of the World said it, for David was not that old.
The righteous one graciously gives to the poor and lends to them.
One who sows for charity — his end is blessing.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The mouth of the righteous uttereth wisdom
Psalms.english_translation: First, in his heart, wisdom, to see the law that the Torah ruled in every matter; and afterward, his tongue speaks judgment.
His steps will not slip.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: spreading himself like a leafy tree
