Psalms.english_translation: Taking root, like “*arot* by the Nile” (Isaiah 19:7); and in the language of the Mishnah: There is many a tree that is split and is *me'urah* in the bark.
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi cites the word *arot*; JPS renders Isaiah 19:7 “The mosses by the Nile.”

Psalms.english_translation: Like one of the natives of the land, who are rooted and filled with possessions; and so Menachem explained: *ezrach ra'anan*, moistened and sprouting like the tamarisk that takes root; and *ezrach* — “from the natives of mankind (*ezrachei bnei adam*)”: they are men of roots. (סא"א)
Psalms.translator_note: it is left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: Look at the ways of the wholehearted, to learn from their deeds.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: there is a future for the man of peace
Psalms.english_translation: If there is no beginning for him, he has an end; but transgressors and sinners and wicked ones, their end is cut off and they are destroyed together.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed words אם ראשית אין לו אחרית יש לו are translated literally; their sense is not clear.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: A Psalm of David, to make memorial
Psalms.english_translation: To say it at a time of distress, to recall the distress of Israel before the Holy One, blessed be He; and they said it corresponding to all of Israel.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thine arrows are gone deep into me
Psalms.english_translation: *Nachatu* — they were thrown. The root *nachat* falls on the bending of a bow, and because the arrows are thrown through the bending of the bow, it is written, “Thine arrows *nachatu* in me”; and so (Exodus 15:9), *arik charbi* — he should have written *arik ta'ari* (“I will empty my sheath”), but since when a sword is taken out the sheath (*ta'ar*) is left empty of it, he attributes the emptiness to the sword. And so (above, 18) “and a bow of brass was bent (*venichata*)”; and the nun is not a root letter in the word, for if it were a root, he would have had to say *nanchatu bi*; but the nun of *nachatu* and that of *vatinchat* is not a root letter and falls away at times, like the nun of *nagaf*, *nashach*, *nadar*, *nakam*: when it is reflexive it says *nigaf*, *nishach*, *nidar*, *nikam*, like *ninnagaf*, *ninnashach*, *ninnadar*, *ninnakam*, because the dagesh comes into the word in place of the nun; and so “*alah nidaf*” (Leviticus 27), “mine eye *niggerah*” (Lamentations 3:49), like *ninnadaf*, *ninnagerah*; so it says *nachatu* like *nenchatu*, and so *venichata keshet nechushah* (2 Samuel 25) like *venenchatah*; for the way of the chet is to behave like a letter with a dagesh in most places, such as *kichash lo*, and from the paradigm with a dagesh, like *diber* from *vayedaber*, so *kichesh* from *vatekhachesh Sarah* (Genesis 18:15), and it does not say *kiyach*, as it says *berech* from the one who blesses and not *birech*, as it says *diber*, because a dagesh is not recognizable on the resh, but on the chet a dagesh is recognizable; and so (Deuteronomy 32) *shayshat*, like *kiper*, *diber*; here too it says *nachatu* like *nigshu*, *nitnu*, from the roots *nachat*, *natan*, *nagash*, and the root nun falls away to admit a dagesh in its place when it is reflexive; and so (1 Samuel 2:4) *keshet gibborim chittim*, from the root *nachat* and *chatat*, as is said from *nasav* *sabav*, from *nasham* *shamam*, “and your ways shall be desolate (*venashmu*)” (Leviticus 26) and “and they shall be astonished (*veshamemu*) at it” (ibid.); and so *balal*, *naval*: “for there the LORD confounded (*balal*)” and “and there confound (*venavlah sham*) their language” (Genesis 11:7). So it says *nachat* and *chatat* in the active.
Psalms.translator_note: This is a technical grammatical discussion; the Hebrew grammatical forms are left transliterated. The printed references do not all match the verses: “Leviticus 27” for *alah nidaf* is Leviticus 26:36 (JPS: “the sound of a driven leaf”); “2 Samuel 25” is 2 Samuel 22:35; “Leviticus 26” for *venashmu* is Leviticus 26:22 (printed ונשמו דרכיהם) and “ibid.” for *veshamemu* is Leviticus 26:32 (JPS: “shall be astonished at it”). The reference “(Deuteronomy 32)” and the word שיחת could not be identified in Deuteronomy 32 and are left as printed; the quotation “the bows of the mighty men are broken” is 1 Samuel 2:4. “Above, 18” is Psalms 18:35.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thy hand is come down upon me
Psalms.english_translation: He explained: “Thine arrows *nachatu* in me”; and so its meaning: What is the way with a bow, to shoot arrows? Your hand is it that came down with the bow, to cast arrows upon me; *vatinchat* is an expression of “and You came down,” and in this word the nun is a root letter; and so (above, 18) “*venichata* a bow of brass,” the nun is not a root letter in the word. (סא"א)
Psalms.translator_note: it is left as printed. Printed “above, 18” is Psalms 18:35.

Psalms.english_translation: Wholeness — *אינטרי"ן* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 38:4 (“Sain, entier”), in forms such as אינטרין; the printed form (אינטרי"ן) matches.

Psalms.english_translation: Heavy ones.
An expression of “convulsion seized him” (*ivvut*) — *אישטורדיש"ון* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 38:7 (“J’ai été saisi de trouble”), in forms such as אישטורדישון; the printed form (אישטורדיש"ון) matches.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: my loins are filled with burning
Psalms.english_translation: In my thought I am light in my own eyes.
I was changed — an expression of “and his heart fainted (*vayafag*)” (Genesis 45), “without any intermission (*hafugot*)” (Lamentations 2).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 45” is Genesis 45:26; printed “Lamentations 2” is Lamentations 3:49.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: all my desire is before Thee
Psalms.english_translation: You know my needs.
Surrounded by grief; and this is of the doubled words, like *yerakrak*, *adamdam* (Leviticus 13), *sagalgal*, *chamarmeru* (Lamentations 1).
Psalms.translator_note: Words cited for their form are left transliterated; JPS renders Leviticus 13:49 “greenish or reddish” and Lamentations 1:20 “Mine inwards burn.”

Psalms.english_translation: They appeared to me as friends at the time of their benefit, and when they see that the plague has come upon me, they do not stand by me at the time of my distress, but “stand aloof”; and they do not help me.
Who show themselves to me as close.
Snares for me.
They will think.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: But I am as a deaf man, I hear not
Psalms.english_translation: Israel hear their reproach from those who reproach, and do not answer; and why? For in You I have hoped, that You will redeem me and save me from them.
Psalms.translator_note: The quotation “For in Thee, O LORD, do I hope” is from Psalms 38:16.

Psalms.english_translation: For this reason we are silent, for we say in our heart: If we answer them insolently, perhaps they will see our downfall and rejoice over us when our feet slip, and will magnify themselves over us, saying: Were you not boasting of your salvation?

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: For I am ready to halt
Psalms.english_translation: For this reason we worry, lest they rejoice over us, since we are accustomed to blows and are prepared and ready to be broken always.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: my pain is continually before me
Psalms.english_translation: It is ready to come upon me always.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: For I do declare mine iniquity
Psalms.english_translation: My heart tells me my iniquity, and therefore I worry and fear lest my sin cause me a limp and pain.
They strengthen life in peace and in goodness.
And they magnified their hatred of me over false things.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: because I follow the thing that is good
Psalms.english_translation: Because we cling to the Holy One, blessed be He, and to His commandments.

The name of one of the singers; and there was also a musical instrument whose name was Jeduthun; and a homiletical teaching: concerning the laws (*datot*), the judgments, and the decrees of distress that is decreed upon Israel.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I will take heed to my ways
Psalms.english_translation: We had it in our heart to guard ourselves through all the troubles that come upon us, so that we would not brood and speak harshly against the attribute of judgment, even though the wicked who oppress us are before us.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I will keep a curb upon my mouth
Psalms.english_translation: Like “Thou shalt not muzzle the ox” (Deuteronomy 25) — *אמושלמנ"ט* in French; “I was dumb with silence” for many days, and we also held our peace from good, even from words of Torah, out of fear; and because of this our pain was stirred and troubled, and when we kept silent our heart waxed hot within us, and in the musing of our heart a fire burns in us, and this causes us to speak with our tongue (in a whisper — סא"א) before You, and this is what we speak: “Lord, make me to know mine end” — until when will we be in trouble, and that we may know when we shall cease from it.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. it is left as printed. Rashi’s quotations here are from Psalms 39:3–4 and 39:5. Printed “Deuteronomy 25” is Deuteronomy 25:4.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou hast made my days as hand-breadths
Psalms.english_translation: The days of man are measured, like a thing measured in handbreadths; so the days of man are fixed. “And mine age” — “and our old age is as nothing before You.” *Cheled* is an expression of rust (*chaludah*) — *רדוייל* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 39:6 (“Ma vieillesse, littéral.: ma rouille”), in forms such as רודייל and רדולייא; the printed form (רדוייל) is a variant spelling.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: every man at his best estate
Psalms.english_translation: Every living man — his life and his standing is vanity.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: man walketh as a mere semblance
Psalms.english_translation: In darkness; Dunash explained it as an expression of *tzalmavet*; and Menachem explained *tzelem* literally, like “for in the image of God made He man” (Genesis 9), but his words are not tenable.
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 9” is Genesis 9:6.

Psalms.english_translation: It is all their tumult and desire.
[He heaps up] grain in the field all the days of the harvest.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: and knoweth not who shall gather them
Psalms.english_translation: He does not know who will gather them into the house; perhaps before the gathering he will die.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: And now, Lord, what wait I for?
Psalms.english_translation: What is the request that I ask and hope for from You? It is nothing but that You save me from my transgressions.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Make me not the reproach of the base
Psalms.english_translation: Do not make me the reproach of the base one; let plagues and pains come also upon him, so that he cannot say to me: You are stricken, and we are not stricken. And this prayer caused diseases of afflictions to come upon them.
That You brought trouble upon us.

From the fear of Your blows. *Tigrat* is an expression of “and Moab was sore afraid (*vayagor*)” (Numbers 22), and the tav is a root letter that falls away from the word, like *tenuvah*, *telunah*, *tekumah*, *tachanah* — so Menachem explained. But I say that *tigrat* is not of the expression of *magor*, for he would have had to say *tegurah*, as is said from *vayashav*, *teshuvah*; *vayakom*, *vayarom*, *vayalen*, *tekumah*, *terumah*, *telunah*; so from *vayagor* he would say *tegurah* or *megurah*, like *magor missaviv* (Jeremiah 20), “I will bring their fears upon them” (Isaiah 66). From this you learn that *tigrat* is nothing but like “why shouldest thou meddle with evil” (2 Chronicles 25), “contend not with them” (Deuteronomy 2), whose verb is *garah*, like *kavah*, *avah*, *tzivah*, whose nouns are *tikvah*, *ta'avah*, *mitzvah*; so it says *tigrat* from *garah*. And so its explanation: From the blow of Your hand with which You provoke against me, I am consumed.
Psalms.translator_note: Grammatical forms are left transliterated. Printed “Numbers 22” is Numbers 22:3; “Jeremiah 20” is 20:3; “Isaiah 66” is 66:4; “2 Chronicles 25” is 25:19; “Deuteronomy 2” is 2:5.

Psalms.english_translation: Written in the Torah, for our iniquities that we committed before You, and You chastened us with them.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: like a moth Thou makest his beauty to consume away
Psalms.english_translation: The rotting of our flesh, like a garment eaten by a moth.
His flesh, which is his desire.
Hold back Your hand from smiting me.
And I may strengthen myself.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I waited patiently for the LORD
Psalms.english_translation: In Egypt; and this psalm too is said corresponding to all Israel.
His ear.
From the prisons of Egypt, and from the tumult of the roaring of the sea.
From the sea; *hayavan* is an expression of mud — *פיינ"ש* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 40:3 (“D’une mer de fange”), in forms such as פנייש and פאוייש; the printed form (פיינ"ש) is a variant spelling.

Psalms.english_translation: He prepared my steps and my goings.
The Song at the Sea.
An expression of coarseness (arrogance), like “The child shall behave insolently (*yirhavu*)” (Isaiah 3:5), “for they have overcome me” (Song of Songs 7).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “Song of Songs 7” is Song of Songs 6:5.

Psalms.english_translation: They turn aside from the straight way after falsehood; *shatei* — *איטורנ"אנץ* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thy wonderful works, and Thy thoughts toward us
Psalms.english_translation: For our sake You created Your world; You split the sea for us; and You planned from afar to do us good; You delayed us in the wilderness forty years because of the Amorites, who cut down the trees and destroyed the land when they heard that Israel were going out to inherit their land.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: There is none to be compared unto Thee!
Psalms.english_translation: No ruler or savior can be likened to You; an expression of *erekh*, like “thy valuation” (Leviticus 27) — *אהפרישי"יר* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. Printed “Leviticus 27” is Leviticus 27:3.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: If I would declare and speak of them
Psalms.english_translation: If I come to declare and to speak, they have grown mighty (*atzmu*) beyond number.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed words עצמו מספר are rendered literally.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Sacrifice and meal-offering Thou hast no delight in
Psalms.english_translation: On the day of the giving of the Torah, as in the matter that is said, “And now if you will hearken to the voice of the LORD” etc. (Exodus 19:5), and so (Jeremiah 7:22) He says, “For I spoke not unto your fathers, nor commanded them” etc. “concerning burnt-offering or sacrifice”: “if any man of you bring” I said, and I did not impose an obligation to burden them; the daily offerings and the additional offerings are only a satisfaction that I said and My will was done, and a small thing. (סא"א)
Psalms.translator_note: it is left as printed. Rashi’s wording of Exodus 19:5 differs from JPS (“if you will hearken unto My voice indeed, and keep My covenant”).

Psalms.english_translation: To say: Hearken to My voice.
You made them hollow, to hear.

At the time of the giving of the Torah I said before You: Behold, I have come to You with the tradition of Your covenant (Exodus 24:7) — “we will do and obey”; this thing is written as testimony about me in the roll of the book, in the Torah of Moses.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Yea, Thy law is in my inmost parts
Psalms.english_translation: Even my food is according to Your Torah.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I have preached righteousness in the great congregation
Psalms.english_translation: The Song at the Sea and the Song at the Well, the Song of Deborah.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I did not refrain my lips
Psalms.english_translation: I will not withhold — an expression of “and the rain was restrained” (Genesis 8).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 8” is Genesis 8:2.

Psalms.english_translation: You will not withhold.
They will guard me.
They surrounded.
To finish it, as it is translated “until all the generation were consumed” (Deuteronomy 2): *ad dasaf kol dara*.
They will be astonished.

When they receive their shame in return for everything, in the measure that they measured and in the way they walked toward me; *al ekev* (below, 77) — “and Thy footsteps (*ve'ikvotekha*) were not known” (Song of Songs 1) — “go thy way forth by the footsteps (*ikvei*) of the flock” — all of them are an expression of the tread of the foot; they are *traces* [printed טרצי"ש] in French; *al ekev* — *en ces traces* [printed אנ"ציש טרצ"יש].
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 40:16 (“En ces traces”), in forms such as טרציש and אינשישטריצים; the readings are *traces* and *en ces traces* (his heading and the REJ transcription *Énsést races*); the printed forms are variant spellings. “Below, 77” is Psalms 77:20 (JPS: “And Thy footsteps were not known”); “go thy way forth by the footsteps of the flock” is Song of Songs 1:8 (printed “Song of Songs 1”).

Psalms.english_translation: Those who say about me, on my account, “Aha”; when trouble comes they boast of my calamity. Every “poor and needy” in Psalms refers only to Israel.
He will put into my heart to consider my poverty and my neediness, to save me.
*פנישוי"יט* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: A sick man, to visit him, as in the matter that is said, “Why art thou thus becoming leaner (*dal*)” of Amnon (2 Samuel 13).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “1 Samuel 13” is 2 Samuel 13:4.

Psalms.english_translation: This is Gehinnom; and in this world, what is his reward?

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The LORD preserve him, and keep him alive
Psalms.english_translation: For the one who visits him and does good to him.

*Eres* — *לי"ט* in French (Deuteronomy 3): “behold, his bedstead (*arsho*) was a bedstead (*eres*) of iron”; when he too falls ill, He will support him. What is “the bed of illness”? This is the seventh day of illness, which is very sick; so it is expounded in Aggadat Tehillim.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. Printed “Deuteronomy 3” is Deuteronomy 3:11.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Mayest Thou turn all his lying down in his sickness
Psalms.english_translation: Even at the time when his illness is heavy upon him, all his repose and rest is turned.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: As for me, I said: ‘O LORD, be gracious unto me
Psalms.english_translation: I have no one who visits for good; and when I cry out from my illness and say, “O LORD, be gracious unto me” etc., my enemies rejoice over me and say evil things about me: “When shall he die” etc.
He shows himself as if he is distressed; and when he sits before me, his heart gathers thoughts of iniquity to itself — what evil to speak when he goes out; and when he goes outside, he speaks it.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Against me do they devise my hurt
Psalms.english_translation: A thing that is evil for me; and what is the thought?

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: An evil thing cleaveth fast unto him
Psalms.english_translation: All the wickedness that he did shall be poured out and spilled into his body; and since he lies, he shall rise up no more — so they curse me.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Hath lifted up his heel against me
Psalms.english_translation: An ambush, as in “and his ambush (*akvo*) on the west of the city” (Joshua 8:13).
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi reads *akev* as “ambush”; JPS (Joshua 8:13) reads “their rear lying in wait on the west of the city.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: By this I know that Thou delightest in me
Psalms.english_translation: When You show me grace and establish me, I will know that You delight in me, when my enemy will not shout a shout of joy over me, and I will see that You have supported me in my integrity.
When I rise from my illness I will bless You thus.

Assir and Elkanah and Abiasaph — they were at first with the counsel of their father, and at the time of the dispute they separated; and when all around them were swallowed up and the earth opened its mouth, their place remained inside the mouth of the earth, as it is said, “But the sons of Korah died not,” and there they said song and there they composed these psalms and rose from there; and the holy spirit rested upon them and they prophesied about the exiles and about the destruction of the House and about the kingdom of the House of David.
Psalms.translator_note: The quotation is from Numbers 26:11 (JPS: “Notwithstanding the sons of Korah died not”); Rashi’s wording differs slightly.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: As the hart panteth after the water brooks
Psalms.english_translation: The expression *arag* falls upon the voice of the hart, as the expression *nahem* falls upon the lion, *shakok* upon the bear, *ge'iyah* upon oxen, and *tzaftzuf* upon birds. Our Rabbis said: This hind is the most pious of the animals, and when the animals are thirsty for water they gather to her, that she may lift her eyes on high; and what does she do? She digs a hole and puts her horns into it and lows, and the Holy One, blessed be He, has mercy on her, and the deep brings up water for her.
Psalms.translator_note: Hebrew expressions are left transliterated.

Psalms.english_translation: It does not say *ke-ayelet ta'arog* (“as a hind she pants”), and it does not say *ke-ayil ya'arog* (“as a hart he pants”), but *ke-ayil ta'arog*: the verse speaks of both male and female. The male pants over the pursuit of water, as explained; the female, when she kneels to give birth and is crying out, the Holy One, blessed be He, has mercy on her. And Menachem connected *ta'arog* with “His cheeks are as a bed (*aruggat*) of spices” (Song of Songs 5:13), but his words are not tenable; and Dunash also explained it as an expression of the voice of a hart. (סא"א)
Psalms.translator_note: it is left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: When shall I come and appear before God?
Psalms.english_translation: To go up on the pilgrimage festival; and here the destruction of the House was prophesied, and “Why art thou cast down” is said here three times, corresponding to the three kingdoms that are destined to nullify the Temple service, and Israel cry out and are redeemed: the kingdom of Babylon, Greece and Edom.
The Community of Israel says so in the exile of Babylon.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: My tears have been my food day and night
Psalms.english_translation: From here, that trouble satiates a person and he does not seek to eat; and so it says of Hannah, “therefore she wept, and would not eat” (1 Samuel 1:7).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: How I passed on with the throng
Psalms.english_translation: *פשוויי"אה* in French. I remember this: and my soul is poured out when I remember the going up for the pilgrimage festivals, when I would pass among the troops of people and walk slowly with them to the house of God. *Sach* — an expression of a count, the sum of people. Another explanation: *sach* is an expression of *sakhakh* and *sukkah*, that is, in covered wagons, which were roofed like a sukkah, and in the language of the Aggadah they are called *sekafastot* and *askopiti*.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. The Greek-looking terms *sekafastot* and *askopiti* are left transliterated as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: *Eddem* — I walk slowly with them, like *medaddim* calves and foals, and a woman *meddah* her son; and this word serves as two words: I walk slowly with them, *אטוויי"אמוץ שנבל"א* in French. And Menachem connected it with an expression of friendship, like “I have given the beloved (*yedidut*) of my soul into the hand of her enemies” (Jeremiah 12:7); and Dunash explained *eddem* as an expression of silence, and so “Resign thyself (*dom*) unto the LORD, and wait patiently for Him” (Psalms 37:7); and the explanation of *eddem* is: I will be mute and keep silent until I come to the house of God with a ringing cry, like “I will keep a curb upon my mouth, While the wicked is before me” (Psalms 39:2), and like “But I am as a deaf man, I hear not; And as a dumb man that openeth not his mouth” (Psalms 38:14); and *dam* is the root in the word.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. Rashi’s *yedidut nafshi* differs from the Hebrew of Jeremiah 12:7 (*yedidut*), which JPS renders “the early beloved of My soul.” The words *medaddim* and *meddah* are left transliterated.

Psalms.english_translation: *Eddem* — I walk slowly with them, like “and could not speak peaceably unto him” (Genesis 37): speak with him in peace.
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 37” is Genesis 37:4.

Psalms.english_translation: For they went to celebrate the festival; and for this reason the liturgical poet composed (in the morning prayer of the portion Shekalim, in the *yotzer* of *Eleh Ezkerah*, ע"ש), “the might of the multitude keeping festival, and overflowing like a river”; and מ"א an expression of Greek, for they call a pool of water *chogegin*.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed abbreviations ע"ש and מ"א are unresolved and are left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: An expression of “for our soul is bowed down (*shachah*) to the dust” (below, 44); and *shach*, when it speaks of the reflexive, the tav divides the root letters of the word, as is the way of every word whose root begins with shin.
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “below, 44” is Psalms 44:26.

Psalms.english_translation: Wait and look for the redemption.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Therefore do I remember Thee from the land of Jordan
Psalms.english_translation: From what You did for us at the Jordan; and the Hermons: after all the anger with which we angered You in Shittim, You dried up the Jordan for us.

From Mount Sinai, which is smaller (*tze'ir*) than the other mountains; after we angered You at it with the deed of the calf, You forgave our iniquities and went with us. All these I remember, that You withheld from doing me good, and Your decrees are renewed upon me one after another.
One trouble calls to its fellow.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: at the voice of Thy cataracts
Psalms.english_translation: *טישקנאל"ש* in French, that pour punishment upon me like overflowing waters, until “all Thy waves and Thy billows are gone over me.” *Mishbarekha* — an expression of the waves of the sea, because its waves rise up on high and break and fall.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: By day the LORD will command His lovingkindness
Psalms.english_translation: The light will come, and HaShem will command His kindness to us.
In the darkness of the trouble.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: His song shall be with me
Psalms.english_translation: May His encampment be among us. *Shirah* — an expression of encampment (*chaniyah*), as it is translated, *vayichan* — *ve-shara*. This I learned from the Masorah Gedolah, which connected this with “and his songs (*shiro*) were a thousand and five” (1 Kings 4), in the alphabetical list of two words that are divided in their meaning, teaching that this is not an expression of song. And the Midrash Aggadah explains it as an expression of song, and this is how it explains it: For thus Israel say to the Holy One, blessed be He: Remember what You did for us in Egypt — one commandment that You commanded us on the day of the eve of Passover, and we kept it, and at night You redeemed us and we sang before You the Hallel; and now I keep many commandments, and for this I say to God my Rock, “Why hast Thou forgotten me?” etc.
Psalms.translator_note: The Aramaic is translated as printed. The printed words באלפ"א בית"א של שתי תיבות are translated literally; their sense is not clear. Printed “1 Kings 4” is 1 Kings 5:12 (JPS: “and his songs were a thousand and five”).

Psalms.english_translation: An expression of blackness, like “and the day shall be black over them” (Micah 3).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “Micah 3” is Micah 3:6 (JPS: “And the day shall be black over them”).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: As with a crushing in my bones
Psalms.english_translation: It seems to me as though they were killing me; thus it is shut up in my bones, what my adversaries do to anger and revile me.
The Holy One, blessed be He, who is the light of my face and my God — I still have hope in Him; and why should you moan?

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Be Thou my judge, O God
Psalms.english_translation: Set me up.
He is Edom, who dwelt between two righteous ones and did not learn from their deeds.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: O send out Thy light and Thy truth
Psalms.english_translation: King Messiah, who is likened to light, as it is said (below, 132), “I have ordered a lamp for Mine anointed”; and Elijah the prophet, who is a true prophet, faithful.
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “below, 132” is Psalms 132:17.

Psalms.english_translation: *מינטרו"נט מו"י* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: [To] God — the Holy One, blessed be He, who is the joy of my gladness.
Because You took me out.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: we have heard with our ears
Psalms.english_translation: From here you learn that the sons of Korah were speaking on behalf of these later generations that came after them; for if it were for themselves, they would not have had to say “our fathers have told us,” since they themselves saw the miracles of the wilderness and the sea and the Jordan and the wars of Joshua; so it is explained in Aggadat Tehillim.
You broke the seven great nations and sent them away from before us; and You, by Your hand, Your might, dispossessed them from their land and planted our fathers in it.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Because Thou wast favourable unto them
Psalms.english_translation: An expression of favor.
Also for those who come after us.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: do we push down our adversaries
Psalms.english_translation: Our enemies will be trampled and trodden; an expression of “wallowing (*mitbosesset*) in thy blood” (Ezekiel 16:6), “*tavus* a honeycomb” (Proverbs 27:7), and “treading down (*bosim*) in the mire of the streets” (Zechariah 10:5).
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi cites the words for their root; JPS renders Proverbs 27:7 “The full soul loatheth a honeycomb.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Yet Thou hast cast off, and brought us to confusion
Psalms.english_translation: Even if You shame us, we will acknowledge Your name forever.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou makest us to turn back from the adversary
Psalms.english_translation: It is the present tense.
They plundered our possessions, each man for himself.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: hast scattered us among the nations
Psalms.english_translation: *אפנדישנו"ש* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Though Thou hast crushed us into a place of jackals
Psalms.english_translation: *Ki* here serves in the sense of “when”: even when You humbled us in a desert land and a pit, a wilderness, a place of jackals, and covered us with the shadow of death, darkness — even in all this, if we forgot the name of our God, He will search this out, for He knows secrets, etc.
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi paraphrases Psalms 44:21–22; JPS reads “If we have forgotten the name of our God … Shall not God search this out? For He knoweth the secrets of the heart.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: We are accounted as sheep for the slaughter
Psalms.english_translation: Like sheep of a slaughterer.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: redeem us for Thy mercy’s sake
Psalms.english_translation: We do not come by the power of our deeds, but act for Your mercy’s sake.
They composed this song in honor of Torah scholars, who are soft as lilies, beautiful as lilies, and moistened with good deeds like lilies.
Through an interpreter.
A song of lovers — a song of praise for them, to make them beloved to the creatures and to make their Torah beloved to them.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: My heart overfloweth with a goodly matter
Psalms.english_translation: So the psalmist began his song: My heart swarmed within me with a good matter, in praising the Torah scholars.
An expression of stirring, and so every expression of *sheretz* and *richush* (swarming).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: My work is concerning a king
Psalms.english_translation: This song that I composed and made, I say to the king, as it is said, “By me kings reign” (Proverbs 8:15).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: My tongue is the pen of a ready writer
Psalms.english_translation: Clear in songs, like the pen of a ready scribe; I saw in the foundation of Rabbi Moses the Preacher: *mahir* — proficient in the Arabic language.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou art fairer than the children of men
Psalms.english_translation: [More than] those who occupy themselves with the work of temporal life. Why? Because grace is poured upon your lips, to teach the law; *hutzak* is like *nishpakh* (“poured out”), like *mutzakot* (Zechariah 4), “and he shall pour oil upon it” (Leviticus 2:1).
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi cites *mutzakot* for its root; JPS renders Zechariah 4:2 “seven pipes.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Therefore God hath blessed thee for ever
Psalms.english_translation: As it is said, “The LORD will give strength unto His people,” and what is their reward? “The LORD will bless his people with peace” (above, 29).
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s first quotation reverses the order of the words of Psalms 29:11. Printed “above, 29” is Psalms 29:11.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Gird thy sword upon thy thigh
Psalms.english_translation: To fight the war of Torah; and it is your glory and your majesty.
To teach as the law, and to conduct oneself with meekness of righteousness.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: let thy right hand teach thee tremendous things
Psalms.english_translation: The Torah and the word of truth with which you occupy yourself — it teaches you the strategies of war, so that your right hand will do tremendous things; because he mentioned Torah study in the language of war, the expression “right hand” falls in it, a hand trained to fight (that is: the order of fighting with the right hand).

Sharp in the heart of the king’s enemies — *אגיישוץ* in French. This is a transposed verse. It is found that students are called arrows, as it is said, “As arrows in the hand of a mighty man, So are the children of one’s youth” (below, 127), and Torah scholars (armed) in halakhah are called enemies to one another for the time being, as it is said, “They shall not be put to shame, When they speak with their enemies in the gate” (ibid.).
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. Printed “below, 127” is Psalms 127:4 and “ibid.” is Psalms 127:5. The word “(armed)” is in parentheses in the printed text.

Psalms.english_translation: In reward for the Torah, the worshippers of idols will fall beneath Israel.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thy throne given of God is for ever and ever
Psalms.english_translation: Your throne is [that of] a ruler and judge forever and ever, as it is said, “I have set thee in God’s stead to Pharaoh” (Exodus 6); and why? Because the sceptre of equity is the sceptre of your kingdom, for your judgments are true and you are worthy to reign.
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “Exodus 6” is Exodus 7:1.

Psalms.english_translation: Every expression of greatness takes the expression of anointing with oil, according to the manner of kings.
*Kiddah* is translated *ketzi'ata*.
All your garments give off a fragrance like the fragrance of spices; and its midrash: all your garments and your stench are atoned for and give a pleasant fragrance.
More than ivory palaces, the palaces prepared for you in the Garden of Eden are praised, to gladden you with them. *Shen* — *איבוייר"א* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: stringed instruments have made thee glad
Psalms.english_translation: Palaces from which — they are the ones who gladden you, who give your reward.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed words היכלות אשר מני הם שמחוך are translated literally; their sense is not clear.

Psalms.english_translation: They will visit you, as in the matter that is said, “And their queens thy nursing mothers” (Isaiah 49).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 49” is Isaiah 49:23.

Psalms.english_translation: The kof has a dagesh because it is an expression of visiting, even though a yod is written before it. I saw in the vocalization of Rav Saadia that this word is arranged with “Who gave Jacob for a spoil” (ibid. 42), in which a yod is written and the samekh has a dagesh; and Menachem connected it with an expression of preciousness, like “more precious than a vessel of fine gold.” (סא"א)
Psalms.translator_note: it is left as printed. The last quotation was not identified. Printed “ibid. 42” is Isaiah 42:24.

Psalms.english_translation: A queen, like “and the consort (*shegal*) sitting by him” (Daniel 5:2) — “that the king and his lords, his consorts and his concubines, might drink therein”; “your wife shall stand at your right.”
Psalms.translator_note: The first quotation is Nehemiah 2:6 (JPS: “the queen also sitting by him”); the Aramaic quotation is Daniel 5:2, for which the JPS reading is given.

Psalms.english_translation: In a collection of golden ornaments that came from Ophir.
Hear, Community of Israel, and see the way of good.
To the Torah.
From beyond the River, among whom you grew up.
Idolatry [ע"א] that your fathers served beyond the River.
Psalms.translator_note: The abbreviation ע"א is read as “idolatry” from the context; the expansion is not confirmed by a permitted source, so the comment is flagged.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: So shall the king desire thy beauty
Psalms.english_translation: And if you do so, the King — the Holy One, blessed be He — will desire the beauty of your deeds.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: entreat thy favour with a gift
Psalms.english_translation: Like “And Moses besought” (Exodus 32); and in reward for this you will merit that they bring you gifts (*eshkarim*) and a present — those who are now the rich of a people.
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “Exodus 32” is Exodus 32:11.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: All glorious is the king’s daughter within the palace
Psalms.english_translation: Those on whom all glory depends, and they are the assemblies of the King, who conducted themselves with modesty — now their garments are more important than the gold settings of the High Priests; *mishbetzot* — *קאטונ"ש* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: She shall be led unto the king on richly woven stuff
Psalms.english_translation: In embroidered garments they will bring them as an offering to the King over all the earth; *rikmot* — *אברודי"ץ* in French; this is what is said, “And they shall bring all your brethren out of all the nations for an offering unto the LORD” etc. (Isaiah 66:20).
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The virgins her companions in her train
Psalms.english_translation: They will go after them, as in the matter that is said, “shall even take hold of the skirt of him that is a Jew, saying: We will go with you, for we have heard that God is with you” (Zechariah 8:23).
The psalmist said this with regard to the Holy One, blessed be He.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Instead of thy fathers shall be thy sons
Psalms.english_translation: He said it to each one of Israel.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I will make thy name to be remembered
Psalms.english_translation: The psalmist said this with regard to the Holy One, blessed be He.
The name of a musical instrument, in Chronicles.

In the future to come, on the day of which it is said, “And the earth shall wax old like a garment” (Isaiah 51), the sons of Korah saw the miracle that was done for them, that all around them were swallowed up and they stood in the air; and they said to Israel through the holy spirit that the like of this miracle will be done for them in the future.
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 51” is Isaiah 51:6.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Though the waters thereof roar and foam
Psalms.english_translation: They will cast out mire and clay and mud (ibid. 57), as is their way; and Menachem connected it with “Mine inwards burn (*chamarmeru*)” (Lamentations 2); *רגורזרונ"ט* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. Printed “ibid. 57” is Isaiah 57:20 (JPS: “its waters cast up mire and dirt”); Rashi’s wording differs. The words *mei chamarmeru* are in Lamentations 1:20 (JPS: “Mine inwards burn”) and *chamarmeru me'ai* in 2:11.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Though the mountains shake at the swelling thereof
Psalms.english_translation: Of the Holy One, blessed be He, who was mentioned at the beginning of the psalm.
*שושרויישיל"ש* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: The Garden of Eden.
At the end of the redemption.
An expression of tumult (*homeh*).

*Tamug* — melts; so Menachem explained: “All the inhabitants of Canaan are melted away” (Exodus 15), and so “that their heart may melt” (Ezekiel 21); but Dunash explained them as an expression of movement, and so “the multitude melted away and they went hither and thither” (1 Samuel 14), and so all of them.
Psalms.translator_note: Printed references are Exodus 15:15, Ezekiel 21:20 and 1 Samuel 14:16.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Who hath made desolations in the earth
Psalms.english_translation: Who made the lands of the nations a desolation.
From upon us.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: unto the end of the earth
Psalms.english_translation: For all the lands of the nations will be at peace with us.
He will break the nations.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He burneth the chariots in the fire
Psalms.english_translation: Chariots of war.
[Restrain] yourselves from coming again against Jerusalem.
That I will execute judgment upon you.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I will be exalted in the earth
Psalms.english_translation: I will be exalted by my vengeance that I will take upon the nations.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: O clap your hands, all you peoples
Psalms.english_translation: Join together with one another to shout to God with a voice of song.

He will put pestilence (*dever*) upon the idolaters in place of our soul, so that His wrath will be cooled in them, and these will be saved, as in the matter that is said, “And I will give Egypt as thy ransom” etc. (Isaiah 43:3); and Menachem connected *yadber* with an expression of leading.
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s wording differs from JPS (Isaiah 43:3): “I have given Egypt as thy ransom.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He chooseth our inheritance for us
Psalms.english_translation: And will return us into it, and then He will be exalted with the blast and the sound of the shofar that is sounded before Him, with song over burnt-offerings and peace-offerings, and it is said, “Sing praises unto God” etc.
So all will say.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: God sitteth upon His holy throne
Psalms.english_translation: Now the throne is complete and recognized in greatness, and they will declare that they were gathered to His city.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The princes of the peoples are gathered together
Psalms.english_translation: Who volunteered themselves for slaughter and killing for the sanctity of His name.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The people of the God of Abraham
Psalms.english_translation: Who was the first to be generous of heart toward the proselytes; now it is known that “unto God belong the shields of the earth” — the power is in His hand to be a shield for all who trust in Him.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: In the city of our God
Psalms.english_translation: In the future to come, when He builds His city, He will be great and praised because of it.

A city that is a beautiful *nof* — an expression of the *nof* of a tree. Another explanation: a bride of beauty, for in the coastal cities they call a bride *ננפי*; and Menachem connected it with “the three regions” (Joshua 17:11), *קונטריא"ה* in French. But Dunash interpreted it as an expression of the *nof* of a tree, and Mount Zion is called fair in situation because it is the Mount of Olives. (סא"א)
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. it is left as printed. The words *kallat shel yofi* are translated literally and their sense is not certain. In Joshua 17:11 Rashi’s word is *hanafat*; JPS renders it “regions.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: the joy of the whole earth
Psalms.english_translation: And what is its joy? “The uttermost parts of the north” — *אנגלא"ש* in French — the side of the altar to the north, where they slaughter sin-offerings and guilt-offerings; and one who was sad over the transgressions in his hand brings sin-offerings and guilt-offerings and is atoned for, and he goes out from there joyful, and through the offerings good comes.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Hath made Himself known for a stronghold
Psalms.english_translation: When He dwells in it in the future they will say so.
To fight against it in the war of Gog and Magog.
To war.
The Holy One, blessed be He, going out and fighting those nations; so they were astonished.
*פור"נט אטורדי"ץ* in French, like *uvechofzutah*.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. The quoted word *uvechofzutah* was not identified.

Psalms.english_translation: It is an expression of retribution, for the Holy One, blessed be He, exacts payment from the wicked with it, as it is said, “and the LORD caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind” etc. (Exodus 14:21), and so concerning Tyre, “The east wind hath broken thee In the heart of the seas” (Ezekiel 27:26), “With the wind I will scatter them before the enemy” (Jeremiah 18:17).
Psalms.translator_note: In Jeremiah 18:17 JPS reads “I will scatter them as with an east wind Before the enemy.”

Psalms.english_translation: They are the neighbours of Tyre; it is Africa, and it is from Edom.
Psalms.translator_note: The last clause (*umi'Edom hi*) is translated literally; its sense is not clear.

Psalms.english_translation: The consolations from the mouth of the prophets — so have we seen.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: We have thought on Thy lovingkindness
Psalms.english_translation: The prophet returns and prays to the Holy One, blessed be He, and says, “We have thought and hoped for Your lovingkindnesses, to see this Your salvation in the midst of Your temple”; and Menachem explained it as an expression of thought, like “Think not with thyself” (Esther 4:13).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: As is Thy name, O God, So is Thy praise
Psalms.english_translation: As Your name is great, so is Your praise great in the mouth of all.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Let the daughters of Judah rejoice
Psalms.english_translation: All the other cities of Judah are daughters to Zion, like “and he took Kenath and her daughters” (Numbers 32:42).
Psalms.translator_note: JPS Numbers 32:42 reads “took Kenath, and the villages thereof”; Rashi’s word is “daughters.”

Psalms.english_translation: That You will execute judgment among the nations.
You who build it.
An expression of counting: know how many towers are fitting for it.
Her walls, like “the rampart and wall” (Lamentations 2:8).
Raise high her *birniyot*, like *ashdot hapisgah* (Deuteronomy 3:17), which is translated *ramta*.
Psalms.translator_note: Word left transliterated. The first citation is under Deuteronomy 3:17 (JPS: “the slopes of Pisgah”).

Psalms.english_translation: Its height and its beauty to the generation after you.
Like a man who leads his small son gently (*le'at*); and Menachem explained it as an expression of “world,” and so its meaning: He will guide us for the worlds (*le'olmei*).
Because this psalm is founded on people who trust in their wealth, he said “all peoples,” for all of them need chastisement.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: all you inhabitants of the world
Psalms.english_translation: *Cheled* is the earth, because it grows old and rusts (*chaludah*); *רדוייל"ייא* in French. And our Rabbis explained it as from the *choldah* (weasel), which is on dry land and not in the sea, for the Rabbis taught: everything that is on dry land is in the sea, except the *choldah*.
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 49:2 (“world, from a word meaning rust, because it changes and grows old”), in forms such as רדויל ידא, רדנלייא, רדוייכא, רויילא, רודיכא, רולייא, ראוליאיה; the printed form (רדוייל"ייא) is a variant spelling.

Psalms.english_translation: Sons of Abraham, who is called “the greatest man among the Anakim” (Joshua 14:15), the sons of Ishmael and the sons of Keturah.
Sons of Noah, who is called “a man righteous” (Genesis 6:9).
The thoughts of my heart — they are understandings.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I will incline mine ear to a parable
Psalms.english_translation: To words of Torah, which is called “the proverb of the ancients” (1 Samuel 24:14).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I will open my dark saying upon the harp
Psalms.english_translation: I will open to you this my riddle with a harp, and this is the riddle: Why should I fear in the days of evil, in the day of the visitation of iniquity? Because the iniquity of my heels surrounds me — iniquities on which I tread with my heel, that I make light of, which in my eyes are light transgressions; they condemn me in judgment, and all the more so the rich.
Psalms.translator_note: The words quoted are those of Psalms 49:6, where JPS reads “Wherefore should I fear in the days of evil, When the iniquity of my supplanters compasseth me about”; Rashi reads *akevai* as “my heels.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Of them that trust in their wealth
Psalms.english_translation: And what profit is there in their money? Surely:

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: No man can by any means redeem his brother
Psalms.english_translation: He cannot redeem his brother with his money, because if they come to redeem one man his brother, the redemption of their soul becomes costly beyond all wealth; therefore, of necessity, he ceases forever from redeeming him.

(That he should live for ever and not see the pit.) And Menachem connected it with an expression of withholding, like “I will make man more rare than fine gold” (Isaiah 13:12) and “then I will walk contrary unto you in fury” (Leviticus 26:28); that is: and the redemption of their soul will be withheld.
Psalms.translator_note: The first words in parentheses are a later printed insertion.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: For he seeth that wise men die
Psalms.english_translation: And they are not saved from death; therefore he must cease to strain and toil over the redemption of his brother.
Their money. Of the wise, “death” is said, for they do not die in this world, only the body; and of the fool and the brutish, “perishing” is said.
Their thoughts are to build for themselves houses that will endure forever.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: They call their lands after their own names
Psalms.english_translation: Their houses that they build, so that it will be a memorial for them; and the city is called by the name of his son, Enoch (Genesis 4:17); Antiochus built Antioch, Seleucus built Seleucia.
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 6” is Genesis 4:17.

Psalms.english_translation: An expression of preciousness and glory. (סא"א)
Psalms.translator_note: it is left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: An expression of *mashal* (likeness).
An expression of silence (*dmamah*).
Folly.
And those who come after them will speak of them and relate with their mouth what happened to the former.

*Yirtzu* is an expression of reciting words, *רטרירונ"ש* in French. And our Sages of blessed memory explained: this is the way of the wicked, whose end is destruction; but “*kesel lamo*” — they have fat upon their loins, and it covers their kidneys, and they do not counsel them to return from their evil. And perhaps you will say it is forgetfulness on their part, that they forgot that their end is to die; the verse says “and after them with their mouth they speak” — that is, the day of their end is always in their mouth, and they do not tremble before it.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Like sheep they are appointed for the nether-world
Psalms.english_translation: Like sheep gathered into the fold, so are they for Sheol.

The dagesh in the tav is in place of a second tav: *lish'ol shotetu*, an expression of the foundations (*shatot*) of Sheol, at the lowest level; and so “*shattu* in the heavens their mouth” (below, Psalms 73:9) — this too is an expression of foundation: they fixed in the heavens their mouth, their evil tongue.
Psalms.translator_note: JPS Psalms 73:9 reads “They have set their mouth against the heavens.”

Psalms.english_translation: The angel of death will eat them; and do not wonder at this expression of eating, for we find in another place “the first-born of death shall devour his members” (Job 18:13). Another version: an expression of crushing, like “Can iron break iron” (Jeremiah 15:12).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: the upright shall have dominion over them in the morning
Psalms.english_translation: For the day of redemption, when the morning of Israel shall shine, they will tread upon them, as it is said, “And you shall tread down the wicked” etc. (end of Malachi).
Psalms.translator_note: The verse is Malachi 3:21.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: their form shall be for the nether-world to wear away
Psalms.english_translation: The form of the wicked will wear away Sheol; Gehinnom ends, and they do not end.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: That there be no habitation for it
Psalms.english_translation: From having an abode; and the Holy One, blessed be He, takes the sun out of its sheath and scorches them, as it is said (ibid.), “and the day that cometh shall set them ablaze”; and our Rabbis explained “*mizvul lo*” as: because they stretched out their hands against the *zevul*, for they destroyed the Temple.
Psalms.translator_note: “ibid.” is Malachi 3:19.

Psalms.english_translation: But I, who inclined my ear to a parable — God will redeem my soul so that I will not go to Sheol, for He will take me in my lifetime to walk in His ways.
The wicked man blesses his soul during his life and says, “Peace be upon you, my soul; no evil at all will befall you”; but others do not say this of him.
And you, if you hearken to the words of all, they will praise you that you do good to your soul, to straighten your way.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: It shall go to the generation of his fathers
Psalms.english_translation: When your days are complete and you die, you will come and see the generation of the wicked — the fathers of a wicked man — condemned in Gehinnom, who forever will not see light.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Man that is in honour understandeth not
Psalms.english_translation: The way of life is placed before him, so that if he walks in it, he is honoured; he does not understand the good.
I will call (the God of gods, HaShem is His name).
And He has shined forth from Zion, which is of the perfection of beauty.
A noun; *parement* [printed פרמנ"ט] in French.
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 50:2 (“adornment of beauty”), in forms such as פרמונט, פרמינט, פרימונט; the reading is *parement* (his index; REJ transcription *Prémnt*); the printed form (פרמנ"ט) is a variant spelling.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Our God cometh, and doth not keep silence
Psalms.english_translation: Further, for the shed blood of His servants.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He calleth to the heavens above
Psalms.english_translation: To visit punishment upon the prince of the nations on high.
To visit punishment upon the kings of Egypt.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: that He may judge His people
Psalms.english_translation: To take vengeance for His people, as “For the LORD will judge His people” and “He will avenge the blood of His servants” (Deuteronomy 32:43).
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s Hebrew combines words of Deuteronomy 32:36 (“For the LORD will judge His people”) and 32:43 (JPS: “For He doth avenge the blood of His servants”); the printed reference is 32:43.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Gather My saints together unto Me
Psalms.english_translation: And again He will call to the heavens and to the earth that the exiles be gathered to Him, as in the matter that is said, “Awake, O north wind; And come, thou south” (Song of Songs 4:16).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Those that have made a covenant with Me by sacrifice
Psalms.english_translation: That they accepted the Torah with covenant and sacrifice, as in the matter that is said, “Behold the blood of the covenant, which the LORD hath made with you” etc. (Exodus 24:8).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I will not reprove thee for thy sacrifices
Psalms.english_translation: If you do not bring Me your sacrifices, and your burnt-offerings are not before Me continually, I do not set My eye and My heart on this.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I will take no bullock out of thy house
Psalms.english_translation: They are not yours but Mine.
It is the sheepfold, like “The flock shall be cut off from the fold” (Habakkuk 3:17); *פאר"ק* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: the cattle upon a thousand hills
Psalms.english_translation: It is the (ox) that grazes a thousand mountains in a day, and every single day they sprout again. Some explain: a thousand mountains, or a thousand parasangs, or the name of a thousand bulls; and some explain that it is like *shegar alafekha* — that is, mountains full of cattle — because he mentioned, “I will take no bullock out of thy house.”
Psalms.translator_note: The word “(ox)” is a later printed insertion. The expression *shegar alafekha* occurs in Deuteronomy 7:13 (JPS: “the increase of thy kine”); Rashi gives no reference.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: the wild beasts of the field
Psalms.english_translation: The creeping things of the field are called *ziz*, because they move (*zazim*) from place to place; *אישמובימנ"ט* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 50:11 (“movement in the fields”), in forms such as אישמובינט, אשמובמנט, אשמוביר, אישמובימינט, אשמובמינט; the printed form (אישמובימנ"ט) is a variant spelling.

Psalms.english_translation: I know them all.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Do I eat the flesh of bulls
Psalms.english_translation: I did not tell you to bring a sacrifice because I need it for eating, but for satisfaction before Me, that I spoke and My will was done.
Confess your deeds and return to Me; this is the sacrifice in which I delight; and afterwards pay your vows to the Most High, for then they will be accepted favourably.
For this is My honour — that I save those who trust in Me.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: that thou hast taken My covenant in thy mouth
Psalms.english_translation: My Torah.
You consented to go with him.
You accustom deceit with you to speak evil; *tatzmid* — *אגוטא"ש* in French — like “covering close-bound” (Numbers 19:15). (סא"א)
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. it is left as printed. The translation of *tatzmid* is literal; the sense is not clear. In Numbers 19:15 Rashi’s words are *tzamid patil*; JPS “covering close-bound.”

Psalms.english_translation: In the seat of scorners.
For you have no suit or quarrel with him, as he does not inherit with you.
*Dofi* — a disgraceful thing, to thrust it away; an expression of *yehadfenu*.
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s lemma *dofi* is the word JPS renders “slanderest.”

Psalms.english_translation: You think that I will be like you, in being pleased by your evil deeds; (and some explain *dimit* as: because I do not know hidden things).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Whoso offereth the sacrifice of thanksgiving honoureth Me
Psalms.english_translation: One who brings Me a sacrifice of repentance and confession of his sins — he will honour Me.
To one who returns to Me, I teach; and one who sets a way for sinners to return to Me, I will show him My salvation.
Psalms.translator_note: The translation is literal; the printed Hebrew is elliptical.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: my sin is ever before me
Psalms.english_translation: Because I regret and am anxious over it, it seems to me as if it were before me always, every hour.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Against Thee, Thee only, have I sinned
Psalms.english_translation: Therefore it is in Your hand to forgive; and even what I did evil to Uriah, I sinned not but against You, for You warned about the matter.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: That Thou mayest be justified when Thou speakest
Psalms.english_translation: Like “in Your manner.” (סא"א) I had power to overcome my inclination, but lest they say the servant overcame his master — for I said before You, “Examine me, O LORD, and try me” (above, Psalms 26:2), and You tested me and I was not found whole — so that You be justified and not I. Another explanation: “that Thou mayest be justified when Thou speakest” — if You forgive me, You will be justified in Your judgment, in the presence of all the wicked who do not repent, so that they cannot say, “Had we repented, it would not have availed us.”
Psalms.translator_note: it is left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Behold, I was brought forth in iniquity
Psalms.english_translation: And how shall I not sin, when the essence of my formation is through intercourse, through which many sins come? Another explanation: the essence of my formation is from male and female, who are all full of iniquity. There are midrashim on this verse, and they do not settle according to the subject of the speaker in the psalm.
An expression of heat, like “and they conceived when they came to drink” (Genesis 30:38). (סא"א)
Psalms.translator_note: it is left as printed. Rashi’s Hebrew word is *vayachamnah*.

Psalms.english_translation: And behold, I confess to the truth, that I have sinned.

These are the kidneys, which are smooth; and Menachem connected it with “as it were a bow-shot” (Genesis 21:16), and so “Who hath put wisdom in the inward parts?” (Job 38:36) — its meaning is an expression of extension (*mashakh*), for as a bow has extension, so knowledge has extension. (סא"א)
Psalms.translator_note: it is left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: And in the heart, which is hidden, You made me know wisdom — to confess.
As one purifies the leper and one unclean by the dead.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Make me to hear joy and gladness
Psalms.english_translation: Forgiveness of sin.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: the bones which Thou hast crushed
Psalms.english_translation: When You were angry with me.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Create me a clean heart, O God
Psalms.english_translation: That I may stumble no more.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: take not Thy holy spirit from me
Psalms.english_translation: That the holy spirit not be distant from me. (סא"א)
Psalms.translator_note: it is left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Restore unto me the joy of Thy salvation
Psalms.english_translation: The holy spirit that was removed from me.
An expression of generosity, nobility.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Then will I teach transgressors Thy ways
Psalms.english_translation: And from me they will learn and return, if they see that You forgive me.
That I not die by the sword for the punishment of Uriah, whom I killed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: O Lord, open Thou my lips
Psalms.english_translation: Forgive me, and let me have an opening of the mouth to declare Your praise.
For a sin-offering does not come for one who sins deliberately.
For if You desired it, I would give it to You.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Do good in Thy favour unto Zion
Psalms.english_translation: To build Your Temple within it in the days of Solomon my son.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Why boastest thou thyself of evil
Psalms.english_translation: And you glory in the evil that you do, you who are mighty in Torah.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The mercy of God endureth continually
Psalms.english_translation: To save the one pursued by you. Another explanation: “The mercy of God all the day” — had Ahimelech not given me bread, do you imagine that I would die of hunger? There is mercy with the Holy One, blessed be He, toward Israel all the day, and if he had not given me, others would give me.
Sharpened.
It cuts the flesh together with the hair.
An expression of demolition.
An expression of breaking.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: pluck thee out of thy tent
Psalms.english_translation: He will uproot you.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: root thee out of the land of the living
Psalms.english_translation: He will uproot after you, to uproot all the roots; *דיראריצינע"ר* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 52:7 (“he will uproot you”), in forms such as אישרציניר, אשרצייר, אשרציניר, אשרצינר, דרצינייר; the printed form (דיראריצינע"ר) is a variant spelling.

Psalms.english_translation: And this is the laughter: they will say of him, “Behold, this is the man who did not place his trust in the Holy One, blessed be He; see what became of him.”
He was growing strong in his wickedness.
I who am now pursued by your hand will be like a leafy olive-tree, with children and grandchildren, in the house of the Holy One, blessed be He.
When You do this for me; and he said this verse toward the Holy One, blessed be He.

The name of a musical instrument. Another explanation: concerning the *machalah* (sickness) of Israel when the Temple would be destroyed; and another psalm already said the like of this (above, Psalms 14), “The fool hath said in his heart: ‘There is no God’” etc.; the one is about the destruction of the First Temple and this one about the second.
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “above, 14” is Psalms 14:1.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The fool hath said in his heart
Psalms.english_translation: This is about Titus, when he cut through the curtain and his sword dripped blood; he said, “He killed himself.”
Psalms.translator_note: The printed words הרג את עצמו are translated literally; the exact sense of the quotation is not clear.

Psalms.english_translation: *Sag* — an expression of dross (*sigim*).
Of all his troops, that He wiped out by his hand.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed words שימחה בידו are translated literally; the subject is not clear.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Shall not the workers of iniquity know it
Psalms.english_translation: Surely it is to be known by those who eat My people as they eat bread, and who did not call upon God, that their end is that they will be seized there with great fear in the end of days.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: There are they in great fear, where no fear was
Psalms.english_translation: This is like the first fear that befell Belshazzar, for in this redemption the Holy One, blessed be He, scattered the bones of him who encamps (*chonekh*) against you, Jerusalem, as in the matter that is said, “Their flesh shall consume away” etc. (Zechariah 14:12); and so Menachem explained. And Dunash explained it like “Train up (*chanokh*) a child in the way he should go” (Proverbs 22:6), and the kaf of *chonekh* is a root letter in the word, like the kaf of *chanokh*. (סא"א)
Psalms.translator_note: it is left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou hast put them to shame
Psalms.english_translation: You, HaShem, [shamed] all my enemies, for You have rejected them.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed text is elliptical and is translated as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: You will take my vengeance, like “For the LORD will judge His people” (Deuteronomy 32:36).
Psalms.translator_note: The printed reference is “Deuteronomy 32”; the words are in 32:36.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: them that lie in wait for me
Psalms.english_translation: To those who look upon me; an expression of “I behold him, but not nigh” (Numbers 24:17).
Psalms.translator_note: The printed word לעויני is unclear; the translation follows the quoted verse (*ashurenu*).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Destroy Thou them in Thy truth
Psalms.english_translation: Because You are true, and You said to exact payment from talebearers and pursuers of killing, therefore You cut them off.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I am distraught in my complaint
Psalms.english_translation: I will lament in my distress, like “Remember mine affliction and mine anguish” (Lamentations 3:19) and “and go down upon the mountains” (Judges 11:37). And Menachem explained it as an expression of dominion, like “and have dominion over the fish of the sea”; and *sichi* is an expression of *siach*, as in “who hath raving?” (Proverbs 23:29). (סא"א)
Psalms.translator_note: it is left as printed. The quotation “and have dominion over the fish of the sea” is Genesis 1:28; Rashi gives no reference.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Because of the oppression of the wicked
Psalms.english_translation: An expression of distress.
Doeg and Ahithophel weigh iniquities against me, to show that I am deserving of death, and they permit my blood.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: My heart doth writhe within me
Psalms.english_translation: Doeg.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Lo, then would I wander far off
Psalms.english_translation: If I had wings, I would wander far off and hasten to save my soul from their hand, for they are like a stormy wind (*ruach so'ah*), a tempest-wind that uproots trees, like “and my hope hath He plucked up like a tree” (Job 19:10); and Menachem connected *so'ah* with “And the children of Israel journeyed” (Exodus 12:37).
*Bala* — *דפא"יי* in French, like “withdrawn His hand from destroying” (Lamentations 2:8); so Menachem explained. (סא"א)
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. it is left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: Separate it, so that no one will listen to them; and Menachem explained *palag* as an expression of division. (סא"א)
Psalms.translator_note: it is left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I have seen violence and strife in the city
Psalms.english_translation: Through them.
The violence and the strife.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Wickedness is in the midst thereof
Psalms.english_translation: Breakages.
An expression of striking.
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s lemma is *tokh*, the word JPS renders “Oppression.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: For it was not an enemy that taunted me
Psalms.english_translation: In my days I did not bear my reproach, but rose against him and killed him.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed opening מימי is translated literally.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Neither was it mine adversary that did magnify himself against me
Psalms.english_translation: And I fled and hid from him. But now, against my will, I bear your reproach, for you reproach me because you are a man great in Torah.
An important man like me.

Like *alufi*; an expression of “and I know thee by name” (Exodus 33:17), which is translated *urabitakh*. And Menachem explained “For it was not an enemy that taunted me” and “then I could have borne it”: there is something of the matter of “Oh that I had a wing like a dove, I would fly and dwell” — if I could grow a wing, I would fly and wander off from before the oppression of the wicked; for when I go out from the midst of the cave of the lawless to lodge in the wilderness, Selah, then it is not an enemy that taunts me, and I would not bear my disgrace and shame, and I would not hide from him as I hid from them when I was among them. And this interpretation is not feasible because of the verses written after them, which are “But it was thou, a man mine equal, My companion, and my familiar friend; We took sweet counsel together, In the house of God we walked with the throng.” Therefore Dunash interprets it in another way, and this is its interpretation: for it is not an enemy that taunts me, that I should bear his taunt, and not one who hates me that magnified himself against me, that I should hide from him, but only “my companion, and my familiar friend; We took sweet counsel together, In the house of God we walked with the throng.” And this thing is known, that a man finds the reproach of a friend harder than the reproach of an enemy, and also he can hide from his enemy but cannot hide from a friend, having told him all his heart; so the context proves.
Psalms.translator_note: The Aramaic is translated as printed. The opening of Menachem’s explanation (*ve'esa yesh alav min ha'inyan*) is elliptical and is translated literally. Rashi’s wording of Psalms 55:7 differs from JPS (“Oh that I had wings like a dove! Then would I fly away, and be at rest”).

Psalms.english_translation: We were accustomed to sweeten counsel in Torah, and in the house of God we walked with the throng, among a multitude of people.
Houses of study.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: May He incite death against them
Psalms.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He, will incite the angel of death against them. *Yashi* — stirs up and incites; an expression of “The serpent beguiled me, and I did eat” (Genesis 3:13). And Menachem explained *yashi* as an expression of *yesh*, like “if you (*yeshkhem*) deal” (Genesis 24:49) and “who is (*yesno*) here” (Deuteronomy 29:14).
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s citations are from Genesis 24:49 (printed “ibid. 24”; JPS “if you will deal kindly and truly”) and Deuteronomy 29:14 (JPS “him that standeth here with us”).

Psalms.english_translation: In their lodging.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Evening, and morning, and at noon
Psalms.english_translation: The evening prayer, the morning prayer and the afternoon prayer — three prayers.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: so that none came nigh me
Psalms.english_translation: From the war that came upon me.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: For they were many that strove with me
Psalms.english_translation: For He did this for me on account of the many who were helping me by praying for me, as it is said, “And all Israel and Judah loved David.”
Psalms.translator_note: JPS 1 Samuel 18:16 reads “But all Israel and Judah loved David.”

Psalms.english_translation: The prayer of those many.
The King who sits of old.
Of those wicked who pursue me — they do not set their hearts to the day of their change; they do not tremble at the day of death.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He hath put forth his hands
Psalms.english_translation: This is Ahithophel the wicked.
*טאנד"יט* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: against them that were at peace with him
Psalms.english_translation: With that which was quiet and at peace with him.
An expression of smoothness (above, Psalms 5:10).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “above, 5” is Psalms 5:10 (JPS: “They make smooth their tongue”).

Psalms.english_translation: An expression of *chem'ah* (butter), and the first mem is a falling root letter in the word, like the mem of *ma'aseh* and like the mem of *ma'amar*.
Psalms.translator_note: The grammatical phrase *yesod nofel* is translated literally.

Psalms.english_translation: His heart is for war.

Menachem explained it as an expression of swords, like “And the land of Nimrod with the keen-edged sword” (Micah 5), *kefiyot cherev*. (סא"א) And I say that it is an expression of cursing in the Aramaic language, as it is said, “Ameimar wrote a *petichah* about it,” and it is a writ of excommunication.
Psalms.translator_note: it is left as printed. The Aramaic is translated as printed. The reference in Micah is 5:5; the quotation of the Talmudic saying was not identified.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Cast thy burden upon the LORD
Psalms.english_translation: *Yehavkha* — your burden; the holy spirit answers him thus.
He will bear your burden, like “the heaven of heavens cannot contain Thee” (1 Kings 8:27); the expression *kilkul* is translated “to bear” in the Targum of Jonathan ben Uzziel.
Psalms.translator_note: JPS 1 Kings 8:27 reads “heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain Thee.”

Psalms.english_translation: A slip of the foot.

He said this of himself, that he was far from the Land of Israel, with Achish, and the brothers of Goliath were asking permission from Achish to kill him, as it is said, “Is not this David the king of the land?” (1 Samuel 21:12); and he was among them like a mute dove.
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “1 Samuel 28” is 1 Samuel 21:12.

Psalms.english_translation: They hope to swallow me up — *גולושי"ר* in French — like “snuffeth up the wind” (Jeremiah 2:24).
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 56:2 (“they aspire to devour me”), in forms such as גולושייר, אגולזשיר, גולושיר, יגולוישיר; the printed form matches.

Psalms.english_translation: An expression of war (*milchamah*).
The Holy One, blessed be He, who sits on high.
Even at the time when He comes with me in the attribute of judgment I will praise His word and trust in Him.
My pursuers grieve me, until all the words of my mouth are sorrow and outcry.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: They gather themselves together, they hide themselves
Psalms.english_translation: They lie in ambush and lodge in the place where they hope that I will go, and they watch my heel (*akevi*) — *טר"צש* in French — to *lerageleni* and to lead pursuers there. All this was agreed among the wicked of Israel who lay in ambush for him, and from fear of them he fled to Achish.
