Psalms.translator_note: Old French: Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 56:1 (“my traces”), in forms such as טרצט, טרצש, טראצש, טראציש, טריאיציש; the printed form (טר"צש) matches. The word *lerageleni* is left transliterated and the phrase *hayah mekubbal al* is translated literally; their sense is not certain.

Psalms.english_translation: They will lodge.
They will lie in ambush.
When they know and hope that I will go this way.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Because of iniquity cast them out
Psalms.english_translation: To find rescue and wealth through a matter of iniquity and wickedness; *pelet* is like “for rescue” — they hope for reward from Saul for that.
Psalms.translator_note: The translation is literal; the printed Hebrew is compressed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: In anger bring down the peoples
Psalms.english_translation: In Your anger bring down this nation among whom I am, from their wisdom and from their plans in which they say to kill me.
You know the number of places in which I wandered to flee.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Put Thou my tears into Thy bottle
Psalms.english_translation: Put my tears into Your bottle, and let it be kept before You.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Are they not in Thy book
Psalms.english_translation: In Your reckoning You will place it, to count it with my other troubles. (And Menachem connected it with the word *sefer* literally.)
For the attribute of judgment and for the attribute of mercy I will praise.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: in the light of the living
Psalms.english_translation: To return to the Land of Israel.
David called this psalm thus because he was near death, and he composed this psalm to say, “Destroy me not, HaShem.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Be gracious unto me, O God, be gracious unto me
Psalms.english_translation: Be gracious to me, that I not kill and that I not be killed.
Until the evil passes.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: When he that would swallow me up taunteth
Psalms.english_translation: And He will save me from the taunt of my swallower, who says to swallow me; *shof'i* — *גולושנט"מוי* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: Abner and Amasa, who were lions in Torah and did not protest against Saul.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I do lie down among them that are flame
Psalms.english_translation: I will lie among flame-ones — *אנפנבלוייאנ"ץ* in French — among the *zifim* that blaze after evil speech.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. The word *zifim* is left transliterated; its sense here is not clear.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Be Thou exalted, O God, above the heavens
Psalms.english_translation: Withdraw from the lower realms that are not fit for Your Presence to dwell among them, and be honoured on the earth through this.
The enemy.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: They are fallen into the midst thereof themselves
Psalms.english_translation: Their end is to fall into it. *Kafaf* — *קלי"נא* in French — an expression of “and raiseth up all those that are bowed down” (below, Psalms 145:14).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “below, 145” is Psalms 145:14. The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: My heart is stedfast, O God, my heart is stedfast
Psalms.english_translation: Faithful with You in the attribute of judgment, and faithful with You in the attribute of mercy.
And I will not sleep until the third hour in my glory like other kings.
Awaken me, you psaltery and harp that hang above my bed, open toward the north, and when midnight arrives a north wind blows upon it, and David stands and engages in Torah.
I awaken the dawn, and the dawn does not awaken me.
A name of pleasantness of song.
It is an expression of faith.

He said this psalm when he came to the encampment where Saul lay, and took the spear and the cruse and went away, and called out “Answerest thou not, Abner?” (1 Samuel 26:14) — that is: now you ought to rebuke Saul and show him that he pursues me for nothing, for had I wished, I would have killed him; and so he said in his song: “Indeed, has the righteousness become mute from your mouths,” which you should have spoken, and the uprightness by which you should have judged, “the righteousness that you speak.”
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “1 Samuel 27” is 1 Samuel 26:14. Rashi’s wording of the verse (*ne'elam mipichem hatzedek*) differs from the JPS reading.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Yea, in heart you work wickedness
Psalms.english_translation: And moreover, in your hearts you plot evil to work wrong.
Like *avlot* (iniquities), as one says from *shor* — *shevorim*, from *ir* — *ayarim*, and “and they had thirty cities (*ayarim*)” (Judges 10:4), which are expressions of city and town.
Psalms.translator_note: The forms *shevorim* and *ayarim* are quoted as printed (שוורים, עיירים).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: You weigh out in the earth the violence of your hands
Psalms.english_translation: In the midst of the earth you tip the scale for the violence of your hands, until it weighs a great weight; *tefalleson* — *קונטערפיי"שץ* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The wicked are estranged from the womb
Psalms.english_translation: From their mother’s womb they become strangers to the Holy One, blessed be He, in the way that Esau did: “And the children struggled together within her” (Genesis 25:22).

*Nazoru* — like “Be astonished (*shomu*), O you heavens” (Jeremiah 2:12), “The archers have dealt bitterly with him (*vayemareruhu*), and shot at him” (Genesis 49:23), “They are exalted (*romu*) for a little while” (Job 24:24); all of them are expressions of *nif'alu*.
Psalms.translator_note: The word *nif'alu* is the Hebrew term, left as printed. In Genesis 49:23 Rashi quotes *vayemareruhu verabu* (JPS: “have dealt bitterly with him, And shot at him”).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Their venom is like the venom of a serpent
Psalms.english_translation: They have poison to kill people, like the serpent.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: the deaf asp that stoppeth her ear
Psalms.english_translation: The serpent, when it grows old, becomes deaf in one ear, and stops the other with dust, so that it will not hear the charm when the charmer adjures it not to harm.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Which hearkeneth not to the voice of charmers
Psalms.english_translation: It is connected to the verse before it: and it stops its ear so that it will not hear the voice of those who whisper charms.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: the most cunning binder of spells
Psalms.english_translation: Who knows how to charm the serpents.
The inner teeth, which are called *מייש"ליש* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word under Psalms 58 (“molar teeth”), in forms such as בויילירש, מישלירש, מייטליירש, מיישיליש, מייטליש, משילדי, מאויישיל; the printed form (מייש"ליש) is a variant spelling.

Psalms.english_translation: That they be loathsome to themselves in their own eyes from worry; and like “let them go like water” — its parallel is “all knees shall go as water” (Ezekiel 21:12). (סא"א)
Psalms.translator_note: it is left as printed. Rashi’s wording of Ezekiel 21:12 differs from JPS (“all knees shall drip with water”).

Psalms.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He, [aims] against them so that they will be cut off; *yitmolalu* — *שיאנ"ט פרוייאיי"ץ* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. The printed word לנגד' is abbreviated and is translated “against them.”

Psalms.english_translation: Some explain it as *limace* [printed לימצ"א] in French, and some explain it like “flood” (*shibbolet mayim*) (below, Psalms 69:3); and the doubled lamed is like “his branch (*yimmal*) withered” (Job 18:16), *yemulal* (below, Psalms 90:6).
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word under Psalms 58 (“slug”), in forms such as לימץ, לימצא, לומץ, לימצון, לימאיץ; the reading is *limace* (REJ transcription: *Limace*); the printed form (לימצ"א) matches. Printed references are “below, 69” and “below, 90”; Rashi’s quotations are *shibbolet mayim* (JPS Psalms 69:3 “the flood”), *yimmal ketziro* (JPS Job 18:16 “above shall his branch wither”) and *yemulal* (JPS Psalms 90:6 “withereth”).

Psalms.english_translation: Melted and going. *Temes* is a noun; the mem is a base and root letter, and the tav in it is a falling root letter, like the tav of *tevel* in “they have wrought corruption” (Leviticus 20:12).
Psalms.translator_note: The printed reference is “Leviticus 20”; the word *tevel* is in 20:12.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: the untimely births of a woman
Psalms.english_translation: *Nefel eshet* — *טלפ"א* in French; it has no eyes, and it is the *tinshemet*, which is translated *ashuta*; so our Rabbis explained it. And some explain it as the miscarriage of a woman, like *eshet hazimah* (Ezekiel 23); and there is a tav without a connection, like “a crown of glory *temaggenekha*” (Proverbs 4:9), like the untimely birth of a woman that never saw the sun. And according to the first explanation, *nefel* and *eshet* are like “And I was like a lamb *alluf*” (Jeremiah 11:19), which is like “lamb and *alluf*”; and Menachem explained “lamb *alluf*” as an ox; here too, *nefel* and *eshet*. (He commanded to correct. סא"א)
Psalms.translator_note: Old French: Darmesteter lists this word under Psalms 58 (“mole”), in forms such as טלפא, מלפא, טל פשא; the printed form (טלפ"א) matches. The Aramaic *ashuta* is translated as printed. it is left as printed. The phrases *tav belo dibbukut* and *tzivah lehagiah* are translated literally and their sense is not certain. In Ezekiel 23:44 JPS reads “the lewd women” (*neshei hazimah*); in Jeremiah 11:19 JPS reads “a docile lamb.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Before your pots can feel the thorns
Psalms.english_translation: Before your tender thorns know to become hard briars (*atadim*) — that is, before the sons of the wicked grow up.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: the raw and the burning alike
Psalms.english_translation: That is: with might and with strength and with burning anger the Holy One, blessed be He, will sweep them away.
An expression of might.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Verily there is a reward for the righteous
Psalms.english_translation: And then people will say: surely there are fruits and payment of reward in the deeds of the righteous, for the Holy One, blessed be He, has avenged their vengeance.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Verily there is a God that judgeth in the earth
Psalms.english_translation: A judge who judges the wicked in the earth.
He named the psalm thus because he was near death and near being destroyed, seeking mercy for the matter.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: they watched the house to kill him
Psalms.english_translation: When Michal told them, “He is sick” (1 Samuel 19:14), and they brought him out secretly by night.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed reference is “1 Samuel 19”; the words are in 19:14.

Psalms.english_translation: They lodge in my house to guard me.
I did not sin against them.
Ready to kill.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Arouse Thyself to punish all the nations
Psalms.english_translation: And judge the wicked as You judge the nations, and do not be gracious to them.

The interpretation of these two verses falls upon one another: “They return at evening” — it was not enough for them what they did by day, but even at evening they return to their evil, to guard that I not flee and go out of the city; and what did they do by day? “Behold, all day they belch out with their mouth,” to spy upon me to Saul.
And they say in their heart, “Who hears?”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: But Thou, O LORD, shalt laugh at them
Psalms.english_translation: You who laugh and mock also at these wicked ones.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Because of his strength, I will wait for Thee
Psalms.english_translation: The might and strength of my enemy, which is strong against me — to You I will look and wait, for You to help me from him.
He will bring my help forward before the hand of those who hate me rules over me.
What I desire to see.
For this is not a noticeable vengeance.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed word הנכרת is translated “noticeable”; it could also mean “cut off.”

Psalms.english_translation: For all the dead are forgotten; rather, shake them from their property, that they be poor, and that is a vengeance that is remembered for a long time.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: For the sin of their mouth
Psalms.english_translation: [The sin] of their mouth is the word of their lips; and the poor who are pursued by them are caught in their pride, because of the curse and the lie that they tell.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed Hebrew is elliptical and is translated literally.

Psalms.english_translation: Them in Your wrath, O King who judges; and they will know that You rule in Jacob.
It is connected to the verse above: “the sin of their mouth” — they speak by day, and at evening they return to ambush those who informed on them.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: They wander up and down to devour
Psalms.english_translation: As the dogs do all night: if they are not sated, they lodge, from within their satiety, and sleep.
Psalms.translator_note: The last clause (*sheyalinu mitokh sov'am veyishanu*) is translated literally; its sense is not clear.

Psalms.english_translation: When I escape from them, in the morning I will sing of Your strength.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: O my strength, unto Thee will I sing praises
Psalms.english_translation: To You, for You are my strength and my stronghold — to You I will sing.

(תו' *Michtam* is an expression of “*ketem paz*” (Song of Songs 5:11), a desirable thing; and our Rabbis expounded it of David, that he conducted himself as one humble and wholehearted (*makh vetam*) even in his kingship; and another aggadah: that his stroke (*makkato*) was whole (*tamah*), for he was born circumcised. Until here, סא"א.) *Michtam* of David, concerning the testimony of the Sanhedrin, who were compared to a lily, as it is said, “Thy navel is like a round goblet” etc., “Set about with lilies” (Song of Songs 7:3). When he needed them to teach him what to do when he fought with Aram-naharaim and sent Joab against them, they said to Joab, “Are you not of the sons of Jacob? Where is the oath that he swore to Laban, ‘This heap be witness’ (Genesis 31:52)?” And he did not know what to answer. He came to David and said to David, “Thus the sons of Aram said to me.” They came and asked the Sanhedrin, and they said to them, “But did they not first transgress the oath, as he said (Numbers 23:7), ‘From Aram Balak bringeth me, The king of Moab’? And moreover, Cushan-rishathaim (Judges 3:8) was an Aramean.”
Psalms.translator_note: The opening of the parenthesis contains the abbreviation תו' which I could not resolve; it is left as printed. The parenthetical passage is a later printed insertion and ends with the abbreviation סא"א.

Psalms.english_translation: Like “when they strove against the LORD” (Numbers 26:9) — that he fought them because they helped the children of Ammon.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: smote of Edom in the Valley of Salt twelve thousand
Psalms.english_translation: The eighteen thousand written in Kings (2 Samuel 8:13 and 1 Chronicles 18:12): Abishai killed six thousand the first time, and Joab twelve thousand when he returned from smiting Aram.
Psalms.translator_note: The references in parentheses are later printed insertions; JPS 2 Samuel 8:13 reads “eighteen thousand men” (after smiting the Arameans) and 1 Chronicles 18:12 “Abishai ... smote of the Edomites in the Valley of Salt eighteen thousand.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou hast cast us off, Thou hast broken us down
Psalms.english_translation: When Edom fell into his hand, he foresaw by the holy spirit that the Edomites were destined to rule over Israel and to decree evil decrees upon Israel; he stood and sought mercy for the subjugation of the exiles. We suffered many troubles in the days of the Judges from our enemies round about.
*Anafta* — You were wrathful with us; from now, restore Your favour to us.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou hast made the land to shake
Psalms.english_translation: Our land with many troops.

You broke it. And I saw in the words of Dunash that it is an Arabic expression, but he did not explain it; and in the *yesod* (foundation) of Rabbi Moshe the Preacher they explained it as an expression of tearing, and he brought proof for the matter: “and cutteth him out windows” (Jeremiah 22:14), which is translated *ufatzim*. But I say that *ufatzim*, which Jonathan translated, is an expression of fixing a window, like all openings that have posts (*pitzimin*).
Psalms.translator_note: In Jeremiah 22:14 Rashi’s words are *vekara lo chalonai*.

Psalms.english_translation: *Refah* — an expression of healing, even though it is written with a heh; many words serve in that way.
*Matah* — an expression of lowliness.
That which stops up the heart and wraps it (*ra'al*) — an expression of wrapping, like “and the cypresses *hur'alu*” (Nahum 2:4); and in the language of the Mishnah, “Median women who are *re'ulot*.”
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s word in Nahum 2:4 is *hur'alu*; JPS renders “and the cypress spears are made to quiver.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou hast given a banner to them that fear Thee
Psalms.english_translation: Trials (*nisyonot*) of many troubles.
To be tested (*menusim*) by them, if they stand in Your fear.

To adorn (*lekashet*) Your attributes in the world, for when You give them the good, the nations will not question after You, but will adorn Your judgments and say, “It is well, it is good for them, for they stood in many trials.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: That Thy beloved may be delivered
Psalms.english_translation: They will be saved from evil.
Whom You turned back when their enemies became strong over them.
For if You answer me, they will be delivered, since I fight for their sake.
That He will gather the exiles and his seed will rule over them (סא"א). Another explanation: “God spoke in His holiness” that I would be king over them.
Psalms.translator_note: it is left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: In His salvation. In another explanation I found: “God spoke in His holiness” to help me, as it is written, “for the LORD hath spoken of David, saying: By the hand of My servant David I will save My people Israel” (2 Samuel 3:18).
I will divide Shechem to them from the property of their enemies.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: mete out the valley of Succoth
Psalms.english_translation: This Succoth — I do not know of which nation it is; I do not know the Succoth to which Israel came when Israel journeyed from Rameses, where it is. And in other commentaries I found: “I will divide Shechem” — I will return to them the inheritance of Jacob their father; “and mete out the valley of Succoth” — when I divide it for Israel; Shechem and Succoth were at the edge of the land of Canaan, as we find the beginning of Jacob’s coming to the land by way of Succoth, Shechem. Another explanation: “and mete out the valley of Succoth” — *Succoth* is an expression of forms and likenesses, as is said, “and Succoth-benoth” (2 Kings 17:30).
I measure their form, as it is said (ibid., 2 8), “and he measured two lines to put to death, and one full line to keep alive.” (סא"א)
Psalms.translator_note: it is left as printed. The reference printed as “ibid., 2 8” is 2 Samuel 8:2.

Psalms.english_translation: To rule over them.

*Mechokeki* — my princes; *mechokek* is an expression of authority, one who decrees and sends writings and commands, like “The sceptre shall not depart from Judah, nor the ruler’s staff from between his feet” (Genesis 49:10). (סא"א)
Psalms.translator_note: it is left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: I will use them like a copper pot prepared for washing in it.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Upon Edom do I cast my shoe
Psalms.english_translation: *Masger* of mine.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed word מסגר is left transliterated; its sense here is not clear to me.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Philistia, cry aloud because of me
Psalms.english_translation: Join together over my dominion, to be subjugated to me, for Gath is of the land of the Philistines, and so is Gaza, which David conquered.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Who will bring me into the fortified city
Psalms.english_translation: Or to a fortified city, to conquer Bozrah — if You do not help me, who will bring me and who will lead me over the fortresses of Edom? In other commentaries I found it so: over the fortresses of Edom upon which I have now been led.
And You do not go out.
He will trample.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: From the end of the earth will I call unto Thee
Psalms.english_translation: Even though I am far from the men whom I send against my enemies to war.
Against them. And for what do I call to You? That You lead me to a rock that is higher and stronger than I.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I will dwell in Thy Tent for ever
Psalms.english_translation: Grant me merit in this world and in the World to Come.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou hast granted the heritage of those that fear Thy name
Psalms.english_translation: You restored the cities of their inheritance through me.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Mayest Thou add days unto the king’s days
Psalms.english_translation: If it was decreed upon me to die in youth, add days to my days, until my years are seventy years, like the years of generation after generation.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: May he be enthroned before God for ever
Psalms.english_translation: The king, forever before God.
Since he occupies himself with them, let them be prepared to guard him.
Preparation, like “And the LORD God prepared a gourd” (Jonah 4:6).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: So will I sing praise unto Thy name for ever
Psalms.english_translation: As You do good to me, so I will sing Your name, as I pay my vows day by day.
The name of a musical instrument; and an aggadic midrash: concerning the decrees (*dates*) and the judgments that are decreed upon Israel by their enemies.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: doth my soul wait in stillness
Psalms.english_translation: My soul hopes, like “Resign thyself unto the LORD, and wait patiently for Him” (above, Psalms 37:7).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “above, 37” is Psalms 37:7.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I shall not be greatly moved
Psalms.english_translation: Great slips (*mitot gedolot*); and an aggadic midrash: *rabbah* is Gehinnom.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: will you set upon a man
Psalms.english_translation: Menachem explained it from the root of “*hetayu*” — “Bring them to devour” (Jeremiah 12:9) — and “and there came (*vayeta*) the heads of the people” (Deuteronomy 33:21): how long will you gather against a man. And ול"נ that one should explain it as an expression of *havvot*, and the heh and the tav are roots, as one says from *met* — *mot*; so it is said from the root *hat* — *hot*, and the plural is *havvot*, and it is an expression of a plan of breaking and of deceit. And some explain *tehotetu* as “you lengthen your tongues over people with evil,” and compared it to the expression of *erev* when he multiplies words. (סא"א)
Psalms.translator_note: it is left as printed. The abbreviation ול"נ is not resolved and is left as printed. The grammatical discussion is translated literally. In Jeremiah 12:9 Rashi quotes *hetayu le'ochlah* (JPS: “Bring them to devour”).

Psalms.english_translation: That is prepared to fall on people.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: They only devise to thrust him down from his height
Psalms.english_translation: Because you are afraid of people, lest he reign and repay your deeds, you plotted to thrust evil against him.
Of each and every one of them — they bless.
And in their thoughts they curse. Selah.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Men of low degree are vanity
Psalms.english_translation: And do not fear them, since the Holy One, blessed be He, is a refuge for us in time of trouble. Selah.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: If they be laid in the balances
Psalms.english_translation: If they come to go up in the scales, and their vanities are equal — that is its plain meaning; and its midrash is concerning the matter of pairs.
Psalms.translator_note: The midrashic reference (*inyan hazugot*) is translated literally and not identified.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: If riches increase, set not your heart thereon
Psalms.english_translation: If you see wicked people whose money prospers and grows, do not set your heart on it.
Money.
It sprouts; an expression of *tenuvah* (produce).

That I heard two from within it. And what are the two? “For strength is Yours,” to repay each man according to his deed; and the second, “for to You, HaShem, is the kindness.” And from which utterance did we hear them? From the second utterance of the Ten Commandments we heard from Him that the Holy One, blessed be He, visits iniquity and keeps kindness, as it is said of it (Exodus 20:5), “visiting the iniquity of the fathers” etc.; therefore I am confident that He will repay good reward to the righteous and retribution to the wicked. This I learned from the *yesod* (foundation) of Rabbi Moshe the Preacher; and our Rabbis expounded it: “Remember” and “Keep” were said in one utterance.
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s wording of the two statements differs from the verses (Psalms 62:12 “That strength belongeth unto God”; 62:13 “Also unto Thee, O Lord, belongeth mercy”).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Also unto Thee, O Lord, belongeth mercy
Psalms.english_translation: And what is the mercy? That You repay each man according to his deed — and not his actual deed, but part of it, as in the matter that is said, “seeing that Thou our God hast punished us less than our iniquities deserve” (Ezra 9:13); thus it is expounded in the Aggadah of Psalms. And one can further interpret it: “and to You, HaShem, is kindness,” for You have it in Your power to repay each man according to his deed.
Fleeing from Saul.
I will request and seek You, like “and Thou wilt seek me (*veshiharetani*), but I shall not be” (Job 7:21), “If thou wouldest seek earnestly (*teshacher*) unto God” (Job 8:5).
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s printed quotation of Job 7:21 reads *ve'eineni*; the verse reads *ve'einenu*.

Psalms.english_translation: I thirst and long to come to You in Your house of prayer.
An expression of longing, and it has no parallel.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: In a dry and weary land
Psalms.english_translation: In a wilderness.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: So have I looked for Thee in the sanctuary
Psalms.english_translation: Like: when I thirsted to see Your might and Your glory, in the way that I beheld You in the sanctuary, the Tabernacle of Shiloh — “my soul is satisfied with the sights of Your might and Your glory.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: So will I bless Thee as long as I live
Psalms.english_translation: Like *az*; *ki az* we translate *uvekhen*; that is: then, when I come before You, I will bless You all the days of my life.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: In Thy name will I lift up my hands
Psalms.english_translation: To pray and to praise.
Languages of joyful songs, like “And the whole earth was of one language” (Genesis 11:1), which is translated *lishna chad*.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: When I remember Thee upon my couch
Psalms.english_translation: When I lie on my bed, I remember Your love.
The night.
I think of You.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thy right hand holdeth me fast
Psalms.english_translation: That I not fall.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: But those that seek my soul
Psalms.english_translation: My enemies.
They come upon me in ambush on a dark day, so that I will not sense them.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Shall go into the nethermost parts of the earth
Psalms.english_translation: In a low place, Sheol and a pit, they will come and fall.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: They shall be hurled to the power of the sword
Psalms.english_translation: They will come upon the pursuers of enemies, and each one of them will be hurled by a sword that will kill him; and this is an abbreviated verse, which did not explain who will hurl them. *Yaguruhu* is an expression of dragging (*girah*), like “poured down a steep place” (Micah 1:4), “He breaketh open a shaft (*paratz nachal*) from the inhabitant (*me'im gar*)” (Job 28:4).
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s wording of Job 28:4 differs from JPS (“He breaketh open a shaft away from where men sojourn”).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: They shall be a portion for foxes
Psalms.english_translation: (I found: “a portion for foxes.” “A sword will return them; foxes will walk in it.”)
Psalms.translator_note: The source gives this comment with no lemma; a phrase from the verse is used. The words are translated literally and their sense is not clear. The parenthesis is a later printed insertion.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: But the king shall rejoice in God
Psalms.english_translation: He was speaking of himself, for he had already been anointed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Every one that sweareth by Him shall glory
Psalms.english_translation: When they see that You will save me, all who cling to You and swear by Your name will praise and glory.
*Yisakher* — it will be stopped, like “and all the fountains of the great deep were stopped” (Genesis 8:2).
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s wording differs from JPS (“the fountains also of the deep and the windows of heaven were stopped”).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Hear my voice, O God, in my complaint
Psalms.english_translation: The masters of the Aggadah of Psalms expounded this psalm on Daniel, who was thrown into the lions’ den, and the whole language of the psalm fits the aggadah well; David foresaw by the holy spirit all that would happen to him and prayed for him, since Daniel was of his seed, as was said to Hezekiah (Isaiah 39:7), “And of thy sons that shall issue from thee, whom thou shalt beget, shall they take away; and they shall be officers in the palace of the king of Babylon” — these are Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: from the terror of the enemy
Psalms.english_translation: These are the satraps who took counsel against him, as it is said (Daniel 6:5), “Then the presidents and the satraps sought to find occasion against Daniel.”
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi quotes the Aramaic of Daniel 6:5; the JPS English is given.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: From the tumult of the workers of iniquity
Psalms.english_translation: For they are agitated to seek deadly pretexts against me, as it is written, “They came tumultuously to the king” etc. (ibid.).
Psalms.translator_note: The quotation is Daniel 6:7 in Aramaic; the JPS English is given.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: have aimed their arrow, a poisoned word
Psalms.english_translation: It is their evil tongue.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: That they may shoot in secret places at the blameless
Psalms.english_translation: They shoot him with their arrows.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: They converse of laying snares secretly
Psalms.english_translation: They speak to the king with cunning, hidden words, so that even the king did not understand why they were doing so; and they intended to lay snares for Daniel, to be caught in them, for they said to Darius, “All the presidents of the kingdom ... have consulted together that the king should establish a statute” etc. (ibid.), that no one should pray his prayer before any god except you for thirty days.
Psalms.translator_note: The quotation is Daniel 6:8 in Aramaic; the JPS English is given.

Psalms.english_translation: They seek pretexts, as it is said (ibid.), “They sought to find occasion against Daniel.”
Psalms.translator_note: The quotation is Daniel 6:5 in Aramaic.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: they have accomplished a diligent search
Psalms.english_translation: In their hearts, and they did not reveal their intent — the search of the pretext that was searched out by them, and the inward part of their thoughts, the depth of their heart.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed Hebrew is elliptical and is translated literally.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Even in the inward thought of every one
Psalms.english_translation: Each and every one of them hid his thought.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: But God doth shoot at them with an arrow suddenly
Psalms.english_translation: He shot them into the lions’ den, as it is written (ibid.), “And the king commanded, and they brought those men that had accused Daniel, and they cast them into the den of lions” etc.
Psalms.translator_note: The quotation is Daniel 6:25 in Aramaic; the JPS English is given.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: make their own tongue a stumbling unto themselves
Psalms.english_translation: The stumbling by which they thought to make him stumble was turned against them: their tongue.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: All that see them shake the head
Psalms.english_translation: *Yitnoddedu* — with their head, to move the head and to laugh at them, whoever sees them.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The righteous shall be glad in the LORD
Psalms.english_translation: Daniel.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: all the upright in heart shall glory
Psalms.english_translation: They will glory in the uprightness of their heart and praise themselves, for they are confident that the Holy One, blessed be He, is helping them.
Silence is praise to You, because there is no end to Your praise, and one who multiplies praise only diminishes it.

God who dwells in Zion. (I found: “Make His praise glorious” (Psalms 66:2) — not more than enough, but “silence is praise”; and it seems: praise Him with awe, in the expression *Halleluyah*, a name of two letters, translated *dachila*; “my strength and song” (below, 118), and “the hand upon the throne of the LORD” (Exodus 17:16); and the expression “and rejoice with trembling” is similar to this.) Another explanation: “To You silence is praise, O God in Zion”: that You were silent and still about what Your enemies did in Zion — it was praise to You, for the ability was in Your hand to take vengeance, and You are long-suffering.
Psalms.translator_note: The parenthetical passage is a later printed insertion; it is translated literally and its sense is not clear. The Aramaic is translated as printed. Rashi’s partial quotation of Psalms 118:14 is “*ozi vezimrat Yah*”; in Exodus 17:16 the words are *yad al kes Yah*.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The tale of iniquities is too heavy for me
Psalms.english_translation: And we cannot manage to arrange them all before You, because they are many; rather, in one general statement we pray before You: that our transgressions — You will atone them.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Happy is the man whom Thou choosest
Psalms.english_translation: He whom You choose and bring near, who shall dwell in Your courts.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: May we be satisfied with the goodness of Thy house
Psalms.english_translation: [The goodness] that is in Your house and from the holiness of Your temple, because Your Presence dwells there.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: With wondrous works dost Thou answer us in righteousness
Psalms.english_translation: In Your righteousness You answer us, to perform awesome deeds among the nations.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou the confidence of all the ends of the earth
Psalms.english_translation: [A confidence] — You, and a refuge for all who dwell at the ends of the earth, from the end of the earth to its other end.
Even to the far ones of the seas You are a confidence, for Your dominion is everywhere.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Who by Thy strength settest fast the mountains
Psalms.english_translation: He makes the mountains, which are hard, sprout by His strength, and arranges and prepares foods in them, and prepares rain, as it is written (below, 147), “Who prepareth rain for the earth, Who maketh the mountains to spring with grass.”
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “below, 147” is Psalms 147:8.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Who art girded about with might
Psalms.english_translation: Because he came to mention the might of the rains, he said “girded about with might.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Who stillest the roaring of the seas
Psalms.english_translation: *Mashbiach* — lowers; and so “but a wise man stilleth it (*yeshabbechenah*) within him” (Proverbs 29:11), “When the waves thereof arise, Thou stillest them” (below, Psalms 89:10).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “Proverbs 29” is Proverbs 29:11 and “below, 89” is Psalms 89:10.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou makest the outgoings of the morning and evening to rejoice
Psalms.english_translation: To You the creatures, the dwellers at the ends, in the morning say, “Blessed is He who forms the luminaries,” and in the evening, “Blessed is He who brings on the evenings.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou hast remembered the earth, and watered her
Psalms.english_translation: When You desire to do good, You remember the earth and water it.
You greatly enrich it from Your channel, which is full of water, and You prepare with it the grain of those who dwell at the ends, for thus You prepare them.
They are the rows of the plough.
Like *lirvoh*.
Like “to settle its furrows (*lenachat gedudeha*)”: to let its furrows rest, to make comfort for the creatures; You make it soft with showers of rain.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou makest her soft with showers
Psalms.english_translation: An expression of melting.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou crownest the year with Thy goodness
Psalms.english_translation: Through the rains You crown the year with all good, since You desire to do good.
They are the heavens, which are the dust of Your feet.
They will drip.
Fat.
The heavens, upon the pastures of the wilderness.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The meadows are clothed with flocks
Psalms.english_translation: The Sharon and the plain will be clothed with the flocks that come to graze the grass that the rain caused to sprout.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The valleys also are covered over with corn
Psalms.english_translation: Through the rain the valleys will be wrapped in grain, and then the creatures will shout a shout of joy and sing from the abundance of blessing.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Sing praises unto the glory of His name
Psalms.english_translation: Sing with the glory of His name; א"נ tell the glory of His name in song and singing.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed abbreviation א"נ is not resolved and is left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: Each one of Your works.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Through the greatness of Thy power
Psalms.english_translation: When You show Your might to the world through pestilence or sword or famine or lightning.
The wicked, from much fear, confess the lies and transgressions in their hands. (Until here, התוס'.)
Psalms.translator_note: The printed ע"כ התוס' is not resolved and is left as printed; the parenthesis is a later printed insertion.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He is terrible in His doing toward the children of men
Psalms.english_translation: To be feared over people, lest a transgression be found in them, for all their deeds are revealed to You.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He turned the sea into dry land
Psalms.english_translation: The Red Sea.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: There let us rejoice in Him
Psalms.english_translation: I found: “there” was a thing in which we rejoiced — that is, that the sea saw the Holy One, blessed be He.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Let not the rebellious exalt themselves
Psalms.english_translation: Let their hand not be exalted.
For His wonders, that He sets our soul in life in exile, and you cannot destroy us.
In trouble, in exile.
To remove the dross from us, so that we return in repentance before You, as one refines silver to remove the dross from it.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou didst bring us into the hold
Psalms.english_translation: In a narrow place, as in prison.
*Mu'akah* — an expression of confinement (*misgar*), and all that presses and oppresses is like it.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou hast caused men to ride over our heads
Psalms.english_translation: The kings of every nation.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I will come into Thy house with burnt-offerings
Psalms.english_translation: When You build the Temple, our vows that we vowed in exile will be paid.
*Mechim* — fat ones; an expression of marrow (*moach*).
These are the proselytes who will convert.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I cried unto Him with my mouth
Psalms.english_translation: When we were in exile, we called Him and told of His exaltedness with our tongue.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He was extolled with my tongue
Psalms.english_translation: *Verom* — like *venitromem*. I found on “I cried unto Him with my mouth, and He was extolled”: there the word of His exaltedness is prepared under my tongue to bring it out with the mouth, like “Though he hide it under his tongue” (Job 20:12).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: If I had regarded iniquity in my heart
Psalms.english_translation: He did not deal with us according to our sins; He dealt with us as one who does not see and does not hear the iniquity that is in our heart.
*Akhen* — truly; it is to be known.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Who hath not turned away my prayer
Psalms.english_translation: From before Him, and His kindness He did not remove from me.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: May He cause His face to shine toward us
Psalms.english_translation: To show a smiling face, to give dew and rain.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: That Thy way may be known upon earth
Psalms.english_translation: To make known that Your attribute is to do good to Your people, and for this the nations will thank You and rejoice and sing.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: For Thou wilt judge the peoples with equity
Psalms.english_translation: For acquittal.
*Tanchem* — You guide them in the path of equity, and for this all the peoples thank You.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The earth hath yielded her increase
Psalms.english_translation: And also to the earth that gave its produce, and because the Name will bless us. (סא"א)
Psalms.translator_note: it is left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: let all the ends of the earth fear Him
Psalms.english_translation: So that they will say: See these who feared the Name, how He blessed them and made them great.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Let God arise, let His enemies be scattered
Psalms.english_translation: Amalek and the like.
*Kehinnadef* — like *kehitnadef*: as the smoke is driven away, so drive them away.
From before the Ark in the days of Moses; and when it rested he said, “Return, O LORD” etc. (Numbers 10:36).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Yea, let them rejoice with gladness
Psalms.english_translation: And this is the rejoicing; and so they will say, “Sing unto God” etc.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Extol Him that rideth upon the skies
Psalms.english_translation: *Solu* — an expression of praise; and so “It cannot be valued with the gold of Ophir” (Job 28:16), “Comparable to fine gold” (Lamentations 4:2).
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s Hebrew in the two citations is *lo tisaleh bechetem* and *hamesulaim befaz*.

Psalms.english_translation: *Beyah shemo* — by the name Yah, which is an expression of fear (awe), as we translate it: *dachila*; “my strength and song, Yah” (below, 118), and so “for the hand upon the throne of Yah” (Exodus 17:16) in the Targum, and so “for in Yah, HaShem” (Isaiah 26:4): “For then you will be redeemed by the word of the Awesome One, HaShem, and the Strong One of the world.” The psalmist says: praise before Him and be afraid of Him and rejoice; and this is like what is said in another place, “and rejoice with trembling” (above, Psalms 2:11).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “below, 118” is Psalms 118:14 and “above, 2” is Psalms 2:11. The Targum quotation is of Isaiah 26:4; the JPS English there is “For the LORD is GOD, an everlasting Rock.”

Psalms.english_translation: This is the praise with which you should praise before Him — the whole matter until the end of the psalm.
That He became a father to Israel, who are orphans, as it is said, “We are become orphans and fatherless” (Lamentations 5:3).
That He executed the judgment of Jerusalem, of which it is said, “How is she become as a widow!” (ibid. 1).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “ibid. 1” is Lamentations 1:1.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: God maketh the solitary to dwell in a house
Psalms.english_translation: Israel, who were scattered — He gathered them together, each from his dispersion, and settled them in a whole house and a complete congregation.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He bringeth out the prisoners into prosperity
Psalms.english_translation: He brought Israel out of Egypt in a month that is fit for those who travel on the road — neither hot nor cold.
Egypt.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: dwell but in a parched land
Psalms.english_translation: And their land remained dry and thirsty. (I found.)

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: when Thou wentest forth before Thy people
Psalms.english_translation: *Betze'dekha* — when You stepped Your step, Your own step.
There You showed me this: Your way forever — for every trouble, redemption.
It too trembled before HaShem, the God of Israel.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: A bounteous rain didst Thou pour down, O God
Psalms.english_translation: Further, this You did for us: when we needed rains, You shook down and cast upon us always rains of free-will and blessing.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: When Thine inheritance was weary, Thou didst confirm it
Psalms.english_translation: When the inheritance of Your land was weary and thirsty for rain, You established it. (I found:) “Your inheritance and it was weary” — that which is called Your inheritance and it is weary; that is, sometimes it is so.

Your congregation dwelt in it, like “And the Philistines gathered their camps into a troop (*lechayah*)” (2 Samuel 23:11). Another explanation: *chayyatekha* — the Community of Israel is called the animal and beast of the Holy One, blessed be He.
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s wording of 2 Samuel 23:11 differs from JPS (“And the Philistines were gathered together into a troop”).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou didst prepare in Thy goodness for the poor
Psalms.english_translation: When they went out from Egypt, You turned them around in the wilderness for forty years, because the Canaanites arose and cut down the trees, and in the meantime that they were delayed in the wilderness, they arose and repaired everything.
He utters an utterance. Further, He will roar with a voice to cause the hosts of the many nations to hear. And what is the utterance?
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s lemma also includes the words “The women that proclaim the tidings” (*hamevasserot*).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Kings of armies flee, they flee
Psalms.english_translation: They will wander and be thrown out from within the Land of Israel; and the Community of Israel, which is the dweller of the house (*navat bayit*), will divide their spoil, as it is said, “And her gain and her hire shall be holiness to the LORD” etc. (Isaiah 23:18).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: When you lie among the sheepfolds
Psalms.english_translation: All this that the speaker says, he will say to them: If you have lain between your borders and delighted in delights — this is my dove, my congregation: “her wings are covered with silver.” And what is the silver and the gold? “When the Almighty scattereth” etc.: when the Holy One, blessed be He, spread out before them His Torah, in which kings are made white as snow (*nishlagim*) and are whitened, in a land of shadow of death and darkness — then her wings (the wings of a dove) were covered with its silver; and the desirability of the Torah and the commandments are the wings of a dove. *פלומ"א* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 68:14 (“feathers”), in forms such as פלובויש, פלומש, פלומייש, פולמייט, פלומט, פלמייש; the printed form (פלומ"א) is a variant spelling. The words “(the wings of a dove)” are a later printed insertion.

Psalms.english_translation: Her wings, with which she flies.

Dunash ben Labrat explained: the *charutz* is gold, and therefore the psalmist placed it next to the silver; and *yeraqraq charutz* is the gold that is brought from the land of Havilah and the land of Cush, very, very good gold, which is neither green nor red, and therefore he called it *yeraqraq*, like “reddish-white” (Leviticus 13:42), which is neither white nor red; therefore *yeraqraq* and *adamdam* are doubled.
*Befares* — an expression of “And they shall spread the garment” (Deuteronomy 22:17): they sort out the matter like a new garment.
These are Torah scholars, as it is said, “By me kings reign” (Proverbs 8:15).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: A mountain of God is the mountain of Bashan
Psalms.english_translation: And where did He expound it? On Mount Sinai, which is the mountain of God, close to Bashan across the Jordan.
The mountain that is singled out among the mountains.
*Gavnunim* — an expression of mountains, because of their height, like “that thou hast built unto thee an eminent place (*gav*)” (Ezekiel 16:24); anything high is called *gav*.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Why look you askance, you mountains of peaks
Psalms.english_translation: All this refers back to “The Lord giveth the word” (Psalms 68:12) — He will further say to them: “Why do you lie in wait (*tirtzedun*), you mountains of peaks” — why do you ambush, you high mountains, to destroy the mountain that God desired for His abode, to rest His Presence upon it? It is the Temple Mount. “Yea, the LORD will dwell therein for ever” — His holiness is an eternal holiness; since it was chosen for His abode, the Presence did not rest in another place. I saw in the *yesod* (foundation) of Rabbi Moshe the Preacher that *ratzad* is “ambush” in the Arabic language; but Menachem explained *tirtzedun* like *tirkedun* (you dance); that expression too falls upon this line of interpretation.
Psalms.translator_note: Printed reference is to the words “The Lord giveth the word” (*Adonai yiten omer*), Psalms 68:12.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The chariots of God are myriads
Psalms.english_translation: Again, this refers back to “The Lord giveth the word”: to mention the love for His people, even when “the chariots of God” were revealed — myriads of thousands, *shin'an* — sharp, keen angels — and HaShem was among them at Sinai in holiness; there too.
You, the leader of His people, Moses son of Amram, [ascended] on high, took the Torah captive, and took gifts from the upper beings to give to human beings.
Further, you caused the Holy One, blessed be He, to dwell in the Tabernacle among a people who were stubborn and rebellious and provoked Him to anger.
This is from the song mentioned above, “Sing unto God.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: day by day He beareth our burden
Psalms.english_translation: He gives us abundant salvation from every burden, as much as we can bear. (I found: “day by day He beareth our burden” — all the days He thus acts with us: for every trouble, salvation.)
Psalms.translator_note: The passage in parentheses is a later printed insertion.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: God is unto us a God of deliverances
Psalms.english_translation: A saving God is He to us, and before Him are many issues of manners of death, issues of ways to death; but not upon us does He give them; rather, with them He will smite the head of His enemies.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The hairy scalp of him that goeth about in his guiltiness
Psalms.english_translation: The head of Esau, who is a hairy man, who walks always in his guilt (and does not return from his evil).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I will bring back from Bashan
Psalms.english_translation: For thus He promised to bring us back from among the mighty ones of Bashan and from the isles of the sea.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: That thy foot may wade through blood
Psalms.english_translation: That our foot may wade in blood: when He smites the head of the enemy, our foot will cleave through their blood. *Timchatz* is an expression of cleaving through the midst of the blood, like “*machatzah vechalfah rakkato*” (Judges 5), which is like “she cleaved” (*bake'ah*); and it is a Mishnaic expression: “and the pilgrims were cleaving up to their knees in blood.” Another explanation: *timchatz* is the name of a vessel with which they draw wine from the pit; *machatz* is its name in tractate ע"ג.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed abbreviation ע"ג is not resolved and is left as printed. The Judges citation is 5:26 (JPS: “she smote through his head, Yea, she pierced and struck through his temples”); the Mishnaic quotation was not identified.

Psalms.english_translation: From the blood of the enemies.
*Minehu* — it will be his sustenance, as we say, “From where is it implied that *man* is an expression of sustenance? For it is written (Daniel 1:10), ‘who hath appointed your food’” etc.
Psalms.translator_note: The quotation is Daniel 1:10 (JPS: “who hath appointed your food and your drink”).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: They see Thy goings, O God
Psalms.english_translation: That is: it is fitting for You to save these; for when they saw Your goings in Your holiness at the sea, the singers went first to sing before You the Song of the Sea, and after them came the minstrels — these are the angels.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: In the midst of damsels playing upon timbrels
Psalms.english_translation: In the midst of Miriam and her maidens, who took the timbrel in her hand, and said in their praise.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Bless you God in full assemblies
Psalms.english_translation: Even embryos in their mothers’ wombs said song.
The youngest became ruler over them.

Like *rodam* with a kamatz; from there he merited to be king, because he went down first into the sea; and so Samuel said to Saul (1 Samuel 15:17), “Though thou be little in thine own sight, art thou not head of the tribes of Israel?” and Jonathan translated it: “The tribe of Benjamin crossed the sea at the head of all the other tribes.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The princes of Judah their council
Psalms.english_translation: They are jealous of them and throw stones at them; and so “the princes of Zebulun and Naphtali”; and so he said to him, “Thy God hath commanded thy strength.” (סא"א) Another explanation: (*rigmatam* — their embroidery; their garments, etc.) *Rikmatam* is an expression of purple (*argaman*); so Menachem connected it.
Psalms.translator_note: it is left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thy God hath commanded thy strength
Psalms.english_translation: Now the psalmist returns to his prayer, in which he prayed “Let God arise, let His enemies be scattered”: “Be strong, O God, and prevail — You who have wrought all these for us.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Out of Thy temple at Jerusalem
Psalms.english_translation: And from what the kings will see of the glory of Your temple, which is at Jerusalem, they will bring You tribute and a present.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Rebuke the wild beast of the reeds
Psalms.english_translation: This is Amalek, who is compared to a beast of the forest dwelling among the reeds.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The multitude of the bulls, with the calves of the peoples
Psalms.english_translation: A people who grew fat and sleek, *kefirim avirim* among the rest of the nations, who are only like calves in comparison with them.
Psalms.translator_note: The words *kefirim avirim* are left transliterated; the opening clause is translated literally.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Every one submitting himself with pieces of silver
Psalms.english_translation: They are not appeased by any person unless one appeases them with money.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He hath scattered the peoples that delight in war
Psalms.english_translation: Scatter the tribes — as is said, “Yea, He loveth the peoples” (Deuteronomy 33:3) — and “they delight in wars” always: they desire to fight us.
Psalms.translator_note: The connection of the quotation from Deuteronomy 33:3 to the first clause is not clear to me; the passage is translated literally.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Nobles shall come out of Egypt
Psalms.english_translation: And then, when You destroy Amalek and the King Messiah arises, they will bring You tribute from Egypt and from Cush. And Menachem explained *chashmanim* as the name of a province, the inhabitants of Chashmonah; and the interpreters interpret it as an expression of tribute.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Sing unto God, you kingdoms of the earth
Psalms.english_translation: For He showed them His greatness and redeemed His people.
*Hen yiten* — behold, He gives.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Awful is God out of thy holy places
Psalms.english_translation: From what You destroyed, He is to be feared: if toward His sanctuary He showed no favour, all the more so toward the wicked. And an aggadic midrash: do not read *mimikdashekha* but *mimekudashekha* (“from those sanctified to You”), for when the Holy One, blessed be He, executes judgment on the righteous, He is feared and exalted and praised, and so He says, “Through them that are nigh unto Me I will be sanctified” (Leviticus 10:3) and “and it shall be sanctified by My glory” (Exodus 29:43) — at the death of the two sons of Aaron. And our Rabbis expounded the whole psalm until “Blessed be the Lord, day by day” as concerning the giving of the Torah, and “a bounteous rain” at the giving of the Torah, and “Thy flock settled therein”; but my heart is not settled to affirm the expression “settled therein” as “they settled in the Torah”; and “the mountain which God hath desired for His abode” cannot be expounded of Mount Sinai, for He did not desire it for His abode nor to dwell on it forever, and here it is written “will dwell for ever”; and likewise they explained “kings of armies” like “angels of armies,” but this is not the language of Scripture.
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “Leviticus 10” is 10:3 and “Exodus 29” is 29:43. The expression “Blessed be the Lord, day by day” is Psalms 68:20.

Psalms.english_translation: Concerning Israel, who are like a lily among the thorns, for the thorns pierce them; and he prayed for them.
The nations.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I am sunk in deep mire
Psalms.english_translation: In the mud, the clay of the depth.
*Shibboleth* — the rush, the strength of the river; *פי"ל* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 69:3 (“current, thread of the water”), in forms such as פיל, פול, פלגס; the printed form (פי"ל) matches.

Psalms.english_translation: *Nachar* — dried, like “my bones are burned with heat” (Job 30:30).
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s Hebrew is *charah mini choreb*.

Psalms.english_translation: Any prolonged hope is called failing of the eyes, as in “and fail with longing for them all the day” (Deuteronomy 28:32), “that shall make the eyes to fail” (Leviticus 26:16), “But the eyes of the wicked shall fail” (Job 11:20).
They hate me falsely, for I do not pursue their falsehood to seize their error.
When they gather against me, I bribe them with money — what I did not rob from them.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Let not them that wait for Thee be ashamed through me
Psalms.english_translation: Do not leave me in their hand, lest those who wait for You be ashamed over what happens to me and say, “Did not just this happen to one who hoped in the Holy One, blessed be He?”
To Esau.
They saw the love You showed toward us while Your house stood, and became jealous of me.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I wept with my soul with fasting
Psalms.english_translation: In my fast.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: that became unto me a reproach
Psalms.english_translation: Because I weep and fast before You, they mock me.
*Neginot* — in me, for the drinkers of strong drink. (סא"א)
Psalms.translator_note: it is left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: let my prayer be unto Thee
Psalms.english_translation: May the time of my prayer be a time of favour.
And do not close upon me.
*Be'er* — a foreign trouble, this [one, opens] its mouth to swallow me.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed Hebrew is elliptical and is translated literally.

Psalms.english_translation: *Ta'tar* — like “*itter yad yemino*” (Judges 3:15): closed of his right hand, so that he does not use it.
Psalms.translator_note: JPS Judges 3:15 reads “a man left-handed.”

Psalms.english_translation: (Draw near to me.)
Redeem it.

*Va'anushah* — and I am sick and ill, like “For her wound is incurable (*anushah*)” (Micah 1:9) and like “and the child fell sick (*vaye'anash*), the child of Bathsheba” (2 Samuel 12). And if you say: how does this aleph serve as a root letter and also serve a use that turns the speech to the speaker? So is the way of a word that begins with an aleph, such as “Yet I loved Jacob” (Malachi 1:2), “I love them that love me” (Proverbs 8:17), which is like *ve'e'ehav*; and so “I will utterly consume” (Zephaniah 1:2) is like *e'esof*.
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s Hebrew in 2 Samuel 12 is *vaye'anash*; JPS 2 Samuel 12:15 reads “and it was very sick.” The citation of Malachi is 1:2 and of Proverbs 8:17.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I looked for some to show compassion
Psalms.english_translation: That friends should come to condole with me and comfort me.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: they put poison into my food
Psalms.english_translation: *Bivrutī* — in my meal, like “Let Tamar my sister come, and I will eat (*ve'evrei*) of her hand” (2 Samuel 13:5).
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s wording of 2 Samuel 13:5 differs from JPS.

Psalms.english_translation: Bitterness (*marah*).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: when they are in peace, let it become a trap
Psalms.english_translation: When they hope for peace, let their peace turn into a snare.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: For they persecute him whom Thou hast smitten
Psalms.english_translation: This people whom You smote.
You were angry a little, and they helped toward evil.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: the pain of those whom Thou hast wounded
Psalms.english_translation: Their words — to come in counsel to destroy us while we are in pain.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: it shall please the LORD better
Psalms.english_translation: My praise to HaShem.

It is the ox that the first man offered, who was created in his full stature; and on the day that the ox was called *shor*, on that day he brought it, for an ox of one day is called *shor*, as it is said, “When a bullock (*shor*), or a sheep, or a goat, is brought forth” (Leviticus 22:27); on that day it was made to resemble a *par*, which is three years old.

His horns preceded his hooves, for he was created in his full stature and with his horns, and his head came out of the earth first, as is the way of all that are born; the earth brought them out; it is found that his horns preceded his feet.

It is an expression of prayer, like “but we will make mention (*nazkir*) of the name of the LORD our God” (above, Psalms 20:8), and so in Chronicles, “to make memorial and to give thanks to the LORD.” And in the Midrash on Psalms I saw a parable: a king was angry at his flock, and tore down the pen and drove out the flock and the shepherd. After a time, he returned the flock and rebuilt the pen, and did not mention the shepherd. The shepherd said, “Behold, the flock is returned and the pen is built, and I am not remembered.” So, earlier in the matter it is said, “For God will save Zion” etc. “and they that love His name shall dwell therein” (Psalms 69:36–37) — behold, the pen is built and the flock gathered, and the shepherd (this is David) is not mentioned; therefore it is said, “of David, to make memorial” — to mention God, to save me.
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s wording of the quotation from Chronicles (*lehazkir ulehodot laShem*) differs from JPS (“to celebrate and to thank”). The words “(this is David)” are a later printed insertion.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Let them be turned back by reason of their shame
Psalms.english_translation: Measure for measure, as they did to me.
In that very track — *anséstraces* [printed אנציש"טראציש] in French (“in these tracks”).
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 70:4 (“on their tracks”), in forms such as אנשישטרצט, אינטישטריצט, אינשישטרצט, אנאיששטרצייט, אנאישישטרציש; the transcription is *anséstraces* (REJ, from Darmesteter’s first manuscript); the printed form (אנציש"טראציש) is a variant spelling.

Psalms.english_translation: Against me.
An expression of joy on seeing his enemy [as he wishes].
Psalms.translator_note: The words “as he wishes” render the printed *kirtzono*.

Psalms.english_translation: To help.
In that very dwelling, to be saved within it from the pursuer.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Which Thou hast appointed to save me
Psalms.english_translation: Many times You saved me through Your messengers.
Like *chomes*; and so “relieve the oppressed (*ashru chamotz*)” (Isaiah 1:17) — one who is robbed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou art he that took me out of my mother’s womb
Psalms.english_translation: *Attah gozi* — You are the one who brings me out and removes me, like “and brought across quails (*vayagoz*)” (Numbers 11:31), “for it is speedily gone (*gaz*), and we fly away” (below, Psalms 90:10).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “below, 90” is Psalms 90:10.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I am as a wonder unto many
Psalms.english_translation: Many saw my troubles and worried lest a trouble like mine befall them: lest I be a sign for them — as it happened to this one, so will it happen to us — as in the matter that is said (Ezekiel 24:24), “Thus shall Ezekiel be unto you a sign.”
Psalms.translator_note: The reference is printed as “Ezekiel 24”.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: in the time of old age
Psalms.english_translation: If I have grown old in sins — that is, I have sinned much.
My enemies spoke about me, and took counsel together, saying, “God has forsaken him; we shall not be punished for him, for he already stumbled in sin.”
For Your salvation; and when You save me, I will add to Your praise.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: For I know not the numbers thereof
Psalms.english_translation: Of the righteous acts and the salvations that You wrought with me.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I will come with Thy mighty acts
Psalms.english_translation: To thank and to praise for Your might.
Until today, for what has passed over me.
When I reach sixty and seventy, forsake me not. (סא"א)
Psalms.translator_note: it is left as printed. Rashi’s lemma is *ve'ad zikenah vesevah*, which is in Psalms 71:18; a phrase from 71:17 is used as the lemma.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: to every one that is to come
Psalms.english_translation: To everyone who comes to me, I will declare Your mighty acts.
Which reaches to the heights; the two verses are connected with “I will declare Thy arm to the generation.”
With the music of the sound of the harp, when I sing to You with the harp.
He prayed this prayer for his son Solomon, for he foresaw by the holy spirit that he was destined to ask of the Holy One, blessed be He, “a heart to understand to hear judgment.”
The wisdom of Your judgment, which You commanded in the Torah.
To justify the judgment.
Both are said of Solomon. Another explanation: “Thy judgments give to the king” — let the afflictions be consumed in me — “and Thy righteousness” do for my son, that there may be peace in his days.
In his days.
And what is the peace that the mountains bear? When they yield fruit, the eye of the people is not narrow, and each one calls to his neighbour, “Under the vine and under the fig-tree.”
Psalms.translator_note: Compare Zechariah 3:10 (JPS: “shall you call every man his neighbour under the vine and under the fig-tree”); Rashi gives no reference.

Psalms.english_translation: And the hills will bear peace for them through the righteousness that they will do.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: They shall fear Thee while the sun endureth
Psalms.english_translation: From me Israel will learn to fear You all the days of the sun and the moon, for generations.
While the moon is still standing and they are before it; and there are many such in the language of the Mishnah: “in the presence of the Temple and not in the presence of the Temple.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: May he come down like rain upon the mown grass
Psalms.english_translation: His word will come down among Your people and in their hearts like rain falling on the greenery of the mown grass, which needs rains after it is mown, as in the matter that is said (Amos 7:1), “and, lo, it was the latter growth after the king’s mowings.”
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s Hebrew is *vehineh lekesh achar gizzei hamelekh*.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: As showers that water the earth
Psalms.english_translation: *Zarzif* — an expression of drops; it is in the Aramaic language, in tractate Yoma: *hu matu zarzifei demaya*.
Psalms.translator_note: The Aramaic is translated as printed. The Talmudic quotation is left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: Israel.

Let [Israel] flourish in his days, and let this peace be long, forever; and this whole prayer was fulfilled except for this matter, for Solomon sinned, therefore his kingdom was not prolonged, for the kingdom was given to David on condition, “if thy children will keep My way” (another version: their way); and Israel flourished in his days, as it is said (1 Kings 4:20), “Judah and Israel were many, as the sand” etc., and abundance of peace there was, as it is said, “And Judah and Israel dwelt safely, every man under his vine” (1 Kings 5:5) all the days of Solomon.
Psalms.translator_note: The reference “1 Kings 4:20” is a later printed insertion; the second quotation, which Rashi gives without a reference, is 1 Kings 5:5.

Psalms.english_translation: The whole Land of Israel, from the Red Sea to the Sea of the Philistines.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: from the River unto the ends of the earth
Psalms.english_translation: For he rules over everything across the River etc. (ibid.).
Psalms.translator_note: The quotation is 1 Kings 5:4 (JPS: “For he had dominion over all the region on this side the River”).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Let them that dwell in the wilderness bow before him
Psalms.english_translation: *Tziyim* — companies of princes, as it is translated, “and ships from the hand of Kittim” (Numbers 24:24): *vesi'an yistachran miRomai*.
Psalms.translator_note: The Aramaic is translated as printed. Rashi’s Hebrew is *vetzim miyad Kittim*; JPS Numbers 24:24 reads “ships shall come from the coast of Kittim.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The kings of Tarshish and of the isles shall render tribute
Psalms.english_translation: For “the king had at sea a navy of Tarshish with the navy of Hiram; once every three years came the navy of Tarshish” etc. (1 Kings 10:22).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The kings of Sheba and Seba
Psalms.english_translation: The queen of Sheba.
A gift (*doron*).
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s lemma is *eshkar*.

Psalms.english_translation: And all the earth bring a present to Solomon, and they bring each man his present (ibid. 4).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “ibid. 4” gives no verse; the words “every man his present” are in 1 Kings 10:25 (JPS: “And they brought every man his present”).

Psalms.english_translation: From blows and from robbery. I found *mitokh* as an expression of *tokh*, *tokhot*: schemers, ploughers of iniquity, like “*ish tekhakhim*” (Proverbs 28).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “Proverbs 28”; the words *ish tekhakhim* are in Proverbs 29:13 (JPS: “the oppressor”).

Psalms.english_translation: Through the judgment and righteousness that he will do among them.
Solomon.
The Holy One, blessed be He.
And so it was: “both riches and honour — so that there hath not been any among the kings like unto thee” etc. (1 Kings 3:13).
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s Hebrew is *gam osher gam kavod asher lo hayah kamokha* etc.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: That they may pray for him continually
Psalms.english_translation: The prayer is the blessing: when the Holy One, blessed be He, says to a man, “Blessed shall you be,” it is an expression of prayer.

*Pissat bar* — an expression of *pisayon*: addition and abundance; and our Rabbis explained it as an expression of fine cakes (*gelosqaot*) for the days of the Messiah, and the whole psalm is about the King Messiah. Another explanation: *pissat bar* — an expression of desire, like *paiyes*, for the creatures are appeased and satisfied by the Omnipresent when He gives satiety in the world.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: May his fruit rustle like Lebanon
Psalms.english_translation: Thick wheat grains, like the fruits of the tree, like the kidneys of the large ox that was in the days of Simeon ben Shetach.
Israel.
From within Jerusalem, like grass of the earth.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: May his name endure for ever
Psalms.english_translation: The name of Solomon is remembered forever for his wealth and his wisdom.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: May his name be continued as long as the sun
Psalms.english_translation: All the days of the sun his name will grow.

*Yinnon* — an expression of kingship and rulership, like “and his end shall be a *manon*” (Proverbs 29:21), and for *nini*, the ruler over the property of others, “they said in their heart, *ninam* altogether” (below, Psalms 74:8) — their kings together.
Psalms.translator_note: The phrase *ulenini hashalit al nichsei acherim* is translated literally; its sense is not clear. Printed “below, 74” is Psalms 74:8 (JPS: “Let us make havoc of them altogether”); Rashi reads *ninam* as “their kings.” In Proverbs 29:21 JPS reads “shall have him become master at the last.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: May men also bless themselves by him
Psalms.english_translation: A man says to his son, “Be wise and rich like Solomon.”
He who does great wonders, in the descent of the fire from heaven through Solomon my son.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The prayers of David the son of Jesse are ended
Psalms.english_translation: Our Rabbis expounded “ended”: all these are the prayers of David, to include the whole book under the name of David, and even what the sons of Korah and the ten elders מ"ש, because he is called “the sweet singer of Israel” (2 Samuel 23). And one can explain “ended” as “were concluded,” like *romu me'at* (Job 24:24), *shomu shamayim* (Jeremiah 2:12); and if so, this psalm was not written in its place, and there is no earlier and later in the book, and it appears that it was in his old age, when he made Solomon king, that he said them.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed abbreviation מ"ש is not resolved and is left as printed. The reference printed “Job 24” is 24:24 and “Jeremiah 2” is 2:12; JPS reads “They are exalted for a little while” and “Be astonished, O you heavens.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Surely God is good to Israel
Psalms.english_translation: Because the matter of the psalm speaks of troubles that come upon the servants of the Omnipresent, he opened it thus; and this is its explanation: although I cry out and am astonished at the troubles of Israel, I knew that the Holy One, blessed be He, is good to them, and that for their good He brings the evil upon them, in order to bring them merit for the life of the World to Come.
Before I set this to my heart.
And my steps were poured out, to turn away from after the Omnipresent.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: For I was envious at the arrogant
Psalms.english_translation: At those who confuse their ways, whose peace I used to see.
*Holelim* — those who mix, like “Thy wine mixed with water” (Isaiah 1:22). (סא"א)
Psalms.translator_note: it is left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: For there are no pangs at their death
Psalms.english_translation: *Charzuvot* — an expression of binding, like “to loose the fetters (*charzuvot*) of wickedness” (Isaiah 58:6), the bonds of the shackles of wickedness with which they bind the poor. Here too, there are no sufferings at their death; those among them who die, die healthy, like their *ulam*, without suffering. And our Rabbis explained *charzuvot* as a notarikon: that they do not tremble (*charidim*) and grieve (*atzevin*) over the day of death. Another explanation: that the Holy One, blessed be He, does not delay their *tzivyonam* (meaning their will).
Psalms.translator_note: The clause “die healthy, like their *ulam*” is translated literally (the verse’s *uvari ulam* is JPS “And their body is sound”).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Therefore pride is as a chain about their neck
Psalms.english_translation: Because of this, that no sufferings come upon them, pride adorned them with a necklace, to go up upon their neck: haughtiness.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Violence covereth them as a garment
Psalms.english_translation: The violence that they do makes them fat, and wraps their *shetotehem* and their *agavotehem* in thickness of fat and flesh.
Psalms.translator_note: The words *shetotehem* and *agavotehem* are left transliterated.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Their eyes stand forth from fatness
Psalms.english_translation: Their eyes bulge from much fat; every lean person’s eyes are sunken.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: They are gone beyond the imaginations of their heart
Psalms.english_translation: More than their heart hoped for and awaited, their desire comes to them; they passed, with the attainment of their hand, the desire of their heart.
Their fellows.
To oppress the needy.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: as if there were none on high
Psalms.english_translation: Such as Pharaoh and Sennacherib and Nebuchadnezzar: “Who is the LORD, that I should hearken unto His voice” (Exodus 5:2), “Who are they among all the gods of these countries” (Isaiah 36:20), “I will ascend above the heights of the clouds” (ibid. 14:14) — and this is “they have set their mouth against the heavens” (verse 9).
Psalms.translator_note: The printed abbreviation נ"נ is read Nebuchadnezzar. Rashi’s wording differs from JPS in Isaiah 36:20 and in Psalms 73:9 (“They have set their mouth against the heavens”).

Psalms.english_translation: Because His people see the way of the wicked prosper, they will turn to the way of the wicked, to walk in their ways.
Like “Who brought thee hither?” (Judges 18:3) — *halom* — here.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: waters of fullness are drained out by them
Psalms.english_translation: And the waters of the full stream — these are the words of Torah — are considered by them as dregs (*tamtzit*), and are belittled in their eyes.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: And they say: ‘How doth God know?
Psalms.english_translation: How can we say that there is knowledge in the Holy One, blessed be He, and that His Torah is true?
They transgress His Torah, and behold, they are at ease in the world and increase strength and wealth.
An expression of ease.

*Hisigu* — they magnified; and Menachem explained “Therefore His people return hither” as “the wicked will return to strike (*lehalom*) the people of the Holy One, blessed be He”; and the first I learned from the words of ר"מ son of Isaac, the cantor, of blessed memory.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed abbreviation ר"מ is not resolved and is left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Surely in vain have I cleansed my heart
