Psalms.english_translation: All this refers back to “And they say: How doth God know?” and further they say: “In vain and for nothing we keep the commandments of the Holy One, blessed be He, and behold, we are plagued all the day.”
It appeared all day, always; from morning to morning new troubles were renewed.
Asaph said: If I said in my heart to tell everything as it is, all that the people say about this.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I had been faithless to the generation of Thy children
Psalms.english_translation: That is: I would make them out to be traitors and wicked.
In my heart.
What is the way of the Holy One, blessed be He; “it was wearisome in my eyes” — this attribute appeared to me as toil and not justice.

“Until I came to the sanctuary of God,” which is in Jerusalem, and I saw what happened to Sennacherib, and then I understood the end of the wicked, that it is destruction, and I said: Surely all the good that comes to them is smoothness — that the Holy One, blessed be He, smooths for them their way, so that it is easy and smooth, so that they will not set their heart to return to Him, and they will perish.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Surely Thou settest them in slippery places
Psalms.english_translation: All the good that comes to them, for their end is their being cast down to ruins.
From demons.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: As a dream when one awaketh
Psalms.english_translation: Like a sleep that has no waking, which is the sleep of eternity, so it was for them: “And the angel of the LORD went forth, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians” (Isaiah 37:36).
In Jerusalem, where they did evil against it, there the image of their likeness was despised and all of them were burned.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: For my heart was in a ferment
Psalms.english_translation: Before I saw this downfall by the holy spirit, my heart was fermenting over the way of the wicked that prospered; “and I was pricked in my reins” (*eshtonan*) — an expression of a sharp sword, and when it is reflexive the tav is placed in the middle of the root of the word, as is the way of every word whose root begins with a shin.
I was brutish and did not know what the attribute is; “and I was as a beast before Thee.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Nevertheless I am continually with Thee
Psalms.english_translation: Although I saw all this always, I was with You and did not move from Your fear.
To hold me in Your fear when my feet were close to turning aside from Your way, as he said above, “my feet were almost gone” (verse 2).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou wilt guide me with Thy counsel
Psalms.english_translation: *Tanchenī* — You led me (*nechitani*).

If the accent were on *kavod*, its interpretation would be: after You completed for Sennacherib all the honour that You had decreed for him, You will take him to You — You performed the wonder of Your miracle for Israel and You destroyed Sennacherib. Now that the accent is on *ve'achar*, its interpretation is: and afterwards, to honour You will take me; You drew me to Yourself for honour and for glory.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Whom have I in heaven but Thee
Psalms.english_translation: Any angel that I chose for myself as a god — I chose none but You.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: My flesh and my heart faileth
Psalms.english_translation: My flesh and my heart longed for You.
An expression of longing, like “My soul pineth for Thy salvation” (below, Psalms 119:81).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “below, 119” is Psalms 119:81.

Psalms.english_translation: Separated from You.
*Melachotekha* — Your messages: the holy spirit that comes into my heart to say.
Everyone who is angry — smoke comes out of his nostrils.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: which Thou hast gotten of old
Psalms.english_translation: Before the creation of the world, as it is said (below, 90), “Thou hast been to us a dwelling-place before the mountains were brought forth.”
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s quotation combines Psalms 90:1 (JPS: “Lord, Thou hast been our dwelling-place in all generations”) and the following verse (“Before the mountains were brought forth”).

Psalms.english_translation: It is an adjustment of language, like “He against whom (*zu*) we have sinned” (Isaiah 42:24), and it is like “in which (*asher*) You dwelt.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Lift up Thy steps because of the perpetual ruins
Psalms.english_translation: Raise Your strides and Your terrors, that they be perpetual ruins for Your enemies, for all the evil that the enemy did in the Temple; so Menachem connected it with “and his spirit was troubled (*vatipa'em*).”
*Mashu'ot* — an expression of destruction, like *she'iyah* (ibid. 6), “and the land become utterly waste (*tisha shemamah*)”. (סא"א)
Psalms.translator_note: it is left as printed. The printed reference “ibid. 6” is to Isaiah 6, where JPS 6:11 reads “Until cities be waste ... And the land become utterly waste.” The printed form *she'iyah* is left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: It is the Temple, of which it is said, “And there I will meet with thee” (Exodus 25:22).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: They have set up their own signs for signs
Psalms.english_translation: When their hand grew strong to destroy it, then they set up for themselves the signs of their divinations, which are true signs; and what are the divinations? “He shaketh the arrows to and fro, he inquireth of the teraphim.”
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi gives no reference; the words are in Ezekiel 21:26.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: It seemed as when men wield upwards Axes
Psalms.english_translation: The enemy knew, when he was striking the gates of the doors of the Temple, that it is as if he were bringing his blows up to the firmament; and how did he know? For he saw that the wood tangled and held the axes and swallowed them, as our Rabbis said: “All of them were swallowed up by one gate of Jerusalem.”
Psalms.translator_note: The Rabbis’ saying is quoted in Aramaic.

Psalms.english_translation: An expression of “caught in the thicket” (Genesis 22:13); the wood entangles them, and they are entangled in it.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: And now all the carved work thereof together
Psalms.english_translation: Although he saw that it was hard before the Holy One, blessed be He, he did not refrain from smiting all its doors and all its gates together.

They are destroying tools of carpenters, and “with axes they came to her” — Targum Jonathan: *bechashilya*; *kilapot* is an Arabic expression, so Dunash explained, and it is among the tools of carpenters.
Psalms.translator_note: The Aramaic is translated as printed. The quotation “with axes they came to her” is as printed; Rashi gives no reference.

Psalms.english_translation: The enemies.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Let us make havoc of them altogether
Psalms.english_translation: *Ninam* — their rulers, and so “May his name be continued (*yinnon*)” (above, 72) and “and his end shall be a *manon*” (Proverbs 29:21); all their rulers have one thought, the first as the last: to engage first with the patron of Israel and afterwards to engage with them; and know that they burned all the meeting-places of God that were in the land, all His houses of assembly — the Philistines destroyed Shiloh, Nebuchadnezzar destroyed the First Temple, and others destroyed the Second Temple.
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “above, 72” is Psalms 72:17.

Psalms.english_translation: That You promised us through Your prophet — we do not see them for many days that we are in exile; Asaph prophesied about the days of the exile.
*Ad meh* — until when will we be in this trouble?

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Draw it out of Thy bosom and consume them
Psalms.english_translation: Cast it and take it out from within Your bosom, and fight Your enemies; *kaleh* is an expression of driving out, like “he shall surely thrust you out (*garesh yegaresh*) hence altogether” (Exodus 11:1).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Yet God is my King of old
Psalms.english_translation: And behold, You are our salvation from of old.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou didst shatter the heads of the sea-monsters
Psalms.english_translation: They are Egypt, who are called sea-monsters (*taninim*), as it is said (Ezekiel 29), “the great dragon” etc.
Psalms.translator_note: The reference is printed “Ezekiel 29”; the words are in 29:3.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou didst crush the heads of leviathan
Psalms.english_translation: Pharaoh is called thus, as it is said (Isaiah 27), “the LORD with His sore and great and strong sword will punish leviathan” etc.
Psalms.translator_note: The reference is printed “Isaiah 27”; the words are in 27:1.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou gavest him to be food to the folk
Psalms.english_translation: You gave his wealth to the people of Israel to eat it, to the *tziyim* — to the companies and hosts that You brought out.
Companies, as “and ships from the hand of Kittim” (Numbers 24:24), as in its Targum, *vesi'an*.
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s Hebrew in Numbers 24:24 is *vetzim miyad Kittim*; JPS reads “ships shall come from the coast of Kittim.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou didst cleave fountain and brook
Psalms.english_translation: For Israel, from the rock, springs.
The Jordan, which is an ever-flowing river.
The redemption of Israel.
And Your people were in troubles at night.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou hast established luminary and sun
Psalms.english_translation: You prepared for them the light of the Torah.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou hast set all the borders of the earth
Psalms.english_translation: For them, all the borders of their land, with all good.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou hast made summer and winter
Psalms.english_translation: This is like “The appointed weeks of the harvest He keeps for us” (Jeremiah 5:24) — You did not change for us the order of the years.
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s Hebrew is *shevu'ot chukkot katzir yishmor lanu*.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: how the enemy hath reproached the LORD
Psalms.english_translation: And since all our salvation is in You, remember this: that the enemy reproached You in destroying us.
To the troops of the nations, like “And the Philistines were gathered together into a troop” (2 Samuel 23:11).
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s Hebrew is *vaye'asfu Pelishtim lechayah*.

Psalms.english_translation: Your turtle-dove; and Targum Jonathan [renders it] as an expression of “turtle-doves and young pigeons.” This turtle-dove, after the male, its mate, dies, does not mate with another; so too Israel did not exchange You for another god, although You distanced Yourself from them and they were like a widow.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed abbreviation וי"ת is read “and Targum Jonathan.”

Psalms.english_translation: The soul of Your poor.
That You made with our fathers.
*Naveh chamas* — *naveh* is an expression of dwelling.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: O let not the oppressed turn back in confusion
Psalms.english_translation: Let not the oppressed return from before You in his prayer, put to shame.
Your blasphemies, like “this, the enemy hath reproached” (verse 18).
[Do not destroy] Israel.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: We give thanks unto Thee, O God
Psalms.english_translation: For the good we give thanks, also for the evil; and Your name is always near in our mouths.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Men tell of Thy wondrous works
Psalms.english_translation: *Sipperu* — our generations [tell of] Your wonders always.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: When I take the appointed time
Psalms.english_translation: When we have a festival, we are not occupied with foul speech and levity.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I Myself will judge with equity
Psalms.english_translation: We set our heart to praise You and laud You, in keeping with the occasion of the day.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: When the earth and all the inhabitants thereof are dissolved
Psalms.english_translation: On the day of the giving of the Torah, when the earth and all its inhabitants were dissolved, because of the condition that You made with the work of Creation: if they do not accept etc., you shall return to chaos.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I Myself establish the pillars of it
Psalms.english_translation: When I said, “We will do and we will hearken.”
To the wicked who confuse Israel.
[The rising] of the sun, and from its west, and not from the deserts that you cross in a caravan to increase wealth — not by all of these does one lift up the horn.
For all the evil that you have done.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He putteth down one, and lifteth up another
Psalms.english_translation: The high ones He will bring down, and the low ones He will raise.
The cup of reeling is in His hand.
*Chamar* — strong; *ווינו"ש* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 75:9 (“a strong wine”), in forms such as וינוש, וייבוש; the printed form (ווינו"ש) is a variant spelling.

Psalms.english_translation: The cup is full of a mixture, to mix and to make all the nations drink.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: And He poureth out of the same
Psalms.english_translation: From this cup He will scatter and pour out their drink; an expression of “as waters that are poured down” (Micah 1:4).
From then on — His vengeance and His might.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: All the horns of the wicked
Psalms.english_translation: Of Amalek.

As in the matter that is said (Ezekiel 25:14), “And I will lay My vengeance upon Edom by the hand of My people Israel”; Israel will cut off the horn of Amalek etc.; and then “the horns of the righteous shall be lifted up” — the righteous of the world, Israel, who are the praise of the Holy One, blessed be He.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: There He broke the fiery shafts of the bow
Psalms.english_translation: Of Sennacherib and his multitude.

*Rishfei keshet* is not an expression of *rishfei esh* (flames of fire), for the expression of *rishfei esh* does not fall upon a bow; and this one is soft, whereas *rishfei esh* has a dagesh; *rishfei keshet* is an expression of “*ulchumei reshef*” (Deuteronomy 32:24), which is translated *of* (bird), “and the sons of *reshef* fly upward” (Job 5:7), and so “and their flocks to *resheph*” (below, 78), to birds; and so “sons of *reshef*” — sons of flying — are demons; “they fly upward” to fly. This too is an expression of flying arrows, as in the matter that is said, “and the arrow that flieth by day.” “There He broke the *rishfei keshet*” — arrows that the bow causes to fly. And this whole psalm speaks of the downfall of Sennacherib, for we do not find an enemy falling at Jerusalem but him.
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s Hebrew in the quotations is *ulchumei reshef* (JPS Deuteronomy 32:24 “the devouring of the fiery bolt”), *uvenei reshef yagbihu of* (JPS Job 5:7 “As the sparks fly upward”) and *umiknehem larshafim* (JPS Psalms 78:48 “And their flocks to fiery bolts”); the last verse is Psalms 91:5 (“Nor of the arrow that flieth by day”). The printed “below, 78” is Psalms 78:48.

Psalms.english_translation: An expression of *na'ar* (abhorring): “He hath abhorred (*ni'er*) His sanctuary” (Lamentations 2:7), “Thou hast abhorred (*ne'artah*) the covenant of Thy servant” (below, Psalms 89:40) — You abhor Your enemies and Your adversaries and sweep them from the world; *na'or* is named for His deeds, like gracious and compassionate and jealous, which are named because He is gracious, because He is compassionate, because He is jealous.
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “below, 89” is Psalms 89:40.

Psalms.english_translation: Stronger than the oppressive giants, who are as high as mountains; and before You their might is not known.

*Eshtolelu* — like *hishtolelu*, like (2 Chronicles 20) “and afterward Ahaziah joined himself” etc., like *hitchabber*; and *eshtolelu* is derived from “He leadeth counsellors away stripped (*shalal*)” (Job 12:17), and it is an expression of error and carelessness, like fools who err; and the tav falls in the reflexive in the middle of the word in every word that begins with a shin.
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s quotation of 2 Chronicles 20 (*ve'acharei chen etchabber Achazyah*) differs from JPS 2 Chronicles 20:35 (“And after this did Jehoshaphat king of Judah join himself with Ahaziah king of Israel”).

Psalms.english_translation: They fell asleep in sleep; an expression of slumber (*tenumah*).
Their hands and their strength, when You came to exact payment from them.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: the riders also and the horses
Psalms.english_translation: The vav of *verokhev* is ancillary, like “These are the sons of Zibeon: Aiah and Anah” (Genesis 36:24) — the vav of *ve'ayah* is ancillary.
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s Hebrew is *elleh benei Tzivon ve'ayah va'anah*.

Psalms.english_translation: From the hour that You are angry.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou didst cause sentence to be heard from heaven
Psalms.english_translation: When Isaiah prophesied about the retribution upon Sennacherib and it was fulfilled on him, the Land of Israel, which feared him and his multitude, was then still.
To execute judgment on his enemies, to save Hezekiah and his company.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Surely the wrath of man shall praise Thee
Psalms.english_translation: The anger of the wicked causes the creatures to acknowledge the Holy One, blessed be He: when they show their anger, and the Holy One, blessed be He, exacts payment from them, everyone praises before Him, and even they themselves praise before Him when they see that their anger is nothing, as we find with Nebuchadnezzar when he threw Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah into the fiery furnace — what is said there? “May the name of God be blessed” etc.; and through this “the residue of wrath shalt Thou gird” — You will hold back and stop: the rest of the wicked are held back and prevented from showing their pride and their wrath. *Tachgor* is an expression of restraint in the language of the Mishnah: “a notch in the knife, so that the nail catches (*tachgor*) in it.” And I heard in the name of Rabbi Eleazar the Gaon son of Rabbi Isaac that he brought this verse as evidence for that Mishnah. And one can further interpret this *chagirah* according to its plain meaning, an expression of a girdle, and its explanation: to You it is fitting to gird wrath and to put on jealousy, for the might and the ability are Yours; and the expression “residue” is this: since the wrath of man is nothing, all girdles of wrath remain for You.
Psalms.translator_note: The Aramaic quotation (*yehe shemei de'alaha mevarakh*) is translated as printed; the Mishnaic quotation was not identified.

Psalms.english_translation: Your vows.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: all that are round about Him
Psalms.english_translation: Those who hear this salvation; and thus they did, as it is said (Isaiah 19:18), “there shall be five cities in the land of Egypt that speak the language of Canaan, and swear to the LORD of hosts.”
Psalms.translator_note: The printed abbreviation כמ"ש is read “as it is said.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: bring presents unto Him that is to be feared
Psalms.english_translation: Why? Because at the time of His desire.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed sentence is a fragment and is translated literally.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He minisheth the spirit of princes
Psalms.english_translation: The haughty spirit of the nobles; He lessens their pride. *Yivtzor* — lessens, like “nothing will be withholden (*yibatzer*) from them” (Genesis 11:6).
Concerning the decrees (*dates*) and the judgments that pass over Israel.
*Yadi* — my wound.
In this exile, which is like night, it streams: moisture and bitterness (*marah*).
And its streaming will not be still.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: When I think thereon, O God
Psalms.english_translation: The kindness that He used to do for me in the days of my love.
On those kindnesses and goods.
*pasmer* [printed פשמי"ר] in French (to faint).
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 77:4 (“(my soul) swoons”), in forms such as פשמיר, פשבוייר; the reading is *pasmer* (REJ transcription: *Psmer*, read *pasmer*); the printed form (פשמי"ר) matches.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou holdest fast the lids of mine eyes
Psalms.english_translation: *Shemurot* — an expression of the *ashmurot* of the night, when a person awakens from his sleep and his mind is settled and his heart returns to him; but I am not so in this night of exile; always my eyes are stuck shut like one who sleeps, his heart stopped up by the troubles that I see; my spirit is struck, and there is no speech in me.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I have pondered the days of old
Psalms.english_translation: To remember the kindnesses that You did with our fathers.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I will call to remembrance my song
Psalms.english_translation: In the days of this exile, which is like night, I remember my songs that I used to sing in earlier days בב"ה.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed abbreviation בב"ה is not resolved and is left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: And my spirit maketh diligent search
Psalms.english_translation: I calculate, and my spirit searches what it is — “is this the attribute of the Holy One, blessed be He?” — and I wonder: will He reject forever?

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Is His mercy clean gone for ever
Psalms.english_translation: Perhaps His kindness has ended.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Is His promise come to an end
Psalms.english_translation: An eternal decree that He will never return from His wrath.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Hath God forgotten to be gracious
Psalms.english_translation: To be gracious; *chenot* is like *asot*, *re'ot*. Another version: *chenot* — graces.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Hath He in anger shut up his compassions
Psalms.english_translation: An expression of “nor shut thy hand” (Deuteronomy 15:7) — that is: has He shut up mercy forever because of the wrath?
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s Hebrew is *lo tikfotz yadkha*; the printed reference is “Deuteronomy 15.”

Psalms.english_translation: My thought says: this is only to make me sick and to make me fear, to return to Him.
Like *lechalloti*; an expression of illness and trembling.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: the right hand of the Most High could change
Psalms.english_translation: That the right hand of the Most High changed — which was “glorious in power,” “dasheth in pieces the enemy,” and now He has turned back His right hand.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I will meditate also upon all Thy work
Psalms.english_translation: That You already did for us.
The way of Your attribute: to sanctify Your name in the world, to execute judgment on the wicked.
Many, when You revealed Yourself at the sea.
The skies dripped a flow of thick waters.
Like *chitzekha*.
Like *kagalgal*: the voice of Your thunder was like a wheel over the sea, to confound the camp of Egypt.
The steps are not recognizable on the water; and *akevotekha* — *טרצ"ש* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 77:20 (“traces”), in forms such as טרצט, טרצשא, טראציש; the printed form (טרצ"ש) matches.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I will open my mouth with a parable
Psalms.english_translation: They are words of Torah.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: We will not hide from their children
Psalms.english_translation: And we also will not hide from the children of our fathers, from informing them of what they told us.
*Kislam* — their hope, and so “If I have made gold my hope (*kisli*)” (Job 31:24).
Who were in Egypt and in the wilderness.

Who went out from Egypt by force before the end, and trusted in their strength and in their arrows, and in the end turned to flee on the day of battle, as explained in Chronicles — and the men of Gath who were born in the land killed them.
They throw and cast, like “hath He cast into the sea” (Exodus 15:4).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Marvellous things did He in the sight of their fathers
Psalms.english_translation: Afterward, when the end came, they too continued to sin against Him, as he goes on to conclude.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: in the sight of their fathers
Psalms.english_translation: Abraham, Isaac and Jacob came upon the sea, and the Holy One, blessed be He, showed them how He redeems their children.
*Ke-ned* — a high mound, as we translate “The floods stood upright as a heap” (ibid. 15:8): *kamu keshur*.
Psalms.translator_note: The Aramaic is translated as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He cleaved rocks in the wilderness
Psalms.english_translation: “And thou shalt smite the rock” etc. (Exodus 17:6).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “ibid. 17” is Exodus 17:6.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: as out of the great deep
Psalms.english_translation: Even when they were going in the midst of the sea, whose waters are salty, He sweetened for them springs in the depth.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: And caused waters to run down like rivers
Psalms.english_translation: They flowed from the well, and the princes made a line with their staves, and the water was drawn after them to each and every tribe’s encampment, as it is said regarding the lawgiver, “with their staves” (Numbers 21:18), as explained in the forty-nine middot.
Psalms.translator_note: The source “the forty-nine middot” (*arba'im vetesha middot*) is translated literally and not identified. Rashi’s words in Numbers 21:18 are *bamechokek bemishenotam*.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: To rebel against the Most High
Psalms.english_translation: *Lamrot* — to provoke, like “ye have been rebellious (*mamrim*)” (Deuteronomy 9).
Psalms.translator_note: The words appear in Deuteronomy 9:7 and 9:24.

Psalms.english_translation: *She'er* — flesh.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: a fire was kindled against Jacob
Psalms.english_translation: Like “and shall set on fire and burn (*uvi'aru vehissiku*)” (Ezekiel 39:9), which is an expression of kindling and burning, as it is written, “and the fire of the LORD burnt among them.”
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s words in Ezekiel 39:9 differ from JPS (“shall make fires of the weapons and use them as fuel”).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Man did eat the bread of the mighty
Psalms.english_translation: The bread of angels. Another explanation: *abirim* — limbs (*evarim*), for it was absorbed into all the limbs, and they had no need for their orifices.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He caused the east wind to set forth in heaven
Psalms.english_translation: “And there went forth a wind from the LORD, and brought across quails” (Numbers 11:31).
Flesh.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: They were not estranged from their craving
Psalms.english_translation: They were not made strangers to their desire, for they attained all their desire.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Their food was yet in their mouths
Psalms.english_translation: “And the anger of the LORD was kindled against the people.” Another explanation: “they were not estranged from their craving” — they were not distanced from their desire until the punishment came upon them.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: smote down the young men of Israel
Psalms.english_translation: *Uvachurei Yisrael* — the chosen among them; and the *asafsuf* are the elders, of whom it is said, “Gather unto Me” (ibid.).
Psalms.translator_note: The reference “ibid.” is to Numbers 11, where the verse is 11:16.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: When He slew them, then they would inquire after Him
Psalms.english_translation: This too was not in truth, but with enticement of the mouth, and they lied with their tongue.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: For their heart was not stedfast with Him
Psalms.english_translation: “Their heart” — not their palms were steadfast; and with all this, He is compassionate to them and atones for their iniquity continually, and did not destroy them.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed words לא כפיהם נכון are translated literally.

Psalms.english_translation: Many times.

From them; and even if He exacted payment from them, He did not arouse all His wrath against them, but only little by little, because He remembered that they are flesh, and the evil inclination is hidden in their heart, and it is “a wind that goeth” when they die, “and cometh not again”; that wind does not return in them in the World to Come when they live; the evil inclination does not rule over them. And one cannot explain “a wind that goeth, and cometh not again” as the spirit of life not returning in them, for if you say so, you deny the resurrection of the dead; and thus it is explained in the Aggadah of Psalms.
Psalms.translator_note: The words quoted are from Psalms 78:39.

Psalms.english_translation: *Kammah* — times; they rebel against Him constantly in the wilderness.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: set bounds to the Holy One of Israel
Psalms.english_translation: *Hitvu* — an expression of a mark, like “and set a mark (*vehitvita tav*)” (Ezekiel 9:4), and a sign is an expression of wonder and testing: they asked of Him a sign and a mark — “Is the LORD among us, or not?” (Exodus 17:7).
They shed their eggs.
*Bachanamal* — the name of the locust; and its midrash: *ba chen umal* — it would crush the greenery of the tree and the grass and eat it.
Psalms.translator_note: The midrashic play on the word (*ba chen umal*) is translated literally.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He gave over their cattle also to the hail
Psalms.english_translation: When the hail began to fall, the Egyptian would drive his flock into the house, and the hail made itself like a kind of wall opposite him, and the Egyptian would slaughter it and put it on his shoulder to carry it to the house and eat it, and the bird would come and take it from him; and this is “and their flocks to *reshafim*” — to birds, like “and the sons of *reshef* fly upward” (Job 5:7). This is its midrash; and by its plain meaning, *reshafim* are flames of fire, as it is written (Exodus 9:24), “and fire flashing up amidst the hail.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He levelled a path for His anger
Psalms.english_translation: Although the plagues were sent in anger, they served only their mission: what they were commanded to kill, they killed, and not all went on their paths. In other commentaries I found thus: “He levelled a path for His anger” — when He smote every firstborn in Egypt, He showed the way to the destroyer, in anger, to come to the houses of Egypt and not to the houses of the children of Israel.
Their bodies.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He drove out the nations also before them
Psalms.english_translation: Seven nations.
Of the nations.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Yet they tried and provoked God
Psalms.english_translation: In the days of the Judges.
That does not shoot the arrow to the place where the marksman wishes.
He handed over the Ark and the tablets into the hand of the Philistines.
His wrath.
*Lo hullalu* — they were not included in the *apiryon* and the *chuppah*, because the young men died in war.
An expression of *hillula* in Aramaic; and our Rabbis expounded it of Nadab and Abihu, but my heart is not settled to explain it so, for it already began in the Tabernacle of Shiloh.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Their priests fell by the sword
Psalms.english_translation: Hophni and Phinehas.
Even his widow was not able to weep for him, for she too died on the day of the report, as is said (1 Samuel 4), “she bowed herself and brought forth; for her pains came suddenly upon her.”
Psalms.translator_note: The words are in 1 Samuel 4:19.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Like a mighty man recovering from wine
Psalms.english_translation: *Mitronen* — awakens and strengthens in speech, to awaken from his wine; *mitronen* is an expression of ringing cry (*rinnah*).
Blows on the back parts, with *ofalim* and with *techorim*; and it is an eternal reproach of blasphemy for them.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He abhorred the tent of Joseph
Psalms.english_translation: It is Shiloh, which is in the portion of Joseph.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: And He built His sanctuary like the heights
Psalms.english_translation: Like heaven and earth, concerning which two hands are said, as it is said, “Yea, My hand hath laid the foundation of the earth, And My right hand hath spread out the heavens” (Isaiah 48:13); so too the Temple with two hands, as it is said (Exodus 15:17), “which Thy hands have established.” Another explanation: “like the heights His sanctuary” — like the earth He founded it: as heaven and earth have no replacement, so the Sanctuary has no replacement, to rest the Presence there.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed reference is “Isaiah 45”; the words are in Isaiah 48:13.

Psalms.english_translation: Pens of the flock, like (end of Habakkuk) “the flock is cut off from the fold” (*mimiklah tzon*).
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s quotation (Habakkuk 3:17) is given in his own wording.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: From following the ewes that give suck He brought him
Psalms.english_translation: That he was shepherding the nursing flock for his father, for he was compassionate: he would bring out the kids first and feed them the topmost grass-tips, which are tender; and bring out the goats after them, and they would eat the middle of the grass; and afterward he would bring out the old ones, and they would eat the roots. The Holy One, blessed be He, said: This one is fit to shepherd My people.

Piles (*gallim*). And why is it called “a Psalm”? Is it not a lamentation? But since it is said (Lamentations 4:11), “The LORD hath accomplished His fury, He hath poured out His fierce anger; and He hath kindled a fire in Zion,” it is a psalm and a song, that He poured out His wrath on wood and on stones and did not make an end of His children.

But were they not wicked? Rather, once they have received their punishment, they are saints; and so it says, “then thy brother should be dishonoured” (Deuteronomy 25:3) — once he has been flogged, he is “thy brother.” So it is explained in the Aggadah.
Psalms.translator_note: Deuteronomy 25:3 in JPS: “then thy brother should be dishonoured before thine eyes.”

Psalms.english_translation: *Vekeles* — an expression of slander, to speak of them as a proverb.
Until when.
You will be furious.
Your wrath, for You are jealous to take vengeance; an expression of “a jealous God” (ibid. 4) — *anfrenment* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 79:5 (“La flamme de ta colère”), in forms such as אינפרינמנט, אנפרינמנט; the printed form (אנפרנמנ"ט) is a variant spelling. “ibid. 4” refers to Deuteronomy 4:24, “a jealous God.”

Psalms.english_translation: *Hotar* — open the prisoners from their prison, like (below 146) “He looseth the prisoners,” and “The king sent and loosed him” (below 105).
Psalms.translator_note: The printed references are Psalms 146:7 and 105:20.

Psalms.english_translation: Sons of the one killed for Your sake; *temutah* — *enmoriniyda* in French. And there is a parallel in the language of the Sages: “It is better that Israel eat the flesh of a *temutah* that was slaughtered, and not eat the flesh of a *temutah* that is carrion”; and its meaning is the flesh of a sick animal that was slaughtered, in tractate Kiddushin.
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 79:11 (“Les fils de la moribonde”), in forms such as אינמורינידא; the printed form (אנמוריניד"א) is a variant spelling. The Talmudic quotation is translated as printed; its source is not identified here beyond the tractate named.

Psalms.english_translation: To the God of Israel.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed words אל ישראל are translated literally.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: A testimony. A Psalm of Asaph
Psalms.english_translation: A psalm of testimony, in which He hinted to them three exiles and prayed for them, for it is said in this psalm three times, “Restore us; cause Thy face to shine, and we shall be saved”; and He hinted in it of the troubles destined to come upon them in the days of the house of Jehu from the kings of Aram, as it is said (2 Kings 13:7), “for the king of Aram destroyed them, and made them like the dust in threshing.”
Psalms.translator_note: The printed words “the days of the house of Jehu” are translated literally. In the passage, 2 Kings 13:7 is the verse about Jehoahaz.

Psalms.english_translation: The one who leads them and provides for them.
And all Israel is called by the name of Joseph, because he provided for them and sustained them in the days of famine.
As it is said (Exodus 25:22), “And there I will meet with thee,” etc.
Show Your might.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Before Ephraim and Benjamin and Manasseh
Psalms.english_translation: When they will need Your salvation, even though they are wicked and not worthy, “stir up Thy might” for them. And why? “And come to save us” — it befits You, and is incumbent upon You, to save both the guilty and the innocent, as it was said to Moses in Egypt (Exodus 3:7), “I have surely seen” — these two sightings: why? I see that they are destined to anger Me, yet nevertheless “I have seen their affliction,” because of the oath I swore to Abraham.
Psalms.translator_note: The double expression *ra’oh ra’iti* is rendered in JPS “I have surely seen.”

Psalms.english_translation: In the war of Aram, when he besieged Samaria (1 Kings 20), and sent messengers to Ahab: “Thy silver and thy gold is mine; thy wives also and thy goodly children are mine.”
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s quotation is from 1 Kings 20:3 and is given in his wording.

Psalms.english_translation: In the days of Jehoash son of Jehoahaz, as it is said (2 Kings 13), “for the LORD saw the affliction of Israel, for the king of Aram destroyed them, and made them like the dust in threshing,” and they smote three times in war, as it is said there, “Thrice did Joash smite him, and recovered the cities of Israel.” In other commentaries I found: as it is said, “thou shalt smite Aram three times” and “which he recovered, the cities of Israel.”
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s quotations from 2 Kings 13 (verses 4, 7, 25 and 19) are given in his wording and joined.

Psalms.english_translation: In the days of Ahasuerus, when Mordecai and Esther were in danger and the whole generation depended on them.

This is not an expression of going, but like “*lekh*” (go/to you); and so it is in the Masorah: “*velekha ephoh*, my son” (Genesis 27:37); “*velekha* there are no tidings to be found” (2 Samuel 18:22); “*simlah lekha* — thou hast a mantle, be thou our ruler” etc. (Isaiah 3:6).
Psalms.translator_note: The Hebrew word *lekha* appears with this spelling in those three verses; the Masoretic citation is translated as printed. JPS renders the three verses differently.

Psalms.english_translation: In the exile of Babylon, where Mordecai was.
*Ad matai ashanta* — in the troubles of the kings of Greece, who did great evil to Israel.
In Egypt.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: tears to drink in large measure
Psalms.english_translation: In Babylon, where it was seventy years, which is a third of the two hundred and ten of Egypt. This I learned from the foundation of Rabbi Moses the Preacher. And one may resolve it by reason that the kingdom of Greece was the third trouble; and if you say, it is the fourth, since Persia and Media preceded it — all seventy years of Babylon are but one exile. And Menachem explained *shalish* as the name of a vessel that one drinks with, and so he explained (Isaiah 40:12) “and comprehended the dust of the earth in a measure (*shalish*).” But our Rabbis explained it as the three tears that Esau shed, as it is said of him (Genesis 27:34), “he cried with an exceeding great and bitter cry” — that is one; “great” — that is two; “and bitter” — that is three. And through them he merited to live by his sword: “And it shall come to pass when thou shalt break loose,” etc. (ibid.).
Psalms.translator_note: The printed phrase “Rabbi Moses the Preacher” is translated as printed. JPS renders Isaiah 40:12 “in a measure.” “Break loose” is JPS Genesis 27:40, whose verse is the one cited by “ibid.”

Psalms.english_translation: You make us a strife for all our neighbours, for Greece contended against us.
From the Greeks.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou didst pluck up a vine out of Egypt
Psalms.english_translation: He returned and hinted at the exile of the Aramaeans: the vine of Israel, which You plucked up from Egypt — You uprooted from there, like “my hope hath He plucked up (*vayyassa*) like a tree” (Job 19:10); and afterward You drove out seven nations and planted them in their land.
Psalms.translator_note: The plucked-up/uprooted wording is Rashi’s; JPS Job 19:10 reads “my hope hath He plucked up like a tree.” The printed words “the exile of the Aramaeans” are translated literally.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou didst clear a place before it
Psalms.english_translation: The inhabitants there.
It put down its roots.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: the mighty cedars with the boughs thereof
Psalms.english_translation: Like “cedars of God” — strong cedars; that is, mighty kings.
She sent out her boughs, like “and put forth boughs (*katzir*)” (Job 14).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “(ibid. 14)”; the words are in Job 14:9, where JPS has “and put forth boughs like a plant.”

Psalms.english_translation: Its border was as far as the Great Sea.
The breadth of the Land of Israel is from the wilderness to the River, the river Euphrates.
Now.
Of that vineyard.
All who came gathered it, like “I have gathered (*arithi*) my myrrh with my spice” (Song of Songs 5:1); and so in the language of the Mishnah: “as much as a basket and its *orah* (picking).”
Psalms.translator_note: The Mishnaic quotation is translated as printed and is not identified here.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The boar out of the wood doth ravage it
Psalms.english_translation: Like a field that ants have stripped (*kirsemuha*), in the language of the Mishnah, and it is an expression of cutting.
Psalms.translator_note: The Mishnaic usage is not identified here.

Psalms.english_translation: The *ayin* is suspended (as if it were written with an *aleph*). When Israel merit, behold, their enemy is made like the beast of the river, which has no strength to come up on dry land; and when punishment is decreed upon them it grows strong like the beast of the forest, which destroys and kills. And “the boar out of the wood” is Amalek, as it is written (in Daniel 7), “it devoured and brake in pieces, and stamped the residue with the feet.” And it (the swine) has some of the signs of purity — so too Amalek has the merit of the fathers.
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s quotation of Daniel 7:7 is given in his wording; the Hebrew letter *ayin* is the one in *mi-ya'ar* that is written suspended in the Masoretic text.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: That which moveth in the field
Psalms.english_translation: Every creeping thing of the field; and the word *ziz* means “that moves (*zaz*) from its place and goes.”
Pastures on its boughs and eats them.
The firmly fixed and settled; an expression of “and restore thee (*vehashivekha*) unto thine office (*al kanekha*)” (Genesis 40).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed (Genesis 40:13); JPS “restore thee unto thine office.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: the branch that Thou madest strong for Thyself
Psalms.english_translation: And upon Esau, who was a beloved son to his father, who called him “my son” — “Thou madest strong (*imatzta*)” the vine of Jacob for Thyself, as it is said (ibid. 27), “and thou shalt serve thy brother” — now.
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s “ibid. 27” is Genesis 27:40.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: It is burned with fire, it is cut down
Psalms.english_translation: *Kesuhah* — an expression of “thou shalt [not] prune” (Leviticus 25); the Aramaic translation: “thou shalt not cut (*tikhsach*).”
Psalms.translator_note: The printed abbreviation ת"א is left as printed; it is not resolved here. JPS Leviticus 25:4: “nor prune thy vineyard.”

Psalms.english_translation: Continually they are going and perishing at the rebuke of Your countenance and Your anger.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: the man of Thy right hand
Psalms.english_translation: Return Your blows upon Esau, who is the man destined for Your right hand to take vengeance upon him.
Whom You made strong for Yourself, that his dwelling be of the fat places of the earth.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: So shall we not turn back from Thee
Psalms.english_translation: And do not cause us to turn back from You.
From exile; and we will make mention of Your goodness and Your might, and then we will call upon Your name.
Here three mentions of names were said, and in the middle one two mentions and in the first one mention — all according to the strength of the exiles, the trouble and the redemption.
An instrument of song that comes from Gath.
On בר"ה.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed abbreviation בר"ה is left as printed and not resolved here.

Psalms.english_translation: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba says: the *nevel* is the *kinnor*; and Rabbi Shimon says: extra strings (and pegs) between this one and that one. Why is it called *nevel*? Because it disgraces (*menabbel*) all kinds of music.
Psalms.translator_note: The words נימין (ויתידות) יתירות are translated literally; the parenthesis is a later printed insertion.

Psalms.english_translation: At the renewal of the moon.
A fixed appointed day for this; and so (Proverbs 7:20) “He will come home at the full moon (*leyom hakeseh*)” — at the fixed appointed time.
Psalms.translator_note: JPS Proverbs 7:20: “He will come home at the full moon.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: For it is a statute for Israel
Psalms.english_translation: It is for Israel from the Holy One, blessed be He, to blow on that day; and it is the day of judgment for the Holy One, blessed be He.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He appointed it in Joseph for a testimony
Psalms.english_translation: On Rosh Hashanah Joseph went out of the prison.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The speech of one that I knew not did I hear
Psalms.english_translation: It is explained in tractate Sotah, that Gabriel taught him seventy languages.
From the labor of slavery, to cook pots as the other slaves do.
*Dud* — a pot, like (1 Samuel 2:14) “and he struck it into the pan, or kettle (*kiyyor o vadud*).”
Psalms.translator_note: JPS 1 Samuel 2:14: “and he struck it into the pan, or kettle, or caldron, or pot.”

Psalms.english_translation: You all called to Me from the trouble of the Egyptian burdens, and I rescued you.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I answered thee in the secret place of thunder
Psalms.english_translation: You called Me in secret between Me and you, and I answered you with the voice of thunder; I made known mighty and awesome deeds publicly.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I proved thee at the waters of Meribah
Psalms.english_translation: Even though it was revealed and tested before Me that you were destined to provoke Me at the waters of Meribah. So it is taught in the Mechilta.
After I have done all this for you, you ought to listen to Me.
To ask from Me all the desire of your heart.
According to all that you ask I will fill.
In the sight of their heart, like (above 5) “because of them that lie in wait (*shorerai*) for me.”
Psalms.translator_note: The printed reference is Psalms 5:9.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Oh that My people would hearken unto Me
Psalms.english_translation: Even now, if they wished to return to Me and to hearken to Me.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I would soon subdue their enemies
Psalms.english_translation: In a little while I would subdue their enemies.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: turn My hand against their adversaries
Psalms.english_translation: I would turn My blow from upon you, to put it upon them; and then —

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The haters of the LORD should dwindle away before Him; And their punishment should endure for ever
Psalms.english_translation: Their punishment, forever.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: They should also be fed with the fat of wheat
Psalms.english_translation: Israel.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: They should also be fed with the fat of wheat
Psalms.english_translation: He satisfied them with honey when they walked in His ways, as in the matter that is said (Deuteronomy 32:13), “And He made him to suck honey out of the crag.”
Psalms.translator_note: The printed lemma is *umitzur*, “and out of the rock”; the nearest JPS phrase of this verse is used, because the words “with honey out of the rock” fall in the next verse of the JPS text.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: God standeth in the congregation of God
Psalms.english_translation: To see whether they judge truth. And you judges, how long will you judge iniquity?
If he is innocent in his case, do not pervert his judgment for the better because of favoring the wicked.
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s wording is translated literally; JPS renders the verse “Do justice to the afflicted and destitute.”

Psalms.english_translation: The judges who pervert the judgment.
That because of this iniquity they walk in darkness (in the manner of “for a gift blindeth,” etc.) and because of it the foundations of the earth are moved.
Psalms.translator_note: The parenthesis is a later printed insertion; it points to Exodus 23:8, “for a gift blindeth them that have sight.”

Psalms.english_translation: Angels: when I gave you the Torah, I gave it to you on the condition that the angel of death would no longer rule over you.
Indeed like the first man you shall die, since you corrupted your deeds as he did.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: fall like one of the princes
Psalms.english_translation: Of the first ones who died, so you shall fall. And the midrash aggadah: like one of the princes above, as it is said (Isaiah 24:21), “The LORD will punish the host of the high heaven on high.”
Psalms.translator_note: JPS Isaiah 24:21: “That the LORD will punish the host of the high heaven on high.”

Psalms.english_translation: Asaph began to pray that He rise and cut off those corrupt judges from Israel.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou shalt possess all the nations
Psalms.english_translation: He is the Inheritor of the nations, and everything is in Your hand to judge.
Do not give silence to our iniquities, for our enemies are shouting at us.
Psalms.translator_note: The wording is translated literally.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Against Thee do they make a covenant
Psalms.english_translation: This covenant is only against You, to make Your name forgotten, for You are called God only by us, the God of Israel; and since the name of Israel will not be mentioned, Your great name too will not be mentioned. So I found.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Assyria also is joined with them
Psalms.english_translation: Even Assyria, which until today was careful of the rest of foolish counsel and would not join with evildoers, as it is said (Genesis 10) “Out of that land went forth Asshur,” who went out from the counsel of the Generation of the Dispersion — here he joined them and helped them for evil (in other commentaries I found so). “Assyria also is joined with them,” etc. This one too, who was beloved from the beginning, מע"ט, who separated from the counsel of Nimrod, as it is said, “Out of that land went forth Asshur” — he too returned to be wicked; therefore he took part in destroying Your house. Genesis Rabbah.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed abbreviation מע"ט is left as printed and not resolved here. Printed “Genesis 4”; the verse quoted is Genesis 10:11.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: an arm to the children of Lot
Psalms.english_translation: All these gave strength and help to Moab and Ammon, our neighbors, to come upon us.
By means of Gideon.
By means of Barak.
I do not know which of the wars it was at En-dor, that of Gideon or that of Barak.
Scattered dung. Targum Jonathan.
These nations mentioned above: Edom and Ishmael and all their companions.
The dwelling of the House of God.

And as stubble driven before the wind. And what is a *galgal*? It is the tops of the thorns of the field, called *קרדנ"ש* in French; and when the days of winter arrive they break off and are destroyed of themselves and fly little by little, and what breaks off from them looks like the wheels of a wagon wheel, and the wind carries them.
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 83:14, in forms such as קרדונש and קרדנוש; the printed form (קרדנ"ש) is a variant spelling.

Psalms.english_translation: *Torbilion* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 83:16 (“tourbillon”), in forms such as טורבליון and טורבילון; the printed form (טורביליו"ן) is a variant spelling.

Psalms.english_translation: How beloved and dear are Your dwelling places.
Is desired.
Longed, like (2 Samuel 13:39) “and David the king longed to go forth to Absalom.”
Psalms.translator_note: JPS 2 Samuel 13:39: “And the soul of king David failed with longing for Absalom.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: for the courts of the LORD
Psalms.english_translation: For they are ruined; and she said this about the exile.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: My heart and my flesh sing for joy
Psalms.english_translation: They will pray for this.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: the sparrow hath found a house
Psalms.english_translation: In our destruction the birds nested in it. And the midrash aggadah: in its building in the wilderness; and the sparrow is the Congregation of Israel.
*Asher shatah* — where she placed (*sham-ah*).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Happy are they that dwell in Thy house
Psalms.english_translation: Whoever will yet merit to dwell in Your house and still praise You within it.
Who has made You the strength of his trust.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: In whose heart are the highways
Psalms.english_translation: He reckons in his heart the highways of his ways, to make his way straight.
Those who transgress Your law, who are in the depth of Gehinnom in weeping and wailing.
With the tears of their eyes.

They bless and acknowledge His name and say: He judged us well and His judgment is true; “and the early rain clotheth with blessings” for us those who teach us to go in the good way, and we did not listen to him.
Psalms.translator_note: The final clause is elliptical in the printed text and is translated literally.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: They go from strength to strength
Psalms.english_translation: Those mentioned above, the dwellers in Your house, in whose heart are the highways.
From the house of study to לב"ה, and their host and their strength will be seen by the Holy One, blessed be He, in Zion.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed abbreviation לב"ה is left as printed and not resolved here.

Psalms.english_translation: To build Your house.
It is the Temple that shields us.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: look upon the face of Thine anointed
Psalms.english_translation: (David) Your anointed, and look at his kindnesses and his labor, with which he labored and toiled for its building.
Psalms.translator_note: The word “David” is in parentheses in the printed text.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: a day in Thy courts is better than a thousand
Psalms.english_translation: One day in Your courts, even if the next day he dies, is better than living a thousand years in another place.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I had rather stand at the threshold
Psalms.english_translation: On the threshold and the doorposts, to be diligent.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: dwell in the tents of wickedness
Psalms.english_translation: Than to dwell at ease in the tents of Esau the wicked, to cling to them.
One may resolve *shemesh* by its plain meaning; and Midrash Tehillim resolves it as an expression of *shinnei chomah* (battlements of a wall).
Psalms.translator_note: The printed words are translated literally.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou hast been favourable unto Thy land
Psalms.english_translation: If You return the captivity of Jacob, and bear their iniquity, and cover their sin, and gather up Your wrath from them, and turn Yourself from Your fierce anger — then “You were favourable to Your land,” and Your world is appeased; and as long as You do not do this, Your land and Your world are not appeased.
Return Yourself, and bring us back.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Wilt Thou not quicken us again
Psalms.english_translation: In the end You will return and revive us, for You promised us so by Your prophet.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I will hear what God the LORD will speak
Psalms.english_translation: I will merit to hear what the Holy One, blessed be He, will speak when He speaks peace unto His people.
To foolishness, to sin before Him.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Mercy and truth are met together
Psalms.english_translation: That Israel will be speakers of truth, and from heaven kindness will meet them.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Righteousness and peace have kissed each other
Psalms.english_translation: The righteousness that Israel does, and the peace from the Holy One, blessed be He, will kiss one another; that is, “and the work of righteousness shall be peace” (Isaiah 32).
Psalms.translator_note: The printed reference is Isaiah 32:17.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Truth springeth out of the earth
Psalms.english_translation: When Israel speak truth, they will look down from heaven upon the righteousness that they do on earth.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: the LORD will give that which is good
Psalms.english_translation: He will open His treasure, the heavens, to give rain, so that His land may yield its produce.
And the Holy One, blessed be He, will set righteousness in the paths of His steps, that He may lead His children in them.

For I hear my blasphemy and my reproach and have power in my hand to take vengeance, and I am silent. So it is in the Aggadah of Psalms. Another explanation: our Rabbis explained in Berakhot: “Am I not godly? For all the kings of East and West sit in their honor, and my hands are soiled with blood and with the fetus and with the afterbirth,” etc.
All the exile, which is day for the nations and night for Israel. So it is explained in the Aggadah of Psalms.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: do I lift up my soul
Psalms.english_translation: I will direct my heart.
Who puts the upper ones before the lower ones.
Before the angels were created, the heavens and the earth were created; therefore all the nations shall honor Your name.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed words are translated literally.

Psalms.english_translation: It is the way of adulterers to be placed in the depth of Sheol, and from there You delivered me, for Nathan the prophet said to me (2 Samuel 12:13), “The LORD also hath put away thy sin.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: the proud are risen up against me
Psalms.english_translation: Doeg and Ahithophel.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: have not set Thee before them
Psalms.english_translation: They did not remember that they saw that Samuel anointed me at Your word.
The son of a maidservant humbles himself before his master more than one bought with money, for the son of a maidservant is born in the house and grows up in his master’s bosom.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Work in my behalf a sign for good
Psalms.english_translation: That it be recognized by others that You have forgiven me.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: That they that hate me may see it
Psalms.english_translation: The sign, and be ashamed. But the Holy One, blessed be He, did not listen to him to give the sign in his days, but in the days of Solomon his son, when the gates stuck to one another and did not open until he said (2 Chronicles 6), “turn not away the face of Thine anointed; remember the mercies of David Thy servant.”
Psalms.translator_note: JPS 2 Chronicles 6:42: “Remember the good deeds of David Thy servant.” The printed Hebrew is *chasdei David*.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: His foundation is in the holy mountains
Psalms.english_translation: The foundation of this psalm — the psalmist founded it on Mount Zion and Jerusalem.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Glorious things are spoken of Thee
Psalms.english_translation: Of Jerusalem: words of honor were spoken in you by the mouth of the Holy One, blessed be He; and what are the glorious things? That you are the city of God, Selah.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I will make mention of Rahab and Babylon as among them that know Me
Psalms.english_translation: He spoke this too concerning you: I will mention Egypt and Babylon among those who know to bring an offering, as it is said (Isaiah 66:20), “And they shall bring all your brethren,” etc., “for an offering unto the LORD,” etc.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Behold Philistia, and Tyre, with Ethiopia
Psalms.english_translation: They too, like Egypt and Babylon, will set their heart to seek and to remember each and every one.
This one was of the families of those born in Zion, as it is said (ibid. 27), “and ye shall be gathered one by one.”
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “ibid. 27” is Isaiah 27:12.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: But of Zion it shall be said
Psalms.english_translation: And when they bring them as an offering to the LORD in Zion, He will say to them of each and every one: This is one of those who went into exile from you and of their descendants. Another explanation: the psalmist says, I will mention to My people and to those who know the greatness of Egypt and Babylon, which they see now in their greatness. “Behold Philistia, and Tyre, with Ethiopia” — because they are near to Rahab and Babylon, all the nations exalt them and say of them, “This one was born there,” in Egypt and Babylon.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: But of Zion it shall be said
Psalms.english_translation: And this praise, which is now for Rahab and Babylon, will turn to Zion, and of it they will say, So-and-so was born in her.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: the Most High Himself doth establish her
Psalms.english_translation: And the Holy One, blessed be He, will establish her above all the cities.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The LORD shall count in the register of the peoples
Psalms.english_translation: This verse is inverted, and the Selah said at its end is turned toward its beginning: “The LORD shall count in the register of the peoples, Selah” — that is, in the future, when the Holy One, blessed be He, writes the idolaters for contempt, He will count the Israelites who are swallowed among them and those who were forced among them, and will bring them out from among them and say, “This one was born of those of Zion,” and will choose them for Himself. And this is what Isaiah said (66), “And of them also will I take for the priests and for the Levites” — from the nations who bring them as an offering, I will take those swallowed among them, and among them there will be priests and Levites who are not recognizable, “and before the revealed they are,” said HaShem. And where did He say (Deuteronomy 29:28), “The secret things belong unto the LORD our God”?
Psalms.translator_note: The printed abbreviation הע"ג is left as printed and not resolved here. The words ולפני גלוים הם אמר ה' are garbled in the printed text and are translated literally. JPS Isaiah 66:21: “And of them also will I take for the priests and for the Levites, saith the LORD.”

Psalms.english_translation: On this; *kechollelim* is an expression of *mecholelim* (dancers).
All my innards.
In Your salvation.
For love-sickness and affliction, that she is afflicted with the sufferings of exile.

Wherever *Maskil* is said, it is said by means of an interpreter: the prophet would station an interpreter before him, and when the spirit of prophecy came upon him he would speak the prophecy to the interpreter, and he would make it heard.
One of the singers with musical instruments; and the sons of Korah founded this psalm, that Heman should say it on the platform.

He was of the sons of Zerah son of Judah, for he is traced (in Chronicles I 2); and the sons of Zerah — Zimri and Ethan and Heman and Calcol and Dara — all five were great sages, as it is said of Solomon (1 Kings 4), “For he was wiser than all men: than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Heman, and Calcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol.” And they composed psalms and they were set in the Book of Psalms; therefore they were called “sons of Mahol.” So I found in precise commentaries.
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s “Dara” is the “Darda” of 1 Kings 5:11 in JPS numbering.

Psalms.english_translation: And at night too I stand ready before You.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: For my soul is sated with troubles
Psalms.english_translation: He says this about the Congregation of Israel.
*Ayil* — no strength, like (above 22) “O Thou my strength (*eyaluti*), hasten to help me.”
Psalms.translator_note: The printed reference is Psalms 22:20.

Psalms.english_translation: Behold, I am among the dead, free from the world — as all the dead are free from the world.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: they are cut off from Thy hand
Psalms.english_translation: From Your commandments they were cut off from the world.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou hast laid me in the nethermost pit
Psalms.english_translation: It is the exile.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thy wrath lieth hard upon me
Psalms.english_translation: It leans and hangs upon me.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: all Thy waves Thou pressest down
Psalms.english_translation: *Mishbarim* are an expression of the waves of the sea: all the storm of Your anger — with all of them You have afflicted me continually.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou hast made me an abomination unto them
Psalms.english_translation: The nations, in whose eyes I was esteemed — now I am loathsome to them.
Shut up in prison, and I cannot go out.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Wilt Thou work wonders for the dead
Psalms.english_translation: For the wicked, who even in their lifetime are called dead — is it for them that You do wonders and miracles?

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: shades arise and give Thee thanks
Psalms.english_translation: Perhaps these nations that slackened their hands from Your service and Your Torah will arise and thank You? — said in astonishment.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Shall Thy mercy be declared in the grave
Psalms.english_translation: If we die at the hand of our enemy, can we then tell Your praise in the grave?

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: at the point of death from my youth up
Psalms.english_translation: Died from the midst of choking, a snatched death, like (Exodus 14) “and the LORD overthrew (*vayna'er*)”; Menachem explained it as an expression of striking, like (Isaiah 33:15) “That shaketh (*no'er*) his hands from holding of bribes”; (ibid. 52) “Shake thyself (*hitna'ari*) from the dust; arise, sit down”; (ibid. 1) “And the strong shall be as tow (*lin'oret*)”; (Job 38:13) “And the wicked be shaken out (*veyinna'aru*) of it”; (Nehemiah 5:13) “even thus be he shaken out (*na'ur*), and emptied.”
Psalms.translator_note: The printed reference “ibid. 52” is Isaiah 52:2, and “ibid. 1” is Isaiah 1:31. The phrase “a snatched death” is Rashi’s wording.

Psalms.english_translation: Your terror is settled and firmly established in my heart; *afunah* is an expression of (Proverbs 25) “A word fitly spoken (*davar davur al ofanav*)” — upon its foundations (*mekhonav*).
Psalms.translator_note: JPS Proverbs 25:11: “A word fitly spoken.” The printed reference is Proverbs 25:11.

Psalms.english_translation: I am darkened and cut off from them.
He too is one of the five brothers, the psalmists; and our Rabbis explained it of Abraham our father, from “Who hath raised up one from the east.”
Psalms.translator_note: The Rabbis’ source is not named in the printed text. The quoted words “Who hath raised up one from the east” are Isaiah 41:2.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: make known Thy faithfulness with my mouth
Psalms.english_translation: What I have known of You, that You keep Your promise and confirm Your words.

For I said: Forever will the throne of David be built in kindness, as it is written (2 Samuel 7:13), “and I will establish the throne of his kingdom,” etc. Another explanation: I thought that the world would be built by Your kindness and that You would establish Your faithfulness in the heavens, that it be firm and fulfilled; and what is the faithfulness? That promise that You promised David through Nathan the prophet, saying, “I have made a covenant with My chosen, to establish his seed for ever” (ibid.).
Psalms.translator_note: The words of the last quotation are in Rashi’s wording; compare Psalms 89:4–5 (“I have made a covenant with My chosen… Thy seed will I establish for ever”).

Psalms.english_translation: If You were keeping Your promise.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed words are elliptical and are translated literally.

Psalms.english_translation: They will acknowledge the faithfulness of Your words in the assembly of the holy ones.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: can be compared unto the LORD
Psalms.english_translation: Would be held in awe like Him.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: great council of the holy ones
Psalms.english_translation: In the great council of angels.
When its waves are lifted up.
You humble them; and so (Proverbs 29:11) “but a wise man afterwards stilleth it (*yeshabbechenah*)” (and so above 65) “Who stilleth (*mashbiach*) the roaring of the seas.”
Psalms.translator_note: The words in the second parenthesis are a later printed insertion. JPS Proverbs 29:11: “but a wise man stilleth it within him”; Rashi’s Hebrew reads *be-achor* (“afterwards”).

Psalms.english_translation: Egypt.
Who know how to appease their Creator on Rosh Hashanah with the *teruah*, for which they arrange Kingship verses, Remembrance verses and Shofar verses.
Psalms.translator_note: The three terms (*malkhuyot, zikhronot, shofarot*) are translated literally.

Psalms.english_translation: That You are pleased with them. *Apiement* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 89:18 (“Et dans ta bonne volonté”), in forms such as אפיימונט and אפיימונטי; the printed form (אפימאנ"ט) is a variant spelling.

Psalms.english_translation: Nathan the prophet and Gad the seer.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I have laid help upon one that is mighty
Psalms.english_translation: Upon David, to help him always.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The enemy shall not exact from him
Psalms.english_translation: He will not prevail over him to be to him like a creditor.
I will make him great.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Then will I visit their transgression with the rod
Psalms.english_translation: So Nathan the prophet said to him about Solomon (2 Samuel 7:14), “if he commit iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men” — this is Rezon son of Eliada, who stood as an adversary to him; “and with the stripes of the children of men” — this is Ashmedai, for the demons were children of the first man.
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s Hebrew for the quotation (*asher beha'avoto*) differs from JPS. The identification of Rezon son of Eliada is as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Surely I will not be false unto David
Psalms.english_translation: An expression of “whose waters fail not (*lo yekhazevu*)” (Isaiah 58:11) — *פיילנצ"א* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: be stedfast as the witness in sky
Psalms.english_translation: The moon and the sun are witnesses to it, that as long as they exist his kingdom will exist, as it is said (Jeremiah 33:20), “If you can break My covenant with the day, and My covenant with the night,” etc., then “may also My covenant be broken with David My servant.”
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s quotation is in his wording; the phrase “then may also My covenant be broken with David My servant” is from the following verse.

Psalms.english_translation: You scrutinized his sons to reckon their iniquity, until You cast them off and rejected them in the days of Zedekiah.
*Ne'artah* — You annulled.
That he built in Jerusalem.
The Temple Mount and the Citadel of Zion.
You turned it back and overturned the sharpness of his sword, like (Joshua 5:2) “knives of flint (*charevot tzurim*),” and so (Isaiah 54:17) “every instrument formed against you.”
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s wording of Isaiah 54:17 differs from JPS (“No weapon that is formed against thee shall prosper”).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: hast not made him to stand
Psalms.english_translation: And You did not make him stand from falling.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou hast made his brightness to cease
Psalms.english_translation: His shining, like *tzohorayim* (noon), which we translate *tihara*, and like (Exodus 24:10) “and the like of the very heaven for clearness (*latohar*).”
Psalms.translator_note: The Aramaic word *tihara* is translated as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: cast his throne down to the ground
Psalms.english_translation: You humbled and destroyed; every expression of *shachayah* (bowing) in Targum Jonathan is *magar*.
Psalms.translator_note: The word *magarta* is the printed Hebrew.

Psalms.english_translation: What old age do I have? Are not my days few? It is enough for You that You exact payment from me by my death, short of days.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed words are translated literally.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: For what vanity hast Thou created
Psalms.english_translation: For nothing and for vanity You created all the children of men.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: How I do bear in my bosom
Psalms.english_translation: In exile I bear their burden and their load.
The end of King Messiah; and it is an expression of the language of the Mishnah: “In the footsteps of the Messiah (*ikvot hamashiach*), insolence will increase.”
Psalms.translator_note: The Mishnaic quotation is not identified here.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Blessed be the LORD for evermore
Psalms.english_translation: For all that He has done for us.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: A Prayer of Moses the man of God
Psalms.english_translation: Eleven psalms from here to “Of David, a Psalm” — Moses said all of them; corresponding to them he blessed eleven blessings for the eleven tribes in “This is the blessing.”
*Ma'on* — a dwelling and a refuge to go to; You were that for us.
From eternity, for You were from of old, before everything.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Before the mountains were brought forth
Psalms.english_translation: They were created; “and ere Thou hadst formed the earth and the world,” and from the first world to the last world, You are God.
You bring afflictions upon man until You return him to be weak of strength and near death, and You say to him through the afflictions: “Return, you children of men” from your evil ways.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: For a thousand years in Thy sight
Psalms.english_translation: A thousand years of men are as one day of the Holy One, blessed be He, and yet some of the night with Him — for one day of the Holy One, blessed be He, and a little of the night of the Holy One, blessed be He, are a thousand years; for the verse did not say that the day of the Holy One, blessed be He, is one like a thousand years, but when a little of the night has passed with Him, then His day is complete and it is a thousand years. And therefore the first man died within a thousand, for if he had lived a thousand it would have been more than the day of the Holy One, blessed be He. And perhaps the measure of that watch is like the span from the death of the first man to a thousand years, and we do not know how long that watch is, except by reasoning (I found) “For a thousand years in Thy sight,” etc. And when repentance arose in Your mind at the beginning, You judged well and created it, and the years were fitting for this, since (not) the days of men were many, for a thousand years were not in Your sight but as a yesterday that goes by and passes, and a little of the night is with it, for You said to the first man (Genesis 2:17), “for in the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die,” and he lived nine hundred and thirty years — it turns out that a thousand years amount to a complete day, and a little of the night with it.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed text of this comment is difficult; it is translated literally. The words in parentheses — (מצאתי) “I found” and (שלא) “not” — are printed in parentheses in the source and are left so.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: as yesterday when it is past
Psalms.english_translation: That has already passed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou carriest them away as with a flood
Psalms.english_translation: Now You have snatched those years and brought them to few days, which are only like a sleep of slumber, for the two generations are seventy years, as is explained at the end of the passage, “The days of our years are threescore years and ten,” and they are reckoned as one sleep, as in the matter (below 127) “When the LORD brought back those that returned to Zion, we were like unto them that dream”; and about the seventy years of the Babylonian exile it is said that it was seventy years.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed reference “below 127” is Psalms 126:1. Rashi’s words “as is explained at the end of the passage” point to Psalms 90:10.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou carriest them away as with a flood
Psalms.english_translation: *Zeramtam* — an expression of sweeping away, like (Habakkuk 3) “the overflowing (*zerem*) of the waters.”
Psalms.translator_note: JPS Habakkuk 3:10: “The tempest of waters floweth over.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: In the morning they are like grass which groweth up
Psalms.english_translation: One who is born at night dies in the morning, at the end of the sleep; and if
Psalms.translator_note: The printed comment breaks off here.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: In the morning it flourisheth, and groweth up
Psalms.english_translation: Immediately it passes away; and until the evening comes it is cut down and withers. Why?

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: For we are consumed in Thine anger
Psalms.english_translation: And on top of all this —

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou hast set our iniquities before Thee
Psalms.english_translation: And our hidden things — the sins of our youth — You have placed in the light of Your face.
Our youth, like (1 Samuel 17) “whose son is this youth (*ha'elem*).”
Psalms.translator_note: JPS 1 Samuel 17:56: “Inquire thou whose son the stripling is.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: in the light of Thy countenance
Psalms.english_translation: Opposite You, to look at them.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: For all our days are passed away in Thy wrath
Psalms.english_translation: And they have turned away and been consumed and have gone in Your wrath.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: as a tale that is told
Psalms.english_translation: Like speech that hurries to its end.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The days of our years are threescore years and ten
Psalms.english_translation: These years of ours, in these iniquities of ours and in these hidden sins of ours, are seventy years.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Or even by reason of strength
Psalms.english_translation: And if his days are very strong, they are eighty years.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Yet is their pride but travail and vanity
Psalms.english_translation: And all the greatness and authority that a man has in these days is only travail and vanity; and why? Because “it is speedily gone, and we fly away” — within wrath we quickly fly away and die.
*Gaz* — an expression of passing, like “they are cut down (*nagozu*), and he shall pass away” (Nahum 1:12) and “and brought across (*vayyaz*) quails from the sea” (Numbers 11:31).
Psalms.translator_note: JPS Nahum 1:12: “Even so shall they be cut down, and he shall pass away.” Rashi’s Hebrew for the Numbers quotation is *vayyaz selavim min hayyam*.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Who knoweth the power of Thine anger
