Psalms.english_translation: In few days like these, who will acquire a heart to know the power of Your anger, so as to fear You? And “according to the fear that is due unto Thee” is Your wrath: as You are to be feared, so Your wrath is severe, and You exact payment from sinners.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: So teach us to number our days
Psalms.english_translation: As at the beginning it was made known in the world to count our days long; and once we lengthen days we can acquire a heart, and we shall bring into them a heart of wisdom; and *navi* is an expression of bringing. (And some say: “to number our days, *ken*” — like the numerical value of כ"ן, seventy years, and we shall die according to the measure of our days, which are few; so You will chasten us; and so “and he taught (*vayoda*) with them the men of Succoth” (Judges 8:16)) (סא"א).
Psalms.translator_note: it is left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: From Your fierce anger.
Think a good thought about Your servants.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: O satisfy us in the morning with Thy mercy
Psalms.english_translation: On the day of redemption and salvation, which is morning to the night of trouble and sighing and darkness.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: That we may rejoice and be glad all our days
Psalms.english_translation: That is, in all the troubles that passed over us in these our days.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Make us glad according to the days wherein Thou hast afflicted us
Psalms.english_translation: Make us glad in the days of our Messiah according to the number of the days that You afflicted us in exiles, and according to the number of years in which we have seen evil.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: the graciousness of the Lord our God
Psalms.english_translation: His Presence and His consolations.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Establish Thou also upon us the work of our hands
Psalms.english_translation: It is a language of supplication: *konenah* is like *shemerah* (guard) and *shofetah* (judge).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: the work of our hands establish Thou it
Psalms.english_translation: Establish it. And twice, “and the work of our hands establish Thou it”: one for the work of the Tabernacle, for which he blessed Israel and prayed that the Presence rest on the work of their hands in the Tabernacle; and one that there be blessing in the work of their hands.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: dwellest in the covert of the Most High
Psalms.english_translation: One who takes refuge in the covert of the wings of the Presence will lodge in His shadow, for the Holy One, blessed be He, shields him. Behold, Moses our teacher — this one urges people to take refuge in the wings of the Presence.
Psalms.translator_note: The word *masi* (“urges”) is translated as it stands in the printed text; its sense here is not certain.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: dwellest in the covert of the Most High
Psalms.english_translation: Like (Song of Songs 2) “in his shadow I desired and sat.”
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s wording (*betzillo chimmadti vesheviti*) differs from JPS Song of Songs 2:3: “Under its shadow I delighted to sit.” The printed reference is “Song of Songs 2”.

Psalms.english_translation: An expression of strength.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I will say of the LORD
Psalms.english_translation: “To HaShem: my refuge” — He and my fortress; and let everyone learn from me. And why do I say so?
To each and every one he says, “who dwellest in the covert of the Most High.”
A wing.
He will shelter.
You will be covered.
It is a shield that surrounds a person close to his four directions; *socherah* is an expression of *sachor sachor* (round about).
If you trust in Him.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: the arrow that flieth by day
Psalms.english_translation: A demon that flies like an arrow.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Of the pestilence that walketh in darkness
Psalms.english_translation: These are names of demons: this one harms at night and this one harms at noon.
Will be despoiled.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: A thousand may fall at Thy side
Psalms.english_translation: An expression of encamping, like (Genesis 25:18) “over the face of all his brethren he fell.”
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s wording of the verse differs from JPS (“over against all his brethren he did settle”).

Psalms.english_translation: On your left a thousand demons will encamp, and to you they will not draw near to harm.
Destruction. And why?
You said, “HaShem is my refuge.” And this is an abbreviated verse.
Psalms.translator_note: The Hebrew term *mikra katzar* is translated literally.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Even the Most High, thy habitation
Psalms.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He, You have made the dwelling of your trust.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: There shall no evil befall thee
Psalms.english_translation: *Lo te'uneh* — will not happen; and so “but God cause it to come to hand” (*ve-ha-Elohim inna leyado*) (Exodus 21:13).
Lest you stumble; and so every expression of striking (*negifah*) — *achopper* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 91:12 (“De peur que ne s’achoppe ton pied”), in forms such as אצופיר, אצופייר; the printed form (אצופי"ר) matches.

Psalms.english_translation: Of the Levites (prophets).
Psalms.translator_note: The word “prophets” is in parentheses in the printed text.

Psalms.english_translation: Because it is said on Sabbaths; and it speaks of the World to Come, which is entirely Sabbath.
At the time of redemption.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thy faithfulness in the night seasons
Psalms.english_translation: And while the trouble of the exile continues, to trust in You that You will keep Your promise — all this is fitting and good.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: an instrument of ten strings, and with the psaltery
Psalms.english_translation: A harp of ten strings.
The matter stated below.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: When the wicked spring up as the grass
Psalms.english_translation: They do not know that their flourishing is only to destroy them forever, for He repays His enemies to their face to destroy them.
In all Your judgments Your hand is uppermost, for everyone vindicates Your judgment upon them.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I am anointed with rich oil
Psalms.english_translation: *Belothi* — to my anointing with the oil of authority; *belothi* is like (Numbers 15) “mingled (*balul*) with oil.”
Psalms.translator_note: JPS Numbers 15:4: “mingled with the fourth part of a hin of oil.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: them that lie in wait for me
Psalms.english_translation: *Beshuri* — in *be'oyyeni*, like *beshorerai*.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed word בעוייני could not be resolved and is left transliterated.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: the evil-doers that rise up against me
Psalms.english_translation: Concerning the wicked who rise up against me, my ears heard from behind the curtain that they will not succeed in destroying us; so I heard.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The righteous shall flourish like the palm-tree
Psalms.english_translation: Like a palm, to make fruit, and like a cedar in Lebanon, to renew its trunk.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Planted in the house of the LORD
Psalms.english_translation: The righteous will be in the House of HaShem.
They will sprout.
They will be fat and fresh, and then “to declare that the LORD is upright.”
They will say in the future.
In His reigning the earth rejoices.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The floods have lifted up, O LORD
Psalms.english_translation: It is an expression of crying out and complaint: Alas, HaShem! Behold, the nations that sweep along like rivers have lifted up their voice, they roar, and the *dokh* of the depths of their sources they lift and raise continually to be haughty against You. Every expression of *dakh* is an expression of depth and lowliness.
Psalms.translator_note: The words *dokh* and *dakh* are left transliterated; the sense “depth” is Rashi’s own explanation.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Above the voices of many waters
Psalms.english_translation: I know that You are mighty on high, HaShem, more than the voices of the many waters that roar over us and than the mighty breakers of this sea, and Your hand is strong over them.
That Your prophets testified and promised concerning Your house that holiness befits it.
And for length of days he waits for them; and although the days have lengthened, they are very faithful to HaShem.
Psalms.translator_note: The subject of “he waits for them” is not stated in the printed text; the sentence is translated literally.

Psalms.english_translation: Like (above 15) “the habitations of God” (*ne'ot Elohim*) — an expression of *navah*; and know that every *naveh* in Scripture does not take out an *aleph*, because they are an expression of beauty, whereas this one takes out an *aleph*.
Psalms.translator_note: The grammatical point about the *aleph* is translated literally. The printed reference “above 15” does not match; the words *ne'ot Elohim* are in Psalms 83:13 (JPS: “the habitations of God”).

Psalms.english_translation: Show and reveal to us Your vengeance.
*Yitamru* — they will glorify themselves, like (Deuteronomy 26) “Thou hast avouched (*he'emarta*) the LORD” and “the LORD hath avouched (*he'emircha*) thee.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Consider, you brutish among the people
Psalms.english_translation: Some fools in the world.
Will perhaps the Holy One, blessed be He, who planted the ear, not hear the cry of His people and His poor?
He will chastise you for this.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The LORD knoweth the thoughts of man
Psalms.english_translation: Your thoughts, that you think to be haughty with the crown of kingship; and know that they are vanity.
Happy are the righteous who are afflicted under your hands, provided that they are occupied with Torah and commandments.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: give him rest from the days of evil
Psalms.english_translation: For the afflictions cause them to be quieted from the days of the judgment of Gehinnom, until he sees that a pit is dug for the wicked.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: For right shall return unto justice
Psalms.english_translation: Their afflictions, until they are justified through them; and after the judgment all the upright in heart will gather, for they will take their reward.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Who will rise up for me
Psalms.english_translation: The merit of whom will stand for us among these evildoers?
*Dumah* — *dumiyah* (silence).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Shall the seat of wickedness have fellowship with Thee
Psalms.english_translation: Can the nations, who make images and molten idols of toil, be likened to You?
Because of a statute — that their worship is a statute for them.
They assemble troops against the soul of the righteous in order to kill.
They find him guilty in judgment in order to kill him.
*Onam* — their compulsion (*onsam*), like (Job 21:19) “God layeth up his iniquity (*ono*) for his children.”
*Vetoafot* — an expression of height, like a flying (*ha-me'ofef*) bird.
An expression of “and he made the camels kneel down” (Genesis 24).
Psalms.translator_note: The printed reference is Genesis 24:11.

Psalms.english_translation: In this world, if you will hearken to His voice.
For nothing.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: even though they saw My work
Psalms.english_translation: In Egypt.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: was I wearied with that generation
Psalms.english_translation: *Katti* — I was disgusted with them, I contended with them; an expression of “my soul is weary (*nakatah*) of my life” (Job 10:1). I fought with them forty years, to make them die in the wilderness, “for I said, they are a people that err in their heart.”
Psalms.translator_note: The quotation “they are a people that err in heart” is Psalms 95:10 in Rashi’s wording.

Psalms.english_translation: To the Land of Israel and to Jerusalem, which I called a resting-place, as it is said (below 132), “This is My resting-place for ever.”
Psalms.translator_note: The printed reference is Psalms 132:14.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: O sing unto the LORD a new song
Psalms.english_translation: This psalm is about the future, and its end proves it: “for He is come to judge the earth.” Everywhere a “new song” is about the future.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Ascribe unto the LORD, you kindreds of the peoples
Psalms.english_translation: And what will you give Him? “Ascribe unto the LORD glory and strength.”
In the future to come this song will be (said).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He will judge the peoples with equity
Psalms.english_translation: Those to whom He will turn a clear language.
Acquittals (*zekhuyot*).
Psalms.translator_note: The word *zekhuyot* is translated as “acquittals”; the sense “merits” is also possible.

Psalms.english_translation: To raise a voice in praise.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: all the trees of the wood
Psalms.english_translation: All the rulers of the nations.
When He takes the kingship from Amalek and from his seed.
This is what is said (Ezekiel 35:14), “When the whole earth rejoiceth, I will make thee desolate.” He prophesied so about Amalek.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed text applies the verse to Amalek; the chapter in Ezekiel is addressed to Mount Seir. The statement is translated as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: In the war of Gog and Magog, as it is written regarding His war (ibid. 38), “And I will be judged with him with pestilence and with blood, and an overflowing shower, and great hailstones, fire, and brimstone.”
Psalms.translator_note: The printed reference is Ezekiel 38:22; Rashi’s wording of the verse differs from JPS (“And I will plead against him with pestilence and with blood; and I will cause to rain upon him… an overflowing shower, and great hailstones, fire, and brimstone”).

Psalms.english_translation: *Zehoraiv* — his brilliance, an expression of “that it may be to it lightning (*barak*), furbished” (Ezekiel 21:15).
Psalms.translator_note: JPS Ezekiel 21:15: “It is furbished that it may glitter.” Rashi’s Hebrew reads *lemaan hayah lah barak murtah*.

Psalms.english_translation: On that day there will be a great quaking on the land of Israel, and the fish of the sea will shake before Him.
An expression of pangs (*chil*), like a woman in labor (Micah 4).
Psalms.translator_note: The printed reference is Micah 4; the words *chil ka-yoledah* are in Micah 4:9.

Psalms.english_translation: For it is written, “and the mountains shall be thrown down, and the steep places shall fall.”
Psalms.translator_note: The quotation is Ezekiel 38:20 and follows JPS.

Psalms.english_translation: *Kedonag* — like *shaavah* (wax).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Ashamed be all they that serve graven images
Psalms.english_translation: For it is written (Isaiah 2:18), “And the idols shall utterly pass away.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: That boast themselves of things of nought
Psalms.english_translation: Those who glory in idolatry [ע"ג].
Psalms.translator_note: The abbreviation (ע"ג / לע"ג) is read as “idolatry” (*avodat gilulim*); the printed form is kept in brackets. Reading from Rashi’s usage in this corpus and the context.

Psalms.english_translation: Your vengeance.
An actual sowing, prepared to sprout for them.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: O sing unto the LORD a new song
Psalms.english_translation: All these are for the future.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Let the floods clap their hands
Psalms.english_translation: The prophets spoke in language that the ear hears — not that the rivers have a palm, but an expression of joy and gladness.
He speaks of the war of Gog and Magog, and then the peoples will tremble, as is said (Zechariah 14:12), “And this shall be the plague,” etc.
*Tanut* — an expression of “my feet were almost gone (*natayu*)” (Psalms 73:2).
Psalms.translator_note: The reference is not in the printed text; the words are in Psalms 73:2, which JPS renders “my feet were almost gone.”

Psalms.english_translation: They will acknowledge the strength of the King who loves justice.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The strength also of the king
Psalms.english_translation: It refers back to the verse above.

Compromise, and the making of peace between people, You have established, by Your saying (Exodus 23:5, 4), “If thou see the ass of him that hateth thee lying under its burden,” etc.; “If thou meet thine enemy’s ox,” etc. And who is it that sees his enemy and does him kindness, whose heart does not urge him to embrace and kiss him? Tanchuma.
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi quotes the two verses of Exodus 23:5 and 23:4 in this order; his wording is given in part.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He spoke unto them in the pillar of cloud
Psalms.english_translation: Even with Samuel; and this is what is said (1 Samuel 9:11–12), “Is the seer here?” And they answered them and said, “There is.” They saw the cloud tied at his door, כד"א “And sometimes the cloud was” (Numbers 9:20).
Psalms.translator_note: The printed abbreviation כד"א is left as printed. Rashi’s wording “And they said, There is” differs from JPS 1 Samuel 9:12 (“He is”).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: the statute that He gave them
Psalms.english_translation: And the statute that He gave them.
He bore the iniquity of Israel.
For their sake.
You were avenging for their deeds: Moses and Aaron (Numbers 20:10), “Hear now, you rebels”; Samuel, because he did not guide his sons in a good way, died a young man (*bachur*).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “Exodus 20” is Numbers 20:10.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: For the LORD our God is holy
Psalms.english_translation: Because He is exacting with the righteous, He is sanctified in the world; and so it says (Exodus 29:43), “and it shall be sanctified by My glory” — through My honored ones.
Psalms.translator_note: JPS Exodus 29:43: “and [the Tent] shall be sanctified by My glory.”

Psalms.english_translation: To give thanks, for the one who says it over thanksgiving offerings.
And why all this? “Know you that the LORD He is God” — when He pays the reward of your deeds. But worshippers of idolatry [ע"ג] have no occasion to serve with gladness, for no reward is paid.
Psalms.translator_note: The abbreviation (ע"ג / לע"ג) is read as “idolatry” (*avodat gilulim*); the printed form is kept in brackets. Reading from Rashi’s usage in this corpus and the context.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: It is He that hath made us
Psalms.english_translation: When we were not in the world.
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s lemma reads “and not” (*velo*), following the written text; JPS follows the read text (“and we are His”).

Psalms.english_translation: With acknowledgment (*hodayah*).
His faithfulness endures. Every expression of truth and faithfulness is faithfulness of promise, that He is faithful and keeps His promise.
Psalms.translator_note: The last clause is translated literally.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I will sing of mercy and justice
Psalms.english_translation: When You do kindness with me I praise You — “Blessed is the Good One and the Doer of good”; and when You execute judgment on me I sing — “Blessed is the true Judge.” Either way, “Unto Thee, O LORD, will I sing praises.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I will give heed unto the way of integrity
Psalms.english_translation: I will set my heart on the way of the perfect.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Oh when wilt Thou come unto me
Psalms.english_translation: The straight way to walk in; and “I will walk within my house in the integrity of my heart” — in secret as in public.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I hate the doing of things crooked
Psalms.english_translation: *Setim* — an expression of “if any man’s wife go aside (*tisteh*)” (Numbers 5:12), to turn aside from the way; *destolement* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists a word at Psalms 101:3 (“Des actions qui détournent du bon chemin”) in forms such as דישטוליר; the printed form (דישטול"מנט) is not among the forms he gives, and its ending differs.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I will know no evil thing
Psalms.english_translation: I will not love, I will not acknowledge anything evil.
That he be my companion, lest I learn from his deeds.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed words are translated literally.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Morning by morning will I destroy
Psalms.english_translation: Day by day I will cut off, little by little, the wicked of Israel who are liable to death.
Israel, who are an afflicted people.
When their soul is enwrapped in trouble.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: my bones are burned as a hearth
Psalms.english_translation: *Nacharu* — the *nun* is auxiliary, as in *na'asu* and *nikku*, and it is an expression of dryness, like (Job 30:30) “my bones are burned (*charah*) with heat” and (Jeremiah 6) “the bellows blow fiercely (*nachar mappuach*).”
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s Hebrew reads *ve-atzmi charah mini chorev* and *nachar mappuach*; JPS: “my bones are burned with heat” and “The bellows blow fiercely” (Jeremiah 6:29).

Psalms.english_translation: *Kaat* is the name of a bird.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: an owl of the waste places
Psalms.english_translation: The name of a bird, like (Leviticus 11:17) “and the little owl, and the cormorant, and the great owl.”
Wildernesses. “I am like a pelican of the wilderness” — so we wander from our place to go into exile.
I examined myself, and behold, I am like the lonely bird that sits alone upon a roof, with no mate.
Sitting alone.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: They that are mad against me
Psalms.english_translation: Those who mock me; an expression of folly (*holelut*).
They saw my misfortune and swear by me, saying: “If it does not happen to me as it happened to Israel — thus may He do to me,” like Israel.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed words are translated literally.

Psalms.english_translation: With tears I mixed.
At first, and You exalted me, and now You have cast me from heaven to earth; and had You not lifted me up at first, my reproach would not be so great.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: My days are like a lengthening shadow
Psalms.english_translation: At evening, when the shadows lengthen; and when it is dark they are not recognizable, but come to an end and go.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed words are translated literally.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: But Thou, O LORD, sittest enthroned for ever
Psalms.english_translation: You who sit forever; and You swore to us by Yourself: as You exist, it is incumbent upon You to establish us; therefore —

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou wilt arise, and have compassion upon Zion
Psalms.english_translation: For You promised (Deuteronomy 32:36), “when He seeth that their stay is gone,” and behold, their stay is gone.

They loved even her stones and her dust. And a midrash aggadah: when Jeconiah went out and his exile, they carried with them stones of Jerusalem and its dust, to build with them a synagogue in Babylon.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: So the nations will fear the name of the LORD
Psalms.english_translation: Your name, when You deliver Your people.
*Ha'ar'ar* — the one who cries out, like (Isaiah 15:5) “a cry of destruction they raise.” Another explanation: *ar'ar* — ruined and destroyed, like (below 137) “Rase it, rase it (*aru aru*).”
Psalms.translator_note: The printed word יעטרו differs from the Masoretic word in Isaiah 15:5; JPS: “They raise up a cry of destruction.” The printed reference “below 137” is Psalms 137:7.

Psalms.english_translation: So will those who see the deliverance say: This deliverance shall be written, to tell it to a last generation.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: a people which shall be created
Psalms.english_translation: That has become a new creation, to go out from slavery to freedom, from darkness to great light.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: From heaven did the LORD behold the earth
Psalms.english_translation: To look upon the affliction of His people.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: those that are appointed to death
Psalms.english_translation: *Temutah* — sick unto death; *enmoriniyda* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 102:21 (“Les enfants de la moribonde”), in forms such as אינמורינידא; the printed form (אנמוריני"דא) is a variant spelling.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He weakened my strength in the way
Psalms.english_translation: He returns to his first complaint: “For Thou hast taken me up and cast me away,” “My days are like a lengthening shadow” — “He weakened in the way, my enemy, my strength.”
Psalms.translator_note: The last clause is translated literally, following the printed order of words.

Psalms.english_translation: To HaShem: “My God.” You —

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: take me not away in the midst of my days
Psalms.english_translation: Do not remove us, to destroy us from the earth by the hand of our enemies, in the midst of our days. And what are our days? All the days of “throughout all generations Thy years.” You promised to establish us before You, as he said at the end of the psalm, “And Thy years shall have no end, and the seed of Thy servants shall be established before You.”
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s wording of the last quotation differs from JPS 102:29, which reads “And their seed shall be established before Thee.”

Psalms.english_translation: From the beginning.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: As a vesture shalt Thou change them
Psalms.english_translation: Like a person who turns his garment to take it off.
The One who stands and endures.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Bless the LORD, O my soul
Psalms.english_translation: There are five “Bless, my soul” here, corresponding to the five worlds in which a person dwells, as our Rabbis said in tractate Berakhot: he dwells in his mother’s womb, he nurses from his mother’s breasts, and so on, all of them.
Like this eagle that renews its wings and plumage from year to year. And there is a midrash aggadah about a kind of eagle that when it grows old returns to its youth.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He made known His ways unto Moses
Psalms.english_translation: He makes known His ways to Moses.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He remembereth that we are dust
Psalms.english_translation: He remembers and does not forget that we are dust, and knows that “As for man, his days are as grass,” etc.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: For the wind passeth over it
Psalms.english_translation: If a mortal illness has passed over it.
Rules.
Which are in all the places where His dominion is.
In the firmament, like a garment (*salmah*).
He makes the winds His messengers.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou didst cover it with the deep as with a vesture
Psalms.english_translation: This is like what is said elsewhere (Job 38:9), “When I made the cloud the garment thereof,” etc.
It is the sea.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The waters stood above the mountains
Psalms.english_translation: The waters of the ocean, which is higher than all the world, stand upon the mountains; and so it says (Amos 5), “That calleth for the waters of the sea, and poureth them out upon the face of the earth” — pouring is only from above to below.
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “Amos 5:9”; the words are in Amos 5:8 and 9:6.

Psalms.english_translation: When You said (Genesis 1:9), “Let the waters… be gathered together,” and at that voice they hasted away, and were gathered to the place that You had founded for them.
The sand that is around its shore.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Beside them dwell the fowl of the heaven
Psalms.english_translation: Beside the springs.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: From among the branches they sing
Psalms.english_translation: *Ofa'im* — branches of trees, and so (Daniel 4) “whose leaves were fair” (*ofyeh shappir*).
Psalms.translator_note: The words are in Daniel 4:9, which JPS renders “The leaves thereof were fair.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: And wine that maketh glad the heart of man
Psalms.english_translation: He also brings it out of the earth; and oil, to make the faces shine with it.
That sustains the heart of man.
In the Garden of Eden.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Wherein the birds make their nests
Psalms.english_translation: Israel shall dwell there.
*Yekannenu* — an expression of a bird’s nest.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The high mountains are for the wild goats
Psalms.english_translation: He created them for the wild goats.
Every expression of *machseh* is an expression of shade and a hiding-place where a person covers himself from the torrent and from the rain: *abri* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 104:18 (“Abri”), in forms such as אבריאמנט and אבריימנט; the printed form (אבר"י) is a variant spelling.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Who appointedst the moon for seasons
Psalms.english_translation: To count by it seasons and festivals.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The sun knoweth his going down
Psalms.english_translation: But the moon does not know its setting: sometimes it comes long, sometimes it comes short.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed words are translated literally.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou makest darkness, and it is night
Psalms.english_translation: Every day You darken and bring the sun to evening, and it becomes night, and in it all the beasts of the forest creep.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The sun ariseth, they slink away
Psalms.english_translation: In hiding places, and they hide there from men; and then every man goes out to his work.
Your acquisitions; the Owner of Your acquisition, like (Genesis 14:19) “Possessor (*koneh*) of heaven and earth” — everything is acquired by You.
Psalms.translator_note: JPS Genesis 14:19 renders *koneh* “Maker.”

Psalms.english_translation: *Rechav yadayim* — a wide place, *large* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 104:25 (“Large détendue”), in forms such as לארייש and לרייש; the printed form (לריי"ש) matches.

Psalms.english_translation: Three hours of the day. So our Rabbis said in tractate ע"א, and so it is explained in the Book of Job: “Wilt thou play with him as with a bird?”
Psalms.translator_note: The printed abbreviation ע"א is left as printed and not resolved here.

Psalms.english_translation: *Tosef* — an expression of destruction, like (above 73) “they are consumed (*safu tammu*).”
Psalms.translator_note: The printed reference is Psalms 73:19; JPS: “They are wholly consumed by terrors.”

Psalms.english_translation: At the resurrection of the dead.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He toucheth the mountains, and they smoke
Psalms.english_translation: As is explained at Sinai (Exodus 19), “And mount Sinai was altogether on smoke.”
*Be'odi* — like “while I am yet alive (*be'odeni chai*)” (Deuteronomy 31).
Psalms.translator_note: The words are in Deuteronomy 31:27.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Let sinners cease out of the earth
Psalms.english_translation: Those who sin (*chote'im*).
His deeds (*ma'allelav*).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Glory you in His holy name
Psalms.english_translation: Boast in the stronghold of His holy name, that you have a patron like Him. *Hitallelu* — *porvantez vous* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 105:3 (“Enorgueillissez-vous”), in forms such as פורוונטיץ ווש; the printed form (פורוונטי"ץ וו"ש) matches.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The word which He commanded to a thousand generations
Psalms.english_translation: The Torah, which He commanded to be made known in the world after a thousand generations; and He saw that the world cannot endure without Torah, and removed from among them nine hundred and seventy-four generations. And one may resolve it by its plain meaning: He remembered for Israel His covenant which He commanded and promised to keep for them for a thousand generations, as in the matter of “keepeth covenant and mercy with them that love Him and keep His commandments to a thousand generations.”
Psalms.translator_note: The last quotation is Deuteronomy 7:9, which JPS renders “keepeth the covenant and the mercy with them that love Him and keep His commandments to a thousand generations.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Unto thee will I give the land of Canaan
Psalms.english_translation: It is the covenant that He made with them.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: And when they went about from nation to nation
Psalms.english_translation: Abraham sojourned in the land of the Philistines and in Egypt and in the land of Canaan; and so Isaac, and so Jacob — all of them went into exile from one sojourning to another.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Yea, for their sake He reproved kings
Psalms.english_translation: “And the LORD plagued Pharaoh” (Genesis 12:17); “For the LORD had fast closed up all the wombs of the house of Abimelech” (ibid. 20).
Psalms.translator_note: The second quotation is Genesis 20:18.

Psalms.english_translation: My great ones; every anointing is an expression of authority and greatness.
In order to exile them to Egypt (I found).
Psalms.translator_note: The words “I found” are in parentheses in the printed text.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He sent a man before them
Psalms.english_translation: (Ibid. 45) “God did send me before you” — and which man? Joseph, who was sold.
Psalms.translator_note: The parenthetical reference is a later printed insertion; the words are in Genesis 45:5.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: His person was laid in iron
Psalms.english_translation: Rabbi Huna bar Idi said: A *shartu'a* was made for him under his beard, so that if he lowered his face, the *shartu'a* would strike him. *Shartu'a* means a spit.
Psalms.translator_note: The Aramaic word *shartu'a* is translated as Rashi explains it.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Until the time that his word came to pass
Psalms.english_translation: The word of the Holy One, blessed be He, to fulfill His decree, that the matter should unfold and Israel go down to Egypt.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The word of the LORD tested him
Psalms.english_translation: He tested Joseph, who was tried and subdued his inclination with his master’s wife; and because of her he was chastised and refined with afflictions, to be put in the prison.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The king sent and loosed him
Psalms.english_translation: Pharaoh, king of Egypt, sent his messengers and released him; “even the ruler of the peoples” is Pharaoh — and he set him free.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: To bind his princes at his pleasure
Psalms.english_translation: This is an expression of love, like (1 Samuel 18:1) “the soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David.” When he interpreted the dream, all loved him. Rabbi Idi said: “his prince (*saro*)” is written — this was Potiphar.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: And He increased His people greatly
Psalms.english_translation: *Vayfer* — the Holy One, blessed be He, His people: He made them fruitful and multiplied them.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: And they rebelled not against His word
Psalms.english_translation: The plagues that He commanded upon them came at His commands, and did not alter His word.
Rabbi Yochanan said: Wherever water was lying, frogs were lying.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: They asked, and He brought quails
Psalms.english_translation: Israel asked for flesh, and the Holy One, blessed be He, brought quails to them.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: a river in the dry places
Psalms.english_translation: Rivers went from the well in a parched land.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: For He remembered His holy word
Psalms.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He, remembered His holy word which was with Abraham His servant, that He promised him (Genesis 15), “afterward shall they come out with great substance” and “in the fourth generation they shall come back hither.”
When You show favor to Your people.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: But were rebellious at the sea
Psalms.english_translation: They were of little faith. They said: As we go up from here on this side, so the Egyptians go up from another side and will come after us — until the Holy One, blessed be He, signaled to the sea, and it cast them up on dry land. “and Israel saw the Egyptians dead upon the sea-shore” (Exodus 14:30); therefore “they believed in the LORD”; but at first they did not believe (I found).
Psalms.translator_note: The words “I found” are in parentheses in the printed text. Audit 4: the quotation now follows JPS (“and Israel saw”) for Exodus 14:30.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He led them through the depths, as through a wilderness
Psalms.english_translation: The Red Sea was in a wilderness, as it is written, “the wilderness hath shut them in” (Exodus 14), “a three days’ journey,” etc. (Numbers 10:33).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: They waited not for His counsel
Psalms.english_translation: They did not hope for Him.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: But lusted exceedingly in the wilderness
Psalms.english_translation: “Would that we were given flesh to eat!” (ibid. 11).
Psalms.translator_note: The words are in Numbers 11:4.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: But sent leanness into their soul
Psalms.english_translation: “And the anger of the LORD was kindled against the people” (ibid. 11).
Psalms.translator_note: The words are in Numbers 11:33; Rashi’s Hebrew reads *ve-af Hashem charah ba'am*.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: They were jealous also of Moses in the camp
Psalms.english_translation: In the wilderness they angered him, like “They have roused Me to jealousy with a no-god” (I found).
Psalms.translator_note: The words “I found” are in parentheses in the printed text; the quotation is Deuteronomy 32:21.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The earth opened and swallowed up Dathan
Psalms.english_translation: It appears that He gave honor to the sons of Korah, not mentioning their father, and hung the corruption on Dathan and Abiram.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: And a fire was kindled in their company
Psalms.english_translation: It consumed those who offered the incense (Numbers 16).
Psalms.translator_note: JPS Numbers 16:35: “devoured the two hundred and fifty men that offered the incense.”

Psalms.english_translation: There is nothing more loathsome and abominable than an ox at the time that it eats grass, for it excretes much dung and is soiled by it. Another version: its spittle.
When the spies were sent and brought out an evil report on the land (ibid. 13).
Psalms.translator_note: Rashi’s wording differs from JPS Numbers 13:32 (“brought up an evil report of the land”).

Psalms.english_translation: With an oath.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: cast out their seed among the nations
Psalms.english_translation: From that hour the destruction of the Temple was decreed upon them, for on the night of the Ninth of Av they wept; and the Holy One, blessed be He, said: They wept a weeping for nothing, and I will fix for them a weeping for the generations.
Moses and Aaron.
“Hear now, you rebels” (Numbers 20:10).
Psalms.translator_note: The printed text has no reference.

Psalms.english_translation: An oath: “therefore you shall not bring this assembly,” etc. (ibid. 20).
Psalms.translator_note: The words are in Numbers 20:12.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: They did not destroy the peoples
Psalms.english_translation: In the days of Joshua.
Of which the LORD said to them (Deuteronomy 20:16), “thou shalt save alive nothing that breatheth”; “they shall not dwell in thy land”; and they left them to dwell among them for tributary labor.
Psalms.translator_note: The second quotation is Exodus 23:33 (JPS: “They shall not dwell in thy land”).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: And He gave them into the hand of the nations
Psalms.english_translation: In the days of the Judges, between one judge and another, such as Eglon and Cushan-rishathaim and Sisera and the Philistines and Midian (I found).
Psalms.translator_note: The words “I found” are in parentheses in the printed text.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Many times did He deliver them
Psalms.english_translation: How many times they anger Him, and He is long-suffering and delivers them.
They became low through their iniquity.
From within prayer.
From within the merit of the fathers.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He remembered for them His covenant
Psalms.english_translation: From within repentance.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: repented according to the multitude of His mercies
Psalms.english_translation: From within the end, when He hears “Save us,” etc. Even Moses included them in one verse: “In thy distress, when all these things are come upon thee,” etc. (Deuteronomy 4:30).
Psalms.translator_note: The first clause is translated literally.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Save us, O LORD our God
Psalms.english_translation: Also now, O LORD our God.
From this world until the world to come (סא"א).
Psalms.translator_note: it is left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: O give thanks unto the LORD
Psalms.english_translation: [The source prints the lemma only, with no comment.]
Psalms.translator_note: The Hebrew source has only the lemma הודו לה׳ with no explanation.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: So let the redeemed of the LORD say
Psalms.english_translation: When He redeems them from the hand of the adversary.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: They wandered in the wilderness in a desert way
Psalms.english_translation: And those who travel through wildernesses also need to give thanks, for sometimes they stray and are hungry and thirsty.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: And He led them by a straight way
Psalms.english_translation: And He leads them; therefore “let them give thanks unto the LORD for His mercy.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Such as sat in darkness and in the shadow of death
Psalms.english_translation: Even those bound in the prison house need to give thanks when they go out of their house of bondage.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: they rebelled against the words of God
Psalms.english_translation: No punishment comes upon a person except for his iniquity.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: For He hath broken the gates of brass
Psalms.english_translation: That were locked before them.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Crazed because of the way of their transgression
Psalms.english_translation: Who because of their iniquities are afflicted with painful sicknesses; they too are among those who need to give thanks. There are signs in this section (that is, the writing of six inverted *nun*s), and they come to be expounded in the place of *akhin* and *rakin* (limiting words), to say: if they cried out before the decree of judgment, they are answered; after the decree of judgment, they are not answered.
Psalms.translator_note: The passage is translated literally. The words in parentheses are Rashi’s as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: *Yachogu* — an expression of breaking, and so “in the clefts (*bechagvei*) of the rock” (Song of Songs 2:14), and so “and the land of Judah shall become a terror (*lechaga*) unto Egypt” (Isaiah 19:17).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Then were they glad because they were quiet
Psalms.english_translation: The waves.
And He leads them.

*Machoz* — an expression of a boundary; and Menachem joined it with “and your vision (*chazutchem*) with the grave” (ibid. 28) — our boundaries, that it not enter into our boundaries; and so “window against window three times (*machazeh el machazeh*)” (1 Kings 7). In Tanchuma, I found.
Psalms.translator_note: The Hebrew is translated literally; the printed “ibid. 28” is Isaiah 28:18, whose JPS text reads “your agreement with the nether-world shall not stand.” The printed words in 1 Kings 7:5 are rendered in JPS “light was over against light in three ranks.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Let them exalt Him also in the assembly of the people
Psalms.english_translation: One must give thanks in the presence of ten.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: praise Him in the seat of the elders
Psalms.english_translation: And two of them must be Torah scholars.
Psalms.translator_note: The Aramaic (*tzurva merabbanan*, “a scholar of the Rabbis”) is translated as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He turneth rivers into a wilderness
Psalms.english_translation: That is, He gives the settlements of the nations to destruction.
To be like a salty land, unable to produce fruit.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He turneth a wilderness into a pool of water
Psalms.english_translation: He gives a ruined settlement to building and restores it to its former state.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: they are minished and dwindle away
Psalms.english_translation: And at first they were bowed and few from the oppression of evil and sorrow.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: maketh his families like a flock
Psalms.english_translation: And He sets the needy man’s family of his seed like a many-membered flock.
*Kafetzah* — closed it, like “thou shalt not shut thy hand” (Deuteronomy 15:7).
Psalms.translator_note: JPS Deuteronomy 15:7: “nor shut thy hand from thy needy brother.”

Psalms.english_translation: Faithful with You.
It is what I sing to You. Another explanation: “even my glory” — even according to my honor I will not refrain from singing to Him, and I will not apportion honor to myself.

The way of other kings is that the dawn awakens them, but I awaken the dawn, for I rise at midnight, because the psaltery and the harp awaken me, as our Rabbis said: A harp hung above David’s bed; when the middle of the night arrived, a north wind blew upon it and it played by itself.
And another verse says (above 57), “unto the heavens.” Our Rabbis explained: here for those who act for its own sake (*lishmah*); there for those who act not for its own sake.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed reference is Psalms 57:11 (JPS: “unto the heavens”).

Psalms.english_translation: For all Your people and Your beloved depend on me.
That I will reign, and the time will come, and I will exult in His word. (See above, section 60, verse 8.)
Psalms.translator_note: The cross-reference in parentheses is a later printed insertion; the verse is Psalms 60:8.

Psalms.english_translation: I will apportion the land of my enemies to Israel; *Shechem* is a portion, like (Genesis 48:22) “one portion (*shechem*) above thy brethren” (and the valley of Succoth I will mete out).
That is, my servant and attendant, like a utensil of service that one uses.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Upon Edom do I cast my shoe
Psalms.english_translation: My service, that their kings will take the shoes from my feet.
I will shout to them with a voice, to make them fear before me.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Who will bring me into the fortified city
Psalms.english_translation: In the days of the Messiah, to stretch out a hand against Esau in fortified cities; “who hath led me” already to Edom, for I struck among them in the Valley of Salt eighteen thousand.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed words are translated literally.

Psalms.english_translation: It is said regarding all Israel.
Esau.
You — they accuse me.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed words are translated literally.

Psalms.english_translation: And I pray to You continually (I found).
Psalms.translator_note: The words “I found” are in parentheses in the printed text.

Psalms.english_translation: Seventy bullocks I offer every year for the seventy nations, and I pray for rain, and they do evil to me (in Shocher Tov).
Before You, may he go out from his judgment guilty and wicked.
*Pekudato* — his greatness, *prevosté* in French, like “and let the king appoint officers (*veyafked hamelekh pekidim*)” (Esther 2:3).
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 109:8 (“Sa charge, dignité”), in forms such as פרובושטיאה and פרובשטיאה; the printed form (פרבושטיא"ה) matches. Printed “Esther 2:4”; the words are in Esther 2:3.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: seek their bread out of their desolate places
Psalms.english_translation: All will ask about them, “What has happened to so-and-so?” from the voice of desolation that has gone out against them.

It implies “from others,” for it is pointed with a *chataf kamatz*; and so “and they shall ask” from the mouth of others — it implies that others will ask about them. And one may resolve *ve-sha'alu* from a heavy form: they will be made to beg at the doors.
Psalms.translator_note: The grammatical remark is translated literally.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Let the creditor distrain all that he hath
Psalms.english_translation: A man who hurries and is eager to do something — the expression *mitnakesh* falls upon him, that is, driven about and stumbling, like (Daniel 5:6) “his knees smote (*nakshan*) one against another” and like “lest thou be ensnared (*tinnakesh*) after them” (Deuteronomy 12:30). So here, let the creditor be Esau, rendering his service, as it is said, “and the elder shall serve the younger.” Another version: “Let the creditor lay hold and approach all that he hath” — *yinkash* — *שייטאצופי"ץ* in French: let the judgment of the creditor be that he grasps and leans upon all his money; and this is Jacob, the creditor, upon Esau, his service, as it is said, “and the elder shall serve the younger.” I found.
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 109:11 (“Que l’usurier se heurte”), in forms such as שיט אצופיץ; the printed form (שייטאצופי"ץ) matches. The rest of the passage is garbled in the source and is translated literally. The quotation “and the elder shall serve the younger” is Genesis 25:23.

Psalms.english_translation: That another may come cutting off his name and his nature, so that not even a remembrance fall upon him in the mouth of the generation born in the world after his name is destroyed — *שארטרמיר"א* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: The iniquity that he caused to his fathers: to Abraham, whose life he shortened by five years, and to his father, he caused dimness of the eyes.

That he destroyed her womb, and caused the day of her burial to be hidden from people so that they would not curse her who bore Esau, as it is said (Genesis 35:8), “And Deborah Rebekah’s nurse died,” etc. “Allon-bacuth” — in the Greek language they call “another” *allon*, for there was another mourning for Jacob besides that of Deborah, for his mother died and they concealed her death.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Let them be before the LORD continually
Psalms.english_translation: These iniquities, before HaShem continually.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: That He may cut off the memory of them from the earth
Psalms.english_translation: Of Esau and his chieftains.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: he remembered not to do kindness
Psalms.english_translation: To occupy himself with the mourning for his father, as Jacob did with the pottage of lentils to comfort Isaac, for on that day Abraham died.
Israel.
The curse of the Holy One, blessed be He, whom he denied.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He clothed himself also with cursing as with his raiment
Psalms.english_translation: He put himself into the curse, and the casting off of the yoke of the offering and the blessing of the priests and the curse of the nations is pleasant to him.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed words are translated literally.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Let it be unto him as the garment
Psalms.english_translation: The curse a covering like a garment (I found).
Psalms.translator_note: The words “I found” are in parentheses in the printed text.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: the girdle wherewith he is girded continually
Psalms.english_translation: A belt; and so “and looseth the belt of the strong (*umezi'ach afikim rippah*)” (Job 12:21) — the girdle of the strong He opened.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: like the shadow when it lengtheneth
Psalms.english_translation: At evening.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I am shaken off as the locust
Psalms.english_translation: *Nin'arti* — an expression of choking and distraction and sealing up, like the locust that wanders and moves and is driven (I found).
Psalms.translator_note: The words “I found” are in parentheses in the printed text.

Psalms.english_translation: *Ya'atu* — one who covers and wraps the whole body, for every garment.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The LORD saith unto my lord
Psalms.english_translation: Our Rabbis expounded it of Abraham our father, and I will explain it according to their words: “The word of HaShem to Abraham,” whom the world called “my lord”: “hear me, my lord” (Genesis 23:11).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Sit thou at My right hand
Psalms.english_translation: Delay for my deliverance and wait patiently for HaShem; “sitting” is only delay, and so it says (Deuteronomy 1:46), “So you abode in Kadesh.”
For the deliverance of my right hand.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Until I make thine enemies thy footstool
Psalms.english_translation: Amraphel and his companions.
*Matteh* — an expression of support, like (above 105) “the whole staff of bread (*mateh lechem*).”
Psalms.translator_note: The printed reference is Psalms 105:16.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: the LORD will send out of Zion
Psalms.english_translation: When you return from the war and your men are weary and pursuing, HaShem will send you Melchizedek king of Salem to bring forth bread and wine (Genesis 14:17–18).
In war.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: in the midst of thine enemies
Psalms.english_translation: Securely.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thy people offer themselves willingly in the day of thy warfare
Psalms.english_translation: When you gather an army to pursue them, your people and those who love you will volunteer to go out with you, as we find there (Genesis 14:14), “he led forth his trained men, born in his house,” and no more; and Aner and Eshcol and Mamre volunteered of themselves to go out and follow him in his aid.
This will be yours in the merit of the glory of holiness that was in you from your mother’s womb, that he recognized his Creator at the age of three.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: from the womb of the dawn
Psalms.english_translation: From when you fell from the womb, as in “they shake fruit down through a skylight on a festival (*yom tov*),” and there are those who teach *meshacharin*.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed words, including the quotation from the language of the Sages, are translated literally; the source of the quotation is not identified here.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thine is the dew of thy youth
Psalms.english_translation: Your youth will be counted for you: the upright ways in which you walked in your youth will be a pleasantness for you, like this dew, which is pleasant and gentle.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The LORD hath sworn, and will not repent
Psalms.english_translation: Because he was afraid that he would be punished for the multitudes he slew, it was said to him (ibid. 15), “Fear not, Abram,” etc. — “will not repent of the good that He spoke concerning you.”
Psalms.translator_note: The last words are Rashi’s own wording and are not a quotation of Genesis 15.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou art a priest for ever
Psalms.english_translation: From you will come the priesthood and the kingship, so that your sons will inherit the name of your father’s father — the priesthood and the kingship that were given to him.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed words are translated literally; the person meant by “your father’s father” is not named.

Psalms.english_translation: *Divrati* — an extra *yod*, like *rabbati am* (Lamentations 1); “on the account (*divrat*) of Melchizedek,” on the command of Melchizedek you are a priest. “Priest” implies priesthood and authority, like (2 Samuel 8) “and David’s sons were priests.”
Psalms.translator_note: JPS 2 Samuel 8:18 renders the Hebrew word *kohanim* “chief ministers.” The printed reference “2 Samuel 40” is 2 Samuel 8:18; the Lamentations phrase is in 1:1.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The Lord at thy right hand
Psalms.english_translation: He who was at your right hand in the war.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Doth crush kings in the day of His wrath
Psalms.english_translation: He will judge the four kings; “among the nations, full of corpses” — this is the tiding of the Covenant Between the Pieces, which was said to him about Egypt: “and also that nation, whom they shall serve, will I judge” (Genesis 15:14).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He filleth it with the dead bodies
Psalms.english_translation: A gathering of corpses; *malei* is an expression of gathering, like (Jeremiah 12) “they have cried aloud after thee, in full” and “a multitude (*melo*) of shepherds” (Isaiah 31:4). And where did He judge with a fullness of corpses? Egypt at the sea (Exodus 15).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “Jeremiah 14”; the words are in Jeremiah 12:6 (JPS: “Even they have cried aloud after thee”). JPS Isaiah 31:4: “Though a multitude of shepherds be called forth against him.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He crusheth the head over a wide land
Psalms.english_translation: This is like the prophecy (Habakkuk 3:13), “Thou woundest the head out of the house of the wicked” — the head of Pharaoh, who was head and ruler over a great land, important above all lands, as it is said (above 105), “the ruler of the peoples,” for all the nations were under the dominion of Egypt.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed reference “above 105” is Psalms 105:20.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He will drink of the brook in the way
Psalms.english_translation: From the Nile, on its way as it went, his land drank and did not need rain water; therefore he lifted up his head and boasted (Ezekiel 29:3), “My river is mine own, and I have made it for myself.” Another matter: this psalm can be explained of David:

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: will he lift up the head
Psalms.english_translation: [1] “The LORD saith unto my lord” — concerning my lord Saul, when I was pursued before him.
Psalms.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under. The comment begins with the lemma “The LORD saith unto my lord” (Psalms 110:1).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: will he lift up the head
Psalms.english_translation: *Le-adoni* — concerning my lord, like “And Pharaoh will say of the children of Israel” (Exodus 14:3), “And the men of the place asked about his wife” (Genesis 26:7).
Psalms.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under. Rashi’s wording of the last quotation differs from JPS Genesis 26:7 (“asked him of his wife”).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: will he lift up the head
Psalms.english_translation: “Sit thou at My right hand” — wait and tarry for my deliverance.
Psalms.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: will he lift up the head
Psalms.english_translation: [2] “The rod of Thy strength the LORD will send out of Zion” — good deeds that are marked in your hand. Another explanation: you will yet reign in Zion, and there a rod of strength will be sent to you, and then you will rule in the midst of your enemies.
Psalms.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: will he lift up the head
Psalms.english_translation: [3] “Thy people offer themselves willingly in the day of thy warfare” — the people of Israel will volunteer to help you on the day that you make an army, as is explained (1 Chronicles 12:21), that they were gathered to him from every tribe: “As he went to Ziklag, there fell to him of Manasseh,” etc., and “And of the Gadites there separated themselves unto David,” etc. (ibid.).
Psalms.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under. The second quotation is 1 Chronicles 12:9.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: will he lift up the head
Psalms.english_translation: “In adornments of holiness, from the womb of the dawn” — because of the glory of holiness that was in you from your youth.
Psalms.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: will he lift up the head
Psalms.english_translation: “Thy youth is thine dew” — a good childhood and a fine period that was in you will be for you like dew, which is pleasant and sweet, and will make fruits for you, to make you prosper.
Psalms.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: will he lift up the head
Psalms.english_translation: [4] “The LORD hath sworn,” etc. — that the kingship will be yours forever.
Psalms.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: will he lift up the head
Psalms.english_translation: “Thou art a priest for ever” — and which of the priesthoods? A priesthood that is above the priesthood of Melchizedek; and this is the kingship, which is above the High Priesthood by thirty degrees.
Psalms.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: will he lift up the head
Psalms.english_translation: “After the manner of Melchizedek” — above the priesthood of Melchizedek, who was priest to God Most High; and if you say that he too was a king, the kingship of Melchizedek is not an important kingship compared with Israel.
Psalms.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: will he lift up the head
Psalms.english_translation: [5] “The Lord” — may He be always at your right hand to save you.
Psalms.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: will he lift up the head
Psalms.english_translation: “Who crushed kings in the day of His wrath” — who fought with Abraham and with Joshua and with Barak.
Psalms.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: will he lift up the head
Psalms.english_translation: [6] “He will judge among the nations, full of corpses” — and furthermore, in the days of Hezekiah your son He will judge among the multitudes of Sennacherib, a gathering of dead corpses, and will crush Sennacherib, who is the head of Nineveh and Assyria, which is a wide land. “Of the brook in the way he drank,” for he boasted that his multitudes drank the waters of the Jordan, as it is said (Isaiah 37:25), “I have digged and drunk water, and I will destroy,” etc.
Psalms.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under. Rashi’s wording of Isaiah 37:25 differs from JPS (“I have digged and drunk water, and with the sole of my feet have I dried up all the rivers of Egypt”).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: will he lift up the head
Psalms.english_translation: [7] “Therefore will he lift up the head” — he praised himself and boasted of his greatness.
Psalms.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Psalms.english_translation: This psalm is founded on the alphabet — one letter at the beginning of the verse and one in its middle, and so all of them, from *alef* to *tav*; and likewise the second psalm. The first speaks of the praise of the Holy One, blessed be He, and the second tells of the praise of the righteous.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He hath made a memorial for His wonderful works
Psalms.english_translation: He fixed for Israel Sabbaths and festivals and commandments concerning which it is said (Deuteronomy 15), “And thou shalt remember that thou wast a bondman in the land of Egypt,” because He is gracious and compassionate to His children and desires to justify them.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He hath given food unto them that fear Him
Psalms.english_translation: Food.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He hath declared to His people the power of His works
Psalms.english_translation: When He gave them the inheritance of the nations, He made known to them His strength and His might. And Midrash Tanchuma: He wrote for Israel the Account of Creation to let them know that the earth is His, and it is in His hand to settle in it whoever He wishes, and to uproot these and settle others, so that the nations could not say to Israel, “You are robbers, for you conquered the land of seven nations.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: They are established for ever and ever
Psalms.english_translation: *Semuchim* — His precepts, “on a support of strength,” made strong with punishments and warnings; and the passages are fixed one upon the other in order, and to expound. And this is what Solomon said, “His legs are pillars of marble,” etc. (Song of Songs 5:15).
Psalms.translator_note: The words “and to expound” are translated literally. Rashi’s wording differs slightly from JPS Song of Songs 5:15 (“His legs are as pillars of marble”).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The generation of the upright shall be blessed
Psalms.english_translation: Who shall be blessed — his seed shall be.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Unto the upright He shineth as a light in the darkness
Psalms.english_translation: *Zarach* — like *hizriach* (caused to shine); and its midrash: He Himself, as it were, becomes a light for them, like “The LORD is my light and my salvation” (above 27).
Psalms.translator_note: The printed reference is Psalms 27:1.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Well is it with the man that dealeth graciously and lendeth
Psalms.english_translation: Who is gracious to the poor and lends to them, and does not scrutinize in order to say, “I have no ability”; and his matters that are needed for food and drink and clothing he sustains with judgment and with measure, and has pity on his property.
He guides his affairs.
His heart is faithful to his Maker.
Leaning and trusting on the Holy One, blessed be He.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The wicked shall see it, and be vexed
Psalms.english_translation: An expression of action, like “and he was vexed (*vayikh'as*)”; therefore it is pointed half with *kamatz* and half with *patach*, and its accent is below.
Psalms.translator_note: The grammatical remark is translated literally.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Who is like unto the LORD our God
Psalms.english_translation: In heaven and on earth: for He raises up to sit and lowers to see; *magbihi, mashpili, mekimi, moshivi* — all of them have an extra *yod*.
Psalms.translator_note: The two clauses refer to Psalms 113:5–6.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: barren woman to dwell in her house
Psalms.english_translation: Zion, which is like a barren woman — He will settle her.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: As a joyful mother of children
Psalms.english_translation: “For as soon as Zion travailed, she brought forth her children” (Isaiah 66:8).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: from a people of strange language
Psalms.english_translation: A people of the speech of another tongue that is not the Holy Tongue; and its companion: “Thou shalt not see the fierce people (*am no'az*), a people of a deep speech” (Isaiah 33); and *nun* and *lamed* are interchanged for each other, like *nishkah*, which is *lishkah*, in the book of Ezra (Nehemiah 13).
Psalms.translator_note: The parenthetical reference is a later printed insertion; the word *lishkah* (JPS “chamber”) is in Nehemiah 13:7. The Isaiah quotation is Isaiah 33:19.

Psalms.english_translation: He took Judah as the lot of His portion and His sanctity; and they too sanctified His name at the descent into the sea, as it is said (above 68), “the princes of Judah, *rigmatam*”; and likewise it is expounded in the Aggadah on this verse, “Judah became His sanctuary,” that Nachshon leapt into the midst of the sea and said, “I will go down first,” and this is what is said, “Judah became His sanctuary.”
Psalms.translator_note: The printed reference is Psalms 68:28; JPS: “The princes of Judah their council.”

Psalms.english_translation: For all the waters of Creation were split.
*Chuli* — the one who causes the earth to writhe; an extra *yod* is in it, like *magbihi, mashpili* and *hahofkhi*.
An extra *vav*, like the *vav* of *vechayto* (above 104).
Psalms.translator_note: The printed reference is Psalms 104:20.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Not unto us, O LORD, not unto us
Psalms.english_translation: Not for our sake and by the fitness of our deeds do You deal with us.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: But unto Thy name give glory
Psalms.english_translation: So that they not say, “Where is now their God?”
Psalms.translator_note: The quotation is Psalms 115:2 in JPS wording.

Psalms.english_translation: *Velo yemishun* — an expression of “my father will feel me (*yemushsheni avi*)” (Genesis 27).
These are the proselytes.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I love that the LORD should hear
Psalms.english_translation: So David said after Saul had died and he was king: “Return, my soul, to your rest, for the LORD hath dealt bountifully with you,” and to You, my Maker, I long, for You have delivered my soul from death.
Psalms.translator_note: The quotation is Psalms 116:7 in Rashi’s wording (JPS: “Return, O my soul, unto thy rest; for the LORD hath dealt bountifully with thee”).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I love that the LORD should hear
Psalms.english_translation: I desired that HaShem hear my voice (סא"א).
Psalms.translator_note: it is left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Therefore will I call upon Him all my days
Psalms.english_translation: In the days of my trouble I will call Him, and in the days of my redemption I will praise Him.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The cords of death compassed me
Psalms.english_translation: The gatherings of our enemies who seek to put me to death.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The cords of death compassed me
Psalms.english_translation: All the *chevlei* of Sheol are an expression of groups, like (1 Samuel 10:5) “a band (*chevel*) of prophets.”
The boundaries of Sheol.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: In the lands of the living
Psalms.english_translation: The Land of Israel, from which my enemies and pursuers drove me out in the days of Saul, and against their will I returned.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I trusted even when I spoke
Psalms.english_translation: I believed the words of Ziba, who said about Mephibosheth when I spoke (2 Samuel 16), “Behold, thine is all that pertaineth unto Mephibosheth” — then I was greatly afflicted: I spoke harshly and was afflicted for you.
Psalms.translator_note: The last clause is translated literally. The printed reference is 2 Samuel 16:4.

Psalms.english_translation: To flee from Absalom.

And betrays the one who loves him, for I saw my son betray me and seek my life, and all Israel repay me evil for good; therefore I believed Ziba and said: Mephibosheth too is false and betrays me. Every expression of *kazav* is only an expression of lack of that in which they trusted — *failence* in French — like (Isaiah 28) “whose waters fail not.” And some resolve it: “I said in my haste” at the Rock of Divisions, where Saul and his men were encircling me and my men to seize us, and there it is said, “And David made haste to get away” (1 Samuel 23:26); “All men are liars” — even Samuel the prophet, who is a faithful prophet, he too is false, for he anointed me as king (I found).
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 116:11 (“Sujet à manquer”), in forms such as פיילנצא and פליינץ; the printed form (פילנ"צא) is a variant spelling. Printed “Isaiah 28”; the words “whose waters fail not” are in Isaiah 58:11. The words “I found” are in parentheses in the printed text.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I will lift up the cup of salvation
Psalms.english_translation: I will bring the libations over the thanksgiving offerings that I vowed, as he said, “To thee I will sacrifice a sacrifice of thanksgiving”; and over that cup, “in Your name I will call” for this deliverance, since the Levite recites song only over wine.
Psalms.translator_note: The quotation is Psalms 116:17 in Rashi’s wording.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: in the presence of all His people
Psalms.english_translation: Opposite all His people.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Precious in the sight of the LORD
Psalms.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He, showed me that it is a hard and heavy matter in His eyes to put His pious ones to death.
*Hamotah* — the death, like *habaitah* and *hachutzah* (Genesis 39).
Psalms.translator_note: The words are in Genesis 39:11 and 39:12.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I am Thy servant, the son of Thy handmaid
Psalms.english_translation: The upbringing of a slave taken from the market is not like that of one born into the household.
You have loosed from my neck bonds and bars.
Thanksgiving sacrifices for the miracles that You did for me.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I will pay my vows unto the LORD
Psalms.english_translation: Offerings that I vowed.
Like *betokhekh*.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: For His mercy is great toward us
Psalms.english_translation: That is, and how much more we, upon whom His mercy has prevailed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: the truth of the LORD endureth for ever
Psalms.english_translation: That He kept His promise that He promised the fathers.
“Give thanks unto the LORD,” etc.; “let Israel now say” — because His mercy endures forever.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: So let them now that fear the LORD say
Psalms.english_translation: These are the sons of Levi, of whom it is written, “Whoso is on the LORD’S side, let him come unto me. And all the sons of Levi gathered themselves together unto him” (Exodus 32:26), in the incident of the calf; and they fought with Israel when they said, “Let us make a captain, and let us return into Egypt” (Numbers 14:4).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: It is better to take refuge in the LORD
Psalms.english_translation: This taking refuge is only an expression of taking shelter in shade, and is a small thing.
*Mivtach* — a sound thing and a strong support; and nevertheless to take refuge in the LORD is better than the promises of human beings.
He speaks of the wars of Gog and Magog, in which all the nations will be, as it is said, “For I will gather all nations against Jerusalem to battle” (Zechariah 14).
*Amilam* — I will cut them off; an expression of “he shall wither and dry up” (above 2).
Psalms.translator_note: The printed reference “above 2” could not be matched; the words *yemulal vayavesh* (“withereth and dries”) are in Psalms 90:6.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: They are quenched as the fire of thorns
Psalms.english_translation: Every expression of extinguishing (*de'ikhah*) is related to an expression of leaping and hurrying: *nitor* — hastening to be torn and cut off from its place; therefore it applies both to an expression of fire and to an expression of water, like “they are extinguished (*nid'achu*) from their place” (Job 6:17), and so “my days are extinct (*nid'achu*)” (ibid. 17), and so “his lamp above him shall be put out (*yid'akh*)” (ibid. 18) — like a flame torn from the wick and rising upward when it goes out.
Psalms.translator_note: The word *ve-nitor* in the printed text is translated as it stands. Printed “ibid. 17” and “ibid. 18” are Job 17:1 and Job 18:6.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou didst thrust sore at me that I might fall
Psalms.english_translation: You, my enemy.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The LORD is my strength and song
Psalms.english_translation: My strength and the might of the Holy One, blessed be He, has become my salvation. The *yod* in *ozzi* is extra; for we do not find in Scripture *ozzi* pointed with a *chataf kamatz* but with a *shuruk*, except for three places; here it is adjacent to *vezimrat*, and therefore *vezimrat* is joined to the word of the Name and you cannot explain it as *vezimrati*. And do not wonder at *vayhi li* — that he did not say *hayah li* for salvation — for there are many like this in Scripture: “and he that regarded not… and he left (*vaya'azov*) his servants” (Exodus 9:21); he should have written *azav* (left).
Psalms.translator_note: The grammatical discussion is translated literally. JPS Exodus 9:21: “and he that regarded not the word of the LORD left his servants and his cattle in the field.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The voice of rejoicing and salvation
Psalms.english_translation: It will be in the future in the tents of the righteous; and what is the voice of rejoicing? “The right hand of the LORD doeth valiantly; the right hand of the LORD is exalted,” etc.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The right hand of the LORD is exalted
Psalms.english_translation: A midrash aggadah: The Holy One, blessed be He, created the upper beings with the right hand, therefore death did not rule over them, as it is said, “Yea, My hand hath laid the foundation of the earth” (Isaiah 45) — this is the left — “and My right hand hath spread out the heavens” — this is the right. And so the psalmist said, “The right hand of the LORD is exalted”: that You created them — for in the height of the world is the right hand of the LORD, which will make armies of the righteous in the future, and with it too He will revive them, and they will live forever, and then “I shall not die, for I shall live” forever.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed reference “Isaiah 45” is Isaiah 48:13.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I shall not die, but live
Psalms.english_translation: I — כנ"י — כע"ג — eternal death; “for I shall live,” etc.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed abbreviations כנ"י and כע"ג are left as printed and not resolved here.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The LORD hath hastened me sore
Psalms.english_translation: In exile, and there all my iniquities were atoned for, and to death He did not give me.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Open to me the gates of righteousness
Psalms.english_translation: And these are the gates of righteousness.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: This is the gate of the LORD
Psalms.english_translation: Of the Temple, which is the LORD’S, and the righteous shall come into it; and there I will give thanks to You, for You have answered me out of the exile.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The stone which the builders rejected
Psalms.english_translation: A people that was low among the nations.
So all will say.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Blessed be he that cometh in the name of the LORD
Psalms.english_translation: They will say to those who bring the first-fruits and to those who go up for the festivals.
*Berakhnukhem* — we blessed you.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Order the festival procession with boughs
Psalms.english_translation: The sacrifices and festival-offerings that were clean and examined for blemish were tied to the legs of their beds until they were brought to the Temple court, to the horns of the altar. And one may resolve the whole end of this psalm, from “I shall not die, for I shall live,” of David himself.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: even unto the horns of the altar
Psalms.english_translation: [18] “The LORD hath hastened me sore” — concerning the incident of Bath-sheba, with afflictions, such as “he shall restore the lamb fourfold” (2 Samuel 12); six months David was a leper.
Psalms.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: even unto the horns of the altar
Psalms.english_translation: “And to death He did not give me” — as it is said, “The LORD also hath put away thy sin; thou shalt not die” (ibid.).
