Psalms.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: even unto the horns of the altar
Psalms.english_translation: [19] “Open to me the gates of righteousness” — and these are the gates of righteousness: those gates of synagogues and houses of study, which are the LORD’S, and the righteous come into them.
Psalms.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: even unto the horns of the altar
Psalms.english_translation: [21] “I will give thanks unto Thee, for Thou hast answered me” — from here on David said, and Samuel, and Jesse, and the brothers of David, as is explained in *Arvei Pesachim*: the one who said this did not say that.
Psalms.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under. The tractate reference *Arvei Pesachim* is translated as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: Happy are they, if all this is in them.

Even though they did no iniquity, their reward is not complete unless they walked in His ways; and so it says (above 35), “Depart from evil, and do good” — even though you depart from evil, all is not complete unless you do good (midrash aggadah).
Psalms.translator_note: The printed reference is Psalms 34:15. The words “midrash aggadah” are in parentheses in the printed text.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Oh that my ways were directed
Psalms.english_translation: The *alef* is a root-letter in the word that drops away at times, like the *alef* of *achavati* in your ears (Job 13:17) and the *alef* of *asukh* of oil (2 Kings 4:2). *Achalai* — my prayers: these are that my ways be directed; and so “Would that my lord were with the prophet that is in Samaria” (ibid. 5), the needs of my lord, to pray that he go before the prophet who is in Samaria. And an expression of *achaliyot* is *souhait* in French, like a person who says, “Would that I were a prophet and wise.”
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 119:5 (“Ah! si… Expression marquant un souhait”), in forms such as שוהייט; the printed form (שוהיי"ט) matches. The words from 2 Kings are in 2 Kings 5:3.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thy word have I laid up in my heart
Psalms.english_translation: I did not allow it to be forgotten by me.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I will delight myself in Thy statutes
Psalms.english_translation: I will occupy myself, like “shall a man regard (*yisheh*) his Maker” (Isaiah 17:7) and “and let them not regard (*yishu*) lying words” (Exodus 5:9).
A thing by which I may live, in the bounty of Your kindness.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Wondrous things out of Thy law
Psalms.english_translation: Things that are covered in it, that are not explained in it.
Wonders from the explanations of Your Torah, which are not explained in it (I found).
Psalms.translator_note: The words “I found” are in parentheses in the printed text.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I am a sojourner in the earth
Psalms.english_translation: Few days.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Hide not Thy commandments from me
Psalms.english_translation: Your concealed commandments, that I may fulfill them, for if not now, when?

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: My soul breaketh for the longing
Psalms.english_translation: *Garesah* — my soul is broken by reason of desire, like (Leviticus 2:14) “groats (*geresh*) of the fresh ear (*karmel*)”; and Menachem connected *lata'avah* with “I abhor (*mit'aev*) the pride of Jacob” (Amos 6:8) — both are an expression of breaking.
Psalms.translator_note: The words of Leviticus 2:14 and Amos 6:8 are as in JPS.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Take away from me reproach and contempt
Psalms.english_translation: An expression of rolling, like “and he rolled (*vayyagel*) the stone” (Genesis 29:10).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Even though princes sit and talk against me
Psalms.english_translation: Even though the kings of the nations of the world mock me for occupying myself with Torah.
*Sha'ashu'ai* — my occupations.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Quicken Thou me according to Thy word
Psalms.english_translation: As You promised me by Nathan the prophet, good.
*Sipparti* — to You my needs and my sin, and You answered me.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: My soul melteth away for heaviness
Psalms.english_translation: *Dalefah* — dripped; that is, diminishing and going.
I set myself to Your ordinances and clung to Your testimonies, to choose the way of faithfulness; to You I ask: remove from me the way of falsehood.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: And I will keep it at every step
Psalms.english_translation: I will keep it in all its paths and the footprints of its ways; *ekev* is an expression of traces (*עקבי*) — *traces* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 119:33 (“Trace”), in forms such as טרצש and טראציש; the printed form (טראצ"ש) is a variant spelling.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Confirm Thy word unto Thy servant
Psalms.english_translation: That which You promised me.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Which pertaineth unto the fear of Thee
Psalms.english_translation: That I and my seed be fearers of Your name, for You promised me on this condition: “If thy children take heed to their way,” etc. (1 Kings 2).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Turn away my reproach which I dread
Psalms.english_translation: Forgive me that sin, and my enemies will no longer be able to reproach me with it.
And I already accept upon myself to pay for the lamb fourfold.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Even Thy salvation, according to Thy word
Psalms.english_translation: Let Your salvation come to me, according to Your word that You promised me.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: take not the word of truth utterly out of my mouth
Psalms.english_translation: And do not separate the word of truth from my mouth, like “Thus God hath taken away (*vayyatzel*) the cattle of your father” (Genesis 31:9) (I found).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 31” is Genesis 31:9.

Psalms.english_translation: In all my rulings and in all my judgments, that I may not stumble in them.
I have hoped.
With a broad and spreading *halakhah* in Israel.
I have asked.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Remember the word unto Thy servant
Psalms.english_translation: That You made me hope, through Nathan the prophet, for Your servant.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thine ordinances which are of old
Psalms.english_translation: That You bring afflictions and turn back from Your anger and forgive; and therefore I shall be comforted.
In a time of trouble and darkness.
A crown that fits me, for me as a testimony and for my seed that is fit to reign, as a reward because I kept Your precepts. So the sages of Israel expounded it (I found).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: that I would observe Thy words
Psalms.english_translation: Fulfill Your words that You made me hope for in this: “You are my portion.”
In the language of “‘The LORD is my portion’, saith my soul; ‘Therefore will I hope in Him’” (Lamentations 3:24).
The loss of a commandment against its reward, and the reward of a transgression against its loss; therefore “and turned my feet unto Thy testimonies,” for I saw that it is the best of them all.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The bands of the wicked have enclosed me
Psalms.english_translation: Bands of wicked men have robbed me, like “he shall devour until (*ad*)” (Genesis 49); so Menachem connected it. And one may interpret it as an expression of *od* (“more”), that is, they have been added and have multiplied against me.
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 49” is Genesis 49:27, where JPS reads “In the morning he devoureth the prey”.

Psalms.english_translation: You with Your commandments: before I pondered them in the houses of study I erred in them and sinned; and now, after I was afflicted in them, I kept Your Torah, for the *midrash* teaches me to turn from transgression; therefore I ask of You: teach me good judgment and knowledge.
Psalms.translator_note: The passage is elliptical and translated literally.

Psalms.english_translation: An expression of repeating and meditating in the house of study, like “Let my tongue sing (*ta'an*) of Thy word” (Psalms 119:172), and so (Malachi 2:12) “the LORD cut off to the man that doeth this, him that calleth (*er*) and him that answereth (*oneh*) out of the tents of Jacob” — *er* among the sages and *oneh* among the disciples.
Psalms.translator_note: JPS renders the Malachi verse “Him that calleth and him that answereth.” Rashi’s Psalms 119:172 quotation uses the JPS rendering “sing”.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: have forged a lie against me
Psalms.english_translation: They composed a lie against me; and so “and Thou smearest (*vatitpol*) upon my iniquity” (Job 14:17).
Psalms.translator_note: JPS Job 14:17 reads “Thou heapest up mine iniquity,” a different rendering of the same word.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: It is good for me that I have been afflicted
Psalms.english_translation: That I was chastised and afflicted, that I might return from an evil way and keep Your statutes. In other commentaries I found thus: “It is good for me that I was afflicted,” etc. — it was good in my eyes when I suffered afflictions in order to learn Torah with pain.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed text of the second explanation is translated literally.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: They that fear Thee shall see me and be glad
Psalms.english_translation: In good fortune, and they will rejoice, for according to my recompense is their recompense, since I am of those who fear You and I hoped for Your word.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: in faithfulness Thou hast afflicted me
Psalms.english_translation: In justice You afflicted me.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: they have distorted my cause with falsehood
Psalms.english_translation: For they declared me wicked for nothing (I found). I say of a fair-faced man that the one who says to him, “He who lies with a married woman — what is his death?” and he did not sin.
Psalms.translator_note: The second sentence is elliptical and translated literally.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Let those that fear Thee return unto me
Psalms.english_translation: That the Sanhedrin separated from him when he became leprous because of that sin; even if she was a divorced woman, he set his eyes on her: “whosoever toucheth her shall not be innocent.”
Psalms.translator_note: The passage is elliptical and translated literally.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: My soul pineth for Thy salvation
Psalms.english_translation: It.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Mine eyes fail for Thy word
Psalms.english_translation: Constantly looking, until they have failed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: like a wine-skin in the smoke
Psalms.english_translation: Like a skin-bottle of leather that dries out in smoke.
That I may see in my days.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The proud have digged pits for me
Psalms.english_translation: Not according to the Torah, those who come to disqualify me.
A Moabite but not a Moabitess; and they pursued me falsely, to bind me.
Psalms.translator_note: The first phrase is elliptical and translated literally.

Psalms.english_translation: In vain my enemies pursued me.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: They had almost consumed me upon earth
Psalms.english_translation: I would almost have been as though non-existent on the earth, and I stood on my clarity; and so “the wicked have waited for me to destroy me” (from entering into the congregation).
Psalms.translator_note: The printed text is elliptical and translated literally; the parenthetical words are as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I have seen an end to every purpose
Psalms.english_translation: To expound and to argue about it, and so “Thou hast loosed my bands” (above 108).
Psalms.translator_note: The printed reference “above 108” could not be matched; the quoted words are in Psalms 116:16.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I have seen an end to every purpose
Psalms.english_translation: For every conclusion of a matter there is an end, a limit; but of Your commandments there is no end or limit to their purpose (I found).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thy commandments make me wiser than mine enemies
Psalms.english_translation: Of Doeg and Ahithophel they said: “their tradition did not come to them in accordance with the *halakhah*.” The secret of the Torah is always in my hands, for from all my teachers I gained understanding: from this one I learned a little and from that one I learned a little (after I had learned from my distinguished master).
Psalms.translator_note: The Aramaic words (“their tradition did not come to them…”) are translated as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: All my conversation was in them.
I held back, like “who hast kept me back (*kelitani*) this day from coming to bloodshed” (1 Samuel 25:33).
Psalms.translator_note: JPS reads “that hast kept me this day from bloodguiltiness.”

Psalms.english_translation: *Nimletzu* — were sweetened.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thy word is a lamp unto my feet
Psalms.english_translation: When I come to give a ruling, I look in the Torah and it keeps me apart from what is forbidden, like a lamp that saves a person from the pits.

I became poor and lowly, like “to humble (*le'anot*) thyself before Me” (Exodus 10:3) and “and the pride of Israel shall humble (*ve-anah*) before him” (Hosea 5:5), which Targum Jonathan renders “and he shall refuse”; and a poor man is considered as dead, therefore “quicken me according to Your word.”
Psalms.translator_note: JPS renders Hosea 5:5 “shall testify to his face.”

Psalms.english_translation: It is a sickness that confuses the mind, and its name is *aniyah* in the language of the Mishnah.
A pleasing thing that my mouth volunteers to You; every *nedavah* is an expression of desire.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: My soul is continually in my hand
Psalms.english_translation: I was greatly endangered, in many dangers close to death, and nevertheless I did not forget Your Torah (and one who has a headache should occupy himself with Torah).
Psalms.translator_note: The parenthetical words are as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: On their paths and on their ways.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I hate them that are of a double mind
Psalms.english_translation: Those who think thoughts of wickedness, like “Therefore my thoughts (*se'ippai*) give answer to me” (Job 20:2) and “between two opinions (*ha-se'ippim*)” (1 Kings 18:21). When you read *se'ippim* it is the name of the thought, and when you read *sa'efim* the expression falls on those who think them.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I will occupy myself with Thy statutes
Psalms.english_translation: And I will occupy myself, like “and let them not regard (*ve-al yish'u*) lying words” (Exodus 5:9). Another explanation: *ve-esh'ah* is an expression of telling and sharpening, as it is translated “*u-leshinah u-leshu'in*.”
Psalms.translator_note: The Aramaic words are translated as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou hast made light of all them
Psalms.english_translation: *Silita* — You trampled; You gave them to be trampled, like “hath set at nought (*silah*) all my mighty men” (Lamentations 1:15).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: My flesh shuddereth for fear of Thee
Psalms.english_translation: *Samar* — like “made the hair of my flesh to stand up (*tesamer*)” (Job 4:15–16), like a person whose hair stands on end — *hériser* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 119:120 (“Se hérisse”), in forms such as הריציר; the printed form (הריציי"ר) is a variant spelling. Printed “Job 4:15–16” is Job 4:15.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I am afraid of Thy judgments
Psalms.english_translation: From the punishments of Your decrees.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Be surety for Thy servant for good
Psalms.english_translation: An expression of rescue, *garantie* in French: be surety for me against the evil (that is, be surety that I shall keep Your commandments).
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 119:122 (“Garantis”), in forms such as גרנטיר; the printed form (גרנטיי"ה) is a variant spelling.

Psalms.english_translation: A promise that You promised me.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: It is time for the LORD to work
Psalms.english_translation: It refers to the verse before it: “Make me understand, that I may know Thy testimonies” — to understand that it is time to act for Your Name; how will they act, those who have broken Your Torah, to find favour and forgiveness, and You will find it for them, and I shall do so for every transgression that is in my hand. And our Rabbis expounded from it that one may transgress words of Torah in order to make a fence and a hedge for Israel, such as Gideon and Elijah on Mount Carmel, who offered on a high place. Further I saw it expounded in aggadah, its explanation: a free man (*panui*) and a stroller who makes his Torah occasional breaks the covenant, for a man (free) must be diligent in Torah all the hours of the day.
Psalms.translator_note: The aggadic explanation is translated literally.

Psalms.english_translation: Because I loved Your commandments, it is fitting for You to teach me a time of favour; and what shall I do for You that You accept me? There are many occurrences of *al ken* that are to be explained as *al asher* (“because”), like “forasmuch as (*ki al ken*) I have seen thy face” (Genesis 33:10), “forasmuch as (*ki al ken*) thou knowest” (Numbers 10:31), “Therefore (*al ken*) the abundance they have gotten” (Isaiah 15:7).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed references are Genesis 33:10, Numbers 10:31 and Isaiah 15:7.

Psalms.english_translation: All my precepts — every matter that You commanded in Your Torah.
They were right in my eyes, and I said of them, “Right.” For all this I am worthy that You forgive and accept me.
Your testimonies are covered and wondrous from men. There are light commandments for which You increased the giving of their reward, such as sending away the nest.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Therefore doth my soul keep them
Psalms.english_translation: All of them, because it is not known which will succeed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The opening of Thy words giveth light
Psalms.english_translation: The beginning of Your words lit up the heart of Israel, for You are the one who gives understanding to the simple, by Your saying (Exodus 20:2) “I who brought thee out…” — You made known to them the good that You had done for them, that they were acquired from the house of bondage, so that they would know that You are Lord over them and would accept Your divinity upon themselves: “Thou shalt have no other gods,” etc. And afterwards You issued Your decrees. Another explanation: “The opening of Thy words giveth light” — the beginning of Your words, in the work of creation: “Let there be light.”
From there all will understand and will open (to begin and to open) in words of Torah. *Tanchuma*.
An expression of swallowing, like “snuffeth up (*sha'afah*) the wind” (Jeremiah 2:24).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “Jeremiah 2:24”.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Redeem me from the oppression of man
Psalms.english_translation: From the evil inclination, which oppresses people. In other commentaries I found: “Redeem me from the oppression of man (*me'oshek adam*),” “Redeem me from the oppression of a man (*me'oshko shel adam*).”
Psalms.translator_note: The two readings are translated as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: The zeal with which I am zealous for Your name against those who forget Your words — it cuts me off and goads me with them (I found).

As it says (1 Samuel 17:14), “And David was the youngest”; I am despised — to belittle myself before those who occupy themselves with Torah, to learn. For I did not forget Your precepts, from expounding and arguing about them, in Your righteousness that is in them, “righteousness and truth for ever”; and even though troubles found me, they were my occupation, and always make me understand their righteousness and I shall live in them, for “that is thy life,” etc. (Deuteronomy 30).
Psalms.translator_note: The passage is elliptical and translated literally.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: And I will observe Thy testimonies
Psalms.english_translation: (The sign of *edotekha*: it resembles *Ben Peretz* — the *vav* is *cholam*; but in the other *edotekha* the *dalet* is *cholam*.)
Psalms.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under. The printed note about vowel signs is elliptical and translated literally.

Psalms.english_translation: Half the night is two watches; and according to the one who says three watches, it is night. David would rise from his bed in the first third of the night and occupy himself with Torah until midnight, as it is said, “That I might meditate in Thy word”; and from midnight onward he occupied himself with songs and praises, as it is said, “At midnight I will rise to give thanks unto Thee.”
Psalms.translator_note: The words “it is night” (*havei laylah*) are translated as printed. The quotation is Psalms 119:62.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: They draw nigh that follow after wickedness
Psalms.english_translation: The counsel of sinners — they walk in the counsel of their sins, and they distance themselves from Your Torah to draw near to the counsel of their evil.
To those far ones who distance themselves from Your Torah, if they return from their way.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Of old have I known from Thy testimonies
Psalms.english_translation: Before the thing was, I knew it from Your testimonies: before they inherited the land You commanded them about first-fruits, heave-offerings and tithes; and before You gave them rest from their enemies You commanded them, “And it shall be, when HaShem thy God giveth thee rest,” etc. (ibid. 25), to set up a king, to blot out Amalek, and to build the Chosen House.
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “ibid. 25” is Deuteronomy 25:19.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou hast founded them for ever
Psalms.english_translation: For all the things that are to be until the end of the world You founded Your testimonies.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The beginning of Thy word is truth
Psalms.english_translation: The end of Your word proves that the beginning is true. For when the nations heard “I am,” and “Thou shalt have no,” and “Thou shalt not take,” they said, “All of it is for His benefit and for His honour.” Once they heard “Honour…,” “Thou shalt not murder,” “Thou shalt not commit adultery,” they conceded concerning the beginning of Your word that it is true.

On Your promise that You promised me. Another explanation: on one of Your sealed sayings, when I understand it. And our Rabbis expounded it of circumcision: David was in the bath-house and saw himself without *tzitzit*, without *tefillin* and without Torah; he said, “Woe is me, for I am naked of all commandments.” Once he looked at circumcision he rejoiced, and when he went out (from the bath-house) he said, “I rejoice at Thy word” — circumcision, which was given from the start by a saying (*ma'amar*) and not by a speaking (*dibbur*), as it is said (Genesis 17:9), “And God said unto Abraham: ‘And as for thee, thou shalt keep My covenant.’”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Seven times a day do I praise Thee
Psalms.english_translation: In the morning, two before the reading of the *Shema* and one after it; and in the evening, two before it and two after it.
On the reading of the *Shema*, which is words of Torah.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I have hoped for Thy salvation
Psalms.english_translation: *Sibbarti* — I hoped.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: for all my ways are before Thee
Psalms.english_translation: You know all my ways.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: give me understanding according to Thy word
Psalms.english_translation: The words of Your Torah as they are in law and in reality.
*Tabbe'nah* — let them speak.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Let my tongue sing of Thy word
Psalms.english_translation: Every expression of *aniyah* is an expression of a loud voice, and the father of them all is “And the Levites shall speak (*ve-anu*) and say” (Deuteronomy 27:14).

That the Levites should say it on the fifteen steps that descend from the Israelites’ court to the women’s court; and there are here fifteen psalms of a Song of Ascents, and our Rabbis said that David composed them to raise up the deep, as is explained in tractate *Sukkah*. And according to aggadah its explanation is: a song for a hundred ascents.
The seed of the wicked, who ensnare people with their mouths with wicked pretexts.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: What shall be given unto thee
Psalms.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: what shall be done more unto thee
Psalms.english_translation: Guarding and partitions: behold, you are set inside two partitions.
And behold, you kill at a distant place like an arrow.

All coals, when they are extinguished outside, are extinguished inside; but these are extinguished outside and not inside. Another explanation: “What shall be given unto thee” — what will be the end of the Holy One, blessed be He, to decree upon you “sharp arrows of the mighty with coals of broom” — arrows from above and Gehinnom from below.
Psalms.translator_note: The word is *retamim* (JPS: “coals of broom”).

Psalms.english_translation: The Congregation of Israel said: since I have already been struck in many exiles, behold, I dwelt in Meshech, with the sons of Japheth, in the kingdom of Persia and Greece and Meshech.
Psalms.translator_note: The passage is translated literally.

Psalms.english_translation: With them.
About them: peace — they come to fight me.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I rejoiced when they said unto me
Psalms.english_translation: I heard people saying, “When will that old man die and Solomon his son reign and build the Temple, and we go up for the festival?” — and I rejoice.
In war, everywhere, for the sake of your gates, Jerusalem, in which they occupy themselves with Torah.
When Solomon my son builds the Temple within it, it will be built with the Shechinah, the sanctuary, the ark and the altar.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: As a city that is compact together
Psalms.english_translation: Shiloh, for Scripture compared these to each other, as it is said (Deuteronomy 12:9), “to the rest and to the inheritance” — rest is Shiloh, inheritance is Jerusalem. And our Rabbis said there is a Jerusalem built in heaven, and the Jerusalem below is destined to be like it.
Where, in Shiloh, the tribes went up when they came up from Egypt, and the Tabernacle was set up within it.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: even the tribes of the LORD
Psalms.english_translation: “Which is a testimony to Israel.” Because the nations used to mock them when they went out of Egypt, saying of them that they are bastards: if the Egyptians had power over their bodies, how much more over their wives! The Holy One, blessed be He, said: I testify about them that they are the sons of their fathers. He placed His Name upon them: the Reubenite, the Simeonite (Numbers 26); He added to them letters of the Name, one from here and one from there; so it turns out that this Name, *Yah*, is a testimony to Israel.
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “Numbers 26” — the forms *ha-Re'uveni* and *ha-Shim'oni* occur in that chapter.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: there were set thrones for judgment
Psalms.english_translation: For also in Jerusalem the Shechinah will rest, and there will sit thrones to judge the nations with them, and thrones of kingship for the house of David.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Pray for the peace of Jerusalem
Psalms.english_translation: And say to it: “May they prosper that love thee, and may there be peace within thy ramparts.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: For my brethren and companions’ sakes
Psalms.english_translation: Israel, my brethren and my companions.
I, David the king: “Peace be within thee.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: O Thou that art enthroned in the heavens
Psalms.english_translation: An extra *yod*.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: With the scorning of those that are at ease
Psalms.english_translation: The scorning of the nations that are at ease — we are sated.
That they despised the valley of the *yonim* (*ge ha-yonim*), which is Jerusalem.
Psalms.translator_note: The source lemma (*ha-buz*) belongs to the second half of the verse, which the site’s JPS text of this verse does not include; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase.

Psalms.english_translation: It is written as one word and we read it as two.
Psalms.translator_note: The source lemma (*lig'ayonim*) belongs to the second half of the verse, which the site’s JPS text of this verse does not include; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: When their wrath was kindled against us
Psalms.english_translation: When their anger was kindled against us. *Bacharot* is like *ba'asot*.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The stream had gone over our soul
Psalms.english_translation: *Nachlah* — an expression of sickness.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Our soul is escaped as a bird out of the snare of the fowlers
Psalms.english_translation: From them, like a bird that escaped from the snare of the fowlers.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: A Song of Ascents. They that trust in the LORD
Psalms.english_translation: They shall not be moved, like mount Zion, which cannot be moved; for as the mountains are round about Jerusalem, so is the Holy One, blessed be He, round about His people.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: For the rod of wickedness shall not rest upon the lot of the righteous
Psalms.english_translation: (For the Holy One, blessed be He, will not give the dominion of the wicked to rest upon the righteous) so that the righteous be careful not to put forth their hands to wrongdoing.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: such as turn aside unto their crooked ways
Psalms.english_translation: Upon people, to find wicked pretexts: HaShem will lead them away with the workers of iniquity.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: When the LORD brought back those that returned to Zion
Psalms.english_translation: From the Babylonian exile; we were like dreamers.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: As the streams in the dry land
Psalms.english_translation: Like water-channels in dry land, which moisten it, so shall we be moistened when You turn back our captivity. Those who sow in it, in the parched land, with tears are anxious, for they think that perhaps it will not sprout; with joy they reap by means of the water-channels when they are sent into it.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Though he goeth on his way weeping
Psalms.english_translation: So Israel sow righteousness before the Holy One, blessed be He, with tears, in exile, and with joy they will reap when their wages are paid in the future.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: A Song of Ascents; of Solomon
Psalms.english_translation: David said this song about Solomon his son, because he foresaw by the holy spirit that he was destined to build the Temple, and on that very day Solomon would marry Pharaoh’s daughter; and of this it is said (Jeremiah 32:31), “For this city hath been to Me a provocation of Mine anger and of My fury from the day that they built it.” Therefore he said this psalm: Why do you, my son, build a house and turn aside from after the Omnipresent? Since He does not desire it, “they labour in vain that build it.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The watchman waketh but in vain
Psalms.english_translation: For nothing the watchman watches over it.
Craftsmen who rise early and stay late at their work and are sustained with toil and labour, with the bread of sorrows, of trouble.
The Holy One, blessed be He, gives sustenance to one who drives sleep from his eyes in order to occupy himself with Torah.
To one who drives sleep from his eyes.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Lo, children are a heritage of the LORD
Psalms.english_translation: To that man.
These are the students whom he raises up, who are to him as sons.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The fruit of the womb is a reward
Psalms.english_translation: The reward of the fruit of the Torah that is in the heart, as it is said (Proverbs 22:18), “For it is a pleasant thing if thou keep them within thee (*bevitnekha*).”
Psalms.translator_note: JPS renders *bevitnekha* “within thee”; the word means literally “in thy belly.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: As arrows in the hand of a mighty man
Psalms.english_translation: To fight with them his enemies.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: So are the children of one’s youth
Psalms.english_translation: The students whom a person raises up from his youth.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Happy is the man that hath his quiver full of them
Psalms.english_translation: Of those arrows. *Ashpah* is a bag of arrows, which they call *quiver* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 127:5 (“Son carquois”), in forms such as קוייברא and קייברא; the printed form (קויכרי"ן) differs slightly from those listed and is left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: They shall not be put to shame, When they speak with their enemies in the gate
Psalms.english_translation: Torah scholars who defeat one another in *halakhah* and appear as enemies to one another (*Tosafot*).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Happy is every one that feareth the LORD
Psalms.english_translation: All these are rebukes and admonitions; because it is written “Happy is the man,” “Happy is the man,” therefore here it says “every one,” to include a woman.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: When thou eatest the labour of thy hands
Psalms.english_translation: One who benefits from the labour of his hands inherits two worlds (in tractate *Berakhot*).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thy wife shall be as a fruitful vine
Psalms.english_translation: Her children are many.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: in the innermost parts of thy house
Psalms.english_translation: Because the way of intercourse is to be in privacy. Another explanation of “in the innermost parts”: if your wife is a menstruant, you shall put her in the innermost parts of your house, so that it not become habitual beside her.
Psalms.translator_note: The last clause is elliptical and translated literally.

Psalms.english_translation: As olives have no grafting, so there is no disqualification in your children.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The LORD bless thee out of Zion
Psalms.english_translation: Which is the gate of heaven.
And you will rejoice in all the good.
And they will not come to quarrel over *chalitzah*, and then “Peace be upon Israel.” *Tosafot*.
They will inherit an inheritance, and no woman will be bound to a levir; then there is peace in the world.
The furrow of the plough, like half a *ma'anah*, a yoke’s length of field.
Psalms.translator_note: The measure is translated as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Which withereth afore it springeth up
Psalms.english_translation: That before it is plucked and pulled from its place, it is dry.
Like “and they shall bring thy sons in their bosom (*bechotzen*)” (Isaiah 49:22), *aisselle* in French; and so “Also I shook out my lap (*chotzni*)” (Nehemiah 5:13).
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 129:7 (“Son aisselle”), in forms such as איישילא; the printed form (איישי"לא) matches. Printed “Isaiah 49:22” and “Nehemiah 5:13” as cited.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: For with Thee there is forgiveness
Psalms.english_translation: You did not give permission to a messenger to forgive, as it is said (Exodus 23:21), “for he will not pardon your transgression.”
On this, that no one should be confident of another’s forgiveness.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I wait for the LORD, my soul doth wait
Psalms.english_translation: “Wait” after “wait,” of the kind (above 27), “Wait on the LORD; Be strong, and let thy heart take courage; Yea, wait thou for the LORD,” and of the kind “watchmen for the morning, watchmen for the morning.”
Psalms.translator_note: The printed reference “above 27” is Psalms 27:14.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: My soul waiteth for the Lord
Psalms.english_translation: Behold, I am among those who look for the redemption.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: More than watchmen for the morning
Psalms.english_translation: They look out and look out again, and look out again for end after end (I found).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: LORD, my heart is not haughty
Psalms.english_translation: I have not conducted myself with authority; I did not make great things — pleasures, buildings and plantings — like what my son did: “Behold, I am upon You like one who has no hands and feet, like a formless clod cast before You” (סא"א).
Psalms.translator_note: it is left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Surely I have stilled and quieted my soul
Psalms.english_translation: “Upon You is my soul, like a weaned child that is placed upon its mother” — a weaned child nursing at the breasts.
Psalms.translator_note: The passage is translated literally.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: My soul is with me like a weaned child
Psalms.english_translation: My soul within me before You is like a child nursing at the breasts of its mother.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: LORD, remember unto David All his affliction
Psalms.english_translation: The affliction of his soul, in that he toiled and laboured to find a place for You.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Until I find out a place for the LORD
Psalms.english_translation: Until it is known where the place of the Sanctuary will be (I found).
The tidings.

In a place that is distinguished and excellent, like “the son of Tohu, the son of Zuph, an Ephraimite” (1 Samuel 1:1) — distinguished, *avginos*. Another explanation: “we heard of it in Ephrath” — in the book of Joshua (15), which came from Ephraim: in all the boundaries it says (ibid.) “and the border went up” and “and the border turned,” but here it says “and the border went up to the side of the Jebusite — the same is Jerusalem.” It turns out that Jerusalem is higher than all the lands, and it is fit for the Temple, as it is said (Deuteronomy 17:8), “and thou shalt arise and go up unto the place,” etc.; this teaches that the Temple is higher than all the Land of Israel. So it is expounded in *Shechitat Kodashim* (tractate *Zevachim*).
Psalms.translator_note: The word אבגינוס is left as printed; I could not confirm it. Printed “Joshua 15” is Joshua 15:8, which JPS gives as “the border went up by the Valley of the son of Hinnom unto the side of the Jebusite southward—the same is Jerusalem.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: in the field of the wood
Psalms.english_translation: In the territory of Benjamin, who is compared to a beast of the forest, as it is said, “Benjamin is a wolf that raveneth” (Genesis 49:27).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Let us go into His dwelling-place
Psalms.english_translation: *Navo'ah* — there, to His dwellings.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Turn not away the face of Thine anointed
Psalms.english_translation: Solomon, when he came to bring the ark in there.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: My testimony that I shall teach them
Psalms.english_translation: *Zo* — “which I shall teach them.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I will abundantly bless her provision
Psalms.english_translation: *Tzeidah* — her sustenance.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: But upon himself shall his crown shine
Psalms.english_translation: *Yatzitz* — will shine, like “and they sparkled like the colour of burnished brass” (Ezekiel 1:7).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: A Song of Ascents; of David
Psalms.english_translation: “Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together” — when the Holy One, blessed be He, dwells in the Chosen House with Israel, who are called brethren and companions, and He too will be together with them.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: the precious oil upon the head
Psalms.english_translation: With which Aaron the priest was anointed.

From his head to his beard, to the opening of his tunic, for the beard lies upon the tunic. So pleasant is the dew of Hermon, which is higher than the mountains of Zion, and the dew descends from Hermon upon the mountains of Zion. As the anointing oil is for greatness, so is mount Zion for glory and honour for Israel; as the precious oil, so the dew of Hermon: as this, so that, like “And it shall be, as with the people, so with the priest” (Isaiah 24:2). And our Rabbis expounded “brethren dwelling together” of Moses and Aaron, concerning misappropriation of the anointing oil, in tractate *Horayot*, the whole psalm. But in the words of Torah and tradition there is a parable and an allegory, the words of the wise and their riddles; and the main point is that the “Song of Ascents” was said about the Temple.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Praise you the name of the LORD
Psalms.english_translation: [The source prints the lemma only, with no comment.]

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He maketh lightnings for the rain
Psalms.english_translation: They are the flashes of the firmament that gleam and give light before the rain, which they call *éclairs* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 135:7 (“Éclairs”), in forms such as אשלויידט and אשלוייטרא; the printed form (אשליילד"ש) differs slightly from those listed and is left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: *Motzi* — an expression of finding; that is, He prepared treasuries for the wind, and there they are found for Him, to send them on His errand.
*Betokhekhi* — like *betokhekh*.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: O LORD, Thy name endureth for ever
Psalms.english_translation: As Your greatness and Your dominion were then, so it is also now, and the power is in Your hand to judge and to avenge our vengeance.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: For the LORD will judge His people
Psalms.english_translation: He will judge their judgment from their enemies.
*Yitnachem* — *yit'ashet* (will tarry).
Psalms.translator_note: The word *yit'ashet* is left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Neither is there any breath in their mouths
Psalms.english_translation: Also, there is no breath in their mouths — even as in a beast; how much more, then, that they do not speak like a man. And since there is no breath in them, there is no need to explain it as the breath of the nostril. This *af* has a *patach*, and *af* “to them and they smell not” has a *kamatz* (סא"א).
Psalms.translator_note: it is left as printed. The grammatical remark is translated literally.

Psalms.english_translation: These are the proselytes (I found).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: To Him who alone doeth great wonders
Psalms.english_translation: At first no angel was created, when He made these wonders: the heavens and the earth, the sun and the moon.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: To Him that smote Egypt in their first-born
Psalms.english_translation: It does not say *bechoreihem* (“their first-born”) but *bivchoreihem* (“in their first-born”): the first-born rose up and cut down the legs of their fathers, who were holding Israel back, when they heard the tenth plague from the mouth of Moses.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: who divided the Red Sea in sunder
Psalms.english_translation: *Ligzarim* — twelve splittings for the twelve tribes.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: To Him that smote great kings
Psalms.english_translation: Here He alluded to thirty-one kings, and compared to them Pharaoh and his army and the plague of Egypt, to mighty kings, harder than they; Sihon is counted equal to all of them, each one by himself; and so He explained above, “to Sihon king of the Amorites, and to Og king of Bashan, and to all the kingdoms of Canaan.” So in aggadah.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed ל"א is read here as the number thirty-one. The phrase “counted equal to all of them” is translated literally.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Who remembered us in our low estate
Psalms.english_translation: In Egypt He remembered us.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: And hath delivered us from our adversaries
Psalms.english_translation: From among them, and He did all this wondrously for us.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Who giveth food to all flesh
Psalms.english_translation: *Notein lechem* — He alludes here to kindness (all the acts).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: O give thanks unto the God of heaven
Psalms.english_translation: He who prepares in them food for every creature. Twenty-six times “for His mercy endureth for ever” is said in this psalm, corresponding to twenty-six generations in which the world was without Torah and was sustained by the kindness of the Holy One, blessed be He.
When we went down into exile, and Nebuchadnezzar asked them to sing before him as they used to sing on the platform.
*Arevei nachal* (willows of the brook).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: our tormentors asked of us mirth
Psalms.english_translation: Kinds of musical instruments, so called because they hang (are hung) them; so Menachem explained; “*ve-tolalenu simchah*” means “*tolalenu* of joy.” And one may interpret *tolalenu* as our enemies, who are mad (*meholalim*) and mock us, an expression of “they that are mad against me (*meholalai*) do curse by me” (above 102).
Psalms.translator_note: The printed “above 102” is Psalms 102:9.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: If I forget thee, O Jerusalem
Psalms.english_translation: The Congregation of Israel says so.
The memory of the mourning of its destruction I will raise, to mention it at the head of all my joy.

An expression of destruction; and so “The broad walls of Babylon shall be utterly overthrown (*ter'er te'orar*)” (Jeremiah 51:58), and so “uncovering (*arot*) the foundation” (Habakkuk 3:13). It applies only to something whose roots are uprooted from the ground.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: In the presence of the mighty will I sing praises unto Thee
Psalms.english_translation: Before the eyes of the princes (angels).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: For Thou hast magnified Thy word above all Thy name
Psalms.english_translation: “Your name” — Master of mighty acts, jealous and avenger; and “Your word” — You promised Your goodness and Your kindness; You magnified Your word above all Your name, for You pass over Your attributes for us and forgive us.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou didst encourage me in my soul with strength
Psalms.english_translation: *Tarhiveni* — You made me great.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: For they have heard the words of Thy mouth
Psalms.english_translation: When they heard the words of Your mouth, “Thou shalt not murder, thou shalt not commit adultery,” they acknowledged the words of Your mouth, regarding “I am” and “Thou shalt have no.” It is fitting to make them accept the yoke of His kingship first, and afterwards to issue all His decrees.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: the haughty He knoweth from afar
Psalms.english_translation: *Yeida* — He will chastise, like “and he taught (*vayoda*) with them the men of Succoth” (Judges 8:16).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The LORD will accomplish that which concerneth me
Psalms.english_translation: He will agree through my requests.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Forsake not the work of Thine own hands
Psalms.english_translation: In the Chosen House, of which it is said, “which Thy hands have established” (Exodus 15).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “Exodus 15” is Exodus 15:17.

Psalms.english_translation: *Bantah* — from afar, to draw me to Your friendship and Your affection.
To bring me near to You.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou measurest my going about and my lying down
Psalms.english_translation: My ways and my lying and my dwelling You surrounded with a partition, so that I have nothing to do without Your knowledge. *Zeritah* is an expression of “a golden *zer* round about” (Exodus 25); so Menachem connected it. And our Rabbis expounded it of the drop of intercourse, that the offspring is formed from the choice part (*barur*) of it, and its meaning is: *zeritah* — an expression of winnowing the grain to sift out the refuse in it.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: art acquainted with all my ways
Psalms.english_translation: *Hiskanta* — You taught.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thou hast hemmed me in behind and before
Psalms.english_translation: My front and my back.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: And laid Thy hand upon me
Psalms.english_translation: *Kappekha* — your palm, and your *ve-redoyekha*, *deshtroyt* in French.
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 139:5 (“Ta main”), in forms such as דישטרוייש and דישטריינט; the printed form (דישטרוי"ט) is a variant spelling. The Hebrew word ורדוייך is left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Such knowledge is too wonderful for me
Psalms.english_translation: Covered and hidden from me is a place to flee from before You (I found).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: If I make my bed in the nether-world
Psalms.english_translation: *Ve-atzi'ah* — bedding and lying.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: If I take the wings of the morning
Psalms.english_translation: If I take wings for myself like this dawn, which gleams for a moment from the end of the world to its end, so I would hasten to fly until I dwell in the uttermost part of the sea.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Surely the darkness shall envelop me
Psalms.english_translation: If I said, “I shall be hidden in the darkness, and the darkness will darken upon me, and You will not see me.” *Yeshufeni* is an expression of *neshef* (twilight).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: the light about me shall be night
Psalms.english_translation: “And the night will be dark before me.” *Or* here is an expression of darkness (*ofel*), like “He spreadeth abroad the cloud of His lightning (*oro*)” (Job 37:11), and so “all you stars of light (*or*)” (below 148), and so “and it lit up the night” (Exodus 14).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed references are Job 37:11, Psalms 148:3 (“below 148”) and Exodus 14:20, where JPS reads “yet gave it light by night.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Even the darkness is not too dark for Thee
Psalms.english_translation: There I have no refuge, for no darkness is dark from You.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The darkness is even as the light
Psalms.english_translation: Both are equal to You.
That think all my thoughts.
*Tesukeni* — *tesokhekheni*.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: When I was made in secret
Psalms.english_translation: In intercourse.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: in the lowest parts of the earth
Psalms.english_translation: In the lower chamber in my mother’s womb.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Thine eyes did see mine unformed substance
Psalms.english_translation: Since You created the world, Your eyes have seen all the unformed substances (*golmei*) of the coming generations.
My form and the shape of my image, before my birth and before my coming into the world, Your eyes saw.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: And in Thy book they were all written
Psalms.english_translation: And all the creatures of the world, like me and like them, all of them also, before they were created, together, are revealed before You.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Even the days that were fashioned
Psalms.english_translation: All the deeds of man and their ends are revealed before You as though they had already been formed, although not one of them yet existed and there was not yet one in the world; and these are the wonders of the works of God and the judgment of His might, that future things are revealed before Him before they come; and so He says, “Before I formed thee in the belly,” etc. (Jeremiah 1:5).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: And in Thy book they were all written
Psalms.english_translation: The book of the generations of man that You showed to the first man.
Like “they were written.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: When as yet there was none of them
Psalms.english_translation: At the end of many days they were destined to be created, and not yet was one of them created in them. According to the written tradition (*masorah*), as it is written [*velo*, “and not”], this is not its explanation; and according to the reading (*mikra*), which is read *velo* (“and to him”), this is its explanation: “days were fashioned” — He showed him the days that were destined to be created, and for his portion He chose one: the Sabbath day. Another explanation: this is the Day of Atonement, for forgiveness.
Psalms.translator_note: The passage is elliptical and translated literally.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: How weighty also are Thy thoughts unto me
Psalms.english_translation: The Congregation of Israel says: How honoured in the eyes of the righteous of every generation.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: How great is the sum of them
Psalms.english_translation: And how mighty are their heads — the count of their numbers, an expression of “When thou takest the sum (*rosh*) of the children of Israel” (Exodus 30:12).
Psalms.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Psalms.english_translation: If I came to count the good of their deeds, they would be more than the sand.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Were I to come to the end of them
Psalms.english_translation: Behold, I have now come to the end of the generations that You have apportioned from then until today, and still this generation is with You and in Your fear, and I have not turned aside from after You.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: If Thou but wouldest slay the wicked, O God
Psalms.english_translation: Would that You would slay Amalek the wicked.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Who utter Thy name with wicked thought
Psalms.english_translation: They mention Your name over all their evil thoughts, and they designate Your divinity to idolatry [לע"ג].
Psalms.translator_note: The abbreviation (ע"ג / לע"ג) is read as “idolatry” (*avodat gilulim*); the printed form is kept in brackets. Reading from Rashi’s usage in this corpus and the context.

Psalms.english_translation: *Nasoh lashav* — like *nas'u lashav*.
*Areikha* — Your enemies; Your enemies took Your name in vain.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: And see if there be any way in me that is grievous
Psalms.english_translation: If there is a way of sorrow and corruption in me.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Every day do they stir up wars
Psalms.english_translation: *Yaguru milchamot* — there will be wars in their dwellings (*megureihem*) and in their settlements.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Vipers’ venom is under their lips
Psalms.english_translation: *Chamat* — an expression of venom, like “Their wine is the venom (*chamat*) of serpents” (Deuteronomy 32:33); for if you explain it as an expression of anger, does an expression of anger fall next to wine? Rather it is an expression of venom, ויצו"ש in French; and so here too an expression of venom falls under the lip.
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: *Akhshuv* — spider, איריינ"א in French.
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 140:4 (“Araignée”), in forms such as איריינא and אירנייא; the printed form (איריינ"א) matches.

Psalms.english_translation: The way of the net is to tie a long rope at its head, and the hunter, when he sees the birds settling beneath the net, pulls the rope and the net falls upon the birds.
*Leyad ma'gal* — beside my path and my step.
*Yad* — beside, like “See, Joab’s field is near mine (*el yadi*)” (2 Samuel 14:30).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Grant not, O LORD, the desires of the wicked
Psalms.english_translation: Amalek the wicked.
His thought do not make succeed.
“Lest they exalt themselves, Selah.” And our Rabbis explained *zemamo* as an expression of a bridle that muzzles (*zomem*) the mouth of the camel, and it is Mishnaic language.
*Al tafek* — do not bring out from his jaws.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: As for the head of those that compass me about
Psalms.english_translation: A company — the sum of the troops of Esau, who say to turn me away from You; “let the mischief of their own lips cover them” (I found).
Psalms.translator_note: The first phrase is elliptical and translated literally.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Let burning coals fall upon them
Psalms.english_translation: The coals will be inclined upon them; they will lie in them until they totter and go out of themselves; it turns out that the body is consumed and perishes.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Let them be cast into the fire
Psalms.english_translation: The One who casts down and avenges: the coals of Gehinnom; “into deep pits He will cast them, that they rise not up again.”
*Bamehamorot* — in wars and strife; an expression of “ye have been rebellious (*mamrim*)” (Deuteronomy 9).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “Deuteronomy 9”; the word occurs at Deuteronomy 9:7 (and 9:24).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: A slanderer shall not be established in the earth
Psalms.english_translation: Esau, for “because venison was in his mouth” — he hunted his father with his mouth.
Psalms.translator_note: The phrase *ki tzayid befiv* is Genesis 25:28, where JPS reads “because he did eat of his venison.”

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: shall be hunted with thrust upon thrust
Psalms.english_translation: The evil that he does will hunt him.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I know that the LORD will maintain the cause of the poor
Psalms.english_translation: That at the end of things HaShem will do justice for the poor and avenge the vengeance of His servants.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Surely the righteous shall give thanks unto Thy name
Psalms.english_translation: He will hasten and act, so that the righteous will give thanks to His name.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The lifting up of my hands
Psalms.english_translation: That which I lift up my palms to You.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Set a guard, O LORD, to my mouth
Psalms.english_translation: When I pray before You, that I speak with eloquence, so that it be acceptable.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Keep watch at the door of my lips
Psalms.english_translation: *Dal sefatai* — it is the upper lip (like the “doors (*daltot*) of my lips”).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Incline not my heart to any evil thing
Psalms.english_translation: Let it not be inclined to evil.
*Et ishim* — with men (I found).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: And let me not eat of their dainties
Psalms.english_translation: And I shall not recline at their meal.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Let the righteous smite me in kindness, and correct me
Psalms.english_translation: It is good for me that a true prophet and a righteous man should rebuke me and chastise me, for all his blows and his rebuke are kindness.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Oil so choice let not my head refuse
Psalms.english_translation: The oil of kingship that was poured upon my head, as it is said (above 23), “Thou hast anointed my head with oil” — let it not turn my head away from the rebuke of the righteous, to go and fight the workers of iniquity.
Psalms.translator_note: The printed “above 23” is Psalms 23:5.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: For still is my prayer because of their wickedness
Psalms.english_translation: For all the while my prayer is in my mouth, behold, it is on account of the evil deeds of the workers of iniquity, that I not stumble through them.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Their judges are thrown down by the sides of the rock
Psalms.english_translation: For their judges and leaders were thrown down from the path of good by the hand of the evil inclination and the stone heart, which is hard as a rock.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: And they shall hear my words, that they are sweet
Psalms.english_translation: The sweet words that I speak concerning the commandments of the Holy One, blessed be He — and they do not return from their evil way. And our Rabbis, in the Baraita of the Sifra, expounded it of Moses and Aaron, who died on account of the rock; but I cannot make the verse fit, its end with its beginning. And one may reconcile it and say: these are like the perverse, like those on whose account Moses and Aaron died at the rock, because these too heard sweet words and do not return.
Psalms.translator_note: The last sentence is elliptical and translated literally.

Psalms.english_translation: Wood.
So our bones were scattered, to reach the door of death, on account of the evil deeds of transgressors.
*Polei'ach* — an expression of splitting, like “He cleaveth my reins asunder (*yefalach kilyotai*)” (Job 15).
Psalms.translator_note: Printed “Job 15” is Job 16:13.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: For mine eyes are unto Thee, O GOD the Lord
Psalms.english_translation: It refers to the verses above: “Set a guard…” and “Incline not my heart…”; “for mine eyes are unto Thee,” etc.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: O pour not out my soul
Psalms.english_translation: *Al ta'ar nafshi* — do not send my soul out from before You, like “and she emptied (*vate'ar*) her pitcher into the trough” (Genesis 24:20).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Let the wicked fall into their own nets
Psalms.english_translation: Let the wicked man himself fall into his nets, which he spreads for my feet.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: when he was in the cave
Psalms.english_translation: In which he cut off the skirt of the robe that belonged to Saul.
How many snares there are in it.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: For there is no man that knoweth me
Psalms.english_translation: There is none among all the servants of Saul who would protest (lit. wipe with his hand).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The righteous shall crown themselves because of me
Psalms.english_translation: For my sake the righteous will crown You and give thanks to Your name, because You support those who fear You.
To believe the promise that You promised me.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: For the enemy hath persecuted my soul
Psalms.english_translation: That is, if I have sinned against You, behold, I have been smitten; and this psalm was said concerning all Israel.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: My heart within me is appalled
Psalms.english_translation: An expression of numbness and astonishment, like “and I remained there appalled (*mashamim*) among them seven days” (Ezekiel 3:15) and “So Tamar remained desolate (*shomemah*)” (2 Samuel 13:20).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: I remember the days of old
Psalms.english_translation: That You did many wonders for us.
In exile.
One who desires and does not attain is called “failing of eyes” and “failing of spirit.”
When redemption sprouts (I found).

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Cause me to know the way wherein I should walk
Psalms.english_translation: “I have lifted up my soul to You” — that You accept my request (סא"א).
Psalms.translator_note: it is left as printed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: With Thee have I hidden myself
Psalms.english_translation: My troubles I conceal from every person, to tell them to You.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Who subdueth my people under me
Psalms.english_translation: He who beats out and spreads my people to rest in its place, like (Job 12) “He spreadeth (*shotei'ach*) the nations” — He enlarges them; *rodeid* is the Targum of *roke'a* (“beating out”), as it is translated “and they beat out (*vayraku'u*)” as “and they spread out (*ve-redidu*).” Some explain “who subdueth peoples under me” — who weakens peoples under me. But in an exact, corrected book it is *ami* (“my people”), with a Masorah note on it: three [are] “think *amim*” and read *ami*; and on *tachti* there is a Masorah note: *tachtav* is read.
Psalms.translator_note: The Masorah note is elliptical and translated literally. Printed “Job 12” is Job 12:23, where JPS reads “He enlargeth the nations.”

Psalms.english_translation: What are Persia and Ishmael before You, that You took note of them to increase greatness for them.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: His days are as a shadow that passeth away
Psalms.english_translation: Solomon said, “and he maketh them as a shadow” (Ecclesiastes 6:12), and he did not specify whether the shadow of a palm tree or the shadow of a wall, which are already fixed; his father explained: “as a shadow that passeth away” — the shadow of a bird in flight.
Psalms.translator_note: JPS Ecclesiastes 6:12 reads “which he spendeth as a shadow.”

Psalms.english_translation: *Patzeni* — take me out; and it is an expression of rescue; and so “who rescueth (*hapotzeh*) David His servant” (I found).

Scripture attributes falsehood (*shav*) to the mouth and lying (*sheker*) to the right hand. They came to tell with the mouth invented exaggerations on falsehood, even to change what is known; they came to stretch out their right hand for an oath. They desist from *shav*, for which one is caught like a thief, but they swear with *sheker*, for such is their lot.
Psalms.translator_note: The passage is elliptical and translated literally.

Psalms.english_translation: He speaks of the Rock of Divisions, where David was close to being caught by Saul, and “a messenger (*mal'ach*) came to Saul, ‘Haste thee, and come’” (1 Samuel 23:27); He saved Saul from shedding innocent blood and David from being killed.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Rescue me, and deliver me out of the hand of strangers
Psalms.english_translation: As You rescued then, so rescue me now.
That is, even now this generation is righteous.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: We whose sons are as plants
Psalms.english_translation: They have no blemish to such a degree; they are clean of sin (I found).
With a good name — that they are like saplings in their youth, growing all their days; and it is impossible to fulfil all this praise except in the generation of Hezekiah.
Tall in stature, comely, like the corners of a house of stones; for the corner of a stone is aligned opposite its fellow and rises upward until the corners are straight.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: carved after the fashion of a palace
Psalms.english_translation: Praised in the mouths of those who see them, and they compare them to the form of the stature of the Temple. And our Rabbis explained “our daughters as corners”: filled with desire, like the corners of the altar that are filled with blood, and they are not known except by their husbands.
The corners of our storehouses are full of good.
They supply food from year to year; “from *zan* to *zan*” — from the time of the ingathering of food for this year until the time of the ingathering for another year; *zan* is גובירניי"ל in French.
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 144:13, in forms such as גובירניל and גוברנייל; the printed form (גובירניי"ל) is a variant spelling.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Whose sheep increase by thousands and ten thousands
Psalms.english_translation: They yield fruit by thousands and by ten thousands.
Our great leaders (*alufim*) are borne upon their smaller ones, for the smaller listen to the greater, and from this there is no breach among us.
Psalms.translator_note: The sentence is translated literally.

Psalms.english_translation: No evil report goes out afar.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: And no outcry in our broad places
Psalms.english_translation: And no sound of the tumult of war.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Happy is the people that is in such a case
Psalms.english_translation: For all this good is His.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: One generation shall laud Thy works to another
Psalms.english_translation: And I too will speak of the glorious splendour of Thy majesty.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: And men shall speak of the might of Thy tremendous acts
Psalms.english_translation: And I too will tell of Your greatness.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: They shall utter the fame of Thy great goodness
Psalms.english_translation: One generation to another will speak of Your might, saying to one another: It is good for us to make known to the children of men His mighty acts and the glorious splendour of the kingdom of the Holy One, blessed be He. (I found)

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The LORD upholdeth all that fall
Psalms.english_translation: The *nun* is missing from the alphabet, because David saw in it a severe downfall — “The virgin of Israel is fallen, she shall no more rise” (Amos 5:2) — and he came back and supported it by the holy spirit: “The LORD upholdeth all that fall.”
Psalms.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: satisfiest every living thing with favour
Psalms.english_translation: According to its sustenance He satisfies His goodness and His will and His blessing. *Ratzon* — אפיימנ"ט in French.
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 145:16, in forms such as אפיימנט and אפיימניט; the printed form (אפיימנ"ט) matches.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: My mouth shall speak the praise of the LORD
Psalms.english_translation: And also all flesh will bless His holy name for ever and ever.
While I am alive.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: In that very day his thoughts perish
Psalms.english_translation: *Eshtonotav* — his thoughts.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Happy is he whose help is the God of Jacob
Psalms.english_translation: He who has the God of Jacob as his help, for the Holy One, blessed be He, promised him: “Behold, I am with thee, and will keep thee, and bring thee back” (Genesis 28:15). And why is he happy? Because He makes heaven and earth and the sea; and since everything is His, it is in His hand to guard him on sea and on land. But a king of idol-worshippers [עו"ג] — if he guards him on land, he cannot guard him on sea.
Psalms.translator_note: The abbreviation עו"ג is read as “idol-worshippers” (*ovedei gilulim*); the printed form is kept in brackets. This reading is from Rashi’s usage and the context, not from a dictionary.

Psalms.english_translation: At the end of many generations He fulfils and guards the truth of His promise.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He upholdeth the fatherless and the widow
Psalms.english_translation: *Ye'odeid* — an expression of strength.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: The LORD will reign for ever
Psalms.english_translation: He will fulfil His kingship by guarding His children.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: For it is good to sing praises unto our God
Psalms.english_translation: For it is good to sing to Him.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He giveth to the beast his food
Psalms.english_translation: *Lachmah* — its food.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: And to the young ravens which cry
Psalms.english_translation: Our Rabbis explained that it is cruel to its young, and the Holy One, blessed be He, has mercy on them and prepares for them gnats from their own excrement, which enter their mouths.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He delighteth not in the strength of the horse
Psalms.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He taketh no pleasure in the legs of a man
Psalms.english_translation: And not in the swiftness of the running of the legs of man does He take pleasure.
The best of fat wheat.
*Gelée* in French (גליז"א).
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 147:16 (“Gelée”), in forms such as גליד and גלזא; the printed form (גליז"א) is a variant spelling.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He casteth forth His ice like crumbs
Psalms.english_translation: The water freezes and is made into pieces, pieces. And a midrash aggadah: *kefatim* — everything is according to the burden of creatures; the poor man, according to the lack of his clothing, it is lightened for him.
Psalms.translator_note: The aggadic sentence is translated literally.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Who can stand before His cold
Psalms.english_translation: That it not be chilly in his cold.
Psalms.translator_note: The sentence is elliptical and translated literally.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He sendeth forth His word, and melteth them
Psalms.english_translation: Those pieces.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He causeth His wind to blow
Psalms.english_translation: A west wind, to stop the ice, and the waters flow.
Stars of night.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: He hath made a decree which shall not be transgressed
Psalms.english_translation: In them: this one serves by day and that one serves by night, and that decree will not be transgressed.
Large fish.
*Glace* in French (גלצ"א).
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 148:8 (“Glace”), in forms such as גלצא; the printed form (גלצ"א) matches.

Psalms.english_translation: *Neige* in French (נייף).
Psalms.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Psalms.english_translation: A matter of *sho'ah*, which they call ברואינ"ה in French.
Psalms.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Psalms 148:8 (“Brouillard”), in forms such as ברואינא and ברואינט; the printed form (ברואינ"ה) is a variant spelling.

Psalms.english_translation: That which does His word and His errand. And our Rabbis said that these things were at first stored away in heaven, and David came and brought them down to earth, because they are kinds of punishment, and it is not fitting for them to be stored in the dwellings of the Holy One, blessed be He.

Psalms.english_lemma_JPS: Let the high praises of God be in their mouth
Psalms.english_translation: And they have a two-edged sword in their hand.
Chains.

“And I will lay My vengeance upon Edom,” etc. (Ezekiel 25:14). And if you say that Ezekiel was not yet born when David said this: David prophesied concerning the end of the redemption, and when the end comes, that judgment has been written for many days.
They are kinds of musical instruments.
Cymbals that make a sound.

*Shama* is a noun, like *shema* with a *segol*, and because of the *etnachta* it is pointed with a great *kamatz*, and therefore its accent is above, under the *shin*. Completed is the book of Psalms.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The proverbs of Solomon
Proverbs.english_translation: All his words are examples and parables: a parable of the Torah in the good woman, and a parable of the idolaters in the harlot woman.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: To know wisdom and instruction
Proverbs.english_translation: He said these parables to make known to people (wisdom and instruction) that they should labour in Torah, which is wisdom and instruction and understanding.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Justice, and right, and equity
Proverbs.english_translation: *Tzedek* — charity from one’s money. *Mishpat* — to judge truly. *Meisharim* — that is compromise, a smooth and level way, equal for this one and for that one.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: To give prudence to the simple
Proverbs.english_translation: Koheleth said these parables to acquire through them prudence for the simple, “to the young man knowledge” — and also to the young man who is stripped of all learning, who has not yet learned anything.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: and discretion
Proverbs.english_translation: A thought of counsel.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: That the wise man may hear
Proverbs.english_translation: These parables.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: and increase in learning
Proverbs.english_translation: Upon his wisdom.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: learning
Proverbs.english_translation: Study.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the wise man
Proverbs.english_translation: This is the master of tradition.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the man of understanding
Proverbs.english_translation: He adds to the knowledge of the wise man, for he knows how to understand one thing from another, and adds to his tradition.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: To understand a proverb, and a figure
Proverbs.english_translation: That they give heart to understand in the Scriptures the two ways, the parable (*mashal*) and the figure (*melitzah*), that they understand what He compared to the *melitzah*, and that their hearts not turn away even from the *melitzah*, for it too they must understand. When he said “to deliver thee from the strange woman, from the alien woman,” it was said about the vanities of Egypt; behold, the parable. And also the figure, for he brought out his parable in the language of a woman; understand it and beware of the strange woman (another version: harlot).
Proverbs.translator_note: The quotation “to deliver thee from the strange woman, from the alien woman” is Proverbs 2:16.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The words of the wise, and their dark sayings
Proverbs.english_translation: Those who expound the markings of Scripture: full and defective spelling, allusion, analogy and riddle.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge
Proverbs.english_translation: Up to here he has explained for what purpose Solomon made this book, and now the book begins.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge
Proverbs.english_translation: It is the choicest part of the essence of knowledge, and it shall be first for you to know: before your wisdom put fear of your Creator first, and it will put it into your heart to act with wisdom and knowledge; for the fools who do not fear HaShem despise wisdom and discipline.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Hear, my son, the instruction of thy father
Proverbs.english_translation: What the Holy One, blessed be He, gave to Moses in writing and orally.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the teaching of thy mother
Proverbs.english_translation: *Immekha* — your nation, the Congregation of Israel, like “How was (*mah*) thy mother (*imekha*) a lioness” (Ezekiel 19:2); and these are the words of the scribes, who innovated and added and made fences for the Torah.
Proverbs.translator_note: JPS renders the Ezekiel verse “How was thy mother a lioness.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: a chaplet of grace unto thy head
Proverbs.english_translation: *Livyat chen* — a joining of grace they are for your head; that is, the Torah and the instruction will be a wreath of grace for your head, and like necklaces of ornaments of gold they will be.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: chains about thy neck
Proverbs.english_translation: *Legargerotekha* — to your neck; and because the windpipe is made rings upon rings, the neck is called in the plural.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: if sinners entice thee
Proverbs.english_translation: *Chatta'im* — *chote'im* (“those who sin”).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Consent thou not
Proverbs.english_translation: Do not consent to them.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Let us lie in wait for blood
Proverbs.english_translation: To shed blood.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Let us lurk
Proverbs.english_translation: An expression of ambush.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Let us lurk for the innocent without cause
Proverbs.english_translation: Scripture says that their lurking is for the innocent without cause.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Let us swallow them up alive
Proverbs.english_translation: The innocent, while they are alive.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: as the grave
Proverbs.english_translation: That swallows an entire body.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And whole
Proverbs.english_translation: It is not an expression of “righteous” but an expression of “whole”: we will swallow them while they are whole, like a man who goes down into the pit while whole; that is, while they are in their wealth we will kill them and inherit their property.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Cast in thy lot among us
Proverbs.english_translation: If you wish, you may divide, or if you wish, it will be a partnership.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Let us all have one purse
Proverbs.english_translation: Together.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: run to evil
Proverbs.english_translation: They run for their own evil and do not know to give heed to the matter.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: For in vain the net is spread
