Proverbs.english_translation: For the birds that see wheat and legumes scattered upon the net — it is for nothing in their eyes, for they do not recognize for what it is strewn, and they descend upon it and eat.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And these lie in wait for their own blood
Proverbs.english_translation: And the hunters lie in wait for the blood of the birds.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: So are the ways of every one that is greedy of gain
Proverbs.english_translation: He robs a robbery that is pleasant and desirable to him, and for nothing is it to him, and its end: “It taketh away the life of the owners thereof” — his own life, who has now become the owner of the money that he robbed from his fellow.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Wisdom crieth aloud in the streets
Proverbs.english_translation: Behold, the wisdoms of the Torah cry out in its streets, to warn you to turn aside to them; and what are its streets? Houses of study.
Proverbs.translator_note: The phrase “to turn aside to them” is translated literally.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: in the broad places
Proverbs.english_translation: In a place where they broaden it. So expounded Rabbi Tanchuma.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: She calleth at the head of the noisy streets
Proverbs.english_translation: In the place where she is heard and proclaimed, there she calls and says — the matter below: “How long, you thoughtless,” etc.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: At the entrances of the gates
Proverbs.english_translation: They are the place where the elders sit.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: you thoughtless
Proverbs.english_translation: *Petayim* — those who are enticed by inciters and heretics (*minim*).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: will you love thoughtlessness
Proverbs.english_translation: *Hasatah* — a noun for foolishness (*petut*), like כלי קרי (שני סא"א) שפי.
Proverbs.translator_note: it is left as printed. The quotation is left as printed.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: I have stretched out my hand
Proverbs.english_translation: To hint to them to turn aside to me, like a person who signals to his fellow with his hand and stretches out his hand to him to turn aside to him.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: you have set at nought
Proverbs.english_translation: *Vatifra'u* — and you annulled.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: all my counsel
Proverbs.english_translation: That I counselled to raise you up in the world.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: your dread cometh as a storm
Proverbs.english_translation: Like a cloud that rises suddenly.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: your calamity cometh on as a whirlwind
Proverbs.english_translation: *Tourbillon* in French.
Proverbs.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Proverbs 1:27 (“Comme un tourbillon”), in forms such as טורביל and טורבילון; the printed form (טורבילו"ן) matches.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: cometh on
Proverbs.english_translation: *Ye'etah* — will come.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: They will seek me earnestly
Proverbs.english_translation: They will seek me.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the fruit of their own way
Proverbs.english_translation: The fruits, which they eat in their lifetime, in the troubles that find them; and the principal is kept for them in Gehinnom.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: For the waywardness of the thoughtless shall slay them
Proverbs.english_translation: Those whose heart is wayward.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And the confidence of fools shall destroy them
Proverbs.english_translation: Because the wicked see that they prosper, they cling to their wickedness and do not return.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: shall dwell securely
Proverbs.english_translation: In this world.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: shall be quiet
Proverbs.english_translation: In the World to Come.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: without fear of evil
Proverbs.english_translation: The judgment of Gehinnom.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: shall be quiet
Proverbs.english_translation: And he will be tranquil and at ease; and *sha'anan* is an expression of the future, therefore it is pointed with a *patach*.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: My son, if thou wilt receive my words
Proverbs.english_translation: My son, you will be, if you receive my words.
Proverbs.translator_note: The sentence is elliptical and translated literally.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: So that thou make thine ear attend unto wisdom
Proverbs.english_translation: To occupy yourself in Torah.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Then shalt thou understand the fear of the LORD
Proverbs.english_translation: It refers to the matter above, where he said, “Yea, if thou call for understanding” (Proverbs 2:3).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: For the LORD giveth wisdom
Proverbs.english_translation: Behold, you have learned that it is great, for it was given from the mouth of the Holy One, blessed be He; therefore you need to acquire it.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He layeth up sound wisdom for the upright
Proverbs.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He, stored it with Himself for twenty-six generations until He gave it to the generation of the wilderness.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He is a shield to them that walk in integrity
Proverbs.english_translation: (“He layeth up a shield for them that walk in integrity”) — that is, and it will be a shield for you.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: That He may guard the paths of justice
Proverbs.english_translation: That through it the paths of justice are guarded; and “the way of His godly ones He preserveth,” that they not stumble.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Discretion shall watch over thee
Proverbs.english_translation: The Torah will watch over you.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: From the men that speak froward things
Proverbs.english_translation: They are the heretics (*apikorsin*), who lead Israel astray from their faith and turn the Torah to evil.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Who are crooked in their ways
Proverbs.english_translation: Every expression of *nalutz* is an expression of crookedness, for in every place (בכ"מ) it is adjacent to *ikesh*, and *ikesh* is an expression of crookedness, as it is said, “and the crooked places (*ma'akashim*) plain” (Isaiah 42).
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 42” is Isaiah 42:16, where JPS reads “and rugged places plain.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Who are crooked in their ways
Proverbs.english_translation: They are crooked in their corrupt ways.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: To deliver thee from the strange woman
Proverbs.english_translation: From the assemblies of heresy (*apikorsut*), which is *minut*; and it is not proper to say that he spoke only of an actual adulteress, for what would be the praise of the Torah that he said here “to deliver thee from the strange woman” and not from another transgression? Rather, this is *minut*, which is casting off the yoke of all the commandments.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: For her house sinketh down unto death
Proverbs.english_translation: It refers to “to deliver thee,” etc.: when you come to her house, it sinks and slides like a slope that descends to death; and the Torah will guard you from this fall; behold, it is a great thing for you.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: unto the shades
Proverbs.english_translation: *Rephaim* — slackened from the way of good, and abandoned with none to support them, until they fall into Gehinnom.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: None that go unto her return
Proverbs.english_translation: It will be hard in their eyes to separate from her and to return.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: That thou mayest walk
Proverbs.english_translation: It refers to the verse above, “to deliver thee from the way of evil” — in order to lead you in the way of good men.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: For the upright shall dwell in the land
Proverbs.english_translation: In the World to Come.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: shall remain in it
Proverbs.english_translation: When the wicked go down to Gehinnom.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: For length of days, and years of life
Proverbs.english_translation: “And peace they will add to you” — my Torah and my commandments.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Trust in the LORD with all thy heart
Proverbs.english_translation: And scatter your money to seek for yourself a teacher to learn from him; and “lean not upon thine own understanding.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Be not wise in thine own eyes
Proverbs.english_translation: To be rejecting the words of your rebuker.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: It shall be health to thy navel
Proverbs.english_translation: Wisdom. *Shorekha* is like “thy navel (*shorrekh*)” (Song of Songs 6); this is your navel.
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed “Song 6”; the word *shorrekh* is in Song of Songs 7:3, where JPS reads “Thy navel is like a round goblet.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And marrow to thy bones
Proverbs.english_translation: It is the marrow, as it is said, “and the marrow of his bones is moistened (*yeshukkeh*)” (Job 21).
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed “Job 21” is Job 21:24.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Honour the LORD with thy substance
Proverbs.english_translation: From all that He graciously gave you, even from a sweet voice (“Do not read *mei-honekha* but *mi-gronekha*,” “from your throat”).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: with the first-fruits
Proverbs.english_translation: These are heave-offerings and tithes.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: despise not the chastening of the LORD
Proverbs.english_translation: If afflictions come upon you, let them be dear to you.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Neither spurn thou His correction
Proverbs.english_translation: From the language of “I am weary (*katzti*) of my life” (Genesis 27).
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 27” is Genesis 27:46.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Even as a father the son in whom he delighteth
Proverbs.english_translation: That he wants good for his son and appeases him after he strikes him with a rod; so the good will be pleasant to you after the blow.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Happy is the man that findeth wisdom, And the man that obtaineth understanding
Proverbs.english_translation: Who learns wisdom until it is fluent, to bring it forth from his mouth.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: For the merchandise of it is better
Proverbs.english_translation: Every exchange that a person makes in merchandise — this one takes this and that one takes that; but he who says to his fellow, “Teach me your chapter and I will teach you my chapter” — it turns out that both are in the hand of each one.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: fine gold
Proverbs.english_translation: *Charutz* — a kind of gold.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: all the things thou canst desire
Proverbs.english_translation: All your desirable things.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: are not to be compared unto her
Proverbs.english_translation: They will not be equal in her worth, nor their value in her value.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: in her right hand
Proverbs.english_translation: For those who go to the right with her and occupy themselves with her for her own sake: length of days, and all the more so riches and honour; and for those who go to the left with her, who occupy themselves with her not for her own sake, in any case (מ"מ) there are riches and honour.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: to them that lay hold upon her
Proverbs.english_translation: To those who hold on to her, like “and he put forth his hand, and laid hold of it” (Exodus 4:4).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: every one that holdest her fast
Proverbs.english_translation: Those who draw near to her; and so every expression of support (*temichah*) in this book means holding on to her.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The LORD by wisdom founded the earth
Proverbs.english_translation: According to the Torah, and it is the Torah, and it is the understanding, and it is the knowledge; and since the whole world was created by them, therefore.
Proverbs.translator_note: The sentence is elliptical and translated literally.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the skies drop down the dew
Proverbs.english_translation: *Ya'afu* — like *yatifu* (“they drip”).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: let not them depart from thine eyes
Proverbs.english_translation: Let them not be bent away from before your eyes, so as to remove them from before you.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: So shall they be life unto thy soul
Proverbs.english_translation: For it is a tree of life.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And grace to thy neck
Proverbs.english_translation: For this is its praise, stated above: “and chains about thy neck.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: thou shalt not dash thy foot
Proverbs.english_translation: *Lo tagof* — an expression of stumbling, *acopér* [printed אצופי"ר] in French (to strike against); and so “lest thou dash thy foot against a stone” (Psalms 91:12), and so “before your feet stumble” (Jeremiah 12), and so “and hurt (*ve-nagefu*) a woman with child” (Exodus 21:22).
Proverbs.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Proverbs 3:23 (“Ton pied ne se heurtera pas”), in forms such as אצופיר and אצופייר; the reading is *acopér* (his index; REJ transcription *Açopér*); the printed form (אצופי"ר) matches. Printed “Jeremiah 12” is Jeremiah 13:16.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: and thy sleep shall be sweet
Proverbs.english_translation: And your sleep will be pleasant when you sleep, that you not fear sudden terror.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the destruction of the wicked
Proverbs.english_translation: When it comes upon the wicked.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: For the LORD will be thy confidence
Proverbs.english_translation: In your trust. Another explanation: in the matters in which you are foolish; thus I found in the Yerushalmi.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Withhold not good from him to whom it is due
Proverbs.english_translation: If you see your fellow wishing to do good to the poor, do not prevent him.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: in the power of thy hand to do it
Proverbs.english_translation: To make him stop. Another explanation: “Withhold not good from the owner thereof” — do not withhold charity from the poor, “when it is in the power of thy hand” to do charity, lest a day come and it is not in the power of your hand.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Say not unto thy neighbour
Proverbs.english_translation: To the poor man.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: when thou hast it by thee
Proverbs.english_translation: What you will give him. And our Rabbis explained “Go, and come again” concerning the wages of a hired worker.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Devise not evil against thy neighbour
Proverbs.english_translation: Do not think — and it does not move from the meaning of ploughing: just as the ploughman prepares a place for the time of sowing, so too one who devises evil prepares in his heart a place of schemes, how he will stand up and do it.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Strive not with a man without cause
Proverbs.english_translation: To complain about him.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: If he have done thee no harm
Proverbs.english_translation: For he has transgressed the commandment written in the Torah, “but thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself” (Leviticus 19); and one who is wicked you are permitted to hate.
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed “Leviticus 19” is Leviticus 19:18.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Envy thou not the man of violence
Proverbs.english_translation: To do like his deeds, if you see him prospering.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: For the perverse is an abomination to the LORD
Proverbs.english_translation: Crooked in his ways.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: But His counsel is with the upright
Proverbs.english_translation: And with the upright is His secret.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: If it concerneth the scorners
Proverbs.english_translation: A person is drawn after them, and in the end he too will be a scoffer with them.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: But unto the humble He giveth grace
Proverbs.english_translation: If he associates with the humble, in the end his deeds will find favour in the eyes of people.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: as for the fools, they carry away shame
Proverbs.english_translation: For himself he sets apart shame as his portion.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Hear, you children, the instruction of a father
Proverbs.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: For I give you good doctrine
Proverbs.english_translation: The prophet prophesies and speaks on the mission of the Holy One, blessed be He, and behold, he is His hands (*kapav*).
Proverbs.translator_note: The last clause is translated literally.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: For I was a son unto my father
Proverbs.english_translation: If you say that Solomon hated people, that he warned them against robbery and forbidden relations, things that a person’s soul desires — therefore it says, “For I was a son,” etc., “tender and an only one,” etc., for he loved me more.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And he taught me, and said unto me
Proverbs.english_translation: “*Veyoreni*” — on this: “and he rebuked me and said to me, ‘Let thy heart hold fast my words’”; and because he rebuked me with these words, therefore I warn you about it (Rabbi Yosef Kara). Another explanation: “For I was a son unto my father” — the prophet says, I was a son to the Holy One, blessed be He, who caused His spirit to rest upon me; and we find that the Holy One, blessed be He, called Solomon a son, as it is said, “I will be to him for a father,” etc. (2 Samuel 7).
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed “2 Samuel 7” is 2 Samuel 7:14.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Let thy heart hold fast my words
Proverbs.english_translation: To my nation I am chosen and beloved, like a tender and only son (“tender and an only one in the sight of my mother,” Proverbs 4:3); therefore “my father taught me.”
Proverbs.translator_note: The source lemma (“tender and an only one”) belongs to Proverbs 4:3, but the comment is filed under 4:4; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of 4:4.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Forsake her not, and she will preserve thee
Proverbs.english_translation: *Ahavah* — love her.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The beginning of wisdom is: Get wisdom
Proverbs.english_translation: The beginning of your wisdom is learning from others: acquire for yourself a tradition from the mouth of the teacher; and afterwards, “with all thy getting get understanding” — contemplate it by yourself, to deduce the reasons, one thing from another.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Extol her, and she will exalt thee
Proverbs.english_translation: *Salselah* — search her; go back over it to analyse it, like “as a grape-gatherer upon the shoots (*salsilot*)” (Jeremiah 6:9) — who goes back and forth in the vineyard and turns back his hand to seek out the gleanings; and in the language of the Sages, “he curls (*mesalsel*) his hair.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: a chaplet of grace
Proverbs.english_translation: *Chaverat chen* — like *livyat chen* (“a chaplet of grace… for thy head”).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Hear, O my son, and receive my sayings
Proverbs.english_translation: [The source prints the lemma only, with no comment.]

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: When thou goest, thy step shall not be straitened
Proverbs.english_translation: One who does not keep his feet apart is close to falling.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Take fast hold of instruction, let her not go
Proverbs.english_translation: Hold on to the Torah, like “and hold him fast by thy hand” (Genesis 21:18), “and laid hold of it” (Exodus 4:4).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: walk not in the way of evil men
Proverbs.english_translation: *Ve-al te'ashsher* — and do not tread, like “My foot hath held fast to His steps (*be-ashuro*)” (Job 23:11), and so “and the man of understanding will understand his step (*le-ashuro*).”
Proverbs.translator_note: The last quotation is left as printed; the words resemble Proverbs 14:15 (*ve-arum yavin le-ashuro*).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Avoid it
Proverbs.english_translation: *Para'ehu* — annul it.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Turn from it
Proverbs.english_translation: *Setah me'alav* — turn aside.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: For they sleep not, except they have done evil
Proverbs.english_translation: They are not able to sleep.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: But the path of the righteous is as the light of dawn
Proverbs.english_translation: For it goes on and gives light from the rising of the dawn.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: unto the perfect day
Proverbs.english_translation: Until midday, which is the clarification of the day.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The way of the wicked is as darkness; They know not at what they stumble
Proverbs.english_translation: Suddenly a stumbling-block comes to them, and they do not know how to beware of it.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: My son, attend to my words
Proverbs.english_translation: [The source prints the lemma only, with no comment.]

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: unto those that find them
Proverbs.english_translation: *Lemotz'eihem* — an expression of finding.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Above all that thou guardest
Proverbs.english_translation: Above everything of which the Torah said “Beware” — guard your heart (from transgressing it), whether a light transgression or a grave transgression.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: For out of it are the issues of life
Proverbs.english_translation: For from that which is light you will have life and great reward if you fulfil it; so expounded Rabbi Tanchuma.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Put away from thee a froward mouth
Proverbs.english_translation: Do not do a thing about which people will mock you and twist their mouths against you.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: a froward mouth
Proverbs.english_translation: *Ikkeshut peh* — crooked speech, like “Though I be innocent, He shall prove me crooked (*va-ya'keseni*)” (Job 9:20); and in the Mishnah, “his teeth are crooked and twisted.”
Proverbs.translator_note: JPS renders the Job verse “Though I be innocent, He shall prove me perverse.” Printed “Job 9:20”.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: perverse lips
Proverbs.english_translation: *Lezut sefatayim* — crookedness of lips, so that people will not open their mouths against you.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Let thine eyes look right on
Proverbs.english_translation: Let them look to the truth and to uprightness.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And let thine eyelids look straight before thee
Proverbs.english_translation: Let them look at the straight, to straighten your way before you.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Make plain the path of thy feet
Proverbs.english_translation: Weigh your way: the loss of a commandment against its reward, and the reward of a transgression against its loss; and then “let all thy ways be established.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Turn not to the right hand nor to the left
Proverbs.english_translation: From the good balance.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: My son, attend unto my wisdom
Proverbs.english_translation: [The source prints the lemma only, with no comment.]

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: drop honey
Proverbs.english_translation: An expression of sweetness.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: For the lips of a strange woman
Proverbs.english_translation: Heresy (*apikorsut*).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: her mouth
Proverbs.english_translation: *Chikah* — an expression of palate (*chech*).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Her feet go down to death
Proverbs.english_translation: An expression of nearness.
Proverbs.translator_note: The comment is translated as printed.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Lest she should walk the even path of life
Proverbs.english_translation: Thus the Sages expounded it: the Holy One, blessed be He, *silsel* the giving of the reward of the commandments and did not specify them, so that a person not see a commandment whose reward is great and cling to it and leave the other commandments. And this is its meaning: “lest thou weigh (*tefales*) the paths of the Torah,” which to take and which to leave; therefore “her ways wander” — the Holy One, blessed be He, moved its paths, and did not make them known. This is a midrash aggadah. But according to the order of the verses, in which after it is written “Remove thy way far from her,” it appears that he has not yet stopped speaking of the harlot woman; and so one may explain “the even path of life lest thou weigh”: do not weigh the path of life against that strange woman, to say which to do, this or that, for the ways of the harlot are moved toward the nether-world, and you will not know to be careful until you move and fall.
Proverbs.translator_note: The word *silsel* is translated as left in the printed text. The quotation “Remove thy way far from her” is Proverbs 5:8.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Lest thou give thy vigour unto others
Proverbs.english_translation: Lest you give to others your majesty (*hodekha*). Lest you turn your heart to other gods, to give them the glory of your majesty and your praise.
Proverbs.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under. JPS renders *hodekha* “thy vigour”; Rashi explains it as “majesty.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: thy years unto the cruel
Proverbs.english_translation: To the prince of Gehinnom.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Lest strangers be filled with thy strength
Proverbs.english_translation: The prophets of Baal, who collect money by their lies and their licentiousness.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: thy labours
Proverbs.english_translation: *Atzaveikha* — your toil and your effort, in which you grieved and laboured.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: in the house of an alien
Proverbs.english_translation: In the house of idol-worshippers [עו"ג].
Proverbs.translator_note: The abbreviation עו"ג is read as “idol-worshippers” (*ovedei gilulim*); the printed form is kept in brackets. This reading is from Rashi’s usage and the context, not from a dictionary.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And thou moan, when thine end cometh
Proverbs.english_translation: In the end you will groan at your end.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: I was well nigh in all evil
Proverbs.english_translation: Like a step between me and Gehinnom (that is, for a small matter I was now in all evil, because I did not listen to the voice of my teachers; for if I had listened to them, it would not have happened to me thus — Rabbi Yosef Kara).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Drink waters out of thine own cistern
Proverbs.english_translation: From the cistern that the Holy One, blessed be He, gave to you as your portion — that is the Torah of Moses.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: thine own cistern
Proverbs.english_translation: Gathered waters.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And running waters out of thine own well
Proverbs.english_translation: Living waters; that is, at first like gathered waters, and in the end they are flowing and going.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Let thy springs be dispersed abroad
Proverbs.english_translation: In the end you will acquire students and teach rulings in public, and you will have a name.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: in the streets
Proverbs.english_translation: A city: “let the streams of your waters be spread.”
Proverbs.translator_note: The comment is translated literally.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Let them be only thine own
Proverbs.english_translation: You alone will be honoured by them, and no other will share with you; since above it said, “lest strangers be filled with thy strength,” here it says, “Let them be only thine own,” and from this.
Proverbs.translator_note: The sentence ends as printed.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Let thy fountain be blessed; And have joy of the wife of thy youth
Proverbs.english_translation: It is the Torah that you learned from your youth.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: With her love be thou ravished always
Proverbs.english_translation: I saw in the words of Rabbi Moshe the Preacher: *tishgeh* means “you shall occupy yourself” always; and it is an Arabic expression; and he brought proof from “to seek occupation.” And I do not know where it is repeated. And our Rabbis explained (*Eruvin* 54) *mishgeh* in its plain sense: for love of her you shall be erring in your other affairs, for she guards what is yours. They said of Rabbi Elazar ben Padat that he was expounding in the lower market while his sheet lay in the upper market; one time a man came and found a snake coiled around it.
Proverbs.translator_note: The Arabic-related explanation is translated literally.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: For the ways of man are before the eyes of the LORD
Proverbs.english_translation: He weighs (*mefales*) his ways and knows how many sins and how many merits are in his hand.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: His own iniquities shall ensnare the wicked
Proverbs.english_translation: Like *yilkeduhu*.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And he shall be holden with the cords of his sin
Proverbs.english_translation: *Yitamekh* — he will be hung, for one who is hanged is held by the rope by which he is hung.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He shall die for lack of instruction
Proverbs.english_translation: Because he did not take instruction.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: My son, if thou art become surety for thy neighbour
Proverbs.english_translation: Our Rabbis explained it as surety for money, according to its plain sense.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Thou art snared by the words of thy mouth
Proverbs.english_translation: For you struck a hand to speak with the strangers.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Go, humble thyself
Proverbs.english_translation: *Hitrapes* — loosen for him the palm (*pas yad*), to pay him his money.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: urge thy neighbour
Proverbs.english_translation: And if you have no money with you, but you are snared by the words of your mouth, speak to him harsh words; many friends upon him, to ask of him that he forgive you.
Proverbs.translator_note: The sentence is translated literally.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Seeing thou art come into the hand of thy neighbour
Proverbs.english_translation: Another explanation: “My son, if thou art become surety for thy neighbour” — after you became surety to the Holy One, blessed be He, who is your neighbour, as it is written, “This is my beloved, and this is my friend” (Song of Songs 5:16), and you accepted upon yourself at Sinai and at the plains of Moab, with an oath and an imprecation, to keep His commandments.
Proverbs.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Seeing thou art come into the hand of thy neighbour
Proverbs.english_translation: That you turn back and depart from His ways and cling to the heretics, to walk in their ways.
Proverbs.translator_note: The source lemma (“If thou hast struck thy hands for a stranger”) belongs to Proverbs 6:1, but the comment is filed under 6:3; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of 6:3.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Seeing thou art come into the hand of thy neighbour
Proverbs.english_translation: That you struck a hand to speak with the strangers.
Proverbs.translator_note: The source lemma (“Thou art snared by the words of thy mouth”) belongs to Proverbs 6:2, but the comment is filed under 6:3; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of 6:3.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Do this now, my son, and deliver thyself
Proverbs.english_translation: Since you came into the hand of your neighbour at Sinai, and accepted His divinity upon you.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Go, humble thyself
Proverbs.english_translation: Humble yourself before Him like a threshold that is trodden and trampled.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: urge thy neighbour
Proverbs.english_translation: Many friends, to pray for you before Him; and so it is expounded in *Midrash Tehillim*.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Deliver thyself as a gazelle from the hand
Proverbs.english_translation: Hurry and slip away from there, like a gazelle that escapes from the hand of man.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Go to the ant, thou sluggard
Proverbs.english_translation: And be wise and make yourself wise.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Which having no chief
Proverbs.english_translation: Who would rebuke her and urge her on and take out of her hand if she robs something from her fellow; and nevertheless.
Proverbs.translator_note: The sentence ends as printed.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Provideth her bread in the summer
Proverbs.english_translation: Her food — each one does not rob from her fellow.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A little folding of the hands to sleep
Proverbs.english_translation: One who sleeps folds his hands — אבראצ"ר in French.
Proverbs.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Proverbs 6:10 (“Croiser les bras”), in forms such as פלייר and פיגר; the printed form (אבראצ"ר) is not among those listed.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: So shall thy poverty come as a runner
Proverbs.english_translation: If you do so, your lack will come, and what you are poor from will come to you immediately, like a man who walks quickly, and your want will come and be filled.
Proverbs.translator_note: The last clause is translated literally.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And thy want as an armed man
Proverbs.english_translation: One who comes quickly to protect his lord. These verses are principally a parable about those who are lazy to occupy themselves with Torah.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: walketh with a froward mouth
Proverbs.english_translation: He who walks with a twisting of the lips.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: That winketh with his eyes
Proverbs.english_translation: Signals of deceit.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: that scrapeth with his feet
Proverbs.english_translation: That is, rubs one against the other.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: That pointeth with his fingers
Proverbs.english_translation: All are from the expression of signs: this falls on the eye, this on the foot, and this on the finger; and the principle is that he speaks of the wicked who incite people to idolatry [לע"ג].
Proverbs.translator_note: The abbreviation (ע"ג / לע"ג) is read as “idolatry” (*avodat gilulim*); the printed form is kept in brackets. Reading from Rashi’s usage in this corpus and the context.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He soweth discord
Proverbs.english_translation: Between a person and his Creator.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Therefore shall his calamity come suddenly
Proverbs.english_translation: *Peta* is an expression of immediacy, and he will not know the downfall that is near to fall upon him.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: There are six things which the LORD hateth
Proverbs.english_translation: “The abomination of His soul” — that is, the seventh also is with them.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: that breatheth out lies
Proverbs.english_translation: *Yafiach* — an expression of speech, for all speech is by the breath of the mouth.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: My son, keep the commandment of thy father
Proverbs.english_translation: [The source prints the lemma only, with no comment.]

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Tie them about thy neck
Proverbs.english_translation: *Ondem* — an expression of binding, like “I would bind it (*e'enden-nu*) unto me as a crown” (Job 31:36).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: When thou walkest
Proverbs.english_translation: In your lifetime.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: it shall lead thee
Proverbs.english_translation: *Tanche otakh* — like *tanhigekha*.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: When thou liest down
Proverbs.english_translation: In the grave.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And when thou awakest
Proverbs.english_translation: (*Ve-hakitzot*) At the resurrection of the dead, to stand in judgment.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: it shall talk with thee
Proverbs.english_translation: It will plead in your behalf.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: For the commandment is a lamp, and the teaching is light
Proverbs.english_translation: As the light shines always, so the merit of the Torah stands for a person forever, while the merit of a commandment is for the moment, like the light of a lamp. Another explanation: “For the commandment is a lamp,” etc. — the commandment of the father is the lamp: whoever fulfils his father’s commandment is as if he took a lamp in his hand to light in a place of darkness, and if he loses anything there he finds it by its light; and so one who fulfils the instruction of his mother, it is a light to him, and so it says, “forsake not the teaching of thy mother.” And certainly this verse speaks of the commandment of his father and mother, as it is written (below 20), “Whoso curseth his father or his mother, his lamp shall be put out in the blackest darkness”; and if a person’s lamp is put out (grows dim) when he does not fulfil the commandment, it turns out that when he fulfils the commandment his lamp shines (Rabbi Yosef Kara).
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed “below 20” is Proverbs 20:20.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And reproofs of instruction are the way of life
Proverbs.english_translation: The reproofs of instruction incline a person to life; it turns out that they are the way of life.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: To keep thee from the evil woman
Proverbs.english_translation: The Torah will keep you from a woman of evil conduct; and perforce Solomon did not speak of an evil woman but against idolatry, which is weighed against everything. For if you say a literal harlot — is all the reward and praise of the Torah that it protects from the harlot alone? Rather, perforce, this is idolatry, which is grave against everything.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: From the smoothness of the alien tongue
Proverbs.english_translation: *Machalkat lashon* — plasterings of eyes of a foreign tongue.
Proverbs.translator_note: The phrase is translated literally.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Neither let her captivate thee with her eyelids
Proverbs.english_translation: *Ve-al tikkachekha* — do not let your wisdom be taken from you by the eyelids of her eyes, with which she winks.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: For on account of a harlot a man is brought to a loaf of bread
Proverbs.english_translation: To poverty and lack of all good.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: hunteth for the precious life
Proverbs.english_translation: A soul that was precious before this, she comes and hunts it down to Gehinnom.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Can a man take fire in his bosom
Proverbs.english_translation: *Hayichteh ish* — can a man scoop coals into the skirts of his garments and they not be burned? Every expression of *chitiyat* coals is an expression of scooping, as its sense, when one fills the vessel from the midst of the fire.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: he that goeth in to his neighbour’s wife
Proverbs.english_translation: As it stands; and even concerning idolatry [לע"ג] there is a way of expounding it: that it is specifically for the nations and not for you.
Proverbs.translator_note: The abbreviation (ע"ג / לע"ג) is read as “idolatry” (*avodat gilulim*); the printed form is kept in brackets. Reading from Rashi’s usage in this corpus and the context.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Men do not despise a thief
Proverbs.english_translation: “Lo yavuzu,” etc.; “and being found he shall pay,” etc.; “he that committeth adultery with a woman,” etc. — the three are joined in one statement. If the thief steals a theft, there is not so much to despise him as the adulterer; why? Because he does it for the hunger of his soul, and perhaps he has nothing to eat; and when he is found he has a remedy in payment, and at the most he pays sevenfold — that is, many double payments, even fifty to one. And some explain “sevenfold” as with one who steals an ox and its vessels and slaughters it, who pays five cattle and double payments on the vessels — behold, seven. “He must give all the substance of his house” — even if he needs to sell all that he has, in any case there is a remedy for him; and at first he acted out of hunger. But:
Proverbs.translator_note: The comment ends as printed with “But:”.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He that committeth adultery with a woman lacketh understanding
Proverbs.english_translation: He — for he did not do it out of hunger.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He doeth it that would destroy his own soul
Proverbs.english_translation: The *zimah*.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Wounds and dishonour shall he get
Proverbs.english_translation: For idolatry and for uncovering nakedness the plagues come.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: For jealousy is the rage of a man
Proverbs.english_translation: He is jealous of him, to exact the wrath of the Holy One, blessed be He, who is mighty over all, and will not spare on the day of vengeance.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He will not regard any ransom
Proverbs.english_translation: *Lo yisa* — face — to any money, to atone for that he denied Him and clung to idolatry. And our Rabbis expounded “Men do not despise a thief”: this is one who steals away behind his fellow, goes to the house of study and occupies himself with Torah; “and being found he pays sevenfold” — in the end he is appointed a judge and gives rulings, for “sevenfold” is only Torah, as it is said, “refined seven times” (Psalms 12).
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed “Psalms 12” is Psalms 12:7. The phrase “steals away behind his fellow” is translated literally.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: My son, keep my words
Proverbs.english_translation: [The source prints the lemma only, with no comment.]

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: my teaching as the apple of thine eye
Proverbs.english_translation: The black of the eye, which resembles darkness, like “the black (*ishon*) of night.”
Proverbs.translator_note: The phrase *ishon laylah* occurs in Proverbs 7:9.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Thou art my sister
Proverbs.english_translation: (Draw her near to you.)

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: thy kinswoman
Proverbs.english_translation: *Moda* — kinsman, like “Boaz our kinsman (*moda'atenu*)” (Ruth 3); that is, draw her near to you always.
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed “Ruth 3” is Ruth 3:2.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: I discerned among the youths
Proverbs.english_translation: *Avinah* — I discerned and saw.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: near her corner
Proverbs.english_translation: The corner of the harlot and of idolatry.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And, behold, there met him a woman
Proverbs.english_translation: As it stands. Another explanation: one of the heretics (*apikorsim*).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: With the attire of a harlot
Proverbs.english_translation: *Shit zonah* — like “their buttocks (*shitoteihem*)” (2 Samuel 10); that is, the nakedness of a harlot.
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed “2 Samuel 10” is 2 Samuel 10:4.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: and wily of heart
Proverbs.english_translation: *Netzurat lev* — like “a besieged city (*ir netzurah*)” (Isaiah 1), surrounded by a *karkom*; and so the heart of this one is *mizkefet* lewdness and folly.
Proverbs.translator_note: The words *karkom* and *mizkefet* are left as printed. Printed “Isaiah 1” is Isaiah 1:8.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: rebellious
Proverbs.english_translation: *Ve-soreret* — she turned aside from the way.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Sacrifices of peace-offerings were due from me
Proverbs.english_translation: That is, I prepared a great meal, for this day I brought my vows and my peace-offerings.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: and I have found thee
Proverbs.english_translation: *Ve-emtza'ekha* — so that I might find you.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: I have decked my couch with coverlets
Proverbs.english_translation: *Marvaddim* — garments of *chofesh* and adornment, and its like at the end of the book, as it is said, “she maketh for herself coverlets” (Proverbs 31:22).
Proverbs.translator_note: The word *chofesh* is left as printed.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: I have decked my couch
Proverbs.english_translation: I have adorned.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: With striped cloths of the yarn of Egypt
Proverbs.english_translation: Praised garments of valuable linen things that come from Egypt, where flax is common, as is written in the book (Isaiah 19:9), “and the workers of flax shall be ashamed.” *Atun* — the Targum of “their cords” is *atoniehon*.
Proverbs.translator_note: The Targum quotation is left as printed. JPS Isaiah 19:9 reads “Moreover they that work in combed flax… shall be ashamed.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: I have perfumed my bed
Proverbs.english_translation: *Hanafti* — I waved the fragrance, like one waving with a cloth in the spice-house to bring the fragrance from above to below; and Dunash explained it as an expression of incense, and said that it has no analogy.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: For my husband is not at home
Proverbs.english_translation: You saw that the Holy One, blessed be He, removed His Shechinah and gave all good to idol-worshippers [עו"ג].
Proverbs.translator_note: The abbreviation עו"ג is read as “idol-worshippers” (*ovedei gilulim*); the printed form is kept in brackets. This reading is from Rashi’s usage and the context, not from a dictionary.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He hath taken the bag of money with him
Proverbs.english_translation: The best of them He killed.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He will come home at the full moon
Proverbs.english_translation: To the fixed appointed time, and so “at the full moon (*bakeseh*) for our feast-day” (Psalms 81:4).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: she causeth him to yield
Proverbs.english_translation: To that one who lacks heart toward her.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: With her much fair speech
Proverbs.english_translation: For she is accustomed to habituate men to this.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: With the blandishment of her lips
Proverbs.english_translation: With smooth speech she will drive him away from the way.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Or as one in fetters
Proverbs.english_translation: This is the venom of a snake.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: to the correction of the fool
Proverbs.english_translation: Like a snake hurrying to run on the mission of the Holy One, blessed be He, to chastise the fool who is obligated to the Omnipresent, blessed be He; so this one runs after her until he stumbles on her, and “an arrow strike through his liver.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: As a bird hasteneth to the snare
Proverbs.english_translation: To run to the snare, and he does not know that the snare is spread there at the cost of the bird’s life.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Now therefore, O you children, hearken unto me
Proverbs.english_translation: [The source prints the lemma only, with no comment.]

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Doth not wisdom call
Proverbs.english_translation: Doth not wisdom call — does not the Torah proclaim to you the things said below in the matter.
Proverbs.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: at the entry of the city
Proverbs.english_translation: *Lefi kiryat* — the roof placed over the gate, and they sit upon it.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: she crieth aloud
Proverbs.english_translation: *Taronah* — she will cry out; and what does she say to you? “Unto you, O men, I call.”
Proverbs.translator_note: The quotation is Proverbs 8:4.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: I will speak excellent things
Proverbs.english_translation: Words of nobility and importance.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: perverse or crooked
Proverbs.english_translation: Crookedness.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: choice gold
Proverbs.english_translation: *Mecharutz* — one of the kinds of gold.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: better than rubies
Proverbs.english_translation: Pearls.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: are not to be compared unto her
Proverbs.english_translation: They will not be likened to her worth.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: dwell with prudence
Proverbs.english_translation: *Shakhanti* — beside prudence (*ormah*), for once a person has learned Torah, a cleverness about everything enters him.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The fear of the LORD is to hate evil
Proverbs.english_translation: This is the instruction that wisdom proclaims to people.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: By me kings reign
Proverbs.english_translation: For I teach the laws and the judgments.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: I love them that love me
Proverbs.english_translation: *Ahav* — like *e'ehav*.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: them that love me
Proverbs.english_translation: *Ohavai* — it is written *ohavehah* (“her lovers”): the Holy One, blessed be He, said, “I am a lover of the Torah.” *Ahav* — this I heard from Rabbi Aaron in the name of Rabbi Nathan.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: shall find me
Proverbs.english_translation: *Yimtza'unani* — an extra *nun*: fifty gates of understanding will I cause him to find.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: That I may cause those that love me to inherit substance
Proverbs.english_translation: *Yesh* — with me is a great inheritance.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The LORD made me as the beginning of His way
Proverbs.english_translation: Before the creation of the world.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: I was set up from everlasting, from the beginning
Proverbs.english_translation: *Nissachti* — an expression of princes (*nesikhei*) of men (Ezekiel 35).
Proverbs.translator_note: The printed reference “Ezekiel 35” could not be matched to the words quoted; it is left as printed.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: I was brought forth
Proverbs.english_translation: I was created.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Before the mountains were settled
Proverbs.english_translation: In the midst of the water.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the earth, nor the fields
Proverbs.english_translation: The Land of Israel and the other lands.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Nor the beginning of the dust of the world
Proverbs.english_translation: The first man.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: When He set a circle upon the face of the deep
Proverbs.english_translation: When He spread out the circle of the earth upon the waters — “a decree, a boundary that shall not be passed.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: a circle
Proverbs.english_translation: *Chug* — an expression of encircling, like “and he marketh it out with the compasses (*u-vamechugah*)” (Isaiah 44), *compas* in French (קונפא"ש).
Proverbs.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Proverbs 8:27 (“Cercle, littéral. : compas”), in forms such as קונפט and קומפש; the printed form (קונפא"ש) is a variant spelling. Printed “Isaiah 44” is Isaiah 44:13.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: When the fountains of the deep showed their might
Proverbs.english_translation: When He strengthened the fountains of the deep.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: When He gave to the sea His decree
Proverbs.english_translation: And He decreed upon the Red Sea, when He created it, on condition that it split before Moses.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: When He appointed the foundations of the earth
Proverbs.english_translation: *Bechuko* — in its engraving, from the language of *chaku*, like “I have graven thee (*chakotikha*) upon the palms” (Isaiah 49:16), and so “from the bottom (*mi-cheik*) of the earth” (Ezekiel 43).
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed references are Isaiah 49:16 (“ibid. 49”) and Ezekiel 43:14.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: as a nursling
Proverbs.english_translation: *Amon* — growing up beside Him; an expression of “they that were brought up (*ha-emunim*) in scarlet” (Lamentations 4:5).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And I was daily all delight
Proverbs.english_translation: *Yom yom* — two thousand years.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Playing in His habitable earth
Proverbs.english_translation: All the generations of the wicked from Adam until Noah and from Noah until Abraham — I was sporting over them.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: my delights are with the sons of men
Proverbs.english_translation: *Ve-sha'ashu'ai* — I waited until the generation of the wilderness came and received me.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Now therefore, you children, hearken unto me
Proverbs.english_translation: [The source prints the lemma only, with no comment.]

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And refuse it not
Proverbs.english_translation: And do not annul my instruction.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Watching daily at my gates
Proverbs.english_translation: *Lishkod* — to guard.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: at the posts of my doors
Proverbs.english_translation: To enter first to the house of study and the synagogue, and to leave last.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Wisdom hath builded her house
Proverbs.english_translation: With wisdom the Holy One, blessed be He, built the world.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: She hath hewn out her seven pillars
Proverbs.english_translation: The seven days of creation. Another explanation: the seven books that are in the Torah, since “And it came to pass when the ark set forward” is a book by itself, in tractate *Shabbat*.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: she hath mingled her wine
Proverbs.english_translation: She mixed them with water, like strong wine that is not fit to drink undiluted.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: She hath also furnished her table
Proverbs.english_translation: All the creation of the moist and the dry.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: She hath sent forth her maidens
Proverbs.english_translation: Adam and Eve. Another explanation: Moses and Aaron.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Whoso is thoughtless, let him turn in hither
Proverbs.english_translation: And let him learn from me and become wise.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: drink of the wine which I have mingled
Proverbs.english_translation: Of the wine that I mixed.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Forsake all thoughtlessness
Proverbs.english_translation: The way of simplicity.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: walk in the way of understanding
Proverbs.english_translation: *Ve-ashru* — an expression of stepping, like “My foot hath held fast to His steps (*be-ashuro*)” (Job 23:11).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: he that reproveth a wicked man
Proverbs.english_translation: It is a blemish for the one who rebukes, for this one reviles him and does not listen to him; this is a warning that it is forbidden to speak with those who incite away from the straight path, even to rebuke them and draw them near.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Give to a wise man, and he will be yet wiser
Proverbs.english_translation: To a worthy student (teach). And a midrash aggadah: it was said to Noah, “Of every clean beast,” etc. (Genesis 6:13), and when he went out, “and took of every clean beast,” etc. (ibid.) — he said, “Why did the Holy One, blessed be He, multiply these, except that He wanted me to offer Him from them?”
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 6:13”: the words quoted are those of Genesis 7:2, where JPS reads “Of every clean beast thou shalt take to thee seven and seven”; the second quotation (“ibid.”) is Genesis 8:20.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Teach a righteous man, and he will increase in learning
Proverbs.english_translation: Wisdom, and he will increase learning — from his own knowledge and upon his tradition.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom, And the knowledge of the All-holy is understanding
Proverbs.english_translation: It is the essence of understanding.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the years of thy life shall be increased
Proverbs.english_translation: Years of life are those of sustenance and wealth.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: she saith to him
Proverbs.english_translation: Those words — what she said to him.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Stolen waters are sweet
Proverbs.english_translation: The taste of coming to an unmarried woman is not like the taste of a married woman (א"א); and also regarding the commandment: “Stolen waters are sweet” — they were afraid to do it openly and do it in secret.
Proverbs.translator_note: The abbreviation א"א is read here as “a married woman” (*eshet ish*).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A wise son maketh a glad father
Proverbs.english_translation: This is the Holy One, blessed be He. Another explanation: his actual father.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: But a foolish son is the grief of his mother
Proverbs.english_translation: He is always with his mother in the house, and she sees his foolishness and is distressed; and according to the parable, a foolish son is like Jeroboam son of Nebat.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the grief of his mother
Proverbs.english_translation: *Tugat* — the grief of *kenisiyuto*.
Proverbs.translator_note: The word כניסיותו is left as printed and not resolved here.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Treasures of wickedness profit nothing
Proverbs.english_translation: For he used to boast of his wealth, as it is said (Hosea 12), “And Ephraim said: Surely I am become rich,” etc.
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed “Hosea 12” is Hosea 12:9.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: But righteousness delivereth from death
Proverbs.english_translation: And if you say, “a righteous man who squanders his possessions for charity — from where will he be sustained?”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: But He thrusteth away the desire of the wicked
Proverbs.english_translation: He will push them, and they fall.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He becometh poor that dealeth with a slack hand
Proverbs.english_translation: One who is poor in Torah gives false rulings.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: with a slack hand
Proverbs.english_translation: Scales of deceit; according to its plain sense, it means among merchants.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the hand of the diligent
Proverbs.english_translation: Upright ones, who decide a matter by its truth and its justice without iniquity.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: But the mouth of the wicked concealeth violence
Proverbs.english_translation: The violence will cover their mouths and kill them.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The memory of the righteous shall be for a blessing
Proverbs.english_translation: One who mentions a righteous man blesses him.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the name of the wicked shall rot
Proverbs.english_translation: Rot rises in their name, so that no one wants to mention his name, and it is forgotten of itself.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The wise in heart will receive commandments
Proverbs.english_translation: Moses our teacher: for all Israel were occupied with the spoil of Egypt, while he was occupied with commandments, as it is said, “And Moses took the bones of Joseph,” etc. (Exodus 13:19).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: But a prating fool shall fall
Proverbs.english_translation: *Yillavet* — an expression of effort; and in the Sifrei, in the portion “And the people were as murmurers” (Numbers 11:1), they said: “How much we have been troubled (*nitlabatnu*) on the way.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: he that perverteth his ways shall be found out
Proverbs.english_translation: He will be broken and chastised, like “and with them he taught (*vayoda*) the men of Succoth” (Judges 8:16).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He that winketh with the eye causeth sorrow
Proverbs.english_translation: This is the one who incites a person with his winks to evil.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The mouth of the righteous is a fountain of life
Proverbs.english_translation: Their mouth conceals the violence that is in their heart, for they smooth their lips while hatred is hidden in their heart; and the explanation of this verse is not like the explanation of the one above, and the matter points to them.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Hatred stirreth up strifes
Proverbs.english_translation: Even a transgression that was given to oblivion is remembered: through the multitude of iniquities the last hatred comes and stirs them up. So Ezekiel rebuked Israel for the transgressions of Egypt and says to them, “Cast you away every man the detestable things of his eyes,” etc. (Ezekiel 20) — for how many (years was) this hatred suppressed, and the Holy One, blessed be He, did not mention them to them until now, when they multiplied transgressions on top of their sins.
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed “Ezekiel 20” is Ezekiel 20:7.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: But love covereth all transgressions
Proverbs.english_translation: When Israel improve their deeds, the Holy One, blessed be He, covers their transgressions.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: In the lips of him that hath discernment wisdom is found
Proverbs.english_translation: When a person rebukes a discerning one, he answers him, “I have sinned” — like David, who said to Nathan, “I have sinned” (2 Samuel 12:13).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: But a rod is for the back of him that is void of understanding
Proverbs.english_translation: But one who lacks heart does not listen until he is smitten, like Pharaoh.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Wise men lay up knowledge
Proverbs.english_translation: They keep it in their heart so that they do not forget it.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The rich man’s wealth
Proverbs.english_translation: In Torah.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: is his strong city
Proverbs.english_translation: It is to him.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The ruin of the poor is their poverty
Proverbs.english_translation: Their poverty, that they did not occupy themselves with Torah, is their ruin.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The wages of the righteous is life
Proverbs.english_translation: As it stands; and a midrash aggadah: Solomon made the work of the Temple for the life of Israel, for their atonement.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The increase of the wicked is sin
Proverbs.english_translation: The produce (another version: the bringing) of Manasseh, who brought into it the image — that was for sin.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He is in the way of life that heedeth instruction
Proverbs.english_translation: The one who keeps instruction — he is the way to life.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: he that forsaketh reproof erreth
Proverbs.english_translation: Himself and others.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He that hideth hatred is of lying lips
Proverbs.english_translation: The flatterer, whose lips are false and who hides hatred in his heart.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: he that uttereth a slander is a fool
Proverbs.english_translation: A defamation (*la'az*) about which people whisper concerning his fellow.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: In the multitude of words there wanteth not transgression
Proverbs.english_translation: One who multiplies words brings sin.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: he that refraineth his lips is wise
Proverbs.english_translation: He is the enlightened one.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The tongue of the righteous is as choice silver
Proverbs.english_translation: For he knows how to rebuke.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The heart of the wicked is little worth
Proverbs.english_translation: For he does not listen to the rebuke of the righteous. And the midrash of Rabbi Tanchuma says: it was said of Iddo the prophet, who cried out against the altar in Beth-el, and Jeroboam, although his hand dried up, did not accept rebuke, as it is said, “Entreat now the favour of the LORD thy God” (1 Kings 13:6) — and not “my God”; and it says, “and his hand was restored to him as before” (ibid.) — he stood and burned incense to idols, and so too in the end.
Proverbs.translator_note: JPS 1 Kings 13:6: “the king’s hand was restored him, and became as it was before.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The lips of the righteous feed many
Proverbs.english_translation: For many eat through his merit and his prayer.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The blessing of the LORD, it maketh rich
Proverbs.english_translation: He need not toil to become rich; the blessing with which He blesses him is enough.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: It is as sport to a fool to do wickedness
Proverbs.english_translation: The counsel of sinners.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And so is wisdom to a man of discernment
Proverbs.english_translation: “As sport to a man of discernment” — that is, it is light in his eyes to do.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The fear of the wicked, it shall come upon him
Proverbs.english_translation: What he fears will come to him: the generation of the dispersion feared and said (Genesis 10), “lest we be scattered,” and in the end it is written, “So the LORD scattered them abroad from thence” (ibid.).
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 10” is Genesis 11:4; “ibid.” is Genesis 11:8.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And the desire of the righteous shall be granted
Proverbs.english_translation: He who has it in his hand to give it (to give).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: When the whirlwind passeth, the wicked is no more
Proverbs.english_translation: Suddenly the passing of a stormy wind comes, and the wicked is cut off from his place.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The hope of the righteous is gladness
Proverbs.english_translation: Its end is established, and they rejoice.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the expectation of the wicked shall perish
Proverbs.english_translation: For it will not come.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The way of the LORD is a stronghold to the upright
Proverbs.english_translation: It is ruin to the workers of iniquity, who do not walk in it, and it takes vengeance on them.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The righteous shall never be moved
Proverbs.english_translation: When he is moved, his moving is not an eternal moving, for he falls and rises.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The mouth of the righteous buddeth with wisdom
Proverbs.english_translation: He speaks — an expression of “the fruit of the lips (*niv sefatayim*)” (Isaiah 57).
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 57” is Isaiah 57:19, where JPS reads “createth the fruit of the lips.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The lips of the righteous know what is acceptable
Proverbs.english_translation: They know how to appease and conciliate their Maker, and know how to please people and to place peace between them.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: with the lowly is wisdom
Proverbs.english_translation: Wisdom will come.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: shall guide them
Proverbs.english_translation: *Tanchem* — will lead them.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: shall destroy them
Proverbs.english_translation: *Yeshaddem* — will destroy them.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: But the faithless shall be trapped in their own crafty device
Proverbs.english_translation: In the mischief that they carry out they are trapped; and the verse is inverted, that is, “and the faithless shall be trapped in their mischief.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: When a wicked man dieth, his expectation shall perish
Proverbs.english_translation: The hope of all who trust in him.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And the hope of strength perisheth
Proverbs.english_translation: The hope of his children, who are his strength, perishes, for through his merit good will not come to them; but at the death of the righteous, their children have a refuge in their righteousness.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The righteous is delivered out of trouble
Proverbs.english_translation: At the death of a wicked man; and this is connected to the verse above.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: With his mouth the impious man destroyeth his neighbour
Proverbs.english_translation: The hypocrite who incites his fellow on an evil path destroys him with his mouth.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: But through knowledge shall the righteous be delivered
Proverbs.english_translation: And the righteous is delivered from him through the knowledge of the Torah, which warned about him, “thou shalt not consent unto him,” etc. (Deuteronomy 13).
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed “Deuteronomy 13” is Deuteronomy 13:9.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: By the blessing of the upright a city is exalted
Proverbs.english_translation: *Tarum keret* — the ceiling (*tikrat*) of the house will stand in its height without falling; so long as the kings of Judah were upright, their prayer kept the Temple standing.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: a man of discernment holdeth his peace
Proverbs.english_translation: When the one lacking heart despises him, like Saul, as it is written, “And they despised him, and brought him no present. But he was as one that held his peace” (1 Samuel 11).
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed “1 Samuel 11” is 1 Samuel 10:27.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Where no wise direction is, a people falleth
Proverbs.english_translation: When trouble comes upon Israel and they do not take it to heart to understand, to fast and to repent, a people will fall.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He that is surety for a stranger shall smart for it
Proverbs.english_translation: *Ra yerou'a* — the wicked will run about, whose heart is pledged to idolatry.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: them that strike hands
Proverbs.english_translation: Those who strike a palm to do evil and to walk in their counsel; and our Rabbis expounded it of suretyship for money.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A gracious woman obtaineth honour
Proverbs.english_translation: The Congregation of Israel always draws near to the honour of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Torah.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And strong men obtain riches
Proverbs.english_translation: The children of Edom draw near to thefts of money and robbery.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The merciful man doeth good to his own soul
Proverbs.english_translation: *Gomel nafsho* — bestows good on his relatives; *ish chesed* — a man who is pious.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: he that is cruel troubleth his own flesh
Proverbs.english_translation: And the cruel one troubles his relatives.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The wicked earneth deceitful wages
Proverbs.english_translation: The work of the wicked deceives him; he thinks his success will be established, and everything is lost.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: he that soweth righteousness hath a sure reward
Proverbs.english_translation: And one who sows charity — it is a work of truth, for he is certainly assured that he will receive his reward in the end.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: a sure reward
Proverbs.english_translation: *Sachar* — קרוניא"ל in French, like a person who dams the water-channel in order to gather fish, and is sure to find many fish there; and similar to it, “all they that make dams (*oseh sachar*) shall be grieved in soul” (Isaiah 19:10).
Proverbs.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Proverbs 11:18 (“Écluse”), in forms such as אשקלושא and אישקלושא; the printed form (קרוניא"ל) is not among those listed and is left as printed.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Stedfast righteousness tendeth to life
Proverbs.english_translation: The truth of righteousness: its end is to life, like “The daughters of Zelophehad speak right (*ken*)” (Numbers 27).
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed “Numbers 27” is Numbers 27:7.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: My hand upon it
Proverbs.english_translation: That is, from the hand of the Holy One, blessed be He, to his hand shall come the reward of his deeds, and he will not be cleared of the evil that he did.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: As a ring of gold in a swine’s snout
Proverbs.english_translation: That he soils it in refuse; so is a Torah scholar who has turned from the good way.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: that turneth aside from discretion
Proverbs.english_translation: He separates from the Torah.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the expectation of the wicked is wrath
Proverbs.english_translation: They trust and hope for Gehinnom.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: There is that scattereth, and yet increaseth
Proverbs.english_translation: His money, as for charity, and he is increased further.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: withholdeth more than is meet
Proverbs.english_translation: Himself from uprightness; but it will be for want to him.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The beneficent soul shall be made rich
Proverbs.english_translation: That he is generous with his money; and every expression of *berachah* means abundance, פישון in French.
Proverbs.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Proverbs 11:28 (“Toute chose bénie : ce verbe indique toujours l’abondance”; the commentary here is on 11:25), in forms such as פיישון and פושון; the printed form (פישון) matches.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: he that satisfieth abundantly
Proverbs.english_translation: Who satisfies the poor.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: shall be satisfied also himself
Proverbs.english_translation: *Yoreh* — he will be sated with good.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He that withholdeth corn
Proverbs.english_translation: A teacher of Torah.
Proverbs.translator_note: The comment is translated as printed.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He that diligently seeketh good
Proverbs.english_translation: He who wishes to guide people on a good way, and rebukes and chastises them.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: seeketh favour
Proverbs.english_translation: He wants the Holy One, blessed be He, to favour them and be reconciled with them. *Ratzon* — *apaiement* [printed אפיימינ"ט] in Old French (goodwill).
Proverbs.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Proverbs 11:27 (“Bienveillance”), in forms such as אפיימנט; the reading is *apaiement* (“goodwill”), from Darmesteter’s index; the printed form (אפיימינ"ט) is a variant spelling.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He that troubleth his own house shall inherit the wind
Proverbs.english_translation: A lazy person who always inherits wind and does not labour in Torah or in work — in the end he troubles the members of his household, who have nothing to eat.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life
Proverbs.english_translation: The reward of the fruits of the deeds of the righteous: they are a tree of life forever.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: he that is wise winneth souls
Proverbs.english_translation: One who is wise acquires souls for himself by teaching them the good way, and they are to him as if he had acquired them, as in the matter that is said, “and the souls that they had gotten in Haran” (Genesis 12:5).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Behold, the righteous shall be requited in the earth
Proverbs.english_translation: Why should the wicked trust in the hour when he prospers? Does he not see that the righteous is repaid for the transgression that is in his hand while he is still on the earth, in life?

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: How much more the wicked and the sinner
Proverbs.english_translation: And all the more so, that the end of the wicked is to be repaid, either in his life or in his death.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A good man shall obtain favour of the LORD
Proverbs.english_translation: *Tov yafik* — brings forth from the Holy One, blessed be He, contentment, to bring good to the world.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: a man of wicked devices will He condemn
Proverbs.english_translation: A schemer will He condemn — he obligates people to bring evil; and so it says, “but one sinner destroyeth much good” (Ecclesiastes 9).
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed “Ecclesiastes 9” is Ecclesiastes 9:18.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A man shall not be established by wickedness
Proverbs.english_translation: He will not be strengthened.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: as rottenness in his bones
Proverbs.english_translation: *Ve-chirakav* — a worm that enters the bones and grinds them; so a shameful and evil woman, whose deeds are shameful.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The words of the wicked are to lie in wait for blood
Proverbs.english_translation: They counsel to murder by their hand or by false testimony.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: But the mouth of the upright shall deliver them
Proverbs.english_translation: When they hear their counsel, they will save the pursued by revealing their counsel; or if they are witnesses, they refute them.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The wicked are overthrown
Proverbs.english_translation: Like *lahafokh* — they are overturned as in the overturning of a moment.
Proverbs.translator_note: The sentence is translated literally.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: and are not
Proverbs.english_translation: Finished, like Sodom.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: But the house of the righteous shall stand
Proverbs.english_translation: It will endure.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A man shall be commended according to his intelligence
Proverbs.english_translation: Whether he is wise a little or a lot, everything — according to his intelligence he receives his reward.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: he that is of a distorted understanding shall be despised
Proverbs.english_translation: *Ve-na'avah lev* — he who has moved his heart entirely from the Torah shall be despised.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: of a distorted understanding
Proverbs.english_translation: *Na'avah* — like “I am bent (*ne'evetti*) so that I cannot hear” (Isaiah 21), and so “thou son of perverse (*na'vat*) rebellion” (1 Samuel 20); and one may say: *na'avah* — one whose heart is shaken (*nu'a'a*), from the root *na va-nad*, as one says *za'avah* from *za*.
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 21” is Isaiah 21:3 and “1 Samuel 20” is 1 Samuel 20:30. The abbreviation וי"ל is read as “and one may say.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Better is he that is lightly esteemed
Proverbs.english_translation: In his own eyes, and he makes himself a servant for himself.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Than he that playeth the man of rank, and lacketh bread
Proverbs.english_translation: *Mitkabbed* in his own eyes, and says, “It is a disgrace for me to labour at work, for I am of the great people” — and his end is to lack bread.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A righteous man regardeth the life of his beast
Proverbs.english_translation: What his beast and the members of his household need.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He that tilleth his ground shall have plenty of bread
Proverbs.english_translation: As it stands; and according to its parable, one who always reviews his learning so that it not be forgotten.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The wicked desireth the prey of evil men
Proverbs.english_translation: *Chamad rasha* — to be fed and sustained from the hunting of the wicked, who ensnare people with robberies and violence.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: But the root of the righteous yieldeth fruit
Proverbs.english_translation: That which it is fit to give, and it is the fruit.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: In the transgression of the lips is a snare to the evil man
Proverbs.english_translation: In the transgression of the lips of the generation of the Flood, who said, “What is the Almighty, that we should serve Him?” (Job 21:15) — an evil snare came upon them, and Noah the righteous came out of the trouble.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A man shall be satisfied with good by the fruit of his mouth
Proverbs.english_translation: From the reward of the mouth of those who engage in Torah they eat good in this world, and the principal remains for them for the World to Come (לעו"ה).
Proverbs.translator_note: The abbreviation לעו"ה is read here as “for the World to Come.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A fool’s vexation is presently known
Proverbs.english_translation: On the day that he is angry, on that very day he makes known his anger, for he provokes and reviles his fellow in public and has no restraint on his spirit; but the prudent covers shame and is not quick to quarrel. And a midrash aggadah: on the day that Adam was created, his rebellion became known, and the Holy One, blessed be He, who is shrewd, did not wish to destroy His creatures, so He covered his shame and postponed His decree from the day of Adam to His own day, which is a thousand years.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He that breatheth forth truth uttereth righteousness
Proverbs.english_translation: One who speaks faithfully declares in judgment true testimony, to acquit the innocent.
