Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: There is that speaketh
Proverbs.english_translation: Speaks, like “to speak clearly (*levatte*) with the lips” (Leviticus 5).
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed “Leviticus 5” is Leviticus 5:4, where JPS reads “swear clearly with his lips.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: like the piercings of a sword
Proverbs.english_translation: Who stirs up quarrel among people and causes them to kill.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the tongue of the wise is health
Proverbs.english_translation: Who brings peace between a person and his fellow.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: is health
Proverbs.english_translation: *Marpe* — למבט' ההוא.
Proverbs.translator_note: The abbreviation in למבט' ההוא is left as printed and not resolved here.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The lip of truth shall be established for ever
Proverbs.english_translation: It will be established and endure.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: But a lying tongue is but for a moment
Proverbs.english_translation: *Ve-ad argi'ah* — for a very little moment it comes to an end, for falsehood has no legs.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Deceit is in the heart of them that devise evil
Proverbs.english_translation: And because they are troubled by thoughts of deceit they have no joy; and to the counsellors of peace there is joy.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: There shall no mischief befall the righteous
Proverbs.english_translation: *Lo ye'uneh* — will not happen; a transgression without knowledge will not come to pass for him.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A prudent man concealeth knowledge
Proverbs.english_translation: Even with his wisdom he is modest, and all the more so does he conceal words of folly. But “the heart of fools proclaimeth foolishness” — announces folly in a loud voice.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The hand of the diligent
Proverbs.english_translation: Upright ones.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: shall bear rule
Proverbs.english_translation: *Timshol* — will become rich.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Care in the heart of a man boweth it down
Proverbs.english_translation: *Yesichenah* — let him drive it from his mind.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: But a good word maketh it glad
Proverbs.english_translation: Let him occupy himself with Torah, and it will gladden the worry that is in his heart and save him from it; and according to the one who says, “let him speak it (*yesichenah*) to others,” this is the end of the verse: “and a good word” — that his friend consoles him — “will gladden the worry.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The righteous is guided by his friend
Proverbs.english_translation: The righteous one forgoes his measures and passes over them — *yeter* — *large* in French (לריי"ש).
Proverbs.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Proverbs 12:26 (“Plus large”), in forms such as לריש and לרייט; the printed form (לריי"ש) is a variant spelling.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: But the way of the wicked leadeth them astray
Proverbs.english_translation: For it is accustomed to do evil, it will lead them astray.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The slothful man shall not hunt his prey
Proverbs.english_translation: *Lo yacharokh* — connected to the verse before it; that is, the way of the wicked will lead him astray, and he will not roast the game of his deceit.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The slothful man shall not hunt his prey
Proverbs.english_translation: He will not succeed in his deceit; and since he speaks in the language of hunting, the expression of roasting falls on it, for the successful hunter catches the birds and roasts them in fire.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: But the precious substance of men is to be diligent
Proverbs.english_translation: The verse is inverted: “and the wealth of a man who is diligent is precious” — the money of an upright man is precious.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: diligent
Proverbs.english_translation: *Charutz* — one who does truth, like “the hand of the diligent (*charutzim*) maketh rich” (above 10).
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed “above 10” is Proverbs 10:4.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: in the pathway thereof
Proverbs.english_translation: Of righteousness.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: there is no death
Proverbs.english_translation: *El mot* — he will not die.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A wise son is instructed of his father
Proverbs.english_translation: The verse is abbreviated: “a wise son asks, and loves, the instruction of a father”; and some say: through the instruction of the father he is wise.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: But a scorner heareth not rebuke
Proverbs.english_translation: He did not hear rebuke, for he does not accept reproofs.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A man shall eat good from the fruit of his mouth
Proverbs.english_translation: From the reward of his Torah he eats good in this world, and the principal remains for the World to Come.
Proverbs.translator_note: The abbreviations (בעה"ז, לעוה"ב) are read here as “in this world” and “for the World to Come.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: But the desire of the faithless is violence
Proverbs.english_translation: And the desire of the faithless is violence, like “If it be your mind (*nafshekhem*)” (Genesis 23) and “Deliver me not over unto the will (*nefesh*) of mine adversaries” (Psalms 27).
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed references are Genesis 23:8 and Psalms 27:12.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: But for him that openeth wide his lips there shall be ruin
Proverbs.english_translation: *Posheq sefatav* — he who opens his lips to speak always; all his spirit is from “and hast opened thy feet (*vatefaskki*)” (Ezekiel 16:25); an expression of breadth.
Proverbs.translator_note: The phrase “all his spirit is from” is translated as printed.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The soul of the sluggard desireth, and hath nothing
Proverbs.english_translation: His soul desires all good, and has nothing.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the soul of the diligent shall be abundantly gratified
Proverbs.english_translation: Upright men who eat the labour of their hands — this is its plain meaning; and according to its parable, in the future he will see the honour of Torah scholars and will desire it and not attain it.
Proverbs.translator_note: The abbreviation ת"ח is read here as “Torah scholars.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A righteous man hateth lying
Proverbs.english_translation: The righteous hates a false word, but the wicked accepts it.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: behaveth vilely and shamefully
Proverbs.english_translation: The people, by this.
Proverbs.translator_note: The comment is elliptical and translated as printed.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: But wickedness overthroweth the sinner
Proverbs.english_translation: *Chatat* is like *chote* (“sinner”), and because he is thoroughly wicked, it calls him *chatat*; and its meaning: his wickedness will pervert the sinner, will ruin and lower him; every *silluf* is ruin and stumbling, like “The foolishness of man perverteth (*tesalef*) his way” (below 19), and evil will come upon him.
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed “below 19” is Proverbs 19:3.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: There is that pretendeth himself rich, yet hath nothing
Proverbs.english_translation: He shows himself rich. Another explanation: there is a man who becomes rich in the end and has nothing at the beginning, and there is one who comes to poverty from great wealth. Another explanation: he becomes rich through robbing the poor and in the end has nothing; and there is one who becomes poor by scattering and giving to the needy, and great wealth is prepared for him.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The ransom of a man’s life are his riches
Proverbs.english_translation: A man’s wealth is the ransom of his soul, for he made charity from it.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: But the poor heareth no threatening
Proverbs.english_translation: Provided that he does not make the poor man hear a rebuke, by giving to him and not shaming him. Another explanation: “The ransom of a man’s life are his riches” — his Torah.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: But the poor heareth no threatening
Proverbs.english_translation: In words of Torah, he did not hear rebuke; he does not know how to turn from evil because he was not careful. And ומ"א: it speaks of the half-shekel that Scripture imposed on all Israel, and made the poor and rich equal in it, so that the poor man does not hear rebuke and shame from the rich man, saying to him, “My portion is greater than your portion in the public offerings.”
Proverbs.translator_note: The abbreviation ומ"א is left as printed and not resolved here.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the lamp of the wicked shall be put out
Proverbs.english_translation: *Yid'akh* — an expression of leaping, for the flame leaps and is cut off.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: By pride cometh only contention
Proverbs.english_translation: Dispute (*machloket*).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: But with the well-advised is wisdom
Proverbs.english_translation: And with those who take counsel wisdom lodges.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Wealth gotten by vanity shall be diminished
Proverbs.english_translation: He who makes his lesson bundles upon bundles will diminish, for it will be forgotten by him little by little.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Hope deferred
Proverbs.english_translation: He assures himself concerning his fellow, and he does not do it.
Proverbs.translator_note: The sentence is translated literally.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: maketh the heart sick
Proverbs.english_translation: It brings sickness to the heart; and this *machalah* is not a noun, like “and I will take sickness (*machalah*) away from the midst of thee” (Exodus 23:25), but like “cheweth (*ma'aleh*) the cud” (Leviticus 11:3).
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed “Leviticus 10:11” is Leviticus 11:3.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: But desire fulfilled is a tree of life
Proverbs.english_translation: It is inverted, that is: “desire fulfilled” is like a tree of life. “Hope” — the Holy One, blessed be He, hoped for Israel and looked that they would return, and they did not return; in the end it comes to them as heart-sickness; and when His desire comes, that they do His will, it is a tree of life to them.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Whoso despiseth the word shall suffer thereby
Proverbs.english_translation: One who despises one of the words of Torah (ד"ת) — in the end he is pledged for it.
Proverbs.translator_note: The abbreviation ד"ת is read here as “words of Torah.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: he that feareth the commandment shall be rewarded
Proverbs.english_translation: He will receive reward. And *Midrash Tehillim* expounds “Whoso despiseth the word shall suffer thereby” of David, who said before the Holy One, blessed be He, “Master of the universe, what benefit is there in the fools that You created?” He said to him, “By your life, in the end you will need folly” — when he came before Achish he feigned madness “and his spittle fell upon his beard,” etc. (1 Samuel 21).
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed “1 Samuel 21:14”.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The teaching of the wise is a fountain of life
Proverbs.english_translation: For it teaches him to depart from the snares of death.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the way of the faithless is harsh
Proverbs.english_translation: Hard for him and for others.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Every prudent man dealeth with forethought
Proverbs.english_translation: His deed — like David: “Let there be sought for my lord the king a young virgin,” etc. (1 Kings 1:2).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: a fool unfoldeth folly
Proverbs.english_translation: This is Ahasuerus: “And let the king appoint officers” (Esther 2:3) — they knew that he would not marry all of them, and whoever had a daughter hid her.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A wicked messenger falleth into evil
Proverbs.english_translation: Like Balaam, to whom the Holy One, blessed be He, said, “Go with the men,” and he acted wickedly to give Balak evil counsel; therefore he fell by the sword.
Proverbs.translator_note: JPS Numbers 22:20 reads “rise up, go with them.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: a faithful ambassador is health
Proverbs.english_translation: This is Moses our teacher.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Poverty and shame shall be to him that refuseth instruction
Proverbs.english_translation: Poverty and shame come upon one who casts off instruction.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The desire accomplished is sweet to the soul
Proverbs.english_translation: When a person’s desire comes to him, it is sweet to his soul; therefore “it is an abomination to fools to depart from evil,” because it is sweet to them to fulfil their desire.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The desire accomplished
Proverbs.english_translation: *Nihyah* — *havah* (“come to be”). Another explanation: “a desire that is fulfilled” — the Holy One, blessed be He, desires that Israel do His will, and when His desire is fulfilled, it is sweet to Him; and it is the abomination of the wicked that they turn from their evil, which would fulfil their desire.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He that walketh with wise men shall be wise
Proverbs.english_translation: He will become wise; and “the companion of fools” is one who joins fools to be his friends.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: shall smart for it
Proverbs.english_translation: *Yeroa* — will be shattered.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Evil pursueth sinners
Proverbs.english_translation: A wicked man — his wickedness pursues him until he is destroyed.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A good man leaveth an inheritance to his children’s children
Proverbs.english_translation: His merit and his money to his children’s children; but a sinner does not leave an inheritance to his children, for “the wealth of the sinner is laid up for the righteous,” as it is written, “And Esther set Mordecai over the house of Haman.”
Proverbs.translator_note: The quotation is Esther 8:2.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Much food is in the tillage of the poor
Proverbs.english_translation: I saw in the Great Masorah: “*rav ochel*” — thirty-three; “*rav*” with *kamatz*; and this is a *chataf-kamatz* and is joined to *ochel* by a *maqqef*; and *ochel* I saw there pointed with a *patach* (that is, a *segol*, which is a small *patach*), and its accent is on the ending, like “all the food (*ochel*) of these good years” (Genesis 41); and according to its pointing, this is its meaning: “A great deal of produce comes into the world through the tillage of poor men” — that is, much Torah goes out through disciples whose teachers learn from them, from their sharp argument by which they argue in *halakhah*.
Proverbs.translator_note: The remarks on the Masorah and the vowels are elliptical and translated literally. Printed “Genesis 41” is Genesis 41:35.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: But there is that is swept away by want of righteousness
Proverbs.english_translation: And there are many of them who are consumed from the world for “lo mishpat” (lack of justice), because they do not conduct themselves properly; and regarding the produce, there is produce that is smitten on account of its owner, who does not take out its tithes and the gifts to the poor as is right. And our Rabbis explained it in tractate *Chagigah*: “And there is one who is swept away by the messenger of the Angel of Death, who exchanges name for name and kills one whose time has not yet come.” But if so, the end of the verse has no connection with its beginning.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He that spareth his rod hateth his son
Proverbs.english_translation: In the end he hates his son, for he sees him in the end going out to an evil upbringing.
Proverbs.translator_note: The phrase *tarbut ra'ah* is translated as “an evil upbringing.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: chasteneth him betimes
Proverbs.english_translation: *Shicharo musar* — always, in the mornings, he chastises him.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The righteous eateth to the satisfying of his desire
Proverbs.english_translation: It seems that he will be sated (סא"א and it is written beneath it).
Proverbs.translator_note: it is left as printed.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the belly of the wicked shall want
Proverbs.english_translation: *Techsar* — it does not seem that he will be sated.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Every wise woman buildeth her house
Proverbs.english_translation: *Chokhmot* is pointed with a *patach*, which means it is not a noun, but “the wisdoms among women build their houses,” which are sustained through them, like the wife of On son of Peleth, as is explained in the chapter *Chelek*.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: But the foolish
Proverbs.english_translation: And a foolish woman.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: plucketh it down with her hands
Proverbs.english_translation: “She tears down her house” — this is the wife of Korah.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He that walketh in his uprightness feareth the LORD
Proverbs.english_translation: One who fears HaShem; and one who is perverse in his ways, that is, distorts his ways.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: despiseth Him
Proverbs.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: In the mouth of the foolish is a rod of pride
Proverbs.english_translation: A staff of pride, like Pharaoh, who said, “Who is the LORD, that I should hearken unto His voice?” (Exodus 5:2).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: shall preserve them
Proverbs.english_translation: *Tishmoram* — like *tishmor otam*; it will guard the wise.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Where no oxen are, the crib is clean
Proverbs.english_translation: Where there are no oxen the crib is empty, for not even straw is found in the house.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: clean
Proverbs.english_translation: *Bar* — clean and empty; that is, where there are no Torah scholars, no ruling is found in accordance with the *halakhah*.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: breatheth forth lies
Proverbs.english_translation: And he always speaks a lie, a false witness.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A scorner seeketh wisdom, and findeth it not
Proverbs.english_translation: When he needs wisdom, he does not find it in his heart.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Go from the presence of a foolish man
Proverbs.english_translation: From joining always with him.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: thou wilt not perceive the lips of knowledge
Proverbs.english_translation: *U-val yada'ta* — in the end you will not know wisdom.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The wisdom of the prudent is to look well to his way
Proverbs.english_translation: One who is wise understands his way, to weigh his paths.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the folly of fools is deceit
Proverbs.english_translation: It is the deceit in their heart; in the end it brings them to folly.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Amends pleadeth for fools
Proverbs.english_translation: For they are sinners who must give money to him against whom they sinned, and their guilt (*asham*) pleads for them, because they bring him their money, like the Philistines, of whom it is said, “Take for yourselves five golden emerods and five golden mice,” etc., “and give glory to the God of Israel; peradventure He will lighten His hand from off you” (1 Samuel 6).
Proverbs.translator_note: The quotation is from 1 Samuel 6:5 (and its context); Rashi’s wording differs from JPS, which reads “Wherefore you shall make images of your emerods, and images of your mice… and you shall give glory unto the God of Israel; peradventure He will lighten His hand from off you.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Amends
Proverbs.english_translation: *Asham* — *amends* in French (אמנד"א).
Proverbs.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Proverbs 14:9 (“Amende”), in forms such as אמינדא and אמינדינצי; the printed form (אמנד"א) is a variant spelling.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: But among the upright there is good will
Proverbs.english_translation: *Ratzon* — *apaiement* [printed אפיימינ"ט] in Old French (goodwill): the Holy One, blessed be He, is pleased with them.
Proverbs.translator_note: Old French. The same word is listed in Darmesteter at Proverbs 11:27 (“Bienveillance”), in forms such as אפיימנט; the reading is *apaiement* (“goodwill”), from Darmesteter’s index; the printed form (אפיימינ"ט) is a variant spelling.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The heart knoweth its own bitterness
Proverbs.english_translation: The bitterness of his soul, his toil and his effort, in which he laboured in Torah; therefore in his joy no stranger will mingle when he receives his reward in the future. Another explanation: “The heart knoweth its own bitterness” — Israel, who are bitter of soul in exile and were killed for the sanctification of the Name, and in their joy no stranger will mingle in the future. “The house of the wicked” — the house of Aram shall be destroyed.
Proverbs.translator_note: The last sentence quotes the next verse (14:11) and is translated as printed (“Aram”).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: There is a way which seemeth right unto a man
Proverbs.english_translation: One who commits a transgression and says, “There is no transgression in it.” Another explanation: “There is a way which seemeth right before a man” — the way of a lazy person was right in the eyes of Esau, who was a man of the field, “and the end thereof,” etc.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Even in laughter the heart acheth
Proverbs.english_translation: For the Holy One, blessed be He, plays with them in this world, their heart will ache in the world to come; and so it says, “but you shall cry for sorrow of heart” (Isaiah 65:14).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The dissembler in heart shall have his fill from his own ways
Proverbs.english_translation: Esau.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: a good man shall be satisfied from himself
Proverbs.english_translation: Jacob.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The thoughtless believeth every word
Proverbs.english_translation: To their words, and is enticed after them. Another explanation, on “Even in laughter the heart acheth” (Proverbs 14:13): laughter is for the fool, “It is as sport to a fool to do wickedness” (Proverbs 10:23), and its end is “the heart acheth.” “*Sug lev*” (14:14), the wicked heart — like “silver dross (*sigim*)” (Proverbs 26:23); *sug* is the name of the refuse; *sug* is silver that is mixed with refuse.
Proverbs.translator_note: The word וניסת is read here as “is enticed.” Printed “Proverbs 10” and “Proverbs 26” are 10:23 and 26:23.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the prudent man looketh well to his going
Proverbs.english_translation: And above him — above the wicked — the righteous man will be.
Proverbs.translator_note: This comment belongs to 14:14 (“And a good man shall be satisfied from himself”); the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The thoughtless believeth every word
Proverbs.english_translation: To the talebearers.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the prudent man looketh well to his going
Proverbs.english_translation: To his steps; that is, he will look out from quarrelling and will wait until it is known to him for certain.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A wise man feareth
Proverbs.english_translation: Of punishment.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: departeth from evil
Proverbs.english_translation: From the evil.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: behaveth overbearingly
Proverbs.english_translation: He strengthens himself to work with force.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: and is confident
Proverbs.english_translation: And slips and falls to the ground, like “in a land of peace thou art secure (*boteach*)” (Jeremiah 12:5), and Targum Jonathan renders it: “you are confident and fall, slipping.” And some explain it as actual trust: “he is confident in his palace,” to say, “No evil will come upon me.”
Proverbs.translator_note: Rashi reads *boteach* in Jeremiah 12:5 as “slips”; JPS there reads “though in a land of peace thou art secure.” The Targum wording is translated as printed.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He that is soon angry
Proverbs.english_translation: One who hastens to take vengeance in his anger.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: a man of wicked devices
Proverbs.english_translation: Thoughts of evil counsel.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the prudent are crowned with knowledge
Proverbs.english_translation: They make it a crown for their head, and the end.
Proverbs.translator_note: The comment ends with the word וסוף as printed.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The evil bow before the good
Proverbs.english_translation: In the future.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: even of his own neighbour
Proverbs.english_translation: Even to his groomsmen and those who love him; *gam* is an expression of “even.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The poor is hated
Proverbs.english_translation: An ignorant man (*am ha'aretz*) who does not know how to conduct himself properly.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: In all labour there is profit
Proverbs.english_translation: In every toil of work there will be profit; but words of vanity lead only to want.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The crown of the wise is their riches
Proverbs.english_translation: For they are rich in Torah.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the folly of fools remaineth folly
Proverbs.english_translation: The ruin of fools is the folly, that he became lazy from wisdom.
Proverbs.translator_note: The sentence is translated literally.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: In the fear of the LORD a man hath strong confidence
Proverbs.english_translation: It was said of Abraham, “for now I know that thou art a God-fearing man” (Genesis 22), and He assured him, “that in blessing I will bless thee,” etc.
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 26” is Genesis 22:12; the second quotation is Genesis 22:17.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: his children shall have a place of refuge
Proverbs.english_translation: He.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: a place of refuge
Proverbs.english_translation: That they may take refuge and hide in the shade of his merit.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: In the multitude of people is the king’s glory
Proverbs.english_translation: When the congregation are meritorious, it is the glory of the Holy One, blessed be He.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: in the want of people
Proverbs.english_translation: When they do not cleave to Him.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the ruin of the prince
Proverbs.english_translation: The lack of His princeship (*roznuto*): as it were, He gives of His glory to a foreign god and lets the nations rule over His children.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: exalteth folly
Proverbs.english_translation: He sets it apart for his portion.
Proverbs.translator_note: The pronoun “it” is translated as printed.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A tranquil heart is the life of the flesh
Proverbs.english_translation: A heart of flesh that heals the evil and passes over its measures — it is the life of the creatures of the Holy One, blessed be He, who are flesh and blood.
Proverbs.translator_note: The phrase עובר על מדותיו is translated literally.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the rottenness of the bones
Proverbs.english_translation: A man given to wrath — he is rot of the bones to all.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the righteous, even when he is brought to death, hath hope
Proverbs.english_translation: When he dies he is confident that he will come to the Garden of Eden.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: wisdom resteth
Proverbs.english_translation: It dwells and is quiet in ease; an expression of rest and repose.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: it maketh itself known
Proverbs.english_translation: The little wisdom that is in his heart proclaims itself: “A coin in a flask cries ‘kish, kish.’”
Proverbs.translator_note: The Aramaic proverb is translated as printed; its sense is not explained in the source.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Righteousness exalteth a nation
Proverbs.english_translation: Israel.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: sin is a reproach to any people
Proverbs.english_translation: They are the idolaters who rob from this one and give to that one.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: his wrath striketh him that dealeth shamefully
Proverbs.english_translation: [And his wrath] shall be upon a servant who brings shame.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: perverseness therein is a wound to the spirit
Proverbs.english_translation: And perverseness therein is a breaking by the wind: when he perverts with the tongue, his end is to bring upon himself a breaking that comes by the wind — the east wind, which is prepared to exact retribution from the wicked, as it is written, “by a strong east wind” (Exodus 14:21); “I will scatter them as with an east wind” (Jeremiah 18:17); “With the east wind Thou breakest the ships of Tarshish” (Psalms 48:8).
Proverbs.translator_note: Rashi reads the last word of the verse as “by the wind” (*ba-ruach*); JPS reads “a wound to the spirit.” The source gives no separate lemma; the comment begins with the verse words, and the lemma shown is that phrase of the verse. Printed “Jeremiah 28” is Jeremiah 18:17.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: In the house of the righteous is much treasure
Proverbs.english_translation: The Temple that David the righteous built is great treasure and a tower of strength for Israel.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: But in the revenues of the wicked is trouble
Proverbs.english_translation: And through the bringing of the image that Manasseh brought into it, it was troubled.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The lips of the wise disperse knowledge
Proverbs.english_translation: They crown knowledge, like a golden crown (*zer*).
Proverbs.translator_note: Rashi connects *yazaru* with *zer*, “a crown”; JPS reads “disperse.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: But the heart of the foolish is not stedfast
Proverbs.english_translation: [Lemma: Not so.] It is not genuine gold.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The sacrifice of the wicked
Proverbs.english_translation: An abomination — Balak and Balaam.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the prayer of the upright
Proverbs.english_translation: This is Moses.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: There is grievous correction for him that forsaketh the way
Proverbs.english_translation: Severe afflictions are prepared for one who departs from the way of the Holy One, blessed be He.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The nether-world and Destruction are before the LORD
Proverbs.english_translation: All that is within it is revealed before Him.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: How much more
Proverbs.english_translation: It is an a fortiori argument (*kal vachomer*).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A merry heart maketh a cheerful countenance
Proverbs.english_translation: If you gladden the heart of the Holy One, blessed be He, by walking in His ways, He will make His face pleasant to you, to do all your will; and if you grieve Him, He will show you a broken spirit, as it is said, “and it grieved Him at His heart” (Genesis 6:6); “And the LORD said: ‘I will blot out man,’” etc. (6:7). *Ruach nekhe'ah* — *talent* in French: a spirit of anger.
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 5” is Genesis 6:6–7. The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: All the days of the poor are evil
Proverbs.english_translation: Even Sabbaths and festivals, for Samuel said: a change of routine is the beginning of intestinal illness.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: he that is of a merry heart
Proverbs.english_translation: One whose heart is good in his wealth.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: hath a continual feast
Proverbs.english_translation: All his years seem to him like days of feasting — to teach you that a man should be happy with his portion. And our Rabbis expounded what they expounded in (the chapter) *Chelek*.
Proverbs.translator_note: The word בחלק is read here as the chapter *Chelek*.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Than great treasure and turmoil therewith
Proverbs.english_translation: The voice of people crying out because the treasure was made from robbery and violence, like “and behold many tumults within it, and the oppressed in its midst” (Amos 3:9).
Proverbs.translator_note: JPS Amos 3:9 reads “And behold the great confusions therein, And the oppressions in the midst thereof.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Than a stalled ox
Proverbs.english_translation: *Avus* — that the food is stuffed into his mouth against his will in order to fatten him; and so “fatted fowl (*barburim avusim*)” (1 Kings 5:3). And one may interpret it as a parable concerning the small handful (*kometz*) of the poor man, which is dearer than the sin-offering ox of the wicked. Another explanation: “Better is a dinner of herbs” — to give to the poor, “and love therewith” — to show him a pleasant face, than a stalled ox — to feed him fat meat and show him an angry face.
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed “1 Kings 4” is 1 Kings 5:3 (the numbering of the site’s JPS text).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A wrathful man stirreth up discord
Proverbs.english_translation: A man who has no restraint on his spirit, to prolong his anger, stirs up strife.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: he that is slow to anger
Proverbs.english_translation: One who does not hasten to take vengeance and to quarrel.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: appeaseth strife
Proverbs.english_translation: For it ends and is stilled from upon him (another version: of itself).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The way of the sluggard is as though hedged by thorns
Proverbs.english_translation: It seems in his eyes as if the roads were fenced before him with a fence of thorns (*chadakim*).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: hedged by thorns
Proverbs.english_translation: *Meshukat* — a fence, like “I will take away the hedge thereof” (Isaiah 5:5); *chedek* — thorns.
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 5” is Isaiah 5:5.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the path of the upright is even
Proverbs.english_translation: Trodden down and cleared. And an Aggadic midrash: the way of Esau is like this thorn that is entangled in a fleece of wool; if you take it away from here, it clings over there; so a man cannot escape his machinations without money.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: a foolish man despiseth his mother
Proverbs.english_translation: He causes his mother to be despised.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Folly is joy to him that lacketh understanding
Proverbs.english_translation: It is a joy to one who lacks heart (sense).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: For want of counsel purposes are frustrated
Proverbs.english_translation: Without counsel a thought will not stand.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A man hath joy in the answer of his mouth
Proverbs.english_translation: As it sounds: through a soft answer and gentle speech people love him. And our Rabbis expounded it of masters of study: if they find an answer in their mouths, then it will be established in them and they will rejoice.
Proverbs.translator_note: The abbreviation בפיה' is read as “in their mouths.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: a word in due season, how good is it
Proverbs.english_translation: They ask about the laws of Passover and the laws of the festival in its time.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The path of life goeth upward for the wise
Proverbs.english_translation: Like “seraphim stand above him” (Isaiah 6:2) — that is, before the wise man the path of life is adorned and prepared.
Proverbs.translator_note: Rashi’s wording differs from JPS Isaiah 6:2, “Above Him stood the seraphim.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: troubleth his own house
Proverbs.english_translation: For he is greedy for gain.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: he that hateth gifts shall live
Proverbs.english_translation: Since he hates gifts, all the more so he hates robbery.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: studieth to answer
Proverbs.english_translation: He thinks and understands what to answer before he gives a reply.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The light of the eyes
Proverbs.english_translation: In Torah.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: rejoiceth the heart
Proverbs.english_translation: When they ask him a matter and he knows what to answer. But according to its plain sense, as it sounds: something that is a desire for the sight of the eyes gladdens the heart and clears the sorrow of the heart, such as a garden of vegetables and rivers that attract.
Proverbs.translator_note: The printed word המושכי' is abbreviated; it is read as “that attract.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And before honour goeth humility
Proverbs.english_translation: Humility causes honour to come.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The preparations of the heart are man’s
Proverbs.english_translation: He arranges his counsel and his words in his heart.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the answer of the tongue is from the LORD
Proverbs.english_translation: When he comes to answer, the Holy One, blessed be He, gives him insight into his words; or, if he is worthy, He prepares for him a good answer.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the LORD weigheth the spirits
Proverbs.english_translation: And He counts the hearts — who is good and who is evil.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Commit thy works unto the LORD
Proverbs.english_translation: Roll and cast upon Him your needs, and your thoughts will be established. Another explanation: “Commit thy works unto the LORD” — pray before Him for all your needs.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: shall be established
Proverbs.english_translation: They will be grounded and endure.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The LORD hath made every things for His own purpose
Proverbs.english_translation: He made everything for the sake of His praise, like “Sing unto the LORD with thanksgiving” (Psalms 147:7). Another explanation: to bear witness to Him — that is, His work bears witness to Him about His mighty acts, which are taught in the Aggadah of Psalms.
Proverbs.translator_note: The printed word שניה' is not clear; it is read here as “taught.” Printed “Psalms 147” is Psalms 147:7.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: even the wicked for the day of evil
Proverbs.english_translation: He made him to keep him for the day of evil, and all this is for His praise.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: My hand upon it!
Proverbs.english_translation: From hand to hand (*miyad leyad*) the recompense for the pride of his heart comes to him.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: by the fear of the LORD men depart from evil
Proverbs.english_translation: Through the fear of the LORD, departing from evil.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He maketh even his enemies to be at peace with him
Proverbs.english_translation: He will desire for him that they be at peace with him.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A man’s heart deviseth his way
Proverbs.english_translation: To walk a straight way.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: But the LORD directeth his steps
Proverbs.english_translation: As we have learned (Shabbat 104): one who comes to purify himself is helped.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A divine sentence is in the lips of the king
Proverbs.english_translation: Upon the lips of a wise man who sits in judgment.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A just balance and scales are the LORD’S
Proverbs.english_translation: To pay a man according to his deeds. *Mishpat* — *justice* in French: the repayment of man’s iniquities with a balance and scales.
Proverbs.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: All the weights of the bag are His work
Proverbs.english_translation: Just as in a bag of stones there are large and small weights, all is according to a man’s deeds.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: It is an abomination to kings to commit wickedness
Proverbs.english_translation: It is an abominable thing for judges, and it is not fitting for them to do wickedness.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The wrath of a king is as messengers of death
Proverbs.english_translation: It is like angels of death, like the emissaries of their death.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: a wise man will pacify it
Proverbs.english_translation: He will appease it.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: In the light of the king’s countenance is life
Proverbs.english_translation: One to whom the Holy One, blessed be He, shows a pleasant face — it is life for him; therefore a man must straighten his way before Him.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: his favour is as a cloud of the latter rain
Proverbs.english_translation: One with whom He is pleased — His favour is good for him, like a cloud that brings the rain.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Better it is to be of a lowly spirit with the humble
Proverbs.english_translation: It is better to associate with the humble and to be of a lowly spirit among them than to divide spoil with the proud.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He that giveth heed unto the word shall find good
Proverbs.english_translation: One who sets his heart to contemplate His words, to level his paths, shall find good.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: whoso trusteth in the LORD
Proverbs.english_translation: When he weighs his paths and sees in it a commandment in which there is danger or financial loss, and he trusts in the Holy One, blessed be He, and does the good.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: happy is he
Proverbs.english_translation: They are his own steps (*ashurav*).
Proverbs.translator_note: Rashi connects *ashrav* with *ashur*, “a step.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The wise in heart is called a man of discernment
Proverbs.english_translation: Who learned wisdom from his teacher.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: is called a man of discernment
Proverbs.english_translation: In the end he will be discerning in matters, sharpened in his wisdom, and they will call him discerning.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the sweetness of the lips increaseth learning
Proverbs.english_translation: When a man gives his words flavour for the student and sweetens his words with reasons, he increases learning.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Understanding is a fountain of life unto him that hath it
Proverbs.english_translation: To its owner; and so the explanation of the verse: the understanding of its owners is a fountain of life to him.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: folly is the chastisement of fools
Proverbs.english_translation: The afflictions of fools come to them through folly; and so it means: folly is affliction for fools.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The heart of the wise teacheth his mouth
Proverbs.english_translation: His heart teaches his mouth to speak with eloquence (“and upon his lips his heart adds learning”).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Pleasant words are as a honeycomb
Proverbs.english_translation: *Tzuf devash* — sweet honey, *brisque* in French.
Proverbs.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters (ברישק"ה) and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Pleasant words
Proverbs.english_translation: Words of Torah.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: There is a way which seemeth right unto a man
Proverbs.english_translation: That is straight before a man.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The hunger of the labouring man laboureth for him
Proverbs.english_translation: For his need he toils.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: For his mouth compelleth him
Proverbs.english_translation: When his mouth compels him and demands food for him, then his labour stands him in good stead, for he eats what he has already laboured for.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: An ungodly man diggeth up evil
Proverbs.english_translation: In his heart he plows evil.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: in his lips there is as a burning fire
Proverbs.english_translation: [And upon] his lips like a scorching fire of evil — like a fire that burns upon his lips until he brings it out with his mouth and finishes it.
Proverbs.translator_note: The source prints only the word ועל as lemma.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: as a burning fire
Proverbs.english_translation: Scorching, like “and all faces shall be scorched (*nitzr'vu*) therein” (Ezekiel 21:3).
Proverbs.translator_note: JPS Ezekiel 21:3 reads “shall be seared thereby.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: a whisperer separateth familiar friends
Proverbs.english_translation: And through his murmuring and complaining he separates from himself the Chief of the world.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He shutteth his eyes
Proverbs.english_translation: An expression of winking, and so “I will counsel thee, Mine eye upon thee” (Psalms 32:8).
Proverbs.translator_note: Rashi’s wording differs from JPS, “I will give counsel, Mine eye being upon thee.” Printed “Psalms 32:8”.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He that biteth his lips bringeth evil to pass
Proverbs.english_translation: Like “for the evil was determined against him,” etc. (Esther 7:7), and he causes evil to come to the world.
Proverbs.translator_note: The quoted words are identified here as Esther 7:7 (JPS: “he saw that there was evil determined against him by the king”); the source gives no reference.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: It is found in the way of righteousness
Proverbs.english_translation: Through charity they lengthen their days.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: he that ruleth his spirit
Proverbs.english_translation: He subdues his inclination (*yetzer*).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The lot is cast into the lap
Proverbs.english_translation: A man casts a lot between himself and himself.
Proverbs.translator_note: The phrase is translated literally.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the whole disposing thereof is of the LORD
Proverbs.english_translation: To choose for each and every one his portion.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Better is a dry morsel and quietness therewith
Proverbs.english_translation: It would have been good for the Holy One, blessed be He, to lay waste (*lehachriv*) His house and His city and be in quiet, because of the sins of Israel.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Than a house full of feasting with strife
Proverbs.english_translation: For they were offering sacrifices of strife in His house.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A servant that dealeth wisely shall have rule over a son that dealeth shamefully
Proverbs.english_translation: Because Nebuchadnezzar had the sense to take three steps for the honour of the Holy One, he rose to greatness and ruled over Israel, who were put to shame by their deeds, and divided their inheritance before their eyes. Another explanation: A righteous proselyte is better than a wicked native-born, and in the future he will divide spoil and inheritance among the children of Israel, as it is said, “And it shall come to pass, that in what tribe the stranger sojourneth,” etc. (Ezekiel 47:23).
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed “Ezekiel 17” is Ezekiel 47:23.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The refining pot is for silver
Proverbs.english_translation: The vessel in which silver is refined, which they make of the ash of parched matter upon a potsherd, is called a *matzref*.
Proverbs.translator_note: The phrase אפר מקלה is translated literally.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the furnace for gold
Proverbs.english_translation: The vessel in which gold is refined, in which they purify gold, like a broken pot, is called a *kur*.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The refining pot is for silver, and the furnace for gold
Proverbs.english_translation: The refining pot is made to refine silver for its work, and likewise the furnace to purify gold; but the hearts the Holy One, blessed be He, purifies and tests, and He knows their thoughts.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: An evil-doer
Proverbs.english_translation: Wicked.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: giveth heed to wicked lips
Proverbs.english_translation: He accepts slander and false witnesses.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: a liar giveth ear to a mischievous tongue
Proverbs.english_translation: *Mezin* — *ma'zin* (gives ear): one who lies gives ear to a tongue of calamities.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Children’s children are the crown of old men
Proverbs.english_translation: When they see their grandchildren walking in a good way.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the glory of children are their fathers
Proverbs.english_translation: When their fathers are righteous, it is the glory of the children.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Overbearing speech
Proverbs.english_translation: Words of pride.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Much less do lying lips a prince
Proverbs.english_translation: And all the more, lying speech does not befit a noble.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: a precious stone
Proverbs.english_translation: When a man comes before the Holy One, blessed be He, and appeases Him with words and returns to Him, it is a precious stone and pearls in His eyes.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Whithersoever he turneth, he prospereth
Proverbs.english_translation: In all that he asks of Him, He makes him succeed.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He that covereth a transgression seeketh love
Proverbs.english_translation: If one man sins against another and this one covers it over and does not mention his sin to him and does not show him an angry face, he causes him to love him.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: he that harpeth on a matter
Proverbs.english_translation: One who bears enmity and mentions it to him at once: “This and that you did to me.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: estrangeth a familiar friend
Proverbs.english_translation: Then he separates from himself the Chief of the world, who is the Holy One, blessed be He, who warned him, “Thou shalt not take vengeance, nor bear any grudge” (Leviticus 19:18).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A rebuke entereth deeper into a man of understanding
Proverbs.english_translation: *Tachat* — its accent is on the upper syllable, on the *tav*, which is not so anywhere else in Scripture; therefore I say that it is a noun, like *chatat*; and so its explanation: the submission produced by a rebuke is more noticeable in a man of understanding than a hundred blows with which one strikes the fool.
Proverbs.translator_note: The remarks on accent and grammar are translated literally.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A rebellious man seeketh only evil
Proverbs.english_translation: That is, one whose every word is rebellion and stubbornness will always seek evil.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Let a bear robbed of her whelps meet a man
Proverbs.english_translation: It is better for a man that a bereaved bear meet him than that one of the fools meet him who incite him to turn away from HaShem and from His Torah.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The beginning of strife is as when one letteth out water
Proverbs.english_translation: One who begins a quarrel is like one who opens a hole in the sides of the water channel, and the water goes out through it, and the hole keeps widening; so strife keeps growing.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: before the quarrel break out
Proverbs.english_translation: Before your disgrace is uncovered, abandon the dispute.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: To buy wisdom
Proverbs.english_translation: To learn Torah.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: seeing he hath no understanding
Proverbs.english_translation: And he has no heart to fulfil it, and he learns Torah only to acquire a name.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A friend loveth at all times
Proverbs.english_translation: Always be a lover of friends, to acquire friends.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: a brother is born for adversity
Proverbs.english_translation: At the time of trouble a friend is born to you like a brother, to help you and to share in your trouble.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A man void of understanding is he that striketh hands
Proverbs.english_translation: Surety for money. Another explanation: he strikes hands with the wicked to walk in their ways, and he has already pledged a pledge before his neighbour; he has already pledged to the Holy One, blessed be He, to keep His commandments.
Proverbs.translator_note: The second sentence is translated literally.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He loveth transgression
Proverbs.english_translation: To transgress against his fellow.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: that loveth strife
Proverbs.english_translation: To quarrel and to contend.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He that exalteth his gate
Proverbs.english_translation: He speaks with pride, like “Keep the doors of thy mouth” (Micah 7:5).
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed “Micah 7” is Micah 7:5.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A merry heart is a good medicine
Proverbs.english_translation: When a man is happy with his portion, his face shines.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A wicked man taketh a gift out of the bosom
Proverbs.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He, accepts words of submission and appeasement out of the bosom of the wicked — that is, in secret, between Him and them.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: To pervert the ways of justice
Proverbs.english_translation: To turn his sentence from bad to good.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Wisdom is before him that hath understanding
Proverbs.english_translation: Wisdom is before the one who has understanding.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the eyes of a fool are in the ends of the earth
Proverbs.english_translation: He says, “Wisdom is not found before me, for it is far from me. How can I learn the order *Nezikin*, which is thirty chapters, tractate *Kelim*, thirty chapters, tractate *Shabbat*, twenty-four chapters?” But to a wise man it is an easy thing: today he learns two chapters and tomorrow two, and says, “So did those who were before me always do.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A foolish son is vexation to his father
Proverbs.english_translation: Like Jeroboam; he is vexation to the Holy One, blessed be He.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: bitterness to her that bore him
Proverbs.english_translation: To the Congregation of Israel, whom he caused to sin.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: To punish also the righteous is not good
Proverbs.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He, did not say to blot out the name of Israel from the earth, for it is not good in His eyes to punish all of them.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Nor to strike the noble for their uprightness
Proverbs.english_translation: To strike the good among them, who were noble in uprightness, as it is said, “and I will leave in Israel seven thousand, all the knees that have not bowed to Baal” (1 Kings 19:18).
Proverbs.translator_note: Rashi’s wording differs from JPS, “Yet will I leave seven thousand in Israel, all the knees which have not bowed unto Baal.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the noble for their uprightness
Proverbs.english_translation: Like what is said in another place, “But the liberal deviseth liberal things; and by liberal things shall he stand” (Isaiah 32:8); so we find a liberal man upon liberal things.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He that spareth his words hath knowledge
Proverbs.english_translation: One who has knowledge does not multiply words.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: he that husbandeth his spirit is a man of discernment
Proverbs.english_translation: *Yekar ruach* — a man of understanding holds back words.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He that separateth himself seeketh his own desire
Proverbs.english_translation: One who separates himself from the Holy One, blessed be He, so as not to keep His commandments, pursues the desire of his heart and his evil inclination, and in the end, “against all sound wisdom he snarls” — among the wise his disgrace will be uncovered. And our Rabbis expounded it of Lot, who separated from Abraham for the desire of his heart, as it is said, “So Lot chose him all the plain of the Jordan” (Genesis 13:11); this whole verse ע"ש adultery was said; and in the end his shame was uncovered in the synagogues and study-houses: “An Ammonite or a Moabite shall not enter…” (Deuteronomy 23:4).
Proverbs.translator_note: The abbreviation ע"ש is left as printed and not resolved here.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: But only that his heart may lay itself bare
Proverbs.english_translation: But only in the revealing of his heart; he desires to reveal what is in his heart.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: with ignominy reproach
Proverbs.english_translation: Reproach will come: one who chooses disgrace and adultery — it is a reproach to him.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The words of a man’s mouth
Proverbs.english_translation: Every *ish* in Scripture is an expression for a mighty man, great in might.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: a fountain of wisdom
Proverbs.english_translation: Like a flowing brook and like deep waters.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: It is not good to respect the person of the wicked
Proverbs.english_translation: As our Rabbis explained: it is not good for the wicked that favour is shown to them in this world, and they are punished in the World to Come.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: So as to turn aside the righteous in judgment
Proverbs.english_translation: It is good for the righteous that the pans of the scales are weighed down against them to condemn them in this world, and they are punished in their lifetime, for the World to Come. And according to its plain sense, as it sounds.
Proverbs.translator_note: The sentence is translated literally.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A fool’s lips enter into contention
Proverbs.english_translation: All his words come in the language of quarrel.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: his mouth calleth for strokes
Proverbs.english_translation: He calls for afflictions to bring them upon himself.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The words of a whisperer are as dainty morsels
Proverbs.english_translation: Blows (*mehalumot*).
Proverbs.translator_note: Rashi reads *mitlahamim* as related to *mehalumot*, “blows.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Even one that is slack in his work
Proverbs.english_translation: He withdraws from Torah, and he is a Torah scholar.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Is brother to him that is a destroyer
Proverbs.english_translation: To Satan.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The righteous runneth into it, and is set up on high
Proverbs.english_translation: And he becomes strong.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And as a high wall in his own conceit
Proverbs.english_translation: His wealth is for him in the chambers of his *maskit*, because the house that is paved with a pavement of stones that cover the ground is called *even maskit*.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The spirit of a man
Proverbs.english_translation: The spirit of a *gever*, that is, a mighty man, who puts no worry in his heart and receives all that comes upon him with joy and affection.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: will sustain his infirmity
Proverbs.english_translation: His strength does not depart from him.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A man’s gift maketh room for him
Proverbs.english_translation: According to its plain sense. And its midrash is about givers of charity: it speaks of one whose portion is enlarged for him in the future, and also in his lifetime he will be led before great men, and they say of him that he is important.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: parteth asunder the contentious
Proverbs.english_translation: These are litigants, like “Bring forth your reasons” (Isaiah 41:21), and in the Mishnah, “two who are *mit'atzmim* in a lawsuit”; named for the fact [ע"ש] that in their disputes they are strong (*atzumot*), they are called *atzumim* — either an expression of strength or an expression of shutting, like “shutteth his eyes” (Isaiah 33:15).
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 43” is Isaiah 41:21 (Rashi’s word is *atzumoteihem*, “their reasons”), and “ibid. 33” is Isaiah 33:15. The abbreviation ע"ש is read as “named for the fact that” (*al shem she-*), a very frequent usage in Rashi; flagged because it is my reading of the context.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A brother offended is harder to be won than a strong city
Proverbs.english_translation: There is a brother who rebelled against his brother and by his rebellion destroys a strong city — for example Lot against Abraham, Esau against Jacob.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: their contentions are like the bars of a castle
Proverbs.english_translation: And the quarrels between them separate them for ever, like the bar with which the gates of a palace are locked so that none may enter by it.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: they that indulge it shall eat the fruit thereof
Proverbs.english_translation: One who loves his tongue and accustoms it to Torah eats its reward in this world.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Whoso findeth a wife findeth a great good
Proverbs.english_translation: He has found Torah; and as it sounds: a good wife.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: obtaineth favour of the LORD
Proverbs.english_translation: *Vayafek* — and brings out; this is its plain sense. Another explanation: a man who has found a wife and found good, “*vayafek retzono*” — that man brings out favour from the Holy One, blessed be He. Rabbi Joseph Kara.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The poor useth entreaties
Proverbs.english_translation: The way of this one is thus and the way of that one is thus; it teaches you proper conduct (*derech eretz*): although the rich man answers impudently, the poor man speaks entreaties; and so is the relation of the teacher to the disciple.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: There are friends that one hath to his own hurt
Proverbs.english_translation: A man who acquires friends for himself — a day will yet come when he will need them and they will draw him near; and if you say, “What of it?” — there is a loving friend who cleaves closer than a brother, who will draw him nearer than his relatives and brothers.
Proverbs.translator_note: Rashi reads *le-hitro'e'a* differently from JPS (“to his own hurt”).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Also, that the soul be without knowledge is not good
Proverbs.english_translation: It is not good for a man to be without Torah.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: he that hasteth with his feet sinneth
Proverbs.english_translation: The sinner tramples and treads sins with his heels and says, “This is a light one; I will pass over it.” And our Rabbis explained “Also, without knowledge” as one who forces his wife to marital relations against her will.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: he that hasteth with his feet sinneth
Proverbs.english_translation: This is one who has relations and repeats. Another explanation: this is one who walks upon grass on the Sabbath.
Proverbs.translator_note: The phrase הבועל ושונה is translated literally.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The foolishness of man perverteth his way
Proverbs.english_translation: The evil comes to him through his iniquity, for through his folly he perverts his way and commits transgressions and is punished; and when trouble comes to him, his heart rages against the Holy One, and he hastens after the attribute of justice — like Joseph’s brothers, who said, “What is this that God hath done unto us?” (Genesis 42:28).
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 42” is Genesis 42:28.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Wealth addeth many friends
Proverbs.english_translation: Many lovers; and one may explain it of one who has learned Torah.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Many will entreat the favour of the liberal man
Proverbs.english_translation: All become friends to a man of gifts. One may explain it of givers of charity, and one may explain it of those who spread Torah.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: All the brethren of the poor do hate him
Proverbs.english_translation: His relatives.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: How much more do his friends go far from him
Proverbs.english_translation: And all the more so his friends, his groomsmen and his lovers.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He that pursueth words
Proverbs.english_translation: *Lo hemah* — he says, “So-and-so and so-and-so are my relatives, and so-and-so and so-and-so are my friends,” and it is all words of vanity. And one may explain it of one who is poor in Torah and good deeds.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He that pursueth words
Proverbs.english_translation: *Lo hemah* — he goes about to teach halakhah, and it is not in his hand. And the Midrash explains it of Joseph, who used to bring an evil report about his brothers and said to his father that they were suspected of eating a limb from a living animal; therefore they hated him, and he is called poor (*rash*) because he used to bring a false report about them. “And he pursues words, they are not” — we read it *lo* (“to him”): he pursues words for his own benefit; and regarding Joseph, “to him they are” (*lo hemah*), for his report returned upon him: he said that they were eating a limb from a living animal, and Scripture testifies about them that even at the time of the calamity they slaughtered a he-goat, as it is said, “and killed a he-goat” (Genesis 37:31); he said that they were treating the sons of the maidservants with contempt, therefore Joseph was sold as a servant; he said that they set their eyes on the daughters of the land; the Holy One, blessed be He, said, “By your life, I will incite the bear against you,” therefore “his master’s wife cast her eyes upon Joseph,” etc. (Genesis 39:7). (Bereshit Rabbah).
Proverbs.translator_note: The abbreviation בב"ר is read as Bereshit Rabbah. Printed “Genesis 37” and “Genesis 39” are 37:31 and 39:7.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Much less for a servant to have rule over princes
Proverbs.english_translation: It is an a fortiori argument, for it is not fitting that a servant rule over nobles.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: It is the discretion of a man to be slow to anger
Proverbs.english_translation: *Ha'arich* is like *leha'arich*; if he does so, it is wisdom for him.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: it is his glory to pass over a transgression
Proverbs.english_translation: That he pass over his measures.
Proverbs.translator_note: The phrase שיעבור על מדותיו is translated literally.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The king’s wrath is as the roaring of a lion
Proverbs.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the contentions of a wife are a continual dropping
Proverbs.english_translation: *Delef* — a dripping of rain that comes down in the house and troubles and disturbs those who dwell in the house; so are the quarrels of an evil woman.
Proverbs.translator_note: The printed word רע' is abbreviated; it is read as “evil.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Slothfulness casteth into a deep sleep
Proverbs.english_translation: Laziness brings sleep upon him — this is the figure of speech (*melitzah*); but the parable is about one who is lazy in his study: in the end they ask him a matter of wisdom and he is asleep.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the idle soul shall suffer hunger
Proverbs.english_translation: In the end he will be poor; and so one who deceives in his study, to make his Torah bundles upon bundles — in the end he will forget.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He that keepeth the commandment keepeth his soul
Proverbs.english_translation: He who does not set his heart to weigh them.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He that is gracious unto the poor lendeth unto the LORD
Proverbs.english_translation: When he falls ill and nears death, his charity pleads for him before the attribute of justice, saying: the poor man’s soul was convulsing to depart from hunger, and this one sustained it and restored it to its body; so I too will restore his soul to him.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Chasten thy son, for there is hope
Proverbs.english_translation: Do not strike him a deathblow.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A man of great wrath shall suffer punishment
Proverbs.english_translation: If you pass over your wrath and save your enemy, if you saw evil coming upon him, you will add days and good.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The lust of a man is his shame
Proverbs.english_translation: The main point is that people desire a man because of his kindness.
Proverbs.translator_note: Rashi reads *chasdo* as “his kindness”; JPS renders “his shame.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: a poor man is better than a liar
Proverbs.english_translation: And if he is a man of falsehood who promises and does not do, a poor man is better than he.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He shall not be visited with evil
Proverbs.english_translation: One who fears the Name will not be visited with any evil.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The sluggard burieth his hand in the dish
Proverbs.english_translation: In a hot cauldron: when they remove it from the fire and empty it, he warms his hand in it, and it is like “and the holy offerings sod they in pots, and in caldrons, and in pans” (2 Chronicles 35:13). And in the name of Rabbeinu Yitzchak HaLevi I heard: *batzalachat*, from the Aramaic “and he split (*vitzlach*)”: in the time of cold and frost, because of the cold and the frost the hands split and are cleft. And I heard: *batzalachat* — the slit of the tunic, which is called *pandadori* in French; that is, he hides it in his bosom (סא"א).
Proverbs.translator_note: it is left as printed. The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters (פאנדאדור"י) and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. Rashi’s quotation differs from JPS 2 Chronicles 35:13.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the simple will become prudent
Proverbs.english_translation: Because of the plagues of Pharaoh and the war with Amalek, Jethro became wise and converted.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: chase away his mother
Proverbs.english_translation: He drives away a mother.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A son that dealeth shamefully and reproachfully
Proverbs.english_translation: His ways: because Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian making sport — of idolatry and uncovering nakedness (forbidden relations) — this caused his mother to be sent away, and “the thing was very grievous in Abraham’s sight” (Genesis 21:11).
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 21” is Genesis 21:11.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Cease, my son, to hear the instruction
Proverbs.english_translation: It is an abbreviated verse, and this is its explanation: cease, my son, from straying from the words of knowledge, in order to hear instruction.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: That causeth to err
Proverbs.english_translation: *Chadal lishgot* is like *milishgot*; and so “and forbeareth to keep the passover” (Numbers 9:13); and so “for he left off counting” (Genesis 41:49).
Proverbs.translator_note: Rashi’s wording of Genesis 41:49 differs from JPS (“until they left off numbering; for it was without number”).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: An ungodly witness mocketh at right
Proverbs.english_translation: He will testify to a man the rhetoric of judgments of afflictions and death.
Proverbs.translator_note: The sentence is translated literally.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the mouth of the wicked devoureth iniquity
Proverbs.english_translation: The iniquity will swallow him.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Judgments are prepared for scorners
Proverbs.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He, has appointed for him judgments of leprosy (*tzara'at*), for this scorner who speaks slander.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He that provoketh him to anger
Proverbs.english_translation: One who angers him.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: It is an honour for a man to keep aloof from strife
Proverbs.english_translation: To rest from quarrelling.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: every fool will be snarling
Proverbs.english_translation: Whoever does not cease from strife — his disgrace will be uncovered.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The sluggard will not plow when winter setteth in
Proverbs.english_translation: Because of the cold the sluggard sits and does no work and does not occupy himself with Torah.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Counsel in the heart of man is like deep water
Proverbs.english_translation: Halakhah in the heart of a wise man is sealed.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: a man of understanding will draw it out
Proverbs.english_translation: And a discerning disciple comes and draws it out of his innards.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Most men will proclaim every one his own goodness
Proverbs.english_translation: There are many people who trust in their friends who promise them kindness, and they call them in their time of distress.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: every one his own goodness
Proverbs.english_translation: One who promises him to do kindness.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: But a faithful man who can find?
Proverbs.english_translation: One who promises and does.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A king that sitteth on the throne of judgment
Proverbs.english_translation: According to its plain sense; or one may explain it of the Holy One, blessed be He; and one may explain it of true judges.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The hearing ear, and the seeing eye
Proverbs.english_translation: That is, they are the work of His hands, and He desires an ear that hears instruction and an eye that sees what will be born (what is to come).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Love not sleep, lest thou come to poverty
Proverbs.english_translation: For you will be made poor.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: ‘It is bad, it is bad’, saith the buyer
Proverbs.english_translation: One who acquires Torah through hardship and the afflictions of hunger says, “Woe is me for this evil and this trouble”; and when he goes away full of wisdom, then he boasts of the suffering he suffered.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: when he is gone his way
Proverbs.english_translation: And goes away.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Bread of falsehood is sweet to a man
Proverbs.english_translation: Adultery with a married woman.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: his mouth shall be filled with gravel
Proverbs.english_translation: Fine stones, and so “He hath also broken my teeth with gravel stones” (Lamentations 3:16).
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed “Lamentations 3” is Lamentations 3:16.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And with good advice carry on war
Proverbs.english_translation: If you have come to fight against Satan, come with the strategies of repentance, prayer and fasting.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: meddle not with him that openeth wide his lips
Proverbs.english_translation: One who speaks smooth things to entice you and to incite you.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Whoso curseth his father or his mother
Proverbs.english_translation: His lamp will be extinguished at the pupil of darkness (*eshon choshekh*), at twilight and at the blackening of the darkness — that is, when the evil comes.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: An estate may be gotten hastily at the beginning
Proverbs.english_translation: Because he hurried to hasten and take first, like the sons of Gad and the sons of Reuben, who hurried to take their portion in Transjordan and spoke in haste, as it is said, “Sheepfolds will we build here for our cattle, and cities for our little ones” (Numbers 32:16); they made the main thing secondary, for they put their flocks before their little ones.
Proverbs.translator_note: Rashi’s wording differs from JPS Numbers 32:16 (“We will build sheepfolds here for our cattle, and cities for our little ones”). Printed “Numbers 32”.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: But the end thereof shall not be blessed
Proverbs.english_translation: For they were exiled several years before the other tribes, as is explained in *Seder Olam* and in Midrash Rabbi Tanchuma: in the second year of Ahaz, “And the LORD stirred up the spirit of the king of Assyria,” etc.; and the other tribes were exiled in the sixth year of Hezekiah, which is the ninth of Hoshea son of Elah.
Proverbs.translator_note: The quotation is identified here as a paraphrase of 1 Chronicles 5:26 (JPS: “And the God of Israel stirred up the spirit of Pul king of Assyria”); the source gives no reference.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: It is a snare to a man rashly to say: ‘Holy’
Proverbs.english_translation: When a man stumbles and is ensnared in transgressions, he spoils his holiness, like “and they shall drink, and swallow down” (Obadiah 1:16).
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed “Obadiah 1” is Obadiah 1:16.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And after vows to make inquiry
Proverbs.english_translation: A man must seek out offerings, to vow and to bring and to seek on behalf of his soul.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A wise king sifteth the wicked
Proverbs.english_translation: Pharaoh and his army.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A wise king
Proverbs.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: turneth the wheel over them
Proverbs.english_translation: He turned their measure back upon them, “and made them to drive heavily” (Exodus 14:25), corresponding to “and he hardened his heart” (Exodus 8:11).
Proverbs.translator_note: The printed reference “ibid. 5” is read as Exodus 8:11, where these words occur.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The spirit of man is the lamp of the LORD
Proverbs.english_translation: The soul within him testifies against him in judgment.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The glory of young men is their strength
Proverbs.english_translation: Just as the glory of young men is their strength, so the splendour of the old is the hoary head.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Sharp wounds cleanse away evil
Proverbs.english_translation: *Tamruk bara'* — our Rabbis expounded: one who cleanses himself for a matter of transgression ends up with wounds and bruises.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: So do stripes that reach the inward parts
Proverbs.english_translation: (This is the dropsy.)

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: But the LORD weigheth the hearts
Proverbs.english_translation: And He counts.
Proverbs.translator_note: The printed word ומונ' is abbreviated; it is read as “and counts” (compare the same comment at Proverbs 16:2).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A haughty look
Proverbs.english_translation: Pride of spirit.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: a proud heart
Proverbs.english_translation: A desire to fulfil the lust of his heart; it is the tillage of the wicked: their plowing and their thoughts are their sin.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The thoughts of the diligent
Proverbs.english_translation: An upright man who walks in truth and justice is diligent.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: tend only to plenteousness
Proverbs.english_translation: They come for success and profit.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: every one that is hasty
Proverbs.english_translation: He presses the hour.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The getting of treasures by a lying tongue
Proverbs.english_translation: *Po'el otzarot* — to increase wealth: with a lying tongue.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: they [that seek them] seek death
Proverbs.english_translation: They are snares (another version: seekers) of death for him.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The violence of the wicked shall drag them away
Proverbs.english_translation: *Yeguram* — *yagur otam*.
Proverbs.translator_note: The comment only restates the verb with its object; it is left untranslated.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The way of man is froward and strange
Proverbs.english_translation: A man who is a stranger, who has turned aside from the commandment — his way is crooked.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Than in a house in common with a contentious woman
Proverbs.english_translation: *Uvayit chaver* — that he enters his fellow’s house to speak with his wife. And an Aggadic midrash prophesied that in the end the Divine Presence would depart from Israel, who are like a woman of contentions.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Than in a house in common with a contentious woman
Proverbs.english_translation: A house in which they join companions to the Holy One, blessed be He, for example the image that Manasseh set up in the Temple of HaShem.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: When the scorner is punished, the thoughtless is made wise
Proverbs.english_translation: Through the afflictions of the scorners, the simple become wise and return in repentance.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The Righteous One considereth the house of the wicked
