Proverbs.english_translation: The Righteous One of the world is the Holy One, blessed be He; He sets His heart to cut off the house of the wicked, for example the memory of Amalek.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A gift in secret
Proverbs.english_translation: Charity.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: a present in the bosom strong wrath
Proverbs.english_translation: This too is charity; it will cover anger — it will cover strong wrath.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: To do justly is joy to the righteous
Proverbs.english_translation: It is joy to the Holy One, blessed be He, to execute judgment upon the righteous, in order to give them merit for life in the World to Come; and it is joy to the righteous that the Holy One, blessed be He, brings afflictions upon them so that they may merit the World to Come. So it is expounded in *Midrash Tehillim*.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: ruin to the workers of iniquity
Proverbs.english_translation: It is for the workers of iniquity, because they do not set their heart to return, and the afflictions do not benefit them, and they suffer without benefit.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The man that strayeth out of the way of understanding
Proverbs.english_translation: He withdraws from Torah.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Shall rest in the congregation of the shades
Proverbs.english_translation: In the assembly of Gehinnom.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: shall be a poor man
Proverbs.english_translation: *Ish machsor* — one who always loves the joy of feasting.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The wicked is a ransom for the righteous
Proverbs.english_translation: A righteous man is rescued, and a wicked man comes in his place, for example Mordecai and Haman.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: It is better to dwell in a desert land
Proverbs.english_translation: This too was said of the departure of the Divine Presence.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: But a foolish man swalloweth it up
Proverbs.english_translation: And the folly of a man.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A wise man scaleth the city of the mighty
Proverbs.english_translation: This is Moses our teacher, who went up among the angels, mighty in strength (“and brought down,” etc. — Torah).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A proud and haughty man, scorner is his name
Proverbs.english_translation: *Yahir* — one proud of spirit; in the end he becomes a scorner who does not care to hear instruction.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: But the righteous giveth and spareth not
Proverbs.english_translation: All the needs of his house, which the Holy One, blessed be He, prepares for him.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: How much more, when he bringeth it with the proceeds of wickedness?
Proverbs.english_translation: And all the more so when he brings it to do wickedness and with evil counsel — like the sacrifices of Balaam and Balak, which they brought only to curse Israel.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: But the man that obeyeth
Proverbs.english_translation: Who accepted what is written in the Torah, “Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbour” (Exodus 20:13).
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed “Exodus 20:13”; in the site’s JPS text these words are Exodus 20:16.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: shall speak unchallenged
Proverbs.english_translation: Always.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A wicked man hardeneth his face
Proverbs.english_translation: The wicked man shows his impudence at the time of his anger.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: hardeneth his face
Proverbs.english_translation: From the language of *af* (anger).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: There is no wisdom nor understanding Nor counsel against the LORD
Proverbs.english_translation: No wise or understanding man is of account before HaShem; wherever there is a desecration of the Name, no honour is given to a teacher.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A good name is rather to be chosen than great riches
Proverbs.english_translation: A good name.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: than silver and gold
Proverbs.english_translation: Good favour is chosen.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The LORD is the maker of them all
Proverbs.english_translation: When a poor man says to a rich man, “Provide for me,” and he answers harshly: “The LORD is the maker of them all” — the Holy One, blessed be He, makes them anew: this one poor and this one rich.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A prudent man seeth the evil, and hideth himself
Proverbs.english_translation: The punishment of sin — and he hides himself and does not commit the sin.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The reward of humility is the fear of the LORD
Proverbs.english_translation: Because of humility the fear of HaShem comes. Another explanation: humility is the main thing and fear is secondary; and *ekev* — a heel to it, a treading-place for its feet.
Proverbs.translator_note: The last phrase is translated literally.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Thorns and snares are in the way of the froward
Proverbs.english_translation: *Tzinim* — like “as thorns in your sides” (Numbers 33:55), and “and they shall come upon thee, *hotzen*” (Ezekiel 23:24) — an expression of troops and robbers.
Proverbs.translator_note: JPS Numbers 33:55 reads “pricks in your sides”; JPS Ezekiel 23:24 reads “they shall come against thee with hosts, chariots, and wheels.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: are in the way of the froward
Proverbs.english_translation: They are hidden in the ways of the one whose ways are crooked — that is, afflictions are prepared for him.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He that keepeth his soul holdeth himself far from them
Proverbs.english_translation: One who straightens his deeds will be saved from them.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Train up a child in the way he should go
Proverbs.english_translation: According to what you teach a child and train him in, whether for good or for evil. “Even when he is old, he will not depart from it.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The rich ruleth over the poor
Proverbs.english_translation: An ignorant man (*am ha'aretz*) always needs a Torah scholar.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He that soweth iniquity shall reap vanity
Proverbs.english_translation: He will reap *aven* according to his sowing; his reaping is according to his deed; his receiving of wages will be according to his doing.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the rod of his wrath shall fail
Proverbs.english_translation: The stalk of his ear of grain is finished and goes away. Some say (סא"א) that the rod of his wrath, by which he rules over people, is finished and goes away because he loses his power.
Proverbs.translator_note: it is left as printed.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Cast out the scorner
Proverbs.english_translation: The evil inclination.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He that loveth pureness of heart, That hath grace in his lips
Proverbs.english_translation: *Tahar lev chen sefatav* — one whose lips have grace.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the king shall be his friend
Proverbs.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He, loves him and holds him dear.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: There is a lion without
Proverbs.english_translation: How shall I go out to learn Torah?

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The mouth of strange women is a deep pit
Proverbs.english_translation: The mouth of idol worshippers.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He that is abhorred of the LORD shall fall therein
Proverbs.english_translation: One whom the Holy One, blessed be He, hates falls and stumbles in it.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He that is abhorred of the LORD
Proverbs.english_translation: *Za'um* — rebuked from before Him.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: One may oppress the poor, yet will their gain increase
Proverbs.english_translation: [To increase for him:] wealth.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: One may give to the rich, yet will want come
Proverbs.english_translation: In the end he gives his money to the wealthy idol-worshippers [עו"ג], and it comes only to want.
Proverbs.translator_note: The abbreviation עו"ג is read as “idol-worshippers” (*ovedei gilulim*); the printed form is kept in brackets. This reading is from Rashi’s usage and the context, not from a dictionary.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Incline thine ear, and hear the words of the wise
Proverbs.english_translation: To learn Torah from any wise man whatever.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: apply thy heart unto my knowledge
Proverbs.english_translation: And if your teacher is wicked, do not learn from his deeds.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: For it is a pleasant thing if thou keep them within thee
Proverbs.english_translation: It will be pleasant for you afterwards if you keep them and store them in your belly so that you do not forget them. And when will they be kept in your heart? When they are established upon your lips, when you bring them out with your mouth.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: That thy trust may be in the LORD, I have made them known to thee this day
Proverbs.english_translation: I am informing you that you should trust in HaShem and occupy yourself with Torah, and not say, “How shall I neglect my work, and how shall I be sustained?”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Have not I written unto thee excellent things
Proverbs.english_translation: *Shalishim* — Torah, Prophets and Writings.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: That I might make thee know the certainty of the words of truth
Proverbs.english_translation: I wrote *shalishim* for you so that you may understand from them the certainty of words of truth, to return words of truth.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: to them that send thee
Proverbs.english_translation: To one who asks you for a ruling.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Rob not the weak, because he is weak
Proverbs.english_translation: Do not rob him because you see that he is weak, because he is weak and has no strength to stand against you.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the LORD will plead their cause
Proverbs.english_translation: *Vekava* — and will rob the soul.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: despoil of life those that despoil them
Proverbs.english_translation: *Kov'eihem* — those who rob them; and in the Aramaic language *kevi'ah* is robbery. In tractate *Rosh Hashanah*: a certain man came before him and said to him, “So-and-so has robbed us (*kava'an*),” etc.
Proverbs.translator_note: The Aramaic is translated as printed.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Make no friendship with a man that is given to anger
Proverbs.english_translation: *Al tit'ra* — do not associate; an expression of friendship (*re'ut*).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Lest thou learn his ways
Proverbs.english_translation: *Pen te'elaf* — lest you learn.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Or of them that are sureties for debts
Proverbs.english_translation: Loans, like “any loan (*mashat*) of anything” (Deuteronomy 24:10).
Proverbs.translator_note: Rashi’s wording differs from JPS Deuteronomy 24:10, “any manner of loan.” Printed “Deuteronomy 24”.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Remove not the ancient landmark
Proverbs.english_translation: Do not draw back from the practice of your fathers. And our Rabbis of blessed memory said: one who places a basket under the vine at the time of its vintage so that the loose grapes (*peret*) fall into it — of this it is said, “Remove not the ancient landmark,” etc. *Tasseg* is like “turned backward” (Psalms 129:5).
Proverbs.translator_note: The printed word תשג is read as a form of *tasseg*. Printed “Psalms 129” is Psalms 129:5.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: When thou sittest to eat with a ruler
Proverbs.english_translation: *Lilchom* — to eat.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Consider well him that is before thee
Proverbs.english_translation: Set your mind to know who he is: whether his eye is stingy or generous.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And put a knife to thy throat
Proverbs.english_translation: In your jaws; if you saw that his eye is stingy, do not eat of his.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: If thou be a man given to appetite
Proverbs.english_translation: If you are ravenous and eager to eat, it is good to put a knife between your teeth. And our Rabbis expounded it of a disciple sitting before his teacher: if he knows of his teacher that he will give him an answer to every matter he asks him, let him be precise and ask for his teaching; and if not, let him be silent.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Be not desirous of his dainties
Proverbs.english_translation: But withdraw from him and go before a worthy teacher, and do not embarrass him with questions, since he does not know how to answer.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Weary not thyself to be rich
Proverbs.english_translation: To make your learning bundles upon bundles, for in the end you will forget it.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Wilt thou set thine eyes upon it? it is gone
Proverbs.english_translation: *Hata'if einekha bo* — as soon as you fold your eyes to itself, that learning is no longer found in you.
Proverbs.translator_note: The sentence is translated literally.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Wilt thou set thine eyes upon it? it is gone
Proverbs.english_translation: *Hata'if* — like “and thou hast doubled” and *ta'if*.
Proverbs.translator_note: The sentence is translated literally.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: For as one that hath reckoned within himself, so is he
Proverbs.english_translation: *Sha'ar* — this is pointed half *patach* and half *kamatz*, and its accent is below (on the last syllable); therefore it is a verb and not a noun, for if it were a noun it would be with *kamatz* and its accent above (on the first syllable), like every *sha'ar* (gate) in Scripture. And its explanation: as if this food had poured gall into the soul of the one with the evil eye, so it is. *Sha'ar* is from the language of “the vile figs (*hashe'arim*), the bitter ones” (Jeremiah 29:17).
Proverbs.translator_note: The grammatical remarks are translated literally. Printed “Jeremiah 29:29” is Jeremiah 29:17.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The morsel which thou hast eaten
Proverbs.english_translation: That you ate in his house — in the end you will vomit it because of the shame.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And lose thy sweet words
Proverbs.english_translation: The favour (*chanut*) that you secured and the gentle words you spoke to him — you have lost it all.
Proverbs.translator_note: The printed word חנות (“favour,” or “shop”) is translated as “favour.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And enter not into the fields of the fatherless
Proverbs.english_translation: In the gleanings, the forgotten sheaf and the corner that are due to them.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: When thy lips speak right things
Proverbs.english_translation: Because your heart is wise.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Let not thy heart envy sinners
Proverbs.english_translation: At their success, to be wicked like them.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: For surely there is a future
Proverbs.english_translation: *Im* here is used in the sense of *asher* (“that”), that is, “because of this there is a future, a hope for you.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Hear thou, my son, and be wise, And guide thy heart in the way
Proverbs.english_translation: Since you will become wise, you will be able to walk in the ways of your heart, for a wise heart will not lead you into transgression.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the drunkard and the glutton shall come to poverty
Proverbs.english_translation: He will become poor.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: drowsiness shall clothe a man with rags
Proverbs.english_translation: Laziness and drowsiness will clothe you in torn garments.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Buy the truth, and sell it not
Proverbs.english_translation: And if you do not find one to learn from for free, learn for payment, and do not say, “As I learned for payment, so I shall teach for payment.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: an alien woman is a narrow pit
Proverbs.english_translation: *Eshtreina* in French.
Proverbs.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: She also lieth in wait as a robber
Proverbs.english_translation: Suddenly.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: increaseth the faithless among men
Proverbs.english_translation: She multiplies in Israel those faithless to HaShem; and he is speaking of the heretics (*apikorsin*).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Who crieth: ‘Woe’? who: ‘Alas’?
Proverbs.english_translation: An expression of crying out and wailing.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Who hath contentions? who hath raving?
Proverbs.english_translation: One who has quarrels with people and excessive talk — woe and alas to him, for in many words there is much transgression.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Who hath redness of eyes?
Proverbs.english_translation: From much wine his eyes grow red, and it is a disgrace.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: mixed wine
Proverbs.english_translation: *Mimsach* — mixed (*mimzag*), and it is a noun, like *mimkar* (sale).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: They that go to try mixed wine
Proverbs.english_translation: Who search and examine where good wine is sold.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Look not thou upon the wine when it is red
Proverbs.english_translation: Do not set your eyes upon me.
Proverbs.translator_note: The printed word בי (“upon me”) is translated as printed; the sense may be “upon it” (בו).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: When it glideth down smoothly
Proverbs.english_translation: One who is prone to drunkenness — all transgressions seem to him like a plain; all the ways are straight in his eyes.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: When it giveth its colour in the cup
Proverbs.english_translation: *Bakis* (“in the purse”) is written; that is, the drinker gives an eye to the cup, and the shopkeeper to his purse.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: At the last it biteth like a serpent
Proverbs.english_translation: *Yifrash* — an expression of stinging, *poignant* in French. In the passage of the ox-goad (*malmad habakar*) the Targum renders *bifrash tori*, and in the Gemara, “who holds a goad (*parsha*)” — *aguillon* in French. And some interpret: it separates him (*mafrisho*) from life.
Proverbs.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Proverbs 23:32 (“Il pique”), in forms such as פוניינט, פויינט; the printed form (פויינ"ט) matches. He also lists “Avec l’aiguillon” there, in forms such as אגולון, אגוליין; the printed form (אגוילו"ן) is a variant spelling.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Thine eyes shall behold strange things
Proverbs.english_translation: When you are drunk, the wine burns in you and leads you to look at harlots.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Yea, thou shalt be
Proverbs.english_translation: Mad.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Or as he that lieth upon the top of a mast
Proverbs.english_translation: The mast of the ship, from which it is easy to fall.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: ‘They have struck me, and I felt it not
Proverbs.english_translation: When he wakes from his wine, he does not feel any of the evils that have passed over him, and he returns to drink.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A wise man is strong
Proverbs.english_translation: A wise man is always in strength.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Wisdom is as unattainable to a fool as corals
Proverbs.english_translation: A kind of precious stone that is not common, as it is said, “coral and crystal” (Job 28:18) — that is, all wisdom seems to the fool like a precious stone or pearls to buy; he says, “How shall I occupy myself in Torah? When will it come into my hand?” But the wise man learns a little today and a little tomorrow.
Proverbs.translator_note: Rashi’s wording differs from JPS Job 28:18, “coral or of crystal.” Printed “Job 28” is Job 28:18.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He that deviseth to do evil
Proverbs.english_translation: He plows the schemes of wickedness.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Men shall call him a mischievous person
Proverbs.english_translation: He causes himself evil, for people call him a schemer — counsel of the wicked.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The thought of foolishness is sin
Proverbs.english_translation: The counsel of folly is a sin to its owner.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the scorner is an abomination to men
Proverbs.english_translation: Scoffing is what makes a man abominable before the Holy One, blessed be He, and before people.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: If thou faint in the day of adversity
Proverbs.english_translation: From Torah.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Thy strength is small indeed
Proverbs.english_translation: The ministering angels will not strengthen your power — this is the midrash of the Sages; and according to its plain sense: you slackened on the day of your beloved’s distress, standing aloof.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Thy strength is small indeed
Proverbs.english_translation: On the day of your punishment, as it is written, “For if thou altogether holdest thy peace…” (Esther 4:14).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Deliver them that are drawn unto death
Proverbs.english_translation: To rescue those taken to death, those tottering toward slaughter.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: wilt thou forbear to rescue?
Proverbs.english_translation: From rescuing them; regarding this I said, “Your strength is small.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: If thou sayest
Proverbs.english_translation: Perhaps you will say; and this is *ki* used in the sense of *dilma* (“perhaps”).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: My son, eat thou honey, for it is good
Proverbs.english_translation: That is: it is the way of people to eat honey because it is good; so too, know wisdom for your soul. And just as you pursue eating honey, so should you pursue knowing wisdom.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: If thou hast found it
Proverbs.english_translation: It — then there is a future.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Fret not thyself because of evildoers
Proverbs.english_translation: *Al tit'char* — to be like them, like “how canst thou contend with horses?” (Jeremiah 12:5), and “because thou strivest to excel in cedar” (Jeremiah 22:15).
Proverbs.translator_note: Rashi quotes only the key words; the fuller JPS wording is given. Printed “ibid. 22” is Jeremiah 22:15.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: My son, fear thou the LORD and the king
Proverbs.english_translation: Fear the king, provided that he does not remove you from the fear of HaShem; and the fear of HaShem always comes first.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: meddle not with them that are given to change
Proverbs.english_translation: Those who say there are two powers (*reshuyot*).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: who knoweth the ruin from them both?
Proverbs.english_translation: The destruction of ע"ג and the destruction of Obadiah.
Proverbs.translator_note: The abbreviation ע"ג is left as printed and not resolved here.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: These also are sayings of the wise
Proverbs.english_translation: All the words in the subject below are said to the wise who sit in judgment, that they not show partiality in judgment, for it is not good.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He kisseth the lips
Proverbs.english_translation: All lips deserve to kiss him.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Prepare thy work without
Proverbs.english_translation: This is Scripture (*Mikra*).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: make it fit for thyself in the field
Proverbs.english_translation: This is Mishnah.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And afterwards build thy house
Proverbs.english_translation: This is Gemara. Another explanation, as it sounds: first take for yourself fields and vineyards, and afterwards — *ve-atdah* is an expression of *atudim* (he-goats) (Genesis 31:10) — put for yourself livestock in the field, and afterwards “build thy house”: take a wife.
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 31:32”; the word *atudim* occurs at Genesis 31:10.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: deceive not with thy lips
Proverbs.english_translation: You will deceive your neighbour with your speech.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: I went by the field of the slothful
Proverbs.english_translation: One who does not review his study of Talmud.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: thistles
Proverbs.english_translation: *Kimshonim* — thorns (*chochim*).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: covered
Proverbs.english_translation: *Kasu* — *niksu*.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: nettles
Proverbs.english_translation: *Charulim* — larger than *kimshonim*, and they are sharp like thorns.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the stone wall thereof was broken down
Proverbs.english_translation: So one who does not review his study: at first he forgets the chapter headings, and in the end he mixes up the words of the Sages from this to that, saying of the pure “impure” and of the impure “pure,” and he destroys the world.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: So shall thy poverty come as a runner
Proverbs.english_translation: The things you are poor of will come to you swiftly.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: These also are proverbs of Solomon, which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out
Proverbs.english_translation: He returned to expound them when Hezekiah was appointed king, and he seated disciples in every city, as we say in the chapter *Chelek*: they searched from Dan to Beersheba and found no ignorant man.
Proverbs.translator_note: The printed word לדורש' is read as “to expound them.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: copied out
Proverbs.english_translation: They strengthened.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: It is the glory of God to conceal a thing
Proverbs.english_translation: For example the Account of the Chariot (*Ma'aseh Merkavah*) and the Account of Creation (*Ma'aseh Bereshit*).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: but the glory of kings is to search out a matter
Proverbs.english_translation: When you expound regarding the honour of kings — or the honour of the Sages, who made fences for the Torah, and the decrees that they decreed — you should investigate and expound and ask the reason for the matter; but when you expound regarding the Account of the Chariot and the Account of Creation and the statutes written in the Torah, such as statutes and matters about which Satan accuses and replies — eating pork, mixed seeds in a vineyard, and *sha'atnez* — you should not investigate, only conceal, and say, “It is a decree of the King.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the heart of kings is unsearchable
Proverbs.english_translation: The height of heaven and the depth of the earth and the heart of kings are unsearchable — for how many cases come before them and how many wars, and they must give heed to all of them; and if all tongues were to speak and all hands to write, they could not write the void of the domain.
Proverbs.translator_note: The last phrase (חללה של רשות) is translated literally.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Take away the dross from the silver
Proverbs.english_translation: *Hago* — draw out, like “when he was removed out of the highway” (2 Samuel 20:13). Just as a silver vessel does not go out to the refiner’s work until they remove from it the dross of copper that is in it, so a congregation is not freed from punishment until the wicked are removed from among them and judgment is carried out upon them.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Glorify not thyself in the presence of the king
Proverbs.english_translation: To show your honour and to be proud before a king, or to stand before one greater than you; for it is better that they say to you “Come up here” than that you come without his permission and they say to you “Go out.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: whom thine eyes have seen
Proverbs.english_translation: That this matter is true.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: lest thou know not what to do in the end thereof
Proverbs.english_translation: Lest you come into a state in which you do not know what to do at its end.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Debate thy cause with thy neighbour
Proverbs.english_translation: And if you must quarrel and rebuke your neighbour, nevertheless “reveal not the secret of another”: do not mention to him the faults of his fathers who have died, which not everyone knows, and you reveal it.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Lest he that heareth it revile thee
Proverbs.english_translation: “The reproach of Egypt” (Joshua 5:9) we translate *chasuda de-mitzraei*; “lest he revile thee” — the hearer, and call you a spreader of slander.
Proverbs.translator_note: The Aramaic is translated as printed. Printed “Joshua 5” is Joshua 5:9.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: apples of gold
Proverbs.english_translation: Like knobs engraved upon settings of silver. *Maskiyot* — vessels overlaid with silver, like “and will cover thee with My hand” (Exodus 33:22).
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed “Exodus 33” is Exodus 33:22.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A word fitly spoken
Proverbs.english_translation: *Al ofanav* — on its base and its likeness; “I have borne Thy terrors, I am distracted (*afunah*)” (Psalms 88:16) — established and settled within me. This is not from the root of *ofan* and *galgal* (Isaiah 28:28), for if it were so, the *pe* would be pointed with a *patach*, like *ha'ofanim*, and a *chataf-kamatz* vowel would not fall in it.
Proverbs.translator_note: The grammatical remarks are translated literally. Rashi reads *afunah* as “established”; JPS Psalms 88:16 renders it “I am distracted.” Printed “Psalms 88” and “Isaiah 28” are Psalms 88:16 and Isaiah 28:28.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: As an ear-ring of gold, and an ornament of fine gold
Proverbs.english_translation: *Nezem zahav vechali ketem* — ornaments of a collection of gold, like “and decked herself with her ear-rings and her jewels” (Hosea 2:15), like *chala'im* (Song of Songs 7:2).
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed “Hosea 2” and “Song 7” are Hosea 2:15 and Song of Songs 7:2.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: an ornament of fine gold
Proverbs.english_translation: *Ketem* — an expression of a golden ornament, and so “most fine gold” (Song of Songs 5:11).
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed “ibid. 5” is Song of Songs 5:11.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: As the cold of snow in the time of harvest
Proverbs.english_translation: Like the cold of snowy days, which a man desires in the days of harvest — not actual snow, for snow is not good at the time of harvest.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: As vapours and wind without rain
Proverbs.english_translation: When there is vain hope — when the heavens are bound up in clouds and the wind blows and a man expects that rain will come and it does not, and they suffer and their eyes fail — so a man who boasts, saying, “So and so much charity I shall give to the hand of the collector,” and he lies, and the eyes of the poor fail for his gift and it does not come.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: By long forbearing is a ruler persuaded
Proverbs.english_translation: While the Holy One, blessed be He, is long-suffering and does not exact payment, the sinners should set their hearts to persuade Him with repentance and prayer.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: a soft tongue
Proverbs.english_translation: With prayer and supplications.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: breaketh the bone
Proverbs.english_translation: The bone of the severity of the decree.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Hast thou found honey? eat so much as is sufficient for thee
Proverbs.english_translation: [The source prints the lemma only, with no comment.]

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Let thy foot be seldom in thy neighbour’s house
Proverbs.english_translation: Just as, if you found honey and it is sweet to your palate, you must refrain from eating of it, lest you be sated by it and vomit it, so make your foot rare in your neighbour’s house — although he draws you near, refrain from coming there day after day, lest he be sated with you and hate you. And regarding its midrash: do not be accustomed to sin inadvertently and to bring always sin-offerings and guilt-offerings to the House of HaShem, who is called a friend (*re'a*) of Israel, as it is written, “This is my beloved, and this is my friend.”
Proverbs.translator_note: The last quotation is Song of Songs 5:16; the source gives no reference.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: As a maul, and a sword
Proverbs.english_translation: *Mefitz* — the name of a weapon of war.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: a broken tooth
Proverbs.english_translation: Shattered.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: a foot out of joint
Proverbs.english_translation: *Mo'edet* — like “and my ankles did not slip (*ma'adu*)” (Psalms 18:37).
Proverbs.translator_note: Rashi’s wording differs from JPS Psalms 18:37, “And my feet have not slipped.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Confidence in an unfaithful man in time of trouble
Proverbs.english_translation: One who deceives him on the very day of his trouble, like a shattered and slipping tooth.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: As one that taketh off a garment in cold weather
Proverbs.english_translation: *Ma'deh beged* — “a garment of *adim*” is a garment that is removed, a garment that is fit to be taken off because it is worn out, as we translate “and he removed” as *ve'adei*; and this is its explanation: a worn-out garment on a cold day is like vinegar upon *neter*. *Neter* — a kind of soft earth, like our earth that is called *creide* (chalk); they used to hollow it out and make vessels, and if vinegar falls on it, it dissolves it and it is spoiled. “So is he that singeth songs to a heart that is evil” resembles both. And what is the song? This is one who teaches Torah to a wicked student who has no heart to fulfil it.
Proverbs.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Proverbs 25:20 (“Sorte de craie”), in forms such as קרידא, קריידא; the printed form (קריד"א) matches.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat
Proverbs.english_translation: As it sounds; and our Rabbis explained it of the evil inclination: if he is hungry and tells you to satisfy him with transgressions, drag yourself to the house of study and feed him with the bread of Torah, and likewise give him water to drink — of the waters of Torah.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: For thou wilt heap coals of fire upon his head
Proverbs.english_translation: They are for him, for you take and draw from the fire-pit to put on his head.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: heap
Proverbs.english_translation: *Chotah* — all drawing of coals from the hearth is called *chotah*, as it says, “to take fire from the hearth” (Isaiah 30:14).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the LORD will reward thee
Proverbs.english_translation: He will make him peaceful with you, so that he does not overcome you.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The north wind bringeth forth rain
Proverbs.english_translation: It gives birth to and creates the rain.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: an angry countenance
Proverbs.english_translation: *Techolel* — a backbiting tongue; slander (*lashon hara*) causes the face of the Holy One, blessed be He, to be angry. And so is the likeness of the explanation of the verse: the north wind is made to bring forth rain, and a backbiting tongue is made for angry faces.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: It is better to dwell in a corner of the housetop
Proverbs.english_translation: It was said concerning the departure of the Divine Presence.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: a contentious woman
Proverbs.english_translation: The Congregation of Israel, for they made their deeds wicked and provoked the Holy One, blessed be He.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: in a house in common with
Proverbs.english_translation: A house in which they joined idols to the Divine Presence.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: As cold waters to a faint soul
Proverbs.english_translation: It is made to restore a faint soul.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: So is good news from a far country
Proverbs.english_translation: This too is the same, and so with Jacob: “the spirit of Jacob their father revived” (Genesis 45:27).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: As a troubled fountain
Proverbs.english_translation: Muddied by feet.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: a righteous man that giveth way before the wicked
Proverbs.english_translation: When the righteous man gives way before the wicked and fears to rebuke him to his face concerning his way, the matter is hateful, like a muddied fountain and a spoiled spring.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: It is not good to eat much honey
Proverbs.english_translation: To eat honey more than enough — a hint to one who expounds the Account of the Chariot and the Account of Creation to reveal it to the many; and the ignorant mock the matters and ask, “What is above? What is below?”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: So for men to search out their own glory is not glory
Proverbs.english_translation: And where should investigation be proper? In the words of the Sages, whose honour is honour: regarding their decrees one may ask what is the reason they decreed so, and why they made a fence in each and every decree.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: As snow in summer
Proverbs.english_translation: At the time when they spread figs in the sun to dry them and make dried fig-cakes (*ketziyot*), as it says, “the bread and summer fruit for the young men to eat” (2 Samuel 16:2).
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed “2 Samuel 15” is 2 Samuel 16:2.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: As the wandering sparrow
Proverbs.english_translation: That wanders; and like a swallow that returns to its nest.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: So the curse that is causeless shall come home
Proverbs.english_translation: [Shall come] to the one who uttered it with his mouth.
Proverbs.translator_note: Rashi reads the word *lo* as “to him”; JPS renders “shall come home.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the flying swallow
Proverbs.english_translation: It is a bird called *rondele* in French, and it is called *dror* because it dwells (*dara*) in a house as in a field.
Proverbs.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Proverbs 26:2 (“Hirondelle”), in forms such as ארונדיילא, ארונדילא; the printed form (רונדל"ע) differs slightly.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A whip for the horse
Proverbs.english_translation: It is made for it; and so “a rod for the back of fools” — afflictions are prepared for the wicked.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Answer not a fool according to his folly
Proverbs.english_translation: In words of quarrel and strife, lest you become like him.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Answer a fool according to his folly
Proverbs.english_translation: One who comes to entice you to idolatry — make known to him his folly.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Lest he be wise in his own eyes
Proverbs.english_translation: And the reason for these two verses is explained within them: do not answer in a matter in which you would become like him; if you answer him, answer the fool in a matter in which, if you do not answer him, he will be wise in his own eyes.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Cutteth off his own feet, and drinketh damage
Proverbs.english_translation: One who sends words by the hand of a fool cuts off the feet of many messengers, to return and send to correct what the first one, whom they sent at first, distorted; and he drinks violence, for his fellow is angry with him over the fool’s mission.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The legs hang limp from the lame
Proverbs.english_translation: *Dalyu* — are high, like “my eyes are raised (*dalu*) on high” (Isaiah 38:14); the legs of every man seem higher than himself to a lame man. And this is a parable in the mouth of the fool, who says it about learning wisdom: “How shall we come to learn wisdom? It is wonderful and higher than we.” The parable says: “The legs hang limp from the lame.”
Proverbs.translator_note: JPS Isaiah 38:14 renders the same words “Mine eyes fail with looking upward.” Printed “Isaiah 38:14”.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: As a small stone in a heap of stones
Proverbs.english_translation: *Be-margemah* — *fronde* in French. For a stone that is bound in it is not to remain; it is a place made for throwing; so one who gives honour to a fool — it is not lasting. And our Rabbis of blessed memory expounded it of one who teaches Torah to an unworthy student, that he is like one who throws a stone at Mercury (*Markolis*).
Proverbs.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Proverbs 26:8 (“Fronde”), in forms such as פרונדיילא, פרונדליא; the printed form (פרונדול"א) is a variant spelling.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: As a thorn that cometh into the hand of a drunkard
Proverbs.english_translation: Like a thorn that sticks in the hand of a drunkard, so the parable stated below sticks in the mouth of the fool, to be for them a thorn and a painful prick; and what is the parable?

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A master performeth all things
Proverbs.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He, created everything and judges everything, fool as wise; we do not need any wisdom.
Proverbs.translator_note: The sentence is translated literally.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: he that stoppeth a fool is as one that stoppeth a flood
Proverbs.english_translation: Not like flesh and blood, who hires only skilled workers and hires only those engaged in his work; but the Holy One, blessed be He, “performs all” and hires (*socher*) fools, and hires passersby, idle from any work. And an Aggadic midrash: “and shutteth (*socher*) the fool” — from the language of “and the fountains of the deep were stopped” (Genesis 8:2) and the language of “they that make dams” (Isaiah 19:10): the Holy One, blessed be He, shuts the constellation Kesil, which serves in the summer days, from Tishrei onwards, and from then He shuts and closes all who cross the sea from going on it until Passover. And in the words of Rabbi Moses I saw: “A master performeth all things” — a rich man has many works, and if he hires a fool in his work, he is like one who hires all passersby who see the spoilage of the work, to show how it is proper and how it has to be done; and it is an empty thing and does not belong here.
Proverbs.translator_note: Rashi’s wording of Genesis 8:2 differs slightly from JPS (“were stopped”). The identity of “Rabbi Moses” is not given in the source.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: in the dish
Proverbs.english_translation: He puts his hand into a hot cauldron because of the cold.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: that give wise answer
Proverbs.english_translation: Wise men.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Is like one that taketh a dog by the ears
Proverbs.english_translation: One who passes by and gets involved in a quarrel not his own is like one who grasps a dog by the ears, causing it to bite him for nothing.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: As a madman who casteth firebrands
Proverbs.english_translation: Like one who toils to shoot *zikim* of fire, like “and with firebrands you have kindled” (Isaiah 50:11), from the language of *zikukin di-nur* (sparks of fire). Another explanation: *zikim* — *pronzolash* in French, from the language of “sling-stones” (Zechariah 9:15); and so in the Gemara, “*zikta* has cut for us.”
Proverbs.translator_note: The Aramaic is translated as printed and the last phrase is unclear. Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Proverbs 26:18 (“Fronde”), in forms such as פרינדלש, פרונדלוש; the printed form (פרונזולא"ש) differs slightly. Printed “Isaiah 50” and “Zechariah 9” are Isaiah 50:11 and Zechariah 9:15; JPS Isaiah 50:11 reads “That gird yourselves with firebrands.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: So is the man that deceiveth his neighbour
Proverbs.english_translation: He entices and incites his fellow from the ways of life to the ways of death, and when his fellow senses that he is misleading him, he says, “I am only joking.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Where no wood is, the fire goeth out
Proverbs.english_translation: That is, these two things are equal: just as without wood the fire goes out, so without a whisperer of slander who stirs up the quarrelers, strife will fall silent.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: As coals are to burning coals, and wood to fire
Proverbs.english_translation: Charcoal is made to kindle smoldering embers, and wood is made to kindle fire; and a man of strife — to inflame quarrel.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The words of a whisperer are as dainty morsels
Proverbs.english_translation: *Kemitlahamim* — an expression of *mitlachamim* (fighting). And our Rabbis explained *kemitlahamim* as *kemet lahem* (“as death for them”): the words of the spies were death for them.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the innermost parts of the body
Proverbs.english_translation: It is death by dropsy.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Are like an earthen vessel overlaid with silver dross
Proverbs.english_translation: Like silver dross that is stuck onto the earthenware in which they refine it, and it shines as if it were silver and has no use; so burning lips and an evil heart — those who pursue people to entice them with smooth words, and speak one thing with the mouth and another in the heart.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: a wicked heart
Proverbs.english_translation: They appear as friends and they are enemies.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Burning lips
Proverbs.english_translation: *Dolekim* — like “that thou hast hotly pursued after me” (Genesis 31:36).
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 31” is Genesis 31:36.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He that hateth dissembleth with his lips
Proverbs.english_translation: *Yinaker sone* — in his speech the hater disguises himself so that they do not recognize that he is a hater; *desconoistre* in French.
Proverbs.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters (דישקנוייש"ט) and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Though his hatred be concealed with deceit
Proverbs.english_translation: One who does his deeds in darkness and covers with *mashon* — that is darkness (another version: *sho'at choshekh*) — the thing hated by the Holy One, blessed be He: in the end the Holy One, blessed be He, reveals his wickedness in the congregation, so that they recognize in him that he is wicked.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein
Proverbs.english_translation: Like Balaam, who gave counsel to Balak against Israel and caused twenty-four thousand of them to fall, and came to Midian to claim his reward and was killed by the hand of Israel.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: he that rolleth a stone
Proverbs.english_translation: That is: the end of one who sets up a stumbling block is that he will stumble on it.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: he that rolleth a stone
Proverbs.english_translation: He rolls it from place to place so that people stumble over it. And an Aggadah explains it of Abimelech, who killed seventy of his brothers upon one stone and in the end died by a stone, as it is said, “And a certain woman cast an upper millstone… and broke his skull” (Judges 9:53).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A lying tongue hateth those that are crushed by it
Proverbs.english_translation: One who accepts slander hates those crushed beneath him; for through slander Saul pursued David and killed Nob.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: a flattering mouth
Proverbs.english_translation: A mouth of smooth speech.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: worketh ruin
Proverbs.english_translation: It causes rejection, for it pushes the one who accepts it away from the Holy One, blessed be He.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Boast not thyself of to-morrow
Proverbs.english_translation: Do not pride yourself now on a thing that is to be tomorrow.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: thou knowest not what a day may bring forth
Proverbs.english_translation: Perhaps today will give birth to some evil that will cancel tomorrow’s plans.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the sand weighty
Proverbs.english_translation: *Venetel* — a burden.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: a fool’s vexation
Proverbs.english_translation: For the fool angers the Holy One, blessed be He, and causes wrath to come into the world.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: who is able to stand before jealousy?
Proverbs.english_translation: Before the jealousy of the One who is jealous and avenges.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: are importunate
Proverbs.english_translation: *Ne'taarot* — an expression of greatness, like “and have multiplied your words against Me” (Ezekiel 35:13).
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed “Ezekiel 35” is Ezekiel 35:13.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: loatheth a honeycomb
Proverbs.english_translation: *Tavus* — it tramples with the foot, like “he will tread down our adversaries” (Psalms 44:6).
Proverbs.translator_note: Rashi’s wording differs from JPS Psalms 44:6, “Through Thy name do we tread them under that rise up against us.” Printed “Psalms 54” is Psalms 44:6.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: every bitter thing is sweet
Proverbs.english_translation: Every bitter thing is sweet to it. And one may explain it concerning Torah study: one who shows himself as sated, who does not desire the words of Torah — “the full soul tramples a honeycomb”; even reasons that settle upon the heart are not important to him; but one who desires it — even things that come to him with bitterness and toil are sweet to him.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: As a bird that wandereth from her nest
Proverbs.english_translation: That goes and wanders; so is the man who wanders from his place: a Torah scholar who wanders from study, from reviewing his learning.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Ointment and perfume rejoice the heart
Proverbs.english_translation: The fragrance of balsam oil and the fragrance of incense gladden the heart.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: So doth the sweetness of a man’s friend by hearty counsel
Proverbs.english_translation: One whose fellow draws him near and sweetens things for him with his words is better than what his own soul counsels him. Another explanation: “and the sweetness of his friend” — the one who makes his deeds fit, which are sweet to the Holy One, blessed be He, is better for him than that he fulfil the desire of his heart.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Thine own friend
Proverbs.english_translation: And your father’s friend is the Holy One, blessed be He, who is called a friend of Israel — “and your father’s friend,” who loved your fathers.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: forsake not
Proverbs.english_translation: If you forsake Him, punishment will come upon you.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Neither go into thy brother’s house
Proverbs.english_translation: Do not trust the sons of Esau and Ishmael to draw you near. We find that when Israel were exiled to Babylon, they would say to those leading them in the collar, “Please, lead us by the way of our brothers the sons of Esau and Ishmael,” and the sons of Ishmael would come out to meet them and greet them with kinds of salted foods and inflated skins.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Better is a neighbour that is near than a brother far off
Proverbs.english_translation: It is good that one near to those who call upon him dwell among you, rather than that you come to a brother who has become distant, saying, “Let the days of mourning for my father be at hand,” etc. (Genesis 27:41).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: My son, be wise
Proverbs.english_translation: Make yourself wise, my son.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: and make my heart glad
Proverbs.english_translation: And let my heart be glad in you.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A prudent man seeth the evil, and hideth himself
Proverbs.english_translation: He sees the punishment coming upon the land and hides from it, having drawn his hand back from sin; but the thoughtless do not hide, but pass on in an evil way.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: and are punished
Proverbs.english_translation: And are destroyed.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Take his garment that is surety for a stranger
Proverbs.english_translation: A man who becomes a surety — this causes the judge to say to the lender, “Take his garment.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He that blesseth his friend with a loud voice
Proverbs.english_translation: There is one who praises his fellow day after day, and the blessing turns into a curse, for they say of him that he is generous with his money and rich, and everyone comes and asks of him, and the government provokes him to collect money; so it is expounded in tractate *Arakhin*. And furthermore there is in *Midrash Rabbi Tanchuma*: against Balaam, who blessed Israel in a loud voice, as it is said, “And he took up his parable” (Numbers 23:7) — an expression of lifting the voice — and in the end he counselled to cause them to sin.
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed “Numbers 23” is Numbers 23:7.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A continual dropping
Proverbs.english_translation: Rain dripping from the roof into the house and disturbing the household.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: in a very rainy day
Proverbs.english_translation: A day of rain, when all are shut in their houses.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And a contentious woman are alike
Proverbs.english_translation: [A woman of] contentions: the two are equal, they are the same.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He that would hide her hideth the wind
Proverbs.english_translation: One who thinks to guard her from her harlotries is hiding the wind; just as it is impossible to hide the wind, so he will not hide her.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the ointment of his right hand betrayeth itself
Proverbs.english_translation: He is calling leprosy to come upon himself until he divorces her, like the leper who is purified with oil on the thumb of his right hand.
Proverbs.translator_note: Rashi reads *yikra* as “calls”; JPS renders “betrayeth itself.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: So a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend
Proverbs.english_translation: *Yachad* — together, Torah scholars sharpen one another in halakhah.
Proverbs.translator_note: Rashi reads *yachad* (“together”); JPS renders “sharpeneth.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: shall eat the fruit thereof
Proverbs.english_translation: And so he who guards his master shall be honoured, and shall eat the fruit of his deeds.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: As in water face answereth to face
Proverbs.english_translation: These faces that you show to the waters, they show back to you.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: So the heart of man to man
Proverbs.english_translation: His fellow — according to what a man knows that his fellow loves him, so he shows him a face.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The nether-world and Destruction are never satiated
Proverbs.english_translation: They will not be sated with receiving the wicked into them, just as the eyes of a wicked man are not sated with straying after the evil inclination to fulfil his desire.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The refining pot is for silver
Proverbs.english_translation: A vessel made to refine silver, and the furnace made to test gold; and a man is refined and reckoned according to those who praise him — because people praise him for his good deeds, he is tested before the many, whether good or evil.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: among groats
Proverbs.english_translation: Wheat pounded in a mortar.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: in a mortar
Proverbs.english_translation: *Asita* — *mortier* in French.
Proverbs.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: with a pestle
Proverbs.english_translation: *Ali* — it is a *buchna*, a pestle, פולין מורטר"ו in French; because they raise it (*ma'alin*) and strike with it continually, it is called *ali*.
Proverbs.translator_note: The Old French is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Be thou diligent to know the state of thy flocks
Proverbs.english_translation: Let it not be light in your eyes to attend to them always, to see what they need.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: For riches are not for ever
Proverbs.english_translation: For if you are rich in silver and gold, perhaps it will not endure for ever; therefore do not despise your small things.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: When the hay is mown
Proverbs.english_translation: When the hay is uncovered in the days of Nissan, and the grass appears, and herbs are gathered to sprout, then it will be good for you that the fleeces of the lambs be for your clothing.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the goats the price for a field
Proverbs.english_translation: The he-goats will be worth it to you, for you will eat the meat and sell the hides.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: there will be goats’ milk enough for thy food
Proverbs.english_translation: Your sustenance.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: for the food of thy household
Proverbs.english_translation: You will be satisfied with goats’ milk — that is its figure of speech; and the parable is thus: “the state of thy flocks” — the rabbi who is appointed over the congregation shall carry them in his bosom and lead them gently, “for riches are not for ever,” and in this he will eat the fruits while the principal remains.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And there will be goats’ milk enough for thy food
Proverbs.english_translation: [Lemma in the source: “When the hay is mown.”] When his reports spread and the Torah grows greater through him, then these lambs will be his clothing: the disciples will be for him a name and a garment of majesty and splendour.
Proverbs.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The wicked flee when no man pursueth
Proverbs.english_translation: The wicked fled when their calamity comes, and fall from a trivial thing with no pursuer.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the righteous are secure as a young lion
Proverbs.english_translation: Their heart is strong in the Holy One, blessed be He, like a young lion that trusts in its strength.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: For the transgression of a land many are the princes thereof
Proverbs.english_translation: For this is a calamity for the land, when its princes are many, who pursue only their own gain.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: But by a man of understanding and knowledge
Proverbs.english_translation: And on account of a man of understanding, the calamity will be delayed from coming.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A poor man
Proverbs.english_translation: An ignorant judge (*am ha'aretz*).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: that oppresseth the weak
Proverbs.english_translation: In judgment — because he is not deliberate in judgment, he is like a rain that sweeps away the field and produces no fruit.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: a sweeping rain
Proverbs.english_translation: *Socheph* — sweeping (flooding); and in the Mishnah, “his field was swept away”; and so “thy strong ones are swept away” (Jeremiah 46:15) — they were swept away and slipped and stumbled.
Proverbs.translator_note: Rashi’s wording differs from JPS Jeremiah 46:15, “Why is thy strong one overthrown?”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Evil men understand not justice
Proverbs.english_translation: They do not give heed to the future punishment, so as to contemplate it, return from their way, and be saved.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: they that seek the LORD understand all things
Proverbs.english_translation: Good and evil. *Mishpat* — *justice* in French; so Rabbi Tanchuma explained, concerning the generation of the Flood.
Proverbs.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters (יושטיצ"א) and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Better is the poor
Proverbs.english_translation: Even one who is poor in Torah.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: that walketh in his integrity
Proverbs.english_translation: In good deeds.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: he that is a companion of gluttonous men shameth his father
Proverbs.english_translation: *Vero'eh zolelim* — he joins gluttons to himself, and it is an expression of friends (*re'im*).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Gathereth it for him that is gracious to the poor
Proverbs.english_translation: [Increase] for one who is gracious to the poor: the authorities hear of him that he grows rich without justice, and they take his money and build bridges with it and repair roads with it, and this is graciousness to the poor. So Rabbi Tanchuma expounded.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: into his own pit
Proverbs.english_translation: *Bishchuto* — from the language of *shachat* (pit).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The rich man is wise in his own eyes
Proverbs.english_translation: He speaks of teacher and student: the student investigates, and through him the teacher becomes wise.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: men must be sought for
Proverbs.english_translation: *Yechupas adam* — he will disguise himself with all kinds of pretexts.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: whoso confesseth and forsaketh them
Proverbs.english_translation: He confesses his transgressions and forsakes them, so as not to return to them again.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Happy is the man that feareth alway
Proverbs.english_translation: He worries about punishment and thereby keeps far from sin.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: As a roaring lion
Proverbs.english_translation: *Ari noheim* — it is so to them.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: a ravenous bear
Proverbs.english_translation: *Nehimah* is for the lion and *shekikah* is for the bear; both are an expression of crying out.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The prince that lacketh understanding
Proverbs.english_translation: Because he lacks understanding he is great in oppressions, for he does not give heed to his life and multiplies oppression, whereas “he that hateth covetousness shall prolong his days.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A man that is laden with the blood of any person
Proverbs.english_translation: (Who has upon him the oppression of blood) — he is the one who causes his fellow to sin, and his soul is lost through him.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Shall hasten his steps unto the pit
Proverbs.english_translation: Until the day of his death he will flee for help, so that it be atoned for him.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: none will support him
Proverbs.english_translation: From Heaven, to supply in his hand the means to repent, so that he not be in the Garden of Eden while his disciple is in Gehinnom. So it is expounded in tractate *Yoma*.
Proverbs.translator_note: The sentence is translated as printed; the source has no explicit negation, though the verse says “none will support him.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: shall fall at once
Proverbs.english_translation: In one evil, and there is no rising from his fall.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: shall have poverty enough
Proverbs.english_translation: Poverty.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A faithful man
Proverbs.english_translation: One who gives his tithes faithfully, for there is no witness to the matter but the Holy One, blessed be He, who sees, and multiplies blessing for him.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: he that maketh haste to be rich
Proverbs.english_translation: He presses the hour to get rich with what belongs to the poor.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: a man will transgress for a piece of bread
Proverbs.english_translation: One who perverts justice.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: hasteneth after riches
Proverbs.english_translation: He hurries to multiply wealth and robs his heave-offerings and his tithes.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: want shall come upon him
Proverbs.english_translation: Lack will come to him, for a curse is sent into the work of his hands.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He that rebuketh a man
Proverbs.english_translation: About the transgressions in his hand, and he separates him from them.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: in the end find more favour
Proverbs.english_translation: After a time he will find favour in his eyes more than one who flatters with the tongue. We find in *Bereshit Rabbah*: wherever it says *acharei*, it means only separated, after, near. In *Tanchuma*, on “These are the words”: “He that rebuketh a man *acharai*” — this is Moses, who rebuked Israel after the Holy One, blessed be He; they are called “man,” as it is said, “are men” (Ezekiel 34:31), and it is said of him, “for thou hast found favour in My sight” (Exodus 33:17). “Than he that flattereth with the tongue” — this is Balaam, who said to Israel proper words, “How goodly are thy tents, O Jacob” (Numbers 24:5); Moses proclaims, “Take heed to yourselves, lest he entice,” and Balaam proclaims and flatters: “Do your desires,” and he is not particular. “God is not a man, that He should lie” (Numbers 23:19) — among the nations he says it, but to you he says “and will He not do it?” And Solomon cried out about both: “Faithful are the wounds of a friend, and the kisses of an enemy are importunate” (above, chapter 27).
Proverbs.translator_note: The passage on Balaam is translated literally. Rashi’s wording of Exodus 33:17 differs from JPS (“thou hast found grace in My sight”). Printed “Ezekiel 34”, “Exodus 33” and “Numbers 26” are Ezekiel 34:31, Exodus 33:17 and Numbers 24:5.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Whoso robbeth his father
Proverbs.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: or his mother
Proverbs.english_translation: The Congregation of Israel, who causes the many to sin, who robs the Holy One, blessed be He — separating His sons from Him and robbing them of good.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The same is the companion of a destroyer
Proverbs.english_translation: Jeroboam.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He that is of a greedy spirit
Proverbs.english_translation: To obtain all his desire.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: stirreth up strife
Proverbs.english_translation: He provokes against himself the attribute of justice.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He that giveth unto the poor
Proverbs.english_translation: Charity.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He that giveth unto the poor shall not lack
Proverbs.english_translation: (There is no lack — to increase charity for him, סא"א), and so the teacher who does not withhold Torah from the mouth of the student.
Proverbs.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under. it is left as printed.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: hardeneth his neck
Proverbs.english_translation: From hearing.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Shall suddenly be broken
Proverbs.english_translation: He will quickly be broken.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: he that keepeth company with harlots
Proverbs.english_translation: *Vero'eh* — he joins harlots to himself. And our Rabbis said: one who says, “This tradition is pleasant, I will study it; and this one is not pleasant, I will not study it.” And a support from Scripture: *zonot* is not written in full in Scripture except this one alone.
Proverbs.translator_note: The remark about the full spelling is translated literally.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The king by justice establisheth the land
Proverbs.english_translation: If he is a true judge, he will establish the land.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: he that exacteth gifts overthroweth it
Proverbs.english_translation: *Ish terumot* — a man of pride who does not care to be deliberate in judgment. And our Rabbis said: if the judge resembles one who has no need to acquire friends and take a bribe, he will establish the land; but if he resembles a priest who asks for heave-offerings at the threshing floors, he will destroy it.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: A man that flattereth his neighbour
Proverbs.english_translation: *Machalik* — speaks smooth words.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: In the transgression of an evil man there is a snare
Proverbs.english_translation: A snare will come.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the righteous doth sing and rejoice
Proverbs.english_translation: One who did not walk in his ways will sing and rejoice.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The righteous taketh knowledge of the cause of the poor
Proverbs.english_translation: The sufferings of the poor, and what they need, and he gives them heart.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Scornful men set a city in a blaze
Proverbs.english_translation: *Yafichu* — they kindle like a flame of fire blown by the wind.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: If a wise man contendeth with a foolish man
Proverbs.english_translation: *Nishpat* — he argues with the fool.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: there will be no rest
Proverbs.english_translation: Whether he shows him an angry face or whether he shows him a laughing face, there is no rest; in neither does he find contentment. We find regarding Amaziah that the Holy One, blessed be He, showed him a smiling face and delivered Edom into his hand, and on his return from smiting (2 Chronicles 25), “and he brought their gods and bowed down to them.” To Ahaz the Holy One, blessed be He, showed an angry face and delivered him into the hand of the kings of Aram, and “he sacrificed to the gods of Damascus, for he said: The gods of Aram help them.”
Proverbs.translator_note: Rashi’s wording differs from JPS 2 Chronicles 25:14 and 28:23. The second quotation has no reference in the source; it is 2 Chronicles 28:23. Printed “2 Chronicles 25”.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: they seek his life
Proverbs.english_translation: *Yevakshu nafsho* — an expression of affection; and it appears that this is so, like what David said to Abiathar: “for he that seeketh my life seeketh thy life” (1 Samuel 22:23), “he who will do me kindness will do you kindness”; but the interpreters do not agree with me.
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed “1 Samuel 22:23”.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: But a wise man stilleth it within him
Proverbs.english_translation: *Be'achor yeshabchenah* — when the fool lets out all his spirit, the wise man comes and humbles him with the answer of his tongue. And it resembles “Who stillest the roaring of the seas” (Psalms 65:8), “When the waves thereof arise, Thou stillest them” (Psalms 89:10).
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed “Psalms 65:8” and “ibid. 89”.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The poor man and the oppressor meet together
Proverbs.english_translation: *Ish tekhakhim* — a man of schemes who is a master of Torah. And our Rabbis (Temurah 16; Leviticus Rabbah, parashah 34) explained: a disciple who said to his teacher, “Teach me one chapter,” and he teaches him.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: a child left to himself causeth shame to his mother
Proverbs.english_translation: One whom his father sent off to walk in the ways of his heart — in the end he shames his mother. Ishmael, because he was wicked, caused Sarah to say to Abraham, “Cast out this bondwoman…” (Genesis 21:10).
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 21:10”.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Where there is no vision, the people cast off restraint
Proverbs.english_translation: When Israel cause prophecy to depart from them by mocking the prophets, breaches will break out among them and they go out to an evil upbringing.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: For though he understand, there will be no response
Proverbs.english_translation: Since he sees him rebuke him, he is silent, and he goes back and spoils; therefore one needs to discipline him with blows and punishments. And it does not speak of an actual servant, but of all who rebel against the words of the judges.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: a man that is hasty in his words
Proverbs.english_translation: Quick and hasty to answer.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: There is more hope for a fool than for him
Proverbs.english_translation: There is more hope for a fool than for him.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He that delicately bringeth up his servant from a child
Proverbs.english_translation: The evil inclination.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Shall have him become master at the last
Proverbs.english_translation: *Manon* — ruler, and so “before the sun shall his name be continued (*yinnon*)” (Psalms 72:17), and so every *nin* in Scripture, for the grandson (*nin*) rises in the place of his father to rule over his possessions.
Proverbs.translator_note: Rashi’s wording differs from JPS Psalms 72:17, “May his name be continued as long as the sun.” Printed “Psalms 72:17”.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: An angry man stirreth up strife
Proverbs.english_translation: As it sounds. *Madon* (strife) — the attribute of justice (*middat hadin*).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: shall attain to honour
Proverbs.english_translation: *Yitmokh kavod* — he will draw near to honour and always hold on to it.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: He heareth the adjuration and uttereth nothing
Proverbs.english_translation: For they adjure him: “If you saw so-and-so, who stole from me such and such,” and because he shares with him he does not tell.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The fear of man bringeth a snare
Proverbs.english_translation: It is transposed: a stumbling block of transgression will give a man trembling. Another explanation, as it sounds: because a man is narrow-eyed and trembles that if he gives charity he will need people, this trembling will give him a snare; and the first is more agreeable to me.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Many seek the ruler’s favour
Proverbs.english_translation: To be judged before him.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: a man’s judgment cometh from the LORD
Proverbs.english_translation: Whether he will be acquitted or found guilty; and Scripture speaks of rulers.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: he that is upright in the way
Proverbs.english_translation: A man who is upright in his ways.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The words of Agur the son of Jakeh
Proverbs.english_translation: The words of Solomon, who gathered (*agar*) understanding and vomited it out (*hekiah*); so the Sages explained it.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the burden
Proverbs.english_translation: He said this prophecy for this reason.
Proverbs.translator_note: The words על כן are translated as printed.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The man saith unto Ithiel
Proverbs.english_translation: The *gever* — this is Solomon — said this burden about himself, on account of Ithiel, because he relied on his wisdom to multiply gold and horses and wives, from which he was warned not to multiply; and so Ithiel said, “and I shall be able — I shall multiply wives and they will not turn my heart; I shall multiply gold and I will not stray; I shall multiply horses and I will not return the people to Egypt.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: unto Ithiel and Ucal
Proverbs.english_translation: Because he said *iti El* (“God is with me”), “and I shall be able” to do and not stumble. *Le-Ithiel* is “about Ithiel,” like “And Pharaoh will say of the children of Israel” (Exodus 14:3), meaning about the children of Israel.
Proverbs.translator_note: The quotation is Exodus 14:3; the source gives no reference.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Surely I am brutish
Proverbs.english_translation: Because I relied on my wisdom in a matter regarding which the Holy One, blessed be He, was concerned lest he come to transgression.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And I have not learned wisdom
Proverbs.english_translation: “And the knowledge of the holy ones I knew not,” for I diminished or added to the words of Moses.
Proverbs.translator_note: Rashi reads *kedoshim* as “holy ones”; JPS renders “the Holy One.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Who hath ascended up into heaven, and descended?
Proverbs.english_translation: Like Moses.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Who hath gathered the wind in his fists?
Proverbs.english_translation: The soot of the furnace.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Who hath bound the waters in his garment?
Proverbs.english_translation: “The deeps were congealed” (Exodus 15:8); “stood upright as a heap” (ibid.) — by the prayer of Moses.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Who hath established all the ends of the earth?
Proverbs.english_translation: The Tabernacle, for through its erection all the ends of the earth were established; so it is expounded in the *Pesikta*.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: What is his name, and what is his son’s name
Proverbs.english_translation: If you say that one like him already existed, say: what is the name of his son? What family came forth from him? And we shall know who he is.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: if thou knowest
Proverbs.english_translation: If you know who he is, how did you not fear to transgress his words?

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Every word of God is tried
Proverbs.english_translation: Refined; and He did not write a thing that was not needed, and I should have been careful.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Lest He reprove thee, and thou be found a liar
Proverbs.english_translation: He will reprove you to your face that through your addition you came to transgression, and all the more so if you diminish.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Two things have I asked of Thee
Proverbs.english_translation: Now he speaks before the Holy One, blessed be He.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Give me neither poverty
Proverbs.english_translation: *Rosh* — poverty.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: feed me with mine allotted bread
Proverbs.english_translation: *Hatrifeni* — an expression of food, and so “He hath given food (*teref*) unto them that fear Him” (Psalms 111:5).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Lest I be full, and deny
Proverbs.english_translation: Out of wealth, and I deny the Holy One, blessed be He, out of great pride; and what is the denial?

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: and say: ‘Who is the LORD?’
Proverbs.english_translation: That is: there is no God.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And profane the name of my God
Proverbs.english_translation: To accustom myself to swear by it falsely.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Slander not a servant unto his master
Proverbs.english_translation: Do not deliver a judgment against a man so as to cry out against him to the Holy One, blessed be He, even if he is wicked — “that curseth his father,” and all the abominations mentioned here refer to him. And proof of the matter from Hosea son of Beeri, as it is in tractate *Pesachim*, in the chapter *Ha-Isha*: he informed against Israel and said, “Exchange them for another nation”; the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him, “take unto thee a wife of harlotry” (Hosea 1:2).
Proverbs.translator_note: Printed “Hosea 1:2”.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: There is a generation, Oh how lofty are their eyes!
Proverbs.english_translation: This is arrogance (haughtiness of spirit).

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: There is a generation whose teeth are as swords
Proverbs.english_translation: The outer ones.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: their great teeth
Proverbs.english_translation: His inner teeth.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: as knives
Proverbs.english_translation: *Ma'achalot* — knives.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The horseleech hath two daughters
Proverbs.english_translation: Menachem interpreted *la'alukah* as it sounds. We have learned that it is Arabic; and the interpreters say that it is an expression of Sheol and descent (*mored*). And so in *Midrash Tehillim* we learned this, that it interprets the two daughters as the Garden of Eden and Gehinnom: this one says, “Give me the righteous,” and this one says, “Give me the wicked.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: Yea, four that say not: ‘Enough’
Proverbs.english_translation: “We have much.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: the barren womb
Proverbs.english_translation: Marital relations.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: despiseth to obey his mother
Proverbs.english_translation: *Likehat em* — to the wrinkles that are gathered and collected before his mother; an expression of “the gathering (*yikhat*) of peoples” (Genesis 49:10), the gathering of peoples; and the *yod* is a root letter, like *yifat* and *ya'alat chen*.
Proverbs.translator_note: Rashi reads *yikhat* as “gathering”; JPS Genesis 49:10 renders it “the obedience of the peoples.” Printed “Genesis 49”.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The ravens of the valley shall pick it out
