Proverbs.english_translation: *Yikruha* — an expression of “thou shalt hew out (*tinkor*),” “the cleft of the rock” (Exodus 33:22); *poirier* in French. May the raven come, which is cruel to its children, and pick it out and not eat it and not derive benefit from it; and may the eagle come, which is merciful to its children, and eat it and derive benefit from it. The raven is cruel, as it is said, “to the young ravens which cry” (Psalms 147:9), and the eagle is merciful, as it is said, “He beareth him on His pinion” (Deuteronomy 32:11).
Proverbs.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters (פוריי"ר) and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. Rashi’s wording of Deuteronomy 32:11 differs from JPS (“taketh them, Beareth them on her pinions”). Printed “Exodus 33:22”.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: There are three things which are too wonderful for me
Proverbs.english_translation: *Niflu mimeni* — they are hidden from me, since they passed from my eyes and I do not know where they went, for they hasten to be hidden from the eye.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: She eateth, and wipeth her mouth
Proverbs.english_translation: *Umachatah* — she turns her mouth downward, as it is written, “as a man wipeth a dish, wiping it and turning it upside down” (2 Kings 21:13).
Proverbs.translator_note: The quotation is 2 Kings 21:13; the source gives no reference.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: She eateth, and wipeth her mouth
Proverbs.english_translation: *Achelah* — Scripture speaks in a clean (euphemistic) language.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The spider
Proverbs.english_translation: *Aragne* in French.
Proverbs.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: thou canst take with the hands
Proverbs.english_translation: She holds with her hand and clings to the walls.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: stately in their march
Proverbs.english_translation: They go and succeed in their might.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: The greyhound; the he-goat also
Proverbs.english_translation: I do not know what it is, and as it appears, it is an animal weak in the loins.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And the king, against whom there is no rising up
Proverbs.english_translation: I do not know what it is, according to its plain sense. An Aggadic midrash explains these five sections of four things each as against the four kingdoms — because their dominion over Israel was strengthened by reason of the sin that they transgressed the five books of the Torah, He mentioned them five times.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And the king, against whom there is no rising up
Proverbs.english_translation: (16) “The grave and the barren womb.” Sheol is the kingdom of Babylon, as it is said of Nebuchadnezzar, “who enlargeth his desire as the nether-world” (Habakkuk 2:5); “and the barren womb” — this is Media, for in their days they restrained mercies from Israel, as it is said, “to destroy, to slay, and to cause to perish” (Esther 3:13).
Proverbs.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment, which is filed at Proverbs 30:31 with the aggadic extension on the sections of Proverbs 30; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of that verse. Printed “Habakkuk 2”.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And the king, against whom there is no rising up
Proverbs.english_translation: “The earth that is not satisfied with water” — this is Greece, which was not sated with decreeing evil decrees upon Israel.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And the king, against whom there is no rising up
Proverbs.english_translation: “And the fire that saith not: ‘Enough’” — against Esau, who acted with burning wrath against Israel, so that they said to destroy little ones and women in one day; and so —
Proverbs.translator_note: The comment ends with the word וכן as printed.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And the king, against whom there is no rising up
Proverbs.english_translation: (19) “The way of an eagle in the air” — this is Babylon: “the great eagle,” ארץ האבר.
Proverbs.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment, which is filed at Proverbs 30:31 with the aggadic extension on the sections of Proverbs 30; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of that verse. The printed ארץ האבר (“land of the pinion”) is left as printed; compare Ezekiel 17:3, “A great eagle with great wings And long pinions.”

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And the king, against whom there is no rising up
Proverbs.english_translation: “A serpent upon a rock” — this is Media.
Proverbs.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment, which is filed at Proverbs 30:31 with the aggadic extension on the sections of Proverbs 30; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of that verse.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And the king, against whom there is no rising up
Proverbs.english_translation: “The way of a ship in the midst of the sea” — this is Greece, which is light in its decrees.
Proverbs.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment, which is filed at Proverbs 30:31 with the aggadic extension on the sections of Proverbs 30; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of that verse.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And the king, against whom there is no rising up
Proverbs.english_translation: “The way of a man with a maid” — this is Persia, which said, “I shall be a mistress for ever”
Proverbs.translator_note: The comment ends without a final stop, as printed. The source gives no lemma for this comment, which is filed at Proverbs 30:31 with the aggadic extension on the sections of Proverbs 30; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of that verse. The quotation is identified here as Isaiah 47:7 (JPS: “For ever shall I be mistress”); the source gives no reference.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And the king, against whom there is no rising up
Proverbs.english_translation: (20) “So is the way of an adulterous woman” — this is the evil that caused them (the Congregation of Israel) to commit adultery with idol worship, and it is fitting for punishment to come upon her.
Proverbs.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment, which is filed at Proverbs 30:31 with the aggadic extension on the sections of Proverbs 30; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of that verse. The sentence is translated literally.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And the king, against whom there is no rising up
Proverbs.english_translation: “And saith: ‘I have done no wickedness’” — as it says, “Behold, I will enter into judgment with thee, because thou sayest: ‘I have not sinned’” (Jeremiah 2:35). Until here the language of Rashi that is in the מק"ג.
Proverbs.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment, which is filed at Proverbs 30:31 with the aggadic extension on the sections of Proverbs 30; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of that verse. The abbreviation מק"ג is left as printed and not resolved here. The closing parenthesis is printed without an opening one. The quotation is identified here as Jeremiah 2:35; the source gives no reference.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And the king, against whom there is no rising up
Proverbs.english_translation: (21) “For three things the earth is disquieted” — the Land of Israel.
Proverbs.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment, which is filed at Proverbs 30:31 with the aggadic extension on the sections of Proverbs 30; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of that verse.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And the king, against whom there is no rising up
Proverbs.english_translation: “For a servant when he reigneth” — this is Nebuchadnezzar, who was a servant to Merodach-baladan and wrote his letters, as we learn in tractate *Chullin*.
Proverbs.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment, which is filed at Proverbs 30:31 with the aggadic extension on the sections of Proverbs 30; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of that verse.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And the king, against whom there is no rising up
Proverbs.english_translation: “And a fool when he is filled with bread” — this is Ahasuerus, who made a feast of a hundred and eighty days.
Proverbs.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment, which is filed at Proverbs 30:31 with the aggadic extension on the sections of Proverbs 30; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of that verse.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And the king, against whom there is no rising up
Proverbs.english_translation: (23) “For a hated woman when she is married” — against Greece.
Proverbs.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment, which is filed at Proverbs 30:31 with the aggadic extension on the sections of Proverbs 30; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of that verse.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And the king, against whom there is no rising up
Proverbs.english_translation: “And a handmaid that is heir to her mistress” — this is Esau, who was to serve Jacob, and the matters were reversed.
Proverbs.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment, which is filed at Proverbs 30:31 with the aggadic extension on the sections of Proverbs 30; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of that verse.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And the king, against whom there is no rising up
Proverbs.english_translation: (25) “The ants are a people not strong” — this is Babylon, as it says, “Behold, the land of the Chaldeans — this is the people that was not” (Isaiah 23:13).
Proverbs.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment, which is filed at Proverbs 30:31 with the aggadic extension on the sections of Proverbs 30; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of that verse.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And the king, against whom there is no rising up
Proverbs.english_translation: “Yet they provide their food in the summer” — Nebuchadnezzar did honour to the Holy One, blessed be He, in the days of Merodach-baladan, who sent letters to Hezekiah and wrote there: “Peace to King Hezekiah; peace to the city of Jerusalem; peace to the great God.” And Nebuchadnezzar was the one who wrote his letters, and he was not there that day; and when he came and they told him what they had done, he said to them, “You called Him the great God, and you wrote to Him at the end?” In the end he ran after the messenger and brought him back; because of that running he merited the kingship. Thus he provided his bread in the summer, in the manner of the ant.
Proverbs.translator_note: The Aramaic is translated as printed. The source gives no lemma for this comment, which is filed at Proverbs 30:31 with the aggadic extension on the sections of Proverbs 30; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of that verse.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And the king, against whom there is no rising up
Proverbs.english_translation: (26) “The conies are but a feeble folk” — this is Media and Persia.
Proverbs.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment, which is filed at Proverbs 30:31 with the aggadic extension on the sections of Proverbs 30; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of that verse.

Proverbs.english_lemma_JPS: And the king, against whom there is no rising up

Job.english_lemma_JPS: There was a man in the land of Uz

Job.english_lemma_JPS: and that man was whole-hearted
Job.english_translation: “And that man was” — although this is a future form, such is the way of the Hebrew language and its figurative style; and “that man was greater than all the children of the east” — the people of the eastern land, for Aram is in the east of the world, as it is said, “From Aram Balak bringeth me, The king of Moab from the mountains of the East” (Numbers 23:7). Another explanation: Uz is Job; Buz is Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite; and behold Job said (below, chapter 31), “*uvuz mishpachot yechatteni*,” this one is of my family, *shemachatah* my words; and this is what people say: *minei uveih Abba lizil beih nargah*. Another explanation: “in the land of Uz” — in a land from which evil counsels (*etzot*) were taken against the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is said, “Out of that land went forth Asshur” (Genesis 10:11). And what counsel did they take? They said: It is not all up to Him to take the upper ones and give us the lower ones; rather, come to the land of Shinar, where there are many gods, as it is said of it, “It is a land of graven images” (Jeremiah 50:38), and let us build a tower whose top reaches heaven, and let us make us a name (Genesis 11:4). And the “name” stated here is nothing but idolatry, as it is said, “and make no mention of the name of other gods” (Exodus 23:13). What did the Holy One, blessed be He, do? He sat with them in judgment and set witnesses against them, as it is said, “And the LORD came down to see the city and the tower” (Genesis 11:5). Does the Omnipresent need to descend to see? Is it not written, “the eyes of the LORD range through all the earth” (Zechariah 4:10)? But it is to teach law for the generations, that one judges only on the testimony of eyewitnesses, as it is said, “whether he hath seen or known” (Leviticus 5:1).
Job.translator_note: The sentence “this one is of my family, *shemachatah* my words” and the Aramaic proverb that follows (*minei uveih Abba lizil beih nargah*) could not be resolved and are left as printed. Printed “below 31” is Job 31:34, where Rashi reads *buz* as a name (JPS: “the most contemptible among families”). Rashi’s phrasing of Genesis 11:4 combines phrases of the verse and differs from JPS; his wording of Zechariah 4:10 differs slightly from JPS. Printed references checked: Genesis 10:11, 11:4, 11:5, Jeremiah 50:38, Exodus 23:13, Zechariah 4:10–11, Leviticus 5:1. Audit 5 source check: a passage with the same wording (6 consecutive words) is found in Bereshit Rabbah 38.6 (Sefaria Hebrew text, labelled Public Domain). This is a wording match only; the translation was not changed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: the greatest of all the children of the east
Job.english_translation: From the generation of the Dispersion, as it is written, “And it came to pass, as they journeyed east” (Genesis 11:2). But from Abraham, it is not so; for of Abraham “the great” is written, as it is said, “and the name of Hebron beforetime was Kiriath-arba, the great man among the Anakim” (Joshua 14:15). He should have written “a great man,” so why did he write “the great man”? Rather, it hints that he is a great man who stood in ten trials; therefore it is written with two *hes*. But Job, of whom “great” is said, did not stand in more than one, as it is said, “whole-hearted and upright,” etc. — of all that generation, that was not seized by that sin (*sa"a*).
Job.translator_note: The ending (“of all that generation, that was not seized by that sin (סא"א)”) is translated literally; it is left as printed. Rashi’s wording of Joshua 14:15 differs from JPS (“which Arba was the greatest man among the Anakim”). Printed “Joshua 14:15”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: his sons used to go and hold a feast in the house of each one upon his day
Job.english_translation: In the house of each and every one, on his day.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: they would send and invite
Job.english_translation: Like “sending and calling,” for they always did so.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: when the days of their feasting were gone about
Job.english_translation: When the days of the feast were over, it was Job’s custom, at the end of every seven days, when the days of their rotation (*chalilah*) came round, to send and sanctify them — that is, to summon them — and he called them, like “Sanctify yourselves against to-morrow” (Numbers 11:18).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Numbers 11”, checked: 11:18.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: rose up early in the morning, and offered burnt-offerings
Job.english_translation: The figure of speech is that he used to rise early and offer burnt-offerings; therefore he wrote in the future form, that he was accustomed to do so always at the end of each seven days.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: according to the number of them all
Job.english_translation: The sons and the daughters.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: and blasphemed God in their hearts
Job.english_translation: “And they blessed (*uverechu*)” — a euphemistic expression regarding the One above.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Thus did Job continually
Job.english_translation: Like “he used to do,” tomorrow; when he wrote of a matter that is present and continual, sometimes he wrote it in the past form and sometimes in the future form.
Job.translator_note: The comment is elliptical and is translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Now it fell upon a day
Job.english_translation: That day was Rosh HaShanah (which is a day of blowing, and the Holy One, blessed be He, commanded Satan to bring the merits and the guilt of all creatures; this is “from going to and fro in the earth”).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: that the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD
Job.english_translation: To contend with Him; for “standing” is only for judgment, as it is said, “The LORD standeth up to plead” (Isaiah 3:13).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 3:13”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: and Satan came also among them
Job.english_translation: To accuse the creatures.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Whence comest thou
Job.english_translation: Scripture speaks in the way of the land: the great one speaks first and permits the small one to answer.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: From going to and fro in the earth
Job.english_translation: As explained above; and in the Aggadah it is of the partners (*hashutafin*).
Job.translator_note: The phrase “of the partners” could not be resolved and is translated as printed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: From going to and fro in the earth, and from walking up and down in it
Job.english_translation: So is my way: to go about and to see the wicked and the good; and I have gone about all the earth and have not found one like Abraham, of whom it is said, “Arise, walk through the land” (Genesis 13:17). And our Rabbis of blessed memory said: Satan intended it for the sake of Heaven, so that the merit of Abraham would not be forgotten before our God.
Job.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 13:17”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Hast thou considered My servant Job
Job.english_translation: That you wish to accuse him.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Hast thou considered
Job.english_translation: It is an expression of wonder.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: a whole-hearted and an upright man
Job.english_translation: Complete in his deeds.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Doth Job fear God for nought
Job.english_translation: As a question of wonder.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Hast not Thou made a hedge about him
Job.english_translation: You have made a hedge about him; for he knows that You are accustomed to do miracles for him, and he is fruitful and multiplies; therefore he does these righteous acts. But You have not tested him.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: made a hedge about him
Job.english_translation: “You have shielded about him” like this partition, like “I will remove its hedge” (Isaiah 5:5) — its partition. And every *be'ad* stated in Hebrew is only an expression of “opposite him” and “before him,” like “and shall make atonement for himself (*ba'ado*)” (Leviticus 16:6): wipe away the sin opposite you and before you, so that the atonement may be a shield for you; and so “But Thou, O LORD, art a shield about me (*ba'adi*)” (Psalms 3:4).
Job.translator_note: Rashi’s wording of Isaiah 5:5 differs from JPS (“I will take away the hedge thereof”). Printed references checked: Isaiah 5:5, Leviticus 16:6, Psalms 3:4.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: his possessions are increased in the land
Job.english_translation: They became strong, like “and so shall it spread” (Exodus 1), which we translate *yitkof*; this is the plain sense. But our Rabbis of blessed memory said in the Aggadah: he broke through the fence of the world, for the goats kill the wolves.
Job.translator_note: Printed “Exodus 1” is Exodus 1:12 (JPS: “the more they spread abroad”). The Targum rendering is as printed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: But put forth Thy hand now
Job.english_translation: Were You to touch all that is his — [see] whether he will not bless You to Your face; immediately, as a question; and then:
Job.translator_note: The sentence is elliptical (“Immediately, as a question, and then:”) and is translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And the LORD said unto Satan: ‘Behold, all that he hath is in thy power
Job.english_translation: (Another explanation: “Now it fell upon a day” — that day on which they had returned in rotation to eat in the house of their eldest brother.
Job.translator_note: The comment is on “Now it fell upon a day” (Job 1:13) but is printed after the lemma of 1:12. The parenthesis is not closed in the source.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: So Satan went forth from the presence of the LORD
Job.english_translation: “The sons of God” — the host of heaven who are near to the Shechinah, to be members of His household, and for that reason they are called His sons.
Job.translator_note: The source files this comment, which belongs to the opening scene (Job 1:6), under Job 1:12; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of 1:12.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: So Satan went forth from the presence of the LORD
Job.english_translation: “To present themselves before the LORD” — around Him, like “all them that stood by him” (Genesis 45:1).
Job.translator_note: The source files this comment, which belongs to the opening scene (Job 1:6), under Job 1:12; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of 1:12.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: the asses feeding beside them
Job.english_translation: *Al yedeihem* — like “every man by his hand” (Numbers 2:17); it is not an expression of place but because it is ready and prepared at his hand. And our Rabbis of blessed memory said in the Aggadah that the Holy One, blessed be He, let them taste something like the World to Come, for after the plowing of the she-asses they sowed along with the plowing, and the she-asses grazed; immediately a *chaziz* came up from the furrow.
Job.translator_note: The word *chaziz* could not be resolved and is left as printed. Rashi’s wording of Numbers 2:17 (“every man by his hand”) differs from JPS (“every man in his place, by their standards”). Printed “Numbers 2:17”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: and the Sabeans made a raid
Job.english_translation: It fell and encamped: the kingdom of Sheba fell upon them, like “over against all his brethren he did settle (*nafal*)” (Genesis 25:18).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 25:18”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: they have slain the servants with the edge of the sword
Job.english_translation: “And the servants” — your attendants who guard them.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: and I only am escaped alone to tell thee
Job.english_translation: *Emalta* — *melitah* is only an expression of escape, that he slipped away from the trouble. (“And I have come to tell thee” — and as soon as he told, he died at once. So it is in another version.)

Job.english_lemma_JPS: and the servants, and consumed them
Job.english_translation: “And among the servants” — Scripture speaks of the attendants, the keepers of the sheep.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: and fell upon the camels
Job.english_translation: This is an expression of plunder, “they took spoil.” According to their custom, all the time they are walking they cling together and go in ambush so that they will not be noticed, and drive off the livestock; and when they reach the place of the livestock they spread out over the expanse of the livestock, this one here and that one there, to gather the livestock. And these messengers were agents of Satan, and to provoke him and make him sin they first announced to him a small loss and afterward a greater one; and so all of them.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: from across the wilderness
Job.english_translation: From the other side of the wilderness; the house was on this side. And this is the meaning of *ever* in Scripture.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: and it fell upon the young people
Job.english_translation: The sons, but there is no need to mention the daughters.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: to tell thee
Job.english_translation: (To tell thee — for he had permission to tell, and he died at that moment, *sa"a*.)
Job.translator_note: The source gives no separate lemma; the comment begins with the words “to tell thee” (Job 1:19), used here as the lemma. it is left as printed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: and shaved his head
Job.english_translation: He plucked, like “Cut off thy hair” (Jeremiah 7:29), which we translate as plucking; and like “from my mother’s womb Thou art my plucker” (Psalms 71:6).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Jeremiah 6” is Jeremiah 7:29 (JPS: “Cut off thy hair, and cast it away”). Rashi reads Psalms 71:6 as “Thou art he that plucked me”; JPS has “Thou art he that took me out of my mother’s womb.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Naked came I out of my mother’s womb
Job.english_translation: The earth from which I was taken, or my actual mother.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And naked shall I return thither
Job.english_translation: He is not speaking of the womb. And “thither” — to the place of his return; and because he is prepared for this and will not change the law to return except to the dust, therefore he did not need to mention it.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: nor ascribed aught unseemly to God
Job.english_translation: He ascribed no taint or unseemliness to the Holy One, blessed be He, like “And I have seen unseemliness in the prophets of Samaria” (Jeremiah 23:13).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Jeremiah 23:13”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: nor ascribed aught unseemly to God
Job.english_translation: “Nor did he ascribe” — to cast unseemliness and a burden upon the Holy One, blessed be He, like “They have ascribed unto David ten thousands, and to me they have ascribed but thousands” (I Samuel 18:8).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: From whence comest thou
Job.english_translation: Where is the place of which you can say, “From there I come”?

Job.english_lemma_JPS: he still holdeth fast his integrity
Job.english_translation: *Machazik* — holding, like “and put forth his hand, and laid hold of it” (Exodus 4:4), “one that taketh a dog by the ears” (Proverbs 26:17).
Job.translator_note: Printed references checked: Exodus 4:4, Proverbs 26:17.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: although thou didst move Me against him, to destroy him without cause
Job.english_translation: “And thou didst incite Me against him” — to swallow him up. Every expression of *hasatah* is only an expression of drawing, for he draws a person to his counsel.
Job.translator_note: Rashi reads “to swallow him up” (*levolo*) where JPS has “to destroy him.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Skin for skin
Job.english_translation: A limb in front of a limb. So is the way of people: when one sees the sword coming upon his head, he shields with his arm in front of it; and all the more so “all that a man hath” of money he will give.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: for his life
Job.english_translation: In front of his life, to shield it; because this one knows in his soul that he is liable, therefore he is not pained over his money.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: But put forth Thy hand now
Job.english_translation: *Ulam* — but.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: surely he will blaspheme Thee to Thy face
Job.english_translation: “If not” — you will see in him at once that he will bless You to Your face.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: only spare his life
Job.english_translation: So that it not go out from here. The Sages said: Satan’s pain was harder than Job’s, like one who says to his fellow, “Break this barrel and keep its wine.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: to scrape himself therewith
Job.english_translation: It is written with a *dalet*, and it is an expression of the Mishnah: “he scrapes it and stands it on its scab.” But *goref* with a *resh* is only an expression of dragging, as in “a man drags a bed and a bench.”
Job.translator_note: The Mishnaic phrases are quoted without a source reference in the printed text.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Dost thou still hold fast thine integrity
Job.english_translation: Holding.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: blaspheme God, and die
Job.english_translation: An expression of command, like “and die in the mount” (Deuteronomy 32:50).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Deuteronomy 32” is 32:50.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil
Job.english_translation: “Also” — is it not enough that He created us, but also the good we shall receive and the evil we shall not receive? — as a question.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: did not Job sin with his lips
Job.english_translation: But in his heart he sinned.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Job’s three friends
Job.english_translation: His beloved ones.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: to bemoan him
Job.english_translation: *Linud* — like “Who shall bemoan (*yanud*) thee?” (Isaiah 51:19), “ye shall not bemoan (*tanudu*) him” (Jeremiah 15:5).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 51:19” and “Jeremiah 15:5”. The words “who shall bemoan thee” are at Jeremiah 15:5 and Isaiah 51:19; the form *lo tanudu lo* printed here resembles Jeremiah 22:10 (“neither bemoan him”), which is not the verse the source cites.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: and knew him not
Job.english_translation: For his face was changed because of the sufferings.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: and threw dust upon their heads toward heaven
Job.english_translation: *Hashamaimah* — that is, upward, above their heads (much); and it was a mourning custom of theirs.
Job.translator_note: The word in parentheses (“much”) is a later printed insertion.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: So they sat down with him upon the ground
Job.english_translation: On the ground, to be pained in his pain.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And Job spoke, and said
Job.english_translation: (Heading: “Job’s reply.”) “And he answered” — he cried out; for every *ineyah* stated in the Torah is only an expression of raising the voice, and the father of them all is “And the Levites shall answer (*ve'anu*) in a loud voice” (Deuteronomy 27:14).
Job.translator_note: Rashi’s wording of Deuteronomy 27:14 differs from JPS (“And the Levites shall speak, and say unto all the men of Israel with a loud voice”).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: wherein I was born
Job.english_translation: A future form: he was saying, “Would that the day on which I was destined to be born would perish, and then I would not have been born.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And the night wherein it was said
Job.english_translation: That too shall perish.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: it was said
Job.english_translation: That the announcer say, upon whom the matter is laid.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally; the sentence is elliptical.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: A man-child is brought forth
Job.english_translation: *Horah gaver* — that my father made my mother pregnant. For a female one is accustomed to say *horatah*, and for a male one is accustomed to say *horah* the female.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally; the explanation of the grammatical forms is elliptical.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And the night wherein it was said
Job.english_translation: This is one of the places where Scripture leaves out its words, because there was no need to specify who it is; and its figure of speech is “the sayer said.” (And like it, “Do horses run upon the rocks? Doth one plow there with oxen?” (Amos 6:12) — it should have said, “if a man plows with oxen.”) And our Rabbis of blessed memory said: the angel appointed over conception — Night is his name.
Job.translator_note: The parenthetical comparison is a later printed insertion; it is unreferenced in the source and is identified here as Amos 6:12. Rashi reads *babekarim* as “with oxen”; JPS: “Doth one plow there with oxen?”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Let that day be darkness
Job.english_translation: Always, every year, when that day arrives.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Let not God inquire after it from above
Job.english_translation: For good.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Neither let the light shine upon it
Job.english_translation: *Nehara* — light, like *tzohar*, which we translate *nihor*.
Job.translator_note: The Targum rendering is as printed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Let darkness and the shadow of death claim it for their own
Job.english_translation: *Yig'aluhu* — like “polluted bread (*lechem meguala*)” (Malachi 1:7), “Wherein have we polluted thee (*ga'alnucha*)?” (ibid.); it is an expression of defilement.
Job.translator_note: Printed “Malachi 1:7”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: the shadow of death
Job.english_translation: *Tzalmavet* — shadow of death (darkness) which never gives light everywhere.
Job.translator_note: The word in parentheses (“darkness”) is a later printed insertion.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Let a cloud dwell upon it
Job.english_translation: *Anana* — gloom.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Let all that maketh black the day terrify it
Job.english_translation: *Kimirirei yom* — demons who rule at noon, like *ketev meriri*, and it rules at noon, as it is said, “nor of the destruction that wasteth at noonday” (Psalms 91:6).
Job.translator_note: The phrase *ketev meriri* is at Deuteronomy 32:24 (JPS: “bitter destruction”); the source gives no reference for it. Printed “Psalms 91:6”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Let it not rejoice among the days of the year
Job.english_translation: *Al yichad* — let it not rejoice, like “And Jethro rejoiced (*vayichad*)” (Exodus 18). (Another version: let it not be united, *sa"a*.)
Job.translator_note: Printed “Exodus 18” is Exodus 18:9. it is left as printed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: let that night be desolate
Job.english_translation: *Galmud* — alone, and lacking man and every creature.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Let them curse it
Job.english_translation: *Yikkevuhu* — let them curse it, like “Come, curse (*kavah*) me” (Numbers 22).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Numbers 22” is Numbers 22:11 (JPS: “come curse me them”).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: that curse the day
Job.english_translation: *Orerei yom* — those who curse their days, because they intend to utter a curse out of their distress.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Who are ready to rouse up leviathan
Job.english_translation: *Ha'atidim orer leviatan* — to be childless (*ariri*) in their union, to join their accompaniment (*livuyam*), the union of a man and his wife without children. And in the Jerusalem Talmud I saw *orer leviatan* — to lament their accompaniment when he dies, like “he shall not wail (*ye'orer*) over his dead.”
Job.translator_note: The passage is obscure and is translated literally; the quotation “he shall not wail over his dead” is given without a reference in the source and could not be matched to a verse.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Let the stars of the twilight thereof be dark
Job.english_translation: *Nishpo* — the darkness of its pupil.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: the eyelids of the morning
Job.english_translation: *Be'afappei* — with its gleamings, like “and our eyelids gush out with waters” (Jeremiah 9:17).
Job.translator_note: The word *zehorurei* is translated as “gleamings”; this rendering is uncertain. Printed “Jeremiah 9:17”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Because it shut not up the doors of my [mother’s] womb
Job.english_translation: One who had the power in his hand to shut; and this too is one of the verses similar to “And the night wherein it was said.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: the doors of my [mother’s] womb
Job.english_translation: That I came out of; for if it had done so, “then trouble would be hidden from my eyes.”
Job.translator_note: The quotation is Rashi’s paraphrase of the second half of the verse.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Why died I not from the womb
Job.english_translation: From my coming out of the womb (I was, *sa"a*) ready to die at once; and he speaks in the future form, as if he were standing now on the day of coming out of the womb and says, “Why should I not die now?” and “Why did I not come out of the belly and expire?” — why was there no expiring ready for me?
Job.translator_note: it is left as printed. The sentence is translated literally. The parentheses are in the source.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Why did the knees receive me
Job.english_translation: The knees of my mother, before death.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And wherefore the breasts, that I should suck
Job.english_translation: It was decreed upon me to suck from them. Since he is speaking of the day of birth, he mentions the things that come after it in the future form.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: should I have lain still
Job.english_translation: I would have been lying in the grave.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Who built up waste places for themselves
Job.english_translation: This is the way of those who establish a name: to build ruined cities as a memorial for themselves, like “And they that shall be of thee shall build the old waste places” (Isaiah 58) and “thou shalt be called The repairer of the breach” — that is, with princes and men of name; or: would that I had not been known and had been like an untimely birth. And as for what he wrote, “I had not been as a hidden untimely birth,” since he stands on the language in which he began to speak, in a language of astonishment, it refers back to “Why did the knees receive me?” or “Why was I not as a hidden untimely birth?”
Job.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 58” is Isaiah 58:12. Rashi’s wording (“And they shall build of thee ruins of the world”) differs from JPS (“shall build the old waste places”). The phrase “hidden untimely birth” is from Job 3:16. The final sentence is elliptical and is translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: As infants that never saw light
Job.english_translation: *Ke'olelim* — babies; and he calls them *olelim* because all of them is play and soiling, like “and I have defiled (*ve'olalti*) in the dust” (below, 16) and like “and they abused her (*vayit'allelu*) all the night” (Judges 19).
Job.translator_note: Printed “below 16” is Job 16:15 (JPS: “laid my horn in the dust”; Rashi reads *ve'olalti* as “I have played/defiled”). Printed “Judges 19” is Judges 19:25.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: There the wicked cease from troubling
Job.english_translation: They refrain from their agitation, which they were accustomed and used to bring about in the land.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And there the weary are at rest
Job.english_translation: “And there they rested” — a matter of the present, written in the future form.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The small and great are there alike
Job.english_translation: There it is recognized who is important and who is lowly; and because that greatness is the greatness of the world, and that lowliness is the lowliness of the world.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally; the sentence is elliptical.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Wherewith is light given
Job.english_translation: (The Giver — and that is the Holy One, blessed be He.)

Job.english_lemma_JPS: to him that is in misery
Job.english_translation: To one who grew up in toil and trouble — why does He give him the light of the world and not put him to death at his birth?

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Who long for death, but it cometh not
Job.english_translation: For the bitter in soul, who yearn and desire death and complain, saying, “It is not.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And dig for it
Job.english_translation: They search after it.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: more than for hid treasures
Job.english_translation: More than those who search after hidden treasures of stores, and they were:
Job.translator_note: The comment ends abruptly (“and they were:”) in the source; translated as printed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Who rejoice unto exultation
Job.english_translation: And they would exult if they found a grave.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Who rejoice unto exultation
Job.english_translation: On account of the exultation and joy of (finding) a grave.
Job.translator_note: The word in parentheses (“finding”) is a later printed insertion.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: To a man whose way is hid
Job.english_translation: All the good that he did is hidden from the Master of Reward, and He did not look at it.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And whom God hath hedged in
Job.english_translation: He made a partition before him to shut him in a prison, like “Behold, I will hedge up thy way” (Hosea 2:8).
Job.translator_note: Rashi’s wording of Hosea 2:8 differs from JPS (“I will hedge up thy way with thorns”). Printed “Hosea 2:8”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: For my sighing cometh instead of my food
Job.english_translation: *Tavo* — has come.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And my roarings are poured out like water
Job.english_translation: *Vayittaku* — an expression of pouring on the ground; they flow and descend like water. And one may explain *netichah* as an expression of multiplying.
Job.translator_note: The last sentence is translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: For the thing which I did fear is come upon me
Job.english_translation: All my days I stood in fear of this, as we said above (chapter 1), “when the days of their feasting were gone about,” etc.
Job.translator_note: Printed “above 1” is Job 1:5.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And that which I was afraid of hath overtaken me
Job.english_translation: Behold, now it has been prepared and decreed that it should come upon me.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: I was not at ease
Job.english_translation: *Lo shalloti* — from this worry; and behold, trouble came.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Then answered Eliphaz the Temanite, and said
Job.english_translation: (Eliphaz’s reply. Eliphaz was the son of Esau, and because he grew up in the bosom of Isaac he merited that the Shechinah should rest upon him.
Job.translator_note: The comment is printed in parentheses, which are not closed in the source.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: the Temanite
Job.english_translation: From the land of Teman, from the land of Esau (*sa"a*).
Job.translator_note: it is left as printed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: If one venture a word unto thee, wilt thou be weary
Job.english_translation: *Hanessah* — an expression of astonishment: Because one ventured a word to you, are you wearied by one trial that your Creator tried you with, and which came upon you? And from now on, who can hold back from answering you with words?
Job.translator_note: Translated literally; the first clause is elliptical.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: thou hast instructed many
Job.english_translation: Those with whom you multiplied words — you reproved them and chastened them.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: the weak hands
Job.english_translation: And those frightened by the punishment that came upon them — you were accustomed to strengthen them and say, “Do not fear,” for such is the attribute of justice.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Thy words have upholden him that was falling
Job.english_translation: *Yekimun* — your words are accustomed to raise the one who stumbles.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Is not thy fear of God thy confidence
Job.english_translation: *Halo* — now your end proves your beginning: your fear — that you were God-fearing.
Job.translator_note: The sentence is elliptical and is translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: thy confidence
Job.english_translation: *Kislatekha* — it is (see Tosafot, Bava Metzia 58) from folly and not from complete knowledge; and likewise your hope and the integrity of your ways — all is folly.
Job.translator_note: The reference in parentheses, printed ע' תוס' ב"מ נח (“see Tos. Bava Metzia 58”), is a later printed insertion.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: cut off
Job.english_translation: *Nichchadu* — they disappeared and perished, like “and thou hadst been cut off (*vatikhached*) from the earth” (Exodus 9:15).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Exodus 9:15”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: According as I have seen
Job.english_translation: That (so) they were cut off, those who plow iniquity and prepare the iniquity in their thoughts, like this plower who prepares before the sowing, and afterward sow toil in their deeds; and I saw that they reap it — that is, their evil that comes upon them; and I saw that:
Job.translator_note: The word in parentheses (“so”) is a later printed insertion; the comment ends with “and I saw that:” in the source.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: By the breath of God they perish
Job.english_translation: From the blowing of His tempest and His anger.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And by the blast of His anger are they consumed
Job.english_translation: They are consumed continually; and he spoke of the generation of the Flood.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The lion roareth, and the fierce lion howleth
Job.english_translation: The *aryeh* is large, the *shachal* middle-sized, and the *kefir* small; all of them strayed — that is, the kings and the princes and the servants; and all these names are names of a lion.
Job.translator_note: Rashi reads *nit'u* as “strayed”; JPS renders “are broken.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The old lion perisheth for lack of prey
Job.english_translation: The princes perished like this *layish* that perishes for lack of food; so their strength to commit violence perished. *Ovad* is not an expression of a person losing something of his; it is that he himself goes to perdition, like “I have gone astray like a lost sheep (*oved*)” (Psalms 119:176) and like “I am like a useless vessel (*keli oved*)” (ibid. 31).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Psalms 119:176” and “ibid. 31” (Psalms 31:13).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And the whelps of the lioness are scattered abroad
Job.english_translation: He speaks of the generation of the Dispersion, who were scattered from there over the face of all the earth.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Now a word was secretly brought to me
Job.english_translation: He returns to his rebuke, with which he reproved him until now: “Why do you cry out? Remember, I pray thee, who ever perished, being innocent?” etc., “According as I have seen,” etc.; and concerning you, “a word of prophecy was secretly brought to me” from the style, like a stolen thing, because the Holy Spirit is not revealed openly to the prophets of the idolaters. A parable of a king who had a wife and a concubine: when he comes to his wife he comes openly, and to his concubine he comes in secret and by stealth. So the Holy One, blessed be He, to the prophets of the idolaters: “But God came to Abimelech in a dream of the night” (Genesis 20:3), and likewise “And God came to Laban,” etc. (ibid. 31); to Balaam, “Fallen down, yet with opened eyes” (Numbers 24:4); to Eliphaz, “visions of the night.” But of the prophets of Israel it is written (ibid. 12), “with him do I speak mouth to mouth, in a vision and not in riddles.” In Midrash Tanchuma I found it corrected, and *vl"sh*.
Job.translator_note: The final abbreviation (ול"ש) could not be resolved and is left as printed. Printed “ibid. 31” is Genesis 31:24; printed “ibid. 12” is Numbers 12:8, where Rashi’s wording (“in a vision and not in riddles”) differs from JPS (“even manifestly, and not in dark speeches”).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And mine ear received a whisper thereof
Job.english_translation: *Shemetz* — a small portion of a spirit of understanding.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: In thoughts from the visions of the night
Job.english_translation: *Bese'ifim* — in thoughts.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Fear came upon me, and trembling
Job.english_translation: From the spirit that came to me; and a “spirit” is an angel, as it is said, “Who makest winds Thy messengers” (Psalms 104:4).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Psalms 104:4”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: That made the hair of my flesh to stand up
Job.english_translation: *Tismar* — the spirit [made] the hair of my flesh [stand up].
Job.translator_note: The sentence is elliptical (“the spirit, the hair of my flesh”); the bracketed words are supplied from the verse.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: That made the hair of my flesh to stand up
Job.english_translation: *Tismar* — it is an expression for a person whose hairs stand on end.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: It stood still, but I could not discern the appearance thereof
Job.english_translation: It was standing before me, and I did not recognize its appearance.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: I heard a still voice
Job.english_translation: *Demamah vakol* — I used to hear a voice of something whispered. Another explanation: “a still voice I heard” — I heard a voice from stillness, but stillness I did not hear. “Stillness” means the angels who say song, as the Targum renders “and after the earthquake a still small voice” (I Kings 19:12): a voice of those who praise in a whisper. Moses heard stillness. From here: the earlier ones used the voice, and the later ones the *bat kol*, like a man who strikes with a hammer and the sound of the blow is heard from afar; so he says:
Job.translator_note: The sentence “Moses heard stillness” and the remark that follows are translated literally; the connection is not clear. The Targum rendering is as printed. Printed “I Kings 19:12”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Shall mortal man be just before God
Job.english_translation: As a question of wonder.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Shall a man be pure before his Maker
Job.english_translation: And if a man could be purer than his Maker — then why does this friend of yours cry out?

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Behold, He putteth no trust in His servants
Job.english_translation: *Hen be'avadav* — the righteous: He does not trust that they will not sin against Him, and removes them from the world before their time.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And His angels He chargeth with folly
Job.english_translation: *Tohalah* — an expression of folly (*holelut*).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: How much more
Job.english_translation: *Af* — all the more so.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: them that dwell in houses of clay, Whose foundation is in the dust
Job.english_translation: Their grave.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: who are crushed before the moth
Job.english_translation: From heaven they weaken their strength until they are low and crushed before the worm that eats them at their death.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Betwixt morning and evening they are shattered
Job.english_translation: In one day they are shattered and crushed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: without any regarding it
Job.english_translation: *Mibli mesim* — upon the heart, to return to their Maker.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: They perish for ever
Job.english_translation: And this too is a verse with something missing.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Is not their tent-cord plucked up within them
Job.english_translation: *Halo nasa yitram bam* — like “Therefore the abundance (*yitrah*) they have gotten” (Isaiah 15:7); their pride and their wisdom will be swallowed up in their bodies, and behold, it is pulled up and torn away, like “neither shall the stakes thereof be plucked up” (ibid. 33).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 15:7” and “ibid. 33” (Isaiah 33:20). Rashi’s wording of Isaiah 33:20 differs from JPS (“The stakes whereof shall never be plucked up”).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Call now; is there any that will answer thee
Job.english_translation: Up to here, the word of the prophecy; from here on he returns to his rebuke: cry out as much as you like — who will answer you?

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And to which of the holy ones wilt thou turn
Job.english_translation: Will you turn to those who decree this upon you, to fight with Him?
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: For anger killeth the foolish man
Job.english_translation: A fool like you — his anger kills him; for if you had been silent, perhaps the attribute of mercy would return to you.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And envy slayeth the silly one
Job.english_translation: *Kin'ah* — it is anger and wrath, like “They have roused Me to jealousy” (Deuteronomy 32:21).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Deuteronomy 32” is 32:21.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: His children are far from safety
Job.english_translation: This is the curse with which I cursed him.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And are crushed in the gate
Job.english_translation: With a *dagesh* it is *yeduka'u* (“they will be crushed”); and if it is vocalised with *rafeh* it serves for “they will crush” others.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally; the note is on the pointing of the word in the Hebrew.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Whose harvest
Job.english_translation: Of the wicked man.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: the hungry eateth up
Job.english_translation: When the wicked man dies, the hungry whom he cut short in his lifetime will come, and his robberies will be repaid from his property.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And taketh it even out of the thorns
Job.english_translation: *Ve'el tzinnim yikkachehu* — like “and they take unto thee” (Exodus 25): that is, for the need of the poor man who is saved from the thorns and the weapons of this wicked man, the judge appointed for it takes it.
Job.translator_note: Printed “Exodus 25”; the words “and they take unto thee” (*veyikchu elekha*) are at Exodus 27:20 (JPS: “that they bring unto thee”).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: and the snare gapeth for their substance
Job.english_translation: *Vesho'ef* — and each and every one will swallow up from the snares that he robbed in his lifetime.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally; the word *tzemim* (“snares”) in this sentence is uncertain.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: for their substance
Job.english_translation: *Cheilam* — their money that he robbed in his lifetime.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: For affliction cometh not forth from the dust
Job.english_translation: A blow that comes upon a man is not for nothing, and does not sprout for him from the dust.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: affliction
Job.english_translation: *Aven* — it is an expression of breaking.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: But man is born unto trouble
Job.english_translation: For it is impossible that he not sin and receive toil for his sin, to receive his punishment. He is not like the *benei reshef*, who are angels and spirits, who rise in flight and are not of the lower beings (rise to fly and to be of the lower beings, *sa"a*), for Satan and the evil inclination to rule over them.
Job.translator_note: The sentence is translated literally. it is left as printed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: As the sparks fly upward
Job.english_translation: *Reshef* — like “the fiery shafts of the bow” (Psalms 76:4); when the arrow flies it is called *reshef*, an expression of flight (*sa"a*).
Job.translator_note: it is left as printed. Printed “Psalms 76:4”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: But as for me, I would seek unto God
Job.english_translation: If these sufferings had come upon me, I would seek the Holy One, blessed be He, with prayer and supplication; and if I were there, I would speak with entreaty.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Who giveth rain upon the earth
Job.english_translation: The Land of Israel.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And sendeth waters upon the fields
Job.english_translation: By a messenger, to the other lands.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: So that He setteth up on high those that are low
Job.english_translation: He gives the rain, and He frustrates the thoughts of the cunning, who imagine raising prices and buying the fields of the poor for a little grain.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: those that mourn are exalted to safety
Job.english_translation: (*Kodrim* — whose faces are wrinkled with hunger.)
Job.translator_note: The source gives no separate lemma; the comment begins with the word *kodrim* (“those that mourn”), so the phrase of the verse containing it is used as the lemma.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: So that their hands can perform nothing substantial
Job.english_translation: That counsel which they imagined to carry out.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And the counsel of the wily is carried headlong
Job.english_translation: *Nimharah* — all counsel made in haste is folly.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: They meet with darkness in the day-time
Job.english_translation: For their counsel is not carried out, and the light of their wisdom is turned into darkness.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: But He saveth from the sword of their mouth
Job.english_translation: Those who stumble.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: the sword of their mouth
Job.english_translation: From whatever sword of their mouth, for they thought to swallow them up and longed to destroy them.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: from the hand of the mighty
Job.english_translation: He will save the needy.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And iniquity stoppeth her mouth
Job.english_translation: *Ve'olatah* — the false accusation and the wickedness, like “They search out iniquities (*olot*)” (Psalms 64:7) — false accusations.
Job.translator_note: Printed “Psalms 64:7”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: stoppeth
Job.english_translation: *Katz'ah* — shut, like “thou shalt not shut (*tikpotz*)”.
Job.translator_note: The quoted words are at Deuteronomy 15:7 (“nor shut thy hand”); the source gives no reference.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Behold, happy is the man whom God correcteth
Job.english_translation: Through sufferings. And just as He (heals) the pains of these, so would I seek Him concerning these sufferings that would come upon me; and you should have accepted them and not despised them.
Job.translator_note: The word in parentheses (“heals”) is a later printed insertion.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He will deliver thee in six troubles
Job.english_translation: When they come to the world, He will save you through the sufferings with which you were chastened; and also in the seventh, when it comes, it will not touch you; and now he counts them.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Thou shalt be hid from the scourge of the tongue
Job.english_translation: Of Satan He will hide you. These are the seven troubles: famine, sword, tongue, and destruction, etc.; and “the beasts of the earth” — they are bandits.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: For thou shalt be in league with the stones of the field
Job.english_translation: They are a kind of man.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And the beasts of the field shall be at peace with thee
Job.english_translation: That which is called *gruscha* in French; and this is the actual beast of the field. And in the language of the Mishnah, Torat Kohanim, they are called “lords of the field.”
Job.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Job 5:23 (“la bête des champs”), in forms such as גרושא and גרובא; the printed form (גרוש"ה) is a variant spelling.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: shall be at peace with thee
Job.english_translation: *Hashlemah lakh* — it will have peace with you.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And thou shalt know that thy tent is in peace
Job.english_translation: And then in every place you will be secure, because your tent is in peace.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And thou shalt visit thy habitation, and shalt miss nothing
Job.english_translation: *Ufakadta nevekha velo techeta* — like “at a hair-breadth, and not miss” (Judges 20); and this is the seventh that we counted above.
Job.translator_note: Printed “Judges 20” is Judges 20:16.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Thou shalt come to thy grave in a ripe age
Job.english_translation: That you will be saved from pestilence. And for *bechelach* there is no support in Scripture for understanding its figure of speech, and it is interpreted according to the sense of the figure, and learned from its context, that it is an expression for the completion of the ripening of the grain, when it has ripened all it needs. And our Rabbis of blessed memory explained *bechelach* by gematria as sixty years.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Like as a shock of corn cometh in in its season
Job.english_translation: When the stack is lifted from the ground in its time.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Then Job answered and said
Job.english_translation: [The source prints the lemma only, with no comment.]
Job.translator_note: The lemma in the source reads “(Job’s reply)”, in parentheses.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: my calamity laid in the balances altogether
Job.english_translation: *Havati* — my breaking.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: laid in the balances altogether
Job.english_translation: With the weight opposite them; and even if they were the sand of the seas, [my calamity] would be heavier than it.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: are my words broken
Job.english_translation: *La'u* — stammering, like a man who has no strength to bring a word out of his mouth properly; and so, “and they shall drink, and swallow down (*vela'u*)” (Obadiah 1:16), for it is the way of a drunkard to stammer in his words.
Job.translator_note: Rashi takes *vela'u* in Obadiah 1:16 as “stammer”; JPS has “swallow down.” Printed “Obadiah 1:16”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The poison whereof my spirit drinketh up
Job.english_translation: *Chamatam* — their venom; it is the way of the Persians to put snake venom in their arrows.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Doth the wild ass bray when he hath grass
Job.english_translation: That is: do I cry out for nothing? Does not a foolish beast bray when it has grass? And so the ox does not low unless it has no fodder. Of the wild ass the expression *nehak* is used, and of the ox the expression of lowing.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Can that which hath no savour be eaten without salt
Job.english_translation: A thing that is without salt, and needs to be salted and has not been salted, is called *tafel* in the language of the Mishnah (Shabbat 128; Chullin 113a; Nedarim 51).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Or is there any taste in the juice of mallows
Job.english_translation: *Im yesh ta'am berir* — that which comes from the *challamut* when one eats something strong that increases spittle and saliva, such as garlic. That is: do you think that answers with no substance in them will be accepted? *Rir* — like “and let his spittle (*riro*) fall down upon his beard” (I Samuel 21:14).
Job.translator_note: Printed “I Samuel 21:14”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: the juice of mallows
Job.english_translation: *Challamut* — like “their young ones wax strong (*yachlemu*)” (below, 39) — an expression of strength; and some interpret it as an expression of dream, but that does not seem right to me because of the *dagesh* in the *lamed*.
Job.translator_note: Printed “below 39” is Job 39:4.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: My soul refuseth to touch them
Job.english_translation: That is: I have much to cry out about; for things that my soul refused and loathed to touch — an expression of touching.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: They are as the sickness of my flesh
Job.english_translation: They are now ready for me to handle, like the cloths of my table, in which my bread is placed; *kedevei* — an expression of “and cut off their garments (*madeihem*)” (II Samuel 10:4); so *k"sh*, from the mouth of Rabbi Meshullam the physician. *A"a*: like the cloths with which they strain the dish, and food flows from them; *devi* is an expression of *davah*, a flowing woman (*zavah*).
Job.translator_note: The abbreviations כ"ש and ע"א could not be resolved and are left as printed. Rashi’s wording of II Samuel 10:4 (“and he cut off their garments”) differs slightly from JPS (“cut off their garments in the middle”). Printed “II Samuel 10:4”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: They are as the sickness of my flesh
Job.english_translation: *Lachmi* — every food is called *lechem*, like “made a great feast (*lechem rav*)” (Daniel 5:1) and like “Let us destroy the tree with its food (*belachmo*)” (Jeremiah 11:19), and Jonathan translated it “poison of death in its food.” Another version: “they are like the sight (*mabbat*) of my food” — that is, my heart is disgusted to look at them, with a worm, as I look at my food. And it is a Mishnaic expression: *umasgu ki davu*, in tractate Shabbat.
Job.translator_note: The last sentence (*umasgu ki davu*) is translated as printed and could not be matched to a passage. Rashi’s wording of Jeremiah 11:19 differs from JPS (“Let us destroy the tree with the fruit thereof”). Printed references checked: Daniel 5:1, Jeremiah 11:19.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: it would please God to crush me
Job.english_translation: *Veyo'el* — and He will wish.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: to crush me
Job.english_translation: *Vayedakke'eni* — an expression of death.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: That He would let loose His hand, and cut me off
Job.english_translation: *Yater yado* — may He make His hand great in His stroke, like “behold, the hand of the LORD is upon thy cattle…” (Exodus 9:3), “a very grievous murrain (*haveyah*).”
Job.translator_note: Rashi’s comparison with *haveyah* at Exodus 9:3 is as printed. Printed “Exodus 9:3”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: cut me off
Job.english_translation: *Veyevatz'eni* — may He finish me, like “He hath performed (*bitza*) His word” (Lamentations 2:17), “his hands shall also finish it (*tevatz'na*)” (Zechariah 4).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Zechariah 4” is Zechariah 4:9.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Then should I yet have comfort
Job.english_translation: And this too would still be a consolation to me.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Yea, I would exult in pain, though He spare not
Job.english_translation: *Ve'esaldah bechilah velo yachmol* — and I would ask Him for forgiveness, that He not spare me from finishing me. And I find no parallel for it in Scripture, except that in the language of the Mishnah it is an expression of fearing and worrying, as the hand recoils (*soledet*) from being burned with hot liquids. That is: I shall writhe in worry and in trembling over this request.
Job.translator_note: The sentence is translated literally; the sense of “forgiveness” here is as printed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: For I have not denied the words of the Holy One
Job.english_translation: And I have not failed to carry out His words.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: What is my strength, that I should wait
Job.english_translation: Strong enough to endure.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: that I should wait
Job.english_translation: That I should wait until the day of healing or until the day of death.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: that I should wait
Job.english_translation: *Ayachel* — like “and he stayed yet (*vayyachel*)” of Noah (Genesis 8:10).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 8:10”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And what is mine end
Job.english_translation: And what is my end, important and strong, that I should wait; for I cannot prolong my end by enduring.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: that I should be patient
Job.english_translation: *Nafshi* — it is the desire of a person’s inclination in several places, like “If it be your mind (*nafshekhem*)” (ibid. 23).
Job.translator_note: The source lemma is the word *nafshi* (“my soul”); the lemma shown is the JPS phrase that renders it. Printed “ibid. 23” is Genesis 23:8.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Is it that I have no help in me
Job.english_translation: An expression of astonishment: shall even this come upon me, that my help is not in me? Those friends who were to help me are not at my help?

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And that sound wisdom is driven quite from me
Job.english_translation: The counsel of counsellors is driven from me, for it has risen against me to provoke and to push away.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: To him that is ready to faint kindness is due from his friend
Job.english_translation: *Lamas merei'ehu chesed* — for one who withholds kindness from his fellow; and the *lamed* serves as in *lerav*, *letzav*, *leshav*; *mas* is also an expression of action, like *ba*, *shav*, *gad*; also these are expressions of doing.
Job.translator_note: The list of grammatical comparisons is translated literally. JPS renders *lamas* as “to him that is ready to faint.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: kindness is due from his friend
Job.english_translation: *Lamas* — the kindness: it consumes it, like “and as the sun waxed hot, it melted (*venamas*)” (Exodus 16:21).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Exodus 16:21”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: My brethren have dealt deceitfully as a brook
Job.english_translation: *Achi* — the members of my discourse.
Job.translator_note: *Benei melitzati* is translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: have dealt deceitfully
Job.english_translation: *Bagedu* — with me, like the brook that deals treacherously, a treachery, as he explains in the passage.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: As the channel of brooks that overflow
Job.english_translation: *Ke'afik nechalim* — the outlet of brooks; they pass from the straight measure and friendship; and what is the treachery of a brook?
Job.translator_note: The words “from the straight measure and friendship” are translated literally; the printed text appears abbreviated.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Which are black by reason of the ice
Job.english_translation: If ice comes upon them they are wrinkled and become cold (boards, cold).
Job.translator_note: The words in parentheses are a later printed insertion and are translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And wherein the snow hideth itself
Job.english_translation: The snow that falls on the ice is covered. Behold one treachery: that it is hidden from the eye, and the thirsty one does not find water to drink.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: What time they wax warm, they vanish
Job.english_translation: *Yezorevu* — an expression of “they will be scorched” (*yitzarevu*) in the heat of the sun.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: they vanish
Job.english_translation: *Nitzmetu* — רטרי"ש in French, like “and vinegar shrivels them (*tzomatan*)” in the language of the Gemara (Pesachim 40b). *Tzadi* is interchanged with *zayin*, like *tze'akah* and *ze'akah*.
Job.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Job 6:17 (“se rétrécissent”), in forms such as רטרייט and רטריינט; the printed form (רטרי"ש) differs slightly.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: What time they wax warm
Job.english_translation: *Yezorevu* — an expression of “and all faces shall be scorched therein” (Ezekiel 21:3) and like “a burning fire (*esh tzoveret*)” (Proverbs 16).
Job.translator_note: Rashi’s wording of Ezekiel 21:3 differs from JPS (“shall be seared thereby”). Printed “Proverbs 16” is Proverbs 16:27.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: they are consumed out of their place
Job.english_translation: *Nid'achu* — they were drawn together out of their place.
Job.translator_note: The word *nikpetzu* is translated as “drawn together”; the exact sense is uncertain.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The paths of their way do wind
Job.english_translation: *Yilafetu* — they take hold of the paths of their way, like “And Samson took fast hold (*vayilafet*)” (Judges 15), and likewise “and the man was startled, and turned himself (*vayilafet*)” (Ruth 3:8), because the woman embraced him.
Job.translator_note: Printed “Judges 15” is Judges 16:29. Rashi’s explanation of Ruth 3:8 (“because the woman embraced him”) differs from JPS.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The caravans of Tema looked
Job.english_translation: The land of Ishmael, which is low, and the waters flow there.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The companies of Sheba waited for them
Job.english_translation: *Kivvu* — an expression of a stretched line (*kav natuy*); another explanation: an expression of “let the waters be gathered” (*yikkavu*).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: They were ashamed because they had hoped; They came thither, and were confounded
Job.english_translation: Those who drink from them will be ashamed, because each and every one trusted to drink from them.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: For now you are become His
Job.english_translation: You have become like that brook.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: You see a terror, and are afraid
Job.english_translation: And the fear of the blow; and you are afraid to speak the truth, and you flatter my adversary.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Offer a present for me of your substance
Job.english_translation: *Umikochakhem* — and from your money.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: How forcible are words of uprightness
Job.english_translation: *Mah nimretzu* — like “a grievous curse (*kelalah nimretzet*)” (I Kings 2:8) — an expression of a word spoken in its proper manner (Proverbs 25); and likewise “How sweet (*nimletzu*) are Thy words unto my palate” (Psalms 119:103). All are expressions of eloquence (*melitzah*), and the *lamed* is interchanged with *resh*.
Job.translator_note: Printed “I Kings 2:8”; “Proverbs 25” is Proverbs 25:11 (“A word fitly spoken”); Psalms 119:103 is cited by Rashi for the root only.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: words of uprightness
Job.english_translation: *Imrei yosher* — if you had spoken words of uprightness, they would be accepted; but now, what will be proved from you? Every “reproof” in Job is a clarification of words, and they establish the truth.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Do you hold words to be an argument
Job.english_translation: Do you think to clarify words?

Job.english_lemma_JPS: But the speeches of one that is desperate to be wind
Job.english_translation: They are likened.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: the speeches of one that is desperate
Job.english_translation: Which have no substance, like “and thou saidst, There is no hope” (Jeremiah 5): I take no heed of the words of the prophets.
Job.translator_note: Printed “Jeremiah 5”; the words “but thou saidst: There is no hope” are at Jeremiah 2:25.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Yea, you would cast lots upon the fatherless, And dig a pit for your friend
Job.english_translation: *Tapilu* — in your judgment you cast anger upon a poor man like me, by the line of judgment; and you dig a pit for your friend, to make him fall.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Now therefore be pleased to look upon me
Job.english_translation: Be willing to turn to me and hear my words, and see whether I lie to your face.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Return, I pray you, let there be no injustice
Job.english_translation: *Shuvu na* — to examine; and you will examine, that there be no more injustice; and return (to investigate, and behold) my righteousness will be found in it.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Cannot my taste discern crafty devices
Job.english_translation: It will not understand, when I speak, calamities.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Is there not a time of service to man upon earth
Job.english_translation: This is the matter I said to you: be willing to turn to me, for how can I be silent from crying out over my calamity? Do you not know that there is a term (*tzava*) and a time for man, for how long he will live?

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And are not his days like the days of a hireling
Job.english_translation: One hired for a year knows that the days of his hire will end; so this man knows that the years apportioned to him will end; and I, that term that has been given to me.
Job.translator_note: The last clause is translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: As a servant that eagerly longeth for the shadow
Job.english_translation: Like a servant who toils all day and yearns and longs for when it will be the shade of evening; and like a hireling who hopes for his wage in the evening, because he had all day for toil, and he longs for the coming of the sun (the setting of the sun).
Job.translator_note: The words in parentheses explain the idiom “the coming of the sun” and are added here.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: So am I made to possess—months of vanity
Job.english_translation: From Heaven, months of vanity and sufferings; that is the term given to man on earth.
Job.translator_note: The word *eli* in the printed text (“…given to man *eli* earth”) is read here as *al* (“on”); the printed text may be corrupt.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And wearisome nights are appointed to me
Job.english_translation: (From Heaven.)

Job.english_lemma_JPS: When I lie down, I say
Job.english_translation: At night I looked, and said, etc.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: But the night is long
Job.english_translation: When will it be light and the time to arise come, and the time of the passing (*midud*) of the twilight; an expression of “and my sleep fled (*vatidod*)” (Genesis 31:40); and the *mem* is the root, falling like in *ma'amar*, *mishmar*.
Job.translator_note: The note on the letter *mem* is translated literally. Printed “Genesis 31:40”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: I am full of tossings to and fro unto the dawning of the day
Job.english_translation: And I am sated with tossing on my bed by day until twilight, because I could not sleep on account of sufferings until the twilight of the day, because worms covered my flesh.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: worms and clods of dust
Job.english_translation: *Gushat afar* — and it brought up rust, for the nature of a clod of earth is to moisten and bring up rust.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: My skin closeth up and breaketh out afresh
Job.english_translation: *Raga* — wrinkled, like “who stirreth up the sea (*roge'a hayam*)” (Isaiah 10). *P"a*: “my skin *raga*” — an expression of rest; wave after (another version: beside) wave, like these wrinkles.
Job.translator_note: The abbreviation פ"א could not be resolved and is left as printed. Printed “Isaiah 10” does not contain the words; “Who stirreth up the sea” is Isaiah 51:15.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: My days are swifter than a weaver’s shuttle
Job.english_translation: The days of my good fortune hurried to go.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: than a weaver’s shuttle
Job.english_translation: *Meni areg* — than woven things, which are made quickly; and so Hezekiah said (ibid. 38), “I have rolled up like a weaver my life.”
Job.translator_note: “Ibid. 38” is Isaiah 38:12.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And are spent without hope
Job.english_translation: I no longer hope for good.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Mine eye shall no more see good
Job.english_translation: After death; and here Job denied the resurrection of the dead.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The eye of him that seeth me shall behold me no more
Job.english_translation: *Lo shuruni* — no eye that would desire to see me will see me again after I die.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: While Thine eyes are upon me, I am gone
Job.english_translation: He speaks to the Holy One, blessed be He: Why was it necessary to wound me and crush me with sufferings? With one look, that You set Your eyes on me, I am no longer in the world.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Therefore I will not refrain my mouth
Job.english_translation: Since You do not cease from me, I too will not hold back from speaking, from crying out against Your attributes.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Am I a sea
Job.english_translation: *Hayam ani* — that You have set sand as a guard over me.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: or a sea-monster
Job.english_translation: *Im tannin* — a great fish that You bound in the depths of the sea; that You set a guard over me, this Satan, to guard me that my soul not go out.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: My couch shall ease my complaint
Job.english_translation: *Yisa vesichi mishkavi* — the bed of the night will bear my distress a little, and I will be able to restrain my complaint.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And death rather than these my bones
Job.english_translation: I choose death more than these limbs of mine.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: I loathe it
Job.english_translation: I loathe my life, for in the end I shall not live for ever.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Let me alone; for my days are vanity
Job.english_translation: From doing evil to me, for my days are vanity and few.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: that Thou shouldest magnify him
Job.english_translation: *Ki tegadlenu* — to set Your heart upon him, to examine his deeds every morning and to test him every moment.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: How long wilt Thou not look away from me
Job.english_translation: *Kammah* — a long time that You do not look away from me, like “and let them not regard lying words” (Exodus 5), and likewise (below, 14) “Look away from me and cease.”
Job.translator_note: Printed “Exodus 5” is Exodus 5:9. Printed “below 14” is Job 14:6, where JPS has “Look away from him, that he may rest”; Rashi’s quotation reads “from me” and “and cease.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: till I swallow down my spittle
Job.english_translation: *Bil'i raki* — the time for swallowing my spittle.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Why hast Thou set me as a mark for Thee
Job.english_translation: As one who strikes a man in his wrath and stirs up against him every deed of his enmity (another version: his liability).
