Job.english_lemma_JPS: So that I am a burden to myself
Job.english_translation: This is one of the words that Scripture altered by euphemism, and they are the emendation of the Scribes (*tikkun soferim*).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And why dost Thou not pardon my transgression
Job.english_translation: And what is this thing, that You do not forgive my transgression?

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And Thou wilt seek me, but I shall not be
Job.english_translation: You will seek me and You will not find me.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: the words of thy mouth are as a mighty wind
Job.english_translation: *Veruach kabbir* — a wind of words.
Job.translator_note: The source lemma reads “(Bildad’s reply)” and the comment begins with the words *veruach kabbir*; the lemma shown is the JPS phrase that renders them.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: a mighty wind
Job.english_translation: *Kabbir* — an expression of abundance.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Doth God pervert judgment
Job.english_translation: The *he* is vocalised with a *patach*, and its figure is an expression of astonishment.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He delivered them into the hand of their transgression
Job.english_translation: By their transgression; (the transgression) became a messenger to lead them.
Job.translator_note: The word in parentheses (“the transgression”) is a later printed insertion.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: If thou wouldest seek earnestly unto God
Job.english_translation: He will awaken your merit on your behalf.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And make the habitation of thy righteousness prosperous
Job.english_translation: *Veshilam nevat tzidkekha* — and He will make the habitation of your righteousness whole and perfect.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And though thy beginning was small
Job.english_translation: Your beginning, which passed in smallness, compared to your end, which will increase exceedingly.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: For inquire, I pray thee, of the former generation
Job.english_translation: Of the first generation, like “For ask now of the days past” (Deuteronomy 4:32).
Job.translator_note: Rashi’s wording of Deuteronomy 4:32 (“for ask now of the first days”) differs slightly from JPS. Printed “Deuteronomy 4:32”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And apply thyself to that which their fathers have searched out
Job.english_translation: *Vekhonen* — prepare and make ready to stand on the investigations of their fathers.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Can the rush shoot up without mire
Job.english_translation: They will say this: the rush does not grow except while the marsh is moist with its waters and its moisture. *Bitzah* (marsh) — *marisk* in French.
Job.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Job 8:11 (“terre humide”), in forms such as מריישק and מרישק; the printed form (מריש"ק) is a variant spelling.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Whilst it is yet in its greenness
Job.english_translation: *Be'ebbo* — in its moisture and in its fruit.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: and not cut down
Job.english_translation: It will not be broken and will not be torn off, like “and thou shalt pluck (*vekatafta*) ears” (ibid. 23).
Job.translator_note: “Ibid. 23” is Deuteronomy 23:26 (the previous reference in the printed text is Deuteronomy 4:32). Rashi cites the Hebrew word *vekatafta*; JPS has “then thou mayest pluck ears”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: It withereth before any other herb
Job.english_translation: Before all grass it dries up, when the waters are consumed and the marsh is dry.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: So are the paths of all that forget God
Job.english_translation: To succeed at the time when his hour smiles upon him, until his measure is filled.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And the hope of the godless man shall perish
Job.english_translation: The end of the flatterer shall perish.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Whose confidence is gossamer
Job.english_translation: *Asher yakut* — he will reap and cut off his confidence and his assurance.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Whose confidence is gossamer
Job.english_translation: *Kislo* — it is the thought of his trust, like “If I have made gold my hope (*kisli*)” (below, 31); *yakut* is an expression of reaping, like “a very little (*kat*)” (Ezekiel 16).
Job.translator_note: Printed “below 31” is Job 31:24. Printed “Ezekiel 16” is Ezekiel 16:47 (“in a very little while”).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And whose trust is a spider’s web
Job.english_translation: His trust will be something that does not endure.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He is green before the sun
Job.english_translation: Moist and strong is his fortune before the time of the visitation of the blow of its heat that dries him comes to him; and since he compared him to the rush, he speaks according to the subject.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And his shoots go forth over his garden
Job.english_translation: *Yonakto* — a root that sucks, or a young branch that grows this year, like “He cropped off the topmost of the young twigs thereof (*mereish yonekotav kataf*)”.
Job.translator_note: The quoted phrase is Ezekiel 17:4; the source gives no reference.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: His roots are wrapped about the heap
Job.english_translation: *Yesubbechu* — they will cling to the branch and the thicket.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He beholdeth the place of stones
Job.english_translation: *Yechezeh* — he sees a strong place; he sees and builds it for himself as a stronghold. And Menachem explained *yechezeh* as an expression of a border: he borders it, he builds it up to its border; and likewise “unto their desired haven (*mechoz chefzam*)” (Psalms 107:30), and likewise “light over against light (*machazeh el machazeh*)” (I Kings 7:5). All these are before his blow.
Job.translator_note: The last sentence (“all these are before his blow”) is translated literally. Printed references: Psalms 107:30, I Kings 7:5.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: If he be destroyed from his place
Job.english_translation: From his place, he who is punished; and this is a verse with something missing.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Then it shall deny him
Job.english_translation: His place.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: I have not seen thee
Job.english_translation: For nothing remains of him, neither root nor branch, and behold he is as though he had never been; for his fall is not like the fall of the righteous, for the righteous falls and rises, and this one falls without rising.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Behold, this is the joy of his way
Job.english_translation: Of the wicked man, whose whole joy and also his success will return to hopelessness.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And out of the earth shall others spring
Job.english_translation: People who until now were bowed down to the dust shall spring up.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And out of the earth shall others spring
Job.english_translation: *Acher* — another man shall spring up to receive the greatness of this one, as we find, “but to the sinner He giveth the task,” etc. (Ecclesiastes 2:26). *A"k*: know about yourself: if you were wicked, there is no rising for your fall, and if you were innocent, etc.
Job.translator_note: The abbreviation ע"כ could be read “therefore” or “up to here”; it is left as printed. Printed “Ecclesiastes 2:26”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: God will not cast away an innocent man
Job.english_translation: And He will not take hold of the hand of your enemies who do evil to you, until He returns to have mercy on you and fills your mouth with laughter.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: If one should desire to contend with Him
Job.english_translation: (Job’s reply.) “To contend with Him” — to argue with Him.
Job.translator_note: The source lemma reads “(Job’s reply)”, in parentheses.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He is wise in heart
Job.english_translation: For contention.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: and mighty in strength
Job.english_translation: To exact punishment.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Who hath hardened himself against Him, and prospered
Job.english_translation: Who hardened his heart and went on whole? Pharaoh hardened himself and was diminished; and so all who harden themselves.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Who removeth the mountains, and they know it not
Job.english_translation: He removes them as one who overturned Sodom.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: and they know it not
Job.english_translation: Until they were overturned.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Who shaketh the earth out of her place
Job.english_translation: When He looks at it, and it trembles.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Who commandeth the sun, and it riseth not
Job.english_translation: To the sun, “Be still,” and it keeps the word of the King and does not rise.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And sealeth up the stars
Job.english_translation: And opposite the stars He closes a partition, and they do not shine.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Who alone stretcheth out the heavens
Job.english_translation: And angels were created on the second day, so that you not say that Michael stretched out in the north and Gabriel in the south.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And treadeth upon the waves of the sea
Job.english_translation: On the heights of the sea. And regarding the work of Creation it is said that the lower waters were raised on high above, and He treads upon them.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Who maketh the Bear, Orion, and the Pleiades
Job.english_translation: They are constellations.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And the chambers of the south
Job.english_translation: To bring a storm in there, as it says, “Out of the Chamber cometh the storm” (below 37).
Job.translator_note: Printed “below 37” is Job 37:9.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Lo, He goeth by me, and I see Him not
Job.english_translation: I know that whatever He wishes, He does.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He passeth on also, but I perceive Him not
Job.english_translation: Before me, and I do not see Him.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Behold, He snatcheth away
Job.english_translation: He strikes suddenly, like “She also lieth in wait as a robber (*kechetef*)” (Proverbs 23:28); it is an expression of suddenness.
Job.translator_note: Rashi reads *chetef* as “suddenly”; JPS: “as a robber.” Printed “Proverbs 23:28”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: God will not withdraw His anger
Job.english_translation: Because of the fear of (and the righteousness of — another version) a man.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The helpers of Rahab did stoop under Him
Job.english_translation: The host on high who came to help Egypt; Egypt is called Rahab, as it is said, “Therefore have I called her arrogancy that sitteth still” (Isaiah 30:7), on account of their arrogance, in which they said, “Who is the LORD?” etc. (Exodus 3).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Exodus 3” is Exodus 5:2. Rashi’s quotation of Isaiah 30:7 reads “Rahab, they sit still”; JPS has “arrogancy that sitteth still.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: How much less shall I answer Him
Job.english_translation: *Af* — all the more so.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: yet would I not answer
Job.english_translation: I would fear to raise my voice before Him.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: to Him that contendeth with me
Job.english_translation: *Limshofti* — like *leshofti*.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Yet would I not believe that He would hearken unto my voice
Job.english_translation: I could not believe, out of my fear of Him; for how would I not fear Him?

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He that would break me with a tempest
Job.english_translation: My form was changed (another version: my row) before Him.
Job.translator_note: The variant *shurati* could not be resolved and is translated as “my row”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He that would break me with a tempest
Job.english_translation: *Yeshufeni* — He will shatter me, as “and I beat it, grinding it very small” (Deuteronomy 9); we translate *veshafit yativ*.
Job.translator_note: Printed “Deuteronomy 9” is Deuteronomy 9:21. The Targum rendering is as printed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And multiply my wounds without cause
Job.english_translation: *Pitzi* — a blow that brings out blood and pus.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: That would not suffer me to take my breath
Job.english_translation: He does not let me bring my spirit back to me.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: If it be a matter of strength, lo, He is mighty
Job.english_translation: How can I contend with Him? If it comes by strength — behold, He is mighty.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And if of justice, who will appoint me a time
Job.english_translation: Who can summon me before Him and uphold my plea of judgment?

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Though I be righteous, mine own mouth shall condemn me
Job.english_translation: For my words will be stopped from fear, and my mouth will make me crooked.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: I am innocent—I regard not myself
Job.english_translation: I know in myself that I am innocent; and yet I do not know my soul, wherein I may find rest.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: It is all one
Job.english_translation: *Achat hi* — in the world; and about it I said that He destroys the innocent and the wicked on account of it; and what is it:

Job.english_lemma_JPS: If the scourge slay suddenly
Job.english_translation: Of Satan [is] the scourge: he will kill the righteous suddenly.
Job.translator_note: The opening abbreviation (ל') is read as “of” and could not be confirmed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He will mock at the calamity of the guiltless
Job.english_translation: That he put to death, he will mock.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked
Job.english_translation: Toward Satan.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He covereth the faces of the judges thereof
Job.english_translation: From discerning a true matter.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: If it be not He, who then is it
Job.english_translation: A true matter, this matter: who is it that destroys the innocent?

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Now my days are swifter than a runner
Job.english_translation: With the destruction of the rest of the innocent, they were lighter than a runner.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: They are passed away as the swift ships
Job.english_translation: *Eveh* — the name of a flowing river.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: As the vulture that swoopeth on the prey
Job.english_translation: *Yatush* — it flies.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: I will forget my complaint
Job.english_translation: *Sichi* — the words of my distress.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: I will put off my sad countenance
Job.english_translation: *Panai* — my anger.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: and be of good cheer
Job.english_translation: *Ve'avligah* — I will take strength, like “that causeth destruction to flash (*hamavlig*) upon the strong” (Amos 5:9).
Job.translator_note: Rashi reads *hamavlig* as “strengthens”; JPS: “causeth destruction to flash.” Printed “Amos 5:9”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: I am afraid of all my pains
Job.english_translation: That they will not let me cease from crying out.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: I know that Thou wilt not hold me guiltless
Job.english_translation: From my iniquity, from being exacted of him.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Why then do I labour in vain
Job.english_translation: To come into judgment.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And make my hands never so clean
Job.english_translation: *Babor* — cleanness.
Job.translator_note: The source lemma is *babor*; the lemma shown is the JPS phrase that renders it.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Yet wilt Thou plunge me in the ditch
Job.english_translation: So as to be bright and defiled; that is, then You will find great iniquity in me.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: That we should come together in judgment
Job.english_translation: In words of reproof. *Mishpat* serves three expressions: its beginning is the reproof of words, its middle is the ruling of the verdict, and its end is the discipline of afflictions and the collection of a debt; and sometimes Scripture writes it according to its beginning, sometimes according to its middle, and sometimes according to its end.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: There is no arbiter betwixt us
Job.english_translation: *Mochiach* — *deresnier* [printed דרשני"ר] in French — who shows each one his guilt and his merit.
Job.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Job 9:33 (“arbitre”), in forms such as דרישנייר and דרישניר; the reading *deresnier* is from Darmesteter’s footnote (his gloss: “arbitre”); the printed form (דרשני"ר) is a variant spelling.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: That might lay his hand
Job.english_translation: *Yashet yado* — the rule of his dread and his exacting.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: upon us both
Job.english_translation: That the strong not overpower the weak.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: for I am not so with myself
Job.english_translation: Because I am afraid, I hold myself back from being found liable in judgment.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: My soul is weary of my life
Job.english_translation: *Nakta nafshi* — my soul quarrels over my being alive; and it is an expression of “and ye shall loathe yourselves (*unekotem*)” (Ezekiel 20).
Job.translator_note: Rashi explains *nakta* as “quarrels”; JPS renders “is weary.” Printed “Ezekiel 20” is Ezekiel 20:43 (“you shall loathe yourselves”).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: I will give free course to my complaint
Job.english_translation: *E'ezvah alai sichi* — my distress is to cry out and to complain, and I cannot praise it and bear up.
Job.translator_note: The final clause (“and I cannot praise it and bear up”) is translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Is it good unto Thee that Thou shouldest oppress
Job.english_translation: *Hatov* — as a question of wonder: that You oppress and rob the righteous of his righteousness, and shone the radiance of Your brightness upon the counsel of the wicked and provokers, to show them a smiling face.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Are Thy days as the days of man
Job.english_translation: To provoke him and to pursue.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Although Thou knowest that I shall not be condemned
Job.english_translation: *Al da'atekha* — You know.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Thy hands have framed me and fashioned me
Job.english_translation: *Itzvuni* — they made me; *etzev* is a mould, like “they do not shape the little one” in tractate Shabbat (page 146); and now Your hosts together round about.
Job.translator_note: The reference to Shabbat is as printed (146).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: yet Thou dost destroy me
Job.english_translation: They are the worms.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And wilt Thou bring me into dust again
Job.english_translation: In the end.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And curdled me like cheese
Job.english_translation: Like the drop of my begetting.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Thy providence hath preserved my spirit
Job.english_translation: *Pekudatekha* — the appointment of Your guarding, that You appointed guards for me.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Thy providence hath preserved my spirit
Job.english_translation: In my mother’s womb, and afterward:

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Yet these things Thou didst hide in Thy heart
Job.english_translation: To swallow me up, as though You (do) not remember them.
Job.translator_note: The word in parentheses (“do”) is a later printed insertion.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: I know that this is with Thee
Job.english_translation: Everything as explained, and You did not forget.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: If I sin, then Thou markest me
Job.english_translation: You set Your eyes upon me, not to overlook and to pass over Your attribute (and from now on), and from my iniquity You do not acquit me; but for everything You exact.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Being filled with ignominy
Job.english_translation: I.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And looking upon mine affliction
Job.english_translation: This is not a command but a noun: *re'eh oni* — בדנ"ץ in French — for every hour I see it. As you say *usevah yamim* (below, at the end), like *usevah yamim* (with a *kamatz* under the *shin*), so you say *ure'eh* as though *ure'eh oni*.
Job.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Job 10:15 (“et vois”), in forms such as בדניץ and בדנץ; the printed form (בדנ"ץ) matches. The final grammatical comparison (with Job 42:17, “full of days”) is translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And if it exalt itself, Thou huntest me as a lion
Job.english_translation: And it grows great in Your eyes, to be a burden to You, and to snare the soul of him whom You hunt like a lion — that You spread a net for me as though I were mighty like a lion.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And again
Job.english_translation: From day to day.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Thou showest Thyself marvellous upon me
Job.english_translation: To be exacting and to do wonders in judgment; an expression of “when he shall make a special vow (*yafli*)” (Numbers 6).
Job.translator_note: Rashi reads *yafli* in Numbers 6:2 as “set apart / make special”; JPS has “shall clearly utter a vow.” Printed “Numbers 6” is 6:2.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Thou renewest Thy witnesses against me
Job.english_translation: To testify to the succession of illnesses and pains.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Host succeeding host against me
Job.english_translation: Fixed times for these afflictions serve (a host, one) and return and change into others, different from these, and another time serves.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Would that I had perished, and no eye had seen me
Job.english_translation: Would that I had expired from the womb.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: I should have been carried from the womb to the grave
Job.english_translation: *Uval* — would that I had been carried.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Cease then, And let me alone
Job.english_translation: *Veshit mimeni* — set Yourself away from me and from upon me, like “Stand by thyself” (Isaiah 65): “draw near to Yourself,” draw near to Yourself and keep far from me.
Job.translator_note: Rashi’s quotation of Isaiah 65:5 reads *kerav elekha* (“draw near to yourself”); JPS: “Stand by thyself, Come not near to me.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Before I go whence I shall not return
Job.english_translation: While I am still alive and the time of my death has not yet arrived, leave me alone, and I shall be calm.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: A land of thick darkness, as darkness itself
Job.english_translation: A noun, darkness, like *shachar ve'afa*.
Job.translator_note: The comparison *shachar ve'afa* is as printed and could not be matched to a verse.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: A land of the shadow of death, without any order
Job.english_translation: *Tzalmavet* — it is, and without orders in it (for there are no human orders there, that is, customs, since there is no habitation there; and its light is like darkness).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And where the light is as darkness
Job.english_translation: The place of its radiance is like darkness.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Should not the multitude of words be answered
Job.english_translation: *Lo ya'aneh* — by others, because of the multitude of his words.
Job.translator_note: The source lemma reads “Zophar’s reply”, and the comment begins with the words *lo ya'aneh*; the lemma shown is the JPS phrase that renders them. Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Thy boastings have made men hold their peace
Job.english_translation: *Bad* — that you invent out of your own heart.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: men hold their peace
Job.english_translation: *Metim* — people.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: My doctrine is pure
Job.english_translation: To the Holy One, blessed be He: “My doctrine is pure, and I was clean in Your eyes.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: That sound wisdom is manifold
Job.english_translation: And know that sound wisdom has a double, for the Torah, which you have not fulfilled.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Know therefore that God exacteth of thee less than thine iniquity deserveth
Job.english_translation: Like “When thou dost lend (*tashe*) thy neighbour any manner of loan” (Deuteronomy 24:10): (that is) he has much more of a debt against you on account of the words of your iniquity.
Job.translator_note: The words in parentheses in the source are later printed insertions. Printed “Deuteronomy 24:10”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Canst thou find out the deep things of God
Job.english_translation: For you think that you have fulfilled everything.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: It is high as heaven; what canst thou do
Job.english_translation: A thing that is as high as the heights of heaven — what can you do now? And the wisdom is deeper than the netherworld.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The measure thereof is longer than the earth
Job.english_translation: Its measuring (another version: *mad* its); and here he used the word for measuring in the masculine form (for he did not say *middatah*).
Job.translator_note: The variant (ס"א מד' שלה) is truncated in the source.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: If He pass by, and shut up, Or gather in
Job.english_translation: With afflictions, whomever He wishes.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Or gather in
Job.english_translation: All His heavenly retinues, to rebuke for having shut up.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: then who can hinder Him
Job.english_translation: Who among them can answer Him with words, to find injustice in His deed? And if it is because the one judged is at ease and quiet for many days — such is His way.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And when He seeth iniquity, will He not then consider it
Job.english_translation: For they do so for days and years, and it appears as though He does not consider (they will not consider), because He is long-suffering.
Job.translator_note: The word in parentheses is a later printed variant.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: But an empty man will get understanding
Job.english_translation: Hollow, without a heart, who has not understood his way.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: will get understanding
Job.english_translation: He will acquire a heart for himself, to return to his Maker and to examine his deeds; or a man who was like a wild ass’s colt — to learn from a light matter without knowledge.
Job.translator_note: The second explanation is translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: is born a man
Job.english_translation: He will teach himself to be a new man, in the order of human beings, and will direct his way.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: If thou set thy heart aright
Job.english_translation: You would have directed your heart after the sufferings.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And stretch out thy hands toward Him
Job.english_translation: In supplication.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: put it far away
Job.english_translation: From your hand; and do not let unrighteousness dwell in your tents.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Surely then shalt thou lift up thy face without spot
Job.english_translation: If you were confident that you would lift your face without blemish, you would bring it about for yourself that you lift your face from every blemish (from this).
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Yea, thou shalt be stedfast
Job.english_translation: *Vehayita mutzak* — strong, like “the pillars of the earth.”
Job.translator_note: The quoted phrase is given without a reference in the source.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: For thou shalt forget thy misery
Job.english_translation: And you would forget every toil.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Thou shalt remember it as waters that are passed away
Job.english_translation: And that have passed away; so would all remembrance of toil be to you.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And thy life shall be clearer than the noonday
Job.english_translation: More than the light of noon will *chaled* arise for you — fortune and time (*mazal vezman*), like “and mine age (*chaldi*) is as nothing before Thee” (Psalms 39:6). Another explanation: *yakum chaled* is like “the light of your rust shall arise,” that is, a place of gloom will shine more than the light of noon. This I heard, but the first does not seem right (*sa"a*).
Job.translator_note: it is left as printed. The second explanation is translated literally. Printed “Psalms 39:6”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Though there be darkness, it shall be as the morning
Job.english_translation: Your gloom will be as morning. *A"a*: *ta'ufah* is an expression of “the eyelids of the dawn” (above, 3), for if it were an expression of *ofel* it should have said *te'ufah* pointed with a *sheva*, like *tenufah*, *tekumah*, *terumah*, *tenumah*.
Job.translator_note: The abbreviation ע"א could not be resolved and is left as printed. Printed “above 3” is Job 3:9.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: But the eyes of the wicked shall fail
Job.english_translation: Your enemies.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: shall fail
Job.english_translation: When they turn with your evil to see, and they shall not attain (their desire). And every “failing of the eyes” in the holy language is that of one who looks to see and does not attain, and like “and thine eyes shall look, and fail with longing for them” (Deuteronomy 28:32).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Deuteronomy 28:32”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And they shall have no way to flee
Job.english_translation: *Umanos* — it is a place of trust.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And their hope shall be the drooping of the soul
Job.english_translation: What they hope to see in you will be a drooping of the soul for them.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And wisdom shall die with you
Job.english_translation: (Job’s reply.) “Wisdom shall die” — when you die, all wisdom will die with you, for all wisdom is in you; but:
Job.translator_note: The source lemma reads “Job’s reply:” and the comment begins with the words *tamut chochmah*; the lemma shown is the JPS phrase that renders them.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: But I have understanding as well as you
Job.english_translation: And who is without such things as these — that the Holy One, blessed be He, is sovereign to do His will and to prolong the tranquillity of the wicked? You are but as those who mock me, and I am (the present) a laughing-stock to his fellow.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: A man that called upon God, And He answered him
Job.english_translation: *Ehyeh kore* — to the Holy One, blessed be He, and He answers him out of the pain of your provocation; and what does He answer him? To give him laughter for the righteous and innocent. Whole.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally; the final word (“Whole”) is as printed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The just, the innocent man is a laughing-stock
Job.english_translation: It is the answer with which He answers him: “I know, as you have said, that —”
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: A contemptible brand in the thought of him that is at ease
Job.english_translation: The fire of Gehinnom stands ready for him who is at ease in his thought, to say, “I shall have peace.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: A thing ready for them whose foot slippeth
Job.english_translation: Prepared is the thought of the one at ease, to be among those of slipping foot, whose feet slip.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The tents of robbers prosper
Job.english_translation: I know that the days *yishlayu* of the tents [belong] to the sons of Kedar, who dwell in tents in the wilderness, and they are robbers, as it is said, “his hand shall be against every man” (Genesis 16:12).
Job.translator_note: Translated literally. Printed “Genesis 16:12”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And they that provoke God are secure
Job.english_translation: There is wholeness for those who provoke God, in all that the Rock brought into his hand — peace, whether good or evil.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Doth not the ear try words, Even as the palate tasteth its food
Job.english_translation: And why did the hearers not know this? Their deed is as the palate tastes to eat.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Is wisdom with aged men, And understanding in length of days
Job.english_translation: To know that wisdom is with Him, etc.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Also He sendeth them out, and they overturn the earth
Job.english_translation: On His mission, as He did to the generation of Enosh, when He flooded a third of the world.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The deceived
Job.english_translation: The man who errs.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: and the deceiver are His
Job.english_translation: Satan, who causes him to err.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He leadeth counsellors away stripped
Job.english_translation: A noun; it is folly. He leads them in folly when He wishes to confuse them and to swallow up their wisdom, like “and he that departeth from evil maketh himself a prey (*mishtolel*)” (Isaiah 59:15), “The stout-hearted are bereft of sense (*ishtolelu*)” (Psalms 76:6). And the *tav* in *mishtolel* and in *ishtolelu* — such is the way of the Hebrew language with a word whose root is *shin* or *samech*, and which comes to say a thing in the reflexive or passive or *hitpael* form: it puts a *tav* after the first letter of the root, like “and they were forgotten (*veyishtakechu*) in the city” (Ecclesiastes 8:10), “and the statutes of Omri are kept (*vayishtamer*)” (Micah 6:16), “exaltest thou thyself (*mistolel*) against My people” (Exodus 9:17), and “the grasshopper shall drag itself along (*veyistabbel*)” (Ecclesiastes 12).
Job.translator_note: Printed references checked: Isaiah 59:15, Psalms 76:6, Ecclesiastes 8:10, Micah 6:16, Exodus 9:17, Ecclesiastes 12:5. Printed “Isaiah 59” is Isaiah 59:15; printed “Ecclesiastes 12” is 12:5.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And judges maketh He fools
Job.english_translation: *Yehollel* — He makes them mad; an expression of folly and stupidity.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He looseth the bond of kings
Job.english_translation: To remove the bond of their burden from others and to remove them from kingship.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And bindeth their loins with a girdle
Job.english_translation: At their beginning, when He desires them, He girds their loins and encourages them with strength for kingship.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He leadeth priests away stripped
Job.english_translation: *Kohanim* — princes, like “the priest of Midian” (Exodus 3:1), “priest of On” (Genesis 41).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 41” is Genesis 41:45.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He removeth the speech of men of trust
Job.english_translation: Even the trusted, for sometimes their lips are confused to speak waywardness, such as Abraham: “and he believed in the LORD” (Genesis 15:6), and in the end he stumbled with “whereby shall I know?” (Genesis 15:8).
Job.translator_note: The references (Genesis 15:6, 15:8) are not given in the source.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And looseth the belt of the strong
Job.english_translation: He loosens the girdle of the strong and opens their girdle to weaken their strength, like “and for the girdle wherewith he is girded continually” (Psalms 109).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Psalms 109” is Psalms 109:19.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: the strong
Job.english_translation: *Afikim* — strong ones, like “pipes of brass (*afikei nechoshet*)” (below, 40), “his scales are his pride (*afikei maginim*)” (ibid. 41).
Job.translator_note: Rashi reads *afikim* as “strong”; JPS renders the passages “pipes of brass” and “his scales.” Printed “below 40” is Job 40:18; “ibid. 41” is Job 41:7.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He increaseth the nations, and destroyeth them
Job.english_translation: Some say it is as He did to Egypt when they overtook Israel before Baal-zephon (Exodus 14): they erred (*shagu*) and said, “Know that he has agreed with us to drown them in the sea, as we decreed, ‘Every son that is born you shall cast into the river’” (ibid. 1); and the fear of Baal-zephon was strong, because no judgments were executed upon him like all the gods of Egypt, and the Omnipresent caused them to err in order to drown them. But this language is not the main one, for if so he should have said, on the right side, *mashgi* like *shogeh*. But this is the main one: *magdil* — an expression of *sagi* (great) strength: He makes the nations great and makes them succeed, and their heart grows proud in their success, and it was their destruction, that they succeeded.
Job.translator_note: The grammatical remark (“he should have said, on the right side, *mashgi* like *shogeh*”) is translated literally. Printed “Exodus 14” is Exodus 14:2; “ibid. 1” is Exodus 1:22.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He enlargeth the nations, and leadeth them away
Job.english_translation: *Shoteach* — He increases them to be spread out on the earth and to cover it.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: where there is no way
Job.english_translation: In a waste that is not a way.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Notwithstanding I would speak to the Almighty
Job.english_translation: I seek only to speak to Him and to argue with Him; I desire.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: But you are plasterers of lies
Job.english_translation: Composers of words of falsehood.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: You are all physicians of no value
Job.english_translation: Every *elil* in Scripture is an expression of *el*; but our Rabbis explained: this is the sinew of the neck, which has no cure, and its name is *alal*.
Job.translator_note: The word *el* in the first clause is translated as printed; its sense there is uncertain.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: the pleadings of my lips
Job.english_translation: *Verivot* — reproofs.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Will you speak unrighteously for God
Job.english_translation: Since you have come to contend in God’s place, it is not good that you speak injustice.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And talk deceitfully for Him
Job.english_translation: *Ulo tedabberu remiyah* — for His sake you speak deceit, like “Behold, I am toward God even as thou art” (below 33) and like “unto the land which He promised unto them” (Deuteronomy 9:28) — for their need — and like “will fight for you” (Exodus 14:14), “Will you contend for Baal?” (Judges 6:31). It was hard in my eyes to liken it here, and it is like “by the hand of Moses, unto him” regarding Korah (Numbers 17:5).
Job.translator_note: The comparison with the *lamed* in these verses is translated literally. Printed “below 33” is Job 33:6. Rashi’s use of Deuteronomy 9:28 and Numbers 17:5 is as printed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Will you show Him favour
Job.english_translation: Have you come to flatter Him by showing favour?

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Will you contend for God
Job.english_translation: For His sake you argue for deceit.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Would it be good that He should search you out
Job.english_translation: And you will be found liars.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Or as one mocketh a man, will you mock Him
Job.english_translation: To say, “For Your honour we made ourselves liars.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He will surely reprove you
Job.english_translation: Will He not make known to you your slander?

Job.english_lemma_JPS: If you do secretly show favour
Job.english_translation: Is it in secret that you will stand before Him in judgment, that you will show Him favour, to say, “There we lifted Your face”?
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Shall not His majesty terrify you
Job.english_translation: *Halo se'eto* — His height and His awe will frighten you. And some say *se'eto* is the burning of His fire, like “and David and his men took them away (*vayisa'em*)” (II Samuel 5) and like “the beacon (*mas'at*) of the city” (Judges 20).
Job.translator_note: Printed “II Samuel 5” is II Samuel 5:21 (JPS: “took them away”); “Judges 20” is Judges 20:40 (JPS: “the beacon”).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Your memorials shall be like unto ashes
Job.english_translation: Proverbs of ashes (*mishlei efer*): your memorials are likened to ashes. You think to be likened to Abraham, who said, “who am but dust and ashes” (Genesis 18:27).
Job.translator_note: The opening words (*nimshal mishlei efer*) are translated literally. Printed “Genesis 18:27”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Your eminences to eminences of clay
Job.english_translation: Let your eminence before Him be equal to dust; your *gav* — your height — like “and thou hast built unto thee an eminent place (*gav*)” (in Ezekiel 15).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Ezekiel 15” is Ezekiel 16:24.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And let come on me what will
Job.english_translation: Whatever will pass upon me for the sin of my cry will pass upon me; and do not worry about what I must bear and hold on to.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Wherefore? I will take my flesh in my teeth
Job.english_translation: To chastise me and to force me into silence.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And put my life in my hand
Job.english_translation: To bring my soul to death in the sufferings of silence.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Though He slay me, yet will I trust in Him
Job.english_translation: Even if He slays me, I do not part from Him, and always I will wait for Him; therefore there is no rebellion or transgression in my words.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: But I will argue my ways before Him
Job.english_translation: And my ways in which I conducted myself.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: I will argue my ways before Him
Job.english_translation: To know what could make me guilty.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: This also shall be my salvation
Job.english_translation: And just as I am whole with Him, so also He will be my salvation; and you will not find favour in His eyes.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: That a hypocrite cannot come before Him
Job.english_translation: And this is what He says to them (below 42): “for you have not spoken of Me the thing that is right.”
Job.translator_note: Printed “below 42” is Job 42:7.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: I have ordered my cause
Job.english_translation: *Arachti mishpat* — proofs of words; I have arranged my arguments in my heart as to what to answer.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: For then would I hold my peace and die
Job.english_translation: If I do not contend, I will be silent and expire.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Only do not two things unto me
Job.english_translation: The judgment above and the judgment below; and if You come to judgment with one, then “I will not hide from You”: if in the judgment above I say, “I have sinned,” “He that covereth his transgressions shall not prosper,” etc. (Proverbs 28:13); and if in the judgment below, I too will not confess — covering of sin, *l"sh* (*sa"a*).
Job.translator_note: it is left as printed. The final clause, including the abbreviation ל"ש, is translated as printed. Printed “Proverbs 28:13”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Withdraw Thy hand far from me
Job.english_translation: *Kappekha* — Your compulsion (*kefiyatekha*), as Elihu answered, “neither shall my pressure (*ekhpi*) be heavy upon thee” (below 33); and some interpret *kappekha* as “Your hand,” and it is hard for me to say so, for we do not find *kaf* used for evil but only for protection, like “and I will cover thee with My hand (*vesakoti kappi*)” (Exodus 33).
Job.translator_note: Printed “below 33” is Job 33:7; “Exodus 33” is Exodus 33:22.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Wherefore hidest Thou Thy face
Job.english_translation: To see the ways of my uprightness.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Wilt Thou harass a driven leaf
Job.english_translation: *Ta'aroz* — will You frighten.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: That Thou shouldest write bitter things against me
Job.english_translation: *Merorot* — rebellious acts, in which I rebelled against Your mouth, You write, and not the good that I did.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Thou puttest my feet also in the stocks
Job.english_translation: *Basad* — in the Aramaic language *sadna*, *besadnia yativ*: a large piece of wood in which the feet of prisoners are placed; and in the Greek language, אשתו"ק.
Job.translator_note: Darmesteter lists this word at Job 13:27 (“dans les ceps”), in forms such as ציפא (Old French *cep*) and אשתוק, which he gives as German; the source here calls the language *Yavani* (“Greek”).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Thou drawest Thee a line about the soles of my feet
Job.english_translation: *Tithakkeh* — you yourself trace my steps: “thus he stepped, thus he acted”; and like “the bosom (*mechek*) of the earth” (Ezekiel 43) and “the bosom (*chek*) of the cubit” (ibid.); this is the root. אפיקיו"ל in French. “Behold, I have graven thee upon the palms of My hands” (Isaiah 49:16).
Job.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Job 13:27 (“en cercle”), in forms such as אפיקייל and אפיקיילי; the printed form (אפיקיו"ל) is a variant spelling. Printed “Ezekiel 43” is Ezekiel 43:13–14; Rashi cites the Hebrew words *mechek* and *chek*, which JPS renders “the bottom.” Printed “Isaiah 49:16”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Though I am like a wine-skin that consumeth
Job.english_translation: *Vehu kerakav yivleh* — this body that You pursue will rot and wear out, and there is no honour to You in Your pursuit.
Job.translator_note: Rashi reads *kerakav* as “like rot”; JPS renders “like a wine-skin.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And dost Thou open Thine eyes upon such a one
Job.english_translation: *Af al zeh* — the vanity and the rotten one.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And dost Thou open Thine eyes upon such a one
Job.english_translation: *Pakachta einekha* — to examine his sins.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And bringest me into judgment with Thee
Job.english_translation: *Ve'oti* — You bring into judgment for my iniquities.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean
Job.english_translation: He speaks of a putrid drop and of semen, which are impure; not one of them is pure so as not to sin.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Seeing his days are determined
Job.english_translation: If this is a recompense that is being repaid, that his days are determined and fixed for a set and appointed day for death.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The number of his months is with Thee
Job.english_translation: Fixed; and this law You made for him, that he will not endure any longer in the world — these payments suffice for You.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Look away from him, that he may rest
Job.english_translation: In that limited fixed number of days, and may He cease for him from pain until he is content in his old age and the failing of his strength with the day of his death, like a hireling who desires the completion of the work of his day, for his passing from the world is decreed and cut off from all other passers.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: For there is hope of a tree
Job.english_translation: That it will renew itself (*yachalof*).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And that the tender branch thereof will not cease
Job.english_translation: *Veyonaktu* — which from its trunk will not cease to be a branch.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And put forth boughs like a plant
Job.english_translation: *Ve'asah katzir* — it is a sprout, like “She sent out her branches (*ketzireha*) unto the sea” (Psalms 80).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Psalms 80” is Psalms 80:12.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: like a plant
Job.english_translation: *Neta* — a noun; its accent is above the *nun*, and it is pointed entirely with a *kamatz* because it is at the end of a verse; it too is of the root of *neta*.
Job.translator_note: The grammatical remark is translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: As the waters fail from the sea
Job.english_translation: From the place where a river comes and goes out from its source, coming of itself from the sea.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And the river is drained dry
Job.english_translation: *Vehanahar* — that comes from there shall be dried up and dry for ever; so a man lies down and will not rise.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: All the days of my service would I wait, till my relief should come
Job.english_translation: For revival.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Thou wouldest call, and I would answer Thee
Job.english_translation: *Tikra* — it is a supplication: “Call to me, and I will answer You,” to prove my words.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Thou wouldest have a desire to the work of Thy hands
Job.english_translation: *Tichsof* — You would desire.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: But now Thou numberest my steps
Job.english_translation: *Ki attah* — You do evil to me.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Thou numberest my steps
Job.english_translation: *Tze'adai* — You count.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Thou dost not even wait for my sin
Job.english_translation: *Lo tishmor* — You do not wait for my sin, from punishing; like “but his father kept the saying in mind” (Genesis 37): he waited for it to be fulfilled. And in the language of the Mishnah (Gemara, Sanhedrin 63): “A man should not say to his fellow, ‘Keep for me [a place] beside such-and-such idol’” — an expression of “wait.”
Job.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 37” is Genesis 37:11. The Sanhedrin reference is as printed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: My transgression is sealed up in a bag
Job.english_translation: Sealed and guarded in a bag of cloth, like silver and pearls, so that it not be lost.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And Thou heapest up mine iniquity
Job.english_translation: *Vattitpol al avoni* — You have joined [it] to my iniquity.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And surely the mountain falling crumbleth away
Job.english_translation: A mountain that falls — its height will crumble (*yavol*) and become dust, and there will be hope to benefit from it; and a rock that is removed from its place, it too; *yavol* is an expression of produce (*tevuah*); or:
Job.translator_note: Translated literally; the comment ends with “or:” in the source.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The waters wear the stones
Job.english_translation: [Stones] which the waters have worn down as they pass over them continually.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The overflowings thereof wash away the dust of the earth
Job.english_translation: The washing away of the aftergrowth of a stone, to turn into dust and for something to sprout in it, as the aftergrowth of a past harvest sprouts; so this dust, its aftergrowth, will turn into stone.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally; the sentence is obscure.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: So Thou destroyest the hope of man
Job.english_translation: *Vetikvat enosh* — is not so; which from … has perished for ever.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally; one word in the source (*meshimot*) could not be resolved.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Thou prevailest for ever against him, and he passeth
Job.english_translation: You become stronger than he and overpower him with Your strength, and he goes from the world.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: His sons come to honour, and he knoweth it not
Job.english_translation: *Yichbedu* — they will be weighty with silver and gold, and he will not know.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And they are brought low, but he regardeth them not
Job.english_translation: *Veyitz'aru* — and they will be diminished of all good, and he will not understand.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: But his flesh grieveth for him
Job.english_translation: The worm is hard on the dead, like a needle in living flesh.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Should a wise man make answer with windy knowledge
Job.english_translation: (Eliphaz’s reply.) “Should a wise man answer with windy knowledge?” — It is a wonder: shall one who is wise answer and raise his voice with knowledge of wind and vanity?
Job.translator_note: The source lemma reads “(Eliphaz’s reply)”, and the comment begins with the words *hechacham ya'aneh da'at ruach*; the lemma shown is the JPS phrase that renders them.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Should he reason with unprofitable talk
Job.english_translation: To argue with a matter from which he will have no benefit, like “and let her be a companion (*soknet*) unto him” (I Kings 1:2) and like “is endangered (*yiskan*) thereby” (Ecclesiastes 10:9) — he will benefit by them.
Job.translator_note: Rashi takes *yiskan* in Ecclesiastes 10:9 as “benefits”; JPS renders “is endangered.” Printed references checked: I Kings 1:2, Ecclesiastes 10:9.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Yea, thou doest away with fear
Job.english_translation: *Af attah* — all the more so you, who are very wise: you will annul fear by the abundance of your words.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And impairest devotion before God
Job.english_translation: *Vetigra sichah* — like “For He draweth away (*yigra*) the drops of water” (below, 36) and like “and thou restrainest (*tigra*) wisdom to thyself” (ibid.).
Job.translator_note: Printed “below 36” is Job 36:27; the second quotation is Job 15:8, in this chapter.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: For thine iniquity teacheth thy mouth
Job.english_translation: Your evil inclination [teaches] your mouth to speak words such as these; and you should have chosen the language of the crafty.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Thine own mouth condemneth thee, and not I
Job.english_translation: That is: answer me to my question, and it turns out that your mouth condemns you; for it is good for me that your mouth condemn you and not I, and this is my question.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Art thou the first man that was born
Job.english_translation: *Harishon adam tivvaled* — [were you born] before man was born? This *he* serves as an expression of wonder; therefore it is pointed with a *chataf patach*. And its figure: were you born first of the man formed from the earth, that you know how to fulfil all the wisdom of the commandments of the Creator?
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And dost thou restrain wisdom to thyself
Job.english_translation: *Vetigra* — and you increase [it] from above to below, to come down upon you.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally; the sense of *tigra* as “increase” here is uncertain.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Much older than thy father
Job.english_translation: *Kabbir* — abundant in days, more than your father.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Are the consolations of God too small for thee
Job.english_translation: That the Rock did good to you until now, for many days; and His good word that dealt gently (*la'at*) with you, with gentleness and quiet, He enriched.
Job.translator_note: The last word (*dishno*) is translated as “enriched”; the sense is uncertain.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And the word that dealeth gently with thee
Job.english_translation: *La'at* — the pleasant. It is a verb and not a noun, and therefore it is pointed half *kamatz* and half *patach*.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Why doth thy heart carry thee away
Job.english_translation: *Yikkachekha* — will teach you, as “My doctrine shall drop (*ya'arof*) as the rain” (Deuteronomy 32:2).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Deuteronomy 32:2”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And why do thine eyes wink
Job.english_translation: *Yirzemun* — like *yirmezun*, like *simlah* [and] *shalmah* (Exodus 22).
Job.translator_note: The source gives no verse; the two forms for “garment” occur in Exodus 22 (*shalmah* in 22:8, *simlah* in 22:26).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: What is man, that he should be clean
Job.english_translation: What is his strength, that he can be innocent before the Holy One, blessed be He?

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Yea, the heavens are not clean in His sight
Job.english_translation: The host of heaven.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Yea, the heavens are not clean in His sight
Job.english_translation: *Zaku* — they will shine; every expression of *zach* is *tzohar* (brightness).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: How much less
Job.english_translation: *Af* — all the more so.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: one that is abominable and impure
Job.english_translation: *Ne'elach* — abominable and mixed; and so, “they are together become impure (*ne'elachu*)” (Psalms 53:4).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Psalms 53:4”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Which wise men have told
Job.english_translation: And they confess their transgression and did not hide their iniquity from their fathers. This is what I have seen, and behold I shall tell you. And where did I see it? Judah confessed and was not ashamed in the matter of Tamar; Reuben confessed and was not ashamed in the matter of Bilhah; and what was their reward?

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Unto whom alone the land was given
Job.english_translation: For this reward Judah merited eternal kingship, and both of them took their portion of the inheritance and were not driven from their inheritance on account of their sin, since they confessed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And no stranger passed among them
Job.english_translation: When Moses came to bless them, as it is said, “Let Reuben live, and not die” and “And this for Judah” (Deuteronomy 33:7). Another explanation: “and no stranger passed among them” — in the inheritance of the future to come, the division is in the book of Ezekiel (48).
Job.translator_note: “Let Reuben live” is Deuteronomy 33:6; the printed reference (33:7) is for “And this for Judah.” Printed “Ezekiel 48”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The wicked man travaileth with pain all his days
Job.english_translation: The wicked man who does not return from his sin and does not confess his transgressions, all his days.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Even the number of years that are laid up for the oppressor
Job.english_translation: And he complains over his assurance that his evil which he did will be repaid; “all the number of years that are laid up for the oppressor, he travaileth with pain.”
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: travaileth with pain
Job.english_translation: *Mitcholel* — an expression of mourning (*aninut*); and I have not heard [a source].
Job.translator_note: The last words (*velo shama'ti*) are translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: A sound of terrors is in his ears
Job.english_translation: Saying, “The time of my repayment has arrived.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: In prosperity the destroyer shall come upon him
Job.english_translation: And when he is dwelling in peace, then the robber comes upon him.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And he is waited for of the sword
Job.english_translation: And he is destined for the sword, and poverty, to wander for bread: where will he find it?
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He wandereth abroad for bread
Job.english_translation: *Noded hu* — that is, he is assured of wandering.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He knoweth
Job.english_translation: *Yada* — for himself, in truth.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: is ready at his hand
Job.english_translation: *Ki nachon* — and prepared to come into his hand, that is, to him, and with him the day of darkness, like “of that which he had with him (*haba beyado*)” (Genesis 32:14).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 32:14”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: They prevail against him
Job.english_translation: *Titkefehu* — the distress will be stronger than he and will overpower him.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: as a king ready to the battle
Job.english_translation: I did not find its parallel; and one may interpret it with the interchange of letters, *resh* for *dalet*, like *Ashkenaz* and *Rifat* in the Torah (Genesis 10) (and in Chronicles I, 1:6) *Ashkenaz* and *Difat*, and so *Kittim* and *Dodanim* (ibid.). So here, *lekhidor* is like *lekhidod*, like that king who is destined to be burned in the fire of Gehinnom, and that is Sennacherib, about whom the prophet prophesied (Isaiah 30:33): “For a hearth is ordered of old; yea, for the king it is prepared” — to burn his armies, “it shall burn, a burning.” And similar to it, “sparks of fire (*kidodei esh*) leap forth” (below, 41). If (another version: fire) torches, if (another version: fire) flames.
Job.translator_note: The explanation is translated literally. The reference in parentheses (Chronicles) and the variants in parentheses are later printed insertions. Printed “Genesis 10” is Genesis 10:3 (JPS: “Riphath”; Chronicles 1:6: “Diphath”); “and so Kittim and Dodanim (ibid.)” — Genesis 10:4 has “Dodanim,” Chronicles 1:7 “Rodanim.” Printed “below 41” is Job 41:11. The words “it shall burn, a burning” are not a verse.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He runneth upon him with a stiff neck
Job.english_translation: He was running to the Creator with haughtiness and a stiffened neck, to anger Him.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: With the thick bosses of his bucklers
Job.english_translation: With the strength of his might; *gabbei* is an expression of height, like “and thou hast built unto thee an eminent place (*gav*)” (Ezekiel 16:24).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Ezekiel 16:24”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And made collops of fat on his loins
Job.english_translation: He made a mouth on his loins, because his fat and the thickness of his fatness is doubled over his loins, and they appear like a mouth.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And made collops of fat on his loins
Job.english_translation: *Pimah* — from the root of “and the file (*hapetzirah*) was *pim*” (I Samuel 13:21); this is the *lima* of the smiths, which has many mouths and is called *haftzirat piyot*.
Job.translator_note: The word לימ"א is left as printed. Printed “I Samuel 13:21”; the JPS text there reads “ba pim.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And he hath dwelt in desolate cities
Job.english_translation: Such is the way of the proud: they build ruins for a name.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: neither shall his substance continue
Job.english_translation: It will not endure for many days.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Neither shall their produce bend to the earth
Job.english_translation: *Velo yitteh* — *lo yinneteh*; its figure is like “and turned aside after lucre (*vayyittu*)” (I Samuel 8:3), which means “and they themselves were inclined.” So here, “it shall not be stretched from heaven to earth”: *minlam*, the gift of their desire and the provision of their thoughts; and it is like two words, *min lahem*.
Job.translator_note: Printed “I Samuel 8:3”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Neither shall their produce bend to the earth
Job.english_translation: *Min* — their preparation, like “and the king appointed (*vayman*) for them” (Daniel 8); and similar to it, “and the file (*hapetzirah*) was *pim*” in two words (I Samuel 13); and so *er'ellam*, Targum Jonathan *itgalei lehon* (Isaiah 33); this appears right to me, and Menachem supports me. Another explanation: *minlam* — an expression of “when thou hast made an end of dealing treacherously (*kinlotecha*)” (ibid.), and the *nun* in it is a falling radical, an expression of purpose: it will not incline to the earth, so that a decree of cutting should be void.
Job.translator_note: The second explanation is translated literally. Printed “Daniel 8” is Daniel 1:5 (JPS: “appointed”); “Isaiah 33” is 33:7 for *er'ellam*; *kinlotecha* is Isaiah 33:1.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: shall he go away
Job.english_translation: *Veyasur* — from the world.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And by the breath of His mouth shall he go away
Job.english_translation: Of the Ruler of the world; and this is a verse with something missing. Some interpret: because of the breath of his mouth, in that he spoke evil, speaking waywardness.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Let him not trust in vanity, deceiving himself
Job.english_translation: He who is led astray by vanity, for vanity will be his recompense and his labour, like “and concerning exchanging (*hatemurah*)” (Ruth 4).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Ruth 4” is Ruth 4:7.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: It shall be accomplished before his time
Job.english_translation: His recompense will stand at its fullness, from growing and from succeeding any more, like “and forty days were fulfilled (*vayimle'u*) for him” (Genesis 50:3), meaning “and they were completed.”
Job.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 50:3”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And his branch shall not be leafy
Job.english_translation: *Kaftah* — the bending of its branches; all the branches of a tree are like a dome (*kippah*).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: They conceive mischief, and bring forth iniquity
Job.english_translation: He did evil, and the reward of the birth will be paid in proportion to the conception.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And their belly prepareth deceit
Job.english_translation: *Tachin* — will prepare.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: deceit
Job.english_translation: Their desire will be turned into deceit for them.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Or what provoketh thee that thou answerest
Job.english_translation: (Job’s reply.) *Yamritzekha* — your mouth will estimate you to think forceful words in their proper manner.
Job.translator_note: The source lemma reads “(Job’s reply)”, and the comment begins with the word *yamritzekha*; the lemma shown is the JPS phrase that renders it. Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: I also could speak as you do
Job.english_translation: As you do, I know how to taunt.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: If your soul were in my soul’s stead
Job.english_translation: In sufferings, in place of my soul, I too would join together against you with words and shake my head at you, at your outcry, and strengthen you with my mouth, saying, “Be silent, take strength, and stand firm in your sufferings,” as you say to me.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And the moving of my lips would assuage your grief
Job.english_translation: *Venid sefati* — for I am shaking and complaining now and crying out; then it would be restrained, and I would no longer cry out and would no longer lament. But now:

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Though I speak, my pain is not assuaged
Job.english_translation: Etc.
Job.translator_note: The comment in the source consists only of “etc.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Thou hast made desolate all my company
Job.english_translation: *Hashimmotah* — an expression of silence, like *eshtomem* and like “Be astonished (*shomu*), O you heavens” (Jeremiah 2:12): they were silent and wondered.
Job.translator_note: Printed “Jeremiah 2:12”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And Thou hast shrivelled me up, which is a witness against me
Job.english_translation: You made me wrinkled and darkened because of a witness that became a witness to my iniquity, to accuse me.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Mine adversary
Job.english_translation: Satan is the adversary.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: sharpeneth his eyes upon me
Job.english_translation: *Yiltosh* — he sharpens, like “the forger (*lotesh*) of every cutting instrument” (Genesis 4).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 4” is Genesis 4:22.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: They have gaped upon me with their mouth
Job.english_translation: *Pa'aru* — they opened, like “and opened (*ufa'arah*) her mouth” (Isaiah 5).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 5” is Isaiah 5:14.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: They gather themselves together against me
Job.english_translation: *Yitmal'un* — they gather; and many similar [forms] are found in Scripture: “they have cried aloud after thee (*male*)” (Jeremiah 5), “a multitude (*melo*) of shepherds be called forth against him” (Isaiah 31:4); and it does not depart from its meaning, for every “fullness” is a gathering.
Job.translator_note: Printed “Jeremiah 5” is Jeremiah 12:6 (JPS: “they have cried aloud after thee”; Rashi reads *male* as “a gathered crowd”). Printed “Isaiah 31:4”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: God delivereth me to the ungodly
Job.english_translation: The Holy One, blessed be He, delivered me to a mocking fool, a wrongdoer, to mock me.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And casteth me into the hands of the wicked
Job.english_translation: The healing of his consolations and my cure He delivered to the wicked, who are nothing but provokers. Another explanation: *yiretni* is like *yiretzeni*, an expression of acceptance and consolations.
Job.translator_note: Rashi reads *yiretni* as “heals me / accepts me”; JPS renders “casteth me.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He broke me asunder
Job.english_translation: *Vayefarfereni* — that wicked one [breaks me]; an expression of crumbs.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: and dashed me to pieces
Job.english_translation: *Vayefatzpetzeni* — an expression of being broken into many pieces by a great blow, like “And I will dash them (*venifatztim*) one against another” (Jeremiah 14) and “that taketh and dasheth thy little ones against the rock” (Psalms 137:9).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Jeremiah 14” is Jeremiah 13:14.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: His archers compass me round about
Job.english_translation: *Rabbav* — one who shoots his arrows, like “and became an archer (*rovveh keshet*)” (Genesis 21).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 21” is Genesis 21:20.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: my gall upon the ground
Job.english_translation: *Meroroti* — my gall.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: I have sewed sackcloth upon my skin
Job.english_translation: *Gildi* — a dry wound and the raising of a scab; and in the language of the Mishnah (Rosh Hashanah 27), “and they stood it on its *gildo*.”
Job.translator_note: The Mishnaic quotation is translated literally; the reference is left as printed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And have laid my horn in the dust
Job.english_translation: *Ve'olali* — and my defilement and my disgrace, like “and abused her (*vayit'allelu*)” (Judges 19:25), an expression of contempt and disgrace, and like “Mine eye affected (*olelah*) my soul” (Lamentations 3).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Lamentations 3” is Lamentations 3:51; Rashi takes *olelah* as disgrace.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And have laid my horn in the dust
Job.english_translation: *Karni* — my splendour; an expression of “Rays hath He at His side (*karnayim miyado lo*)” (Habakkuk 3:4).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: My face is reddened with weeping
Job.english_translation: *Chamarmeru* — were wrinkled, like “his inwards were wrinkled (*nechmeru*)” in the language of the Mishnah (Chullin 10), and so “Mine inwards burn (*chomarmaru*)” (Lamentations 1).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Lamentations 1” is Lamentations 1:20. The Mishnaic quotation is translated literally; the reference is left as printed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And on my eyelids is the shadow of death
Job.english_translation: *Tzalmavet* — that they grew dark because of weeping and tears.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And my prayer is pure
Job.english_translation: I did not curse my fellow and did not pray evil for him.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And let my cry have no resting-place
Job.english_translation: In the earth, to swallow up my cry in it, for it goes up to heaven.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: my Witness is in heaven
Job.english_translation: My Maker, who knows my ways.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Mine eye poureth out tears unto God
Job.english_translation: *Dalfah* — weeping and dripping a tear; an expression of *dilluf* (dripping).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: That He would set aright a man contending with God
Job.english_translation: And would that He do this for me, that He give me a place to contend, a man with God, to make equal the two disputes — the dispute of a man with his Maker, and the dispute between a man and his fellow.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: For the years that are few are coming on
Job.english_translation: Those fixed in number for the days of my life.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: For the years that are few are coming on
Job.english_translation: *Ye'etayu* — will arrive; and then “the way whence I shall not return I shall go.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: My spirit is consumed
Job.english_translation: *Nizche'u* — were contracted, like *nid'achu* (above, 10).
Job.translator_note: Printed “above 10”: I could not confirm the verse.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The grave is ready for me
Job.english_translation: *Kevarim li* — I am prepared for the grave.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Surely there are mockers with me
Job.english_translation: If not this: that mocking men have come upon me, that they have gathered with me in my consolations to mock me.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: in their provocation
Job.english_translation: *Uvehamrotam* — like “But they rebelled against Me (*vayyamru vi*)” (Ezekiel 20:8), “you have been rebellious (*mamrim heyitem*)” (Deuteronomy 9:7): an expression of your provocation.
Job.translator_note: Printed references: Ezekiel 20:8, Deuteronomy 9:7.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And mine eye abideth in their provocation
Job.english_translation: *Talan eini* — my eye and my heart and my thought, to rest in them.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Give now a pledge
Job.english_translation: The Creator.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: be surety for me with Thyself
Job.english_translation: *Arvenni* — with a clasping of the hand, to contend together, like “Who is there among these who will strike hands for me and make it good for him?”
Job.translator_note: Rashi’s quotation is a paraphrase of the verse; it is translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Therefore shalt Thou not exalt them
Job.english_translation: And therefore You will not raise Your glory through them.
Job.translator_note: The source lemma begins “For their heart Thou hast hid from understanding”; the comment explains the end of the verse.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He that denounceth his friends for the sake of flattery
Job.english_translation: *Lechelek yaggid* — for smooth words each one of them informs against his fellow, and this will come upon them: “the eyes of his children shall fail.”
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And I am become one in whose face they spit
Job.english_translation: *Vetofet* — like *tof* (a drum).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And I am become one in whose face they spit
Job.english_translation: *Lefanim* — of the people am I.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: all my members are as a shadow
Job.english_translation: *Vitzurai* — the limbs in which I am formed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Upright men are astonished at this
Job.english_translation: *Yoshommu* — will be amazed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And the innocent stirreth up himself against the godless
Job.english_translation: *Venaki* — if there is a righteous man who hears these mockeries of the flatterers.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: stirreth up himself against the godless
Job.english_translation: *Yit'orer* — to contend against you.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Yet the righteous holdeth on his way
Job.english_translation: Every righteous man [holds] his way, to stand against the company of flatterers.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: do you return, and come now
Job.english_translation: I say to you: return, please, and come, please.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And I shall not find a wise man among you
Job.english_translation: In that you scoff at my acceptance [of suffering].
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: My days are past
Job.english_translation: Behold, my days of goodness, to which I was accustomed, have passed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: my purposes are broken off
Job.english_translation: My plans, to prolong in goodness.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Even the thoughts of my heart
Job.english_translation: *Nitku morashei levavi* — the thoughts of my heart, which made me heir, for my heart was telling me to inherit good according to my ways.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: They change the night into day
Job.english_translation: These mockers turn night into day for me, for from the distress of the mockery I cannot sleep at night.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The light is short because of darkness
Job.english_translation: And it is short for me because of the troubles of the darkness of night. “The light is near”: when the sun comes, it appears to me that the day has only just dawned, and it has been shortened and passed — like “this city is near (*kerovah*)” (Genesis 19:20), [meaning] settled only recently, newly; and like “For the triumphing of the wicked is short (*mikarov*)” (below, 20) and “New gods that came up of late (*mikarov*)” (Deuteronomy 32:17).
Job.translator_note: Printed “below 20” is Job 20:5. Rashi reads *mikarov* as “recently”; JPS renders “short” and “of late.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: If I look for the nether-world as my house
Job.english_translation: Like “Seeing his days are determined (*charutzim*)” (above, 14) — that is, since I hope for the nether-world as my house.
Job.translator_note: Printed “above 14” is Job 14:5.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: If I have spread my couch in the darkness
Job.english_translation: I have spread my couch in the grave.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: If I have said to corruption: ‘Thou art my father’
Job.english_translation: To complain against it for many days, as though it were my father, since this is my hope.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Where then is my hope?
Job.english_translation: *Ve'ayeh efo tikvati* — and this [hope], why is it drawn out, and who will direct it to bring it running to me?
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: They shall go down to the bars of the nether-world
Job.english_translation: Those limbs that are destined to go down to the nether-world, so that together upon the dust there may be rest.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: When we are at rest together in the dust
Job.english_translation: *Nachat* — a lodging; an expression of “and the spirit rested (*vatanach*) upon them” (Numbers 11:26).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: How long will you lay snares for words?
Job.english_translation: (Bildad’s reply.) *Kintzei* — end.
Job.translator_note: The source gives “(Bildad’s reply)” before the lemma *kintzei*; the lemma shown is the JPS phrase that renders it.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Consider, and afterwards we will speak
Job.english_translation: *Tavinu* — be silent in order to understand and to hear what we shall speak.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: reputed dull in your sight
Job.english_translation: *Nitmeinu be'eineichem* — we are considered in your eyes as hidden ones (*temunin*). And there is no root for this word other than *tet*, *mem*, like *temunin Pelishtai*, the Targum of “the Philistines had stopped them” (Genesis 26:15). Some interpret it as an expression of *temina* (hiding), and they are mistaken, for then the word would need two *nuns*, one in the root and one in the plural form.
Job.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 26:15”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Thou that tearest thyself in thine anger
Job.english_translation: He turns back to Job: To you I say, the one who tears and destroys his soul in his anger and in his wrath.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Shall the earth be forsaken for thee?
Job.english_translation: Shall the earth be forsaken for the sake of your righteousness, from the judgment of its measure?
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Or shall the rock be removed out of its place?
Job.english_translation: The Maker (from its place) from His knowledge and from His measure.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally. “(from its place)” is a later printed insertion (PI).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Yea, the light of the wicked shall be put out
Job.english_translation: *Gam* — now, according to this outcry of yours, it will be conducted for generations.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: the spark of his fire shall not shine
Job.english_translation: *Or resha'im yid'ach* — a spark (*shaviv*) will leap from its place. *Ashtantzil'a*.
Job.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Job 18:5 (“étincelle”), in forms such as אַשְׁטַנְצִילְא; the printed form (אשטנציל"א) matches, apart from the printed quotation mark. The source lemma is *or resha'im yid'ach*; the lemma shown is the JPS phrase for the same verse.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The steps of his strength shall be straitened
Job.english_translation: *Yetzaru* — the steps of his strength will be short.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And his own counsel shall cast him down
Job.english_translation: *Vetashlichehu* — from upon him, his counsel which he counselled, which will not stand.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: For he is cast into a net by his own feet
