Job.english_translation: *Ki vegomer* — his end is that he sends into a net (“his sender”) his feet, to step upon the net and to be caught.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally. The parenthetical (*shulcho*) is a later printed insertion (PI).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And he walketh upon the toils
Job.english_translation: *Ve'al sevacha yithalech* — that is a net; every *sevacha* is made like a net, and it is the *kaifa* that is on the heads of women.
Job.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Job 18:8 (“coiffe, c.-à-d. filet”), in the form קוייפא; the printed form (קייפ"א) is a variant spelling.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: A gin shall take him by the heel
Job.english_translation: *Yochez* — a snare will seize him by the heel.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: A noose is hid for him in the ground
Job.english_translation: *Tamun ba'aretz* — beneath his feet.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: A noose is hid for him in the ground
Job.english_translation: *Chavlo* — the cord of his snare, in which he will be caught.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And a trap for him in the way
Job.english_translation: *Umalkudto* — hidden upon his path, as one hides the cord of a trap for birds.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Terrors shall overwhelm him on every side
Job.english_translation: *Ballahot* — demons.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And shall entrap him at his feet
Job.english_translation: (*Yenapetzehu*) they will dash him on the ground.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: His trouble shall be ravenous
Job.english_translation: *Ono* — his son.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: calamity shall be ready for his fall
Job.english_translation: *Letzal'o* — his wife.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: It shall devour the members of his body
Job.english_translation: And he will consume all the rest of his limbs: his sons and his daughters.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Yea, the first-born of death shall devour his members
Job.english_translation: *Bechor mavet* — the prince of death, like “I also will appoint him first-born (*bechor*)” (Psalms 89:28).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Psalms 89:28”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: That wherein he trusteth shall be plucked out of his tent
Job.english_translation: *Yinnatek me'oholo* — from his wife.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: That wherein he trusteth
Job.english_translation: *Mivtacho* — that she is confident in him; (*mivtacho*) her confidence, his, in that she relies upon him.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And he shall be brought to the king of terrors
Job.english_translation: *Vetatz'idehu* — and she will lead him and send him (from her) to the grave, to the king of the demons.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: There shall dwell in his tent that which is none of his
Job.english_translation: *Tishkon be'oholo* — a widow.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: that which is none of his
Job.english_translation: *Mibli lo* — (that she not be his) for he is dead; and at the end, “Brimstone shall be scattered (*yuzzeh*) upon his habitation.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He shall be driven from light into darkness
Job.english_translation: *Yehdefuhu* — from heaven.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He shall have neither son nor son’s son among his people
Job.english_translation: *Nechad* — a son’s son.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: They that come after shall be astonished at his day
Job.english_translation: *Nashammu acharonim* — they were amazed on hearing of the calamity that came upon him.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: As they that went before are affrighted
Job.english_translation: *Sa'ar* — it cannot be from the root of *sa'ar* (storm), for the sense of *sa'ar* (with a *shin* but with an *ayin*) and it does not turn to *kamatz* at an *etnachta* and end of verse. ל"ש
Job.translator_note: Translated literally; the grammatical argument is unclear in the printed text. The abbreviation ל"ש is left as printed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Surely such are the dwellings of the wicked
Job.english_translation: *Eleh mishkenot avval* — this is their end.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: How long will you vex my soul
Job.english_translation: (Job’s reply.) *Tugyon* — an expression of grief (*tugah*).
Job.translator_note: The source gives “(Job’s reply)” before the comment, which is on *tugyun* in the verse; the lemma shown is the JPS phrase that renders it. The printed form *tugyon* is translated as printed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: These ten times have you reproached me
Job.english_translation: *Eser pe'amim* — there are ten sections up to here.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: You are not ashamed that you deal harshly with me
Job.english_translation: *Tachkeru li* — you will estrange yourselves from me.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Mine error remaineth with myself
Job.english_translation: *Iti talin* — I am the one who takes the blows for my error.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: If indeed you will magnify yourselves against me
Job.english_translation: *Im omnam* — you add to my distress, and you will reprove against me my reproach, showing and reproving my reproach to my face.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Behold, I cry out: ‘Violence! ’ but I am not heard
Job.english_translation: *Etz'ak* — over violence, and I am not answered.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And my hope hath He plucked up like a tree
Job.english_translation: *Vayyasa* — an expression of uprooting.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And cast up their way against me
Job.english_translation: *Vayyasollu* — an expression of a highway (*mesillah*).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And mine acquaintance are wholly estranged from me
Job.english_translation: *Ach zaru* — an expression of cruelty (*akhzar*).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And I am loathsome to the children of my tribe
Job.english_translation: *Livnei vitni* — to those whom I raised in my house as though they were my sons.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Even urchins despised me
Job.english_translation: *Avilim ma'asu vi* — I am despised in the eyes of children, and how much more so [כ"ש] in the eyes of princes.
Job.translator_note: The abbreviation כ"ש is read as “how much more so” (*kal shekken*) from the context; flagged as my reading.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: My bone cleaveth to my skin and to my flesh
Job.english_translation: *Davkah atzmi* — for I am lean compared with the thickness of my flesh.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And I am escaped with the skin of my teeth
Job.english_translation: *Be'or shinai* — all my flesh was afflicted with boils and worms, except the gums of his teeth.
Job.translator_note: The source changes from “my” to “his” in the last words; translated as printed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: That with an iron pen and lead
Job.english_translation: *Be'et barzel* — they will be hewn in the rock, and afterwards they pass the lead over them, to give the letters a blackish appearance so as to recognize them, and so is the way of one who engraves stone; and it is not possible to interpret it as a pen of lead, for it is soft compared with the stone.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: But as for me, I know that my Redeemer liveth
Job.english_translation: *Va'ani yadati go'ali chai* — this *vav* refers back to above: “You will pursue me, but I know that my Redeemer liveth,” to exact payment, and He will endure and stand.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And that He will witness at the last upon the dust
Job.english_translation: *Ve'acharon al afar yakum* — after all who dwell in the dust have perished, He will stand last.
Job.translator_note: Rashi reads *yakum* as “will stand”; JPS renders “will witness.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He will witness at the last upon the dust
Job.english_translation: *Yakum* — will endure.
Job.translator_note: Rashi reads *yakum* as “will endure”; JPS renders “will witness.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And when after my skin this is destroyed
Job.english_translation: *Ve'achar ori nikfu zot* — and they do not pay heed to my Redeemer, but after the blow to my skin, this provocation and persecution was struck and gouged out, which I said was to me like one who strikes and cuts in my skin, like “And He shall cut down (*venikaf*) the thickets of the forest” (Isaiah 10:34).
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Then without my flesh shall I see God
Job.english_translation: *Umibesari* — I see judgments.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: shall I see God
Job.english_translation: *Eloha* — an expression of judgment and sufferings.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: If you say: ‘How we will persecute him! ’
Job.english_translation: *Ki tomru mah nirdaf lo* — like “If thou shalt say in thy heart” (Deuteronomy 7:17), where it is used in the sense of *dilma* (“lest”); that is: and that you would set your heart to have pity and to say, “Why do we pursue him?”
Job.translator_note: Translated literally; the Aramaic *dilma* is left as printed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Seeing that the root of the matter is found in me
Job.english_translation: *Veshoresh davar* — what is it that is found in him? Never will this good [thought] come up in your hearts: “the root of the matter” — on what does it stand?
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: For wrath bringeth the punishments of the sword
Job.english_translation: *Ki chemah* — that you magnify the sin that brings about the sword.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: That you may know there is a judgment
Job.english_translation: *Lema'an tede'un* — and you will understand the secret of the punishment that comes upon the wicked. And there is an *em lamasoret*: *shaddin* is written, as there is judgment (*din*) in the world, like “until that I, Deborah, arose (*shakkamti*)” (Judges 5:7); so I saw in Tanchuma.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally. The Hebrew of Judges 5:7 reads *shakkamti* (“I arose”); JPS renders “thou didst arise.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Therefore do my thoughts give answer to me
Job.english_translation: (Zophar’s reply.) *Se'ifai yeshivuni* — my thoughts will answer me an answer for my mouth; and because I am quiet and silent, and I have set within me my silences, my thoughts answer me to reply: I hear from you the afflictions of my humiliation, that you would humiliate me, and therefore a spirit answers me out of my understanding, to answer you.
Job.translator_note: The source begins “(Zophar’s reply)”; the comment is on *se'ifai yeshivuni*. Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Even by reason of mine agitation that is in me
Job.english_translation: *Chushi* — my silence, like “a time to keep silence (*lachashot*)” (Ecclesiastes 3).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Ecclesiastes 3” is Ecclesiastes 3:7.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Knowest thou not this of old time
Job.english_translation: *Zot* — it is a wonder: do you know a rule that goes upon the face of all generations from of old?
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: That the triumphing of the wicked is short
Job.english_translation: *Ki rinnat resha'im* — all the days of its being, it came recently and does not stand for length of days.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: the joy of the godless but for a moment
Job.english_translation: *Usmachat chaneph adei rega* — in a little time it will be consumed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Though his excellency mount up to the heavens
Job.english_translation: *Si'o* — his height.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Yet he shall perish for ever like his own dung
Job.english_translation: *Kegelalo* — the dung (*gelal*) of excrement.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He shall fly away as a dream, and shall not be found
Job.english_translation: *Velo yimtza'uhu* — those who knew him.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The eye which saw him shall see him no more
Job.english_translation: *Shezafato* — saw him.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: His children shall appease the poor
Job.english_translation: *Banav yeratzu dalim* — this answer is said concerning the people of Sodom, who were robbers and cruel to the poor.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And his hands shall restore
Job.english_translation: *Veyadav tashavnah* — the violence of his palms.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: restore his wealth
Job.english_translation: *Ono* — the strength of his coercion.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: His bones are full of his youth
Job.english_translation: *Atzmotav male'u alumav* — the strength of his youth.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: But it shall lie down with him in the dust
Job.english_translation: *Ve'imo al afar tishkav* — for he will die suddenly with his strength.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Though wickedness be sweet in his mouth
Job.english_translation: *Im tamtik* — such is the way of the wicked: if evil is sweet in his mouth and he does not see for it now the hour in which it will befall, he will conceal it under his tongue, until the time comes when it succeeds.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Yet his food in his bowels is turned
Job.english_translation: On the day of his calamity it is turned into the bitterness of asps.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He hath swallowed down riches
Job.english_translation: *Chayil* — money.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The viper’s tongue shall slay him
Job.english_translation: *Efeh* — a burning serpent (*nachash saraf*).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He shall not look upon the rivers
Job.english_translation: *Befalgot naharei nachalei* — of the Garden of Eden, which are sweet as honey and butter.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: That which he laboured for shall he give back
Job.english_translation: *Meshiv yaga* — the plunder that he plundered.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: According to the substance that he hath gotten, he shall not rejoice
Job.english_translation: *Kechayil temurato* — when its exchange is for wealth, great possessions, then lack will bring him [low].
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: he shall not rejoice
Job.english_translation: *Velo ya'alos* — in it; and so *ya'aloz* and so *ya'alotz*: the three are interchanged.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: For he hath oppressed and forsaken the poor
Job.english_translation: *Ki ritzatz azav dalim* — after he crushed the poor he forsook the poor and was driven out of the world and went away, and they return and collect from him his robberies.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: For he hath oppressed
Job.english_translation: *Ki ritzatz* — when he crushes, like “when they have a matter, it cometh unto me” (Exodus 18:16) — when they have.
Job.translator_note: Printed “Exodus 18:16”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Because he knew no quietness within him
Job.english_translation: *Ki lo yada* — his belly he never knew at ease; his belly says to him continually, “Rob and bring, to fill me,” and therefore “in his greed.” “In flesh of beauty is his desire.”
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: In his greed he suffered nought to escape
Job.english_translation: *Lo yemalet* — for it will be diminishing and going, and similar to it, “and like a moth Thou makest his beauty to consume away” (Psalms 39:12).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Psalms 39:12”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: There was nothing left that he devoured not
Job.english_translation: He did not leave any of his food to share with the poor.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Therefore his prosperity shall not endure
Job.english_translation: *Al ken lo yachil tuvo* — will not succeed, like (ibid.) “His ways prosper (*yachilu*)”; and it speaks of the people of Sodom, whose eyes were narrow toward guests, for so He testified (Ezekiel 16:49) concerning Sodom: “pride, fulness of bread,” etc. “and neither did she strengthen the hand of the poor and needy.” And our Rabbis explained *ein sarid le'ochlo*: he did not let a Torah scholar rest at his table, like “and among the remnant (*uvasseridim*) those whom the LORD shall call” (Joel 3:5).
Job.translator_note: The word *yachilu* occurs in Psalms 10:5; the reference “(ibid.)” in parentheses is a later printed insertion (PI). Rashi’s printed wording of the second quotation in Ezekiel 16:49 differs slightly in grammatical form from the verse.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: In the fulness of his sufficiency he shall be in straits
Job.english_translation: *Bimlot sifko* — when the desire of his heart is filled, enough — then it will be narrow for him. Distress will come upon him.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: In the fulness of his sufficiency
Job.english_translation: *Sifko* — an expression of “enough,” as we translate *kad sefiku gamlaya*, and “he found for them *hispakon*.”
Job.translator_note: The Aramaic and the word *hispakon* are left as printed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The hand of every one that is in misery shall come upon him
Job.english_translation: *Kol yad amal tevo'enu* — it will grow strong against him, and the hand of the poor will press him.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: It shall be for the filling of his belly; He shall cast the fierceness of His wrath upon him
Job.english_translation: *Yehi lemalei bitno yishlach bo charon apo* — the sending of His fierce anger will be to fill his belly; and this is not an expression of curse but an expression of prophecy and of the future.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And shall cause it to rain upon him into his flesh
Job.english_translation: *Veyamter alemo* — the Holy One, blessed be He.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: into his flesh
Job.english_translation: *Bilchumo* — in the fury of His war: snares, fire and brimstone, as it is said, “the LORD caused to rain upon Sodom,” etc. (Genesis 19:24).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The bow of brass shall strike him through
Job.english_translation: *Tachalfehu* — the arrows that the bow shoots will pass through his body to go from side to side. Another version: *tachalfehu* like *tachlifehu* (*tekademehu*) — a bow of brass.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He draweth it forth
Job.english_translation: *Shalaf* — the one who draws the weapon upon him.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: and it cometh out of his body
Job.english_translation: *Vayetze* — the weapon.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: out of his body
Job.english_translation: *Miggevah* — from within its sheath.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: the glittering point cometh out of his gall
Job.english_translation: *Uvarak* — *flandors* in French, like “that it may glitter (*barak*)” (Ezekiel 21:15). *Forbir*.
Job.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Job 20:28 (“l'éclair”), in forms such as פלנדורש, and, in the same place, forbir (“fourbie”) in forms such as פורביר; the printed forms (פלנדור"ש, פורבי"ר) match, apart from the printed quotation marks. Rashi’s comment is on 20:25. Printed “Ezekiel 21:15”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Terrors are upon him
Job.english_translation: *Mimmerorato yahalo'ch* — from the *merorah* of the weapon it goes, and from there there will be terrors and fear upon the wicked.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: All darkness is laid up for his treasures
Job.english_translation: *Letzfunav* — for the need of the hidden treasures, the stored [things] that are hidden for him.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: A fire not blown by man shall consume him
Job.english_translation: *Esh lo nufach* — the fire of Gehinnom.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: It shall go ill with him that is left in his tent
Job.english_translation: *Yera sarid be'oholo* — evil will come to the survivor who remains in his tent. The whole section is about the people of Sodom.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: It shall go ill with him that is left in his tent
Job.english_translation: Even Lot, who escaped from them — evil came to his tent, that is his wife, who became a pillar of salt. So I found in Midrash Rabbi Tanchuma.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And the earth shall rise up against him
Job.english_translation: *Mitkomemah* — an expression of an enemy who rises against him.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The increase of his house shall depart
Job.english_translation: *Yigel* — an expression of exile.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: His goods shall flow away in the day of his wrath
Job.english_translation: *Nigarot* — his treasures will be given to plunder and to spoil, like “as waters that are poured down (*hamugarim*) a steep place” (Micah 1:4).
Job.translator_note: Rashi’s printed wording ends with *artzah* (“to the ground”) where the verse reads *bamorad* (“a steep place”). Printed “Micah 1:4”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And the heritage appointed unto him by God
Job.english_translation: *Imro me'el* — that which was said concerning him before the Omnipresent. *Imro* is masculine, from the root of “Give ear to my words (*amarai*)” (Psalms 5); *imrato* is feminine, from the root of *amarot tehorot*.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally. Printed “Psalms 5” is Psalms 5:2.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And let this be your consolations
Job.english_translation: (Job’s reply.) *Utehi zot tanchumoteichem* — that you be silent and listen to me: let this be a consolation to me from you.
Job.translator_note: The source begins “(Job’s reply)” before the lemma.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Suffer me, that I may speak
Job.english_translation: *Sa'uni* — bear with me.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: As for me, is my complaint to man?
Job.english_translation: *Ha'anochi le'adam sichi* — why do you stand upon my outcry? Am I a complaint to a man like me, that he would hear my voice? And if [so], why should my spirit not be short, to cry out from the distress that is mine?
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Turn unto me
Job.english_translation: *Pnu elai* — to listen.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: and be astonished
Job.english_translation: *Vehasomu* — be astonished at my words.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And lay your hand upon your mouth
Job.english_translation: So that you will not know how to answer.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Even when I remember I am affrighted
Job.english_translation: *Ve'im zacharti* — the thing I want to say: why do the wicked live?

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Even when I remember I am affrighted
Job.english_translation: *Venivhalti* — for I see the wicked of the generation of the Flood: “become old, yea, wax mighty in power.”
Job.translator_note: Printed words are from Job 21:7.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Their houses are safe, without fear
Job.english_translation: *Shalom mipachad* — that no harmful beings ruled over them.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Their bull gendereth, and faileth not
Job.english_translation: *Shoro avar* — the female.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Their bull gendereth, and faileth not
Job.english_translation: *Velo yagil* — he will not shoot into her refuse seed that would return and be expelled from her body without pregnancy. Every expression of *hag'alah* is expulsion, and so in the language of the Mishnah, “he purges them (*mag'ilan*) in boiling water,” and so “for there the shield of the mighty was vilely cast away (*nig'al*)” (2 Samuel 1) — expelled from its anointing, and it was as if it had not been anointed with oil, for they used to anoint shields of leather so that it would be smooth and the spear and the lance that strike it would slide off; and it is like “anoint the shield” (Isaiah 21).
Job.translator_note: The Mishnaic quotation is translated literally; the reference is not given in the source. Printed “2 Samuel 1” is 2 Samuel 1:21; “Isaiah 21” is Isaiah 21:5.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Their cow calveth
Job.english_translation: *Tefalet paratho* — at the time she bears her offspring.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: and casteth not her calf
Job.english_translation: *Velo teshakkel* — out of its time.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: They send forth their little ones like a flock
Job.english_translation: At the time of its birth it would go and dance at once, and if it meets a harmful being it fights it, and its mother would say to it, “Bring me scissors and I will cut your hair.” In the Aggadah of Bereshit: “Go and light the lamp for me.” Bereshit Rabbah.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: They sing to the timbrel and harp, And rejoice at the sound of the pipe
Job.english_translation: *Yis'u* — they would lift up the voice in song with drum and harp; *ugav* is nothing but an expression of laughter, on account of lusts (*agavot*). *Asbanayemant* in French, כ"ש.
Job.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Job 21:12 (“jeu”), in forms such as אשבניימנט; the printed form (אשביימנ"ט) differs slightly (the *nun* after the *bet* is missing). The abbreviation כ"ש is left as printed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And peacefully they go down to the grave
Job.english_translation: *Uveregah sheol yechatu* — when the day of his death comes, he would die at that moment, in comfort, without sufferings.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: go down to the grave
Job.english_translation: *Yechatu* — went down; and in the Targum, *nechitu*.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And what profit should we have, if we pray unto Him?
Job.english_translation: *Umah no'il* — what benefit do we have that we should entreat Him? We have no need of Him, not even for a drop of rain, for “there went up a mist from the earth” (Genesis 2).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 2” is Genesis 2:6.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Lo, their prosperity is not in their hand
Job.english_translation: A wonder: is not all their goodness in their hand?

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The counsel of the wicked is far from me
Job.english_translation: Job was praising himself, that he saw them and was not counted with them.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: How oft is it that the lamp of the wicked is put out?
Job.english_translation: *Kamah ner resha'im yid'ach* — it goes back above, “Wherefore do the wicked live?” — how long will this time be prolonged? And he returns and curses them: “the lamp of the wicked is put out,” etc.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: That He distributeth pains in His anger
Job.english_translation: *Chavalim* — the lot fitting for them.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: ‘God layeth up his iniquity for his children! ’
Job.english_translation: *Eloha yitzpon livanav oni* — a wonder: is it a [just] measure that this one was wicked all his days, and was at peace and died in peace, and the Holy One, blessed be He, will store up his iniquity and his wickedness for his sons, to smite them?

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Let Him recompense it unto himself, that he may know it
Job.english_translation: It is praise for the Holy One, blessed be He, that He recompense the wicked man himself with his due, and he will understand that he acted wickedly.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Let his own eyes see his destruction
Job.english_translation: *Yir'u einav kido* — his breaking; and I cannot find a parallel for it in the Torah, except according to the sense of the verse, [which] appears [to mean] breaking; and so the Rav did not find a parallel for it. (*Kido*: an expression of *eido*; an *aleph* is interchanged with a *kaf*.)
Job.translator_note: Translated literally. The last sentence in parentheses is a later printed insertion (PI).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: For what pleasure hath he in his house after him? Seeing the number of his months is determined
Job.english_translation: *Ki mah chefzo beveito acharav umispar chodashav chutztzu* — for what does he care (*sekliri'er* in French) and desire for his house after his death, to be anxious in his lifetime about the punishment that is to come upon them, since the number of his months has been gathered and will end before the evil that the Omnipresent promised them, and his days were a hundred and twenty years (Genesis 6)? This is what I said to you: “Turn unto me, and be astonished.”
Job.translator_note: The Old French form (שקלירי"ר) is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. Printed “Genesis 6” is Genesis 6:3.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Shall any teach God knowledge?
Job.english_translation: *Hale'el yelammed da'at* — is there one of you who is under God who would teach knowledge — what is this measure?
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Seeing it is He that judgeth those that are high
Job.english_translation: *Vehu ramim yishpot* — such as I and the righteous and the distinguished: He chastises and judges and exacts payment from them, like “He turneth not by the way of the vineyards” (below, 24), said of Noah and Methuselah in the Aggadah of Chelek. Another version: *Hale'el yelammed da'at* — that is, must I teach Him knowledge to judge truthfully? He Himself is known to be so. But He judges exalted judgments in His height and His greatness, and does not care to be exact. This I heard, and not the first.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally. Printed “below 24” is Job 24:18.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: One dieth
Job.english_translation: *Zeh* — the wicked.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: One dieth in his full strength
Job.english_translation: *Yamut* — is punished in the very essence of his integrity, in the appearance of his wholeness, lacking nothing.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Being wholly at ease
Job.english_translation: *Shalanan* — like *sha'anan*.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: His pails are full of milk
Job.english_translation: *Atinav male'u chalav* — it is an expression of the Mishnah (Menachot 86a): *otno* in the olive press, they heap the olives together and their fat rolls and gathers into it, so that it is ready when it is pressed in the press; and that vessel in which they heap them, so that their oil gathers into it, is called *ma'atan*. Here too, his milk and his moisture and his fat are called *atinav*.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And another dieth in bitterness of soul
Job.english_translation: *Vezeh yamut benefesh marah* — the exalted and the holy: from them He exacts payment immediately.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: They lie down alike in the dust
Job.english_translation: And after their death it is not recognizable to people who was bad and who was good, for like this one, so this one: together upon the dust they lie.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Behold, I know your thoughts
Job.english_translation: *Hen yadati machshevoteichem* — and the devices which you wrongfully imagine against me: *tachmossu*, you do evil, to think violence.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: For you say: ‘Where is the house of the prince? And where is the tent wherein the wicked dwelt?’
Job.english_translation: Because of the evil that has come upon me you say, “See, where is the house of this one who was a nobleman, and where is the tent and the dwellings of the other wicked?” — that is, like him [are] they; in his wickedness his house perished (and why do you trust in your tranquillity?).
Job.translator_note: Translated literally. The last clause in parentheses is a later printed insertion (PI).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Have you not asked them that go by the way
Job.english_translation: All this you speak against me as parables.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And will you misdeem their tokens
Job.english_translation: *Ve'ototem* — those whom they informed you, you will not treat as strangers, to set it to heart, like “but made himself strange (*vayitnaker*) unto them” (Genesis 42).
Job.translator_note: Translated literally. Printed “Genesis 42” is Genesis 42:7.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: That the evil man is reserved to the day of calamity
Job.english_translation: *Ki leyom* — they told you that for the day of calamity the evil one is withheld; the wicked is restrained and withheld from evil and kept for the day fixed for his calamity, like “Which I have reserved (*chasachti*) against the time of trouble” (below, 38) — I concealed them and withheld them, to make them known until the day of battle and war.
Job.translator_note: Printed “below 38” is Job 38:23.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: But who shall declare his way to his face?
Job.english_translation: *Mi yaggid al panav darko* — who is the great king who will declare his way to his face, and they will not fear him? How exalted is this one: the Holy One, blessed be He, who made [it].
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And who shall repay him what he hath done?
Job.english_translation: And the recompense of his wickedness — who will repay him?

Job.english_lemma_JPS: For he is borne to the grave
Job.english_translation: *Vehu lekvarot yuval* — in the end, he will be borne to the grave.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And watch is kept over his tomb
Job.english_translation: *Ve'al gadish yishkod* — when he is buried in the fields near the stacks. (“*Ve'al gadish yishkod*” — they will judge him because he did not fulfil the commandments that belong to the field: gleanings, the forgotten sheaf and the corner, and the other commandments that apply to the omer and the stack, and therefore the punishments watched and hastened upon him. Gloss מר"ע.)
Job.translator_note: The sentence in parentheses is a later printed insertion (PI); the abbreviation מר"ע is left as printed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The clods of the valley are sweet unto him
Job.english_translation: *Rigvei* — *blasetz* in French.
Job.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Job 21:33 (“mottes de terre”), in forms such as בלישטש; the printed form (בלשט"ז) differs slightly.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: As there were innumerable before him
Job.english_translation: To those who are drawn after that way. All these are devices: you do violence against me.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: How then comfort you me in vain?
Job.english_translation: *Ve'eich tenachamuni hevel* — since your answers leave faithlessness, the answers of wisdom are forgotten and lost from you, and of your answers there remains in your hand nothing but an answer of faithlessness. *Ma'al* is a noun, therefore it is all pointed with *kamatz* and its accent is on the penultimate syllable. כ"ש.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally; the abbreviation כ"ש is left as printed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Can a man be profitable unto God?
Job.english_translation: (Eliphaz’s reply.) *Hale'el yiskan gaver* — for the need and benefit of the Maker would a man benefit and be profitable when he teaches knowledge of God to the creatures, and wisdom? *Yiskan* the first is an expression of benefit, like “and let her be a companion (*soknet*) unto him” (I Kings 1:2), and the second an expression of learning, like “was I ever wont (*haskēn hiskanti*)” (Numbers 22:30); and also the first can be interpreted as an expression of learning: for the benefit of the Maker and for His need would a man learn, as he learns understanding?
Job.translator_note: The source begins “(Eliphaz’s reply)” before the lemma. Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Is it any advantage to the Almighty, that thou art righteous?
Job.english_translation: *Hachefetz leShaddai* — like “For what pleasure (*chefzo*) hath he in his house after him?” (above, 21): the benefit and concern for Him if you make your deeds righteous in contending before Him, that He should come with you to contend over your words.
Job.translator_note: Printed “above 21” is Job 21:21.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Or is it gain to Him, that thou makest thy ways blameless?
Job.english_translation: *Ve'im betza* — money for Him if you make your ways perfect.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Is it for thy fear of Him that He reproveth thee
Job.english_translation: *Hamiyiratecha yochichecha* — or is it from fear that He would fear before you, that He will come and contend with you?

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Is not thy wickedness great?
Job.english_translation: *Halo* — He knows that your wickedness is great.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And as a mighty man, who hath the earth
Job.english_translation: *Ve'ish zeroa lo ha'aretz* — a wonder: because you were great, shall you inherit the earth? Is he worthy of enduring at all?

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And as a man of rank, who dwelleth in it
Job.english_translation: *Yoshev bah* — will be long in it, like “and ye abode in Kadesh” (Deuteronomy 11).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Deuteronomy 11”: the words occur in Deuteronomy 1:46 (JPS: “So you abode in Kadesh many days”); I could not confirm the printed chapter.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Or darkness, that thou canst not see
Job.english_translation: *O choshech lo tir'eh* — that is: do not set your eyes and your trust on strength, to say:
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Is not God in the height of heaven?
Job.english_translation: *Halo Eloha govah shamayim* — and He will not lower [Himself] to see.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And behold the topmost of the stars, how high they are!
Job.english_translation: *Ur'eh rosh kochavim ki ramu* — like “looking upon mine affliction (*ur'eh onyi*)” at the end of the fifth answer (above, 10); that is, you set your eye on the top of the stars, for they are high, and therefore you said:
Job.translator_note: Translated literally. Printed “above 10” is Job 10:15; the JPS rendering there is “And looking upon mine affliction.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: What doth God know?
Job.english_translation: *Mah yeda El* — in the work of darkness.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Can He judge through the dark cloud?
Job.english_translation: *Haba'ad arafel yishpot* — will He see and judge opposite this darkness? Behold.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Thick clouds are a covering to Him, that He seeth not
Job.english_translation: *Avim seter* — before Him, and He cannot see.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And He walketh in the circuit of heaven
Job.english_translation: *Vechug shamayim yithalech* — and He does not know what is on the earth.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: in the circuit of heaven
Job.english_translation: *Chug* — a circle, from the *michugah* of heaven, like “and he marketh it out with the compasses (*uvamchugah*)” (Isaiah 44:13): *compas* in French.
Job.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Job 22:14 (“cercle, compas”), in forms such as קונפט and קומפש; the printed form (קומפ"ש) matches, apart from the printed quotation mark.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Wilt thou keep the old way
Job.english_translation: *Ha'orach olam* — the way of the first ones, who [lived] long ago.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Wilt thou keep the old way
Job.english_translation: *Tishmor* — you kept in your heart to remember what happened to them.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Who were snatched away before their time
Job.english_translation: *Kumtu velo et* — they were cut off without their time.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Whose foundation was poured out as a stream
Job.english_translation: *Nahar vegomer* — and a river of the Flood, or the brimstone and fire of Sodom, was poured on their foundation.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: ‘Surely their substance is cut off
Job.english_translation: *Im lo nichchad kimanu* — will you keep [watch] and see whether their existence is not cut off?
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: ‘Surely their substance is cut off
Job.english_translation: *Kimanu* — like the stature (*komato*) of that generation, like “At Beth-el he would find him, and there he would speak with us (*immanu*)” (Hosea 12:5) — like *immo*.
Job.translator_note: Rashi reads *kimanu* as “their stature”; JPS renders “their substance.” Printed “Hosea 12:5”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And their abundance the fire hath consumed
Job.english_translation: *Veyitram* — their pride.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: the fire hath consumed
Job.english_translation: *Achlah esh* — they were judged with boiling water. Rabbi Tanchuma expounded that they were men of stature and did not die in the depths, and boiling water came upon them from above; and this is *yitram*, their surplus stature. כ"ש.
Job.translator_note: The abbreviation כ"ש is left as printed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Acquaint now thyself with Him, and be at peace
Job.english_translation: *Haskēn* — learn to be at peace with Him.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: and be at peace
Job.english_translation: *Ushelam* — and you will be whole and not lack in these things.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Thereby shall thine increase be good
Job.english_translation: *Tevu'atecha tovah* — your coming [will be] good.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And lay thy treasure in the dust
Job.english_translation: *Veshit al afar betzer* — because you will return to Him, you will place on the earth strength and fortresses.
Job.translator_note: Rashi reads *betzer* as “fortress”; JPS renders “treasure.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And the gold of Ophir among the stones of the brooks
Job.english_translation: *Uvtzur nechalim* — the high rocks that are in the deep brooks: you will have a gathering, a collection of Ophir; it is the treasure of kings, who used to treasure up and store gold that comes from Ophir.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And the Almighty be thy treasure
Job.english_translation: *Vehayah Shaddai betzarecha* — if this *Shaddai* is holy, I was amazed at its interpretation, for its implication is a curse, that He will be counted with his enemies, like “and thou art become my troubler (*be'ochrai*)” (Judges 11:35) — with my troublers; and by way of need we judge from the verses which are defective (like “*vehayah Shaddai shofet betzarecha*,” and if we can say it as secular, an expression of judge, and strength — this is its interpretation): “and Shaddai will be strength from your fortresses (*mivtzarecha*),” like “and lay thy treasure (*betzer*) in the dust,” that is, you will be an abundant wealth, a fortification; and according to the context so is its interpretation, for its end proves it: “and precious silver (*kesef to'afot*) unto thee” — an expression of strength, like “*vetoafot re'em lo*” (Numbers 23:22).
Job.translator_note: Translated literally; the text is difficult. The sentence in parentheses is a later printed insertion (PI). JPS renders Numbers 23:22 “like the lofty horns of the wild-ox.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And shalt lift up thy face unto God
Job.english_translation: *Vetisa el Eloha paneicha* — you will come to lift up your face only to ask your needs from Him.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And thou shalt pay thy vows
Job.english_translation: You are assured that the offerings, the payments of your vows, will be accepted.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: and it shall be established unto thee
Job.english_translation: *Vayakom lach* — like *veyakum lach*.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: When they cast thee down, thou shalt say: ‘There is lifting up’
Job.english_translation: *Ki hishpilu vetomer gevah* — and if one sees you walking in a lowly [way], you will say with assurance to lift him up, and he will be lifted.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: For the humble person He saveth
Job.english_translation: *Veshach einayim* — in the trouble that came (upon him) because of his iniquity.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: For the humble person He saveth
Job.english_translation: *Yoshia* — God [saves] him by your hand and by your prayer.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He delivereth him that is innocent
Job.english_translation: *Yemalet i naki* — “there is no innocent,” like *i-chavod* (I Samuel 4:21), “no glory”; and so (Proverbs 31) “and for princes *i shechar*” — no strong drink; no drunkenness is fitting for them; the three Menachem joined in one dispute, and although they are two words, they interpret it thus: “and thou shalt be delivered (*venimlat*) *i naki* by the cleanness of thy hands”; and so I heard. Another explanation I heard, that they said it from the mouth of Rabbi Jacob: that it is an expression of a man in the midst of sorrow and groaning (*anakah*), and the *yod* is extra in the word, like “O Thou that art enthroned (*hayoshevi*) in the heavens” (Psalms 123); but I did not hear it from the mouth of the Rav.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally. Printed “Proverbs 31” is Proverbs 31:4; “Psalms 123” is Psalms 123:1.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Even to-day is my complaint bitter
Job.english_translation: (Job’s reply.) *Gam hayom* — after all these consolations.
Job.translator_note: The source begins “(Job’s reply)” before the lemma.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Even to-day is my complaint bitter
Job.english_translation: *Meri sichi* — stands in its place, for there is no consolation in your words.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: My hand is become heavy because of my groaning
Job.english_translation: *Yadi kevedah* — the stroke of my plagues is stronger than my groaning, for I do not complain and cry out in proportion to my blow.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Oh that I knew where I might find Him
Job.english_translation: *Ve'emtza'ehu* — to my judge.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: That I might come even to His seat!
Job.english_translation: *Tichunato* — the foundation of His throne.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: I would order my cause before Him
Job.english_translation: *Mishpat* — the reproof of words.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: I would know the words which He would answer me
Job.english_translation: And even if He would stop me from speaking before Him, perhaps He will speak with me, and “I would know the words which He would answer me.” Rabbi Tanchuma.
Job.translator_note: The whole comment, including the lemma, is printed in parentheses (PI).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Would He contend with me in His great power?
Job.english_translation: Words and rebukes of his sins — would He contend with me?
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Nay; but He would give heed unto me
Job.english_translation: *Lo ach* — a stroke and compulsion, He will not set upon me His pressure and His terror (and again it may be interpreted): “Nay, but He would give heed unto me,” for He will not set upon me anything but the contention of rebuke for my transgression, and not the setting of pretexts.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: There the upright might reason with Him
Job.english_translation: *Sham* — in the place of our contention.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: There the upright might reason with Him
Job.english_translation: *Yashar* — the rightness of my deeds will be evident and revealed and seen with Him, before Him.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: So should I be delivered for ever from my Judge
Job.english_translation: *Nochach* — proven; “and there I shall be delivered for ever,” for no iniquity will be found in me.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Behold, I go forward, but He is not there
Job.english_translation: *Hen kedem* — it goes back above, “Oh that I knew,” etc.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Behold, I go forward
Job.english_translation: *Kedem* — east, as it is said, “*kedmah mizrachah*” (Exodus 21).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Exodus 21”: the phrase occurs at Exodus 27:13 (JPS: “on the east side eastward”); I could not confirm the printed chapter.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And backward, but I cannot perceive Him
Job.english_translation: *Achor* — west; since the east is the front (*kedem*) of the world, the west is found to be the back (*achorav*) of the world.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: On the left hand, when He doth work
Job.english_translation: *Semol* — north.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: On the left hand, when He doth work
Job.english_translation: *Be'asoto* — when He created it, He did not make the place of His throne there, that I might see Him there.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: but I cannot behold Him
Job.english_translation: *Achaz* — the Targum of *er'eh* (“I see”); and know that the accent is under the *aleph*, and if it were an expression of grasping, its accent would be on the last syllable, under the *chet*.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He turneth Himself to the right hand, but I cannot see Him
Job.english_translation: *Ya'tof yamin* — He covered the face of the south with His face, so that I might not see Him.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: For He knoweth the way that I take
Job.english_translation: *Ki yada derech* etc. — that which is with me, what it is; therefore He does not come to contend with me.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: When He hath tried me, I shall come forth as gold
Job.english_translation: *Bechanani* etc. — that I shall come forth as gold if He contends with me.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: My foot hath held fast to His steps
Job.english_translation: *Be'ashuro* — in His path (*be'ma'gelo*), like “If my step (*ashuri*) hath turned out of the way” (below, 31) and “He established my goings (*ashurav*)” (Psalms 40).
Job.translator_note: Printed “below 31” is Job 31:7; “Psalms 40” is Psalms 40:3. Rashi’s printed form there is *ashurav* (“his goings”); the verse reads *ashurai* (“my goings”).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: and turned not aside
Job.english_translation: *Velo atteh* — I am not accustomed to turn aside.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: I have treasured up the words of His mouth more than my necessary food
Job.english_translation: *Mechukki tzafanti imrei fiv* — more than my allotted sustenance I was diligent to treasure up the sayings of His mouth, like “mine allotted bread (*lechem chukki*)” (Proverbs 30:8) — my sustenance.
Job.translator_note: Printed “Proverbs 30:8”. The printed wording adds *mezonotai* (“my sustenance”) after *lechem chukki*.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: But He is at one with Himself
Job.english_translation: *Vehu* — because He is alone in the world and knows the mind and thoughts of the creatures, and what they have to say before Him, therefore answers are prepared before Him.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: and who can turn Him?
Job.english_translation: *Umi yeshivenu* — therefore, “what His soul desireth, even that He doeth.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: For He will perform that which is appointed for me
Job.english_translation: *Ki yashlim chukki* — I know that He will not withdraw His hand until He completes the decree of His decisions, the punishments that He decreed upon me.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And many such things are with Him
Job.english_translation: *Vechahenah rabbot imo* — for such [things] He has done many times.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Therefore am I affrighted at His presence
Job.english_translation: *Al ken* — that He does not repay a man according to his ways.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: When I consider, I am afraid of Him
Job.english_translation: *Mipanav evahel* — and when I contemplate His ways I fear Him.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Because I was not cut off before the darkness
Job.english_translation: *Ki lo nitzmati mipnei choshech* — over this I am terrified: that I was not cut off completely and for ever in the grave because of this darkness that has come upon me, and neither did He cover from before me this gloom until my death.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Neither did He cover the thick darkness from my face
Job.english_translation: *Umipanai kissah ofel* — the *lo* at the head of the verse repeats.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Why are times not laid up by the Almighty?
Job.english_translation: *Madua mishaddai lo nitzpenu itim* — this is a tradition (*kabbalah*): why were the times of the days of man not stored up by the Holy One, blessed be He, so that He should not know the day of man’s death — perhaps the punishment would not be hastened and the day of death would forestall it.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And why do not they that know Him see His days?
Job.english_translation: *Veyode'av lo chazu yamav* — from the day of man, like “a full month (*chodesh yamim*)” (and we translate *iddan be'iddan*, סא"א); another explanation: why can those who know Him and those who love Him of the Holy One, blessed be He, not see the end of His ways and His attributes?
Job.translator_note: it is left as printed. The Aramaic is translated as printed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: see His days
Job.english_translation: *Yamav* — this is the way He conducted in His days, like “my heart shall not reproach me so long as I live (*mimai*)” (below, 27) — and what are the astonishing attributes?
Job.translator_note: Printed “below 27” is Job 27:6; Rashi reads *mimai* here as “from my days.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: There are that remove the landmarks
Job.english_translation: *Gevulot yasigu* — those whose way is to remove landmarks: they buy fields adjoining other fields, and at night they enlarge their boundaries, for they would make their fences at night within the boundary of their neighbours (and this is *masig*, which we translate *mashgeh*, for they would remove the boundary סא"א).
Job.translator_note: it is left as printed. The Aramaic is translated as printed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: They violently take away flocks, and feed them
Job.english_translation: *Eder gazelu vayiru* — for themselves.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: They drive away the ass of the fatherless
Job.english_translation: And they do all the evils mentioned in the passage. The end of the matter: “Yet God imputeth it not for unseemliness” — to make known to them their iniquity and to cause them to find their recompense.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally. The quotation is Job 24:12.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The poor of the earth hide themselves together
Job.english_translation: *Yachad chuvu* — the poor of the earth, because they fear them.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Behold, as wild asses in the wilderness
Job.english_translation: *Hen pera'im* — the wild asses, which are trained in the wilderness to lie in wait for passers-by.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: They go forth to their work, seeking diligently for food
Job.english_translation: *Yatze'u fo'alam* — they go out to their work, and what is the work? *Meshacharei latref* — seeking to prey.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The desert yieldeth them bread for their children
Job.english_translation: *Aravah lo lechem lan'arim* — for the servants and youths of a wicked man, the plain and the wilderness become for him bread for their need, for from there he seizes and eats and plunders what they eat.
Job.translator_note: Rashi reads *na'arim* as “youths, servants”; JPS renders “children.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: for their children
Job.english_translation: *Lan'arim* — they are those who go with him to rob, like “save only that which the young men (*hane'arim*) have eaten” (Genesis 14:24).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 14:24”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: They cut his provender in the field
Job.english_translation: *Basadeh* — of others.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: his provender
Job.english_translation: *Belilo* — his produce.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: They cut
Job.english_translation: *Yiktzoru* — to rob.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And they despoil the vineyard of the wicked
Job.english_translation: *Vecherem rasha yelaktshu* — and the vineyards of others: these wicked ones take their fruit; *yelakeshu* — *asprayment* — they take their *leket* (late growth); *lekesh* is an expression of fruit growth, like “in the beginning of the shooting up of the latter growth (*halaket*)” (Amos 7:1) — Jonathan translated it “growth” (*tzimuach*), and so R. Eleazar composed (in the Hoshana “Adamah me'arer”) “*leket me'arbeh*” (another explanation: “*vecherem rasha yelaktshu*” — they will glean it from the destruction, for that of the poor and the orphans they eat; *yelaktshu* is like “and they opened their mouth wide as for the latter rain (*malkosh*)” a long time, and like *lekishya lelavan*).
Job.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Job 24:6 (“ils récoltent”), in forms such as אשפרויינטש and אשפרוייטנט; the printed form (אשפריימנ"ט) differs slightly. The reference “(in the Hoshana ‘Adamah me'arer’)” and the sentence in parentheses are later printed insertions (PI); the abbreviation ר"א is left as printed. The Aramaic *lekishya lelavan* is left as printed. Printed “Amos 7:1”; the second quotation is Job 29:23.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: They lie all night naked without clothing
Job.english_translation: *Arom yalinu* — they make the poor lodge [naked].

Job.english_lemma_JPS: without clothing
Job.english_translation: *Mibli levush* — for they took their garments.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: They are wet with the showers of the mountains
Job.english_translation: *Mizerem* — that comes down from the mountains: those naked ones are soaked and drenched, because without covering there is no shelter in which to take shelter.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And embrace the rock for want of a shelter
Job.english_translation: *Chibku tzur* — hiding in the clefts of the rocks, and even there the stream comes down and pours upon them and soaks them. *Ratov* is the Targum of *lach* (moist), and anyone who is not dried is called *lach*.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: They are wet
Job.english_translation: *Yirtavu* — *moyesta* in French.
Job.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: There are that pluck the fatherless from the breast
Job.english_translation: *Mishad yatom* — the nursing of the orphan, the place where his food and his sustenance come out, like “and thou shalt suck the breast of kings (*shod melachim*)” (Isaiah 60:16).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 60:16”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And take a pledge of the poor
Job.english_translation: *Yachbolu* — an expression of “If thou at all take to pledge (*chavol tachbol*)” (Exodus 22:25) and like “hath not taken aught to pledge (*chavol lo yachbol*)” (Ezekiel 18:16).
Job.translator_note: Printed references: Exodus 22:25, Ezekiel 18:16.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: So that they go about naked without clothing
Job.english_translation: *Halechu* — they made him walk without clothing.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And being hungry they carry the sheaves
Job.english_translation: *Ur'evim nasu omer* — and from the hungry they took the sheaves of gleaning. And it may further be interpreted: “and being hungry they carry the sheaves” — those who were carrying the sheaves, because these rob them from them, and they remained hungry.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: They make oil within the rows of these men
Job.english_translation: *Bein shurotam yatzhiru* — and they make oil: owners of olives.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: They tread their winepresses
Job.english_translation: *Veyekavim daruch* — owners of vineyards.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: and suffer thirst
Job.english_translation: *Vayitzmau* — after a time, because these wicked rob them of it.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: within the rows of these men
Job.english_translation: *Bein shurotam* — it seems to me that they arrange the olives in rows in the olive press, and the oil flows between them.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: From out of the populous city men groan
Job.english_translation: *Me'ir metim yin'aku* — its dead and its good ones, of the city, groan because of those acts of violence.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Yet God imputeth it not for unseemliness
Job.english_translation: *Lo yasim tiflah* — to take it to heart against them and to take vengeance.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: These are of them that rebel against the light
Job.english_translation: *Hemah* — these wicked are the generation of the Flood, who rebelled against the light, because of the rain that went up from the earth, and they had no need of anything.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The murderer riseth with the light
Job.english_translation: *La'or yakum* — if they stood by day, they would kill wayfarers.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And in the night he is as a thief
Job.english_translation: *Uvalailah yehi chaganav* — to dig through houses.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The eye also of the adulterer waiteth for the twilight
Job.english_translation: *Ve'ayin no'ef* — and the adulterer among them would watch and wait until twilight, saying, etc.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And he putteth a covering on his face
Job.english_translation: *Vesetter* — and in secret he puts a covering on his face to commit a transgression; for of all these the generation of the Flood were suspected: of robbery, as it is said, “and the earth was filled with violence” (Genesis 6:11), and of forbidden relations, as it is said, “for all flesh had corrupted their way” (ibid.).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 6:11”; “ibid.” is Genesis 6:12.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: In the dark they dig through houses; They shut themselves up in the day-time
Job.english_translation: *Yomam chatmu lamo* — those of them who were weak became robbers: by day they would dig through houses at night, and by day they were sealed and shut up in their houses.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: They know not the light
Job.english_translation: *Lo yade'u or* — they did not recognize the light, and it was not the time of their walking.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: For the shadow of death is to all of them as the morning
Job.english_translation: *Ki yachdav boker lamo tzalmavet* — for by day they were shut in, and at night they would go to their tunnel, and they did not fear the harmful beings at all.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: For they know the terrors of the shadow of death
Job.english_translation: *Ki yakir ballahot tzalmavet* — each one knew the demons that terrify, and was not afraid of them. And our Rabbis explained *yomam chatmu lamo*: by day they made marks where the cellar of the house was and where the treasuries of the rich man were, for they would deposit balsam with wealthy householders, and they knew that he would place it in his treasure house; and at night they would smell [it] and go there and dig there.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He is swift upon the face of the waters
Job.english_translation: When the righteous, Noah and Methuselah, were rebuking them and telling them that the Flood was destined to come upon them, they would say, “We are light for sailing on the water, and we have reeds and light things to make ships from and to sail.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Their portion is cursed in the earth; He turneth not by the way of the vineyards
Job.english_translation: *Tekullal chelkatam ba'aretz lo yifneh derech keramim* — they would curse their portion in the earth, saying, “Let not the way of good turn toward the ways of the righteous, the exalted ones who dwell in the height of the world.” Another version: *keramim* are the righteous and the leaders of the generation, like “And I will give her her vineyards (*karmeha*) from thence” (Hosea 2:17), Targum Jonathan *yat parnesaha*. They would curse their portion in the earth, saying, “Let them not turn (the way of good),” swearing that they would not turn their way. Another version: *tekullal chelkatam* — their portion was being corrupted, for they were destroying their seed in vain, like “for all flesh had corrupted (*hishchit*) their way” (Genesis 6:12). *Tekullal* is an expression of spoiling, like “that his sons did bring a curse upon themselves (*mekalelim lahem*)” (I Samuel 3:13). Another version: *tekullal chelkatam* — the generations after them curse by them: “He who punished the generation of the Flood,” כ"ש. Another version: *tekullal chelkatam lo yifneh derech keramim* — they did not accept rebuke from the good ones. Another explanation: they were swift to sail in ships to kill and to rob money, and the way of human settlement and the planting of vineyards they did not care to go.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally; the Aramaic is left as printed and the abbreviation כ"ש is left as printed. Rashi reads *karmeha* as “her leaders,” following Targum Jonathan; JPS renders “her vineyards.” Printed “I Samuel 3:13”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Drought and heat consume the snow waters
Job.english_translation: *Tziyah gam chom yigzelu* — on account of their wickedness they caused that one year the world was altered from its six orders: sowing and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: the snow waters
Job.english_translation: *Mimei sheleg* — like “and the waters of snow” — they too were taken away from the world; because the nether-world, they have sinned (*sheol chatau*). There are words lacking *vav*s, like “But I was like a docile lamb (*kekeves alluf*)” (Jeremiah 11:19), and it is interpreted *kekeves ve'alluf*; many more in the notebook of Menachem ben Saruk.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally. Printed “Jeremiah 11:19”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The womb forgetteth him
Job.english_translation: *Yishkachehu rechem* — his mother. Rabbi Tanchum expounded that the generation of the Flood would take their children and place them in their stead to stop up the openings of the deep, and even his mother had no pity on him.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: the worm feedeth sweetly on him
Job.english_translation: *Metaku rimmah* — to die, and for the worm to eat their flesh.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He shall be no more remembered
Job.english_translation: *Od lo yizacher* — in one year they were uprooted, and over the reprieve that was given them at the outset Job complained, that many died and did not see this punishment.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He devoureth the barren that beareth not; And doeth not good to the widow
Job.english_translation: *Ro'eh akarah lo teled* — such was their custom: he would marry two wives, one for conjugal use and one for children; the one who stood for conjugal use he would give to drink a cup of roots (*ikarin*) so that she would never bear, and he would feed her delicacies and bathe her and adorn her so that she would be beautiful, and the one who stood for children he would clothe in widow’s garments and starve. And this is what it says: the barren who would not bear he would shepherd and treat well, and the widow who stood for children he would not do good to.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He draweth away the mighty also by his power
Job.english_translation: *Umashach* — the Holy One, blessed be He, those mighty ones, with His strength, to punishment and to blotting out, from the reprieve that He extended to them.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He riseth up
Job.english_translation: *Yakum* — one day.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: and he trusteth not his own life
Job.english_translation: *Velo ya'amin bachayin* — like *bachayim*, “on the same day were all the fountains … broken up” (Genesis 7:11).
Job.translator_note: Translated literally. Printed “Genesis 7:11”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Though it be given him to be in safety, whereon he resteth
Job.english_translation: *Yiten lo lavetach* — until the day of their calamity, and they leaned.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: They are exalted for a little while, and they are gone
Job.english_translation: *Romu me'at* — they were removed from the world in almost a moment.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Yea, they are brought low
Job.english_translation: *Vehumeku* — they were crushed and became poor.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: they are gathered in as all others
Job.english_translation: *Kakol yikpetzun* — like all the rest who are gathered and escape at harvest and vintage and olive-gathering, who are gathered together; so they came to an end in a moment.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And if it be not so now, who will prove me a liar
Job.english_translation: *Ve'im lo efo* — as I said, one of you will come and call me a liar.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And make my speech nothing worth?
Job.english_translation: *Vayasem le'el milati* — for I reflect upon Him, to know His attributes: that He is long-suffering even to the wicked, and His lovers like me He chastises and does not put to death, as he complains (above, 23), “Because I was not cut off before the darkness”; and those who remove landmarks and did all these were not smitten with sufferings.
Job.translator_note: Printed “above 23” is Job 23:17.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Dominion and fear are with Him
Job.english_translation: (Bildad’s reply.) *Hamshel vafachad imo* — since Job said, “I would order my cause before Him,” he said to him: dominion and fear are with Him. “Dominion” is Michael, and “fear” is Gabriel; can you answer even one of them?
Job.translator_note: The source begins “(Bildad’s reply)” before the lemma.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He maketh peace in His high places
Job.english_translation: *Oseh shalom bimromav* — when the constellations rise, each one thinks, “I rise first,” because it does not see what is before it; therefore it is not jealous, כ"ש. Another version: *Oseh shalom bimromav* — fire and water are mixed, and the water does not extinguish the fire, כ"ש.
Job.translator_note: The abbreviation כ"ש is left as printed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: How then can man be just with God?
Job.english_translation: *Umah yitzdak* etc. — one born of woman, of whom you said, “When He hath tried me, I shall come forth as gold” (above, 23).
Job.translator_note: Printed “above 23” is Job 23:10.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: even the moon
Job.english_translation: *Ad yare'ach* — like “nor hath the lion passed (*adah*) thereby” (below, 28).
Job.translator_note: Rashi reads *ad* here as “passes over.” Printed “below 28” is Job 28:8.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: hath no brightness
Job.english_translation: *Velo ya'ahil* — like “shall not give their light (*yehallu*)” (Isaiah 13:10), and this *aleph* comes like “and thy heart to languish (*ule'adiv et nafshecha*)” (I Samuel 2:33), an extra *aleph*. Another version: *lo ya'ahil* — it will have no shade (*tzel*); when it does not give light, it has no shade; and the first appears [right], and I heard both.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally. Printed “Isaiah 13:10” and “I Samuel 2:33”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And whose spirit came forth from thee?
Job.english_translation: (Job’s reply.) *Unishmat mi yatz'ah mimecha* — who placed in you this spirit that comes out of your mouth? Who does not know this?
Job.translator_note: The source begins “(Job’s reply)” before the lemma.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: tremble
Job.english_translation: *Harefa'im* — Gehinnom, which weakens the creatures.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: tremble
Job.english_translation: *Yecholalu* — seven of its slain.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Beneath the waters and the inhabitants thereof
Job.english_translation: *Mitachat mayim veshochneihem* — in the depths of the depths, and also He.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The nether-world is naked before Him
Job.english_translation: To know and to see all that is within it.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And hangeth the earth over nothing
Job.english_translation: *Al belimah* — there is nothing at the foundation, for they stand in the air by the strength of the arms of the Holy One, blessed be He; and Dunash explained *belimah* as “level,” like “Whose mouth must be held in with bit and bridle (*livlom*)” (Psalms 32). (So I saw סא"א.)
Job.translator_note: it is left as printed. Printed “Psalms 32” is Psalms 32:9.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And the cloud is not rent under them
Job.english_translation: *Velo nivka anan* — never will its waters fall all together.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: under them
Job.english_translation: *Tachtam* — under the waters.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He closeth in the face of His throne
Job.english_translation: *Me'achaz* — with partitions, the face of the Throne of Glory, entire, such as “He made darkness His hiding-place” (ibid. 18).
Job.translator_note: Printed “ibid. 18” is Psalms 18:12.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And spreadeth His cloud upon it
Job.english_translation: *Parshez* — His cloud over the Throne, like “And over the heads of the living creatures there was the likeness of a firmament” (Ezekiel 1:22).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He hath described a boundary upon the face of the waters
Job.english_translation: *Chug chag* — *compas* in French, an expression of “and he marketh it out with the compasses (*uvamchugah*)” (Isaiah 44:13). He encircled it with sand, so that the (sand) would be for it an eternal boundary-law, and the sea would not pass that circle until light and darkness cease.
Job.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Job 22:14 (“cercle, compas”), in forms such as קונפט and קומפש; the printed form (קומפ"ש) matches, apart from the printed quotation mark.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The pillars of heaven tremble
Job.english_translation: *Yerofafu* — when He created them and congealed them, they were shaking, and He rebuked them and they stood in dryness and in strength.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And are astonished at His rebuke
Job.english_translation: *Vayitmahu* — wondering and going up (another version: as a man wondering and standing) in one place.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He stirreth up the sea with His power
Job.english_translation: *Raga hayam* — like “My skin closeth up (*raga*)” (above, 7): it was wrinkled into folds (so when He said, “Let the waters … be gathered together,” they were gathered from their spreading and wrinkled into folds) until they were gathered into one place prepared for them.
Job.translator_note: Rashi reads *raga* as “wrinkled”; JPS renders “stirreth up.” Printed “above 7” is Job 7:5. The sentence in parentheses is a later printed insertion (PI).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He smiteth through Rahab
Job.english_translation: *Machatz rahav* — Egypt is called Rahab.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: By His breath the heavens are serene
Job.english_translation: *Beruchu shamayim shifrah* — with His words and the breath of His mouth He spread them out, like “and he shall spread his royal pavilion (*shafrirô*)” (Jeremiah 42).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Jeremiah 42” is Jeremiah 43:10.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: His hand hath pierced the slant serpent
Job.english_translation: *Cholelah yado* — Pharaoh, who is called “the slant serpent” (Isaiah 27:1), an expression of pain and anguish; and so elsewhere, “Art thou not it that hewed Rahab in pieces, That pierced the dragon” (ibid. 51). Another version: His hand founded Leviathan, like “Before the hills was I brought forth (*cholalti*)” (Proverbs 8).
Job.translator_note: Printed “ibid. 51” is Isaiah 51:9; “Proverbs 8” is Proverbs 8:25.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Lo, these are but the outskirts of His ways
Job.english_translation: *Ketzot derachav* — light and few, compared with the rest of His greatness.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And how small a whisper is heard of Him!
Job.english_translation: *Umah shemetz davar nishma bo* — what hint of a matter can a man understand of His works? Another explanation: *shemetz* is like *lishmatzah* (“for reproach”), to disgrace.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And Job again took up his parable
Job.english_translation: *Vayosef* — his friends ceased answering when Elihu rebuked them, for “they stood still, and answered no more” (below, 32).
Job.translator_note: Printed “below 32” is Job 32:16.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: As God liveth, who hath taken away my right
Job.english_translation: *Chai El* — it is an oath, that in truth He removed my judgment. And from here Rabbi Joshua expounded that Job served the Omnipresent out of love: no man swears by the life of the king unless he loves the king.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Far be it from me that I should justify you
Job.english_translation: *Im atzdik etchem* — if I say that the judgment is with you, to condemn me.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Till I die I will not put away mine integrity from me
Job.english_translation: *Lo asir tummati* — I will not agree to your words by saying that I am not perfect.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: My righteousness I hold fast, and will not let it go
Job.english_translation: *Betzidkati hechezakti* — to say that I am righteous.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: My heart shall not reproach me so long as I live
Job.english_translation: *Lo yecheraf levavi* — me, from my days, from any way and measure that I conducted in my days; and against his will, let him be like the wicked, my enemy.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: For what is the hope of the godless, though he get him gain
Job.english_translation: *Ki mah tikvat chaneph* — for why should I be wicked and a robber? What is the end of a wicked man who robs money?

Job.english_lemma_JPS: When God taketh away his soul
Job.english_translation: *Ki yesheil* — when the Omnipresent casts his soul from upon him; an expression of “put off thy shoes (*shal na'alecha*)” (Exodus 3:5) and “and the head slippeth (*venashal*) from the helve” (Deuteronomy 19:5).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Exodus 3” is Exodus 3:5; “Deuteronomy 19” is Deuteronomy 19:5.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Will he have his delight in the Almighty
Job.english_translation: *Im al Shaddai yitanag* — it is a double question, like all double questions, for the way is the first with *he* and the second with *im*, like “Do horses run upon the rocks? Doth one plow there with oxen?” (Amos 6:12), “Is there injustice on my tongue? Cannot my taste discern crafty devices?” (above, 6). So also here: “Will God hear his cry? Will he have his delight in the Almighty?” — perhaps; or one who is wicked and godless, can he delight and rely on the salvation of the Holy One, blessed be He, and call upon Him in his time of trouble? — as a question.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally. Printed “above 6” is Job 6:30.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: I will teach you concerning the hand of God
Job.english_translation: *Oreh etchem* — what is the measure that is in the hand of God, and “the way that is with the Almighty I will not conceal,” like “For He knoweth the way that is with me (*imadi*)” (above, 23).
Job.translator_note: Printed “above 23” is Job 23:10; JPS renders “the way that I take.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Behold, all you yourselves have seen it
Job.english_translation: *Kulchem chazitem* — for this is the portion of a wicked man.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Why then are you become altogether vain?
Job.english_translation: *Velamah zeh hevel tehbalu* — to be wicked and flatterers.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: If his children be multiplied, it is for the sword
Job.english_translation: *Im yirbu banav lemo cherev* — they will multiply and die by sufferings and sicknesses, so that his widows rejoice at their death and do not weep.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And the innocent shall divide the silver
Job.english_translation: (*Vechesef naki* — the money of the wicked man, the Holy One, blessed be He, will divide to the innocent.)
Job.translator_note: The whole comment, including the lemma, is printed in parentheses (PI).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He buildeth his house as a moth, And as a booth which the keeper maketh
Job.english_translation: *Banah ke'ash* — like a worm that builds a hole that does not last, and like a booth that the keeper of the fig tree and the vineyard made, which is not permanent (another version: the guard of the vineyard who does not guard it at all times; this I heard סא"א).
Job.translator_note: it is left as printed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He lieth down rich, but there shall be nought to gather
Job.english_translation: *Ashir yishkav* — he will die in his wealth, and sometimes he is not gathered for burial.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Terrors overtake him like waters
Job.english_translation: *Ballahot* — demons.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: A tempest stealeth him away in the night
Job.english_translation: *Genavato sufah* — and it will cast him to abhorrences (*dera'onim*).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Yea, it hurleth at him, and spareth not
Job.english_translation: *Vayashlech alav* — the one who casts evil upon him and does not spare.
