Job.english_lemma_JPS: He would fain flee from its power
Job.english_translation: *Miyado* — of the wicked, and from his strength and from his place.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He would fain flee from its power
Job.english_translation: *Baruach yivrach* — his counsellor, who helped him at first, will flee from helping his hand in the hour of his failure, as Harbonah did to Haman (Megillah 16a).
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Men shall clap their hands at him
Job.english_translation: *Yispok alemo kapemo* — those who knew (him) beforehand and now see his breaking.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: For there is a mine for silver
Job.english_translation: *Ki yesh lakesef motza* — this too is another reason for his first statement, which he said, “My righteousness I hold fast”: why should I be wicked, if for silver and gold — for everything there is a source and an end; but wisdom, from where does it come? This is the end of the section: it is more precious than all; therefore all my days I set my heart to it, to learn.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And a place for gold which they refine
Job.english_translation: *Umakom* — there is [a place] for gold, from which they refine and melt it.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And brass is molten out of the stone
Job.english_translation: *Ve'even yatzuk nechushah* — from the mountain the craftsman casts the copper; behold, there is a beginning and an end to everything, for the whole world will come to an end and all that is in it.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Man setteth an end to darkness
Job.english_translation: *Ketz sam* — the Omnipresent: when will the darkness be, for the heavens will be dissolved and the earth will wear out, and to every end of a thing He searches.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The stones of thick darkness and of the shadow of death
Job.english_translation: *Even* — from which darkness and the shadow of death went out for him; a stone is the place from which punishment issues; therefore it is called “stone” in a place of punishment, like a man who stubs his feet on a stone and has pain, כ"ש; like “and the plummet of emptiness (*avnei vohu*)” (Isaiah 34:11) and “for that thou sawest that a stone was cut out of the mountain” (Daniel 4).
Job.translator_note: The Aramaic quotation is translated as printed; the abbreviation כ"ש is left as printed. Printed “Daniel 4”: the Aramaic words occur in Daniel 2:45, and I could not confirm the printed chapter.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He breaketh open a shaft away from where men sojourn
Job.english_translation: *Paratz nachal* — upon Sodom and Gomorrah, streams of fire and brimstone.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: away from where men sojourn
Job.english_translation: *Me'im gar* — from the place that gushes and flows.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: They are forgotten of the foot that passeth by
Job.english_translation: *Hanishkachim mini regel* — these are the people of Sodom, who caused the law of the feet of guests to be forgotten from their land, for they would lay the guest on a bed; if he was longer, they cut off his legs, and if he was shorter, they stretched him; so it is explained in the Aggadah.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: They hang afar from men
Job.english_translation: *Dallu* — through the bursting of this stream, and from man they moved.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: As for the earth, out of it cometh bread
Job.english_translation: *Eretz* — out of which bread comes: its place was overturned like fire.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The stones thereof are the place of sapphires
Job.english_translation: *Mekom sapir* — its stones were.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: That path no bird of prey knoweth
Job.english_translation: *Lo yade'u ayit* — no army of robbers passed over them.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Neither hath the falcon’s eye seen it
Job.english_translation: *Velo shezafato ein ayah* — for it sees more than other birds, and therefore it is called *ra'ah*, for it stands in Babylon and sees carcasses in the Land of Israel; so it is explained in the Aggadah (Chullin 63a) — that is, spies did not dig it out.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The proud beasts have not trodden it
Job.english_translation: *Lo adah alav* — passed over, as we translate “that passed between these pieces” (Genesis 15) (it should be *hagezarim*; see the Targum) *de'ada*.
Job.translator_note: The parenthetical is a later printed insertion (PI); the Aramaic is left as printed. Printed “Genesis 15” is Genesis 15:17.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Nor hath the lion passed thereby
Job.english_translation: *Shachatz veshachal* — [these] are of the seven names of the lion (in Sanhedrin 95); there are six names of the lion, and what did the Holy One, blessed be He, do?
Job.translator_note: Translated literally; the reference is left as printed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He putteth forth his hand upon the flinty rock
Job.english_translation: *Bachalamish shalach yado* — and He overturned the roots of the mountains from above to below.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He cutteth out channels among the rocks; And his eye seeth every precious thing
Job.english_translation: *Batzurot ye'orim bika* — he returns to the beginning of his subject, when he said, “for everything there is a source”: “among the rocks He cut channels” for the source of the streams; and so “his eye seeth every precious thing” — from where it came out for the creatures (as He did for Israel: smote the rock and its waters gushed out).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He bindeth the streams that they trickle not
Job.english_translation: *Mibchi neharot chavash* — at the creation of the world, when the lower waters wept; *bechi* is like “the springs of the sea (*nivchei yam*)” (Job 39).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Job 39” is Job 38:16.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He bindeth the streams
Job.english_translation: *Chavash* — like “and saddled (*vayachavosh*) his ass” (Genesis 22:3), כ"ש. (Another version: *mibchi* etc. — on account of the weeping of Israel, who were weeping, saying, “What shall we drink?” He bound and prepared for them rivers of water from the rock; and *vayachavosh lahem* the Targum translates *ve'atkin*.)
Job.translator_note: The abbreviation כ"ש is left as printed. The sentence in parentheses is a later printed insertion (PI). The Aramaic is translated as printed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And the thing that is hid bringeth he forth to light
Job.english_translation: *Ve'ta'alumah yotzi or* — there is a window in the firmament and its name is *ta'alumah*; from there come the sources of the sun for its season (in Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer). That is, everything has a source and an end, only wisdom has no source except from His mouth, and no end of worlds.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: But wisdom, where shall it be found?
Job.english_translation: *Vehachochmah* — the Torah.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Neither is it found in the land of the living
Job.english_translation: [It is found] not in one who gives himself life, but in one who puts himself to death over it, with toil and hunger.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The deep saith: ‘It is not in me’
Job.english_translation: *Tehom amar lo vi hi* — if you ask those who descend to the deep, who engage in finding pearls and finding gold and silver from the place of the depths of the earth, they will say to you, “It is not in me — I am not expert in teaching.” (Shabbat 89a, see there carefully [ע"ש היטב] וצ"ע.)
Job.translator_note: The words in parentheses are a later printed insertion (PI); the abbreviation צ"ע is left as printed. ע"ש היטב is read as “see there carefully” (*iyyun sham*) because it follows a Talmud reference; flagged as my reading.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And the sea saith: ‘It is not with me.’
Job.english_translation: *Vayam amar* — and those who go down to the sea for trade will say to you, “Wisdom is not with me.” Why? Because they cannot acquire it like other merchandise, to give of their wealth as its price. And in the Aggadah it says that at the giving of the Torah, Satan came before the Holy One, blessed be He, and said to Him, “Where is the Torah?” He said to him, “With the son of Amram.” He came to Moses [and] said to him, “Where is the Torah?” [He said,] “With the sea.” He came to the sea [and] said to it, “Where is the Torah?” “It is not in me; go to the son of Amram.” He came to the son of Amram [and] said to him, “Where is the Torah?” [He said,] “With the deep.” He came to the deep [and] said to it, “Where is the Torah?” It said to him, “It is not with me; go to the son of Amram.” He came to the son of Amram [and] said to him, “Where is the Torah?” [He said,] “With the Holy One, blessed be He.” And this is what it says: “The deep saith: ‘It is not in me,’” and “the sea saith: ‘It is not with me.’”
Job.translator_note: Translated literally; the speakers’ replies are not marked in the printed text, and the words in square brackets are supplied.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: It cannot be gotten for gold
Job.english_translation: *Lo yuttan segor* — *zahav sagur* is good gold, for at the time it opens, all the shops of gold close.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: It cannot be valued with the gold of Ophir
Job.english_translation: *Lo tesulah* — will not be praised; an expression of “Extol (*solu*) Him that rideth upon the skies” (Psalms 68:5): the one who praises it by saying that it is as valuable as the gold of Ophir and as the precious onyx — it is no praise for it; and so “Comparable (*hamesulaim*) to fine gold” (Lamentations 4).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Lamentations 4” is Lamentations 4:2.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Gold and glass cannot equal it
Job.english_translation: *Zahav* — pure, shining like a pearl.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Neither shall the exchange thereof be vessels of fine gold
Job.english_translation: *Utmuratah* etc. — and its exchange [is] not with vessels of fine gold.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: No mention shall be made of coral or of crystal
Job.english_translation: *Ra'amot vegavish* — names of precious stones that are in the sea.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: No mention shall be made
Job.english_translation: *Lo yizacher* — beside it.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The topaz of Ethiopia shall not equal it
Job.english_translation: *Pitdat Kush* — a precious stone, like *odem*, *pitdah*. *Ketem* is a cluster of ornaments for women’s jewellery, and the cluster is called *ketem* in the Hebrew language, and in the Arabic language *al-chali*, and it is a gold ring, and “an ornament of fine gold (*chali ketem*)” (Proverbs 25:12), and so “and decked herself with her ear-rings and her jewels (*chelyatah*)” (Hosea 2:15). And some interpret *ketem* as “crown,” but it is not correct, for we do not find an action in this language, as we find in the language of *keter*, *machtir kotarot*.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally. Printed references: Proverbs 25:12, Hosea 2:15.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And kept close from the fowls of the air
Job.english_translation: *Ume'of hashamayim* — flying angels.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Destruction and Death say: ‘We have heard a rumor thereof with our ears.’
Job.english_translation: *Avaddon vamavet amru* — those who destroy and put themselves to death over it said, “With our ears we heard a rumor of it,” for the one who toils in it, it endures with him. And some say, as in the Aggadah that I explained above, that Satan came before the Omnipresent [and] said to Him, “Where is the Torah?” He said to him, etc., and that is what is written: “Destruction and Death say: ‘We have heard a rumor thereof with our ears’” — when it was given to Israel. But:
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: God understandeth the way thereof, And He knoweth the place thereof
Job.english_translation: *Elohim hevin darkah* — for He knows where it dwells; and also they will praise it and say of it, “For God understandeth the way thereof”: He looked into it and created the world with the letters in their order, and by their weight formed all the creatures, as is written in the Secret of Sefer Yetzirah.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: For He looketh to the ends of the earth, And seeth under the whole heaven
Job.english_translation: *Ki hu liktzot ha'aretz yabit* — in it, how He would build them and create them; and under all the heavens He saw in it the needs of their creation.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: When He maketh a weight for the wind, And meteth out the waters by measure
Job.english_translation: *La'asot* etc. — in it, a weight for the wind, to every land according to its strength; and likewise the waters by measure, according to what the land needed to be watered: there is a dry land that needs much rain, and there is a land that does not need so much.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: When He made a decree for the rain, And a way for the storm of thunders
Job.english_translation: *Chok* — a decree set for all lands, and a spring and a stream to water each and every land; and “when He made a way for the thunderbolts,” so that two sounds should not come out through one opening, lest it destroy the world.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Then did He see it
Job.english_translation: *Az ra'ah* — He saw it, looked into it, and by its counsel He makes everything.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: and declare it
Job.english_translation: *Vayesapperah* — He counted its letters, doubled and single, first and middle and final: it is *emet* (truth), the seal of the Holy One, blessed be He; and so in the other orders He created each and every thing with these letters, and all is explained in the Secret of Sefer Yetzirah.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He established it, yea, and searched it out
Job.english_translation: *Hechinah* — He prepared it for creation.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Behold, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom
Job.english_translation: *Hen yirat Adonai hi chochmah* — this needs that, and wisdom is not good without fear.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Oh that I were as in the months of old
Job.english_translation: (Job’s reply.) *Mi yitteni keyarchei kedem* — as the ancient days when I was in my greatness.
Job.translator_note: The source begins “(Job’s reply)” before the lemma.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: When His lamp shined above my head
Job.english_translation: *Behilo nero* — an expression of light and gladness.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And by His light I walked through darkness
Job.english_translation: *Le'oro* — I was walking in every darkness and trouble that came to the world; for me there was light.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: As I was in the days of my youth
Job.english_translation: *Bimei chorpi* — in the days of my earliness; it is an Aramaic expression, *chorpi* and *apli*.
Job.translator_note: The Aramaic is translated as printed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: When the converse of God was upon my tent
Job.english_translation: *Besod Eloha ali oholi* — when the upright of the generation would come to my tent to be established in the words of the Holy One, blessed be He, in the Torah, and in making a fence for the hour.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And my children were about me
Job.english_translation: *Na'arai* — my servants.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: When my steps were washed with utter
Job.english_translation: *Halichai* — my feet.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: When my steps were washed with utter
Job.english_translation: *Bacheimah* — like *bechem'ah* (butter).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And the rock poured me out rivers of oil!
Job.english_translation: *Vetzur yatzuk imadi palgei shamen* — that is, contentment and every desire of the heart, which flow like streams of oil.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: poured me out
Job.english_translation: *Yatzuk* — like *veyatzakta*.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: When I went forth to the gate unto the city
Job.english_translation: *Kiryat* — a high roof, prepared like a seat for the elders of the city to sit.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: When I prepared my seat in the broad place
Job.english_translation: *Barechov* etc. — and when I was preparing my seat in the broad place.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The young men saw me and hid themselves
Job.english_translation: *Ra'uni ne'arim* — they feared me and hid, and the aged stood up before me.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The princes refrained talking
Job.english_translation: *Sarim atzru bemillim* — and they hoped that I would open first.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: For when the ear heard me, then it blessed me
Job.english_translation: *Ki ozen* — which heard my word and called me happy.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And when the eye saw me, it gave witness unto me
Job.english_translation: *Ve'ayin ra'atah* — everywhere, in my greatness and the rightness of my measure.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The blessing of him that was ready to perish came upon me
Job.english_translation: *Birkat oved* — a man who died through his iniquity and was driven out.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The blessing of him that was ready to perish came upon me
Job.english_translation: *Alai tavo* — for I would sustain his sons and his wife. And our Rabbis said that he would rob the field of orphans and improve it and return it to them; and the plain sense of the verse does not appear so, for nothing is called *oved* but something that is itself lost, like “a useless vessel (*kikli oved*)” (Psalms 31:13), and so “I have gone astray like a lost sheep (*kese oved*)” (ibid. 119), “lost sheep (*tzon ovdot*)” (Jeremiah 20).
Job.translator_note: Printed “ibid. 119” is Psalms 119:176; “Jeremiah 20” is Jeremiah 50:6.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: and I caused the widow’s heart to sing for joy
Job.english_translation: *Velev almanah aranin* — for he would put his name upon widows, saying, “She is my relative,” or “I will marry her,” so that claimants would leap upon her.
Job.translator_note: The sense of *yikpetzu aleha* (literally “would leap upon her”) is uncertain; it may mean that claimants would draw back.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: I put on righteousness, and it clothed itself with me; My justice was as a robe and a diadem
Job.english_translation: *Tzedek lavashti vayilbashseni* — I pursued righteousness and it was found for me like a robe and a turban, which are handsome ornaments; so my judgment was handsome and pure.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Then I said: ‘I shall die with my nest
Job.english_translation: *Va'omar im kini egva* — on account of the rightness of my measure, I used to say in my heart, when I die, my nest and my house will be established with me.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And I shall multiply my days as the phoenix
Job.english_translation: *Vechol arbeh yamim* — a bird whose name is *chol*, on which death was not decreed because it did not taste of the Tree of Knowledge; and at the end of a thousand years it is renewed and returns to its youth.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: My root shall be spread out to the waters
Job.english_translation: *Shorshi patuach* etc. — all this I used to say in my heart: that my root would not dry up and my harvest would not die, like “and put forth boughs (*ve'asah katzir*)” (above, 14), and they are the soft suckling branches of a tree. And I said:
Job.translator_note: Printed “above 14” is Job 14:9.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: My glory shall be fresh in me
Job.english_translation: *Shekevodi* — will be renewed with me always.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And my bow shall be renewed in my hand
Job.english_translation: *Veshashti* — and my strength it will renew always for the better.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Unto me men gave ear, and waited
Job.english_translation: *Li shame'u vayyachallu* — those who heard my words hoped that they would be fulfilled, and they were fulfilled, for the tradition of wisdom was in my hand.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And my speech dropped upon them
Job.english_translation: *Tatof millati* — an expression of prophecy, and so “and preach not (*lo tatif*) against the house of Isaac” (Amos 7:16); that is, my word was like prophecy.
Job.translator_note: Printed “Amos 7:16”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And they opened their mouth wide as for the latter rain
Job.english_translation: *Lemalkosh* — for a long time they were speaking, for most of their hours was silence, for they longed to hear my words.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: If I laughed on them, they believed it not
Job.english_translation: *Lo ya'aminu* — that I am jesting with them, because of my importance.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And the light of my countenance they cast not down
Job.english_translation: *Ve'or panai lo yapilun* — they were afraid to approach me and to exalt their heart against me.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: I chose out their way, and sat as chief
Job.english_translation: *Evchar darkam* — all their ways and their counsel I used to choose for them, for they would ask me, “Which way shall we go and what shall we do?”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: and sat as chief
Job.english_translation: *Ve'esheiv rosh* — if they were reclining, I would recline at the head of those reclining.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Yea, the strength of their hands, whereto should it profit me?
Job.english_translation: *Gam ko'ach yedeihem lamah* — it was for me in those days; they were wicked and there was no profit in them, for punishment came through them.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Men in whom ripe age is perished
Job.english_translation: *Alemo avad chelach* — old age.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: They are gaunt with want and famine
Job.english_translation: *Bechesed uvechafan* — they were solitary.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: They gnaw the dry ground
Job.english_translation: *Ha'orekim tziyah* — for they drive them away in his days from the midst of people, to go in darkness.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: in the gloom of wasteness and desolation
Job.english_translation: *Emesh sho'ah umesho'ah* — *bro'ina* in French.
Job.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Job 30:3 (“destruction”), in forms such as ברייונא and בריניאה; the printed form (ברואינ"א) is a variant spelling.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: They pluck salt-wort with wormwood
Job.english_translation: *Hakotfim malu'ach alei siach* — when they were in the wildernesses they would pluck for themselves *malluchim* from the trees of the forests and eat; *malu'ach* is the name of a plant, and in the Aramaic language it is called *kakulin*, and in the language of the Mishnah *malluchim*, *moots* in French, like that which we learned (Kiddushin 66a): “They brought up *malluchim* on tables of gold.”
Job.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Job 30:4 (“sorte d’herbe amère croissant sur les arbres des forêts”), in forms such as מושא; the printed form (מצו"ש) differs slightly.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: wormwood
Job.english_translation: *Siach* — a tree, like “under one of the shrubs (*achad hasichim*)” (Genesis 21).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 21” is Genesis 21:15.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: They are driven forth from the midst of men
Job.english_translation: *Min gev* — from the midst of the city they were driven out.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: In the clefts of the valleys must they dwell
Job.english_translation: *Be'arutz nechalim* — there is a salty land that cracks open, where they would lie in holes of the dust and holes of the clefts of the rocks.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: In holes of the earth and of the rocks
Job.english_translation: *Vechafim* — the Targum of *sela'im* (rocks). (Another explanation: *be'arutz nechalim* — it is the cleft that the stream makes around itself.)
Job.translator_note: The sentence in parentheses is a later printed insertion (PI).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Under the nettles they are gathered together
Job.english_translation: *Charul yesupachu* — *orshi'ash* in French; they were gathered, like “and they shall cleave (*venispechu*) to the house of Jacob” (Isaiah 14:1).
Job.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter at this verse; left as printed. Darmesteter has an entry “orties” (nettles) in this passage whose verse number is garbled in the scanned text; I did not rely on it. Printed “Isaiah 14:1”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: They were scourged out of the land
Job.english_translation: *Nechu'u* — in my days, from the land, in that I used to lower them; an expression of *nechei ruach* (“smitten of spirit”).
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: For He hath loosed my cord, and afflicted me
Job.english_translation: *Ki yitri* — He loosed the string of my bow, He loosed (as I said above, “and my bow shall be renewed”), that is: He weakened my strength, He in whose hand it is to do so.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And they have cast off the bridle before me
Job.english_translation: *Verasan mipanai shillechu* — my bridles, with which they had been bridled by me, they sent away from before me, for they no longer fear me.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Upon my right hand rise the brood
Job.english_translation: *Al yamin* — on my right stand little sprouts, like other common folk, for I am not important in their eyes, to submit before me.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: They entangle my feet
Job.english_translation: *Raglai shillechu* — if the place is narrow for them, they push me farther.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And they cast up against me their ways of destruction
Job.english_translation: *Vayasollu alai orchot eidam* — any wicked way that they have to do, they make their highway before me and beside me, and they do not fear.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: They break up my path
Job.english_translation: *Nattesu netivati* — the good, and they pay no heed to it; *nattesu* is like *nattetzu*, and a *samech* is interchanged with a *tzadi*.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally; the first word of the explanation is printed abbreviated and is uncertain.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: They further my calamity
Job.english_translation: *Lehavvati yo'ilu* — they add to provoke me.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: As through a wide breach they come
Job.english_translation: *Keferetz rachav* — as in a fence where all come and pass through there, so they come together upon me to put me to shame.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: In the midst of the ruin they roll themselves upon me
Job.english_translation: *Tachat sho'ah hitgalgalu* — that is, they roll and come in secret until they reach me to provoke me, so that I not slip away from them.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Terrors are turned upon me
Job.english_translation: *Hohpach alai* — is turned upon me.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Terrors are turned upon me
Job.english_translation: *Ballahot* — demons.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: They chase mine honour as the wind
Job.english_translation: *Tirdof karuach* — evil.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: mine honour
Job.english_translation: *Et nedivati* — the noble spirit that rested upon me at the start.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And now my soul is poured out within me
Job.english_translation: *Ve'attah* — to this trouble my soul is poured out, like a man whose spirit is troubled, for they seize me and force me to lower my soul.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Days of affliction have taken hold upon me
Job.english_translation: *Yemei oni* — in which I am.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: In the night my bones are pierced
Job.english_translation: *Nikkar* — like “wilt thou put out the eyes of these men (*ha'einei ha'anashim hahem tenakker*)?” (Numbers 16:14); *nikkar* — *fourier* in French: the worms peck my flesh from my bones.
Job.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Job 30:17 (“(la nuit) perce”), in forms such as פורייר and פורקייר; the printed form (פוריי"ר) matches the first, apart from the printed quotation mark. Printed “Numbers 16:14”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And my sinews take no rest
Job.english_translation: *Ve'orkai* — my sinews have no rest. *Gid* (sinew) in the Arabic language is *orek*; so Dunash explained. Another version: *orkai* — my pursuers, who drive me away.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: By the great force [of my disease] is my garment disfigured
Job.english_translation: *Yitchapes levushi* — my garment changes, scab after scab, as when a man takes off his clothes and puts on other clothes different from the first ones, they are called *bigdei chofesh*, like “disguised himself, and went into the battle” (I Kings 22), and it is translated *ishtani*.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally. The Aramaic *ishtani* is left as printed. Printed “I Kings 22” is I Kings 22:30.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: It bindeth me about as the collar of my coat
Job.english_translation: *Kefi khutonti ya'azreni* — that girds and encircles my neck; so my garment girds me round about on every side.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He hath cast me into the mire
Job.english_translation: *Horani lachomer* — *horani*: the boil teaches me to sit as in clay, as we said (above, 2), “and he sat among the ashes.” Another explanation: *horani lachomer* means “cast me,” an expression of “hath He cast (*yarah*) into the sea” (Exodus 15).
Job.translator_note: Printed “above 2” is Job 2:8; “Exodus 15” is Exodus 15:4.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And I am become like dust and ashes
Job.english_translation: *Ve'itmashal* — I became like; and in Midrash Rabbi Tanchuma, Rabbi Berechiah said: he reversed the verse: “I was compared to Abraham in my righteousness, who called himself ‘dust and ashes’ (Genesis 11), and He judges me like the wicked of the generation of the Dispersion (who rebelled against Him in the building of the Tower), of whom it is written, ‘and slime had they for mortar’ (ibid. 11).”
Job.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 11” for “dust and ashes” is Genesis 18:27; “ibid. 11” is Genesis 11:3.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: I stand up, and Thou lookest at me
Job.english_translation: *Amadti* — to see, to be silent and to understand, like “and as he opened it, all the people stood, and answered no more” (Nehemiah 8:5).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Nehemiah 8:5”; the last words (“and answered no more”) are not in that verse (compare Job 32:16).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: I stand up, and Thou lookest at me
Job.english_translation: *Vattitbonen bi* — He devises against me to change my plagues.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Thou liftest me up to the wind
Job.english_translation: *Tisa'eni el ruach* — demons.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Thou causest me to ride upon it; And Thou dissolvest my substance
Job.english_translation: *Tarkiveni utemogeggeni tushiyah* — weakness and ebbing of strength was that which dissolved me.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And Thou dissolvest my substance
Job.english_translation: *Utemogeggeni tushiyah* — feminine, and it depends on *tushiyah*; and this *tav* is not like the *tav* of *tisa'eni*.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: For I know that Thou wilt bring me to death
Job.english_translation: *Ki yadati* — for I knew that You would return me to death, a place appointed for all living, in the grave.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Surely none shall put forth his hand to a ruinous heap
Job.english_translation: *Ach lo vi* — and in destruction the judge was accustomed to stretch out his hand, like *i hasadeh* (“a heap of the field”).
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Neither because of these things shall help come in one’s calamity
Job.english_translation: *Im befido* — if He would send *pid*, which is a breaking, upon His creatures.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Neither because of these things
Job.english_translation: *Lahen shua* — He would soothe with consolations somewhat; and so our Rabbis explained: the Holy One, blessed be He, does not smite a nation and leave [another] sitting at its side, but brings calamity upon this one and soothes it with the company of the other that was already smitten, and it is comforted by it: He brought calamity upon Assyria and soothed with Egypt, as it is said, “Art thou better than No-amon” (Nahum 3:8); He brought calamity upon Egypt and soothed with Assyria, as it is said, “Behold, Assyria in Lebanon” (Ezekiel 31); and it may further be interpreted: *lahen shua* — prayer and supplication are effective for them.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally. Rashi’s printed quotation from Ezekiel 31:3 is abbreviated; the verse reads “Behold, the Assyrian was a cedar in Lebanon.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: If I have not wept for him that was in trouble
Job.english_translation: *Im lo vachiti liksheh yom* — He knows and recognizes whether I was not merciful and weeping over the poor, hard of day, and my soul grieved for the needy, for over all these this has come upon me.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Yet, when I looked for good, there came evil
Job.english_translation: *Ki tov kivviti* etc. — that is: for this recompense is fitting for me.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Mine inwards boil, and rest not
Job.english_translation: *Velo damu* — they cannot be silent and still.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: I go mourning without the sun
Job.english_translation: *Bli chamah* — the sun did not gaze on me, and behold, I am dark.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: I am become a brother to jackals
Job.english_translation: *Ach hayiti letannim* etc. — the jackals and the ostriches are engaged in weeping all their days.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And my bones are burned with heat
Job.english_translation: *Charah* — an expression of something that is parched and dries from the heat of the fire, like “The bellows are burned (*nachar mapuach*)” (Jeremiah 6:29) and “the midst of it is burned (*nachar*)” (Ezekiel 15:4).
Job.translator_note: Rashi reads *nachar* in both verses as “burned”; JPS renders Jeremiah 6:29 “The bellows blow fiercely” and Ezekiel 15:4 “the midst of it is singed.” Printed references: Jeremiah 6:29, Ezekiel 15:4.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: I made a covenant with mine eyes
Job.english_translation: *Berit karati le'einai* — not to look at a married woman.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: How then should I look upon a maid?
Job.english_translation: *Umah etbonen al betulah* — what is it to me to look at her? Such was my piety, not to set an eye even on an unmarried woman, lest after some days she be married and I be found bound after her. So it is explained in Avot de-Rabbi Natan.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: For what would be the portion of God from above
Job.english_translation: *Umah chelek* etc. — that He repaid me thus.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Is it not calamity to the unrighteous
Job.english_translation: *Halo eid la'avval* — for him it is fitting, and not for me.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And disaster to the workers of iniquity
Job.english_translation: *Venechar* — like “But thou shouldest not have gazed on the day of thy brother in the day of his disaster (*nochro*)” (Obadiah 1:12).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And count all my steps
Job.english_translation: *Vechol tze'adai yispor* — and He sees whether I walked with vanity.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And my foot hath hasted to deceit
Job.english_translation: *Vatachash* — and hasted, like “I will hasten it (*achishenah*)” (Isaiah 60) and “for it is speedily gone (*gaz chish*)” (Psalms 90).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 60” is Isaiah 60:22; “Psalms 90” is Psalms 90:10.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And if any spot hath cleaved to my hands
Job.english_translation: *Me'um* — it is *mum* (blemish), something of taint; and this *aleph* is written but not read, in the Masorah Gedolah, and it is from the root of “you shall not gather (*lo ta'asifun*)”: if I did this, I would deserve that this curse should come upon me.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Then let me sow, and let another eat
Job.english_translation: *Ezra'ah v'acher yochal vetze'etza'ai yeshorashu* — the roots will be uprooted.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And I have lain in wait at my neighbour’s door
Job.english_translation: To his wife may he return to me my recompense.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Then let my wife grind unto another
Job.english_translation: *Titchan le'acher ishti* — our Rabbis explained it as an expression of marital relations, like “and he did grind (*tochen*) in the prison-house” (Judges 16:21).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Judges 16:21”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: For that were a heinous crime
Job.english_translation: *Ki hi* — lewdness, and I was afraid, if I did [it], for it is an iniquity for judges, an iniquity for which a judgment of sufferings fittingly comes through it.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: root out all mine increase
Job.english_translation: *Uvechol tevu'ati tesharesh* — this fire; therefore I refrained from doing [it]. When it speaks in the language of uprooting it says תשרש, and in the language of root it says תשרש, and so ישורשו is an expression of uprooting, ישרשו an expression of root.
Job.translator_note: The printed text spells the two forms identically (תשרש); the vocalisation is not shown.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: What then shall I do when God riseth up?
Job.english_translation: *Umah e'eseh* etc. — this I set to my heart: and if He should visit my ways, what shall I answer Him?

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And did not One fashion us in the womb?
Job.english_translation: *Vaychonenu varachem* — I in the belly of my mother, and he in the belly of his mother: one Maker formed us.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Or have caused the eyes of the widow to fail
Job.english_translation: *Achalleh* — that I did not fulfil her desire, which is the “failing of the eyes”: one who desires and does not obtain is called “failing of the eyes.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Nay, from my youth he grew up with me as with a father
Job.english_translation: *Ki mine'urai gedelani* — this capability, like a father who raised me and taught me; so we learned the uprightness of my heart from my youth.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And I have been her guide from my mother’s womb
Job.english_translation: *Umibeten immi anchennah* — this trait.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Then let my shoulder fall from the shoulder-blade
Job.english_translation: *Mishichmah* — it is the width of the shoulder.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And mine arm be broken from the bone
Job.english_translation: *Mikaneh* — it is the upper bone, round like a reed (*kaneh*), and because it is round like a reed, he calls it so.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: For calamity from God was a terror to me
Job.english_translation: *Ki pachad elai* etc. — the calamity that He brings on the wicked was a terror in my eyes; therefore I ceased to do [it].

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And by reason of His majesty I could do nothing
Job.english_translation: *Umissa'to* — and from His weightiness.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: If I have made gold my hope
Job.english_translation: *Kislai* — like “Whose confidence (*kislo*) is gossamer” (above, 8): my hope and my thought; and because the kidneys are upon the loins (*kesalayim*) and the kidneys counsel, thought is called *kesel*.
Job.translator_note: Printed “above 8” is Job 8:14.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And have said to the fine gold
Job.english_translation: *Velaketem* — clusters of gold and treasures.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Thou art my confidence
Job.english_translation: *Amarti mivtachi* — to strengthen themselves with them against the poor.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: If I rejoiced because my wealth was great
Job.english_translation: *Im esmach ki rav chaili* — I was not accustomed to display gladness in the presence of the poor on account of my wealth, so as not to make them jealous of me.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: If I beheld the sun when it shined
Job.english_translation: *Im er'eh or ki yahel* — the sun in the period of its might and brightness.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Or the moon walking in brightness
Job.english_translation: *Veyare'ach yakar holech* — shining and going, like “*or yekarot*” (Zechariah 14:6), “*kiyekar karim*” (Psalms 37).
Job.translator_note: JPS renders Zechariah 14:6 “there shall not be light, But heavy clouds and thick” and Psalms 37:20 “as the fat of lambs.” Printed “Psalms 37” is Psalms 37:20.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And my heart hath been secretly enticed
Job.english_translation: To the sun and to the moon, saying that they are divinities, like some of the star-worshippers, the outcast, (who worship) all the host of heaven.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Yea, I suffered not my mouth to sin By asking his life with a curse
Job.english_translation: *Velo natati lachato chikki* — to provoke my enemy and to claim from him money that I have no claim to, in order to make him swear, and to ask with curses the life of my enemy.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Who can find one that hath not been satisfied with his meat?
Job.english_translation: *Lo sava* — out of the hatred with which they hated me for troubling them with the receiving of guests.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: My doors I opened to the roadside
Job.english_translation: *Le'orach* — the doors of my house were not inner ones, surrounded by a gatehouse outside, or turned at the corners of an angle, to prevent guests from coming, but open to the wayside, for anyone who came to come in.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: By hiding mine iniquity in my bosom
Job.english_translation: *Bechobbi* — in my hiding-place.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Because I feared the great multitude
Job.english_translation: *Ki e'erotz* — at first I was subduing a great multitude of the wicked, and now even among the Chaldeans — “this people was not” (Isaiah 23:13).
Job.translator_note: Translated literally. Printed “Isaiah 23:13”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: terrified me
Job.english_translation: *Yechitteni* — from my fear.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Lo, here is my signature, let the Almighty answer me
Job.english_translation: *Hen tavi Shaddai ya'aneni* — would that the Omnipresent testify concerning me in judgment, as He said of me, “that there is none like him in the earth, a whole-hearted and an upright man, one that feareth God” (above, 1); Moses too, who wrote his book, and my book would testify of me. (Another explanation) so was Job saying: Let there be given to mark me and my uprightness.
Job.translator_note: The words “(Another explanation)” are a later printed insertion (PI). Printed “above 1” is Job 1:8.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: let the Almighty answer me
Job.english_translation: *Shaddai ya'aneni* — to this request.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: the indictment which mine adversary hath written
Job.english_translation: *Vesefer katav ish rivi* — let him too write his book, to contend with me.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Surely I would carry it upon my shoulder
Job.english_translation: *Esa'enu* — to write my book.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: I would bind it unto me as a crown
Job.english_translation: *E'anedenu* — I would bind it to a book of crowns for me.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: I would declare unto him the number of my steps
Job.english_translation: *Mispar tze'adai agidenu* — to that man.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: If my land cry out against me
Job.english_translation: *Im alai admati tiz'ak* — over gleanings, the forgotten sheaf and the corner, and tithes, that I did not separate tithes properly.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And the furrows thereof weep together
Job.english_translation: *Veyachad telameha yivkayun* — that I ploughed with an ox and a donkey together.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: If I have eaten the fruits thereof without money
Job.english_translation: *Bli chesef* — to hire labourers and defraud them. Another explanation: this is the second tithe, as it is written, “and bind up the money (*vetzarta hakesef*) in thy hand” (Deuteronomy 14:25).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Or have caused the tillers thereof to be disappointed
Job.english_translation: *Venefesh be'aleha* — the tenant farmer who works it.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And noisome weeds instead of barley
Job.english_translation: *Be'ashah* — (a thing that stinks) like *be'ushim* (“wild grapes,” Isaiah 5); and if I did not do so, “let thistles grow instead of wheat” (Rabbi Oshaya taught: I have taught you Torah, the way of the land: a field that brings up thistles is good to sow with wheat; one that brings up *be'ushim* is good to sow with barley; כ"ה in Yalkut). And what is the reason for “instead of wheat let thistles grow”?
Job.translator_note: The sentence in parentheses is a later printed insertion (PI); the abbreviation כ"ה is left as printed. Printed “Isaiah 5” is Isaiah 5:2.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The words of Job are ended
Job.english_translation: *Tamu* etc. — up to here he returns and prophesies several prophecies, and you say “The words of Job are ended”? Rather, thus says Job: if I did not do so, may the words of Job be ended, and let there be no opening of the mouth to say before You, “I have put away the hallowed things (*bi'arti hakodesh*)” (Deuteronomy 20) — so I saw in the Pesikta, in the section “*Aser te'aser*” (ibid. 14); it is explained so from these verses.
Job.translator_note: Printed “Deuteronomy 20” is Deuteronomy 26:13; “ibid. 14” is Deuteronomy 14:22.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: of the family of Ram
Job.english_translation: (Elihu’s reply.) *Mimishpachat Ram* — Abraham, as it is said, “the greatest man among the Anakim” (Joshua 14:15) — this is Abraham.
Job.translator_note: The source begins “(Elihu’s reply)” before the lemma. Printed “Joshua 14:15”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: rather than God
Job.english_translation: *Me'Elohim* — more than the Omnipresent.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: and yet had condemned Job
Job.english_translation: *Vayarshi'u et Iyov* — this is one of the verses where the Scribes corrected the language of the text: “and they condemned” toward the Omnipresent in their silence, he should have written; but the text used a euphemism. And so “Thus they exchanged their glory for the likeness of an ox” — *kevodi* he should have written, but the text used a euphemism; and so “and let me not look upon my wretchedness (*bera'ati*)” (Numbers 11:15–16) — *bera'at'* he should have written, but the text used a euphemism; and so [in] many places in the Sifrei and in the Masorah Gedolah.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally; the abbreviated form *bera'at'* is left as printed. The first quotation is Psalms 106:20; the printed reference is Numbers 11:15–16.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: had waited to speak unto Job
Job.english_translation: *Chikkah* — waited.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: because they were older than he
Job.english_translation: *Ki zekenim hemah mimmenu layamim* — the others; therefore he refrained until they were silent. (Elihu’s reply.)
Job.translator_note: Translated literally. The words “(Elihu’s reply)” at the end are printed in parentheses (PI).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Wherefore I held back
Job.english_translation: *Zachalti* — I was afraid.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: But it is a spirit in man
Job.english_translation: *Achen ruach hi be'enosh* — wisdom, not through days and old age, but it is the spirit of the Omnipresent.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Yea, I attended unto you
Job.english_translation: *Ve'adeichem etbonen* — I paid attention to you, and saw that there is no one to reprove Job.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Beware lest you say: ‘We have found wisdom; God may vanquish him, not man! ’
Job.english_translation: *Pen tomru matzanu chochmah* — in our silence, so as not to provoke him further; “God may vanquish him, not man.” You should not have diminished the honour of the Omnipresent thus.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: For he hath not directed his words against me
Job.english_translation: *Velo arach elai millin* — this is a tradition (*kabbalah*), or: that he has not set in order words to me.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Neither will I answer him with your speeches
Job.english_translation: *Uve'imreichem lo ashivenu* — not with those sayings with which you answered him would I answer him.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Words are departed from them
Job.english_translation: *He'tiku* — words departed from them.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Behold, mine inwards are as wine which hath no vent
Job.english_translation: *Hineh bitni* — full of wind, words to answer with desire.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: as wine which hath no vent
Job.english_translation: *Keyayin lo yippatach* — like new wine that is not opened, and swells, and even within new skins, and bursts them.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Like new wine-skins which are ready to burst
Job.english_translation: *Ovot* — wineskins made to the height of a man, tall.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Neither will I give flattering titles unto any man
Job.english_translation: *Lo achuneh* — I will not alter my words to change them for his honour, as I said above, “and they condemned Job”: this is a euphemism that changes the speech for the sake of His honour; and this too I will not do, for I will rebuke him with a full mouth.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Else would my Maker soon take me away
Job.english_translation: *Kim'at yissa'eni* — He will remove me from the world; and some interpret *yissa'eni* like “and the earth is upheaved (*vattissa*) at His presence” (Nahum 1:5).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Nahum 1:5”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The spirit of God hath made me
Job.english_translation: *Ruach El asatni* — and I am not stronger than you.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Behold, I am toward God even as thou art
Job.english_translation: *Hen ani keficha la'el* — as your mouth asked, to contend with one who will not frighten you; behold, I am in the place of the Holy One, blessed be He, and for His sake to speak His words.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Neither shall my pressure be heavy upon thee
Job.english_translation: *Ve'akpi* — my compulsion, like “for his mouth compelleth him (*akaf alav pihu*)” (Proverbs 17).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Proverbs 17” is Proverbs 16:26.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: ‘I am clean, without transgression
Job.english_translation: *Chaf* — pure and scraped, like “a Nazirite shall not shave (*lo yachof*) his head” and like “in all, they scrape (*chafin*) the vessels.”
Job.translator_note: Translated literally; the quotations are from the Mishnah and the references are not given in the source.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Behold, He findeth occasions against me
Job.english_translation: *Tenu'ot* — pretexts, an expression of *to'anah* (“occasion”) (Judges 14:4), to turn away from the Omnipresent.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally. Printed “Judges 14”; the word *to'anah* occurs in Judges 14:4.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: That God is too great for man
Job.english_translation: *Ki yirbeh Eloha me'enosh* — the Omnipresent need not scrutinize man so much, for the Holy One, blessed be He, has many more righteous acts than man.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Then He openeth the ears of men
Job.english_translation: As He did to Abimelech in a dream of the night.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And by their chastisement sealeth the decree
Job.english_translation: *Uvemusaram yachtom* — He seals them and binds them with sufferings for their iniquity.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: That men may put away their purpose
Job.english_translation: *Lehasir adam* — in his illness.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: That men may put away their purpose
Job.english_translation: *Ma'aseh* — that which he had in mind to do.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And that He may hide pride from man
Job.english_translation: *Vegevah miggever yechasseh* — with his sufferings, in order to subdue and humble him to repent, so that He may hold back his soul from complete death.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: pride
Job.english_translation: *Gevah* — like *ga'avah*.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And his life from perishing by the sword
Job.english_translation: *Vechayyato me'avor bashalach* — by the missile and sword of the angel of death; that is, for your good He brought sufferings upon you.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: by the sword
Job.english_translation: *Shalach* — weapon, and so “one hand holding the weapon (*hashelach*)” (Nehemiah 4:11).
Job.translator_note: JPS renders Nehemiah 4:11 “with the other held his weapon.” Printed “Nehemiah 4:11”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He is hastened also with pain upon his bed
Job.english_translation: *Vehuchach* — an expression of reproof, that he repent of his iniquity.
Job.translator_note: Rashi reads *vehuchach* as “reproved”; JPS renders “hastened.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And all his bones grow stiff
Job.english_translation: *Verov atzamav* — for he is strong, He reproves them with pain.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: So that his life maketh him to abhor bread
Job.english_translation: *Vezihamato chayyato lachem* — his soul loathes it, and the life of the sick man [loathes] every food.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And his soul dainty food
Job.english_translation: *Venafsho* — makes loathsome every food of desire.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: His flesh is consumed away, that it cannot be seen
Job.english_translation: *Yichal besaro mere'i* — his flesh will grow dim from appearance, like “Mine eyes do fail with tears” (Lamentations 2:11), “that shall make the eyes to fail” (Leviticus 26).
Job.translator_note: Translated literally. Printed “Lamentations 2:11”; “Leviticus 26” is Leviticus 26:16.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And his bones corrode to unsightliness
Job.english_translation: *Veshufu atzmotav* — they are torn from their place; and *shufu* is like *dashef medukhteih* (Chullin 42).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And his bones corrode to unsightliness
Job.english_translation: *Lo ruu* — they have no appearance and form.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: one among a thousand
Job.english_translation: *Echad mini alef* — among those who tell his transgression, and he will intercede for his uprightness.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Then He is gracious unto him
Job.english_translation: *Vayechunnenu* — the Omnipresent.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Deliver him from going down to the pit
Job.english_translation: *Pedao'hu* — like *pedaehu*; an *aleph* is interchanged with an *ayin*, and the context proves it: “I have found a ransom,” which is redemption.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: His flesh is tenderer than a child’s
Job.english_translation: *Rutafash* — *ashkosh'a* in French.
Job.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: His flesh is tenderer than a child’s
Job.english_translation: *Minno'ar* — his flesh was aroused from the shaking (*no'ar*), for it was shaken out and strangled (by the sufferings of) his illness; and this word has no parallel in Scripture, and according to the context we had to explain it as the sense of the context. And the one who interprets it in the language of *refesh* (mire) and says that the *tet* was added in it, like (Genesis 44) *nitztaddak*, is greatly mistaken, for a *tet* is not added in a word except in the *hitpa'el* or *nitpa'el* form, and in a word whose root is *tzadi*, and not in other words, like *tzedek* and *nitztaddek*, and like *tzaru'a* (Leviticus 13) [and] *nitzta're'a*, *tzir ne'eman*, “and they went and made as if they had been ambassadors (*vayitztayyaru*),” “our provision (*hitztayyadnu*)” (Joshua 9:4).
Job.translator_note: Translated literally. The words “(by the sufferings of)” are a later printed insertion (PI). Printed “Genesis 44” is Genesis 44:16; “Joshua 9:4” is for *vayitztayyaru*, and *hitztayyadnu* is Joshua 9:12.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He returneth to the days of his youth
Job.english_translation: *Yashuv* — in his strength and with healing, to the days of his youth.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: So that he seeth His face with joy
Job.english_translation: *Bitru'ah* — in prayer.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He cometh before men, and saith
Job.english_translation: *Yashor al anashim* — he will make rows of people when he is saved from his illness and confess to his Maker.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And it profited me not
Job.english_translation: *Velo shaveh li* — no reward came to me through his words.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Twice, yea thrice, with a man
Job.english_translation: *Pa'amayim shalosh* — He chastises him for his iniquities with his illness, so as not to destroy him; and if he angers Him further, he will be anxious about Gehinnom and about death, as it is said, “and for four I will not reverse it” (Amos 1).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Amos 1” is Amos 1:3.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: For the ear trieth words
Job.english_translation: (Elihu’s reply.) *Ki ozen millin tivchan* — as the palate tastes food.
Job.translator_note: The source begins “(Elihu’s reply)” before the lemma.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And God hath taken away my right
Job.english_translation: *Mishpati* — the reproof of words.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Notwithstanding my right I am accounted a liar
Job.english_translation: *Achzav* — I am called a liar by my Judge, who did not judge me truthfully.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: incurable
Job.english_translation: *Anush* — sick is my wound, like “and it was very sick (*vayyenash*)” (II Samuel 12).
Job.translator_note: Printed “II Samuel 12” is II Samuel 12:15.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: My wound is incurable
Job.english_translation: *Chitzi* — my plagues.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: It profiteth a man nothing
Job.english_translation: *Lo yiskan gaver* — a man will not benefit if he perfects his ways.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Who gave Him a charge over the earth?
Job.english_translation: *Mi fakad alav artzah* — who rules over Him, to say, “Why did You do thus? I did not command You thus”? For who commanded Him in His dominion? And why should He find pretexts against creatures? He need not answer anything to one who rules over Him, to say, “For this I did evil to him.”
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: If He set His heart upon man
Job.english_translation: *Im yasim elav libbo* — upon man to destroy him, why would He come with a pretext against him? Behold, at once He will gather to Himself his spirit and his breath, the spirit and breath of his, which is (blown into him), and none can protest against His hand; and all flesh will expire together.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: If now thou hast understanding, hear this
Job.english_translation: *Ve'im binah* — and if you wish to understand, hear this. *Binah* here is not a noun but an expression of command, like “consider (*binah*) my meditation” (Psalms 5:2); therefore these two have their accent above, on the *bet*, and all other [instances of] *binah* have their accent below, on the *nun*.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Shall even one that hateth right govern?
Job.english_translation: *Ha'af soneh mishpat* — the judgment of the Judge of righteousness He will restrain. The Omnipresent; and if you say it is not a [just] judgment because He did not act according to law: is it possible that you would condemn Him who is exceedingly righteous?
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Him that is just and mighty
Job.english_translation: *Kabbir* — an expression of “exceedingly.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Is it fit to say to a king: ‘Thou art base’?
Job.english_translation: *He'amor lemelech beliyaal* — is it proper and fitting to say to a king, “Base,” and to say “Wicked” to nobles?

Job.english_lemma_JPS: That respecteth not the persons of princes
Job.english_translation: *Asher lo nasa penei sarim* — that is, to the King of the universe, before whom there is no respect of persons.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Nor regardeth the rich more than the poor
Job.english_translation: *Shua* — prince, like “nor the churl said to be noble (*shua*)” (Isaiah 32:5).
Job.translator_note: Rashi reads *shua* as “prince”; JPS renders “the rich.” Printed “Isaiah 32:5”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: In a moment they die, even at midnight
Job.english_translation: *Rega yamutu* — when He wills.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: even at midnight
Job.english_translation: *Vachatzot lailah* — as He did to Egypt.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The people are shaken and pass away
Job.english_translation: *Yegu'ashu am* — that is, in a moment they will pass away.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And the mighty are taken away without hand
Job.english_translation: *Veyasiru abbir* — their strength.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: without hand
Job.english_translation: *Lo veyad* — they will not change by their hand, and they have no strength.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: For He doth not appoint a time unto any man
Job.english_translation: *Ki lo al ish yasim od* — that is: you said, “Nay; but He would give heed unto me” (above, 23), only my sins alone, and I answer you: the Holy One, blessed be He, does not set pretexts upon His creatures in addition to their transgression; *od* is an expression of addition.
Job.translator_note: Printed “above 23” is Job 23:6. Rashi reads *yasim* as “sets upon.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: When he should go before God in judgment
Job.english_translation: *Lehalloch el El bamishpat* — when He comes upon His creatures to contend with them.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He breaketh in pieces mighty men without inquisition
Job.english_translation: *Yarua* — He will crush, like “The earth is broken, broken down (*ro'a hit'ro'ah*)” (Isaiah 24).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 24” is Isaiah 24:19.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And setteth others in their stead
Job.english_translation: *Vaya'amed acherim* — in their place.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Therefore He taketh knowledge of their works
Job.english_translation: *Lachen yakir ma'avideihem* — because He knows their deeds, good and bad, and has no need to contend.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And He overturneth them in the night, so that they are crushed
Job.english_translation: *Vehafach lailah* — a time of darkness and trouble for them, and they will be crushed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He striketh them as wicked men
Job.english_translation: *Tachat resha'im* — in their place.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He striketh them as wicked men
Job.english_translation: *Sefakam* — to the people of Sodom.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: In the open sight of others
Job.english_translation: *Bimkom ro'im* — before the eyes of all.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Because they turned aside from following Him
Job.english_translation: *Asher al ken saru me'acharav* — like “forasmuch as (*al ken*) thou knowest how we are to encamp in the wilderness” (Numbers 10:31); like “because they turned aside from following Him”; and they brought before Him, and upon Him, the cry of the poor.
Job.translator_note: Printed “Numbers 10:31”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: When He giveth quietness, who then can condemn?
Job.english_translation: *Vehu yashkit* — He quiets the poor from those oppressors; and who can condemn any more? And while He hid His face, who will behold Him?
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Whether it be done unto a nation, or unto a man, alike
Job.english_translation: *Ve'al goy ve'al adam yachad* — individuals and multitudes are the same before Him, to quiet and to hide the face.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: That the godless man reign not
Job.english_translation: (*Veyishkot*) *mimmloch adam chaneph mimmokshei am* — upon the poor whom he ruled.
Job.translator_note: The word in parentheses in the source lemma is a later printed insertion (PI). Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: That there be none to ensnare the people
Job.english_translation: *Mimmokshei am* — iniquity; and for such a God you should not have said “base” and “wicked.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: For hath any said unto God: ‘I have borne chastisement, though I offend not
Job.english_translation: *Ki el El ha'amar* — it is proper and fitting for it to be said to Him by all who suffer afflictions: “I have borne; I accept and I bear Your judgments, and I will not wound myself.” And further, the one judged must say:
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: That which I see not teach Thou me
Job.english_translation: *Bilade'i echezeh* — apart from what I know to see and to understand in Your words, You teach me; and if I have done iniquity, I will do it no more.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Shall His recompense be as thou wilt?
Job.english_translation: *Hame'imcha yeshallemennah ki ma'asta* etc. — thus said Elihu to Job: was it for the Holy One, blessed be He, to take counsel with you about the payment of repayment?
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: For thou loathest it, So that thou must choose, and not I
Job.english_translation: *Ki ma'asta* — to say, “I loathe it; I shall not live alway” (above, 7), “that He would let loose His hand and cut me off” (above, 6): do you suppose that He will collect from you according to your mind and your will, and that you will choose the payments and not I? Elihu spoke in the place of the Holy One, blessed be He, as a question.
Job.translator_note: Printed “above 3” is Job 7:16; “above 6” is Job 6:9.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Men of understanding will say unto me
Job.english_translation: *Anshei levav yomru li* — for Job speaks without knowledge.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Would that Job were tried unto the end
Job.english_translation: *Avi yibbachen* — “My Father”: You, the Holy One, blessed be He, Father of all — would that Job be tried to the end, so that there be a reply to men of iniquity; and he spoke thus even to human beings, like “My father (*avi*), if the prophet had bid thee do some great thing” (II Kings 5:13). (Another explanation: *avi* like “and the *evyonah* shall fail” (Ecclesiastes 12:5), an expression of desire; so Menachem composed, and so its interpretation: *avi yibbachen Iyov ad netzach* — my wish and my desire that Job be tried to the end, סא"א.)
Job.translator_note: it is left as printed. JPS renders Ecclesiastes 12:5 “the caperberry shall fail.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He clappeth his hands among us
Job.english_translation: *Yispok* — an expression of abundance of words and raising of the voice.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He clappeth his hands among us
Job.english_translation: *Beineinu yispok* — he says, “What is it to us and to his words? Even if indeed I erred, my error remaineth with me” (above, 19); and he does not know that we are punished, and iniquities suffice for us, for we hear thus. So it is explained in Vayikra Rabbah.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally. Printed “above 19” is Job 19:4.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Thinkest thou this to be thy right
Job.english_translation: (Elihu’s reply.) *Hazot chashavta lemishpat* — which is the judgment of creatures against their Maker, as you said, “My righteousness is more than the Creator’s.”
Job.translator_note: The source begins “(Elihu’s reply)” before the lemma. Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: That thou inquirest: ‘What advantage will it be unto Thee?’
Job.english_translation: *Ki tomar mah yiskan lach* — ways of uprightness.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: What profit shall I have, more than if I had sinned
Job.english_translation: *Mah ho'il* — in my righteousness more than in my sin.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And thy companions with thee
Job.english_translation: *Ve'et re'echa immach* — who were silent at your words.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Look unto the heavens, and see
Job.english_translation: *Habet shamayim* — and since He is high and you are low, and He has no benefit from your wickedness and your righteousness, why do you boast to Him of your righteousness?

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Thy wickedness concerneth a man as thou art
Job.english_translation: *Le'ish* — like yourself, your wickedness and your righteousness may be able and useful; see many wicked ones who:
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: By reason of the multitude of oppressions they cry out
Job.english_translation: *Merov ashukim* — those who oppress, they make creatures cry out before Him, and the poor cry for help from the arm of the many who oppress them.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: But none saith
Job.english_translation: *Velo amar* — the wicked.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Where is God my Maker
Job.english_translation: *Ayeh Eloha osai* — to fear before Him.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Who giveth songs in the night
Job.english_translation: *Noten zemirot* — like “thou shalt not prune (*tizmor*) thy vineyard” (Leviticus 25), for He cuts off the wicked at night, such as Amraphel and his companions, and Egypt and Sennacherib.
Job.translator_note: Printed “Leviticus 25” is Leviticus 25:4.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Who teacheth us more than the beasts of the earth
Job.english_translation: *Melafenu* — He teaches us wisdom more than the beasts; that is, we are considered and made greater than beasts and fowl.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: There they cry, but none giveth answer
Job.english_translation: *Sham yitz'aku* — and see that there the poor cry because of the pride of those who oppress them, and He does not answer.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Surely God will not hear vanity
Job.english_translation: *Ach shav lo yishma* — immediately.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Neither will the Almighty regard it
Job.english_translation: *Veshaddai lo yeshurennah* — to take vengeance immediately, but He is slow to anger.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Yea, when thou sayest thou canst not see Him
Job.english_translation: *Af ki tomar* — How much more so [כ"ש] you, whose cry comes only through Him, and you say and cry out about what you do not see in order to contend with Him; that is, those who complain and cry out, He does not hasten to answer them, and you cry out that you do not see Him.
Job.translator_note: The abbreviation כ"ש is read as “how much more so” (*kal shekken*) from the context; flagged as my reading.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The cause is before Him
Job.english_translation: *Din lefanav* — (your word סס"א) everywhere that He is.
Job.translator_note: The words in parentheses are a later printed insertion (PI); the abbreviation סס"א is left as printed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: therefore wait thou for Him
Job.english_translation: *Vetechollel* — and hope for consolations.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And now, is it for nought that He punished in His anger?
Job.english_translation: *Ve'attah* — know that this visitation (of His anger) upon you is nothing compared with the abundance of your iniquities.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And hath He not full knowledge of arrogance?
Job.english_translation: *Velo yada befash me'od* — in the abundance of your sins the Creator behaved as if He did not know them.
Job.translator_note: Rashi reads *fash* as “abundance”; JPS renders “arrogance.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: arrogance
Job.english_translation: *Befash* — an expression of abundance, like “and you shall multiply (*ufashtem*)” (Malachi 3) and like “for you multiply (*tafushu*),” etc. (Jeremiah 50:11), “if the plague be spread (*pashah*)” (Leviticus 13).
Job.translator_note: Rashi reads *ufashtem* and *tafushu* as “multiply”; JPS renders Malachi 3:20 and Jeremiah 50:11 “gambol.” Printed “Malachi 3” is Malachi 3:20; “Leviticus 13” is Leviticus 13:51 (the same root, *pashah*).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He multiplieth words without knowledge
Job.english_translation: *Yachbir* — an expression of “exceedingly.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Elihu also proceeded, and said
Job.english_translation: *Vayosef Elihu* — I saw in the reasons (*ta'amei*) of Rabbi Moses HaDarshan that he therefore spoke three replies corresponding to Job’s three friends, and this is a fourth; therefore it is called “addition.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Suffer me a little, and I will tell thee
Job.english_translation: *Katter li ze'eir ve'achavekha* — all of it is Aramaic: bear with me (*hochal li*) a little and I will tell you. *Katter* is an expression of waiting (*hochal*), as Jonathan translated “and the isles shall wait (*yeyachalu*) for his teaching” (Isaiah 42:4) as *yekatterun*.
Job.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 42:4”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: For there are yet words on God’s behalf
Job.english_translation: *La'Eloha* — for those who come in His place.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: One that is upright in mind is with thee
Job.english_translation: *Tamim de'ot immach* — behold, I begin now to speak with you, for you think that your mind is perfect.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Behold, God is mighty, yet He despiseth not any
Job.english_translation: *Hen El kabbir* — in wisdom and in mercy.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: yet He despiseth not any
Job.english_translation: *Velo yimas* — the poor man.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He is mighty in strength of understanding
Job.english_translation: *Kabbir koach lev* — to take vengeance; therefore the wicked will not live.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He withdraweth not His eyes from the righteous
Job.english_translation: *Lo yigra mitzaddik einav* — until He seats them with kings.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And if they be bound in fetters, And be holden in cords of affliction
Job.english_translation: *Ve'im asurim* — and if you see righteous men bound with fetters of sufferings and illnesses, or caught “in cords of affliction”: in the language of lot and cords it is called *chevlei*; and in the language of worry it is called *chevlei yoledah* (“pangs of a woman in travail”). *Bechavlei oni* — *cordes* in French; it is only that they sinned before Him, and He comes to exact payment from them, for their good, to cleanse them and to warn them to return to Him.
Job.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Job 36:8 (“liens”), in forms such as קורדש and קורדיש; the printed form (קודר"ש) differs slightly (two letters are in the other order).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Then He declareth unto them their work
Job.english_translation: *Vayaged lahem pa'alam* — through these sufferings He makes known to them that they sinned before Him; and all the words of Elihu were complete consolations and not *kintorin*; that is: do not worry about the sufferings if you are righteous, for they are for your good.
Job.translator_note: The word *kintorin* is left as printed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And commandeth that they return from iniquity
Job.english_translation: *Vayomer* — that through sufferings they will return from iniquity.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: If they hearken and serve Him
Job.english_translation: *Im yishma'u* — and serve Him.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: But they that are godless in heart lay up anger
Job.english_translation: *Vechanfei lev* — they are wicked, they will set anger. When sufferings come upon them, they revile and blaspheme.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: They cry not for help
Job.english_translation: *Velo yeshav'u* — before Him with supplication.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: when He bindeth them
Job.english_translation: *Ki asaram* — when He binds them with sufferings; therefore He will not heal them.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Their soul perisheth in youth
Job.english_translation: *Tamut bano'ar* — and in the choking that is upon them, their souls.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He delivereth the afflicted by His affliction
Job.english_translation: *Yechalletz ani* — the poor man who makes himself poor in matters of supplication He will rescue from Gehinnom, on account of his affliction which He brought upon him.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And openeth their ear by tribulation
Job.english_translation: *Veyigel balachatz oznam* — through the pressure that He brought upon him, He uncovers his ear, to say, “Return to Me.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Yea, He hath allured thee out of distress
Job.english_translation: *Ve'af* — He did this further great thing for you through these sufferings: He allured you and drove you away from Gehinnom, whose mouth is narrow and whose bottom is wide.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: where there is no straitness
Job.english_translation: *Lo mutzak* — so that its smoke be gathered into it; and not only that, but you will merit the World to Come, “and the rest of thy table full of fatness.”
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And thou art full of the judgment of the wicked
Job.english_translation: *Vedin resha malleta* — and if you were filled with the sufferings of the wicked: the judgment and justice, these are the sufferings; they will uphold you in the future [and save you] from Gehinnom, and you should accept them with love.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: For beware of wrath
Job.english_translation: *Ki chemah* — it will be great.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: lest thou be led away by thy sufficiency
Job.english_translation: *Pen yesitecha* — your inclination to speak words.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: by thy sufficiency
Job.english_translation: *Bessafek* — this *sefek*, that you clap and multiply your words against God; and since the wrath will rise, let great wealth not turn you from it.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Will thy riches avail, that are without stint
Job.english_translation: *Hayaaroch shu'acha lo vetzar* — would you come to set out a cry that no trouble come upon you and no exertion of strength for your compulsion? If so, with what will He collect His debt?
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Desire not the night, When peoples are cut off in their place
Job.english_translation: *Al tish'af halailah* — that is: you have no [right] to choose other sufferings; do not long for and desire the night that came to Amraphel, to Egypt, and to Sennacherib, to remove peoples from the world while they are in their place in tranquillity, for they perished in this world and in the World to Come.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: peoples are cut off in their place
Job.english_translation: *La'alot* — like “O my God, take me not away (*al ta'aleni*) in the midst of my days” (Psalms 102:25), like “as a shock of corn cometh in (*ka'alot*) in its season.”
Job.translator_note: The second quotation is Job 5:26.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Take heed, regard not iniquity
Job.english_translation: *Hishamer al tifen el aven* — to argue and to say, “He should have judged me with the sufferings of poverty.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: For this hast thou chosen rather than affliction
Job.english_translation: *Ki al zeh vacharta me'oni* — for these sufferings should be chosen rather than poverty: a man who was treated with honour and was accustomed to wealth all his days, and he stands at the purchase and has no money, and is ashamed and returns to his house in anguish of soul.
