And if you say Job was poor with the sufferings — we do not find that he lost anything but his cattle, but not silver and gold; and even if he lost his cattle with silver and gold, it is better for him to be poor and sick than to be whole and walk in the markets with nothing in his hand. And so it is explained in Midrash Rabbi Tanchuma from this verse, that Job’s sufferings were easier than the sufferings of poverty; and so in the Aggadot of the Gemara.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Behold, God doeth loftily in His power
Job.english_translation: *Hen El yasgiv bechocho* — since His strength is great and there is no escaping Him, therefore there is none like Him as a teacher. When He teaches the sinner to return to Him, He warns before He smites, because He knows that one cannot guard against His blow, as He warned Pharaoh before each and every plague: “Behold, tomorrow about this time I will cause it to rain a very grievous hail” (Exodus 9:18) and “Behold, tomorrow I will bring locusts,” and so all of them. And flesh and blood, when he wants to take vengeance on his enemies, comes upon him suddenly, for if he warns him, he will repent and be saved from him.
Job.translator_note: The locust warning is Exodus 10:4.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Who hath enjoined Him His way?
Job.english_translation: *Mi fakad alav darko* — who commanded Him, ever, “Walk in this way”?

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Remember that thou magnify His work
Job.english_translation: *Zechor* — His ways, and in your remembering you will, of yourself, magnify the praise of the Maker of His attributes.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Whereof men have sung
Job.english_translation: *Asher shorru anashim* — which men have seen, like “I behold him (*ashurenu*), but not nigh” (Numbers 24:17).
Job.translator_note: Rashi reads *shorru* as “saw”; JPS renders “sung.” Printed “Numbers 24:17”.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: All men have looked thereon
Job.english_translation: *Chazu vo* — in His work.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Man beholdeth it afar off
Job.english_translation: *Merachok* — from the creation of the world until now.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The number of His years is unsearchable
Job.english_translation: *Mispar shanav velo cheker* — therefore a man must look from afar, to ask what happened to the earlier [generations] and learn from them.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: For He draweth away the drops of water
Job.english_translation: *Ki yigra* — for He will multiply, like “and thou restrainest (*vetigra*) devotion” (above, 15); and some interpret: He draws them from the heavens to bring them down to the earth.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally. Printed “above 15” is Job 15:4 (JPS: “And impairest devotion before God”).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Which distil rain from His vapour
Job.english_translation: *Veyazoku* — the firmaments [distil] the rain.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: from His vapour
Job.english_translation: *Le'ido* — to His cloud.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Yea, can any understand the spreadings of the clouds
Job.english_translation: *Af im yavin* — or if a man could understand what is in the spreadings of the cloud, as a question.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The crashings of His pavilion
Job.english_translation: *Tish'ot* — an expression of the cloud of His booth.
Job.translator_note: Rashi reads *tish'ot* as “darkness / cloud”; JPS renders “crashings.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Behold, He spreadeth His light upon it
Job.english_translation: *Hen paras* — (upon the cloud, His light) and the roots of the sea He covered with it.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: For by these He judgeth the peoples
Job.english_translation: *Ki vam* — by clouds He judges peoples; He chastises them by the withholding of rains, with famine and every plague: the generation of the Flood sinned, and “the windows of heaven were opened” (Genesis 7:11); the people of Sodom, “brimstone, and salt, and a burning” (Deuteronomy 29:22); Sisera, “They fought from heaven, the stars in their courses fought against Sisera” (Judges 5:20).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He giveth food in abundance
Job.english_translation: *Yiten ochel lamachbir* — from there come provisions: “Behold, I will cause to rain bread from heaven for you” (Exodus 15). A parable of a baker standing before the oven: his enemy enters, rakes coals and throws them at him; his friend enters, takes out hot bread and gives it to him.
Job.translator_note: Printed “Exodus 15” is Exodus 16:4.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He giveth food in abundance
Job.english_translation: *Lamachbir* — to one whose dependents are many and mighty, and who needs provisions.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He covereth His hands with the lightning
Job.english_translation: *Al kappayim* — upon the clouds; and so, “Let us lift up our heart with our hands (*el kappayim*)” (Lamentations 3), because of a small cloud like a man’s palm (*kaf*) (I Kings 18); and our Rabbis said: because of (violence) and the iniquity of palms, He covered the light; the rain was withheld.
Job.translator_note: Rashi reads *kappayim* as “clouds.” Printed “Lamentations 3” is Lamentations 3:41; “I Kings 18” is I Kings 18:44.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And giveth it a charge that it strike the mark
Job.english_translation: *Vayetz al eha* — to come through the intercessor in prayer: the beloved of the generation, the greatest and wisest in it, will tell before the Holy One, blessed be He, the trouble of the generation and its needs.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The noise thereof telleth concerning it
Job.english_translation: *Yaggid alav re'o* — he will expound to them, to examine them in their deeds and to return to Him.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The cattle also concerning the storm that cometh up
Job.english_translation: *Mikneh* — and this is the acquisition (*kinyan*) by which the rains are acquired.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: concerning the storm that cometh up
Job.english_translation: *Af al oleh* — also above, above (so ascending), like “they return upward (*yashuvu el al*)” (Hosea 7) or “raised on high (*hukam el*)” (II Samuel 23); and our Rabbis interpreted it: acquisition of anger and wrath upon one who is arrogant; but the vocalization with which *mikneh* is vocalized, a *patach*, proves that it is not connected to *af*, for if it were connected, it would be vocalized with a *kamatz* and there would be no pausal accent; it is accented with a *revi'i*.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally. Rashi’s printed wording differs from the verses: Hosea 7:16 reads *lo al* (JPS: “not upwards”), and II Samuel 23:1 reads *al* (JPS: “raised on high”).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And is moved out of its place
Job.english_translation: *Veyatar* — and it will jump, like “to leap (*lenatter*) upon the earth” (Leviticus 11); and this is that his heart is astonished.
Job.translator_note: Printed “Leviticus 11:41” is Leviticus 11:21.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Hear attentively the noise of His voice
Job.english_translation: *Shim'u shamo'a berogez kolo* — the thunders that He thunders in the firmament, like the utterance that comes from His mouth.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He sendeth it forth under the whole heaven
Job.english_translation: *Tachat kol hashamayim yishrehu* — I saw it, like “I behold him (*ashurenu*)” (Numbers 24); and they are those lights that the lightnings illuminate.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: After it a voice roareth
Job.english_translation: *Acharav* — of that light, a roar will roar the thunder, and He thunders with the voice of His majesty; and they are lightnings and thunders that bring the rain.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And He stayeth them not
Job.english_translation: *Velo ya'ekvem* — the Omnipresent.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: when His voice is heard
Job.english_translation: *Ki yishama* — before Him, the voice of the intercessor.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And He stayeth them not
Job.english_translation: *Ya'ekvem* — He will cut them off; and in the language of the Mishnah we learned (Sotah 16a), “In three places the halachah uproots (*okevet*) the Scripture.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: For He saith to the snow
Job.english_translation: *Ki lashaleg yomar* — through these voices.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Likewise to the shower of rain, and to the showers of His mighty rain
Job.english_translation: הוא ארץ וגשם מטר וגשם מטרות עזו — that is, it will come from the four directions.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He sealeth up the hand of every man
Job.english_translation: *Beyad kol adam yachtom* — when a man sins before Him, the man himself seals his handwriting on the day of his death on the transgressions that he committed, which are written before Him.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: That all men whom He hath made may know it
Job.english_translation: *Lada'at kol anshei ma'asehu* — to make known for what he is judged.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Then the beasts go into coverts
Job.english_translation: *Vetavo chayah vemo arev* — that is: further, the Omnipresent has many messengers by which to exact His punishments: the sending of wild beasts, and storm, and cold.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Out of the Chamber cometh the storm
Job.english_translation: *Umimezarim* — there is a treasury, and its name is *Mezarim*.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: By the breath of God ice is given
Job.english_translation: *Minishmat* — from His wind.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: the breadth of the waters is straitened
Job.english_translation: *Verochav mayim bemutzak* — in a pouring, for punishment.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Yea, He ladeth the thick cloud with moisture
Job.english_translation: *Af beri* — the name of the angel appointed over the clouds; and he will scatter the rain-cloud of the Omnipresent.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: the cloud of His lightning
Job.english_translation: *Anan oro* — the cloud of His rain.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And they are turned round about
Job.english_translation: *Vehu* — the appointed one.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: by His guidance
Job.english_translation: *Mesibbot mithapech bethachbulotav* — of the Omnipresent.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: That they may do
Job.english_translation: *Lefa'alam* — of the rains, to the work laid upon them to do, whether for good or for evil, He turns about through many circuits, as in that which we learned: if Israel were wholly righteous on Rosh Hashanah and the rains were decreed to be withheld from them, and afterwards they sinned, one cannot diminish from them, since the decree was already decreed; but the Holy One, blessed be He, sends them down not in their season and on a land that does not need them; and at times for good — how? etc.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally; “etc.” is as printed (Taanit 19b).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: whatsoever He commandeth them
Job.english_translation: *Kol asher yetzavem* — those rains, to do to the earth. (Another explanation: “and He, through circuits, turns about by His devices”: He surrounds clouds and winds around the mountains, so that they drink from all their winds, in the Aggadah on “And it shall be, because ye hearken.”)
Job.translator_note: The parenthetical comment is a later printed insertion (PI).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Whether it be for correction
Job.english_translation: *Im leshevet* — if for the punishment of men, He sends them down on mountains and hills, where there is no place for sowing.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: or for His earth
Job.english_translation: *Im le'artzo* — to send them down as decreed at the beginning of the judgment: not for the rod and not within the line, but for the middling.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Or for mercy
Job.english_translation: *Im lechesed* — that the generation has now become more righteous than it was on Rosh Hashanah; and those rains that were decreed for the middling He turns about by the devices of their circuits to come down in kindness, in their season and on the land that needs them, so that not a drop of them falls to waste.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: that He cause it to come
Job.english_translation: *Yamtzi'ehu* — for rain, to one of these measures.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Dost thou know how God enjoineth them
Job.english_translation: *Besum Eloha* — a statute of covenant upon them, how they are suspended on a word.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Dost thou know the balancings of the clouds
Job.english_translation: *Mifleshei av* — the uncovering of the cloud; an expression of an open (*mefulash*) alley: that is, the length and breadth of clouds.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The wondrous works of Him who is perfect in knowledge
Job.english_translation: *Hatede'a* — about them, “the wondrous works of Him who is perfect in knowledge.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Thou whose garments are warm
Job.english_translation: *Asher begadekha chamim* — by what are your garments warm? When I quiet the earth from the south wind, which does not kill the world with cold; for an east wind warms, as it is said, “a vehement east wind” (Jonah 4:8), which silences all the winds before it.
Job.translator_note: Rashi reads *charishit* (Jonah 4:8) as “silencing”; JPS renders “vehement.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Which is strong
Job.english_translation: *Chazakim* — the firmaments.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: as a molten mirror
Job.english_translation: *Kero'i mutzak* — like the mirror in which women look. (*Mutzak*: טרישטייר [in Old French], and it is exceedingly strong.)
Job.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Job 37:18 (“fondu”), in forms such as טרישייטיר; the printed form (טרישטייר) is a variant spelling. The parenthetical comment is a later printed insertion (PI).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Teach us what we shall say unto Him
Job.english_translation: *Hodi'enu mah nomar lo* — to the Holy One, blessed be He, in our dispute with Him; we cannot arrange [words] to Him because of the darkness that covers Him and surrounds Him.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Shall it be told Him that I would speak?
Job.english_translation: *Hayesupar lo ki adabber* — is He then like human measure, that the words that go out of our mouths must be told to Him?

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Or should a man wish
Job.english_translation: *Im amar ish* — says from his mouth.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: that he were swallowed up
Job.english_translation: *Ki yevulla* — will be revealed to Him at once, like “lest the king be swallowed up (*yevulla*)” (II Samuel 17:16) — revealed. But our Rabbis interpreted: “Shall all His praise be told to Him, that I speak?” — for we speak of Him and of His might; “if a man say” — to tell them all, “surely he will be swallowed up” — from his place.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally. Rashi glosses *yevulla* as “be revealed”; JPS renders “be swallowed up.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And now men see not the light
Job.english_translation: *Ve'attah lo ra'u or* — at the end of his words Elihu returned to taunt those three friends of Job because they found no answer, and said: and now your three friends, these, who should have answered you all these words that I said to you, “have not seen light”; they have become like the untimely births who never saw wisdom.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: which is bright in the skies
Job.english_translation: *Bahir hu bashechakim* — like bright patches seen in the skies, to bring down rain.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: But the wind passeth, and cleanseth them
Job.english_translation: *Veruach avrah* — and a wind comes and cleanses them and removes them, and no rain falls; thus is their example: they began to answer you, and in the end they stopped and did not answer.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Out of the north cometh golden splendour
Job.english_translation: *Mitzafon zahav ye'eteh* — this is as though repeating the first [words] (“And now they saw not light”). Another explanation: a midrash of the Sages: when the firmament is full of patches of clouds to bring down rain, a wind passes and cleanses them and no rain falls. This is a midrash of the Sages, and it is not settled according to the order of the verses.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Out of the north cometh golden splendour
Job.english_translation: *Mitzafon zahav ye'eteh* — a north wind blows and removes the rain, and the sun shines; like “that empty the gold out of themselves” (Zechariah 4:12).
Job.translator_note: JPS Zechariah 4:12: “that empty the golden oil out of themselves.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: About God
Job.english_translation: *Al Eloha* — from before Him.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Out of the north cometh golden splendour
Job.english_translation: (*Mitzafon zahav ye'eteh* — the good gold is hidden (*nitzfan*) for those who come (*she-ye'eitu*) themselves to the commandments of the Holy One, blessed be He, and believe in the exceedingly awesome God.)
Job.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under. The whole comment is in parentheses in the print, a later printed insertion.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The Almighty, whom we cannot find out, is excellent in power
Job.english_translation: *Shaddai lo metza'nuhu sagi koach* — to arouse His judgments upon creatures in the greatness of His strength, but only with mercy; and He atones for creatures with a small thing according to capacity: a handful of meal-offering, half a shekel, turtledoves and young pigeons, ox and flock; and He did not trouble [creatures] to seek a wild ox and a wild ass.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally; the sentence is elliptical.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: judgment
Job.english_translation: *Umishpat* — sufferings.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He doeth no violence
Job.english_translation: *Lo ya'aneh* — creatures too much; and so the righteous man is not afflicted too much beyond what is possible, but each man according to the gift of his hand.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Men do therefore fear Him
Job.english_translation: *Lachen yire'uhu anashim* — from arguing with Him; “He regardeth not (*ki*) any that are wise of heart” — those who act wise toward Him, for their wisdom is nothing in His eyes. And our Rabbis interpreted it of Job, to whom Elihu said: since you cast excessive fear upon your generation for nothing, therefore you did not merit that sons wise of heart should be established for you.
Job.translator_note: The word “ki” in the printed text appears in parentheses, a later printed insertion (PI).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: out of the whirlwind
Job.english_translation: (Reply from the whirlwind.) *Min hasa'arah* — count your hairs (*se'arot*) and I will answer you words corresponding to them; “from the whirlwind,” in which you reviled Me — “who breaketh me with a tempest (*bis'arah*)” (above 9) — from it I will answer you, as you will hear at the end of the matter: “Who hath cleft a channel for the waterflood” — a channel, a pit, for every hair. Another explanation: “with a whirlwind He smote him, with a whirlwind He healed him,” as explained in the Sifrei.
Job.translator_note: The source begins “(reply from the whirlwind)” before the lemma.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Who is this that darkeneth counsel
Job.english_translation: *Machshich etzah* — counsel is darkness and folly. Another explanation: “Who is this that darkeneth counsel without knowledge?” The Holy One, blessed be He, said: who is this who darkens counsel, spoils with words and with the multitude of words — I wrote of him at the beginning of the book “whole-hearted and upright,” so that My name would rest upon him, and he came and darkened and spoiled what I had counselled, by his many words. And Job answered Him, “Who is this that hideth counsel” (below 42): if I had known Your counsel I would not have multiplied words. And the Holy One, blessed be He, answered him: did not Abraham not know, and yet he stood in ten [trials]? Thus I found.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally. Printed “below 42” is Job 42:3; for “whole-hearted and upright” compare JPS Job 1:1.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Gird up now thy loins like a man
Job.english_translation: *Ezor na kegever chalatzekha* — He hinted to him that he should rouse himself from his illness and his sufferings.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Where wast thou
Job.english_translation: *Eifoh* — *ei foh* (“where here”).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Who determined the measures thereof
Job.english_translation: *Memadeha* — its measures.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Or who laid the corner-stone thereof
Job.english_translation: *Yarah even pinnatah* — in the middle of the sea, and from there the whole world was founded.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: When the morning stars sang together
Job.english_translation: *Beran yachad* — at the beginning, the stars of light.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Or who shut up the sea with doors
Job.english_translation: *Bidlatayim yam* — sand, a boundary for it.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: When it broke forth
Job.english_translation: *Big'icho* — in its being drawn out, going forth from the deep, like *gochi mibaten*, *moshchi*.
Job.translator_note: No source is printed for this phrase; left as printed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: When I made the cloud the garment thereof
Job.english_translation: *Besumi anan* — around the Ocean Sea, which is the circumference of the world, and clouds surround it like a garment.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: a swaddlingband for it
Job.english_translation: *Chatullato* — its wrapping, like “nor swaddled at all (*vehachtel lo chuttalt*)” (Ezekiel 16:4).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And prescribed for it My decree
Job.english_translation: *Va'eshbor* — I made for it breakers (*shevarim*) around, to hold it in their midst, and they are a statute for it, which it shall not pass; like “and they chased them from before the gate even unto Shebarim” (Joshua 7:5); and they are trenches around the city.
Job.translator_note: *To'alot* is rendered “trenches” as the probable sense.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: since thy days began
Job.english_translation: *Hamiyamekha* — from the day you were born.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: That it might take hold of the ends of the earth
Job.english_translation: *Le'echoz bechanfot ha'aretz* — and further: did you, since your days, command it to seize the corners of the earth, as a man seizes the corners of cloaks and shakes them out? So I am destined to seize its corners and shake out the wicked; and so it says, “and the LORD shall stretch out His hand, and he that helpeth shall stumble” (Isaiah 31:3) — like a man who holds a thing in his hand and tilts his hand, and it falls.
Job.translator_note: JPS Isaiah 31:3: “So when the LORD shall stretch out His hand, Both he that helpeth shall stumble.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: It is changed
Job.english_translation: *Tithapech* — in forms.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: as clay under the seal
Job.english_translation: *Kechomer chotam* — a coin, the form of man in their death; and at the resurrection of the dead they will live and stand in their garments.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: But from the wicked their light is withholden
Job.english_translation: *Vayimana* — then from the wicked their light; and so it says, “and the high arm is broken.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: the springs of the sea
Job.english_translation: *Nivkhei yam* — enclosures of the sea, like “they are entangled (*nevuchim*) in the land” (Exodus 14:3).
Job.translator_note: Rashi reads *nivkhei* as “enclosures”; JPS renders “springs.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Have the gates of death been revealed unto thee?
Job.english_translation: *Sha'arei mavet* — this is Gehinnom.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Thou knowest it
Job.english_translation: *Yada'ta* — all this.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: for thou wast then born
Job.english_translation: *Ki az tivvaled* — when I created them.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Which I have reserved
Job.english_translation: *Asher chasachti* — I withheld.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: against the time of trouble
Job.english_translation: *Le'et tzar* — for the five kings at Gibeon.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Against the day of battle and war
Job.english_translation: *Leyom krav* — the war of Gog and Magog.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: By what way is the light parted
Job.english_translation: *Yechelak or* — the column (*timor*) of the sun, which bursts forth here and there like the horns of a ram.
Job.translator_note: *Timor* is rendered “column”; the exact sense (a shaft of sunlight) is uncertain.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: the east wind
Job.english_translation: *Kadim* — the sun of the east.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Who hath cleft a channel for the waterflood
Job.english_translation: *Mi pilleg lashetef te'alah* — in Arabic they call hair *shitfa*. For each and every hair on the head I split a channel for it, a pit, to suck from it; for if two were to suck from one pit, they would darken the light of a person’s eyes. And they were not mixed up for Me — between Job (*Iyov*) and enemy (*oyev*) was it mixed up for Me? And this is “from the whirlwind.” Another explanation: *lashetef* — a drop of rain that overflows; I split for each drop a pit in the clouds, for if two drops fell from one pit, they would blur the earth and it would become mud.
Job.translator_note: The sentence about Job and enemy is translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Or a way for the lightning of the thunder
Job.english_translation: *Vederech lachaziz kolot* — who split? Every single voice has a path; and if two were to go on one path, creatures would not bear the sound.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: desolate and waste ground
Job.english_translation: *Sho'ah* — a land that is dark with hunger.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: the drops of dew
Job.english_translation: *Agley tal* — *gelei tal* (“waves of dew”), and the alef is superfluous, like “and my declaration (*ve'achvati*) in your ears” (above 13) — a superfluous alef at the beginning of the word, since it is a noun; and so “*avchat* sword” (Ezekiel 28), like *nibuach cherev*, “the cry of the sword.” Another version: *agley* like *aganei tal* — a kind of basin-channels in which the dew is placed; lamed interchanges with nun, and so in the book of Ezra, *nishkah* like *lishkah* (Nehemiah 13).
Job.translator_note: Printed “above 13” is Job 13:17. Printed “Ezekiel 28” is Ezekiel 21:20 (*avchat cherev*). *Nishkah* appears in Ezra 10:6; *lishkah* is Nehemiah 13:7; the printed “Nehemiah 13” is thus 13:7.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: the hoar-frost of heaven
Job.english_translation: *Kefor* — גריס"א (in Old French).
Job.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Job 38:29 (“grêle”), in forms such as גרישלא; the printed form (גריס"א) differs slightly.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The waters are congealed like stone
Job.english_translation: *Ke'even mayim yitchabe'u* — by the ice that hardens the drop that is on their surface.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: the face of the deep is frozen
Job.english_translation: *Ufnei tehom yitlakkadu* — in it, and they cling together as one.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: the chains of the Pleiades
Job.english_translation: *Ma'adanot kimah* — the binding of the Pleiades, so that all its beams not go forth and destroy the world with cold.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: loose the bands of Orion
Job.english_translation: *O moshchot kesil tefatte'ach* — to bring forth the sun to dispel the cold of the Pleiades.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: the Mazzaroth
Job.english_translation: *Mazzarot* — all the other constellations.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: the Bear with her sons
Job.english_translation: *Ve'ayish* — a large star in the Pleiades, and many stars are fixed in it; and He took two stars from it to open the windows of the flood, and they were split in the sign of Aries; and the Holy One, blessed be He, is destined to return them to it. Tanchuma.
Job.translator_note: Rashi takes *ayish* as a star of the Pleiades; JPS renders “the Bear.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: the ordinances of the heavens
Job.english_translation: *Mishtaro* — the authority (*shetirat*) of the constellations appointed to bring upon the earth cold and heat, summer and winter.
Job.translator_note: *Shetirat* is rendered “authority” as the probable sense.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Canst thou lift up thy voice to the clouds
Job.english_translation: *Hatarim la'av kolekha* — to command it to be bound in the darkness of water, so that an abundance of water cover you; and that is the blackness of the clouds, like “or darkness, that thou canst not see” (above 22); “an abundance of waters” — at your word it will cover you from the heavens.
Job.translator_note: Printed “above 22” is Job 22:11.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And say unto thee
Job.english_translation: *Veyomeru lakh* — in the place to which they were sent, “Here we are; we have done your errand,” for they need not return to their place and report their errand, since the Divine Presence is everywhere.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: the inward parts
Job.english_translation: *Battuchot* — these are the kidneys.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: the mind
Job.english_translation: *Lasechvi* — this is the rooster, in the language of the Sages; and some say this is the heart, which sees and looks ahead and reckons the things that will come to be.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Who can number the clouds by wisdom?
Job.english_translation: *Yesapper* — will speak and warn his charge.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally; the last word is printed in abbreviated form.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: the bottles of heaven
Job.english_translation: *Nivlei* — made like skins, and the rains are gathered in it there, like *nevel yayin* (“a jar of wine”).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: When the dust runneth into a mass
Job.english_translation: *Betzeket afar* — on the day that I poured (*yatzakti*) dust.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: into a mass
Job.english_translation: *Lemutzak* — to the foundation of the world, in its midst.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: the clods cleave fast together
Job.english_translation: *Uregavim yedubbaku* — around it, on the sides, until its length and breadth were filled.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: couch in their dens
Job.english_translation: *Yashochu* — standing crowded together.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: abide in the covert to lie in wait
Job.english_translation: *Lemo arev* — to lie in wait; so is the way of those who lie in ambush: to crouch and bend themselves, so that they not be recognized.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: wander for lack of food
Job.english_translation: *Yit'u levli ochel* — for their father hates them; the Holy One, blessed be He, prepares for them gnats, created from their excrement, and they enter into their mouths.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: the wild goats of the rock
Job.english_translation: *Ya'alei sela* — אשטנבו"ק [Old French]; and she hates her young, and goes up to the top of a high rock when she crouches to give birth, so that it falls to the ground and dies; and the Holy One, blessed be He, prepares an eagle for it, and it receives it on its wings.
Job.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Deuteronomy 14:5 (“le bouquetin”), in forms such as אשטנבוק; the printed form (אשטנבו"ק) matches.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Or canst thou mark when the hinds do calve
Job.english_translation: *Chollel ayalot tishmor* — an expression of the pangs of a woman in travail (Jeremiah): the hind’s womb is narrow and the offspring cannot come out, and at the time of her giving birth I prepare for her a serpent, and it bites her in her womb and it opens; and if it is early or late by a moment, she dies at once; and between those moments I make no exchange — and between Job and enemy was it mixed up for Me?
Job.translator_note: The last clause is translated literally. Printed “Jeremiah” gives no chapter; the expression *chil kayoledah* occurs at Jeremiah 6:24 and 22:23, among others.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: they bring forth their young
Job.english_translation: *Tefalachnah* — their womb splits and brings out the offspring and their birth-pangs.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: They cast out their fruit
Job.english_translation: *Teshallachnah* — from upon them at their giving birth, at the moment that I appoint for them.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Their young ones wax strong
Job.english_translation: *Yachlemu* — they become strong.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: They go forth, and return not again
Job.english_translation: *Velo shavu lamo* — when they have multiplied somewhat, they grow in the open field, among seeds and grasses, and they do not need the raising of their father and mother.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: free
Job.english_translation: *Chofshi* — for no man can raise a wild ass to teach it the work of beasts.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: the wild ass
Job.english_translation: *Arod* — the wild donkey.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: who hath loosed the bands
Job.english_translation: *Mi pitach* — its bonds, for no man’s yoke is upon it.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The range of the mountains is his pasture
Job.english_translation: *Yetur harim mir'ehu* — he himself searches out for himself a place of pasture.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Will the wild-ox
Job.english_translation: *Reim* — like *re'em*.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: to serve thee
Job.english_translation: *Ovdekha* — *le'ovdekha*.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Canst thou bind the wild-ox with his band in the furrow?
Job.english_translation: *Betelem avoto* — (“Or have you bound the wild ox for the sake of the furrow of your ox?”) *avot* is the rope with which (oxen) are tied to the furrows of the plowman.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: will he harrow the valleys after thee
Job.english_translation: *Yesaded* — he will put the field in order.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Wilt thou trust him, because his strength is great?
Job.english_translation: *Hativtach bo* — to gather in your grain, because his strength is great and he can bear much.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: wilt thou leave thy labour to him
Job.english_translation: *Vetaazov elav yegi'acha* — to gather into the house.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The wing of the ostrich eateth joyously
Job.english_translation: *Kenaf renanim ne'elasah* — *ken* is the name of a large bird, *renanim*, and in the language of the Mishnah it is called *bar yochni*.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: her pinions and feathers
Job.english_translation: *Evrah* — every bird is called *evrah* because it flies; that is: or is it a bird named *chasidah*, and a bird named *notzah*? See what its custom is.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: For she leaveth her eggs on the earth
Job.english_translation: *Ta'azov la'aretz beitzeha* — and she goes and warms herself at a distance upon the dust.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And forgetteth that the foot may crush them
Job.english_translation: *Vatishkach ki regel tezureha* — her egg: they would split it.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: She is hardened against her young ones, as if they were not hers
Job.english_translation: *Hiksiach* — she hardens her young from her heart, as if they were not hers.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: her labour be in vain
Job.english_translation: *La'rik yegi'ah* — and she does not fear that she will lose them.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: When the time cometh, she raiseth her wings on high
Job.english_translation: *Ka'et bamarom tamri* — every expression of *hamra'ah* is like a man whose heart leads him astray to go out of his measure and his upbringing and his land, to wander in lands and try other ways; and so “a stubborn and rebellious son” (Deuteronomy 21:18); and in the language of the Gemara, “*imrai*, the daughter-in-law of Rav Zevid, *imrai*, and she went out” (Ketubot 63; and there it reads *imredah*, and see Rashi in Chullin 58 and Bava Metzia 76, s.v. *ve'imru*).
Job.translator_note: Rashi reads *tamri* as “rebel / depart”; JPS renders “raiseth.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: clothed his neck with fierceness
Job.english_translation: *Ra'amah* — an expression of thunder (*ra'am*) and terror, like “their faces thunder (*ra'amu panim*)”.
Job.translator_note: The phrase quoted occurs at Ezekiel 27:35; no reference is printed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Hast thou made him to leap as a locust?
Job.english_translation: *Ka'arbeh* — he leaps and springs like a locust, and makes a commotion around him.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The glory of his snorting is terrible
Job.english_translation: *Nachro* — when he blows with his nostrils with a sound of terror, it is so.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He paweth in the valley
Job.english_translation: *Yachperu ba'emek* — like “and they shall dig (*veyachperu*) for us the land” (ibid. 1); for the way of horsemen is to lie in ambush in valleys and by brooks.
Job.translator_note: Printed “ibid. 1” is Deuteronomy 1:22 (JPS: “that they may search the land for us”).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: rejoiceth in his strength
Job.english_translation: *Veyasis bekoach* — the horse rejoices and goes forth to meet weapons.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: and is not affrighted
Job.english_translation: *Velo yechat* — and will not fear.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The quiver rattleth upon him
Job.english_translation: *Tarneh ashpah* — full of arrows, and they clatter against one another, and their sound is heard.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The glittering spear
Job.english_translation: *Lahav chanit* — a vessel of iron (and a spear of iron) is called *lahav*, like “and the haft also went in after the blade (*lahav*)” (Judges 3:22).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He swalloweth the ground with storm and rage
Job.english_translation: *Yigma eretz* — he makes pits with his feet. ע"א *yigma* like “give me to drink (*hagmi'ini*), I pray thee” (Genesis 24).
Job.translator_note: The abbreviation ע"א is left as printed. Printed “Genesis 24” is Genesis 24:17.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Neither believeth he
Job.english_translation: *Velo ya'amin* — from great joy, for he longs for battle.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: that it is the voice of the horn
Job.english_translation: *Ki kol shofar* — of war.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: As oft as he heareth the horn
Job.english_translation: *Bedei shofar* — an expression of *dai* (“enough”); He answered him with a multitude of horns.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: he saith: ‘Ha, ha! ’
Job.english_translation: *Yomar he'ach* — an expression used by (those who pass) when they rejoice, as one says *ahah* because of grief.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Doth the hawk soar by thy wisdom
Job.english_translation: *Ye'aber netz* — the hawk grows a wing; and it is an angel, resembling the form of a hawk, which holds back the harshness of the south wind by the spreading of its wings, so that it not destroy the world.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Doth the vulture mount up at thy command
Job.english_translation: *Im al picha yagbiah nesher* — the Divine Presence, as it is said, “As an eagle that stirreth up her nest” (Deuteronomy 32:11); He used to remove His retinue so that they not harm Aaron when he came to the Holy [of Holies] on Yom Kippur.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: She dwelleth and abideth on the rock
Job.english_translation: *Sela yishkon veyitlonan* — Aaron was secure with the pan of incense when it was placed on the Foundation Stone.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: From thence she spieth out the prey
Job.english_translation: *Misham chafar ochel* — he prays for the needs of the whole year; and after all this honour he saw the death of his two fledglings, Nadab and Abihu, who died so that My name be sanctified through them, so that My awe fell upon the rest.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Her young ones also suck up blood
Job.english_translation: *Ye'al'u* — and it is only according to the measure: they swallowed blood and water, and it appears as one swallowing much, like one who says “*al, al*”; and so in the language of the Sages, in the giving to drink of the *sotah* (Sotah 20a), “they confuse her (*me'arerin*) and give her to drink against her will”; and so “they raise up a cry of destruction (*ye'o'eru*)” (Isaiah 15:5), an expression of a call of the throat, similar to that; and according to the way, the prophet spoke.
Job.translator_note: The last clause is translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: where the slain are, there is she
Job.english_translation: *Uva'asher chalalim sham hu* — to eat; and our Rabbis likened this whole matter to Aaron, in the Pesikta of *Acharei Mot*.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Shall he that reproveth contend with the Almighty?
Job.english_translation: (The LORD’s reply.) *Harov im Shaddai vesur* — shall the Almighty, a man, domineer?
Job.translator_note: The source begins “(the LORD’s reply)” before the lemma; the printed words are translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He that argueth with God, let him answer it
Job.english_translation: *Mochiach Eloha ya'anenah* — he who comes to argue will answer his words.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Once have I spoken, but I will not answer again
Job.english_translation: (Job’s reply.) *Achat dibbarti* — that is: I said little and I will not add more. And some interpret *achat dibbarti* as that which I said (above 9), “He destroyeth the innocent and the wicked”: I will not answer any more.
Job.translator_note: The source begins “(Job’s reply)” before the lemma. Printed “above 9” is Job 9:22.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Yea, twice
Job.english_translation: *Ushtayim* — that I said (above 13), “Only do not [two things] unto me”; I will not add.
Job.translator_note: Printed “above 13” is Job 13:20.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Wilt thou even make void My judgment?
Job.english_translation: (The LORD’s reply from the whirlwind.) *Ha'af tafer mishpati* — will you even prove that your words are to make void My judgment and to show that it is crooked?
Job.translator_note: The source begins “(the LORD’s reply from the whirlwind)” before the lemma.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Deck thyself
Job.english_translation: *Adeh* — an expression of ornament and jewel.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: tread down
Job.english_translation: *Vehadoch* — an expression of “they ground it (*daku*) in a mortar” (Numbers 15).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Numbers 15” is Numbers 11:8.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Behold now behemoth
Job.english_translation: *Behemot* — prepared for the future.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: his strength is in his loins
Job.english_translation: *Kocho bemotnav* — his testicles are crushed and hidden, and not completely cut off.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: the stays of his body
Job.english_translation: *Bisherirei* — like *shorrekh* (“thy navel”) (Song 7).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Song 7” is Song of Songs 7:3.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He straineth his tail
Job.english_translation: *Yachpotz* — like *yachpoz*: he becomes hard; and so in the language of the Sages, *dechafiza ki ofta* (Chullin 47): hard as wood.
Job.translator_note: The Aramaic phrase is left as printed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: his thighs
Job.english_translation: *Pachadav* — his testicles.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: are knit together
Job.english_translation: *Yesoragu* — twisted strands, like “and they are knit together (*vayishtaregu*)” (Lamentations 1); or *sarigei matteh* in the language of the Mishnah, and it is an expression of *gadil* (a twisted cord).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Lamentations 1” is Lamentations 1:14.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: pipes of brass
Job.english_translation: *Afikei* — strength.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: His gristles
Job.english_translation: *Garmav* — his bones.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: bars of iron
Job.english_translation: *Kematil* — like a load of iron.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He is the beginning of the ways of God
Job.english_translation: *Reshit darkhei El* — from the beginning of creation he was created, chief of the beasts.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He only that made him
Job.english_translation: *Ha'osso* — the Holy One, blessed be He, Himself will slaughter him.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Surely the mountains bring him forth food
Job.english_translation: *Ki bul harim yis'u lo* — and in the Book of Psalms it is written “the beasts upon a thousand hills”: a thousand mountains bring him produce, and every day he grazes all of them. (Up to here Rashi composed; from here on is not Rashi’s language.)
Job.translator_note: The parenthetical remark is a later printed insertion (PI). Psalms 50:10 reads, in JPS, “the cattle upon a thousand hills.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: lotus-trees
Job.english_translation: *Tze'elim* — the shade of trees.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The lotus-trees cover him with their shadow
Job.english_translation: *Yesukkuhu tze'elim tzilalo* — that shade of the covert of the reed and the fen; he is entwined and overshadowed by (many) trees.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Behold, if a river overflow
Job.english_translation: *Hen ya'ashok nahar velo yachpoz* — the Euphrates (*Perat*), whose waters are fruitful and many (*perim verabim*), and it is a great river; he oppresses it and robs it from creatures by his drinking.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: he trembleth not
Job.english_translation: *Velo yachpoz* — his belly does not harden on account of his drinking, like *yachpoz zenavo*.
Job.translator_note: Printed *yachpoz zenavo*; the verse (Job 40:17) reads *yachpotz zenavo*.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He is confident, though the Jordan rush forth
Job.english_translation: *Yivtach ki yaggiach Yarden* — he is confident to draw the whole Jordan into his mouth, if he were drinking there, like *gochi mibaten* (Psalms 22).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Psalms 22” is Psalms 22:10 (*gochi*).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Shall any take him by his eyes
Job.english_translation: *Be'einav yikkachenu* — the Omnipresent will take him when He looks upon him, and he trembles at His awe.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally; Rashi reads the verse differently from JPS.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: with a snare
Job.english_translation: *Bamokeshim* — implements of the craft of hunters, with which they draw up fish.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Canst thou draw out leviathan with a fish-hook?
Job.english_translation: *Timshoch Livyatan* etc. — when you draw him with a hook and put a ring in his nose, will he speak entreaties to you? That is: you will not be able (to approach him) with implements of the net.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: press down his tongue with a cord
Job.english_translation: *Tashkia leshono* — you will lower a rope onto his tongue, to bring him out of his place.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: put a ring into his nose
Job.english_translation: *Agmon* — it is bent like a dome, as in “*agmon*” (Isaiah 9), and it is made of iron, to catch fish with.
Job.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 9” is Isaiah 9:13 (JPS: “rush”).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Canst thou put
Job.english_translation: *Hatasim* — if you put a ring in his nose, to bring him out of the sea.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: with a hook
Job.english_translation: *Uvachoach* — an implement of fishermen.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: bore his jaw through
Job.english_translation: *Tikkav* — like *tinkov*.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Will he make many supplications unto thee?
Job.english_translation: *Harbeh elekha tachanunim* — if he will multiply entreaties to you and ask for his life, that you let him go.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Or will he speak
Job.english_translation: *Im yedabber* — a doubling of the word.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: soft words
Job.english_translation: *Rakkot* — words of entreaty.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Will he make a covenant with thee
Job.english_translation: *Hayikrot brit immakh* — if he will make a covenant to serve you, that you take him to be a slave to you for ever.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Wilt thou play with him as with a bird?
Job.english_translation: *Hatesachek* — if you will play and amuse yourself with him, as if he were a little bird.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: wilt thou bind him for thy maidens
Job.english_translation: *Ve'im tikshernu* — for the necks (another version: for the need) of your little girls, that they may play with him like little birds that are given to infants to play with and to appease them.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Will the bands of fishermen make a banquet of him?
Job.english_translation: *Yikru alav chaverim* — if companions and sorcerers will dig and act wisely against him, to catch him and bring him out of the sea by sorcery, so that they cut him up and divide him among merchants, in the manner of sea-hunters who catch large fish by their wisdom, and merchants come and buy from them.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: make a banquet of him
Job.english_translation: *Yikru* — an expression of “he digs (*koreh*) a pit” (Jeremiah 18).
Job.translator_note: Printed “Jeremiah 18” is Jeremiah 18:20.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: bands of fishermen
Job.english_translation: *Chaverim* — an expression of *vechover chaver*.
Job.translator_note: No reference is printed; the words occur at Deuteronomy 18:11 (JPS: “or a charmer”).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: the merchants
Job.english_translation: *Kena'anim* — merchants.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Canst thou fill his skin with barbed irons?
Job.english_translation: *Hatemalle* — if you will fill your desire and make booths from his skin.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Or his head with fish-spears?
Job.english_translation: *Uvtzaltzal dagim rosho* — and if you will make from his head a fish-*tzaltzal*; a doubling of language.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: fish-spears
Job.english_translation: *Tzaltzal* — a fish-booth; and a booth made from his head he calls a “fish-*tzaltzal*” because it is made from it.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: fish-spears
Job.english_translation: *Tzaltzal* — אמבוריץ in Old French; it is an expression of shade (*tzel*), and it is of doubled words, like *yerakrak*, *adamdam* (Leviticus 14), *petaltol* (Deuteronomy 32), *kaake* (Leviticus 19).
Job.translator_note: Old French. The Old French form is not found in Darmesteter. Printed “Leviticus 14” is Leviticus 14:37; “Deuteronomy 32” is 32:5; “Leviticus 19” is 19:28.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Lay thy hand upon him
Job.english_translation: *Sim alav kappekha* — gather strength to arrange yourself before him, that you place your hands on him to strike him.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Think upon the battle, thou wilt do so no more
Job.english_translation: *Zechor milchamah al tosaf* — and do not add: remember your might, to fight with him in battle.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: thou wilt do so no more
Job.english_translation: *Al tosaf* — from *yasaf*, like “and he knew her again (*lo yasaf od*) no more” (Genesis 38:26), and in Old French רקרייטר"ש; in *al tosaf* the samech is opened because of the end of the verse, like *al tothar* (Genesis 49) and *vatotar* (Ruth 2), and there are many like it.
Job.translator_note: Old French. The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. Printed “Genesis 49” is Genesis 49:4; “Ruth 2” is Ruth 2:14.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Behold, the hope of him is in vain
Job.english_translation: *Hen tochalto nichzavah* — if his hope is deceived, so that he has no strength to fight and to move from his place.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Shall not one be cast down even at the sight of him?
Job.english_translation: *Hagam el mar'av yutal* — if even at the sight of his face a man will be cast down and thrown, to stand before him and look at him because of his awe.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: None is so fierce that dare stir him up
Job.english_translation: *Lo achzar ki ye'orenu* — there is no cruel, mighty and fierce one who will wake him from his sleep and rouse him from his place to raise him.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Who then is able to stand before Me?
Job.english_translation: *Umi hu* etc. — who will present himself and stand before Me, who make all these.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Who hath given Me anything beforehand
Job.english_translation: *Mi hikdimani* — and who is he that anticipated Me by his acceptance to serve Me and to keep My commandments, that I should pay him his reward.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Whatsoever is under the whole heaven is Mine
Job.english_translation: *Tachat kol hashamayim li hu* — all that is in the heavens is Mine, and it is in My hand to pay him his reward, and the wage of his work and service.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Would I keep silence
Job.english_translation: *Lo* — shall I keep silent about his boughs? I will not keep silent about the sons of the righteous man who walked before Me in perfection; and to his sons the good reward of their father will be paid, and they will find good through his merit.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally; the opening is read as a question.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: or his fair array of words
Job.english_translation: *Udevar gevurot vechin erko* — and the matter of his mighty deeds, in which he strengthened himself to do the good and the upright, and the supplication of the righteous man’s order; I will pay his reward, also to his sons after him.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally; “the supplication of the righteous man’s order” (*techinat siduro*) is obscure.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: his boastings
Job.english_translation: *Badav* — his branches, and they are his sons, like “and brought forth branches (*badim*), and shot forth sprigs” (Ezekiel 17:6).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Who can uncover the face of his garment
Job.english_translation: *Mi gillah penei levusho* — returning to the first matters, to speak of Leviathan: who can uncover the scales that are in the doubling of his bridle, in the doubling of his lips when they are open; who is it that will enter there? “In the doubling” — these are the lips, which are double, one above and one below, so that no creature is permitted to enter there because of his awe.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Who can open the doors of his face?
Job.english_translation: *Dalte fanav* — these are the lips when he shuts his mouth: who can open them?

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Round about his teeth is terror
Job.english_translation: *Sevivot shinav eimah* — for because of his fear and terror no creature can approach his teeth.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: His scales are his pride
Job.english_translation: *Ga'avah afikei maginnim* — he has great pride in the strength of his shields: these are the scales upon him that protect him like a shield.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Shut up together as with a close seal
Job.english_translation: *Sagur* — that is the seal of his armour, which is narrow and closed and mighty, for each and every scale is attached to it and clings to its fellow, so that no creature can strike him between the joinings; and this is what is said, “One is so near to another” (Job 41:8), for all are pressed and adjoining one to another.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: They stick together, that they cannot be sundered
Job.english_translation: *Yitlakkedu velo yitparadu* — he still doubles his language: they are joined and united, each one with its fellow, so that they are not separated from one another.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: His sneezings flash forth light
Job.english_translation: *Atishotav tahel or* — with every sneeze that he sneezes, light will shine and gleam.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: flash forth
Job.english_translation: *Tahel* — like “when His lamp shined (*bihilo nero*)” (above 29).
Job.translator_note: Printed “above 29” is Job 29:3.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: his eyes are like the eyelids of the morning
Job.english_translation: *Ve'einav ke'afapei shachar* — his eyes shine and give light like the twilight of the sun, like the time of morning when the sun turns red.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Out of his mouth
Job.english_translation: *Mipiv* — from the flame that goes out from him.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: go burning torches
Job.english_translation: *Mipiv lappidim yehalechu* — torches go out from his mouth.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: sparks of fire
Job.english_translation: *Kidodei esh* — like torches.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: leap forth
Job.english_translation: *Yitmaletu* — its explanation is according to its context: שוינ"ט אישקמוצי"ר in Old French.
Job.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Out of his nostrils goeth smoke
Job.english_translation: *Minchirav yetze ashan* — like a pot blown upon the fire, which sends up smoke.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: burning rushes
Job.english_translation: *Ve'agmon* — its explanation is according to its context: an expression of an earthenware vessel, like *dud nafuach* (“a blown pot”), as it is said (Jeremiah 1:13), “I see a seething pot.”
Job.translator_note: Rashi reads *agmon* as a vessel; JPS renders “rushes.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: His breath kindleth coals
Job.english_translation: *Nafsho gechalim telahet* — burning and blazing coals and kindled flames go out from his mouth.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: In his neck abideth strength
Job.english_translation: *Betzavaro yalin oz* — might.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: dismay danceth before him
Job.english_translation: *Velifanav taduz de'avah* — for there is no languishing and sorrow before him, since he does not fear any creature; *taduz* is an expression of dancing and gladness.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The flakes of his flesh are joined together
Job.english_translation: *Mapelei vesaro davaku* — they cling and are close to one another, for the fish are made into pieces, piece upon piece in his flesh, joined to one another; and in a large fish, when it is cooked, the pieces are seen lying one on another and one next to another; and so goes the order of the word: first he spoke of the scales of Leviathan, and afterward of the pieces of his flesh and the strength of his heart.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: flakes of his flesh
Job.english_translation: *Mapelei* — an expression of doubling of pieces; and it may be said: like *pil'ei pluvei* in the language of the Gemara (Niddah 21), an expression of splitting: the splittings of his pieces.
Job.translator_note: The Aramaic words are left as printed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: are joined together
Job.english_translation: *Davaku* — the bet is vocalized with a short *kamatz*, like “and their tongue cleaved (*davekah*)” and so many with *etnachta* and the end of a verse.
Job.translator_note: No reference is printed; the words occur at Job 29:10 (JPS: “And their tongue cleaved to the roof of their mouth”).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: They are firm upon him
Job.english_translation: *Yatzuk alav* — each and every flake is cast one upon another, so that it will not totter and not separate one from another; *yatzuk* is an expression of *mutzak*, which is an expression of “made,” like *yarod* from *yarad*, *yatzuk* from *yatzak*, *yadua* from *yada*.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: His heart is as firm as a stone
Job.english_translation: *Libo yatzuk kemo even* — his heart within him is firm and founded like a stone fixed in the foundation of the building, firmly.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: firm as the nether millstone
Job.english_translation: *Yatzuk kefelach tachtit* — he doubles his word: that his heart is founded and fixed like the stone of a mill that is placed at the bottom beneath the *pelach rechev*; the upper *pelach rechev* turns and rolls and grinds, and the lower does not move from its place, for it is fixed in its place so that it will not totter. It is called *pelach*, as it is said (Judges 9:53), “And a certain woman cast an upper millstone (*pelach rechev*) upon Abimelech’s head”; and the lower one is called *pelach tachtit*.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally; the sentence “It is called *pelach*” is ambiguous in the print.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: When he raiseth himself up, the mighty are afraid
Job.english_translation: *Mesetto yaguru elim* — from his fear mighty and strong ones are afraid, among fish and among other creatures.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: By reason of despair they are beside themselves
Job.english_translation: *Mishsheverim yitchata'u* — the waves of the sea, which are called *mishbarim*, are diminished before him, for he breaks them with his soaring when he soars and floats in the waves of the sea.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: they are beside themselves
Job.english_translation: *Yitchata'u* — an expression of lack, like “I and my son Solomon shall be *chata'im*” (I Kings 1).
Job.translator_note: Rashi reads *chata'im* as “lacking”; JPS (I Kings 1:21) renders “shall be counted offenders.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: If one lay at him with the sword, it will not hold
Job.english_translation: *Masigehu cherev bli takum* — a mighty man who overtakes him to fight with a sword: his sword will not endure, for he will break it.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: nor the pointed shaft
Job.english_translation: *Chanit massa veshiryah* — and so all these implements of war in the hand of the pursuer will not endure and will not stand before Leviathan. *Massa*: it may be said that it is one of the implements of war, like sword and spear and *siryah*; and it may be said that *massa* is like “a whole stone, quarried (*massa*)” etc. (ibid. 13), and this is its explanation: *chanit massa* — a spear that is great and not easy to carry so much, because it is great and exceedingly strong, as it is said of Goliath the Philistine, “and the shaft (*chetz*) of his spear was like a weaver’s beam, and the head of his spear six hundred,” etc.
Job.translator_note: Printed “ibid. 13” could not be identified; the words “a whole stone, quarried” occur at I Kings 6:7 (JPS: “stone made ready at the quarry”). The quotation about Goliath is I Samuel 17:7; the verse reads *etz* (JPS: “the shaft of his spear”).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: the pointed shaft
Job.english_translation: *Veshiryah* — a coat of mail.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He esteemeth iron as straw, And brass as rotten wood
Job.english_translation: *Yachshov letaven barzel* — weapons of iron are considered before him as straw, and weapons of brass are before him as rotten wood.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: The arrow cannot make him flee
Job.english_translation: *Lo yavricheno ben kashet* — he does not flee from a man with a bow and arrows; and stones of בלסתראו' [Old French] are before him like straw.
Job.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Clubs
Job.english_translation: *Totach* — it is a weapon, and its explanation is according to its context.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He laugheth at the rattling of the javelin
Job.english_translation: *Vayischak lera'ash kidon* — at the noise of the tumult of warriors who carry a javelin, he laughs and plays, for he does not fear them.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Sharpest potsherds are under him
Job.english_translation: *Tachtav chaduddei cheres* — in the place of his spear there are rays of the sun, for his fins which are beneath him, in his belly, shine and give light like the sun.
Job.translator_note: Rashi reads *cheres* as “sun”; JPS renders “potsherds.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Sharpest
Job.english_translation: *Chaduddei* — like a sharp sword, which is sharpened, bright and burnished; and for this reason he calls the rays *chaduddei*.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: potsherds
Job.english_translation: *Cheres* — sun, like “Who commandeth the sun (*cheres*), and it riseth not” (above 9), “before the sun went down” (Judges 14:18).
Job.translator_note: Printed “above 9” is Job 9:7. The printed form in Judges 14:18 reads *tavo*; the verse reads *yavo*.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He spreadeth a threshing-sledge upon the mire
Job.english_translation: *Yirpad charutz alei tit* — a doubled word: *yirpad charutz* refers to *chaduddei cheres*; *alei tit* refers to his underside, in the place where he lays himself on the sand; this mud is the spreading (*ripudo*) that shines like gold, as it is said *rephidato zahav* (Song 3); *charutz* is a kind of gold, as it is said “than fine gold (*micharutz*), her produce” (Proverbs 3), “her fruit is better than *charutz* and than *paz*” (ibid. 8); *yirpad* is an expression of a spread and a couch, like *rephidato zahav* (Song 3).
Job.translator_note: JPS Song 3:10 renders *rephidato zahav* “the top thereof of gold.” The Proverbs quotations are Proverbs 3:14 and 8:19, in Rashi’s wording.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He maketh the deep to boil like a pot
Job.english_translation: *Yartiach kasir metzulah* — like a small pot, blown upon, which quickly brings frequent and continuous boilings; so he makes the deep, which is great and deep, boil.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He maketh the sea like a seething mixture
Job.english_translation: *Yam yasim kamerkachah* — like the compounding of spices, which is mixed and blended; so too he mixes and blends the sea when he moves from his place.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He maketh a path to shine after him
Job.english_translation: *Acharav ya'ir nativ* — when he soars and glides in the sea, behind him the path of the deep shines, for at the time that he soars there is no water there because of the speed of his soaring.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: One would think the deep to be hoary
Job.english_translation: *Yachshov tehom lesevah* — the deep is considered before him as weakness and exhaustion.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: hoary
Job.english_translation: *Lesevah* — to the weakness of old age and hoariness.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Upon earth there is not his like
Job.english_translation: *Ein al afar mashlo* — the mem is *chataf kamatz*, and its explanation is *memshaltho* (“his dominion”), that no creature rules over him; and it is a noun, ruler and dominion; and therefore the mem is vocalized with *chataf kamatz*.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Who is made to be fearless
Job.english_translation: *He'asu* — like *he'asui* (“the made one”), and I do not know a companion for it; and its explanation: the one made without fear and terror, who does not fear creatures, as it is said of the horse, “He mocketh at fear, and is not affrighted” (above 39).
Job.translator_note: Printed “above 39” is Job 39:22.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He looketh at all high things
Job.english_translation: *Et kol gavoah yireh* — he sees all the high ones in the world beneath him; and so is the way of the world: one who stands above sees the one below more than the lower one sees, and the lower one has no might and victory against the upper; and this Leviathan sees all the mighty ones, to say that they have no might against him.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He is king over all the proud beasts
Job.english_translation: *Hu melech al kol bnei shachatz* — a doubled word: over all pride he looks, and he is king over all the sons of *shachatz*, the sons of haughtiness whom I created in My world, who have no dominion and rule against him; and how did your heart lift you to lift up your head before Me, to argue against Me, when I make all these wonders!

Job.english_lemma_JPS: I know that Thou canst do every thing
Job.english_translation: (Job’s reply.) *Yada'ti ki chol tuchal* — that You are able to do everything, as is right in Your eyes.
Job.translator_note: The source begins “(Job’s reply)” before the lemma.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: no purpose can be withholden from Thee
Job.english_translation: *Velo yibatzer mimmekha mezimmah* — he doubles his word: no plan and thought is withheld and hidden from You, for all Your thoughts You can complete and fulfil, for in Your hand are strength and might, and in Your hand to do all that is good in Your eyes; and this verse is like “and now nothing will be withholden (*lo yibatzer*) from them, which they purpose to do” (Genesis 11:6).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Who is this that hideth counsel
Job.english_translation: *Mi zeh ma'lim* — who has hidden and covered the counsel and wonders of the Holy One, blessed be He, without knowledge; I know that all is in Your hand to do, and therefore I told some of His mighty deeds, as they were with my heart, as I knew.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: I understood not
Job.english_translation: *Velo avin* — but I did not understand so much as You have made known to me, for how many wonders are hidden and concealed from me that I do not know.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: I had heard of Thee by the hearing of the ear
Job.english_translation: *Leshema ozen shema'ticha* — many and many times I heard Your report, and now my eye has seen Your Divine Presence.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Wherefore I abhor my words, and repent
Job.english_translation: *Al ken* — since I have merited to behold Your Divine Presence, I despise my life, and I would be comforted were I lodged in the grave, to return to the dust and ashes from which I was taken.
Job.translator_note: Rashi reads “I despise my life”; JPS reads “I abhor my words.”

Job.english_lemma_JPS: and against thy two friends
Job.english_translation: *Uvishnei re'ekha* — Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: for you have not spoken of Me the thing that is right
Job.english_translation: *Ki lo dibbartem* — for you did not speak to Me a right claim, like My servant Job, for he did not transgress against Me, except in what he said (above 9), “He destroyeth the innocent and the wicked,” and through the Satan, who accuses the world, as it is said (ibid.), “If the scourge slay suddenly,” etc.; and if he added to speak because of the severity of the sufferings that weighed heavily and strongly upon him, he spoke; but you transgressed in that you declared him wicked, saying (above 4), “Is not thy fear of God thy confidence,” and you strengthened yourselves against him with the presumption of wickedness, and in the end you were silenced and defeated before him; and you should have comforted him, as Elihu did; and it was not enough for Job, his trouble and his sufferings, but you added to your sins a transgression, to provoke him.
Job.translator_note: Printed “above 9” is Job 9:22; “ibid.” is Job 9:23; “above 4” is Job 4:6.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: offer up for yourselves a burnt-offering
Job.english_translation: *Veha'alitem olah ba'adchem* — so that you may be appeased and reconciled before Me, provided that My servant Job pray for you, so that I forgive your sins, and your transgressions I will remember no more.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: for him will I accept
Job.english_translation: *Ki im panav essa* — for I will lift up his face to receive his prayer; behold, *im* is like *asher*, and so “until they have done drinking (*ad im killu lishtot*)” (Genesis 24:19), “if there be laid on him a ransom (*im kofer*)” (Exodus 21:30), and many like it.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: for you have not spoken of Me the thing that is right
Job.english_translation: *Ki lo* — for you did not.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: and the LORD accepted Job
Job.english_translation: *Vayisa HaShem et penei Iyov* — *vayisa* is like “I have accepted thee (*nasati fanekha*) concerning this thing also” (Genesis 19:21): that He received his prayer and showed him a gracious face.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: changed the fortune of Job
Job.english_translation: *Shav et shevut* — Job, when he prayed, *shav* is an expression of falling, to say in this matter; and it is as though it were written “and He restored the fortune of Job.”
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: when he prayed for his friends
Job.english_translation: *Behitpallelo be'ad re'ehu* — by the merit that he prayed for each and every friend of his.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: twice as much
Job.english_translation: *Lemishneh* — for one, two (it appears that this refers also to what is written above, that it should have said *lehashiv* — Maharaz); and the Scripture was not careful with its word.
Job.translator_note: The parenthetical remark is a later printed insertion (PI); the abbreviation מהר"ז is left as printed.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: of his acquaintance before
Job.english_translation: *Lefanim* — all who were his friends and acquaintances before the sufferings reached him.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: they bemoaned him
Job.english_translation: *Vayanudu lo* — an expression of קונפליינט"א in Old French.
Job.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Job 2:11 (“pour le plaindre”; the same root), in forms such as קונפליינט; the printed form (קונפליינט"א) is a variant spelling.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: a piece of money
Job.english_translation: *Kesitah* — a *ma'ah*.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: every man also gave him a piece of money
Job.english_translation: *Ve'ish* — and each and every one (that is: lest you say the intent is that some gave him a *kesitah* and some gave him a ring, therefore Rashi wrote: *ve'ish* means each and every one — Maharaz).
Job.translator_note: The parenthetical remark is a later printed insertion (PI).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: more than his beginning
Job.english_translation: *Merei'shito* — more than the beginning of his wealth.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: He had also seven sons
Job.english_translation: *Shiv'anah* — they are “times seven,” two sevens, like *shavu'im* (Leviticus 12), which are two weeks.
Job.translator_note: Translated literally; Rashi’s remark appears to count two sevens, whereas JPS reads “seven sons.” Printed “Leviticus 12” is Leviticus 12:5.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And he called the name of the first, Jemimah
Job.english_translation: *Vayikra shem ha'achat Yemimah* — their names were called according to their beauty.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Jemimah
Job.english_translation: *Yemimah* — bright and burnished like the day (*yom*).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Keziah
Job.english_translation: *Ketzi'ah* — her fragrance wafts, pleasant and perfumed like *ketzi'ah* of spice.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: Keren-happuch
Job.english_translation: *Keren hapuch* — after the horn (*keren*) in which they put eye-paint (*kachol*) and soap (*borit*), as it is said, “that thou enlargest thine eyes with paint (*bapuch*)” (Jeremiah 4:30).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: And in all the land were no women found so fair as the daughters of Job
Job.english_translation: *Velo nimtze'u nashim yafot kivnot Iyov* etc. — and no work of beautiful women was found like the work of beauty of the daughters of Job; and this verse is like “and there were men who were unclean” (Numbers 20), and many like it.
Job.translator_note: Printed “Numbers 20” is Numbers 9:6 (JPS: “certain men, who were unclean”).

Job.english_lemma_JPS: their father gave them inheritance among their brethren
Job.english_translation: *Vayiten lahem avihem nachalah betoch acheihem* — because of their importance and beauty he gave them an inheritance together with their brothers.

Job.english_lemma_JPS: being old and full of days
Job.english_translation: *Usva yamim* — from *sava*; one says *sva* in attachment (*bedevekut*).
Job.translator_note: Translated literally.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: The song of songs, which is Solomon’s
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Shir hashirim asher lishlomo* — our Rabbis taught: every “Solomon” (דק"ל why does he not attribute it to his father, as in Proverbs and Ecclesiastes?) mentioned in the Song of Songs is holy — the King to whom peace belongs; a song that is above all songs, which is said to the Holy One, blessed be He, from His congregation and His people, the Assembly of Israel. Rabbi Akiva said: the world was not worthy [as] on the day that the Song of Songs was given to Israel, for all the Writings are holy, and the Song of Songs is the Holy of Holies. Rabbi Elazar ben Azariah said: to what is the matter likened? To a king who took a *se'ah* of wheat and gave it to a baker; he said to him, “Bring out for me so much fine flour, so much bran, so much coarse bran, and sift out for me from it one loaf, sifted and choice.” So all the Writings are holy, and the Song of Songs is the Holy of Holies, for all of it is the fear of Heaven and the acceptance of the yoke of His kingdom.
Song of Songs.translator_note: The abbreviation דק"ל is left as printed. The parenthetical remark is a later printed insertion (PI).

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Yishakeni minshikot pihu* — this song she says with her mouth in her exile and in her widowhood: who will give that King Solomon (*Shelomoh*) would kiss me with the kisses of his mouth, as of old (*me'az*); because there are places where they kiss on the back of the hand and on the shoulder; but I long and yearn that he conduct himself with me as in the first custom, like a bridegroom to a bride, mouth to mouth.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: For thy love is better than wine
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Ki tovim* — to me Your love-tokens (*dodekha*) are better than any wine banquet and than any delight and joy; and it is a Hebrew idiom that every banquet of delight and joy is called by the name of wine, as in “into the place of the banquet of wine” (Esther 7), “They drink not wine with a song” (Isaiah 24), “and there shall be harp and psaltery and pipe and drum, and wine at their feasts” (ibid.). This is the explanation of its meaning; and an example of it is said because He gave them His Torah and spoke with them face to face, and those love-tokens are still sweeter to them than any delight, and they are assured by Him that He will shine forth again upon them, to explain to them the secret of its reasons and the hiddenness of its secrets, and they entreat His face to fulfil His word; and this is “let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth.”
Song of Songs.translator_note: Translated literally. Printed “Esther 7” is Esther 7:8; “Isaiah 24” is Isaiah 24:9; “ibid.” is Isaiah 5:12, where the order of the instruments differs.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Thine ointments have a goodly fragrance
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Lerei'ach shemanekha tovim* — a good name is called after good oil.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Thine ointments have a goodly fragrance
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Lerei'ach shemanekha tovim* — for by them the ends of the earth were made to smell, they who heard Your good report when You did awesome things in Egypt.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Translated literally.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Thy name is as ointment poured forth
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Shemen turak* — your name is called so that it should be said of you, “You are oil that is constantly poured out,” so that your pleasant fragrance goes out afar; for so is the way of pleasant oil: at all times that it is in a sealed phial, its fragrance does not waft; when one opens it and pours out its oil into another vessel, its fragrance wafts.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Therefore do the maidens love thee
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Al ken alamot ahevucha* — Jethro came at the sound of the report and converted; even Rahab the harlot said (Joshua 2), “For we have heard how the LORD dried up,” etc., and through this (ibid.), “for the LORD your God, He is God in heaven above,” etc.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: the maidens
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Alamot* — virgins, because the Speaker likened Him to a young man whom his beloved cherishes; and according to the allegory, the *alamot* are the nations.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Draw me, we will run after thee
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Moshcheni acharekha nartzah* — I heard from your messengers a hint that you said to draw me, and I said, “After you we will run,” to be a wife to you.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: The king hath brought me into his chambers
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Hevi'ani hamelech chadarav* — and also this day I still have gladness and joy that I clung to you.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: We will find thy love more fragrant than wine
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Nazkirah dodekha* — also today, in a living widowhood, I will always mention your former love-tokens, more than any banquet of delight and joy.
