Song of Songs.translator_note: Rashi reads *nazkirah* as “we will mention”; JPS renders “We will find thy love more fragrant than wine.”

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Sincerely do they love thee
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Meisharim ahevucha* — strong love, the love of a plain (*mishor*) without crookedness (*akivah*), an expression of the verse (Isaiah 40), “And the crooked shall be made straight, and the rough places a plain”: that I and my fathers loved you in those days; this is its plain sense according to its context. And according to its allegory, they mention before Him “the kindness of youth, the love of espousals,” your going after Him in the wilderness, a land of drought and of the shadow of death, and they had not even prepared provisions for themselves, and they believed in Him and in His messenger, and did not say, “How shall we go out into the wilderness, not a place of seed and sustenance?” — but went after Him; and He brought them into the chambers of the encirclement of His clouds. In this they are today still glad and rejoicing in Him, even in their poverty and their distress, and they delight in the Torah; and there they mention His love-tokens, more than wine, and the uprightness of their love for Him.
Song of Songs.translator_note: The printed text of this comment appears to break off at the end. No reference is printed for the quoted phrases; they occur at Jeremiah 2:2 and 2:6, and Exodus 12:39 (“neither had they prepared for themselves any victual”). The Isaiah quotation is Isaiah 40:4; the printed העקוב differs from the verse’s העקב (JPS: “the rugged”).

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: I am black, but comely
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Shechorah ani venavah* etc. — you, my companions: let me not be lightly regarded in your eyes, even if my husband forsook me because of the blackness in me; for I am black through the scorching of the sun, and I am comely in the cut of fair limbs. If I am black like the tents of Kedar, which are blackened because of the rains, since they are always spread in the wildernesses, I am easily washed, to be like the curtains of Solomon. This is an allegory: the Assembly of Israel says to the nations, “I am black in my deeds and comely in the deeds of my fathers; and even in my deeds some of them are comely: if there is in me the sin of the Calf, there is in me against it the merit of receiving the Torah.” And she calls the nations “daughters of Jerusalem” because she is destined to become a metropolis for all of them, as Ezekiel prophesied (Ezekiel 16), “and I will give them unto thee for daughters,” like (Joshua 15) “Ekron and her daughters.”
Song of Songs.translator_note: Printed “Ezekiel 16” is Ezekiel 16:61; “Joshua 15” is Joshua 15:45, where JPS renders “Ekron, with its towns.”

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Look not upon me
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Al tir'uni* — do not look at me with contempt, like (I Samuel 6), “because they had gazed upon the ark of the LORD.”
Song of Songs.translator_note: Printed “I Samuel 6” is I Samuel 6:19.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: that I am swarthy
Song of Songs.english_translation: *She'ani shecharchoret* — because my blackness and my ugliness are not from my mother’s womb, but only through the scorching of the sun, for that blackness is easy to whiten when it stands in the shade.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: My mother’s sons were incensed against me
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Bnei immi nicharu vi* — they are the Egyptians among whom I grew up, and who went up with me as a mixed multitude; they were incensed against me secretly and with enticements, until they set me.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Translated literally.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: keeper of the vineyards
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Noterah et hakeramim* — and there the sun scorched me and I was blackened; that is, they gave me to ע"א others; and my vineyard, which was mine from my fathers, I did not keep. We find leaders (*parnasim*) called in Scripture by the language of vineyards, as it is said (Hosea 2), “And I will give her her vineyards from thence,” and we translate (the Targum), *ve'amni lah yat parnasah* (“and I will appoint for her her leaders”); and so (Job 24), “He turneth not by the way of the vineyards.”
Song of Songs.translator_note: The abbreviation ע"א is left as printed. The Aramaic is translated as printed. Printed “Hosea 2” is Hosea 2:17; “Job 24” is Job 24:18.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Tell me, O thou whom my soul loveth
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Haggidah li she'ahavah nafshi* — now the Holy Spirit returns and likens her to a flock beloved by the shepherd. The Assembly of Israel says before Him, as a wife to her husband: “Tell me, you whom my soul loves, how will You pasture Your flock among these wolves in whose midst they are, and how will You make them lie down at noon in this exile, which is a time of distress for them, like noon, which is a time of distress for the flock?”

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: For why should I be as one that veileth herself
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Shalmah ehyeh ke'ot'yah* — and if you say, “What concern is it of yours?” — it is not Your honour that I be like a mourner wrapped over the lip, weeping over my flock.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Translated literally.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Beside the flocks of thy companions
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Al edrei chaverekha* — beside the flocks of the other shepherds who pasture sheep as You do; that is, among the troops of the nations who rely on other gods and have kings and princes who lead them.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: If thou know not, O thou fairest among women
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Im lo teda'i lakh* — this is the reply of the Shepherd: “If you do not know where you should go to pasture your flock, you fairest among women, since the Shepherd has ceased to lead them.”

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Go thy way forth by the footsteps of the flock
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Tze'i lakh be'ikvei hatzon* — look at the stride of the way that the flock went, and the footprints are recognizable: טראצי"ט in Old French. And so many in Scripture: (Psalms 77) “And Thy footsteps (*ikvotekha*) were not known,” (Jeremiah 13) “and thy heels (*akevayikh*) suffer violence,” (Genesis 49) “but he shall troop upon their heel (*akev*),” *yashuv al akeveihem*; and that is the way: go.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Song of Songs 1:8 (“sur les traces de”), in forms such as טראציש and טרצייט; the printed form (טראצי"ט) is a variant spelling. Printed “Psalms 77” is Psalms 77:20; “Jeremiah 13” is Jeremiah 13:22; “Genesis 49” is Genesis 49:19. The phrase *yashuv al akeveihem* is left as printed.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: feed thy kids, beside the shepherds’ tents
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Ur'i et gediotayikh al mishkenot haro'im* — among the dwellings of the other shepherds, with whom you are; and this is the allegory: “If you do not know, my congregation and my assembly, you fairest among women among the other nations, how you will pasture and be saved from the hand of those who oppress you, being among them, so that your sons not perish — look closely at the ways of your first fathers, who received My Torah and kept My charge and My commandments, and go in their ways; and even as a reward for this you will pasture your kids beside the princes of the nations.” And so Jeremiah said (Jeremiah 31), “Set thee up waymarks... set thy heart toward the highway,” etc.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Printed “Jeremiah 31” is Jeremiah 31:21.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: I have compared thee, O my love, To a steed in Pharaoh’s chariots
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Lesusati berichvei Par'oh dimmitikh ra'ayati* — this *lamed* is like the *lamed* in (ibid. 10), “At the sound of His giving a multitude of waters,” and like the *lamed* in “for the fragrance of thy ointments” (*lerei'ach shemanekha*): to a company of many horses that I gathered of my camps to go out to meet you in Pharaoh’s chariots, to save you, as it is said (Habakkuk 3), “Thou hast trodden the sea with Thy horses” — many horses; there *dimmitikh ra'ayati*: I silenced you from your cry, as it is said (Exodus 14), “and you shall hold your peace.” This I saw in the Aggadic books. Another explanation: *dimmitikh ra'ayati*: there I showed everyone that I had pastured [you].
Song of Songs.translator_note: The printed text of the last sentence breaks off after “את” (“you”). Printed “ibid. 10” is Jeremiah 10:13; “Exodus 14” is Exodus 14:14.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: I have compared thee
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Lesusati* — a company of horses, and in Old French קבליי"שא.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Song of Songs 1:9 (“à ma houppe de chevaux”), in forms such as קבליישא; the printed form (קבליי"שא) matches.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: I have compared thee
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Dimmitikh* — אר"ישמאי in Old French, like (Judges 20), “and me they thought to have slain (*dimu*)”; for there I adorned you with fair ornaments.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Song of Songs 1:9 (“je t’ai comparée”), in forms such as אדישמאי and אשמאי; the printed form (אר"ישמאי) differs slightly (ר for ד). Printed “Judges 20” is Judges 20:5.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Thy cheeks are comely with circlets
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Na'vu lechayayikh bator'im* — rows of ear-rings and golden forehead-plates.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Thy neck with beads
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Tzavarekh bacharuzim* — golden necklaces and pearls strung on golden threads, from the spoil of the sea.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: We will make thee circlets of gold
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Torei zahav na'aseh lakh* — I and my court took counsel before Pharaoh came, that I would entice him and strengthen his heart to pursue you with all the splendour of the treasures of his storehouses, so that we might make for you the circlets of golden ornaments.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Translated literally.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: With studs of silver
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Im nekudot hakesef* — that you already had, which you took out of Egypt; for the spoil of the sea was greater than the spoil of Egypt.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: studs of silver
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Nekudot* — silver vessels dotted and adorned with spots and colours.
Song of Songs.translator_note: The printed word *chavarburot* is translated as “spots.”

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: While the king sat at his table
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Ad shehamelech bimesibbo* — the Assembly of Israel replies and says: all this is true; You repaid me with good and I repaid You with evil, for while the King was at the table, the reclining-place of His wedding-canopy.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: My spikenard sent forth its fragrance
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Nardi natan richo* — a substitution for “to cause a stench”: while the Divine Presence was at Sinai, I spoiled with the Calf; and the Scripture wrote the language of affection, “gave its fragrance,” and did not write “made stink” or “made rot,” because Scripture speaks in clean language. (See Rashi in tractate Shabbat, chapter “Rabbi Akiva,” that the reason it did not write “made stink” or “made rot” is out of affection; however, according to the explanation of the Tosafot there, who explain: and this is what it says: that it wrote “gave” and not “left” is out of affection; however, that it did not write “made stink” or “made rot” is in any case out of clean language.)
Song of Songs.translator_note: Translated literally. The parenthetical remark is a later printed insertion (PI).

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: My beloved is unto me as a bag of myrrh
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Tzror hamor dodi li* — my beloved is made for me like one who has a bundle of myrrh in his bosom and says to him, “Here is this bundle, which will give a better fragrance than the first one that you lost.” So the Holy One, blessed be He, was appeased toward Israel for the deed of the Calf, and found atonement for their iniquity, and said, “Donate for the Tabernacle,” and the gold of the Tabernacle came and atoned for the gold of the Calf.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: lieth betwixt my breasts
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Bein shaddai yalin* — even though I had trespassed against Him, He said to dwell there.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: betwixt my breasts
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Bein shaddai* — between the two staves of the Ark.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: a cluster of henna
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Eshkol hakofer* — there is a perfume named *kofer*, like (Song 4) “henna with spikenard,” and it is made like clusters.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: In the vineyards of En-gedi
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Bekarmei Ein Gedi* — a place name, and there it is found; and I saw in the Aggadah that those vineyards make fruit four or five times a year; and it is an allegory for the many atonements and pardons that the Holy One, blessed be He, pardoned them for the many trials with which they tried Him in the wilderness.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Behold, thou art fair, my love
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Hinakh yafah ra'ayati* — I was ashamed of my spoiling, and He strengthened me with pleasing words, saying (Numbers 14), “I have pardoned according to thy word,” and behold you are fair, and fair, for your eyes are doves. That is: a bride whose eyes are ugly, her whole body needs examination, and one whose eyes are comely, her body needs no examination; and the allegory is this: I pardoned you for your iniquity, and behold you are fair in what was done, and you are fair in what is heard; fair in the deeds of the fathers, fair in your deeds, for:
Song of Songs.translator_note: The printed text of this comment breaks off at the end (“for:”). Printed “Numbers 14” is Numbers 14:20.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Thine eyes are as doves
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Einayikh yonim* — there are righteous ones in your midst who cling to Me, like this dove which, once it has known its mate, does not let him mate with another: (Exodus 32) “And all the sons of Levi gathered themselves together unto him,” and they did not err with the Calf. And further, you are fair in the work of the Tabernacle, as it is said (Exodus 39), “and, behold, they had done it,” etc., “And Moses blessed them”; behold, He praised her for this.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Translated literally (the printed verb *shemashmekheret*).

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Behold, thou art fair, my beloved, yea, pleasant
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Hinekha yafeh dodi af na'im* — it is not my beauty but Yours: You are the fair one.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: yea, pleasant
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Af na'im* — for You passed over my transgressions and made Your Divine Presence dwell within me; and this is the praise of the descent of the fire (Leviticus 9), “and when all the people saw it, they shouted.”

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Also our couch is leafy
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Af arsenu ra'ananah* — through Your pleasantness, behold, our couch is leafy with our sons and our daughters, who are all gathered to You here, as it is said (ibid. 8), “and the congregation was assembled,” etc. The Tabernacle is called a bed (*mittah*), as it is said, “Behold, it is the litter of Solomon” (Song 3); and so the Temple is called *mittah*, as it is said of Joash (II Chronicles 25), “in the bed-chamber (*chadar hamittot*), which is in the house of the LORD,” because they are the fruit and increase of Israel.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Printed “ibid. 8” is Leviticus 8:4. Printed “II Chronicles 25” could not be matched; the words *chadar hamittot* occur at II Chronicles 22:11 and II Kings 11:2, and II Chronicles 22:12 has “the house of God.” “Song 3” is Song of Songs 3:7.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: The beams of our houses are cedars
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Korot bateinu arazim* — this is praise of the Tabernacle.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: our panels are cypresses
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Rahitenu* — I do not know whether it is an expression of boards or an expression of bars; but I know that even in the language of the Mishnah we learned, “the *rahitei* of a man’s house testify about him.”

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: I am a rose of Sharon
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Chavatzelet* — it is a rose (*shoshanah*).

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: A lily of the valleys
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Shoshanat ha'amakim* — more fair than the lily of the mountains, because it is always moist, since the power of the sun does not rule there.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: As a lily among thorns
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Keshoshanah bein hachochim* — that they pierce them, and always she stands built up and red; so is my beloved among the daughters: they entice her to run after them, to commit harlotry like them after other gods, and she stands in her faithfulness.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Translated literally.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: As an apple-tree among the trees of the wood
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Ketapuach* — a tree of apples, when it is among barren trees it is dear above all of them, for its fruit is good in taste and smell.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: So is my beloved among the sons
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Ken dodi bein habanim* — among the young men; the allegory: so the Holy One, blessed be He, is chosen from among all the gods; therefore “in His shade I delighted and sat.” And an Aggadic midrash: all flee from this apple tree because it has no shade; so all the nations fled from the Holy One, blessed be He, at the giving of the Torah, but I “in His shade delighted and sat.”

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: He hath brought me to the banqueting-house
Song of Songs.english_translation: *El beit hayayin* — the Tent of Meeting, where its details and explanations of the Torah were given.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: his banner over me is love
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Vediglo alai ahavah* — and my company, which He made into a banner for Himself, love is upon me; I still remember His love; and *diglo*: אשר"ייט in Old French.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Song of Songs 2:4 (“il lève l’étendard”), in forms such as אטרייט; the printed form (אשר"ייט) differs slightly. The rest is translated literally.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Stay you me with dainties
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Samchuni* — now in the manner of the sick, with *ashishei anavim* or with *ashishot* of pure fine flour.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Translated literally; *ashishei* and *ashishot* are left as printed.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: refresh me with apples
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Rapaduni* — spread my couch (*ripidati*) around me with apples for good fragrance, in the manner of the sick, for I am sick for His love, for I thirst for Him here in my exile; *ripidah* is an expression of spreading, like (Job 41) “He spreadeth a threshing-sledge (*yirpad*) upon the mire.”

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Let his left hand be under my head
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Semolo tachat leroshi* — in the wilderness.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: And his right hand embrace me
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Vimino techabkeni* — a journey of three days He journeys to search out for them a resting-place, and at the place of rest He sends down for them manna and quail; all this I now remember in my exile, and am sick for His love.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Hishba'ti etchem* — you, the nations.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: By the gazelles, and by the hinds of the field
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Bitzva'ot o be'ayalot* — that you be ownerless and food, like gazelles and hinds.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: That you awaken not, nor stir up love
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Im ta'iru ve'im te'orerru et ha'ahavah* — that is between me and my beloved, to change it and exchange it and to ask me to be enticed after you.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: until it please
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Ad shetechpatz* — as long as it is fixed in my heart and He desires me.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: until it please
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Ad shetechpatz* — like *ad shehamelech bimesibbo*, “while the King is at his table.”

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: That you awaken not
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Im ta'iru* — if you cause hatred, like (I Samuel 24) *vayehi arekha*, (Daniel 4) “and the interpretation thereof to thine enemies (*la'arekha*).”
Song of Songs.translator_note: Translated literally. Printed “I Samuel 24” could not be matched; the form *ariekha* occurs at I Samuel 28:16 (JPS: “is become thine adversary”). Printed “Daniel 4” is Daniel 4:16.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: nor stir up love
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Ve'im te'orerru* — like “he who claims (*ha'orer*) against a field,” *calonjier* in Old French. There are many Aggadic midrashim, and they are not settled according to the order of the matters, for I see that Solomon prophesied and spoke of the going out of Egypt, and of the giving of the Torah, and the Tabernacle, and the entry into the Land, and the Chosen House, and the Babylonian exile, and the coming of the Second Temple and its destruction.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Song of Songs 2:7 (“si vous réclamez”), in forms such as קלוניר; the printed form (קלניי"ר) is a variant spelling.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Hark! my beloved!
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Kol dodi* — the singer returns to the first matters, like one who has abridged his words and goes back to say, “Did I not tell you the beginning of the matters? He began and said, ‘The king hath brought me into his chambers,’ and did not recount how He remembered them in Egypt in the language of affection”; and now he returns and says: this drawing that I told of, that my beloved drew me and I ran after Him — thus I was despairing, I used to say of the redemption, until the end of the four hundred years that were said at the Covenant between the Pieces.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Translated literally.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: behold, he cometh
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Kol dodi hineh zeh ba* — before the end, leaping on the mountains and skipping on the hills.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: My beloved is like a gazelle or a young hart
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Dome dodi litzvi* — in the lightness of his running, that he hastened to come like a gazelle and like a young hart; *ofer ha'ayalim*: a young hart (*ofer ayil*), a youth.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Behold, he standeth behind our wall
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Hineh zeh omed* etc. — I thought to sit as an abandoned wife for many days, and behold, He made known that He was standing and peering from the windows of heaven at what was being done to me, as it is said (Exodus 3), “I have surely seen the affliction of My people,” etc.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: My beloved spoke
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Anah* — an expression of answering and an expression of crying out, a loud voice; and this is the prototype for all (Deuteronomy 27), “And the Levites shall speak.”
Song of Songs.translator_note: Rashi reads *anah* as “raised his voice”; JPS renders Deuteronomy 27:14 “shall speak.”

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: and said unto me
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Ve'amar li* — through Moses.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Rise up, my love, my fair one, and come away
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Kumi lakh* — (Exodus 3) “I will bring you up out of the affliction of Egypt.”
Song of Songs.translator_note: Printed “Exodus 3” is Exodus 3:17.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: the winter is past
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Hineh hastav avar* — there is now no toil on the road; *stav*, winter, Targum *sitva*.
Song of Songs.translator_note: The Aramaic is translated as printed.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: The flowers appear on the earth
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Hanitzanim nir'u va'aretz* — the days of the summer sun have drawn near, when the trees put forth blossoms and travellers delight to see them.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: The time of singing is come
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Et hazamir higia* — for the birds give song and a pleasant voice to travellers.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: the voice of the turtle is heard in our land
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Vekol hator* — as its plain sense: turtle-doves and young pigeons; it is the way of the birds to be singing and chirping in the days of Nisan.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: The fig-tree putteth forth her green figs
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Hate'enah chanetah pageha* — as its plain sense.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: the vines in blossom
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Vehagefanim semadar* — when the blossom falls and the grapes are separated from one another and recognizable, each grape by itself is called *semadar*. All this matter in its plain sense is the language of loving enticement, with which a young man pleases his betrothed to go after him; so did my beloved do for me.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Arise, my love, my fair one, and come away
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Anah dodi* — through Moses.
Song of Songs.translator_note: The source lemma belongs to Song of Songs 2:10–12 and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Arise, my love, my fair one, and come away
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Ve'amar li* — through Aaron.
Song of Songs.translator_note: The source lemma belongs to Song of Songs 2:10–12 and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Arise, my love, my fair one, and come away
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Kumi lakh* — rouse yourself (Exodus 11), “and let them ask every man of his neighbour.”
Song of Songs.translator_note: Printed “Exodus 11” is Exodus 11:2.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: The fig-tree putteth forth her green figs
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Ki hineh hastav avar* — these are the four hundred years: I skipped over them, counting them from the birth of Isaac.
Song of Songs.translator_note: The source lemma belongs to Song of Songs 2:10–12 and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: The fig-tree putteth forth her green figs
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Hagashem* — which is the toil of the winter, has passed and gone; that is: eighty-six years of the severity of the bondage were decreed upon you, and they have gone; from the birth of Miriam the Egyptians made the bondage hard upon Israel, and therefore she was called Miriam, from *mererum* (“they embittered them”).
Song of Songs.translator_note: The source lemma belongs to Song of Songs 2:10–12 and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: The fig-tree putteth forth her green figs
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Hanitzanim nir'u va'aretz* — behold, Moses and Aaron are prepared for you for all your needs.
Song of Songs.translator_note: The source lemma belongs to Song of Songs 2:10–12 and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: The fig-tree putteth forth her green figs
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Et hazamir higia* — for you are destined to say a song at the sea.
Song of Songs.translator_note: The source lemma belongs to Song of Songs 2:10–12 and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: The fig-tree putteth forth her green figs
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Vekol hator* — the voice of the great traveller (*hatayyar*); another explanation: *kol hator* — a voice that the time of your going out of Egypt has come.
Song of Songs.translator_note: The source lemma belongs to Song of Songs 2:10–12 and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under. The words “the great traveller” are translated literally.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: The fig-tree putteth forth her green figs
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Hate'enah chanetah pageha* — the time of the first-fruits has drawn near, for you will enter the Land.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: the vines in blossom
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Vehagefanim semadar* — the time of the wine libations has drawn near. Another explanation: the upright among you have formed fruit and blossomed before good deeds, and have given forth a good fragrance.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Translated literally (“before good deeds”).

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Arise, my love, my fair one, and come away
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Kumi lechi* — it is written with a superfluous yod: *kumi lakh*, to receive the Ten Commandments.
Song of Songs.translator_note: The written form (*ketiv*) is לכי, with an extra yod.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: The fig-tree putteth forth her green figs
Song of Songs.english_translation: Another explanation: *hate'enah chanetah pageha* — these are the transgressors of Israel who perished in the three days of darkness.
Song of Songs.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: the vines in blossom give forth their fragrance
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Vehagefanim semadar natenu rei'ach* — these are those remaining among them, who repented and were accepted; thus it is expounded in the Pesikta.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: O my dove, that art in the clefts of the rock
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Yonati bechagvei hasela* — this is said of that hour when Pharaoh pursued after them and overtook them camping at the sea, and there was no place to flee before them because of the sea, nor to turn aside because of wild beasts. To what were they likened at that hour? To a dove fleeing from the hawk and entering the clefts of the rocks, with a serpent blowing at her: if she enters inside, behold the serpent; if she goes outside, behold the hawk. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to her: “Show me your appearance, the excellence of your deeds: to whom do you turn in time of trouble?”

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: let me hear thy voice
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Hashmi'ini et kolekh* — (Exodus 14) “and the children of Israel cried out unto the LORD.”
Song of Songs.translator_note: Printed “Exodus 14” is Exodus 14:10.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: in the clefts of the rock
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Bechagvei* — in a cleft, and it is an expression of breaking; similar to it: (Psalms 107) “they reel to and fro” (*yachogu veyanu'u*), (Isaiah 19) “and the land of Judah shall become a terror (*lechaga*) unto Egypt”; and when they are many he calls them *chagvei*; and so *katzeh* (“end”) — *ketzvei*; and so (II Samuel 10) “and he cut off their garments (*midveihem*).”
Song of Songs.translator_note: Rashi reads *chaga* as “a break”; JPS renders Isaiah 19:17 “a terror.” Printed “Psalms 107” is Psalms 107:27; “Isaiah 19” is Isaiah 19:17; “II Samuel 10” is II Samuel 10:4.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: the cliff
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Madregah* — *eschelons* [printed אישקלו"יוש] in Old French (steps): when they make a trench around the towers and pour the earth on top, to raise the mound around, they make it into steps, steps one above another.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Song of Songs 2:14 (“les échelons”), in forms such as אישקליש and אישקלשא; the reading is *eschelons*, from Darmesteter’s footnote; the printed form (אישקלו"יוש) is a variant spelling.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: in the covert of the cliff
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Beseter hamadregah* — at times there are holes in them, and creeping things and birds enter there.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Take us the foxes, the little foxes, that spoil the vineyards
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Echezu lanu shu'alim* — the Holy One, blessed be He, heard their voice, commanded the sea and it swept them away; this is “take us the foxes”: these little ones with the big ones, for even the little ones were destroying the vineyards while “our vineyards are in blossom,” that is, the grapes are tender: when a daughter of Israel gave birth to a male and hid him, the Egyptians would enter their houses and search for the males, and the infant was hidden, a year old or two years old; and they would bring infants from an Egyptian house, and the Egyptian infant would speak and the Israelite infant would answer him from the place where he was hidden, and they would search and throw him into the Nile. And why did he call them foxes? As this fox looks behind him to flee, so the Egyptians looked behind them, as it is said (Exodus 14), “Let us flee from the face of the children of Israel.”
Song of Songs.translator_note: Printed “Exodus 14” is Exodus 14:25, where the verse reads *mipnei Yisra'el* (JPS: “from the face of Israel”).

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: the little foxes
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Shu'alim ketanim* — it is written defectively, without a vav, because He exacted punishment from them with water that was measured in the hollow (*sho'al*) of the Omnipresent.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: My beloved is mine, and I am his
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Dodi li va'ani lo* — He demanded all His needs from me and commanded only me: “Make the Passover,” “Sanctify the firstborn,” “Make the Tabernacle,” “Offer burnt-offerings”; and He demanded nothing from any other.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: and I am his
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Va'ani lo* — I demanded all my needs from Him, and not from other gods.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: That feedeth
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Haro'eh* — His flock.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: among the lilies
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Bashoshanim* — in a good, pleasant and beautiful pasture.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Until the day breathe
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Ad shefayach hayom* — this refers to the verse above it, “My beloved is mine, and I am his,” until the time that sin caused it, and the sun scorched me, like the heat of the day, and the scorching heat grew strong.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: and the shadows flee away
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Venasu hatzelalim* — we sinned with the Calf, we sinned with the spies; and “the shadows flee”: the merits that shield us; I have broken off His yoke.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Turn, my beloved
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Sov demeh lekha dodi* — I caused Him to withdraw from me, on mountains that are separated from me.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: mountains of spices
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Bether* — an expression of division and separation.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: By night on my bed
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Al mishkavi baleilot* — in my distress, when I sat in darkness for thirty-eight years in which Israel were under ban.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: I sought him, but I found him not
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Bikkashtiv velo metzativ* — (Exodus) “for I am not among you” (ibid.) “for I will not go up in the midst of thee.”
Song of Songs.translator_note: Printed “Exodus” gives no chapter; the first quotation occurs at Deuteronomy 1:42, the second at Exodus 33:3.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: I will rise now
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Akumah na* — “and I will seek” (Exodus 33), “And Moses besought” (ibid. 32), “I will go up unto the LORD” (ibid.).
Song of Songs.translator_note: Compare Exodus 33:7, 32:11 and 32:30.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: The watchmen that go about the city found me
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Metza'uni hashomerim* — Moses and Aaron.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Saw you him whom my soul loveth
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Et she'ahavah nafshi re'item* — what did you find in his mouth?

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Scarce had I passed from them
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Kim'at she'avarti mehem* — close to their separation from me, at the end of forty years.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: When I found him whom my soul loveth
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Ad shemetzati* — who was with me in the days of Joshua, to conquer thirty-one kings.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: I held him, and would not let him go
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Achaztiv velo arpennu* — I gave him no slackening until I brought him to the Tabernacle at Shiloh, on account of all this that he did for me.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Hishba'ti etchem* — the nations, when I was in exile among you.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: That you awaken not, nor stir up love
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Im ta'iru ve'im te'orerru* — the love of my beloved from me, by enticement and incitement to forsake Him, to turn back from following Him.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Until it please
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Ad shetechpatz* — while His love is desired upon me.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Who is this that cometh up out of the wilderness
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Mi zot olah min hamidbar* — when I was walking in the wilderness and the pillar of fire and the cloud went before me and killed snakes and scorpions and burned the thorns and the briers to make the road level, and the cloud and the smoke rose, and the nations saw them and were astonished at my greatness and said, “Who is this?” — that is, how great is this one who comes up from the wilderness, etc.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Like pillars of smoke
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Ketimrot ashan* — tall and erect like a palm (*tamar*).

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Perfumed with myrrh and frankincense
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Mekutteret mor* — after the cloud of incense that rose in columns above the inner altar.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: of the merchant
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Rochel* — the name of the one who sells all kinds of spices.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: all powders
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Avkat* — because it is crushed and ground fine like dust (*avak*).

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Behold, it is the litter of Solomon
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Hinneh mitato shelishlomo* — the Tent of Meeting and the Ark, which they carried in the wilderness.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Threescore mighty men are about it
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Shishim gibborim saviv lah* — sixty myriads around it.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Of the mighty men of Israel
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Migibborei Yisrael* — of those who go out to the army only, apart from those younger than twenty and those past sixty.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: expert in war
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Melummedei milchamah* — the war of the Torah; and so the priests who surround it, camping around the Tabernacle, who are taught the order of their service.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Every man hath his sword upon his thigh
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Ish charbo* — their weapons are tradition (*masoret*) and mnemonic signs, by which they establish the learning and the transmission so that it not be forgotten.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Because of dread in the night
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Mipachad baleilot* — lest they forget it and troubles come upon them; and so it says (Psalms 2), “Do homage in purity, lest He be angry, and you perish in the way.”
Song of Songs.translator_note: Printed “Psalms 2” is Psalms 2:12.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: King Solomon made himself a palanquin
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Apiryon asah lo* — this is the Tent of Meeting that was set in the Tabernacle at Shiloh; “made for himself a palanquin”: a canopy, a crown, for honour.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: The top thereof of gold
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Rephidato* — his couch and his dwelling upon the cover (*kapporet*), which is of gold.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: The seat of it of purple
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Merkavo argaman* — this is the curtain (*parochet*) that hung and rode on poles from pillar to pillar.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: The inside thereof being inlaid with love
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Tocho ratzuf* — arranged with the pavement (*ritzpat*) of love: the Ark, the cover, the cherubim and the tablets.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: From the daughters of Jerusalem
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Mibnot Yerushalayim* — these are Israel, fearing and whole toward the Holy One, blessed be He.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: O you daughters of Zion
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Benot Tzion* — sons who are distinguished for Him by circumcision, tefillin and tzitzit.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: the crown wherewith his mother hath crowned him
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Ba'atarah she'itrah lo immo* — the Tent of Meeting, which is crowned with the colours of blue, purple and scarlet wool. Rabbi Nechunia said: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai asked his teacher Elazar son of Rabbi Yose: “Is it possible that you heard from your father what is meant by ‘wherewith his mother hath crowned him’?” He said to him: A parable of a king who had an only daughter and loved her exceedingly; he did not cease to cherish her until he called her “my daughter,” as it is said (Psalms 45), “Hearken, O daughter”; he did not cease to cherish her until he called her “my sister,” as it is said, “Open to me, my sister”; he did not cease to cherish her until he called her “my mother,” as it is said (Isaiah 51), “Attend unto Me, O My people, and give ear unto Me, O My nation” — and it is written *ulimmi* (“and to my mother”). Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai arose and kissed him on his head, etc.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Printed “Psalms 45” is Psalms 45:11; “Open to me, my sister” is Song of Songs 5:2. Printed “Isaiah 51” is Isaiah 51:4, where JPS renders *ulumi* “My nation”; Rashi (as the Midrash) reads it as “my mother.”

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: in the day of his espousals
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Beyom chatunato* — the day of the giving of the Torah, when they crowned Him for themselves as King and accepted His yoke.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: in the day of his espousals
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Uveyom simchat libo* — this is the eighth day of the consecration, on which the Tabernacle was dedicated in the wilderness.
Song of Songs.translator_note: The source lemma (“And in the day of the gladness of his heart”) falls in the next verse in JPS’s division (Song of Songs 4:1 begins with it); the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Behold, thou art fair, my love
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Hinakh yafah ra'ayati* — He praised them and accepted them, and their offerings were pleasing to Him.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Behold, thou art fair, my love
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Ad shefayach hayom* — for they sinned before Me in the days of Hophni and Phinehas.
Song of Songs.translator_note: The source lemma belongs to another verse of the Song of Songs and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Thine eyes are as doves
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Einayikh yonim* — your colours and your appearance and your likeness are like this dove, which clings to its mate; and when it is slaughtered it does not flutter but stretches out its neck; so you gave the shoulder to bear My yoke and My fear.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: behind thy veil; Thy hair is as a flock of goats
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Mibe'ad letzamatekh, sa'arekh ke'eder ha'izim* — this praise is like the praise of a woman beloved by the bridegroom: from within your bands, your hair is beautiful and shines like *tzohar* and *levanonit*, like the hair of white goats that descend from the mountains, whose hair shines from afar. And the allegory in which the Assembly of Israel is likened to this is: from within your camps and your dwellings, even the empty ones among you are dear to Me, like Jacob and his sons who streamed down from Mount Gilead when Laban overtook them there. Another explanation: like those who warred against Midian across the Jordan, which is in the land of Gilead; and this language is in the Midrash of the Song of Songs.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Translated literally; *tzohar* and *levanonit* are left as printed.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: behind thy veil
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Mibe'ad* — an expression of “from within,” for most occurrences of *be'ad* in Scripture are a thing that covers and shields against another thing, like (Job 9) “And sealeth up the stars (*uve'ad kochavim*),” (Jonah 2) “The earth with her bars (*be'adi*) closed upon me,” (Job 28) “Can He judge through (*ha-be'ad*) the dark cloud?”; and *mibe'ad* is the thing that is within with respect to that *be'ad*; therefore it says *mibe'ad*.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Printed “Job 28” is Job 22:13.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: thy veil
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Tzamatekh* — an expression of a thing that compresses the hair so that it does not fly loose, and this is the net (*sevachah*) and the bands. And it is not possible to explain *tzamatekh* as an expression of *tzomet*, with the tav rooted in the word, for then it would have had to be dageshed when it is attached to a *heh* to act on it as a feminine, or to a *vav* to act on it as a masculine, like the tav of *Shabbat*: when he gives it to a feminine it is dageshed, like *chaggah*, *chodesh*, *veshabbetah*, and so for a masculine, “the burnt-offering of the Sabbath on its Sabbath” (*olat Shabbat beshabbato*); and the tav of *tzamatekh*, which is soft, must by necessity come in place of a *heh*, and the name of the band would be *tzamah*; and when it is attached to give it to a masculine or a feminine the *heh* turns into a *tav*, such as *shifchah*, which turns, so as to say *shifchato*, *shifchatah*; and so *amah* — *amato*, *amatah*; *ervah* — *ervato*, *ervatah*; and so this: *tzamah*, *tzamato*, *tzamatah*, *tzamati*, *tzamatekh*.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Translated literally; the examples “*chaggah*, *chodesh*, *veshabbetah*” are left as printed.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: that trail down
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Shegalshu* — that were shorn bald; *gibe'ach* is translated *gelush*: when the animals descend from the mountain, the mountain is found bald and stripped by them.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Thy teeth are like a flock of ewes all shaped alike
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Shinayikh ke'eder haktzuvot* etc. — this praise too is in the language of a woman’s beauty.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Thy teeth
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Shinayikh* — thin and white and arranged in their order like wool; and the order of a flock of ewes that are selected from the rest of the flock by count and number, entrusted to a wise and proper shepherd to take care of their wool, which they make into articles of *milat*, and they guard them from the time of their birth so that the wool not be soiled, and wash them day after day.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Translated literally; *milat* is left as printed.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: all are paired
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Shekulam mat'imot* — an expression of *tom* (Psalms 38), “There is no soundness (*metom*) in my flesh” — that is, whole: אינטכי"ש in Old French.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Song of Songs 4:2 (“entières”), in forms such as אנטירט and אנטיריש; the printed form (אינטכי"ש) differs slightly (a *kaf* where the forms have *resh*). Printed “Psalms 38” is Psalms 38:4.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: none faileth among them
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Veshakkulah* — no bereavement (*shekhol*) and no blemish are in them; and this likeness is said of the mighty men of Israel, who cut down and devour their enemies with their teeth around them, and they keep far from the plunder of Israel and from forbidden relations, that they not be sustained by transgression. And this praise is said of the twelve thousand men who warred against Midian by count and number, that none of them was suspected of forbidden relations, as it is said (Numbers 31), “and there lacketh not one man of us”; and even for the thought of the heart they brought their atonement; and also for robbery they were not suspected, for Scripture testifies of them (ibid.), “and they took all the spoil, and brought to Moses and to Eleazar the priest,” etc.; and not one of them kept back one cow or one donkey.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Printed “Numbers 31” is Numbers 31:49; the second quotation combines Numbers 31:11–12.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Thy lips are like a thread of scarlet
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Kechut hashani sifotayikh* — fit to promise and to keep their promise, as the spies did for Rahab the harlot, to whom they said (Joshua 2), “this line of scarlet thread,” etc., and they kept their promise.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Printed “Joshua 2” is Joshua 2:18.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: thy mouth is comely
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Umidbarekh* — your speech; and it is from the root (Ezekiel 33) “that talk of thee (*hanidberim*) by the walls,” (Malachi 3) “Then they that feared the LORD spoke one with another (*nidberu*)” — *parleriz* in Old French.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Song of Songs 4:3 (“et ton langage”), in forms such as פרלדיץ and פרלריץ; the printed form (פרל"ריץ) matches the second. Printed “Ezekiel 33” is Ezekiel 33:30; “Malachi 3” is Malachi 3:16. The Old French in the printed text is written פרל"ריץ.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Thy temples are like a pomegranate split open
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Rakatekh* — it is the height of the face, which is called *pommelis* in Old French, near the eyes; and in the language of the Gemara they call it *rumni dape*; and they are like a split half of a pomegranate on the outside, which is red and round. Behold, praise of a woman’s beauty; and the allegory our Rabbis explained: the empty ones among you are full of commandments like a pomegranate.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Song of Songs 4:3 (“tes pommettes”), in forms such as פומילש and פומילאש; the printed form (פומי"ליש) is a variant spelling.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Behind thy veil
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Mibe'ad letzamatekh* — from within your bands.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Thy neck is like the tower of David
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Kemigdal David tzavarekh* — an erect stature is beauty in a woman; and the allegory: “like the tower of David” is the fortress of Zion, a place of strength and *ophel* and stronghold; so is your neck: this is the Chamber of Hewn Stone, which was their strength and stronghold of Israel. And that tower is “builded for *talpiyot*”: built for beauty, so that all would gaze at it to learn its forms and the beauty of the work of its construction; and it is from the root (Job 35), “Who teacheth us (*melappenu*) more than the beasts of the earth”; and the tav in *talpiyot* is like the tav in *tarmit* and in *tavnit*.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Rashi reads *talpiyot* as “for learning / beauty”; JPS renders “Builded with turrets.” Printed “Job 35” is Job 35:11.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Whereon there hang a thousand shields
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Elef hamagen taluy alav* — so is the practice of princes: to hang their shields and their *shelatim* on the walls of towers.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: armour
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Shilte* — quivers in which arrows are put, like (Jeremiah 51) “Make bright the arrows, fill the quivers (*hashelatim*)”; and similar to it is the Chamber of Hewn Stone, from where the teaching goes forth, for the Torah is a shield (*magen*) for Israel; and it can be said that *elef hamagen* is like *magen ha'elef*, after (I Chronicles 16) “the word which He commanded to a thousand generations.”
Song of Songs.translator_note: Printed “Jeremiah 51” is Jeremiah 51:11; “I Chronicles 16” is I Chronicles 16:15.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: All the armour of the mighty men
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Kol shiltei hagibborim* — we find that students are called by the name of arrows and quivers, as in (Psalms 127), “As arrows in the hand of a mighty man, so are the children of one’s youth. Happy is the man that hath his quiver full of them.”
Song of Songs.translator_note: Printed “Psalms 127” is Psalms 127:4–5.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Thy two breasts are like two fawns
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Shnei shadayikh* — those who nursed you; this is Moses and Aaron.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: That are twins of a gazelle
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Kishnei ofarim te'omei tzviyah* — the way of a gazelle is to give birth to twins; so both are equal, balanced one like the other. Another explanation: *shnei shadayikh* — after the Tablets, twins of a gazelle, which are matched in one measure, five commandments on this one and five on that, matched, commandment against commandment: “I am” against “Thou shalt not murder,” for the murderer diminishes the image of the Holy One, blessed be He; “Thou shalt have no other” against “Thou shalt not commit adultery,” for the adulteress goes after idolatry, the way of a woman who commits adultery: “instead of her husband she taketh strangers”; “Thou shalt not take” against “Thou shalt not steal,” for the thief ends by swearing falsely; “Remember” against “Thou shalt not bear false witness,” for the profaner of the Sabbath testifies falsely against his Creator, saying that He did not rest on the Sabbath of Creation; “Honour” against “Thou shalt not covet,” for the one who covets ends by begetting a son who will disparage him and honour as father one who is not his father.
Song of Songs.translator_note: The words “instead of her husband she taketh strangers” are from Ezekiel 16:32 (no reference is printed).

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Which feed among the lilies
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Haro'im* — their flock among the lilies, and lead them on a pleasant and straight road.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: the day breathe
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Ad shefayach hayom* — until the sun spreads.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: the shadows flee away
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Venasu hatzelalim* — it is the time of heat and the heat of the day; I will shade you, and you will be pleasant to Me.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: the day breathe
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Hayom* — it is the sun, and so (Genesis 3) “toward the cool of the day (*leruach hayom*)” and (Malachi 3) “For, behold, the day cometh, it burneth as a furnace”; and “from when the day breathes I will go to the mount of Moriah, to the Eternal House,” in Bereshit Rabbah. That is: from when they sinned before Me, to profane My holy things and to scorn My offering in the days of Hophni and Phinehas, I will withdraw from you and abandon this Tabernacle, and I will *ve'avaer* for Myself on Mount Moriah the Eternal House, and there you are all fair and there is no blemish in you, and I will accept there all your offerings.
Song of Songs.translator_note: The word *ve'avaer* is left as printed. Printed “Genesis 3” is Genesis 3:8.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Come with me from Lebanon, my bride
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Iti miLevanon kallah* — when you go into exile from Lebanon, you go into exile with Me, for I will go into exile with you.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: With me from Lebanon
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Iti miLevanon tavo'i* — and when you return from the Exile I will return with you; and also all the days of the Exile, in your trouble I am troubled; and therefore it is written “with me from Lebanon you shall come”: when you go into exile from Lebanon with Me, you shall come; and it is not written “with me to Lebanon you shall come,” to say that from the time of your going out from here until the time of your coming here I am with you in all that you go out and come in.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Look from the top of Amana
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Tashuri merosh Amanah* — when I gather your scattered ones, you will gaze and consider what is the reward of your deed from the beginning of faith (*emunah*), with which you believed in Me, your going after Me in the wilderness, and your journeys and your encampments by My mouth, and your coming to the top of Senir and Hermon, which were the dwellings of lions — Sihon and Og. Another explanation: from the top of Amanah, a mountain at the northern border of the Land of Israel, whose name is Amanah, and in the language of the Mishnah *Turei Amanon*, and *Hor HaHar*, of which it is said (Numbers 34), “From the Great Sea you shall mark out your line unto mount Hor (*Hor HaHar*)”; and when the exiles are gathered and reach there, they gaze from there and see the border of the Land of Israel and the air of the Land of Israel, and rejoice and say thanksgiving; therefore it is said, “Look from the top of Amana.”
Song of Songs.translator_note: Printed “Numbers 34” is Numbers 34:7.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Thou hast ravished my heart
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Libavtini* — you drew my heart to you.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: with one of thine eyes
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Be'achat me'einayikh* — many good qualities are in you; if only one of them were in you I would cherish you exceedingly, and how much more all of them. And so “with one bead (*anak*) of thy necklace (*mitzvonayikh*)”: with one of the strings of your ornaments (*anakai kishutayikh*): these are the ornaments of commandment by which Israel are distinguished. Another explanation: “with one *anak*”: with one of your fathers, who was unique, and he was one — this is Abraham, who is called (Joshua 14) “the greatest man among the Anakim.”
Song of Songs.translator_note: Printed “Joshua 14” is Joshua 14:15. The printed word in the first sentence is *mitzvonayikh* (the verse has *mitzavonayikh*).

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: How fair is thy love
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Mah yafu dadayikh* — every place where you showed Me affection is fair in My eyes: Gilgal, Shiloh, Nob and Gibeon, and the Eternal House that the Babylonian founded; “rest” and “inheritance” — “rest” is Jerusalem, and “inheritance” is the place where the Divine Presence was gathered for Israel.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Translated literally; “that the Babylonian founded” is left as printed.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: And the smell of thine ointments
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Veriach shemanayikh* — a good name.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Thy lips, O my bride, drop honey
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Nofet* — sweet.
Song of Songs.translator_note: The source gives *nofet* as the lemma; the verse has *tittofnah nofet*.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Thy lips, O my bride, drop honey
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Tittofnah siftotayikh* — the reasons of the Torah.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: And the smell of thy garments
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Veriach salmotayikh* — the fitting commandments that apply to your garments: tzitzit, blue thread, the garments of the priesthood, the prohibition of *sha'atnez*.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: A garden shut up is my sister
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Gan na'ul* — on account of the modesty of the daughters of Israel, who do not break through into forbidden relations.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: A spring shut up
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Gal na'ul* — it can be explained as an expression of a spring, like (Joshua 15) “springs (*gullot*) … Upper,” and it can be explained as an expression of a gate, and it is Aramaic: in the Talmud, *tarku gelei*.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Printed “Joshua 15” is Joshua 15:19 (JPS: “the Upper Springs”). The Talmudic phrase is left as printed.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Thy shoots are a park of pomegranates
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Shelachayikh* — dry land is called *beit hashelachin* and needs to be watered always, and a field that is *beit haba'al* is better than it; and here He praised: your dry land — behold, it is full of all good like an orchard of pomegranates; and this is on account of the small ones in Israel, who are moist with good deeds like an orchard of pomegranates.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Henna with spikenard plants
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Kofarim im nerdim* — kinds of spices they are.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Thou art a fountain of gardens
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Ma'ayan ganim* — all this refers back to “thy shoots,” and He praises them as a spring that waters them; and the likeness is on account of the purifying immersions that the daughters of Israel immerse.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: And flowing streams from Lebanon
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Venozelim min Levanon* — from a place of cleanness, with no muddy turbidity.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Awake, O north wind; And come, thou south
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Uri tzafon uvo'i teiman* — after your fragrance and the beauty of your dwellings have become sweet to Me, I command the winds, north and south, to blow upon your garden, that your good fragrance go forth far away; and the likeness is on account of the exiles who are gathered, and from all the nations they bring them as an offering to Jerusalem; and in the days of the Building Israel will be gathered there for the festivals and the pilgrimages; and Israel answer: “Let my beloved come into his garden” — if You are there, all is there.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: I am come into my garden
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Ba'ti legani* — in the days of the dedication of the House.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: I have gathered my myrrh
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Ariti* — I picked; and it is an expression of the Mishnah, like “*melo ora usalo*,” and also an expression of Scripture (Psalms 80), “and all they that pass by the way do pluck her (*ve'aruha*)”; and it was said on account of the incense, because the princes offered individual incense on the outer altar and it was accepted — a thing that does not apply for the generations — and therefore it says, “I have eaten my honeycomb (*ya'ri*) with my honey.” There is honey that grows on reeds, as it is said (I Samuel 14), “in the honeycomb (*beya'arat hadevash*)” — and *ya'arat* is an expression of a reed, like (Exodus 2) “and she laid it in the flags (*vattasem bassuf*)” and the Targum “*veshaviteh beya'ra*” — and they suck out the honey and throw away the wood; and I, from the abundance of affection, ate my reed with my honey: I ate what is unfit together with what is fit — a voluntary incense, and likewise the he-goats of sin-offering that the princes brought, though a sin-offering is not brought as a freewill offering, and I accepted them on that very day.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Translated literally; “*melo ora usalo*” is left as printed. Printed “Psalms 40” is Psalms 80:13; printed “Samuel 5 6” is I Samuel 14:27 (JPS: “honeycomb”); “Exodus 2” is Exodus 2:3 (JPS: “in the flags”).

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: I have drunk my wine with my milk
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Shatiti yayni* — these are the libations.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: with my milk
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Im chelavi* — they were sweet and clear as milk.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Eat, O friends
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Ichlu re'im* — in the Tent of Meeting, Aaron and his sons, and in the Eternal House, all the priests.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Drink, yea, drink abundantly, O beloved
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Shetu veshichru dodim* — these are Israel, who eat the flesh of the peace-offering that they brought for the dedication of the altar.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: I sleep, but my heart waketh
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Ani yeshenah* — when I was at ease and quiet in the First Temple I despaired of serving the Holy One, blessed be He, like one asleep and slumbering.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: but my heart waketh
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Velibbi er* — this is the Holy One, blessed be He; so it is expounded in the Pesikta.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: but my heart waketh
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Velibbi er* — the Holy One, blessed be He, who is the rock of my heart and my portion, is awake to guard me and to do me good.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Hark! my beloved knocketh
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Kol dodi dofek* — He causes His Presence to rest upon the prophets and warns by their hand, “rising early and sending.”

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Open to me
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Pitchi li* — do not cause Me to withdraw from you.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: For my head is filled with dew
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Sheroshi nimla tal* — the language of a man who comes at night knocking at the door of his beloved: he says so — “because of your affection I came by night, in the time of dew or rain.” And the likeness: “my head is filled with dew” — that I am full of favour and contentment: Abraham your father, whose deeds were sweet to Me like dew; behold, I come to you laden with blessings and with the payment of good deeds, if you return to Me.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: My locks with the drops of the night
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Kutzotai revisei lailah* — also in My hand are many bundles (*kevitzot*) of kinds of punishment, to exact payment from those who forsake Me and who spurn Me; *tal* is an expression of contentment.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: with the drops of the night
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Revisei lailah* — the rains of the night, which are toil and weariness; *revisei* is the Targum of *revivim* (Deuteronomy 32), “and as the showers upon the herb,” and (the Targum) *ukhrisisei malkusha*; *kutzot* are the tufts of the hair of the head that are stuck together, which are called כלוציי"לש in Old French; and since Scripture took hold of the language of dew and rain, it took hold of the language of the head, and “locks” — for the way of dew and rain is to cling to the hair and the locks. And it can be explained that “dew” and “drops of the night” are both for good: the reward of light commandments, which are easy to perform, is like dew, and the reward of severe, difficult commandments is like the toil of the drops of the night.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Song of Songs 5:2 (“mes boucles”), in forms such as פלוצילש and פלוצייש; the printed form (כלוציי"לש) differs slightly (a *kaf* where the forms have *pe*). Printed “Deuteronomy 32” is Deuteronomy 32:2; the Aramaic is translated as printed.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: I have put off my coat
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Pashatti et kuttanti* — that is: I have already learned other ways for myself; I cannot return to You any more, as it is said (Jeremiah 44), “since we let off to offer to the queen of heaven,” etc., for these ways were right in their eyes. And the language “I have put off my coat, I have washed my feet” is the language of the reply of the adulterous woman who does not wish to open the door to her husband. Since Scripture began with the language “I sleep … Hark! my beloved knocketh,” it concluded with a language of reply that falls upon the language of knocking at the door at the time of lying down to sleep at night.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Printed “Jeremiah 44” is Jeremiah 44:18.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: My beloved put in his hand by the hole of the door
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Dodi shalach yado min hachor* — that is beside the door; and I saw his hand, and my inward parts were turned within me to return to His love and to open to Him.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: I rose up to open to my beloved; And my hands dropped with myrrh
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Kamti ani liftoach ledodi vyadai natefu mor* — that is: with a whole heart and a willing soul, like a woman adorning herself to be loved by her husband with a good fragrance.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: flowing myrrh
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Mor over* — a fragrance that passes and spreads to every side.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: But my beloved had turned away, and was gone
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Vedodi chamak avar* — hidden and covered from me, like (Song of Songs 7) “the roundings (*chamukei*) of thy thighs” — the hidden places of thy thighs, on account of the thigh being in a hidden place; (Jeremiah 31) “How long wilt thou turn away (*tit'chammakin*)” — wilt thou hide and cover thyself because of the shame that thou hast brought upon Me.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Printed “Song of Songs 6” is Song of Songs 7:2. Rashi reads *tit'chammakin* as “hide yourself”; JPS renders “turn away coyly” (Jeremiah 31:22; printed “Jeremiah 31”).

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: My soul failed me when he spoke
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Nafshi yatz'ah vedabbero* — because He said, “I will not come to your house,” for in the beginning I did not agree to open.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: The watchmen that go about the city found me
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Bikkashtihu* etc. *Metza'uni hashomerim hasovevim ba'ir* — and they seize thieves who walk at night.
Song of Songs.translator_note: The source lemma begins with the preceding verse’s “I sought him”; the lemma shown is the portion that lies in this verse.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: they wounded me
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Hikkuni petza'uni* — they made a wound in me; every *petza* is an expression of a blow of a weapon: *navradur'ia* in Old French.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Song of Songs 5:7 (“ils m’ont fait une blessure”), in forms such as נברדורא and נאברורא; the printed form (נברדור"יא) is a variant spelling.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: my mantle
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Redidi* — my ornament, which is beaten out and hammered upon me; and so the whole matter is the language of a wife of one’s youth who laments for the husband of her youth and seeks him, and this is the likeness.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: The watchmen that go about the city found me
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Dodi shalach yado min hachor* — when I said, “I have washed my feet, and I will not open to You and I will not return from the ע"א that I chose.”
Song of Songs.translator_note: The source lemma belongs to another verse of the Song of Songs and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under. The abbreviation ע"א is left as printed (it may stand for idolatry, *avodah zarah*, but this is not stated).

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: The watchmen that go about the city found me
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Shalach yado* — and He showed His vengeance in the days of Ahaz, and brought upon him the army of the king of Aram (II Chronicles 28), “and they smote him, and carried away of his a great multitude of captives,” etc., “and Pekah the son of Remaliah slew in Judah a hundred and twenty thousand in one day.”
Song of Songs.translator_note: The source lemma belongs to another verse of the Song of Songs and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under. Printed “II Chronicles 28” is II Chronicles 28:5–6.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: The watchmen that go about the city found me
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Ume'ai hamu alav* — Hezekiah his son came and returned with all his heart to seek the Holy One, blessed be He, and all his generation were perfect; there did not arise a generation in Israel like them, as is explained in (the chapter) *Chelek*: they searched from Dan to Beersheba and did not find an *am ha'aretz*; from Gebat to Antioch, and did not find a man or woman who was not versed in the laws of uncleanness and cleanness; and this is “and my hands dropped with myrrh,” etc. Josiah too — of him it is said (II Kings 23), “and like unto him was there no king before him,” for he saw the punishment that came upon Manasseh and upon Amon, to fulfil “put in his hand by the hole of the door, and my inward parts were moved for him.”
Song of Songs.translator_note: The source lemma belongs to another verse of the Song of Songs and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under. The reference is to the chapter *Chelek* of the Talmud (tractate Sanhedrin); no page is printed. Printed “II Kings 23” is II Kings 23:25.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: The watchmen that go about the city found me
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Pathachti ani ledodi vedodi chamak avar* — He did not annul His decree, as it is said of Hezekiah (Isaiah 35), “Behold, the days come, that all that is in thy house shall be carried,” etc., “and of thy sons that shall issue from thee” — these are Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah. And also of Josiah, through Huldah the prophetess (Jeremiah 19), “Behold, I will bring evil upon this place, and upon the inhabitants thereof,” etc., and it says (II Kings 3), “and like unto him was there no king before him. Notwithstanding the LORD turned not from the fierceness of His great wrath, wherewith His anger was kindled against Judah, because of all the provocations wherewith Manasseh had provoked Him. And the LORD said: I will remove Judah also out of My sight, as I have removed Israel, and I will cast off this city.”
Song of Songs.translator_note: The source lemma belongs to another verse of the Song of Songs and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under. Printed “Isaiah 35” is Isaiah 39:6–7; the first quotation of Huldah’s words is II Kings 22:16, printed “Jeremiah 19” (compare Jeremiah 19:3); printed “II Kings 3” is II Kings 23:25–27, quoted here from 23:25, 26 and 27 in the printed wording.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: The watchmen that go about the city found me
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Nafshi yatz'ah bedabbero* — it went out of me at His speaking this word.
Song of Songs.translator_note: The source lemma belongs to another verse of the Song of Songs and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: The watchmen that go about the city found me
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Bikkashtihu velo metzatihu* — and if you say: but behold, Jeremiah stood and prophesied in the days of Jehoiakim and Zedekiah, “Return to Me, and I will return to you” — it was not to annul the decree but to lighten the punishment and to establish their kingdom upon their return from the exile, to plant them without uprooting and to build them without destruction.
Song of Songs.translator_note: The source lemma belongs to another verse of the Song of Songs and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under. The source lemma (“I sought him”) lies at the start of this verse; the comment sits under 5:7 in the printed text. The words “Return to Me, and I will return to you” are not a quotation of Jeremiah in JPS’s text (compare Zechariah 1:3, Malachi 3:7).

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: The watchmen that go about the city found me
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Metza'uni hashomerim* — Nebuchadnezzar and his armies.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: that go about the city
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Hasovevim ba'ir* — to take the vengeance of the Omnipresent.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: took away my mantle from me
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Nas'u et redidi* — the Temple.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: The keepers of the walls
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Shomerei hachomot* — also the ministering angels who were guarding its walls, as it is said (Isaiah 62), “I have set watchmen upon thy walls, O Jerusalem”; they set fire to it, as it is said (Lamentations 1), “From on high hath He sent fire.”
Song of Songs.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 62” is Isaiah 62:6; “Lamentations 1” is Lamentations 1:13.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Hishba'ti etchem* — the nations, the men of Nebuchadnezzar, whom you saw in Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah delivering themselves to the fiery furnace, and Daniel to the lions’ den, on account of prayer, and the generation of Mordecai in the days of Haman.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: If you find my beloved
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Im timtze'u et dodi* — in the time to come, on the Day of Judgment, when you will be asked to testify for me, as it is said (Isaiah 15), “let them bring their witnesses, that they may be justified.”
Song of Songs.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 15” is Isaiah 43:9.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: what will you tell him
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Mah tagidu lo* — that you will testify for me that for the sake of His love I was sick with severe sufferings. Among you let Nebuchadnezzar come and testify, let Eliphaz and Zophar and all the prophets of the nations come and testify for me that I fulfilled the Torah.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: What is thy beloved more than another beloved
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Mah dodekh midod* — so the nations used to ask Israel: What is your God more than all the gods, that you are burned and crucified for Him?

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: That thou dost so adjure us
