Song of Songs.english_translation: *Shekakhah hishbatanu* — to testify to Him of your love.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: My beloved is white
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Dodi tzach* — white, like (Lamentations 4) “they were whiter than milk (*tzachu mechalav*).”
Song of Songs.translator_note: Printed “Lamentations 4” is Lamentations 4:7.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: and ruddy
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Ve'adom* — I shall first explain the whole matter according to its plain meaning: praise of the beauty of a young man when he is white and his face ruddy.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Pre-eminent above ten thousand
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Dagul merevavah* — he is distinguished (*nidgal*) among many armies; many are his armies; many myriads are called *revavah*, as it is said (Ezekiel 17), “a myriad (*revavah*), like the growth of the field, have I made thee.”
Song of Songs.translator_note: Printed “Ezekiel 17” is Ezekiel 16:7; JPS renders the verse “I cause thee to increase, even as the growth of the field.”

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: His head is as the most fine gold
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Rosho* — shining like pure gold; *ketem* is an expression of the choice treasure of kings, which they store in their treasure-houses; and so (Lamentations 4) “How is the most fine gold (*hakketem hatov*) changed”; and so (Job 31) “and have said to the fine gold (*laketem*): Thou art my confidence”; and so (Proverbs 25) “an ornament of fine gold (*vechali ketem*).”
Song of Songs.translator_note: Printed “Lamentations 4” is Lamentations 4:1; “Job 31” is Job 31:24; “Proverbs 25” is Proverbs 25:12. The wording of the first quotation differs slightly from JPS (“How is the most fine gold changed!”).

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: His locks are curled
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Kutzotav taltalim* — an expression of hanging: *pendelois* [printed פנדלוי"יש] in Old French.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Song of Songs 5:11 (“boucles flottantes”), in forms such as פינדליוש and פנדילוש; the reading is *pendelois* (from *pendeler*), from Darmesteter’s footnote; the printed form (פנדלוי"יש) is a variant spelling.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: And black as a raven
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Shecharut ke'orev* — all these are beauty for a young man.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: His eyes are like doves Beside the water-brooks
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Einav keyonim al afikei mayim* — his eyes by the water-brooks are pleasant like the eyes of doves; the water-brooks are agreeable to the sight, and the young men go out there to stroll; and so the poet praises the eyes of my beloved when he looks upon the water-brooks, that they resemble the beauty of the eyes of doves.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Washed with milk
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Rochetzot* — the eyes of my beloved, in milk.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Translated literally; the printed comment is elliptical.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: And fitly set
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Yoshevot al melet* — all this is an expression of beauty: not protruding too much, not sunken, but sitting upon their *melet*, their socket (*gumah*). The matter (another version: the eye according to the socket) according to the pattern; and it is an expression of anything made to fill a hollow that has been made for it as a seat, like (Exodus 25) “stones to be set (*avnei milluim*),” (ibid. 25) “and thou shalt set in it a setting of stone (*umille'ta vo milluat even*).”
Song of Songs.translator_note: Printed “Exodus 25” is Exodus 25:7; the second “ibid. 25” is Exodus 28:17, where JPS renders “And thou shalt set in it settings of stones.”

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: His cheeks are as a bed of spices
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Lechayav ka'arugat habosem* — in which there are, in those beds, growths of spice-mixtures.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: As banks of sweet herbs
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Migdelot merkachim* — growths of spice-mixtures, growths of balsams, which they compound in the work of a perfumer.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: rods of gold
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Gelilei zahav* — like wheels of gold.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Set with beryl
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Memulaim battarshish* — every expression of the setting of a precious stone in gold is called *melet*.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: His body
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Eshet* — an expression of (Jeremiah 5) “They are waxen fat, they are become sleek (*shamenu ashetu*)”: a thick mass is called *eshet*: משש"יאה in Old French.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Song of Songs 5:14 (“une masse (d’ivoire)”), in forms such as משיץ and מרשיץ; the printed form (משש"יאה) differs. Printed “Jeremiah 5:25” is Jeremiah 5:28.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: polished ivory
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Shen* — of the bones of an elephant.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Overlaid with sapphires
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Me'ulefet sappirim* — adorned and fitted with sapphires; an expression of “and she wrapped herself (*vattit'alaf*),” which the Targum renders *ve'itkenat*.
Song of Songs.translator_note: No reference is printed for “and she wrapped herself”; it is Genesis 38:14.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: His legs are as pillars of marble
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Shokav* — like pillars of marble founded upon sockets of fine gold.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: pillars of marble
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Amudei shesh* — pillars of marble (*shayish*), and its fellow is in the Scroll of Esther (Esther 1), “upon silver rods and pillars of marble”; and his appearance is high like the cedars of Lebanon.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Excellent as the cedars
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Bachur ka'arazim* — chosen among the sons as the cedar among the other trees.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: His mouth is most sweet
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Chikko mamtakkim* — his words are pleasant.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: This is my beloved, and this is my friend
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Zeh dodi* — this is the likeness of my beloved and this is the likeness of my friend, and for all these I am sick with love of him; and the likeness with respect to the Holy One, blessed be He, is as follows:

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: This is my beloved, and this is my friend
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Dodi tzach* — and white, to whiten my iniquities; white and pure: when He appeared at Sinai He appeared as an old man teaching rulings, and so when He sits in judgment (Daniel 7), “His raiment was as white snow, and the hair of his head like pure wool.”
Song of Songs.translator_note: The source lemma (Song of Songs 5:10) does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under. Rashi quotes the Aramaic of Daniel 7:9; the English is JPS.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: This is my beloved, and this is my friend
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Ve'adom* — to exact payment from His haters, as it is said (Isaiah 43), “Wherefore is Thine apparel red.”
Song of Songs.translator_note: The source lemma (Song of Songs 5:10) does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under. Printed “Isaiah 43” is Isaiah 63:2.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: This is my beloved, and this is my friend
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Dagul merevavah* — many armies surround Him.
Song of Songs.translator_note: The source lemma belongs to another verse of the Song of Songs and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: This is my beloved, and this is my friend
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Rosho ketem paz* — the beginning of His words shone like pure gold, and so it says (Psalms 119), “The opening of Thy words giveth light”; “I am the LORD thy God” — He showed them first that He has the prerogative of kingship over them, and afterward decreed upon them His decrees.
Song of Songs.translator_note: The source lemma belongs to another verse of the Song of Songs and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under. The words “I am the LORD thy God” are Exodus 20:2 (no reference is printed). Printed “Psalms 119” is Psalms 119:130.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: This is my beloved, and this is my friend
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Kutzotav taltalim* — on every single tittle, heaps and heaps of laws.
Song of Songs.translator_note: The source lemma belongs to another verse of the Song of Songs and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: This is my beloved, and this is my friend
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Shecharot ke'orev* — because there was written before Him black fire upon white fire. Another explanation: “his locks are curled” — when He appeared at the Sea He appeared as a young man fighting with might.
Song of Songs.translator_note: The source lemma belongs to another verse of the Song of Songs and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: This is my beloved, and this is my friend
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Einav keyonim al afikei mayim* — like doves, whose eyes look toward their dovecotes: so His eyes are upon synagogues and houses of study, where are the sources of the Torah, likened to water.
Song of Songs.translator_note: The source lemma belongs to another verse of the Song of Songs and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: This is my beloved, and this is my friend
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Rochetzot bechalav* — when they look into a judgment, they clarify the case to its truth, to justify the righteous, to give him according to his righteousness, and to condemn the wicked, to give him his way upon his head.
Song of Songs.translator_note: The source lemma belongs to another verse of the Song of Songs and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: This is my beloved, and this is my friend
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Yoshevot al melet* — upon the fullness of the world they roam throughout the earth, looking at the good and the bad. Another explanation: disciples of the wise, whom the Holy One, blessed be He, gives as eyes to illuminate the world, as the eyes illuminate a man; like doves that wander from dovecote to dovecote to seek their food, so they go from the house of study of Sage so-and-so to the house of study of Sage so-and-so to seek the reasons of the Torah.
Song of Songs.translator_note: The source lemma belongs to another verse of the Song of Songs and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: This is my beloved, and this is my friend
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Al afikei mayim* — upon houses of study, which are the sources of the waters of Torah.
Song of Songs.translator_note: The source lemma belongs to another verse of the Song of Songs and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: This is my beloved, and this is my friend
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Rochetzot bechalav* — since He called them “eyes,” and *ayin* is feminine, *rochetzot* is feminine: they polish themselves with the milk of the Torah and whiten its hidden and sealed matters.
Song of Songs.translator_note: The source lemma belongs to another verse of the Song of Songs and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: This is my beloved, and this is my friend
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Yoshevet al melet* — settling matters according to their proper ways. Another explanation: *einav* (his eyes) is *inyanav* (his subjects): sections of the Torah, and laws, and Mishnayot, like doves, who are pleasant in their going by the water-brooks, in houses of study, washed in milk, polished as milk, as I have explained.
Song of Songs.translator_note: The source lemma belongs to another verse of the Song of Songs and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: This is my beloved, and this is my friend
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Lechayav* — the Ten Commandments at Mount Sinai, in which He showed them a pleasant and smiling face.
Song of Songs.translator_note: The source lemma belongs to another verse of the Song of Songs and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: This is my beloved, and this is my friend
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Siftotav shoshannim* — the speeches spoken in the Tent of Meeting, which are for acceptance, and for atonement, and for a good fragrance: the law of the sin-offering, the guilt-offering, the meal-offering, the burnt-offering and the peace-offerings.
Song of Songs.translator_note: The source lemma belongs to another verse of the Song of Songs and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: This is my beloved, and this is my friend
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Yadav* — the Tablets that He gave from His right hand, and they are the work of His hands.
Song of Songs.translator_note: The source lemma belongs to another verse of the Song of Songs and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: This is my beloved, and this is my friend
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Gelilei zahav* — these are the Commandments, in which are those “more to be desired than gold, yea, than much fine gold.” Rabbi Joshua ben Nehemiah said: They were a work of miracles; they were of *sanpirinon* and they were rolling. Another explanation: because they roll goodness to the world.
Song of Songs.translator_note: The source lemma belongs to another verse of the Song of Songs and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under. The words “more to be desired than gold, yea, than much fine gold” are Psalms 19:11 (no reference is printed). The word *sanpirinon* is left as printed.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: This is my beloved, and this is my friend
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Memulaim battarshish* — for He included in the Ten Commandments the 613 commandments.
Song of Songs.translator_note: The source lemma belongs to another verse of the Song of Songs and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: This is my beloved, and this is my friend
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Me'av eshet shen* — this is the Torat Kohanim (Leviticus), which is given in the middle of the five Books, like these intestines, which are placed in the middle of the body.
Song of Songs.translator_note: The source lemma belongs to another verse of the Song of Songs and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: This is my beloved, and this is my friend
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Eshet shen me'ulefet sappirim* — it appears smooth as a body of ivory, and it is arranged with many fine points: analogies (*gezerot shavot*), the principle derived from one passage (*binyan av*), and light and weighty rules (*kalim vachamurim*).
Song of Songs.translator_note: The source lemma belongs to another verse of the Song of Songs and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: This is my beloved, and this is my friend
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Meyusadim al adnei faz* — Rabbi Elazar HaKappar said: This pillar has a capital above and a base below. Rabbi Shmuel bar Gera said: The sections of the Torah have a capital above and a base below, and they are juxtaposed before and after them, such as the sections of the seventh year and the Jubilee (Leviticus 25), “And if you sell a sale,” to inform you how severe is the dust of the seventh year, as it appears in tractates Arachin and Sukkah; and such as (Numbers 16) “Let the LORD appoint a man over the congregation” (followed by) “Command my offering, my bread”: while You charge me concerning my children, charge them concerning Me. And so, many; therefore it is said, “his legs are pillars of marble, founded,” etc.
Song of Songs.translator_note: The source lemma belongs to another verse of the Song of Songs and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under. Translated literally; the sentence “while You charge me … concerning Me” and “And so, many” are elliptical. Printed “Leviticus 25” is Leviticus 25:14 (JPS: “And if thou sell aught unto thy neighbour”); printed “Numbers 16” is Numbers 27:16; “Command my offering, my bread” is Numbers 28:2 (JPS: “Command the children of Israel … My food which is presented unto Me”).

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: This is my beloved, and this is my friend
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Mar'ehu kaLevanon* — one who looks and considers his words finds in them blossoms and sprouts, like this forest, which sprouts; so the words of Torah: one who meditates in them continually renews reasons in them.
Song of Songs.translator_note: The source lemma belongs to another verse of the Song of Songs and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: This is my beloved, and this is my friend
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Bachur* — chosen, like the cedars that are chosen for building and for strength and for height.
Song of Songs.translator_note: The source lemma belongs to another verse of the Song of Songs and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: His mouth is most sweet
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Chikko mamtakkim* — his words are pleasant; (Leviticus 19) “and a gash for the dead you shall not put in your flesh: I am the LORD,” faithful to pay reward; is there a palate sweeter than this? Do not wound yourselves by your deeds, and you will receive reward. And (Ezekiel 14) “And when the wicked turneth from his wickedness, … and doeth justice and righteousness, … he shall surely live”: iniquities are counted for him as merits; is there a bosom sweeter than this?
Song of Songs.translator_note: Printed “Leviticus 19” is Leviticus 19:28; JPS renders “You shall not make any cuttings in your flesh for the dead.” Printed “Ezekiel 14” is Ezekiel 33:19; Rashi’s wording (*ve'asah mishpat utzedakah aleihem chayo yichyeh*) differs from JPS (“and doeth that which is lawful and right, he shall live thereby”). The second printed “palate” reads *chayk* (“bosom”), evidently for *chekh* (“palate”); left as printed.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Whither hath thy beloved turned him
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Anah halakh dodekh* — the nations taunt and provoke Israel: “Whither has your Beloved gone? Why did He leave you forsaken, a widow?”
Song of Songs.translator_note: The source lemma (“Whither is thy beloved gone”) is the end of the preceding verse in JPS’s division; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Whither hath thy beloved turned him
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Anah fanah dodekh* — when He returned and caused His spirit to rest upon Cyrus and gave permission to build the House, and they began to build, they came and said to them: “Whither has your Beloved turned? If He returns to you, let us seek Him with you,” as it is said (Ezra 4), “And the adversaries of Judah and Benjamin heard that the children of the captivity were building a temple,” etc.; “and they drew near to Zerubbabel,” etc., “Let us build with you, for we seek your God as you do,” etc. And their intention was for evil, to make them cease from the work; and they reply:
Song of Songs.translator_note: Rashi’s wording of Ezra 4:1–2 differs slightly from JPS (“Now when the adversaries of Judah and Benjamin heard that the children of the captivity were building a temple unto the LORD …”). Printed “Ezra 4” is Ezra 4:1–2.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: My beloved is gone down into his garden
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Dodi yarad legano* — He commanded us to build His Sanctuary and He was there with us.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: To the beds of spices
Song of Songs.english_translation: *La'arugat habosem* — the place where the incense is burned.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: To feed in the gardens
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Lir'ot baganim* — and further, He went down to feed His flock in the gardens: those who were scattered there, who did not go up from the Exile — He causes His Presence to rest upon them in synagogues and in houses of study.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: And to gather lilies
Song of Songs.english_translation: *UleLaket shoshannim* — He hears and listens to those who speak in His Torah, to gather up their merits and to write them in the book of remembrance before Him, as it is said (Malachi 3), “Then they that feared the LORD spoke one with another,” etc. And as for what you say, to seek Him with us and to build with us — “I am my beloved’s,” and not you His, and you shall not build with us, as it is said (Ezra 4), “Not for you and for us to build the house of our God”; and it says, “but you have no portion, nor right, nor memorial, in Jerusalem.”
Song of Songs.translator_note: Printed “Ezra 4” is Ezra 4:3 (JPS: “You have nothing to do with us to build a house unto our God”); the last quotation is Nehemiah 2:20 (no reference is printed).

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: That feedeth among the lilies
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Haro'eh bashoshannim* — He who feeds His flock in a pleasant and good pasture.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Thou art beautiful, O my love, as Tirzah
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Yafah at ra'yati kitirtzah* — and the Holy One, blessed be He, praises her for this: “Thou art beautiful, my love,” when thou art acceptable (*retzuyah*) to Me. So it is expounded in the Sifre.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Comely as Jerusalem
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Na'avah* — thou art now as at the first in Jerusalem.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Terrible as an army with banners
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Ayumah kanidgalot* — hosts of angels: I will cast thy dread upon them, not to fight, and to make you cease from the work, as it is stated in Ezra.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Translated literally; the printed text is elliptical.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Turn away thine eyes from me
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Hasebbi einayikh minnegdi* — like a young man whose betrothed is dear and pleasant to him and her eyes are beautiful, and he says to her: “Turn away thine eyes from me, for when I see thee my heart swells and grows proud within me, and my spirit is haughty, for I cannot restrain myself.”

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: For they have overcome me
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Hirhivuni* — they made my heart haughty, like (Psalms 90) “yet is their pride (*verahbam*) but travail and vanity”; (Isaiah 30) “arrogancy (*rahav*) that sitteth still”: אישמיי"ר in Old French. And the likeness: thus the Holy One, blessed be He, said regarding this Temple: it is impossible to restore to you the Ark and the cover and the cherubim, which made Me haughty in the First Temple, to show you exceeding affection, until you trespassed against Me.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Song of Songs 6:5 (“m’ont rendu fort”), in the form אישוויר; the printed form (אישמיי"ר) is a variant spelling. Printed “Psalms 90” is Psalms 90:10; “Isaiah 30” is Isaiah 30:7 (the printed Hebrew reads *rahav hem shavet*).

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Thy hair is as a flock of goats
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Sa'arekh ke'eder ha'izim* — among the small, tender and thin ones among you there is much praise.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Thy teeth
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Shinayikh* — the leaders and the mighty ones among you, all for good.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: like a flock of ewes
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Ke'eder harechelim* — this ewe is entirely holy: its wool for blue, its flesh for sacrifice, its horns for shofars, its shins for flutes, its intestines for harps, its skin for a drum; but the wicked are likened to dogs, none of whom is of any holiness.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: There are threescore queens
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Shishim hemah malkhot* — Abraham and those who came forth from his loins: the sons of Keturah, sixteen; Ishmael and his sons, thirteen; Isaac and his sons, three; the sons of Jacob, twelve; the sons of Esau, sixteen — in Chronicles. Behold, sixty. And if you say, remove from them Timna, who is a wife of Abraham, from the count —
Song of Songs.translator_note: Translated as printed. Timna is called concubine to Eliphaz, Esau’s son, in Genesis 36:12 (JPS); the printed “wife of Abraham” is left as printed.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: And fourscore concubines
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Ushmonim pilagshim* — Noah and his sons up to Abraham: the generations of those who came out of the ark, you will find eighty. And just as the queens, who are the wives of the king, exceed the concubines in greatness, so were Abraham and those who came forth from his loins important, great, and exceeding all in importance, as you see: Hagar was the daughter of kings; Timna was the daughter of rulers and became a concubine to Esau; and it says (Genesis 14), “unto the vale of Shaveh,” etc.: all were made equal in one counsel and made Abraham king over them.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Translated as printed (“concubine to Esau”; compare Genesis 36:12, where JPS has “concubine to Eliphaz Esau’s son”). Printed “Genesis 14” is Genesis 14:17 (JPS: “at the vale of Shaveh”).

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: And maidens without number
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Va'alamot ein mispar* — into many families all these were divided.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: My dove, my undefiled, is but one
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Achat hi yonati* — and of them all, one is chosen by Me as a dove, perfect, who is whole-hearted with her mate.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: She is the only one of her mother
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Achat hi le'immah* — for her assembly, many disputes in the houses of study — all of them have their hearts set to understand the Torah on its proper basis and toward its truth.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: She is the choice one of her that bore her
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Barah hi leyoladtah* — Jacob saw his bed whole, without blemish, and gave thanks and praised the Omnipresent, as it is said (Genesis 15), “And Israel bowed down upon the bed’s head.”
Song of Songs.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 15” is Genesis 47:31.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: The daughters saw her
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Ra'uhah banot* — Israel in her greatness.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: and called her happy
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Vaye'asheruhah* — and what is your praise —

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Who is she that looketh forth
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Mi zot hanishkafah* — a looking upon us from a high place to a low one is called *hashkafah*; so the Temple is higher than all lands.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: as the dawn
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Kemo shachar* — it goes and brightens little by little; so were Israel in the Second Temple: at first, Zerubbabel, governor of Judah and not a king, and they were subjugated to Persia and Greece, and afterward the House of the Hasmoneans overcame them and they became kings.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Terrible as an army with banners
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Ayumah kanidgalot* — awesome in her mighty deeds, like the banners of kings. All this is the Holy One, blessed be He, praising the Assembly of Israel — “Thou art beautiful, my love, as Tirzah” — and the whole subject up to here.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: I went down into the garden of nuts
Song of Songs.english_translation: *El ginnat egoz yaradti* — this too is from the words of the Divine Presence: Behold, I have come to this Second Temple, to you.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: To look at the green plants of the valley
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Lir'ot be'ibbei hanachal* — what moisture of good deeds I shall see in thee.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: To see whether the vine budded
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Hafarechah hagefen* — if you will bring forth before Me disciples of the wise, scribes and repeaters (of the Mishnah).

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: And the pomegranates were in flower
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Henetzu harimmonim* — those who keep the commandments, full of merits. Why were Israel likened to a nut? Just as this nut, you see it all wood, and nothing within it is recognized; split it and you find it full of *megurot*, *megurot* of edible things: so Israel are modest and humble in their deeds, and the scholars among them are not recognized and do not vaunt themselves to proclaim their praise; examine them and you find them full of wisdom; and there are many more midrashim on the matter. Just as this nut falls into mud and what is within it does not become loathsome, so Israel go into exile among the nations and are smitten with many lashes, and their deeds do not become loathsome.
Song of Songs.translator_note: The word *megurot* is left as printed.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Before I was aware
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Lo yadati* — the Assembly of Israel laments: I did not know to take care against sin, so as to stand in my glory, in my greatness, and I stumbled in causeless hatred and strife that grew strong among the kings of the House of the Hasmoneans, Hyrcanus and Aristobulus, until one of them brought in the kingdom of Rome and received the kingship from its hand, and became its slave; and from then my soul set me to be chariots, to carry upon me the nobles of the other nations.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: my princely people
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Ammi nadiv* — like *am nadiv*, with an extra yod, like the yod of (Deuteronomy 33) “*shokhni seneh*,” (Genesis 10) “*genuvati yom*,” (Lamentations 1) “*rabbati am*.”
Song of Songs.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 10” is Genesis 31:39 (JPS: “whether stolen by day”); “Deuteronomy 33” is Deuteronomy 33:16 (JPS: “him that dwelt in the bush”); “Lamentations 1” is Lamentations 1:1 (JPS: “full of people”).

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: my soul set me
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Nafshi samatni* — I myself appointed them over me, as it is said (Jeremiah 13), “and thou thyself hast taught them over thee as chiefs for a head.”
Song of Songs.translator_note: Rashi’s wording differs from JPS’s rendering of Jeremiah 13:21 (“Whom thou thyself hast trained against thee”).

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Return, return, O Shulammite
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Shuvi shuvi haShulammit* — they say to me: Return, return from following the Omnipresent.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: O Shulammite
Song of Songs.english_translation: *HaShulammit* — she who was whole (*hashlemah*) in her faith with Him; return, return to us.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: that we may look upon thee
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Venechezeh bakh* — we shall appoint from you appointees and rulers, like “and thou shalt provide out of all the people” — so Rabbi Tanchuma expounded. Another explanation: “and we shall gaze at thee”: we shall consider thee, what greatness we shall give thee; and she says: What will you see in the Shulammite? What greatness can you decree for me that would equal my greatness, even the greatness of the banners of the dances of the camps of the wilderness?
Song of Songs.translator_note: No reference is printed for “and thou shalt provide out of all the people”; it is Exodus 18:21 (Rashi’s printed words are *ve'attah techezeh mikol ha'am*).

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: How beautiful are thy steps in sandals
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Mah yafu fe'amayikh bannealim* — they say to her: We desire that you cling to us because of the beauty and importance that we saw in you when you were in your beauty.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: O prince’s daughter
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Mah yafu fe'amayikh* — in the going up of the festivals, O daughter of nobles.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: The roundings of thy thighs are like the links of a chain
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Chamukei yerekhayikh kemo chala'im* — a collection of golden ornaments is called *chali ketem*, *el chali* in the Arabic language; and our Rabbis expounded it of the holes of the *shittin* of the libations, which were made from the six days of Creation round like a thigh; *kemo chala'im* is an expression of digging, like *chuliyot habor*.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Translated literally; *el chali*, *shittin* and *chuliyot habor* are left as printed.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: The work of the hands of a skilled workman
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Ma'aseh yedei aman* — the hands of the Holy One, blessed be He; in tractate Sukkah, *aman* is like the *uman* of the Holy One. Israel praise Him from above to below: they begin from His head, “His head is as the most fine gold,” and go down until they come to His legs, “pillars of marble,” because they come to appease Him to bring down His Presence from the upper regions to the lower; but He counts their praise from below to above: “How beautiful are thy steps” — these are the feet — and goes on counting until “Thy head upon thee is like Carmel,” until He comes to draw her to Himself.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Translated literally; the sentence on tractate Sukkah is elliptical.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Thy navel is like a round goblet
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Shorrekh agan hassahar* — thy navel: a basin of clear water in which they wash, and it is made of marble stones; and in the Arabic language it is called *sahar*, because the navel is like a round hole; he likened it to a round basin. And this praise is not of the matter of a woman’s beauty like the upper praise, for the upper is her Beloved praising her, and this is her companions praising her on account of her deeds, to say: Thou art fit to be joined with us. And the likeness: on account of the Chamber of Hewn Stone that sits in the navel of the earth.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Wherein no mingled wine is wanting
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Al yechsar hammazeg* — drink shall not fail from there; he means: there shall not cease and not stop from there any words of ruling (*hora'ah*).

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Thy belly is like a heap of wheat
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Bitnekh arimat chittim* — for all need it.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Set about with lilies
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Suggah bashoshannim* — fenced and hedged by a fence of lilies; a light fence suffices for her, and none of you breaks through it to enter. Behold, a bridegroom entering the chuppah, his heart yearning for the chuppah and for the affection of his marriage, comes to be intimate with her; she says to him, “I saw a drop of blood the size of a mustard seed” — behold, he turns his face to another side. And no snake bit him and no scorpion stung him; behold, one passes on the road, sees first-ripe figs at the tops of the fig trees, stretches out his hand to take; they say to him, “They belong to Israel” — he draws back his hand because of robbery. Behold: fenced about with lilies.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Translated literally; the sentence about the snake and the scorpion is elliptical.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Thy two breasts
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Shenei shadayikh* — the two Tablets. Another explanation: the king and the High Priest.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Thy neck is as a tower of ivory
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Tzavvarekh* — the Sanctuary and the altar, which are erect and high; and the Chamber of Hewn Stone is also made there, for strength and as a shield, like the tower of ivory.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Thine eyes as the pools in Heshbon
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Einayikh* — like the pools that are in Heshbon that draw water, so your eyes: “by the gate of Bath-rabbim” — your sages, when they sit in the gates of Jerusalem, the city daughter of a populous people (*rabbat am*), and are engaged in the calculation (*cheshbon*) of the seasons and the constellations, their wisdom and understanding draw the eyes of the nations like pools of water. And it can further be explained that *berekhot* in Heshbon are doves; and it is an expression of the Mishnah: “He who buys the doves of a dovecote must let fly the first *berekhah*”: קובי"רש in Old French.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Song of Songs 7:5 (“couvées”; the entry is numbered VII, 8 in the printed Darmesteter), in forms such as קובידש and קובירא; the printed form (קובי"רש) is a variant spelling.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Thy nose is like the tower of Lebanon
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Appekh keMigdal haLevanon* — I cannot explain it as “nose,” neither according to the plain sense nor according to the likeness, for what praise of beauty is there in a large nose, erect like a tower? So I say that *appekh* is an expression of “face”; and that is why it says it in the singular and does not say *appayikh*: it speaks of the forehead, which is the principal recognition of a face, as it is said (Isaiah 3), “The show of their countenance (*hakkarat penehem*) doth witness against them.” And you may know it, for He praises her going from below upward: “thine eyes — pools in Heshbon,” and after them the forehead; and so the nations praise (Ezekiel 3) “thy forehead hard against the forehead of all who come to do thee evil and to entice thee.”
Song of Songs.translator_note: Rashi’s wording of Ezekiel 3 differs from JPS (Ezekiel 3:8: “thy forehead hard against their foreheads”). Printed “Isaiah 3” is Isaiah 3:9.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Which looketh toward Damascus
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Kemigdal haLevanon tzofeh penei Dammesek* — I saw in a Midrash: this is the House of the Forest of Lebanon that Solomon built, so that one standing on it sees and counts how many houses there are in Damascus. Another explanation: “thy faces look toward Damascus” — looking forward to the coming of the gates of Jerusalem as far as Damascus, for it is destined to widen as far as Damascus.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Thy head upon thee is like Carmel
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Roshekh alayikh kaKarmel* — these are the tefillin of the head, of which it is said (Deuteronomy 25), “shall see that the name of the LORD is called upon thee, and they shall be afraid of thee”; behold, their strength and their dread are like a rock of the mountains; and Carmel is the head of the mountains.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Printed “Deuteronomy 25” is Deuteronomy 28:10.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: the hair of thy head like purple
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Vedallat roshekh* — the braiding of thy Nazirite hair, beautiful in its commandment, like the braiding of purple.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: the hair of thy head like purple
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Dallat roshekh* — because the braid is suspended (*mudalledet*) upon the height of the head.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: The king is held captive in the tresses thereof
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Melekh asur barehatim* — the Name of the Omnipresent is bound in tresses, as it is said (Numbers 6), “the crown (*nezer*) of his God is upon his head.”
Song of Songs.translator_note: Printed “Numbers 6” is Numbers 6:7 (JPS: “his consecration unto God is upon his head”).

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: in the tresses thereof
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Rehatim* — *korenz* in Old French; so they call the curls of the girdles (*azorot*) with which the belts are fastened. Another explanation: “the king is bound in *rehatim*” — the Holy One, blessed be He, is bound with love in commandments and in the acceptances (*retzuyot*) by which you run before Him.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Song of Songs 7:6 (“par tes boucles”), in forms such as קורנץ and קורנט; the printed form (קור"נץ) matches.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: How fair and how pleasant art thou
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Mah yafit umah na'amt* — after He specified the praise of each and every limb, He summed up everything: How fair art thou in all of thee, and how pleasant to cling to thee, a fitting love, to take delight in it.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: This thy stature is like to a palm-tree
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Zot komatekh damtah letamar* — we saw the beauty of thy stature in the days of Nebuchadnezzar, when all the nations were bowing and falling before the image, and thou wast standing in an erect stature like this palm.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: And thy breasts to clusters of grapes
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Veshadayikh le'eshkolot* — Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah, who were to thee like breasts from which to suck, resembled clusters that pour forth drink; so they poured forth to nurse and to teach all, for there is no fear like your fear. Until here the nations praised Him; from here on are the words of the Divine Presence to the exile of Israel among the nations.
Song of Songs.translator_note: The printed word for “breasts” is *kashdim*, evidently *kashadayim*; translated as “like breasts.”

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: I will climb up into the palm-tree
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Amarti e'eleh vetamar* — I take pride among the hosts above in you, that I shall be exalted and sanctified through you in the lower worlds, when you sanctify My name among the nations.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: I will take hold of the branches thereof
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Ochazah besansinav* — and I shall hold and cling to you; *sansinim* are branches.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: And let thy breasts be as clusters of the vine
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Veyihyu na shadayikh* — and now confirm My words, that thou be not enticed after the nations, and let the good and the wise among you stand in their faith, to answer words to those who entice thee, so that the small ones among them learn from them.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: And the roof of thy mouth like the best wine
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Vechikekh keyayin hatov* — be careful in thy answers that they be like the good wine.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: That glideth down smoothly for my beloved
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Holekh ledodi lemesharim* — I am careful to answer them that I stand in my faith, so that my palate go before my Beloved in love of uprightness, that is from the heart and not in deceit and crookedness.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: the best wine
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Keyayin hatov* — that makes the lips of the sleeping speak; even my fathers in the grave shall rejoice in it and give thanks for their lot. *Dovev* is “to cause to stir”: פרומ"יר in Old French, and its root is an expression of speech; and so is the answer: I am my Beloved’s and He too yearns for me.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Song of Songs 7:10 (“qui fait ouvrir (les lèvres des endormis)”), in forms such as פרומייר and פרומייד; the printed form (פרומ"יר) matches.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Come, my beloved, let us go forth into the field
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Lekhah dodi netze hassadeh* — our Rabbis expounded in Eruvin: The Assembly of Israel said: Master of the Universe, judge me not like the inhabitants of cities, in which there is robbery and forbidden relations, but like the inhabitants of unwalled towns, who are craftsmen and engage in Torah under pressure.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Let us lodge in the villages
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Nalinah bakefarim* — *nalinah bekhofrim*: Come and I will show thee the sons of Esau, to whom Thou hast shown goodness, and who deny Thee.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Let us get up early to the vineyards
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Nashkimah lakeramim* — these are synagogues and houses of study.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Let us see whether the vine hath budded
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Nir'eh im parechah hagefen* — these are the masters of Scripture.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Whether the vine-blossom be opened
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Pittach hasemadar* — when the blossom falls and the grapes are recognizable, it is “the *semadar* opened”; and to them He likened the masters of Mishnah, who are near to being benefited from in the rulings of the Torah.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: And the pomegranates be in flower
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Henetzu harimmonim* — when they are complete and the blossom around them falls; *henetzu* is “fell off”; and to them He likened the masters of Talmud, who are complete in wisdom and fit to rule.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: There will I give thee my love
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Sham eten et dodai* — there I will show thee My glory and My greatness, the praise of My sons and daughters.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: The mandrakes give forth fragrance
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Haduda'im natenu reiach* — *duda'ei* are figs, good and bad, as it is said (Jeremiah 24), “The LORD showed me, and behold two baskets (*duda'ei*) of figs,” etc., “the one basket had very good figs,” etc., “and the other basket had very bad figs, which could not be eaten” — these are the transgressors of Israel; now both gave fragrance: all of them seek Thy face.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Printed “Jeremiah 24” is Jeremiah 24:1–2; Rashi’s wording differs slightly from JPS (“One basket had very good figs …”).

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: And at our doors are all manner of precious fruits
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Ve'al petachenu kol megadim* — we have in our hands the reward of many commandments.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: New and old
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Chadashim gam yeshanim* — that the scribes renewed together with the old, that Thou hast written upon me.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Which I have laid up for thee
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Tzafanti lakh* — for Thy name and for Thy service I have hidden them in my heart. Another explanation: I have hidden them to show thee that you have fulfilled them.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Translated literally; the shift from “Thee” to “you” is as printed.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Oh that thou wert as my brother
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Mi yittenkha ke'ach li* — that Thou mayest come to comfort me in the way that Joseph did to his brothers, who repaid him evil, and of him it is said (Genesis 50), “And he comforted them.”
Song of Songs.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 50” is Genesis 50:21.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: When I should find thee without, I would kiss thee
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Emtza'akha vachutz eshakkekha* — I shall find Thy prophets speaking in Thy name, and I shall embrace them and kiss them; also I know that they will not despise me, for Thy love is worthy that Thy beloved go about seeking after it.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: my mother’s house
Song of Songs.english_translation: *El beit immi* — the Temple.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: That thou mightest instruct me
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Telammedeni* — as Thou wast accustomed to do in the Tent of Meeting.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: I would cause thee to drink of spiced wine
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Ashkekha miyayin haregach* — libations.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Of the juice of my pomegranate
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Asis* — sweet wine.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: His left hand should be under my head
Song of Songs.english_translation: [The source prints the lemma only, with no comment.]
Song of Songs.translator_note: The Hebrew source has only the lemma *semolo tachat roshi*.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Hishba'ti etchem* — now the Assembly of Israel turns her speech toward the nations: Although I complain and lament, my Beloved holds my hand and He is my support in my exile; therefore I have adjured you.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Why should you awaken, or stir up love
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Mah ta'iru umah te'orerru* — for it will not profit you.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Who is this that cometh up from the wilderness
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Mi zot* — the Holy One, blessed be He, and His court say of the Assembly of Israel: Who is this? — how important is this one who went up from the wilderness with all good gifts; there she was exalted, at the giving of the Torah and the cleaving of the Presence, and her affection was seen by all, and still she is in her exile.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Leaning upon her beloved
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Mitrappekket al dodah* — joining herself to her Beloved, acknowledging that she is His companion and cleaving to Him; *rafak* in the Arabic language is *rafakta*, a joining.
Song of Songs.translator_note: The Arabic word is left as printed.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Under the apple-tree I awakened thee
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Tachat hattapuach orartikha* — thus she says, requesting the affection of her Beloved: “Under the apple-tree I awakened thee” — remember that at the foot of Mount Sinai, which was made over my head in the form of an apple, there I awakened thee; and it is an expression of the affection of a wife of one’s youth who awakens her beloved in the nights, in slumbers upon the bed, embracing him and kissing him.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: There thy mother was in travail with thee
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Shammah chiblatekha immekha* — behold, we have said that the Holy One, blessed be He, called her His mother: there she became a mother to Thee.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: There was she in travail and brought thee forth
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Chiblatekha* — an expression of the pangs of a woman in childbirth; *chiblatekha*: pangs came to thee from thee, like (Jeremiah 10) “my children are gone forth of me” (*banai yetza'uni*; they went out from me).
Song of Songs.translator_note: Printed “Jeremiah 10” is Jeremiah 10:20.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Set me as a seal upon thy heart
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Simeni kachotam* — for the sake of that love, seal me upon Thy heart, that Thou forget me not, and see —

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: For love is strong as death
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Ki azzah kamavet ahavah* — the love with which I loved Thee is set against my death, for I was killed for Thy sake.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Jealousy is cruel as the grave
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Kashah khishe'ol kin'ah* — the contention in which the nations were jealous and contended against me for Thy sake; *kin'ah* everywhere is אינפ"רמנט in Old French, an expression of a grip of the heart to take vengeance.
Song of Songs.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: A very flame of the LORD
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Esh shalhevetyah* — sparks of strong fire that comes from the force of a flame of Gehinnom. The sense of the great *zakef* marked on *reshafeha* teaches us concerning the word *esh* that it is joined to *shalhevetyah*, to say: “fire of the flame of Yah.”

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Many waters cannot quench love
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Mayim rabbim lo yuchelu lechabbot et ha'ahavah* — since He called them by the term *reshafim* (sparks), the term “shall not be quenched” falls upon them.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Many waters
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Mayim rabbim* — the nations.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Neither can the floods drown it
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Unharot* — their princes and their kings.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Neither can the floods drown it
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Lo yishtefuhah* — by force and terror, and also by enticement and incitement.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: If a man would give all the substance of his house for love
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Im yitten ish et kol hon beito* — in order to exchange thy love.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: He would utterly be contemned
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Buz yavuzu lo* — all this the Holy One, blessed be He, and His court testify: that thus the Assembly of Israel clings to her Beloved.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: We have a little sister
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Atah achot lanu* — in the lower realms, that she is joined and associated and desires to be with us; and she is small, and makes herself small before all the nations, as it is said, “Not because you were more in number,” etc., for they make themselves small.
Song of Songs.translator_note: No reference is printed; the quotation is Deuteronomy 7:7.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: We have a little sister
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Achot* — an expression of mending: these are tears that are not mended.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Translated literally; the printed text is elliptical.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: And she hath no breasts
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Veshadayim ein lah* — as it is said regarding the exile of Egypt (Ezekiel 16), “thy breasts were fashioned,” when the time of redemption arrived; but this one has no breasts: the time has not yet arrived for “the time of love.”
Song of Songs.translator_note: Printed “Ezekiel 16” is Ezekiel 16:7 (JPS: “thy breasts were fashioned”); “the time of love” is Ezekiel 16:8.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: In the day when she shall be spoken for
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Mah na'aseh le'achotenu bayom sheyedubbar bah* — when the nations whisper against her to destroy her, as it is said (Psalms 83), “Come, and let us cut them off from being a nation.”
Song of Songs.translator_note: Printed “Psalms 83” is Psalms 83:5.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: If she be a wall
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Im chomah hi* — if she is strong in her faith and in her fear, to be against them like a wall of brass, that they not enter into her — he means that she not intermarry with them, and they not come into her, and she not be enticed by them.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: We will build upon her a turret of silver
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Nivneh aleha tirat kasef* — we shall be to her a fortified city, and a crown, and beauty, and we shall build for her the Holy City and the House of Choice.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: And if she be a door
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Ve'im delet hi* — that turns on its hinge, and by knocking upon it it is opened; so she too, if she opens to them, that they come into her and she into them.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: We will enclose her with boards of cedar
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Natzur aleha luach erez* — we shall put in her door boards of wood, which rot, and the worm drags them and eats them; and the Assembly of Israel says:

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: I am a wall
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Ani chomah* — strong in the love of my Beloved.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: And my breasts like the towers thereof
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Veshadai kamigdalot* — these are synagogues and houses of study, which nurse Israel with words of Torah.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Then was I in his eyes
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Az* — when I say this.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: As one that found peace
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Hayiti be'einav kemotzet shalom* — like a bride who is found whole and finds peace in her husband’s house.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Solomon had a vineyard at Baal-hamon
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Kerem hayah lishlomo* — this is the Assembly of Israel, as it is said (Isaiah 8), “For the vineyard of the LORD of hosts is the house of Israel.”
Song of Songs.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 8” is Isaiah 5:7.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Baal-hamon
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Beva'al hamon* — in Jerusalem, which is rich in people and a great multitude.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Baal-hamon
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Ba'al* — an expression of a plain, like (Joshua 12) “from Baal-gad in the valley of Lebanon.”
Song of Songs.translator_note: Printed “Joshua 12” is Joshua 12:7.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: He gave over the vineyard unto keepers
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Natan et hakerem lanotrim* — He delivered her into the hand of hard masters: Babylon, Media, Greece and Edom. In the Midrash of the Song of Songs I found some support for these *notrim*, that they are the kingdoms.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Every one for the fruit thereof
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Ish yavi befiryo* — all that they could collect from them, poll-taxes and levies and forced labour: everything they collected from them, to bring into their houses.
Song of Songs.translator_note: The words rendered “poll-taxes and levies and forced labour” (*gulgoliyot*, *arnoniyot*, *anfarot*) are translated by sense from the printed words.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: My vineyard, which is mine, is before me
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Karmi sheli lefanai* — on the Day of Judgment the Holy One, blessed be He, will bring them into judgment and say: “My vineyard, although I delivered it into your hands, is Mine and comes before Me; all that you seized for yourselves of its fruit and what you collected from them is not hidden from Me”; and they say:

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Thou, O Solomon, shalt have the thousand
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Ha'elef lekha Shelomoh* — the thousand of silver that we collected from them, all of it we shall return.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: And those that keep the fruit thereof two hundred
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Umatayim lanotrim et piryo* — and further we shall add much of our own, and give it to their heads and their sages, as it is said (Jeremiah 15), “Instead of the brass I will bring gold.”
Song of Songs.translator_note: Printed “Jeremiah 15” is Isaiah 60:17 (JPS: “For brass I will bring gold”); Rashi’s wording differs slightly.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: those that keep the fruit thereof
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Lanotrim et piryo* — these are disciples of the wise, and these payments are for disciples of the wise, as it is said (Isaiah 23), “for to those who dwell before the LORD shall be her merchandise, and the hire of Tyre.” And it can be explained: *umatayim lanotrim et piryo* — as the law of one who benefits from consecrated property, who pays the principal and a fifth; so too we shall pay for “Israel is holy to the LORD, the first-fruits of his increase,” principal and a fifth; the fifth of the principal, and two hundred is the fifth of a thousand.
Song of Songs.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 23” is Isaiah 23:18; Rashi’s wording differs from JPS (“for her gain shall be for them that dwell before the LORD”). The words “Israel is holy to the LORD, the first-fruits of his increase” are Jeremiah 2:3 (no reference is printed; JPS: “Israel is the LORD’S hallowed portion, His first-fruits of the increase”).

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Thou that dwellest in the gardens
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Hayoshevet baganim* — the Holy One, blessed be He, says to the Assembly of Israel: Thou who art scattered in the Exile, grazing in the gardens of others and dwelling in synagogues and houses of study.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: The companions hearken for thy voice
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Chaverim makshivim lekolekh* — the ministering angels, thy companions, the sons of God like thee, listen and come to hear thy voice in the synagogues.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Cause me to hear it
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Hashmi'ini* — and afterward they sanctify, as it says (Job 38), “sang together the morning stars” — these are Israel — and afterward “and all the sons of God shouted for joy.”
Song of Songs.translator_note: Printed “Job 38” is Job 38:7.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: Make haste, my beloved
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Berach dodi* — from this Exile, and redeem us from among them.

Song of Songs.english_lemma_JPS: And be thou like to a gazelle
Song of Songs.english_translation: *Udmeh lekha latzvi* — to hasten the redemption and cause Thy Presence to rest upon the mountains of spices, which is Mount Moriah and the Temple, which shall be built speedily in our days, Amen. The commentary on the Song of Songs is completed; praise to the Creator.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: in the days when the judges judged
Ruth.english_translation: *Vayehi bimei shefot hashofetim* — before Saul reigned as king, when the generations were provided for by judges; and it was in the days of Ibzan, as our Rabbis said: Ibzan is Boaz.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: And a certain man of Beth-lehem in Judah went
Ruth.english_translation: *Vayelekh ish* — he was very wealthy and the leader of the generation, and he left the Land of Israel for outside the Land because of narrowness of eye: his eye was narrow toward the poor who came to press him; for this he was punished.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: Ephrathites of Beth-lehem in Judah
Ruth.english_translation: *Efratim* — important ones; and so (I Samuel 1) “the son of Tohu, the son of Zuph, an Ephraimite” — *avgi'nus*: see his importance, for Eglon king of Moab married his daughter to Mahlon, as the Master said: Ruth was the daughter of Eglon. Another explanation: *Efratim* — Beth-lehem is called Ephrath.
Ruth.translator_note: The word אבגי"נוס is left as printed. Printed “I Samuel 1” is I Samuel 1:1.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: Naomi’s husband
Ruth.english_translation: *Ish Naomi* — why is it said? From here they said: a man dies only for his wife. (And it says “Naomi’s husband,” that is: since he was Naomi’s husband and ruled over her and she was secondary to him, therefore the attribute of judgment struck him and not her.)

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: both of them
Ruth.english_translation: *Gam shenehem* — what is “also”? At first they were struck in their property, and their camels and their cattle died; afterward they too died.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: And she went forth out of the place where she was
Ruth.english_translation: *Vatetze min hamakom* — why is it said? Behold, it was already said “and she returned from the field of Moab” — and from where could she return unless she went out of the place where she was? But it tells that the departure of a righteous person from a place is noticed and makes an impression: its splendor departed, its glory departed, the praise of the city departed; and so (Genesis 25) “And Jacob went out from Beer-sheba.”
Ruth.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 25” is Genesis 28:10. The words “and she returned from the field of Moab” are Ruth 1:6.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: for I am too old to have a husband
Ruth.english_translation: *Ki zakanti mihyot le'ish* — that I would marry and bear sons, and you would be married to them, for they are not forbidden to you and you are not forbidden to them on account of “the wife of his brother who was not in his world” — one who is not bound to a levirate marriage — because they were not Mahlon’s and Chilion’s: betrothal does not take effect with them, for they were foreigners and had not converted, and now they come to convert, as it is said, “for with thee we will return to thy people; from now on we shall be one people.”
Ruth.translator_note: The words “for with thee we will return to thy people” are Ruth 1:10 (JPS: “Nay, but we will return with thee unto thy people”); the words “from now on we shall be one people” do not occur in that verse in JPS’s text. No reference is printed.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: If I should say: I have hope
Ruth.english_translation: *Ki amarti yesh li tikvah* — for even if my heart said to me, I have hope to be married again and to bear sons.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: should I even have an husband to-night
Ruth.english_translation: *Vegam hayiti halaylah le'ish* — and more than that, even if I had conceived males tonight.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: and also bear sons
Ruth.english_translation: *Vegam yaladti banim* — or even if I had already borne sons.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: would you tarry for them till they were grown
Ruth.english_translation: *Halahen tesabberna* — as a question of astonishment: Perhaps for them you will wait until they grow up? An expression of (Psalms 146) “whose hope (*sivro*) is in the LORD his God.”
Ruth.translator_note: Printed “Psalms 146” is Psalms 146:5.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: would you shut yourselves off for them
Ruth.english_translation: *Te'agenah* — an expression of binding, of prison, like “he drew a circle (*ug ugah*) and stood within it”; and some explain it as an expression of *igun* (being chained), but that cannot be, for if so it should have had its nun pointed with a dagesh or been written with two nuns.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: for the hand of the LORD is gone forth against me
Ruth.english_translation: *Ki yatz'ah vi yad Hashem* — Rabbi Levi said: Wherever it says “the hand of the LORD,” it is a plague of pestilence, and the prototype for all of them is (Exodus 9) “Behold, the hand of the LORD is (*hoveh*) …”
Ruth.translator_note: Printed “Exodus 9” is Exodus 9:3 (JPS: “behold, the hand of the LORD is upon thy cattle … there shall be a very grievous murrain”).

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: Behold, thy sister-in-law is gone back unto her people
Ruth.english_translation: *Hinneh shavah yevimtekh* — its accent is above, over the *shin*, because it is past tense, (Esther 2) “and in the morning she returned (*hi shavah*)”; its accent is below, on the *bet*, because it is present tense; and so with all like these.
Ruth.translator_note: Printed “Esther 2” is Esther 2:14 (JPS: “and on the morrow she returned”).

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: Entreat me not to leave thee
Ruth.english_translation: *Al tifge'i vi* — do not press me.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: for whither thou goest, I will go
Ruth.english_translation: *Ki el asher telekhi elekh* — from here our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said: A proselyte who comes to convert, they inform him of some of the punishments, so that if he comes to retract he may retract; for from the words of Ruth you learn that Naomi said to her: “It is forbidden for us to go outside the boundary on the Sabbath”; she said to her: “Whither thou goest I will go.” “It is forbidden for us that a female be alone with a male who is not her husband”; she said to her: “Where thou lodgest I will lodge.” “We are separated from the other peoples by six hundred and thirteen commandments”; “thy people shall be my people.” “It is forbidden for us ע"א”; “thy God my God.” “Four death penalties were handed over to the court”; “where thou diest I will die.” “Two graves were handed over to the court, one for those stoned and burned and one for those slain and strangled”; she said to her: “and there will I be buried.”
Ruth.translator_note: The abbreviation ע"א is left as printed and not resolved here.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: the LORD do so to me
Ruth.english_translation: *Koh ya'aseh Hashem li* — as He began to do evil, that His hand went forth against me, to kill my husband and to bring me down from my property.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: and more also
Ruth.english_translation: *Vechoh yosif* — if He should separate between me and between thee except for death.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: she left off speaking unto her
Ruth.english_translation: *Vattechdal ledabber elehah* — from here they said: they do not press him further and do not examine him too closely.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: So they two went
Ruth.english_translation: *Vattelakhnah shetehem* — Rabbi Abbahu said: Come and see how beloved proselytes are before the Holy One, blessed be He; as soon as she set her mind to convert, Scripture made her equal to Naomi.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: all the city was astir concerning them
Ruth.english_translation: *Vattehom kol ha'ir* — the whole city became astir; all of them were gathered to bury the wife of Boaz, who died on that day.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: Is this Naomi?
Ruth.english_translation: *Hazot Naomi* — the *heh* is pointed with a *chataf* because it is a question of astonishment: Is this Naomi, who was accustomed to go out in covered wagons (*tzavim*) and on mules? See what has come upon her, for having gone out to outside the Land.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: I went out full
Ruth.english_translation: *Meleah halakhti* — with wealth and sons. Another explanation: that she was pregnant.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: hath testified against me
Ruth.english_translation: *Anah vi* — He testified against me that I was wicked before Him. Another explanation: *anah vi* — the attribute of judgment, like “and the pride of Israel shall testify (*ve'anah ge'on Yisrael*).”
Ruth.translator_note: The quotation is Hosea 5:5 (no reference is printed; JPS: “But the pride of Israel shall testify to his face”).

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: in the beginning of barley harvest
Ruth.english_translation: *Bitchilat ketzir se'orim* — Scripture speaks of the cutting of the Omer.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: a kinsman of her husband’s
Ruth.english_translation: *Moda* — a relative; he was the son of the brother of Elimelech. Our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said: Elimelech and Salmon, the father of Boaz, and Peloni Almoni, the redeemer, and the father of Naomi were all sons of Nahshon son of Amminadab, and the merit of their fathers did not help them when they left the Land for outside the Land.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: Let me now go to the field
Ruth.english_translation: *Elkhah na hassadeh* — to one of the fields of the men of the city, after one of them in whose eyes I shall find favour, that he not rebuke me.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: after him in whose sight I shall find favour
Ruth.english_translation: *Ve'alakketah vashibbolim achar asher emtza chen be'einav* — after whom? He in whose eyes I shall find favour.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: And she went, and came and gleaned in the field
Ruth.english_translation: *Vattavo vattelakket bassadeh* — we find in the Midrash Ruth: “before she went she came,” for it says “and she came” and afterward “and she gleaned”; but she was marking the roads before she entered the field, and went and came and returned to the city, in order to make signs and markers, that she not err in the paths and would know how to return.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: and her hap was to light on the portion of the field
Ruth.english_translation: [The source prints only the words of the verse here:] *Vayyiker mikreha lavo bechelkat hassadeh asher leVo'az* — “and her hap was to light on the portion of the field belonging unto Boaz.”
Ruth.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment; the lemma shown is the corresponding phrase of the verse.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: Whose damsel is this?
Ruth.english_translation: *Lemi hanna'arah hazot* — but was it Boaz’s way to ask about women? Rather, he saw in her matters of modesty and wisdom: two ears of grain she gleaned; three she did not glean; and she was gleaning the standing ones while standing and the fallen ones while sitting, so as not to bend down.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: that came back with Naomi
Ruth.english_translation: *Hashavah im Naomi* — the accent is above, over the *shin*, because it is past tense and not a language of acting.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: and she said
Ruth.english_translation: *Vato'mer* — in her heart.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: Let me glean, I pray you
Ruth.english_translation: *Alakketah na* — the gleaning of ears.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: gather after the reapers among the sheaves
Ruth.english_translation: *Ve'asafti ba'omarim* — the forgotten portion of sheaves.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: and when thou art thirst
Ruth.english_translation: *Vetzamit vehalakhta el hakelim* — and if you are thirsty, be not ashamed to go and drink from the vessels of water that the young men draw.
Ruth.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment; the lemma shown is the corresponding phrase of the verse. The printed word is *vetzamit* (the verse has *vetzamt*).

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: though I be not as one of thy handmaidens
Ruth.english_translation: *Lo ehyeh ke'achat shifchotekha* — I am not as important as one of thy maidservants.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: dip thy morsel in the vinegar
Ruth.english_translation: *Vetavalt pittekh bachometz* — from here: vinegar is good for the heat.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: they reached her parched corn
Ruth.english_translation: *Vayitzbot lah kali* — and he handed to her; it has no parallel in Scripture but in the language of the Mishnah: “the outsides and the inside and the house of gripping (*beit hatzeviyah*).”
Ruth.translator_note: Translated literally; the Mishnaic phrase is left as printed.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: And also pull out some for her of purpose
Ruth.english_translation: *Vegam shol tashollu* — *shachoach tishkechu*: make yourselves as though you are forgetting; the Targum of “every error (*shegagah*)” is *shelutah*, and so *al hashal*. Another explanation: an expression of “for thine olives shall drop off (*yeshal*).”
Ruth.translator_note: Translated literally; in the source the whole comment is printed inside the lemma brackets, and the phrase *al hashal* is left as printed. The quotation “for thine olives shall drop off” is Deuteronomy 28:40 (no reference is printed). The Aramaic is translated as printed.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: from the bundles
Ruth.english_translation: *Tzevatim* — small sheaves; there is a parallel to it in the language of the Mishnah: “he found them *tzevatim* or bundles (*kerikhot*).”
Ruth.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: blessed be he that did take knowledge of thee
Ruth.english_translation: *Yehi makirekh barukh* — the owner of the field, who showed thee favour to glean in his field.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: to the living and to the dead
Ruth.english_translation: *Et hachayyim ve'et hametim* — that He sustains and provides for the living and attends to the needs of the dead.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: Boaz our kinsman
Ruth.english_translation: [The source prints the lemma only, with no comment.]
Ruth.translator_note: The Hebrew source has only the lemma *moda'atenu kerovenu*, which differs from the words of the verse.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: he winnoweth barley to-night
Ruth.english_translation: *Hinneh hu zoreh* — the chaff: ווונטו"ר in Old French.
Ruth.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Ruth 3:2 (“vannant”), in forms such as ווניר and בונייר; the printed form (ווונטו"ר) differs. The source gives no lemma for this comment; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: to-night
Ruth.english_translation: *Halaylah* — for the generation was breached by theft and robbery, and he slept in his threshing-floor to guard his threshing-floor.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: Wash thyself therefore
Ruth.english_translation: *Verachatzt* — from the filth of your idolatry.
Ruth.translator_note: The printed text abbreviates “idolatry” as ע"ז.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: anoint thee
Ruth.english_translation: *Vasakht* — these are commandments.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: put thy raiment upon thee
Ruth.english_translation: *Vesamt simlotayikh* — Sabbath garments.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: get thee down to the threshing-floor
Ruth.english_translation: *Veyaradt hagoren* — *veyaradti* is written: my merit will go down with thee.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: make not thyself known unto the man
Ruth.english_translation: *Al toda'i la'ish* — to Boaz.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: And she went down unto the threshing
Ruth.english_translation: *Vattered hagoren vatta'as* — she said to her: “Wash thyself, and anoint thee, and put thy raiment upon thee,” and afterward “get thee down to the threshing-floor,” but she did not do so; rather she said: If I go down adorned, whoever meets me and sees me will say that I am a harlot; therefore she first went down to the threshing-floor and afterward adorned herself, as her mother-in-law had commanded.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: his heart was merry
Ruth.english_translation: *Vayyitav libbo* — he engaged in Torah.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: she came softly
Ruth.english_translation: *Vattavo valat* — gently.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: the man was startled
Ruth.english_translation: *Vayecherad ha'ish* — he supposed it was a demon and wished to cry out, and she held him and wrapped him in her arms.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: turned himself
Ruth.english_translation: *Vayyilafet* — and he took hold, like (Judges 16) “and Samson took fast hold” (*vayyilfot Shimshon*).
Ruth.translator_note: Printed “Judges 16” is Judges 16:29.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: behold, a woman lay at his feet
Ruth.english_translation: *Vehinneh ishah* — he put his hand on her head and recognized that she was a woman.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: spread therefore thy skirt over thy handmaid
Ruth.english_translation: *Ufarasta kenafekha* — the corner of thy garment, to cover me with thy cloak, and it is an expression of marriage.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: for thou art a near kinsman
