Ruth.english_translation: *Ki go'el attah* — to redeem the inheritance of my husband, as it is said (Leviticus 25), “then shall his kinsman that is next unto him come, and shall redeem,” etc.; and my mother-in-law and I need to sell our inheritance, and now it is upon thee to buy; buy me also with it, that the name of the dead be remembered upon his inheritance; when I come to the field they will say: This is the wife of Mahlon.
Ruth.translator_note: Printed “Leviticus 25” is Leviticus 25:25; Rashi’s wording (*ba go'alo hakarov elav ug'al*) differs slightly from JPS (“his kinsman that is next unto him come, and shall redeem”).

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: in the end than at the beginning
Ruth.english_translation: *Min harishon* — that which thou didst with thy mother-in-law.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: it is true that I am a near kinsman
Ruth.english_translation: *Ve'attah ki omnam* — *im* is written and not read, that is: it implies doubt; certainly there is a redeemer nearer than he. (Another version: if it implies doubt, and it is certain.) Rabbi Joshua ben Levi said: Salmon and Elimelech and Tov were brothers; and what is “who was our brother Elimelech’s”? A man always calls his uncle his brother, as it is said (Genesis 14), “And when Abram heard that his brother was taken captive” — but was Abraham not his uncle? So was Boaz to Elimelech a brother’s son, a relative of Mahlon; but Tov was a nearer relative.
Ruth.translator_note: The quoted words “who was our brother Elimelech’s” are Ruth 4:3 (no reference is printed). Printed “Genesis 14” is Genesis 14:14.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: a kinsman nearer than I
Ruth.english_translation: *Karov mimmeni* — for he is a brother and I am a brother’s son.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: Tarry this night
Ruth.english_translation: *Lini halaylah* — lodge without a man.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: as the LORD liveth
Ruth.english_translation: *Chai Hashem* — she said to him: With words thou art putting me off; he sprang up and swore to her that he was not putting her off with words. Some of our Rabbis said: he swore to his inclination, for his inclination was accusing him: Thou art single and she is single — come upon her; and he swore that he would not come upon her except by marriage.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: Let it not be known that the woman came to the threshing-floor
Ruth.english_translation: *Vayomer al yivvada* — it refers back to “and she rose up before one could discern”; he urged her to rise, for he said in his heart: It is not to my honour that it be known that the woman came to the threshing-floor.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: he measured six measures of barley
Ruth.english_translation: *Shesh se'orim* — it is impossible to say six *se'ah*, for it is not a woman’s way to carry such a burden; rather six actual barleys; and he hinted to her that there is destined to issue from her a son who will be blessed with six blessings: the spirit of wisdom and understanding, counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and the fear of the LORD.
Ruth.translator_note: The six blessings are listed from Isaiah 11:2 (no reference is printed).

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: until he have finished the thing this day
Ruth.english_translation: [The source prints the lemma only, with no comment.]
Ruth.translator_note: The Hebrew source has only the lemma *ki im kilah ha'ish et hadavar hayom*.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: Ho, such a one!
Ruth.english_translation: *Peloni almoni* — and his name is not written because he did not wish to redeem.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: Ho, such a one!
Ruth.english_translation: *Peloni almoni* — it is translated in the Prophets (I Samuel 21) as *kasi vetamir* (“hidden and concealed”).
Ruth.translator_note: Printed “I Samuel 21” is I Samuel 21:3 (the Targum of the Prophets).

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: Ho, such a one!
Ruth.english_translation: *Peloni* — covered and hidden; an expression of (Deuteronomy 17) “If there arise a matter too hard (*yippale*) for thee,” (Genesis 18) “Is any thing too hard (*hayippale*) for the LORD.”
Ruth.translator_note: Printed “Deuteronomy 17” is Deuteronomy 17:8; “Genesis 18” is Genesis 18:14.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: Ho, such a one!
Ruth.english_translation: *Almoni* — *almon*, without a name. (Another version: *Almoni*, who was a widower (*alman*) of words of Torah, for he should have expounded “an Ammonite” and not “an Ammonitess,” “a Moabite” and not “a Moabitess”; and he said, “lest I mar mine own inheritance.”)
Ruth.translator_note: The printed abbreviation מד"ת is read here as “of words of Torah.”

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: for there is none to redeem it beside thee
Ruth.english_translation: *Ve'eda'ah ki ein zulatekh* — a near relative to redeem.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: hast thou also bought of Ruth the Moabitess
Ruth.english_translation: *Umei'et Rut haMo'aviyah* — thou must buy, and she does not consent unless thou take her as wife.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: lest I mar mine own inheritance
Ruth.english_translation: *Pen ashchit et nachalati* — my seed, as (Psalms 127) “Lo, children are a heritage (*nachalat*) of the LORD”; to put a blemish in my seed, as it is said (Deuteronomy 23) “An Ammonite or a Moabite shall not enter”; and he erred about an Ammonite and not an Ammonitess.
Ruth.translator_note: Printed “Psalms 127” is Psalms 127:3; “Deuteronomy 23” is Deuteronomy 23:4.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: concerning redeeming
Ruth.english_translation: *Al hage'ullah* — this is sale.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: and concerning exchanging
Ruth.english_translation: *Temurah* — this is exchange.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: a man drew off his shoe
Ruth.english_translation: *Shalaf ish na'alo* — this is the acquisition, as we acquire by a kerchief in place of a shoe; and our Rabbis, of blessed memory, differed on the matter, who gave to whom: some say that one acquires with the vessel of the acquirer, and Boaz gave to the redeemer; and some say that one acquires with the vessel of the one who transfers, and the redeemer gave to Boaz.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: this was the attestation in Israel
Ruth.english_translation: *Vezot hate'udah beYisra'el* — the law of testimony.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: to raise up the name of the dead upon his inheritance
Ruth.english_translation: *Lehakim shem hamet al nachalato* — since his wife goes out and comes in the inheritance, bringing in and taking out, they say: This was the wife of Mahlon; his name is mentioned through her.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: like Rachel and like Leah
Ruth.english_translation: *KeRachel vechLe'ah* — although they were of the tribe of Judah and of the sons of Leah, they acknowledge Rachel, who was the mainstay of the house, and they put Rachel before Leah.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: be famous in Beth-lehem
Ruth.english_translation: *Ukra shem* — that is: may thy name be great.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: like the house of Perez
Ruth.english_translation: *Kevet Peretz* — from whom we came out.

Ruth.english_lemma_JPS: Now these are the generations of Perez
Ruth.english_translation: *Ve'elleh toledot Peretz* — since he traced David by the name of Ruth the Moabitess, he returned and traced him by the name of Judah. The Scroll of Ruth is concluded.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: HOW DOTH the city sit solitary
Lamentations.english_translation: *Eichah yashvah vadad* — Jeremiah wrote a book of lamentations; it is the scroll that Jehoiakim burned, upon the brazier that was on the fire, and it had in it three alphabetical acrostics: “How doth the city sit solitary,” “How hath … cloud” (*Eichah ya'iv*), “How is the gold become dim” (*Eichah yu'am*). Afterward he added to it “I am the man” (*Ani hagever*), which is three alphabetical acrostics, as it is said (Jeremiah 36), “and there were added besides unto them many like words”: three against three.
Lamentations.translator_note: Printed “Jeremiah 36” is Jeremiah 36:32.

Lamentations.english_translation: *Badad* — bereft of her inhabitants.

*Rabbati am* — an extra yod, as in *rabbat am*, that had a multitude with her. There are many midrashim of Aggadah, and I have come to explain the language of Scripture according to its plain meaning.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: How is she become as a widow!
Lamentations.english_translation: *Hayetah ke'almanah* — and not a widow in fact, but like a woman whose husband went to a country overseas and whose mind is to return to her.
*Bakho tivkeh* — two weepings for two destructions.

*Balailah* — for the Temple was burned at night, as the Master said: “Toward evening they set fire to it.” Another explanation: *balailah* — the night of the weeping of the spies, on the Ninth of Av, caused it to them. Another explanation: *balailah* — for whoever weeps at night, the one who hears his voice weeps with him.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: And her tears are on her cheeks
Lamentations.english_translation: *Vedim'atah al lechayah* — because she weeps constantly.
*Kol re'eha* — her lovers.
*Galetah Yehudah* — from her land.
*Me'oni* — on account of poverty.
*Umerov avodah* — for the Chaldeans made it heavy upon her.
*Hi yashvah baggoyim* — and in the place where she was exiled and dwelt, she found no rest.
*Bein hammetzarim* — for there is a height on this side and on that side, and no place to flee.
*Hammetzarim* — the borders of a field and a vineyard; and an aggadic midrash: between the Seventeenth of Tammuz and the Ninth of Av.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: none come to the solemn assembly
Lamentations.english_translation: *Ba'ei mo'ed* — pilgrims.
*Nugot* — an expression of sorrow, and there is no root in the word except the gimel alone.
*Shalu* — dwelling at ease.
*Hugah* — He grieved her; and it is an expression of sorrow.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: Her princes are become like harts That find no pasture
Lamentations.english_translation: *Ke'ayalim lo matze'u mir'eh* — like harts that have found no pasture, that have no strength to flee, for their strength was weakened by hunger.

*Lifnei rodef* — every *rodef* in Scripture is defective, and this one is full, for they were pursued with a complete pursuit; therefore the paytan composed, “full is *rodfati*, and defective *shnat ge'ulai*”; “the year of my redeemed is come” is written defective.
Lamentations.translator_note: Translated literally; the poem quoted is not identified, and the second quotation is Isaiah 63:4 (no reference is printed; JPS: “And My year of redemption are come”).

Lamentations.english_translation: *Zacharah Yerushalayim* — in her exile.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: In the days of her affliction
Lamentations.english_translation: *Yemei oneyah* — the days of her destruction, which brought her to poverty.
*Umerudeha* — an expression of distress, like (Judges 11) “and go down upon the mountains” (*veyaradti*), (Psalms 55) “I am distraught (*arid*) in my complaint, and will moan.”
Lamentations.translator_note: Printed “Judges 11” is Judges 11:37; “Psalms 55” is Psalms 55:3.

Lamentations.english_translation: *Kol machamaddeha* — and she remembered all the good of her treasures from days of old.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: They have mocked at her desolations
Lamentations.english_translation: *Sachaku al mishbatteha* — they rejoiced over the cessation of her joy, her festival, her new moon and her Sabbath; and ומ"א expounds it in another way: that they used to rest in exile on Sabbaths and festivals and let the land rest in sabbatical years, and the nations mocked them and said: Fools! In your land you did not observe, and now in exile you will observe.
Lamentations.translator_note: The abbreviation ומ"א is left as printed and not resolved here.

Lamentations.english_translation: *Lenidah* — to exile, an expression of “wandering and fugitive” (*na vanad*): אישמוב"ר in Old French.
Lamentations.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Lamentations 1:8 (“condamnée au mouvement”), in forms such as איטמובמינט and אשמוביר; the printed form (אישמוב"ר) is a variant spelling.

Lamentations.english_translation: *Ervatah* — her disgrace.
*Nenechah* — an expression of a passive verb: שושפי"דר in Old French. “They have heard that I sigh” is a noun: שושפורי"דא.
Lamentations.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Lamentations 1:8 (“elle gémit”), in forms such as שושפיריר and שושפיריאה, and distinguishes the verb from the noun (שושפירוזא and similar forms); the printed forms (שושפי"דר, שושפורי"דא) are variant spellings. The quotation “They have heard that I sigh” is Lamentations 1:21 (no reference is printed).

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: Her filthiness was in her skirts
Lamentations.english_translation: *Tum'atah bishuleha* — an expression of disgrace: the blood of her impurity is evident in the hems of her garments; that is, her sins are revealed; she did them much in the open.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: She was not mindful of her end
Lamentations.english_translation: *Lo zacharah acharitah* — when they sinned they did not set their heart to what their end would be; therefore “she is come down wonderfully”: their descent is wondrous, very wondrous, for all were amazed at what befell her that befell no other city.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: The adversary hath spread out his hand
Lamentations.english_translation: *Yado paras tzar* — Ammon and Moab.
Lamentations.translator_note: The source gives no separate lemma; the printed comment begins with the words of the verse (before the dash), and the lemma shown is the corresponding phrase of the verse.

Lamentations.english_translation: *Al kol machamaddeha* — Torah scrolls, of which it is said (Psalms 19), “those more to be desired than gold”; all turned to plunder silver and gold, and they turned to the Torah scrolls to burn them, because it is written in them (Deuteronomy 23), “An Ammonite … shall not enter,” etc.
Lamentations.translator_note: The source gives no separate lemma; the printed comment begins with the words of the verse (before the dash), and the lemma shown is the corresponding phrase of the verse. Printed “Psalms 19” is Psalms 19:11 (JPS: “More to be desired are they than gold”); “Deuteronomy 23” is Deuteronomy 23:4.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: Concerning whom Thou didst command That they should not enter into Thy congregation
Lamentations.english_translation: *Asher tzivvita lo yavo'u vakahal lakh* — these are Ammon and Moab.
Lamentations.translator_note: The source gives no separate lemma; the printed comment begins with the words of the verse (before the dash), and the lemma shown is the corresponding phrase of the verse.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: Let it not come unto you
Lamentations.english_translation: *Lo aleikhem* — there shall not be a distress like this any more, for all who pass by. *Al dat*: the Sages said: from here a complaint from the Torah; “See what He did to me,” “Behold, and see,” etc.
Lamentations.translator_note: Translated literally; the clause “*al dat* … a complaint from the Torah” is elliptical as printed.

Lamentations.english_translation: *Asher olal* — that was done to me.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: Wherewith the LORD hath afflicted me
Lamentations.english_translation: *Asher hugah Hashem* — me, on the day of His fierce anger; this too is an expression of sorrow.

*Vayeridenah* — and he subdued it and broke it by subjugation and sufferings; therefore the nun has a dagesh, to interpret it in the singular, like *ya'asennah*, *yekharsemennah*, *yir'ennah*, for the bone is a feminine noun, as you say (Ezekiel 36) “the dry bones” — he broke each and every one. Another explanation: *vayeridenah* is like (Judges 14) “and he scraped it out (*vayyerdehu*) into his hands”: he empties the brain, drags and scrapes the brain out of it.
Lamentations.translator_note: Printed “Ezekiel 36” is Ezekiel 37:4 (JPS: “O you dry bones”); printed “Judges 14” is Judges 14:9.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: The yoke of my transgressions is impressed by His hand
Lamentations.english_translation: *Nisqad ol pish'ai beyado* — this word has no parallel in Scripture; and in the Aramaic language of the Pesikta a goad is called *masqeda*, “ox-goad” (*malmad habakar*); and I say *nisqad* — פויינט"רינט in Old French: dotted, spotted and marked were my transgressions in the hand of the Holy One, blessed be He, as a memorial, that their number and their payments not be forgotten.
Lamentations.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Lamentations 1:14 (“marquée, littéralement pointée”), in forms such as פויינטוריץ and פוינטריץ; the printed form (פויינט"רינט) is a variant spelling.

Lamentations.english_translation: *Yistaregu* — they were made into braids upon braids and went up upon my neck; an expression of the Mishnah: “One does not interlace the beds (*ein mesharegin et hammittot*).”
Lamentations.translator_note: Translated literally; the Mishnaic phrase is left as printed.

Lamentations.english_translation: *Silah* — trampled and trod down; an expression of (Isaiah 62) “Cast up, cast up the highway (*solu solu hammesillah*).”
Lamentations.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 62” is Isaiah 62:10.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: He hath called a solemn assembly against me
Lamentations.english_translation: *Kara alai mo'ed* — a gathering of troops to come against me. And our Rabbis expounded what they expounded: Tammuz of that year was full — the fullness of the second year of their exodus from Egypt; therefore it befell, the return of the festivals, on the night of the Ninth of Av, on which weeping was fixed for the generations.
Lamentations.translator_note: Translated literally; the printed passage is elliptical. The Aramaic is translated as printed.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: The Lord hath trodden as in a winepress
Lamentations.english_translation: *Gat darakh* — an expression of killing, like (Isaiah 62) “I have trodden the winepress alone”; like treading grapes to bring out their wine, so He trampled the women to bring out their blood.
Lamentations.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 62” is Isaiah 63:3.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: Mine eye, mine eye runneth down with water
Lamentations.english_translation: *Eini eini* — that is: constantly my eye runs down with water; the doubling of the language teaches that there are no pauses.

*Perasah Tziyyon beyadeha* — like (Isaiah 25) “And he shall spread forth his hands in the midst thereof”: like a man who moves his hands, taking them back and forth and distressing over them. Another explanation: *perasah Tziyyon* is an expression of breaking, like (Lamentations 4) “and none breaketh it unto them” (*uforesh ein lahem*), to receive, to comfort him for the dead; so Menachem composed it. And in the language of the Mishnah its explanation is “established,” and its sense is like a man who is distressed, who clasps his hands and breaks them. I found an addition.
Lamentations.translator_note: Translated literally; the sentence on the language of the Mishnah is elliptical. Printed “Isaiah 25” is Isaiah 25:11; “Lamentations 4” is Lamentations 4:4.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: That they that are round about him should be his adversaries
Lamentations.english_translation: *Tziva Hashem leYa'akov sevivav tzarav* — He commanded concerning Jacob that his adversaries be round about him; even when they were exiled to Babylon and to Assyria, Sennacherib exiled their enemies, Ammon and Moab, and settled them beside them, and they taunt them, as stated in tractate Kiddushin: “There is a Humanya in Babylon, all of it of Ammonites.”
Lamentations.translator_note: The Aramaic is translated as printed: *Humanya ika beBavel kulah de'amonai*.

Lamentations.english_translation: *Lenidah* — for distancing, for scorn.
*Karati lamevahavai* — to those who show themselves as lovers.

*Hemmah rimmuni* — such as the sons of Ishmael, who used to go out to meet the exiles when the Sabeans were leading them by a road upon them, and showed themselves as though pitying them, and brought out for them kinds of salted food and inflated skins which they supposed were wine, and they ate and were thirsty and wished to drink, and when one untied the skin with his teeth the wind entered his bowels and he died; and this is what Scripture says (Isaiah 21), “In the thickets in Arabia shall you lodge,” etc., (ibid.) “Unto him that is thirsty bring you water! The inhabitants of the land of Tema did meet the fugitive with his bread.”
Lamentations.translator_note: Translated literally; “when the Sabeans were leading them by a road upon them” is as printed. Printed “Isaiah 21” is Isaiah 21:13–14.

Lamentations.english_translation: *Veyashivu et nafsham* — so that they might refresh their souls.
*Chamarmaru* — they shrank; and there is in the language of the Mishnah: “she fell into the fire and her bowels shrivelled up (*venitchamru*).”
Lamentations.translator_note: Translated literally; the Mishnaic phrase is left as printed.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: At home there is the like of death
Lamentations.english_translation: *Babayit kamavet* — inside the house was the terror of demons and harmful spirits and angels of death, and outside the sword of the enemy bereaves.

*Ki attah asita* — Thou didst cause me that they hate me, for Thou didst separate me from their food and from their banquets and from intermarrying with them; if I had intermarried with them they would have had pity on me and on the children of their daughters.
Lamentations.translator_note: The printed word for “didst cause” is *yagramt*, left as printed.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: Thou wilt bring the day that Thou hast proclaimed
Lamentations.english_translation: *Hevet yom karata* — would that Thou wouldst bring upon them the appointed day that Thou didst proclaim against me.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: And they shall be like unto me
Lamentations.english_translation: *Veyihyu chamoni* — in evil.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: Let all their wickedness come before Thee
Lamentations.english_translation: *Tavo chol ra'atam lefanekha* — may their iniquities be remembered and visited before Thee.
*Ve'olel lamo* — and do to them, like (Proverbs 20) “Even by his doings (*ma'alalav*) a child is known,” (Jeremiah 21) “according to the fruit of your doings (*ma'alleikhem*).”
Lamentations.translator_note: Printed “Proverbs 20” is Proverbs 20:11; “Jeremiah 21” is Jeremiah 21:14. Rashi’s quotation of Proverbs 20:11 omits the word “child.”

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: How hath the Lord covered with a cloud
Lamentations.english_translation: *Eichah ya'iv* — He darkens, as it is said (I Kings 18), “and the heaven grew black with clouds (*hishtakkedru be'avim*).”
Lamentations.translator_note: Printed “I Kings 18” is I Kings 18:45.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: He hath cast down from heaven unto the earth
Lamentations.english_translation: *Mishamayim eretz* — after He had raised them up to the heavens He cast them to earth all at once and not little by little: from a high roof to a deep pit.
Lamentations.translator_note: The Aramaic proverb (*me'igra rama levira amikta*) is translated as printed.

Lamentations.english_translation: *Hadom raglav* — a stool for His feet; and this is the Temple.
*Ne'ot Ya'akov* — the houses of Jacob, an expression of dwelling.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: He hath brought them down to the ground
Lamentations.english_translation: *Higia la'aretz* — He lowered them to the ground.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: He hath profaned the kingdom and the princes thereof
Lamentations.english_translation: *Chillel mamlakhah* — these are Israel, who were called (Exodus 19) “a kingdom of priests.”
Lamentations.translator_note: Printed “Exodus 19” is Exodus 19:6.

Lamentations.english_translation: *Vesareha* — a midrash of Aggadah: these are the princes above, whom the one appointed over fire exchanged — he appointed him over water — and exchanged all the appointees; because among the wicked of Israel there were masters of the Explicit Name, and they trusted that they would adjure the princes above to save them from fire and from water and from sword; and now when he adjured the prince of fire by his name, he answers: this dominion is not in my hand; and so all of them.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: He hath drawn back His right hand From before the enemy
Lamentations.english_translation: *Heshiv achor yemino* — He drew Himself back as one who draws back his right hand from fighting on behalf of His sons.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: He hath bent His bow like an enemy
Lamentations.english_translation: *Darakh kashto* — since it is the way of bows, which are strong, to set one’s foot upon them when bending them, therefore it is written in the language of treading.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: He hath poured out His fury like fire
Lamentations.english_translation: *Shafakh ka'esh chematho* — thus is the connection of the words: He poured out His fury, which is like fire; for we do not find a pouring of fire except in connection with fury, as it is written (Psalms 79), “Pour out Thy wrath upon the nations.”
Lamentations.translator_note: Printed “Psalms 79” is Psalms 79:6.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: And He hath multiplied in the daughter of Judah
Lamentations.english_translation: *Vayerev bevat Yehudah* — He multiplied in the assembly of Judah.
*Ta'aniyah va'aniyah* — sorrow and wailing.

*Vayerev* — pointed with a yod with a small kamatz, which is an expression of multiplying others; “*vayerev ha'am vaya'atzemu me'od*” is pointed with a chirik, which is an expression of himself multiplying; and so every word whose action ends in a heh, such as *panah*, *zakhah*, *bakhah*: this is its way of being used when the heh is dropped from it: when it speaks of itself, the pointing is chirik, like (Exodus 7) “and Pharaoh turned” (*vayifen*), and when it speaks of others, the pointing is kamatz, like (Judges 15) “and turned tail to tail” (*vayifen*), (II Kings 25) “So Judah was carried away captive” (*vayigel*), (ibid. 18) “and the king of Babylon carried Israel away to Assyria” (*vayigel*).
Lamentations.translator_note: Translated literally; the grammatical terms are rendered as printed. The words “and the people multiplied, and waxed very mighty” are Exodus 1:20 (no reference is printed). Printed “Exodus 7” is Exodus 7:23; “Judges 15” is Judges 15:4; “II Kings 25” is II Kings 25:21; “ibid. 18” is II Kings 18:11, where JPS has “the king of Assyria” (the printed text reads “Babylon”).

Lamentations.english_translation: *Vayachmos* — an expression of cutting off, and so (Job 15) “He shall shake off (*yachmos*) his unripe grape as the vine,” (Jeremiah 13) “thy heels suffer violence (*nechmesu*).”
Lamentations.translator_note: Printed “Job 15” is Job 15:33; “Jeremiah 13” is Jeremiah 13:22.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: as if it were a garden
Lamentations.english_translation: *Kagan* — as they trim the vegetables of the garden.
*Sukko* — His dwelling. *Sekho* is written, for He assuaged His wrath upon His sons by the destruction of His house; it is expounded in the Midrash of Lamentations.
*Shichet mo'ado* — the Holy of Holies, where He met with His sons, as it is said (Exodus 25), “And there I will meet with thee.”
Lamentations.translator_note: Printed “Exodus 25” is Exodus 25:22.

Lamentations.english_translation: *Melekh vekohen* — Zedekiah the king and Seraiah the High Priest.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: The Lord hath cast off His altar
Lamentations.english_translation: *Na'ar* — He annulled, and so (Psalms 89) “Thou hast abhorred (*ne'arta*) the covenant of Thy servant.”
Lamentations.translator_note: Printed “Psalms 89” is Psalms 89:40.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: As in the day of a solemn assembly
Lamentations.english_translation: *Keyom mo'ed* — for they were rejoicing and singing within it in a loud voice; so the enemies gave, in our destruction, a voice of joy.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: The LORD hath purposed to destroy
Lamentations.english_translation: *Chashav Hashem lehashchit* — for many days it had come up in His mind so, as it is said (Jeremiah 32), “for upon My anger and upon My fury was this city to Me, to remove it from before My face.”
Lamentations.translator_note: Printed “Jeremiah 32” is Jeremiah 32:31; Rashi’s wording differs from JPS (“For this city hath been to Me a provocation of Mine anger and of My fury …”).

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: He hath stretched out the line
Lamentations.english_translation: *Natah kav* — the line of judgment, to exact payment for our iniquities.
*Mibbalea* — from destroying.
*Chel vechomah* — *shura uvar shura*: a low wall opposite a high wall.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: Her gates are sunk into the ground
Lamentations.english_translation: *Tav'u va'aretz sh'areha* — a midrash of Aggadah: because they gave honour to the Ark, as it is said (Psalms 24), “Lift up your heads, O you gates,” therefore no creature ruled over them, and they sank into the ground; and our Rabbis said: they were the work of David’s hands, therefore the enemies did not rule over them.
Lamentations.translator_note: Printed “Psalms 24” is Psalms 24:7.

Lamentations.english_translation: *Ein torah* — there is none among them who gives teaching.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: They sit upon the ground, and keep silence
Lamentations.english_translation: *Yashevu la'aretz* etc. — as it is understood; and a midrash of Aggadah: Nebuchadnezzar seated them on the ground. When Zedekiah rebelled against him and transgressed his oath, he came and sat in Daphne of Antioch and sent for the Sanhedrin, and they came to meet him, and he saw them to be men of form, and seated them on golden chairs and said to them: Arrange for me your Torah, section by section, and translate it for me. When they reached the section of vows, he said to them: If he wishes to retract, can he retract? They said to him: Let him go to a sage and he will release him. He said to them: If so, you released Zedekiah from his oath. He commanded, and they were cast down and seated on the ground, and they tied the hair of their heads to the tails of horses and dragged them.
*Chamarmaru* — רגרז"לירט in Old French, the way of the bowels when a man throws them into the fire: they shrink and shrivel.
Lamentations.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Lamentations 2:11 (“mes entrailles sont brûlées”), in forms such as רגריזילינט and רגיזלרנט; the printed form (רגרז"לירט) is a variant spelling.

Lamentations.english_translation: *Be'ateif* — פשמ"יר.
Lamentations.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Lamentations 2:11 (“quand se pâme (l’enfant)”), in forms such as פשמייר and פשמיר; the printed form (פשמ"יר) is a variant spelling.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: What shall I take to witness for thee
Lamentations.english_translation: *Mah a'idekh umah adammeh lakh* — to say to thee: Why art thou astonished at thy breaking? Behold, also to such-and-such a nation there befell the like of thee.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: What shall I equal to thee, that I may comfort thee
Lamentations.english_translation: *Mah ashveh lakh ve'anachamekh* — when a distress comes upon a man, one says to him: Also upon so-and-so it came, thus; these are his consolations.
*Shav vetafel* — words in which there is no taste; and in Old French אפלשטרי"מנט.
Lamentations.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Lamentations 2:14 (“et fades”), in forms such as אפלשטרימינט and אשפלטירימנט; the printed form (אפלשטרי"מנט) is a variant spelling.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: And they have not uncovered thine iniquity
Lamentations.english_translation: *Velo galu al avonekh* — to rebuke thy way to thy face.

*Lehashiv shevutekh* — to straighten thy turning away (*meshuvotekh*), an expression of backsliding (*shovevah*), “backsliding children” (*shovevim*); (Isaiah 56) “and he went on frowardly (*vayelekh shovav*).”
Lamentations.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 56” is Isaiah 57:17.

Lamentations.english_translation: *Umaduchim* — they caused thee to be driven away from Me.
*Sharku* — blowing with the mouth: שיבלי"ר in Old French; and it is the way of a man to do so when he sees something important that has been destroyed and consumed.
Lamentations.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Lamentations 2:15 (“sifflant”), in forms such as שיבליר and שובליר; the printed form (שיבלי"ר) matches.

Lamentations.english_translation: *Kelilat yofi* — all the beauty was hers.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: have opened Their mouth wide against thee
Lamentations.english_translation: *Patzu alayikh pihem* — why was the *peh* put before the *ayin*? Because they were saying with their mouths what they had not seen with their eyes.
*Bitza imrato* — He completed His decree, like (Job 6) “that He would let loose His hand and cut me off (*yattar yado veyevatze'eni*).”
Lamentations.translator_note: Printed “Job 6” is Job 6:9.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: That He commanded in the days of old
Lamentations.english_translation: *Asher tzivvah mimei kedem* — for it is written in the Torah (Leviticus 26), “And I will add to chastise you seven.”
Lamentations.translator_note: Printed “Leviticus 26” is Leviticus 26:18 (JPS: “then I will chastise you seven times more for your sins”).

Lamentations.english_translation: *Pugat* — cessation: טרישאלמי"נט in Old French, like (Genesis 45) “and his heart fainted (*vayafag*).”
Lamentations.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Lamentations 2:18 (“ne te donne pas (de répit)”), in forms such as טרישאלמינט and טרישלימנט; the printed form (טרישאלמי"נט) matches. Printed “Genesis 45” is Genesis 45:26.

Lamentations.english_translation: *Bat einekh* — the black of the eye, which they call פרוני"לש in Old French.
Lamentations.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Lamentations 2:18 (“ta prunelle”), in forms such as פרוניילא and פרונילא; the printed form (פרוני"לש) is a variant spelling.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: At the beginning of the watches
Lamentations.english_translation: *Ashmurot* — two parts of the night, for the night is divided into three parts, as our Rabbis said in tractate Berakhot.
*Ha'atufim* — אשפומי"ן in Old French.
Lamentations.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Lamentations 2:19 (“pâmée”), in forms such as פשמיץ and פאמייץ; the printed form (אשפומי"ן) differs.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: The children that are dandled in the hands
Lamentations.english_translation: *Olelei tippuchim* — soft children who are still growing in the swaddling of their mothers; and our Rabbis expounded it of Doeg son of Joseph, whose mother used to measure him by handbreadths every day, to give gold to the Temple according to how he grew, and in the end she ate him.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: Shall the priest and the prophet be slain In the sanctuary of the Lord?
Lamentations.english_translation: *Im yehareg bemikdash Adonai kohen venavi* — the Holy Spirit answers them: And is it fitting for you that you killed Zechariah son of Jehoiada, as it is written in Chronicles, that he rebuked them when they came to bow down to Joash and made him an idolater [ע"א] (II Chronicles 24), “And the spirit clothed Zechariah the son of Jehoiada” — and he was a priest and a prophet — and they killed him in the court.
Lamentations.translator_note: Printed “II Chronicles 24” is II Chronicles 24:20. The abbreviation ע"א is read as “idolatry” from the context; the expansion is not confirmed by a permitted source, so the comment is flagged.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: Thou hast called, as in the day of a solemn assembly
Lamentations.english_translation: *Tikra keyom mo'ed* — like *karata*, and it is a present-tense form.
*Megurai* — my evil neighbours gathered against me to destroy.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: Those that I have dandled and brought up
Lamentations.english_translation: *Asher tippachti verabbiti oyevi khallam* — the children whom I dandled and raised, the enemy came and destroyed them.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: I am the man that hath seen affliction
Lamentations.english_translation: *Ani hagever ra'ah oni* — Jeremiah was lamenting, to say: I am the man who saw affliction, who saw more affliction than all the prophets who prophesied about the destruction of the Temple, for in their days the Temple was not destroyed, but in my days.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: By the rod of His wrath
Lamentations.english_translation: *Beshevet evrato* — of the One who rules and strikes: He is the Holy One, blessed be He.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: Surely against me He turneth His hand again and again
Lamentations.english_translation: *Akh bi yashuv* — I alone am constantly smitten, for all the returns of His blows are upon me.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: My flesh and my skin hath He worn out
Lamentations.english_translation: *Billah besari* — like (Isaiah 40) “the stock of a tree (*levul etz*)”; another explanation: *billah besari ve'ori* is like (Isaiah 51) “and the earth shall wax old like a garment (*tivlah*)”; that is, they lay on the ground in the streets, young and old; they had no pillow or cushion, and their flesh wore out as they were exiles.
Lamentations.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 40” is Isaiah 44:19 (JPS: “Shall I fall down to the stock of a tree?”); “Isaiah 51” is Isaiah 51:6.

Lamentations.english_translation: *Vayakef* — He surrounded me.

*Rosh vetela'ah* — like (Deuteronomy 29) “gall and wormwood (*rosh vela'anah*)”; and a midrash of Aggadah: *rosh* is Nebuchadnezzar, for the exile of Jehoiachin, and *tela'ah* is Nebuzaradan, who finished the blow in the days of Zedekiah, and wearied me.
Lamentations.translator_note: Printed “Deuteronomy 29” is Deuteronomy 29:17.

Lamentations.english_translation: *Gadar ba'adi* — He made a wall opposite me, that I be shut in.
*Velo etze* — He settled round about me camps and troops of ambushers.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: He hath made my chain heavy
Lamentations.english_translation: *Hikhbid nechoshti* — He made heavy brazen fetters for my feet so that I cannot walk: פיר"ייש in Old French.
Lamentations.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Lamentations 3:7 (“il m’a chargé de fers”), in forms such as פירייש and פיירגש; the printed form (פיר"ייש) matches.

Lamentations.english_translation: *Satam tefillati* — He stopped up the windows of the firmament before it.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: He hath made my paths crooked
Lamentations.english_translation: *Netivotai iwwah* — if I came to go out, I cannot go out by the paved roads, in a straight way, because of the enemies, and I go out by a roundabout way.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: He is unto me as a bear lying in wait
Lamentations.english_translation: *Dov orev hu li* — the Holy One, blessed be He, has been turned for me into a bear lying in wait.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: He hath turned aside my ways
Lamentations.english_translation: *Derakhai sorer* — an expression of thorns (*sirim*): *sorer* — He thorned them, scattering thorns in my paths.

*Vayfashchani* — an expression of spreading the legs, for one who goes on roads that are not cleared must widen his steps; and there is a parallel in the language of the Gemara: “this one who *pashach* a palm tree.”

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: As a mark for the arrow
Lamentations.english_translation: *Vayatzibeni kamatara* — He set me up opposite His arrows to shoot at me, as a *matara*: אשניי"לא in Old French.
Lamentations.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Lamentations 3:12 (“comme une cible”), in forms such as אשנייל and אשנאייל; the printed form (אשניי"לא) is a variant spelling.

Lamentations.english_translation: *Benei ashpato* — arrows that are put in a quiver, which they call קויכ"רא.
Lamentations.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Lamentations 3:13 (“son carquois”), in forms such as קוייברי and קרייברא; the printed form (קויכ"רא) is a variant spelling.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: He hath also broken my teeth
Lamentations.english_translation: *Vayagres* — and He broke; and its parallel is (Psalms 119) “My soul breaketh (*garesah*),” and so (Leviticus 2) “*geres* Carmel.”
Lamentations.translator_note: Printed “Psalms 119” is Psalms 119:20; “Leviticus 2” is Leviticus 2:14 (JPS: “even groats of the fresh ear”).

Lamentations.english_translation: *Bachatzatz* — fine stones that are in the dust; for the exiles used to knead their dough in pits that they dig in the ground, and the gravel entered it; when the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Ezekiel (Ezekiel 12), “Make for yourself a vessel of exile, to drink with and to knead in, a small trough,” so that they would learn and do likewise, as it is said (ibid. 24), “And Ezekiel shall be unto you a sign” — they were mocking him and did not do so; in the end their teeth were broken.
Lamentations.translator_note: Rashi’s wording of Ezekiel 12:3 differs from JPS (“prepare thee stuff for exile”). Printed “ibid. 24” is Ezekiel 24:24.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: He hath made me to wallow in ashes
Lamentations.english_translation: *Hikhpishani* — He covered me with ashes, like a vessel turned over on its mouth: ארנ"טיר in Old French; and there is a similar in the Mishnah (Yevamot 106), “the *pishon* of the camel is measured with a *kafusha* measure.”
Lamentations.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Lamentations 3:16 (“il m’a renversé”), in forms such as אדגטייר and ארנטיר; the printed form (ארנ"טיר) matches one of them. The Mishnaic phrase is left as printed.

Lamentations.english_translation: *Va'omar avad nitzchi* — I said in my heart, in the abundance of my troubles: my world and my hope have perished.
*Umerudi* — קומפלויי"נט in Old French.
Lamentations.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Lamentations 3:19 (“ma plainte”), in forms such as קומפליינט and קונפליינט; the printed form (קומפלויי"נט) is a variant spelling.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: My soul hath them still in remembrance
Lamentations.english_translation: *Zakhor tizkor* — my soul, my affliction and my anguish, and it is bowed down within me: so it is by its plain sense according to the order of Scripture’s matter. And ומ"א: *zakhor tizkor* — I know that in the end Thou wilt remember what was done to me, but my soul is bowed down within me to wait until the time of remembering; and from here the paytan composed, “This I know, that Thou art to remember, but my soul is bowed down within me until Thou rememberest.”
Lamentations.translator_note: The abbreviation ומ"א is left as printed. Translated literally; the paytan’s line is quoted as printed.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: This I recall to my mind
Lamentations.english_translation: *Zot ashiv el libbi* — after my heart said to me, “My hope from the LORD is lost,” I will return this to my heart and hope again; and what is this that I return to my heart?

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: Surely the LORD’S mercies are not consumed
Lamentations.english_translation: *Chasdei Hashem ki lo tamnu* — and the whole matter, up to “Wherefore doth a living man complain,” etc.

*Ki lo tamnu* — like *ki lo tamu*; and some explain *ki lo tamnu* like (Numbers 16) “shall we wholly perish (*tamnu*)?”: it is the LORD’s mercies that we are not consumed and did not perish in our iniquities.
Lamentations.translator_note: Printed “Numbers 16” is Numbers 17:28.

Lamentations.english_translation: *Chadashim labbekarim* — Thy mercies are renewed from day to day.
*Rabbah emunatekha* — great is Thy promise, and it is a great thing to believe in Thee, that Thou wilt fulfil and keep what Thou hast promised us.
*Chelki Hashem amrah nafshi* — the LORD is my allotted portion, and it is right that I hope in Him.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: It is good that a man should quietly wait
Lamentations.english_translation: *Tov veyachil vedumam* — the *vav* of *veyachil* is extra, like the *vav* of (Genesis 36) “*ve'ayah va'anah*”; it is good that a man should wait and be silent and look for the salvations of the LORD.
Lamentations.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 36” is Genesis 36:24.

Lamentations.english_translation: *Yeshev badad* — one who has met with mourning and distress should sit alone and look for good.
*Veyidom* — an expression of waiting, like (I Samuel 14) “If they say thus unto us: Tarry (*dumu*),” of Jonathan.
Lamentations.translator_note: Printed “I Samuel 14” is I Samuel 14:9.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: Because He hath laid it upon him
Lamentations.english_translation: *Ki natal alav* — for the Master of decrees has borne this decree upon him.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: For the Lord will not cast off
Lamentations.english_translation: *Ki lo yiznach le'olam Adonai* — therefore it is good to keep silent.
*Ki im hugah* — if a man brings grief upon himself because of his iniquity, afterward “yet will He have compassion according to the multitude of His mercies.”
*Hugah veyagah* — both are an expression of sorrow.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: For He doth not afflict willingly
Lamentations.english_translation: *Ki lo inah* — “nor grieve the children of men” from His heart and from His will, for the iniquity causes it.

*Ledakka tachat raglav* — it refers back to “for He doth not afflict willingly,” to be crushing under His feet, etc.; and “to turn aside the right of a man,” etc.; and “to subvert a man in his cause”: all these the Lord “approveth not” — it was not seen by Him, and it did not come up before Him in His thought to do so.
*Lo ra'ah* — it was not proper in His eyes that the Heavenly Court pervert a man in his cause, like “What sawest thou that thou hast done,” etc.
Lamentations.translator_note: The quotation is Genesis 20:10 (no reference is printed).

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: Who is he that saith, and it cometh to pass
Lamentations.english_translation: *Mi zeh amar vattehi* — etc.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: Out of the mouth of the Most High proceedeth not
Lamentations.english_translation: *Mipi elyon* etc. — and if I come to say: this evil did not come to me from His hand, it is a chance that happened to me — it is not so; rather, between evils and goods, “Who is he that saith, and it cometh to pass, when the Lord commandeth it not?” and from His mouth proceedeth neither evil nor good. But what has a living man to complain of? Let every man complain of his sins, for they are what bring the evil upon him. “Out of the mouth of the Most High proceedeth not” — Rabbi Yochanan said: From the day the Holy One, blessed be He, said (Deuteronomy 30), “See, I have set before thee this day life and good,” etc., neither evil nor good has proceeded from His mouth; rather the evil comes of itself to the doer of evil, and the good to the doer of good. Therefore why should he complain? Why should a man murmur, if not over his sins?
Lamentations.translator_note: Printed “Deuteronomy 30” is Deuteronomy 30:15.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: Let us lift up our heart with our hands
Lamentations.english_translation: *Nissa levavenu el kappayim* — when we lift our hands to the heavens, let us lift our hearts also with them, to return — to turn our hearts back before the Omnipresent, blessed be He. Another explanation: *el kappayim* — to the clouds, to the heavens, as you say (I Kings 19), “And behold, there ariseth a cloud as small as a man’s hand,” and so (Job 36), “upon the *kappim* He covered light.” And the midrash of our Rabbis: let us lift our hearts in truth to the Holy One, blessed be He, like a man who washes with the cleanness of his hands, who throws off from his hands every filth; for “whoso confesseth and forsaketh shall obtain mercy,” and he who confesses and does not forsake is like one who immerses with a creeping thing in his hand.
Lamentations.translator_note: Printed “I Kings 19” is I Kings 18:44; “Job 36” is Job 36:32 (JPS: “He covereth His hands with the lightning”; Rashi reads *kappim* as clouds). The words “whoso confesseth and forsaketh” are Proverbs 28:13 (no reference is printed).

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: We have transgressed and have rebelled
Lamentations.english_translation: *Nachnu fasha'nu umarinu* — this is our way through the evil inclination.
Lamentations.translator_note: A stray “[” is printed at the end of this comment.

Lamentations.english_translation: *Attah lo salachta* — and to Thee forgiveness was fitting, for such is Thy way.
*Sakkota va'af* — Thou didst partition off anger, to be a partition between Thee and us, and Thou didst pursue us with it.
*Sechi umaos* — it is *nia* in the language of the Mishnah: “his spittle and his *ni'o*,” which is drawn out from the lung and comes out through the throat.
Lamentations.translator_note: Translated literally; the Mishnaic phrase is left as printed.

Lamentations.english_translation: *Simenu* — it is a present-tense form.
*Pachad vafachat* — when we fled from the terror, we fell into the pit, a ditch.
*Hasha't* — an expression of *sha'iyah*, like *hasha'eit*.
Lamentations.translator_note: Translated literally; the printed explanation is circular.

Lamentations.english_translation: *Me'ein hafugot* — without alternation or interval.
*Eini olelah lenafshi mikkol benot iri* — Jeremiah was of a priestly family, and said: My eye, with tears, has disfigured and spoiled my face, over my soul, more than all the daughters of my city.
Lamentations.translator_note: Translated literally; the printed sentence is compressed.

Lamentations.english_translation: *Olelah* — an expression of disgrace, like (Job 16) “and have laid my horn in the dust” (*ve'olalti*).
Lamentations.translator_note: Printed “Job 16” is Job 16:15.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: Because of all the daughters of my city
Lamentations.english_translation: *Mikkol benot iri* — my family has more to weep over than all the families of the city, for it was chosen for holiness and for the service of the Holy One, blessed be He, out of all Israel.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: They have cut off my life in the dungeon
Lamentations.english_translation: *Tzamtu vabor chayyai* — in the prison house.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: They have cut off my life
Lamentations.english_translation: *Tzamtu* — they bound, like the *tzomet* of the sinews; (Song of Songs 4) “behind thy veil” (*letzamatekh*): אישריי"טור.
Lamentations.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Lamentations 3:53 (“ils ont enchaîné”), in forms such as אישטריידורא and אישטרייטורא; the printed form (אישריי"טור) is a variant spelling. Printed “Song of Songs 4” is Song of Songs 4:1.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: And have cast stones upon me
Lamentations.english_translation: *Vayyedu even bi* — over the mouth of the well; so they did to Daniel and Jeremiah; Jeremiah saw it by the Holy Spirit.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: They have cut off my life in the dungeon
Lamentations.english_translation: *Tzamtu vabor chayyai* — and although they cut off my life in the dungeon, so that I cannot go up out of it, they did not set their hearts even to this, until they cast a stone upon me.
*Tzafu mayim* etc. — for when a man enters water up to his loins there is still hope, but if the waters flow over his head, then he says: my hope is lost; but I do not do so; rather, “I called,” etc.
*Tzafu mayim* — the nations of the world.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: Thou drewest near in the day that I called upon Thee
Lamentations.english_translation: *Karavta beyom ekra'ekha* — thus wert Thou accustomed, in the former days, to draw near to me on the day of my calling.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: Thou hast pleaded the causes of my soul
Lamentations.english_translation: *Ravta Adonai rivei* — in the days that passed.
*Ra'itah Hashem avvatati* — in this trouble in which my enemies have wronged me.
*Shofetah mishpati* — as Thou didst already do.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: Thou wilt give them hardness of heart
Lamentations.english_translation: *Meginat lev* — breaking of heart, as you say (Hosea 11) “*amaggenekha* Israel,” (Genesis 14) “who hath delivered (*miggen*) thine enemies into thy hand.” Another explanation: *meginat lev* — a closing of the heart: distress and sighing that are like a shield (*magen*) against their heart; and one who explains it in the language of sorrow and grief errs, for no nun falls in it, since the nun in *yagon* is not a root letter, but is like the nun of *hamon* from the form *hamu goyim*, and like the nun of *kalon* from the form *niklah*, and like the nun of *Tziyyon* from the form *tziyyah*, and so the nun of *shiverron* from the form *sheber* (and like the nun of *shimmamon*, *shiga'on*; it seems to me that it should read וק"ל).
Lamentations.translator_note: Translated literally; the grammatical argument and the final parenthesis are as printed (the letters וק"ל are left unresolved). Printed “Hosea 11” is Hosea 11:8 (JPS: “How shall I surrender thee, Israel?”); “Genesis 14” is Genesis 14:20.

Lamentations.english_translation: *Ta'alatekha* — an expression of (Isaiah 19) “The princes of Zoan are become fools (*nou'alu*).”
Lamentations.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 19” is Isaiah 19:13.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: How is the gold become dim
Lamentations.english_translation: *Eichah yu'am zahav* — this lament was said over Josiah, as it is said in Chronicles (II 19), “Behold, it is written in the Book of Lamentations”; and with it he composed, within the lament, the rest of the sons of Zion.
Lamentations.translator_note: Printed “II 19” is II Chronicles 35:25 (JPS: “behold, they are written in the lamentations”).

Lamentations.english_translation: *Yu'am* — it grows dim, as you translate (Leviticus 13) “*kehah ammaya*.”
Lamentations.translator_note: Printed “Leviticus 13” is Leviticus 13:6 (JPS: “if the plague be dim”).

Lamentations.english_translation: *Zahav* — an appearance of the face that turns yellow like gold.
*Yishne* — it is changed from its appearance.
*Hakketem* — a collection of ornamental vessels of gold, which are for adornment, is called *ketem*.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: The hallowed stones are poured out
Lamentations.english_translation: *Avnei kodesh* — sons who shine like precious stones. And ומ"א: every quarter-log of blood that came out of Josiah from each and every arrow they stuck in him, Jeremiah buried in its place, and of it he reads, “the hallowed stones shall be poured out.”
Lamentations.translator_note: The abbreviation ומ"א is left as printed and not resolved here.

Lamentations.english_translation: *Hamsulla'im bapaz* — praised and valued as fine gold; one who sees them says: See the appearance of these, like the appearance of fine gold; and so (Job 25) “It cannot be valued with the gold of Ophir,” (ibid.) “neither shall it be valued with pure gold”; (Psalms 65) “Extol Him that rideth upon the skies” (*solu larokhev ba'aravot*): an expression of praise and valuation they are.
Lamentations.translator_note: Printed “Job 25” is Job 28:16 and 28:19; “Psalms 65” is Psalms 68:5.

Lamentations.english_translation: *Lenivlei charash* — earthen vessels in which wine is put, such as *nivlei yayin* (Jeremiah 28), “and break their bottles in pieces” (*unevaleihem yenapetzu*).
Lamentations.translator_note: Printed “Jeremiah 28” is Jeremiah 48:12.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: Even the jackals draw out the breast
Lamentations.english_translation: *Gam tannin* — although it is cruel, it draws out the breast: when it sees its son coming from afar, hungry, it draws its breasts out of its sheath — for it has a covering over its breasts — and takes them out of it, so that its son should not see it covered and turn back; and they suckled their whelps.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: The daughter of my people is become cruel
Lamentations.english_translation: *Bat ammi le'akhzar* — they see their children crying for bread and none breaks it for them, for their own lives take precedence over the lives of their children because of the hunger.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: They that were brought up in scarlet
Lamentations.english_translation: *Ha'emunim alei tola* — upon dyed garments.
*Ha'emunim* — an expression of (Esther 2) “And he brought up (*omen*) Hadassah.”
Lamentations.translator_note: Printed “Esther 2” is Esther 2:7.

Lamentations.english_translation: *Ashpatot* — dunghills of refuse; they lie on the dunghills outside.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: For the iniquity of the daughter of my people is greater
Lamentations.english_translation: *Vayigdal avon* etc. — their punishment proves about them that their iniquity is greater than that of Sodom.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: That was overthrown as in a moment
Lamentations.english_translation: *Hahafukhah kemo rega* — for Sodom’s trouble was not prolonged; in an instant it was overturned.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: And no hands fell upon her
Lamentations.english_translation: *Velo chalu vah yadayim* — the hands of the enemy, for it was overturned by angels; and there are midrashim of Aggadah, but it is not settled according to the order of the verses.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: Her princes were purer than snow
Lamentations.english_translation: *Zaku nezireha* — her princes, like *nezer* and crown; but I say *nezireha* literally: those who had grown their hair and were exceedingly beautiful; and it refers back to “the daughter of my people.”

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: They were more ruddy in body than rubies
Lamentations.english_translation: *Adhmu etzem mipeninim* — those whose appearance was redder than rubies, and their cut like sapphire; “their visage is blacker than coals.”
*Mishachor* — it is coal.
*Etzem* — an expression of appearance, like (Exodus 24) “and as the very heaven (*ke'etzem hashamayim*) for clearness”: קו"לר in Old French.
Lamentations.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Lamentations 4:8 (“couleur”), in forms such as קולור and קוליר; the printed form (קו"לר) is a variant spelling. Printed “Exodus 24” is Exodus 24:10.

Lamentations.english_translation: *Tzafad* — wrinkled and joined, and it has no parallel.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: For these pine away, stricken through
Lamentations.english_translation: *Shehem yazuvu medukkarim* etc. — those slain by hunger were swollen from the smell of the produce of the field, for the enemies were roasting meat on the grass outside the wall, and the smell entered the swollen ones of the hunger, and their bellies burst and their dung flowed, and this is a death of disgrace more than those slain by the sword.
*Medukkarim* — split open; whether by the swelling of hunger or by the splitting of a sword, it is called piercing.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: For want of the fruits of the field
Lamentations.english_translation: *Mitnuvot sadai* — from roots and herbs that they gather and eat; great is their dung and their loathsomeness.
*Levarot* — for food, like (II Samuel 12) “neither did he eat bread with them” (*velo barah otam lechem*), (ibid. 3) “to cause David to eat” (*lehavrot*).
Lamentations.translator_note: Printed “II Samuel 12” is II Samuel 12:17; “ibid. 3” is II Samuel 3:35.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: The LORD hath accomplished His fury
Lamentations.english_translation: *Kilah Hashem et chematho* — which had burned in Him for many years; now He has finished it, taking vengeance from them.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: It is because of the sins of her prophets
Lamentations.english_translation: *Mechatot nevi'eha* — of the false ones was this evil to her.
Lamentations.translator_note: Translated literally; the printed comment is compressed.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: They wander as blind men in the streets
Lamentations.english_translation: *Na'u ivrim bachutzot* — when the blind were walking in the marketplace, they were staggering and their feet slipped in the blood of the slain whom the wicked were killing in her midst.
*Nego'alu badam* — they were defiled with blood so that those near them could not touch their garments, and they called to them:
*Suru* — from us, you unclean ones, defiled with blood.
*Ki natzu* — an expression of stench and filth, as (Leviticus 1) “its crop with its feathers” (*moratho benotzatah*), which we translate *be'okhleha*; so Menachem composed it.
Lamentations.translator_note: Printed “Leviticus 1” is Leviticus 1:16.

Lamentations.english_translation: *Gam na'u* — they slipped in blood.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: The anger of the LORD hath divided them
Lamentations.english_translation: *Penei Hashem chilkam* — a face of wrath from the Holy One, blessed be He, divided them and scattered them among the nations, because they did not respect the persons of the priests when they were in their tranquillity.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: our eyes do yet fail For our vain help
Lamentations.english_translation: *Odenu tikhlenah einenu el ezratenu hevel* — when the evil came upon us, our eyes were still looking toward the army of Pharaoh, of whom it is said (Isaiah 30), “And Egypt is vain and empty — they will help,” for they promised us help and did not come, as it is said of them (Jeremiah 36), “Behold, the army of Pharaoh that is coming out for you to help shall return to its land, to Egypt.” We find in the Midrash of Lamentations that they were coming in ships; the Holy One, blessed be He, signalled to the sea and it floated before them inflated skins like human intestines, shaken in the water; they said to one another: These skins are our fathers, the men of Egypt, who drowned in the sea because of these Jews, and we are going out to their help; they stood and turned back.
Lamentations.translator_note: Rashi’s wording of Isaiah 30:7 and Jeremiah 37:7 differs from JPS (Isaiah 30:7: “For Egypt helpeth in vain, and to no purpose”; Jeremiah 37:7: “Behold, Pharaoh’s army, which is come forth to help you, shall return to Egypt into their own land”). Printed “Isaiah 30” is Isaiah 30:7; “Jeremiah 36” is Jeremiah 37:7.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: In our watching we have watched
Lamentations.english_translation: *Tzafinu* — we waited.

*Tzadu tze'adenu* — our enemies lay in ambush for our steps, from going in our streets, like (Exodus 21) “and he that lay not in wait” (*asher lo tzadah*), (I Samuel 24) “and thou layest wait for my soul” (*ve'attah tzoded et nafshi*).
Lamentations.translator_note: Printed “Exodus 21” is Exodus 21:13; “I Samuel 24” is I Samuel 24:12 (JPS: “though thou huntest my soul”).

Lamentations.english_translation: *Mashiach Hashem* — he is Josiah, as it is said (II Chronicles 31), “And Jeremiah lamented for Josiah.”
Lamentations.translator_note: Printed “II Chronicles 31” is II Chronicles 35:25.

Lamentations.english_translation: *Bishchitotam* — in the pits that they dug.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: Rejoice and be glad, O daughter of Edom
Lamentations.english_translation: *Sisi vesimchi bat Edom* — Jeremiah prophesied about the destruction of the Second Temple, that the Romans would destroy it.
*Sisi vesimchi* — for the moment; but your end is that the cup of punishment shall pass over you too, and you shall be drunken from it.
*Vetit'ari* — and thou shalt vomit, like (Genesis 24) “and she emptied (*vatte'ar*) her pitcher.”
Lamentations.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 24” is Genesis 24:20.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: The punishment of thine iniquity is accomplished, O daughter of Zion
Lamentations.english_translation: *Tam avonekh bat Tziyyon* — thou hast been smitten for all thy sins.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: He will no more carry thee away into captivity
Lamentations.english_translation: *Lo yosif lehaglotekh* — from the exile of Edom onward, never again.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: We have drunk our water for money
Lamentations.english_translation: *Meimenu bechesef shatinu* — for they were afraid to draw water from the river because of the enemies, and we bought it from them for money.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: To our very necks we are pursued
Lamentations.english_translation: *Al tzavvarenu nirdafnu* — with the yoke of hard labour.
*Yaga'nu* — to gather money and possessions.
*Velo hunach lanu* — our toil is in our hands, for the enemies collect and seize everything in taxes and poll-taxes and levies.
Lamentations.translator_note: The words rendered “poll-taxes and levies” (*gulgoliyot*, *arnoniyot*) are translated by sense from the printed words.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: We have given the hand to Egypt
Lamentations.english_translation: *Mitzrayim natanu yad* — the way of a man who falls and wants to stand is to stretch out a hand to the one near him to help him; so here too we stretched out a hand to Egypt, that they might help us.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: And to Assyria, to have bread enough
Lamentations.english_translation: *Ule'Ashur* — that they should satisfy us with their bread.

*Nattenu* — like *nattanu* (“we have given”); the dagesh in the nun takes the place of a second nun; and so (I Chronicles 29) “for all things come of Thee, and of Thine own have we given Thee” (*nattenu lakh*), and so (Genesis 34) “then will we give our daughters unto you.”
Lamentations.translator_note: Printed “I Chronicles 29” is I Chronicles 29:14 and printed “Genesis 34” is Genesis 34:16 (JPS: “then will we give our daughters unto you”).

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: We get our bread with the peril of our lives
Lamentations.english_translation: *Benafshenu navi lachmenu* — at the peril of our lives [we were in danger when we brought our sustenance from the field because of the sword of the wilderness.
Lamentations.translator_note: The printed text contains a stray “[” which is left as printed.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: Our skin is hot like an oven
Lamentations.english_translation: *Nikhmaru* — they became hot; and so (there, 43) “for his compassion yearned” (*nikhmeru*); and in the language of the Gemara there is much: on “the *komer* of grapes,” “*mekhamer bisra*.”
Lamentations.translator_note: Printed “there, 43” is Genesis 43:30 (JPS: “for his heart yearned toward his brother”). The Gemara phrase is Aramaic and is translated as printed; its meaning is not resolved here.

Lamentations.english_translation: *Zalafat ra'av* — like (Psalms 11) “and a wind of burnings” (*ruach zila'afot*); an expression of burning.
Lamentations.translator_note: Printed “Psalms 11” is Psalms 11:6 (JPS: “burning wind”).

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: The young men have borne the mill
Lamentations.english_translation: *Tachon nasu* — when the enemies led them in collars (*kolarin*), they would place mills and loads on their shoulders in order to weary them; and so “in the wood they stumbled” — their strength stumbled; and the language of stumbling (*kishalon*) is used for weakness of strength, as is said in Ezra (Nehemiah 2) “the strength of the bearer of burdens has stumbled,” and so (above 1) “He hath made my strength to stumble.”
Lamentations.translator_note: Printed “Ezra (Nehemiah 2)” is Nehemiah 4:4 (JPS: “The strength of the bearers of burdens is decayed”); “above 1” is Lamentations 1:14 (JPS: “He hath made my strength to fail”).

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: For this our heart is faint
Lamentations.english_translation: *Al zeh hayah daveh libbenu* etc. — on that which is explained in the verse after it: that Mount Zion is desolate, and foxes walk upon it.
Lamentations.translator_note: The following verse (5:18) reads in JPS: “For the mountain of Zion, which is desolate, The foxes walk upon it.”

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: Thou, O LORD, art enthroned for ever
Lamentations.english_translation: *Attah Adonai* — we know that You sit forever; and since it is so:
Lamentations.translator_note: The comment ends with a colon and no completion; translated as printed.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: Wherefore dost Thou forget us for ever
Lamentations.english_translation: *Lamah lanetzach tishkachenu* — Did You not swear to us by Yourself? As You exist, so Your oath exists.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: Thou canst not have utterly rejected us
Lamentations.english_translation: *Ki im ma'os ma'astanu* — because we sinned, You should not have increased wrath exceedingly, as You were wroth.

Lamentations.english_lemma_JPS: Turn us unto Thee, O Lord, and we shall be turned
Lamentations.english_translation: [*Hashivenu Adonai.* Because the book ends with words of reproof, it was necessary to repeat the verse before it a second time; and so Isaiah, the Twelve, and Ecclesiastes.]
Lamentations.translator_note: The source gives no separate lemma; the printed comment begins with the verse's words, and the lemma shown is the corresponding phrase of the verse. The source prints the whole comment inside brackets.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: The words of the Koheleth
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Divrei Koheleth* — everywhere that “words” (*divrei*) is said, it is nothing but words of reproof: (Deuteronomy 1) “These are the words which Moses spoke”; (there, 32) “But Jeshurun waxed fat”; (Amos 1) “The words of Amos”; (there, 4) “Hear this word, you kine of Bashan”; (Jeremiah 1) “The words of Jeremiah”; (there, 36) “Ask now, and see whether a man doth travail with child,” etc.; (II Samuel 22) “Now these are the last words of David”; (II Samuel 23) “But the ungodly, they are as thorns thrust away, all of them.” “The words of Koheleth.” “The sun also ariseth,” “All the rivers run into the sea” — he designated the wicked by the sun, the moon, and the sea, which have no gift of reward. So it is taught in Sifre, and I learned from there that the subject speaks of the wicked, and he likened them to the strength of the sun, whose end is to set. Tosefta (?): Another explanation: “All the rivers run into the sea” — why does Scripture say this? Of the worshippers of ע"א it is said: fools who bow to the water, thinking that there is substance in them, because they see the great sea, that all the rivers go into it and it is not full; and they do not know to understand that to the place whither the rivers go, thither they return to go; for the waters of the rivers that go into the sea are the very waters that went already; they well up from beneath the deep and go above the ground to the sea, and they return and well up again; therefore the rivers do not cease and the sea is not full — and not because there is substance in them. End.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The printed references are as follows: “Deuteronomy 32” is Deuteronomy 32:15 (JPS: “But Jeshurun waxed fat, and kicked”); “Amos 4” is Amos 4:1; “Jeremiah 36” is Jeremiah 30:6 (JPS: “Ask you now, and see whether a man doth travail with child”); “II Samuel 22” is II Samuel 23:1 (the “last words of David”), and “II Samuel 23” is 23:6. The abbreviation ע"א and the source marker תוספ' are left as printed and not resolved here; ד"א (“another explanation”) is rendered as such.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: the Koheleth
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Koheleth* — so called because he gathered (*kihel*) much wisdom; and so in another place he calls him (Proverbs 30) “Agur son of Jakeh,” because he gathered (*agar*) all the wisdom and brought it up (*hekiah*); and some say that he would speak all his words in assembly (*behakhel*).
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Proverbs 30” is Proverbs 30:1 (JPS: “The words of Agur the son of Jakeh”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: king in Jerusalem
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Melekh biYerushalayim* — the city of wisdom.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Vanity of vanities, saith Koheleth
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Hevel havalim amar Koheleth* — Koheleth lodges a protest and says of every creature of the seven days of creation [ד*] that everything is a vanity of vanities.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The printed text contains a stray “[ ד* ]”, which is left as printed.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Vanity of vanities
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Hevel* — the word *hevel* is pointed with a chataf-patach because it is joined (to the next word); that is, a vanity among vanities — seven vanities, corresponding to the work of the seven days of creation.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: What profit
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Mah yitron* — reward and surplus.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: under the sun
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Tachat hashamesh* — in exchange for (*temurat*) the Torah, which is called light, as it is said (Proverbs 6) “and the teaching is light”: every labor in which he exchanges the study of Torah — what reward is there in it?
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Proverbs 6” is Proverbs 6:23 (JPS: “and the teaching is light”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: One generation passeth away, and another generation cometh
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Dor holekh vedor ba* — all that the wicked man toils and labors to oppress and to rob does not wear out his deeds, for one generation goes and another generation comes and takes everything from the hand of his sons, as is said (Job 20) “His sons shall seek the favor of the poor.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Job 20” is Job 20:10 (JPS: “His children shall appease the poor”). The words “does not wear out his deeds” are translated literally and the sense is not resolved here.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: the earth abideth for ever
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Veha'aretz le'olam omedet* — and who are the ones who endure? The humble, the lowly, who bring themselves down to the ground, as is said (Psalms 37) “But the humble shall inherit the land”; and Midrash Tanchuma says: all the righteous of Israel are called “land,” as it is said (Malachi 3) “And you shall be to Me a delightsome land.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Psalms 37” is Psalms 37:11 (JPS: “But the humble shall inherit the land”); “Malachi 3” is Malachi 3:12 (JPS: “For you shall be a delightsome land”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: The sun also ariseth
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vezarach hashemesh* etc., *dor holekh vedor ba* — as the sun rises in the morning and sets in the evening, and goes all night longing to return to the place where it rose yesterday, in order to rise from there today also.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The printed lemma also repeats the words “One generation passeth away, and another generation cometh” (verse 4), which do not occur in this verse.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: The wind
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Haruach* — the wind of the sun is *talent* in Old French; like (Ezekiel 1) “whither the spirit was to go.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Ecclesiastes 1:6 (“selon sa volonté”), in forms such as טלנט; the printed form (טלנ"ט) matches. Printed “Ezekiel 1” is Ezekiel 1:12 (JPS: “whither the spirit was to go”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: the wind returneth again to its circuits
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ve'al svivotav shav* — tomorrow also, every circuit and revolution that it circled yesterday, it circles and revolves today.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: The wind goeth toward the south
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Holekh el darom* — always by day.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: turneth about unto the north
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vesovev el tzafon* — always by night.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: It turneth about continually in its circuit
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Sovev sovev holekh* — toward the east and west, for sometimes its going is by day and sometimes its circling is by night; in Tammuz it goes and in Tevet it circles. So also the wicked: all that their sun shines, their end is to set; all that they go and grow strong, their end is to return to the place of their stench; from the place of filth they came and to the place of filth they shall go. And so “all the rivers go to the sea, and the sea is not full,” because they do not remain in it; for the Ocean sea is higher than the whole world, as it is said (Amos 8) “That calleth for the waters of the sea, and poureth them out,” etc.; and from where does a man pour? From above to below; and the rivers go through tunnels under the mountains from the Ocean and return and well up, and this is “to the place whither the rivers go, thither they return.” So the wicked man: exactly as he came, so shall he go.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Amos 8” is Amos 5:8 or 9:6 (JPS: “That calleth for the waters of the sea, And poureth them out upon the face of the earth”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: All things toil to weariness
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Kol hadevarim yegei'im* etc.: *lo tisba ayin velo timmale ozen* — it refers back to “What profit”: if he exchanges the study of Torah for speaking vain words, they are wearying and he cannot attain all of them; and if he comes to occupy himself with sights of the eye, his eye is not satisfied, and if with the hearing of the ear, his ear is not filled.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: That which hath been is that which shall be
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Mah shehayah hu sheyihyeh* etc. — in all that he learns in a matter that is the exchange of the sun, there is no novelty; he will see nothing but what already was, what was created in the six days of creation; but one who meditates in the Torah always finds in it new reasons, as is said (Proverbs 5) “Let her breasts satisfy thee at all times”: as with this breast, whenever the infant fondles it, he finds taste in it. And so it is found in tractate Chagigah that Rabbi Eliezer ben Hyrcanus said things that no ear had heard, concerning the Work of the Chariot.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Proverbs 5” is Proverbs 5:19 (JPS: “Let her breasts satisfy thee at all times”). “The exchange of the sun” is translated literally.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Is there a thing whereof it is said
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Yesh davar* — that comes to your hand under the sun, of which the speaker says to you: “See, this is new” — it is not new, for it already was in the ages that passed before us; only there is no remembrance of the former things, therefore it seems to be new. And also of the latter ones, who will be after us, there will be no remembrance among the generations that will come last of them. And Midrash Aggadah expounds it concerning the destruction of the memory of Amalek and the end of the memory of Edom, to be blotted out, as it is said (Obadiah 1) “and there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Obadiah 1” is Obadiah 1:18 (JPS: “And there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: I Koheleth have been king over Israel in Jerusalem
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ani Koheleth hayiti melekh* — over the whole world, and at the end over Israel, and at the end over Jerusalem alone, and at the end over my staff (*makli*), for it is said “I was king in Jerusalem,” but now he is not king.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: And I applied my heart to seek
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Venatati et libbi lidrosh* — in the Torah, which is wisdom, and to contemplate it concerning all the evil conduct mentioned above that is done under the sun; and I understood in it that it is the evil matter which the Holy One, blessed is He, gave before the sons of man: (Deuteronomy 30) “the life and the death, the good and the evil.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Deuteronomy 30” is Deuteronomy 30:15 (JPS: “life and good, and death and evil”); the printed wording differs from the verse.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: sore task
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Inyan ra* — an evil custom of theirs.
