Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: to be exercised therewith
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *La'anot bo* — to conduct oneself in it. The word *inyan* may be interpreted as an expression of *ma'on* (dwelling and abode), and it may be interpreted as an expression of reflection (*iyyun*) and thought, and so *la'anot bo*.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: hath given
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Natan* — He laid it before them.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: a striving after wind
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ure'ut ruach* — a breaking of spirit, like (Isaiah 8) “*ro'u* (be broken), O peoples, and be dismayed.” *Ruach* is *talent* in Old French [printed טל"נש]; the end of the deed comes to heartache.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Ecclesiastes 1:14 (“esprit”), in forms such as טלנט; the printed form (טל"נש) is a variant spelling. Printed “Isaiah 8” is Isaiah 8:9 (JPS: “Make an uproar, O you peoples, and you shall be broken in pieces”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: That which is crooked
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Me'uvvat* — in his lifetime he cannot be repaired; after he dies, he who toiled on the eve of the Sabbath shall eat on the Sabbath. And our Rabbis explained it of one who has relations with a forbidden woman and begets a *mamzer*, or of a Torah scholar who departs from the Torah, who was straight at the beginning and became crooked.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Translated literally; the punctuation of the printed sentence “in his lifetime he cannot be repaired; after he dies, he who toiled…” is as printed.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: that which is wanting cannot be numbered
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vechesron lo yukhal lehimanot* — this one who diminished himself from the number of the upright cannot be counted with them in receiving their reward.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: I spoke with my own heart
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Dibbarti ani im libbi* — now that I have come down from my greatness, I set my heart to say: Who would say of me that I would come to this measure? I, behold, I have grown great, etc.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The verse in JPS reads: “Lo, I have gotten great wisdom.”

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: And I applied
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Va'ettenah* — now, my heart, to know the goodness of wisdom, what its end is, and the goodness of foolish revelry and folly; and *holelot* is confusion and derangement of mind, an expression of mixing, like (Isaiah 1) “mixed (*mahul*) with water”; and *sikhlut* is stupidity.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The lemma *va'ettenah* (“and I applied”) runs on into the comment as printed (“now my heart”). Printed “Isaiah 1” is Isaiah 1:22 (JPS: “Thy wine mixed with water”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: I perceived
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Yadati* — now that wisdom too has in it a breaking of spirit; for with much wisdom a man relies on his abundant wisdom and does not keep far from the forbidden, and great anger comes to the Holy One, blessed is He. I said: “I will multiply horses, and I will not return the people to Egypt,” and in the end I returned them; I said: “I will multiply wives, and my heart will not turn away,” and behold, it is written of me (I Kings 11) “his wives turned away his heart.” And so he says that he relied upon his great wisdom and did several things, as it is said (Proverbs 30) “The saying of the man to Ithiel, to Ithiel and Ucal.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “I Kings 11” is I Kings 11:3 (JPS: “and his wives turned away his heart”); “Proverbs 30” is Proverbs 30:1 (JPS: “The man saith unto Ithiel, unto Ithiel and Ucal”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: I said in my heart
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Amarti ani belibbi* — since it is so, I will cease from wisdom and occupy myself with feasting continually.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: I will try thee with mirth
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Asakhah* — an expression of *mesakh yayin* (mixing wine) for drinking, like (Proverbs 9) “she hath mingled her wine” (*mas'khah yeinah*): the mixing of wine with water to improve it, or the mixing of spices into wine, for *konditon*.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Proverbs 9” is Proverbs 9:2 (JPS: “she hath mingled her wine”). The term *konditon* is left as printed.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: and enjoy pleasure
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ure'eh betov* — like *ure'ot betov*.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: this also was vanity
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vehineh gam hu hevel* — for I saw in prophecy that many ruins come out of laughter: Belshazzar died in the midst of a feast; the people of the generation of the Flood were swept away in the midst of the abundance of good that You bestowed upon them.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: I said of laughter
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Lisechok amarti mehollal* — it is mixed with weeping and sighing.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: What doth it accomplish?
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ulesimchah mah zo* — does it do good? Behold, its end is sorrow.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: I searched in my heart
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Tarti belibbi* — I turned again to search in my heart, to hold fast to all of them: feasting, wisdom, and folly; and to draw out and pamper my flesh with the feast of wine. Every banquet of pleasure is called by the name of wine.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: my heart conducting itself with wisdom
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Velibbi noheg bechokhmah* — even if my flesh is drawn after wine, my heart rolls along in wisdom, to hold fast to the Torah.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: to lay hold on folly
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ulechoz besiklut* — in things that seem to me like folly, of which I said (Proverbs 31) “Ithiel and Ucal,” such as wearing *sha'atnez* and the mixed seed of the vineyard, about which Satan raises objections and the nations of the world raise objections; and so he says (below 7) “It is good that thou shouldest take hold of this”; and also concerning Saul, to whom it seemed folly in his eyes to kill from man to woman, from child to suckling, though it was the commandment of the Omnipresent, and he calls it folly.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Proverbs 31” is Proverbs 30:1; printed “below 7” is Ecclesiastes 7:18 (JPS: “It is good that thou shouldest take hold of the one”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: I made me great works
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Higdalti ma'asai* — in the days of my greatness.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: trees in them of all kinds of fruit
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Etz kol peri* — for Solomon, in his wisdom, knew the veins (*gidei*) of the earth: which vein goes to Cush, and he planted peppers in it; which goes to the land of Charuvi, and he planted carobs (*charuvin*) in it; for all the veins of the lands come to Zion, from where the foundation of the world is, as it is said (Psalms 50) “Out of Zion, the perfection of beauty”; therefore it says “trees of every fruit.” In Midrash Tanchuma.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Psalms 50” is Psalms 50:2 (JPS: “Out of Zion, the perfection of beauty”). The place name “Charuvi” is left as printed.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: pools of water
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Berekhot mayim* — like fishponds for fish, which are dug in the ground.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: treasure such as kings
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Usegullat melakhim* — the treasures of kings: gold, silver, and precious stone, which kings treasure in their treasuries.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: and the provinces
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vehamedinot* — the treasure of all merchants.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: men-singers and women-singers
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Sharim vesharot* — kinds of musical instruments.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: women very many
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Shiddah veshiddot* — ornamental chariots, covered wagons (*egloth tzav*), and in the language of the Gemara there is: *shiddah, teivah, umigdal*.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The Gemara terms are left as printed (שדה תיבה ומגדל).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: also my wisdom stood me in stead
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Af chokhmati* — my wisdom too I did not abandon because of all these works, and it stood by me and I did not forget it; another explanation: it stood by me as help from all these.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: I kept not from them
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Lo atzalti* — I did not distance myself so as to be separated from them; and so (Numbers 11) “and He took of the spirit and put it upon the elders,” like a lamp from which many lights are kindled and its light is not diminished at all.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Numbers 11” is Numbers 11:25 (JPS: “and took of the spirit that was upon him, and put it upon the seventy elders”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: this was my portion from all my labour
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vezeh hayah chelki* — and after I did all these, I have from all of them only this. Rav and Shmuel: one said his staff (*maklo*) and one said his *kido* — from the *kidah* of an earthenware vessel from which they drink. And some explain from Midrash Aggadah that the whole matter concerns the houses of study and students and the synagogues.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The words *maklo* / *kido* / *kidah* are left as printed and not resolved here.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: for my heart had joy of all my labour
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ya'ar tzomeach etzim* — ignorant people, for the work of fields and vineyards.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The source lemma belongs to another verse (Ecclesiastes 2:6) and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Then I looked on
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ufaniti* — now at all my deeds, and I see that there is no profit in them, for I am lacking from all of them.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Translated literally; the construction is elliptical.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: And I turned myself to behold wisdom
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ufaniti ani lir'ot chokhmah* — I turn away from all my occupations to contemplate the Torah; and *holelut* and *sikhlut* are the punishment of transgressions.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: for what can the man do that cometh after the king?
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki mah ha'adam sheyavo acharei hamelekh* — to plead with him about a decree that he decreed upon him, when they have already made him for the act of the decree, to the one who decreed it; it is good for him to contemplate his deeds first, and he will not need to beg.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Translated literally; the clause “they have already made him for the act of the decree, to the one who decreed it” is as printed and its sense is not resolved here.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: folly
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Min hasiklut* — that is the wicked man.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: The wise man, his eyes are in his head
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Hechakham einav berosho* — at the beginning of a matter he considers what will be at its end. “And I also perceived (*vayadati gam ani*)” — also I (knew) that although he praises the wise man over the fool, I know (I) that both of them will die.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Then said I in my heart
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ve'amarti ani belibbi* etc. — that is: since both die, perhaps I shall now ponder in my heart: as the fate of the wicked man, to me also it will befall; and why should I be more righteous then? “And I spoke in my heart” that if I ponder thus, it is vanity; for the remembrance of the wise man and of the fool is not alike after their death — they will not be remembered together, since this one's memory is for good and that one's memory is for evil.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: in the days to come all will long ago have been forgotten
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Beshekvar hayamim haba'im hakol nishkach* — because I see the wicked who already were and prospered greatly, and in the days after them all their might and prosperity were forgotten.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: And how must the wise man die even as the fool!
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ve'eikh yamut hachakham im hakesil* — I see the righteous prospering in their death and benefiting their sons, as (Leviticus 27) “and I will remember My covenant with Jacob,” etc., (Jeremiah 2) “I remember for thee the affection of thy youth.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Leviticus 27” is Leviticus 26:42 (JPS: “then will I remember My covenant with Jacob”); “Jeremiah 2” is Jeremiah 2:2 (JPS: “I remember for thee the affection of thy youth”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: So I hated life
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Veshanati et hachayyim* — for he was prophesying about the generation of Rehoboam, who were wicked.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: This also is vanity
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Gam zeh hevel* — this too is one of the vanities that were created in the world: that the wise man toils and the fool inherits him.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: I turned about to cause my heart to despair
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vesavoti ani leya'esh* — not to weary himself and toil.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: For there is a man
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki yesh adam* — according to its plain meaning; and Midrash Aggadah in Tanchuma designates it as concerning the Holy One, blessed is He, of whom it is said (Ezekiel 1) “and upon the likeness of the throne was a likeness as the appearance of a man.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Ezekiel 1” is Ezekiel 1:26 (JPS: “and upon the likeness of the throne was a likeness as the appearance of a man upon it above”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: whose labour is with wisdom
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *She'amalo bechokhmah* — as it is said (Proverbs 3) “The Lord by wisdom founded the earth; by His knowledge the depths were broken up”; and to creatures who did not labor in it He gave a portion in it.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Proverbs 3” is Proverbs 3:19–20 (JPS: “The LORD by wisdom founded the earth… By His knowledge the depths were broken up”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: This also is vanity and a great evil
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Gam zeh hevel verah rabbah* — and they became a generation of vanity, and the wickedness of man in the earth was great in the generation of the Flood.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: For what hath a man of all his labour
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki mah hovveh* etc. — for what surplus is there to a man from all his labor and the breaking of his heart, in toil and worry, for he toils and leaves it to others.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: his occupation
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Inyano* — his conduct. This too is one of the vanities that prevail in the world.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: There is nothing better for a man than that he should eat and drink
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ein tov ba'adam* — in astonishment, that he should eat and drink and show his soul good — that is, he should set his heart to do justice and righteousness along with the eating and the drinking; and so it was said to Jehoiakim (Jeremiah 22) “Did not thy father eat and drink, and do justice and righteousness? Then it was well with him.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Jeremiah 22” is Jeremiah 22:15 (JPS: “Did not thy father eat and drink, and do justice and righteousness? Then it was well with him”). “In astonishment” is translated literally.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: For who will eat
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki mi yokhal* etc. — why should I not rejoice in my portion, in food and drink? Who is fit to eat my toil, and who will hasten to swallow it, besides me?

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: if not I
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Chutz mimmenni* — *mibal'adai* (besides me). This is the way of the wicked, who gather for the needs of others.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: For to the man that is good in His sight
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki le'adam shetov lefanav* — before the God mentioned above, for it is from the hand of God.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: He giveth wisdom, and knowledge, and joy
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Natan chokhmah veda'at vesimchah* — a heart to occupy oneself with the Torah and the commandments, and to rejoice in one's portion in food and drink and clean clothing.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: but to the sinner He giveth the task
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Velachote natan inyan* — a custom of worry, to gather and to amass, and to give to the one who is good before God, as is said (Esther 8) “And Esther set Mordecai over the house of Haman.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Esther 8” is Esther 8:2 (JPS: “And Esther set Mordecai over the house of Haman”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: This also is vanity and a striving after wind
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Gam zeh* — one of the vanities that were given to creatures: that they toil and another takes.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: To every thing there is a season
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Lakol zeman* — let not the one who gathers in wealth of vanity rejoice; for if now it is in his hands, the righteous will yet inherit it; only the time has not yet arrived, for every matter has an appointed time when it will be.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: a time to every purpose
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Lekhol chefetz* — for every matter; all matters are called *chafatzim* in the language of the Mishnah.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: A time to be born
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Et laledet* — at nine months.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: a time to die
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ve'et lamut* — the fixed measure of the years of each and every generation.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: A time to plant
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Et lata'at* — a nation and a kingdom.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: a time to pluck up that which is planted
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ve'et la'akor* — a time when it shall come to be uprooted.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: A time to kill
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Et laharog* — a whole nation, when the day of its reckoning arrives, as is said (Isaiah 67) “and thy remnant shall be slain by the sword.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 67” does not exist (the book has 66 chapters); the reference and the quoted words could not be identified and are translated as printed.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: a time to heal
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ve'et lirpo* — their fracture, as is said of Egypt (there, 19) “and they shall return to the Lord, and He shall be entreated of them, and heal them.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “there, 19” is Isaiah 19:22 (JPS: “they shall return unto the LORD, and He will be entreated of them, and will heal them”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: A time to break down
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Et lifrotz* — the wall of the city when it is decreed upon it, as it is said (Nehemiah 1) “and the walls of Jerusalem are breached.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Nehemiah 1” is Nehemiah 1:3 (JPS: “the wall of Jerusalem also is broken down”); the printed wording differs from the verse.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: a time to build up
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ve'et livnot* — as it is said (Amos 9) “and I will build it as in the days of old.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Amos 9” is Amos 9:11 (JPS: “And I will build it as in the days of old”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: A time to weep
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Et livkot* — on the Ninth of Av.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: a time to laugh
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ve'et lischok* — in the future to come, as it is said (Psalms 127) “Then shall our mouth be filled with laughter.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Psalms 127” is Psalms 126:2 (JPS: “Then was our mouth filled with laughter”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: A time to mourn
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Et sefod* — in the days of mourning.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: a time to dance
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ve'et rekod* — among bridegrooms and brides.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: A time to cast away stones
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Et lehashlikh avanim* — the young men of Israel are cast out: (Lamentations 4) “the hallowed stones are poured out.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Lamentations 4” is Lamentations 4:1 (JPS: “The hallowed stones are poured out”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: a time to gather stones together
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ve'et kenos* — them from the exile: (Zechariah 9) “And the Lord God shall save them in that day as the flock of His people, as the stones of a crown glittering over His land.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Zechariah 9” is Zechariah 9:16 (JPS: “And the LORD their God shall save them in that day As the flock of His people; For they shall be as the stones of a crown, Glittering over His land”); the printed wording differs from the verse.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: A time to embrace
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Et lachavok* — (Jeremiah 13) “for as the girdle cleaves,” etc.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Jeremiah 13” is Jeremiah 13:11 (JPS: “For as the girdle cleaveth to the loins of a man”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: a time to refrain from embracing
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ve'et lirchok mechabbek* — (Isaiah 6) “and the Lord removed man far away.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 6” is Isaiah 6:12 (JPS: “And the LORD have removed men far away”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: A time to seek
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Et levakesh* — as it is said (Ezekiel 34) “and the lost ones I will seek,” concerning the dispersed of Israel.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Ezekiel 34” is Ezekiel 34:16 (JPS: “I will seek that which was lost”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: a time to lose
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ve'et le'abbed* — and a time when He loses them in the exile, as it is said (Leviticus 27) “and you shall perish among the nations.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Leviticus 27” is Leviticus 26:38 (JPS: “And you shall perish among the nations”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: A time to keep
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Et lishmor* — (Numbers 6) “The Lord bless thee and keep thee,” when you do His will.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Numbers 6” is Numbers 6:24 (JPS: “The LORD bless thee, and keep thee”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: a time to cast away
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ve'et lehashlikh* — (Deuteronomy 29) “and He cast them into another land.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Deuteronomy 29” is Deuteronomy 29:27 (JPS: “and cast them into another land”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: A time to rend
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Et likroa* — the kingdom of the house of David (I Kings 10:14 [as printed]): “and I rent the kingdom,” etc.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The printed reference “I Kings 10:14” appears to be I Kings 14:8 (JPS: “and rent the kingdom away from the house of David”); the printed wording is translated as printed.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: a time to sew
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ve'et litpor* — (Ezekiel 30:36 [as printed]) “and they shall be one in thy hand, and they shall be no more divided into two kingdoms.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The printed reference “Ezekiel 30:36” appears to be Ezekiel 37:17 (JPS: “that they may become one in thy hand”) and 37:22 (JPS: “they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more”); the printed wording is translated as printed.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: A time to keep silence
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Et lachashot* — sometimes a man is silent and receives reward, as it is said (Leviticus 10) “And Aaron held his peace,” and he merited that the speech was singled out for him, as it is said (there, 10) “And the Lord spoke to Aaron: Drink no wine nor strong drink.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Leviticus 10” is Leviticus 10:3 (JPS: “And Aaron held his peace”); “there, 10” is Leviticus 10:8–9 (JPS: “And the LORD spoke unto Aaron… Drink no wine nor strong drink”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: a time to speak
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ve'et ledabber* — (Exodus 15) “Then Moses sang,” (Judges 4) “And Deborah sang,” (Hosea 14) “Take with you words.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Judges 4” is Judges 5:1 (JPS: “Then sang Deborah and Barak the son of Abinoam”); “Exodus 15” is Exodus 15:1 and “Hosea 14” is Hosea 14:3 (JPS: “Take with you words”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: A time to love
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Et le'ehov* — “and He will love you.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The printed comment consists of these words alone; no reference is printed.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: a time to hate
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ve'et lisno* — as it is said (there, 9) “All their wickedness is in Gilgal, therefore I hated them.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “there, 9” is Hosea 9:15 (JPS: “All their wickedness is in Gilgal, For there I hated them”); the printed wording differs from the verse.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: What profit hath he that worketh
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Mah yitron ha'oseh* — what advantage has the one who does evil in all that he toils? He too — his time will come, and everything is lost.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: the task
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ha'inyan* — the custom.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: to be exercised therewith
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *La'anot* — to conduct oneself.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: beautiful in its time
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Yafeh be'ito* — in the good time, it is fitting that the payment of reward for the good deed come; and in the evil time, it is fitting for the payment for the evil deed.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: also He hath set the world in their heart
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Gam et ha'olam natan belibbam* etc. — also the wisdom of the world that He placed in the heart of creatures: He did not place all of it in the heart of each and every one, but this one a part and that one a part, so that man shall not find all the work of the Holy One, blessed is He, to know it, and shall not know the time of his reckoning or in what he will stumble, in order that he set his heart to repent, that he worry and say: today or tomorrow I shall die. Therefore *ha'elem* is written here defective, an expression of concealment (*he'elamah*); for if a man knew that the day of his death was near, he would not build a house nor plant a vineyard. Therefore he says that He made everything beautiful in its time: that there is a time for death is a good thing, for man relies, saying: perhaps the time of my death is still far off, and he builds a house and plants a vineyard — and this is beautiful, that it is hidden from creatures.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The word *ha'olam* (“the world”) is read in the comment as *ha'elem* (“concealment”), written without the vav, as the printed comment states.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: I know that there is nothing better for them
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Yadati* — now, since the time of reckoning is hidden, for there is nothing good among creatures except to rejoice in one's portion, to do what is good in the eyes of his Creator while he is alive.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: enjoy pleasure
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ure'eh tov* — Torah and commandments.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: I know that, whatsoever God doeth, it shall be for ever
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Yadati ki kol asher asah* — the Holy One, blessed is He, in the work of creation: it is fit to be forever, and it is not to be changed, neither by addition nor by subtraction; and when it was changed, God commanded and made it so that it be changed, in order that they fear before Him: the Ocean broke its boundary in the generation of Enosh and flooded a third of the world, and God made it so that they fear before Him; for seven days the course of the sun was changed in the generation of the Flood, to shine in the west and to set in the east, in order that they fear before Him; the sun returned backward ten degrees in the days of Hezekiah; and in the days of Ahaz his father the day was shortened and the night lengthened on the day of his death, so that he not be eulogized — all this in order that they fear before Him. Therefore there is nothing good for a man except to occupy himself with His commandments and to fear before Him.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The ten degrees correspond to the shadow of the dial of Ahaz (II Kings 20:11, JPS: “he brought the shadow ten degrees backward, by which it had gone down on the dial of Ahaz”); no reference is printed.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: That which is hath been long ago
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Mah shehayah kvar hu* — what was before us is already done, and we saw it or heard it from others who saw it, and we have to testify about it, that we saw that the Holy One, blessed is He, seeks the pursued: Jacob pursued, Esau the pursuer — (Malachi 1) “And I loved Jacob, and Esau I hated”; the Egyptians pursuing Israel — the Egyptians sank in the sea, and Israel went with a high hand.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Malachi 1” is Malachi 1:2–3 (JPS: “Yet I loved Jacob; But Esau I hated”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: that which is to be hath already been
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Va'asher* — what is to be at the end is like what already was: as at the first, so at the last; the Holy One, blessed is He, does not change His ways in the world.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: God seeketh that which is pursued
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Veha'Elohim yevakkesh et nirdaf* — to exact payment from the pursuer; therefore, what is the advantage of the one who does evil in that he toils? Behold, his end is to be repaid.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: in the place of justice
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Makom hamishpat* etc. — I saw by the Holy Spirit the place of the Chamber of Hewn Stone in Jerusalem, which was (Isaiah 1) “full of justice”; there they would judge *rasha*, as it is said (Micah 3) “Her heads judge for reward,” and I saw their punishment.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 1” is Isaiah 1:21 (JPS: “She that was full of justice”) and “Micah 3” is Micah 3:11 (JPS: “The heads thereof judge for reward”). The word *rasha* may mean “wickedness” or “a wicked man”; it is left untranslated.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: in the place of righteousness
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Makom hatzedek* — the Middle Gate, which was the place where the laws were determined; there the wicked sat: Sarsechim, Rab-saris, Nergal-sharezer, Rab-mag, and Nebuchadnezzar and his armies, judging Israel with harsh punishments and judgments of death.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The names correspond to Jeremiah 39:3 (JPS: “sat in the middle gate, even Nergal-sarezer, Samgar-nebo, Sarsechim Rab-saris, Nergal-sarezer Rab-mag”); no reference is printed.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: wickedness was there
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Sham harasha* — its accent is above, to say that it is a noun like *harasha* (and it should have been pointed with a segol under the resh), but because it is the end of a verse it is changed to be pointed with a great kamatz; and although in every place we have not found it any more that it changes at an etnachta and at the end of a verse.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Translated literally; the last clause is difficult as printed and its sense is not resolved here.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: I said in my heart
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Amarti ani belibbi* etc. — therefore I say: the Holy One, blessed is He, judges everything after a time; and although the matter is delayed, its end is to come to its hour, for there is a time for every purpose, even for punishment, and for the reckoning of judgment there is a time when it shall come.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: for every work
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ve'al kol hama'aseh* — that a man did, there they will judge him when the time of reckoning comes; there, at that time, a time is given for every deed to be judged. אבי חוטרי מילי ואבי דרי חושבנא.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The final Aramaic phrase is left as printed and not resolved here.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: I said in my heart
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Amarti ani belibbi* — when I saw this.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: It is because of the sons of men
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Al divrat bnei ha'adam* — that they took hold of a trait of pride, to exercise rulership and mastery over those smaller than they.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: that God may sift them
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Levaram* (another version: *levararam*) — the Holy One, blessed is He, to make known to them that their rulership is nothing, and to show them that they, and even the officers and the kings:
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The comment ends with a colon and is completed in the next comment. The abbreviation ס"א (“another version”) is left as printed.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: that they themselves are but as beasts
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Behemah hemmah lahem* — they are like the rest of the beasts and animals, unto themselves.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: For that which befalleth the sons of men befalleth beasts
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki mikreh bnei ha'adam* etc. — this is the reason of the matter: the Holy One, blessed is He, gave a happening and an event to the sons of men, and there is a happening and an event for the beast, and one happening He gave to both, for as this one dies, so that one dies.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: man hath no pre-eminence above a beast
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Umotar ha'adam min habehemah ayin* — and the superiority and success of man over the beast is not seen after he dies, for everything turns to vanity, to return to the dust.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Who knoweth
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Mi yodea* — like (Joel 2) “Who knoweth, he will return”: who is the one who understands and gives heed that the spirit of the sons of man is the one that ascends upward and stands in judgment, and the spirit of the beast is the one that descends downward to the earth, and it has no giving of judgment and reckoning; one needs not to conduct oneself like a beast that is not particular about its deeds.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Joel 2” is Joel 2:14 (JPS: “Who knoweth whether He will not turn and repent”). The final sentence is joined to the preceding one as printed and is translated literally.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: I perceived
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vera'iti* — in all these.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: there is nothing better
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki ein tov* — for a man.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: than that a man should rejoice in his works
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Me'asher yismach ha'adam bema'asav* — in the toil of his hands he shall rejoice and eat, and not widen his soul like Sheol to covet to become rich, to multiply what is not for him.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: for that is his portion
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki hu chelko* — the toil of his hands is the portion given to him from heaven, and in it he shall rejoice.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: for who shall bring him to see what shall be after him?
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki mi yevi'ennu* — to see, after he has died, what will be with his sons: whether they too will prosper in the wealth that he gathered and left to them, or will not prosper.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: But I returned
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Veshavti ani va'er'eh* — by the Holy Spirit.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: all the oppressions
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Et kol ha'ashukim* — those who are made oppressed in Gehinnom through the deeds that are done.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: under the sun
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Tachat hashamesh* — beneath the substitutes of the Torah.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Translated literally (*tachat chalifeha shel haTorah*).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: behold the tears of such as were oppressed
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vehineh dim'at ha'ashukim* — they weep over their oppressed souls at the hand of angels of destruction and cruel ones; and so he says (Psalms 84) “Passing through the valley of weeping, they make it a spring” — these are the ones who descend to Gehinnom; and this verse too is expounded so in Sifre.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Psalms 84” is Psalms 84:7 (JPS: “Passing through the valley of Baca they make it a place of springs”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: on the side of their oppressors there was power
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Umiyad oshkeihem koach* — their oppressors compel them and overpower them by force.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: that are already dead
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Shekvar metu* — before this evil inclination had power over them to push them away from the Holy One, blessed is He, such as the early fathers, for Moses was answered only through them, and such as David my father, for I was not answered with the twenty-four songs until I said (II Chronicles 6) “Remember the good deeds of David Thy servant.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “II Chronicles 6” is II Chronicles 6:42 (JPS: “Remember the good deeds of David Thy servant”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: not yet
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Adenah* — still.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: who hath not seen the evil work
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Asher lo ra'ah et hama'aseh* — I saw in Midrash Koheleth: these are the 974 generations that were pressed to be created and were not created.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Again, I considered all labour
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vera'iti ani et kol amal* — these are transgressions, which are toil in the eyes of the Holy One, blessed is He.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: all excelling in work
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ve'et kol kishron hama'aseh* — that is not for the sake of Heaven but for a man's envy of his neighbor, for both are vanity.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: rivalry with his neighbour
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki hi kin'at ish* — which is a man's envy of his neighbor.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: The fool foldeth his hands together
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Hakesil* — the wicked man: he folds his hands and does not toil, and he eats only from robbery.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: eateth his own flesh
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ve'okhel et besaro* — for the Day of Judgment, in that he sees the righteous in honor and he is judged; so it is expounded in Sifre.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Better is a handful of quietness
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Tov melo khaf nachat* — to acquire few possessions and from his toil, so that there be in them contentment of spirit to his Maker.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Than both the hands full of labour
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Mimmelo chofnayim* — many possessions through transgression, which is toil and grief of spirit before the Omnipresent.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: under the sun
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Tachat hashamesh* — like *tachat hashamayim* (“under the heavens”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: There is one that is alone, and he hath not a second
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Yesh echad ve'ein sheni* — there is a person who does his affairs alone.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: neither son nor brother
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Gam ben ve'ach ein lo* — if he is a Torah scholar, he does not acquire for himself a student who is like a son, nor a companion who is like a brother; and if he is single, he does not marry a wife to be for him like a brother, a help, and to beget a son; and if he is a merchant, he does not acquire partners for himself, and he goes out on the road alone.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: no end of all his labour
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ve'ein kez lekhol amalo* — he toils in study; and if he is a merchant, he toils in trade. Also his eyes:
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The words “Also his eyes:” at the end are the start of the next comment and are printed here as in the source.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: neither is his eye satisfied with riches
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Lo tisba osher* — he is not satisfied with the reasons of the Torah, for a man learns much Torah from his students; and in regard to money, he pursues money constantly.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: for whom then do I labour
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ulemi ani amel* — since I do not raise up students and do not marry a wife to beget sons.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Two are better than one
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Tovim hashenayim* — for every matter, than the one; therefore a man should acquire a companion for himself and marry a wife, who have more profit in their toil; much work is done by two that an individual would not begin alone.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: For if they fall
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki im yippolu* — according to its plain meaning; and in regard to the Mishnah: if his Mishnah overpowers him, his friend restores it to him; or if he stumbles and was not precise in what he heard from his teacher, his friend comes and sets him on the truth.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: but woe to him that is alone when he falleth
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ve'i lo* — and woe to him.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: then they have warmth
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vecham lahem* — according to its plain meaning; and in regard to male and female: they warm from each other and beget.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: And if a man prevail against him that is alone
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ve'im yitkefu ha'echad* — if robbers came upon him to overpower him, if there are two they will stand against them, and all the more if there are three; “and the threefold cord is not quickly broken.” Another explanation: one who is a Torah scholar, and his son, and his son's son — Torah never ceases from his seed; and so He says (Isaiah 59) “They shall not depart out of thy mouth, and out of the mouth of thy seed, and out of the mouth of the seed of thy seed.” Another explanation: the threefold cord — in Scripture, in Mishnah, and in the way of the world (*derekh eretz*): he does not quickly sin. In other ways it is expounded in the Midrash on “There is one and no second to him,” but the order of all these verses is not settled upon them.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 59” is Isaiah 59:21 (JPS: “shall not depart out of thy mouth, nor out of the mouth of thy seed, nor out of the mouth of thy seed's seed”). The last clause is translated literally.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Better is a poor and wise child
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Tov yeled misken vechakham* — this is the good inclination; and why is it called a child? Because it does not come into a man until thirteen years.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: poor
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Misken* — for the limbs do not listen to him, as [they do] to ליצ"הר.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The printed ליצ"הר appears to be an abbreviation of ליצר הרע (“to the evil inclination”); it is left as printed.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: wise
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Chakham* — for he instructs a person in a good way.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: an old and foolish king
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Mimelekh zaken ukhsil* — the evil inclination, which rules over all the limbs; old, for from the moment the child is born it is placed in him, as it is said (Genesis 4) “sin couches at the door.” And foolish, for it leads him astray in an evil way. So it is expounded in the Midrash.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 4” is Genesis 4:7 (JPS: “sin coucheth at the door”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: who knoweth not how to receive admonition any more
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Asher lo yada lehizahar od* — for he has grown old and does not accept reproof.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: For out of prison he came forth to be king
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki mi-beit hasurim yatza limlokh* — from the place of filth and stench, as we translate *vayavash* [as] *vesari*.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The Aramaic is translated as printed; no reference is printed.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: although in his kingdom he was born poor
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki gam bemalkhuto* — since he reigned over man, there is born the poor, needy one, who is better than he, and who came out of purity and not out of the filth of the womb; so they expounded it in the Midrash. Another explanation: “For better is a poor child,” etc., according to its plain meaning; “who knoweth not how to be admonished any more,” for he has already grown old in his wickedness and folly; “for out of the house of prisoners he came forth to reign” — for the poor child, in the end they will say of him that he came forth to reign out of his poverty and out of the house of his prisoners, for the samekh of *hasurim* is pointed with a *rafe*, and it is like *ha'asurim*; another version: like (Isaiah 13) “nor shall the Arabian pitch tent (*yahel*) there,” like *ya'ahel*; for so we find with Joseph, who reigned out of his going forth from the house of prisoners; and so David (II Samuel 7) “I took thee from the sheepcote, from following the sheep.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 13” is Isaiah 13:20 (JPS: “Neither shall the Arabian pitch tent there”) and “II Samuel 7” is II Samuel 7:8 (JPS: “I took thee from the sheepcote, from following the sheep”). The abbreviation ס"א (“another version”) is left as printed. The grammatical remarks are translated literally.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: born poor
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki gam bemalkhuto nolad rash* — for he is fit and worthy to reign, for even in his kingdom he turns from the way of authority and makes himself small before the wise, like the way of the poor; and so (Job 11) “a wild ass's colt is born (*yivvaled*) a man” — that he turns and is changed from what he was, a wild ass's colt, and becomes a man.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Job 11” is Job 11:12.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: born poor
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Nolad* — became; and it is the present tense.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: I saw all the living that walk under the sun
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ra'iti et kol hachayyim* etc. — I found in the Midrash of this book that this is the generation of the Flood, of whom it is said (Genesis 6) “and of every living thing.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 6” is Genesis 6:19 (JPS: “And of every living thing of all flesh”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: with the child, the second, that was to stand up in his stead
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Im hayeled hasheni* — who will endure in place of that generation, who are Noah and his sons.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: There was no end of all the people
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ein kez lekhol ha'am* — they were fruitful and multiplied too much, as it is said (Job 21) “Their seed is established before them; a woman conceives and bears within three days; they send forth their little ones like a flock.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Job 21” is Job 21:8 and 21:11 (JPS: “Their seed is established in their sight with them”; “They send forth their little ones like a flock”). The middle clause “a woman conceives and bears within three days” is not found in Job 21 and is translated as printed.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: all them whom he did lead
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Lekhol asher hayah lifneihem* — there was no end to all the good that was before them, and all was lost, and in a moment they descend to Sheol.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: they that come after
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Gam ha'acharonim* — the generation of the Dispersion.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: shall not rejoice in him
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Lo yismechu* — they too, in the good that is given into their hand.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Surely this also is vanity and a striving after wind
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki gam zeh* — the end of vanity and a striving after wind (*ra'yon ruach*), when a man walks after his inclination.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Guard thy foot when thou goest to the house of God
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Shemor raglekha* — how will you go? If you bring a thanksgiving-offering and a freewill peace-offering, that is the good; and guard yourself that you not need to bring sin-offerings and guilt-offerings.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: be ready to hearken
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vekarov* — be ready to hear the words of the Holy One, blessed is He, and that is good and near to the Holy One, blessed is He.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: than when fools give sacrifices
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Matat hakesilim zavach* — that he sin and bring a sacrifice.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: for they know not that they do evil
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki einam yod'im la'asot ra* — the fool does not understand that he does evil to himself.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: to utter a word before God
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Lehotzi davar lifnei Elohim* — to speak a hard word toward on high.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: for God is in heaven, and thou upon earth
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki ha'Elohim bashamayim ve'atah al ha'aretz* — even a weak one above and a mighty one below, the awe of the weak is upon the mighty; and all the more so a mighty one above and a weak one below.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: For a dream cometh through a multitude of business
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki va hachalom berov inyan* — for the way of a dream is to come with many thoughts, in that a man studies and thinks by day; and the way of a fool's voice is to come with many words, for in multiplying words he brings a voice of folly out of his mouth, “for transgression does not cease”; therefore I say: let your words be few.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: He hath no pleasure in fools
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ein chefetz bakesilim* — there is no pleasure before the Holy One, blessed is He, in the wicked who vow and do not pay.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Suffer not thy mouth
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Al titen et picha* — in a vow.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: to bring thy flesh into guilt
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Lehachti et besarekha* — that iniquity be visited upon your sons.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: neither say thou before the messenger
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ve'al tomar lifnei hamal'akh* — the emissary who comes to demand from you the charity that you pledged in public.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: that it was an error
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki shegagah hi* — I pledged it in error; I thought that I had the ability in my hand to give.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: destroy the work of thy hands
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vechibbel et ma'aseh yadekha* — the commandments that were in your hand, that you had already performed — you have lost them; so it is expounded in the Midrash.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: at thy voice
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Al kolekha* — because of your voice.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: For through the multitude of dreams and vanities
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki berov chalomot* etc. — that everything that dreams and prophets of vanity and many words will say to you is to make you turn away from the Omnipresent.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Translated literally; the sentence is elliptical as printed.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: but fear thou God
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki et ha'Elohim yera* — behold, *ki* serves in the sense of *ela* (“but”): do not listen to the dreams, but fear God.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: If thou seest the oppression of the poor
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Im ok rash vegezel mishpat vatzedek* etc. — if you see in the province that they oppress the poor and rob justice and righteousness.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: marvel not at the matter
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Al titmah* — at the will of the Omnipresent, when He brings evil upon them.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: for one higher than the high watcheth
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki gavoha me'al gavoha shomer* — and sees their deeds, and there are higher ones above them who do the mission of the Omnipresent, and their hand is strong to exact payment from them.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: the violent perverting of justice
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vegezel mishpat* — *gezel* of *mishpat*, because it is joined, is pointed *gezel* with a small patach, for if it were not joined it would be pointed *gezel* with kamatz. Another explanation: if you see that they oppress the poor and rob justice, and you see righteousness coming to the city, that the Holy One, blessed is He, bestows goodness upon them and does not exact payment from them, do not marvel at the will of the Omnipresent, for such is His way, to lengthen His anger.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The sentence “and you see righteousness coming to the city, that the Holy One… bestows goodness upon them” is translated literally; its construction is difficult as printed.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: for one higher than the high watcheth
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki gavoha me'al gavoha shomer* — He waits until their measure is filled.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: and there are higher than they
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ugvohim* — He has authority over them to exact payment from them when the time of their reckoning arrives, like (Job 14) “and Thou dost not keep (*tishmor*) over my sin,” (Isaiah 27) “keeping faithfulness,” (Genesis 37) “he kept the matter.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Job 14” is Job 14:16 (JPS: “Thou dost not even wait for my sin”); “Isaiah 27” is Isaiah 26:2 (JPS: “that keepeth faithfulness”); “Genesis 37” is Genesis 37:11 (JPS: “his father kept the saying in mind”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: But the profit of a land every way
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Veyitron eretz bakkol hi* — and the advantage of the dwellers of the land, who are haughty and anger the Omnipresent. *Bakkol hu* — in everything He performs His mission to exact payment, even through gnats, as He did to Titus.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: a king that maketh himself servant to the field
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Melekh lasadeh ne'evad* — the Holy One, blessed is He, becomes a worker for Zion, to demand her insult from her destroyer and to pay her reward to her builder.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: He that loveth silver shall not be satisfied with silver
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ohev kesef lo yisba kesef* — one who loves commandments is not satisfied with them.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: nor he that loveth abundance
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Umi ohev behamon* — many commandments.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: with increase
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Lo tevu'ah* — and in none of them is there a specific, recognizable commandment, such as the building of the Temple, a synagogue, and a beautiful Torah scroll.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: this also is vanity
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Gam zeh hevel* — so these two verses are expounded in the Midrash, and other fitting aspects too; but I put this first because it is connected with “and there are higher than they,” which Scripture placed together.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: He that loveth silver shall not be satisfied with silver
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: Another explanation: *Veyitron eretz bakkol hi* — the reward of working the soil is important above all, for even if he is a king, he must be a servant to the field; if the earth produced fruit he has what to eat, and if not he dies of hunger.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The source gives no separate lemma; the printed comment begins with words of Ecclesiastes 5:8 (“the profit of a land…”), which do not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: He that loveth silver shall not be satisfied with silver
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ohev kesef lo yisba kesef* — he will not eat silver.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: nor he that loveth abundance
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Umi ohev behamon* — in money.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: with increase
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Lo tevu'ah* — for he does not gather fruit for himself. This also is vanity.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: this also is vanity
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: Another explanation: *Veyitron eretz bakkol hu* — the reward of Israel is in all the words of Torah, whether in Scripture, in Mishnah, or in Gemara.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The source gives no separate lemma; the printed comment begins with words of Ecclesiastes 5:8 (“the profit of a land…”), which do not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: this also is vanity
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Melekh lasadeh ne'evad* — a king in Scripture and Mishnah still needs to be made servant to a master of Gemara, who arranges before him the rulings of forbidden and permitted, impurity and purity, and laws.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The source lemma (“a king that maketh himself servant to the field”) belongs to Ecclesiastes 5:8 and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: He that loveth silver
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ohev kesef* — one who loves Torah is not satisfied with it.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: nor he that loveth abundance
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Veha'ohev behamon* — Torah.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: with increase
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Lo tevu'ah* — one who has Scripture and Mishnah but has no Gemara, what benefit does he have? All these are in Leviticus Rabbah.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: When goods increase
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Birvot hatovah* — when Israel improve their deeds.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: they are increased that eat them
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ravu okhleha* — the giving of reward for the commandments.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: what advantage is there to the owner thereof
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Umah kishron levalehah* — to the Holy One, blessed is He, in all the improving of their deeds.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: saving the beholding of them with his eyes
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki im re'ut* — of His eyes, in that He sees that they are bowed to Him, and contentment before Him, in that He spoke and His will was done; and so with regard to the offerings.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: When goods increase, they are increased that eat them
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Birvot hatovah ravu okhleha* — that they bring many freewill offerings, the priests who eat them increase.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: what advantage is there to the owner thereof
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Umah kishron levalehah* — before the Holy One, blessed is He.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: saving the beholding of them with his eyes
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki im re'ut einav* — in that He spoke and His will was done.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Sweet is the sleep of a labouring man
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Metukah shenat ha'oved* — the one who works the soil sleeps, and his sleep is sweet to him, whether he eats little or whether he eats much, for he is already accustomed to it.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: but the satiety of the rich will not suffer him to sleep
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vehassava le'ashir einennu mani'ach lo lishon* — and the abundance of possessions of a rich man, an owner of many businesses, does not let him sleep all night, thinking about them. Another explanation: “Sweet is the sleep of one who serves God” — whether the days of his years are few or whether the days of his years are many, he eats his reward: the little as the much. Moses sustained Israel forty years, and Samuel the prophet sustained them ten years, and Scripture weighed them one against the other, as it is said (Psalms 99) “Moses and Aaron among His priests, and Samuel among those who call His name,” etc. So it is expounded in Tanchuma.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Psalms 99” is Psalms 99:6 (JPS: “Moses and Aaron among His priests, And Samuel among them that call upon His name”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: the satiety of the rich
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vehassava le'ashir* — a master of traditions.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: will not suffer him to sleep
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Einennu mani'ach lo lishon* — in the grave, as it is said (Song of Songs 7) “moving the lips of those who are asleep”: every Torah scholar of whom they say a word of tradition in his name — his lips are moving in the grave.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Song of Songs 7” is Song of Songs 7:10 (JPS: “Moving gently the lips of those that are asleep”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: riches kept by the owner thereof to his hurt
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Osher shamur levalav lera'ato* — like the wealth of Korach, through which he grew haughty and went down to Sheol.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: there is nothing in his hand
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ve'ein beyado me'umah* — even the merit of the fathers.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: shall take nothing for his labour
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Umeumah lo yisa va'amalo* — when he dies he shall not carry in his hand any merit of charity that he did with his money in his life; exactly as that money came, so it went.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: sickness
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vecholyo* — like *vecholi*, and the “הו"יו” is extra, like the vav of (Psalms 104) *chayto ya'ar*.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The printed הו"יו is left as printed and not resolved here. Printed “Psalms 104” is Psalms 104:20 (JPS: “all the beasts of the forest”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: to eat and to drink, and to enjoy pleasure
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Le'echol uleshtot ulre'ot tovah* — to engage in the Torah, which is a good teaching (*lekach tov*); and let him not gather great wealth, but rejoice in the portion given to him, for it is his portion.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: power to eat thereof
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vehishlito le'echol mimmenu* — in his life.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: to take his portion
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Lasset et chelko* — at his death, that He grant him to engage in Torah and commandments in his life in order that he receive reward.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: that they are not many
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki lo harbeh* — for there is no length of days in this world.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: let him remember the days of his life
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Yizkor et yemei chayav* — for they are few and not many; and why should he toil to gather wealth? Let him toil in a thing that will stand for him for the World to Come, in his lifetime.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: for God answereth him
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki ha'Elohim ma'aneh* etc. — the Holy One, blessed is He, is a fixed testimony to this forever.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: in the joy of his heart
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Besimchat libbo* — for he rejoices to do good in his life. And I saw in the Midrash: this is Elkanah, who guided Israel to go up to Shiloh on the festivals; and by the way by which he took them up in this year, he would not take them up in the next year, in order to publicize the matter and to accustom them; therefore Scripture ascribed to him “and that man went up out of his city,” etc. And I say that this Midrash is the end of the verse: “for God answereth in the joy of his heart” — this is Elkanah, whom the Holy One, blessed is He, fixed for him in the Writings (*bakketuvim*) and testified of him (I Samuel 11) “and that man went up out of his city.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “I Samuel 11” is I Samuel 1:3 (JPS: “And this man went up out of his city from year to year”). The phrase *bakketuvim* is translated literally as printed.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: answereth
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ma'aneh* — pointed with a small patach; therefore I explain it as a noun, like (Job 32) “for there is no answer (*ma'aneh*) in the mouth of the three men.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Job 32” is Job 32:5 (JPS: “there was no answer in the mouth of these three men”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: in the joy of his heart
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Besimchat libbo* — that he rejoiced on the festival.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: it is heavy upon men
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Verabbah hi al ha'adam* — it is practiced among many people.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: riches, wealth
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Osher unekhasim* — according to its plain meaning.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: yet God giveth him not power to eat thereof
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Velo yashlitennu ha'Elohim le'echol mimmenu* — that he be glad in his portion, to find contentment in his wealth, for he strives to make and to increase wealth, as it is said (Habakkuk 2) “and he dies and is not satisfied”; and also He did not enable him to give charity, to eat of it in the future; and a stranger takes that money and gives charity with it and benefits from it. And Midrash Aggadah is on words of Torah.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Habakkuk 2” is Habakkuk 2:5 (JPS: “And is as death, and cannot be satisfied”); the printed wording differs from the verse.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: riches, wealth
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Osher unekhasim vechavod* — Scripture, Mishnah, and Aggadah.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: yet God giveth him not power to eat thereof
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Lo yashlitennu* — that he did not merit Gemara, and as a result there is no benefit from him in any matter of ruling. “For a stranger eateth it” — this is the master of Gemara.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: If a man beget a hundred children
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Im yolid ish me'ah* — sons.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: so that the days of his years are many
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Verav sheyihyu yemei shanav* — (and much wealth and every good thing) his days of years — his; and *rav* is an expression of “enough”: enough for every good.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The parenthesis is printed in the source and is translated as printed.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: but his soul have not enough of good
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Venafsho lo tisba* — of that good, in that he does not rejoice in his portion so that his spirit be cooled by what is in his hand.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: and moreover he have no burial
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vegam kevurah lo hayetah lo* — sometimes he is killed and dogs eat him; and all these things were found in Ahab, who begot many sons and had much wealth and coveted what belonged to others and did not find contentment in his wealth, and dogs ate him.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: an untimely birth is better than he
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Tov mimmennu hanefel* — of a woman; for the untimely birth comes in vanity and goes, and has not seen good and has not desired it, and has nothing to grieve over.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: yea, though he live a thousand years twice told
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ve'illu chayah* — and if he lived two thousand years, what advantage does he have, since he has not seen good? Behold, his end is to return to the dust like the rest of the poor.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: All the labour of man
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Kol amal ha'adam* — for his mouth, that he may enjoy and eat in this world and the next; and this one did not enjoy in his life.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: And yet the appetite is not filled
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vegam hanefesh lo timmale* — in astonishment; that is, even his desire was not filled with a little enjoyment, like (Exodus 15) “my soul shall be filled (*timla'emo*) with them,” an expression of attaining a desire; and since it is so:
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Exodus 15” is Exodus 15:9 (JPS: “My lust shall be satisfied upon them”). The comment ends with a colon and no completion; translated as printed.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: For what advantage hath the wise more than the fool?
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Mah yoter lo* — in his wisdom, over if he had been a fool.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: or the poor man that hath understanding
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Umah la'ani* — a lack compared with the rich man, who has no contentment; he too knows how to walk in the land among the living. Another explanation: “and the soul is not filled” in the World to Come, for he did not do good deeds in his life.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Better is the seeing of the eyes than the wandering of the desire
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Tov mar'eh einayim mehalakh nafesh* — it was good and he was fitted for this, to see his wealth with his eyes, in food and drink that goes into the soul. Another explanation: *tov mar'eh einayim mehalakh nafesh* — it was good for this one, and he was fitted to go after his eyes to rob and to oppress, from the wandering of his soul, because he did not set his heart to where his soul will go when he dies.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: this also is vanity
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Gam zeh hevel* — it is what is given to the wicked.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Whatsoever cometh into being, the name thereof was given long ago
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Mah shehayah kvar nikra shemo* — the importance and greatness that he had in his life: “already his name was called,” that is: it already was and passed; already a name went forth for him in authority, and now it has passed, and it is known that he is a man and not God, and his end is that he died, and he cannot contend with the Angel of Death, who is stronger than he.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Seeing there are many words that increase vanity
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki yesh devarim harbeh* — in which he occupied himself in his life, like the laughter of kings: monkeys, elephants and lions; all of it increased for him, and what advantage does he have after he dies?

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: For who knoweth what is good for man in his life
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki mi yodea* — for who is it who knows good deeds and what a man should do in his life so that they be good for him for the long world?

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: all the days of his vain life
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Mispar yemei chayyei havlo* — which are few in number.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: which he spendeth as a shadow
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vaya'asem* — those deeds in the little time that he lives, which is a short time, like the shadow of a bird that passes; and although Solomon said “as a shadow” without specifying whether the shadow of a palm tree or the shadow of a wall, which are fixed, David his father had already explained (Psalms 144) “his days are as a shadow that passeth away” — that is the shadow of a bird that flies; so it is expounded in the Midrash.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Psalms 144” is Psalms 144:4 (JPS: “His days are as a shadow that passeth away”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: for who can tell a man what shall be after him under the sun?
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Asher mi yaggid le'adam* — by what will the wealth that he gathered through oppression endure for his sons after him under the sun?

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: A good name is better than precious oil
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Tov shem mishemen tov* — a good name is better for a man than good oil; and on the day of death the name is better than the day of his birth. Therefore a good name was likened to oil more than to other liquids, for oil, you put water into it and it floats and rises and is recognized, but other liquids, you put water into them and they absorb it. “A good name is better than good oil” — good oil goes down, as it is said (Psalms 133) “like the good oil that comes down upon the beard”; a good name goes up, as it is said (Genesis 12) “and I will make thy name great.” Oil is good for an hour and a good name for ever, as it is said (Psalms 72) “May his name be for ever.” Good oil goes from a jug to a hall and no further, and a good name to the end of the world. Rabbi Judah son of Rabbi Simon said: we find that those who had good oil entered a place of life and came out burned, and they were Nadab and Abihu, who were anointed with the anointing oil; and we find that those who had a good name entered a place of death and came out alive: Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah, who came out of the fiery furnace.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Psalms 133” is Psalms 133:2 (JPS: “Like the precious oil upon the head, Coming down upon the beard”), “Genesis 12” is Genesis 12:2 (JPS: “and make thy name great”), and “Psalms 72” is Psalms 72:17 (JPS: “May his name endure for ever”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: the day of death than the day of one’s birth
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Veyom hamavet miyom hivvaldo* — when Miriam was born, not everyone knew what she was; when she died, the well departed; and so Aaron, with the pillar of cloud; and so Moses, with the manna.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: It is better to go to the house of mourning
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Tov lalekhet el beit eivel* — a conduct that applies to the living and to the dead.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Than to go to the house of feasting
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Milekhet el beit mishteh* — for that is a conduct that applies only to the living.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: For that is the end of all men
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ba'asher hu sof kol ha'adam* — because mourning is the end of every man, the end of every man is to come to this; therefore the living should lay to his heart: all the kindness that I do with the dead, I shall need that it be done for me at my death — דידל ידלוניה דיטען יטענוניה דיספד יספדוניה דיילוה ילויניה. Another explanation: “for that is the end of all men” — that death is the end of all the days of man, and if now he does not do him kindness, he will not do him any more; but the house of feasting — he invited him and he did not go, he can say to him: in the end you will have a son, and there I shall be with you; the joy of the wedding of your sons will come to you, and there I shall go.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The Aramaic sentence is left as printed and not resolved here.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: And the living will lay it to his heart
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vehachai yitten el libbo* — this matter, that if now he does not do kindness for him, he will not do it for him any more.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Vexation is better than laughter
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Tov ka'as mischok* — one whom the attribute of judgment pursues should not grieve. It would have been good for the generation of the Flood if the Holy One, blessed is He, had shown a frowning face over the transgressions in their hands, rather than the laughter He laughed with them, for had He shown them a little ill favor, they would have returned to the good. It would have been good for Adonijah if his father had grieved him over each transgression that he committed, rather than the laughter he showed him, and in the end he was killed on account of it.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: the heart may be gladdened
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Yitav lev* — the heart of a man will turn to improve his ways.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Lev chakhamim beveit eivel* — their thought is on the day of death.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: But the heart of fools is in the house of mirth
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ulev kesilim beveit simchah* — they are not afraid of the day of death, and their heart is as healthy as a hall.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: the crackling of thorns
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki kekol hassirim* — wood of thorns; *ashpinesh* in Old French.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Ecclesiastes 7:6 (“épines”), in forms such as אישפינש and אספינש; the printed form (אשפי"נש) is a variant spelling.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: under a pot
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Tachat hassir* — under a copper pot placed upon a kindling of thorns, and they crackle into it. Rabbi Joshua ben Levi said: all the woods, when they burn, their sound does not go forth; but these thorns, their sound goes forth — to say: we too are of the woods. They make it known: we too are of the trees and there is need of us; so also fools multiply words to say: we too are among the important.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The Aramaic of Rabbi Joshua ben Levi is translated as printed.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: this also is vanity
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Gam zeh hevel* — and it is a toil that the Holy One, blessed is He, gave to creatures, to be wearied and to be taunted by them.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Surely oppression turneth a wise man into a fool
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki ha'oshek yehollel chakham* — when the fool taunts the wise man, he confuses his mind, and he too stumbles. Dathan and Abiram taunted Moses, saying (Exodus 5) “The Lord look upon you and judge,” etc., and they confused him and destroyed his heart, and caused him to be exacting against the Holy One, blessed is He, and he said (there, 5) “neither hast Thou delivered Thy people at all”; and he was punished with that which He answered him, “Now shalt thou see,” and thou shalt not see in the war of the thirty-one kings.
