Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Exodus 5” is Exodus 5:21 and “there, 5” is Exodus 5:23 (JPS: “neither hast Thou delivered Thy people at all”); “Now shalt thou see” is Exodus 6:1 (JPS: “Now shalt thou see what I will do to Pharaoh”); no reference is printed for it.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: And a gift destroyeth the understanding
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Lev matanah* — a heart of wisdom, which is a gift to a man, as it is said (Proverbs 2) “For the Lord giveth wisdom.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Proverbs 2” is Proverbs 2:6 (JPS: “For the LORD giveth wisdom”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Surely oppression
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Oshek* — an expression of strife and taunting. There are other explanations, but they separate the verses from one another; and what is stated at the head of the verse proves that it is connected to the verse before it.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Better is the end of a thing than the beginning thereof
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Tov acharit davar merei'shito* — according to its plain meaning: at the beginning of a matter we do not know what will be at its end, but when the end is good, it is completed in good. Another explanation: “Better is the end of a thing than its beginning” — when its beginning is good, that they intended for good when they began it. Rabbi Meir was standing and expounding the whole matter concerning Elisha ben Abuyah, in Midrash Koheleth.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The Aramaic sentence about Rabbi Meir is translated as printed.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: the patient in spirit
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Erekh ruach* — one who lengthens his anger and does not hurry to quarrel.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Be not hasty in thy spirit to be angry
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Al tevahel* — do not hurry.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Say not thou
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Al tomar mah hayah shehayamim* etc. — do not wonder at the good that came upon the early righteous, such as the generation of the wilderness, the generation of Joshua, and the generation of David.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: for it is not out of wisdom that thou inquirest concerning this
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki lo mechokhmah sha'alta* — for everything is according to the merit of the generations.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Wisdom is good with an inheritance
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Tovah chokhmah* etc. — their wisdom stood by them together with the inheritance of the merit of their fathers, for wisdom is good.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: a profit to them that see the sun
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Veyoter lero'ei hashamesh* — wisdom is an advantage to all creatures.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: to them that see the sun
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Lero'ei hashamesh* — these are all creatures, as we learn in the Mishnah: one who vows [abstention] from “those who see the sun” is forbidden even regarding the blind; he intended only those whom the sun sees.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: For wisdom is a defence, even as money is a defence
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki betzel hachokhmah betzel hakesef* — whoever is in the shadow of wisdom is in the shadow of money, for wisdom causes wealth to come.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: wisdom preserveth the life of him that hath it
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Veyitron da'at hachokhmah techayyeh va'aleha* — and further, wisdom is superior to money, for wisdom gives life to its owner.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Consider the work of God
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Re'eh et ma'aseh ha'Elohim* — how everything is set right according to a man's deed: the Garden of Eden for the righteous and Gehinnom for the wicked; see for yourself to which you will cling.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: for who can make that straight, which He hath made crooked?
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki mi yukhal letaken* — after death, the thing which he made crooked in his life.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: In the day of prosperity be joyful
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Beyom tovah heyeh vetov* — on the day that you have it in your hand to do good, be among those who do the good.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: in the day of adversity consider
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Uveyom ra'ah re'eh* — when evil comes upon the wicked, you shall be among the seers, as it is said (Isaiah 66) “And they shall go forth and look upon the carcasses of the men,” etc., and you shall not be among those who are seen, “and they shall be an abhorrence to all flesh.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 66” is Isaiah 66:24 (JPS: “And they shall go forth, and look Upon the carcasses of the men that have rebelled against Me… And they shall be an abhorring unto all flesh”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: God hath made even the one as well as the other
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Gam et zeh le'umat zeh* — the good and the reward of its deed, against the evil and the reward of its deed.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: to the end that man should find nothing after him
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Shelo yimtza ha'adam acharav me'umah* — to ponder after the Holy One, blessed is He.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Translated literally; the idiom “to ponder after” is not resolved here.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: there is a righteous man that perisheth in his righteousness
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Yesh tzaddik oved betzidko* — although he perishes, he still stands in his righteousness. An incident: Yosef ben Pinchas the priest, in whose foot a thread (*nima*) came up. They called the physician to cut off his foot. He said to him: when you reach the hair's breadth, let me know; and so he did. He called Chunia his son. He said to him: my son, until here you were obligated to attend to me; from here on you are not obligated to attend to me, for a priest does not become defiled for a limb from the living of his father.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The word *nima* is translated literally as “thread” and its sense is not resolved here.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Be not righteous overmuch
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Al tehi tzaddik harbeh* — like Saul, who imagined himself to be righteous and had pity on the wicked. “And do not make yourself overwise” — to reason an a fortiori argument of folly: and if for one soul the Torah said, bring a decapitated heifer, etc.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Be not overmuch wicked
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Al tirsha harbeh* — even if you have been wicked a little, do not add to being wicked [ר*].
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The printed text contains a stray “[ ר* ]”, which is left as printed.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: why shouldest thou die before thy time?
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Lamah tamut belo itekha* — like Saul, as it is said (I Chronicles 10) “And Saul died for his trespass which he trespassed at Nob the city of the priests and at Amalek.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “I Chronicles 10” is I Chronicles 10:13 (JPS: “So Saul died for his transgression which he committed against the LORD, because of the word of the LORD, which he kept not”); the words “at Nob the city of the priests and at Amalek” are not in that verse and are translated as printed.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: It is good that thou shouldest take hold of the one
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Tov asher ta'achoz bezeh* etc. — hold to righteousness and to wickedness: if the righteous prophet says to you a thing that seems to you like wickedness, such as what Samuel said to Saul, let it not be light in your eyes to doubt it.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: shall discharge himself of them all
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Yetze et kullam* — the hands of both, to fulfill the righteous and the wicked according to their proper law.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Translated literally.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Wisdom is a stronghold to the wise man
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Hachokhmah ta'oz lechakham* — because he said “be not overmuch wicked,” if you were wicked a little do not add to it, but examine your deeds and be astonished at the sin; he said: wisdom is a strength to the wise man, for it advises him to return in repentance.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: more than ten rulers
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Me'asarah shalitim* — we find in Josiah, of whom Scripture testified (II Kings 23) “And like him there was no king before him,” etc.: behold, his wisdom stood him in stead, for he examined his deeds, and it was better for him than ten kings who were wicked and did not return from their ways.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “II Kings 23” is II Kings 23:25 (JPS: “And like unto him was there no king before him”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: that are in a city
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Asher hayu ba'ir* — in Jerusalem: Rehoboam, Abijah, Ahaziah, Joash after the death of Jehoiada, Amaziah, Ahaz, Manasseh, Amon, Jehoiakim, Zedekiah.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: For there is not a righteous man upon earth
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki adam ein tzaddik ba'aretz* — therefore he must examine his deeds.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Also take not heed unto all words that are spoken
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Gam lekhol hadevarim* etc. — because it was spoken of Saul, who accepted slander about Nob the city of the priests, and of him it was said “Be not overmuch wicked”; he said: “Also to all the words that talebearers speak to you, do not give your heart to accept them.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The printed lemma reads גט, which appears to be a misprint for גם (“also”); it is translated as גם.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: lest thou hear thy servant curse thee
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Asher lo tishma et avdekha mekallelekha* — it is not good that you incline your ear to hear your servant curse you. Another explanation: “than ten rulers” — these are ten things that obligate a man: his two eyes, which show him matters of transgression; his two ears, which make him hear idle words; his two hands, with which he robs and plunders; his two feet, which carry him to a matter of transgression; and his mouth and his heart. Another explanation: “Wisdom is a stronghold to the wise man” — this is Noah, “than ten rulers” — than the ten generations before him. Another explanation: “to the wise man” — this is Abraham, “than ten rulers” — than the ten generations before him. Another explanation: “to the wise man” — this is Joseph, “than ten rulers” — these are his brothers. Another explanation: “to the wise man” — this is Moses, “ten rulers” — ten things that serve the body through food: from the mouth to the gullet, from the gullet to the stomach, etc., as it is in Midrash Koheleth; and his wisdom stood Moses in stead, so that he did not need food for forty days and forty nights. All these aspects are in the Midrash, and I cannot settle upon them the verse after it, “For there is not a righteous man upon earth”; “All this have I tried by wisdom” refers to the verses below (another version: and not — examine) and to those above.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The Aramaic phrase “from the mouth to the gullet, from the gullet to the stomach” is translated as printed, and the parenthesis “(ס"א ולא ודוק)” is left as printed. Audit 5 source check: a passage with the same wording (8 consecutive words) is found in Bereshit Rabbah 34.5 (Sefaria Hebrew text, labelled Public Domain). This is a wording match only; the translation was not changed.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: All this have I tried by wisdom
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Nisiti bechokhmah* — in the Torah.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: I will get wisdom
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Amarti echkamah* — to know wisdom.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: but it was far from me
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vehi rechokah mimmenni* — and what is this?

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: That which is is far off
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Rechok mah shehayah* — the far things that were in the creation of the world.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: and exceeding deep
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ve'amok amok* — “who shall find it?” for I have no permission to ponder them: what is above and what is below, what is before and what is behind.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: I turned about, and applied my heart to know
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ve'od savoti* — to know and to search out and to seek the wisdom of the section of the red heifer and the reckoning of the end of redemption.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: and to know wickedness to be folly
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ulada'at resha kesel* — to stand on the end of the reasoning of its commandment, and the folly — the mixed-up, confused revelry — in it.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: and I find more bitter than death the woman
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Umotzeh ani mar mimmavet* — for it is harsher than the ten hard things that were created in the world, as it is in Bava Batra, in the chapter *HaShutafin*; “and I find bitterer and harder than it the woman” — this is heresy (*minut*).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: whose heart is snares and nets
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vecharamim libbah* — an expression of a net, like (Habakkuk 1) “He draweth it up in his net (*becharmo*), he gathereth it in his drag (*bemakhmaro*).”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Habakkuk 1” is Habakkuk 1:15 (JPS: “They catch them in their net, And gather them in their drag”); the printed wording differs from the verse.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: and her hands as bands
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Asurim yadeha* — and once she has taken hold of a man, behold, he is like one bound with cords of rope.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: bands
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Asurim* — a noun of things bound, like (Judges 15) “and his bonds melted (*vayamassu asurav*)”; so Menachem explained.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Judges 15” is Judges 15:14 (JPS: “and his bands dropped from off his hands”); the printed wording differs from the verse.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Behold, this have I found, saith Koheleth, adding one thing to another, to find out the account
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Re'eh zeh matzati amerah Koheleth achat le'achat limtzo cheshbon* — all the commandments that the righteous perform and the transgressions that the wicked commit are counted before the Holy One, blessed is He, one upon one, until they add up to a great sum; so our Rabbis explained in tractate Sotah.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: saith Koheleth
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Amerah Koheleth* — the gathering of wisdom said, and his intelligent soul, which gathers wisdom, said.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Koheleth
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Koheleth* — it is feminine, and when its saying is in the masculine, it refers to the collection, and that is Solomon. And in the Midrash we find: Rabbi Jeremiah ben Elazar said: the Holy Spirit speaks sometimes in the masculine and sometimes in the feminine; one verse says (Psalms 70) “my help (*ezri*) and my deliverer,” and another verse says (there, 40) “for Thou art my help (*ezrati*)”; one verse says (Nahum 2) “the voice of a herald (*mevasser*),” and another verse says (Isaiah 8) “the voice of the herald (*mevasseret*) Zion.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Psalms 70” is Psalms 70:6 (JPS: “Thou art my help and my deliverer”) and “there, 40” is Psalms 40:18 (JPS: “Thou art my help and my deliverer”). Printed “Isaiah 8” appears to be Isaiah 40:9 (JPS: “O thou that tellest good tidings to Zion”); the Nahum quotation (“the voice of a herald”) was not identified in Nahum 2:1 (JPS: “the feet of him That bringeth good tidings”). The printed wording differs from the verses.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: which yet my soul sought, but I found not
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Asher od bikshah nafshi* — besides these mentioned above, which I sought and did not find, my soul sought yet again a fit one among women, and I did not find, for all of them have light minds.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: one man among a thousand have I found
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Adam echad me'elef matzati* — in the way of the world: a thousand enter Scripture; of them only a hundred emerge who are fit for Mishnah; and of those hundred who entered Mishnah, only ten emerge for Gemara; and of those ten who enter Gemara, only one succeeds in rendering rulings: behold, one out of a thousand.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: but a woman among all those have I not found
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ve'ishah bekhol eleh* — even among a thousand; therefore you must be careful with her.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Behold, this only have I found
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Levad re'eh zeh matzati* — that a stumbling-block came into the world through her.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: that God made man upright
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Asher asah* — the Holy One, blessed is He, the first man, upright.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: but they have sought out many inventions
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vehemmah* — once Eve his wife was joined to him, and they became two, and were called “they” (*hemmah*).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: many inventions
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Bikshu cheshbonot rabbim* — schemes and thoughts of sin; so it is expounded in the Midrash.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Who is as the wise man?
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Mi kehechakham* — who in the world is as important as a wise man.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: who knoweth the interpretation of a thing?
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Umi yodea pesher davar* — the interpretation (*pisharon*) of a matter, as we find in Daniel, that from his wisdom, in that he was wise in the fear of Heaven, the secrets of interpretations were revealed to him; who is like Moses, who makes compromises (*peshorim*) between Israel and their Father in heaven.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: the boldness of his face is changed
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ve'oz panav yeshunne* — from the rest of creatures, until (Exodus 34) “they were afraid to come nigh him, for the skin of his face sent forth beams.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Exodus 34” is Exodus 34:30 (JPS: “the skin of his face sent forth beams; and they were afraid to come nigh him”); the printed wording combines the two parts of the verse.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: keep the king’s command
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ani pi melekh shemor* — therefore I must and am ready to keep the word of the King of the world, which is the best of them all.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: in regard of the oath of God
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ve'al divrat shevu'at Elohim* — that we swore to Him at Horeb to keep His commandments. Another explanation: I am ready to keep the word of the kings of the nations who rule over us with head-taxes (*gulgaliyot*) and levies (*arnoniyot*), “and in regard of the oath of God,” provided that they do not make us transgress the oath that we swore to the Omnipresent; *al divrat* — and beside the oath of God I will keep the word of the kings. So we find with Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah, who said to Nebuchadnezzar (Daniel 3): “To you we say, king Nebuchadnezzar, we have no need to answer thee in this matter” [Aramaic]. If “king,” why “Nebuchadnezzar”; and if “Nebuchadnezzar,” why “king”? But thus they said to him: to you we say that you are king over us for service and taxes and head-taxes; but concerning this that you say to us, to serve idolatry, you are Nebuchadnezzar and not king, and you and a dog are equal.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Daniel 3” is Daniel 3:16 (JPS: “O Nebuchadnezzar, we have no need to answer thee in this matter”); the printed Aramaic wording differs slightly from the verse.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Be not hasty to go out of his presence
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Al tibbahel mipanav telekh* — do not be hasty to say that you will go and flee from before him to a place where he does not rule, for in every place He rules.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: stand not in an evil thing
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ve'al ta'amod bedavar ra* — do not set yourself to engage in evil things.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: he doeth whatsoever pleaseth him
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki kol asher yachpotz* — to exact payment from you, authority and ability are in His hand to do.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Forasmuch as the king’s word hath power
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Be'asher devar melekh shiltton* — because the word of the Holy One, blessed is He, rules, “and who may say unto Him: What doest Thou?”; and if you keep a commandment, you will not know an evil thing and it will not come upon you.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: a wise man’s heart discerneth time and judgment
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ve'et umishpat yeda lev chakham* — the wise man knows that there is a fixed time for the reckoning of the wicked, and that there are judgments before the Holy One, blessed is He, that in the end He will exact payment from them; *mishpat* is *justitsa* in Old French, and it is the punishment.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word under Ecclesiastes 8 (“justice”), in forms such as יוסטיצא and יושטיקא; the printed form (יוסטי"צא) matches. The verse number in the OCR of his text is not legible, so only the chapter is given.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: to every matter
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki lekhol chefetz* — for a man does his will and transgresses the law; there is a time to be repaid, and a judgment and a punishment are ready.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: the evil of man is great upon him
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki ra'at ha'adam rabbah alav* — when the evil of a man is great and his load is full, then his reckoning comes; and *ki* is used in the sense of “when,” as (Exodus 18) “when they have a matter, it cometh unto me.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Exodus 18” is Exodus 18:16 (JPS: “when they have a matter, it cometh unto me”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: he knoweth not that which shall be
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki einennu yode'a mah sheyihyeh* — when the wicked man commits a transgression, he does not give heed to what the Holy One, blessed is He, is going to bring him to in judgment, and woe to him for that.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: even when it cometh to pass
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki ka'asher yihyeh* — the punishment: who will tell him, so that he can take counsel in it, take advice in it, and take permission, for it will come upon him suddenly.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: no man that hath power over the wind
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ein adam shalit baruach* — over his spirit and the inclination of the emissary of the Omnipresent, to shut up and withhold from him the spirit in his body so that the angel of death not take it.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Translated literally; the construction is difficult as printed.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: neither hath he power over the day of death
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ve'ein shilton* — of any king is recognizable on the day of his death; in every place you find this. And King David, on the day of his death (I Kings 2) “And the days of David drew nigh to die” — kingship is not mentioned here.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “I Kings 2” is I Kings 2:1 (JPS: “Now the days of David drew nigh that he should die”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: there is no discharge in war
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ve'ein mishlachat bamilchamah* — this is to say: I will send my son or my servant in my place.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: All this have I seen
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Et kol zeh ra'iti* — what is mentioned above.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: even applied my heart thereto
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Venatun et libbi lekhol ma'aseh* — and also to all the deeds of men I gave my heart, and I saw a time when one man had power over another and prevailed over him, and his end turned to his evil: Amalek prevailed over Israel and his end was (Numbers 24) “and his end shall come to destruction”; so Pharaoh, so Nebuchadnezzar, and so Sennacherib.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Numbers 24” is Numbers 24:20 (JPS: “But his end shall come to destruction”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: And so
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Uvekhen* — and then.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: I saw the wicked buried
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ra'iti resha'im kevurim* — in this prophecy I saw buried wicked ones, who were fit to be hidden in the dust, for they were despised among the other nations, of whom it is said (Isaiah 23) “this is the people that was not,” and they ruled in the House of the Holy One, which is a holy place; and when they went from there to their land they would boast in their city that thus and thus they had done in the House of the Omnipresent. “Do not read *vayishtakchu* but *vayishtabbechu*” (they were praised) — so our Sages of blessed memory expounded it; and with regard to forgetting, so it is expounded in Aggadah: and in the end their name and memory will be forgotten from the city itself in which they did so, as it is said (Joel 4) “I will gather all nations into the valley of Jehoshaphat”; at the place where they blasphemed before Him He will exact payment from them; and so he says (Psalms 73) “O Lord, in the city Thou wilt despise their image.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 23” is Isaiah 23:13 (JPS: “this is the people that was not”); “Joel 4” is Joel 4:2 (JPS: “I will gather all nations”). Printed “Psalms 73” is Psalms 73:20 (JPS: “So, O Lord, when Thou arousest Thyself, Thou wilt despise their semblance”); the printed Hebrew of the quotation (צלננם ותבזה) looks garbled and is translated as “Thou wilt despise their image.”

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: this also is vanity
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Gam zeh* — one of the vanities delivered to the world to weary creatures: that the Holy One, blessed is He, is not quick to exact payment from the doers of evil, and creatures think there is no judgment and no judge.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Asher ein na'aseh pitgam* — the judgment of the evil deed is not quick, for the Holy One, blessed is He, is not quick to exact payment from the doers of evil, and therefore they think there is no judgment and their heart is filled within them to do evil.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Translated literally; the opening phrase is elliptical as printed.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: a sinner doeth evil a hundred times
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Asher chote* etc. — because they see that the sinner does evil a hundred thousand, tens of thousands of times, and the Holy One lengthens His patience for him and does not exact payment from him.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: a hundred times
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Me'at* — an elliptical verse (*mikra katzar*) joined to what precedes it, to say *me'at yamim, me'at shanim, me'at elef* (a hundred days, a hundred years, a hundred thousand); and so (Isaiah 21) “and drunken” (*ushekhurat*) — an elliptical and lacking verse: drunk with anger and not with wine like other drunkenness.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 21” is Isaiah 51:21 (JPS: “thou afflicted, And drunken, but not with wine”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: it shall be well with them that fear God
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki gam yode'a ani* — for even with all this, that He is not quick to exact payment from the wicked, so that there be a difference between the righteous and the wicked, I know that the end of each and every one is to receive his reward, and for those who fear Him it will be well, and good will not be to the wicked, because he does not fear before God.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: There is a vanity which is done upon the earth
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Yesh hevel* — a matter that alarms creatures.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: there are righteous men
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Asher yesh tzaddikim* — to whom evil reaches according to the deeds of the wicked, and there are wicked to whom good reaches according to the deeds of the righteous; I said that this too is one of the vanities that prevail in the world. And our Rabbis expounded it in a different direction in tractate Horayot, and it does not settle for me on the lines of the discourse, for the wise man concluded by saying that this too is vanity.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: I commended mirth
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Et hasimchah* — that he be glad in his portion and engage in upright precepts that gladden the heart, and not be given over to increasing wealth by interest (*neshekh*) and usury (*marbit*) and robbery; whoever is not glad in his portion and is given over to money comes to transgressions of robbery and overreaching (*ona'ah*) and interest; and whoever is not glad in his portion in regard to the love of his wife is given over to women, to ponder after a married woman.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: to eat, and to drink
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Le'echol uleshtot* — of what the Holy One, blessed is He, graciously gave him, and to rejoice in his portion; and Midrash Aggadah: every eating and drinking in Ecclesiastes is nothing but the study of Torah, as it is said (Isaiah 28) “Go, buy (*shivru*) and eat,” etc.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 28” is Isaiah 55:1 (JPS: “Come you, buy, and eat”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: should accompany him
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vehu yilvenu* — he will join with him, as it is said (there, 58) “and thy righteousness shall go before thee.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “there, 58” is Isaiah 58:8 (JPS: “Then shall thy light break forth as the morning… thy righteousness shall go before thee”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: all the days of his life which God hath given him under the sun
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Yemei chayav asher natan lo ha'Elohim* — he should do so; and the end of the verse refers back to its beginning, and it is a transposed verse: there is nothing good for a man, the days of his life that God gave him, except to eat and to drink and to rejoice, and it will accompany him in his labor.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: When I applied my heart to know wisdom
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ka'asher natati et libbi* — this *ka'asher* is not used in the sense of comparison, like *ka'asher asah ken ye'aseh* (as he did, so shall be done), but in the sense of time, as (Genesis 37) *ka'asher ba Yosef* (when Joseph came), when (there, 43) *kilu le'echol* (they had finished eating), etc. So here too: when I was setting my heart to know and to search, etc., then “I beheld all the work of God.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 37” is Genesis 37:23 and “there, 43” is Genesis 43:2.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: see sleep with their eyes
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Shenah be'einav einennu ro'eh* — the wicked man given over to money and forbidden unions.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: I beheld all the work of God
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Et kol ma'aseh ha'Elohim* — that He delivered to creatures. “That man cannot find out,” etc. — creatures cannot stand on the end of the ways of the Holy One, blessed is He, what is the reward of all the work done under the sun, for they see the wicked prospering and the righteous going down.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: though a man labour to seek it out
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Besheil asher ya'amol ha'adam levakesh* — because I saw many who toil to seek and to find the end of the measure, and they cannot.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: though a wise man think to know it
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vegam im yomar hachakham* — that he knows, he cannot; for Moses our Teacher, peace be upon him, did not stand on the matter, saying (Exodus 33) “Make known to me Thy ways.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Exodus 33” is Exodus 33:13 (JPS: “show me now Thy ways”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: to make clear
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Velavur* — and to clarify.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: For all this I laid to my heart
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Et kol zeh* — I clarified and discerned that the righteous and the wise and their servants are in the hand of God; He helps them and He judges them in order to benefit them in their end.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: and their works
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ve'avdeihem* — they are their students, their attendants, those who walk in their ways.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: whether it be love or hatred, man knoweth it not
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Gam ahavah gam sin'ah* — the rest of creatures do not know and do not recognize, so as to give heed, why they are loved by the Omnipresent and why they are hated.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: all is before them
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Hakol lifneihem* — before the righteous and the wise.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: All things come alike to all
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Hakol ka'asher lakol* — they all take to heart what reaches every man, that the end of the matter is to give to every man according to his ways.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: there is one event
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Mikreh echad* — and they know that the end of all, the righteous and the wicked, is to die, and there is one event in this world for all; all this they know, and nevertheless they choose for themselves the way of good, because they know that there is a difference between them in the World to Come.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: the righteous
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Latzaddik* — such as Noah.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: the wicked
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Larasha* — Pharaoh Necho: this one was made lame and that one was made lame.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: to the good
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Latov* — this is Moses.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: to the clean
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Latahor* — this is Aaron.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: to the unclean
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Velatame* — these are the spies: these said the praise of the Land of Israel and those said its disparagement; these did not enter the Land and those did not enter the Land; behold, one event for them.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: to him that sacrificeth
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Velazove'ach* — this is Josiah, as it is said (II Chronicles 37) “and Josiah sacrificed.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “II Chronicles 37” does not exist (II Chronicles has 36 chapters); the quoted words could not be located and are translated as printed.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: to him that sacrificeth not
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ula'asher einennu zove'ach* — this is Ahab, who prevented Israel from going up for the festival pilgrimage; this one died by arrows and that one died by arrows.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: as is the good
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Katov* — this is David.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: so is the sinner
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Kachote* — this is Nebuchadnezzar: this one built the Temple and that one destroyed it; this one reigned forty years and that one reigned forty years.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: he that sweareth
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Hanishba* — this is Zedekiah, who swore falsely, as it is said (II Chronicles 37) “and he also rebelled against king Nebuchadnezzar, who had made him swear,” etc.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “II Chronicles 37” is II Chronicles 36:13 (JPS: “And he also rebelled against king Nebuchadnezzar, who had made him swear by God”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: as he that feareth an oath
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ka'asher shevu'ah yare* — this is Samson, as it is said (Judges 13) “And Samson said to them: Swear to me, lest you fall upon me yourselves” — we learn that the oath was grave to him; this one died by the gouging out of eyes and that one died by the gouging out of eyes. Therefore:
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Judges 13” is Judges 15:12 (JPS: “Swear unto me, that you will not fall upon me yourselves”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: the heart of the sons of men is full of evil
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Lev bnei ha'adam male ra* — for they say there is no judgment and no punishment for the wicked; it is all only according to chance, sometimes to the righteous and sometimes to the wicked.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: after that they go to the dead
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ve'acharav el hametim* — and their end is that they go down to Gehinnom.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: For to him that is joined to all the living there is hope
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki mi asher yivchar* — to all the living there is trust (*bitachon*); for as long as he is alive, even if he is wicked and has joined the wicked, as it is said: to all the living, even to the wicked, there is trust, perhaps he will return before his death.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: a living dog is better than a dead lion
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki lekhelev chai hu tov min ha'aryeh hamet* — and both are wicked; it was good for Nebuzaradan, who was a wicked servant and converted, that death did not precede him from Nebuchadnezzar his master, who is called a lion, as it is said (Jeremiah 4) “A lion is gone up from his thicket”; and he died in his wickedness in Gehinnom, and his servant in the Garden of Eden. And our Rabbis expounded it with regard to cutting up a carcass before the dogs on the Sabbath, and a dead body lying in the sun, that it is forbidden to move it unless a child or a loaf has been placed upon it.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Jeremiah 4” is Jeremiah 4:7 (JPS: “A lion is gone up from his thicket”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: For the living know that they shall die
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki hachayyim yod'im shemutu* — and perhaps the day of death will return to their heart, and they will return from their way; but after they die they do not know anything, and there is no more reward for them, for deeds that they would do from death onward; rather, whoever toiled on the eve of the Sabbath shall eat on the Sabbath.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: their love
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Gam ahavatam* — that they loved simplicity and mockery.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: their hatred
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Gam sin'atam* — that they hated knowledge.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: their envy
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Gam kin'atam* — that they provoked the Holy One, blessed is He, to jealousy with the works of their hands.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: neither have they any more a portion for ever
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vechelek ein lahem* etc. — in all that is done etc.: the merit of a son and daughter did not help those wicked who worshipped idols [ע"א], and there is no atonement for them after death.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The abbreviation ע"א is read as “idolatry” from the context; the expansion is not confirmed by a permitted source, so the comment is flagged.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Go thy way, eat thy bread with joy
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Lekh ekhol besimchah* — but you, the righteous, since the Holy One, blessed is He, has already accepted your good deeds and you will merit the World to Come: go, eat with joy.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Let thy garments be always white
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Bekhol et yihyu begadekha levanim* — prepare yourself at every hour with a good deed, so that if you die today you will enter in peace. And Solomon the wise likened the matter to a man whom the king invited to a day of feast and did not fix a time for him: if he is wise or clever, he immediately launders his garment, washes and anoints himself; and so from tomorrow on until the time he is called to the feast, his garments will be white at every hour and he will be washed and anointed. So our Rabbis expounded it in tractate Shabbat.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Enjoy life with the wife whom thou lovest
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Re'eh chayyim im ishah asher ahavta* — see and understand to learn a trade by which to be supported, together with the study of Torah that is in your hand.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: for that is thy portion in life
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki hu chelkekha bachayyim* — if you did so, this will be your portion in life: in this world, to be supported by the trade, and in the World to Come, for the toil of both causes iniquity to be forgotten.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Whatsoever thy hand attaineth to do by thy strength
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Kol asher timtza yadekha la'asot* — the will of your Maker, while you are in your strength, do.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: there is no work, nor device
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki ein ma'aseh* etc. — in Sheol, to your merit, after you die; and if you did so, you have no reckoning in Sheol of which to worry; and so the verse is transposed: for there is no work, knowledge, or wisdom in Sheol for the wicked, and no reckoning for the righteous when sinners give judgment and reckoning. So it is expounded in the Midrash. And one who comes to explain it without transposition, according to its plain meaning, explains *cheshbon* as an expression of thought: what can he still do to be exempted from judgment?

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: I returned, and saw under the sun
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Shavti vera'oh* — like *zakhor*; וי"דונט in Old French.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Ecclesiastes 9:11 (“en regardant”), in forms such as ווידונט; the printed form (וי"דונט) is a variant spelling.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: the race is not to the swift
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Lo lakallim hamerotz* — his swiftness did not help Asahel when his appointed time arrived.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: nor the battle to the strong
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Velo lagibborim hamilchamah* — his might did not help Abner when his day arrived.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: neither yet bread to the wise
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vegam lo lachakhamim lechem* — such as I, whose bread for a day was (I Kings 4) “sixty measures of fine flour,” etc., and now this is my portion of all my toil: my staff and my cup.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “I Kings 4” is I Kings 4:22 in the Hebrew numbering (5:2 in JPS: “thirty measures of fine flour, and threescore measures of meal”); the printed wording differs from the verse.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: nor yet riches to men of understanding
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vegam lo lanevonim osher* — such as Job at first (Job 1) “and his possessions were,” etc.; when his time came he said (there, 19) “Have pity upon me, O you my friends.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Job 1” is Job 1:3 and “there, 19” is Job 19:21 (JPS: “Have pity upon me, have pity upon me, O you my friends”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: nor yet favour to men of skill
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Velo layode'im chen* — behold Moses, no one in Israel knew and understood more than he, and he did not find favor in his prayer that he enter the Land.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: but time and chance happeneth to them all
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki et vafega* — according to its plain meaning. Another explanation: “for a time will befall them,” and entreaty (*pegi'ah*) and supplication should be habitual with them, so that they not come to these things.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: as the fishes that are taken in an evil net
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Kadagim she'echazim bametzudah* — like large fish that are caught in a poor and weak net; and our Rabbis explained: it is a hook, which is only like a needle, and a large fish is caught by it.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: even so are the sons of men snared in an evil time
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Kehem yokshim bnei ha'adam* — by a small and weak stumbling-block, like the evil net and the snare, men stumble at the time of the reckoning of their evil, when their time comes for evil to fall upon them suddenly; in an evil net — מלאווי"שה in Old French.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Ecclesiastes 9:12 (“mauvais”), in forms such as מלווישא and מליישא; the printed form (מלאווי"שה) is a variant spelling.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: even so
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Kahem* — like them.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: yet no man remembered that same poor man
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ve'adam lo zakhar* — he did not count him as anything.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Wisdom is better than strength
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Va'amarti ani* — when I saw so: wisdom is better than strength, and behold, this man's wisdom is despised by all, and now all escaped through him. And Midrash Aggadah: “a little city” — this is the body.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Wisdom is better than strength
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ve'anashim bah me'at* — these are the limbs of a man.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The source lemma belongs to another verse of Ecclesiastes (9:14–15) and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Wisdom is better than strength
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Melekh gadol* — this is the evil inclination, of whom all the limbs are aware.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The source lemma belongs to another verse of Ecclesiastes (9:14–15) and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Wisdom is better than strength
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ish misken* — the good inclination.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The source lemma belongs to another verse of Ecclesiastes (9:14–15) and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: spoken in quiet
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Benachat nishma'im* — they are accepted by creatures.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: the cry of a ruler among fools
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Mize'akat moshel bakesilim* — the kings of the nations ע"א: Moses departed so many years ago and his decrees are still accepted by Israel, and how many kings of the nations decree decrees upon Israel and their words do not endure.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The abbreviation ע"א is left as printed and not resolved here.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Wisdom is better than weapons of war
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Tovah chokhmah mikeli krav* — the wisdom of Serah, as it is said (II Samuel 20) “And the woman came to the people in her wisdom”; it stood for them more than the weapons of war that they had to fight Joab.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “II Samuel 20” is II Samuel 20:22 (JPS: “Then the woman went unto all the people in her wisdom”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: But one sinner destroyeth much good
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vechote echad yeabbed tovah harbeh* — had she not killed Sheba son of Bichri, they would all have been lost through him. Another explanation: “and one sinner destroyeth much good” — behold, Israel were half righteous and half wicked, and one came and sinned and made them a majority; it turns out that he tipped all of them to guilt.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Dead flies make the ointment of the perfumer fetid and putrid
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Zevuvei mavet yav'ish yabia* etc. — such as in the days of winter, when flies have no strength and are near death; even if one comes into the oil of the perfumer and mixes with the spices, it makes it stink and raises foam, which they call *ascume* [printed אשקו"מא] in Old French, and it looks like blisters, and this is the meaning of *yabia*. Behold, a small thing spoiled an important thing; so a little folly is more precious (weighty) than wisdom and honor, for it tipped them all. Behold, a man was balanced between half sins and half merits, and came and committed one sin and it tipped him to the scale of guilt; it turns out that this folly, a small thing, is precious, and weighs and is heavier than all the wisdom and honor that were in him, for it tipped them all.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Ecclesiastes 10:1 (“fait écumer”), in forms such as אישקומא; the reading is *ascume* (REJ transcription of his first manuscript: *Askume*; Darmesteter’s footnote derives it from the verb *ascumer*); the printed form (אשקו"מא) is a variant spelling.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: a little folly outweigh wisdom and honour
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Yakar* — an expression of heaviness; it is heavy and weighs more than the wisdom and honor in him; and Midrash Aggadah likens the evil inclination to dead flies.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: fetid and putrid
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Yav'ish yabia* — a good name, which is sweeter than the oil of the perfumer.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: A wise man’s understanding is at his right hand
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Lev chakham liminno* — his wisdom is prepared to incline him to the practiced way, for his good.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: a fool’s understanding at his left
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ulev kesil lismolo* — to distort him from the practiced way, which is beautiful and comfortable for him.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: he saith to every one that he is a fool
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ve'amar lakol sakhal hu* — in his walking and in his speaking everyone recognizes that he is a fool.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: If the spirit of the ruler rise up against thee
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Im ru'ach hamoshel* — the Ruler of the world rises upon you to be exacting with you with the attribute of judgment.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Leave not thy place
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Mekomkha al tanach* — do not abandon your good attribute, to say to Him: what will my righteousness avail me?

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: For gentleness allayeth great offences
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki marpe* — the exactings of judgment in the sufferings that come upon you are a healing for your iniquities, and He will leave aside for you the great sins.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Like an error which proceedeth from a ruler
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Kishgagah sheyotze milifnei hashalit* — it is like a ruler who let out a matter of error from his mouth unwittingly, and it is impossible to retract; so says the Holy One, blessed is He, and there is no reply.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Folly is set on great heights
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Natan hasekhel bamromim rabbim* — this is the evil that is like an error that proceeds from the ruler: that folly and wickedness are placed in the heights of elevation, that the Holy One, blessed is He, exalted the fools and the wicked, for I see by the Holy Spirit that they are destined to stretch out a hand in His Sanctuary and to set their signs for signs.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: the rich sit in low place
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ve'ashirim bashefel yeshevu* — Israel, whose entire greatness and honor now in my days — they are destined to sit in lowness, as it is said (Lamentations 2) “They sit upon the ground, they keep silence.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Lamentations 2” is Lamentations 2:10 (JPS: “They sit upon the ground, and keep silence”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: I have seen servants upon horses
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ra'iti avadim al susim* — these are the Chaldeans, of whom it is said (Isaiah 23) “this is the people that was not”; they will be exalted to be on horses, leading the captives of Israel bound in collars.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 23” is Isaiah 23:13 (JPS: “this is the people that was not”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: walking as servants upon the earth
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Holekhim ka'avadim al ha'aretz* — before the carriages of the Chaldeans.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: He that diggeth a pit
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Chofer gummatz* — a pit.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: shall fall into it
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Bo yippol* — sometimes he falls into it; that is: you have one who plots evil, and in the end it returns upon him, as the seed of Nebuchadnezzar was cut off through the vessels of the Temple, as it is said (Daniel 8) “and against the Lord of heaven you have lifted yourself up.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Daniel 8” is Daniel 5:23 (JPS: “but hast lifted up thyself against the Lord of heaven”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: whoso breaketh through a fence
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Poretz gader* — the fence of the Sages, to transgress their words.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: a serpent shall bite him
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Yishkhenu nachash* — death at the hands of Heaven; and because he spoke in the language of breaking a fence, he mentioned in completion the language of a snake bite, which dwells in the holes and crevices of the walls of breached houses.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Whoso quarrieth stones
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Masia avanim ya'atzev bahem* — one who removes stones from their quarry in the mountains toils for them.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: is endangered thereby
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ye'atzev* — an expression of toil, like (Genesis 3) “in toil shalt thou eat of it,” that is: every man according to his work is his toil; so too the doer of evil: according to his sowing he reaps. *Yiskan bam* — he shall be warmed by them, as (I Kings 1) “and she was a companion (*soknet*) to him”; so too one who engages in Torah and commandments, in the end he will benefit from them.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 3” is Genesis 3:17 (JPS: “in toil shalt thou eat of it”); “I Kings 1” is I Kings 1:2 (JPS: “be a companion unto him”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: If the iron be blunt
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Im kahah habarzel* — flint swords whose edges and sharpness have grown dull.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: do not whet the edge
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vehu lo fanim kilkal* — and they are not polished and burnished (Ezekiel 21) “that it may glitter” (*lema'an heyot lahem barak*); nevertheless “and armies will prevail” — he strengthens in battle the mighty men of the armies to win.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Ezekiel 21” is Ezekiel 21:15 (JPS: “It is furbished that it may glitter”); the printed wording differs from the verse. The printed אע"פכ (“nevertheless”) appears to be a misprint.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: But wisdom is profitable to direct
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Veyitron hakhshēr chokhmah* — and the superiority of skill is yet in wisdom more than in iron: if a Torah scholar blackens his face with hunger and you see him poor among the rich, many armies are strengthened through him; and do not wonder at the vav of *vechayalim*, for many vavs fall thus in the Hebrew language, as (Psalms 3) “If thou sawest a thief, thou didst run with him”; (Exodus 15) “The Lord is my strength and song, and He became my salvation”; and many are explained like this.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Psalms 3” is Psalms 50:18 (JPS: “When thou sawest a thief, thou hadst company with him”) and “Exodus 15” is Exodus 15:2 (JPS: “The LORD is my strength and song, And He is become my salvation”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: If the serpent bite
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Im yishokh hanachash* — a man.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: before it is charmed
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Bela lachash* — because the charmer had not charmed it so that it not bite.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Then the charmer hath no advantage
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ve'ein yitron* — to the wicked charmer who was accustomed to charm it, without a charm. So too, if the people of your city stumble in prohibitions because there is no sage to expound to them and teach them the statutes of the Torah, there is no advantage to him in his silence and he will not profit.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Translated literally; the first sentence is difficult as printed.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: The words of a wise man’s mouth are gracious
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Divrei fi chakham chen* — upon those who hear them and who listen to him, and it is good for him, for he takes greatness over them.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: the lips of a fool will swallow up himself
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Usfatot kesil tevalle'ennu* — this is one who incites his fellow away from the good way, such as Balaam, who breached the fence of the nations, who had fenced themselves off from forbidden unions from the generation of the Flood onward, and he advised them to abandon their wives to harlotry.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: The beginning of the words of his mouth is foolishness
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Techillat divrei fihu sikhlut* — when the Holy One, blessed is He, said to him (Numbers 22) “What men are these with thee?” he should have answered “Thou, Lord, knowest,” but he said “Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab, hath sent unto me” — that is: if in Your eyes I am despised, I am important in the eyes of the kings of the earth.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Numbers 22” is Numbers 22:9–10 (JPS: “What men are these with thee?”; “Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab, hath sent unto me”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: the end of his talk is grievous madness
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ve'acharit pihu holelut* — stupidity and confusion: “Come, I will advise you” — schemes of folly.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The quoted words are Numbers 24:14 (JPS: “come, and I will announce to thee what this people shall do to thy people”); no reference is printed.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: A fool also multiplieth words
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vehassakhal yarbeh devarim* — for he boasted of himself that he knew the knowledge of the Most High; “for man does not know what will be.” To him after a time, for he went to take his reward in Midian and did not know that he would fall by the sword; and according to its plain meaning: the fool multiplies words, decrees and says, tomorrow I will do thus to so-and-so, and does not know what will be tomorrow.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The sentence “To him after a time” is translated literally.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: that which shall be after him
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Va'asher yihyeh me'acharav mi yaggid lo* — that is: not only that he does not know what will be after a time, but even the present, now, behind him — not before his eyes but behind his neck, at a distance — he needs someone to tell him.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: The labour of fools wearieth every one of them
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Amal hakesilim tiyge'ennu* — their folly causes them toil that wearies, those who have not learned the ways of the entrances of the city, and toil to enter by way of pits and marshes of water, and weary themselves with the print of their feet in the mire; that is, the laziness of those who abandon the Torah causes them the weariness of toil in Gehinnom, who know not how to walk to the path of truth to turn away from transgression, because they did not learn Torah, as it is said (Psalms 119) “Thy word is a lamp unto my feet.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Psalms 119” is Psalms 119:105 (JPS: “Thy word is a lamp unto my feet”); the printed word order differs from the verse.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Woe to thee, O land, when thy king is a boy
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ei lakh eretz shemalkhekh* — when your king and your judges conduct themselves childishly.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: In strength, and not in drunkenness
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Big'vurah velo vashti* — they occupy themselves with the might of wisdom and understanding, and not with the drinking of wine.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: By slothfulness the rafters sink in
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Be'atzaltayim yimakh hamekareh* — when a man is lazy and does not repair a small breach in the roof of the house.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: the rafters sink in
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Yimakh hamekareh* — the structure that roofs the house and covers it will sink.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: the house leaketh
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Yidlof* — will drip, a dripping of rain; that is, when Israel are lazy in Torah, they waste away, and the house of the pride of their strength is ruined and sinks.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: A feast is made for laughter
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: [*Lischok osim lechem* — for laughter they make a feast. For the joy of *mizmutei* bridegrooms and kings they make a banquet, and an unspecified great banquet is called *lechem* (“bread”), as you say (Daniel 5) “Belshazzar the king made a great feast” (*lechem rav*). And wine —] drinks at the banquet, which cheer the living.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The source gives no separate lemma; the printed comment begins with the verse's words, and the lemma shown is the corresponding phrase of the verse. The source prints the first part of the comment inside the lemma brackets; the word *mizmutei* is left untranslated. Printed “Daniel 5” is Daniel 5:1 (JPS: “Belshazzar the king made a great feast to a thousand of his lords”); the printed Aramaic wording is translated as printed.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: money answereth all things
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vehakesef ya'aneh et hakol* — if there is no money there is no banquet; therefore a man should not be lazy at work, so that he will have something to spend.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Curse not the king, no, not in thy thought
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Gam bemadda'akha melekh* — even in your thoughts, without speech; “even a king do not curse”: do not provoke the King of the world. Another explanation: according to its plain meaning, a king of flesh and blood.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: a bird of the air shall carry the voice
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Of hashamayim* — the soul given within you, which is destined to fly above the heavens.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: that which hath wings shall tell the matter
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Uva'al* — *kenafayim*: the angel who accompanies you, as it is said (Psalms 91) “for He will give His angels charge over thee”; and according to its plain meaning, those who pass by and return: you must worry about every creature, lest there be hearers who will tell others.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Psalms 91” is Psalms 91:11 (JPS: “For He will give His angels charge over thee”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Cast thy bread upon the waters
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Shelach lachmekha al penei hamayim* — do good and kindness to a man of whom your heart tells you: you will not see him again, like a man who throws his provisions on the surface of the water.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: thou shalt find it after many days
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki berov hayamim timtza'ennu* — more days are coming and you will receive your payment. See what is said of Jethro (Exodus 2) “call him, that he may eat bread” — and he thought that he was an Egyptian and that he would not see him again; what was his end? He became his son-in-law, and he reigned over Israel, and brought him in under the wings of the Divine Presence, and his sons and his sons' sons merited to sit in the Chamber of Hewn Stone.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Exodus 2” is Exodus 2:20 (JPS: “call him, that he may eat bread”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Divide a portion into seven, yea, even into eight
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ten chelek lesiv'ah vegam lishmonah* — divide of your bread and of what is yours among seven who need kindness; divide further for eight who will come after them, and do not say, enough.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: For thou knowest not what evil shall be upon the earth
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki lo teda mah yihyeh ra'ah* — perhaps more days are coming and you will need them all, or you will be saved by charity from the evil; and if not now, when? And our Rabbis said: “Give a portion,” etc.: these are the seven days of creation — give one of them as a portion to your Maker, to rest on the Sabbath; “and also to eight” — these are the eight days of circumcision. Another explanation: give a portion to seven — the public offerings of the seven days of Passover, “and also to eight” — of the eight days of the Festival.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The printed text reads לטבעה, which appears to be a misprint for לשבעה (“to seven”); it is translated as “to seven.”

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: upon the earth
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki lo teda mah yihyeh ra'ah* — if the Temple is destroyed and you will no longer offer; and they will profit, and his wisdoms and the measures of his contributions and the payment of good to the inhabitants of the place for the good conduct by which he led them in an upright way.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Translated literally; the printed sentence is difficult and its construction is not resolved here.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: upon the earth
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Yippol* — will dwell, like (Genesis 25) “over against all his brethren he settled” (*nafal*).
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 25” is Genesis 25:18 (JPS: “over against all his brethren he did settle”). The source lemma belongs to the next verse (Ecclesiastes 11:3) and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: upon the earth
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Etz* — a Torah scholar who protects by his merit, like a tree that gives shade over the earth.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The source lemma belongs to the next verse (Ecclesiastes 11:3) and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: He that observeth the wind
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Shomer ruach* — waits and looks out until the wind comes.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: shall not sow
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Lo yizra* — sometimes he waits and it does not come.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: he that regardeth the clouds shall not reap
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ure'eh ba'avim* — he sets his eyes on the clouds, and when he sees them dark he is afraid to harvest because of the rains, and he never reaps because he is always afraid.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: As thou knowest not what is the way of the wind
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ka'asher einkha yode'a; ka'atzamim babeten hamele'ah* — things that are shut up and ossified in a belly that is full, even though it protrudes outward. “As you do not know” — behold, this is a transposed verse, expounded from its end to its beginning: “As you do not know the way of the wind” — that is: the knowledge of these two is equal; neither this is revealed to you nor this is revealed to you. Sometimes you think to recognize in the clouds that the wind will come, and it does not come here, for it passes by and goes to another land. And this language is like (Genesis 13) “like the garden of the Lord, like the land of Egypt,” (Isaiah 24) “as the maid, so her mistress; as the buyer, so the seller”; and sometimes it equates the earlier to the later and sometimes the later to the earlier; so here too he learned the knowledge of the wind from the knowledge of the belly, that is: you have no need to watch the wind, to look at the clouds. (Gloss: This matter is transposed and inverted in the words of Rashi, and it needs to be emended according to what is in the exact books, and then it will be understood well, and thus is the true text:
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 13” is Genesis 13:10 (JPS: “like the garden of the LORD, like the land of Egypt”) and “Isaiah 24” is Isaiah 24:2 (JPS: “As with the maid, so with her mistress; As with the buyer, so with the seller”); the printed wording of the latter differs. The bracketed gloss that begins “This matter is transposed” is a later editorial insertion; the corrected text follows in the next comment.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: As thou knowest not what is the way of the wind
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ka'asher einkha yode'a* — behold, this is a transposed verse, expounded from its end to its beginning: “As you do not know the bones in the full belly” — things that are shut up and ossified in the full belly, and even though it protrudes outward you do not know what is in her belly; so you do not know the way of the wind; that is, the knowledge of these two is equal, etc. Siftei Chakhamim.)
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The closing parenthesis and the words “Siftei Chakhamim” (the name of a later commentary) are later printed insertions and are translated as printed.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: how the bones do grow
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ka'atzamim* — אינק"לישורש in Old French; *kino otzem einav*.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Ecclesiastes 11:5 (“comme les choses enfermées”), in forms such as אינקלושוריש and אינקלוטורש; the printed form (אינק"לישורש) is a variant spelling. The closing words are left in transliteration and not resolved.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Even so thou knowest not the work of God
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Kakhah lo teda* etc. — even the decrees of the Omnipresent regarding poverty and wealth are thus concealed from you, and you should not withhold from kindness out of worry: perhaps I shall lack from my possessions and become poor; I will not engage in Torah and neglect my work and become poor; I will not marry a wife, and I will have sons and need to spend on them.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: In the morning sow thy seed
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Baboker zera et zar'ekha* etc. — if you learned Torah in your youth, learn Torah in your old age; if you had students in your youth, you will have students in your old age; if you married a wife who bears sons in your youth, marry a wife who bears sons in your old age; if you gave charity in your youth, give charity in your old age.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: which shall prosper
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki einkha yode'a ei zeh yikhshar* — whether the students and sons of your youth will endure for you or perhaps not, but only those of your old age. We find of Rabbi Akiva that he had twenty-four thousand students from Gevat to Antipatris, and all of them died from Passover to Shavuot, and he came to our Rabbis of the south and taught it to them. And regarding sons, we find of Ibzan that he sent thirty daughters outside and brought thirty for his sons, and all of them died in his lifetime, and in his old age he begot Obed and he endured for him.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: And the light is sweet
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Umatok ha'or* — sweet is the light of the Torah.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: a pleasant thing it is for the eyes to behold the sun
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vetov la'einayim lir'ot et hashamesh* — and happy are the students whose eyes see a halakhah made clear and made plain on its basis; so it is expounded in Aggadat Tehillim.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Let him rejoice in them all
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Bekhullam yismach* — let him be glad in his portion, provided that he remembers the days of darkness and improves his deeds so as to be saved from them, which are the days of the death of the world — they are the days of the wicked.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: For they shall be many
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki harbeh yihyu* — in those days, more than the days of life.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: All that cometh is vanity
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Kol shebba* — upon him will be vanity and darkness; there is a vanity that is an expression of punishment and troubles, as (Ecclesiastes 6) “for in vanity it came, and in darkness it goes.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The quoted words are Ecclesiastes 6:4 (JPS: “for it cometh in vanity, and departeth in darkness”); no reference is printed.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Rejoice, O young man, in thy youth
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Sameach bachur beyalduteikha* — like a man who says to his servant and his son: sin, sin, for once you will be punished for everything; so here the wise man said: “rejoice, O young man, in thy childhood, and walk in the ways of thy heart” and be in good; “but know thou that for all these things God will bring thee into judgment.”

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: remove vexation from thy heart
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vehaser ka'as* — matters that anger the Omnipresent.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: put away evil from thy flesh
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Veha'aver ra'ah* — the evil inclination.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: from thy flesh
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Mibesarekha* — that you have a heart of flesh.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: childhood and youth
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vehashacharut* — youth, for a man's head is black in the days of his youth.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Remember then thy Creator
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Uzkhor et bore'ekha* — there we learned: Akavya ben Mahalalel says: look at three things, etc.; and from this verse he expounded: “and remember your Creator” — that you will give judgment and reckoning before Him; “remember your pit (*borekha*)” — your grave, a place of dust, worm and maggot; “remember your well (*be'erekha*)” — a well that gushes from its source, which is a putrid drop of semen and of whiteness.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The Mishnah cited is Avot 3:1; it is not named in the printed text.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Before the evil days come
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Yemei hara'ah* — the days of old age and weakness.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Before the sun
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ad asher lo techeshakh hashemesh* — our Rabbis said: this is the forehead, which is lit up and *metzahevet* in a young man, and when he grows old it raises wrinkles and is not *metzahevet*.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The word *metzahevet* (from the root for “yellow”) is left untranslated.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: and the light
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Veha'or* — this is the nose, which is the form of the facial features.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: and the moon
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vehayarei'ach* — this is the soul that gives light to a man, for once it is taken from him he has no light of the eyes.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: And the stars
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vehakokhavim* — these are the jaws, *rummanei de'appei*, which they call פומ"ליש, of the cheeks, which turn yellow.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Ecclesiastes 12:2 (“les pommettes (du visage)”), in forms such as פומיילש and פומיילוש; the printed form (פומ"ליש) is a variant spelling.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: And the clouds return after the rain
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Veshavu he'avim achar hagashem* — a dimming of the light will come after the tears of weeping from the many troubles that passed over him.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: shall tremble
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Sheyazu'u* — they will be agitated.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: the keepers of the house
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Shomrei habayit* — these are the ribs and the loins that protect the entire cavity of the body.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: shall bow themselves
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vehit'otu* — a cramp (*ivvut*) will seize it, which they call קראנ"פף; “and they shall be contorted”: אנקרופי"רונט in Old French.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Ecclesiastes 12:3 (“et seront saisis de crampe”), in forms such as קרנפא and איכקרנפירונטא; the printed forms (קראנ"פף, אנקרופי"רונט) are variant spellings.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: the strong men
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Anshei hachayil* — these are the legs, on which the whole body leans.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: And the grinders cease
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Uvatelu hatochanot* — these are the teeth.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: because they are few
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki ma'atu* — at the time of old age most of his teeth fall out.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: those that look out
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Haro'ot ba'arubot* — these are the eyes.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: the doors shall be shut in the street
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vesugeru delatayim* — these are his orifices.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: When the sound of the grinding is low
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Bishfal kol hatachanah* — the sound of the mills that grind the food that is in his bowels, which is the *korkevan* and the *masas*.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The terms *korkevan* and *masas* are left untranslated.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: one shall start up at the voice of a bird
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Veyakum lekol hatzippor* — for even the voice of a bird rouses him from his sleep when he has grown old.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: all the daughters of music shall be brought low
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Veyishachu kol benot hashir* — all the sounds of musical instruments seem to him like speech (*sichah*); and according to its plain meaning, *yishachu* means “be lowered”: all singers, male and female, will be low in his eyes; and so Barzillai the Gileadite said to David (II Samuel 19) “if I hear any more the voice of singing men and singing women.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “II Samuel 19” is II Samuel 19:36 (JPS: “can I hear any more the voice of singing men and singing women?”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Also when they shall be afraid of that which is high
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Gam migavoha yira'u* — of bumps and mounds in the streets he worries when going out to the market, lest he stumble on them.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: And terrors shall be in the way
