Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vachatachtim baderekh* — he has many terrors and fears on the roads.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: terrors
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Chatachtim* — a doubled form within the word, like *galgalim*, *kasekasim*, *zalzalim*.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: the almond-tree shall blossom
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Veyanetz hashaked* — an expression of (Song of Songs 7) “the pomegranates are in flower” (*hanetzu*), for the alef is not pronounced in it. Our Rabbis said: this is the *kelivoset*, הנק"א in Old French, in which the thighbone is fixed, and in his old age his flesh is lean and the bone sticks out like the blossom of a tree, which sticks out.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Ecclesiastes 12:5 (“hanche”), in forms such as הנקא; the printed form (הנק"א) matches. Printed “Song of Songs 7” is Song of Songs 7:13 (JPS: “the pomegranates be in flower”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: the almond-tree shall blossom
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Hashaked* — a tree of almonds; that is, old age will leap upon him like this almond, which hurries to blossom before all the trees.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The lemma shown is the corresponding phrase of the verse.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: the grasshopper shall drag itself along
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Veyistabbel hachagav* — these are the buttocks (*agavot*); his buttocks will seem to him like one who bears a heavy burden.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: the grasshopper shall drag itself along
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Veyistabbel* — אישד"רייד שורפיי"שין in Old French.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Ecclesiastes 12:5 (“et il sera surchargé”); the forms printed in the available text of his entry are partly illegible (such as אידאייריש פורפישיץ), so the printed form (אישד"רייד שורפיי"שין) is left as printed and not confirmed. The source lemma is the single word *veyistabbel*; the lemma shown is the corresponding phrase of the verse.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: the caperberry shall fail
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vetafer ha'evyonah* — the desire of the lust for women, that he is not drawn to women for intercourse. *Evyonah* is desire, like (Deuteronomy 1) “and you would not” (*velo avitem*), (Psalms 119) “I have longed for Thy salvation.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Deuteronomy 1” is Deuteronomy 1:26 (JPS: “Yet you would not go up”) and “Psalms 119” is Psalms 119:174 (JPS: “I have longed for Thy salvation, O LORD”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: the silver cord is snapped asunder
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ad asher lo yeratek chevel hakesef* — this is the spinal cord, which is white like silver; at his death his marrow is lacking and empties and dries and stiffens within the vertebrae and becomes like a chain. *Yeratek* is an expression of *retukot* (“chains”) of silver.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: the golden bowl is shattered
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vetarutz gullat hazahav* — this is the male organ, which used to spurt water and well up like a spring, like “bowls” (*gullot*) above; *vetarutz* is an expression of crushing (*retzitzah*).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: the pitcher is broken at the fountain
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vetishaver kad al hamavu'a* — this is the belly, which is thick and splits at his death.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: the wheel falleth shattered, into the pit
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Venarotz hagalgal el habor* — the eyeball will be crushed within its socket. And according to its plain meaning, it is the wheel of the drawers, with which water is drawn from the well. So the entire matter is expounded in tractate Shabbat, and the Midrash on Lamentations interprets it as referring to all of Israel: “Remember your Creator in the days of your youth (*bechurotekha*)” — while your chosen state (*habechurot*) still stands: while the priesthood still stands, as it is said (Isaiah 40) “and to choose him out of all the tribes of Israel to be My priest”; while the Levites still stand, as it is said (Deuteronomy 11) “for the Lord thy God has chosen him out of all thy tribes”; while the kingdom of the house of David still stands, as it is said (Psalms 78) “and He chose David His servant”; while Jerusalem still stands, of which it is said (I Kings 11) “the city which I have chosen”; while the Chosen House still stands, of which it is said (II Chronicles 15) “now I have chosen and hallowed this house”; while you still exist, as it is said (Deuteronomy 14) “and the Lord has chosen thee.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 40” is I Samuel 2:28 (JPS: “And did I choose him out of all the tribes of Israel to be My priest”); “Deuteronomy 11” is Deuteronomy 18:5 (JPS: “For the LORD thy God hath chosen him out of all thy tribes”); “Psalms 78” is Psalms 78:70 (JPS: “He chose David also His servant”); “I Kings 11” is I Kings 11:32 (JPS: “the city which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel”); “II Chronicles 15” is II Chronicles 7:16 (JPS: “For now have I chosen and hallowed this house”); “Deuteronomy 14” is Deuteronomy 14:2 (JPS: “the LORD hath chosen thee”). The printed wording of several of these differs from the verse. The Midrash on Lamentations is named as printed. Located in the Hebrew Tanakh: ובחר אותו מכל שבטי ישראל is I Samuel 2:28 (printed “Isaiah 40”); ויבחר בדוד עבדו is Psalms 78:70; העיר אשר בחרתי is I Kings 11:32 (also 11:36); עתה בחרתי והקדשתי is II Chronicles 7:16 (printed “15”, and the verse reads ועתה). Audit 5, with the Torah Hebrew text now available: כי בו בחר is Deuteronomy 18:5 (printed “Deuteronomy 11”) and ובך בחר is Deuteronomy 14:2 (printed “14” is the chapter, correct).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Before the silver cord is snapped asunder
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ad asher lo yavo'u yemei hara'ah* — these are the days of the exile.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The source lemma belongs to an earlier verse of the chapter (Ecclesiastes 12:2–5), as this passage repeats the sequence of verses with a second exposition, and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Before the silver cord is snapped asunder
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ad shelo techeshakh hashemesh* — this is the kingdom of the house of David, as it is said (Psalms 89) “and his throne as the sun before Me.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Psalms 89” is Psalms 89:37 (JPS: “And his throne as the sun before Me”). The source lemma belongs to an earlier verse of the chapter (Ecclesiastes 12:2–5), as this passage repeats the sequence of verses with a second exposition, and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Before the silver cord is snapped asunder
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Veha'or* — this is the Torah, as it is said (Proverbs 6) “for the commandment is a lamp, and the Torah is light.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Proverbs 6” is Proverbs 6:23 (JPS: “For the commandment is a lamp, and the teaching is light”). The source lemma belongs to an earlier verse of the chapter (Ecclesiastes 12:2–5), as this passage repeats the sequence of verses with a second exposition, and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Before the silver cord is snapped asunder
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vehayarei'ach* — this is the Sanhedrin, as we learned: the Sanhedrin was like half of a round threshing-floor.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The Mishnah cited is Sanhedrin 4:3; it is not named in the printed text. The source lemma belongs to an earlier verse of the chapter (Ecclesiastes 12:2–5), as this passage repeats the sequence of verses with a second exposition, and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Before the silver cord is snapped asunder
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vehakokhavim* — these are the Rabbis, as it is said (Daniel 12) “and they that turn the many to righteousness as the stars.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Daniel 12” is Daniel 12:3 (JPS: “and they that turn the many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever”). The source lemma belongs to an earlier verse of the chapter (Ecclesiastes 12:2–5), as this passage repeats the sequence of verses with a second exposition, and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Before the silver cord is snapped asunder
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Veshavu he'avim achar hagashem* — trouble after severe trouble. You find that all the harsh prophecies that Jeremiah prophesied against them came upon them only after the destruction of the Temple.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The source lemma belongs to an earlier verse of the chapter (Ecclesiastes 12:2–5), as this passage repeats the sequence of verses with a second exposition, and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Before the silver cord is snapped asunder
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Bayom sheyaz'u shomrei habayit* — these are the priestly and Levitical watches.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The source lemma belongs to an earlier verse of the chapter (Ecclesiastes 12:2–5), as this passage repeats the sequence of verses with a second exposition, and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Before the silver cord is snapped asunder
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vehit'avvetu anshei hachayil* — these are the priests, who are mighty in strength. Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said: Aaron waved twenty-two thousand Levites in one day. Rabbi Chanina said: this *morah* is a light matter, and the priest throws it more than thirty cubits.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The word *morah* is left untranslated. The source lemma belongs to an earlier verse of the chapter (Ecclesiastes 12:2–5), as this passage repeats the sequence of verses with a second exposition, and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Before the silver cord is snapped asunder
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Uvatelu hatochanot* — these are the great Mishnayot: the Mishnah of Rabbi Akiva, the Mishnah of Rabbi Chiyya and the Mishnah of Bar Kappara.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The source lemma belongs to an earlier verse of the chapter (Ecclesiastes 12:2–5), as this passage repeats the sequence of verses with a second exposition, and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Before the silver cord is snapped asunder
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vechashkhu haro'ot* — that the Gemara will be forgotten from the heart.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The source lemma belongs to an earlier verse of the chapter (Ecclesiastes 12:2–5), as this passage repeats the sequence of verses with a second exposition, and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Before the silver cord is snapped asunder
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vesugeru delatayim bashuk* — such as the doors of Nechushta ben Elnatan, which were wide open.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The name is translated as printed. In II Kings 24:8 (JPS) the name appears as “Nehushta the daughter of Elnathan”; the printed text reads “ben.” The source lemma belongs to an earlier verse of the chapter (Ecclesiastes 12:2–5), as this passage repeats the sequence of verses with a second exposition, and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Before the silver cord is snapped asunder
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Bishfal kol hatachanah* — because they did not engage in Torah. Rabbi Shmuel said: Israel were likened to the grinding of mills; as mills are not idle, neither by day nor by night, so here (Joshua 1) “and thou shalt meditate therein day and night.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Joshua 1” is Joshua 1:8 (JPS: “but thou shalt meditate therein day and night”). The source lemma belongs to an earlier verse of the chapter (Ecclesiastes 12:2–5), as this passage repeats the sequence of verses with a second exposition, and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Before the silver cord is snapped asunder
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Veyakum lekol hatzippor* — this is Nebuchadnezzar the wicked. Rabbi Levi said: for eighteen years a heavenly voice went forth and *mefotzetzet* in the palace of Nebuchadnezzar: “Wicked servant Nebuchadnezzar, go, destroy the house of your Master, for your Master's children do not listen to Him.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The word *mefotzetzet* is left untranslated; the Aramaic is translated as printed. The source lemma belongs to an earlier verse of the chapter (Ecclesiastes 12:2–5), as this passage repeats the sequence of verses with a second exposition, and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Before the silver cord is snapped asunder
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Veyishachu kol benot hashir* — (Isaiah 24) “they shall not drink wine with a song.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Isaiah 24” is Isaiah 24:9 (JPS: “They drink not wine with a song”). The source lemma belongs to an earlier verse of the chapter (Ecclesiastes 12:2–5), as this passage repeats the sequence of verses with a second exposition, and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Before the silver cord is snapped asunder
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Gam miggavoha yira'u* — from the height of the world he will be afraid, and his heart will worry lest it be done to him as it was done to those before.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The source lemma belongs to an earlier verse of the chapter (Ecclesiastes 12:2–5), as this passage repeats the sequence of verses with a second exposition, and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Before the silver cord is snapped asunder
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vachatachtim baderekh* — because of this he will seek for himself signs and hints whether he will succeed on the way he goes, as in the matter that is said (Ezekiel 21) “for the king of Babylon stood at the parting of the way, at the head of the two ways, to use divination: he shook the arrows, he inquired of the teraphim.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Ezekiel 21” is Ezekiel 21:26 (JPS: “For the king of Babylon standeth at the parting of the way, at the head of the two ways, to use divination; he shaketh the arrows to and fro, he inquireth of the teraphim, he looketh in the liver”); the printed wording differs from the verse. The source lemma belongs to an earlier verse of the chapter (Ecclesiastes 12:2–5), as this passage repeats the sequence of verses with a second exposition, and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Before the silver cord is snapped asunder
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Veyanetz hashaked* — the prophecy of Jeremiah will sprout, as it is said (Jeremiah 1) “I see a rod of an almond-tree.” Rabbi Eliezer said: this almond, from the time it blossoms until its fruits are complete, is twenty-one days; so from the seventeenth of Tammuz to the ninth of Av, twenty-one days.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Jeremiah 1” is Jeremiah 1:11 (JPS: “I see a rod of an almond-tree”). The source lemma belongs to an earlier verse of the chapter (Ecclesiastes 12:2–5), as this passage repeats the sequence of verses with a second exposition, and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Before the silver cord is snapped asunder
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Veyistabbel hachagav* — this is the image of Nebuchadnezzar (Daniel 3): “its height sixty cubits, its width six cubits.” And if its thickness is not six, it cannot stand; and you say he set it up in the plain of Dura? Rav Bibi said: they set it up and it falls, set it up and it falls, until they brought all the gold that was in Jerusalem and poured *dimus* on its feet, to fulfil what is said (Ezekiel 7) “and their gold shall be as an unclean thing and for tribute (*mas*).”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Daniel 3” is Daniel 3:1 (JPS, in English: “whose height was threescore cubits, and the breadth thereof six cubits; he set it up in the plain of Dura”); the printed Aramaic is translated as printed. Printed “Ezekiel 7” is Ezekiel 7:19 (JPS: “their gold shall be as an unclean thing”); the printed words “and for tribute” have no equivalent in the JPS verse. The word *dimus* is left untranslated. The source lemma belongs to an earlier verse of the chapter (Ecclesiastes 12:2–5), as this passage repeats the sequence of verses with a second exposition, and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Before the silver cord is snapped asunder
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vetafer ha'evyonah* — this is the merit of the fathers; it *tofer* the support of the fathers, “shelakh” (?); and “*evyonah*” will be from the expression of *av* (“father”).
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The printed sentence is difficult (the word after “support of the fathers” is abbreviated or corrupt) and is translated literally. The source lemma belongs to an earlier verse of the chapter (Ecclesiastes 12:2–5), as this passage repeats the sequence of verses with a second exposition, and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Before the silver cord is snapped asunder
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki holekh ha'adam* — Israel, who are called a flock: “you are men.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The quoted words are Ezekiel 34:31 (JPS: “And you My sheep, the sheep of My pasture, are men”); no reference is printed. The source lemma belongs to an earlier verse of the chapter (Ecclesiastes 12:2–5), as this passage repeats the sequence of verses with a second exposition, and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Before the silver cord is snapped asunder
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *El beit olamo* — from Babylon they came, to Babylon they returned; Terach, the father of Abraham, was from across the river.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The source lemma belongs to an earlier verse of the chapter (Ecclesiastes 12:2–5), as this passage repeats the sequence of verses with a second exposition, and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Before the silver cord is snapped asunder
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vesovevu bashuk hasofedim* — the exile of Jeconiah preceded the exile of Zedekiah by eleven years. When Nebuchadnezzar exiled the exile of Zedekiah in *kolarin*, the exiles of Jeconiah went out against their will, with the rest of the people of the city, to meet Nebuchadnezzar and praise him, that he is mighty and successful; and they saw the captives and asked them, each man about his relative, what had been done to him; and they answered them (Jeremiah 15) “such as are for death, to death; and such as are for captivity, to captivity; and such as are for the sword, to the sword”; and they praised with one hand, and with the other hand they struck and clapped (*mesapkin umetapchin*), a lament for their brothers and their sons.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Jeremiah 15” is Jeremiah 15:2 (JPS: “Such as are for death, to death; and such as are for the sword, to the sword; and such as are for the famine, to the famine; and such as are for captivity, to captivity”); the printed wording and order differ. The word *kolarin* is left untranslated. The source lemma belongs to an earlier verse of the chapter (Ecclesiastes 12:2–5), as this passage repeats the sequence of verses with a second exposition, and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: the silver cord is snapped asunder
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ad asher lo yeratek chevel hakesef* — this is the chain of genealogy.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: the golden bowl is shattered
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vetarutz gullat hazahav* — these are the words of the Torah, as it is said (Psalms 19) “more to be desired than gold.”
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Printed “Psalms 19” is Psalms 19:11 (JPS: “More to be desired are they than gold”).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: the pitcher is broken at the fountain
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vetishaver kad al hamavu'a* — the jar of Baruch ben Neriah, by the fountain of Jeremiah, for both were exiled to Babylon and ceased from their study through the hardship of the road. First they were exiled to Egypt, for Johanan son of Kareah exiled them, and when Nebuchadnezzar destroyed Egypt he exiled them to Babylon.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: the wheel falleth shattered, into the pit
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Venarotz hagalgal el habor* — this is Babylon, which is the small part of the world (*zuto shel olam*).

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: And the dust returneth to the earth as it was
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Veyashov ha'afar* etc. — from Babylon they came, to Babylon they returned.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: the spirit returneth unto God who gave it
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Veharuach tashuv* — this is the Holy Spirit, for when the Holy Spirit departed, they were exiled.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Vanity of vanities
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Hevel havalim* — I see in the world.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: saith Koheleth
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Amar haKohelet* — he in whom is the gathering of wisdom.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: all is vanity
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Hevel havalim* — everything that was created in the six days of creation.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The source lemma (“Vanity of vanities”) is the first phrase of the verse and also occurs there; the lemma shown is the corresponding phrase for the comment's wording.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Koheleth was wise
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Veyoter shehayah Kohelet chakham* — and beyond what is written in this book, Koheleth was wise.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: he pondered
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ve'izzen* — he made handles (*oznayim*) for the Torah, like this basket which has no handles to hold it, and he came and made handles for it: for he instituted *eruvin* as a fence for the guarding of the Sabbath, and instituted the washing of hands as a fence for purity, and decreed the secondary relations as a fence for forbidden relations.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The lemma shown is the corresponding word of the verse.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: Koheleth sought to find out
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Bikkesh Kohelet* — he set his heart and returned to the matter and found it.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: words of delight
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Divrei chefetz* — a law given to Moses at Sinai.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: that which was written uprightly
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vekhatuv yosher* — this is the written Torah and the Prophets.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: The words of the wise
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Divrei chakhamim* — who made a fence around the Torah by decrees, to keep a man far from transgression, such as the eating of sacrifices until dawn, which they said until midnight, and the reading of the Shema in the evening likewise.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: as goads
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Kadarvanot* — as this goad directs the cow to its furrow, so their words direct a man to the ways of life.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: as nails well fastened
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vekhamasmerot netu'im* — as this nail is fixed, so their words are fixed; and as a planting is fruitful and multiplies, so their words are fruitful and multiply, to find a reason in them.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The printed lemma reads *vekhamishmerot*, but the verse (JPS: “as nails well fastened”) has *masmerot*, and the comment's explanation speaks of a nail; the lemma is translated accordingly.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: composed in collections
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ba'alei asufot* — nails that have a gathered, thick head, *grose* [printed גרו"סה] in Old French (thick); so explained Dunash ben Labrat.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Ecclesiastes 12:11 (“des clous à grosse tête”), in forms such as גרושא and גרישא; the reading *grose* is from Darmesteter’s index; the printed form (גרו"סה) is a variant spelling.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: they are given from one shepherd
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Nittenu mero'eh echad* — all their words are the words of the living God; He spoke them, and one shepherd, Moses, gave them from the mouth of the Almighty.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: as nails well fastened
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Vekhamishmerot* — it is written with a *shin*, for the Torah is in twenty-four books, and like the number of the priestly and Levitical watches.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The printed lemma reads *vekhamishmerot* (“and like watches”); the verse (JPS: “as nails well fastened”) has *masmerot*. The comment explains the *shin* spelling, and is translated as printed.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: And furthermore, my son, be admonished
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Veyoter mehemmah beni hizzaher* — and beyond the upright words of truth, matters written in the books mentioned above.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: my son, be admonished
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Beni hizzaher* — to keep the words of the Sages; and if you say, if there is a need for them, why were they not written?

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: of making many books there is no end
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Asot sefarim harbeh ein ketz* — if we had come to write, we would not have sufficed.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The printed text has the first-person plural “we”; it is translated as printed.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: much study is a weariness of the flesh
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Velahag harbeh yegi'at basar* — and if to set the heart to the study of bundles beyond what the heart can grasp, it is a toil for people, for it cannot be grasped; and let him not say, since I cannot finish the work, why should I begin? But —
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The comment ends with a single word (“But”) that continues in the next verse's comment; translated as printed.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: fear God
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Sof davar hakol nishma et ha'Elohim yera* — what you can do, do, and let your heart be to Heaven.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: keep His commandments; for this is the whole man
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ve'et mitzvotav shemor ki zeh kol ha'adam* — for the whole man was created for this thing.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: For God shall bring every work into the judgment
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Ki et kol ma'aseh* — that a man does, God will bring into judgment; and for this *ma'aseh* is vowelled with a *patach*, and the accent is above, because it is not joined to the word after it.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The grammatical remark on the vowelling and accent of *ma'aseh* is translated literally; the printed phrase “the accent is above” is not resolved.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: concerning every hidden thing
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Al kol ne'lam* — even for the unintentional.

Ecclesiastes.english_lemma_JPS: whether it be good or whether it be evil
Ecclesiastes.english_translation: *Im tov ve'im ra* — even one who stumbled in a commandment, such as one who gives charity to a poor man publicly. “The end of the matter, all having been heard: fear God,” etc. Here ends Rashi's commentary on Ecclesiastes.
Ecclesiastes.translator_note: The closing words “Here ends Rashi's commentary on Ecclesiastes” are printed after the final verse quotation and are translated as printed.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: in the days of Ahasuerus
Esther.english_translation: *Vayehi bimei Achashverosh* — he was the king of Persia who reigned after Cyrus, at the end of the seventy years of the Babylonian exile.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: this is Ahasuerus
Esther.english_translation: *Hu Achashverosh* — he was wicked from his beginning to his end.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: who reigned
Esther.english_translation: *Hamelekh* — who became king of himself, and was not of the royal seed.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: from India even unto Ethiopia
Esther.english_translation: *Mehodu ve'ad Kush* etc. — who ruled over one hundred and twenty-seven provinces as he ruled from India to Cush, which stand next to each other; and so (I Kings 4) “for he ruled over all the region beyond the River, from Tiphsah to Gaza,” that he ruled over all the region beyond the River as he ruled from Tiphsah to Gaza.
Esther.translator_note: Printed “I Kings 4” is I Kings 5:4 (JPS: “For he had dominion over all the region on this side the River, from Tiphsah even to Gaza”); the printed wording differs.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: sat on the throne of his kingdom
Esther.english_translation: *Keshevet hamelekh Achashverosh* etc. — when the kingdom was established in his hand; and our Rabbis explained it in another way in tractate Megillah.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: the nobles
Esther.english_translation: *Hapartemim* — rulers, in the Persian language.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: many days
Esther.english_translation: *Yamim rabbim* — he made a feast for them.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: the court of the garden
Esther.english_translation: *Ginnat* — a place of seeds of vegetables.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: palace
Esther.english_translation: *Bitan* — planted with trees.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: hangings of white, fine cotton, and blue
Esther.english_translation: *Chur karpas utekhelet* — kinds of coloured garments that he spread for them as coverings.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: bordered with cords of fine linen and purple
Esther.english_translation: *Achuz bechavlei butz ve'argaman* — embroidered with cords of fine linen and purple; these he spread for them upon silver cylinders and upon pillars of marble.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: the couches were of gold and silver
Esther.english_translation: *Mittot zahav vakhesef* — he arranged them for sitting upon at the meal.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: upon a pavement of green, and white, and shell, and onyx marble
Esther.english_translation: *Al ritzpat* — floors of *bahat* and *shesh* etc.: kinds of precious stones; our Rabbis explained, and according to the sense of the verse, so is their name.
Esther.translator_note: The terms *bahat* and *shesh* are left untranslated.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: in vessels of gold
Esther.english_translation: *Vehashkot bikhlei zahav* — like “and to give drink” (*ulhashkot*).

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: the vessels being diverse one from another
Esther.english_translation: *Shonim* — different from one another; and so “and their laws are diverse” (Esther 3); and our Rabbis expounded what they expounded.
Esther.translator_note: The quoted words are Esther 3:8 (JPS: “and their laws are diverse from those of every people”); no reference is printed.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: royal wine in abundance
Esther.english_translation: *Veyayin malkhut rav* — much; and our Rabbis said that he gave each and every one of them wine that was older than himself.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: according to the law
Esther.english_translation: *Kadat* — because there are feasts at which the guests are compelled to drink a large vessel, and there is one who cannot drink it except with difficulty; but here there was no compulsion.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: the king had appointed
Esther.english_translation: *Yissad* — an expression of foundation (*yesod*); that is, so he ordained and commanded.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: all the officers of his house
Esther.english_translation: *Al kol rav beito* — over all the chiefs of the feast: the chief of the bakers, the chief of the cooks and the chief of the cupbearers.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: according to every man’s pleasure
Esther.english_translation: *La'asot kirtzon ish va'ish* — to each one, his desire.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: On the seventh day
Esther.english_translation: *Bayom hashevi'i* — our Rabbis said: it was the Sabbath.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: the queen Vashti refused to come
Esther.english_translation: *Vatema'en hamalkah Vashti* — our Rabbis said: because leprosy had broken out on her, so that she would refuse and be killed; because she used to strip the daughters of Israel naked and make them work on the Sabbath, it was decreed upon her that she be stripped naked on the Sabbath.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: therefore was the king very wroth
Esther.english_translation: *Vayiktzof* — because she had sent him words of disgrace.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: for so was the king’s manner
Esther.english_translation: *Ki khen devar hamelekh* — for it was the king's custom, in every judgment, to place the matter before all who know law and justice.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: the next unto him
Esther.english_translation: *Vehakarov elav* — to arrange his words before them. [These are Carshena, Shethar,” etc.
Esther.translator_note: The printed text has an opening bracket before the second sentence with no closing bracket; the stray bracket is left as printed.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: according to law
Esther.english_translation: *Kedat mah la'asot* — this refers back to “and the king said to the wise men.”

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: hath not done wrong to the king only
Esther.english_translation: *Avtah* — an expression of iniquity (*avon*).
Esther.translator_note: The printed lemma is *avtah*; the comment is translated as printed.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: this deed of the queen will come abroad unto all women
Esther.english_translation: *Ki yetze devar hamalkah al kol hanashim* — that she shamed the king before all the women, so that they too would shame their husbands.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: the princesses of Persia and Media
Esther.english_translation: *Tomarnah sharot Paras uMadai* — to all the king's princes, this thing; and behold, this is an abbreviated verse.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: enough contempt and wrath
Esther.english_translation: *Vekhedai bizayon* — and in this matter there is much contempt and wrath.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: a royal commandment
Esther.english_translation: *Devar malkhut* — a royal decree of vengeance, that he commanded to kill her.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: among the laws of the Persians and the Medes
Esther.english_translation: *Veyikatev bedatei Paras uMadai* — in the books of the statute and custom of the kingdom.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: that it be not altered
Esther.english_translation: *Velo ya'avor* — this statute shall not pass from among them, so that it be a statute and law for everyone who shames her husband.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: that Vashti come no more before king Ahasuerus
Esther.english_translation: *Asher lo tavo Vashti* — and therefore she was killed.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: speak according to the language of his people
Esther.english_translation: *Umedaber kilshon amo* — he compels his wife to learn his language, if she is of another language.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: he remembered Vashti
Esther.english_translation: *Zakhar et Vashti* — her beauty, and was grieved.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: let the king appoint officers
Esther.english_translation: *Veyifked hamelekh pekidim* — because each and every officer knows the beautiful women of his province.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: let their ointments be given them
Esther.english_translation: *Tamrukeihen* — these are things that polish, like “*umoruk veshutaf*” — pleasant oil and kinds of spices and perfumes that cleanse and soften the flesh.
Esther.translator_note: The quoted words are close to Leviticus 6:21 (JPS: “scoured, and rinsed in water”); no reference is printed, and the wording differs from the verse. The oil is called *shemen arev*, translated here as “pleasant oil.”

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: a certain Jew
Esther.english_translation: *Ish yehudi* — because he was exiled with the exile of Judah; all those who were exiled with the kings of Judah were called Jews among the nations, even though they are of another tribe.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: a Benjamite
Esther.english_translation: *Ish yemini* — he was from Benjamin; this is the plain meaning, and our Rabbis expounded what they expounded.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: took her for his own daughter
Esther.english_translation: *Lo levat* — our Rabbis explained: *levayit* (“to a house”), as a wife.
Esther.translator_note: The printed lemma is *lo levat* and the comment reads *levayit*, a rabbinic reading of the word; it is translated as printed.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: he speedily gave her her ointments
Esther.english_translation: *Vayevahel et tamrukeiha* — he was diligent and hurried with hers beyond all of them.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: who were meet to be given her
Esther.english_translation: *Hare'uyot latet lah* — to serve her, and so they do for all of them; and our Rabbis expounded what they expounded.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: he advanced her
Esther.english_translation: *Vayeshanneha* — he changed her.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: she should not tell it
Esther.english_translation: *Asher lo taggid* — so that they would say that she was of a despised family and send her away; for if they knew that she was of the family of King Saul, they would hold on to her.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: what would become of her
Esther.english_translation: *Umah ye'aseh bah* — this is one of two righteous men to whom a hint of salvation was given, David and Mordecai. David, as it is said (I Samuel 17) “both the lion and the bear thy servant smote”: he said, this did not come to my hand except to rely upon it to fight with this one; and so Mordecai said: this did not befall this righteous woman, that she be taken to the bed of an uncircumcised man, except that she is destined to arise to save Israel; therefore he went about to know what would be at her end.
Esther.translator_note: Printed “I Samuel 17” is I Samuel 17:36 (JPS: “Thy servant smote both the lion and the bear”); the printed word order differs.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: the turn of every maiden
Esther.english_translation: *Tor* — time.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: whatsoever she desired was given her
Esther.english_translation: *Kol asher tomar* — all laughter and kinds of song.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: the second house of the women
Esther.english_translation: *El beit hanashim sheni* — the second.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: in the tenth month
Esther.english_translation: *Bachodesh ha'asiri* — a cold season, when the body takes pleasure from the body; the Holy One, blessed be He, arranged that it be a cold season, in order to make her dear to him.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: above all the women
Esther.english_translation: *Mikol hanashim* — the *be'ulot* (women who had been with a man); for he gathered even the *be'ulot* women.
Esther.translator_note: The term *be'ulot* is left untranslated; the bracketed gloss is the translator's.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: made a release to the provinces
Esther.english_translation: *Vehanachah lamedinot asah* — in her honour he lifted from them some of the tax upon them.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: gave gifts
Esther.english_translation: *Vayiten masset* — he sent gifts to them, all in order to entice her, perhaps she would tell her birthplace; and even so —

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: Esther had not yet made known her kindred
Esther.english_translation: *Ein Ester maggedet moladtah* — because Mordecai sat in the king's gate, urging her and hinting to her about this.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: sought to lay hands on the king
Esther.english_translation: *Lishlo'ach yad* — to give him a deadly poison to drink.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: the thing became known to Mordecai
Esther.english_translation: *Vayivada hadavar leMordekhai* — for they were speaking their words before him in the Tarsian language, not knowing that Mordecai knew seventy languages, since he was one of the sitters of the Chamber of Hewn Stone.
Esther.translator_note: The language is called *lashon Tarsi*, translated as “Tarsian language.”

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: written in the book of the chronicles
Esther.english_translation: *Vayikatev besefer divrei hayamim* — the good that Mordecai did for the king.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: After these things
Esther.english_translation: *Achar hadevarim ha'eleh* — for this remedy was created to be a salvation for Israel.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: did king Ahasuerus promote Haman
Esther.english_translation: *Gidal hamelekh* etc. — Haman, for the Holy One, blessed be He, creates the remedy for the blow of Israel before He brings the blow upon them.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: bowed down, and prostrated themselves before Haman
Esther.english_translation: *Kor'im umishtachavim* — for he made himself a god; therefore, “but Mordecai bowed not down, nor prostrated himself.”

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: whether Mordecai’s words would stand
Esther.english_translation: *Hayaamdu divrei Mordekhai* — the one who said that he would never prostrate himself, because he is a Jew and was warned about idolatry [ע"א].
Esther.translator_note: The abbreviation ע"א is read as “idolatry” from the context; the expansion is not confirmed by a permitted source, so the comment is flagged.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: they cast pur
Esther.english_translation: *Hippil pur* — he cast the lot, whoever cast it, and it did not specify who; and it is an abbreviated verse.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: that is, the lot
Esther.english_translation: *Hu hagoral* — the verse explains: what is the *pur*? It is a lot. He cast the lot [to see] in which month he would succeed.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: from day to day
Esther.english_translation: *Miyom leyom* — on which day of the month he would succeed.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: neither keep they the king’s laws
Esther.english_translation: *Ve'et datei hamelekh* — to give tax for the king's service.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: it profiteth not the king
Esther.english_translation: *Ein shoveh* — there is no concern; that is, no profit.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: let it be written that they be destroyed
Esther.english_translation: *Yikatev le'abbedam* — let letters be written, to be sent to the governors of the provinces, to destroy them.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: the king took his ring from his hand
Esther.english_translation: *Vayasar hamelekh et tabba'to* — this is the granting of every great thing that they might request of the king, so that whoever has the ring in his hand is ruler over every matter of the king.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: letters were sent by posts
Esther.english_translation: *Venishlo'ach sefarim* — letters would be sent, *estre tramis* [printed אישט"רא טרמי"ש] in Old French; and it is from the form of (Judges 11) “if we fight” (*nilcham*), (I Samuel 2) “did I indeed reveal myself” (*hinnaglo niglet*), (Hosea 10) “utterly cut off” (*nidmo nidmah*).
Esther.translator_note: Old French *estre tramis* (“to be sent”): read from Darmesteter (1909) at Esther 3:13 (“Et les livres seront envoyés”), where his footnote gives the reading *éstre tramis*; the printed form is one of the manuscript variants he lists (אישטרא טרמיש). Printed “Judges 11” is Judges 11:25 (JPS: “did he ever fight against them”); the printed reference “I Samuel 2” (written ש"א א ב) is read as I Samuel 2:27 (JPS: “Did I reveal Myself unto the house of thy father”); “Hosea 10” is Hosea 10:15 (JPS: “At daybreak is the king of Israel utterly cut off”). The point of the comment is the Hebrew grammatical form, which does not show in the English.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: upon the thirteenth day of the twelfth month
Esther.english_translation: *Bishloshah asar lechodesh shenem asar* — on the thirteenth day of that month, which is the twelfth of the months of the year.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: The copy of the writing
Esther.english_translation: *Patshegen* — an Aramaic expression: the recital of the writing, דרישממ"נט in Old French.
Esther.translator_note: Darmesteter (1909) lists this word at Esther 3:14 (“La teneur de la lettre,” the tenor of the letter) in forms such as דרישנמנט; the printed form is a variant spelling, but his reading of it is not legible in my copy, so it is left as printed. Godefroy has *deraisnement / desrenement* (“setting out one’s case”), which fits the letters but not clearly the sense, so I do not adopt it.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: to be given out for a decree in every province
Esther.english_translation: *Lehinnaten dat* — the command of the writing, which said: to be given out as a statute, the king's decree.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: was to be published unto all peoples
Esther.english_translation: *Galui lekhol ha'amim* — this matter.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: the decree was given out in Shushan the castle
Esther.english_translation: *Vehadat nitnah beShushan* — in the place where the king was, the law was given on that day, that they be prepared for the thirteenth day of the month of Adar; therefore —

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: the city of Shushan was perplexed
Esther.english_translation: *Veha'ir Shushan nevokhah* — the Jews who were in it.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: when Mordecai knew all that was done
Esther.english_translation: *UMordekhai yada* — the Master of the Dream told him that the upper beings had agreed to this, because they had prostrated themselves to the image in the days of Nebuchadnezzar, and because they had enjoyed the feast of Ahasuerus.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: none might enter within the king’s gate clothed with sackcloth
Esther.english_translation: *Ki ein lavo* — it is not proper conduct to come to the king's gate clothed in sackcloth.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: the king’s commandment and his decree came
Esther.english_translation: *Devar hamelekh vedato* — when the messengers who carried the letters passed there, the law was given in the city.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: the exact sum of the money
Esther.english_translation: *Parashat hakesef* — the explanation of the money.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: Think not with thyself
Esther.english_translation: *Al tedammi venafshekh* — do not think, like (Numbers 33) “and it shall come to pass, as I thought” (*dimiti*): “do not imagine in your soul” — do not be of the opinion that you will escape on the day of the killing in the king's house; for you do not want to endanger yourself now, on a doubt, by coming to the king without permission.
Esther.translator_note: Printed “Numbers 33” is Numbers 33:56 (JPS: “as I thought to do unto them”); the printed wording differs.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: who knoweth whether thou art not come to royal estate for such a time as this
Esther.english_translation: *Umi yode'a im le'et kazot higa'at* — and who knows whether the king will desire you next year, which is the time of the killing.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: for such a time as this
Esther.english_translation: *Le'et kazot* — for it was happening in Nisan, and the time of the killing is in Adar of the following year.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: royal estate
Esther.english_translation: *Higa'at lamalkhut* — whether you will reach the greatness in which you are now.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: which is not according to the law
Esther.english_translation: *Asher lo khadat* — for there is no law to enter “who is not called”; and another explanation (ומ"א): “which is not according to the law” — for until now it was under compulsion, and now it is by will.
Esther.translator_note: The printed abbreviation ומ"א is left as printed (it appears to introduce a second explanation).

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: if I perish, I perish
Esther.english_translation: *Vekha'asher avadti avadti* — as I began to go to perish, I will go and die; and another (ומ"א): as I have perished from my father's house, so I will be lost from you, for from now that I voluntarily am taken (*nivelet*) by a gentile, I am forbidden to you.
Esther.translator_note: The printed abbreviation ומ"א is left as printed; the word *nivelet* is left untranslated.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: Mordecai went his way
Esther.english_translation: *Vaya'avor Mordekhai* — he transgressed the law by fasting on the first festival day of Passover, for he fasted on the fourteenth, fifteenth and sixteenth of Nisan, for on the thirteenth the letters were written.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: put on her royal apparel
Esther.english_translation: *Malkhut* — royal garments; and our Rabbis said that the Holy Spirit clothed her, as you say (I Chronicles 12) “and the spirit clothed Amasai.”
Esther.translator_note: Printed “I Chronicles 12” is I Chronicles 12:19 (JPS: “Then the spirit clothed Amasai”).

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: even to the half of the kingdom
Esther.english_translation: *Ad chatzi hamalkhut* — a thing that is in the middle; and the half of the kingdom is the Temple, which they began to build in the days of Cyrus, and he retracted and commanded to cancel the work, and Ahasuerus, who stood after him, also cancelled the work; and the plain meaning of the verse is: even if you ask of me half the kingdom, I will give you.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: let the king and Haman come this day
Esther.english_translation: *Yavo hamelekh veHaman* — our Rabbis gave many reasons for this: what did Esther see that she invited Haman? To make him jealous toward the king and the officers, so that the king would think he was beloved of her and would kill him; and many other reasons.
Esther.translator_note: The phrase “to make him jealous toward the king” is translated literally; who is jealous of whom is not stated in the printed sentence.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: unto the banquet
Esther.english_translation: *El hamishteh* — every meal is called by the name of the wine, which is the main thing.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: I will do to-morrow as the king hath said
Esther.english_translation: *Umachar e'eseh kidvar hamelekh* — what you have asked of me all these days, to reveal to you my people and my birthplace.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: Haman refrained himself
Esther.english_translation: *Vayit'appak* — he strengthened himself to withstand his anger, for he was afraid to take revenge without permission; *vayit'appak*, אישט"ניר in Old French (in his base manuscript Darmesteter reads the word *é se retint*, “and he restrained himself”).
Esther.translator_note: Darmesteter (1909) lists this word at Esther 5:10 (“Et il se contint,” and he restrained himself) with a variant אישטניר, which is the printed form; his footnote gives the reading of his base manuscript as *é se retint*. I keep the printed form because I cannot show that the two readings are the same word.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: availeth me nothing
Esther.english_translation: *Einenu shoveh li* — I take no heed of all the honour that I have.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: so long as I see Mordecai the Jew sitting at the king’s gate
Esther.english_translation: *Bekhol et* etc. — our Rabbis said that he showed him a deed by which he had sold himself as a slave for lack of food, when Mordecai and Haman were appointed heads of troops in one war.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: could not the king sleep
Esther.english_translation: *Nadedah shenat hamelekh* — it was a miracle; and some say that he set his heart on Esther having invited Haman: perhaps she had set her eyes on him and would kill him.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: the book of records of the chronicles
Esther.english_translation: *Lehavi et sefer hazikhronot* — the way of kings, when their sleep wanders, is that parables and conversations are told before them until their sleep returns to them; and our Rabbis said: since he set his heart on Haman and Esther, he said, it is impossible that no one knows their plan, for he is my friend and would reveal it to me; and he said again, perhaps someone did me a good deed and I did not repay him, and they no longer care about me; therefore “and he said to bring the book of records.”

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: delivered to the hand of one of the king’s most noble princes
Esther.english_translation: *Venatan halevush vehasus al yad ish* — and he did not mention the crown, because he saw that the eye of the king was evil about this, since he had said that they should put the crown on a man's head.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: Mordecai returned to the king’s gate
Esther.english_translation: *Vayashav Mordekhai* — to his sackcloth and to his fast. [
Esther.translator_note: The printed text ends with an opening bracket with no closing bracket; it is left as printed.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: mourning and having his head covered
Esther.english_translation: *Avel vachafui rosh* — our Rabbis explained the matter in tractate Megillah.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: before whom thou hast begun to fall
Esther.english_translation: *Asher hachillota linpol* etc. — she said: this nation has been likened to the stars and to the dust: when they go down, they go down to the dust, and when they go up, they go up to the firmament and to the stars.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: let my life be given me at my petition
Esther.english_translation: *Tinnaten li nafshi* — that I not be killed on the thirteenth of Adar, for you have decreed a decree of killing upon my people and my birthplace.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: and my people at my request
Esther.english_translation: [no lemma printed] — “and my people be given to me at my request” — that they not be killed; and if you say, what is it to you? “For how can I endure, and see,” etc.
Esther.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment; the lemma shown is the corresponding phrase of the verse. The closing words are Esther 8:6 (JPS: “for how can I endure to see the evil that shall come unto my people?”); no reference is printed.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: the adversary is not worthy that the king be endamaged
Esther.english_translation: *Ki ein hatzar shoveh benezek hamelekh* — he does not care about the king's loss, for if he were pursuing your benefit, he should have said: sell them as slaves and as maidservants and take the money, or let them live to be slaves to you, they and their seed.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: Then spoke the king Ahasuerus and said unto Esther the queen
Esther.english_translation: *Vayomer hamelekh Achashverosh vayomer le'Ester hamalkah* — everywhere that it says “and he said, and he said” twice, it is only for a midrash; and the midrash of this: at first he used to speak with her through a messenger; now that he knew that she was of a family of kings, he spoke with her himself.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: there was evil determined against him by the king
Esther.english_translation: *Ki khaletah* — the evil and the hatred and the vengeance were completed.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: Haman was fallen
Esther.english_translation: *VeHaman nofel* — the angel pushed him.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: upon the couch whereon Esther was
Esther.english_translation: *Al hamittah asher Ester aleiha* — their way was to sit at the meal on their side on couches, as it says at the beginning of the book, “couches of gold and silver” for the guests of the feast.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: Will he even force the queen
Esther.english_translation: *Hagam likhbosh* — an expression of astonishment. *Likhbosh* is to compel by force, like (Numbers 32) “and the land be subdued.”
Esther.translator_note: Printed “Numbers 32” is Numbers 32:22 (JPS: “and the land be subdued before the LORD”).

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: Behold also, the gallows
Esther.english_translation: *Gam hineh ha'etz* — he also did another evil, for he prepared the tree to hang the friend of the king who saved the king from the deadly poison.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: Esther had told what he was unto her
Esther.english_translation: *Mah hu lah* — how he is related to her.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: to put away the mischief of Haman the Agagite
Esther.english_translation: *Leha'avir et ra'at Haman* — that his evil plan not be fulfilled.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: Behold, I have given Esther the house of Haman
Esther.english_translation: *Hineh veit Haman* etc. — and from now on all see that I desire you, and everything you say, all will believe is from me; therefore you do not need to answer them, but write other letters as is good in your eyes.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: may no man reverse
Esther.english_translation: *Ein lehashiv* — it is not fitting to reverse it and make the king's writing a forgery.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: according to the writing thereof
Esther.english_translation: *Kikhtavah* — in its letters.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: according to their language
Esther.english_translation: *Kilshono* — the speech.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: sent letters by posts on horseback
Esther.english_translation: *Beyad haratzim* — riders of horses whom he commanded to run.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: bred of the stud
Esther.english_translation: *Ha'achashteranim* — a kind of camels that hurry to run.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: to take the spoil of them for a prey
Esther.english_translation: *Ushelalam labuz* — as was written in the first ones; and they did not stretch out their hand to the spoil, to show everyone that it was not done for the sake of money.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: The copy of the writing
Esther.english_translation: *Patshegen* — a letter, explained.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: being hastened and pressed on
Esther.english_translation: *Mevohalim* — they hurry them to act quickly, because they had no leisure, for they had to get ahead of the first runners in order to pass them.
Esther.translator_note: The last clause (*lehe'aviram*, “to pass them”) is translated literally; its sense is not resolved here.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: a rob of fine linen and purple
Esther.english_translation: *Vetakhrikh butz* — a covering of fine linen, a cloak made for wrapping oneself.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: became Jews
Esther.english_translation: *Mityahadim* — converting.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: they that did the king’s business
Esther.english_translation: *Ve'osei hamelakhah* — those who were appointed to do the king's needs.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: the ten sons of Haman
Esther.english_translation: *Aseret benei Haman* — I saw in Seder Olam: these are ten who wrote an accusation against Judah and Jerusalem, as it is written in the book of Ezra (Ezra 4) “and in the reign of Ahasuerus, in the beginning of his reign, they wrote an accusation against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem.” And what was the accusation? To nullify those who went up from the exile in the days of Cyrus, who had begun to build the House; and the Cutheans informed against them and made them stop; and when Cyrus died and Ahasuerus reigned and Haman was exalted, he worried that those in Jerusalem would not engage in the building, and they sent in the name of Ahasuerus to the governors beyond the river to cancel them.
Esther.translator_note: Printed “Ezra 4” is Ezra 4:6 (JPS: “And in the reign of Ahasuerus, in the beginning of his reign, wrote they an accusation against the inhabitants of Judah and Jerusalem”).

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: on the spoil they laid not their hand
Esther.english_translation: *Uvabizah lo shalchu et yadam* — so that the king would not look with an evil eye at the money.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: let Haman’s ten sons be hanged upon the gallows
Esther.english_translation: *Ve'et aseret benei Haman yitlu al ha'etz* — those who had been killed.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: a decree was given out in Shushan
Esther.english_translation: *Vatinnaten dat* — a statute was decreed by the king.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: that dwell in the unwalled towns
Esther.english_translation: *Haperazim* — who do not dwell in walled cities, on the fourteenth; and those enclosed by a wall, on the fifteenth, like Shushan; and this enclosure must date from the days of Joshua son of Nun; so our Rabbis expounded and learned.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: of sending portions one to another
Esther.english_translation: *Umishlo'ach* — a noun, like *mishmar* (“guard”) is understood; therefore the *shin* is vowelled *rafeh*.
Esther.translator_note: This is a technical remark on the vowelling of the word; it is translated literally.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: Mordecai wrote these things
Esther.english_translation: *Vayikhtov Mordekhai* — this is this Megillah as it is.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: Haman the son of Hammedatha, the Agagite
Esther.english_translation: *Ki Haman ben Hamedata* — he plotted to confound them and to destroy them.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: came before the king
Esther.english_translation: *Uvevo'ah* — Esther to the king, to supplicate him.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: he commanded by letters
Esther.english_translation: *Amar im hasefer* — the king said with his mouth and commanded to write letters that his evil thought return upon his head.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: Therefore because of all the words of this letter
Esther.english_translation: *Al ken al kol divrei ha'iggeret hazot* — these days were fixed, and therefore it was written, for the knowledge of the coming generations.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: that which they had seen
Esther.english_translation: *Umah ra'u* — those who did these deeds, who did them.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: that which had come unto them
Esther.english_translation: *Umah higia aleihem* — what did Ahasuerus see that he used the holy vessels, and what befell them, that Satan came and danced among them and killed Vashti; what did Haman see that he became jealous of Mordecai, and what befell him, that they hanged him and his sons; what did Mordecai see that he would not bow down nor prostrate himself; and what did Esther see that she invited Haman.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: all such as joined themselves unto them
Esther.english_translation: *Hanilvim aleihem* — proselytes who are destined to convert.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: according to the writing thereof
Esther.english_translation: *Kikhtavam* — that the Megillah be written in Assyrian script.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: should be remembered
Esther.english_translation: *Nizkarim* — by the reading of the Megillah.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: and kept
Esther.english_translation: *Ve'na'asim* — a feast and joy and a good day, to give portions and gifts.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: every family
Esther.english_translation: *Mishpachah umishpachah* — they gather together and eat and drink together; and so they accepted upon themselves that the days of Purim shall not pass away.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: the memorial of them
Esther.english_translation: *Vezikhram* — the reading of the Megillah.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: should not fail
Esther.english_translation: *Lo yasuf* — the Targum renders “that it not end”; for the translator renders *ad tom* (“until the end”) as *ad desaf*. And it is impossible to say that it is from the form of (Genesis 19) “lest thou be swept away” (*tispeh*) or from the form of (I Samuel 27) “now I shall be swept away one day” (*espeh*), for if so he should have written *lo yispeh mizar'am*.
Esther.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 19” is Genesis 19:15 (JPS: “lest thou be swept away in the iniquity of the city”) and “I Samuel 27” is I Samuel 27:1 (JPS: “I shall now be swept away one day”). The printed abbreviation וא"א is read as “and it is impossible”; the point of the comment is the Hebrew grammatical form.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: all the acts of power
Esther.english_translation: *Et kol tokef* — the might of the miracle of Ahasuerus and of Haman and of Mordecai and of Esther [
Esther.translator_note: The printed text ends with an opening bracket with no closing bracket; it is left as printed.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: this second letter of Purim
Esther.english_translation: *Hashenit* — in the second year they again sent letters to make Purim.

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: the commandment of Esther confirmed these matters of Purim
Esther.english_translation: *Uma'amar Ester kiyyam* etc. — Esther asked the sages of the generation to fix it and to write this book with the rest of the Writings; and this is “and it was written in the book.”

Esther.english_lemma_JPS: accepted of the multitude of his brethren
Esther.english_translation: *Lerov echav* — and not by all his brethren; this teaches that some of the Sanhedrin separated from him, because he became close to the monarchy and was idle from his study. “To all his seed” refers to “his people”: to all the seed of his people. Here ends the Scroll of Esther.
Esther.translator_note: The closing words “Here ends the Scroll of Esther” are printed at the end of the comment and are translated as printed.

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim king of Judah
Daniel.english_translation: *Bishnat shalosh lemalkhut Yehoyakim* — and is it possible to say so? Was he not king in the fourth year of Jehoiakim, as it is said (Jeremiah 25) “in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah king of Judah, which is the first year of Nebuchadnezzar”? And what does the verse teach by “in the third year”? In the third year of his rebellion, as it is said (II Kings 24) “and Jehoiakim became his servant three years, and he turned and rebelled against him three years”; and in the third year he came up against him, and it was the eighth year of Nebuchadnezzar, for the Master said: the first year he conquered Nineveh, the second he went up and conquered Jehoiakim, and three years they served him and three years he rebelled against him, and it was the eleventh year of the reign of Jehoiakim: five years before he conquered him, and three that he served and three that he rebelled against him; and then Jehoiakim died under his hand, and Nebuchadnezzar made Jehoiachin, his son, king in his place.
Daniel.translator_note: Printed “Jeremiah 25” is Jeremiah 25:1 (JPS: “in the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah, king of Judah, that was the first year of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon”). Printed “II Kings 24” is II Kings 24:1 (JPS: “Jehoiakim became his servant three years; then he turned and rebelled against him”); the printed text adds “three years” after “rebelled against him,” which the verse does not have. The chronology is translated as printed.

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: with part of the vessels of the house of God
Daniel.english_translation: *Umiktzat kelei beit ha'Elohim* — he took, and some of them remained, as it is said (Jeremiah 27) “For thus said the Lord of hosts concerning the pillars, and concerning the sea, and concerning the bases, and concerning the residue of the vessels that remain in this city.”
Daniel.translator_note: Printed “Jeremiah 27” is Jeremiah 27:19 (JPS: “For thus saith the LORD of hosts concerning the pillars, and concerning the sea, and concerning the bases, and concerning the residue of the vessels that remain in this city”).

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: he carried them into the land of Shinar to the house of his god
Daniel.english_translation: *Vayeviem eretz Shin'ar beit elohav* — to glorify (*lekalles*) his idolatry. He brought there all the captivity, even the people; and the vessels he afterwards brought into the treasure-house.
Daniel.translator_note: The verb *lekalles* is rendered “to glorify.”

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: of the nobles
Daniel.english_translation: *Hapartemim* — dukes.

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: such as had ability to stand in the king’s palace
Daniel.english_translation: *Va'asher ko'ach bahem* — our Sages of blessed memory explained: that they would force themselves from laughter, and from conversation, and from sleep, because of the awe of the monarchy, and that they would hold themselves in when they needed to relieve themselves.

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: the learning and the tongue of the Chaldeans
Daniel.english_translation: *Ulelammedam sefer* — this refers back to “in whom was ability.”

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: the king appointed for them
Daniel.english_translation: *Vayeman* — an expression of appointment.

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: a daily portion of the king’s food
Daniel.english_translation: *Mipat bag* — this is the name of the king's food in the language of the Chaldeans; and some interpret *pat bag* as bread, but it does not appear so, for it is written “and the steward took away their *pat bagam*, and gave them pulse,” and pulse is not a substitute for bread, but a substitute for cooked food.

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: Belteshazzar
Daniel.english_translation: *Belteshatzar* — after the idolatry of Babylon, which is called Bel, as it is said “whose name is Belteshazzar, according to the name of my god”; *Belteshazzar* is a name of an expression of wisdom in the Aramaic language.
Daniel.translator_note: The quoted Aramaic words are Daniel 4:5 (JPS: “whose name was Belteshazzar, according to the name of my god”); no reference is printed.

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: defile himself
Daniel.english_translation: *Yitga'al* — an expression of soiling.

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: the chief of the officers
Daniel.english_translation: *Sar hasarisim* — who was a chief over the king's servants.

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: who hath appointed your food and your drink
Daniel.english_translation: *Asher mannah* — who prepared and provided.

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: of your own age
Daniel.english_translation: *Kegilkhem* — like you; and it is a Mishnaic expression: *ben gilo* (“his age-mate”).

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: would you endanger my head with the king
Daniel.english_translation: *Vechiyyavtem et roshi lamelekh* — you will cause me to become liable to have my head cut off.

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: Then said Daniel to the steward
Daniel.english_translation: *Hamaltzar* — the one who arranges the portions and the bowls, which are called מאישטרי"ב אל"ה in Old French.
Daniel.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Daniel 1:11 (“le maître cuisinier”), in forms such as שנקל and שנישקאל; the printed form (מאישטרי"ב אל"ה) differs.

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: Try thy servants
Daniel.english_translation: *Nas* — an expression of testing.

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: pulse to eat
Daniel.english_translation: *Min hazero'im* — a kind of legumes, in place of *pat bag*.

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: as thou seest, deal with thy servants
Daniel.english_translation: *Uke'asher tire* — according to what you see, do.

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: took away their food
Daniel.english_translation: *Nosei et pat bagam* — he took it for himself.

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: for bringing them in
Daniel.english_translation: *Asher amar hamelekh lehaviam* — that they come before him.

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: magicians
Daniel.english_translation: *Hachartumei* — these are those who inquire of the dead through the bones of the dead, as you say *shachik atzamot, shachik timya*.
Daniel.translator_note: The Aramaic phrase *shachik atzamot, shachik timya* and the earlier word *bitimei* are left as printed; their sense is not resolved here.

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: enchanters
Daniel.english_translation: *Ha'ashafim* — these are those who press upon the constellation (*mazal*); so it is explained in Tanchuma.

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: Daniel continued even unto the first year of king Cyrus
Daniel.english_translation: *Vayhi Daniel* — in greatness in Babylon, until the first year of Cyrus the king; according to the one who says that Hathach is Daniel — and why was he called Hathach? Because they cut him (*chatkhuhu*) off from his greatness — we must say that this is the first Cyrus, who was before Ahasuerus; and according to the one who says that all the matters of the kingdom were cut (*nechtakhin*) by his word, we say that this Cyrus is Darius the Second, after Ahasuerus. And in the days of Darius the Mede, when they threw him into the lions' den, he did not descend from his greatness, as it is said (below, 6) “and this Daniel prospered in the reign of Darius, and in the reign of Cyrus the Persian”; we learn that in the days of the first Cyrus he was in greatness.
Daniel.translator_note: Printed “below, 6” is Daniel 6:29 (JPS: “So this Daniel prospered in the reign of Darius, and in the reign of Cyrus the Persian”); the name Hathach occurs in Esther 4. The Aramaic quotation is translated as printed.

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: in the second year of the reign of Nebuchadnezzar
Daniel.english_translation: *Uvishnat shetayim lemalkhut Nevukhadnetzar* — it is impossible to say so; rather, in the second year after the destruction of the House, so it is taught in Seder Olam; and they called it the “reign of Nebuchadnezzar” because he showed his wickedness by entering the inner sanctum of the King of the world.

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: his spirit was troubled
Daniel.english_translation: *Vatitpa'em ruchou* — of Pharaoh it is said “and his spirit was troubled” (*vatippa'em*; Genesis 41), because only the interpretation of the dream was hidden from him; but here, where the dream itself was also hidden from him, the language is doubled: *vatitpa'em*, an expression of a beat (*pe'imah*) and a blow (*halimah*). And in the Chumash, Rashi of blessed memory explained: an expression of knocking (*nekifah*).
Daniel.translator_note: Printed “Genesis 41” is Genesis 41:8 (JPS: “his spirit was troubled”). The last sentence refers to Rashi by name in the third person, so it is not in his own wording; it is translated as printed.

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: his sleep broke from him
Daniel.english_translation: *Nehyetah alav* — an expression of breaking, like (Ezekiel 6) “calamity upon calamity” (*havvah al havvah*).
Daniel.translator_note: Printed “Ezekiel 6” is Ezekiel 7:26 (JPS: “Calamity shall come upon calamity”).

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: O king, live for ever
Daniel.english_translation: *Le'almin chei* — may he live forever.

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: tell thy servants the dream
Daniel.english_translation: *Emar chelma la'avdakh* — tell the dream to your servant.

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: The thing is certain with me
Daniel.english_translation: *Millata minni azda* — the matter has gone from me.

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: if you make not known unto me the dream and the interpretation thereof
Daniel.english_translation: *Hen la tehodi'unanni chelma ufishreih* — if you do not make known to me the dream and its interpretation.

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: you shall be cut in pieces
Daniel.english_translation: *Hadamin tit'abedun* — you shall be cut into limbs; and there are many in the Gemara: *hadomi hadmoh*, in tractate Gittin.
Daniel.translator_note: The Aramaic phrase *hadomi hadmoh* is left as printed; the Gemara reference is not resolved here.

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: your houses shall be made a dunghill
Daniel.english_translation: *Nevalu* — a refuse heap.

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: shall be made
Daniel.english_translation: *Yitashmun* — an expression of “and he placed” (*vayasem*): they will become *shumot* for refuse heaps.
Daniel.translator_note: The word *shumot* is left untranslated.

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: But if you declare the dream
Daniel.english_translation: *Vehen* — and if.

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: gifts
Daniel.english_translation: *Unevizbah* — gifts.

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: only declare unto me
Daniel.english_translation: *Lahen* — but.

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: only declare unto me the dream
Daniel.english_translation: *Hachavuni* — tell me.

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: They answered the second time
Daniel.english_translation: *Tinyanut* — a second time.

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: we will declare the interpretation
Daniel.english_translation: *Nehachvei* — we will tell.

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: I know of a truth
Daniel.english_translation: *Min yatziv yeda anah* — in truth I know.

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: of a truth
Daniel.english_translation: *Yatziv* — a true and firm thing.

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: that you would gain time
Daniel.english_translation: *Di idna antun zavnin* — that at this hour you are delivered to death.
Daniel.translator_note: Rashi's explanation differs from the JPS rendering (“you would gain time”).

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: inasmuch as you see the thing is certain with me
Daniel.english_translation: *Kol kevel di chazitun* — in view of the fact that you see that the matter has gone from me, and you repeat to me [your demand] that I tell you.

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: if you make not known unto me the dream, there is but one law for you
Daniel.english_translation: *Di hen chelma la tehoda'unani* — for if you do not make known to me the dream and its interpretation, your law is one: to die.

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: lying and corrupt words
Daniel.english_translation: *Umillah khidvah ushechitah hizdamantun* — or if you prepare yourselves to say before me a false and corrupt thing.

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: till the time be changed
Daniel.english_translation: *Ad di idna yishtanna* — until the time changes; that is, before the shadows of the evening incline, so that the appointed time of the morning changes.

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: till the time be changed
Daniel.english_translation: *Ad di idna yishtanna* — it is an expression of rebuke and of cutting off; thus will he be punished, and the punishment was already explained above, and its like: “therefore (*lachen*) whosoever slayeth Cain” (Genesis 4).
Daniel.translator_note: The printed lemma repeats the preceding one, but the comment concerns the word *lahen* (“therefore”); the lemma shown is the corresponding phrase of the verse. Printed “Genesis 4” is Genesis 4:15 (JPS: “Therefore whosoever slayeth Cain, vengeance shall be taken on him sevenfold”).

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: only tell me the dream
Daniel.english_translation: *Lahen* — but tell me the dream, tell me what I dreamed, and I will know all the more that you can tell the interpretation.
Daniel.translator_note: The printed abbreviation כ"ש is read as “all the more.”

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: that can declare the king’s matter
Daniel.english_translation: *Di millat malka* — that the king's matter he can tell.

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: forasmuch as no great and powerful king hath asked such a thing
Daniel.english_translation: *Kol kevel* — in view of the fact; that is, this answer of ours is true, in view of the fact that there never was a king who asked such a thing.

Daniel.english_lemma_JPS: such a thing
