Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: For there were many in Judah sworn unto him
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Ki rabbim beYehudah* — for there were many princes in Judah who were allies of Tobiah and bound to him by oath.

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: he was the son-in-law of Shecaniah
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Ki chatan hu* — that Tobiah, to Shecaniah.
*Viyhochanan b'no* — of Tobiah.
*Bat Meshullam* — that Meshullam was a prince and a great man.

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: they spoke of his good deeds before me
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Gam tovotav* — of Tobiah, those who were bound to him by oath and his relatives used to recount before me.
*Tovotav* — *sesproetsosh* in the vernacular.
Nehemiah.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Nehemiah 6:19 (“les exploits”), in forms such as שיש פרואיצש, שישפרוציאט, ששפרווצש and ששפרואייש; the printed form (ששפרואוצ"ש) is close to them and is a variant spelling.

Nehemiah.english_translation: *Hayu motzi'im lo* — to tell Tobiah.

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: Tobiah sent letters to put me in fear
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Iggerot shalach Tovyah* — he was continually sending letters to frighten me, so that I should not build the building of the wall.
*Vayyippakedu* — now the Levites were made officers over their offices, to be porters and singers from among the Levites, בב"ה.
Nehemiah.translator_note: The printed abbreviation בב"ה is left as printed because I could not resolve it.

Nehemiah.english_translation: *Al Yerushalayim* — to guard the gates of Jerusalem.
*Merabbim* — from many days.
Nehemiah.translator_note: Rashi’s printed wording (“from many days”) differs from JPS (“above many”); translated as printed.

Nehemiah.english_translation: *Ad chom hashemesh* — until midday, when the day was great.

*Ve-ad hem omedim* — and while the gates are open they shall stand and not move until they close and shut the doors; and whoever wishes to go out goes out of the city, and whoever wishes to enter comes and enters. So they did, because of the enemies.
*Ve-ochezu* — let them take hold of the doors to lock them.

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: let watches be appointed of the inhabitants of Jerusalem
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Mishmerot yoshevei Yerushalayim* — from among the inhabitants of Jerusalem they set up watches, *gaite* in the vernacular.
Nehemiah.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Nehemiah 7:3 (“des gardes”), in forms such as גייטש, גיטש and גייטא; the printed form (גיט"ש) matches the form גיטש.

Nehemiah.english_translation: *Rachavat yadayim* — wide of place and large.
*Lehityached* — to investigate their lineage.

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: them that came up at the first
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Ha'olim barishonah* — of those Jews who went up with Ezra at first.
Nehemiah.translator_note: Rashi’s printed text says “with Ezra”; the next verses (7:6–7) name Zerubbabel as leader of those who came up.

Nehemiah.english_translation: *Va-emtza katuv bo* — all these things were written in that letter.

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: These are the children of the province
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Eleh benei hamedinah* etc. — up to “and we cast lots for the wood-offering” (below, 10, 35).
Nehemiah.translator_note: The reference is Nehemiah 10:35 (JPS: “And we cast lots, the priests, the Levites, and the people, for the wood-offering”).

Nehemiah.english_translation: *Vliyhudah* — to the province of Judah.
*Ish le-iro* — each to his city.
*Habba'im im Zerubavel* — who came from the captives of the exile with Zerubbabel.

*Yeshua* — that is Joshua son of Jehozadak, the High Priest. These computations sometimes agree with the computations above, and sometimes they do not agree one with the other, and Scripture was not so exact in the computations; but the total is the same here and there (see Ezra, chapter 2, פ"ב, and it requires study, יוש"ה), as it is said “The whole congregation together,” etc., and the writer of the book relied on this total and was not so exact in the computation of the details; and everything is explained above.
Nehemiah.translator_note: The parenthesis is a later printed insertion; its abbreviations פ"ב and יוש"ה are left as printed because I could not resolve them. The quotation is Nehemiah 7:66 (and Ezra 2:64) (JPS: “The whole congregation together was forty and two thousand three hundred and threescore”).

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: upon the first day of the seventh month
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Beyom echad lachodesh hashevi'i* — that is the day of Rosh Hashanah.
Nehemiah.translator_note: The printed abbreviation ר"ה is read as Rosh Hashanah.

Nehemiah.english_translation: *Min ha-or* — of the beginning of the day.

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: attentive unto the book of the Law
Nehemiah.english_translation: *El sefer hatorah* — all the people were inclining their ears.

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: which they had made for the purpose
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Asher asu ladavar* — that wooden tower they made for this purpose, to read on it from the book of the Law.

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: for he was above all the people
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Ki me'al kol ha'am hayah* — and therefore all saw him.
*Uchfitcho amdu kol ha'am* — and when he opened it to read, all the people were silent.
*Amadu* — language of silence (they were silent), like “They stand still, and answer no more” (Job 32).
Nehemiah.translator_note: The quotation is Job 32:16 (JPS: “Because they stand still, and answer no more”); Rashi’s printed form is “they stood and answered no more.”

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: with the lifting up of their hands
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Bemo'al yedeihem* — in the lifting of their hands, for they lifted their palms upward to give thanks to the Holy One, blessed be He, as in the matter that is said “and spread forth his hands toward heaven” (I Kings 8).
Nehemiah.translator_note: The quotation is I Kings 8:22 (JPS: “and spread forth his hands toward heaven”).

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: caused the people to understand the Law
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Mevinim et ha'am* — for they were translating the words of the Law to the people.

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: the people stood in their place
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Al omdam* — for they were standing on their feet.
*Ve-som sechel* — and the setting of wisdom; and *som* is a passive form.

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: This day is holy unto the LORD your God
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Hayom kadosh* — for it is the day of Rosh Hashanah.
Nehemiah.translator_note: The printed abbreviation ר"ה is read as Rosh Hashanah.

Nehemiah.english_translation: *Ki vokhim kol ha'am* — because they had not fulfilled the Law as was proper.
*Le-ein nachon lo* — to the poor man for whom his food has not been made ready.

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: the Levites stilled all the people
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Machashim* — they warned all the people to be silent, that they should weep no more.
*Hassu* — language of silence, like “And Caleb stilled (*vayhas*)” (Numbers 13).
Nehemiah.translator_note: The printed reference “Numbers 13” is incomplete; the quotation is Numbers 13:30 (JPS: “And Caleb stilled the people toward Moses”).

Nehemiah.english_translation: *Uvayom hasheni* — of Rosh Hashanah.
Nehemiah.translator_note: The printed abbreviation ר"ה is read as Rosh Hashanah.

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: that they should publish and proclaim
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Va-asher yashmi'u* — and they commanded that they should make a voice heard to celebrate the festival of Sukkot; and so Scripture is accustomed to speak in a matter like this, as in “Bid the servant pass on before us” (I Samuel 9).
Nehemiah.translator_note: The quotation is I Samuel 9:27 (JPS: “Bid the servant pass on before us—and he passed on—”).

Nehemiah.english_translation: *Ve-alei hadas* — explained in tractate Sukkah: this is wild myrtle, which is not fit for the *lulav*, but only for making a *sukkah*.
*Ve-alei temarim* — for the *lulav*.
*Ve-alei etz avot* — this is the myrtle that is fit for the *lulav*, as is explained in tractate Sukkah.
*Yom beyom* — every single day.
*Va-adamah aleihem* — they put dust upon their heads.
*Mikol benei nechar* — and from the wives of the idolaters, as is said above.

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: upon the platform of the Levites
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Al ma'aleh haLevi'im* — there were steps there, on which the Levites stood at the time when they said song.
*Min ha'olam ve-ad ha'olam* — from the beginning of the world until its end, may He be blessed.

*Vivarkhu shem kevodekha* — now the Levites spoke toward the Divine Presence in prayer: “and let them bless Thy glorious Name,” for He is great and exalted above all blessing and praise, for all blessings and praises are His. Another explanation (*davar acher*): “and exalted above all blessing and praise,” for no creature can bless Him and praise Him according to His greatness and loftiness, for He is exalted and lifted up beyond what the mouth can speak.
Nehemiah.translator_note: The printed abbreviation ד"א is read as *davar acher* (“another explanation”).

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: gavest him the name of Abraham
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Ve-samta* — its accent is above, on the *shin*, because its meaning is in the past tense.
Nehemiah.translator_note: The word *lemalah* (“above”) is translated literally; how it describes the position of the accent is not certain.

Nehemiah.english_translation: *Ve-karot immo* — a passive form.
*Ki hezidu* — for they acted wickedly against them, as in “for in the thing wherein they dealt proudly against them” (Exodus 18).
Nehemiah.translator_note: The quotation is Exodus 18:11 (JPS: “yea, for that they dealt proudly against them”); Rashi’s printed wording differs slightly and is translated as printed.

Nehemiah.english_translation: *Shem* — *ratzon* in the vernacular.
Nehemiah.translator_note: Old French. Darmesteter lists this word at Nehemiah 9:10 (“renom”), in the form רנום; the printed form (רצון) differs.

Nehemiah.english_translation: *Yomam* — every single day.
*Ve-dabber* — like *ve-ladabber* (“and to speak”), as is said “Out of heaven He made thee to hear His voice, that He might instruct thee” (Deuteronomy 4).
Nehemiah.translator_note: The quotation is Deuteronomy 4:36 (JPS: “Out of heaven He made thee to hear His voice, that He might instruct thee”).

Nehemiah.english_translation: *Lera'avam* — from *ra'av* (“hunger”) one says *lera'avam*, like from *tzama* (“thirst”) *litz'amam*.

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: which Thou hadst lifted up Thy hand
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Asher nasata et yadkha* — with an oath, as in “which I lifted up My hand to give it” (Exodus 6).
Nehemiah.translator_note: The quotation is Exodus 6:8 (JPS: “concerning which I lifted up My hand to give it”).

Nehemiah.english_translation: *Bemiram* — because of their rebelliousness.

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: to lead them in the way
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Behaderekh* — like *baderekh* (“in the way”).
*Lefe'ah* — like to be at one corner-side, divided apart without mixing with the nations of the lands.
*Vattakhna* — and You subdued.
*Ve-atah mishamayim tishma* — You were hearing.

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: didst Thou extend mercy unto them
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Vatimshokh aleihem* — You drew out mercy upon them, so as not to destroy them.

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: all that is come upon us
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Al kol habba* — for all the work of Your evil chastisements that have come upon us.
*Hineh anachnu avadim aleha* — for we bring up tribute to all the idolaters.
*Utvu'atah* — of the Land of Israel.
*Marbah* — delicacies of food for the kings of the idolaters.

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: whom Thou hast set over us
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Asher natatah aleinu* — for they rule over us.
*Uvekhol zot* — and despite all this evil that has come upon us, we make a covenant of faith with the Holy One, blessed be He, to believe and to trust in Him.
*Vekhotvim* — and we write in a book to accept His kingship upon us, that it may be a testimony for us.
*Ve-al hachatum* — for most of the great and important among us are signed on the book of the acceptance of the commandments, to be a testimony for us.
*Ve-al hachatumim* — now he proceeds to count those who signed in the book as a testimony to the acceptance of the commandments.

*Nechemyah haTirshata* — it is one name, and this is what I explained (Ezra 2), that the Tirshatha is Nehemiah; and why was he called Tirshatha? Because the Sages permitted him (*hitiru lo*) to drink *yayin nesekh* (libation wine), since he was cupbearer to the king.
Nehemiah.translator_note: The Tirshatha is mentioned in Ezra 2:63 (JPS: “And the Tirshatha said unto them”); the printed reference gives only the chapter.

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: all they that had separated themselves from the peoples of the lands
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Vekhol hanivdal* — these are the proselytes who separated themselves from the religion of the idolaters, to cleave and be joined to the Law of the Holy One, blessed be He, and to keep His commandments.
*Al acheihem* — with their brethren.
*Addireihem* — the great ones among them.
*Hammakkachot* — the merchandise.
*Shever* — grain, like “in the *sheber* that they break (*shovrim*)” (Genesis 46).
Nehemiah.translator_note: The printed quotation could not be matched to a verse, and the printed reference “Genesis 46” is not confirmed; it is translated as printed.

Nehemiah.english_translation: *Uvyom kodesh* — of a festival day (*yom tov*).
Nehemiah.translator_note: The printed abbreviation י"ט is read as *yom tov* (“festival day”).

Nehemiah.english_translation: *Venatosh et hashanah hashevi'it* — as in the matter that is said “and the seventh year thou shalt let it drop (*tishmetenah*) and leave it (*unteshtah*)” (Exodus 23).
Nehemiah.translator_note: The quotation is Exodus 23:11 (JPS: “but the seventh year thou shalt let it rest and lie fallow”); Rashi’s printed wording is shorter than the verse and is translated as printed.

Nehemiah.english_translation: *Umassa khol yad* — the remission of the loan in the seventh year.

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: all the work of the house of our God
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Vekhol melekhet beit Eloheinu* — to be done out of the money.
*Hipalnu* — how much each one would bring.
*Korban ha-etzim* — the offering of the wood of the fire-pile (*ma'arakhah*) for the altar.
*Levet avotenu* — which is the house of the holiness of our fathers.

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: the first-fruits of all fruit of all manner of trees
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Uvikkurei kol peri kol etz* — the first-fruits of all the fruit of the tree are from the words of the Sages.

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: unto the priests, to the chambers of the house of our God
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Navi lakohanim el lishkot* — for there they were accustomed (to bring them).

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: take the tithes in all the cities of our tillage
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Hamma'asrim bekhol arei avodatenu* — for they take their tithes in all the cities of Israel.
Nehemiah.translator_note: The printed text abbreviates the word מעשרותיה'; it is read as “their tithes.”

Nehemiah.english_translation: *Be'asser* — language of *ba'asor* (“in the tenth”).
*Et ma'aser hamma'aser* — for the Levites would tithe a tithe from the tithe and bring it to the priests, who did not forsake the Temple.
*Echad min ha'asarah* — of Israel, that they might dwell in Jerusalem to guard the city.
*Vetesha hayadot* — nine portions of Israel.
*Hammitnaddevim* — whose spirit moved them to dwell in Jerusalem to guard the city against the enemies.

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: chiefs of the province that dwelt in Jerusalem
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Ve-eleh roshei hamedinah asher yashevu viYerushalayim* — this is what is said immediately after: “And in Jerusalem dwelt certain of the children of Judah,” etc.
*Mibbenei Yehudah Atayah* etc. — he returns and specifies who and who were of the children of Judah; and the whole section counts only the great and important among them.
*Pakid* — appointed.
*Mishneh* — after (the overseer).

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: the ruler of the house of God
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Nagid* — appointed.

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: the ruler of the house of God
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Nagid beit haElohim* — appointed over the house of God.

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: their brethren that did the work of the house
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Ve-acheihem oseh hamelakhah labayit* — and their companions who were performing the service of the house and its offerings.
*Rashim la-avot* — heads of a father’s house from the families of the priests.
*Ufakid aleihem* — appointed over them.

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: the outward business of the house of God
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Al hamelakhah hachitzonah* — that belongs to the house, such as the building of the repair of the house and the wood for the altar fire, which they brought from outside.

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: who was the chief to begin the thanksgiving in prayer
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Rosh hatchilah Yehudah letefilah* — he was head and appointed and great, to open first the giving of thanks in prayer and in the songs of the Levites’ singing. *Yehudah* is like *yodeh* (“would give thanks”), and the *heh* enters the word needlessly, like *Yosef — Yehosef*.
Nehemiah.translator_note: The printed text abbreviates וממונ' as “and appointed” (וממונה). The comparison *Yosef — Yehosef* is printed without a reference.

Nehemiah.english_translation: *Vehasho'arim* — appointed over the gates of the Temple.
*Ish benachalato* — each one dwelt in his inheritance.
*Be-Ofel* — a certain place that is in Jerusalem.
*Al hannetinim* — appointed over the Nethinim.

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: The overseer also of the Levites at Jerusalem
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Ufekid haLevi'im* — appointed over the Levites who are in Jerusalem.

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: over the business of the house of God
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Leneged melekhet* — he was appointed over the work of the house, such as the building of the repair of the house, and other matters for which they spend money for the work (for the tithe) of the house, as in the matter that is said above, “and Shabbethai and Jozabad … over the outward business,” etc.
Nehemiah.translator_note: The words “(for the tithe)” (למעשר) are a later printed insertion, set beside the printed word למעשה (“for the work”). The quotation is Nehemiah 11:16 (JPS: “and Shabbethai and Jozabad, of the chiefs of the Levites, who had the oversight of the outward business of the house of God”).

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: For there was a commandment from the king concerning them
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Ki mitzvat hamelekh aleihem* — and the king trusted them.
*Al hamsho'rerim* — to spend money from the treasury of King Darius.
*Devar yom beyomo* — in order to do the needs of the house.
*Leyad hamelekh* — he was adjacent (*mitzran*) to the counsel of King Darius.
Nehemiah.translator_note: The word *mitzran* is translated literally as “adjacent”; its exact sense here is not certain.

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: in all matters concerning the people
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Lekhol davar* — in all their matters that belong to the people, to speak about them to the king.

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: certain courses in Judah were joined to Benjamin
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Machlekot Yehudah liVnyamin* — they were divided in their divisions this way and that in the land of Judah and Benjamin.
*Veyeshua* — he is Joshua the High Priest.
*Bimei Yeshua* — for they were chiefs in the days of Joshua the High Priest.
*Haydot* — of the musical instruments, to say song.

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: were over against them in wards
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Lemishmarot* — as we find (in I Chronicles 24 and onward) that the Levites were divided into twenty-four wards.
*Veyeshua holid et Yoyakim* etc. — all these in this verse were High Priests.

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: And in the days of Joiakim were priests
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Uvimei Yoyakim* — who was High Priest, there were these priests; they were chiefs, heads of a father’s house of their wards.

*Lesrayah Meraiah* — for the ward of Seraiah, Meraiah was head of a father’s house; and for the ward of Jeremiah, Hananiah was head of a father’s house; and so all of them. And those whom he did not specify, of all the twenty-four wards, Scripture was not careful in this to count them all.

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: The Levites in the days of Eliashib
Nehemiah.english_translation: *HaLevi'im bimei Elyashiv* — these Levites were heads of a father’s house in the wards of the Levites in the days of Eliashib the High Priest; and the priests counted above, immediately before, they were heads of fathers’ houses in their wards also in the days of Eliashib.

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: in the reign of Darius the Persian
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Al malkhut* — in the days of the reign of Darius this thing was.

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: even until the days of Johanan the son of Eliashib
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Ve-ad yemei Yochanan* — all those who were heads of fathers among the Levites until the days of Johanan the High Priest are counted there in Chronicles.
*Mishmar le'ummat mishmar* — for they were divided into their wards to say song.
*Sho'arim mishmar* — they were porters in their ward, to guard the gates of the House.

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: at the store-houses of the gates
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Be-asuppei* — like *bis'ippei hasha'arim* (“at the thresholds of the gates”).

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: These were in the days of Joiakim
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Eleh bimei Yoyakim* — these were porters in the days of Joiakim.

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: at the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Uvchanukkat chomat Yerushalayim* — at the completion of the wall of the city, to sanctify the city.
*Uvtodot* — and with acknowledgments.

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: out of the Plain round about Jerusalem
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Umin hakikkar* — the singers came from the surroundings of Jerusalem.
*Vayyitharu* — first they purified themselves, and afterward they purified others.
*Ve-et hasha'arim ve-et hachomah* — so that there should be no impurity there in the city.

*Me'al lachomah* — for he sanctified the city; and the princes went, and the court, and the priests and the Levites, with two thanksgiving-loaves, around the city, all as explained in tractate Shevuot, in order to sanctify the city.

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: two great companies that gave thanks
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Shtei todot* — two loaves of thanksgiving; each loaf is called *todah*.
*Uttehalukhot layamin* — and when they went out of the city in order to go around it, they went toward its right side.
*Yehudah uVinyamin* — they were two princes.
*Ve-echav* — the companions of Zechariah the priest.
*Ve-al sha'ar ha-ayin* — in front of the Fountain Gate they went around the city.
*Unegdam alu* — and before them they went up from the Fountain Gate to the steps of the City of David, and those steps belonged to the wall.

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: the other company of them that gave thanks
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Vehatodah hasheniyah hahole'khet lemul* — another thanksgiving company, which was second to its fellow, was going opposite its fellow, evenly, and not one behind the other.
*Va-ani acharehah* — and I would go after it, that of the thanksgiving.
*Ve-amedu* — there they stood, so as not to go any further.

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: the two companies of them that gave thanks
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Shtei hatodot* — whom they bore to the Temple.
Nehemiah.translator_note: The printed abbreviation בהמ"ק is read as *Beit HaMikdash* (“the Temple”).

Nehemiah.english_translation: *Bachatzotzerot* — they sounded them out of their joy.
*Vayyippakedu* — language of appointment (*pekidut*).
*Hannishkot* — like the chambers of the Temple.
*Likhnos bahem* — and in those chambers they put all the gifts of the priests and Levites, and from there they divided among them.

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: the portions appointed by the law
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Minaot* — like *manot* (“portions”).
*Lakohanim laLevi'im* — the priests took what was due to them, and the Levites what was due to them.
*Ha'omdim* — and serving there before the Holy One, blessed be He, with thanksgivings and acknowledgments.
*Minyot* — like *manot* (“portions”).
*Umakdishim laLevi'im* — they gave in tithe to the Levites, and they took a tithe from the tithe and gave it to the priests.
*Kol erev* — every mixture of the idolaters, like “And a mixed multitude (*erev rav*) went up also with them” (Exodus 12).
Nehemiah.translator_note: The quotation is Exodus 12:38 (JPS: “And a mixed multitude went up also with them”).

Nehemiah.english_translation: *Ulifnei mizeh* — and previously.
*Karov leTovyah* — this Eliashib the priest was a relative of Tobiah, the companion of Sanballat, and the priest placed Tobiah’s vessels there.
*Va-ya'as* — Eliashib.
*Lefanim* — there they used to put them, before I came to Jerusalem.

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: given by commandment to the Levites
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Mitzvat haLevi'im* — gifts due to the Levites.
*Uvekhol zeh* — and in all this matter I came to the king and returned to Babylon.

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: asked I leave of the king
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Nish'alti* — that he give me permission to go up to Jerusalem and to return.
*Va-omerah* — I commanded to cleanse, “and they cleansed the chambers,” and so on.
*Minyot* — portions (*manot*).
*Lo nitenah* — for Israel had not given the gifts there, and therefore they fled and went this way and that to ask for their gifts, and were not so occupied with their service.
*Va-akabtzem* — I gathered the priests and the Levites to set them at their post in their service, and all Israel brought them their gifts there.
*Ki ne'emanim* — they were (counted faithful) to distribute the gifts among them.
*Ha'aremot* — sheaves of grain.
*Va-aid* — I warned them not to do it.
*Beyom mikhram tzayid* — on the day when they sold food and *tzayid*; *tzayid* is like “and gave them provision (*tzeidah*) for the way” (Genesis 48).
Nehemiah.translator_note: The printed reference “Genesis 48” does not contain these words; they are found at Genesis 45:21 (JPS: “and gave them provision for the way”).

Nehemiah.english_translation: *Vehatzurim* — merchants of Tyre bringing fish to sell.

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: began to be dark before the sabbath
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Vayehi ka-asher tzalelu* — when the shadows of the eve of the Sabbath stretched over the gates, I commanded to shut the doors of the city so that they would not be opened until after the Sabbath, so that the peddlers would not come into the city to sell their wares, so that Israel would not profane the Sabbath through them.
*Vayalinu* — and the peddlers and merchants lodged on the Sabbath day outside Jerusalem once and twice, so that the children of Israel would come to open the gates and buy from them on the Sabbath.
*Va-omerah aleihem* — I warned those peddlers.
*Im tashnu* — if you continue to do it a second time.
*Min ha'et* — from that day onward they did not come on the Sabbath day.
*Hoshivu nashim* — who had taken wives of the idolaters for themselves.

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: spoke half in the speech of Ashdod
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Chetzi medabber* — many of their sons spoke the language of the Ashdodites like their mothers.
*Va-akkeh* — I gave them lashes, to scourge them in order to rebuke them and to remind them.

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: even him did the foreign women cause to sin
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Gam oto hecheti'u* — all the more so will you be sinning through your wives who are idolaters; and this is what is said immediately after, “and shall we hearken to you,” etc., in astonishment; that is, Solomon king of Israel was found to have sinned through his wives who were idolaters, and you have taken wives who are idolaters, to be sinners.
Nehemiah.translator_note: The abbreviation ע"י is read as “through.” The quoted words are from Nehemiah 13:27 (JPS: “Shall we then hearken unto you to do all this great evil”).

Nehemiah.english_lemma_JPS: was son-in-law to Sanballat the Horonite
Nehemiah.english_translation: *Umibbenei Yoyada* — one of the sons of Joiada was son-in-law to Sanballat, the persecutor of the Jews; and I drove him away from me, so that he would not be accustomed to Jerusalem on account of his father-in-law, to see the city and its exits and its entrances.
*Zochrah lahem* — the good that they did.
*Be'ittim* — at times they used to cut wood for the altar fire.
*Ulevikkurim* — that they brought first-fruits in a single period (*perek*); for each and every thing I fixed its time.
Nehemiah.translator_note: The word *perek* (“chapter, period”) is translated as “period”; the sense is not certain.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Adam, Seth, Enosh
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Adam, Shet, Enosh* — Ezra wrote this book of genealogy by means of Haggai, Zechariah and Malachi, within eighteen years, from the time when Zerubbabel and Joshua the priest came to Jerusalem in the days of Cyrus the First until Cyrus son of Esther came; and all of it is on account of the lineage of King David; and the Levites, for the porters and for the guards and for the singers, how David set them in their station, and the priests for their wards. Therefore he traces their lineage from Adam until Abraham; and since it was necessary to trace Abraham’s lineage, he also mentioned the other idolaters, his sons and his sons’ sons; and on account of his sons it was necessary to trace the other idolaters, the sons of Canaan, to make known how Abraham inherited their land; and since it was necessary to mention and trace the generations of Canaan, he mentioned on top of them (the generations of) the other idolaters; and he mentions them little by little and casts them aside until he reaches the main thing, as it is explained in Bereshit Rabbah: a parable of a man who was passing from place to place and a pearl fell from him; and the man stood and sifted the dust in a sieve until he found the pearl. So said the Holy One, blessed be He: What have I to do with tracing Shem, and Arpachshad, etc., and Terah? Only to find Abraham: “and foundest his heart faithful (before Thee).” And out of respect for Isaac he traced the sons of Esau and Ishmael and the sons of Keturah, and he casts them aside little by little and leaves them. And the sons of Seir the Horite he mentions because “the sons of Esau inherited them”; and also to trace Timna, who became a concubine to the sons of Abraham, to make known the praise of Abraham, that she was a daughter of princes and chiefs and wished to be a concubine to the seed of Abraham, as it is written “and Lotan’s sister was Timna” (Genesis 37), and it is written “and Timna was a concubine” (there); but [it is] because she said: If I am not worthy to be married to him as a wife, I will be a concubine to him. And furthermore, therefore he traced the sons of Seir, for they were chiefs and kings, and Mount Seir was Seir’s, and out of the love of Isaac the Holy One, blessed be He, gave it to Esau, as it is written “and the sons of Esau shall inherit them, and dwell in their stead” (Deuteronomy 2:12); and to make known the fulfilment of the words of the Holy One, blessed be He, who said to Isaac to multiply his seed and to make him rule over all; and for the sake of Isaac’s honor he wrote likewise “And these are the kings that reigned in the land of Edom,” etc. (below, 1).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed phrases “Cyrus the First” and “Cyrus son of Esther” are translated as printed, and the identifications were not confirmed. The words “(the generations of)” and “(before Thee)” and the references in parentheses are later printed insertions. The quotation “and foundest his heart faithful before Thee” is Nehemiah 9:8 (printed without a reference). The printed “Genesis 37” is incorrect: “and Lotan’s sister was Timna” is Genesis 36:22, and “and Timna was a concubine” is Genesis 36:12 (JPS: “And Timna was concubine to Eliphaz Esau’s son”); the printed text says she was a concubine “to the sons of Abraham,” where the verse names Eliphaz, Esau’s son. Deuteronomy 2:12 (JPS: “but the children of Esau succeeded them; and they destroyed them from before them, and dwelt in their stead”) is quoted in a different tense from JPS. The last reference is 1 Chronicles 1:43. The printed abbreviation ב"ר is read as Bereshit Rabbah. The printed abbreviation עכומ"ז is read as “idol-worshippers” (עובדי כוכבים ומזלות) and rendered “idolaters.”

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Adam, Seth, Enosh
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Adam, Shet, Enosh* — its meaning is like “the sons of Adam: Seth, and the sons of Seth: Enosh”; and because it is not the main lineage, he abbreviates them. And that he did not mention Cain and Abel is because they did not establish descendants; but from Seth came the generations of Noah and Abraham, and from Abraham until David.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Noah, Shem, Ham
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Noach, Shem, Cham* — and he should have counted the sons of Shem immediately, to find the pearl of Abraham, etc., until David, and cast aside the secondary and abbreviate its lineage and take hold of the main thing; and so is the way of all this genealogy of Chronicles. And so immediately below: “The sons of Abraham: Isaac and Ishmael. These are their generations: the first-born of Ishmael, Nebaioth,” etc.; “And Abraham begot Isaac. The sons of Isaac: Esau and Israel. The sons of Esau: Eliphaz,” for he mentions first the secondary in order to trace it, and afterward the main one.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotations are 1 Chronicles 1:28, 1:29, 1:34 and 1:35.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Ashkenaz, and Diphath
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ashkenaz* and *Difat* (with a *dalet*) — and in the Pentateuch it is written (Genesis 17) *Rifat*, for at first they were weak (*rafin*) and did not overcome Israel, and in the end they were filled with blemish (*dofi*) and shakiness (*ri'u'a*).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed reference “Genesis 17” is incorrect; the name is at Genesis 10:3 (JPS: “Ashkenaz, and Riphath, and Togarmah”). The parentheses “(with a *dalet*)” and the reference are later printed insertions.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the sons of Javan
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uvnei Yavan Elishah* — and as for his not mentioning Magog and Madai: because he mentioned only the lineage; but the sons of Magog and the sons of Madai he did not mention, because the heads of the idolaters did not come out from them; rather all idolaters were called by the name of Kittim and Dodanim.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The first clause is translated as printed. Verse 5 itself lists Magog and Madai among the sons of Japheth; their own sons are not listed, which fits the rest of the comment.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Rodanim
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Verodanim* — and further on (there) he says *Vedodanim*: when Israel sin, they come and rule (*rodim*) over them, and when Israel’s hand is strong they say: “You are the sons of our cousins (*dodeinu*).” At first they appeared as lovers at the time of their benefit, and in the end they rule over them.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The parallel is Genesis 10:4 (JPS: “Elishah, and Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim”); the printed “(there)” is a later insertion.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: he began to be a mighty one in the earth
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Hu hechel liheyot gibbor ba'aretz* — he began to make wars and feats of valor in the earth.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: And Mizraim begot Ludim
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *U-Mitzrayim yalad et Ludim* — in Bereshit Rabbah: Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said: every *monigna* of Egypt is only at the sea (*yam*). Rabbi Joshua ben Korchah said: in Divrei HaYamim *Ludim* is written *Ludiyim*, with two *yods*, to tell you: *Ludiyim* — Ludei-yam (Luds of the sea); *Anamim* — Anamei-yam; *Lehavim* — Lehavei-yam; *Naftuchim* — Naftuchei-yam.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The word מוניגנא (*monigna*) is left transliterated because I could not translate it. The printed abbreviations are read: בב"ר “in Bereshit Rabbah”, א"ר “said Rabbi”, בד"ה “in Divrei HaYamim (Chronicles)”.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Pathrusim
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Patrusim* — Patrusei-yam; *Kasluchim* — Kasluchei-yam; *Pelishtim* — Pelishtei-yam; *Kaftorim* — Kaftorei-yam. Therefore it is written with two *yods*, to expound; and so all of them.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: And Canaan begot Zidon
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uchna'an yalad* etc. — they are eleven, and Canaan with them makes twelve; and that is what is written “He set the borders of the peoples according to the number of the children of Israel” (Deuteronomy 32:8) — that is, He set borders of peoples corresponding to the tribes of Israel, who also are twelve; corresponding to the tribes of Israel He set borders of peoples, like “which thou hast set (*hitzavta*) by themselves” (Genesis 21:29).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: Check of the count: the descendants of Canaan listed in 1 Chronicles 1:13–16 are Zidon, Heth, the Jebusite, the Amorite, the Girgashite, the Hivite, the Arkite, the Sinite, the Arvadite, the Zemarite and the Hamathite, which is eleven. Deuteronomy 32:8 (JPS: “He set the borders of the peoples According to the number of the children of Israel”) and Genesis 21:29 (JPS: “which thou hast set by themselves”) are correct.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: for in his days the earth was divided
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki vimav nifleghah ha'aretz* — the days of the creatures were divided and diminished; for at first people lived nine hundred years and more, and in the days of Arpachshad and onward they were halved to four hundred years and more, and from Peleg onward they were halved to two hundred out of those four hundred.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: Check against the text: Genesis 11:12–13 gives Arpachshad 35 + 403 = 438 years, and Genesis 11:18–19 gives Peleg 30 + 209 = 239 years.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: All these were the sons of Joktan
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Kol eleh benei Yoktan* — for they were from one who diminished his dealings (*miktin asakav*). Eber was a great prophet, but other names were not given to be expounded, for it was not by the word of a prophet that names were given to them.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed abbreviation ע"פ is read as *al pi* (“by the word of”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Shem, Arpachshad, Shelah
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Shem, Arpachshad, Shelach* — above he counted the sons of Shem, and now he began again another time on account of the honor of Abraham; a parable of a man who a pearl fell from him, etc., as above.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Abram—the same is Abraham
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Avram hu Avraham* — now he traces from Shem to Abraham; and who is this Abram who is called Abraham?

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Abraham’s concubine
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Keturah pilegesh Avraham* — every disgrace that he can tell about them he tells, on account of the honor of Isaac, for all of them were sons of a concubine, but he was the main one and the master of the house.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the sons of Midian: Ephah, and Epher
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uvnei Midyan Eifah ve-Efer* etc. — five heads of idolaters; therefore they set up five kings for each nation, a kingdom (*malkah*), as it is written “Evi, and Rekem, and Zur, and Hur,” etc., “the five kings of Midian” (Numbers 31).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The word *malkah* is translated as “a kingdom” and the sentence literally; its sense is not certain. The quotation is Numbers 31:8 (JPS: “Evi, and Rekem, and Zur, and Hur, and Reba, the five kings of Midian”); the printed reference “Numbers 31” is incomplete. The printed abbreviation עכומ"ז is read as “idol-worshippers” (עובדי כוכבים ומזלות) and rendered “idolaters.”

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: All these were the sons of Keturah
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Kol eleh benei Keturah* — for the sake of Abraham’s honor.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: The sons of Isaac: Esau, and Israel
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Benei Yitzchak Esav veYisrael* — out of the honor of David he said Israel and not Jacob.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: The sons of Esau: Eliphaz
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Benei Esav Elifaz* — in order to abbreviate and cast him aside; and he mentioned him in honor of Isaac.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Hamran, and Eshban
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Chamran ve-Eshban* — and in the Pentateuch (Genesis 36) it is written *Chemdan*: at first they were desirable (*chamudim*) and coveted, like righteous men, and at the end ugly like a donkey (*chamor*); so is the way of the donkey: at first desirable, and at the end it becomes ugly; and the horse is at first ugly and at the end beautiful.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The Pentateuch reading is Genesis 36:26 (JPS: “Hemdan and Eshban and Ithran and Cheran”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: these are the kings that reigned in the land of Edom
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve-eleh hamelakhim* — it is explained in Bereshit Rabbah: Rabbi Ivo said: before a king stood up from Israel (but after a king reigned over Israel) a king was set up in Edom. Rabbi Yose ben Chanina says: at the time when this one sets up kings, that one sets up judges; this one sets up chiefs, that one sets up princes. Rabbi Joshua ben Levi said: this one set up eight and that one set up eight. And I heard: but did Edom have only these eight kings, and Israel eight? Were there not more — Joram, Ahaziah, Joash, etc.? Rather, “this one set up eight kings” means: from the time that those eight kings of Edom were crowned, they did not crown the kings of Israel, for it was before David, “and the heads of his father’s house.”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The last clause (“and the heads of his father’s house”) is translated literally and its sense is not clear to me. The words in the first parentheses are a later printed insertion. The printed abbreviation ב"ר is read as Bereshit Rabbah. Audit 5 source check: a passage with the same wording (7 consecutive words) is found in Bereshit Rabbah 83.2 (Sefaria Hebrew text, labelled Public Domain). This is a wording match only; the translation was not changed.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: wicked in the sight of the LORD
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ra be-einei Hashem* — it is explained in Bereshit Rabbah that he was ploughing in gardens (and a cave for dung-heaps); he came upon her not in the natural way.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The words in parentheses are a later printed insertion; the passage is translated literally. The printed abbreviation ב"ר is read as Bereshit Rabbah.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Tamar his daughter-in-law
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve-Tamar kallato* — I wonder how he mentions the disgrace of David’s grandmother.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Ethan, and Heman, and Calcol, and Dara
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve-Eitan ve-Heiman ve-Kalkol ve-Dara* — all of them were in the days of David and in the days of Solomon, and they were exceedingly wise, and concerning this it is said (Kings I 5:11) “and he was wiser than all men, than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Heman, and Calcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol.” Below, concerning Solomon’s wisdom, this wording *Darda* occurs, although he is called *dor de'ah* (“generation of knowledge”) on account of his wisdom; Solomon became wiser than all of them. And as for what is said *ha-Ezrachi*, the *aleph* is superfluous, like *ha-Zarchi* (Numbers 27): “came out of the east” (*mizrach yatza*); and in many places an *aleph* enters a word and is not pronounced, and its parallels (Job 13) *ve-achvati*, and (Isaiah 9) *ve-he'aznichu*, and so *ha-asafsuf* (Numbers 11); and sometimes it is missing, like *vatamru* (Samuel II 19), *vayaku haRammim* (below, II 22), like *ha-Arammim*. And the Pesikta expounds: “than all men” — this is Adam the first; Ethan — this is Abraham; Heman — this is Moses; Calcol — this is Joseph; and Darda — this is the generation of the wilderness; Mahol — because He forgave (*machal*) them the deed of the calf.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The sentence about *Darda* and *dor de'ah* is translated literally and is not fully clear to me. The references are as follows. “Numbers 27” is incorrect; *ha-Zarchi* is Numbers 26:13 (JPS: “the family of the Zerahites”). “Job 13” is Job 13:17 (JPS: “let my declaration be in your ears”). “Isaiah 9” is incorrect; *ve-he'aznichu* is Isaiah 19:6 (JPS: “And the rivers shall become foul”). “Numbers 11” is Numbers 11:4 (JPS: “the mixed multitude”). “Samuel II 19” for *vatamru* could not be confirmed. “Below, II 22” is 2 Chronicles 22:5 (JPS: “the Arameans wounded Joram”). I Kings 5:11 is correctly cited.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Achar, the troubler of Israel
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uvnei Karmi Achar* — and why do I call him Achar, when Achan is his name? (And it is explained) because he troubled (*akhar*) Israel, for he transgressed the ban and thirty-six (thousand) men fell through him; and this is what I explained, that whatever he can tell in disgrace he tells (and nevertheless) (ס"א “and therefore not”) kingship came forth from them.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The parentheses are later printed insertions, and the abbreviation ס"א is left as printed because I could not confirm its meaning. The printed “(thousand)” does not agree with Joshua 7:5 (JPS: “about thirty and six men”). The last sentence is translated literally and is not clear to me.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the sons of Ethan: Azariah
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uvnei Eitan Azaryah* — like “and the sons of Dan: Hushim” (Genesis 43).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed reference “Genesis 43” is incorrect; the quotation is Genesis 46:23 (JPS: “And the sons of Dan: Hushim”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Chelubai
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve-et Kelubai* — this is Caleb, as is proved below, “and Caleb the son of Hezron”; and in the book of Samuel (I Samuel 25) it is written “and he was *Kalibbi*,” and the Targum [renders] “of the house of Caleb”; and so the Targum of *Kalibbi*: he was strong, and boasted of himself that no one in any tribe was as well-born as he, that is, if Samuel gave him kingship (“to me the kingship will come”); and therefore it is said “Who is David and who is the son of Jesse? Today servants abound,” for he came from Ruth the Moabitess, and Jerahmeel his brother took a foreign woman, as written below; and this Chelubai exalts himself and boasts with (all) that his heart lifted him.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The comment is translated literally and is not clear to me in several places (the Targum explanation of *Kalibbi* and the sentence “if Samuel gave him kingship”). The quotation “and he was of the house of Caleb” is 1 Samuel 25:3, and “Who is David? and who is the son of Jesse? there are many servants now-a-days” is 1 Samuel 25:10 (JPS wording).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Nahshon, prince of the children of Judah
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Nachshon nesi benei Yehudah* — he came to specify this only on account of the honor of David.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Salma begot Boaz
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve-Salma holid et Bo'az* — our Rabbis said: Ibzan is Boaz. And there is a wonder: how can it be? For Nahshon died in the second year after the exodus from Egypt, and Salmon his son was already dead — and he was among those who came into the land — and Boaz his son, who is Ibzan, was born at the entering into the land; and from the exodus from Egypt until Jephthah were three hundred years. And the Sages said: at the time that Boaz came to Ruth and she conceived, Boaz died at once; and Ibzan was a judge after the death of Jephthah, as written (Judges 12:8) “And after him Ibzan of Beth-lehem judged Israel.” And at this I wonder, for we find that Abram said, after his blood was bound up (*shenitzrar damo*), etc., “Shall a child be born to him that is a hundred years old?” — so how did Boaz beget at three hundred years? And it is to be said: therefore it says (Ruth 4:13) “and the LORD gave her conception”; its parallel is “and the LORD showed him” (Deuteronomy 32:46). *Ibzan*: *av* (“father”) of all the *tzenunim* (“the chilled ones”), for a young woman lay beside him and he became chilled and did not touch her. (ס"א)
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The comment is translated literally and is obscure in places. The printed reference (Deuteronomy 32:46) does not contain “and the LORD showed him”; those words are at Deuteronomy 34:1 (JPS: “And the LORD showed him all the land”). The quotation “Shall a child be born unto him that is a hundred years old?” is Genesis 17:17 (printed without a reference); “three hundred years” is as in Judges 11:26. The final ס"א is left as printed because I could not confirm its meaning.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Jesse begot his first-born Eliab
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve-Ishai holid et bekhoro* — written fully with an *aleph* (*Ishai*), meaning “a mighty man of valor” (*ish gibbor chayil*).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: David the seventh
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *David hashvi'i* — written fully with a *yod* (*Davi*d), on account of the honor of David; and now he has found the pearl; therefore he did not count the eighth, Elihu.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: their sisters were Zeruiah and Abigail
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve-achyoteihem Tzeruyah va-Avigayil* — on account of the honor of David, for the sons of his sister were mighty men and men of valor and chiefs; so it is explained.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Jether the Ishmaelite
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Yeter hayishme'eli* — (and in Samuel II 17) it is written “the Israelite”; he dwelt in the land of Ishmael, like Obed-edom the Gittite (there, II 6), and so (Kings I 6) “and the king sent and took Hiram from Tyre, the son of a widow woman, and his father was a man of Tyre.”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: Samuel II 17 is 2 Samuel 17:25 (JPS: “Ithra the Jesraelite”); Rashi’s printed word is “Israelite” and is translated as printed. The reference to Obed-edom is 2 Samuel 6:10 (JPS: “the house of Obed-edom the Gittite”). The printed “Kings I 6” is incorrect; Hiram is at 1 Kings 7:13–14 (JPS 7:14: “He was the son of a widow … and his father was a man of Tyre”), and Rashi’s sentence is a paraphrase.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Caleb the son of Hezron begot children of Azubah
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vekhalev ben Chetzron holid et Azuvah ishah* — because he had a wife whose name was Azubah, therefore he called the name of his daughter Azubah Ishah, as it is written “And Azubah died, and Caleb took unto him Ephrath”; from this [it appears] that he had a wife whose name was Azubah.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: Rashi’s reading takes *Azubah ishah* as a name; JPS renders the Hebrew “children of Azubah his wife.” The comment is translated as printed.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Caleb took unto him Ephrath, who bore him Hur
1 Chronicles.english_translation: [The source prints the lemma only, with no comment.]
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The Hebrew source has only the lemma ותלד לו את חור with no explanation.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Hur begot Uri, and Uri begot Bezalel
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vechur holid et Uri ve-Uri holid et Betzalel* — go and reckon: each of them was less than eight years old when he begot; for Caleb was forty years old at the time of the spies, as it is written (Joshua 14:6–7) “Forty years old was I when [Moses] sent me,” etc., and at that time all of them were already born, for the Tabernacle that Bezalel made had been erected. Caleb was eight when he begot Azubah Ishah, and nine when he begot Jerioth, and after the death of Azubah his wife he took Ephrath, and she bore Hur in another year; so he was ten years old; and Hur was eight when he begot Uri, and Uri was eight when he begot Bezalel; that is twenty-six years. And it is written (Exodus 36:2) “and every wise-hearted man,” and no man is less than thirteen years; so Bezalel at the time he made the Tabernacle was eighteen years old; so forty years less one. It turns out that each one of the five was less than eight when he begot. And so it is explained in the chapter Ben Sorer U-Moreh, and the Midrash: at six and six they begot.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The computation is translated as printed. The sums 10 + 8 + 8 = 26 are correct. With Bezalel at thirteen the total is 39, which is “forty less one”; the printed “eighteen” would give 44, so it does not fit the stated total and may be a misprint. It is translated as printed. The quotations are Joshua 14:7 (JPS: “Forty years old was I when Moses the servant of the LORD sent me from Kadesh-barnea to spy out the land”) and Exodus 36:2 (JPS: “and every wise-hearted man”). The chapter Ben Sorer U-Moreh is printed without a reference.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Hezron went in to the daughter of Machir
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve-achar ba Chetzron el bat Machir* — all this on account of the honor of David; for Hezron came to the daughter of Machir to take her as a concubine, not for marriage, as in the example of “after he had gone in to Bath-sheba” (Psalms 51:2); and he was sixty. Behold two things for the disgrace of the daughter of Machir: one, that he did not take her for marriage, and one, that Hezron was old. Out of respect for the families of Judah they gave her to him; and when he begot Jair, the sons of Machir gave him twenty-three cities, to take one wife from among his daughters.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The last sentence is translated literally and is not clear to me. The quotation is Psalms 51:2 (JPS: “after he had gone in to Bath-sheba”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Geshur and Aram took Havvoth-jair from them
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayikach Geshur va-Aram* — Geshur is the Geshurite and the Maachathite, because they were close to the Arameans, who dwelt in the east of the Land of Israel, and Aram dwelt in the east, as it is written (Isaiah 9) “Aram on the east, and the Philistines on the west”; and in the days of the Judges, when Israel sinned, He delivered them into the hand of the enemy, into the hand of Aram, and then they went (these, ס"א) and took them from them; and when David came he returned them, and because he returned them he wrote them here.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The abbreviation ס"א is left as printed because I could not confirm its meaning; the parenthesis is a later printed insertion. The quotation is Isaiah 9:11 (JPS: “The Arameans on the east, and the Philistines on the west”); the printed reference “Isaiah 9” is incomplete.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Caleb-ephrath
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Bekhalev Efratah* — after the name of (Caleb) his wife they called the city (Caleb) Ephrathah.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The words “(Caleb)” are later printed insertions and are translated as printed.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: bore him Ashhur the father of Tekoa
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vatled lo et Ashchur avi Tekoa'* — after the death of Hezron.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the father of Tekoa
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Avi Tekoa'* — the ruler of the city of Tekoa, which is of the tribe of Judah.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the sons of Jerahmeel the first-born of Hezron
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayihyu venei Yerachme'el bekhor Chetzron* — because he interrupted with the family of Caleb, therefore it was necessary to say “first-born of Hezron,” first-born of Jerahmeel, first-born of Jerahmeel.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed abbreviation ע"כ is read as *al ken* (“therefore”); the repeated final words are translated as printed.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Jerahmeel had another wife, whose name was Atarah
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vatehi ishah acheret leYerachme'el ushmah Atarah* — according to its plain sense she was an Israelite; and in Yevamot of the Yerushalmi it is written that he took a foreign woman to be adorned (*lehitater*) with her; she was beautiful and a noblewoman.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The reference to Yevamot of the Yerushalmi was not checked, and *sherit* is translated literally as “a noblewoman.”

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: she was the mother of Onam
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Hi em Onam* — (I heard) *em* is like “until that I arose a mother in Israel” (Judges 5); (and she was ס"א); Onam was low and weak, from the language of *onen*, and like “I have not eaten thereof in my mourning (*be'oni*)” (Deuteronomy 26) and like “as men that complain (*kemit'onenim*)” (Numbers 11); and from him came Sheshan, who gave his daughter to Yarcha the Egyptian, his servant; and he tells of their disgrace, that is, they were not worthy of kingship; and from him came Ishmael son of Nethaniah son of Elishama, who killed Gedaliah son of Ahikam (Jeremiah 41).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The abbreviation ס"א is left as printed because I could not confirm its meaning; the words in parentheses are later printed insertions. The quotations are Judges 5:7 (JPS: “That thou didst arise a mother in Israel”), Deuteronomy 26:14 (JPS: “I have not eaten thereof in my mourning”), Numbers 11:1 (JPS: “And the people were as murmurers”) and Jeremiah 41:1.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Sheshan had no sons, but daughters
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Velo hayah leSheshan banim ki im banot* — and as for what he said above, “and the sons of Sheshan: Ahlai” — he was sick, low, and died without sons.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 1 Chronicles 2:31 (JPS: “And the sons of Sheshan: Ahlai”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Sheshan gave his daughter to Jarha his servant to wife
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayiten Sheshan et bito leYarcha avdo le-ishah* — from here they said: your daughter has come of age — free your slave and give him to her; and from here the Sages said in Yevamot of the Yerushalmi: Do not trust a convert until fifteen generations; and the fifteen generations are from Attai the Egyptian until Ishmael, and some say sixteen generations with Yarcha; and a midrash of our Rabbis: is it possible so, that he was of the royal seed? Was not Ishmael of the seed of Jerahmeel, and not from Ram? Rather, he passed on some of his seed to Molech.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The comment is translated literally and is obscure in places, and whether the midrash sentence is a statement or a question is not certain. The reference to Yevamot of the Yerushalmi was not checked.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the sons of Caleb the brother of Jerahmeel
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uvnei Kalev achi Yerachme'el* — because he traced above some of the families of Caleb and interrupted with the lineage of Jerahmeel, it is necessary to say “Caleb the brother of Jerahmeel,” so that you will not say that he already traced all the families of Caleb; therefore it was necessary to say “Caleb the brother of Jerahmeel,” for this is not another Caleb. And so is the way of all the genealogy: it does not trace in order, but traces some of the family of so-and-so and takes hold of another family; and when it has traced some of this family it begins to trace the first family as at the beginning, and again the other; so this whole book of genealogy is mixed.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the father of Ziph
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Hu avi Zif* — the ruler of Ziph and the ruler of all the sons of Mareshah and the ruler of Hebron; and the names of these towns are written in the book of Joshua (Joshua 15), as it is written “Ziph, and Telem, and Bealoth,” (and it is written) “Keilah” (there) “and Achzib, and Mareshah.”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotations are Joshua 15:24 (JPS: “Ziph, and Telem, and Bealoth”) and Joshua 15:44 (JPS: “and Keilah, and Achzib, and Mareshah”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the father of Jorkeam
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Avi Yorke'am* — every “father of” said here means the ruler of that city written immediately after.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the sons of Jahdai
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uvnei Yahdai* — he was one of the sons of Ephah; and that he did not mention who his father was is because there is no need to mention any of the sons of Ephah except this Jahdai.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: bore Sheva the father of Machbenah and the father of Gibea
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vatled Sha'af avi Madmannah et Shava avi Machbenah va-avi Giv'a* — these two towns were his.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the daughter of Caleb was Achsah
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uvat Kalev Achsah* — now he begins at the head, and puts Achsah first because she was the wife of Othniel, as it is written there, “And Caleb said: He that smiteth Kiriath-sepher,” etc.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The words occur at Joshua 15:16 and Judges 1:12 (JPS: “He that smiteth Kiriath-sepher, and taketh it, to him will I give Achsah my daughter to wife”); the printed text says only “there.”

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: These were the sons of Caleb
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Eleh hayu benei Kalev ben Chur bekhor Efratah* — its meaning is “These were the sons of Caleb the son of Hur,” like “his son, Hur”; and he, Hur, was his first-born son to Ephrath his wife, and not a first-born to Caleb; and so it is explained above, “and Caleb took unto him Ephrath, and she bore him Hur.” Another version (ע"א): “These were,” etc., Hur was a son of Caleb, and begot a son, and called his name Caleb; therefore its meaning is: “and these were the sons of Caleb, the son of Hur: Shobal,” etc.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The abbreviation ע"א is left as printed because I could not confirm its meaning.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the first-born of Ephrath
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Bekhor Efratah* — and not a first-born to Caleb; he says this about Hur; so it appears to us.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Haroeh, and half of the Menuhoth
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Haro'eh chetzi hamenuchot* — there was a province in the land and Menuchot was its name, as it is written “and they carried them captive to Manahath” (below, 8), and he is the ruler of half of the province; and below it is said “who ruled over half of the province,” the other (half). *Haro'eh*: *formandrifio* in the vernacular.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. The comment is translated as printed and the sentence about “below” is not clear to me. The quotation is 1 Chronicles 8:6 (JPS: “and they were carried captive to Manahath”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the families of Kiriath-jearim
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Umishpechot Kiryat Ye'arim* — the inhabitants of Kiryat Ye'arim.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: of them came the Zorathites, and the Eshtaolites
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Mei'eleh yatze'u haTzor'ati veha-Eshta'uli* — the inhabitants of Zorah. And do not wonder that it is written (Judges 13) “And the spirit of the LORD began to move him between Zorah and Eshtaol,” which implies that these two towns belonged to the sons of Dan, for all these mentioned here were of the sons of Judah; for we can say that the towns and the border that was between Zorah and Eshtaol were Dan’s, but Zorah and Eshtaol themselves were of the sons of Judah.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Judges 13:25 (JPS: “And the spirit of the LORD began to move him in Mahaneh-dan, between Zorah and Eshtaol”); the printed reference “Judges 13” is incomplete.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: The sons of Salma: Beth-lehem
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Benei Salma Beit Lechem* — the sons of Salma were from the inhabitants of Beth-lehem, the Netophathite.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Atroth-beth-joab, and half of the Manahathites
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Atrot beit Yo'av* — and also from the inhabitants of Netophah and Atroth-beth-joab; half of the province of the Manahathite the sons of Zorah took for themselves, and they dwelt in them. They are names of places: from them [came] Maharai the Netophathite, Baanah the Netophathite (Samuel II 23), mighty men of David; and Manahath, “and they carried them captive to Manahath” (below, 8).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The sentence is translated literally and the word *hen* is read as “they are”; its sense is not certain. Maharai the Netophathite is 2 Samuel 23:28; the printed “Baanah the Netophathite” is at 2 Samuel 23:29 (JPS: “Heleb the son of Baanah the Netophathite”). The last quotation is 1 Chronicles 8:6.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the families of scribes that dwelt at Jabez
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Umishpechot soferim* — the inhabitants of Jabez, the company of Jabez, who ruled over them, as it is written below, “And Jabez was more honourable than his brethren.”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 1 Chronicles 4:9.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the Tirathites, the Shimeathites, the Sucathites
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Tir'atim Shim'atim Sukhatim* — all are names of their father’s house.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: These are the Kenites
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Hammah haKinim* — and where is their place? Are they not the inhabitants of Kain, the name of a place, as it is written “Kain, and Gibeah, and Timnah, ten cities” (Joshua 16)?
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed reference “Joshua 16” is incorrect; the quotation is Joshua 15:57 (JPS: “Kain, Gibeah, and Timnah; ten cities with their villages”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: that came of Hammath, the father of the house of Rechab
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Habba'im mechammat avi veit Rechav* — who came out because of Hammath, who was of the house of Rechab, and dwelt in Kain. Another version (ע"א): Jabez is the name of a city and it belonged to Issachar, as it is written “and Rabbith, and Kishion, and Ebez” (there, 19).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The abbreviation ע"א is left as printed because I could not confirm its meaning. The quotation is Joshua 19:20 (JPS: “and Rabbith, and Kishion, and Ebez”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: These are the Kenites
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Hammah haKinim* — refiners: “and he gave it to the refiner (*latzoref*),” its Targum is “to the *kina'ah*” (Judges 17).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Judges 17:4 (JPS: “and gave them to the founder”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Daniel, of Abigail the Carmelitess
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Sheni Daniel la-Avigayil* — and in Samuel (II 3) it is written “and the second, Chileab, of Abigail,” and the Midrash *Vayekhulu* explains: because David married Abigail after the death of Nabal, and they suspected the son of being Nabal’s, therefore David called him two names, Chileab and Daniel: Daniel — *Dani El* (“God has judged me”); Chileab — because he resembled the father entirely.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The reference is 2 Samuel 3:3 (JPS: “and his second, Chileab, of Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite”). The Midrash *Vayekhulu* was not checked.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Ithream by Eglah his wife
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Hashishi Yitre'am le-Eglah ishto* — Midrash: is she alone his wife? Rather she was abundant (*shafa'at*) like a calf (*eglah*) and bore him; and because she was beloved to him like a calf, as in “If you had not plowed with my heifer” (Judges 14); and because of the beloved-ness of Michal, he calls her “his wife.”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The word *shafa'at* is translated literally as “abundant,” and the comment is not fully clear to me. The quotation is Judges 14:18 (JPS: “If you had not plowed with my heifer”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Elishama, and Eliphelet
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve-Elishama ve-Eliphelet* — and Eliada and Eliphelet. In Samuel (II 5) he does not count Eliphelet except once, and he counts only seven, and here he counts nine; and this is the reason: Eliphelet his son died and another son was born to him after that, and his name was likewise called Eliphelet, and this is the one who is counted there; and also Elishama he counts here twice, so likewise we can say that he died and another was born to him; and also one of these died and seven remained, and this is why he counts there only seven, and the nine he counts on account of the honor of David, that he had many sons, for the whole book was written on account of the honor of David and his seed.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: Check of the counts: 1 Chronicles 3:6–8 lists nine names (Ibhar, Elishama, Eliphelet, Nogah, Nepheg, Japhia, Elishama, Eliada, Eliphelet; JPS 3:8 ends “nine”), and 2 Samuel 5:15–16 lists seven (Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Japhia, Elishama, Eliada, Eliphelet).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Ahaziah his son, Joash his son
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Achazyahu b'no Yo'ash* — from Solomon to Joash are eight generations; and because David saw that his seed was ending in the days of Joash through Athaliah, as it is written in this book (II 22) “and she arose and *tedabber*,” in the language of *dever* (pestilence), by means of a deadly drug, he stood in prayer and said this psalm: “For the leader, on the *Sheminith*” — eight strings (ס"א “in number”) — “on the eighth generation”: “Help, LORD; for the godly man ceaseth,” etc. (there); and Joash escaped. And from Joash to Josiah are eight generations, for David saw that Josiah and his sons were all going to destruction — this one was killed and that one had his eyes put out — and he prayed again “on the *Sheminith*,” on the eighth generation: “O LORD, rebuke me not in Thine anger” (there, 6); and because of his prayer the sons of Jehoiakim were left. And in the whole book of Psalms there is no “on the *Sheminith*” except these two. And from Jeconiah (ס"א “and from Jehoiakim”) until Anani are seven, who is the king Messiah, as it is written (Daniel 7) “and behold, with the clouds of heaven”; thirty-eight sons, between sons and generations; the Holy One, blessed be He, did so because he said to the Holy One, blessed be He, thirty-eight praises in the book of Ezra (Chronicles I 29) (and they called it the book of Ezra because Ezra wrote Chronicles, יוש"ה) from “Blessed be the LORD God of Israel,” etc., until “and to make strong” — thirty-eight words.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The abbreviations ס"א (twice) and יוש"ה are left as printed because I could not confirm their meaning; the parentheses are later printed insertions. The printed abbreviation ע"י is read as “through.” The counts of generations, sons and words in this comment were not recomputed. The quotations are 2 Chronicles 22:10 (JPS: “she arose and destroyed all the seed royal”), Psalms 12:1–2 (JPS: “For the Leader; on the Sheminith … Help, LORD; for the godly man ceaseth”), Psalms 6:1–2 (JPS: “O LORD, rebuke me not in Thine anger”), Daniel 7:13 (JPS: “there came with the clouds of heaven One like unto a son of man”) and 1 Chronicles 29:10 (JPS: “Blessed be Thou, O LORD, the God of Israel our father”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Hasadiah, Jushabhesed, five
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vachasadyah Yushav Chesed chamesh* — there were five, besides Shelomith their sister.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Bariah, and Neariah, and Shaphat, six
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uvnei Shemayah Chatush veYigal uVriach uNe'aryah veShafat shishah* — they are only five, and there is a reason in it, as it is written below (25) concerning the wards of the Levites: “Of Jeduthun: the sons of Jeduthun: Gedaliah, and Zeri, and Jeshaiah, Hashabiah, and Mattithiah, six,” and they are only five.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: Check: 1 Chronicles 3:22 names five sons of Shemaiah (Hattush, Igal, Bariah, Neariah, Shaphat), and 1 Chronicles 25:3 names five sons of Jeduthun (Gedaliah, Zeri, Jeshaiah, Hashabiah, Mattithiah), each followed by the word “six.”

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Reaiah the son of Shobal
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve-Re'ayah* — so is the way of this genealogy, even though he has not yet mentioned Reaiah, for he counts generation by generation; and so “the sons of Helah: Zereth, and Izhar, and Ethnan, and Koz begot,” and he has not yet mentioned Koz, and he mentions his sons.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 1 Chronicles 4:7–8 (JPS: “And Koz begot Anub”). The word *kachshiv* (“he counts”) is Aramaic.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Ashhur the father of Tekoa had two wives
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ule-Ashchur avi Tekoa'* — it refers back above, “and the wife of Hezron … bore him Ashhur the father of Tekoa,” for he had not traced [him] until now.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 1 Chronicles 2:24.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Because I bore him with pain
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve-immo karah shemo Ya'abetz* — and he gave him the name Jabez; and its parallel is Ben-oni (ס"א “and his father called him Benjamin”) (Genesis 35).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The abbreviation ס"א is left as printed because I could not confirm its meaning; the parentheses are later printed insertions. The quotation is Genesis 35:18 (JPS: “she called his name Ben-oni; but his father called him Benjamin”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: enlarge my border
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vehirbeita et gevuli* — in inheritances.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: that Thy hand might be with me, and that Thou wouldest work deliverance from evil
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vehayetah yadkha immi ve-asita mera'ah* — if You will be with me and save me from evil, that I not be pained, that no harm or distress or pain befall me; and it was a vow that he vowed.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: that which he requested
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayavei Elohim et asher sha'al* — and he fulfilled his vow; and from here they bring proof when they pledge charity (in the congregation) on account of what one does not vow but gives without a vow; and its midrash is known.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The sentence about pledging charity is translated literally and is not clear to me; the words “(in the congregation)” are a later printed insertion.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Chelub the brother of Shuhah
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve-Kelub achi Shuchah* — he counts families in brief wording (ל'), although he did not mention him above; and so “and the sons of Kenaz,” although he did not mention him above; and so Meonothai, likewise he did not mention; for such is the way of this whole book.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The abbreviation ל' is read as “wording” (לשון) but is not certain.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the father of Ir-nahash
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Avi Ir Nachash* — the name of a city, and Tehinnah was (a) ruler over it.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The word “(was)” is a later printed insertion.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: These are the men of Recah
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Eleh anshei Rechah* — the sons of Eshton dwelt in that place, in Recah. Another version (ע"א): “the men of Recah” — the family was called “the men of Recah.”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The abbreviation ע"א is left as printed because I could not confirm its meaning.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: begot Joab the father of Ge-harashim
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uvrayah holid et Yo'av avi Gei Charashim* — Joab was prince of a valley in which there were craftsmen; and why do I call it “the valley of craftsmen”? Because the explanation of “for they were craftsmen” is that those who dwelt in the valley of the craftsmen were craftsmen, and the valley is called after their name.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the sons of Caleb the son of Jephunneh
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uvnei Kalev ben Yefuneh* — our Rabbis said: Caleb son of Jephunneh is Caleb son of Hezron; and why is he called son of Jephunneh? Because he turned away (*shepinah*) from the counsel of the spies. And do not wonder, for he already traced the family of Caleb son of Hezron, for such is the way, that he traces some and skips another family, and afterward takes hold of the first family.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the sons of Elah: Kenaz
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uvnei Elah u-Kenaz* — such was his name, *U-Kenaz*.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: JPS renders the verse “and the sons of Elah: Kenaz”; Rashi’s meaning (that the name is “Ukenaz”) is translated as printed.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: his wife Hajehudijah
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve-ishto haYehudiyah* — the wife of Caleb, who was born of a Jewess (*Yehudit*).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Jered the father of Gedor
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Yered avi Gedor* etc. — rulers of the towns, as it is written in Joshua, “and Jokdeam, and Zanoah, Halhul, Beth-zur, and Gedor, Jarmuth, and Adullam, Socoh, and Azekah.”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The words are a composite of Joshua 15:56, 15:58 and 15:35 (JPS 15:56: “and Jezreel, and Jokdeam, and Zanoah”; 15:58: “Halhul, Beth-zur, and Gedor”; 15:35: “Jarmuth, and Adullam, Socoh, and Azekah”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: these are the sons of Bithiah the daughter of Pharaoh
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve-eleh benei Bityah bat Par'oh* — the *vav* separates between the sons of Jehudijah and the sons of Bithiah.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: whom Mered took
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Asher lakach Mered* — Caleb is Mered, for he rebelled (*marad*) against the counsel of the spies; and so is the way of the genealogy, that even for one it says “sons,” like “and the sons of Elah, and Kenaz.”

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: The sons of Shelah the son of Judah
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Benei Shelah ben Yehudah* — because they had not yet been traced, he traces them now; for on account of the honor of David he first traces the sons of Tamar, Perez and Zerah, from whom he also came; and now that he has traced all the families of Perez, he begins to trace all the families of Shelah who were in that generation.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the families of the house of them that wrought fine linen
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Umishpachat beit avodat habbutz* — for the curtains of the Sanctuary; they too were of the sons of Shelah.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: and Jokim, and the men of Cozeba
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Veyokim ve-anshei Kezeva* — up to “and Jashubi-lehem,” all these are the sons of Shelah the son of Judah.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Joash, and Saraph
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Veyo'ash ve-Saraf* — our Rabbis say: this is Mahlon and Chilion.
