1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the records are ancient
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vehadevarim atikim* — its meaning: do not say that because I began to trace from the men of our generation, all of them were afterward; rather all those who are said in this verse (the ancient ones) were the first ones, who were in ancient days.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The words “(the ancient ones)” are a later printed insertion.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: who had dominion in Moab
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Asher ba'alu leMo'av* — who took Moabite wives.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: These were the potters
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Hammah hayotzerim* — these, Jokim and the men of Cozeba and the inhabitants of Lehem, were makers of clay vessels for the king’s work, and also pots for the king’s food, and also for the priests.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: those that dwelt among plantations
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Veyoshvei neta'im* — who were occupied with the king’s plantings.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: hedges
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vegederah* — craftsmen, builders of stone fences for the king’s work.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: in the king’s work
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Im hamelekh* — its meaning: the king settled them in those towns because they did his work; an example in Mishpatim (Exodus 22:14): “If the owner thereof be with it (*imo*), he shall not make it good,” that is, with him in his work.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Exodus 22:14 (JPS: “If the owner thereof be with it, he shall not make it good”); the printed text names only the section Mishpatim.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: The sons of Simeon
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Benei Shim'on* — because Simeon dwells in the portion of Judah, he puts him first, to trace him and to speak of his towns before Reuben.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: neither did all their family multiply, like to the children of Judah
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Velo'acheiv ein banim rabbim vekhol mishpachtam lo hirbu ad benei Yehudah* — they did not multiply children like the children of Judah, because they were few, and the portion of Judah was greater than theirs; Judah received Simeon in his portion, for Simeon had no portion in the Land of Israel, as it is said, “I will divide them in Jacob, and scatter them in Israel” (Genesis 49), and we learned in Bereshit Rabbah: “I will divide them” — to establish scribes in Israel in the synagogues, etc. And from where [do we know] that they received? As it is written (Joshua 19:9) “Out of the portion of the children of Judah was the inheritance of the children of Simeon, for the portion of the children of Judah was too much for them; and the children of Simeon had their inheritance within their inheritance,” lest the beast of the field multiply against them. And what is written (there) “And the lot came up for the sons of Simeon” — thus was the matter: they cast lots which tribe would receive Simeon in its portion, and the lot fell in the portion of Judah. And also what is written (Judges 1:3) “And Judah said to Simeon his brother: Come up with me in my lot, and we will fight against the Canaanite, and I too will go with thee” — in the portion that I gave you.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotations are Genesis 49:7 (JPS: “I will divide them in Jacob, And scatter them in Israel”), Joshua 19:9 (the words “lest the beast of the field multiply against them” are Rashi’s addition and are not in that verse), Joshua 19:1 (JPS: “And the second lot came out for Simeon”) and Judges 1:3 (JPS: “Come up with me into my lot, that we may fight against the Canaanites; and I likewise will go with thee into thy lot”). Rashi’s wording differs somewhat from JPS and is translated as printed. The printed abbreviation א"י is read as “the Land of Israel.” The printed text names Bereshit Rabbah as ב"ר.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: they dwelt at Beer-sheba
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayeshvu beVe'er Sheva* — the sons of Simeon dwelt in those towns of Judah.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: These were their cities unto the reign of David
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Eleh areihem ad molokh David* — its meaning: when the sons of Judah multiplied, they made complaints against the sons of Simeon from the days of Saul and wished to expel them from their land, and he could not expel them, all the more since all his days were in distraction and wars; and when David reigned, his tribe came to demand from the sons of Simeon their land, which they had lent them, and David went and dwelt there, for Saul had not troubled himself about this, because of hatred of David, who was of Judah; and this is what it says: “These were their cities until David reigned,” and when he reigned he expelled them. From the explanation of Rabbi Eliezer bar Meshullam, of blessed memory, and so Rabbi Shlomo bar Levi, brother of Rabbi Moshe the Preacher, explained to me.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The pronouns in this comment are ambiguous and it is translated literally. The printed abbreviation ז"ל is read as “of blessed memory.”

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: their villages were Etam, and Ain
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vechatzereihem* — the villages, who were they? Etam and Ain and Rimmon, etc.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: they have their genealogy
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Zot moshvotam vehityachasam lahem* — its meaning: even though he traced some of them here, do not say that there were only these, for there is another book of genealogy, and there were the genealogies of every single tribe; thus it was to explain its genealogy by itself.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Meshobab
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Umeshovav* — and all those written.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: their fathers’ houses increased greatly
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Eleh habba'im beshemot nesi'im bemishpechotam uveit avoteihem partzu larov* — they had no place to dwell.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: to the entrance of Gedor
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayelkhu* — therefore “to the entrance of Gedor,” etc., “to seek pasture for their flocks.”

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: they that dwelt there aforetime were of Ham
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki min Cham hayoshvim sham lefanim* — they dwelt in quiet and tranquillity, and no man came to harm them; therefore they were not careful when [others] came upon them to fight; and its parallel in Judges: “and they came to Laish, to a people quiet and secure,” etc., “and they had no dealings with any man” — because they were quiet they were not afraid, and they did not make a covenant with any man to help them; therefore those five hundred conquered them. And it is also written there, “after the manner of the Zidonians, quiet and secure,” etc.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotations are Judges 18:27 (JPS: “unto a people quiet and secure”) and Judges 18:7 (JPS: “after the manner of the Zidonians, quiet and secure”); the printed text names only “Judges.” The figure “five hundred” is translated as printed and was not checked.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the remnant of the Amalekites that escaped
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayyakhu et she'erit hapeleitah* — from the cutting off by David, for David cut off every male in Edom.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the sons of Reuben the first-born of Israel
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uvnei Re'uven bekhor Yisrael* — and if you say, if so that he was a first-born, why did kingship not come forth from him, for he is certainly the first-born? And when he defiled his father’s couch his birthright was given to the sons of Joseph; and if you say, if so, why did the sons of Joseph not reign? Therefore it says “and not to be reckoned in the genealogy as first-born” — a portion of the birthright, and not the birthright; for Judah, even if Reuben had not defiled the birthright and it had not been taken from him, even so Judah was fit to be king.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The phrase *chelek bekhorot ve-lo bekhor* is translated literally and the comment is not fully clear to me.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Judah prevailed above his brethren
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki Yehudah gavar be-echav* — as it is said, “Judah is a lion’s whelp” (Genesis 49).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Genesis 49:9 (JPS: “Judah is a lion’s whelp”); the printed reference “Genesis 49” is incomplete.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: of him came he that is the prince
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ulenagid mimmenu* — that kingship came out of him; and for this reason the king is called *nagid*, for he is the one who brings out and brings in. And the birthright and the kingship were taken from Reuben, and the kingship was given to Judah, as it is written, “for Judah prevailed above his brethren”; but the portion of the birthright was given to Joseph, to his two sons.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the sons of Reuben the first-born of Israel
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Benei Re'uven bekhor Yisrael* — now he begins as at first.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: The sons of Joel
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Benei Yo'el* — generation by generation he counts.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Tillegath-pilneser king of Assyria carried away captive
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Asher higleh Tilgat Pilne'eser* — before Sennacherib; and so was their order: Pul (Kings II 15:29) was when Menahem son of Gadi reigned, and in the days of Pekah son of Remaliah (there) came Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria, and in the days of Hoshea son of Elah (there, 17) came Shalmaneser king of Assyria (there, 15), and in the days of Hezekiah, Sennacherib; and our Rabbis explained: Pul and all of them are Sennacherib.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed reference after “Pul” (2 Kings 15:29) is where Tiglath-pileser comes in the days of Pekah (JPS: “In the days of Pekah king of Israel came Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria”); Pul is at 2 Kings 15:19 (JPS: “There came against the land Pul the king of Assyria”). Shalmaneser in the days of Hoshea is 2 Kings 17:3 (JPS: “Against him came up Shalmaneser king of Assyria”). The last printed reference “(there, 15)” is as printed and does not fit Shalmaneser.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: he was prince of the Reubenites
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Hu nasi laRe'uveni* — at the time that Tiglath-pileser exiled him.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: when the genealogy of their generations was reckoned: the chief Jeiel
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Behityacheis letoldotam harosh Ye'i'el uZkharyahu* — its meaning: behold, I have not traced for you from Reuben but some, and the main genealogy is in its place of genealogy, in the Chronicles of the kings of Israel; Jeiel and Zechariah were the head, through whom their genealogy ended.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: even unto Nebo and Baal-meon
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve-ad Nevo uVa'al Me'on* — for in ancient days, before they came into the hand of Israel, they were called Nebo and Baal-meon after their abominations, for such was the custom of idol-worshippers until that day, to call their abominations by the names of their towns; but when they came into the hand of Israel, they changed their names, as it is written “and Nebo and Baal-meon, their names being changed” (Numbers 32), that is, Israel changed their names; and Sibmah, because it was not called after its abominations, they did not change its name. And in Megillah it is explained that Nebo and Baal-meon are names of idolatry.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Numbers 32:38 (JPS: “and Nebo, and Baal-meon—their names being changed—and Sibmah”); the printed reference is Numbers 32:37–38. The printed abbreviation ע"ש is read as “after the name of.” The reference to Megillah is printed without a page and was not checked.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the Hagrites
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Im haHagra'im* — they are the Ishmaelites, and after the name of their mother he calls them Hagrites; they were sons of Hagar.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed abbreviation ע"ש is read as “after the name of.”

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: they dwelt in their tents
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayeshvu be-ohaleihem* — for such is the custom of the Arabs, to dwell in tents.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the sons of Gad dwelt over against them
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uvnei Gad leneggedam yashvu* — beside them, like “and I will go (*ve-elkhah*) before thee (*leneggedekha*)” (Genesis 13).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed reference “Genesis 13” does not contain these words; they are found at Genesis 33:12 (JPS: “and I will go before thee”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: their brethren of their fathers’ houses
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve-acheihem leveit avoteihem* — in the place of their genealogy.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Michael, and Meshullam
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Mikha'el uMeshullam* — these were the heads of their fathers of that genealogy, for all of them were reckoned in the days of Jotham king of Judah and in the days of Jeroboam king of Israel.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the half-tribe of Manasseh, as many as were valiant men
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Benei Re'uven veGad vachatzi shevet Menasheh* etc. — that is, all of them gathered and made war with the Hagrites.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: with Jetur, and Naphish
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *VeYetur veNafish* — they are the sons of Ishmael.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: they were helped against them
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vaye'azeru aleihem* — for the LORD helped them.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the Hagrites were delivered into their hand, and all that were with them
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayinnatnu beyadam haHagra'im vechol she'immahem* — other nations, to help them.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: He was entreated of them
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve-na'tor lahem* — its parallel is “and the LORD was entreated of them.”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The parallel is printed without a reference.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the gods of the peoples of the land, whom God destroyed before them
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayiznu acharei elohei ammei ha'aretz asher hishmid Elohim mipneihem* — its meaning: they went astray after the gods of the peoples of the land, and what people was it that God destroyed before them? Their gods could not help them, and they did not take it to heart, after He destroyed them before them and they were not able to help them, that for us likewise [he] will not help.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The last clause is translated literally and its subject is not clear to me.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: he it is that executed the priest’s office in the house that Solomon built
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Hu asher kihen babayit asher banah Shelomoh* — some explain: Azariah, he was the first Azariah, and from Azariah to Seraiah, who was at the destruction of the Temple, eight priests; and from here they emended in Yoma chapter 1 and in Vayikra Rabbah and in the Sifrei, section Pinchas: eight priests served in the First Temple; and some say eighteen; but neither this nor that has the breath of life in it, for Zadok was the first who served as priest in the days of Solomon; and further, who was Amariah, who was in the days of Jehoshaphat, as it is written “and, behold, Amariah the chief priest” (Chronicles II 19), and he (Amariah) was the son of Azariah, who was in the days of Uzziah, in the days of Hezekiah, who was after Jehoshaphat. And if you say, Azariah was the father of Seraiah, then where is Hilkiah the High Priest, who was in the days of Josiah? Rather, from Zadok one must count twelve priests, there were from Zadok to Seraiah; and so we find in Vayikra Rabbah, accurately. And as for what is written of Azariah “he it is that executed the priest’s office in the house,” it is explained in the Sifrei ירוש' thus: Was he alone a priest in the days of Solomon? Were not the other priests likewise priests? But because he gave his life for the sanctity of the House, in that he did not let Uzziah burn incense, therefore it is said “he it is that executed the priest’s office in the house that Solomon built”; and he is Azariah who was in the days of Uzziah (below, II 26) and in the days of Hezekiah; and Azariah son of Ahimaaz is Amariah who served as priest in the days of Jehoshaphat, as Uzziah is called Azariah, as it is written (Kings II 15) “In the twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam,” etc., “began Azariah to reign”; and he is called Azariah son of Ahimaaz, Zechariah, as it is written “And he set himself to seek God” (below, II 26) “in the days of Zechariah, who had understanding in the fear of God,” etc.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: This comment is obscure and in places appears to contradict itself, and it is translated literally; the abbreviation ירוש' is left as printed, and the verb *hugehu* (“they emended”) is translated literally. The printed abbreviations וא"ת and ומ"ש are read as “and if you say” and “and what is written.” The quotations are 2 Chronicles 19:11 (JPS: “And, behold, Amariah the chief priest is over you”), 2 Kings 15:1 (JPS: “In the twenty and seventh year of Jeroboam king of Israel began Azariah son of Amaziah king of Judah to reign”) and 2 Chronicles 26:5 (JPS: “in the days of Zechariah, who had understanding in the vision of God”); Rashi’s printed “in the fear of God” differs from JPS and is translated as printed. The counts of priests were not recomputed.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Jehozadak went into captivity
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vihotzadak holekh behaglot* — and what is written in the book (Haggai 1) “Joshua son of Jehozadak the High Priest”: Jehozadak never served in the high priesthood, for he was exiled to Babylon in the days of Jeconiah, as it is written, “and Jehozadak went into captivity,” etc.; rather Joshua his son was High Priest when they went up from Babylon, in the Second Temple. And that Ezra son of Seraiah the scribe was not High Priest, and the son of his brother, Joshua son of Jehozadak, served — this is the reason: because Joshua went up with Zerubbabel some days and years before Ezra went up.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Haggai 1:1 (JPS: “Joshua the son of Jehozadak, the high priest”). The exile “in the days of Jeconiah” is Rashi’s statement; the verse itself says “when the LORD carried away Judah and Jerusalem by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar.”

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Vashni
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Veshani* — this is Joel. The meaning: “and the second” is Abiah; that is, second to the first he was Abiah, and second to Abiah was Joel, who is not written. Similar to this: “but the horse is tied, and the ass is tied” (II Kings 6), meaning “and the ass”; and so “the second bullock of Gideon”; and so “the first” (Judges 6:26).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: Rashi reads *veshani* as “and the second” (Abiah), while JPS takes Vashni as a name. The printed reference “II Kings 6” is wrong: the phrase is at 2 Kings 7:10 (JPS: “but the horses tied, and the asses tied”). Judges 6:26 reads “take the second bullock.”

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: And these are they whom David set over the service of song
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’eleh asher he’emid David* etc. — when they brought it back from the house of Obed-edom, as it is written (below, 16): “So he left there, before the ark of the covenant of the LORD, Asaph and his brethren, to minister before the ark” etc.; and it is written “and Obed-edom” (ibid.) “the son of Jedithun and Hosah to be doorkeepers” etc. (ibid.) “before the tabernacle of the LORD,” “in the high place that was at Gibeon.” And Solomon stationed them in the Temple in Jerusalem.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The citations are 1 Chronicles 16:37, 38 and 39; the printed reference gives only the chapter (16). The JPS rendering of 16:38 reads “Obed-edom also the son of Jedithun and Hosah to be doorkeepers.”

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: they took their station at their service according to their order
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vaya’amdu kemishpatam al avodatam* — according to the ordinance by which David stationed them.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: who stood on his right hand
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’achiv Asaf ha’omed al yemino* — of Heman and his sons.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: their brethren the sons of Merari
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uvnei Merari acheihem al hasemol* — (*acheihem*, “their brethren”) similar to what is said in the Ashkenazic language *gebroder*: on the left of Heman and his sons, for Heman and his sons were in the middle.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed word גברודי"ר is German written in Hebrew letters; I read it as *gebroder* (“brothers”), but this is not confirmed. The word אחיהם in parentheses is a printed insertion.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: And their brethren the Levites were appointed for all the service of the tabernacle
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’acheihem haLevi’im netunim lekhol avodat mishkan beit ha’Elohim* — for the gatekeepers and for the flaying, as it is written below (II Chronicles 35): “and the Levites flayed them.”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The citation is 2 Chronicles 35:11; the printed reference gives only the chapter. JPS: “and the Levites flayed them.”

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: these are the sons of Aaron
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’eleh bnei Aharon* — those who burn [offerings] on the altar of the burnt-offering and on the altar of incense.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Zadok his son, Ahimaaz his son
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Tzadok bno Achima’atz bno* — he counted only those who lived until Solomon.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Now these are their dwelling-places according to their encampments in their borders
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’eleh moshvotam letiroteihem bigvulam* etc. — until “for theirs was the lot”: for the Levites and for the priests, from the inheritance of all Israel. They cast lots over the Land of Israel, how much of the Land of Israel would come to them and to the priests and to the Levites; and the lot came to Judah at the first. And this is “for theirs was the lot at the first”: to give them those towns that are written here.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The syntax of this comment is compressed; it is translated as printed.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: they gave to Caleb the son of Jephunneh
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Nat’nu leKalev* — for Moses gave it to him.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: out of the tribe of Benjamin
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Umimatteh Binyamin et Geva* — for the lot fell to Benjamin to give these towns.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: unto the rest of the sons of Kohath
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ulivnei Kehat hanoteirim* — for the priests came forth from Kohath, and they have already said what was given to the priests, the sons of Kohath.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: out of the family of the tribe
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Mimishpachat hamatteh* — of Levi.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: out of the half-tribe, the half of Manasseh, ten cities
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Mimachatzit mateh chatzi Menasheh begoral arim asar* — and the lot fell to half the tribe of Manasseh to give ten towns to the sons of Kohath the Levites.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: out of the tribe of the children of Judah, and out of the tribe of the children of Simeon
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayitnu begoral mimatteh bnei Yehudah umimatteh bnei Shimon* — although it did not mention Simeon in the giving, he gave his share, what Judah gave him; and Judah too is not mentioned above in the main giving. And everything that it mentions above from “and they gave them Hebron” until “and out of the tribe of Benjamin,” all of it the sons of Judah and the sons of Simeon gave; and because it did not mention them above, it mentions it now here.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: these cities which are mentioned by name
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Asher yikare’u otam beshemot* — that is, which we called by name above. Because Benjamin was joined with them for the sons of Aaron, it mentions it although it already mentioned it.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: had cities of their borders out of the tribe of Ephraim
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Umimishpechot bnei Kehat vayehi arei* etc. — although they gave them half the tribe of Manasseh, they also gave them Ephraim, by the lot.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: out of the half-tribe of Manasseh
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Umimachatzit mateh Menasheh* — up to the half of Manasseh that is across the Jordan, which is in the Land of Israel.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: for the rest of the family of the sons of Kohath
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lemishpachat livnei Kehat hanoteirim* — they are the Levites. And the meaning of the whole: Ephraim and Manasseh gave to that remainder that it said above, “And to the sons of Kohath who were left, of the families of the tribe.”

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Unto the sons of Gershom were given, out of the family of the half-tribe of Manasseh
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Livnei Gershom mimishpachat chatzi mateh Menasheh* — although they gave to the sons of Kohath by the lot, the lot also fell to them to give likewise to Gershom.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the sons of Merari, were given, out of the tribe of Zebulun
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Livnei Merari hanoteirim mimatteh Zevulun* — that is, that those twelve towns which Reuben and Gad and Zebulun gave them did not reach them; and this is “the remaining ones of the tribe of Zebulun”: from Zebulun’s portion they gave to the sons of Merari, the remaining ones.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The syntax of this comment is compressed and its exact sense is uncertain.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Jashub
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uvnei Yissachar Tola’ uFu’ah Yashuv uShimron* — in the Chumash it is written (Genesis 47) “Iob.” Iob was his name, and because they settled down to study Torah, as it is written (below, 12) “of the children of Issachar, men that had understanding of the times,” therefore he merited and was called Yashuv.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed reference “Genesis 47” is wrong; “Iob” (JPS spelling) is at Genesis 46:13. The citation “below, 12” is 1 Chronicles 12:33 (“men that had understanding of the times”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: their number in the days of David was two and twenty thousand and six hundred
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uvnei Tola’* — their number in the days of David was twenty-two thousand six hundred; all these are the sons of Tola, apart from the sons of Uzzi.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the sons of Uzzi
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uvnei Uzzi* etc. — thirty-six thousand, for they multiplied wives and sons; and all these were apart from those twenty-two thousand six hundred of the sons of Tola.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: Verse 4 (JPS) reads “six and thirty thousand; for they had many wives and sons.”

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: among all the families of Issachar
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’acheihem lekhol mishpachot* — whether the sons of Tola, or the sons of Uzzi, or all the mighty men of the armies of David: eighty-seven thousand.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: reckoned in all by genealogy
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Hityachasam lekhol* — its meaning: for their whole genealogy.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Bela, and Becher, and Jediael, three
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Binyamin Bela’ uVekher uYedi’a’el* — this is what is called in *Sefer HaYashar* “Ashbel” (Genesis 47).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed reference “Genesis 47” is wrong; Ashbel appears at Genesis 46:21 (“Bela, and Becher, and Ashbel”). *Sefer HaYashar* is understood here as the book of Genesis, since the verse cited is in Genesis.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Shuppim also, and Huppim, the sons of Ir, Hushim, the son of another
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Veshupim vechupim bnei Ir Chushim bnei Acher* — Ezra, who wrote this book of genealogy, did not know whether they were of the sons of Benjamin or not; therefore he wrote them by themselves; and also because it is written “and Machir took a wife of Huppim,” he was in doubt.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quoted words are from 1 Chronicles 7:15.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: The sons of Naphtali: Jahziel, and Guni, and Jezer, and Shallum
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Bnei Naftali Yachtze’el* etc. — as for why they are not traced further, this is the reason, as explained at the end of Megillah in the Yerushalmi: Ezra found three books, and in each and every one of them was part of the genealogy; and what he found he wrote, and what he did not find he did not write. And of the sons of Naphtali he found no more. And this is the reason that this whole genealogy is marked by skips: he skipped from this book to that book and joined them; and what he could not write in this book he wrote in the book of Ezra. Know it, for it is said soon after (below, 9): “And all Israel were reckoned by genealogies; and, behold, they are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah; they were carried away to Babylon.” The meaning: if you wish to know the genealogy of the ten tribes, go to Halah and the Habor, the river of Gozan, and the cities of Media, for their book of Chronicles was exiled with them. But Judah — I found their book in Babylon, and what I found I wrote.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The Yerushalmi passage is cited as printed (the end of tractate Megillah in the Jerusalem Talmud); I did not verify it. The quotation is 1 Chronicles 9:1 in Rashi’s punctuation (“…the kings of Israel and Judah; they were carried away to Babylon”); JPS divides it differently (“…the kings of Israel; and Judah was carried away captive to Babylon”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Asriel, whom his wife bore
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Bnei Menasheh Asri’el asher yaldah* — the explanation: whom his wife bore to him, like “whom she bore to Levi in Egypt” (Numbers 26:59); but his concubine the Aramitess bore Machir.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: Numbers 26:59 in JPS reads “who was born to Levi in Egypt.”

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: whom the men of Gath that were born in the land slew
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uvnei Efrayim Shutelach* etc. “and the men of Gath… slew them” etc. “because they came down to take away their cattle” — and they were not expert in the exits of the roads or the exits of the land; and the men of Gath who were born in the land slew them, for they were expert in that land.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: who built Beth-horon the nether and the upper
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uvito Shee’rah vativen et Beit Choron* — Sheerah was its builder.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Uzzen-sheerah
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’et Uzen Shee’rah* — she called the name of the city after her own name.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: And Rephah was his son
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Verefach bno* — of Beriah.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: and Resheph, and Telah
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Veresheph vetalach* — sons of Rephah; likewise he counted generations.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: and by the borders of the children of Manasseh
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’al yedei bnei Menasheh Beit She’an* — the meaning: adjoining the sons of Manasseh, like “every man at his side, by their standards” (Numbers 2:17).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: JPS renders Numbers 2:17 “every man in his place, by their standards”; Rashi’s quoted phrase uses *al yado* (“at his side”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: who was the father of Birzaith
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Hu avi Birzavit* — the prince of that city. And in Bereshit Rabbah, R. Levi and R. Simon: R. Levi says that his daughters were beautiful and married to priests, who were anointed with olive oil (*shemen zayit*). R. Simon says that his daughters were beautiful and married to kings, who were anointed with the anointing oil; and because they had much oil, they would anoint with it; therefore they were beautiful, for with Asher it is written “and let him dip his foot in oil” (Deuteronomy 33:24). And R. Chananiah said: the hot water and oil that my mother rubbed on me restored me to my youth.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed abbreviation ב"ר is read as Bereshit Rabbah. I did not verify the Midrash passage.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: And Benjamin begot Bela his first-born
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uvinyamin holid et Bela bekhoro* — they already traced him (above, 7), and because he wished to trace up to King Saul, he begins to trace from Benjamin, and other names he calls here. And the whole genealogy is in reverse; and whoever wishes to examine closely [will find that] most of the Levites’ cities and their open lands mentioned here, in reverse, are in Joshua, for Ezra found books.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The last sentence is compressed and its sense is uncertain; it is rendered closely.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: they were carried captive to Manahath
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayglum el Manachat* — who exiled them? And it explains afterward in the verse: “and Naaman, and Ahijah, and Gera” — he exiled them.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The words are from 1 Chronicles 8:7; JPS renders “and Naaman, and Ahijah, and Gera, were they that carried them captive.”

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Manahath
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Manachat* — the name of a district, as it is written (above, 2): “Haroeh, half of the Menuchot,” and it is written “and half of the Manahathites” (ibid.).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The citations are 1 Chronicles 2:52 (“Haroeh, and half of the Menuhoth”) and 2:54 (“half of the Manahathites”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Shaharaim begot children in the field of Moab
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ushacharaim holid* — he was one of the exiles, and after they sent him out of the exile he begot these.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: to wit, Hushim and Baara his wives
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Chushim ve’et Ba’ara nashav* — such were the names of his wives.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: and of Hushim he begot Abitub
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *UmeChushim holid* — this is Hushim his wife, who was mentioned above; and [it mentions her again] because [the account] was interrupted by Hodesh his wife.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The last clause is terse; the words in brackets are my reading.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: And Ahio, Shashak, and Jeremoth
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’achiv Shashak* — all these are the sons of Elpaal, ע"א. And the main point: from “Ahio, Shashak” until “and Joha,” all these are the sons of Beriah; and from “Zebadiah” until “Jobab,” all these are the sons of Elpaal; and from “Jakim” until “Shimrath,” all these are the sons of Shimei.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The verses are 1 Chronicles 8:14–16 (sons of Beriah), 8:17–18 (sons of Elpaal) and 8:19–21 (sons of Shimei), which agree with Rashi’s division. The abbreviation ע"א is left as printed because I could not confirm its meaning.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: And in Gibeon there dwelt the father of Gibeon
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uvgiv’on yashvu avi Giv’on* — this passage, up to “all these were the sons of Azel,” is written twice in this book; also the passage “Now the first inhabitants that dwelt in their possessions in their cities” (below, ch. 9) and the passage “And of the priests: Jedaiah, and Jehoiarib” — likewise in the book of Ezra (that is, Nehemiah 11:3), for it is written “And these are the chiefs of the province.” And this is what is explained at the end of Megillah in the Yerushalmi: Ezra found three books, *Sefer Me’onim*, *Sefer Za’atutei*, *Sefer HaAchim*; and they set aside the words of the one and upheld the words of the two. And so they found many books of genealogies: when three or five were found, they set aside the minority and upheld the majority; and when pairs were found, like “And in Gibeon dwelt the father of Gibeon,” it was necessary to write it twice, for the order of their genealogy is not the same. So too “the first inhabitants”: he found pairs differing from each other, and they wrote it twice, here and in his book. And why did he not write both here — those that are in Ezra, “And these are the chiefs of the province” etc.? Because he traces there up to “And these are the priests, the Levites,” and traces up to Jedaiah, who was after Ezra; and what point is there in explaining and tracing in Chronicles generations together and after Ezra, except those who were in the First Temple? And [likewise] in the other passage, “And in Gibeon dwelt” etc. And further the Sages said in the *Sefar’*: “And to Azel six sons” — thirteen thousand camels laden with expositions.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The abbreviation ל' סי' ט' is read here as “below, chapter 9,” and the abbreviation בספר' is left as printed; neither could be confirmed. The names of the three books are transliterated as printed, and the Yerushalmi passage is cited as printed without verification. The Aramaic in the last sentence is translated as printed.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: So all Israel were reckoned by genealogies
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vekhol Yisra’el hityachasu* — I told you some of their genealogy, what I found; but the main genealogy is in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah, who were exiled to Babylon in their trespass, and with them was I, Ezra; and I found their genealogy written, and I wrote it.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: JPS divides this verse differently (“…the kings of Israel; and Judah was carried away captive to Babylon because of their transgression”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: who hitherto waited in the king’s gate eastward
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’ad hennah besha’ar hamelekh mizrachah* — the meaning: “until” from there onward, up to a gate whose name is the King’s Gate, the eastern one.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The first phrase of the comment is terse; it is rendered closely.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: they were the porters for the camp of the children of Levi
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Hemmah hasho’arim* — Shallum and his brethren, of the camps of the sons of Levi.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: keepers of the gates of the Tent
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Shomrei hasippim la’ohel* — Shallum the son of Kore and his brethren, of his father’s house, the Korahites, keepers of the thresholds of the Tent of Meeting, for they would not let any person come into the Tent of Meeting except the priests in their service.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Phinehas the son of Eleazar was ruler over them in time past, the LORD being with him
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *UFinchas ben Elazar nagid hayah aleihem lifanim HaShem imo* — because he prophesied in former times. And our Rabbis said: he is Phinehas the priest; and because he did not annul Jephthah’s vow, the Divine Presence departed from him.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: whom David and Samuel the seer did ordain in their set office
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Hemmah yissad David uShemuel haro’eh be’emunatam* — in their establishment.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: every seven days
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lishvat hayamim* — at the end of seven days.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: from time to time
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Me’et el et* — from seven to seven, each watch in its sitting.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: to them pertained the opening thereof
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vehem al hamafte’ach* — over the key of the Temple court.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: morning by morning
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Velaboker laboker* — to open.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: had charge of the vessels of service
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Umehem al keli* — the vessels of service: by number they take them out and by number they bring them in.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: Rashi’s order differs from JPS (“by tale were they brought in and by tale were they taken out”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: who dwelt in the chambers and were free from other service
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’eleh hameshorerim* etc. — exempt from every matter of labor except to sing the song.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Eshbaal
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Eshba’al* — he is Ish-bosheth, and therefore he called him *Bosheth*: because *ba’al* is a term for “lord,” and he called him *Bosheth* as a term of disgrace.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Merib-baal
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Merib Ba’al* — this is Mephibosheth. R. Yitzchak bar Shemuel of Narbonne said: from the time Israel served the Baal, the Baal was called *Bosheth*, as it is written “to burn incense to *Bosheth*, to burn incense to Baal” (Jeremiah 11:13), for the Baal is *Bosheth*. And Gideon was called Jerubbaal because Baal contended with him (Judges 6); and he was called Jerubbesheth, as it is written about Abimelech: “Who smote Abimelech the son of Jerubbesheth?” etc. in the book of Samuel (II 11); and he was called Jerubbesheth and Jerubbaal, because *Baal* and *Bosheth* are one.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: Rashi’s quotation of Jeremiah 11:13 differs slightly from the verse (JPS: “altars to the shameful thing, even altars to offer unto Baal”). Judges 6:32 reads “Therefore on that day he was called Jerubbaal, saying: ‘Let Baal contend against him’”; the name Jerubbesheth is at 2 Samuel 11:21.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Now the Philistines fought against Israel
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *UFlishtim nilchamu beYisra’el* — he relates only the downfall of Saul; and when he comes to relate the deeds of David, he does not relate his humiliation but his might and his greatness, for the book is his and that of the kings of Judah.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the archers overtook him
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayimtze’uhu hamorim bakkeshet* — come and see: “There is no wisdom nor understanding… against the LORD” (Proverbs 21). For against the LORD the ways of a man of Benjamin — their enemies would fall before them by the bow, for they are expert in the bow, as it is written: “left-handed” (*iter yad yemino*) etc. in Judges (21); and so with Jonathan, “…to shoot at a mark for me” (I Samuel 20); and it is written below (12, 2): “Benjamin, armed with bows, using the right hand” etc.; and so with Asa in this book (II 14): “and from Benjamin, bearing shields and drawing bows” etc. But when the Name departed from Saul, he fell into the hand of an archer, in the very thing that is his craft. *Vayachel min hayorim* — like “and the queen was exceedingly pained” (Esther 10).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The words כי נגד ה' דרכי איש are printed as shown and the sentence is hard to follow; it is rendered word for word. The word מימיני' in 12:2 is truncated; JPS reads “could use both the right hand and the left.” The printed references are corrected as follows: Proverbs 21:30 is correct; “Judges 21” should be Judges 20:16 (“left-handed”); 1 Samuel 20:20 (“as though I shot at a mark”); 1 Chronicles 12:2; 2 Chronicles 14:7 (“bore shields and drew bows”); “Esther 10” should be Esther 4:4 (“the queen was exceedingly pained”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: brought them to Jabesh
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayeviu Yavesha* — to Jabesh-gilead.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: and fasted seven days
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayatzumu shiv’at yamim* — and why did they put themselves in danger to take the bodies of Saul and his sons from Mount Gilboa more than the rest of Israel? Because Saul had done them a kindness, that he saved them when Nahash the Ammonite came up against them; and corresponding to those seven days that they were given as a time, if a deliverer would come to them, they were fasting and afflicting themselves, perhaps a deliverer would come to them, and Saul came and delivered them. Corresponding to them, they too now fasted seven days; and also because of the mourning, which they observed for seven days, for they too were relatives of theirs: when Israel slew the inhabitants of Gibeah in the affair of the concubine in Gibeah (end of Judges), the men of Jabesh gave their daughters to Benjamin when they seized them from the dances.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: Judges 21:12 records four hundred young virgins of Jabesh-gilead given to Benjamin, and 21:23 records that Benjamin took wives “of them that danced”; Rashi’s wording joins the two.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: So Saul died for his transgression which he committed against the LORD
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayamot Sha’ul bema’alo asher ma’al* — two trespasses he committed in asking of a ghost: one that he asked, after Samuel, and one that he inquired; and in the Aggadah of Samuel we learned: he committed five trespasses.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The phrase “after Samuel” is ambiguous (after Samuel’s death, or concerning Samuel); it is rendered literally. I could not identify “the Aggadah of Samuel” and left it as printed.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: because of the word of the LORD, which he kept not
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Al devar HaShem asher lo shamar* — what Samuel commanded him, as it is written “seven days shalt thou tarry” (I Samuel); and for what he trespassed in the war with Amalek.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The words “seven days shalt thou tarry” are at 1 Samuel 10:8; see also 13:8 (“he tarried seven days”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Thou shalt feed My people Israel
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Atah tir’eh et ami* — about this David said, “The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want” (Psalm 23:1): You say to me, “You shall shepherd”; what can I shepherd? The matter does not depend on me, but “The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want,” and I too shall not lack for you. And a parallel in Samuel (II 21): “Then the men of David swore unto him, saying: Thou shalt go no more out with us to battle, that thou quench not the lamp of Israel.” David said to them: “For Thou art my lamp, O LORD, and the LORD will lighten my darkness” (ibid. 22).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The citations are Psalm 23:1, 2 Samuel 21:17 and 2 Samuel 22:29.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: David made a covenant with them in Hebron
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayikhrot lahem David berit* — like that covenant which Jehoiada made, as it is written (II Kings 11): “And Jehoiada made a covenant between the LORD and the king and the people, to be a people unto the LORD” — the meaning: to be servants of the LORD; and also between the king and the people, to be servants to him according to the law of the king, and also for the king to act according to the statute for his servants, to fight their wars.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The citation is 2 Kings 11:17 (JPS: “that they should be the LORD’S people; between the king also and the people”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: before the LORD
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lifnei HaShem* — but the Tabernacle was not in Hebron! What then is “before the LORD”? Wherever they make a condition or cut a covenant, the Omnipresent is there. A parallel with Jephthah: “before the LORD in Mizpah” (Judges 11:11); and a parallel: “and commit a trespass against the LORD, and deal falsely with his neighbour” (Leviticus 5:21), as is explained in Torat Kohanim.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: I did not verify the Torat Kohanim passage.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: And David and all Israel went to Jerusalem
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayelekh David* etc. — he went immediately to war when all Israel made him king, so that Israel should not say, “All the wars that David waged in the days of Saul — it was Saul’s fortune that prevailed; and now he is afraid to fight”; therefore he went immediately to war.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Thou shalt not come in hither
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayomeru yoshvei Yevus leDavid lo tavo henna* — it does not explain here why; but in Samuel (II 5) it explains: “And he said to David: Thou shalt not come in hither, except the blind and the lame take thee away.” They saw that they could not stand before David, and they placed blind and lame people before the city gate to say, “David shall not come in here unless he fights these blind people,” for they knew that it is contemptible for a king to fight the blind, and thereby he would turn back and not fight them. And David said in his heart: It is true, for it is not proper or fitting for me to fight blind and lame people; but whoever smites the Jebusite, how he reaches the channel and draws them and casts them from there, the blind. Therefore they say, “A blind man and a lame man shall not come into the house,” into the house of David — that it should be a disgrace to him, lest they say: With these David fought.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The sentence “but whoever smites the Jebusite, how he reaches the channel…” is compressed and is rendered word for word. The quotation is 2 Samuel 5:6 (JPS: “Except thou take away the blind and the lame, thou shalt not come in hither”); see also 5:8, where JPS reads “and getteth up to the gutter.”

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Joab repaired the rest of the city
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Veyo’av yechayeh et she’ar ha’ir* — he built, and kept on building the breaches of the wall. A parallel in Ezra: “will they revive the stones out of the heaps of rubbish” (Nehemiah 3:34).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The parenthetical citation is Nehemiah 3:34; Rashi’s own words refer to “Ezra.”

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the chief of the captains
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Rosh hashalishim* — chief of the mighty men, like “and captains over all of them” (Exodus 14:7).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: JPS renders Exodus 14:7 “and captains over all of them.”

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: he lifted up his spear against three hundred and slew them at one time
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Orer et chanito* — when he fought in a battle, he would not return from the battle until he had slain three hundred slain with his spear.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the son of a Hachmonite
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ben Chachmoni* — in Samuel (II 23) it is written *Tachkemoni*; he is his father; and the strength of the father was greater than the strength of the son, of whom it is written (ibid.) “against eight hundred mighty men slain at one time.”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The citation is 2 Samuel 23:8 (JPS: “against eight hundred, whom he slew at one time”); Rashi’s quotation adds the word “mighty men.”

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: who was one of the three mighty men
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Hu bishloshah hagibborim* — he is included among the three mighty men, for he is one of them; and these three are mightier than the rest of the thirty and three mentioned nearby; and here it mentions only two, Jashobeam and Eleazar, and in Samuel (II 23) it mentions the third as well, for it is written “and after him Shamma the son of Aga the Harari” (ibid.).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The phrase “the rest of the thirty and three mentioned nearby” is rendered word for word and its sense is uncertain. The citation is 2 Samuel 23:11 (JPS: “Shammah the son of Age the Ararite”); the second parenthetical reference (שם א') is unclear and is rendered “ibid.”

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Pas-dammim
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Befas Dammim* — a place name; and in Samuel, *be-Efes Dammim*.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The form Ephes-dammim occurs at 1 Samuel 17:1.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the Philistines were gathered together to battle
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vehapelishtim ne’esfu sham lamilchamah* — for they hastened to take vengeance on Israel and on those mighty men who had taunted, as explained in Samuel (II 23): “when they defied the Philistines.”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The citation is 2 Samuel 23:9, where JPS renders the verb as “jeoparded their lives against the Philistines”; Rashi’s quotation uses the verb *chirpam* (“defied”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: full of barley
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Melei’ah se’orim* — and the Philistines wished to reap it and to set it on fire.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: three of the thirty chiefs went down
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayeredu sheloshah min hashloshim* — these three were the head of all the thirty.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the garrison of the Philistines was then in Beth-lehem
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Unetziv Pelishtim az beVeit Lechem* — for they had already taken Beth-lehem and had set up in it a governor, a ruler. This was at the beginning of his reign, when the Philistines still ruled over them; for so we find that before David came they ruled over Israel, in the days of Samson and Samuel, as it is written (I Samuel 4:9): “Be strong and be men, O Philistines, lest you serve the Hebrews,” etc.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The citation is 1 Samuel 4:9.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Oh that one would give me water to drink of the well of Beth-lehem
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Mi yashkeni mayim mibor Beit Lechem* — this was David’s place, as it is written “and David the son of Jesse, of the Beth-lehemite” (I Samuel 18:3); and since David was constantly accustomed and used to those waters, he longed for them. And any water and any air to which a person is accustomed is pleasant to him, and that to which he is not accustomed harms him. A parallel at the beginning of *Yosiphon*: a certain queen fell ill because she was married away from the land of her birth, and the physicians said there is no cure for her until she bathes and benefits from the waters of her own place; and so they did for her.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed reference (1 Samuel 18:3) does not contain these words (it records the covenant of Jonathan and David); the wording is nearest to 1 Samuel 16:18 and 17:12, but I could not confirm which verse is meant. I did not verify the passage in *Yosiphon*.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: broke through the host of the Philistines
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayivke’u hashloshah bemachaneh Pelishtim* — in German: *durch brechen die schar*.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The abbreviation בל"א is read here as “in German” because the glossed words are German written in Hebrew letters; this is not confirmed.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: drew water out of the well of Beth-lehem
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayish’avu* — while the Philistines were standing before the well, three mighty men of Israel came and broke through among them and drew [water] against their will.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: poured it out unto the LORD
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayenasech otam laShem* — Bar Kappara says: it was the Festival of Sukkot, and he poured them out on the altar.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: for with the jeopardy of their lives they brought it
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki benafshotam hevi’um* — for they gave themselves up to be killed for the sake of the water.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Abishai, the brother of Joab, he was chief of the three
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’Avshai achi Yo’av hu hayah rosh hashloshah* — of those three who broke through the camp of the Philistines and drew the water. And as to why it does not mention Joab among the mighty men: because it is not to his honor to count him with these, for he was the commander of the army, head of them all.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: had a name among the three
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Velo shem bashloshah* — he had that name, for his might was equal to the might of all of them; and it is an error.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The closing words וטעות הוא (“and it is an error”) are translated as printed; I could not tell whether they are Rashi’s or a later editor’s.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Of the three in the second rank he was the most honourable
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Min hashloshah bashenayim* — he was honored, but not like those three; his might corresponded to the two, but he did not reach the sum of the might of the three. (And this is) “and he attained not to the first three.”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The word וזהו (“and this is”) is in parentheses in the source, as a later printed insertion.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the son of a valiant man of Kabzeel
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ben ish chayil* — like *ben beliyya’al*; and in Samuel (II 23) it is written *ben ish chai*, for such is the way of people: when they see a person who is zealous, they say, “This one is all alive.”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The citation is 2 Samuel 23:20; JPS renders both forms “the son of a valiant man.”

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: two altar-hearths of Moab
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ari’el* — mighty men, masters of strength: *ari* (lion) is mighty, and *el* too is an expression of “the mighty of the land” (Ezekiel 17).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: JPS renders *ariel* here as “altar-hearths”; Rashi reads it as “mighty men.” The citation is Ezekiel 17:13 (JPS: “the mighty of the land”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: who had done mighty deeds
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Rav pe’alim* — he performed many deeds of might.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: he went down also and slew a lion in the midst of a pit in time of snow
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vehu yarad vehikkah et ha’aryeh betokh habor beyom hasheleg* — and he did not fear the chill and the cold. And some say: on a snowy day — the whole year through the lion is not more dangerous than on a snowy day: when a person comes against it, it flings the snow with its foot between the person’s eyes until he cannot see, and kills him. And I heard it so about this.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: a man of great stature
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ish middah* — other people need not be measured, for one can know by estimation; and a parallel: “and all the people that we saw in it are men of great stature (*anshei middot*)” (Numbers 13:32).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: JPS renders Numbers 13:32 “men of great stature.”

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: like a weaver’s beam
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Kimnor orgim* — the wood around which the cloth is wound.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: he was more honourable than the thirty
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Min hashloshim hinneh nikhbad hu ve’el hashloshah* — he did not reach the sum of the might of the three, those three whom it mentions above; and therefore it is written *lo ba’alaf* (“not to the thousand”).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The words לא באלף (“not to the thousand”) appear to be a printing error, since the verse reads “he attained not to the three”; they are rendered as printed.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: set him over his guard
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Al mishma’to* — an expression of appointment, and so “and the children of Ammon shall be their *mishma’at*” (Isaiah 11:14).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: JPS renders Isaiah 11:14 “and the children of Ammon shall obey them.”

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the mighty men of valour
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ugibborei hachayalim* — but not like those above.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: he was yet shut up
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Od atzur* — hidden.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: They were armed with bows
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Noshkei keshet* — armed with bow and with arrows, and shooters before them and behind them; even with stones they would put a stone, shooting, on the bowstring; and I have seen this often.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The words אבן מורים are ambiguous and are rendered closely.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: they were of Saul’s brethren of Benjamin
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Me’achei Sha’ul miBinyamin* — because all of them descended from one man of Benjamin, all of them are called brothers; and for the honor of David’s greatness it says “of Saul’s brethren,” for even Saul’s brethren came to him while Saul was alive.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: and over the thirty
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’al hashloshim* — head of the thirty.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: to the stronghold in the wilderness
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lamatzad midbarah* — to the strongholds of the wilderness, where he hid from Saul, as it is written (I Samuel 23): “And they arose, and went to Ziph before Saul; and David and his men were in the wilderness of Maon, in the Arabah”; and it is written (ibid. 24): “And David went up from thence and dwelt in the strongholds of En-gedi.”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The citations are 1 Samuel 23:24 and 24:1. The second parenthetical reference (שם כ, 'ד) is garbled in the source and is rendered “ibid. 24.”

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: whose faces were like the faces of lions
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ufenei aryeh* — their faces were fearsome like a lion’s.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed word מפוחדים is rendered “fearsome.”

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: as swift as the roes upon the mountains
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vekhitzvaim al heharim lemaher* — they were swift in their running, for it is the way of gazelles to run on the mountains when they are hunted.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: These of the sons of Gad were captains of the host
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Eleh mibnei Gad* — as it is written above: “And of the Gadites there separated themselves unto David.”

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: he that was least was equal to a hundred
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Echad lame’ah hakatan* — the least of them all would pursue a hundred.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the greatest to a thousand
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vehagadol le’alef* — and the greatest of them all would pursue a thousand. Here the verse was fulfilled: “and five of you shall chase a hundred, and a hundred of you…” etc.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The verse is Leviticus 26:8.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: in the first month
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Eleh hem asher avru et haYarden bachodesh harishon* — in Nisan, when the snows had already melted.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: they put to flight all them of the valleys, both toward the east, and toward the west
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayavrichu et kol ha’amakim lemizrach ulema’arav* — they crossed the Jordan and broke through with their shields all the valleys of water, to the east and to the west, and crossed on dry land. And some say: “they put to flight all the valleys” — the peoples dwelling in the valleys.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: there came of the children of Benjamin and Judah to the stronghold unto David
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Min bnei Binyamin Yehudah ad lamatzad leDavid* — to the stronghold where David was hiding from Saul; and they took with them David’s nephew, his sister’s son, because the Benjaminites were anxious about David, lest David think that the Benjaminites had come to bind him and give him into the hand of Saul; therefore they took Amasai with them; and also others from Judah, David’s relatives, as it is written “of the sons of Benjamin and Judah,” so that when David sees that they came with them in their trustworthiness, he will not suspect them in any matter.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: David went out to meet them
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayetze David lifneihem* — from the stronghold.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: my heart shall be knit unto you
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vaya’an vayomer lahem* etc. — *Levav*: to unite your heart and my heart, that it be as one heart.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: seeing there is no wrong in my hands
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’im lerammotani letzarai bela chamas bekhapi* — for what have I done to Saul, that he hunts my life to take it for nothing.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the spirit clothed Amasai
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Veru’ach lavshah et Amasai* — *talent* in the vernacular — and not the spirit of prophecy; that is, this spirit and will clothed him, so that he leapt first to speak before Benjamin and Judah who came with him; and a parallel: “and the spirit of the LORD was upon Jephthah” (Judges 11). And he said, “Thine are we, David” — you say, “If you have come peaceably”; surely we have come to you in peace, and with you, son of Jesse. We want to be with you and to help you.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The citation is Judges 11:29. The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Peace, peace be unto thee, And peace be to thy helpers
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Shalom shalom lekha veshalom le’ozrekha* — and you ask me [whether we come] to help you — surely we have come to help you, and you have no need to be grateful to us, for it is from the Name; and this is “for thy God helpeth thee.”

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Then David received them
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayekabbelem David* — those sons of Benjamin; and he placed them as heads of his band.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Of Manasseh also there fell away some to David
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *UmiMenasheh nafelu al David* — to help him.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: when he came with the Philistines against Saul to battle
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Bevo’o im Pelishtim al Sha’ul lamilchamah* — in that war in which Saul was killed.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: but they helped them not
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Velo azaruM* — Heaven forbid that they helped the Philistines! But the lords of the Philistines sent him away by counsel; rather, the lords took counsel to send him to his house, for they said, “On our heads he will fall” to his master; like “*nafelu el David*” (“they fell away to David”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: they helped David against the troop
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Al hagedud* — of the Amalekites, when his wives were taken captive; for it was at that time: as he was going to Ziklag when the lords of the Philistines sent him away, and he came to Ziklag, they had already been taken captive.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: For from day to day men came to David to help him
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki le’et yom beyom yavo’u al David le’ozro* — its meaning: why should you relate more, who and who came to him? In short, at every time they came to David.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: until there was a great host, like the host of God
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ad lemachaneh gadol kemachaneh Elohim* — the meaning: David’s camp did not become so great of itself, but from the Name the camp was so great, for they came to him by the counsel of God; and this is “like the host of God.” And compare the camp of God of Jacob (Genesis 32:3). And one may say: from the multitude of hosts, a “camp of God” befell him.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The last sentence is terse and is rendered closely. Genesis 32:3 reads, in JPS, “This is God’s camp.”

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: to turn the kingdom of Saul to him
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lehasev malkhut Sha’ul elav* — from the sons of Saul; and compare “and the kingdom was turned about” (*vatissov hamelukhah*).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 1 Kings 2:15 (JPS: “the kingdom is turned about”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: The children of Judah that bore shield and spear were six thousand and eight hundred
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Bnei Yehudah nos’ei tzinnah veromach shishah alafim ushmoneh me’ot* — and do not wonder that few came to him from Judah in comparison with each and every tribe that came to him; for no one from Judah needed to come to him to make him king, since the sons of Judah had already made him king in Hebron; but the other tribes, who had been with the sons of Saul until now, needed to come to Hebron to make him king.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: armed for war
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Chalutzei tzava* — those who go out from among the people; and its parallel is *chalutzei tzava* of Matot; and some say *chalutzim* is like “zealous,” like “*ratzeh vehachlitzenu*.”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The word דמטות is read here as “of Matot” (the Torah portion; compare Numbers 31:5, “twelve thousand armed for war”), and the closing words רצה והחליצנו are printed as shown and could not be identified; neither reading is confirmed.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Jehoiada was the leader of the house of Aaron
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vihoyada hanagid le’Aharon* — he is the father of Benaiah.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: leader of the house of Aaron
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Hanagid le’Aharon* — the one who goes out and comes in.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: with him were three thousand and seven hundred
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’immo sheloshet alafim veshev me’ot* — all of them of the sons of Aaron the priest; and the Jehoiada who lived in the days of Joash was the son of Benaiah, the son of Jehoiada.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Zadok, a young man mighty of valour
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vetzadok na’ar* — therefore do not wonder that he was not a leader.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: of his father’s house twenty and two captains
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uveit aviv sarim esrim ushnayim* — this is great eminence, and therefore they took the high priesthood from Abiathar and gave it to Zadok the priest.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the brethren of Saul, three thousand
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *UmiBnei Binyamin achei Sha’ul* etc. — and do not wonder that only three thousand came, for until now the majority of them were keeping the charge of the sons of Saul, to help them.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: men that had understanding of the times
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *UmiBnei Yissachar yod’ei vinah la’ittim* — who know how to give counsel according to the matter of the event, for David needed to take counsel how to strengthen the kingdom against the sons of Saul.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the heads of them were two hundred
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Rasheihem matayim* — apart from the rest.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: all their brethren were at their commandment
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vekhol acheihem al pihem* — at their counsel.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: that could order the battle array
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vela’adur* — literally an expression of hoeing (*adur*), like (Isaiah 10) “all the hills that are hoed with the hoe” (*bamma’der ye’aderun*); and through this they would stand as arrangers of the war. And some interpret *la’adur* as “to arrange a war.”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Isaiah 7:25 (JPS: “And all the hills that were digged with the mattock”); the printed reference “Isaiah 10” is wrong.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: were not of double heart
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Belo lev valev* — explained in Bereshit Rabbah: whether intentionally or unintentionally, they were victorious.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed abbreviation ב"ר is read as Bereshit Rabbah. I did not verify the Midrash passage.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: a hundred and twenty thousand
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vegam kol she’erit Yisra’el lev echad lehamlikh et David* — although they did not come to Hebron, therefore *she’erit* [is written] lacking an alef; that is, there was not even a remnant, for only a few remained, since all of them came to Hebron with joy.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The first clause (“although they did not come to Hebron”) seems to conflict with the end of the comment and is rendered as printed. The source lemma belongs to the next verse (1 Chronicles 12:39) and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under. The verse spells the word *sherit* without an alef.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: came with a whole heart to Hebron
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayihyu sham im David yamim shlosha* — and do not wonder where they got so much food and drink for all this army, that it sufficed for them: their brethren had prepared for them beforehand.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The source lemma belongs to the next verse (1 Chronicles 12:40) and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: for there was joy in Israel
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki simchah beYisra’el* — because they had a successful and wise king.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: David consulted with the captains of thousands and of hundreds
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayivvaetz David im sarei ha’alafim* — for David said to them: You have already engaged in your own welfare, that you have a king to save you; and now engage in the honor of God.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: let us send abroad everywhere unto our brethren
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Nifretz nishlechah* — let that fence which has been fenced until now be breached, [since] no person sought God; and let it be sent to our brethren who remain, for the sake of the honor of the Ark.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: from Shihor the brook of Egypt even unto the entrance of Hamath
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Min Shichor Mitzrayim ve’ad levo Chamat* — a parallel: “from the entrance of Hamath unto the brook of Egypt.”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: A similar wording occurs at 1 Kings 8:65 (JPS: “from the entrance Hamath unto the Brook of Egypt”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Baalah, that is, to Kiriath-jearim
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Be’alatah el Kiryat* — the meaning: Baalah is Kiriath-jearim.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: whereon is called the Name
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Leha’alot misham* etc. — as it is written (II Samuel 7): “whereon is called the Name, even the name of the LORD of hosts that sitteth upon the cherubim”; that is, the Name of the Holy One, blessed be He, was called upon the Ark; although the Ark was exiled to the Philistines, this Name that had been sanctified did not depart from it.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed reference “II Samuel 7” is wrong; the verse is 2 Samuel 6:2 (JPS: “whereupon is called the Name, even the name of the LORD of hosts that sitteth upon the cherubim”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: they set the ark of God upon a new cart
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayarkivu et aron ha’Elohim al agalah chadashah* — what did David see, that they put it on a new cart and not on the shoulders of the Levites, as he did when he brought it from there to Zion at the end? Because David said: all that corresponds to what came to me, when the Philistines returned it on a new cart, as it is written, “and they put the ark of the LORD on a cart,” etc.; therefore he was punished.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The words כל עומת שבא אלי are obscure and are rendered closely. The quotation is 1 Samuel 6:11 (JPS: “And they put the ark of the LORD upon the cart”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Uzza and Ahio
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uzza ve’achyo* — they were the sons of Abinadab, as it is written in Samuel (ibid. I 6).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The statement that they were the sons of Abinadab is at 2 Samuel 6:3 (JPS: “Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab”); the printed reference “I 6” is not that verse.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Uzza and Ahio drove the cart
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Noheigim ba’agalah* — in the manner of cart-drivers: one goes before the cart and straightens it on the straight way, and one at the side of the cart, so that it will not overturn and fall; and so it is written (I Samuel 6): “and his brother went before the ark, and Uzza at the side of the cart” (ibid.); therefore Uzza put forth his hand to hold the ark when the oxen stumbled, and for that he was punished.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The words “and his brother went before the ark” correspond to 2 Samuel 6:4 (JPS: “and Ahio went before the ark”); the printed reference to “I Samuel 6” is wrong, and the words “and Uzza at the side of the cart” do not occur in that verse.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: with all their might
1 Chronicles.english_translation: Here it is written *bechol oz* (“with all their might”), and in Samuel (ibid.) it is written *bechol atzei*. The meaning of *bechol atzei* is wooden musical instruments; and here the meaning of *bechol oz* is musical instruments.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under. The parallel is 2 Samuel 6:5 (JPS: “with all manner of instruments made of cypress-wood”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: with songs, and with harps, and with psalteries, and with timbrels
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uvashirim uvakinnorot uvaneivalim uvatuppim* — all of them are musical instruments; but *metzaltayim* (cymbals) was a musical instrument made only for producing sound; and similar to it is a musical instrument they call *poykin* in German, which they strike with sticks and it produces sound; and so he proves below (15): “and with cymbals they sound,” and it is written (ibid.) “and the singers Heman, Asaph and Ethan with cymbals of brass to sound aloud,” and further below it is written “for song in the house of the LORD with cymbals,” etc. (below, 25); and for this reason it is called *metzaltayim*, and so “the locust (*hatzelatzal*) shall possess” (Deuteronomy 28:42), a kind of locust that makes a sound, as it is written in the prophecies (Joel 2:5): “Like the noise of chariots on the tops of the mountains do they leap,” etc.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The word פויקי"ן and the abbreviation בל"א are left as transliterated (“in German”); the exact meaning of *poykin* is not confirmed. The citations are 1 Chronicles 15:28 (“with cymbals, sounding aloud”), 15:19 (“with cymbals of brass to sound aloud”), 25:6 (“with cymbals”), Deuteronomy 28:42 and Joel 2:5.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the threshing-floor of Chidon
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ad goren Kidon* — a place name.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: because he put forth his hand to the ark
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayakkehu al asher shalach yado al ha’aron* — and this is what is written in Samuel (II 6): “and God smote him there *al hashal*”; the meaning: *al hashalach*, because he grasped the Ark. And a parallel (I Kings 21:23): “The dogs shall eat the flesh of Jezebel in the *chayil* of Jezreel,” and another verse is written, “in the *chelek* of Jezreel” (ibid. II 9); so we explain here *al hashal* as *hashalach*.
