1 Chronicles.translator_note: JPS renders 2 Samuel 6:7 “God smote him there for his error.” The other verses are 1 Kings 21:23 (JPS: “in the moat of Jezreel”) and 2 Kings 9:10 (JPS: “in the portion of Jezreel”; see also 9:36).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: and there he died before God
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayamot sham lifnei Elohim* — before the ark of God; in Samuel (II 6:7) it is written “and there he died by the ark of God.”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: JPS renders 2 Samuel 6:7 “and there he died by the ark of God.”

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: David was afraid of God that day
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayira David et ha’Elohim bayom hahu lemor* — what did he fear, in saying? That he said, “How shall I bring the ark of the LORD to me?”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The wording is that of 2 Samuel 6:9 (JPS: “How shall the ark of the LORD come unto me?”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the Gittite
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Haggiti* — he was from Gath at first; previously he dwelt in Gath, and he was a Levite, as it is written (below, 15): “And David spoke to the chief of the Levites to appoint their brethren the singers,” and it is written soon after (ibid.): “and Obed-edom and Jehiah were doorkeepers for the ark.”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The citations are 1 Chronicles 15:16 and 15:24.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: And Huram king of Tyre sent messengers to David
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayishlach* — Hiram king of Tyre — it is explained in Bereshit Rabbah: this man was accustomed to be a friend of the tribe of Judah; so did Hirah the Adullamite act toward Judah.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed abbreviation ב"ר is read as Bereshit Rabbah. Hirah the Adullamite appears at Genesis 38:1. Audit 5 source check: a passage with the same wording (7 consecutive words) is found in Bereshit Rabbah 85.4 (Sefaria Hebrew text, labelled Public Domain). This is a wording match only; the translation was not changed.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: masons, and carpenters
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vecharashei kir vecharashei etzim* — craftsmen.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: David perceived that the LORD had established him king over Israel
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayeda David ki hekhino HaShem lemelekh* — when he saw that the kings of the peoples sent him gifts.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: David took more wives at Jerusalem
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayikach David* etc. — and all this was David’s strengthening.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: all the Philistines went up to seek David
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayishme’u Pelishtim ki nimshach David lemelekh al kol Yisra’el vaya’alu kol Pelishtim* — because the Philistines ruled all the days until Saul and David came, as it is written (Judges 15:11) of Samson: “and they said to Samson: Do you not know that the Philistines rule over us?”; and so (I Samuel 4:9): “Be strong and be men, O Philistines, lest you serve the Hebrews as they served you,” etc.; and so above in this passage: “And when all the men of Israel saw,” etc., “and they forsook their cities and fled; and the Philistines came and dwelt in them” — in those seven years that David reigned in Hebron alone, they said nothing and were not concerned that David reigned over Hebron, for they said: What is it to us? Perhaps a governor or an officer appointed David over Hebron. But when he was anointed king over all Israel, then all the Philistines went up to seek David, for they did not want there to be a king in Israel, but that they should still rule over them.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The ‘above’ citation is 1 Chronicles 10:7 (JPS: “they forsook their cities, and fled; and the Philistines came and dwelt in them”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: David inquired of God
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayish’al David be’Elohim* — through the Urim and Tummim.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: So they came up to Baal-perazim
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vaya’alu veVa’al Peratzim* — which was afterward called Baal-perazim on account of the event in which God broke (*paratz*) his enemies by his hand, so that they fled and were broken apart from one another.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: like the breach of waters
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Keferetz mayim* — like waves of water that burst out of their place and fall to another place.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: turn away from them
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Hasev me’aleihem* — the Attribute of Justice said before the Omnipresent: Master of the Universe, why did You remove Saul from before David? He said to it: Because he did not wait for Samuel seven days, as he commanded him. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to it: I will now test David — “turn away from them,” etc.; and David kept all this.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: for them hath the LORD chosen
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki im haLevi’im ki vahem bachar* — that is: He chose the Levites, and not a cart; for since we put it on a cart, Uzza was punished; and this is what it says below: “For because you bore it not at the first, the LORD our God broke forth upon us, because we sought Him not according to the ordinance,” because we put it on a cart.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The citation is 1 Chronicles 15:13 (JPS: “the LORD our God made a breach upon us”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: upon their shoulders with the bars thereon
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Kidevar HaShem bechitfam* — to carry it; not literally on their shoulders, but with poles upon them.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: their brethren of the second degree
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’immahem acheihem hamishnim* — a second rank for them: for the doorkeepers.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Zechariah, Ben, and Jaaziel
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Zecharyahu Ben* — such was his name. And all these were singers and doorkeepers on the way when they brought the Ark; and the singers and the doorkeepers whom David appointed, [that was] after they put the Ark in the tent that David pitched for it; and in the Tabernacle of Shiloh they were doorkeepers, but on the way they were not doorkeepers, for so many doorkeepers were not needed; therefore they became singers, except for two: Berechiah and Elkanah. And all this was on the way; but when the Ark rested, they were singers and doorkeepers.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: Berechiah and Elkanah as doorkeepers are at 1 Chronicles 15:23.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: with cymbals of brass to sound aloud
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vehameshorerim Heman Asaf ve’Eitan* etc. — to sound aloud: they were appointed over that musical instrument.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Zechariah, and Aziel, and Shemiramoth
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uzecharyah ve’Aziel* etc. — these who were mentioned in the verse above as doorkeepers, he made them here singers again.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: with psalteries set to Alamoth
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Al alamot* — on those musical instruments on which those psalms are played: “For the leader; upon Alamoth,” etc.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: with harps on the Sheminith, to lead
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Al hashminit lenatzeach* — that musical instrument on which those psalms are played: “For the leader; upon the Sheminith.”

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Chenaniah, chief of the Levites, was over the song
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uchenanyahu sar haLevi’im bamassa* — in what was he chief? In the *massa*, in the lifting (*nesu’at*) of song.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: he was master in the song
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Yasor bamassa* — he instructs and rebukes them about the *massa*, in playing the sweet tunes of the song, whether to raise the voice or to lower it.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: because he was skilful
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki mevin hu* — in the *massa*, in the bearing of the melody; and the expression *mevin* applies to learning song, and a parallel: “And the number of them, with their brethren that were instructed in singing unto the LORD, even all that were skilful” etc.; and it is written “And they cast lots,” etc., “the *mevin* with the pupil.”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The citations are 1 Chronicles 25:7 and 25:8 (JPS: “the teacher as the scholar”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: when God helped the Levites
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayehi be’ezor ha’Elohim* — our Rabbis said: from here, that the Ark carries itself.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: David was clothed with a robe of fine linen
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *VeDavid mekharbal* — like in Daniel, “*bekharbelatehon*”; a parallel: the *karbalta* of a rooster.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The Daniel phrase is at Daniel 3:21 (JPS: “in their cloaks”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: all the Levites that bore the ark
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vekhol haLevi’im* — likewise wrapped in a robe of fine linen; and since David was a singer, like the Levites, he too wore the garments that they wore; and as a proof, by way of distinction (*lehavdil*): such was the custom of the kings and officials of the worshippers of stars and constellations, who eat with their priests: according to their custom they would wear the garments of their priests.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: an ephod of linen
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’al David efod bad* — like that ephod of Aaron, which was a kind of two *levadin*, one in front and one behind, reaching to his loins, and the girdle was woven from it, and he girded himself with it.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The word לבדין is left transliterated; I take it to mean linen pieces, but this is not confirmed.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Michal the daughter of Saul looked out at the window
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *UMikhal bat Sha’ul* etc. — since the Book of Chronicles is for the honor of David, it does not write here what Michal said to David, as it is written in Samuel: “How glorious was the king of Israel today, who uncovered himself today in the eyes of the handmaids of his servants, as one of the vain fellows shamelessly uncovers himself,” for it was a disgrace to David that a woman said such a thing to him.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 2 Samuel 6:20; JPS reads “How did the king of Israel get him honour to-day…”.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: he blessed the people in the name of the LORD
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayevarekh et ha’am beshem HaShem* — that is called upon the Ark, as it is written above: “the ark of God, the LORD that sitteth upon the cherubim, whereon the Name is called.”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 1 Chronicles 13:6.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: a cake made in a pan
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’eshpar* — one of six in a bullock (*par*).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: That is, one-sixth of a bullock. JPS renders *eshpar* here “a cake made in a pan.”

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: a sweet cake
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’ashishah* — one of six in a *hin*; and *ashishah* is like “*ashishei anavim*” (Hosea 3:1): a small flask.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: JPS renders Hosea 3:1 “cakes of raisins”; Rashi explains *ashishah* as a flask.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: to celebrate and to thank and praise
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ulehazkir ulehodot ulehallel* — *lehazkir*: to say those two psalms in which it is written “A psalm of David, *lehazkir*” (Psalm 38:1); *ulehodot*: “Give thanks to the LORD, call upon His name” (ibid. 105); and *ulehallel*: and those psalms that begin “Hallelujah.”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The phrase “to make memorial” occurs at Psalms 38:1 and 70:1; Psalm 105:1 begins “O give thanks unto the LORD, call upon His name.”

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: with trumpets continually
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uvnayahu veYachaziel hakohanim bachatzotzerot tamid* — trumpets are a musical instrument of the priests; a parallel above (15): “and Shebaniah,” etc., “and Benaiah and Eliezer the priests blew the trumpets.”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The citation is 1 Chronicles 15:24.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: to give thanks unto the LORD, by the hand of Asaph and his brethren
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lehodot laShem beyad Asaf ve’echav* — for Asaph used to begin “Give thanks to the LORD, call upon His name,” and afterward all his brethren answered after him; and a parallel in Ezra (Nehemiah 11): “and Mattaniah the son of Micha the son of Zabdi the son of Asaph, *rosh hatehillah yehudah letefillah*”; *hayyedot* is the name of a musical instrument, as it is written in Ezra (ibid. 12): “The Levites: Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, Mattaniah, over the *hayyedot*.”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation of Nehemiah 11:17 is garbled in the printed text (JPS: “who was the chief to begin the thanksgiving in prayer”); it is transliterated as printed. Nehemiah 12:8 reads, in JPS, “who was over the thanksgiving.”

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Make known His doings among the peoples
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Hodi’u va’ammim alilotav* — the deed of His mighty acts and His wonders that He did with the Ark.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: call upon His name
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Kir’u vishmo* — call the LORD to help His Ark; a parallel (I Kings 18): “and call you on the name of your god, and I will call on the name of the LORD”; the “with” next to the LORD falls to say an expression of calling, for He did wonders.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The last clause is terse and is rendered closely; the second ה' is printed in parentheses as a later insertion. The quotation is 1 Kings 18:24.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Glory you in His holy name
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Hithallelu beshem kodsho* — to say: whoever believes in our God, He will help him; and a parallel: “and thou shalt glory in the Holy One of Israel” (Isaiah 41:16).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: His holy name
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Beshem kodsho* — that you have a holy God; and so “as the LORD our God is whensoever we call upon Him” (Deuteronomy 4:7).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Let the heart of them rejoice that seek the LORD
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Yismach lev mevakshei HaShem* — and when it goes well, the heart of one who seeks the LORD with a whole heart for this purpose can rejoice.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The sentence is compressed and is rendered closely.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Seek you the LORD and His strength
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Dirshu HaShem ve’uzzo* — the Temple and the Ark are called “His strength,” as it is written “and delivered His strength into captivity” (Psalm 78:61), for He gave His Ark to be brought into captivity; and it is written “Arise, O LORD, unto Thy resting-place; Thou, and the ark of Thy strength” (ibid. 132); and therefore Eleazar who guarded it was called Uzza, because he guarded the Ark, which is called *oz*; a parallel: “four hundred shekels of silver” (Genesis 23:16), which is the numerical value (gematria) of Ephron; and so “Dan shall judge his people”; “Judah, thee shall thy brethren praise” (ibid.).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed references are Psalm 78:61, Psalm 132:8 and Genesis 23:16; the last two quotations (“Dan shall judge his people”) are at Genesis 49:16 and (“Judah, thee shall thy brethren praise”) 49:8, so the printed references there are misplaced. The numerical value of *Ephron* spelled without a vav (עפרן) is 70 + 80 + 200 + 50 = 400, which matches the four hundred shekels. Eleazar as keeper of the ark is at 1 Samuel 7:1.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Remember His marvellous works
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Zikhru nifle’otav* — the plague of mice, and that they took nursing cows while their young were shut up at home, “and the cows went straight” (I Samuel 6:12), and did not turn back; and the breach upon Uzza; and the whole song was made for the Ark (ibid.), and they used to say it over the morning *tamid*, and “Sing to the LORD” over the afternoon *tamid*; and to whom do I say that they should remember the wonders of Him who is perfect in knowledge?
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The final sentence is obscure and is rendered closely. The quotation is 1 Samuel 6:12 (JPS: “And the kine took the straight way”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: O you seed of Israel His servant
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Zera Yisra’el avdo* etc. — He is the LORD our God, etc.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: The word which He commanded to a thousand generations
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Zikhru le’olam brito davar tziva le’elef dor* — the Torah, which He commanded to be made known in the world after a thousand generations; and He saw that the world does not endure without Torah and removed from them nine hundred and seventy-four generations; and now, what is the number?
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The comment as printed ends with a question and gives no answer; 1,000 − 974 = 26.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: And He established it unto Jacob for a statute
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vaya’amideha leYa’akov lechok* etc.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The source gives no lemma for this comment; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under. The comment consists only of the quoted words of the verse.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Unto thee will I give the land of Canaan
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lemor lekha eten eretz Kena’an* — for with each and every one He made a covenant to give them the Land of Canaan.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: When you were but a few men in number
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Bihyotkhem metei mispar* — then He swore to give them the Land of Canaan, “the lot of your inheritance.” And this is a great thing: it is not to be said that because of the multitude of people you were, you took hold of the Land of Canaan, but when you were few in number. And if you say that even for a thousand and more there is a number, and what is it that is written of it, “when you were few in number”? Therefore it says “yea, very few, and sojourners in it.” The meaning: if to one settled man, I would say, to Abraham alone, to Isaac alone, to Jacob alone — if to one of them He said “To thee will I give the land of Canaan,” it would be no wonder, for they were settled in it; rather He swore to give them the land at the time when your fathers were sojourners in it, as it is written “the same is Hebron, where Abraham and Isaac sojourned.” And further, if He had said to a resident alien, “To thee and to thy seed will I give this land,” it would not be so wonderful; in this, that they were not even sojourners and residents but only…
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The comment ends abruptly in the source (“…but only”). The printed נתלתכם is read as נחלתכם (“your inheritance”). The quotation “where Abraham and Isaac sojourned” is Genesis 35:27.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: And when they went about from nation to nation
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayithalekhu migoy el goy* — Abraham went to Egypt and to Gerar, and so Isaac, and Jacob was in Laban’s house twenty years; and also now, for it is not said *vayelekhu* (“and they went”) but *vayithalekhu*: *poleitar* in the vernacular.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: He suffered no man to do them wrong
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lo hinniach le’ish la’ashkam* — even though they went from place to place, and it is the custom to harm wayfarers, who when they come to an inn have accusations found against them — but these the Holy One, blessed be He, did not allow to be harmed or wronged; a parallel: “or have oppressed his neighbour” (Leviticus 5:21). And if you say that highwaymen and the people of the other lands through which these passed did not wrong them because they did not notice them, but if they had noticed them they would have wronged them — therefore it says “yea, for their sake He reproved kings,” meaning: surely they wronged them, for example Pharaoh to Abraham, and Abimelech to Isaac, and Laban and Shechem to Jacob; and the Holy One, blessed be He, said to them:

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Touch not Mine anointed ones
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Al tig’u bimshichai uvinvi’ai al tarei’u* — with Abraham it is written (Genesis 12:17) “And the LORD plagued Pharaoh,” and it is written (ibid. 20) “But God came to Abimelech in a dream of the night, and said to him: Behold, thou shalt die,” etc.; with Jacob it is written “And God came to Laban the Aramean in a dream of the night” (ibid. 38) “and said to him: Take heed to thyself,” etc.; and further with Jacob, that they came to him to kill him because he killed Shechem and Hamor, and it is written (ibid. 35): “And they journeyed; and a terror of God was upon the cities”; and in the book (Psalm 105:16) it is explained more, for the psalm is not specified here, as it is written there: “And He called a famine upon the land,” etc., in order to exile them to Egypt.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed reference “ibid. 38” is wrong; the Laban verse is Genesis 31:24. The other citations are Genesis 12:17, 20:3 and 35:5, and Psalm 105:16.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Declare His glory among the nations
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Saperu* — the salvation that He wrought for us when the Ark was exiled to the land of the Philistines.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: His marvellous works among all the peoples
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Bekhol ha’ammim nifle’otav* — that He did with the Ark.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: For all the gods of the peoples are things of nought
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki kol elohei ha’ammim elilim* — vain, the work of human hands; and its parallel in the prophecy of (Habakkuk 2:18): “What profiteth the graven image, that the maker thereof hath graven it,” etc., up to “to make dumb idols”; “but the LORD made the heavens” — with idols it is written “to make,” but the Holy One, blessed be He, makes heaven and earth and all their hosts.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Honour and majesty are before Him
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Hod vehadar lefanav oz vechedvah bimkomo* — but the others lie like a corpse in the place where they are put, set there; because our God is the God of truth.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Ascribe unto the LORD, you kindreds of the peoples
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Havu laShem mishpechot ammim* — and what shall they give Him? It explains: honor and strength.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Ascribe unto the LORD the glory due unto His name
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Havu laShem kevod shemo* — His name is Adonai, and He is Lord of all; and this is “Ascribe unto the LORD the glory due unto His name,” for as is His name, so is His praise.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Worship the LORD in the beauty of holiness
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Hishtachavu laShem behadrat kodesh* — for so we have said: “Honour and majesty are before Him.”

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Tremble before Him, all the earth; The world also is established that it cannot be moved
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Chilu milfanav kol ha’aretz af tikon tevel bal timmot* — a king, when he sees that they are anxious and afraid of him, then casts more dread upon them, and they are more anxious about him, lest he destroy all their houses; but the way of the Holy One, blessed be He, is not so: when the world fears Him, then “the world is established that it cannot be moved,” for He takes vengeance and the upright endure, and the earth endures and is not shaken. Therefore “tremble before Him, all the earth” — but do not be anxious, for the Holy One, blessed be He, comes only to repair the world, to settle it; but when creatures are not anxious about Him and sin, then He overturns them and destroys them.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Let the heavens be glad, and let the earth rejoice
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Yismechu hashamayim vetagel ha’aretz veyomeru vagoyim HaShem malakh* — when a man reigns, all are sad, for they do not know whether there is an overflow in his judgment; but when the Holy One, blessed be He, reigns, the heavens and the earth will rejoice and all the upright will say: Now the LORD reigns, who has returned to us the Ark.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Let the sea roar, and the fulness thereof
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Yir’am hayam umelo’o* — all the creatures in the sea; a parallel: “Sing, O ye heavens, for the LORD hath done it” — because He returned to us the Ark and sent angels of destruction to execute judgment on the Philistines.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Isaiah 44:23.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: O give thanks unto the LORD; for He is good; For His mercy endureth for ever
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Hodu laShem ki tov ki le’olam chasdo* — this verse is not the end of the psalm; rather, the psalm “Give thanks to the LORD, call upon His name,” and they also said “Save us, O God of our salvation” from that psalm; and even the psalm (Psalm 106:47) begins with this verse, for how does it fit here, “and say, Save us and gather us from the nations”? Where were they exiled in the days of David, that he says “gather us from the nations”? And so is the order in Psalms: the psalm begins “Give thanks to the LORD, call upon His name,” and does not conclude until “Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel” etc. (ibid.), until “Amen. Hallelujah,” for it is all one subject; and because it is a long psalm, it was divided, and it begins “Give thanks to the LORD, for He is good.” And so with Job (Job 27:1): when it was necessary to lengthen the reply, they shortened it and divided it in two, and it says “And Job again took up his parable”; for in song, from the pangs of his joy he could not lengthen it, and divided it in two; and so with lament, from the abundance of his distress he cannot lengthen it, and divided it in two; for both song and lament are said as one, for Hannah, when she came to pray in the court (I Samuel 8), Eli thought her drunk, for he thought she did so from wine, and she said, “Wine and strong drink I have not drunk,” etc., because “out of the abundance of my complaint and my vexation”; from this, in one matter, drunkenness and distress behave alike.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The reasoning of this comment is compressed and is rendered closely. The printed reference “I Samuel 8” is wrong; Hannah’s words are at 1 Samuel 1:15–16. The citations in parentheses are Psalm 106:47 and Job 27:1 (JPS: “And Job again took up his parable, and said”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Save us, O God of our salvation
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’imru hoshi’enu* — at the end of the psalm (Psalm 105) that speaks above about captivity: “Their enemies also oppressed them, and they were subdued under their hand,” and it is written after it: “He made them also to be pitied of all those that carried them captive”; and now it is fitting to say “Save us, O LORD our God, and gather us from the nations,” as You did for them; and in Psalms it is not written “and say,” only “Save us,” for so it is fitting to say; and therefore David said these two psalms when he brought the Ark. And it is explained in Bereshit Rabbah that when the cows sang, they said these two psalms (see tractate A.A. 24): R. Samuel bar Nahmani said: “And the kine took the straight way” (*vayisharnah*) — what song did they say? “Give thanks to the LORD, call upon His name.” R. Eliezer said: “Sing unto the LORD, all the earth,” etc. Therefore David instituted them, to be said before the Ark, one psalm in the morning and one psalm in the evening. — From the mouth of our teacher Eleazar bar Meshullam, of blessed memory.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed abbreviation ב"ר is read as Bereshit Rabbah. The abbreviation ע"א is left as printed because I could not confirm its meaning. The printed reference “Psalm 105” is not where the quoted words occur: “Their enemies also oppressed them” is Psalm 106:42, and “He made them also to be pitied” is 106:46. I did not verify the passage in Bereshit Rabbah.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: to minister before the ark continually
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lesharet lifnei ha’aron tamid* — in song.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: as every day’s work required
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ledvar yom beyomo* — evening and morning.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Obed-edom with their brethren
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’Oved Edom ve’acheihem* — he left with Asaph to sing.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Obed-edom also the son of Jedithun
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’Oved Edom ben Yedituun* — [David] left [him] among the doorkeepers for the Ark.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Zadok the priest, and his brethren the priests
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’et Tzadok hakohen* — he was the head, and his brethren the priests with him; David placed them before the Tabernacle of the LORD that was at Gibeon, and he left no priest with the Ark, for there was no need to perform the service of sacrifice for an offering.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the rest that were chosen
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ush’ar habrurim* — the select ones.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: who were mentioned by name
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Asher nikvu veshemot* — great men called by name to sing before the altar at the time of the offering of the sacrifices.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the sons of Jeduthun to be at the gate
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uvnei Yedutun lasha’ar* — like “for doorkeepers”; and in the fortieth year of the kingdom of the house of David they appointed them head of the singers, as it is written (below, 25): “Of Jeduthun: the sons of Jeduthun,” etc., “six, under the hands of their father the prophet, for giving thanks and praising the LORD.”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The citation is 1 Chronicles 25:3. I did not verify the statement about the fortieth year.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: when David dwelt in his house
1 Chronicles.english_translation: (II Samuel 7:2) it is written “and the LORD had given him rest,” etc., “and the ark of God dwelleth within the curtain,” as it is written above this, “in the tent that David pitched for it.” David said: the Holy One, blessed be He, has fulfilled in me “and He giveth you rest from all your enemies round about”; and also it is incumbent upon me to do what is written soon after: “then it shall come to pass that the place which the LORD your God shall choose to cause His name to dwell there” — meaning: I will make a dwelling for Him.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quoted words are at 2 Samuel 7:1–2 and Deuteronomy 12:10–11.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the word of God came to Nathan
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayehi balaylah hahu* etc. — explained in the Midrash: the Holy One, blessed be He, said to Nathan the prophet: This man to whom I am sending you is a vower; go and say to him, before he swears to build it: You shall not build the House for My dwelling. Another explanation: the man to whom I send you is zealous; go, say it to him before he hires workmen.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: I did not verify the Midrash passage.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: from tent to tent
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Va’ehyeh me’ohel el ohel umimishkan* — that is, “and I was walking about from tent to tent and from tabernacle to tabernacle”: from Gilgal to Shiloh, and from Shiloh to Nob, and from Nob to Gibeon; and even though I was moved about from tent to tent and from tabernacle to tabernacle.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: In all places wherein I have walked among all Israel
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Bekhol asher hit’halakhti bekhol Yisra’el* etc. — this I did not do; and they too, of their own accord, it never came to their mind to build Me a house, as it came to your mind.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Thus saith the LORD of hosts
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Koh amar HaShem Tzeva’ot* — what came to your mind, I will repay you.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: from the sheepcote
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Min hanaveh* — the pasture of shepherds and sheepfolds.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: I will make thee a name, like unto the name of the great ones that are in the earth
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’asiti lekha shem keshem hagedolim* — like the name of great kings; for above it is written, “And David’s name went out into all lands” (I Samuel 31).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 1 Chronicles 14:17 (JPS: “And the fame of David went out into all lands”); the printed reference “I Samuel 31” is wrong.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: And I will appoint a place for My people Israel
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vesamti makom* etc. — “and he shall dwell in his place,” not as it was in the days of Saul, when Saul was killed and Israel fled and the Philistines dwelt in their place.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: neither shall the children of wickedness waste them any more
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Velo yosifu bnei avlah levalloto* — like *le’annoto* (“to afflict him”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: from the day that I commanded judges to be over My people Israel
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ulemimim asher tzivviti shofetim al ammi Yisra’el* — there was no rest for them like yours, in that I subdued all your enemies before you.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Moreover I tell thee
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Va’aggid lekha* — what will be your reward, that you wished to build Me a house.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the LORD will build thee a house
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uvayit yivneh lekha HaShem* — you thought to build a house for My name; by the same measure will your reward be; and the Holy One, blessed be He, announces to you that “the LORD will make you a house”: He will give you a son who will reign in your place and sit upon the throne of Israel in your stead; and anything that endures through a person after him is called a house; and so it says, “and I will set up thy seed after thee.”

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: when thy days are fulfilled that thou must go to be with thy fathers
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vehayah ki male’u yamekha lalekhet im avotekha* — that is: do not fear that I am hastening the matter, but when your days are fulfilled, then it will be, and then “I will set up thy seed after thee,” etc. (I Kings 1:14), “and I will establish his kingdom”; and so it says of Solomon, “and his kingdom was established greatly.”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed reference (1 Kings 1:14) does not contain these words; the phrase “and his kingdom was established” is at 1 Kings 2:12 (JPS: “established firmly”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: I will be to him for a father, and he shall be to Me for a son
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ani ehyeh lo le’av vehu yihyeh li levan* — (and in II Samuel 7:14) it is written, “if he commit iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men.” And the meaning: if he sins against Me, I will chasten him by the hand, like a man who chastens his son with the rod of men — for He raised up against him as an adversary Rezon, and … and Hadad; and about that verse it fits to say, “but My mercy shall not depart from him, as I took it from Saul who was before thee,” and when he transgressed before Me I removed the kingship from him and from his seed. In Samuel (ibid.) it is written “from Saul”; and the reason it is not written here, “if he commit iniquity,” etc., is out of respect for David, for he does not wish to speak in this book of any disgrace to the House of David.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed words את רזון ואת ואת הדד (“Rezon, and … and Hadad”) are incomplete or garbled. Hadad and Rezon are the adversaries at 1 Kings 11:14 and 11:23. JPS 2 Samuel 7:14 reads “if he commit iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men.”

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: that Thou hast brought me thus far
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki hevi’otani ad halom* — from the shepherds’ pasture You brought me to kingship.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: this was a small thing in Thine eyes
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vattiktan zot be’einekha* — that You gave me the kingship.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: for a great while to come
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lemerachok* — that You established my kingdom for distant times, for You said, “and I will settle him in My house and in My kingdom for ever.”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 1 Chronicles 17:14.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: after the manner of a man of high degree
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Veraitani keto’r ha’adam hama’aleh* — that You made me equal and seated me among the rows of the great; that is, I was small, and You seated me among the rows of the nobles of Your people, for You said to me, “and I will make thee a name, like unto the name of the great ones.”

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: after the manner of
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Keto’r* — the meaning: a row; and a parallel (in Kil’ayim): *rosh tor yarak* (“the head of a row of vegetables”).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: I did not verify the passage in Kil’ayim.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: What can David say yet more unto Thee
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Mah yosif od David elekha* — the meaning: what further need has David to ask of You?

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: concerning the honour which is done to Thy servant
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lekhavod et avdekha* — in order to do me honor, I who am Your servant; and You know of Yourself; and in Samuel (ibid.) it is written, “and what can David say more unto Thee? for Thou, O LORD, knowest Thy servant.”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The citation is 2 Samuel 7:20.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: for Thy servant’s sake
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *HaShem ba’avur avdekha* — thus this verse refers back to the one above; and on this account You did it to make known to me all this greatness that You have made known to me; and all is of the will of Your heart; therefore
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The comment ends with the word “therefore” and appears to be incomplete in the source.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: there is none like Thee
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *HaShem ein kamokha* — and perhaps you will say: one great like Him there is not, but one a little smaller than He there is; therefore it says:

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: neither is there any God beside Thee
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’ein Elohim zulatekha* — there is none like You and none besides You among the gods, even among the nations.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: according to all that we have heard with our ears
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Bekhol asher shama’nu be’oznenu* — all our days.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: a nation one in the earth
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Umi ke’ammekha Yisra’el goy echad* — in what are they distinguished from all peoples? In this, that God went Himself to redeem them for Himself for a people, as it is written, “I will go out into the midst of Egypt” (Exodus 12); in this we are distinguished, that He did this for no other nation in the world.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The words are Exodus 11:4 (JPS: “About midnight will I go out into the midst of Egypt”); see also 12:12. The printed reference “Exodus 12” is not the exact verse.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: in driving out nations from before Thy people
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Legaresh mipnei ammekha asher pedita miMitzrayim goyim* — and since You are unique in Your world, and Your people are distinguished from every nation, therefore it is fitting for You to give them a worthy and great king.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: let Thy name be magnified for ever, that it may be said
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Veye’aman veyigdal shimkha ad olam lemor* — that they may say, “The LORD of hosts is the God of Israel, a God to Israel,” and also that He has fulfilled His word.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the house of David Thy servant shall be established before Thee
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uveit David avdekha nakhon lefanekha* — that You have spoken, and his throne shall be established for ever.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Thou, O my God, hast revealed to Thy servant
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki attah Elohai galita* — the meaning: surely it is fitting for You to confirm Your words, for You Yourself revealed the ear to build me a house, as it is written (above): “And I tell thee, and the LORD will build thee a house.”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 1 Chronicles 17:10.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: taken heart to pray before Thee
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Al ken matza avdekha lehitpallel lefanekha* — that is: if You Yourself had not said to me to bring these good things upon my seed, it would not have come to my mind to ask, for who am I that You have brought me even thus far; but since You said, for Your own sake, to bring me all these good things, therefore I pray that You confirm Your words.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: for Thou, O LORD, hast blessed
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki attah HaShem beirakhta* — that is: You have blessed me.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: be blessed for ever
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Umevorakh le’olam* — that is: and Your servant shall be blessed for ever.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: David smote the Philistines, and subdued them
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayehi acharei khen vayakh David* — after David said to build a house and the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him, “You shall not build,” David said: since it is not for me to build the House but for my son, now I will prepare and arrange everything for him, so that when my son comes to build the House, all will be ready for him. And now the text leaves everything and goes on to relate how he prepared the building for him: that he fought with his enemies and sanctified their spoil for the building of the House. And so is the way of the verse to speak; and a parallel with Elijah and Elisha: after he said, “let a double portion of thy spirit be upon me,” the text leaves the whole account of the kings and goes on to relate of the wonders of Elisha, how they were a double portion, until it completes everything.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 2 Kings 2:9.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: king of Zobah by Hamath
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayakh David et Hadad’ezer melekh Tzovah Chamatah* — the war was at Hamath, and David smote [him] at Hamath.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: by Hamath
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Chamatah* — like *lechamat* (“to Hamath”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: to establish his dominion
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lehatziv yado* — its meaning: when he went to establish his power, to restore his border, and to set up at the river Euphrates, for he was restoring the border of the Euphrates river; and a parallel (II Samuel 18:18): “And Absalom in his lifetime had taken and reared up for himself,” etc., “and he called it Absalom’s *yad*,” whose meaning is “the power of Absalom’s border.” Another explanation: “and he called it Absalom’s *yad*” — inside the pillar he formed Absalom’s likeness, the form of the length of his hand, as it is written in the same verse, “for he said” — this form that was drawn after Absalom’s hand. (I heard this from R. Yitzchak bar Shemuel in Narbonne.)
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The second explanation is compressed and the quoted words “for he said” do not obviously fit it; it is rendered closely. JPS 2 Samuel 18:18 reads “…for he said: ‘I have no son to keep my name in remembrance’; and he called the pillar after his own name; and it is called Absalom’s monument.” The closing attribution is printed in parentheses as a later insertion.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: David houghed all the chariot horses
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vaye’aker David* — because it is written, “he shall not multiply horses to himself,” as it is written (Deuteronomy 17), “and thou shalt hough their horses” (Joshua 11:6).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The citations are Deuteronomy 17:16 and Joshua 11:6.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: reserved of them for a hundred chariots
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Veyoter mimmenu me’ah rekhev* — “he shall not multiply horses to himself”; but as much as his chariot needs is permitted.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the Arameans of Damascus
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayavo Aram deRemesek* — (II Samuel 8:5) it is written *Dammesek*, and the way of the verse is to speak so, like “from *shevet*, *sharbit*,” for “I will chasten you with whips” — Targum: *sharbitim*. This too R. Yitzchak said.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The illustration from *shevet* and *sharbit* is obscure and is rendered closely. The parallel is 2 Samuel 8:5 (JPS: “the Arameans of Damascus”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: put [garrisons] in Aram Damascus
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayasem David be’Aram Dar’mesek* — the meaning: garrisons (*netzivim*); and in Samuel there it is written explicitly, “And David put garrisons in Aram of Damascus.”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The parallel is 2 Samuel 8:6.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the shields of gold
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Shiltei hazahav* — *boukhrash* in the vernacular; a parallel: “Make bright the arrows, fill the shields” (Jeremiah 51:11).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed Old French word בויכר"ש is left as printed; I could not identify it. JPS renders Jeremiah 51:11 “Make bright the arrows, fill the quivers.” The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: David took very much brass
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Nechoshet rabbah me’od bah asah* etc. — and this is what it said: once David said to build the House and the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him, “You shall not build the House but your son,” it relates and goes on how he prepared for him to build the building.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: for Hadarezer had wars with Tou
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki ish milchamot To’u* — he was his contender, and so he proves above, “And David smote Hadarezer”; for what concern had they with Hamath, to wage war against it? Rather, Hadarezer king of Zobah went to fight against Tou king of Hamath at Hamath, and while so, David came upon him and smote him; and every vessel of gold and silver and brass he brought to David; and so (II Samuel 8:10): “and in his hand were vessels of silver and vessels of gold and vessels of brass.”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The citation is 2 Samuel 8:10 (JPS: “and he brought with him vessels of silver, and vessels of gold, and vessels of brass”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: put garrisons in Edom
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayasem be’Edom netzivim* — governors, for he did not wish to set a king over them.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: he executed justice and righteousness unto all his people
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Mishpat utzedakah* — he withdrew himself from fighting further, and from going out and coming in to battle further, and he was sitting and judging Israel always in righteousness.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Joab the son of Zeruiah was over the host
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Veyo’av vegomer* — “over the host”: since he withdrew his hand from going out further with the army, he left Joab over the army to fight all his wars; all this refers back to “he executed justice and righteousness.” And as for its interruption with “and Joab was over the host,” it was necessary, lest you say: since David executed justice, then Israel were no longer fighting; therefore it says “and Joab was over the host.”

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: was recorder
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Mazkir* — he goes back to the head, in that he would recall which case came before the king first; a parallel: “to bring the book of records of the chronicles” (Esther 6:1).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The phrase “goes back to the head” is ambiguous and is rendered literally.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Shavsha was scribe
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Veshavsha sofer* — Ahilud recalls, and Shavsha writes by his hand.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: over the Cherethites and the Pelethites
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Al haKreti vehaPleti* — its meaning: they were nations, as it is written (Zephaniah 2), “Woe unto the inhabitants of the sea-coast, the nation of the Cherethites”; and from their nations there were with David men of valour, and Benaiah over them; and a parallel (in II Samuel 15): “and all his servants passed on beside him; and all the Cherethites, and all the Pelethites, and all the Gittites,” etc.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The citations are Zephaniah 2:5 and 2 Samuel 15:18.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the sons of David were chief about the king
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uvnei David harishonim leyad hamelekh* — its meaning: the sons of David were always the first beside the king, to do all his needs.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: because his father showed kindness to me
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki asah aviv immi chesed* — David took his father and his mother and his brothers and his father’s house and settled them in the stronghold of the king of Moab, as it is written (I Samuel 22:3): “And David went thence to Mizpeh of Moab; and he said to the king of Moab: Let my father and my mother, I pray thee, come forth with you,” etc.; and the sons of Moab came and slew them all, except Elihu, David’s brother, who fled to the land of the children of Ammon, and Nahash king of the children of Ammon received him; for they are not mentioned any more except Elihu, as it is written in the divisions among the princes of Judah, “Elihu, of the brethren of David” (below, 27). And this is “that his father showed kindness to me”; and because of that enmity David smote Moab and dealt with them more severely than with the rest of his enemies, as it is written (II Samuel 8:2): “And he smote Moab,” etc.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The citations are 1 Samuel 22:3 (JPS: “come forth, and be with you”), 1 Chronicles 27:18 and 2 Samuel 8:2.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Thinkest thou that David doth honour thy father
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Hamekhabbed David et avikha be’einekha* — is it not written in their Torah (Deuteronomy 23:7), “Thou shalt not seek their peace nor their prosperity”? And do you think that he sets aside the commandment of his God and comes to seek your welfare, and for the honor of your father has sent you comforters? Surely it is to search out, etc.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: cut off their garments
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Madveihem* — like *maddo bad* (“his linen garment”; Leviticus 6).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The citation is Leviticus 6:3.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: even to their hips
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Bachetzi ad hamafsa’ah* — up to their nakedness, front and back; (and in II Samuel 9) it is written *shitoteihem* — up to their nakedness, like “with buttocks uncovered, the nakedness of Egypt” (Isaiah 20:4).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The parallel is 2 Samuel 10:4 (JPS: “even to their buttocks”); the printed reference “II Samuel 9” is wrong.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: out of Aram-naharaim, and out of Aram-maacah
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Min Aram Naharayim umin Aram Ma’akhah* — there were many Arams; and this is Aram-maacah, the Arameans dwelling in Maacah, and from the Arameans dwelling on the river Euphrates; and Aram Zobah, and Aram without qualification, is the main nation; and so the Ammonites dwelling in Ammon are called Ammonites, though the main nation is in other places; and so the sons of Esau in the land of Seir, in Edom.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: by themselves in the field
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Levaddam basadeh* — they divided their armies into two battle lines: the Ammonites in one line, at the gate of the city, opposite all Israel; and the kings who were with them in the other line, by themselves in the field, behind Israel.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: committed into the hand of Abishai his brother
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Beyad Avshai* — to Abishai: for throughout Chronicles it is written *Avshai*, and we also read *Avshai*, apart from these two that depart from the rule according to the Masorah; and therefore in this entire book *Avshai*, since this entire book was written for David’s honor, and it is not his honor that his sister’s son be called *Avishai*, which implies “I too am as important as David, for my father is Ishai (Jesse)”; therefore in this entire book *Avshai*, and in the entire book of Samuel *Avishai*, except for one *Avshai*: “and the rest of the people he gave into the hand of Avshai,” and according to the Masorah; for so it is, that Jesse was the father of his mother Zeruiah, who was his mother.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The closing sentence is compressed and the Masoretic point is rendered closely; JPS renders the name “Abishai” throughout.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Shophach the captain of the host of Hadarezer
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Veshofakh sar tzava* — (and in Samuel 29) it is written *Shovakh* the captain of the host; our Rabbis explained in Sotah: *Shovakh*, who is high like a dovecote (*shovakh*); *Shofakh*, who spilled blood like water.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The parallel is 2 Samuel 10:16 (JPS: “Shobach”); the printed reference “Samuel 29” is wrong. I did not verify the passage in Sotah.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: at the time of the return of the year
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayehi le’et teshuvat hashanah* — when there is grass in the field to feed the horses.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: precious stones in it
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uvah even yekarah* — in the crown.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: it was set upon David’s head
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vattehi al rosh David* — some interpret: literally on David’s head, and it is astonishing how his head could bear it; and our Rabbis interpreted: there was a magnet (lodestone) in it. And I heard in Narbonne that it is the custom in the land of Ishmael that they hang the king’s crown above his head, and he sits opposite it below, beneath it, on a chair; and what is written, “and it was upon David’s head,” means that it appeared as if on his head.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: there arose war at Gezer with the Philistines
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayehi acharei khen vata’amod milchamah beGezer* — what is lacking here in this passage is written in Samuel (II 21): “And the Philistines had war again with Israel; and David went down, and his servants with him, and fought against the Philistines”; and this too, out of respect for David, is not written here, for it is written there, “and David waxed faint,” and it is written (ibid.), “and Ishbi-benob, who was of the sons of the giant,” up to “he being girded with new [armour],” and he thought to smite David; and had Abishai the son of Zeruiah not helped him, he would have fallen into the hand of Ishbi; and because of that disgrace they did not write it here.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The citations are 2 Samuel 21:15–16.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Sibbecai the Hushathite slew Sippai
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Az hikkah Sibbekhai haChushati et Sippai miyyelidei harafa* — and in Samuel (ibid.) it is written *Saph*, who was of the sons of the giant, who was the brother of Goliath the Philistine and the brother of Ishbi in Nob.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The parallel is 2 Samuel 21:18 (JPS: “Sibbecai the Hushathite slew Saph, who was of the sons of the giant”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Elhanan the son of Jair
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayakh Elchanan ben Ya’ir* — he was one of David’s mighty men.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the staff of whose spear was like a weaver’s beam
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Et Lachmi achi Golyat haGitti ve’etz chanito kimnor orgim* — like that round wood around which the cloth is wound at the time of weaving; and Jonathan translated that verse in Samuel: “and David the son of Jesse, the weaver of the veil of the Temple, who was from Bethlehem, slew…” And the meaning of Ya’ir is like the forest (*ya’ar*) of Lebanon: measure for measure — let David come, whose mother weaves the veil for the Temple with a weaver’s beam, and slay Goliath, whose spear shaft is like a weaver’s beam. And why was he called Elhanan? Because the LORD was gracious to him (*chananno*). And it appears that Goliath the Gittite is not Goliath the Philistine: one, because there he calls him Goliath the Philistine; and one, because above it is written, “then Sibbecai the Hushathite slew Sippai, of the sons of the giants,” and below it is also written so, “and he also was born to the giant,” which implies that it does not mention, even regarding the brother of Goliath the Gittite, “of the sons of the giant,” that he is not his son.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The Aramaic word מחי in the Targum quotation is obscure, and I render it “weaver” on the basis of Rashi’s own explanation that follows; the last sentence is compressed and is rendered closely. The parallel is 2 Samuel 21:19 (JPS: “Elhanan the son of Jaare-oregim the Beth-lehemite slew Goliath the Gittite”). The Aramaic is translated as printed.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: a man of great stature
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayehi ish middah* — a parallel: “men of great stature” (Numbers 13:32), meaning a large man; and since he is so large that he needs to be measured, he calls him *ish middah*.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: whose fingers and toes were four and twenty
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’etzba’otav shesh vashesh esrim v’arba* — twelve on the hands and twelve on the feet; (and in II Samuel 21:20) it says “twenty and four in number,” meaning this beside that, so that one can count; and this too was his strength, that he could hold the sword with great force in his hand. And in tractate Berakhot it is explained: why is it written? For it is written “six and six, twenty and four.” It is necessary: if the Merciful One had written “six and six,” we would say: six of his [hand] and six of his foot; therefore it is written twenty-four; and if it had written twenty-four, we would say seven in this and five in that; therefore the Merciful One wrote “six and six, twenty and four.”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The parallel is 2 Samuel 21:20. I did not verify the passage in Berakhot; the Aramaic phrases in it are translated as printed.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Satan stood up against Israel
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vaya’amod Satan al Yisra’el* — even though this passage is not for David’s honor, it was written here because it says at the end of the passage that he built an altar and the LORD answered him from heaven, and this is David’s honor.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the sum of the numbering of the people
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Mispar mifkad ha’am* — a parallel: “and all your numbered (*pekudeikhem*), according to your whole number (*mispar*).”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Numbers 14:29 (JPS: “all that were numbered of you, according to your whole number”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: a thousand thousand and a hundred thousand men that drew sword
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayehi kol Yisra’el elef alafim ume’ah elef* — and Judah four hundred and seventy thousand; (and in II Samuel 24:9) it is written eight hundred thousand, and the men of Judah five hundred thousand, which implies that there were not so many of Israel as is said here; but since the wrath was from the Holy One, blessed be He, against David, there it did not write the number of all those he counted, and even Joab did not count all the tribes, as it is written, “because the king’s word was abominable to Joab”; but here, for David’s honor, it mentions the number and the count that he counted, for this is his honor, that such a large army was in his tribe. And so it proves, as I explained, that even that part of Israel which he counted — it did not write their entire number in Samuel; but here it wrote the entire number that he counted. For here it is written “And all Israel were,” and in Samuel “all” is not written; and explicitly it proves here before us, as it is written, “Joab the son of Zeruiah began to number, but he finished not, and there came wrath for this upon Israel; neither was the number put into the account of the chronicles of king David” (below, 27:24).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The numbers in 1 Chronicles 21:5 are 1,000,000 + 100,000 = 1,100,000 for Israel and 470,000 for Judah; in 2 Samuel 24:9 they are 800,000 for Israel and 500,000 for Judah.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: But Levi and Benjamin he did not number among them
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Veliy uvinyamin lo fakad betokham* etc. — Joab knew that it would be a guilt for the people, a plague; therefore Joab said: I can save these tribes from the count. Levi: if David says, why did you not number Levi? I will answer him, “for they were not numbered among the children of Israel” (Numbers 2:33). And so he says of Benjamin: were they not struck in the affair of the concubine at Gibeah? And if they are struck now, what will be left to them?

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: put away, I beseech Thee, the iniquity of Thy servant
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’attah ha’aver na et avon avdekha* — this *avon* is spelled full, with two vavs; that is: pass over the full iniquity that I have done. And four are full in the reading, and this is one of them; and the second (Psalm 51:7): “Behold, in iniquity I was brought forth”; and as explained in Vayikra Rabbah on “If a woman be delivered” (chapter 14, see there): even the most pious of the pious cannot but have one in sin without intending (Abba); and he surely did not intend except for his own need. And the third: “His own iniquities shall ensnare the wicked” (Proverbs 8), his many iniquities; and the fourth (II Kings 7:9): “and some punishment (*avon*) will overtake us”; “now therefore come, let us go and tell the king’s household,” for they said: if we do not go and tell the king’s household, it will be a great iniquity, for enemies will come upon them.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The sentence from Vayikra Rabbah is compressed and is rendered closely; I did not verify it. The printed reference “Proverbs 8” is wrong; the verse is Proverbs 5:22. The other citations are Psalm 51:7 and 2 Kings 7:9.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: I am in a great strait
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Tzar li me’od* — you say, “choose for yourself the lightest of them”; it is hard for me, and I am greatly distressed over it. A parable: to a man to whom they said, “You are dying, and in which grave do you wish to be buried — beside your father or your mother?” He said to them: Woe to the ears that hear this.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: let me fall now into the hand of the LORD
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Nippela na beyad HaShem* — in a thing that is the same for all, rich and poor.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: for very great are His mercies
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki rabbim rachamav* — perhaps He will have mercy; but our enemies will not have mercy on us.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: stretched out over Jerusalem
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Netuyah al Yerushalayim* — and as for what is written (Joshua 5:13), “and behold, there stood a man over against him, with his sword drawn in his hand,” etc., “Art thou for us, or for our adversaries?” — Joshua was standing with his back toward his enemies, and an angel came opposite him; therefore he wondered and said to him, “Art thou for us, or for our adversaries?” — to our help, since you are standing before me, or for our adversaries, to help, since you stand also opposite them. But here, when he saw the sword of the angel that was stretched out over Jerusalem, he knew by himself that he had come to smite Israel.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: these sheep, what have they done
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’eleh hatzon mah asu* — for they are like those sheep that are brought to slaughter, which cannot be saved from slaughter, for they are standing for slaughter.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: hid themselves
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Mitchabbe’im* — from the angel, to fulfill the verse (Isaiah 27): “Come, my people, enter thou into thy chambers, and shut thy doors about thee; hide thyself for a little moment, until the indignation be overpast”; and it says (Exodus 12:22): “and none of you shall go out of the door of his house until the morning.”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed reference “Isaiah 27” is wrong; the verse is Isaiah 26:20.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Ornan was threshing wheat
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’Ornan dash chittim* — because it says before us, “and the wheat for the meal-offering,” lest you wonder how there was wheat there.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the threshing-instruments for wood
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vehamorgim la’etzim* — boards with which they thresh the grain, as we learned in [ע"ג]: “*azya dekirkesa dedayyesha deyishta* is like a *morag charutz chadash* (a new sharp threshing-sledge).”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The abbreviation בע"ג and the quoted Aramaic words are left as printed; I could not identify the source. The phrase “a new sharp threshing-sledge” corresponds to Isaiah 41:15 (JPS: “a new threshing-sledge having sharp teeth”). The Aramaic is translated as printed.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: six hundred shekels of gold by weight
1 Chronicles.english_translation: (And at the end of Samuel) it is written, “fifty shekels of silver.” How so? He took from each and every tribe fifty shekels, which makes six hundred shekels, so that every Israelite would have a share in the altar.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The citation is 2 Samuel 24:24. Twelve tribes × 50 shekels = 600 shekels.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the LORD commanded the angel
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayomer HaShem lamal’akh* — to return his sword: “and he put up his sword back into the sheath thereof”; and so “And the LORD spoke to the fish and it vomited out Jonah,” etc.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Jonah 2:11.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: At that time, when David saw that the LORD had answered him
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ba’et hahi bir’ot David ki anahu HaShem* — this passage was not written in Samuel, and out of respect for David it was written here, that he made an altar; and all the verses of this passage are joined verse to verse, as if all of it were one verse.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the altar of burnt-offering
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Umizbe’ach ha’olah* — Moses’ [altar] was still at that time at the high place that was at Gibeon.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: But David could not go before it to inquire of God
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Velo yakhol David* — then, when that event occurred in which the Holy One, blessed be He, commanded him to offer a sacrifice, David was not able to go before it to inquire of God, that is, before the altar that was at Gibeon.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: he was terrified because of the sword of the angel of the LORD
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki niv’at mipnei cherev mal’akh HaShem* — and David went according to the word of the LORD and built an altar, and the LORD answered him.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: This is the house of the LORD God
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayomer David zeh hu beit HaShem ha’Elohim vezeh mizbe’ach le’olah leYisra’el* — from here on, that whoever wishes to offer a sacrifice to Him shall go out and offer on that altar.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed ה' in the middle of this sentence is unclear; the sentence is rendered as “whoever wishes to offer a sacrifice to Him.”

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the strangers that were in the land of Israel
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lichnos et hagerim* — converts, for he did not wish to employ Israelites in crushing labor; and so we find with Solomon below (II 2): “And Solomon numbered,” etc., “and he made of them seventy thousand to bear burdens,” etc.; and further it is written, “As for all the people that were left of the Hittites,” etc. — two verses (below, 21); and further it is written, “But of the children of Israel did Solomon make no servants,” etc. (ibid.).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The citations are 2 Chronicles 2:16–17 and 8:7–9; the printed chapter references are unclear.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: for the nails for the doors of the gates
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lamismerot ladlatot hasha’arim* — *nagel* in German.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The abbreviation בל"א is read as “in German”; the glossed word נעג"ל is read as *nagel*. This is not confirmed.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: and for the couplings
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ulemachbarot* — David prepared the iron with which they join and hold the doors and the gates.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: they of Tyre
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vehatzurim* — with Hiram king of Tyre.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Solomon my son is young and tender
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Na’ar varakh* — for even one forty-two years old is called *na’ar*, as it is written, “and Joshua the son of Nun, a young man (*na’ar*), departed not,” etc. (Exodus 33); for Joshua ruled after Moses only twenty-eight years and lived one hundred and ten years; it turns out that in the first year, when Israel were in the wilderness, Scripture testified about him, “and Joshua the son of Nun, a *na’ar*” — from then he was forty-two years old; therefore it was necessary to write *rakh* (“tender”), for he was only twelve years old when he reigned.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The source prints this reading with a correction: “(בשנת ל"א שנה)[בשנה ראשונה]” — the parenthetical “in the thirty-first year” is replaced in brackets by “in the first year.” The arithmetic: 110 − 28 = 82 years of age at Moses’ death, and 82 − 40 = 42 at the first year in the wilderness. The citation is Exodus 33:11.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: must be exceeding magnificent
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lehagdil lema’lah* — exceedingly great, for Solomon raised it to a hundred and twenty cubits, as it is written (I Kings 6): “and the porch before the temple of the house,” etc.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The height of one hundred and twenty is given at 2 Chronicles 3:4; the verse cited (1 Kings 6:3) gives the porch’s length (twenty cubits) and breadth (ten cubits) and no height.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the sons of Levi were numbered from twenty years old and upward
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Hemmah mispar bnei Levi miben esrim shanah vama’lah* — that is: then David instituted these watches, so that they would be ready for Solomon his son when he should come.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: their station was at the side of the sons of Aaron
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki ma’amadam leyad bnei Aharon* etc. — a parallel: “and they shall be joined unto thee, and minister unto thee.”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Numbers 18:2.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: in the purifying of all holy things
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’al tohorat lekhol kodesh* — that if the House and its vessels become unclean, they are appointed to cleanse it; for so we find with Hezekiah, as it is written (below, II 29): “And the Levites took it, to carry it out abroad to the brook Kidron,” and it is written, “Now they began on the first day of the first month to sanctify,” etc.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The citations are 2 Chronicles 29:16–17.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: to offer all burnt-offerings unto the LORD, on the sabbaths, on the new moons
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ulekhol ha’olot olot laShem leshabbatot lechadashim* — the meaning: they shall be appointed over the chambers, and also over the chamber of the Lambs’ House (*Beit HaTela’im*), where the sacrifices are, and they shall bring to the priests continually every day, by number, what is needed every day, both on weekdays and on Sabbaths and new moons and festivals, on which they add to the daily offering; all these they shall bring by number according to the ordinance; and they also help the priests to flay the sacrifice; and so we find with Hezekiah: “but the priests were too few, so that they could not flay all the burnt-offerings; wherefore their brethren the Levites did help them,” etc.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 2 Chronicles 29:34.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the courses of the sons of Aaron
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ulivnei Aharon* — the meaning: “These are the sons of Aaron,” etc., according to their courses.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: But Nadab and Abihu died before their father, and had no children
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayamot Nadav va’Avihu* etc. — and they had no sons; because they had no sons, Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests in their place; but if Nadab and Abihu had had sons, they would have preceded Eleazar and Ithamar in the high priesthood. For so we find (Ezra 3) that Jehozadak was the father of Joshua; and Jehozadak and Ezra were the sons of Seraiah, as it is written (above, 8): “and Seraiah begot Jehozadak,” and in Ezra (5) it is written, “Ezra the son of Seraiah”; and Jehozadak went into exile to Babylon, and when they went up from Babylon, Joshua went up and served, and Ezra did not serve, because Jehozadak was the firstborn and preceded his brother, the firstborn, as it is written in the prophecy of Haggai (7), “Joshua the son of Jehozadak, the high priest.”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed references are corrected as follows: “and Seraiah begot Jehozadak” is 1 Chronicles 5:40 (not chapter 8); “Ezra the son of Seraiah” is Ezra 7:1 (not chapter 5); “Joshua the son of Jehozadak, the high priest” is Haggai 1:1 (not chapter 7); “Jeshua the son of Jozadak” is at Ezra 3:2. Rashi takes Ezra and Jehozadak as brothers, both sons of Seraiah.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Ahimelech of the sons of Ithamar
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’Achimelekh min bnei Itamar* — this is Ahimelech the son of Abiathar, as is proved soon after (24:6): “And Shemaiah,” etc., “and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar.”

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: of the sons of Eleazar there were sixteen, heads of fathers’ houses
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayechalkum livnei Elazar rashim leveit avot shishah asar* — at first, in the Tabernacle of Shiloh, there were only sixteen watches, eight from Eleazar and eight from Ithamar, as explained in tractate Ta’anit; and when David saw that the heads of the mighty ones of Eleazar were many, he divided each and every watch of Eleazar into two, and established them as sixteen watches; and the watch of the sons of Ithamar he left standing as a post, as at first, as eight watches; and so he proves soon after: “one father’s house being taken for Eleazar, and taken, taken for Ithamar,” that is, like the standing-post for the watch in the Tabernacle, so David now established them in the Temple.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The arithmetic: 8 + 8 = 16 watches at first; Eleazar’s eight divided in two gives sixteen, and with Ithamar’s eight this makes 24. I did not verify the passage in Ta’anit. The phrase “taken, taken” follows the Hebrew of 1 Chronicles 24:6; JPS reads “one father’s house being taken for Eleazar, and proportionately for Ithamar.”

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Thus were they divided by lot, one sort with another
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayechalkum begoralot eleh im eleh* — to whom the lot would fall to be first or second or third or fourth, and so all of them.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Shemaiah the son of Nethanel the scribe
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayikhtevem Shema’yah* — so that they would have a record of who is first and who second, and so all of them.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: These were the orderings of them in their service
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Eleh pekuddatam la’avodatam* — these who are written here, the heads of the watches, their appointment was over the watches.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: separated for the service
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayavdel David vesarei hatzava la’avodah* — to sing the song.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: certain of the sons of Asaph, and of Heman, and of Jeduthun
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Livnei Asaf* etc. — of all the Levites he separated only the sons of Asaph.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: This is translated as printed; the verse also names Heman and Jeduthun.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: who should prophesy with harps
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Veheiman vidutun hanniv’im* — when they played these musical instruments, they would prophesy; a parallel with Elisha: “But now bring me a minstrel” (II Kings 3:15), “and it came to pass, when the minstrel played, that the hand of the LORD came upon him.”

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the number of them that did the work according to their service was
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayihyu mispharam anshei melakhah* — that is: the watches, twenty-four for twenty-four watches: four sons of Asaph, and six of Jeduthun, and fourteen of Heman, which makes twenty-four; below it sums up the number of all of them, as it is written, “so the number of them, with their brethren,” etc.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The arithmetic: 4 + 6 + 14 = 24. The closing quotation is 1 Chronicles 25:7.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: and Mattithiah, six
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Umattityahu shishah* — but you find only five; his wife was pregnant with Shimei, and he saw by the holy spirit that he too was destined to be head of a watch; therefore he said six; and this is what is said before us, “the tenth, Shimei”; this is what the paytan composed (in the *Kedushah* of the *Yotzer* for Parashat Shekalim): “Marked out from the womb to be appointed to the holy watch.”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: Five names are listed in the verse; Shimei appears at 1 Chronicles 25:17 (“The tenth to Shimei, his sons and his brethren, twelve”). I did not verify the piyyut.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: under the hands of their father Jeduthun
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Al yedei avihem Yedutun* — a parallel: “at his side made repairs” (Nehemiah 3:8).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: JPS renders Nehemiah 3:8 “Next unto him repaired Uzziel.”

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: who prophesied in giving thanks and praising the LORD
