1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Hanniva al hodot vehallel* — for they played on the harp the psalms of “Give thanks” and the psalms of “Hallelujah,” and he prophesied.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Romamti-ezer
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Veromamti Ezer* — it is one name.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the king’s seer in the things pertaining to God, to lift up the horn
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Chozeh hamelekh bedivrei ha’Elohim leharim keren* — the horn of prophecy, that he prophesies for the king; a parallel: “and exalt the horn of His anointed” (I Samuel 2:10).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: God gave to Heman fourteen sons and three daughters
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayiten ha’Elohim leHeiman* — that is: had God not given him the sons, it would not have been possible for him to have fourteen sons and three daughters, all of them fit to be heads of watches. A parallel (Ruth 4): “and the LORD gave her conception, and she bore a son” — had this gift not been from the LORD, it would not have been possible for Boaz, who was old, to beget; and so “and the LORD showed him all the land” (Deuteronomy 32) — had this not been fit from the LORD, it would not have been possible to look so far into the distance.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed text has a stray reference ד׳:י״ג before the Ruth quotation (Ruth 4:13). The printed reference “Deuteronomy 32” is wrong; the verse is Deuteronomy 34:1.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: even all that were skilful
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Kol hamevin* — in the matter of song, *mevin* is the word that applies, as it is written, “*mevin* with the pupil,” and “And Chenaniah, chief of the Levites, in the *massa*; he instructed in the *massa*, for he was *mevin*.”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The second quotation is 1 Chronicles 15:22.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: they cast lots ward against [ward]
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayafilu goralot mishmeret le’umat* — its meaning: watch against watch; and a parallel above (16): “and I have walked from tent to tent and from tabernacle” — its meaning: from tabernacle to tabernacle.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 1 Chronicles 17:5; the printed reference (16) is not that chapter.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: as well the small as the great, the teacher as the scholar
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Kakatan kagadol mevin im talmid* — the meaning: they cast lots over the watches, this opposite that, watch against watch; “the small as the great, the teacher with the pupil”: all were equal in this; to whomever the first lot came, if to the small one, he precedes to be first, and if last, he is last, and so all of them, whether teacher or pupil, whether small or great. And these watches of the Levites follow the watches of the priests: to whomever the first lot falls, his watch is first, with the watch of Jehoiarib the priest; and to whomever the second lot falls, he and his watch will serve with the watch of Jedaiah the priest.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The first two priestly watches are Jehoiarib and Jedaiah (1 Chronicles 24:7).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the first lot came forth for Asaph to Joseph
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayetze hagoral harishon le’Asaf leYosef* — his son, first.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The words בנו ראשון are ambiguous: Joseph is listed second among Asaph’s sons (Zaccur is first), and Rashi calls Zaccur the firstborn of Asaph at verse 10; the words are rendered literally.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: The second to Gedaliah
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Gedalyahu hasheni* — Gedaliah is the firstborn of Jeduthun.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: he and his brethren and sons were twelve
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’achav uvanav shneim asar* etc. — the meaning: over each and every watch twelve Levites shall come, for all of them were 288, and when you divide them into 24 parts, each and every part will be 12 Levites. It seems to me that this is “his brethren and his sons” refers to Joseph and to Gedaliah; and since both are mentioned in one verse, it wrote only once “he and his sons and his brethren”; and “all his brethren and their brethren” in the matter are not literally his brethren, but one band, which it calls brothers (*brodir shpat*) in the German language.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed words ברודי"ר שפ"ט are left transliterated and could not be identified. The arithmetic: 288 ÷ 24 = 12. The number 288 is given at 1 Chronicles 25:7.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: The third to Zaccur
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Hashlishi Zakkur* — firstborn of Asaph.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: The fourth to Izri
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Harevi’i leYitzri* — second of Jeduthun.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: The fifth to Nethaniah
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Hachamishi Netanyahu* — third of Asaph; so the lot fell from one to the other.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: For the courses of the doorkeepers
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lemachlekot lasho’arim* — they do not go in rotation, but the portions were divided opposite the gates, and then they cast lots, who for this gate and who for another gate; so it is explained below.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: of the Korahites: Meshelemiah the son of Kore
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *LaKorchim Meshelemyahu ben Kore* etc. — and a parallel above: “and Shallum the son of Kore,” etc. (above, 9).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The parallel is 1 Chronicles 9:19.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: for God blessed him
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki beirakho Elohim* — as it says above (13): “And the LORD blessed the house of Obed-edom,” etc.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The citation is 1 Chronicles 13:14.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: that ruled over the house of their father
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Hamamshalim levet avihem* — its meaning: they were rulers at their father’s side; and a parallel at the end of Daniel: “and rule with great dominion.”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Daniel 11:3.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: able men in strength for the service
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ish chayil* — not in strength and not in war, but like a man of whom they say, so-and-so is important; and so “Is not Boaz our kinsman, a mighty man of valour” (Ruth 3:2).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The words are Ruth 3:2 (“Is not Boaz our kinsman”) joined with 2:1 (“a mighty man of valour”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: had wards over against their brethren
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Mishmarot le’umat acheihem* — the heads of the twenty-four watches.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: they cast lots, as well the small as the great, according to their fathers’ houses, for every gate
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayafilu goralot kakatan kagadol leveit avotam lasha’ar vasha’ar* — to whom this gate would come, and to whom this gate, to the east, west, north, south; and so for all the gates in the court.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: for the Storehouse two and two
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ule’asuppim* — a place whose name is Asuppim.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: two at the Precinct
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Shenayim laParbar* — and it is explained in tractate Tamid: Rava said: *parbar* means *klapei bar* (toward the outside).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: I did not verify the passage in Tamid.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Ahijah was over the treasuries of the house of God
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vehaleviyim Achiyah al otzerot* etc. — he was appointed over the money with which sacrifices are purchased for the house of God, such as a sacrifice of holy things.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: The sons of Ladan
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Bnei Le’adan* — for Ladan the Gershonite the head of the fathers was Jehieli; he is the Ladan mentioned above.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: Ladan and his son Jehiel are mentioned at 1 Chronicles 23:7–8.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Joel his brother
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Veyo’el achiv* — the brother of Jehieli, as it is written above: “Jehiel, and Zetham, and Joel.”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The citation is 1 Chronicles 23:8.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: over the treasuries of the house of the LORD
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Al otzerot beit HaShem* — there were many treasuries in the court, each and every treasury for its own purpose, and over each and every one one man was appointed.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Shebuel the son of Gershom, the son of Moses, was ruler over the treasuries
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *VeShevuel ben Gershom ben Mosheh nagid al ha’otzarot* — likewise, a ruler over one of the treasuries of the court; and some interpret: a ruler over the treasuries — all the officers (*amarkalin*) were under him.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: for the outward business over Israel
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *LaYitzhari Chenanyahu uvanav lamelakhah hachitzonah* — work done outside the city, in forests and in mountains, and to cut cedars and to hew stones and to plow the field of the Hallowed-property (*hekdesh*).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Of the Hebronites, Hashabiah and his brethren
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *LaChevroni Chashavyahu* — [up to] “for all the work of the LORD”: they are officers over those who were doing the work of the LORD beyond the Jordan.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: for the service of the king
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ule’avodat hamelekh* — they too are appointed over the dwellers of the king’s inheritance, the king’s treasuries; and so before us: “for every matter pertaining to God, and for the affairs of the king.”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 1 Chronicles 26:32.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: In the fortieth year of the reign of David
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Bishnat ha’arba’im* etc. — and all these reckonings were also in the fortieth year.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: in any matter of the courses
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lekhol davar hamachlokot* — all this was from the beginning of his reign onward; and since the number of the Levites was mentioned, it relates and goes on who were the officers of David’s divisions.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: which came in and went out month by month throughout all the months of the year
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Haba’ah vehayotze’ah chodesh bechodesh lekhol chodshei hashanah* — for Israel was divided into twelve portions, and each and every portion served the king one month, and the king gave them their expenses, as it is written in the Book of Kings: “And Solomon had twelve officers over all Israel, and they provided victuals for the king and his household”; and they were ready to fight his wars and for all his service in that month; and all this was from the beginning of his reign.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 1 Kings 4:7.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: of every course were twenty and four thousand
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Esrim ve’arba’ah elef* — although Israel were more than twelve times twenty-four thousand, David chose only men of valour and the wealthy of the people, who could leave their business and engage in the king’s business; but the poor of the people, who needed to provide for themselves, David did not take.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the chief of all the captains of the host
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Harosh lekhol sarei hatzva’ot* — Jashobeam was of the sons of Perez, and was head of all twelve captains of the hosts; and because he was of the sons of Perez, David appointed him head.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Mikloth the ruler
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *UMiklot hanagid* — a member of his division who assisted him; and Mikloth.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: The third captain of the host for the third month
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Sar hatzava hashlishi* — for Benaiah’s honor it calls him “captain of the host” more than the others, except for Jashobeam, who was of the sons of Perez, whom it likewise calls “chief,” as it is written, “the chief of all the captains of the hosts,” out of respect for David, who was of the sons of Perez like him.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the priest, chief
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Hakohen rosh* — for he was chief; and some say that he was a high priest; but it is not so, for Zadok and Abiathar were high priests.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the mighty man of the thirty, and over the thirty
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Gibbor hashloshim* — as above, where it is written, “he was more honourable than the thirty,” etc.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 1 Chronicles 11:25.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Asahel the brother of Joab, and Zebadiah his son after him
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Harevi’i Asa’el achi Yo’av uZvadyah bno acharav* — for Asahel was killed at the beginning of his reign; Abner killed him (II Samuel 2); and he put Zebadiah his son after him, in his place, over his division.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The event is 2 Samuel 2:23.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Shamhuth the Izrahite
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Hasar Shamhut hayizrach* — the Zerahite.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: over the tribes of Israel
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’al shivtei Yisra’el* — we have already spoken of the heads of the divisions that were David’s, and now it relates who were the chiefs of the tribes of Israel, the chief of each and every tribe.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: David took not the number of them from twenty years old and under
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Velo nasa David mispharam lemiben esrim shanah vamatah* — its meaning: we already said that he numbered Israel and divided them into divisions, and he also numbered the Levites and set them over their service; and of all these whom he counted, he did not count a single one under twenty.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: like to the stars of heaven
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Kechokhevei hashamayim* — just as no man can count the stars of heaven, so one cannot count them.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: began to number, but finished not
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Velo khilah* — its meaning: and further I say to you: did not Joab begin another time to number the people above twenty, and he did not finish?

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: there came wrath for this upon Israel
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayehi bezot ketzef al Yisra’el* — from that portion that he numbered there was wrath upon Israel, because it came into his mind to number all Israel, to transgress the verse, “if a man can number the dust of the earth,” etc. (Genesis 13:16), and to transgress the verse, “Look now toward heaven,” etc. (ibid. 15).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The citations are Genesis 13:16 and 15:5.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: neither was the number put into the account
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Velo alah hamispar* — its meaning: although I say, “he began to number and did not finish,” and counted only a little, [yet] the number of those counted in the book of Samuel did not equal the number of those counted here (in Chronicles here): a thousand thousand and a hundred thousand, and Judah four hundred and seventy thousand; and in Samuel (at the end) eight hundred thousand, and Judah five hundred thousand. And if you say there were two numbers, that twice he numbered them, one in Samuel and one here — rather, it is so: “the number did not go up” as the number of Chronicles; for the number that he counted was not written in Samuel except a part of the number, out of grief and mourning, that they were smitten even for that little; and here, out of David’s honor, even if the number were more they would have stated it, since it implied that it was not for nothing that there was wrath upon Israel, for he had already counted many of Israel; and further, for his honor, that all of them were servants to him as one man.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The numbers: 1 Chronicles 21:5 gives 1,000,000 + 100,000 = 1,100,000 for Israel and 470,000 for Judah; 2 Samuel 24:9 gives 800,000 for Israel and 500,000 for Judah.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: over the king’s treasuries
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’al otzerot hamelekh* — treasuries of silver and gold; all this goes on to relate the greatness of David, even [the one] who was appointed over his she-asses.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: over the treasuries in the fields
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’al ha’otzarot basadeh* — and over what grows in the field: crops, wine and oil, and all kinds of foods and drinks.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: in the cities
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ba’arim* — for the five cities and for the five cities of the king and his towers.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The phrase “the five cities and the five cities of the king” is translated as printed and its sense is uncertain.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: over them that did the work of the field for tillage of the ground
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’al osei melekhet hasadeh la’avodat ha’adamah* — to plow the ground.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Ezri the son of Chelub
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ezri ben Kelub* — he was appointed over this, to command the plowing of the ground, and he gave them oxen and all the plow implements.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: over the vineyards was Shimei the Ramathite
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’al hakeramim* — to hoe and to prune the vineyards.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: over the increase of the vineyards for the wine-cellars
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’al shebakkeramim* — that is the wine treasuries.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: over the olive-trees and the sycomore-trees
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’al hazeitim* — to plant them and to pick them.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: over the herds that fed in Sharon was Shirtai the Sharonite
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’al habakar haro’im baSharon* — Shirtai the Sharonite, who was expert in their affairs.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Obil the Ishmaelite
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Hayishma’eli* — who knows the business of camels well.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: over the flocks was Jaziz the Hagrite
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’al hatzon Yaziz haHagri* — for the Hagrites dwell in tents in the field; therefore he appointed him over his flock.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Jehiel the son of Hachmoni was with the king’s sons
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *VeYechi’el ben Chakhmoni im bnei hamelekh* — their rearer and guardian, teaching them good conduct.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Hushai the Archite was the king’s friend
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *VeChushai ha’Arki re’a hamelekh* — his groomsman (*shoshvin*); Kiriath-sepher; Targum: *Kiryata di’Arki*; and in Midrash Rabbah, when David sinned with Bathsheba, he asked Hushai the Archite whether he could repent, whether the Holy One, blessed be He, would accept him with repentance, to give healing for his sin, and he told him yes; “to his friend (*lemere’ehu*) who had been his friend” of Samson, the Targum is *shoshvineih* (Judges 14:20).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed דשמעון (“of Simeon”) is read as “of Samson,” since the verse cited is Judges 14:20 (JPS: “But Samson’s wife was given to his companion, whom he had had for his friend”); the Midrash passage is unidentified and not verified.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: after Ahithophel was Jehoiada the son of Benaiah, and Abiathar
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’acharei Achitofel* — after he died, David took Jehoiada and Abiathar in his place.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: all the princes of Israel, the princes of the tribes
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayakhel David et kol sarei Yisra’el* — these princes are the princes of the tribes, as it is written (above, 27): “Furthermore over the tribes of Israel: of the Reubenites was Eliezer.”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The citation is 1 Chronicles 27:16.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the captains of the companies that served the king by course
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vesarei hamachlokot* — these are the twelve divisions of the king (as above, 27): “Now the children of Israel after their number,” etc.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The citation is 1 Chronicles 27:1.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the captains of thousands
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vesarei ha’alafim* — as above.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the captains of hundreds
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vesarei hame’ot* — their officers (*shoterehem*).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the rulers over all the substance and cattle of the king
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vesarei kol rechush umikneh lamelekh* — those whom he mentioned above in connection with the king’s treasuries, the vineyards, the olive trees and the livestock: the officers who were over the herd, the camels and the flock, for every kind of beast is called *mikneh*, as it is written, “also I had great possessions (*miknei*) of herds and flocks” of Ecclesiastes.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The Ecclesiastes quotation is 2:7 (JPS: “also I had great possessions of herds and flocks”). “Above” is read as 1 Chronicles 27:25–31, where treasuries, vineyards, olive trees, herds, camels and flocks are listed.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: all Israel
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Kol Yisra’el* — like the stranger, like the native-born.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: in the hearing of our God
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uve’oznei Eloheinu* — before our God; an example: “You are standing this day all of you before the LORD your God,” and likewise “And the king stood on the platform which was before the LORD” (2 Kings 23:3).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The first quotation is Deuteronomy 29:9 (JPS: “You are standing this day all of you before the LORD your God”); the reference is not printed. The printed second quotation (“which was before the LORD”) differs from 2 Kings 23:3 (JPS: “And the king stood on the platform, and made a covenant before the LORD”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: observe and seek out all the commandments of the LORD your God
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Shimru vedirshu kol mitzvot HaShem Eloheikhem* — this he said to all Israel together, but to Solomon he said before all Israel, “and serve Him.”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The words “and serve Him” are from the next verse (28:9). The printed word order is translated as printed.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: with a whole heart
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Belev shalem* — it does not say *bilvav shalem*, so that it would imply two hearts (*levavot*), but *belev shalem*: that you should have only one heart (*levav*) for our Father in heaven. And so the liturgical poet composed (in the *kedushta* of the Musaf of the first day of Rosh Hashanah), “Two hearts to You as one for the One.” A parallel is (1 Kings 8:61) “And your heart (*levavkhem*) shall be whole (*shalem*) with the LORD our God”; it is not written *shelemim* but *shalem*: all their two hearts shall be one whole heart. And so it is explained in Bereshit Rabbah: “and stay you your heart” (Genesis 18:5) — this teaches that the angels have only one heart; and in the future to come it will also be so, as it is written, “Mark you well her ramparts” (Psalm 48:14).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed form of the 1 Kings 8:61 quotation (*vehayah levavkhem shalem*) differs from the JPS wording (“Let your heart therefore be whole with the LORD our God”); the quotation is translated as printed. I did not verify the Rosh Hashanah poem or the Bereshit Rabbah passage. The printed abbreviation ב"ר is read as Bereshit Rabbah.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: for the LORD searcheth all hearts
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki kol levavot doresh HaShem* — here it is fitting to say “hearts” (*levavot*): the LORD searches all hearts, both the good and the evil.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: all the imaginations of the thoughts
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vechol yetzer machshavot mevin* — we learned in Bereshit Rabbah: before a creature is formed, the Holy One, blessed be He, understands what a person is destined to think.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: I did not verify the Bereshit Rabbah passage. The printed abbreviation ב"ר is read as Bereshit Rabbah.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: if thou seek Him
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Im tidreshennu yimatze lakh* — therefore I say (above), “and seek out all the commandments of the LORD.”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: “Above” is verse 8 of this chapter.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: He will cast thee off for ever
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Yaznichekha la’ad* — “He will forsake you” (*ya’azovkha*) is not written here, but *yaznichekha*, which is harsher than it, like “and they shall become foul” (*veha’aznichu*, Isaiah 19), “The Lord hath cast off (*zanach*) His altar” (Lamentations 2).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The Isaiah word is in 19:6 (JPS: “And the rivers shall become foul”) and the Lamentations quotation is 2:7 (JPS: “The Lord hath cast off His altar”); the printed references give chapters only.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the LORD hath chosen thee to build a house for the sanctuary
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki HaShem bachar bekha livnot bayit lamikdash* — not to build for Him to dwell in, for “the heavens and the heaven of heavens cannot contain Him,” but for the sanctuary (*lamikdash*), for the need of the Ark, which is called “sanctuary,” as it is written (Numbers 10), “And the Kohathites, the bearers of the sanctuary (*nosei hamikdash*), shall bear,” and that is the Ark. And He did not choose you because you are more praiseworthy than other people, but for His sake and for the sake of His mercy; therefore be strong and do it.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The Numbers quotation is 10:21 (JPS: “And the Kohathites the bearers of the sanctuary set forward”); the printed verb (*venas’u*, “shall bear”) differs from the verb of that verse (JPS: “set forward”); the quotation is translated as printed. The words “the heavens and the heaven of heavens cannot contain Him” are not given a reference; similar words occur in 1 Kings 8:27 (JPS: “heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain Thee”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the pattern of the porch
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Tavnit ha’ulam* — its length, its breadth and its height, as it is written (1 Kings 6:3), “And the porch before the temple of the house,” etc.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 1 Kings 6:3 (JPS: “And the porch before the temple of the house, twenty cubits was the length thereof…”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the treasuries thereof
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ugenazav* — the place where the treasures of the holy things are placed.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: all that he had by the spirit
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Asher hayah veru’ach immo* — as Samuel the seer showed him, as it is written below (1 Chronicles 9:22), “David and Samuel the seer established them”; and our Rabbis said: “And he asked and said, ‘Where are Samuel and David?’ And he said, ‘Behold, they are at *Beniyot* in Ramah’” — they were engaged in the building of the world, which is B.H. (*hu b"h*), and he taught him at that time what a veteran student cannot learn in many years.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed text applies a midrashic play on “Naioth in Ramah” (1 Samuel 19:19; JPS: “Behold, David is at Naioth in Ramah”), reading the place name as *beniyot*, “buildings,” and the printed form of the question omits “David” from the answer; the abbreviation ב"ה is left as printed because I could not confirm its meaning, and I did not identify or verify the midrashic source. The quotation “David and Samuel the seer established” is 1 Chronicles 9:22 (JPS: “David and Samuel the seer did ordain in their set office”); the printed form is *hemah yissad David uShemu’el haro’eh*.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the treasuries of the house of God, and for the treasuries of the hallowed things
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Le’otzrot beit ha’Elohim ule’otzrot hakodashim* — it does not specify which of the hallowed things, “which David and the heads of the fathers’ houses had dedicated”; in that chapter they were appointed over it until the Temple would be built; but these treasuries were there always, as long as the building stood.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The words quoted recall 1 Chronicles 26:26 (JPS: “which David the king, and the heads of the fathers’ houses… had dedicated”); the reference is not printed and the reading of the last clause is mine and should be checked.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: for the courses of the priests and the Levites
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ulemachlekot hakohanim vehaLeviyim* — that he divided into twenty-four watches, as above; all of this he delivered to him.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: all the vessels of service in the house of the LORD
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ulekhol kelei avodat beit HaShem* — the weight of each and every vessel, how much, as is explained.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: of gold by weight for the vessels of gold, for all vessels of every kind of service
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lazahav bemishkal lazahav lekhol keli avodah va’avodah* — and likewise for all the silver vessels, by weight.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: and for the lamps thereof, of gold
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Unerotehem zahav* — the weight for each and every lamp.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: by weight for every candlestick and for the lamps thereof
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Bemishkal menorah umenorah* — for he made ten lampstands.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: according to the use of every candlestick
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ke’avodat menorah umenorah* — and the weight of the vessels of service of the lampstand: its tongs and its fire-pans, and also the weight:
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed text ends abruptly (“and also the weight:”) and is left as printed.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the tables of showbread
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Shulchanot hama’arekhet* — to arrange upon it the showbread, for the weight of each and every table, for he made ten tables of gold in the Sanctuary (*heikhal*); and the weight of the silver for the tables that are in the Courtyard, on which the offerings are flayed, and the weight of the forks and the basins.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the golden bowls by weight
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ulekhfurei hazahav bemishkal* — *kefurei* are vessels of service to wipe the blood from the vessels; and an example is in the first chapter of Bava Metzia: “That man who wiped (*kafar*) his hands on his fellow’s cloak”; and every *kafarah* is a term for wiping and *chittuy*.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The word חטוי is left transliterated (*chittuy*) because I could not confirm its sense. I did not verify the Bava Metzia passage.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: refined gold
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Zahav mezukak* — like “refined silver.”

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the pattern of the chariot
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Velatavnit hamerkavah* — they are the cherubim on which the Divine Presence rides.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: that spread out their wings
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Laparsim* — that is, those who are spread out and who cover over the Ark, as it says (Exodus 25:20), “And the cherubim shall spread out their wings,” etc.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Exodus 25:20 (JPS: “And the cherubim shall spread out their wings on high”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: All this [do I give thee] in writing
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Hakol bikhtav* — its interpretation: everything in writing; Samuel the seer set out for him the sum of the weight of each and every vessel.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: all the works of this pattern
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Kol melakhot hatavnit* — the pattern of the House: “He made me wise and gave me understanding,” like a pattern of length, breadth and height; and Samuel expounded everything from the Torah by the Holy Spirit, as we learned: the Temple Mount was five hundred cubits by five hundred cubits (there, 27); he expounded “the length of the court, a hundred by the cubit, and the breadth fifty by fifty”; fifty times fifty is twenty-five hundred; it seems to me that he cut them into five strips, to be five hundred by five hundred. And it is founded in the *siluk* of the *kerovetz* of the Sabbath of Hanukkah that begins “Manasseh Ephraim, and Ephraim Manasseh.” And Samuel expounded all of it by the Holy Spirit, and taught David so.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The arithmetic and the exposition are translated as printed and the argument is unclear to me; fifty times fifty is indeed 2,500. The Mishnah about the Temple Mount (Middot 2:1) and the liturgical poem were not verified. The printed reference (שם כ״ז) is left as printed; the words “a hundred by the cubit, and the breadth fifty by fifty” resemble Exodus 27:18 (JPS: “The length of the court shall be a hundred cubits, and the breadth fifty every where”), but I could not confirm that this is the reference meant. Audit 5 source check: a passage with the same wording (10 consecutive words) is found in Mishnah Middot 2.1 (Sefaria Hebrew text, labelled Public Domain). This is a wording match only; the translation was not changed.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Be strong and of good courage
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Chazak ve’ematz* — so that your kingdom will endure, as (above, 28) the Holy One, blessed be He, promised you: “And I will establish his kingdom for ever, if he be constant to do My commandments,” etc.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 1 Chronicles 28:7 (JPS: “And I will establish his kingdom for ever, if he be constant to do My commandments and Mine ordinances”); the printed wording (*vehekhinoti malkhuto ad olam*) differs slightly from that verse.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: there are the courses of the priests and the Levites, for all the service of the house of God; and there shall be with thee in all manner of work
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vehineh machlekot hakohanim vehaLeviyim lekhol avodat beit ha’Elohim immekha bekhol melakhah* — that is, I have arranged, ordered and prepared for you divisions and workers, and you have nothing to delay, but to build the House at once.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the captains
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vehasarim* — those appointed over the workers, and their officers.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: all the people will be wholly at thy commandment
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vekhol ha’am lekhol devarekha* — to carry out your commands.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Solomon my son, whom alone God hath chosen
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Shlomo beni echad vegomer* — and even if there were a hundred, it would not suffice to build it; and moreover he is a youth and tender.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the work is great
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vehamelakhah gedolah* — and if you say, make the House smaller, that is impossible, for “the palace is not for man, but for the LORD God,” the great and awesome, whom “the heavens and the heaven of heavens cannot contain”; and nevertheless do not be in haste to build so great a house, for “with all my might I have prepared for the house of my God the gold for the things of gold and the silver for the things of silver,” etc.; therefore you have no labor so great.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The first quotation is from this verse (JPS: “the palace is not for man, but for the LORD God”) and the last from 29:2. The words “the heavens and the heaven of heavens cannot contain” have no printed reference; see 1 Kings 8:27 (JPS: “heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain Thee”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: onyx stones, and stones to be set
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Avnei shoham umilu’im* — like the Tabernacle, “onyx stones, and stones to be set,” etc. (Exodus 29).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The words occur at Exodus 25:7 (JPS: “onyx stones, and stones to be set, for the ephod, and for the breastplate”); I have left the printed reference (Exodus 29) unchanged.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: glistering stones, and of divers colours, and all manner of precious stones
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Avnei fuch verikmah vekhol even yekarah* — to set in the golden walls and in the silver vessels.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: marble stones
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’avnei shayish* — for the columns and the tables and for the pavement.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: because I have set my affection on the house of my God
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uvod beritzoti beveit Elohai* — the interpretation: out of the great desire that I desired the House of my God.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: I have a treasure of mine own of gold and silver
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Yesh li segulah* — I have gathered for myself a collection of gold and silver, as the text explains to us.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: refined silver
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Mezukak* — very white.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: to overlay the walls of the houses
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Latuach kirot habayit* — and one cannot overlay anything with silver or with gold unless it is refined.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: of gold for the things of gold, and of silver for the things of silver, and for all manner of work
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lazahav lazahav ulkhesef lakhesef ulkhol melakhah* — and I gave it into the hands of craftsmen and artisans, and this is what I prepared for the Temple; and although I have gathered all this, who among you will volunteer to fill my hand today for the LORD, to bring gold and silver and anything for the building? An example: “Every one whose heart was generous brought brooch and ring” (Exodus 35:22).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Exodus 35:22 (JPS: “as many as were willing-hearted, and brought nose-rings, and ear-rings”); the printed words (*kol nediv libbo hevi’u chach venezem*) differ from that verse. The sentence is awkward in the Hebrew and is translated as printed.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: to consecrate himself
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lemale* — like “and you shall fill the hand of Aaron and the hand of his sons” (there, 29), and its Targum is “and you shall bring near the offering of Aaron.”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Exodus 29:9 (end of the verse; JPS: “and thou shalt consecrate Aaron and his sons”). I did not verify the Targum wording.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the princes of the fathers’ houses
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayitnadvu sarei ha’avot* etc. — those who are written above regarding the tribes of Israel, etc.; and it is likewise written above (26), “Now the children of Israel after their number, the heads of the fathers’ houses,” etc.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed chapter number (26) does not match; the quotation is 1 Chronicles 27:1 (JPS: “Now the children of Israel after their number, to wit, the heads of fathers’ houses”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the rulers over the king’s work
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ulesarei melekhet hamelekh* — and also the officers of the work of the king’s land, and those over the king’s vineyards, etc., as above.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: darics
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’adarkonim ribbo* — *qetsonesh* in the vernacular.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The Old French word קצונ"ש is left as printed; I could not identify it. The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: to the treasure of the house of the LORD, under the hand of Jehiel the Gershonite
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Venatnu le’otzar beit HaShem al yad Yechiel haGershoni* — for he was chief over the treasuries, as above (26), “the sons of Jehiel, Zetham and Joel his brother, over the treasuries of the house of the LORD.”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 1 Chronicles 26:22 (JPS: “The sons of Jehieli: Zetham, and Joel his brother, over the treasuries of the house of the LORD”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: with a whole heart
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Belev shalem* — they gave with one heart, willingly of their own soul, and not with two hearts; for there is a person who gives against his will and not with a willing soul, or who is ashamed before others, and that is called two hearts; but these gave willingly, all of them.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: David the king also rejoiced with great joy
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vegam David hamelekh samach simchah gedolah* — and lest you say that he was like them and not more than all of them, therefore it says, “and David the king also rejoiced,” etc., more than all of them, for he was the doer of the deed; like “The mountains quaked (*nazlu*) at the presence of the LORD” (Judges 5:5), this is Sinai, more than all of them, “because the LORD descended upon it in fire” (Exodus 19:18).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotations are Judges 5:5 (JPS: “The mountains quaked at the presence of the LORD, Even yon Sinai at the presence of the LORD, the God of Israel”) and Exodus 19:18 (JPS: “because the LORD descended upon it in fire”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: David blessed the LORD before all the congregation
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayevarekh David et HaShem le’einei kol hakahal* — that he assembled them, as it says above (28), “And David assembled,” and he blessed them for their volunteering.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is from 1 Chronicles 28:1 (JPS: “And David assembled all the princes of Israel”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Blessed be Thou, O LORD, the God of Israel our father
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayomer David barukh attah HaShem Elohei Yisra’el avinu* — therefore he mentioned Israel more than Abraham and Isaac, because Jacob too vowed, as it is written, “And Jacob vowed a vow” (Genesis 28:20).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Genesis 28:20 (JPS: “And Jacob vowed a vow, saying…”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Israel our father
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Yisra’el avinu* — Israel the Elder (*Yisra’el Saba*). And so it is explained in Bereshit Rabbah: “I, David, and my people have vowed,” like Israel the Elder; and everyone who vows must mention Israel in his vow, and so “who vowed to the Mighty One of Jacob” (Psalms 32).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The Psalm quotation is 132:2 (JPS: “How he swore unto the LORD, And vowed unto the Mighty One of Jacob”); the printed reference is Psalms 32, which does not contain it. I did not verify the Bereshit Rabbah passage. The printed abbreviation ב"ר is read as Bereshit Rabbah.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: for ever and ever
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Me’olam ve’ad olam* — David said: Jethro was one convert among six hundred thousand, and he said, “Blessed be the LORD, who has delivered you”; this is a great disgrace to all Israel; and I hereby add to bless the Holy One, blessed be He, more than Jethro.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: Jethro’s words are Exodus 18:10 (JPS: “Blessed be the LORD, who hath delivered you out of the hand of the Egyptians…”); the reference is not printed.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Thine, O LORD, is the greatness
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lekha HaShem hagedulah* — he gave praise to the Holy One, blessed be He, who gave him so much to collect such wealth for the building of the Temple. And it is written above, “He shall build a house,” and next to it, “O LORD, for Thy servant’s sake (and according to Thine own heart) hast Thou wrought all this greatness”; and the term “greatness” (*gedulah*) is also fitting for the building of the Temple, as it is written (above, 22), “and the house that is to be builded for the LORD (must be) exceeding magnificent” (*lehagdil lema’lah*).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotations are 1 Chronicles 17:12 (JPS: “He shall build Me a house”), 17:19 (JPS: “O LORD, for Thy servant’s sake, and according to Thine own heart, hast Thou wrought all this greatness”) and 22:5 (JPS: “the house that is to be builded for the LORD must be exceeding magnificent”). The printed abbreviation בה"מ is read as “the Temple” (*beit hamikdash*). The words in parentheses are printed insertions.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Thine, O LORD, is the greatness
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lekha HaShem hagedulah* — although I gathered all this wealth for the building of the Temple, which is called “greatness,” You gave me all this greatness.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: and the power
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vehagevurah* — that You gave me might to fight with the enemies of Israel and to plunder their spoil before me, in order to build the House, as above: after he fought all his enemies and defeated them, it is written (above, 18), “These also did king David dedicate,” etc.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 1 Chronicles 18:11 (JPS: “These also did king David dedicate unto the LORD”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: and the glory
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vehatiferet* — all these are his praises for the fact that the Holy One, blessed be He, gave him strength to collect wealth for the building of the House, which is called *pe’er*, as it is written (Isaiah 60:13), “to beautify (*lefa’er*) the place of My sanctuary,” and also above (22) it is written, “of fame and of glory” (*leshem ultiferet*).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotations are Isaiah 60:13 (JPS: “To beautify the place of My sanctuary”) and 1 Chronicles 22:5 (JPS: “of fame and of glory throughout all countries”). The printed abbreviation ב"ה is read as “the House” from the context.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: and the victory
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vehanetzach* — that the Holy One, blessed be He, gave him victory to take the spoil of the idolaters for the need of the building.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: for all that is in the heaven
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki khol bashamayim* — it is Yours; even over what is in the heavens You rule, all the more so over what is on the earth; therefore You can give greatness to whomever You wish.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: and in the earth
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uva’aretz* — an *etnachta* (the cantillation mark), for there the verse ends, and it turns back to what is above it, as I explained.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Thine is the kingdom, O LORD, and Thou art exalted as head above all
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lekha HaShem hamamlakhah vehamitnasse lekhol lerosh* — the interpretation: a king who gave one of his servants authority and rule in the kingdom of another: the officer is his servant wherever he is, but the kingdom is not the king’s; and he to whom the kingdom belongs, the ruling servant is not his. But the Holy One, blessed be He, His is the servant appointed to rule, and the kingdom too is His — *akutria* in the vernacular. And therefore it is written, “Thine is the kingdom, O LORD, and Thou art exalted over them,” for even a *resh gargota* is appointed for him from heaven. And others explained further “and Thou art exalted as head above all”: when we think that we have praised You with all the thanksgivings and that there is no further praise, it is still nothing, for the One praised stands at the head of the praises. And so when David finished all his praises in Psalms, he begins the last psalm, “Sing unto the LORD a new song” — that is, all the praises are new, as if we had never praised Him. So Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Meir son of Rabbi Isaac of Orléans explained to me, and likewise in the Jerusalem Talmud, Chagigah, as it seems to me.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The Old French word אקוטריא is left as printed; I could not identify it. The Aramaic phrase *resh gargota* is left transliterated and the Talmudic passage was not verified. The printed quotation reads “exalted over them” where the verse has “above all”; the “last psalm” is read as the closing psalm group (Psalm 149:1, JPS: “Sing unto the LORD a new song”; Psalm 150 follows). The printed attribution to a named rabbi and to the Jerusalem Talmud is translated as printed. The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. The Aramaic phrase is translated as printed.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Both riches and honour come of Thee
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Veha’osher vehakavod milfanekha* — from Your hand; and *kavod* (“honour”) can refer to wealth, as it is written, “Take the spoil of silver, take the spoil of gold,” etc. (Nahum 2:10), and as “and of that which was our father’s hath he gotten all this *kavod*” (Genesis 35); that is, all the wealth that I have accumulated is from You, for You rule over all and in Your hand is power and might, etc.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The Nahum quotation is 2:10 (JPS: “Take you the spoil of silver, take the spoil of gold; For there is no end of the store, Rich with all precious vessels”). The Genesis quotation is 31:1 (JPS: “and of that which was our father’s hath he gotten all this wealth”); the printed reference is chapter 35, which does not contain it.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Now therefore, our God, we thank Thee
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’attah Eloheinu modim anachnu lakh* — for having apportioned to us of Your goodness.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: But who am I, and what is my people, that we should be able to offer so willingly after this sort
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vekhi mi ani umi ami ki na’atzor ko’ach lehitnadev* — that we pressed ourselves to volunteer so much in this offering; and it is not from our own, but everything is from You, and You apportioned to us a little.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: of Thine own have we given Thee
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Umiyadekha natanu lakh* — and from what You gave us from Your hand, we gave You a part. A *nun* with a *dagesh* stands in place of the second *nun*: *natannu lakh*.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: For we are strangers before Thee
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki gerim anachnu lefanekha* — and we have no portion and no inheritance in the land, and no possession, except to dwell in it; an example: “for you are strangers and settlers with Me” (Leviticus 25:23).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Leviticus 25:23 (JPS: “for you are strangers and settlers with Me”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: as all our fathers were
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Kekhol avoteinu* — a person who has sons and estates, and sold all the estates, and then his sons come to dwell in that estate after days and years, they are called strangers and settlers; but our fathers were guests. And so David said: We are not so, but we too and our fathers, all of us, are strangers and settlers in the world, as it is written, “Thine are the heavens, Thine also the earth; the world and the fulness thereof, Thou hast founded them” (Psalms 89:12).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The Psalm quotation is 89:12 (JPS: “Thine are the heavens, Thine also the earth; The world and the fulness thereof, Thou hast founded them”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: our days on the earth are as a shadow
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ketzel yameinu al ha’aretz* — it is explained in Midrash Kohelet: not like the shadow of a tree, and not like a flying bird that makes a shadow for days and years or for a single hour, but like the shadow of the wings of the bee, which has wings and has no shadow.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: I did not verify the Midrash Kohelet (Ecclesiastes Rabbah) passage.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: there is no abiding
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’ein mikveh* — there is no one who has hope that he will not die.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: that we have prepared
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Asher hekhinonu* — like *asher hevi’unu*.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The parallel form is translated as printed (*hevi’unu*, “they brought us”); I could not identify the verse it refers to.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: I know also, my God, that Thou triest the heart
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Veyada’ti Elohai ki attah bochen levav* — You test one who has two hearts, one for good and one for evil.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: hast pleasure in uprightness
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Umeisharim tirtzeh* — and a good heart and uprightness You desire; and I know that in the uprightness of my heart I made my heart upright for good, for one heart, in my volunteering all these; and as to Your people who volunteered, the interpretation is: in what is mine I am expert and know, and in what is others’ I do not know, except what I saw — that they volunteered with joy, I say.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed וכי (“and”) is read as a statement (“and I know that…”), not a question; the sentence is difficult and is translated as printed.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: now have I seen with joy Thy people, that are present here, offer willingly unto Thee
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’attah amkha hanimtze’u foh ra’iti besimchah lehitnadev lakh* — that is, I saw that they rejoiced in their volunteering, and I do not know whether it was from the willingness of their hearts, as it is written, “Then the people rejoiced for that they offered willingly.”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 1 Chronicles 29:9 (JPS: “Then the people rejoiced, for that they offered willingly”); the printed form begins *vayismechu ha’am*.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: that are present here
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Hanimtze’u foh* — those present here are those written above, “And David assembled all the princes of Israel,” etc.; but all the wealthy of Israel who are in each and every city were not present here, and therefore, Master of the World, the offering was diminished; for if all the rest of Israel had been here, then the offering would have increased.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 1 Chronicles 28:1 (JPS: “And David assembled all the princes of Israel”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: keep this for ever
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Shomrah zot le’olam* — remember for us this offering as a great commandment and as charity.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the imagination of the thoughts of the heart of Thy people
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Leyetzer machshevot levav amekha* — for the *yetzer* of their two hearts and their thoughts is for good; and it refers back to “for You try the heart,” etc.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed clause is ambiguous (*ki yetzer shenei levavam umachshevotam letovah*) and is translated as printed.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: direct their heart unto Thee
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vehakhen levavam eilekha* — their two hearts whole, to be one heart toward You; and so you should explain it.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: give unto Solomon my son a whole heart
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ulishlomo beni ten levav shalem* — to prepare his heart whole with his God to keep His commandments, etc.; and so Solomon asked, “The LORD our God be with us” until “And let your heart be whole” (1 Kings 8).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotations are 1 Kings 8:57 (JPS: “The LORD our God be with us, as He was with our fathers”) and 8:61 (JPS: “Let your heart therefore be whole with the LORD our God”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: to build the palace
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Velivnot habirah asher hekhinoti* — *apreitesh’i* in the vernacular; and now, since I have prepared and arranged everything, therefore it is easy for Solomon to build, provided that Your hand is in it.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The Old French word אפרייטש"י is left as printed; I could not identify it. The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: David said to all the congregation
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayomer David lekhol hakahal* — it refers back to “And David assembled all the princes,” etc.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 1 Chronicles 28:1.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Now bless the LORD your God
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Barkhu na et HaShem Eloheikhem* — “the God of your fathers” is not said but “your God,” which implies and not the God of their fathers; therefore it says, “Bless the LORD your God,” and they said, “our God and the God of our fathers”; and therefore, “And all the congregation blessed the LORD, the God of their fathers,” out of the conciliation of speech and because of His holiness.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The reasoning is difficult in the Hebrew and is translated as printed; the phrase *ritzuy lashon* is rendered “conciliation of speech.”

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: on the morrow after that day
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lemacharat hayom* — that day of this assembly, in which David spoke all his words, for that day they had no leisure, since when they left the assembly they were occupied buying animals for the needs of the sacrifices until night; and on the morrow, “And they sacrificed sacrifices unto the LORD,” etc.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: a thousand bullocks, a thousand rams, and a thousand lambs
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Parim elef* etc. — “a thousand lambs” and their libations; an example: “five rams, five he-goats,” etc. (Numbers 7:17): one measure for all of them.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Numbers 7:17 (JPS: “five rams, five he-goats, five he-lambs of the first year”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: sacrifices in abundance
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uzvachim larov* — such is the way of Scripture in speaking: when it speaks of two or three things, it leaves the first until the end and explains the last immediately. And so “And Laban went into Jacob’s tent” until “and entered into Rachel’s tent”; but was it not already said, “And Laban went into Jacob’s tent”? It is Rachel’s tent. Rather, “and he found them not” refers back to the last handmaids, and then it explains the first: “And he went out of Leah’s tent” first, “and entered into Rachel’s tent” — from Leah’s tent he went to Rachel’s tent, because other things must be said about this one, “Now Rachel had taken,” etc.; and then it is no longer fitting to say “and in the tent of the two maid-servants, and he found not.” Here too one must say other things about the sacrifices.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Genesis 31:33 (JPS: “And Laban went into Jacob’s tent, and into Leah’s tent, and into the tent of the two maid-servants; but he found them not. And he went out of Leah’s tent, and entered into Rachel’s tent”); “Now Rachel had taken” is 31:34. The sentence “It is Rachel’s tent” is translated as printed.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: and did eat and drink before the LORD on that day
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayochlu vayishtu* etc. — “on that day,” etc. And if it had said, “And they sacrificed sacrifices unto the LORD,” it would have interrupted between the sacrifices and the burnt-offerings with other things; and in order not to interrupt, it did not say them at once and waited until the end and says, “and sacrifices in abundance, and they ate and drank”; and so in many places, an example: “and did eat and drink before the LORD”; an example: “And Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law, took,” etc. (Exodus 9).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The Jethro quotation is Exodus 18:12 (JPS: “And Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law, took a burnt-offering and sacrifices for God”); the printed reference (Exodus 9) does not contain it.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: And they made Solomon the son of David king the second time
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayamlikhu shenit leShlomo ben David* — they had already made him king once, as it is written in Kings (1 Kings 1), “And Zadok the priest took the horn,” etc. It is explained in Horayot: a king (the son of a king) is not anointed; and why was Solomon anointed? David commanded to anoint him, in order to remove from the heart of Adonijah’s helpers the thought of making him king.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 1 Kings 1:39 (JPS: “And Zadok the priest took the horn of oil out of the Tent, and anointed Solomon”). I did not verify the Horayot passage. The words in parentheses are a printed insertion.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: anointed him unto the LORD to be prince
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayimshechu laShem leNagid* — from the term *nagidu*, the Targum of *meshakhu*; and because of “who shall go out before them, and who shall come in before them, and who shall lead them out, and who shall bring them in” (Numbers 27:17).
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Numbers 27:17 (JPS: “who may go out before them, and who may come in before them, and who may lead them out, and who may bring them in”). I did not verify the Targum wording.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: and Zadok to be priest
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ulezadok lekohen* — because Abiathar had anointed Adonijah.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The statement that Abiathar anointed Adonijah is translated as printed; 1 Kings 1:7 says only that Abiathar, with Joab, followed Adonijah and helped him (JPS: “they following Adonijah helped him”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Solomon sat on the throne of the LORD as king
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayeshev Shlomo al kisse HaShem lemelekh* — here it is fitting to say “he reigned on the throne of the LORD,” since the throne is the LORD’s, to make king over it whom He wishes. And in the Midrash it is explained: his throne was full like the moon on the fifteenth of the month, for from Abraham to Solomon are fifteen generations: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Judah, Perez, Hezron, Ram, Amminadab, Nahshon, Salmah, Boaz, Obed, Jesse, David, Solomon. And this is what is written, “His throne as the sun before Me” (Psalms 89:37), which never diminishes; and if you wish to compare it to the moon, it will be like the moon that will be established in the future to come; and from Solomon onward the kings diminished from their greatness like the waning moon, continuing until Zedekiah, and Zedekiah’s eyes were put out.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Psalm 89:37 (JPS: “His seed shall endure for ever, And his throne as the sun before Me”); “like the moon that will be established” echoes 89:38 (JPS: “It shall be established for ever as the moon”). The printed tenth name שלמה is the Salmah of Ruth 4:20–21, where JPS has “Salmon”; the list counts to fifteen. I did not verify the Midrash.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: all Israel hearkened to him
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayishme’u elav kol Yisra’el* — immediately; which was not so with Saul, as it is written, “And the base fellows said, ‘How shall this man save us?’” (1 Samuel 10:27); and David too did not reign at first except in Hebron for seven years.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 1 Samuel 10:27 (JPS: “certain base fellows said: ‘How shall this man save us?’”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: all the princes, and the mighty men
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vekhol hasarim vehagiborim* — which was not so with Adonijah, as it is written in Kings (1 Kings 1), “but the mighty men who belonged to David were not with Adonijah.”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 1 Kings 1:8 (JPS: “and the mighty men that belonged to David, were not with Adonijah”).

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: all the sons likewise of king David, submitted themselves
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vegam kol benei hamelekh David nat’nu yad* — which was not so with Adonijah, for they did not place their hand under him.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: submitted themselves
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Nat’nu yad* — they pledged faithfulness, they struck the palm to Solomon, to serve him with a whole heart.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: bestowed upon him such royal majesty
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayiten alav hod malkhut* — the interpretation: he put upon him the grace of kingship; an example: “And thou shalt put of thy honour upon him” (Numbers 27:20), so that all said, “This one is fitting.” And in Daniel it is written, “and in his place shall stand up a contemptible person” (Daniel 11:21), and they did not put upon him the majesty of kingship.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotations are Numbers 27:20 (JPS: “And thou shalt put of thy honour upon him”) and Daniel 11:21 (JPS: “And in his place shall stand up a contemptible person, upon whom had not been conferred the majesty of the kingdom”); the printed form of the Daniel quotation is a close paraphrase.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the acts of David the king, first and last
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Udevarei David hamelekh harishonim* — what befell David from his beginning to his end.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: they are written in the words of Samuel the seer
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Hinam ketuvim al divrei Shemu’el* — in the Book of Samuel.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: in the words of Gad the seer
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’al divrei Gad* — in the matter of the plague; and out of honor for the king, it tells and mentions, to say that the whole account of his greatness is written here and in other places; and so that of Mordecai, concerning the book of the chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia.
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The sentence is translated as printed and its subject is unclear. The Mordecai reference is Esther 10:2 (JPS: “are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia?”); the reference is not printed.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the times that went over him
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vehe’itim asher avru alav* — times of distress that passed over him, and this is what David said (Psalms 31), “My times are in Thy hand; deliver me from the hand of mine enemies and from them that persecute me.”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Psalm 31:16 (JPS: “My times are in Thy hand; Deliver me from the hand of mine enemies, and from them that persecute me”); the printed wording differs slightly.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: and over Israel
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’al Yisra’el* — times that passed over Israel.

1 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: over all the kingdoms of the countries
1 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’al kol mamlekhot ha’aratzot* — that came upon Israel; an example in Samuel (1 Samuel 7), “And the LORD thundered with a great thunder upon the Philistines, and discomfited them,” etc.; and likewise with Jehoshaphat (2 Chronicles 20), “And when they began to sing and to praise, the LORD set liers-in-wait,” etc.; and likewise with Sennacherib (Isaiah 37:36), “and when men arose early in the morning, behold, they were all dead corpses.”
1 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotations are 1 Samuel 7:10, 2 Chronicles 20:22 and Isaiah 37:36 (JPS: “the LORD thundered with a great thunder on that day upon the Philistines, and discomfited them”; “And when they began to sing and to praise, the LORD set liers-in-wait”; “when men arose early in the morning, behold, they were all dead corpses”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Solomon the son of David was strengthened
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayitchazzek Shlomo* etc. — because the LORD his God was with him.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Solomon spoke unto all Israel
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayomer Shlomo lekhol Yisra’el* — and who are those “all Israel”? They are the captains of thousands, as it is written (above, 28), “And David assembled all the princes of Israel”; and what did he say to them? That they should come with him to the high place that is in Gibeon.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 1 Chronicles 28:1 (JPS: “And David assembled all the princes of Israel”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Solomon, and all the congregation with him, went to the high place
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayelkhu Shlomo vekhol hakahal immo* etc. — and so it is the way of the verses to be brief: “And the LORD spoke unto the fish, and it vomited out Jonah” — He told it to vomit, and it vomited; and so (above, 21) “And the LORD commanded the angel, and he put up his sword back into the sheath thereof.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotations are Jonah 2:11 (JPS: “And the LORD spoke unto the fish, and it vomited out Jonah upon the dry land”) and 1 Chronicles 21:27 (JPS: “And the LORD commanded the angel; and he put up his sword back into the sheath thereof”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Ask what I shall give thee
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *She’al mah eten lakh* — choose and ask whatever you wish, and I will give you.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Now, O LORD God, let Thy promise unto David my father be established
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Attah HaShem Elohim ye’aman* — *prabritsh* in the vernacular.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The Old French word פראבריט"ש is left as printed; I could not identify it. The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Thou hast made me king
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki attah himlakhtani* — that is, since You made me king over such a great people, I need to have wisdom and strength to go out before them and to fight their wars, in the sense of what is said in Samuel (1 Samuel 8), “and our king shall judge us and go out before us and fight our battles”; and since I must ask for what is in my heart, I shall ask for what I need, and that is that You give me wisdom.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 1 Samuel 8:20 (JPS: “that our king may judge us, and go out before us, and fight our battles”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: that I may go out and come in before this people
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’etze’ah lifnei ha’am hazeh ve’avo’ah* — and also a king must have a wise heart to know how to judge the people, and I am a youth and tender; even for a thousand wise men it would be hard to judge so great a people. It is impossible that there not be many matters that come for judgment, and he has no patience to examine their case, for while this one is still complaining and does not stop his words, behold another comes and cries out; and who can decide a thousand cases in one day unless he is wise and understanding, in whom is the spirit of God? And this I ask, that You give me wisdom and knowledge to judge this great people of Yours, for this I need You to give me.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Because this was in thy heart
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Yaan asher hayetah zot im levavekha* — for no one asks this thing except one who has fear of Heaven in his heart, in the sense of what is said, “Moreover thou shalt provide out of all the people able men, such as fear God” (Exodus 18:21).
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Exodus 18:21 (JPS: “Moreover thou shalt provide out of all the people able men, such as fear God”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the life of them that hate thee
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’et nefesh son’ekha* — to defeat them.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: wisdom and knowledge is granted unto thee
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *HaChokhmah vehamadda nathun lakh* — that which you asked.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: I will give thee riches, and wealth, and honour
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Osher unekhasim vekhavod* — that which you did not ask, I will give you.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: such as none of the kings have had that have been before thee, neither shall there any after thee have the like
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Asher lo hayah khen lamelakhim asher lefanekha ve’acharekha lo yihyeh* — it refers to the riches and honor that you did not ask, for on the wisdom that I give you depend also riches, also honor, also length of days, as it is written, “Length of days is in her right hand; in her left hand are riches and honour” (Proverbs 3:16); and this is what is written in Kings (1 Kings 11), “So king Solomon exceeded all the kings of the earth in riches and in wisdom,” etc.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotations are Proverbs 3:16 and 1 Kings 10:23 (JPS: “So king Solomon exceeded all the kings of the earth in riches and in wisdom”); the printed reference (1 Kings 11) does not contain it.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: he placed in the chariot cities
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayanichem be’arei harekhev* — he placed some of those horsemen and chariots in the chariot cities, and because the king’s riders were there, those towns were called “chariot cities”; and some of them he placed with him in Jerusalem. (See Kings I on this verse, what Rashi explained there, and it requires study.)
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The last sentence in parentheses is a later printed insertion addressed to the reader.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: as stones
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ke’avanim* — from the abundance of silver and gold that he had, he was not concerned about putting silver and gold throughout the whole city to make tables and chairs; and our Rabbis said, “like stones of ten and eleven cubits” — since he had hewn stones, so he made of the silver.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed words עשר וי"א אמות are read as “ten and eleven cubits”; the abbreviation וי"א could also be read “and some say,” and I could not resolve it. The rabbinic source is not identified.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the horses which Solomon had were brought out of Egypt
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Umotza hasusim asher liShlomo* — that is, all the importing of horses that Solomon had was only from Egypt.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: out of Keve, the king’s merchants
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Umiqve socharei hamelekh* — and *miqve* is the gathering of horses in Egypt, and it is called in German *shtuta*.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The abbreviation בל"א is read as “in German” because the glossed words appear to be German written in Hebrew letters; this is not confirmed, and the glossed word is left as printed.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: to dedicate it to Him
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lehakdish lo* — for what need.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The comment is a short phrase introducing what follows in the verse and is translated as printed.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: to burn before Him incense
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lehaktir lefanav ketoret* — for it is a way of honor; and he also repeats, “but only to burn before Him.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The repeated phrase is in verse 5 (JPS: “save only to offer before Him”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: This is an ordinance for ever to Israel
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Le’olam zot al Yisra’el* — therefore I ask you to send me a good and strong building, because it is forever incumbent on Israel to bring their offerings in this house which I am building.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The word *binyan* (“building”) is translated as printed.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the house which I build is great
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *VeHabayit asher ani voneh gadol* — therefore I need you to send me of your building; and if you say, make the house smaller so that you will not need others, I cannot, for “great is our God above all gods,” and therefore I cannot make it small or reduce it.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: who is able to build Him a house
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Umi ya’atzor ko’ach livnot lo bayit* — since he said, “and the house which I build is great,” lest you understand “great” as meaning all its provision; but this is not so, for “who is able” (*ya’atzor ko’ach*) — who can press and gather his own strength so much to build Him a house worthy of Him? And an example above (29): “that we should be able” (*ki na’atzor ko’ach*) “to offer so willingly.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The phrase כל סיפוקו is translated literally (“all its provision”). The quotation is 1 Chronicles 29:14 (JPS: “that we should be able to offer so willingly after this sort”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain Him
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki hashamayim ushemei hashamayim lo yekhalkhelu* — and therefore he says, “who am I that I should build Him a house,” and what I am building for Him is nothing, except to burn before Him in it.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: purple
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uvaargevan* — this is *argaman*.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: crimson
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uvakarmil* — this is *tola’at shani*; know it, for *tola’at shani* is not mentioned here.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: skill to grave all manner of gravings
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Veyode’a lefatei’ach pitucheim* — like “the engravings of a signet”: one who knows how to engrave and to carve in stones — *grabir* in German.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The abbreviation בל"א is read as “in German” because the glossed words appear to be German written in Hebrew letters; this is not confirmed, and the glossed word is left as printed.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: beaten wheat
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Natati chittim makkot* — in German (*pul oyf*); and some say *makkot* means beaten, to take the wheat out of the ear.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The abbreviation בל"א is read as “in German” because the glossed words appear to be German written in Hebrew letters; this is not confirmed, and the glossed word is left as printed.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: baths of wine
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Veyayin batim* — the term *bat* is a measure for liquids; *kor* for dry things.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: endued with understanding, even Huram my master craftsman
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Yode’a binah leChuram avi* — a wise craftsman of my father he was; he is also mine.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The speaker is the king of Tyre; “my father” is translated as printed.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the son of a woman
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ben ishah* — she was a widow.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: of the daughters of Dan
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Mi-benot Dan* — of the tribe of Dan.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: his father was a man of Tyre
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’aviv ish Tzori* — he was a Jew who dwelt in Tyre, like “Obed-edom the Gittite” (2 Samuel 6), who dwelt in Gath and was a Levite. And in Kings (1 Kings 7) it is written, “and he was the son of a widow of the tribe of Naphtali, and his father was a man of Tyre”; rather, his mother was from Dan and his father from Naphtali.
