And what need is there to specify from which tribe his father and mother were? This is what is written (Genesis 30), “God hath judged me” (*dananni*) and also “with mighty wrestlings” (*naftulei Elohim*), etc. (there): Rachel said, “From now on I have twisted twistings, I have made crookednesses, until I can liken myself to Leah my sister.” If Leah will boast in Bezalel her son, who will make the Tabernacle, one of the sons of Dan must take part in his work, as it is said, “and I, behold, I have appointed with him Oholiab the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan”; and if Solomon, my sister’s son, will build the House, one of the sons of Dan and Naphtali must take part with him.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The references are 2 Samuel 6:10–11 (JPS: “the house of Obed-edom the Gittite”), 1 Kings 7:14 (JPS: “He was the son of a widow of the tribe of Naphtali, and his father was a man of Tyre”), Genesis 30:6 and 30:8 and Exodus 31:6 (JPS: “Oholiab, the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan”). The statement that Obed-edom was a Levite is translated as printed; it is not in 2 Samuel 6:10–11. The printed abbreviation ב"ה is read as “the House” from the context.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: his father was a man of Tyre
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’aviv ish Tzori* — to teach you that even though his mother was a widow, a person must take up his father’s trade (and sustain his mother — *s"a*). (So I heard from the mouth of Rabbi Solomon son of Levi of Mantuil’a, the nephew of Rabbi Moses the Preacher.)
2 Chronicles.translator_note: it is left as printed. The place name ממנטויל"א is left transliterated. The parentheses are later printed insertions.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: floats
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Rafsodot* — (and in Kings I, 5) *dovrot* — in German *pleitzitz*.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The abbreviation בל"א is read as “in German” because the glossed words appear to be German written in Hebrew letters; this is not confirmed, and the glossed word is left as printed. The parentheses are a later printed insertion; the Kings reference is 1 Kings 5:23 (JPS: “I will make them into rafts”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: by sea to Joppa
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Al yam Yafo* — the interpretation: on the seashore, like “and he went down Joppa” of Jonah.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Jonah 1:3 (JPS: “and he went down to Joppa”); the comparison is to the form without a preposition, as printed.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Solomon numbered all the strangers
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayispor Shlomo kol ha’anashim hagerim* — written full, with two *yods* (*hagiyrim*), and at first, when David numbered them, they were called there *gerim* with one *yod*; but Solomon numbered them at the time of action, when he built, and therefore it is written full. And an example: “and you shall carry up my bones from hence” — “with you” (*itkhem*) is missing in Parashat Vayechi; at the time of action, when he took them (in Parashat Beshalach), “with you” is written.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The comparison is between Genesis 50:25 (JPS: “you shall carry up my bones from hence”) and Exodus 13:19 (JPS: “you shall carry up my bones away hence with you”); the earlier numbering is 1 Chronicles 22:2. I read the printed word חסר as saying that “with you” is lacking in Genesis.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: after the numbering wherewith David his father had numbered them
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayispor* etc. — after the counting above, as it is written (above, 22), “And David commanded to gather together the strangers.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 1 Chronicles 22:2 (JPS: “And David commanded to gather together the strangers that were in the land of Israel”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: he set threescore and ten thousand of them to bear burdens
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vaya’as meihem shiv’im elef* etc. — that it repeats and mentions them and mentions the number, because it interrupted the matter, so it was necessary to say it even now; and it does not interrupt until the whole building is complete, and it says at once, “And Solomon began to build,” etc. And even within a single verse it is its way to interrupt the matter and begin again with its first words, as in “This do: take you censers, Korah, etc.” (Numbers 15), and on the morrow it is written (there), “And Moses said unto Korah: Be thou and all thy congregation, etc.,” and it repeats and says, “and take you every man his fire-pan,” etc.; but because it interrupted for several verses, it needed to be written a second time, and all the more so here.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The Korah quotations are Numbers 16:6, 16:16 and 16:17 (JPS: “This do: take you censors, Korah, and all his company”; “Be thou and all thy congregation before the LORD”; “and take you every man his fire-pan”); the printed chapter number (15) does not match.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: mount Moriah
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Behar haMoriyah* — because there the Holy One, blessed be He, appeared to David in the threshing-floor of Ornan, when the plague was stayed; and it is Mount Moriah, the Place of David.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: to build in the second day of the second month
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayachel livnot bachodesh hasheni* — it is explained at the beginning of Rosh Hashanah in the Jerusalem Talmud. And the interpretation of “in the second month” is: on the second of the month of Iyar; since he wants to say “in the fourth year of his reign,” it was necessary to repeat and say “in the second.” And an example: “and the waters decreased continually until the tenth month” (Genesis 8); and an example in Kings (1 Kings 6), “in the fourth year, in the month Ziv, which is the second month of Solomon’s reign,” etc., it refers to the fourth year. And then, in the fourth year of his reign, he began on the second, for all the days of winter he could not because of the cold, and in Nisan he could not because of Passover.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: I did not verify the Jerusalem Talmud passage. The quotations are Genesis 8:5 (JPS: “And the waters decreased continually until the tenth month”) and 1 Kings 6:1 (JPS: “in the fourth year of Solomon’s reign over Israel, in the month Ziv, which is the second month”); the printed wording is a paraphrase.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: The length by cubits after the ancient measure
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ha’orekh amot bamiddah* — and because it interrupted and said “after the first measure,” it says “cubits” again: that is, the length of the House in cubits was sixty cubits, between the Holy of Holies (*devir*) and the Sanctuary (*heikhal*), and the breadth twenty cubits.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The sixty cubits agree with 1 Kings 6:2 (JPS: “the length thereof was threescore cubits, and the breadth thereof twenty cubits”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: And the porch that was before [the house]
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *VehaUlam asher al penei ha’orekh* — the length of the porch, which is across the breadth of the House, twenty; for the length of the porch is the entire breadth of the House, twenty cubits, from north to south. And every greater measure is called length and the lesser is called breadth; and since in the Sanctuary its measure from east to west is greater, it is called length, and from north to south, which is smaller, it is called breadth; but in the porch, whose measure from north to south is greater, it is called length, and its measure from east to west, which is smaller, is called breadth. And the breadth of the porch is ten, as explained (1 Kings 7:27), “ten cubits was the breadth thereof before the house.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 1 Kings 6:3 (JPS: “and ten cubits was the breadth thereof before the house”); the printed reference (7:27) does not contain it, and the printed wording differs slightly.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: and the height a hundred and twenty
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *VeHagovah me’ah ve’esrim* — and in Kings (there) it is written, “and thirty cubits was its height.” How is this? The height of the story from the floor of the House to the ceiling of the first upper room is thirty cubits, and from upper room to upper room up to the uppermost roof, ninety cubits, as it is written (1 Chronicles 28), “Then David gave to Solomon his son the pattern of the porch, and of the houses thereof, and of the treasuries thereof, and of the upper rooms thereof” — by implication there were upper rooms there.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation from Kings is 1 Kings 6:2 (JPS: “and the height thereof thirty cubits”); thirty and ninety make one hundred and twenty. The other quotation is 1 Chronicles 28:11.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: he overlaid it within with pure gold
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayetzapehu mipenimah zahav* — within the Sanctuary (*heikhal*), which is the great house, he overlaid with gold, and not the porch; and this is what it explains going on, how he did it: “And the greater house he covered … within,” the whole house, pure gold; he covered it with cypress wood, for the whole House, the Holy of Holies and the Sanctuary, he first overlaid with cypress wood, and afterwards “and he overlaid it with fine gold” upon the walls of cypress. And because of the gold plating, for he wished to overlay the House, he covered it first with wood, so that the gold would hold firmly, for he would fasten the gold with nails in the carvings of the wood, which he carved: carvings in the wood: *temorim* are trees like palms (*tamarim*), and cherubim; and in Kings (there) it is written, “and he carved on them carvings of cherubim and palm-trees and open flowers”; *piturei* is like “a man divorces (*poter*) his wife”; like “and put forth buds” (Numbers 18) — *antverfin* in German. (From Rabbi Eleazar son of Rabbi Meshullam, of blessed memory.)
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed quotation of 2 Chronicles 3:5 is garbled and is translated as printed. The Kings quotation resembles 1 Kings 6:32 (JPS: “he carved upon them carvings of cherubim and palm-trees and open flowers”); “and put forth buds” is Numbers 17:23, not chapter 18 as printed. The abbreviation בל"א is read as “in German” because the glossed words appear to be German written in Hebrew letters; this is not confirmed, and the glossed word is left as printed. The parentheses are later printed insertions.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: which he overlaid with fine gold
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayechapehu zahav* — that is, when he had carved all the carvings, he overlaid the beams with gold after the carvings, and fastened them with nails in the wooden wall so that it would not slip, which he could not have done in the stone wall; and for this reason he covered the whole House at first with cypress wood.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: chains
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Veshasherot* — its interpretation: he carved many carvings, filling everything; and when he saw that it was all smooth between one carving and the next, he would carve a carving like a chain with which they attach anything; so he did here between one carving and another, so that it would not be smooth in between. Another interpretation: actual chains of gold he made, and joined the figures with them together.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: he garnished the house with precious stones for beauty
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayetzaf et habayit even yekarah* — he sank and set precious stones in gold in the walls of the House, for glory and beauty.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the gold was gold of Parvaim
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vehazahav* — that it says, “and he overlaid it with pure gold,” of the gold of Parvaim. Parvaim is the name of a place; and our Rabbis explained that it resembles the blood of bulls (*parim*) because of its excellence and its redness.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: I did not verify the rabbinic explanation.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: He overlaid also the house
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayachaf* — like *vayetzaf*; and it explains what he overlaid in the House: the walls and the thresholds.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the walls thereof
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vekhirotav* — of the thresholds of the House, which were of stones; and it explains, “its walls and its doors” with gold. And in Kings (1 Kings 6) it is written, “unto the walls of the ceiling” (*kirot hasefin*), and for that reason it calls the roof “the walls of the ceiling” (*kirot hasafun*), for the roof was like a ship (*sefinah*) and an overturned trough, for it is the custom to call what is round “like a ship.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The Kings quotation is 1 Kings 6:15 (JPS: “unto the joists of the ceiling”); the printed form *hasefin* differs from the Hebrew of the verse.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: he made the most holy place
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vaya’as et beit* etc. — thus he should have said, “And he made the house of the Holy of Holies, twenty by twenty”; but because he said above in this way, “And the porch … across the breadth of the house, twenty cubits,” etc., he says here likewise.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: he overlaid it with fine gold
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayechapehu zahav tov* — even in the Holy of Holies he first built walls of wood, and over it he overlaid the gold; and that it does not mention here any wood in the Holy of Holies is because of the greatness of B.H.; that is, all the walls of the Ark’s house were of gold, and there was no wood in them, and this is an honor to the Holy of Holies; and Kings (there) proves this. And know that for the honor of the House it does not mention any wood, for it is written (there), “And he garnished the house with precious stones,” and in Kings “precious stones” is not written. How is this? Rather, because the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah informs you that Solomon’s intention was for the honor of the House.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed abbreviation ב"ה (“B.H.”) is left as printed because I could not confirm its meaning here. The quotation “And he garnished the house with precious stones” is 2 Chronicles 3:6 (JPS: “And he garnished the house with precious stones for beauty”). I did not check Kings for the absence of “precious stones.”

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: six hundred talents
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lakikarim* — from talents (*mikikarim*).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the weight of the nails
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Umishkal lamasmerot* — to fasten with them the gold on the wooden walls.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: fifty shekels
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lishkalim* — for the weight of shekels: fifty shekels’ weight of gold.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: image work
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ma’aseh tza’atzu’im* — its parallel is “the offspring and the issue” (*hatze’etza’im vehatzefi’ot*, Isaiah 22:24), and its Targum is *uvenaya*; the form of boys and girls he made for the cherubim, like a *kerav’ya*; and they were of wood, and afterwards “he overlaid them with gold”; (and in Kings, 1 Kings 6:22–23) “And in the Sanctuary he made two cherubim of olive-wood”; and everything inside that was of wood he did not wish to mention in this book, out of honor.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The words *uvenaya* and *kerav’ya* are left transliterated and are not confirmed. The Aramaic phrase is translated as printed. The quotations are Isaiah 22:24 (JPS: “the offspring and the issue”) and 1 Kings 6:23 (JPS: “And in the Sanctuary he made two cherubim of olive-wood”); the printed insertion cites verses 22–23.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the wings of the cherubim were twenty cubits long
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vekhanfei hakeruvim orkham amot esrim* — how so? The wing of the one extends opposite five, and the end of the five reaches the wall of the house to the south, and the other wing reaches the wing of the other cherub at its side; that is ten cubits for the one cherub, and likewise for the other; so it comes out that the wing of one cherub reaches the north and the wing of one cherub the south; so they were as long as the whole west wall, which was twenty cubits. And as for their bodies, our Rabbis said they stood by a miracle; and by the plain sense it seems to me that their bodies protruded from them, like this bird that spreads its wings, its body protrudes outside its wings. And their height is explained in Kings (there): “the height of the one cherub was ten cubits, and so was it of the other cherub.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: I did not verify the rabbinic statement that the cherubim stood by a miracle. The Kings quotation is 1 Kings 6:26 (JPS: “The height of the one cherub was ten cubits, and so was it of the other cherub”). Arithmetic: five cubits plus five cubits is ten for each cherub, and two cherubim make twenty.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: they stood on their feet
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Omedim al raglehem* — on the floor of the house, to the west.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: their faces were inward
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ufeneihem labayit* — inward: for their heads were not erect, so that they would appear to be looking outward, but their heads were bowed and looking before them, as it is written, “with their faces one to another” (Exodus 25:20); and here it says, “and their faces were inward”; rather, they turned their heads one toward the other, and their heads were also bowed toward the house, inward. And the Ark stood in the place of the spreading of the two cherubim, and the wings of the cherubim leaned away from the wall and covered the ark-cover and the Ark with their wings; and apart from these cherubim there were the cherubim that Moses made out of the ark-cover, still attached and joined to the ark-cover and standing upon it. And do not wonder, for he likewise made ten tables and ten lampstands apart from those of Moses.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Exodus 25:20 (JPS: “with their faces one to another”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: he made the veil of blue, and purple, and crimson, and fine linen
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vaya’as et haParokhet tekhelet ve’argaman* — and he hung it on the door that was at the *amah traksin*, by which one enters the innermost part; even though it had doors, he hung it over it, as below: “And as for the entry of the house, the inner doors thereof for the most holy place,” etc.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The phrase *amah traksin* is left transliterated because I could not confirm its sense in this comment. The quotation “as below” is 2 Chronicles 4:22.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: wrought cherubim thereon
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vaya’al alav keruvim* — figures of cherubim.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: thirty and five cubits high
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Shloshim vechamesh orekh* — height. And in Kings: “And he fashioned the two pillars of brass, eighteen cubits”; Rabbi Solomon of blessed memory explained: he cast both of them as one, and afterwards divided them in two, and the missing cubit is not counted, because it is not like the work of the rest of the pillar, as it says there in the matter (2, 21), “and upon the top of the pillars lily-work”; and Rabbi Joseph also explained so. But it does not seem right, for what concern is it to us that the height was eighteen? But so I heard: surely he cast both of them as one and afterwards divided them in two, and each one came out seventeen and a half cubits.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The Kings quotation is 1 Kings 7:15 (JPS: “of eighteen cubits high each”); “lily-work” is 1 Kings 7:22 (JPS: “And upon the top of the pillars was lily-work”), but the printed reference (ב' כ"א) is left unresolved. The two pillars total thirty-five cubits; thirty-five divided by two is seventeen and a half. I did not identify “Rabbi Joseph.”

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the capital
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vehatzefet* — that is the capital, as it says there, “its thickness half a cubit,” so each is eighteen cubits. *Tzefet* means overlaid, like “and he overlaid them with gold”: that is, it was made like a hollow cap, and its thickness was half a cubit from below, and when he turned it over and put it on the pillar, the thickness comes to half a cubit, so that makes eighteen cubits. (And in 1 Kings 7:16) he calls it *koteret*, a term for crown (*keter*), as it is written, “and two capitals,” etc.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation “its thickness half a cubit” has no reference that I could confirm; seventeen and a half plus a half makes eighteen. 1 Kings 7:16 reads (JPS) “And he made two capitals of molten brass.”

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: and put them on the chains
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Veyiten ba-sharsherot* — he made chains at the top of the capital below it, and within the chains he fixed the form of pomegranates in order to cover the hollow of the capital, as it is written (there), “to cover the two bowls of the capital”; and because of its hollow he calls them *gulot* (“bowls”). This lattice (*sevakhah*) that is written there — they are the chains, a term like “and he walks upon a net” (*sevakhah*, Job 18:8), a term for branches, like “in the thicket (*besevakh*) by his horns” (Genesis 22:13); and some say *kofya*, and Rabbi Eleazar’s interpretation is “branches.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The word *kofya* is left transliterated and not confirmed. The quotations are Job 18:8 (JPS: “he walketh upon the toils”) and Genesis 22:13 (JPS: “caught in the thicket by his horns”); the words about covering the bowls are from Kings (cf. 1 Kings 7:41).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: before the temple
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Al penei haHeikhal* — at the entrance of the Sanctuary on the outside, in the porch, as is proven (1 Kings 7:17), “and the capital that is upon the top of the pillars, the porch of the Sanctuary, lily-work.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed quotation resembles 1 Kings 7:19 (JPS: “And the capitals that were upon the top of the pillars in the porch were of lily-work”); the printed reference (7:17) is left unresolved.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: one on the right hand
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Echad mimin* — of the entrance.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the other on the left
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’echad mehasemol* — of the entrance.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Jachin
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Yakhin* — and Boaz: *Yakhin* is named for the kingdom of the House of David, which is likened to the moon, as it is written, “as the moon, established (*yikon*) for ever” (Psalms 89).
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Psalm 89:38 (JPS: “It shall be established for ever as the moon”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Boaz
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Bo’az* — (corresponding to the sun, which goes forth with might and strength, *yush"h*), as it is said, “rejoiceth as a strong man to run his course” (Psalms 19); and the *bet* in *Bo’az* is like (Genesis 5) the *mem* in *Noach*, “shall comfort us” (*yenachamenu*) (in 1 Samuel 1) “because I have asked him of the LORD.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed abbreviation יוש"ה is left as printed, and the grammatical comparison is translated as printed without resolving it. The quotations are Psalm 19:6 (JPS: “rejoiceth as a strong man to run his course”), Genesis 5:29 (JPS: “This same shall comfort us”) and 1 Samuel 1:20 (JPS: “because I have asked him of the LORD”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: called the name of that on the right hand Jachin
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayikra shem hayemini Yakhin* — although the moon is smaller than the sun, what would benefit it, that it be established, is “as the moon, established (*yikon*),” and not like the waning moon. Solomon said: If the Holy One, blessed be He, has called my kingdom sun and moon, I too will make something established and enduring: mighty pillars of brass. Another explanation: Huram, who was of the sons of Dan, made the pillars; he called the one *Yakhin* after his father Samson, of whom it is said (Judges 16), “And Samson took fast hold of the two middle pillars (etc. ‘established,’ etc.)”; and Solomon called the second *Bo’az* after his grandfather Boaz; an example: “And Laban called it Jegar-sahadutha” (Genesis 31:47).
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotations are Judges 16:29 (JPS: “And Samson took fast hold of the two middle pillars upon which the house rested”) and Genesis 31:47 (JPS: “And Laban called it Jegar-sahadutha; but Jacob called it Galeed”); “my kingdom sun and moon” recalls Psalm 89:37–38. The printed “his father Samson” is translated as printed.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: ten cubits from brim to brim
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Eser ba’amah misfato el sefato* — ten by ten in its middle, round all around.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: a line of thirty cubits did compass it round about
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vekav shloshim ba’amah yasov oto* — whatever has three handbreadths in its circumference has a handbreadth in its breadth.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: This is the rule that a circle’s circumference is three times its diameter; thirty cubits over ten is three.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the height thereof was five cubits
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vachamesh ba’amah komato* — its depth.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: under it was the similitude of oxen
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Udemut bekarim tachat lo* — the form of the likeness of oxen he cast from it, to stand upon it, attached to it, as it says at the end of the verse, “the oxen were cast when it was cast.”

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: for ten cubits, compassing the sea round about
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Saviv sovevim oto eser ba’amah makifim et hayam* — it is not explained here what it was that encircled them; but in Kings (1 Kings 7) it is written, “knops (*pekaim*) beneath its brim round about,” etc. *Pekaim* are like those that are made for cups, *pimilish*, round, for ornament; and beneath its brim and around they stood, in the lower three cubits squared and the upper two round. And it is impossible for it to hold two thousand baths, which are one hundred and fifty ritual baths, except in this way, as is explained in Eruvin: the upper squared and the lower round is impossible to say, for it is written “round about from its brim.” And what it said of these knops — ten cubits on each side — but in the place of its roundness it is impossible to say ten cubits around.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The word פימילי"ש is left as printed and the argument is translated as printed; its sense is difficult. The Kings quotation is 1 Kings 7:24 (JPS: “And under the brim of it round about there were knops which did compass it, for ten cubits”). I did not verify the Eruvin passage.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: in two rows
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Shenayim turim* — the knops were.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: cast when it was cast
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Yetzukim bemutzaketo* — all of it cast together; not that he joined the knops to it after its casting, by nails or by an adhesive that is called *shuldora* in the vernacular.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The Old French word שולדור"א is left as printed; I could not identify it. The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: all their hinder parts were inward
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vekhol achoreihem bayetah* — the hindquarters of these oxen faced inward, toward what is beneath them; those in the north turned their hindquarters toward those in the south, and those of the east toward those of the west.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: a handbreadth thick
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’avyo tefach* — its base and its sides; but near its mouth it was thin, hammered and beaten out.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the brim of a cup
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Kema’aseh sefat kos* — from which one drinks, and a lily flower was depicted on it.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: it received and held three thousand baths
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Machazik batim sheloshet alafim yakhil* — this too is “held”; and in Kings (there) it is written, “it held two thousand baths”: the heaping, three. For the bath is three *se’ah*, as it is said, “The ephah and the bath shall be of one measure,” so you have six thousand *se’ah*; thus a hundred and fifty ritual baths — at four thousand *se’ah*, a hundred ritual baths; so also for the remaining two thousand *se’ah*, fifty ritual baths. And even if you divide the vessel according to the measure the Sages estimated for a ritual bath, a cubit by a cubit by a height of three cubits, you will find it so: three cubits squared in height and ten by ten from brim to brim squared, a hundred ritual baths; and two cubits round in height, ten by ten from brim to brim round, fifty ritual baths, since the square exceeds the round by a quarter.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The Aramaic words *gudsha talta* are translated as printed (“the heaping, three”) and their sense is uncertain. The quotations are 1 Kings 7:26 (JPS: “it held two thousand baths”) and Ezekiel 45:11 (JPS: “The ephah and the bath shall be of one measure”), not printed with references. Arithmetic checked: 2,000 baths × 3 *se’ah* = 6,000 *se’ah*; 6,000 ÷ 40 = 150; a square of 10 × 10 × 3 cubits ÷ 3 = 100; a round vessel at three-quarters of the square, 10 × 10 × ¾ × 2 ÷ 3 = 50; 100 + 50 = 150. I did not verify the Sages’ measure. The Aramaic phrase is translated as printed.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: ten lavers
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vaya’as kiyorim asarah* — apart from those of Moses.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: put five on the right hand
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayiten chamishah mimin* — of the laver of Moses.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: five on the left
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vachamishah mismol* — for washing in them, the sanctification of hands and feet.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: such things as belonged to the burnt-offering they washed in them
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Et ma’aseh ha’olah yadichu vam* — from the water of the laver they rinsed the entrails of the burnt-offering, and specifically the burnt-offering, but not peace-offerings, for those are eaten by their owners throughout the city. The lavers were for the sanctification of immersion.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The last sentence is translated as printed and its sense is unclear to me.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: he made the ten candlesticks of gold according to the ordinance concerning them
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vaya’as et menorot hazahav asar kemishpatam* — why is “according to their ordinance” said of the lampstands? Because it informs us why he made ten lampstands, and he expounded everything from the Torah: flowers, knops, cups, almond-shaped — they were stated in the passage of seventy; so for ten lampstands there are seven lamps each. (So explained my mother’s brother, my uncle, Rabbi Kalonymus son of Rabbi Judah, and it is Midrash.) And its seven lamps correspond to the seven planets: חנכ"ל שצ"ם.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The phrase “the passage of seventy” (בפ' שבעים) is translated literally and its sense is unclear to me; ten lampstands of seven lamps each make seventy lamps. The printed mnemonic חנכ"ל שצ"ם is left as printed; it appears to list the seven planets, but I did not verify the expansion.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: he set them in the temple, five on the right hand
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayiten baheikhal chamesh mimin* — of the lampstand of Moses.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: five on the left
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vachamesh mismol* — and all of them in the south.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: five on the left
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Mismol* — of the table, in the north.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: a hundred basins of gold
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vaya’as mizrekei zahav me’ah* — with which they throw the blood upon the altar.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the court of the priests
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vaya’as chatzer hakohanim* — the Courtyard of the Priests.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the great court
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Veha’azarah hagedolah* — this is the Courtyard of Israel.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: on the right side [of the house] eastward, toward the south
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Mikkatef hayemanit kedmah mimul negbah* — he put it at a distance from the east, from opposite the entrance, to the south of the Courtyard, because it is not honorable and fitting that people immerse opposite the entrance of the porch.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Huram made the pots
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vaya’as Churam et hasirot* — copper pots made for scooping up the ashes, to put them into the pots.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the two capitals which were on the top of the pillars
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vehagulot vehakotarot al rosh ha’amudim shetayim* — for the two pillars.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the two networks
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vehasevakhot shetayim* — these are the chains mentioned above; and know that it is so, for neither here nor in Kings does it mention chains anywhere in this passage.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: “Above” is 2 Chronicles 3:16.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: to cover the two bowls of the capitals
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lekhasot et shetei gulot hakotarot* — to cover the hollow of the capital with the nets, and those branches are like the branches of palm-fronds, as I explained.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the four hundred pomegranates
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’et harimonim arba me’ot* — above it says, “and he made a hundred pomegranates”; how is this? Rather, so we must explain: certainly he made four hundred pomegranates, as stated here; and what it said, “a hundred,” is a hundred for each row, and there are four rows, as it said two rows for one network, and likewise two rows of pomegranates for one network, so that is four rows. And the pomegranates were set round about within the lattice-work, studded and fixed, to cover well the two bowls of the capitals.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: “Above” is 2 Chronicles 3:16 (JPS: “he made a hundred pomegranates”); four rows of a hundred make four hundred.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the bases
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’et hamekhonot asah* — and in Kings it is written, “And he made the ten bases”; they are the stands of the laver, and there their work is explained.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 1 Kings 7:27 (JPS: “And he made the ten bases of brass”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: The pots also, and the shovels, and the flesh-hooks
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’et hasirot ve’et hayi’im ve’et hamizlagot* — although we already said it above, it comes and repeats and teaches further, to inform us that they were of brass, and it also informs us of the flesh-hooks, which were not mentioned above.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: bright brass
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Maruk* — like “Furbish (*mirku*) the spears” (Jeremiah 46:4) and “it shall be scoured (*murak*) and rinsed in water” (Leviticus 6:21); and in Kings (1 Kings 7) it is written *memorat*, like “if his head be made bald” (*yimmaret*, Leviticus 13:40), and its Targum is “good brass.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotations are Jeremiah 46:4 (JPS: “Furbish the spears”), Leviticus 6:21 (JPS: “it shall be scoured, and rinsed in water”), 1 Kings 7:45 (JPS: “burnished brass”) and Leviticus 13:40 (JPS: “And if a man’s hair be fallen off his head, he is bald”). I did not verify the Targum wording.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: in the clay ground
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Be’avi ha’adamah* — the Targum is *gargushta*; *ardila* in the vernacular.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The Old French word ארדי"לא is left as printed; I could not identify it. The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. The Aramaic phrase is translated as printed.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: between Succoth and Zeredah
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ben Sukkot uvein Tzeredatah* — and in Kings it is written “Zarethan.” Zeredah is the place of Jeroboam, “and Jeroboam son of Nebat, an Ephraimite of Zeredah, and the name of his mother Zeruah, a widow woman” (1 Kings 11:26); because the dead defiles in a tent, and a leper likewise, and so idolatry, as we learned in the third chapter of Avodah Zarah at its end: “a widow” — one who has widowed Israel from his God. From “Zeredah” it appears that he narrowed (*hetzar*) the Torah and did not broaden it: “he narrowed the law (*dat*) of our God.” So my uncle of blessed memory explained to me.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The wordplay is translated as printed and its sense is unclear to me; I did not verify the Avodah Zarah passage. The quotations are 1 Kings 7:46 (JPS: “between Succoth and Zarethan”) and 1 Kings 11:26 (JPS: “an Ephraimite of Zeredah… whose mother’s name was Zeruah, a widow”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the candlesticks with their lamps
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’et hamenorot ner’oteihem* — to remove from the heart of the interpreters (the idea) that they made the lamps from the body of the lampstand and attached to it, since it is written “and the lampstands and their lamps.” That it mentions the lamps separately, and not the other parts of the lampstand separately — cups, knops and flowers — implies that the lamps were not attached; and since they were not attached, they look like a separate work and it is necessary to mention their lamps, but the other works that were attached to it it does not mention, for they are called by the name of the lampstand. And that he made ten lampstands and ten tables and ten lavers and the cherubim, and everything that he made, is explained in the Baraita of Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: I did not verify the Baraita of Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the flowers
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vehaperach* — our Rabbis explained: this corresponds to that flower which Moses added in the passage Beha’alotekha, “unto the base thereof, unto the flowers thereof,” etc., which was not said in Terumah.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Numbers 8:4 (JPS: “unto the base thereof, and unto the flowers thereof”); Exodus 25:31 (Terumah) also mentions “its flowers,” so the point of the rabbinic comparison is not clear to me, and I did not verify the rabbinic source.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the tongs
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vehamalkachayim zahav* — with which they raise the wick from the lamp that has the oil in it.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: that perfect gold
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Hu mikhlot zahav* — refined and purified, *peyin* in the vernacular; and in Menachot it is explained: from all the gold that Solomon had, from the abundance of the gold that went into the lampstand, to refine it and to fulfil “a lampstand of pure gold.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The Old French word פיי"ן is left as printed; I could not identify it. I did not verify the Menachot passage. The Old French form is printed in Hebrew letters and could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the snuffers
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vehamezamerot* — musical instruments (*kelei zemer*).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the basins
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vehamizrakot* — to throw blood with them upon the altar.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the pans
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vehakappot* — for the dishes of frankincense.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the fire-pans
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vehamachtot* — to scoop up with them the *terumat hadeshen* (the lifting of the ashes), to lift it off the altar, “and he shall take a fire-pan full,” etc.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The last quotation resembles Leviticus 16:12 (JPS: “And he shall take a censer full of coals of fire from off the altar”); the reference is not printed.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Solomon brought in the things that David his father had hallowed
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayavo Shlomo et kodshei* — everything in the verse, by its plain sense, is what remained to him of the dedicated things that David dedicated, as it is written above, “These also did king David dedicate unto the LORD with the silver and the gold that he carried away from all the nations,” etc.; and what remained he put in the treasuries of the house of God. Aggadic Midrash: Some of the Sages say that it was because he knew that its end was to be destroyed, and so that the idolaters should not say, “our fear is hard, for it took its vengeance from this House, which was built from the robberies and plunder that David plundered from the houses of idolatry.” And some say that Solomon said thus (printed: the Holy One, blessed be He): There was a famine in the days of David (my father) for three years, year after year, and he should have spent these dedicated things to sustain the poor of Israel; and I bring support, for in all the dedications that David dedicated, as written above (there), it is not said of them “Solomon made such and such,” as it is said of the brass, as it says (there), “and from Tibhath and Cun, cities of Hadarezer, David took very much brass, wherewith Solomon made the brazen sea,” etc.; but of silver and gold, of which it is not said that Solomon made anything, it follows that he did not make; and this is why no brass is written here, only silver and gold. And by the plain sense it seems to me that it did not say brass because brass is cheap, and it is not proper or fitting to bring brass into the treasuries of the house of the LORD.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The sentence about “our fear is hard” is obscure and is translated as printed. The words in parentheses are printed corrections (“Solomon” is substituted for “the Holy One, blessed be He”). The quotations are 1 Chronicles 18:11 and 18:8 (JPS: “David took very much brass, wherewith Solomon made the brazen sea”); the famine is 2 Samuel 21:1 (JPS: “a famine in the days of David three years, year after year”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Solomon assembled the elders of Israel
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Az yakhel Shlomo et ziknei Yisra’el* — he acted with the quality of wisdom, in that he assembled the elders and not the young men, more than David, who assembled even the young men, as it is written, “And David assembled all Israel to Jerusalem,” etc. (above, 28).
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed reference (28) is left as printed; 1 Chronicles 28:1 reads “And David assembled all the princes of Israel,” while the printed words match 1 Chronicles 15:3 (JPS: “And David assembled all Israel at Jerusalem”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the feast
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *BeChag* — it is the Feast of Tabernacles.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the tent of meeting
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Et Ohel Mo’ed* — that Moses made; Solomon stored it in the house of the treasuries of God with the other vessels and the dedicated things, since he had no need of it; and our Rabbis said that it was hidden.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: all the holy vessels that were in the Tent
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’et kol kelei hakodesh asher ba’ohel* — that David gave (another version: pitched) for the Ark.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed abbreviation ס"א is read as “another version.”

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: these did the priests and the Levites bring up
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ha’alu otam hakohanim haLeviyim* — its interpretation refers back to above, where it said, “and the Levites took up the ark,” and it explains who those Levites were of whom I told you above: “the priests the Levites,” for the priests too are of the sons of Levi, and they were not actually Levites. And so it is written in Kings (1 Kings 8), “And the priests took up the ark,” and the vessels and the tent of meeting the Levites also brought up with them, according to their ordinance.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotations are 2 Chronicles 5:4 (JPS: “and the Levites took up the ark”) and 1 Kings 8:3 (JPS: “and the priests took up the ark”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the cherubim spread forth their wings over the place of the ark
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayihyu hakeruvim porsim kenafayim al mekom ha’aron* — in the place where the Ark stands, there; therefore “and the cherubim covered the ark.”

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the staves thereof above
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’al baddav mil’ma’lah* — above the Ark. So the staves stood, and were drawn so far outward toward the east that the Ark could stand exactly under the cherubim without the staves obstructing; therefore “and the cherubim covered the ark,” and they covered the staves too a little near the Ark, but not all of them, for they reached to the east; and you cannot explain that the cherubim covered all the staves. And also because of this “and they drew out the staves,” and the ends of the staves were seen from the Ark before the Sanctuary; for if it were not so, but they were of one measure, they would pull apart from one another. But were not the staves that Moses made still there? And they stood in the Holy of Holies of the tent of meeting, which was only ten, and this one was twenty, and it reached from wall to wall. And as for the cherubim of Moses, of which it is said that they too spread and covered, there is no need for them to move at all from the staves, from their place, for the cherubim of Moses stood above the Ark on the ark-cover, and the cherubim mentioned here, those that Solomon made, stand on their feet on the ground; and nevertheless those of Moses were still attached to the ark-cover. So Rabbi Nathan explained (and my Rabbi explained): the priests wanted to bring the Ark with its staves into the Sanctuary (*devir*) and did not have time, for the cloud filled the house of the LORD, and they could not bring the cherubim up to the western wall itself, and therefore they protruded through the curtain. But it is difficult for me, for it is written, “when the priests were come out,” and only afterwards “the glory of the LORD filled the house of God.” (And Rabbi Joseph of blessed memory explained:) “And they were lengthened” (*vayitarku*) is not said, which would mean that they lengthened themselves, but “and they lengthened” (*vaya’arikhu*), which means that others lengthened them; and he explains that the craftsmen lengthened the staves to twenty, and their two ends touched the eastern wall and their other two ends the western wall. And there is a difficulty: how could the cherubim spread their wings and cover the Ark, which was ten cubits from them?
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The passage is elliptical and several sentences are hard to follow; it is translated as printed. The words “and they drew out the staves” and “the ends of the staves were seen” are 2 Chronicles 5:9 (JPS: “the staves were so long that the ends of the staves were seen from the ark before the Sanctuary”). The persons named (Rabbi Nathan, “my Rabbi,” Rabbi Joseph) are not identified. The parentheses are later printed insertions.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: when the priests were come out of the holy place
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayehi betzet hakohanim min hakodesh* — it should have connected immediately “and the house was filled with a cloud, the house of the LORD,” except that it interrupts in between; and so in Kings (1 Kings 8), “And it came to pass, when the priests were come out of the holy place, that the cloud filled the house of the LORD.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 1 Kings 8:10 (JPS: “when the priests were come out of the holy place, that the cloud filled the house of the LORD”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: all the priests that were present had sanctified themselves
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki khol hakohanim hanimtze’im hitkadashu* — for this matter.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: did not keep their courses
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ein lishmor lemachlakot* — twenty-four of the Levites and twenty-four of the priests; but all who were present sanctified themselves.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: were as one
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayehi ke’echad* — as to the trumpeters, the interpretation: the trumpeters were united together, all of them together; and in what were they united? In this matter: to make one voice heard as one, to praise and to give thanks to the LORD.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: The LORD hath said that He would dwell in the thick darkness
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Az amar Shlomo* — since the house was full of smoke, now I know that the Divine Presence rests in it in the thick darkness (*arafel*), for such is His way, as it is written (Exodus 20:18), “And Moses drew near unto the thick darkness where God was”; certainly it is His will to linger in it. And in the Sifre it is explained: “Then spoke Solomon” — when he saw the cloud, he said, Now I see that the Divine Presence rests in the house that I built, for so He promised to come and dwell in it from within cloud and thick darkness; and where did He say (Leviticus 16:2), “for I appear in the cloud upon the ark-cover”?
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The Exodus quotation is 20:21 (JPS: “Moses drew near unto the thick darkness where God was”); the printed chapter-verse is 20:18. The printed word is “smoke” (*ashan*), though the verse says “cloud.” The Leviticus quotation is 16:2 (JPS: “for I appear in the cloud upon the ark-cover”). I did not verify the Sifre passage.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: a house of habitation
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Beit zevul* — a dwelling.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: for Thee to dwell in for ever
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Leshivtekha olamim* — for since it was chosen, the Divine Presence has not rested in another place, and the high places were not permitted.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: blessed all the congregation of Israel
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayevarekh et kol kehal Yisra’el* — the blessing mentioned at the end of the matter.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: who spoke with His mouth
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Asher diber befiv* — that He would give him a son who would build Him a house.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: fulfilled it
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Mille* — He fulfilled His good word.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Since the day that I brought forth My people out of the land of Egypt
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Min hayom asher hotzeti* — for this too You spoke to my father.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: I have chosen Jerusalem
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Va’evchar biYerushalayim* — it refers back to “I chose no city.”

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: have chosen David to be over My people Israel
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Va’evchar beDavid* — it refers back to “neither chose I any man.”

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: thou didst well that it was in thy heart
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Heitivot ki hayah im levavekha* — that is, I too choose the house that came up in your heart to build, to cause His name to dwell there, as He said above.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: spread forth his hands
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayifrosh kappav* — it should have said thus: “And he spread forth his hands toward heaven and said,” etc.; but it interrupts in between to inform upon what he stood; and so in Kings (1 Kings 8), “And he spread forth his hands toward heaven, and he said.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 1 Kings 8:22 (JPS: “And Solomon stood before the altar of the LORD… and spread forth his hands toward heaven”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Solomon had made a brazen scaffold
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki asah Shlomo* — it refers back to “in the presence of all the congregation of Israel”; that is, how he was higher than all, to make his words heard.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: upon it he stood
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vaya’amod alav* — and now all Israel could see him; and because the matter was interrupted, it needs to say, as at first, “in the presence of all the congregation of Israel,” and likewise “and spread forth his hands toward heaven.”

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: there is no God like Thee
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ein kamokha Elohim* — from the fact that You keep the covenant and the lovingkindness that You decree from heaven to give to those who love You, You keep it hidden and stored away, the covenant and the lovingkindness, to fulfill Your promise on earth.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: that walk before Thee with all their heart
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Hahol’khim lefanekha* — as David my father walked; and this is what You kept for Your servant David, in the sense of a reliable promise.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: But will God in very truth dwell with men on the earth
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki ha’umnam yeshev Elohim et ha’adam al ha’aretz* — an expression of astonishment: can a person believe that God dwells on the earth, since “heaven and the heaven of heavens,” etc.? But because of the kindness You did for David my father, You contracted Your Presence.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: how much less this house which I have builded
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Af ki habayit hazeh asher banitti* — and why did I build it? To pray before God, and that He turn to our prayer.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: to hearken unto the cry
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lishmo’a el harinnah* — this is a shout, like (1 Kings 22) “and the cry (*harinnah*) passed through the host”; and perforce, concerning the cry of any person who flees from his trouble, let him not pray except with his cry in secret. So is the connection of the verses, and the end of the matter proves it, for he said, “and hear Thou from the place of Thy dwelling”; you learn that he built it only with this intention: to bring down the Divine Presence in it, so that He should dwell on earth to hear, from the place of His dwelling, the prayers that will be prayed in it.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The sentence beginning “and perforce” is obscure and is translated as printed. The quotation is 1 Kings 22:36 (JPS: “And there went a cry throughout the host”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: that Thine eyes may be open
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lihyot einekha ptuchot* — at every time that they pray to You.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: If a man sin against his neighbour
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Im yecheta ish* — this verse is about all Israel: one who obliges his fellow to an oath; if he truly makes him swear and the one who swears swears falsely, “You will hear from heaven”; and if the right is with the one who swears, for the claimant obliged him to a vain oath, even the one who made him swear is called wicked.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: justifying the righteous
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ulehatzdik tzaddik* — that he not be punished for the oath, for he swore in truth. And the Tosefta of Sotah explains “If a man sin” as one who has relations with a married woman; “and an oath be exacted of him” — and he shall be bound by an oath; just as the water tests her, so the water tests him; “before Thine altar,” as it is written (Numbers 5:18), “and the priest shall set the woman.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: I did not verify the Tosefta of Sotah passage. The quotation is Numbers 5:18 (JPS: “And the priest shall set the woman before the LORD”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: to bring his way upon his own head
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Latet darko berosho* — as it is written, “and her belly shall swell” (there).
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Numbers 5:27 (JPS: “and her belly shall swell”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: justifying the righteous
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ulehatzdik tzaddik* — for it is written, “then she shall be cleared and shall conceive seed” (there).
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Numbers 5:28 (JPS: “then she shall be cleared, and shall conceive seed”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: if Thy people Israel be smitten down before the enemy
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’im yinnagef amkha* — and not because Your hand is too short to save, but this causes it: “when they sin against Thee.”

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: shall turn again and confess Thy name
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Veshavu vehodu et shemekha* — the interpretation: and they will confess their iniquity; and the last verse proves it: “and confess Thy name and turn from their sin, when Thou dost afflict them.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 2 Chronicles 6:26 (JPS: “confess Thy name, turning from their sin, when Thou dost afflict them”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: bring them back unto the land
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vahashivotam* — and bring them back to the land; for when they fall and are smitten before their enemies, they seize what they can and bring them as captives to another land.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: When the heaven is shut up
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Be’atzer hashamayim* — as it is written, “and He shut up the heaven, so that there shall be no rain” (Deuteronomy 11:17).
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Deuteronomy 11:17 (JPS: “and He shut up the heaven, so that there shall be no rain”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Thou dost direct them on the good way
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki torem el haderekh* — as You did when there was a famine in the days of David for three years (2 Samuel 21:1), and You instructed and said to them, “for Saul and for his bloody house”; likewise “You direct them”: which sin causes it for them, for what the heavens were shut.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 2 Samuel 21:1 (JPS: “It is for Saul, and for his bloody house”); the printed wording differs slightly.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: whatsoever plague or whatsoever sickness there be
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Kol nega* — the interpretation: behold, I have mentioned to you blasting, mildew and pestilence, and also the shutting of rain; and what more is there to multiply? Rather, “whatsoever plague and whatsoever sickness there be,” and he prays.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: spread forth his hands toward this house
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ufarash kappav el habayit hazeh* — and this is what he said: “what prayer and supplication soever” that he prays and supplicates concerning any one of these things.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: who shall know every man his own plague
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Asher yed’u ish nigo* — that is, if he prays about his plague and his pain, to remove it from him.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: forgive, and render unto every man according to all his ways
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vesalachta unatatta le’ish kekhol derakhav* etc. — to the wicked according to his wickedness and to the righteous according to his righteousness; for if He does not repay the wicked according to the evil of his deeds, he will speak insolently toward heaven and say, “there is no God (then) who knows his heart,” and it will be a profanation of the Name; likewise You will do to the righteous according to his righteousness, what You will do for him when he prays before You.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The word “(then)” is a printed insertion.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: that they may fear Thee
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lema’an yir’ukha* — and the wicked will turn from his way; therefore I pray to give to each man according to his ways.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: all that the stranger calleth to Thee for
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’asita kekhol asher yikra eilekha hanokhri* — for Israel I pray to give each according to his ways, but for the idolater, “according to all that he calls to You,” because Israel recognizes the Holy One, blessed be He, and knows that the power to do is in His hand; if his prayer is not heard, he attributes it to himself, to his sins, and examines his deeds; but the idolater lodges a protest and says: I heard — they heard throughout the world — and I wearied myself on many roads until I came and prayed in this place, and I found nothing real in it, like other deities. Therefore, “and do according to all that the stranger calls to You.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed abbreviation עו"ג is read as “idolater.”

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: toward this city which Thou hast chosen
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Derekh ha’ir* — with their faces toward Jerusalem.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: maintain their cause
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’asita mishpatam* — their vengeance on their enemies; *a"a*: their needs; an example: “to maintain the cause of His servant” (1 Kings 8).
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 1 Kings 8:59 (JPS: “that He maintain the cause of His servant”). The abbreviation ע"א is left as printed because I could not confirm its meaning.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: which I have built for Thy name
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Asher banitti leshemekha* — the interpretation: this house that I built in order to magnify Your name; for then, when You accept their prayer, they will pray to You in this house, or in any place where they are, and they will turn toward this house of Yours.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: hear Thou from heaven
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Veshama’ta* — their prayer; and through this Your name will be magnified in the world.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: arise, O LORD God
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’attah kumah HaShem* — that it not be moved about as until now, from Shiloh to Nob and from Nob to Gibeon.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Thou, and the ark of Thy strength
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Attah va’aron uzzekha* — that it not be moved about any more from now on.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the ark of Thy strength
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uzzekha* — for this reason it is called “Thy strength,” because it did His wonders and mighty acts against the Philistines; and so it is written (above, 16), “When he gave thanks to the LORD… Seek the LORD and His strength.” And furthermore our Rabbis said in tractate Avodah Zarah: “and the kine went straight” (*vayisharnah*, 1 Samuel 6:12) — what song (*shirah*) did they say? “His right hand, and His holy arm, hath wrought salvation for Him” (Psalms 98:1).
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotations are 1 Chronicles 16:8 and 16:11 (JPS: “Seek you the LORD and His strength”), 1 Samuel 6:12 (JPS: “And the kine took the straight way”) and Psalm 98:1 (JPS: “His right hand, and His holy arm, hath wrought salvation for Him”). I did not verify the Avodah Zarah passage.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: be clothed with salvation
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Yilbeshu teshu’ah* — because they will not be moved about from place to place, like “and righteousness shall be the girdle of his loins” (Isaiah 11:5).
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Isaiah 11:5 (JPS: “And righteousness shall be the girdle of his loins”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: let Thy saints rejoice in good
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vachasidekha yismechu vatov* — with the abundance of goods and tithes given to the Levites as the reward for guarding the Ark and singing before it.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: turn not away the face of Thine anointed
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Al tashev penei meshichekha* — from doing good with me; and if not for my sake, do it for Your sake.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the priests stood, according to their offices
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *VeHakohanim al mishmerotam* — as David divided them into twenty-four watches to serve, each and every watch having its week; and the Levites likewise by their twenty-four watches.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: to give thanks unto the LORD
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lehodot* — with the instruments of song, who said, “Give thanks to the LORD, for He is good, for His mercy endureth for ever.”

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: with the praises of David by their hand
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Behillel David* — the instruments of song with which they said the Hallel of David, and the thanksgivings were in the hand of the Levites.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the priests sounded trumpets
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *VeHakohanim* — sounded trumpets opposite them, for it is upon them to sound the trumpets, as it is said, “And the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall blow with the trumpets,” etc. (Numbers 10).
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Numbers 10:8 (JPS: “And the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall blow with the trumpets”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Solomon hallowed the middle of the court
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayekadesh Shlomo et tokh hechatzer* — our Rabbis disagree about this (Zevachim 59): Rabbi Judah says that he sanctified the pavement of the Courtyard with the sanctity of the altar, to offer upon the pavement, because the copper altar was too small to contain, for the offerings to be brought were many. Rabbi Yose said to him: Was it not already said (above, 2, 8), “A thousand burnt-offerings Solomon offered upon the altar that Moses made”? And when you come to the computation of the cubits and the number of the burnt-offerings, you will find that this one of stones is larger than that of Moses: for the place of arrangement of Moses’ altar was a cubit by a cubit, and Solomon’s place of arrangement twenty-four by twenty-four, so Solomon’s is five hundred and seventy-six times Moses’. If so, what is “the king hallowed the middle of the court”? That he set in it an altar of stones joined to the pavement.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed reference (2, 8) is left unresolved; the words are close to 2 Chronicles 1:6 (JPS: “he offered a thousand burnt-offerings upon it”). Twenty-four times twenty-four is 576. I did not verify the Zevachim passage.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: was not able to receive
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lo yakhol lehakhil* — it speaks of that of Moses, like a person who says: so-and-so is a dwarf and unfit for the service.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The comparison is translated as printed and its sense is not clear to me.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: from the entrance of Hamath
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Milevo Chamat* — which is in the north of the Land of Israel.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: unto the Brook of Egypt
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ad Nachal Mitzrayim* — which is opposite it, as explained in *Eleh Masei*.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The reference is Numbers 34:5 (JPS: “the Brook of Egypt”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: on the three and twentieth day of the seventh month he sent the people away
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *UVeyom esrim ushloshah lachodesh hashevi’i shilach et ha’am* — which is the ninth of the dedication of the House; and in Kings (1 Kings 8) it is written “on the eighth day,” which is the twenty-second of the month. The interpretation: on the eighth day he gave them permission to go after the festival, and on the morrow, when the festival was over, they all went together. *A"a*: on the eighth day he gave them permission and sent away those who dwell within the Sabbath limit, and anyone who wished to travel and go that day within that limit; and on the morrow he sent away all the people entirely. And in Bereshit Rabbah it is explained: they took leave from him and waited there one more day, and again took leave on the morrow a second time; therefore it is said “on the twenty-third day of the month.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The Kings quotation is 1 Kings 8:66 (JPS: “On the eighth day he sent the people away”). I did not verify the Bereshit Rabbah passage. The abbreviation ע"א is left as printed because I could not confirm its meaning. The printed abbreviation ב"ר is read as Bereshit Rabbah.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: joyful and glad of heart
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Smechim vetovei lev* etc. — to David and to Solomon: for what He spoke with His mouth (above, 28), “Thy son Solomon, he shall build My house,” He fulfilled by His hand, in giving him a son sitting on his throne who built the House for the name of the LORD. And in Bereshit Rabbah it is explained: Rabbi Levi said, it is written, “for the dedication,” etc.; “joyful” refers back to what the LORD said to David, that He fulfilled what He vowed to Solomon, for He chose him from among all his brothers, for he is wise.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The last sentence is compressed and is translated as printed. The quotations are 1 Chronicles 28:6 (JPS: “Solomon thy son, he shall build My house and My courts”) and 2 Chronicles 7:9 (JPS: “for they kept the dedication of the altar seven days”). I did not verify the Bereshit Rabbah passage. The printed abbreviation ב"ר is read as Bereshit Rabbah.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Israel His people
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ule-Yisra’el ammo* — as it is written in Kings (1 Kings 8), “there hath not failed one word,” etc. *A"a*: “and to Israel His people” — that they had a ruler, so that they dwelt in security and quiet, as it is written, “And Judah and Israel dwelt safely,” etc. (there, 5).
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotations are 1 Kings 8:56 (JPS: “there hath not failed one word of all His good promise”) and 1 Kings 5:5 (JPS: “And Judah and Israel dwelt safely”). The abbreviation ע"א is left as printed because I could not confirm its meaning.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the LORD appeared to Solomon by night
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayera HaShem el Shlomo balaylah* — in a night vision.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: I have heard thy prayer
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Shama’ti et tefillatekha* — in the very language in which Solomon said “and hear,” the Holy One, blessed be He, answered, “I have heard thy prayer.” He prayed concerning the shutting of the heaven; the Holy One, blessed be He, answered, “Behold, I shall shut up.” He prayed concerning famine and locust, and the Holy One, blessed be He, answers him, “and if I command the locust.” He prayed concerning pestilence, and the Holy One, blessed be He, answers him, “and if I send pestilence among My people.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The answering words are from 2 Chronicles 7:13 (JPS: “If I shut up heaven that there be no rain, or if I command the locust to devour the land, or if I send pestilence among My people”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: have chosen this place to Myself for a house of sacrifice
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Veyikanu ami* — through what they will pray and seek My face and turn from their evil ways; behold, three against three.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The source lemma belongs to a later verse (2 Chronicles 7:14) and does not occur in this verse; the lemma shown is a nearby phrase of the verse it is filed under.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: If I shut up heaven that there be no rain
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Hen e’etzor* — and “if I command,” and “if I send,” against the three prayers; “and I will hear, and forgive their sin, and heal their land.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The closing words are from 2 Chronicles 7:14.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Mine eyes and My heart shall be there perpetually
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vehayu einai velibbi* — Jonathan translated: “and My Divine Presence shall dwell in it, ’im My will is done there all the days”; “and Mine eyes shall be there” — ’im My heart and My desire are there.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed Aramaic and the word אם (’im) are left as printed and I could not resolve their sense. The Aramaic phrase is translated as printed.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: will I cast out of My sight
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ashlikh me’al panai* — like the condition between Me and you: “and if you will not hearken unto Me” (Leviticus 26), what is said? “And I will bring your sanctuaries unto desolation.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotations are Leviticus 26:14 (JPS: “But if you will not hearken unto Me”) and 26:31 (JPS: “and will bring your sanctuaries unto desolation”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: a proverb and a byword
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’etnenu lemashal uleshinnah* — in the sense that they use a proverb about one to whom something has befallen.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: a byword
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uleshinnah* — like “and thou shalt teach them diligently (*veshinnantam*) unto thy children” (Deuteronomy 6:7), and *vetitninun* — a term for recounting evils; and so the Targum of “and he told” is *ve’ishtta’i* and *leshu’ei*.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Deuteronomy 6:7.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: every one that passeth by it shall be astonished
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lekhol over alav yashom* — that is, the House will be destroyed, and then everyone who passes by it will be astonished, like “They that come after shall be astonished at his day” (Job 18).
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Job 18:20 (JPS: “They that come after shall be astonished at his day”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Why hath the LORD done thus
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Bammeh asah HaShem* — like “for what” (*al meh*) did the LORD do (Deuteronomy 29), and so it is written (in Kings I, 9).
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotations are Deuteronomy 29:23 (JPS: “Wherefore hath the LORD done thus unto this land?”) and 1 Kings 9:8 (JPS: “Why hath the LORD done thus unto this land, and to this house?”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: at the end of twenty years
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayehi mikketz esrim shanah* — the interpretation: at the end of twenty years in which the whole building of the house of the LORD was completed, seven years, and his own house, thirteen years, as it is written in Kings (there, 6).
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The figures are 1 Kings 6:38 (“seven years in building it”) and 7:1 (“thirteen years”); seven and thirteen make twenty.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: he built Tadmor in the wilderness
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayiven et Tadmor bamidbar* — (and in Kings, 1 Kings 9:18) it is written *Tamor*, and we read *Tadmor*; and this is what we learned in Yevamot: “We do not accept converts from the Tadmorites.” And in Bereshit Rabbah, in the section of the Binding, it is explained that they helped the enemies of Israel; and because they changed themselves and turned to evil in the end, therefore in Kings *Tamor* is written, a term of *temurah* (exchange). They ought to have done kindness to Israel; Solomon did kindness with them in building them the city of Tadmor; and for Solomon’s sake *Tamor* is not written here but *Tadmor*, that is, an important city. All is for the honor of Solomon, for it is not to Solomon’s honor to say here: behold, he built a city that rebelled against him and corrupted him; and therefore he wrote *Tadmor* and not *Tamor*.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: JPS shows “Tadmor” in 1 Kings 9:18 and does not show the difference between the written and the read form. I did not verify the Yevamot or Bereshit Rabbah passages. The printed abbreviation ב"ר is read as Bereshit Rabbah.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: fortified cities
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Arei matzor* — because they stood on the border, they needed so much strengthening.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: for his work
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lemelakhto* — for the work of his building; why? Because the strangers were for his work and not the men of Israel, since Israel were men of valor and men of war, and captains of his chariots and horsemen.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: two hundred and fifty
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Chamishim umatayim* — and in Kings (1 Kings 9) “five hundred and fifty”; but this and that are one, for there it lacks three hundred, and it taught and counted them again; for there it is written above, “besides Solomon’s chief officers… three thousand and three hundred, who bore rule,” and here it is written above three thousand and six hundred; so what is lacking in one verse he added in the other verse, and he divides them because the three extra hundred were strangers, and were appointed over those three thousand three hundred who ruled over the seventy thousand bearers of burdens and the eighty thousand hewers in the mountain; and these two hundred and fifty mentioned here were Israelites appointed over those three hundred strangers.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The Kings figures are 1 Kings 9:23 (“five hundred and fifty”) and 5:30 (“three thousand and three hundred”); the other figure is 2 Chronicles 2:17 (“three thousand and six hundred”). Arithmetic: 250 + 300 = 550 and 3,300 + 300 = 3,600.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Solomon brought up the daughter of Pharaoh out of the city of David
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *He’elah Shlomo me’ir David* — it is Zion, where he had settled her in the City of David when he took her, and she was there until he finished building his house.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the places are holy
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki kodesh hemah* — the whole city and all the houses.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: whereunto the ark of the LORD hath come
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Asher ba’ah aleihem* — because the Ark of the LORD came to them, “came” (*ba’ah*) is in the feminine; a parallel (1 Samuel 4:3): “and the ark of the covenant of the LORD was taken” (*nilkachah*).
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed quotation does not appear word for word in 1 Samuel 4:3 (JPS: “Let us fetch the ark of the covenant of the LORD out of Shiloh”); 4:11 reads “And the ark of God was taken.” I could not match it.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the altar of the LORD
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Al mizbach HaShem* — this is the copper altar that Solomon built; and some explain: the copper altar that Solomon made in place of the copper altar that Moses built; and it is astonishing, for it is written (2 Kings 17), “and the burnt-offering of all the people, and all the blood of the burnt-offering,” etc.; “shall be for me to inquire by” — that is, the copper altar that was there before shall be for me to inquire by; it follows that the altar was of copper.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 2 Kings 16:15 (JPS: “but the brazen altar shall be for me to look to”); the printed reference (17) is wrong.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: from the day of the foundation of the house of the LORD
