2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ad hayom musad bayit* — from the day it was founded until it was finished.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: to prove Solomon
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lenasot et Shlomo* — whether what she had heard of his wisdom was true, and she came to test him.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: hard questions
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Bechidot* — like “Let me now put forth a riddle (*chidah*) unto you,” of Samson (Judges 14:12).
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Judges 14:12 (JPS: “Let me now put forth a riddle unto you”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: there was not any thing hid from Solomon
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Velo ne’lam davar* — when she saw that he told her everything, that nothing was hidden of what she asked, then she acknowledged the report, that she had heard the truth; and in the Targum of the Scroll of Esther some of the riddles that she asked him are written.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: I did not verify the Targum of Esther passage.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the food of his table
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uma’akhal shulchano* — *barburim* and kinds of delicacies that came up on his table in abundance.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The word *barburim* (a kind of fowl) is left transliterated.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the sitting of his servants
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Umoshav avadav* — for each and every one knew his place when they sat at the table, and those who saw the king’s face continually; no one was permitted to sit in his fellow’s place all the days of his life.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the attendance of his ministers
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uma’amad meshartav* — each and every one held to his post and his service, and did not change on the morrow.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: their apparel
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Umalbushehem* — not as their clothing which they wear today do they put on tomorrow.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: his cupbearers
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Umashkav* — the multitude of his cupbearers.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: his ascent by which he went up into the house of the LORD
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’aliyyato* — the stairways of his ascents by which he went up from his house to the house of the LORD.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: there was no more spirit in her
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Velo hayah od bah ruach* — for she had thought that there was no wisdom in all the kingdoms save in her land, and likewise her sages, for her land is in the east, and therefore they are exceedingly wise, because they observe the constellations, as stated in the first chapter of Rosh Hashanah: “for us the moon is hidden eighteen hours,” for the Land of Israel is west of Babylon. And this is what is written, “And Solomon’s wisdom excelled the wisdom of all the children of the east” (they who were in the east, as it is written, “And it came to pass, as they journeyed east,” Genesis 11), “and all the wisdom of Egypt,” for they were sorcerers, magicians and enchanters; and “wise was he in *tayyar*” — so it is written in the Pesikta; *tayyar* is an Arabic term; and in Vayikra Rabbah, in the section of “the son of the Egyptian”: “for a bird of the air shall carry the voice” (Ecclesiastes) — this is a raven, and the wisdom of *tuyari*.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The Aramaic sentence about the moon and the phrase “wise in *tayyar*” are translated as printed and their sense is not clear to me. The quotation “And it came to pass, as they journeyed east” is Genesis 11:2 (JPS), and “a bird of the air shall carry the voice” is Ecclesiastes 10:20 (JPS). The citation of the first chapter of Rosh Hashanah and of the Pesikta and Vayikra Rabbah is not verified. The wording of the first quotation (“the children of the east… all the wisdom of Egypt”) is from 1 Kings 5:10, not looked up. The Aramaic phrase is translated as printed.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the half of the greatness of thy wisdom
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Chetzi merbit* — a multitude of wisdoms.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: sandal-wood
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Atzei algumim* — it is explained in the Pesikta: one verse says *almugim* and another verse says *algumim*; but *algumim* is their name, and it is called *almugim* because it melts (*mitmogeg*) and bends from its softness, like *kosot*, which bends because of its value.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The comparison with *kosot* is translated as printed and its sense is not clear to me. The Pesikta citation is not verified.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: paths for the house of the LORD
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Mesillot* — steps; and in Kings I (10) it is written *mis’ad*, in the manner of what is made for those who go up on the way, ascents and steps; and some say *mis’ad* and *mesillah* are one and the same.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The Kings passage is 1 Kings 10:12, where JPS reads “pillars.”

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: harps and psalteries for the singers
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vechinnorot unvalim lasharim* — some say for the sons of Levi, the singers with instruments of song; but Rabbi Eliezer, of blessed memory, explained: “for the singers” — for the *singers* who stroll before the king. An example (there, 4): “And his songs were five and a thousand” (1 Kings 5:12) — these are secular songs that he made for singers to sing before him, to stroll; and this is what is written (below, 35), “And Jeremiah lamented for Josiah, and all the singing men and singing women spoke,” etc.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 1 Kings 5:12 (JPS: “his songs were a thousand and five”; the printed Hebrew reads “five and a thousand”) and 2 Chronicles 35:25 (JPS: “all the singing men and singing women spoke of Josiah in their lamentations”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: beside that which she had brought unto the king
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Milvad asher hevi’ah* — for the honor of the kings of Judah it is written so here, for this implies that she gave him more than he gave her; but in Kings (there, 10) it is written “beside that which Solomon gave her of his royal bounty” — things that are found in the Land of Israel and are not found in her place.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The Kings verse is 1 Kings 10:13 (JPS: “beside that which Solomon gave her of his royal bounty”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: beside that which the traffickers and merchants brought
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Levad me’anshei hatarim* — who were anxious to pass from country to country and from kingdom to kingdom without a *tayyar* (guide), and they gave him the payment of a *tayyar*.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The word *tayyar* is left as printed.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: and merchants brought
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vehassochrim mevi’im* — who brought him through a pretext, in order to see his wisdom.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: two hundred targets
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Matayim tzinnah* — a *tzinnah* surrounds a person on three sides; this is what is written (Psalms 5), “as with a shield wilt Thou encompass him with favor.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Psalm 5:13 (JPS: “Thou dost encompass him with favour as with a shield”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: beaten gold
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Zahav shachut* — gold soft and easy to hammer because of its great value, that it could be spun like a thread.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: six hundred shekels of beaten gold went to one target
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Shesh me’ot* — six hundred *zehuvim*, which is six *manim*, for the *zahuv* is the dinar.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The equation of six *manim* with six hundred assumes a *maneh* of one hundred dinars; the text does not state it and I did not verify it.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: in the house of the forest of Lebanon
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ya’ar haLevanon* — a great house that Solomon built in Jerusalem, as is proved below; and all those shields Shishak took; and from the abundance of the great cedars of Lebanon he made it, as it is written in Kings (I, 7), “For he built the house of the forest of Lebanon… upon four rows of cedar pillars”; and there he put them, the shields; and this is what is written (Isaiah 22), “And thou didst look in that day to the armour in the house of the forest.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotations are 1 Kings 7:2 (JPS: “For he built the house of the forest of Lebanon… upon four rows of cedar pillars”) and Isaiah 22:8 (JPS: “thou didst look in that day to the armour in the house of the forest”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: a great throne of ivory
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Kisse shen* — the tooth of an elephant.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: there were six steps to the throne
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Veshesh ma’alot lakisse* — steps for going up to it.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: arms on either side by the place of the seat
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Veyadot mizeh umizeh al makom hashevet* — like sticks from side to side, on the right and on the left, to lean his arms upon them.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: twelve lions stood there on the one side and on the other
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ushneim arayot omdim etzel hayadot* — of gold; and the whole form of the throne and the form of the animals on the throne is explained in the Targum of the Scroll of Esther.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: I did not verify the Targum passage.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: ivory
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Shenhabbim* — the tooth of an elephant, and the elephant itself.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: apes
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vekofim* — *mea"r katz"an*.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed gloss מע"ר קאצ"ן is left as printed; I could not identify it.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: peacocks
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vetukkiyyim* — peacocks.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: So king Solomon exceeded all the kings of the earth in riches and wisdom
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayigdal hamelekh Shlomo vegomer* — to fulfill what He said to him, “And I have also given thee that which thou hast not asked, both riches and honour” (1 Kings 3).
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 1 Kings 3:13 (JPS: “And I have also given thee that which thou hast not asked, both riches and honour”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: And all the kings of the earth sought the presence of Solomon
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vechol malkhei ha’aretz vegomer* — to fulfill what He said to him, “Behold, I have given thee a wise and an understanding heart; so that there hath been none like thee” (there).
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 1 Kings 3:12 (JPS: “I have given thee a wise and an understanding heart; so that there hath been none like thee before thee”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: they brought every man his present
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vehem mevi’im ish minchato* — through a pretext, that they came to hear his wisdom, for it is no honor to come before the king empty-handed, like “and they shall not appear before the LORD empty” (Deuteronomy 16).
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Deuteronomy 16:16 (JPS: “and they shall not appear before the LORD empty”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: armour
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Neshek* — implements of war.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: that he bestowed in the chariot cities, and with the king at Jerusalem
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayaniychem be’arei harekhev ve’im hamelekh biYrushalayim* — some of them; and he transgressed “he shall not multiply horses to himself.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Deuteronomy 17:16 (JPS: “Only he shall not multiply horses to himself”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the words of Nathan the prophet
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Al divrei Natan* — “And it came to pass the same night, that the word of the LORD came unto Nathan,” etc., until “and he called his name Jedidiah.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The passage runs from 2 Samuel 7:4 (JPS: “And it came to pass the same night, that the word of the LORD came unto Nathan”) to 2 Samuel 12:25 (JPS: “and he called his name Jedidiah”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’al nevu’at Achiyyah haShiloni* — in which he tore the kingdom from him and gave it to Jeroboam.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The reference is 1 Kings 11:29–31.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: over all Israel forty years
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Al kol Yisra’el arba’im shanah* — which is not so with David, who reigned in Hebron seven years and in Jerusalem thirty-three.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: JPS (2 Samuel 5:5) reads “seven years and six months” in Hebron; the printed text says seven years.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: for all Israel were come to Shechem to make him king
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki Shechem ba’u kol Yisra’el lehamlikh oto* — in Shechem, the place of Jeroboam in the portion of Ephraim, for Jeroboam was an Ephraimite; and all this was a cause from the Holy One, blessed be He, to fulfill His word, “I will surely rend the kingdom.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 1 Kings 11:11 (JPS: “I will surely rend the kingdom from thee”), and 1 Kings 11:26 calls Jeroboam an Ephraimite.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: when Jeroboam the son of Nebat heard of it
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayehi kishmo’a* — the interpretation: *vayehi kishmo’a* is from before, when they came to make him king in Shechem while he was still in Egypt.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: And they sent and called him
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayishlechu vayikre’u lo vayavo* — and all this is to make known to us the will of the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, that even Jeroboam himself came to make Rehoboam king; and the Holy One, blessed be He, turned events after His words until Jeroboam reigned.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Thy father made our yoke grievous
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Avikha hiksha et ullenu* — for he was a man who toiled at work, and he laid upon us the burden of supporting his workers, and the tax, as it is written in Kings (I, 5), “And king Solomon raised a levy,” etc.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 1 Kings 5:27 (JPS: “And king Solomon raised a levy out of all Israel”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: took counsel with the old men
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *No’atzim* — like *yo’atzim*; and so Scripture says from *yode’im*, *nodaim*; but *yo’atzim* is for the future and *no’atzim* is those who already took counsel.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The grammatical comment is translated as printed.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: My little finger is thicker than my father’s loins
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Kotni avah mimmotnei avi* — my little finger is bigger than the loins of my father, that is, I am stronger than he.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: did lade you
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *He’emis* — like (Genesis 43) “and laded every man his ass.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Genesis 44:13 (JPS: “and laded every man his ass”); the printed chapter number 43 is wrong.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: I will chastise you with scorpions
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ba’akravvim* — *berim"n* in the German language, which sting like scorpions.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed word ברימ"ן is left as printed. The printed abbreviation בל"א is read as “in German”; I could not confirm this, and the glossed word is left as printed.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: for it was brought about of God
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki hayetah nessibbah* — in order that the LORD establish His word, as is explained (1 Kings 11), to remove from him ten tribes and give them to Jeroboam; and this is “The sceptre shall not depart from Judah” (Genesis 49), “nor the ruler’s staff from between his feet, as long as men come to Shiloh” — the interpretation: until Judah comes to Shiloh to make Rehoboam king there, “and unto him shall the obedience of the peoples be” — and there the kingdom was divided and the kingdom of the ten tribes was lost. And Shechem is a small city near Shiloh, as it is written (end of Judges), “Behold, there is the feast of the LORD from year to year in Shiloh, which is on the north of Beth-el, on the east side of the highway that goeth up from Beth-el to Shechem”; and it is written in Jeremiah, “from Shechem, from Shiloh.” And in honor of the Tabernacle of Shiloh they gather at Shechem, which is fit for the gathering of people and is near Shiloh; and when they gather at Shechem, then the sceptre departs from Judah, for there the kingdom was divided.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotations are 1 Kings 11:31 (the ten tribes), Genesis 49:10, Judges 21:19 and Jeremiah 41:5 (JPS: “from Shechem, from Shiloh, and from Samaria”). The printed form “until Shiloh come” is read as Rashi’s own interpretation and is translated as printed.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: every man to your tents, O Israel
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Le’ohalekha Yisra’el* — it refers back to “What portion have we in David?” — why should we leave our tents and go after him? Not so; rather, “Go, all Israel, every man to his tent.”

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: now see to thine own house, David
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Attah re’eh veitkha David* — it refers back to “neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse”; that is, we have no inheritance in him except in the Temple in Jerusalem, where we sacrifice and appear on the three festivals.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: see to thine own house
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Re’eh veitkha David* — we have no need of him that we should go there; it shall be for you alone (and all this does not seem right to me); rather, “see to thine own house, David” — it is not possible for us, neither with you nor with your Temple.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The last clause is difficult and is translated as I read it; Rashi himself says the first explanation “does not seem right to me.”

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Hadoram, who was over the levy
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Hadoram* — this is Adoniram (1 Kings 4), whose greatness was great in the days of Solomon, and in the days of Rehoboam his greatness was lowered; therefore he was called Hadoram.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The reference is 1 Kings 4:6 (JPS: “Adoniram the son of Abda was over the levy”); 1 Kings 12:18 calls him Adoram.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: stoned him with stones
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayirgemu bo Bnei Yisra’el even* — and because Rehoboam did not know the cause and the plot that was turned against him, therefore he was slain when he asked for the tax that Solomon had fixed on them.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Israel rebelled against the house of David
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayifshe’u Yisra’el beveit David* — a term of rebellion; an example (Kings II) “In his days Moab rebelled,” etc.; (Proverbs 18) “A brother offended (*nifsha*) is harder to be won than a strong city”; “then did Libnah revolt” (below, 31).
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed “In his days Moab rebelled” does not appear in JPS in that form; 2 Kings 1:1 reads “And Moab rebelled against Israel after the death of Ahab” and 2 Kings 8:20 reads “In his days Edom revolted.” The Proverbs quotation is Proverbs 18:19 (JPS: “A brother offended is harder to be won than a strong city”) and the Libnah verse is 2 Chronicles 21:10 (JPS: “then did Libnah revolt”); the printed number 31 is wrong. Located in the Hebrew Tanakh: בימיו פשע אדום is II Kings 8:20 (also II Chronicles 21:8), so the printed “Moab” does not match those verses; אח נפשע מקרית עז is Proverbs 18:19 (printed “11”, and the verse reads אח); אז תפשע לבנה is II Chronicles 21:10 (printed “31”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: he assembled the house of Judah and Benjamin
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayakhel et beit Yehudah uVinyamin* — who were in one territory together, and Jerusalem too was of both, and the Temple is built on the border of both; and in the borders in Joshua it is explained how their territory was together. And our Rabbis also said: a strip goes out from Benjamin’s portion and enters Judah’s portion, and an altar is built upon it; therefore they could not be separated from one another; and it is also written nearby.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: I did not verify the statement of the Rabbis.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: against your brethren
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Im achekhem* — but are not your brethren the sons of one man?

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: built cities for defence in Judah
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayiven arim lemator* — he built small cities and surrounded them on every side with water, for strength, and this is *matzor*, as we say (Isaiah 37): “I have digged and drunk water, and with the sole of my feet have I dried up all the rivers of *matzor*”; and now he needed this because Israel had rebelled against him.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Isaiah 37:25 (JPS: “And with the sole of my feet have I dried up All the rivers of Egypt”); JPS reads *matzor* there as Egypt, while Rashi reads it as a moat or siege-work.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: put captains in them
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayiten bahem negidim* — officers and overseers to guard the cities and the fortresses.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: store of victual, and oil and wine
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’otzerot ma’akhal veshemen vayayin* — so that there would be prepared food for them if the house of Israel should come up to besiege.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: left their open land and their possession
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki azvu haLevi’im et migreshehem* — which were in all the land of the ten tribes.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: cast them off
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki hiznichum Yarov’am* — he cast them off from serving and from officiating for the LORD.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: and he appointed him priests for the high places
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Kohanim labamot* — that is, why Jeroboam cast off the priests and the Levites: because he appointed *komarim* priests for the satyrs.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The word *komarim* (idolatrous priests) is left transliterated.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: And after them
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’acharehem* — of the Levites and the priests.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Abihail the daughter of Eliab the son of Jesse
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Avichayil bat Eli’av* — like “and Abihail”: before Samuel, and he said, “Surely the LORD’s anointed is before Him” — this one of whom the Holy One, blessed be He, was destined to say, “Arise, anoint him, for this is he”; and Samuel erred about him, for he saw the daughter of Eliab, the wife of Rehoboam, a queen. And for this matter Samuel was punished, for when Saul asked him, “Which is the seer’s house?” (1 Samuel 9), Samuel said, “I am the seer” — he did not answer him in the way of humility, saying, “What do you wish?” The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: By your life, you are destined to see and not know what you see, for he erred about Eliab and his daughter the queen.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The first clause (“like ‘and Abihail’: before Samuel”) is translated as printed and its sense is not clear to me. The quotation “Surely the LORD’s anointed is before Him” is 1 Samuel 16:6 (JPS: “Surely the LORD’S anointed is before Him”); the printed reference 17:31 is wrong. “Arise, anoint him” is 1 Samuel 16:12, and the exchange with Saul is 1 Samuel 9:18–19 (JPS: “Tell me, I pray thee, where the seer’s house is… I am the seer”). The Rabbinic story of Samuel’s punishment is not verified.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: to be chief, even the prince among his brethren
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lenagid be’achiv* — in order to make him king.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: dispersed of all his sons throughout all the lands of Judah and Benjamin
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayifrotz* — he scattered his sons to all the lands of Judah; an example (above 1, 4), “and their fathers’ houses increased (*paretzu*) greatly.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The reference is 1 Chronicles 4:38 (JPS: “their fathers’ houses increased greatly”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: They have humbled themselves; I will not destroy them
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Nichn’u lo ashchitem* — an example below (14): “the land is yet before us, because we have sought the LORD our God; we have sought…”; so is the way of the verse, when it interrupts in the middle it doubles again the matter in order to say it; an example (Numbers 10): “And it shall be, if thou go with us, yea, it shall be that what good,” etc.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The first quotation is 2 Chronicles 14:6 (JPS: “the land is yet before us, because we have sought the LORD our God; we have sought Him”). The second is Numbers 10:32 (JPS: “And it shall be, if thou go with us, yea, it shall be, that what good soever the LORD shall do unto us”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: they shall be his servants
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki yihyu lo la’avadim* — to Shishak and to the other idolaters, as is explained.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed abbreviation עובדי כוכבים is read as “idolaters.”

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: that they may know My service, and the service of the kingdoms of the countries
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Veyed’u avodati* — when they return, no ruler of the idolatrous kings will be over them; but when you turn away from after My Torah, you will know the service of the kings of the lands, and you will serve them.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: committed them to the hands of the captains of the guard
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vehifkid al yad sarei haratzim* — he took the shields from the house of the forest of Lebanon and committed them to the captains of the guard, and afterward returned them to the guard-chamber, the chamber of the guard, that is, to their place. Another explanation, from my teacher: because he feared the king of Egypt and the king of Israel, they carried them before him.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The guard-chamber is mentioned in 2 Chronicles 12:11 (JPS: “brought them back into the guard-chamber”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the anger of the LORD turned from him
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uvehikkana shav mimmenu charon af HaShem* — he should have said it above, immediately when it says “And Shishak went up,” etc.; but he interrupted in between for the need of “and made in their stead shields of brass.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed quotation “And Shishak went up” is 2 Chronicles 12:2 (“Shishak king of Egypt came up”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: So king Rehoboam strengthened himself in Jerusalem
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayitchazzek hamelekh Rechav’am* — and it explains why: for when he was first made king he was forty-one, so he had strength and power to strengthen himself, for he was one year old when David died; for Solomon reigned forty years, and Solomon had not yet reigned when Rehoboam was born; it turns out that Rehoboam was forty-one when he reigned.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The figures agree with 1 Kings 11:42 (Solomon reigned forty years) and 1 Kings 14:21 (Rehoboam was forty-one when he began to reign). Arithmetic: one year at David’s death plus Solomon’s forty makes forty-one.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the city which the LORD had chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, to put His name there
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ha’ir asher bachar HaShem lasum et shemo sham mikkol shivtei Yisra’el* — but they were corrupted by their deeds, as it is written, “And he did that which was evil, because he set not his heart,” and they caused the Divine Presence to withdraw from them; and it is as though He complains and is grieved over this.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The last clause is translated as I read it; one printed word (ומפיגין) is difficult. The quotation is 2 Chronicles 12:14 (JPS: “And he did that which was evil, because he set not his heart to seek the LORD”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: histories of Shemaiah the prophet and of Iddo the seer
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Bediverei Shema’yah hanavi* — each and every prophet wrote his book, what he prophesied; and this is Shemaiah, who is mentioned above (2, 11) and who is shown below (12) to rebuke; and “the rest of the acts of Abijah, and his ways, and his sayings, are written in the commentary of the prophet Iddo” — his book was called *midrash*.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The references are 2 Chronicles 11:2, 12:5 and 13:22 (JPS: “written in the commentary of the prophet Iddo”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Three years reigned he in Jerusalem
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Shalosh shanim malakh biYrushalayim* — and not more, as is proved in Kings: “And in the twentieth year of Jeroboam king of Israel Asa king of Judah reigned”; it turns out that he did not reign even three full years.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 1 Kings 15:9 (JPS: “And in the twentieth year of Jeroboam king of Israel began Asa to reign over Judah”); 1 Kings 15:1 places Abijam’s accession in the eighteenth year of Jeroboam.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Micaiah the daughter of Uriel of Gibeah
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Michayahu bat Uri’el* — and above (11, 20) he calls her by another name, Maacah the daughter of Absalom, and in Kings it is written likewise, Maacah the daughter of Abishalom; but Micaiah daughter of Uriel was her name, and here he calls her so because this is the book of the genealogy of Judah; and in Kings, which is the book of the kings of Israel and Judah, he called her by the nickname Maacah daughter of Abishalom; and therefore they nicknamed her name from her true name: Micaiah — Maacah, and her father’s name Uriel — Abishalom, because she was called after her daughter-in-law, who was a woman of valor, powerful, as it is written (below, 22), “And also Maacah the mother of Asa he removed from being queen”; and for the honor of her daughter-in-law he called the mother-in-law by the daughter-in-law’s name. So it is explained in the Jerusalem Talmud, and take this tradition in your hand in the name of Rabbi Eleazar, and so he told me in the name of his father, and so I found in the commentary of his father: everywhere that a *vav* is added to the name of this woman, it is for her praise, like Athaliah and Athaliahu, “reigning over the land,” for she was a woman of valor; and likewise Yechalyah and Yechalyahu, because she was powerful, for Amaziahu her husband fled to Lachish and was there fifteen years until he died, and she judged the people all those fifteen years, and afterward, when he died, they made his son Uzziah king after him, being sixteen years old.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The explanation of the two names and of the daughter-in-law is difficult and is translated as printed. The reference “(below, 22)” does not match: the quoted words are 2 Chronicles 15:16 (JPS: “Maacah the mother of Asa the king, he removed her from being queen”). Kings gives Abijam’s mother as “Maacah the daughter of Abishalom” (1 Kings 15:2) and Asa’s as the same (15:10). The Athaliah quotation is 2 Kings 11:3 (“Athaliah reigned over the land”). 2 Kings 14:17 says Amaziah lived fifteen years after the death of Jehoash, 14:19 says he fled to Lachish and was slain there, and 14:21 says Azariah was sixteen when made king; the verses do not say that Amaziah spent the fifteen years at Lachish. The Jerusalem Talmud passage and the chain of tradition are not verified.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Abijah stood up upon mount Zemaraim
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayakom Aviyah* — for Abijah went to war against Jeroboam in the district of Jeroboam in Mount Ephraim.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: a covenant of salt
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Brit melach* — with permanence and faithfulness; and now:

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Jeroboam the son of Nebat, the servant of Solomon the son of David, rose up
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayakom Yarov’am* — “the servant of Solomon,” etc.; and for this there is great disgrace.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: vain men
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayikavtzu alav anashim rekim* — wicked men.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: when Rehoboam was young and faint-hearted
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayit’ametzu al Rechav’am ben Shlomo, veRechav’am hayah na’ar verakh levav* — and because they found in him lowliness and softness of heart, they strengthened themselves against him.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: was young
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Na’ar* — although he was forty-one years old when he began to reign, he calls him *na’ar*; and the explanation (above, 1, 22) is about Solomon.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The reference is 1 Chronicles 22:5 (JPS: “Solomon my son is young and tender”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: with a young bullock and seven rams
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ke’ammei ha’aratzot* — whoever wishes to come and fill his hand and be a priest for the golden calf brings with him a young bullock and seven rams, and they accept him.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the same becometh a priest of them that are no gods
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vehayah kohen lelo Elohim* — to fill his hand, to distinguish between impure and pure; an example (Exodus 29), “to be anointed in them, and to fill in them their hand.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The phrase “to distinguish between impure and pure” is translated as printed and its sense here is not clear to me. The quotation is Exodus 29:29 (JPS: “to be anointed in them, and to be consecrated in them”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the Levites in their work
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vehaleviyim bemelakhet* — that is, in their work: this one to sing and this one as gatekeeper, each man to his work as David arranged.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the LORD smote him
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Velo atzar ko’ach vegomer* — “and the LORD smote Jeroboam.”

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: and he died
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayamot* — not that he died at once, but he went on diminishing on account of the wars; and in Bereshit Rabbah it is explained, “and the LORD smote Abijah.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: I did not verify the Bereshit Rabbah passage. The printed abbreviation ב"ר is read as Bereshit Rabbah.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: commanded Judah to seek the LORD
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayomer liYhudah lidrosh* — and not like the ten tribes, who sought new gods that came lately, and did not seek the God of their fathers.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the land is yet before us
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Odenu ha’aretz lefaneinu* — while the kingdom is established before us, so that if they are needed they will be a refuge for us; and all this was in ten years, as it is written, “in his days the land was quiet”; and after those ten years there was war between him and Baasha all their days, for in the third year of Asa Baasha reigned, and seven years there was peace between them; and so it is proved: here too he had no war with him in those years, but in other years there was war with him. And below (15) it is written, “And there was no more war until the thirty-fifth year of the reign of Asa” — but we can explain that war as the one he had with the Cushite, that there was none until the thirty-fifth year of his reign; but this is difficult for me, for it is written below (16), “In the thirty-sixth year of Asa Baasha went up,” etc., until “thou hast done foolishly in this, for from henceforth thou shalt have wars,” which implies that before this he had no wars, and it is only after three years; and in Kings (I, 15) it is written, “And there was war between Asa and Baasha all their days”; and in Seder Olam it is explained well.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The verses are 2 Chronicles 13:23 (JPS: “in his days the land was quiet ten years”), 1 Kings 15:33 (“In the third year of Asa king of Judah began Baasa”), 2 Chronicles 15:19, 16:1 and 16:9, and 1 Kings 15:16 (JPS: “And there was war between Asa and Baasa king of Israel all their days”). Arithmetic as printed: three years plus seven years makes ten. I did not verify the Seder Olam passage.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: we have sought Him
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki darashnu et HaShem Eloheinu darashnu vegomer* — because we sought Him, He gave us rest on every side.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: So they built
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayivnu* — cities.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: and prospered
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayatzliychu* — and an example (above, 12), “And when the LORD saw that they humbled themselves,” etc.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The reference is 2 Chronicles 12:7 (JPS: “And when the LORD saw that they humbled themselves”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: there is none beside Thee to help, between the mighty and him that hath no strength
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ein immekha la’azor* — that is, although we are few and they are many as the sand of the sea and we have no strength before them, with You is power to help, between the many and him that hath no strength; that is, it is known that You have power to help; therefore help us, O LORD our God, for upon You we rely.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: let not man prevail against Thee
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Al ya’tzor immekha enosh* — let there not be for our enemies, to that man, for *enosh* is a ruler, a restrainer of the hands of Your people before You, to conquer us, so that he not say, “Their God has conquered us.” Another explanation, from the Master: let there not be to us, for we are *enoshim*, a restrainer of the hand from conquering them. An example (Deuteronomy 11): “and He shut up (*ve’atzar*) the heaven”; “for the LORD had fast closed up (*atzor atzar*)” (Genesis 20); like “Though thou detain me (*ta’atzereni*)” (Judges 13).
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The two explanations are compressed and are translated as I read them. The quotations are Deuteronomy 11:17 (JPS: “He shut up the heaven”), Genesis 20:18 (JPS: “the LORD had fast closed up all the wombs”) and Judges 13:16 (JPS: “Though thou detain me”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Israel was without the true God
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Veyamim rabbim leYisra’el lelo Elohei emet* — until you came.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: without a teaching priest
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Velelo kohen moreh* — for there was none who asked of them any matter of Torah; therefore the priests did not teach you.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The second clause is translated as I read it.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: He was found of them
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayashav batzar lo al HaShem Elohei Yisra’el* — that is, now that distress has come upon them they sought the LORD, the God of Israel, and they sought Him; therefore He was found to them, the One who is present, and saved you wherever you went.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The last clause is translated as printed.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: there was no peace to him that went out
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uva’ittim hahem ein shalom* — in those days (“many days for Israel without the true God”) there was no peace to him that went out or came in, etc. Of Rehoboam it is written (above, 12), “Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem because they trespassed against the LORD,” and the whole passage; and to Abijah also there were many tumults.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 2 Chronicles 12:2 (JPS: “Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem, because they had dealt treacherously with the LORD”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: they were broken in pieces
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vekhuttetu goy begoy* — an example (Numbers 14): “and beat them down (*vayakkatum*).”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Numbers 14:45 (JPS: “and beat them down”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: But be you strong
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’attem chizku* — to seek God.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: of the spoil which they had brought
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayizbechu laShem bayom hahu min hashalal hevi’u* — the interpretation: and from the spoil which they brought they sacrificed seven hundred oxen and seven thousand sheep which they took captive, and from it they brought, as above (2, 14), “and they also brought tents of cattle and took captive sheep in abundance,” etc. Another explanation, it appears to me: “And they sacrificed unto the LORD in that day” on which they conquered and came in peace to Jerusalem, “of the spoil which they had brought” — that is, from the spoil which they brought, they brought seven hundred oxen and seven thousand sheep.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed quotation is from the account of the Cushite war, 2 Chronicles 14:14 (JPS: “They smote also the tents of cattle, and carried away sheep in abundance and camels”); the printed number “2, 14” does not match that verse.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: an abominable image for an Asherah
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vegam Ma’akhah em Asa hamelekh hesirah migevirah* — because she made for the Asherah a *mifletzet*, a wondrous mockery; she made for it male organs, for an image, and was cohabited by it.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed abbreviation לצל׳ after “for it” is read as “for an image,” which I could not confirm.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the high places were not taken away out of Israel
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vehabamot lo saru* — private high places, on which they had been accustomed to offer to Heaven from the destruction of Shiloh until the Temple was built; and they were punished for them with *karet* (being cut off).
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The reference to the penalty of *karet* is as printed; I did not verify it.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: And there was no more war unto the five and thirtieth year of the reign of Asa
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Umilchamah lo hayetah vegomer* — it was taught in Seder Olam: In the thirty-sixth year of Asa’s reign Baasha went up. Is it possible to say so? But Baasha had already died in the twenty-sixth year of Asa’s reign, as it is written (1 Kings 16), “In the twenty and sixth year of Asa… began Elah the son of Baasha to reign.” Rather, what does it teach with “in the thirty-sixth year of King Asa”? Corresponding to the thirty-six years since Solomon allied himself with the daughter of Pharaoh; for it is written in Kings (I, 2), “And two servants of Shimei fled,” until “and the king commanded Benaiah, and he went and fell upon him”; and nearby (there, 3) it is written, “And Solomon allied himself with Pharaoh’s daughter” — that is, immediately after those three years, and in year four he took her; and he reigned forty years, so she was with him thirty-six years; and corresponding to those thirty-six years a decree was decreed against the kings of Aram, to be adversaries of Israel and in the end to fall into the hand of the sons of David. Therefore it says “in the thirty-sixth year of King Asa.” And in the sixteenth year of his reign, from when Zerah the Cushite fell into his hand, it is the thirty-sixth year since Solomon died; and in the sixteenth year of Asa the king of Israel and the king of Aram made a covenant to go up and provoke Asa; and Asa spoiled it, as it is said, “And Asa brought out silver and gold… saying, Let there be a league between me and thee,” and Ben-hadad hearkened. And the kings of Aram did not cease being adversaries of Israel until Ahaz died; and in the third year of Ahaz the king of Israel and the king of Aram made a covenant to go up and provoke Ahaz, and Ahaz had no merit that they should fall into his hand, and both fell into the hand of Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The verses are 1 Kings 16:8 (JPS: “In the twenty and sixth year of Asa king of Judah began Elah the son of Baasa to reign over Israel in Tirzah”), 1 Kings 2:39 (“at the end of three years, that two of the servants of Shimei ran away”), 2:46 (“the king commanded Benaiah… and he went out, and fell upon him”) and 3:1 (“Solomon became allied to Pharaoh king of Egypt by marriage”). Arithmetic: forty years minus the first four makes thirty-six; seventeen years of Rehoboam, three of Abijah and sixteen of Asa make thirty-six since Solomon’s death. The references to Ahaz correspond to 2 Kings 16:5–9, which describes Rezin and Pekah coming up against Ahaz and Tiglath-pileser taking Damascus. The Seder Olam passage is not verified. Audit 5 source check: a passage with the same wording (11 consecutive words) is found in Seder Olam Rabbah 16.1 (Sefaria Hebrew text, labelled Public Domain). This is a wording match only; the translation was not changed.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: that dwelt at Damascus
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Bedarmeshek* — and in Kings (II, 16) it is written *Dammesek*, and in another verse *Dumesek*, and all are one; an example: *shot*, *shevet*, *sharvit*.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: JPS renders the name “Damascus” throughout and does not show the spelling variants.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: therefore is the host of the king of Aram escaped out of thy hand
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Al ken nimlat* — that you were not able against him, because you did not trust in the Holy One, blessed be He; for if you had trusted in the Holy One, blessed be He, when the king of Israel and the king of Aram swore and made a covenant together against you, as you trusted in Him when the Cushites came upon you, they would not have escaped from your hand, and you would have conquered all of them; nor would you have lost your money which you gave him to break his covenant with Baasha; and now that you did not trust in the Holy One, blessed be He, you lost your money, and also the king of Aram escaped from your hand.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: put him in the prison-house
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Beit hamahpekhet* — the house of confinement, made with the work of the *mahpekhet* (stocks), *govelbet* in the German language.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed phrase בלשון אשכנז is read as “in the German language”; the glossed word is left as printed and I could not identify it.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: his disease was exceeding great
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ad lema’lah cholyo* — a swelling that was in his feet went up from the sole of his foot to his crown.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: divers kinds [of spices]
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vezanim* — kinds of spices; and the spices were compounded with a compounding, the work of the perfumer; and this is the interpretation of “prepared by the perfumers’ art.”

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: they made a very great burning for him
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayisrefu lo sereifah gedolah* — they burned good spices to ashes, and scattered that ash upon him; and some explain it as they burn for kings; and what do they burn, etc., and they hamstring for kings.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The reference to burning and hamstringing for kings is cut off in the printed text (“etc.”); I did not verify the underlying Talmudic passage.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: walked in the first ways of his father David
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Bedarkhei David aviv harishonim* — and not the last ones, in which he was negligent in the matter of Bath-sheba, and Satan also incited him to number Israel; and this is the main point. And some explain “first” as the head of Solomon and Rehoboam: Solomon, whose wives turned his heart in the end of his days, and he built a high place for Chemosh, the abomination of Moab, and for Molech, the detestation of the children of Ammon; and of Rehoboam it is written (above, 2, 12), “And it came to pass, when the kingdom of Rehoboam was established, and he was strong, that he forsook the law of the LORD”; and not like his father, of whom it is written in Kings (I, 9), “and his heart was not whole with the LORD his God”; and not like Asa, who did not rely on the LORD, but like David his father, who had only one heart for his Father in Heaven.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The second explanation (“first” as the head of Solomon and Rehoboam) is compressed and is translated as I read it. The verses are 1 Chronicles 21:1 (JPS: “And Satan stood up against Israel, and moved David to number Israel”), 1 Kings 11:7 (the high places for Chemosh and Molech), 2 Chronicles 12:1 and 1 Kings 11:4 (JPS: “his heart was not whole with the LORD his God, as was the heart of David his father”); the printed reference “Kings I, 9” does not match, and 11:4 is the verse. Audit 5 source check: a passage with the same wording (9 consecutive words) is found in Seder Olam Rabbah 16.1 (Sefaria Hebrew text, labelled Public Domain). This is a wording match only; the translation was not changed.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: and sought not unto the Baalim
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Velo darash laBe’alim* — like the deed of Israel in his days, for Ahab was in his days, who served the Baalim, he and the Israel of his days.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: his heart was lifted up in the ways of the LORD
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayigbah libbo bedarkhei HaShem* — his heart was lifted up in this thing, that he walked only in the ways of the LORD; an example (Exodus 35): “whose heart stirred them up (*nasa libban*) in wisdom.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Exodus 35:26 (JPS: “whose heart stirred them up in wisdom”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: even Ben-hail
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Shalach lesarav levein chayil* — so was his name; and some explain: he sent his officers, each officer a man of valor (*ben chayil*); and it is difficult for me, for if so he should have said only “to Obadiah”; but from his saying “and to Obadiah,” it follows that *Ben-hail* is the name of a man.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The last argument is compressed and is translated as I read it.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: to teach in the cities of Judah
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lelammed be’arei Yehudah* — Torah, and to instruct the children of Israel.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: and with them the Levites
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’imahem* — of the Levites: Shemaiah and Nethaniah, etc.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: and with them Elishama and Jehoram, the priests
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’immahem Elishama veYehoram haKohanim* — for it is upon the priests and the Levites to teach and to instruct, as it is written (Deuteronomy 24), “according to all that the priests the Levites shall teach you”; and the officers went with them so that they would not disobey their word, and to compel them to listen to them and to keep and do as the judges command; like (there, 16) “Judges and officers shalt thou make thee,” judges to judge the people and officers to compel them and carry out the orders of the judges.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotations are Deuteronomy 24:8 (JPS: “according to all that the priests the Levites shall teach you”) and Deuteronomy 16:18 (JPS: “Judges and officers shalt thou make thee in all thy gates”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: a terror from the LORD fell upon all the kingdoms of the lands
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayehi pachad HaShem al kol mamlekhot ha’aratzot* — by the merit that they learned Torah.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: silver for tribute
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vechesef masa* — loads of silver; an example (Isaiah 47): “The things that you carried about are made a load.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Isaiah 46:1 (JPS: “The things that you carried about are made a load”); the printed chapter number 47 is wrong.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: And Jehoshaphat waxed great exceedingly
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayehi Yehoshafat holekh vegadel* — three of whom it is said in this language: Isaac, Samuel, Jehoshaphat; but of Moses, David and Mordecai it is said *vegadol*; but of Isaac, Samuel, Jehoshaphat it is written *vegadel*, for it is not right to say *vegadol*. Of Samuel it is written, “And the child Samuel grew (*vayigdal*) before the LORD,” and Heaven forbid to say “great with the LORD”; and here likewise, “grew exceedingly” (*gadal ad lema’lah*); therefore it is not fitting to say *vegadol*, and likewise of Isaac.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The Samuel quotation is 1 Samuel 2:21 (JPS: “And the child Samuel grew before the LORD”). I did not look up the other verses in which these forms occur.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: castles
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Biraniyyot* — from the root *birah*, great towers for strength.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: cities of store
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’arei miskenot* — cities of storehouses, to put in them grain and wine and corn.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: next to him
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’al yado* — beside him; an example, “See, Joab’s field is beside me” (2 Samuel 14).
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 2 Samuel 14:30 (JPS: “Joab’s field is near mine”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: who willingly offered himself unto the LORD
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *HaMitnadev laShem* — an example (Judges 5): “those who offer themselves willingly among the people, bless the LORD.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Judges 5:2 and 5:9 (JPS: “When the people offer themselves willingly, Bless you the LORD”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: after a lapse of years
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayered liketz shanim* — and in Kings (I, 22) it is written, “And it came to pass in the third year, that Jehoshaphat went down,” etc.; in the third year from when he sent away Ben-hadad.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 1 Kings 22:2 (JPS: “in the third year, that Jehoshaphat the king of Judah came down to the king of Israel”); 1 Kings 22:1 says they continued three years without war between Aram and Israel, and 20:34 tells of Ahab letting Ben-hadad go.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: persuaded him to go up with him to Ramoth-gilead
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayesitehu la’alot el Ramot Gil’ad* — as it is written there in the Book of Kings, “Know you that Ramoth-gilead is ours”; for when Jacob set up his stones there, the heap (Genesis 31), and called it Gilead, it was held by him; and our fathers took Gilead, and the Ramoth are drawn out and held behind the city; and our fathers then, in the days of Moses, when they seized Gilead, were silent then from taking it, because they did not worry about them; or perhaps in the days of Moses they took it, and afterward the nations took it from the hand of Israel, and they are ours.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The reasoning is compressed and is translated as I read it. The quotation is 1 Kings 22:3 (JPS: “Know you that Ramoth-gilead is ours”), and the heap is Genesis 31:46–47.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Inquire, I pray thee, at the word of the LORD today
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Derash na kayom et devar HaShem* — and not of the prophets of the Baalim in whom you trust.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the king of Israel gathered the prophets together, four hundred men
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayikbotz melekh Yisra’el et haNevi’im arba me’ot* — and all of them were true prophets; for what Jehoshaphat asked of him, he gathered for him. So it is proved nearby (verse 20): “And the spirit came forth and said, I will entice him,” etc., until “and I will be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets,” that he says to them to say to Ahab, “Go up, and God will deliver it into the hand of the king” — which implies that they were prophets of the LORD, who did not prophesy except the word of the LORD; for if they had been false prophets, the enticement would not fall upon them, for they would not prophesy anything except what they invented from their own hearts. And furthermore, Jehoshaphat said afterward, “Is there not here yet a prophet of the LORD?” — surely I know that they are prophets of the LORD, but I have a tradition from the house of my father’s father that two prophets do not prophesy in one style and one language, and these all prophesy, “Go up and prosper.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The verses are 2 Chronicles 18:20–21 (JPS: “I will go forth, and will be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets”) and 18:6 (compare 1 Kings 22:7, JPS: “Is there not here besides a prophet of the LORD, that we might inquire of him?”). I did not verify the tradition that two prophets do not prophesy in the same style.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: for he never prophesieth good concerning me, but always evil
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki khol yamav lera’ah* — for this is what is said (Kings I, 22), “Because thou hast sent a man of Charmi,” etc.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quoted words “Because thou hast let go out of thy hand the man whom I had devoted to destruction” are 1 Kings 20:42; the printed chapter number 22 is wrong.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Fetch quickly Micaiah the son of Imla
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Maher Michehu* — it is written lacking a *yod*, out of contempt; he gave him another name, *Michehu*.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The note is about the spelling of the name in the Hebrew text, which JPS does not show.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: they sat in a threshing-floor at the entrance of the gate of Samaria
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Mulbashim begadim* — royal garments; “and they sat in a threshing-floor at the entrance of the gate of Samaria” — it comes to inform us that when the prophets prophesied before them they were sitting outside the city, and there came the spies of the king of Aram and heard that he told the king of Israel that he alone would fall in the war; this is why the king of Aram commanded his troops (below, 18:30), “Fight neither with small nor great, save only with the king of Israel,” to fulfill the words of Micaiah. Therefore it is written “in a threshing-floor,” for it was a place for spies to spy; but if the assembly had been inside the city, the spies of the king of Aram could not have come, lest they be noticed that they were spies; but when they are outside the city, even if they notice them and understand that they are spies, they can say, “We are going to another place, and our coming near here to the threshing-floor was because of a great noise and the gathering of troops; behold, at the entrance of the city we marveled and turned from the way to see what this was.” And the spies informed the king of Aram, and he commanded not to kill any man except the king of Israel alone; for otherwise, what came into his heart that he commanded not to kill any of Israel but the king alone? Rather, he had spies, and they heard Micaiah saying, “I saw all Israel scattered,” etc.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quoted command is 2 Chronicles 18:30 (JPS: “Fight neither with small nor great, save only with the king of Israel”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Go you up, and prosper
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Alu vehatzliychu vayinnatenu beyedkhem* — that is, would that you prosper and they be delivered into your hands.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: I saw all Israel scattered upon the mountains
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Nefutzim al heharim* — for when they flee from the battle they flee to the mountains, a house of refuge, like “and they that remained fled to the mountain” (Genesis 14); and furthermore the war was at Ramoth-gilead, a place of mountains and hills.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Genesis 14:10 (JPS: “and they that remained fled to the mountain”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: These have no master
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayomer HaShem lo adonim le’eleh* — a sign that the king would be killed, but Israel would return every man to his house in peace; and they heard this that he said, “If thou return at all in peace”; the spies heard it all and told the king of Aram, and then the king of Aram commanded to do as Micaiah’s word, to kill the king alone.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The reference to “If thou return at all in peace” is 2 Chronicles 18:27.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: as sheep that have no shepherd
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayomer HaShem lo adonim le’eleh* — therefore scattered like sheep on the mountains that have no shepherd, for their king will be killed.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: let them return every man to his house in peace
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Yashuvu ish levaito beshalom* — for Ahab alone would be killed, but the rest of Israel would return every man to his house in peace, as Aram commanded his people.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: all the host of heaven standing on His right hand and on His left
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vekhol tzeva hashamayim omdim al yemino usemolo* — these are the angels of destruction (another version: the ministering angels) standing before Him.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed variant is noted as ס"א, read as “another version.” The printed abbreviation ס"א is read as “another version.”

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: there came forth the spirit
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayetze haRuach* — the interpretation: the angel came forth, for it said above “and all the host of heaven,” etc., and now one of the angels came forth and said, “I will entice him,” as it says (Psalms 104), “Who makest winds Thy messengers”; therefore it first said above “and all the host of heaven standing,” so that you not wonder when you read “And the spirit came forth” — who is it and from where did it come forth; and when it said “and all the host of heaven standing,” it was to make known from where it came forth, from among the other spirits standing by Him. And our Rabbis explained: this is the spirit of Naboth.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Psalm 104:4 (JPS: “Who makest winds Thy messengers”). I did not verify the Rabbinic identification with Naboth.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Bifi khol nevi’av* — that he would put a word in their mouth to say, “Go up and prosper,” and he would go up and fall; it follows that they were true prophets, who did not prophesy except what the Name put in their mouth.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Thou shalt entice him, and shalt prevail also
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Tefatteh vegam tukhal* — for there is an enticer who comes to entice his fellow, and sometimes the one enticed understands that this one wishes to entice him, and he is careful and does not listen to be enticed; but with Ahab, “thou shalt entice him, and shalt prevail also.”

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: thou shalt see on that day
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Hinekha ro’eh* — that Ahab will be killed.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Put this fellow in the prison
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Simu zeh beit hakele* — and although we have not seen that they put him before this in prison, from the fact that it says “bring him back” you can say that they had put him before this in prison; and if you wish to say that they had never put him before this, it should not be difficult for you with “bring him back,” for this is the way of the verses, like (Psalms 9) “The wicked shall return to the nether-world,” and so in many places.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Psalm 9:18 (JPS: “The wicked shall return to the nether-world”). The “bring him back” is 2 Chronicles 18:25.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: feed him with scant bread and with scant water
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lechem lachatz umayim lachatz* — an example (Isaiah 20): “bread of adversity and water of affliction.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Isaiah 30:20 (JPS: “sparing bread and scant water”); the printed chapter number 20 is wrong.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: I will disguise myself, and go into the battle
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Hitchapes uva* — the interpretation: I need to disguise myself in other clothes, so that they not recognize me, that I am the king of Israel; for he was apprehensive of Micaiah’s words, who said to him, “If thou return at all in peace,” etc.; and he said to Jehoshaphat: I wish to change myself and come into the battle, for I have reason to fear that the Arameans heard what Micaiah said, “If thou return at all in peace,” and will turn to fight only against me.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: put thou on thy robes
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’attah levash begadekha* — royal armor and coats of mail and royal weapons of war, for there is no need to fear the prophet’s words except for the king of Israel alone, for his spies reported Micaiah’s words.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Jehoshaphat cried out, and the LORD helped him
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayiz’ak Yehoshafat* — after the sons of his standard and his troops, that they come to help him, like the sign of the lion in his standard or the standard of the sons of Judah; and so it is the custom when two bands fight, each band names one name as a sign for its standard, for the need of the band with it, so that if they are separated each from his fellow or the bands become mixed with each other, each and every band will cry out its sign name, and they will recognize the voice of the sign and gather all together and be in one body as at first; and not that he cried to his God. And so it proves (1 Kings 22): “and Jehoshaphat cried out” — and it is not said “to the Name, and the LORD helped him, and God moved them from him”; but there it is written, “And it came to pass, when the captains of the chariots saw that it was not the king of Israel,” that they recognized and understood at once when he cried after the sign of his standard, as it explains: when they recognized him, “they turned back from pursuing him,” as the command of the king of Aram, and it was from the LORD that they recognized him.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The Kings verses are 1 Kings 22:32 (JPS: “and Jehoshaphat cried out”) and 22:33 (JPS: “when the captains of the chariots saw that it was not the king of Israel, that they turned back from pursuing him”). The explanation is Rashi’s own and differs from the plain sense of the verse here, which says that the LORD helped him.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: And a certain man drew his bow at a venture
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’ish mashakh bakeshet* — a man of Israel aiming to shoot into the camp of Aram, and not aiming at him.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: smote the king of Israel
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayakh* — the arrow struck the king of Israel.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: between the lower armour and the breastplate
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Bein hadevakim uvein hasiryon* — between that strap by which the helmet on his head is fastened to the coat of mail; and it is not to be said that he was an Egyptian, for at whom would he aim? Did not the king of Aram command, “Fight neither with small nor great, save only with the king of Israel”? And nor did he aim at him, for it is written “at a venture” (*letumo*); rather, perforce it must be said that an Israelite was the archer, and he aimed to shoot into the camp of Aram, and in his innocence struck the king of Israel.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The word “Egyptian” (מצרי) is translated as printed; the context suggests an Aramean was meant, and I could not confirm it. The Aramean command is 2 Chronicles 18:30.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the driver of the chariot
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayomer larekhev* — to the one who leads the chariot.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: carry me out of the host
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vehotzeitani min hamachaneh* — that is, from this first line of battle, and seat me in the last lines.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the battle increased that day
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vata’al hamilchamah* — it withdrew; and not one of Israel was harmed except the king of Israel alone, as the prophet said (above, 18), “These have no master; let them return every man to his house in peace”; “to peace” is not said, for Ahab was slain.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 2 Chronicles 18:16 (JPS: “These have no master, let them return every man to his house in peace”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: stayed himself up in his chariot
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ma’amid bamerkavah* — he held fast and stood in the chariot so that Israel not perceive his wound and flee; and the beginning of a fall is flight.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: thou hast put away the Asheroth out of the land
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki bi’arta ha’asherot* — as above, and moreover he took away the high places, etc.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: hast set thy heart to seek God
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ladrosh ha’Elohim* — as above (2, 17): “but sought to the God of his father,” etc.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 2 Chronicles 17:4 (JPS: “but sought to the God of his father”); the printed number “2, 17” refers to it.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: And he set judges in the land
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vaya’amed shofetim* — when the seer said to him, “Good things are found with thee, for thou hast put away the Asheroth,” he came to the Torah scroll to see whether he had removed them according to the law; and at first he saw written “ye shall surely destroy” until “and their Asherim ye shall burn with fire, and the graven images of their gods ye shall hew down”; and he remembered that it is written in *Ki Tissa* (Exodus 34), “and their pillars ye shall break,” etc.; he wondered to himself that he had done good in the eyes of the LORD in that he removed the Asherim, the Asherim of Israel, for He had warned them only about their Asherim; and then he turned back to “judges and officers” and found written (Deuteronomy 15) “Thou shalt not plant thee an Asherah,” and then he rejoiced that he had removed them, and he also saw there written, “Judges and officers shalt thou make thee” (there); immediately, “And he set judges” established in all the cities of Judah, city by city.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The reasoning about “their Asherim” is compressed and is translated as I read it. The abbreviation סה"ת is read as “Torah scroll.” The verses are Deuteronomy 12:2–3 (JPS: “And you shall break down their altars… and burn their Asherim with fire; and you shall hew down the graven images of their gods”), Exodus 34:13 (JPS: “you shall cut down their Asherim”), Deuteronomy 16:21 (JPS: “Thou shalt not plant thee an Asherah of any kind of tree”; the printed number 15 is wrong) and Deuteronomy 16:18 (“Judges and officers shalt thou make thee”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: all the fortified cities of Judah
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Bekhol arei Yehudah habetzurot* — he appointed established ones to compel them and force them to the law at first, and afterward he appointed judges who are not so established for the towns that are not fortified, because they fear being refractory more than those who dwell in fortified cities, who trust in their fortified cities.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: you judge not for man, but for the LORD
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki lo le’adam tishpotu* — the interpretation: do not think in your hearts, saying, “What is it to us if we bend the judgment to acquit our friends, to pervert the judgment of the poor and to favor the faces of the rich? Is not the judgment the LORD’s?” Therefore it says “for the LORD,” it is His; if you convict the innocent it is as though you took and seized from your Creator, and perverted the judgment of Heaven by giving perverted judgment. Therefore see what you do, and let your heart be in every case as though the Holy One, blessed be He, were standing before you in judgment; and this is “and He is with you in giving judgment.” And in Sanhedrin it is explained: “Consider what you do, for you judge not for man, but for the LORD”; and lest the judge say, “What have I to do with this trouble?” Scripture says, “and He is with you in giving judgment”; that is, it is incumbent upon you to do, and a judge has nothing but what his eyes see.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: I did not verify the Sanhedrin passage.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: there is no iniquity with the LORD our God, nor respect of persons, nor taking of bribes
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ein im HaShem Eloheinu avlah umasso fanim umikach shochad* — and He is with you in judgment; therefore He does not wish you to do iniquity in judgment.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Moreover in Jerusalem did Jehoshaphat set
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vegam biYrushalayim he’emid* — although he himself was in Jerusalem.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: for the judgment of the LORD, and for controversies
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lemishpat HaShem velarriv* — *mishpat* is used for civil cases; an example (Numbers 26): “and it shall be unto the children of Israel a statute of judgment”; and *riv* is used mostly for capital cases and injuries, like (Exodus 21) “And if men contend (*yerivun*),” etc.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotations are Numbers 27:11 (JPS: “And it shall be unto the children of Israel a statute of judgment”; the printed number 26 is wrong) and Exodus 21:18 (JPS: “And if men contend”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Thus shall you do in the fear of the LORD
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Koh ta’asun* — for the sake of alacrity and care and for strength an additional *nun* was added, like (Ruth 3) “until thou know (*teda’in*) how the matter will fall,” and like (Genesis 32) “Thus shall you say (*tomrun*) to my lord Esau,” and “abide fast (*tidbakin*)… that they reap (*yiktzorun*)” (Ruth 2).
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotations are Ruth 3:18, Genesis 32:5 and Ruth 2:8–9 (JPS: “abide here fast by my maidens… the field that they do reap”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: between blood and blood
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Bein dam ladam* — between the blood of unintentional killing and intentional.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: you shall warn them
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vehizhartem otam* — your brethren.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: and so wrath come upon you and upon your brethren
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vehayah ketzef aleikhem ve’al acheikhem* — therefore, thus shall you do, and you shall warn your brethren.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: and you shall not be guilty
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Velo te’shamu* — them, in any case; for if you accept the warning, there will be no wrath upon you, and neither will there be in any matter guilt upon you, since you did your duty that was incumbent upon you to do.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the LORD be with the good
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vihi HaShem im hatov* — with him who does the good and the right.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: some of the Ammonites
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’immahem me’ha’Ammonim* — this is Amalek; and why were they called Ammonites? Because he changed his garment and his language like the Ammonites and mingled among them, and came to fight against Israel. And so it is proved below, in the matter: “And when they began to sing and to praise, the LORD set liers-in-wait against the children of Ammon, Moab, and mount Seir,” etc.; it turns out that the Ammonites mentioned here are the Amalekites who changed their language and their garment. And this is what Kalir composed in the portion *Zachor*: “Remember the tyrant who hid among the Ammonites, who broke into the vineyards of En-gedi”; that is, remember what Amalek the tyrant did, who hid among the Ammonites and came to break into the vineyards of Israel at that time, as it is written, “and behold, they are in Hazazon-tamar, the same is En-gedi,” and En-gedi is near the territory of Amalek, as it is said in *Lekh Lekha* (Genesis 14): “and smote all the country of the Amalekites, and also the Amorites that dwelt in Hazazon-tamar.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The verse quoted is 2 Chronicles 20:22 (JPS: “the LORD set liers-in-wait against the children of Ammon, Moab, and mount Seir”), 20:2 and Genesis 14:7 (JPS: “smote all the country of the Amalekites, and also the Amorites, that dwelt in Hazazon-tamar”). I did not verify the wording of Kalir’s poem.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the same is En-gedi
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Hi Ein Gedi* — that is, they told him that they had already come so near to us.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: even out of all the cities of Judah
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Gam mikkol arei Yehudah* — lest you say that when it says at first “And Judah gathered themselves together to seek,” these were only the inhabitants of Jerusalem; rather, from all the cities of Judah they came.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: ruler over all the kingdoms of the nations
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’attah moshel bekhol mamlekhot hagoyim* — to exercise Your dominion over them; therefore we ask You to help us against them.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: and in Thy hand is power and might
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uvyadekha ko’ach* — master of power and might, *hardin* in Old French.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The Old French form printed in Hebrew letters (הרדי"ן) could not be confirmed; left as printed. The printed abbreviation בלע"ז is read as “in Old French.”

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: so that none is able to withstand Thee
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’ein immekha lehitzayyev* — no creature can stand before You, among all the kingdoms of the nations; an example (Joshua 1) “There shall not any man be able to stand before thee,” and likewise (Job 41) “Who then is able to stand before Me?” (So explained Rabbi Menachem bar Helbo, of blessed memory.)
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotations are Joshua 1:5 (JPS: “There shall not any man be able to stand before thee”) and Job 41:2 (JPS: “Who then is able to stand before Me?”); the printed book name “מ"א” is read as Job on the evidence of the wording.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: gavest it to the seed of Abraham Thy friend for ever
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vatitnah lezera Avraham* — therefore it is upon You to keep it in their hands and drive out these nations; for even a king, and even any man, who gave a gift to his friend, and another comes to rob it from him, will exert himself to keep it in his hand; all the more You; and lest you say: I gave it to you only for a time — for this reason it was said above, “an everlasting inheritance You gave us.”
