2 Chronicles.translator_note: I could not locate the quoted words “an everlasting inheritance” above in this chapter.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: have built Thee a sanctuary therein for Thy name
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayivnu lekha vah mikdash leshimekha lemor* — that if evil comes upon us, sword, judgment, or any suit and dispute, and famine.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: and cry unto Thee in our affliction
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Venaze’ak eilekha mitzaratenu* — in the Temple.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Thou wilt hear and save
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vetishma vetoshia* — as Solomon prayed before You and Your promise to do so, as it is written (above, 2, 6), “And if Thy people be smitten,” and the whole passage, until “and render unto every man according to all his ways,” and the LORD granted his prayer, as it is written (there), “And the LORD appeared to Solomon, and said to him, I have heard thy prayer,” and the whole passage until “and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land”; and now I pray that You remember that promise which You promised and hear and save us from our enemies who come upon us.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The passages are 2 Chronicles 6:24–30 (JPS: “And if Thy people Israel be smitten down before the enemy”) and 7:12–14 (JPS: “will forgive their sin, and will heal their land”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: And now
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’attah* — upon all this that You promised to save us from our enemies who come upon us.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: whom Thou wouldest not let Israel invade
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Hineh Venei Ammon uMo’av veHar Se’ir asher lo natatta leYisra’el lavo bahem* — to fight.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: when they came out of the land of Egypt
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Bevo’am me’eretz Mitzrayim* — and they ought to have remembered the kindness and come to our help; and it was not enough for them that they do not remember that kindness to be with us in all our troubles, but they repay us with evil and come upon us.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: to come to cast us out of Thy possession, which Thou hast given us to inherit
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Legareshenu miyerushatekha asher horashtanu* — You Yourself; and therefore what have they to contest our inheritance?

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: our eyes are upon Thee
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki alekha eineinu* — to save us.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: with their little ones, their wives, and their children
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Gam tapam* — as is the custom, when bands come upon the land, they flee from the villages to their fortified cities, their little ones, their wives and their sons.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Fear not you, neither be dismayed by reason of this great multitude
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Al tire’u ve’al techattu* — it refers back to what they said, “We have no strength before the multitude”; and the prophet said to them, although they are more numerous than you, do not fear them.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: for the battle is not yours, but God’s
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki lo lakhem hamilchamah ki Lelohim* — it refers back to “neither know we what to do,” and the prophet replied: surely, as you said that your eyes and your trust are upon the Holy One, blessed be He, to save you, so He will do; for the battle is not yours but God’s.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: Compare 2 Chronicles 20:12 (JPS: “neither know we what to do; but our eyes are upon Thee”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: by the ascent of Ziz
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Bema’aleh haTzitz* — the name of a place.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: set yourselves
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Hityatzevu* — it refers back to “the battle is not yours.”

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: see the salvation of the LORD with you
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ur’u et yeshu’at HaShem* — it refers back to above, “Art not Thou our God, who gavest us possession,” and the Holy One, blessed be He, said to them: the claim is with you, it is upon Me to keep it in your hands.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: Compare 2 Chronicles 20:7 (JPS: “Didst not Thou, O our God, drive out the inhabitants of this land”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: to-morrow go out against them
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Machar tze’u* — and I shall fight for you; and they believed and hurried and rose early in the morning.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: believe in the LORD your God
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vete’amenu* — be people of faith and you shall prosper; an example (Isaiah 7), “If you will not believe.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Isaiah 7:9 (JPS: “If you will not have faith, surely you shall not be established”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the LORD set liers-in-wait against the children of Ammon
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Natan HaShem me’arvim* — He set ambushes to destroy them and to put them under the ban; an example with Abijah the son of Rehoboam (above, 2, 13): “And Jeroboam caused an ambushment to come about (*hesev*)”; so too the Holy One, blessed be He, turned them (*hesibam*) one against another; and afterward Moab turned back and helped the children of Ammon, and both rose up against the sons of Seir.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 2 Chronicles 13:13 (JPS: “But Jeroboam caused an ambushment to come about behind them”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: every one helped to destroy another
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vaya’amdu Bnei Ammon uMo’av al Yoshvei Har Se’ir… ezru ish bere’ehu* — the Holy One, blessed be He, turned them against one another to destroy them until they were finished, until the *hagrim* fell to the ground with none escaping.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The word *hagrim* is translated as printed (“Hagrites”) and its sense here is not clear to me.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: more than they could carry away
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Le’ein masa* — from the abundance.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: they assembled themselves in the valley of Beracah
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Nikhalu le’emek Berakhah* — in that valley, which afterward was called the valley of Beracah because of the event, as it is explained nearby, as it says, “for there they blessed the LORD,” and gave thanks for all the good that He did for them, that He helped them against the idolaters.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed abbreviation עכומ"ז is read as “idolaters.”

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: with psalteries and harps and trumpets
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayavo’u Yerushalayim binvalim uvechinnorot uvachatzotzerot* — behold, three instruments of song, corresponding to the three: all the men of Judah, and Jerusalem, and Jehoshaphat.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The three are named in 2 Chronicles 20:27 (JPS: “every man of Judah and Jerusalem, and Jehoshaphat in the forefront of them”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: he walked in the way of Asa his father
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayelekh bederekh aviv Asa* — in what thing did he not turn aside from doing the right? From his father’s way of good and right he did not turn aside, but from Asa’s evil way he turned aside, as it is written (above, 2, 15), “And Asa brought out silver and gold,” and the whole passage; but Jehoshaphat did not do so, but trusted all his days in the Holy One, blessed be He.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 2 Chronicles 16:2 (JPS: “Then Asa brought out silver and gold”); the printed number “2, 15” does not match.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the words of Jehu the son of Hanani
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Bedivrei Yehu ben Chanani* — who said to King Jehoshaphat (there, 19), “Shouldest thou help the wicked?”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 2 Chronicles 19:2 (JPS: “Shouldest thou help the wicked, and love them that hate the LORD?”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: they were not able to go to Tarshish
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Velo atzaru* — the interpretation: the ships had no strength to go, and were broken.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: a lamp
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Nir* — its explanation: a yoke upon Israel.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: JPS renders *nir* here as “a lamp.”

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: In his days Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Bimav pasha Edom vegomer* — for David cut off every male in Edom, and placed governors among them in place of a king, and they paid him tribute; and so all the kings of Judah did, placing governors good in their eyes; and from the days of Jehoram onward they rebelled from under the hand of Judah.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: smote the Edomites that compassed him about
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Hasoveiv elav* — and he smote Edom, those who surrounded and supported him to help him; for it was their way, when they were defeated in a war, to seize the mighty men and bring them with them, so that they not be added to their enemies as help for Edom, their own people; and he rose by night suddenly and slew them. And our Rabbis explained *hasoveiv elav* as those close before him.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: So Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah unto this day
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayifsha Edom* — but was it not already said above, “In his days Edom revolted”? But so is the way of the verse: because one verse intervened between, and it wishes to say “then did Libnah revolt,” therefore it arranged them at first, and it says “So Edom revolted”; “then did Libnah revolt” — Libnah belonged to Judah and stood on the border of Edom, as it is written in the Book of Joshua, “And the cities at the uttermost part of the tribe of the children of Judah toward the border of Edom”; and when they saw that the Edomites rebelled, they too rebelled at that time, since they dwell on the border of Edom, and helped Edom; and this is “then did Libnah revolt.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Joshua 15:21 (JPS: “the cities at the uttermost part of the tribe of the children of Judah toward the border of Edom”). The earlier verse is 2 Chronicles 21:8.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: because he had forsaken the LORD
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki azav et HaShem Elohei avotav* — it tells what caused them to rebel in his days more than in the days of the kings of Judah who were before him.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: made the inhabitants of Jerusalem to go astray
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayezen* — anyone who abandons and changes the fear of the Holy One, blessed be He, for idolatry and constellations, falls under the term of harlotry which he committed, like a wife who goes astray and commits adultery with others; it resembles “for the land doth commit great harlotry” (Hosea 1), “and they will go astray after the foreign gods” (Deuteronomy 31).
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotations are Hosea 1:2 (JPS: “the land doth commit great harlotry”) and Deuteronomy 31:16 (JPS: “go astray after the foreign gods of the land”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: a writing to him from Elijah the prophet
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayavo elav mikhtav me’Eliyahu* — after Elijah had gone up to heaven, this writing of this prophecy came to him.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: broke into it
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayivke’uha* — like (Isaiah 7) “Let us go up against Judah and vex it and let us make a breach (*nevki’enah*) therein,” and likewise (Kings II, 3) “to break through (*lehavki’a*) unto the king of Edom.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotations are Isaiah 7:6 (JPS: “let us make a breach therein for us”) and 2 Kings 3:26 (JPS: “to break through unto the king of Edom”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: in process of time
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vekha’et tzet hakketz* — that end which the prophet told him.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: Compare the prophecy in 2 Chronicles 21:15 (JPS: “until thy bowels fall out by reason of the sickness, day by day”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: made no burning for him
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Velo asu lo ammo sereifah* — although he needed that burning, because he fell ill with evil sicknesses and his flesh stank, the Holy One, blessed be He, did not desire his honor that they make a burning for him; and he was not buried in the burial places of the kings either.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: he departed joyless
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Belo chemdah* — the interpretation: all his days he was in evil and in illnesses, and upon him was fulfilled (Deuteronomy 31), “See, I have set before thee this day life,” etc.; and also “few of days and full of trouble.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotations are Deuteronomy 30:15 (JPS: “See, I have set before thee this day life and good, and death and evil”; the printed number 31 is wrong) and Job 14:1 (JPS: “Man that is born of a woman is of few days, and full of trouble”). The way the first verse applies here is Rashi’s own.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Forty and two years old was Ahaziah when he began to reign
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ben arba’im ushtayim* — and in Kings (II, 28) he says “twenty and two years old.” How is this? According to this, the son was older than his father by two years. Rather, two years before Jehoram his father was born, this decree was decreed upon the house of David, that it be cut off with the house of Ahab, and so it says, “And the downfall of Ahaziah was of God,” etc.; and on the day that Asa married the daughter of Omri to Jehoshaphat his son, this decree was decreed; so it is taught in Seder Olam and in the Tosefta of Sotah. Yet in all the verses we do not find that Jehoshaphat married the daughter of Omri; but I found (Kings and above, 2, 18) “and he allied himself by marriage with Ahab,” and perhaps she was his sister whom he married. And in the thirty-first year of Asa he married her, as it is said (Kings I, 16), “And in the thirty-first year of Asa Omri reigned”; and when Asa married his daughter to Jehoshaphat his son, Omri was exalted and Tibni was killed; go and reckon from the thirty-third year of Asa until Ahaziah reigned, and you will find forty-two years. And furthermore, one verse says (in Kings II, 8), “In the twelfth year of Joram the son of Ahab, Ahaziah the son of Jehoram reigned,” and another verse says (there, 9), “And in the eighteenth year of Joram Ahaziah reigned”; perforce, Jehoram his father did not die until the twelfth year of Joram the son of Ahab, for it is written (there, 8), “In the fifth year of Joram the son of Ahab Jehoram the son of Jehoshaphat reigned,” and eight years he reigned; and what it says again, “in the eleventh year of Joram,” is because he reigned in his father’s lifetime one year, because his father was afflicted with severe illnesses, as it is written (above, 2, 21), “And after all this the LORD smote him,” etc., and the inhabitants of Jerusalem made Ahaziah his youngest son king one year in the lifetime of his father; and this is what is written, “in the eleventh year of Joram”; and what it said, “in the twelfth year of Joram,” is after his father died, when it was the twelfth of Joram.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: This comment is long and compressed and is translated as printed. The verses are 2 Kings 8:26 (JPS: “Two and twenty years old was Ahaziah”; the printed number 28 is wrong), 2 Chronicles 22:7, 2 Chronicles 18:1 (JPS: “he allied himself with Ahab by marriage”), 1 Kings 16:23 (JPS: “In the thirty and first year of Asa king of Judah began Omri to reign”), 1 Kings 16:22 (Tibni died), 2 Kings 8:25 (twelfth year), 2 Kings 9:29 (JPS: “in the eleventh year of Joram”; the printed “eighteenth” disagrees with the verse and with the same comment’s later “eleventh”), 2 Kings 8:16 (fifth year), and 2 Chronicles 21:18–19. Arithmetic: counting year thirty-three of Asa inclusive, years 33–41 are nine, plus Jehoshaphat’s twenty-five (1 Kings 22:42) and Jehoram’s eight (2 Chronicles 21:20) makes forty-two. A reign beginning in the fifth year and lasting eight years ends in the twelfth. The Seder Olam and Tosefta Sotah passages are not verified. Audit 5 source check: a passage with the same wording (11 consecutive words) is found in Seder Olam Rabbah 17.1 (Sefaria Hebrew text, labelled Public Domain). This is a wording match only; the translation was not changed.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the Arameans wounded Joram
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayyaku haRamim* — like *ha’Aramim*; in many places the *aleph* is lacking, for example *la’Amasa tomeru*; and sometimes the *aleph* is added to a word, for example (Psalms 89:1) *Eitan ha’Ezrachi*, like *haZarchi*; and the *aleph* of *ve’achavati be’aznekhem* (Job 13).
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The first example is 2 Samuel 19:14 (JPS: “And say you to Amasa”), where *tomeru* lacks the *aleph* of *te’meru*. The others are Psalm 89:1 (JPS: “Maschil of Ethan the Ezrahite”) and Job 13:17 (JPS: “let my declaration be in your ears”). The Hebrew spellings are not shown in JPS.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the wounds which they had given him
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki hammakkim asher hikkuhu* — the interpretation: from the wounds; and so in Kings (II, 8).
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The Kings verse is 2 Kings 8:29 (JPS: “of the wounds which the Arameans had given him at Ramah”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Azariah the son of Jehoram king of Judah
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’Azaryahu ben Yehoram* — this is Ahaziah, and so it says (there), “And Ahaziah king of Judah went down to see Joram.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 2 Kings 8:29 (JPS: “And Ahaziah the son of Jehoram king of Judah went down to see Joram the son of Ahab”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the downfall of Ahaziah
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Tevusat* — the interpretation: confusion, like (Ezekiel 16) “wallowing (*mitbosesset*) in thy blood.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Ezekiel 16:6 (JPS: “wallowing in thy blood”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the sons of the brethren of Ahaziah
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uvenei achei Achazyahu* — and the reason it did not say “and the brethren of Ahaziah” is that they were killed in the days of Jehoram their father, as it is written above (2, 21), “and they came up against Judah and broke into it,” and no son was left except Ahaziah, the youngest of his sons.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 2 Chronicles 21:17 (JPS: “there was never a son left him, save Jehoahaz, the youngest of his sons”), and 22:1 (JPS: “Ahaziah his youngest son”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: she arose and destroyed all the seed royal of the house of Judah
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vatakom vatedaber* — a term of *dever* (pestilence); and in Kings (II, 11) it is written *vate’abed* (“she destroyed”). And about this generation David said (Psalms 12), “For the Leader, on the Sheminith,” for he saw by the holy spirit that in the eighth generation all his seed would be killed by Athaliah, for from Solomon to here are eight generations; and he prayed that some of his seed be left as a remembrance, and he says (there), “Help, O LORD, for the godly man ceaseth,” etc. And in Kings (II, 11) it says that she killed them by a deadly drug, for it is written there, “and she stole him from among the king’s sons that were put to death (*hamumatim*),” and we read *hamomatim*; and there is a mother of the reading and a mother of the Masorah: *hamumatim* implies that they had already died; and the mother of the Masorah, *hamomatim*, implies that they were dying and going by suffering, a present-tense form, and not at once; and this is a death by sorcery and a deadly drug, that they do not die at once but go on being crushed by illnesses and then die; and an example is “They shall die of grievous deaths (*mamotei tachaluim*),” for these too do not die at once.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The verses are 2 Kings 11:1–2 and Psalm 12:1; the “eight generations” count is Rashi’s own and I did not check it. The final example corresponds to Jeremiah 16:4 (JPS: “They shall die of grievous deaths”); the printed form joins it to a phrase about famine. Statements about the written and read forms are not shown in JPS.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: in the bed-chamber
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Bechadar hamittot* — the Targum: *be’adron beit arsata*; that is, in the Court, in the sleeping chamber of the priests; and Rabbi Solomon, of blessed memory, explained: in the upper chamber of the Holy of Holies, as it is written in Kings (II, 10), “And he was with her hid in the house of the LORD,” etc.; and about it David said (Psalms 27:5), “For He shall hide me in His pavilion,” etc.; and he calls it the *chadar hamittot* (chamber of the beds) because of “betwixt my breasts shall he lie”; and this is what Kalir composed (Rabbi Eliezer called, and in the *Zikhronot* of the first day of Rosh Hashanah he composed this, on this account): “If he broke into the chamber of the beds, he broke the chamber of the beds, to atone; may He remember the destruction of the House, may He atone for you.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The attribution to Rabbi Solomon and the lines of Kalir are translated as printed and their wording is not clear to me. The verses are 2 Kings 11:3 (JPS: “And he was with her hid in the house of the LORD six years”; the printed number 10 is wrong), Psalm 27:5 (JPS: “He concealeth me in His pavilion”; the printed wording differs slightly) and Song of Songs 1:13 (JPS: “That lieth betwixt my breasts”). The Aramaic phrase is translated as printed.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: all the congregation made a covenant with the king in the house of God
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayikhrot kol hakahal brit bevet haElohim im hamelekh* — that they be to his help.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: that come in on the sabbath
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ba’ei hashabbat* — and also those who go out, as it is written nearby, “and they took every man his men, those that were to come in on the sabbath, with those that were to go out on the sabbath.” The courses were renewed on the Sabbath: one priestly and Levitical course going out and one coming in; and then Jehoiada kept there the going-out course with the coming-in course, and divided them into three parts.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: a third part shall be at the king’s house
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *VeHashelishit bevet hamelekh* — to guard so that they not gather against him to kill him.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: and a third part at the gate of the foundation
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *VeHashelishit* — this is the second.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the gate of the foundation
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Besha’ar haYesod* — and in Kings (II, 11) it is written “and at the gate Sur”; and in the Jerusalem Talmud, Yoma, it is explained that it had seven names: the gate of the foundation, Sur, because they purified the lepers there on the thumb of their hand, and because of “Depart ye! unclean! they cried unto them” (Lamentations 4).
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotations are 2 Kings 11:6 (JPS: “another third part was at the gate Sur”) and Lamentations 4:15 (JPS: “‘Depart you! unclean!’ men cried unto them”). I did not verify the Yoma passage.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: all the people shall keep the charge of the LORD
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vekhol ha’am yishmeru* — that they not enter the house of the LORD.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: every man with his weapons in his hand
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vekhelav beyado* — his weapons of war in his hand.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: for Jehoiada the priest dismissed not the courses
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ba’ei hashabbat im yotz’ei hashabbat ki lo patar* — those divisions of those going out, to go to their houses, but he held them there with those coming in. An example, “in the chambers, exempt,” that is, they were exempt from every work in the Court except to guard the chambers, for day and night it is incumbent on them in work to guard the Courts and the chambers; therefore they were exempt from all the rest of the work of the Court.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: I did not identify the Rabbinic source of the quotation “in the chambers, exempt.”

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: every man with his weapon in his hand
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’ish shilcho beyado* — his weapon of war, like “and they break through the weapons” (Joel).
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Joel 2:8 (JPS: “And they break through the weapons”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the crown
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *HaNezer* — it is the crown that David took from Rabbah of the children of Ammon, as it is written (above, 1, 20), “And David took the crown of Malcam,” and it was upon David’s head; and from then on the kings of Judah placed it, the *nezer*, upon their heads.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 1 Chronicles 20:2 (JPS: “And David took the crown of Malcam from off his head… and it was set upon David’s head”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the insignia
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’et ha’edut* — this is the Torah scroll, and so it says (Deuteronomy 17), “and he shall read therein all the days of his life”; and our Rabbis said: “the *nezer*” — this is the *edut* (testimony), for whoever is fit for kingship, it fits him, and whoever is not fit for kingship, it does not fit him.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Deuteronomy 17:19 (JPS: “and he shall read therein all the days of his life”). The Rabbinic saying is not verified.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the king stood on his platform at the entrance
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Omed al amudo* — as said (above, 2, 6), “And the king stood on the platform: for Solomon had made a brazen laver… and he stood upon it and knelt on his knees”; and to this day it is the custom, when they assemble together, the king or the duke stands in a high place so that they can see him and hear his word.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The second quotation is 2 Chronicles 6:13 (JPS: “Solomon had made a brazen scaffold… and upon it he stood, and kneeled down upon his knees”). I did not locate the first quotation in 2 Chronicles 6; similar words are in 2 Kings 11:14 and 23:3 (JPS: “the king stood on the platform”). The word “duke” is as printed.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Treason, treason
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Kesher keshar* — rebellion, rebellion.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: between the ranks
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *HaSederot* — the explanation: the place of the king’s entrance from his house to the house of the LORD; I do not know what the term *sederot* is; and Jonathan translated *sidriya*.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: Rashi himself says he does not know the term. The Aramaic phrase is translated as printed.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: whoso followeth her, let him be slain with the sword
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vehaba acharehah yumat* — do not let her go out by the exit of the Court to the city, lest she find helpers joining her.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: whoso followeth her
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vehaba acharehah* — to the Court.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: let him be slain
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Yumat* — they shall put him to death.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: So they made way for her
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayasimu lah yadayim* — a place to flee.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: made a covenant between himself, and all the people, and the king
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Brit beino uvein kol ha’am uvein hamelekh* — that all of them, the king and the people, would be after the LORD.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: appointed the offices of the house of the LORD
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Pekudot* — those appointed over this, to offer burnt-offerings and all that is said in the passage; an example (Jeremiah 20) “Now Pashhur heard,” etc., “and he was *pakid nagid* (chief officer) in the house of the LORD.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Jeremiah 20:1 (JPS: “Pashhur the son of Immer the priest, who was chief officer in the house of the LORD”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: that none that was unclean in any thing should enter in
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Velo yavo tamei lekhol davar* — and they were also officers, so that they would not let any unclean person enter the Court for any need at all.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: all the days of Jehoiada the priest
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Kol yemei Yehoyada* — and in Kings (II, 12) it is written, “all his days wherein Jehoiada the priest instructed him”; but after he died, then the king’s princes came to bow down to him, to make him holy; and in the Midrash it is explained: because he was hidden in the Holy of Holies and was not harmed, they said: you are fit to be a god.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 2 Kings 12:3 (JPS: “all his days wherein Jehoiada the priest instructed him”). I did not verify the Midrash.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: he begot sons and daughters
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayoled banim uvanot* — since it says below (24) that Joash killed the sons of Jehoiada, it was necessary to say that he had sons.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The reference is 2 Chronicles 24:25 (JPS: “for the blood of the sons of Jehoiada the priest”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: gather of all Israel money
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vekivtzu mikkol Yisra’el* — that is, gather that money that Israel gave year by year, as it is written (Exodus 30), “every one that passeth among them that are numbered,” and in Kings (II, 12), “all the money of the hallowed things that is brought into the house of the LORD, in current money,” etc.; for there were three monies: current money, the shekels each year, as it says, “every one that passeth among them that are numbered”: *over* (“passeth”) from *ha’over* (he who passes); “the money of the persons for whom each man is rated,” of a man who vowed the valuation of his person, like one who says “my valuation be upon me”; and “all the money that cometh into any man’s heart,” a freewill offering for the repair of the house.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The verses are Exodus 30:13 and 2 Kings 12:5 (JPS: “All the money of the hallowed things that is brought into the house of the LORD, in current money, the money of the persons for whom each man is rated, all the money that cometh into any man’s heart”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: see that you hasten the matter
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’attem temaharu ladavar velo mihheru haLevi’im* — it is explained well in Kings (II, 12), that the king said, “Let the priests take it to them, every man from his acquaintance,” and they were slow in the matter, to trouble their acquaintances; and when the king saw this he said to them (there), “And now take no longer money from your acquaintances, but for the repair of the house give it”; this is what it says here, “And you hasten the matter, but the Levites hastened it not.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotations are 2 Kings 12:6 (JPS: “let the priests take it to them, every man from him that bestoweth it upon him”) and 12:8 (JPS: “now therefore take no longer money from them that bestow it upon you”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the tax of Moses the servant of the LORD
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Massat Moshe eved HaShem* — that is, the shekels which he commanded in the wilderness.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the tax of Moses
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Massat* — from the name *Ki Tissa*.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The reference is to Exodus 30:12 (JPS: “When thou takest the sum of the children of Israel”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: For the sons of Athaliah, that wicked woman, had broken up the house of God
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki Atalyahu hammirsha’at banehah partzu* — it was necessary to say this because Solomon built it anew, a strong building; for from when Solomon built it until Joash there were only one hundred twenty-five years, and it had already been breached; and if not that Athaliah and her sons breached it, it would still have stood, for from Joash to Josiah is more than two hundred years, and they did not need to strengthen it until Josiah; and nevertheless Joash did not make it new as at first. And from the completion of the House to Joash, one hundred twenty-five: how? Solomon reigned forty years, and in the fourth year of his reign he began to build it, and for seven years he delayed in building it; that is ten years, and thirty remain; and Rehoboam reigned seventeen, that is forty-seven; and Abijah three, that is fifty; and Asa forty-one, that is ninety-one; and Jehoshaphat twenty-five, that is one hundred sixteen; Jehoram eight, that is one hundred twenty-four; and Ahaziah one, that is one hundred twenty-five. And from Joash to Josiah, how? Amaziah reigned twenty-nine years, Uzziah fifty-two, Jotham sixteen, Ahaz sixteen, Hezekiah twenty-nine, Manasseh fifty-five, and Amon two: that is two hundred less one; and those years more that Joash lived after the strengthening of the House. So it turns out that they would not have needed to strengthen the repair of the House, if not that wicked Athaliah and her sons had breached it.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The reign lengths agree with the verses: 1 Kings 6:1 (fourth year of Solomon), 1 Kings 14:21 (Rehoboam 17), 1 Kings 15:2 (Abijam 3), 15:10 (Asa 41), 22:42 (Jehoshaphat 25), 2 Chronicles 21:20 (Jehoram 8), 22:2 (Ahaziah one year), 2 Kings 14:2 (Amaziah 29), 15:2 (Azariah 52), 15:33 (Jotham 16), 16:2 (Ahaz 16), 18:2 (Hezekiah 29), 21:1 (Manasseh 55), 21:19 (Amon 2). Arithmetic as printed: 3 + 7 = 10, 40 − 10 = 30, 30 + 17 + 3 + 41 + 25 + 8 + 1 = 125; and 29 + 52 + 16 + 16 + 29 + 55 + 2 = 199, which is “two hundred less one.” The first step counts three years before the building began plus seven years of building.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: all the hallowed things of the house of the LORD did they bestow upon the Baalim
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki Atalyahu vegomer* — therefore it is no wonder if it needed repair so quickly; and also do not wonder that there was no silver and gold of the hallowed things in the treasuries of the house of the LORD, so that they had to give a proclamation in Judah and Jerusalem to bring the tax; for they made even all the hallowed things of the house of the LORD for the Baalim.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: they made a chest
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vaya’asu aron echad* — and in Kings (II, 12) it is written “and bored a hole in its door”; through that hole they would throw the dedicated things into the chest, and not open the door, lest a cheat come and steal from it.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The Kings verse is 2 Kings 12:10 (JPS: “bored a hole in the lid of it”). The printed word is “door.”

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: set it without at the gate of the house of the LORD
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayitnuhu besha’ar bet HaShem chutzah* — so that every one of generous heart could come to it to give the offering of the LORD.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: and when they saw that there was much money
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vekhir’otam ki rav hakesef* — then the king’s scribe came.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the chief priest’s officer
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ufekid kohen rosh* — a servant appointed under the chief priest, and he is the deputy of the priesthood, with the king’s scribe; and in Kings (there) it is written, “and the king’s scribe and the high priest came up”: the interpretation: the king’s scribe came up, and the high priest also sent his officer, who is the scribe who writes what the high priest commands him; for it is not fitting, nor an honor to the high priest, to go with the king’s servants.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The Kings verse is 2 Kings 12:11 (JPS: “the king’s scribe and the high priest came up”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: emptied the chest
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vaye’aru et ha’aron* — an example, “and she emptied (*vatar*) her pitcher” (Genesis 24).
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Genesis 24:20 (JPS: “and emptied her pitcher into the trough”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: and took it
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayis’ahu* — every day, when they saw that the money in it was much, they would bring it to the king’s officer inside the Court, empty it, carry it, and return it to its place at the gate of the LORD outside.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the work was perfected by them
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vata’al arukhah lamelakhah* — an example, “Will they revive the stones?” (Ezra), and also above (1 Chronicles) “and Joab revived the rest of the city.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The first quotation is in Nehemiah, not Ezra, at Nehemiah 3:34 (JPS: “will they revive the stones out of the heaps of rubbish”); the printed name is Ezra. The second is 1 Chronicles 11:8 (JPS: “Joab repaired the rest of the city”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: in its state
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Al matkunto* — on its foundation.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: vessels wherewith to minister, and buckets
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Kelei sharet vehe’olot* — *teshil* in German, in which they pound the spices in a mortar; an example (Proverbs 27) “Though thou shouldest bray a fool in a mortar”; so Rabbi Isaac bar Samuel of Narbonne told me; and some say *ve’ha’olot* are the boards on which they cut meat, and an example in Beitzah: “one does not carry the block (*ha’ali*) to cut meat upon it.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed word is a glossed German form; I could not confirm it and left it as printed. The printed abbreviation בל"א is read as “in German.” The quotation is Proverbs 27:22 (JPS: “Though thou shouldest bray a fool in a mortar with a pestle”). I did not verify the Beitzah passage.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: and vessels of gold and silver
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vekhappot vekhelei zahav vekhasef* — and in Kings (II, 12) it is written, “But there were not made for the house of the LORD cups of silver”; how so? It is explained in *Ketuvo(t)*, in the first chapter: Rav Huna asked Rav: “The vessels of service — may they be made from the hallowed things of the repair of the House?” etc.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed abbreviation בכתובו' is left as printed, and I could not confirm which source is meant. The Kings verse is 2 Kings 12:14 (JPS: “there were not made for the house of the LORD cups of silver”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: he stood above the people
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Me’al la’am* — higher than all the people, in order to make his voice heard; and in Eichah Rabbati he expounds: he relied on himself, for he was a prince higher than all the people, prophet and priest, and on the Day of Atonement, and the son-in-law of the king, and he was not afraid to speak prophecy; and about this it is said (Lamentations 2), “Shall the priest and the prophet be slain in the sanctuary of the LORD?”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Lamentations 2:20 (JPS: “Shall the priest and the prophet be slain in the sanctuary of the Lord?”). I did not verify the Eichah Rabbati passage.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: The LORD look upon it, and require it
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uvemoto amar yere HaShem veyidrosh* — for they did not kill me except because I spoke the mission of the Omnipresent, and since I am slain for it, justly and rightly, it is fitting that He require my blood; and so it was, for at once his blood was required, “at the turn of the year,” etc.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the year was come about
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayehi litkufat hashanah* — because the sons of Judah sinned more than the rest of the tribes, as it said above, “and they forsook the house of the LORD, the God of their fathers.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 2 Chronicles 24:18 (JPS: “And they forsook the house of the LORD, the God of their fathers”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: destroyed all the princes of the people from among the people
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayashchitu et kol sarei ha’am* — it refers back to above, “And after the death of Jehoiada came the princes of Judah, and bowed down to the king,” and caused Joash to sin after them; for this they were repaid their reward, that the army of Aram came and destroyed all the princes of the people.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quoted verse is 2 Chronicles 24:17.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: from among the people
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Me’am* — from being a people.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: for the blood of the sons of Jehoiada the priest
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Bedemei benei Yehoyada* — because of the blood of Zechariah, who was the son of Jehoiada, for he should have remembered the favor and kindness which Jehoiada did with him, and for that sin his servants conspired against him and slew him on his bed; they measured to him measure for measure: for Zechariah was killed quiet and at ease and trusting that he had nothing to worry about, since he was the son of Jehoiada and in his honor they would treat him with respect, and they spilled his blood to the ground; and therefore he too was killed in peace and quiet on his bed.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Shimrith the Moabitess
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *HaMo’avit* — what is it to me who they were and from whom they came, whether from the children of Israel or from the Moabites? Rather, ungrateful ones would come — those who denied the kindness of Abraham our father to Lot their father, who fought with the kings when he heard that Lot was taken captive, and they hired Balaam to curse his sons — and exact payment from Joash, who denied the kindness of Jehoiada and killed Zechariah his son. So it is explained in the Mekhilta.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: I did not verify the Mekhilta passage.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: for the LORD is not with Israel, even with all the children of Ephraim
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki ein HaShem im Yisra’el kol benei Efrayim* — because Jeroboam was of the tribe of Ephraim, and he was the first who caused Israel to sin, and in every generation after him they were a snare, for they served the golden calves of Jeroboam.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: But if thou wilt go
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki im ba attah* — the interpretation: if you do not believe my words, will you not try it? Go, and act, and be strong for the battle.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: for God hath power to help, and to cast down
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *La’azor ulehakhshil* — the interpretation: He has power and might to help you without the army of Ephraim, and to cause you to stumble if you take them with you.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: that they all were broken in pieces
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vekhullam nivke’u* — “And it came to pass after Amaziah came,” etc.; in Eichah Rabbati it is said of him, “he rages and laughs, and there is no rest” (Proverbs 29).
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Proverbs 29:9 (JPS: “Whether he be angry or laugh, there will be no rest”). The verse quoted at the start is 2 Chronicles 25:14. I did not verify the Eichah Rabbati passage.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: fell upon the cities of Judah, from Samaria even unto Beth-horon
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayifshetu be’arei Yehudah miShomron ve’ad Beit Choron* — after they had returned to their place, as above, “and their anger was greatly kindled against Judah, and they returned home”; for if it were not so, but immediately upon their separation from Amaziah they fell upon the cities of Judah, he should have said, “from Beth-horon unto Samaria.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 2 Chronicles 25:10 (JPS: “wherefore their anger was greatly kindled against Judah, and they returned home in fierce anger”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: God hath determined to destroy thee
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki ya’atz Elohim lehashchitekha* — that is, if you do not listen to my counsel to go in a straight way, know, O king, that the LORD has determined to destroy you since you did this and did not listen to the counsel; and what is the counsel? That which advised you to provoke the king of Israel and fall before him, as it is written, “Then Amaziah king of Judah took advice, and sent to Joash,” etc.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 2 Chronicles 25:17 (JPS: “Then Amaziah king of Judah took advice, and sent to Joash”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: let us look one another in the face
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lekh nitra’eh fanim* — to show our might on horses with spears.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: The thistle that was in Lebanon
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *HaChoach asher baLevanon* — which is low of spirit.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: to the cedar that was in Lebanon
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Shalach el ha’Erez* — which is a prince greater than all the trees.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: trod down the thistle
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vata’avor* — and trod down; and the cedar did not wish to kill it, for it was contemptible in his eyes to devour the thistle, but passed by it and trod it down as a disgrace; for how did his heart carry him to send such great shame to a high cedar? You too are like a thistle, for you have only two tribes, and now my servants will rise up against you and trample you when they hear this insult.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: will thy heart therefore lift thee up to glory therein
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Venissa’akha libbekha* — to pursue glory, and you wish to be honored even over me; and in Kings (II, 14), “Be honored, and stay at home.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The Kings verse is 2 Kings 14:10 (JPS: “and will thy heart lift thee up? glory therein, and remain at home”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: that He might deliver them into the hand [of their enemies]
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki meha’Elohim hi lema’an titam beyad* — that is, into their hands, as above, “I know that God hath determined to destroy thee.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 2 Chronicles 25:16 (JPS: “I know that God hath determined to destroy thee”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: at Beth-shemesh, which belongeth to Judah
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *BeVeit Shemesh* — the war was there, and it was necessary to say this lest you say, when they seized Amaziah, why did they bring him to Jerusalem and not to Samaria? Because Beth-shemesh was near Jerusalem.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: broke down the wall of Jerusalem
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayifrotz bechomat* — for he said: Henceforth he will not rebel against me, for his heart would not be so lifted up as to rebel, since the wall is breached.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: with Obed-edom
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Hanimtza’im beveit haElohim im Oved Edom* — for he and his sons were in charge of the treasures all their days, as above.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: Compare 1 Chronicles 26:15 (JPS: “To Obed-edom southward; and to his sons the Storehouse”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the hostages also
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’et benei hata’arubot* — for Israel did not let Amaziah be king again in Jerusalem until he gave the sons of the princes as a pledge (*eravon*) that they would not rebel against him again; and so Jonathan translated it in Kings (II, 14), *bnei rabrevaya*; and Rabbi Joseph explained *ta’arubot* as those pledges that the king had been given in surety so that their fathers would not rebel against him; and it does not seem right to me, for we do not find that the hand of Judah prevailed so much over others that they would need to give Judah their sons as a pledge.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The Kings verse is 2 Kings 14:14 (JPS: “the hostages also”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Now from the time that Amaziah did turn away from following the LORD
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Umei’et asher sar Amatzyah me’acharei HaShem* — and he fell before the king of Israel, immediately “they made a conspiracy against him in Jerusalem” to kill him, for their hearts were sick, each for his son and his brother and his kinsman who had been killed by him, because he provoked the king of Israel.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: he fled to Lachish
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayanas Lakhishah* — a fortress city against which Sennacherib fought; and he fled to Lachish and was there fifteen years until they sent after him to Lachish and killed him there; and those fifteen years that he was in Lachish, Yechalyah, the mother of Uzziah, reigned in his place. But it is difficult for me, and in the commentary of Rabbi Joseph, of blessed memory, I saw: those fifteen years that he was in Lachish, his son Uzziah reigned in his place; and it is not right to interpret so, for it is written nearby, “and he was sixteen years old,” so at the time his father fled he was only a year old; and furthermore, if so he should have said, “and they took Uzziah and made him king in place of his father in his lifetime”; but it implies that he did not reign in his father’s lifetime.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The verses are 2 Kings 14:17 (Amaziah “lived after the death of Jehoash… fifteen years”), 14:19 (“he fled to Lachish”), 2 Kings 18:14 (Hezekiah sent to the king of Assyria at Lachish), and 2 Chronicles 26:1 (JPS: “Uzziah, who was sixteen years old”). The verses do not say that Amaziah spent the fifteen years at Lachish. Arithmetic as printed: sixteen minus fifteen makes one year.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: according to all that his father Amaziah had done
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vaya’as hayashar be’einei HaShem* — all the right that his father did, he did, but he did not do like his wickedness.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: in the days of Zechariah
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Bimei Zekharyahu* — this is Uzziah; and three names were called to him: Uzziah, Zechariah, Azariah; and an example (Kings II, 12) Jehoahaz — Ahaziah.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: I could not match the printed reference for the last example; the identification of Jehoahaz and Ahaziah appears in 2 Chronicles 21:17 and 22:1.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: who had understanding in the vision of God
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *HaMevin bir’ot haElohim* — that he understood in the fear of God that it is good, and feared the LORD.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: Rashi reads the printed *bir’ot* (“in the vision of”) as “in the fear of.”

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Uzziah built towers in Jerusalem at the corner gate
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayiven Uzziyahu migdalim vegomer* — he needed to strengthen what had been breached in the wall in the days of his father.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: husbandmen
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ikkarim* — *aratori* in Old French.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The Old French form printed in Hebrew letters could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: vinedressers
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vekhoremim* — an example (there, 2, 25), “to be vinedressers and husbandmen”; he had keepers of cattle.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 2 Kings 25:12 (JPS: “to be vinedressers and husbandmen”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: for he loved husbandry
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki ohev adamah hayah* — it is explained in Bereshit Rabbah, chapter 2: two were eager after the ground (*adamah*), and no benefit was found in them — he and Cain.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: I did not verify the Bereshit Rabbah passage. The printed abbreviation ב"ר is read as Bereshit Rabbah.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: engines, invented by skilful men
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Chishbonot machshevet choshev* — an example (Exodus 28) “the work of the skilful workman”; he made instruments of war by craft, such as a siege tower and battering rams striking the wall, as it is written (Proverbs 24), “for with wise advice thou shalt make thy war.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The Exodus phrase is “the work of the skilful workman” (Exodus 28:6, 15) and the Proverbs verse is 24:6 (JPS: “For with wise advice thou shalt make thy war”). The word *dik* is left as printed.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: he trespassed against the LORD his God
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayim’al baShem Elohav* — here it is fitting to say *me’ilah* (trespass), for he did it in error; an example (Leviticus 5), “If any one commit a trespass and sin through error.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Leviticus 5:15 (JPS: “If any one commit a trespass, and sin through error, in the holy things of the LORD”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: went into the temple of the LORD to burn incense upon the altar of incense
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayavo el heikhal HaShem* — for he said: it is fitting for a king to serve the King of glory.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: he had a censer in his hand to burn incense
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uvyado miktert lehaktir* — and he wished to strike with it the priest who prevented him from burning incense.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: dwelt in a house set apart
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Beit hachofshit* — and in the Jerusalem Talmud it is explained: he made himself a house in the cemetery, because of “Set apart (*chofshi*) among the dead” (Psalms 88).
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Psalm 88:6 (JPS: “Set apart among the dead”). I did not verify the Jerusalem Talmud passage.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: he was cut off from the house of the LORD
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki nigzar* — to him, from entering again among people; an example (Megillah 2), “and what was decreed against her.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Esther 2:1 (JPS: “and what was decreed against her”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: in the field of burial which belonged to the kings
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Bisdeh hakeverah* — and not in the cave with the kings.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: according to all that his father Uzziah had done
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Kekhol asher asah Uzziyahu aviv* — the good things that his father did. And this is what Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai said in tractate Sukkah: Were Abraham our father to accept upon himself all the iniquities of the generations until him, I would accept upon myself the sins of the generations from Abraham until me; and if Jotham son of Uzziah were with me, we would accept upon ourselves from Abraham to the end of the generations. For among all the kings before him and after him we find sin in them except Jotham: David — only in Uriah the Hittite; Solomon — his wives turned his heart; Rehoboam — forsook the Torah of the LORD; Abijah — “and walked in all the sins of his father”; Asa — brought out silver and gold from the treasuries of the house of the LORD, and Hanani the prophet [was put in] the prison-house; Jehoshaphat — joined with the wicked; Jehoram — killed his brothers; Ahaziah — his mother his counsellor to do wickedly; Joash — killed Zechariah and became holy; Amaziah — bowed down to the idols of Seir; Uzziah — entered the Temple to burn incense; Ahaz — walked in the ways of the kings of Israel and also made pillars for the Baalim; Hezekiah — his heart was lifted up and there was wrath upon him, and for three they did not acknowledge him; Manasseh — did evil in the eyes of the LORD; Josiah — did not hear words of prophecy from the mouth of God; Zedekiah — did evil in the eyes of the LORD and did not humble himself before Jeremiah; but of Jotham nothing blameworthy was found. (So Rabbi Eleazar bar Moses told me.)
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The phrases “became holy” (of Joash) and “for three they did not acknowledge him” (of Hezekiah) are translated as printed and their sense is not clear to me. The quotation of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai is translated as printed; I did not verify it against the Talmud text. The verses correspond to 1 Kings 15:5 (David: “save only in the matter of Uriah the Hittite”) and 15:3 (Abijam: “he walked in all the sins of his father”), 2 Chronicles 21:4 (Jehoram slew all his brethren), 22:3 (“his mother was his counsellor to do wickedly”), 25:14 (Amaziah and the gods of Seir), 26:16 (Uzziah), 28:2 (Ahaz: JPS “made also molten images for the Baalim”; the printed word is “pillars”), 32:25 (“his heart was lifted up; therefore there was wrath upon him”), 35:22 (Josiah “hearkened not unto the words of Neco, from the mouth of God”) and 36:12 (Zedekiah “humbled not himself before Jeremiah”). The reference to Asa is 2 Chronicles 16:2 and 16:10 (“the prison-house”); I did not look up the verses for Rehoboam, Joash or Manasseh. Audit 5 source check: a passage with the same wording (5 consecutive words) is found in Mishnah Pesachim 4.9 (Sefaria Hebrew text, labelled Public Domain). This is a wording match only; the translation was not changed.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the people did yet corruptly
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’od ha’am mashchitim* — as it is written (in Kings II, 9), “the people still sacrificed and burnt incense.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 2 Kings 15:35 (JPS: “the people still sacrificed and offered in the high places”); the printed number 9 is wrong.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: on the wall of Ophel he built much
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uvechomat ha’Ofel* — an example (Isaiah 32) *Ofel uvachan*; and in *bachan* he built strongholds.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Isaiah 32:14 (JPS: “The mound and the tower”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: castles and towers
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uvachorashim banah biraniyyot* — a term for a great *birah* (fortress).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Maaseiah the king’s son
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Et Ma’asehu ben hamelekh* — Ahaz; Zichri the mighty man of Ephraim killed him.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed sentence is translated literally; “the king’s son” is not identified further.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Azrikam the ruler of the house
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’et Azrikam* — “and… and,” an example (Genesis 36), “Aiah and Anah,” and likewise “both chariot and horse” (Psalms 76).
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The point of the comparison is not clear to me. The quotations are Genesis 36:24 (JPS: “Aiah and Anah”) and Psalm 76:7 (JPS: “the riders also and the horses”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the men that have been mentioned by name
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayakumu ha’anashim asher nikvu veshemot* — above, who are those men? They are of the heads of the children of Ephraim: Azariah son of Jehohanan and his companions.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The reference is 2 Chronicles 28:12.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: all that were naked among them
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vekhol ma’arumeihem* — from *arom* and *eryah* (naked).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the Lowland, and of the South of Judah
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *UFelishtim pashetu be’arei hashfelah vehaNegev* — which is opposite them, as it is written, “and the Canaanite dwelleth by the sea.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Numbers 13:29 (JPS: “and the Canaanite dwelleth by the sea”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: he had cast away restraint in Judah
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki hifria beYehudah* — an example (Exodus 32), “for Aaron had let them loose (*pera’oh*),” and “when men let grow their hair (*bifro’a pera’ot*)” (Judges 5).
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotations are Exodus 32:25 (JPS: “Aaron had let them loose”) and Judges 5:2 (JPS: “When men let grow their hair in Israel”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Tillegath-pilneser king of Assyria came unto him
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayavo alav* — for he had sent after him to help him, as it is written in Kings (II, 16), “And Ahaz sent messengers to Tiglath-pileser.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 2 Kings 16:7 (JPS: “So Ahaz sent messengers to Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: distressed him
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayatzer lo* — from what he apportioned to him: the house of the LORD and the king’s house, etc.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: Compare 2 Chronicles 28:21.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: but it helped him not
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Velo le’ezrah lo* — although we find in Kings (there), “And the king of Assyria went up against Damascus and took it, and carried the people of it captive to Kir, and slew Rezin,” he was not a help to him so as to strengthen him and return to him the cities which the Philistines had taken from him.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 2 Kings 16:9 (JPS: “went up against Damascus, and took it, and carried the people of it captive to Kir, and slew Rezin”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: shut up the doors of the house of the LORD
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayisgor et daltot Beit HaShem* — so that the priests would not come to do their service in the Tent of Meeting, but would come to the altars that he made in every corner of Jerusalem; and Hezekiah opened the doors of the house of the LORD because his father had shut the doors of the house of the LORD.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: opened the doors of the house of the LORD, and repaired them
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayechazzekem* — because Ahaz had cut off all the vessels of the house of God.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: Compare 2 Chronicles 28:24 (JPS: “cut in pieces the vessels of the house of God”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: carry forth the filthiness out of the holy place
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vehotzi’u et hannidah* — idolatry; “the dead” is not said here, but *niddah*, and it is more loathsome than a whole lying corpse; an example, “as the uncleanness of the menstruant,” for menstrual blood is loathsome and putrid.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The phrase is Ezekiel 36:17 (JPS: “as the uncleanness of a woman in her impurity”); the printed text does not name the verse.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: and have not burned incense nor offered burnt-offerings in the holy place unto the God of Israel
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayekhabbu et hanerot… ve’olah lo he’elu* — but to other gods they made high places in every city to burn incense to them.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: be not now negligent
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Al tishlu* — a term of error.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: went in unto the inner part of the house of the LORD
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayavo’u haKohanim lifnimah* — for it is not for the Levites to enter inside.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: into the court of the house of the LORD
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lechatzer Beit HaShem* — the place where the Levites stood, as it says, “And the Levites took it,” etc., “and they began on the first of the month.”

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: they sanctified the house of the LORD in eight days
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayekadshu et Beit HaShem leyamim shemonah* — they delayed in the purification to purify so much because Ahaz had painted all the walls with images of *maskit*, as it is written (Ezekiel 23), “the images of the Chaldeans engraved with *shashar*”; and they delayed eight days until they had destroyed the likeness of the images from the walls; and on the sixteenth day of the month the whole House and the Court were finished.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Ezekiel 23:14 (JPS: “the images of the Chaldeans portrayed with vermilion”); the printed word is “engraved.” The dates are in 2 Chronicles 29:17.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: have we prepared and sanctified
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Hekhanu vehikdashnu* — it is explained in Avodah Zarah, in the chapter of Rabbi Ishmael: Vessels that were used in the house of Hanyo — what is the law? etc., until: He raised an objection: “which king Ahaz in his reign did cast away… have we prepared and sanctified” — is it not that “prepared” means that we immersed them, and “sanctified” that we sanctified them? He said to him: Blessed are you to Heaven, that you returned my loss! “Prepared” — that we hid them; “sanctified” — that we sanctified others in their place.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The Talmudic Aramaic is translated as printed and the name “house of Hanyo” is left as printed. I did not verify the Talmudic passage. The Aramaic phrase is translated as printed.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: and seven he-goats
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vetzefirei izzim vegomer* — it was a temporary ruling.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: to offer them on the altar of the LORD
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Al mizbach HaShem* — and not on those altars that Ahaz his father had made.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: to make atonement for all Israel
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lekhapper al kol Yisra’el* — for they had sinned with idolatry; so the king said: let the burnt-offering and the sin-offering be for all Israel. In the portion *Shelach Lekha* (Numbers 15) it is written, “and all the congregation shall offer a young bullock,” etc., and it is written (Leviticus 4), “and the assembly shall offer a young bullock for a sin-offering”; and here it is written, “And they brought seven bullocks, and seven rams, and seven lambs, and seven he-goats”; rather, it was a temporary ruling.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The verses are Numbers 15:24 (JPS: “all the congregation shall offer one young bullock for a burnt-offering”) and Leviticus 4:14 (JPS: “the assembly shall offer a young bullock for a sin-offering”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: for the commandment was of the LORD by His prophets
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki beyad HaShem hamitzvah beyad nevi’av* — to sing by the Levites with instruments of song: it is not written in the Torah that an offering requires song; rather it is the commandment of the LORD which He commanded by His prophets, to sing over the offering. And our Rabbis explained in tractate Arakhin: Whence that the Levites are required to sing with instruments of song? For it is written, “the service of service.” What service needs another service with it? Say: this is song with instruments of song. “And the service of burden” (there) — it is right to explain it of song, as it is written (above, 1, 15), “And Chenaniah, chief of the Levites, was over the *massa*,” for he was skilled, being appointed to raise the voice of the melody of the song.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The verses are Numbers 4:47 (JPS: “the work of service, and the work of bearing burdens”) and 1 Chronicles 15:22 (JPS: “Chenaniah, chief of the Levites, was over the song; he was master in the song, because he was skilful”). I did not verify the Arakhin passage.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the priests with the trumpets
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *VeHakohanim bachatzotzerot* — as it is written, “And the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall blow with the trumpets” (Numbers 10).
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Numbers 10:8 (JPS: “the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall blow with the trumpets”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: to sing praises unto the LORD with the words of David
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lehallel laShem bedivrei David* — this is “Give thanks to the LORD, call upon His name,” as it is written above (1, 16), “Then on that day did David first ordain to give thanks,” etc.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 1 Chronicles 16:7 (JPS: “Then on that day did David first ordain to give thanks unto the LORD”); the words “Give thanks to the LORD, call upon His name” are 1 Chronicles 16:8.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: brought in sacrifices and thank-offerings
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayavi’u hakahal zevachim vetodot* — things permitted to their owners for eating.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: brought burnt-offerings
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vekhol nedivei lev olot* — some of them, whose heart volunteered, brought burnt-offerings, and not all, because the owners have no permission to eat from them.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the consecrated things
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vehakkodashim* — lesser holy things, sacrifices and peace-offerings, from which the owners benefit.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: But the priests were too few
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Rak haKohanim hayu lema’at* — that is, those who had sanctified were still few; and their brethren the Levites strengthened them until the work was finished and until the priests sanctified themselves. And if you say: how is it that the Levites sanctified themselves and the priests did not sanctify themselves? it explains: because the Levites were upright in heart to sanctify themselves more than the priests. And the priests and the Levites and all who feared the Name were disguising and hiding themselves, and even concealing themselves, all the days of the wicked kings; and when Hezekiah, who was righteous, came, they could not at once sanctify and purify themselves, for this was in the first year of his reign, and they came and sanctified themselves little by little, as it is written (Proverbs 28), “When the righteous exult, there is great glory; but when the wicked rise, a man is hidden,” and it is written (there), “When the wicked rise, men hide themselves; but when they perish, the righteous increase”: that is, when the wicked Ahaz rises, a man hides himself; and when they perish, the righteous increase — Hezekiah and his company.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotations are Proverbs 28:12 and 28:28 (JPS: “When the wicked rise, men hide themselves; But when they perish, the righteous increase”); the printed form of 28:12 reads *yechuppas adam* (“a man is hidden”), where JPS reads “men must be sought for.”

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: that which God had prepared for the people
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Al hehakhin haElohim la’am* — to serve Him and to do His will; an example below (30, 19), “every one that setteth his heart (*hekhin*)”; and also they rejoiced because the thing came upon them suddenly, in the first year of his reign, to return to the LORD, and they returned at once.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 2 Chronicles 30:19.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: wrote letters also to Ephraim and Manasseh
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vegam igerot katav al Efrayim uMenasheh vegomer* — for they had not yet gone into exile, since this was in the first year of his reign, and they did not go into exile until the sixth of his reign, as it is written (in Kings II, 18), “And at the end of three years they took it, in the sixth year of Hezekiah, which was the ninth year of Hoshea king of Israel,” as you will find written at the end of the book.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 2 Kings 18:10 (JPS: “And at the end of three years they took it; even in the sixth year of Hezekiah, which was the ninth year of Hoshea king of Israel, Samaria was taken”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: they could not keep it at that time
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki lo yakholu la’asoto ba’et hahi* — in the first month, in Nisan.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the priests had not sanctified themselves in sufficient number
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki haKohanim lo hitkadshu lemaddai* — they had sanctified enough for Israel to offer their Passover offerings with them; and there is no need to say that they could not do it in Nisan, for they had not finished sanctifying the House until the sixteenth of Nisan; and so the interpretation of “they could not keep it at that time” is: even if they had not delayed the purification of the House, which was not finished until the sixteenth of Nisan, we could not have done it now, because the priests had not sanctified themselves in sufficient number.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: neither had the people gathered themselves together to Jerusalem
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Veha’am lo ne’esafu* — still, all of them to Jerusalem.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: from Beer-sheba even to Dan
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *MiBe’er Sheva ve’ad Dan* — this is the territory of the ten tribes.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: for they had not kept it in great numbers according as it is written
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki lo larov* — the interpretation: for many years had passed in which it had not been done according to its rule.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: that He may return to the remnant that are escaped of you out of the hand of the kings of Assyria
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Veyashuv el happeletah hanish’eret lakhem mikkaf malkhei Ashur* — although they had not yet been exiled, he calls them a remnant, because in their eyes it was counted as though they had already been exiled; and furthermore the kings of Assyria had seized everything in the days of Ahaz; and that it was in their eyes as if they had been exiled, because for six years Israel were servants to the king of Assyria, bearers of tribute, and he ruled over them and carried them into exile and did with them as he wished, and this was within those six years, and they had already gone into exile several times in the days of the kings of Israel and of Ahaz; and they knew that as soon as Israel rebelled against the king of Assyria he would carry them into exile; and to them he calls “the remnant of Assyria,” because he did not rule over them nor over all the land of Judah.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The reasoning is compressed and is translated as printed. The “six years” is not stated in the verses I checked; compare 2 Kings 17:3 (JPS: “Hoshea became his servant, and brought him presents”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: And be not you like your fathers, and like your brethren
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’al tihyu ka’avotekhem* — the interpretation: and if you say, we still trust that the king of Assyria will go up from us, do not be like your fathers, every generation that was before you; and what happened to them when they forsook the LORD and trespassed against Him, and He gave them up to desolation, as you see.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: your brethren and your children shall find compassion before them that led them captive
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Atah al taksu orpekhem vegomer… beshuvkhem al HaShem acheikhem uvneikhem yihyu lerachamim lifnei shoveihem* — even those few who had already been exiled, who fought with Israel and overcame them and carry off their sons and their daughters into captivity; and if you return to Him, He will give them to compassion before their captors, that they return to this land; for gracious and merciful is the LORD your God.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: all the altars for incense
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *HaMiktarot* — the place where priests and Levites were.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The explanation is translated as printed and its sense is not clear to me.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the priests and the Levites were ashamed
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *VeHakohanim vehaLevi’im nikhlemu* — for they had delayed to sanctify themselves, and therefore they delayed so long from coming until now, because they could not believe this thing before, since Ahaz had cast off priests; and thus they were saying: Is it possible that yesterday Ahaz served idolatry, and his son Hezekiah at once, in the first year, at once in the first month, says to the priests and the Levites to serve the one God alone, and will need us? And for this they were slow and neglectful in coming; and the rest of Judah likewise, whom Ahaz before him had cast off; and when they examined and understood the matter, that everything was for the sake of Heaven, they came and all sanctified themselves.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the priests dashed the blood
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *HaKohanim zorekim* — for from the receiving onward is the commandment of the priesthood; and do not wonder why the owners did not themselves slaughter, for it is written nearby, “For there were many in the congregation that had not sanctified themselves,” and the Levites were in charge of slaughtering their Passover offerings.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: for every one that was not clean
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lekhol lo tahor* — for the Levite was in his place to sanctify to the LORD.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: yet did they eat the passover otherwise than it is written
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki akhelu et hapesach belo kakkatuv* — not according to the rule, for they ate it in uncleanness, for Hezekiah prayed for them, etc.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: every one that setteth his heart to seek God
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Kol levavo hekhin* — so it is explained in the Baraita of Rabbi Eliezer son of Rabbi Jose the Galilean, which begins: Wherever you find the words of Rabbi Eliezer son of Rabbi Jose the Galilean in the Aggadah, make your ear like a funnel, as it is said (Proverbs 20), “to make thine ear attend to understanding”; it is expounded from the thirty-two rules of the Aggadah, and this is one of them: *nechlak hasseder* (the order is divided). Such as this: “The good LORD pardon every one that setteth his heart to seek God” — that is, “the good LORD pardon” “every one who set his heart to seek God, to make his Passover, to bring his offering, even though they did not do it in the purity of the sanctuary”; for they had not cleansed themselves; and Judah all were cleansed because they were near Jerusalem and could purify themselves and sanctify and return to Jerusalem; but a multitude of Ephraim, Manasseh, Issachar, Zebulun — they had not so much transgression in the matter, because for them the thing was distant by letters; they did not have to wait and delay coming until they sanctified; therefore they came and were not purified; and since their fault was not great, therefore “may He pardon for them”; and so (Isaiah 35) “The wilderness and the parched land shall be glad,” etc.: it is *nechlak hasseder*.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The Baraita’s rule and its application are compressed and are translated as printed. The Proverbs quotation is closest to Proverbs 2:2 (JPS: “So that thou make thine ear attend unto wisdom, And thy heart incline to discernment”); I could not match the printed reference “20.” The Isaiah verse is 35:1 (JPS: “The wilderness and the parched land shall be glad”). Audit 5 source check: a passage with the same wording (7 consecutive words) is found in Tosefta Sotah 7.13 (Sefaria Hebrew text, labelled Public Domain). This is a wording match only; the translation was not changed.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: singing with loud instruments unto the LORD
