2 Chronicles.english_translation: *VeHakohanim bikhlei oz* — with trumpets.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: that were well skilled in the service of the LORD
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *HaMaskilim sekhel tov laShem* — in regard to song, it is fitting to say the term *sekhel*, as it is said (above, 1, 26), “And the lot came out eastward to Shelemiah; and Zechariah his son, a counsellor with understanding”; and Hezekiah spoke to their hearts comforts and good words to strengthen them and to help them, so that they too would be strong in song, who were “well skilled in the service of the LORD.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 1 Chronicles 26:14 (JPS: “And the lot eastward fell to Shelemiah. Then for Zechariah his son, a discreet counsellor”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: giving thanks to the LORD
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Mitvaddim laShem* — over a thanksgiving offering, and giving thanks to the LORD for the miracle He did for them, for a thanksgiving offering comes on account of a miracle.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: to keep other seven days
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Shiv’at yamim acherim* — as it is explained, “and they kept other seven days with gladness.”

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: did give to the congregation for offerings
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Herim lakahal* — from his flock and from his herd.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: a thousand bullocks and seven thousand sheep
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lakahal elef parim vegomer* — and they ate together, king and princes, and the people rejoicing.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: since the time of Solomon the son of David king of Israel there was not the like in Jerusalem
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki mimei Shlomo ben David melekh Yisra’el lo* — there was the like in Jerusalem. Perhaps a larger people came on pilgrimage to Jerusalem in the days of Solomon, but there was not such great joy in Jerusalem since the days of Solomon; for they rejoiced most over this: if every pilgrimage festival were gathered in Jerusalem, because they had nothing new, they would have no joy; but now, that in all the days of Ahaz and the wicked kings of Judah they did not go up on pilgrimage to Jerusalem, and now they were permitted to go up to Jerusalem, they rejoiced with great joy; and because it was several years that they had not gone up to Jerusalem until now, the seven days of the Feast of Unleavened Bread seemed small in their eyes, and they added another seven days to rejoice in them, and they rejoiced with great joy.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: blessed the people
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayevarekhu et ha’am* — if you wish to say: he blessed them in this, that they asked to return from the land of their captors, and “the LORD heard their voice” and brought them back then. Another explanation: “and their voice was heard”; and so it is written above (30), “And the LORD hearkened to Hezekiah, and healed the people.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 2 Chronicles 30:20 (JPS: “And the LORD hearkened to Hezekiah, and healed the people”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: every man according to his service
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ish kefi avodato* — the priests to minister and the Levites to be singers and gatekeepers, and every man to his proper service.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the king’s portion of his substance for the burnt-offerings
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Umnat hamelekh min rekhusho la’olot vegomer* — which he gave to make them (willingly).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: to give the portion of the priests and the Levites
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayomer la’am leyoshvei Yerushalayim vegomer* — so that they would be strong in the Torah of the LORD more willingly, and furthermore, while their sustenance is prepared for them, they can do and occupy themselves in the Torah of the LORD; for the Torah was given only to those who eat the manna, and second to them, to those who eat *terumah*.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The saying that the Torah was given only to those who eat manna is translated as printed; I did not verify its source.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: gave in abundance the first-fruits of corn, wine, and oil, and honey
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ukhefrotz hadavar* — from the king’s mouth, to give the portion to the priests and the Levites, the children of Israel increased the first-fruits of corn, new wine and oil and honey — date honey.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: of all the increase of the field
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vekhol tevu’at sadeh* — and all these are not from the increase of the field; rather, so it is explained in tractate Nedarim, in the chapter *Hanodeir min hayarak*: One who vows off vegetables is permitted gourds. Rav Joseph raised an objection: “And as soon as the commandment came abroad, the children of Israel gave in abundance,” etc.; and if you say “corn,” anything from corn is implied; what, then, is “and as soon as it came abroad”? Abaye said: to bring in tree fruits and vegetables… Rava said: grain separately and the increase of the field separately.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The Talmudic discussion is compressed and is translated as printed. I did not verify the Talmudic passage. The Aramaic phrase is translated as printed.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the tithe of hallowed things which were hallowed unto the LORD their God
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uma’aser kodashim hamekuddashim laShem* — the tithe from the tithe, which the Levites give to the priests.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: laid them by heaps
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayitnu arumot arumot* — *hoypin* in the German language; an example (Song of Songs 7), “a heap of wheat.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed word is a glossed German form; I could not confirm it and left it as printed. The printed abbreviation בלשון אשכנז is read as “in the German language.” The quotation is Song of Songs 7:3 (JPS: “Thy belly is like a heap of wheat”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: began to lay the foundation of the heaps
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Hechelu ha’arumot lisod* — for the beginning of a thing is called a foundation, like the foundation of the house, which is the head of the building; and like it (Ezra 7), “for upon the first day of the first month was the foundation of the going up,” etc.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Ezra 7:9 (JPS: “upon the first day of the first month began he to go up from Babylon”); the printed form is *hu yesod hamma’alah*.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: they blessed the LORD
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayevarekhu et HaShem* — that He put it in the heart of Israel to separate their *terumot* and their tithes.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Hezekiah questioned the priests and the Levites concerning the heaps
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayidrosh Yechizkiyahu* — because Hezekiah saw that the heaps were great, he said in his heart: Perhaps the priests and the Levites did not take from them and did not touch them, for if they had touched them, how did they become so many? And he wondered, and inquired of them concerning the heaps, why this was.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Azariah the chief priest, of the house of Zadok
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayomer elav Azaryahu* — he was in the days of Uzziah.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: we have eaten and had enough
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Mehachel hatrumah lavi* — we ate eating, and not a casual eating, but eating and satisfaction and leaving over; and as for what you wonder at, that we ate four months and yet their heaps are so great, this is the matter: for the LORD blessed His people and gave them much produce; therefore our *terumot* and tithes were many.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: that which is left
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vehanoter* — from our eating this.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: this great store
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *HeHamon hazeh* — which you see, heaps upon heaps.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: prepare chambers in the house of the LORD
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lehakhin lishkot bevet HaShem* — and to put the *terumot* in them.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: them that were reckoned by genealogy of the priests by their fathers’ houses
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’et hityaches haKohanim lebeit avotam vehaLevi’im* — with the genealogy of their little ones, their wives, their sons and their daughters; to all that congregation they supplied their food from the *terumot* and the holy tithes; and the *terumot* and tithes, all those of which we spoke, were for those who stood to serve in the Court and also for the sons of Aaron the priests whose course had not come to serve, and who were in the field of the open land of their cities, in every city.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: men that were mentioned by name
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Anashim asher nikvu veshemot* — above (2, 31), Conaniah and his brothers were appointed over them to receive the portions, the *terumot* and the tithes from Israel, to give the portions to every male among the priests and the Levites.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The reference is 2 Chronicles 31:12 (JPS: “over them Conaniah the Levite was ruler, and Shimei his brother was second”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: to give portions to all the males among the priests
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lekhol zakhar baKohanim* — and also to all their wives, their sons and their daughters; and what it says here, “to every male,” is for emphasis, for even to minor males they supplied, as above (there), “to males from three years old and upward”; and certainly they supplied for their wives and their sons and their daughters.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 2 Chronicles 31:16 (JPS: “of males, from three years old and upward”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: thought to make a breach therein for himself
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayomer levak’am* — like *livko’am*, like (Amos 2) “because they sell (*al mikhram*) for silver,” like *mikhram*, and next to it (there) “because they have ripped up (*al bik’am*) the women with child of Gilead”; its interpretation and example (Isaiah 7) “and let us make a breach therein (*nevki’enah*)”; “and he cleaved (*vayvaka*) the wood for the burnt-offering” (Genesis 22).
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The grammatical comparison is compressed and is translated as printed. The verses are Amos 2:6 (JPS: “Because they sell the righteous for silver”), Amos 1:13 (JPS: “because they have ripped up the women with child of Gilead”), Isaiah 7:6 and Genesis 22:3 (JPS: “he cleaved the wood for the burnt-offering”; the printed number 25 is wrong).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: strengthened Millo in the city of David
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayechazzek et haMillo* — an example (Samuel II, 5), “and he built Millo.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The words are close to 2 Samuel 5:9 (JPS: “And David built round about from Millo and inward”) and 1 Kings 9:24 (JPS: “then did he build Millo”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: made weapons and shields in abundance
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vaya’as shelach larov* — implements of war, like “and every man with his weapon in his hand” (2 Chronicles 23), “every one went with his weapon to the water” (Nehemiah 4).
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Nehemiah 4:17 (JPS: “every one that went to the water had his weapon”). The printed text carries an editorial remark about the first reference, which I could not resolve.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Whereon do you trust
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Al meh attem bot’chim* — because it is written (Kings II, 11), “He trusted in the LORD God of Israel,” and also it is written there, “and he rebelled against the king of Assyria”; therefore he said, “Whereon do you trust,” for you rebelled against me.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotations are 2 Kings 18:5 (JPS: “He trusted in the LORD, the God of Israel”) and 18:7 (JPS: “and he rebelled against the king of Assyria, and served him not”); the printed number 11 is wrong.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: that you abide the siege in Jerusalem
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Veyoshvim bamatzor biYrushalayim* — as it is written (here), “to die by famine and by thirst.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 2 Chronicles 32:11 (JPS: “to die by famine and by thirst”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Hath not the same Hezekiah taken away His high places and His altars
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Halo hu Yechizkiyahu* — he who trusts in his God — is he not the one who transgressed? And even if He had the ability to help him, He would not help him, for he sinned against Him in that he removed His high places and His altars, and said to Judah and Jerusalem, “Before one altar you shall worship”; is it not better that Judah worship before one altar, and Jerusalem before one or two or more? And what use is one for so great a people! For they thought that all those high places which he removed, as above (38), “and he cut down the Asherah,” etc., were built in the name of the God of Israel.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: This is Sennacherib’s argument, as Rashi reports it. The printed reference “(38)” does not match; compare 2 Chronicles 31:1 (JPS: “hewed down the Asherim, and broke down the high places and the altars”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: which my fathers utterly destroyed
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *He’cherimu avotai* — Pul king of Assyria and Tiglath-pileser.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: He wrote also a letter, to taunt the LORD
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Usfarim katav lecharef laShem Elohei* — and in Kings (II, 19) and in Isaiah (37) it is written, “And Hezekiah received the letters from the hand of the messengers, and read them, and went up to the house of the LORD, and Hezekiah spread them before the LORD.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 2 Kings 19:14 and Isaiah 37:14 (JPS: “And Hezekiah received the letter from the hand of the messengers, and read it; and Hezekiah went up unto the house of the LORD, and spread it before the LORD”); the printed form is plural.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: in the Jews’ language
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Bekol gadol Yehudit vegomer* — to frighten them and to affright them; here the matter is stated generally, and in Kings it is explained well what he said to them, and also in Isaiah.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: spoke of the God of Jerusalem
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayedabberu el Elohei Yerushalayim* — he who wrote this book is complaining about this scoundrel Sennacherib, who blasphemed the living God.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: which are the work of men’s hands
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ke’al Elohei ammei ha’aretz* — that they are the work of man’s hands, and they compared the God of our Maker, the Maker of all, to the gods of the nations, who are the work of their hands, as he said above, “Who among all the gods… that your God should be able to deliver you out of my hand.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 2 Chronicles 32:14 (JPS: “that your God should be able to deliver you out of my hand”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: prayed because of this
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayitpallel Yechizkiyahu* — in Kings and in Isaiah the prayer is explained.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: slew him there with the sword
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Umiyetzi me’av* — as it is written (there), “and his sons smote him with the sword.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 2 Kings 19:37 (JPS: “Adrammelech and Sarezer his sons smote him with the sword”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: he prayed unto the LORD
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayitpallel el HaShem* — as it is explained in Kings.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: He spoke unto him
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayomer lo* — what the sign is.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: gave him a sign
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Umofet natan lo* — “and this shall be the sign for thee”; everything is explained there.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Hezekiah rendered not according to the benefit done unto him
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Velo khigmul alav hesheev* — not as the Holy One, blessed be He, dealt with Hezekiah, healing him, did Hezekiah repay Him.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: his heart was lifted up
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki gavah libbo* — for he showed all his treasure-house, etc., until “and in all his dominion.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 2 Kings 20:13 (JPS: “showed them all his treasure-house”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: therefore there was wrath upon him, and upon Judah and Jerusalem
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayehi alav ketzef ve’al Yehudah viYrushalayim* — for this; and the writer of this book abbreviated here because it is written in Kings and in Isaiah.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: humbled himself for the pride of his heart
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayikkana Yechizkiyahu bigvoah libbo* — as it is written there, “Then said Hezekiah unto Isaiah: Good is the word of the LORD,” etc.; and when he humbled himself the wrath did not come upon them in his days.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 2 Kings 20:19 (JPS: “Good is the word of the LORD which thou hast spoken”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: all manner of goodly vessels
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ulekhol kelei chemdah* — he made various kinds of treasuries.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: store-houses also for the increase of corn, and wine, and oil
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Umiskenot litvu’at* — regarding granaries, it is fitting to say *miskenot* everywhere, like (Exodus 1) “store-cities for Pharaoh,” and likewise above (2, 8), “And he built Tadmor in the wilderness, and all the store-cities which he built in Hamath”; and you must say it was for grain, for in the wilderness he would not store gold and silver.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotations are Exodus 1:11 (JPS: “And they built for Pharaoh store-cities”) and 2 Chronicles 8:4.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: stalls for all manner of beasts
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’urot lekhol behemah uvehemah* — large stables (*itztabla’ot*).
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed word *itztabla’ot* is given as printed and glossed “large stables.”

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: brought them straight down on the west side of the city of David
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayyisharem lemattah ma’aravah* — he led them in a straight way downward westward to the city of David.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: in the business of the ambassadors of the princes of Babylon
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vekhen bemalitzei* — messengers; an example (Genesis 42), “for the interpreter was between them”; because the messenger interprets between the sender and the one sent to; and it falls on the verse that says “And Hezekiah prospered in all his works”; and after all this good with which the Holy One, blessed be He, made him prosper, God left him to try him, to know all that was in his heart, by the hand of the interpreters of the princes of Babylon who were sent to him.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Genesis 42:23 (JPS: “for the interpreter was between them”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: to inquire of the wonder that was done in the land
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lidrosh hamofet asher hayah ba’aretz* — he did not stand the test, and showed them all his treasure-house; and it is expounded from its end to its beginning.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: in the ascent of the sepulchres of the sons of David
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Bamma’aleh* — with the choicest, as is explained at the end of the first chapter of Bava Kamma.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: I did not verify the Bava Kamma passage.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: In Jerusalem shall My name be for ever
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Birushalayim yihyeh shemi le’olam* — this verse is a complaint: this Manasseh built altars to idolatry in the House of which the Holy One, blessed be He, said, “I want My name to dwell there”; and the verse that comes nearby is also a language of complaint: “And he set the graven image of the idol which he had made in the house of God,” etc.; and also the verse “neither will I any more remove the foot.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed abbreviation עכומ"ז is read as “idolatry.”

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: appointed them that divined by a ghost or a familiar spirit
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’asah ov veyid’oni* — [written] full with a *vav*, because he did much, and he added to the graven image which he made.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The remark about the full spelling is translated as printed and its reference is not clear to me. The same phrase is in 2 Kings 21:6.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: will I put My name for ever
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Le’ilum* — for ever.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: neither will I any more remove the foot of Israel from off the land
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Velo osif lehasir et regel Yisra’el* — it refers back to the verse above, and all of it is a complaint; that is, the Holy One, blessed be He, says: This is what I said to David and to Solomon, “In this house will I put My name for ever,” and I also promised them, “neither will I any more remove the foot of Israel from off the land, if only they will observe,” etc.; and now “Manasseh made them go astray,” etc.; it turns out that through him the Divine Presence withdrew, and we too are still in exile through him.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quoted words are 2 Chronicles 33:7–8 (JPS: “In this house, and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen… will I put My name for ever; neither will I any more remove the foot of Israel from off the land”) and 33:9.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: on the west side of Gihon, in the valley
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *LeGichon banachal* — beside the Gihon stream; the name of a place.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: he compassed about Ophel
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vesavav le’Ofel* — and from there he surrounded the strength of the towers built at the work of Ophel.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The sense of “the work of Ophel” is not clear to me.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: cast them out of the city
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayashlekh chutzah* — and he did not break them nor hide them from sight; therefore his son stumbled over them, as it is written, “And Amon sacrificed unto all the graven images which Manasseh his father had made,” for he took them from the place where he had thrown them.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 2 Chronicles 33:22 (JPS: “And Amon sacrificed unto all the graven images which Manasseh his father had made”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: sacrifices of peace-offerings and of thanksgiving
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayizbach alav zivchei shelamim vetodah* — he brought a thanksgiving offering and gave thanks to the Holy One, blessed be He, that He had returned him to Jerusalem and to his kingdom.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: His prayer also
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Utefillato* — how he prayed.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: how [God] was entreated of him
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Veha’ater lo* — and He restored him to his kingdom.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: they buried him in his own house
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayikberuhu beito* — like *beveito*; and in Kings (II, 28) it is written, “in the garden of his house”; he was not privileged to be buried with his fathers.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The Kings verse is 2 Kings 21:18 (JPS: “was buried in the garden of his own house, in the garden of Uzza”); the printed number 28 is wrong.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: while he was yet young
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vehu odenu na’ar hechel lidrosh* — the interpretation: although he was a lad, he began to seek the God of David his father; an example (Genesis 36), “and he was a lad with the sons of Bilhah, and Joseph brought evil report of them,” and there is nothing astonishing in the matter; but if he had been thirty years old, he would not have done so; and this is astonishing, that he was a lad, and nevertheless he began to seek, etc.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The reasoning is translated as printed and is not clear to me. The quotation is Genesis 37:2 (JPS: “being still a lad even with the sons of Bilhah… and Joseph brought evil report of them”); the printed number 36 is wrong.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: he began to purge Judah and Jerusalem
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Hechel letaher et Yehudah viYrushalayim* — from the high places and the Asherim that Manasseh made and Amon his son renewed, as above (2, 33), “and he built again the high places which Hezekiah his father had broken down,” etc.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 2 Chronicles 33:3 (JPS: “For he built again the high places which Hezekiah his father had broken down”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the sun-images
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vehachammanim* — forms of the sun.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: that were on high above them
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Asher lemalah mehem* — which they set up above them, high, opposite the sun, and bow down to it; all this Manasseh did, as it is written above (there), “and worshipped all the host of heaven, and served them.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 2 Chronicles 33:3.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: made dust of them, and strewed it upon the graves of them that had sacrificed unto them
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayizrok al penei hakkevarim* — here was fulfilled what was said to Jeroboam (Kings I, 13), “Thus saith the LORD: Behold, a child shall be born unto the house of David, Josiah by name, and upon thee shall he sacrifice the bones of men, the priests of the high places who burn incense.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 1 Kings 13:2 (JPS: “Behold, a son shall be born unto the house of David, Josiah by name; and upon thee shall he sacrifice the priests of the high places that burn incense upon thee, and men’s bones shall they burn upon thee”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: in the cities of Manasseh and Ephraim and Simeon, even unto Naphtali
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *UVe’arei Menasheh ve’Efrayim vegomer* — of those gleanings who remained from the sword and from the captivity of Sennacherib.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: with their axes round about
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Becharvotehem* — it is written *behar bateihem* (“in the mountain of their houses”); because they were only a few gleanings, they were afraid to dwell in the lowland, but only to settle in the mountain of their houses.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: JPS follows the read form (“axes”); the printed note explains the written form.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Joah the son of Joahaz the recorder
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *HaMazkir* — everywhere that *sofer* (scribe) is written, *mazkir* is written nearby; for every king had a scribe to write everything that befell him in his kingdom, whether good or bad, and he had a *mazkir* who sat beside the scribe to recall every single thing, and the scribe wrote at his mouth.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: which the Levites, the keepers of the door, had gathered
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Asher asfu haLevi’im shomrei hassaf vegomer* — with their axes round about.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed words repeat the comment on 2 Chronicles 34:6 and seem out of place here; they are translated as printed.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: to mend and repair the house
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Livdok ulechazzek* — to see the nakedness of the land (Genesis 42); we translate *ulmechezei yat bedaka de’ar’a*.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Genesis 42:9 (JPS: “to see the nakedness of the land you are come”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: timber for couplings
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’etzim lamechabberot* — *shpangin* in the German language.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed word is a glossed German form; I could not confirm it and left it as printed. The printed abbreviation בלשון אשכנ"ז is read as “in the German language.”

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: to make beams for the houses
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ulekarot* — *trabir* in Old French.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The Old French form printed in Hebrew letters could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. The printed abbreviation בלע"ז is read as “in Old French.”

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: to preside over it
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lenatzeach* — *romis trir* in Old French; and so (Ezra 3) “to have the oversight of the work,” and likewise “six hundred overseers” (above, 2, 2).
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The Old French form printed in Hebrew letters could not be confirmed in Darmesteter; left as printed. The printed abbreviation בלע"ז is read as “in Old French.” The quotations are Ezra 3:9 (JPS: “to have the oversight of the workmen in the house of God”) and 2 Chronicles 2:1 and 2:17 (JPS: “three thousand and six hundred overseers”); the printed “six hundred” does not match the figure in the verses I checked.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: all that had skill with instruments of music
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *VehaLevi’im kol mevin* — everywhere it is said of song, understanding; and so above (1, 25), when they cast lots, it is written, “as well the small as the great, the teacher as the scholar”; and likewise (there), “every one that was skilful in instruments of song”; and it is written, “And Chenaniah” (above, 1, 15), the chief of the Levites, etc., for he was skilful, and was appointed over them to teach how to carry the burden, for he is skilful.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotations are 1 Chronicles 25:8 and 25:7, and 15:22 (JPS: “Chenaniah, chief of the Levites, was over the song; he was master in the song, because he was skilful”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: of the Levites there were scribes
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *UMehaLevi’im soferim* — to write the money that was brought to the house of the LORD, and how they collected it.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: officers
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Veshoterim* — at the work.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the book of the Law of the LORD given by Moses
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Et sefer Torat HaShem beyad Moshe* — Deuteronomy.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Hilkiah delivered the book to Shaphan
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayiten Chilkiyahu et hasefer el Shafan* — for it is the scribe’s task to read all of it before the king.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: brought back word unto the king
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayashev od et hamelekh davar* — for at first he returned word to the king about the mission on which the king had sent him, to strengthen the house of the LORD his God, as it is written above, “he sent Shaphan the son of Azaliah,” etc.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 2 Chronicles 34:8.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: they have poured out the money
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayyatiku* — and they poured out, like (Genesis 21) “and he poured oil,” and we translate *ve’attiq*.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: I could not match the printed reference; “poured oil” occurs in Genesis 28:18 and 35:14 (JPS: “and poured oil upon the top of it”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Shaphan the scribe told the king
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayaged Shafan haSofer* — after he returned word to the king of his mission, he told him of the mission of Hilkiah the priest, and read the book before him.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: he rent his clothes
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayikra et begadav* — when he heard that they were reading (Deuteronomy 28), “The LORD will bring thee, and thy king,” etc., and he expounded for himself: “whom thou shalt set over thee” — the people made him king, and not a prophet by the word.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Deuteronomy 28:36 (JPS: “The LORD will bring thee, and thy king whom thou shalt set over thee”). The exposition is as printed.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: that is poured out upon us
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Asher nitkhah banu* — because wrath is fire, the term *nittuch* (melting) applies to it, and an example of it below, “and My wrath shall be poured out upon this place, and shall not be quenched.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 2 Chronicles 34:25 (JPS: “therefore is My wrath poured out upon this place, and it shall not be quenched”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Huldah the prophetess
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *El Chuldah haNevi’ah* — our Rabbis expounded: because a woman is more merciful than a man, therefore he did not send to Jeremiah the prophet.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: I did not verify the Rabbinic passage.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: keeper of the wardrobe
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Shomer habbegadim* — if you wish to say, either the priestly garments or the royal garments.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: dwelt in Jerusalem in the second quarter
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Yoshevet biYrushalayim bamishneh* — the city had two walls, and she sat between the two walls; and its Targum is *beit ulpana*, which means in a place of Torah; for there was one chamber of Huldah near the Chamber of Hewn Stone; the chamber of Huldah was open to the outside and closed toward the Sanhedrin that sat in the Chamber of Hewn Stone; so it is written in tractate Middot, for the sake of modesty.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: I did not verify the Middot passage.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Tell you the man that sent you unto me
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Imru la’ish* — because she wanted to interrupt the vision of the people concerning this place and its inhabitants; and when she finished that vision, then she explains well “and to the king of Judah who sent you,” and shortens the prophecy of the place and its inhabitants, and removes it, and holds it with the prophecy of the king, which is longer.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The explanation is translated as printed and its sense is not clear to me.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: thou shalt be gathered to thy grave in peace
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’ne’esafta el kivrotekha beshalom* — but was he not slain? But “in peace” in this: that your eyes will not see all the evil that I will bring upon this place and upon its inhabitants — that is, the destruction of the House.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The slaying of Josiah is in 2 Chronicles 35:23–24.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the book of the covenant
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Sefer haBrit* — behold, all the trembling with which the king trembled because he found written (there), “The LORD will bring thee,” and he saw that the Torah calls it a covenant (there), “These are the words of the covenant”; and therefore he too made a covenant. And he saw written near it after it (there, 39), “Observe therefore the words,” etc., “and do them”; Josiah also saw written near it, “You are standing this day all of you,” etc., until “your little ones, your wives,” until “that thou shouldest enter into the covenant,” until “which the LORD thy God maketh with thee this day,” he said: also in that example I will make a covenant, since there it is written, “You are standing,” etc.; so I too. “And he caused all that were found in Jerusalem… to stand,” from small to great.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The comment is dense and is translated as printed. The verses are Deuteronomy 28:36 and 28:69 (JPS: “These are the words of the covenant which the LORD commanded Moses to make”), 29:8 (JPS: “Observe therefore the words of this covenant, and do them”), 29:9–11 (JPS: “You are standing this day all of you before the LORD your God… that thou shouldest enter into the covenant of the LORD thy God… which the LORD thy God maketh with thee this day”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: with all his heart, and with all his soul
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Bekhol levavo uvekhol nafsho vegomer* — which he found written there (30), “And return unto the LORD thy God with all thy heart and with all thy soul.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Deuteronomy 30:2 (JPS: “and shalt return unto the LORD thy God… with all thy heart, and with all thy soul”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the king stood in his place
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vaya’amod hamelekh al ommdo* — a term of standing (*nitzavim*).
2 Chronicles.translator_note: Compare Deuteronomy 29:9 (JPS: “You are standing this day”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: according to the covenant of God, the God of their fathers
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Kivrit Elohim Elohei avotehem* — like all those where it is written “the God of their fathers”; therefore it is written here “the God of their fathers,” which He cut with their fathers in the wilderness; and every covenant there is about idolatry, as it is written (there, 29), “and you have seen their detestable things,” etc., until “turneth away this day from the LORD”; therefore “And Josiah took away all the abominations,” etc.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotations are Deuteronomy 29:16–17 (JPS: “and you have seen their detestable things… whose heart turneth away this day from the LORD our God”) and 2 Chronicles 34:33 (JPS: “And Josiah took away all the abominations”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: kept a passover unto the LORD in Jerusalem
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vaya’as Yoshiyahu biYrushalayim Pesach* — because all the wicked kings of Judah did not keep the Passover according to its rule.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Put the holy ark in the house which Solomon the son of David king of Israel did build
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Tenu et aron hakodesh* — according to the plain sense, Manasseh and Amon had removed the ark and put their idols in its place, as is proved above (2, 33) about Manasseh, “and he set the graven image of the idol,” etc.; therefore Josiah commanded to seat it and put the ark in its place which Solomon built. And our Rabbis said that he told the Levites to hide it there.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 2 Chronicles 33:7. I did not verify the Rabbinic statement.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: there shall no more be a burden upon your shoulders
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ein lakhem massa bakkatef* — this is another argument, and the beginning of the clause is that he said to them, You have no labor of carrying a burden on the shoulder from any of the vessels of the house of the LORD, so that you could say, because of the labor of carrying on the shoulder we cannot serve the LORD and His people; therefore from now on serve the LORD your God with song, and His people Israel to slaughter and flay their Passover offerings, as is proved below, “and kill the passover lamb and sanctify yourselves,” etc.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 2 Chronicles 35:6.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: according to the divisions of the fathers’ houses
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lifluggot* — to a division, to make the Passover according to its rule, as the LORD commanded by Moses.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Josiah gave to the children of the people
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayarem Yoshiyahu livnei ha’am* — an example (Numbers 18) “Thus you also shall set apart”; a term of the portion.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Numbers 18:28 (JPS: “Thus you also shall set apart a gift unto the LORD”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: unto all that were present
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lekhol hannimtza* — for all Israel who were present he set apart flock for the Passover offerings.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: to the number of thirty thousand
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lemispar sheloshim elef* — whether sheep, lambs or goats.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: three thousand bullocks
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Uvakar sheloshet alafim* — for the festival peace-offerings.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: they roasted the passover with fire according to the ordinance
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayvashlu hapesach ba’esh kamishpat* — “roast with fire” (Exodus 12).
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Exodus 12:9 (JPS: “but roast with fire”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: carried them quickly to all the children of the people
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayaritzu lekhol benei ha’am* — the Levites; and when they had prepared for all Israel, afterward the Levites prepared for themselves and for the priests, who had no leisure to prepare.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Jeduthun the king’s seer
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Chozeh hamelekh* — each and every one was a seer.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: there was no passover like to that kept in Israel
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Velo na’asah Pesach kamohu* — (in Kings II, 23) it is written, “For there was not kept such a passover from the days of the judges”; from the day that Israel was divided into two kingdoms, when the ten tribes departed from the kings of Judah and set a king over themselves alone; for all the days that they were two nations, the tribes of Judah and Benjamin made the Passover for the name of the LORD in Jerusalem, and those for the name of idolatry in Beth-el and in Dan; and this did not happen in all the days of the judges, when Israel was divided into two families; and they had in every generation only one judge, and that judge compelled them to go in the way of the LORD, as explained in Judges, “and the LORD was with the judge, and saved them out of the hand of their enemies all the days of the judge”; and all the ten tribes went to Shiloh and made the Passover for the name of the LORD; and the like of this Passover was not made in all the days of the kings of Israel and Judah together making a Passover; but in the days of Josiah, when the kingdom of the ten tribes had already ceased, and when Jeremiah returned the ten tribes, they did not set a king over themselves any more, but Josiah reigned over them, and they all made the Passover together for the sake of Heaven in Jerusalem; and this is “there was not kept such a passover to the LORD in Jerusalem.” But this interpretation misleads me very much and does not seem right to me; granted that Jeremiah returned the ten tribes and Josiah reigned over them in Jerusalem, how can it be that they did not make the like of this Passover in all the days of the judges and in the days of Samuel the seer and in the days of David and Solomon, when Israel were settled on their land, secure and quiet, and had only one king, and their hearts were toward Heaven? Rather, so is its interpretation, and so Rabbi Eliezer son of Rabbi Meshullam, of blessed memory, interpreted to me: “and there was no passover like it” ever, in that the king and the princes gave animals for the Passover offerings sufficient for their needs, and bullocks for the festival peace-offerings, and commanded the Levites to prepare for them and to send to every man according to his eating.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The Kings quotation is 2 Kings 23:22 (JPS: “For there was not kept such a passover from the days of the judges that judged Israel, nor in all the days of the kings of Israel, nor of the kings of Judah”). The statement that Jeremiah returned the ten tribes is a Rabbinic tradition that I did not verify. Rashi rejects the first interpretation himself.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Neco king of Egypt went up to fight against Carchemish by the Euphrates
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Acharei kol zot asher hekhin Yoshiyahu et habayit alah Nekho melekh Mitzrayim* — the verse complains and laments over Josiah, that no miracle was done for him as for Hezekiah, of whom it is written, “After these things, and this faithfulness, Sennacherib came,” and a miracle was done for him.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 2 Chronicles 32:1 (JPS: “After these things, and this faithfulness, Sennacherib king of Assyria came”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: to fight against Carchemish
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lehillachem beKharkemish al Perat* — against the king of Assyria, as it is written (Kings II, 23), “Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt went up against the king of Assyria to the river Euphrates”; and he wished to pass through the Land of Israel, upon him; and Pharaoh Neco could not come upon him by the way of the river Euphrates unless he passed through the Land of Israel, for Egypt is in the south of the Land of Israel and the river Euphrates is in the north of the Land of Israel.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 2 Kings 23:29 (JPS: “Pharaoh-necoh king of Egypt went up against the king of Assyria to the river Euphrates”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Josiah went out against him
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayetze likratto* — for he expounded “neither shall the sword go through your land” (Leviticus 26): even a sword of peace shall not go through your land; and he did not know the sin of the scoffers of the generation, who stood behind the door to arrange, as is explained in tractate Taanit.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The phrase about the scoffers “behind the door” is translated as printed and its sense is not clear to me. The quotation is Leviticus 26:6 (JPS: “neither shall the sword go through your land”). I did not verify the Talmudic passage.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: hearkened not unto the words of Neco, from the mouth of God
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Velo shama el divrei Nekho mipi Elohim* — for He said it to him from the mouth of God, as Isaiah said, “And I will set Egypt against Egypt”; and this is what Kalir composed: “All his multitude to go to Aram-naharaim, so that a sword of any kind not pass through Ephraim; he did not hearken to the seer, and turned backward, for a decree was decreed to set Egypt against Egypt.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Isaiah 19:2 (JPS: “And I will spur Egypt against Egypt”). I did not verify the lines of Kalir.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: put him in the second chariot that he had
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Al rekhev hammishneh* — because it is the way of the king to ride in two chariots; the first is the main one, and if he needs, he sits in the second; in the first he went out before them, and when he was wounded they put him on the second chariot.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: all the singing men and singing women spoke of Josiah in their lamentations
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayyamu* — “and all the singers”: a term of song, singers; for song and lament are said in one voice about him. Amos prophesied, “And I will cause the sun to go down at noon, and I will darken the earth in the clear day” — this is the day of Josiah, who died at thirty-nine years, in the middle of his days, as it is written (Psalms 90), “The days of our years are threescore years and ten,” and it is written (Amos 8), “And I will turn your feasts into mourning, and all your songs into lamentation, and I will make it as the mourning for an only son, and the end thereof as a bitter day”; and this is what it says, “and all the singing men and singing women spoke… and all Judah and Jerusalem mourned for him.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The verses are Amos 8:9–10 (JPS: “I will cause the sun to go down at noon, And I will darken the earth in the clear day… And I will turn your feasts into mourning, And all your songs into lamentation… as the mourning for an only son”), Psalm 90:10 and 2 Chronicles 35:24 (“And all Judah and Jerusalem mourned for Josiah”). Arithmetic: Josiah was eight when he began to reign and reigned thirty-one years (2 Chronicles 34:1), making thirty-nine. The printed lemma *vayyamu* is a form I could not match to the verse.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: they made them an ordinance in Israel
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayittenum lechok* — when some grief or weeping befalls them, that they lament and weep over the event, they mention this grief along with it; an example on the Ninth of Av, when they recite laments over those slain in the persecutions that took place in our days, so shall they weep over the death of Josiah; an example (Judges 11) “and it was a custom in Israel,” etc., “to lament the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite four days in the year.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Judges 11:39–40 (JPS: “And it was a custom in Israel, that the daughters of Israel went yearly to lament the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite four days in a year”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: behold, they are written in the lamentations
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vehinam ketuvim al hakkinot* — in the Book of Lamentations.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: his good deeds, according to that which is written in the Law of the LORD
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vachasadav kakkatuv beTorat HaShem* — (and in Kings II, 23) it is written, “and like unto him was there no king before him”; and this is what it says here, “behold, they are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 2 Kings 23:25 (JPS: “And like unto him was there no king before him”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: made him king in his father’s stead in Jerusalem
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayamlikhuhu tachat aviv* — although Jehoiakim his brother was older than he by twenty-one months.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The verses give Jehoahaz’s age at accession as twenty-three (2 Chronicles 36:2, 2 Kings 23:31) and Jehoiakim’s as twenty-five (2 Chronicles 36:5, 2 Kings 23:36); the printed “twenty-one months” is as printed.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: deposed him
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayasiyu* — he, the king of Egypt, at Jerusalem; it is explained well in Kings (there): “And Pharaoh-necoh put him in bands at Riblah in the land of Hamath.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed first word (*vayasiyu*) and the first words of the comment are garbled; the translation follows the sense of the explanation. The quotation is 2 Kings 23:33 (JPS: “And Pharaoh-necoh put him in bands at Riblah in the land of Hamath”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: at Jerusalem
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *BiYrushalayim* — from reigning in Jerusalem.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: Compare 2 Kings 23:33 (JPS: “that he might not reign in Jerusalem”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: fined the land
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vaya’anesh et ha’aretz* — to give tribute. An example: “and they shall fine him a hundred of silver” (Deuteronomy 22).
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Deuteronomy 22:19 (JPS: “And they shall fine him a hundred shekels of silver”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: changed his name to Jehoiakim
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayesev et shemo Yehoyakim* — so is the way of kings and princes, that they give their servants a name that they desire. An example (Genesis 41), “And Pharaoh called Joseph’s name,” etc.; and so (Numbers), “And Moses called Hoshea the son of Nun Joshua”; and so (Daniel 1), “And the chief of the officers gave names,” etc.; and all of it is to make known that he rules over him, to give him a name as he wishes.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The verses are Genesis 41:45, Numbers 13:16 and Daniel 1:7 (JPS: “And the chief of the officers gave names unto them”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: changed his name to Jehoiakim
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayesev et shemo Yehoyakim* — why did he call his name Jehoiakim? It is explained above that after Pharaoh slew Josiah he made a king and fined him, to be a tributary servant.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The reference is to 2 Chronicles 36:3 and 2 Kings 23:33–34.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Against him came up Nebuchadnezzar
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Alav alah Nevukhadnetzar* — for Pharaoh could not go out of his land, as it is written (Kings II, 24), “And the king of Egypt came not again any more out of his land; for the king of Babylon had taken, from the Brook of Egypt unto the river Euphrates, all that pertained to the king of Egypt,” for he defeated him in the fourth year at Carchemish on the river Euphrates, as is explained (Jeremiah 45).
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 2 Kings 24:7. The defeat at Carchemish is in Jeremiah 46:2 (JPS: “which Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon smote in the fourth year of Jehoiakim”); the printed Jeremiah 45:1 mentions the fourth year of Jehoiakim but not Carchemish.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: to carry him to Babylon
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Lehoilkho Bavelah* — but he did not bring him to Assyria; rather, on the way he died and he cast out his carcass. And so Jeremiah prophesied (22), “He shall be buried with the burial of an ass, drawn and cast forth beyond the gates of Jerusalem”; and where is the burial of an ass? In the belly of the dog. And so (Kings II, 24) proves it: “So Jehoiakim slept with his fathers,” and it does not write “and they buried him.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotations are Jeremiah 22:19 and 2 Kings 24:6 (JPS: “So Jehoiakim slept with his fathers”). The printed “Assyria” is as printed (the verse says Babylon). The remark about the dog is as printed.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: vessels of the house of the LORD
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *UMikhlei Beit HaShem* — and some of the vessels of the house of the LORD; and about this Jeremiah prophesied (26), “For thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, concerning the vessels that remain,” etc. And he (Seder Olam) asks: “In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim king of Judah… and the LORD gave into his hand,” while here it proves that it was in the eleventh year of his reign. And what does the text teach: “In the third year of his rebellion”? As it is said (Kings II, 24), “And Jehoiakim became his servant three years, and he turned and rebelled against him”; he served three years and rebelled three years, and in the third year of his rebellion he came up against him, and that is the eighth year of Nebuchadnezzar. For Mar said: in the first year he conquered Nineveh, in the second he conquered Jehoiakim, and three years he rebelled against him; and he did not reign except in year four of Jehoiakim, as it is said (Jeremiah 25), “In the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah, that was the first year of Nebuchadrezzar.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The chronological argument is dense and is translated as printed. The verses are Jeremiah 27:19–22 (printed “26”), Daniel 1:1–2 (“In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim king of Judah came Nebuchadnezzar… and the Lord gave Jehoiakim… into his hand”), 2 Kings 24:1 (JPS: “Jehoiakim became his servant three years; then he turned and rebelled against him”) and Jeremiah 25:1. The words “in the third year of his rebellion” are not a verse that I found. I did not verify the Talmudic or Rabbinic passage.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: his abominations
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vetoavotav* — that he lay with his mother.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: I did not verify the Talmudic or Rabbinic passage.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: that which was found in him
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *VehaNimtza alav* — a tattoo inscription.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: at the return of the year
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ulteshuvat hashanah* — when he exiled Jehoiachin.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed name is Jehoiakim (*Yehoyakim*), but the exile was of Jehoiachin; I translated the name as printed and the verse is about Jehoiachin (2 Kings 24:12–15).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: goodly vessels of the house of the LORD
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Im kelei chemdat Beit HaShem* — the precious things he took, and the rest he left until the exile of Zedekiah; then he took everything with him. In Kings II (24) it is explained, “And Jehoiachin the king of Judah went out to the king of Babylon,” etc.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 2 Kings 24:12 and the vessels are in 2 Kings 24:13.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: made Zedekiah his brother king
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayamlekh et Tzidkiyahu achiv* — the brother of Jehoiakim; and so (Kings, there), “And the king of Babylon made Mattaniah his father’s brother king in his stead, and changed his name to Zedekiah,” the uncle of Jehoiachin.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is 2 Kings 24:17.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: he did that which was evil
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vaya’as hara* — what was the evil? That he humbled not himself before Jeremiah the prophet, from the mouth of the LORD, as is explained (Jeremiah 38): “Then said Jeremiah unto Zedekiah: Thus saith the LORD, the God of hosts, the God of Israel: If thou wilt go forth,” etc., “I am afraid of the Jews,” etc.; and apart from this sin he sinned only in this, that he did not hearken to the word of the prophet from the mouth of the LORD and that he transgressed the oath of Nebuchadnezzar. But in the abominations and “that which was found in him” of Jehoiakim, he did not do evil — from the mouth of Rabbi Eliezer son of Rabbi Meshullam, of blessed memory.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotations are Jeremiah 38:17 and 38:19 (JPS: “I am afraid of the Jews that are fallen away to the Chaldeans”).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: who had made him swear by God
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Asher hishbio b’Elohim* — as explained (Ezekiel 17), “Say now to the rebellious house,” etc.; and the whole section is said about Jehoiachin and Zedekiah: “and took the king thereof and the princes thereof and brought them to him to Babylon” — this is Jehoiachin and his company; “and he took of the seed royal and made a covenant with him” — this is Zedekiah.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotations are Ezekiel 17:12–13.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: all the chiefs of the priests
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Gam kol sarei hakohanim* — to instruct Israel, as it is written (Deuteronomy 24), “according to all that the priests the Levites shall teach you”; not common priests, to protest, but the chiefs of the priests, who had the power to protest and did not protest.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Deuteronomy 24:8.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: they polluted the house of the LORD
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayetamu et Beit HaShem* — with its abominations.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: which He had hallowed in Jerusalem
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Asher hikdish biYrushalayim* — to cause His name to dwell there forever.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the LORD, the God of their fathers, sent to them
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayishlach HaShem* — all this is the righteousness of the judgment, that you not say that He did not warn them to return from their evil ways, but immediately “and tore perpetually in His anger”; therefore it is said, “And the LORD, the God of their fathers, sent to them by His messengers,” and warned them to return from their evil, and not once in a year or in a month, but every single day, “betimes and often.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The phrase “tore perpetually in His anger” alludes to Amos 1:11; the printed words (*ve’yitrof la’ad apo*) are translated as printed.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: He had compassion on His people
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ki chamal al amo* — and He did not desire their death.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: on His dwelling-place
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ve’al me’ono* — on the dwelling of the Temple, for even a king of flesh and blood has compassion on his people and on the house of his residence, not to destroy them.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: they mocked the messengers of God
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayihyu mal’ivim bemalakhei haElohim* — the messengers of the Holy One, blessed be He.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The printed text spells out the Name in full (*HaKadosh Barukh Hu*).

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: despised His words
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *UVozim devarav* — of the Holy One, blessed be He, that certainly the judgment is with Him; for even the messengers of flesh and blood are not despised, and they fear to transgress their command, whether for evil or for good; but with Him they despised His words and mocked and scoffed at His prophets, so much, etc.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: He brought upon them the king of the Chaldeans
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vaya’al aleihem et melekh Kasdim* — for they are a lowly nation, as it is said (Isaiah 23), “Behold, the land of the Chaldeans — this is the people that was not”; and here was fulfilled (Deuteronomy 32), “They have roused Me to jealousy with a no-god,” etc., until “I will provoke them with a vile nation.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotations are Isaiah 23:13 and Deuteronomy 32:21.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: slew their young men with the sword in the house of their sanctuary
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayahorog bachureihem bacherev beveit mikdasham* — and their recompense was returned to them, as it is written, “they polluted the house of the LORD”; and what was said was fulfilled (Ezekiel 9), “Smite; let not your eye spare,” etc., until “go you forth. And they went forth and smote in the city.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotations are Ezekiel 9:5–7.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: had no compassion upon young man or maiden, old man or hoary-headed
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Velo chamal al bachur uvetulah zaken veyashesh* — which is not the custom of men of the armies when they conquer in war: they slay the men of war, but on the old man, the young man and the maiden they have compassion and are filled with mercy. And the prophecy of Moses our teacher was also fulfilled (Deuteronomy 32): “Without shall the sword bereave, and in the chambers terror; slaying both young man and virgin,” etc.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Deuteronomy 32:25.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: all the vessels of the house of God, great and small
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vekhol kelei Beit HaElohim haGedolim vehaKetanim* — that remained from the exile of Jehoiakim and Jeconiah.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: they were servants to him and his sons until the reign of the kingdom of Persia
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vayihyu lo ulevanav la’avadim ad molekh malkhut Paras* — and why until the kingdom of Persia? Because until the kingdom of Persia, until that time the land had not been paid her sabbaths; and that is what is written (Leviticus 26), “as long as it lieth desolate it shall have rest.”
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotation is Leviticus 26:35.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: until the land had been paid her sabbaths
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Ad retzatah ha’aretz et shabbetoteha* — “shall be paid” (*tirtzeh*); for before this the land had not been paid her sabbaths.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: for as long as she lay desolate she kept sabbath, to fulfil threescore and ten years
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Kol yemei hashamah shavetah lemalot shiv’im shanah* — of the sabbatical year and the jubilee, which Israel nullified in the Land; and corresponding to them they were exiled for seventy years — those seventy years that the Land of Israel kept sabbath. The years in which Israel provoked in their Land: four hundred and thirty years; of them three hundred and ninety from when they entered the Land until the ten tribes were exiled from it. And you find them explicitly: two hundred and forty-three from when Jeroboam reigned until Hoshea son of Elah was exiled, and in the days of the judges that they provoked, one hundred and eleven years, and the rest are unspecified. That is what is said (Ezekiel 4), “And lie thou upon thy left side, and lay the iniquity of the house of Israel upon it,” etc., “three hundred and ninety days,” etc., “and when thou hast accomplished these, thou shalt lie on thy right side, and shalt bear the iniquity of the house of Judah forty days, each day for a year.” This teaches that the house of Judah sinned from the time the ten tribes were exiled until Jerusalem was destroyed forty years. How? Twenty-two of Manasseh, as it is written (Kings II, 21), “as did Ahab,” and Ahab reigned twenty-two years, and for thirty-three he repented; behold, fifty-five he reigned; and two of Amon, and eleven of Jehoiakim — behold, thirty-five years; and this prophecy was said to Ezekiel in the fifth year of Zedekiah — behold, forty. The sum of all of them, of Israel and Judah: four hundred and thirty. Behold, for four hundred years: sixty-four sabbatical years and jubilees; thirty-five years: five sabbatical years; behold, sixty-nine; and the last jubilee year was counted against them as a sin, for it was through their sin that they were exiled from it. Behold, seventy years of holy sabbatical years that Israel did not release; therefore they were exiled seventy years, to fulfil what is said (Leviticus 27), “Then shall the land be paid her sabbaths.” So it is explained in Seder Olam. And here the Book of Chronicles ends with this because it said “to fulfil threescore and ten years,” it was necessary to say these verses here, and those of Ezra (at its beginning), to inform us when those seventy years were completed, how the wheel turned, that they returned to their land. Therefore it was necessary to say here “in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia” until “Whosoever there is among you of all His people… and let him go up.” And therefore this *vav* of *uvishnat* is added, because the Book of Daniel intervenes between them, for the Book of Ezra is continuous and arranged after the Book of Daniel, and so the *vav* refers from this to that.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The long chronological passage is translated as printed; its figures do not all agree. Arithmetic: 390 + 40 = 430 (Ezekiel 4:5–6); 243 + 111 = 354, and the remaining 36 are not specified (the printed “the rest are unspecified”); 22 + 2 + 11 = 35, plus the five years of Zedekiah before the prophecy, makes 40. The reigns are 55 years for Manasseh (2 Kings 21:1) and Ahab’s 22 years are in 1 Kings 16:29. The count “four hundred years: sixty-four, thirty-five years: five” totals four hundred and thirty-five, not four hundred and thirty as printed, and I did not resolve this. The printed reference “(Leviticus 27)” is a mistake; “Then shall the land be paid her sabbaths” is Leviticus 26:34 (JPS: “Then shall the land be paid her sabbaths, as long as it lieth desolate”). “Ezekiel” is misspelled in print. The first and last verses of Ezra 1 are quoted: Ezra 1:1–3. I did not verify Seder Olam.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: the spirit of Cyrus
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Et ruach Koresh* — his will.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: made a proclamation
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vaya’aver kol* — he had a herald proclaim to all the people of his kingdom.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: put it also in writing
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vegam bemikhtav* — he sent to all the people of his kingdom, saying.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Thus saith Cyrus king of Persia: All the kingdoms of the earth
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Koh amar Koresh melekh Paras kol mamlekhot* — that I rule as king over all kingdoms.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: He hath charged me
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Vehu pakad alai* — and He commanded me through Isaiah to build Him a house in Jerusalem, as it is said (Isaiah 44), “That saith of Cyrus: He is My shepherd,” etc.; “Thus saith the LORD to His anointed, to Cyrus” (there, 45); and this prophecy of Isaiah had already been told to him.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: The quotations are Isaiah 44:28 and 45:1.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: which is in Judah
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Asher biYhudah* — Jerusalem among the provinces of Judah.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: Whosoever there is among you of all His people—the LORD his God be with him—let him go up
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Mi vakhem mikol amo HaShem Elohav imo veya’al* — so was the proclamation in the provinces: whoever is of all the people of the Holy One, blessed be He, let him come to build His house which is in Jerusalem.

2 Chronicles.english_lemma_JPS: let him go up
2 Chronicles.english_translation: *Veya’al* — and may the Holy One, blessed be He, be at his help and at our help.
2 Chronicles.translator_note: This is the last comment of Rashi on the Book of Chronicles.
